Defeat Orcs in Urugarth and Carn Dûm (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Thinning the Horde
The Hillman called Donaith is concerned about the Orcs in the vicinity of Urugarth and Carn Dûm.
'Go into Urugarth or Carn Dûm and thin the Orc-hordes.'

Urugarth and Carn Dûm lie to the west of Gath Forthnír.
Donaith asked you to support the cause of his people and defeat the Orcs which gather in Urugarth or Carn Dûm.

Donaith can be found at Gath Forthnír.
Return to Donaith in eastern Angmar and tell him of your deeds.

'My brothers and I have not seen our uncle for many years. Rammas Deluon prevents safe passage to the lands beyond, and Uncle Donaith lives far to the east.
'If you find yourself in those distant lands, perhaps you may pay Uncle Donaith a visit? I am sure he would want to hear from us. It has been a long time, and much has happened in his absence.
'I do not know where he is now, only that he dwells far in the east.'

'It is good to meet you as well, ${PLAYER}. And you bring news from Aughaire? What a journey that must have been! And how did you pass through Rammas Deluon?
'Ah, but it matters not. Tell me, how do my nephews fare?'
A Distant Uncle
Rammas Deluon prevents the brothers Eilig, Machar, and Torquil from seeing their uncle Donaith, who lives far in the east of Angmar.
'Our uncle, Donaig, is lost somewhere beyond Rammas Deluon...please find him.'

Donaith is somewhere far to the east of Aughaire, well beyond Rammas Deluon.
Eilig and his brothers in Aughaire wish you to find their long-lost uncle.

'We have fought against the Trév Duvárdain and we have fought against the Orcs, and we will continue doing so until we are defeated or we drive each of them from our lands!
'Far to the north of Aughaire, the Orcs have taken the old city of Dûn Covád in the western hills. Two of their leaders are known to me: Nûlthauk and Ranghâsh. If you are able to defeat one or both of them, their ranks may fall into disarray.
'But that is a secondary consideration for me. Several months ago, these Orcs were part of the band that slew my sister Mairád. If you slay one of them, the other will know my vengeance is coming, either soon or late. That will be enough for me. Bring an ally or two, for the city is dark and full of peril.'
'I am glad of your victory on my behalf, ${PLAYER}. You have brought my vengeance against those who inhabit Dûn Covád. Let the other quake and wonder when my vengeance will find him!'
Dark Vengeance
Eilig, a warrior of the Trév Gállorg, seeks to cause disarray in the ranks of the Orcs that have taken the city of Dûn Covád and to visit his vengeance upon them for his sister, as well.

'The Orcs Nûlthauk and Ranghâsh are in the city of Dûn Covád, far to the north of Aughaire, among the western hills. Defeat one of them, and I will have vengeance upon both!
'Bring an ally or two with you, for the city is very dangerous and my foes no less so.'
'Let the Orcs quake at the rumour of our footfall.'
'The Orcs will not hold Dûn Covád forever.'

The Orcs Nûlthauk and Ranghâsh are in the city of Dûn Covád, far to the north of Aughaire, among the western hills.
Eilig has asked you to defeat one of the two Orcs that slew his sister and so avenge her memory.

Eilig is in the Búth Luikh in Aughaire.
You should return to Eilig and tell him of your journey into Dûn Covád.

'My brothers and I thirst for revenge against Orcs and Uruks who slew our kin. One seeks mindless vengeance, while the other seeks restitution - neither understands our foes truly. Orcs are cowards at heart, fighting only when driven by stern and heartless leaders. If we are to know peace again, then these leaders must be felled before they drive their hordes upon us once again.
It is the ones who led the raid who must be slain. The Ongburz chieftain Nûlthauk can be found deep within their cave north of here. Destroy him and the driving power behind the Orcs will be shattered for a time.'
'So, you have slain Nûlthauk? This was a deed well done! But there is more yet for you to do to complete our vengeance.'
Deep Vengeance
Eilig and his brothers Machar and Torquil are seeking vengeance against Orc-raiders who slew their kin.
'You must slay Nûlthauk, the Orc who led his minions when they slew our kin!'

The Orc-cave is north of Aughaire, just east of Dûn Covád.
Eilig has asked you to slay the Ongburz Chieftain, Nûlthauk who led the Orcs who slew his kindred.

Eilig is back at Aughaire.
Nûlthauk is dead, so you should return to Eilig to tell him the tale of your deeds.
Collected silver-nuggets (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'${PLAYER}...you said...? I've heard...of your deeds, for the people here...speak of...little else. I've just run from the city of Dûn Covád, far to the north; give me a moment to catch my breath.
'Thank you, ${PLAYER}. It was my Fém to recover nuggets of silver from the Orcs that now occupy Dûn Covád, and though I did gather one arm-load, it is not enough. The Ongbúrz are paid in silver for their cruelty; we must take it from them both as a remembrance of their victims and as an aid for those still with us.
'Travel to Dûn Covád, the city in the western hills, far to the north of Aughaire. The Ongbúrz have erected a great palisade in front of the city, but if you can make it past the barrier, many of the Orcs beyond will carry silver-nuggets. Collect several arm-loads of these and bring them here to me. I will rest in the meantime.'

'You have returned with silver-nuggets from the Ongbúrz! You are truly a friend to the Trév Gállorg, ${PLAYER}, and you do me honour by aiding with my Fém.
'If you need to have a rest after the long journey from Dûn Covád, pull up a sleeping mat.'
'You have not returned with enough silver-nuggets taken from the Ongbúrz. Dûn Covád is far to the north of Aughaire, in the western hills of Fasach-falroid.'
Bring silver-nuggets to Machar
Collect silver-nuggets (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Buried Treasure
Machar, exhausted from his long run out of Dûn Covád, has asked for your help recovering treasure from the Ongbúrz.
'Machar runs with great speed. Any other of my people would not have escaped from Dûn Covád with all the Ongbúrz alerted. He is to be praised for this, but his recklessness displeases me.'
'It is a great distance from here to Dûn Covád.'
'The Ongbúrz chased me with great speed, but I had the mastery!'

The city of Dûn Covád is in the western hills of Fasach-falroid, far to the north of Aughaire. The Ongbúrz have constructed a wooden palisade in front of the entrance. Machar is in the Búth Sánkhas of Aughaire, south-east of the market.
Machar, winded from his previous excursion into Dûn Covád, has asked you to travel into the city and collect silver-nuggets from the Orcs that now live there.
Collected gold-dust (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'The silver goes to lay our kin to rest. But there is more weregild yet to collect. As Torquil no doubt told you, the Tarkrîp were also allied with the Ongbúrz during their raid.
'I would have you reclaim the gold which they stole from us during their raid, so that it may restitute those who were bereft of family. You may find the Tarkrîp at the cave they call Burzum Pushdug, north of Tór Gailvin.'
'Gold of the Tarkrîp! You have done very well indeed. Now the spirits of my family can rest, satisfied with our vengeance.'
'You must collect weregild for the deaths of my kindred!'
Bring the gold-dust back to Machar
Collect gold-dust (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Hidden Hoard
Machar and his brothers Torquil and Eilig are seeking vengeance against Orc-raiders who slew their kin.
'The weregild you collected will soothe the spirits of the dead. Thank you, Southron!'
'The punishment of the Orcs has appeased my kindred.'

The Tarkrîp are just north of Tór Gailvin -- seek out the cave they call Burzum Pushdug.
Machar has asked you to collect gold from the cave of the Orcs who slew his kindred.
Defeated Ongbúrz Warriors at Morfil (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeated Ongbúrz Skirmishers at Morfil (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeated Ongbúrz Captain at Morfil

'My brothers were great warriors, and they gained much honour in battle against the Trév Duvárdain and the Orcs of Angmar. All spoke highly of them, and both women and men called them mighty.
'But even the mightiest man can be felled by a single arrow loosed from hiding, and so it was with my brothers. Orcs beset them by the cave Morfil, and they were defeated.
'I have petitioned Crannog for vengeance, and now he sees fit to unleash you upon the Orcs in my stead! I hope you are worthy, for if your strength is found lacking, it will go poorly for you. The entrance to Morfil is in Fasach-larran, east of Aughaire. Defeat Orcs in and around the cave and make them pay for the deaths of my brothers!'

'My brothers would be pleased by your service in their honour, ${PLAYER}. I give you thanks in their stead for the slaying of the Orcs at Morfil.
'For my part, I believe you are trustworthy. But it is up to Crannog to rule on this matter.'
Defeat Ongbúrz Warriors at Morfil (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeat Ongbúrz Skirmishers at Morfil (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeat Ongbúrz Captain at Morfil
Dark Raiders
Torquil's brothers were slain by Orcs, and he seeks allies to take his vengeance upon them.
'Morfil is in Fasach-larran, east of Aughaire. That is where you will find the Orcs that killed my brothers, and that is where you must go.'
'I thank you on behalf of my brothers, ${PLAYER}, for the deaths of many Orcs.'
'The Orcs will not soon forget the vengeance of Torquil and ${PLAYER}!'

The cave Morfil is in Fasach-larran, east of Aughaire.
Torquil has asked you to journey to Morfil and defeat the Orcs that killed his brothers.

Torquil is at Aughaire, near Crannog's ruling-seat, west of the settlement's centre island.
You have slain many Orcs at Morfil and should return now to Torquil at Aughaire.
Defeated Tarkrîp warriors at Bûrzum Pushdug (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeated Tarkrîp skirmishers at Bûrzum Pushdug (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Crannog is the chieftain of Aughaire, and he is right to challenge outsiders to prove their worthiness. But I, Finnán, have always prided myself on my keen eye and keener judgement. I know you are to be trusted, and that you will bring glory to the Trév Gállorg of Aughaire.
'You have already ventured into the fortress of Tór Gailvin, north-east of this settlement, and taken the prizes of the Trév Duvárdain from them; the traitors will surely rue their loss, and question whether their loyalty was given too quickly to the savage rulers of this land. But their treachery runs deeper than greed, for a tribe of Orcs is quartered in the cave of Bûrzum Pushdug, just north of Tór Gailvin! The Trév Duvárdain have these Orcs for neighbours, and this is a treachery so low that even their greed cannot justify it!
'Travel to Bûrzum Pushdug with an ally or two, and slay the Orcs there to remind the Trév Duvárdain what they would do were they worthy to walk the land of their fathers. The cave is on the west side of the hill on which Tór Gailvin is built, north-east of Aughaire.'
'I rejoice at your victory, ${PLAYER}! I knew I was right to give you my trust. The Trév Duvárdain will surely see that you have done what they should have and will feel remorse at their failing.'
Defeat Tarkrîp warriors at Bûrzum Pushdug (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeat Tarkrîp skirmishers at Bûrzum Pushdug (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Dark Hunters
Finnán believes that you are trustworthy and can help the Trév Gállorg combat the Orcs of Bûrzum Pushdug.

'The Trév Duvárdain of Tór Gailvin have been remiss, ${PLAYER}, and have allowed Orcs to muster in the cave of Bûrzum Pushdug. The two are neighbours, and it fills me with anger, as it would fill any who hear of it!
'You have agreed to defeat the Orcs of Bûrzum Pushdug, and I await news of your success. The cave is in the western side of the hill on which Tór Gailvin is built, north-east of Aughaire. An ally or two will be helpful, for the cave is dangerous and full of Orcs.'
'The Orcs of Bûrzum Pushdug will not forget you, ${PLAYER}, nor will I!'
'Hail, ${PLAYER}, slayer of Orcs!'

The cave Bûrzum Pushdug is north of Tór Gailvin, in the western side of the hill on which that fortress is built. Tór Gailvin is north-east of Aughaire.
Finnán asked you to defeat the Orcs of Bûrzum Pushdug in order to send a message of reproach to the Trév Duvárdain.

Finnán is at the centre island in the settlement of Aughaire.
You have defeated many Orcs in Bûrzum Pushdug and should now bring news of your victory to Finnán.
You escorted Dírdrë to safety

'I cannot believe that someone has come to my aid. I thought this nightmare would never end. My mother is Éa, perhaps you have heard of her? It has been such a long time without my loved ones.
'Please help me return to her. I fear that I cannot make it back on my own.'
'My Dírdrë is safe? Oh, thank you! Thank you, brave Southron!'
Escort Dírdrë to safety
End the Nightmare
You have found Dírdrë, daughter of Éa, alive and well.

Éa is at Tármunn Súrsa, near Carn Dûm.
Dírdrë has asked your aid returning to her mother, Éa.

Éa is at Tármunn Súrsa, near Carn Dûm.
You returned Dírdrë to the Hillmen. You should speak with Éa, her mother, at once.
Freed slaves in Carn Dûm (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'${CLASS}, you must help me. My people are gone, spirited away by the Orc-slavers of Carn Dûm.
'These slavers raid our villages and take our best warriors away to toil in their work-camps. Chained and shackled, they are forced to labour for the False King. Those that become injured or fall ill are left to die.
'My husband, Erscin, is among the captured slaves -- if he even lives and breathes. Please hurry! The slaves must be freed. You will find them in Carn Dûm, far to the west.'
'Thank you for doing this. My people will never forget your bravery. But please, tell me... did you find Erscin? Be he living or dead, I must know what happened to him.'
Free slaves in Carn Dûm (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Lifting the Yoke
Carn Dûm is the evil heart of Angmar, a terrible city protected by gates and hordes of Orc-warriors.
'You must free my people from Carn Dûm.'

Carn Dûm lies to the west of Tármunn Súrsa.
Éa's husband Erscin and his fellow warriors were captured by Orcs and taken to Carn Dûm. She has asked you to enter Carn Dûm and rescue Erscin.

Éa is at Tármunn Súrsa, east of Carn Dûm.
The slaves of Carn Dûm were set free and may now return to their homes, but you were unable to find Éa's husband, Erscin. You should return to Éa with the news.
Found Dírdrë

'Could it be that my Dírdrë still lives?
'It may be too much to hope for, but if you did not see her in Carn Dûm, perhaps they took her into Nan Gurth?
'Please, I beg you to go there and search for her. Nan Gurth lies to the south and east.'
Find Dírdrë
My Heart's Hope
The bracelet you found belonged to a girl of the Hillmen called Dírdrë. Her mother wonders if she could still be alive.
'Is it possible that Dírdrë yet lives?'

Dírdrë might be found in Nan Gurth, south-east of Carn Dûm.
Éa's daughter was taken from her many years ago. It could be that Dírdrë still lives.
You escorted Erscin to safety

'My husband remains in Carn Dûm. I know you have already done so much, but please... find it in your heart to help me once more.
'Erscin is strong of back and force of will. I cannot imagine that he fell to the Orcs, though perhaps he tried to escape and was killed. I cannot bear to imagine such things.
'If he lives, I fear he will not live long. I am sure that the Evil Ones will punish any slaves that remained behind. You must return to Carn Dûm and find him!'

'Thank you, ${PLAYER}, for rescuing me. I must return now to my wife. She will be worried that I have left her.
'You may continue on. I know the way from here. Be well, friend.'
'My dear husband has returned to me! Thank you, Southron, for all you have done!'
'Thank you, stranger. Whoever you are, I can see that you are no Orc-friend. Let us depart this evil place. And please, whatever you do, do not awaken the gorthorog!'
Find Erscin
Speak to Erscin
The Strongest Back
The slaves of Carn Dûm were set free, but Éa, a woman of the hillmen dwelling at Tármunn Súrsa, is still missing her husband.
'Please, return to Carn Dûm and find Erscin!'

Carn Dûm lies far to the west of Tármunn Súrsa.
Éa begged you to find her missing husband, the hillman-warrior called Erscin.

Erscin is at Carn Dûm, far to the west of Gath Forthnír.
Erscin is waiting to speak with you again.

Éa is at Tármunn Súrsa, east of Carn Dûm.
You found Erscin, alive and well, within Carn Dûm and returned him to safety. You should let Éa know the good tidings.
Defeated trolls in Urugarth (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'No doubt you are here at the behest of my cousin. Your help may or may not be needed, but as you seem to have experience in these matters, let me explain the situation.
'Long have my brethren and I suffered the trolls of Angmar, the gertheryg. We must strike a blow against Angmar by defeating these creatures and their master.
'The fortress-city of Urugarth is their stronghold. Cross the narrow bridge, and eventually the path turns south to Urugarth -- or so it is said.'
'You have done well, but there is more still to do. The leader of the gertheryg must be slain.'
Defeat trolls in Urugarth (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Moving Mountains
The gertheryg, the terrible troll-kin of Angmar, pose one of the greatest threats to the Free Peoples.
'Go into Urugarth and defeat the gertheryg and their leader. Cross the bridge and follow the paths south-west until they turn at last south to Urugarth.'

Gertheryg may be found in Urugarth, west of Tármunn Súrsa.
Táni asked you to seek out the trolls and their leader and slay them all.

Táni is at Tármunn Súrsa, east of Urugarth.
With the trolls and their leader defeated, it is time to return to Táni.

'I can see why you were sent all the way up here to help us. You did a commendable job back there against the trolls, but there is more work to do.
'The Gertheryg of Carn Dûm are commanded by a vile fiend called Barashal. You must go there and slay him.
'Barashal won't go down without a fight, so be sure to rest well before you head out west into Carn Dûm.'
'A great hero is what you are! A few more like you, and we can surely turn the tide against the Enemy!'
Lord of the Gertheryg
You fought the trolls of Urugarth with great success, but the leader of the Gertheryg remains a threat.
'Go into Carn Dûm and defeat Barashal, the leader of the Gertheryg.'

Barashal is at Carn Dûm, to the west of Tármunn Súrsa.
Táni was impressed by your efforts to purge the trolls from Urugarth and has sent you on another mission: to defeat Barashal, the leader of the Gertheryg.

Táni is at Tármunn Súrsa, to the east of Carn Dûm.
You defeated Barashal, the Lord of the Gertheryg, in battle and should return to Táni with the tidings of your success.

'You have been a great help to us here, ${PLAYER}, but my cousin Eiláf is facing a whole different set of problems up to the north and might have need for your help as well. He is helping to oversee a small outpost we have built there. It is called Myrkworth, and it rests within Imlad Balchorth.
'If you wish to continue to help us, travel to Myrkworth and find my cousin Eiláf. Myrkworth lies north of here atop a high hill in that treacherous land.
'Oh, and if you do make it to Myrkworth, give Eiláf my regards!'

'Ah, Hwati sent you, did he? A good, solid dwarf, he is! I haven't seen him in far too many days. But there is time for talk when the work is done....
'While Orcs and trolls are an immediate threat to Gabilshathûr, Angmar's Dead are a more subtle and dangerous one. We dwarves have come here to try to find a way to counter this threat.
'Speak to Gautar, Birgir, or Oflár and see if there is something they have for you to do. Perhaps in time, I may have a task for you as well.'
The Northern Cousin
Hwati in Gabilshathûr thinks his cousin to the north in Myrkworth may have need for your help.
'My cousin Eiláf can be found in Myrkworth, which lies atop a high hill to the north, in Imlad Balchorth. Beware those lands, for Angmar's Dead walk the earth there!'

Myrkworth lies in Imlad Balchorth atop a high hill, north of Gabilshathûr.
Hwati has asked you to travel to Myrkworth and speak with his cousin, Eiláf.
Claimed one of Ronkûrz' maces

'We have had a stroke of luck! While you were away, a dwarf-prospector returned and told us that he saw Ronkûrz entering the Orc-encampment of Mor Maudhúl. No doubt he is going there to train the Uruks, but being away from the arena leaves him vulnerable!
'Wait, wait, I am getting ahead of myself. Allow me to explain my plan. You see, to truly end Maethad's threat, we must defeat its master, a Gorthorog named \qKhurrákh.\q Khurrákh rarely shows himself though, and only fights those he deems worthy of his attention. Ronkûrz, another Gorthorog and current champion of Maethad, is his prize student. If you were to defeat him and claim one of his maces, Khurrákh would have to fight you!
'Mor Maudhúl lies to the north of here, on the far side of the foul lake in Duvuinen. Ronkûrz should be found somewhere within the encampment. Hurry now!'
'Wonderful, you have done it! You have shown yourself to be a hardy warrior, which is good, for your hardest challenge lies ahead: defeating the master of Maethad.'

'If we are to end Maethad's threat, we must defeat its master, Khurrákh. However, to draw him forth, we must defeat his prized student, Ronkûrz, and claim one of his maces.
'Ronkûrz can be found to the north in the Orc encampment of Mor Maudhúl, which lies on the far side of the foul lake in Duvuinen.'
Bring Ronkûrz's mace to Hwati
Claim one of Ronkûrz' maces
Champion of Maethad
Hwati told you that to truly end the threat of Maethad, you must defeat its master, Khurrákh. However, this Gorthorog will only fight you if you can prove yourself worthy of his attention.

Ronkûrz, the champion of Maethad, can be found training Uruks within the the Orc encampment of Mor Maudhúl, north of Gabilshathûr, on the far side of the lake in Duvuinen.
Once you have claimed one of Ronkûrz's maces, bring it back to Hwati in Gabilshathûr.
Defeated gertheryg in Maethad (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeated trolls in Maethad (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Ah, welcome to you! It is good to have unexpected allies in our struggle to survive! It feels that -- after many years of hiding in the shadow of Angmar -- we can now finally strike back!
'In this matter, you may be able to help. To the north and east there is a place called \qMaethad.\q It is a great arena in which those of troll-kind, especially the gertheryg, train for battle. Those who survive the arena go on to lead and train others of Angmar. Striking at this arena would deal a blow to Angmar's ability to raise and train its army!
'To end this threat, we must first defeat those who are training within the arena's walls, then we can move on and crush those who lead the training efforts. Go and reduce the number of the gertheryg and trolls within Maethad.'
'You have thinned their numbers? Good! Ah, a strong blow against Maethad! Now we can turn our attention to those who lead the training!'
Defeat gertheryg in Maethad (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeat trolls in Maethad (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
The Arena of Maethad
To the north-east of Gabilshathûr is a place named \qMaethad\q. Here, trolls and their gorthorog-masters train to fight and lead Angmar's armies.
'Maethad lies to the north and east. If we hold any hope of ending the threat of Maethad, we must first defeat some of the gertheryg and the trolls training within.'

The arena of Maethad is north and east of Gabilshathûr.
Hwati has asked you to find the arena and thin the numbers of gertheryg and trolls training within.

Hwati is back at Gabilshathûr, west and south of Maethad.
Having defeated a number of gertheryg and trolls, you should return to Hwati.
Defeated Khurrákh

'We are now ready to strike at the very heart of Maethad, its master: Khurrákh. He is a great and terrible Gorthorog, having slain many to achieve and keep his position. Defeating him will not be easy, but must be done, if Maethad's threat is to be ended.
'Take Ronkûrz' mace and enter the centre of Maethad. From what we have been told of what happens there, you should find something the Gertheryg call the \qUshum-ghâsh\q in the centre of Maethad. Once there, display Ronkûrz' mace near the fire. Khurrákh will have no choice but to face you. His sense of \qhonour,\q if a such a concept exists within a Gorthorog, will force him to fight you.
'It will not be an easy fight, but it must be done.'

'It is done? Khurrákh is dead? I cannot believe it! Maethad's master is dead!
'While some day I'm sure there will be another Master of Maethad, for now, you have thrown Maethad into confusion.
'However, there is more work to be done, further to the north....'
'Where is Ronkûrz mace?'
Draw Khurrákh forth and defeat him
Defeat Khurrákh
Talk to Hwati
Master of Maethad
Hwati has told you that now that you have Ronkûrz' mace, you can draw forth Khurrákh, the Master of Maethad, and challenge him.
'Go now to Maethad, north and east of here and draw Khurrákh out. End Maethad's threat, once and for all!'
'Only the greatest of heroes could have defeated the Master of Maethad!'

Maethad is north and east of Gabilshathûr.
Hwati has instructed you to enter the centre of Maethad and use the Ushum-ghâsh to draw Khurrákh forth.

Hwati is back at Gabilshathûr, west and south of Maethad.
Having defeated Khurrákh, you should return to Hwati and tell him the tale of your deeds.
Collected weapons from weapon-crates (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Our stores of weapons run low, and we lack the materials to craft more. Without proper weapons, our cause seems hopeless. Unless....
'There is a possibility. We can pillage the supplies of the Enemy at Carn Dûm and bring them back here where they can be reforged. Not only will we increase our store of weapons, we will take the same out of the hands of the Enemy.
'If you will, travel west into Urugarth and spirit away their weapon crates. When you have the crates, return to me.'
'Excellent! I will get these to the forge, and we'll set about restocking our weapons stores.'
'You were asked to bring back weapons, but all I see are empty hands.'
Collect weapons from weapon-crates (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring the weapons to Throst
The Enemy's Arms
The resistance at Gath Forthnír needs equipment if they are to make a stand against Carn Dûm.
'I cannot say it will be a pleasure to touch Uruk-forged iron, but we'll melt it down into proper swords and axes.'

Urugarth is in Carn Dûm to the west of Gath Forthnír.
Throst devised a clever plan to steal supplies from the Enemy and use them to equip the resistance at Gath Forthnír.

Throst is at Gath Forthnír, east of Carn Dûm.
You should return to Throst with tidings of your victory.
Collected white Warg-hide
Collected rugged Warg-hides (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Throst told me what you did. An admirable feat! It will be a fine thing when the Enemy realizes we are cutting them down with their own iron and steel.
'If we are to go to battle, we will need more than sharp blades. You must return to Urugarth and hunt the Wargs there for their hides. We can tan their thick hides and fashion them into good quality armour.
'Skin the pelts from the largest Wargs you can find. Their leader will have the toughest hide of them all so be sure to track him down as well.'

'These will do well. It is a shame that we cannot get rid of the rank stench of these furs.
'Ah, well. At least the hides themselves can be saved. I will begin work on that armour right away!'
'Those Wargs are not going to skin themselves.'

'I cannot thank you enough for your help, good ${PLAYER}! I do not know if you have ever been thrown in the stocks... but I can tell you, it is not a comfortable experience.
'I do think Captain Trotter was ready to hang me for what happened. You have likely saved my life, my friend.'
'Humph, well then. I'm glad that debacle is over with. Perhaps now we can focus on more pressing issues....'

Talbot Hinton is in the stocks in Trestlebridge.
You should free Talbot Hinton from his bonds, for his innocence is proven.
Free Talbot Hinton from the stocks

'Please, show the sleeping-draught to Captain Trotter. Then he will know I was not remiss in my duties.
'We have been sabotaged!'

Captain Trotter listens to your explanation, and takes a deep sniff from the potion flask.
'The Orcs brewed this, did they? This is not good for us. It appears they have taken to using sabotage when their raids have been dashed against our defences at the Trestlespan.
'I suppose Talbot may be freed from his bonds. But the guards must be on the alert for any suspicious travellers from this point on. It is a sad day for Trestlebridge....'
Talbot Redeemed

Talbot Hinton is in Trestlebridge.
You should speak with Talbot Hinton.

Captain Trotter can be found in Trestlebridge.

You have freed the innocent guard from his unjust imprisonment

Show the Orc-brewed sleeping draught to Captain Trotter

Captain Trotter can be found in Trestlebridge.
Talbot Hinton asked you to show Captain Trotter the strange potion brewed by the Orcs near Nan Wathren.

'I have half a mind to lock up every last guard in this sorry excuse for a town, after they let this catastrophe take place. Look at our town! People burned out of their homes, ash falling like snow....
'Aggy Digweed was the only one who kept her mind during this attack. If not for her, we would all be dead. Nobody even remembers what happened -- just Aggy, running to and fro trying to rouse everyone!
'I'll see that Talbot Hinton hanged for letting this happen! Mark my words.'

'Captain Trotter is very preoccupied with punishing those who slept through the attack, but I am much more concerned about what may happen if we let down our guard again.
'I have not slept in two days, but I will not abandon my post here. Would you be willing to help me?'
Find and speak with Aggy Digweed
One Present Mind

The residents of Trestlebridge are all very shaken by the explosions and fires of the previous evening. Guards were nowhere to be found during the commotion -- all but Aggy Digweed, who showed a keen presence of mind during the attack.

Aggy Digweed is at the Trestlespan on the northern edge of town.
According to Captain Trotter, Aggy Digweed was the only guard who may be able to shed light on the unfortunate circumstances that have befallen Trestlebridge.
The Pass of Nan Wathren
You have explored the edge of Nan Wathren.
Find and enter the dangerous pass of Nan Wathren

'I wonder, ${PLAYER} -- did you even find the brewer of the foul potion while you explored the Orc-encampments?'
You tell Captain Trotter that you had no such luck.
'Ah. That is dire news indeed, for it means that the enemy's influence stretches further than I ever thought. I have a troubling notion that Nan Wathren has fallen to Orcs.
'The pass of Nan Wathren is a dangerous place in the best of times. If you wish to help Trestlebridge once and for all, you must wipe out the Orc presence from Nan Wathren.'
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTE: Nan Wathren is a dangerous area. It would be wise to travel there in the company of a fellowship.</rgb>

You have come to the edge of Nan Wathren.
You may enter if you wish, but it will be a dangerous path.
Nan Wathren lies beyond this bridge....
Since no sign has been found of the potion-master who made the powerful sleeping draught, Captain Trotter has asked you to extend your search into a more dangerous territory: Nan Wathren.

Nan Wathren lies to the north-east of Trestlebridge.
You should head to the pass of Nan Wathren to search for the source of Trestlebridge's troubles.

'You found something to prove that we were drugged? That is wonderful, ${PLAYER}! You must show the captain at once, so that he can set me free!'

'Someone to hear me out at last! Yes, I was on guard duty the night of the blasts... but I did not fall asleep! Well, I did, but I cannot remember anything about it. It is almost like I was drugged.
'I only remember waking up to Aggy shaking me, fires roaring all around us. We all slept through the thunderous blasts. How do you explain that?
'But Captain Trotter will hear none of it....'
A Poor Guard
Talbot Hinton claims he was not remiss in his guard duties the night of the attack, and that someone may have drugged him and the other guards.

Orc encampments can be found to the north-east of Trestlebridge.
You should search Orc encampments for signs that the guards of Trestlebridge were drugged before the attack, proving Talbot's innocence.

Talbot Hinton can be found in Trestlebridge.
At the Orc camps north of Trestlebridge, you were able to find cauldrons of a vile liquid, and collect some of the contents.

A clue to the great boom heard in Trestlebridge may be found somewhere in town.

'I dare not abandon my guard post to investigate the carnage, but would you like to help? You could search the town and figure out how this could have happened.
'The explosion was deafening; why did no one wake? What caused this mayhem? I have never heard a thing like it in all my life....'
'What's this, then? Incendiary powder of some sort... how strange! Who would do such a thing?'
A Great Boom in the Night

Aggy Digweed recalls a great explosion in town, and that no guards but herself were roused by the sound.

'So much... was it all destined for us? Or perhaps they were planning it to bring it along to Bree once we were all dead.
'Evil surrounds us, ${PLAYER}. This is a bad time, mark my words. I've never seen Orcs dare to come so close, or interfere with our lives other than scare travellers on the road. I've never seen such great numbers of them.
'You'll be wanting to tell Captain Trotter all about this.'
Find the black-fire at the first encampment
Find the black-fire at the second encampment

'Flaming powder! I like this not at all. I want to know how it came here, but more than that, I want to ensure that it never comes here again.
'Speak with Aggy at the span, and see if she knows anything of this... this... black-fire stuff! I have never seen anything like it.'

'Captain Trotter is right to be afraid of this... black-fire. It must be the Orcs that have been cropping up near here of late, to the north-east near the pass of Nan Wathren. Surely they have wrought some fell magic, and are using it to bring down our town and choke off the Greenway!
'We cannot let them, ${PLAYER}. They failed to destroy us once, so we must assume that they will try again. You cannot let them!'

'So the Orcs were behind it all, eh? But how did they come in, if nobody saw them?
'Hopefully you have ensured that they won't be back to the same mischief any time soon, which will give us time to rebuild, but there are still mysteries to be solved. How did they sneak the stuff in?'
The Black-fire
Aggy Digweed wants you to search nearby Orc-encampment for signs of more black-fire
Aggy Digweed has asked you to ensure that no more of the suspicious black-fire can find its way into Trestlebridge.

Orc encampments have been spotted north-east of Trestlebridge.
You should investigate the Orc-camps for signs of the black-fire, and carefully destroy any that you find.

Aggy Digweed can be found in Trestlebridge.

The half-orc rumoured to have been in Trestlebridge can likely be found in the Orc camp north-east of Trestlebridge.
You should search for anyone matching Aggy Digweed's description.

'The question remains as to how the suspicious powder got into town at all. We have many travellers here, being on the Greenway... and I did hear rumours of an ugly, mean-looking man that came through last night.
'I didn't see him myself, but he made a few folks uneasy. He was already gone when I went to look for him.
'Folks say he looked more than a little Orkish. Have you ever heard of such a thing?'

'You defeated the ugly brute? Thank you, ${PLAYER}. We will have to be less welcoming to travellers, now, I'm afraid.
'If such a man could come unhindered and wreak such havoc, then we will never be safe. Orcs creep ever closer to our gates. These are dangerous times, my friend.'
Search for the half-orc who planted the powder
Return to Aggy Digweed

Aggy Digweed heard rumour of a man that was likely a half-orc slinking around Trestlebridge the night of the blast.

Aggy Digweed is in Trestlebridge.
You should return to Aggy Digweed with news of your victory against Lugbas.

'For one so small, you are very good at killing Orcs. The Orcs are many, but we think they run through Ram Dúath because Men tell them to go. Evil Men from the North, from Angmar, have come to Ram Dúath.
'One of the Men is the leader. We think he will send the Orcs against us soon. We cannot fight them in their camp, they are too strong, but you are strong too. Maybe you can help us fight this Man, this Captain from Angmar.
'The Angmarim have a camp north and east of here called Frith-vailë.'
'The captain of the Angmarim is dead? Good! Maybe the Angmarim will send another leader, but for now we are safe!'
The Far Reaching Hand
Chief Tuokki is worried that the Angmarim who command the Orcs will send them to fight the Earth-kin.
'The Orcs may not come if you kill the leader of the Angmarim.'

Frith-vailë is in the north-east part of Ram Dúath.
Chief Tuokki, hoping to discourage the Orcs and the Angmarim, has asked you to defeat the Captain of the Angmarim in Ram Dúath.

Chief Tuokki is at the Suuri-lehmä camp in Ram Dúath.
Now that you've defeated the Iron-crown Captain, return to the Earth-kin Chief and tell him of your deed.
Collected goblin-gems (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'I know you little folk prize the glittering stones. We care little for most of these stones, but we treasure the kind we call Eyes of the Earth. I think in your tongue you call them cat's-eyes and moonstones.
'It seems that the goblins who serve the Angmarim in their fort just north-east of the Ram Dûath have stolen a great many of these stones, including eyes of the earth from our people.
'I would ask you to go to this fort and take back the goblin-treasures. They should be stored in chests filled with many gems. We will take the Eyes of the Earth, and you will take the rest, with our thanks.'
'Ah, yes, you have done it! Here... I will separate out the Eyes of the Earth, and the rest shall be yours!'
'The goblins guard their chests glittering stones well, do they not? Beware their Angmarim masters as well!'
Collect goblin-gems (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring the goblins' gems back to Aslak at Lehmä-koti
The Goblins' Treasure
Aslak of the Suuri-lehmä told you that the goblins have collected hoards of gems in the fort they share with the Angmarim on the north-eastern pass of Ram Dúath.

The goblins of the Ram Dúath have stolen several treasures from the Suuri-lehmä.
Aslak has told you that the gems might be found in chests within the Angmarim fort to the North-east.

You have recovered several semi-precious gems stolen from the Surri-lehmä by the goblins of the Ram Duath.
You must return them to Aslak at Lehmä-koti.

'North of here, Ram Dúath opens into the dark land of Angmar. There are many evil Men and Orcs in that land, and worse things too, so we do not go there ourselves. But not all the folk of Angmar are enemies to us. There is one clan of Hillmen in those lands who have ever been our friends, sending south to trade with us when they can. Perhaps they will be friendly to you as well.
'Like us, they hate the Orcs, and they stand against the evil ones who rule in the black city. We want to let them know that the main body of Orcs has now passed south into the North Downs. This may help them in their counsels, and perhaps they can resume their trade with us.
'Find the man called Crannog. He is the Chief in Aughaire. Tell him the news I have told you. Aughaire is west from the northern pass of Ram Dúath, in a concealed valley over a steep rise in the hills. Sometimes in the past, the men of Aughaire travelled a steep trail to our village -- a trail the Jorthkyn are too big to walk, but perhaps you can find it not far from here.'

'Ho, Southron! The Jorthkyn sent you to us? It is long and longer still since last we had enough goods of our own to be able to trade with those strange folk.
'Your words are welcome, though little good do they do us. We are hard-pressed on all sides, even with the Orc-army no longer encamped upon our doorstep.
'Still, I will open the host-hearth of Aughaire to you. You are welcome here, for so long as we ourselves remain.'
Men of the Hills
Pirkka of the Suuri-lehmä, told you of a clan of Hillmen in Angmar who are friendly to them and should be made aware that the main body of the Orc-host has passed south into the North Downs.
'Will you bring the news of the Orc-army to Crannog?'

Aughaire is west of the northern pass of Ram Dúath, a valley concealed and surrounded by hills. There is also said to be a secret trail that goes there directly from the Earth-kin village.
Pirkka has asked you to take the news of the passage of the Orc-army to Crannog, chief of the Hillmen of Aughaire.
You have slain Morcheryn!

'You are a proven friend to our people, but what I ask of you now may be too much. There is a cave in this very place where the merrevail make their lair, and in this cave dwells their leader, a bloody-handed creature we have heard the Orcs call Morcheryn.
'The merrevail are cruel and vicious, worse even than the Orcs and the evil Men of Carn Dûm. They will continue to prey on us if we do not fight them. I ask you to enter this cave and to destroy this 'Morcheryn'. If she falls, then perhaps the others will leave Ram Dúath and return to whatever foul place in Angmar it is that spawned them.
'These evil things have slain many of the Suuri-lehmä... I think you should take friends with you if you go there.'
'I am pleased that you have returned safely from such a dangerous quest. In the name of my people, I thank you for your deeds.'
Slay Morcheryn
Mistress of Shadows
You have assisted the Earth-kin scout, but the morroval-threat remains, endangering the Earth-kin and all else who dwell in the hills of Angmar.
'For the sake of my people, I ask you to slay Morcheryn.'
'It is good that you were able to slay Morcheryn.'
'The queen of the bat-women will trouble us no more!'

Morcheryn dwells in a cave on the east side of Ram Dúath, where the other merrevail can also be found.
The Earth-kin scout has asked you to seek out and destroy the leader of the Merrevail for the safety of his people. He also suggested you take friends.

The Earth-kin Scout is hidden in a valley east of Duvairë in the Ram Dúath.
With the Mistress of Shadows slain, you should return to him.
Defeated Blogmal fighters (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeated Blogmal skirmishers (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'For much time now, Orcs and evil Men and other evil things have come through Ram Dúath from the North, from Angmar. They go to fight in the South, but they cause much trouble here, too.
'We hate Orcs and their friends, and we try to fight them when we can, but now there are too many for us, and our hunters cannot return from the southern plains. Will you fight the Orc-folk, too? Help us, and kill the Orcs in Ram Dúath. Many Orcs of the Blogmal tribe can be found in the south-east part of the pass.
'We will give you the coins that we take from the dead Orcs. We have little need for them.'
'You have shed much Orc blood. This is good. We thank you for your help.'
Defeat Blogmal fighters (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeat Blogmal skirmishers (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Orcs in the Ram Dúath
Orcs marching through Ram Dúath have unsettled the Earth-kin dwelling there and have cut off any hope of safe return for the Earth-kin hunters sojourning in the North Downs.
'As long as the Orcs fill the pass, our hunters cannot return, and our people will starve.'

There are Blogmal Orcs in the south-east part of the Ram Dúath.
The Tuokki, the Earth-kin elder leading the Suuri-lehmä tribe while their chieftain is away south in the North Downs, has asked you to help drive the Blogmal Orcs from Ram Dúath.

Chief Tuokki is at the Suuri-lehmä camp in Ram Dúath.
You should return to Chief Tuokki and tell him of your victory against the Orcs of the Blogmal tribe.
Collected Aurochs Skull (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Many years ago, we brought with us from the South some skulls of lehmä -- what you little people call aurochs. Very important skulls. The skulls honour Suuri-lehmä.
'Jorthkyn take the skulls on path through Ram Dúath to see new sights in this place. This must be done every year. This year, our brethren did not return. Scouts say that Orcs killed Jorthkyn and took the skulls. Orcs are in a strong place in the east side of Ram Dúath.
'Bring back a skull from the Orcs. Maybe they are in their strong place called Skathmur?'

'A skull has returned to us. Welcome home, skull! What have you seen amongst the Orcs?
'Thank you, ${PLAYER}. You are a friend to the Jorthkyn. All the lehmä now rejoice!'
'We need our skull back.'
Bring the aurochs-skull back to Santtu at Lehmä-koti
Collect Aurochs Skull (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Stolen Skulls
Aurochs skulls apparently have some significant meaning to the Earth-kin of the Suuri-lehmä, and some have been stolen from them.

The aurochs skulls are likely in Skathmur in the eastern part of Ram Dúath.
Santtu has asked you to recover a stolen aurochs skull.
Destroyed catapults (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Destroyed siege-towers (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'The Men and Orcs of Angmar have been bringing great wheeled war-engines through Ram Dúath. At first, they often broke on their own. It took many tries before the stupid Orcs learned how to move these clumsy things safely through the pass.
'We thought, they are taking such pains, perhaps we can help them too. So we showed them the strength of stone and broke many of them ourselves, seeing as the evil ones seemed to want them in the South so badly.
'Now, though, they have learned again, and the war-engines are too well-guarded for us. But maybe you can fight through to them. These must be treasures for these evil folk, things they need to make war in the South. You can find them in the eastern pass.'

'It is good that those engines were broken. We would not want the Orcs to think they had easy lives!
'I know you fight the Orcs and Men of Angmar for your own reasons, but it is good that we can fight them together in Ram Dúath.'
Destroy catapults (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Destroy siege-towers (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Strength of Stone
The Earth-kin have been destroying the siege-engines of the Angmarim as they wheel them through Ram Dúath, but now they are too strongly guarded for the Earth-kin to reach.
'Destroy the war-engines and show the Orcs the strength of stone.'
'We have done a great hurt to the evil ones, have we not?'
'Orcs will not find it so easy to fight without their war-carts. You have done well, little ${PLAYER}.'

The war-engines -- siege towers and catapults -- of the Angmarim are in the eastern part of Ram Dúath.

'Another thing there is now in Ram Dúath stranger than Men or Orcs, maybe worse than either of them. Evil people like women, but with wings! They are vicious, deadly creatures, while I was scouting the Orcs they attacked me.
'You must destroy these bat-women, they are fierce and kill without mercy. Others will come to look for me, they must not hurt more of the Jorthkyn.
'I am afraid of these foul creatures. Such things do not belong in the world.'
'They are cruel creatures, these bat-women; it is good that you have thinned their numbers. My wound is quickly healing, soon I will return and warn the Suuri-lehmä.'
Defeat merrevail (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Wings of Darkness and Death
The Earth-kin Scout has been attacked by strange folk who have come into Ram Dúath from the North. He told you the women with wings are in league with the Angmarim.
'You must hurry, I do not know when my people will come in search of me. Slay the bat-women, protect Jorthkyn.'

The bat-winged creatures who injured the Earth-kin scout are in the eastern gorges of Ram Dúath.
The Earth-kin scout's request was for you to kill the vicious merrevail so that others will not be injured or worse.

The Earth-kin Scout is hidden in a valley east of Duvairë in the Ram Dúath.
You should return to the Earth-kin Scout and tell him of your success against the merrevail.

'So, another Southron comes to trouble us. Well, we are not like those who crawl before the Iron Crown, and we still hallow the guest-law. So... be welcome.
'You will not find much love amongst us for your kind, stranger. We listened to the Southron Golodir and stood against the Iron Crown, but now that he has abandoned us, we are on our last leg. The other clans have joined against us, and only the last frail vestiges of the Treaty of the Hills protects us from war. Soon enough, though, we will fall, one way or the other.
'Oh, you wish to hear more of our troubles? I have no breath to repeat the tale of woe. Ask the Lore-singer, Arzhur, if you must know the long, sad story. He is near the tents to the north.'

'Ah, another stranger. Crannog has sent you, eh? Listen well, then. Some years past, when the evil men of Angmar were busily corrupting and subjugating the men of the hills, a Southron, Golodir by name, came to us. He was a noble man and a strong warrior, and we could tell he spoke truth in all things.
'Golodir warned us not to follow the Iron Crown and showed us the evil secrets of Angmar. He led us to confront our brothers in the other clans and to expel the Angmarim emissaries who whispered in the ears of our elders.
'But then Golodir disappeared. Some say he was slain, others say he has returned to the South, abandoning us to our fate. Now most of the men of Aughaire still stand against Angmar and their slave-clans, but we have lost hope for the future.'
The Free Folk
Chief Crannog has sent you to Lore-singer Arzhur to learn something of the Free Folk of Angmar.
'Speak to Arzhur. I have not the breath to waste.'
'Leave me, southron, I am weary of your presence.'

Arzhur is in Aughaire, north-east of Chief Crannog.
Chief Crannog has sent you to speak to the Lore-singer Arzhur to hear about the history of his clan.
Collected pea-plants (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'The herbal poultice will help with our defence, ${PLAYER}; now we must see to the attack, and I know upon what to focus our efforts: peas!
'The farms north-east of here have been taken from my people and put to the use of the Trév Duvárdain. Now that we have retaken Fail-á-Khro, we can do something about it.
'Travel north-east to the farmland outside the city of Donnvail and harvest the pea-plants you find there. We may not have the numbers to take the farms, but we can at least take their peas!'
'Thank you for these pea-plants, ${PLAYER}. Our enemies will go hungry tonight and know that we are serious about taking what is ours!'
'The pea-plants belong to us, and you should recover them from the farms outside Donnvail, to the north-east!'
Collect pea-plants (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring pea-plants to Cána
Restoring the Peas
Cána is worried that the Trév Duvárdain and their Angmarim masters are getting fat off the land that is rightfully that of the Trév Gállorg.
'Harvest pea-plants from the farms outside the city of Donnvail, to the north-east. Bring them to me, and we will keep them from feeding our enemies!'
'You have performed many great deeds, ${PLAYER}. I thank you for the pea-plants.'
'Peas can be used in several delicacies of the Trév Gállorg.'

Pea-plants can be found in the farmland outside the city of Donnvail, north-east of Fail-á-Khro.
Cána has tasked you with recovering the pea-plants from the farms outside Donnvail.

Cána is at Fail-á-Khro, on the road north of Aughaire.
You have harvested pea-plants from the farms near Donnvail to keep them from the enemies of the Trév Gállorg.
Collected food-stores (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'The farms of Fasach-falroid produce as much as our people can coax from them, but the Angmarim exert pressure on the people of Donnvail and take most of the food for themselves and their army.
'The surplus food is stored in crates within the city of Donnvail until such time as the army has need of it...but the Trév Gállorg need it now! It seems that the Angmarim would rather let it rot than go to feed the hungry mouths of my people!
'Travel north-east to the city of Donnvail and return to me with the food-stores. I will make sure that it goes to those who need it. Let the army of Angmar starve!'
'I thank you, ${PLAYER}. My people have greater need for these food-stores than do the Orcs and Trév Duvárdain who fight for Angmar.'

'You have not brought me the food-stores from Donnvail that you promised? How can this be so?
'The city is to the north-east of Fail-á-Khro.'
Bring food-stores to Ekhagan

Stealing Stores
The farmers of Donnvail produce as much food as they are able in this harsh land, but the Angmarim seize most of it for themselves and their army.

Food-stores are kept within the city of Donnvail, north-east of Fail-á-Khro.

'We of Aughaire have many troubles. Too many, I think for Chief Crannog, who has lost heart and hope. But perhaps you might wish to aid us, as Golodir once did?
'We are trapped in a maze of clan-laws. Those who serve Angmar have tried to make it impossible for us to fulfill our obligations. If we fail, we will be subject to open warfare.
'Our first obligation is to obtain a drake's egg from Nád Nathair. We need this as a token of honour to meet the blood challenges of the other clans. Yet our hunters are mercilessly harrassed by our enemies when we approach the drakes. Will you go to the drake lair not far to the north and obtain an egg for us? The drakes are attended by many hill-beasts, so you will know the lair by their presence.
'Listen well: the drakes are fearsome foes, but they are not devoted parents. It would be best to take an egg from a nest which is not guarded by a drake.'
'Good. You have proven yourself worthy, friend ${PLAYER}.'
'We need a drake egg to present to the other clans.'
Bring the drake egg to Arzhur
Collect a drake egg
The Drake's Egg
A challenge has been set before Arzhur's clan, but a token of honour is required before the folk of Aughaire can fulfill their lawful obligations to the other clans of Angmar.

The drake-lair is Nád Nathair, north of Aughaire. Nád Nathair can be recognized not only by the drakes but by the many hill-beasts in the area.
Lore-singer Arzhur has asked you to obtain a drake egg. The egg is needed as a token for the men of Aughaire to present to the other hill-clans. He has warned you to avoid the drakes themselves in seeking an egg.

'Another challenge has been placed before us. Again, we need a token of honour before we can fight. This time, I am afraid clan law is set against us, as there has been a dispute over your participation in the last challenge. If we are to win our way free of this morass, you must fight this time alone.
'First, we require a stone from the Cairn of Honour. The Cairn is in Fasach-Falroid to the north, in the territory of the hostile clans, and their scouts and warriors are entitled by clan-law to defend their land. Yet you must not shed any blood of these Hillmen while obtaining the stone, or the stone will be tainted with blood-debt.
'So I must ask you to journey north to the Cairn, and yet you must not kill any of our enemies, no matter if they attack you or not! You will find the Cairn atop a high hill west of the north road, and at night the path up the hill is lit by torches.'
'Well done. Now it is time for you to fight once more.'
'You must obtain a stone from the Cairn of Honour.'
Obtain a stone from the Cairn of Honour
Bring the Cairn-stone to Arzhur
Avoid killing hillmen
The Cairn of Honour
Another challenge was sent to Arzhur's clan. Before the challenge can be accepted, another token of honour must be brought forth.

The Cairn of Honour is in the centre of Fasach-Falroid to the north of Aughaire. It is atop a high hill, west of the north road, and at night the path to it is lit by torches.
Arzhur has asked you to obtain a stone from the Cairn of Honour. You must not spill any blood of the Hillmen who patrol the area.

Arzhur is back at Aughaire.
You should bring the stone you recovered to Arzhur and prepare for the next challenge.

'Alas your victories have not come without cost. Walraig, Chief of the clan of our enemies, has lost all reason after your defeat of his champions, and he has declared a blood-feud against us! This may make him an outcast if he is not successful in his feud, but if he is not stopped, he will lead the full force of his clan against us here in Aughaire.
'Our one hope is to stop this feud before it begins. If we raid his camp in Tór Gailvin to the north-east, not far from Fail-á-Khro, and defeat Chief Walraig in person, we will have obeyed the law, and our enemies will be unable to proceed against us.
'But our Chief, Crannog, refuses to lead such a raid without Golodir's presence to guide him! I must ask you to do what we cannot and defeat Chief Walraig before we ourselves are overwhelmed.'

'You have done a noble deed for us, Southron. Something we should have done for ourselves. Are we doomed forever to wait for others to lead us?
'Well, no matter. We are in your debt. You will always find a warm welcome in our tents.'
The Final Challenge
Enraged by their repeated defeats in duels, Chief Walraig of the hostile Hillmen has declared a feud against the men of Aughaire.
'Please! You must defeat Chief Walraig!'
'We are still in your debt, Outlander.'
'You have shown great honour, friend ${PLAYER}.'

Chief Walraig is with his kin in Tór Gailvin, a camp north-east of Aughaire.
Lore-singer Arzhur has asked you to raid the Hillman fort to the north-east. If you can defeat Chief Walraig, you may be able to forestall a war between the clans.

Arzhur is in Aughaire, south-west of Chief Walraig's camp.
You should return to Arzhur with news of your victory over Chief Walraig.
You are victorious

'Now we must take the egg you found to Aidan, our clan champion, who awaits it at Fail-á-Khro north-east of Aughaire.
'I am afraid we must ask you for another boon, friend from the south. Aidan is a strong fighter, but he is the last such of whom our clan can boast. We have many bold hunters, skilful hearth-keepers, and perhaps even a few wise lore-singers, but of warriors we have few; our foes have been biting away at our strength like dogs worrying a bone.
'The challenge Aidan must face is not a single combat. I ask that you fight by his side, for the honour of our clan, no less than for its survival.'
'You have done well, Southron. But the rival clans have more trouble for us.'
'Now it is time to fight. Let us see who comes against us!'

'Good. I thought no one would come with that egg. But you are to fight at my side? I do not know....
'Well, needs must. I hope you are stronger than you look, Southron!'
'Why do you come to this place, Southron?'

Lore-singer Arzhur has asked you to take the drake's egg to Aidan and then to fight by his side against the challengers from the clans loyal to Angmar.

'You fought bravely in Clúcath, ${PLAYER}, but the Trév Duvárdain will not stop harrying us. We should have expected it: they will not obey the ancient rites, and their Angmarim masters push them still against us.
'With many battles ahead, we need to be ready to care for our wounded. I can make a poultice that will be of great aid to the healers in the Búth Sánkhas and the Búth Luikh. Pick the following herbs from the surrounding hills, and in the lands around the city of Donnvail, to the north: red lovage by the farms of Donnvail, spiky mugwort near the lakes to the south-west, and silverbell by the fortress of Tór Gailvin, to the east.
'Not all battles are fought with weapons, friend ${RACE}; some are won by the healing arts.'
'These herbs will do very well, ${PLAYER}. I can make a healing poultice from this with little difficulty.'
'I hope you can find the herbs we need. They grow on the hillsides around Fail-á-Khro and by the city of Donnvail, to the north.'

A Poultice for Our Hurts
The Trév Gállorg gather herbs from the low-lands with which they treat wounds and season their food.

'You will find the herbs I require growing on the hillsides near Fail-á-Khro and by the city of Donnvail, to the north: red lovage by the farms of Donnvail, silverbell by the fortress of Tór Gailvin, and spiky mugwort near the ponds to the south-west.'

Spiky mugwort, silverbell, and red lovage can be found in the lands around Fail-á-Khro and the northern city of Donnvail: spiky mugwort near the ponds south-west of Fail-á-Khro; red lovage by the farms outside Donnvail; and silverbell by the fortress of Tór Gailvin, to the east.
Cána has asked you to gather some herbs so she can make a poultice to heal the hurts of those injured in the battles sure to come.

Cána is at Fail-á-Khro, north of Aughaire along the road.
Cána has asked you to bring her the herbs she needs to make a healing poultice for her people.
You are victorious

'Once again it is time to fight for the honour of my clan. You have proven yourself worthy, Southron, but now the rules have changed.
'This time, the two brothers Donnan and Mungan claim to have been slighted by our clan. They lie, but the Judge has permitted both of them to fight us at once. Be wary of the younger brother, Donnan, for he is the fiercer of the two. You can find them here in Aughaire, on the west side of the town, waiting for you to answer their challenge.'
'Again, you have triumphed, Southron, this time against unfair odds. But I fear that despite your victory, matters will soon grow more desperate.'
'Who are you to fight for this clan of weaklings? Well, it matters not, we will crush you, and then the Iron Crown will take Aughaire!'
Accept Donnan's challenge

'Hail, fellow adventurer! I can't tell you how good it is to see a stranger who's real flesh and blood, and not of the Orc-made kind.
'You have found us a humble band of adventurers stranded here in a dark place. We came for treasure, and to fight through the fabled paths of Fornost, but found ourselves overwhelmed by the dead right quick.
'Now we're only trying to survive. We haven't been the same since we set foot in that evil place....'
Defeat shades and dreadmists (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Return to Maedhrusc
'I can't believe you drove off all those shades, ${PLAYER}. Is it really true? You have given us hope.'
Fornost: Putting Down the Dead
Maedhrusc ventured briefly into Fornost and saw that it was overrun with the dead.

Shades can be found within the heart of Fornost.

Defeated Uthagan

'Donnvail is draped in the shadow of fear, ${PLAYER}, and the Trév Gállorg here are tormented. We keep our heads down and try not to draw attention to ourselves.
'The lords of Carn Dûm have sent cruel taskmasters to this city to stop any chance of rebellion before it begins: Fûshath the Beast, a terrible Gorthorog; Muiráthakh, the Silent Judge, doom-sayer and executioner; and Gillë Andras, the Lord of the Western Marches, cruel leader of the armies that tread upon Fasach-falroid.
'I will say no more. Seek out Garvan, further within the city. He will tell you more, if he is as fool-hardy as I, and I pray that you tell no one that I gave you his name.'

'I am sorry, you must have me mistaken for someone else. I am just going about my business.
'Find Morven, further into the city. I cannot be seen talking to you, but she might be willing to hear you out!'

'You speak boldly for a stranger newly-arrived in Donnvail. Do you not fear Muiráthakh or Fûshath the Beast?
'Uthagan, further into the city, may be able to help you, but speak with him cautiously; his family was recently \qinvited\q to a dinner at the house of Muiráthakh, and I have not seen them since. I do not know if any have.
'We must organize if we are to strike a blow against our Angmarim masters. Uthagan may be able to guide you.'

'You have followed a long road to me, ${PLAYER}, and I pray that it was not too painful. Donnvail has not been a peaceful city since the lords of Carn Dûm sent their minions here.
'We few that stand against the shadow welcome your aid. This neighbourhood will be the heart of the struggle. Call allies if you have them and if they are willing to stand with you! The foes you will soon face cannot be defeated by one alone; it will take many hearts to overthrow the masters of this city.'

'You speak to me of rebellion? Tell that to my family, taken by Muiráthakh on the charge that they were planning an uprising! That dog knows it was I who aided Una in that, but he took my family instead, as a warning to me!
'There was a time when I would have aided you, but Una will have to fight her battles alone!
'I will kill you myself and teach you something of despair!'
Talk to Uthagan
The Light of Hope
Búdan sent you to the city of Donnvail to speak with the Trév Gállorg there who might rise up against the Angmarim.

'I have nothing more to say to you, and I will repeat no names; there are too many unfriendly ears within this city.
'Perhaps you wrote down what I said to you? Consult your journal and draw no more attention to me!'

'I weep for Uthagan. Look for Una somewhere deep within Donnvail, and may his family not have suffered in vain.
'You must go now. The guards will become suspicious.'
'You will find Morven further in the city. Now leave me be!'

'Poor Uthagan. Would any of us been able to withstand the torment he must have suffered?
'Yet he aids us, even still: look for Una deep within Donnvail.'
'Uthagan is further within the city, and he may be able to help you.'

'That is as I feared. That Uthagan's family should suffer for his deeds is very much in keeping with what we know of Muiráthakh.
'Look for Una deep within Donnvail, and may Uthagan's mind be eased by our eventual triumph.'

Garvan is in the city of Donnvail, north-east of Fail-á-Khro.
Búdan told you of the three leaders sent to Donnvail by Carn Dûm: Fûshath the Beast, Muiráthakh the Silent Judge, and Gillë Andras the Lord of the Western Marches. He also told you to speak to a Man named Garvan further within the city of Donnvail.

Morven is within the city of Donnvail, north-east of Fail-á-Khro.
Garvan gave you the name of someone who might be sympathetic to the cause, telling you to seek Morven further into the city.

Uthagan is in the city of Donnvail, north-east of Fail-á-Khro.
Morven has told you to speak with Uthagan, but with caution: his family was recently taken by Muiráthakh, and she does not think they have been seen since.

Uthagan spoke of Una, located somewhere within the city of Donnvail, north-east of Fail-á-Khro.
Though he sought to slay you, Uthagan unwittingly gave you the name of someone you might speak to: a woman named Una.

'Your courage and grace give us hope, ${PLAYER}. But as I told you, the threat is not yet vanquished.
'You must go to Carn Dûm, though you should speak with Glyn on the way. He is in a small look-out camp past the Gates of Carn Dûm.
'Speak with him quickly. We must attack before the merrevail return.'

'Your deeds precede you, friend, but I will speak plainly. The merrevail follow a queen, a most powerful creature called Azgoth.
'She is a terror most foul, with many minions at her beck and call. Azgoth nests within Carn Dûm, the great city of Angmar that lies to the west.
'It will not be an easy journey, and the city is well protected. Return to me when you have slain the mighty Azgoth.'

'You claim that Azgoth is no more, but how can this be? You are but one and succeeded where we could not!
'Ah, but I can see her black blood upon you and the fire in your eyes. Yes, you speak the truth. This is a great day, a day of celebration where we stood as one against the Enemy.'
Queen of the Host
Though you defeated the merrevail and the bats that plagued the Rangers of Gath Forthnír, Thoriel spoke of taking the fight to Carn Dûm and to the queen of the merrevail herself.

'You must defeat Azgoth, or she will lead her minions against us... and our numbers are dwindling daily.
'You must travel to Carn Dûm and find a way inside.'
'Seek Glyn upon the eastern path to Carn Dûm... he may know more about the evils that plague Angmar.'
'Azgoth is the terrible Queen of the Winged Host... do as Glyn instructed and defeat her!'
'Azgoth is no more? Glyn will wish to know of this.'
'An incredible tale will be told of you some day soon.'
'You have gone into the city of the Enemy and come out again, not only alive, but victorious!'

Glyn is at a small camp on the eastern path to Carn Dûm.
Thoriel has sent you to Carn Dûm to deal with the queen of the merrevail, though she asked you to speak with Glyn on your way there.

Azgoth dwells within Carn Dûm, the city of Angmar that lies to the west.
Glyn told you of the morroval-queen, a creature called Azgoth, that must be slain.

Glyn is in Tármunn Súrsa, to the east of Carn Dûm, near the Gates of Carn Dûm.
You braved the city of Carn Dûm and defeated Azgoth. Glyn will want to hear of your feat.
Defeated merrevail in Himbar (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeated bats in Himbar (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'These are dark days, ${CLASS}. The morroval scourge preys upon my men, snatching them from where they sleep and carrying them off to their dens.
'You will find the merrevail stalking the lands of Himbar to the west. They are the eyes of Angmar, watching our movements and preying upon us. Slay them now, lest they return to Gath Forthnír.
'Beware the spies of the merrevail, their kindred, the bats.'

'You alone accomplished what we could not, ${PLAYER}. We are so few in number, and without Golodir to guide us, we feared the worst.
'I can only hope you possess the spirit to face an even greater threat. There must be one that leads these Merrevail to our doorsteps.'
Defeat merrevail in Himbar (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeat bats in Himbar (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
The Winged Host
Himbar is haunted by the merrevail and their kindred, the bats. These creatures prey upon the Rangers of Gath Forthnír, showing no mercy.
'If you desire to assist us in our plight, journey west and defeat the winged servants of the Enemy.'
'Well done. There is still much to be done concerning the Merrevail, however!'
'You are making a name for yourself among my people, ${PLAYER}!'

The merrevail and the bats hunt throughout Himbar, the lands west of Gath Forthnír.
Thoriel warned you of the merrevail, winged monsters in service to the Enemy. They prey upon the Rangers and must be destroyed, along with their lesser kindred, the bats.

Thoriel waits for you in Gath Forthnír, the hidden Ranger camp east of Himbar.
You defeated the winged servants of the Enemy and may now return to claim victory.

'You are deserving of equipment that reflects the good you do for the people of Middle-earth, ${PLAYER}, the better with which to serve them. It would be my privilege to help you fashion it, but I must give to you this cautionary word: these articles will not be easily come by, for their tale must be one of danger and of hardship. Only through these perils will they have strength enough.
'Speak with me when you are ready to begin, and I will tell you what must be done to fashion equipment befitting a true champion.'

'I would like to take a moment to congratulate you on your achievements, ${PLAYER}. You have accomplished many brave deeds, and I marvel at your dedication! You are a mighty champion!
'A company of dwarves visited Imladris not long ago, and a number of champions travelled with them. They are now staying at an outpost in the Misty Mountains north of the vale. One of them might be able to advise you, for you have exceeded the teaching that I can provide. I salute you for that, friend champion!
'What was the name, again? Gimli, I think it was. Look for him in one of the guest rooms of Elrond's House.'

'You flatter me, ${PLAYER}! There are some would say I am a champion among dwarves, but certainly I would not do so, not so boldly! Ha ha ha!
'The trick to combat, my friend, is to give it everything you've got. There are no half-measures, not in battle and not ever! If you swing your axe as though every swing were its last, you'll be a real force!
'I understand that you're a mighty champion yourself, ${PLAYER}, and I applaud you! You'll do fine in the times that lie ahead, I'm sure of it. Until we meet again!'

'${PLAYER}! How goes the fighting?'

'I can make you a piece of equipment that will be a worthy addition to your raiment, ${PLAYER}, but I will need a number of components with which to fashion it.
'Many of these items will be difficult to come by, but you are a champion! I do not doubt your courage or your dedication and am sure that you will emerge from this task victorious.
'The first items I need you to collect are the hide of the vile worm Raillug, who may be found in the north-eastern corner of the Misty Mountains, and the brimstone-tinged boots of the Tarkrîp goblins which dwell among the Orc-camps of Malenhad in Angmar.'

'I am glad you have returned, ${PLAYER}, for it means that you have successfully dispatched Raillug. I see too that you bring the Tarkrîp-boots I need.
'While I make use of these items, you should set out to collect the next set of components. I will need mandibles from spiders such as those found in Angmar and other dangerous places. I will also need bubbling droplets from the brimstone-leeches which creep through the swamp of Malenhad in Angmar.'
'You do not have the components for which I asked, ${PLAYER}.'

'You do not have the components I need, ${PLAYER}?'

'You do not have the components for which I asked, ${PLAYER}.'

'I can make you a weapon that you will bear with pride, ${PLAYER}, for those that behold it will know you to be a mighty champion. Mightier still are deeds done with honour, and you have performed many!
'But proceed with caution, ${PLAYER}. The components I will need for this weapon will not be easy to come by.
'First, I need you to gather swords from the Ongbúrz Orcs of Fasach-falroid in Angmar, then travel east to Malenhad and obtain the hand-axe of the goblin Tramug.'

'I am pleased to see you have returned, ${PLAYER}, and that you bring with you some of the swords of the Ongbúrz. They will no longer add notches to these for each of our friends they slay.
'I rejoice too that you have deprived Tramug of his hand-axe! His tale ends with you, it seems!
'Go now and bring me claws from the Wargs who stalk through eastern Angmar and other dangerous places, like Eregion and the Misty Mountains. I also need the barbed barghest-tails from those creatures which haunt Imlad Balchorth.'
'Where are the components I requested, ${PLAYER}?'

'I am glad to see you again, ${PLAYER}. These components will greatly improve the weapon I am making for you.
'Seek out the vile drake Lhugrien and obtain from her a flawless scale. Also acquire for me a Sigil of War from the evil Gruglok. Both may be found at Urugarth.'
'You do not have the components for which I asked, ${PLAYER}.'

'You return victorious, ${PLAYER}! I bow to your skill, for I know Lhugrien and Gruglok to be fearsome opponents!
'You are a most worthy champion, my friend, and it is an honour to know you. I give to you this weapon with my earnest hope that it will serve you long and well!'
'You do not have the components I need, ${PLAYER}?'

'Welcome, ${PLAYER}. I heard of your victories in Bree-land and rejoiced in particular that you slew Morley the Fierce. A truer name for him would be \qMorley the False!\q He had long been a foe of my family, and I am glad that you put an end to his villainy.
'It is with confidence that I then ask for your help, ${PLAYER}, for I know you to be a true champion. A band of Orcs have come to the ruins of Ost Cyrn, not far from here, and I know that together we can drive them out. These lands may be wilderness, but every yard of land we allow the Orcs to take brings them one yard closer to Bree-town, and the lands of good folk!
'The leader of these Orcs has the vile name Mosal-ruk, and he, like others of his kind, will not resist a challenge issued from a true champion. Let us journey together to Ost Cyrn, ${PLAYER}, defeat Mosal-ruk's war-band, and put an end to his designs on the Lone-lands!'

'Your victories over Morley, Zhurpukh, and Fair Sherman were not accidental, ${PLAYER} -- you are a mighty champion indeed, and you have proved it sevenfold this day! The defeat of Mosal-ruk is already being spoken of by the minstrels I have seen, and that tale is sure to grow in the telling!'

'We are victorious, ${PLAYER}, true champions of the Lone-lands! Mosal-ruk will no more threaten the folk who try to make their living in these hard lands, and we have sent a message to his masters this day -- we will stand against you, no matter the odds!
'Tell me when you are ready, and we will journey back to Ost Guruth with this happy news!'

'What we accomplished today is a thing of which legends are made -- \qThe Song of Slade and ${PLAYER} at Ost Cyrn,\q if you like!
'Are you ready to return to Ost Guruth? Perhaps I'll find a minstrel to whom I can relate this tale!'

'Ost Cyrn lies ahead, ${PLAYER}, and if we are true of heart and strong of arm, the Orcs within will not remain there by this time tomorrow!
'Let us take a circuitous route into the ruins and slay as many Orcs as lie within our path. Mosal-ruk will test our courage even by himself, and the fewer of his band that remain when we face him, the more confident I will be of our victory!'
'Let us continue, ${PLAYER} -- the deadliest leg of our journey lies ahead, for Mosal-ruk has surely learned of our coming by now. We will show him he and his kind are not welcome in these lands!'

'I will recognize you as a champion only if you can slay three of the evils that threaten this town of Men. I give you their names and their favourite haunts and ask only that you end them and return to me!
'With the use of these notes, a real champion would be able to bring safety to these lands and inspire the people with word of his deeds.'

'News of your battles come before you, ${PLAYER}, for the whole town speaks of them!
'Zhurpukh of the Deeps will no more sneak from the marshes in search of open windows and unlatched doors! Fair Sherman? More lovely in death, they say! And of Morley the Fierce, the people say only this -- that he was not fierce enough to best ${PLAYER}, a worthy champion indeed!
'The people in this town of Men speak the truth, friend champion. I will give you some measure of instruction in the fighting arts, the better to improve the strikes you make at your enemies!'

'Master Elrond sent a scout into the Misty Mountains to watch the activities of the giants. At present, Gwaemithrin is encamped at the small outpost our dwarf-visitors have established north of Imladris.
'Bring Gwaemithrin word of your adventures in Arifael's vale and of the hostile giants there. She may have learned something more about them, though you would think she would have already reported this to Master Elrond if she had.
'Glóin's camp is north and east of Rivendell. Farewell, ${PLAYER}, and go with haste.'

'Ringhul sends word from Arifael of his kinsmen? I cannot say that I am surprised. I had attempted to journey to their halls in the south and east, but I was driven back.
'The journey is treacherous, and I do not recommend attempting it now, but if you should find yourself travelling that way in the future, the Elves of Rivendell would welcome any news you could bring back.
'When the time comes, try to make for the Giants' Table, a place of parley in elder days...and do not travel alone.'
