A Threat from Spiders
Cal Sprigley's farm has been overrun by spiders. The farmer and his wife fled to Archet, leaving their belongings behind.
'Sprigley and his wife fled to Archet with what little he could carry from his farm. The spiders must have come upon them suddenly.'
'I am sure you will be of great help to Sprigley. Spiders are no friends of Men and must be dealt with severely if they are to be dealt with at all.'
'You should bring Sprigley his belongings at once. Such possessions are nearly as important to a farmer as my axe is to me.'
'My farm is to the south of Bronwe's Folly, down the second eastward trail from the south road. The place is much changed now -- a wretched nest of spiders.'

'The spiders came up from the cellar in the night, and we had barely enough time to escape! Many of the farmhands weren't so lucky. We saw poor Henry trying to fight off the spiders in the side yard with Cal's bow.
'If you can recover that bow, our seed bag from the livestock pens, and my strongbox near the storage shed, we'll be mighty grateful.'
'I hope you can drive those horrible spiders off our land for good! We're decent, law-abiding folk and shouldn't have to put up with such troubles!'
'I can't thank you enough for bringing me my goods.'
'At least the spiders won't have the satisfaction of ruining my father's bow.'
'One day, we'll take that farm back from the spiders.'

'Them spiders have et my workhands and driven me and Holly out of our home. There's got to be some way to get 'em off our land!
'I would think that Atli Spider-bane might know more about spiders than I do. Perhaps you should go speak with him again.

You search Bali's corpse and find a journal with several pages missing. The journal text reads:
'I would not believe it, but the spiders have pushed the cave mouth clear! I have entered the cave, and the spiders reacted to me instantly, as if drawn to me. I am unsure why. I spent my day carefully searching near the entrance only and found several corpses bound into cocoons. These spiders seem to wrap everything up into their cocoons! I will write more tomorrow when I go further into the cave.'
Perhaps it would be best to enter the cave to see if you can find the rest of the journal pages before returning to Atli.

'Good, you have returned! It seems there is much more going on here than I first thought. While you were away, my cousin Bali arrived, and I sent him to search some caves in the ruins outside the east wall of Archet. A few of the hunters had dropped a huge stone in front of the cave, and I wanted him to ensure the stone remained. He has not yet returned, and I am worried.
'Now, from what you told me of Sprigley's troubles, the spiders came up through the cellar in his shed. Perhaps seeing the cave blocked off, they tunnelled up through there.
'We won't know for certain, though, until you find Bali. Hopefully he'll have some answers.'

'I cannot believe it. Bali... gone. He must be avenged! And this journal tells me what is behind this: a spider-queen from the Blue Mountains. She and her brood must have followed me from Thorin's Halls.
'Know this! Even if I am slain, she will never leave this place... she has found easy prey here. We must destroy her, or Archet shall become a new abode for the queen and her spawn.'
'Have you found the missing pages of Bali's journal?'

'\qMany seeds did the Dread-weaver sow throughout our mountains....\q

'Arinora has no choice but to see to it. Your first blankets are good enough for those used to the harder life, but their betters need something better, according to Anlaf.
'So I figure I can help her while I work to frighten off these goblins! When you are killing lynx in Nain Enidh, north of here and east of Weathertop, tear off their hides! Their fur is soft and well-kept. Bring it to me, and I will make these blankets and get them back to Arinora.'

'There are too many travellers, even through this remote land, and the nearest water sits foul and stagnant. We've the well, of course, but water is rationed among all the guests and does not go as far as it might.
'Blankets need making and mending, and there are no better hides to be found than those of the wolves. The hide of a Warg is too coarse, but a wolf's fur can be made soft with a comb. If you've the time and a good heart, I would ask for your assistance; you'll not see me stomping through the brush to get to the wolves, as deadly as they are!
'There are a few places you may want to look for wolves with proper hides. Wolves creep among the ruins of Minas Eriol to the south, though that place is also crawling with Wargs and goblins. Wolves hunt too among the Weather Hills, to the east and north. Finally, you could travel even further north, but the Midgewater Pass is dangerous and full of even worse things than wolves. When you have the wolf-hides, return to me, and I'll see that you are rewarded.'

'These are fine furs indeed! I'll cure these and sew a nice batch of new blankets for the guests.
'I'll thank you for your time with a bit of coin from my purse.'

'Ever since Gadaric Munce showed up, I've had no rest! Normally, we see no guests for months on end, but the glut of guests here has me stretched to my limit!

'Is that awful smell coming from these feathers? Oh my, I had never thought that those terrible, little birds could give off such a stench!

'Please go and explore the cave, perhaps you can find Bethad within. I fear that it would be most unwise to explore this cave alone, so you should go with what allies you can gather.'
'You are a friend of Fonn? It is well that you have found me, for I need your help!'

Ancient Lair
Fonn has learned that Gertheryg have been seen travelling to a particular cave in Malenhad. He has sent a scout to investigate, but the scout has not returned.
'I fear that something has become of Bethad in that Gorthorog-cave. I would ask that you go there and search for him.'

'I am glad you are here. I was wounded by one of these cursed worms and have been forced to hide in the dark corners of this cave for some days. But now that my wound is almost healed, I have learned much by spying on the comings and goings of the Gertheryg.
'This cave is inhabited by an ancient Gorthorog called Ulkrank. He is an old one...the oldest such creature I have ever seen. The other brutes seem to treat him with the greatest reverence. He may perhaps be their ruler.
'For my own part, I am ready to leave this place, but if you would, I think you can do more here. Slay as many of these vile worms as you can, and fight your way to the depths of the cave where Ulkrank dwells. Once he is defeated, tell my friend Fonn in Tyrn Lhuig of your victory. He will surely be concerned about me.'

'You bring good tidings! I am very pleased to hear that Bethad is safe, for I had been cursing myself for sending him alone into such danger.
'But it is also a great deed that you have done, too, my friend. The Gertheryg are some of the most terrible fighters for the Iron Crown, and if they can be dismayed or disheartened even a little by the death of their elder, then the Enemy will be sorely weakened as a result. You have truly won a great victory!'

'I made a special draught for them, though. It'll make them sluggish and unruly -- maybe unruly enough to fight amongst themselves! And if not... well, it'll have other effects that just might make them change their minds about staying here.
'Take these draughts and pour them into the barrels located in the goblins' camps to the north-east of the inn at Weatherfoot, at the base of Weathertop. Return to me when the deed is done.'

'The goblins didn't seem to show any ill effects from the draught? Well, I guess I shouldn't really be surprised. Goblins eat anything and everything!

'The draught didn't work, did it? Confound it all! Goblins must have iron stomachs.'

'The folk at The Forsaken Inn are not the wealthiest sort here, friend. We barely make our lives comfortable, and the goblins overrunning the eastward stretch of road have turned the inn into a lonelier place than ever. If you've time to offer, there's work to be done!
'Our fortune is about to change, though -- I've devised a way to make the road safe! Kill the creature at the top, and the rest will turn aside!
'I need some help making this work. If you're willing, head north or north-east into the brush and get me some lynx-meat. Everyone knows that dog-like things eat cat-like things. Get just enough meat to make a meal for a Warg or two! What's wrong? Lynx are deadly creatures when angry, and their meat will serve my purposes nicely. Don't you want to end the threat of goblins and Wargs? Then get out there and hunt some lynx! No excuses! We'll be killing two lynx or Wargs with one stone! Ha ha ha!'

'This one is a bit tough and this one a bit tender. Hmm... no matter, they'll all go into the grinder nonetheless! A pinch of sickle-fly eyes, a dollop of gooey crawler-flesh. Really tasty things, crawlers.
'This will take me a while, I'm afraid.'

'Get out there and get that lynx-meat. I can't make something that the Wargs will eat without the proper supplies. Without the food, the Wargs will keep attacking travellers. Without travellers, the inn is barren, and I make no money to send back to my Gammer! So hurry, you fool! It'll be lynx, and lynx, and boars... and that will mean fewer goblins and fewer Wargs!'

A Fitting Meal
Passage through the Lone-lands has become difficult with the arrival of goblins. Worse still are their pets, the fearsome Wargs who roam the plains and attack unwary travellers.
'I have a plan to get rid of the goblins and the Wargs!'
'Boars! Boars! Boars! Always with the boars!'

Lynx can be found throughout Nain Enidh -- the central Lone-lands -- north and north-east of the encampment at the east edge of Minas Eriol.

'It's going to take awhile before the special meal I am preparing will be ready. What should I have you do in the meantime?
'Ah, I have it! Wargs are mean-tempered sorts of beast, and they're smarter than your everyday wolf... stronger too. That means that they can get angry, and if they can get angry, they can make mistakes!
'The logic of that all works out, I'm sure of it! Now, you listen well: go east! Go to the far side of Nain Enidh and search the wilderlands off the road near Ost Cyrn for Wargs; defeat all those you find! Let's get them good and angry, and their leader is sure to come forth, hungry to taste some flesh!'

'So you defeated a good number of Wargs? You've a hand for this, that much is certain!
'I finished my cooking too, I think. Maybe not quite yet, but I'm sure this will draw out their leader, or leaders, and then....
'Then you'll defeat them and make the road safe for travellers, that's what, and we'll have more guests at the inn!'

'Go into Nain Enidh, far to the east, and slay Wargs. Get them nice and angry! We don't want them wandering all over the Great East Road after all. Let's send that message to their leader!'
'I do hate Wargs. I'm glad you've sent the Wargs of Nain Enidh my message!'
'We'll soon have more travellers at the inn, I'm sure of it!'

'Once Master Deluros hears I was correct in my belief that pieces of pottery and other relics could become entangled in the root-like legs of the snow lurkers of the Misty Mountains, he is certain to give me more interesting assignments!
'Bring these relic fragments to him, ${PLAYER}, and tell him from whence you retrieved them! Perhaps he will send you back to me with an invitation to examine the most precious artifacts kept at Imladris. I cannot wait to study them with my own eyes!
'You will find Master Deluros within the library of Lord Elrond's house. He is always to be found there, deep in thought.'

'You retrieved these relic fragments from snow lurkers in the Misty Mountains? That is very interesting, ${PLAYER}, and Glorenglir is to be commended for thinking it possible -- in one blow, the mountain passes are made safer for those who must travel them, and we collect pieces of our history for further study. Worthy accomplishments.
'And yet, I would ask you one question -- did Glorenglir examine these fragments before she sent you to me? I thought not. This has always been her main fault, and it is the reason I refuse to allow her access to the most interesting artifacts kept here.
'Glorenglir is more concerned with boasting of her finds, with celebrating her accomplishments, than with examining the pieces she has uncovered. Until she learns to contemplate and appreciate the history of the pieces, she will never become a true scholar.'
Bring relic fragments to Deluros
Deluros of Rivendell
Glorenglir believed that snow lurkers could be used to unearth fragments of history from the snows of the Misty Mountains, and you have proven her correct.

'Master Deluros is a scholar and jeweller of great skill. Look for him in the library of Master Elrond's House and show him the relic fragments you retrieved from the snow lurkers.
'I eagerly await what he has to say!'
'I cannot wait to hear that Master Deluros will allow me to see the truly interesting artifacts!'
'Thank you for your assistance, ${PLAYER}! It will only be a little while until I am a master scholar!'
'A true scholar takes her time to appreciate the beauty and history of an item.'
'You cannot hurry understanding. Sometimes it never comes at all.'

The scholar Deluros is within the library of the House of Elrond in Rivendell.
Glorenglir has asked you to bring the relic fragments you recovered from the snow lurkers of the Misty Mountains to Deluros with the hope that he will recognize her readiness to advance as a scholar.

'Glorenglir has not understood the significance of these fragments, ${PLAYER}, but I do. These are shards from what must once have been a beautiful vase, crafted long ago by some lord of the Eldar.
'If you can retrieve more fragments of this vase, it might be possible to reassemble it. Its former glory might have been lost to carelessness or necessity, but history leaves us with one certainty -- though broken, something once fair can be made beautiful again through care and good will.
'Return to the source of the Bruinen and search the drifts there for more fragments. The remaining pieces are sure to be most jagged. Whether you dig them out of the drifts yourself or rely on Glorenglir's snow-lurkers, I leave to you. Be warned, however, that the chance of finding the remaining fragments will likely be quite low.'

'While you were away, ${PLAYER}, I was able to partially reassemble the vase. It is a thing of beauty, even incomplete! I wonder at its maker, and the circumstances that brought it to lie abandoned in pieces beneath the snow of the mountains.
'I see you have brought some jagged fragments back with you! I will see if any of them belong to this vase.'
Bring jagged relic fragments to Deluros
The Missing Fragments
The fragments you retrieved from the snow-lurkers of the Misty Mountains are of interest to the scholar Deluros, though Glorenglir missed their significance.

'If you can retrieve jagged relic fragments from the same area to which Glorenglir sent you, I may be able to reassemble this ancient vase.
'You may find these jagged fragments on snow-lurkers, as you did before, but I do not have as much confidence in this as Glorenglir does. Rather, I would have you search the snowdrifts near the source of the Bruinen, north of Rivendell in the Misty Mountains, to find these fragments.'

Snow-lurkers can be found near the source of the Bruinen and drifts of snow in the area may also hold the jagged relic fragments sought by Deluros.
Scholar Deluros has asked you to collect jagged relic fragments from near the source of the Bruinen so he may reassemble the vase so readily dismissed by Glorenglir.

Scholar Deluros is in the library of the House of Elrond in Rivendell.

You set the vase on the display table

'We have been very fortunate, ${PLAYER}, for some of those fragments were indeed once part of this vase. I have repaired it as best I can, and the beauty it once had has returned in some measure!
'I have another task for you, ${PLAYER}. There are tables throughout Rivendell on which pieces of art and history are sometimes placed for contemplation. Bring this vase to a table near Glorenglir. If she recognizes it as being the sum of the fragments you earlier uncovered for her, I shall agree to further her instruction as a scholar and give her leave to study some of the more valuable artifacts kept here at Imladris.
'If she does not recognize the vase, she will have received my final lesson. Place the vase on the table, observe her reactions, then return to me, and we will speak further.'

'It does not surprise me that Glorenglir failed to recognize the vase, ${PLAYER}, even though she had some part in restoring it.
'I thank you for your assistance, and I hope the lesson of Glorenglir will stay with you! Be not so eager to advance that you fail to experience the moment, ${PLAYER}, in life and in all things.'
Place reassembled vase on display table

'Glorenglir is in Imladris. Go to her and place the vase I have reassembled on a table by her location. Gauge her reaction to it and return to me.'
'Hello, ${PLAYER}. Any word yet from Master Deluros?'

'That vase has a small measure of beauty, ${PLAYER}. Is it from Lord Elrond's collection?
'Have you forgotten to tell Master Deluros of my inspiration concerning the snow-lurkers, ${PLAYER}? You will find him in the library of the House of Lord Elrond!'
'Relish the moment, ${PLAYER}. Learn from the past, but do not dwell there.'
'The snows of the mountains cover many fascinating relics of the past.'
'I am afraid I have done something wrong. Master Deluros refuses to continue my instruction!'
'I do not understand why Master Deluros will no longer give me lessons.'

'You performed so wonderfully in the acquisition of these relics that I think it only fair that you have the job of delivering them!
'My employer awaits the delivery of these relics -- his name is Ollie Redbrush, and you will find him in the armour and weapons shop east of Bree Town Hall. I have placed all the relics in a sack to make the carrying of them easier.
'If you make this delivery, I am sure that Ollie will give you my payment and send you back to me. Upon your return, I will give you a courier's fair wage.'

'These artifacts are hardly worth a courier's fee. Falster thinks me a fool if he believes I will pay him his full fee for a handful of useless cups and flagons. Trying to make me more accepting of his inadequacies by throwing in a handful of wolf-teeth is maddening!
'Take this. He'll find that it is significantly lighter than he wanted, but it is what he deserves for such a poor collection.
'Make your way quickly, ${RACE}. I want that good-for-nothing trickster to know that Ollie Redbrush is no fool!'
'I have no business to conduct with you, and you're doing nothing more than cluttering the space around my home. Make yourself useful or scarce. It is your choice.'

'Ungrateful! Redbrush has some gall trying to push me around. You made the delivery, but his message to me is that it is not enough. Does he not realize that the fortunes of trade change?
'I'll not forsake you as he has me. Here is your payment. I wish there was more that I could give, but he's made this difficult for me.'
'Didn't Redbrush give you the payment for the goods we brought him?'

'Redbrush will be anxious to see what we've done, and I am anxious to pay you, friend! Look for him in the armour and weapons shop east of Bree Town Hall!'
'Thanks again for your help, ${PLAYER}.'
'I cannot believe that Redbrush paid me so poorly!'
'I'll find some way to get by, with or without Ollie Redbrush!'
'Ollie Redbrush is no fool, I'll tell you that!'
'I am finished dealing with Falster. He is a villain!'

'A vale beneath the ruins of Minas Eriol, south-east of The Forsaken Inn, contains the coins and heirlooms I need, and more! Wolves inhabit the valley, and Ollie may forgive me the delay if I include some pristine wolf-teeth with the shipment.
'If you assist me in collecting these curiosities, I will ensure that you are paid for the favour! Make your way to the valley beneath Minas Eriol and obtain coins, heirlooms, and wolf-teeth for me.'

'Ollie will be pleased with these curiosities, for certain, and the wolf-teeth should help sweeten the deal.

'You have earned this reward, friend, and I hope you find this sufficient. I know that Redbrush will be pleased with this delivery.'
'Head to the valley beneath the ruins of Minas Eriol, south-east of here. I need some coins and heirlooms to send to Ollie Redbrush. A few wolf-teeth wouldn't hurt either.'

'I'll need a goodly number of scabbards, so hunt the goblins of Minas Eriol, to the south or the goblins in the shadow of Weathertop to the north-east. You will find plenty of the creatures there, I reckon.'

'I have need of an adventurer, ${PLAYER}, and it may be that you will serve nicely. My friend Frodo here will soon be leaving on an errand both urgent and secret.
'Hobbits are remarkable creatures, and Frodo is more remarkable than most -- he has stepped forward to accept a charge that would daunt even those counted most brave in all the annals of the world.
'Do not ask me about his task! And do not ask Frodo, either. He may wish to speak of it, but it is better that he not do so. I do ask you this: speak with him and gauge his feelings. 'Would you take a walk with me? The cool air will do me good, and I would very much like to hear about your adventures.'

'Frodo remains as high in my esteem as ever he did, ${PLAYER}, and I thank you for accompanying him. He is made of stern stuff, our Frodo, and his worries are natural. They will give him strength in hard times, rather than bring him to weakness. Frodo will be fine.
'I thank you, ${PLAYER}. May your travels bring you out of danger quickly if they chance to bring you into it!'

'Hello there, friend. I was just thinking of all the things I've got to do and me here on duty.
'I've got my brother's armour to get polished. He'd do it himself, if he had a mind to, but I'm afraid Kalli does not have our family's sense of duty. He'll never earn his commander's respect; always being late, never diligent in his duties, always wearing his old, worn armour and filthy uniform.
'Perhaps you could be of some service to an old warrior. Could you bring this armour up to Brúni Stonehelm and have him polish it for me? Brúni's stands among the armour merchants of Thorin's Hall, where the canal runs through the mountain.'

'Brúni's got someone else to do his errands for him again, eh? Very well, here's my other armour. You might want to check with Olafr, too. His armour was torn up bad a few days back in a scuffle with some goblins.'

'I've been waiting for Brúni to come down. We expected him the other day, but as usual, he put us off again! I've got a dent in my armour a hand and a half long. Poxy goblin would have cut me from shoulder to belly if not for that hunk of metal!'

'What's this? I know that armour! That's Halli's, unless I miss my guess. I haven't the time to polish his armour again. I'm far too busy!
'I was supposed to go down to Noglond, the way-station to the south, and pick up the guards' damaged armour. No, I have no time to clean Halli's armour today. You will just have to leave it here, and I will see if I can get to it before next week. Unless... you can go down to Noglond and retrieve the guards' armour for me.'
'I'll never have time to polish Halli's armour if I have to travel to Noglond and back again.'

The dwarf-smith looks up at you. 'Oh yes, here is the armour you wanted shined.'
'That armour's not going to drag itself up through Thrain's Vale! The Watch in Noglond, the way-station, expects that armour to be picked up today.'
'Aye, that's just the thing. Kalli will look sharp as an axe in this. The commander's sure to notice him now!'

You should take the armour you collected to Brúni to be mended.

Halli is in Frerin's Court, south of Thorin's Hall.
Brúni has given you Halli's armour, cleaned and polished, to return to its owner.

'I've got some complaints from Noglond, down in the Vale of Thráin to the south, that the canal hasn't been flowing the way it should. Hopefully that repair you made to the leak has solved that problem, as well.
'Could you go down to Noglond and talk to Geitir about the problem? He can tell you if the canal is back to normal. Just follow the road south as it curves through the Vale of Thráin, and you will eventually come upon Noglond.
'With the Dourhands stirring up trouble, we are so short on workhands.'
'Has the waterflow been restored? I should say not. It's just a trickle, really, when it should be a torrent!'
The Flow to Noglond
Tindr hopes the repairs to the canal in Thorin's Hall has restored the flow of water to Noglond, the way-station in the Vale of Thráin.
'Have you not been to Noglond yet?'

Geitir is in Noglond, south on the road from Thorin's Halls.
Tindr has asked you to speak with Geitir in Noglond to learn if the flow of water in the canal has returned to normal.

'This canal water is used down in Gondamon in the Low-lands as well as here in the Vale of Thráin. You should go down there and make sure they know we removed the blockage up here.
'Travel down the road to the east, then turn south at the first crossing and Gondamon will be right there. You will want to talk to old Otkell.
'Their cisterns must be nearly dry down there, what with the blockage as bad as it was!'
'You restored the waterflow? Why it's not flowing nearly enough at all! You may have cleared out some problems over at Noglond, but there must be something else blocking the flow around here.'
On to Gondamon
With the thickets removed from the canal, the waterflow has been restored to Noglond in the Vale of Thráin.
'Gondamon is easy to find. Just take the road east, then turn south at the first crossing.'

Otkell is in Gondamon, east down the road from Noglond, and south at the first crossing.
Geitir has asked you to inform Otkell in Gondamon about the restoration of the canal.
There are thickets clogging the canal
Thickets cleared away (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'The water has not been flowing down to Noglond for several days. I sent a message back to the Halls, but I've not received a reply from the builders. I'm not about to send one of my boys to do builder's work, and I can't have them trapessing to the river every time we need water.
'Would you look into it? The canal runs all the way down the mountain from Thorin's Halls and to Gondamon below. The problem must be up-river from here.
'The above-ground part of the canal, the place that may be blocked, is south and west of here. Just take the road south to the bridge and look underneath it. Follow the canal all the way up to the big gate if you have to, just find the problem!'

'Done already? Good work! We could use someone like you on the guard... better than these layabouts. Can I interest you in signing up? Oh, the pay's not that good, and you'll find yourself in some cold, out-of-the-way post like this, but it's a living. No? I thought not....
'Ah well, thanks for your work, anyway.'
Discover the source of the canal's waterflow problem
Clear away the thickets clogging the canal (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Quenching a Thirst
According to Geitir, the waterflow from the canal has been staunched for several days, and the builders have not replied to his message requesting assistance.
'Have you found the source of the problem?'
'Aye, it would be a great help if you would clear away the thickets clogging the canal.'

The canal can be found south of Noglond, flowing down from Thorin's Halls.
Geitir asks you to investigate the flow of the canal to Noglond and learn the cause of the problem.

There are thickets blocking the canal between Noglond and Thorin's Halls.
Now that you have discovered the problem in the canal, you should clear away enough of the thickets to allow the water to flow more freely. There may be several patches of thickets along the canal.

Geitir is at Noglond to the north of the canal, south of Thorin's Halls.
You should return to Geitir with news of your success.

'The goblins in these hills are causing us no end of grief. They've blocked off the river with debris and slowed the flow to a trickle, and what water exists is fouled by their presence.
'I can send a crew to remove the debris, but I need someone with a stout heart and a strong sword-arm to clear out some of the goblins. I can't afford to lose any workers, what with the Dourhands to contend with.
'You can find the canal west of here, just past the hills. The goblins have a camp west of their make-shift dam.'
'Is it safe for my work crews? Excellent. I wouldn't send my lads out with all those goblins around. We need all the guards here to protect us from the cursed Dourhands in case they attack.'
Clear the Way
The water supply coming into Gondamon is still interrupted, despite your efforts to clear the canal.
'No luck with the goblins? Well keep at it. My crew can clear away the blockage just as soon as your part is done. The goblin camp is west of here.'

The canal near Gondamon is to the west, past the hills.
Otkell, the Chief Builder of Gondamon, informed you that goblins are responsible for the lack of fresh water. He asked you to go to the area west of the canal and remove the goblin threat.

Otkell is at Gondamon to the east of the canal, beyond the hills.
You should return to Otkell and tell him about the goblins you defeated.
Fissure sealed (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
'Hurry! Take the mortar and make the repairs before the fissures expand. It's only a matter of time before the wall is breached.'
'That's one less task to concern me. Perhaps that will fix the problems with the water supply they've been reporting down at Noglond, the way-station in the Vale.'
Seal the fissure with Tindr's mortar (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
A Patch in Time
A fissure has opened in the great dwarf-canal leading down from Thorin's Hall, threatening to flood the Vale of Thráin.
'The canal is leaking into the tunnels beneath the Hall of Merchants. Hurry and patch the fractures!'

Enter Thorin's Hall to the north, then go west to the Hall of Merchants.
Tindr gave you some mortar with which to repair the cracks in the canal walls.

Tindr is in the courtyard outside Thorin's Hall.
The fissure was sealed. You should return to Tindr with news of your success.
Collected gypsum (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collected sand (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collected stones (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'I am Tindr, Master Builder of Thorin's Hall. The great canal, for which I am responsible, has recently fissured. The crack has not yet become a serious threat, but it is only a matter of time, and I haven't any builders available to assist with its repairs. Could you help me seal the fissure?
'I need to mix a mortar to seal the crack but our stores are barren. I will need stone and gypsum from the new Mirkstone Tunnels and sand from the Rockbelly Pit. The Mirkstone Tunnels are above the great statue of Thorin to the north-west. Fool goblins dug another entrance after we closed off the original with the Arming Cave. The Rockbelly Pit is to the south-east in the Winterheight.
'If we do not seal the crack soon, it may break, flooding the Vale of Thráin below.'

'It will just take me a moment to make the mortar. You learn a few tricks when you've done this as long as I have.
'There we are! Now take this mortar to the fissures in the canal walls in the Hall of Merchants inside the western parts of Thorin's Hall.'
'Where are the materials I asked you to gather?'
Bring the mortar ingredients to Tindr

Collect sand (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collect stones (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

A fissure has opened in the great dwarf-canal leading down from Thorin's Hall, threatening to flood the Vale of Thráin.

Tindr is in the courtyard in front of Thorin's Hall. Sand is in the Rockbelly Pit south-east of Frerin's Court in a place called Winterheight. Gypsum and small stones can be found in the Mirkstone Tunnels above Frerin's Court to the north-west.

'The lynx that roam the hills in the Vale of Thrain have become bold with hunger in recent months. There have even been reports of them attacking unwary travellers! I have the unwelcome task of dealing with these beasts, but there are too many for me to handle alone.
'Grimkell has ordered me to take care of the problem, but I could use your help. We must teach the beasts to fear the bite of metal again and keep to four-legged game.
'Head to the north, along the road back to Thorin's Hall. Look to the west side of the road, near the Thrushstones, and you will find lynx in great numbers.'
'Good work with those vicious cats. Perhaps now lone travellers will have less to fear in this land. Grimkell will be pleased, for a change.'
Defeat lynx in the Vale of Thrain (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Óláfr at Noglond
Herding Cats
Óláfr needs help dealing with the lynx in Thrain's Vale.
'Please help me out by hunting the lynx in the area.'

Lynx can be found throughout the Vale of Thráin, but Óláfr suggested heading north to the Thrushstones.
Óláfr has asked you to secure the safety of the road leading through the Vale of Thráin by hunting the lynx that dwell there.

'The hunters who have been plying the forests north of Gondamon have come to me with stories of being threatened or even attacked by those backstabbing Dourhand brigands.
'If you're of a mind to lend us a hand, you could head out there and deal with the treacherous thin-beards! They need to learn not to meddle with the hunters of Gondamon!
'The Dourhands have built a small camp to the north of here, in the hills somewhere. You will find plenty of heads to break there, I'd warrant.'

'Ah good. That should teach the Dourhands a little lesson. You have done us a fair favour, ${PLAYER}, and helped ensure that Gondamon remains secure over the coming winter months.
'Let me see if I can find some suitable reward for you.'
Defeat Dourhand warriors (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeat sturdy Dourhands (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

Protecting the Hunt
Since the Dourhands were driven out of Thorin's Halls, they have harried the hunters of the Blue Mountain Dwarves.
'You should be able to find those brigands in a camp in the hills to the north. They mostly stay holed up in there like rats in their warren.'
'Ha! You showed those Dourhands what we're made of!'
'Well done, ${PLAYER}! I doubt those Dourhands will trouble our hunters anymore.'

The Dourhand brigands can be found to the north of Gondamon.

'The wind coming down from the mountains makes my bones ache year-round, but even the younger sentries feel the chill when the days grow short.
'We could use more pelts to make blankets and clothing in preparation for the coming winter. There is no shortage of wolves prowling in the wilds, especially to the west. I expect you will have no difficulty obtaining some furs for me.
'Wolves are vile creatures, but at least their fur is warm.'
'The Dwarves of Gondamon will be grateful for these pelts when winter arrives, ${PLAYER}. Thank you.'
'A cold dwarf is a grumpy dwarf, ${PLAYER}. Have you had any luck getting those pelts for us?'
Bring the wolf-pelts to Dorri in Gondamon

'Our huntsmen are skilled, but this year's hunt has proven particularly difficult, what with the cold and the wretched Dourhands. I have found myself short of supplies for the coming winter.
'You can help us by bringing in some bear-meat. There are plenty of bears in the wilds around Gondamon, especially to the north.
'We will preserve and store the meat for the coming months.'
'Thank you for bringing in this bear-meat! I will see that it is properly salted and stored for the winter months.'
'We still have need of that bear meat, ${PLAYER}. You ought to be able to find some in the wilds surrounding Gondamon.'
Bring the bear-meat to Gafí in Gondamon

Gafí, the provisioner of Gondamon, has asked for your help building up their winter stores.

Bears can be found in the wilds around Gondamon, especially to the north.

Collected ancient dwarf-chest

'I see... so you were sent by a dwarf from the Blue Mountains, were you? Perhaps it is the long years alone here, but I believe you. Now, allow me to tell you a tale.
'Long ago, the first Halmur Stoneshaper, son of Vithurr, was charged with guarding the treasures here. He stood sentry day and night, maintaining his post even on days of feasting. Yet he let his guard drop, only once, and a vile dwarf, Hjortur Dourhand, slipped in and stole a single ingot of dwarf-gold. Having failed in his duty, Halmur swore that he and his sons would keep vigil over the remaining gold until that ingot was returned. I am but one in a long line of Halmurs who have kept his oath.
'If you return the stolen ingot, the oath will be fulfilled. The strongbox will then be yours to return to the dwarf who sent you. I cannot say, though, where to find Hjortur, although the legends of Halmur's failure tells that Hjortur is somewhere within Gabilazan. Perhaps there you will be able to find the gold.'

'Ha! You've come from one of those fool Stoneshapers, haven't you? You've heard the tale of their \qoath\q over that strongbox, haven't you? Well, allow me to tell you a tale!
'The first Hjortur Dourhand stole the gold not for his own treasure, but to make Halmur Stoneshaper look the fool! Upon hearing of Halmur's oath, Hjortur swore one of his own: he and his sons would forever keep the ingot and forever keep the Stoneshapers looking the fool!
'I too come from a long line... a long line of Hjortur Dourhands! And I shall keep to the oath! You shall only have the ingot if you can take the strongbox over my dead body. And I don't think that's too likely....'

'My eyes must betray me, you ${RACE}, you trickster. You cannot have the stolen ingot that has kept me and my kin chained to this place for the long years.
'And yet, it is... it is! Can it be so? Has my duty at last been fulfilled?'
'You have not retrieved the stolen ingot, faithless ${RACE}. I maintain my vigil.'

'Good, good! I hope the strongbox wasn't too hard to find! Heikki Goldwatcher is sure to be pleased with this. Those records of his won't have a bad thing to say about me!
'Now, I know you've already done so much, but perhaps there is a bit more I could ask of you?'
'Have you found the other strongbox yet?'
Collect the stolen dwarf-gold ingot
Find Hjortur Dourhand
Search Hjortur's strongbox for the stolen ingot
Bring the stolen dwarf-gold ingot to Halmur Stoneshaper
Bring the ancient dwarf-chest to Larus Sharpshard
The Last Ingot
Halmur Stoneshaper, a descendant of the original Halmur Stoneshaper, son of Vithurr, has been charged with guarding the strongbox you seek until all its contents are returned.

'I know not where you might find the gold Hjortur stole, although the tale of Halmur's failure says Hjortur is within the walls of Gabilazan. Perhaps you will find some clue to the stolen ingot there.'
'You defeated Hjortur, but did not search his strongbox? Return to the spot you defeated him at once and reclaim the stolen ingot from the strongbox he guarded!'
'The chest is yours, friend. My oath is fulfilled. I'm free now. Free to go where I please!'

The stolen ingot might be found within the walls of Gabilazan.
Halmur Stoneshaper suggested you seek the stolen ingot there.

The stolen ingot might be inside Hjortur's strongbox, within the walls of Gabilazan.
You defeated Hjortur Dourhand and should now search the strongbox he guarded for the stolen ingot.

Halmur Stoneshaper is in the tomb of his ancestor on the hill to the left as you approach the dwarf-keep in the pass of Gabilazan from the north.
Halmur Stoneshaper is waiting for you to return with the stolen dwarf-gold ingot you retrieved from the descendant of the thief who stole it long ages ago.

The second strongbox is within the tomb of Halmur Stoneshaper in the pass of Gabilazan. Larus Sharpshard is located in a camp north of High Crag.
After helping Halmur Stoneshaper reclaim the stolen ingot and fulfil his family's oath, he has allowed you to take the strongbox to bring it to Larus Sharpshard.

'How could I have missed this? There was a second page to Heikki's records! It describes a second strongbox, ${PLAYER}! Heikki is not the kind of dwarf you want to cross, because he'll remember it -- he'll write it down in one of his books and never let you forget how you let him down! If I don't get that second strongbox, it wouldn't surprise me if someone found his records four hundred years from now and thought badly of Larus Sharpshard, son of Tralli!
'So we've got to find it, ${PLAYER}. Let me just look at this paper and tell you where it should be. Ah, the dwarf-keep among the High Crags, to the south. It's the keep that guards Gabilazan, and it's full of those good-for-nothing Dourhands.
'You might want to take the farthest west pass into High Crag. Look for a building on a hill to your left as you approach the keep. The strongbox should be just inside, so don't delay!'

'Who dares to enter the tomb of Halmur Stoneshaper, son of Vithurr of old? Not even a Dourhand is foolish enough to enter here! They know the tale of the Stoneshapers and quake in fear! Yet you are different....
'You are here for the strongbox, aren't you, thieving ${RACE}? You've only moments to tell me your tale before I cleave you in twain!'
Collect the second strongbox
The Other Chest
Larus Sharpshard discovered that there was a second strongbox, which remains missing.

'The second strongbox will be inside a building on a hill to your left as you approach the Dourhand keep in the pass of Gabilazan from the north. Journey there and bring back this strongbox, ${PLAYER}!'

Larus Sharpshard believes the second strongbox is inside a building on the hill to your left as you approach the Dourhand-controlled keep in the pass of Gabilazan from the north. Gabilazan is south of the camp that Larus is located.
Larus Sharpshard is very worried that Heikki Goldwatcher will record unflattering things about him if you are not able to recover a second dwarf-strongbox from the Misty Mountains.

'Those despicable goblins must have stolen some of the dwarf-gold ingots from this strongbox, ${PLAYER}! According to the records given me by Heikki Goldwatcher, the strongbox is missing twelve ingots!
'This is unforgiveable! To think that the gold of his ancestors has been pilfered by goblins is more than any dwarf could bear.
'The goblins have camps in the mountains somewhere to the north and east, ${PLAYER}. Find the creatures and slay them until you recover the missing ingots! Look especially on the ridges of Pinnath Fenui, east of the source of the Bruinen, for I have heard that many goblin-fires have been spotted that way.'

'Perfect, ${PLAYER}, perfect! This should do it! Now all of the ingots are accounted for, and Heikki Goldwatcher will be happy to know that we have recovered the treasure mentioned in his records.
'Yes, according to Heikki's records we've got everything... needed....
'Oh no, what's this?'
Bring dwarf-gold ingots to Larus Sharpshard
Every Last Ingot
According to the records Larus Sharpshard was given by Heikki Goldwatcher, the strongbox you recovered is missing some of its contents.
'Those goblins will be made to pay, ${PLAYER}. Look for their camps east of the source of the Bruinen, and recover all of the stolen dwarf-gold ingots from their filthy fingers.'

Goblins carrying dwarf-gold ingots can likely be found on the Pinnath Fenui, the ridges east of the source of the Bruinen, in the Misty Mountains.
Larus Sharpshard is outraged that goblins have pilfered from the strongbox you recovered and has demanded that you retrieve all of the stolen ingots.

Larus Sharpshard is located at a camp north of High Crag.
Larus Sharpshard will be delighted that you have recovered the stolen ingots from the goblins of the Misty Mountains.

There are ruins in the distance to the north-west that may contain treasures of great value.
There are some ruins to the north-west. There may be something of value to be found within them.

'This is the box Heikki Goldwatcher of Thorin's Hall has ordered me to retrieve! It appears to be damaged, and not by the passage of time, I think. These marks might have been caused by goblin-weapons. Perhaps a party of goblins sought to carry the strongbox away and quarrelled among themselves?
'Why then did the victors not take the strongbox, I wonder? Ah, no matter. At least it still remains, ${PLAYER}?
'I'll just open it up and compare the contents with the record that Heikki gave to me before I set out.'

'The Bruinen flows out of the mountains to the north, and an old dwarf-keep can be found overlooking the water. Search the area for signs of the strongbox Heikki Goldwatcher told me about, and I will reward you for your trouble.'
Bring damaged dwarf-chest to Larus Sharpshard
Search the ruins to the north-west for treasure
Search the ruins to the north-west for treasure

An old dwarf strongbox catches your eye. Word is, Larus Sharpshard is looking for a specific treasure and this may be the one he seeks.

'There's but one thing left to do, take the strongboxes to Heikki Goldwatcher in Thorin's Hall.
'I know it's a bit of a trek to go all the way there, but I think it's the proper thing to do. I wish I could do it myself, since it's my reputation that will be besmirched in Heikki's records if he's not happy, but I'm far too busy here to make such a journey.
'You'll find Heikki in Thorin's Hall in the Blue Mountains. Hopefully Heikki won't be too unhappy when you get there!'

'Finally, word from Larus Sharpshard. What, what's this? You've brought the strongboxes? That fool, did he even read my note to him? I wanted the name of Halmur Stoneshaper's father! I will make a note of this in my records!
'Wait, you met Halmur's descendant? Good, good! Did he tell you his father's name? Halmur? Oh, Vithurr was the first Halmur's father! Ah, very good! That is exactly what I wanted to know.
'I suppose I'll add the gold here to the treasury, although it really matters not to me. I honestly did not expect there to be any treasure left, after all these years. No, the name of Halmur Stoneshaper's father is really all I needed. Filling in the gap in the records is the real treasure!'
Bring the strongboxes to Heikki Goldwatcher
Real Treasure
You have recovered both strongboxes for Larus Sharpshard. Now but one task remains.

'The fifth missing gear was placed in a chest hidden in the woods in eastern Haudh Lin, north and east of Kheledûl. However, a brood of vicious spiders have made the place their lair.
'It will be a challenge to find the chest without running afoul of the vile creatures.'
'Wonderful! This is the last of the missing pieces! Everything should fit together now... I hope....'
'Look to the spider lair north and east of Kheledûl for the fifth and final gear.'

'Greetings! I wonder if you could lend me a hand? I have been trying to repair this device, which opens access to the old Vault of the Mountain, but some key pieces, ancient gears, were removed and scattered long ago to prevent the Dourhands getting their grubby hands on the vault treasure.
'Now that we have finally ousted the Dourhands from Thorin's Hall, it is time to open the Vault, but first this device must be repaired. Old Sindri Winchmaster, the artificer who made this, had skill far beyond mine, so I'll need the actual pieces that were lost to have any hope of getting it to work again.
'They say the first missing gear was hidden somewhere in an old cave in the Winterheight, up the path south-east from Thorin's Hall. You will probably find it in a chest somewhere in the cave. There's a trick to the chest, by the way, you have to press in at the corners to open it....'

'Ha! This looks like the gear! It goes here... or maybe here....
'No matter. I will work it out given time, I am sure of it!'
'Please find the gear that is hidden in the abandoned mine west of here. It's in a chest somewhere in the cave. Beware of cave-claws!'

'I'm not sure exactly where you'll find the gear, but I would not be surprised if it was well-guarded, as the Dourhands know very well that it is essential for getting into the Vault.'

'Well done! I'll have this fitted in a moment. Get in there! Fit, blast you! Ow! My thumb!

'Finally! It's working.... I think.
'I'm going to have to stay here to care for this machine. You go open the vault! It's quite a distance away -- on the other side of Thorin's Hall -- here, to the north and up the stairs. The chains and cables run all through the walls -- a real work of art!
'Make sure you get the order of the levers right, or you'll have to come back here so I can reset the gears. Perhaps those clues you found in the boxes will help with the order.'

'This was in the vault? This?
Bávor stares incredulously at the black rock. 'Amazing! Fantastic! Incredible!
'Listen, no one knew just what was sealed in that vault! This is one of the greatest of all the treasures of the dwarves!
'Oh, I know it doesn't look like much, but the story goes that Durin himself hewed this from Gundabad, the mountain where he first awoke! It's the first chunk of ore ever mined by the father of our line! This is the most ancient artifact of the dwarves and serves as a symbol of our heritage. You have unearthed a true treasure with all your hard work, and you deserve all our thanks.'
'Please don't tell me there was nothing in the vault!'

You have safely escorted Lalia out of the Barrow-downs

'I came here to find the \qLast Prince,\q like Mr. Butterbur talks about in his stories. I was going to find him, and then be with him forever and be his princess! But he wasn't here to be found! There's just all these skeletons and bones and walking dead! It isn't nice to go misleading young hobbits like that!
'When you are ready to go, could you help me get back home to Bree? I couldn't leave before, but now with a strong warrior like you here, I'm sure you can get me home safely!
'Oh, and I lost my cloak. I simply must find it, or dad will yell at me something terrible!'

'Oh, that is a relief! It seems I know my daughter well. She actually had gone after that \qLast Prince\q of hers. Well, maybe she's learned her lesson and won't be so foolish in the future. I know I will certainly never come here again.
'I do hope I can survive her tweens. Maybe then she'll get some hobbit-sense. Maybe....'

'Oh, do help my daughter get back to Bree safely! I shall get there in time!
'Thank you for bringing my Lalia home!'
'I do wish Mr. Butterbur wouldn't tell stories like \qThe Last Prince.\q'

You must take Lalia to the North-gate of the Barrow-downs.

You have found Lalia

'I came here to find my missing daughter, Lalia. I'm terribly worried about her. You see, she'd been going on about \qThe Last Prince,\q one of Mr. Butterbur's tales. It's one of his better ones, that's for sure, but I'd say the tale isn't quite the truth of it.
'Lalia has been going on for a long while, I fear she came here to the Barrow-downs in search of this \qprince\q of hers. I came here in search of my daughter, and I am now lost myself.
'In the tale, the Last Prince's barrow is between the Northern Barrow and the Dead Spire, by a large stone. If I could, I would start searching there.'
Find Bob's daughter, Lalia
The Search for Lalia

Bob's daughter, Lalia, has gone missing. Bob fearing she may have gone off in search of the \qLast Prince,\q a character in one of the tales Barliman Butterbur tells to travellers, joined a foray into the Barrow-downs to find his daughter.

'Have you found my girl, Lalia, yet? If she's gone off in search of her \qLast Prince,\q she's probably gone to the barrow Barliman talks about in his tale. His tale says the Prince's barrow could be found near a standing stone, between the Northern Barrow and the Dead Spire.
'If I am afraid of this place -- and I am! -- I am certain that she is terrified!'

According to Butterbur's tale, the Barrow of the Last Prince lies between Northern Barrow and the Dead Spire, near a large standing stone.
Bob has asked you to search the Barrow-downs for his missing daughter, who likely has come here in search of the fabled \qLast Prince.\q

'The Quick Post service will surely live up to its name again if we continue at this rate, ${PLAYER}! There is something you can help me with, and maybe that will...
'Oh, don't start towards the mail satchels just yet! I'm actually on top of the deliveries for today and don't need you to take any of these anywhere. No, what I want you to do is to bring word to Postman Oddfoot in Frogmorton about our efforts to improve the speed at which we deliver the mail. He's been rather depressed lately -- hobbits in Frogmorton are not shy about expressing their complaints, and Oddfoot has always been one to take things rather to heart.
'Frogmorton is east of Bywater. Tell Oddfoot that we're repairing the reputation of the Quick Post service and offer him whatever help you can.'

'Hello there. I'm the postman for Frogmorton. I'm sorry for any inconvenience the Quick Post service may have caused you....
'What's that? You're not here to complain? Oh. Oh, I see. That's nice. Yes, I'm glad we haven't disappointed you today. I get so many complaints, you know. It does get to a hobbit, after a while.
'You say that Postman Cotton is trying to revitalize the Quick Post service and make it what it used to be? Even with all the letters that get sent these days? That's incredible news! If we can recapture our old reputation, maybe we won't need to spend so much time answering complaints!'

'This task, at least, is finished. I have much work to do to help my kindred prepare for the coming war, but my oath to Trestlebridge shall at least be fulfilled.
'I need you, if you are willing, to deliver this armour to Jarred Mason in Trestlebridge. He is a man of some crafting skill himself. I believe he is acting as the armourer for his people.
'I am sure you have crossed through Trestlebridge and know well their plight, but should you have lost your direction, it lies far to the west and south of Esteldín, along the Greenway leading to Bree-land.'

'Jarred is a good man. I have often wanted to tell him of our home here at Esteldín, but our way of life is too dangerous to explain to those who know it not already.
'If this war which rages about us ends and my Lord Aragorn takes his rightful place, perhaps there will be a time when I may tell Jarred my whole tale, but for now, his safety -- and ours -- must hold precedence.
'I have something for you. Your efforts are deserving of a greater gift. I used the remnants of what you brought me to craft you this fine armour.'

'What is this? You say this came from Gondranc? I will admit I had not thought to hear from him again!
'My friend is a wanderer, rarely staying in one place too long, and when he decided to pass north, I could not help but wonder what he hoped to find in the barrens. Then the Orcs came, and I was sure he had perished.
'My people, what few are left here, need it more than ever. If you know where Gondranc is, return to him with my thanks!'

'I fear the worst of my friend Gondranc. He is a traveller versed in the art of leatherwork. He had promised me armour for our guards before the arrival of the Orcs. Now I fear he was slain somewhere in the wilds of the North Downs.'

At the request of the Ranger Gondranc, you went to the camp of the Earth-kin north-east of Esteldín to retrieve a book of leatherworking lore Asikko, the Earth-kin's chieftain, had promised him. With this lore, he has crafted armour for the people of Trestlebridge.
'Make your way west and south to the town of Trestlebridge at the border of the North Downs and Bree-land. Deliver his armour to Jarred Mason.'
'Please, tell Gondranc that he has helped to restore hope to us in this beleaguered time.'
'Our task here has only begun, but thanks to you, ${PLAYER}, we have at least aided Trestlebridge.'
'Asikko's book has given me a much better understanding of leatherwork, ${PLAYER}. Thank you for bringing it.

'I am pleased to know that Gondranc is alive and well...and crafting such fine armour!'

I need this book to fulfil a promise I made to a man in Trestlebridge as I came north from Rivendell in the guise of a common leatherworker. I promised to make for his people armour suitable for use against the Orcs.
'Will you go to Asikko and ask for the book? The Earth-kin are encamped north-east of here. Just skirt the hills northward from the eastern entrance to Esteldín.'

'My people's pride binds us. I do not wish to raise arms against my brethren, but I have been forced to do so. I will fight them when the time comes, though it does not please me. I am also bound by honour, and that honour must be satisfied, even in the face of the First Hunter's betrayal.
'I know only names, not faces. The name I know is Gondranc, a man who knows well the crafting of leather and tanned hides. I promised to share with him the secrets of our art in return for the letters he once taught me.
'I wrote a book for the man before the betrayal, but it is lost now to the Rauta-lehmä in the east. I dare not go there yet. Will you go to the camp of the traitors and find this book for me?'

'In a time past, I would ask my brethren for the book, and it would be given freely. Since the arrival of the Men of the North, my brethren have changed. They have forsaken their oaths and follow the Men without thinking of the damage they do to the land. It is sad that the book had to be taken from them with war and death, but honour says it must be so.
'Take this book to little Gondranc and tell him honour is satisfied. May he use its knowledge well.'

'In a time past, I would ask my brethren for the book, and it would be given freely. Since the arrival of the Men of the North, my brethren have changed. They have forsaken their oaths and follow the Men without thinking of the damage they do to the land.

'Ah, my thanks to Asikko for his courtesy and to you for your assistance. With this lore, I will be able to craft the best possible armour I may for the people of Trestlebridge.'

'The Orcs' invasion from the North has caught the Rangers of the North unprepared. Many of our kindred are abroad in other lands, preparing a defence against the Shadow in the East, and our eyes were not turned northwards.
'This army that has come down from Angmar is too great for our forces in the North Downs to defeat without support, yet we must still prepare for the fighting that is to come.
'My predecessor stored many weapons and supplies throughout eastern Nan Amlug and Rhunenlad, but I do not know exactly where. I need you to seek out these troves and bring them to me. The thing that I do know is that these troves were all hidden near rocks and trees. This will not be an easy search without proper guidance, but in these dark times every resource we can gather will be of great help to us.'

'It will take some work to make many of these weapons usable, but they are better than hoes and hay-forks. We shall set about the repairs at once.
'I trust that your search was not too difficult. We must be resolute and fight back against these Orcs before the North Downs are lost. They must not be allowed to invade Bree-land, or many innocents will be killed and all the North may fall.'

'We hid the troves well; it is unlikely that the Orcs have despoiled them. Search in the area of Rhunenlad and eastern Nan Amlug.
'Be careful not to stray too close to the Earth-kin camps on the eastern edges of the plains. They have fallen under the sway of the Angmarim.'
