'I was asked to take stock of our provisions and appraise the repair of our tents. I have found that both are lacking. Without preparations, we will be forced to split our forces both to hunt the remaining game in the region and to fight the Orcs. Our numbers are too few for such a task.
'My request is simple: gather your allies and head into Rhunenlad and Nan Amlug, east of Esteldín, where the Aurochs are more plentiful. From the bulls collect hides...they can be used as shelter. The yearlings and cows will provide the best meat.
'Our needs will be great, so do not be frugal in your hunt.'

'This will help solidify our stores and allow us to remain focused on the trial at hand. We are moving closer to the inevitability of war each day.
'Take heart, for you have aided us in our hour of need, and you are to be thanked and rewarded, ${PLAYER}.'
'Search the plains east of Esteldín, in Rhunenlad and Nan Amlug. Aurochs wander those hills and plains in fair number.'
Speak with Mallennor
Collect thick aurochs hides (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collect aurochs meat (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Food and Shelter

The terrible slaughter of the Orc invasion has driven away the farmers from the western Nan Amlug, and with them any trade the Rangers had maintained. Short on supplies and provender, the Rangers of Esteldín must rely on their own resourcefulness to restock their supplies.
'Our stores should hold for some time now.'
'Thank you for your assistance, ${PLAYER}. These stores will aid us in our efforts.'

Aurochs can be found in Rhunenlad and Nan Amlug, east of Esteldín.
Mallennor has been tasked with providing shelter and food for the Rangers of Esteldín and has asked you to help them by hunting aurochs for hide and meat.
Collected relics (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'A year ago, we lost a rich ruin to Men from the South... at least we thought they were Men. They bore the manner, height, and look of Men but were nearly as savage as the Orc-folk we learned they were descended from.
'Naerost, north of here, in the eastern shadow of the great hill of Weathertop, fell to the half-breeds and our trade was lost with it. If we could recover some of those goods, we might restore trade with the west and some more hope for Eglain.
'Will you help us sift through the ruins for our goods?'

'Worthy finds, ${PLAYER}. These will fetch enough food for many families in Ost Guruth. You are becoming a true friend to the Eglain.
'So many perished when the half-breeds approached from the south, it is painful to recall. For now, know that you have done a great good for us all.'

'In Nain Enidh, north of the Great East Road and east of Weathertop, you will find the ruins of Naerost. You will know it by the half-breeds who make it their home.
'Among the rubble, you will find piles which appear to be nothing of import, but I tell you these relics will fetch a sum of food most bountiful from traders out of Bree.'
Return the relics to Hunulf Munce
Collect relics (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Half-breed Thieves

In the shadow of Amon Sûl, at the edge of Nain Enidh, lay an Arnorian ruin. Those ruins afforded the Eglain of Ost Guruth a wealth of material to trade with collectors in Bree-land... until the arrival of half-breeds from the South.

The ruins of Naerost are just east of Weathertop, north of Hunulf's camp.
A year ago, half-orcs wrested the ruins of Naerost from the Eglain, causing the Eglain to lose a valuable source of trade-goods. Hunulf asked you to return to ruins to sift through the relics there to recover the trade-goods they lost.
Collected stolen crates (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeated half-orcs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Many lost their lives when the half-orcs raided Naerost. Since then, we have struggled greatly. Most recently, as you likely know, we lost the ruin to goblins forced through the mountains in the north.
'Yet the half-orcs came first, and they slaughtered our people, stole our livelihood, and began despoiling the ruin. We do not know why, but we know they have collected many relics within the ruins and have packed them for delivery to the South.
'If you are willing, I would ask you to enter Naerost and seek the hirelings who guard the relics and slay them. Bring back any of the relics you find.'

'We will ensure that none of these relics were taken from the tombs of the men who perished within the ruins in ages past. If they are not, they will be used to feed and clothe our people. If they prove to be stolen from tombs, they will be buried once more to honour the fallen.
'You have proven yourself a brave and honourable warrior, ${PLAYER}, and your aid is valued by the Eglain.'

'The half-orcs are vile creatures, the result of breeding between Man and Orc. They are a blight in these lands and the world at large. Their murderous and thieving nature requires some manner of retaliation, even if the hour of its coming is late.'
Collect stolen crates (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeat half-orcs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring the stolen crates to Hunulf Munce
Bring the stolen crates to Hunulf Munce
A Righteous Recovery

In the shadow of Amon Sûl, at the edge of Nain Enidh, lays an Arnorian ruin. Those ruins afforded the Eglain a wealth of material to trade with collectors in Bree-land... until the arrival of half-breeds from the South.

'The half-orcs are vile creatures, the result of breeding between Man and Orc. They are a blight in these lands and the world at large. Their murderous and thieving nature requires some manner of retaliation, even if the hour of its coming is late.'

Naerost lies just east of Amon Sûl, north of Hunulf Munce.
Hunulf Munce has asked you to seek out and slay the hirelings who guard the relics packed for shipment and return as many of the relics as you can to the Eglain.

Hunulf awaits your return at the east edge of Minas Eriol, near the bridge over the gorge.
You should return with the recovered relics to Hunulf Munce.
Defeated Hontimûrz
Defeated Hontimûrz's guards (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Your efforts on behalf of the Eglain are noble, my friend, but I deem our peril is greater than first we thought. These half-breeds bear a standard with the mark of a white hand? Ordinary brigands and ruffians do not bear such charges. The mark of the White Hand tells me they serve a greater master.
'Whatever their purpose, such creatures cannot be allowed to take a foothold in the North. They do not belong here. If you can enter Naerost and slay Hontimûrz, their leader, and his guards, perhaps the rest will flee.
'Hontimûrz became known to us when he sent us gifts of the dead with his crudely-scrawled threats. I think, that you are here to avenge that disservice and restore more faith to the Eglain.'

'Ah, so the half-breeds will not run? No matter... the grip of the White Hand is loosened. I think that they will not trouble us again thanks to you.
'Your efforts on behalf of the Eglain will not be forgotten, ${PLAYER}.'
Defeat Hontimûrz
Defeat Hontimûrz's guards (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Hunulf Munce
Sever the White Hand

In the shadow of Amon Sûl, at the edge of Nain Enidh, lay an Arnorian ruin. Those ruins afforded the Eglain of Ost Guruth a wealth of material to trade with collectors in Bree-land... until the arrival of half-breeds from the South.

'I will spare the grim details of the delivery made to us by Hontimûrz. Know only that the depravation of these creatures proves that they are not Men. They are something wholly bestial and destructive. We have longed for a chance at revenge, and it seems that your arrival may herald a chance to seek that revenge.'
'We shall ever remember you, ${PLAYER}.'
'I can find my strength once again, thanks to all you have done.'

Naerost lies just east of Weathertop, north of Hunulf Munce.
Hunulf Munce is concerned that the half-orcs are servants of a greater power, perhaps even Mordor. He has asked you to enter Naerost and defeat their leader and his guards in hopes that the rest will flee.

Hunulf Munce awaits your return at his camp on the east side of Minas Eriol, south of Naerost.
Though the half-orcs did not flee, their leader and his guards have been defeated. You should return to Hunulf Munce with the news.

At first glance, this looks like a piece of worthless jewellery, but upon further inspection you discovered an inscription engraved on the back of the pendant.
'I will ever and always love you.
- D'
Beneath this inscription is carved a symbol of the Eglain. Perhaps someone of the Eglain can assist you with finding the owner of this necklace?

Daegwalt's face contorts briefly in a look of anguish, before he fights back the pain and issues a smile.
'This is my wife's. I gave it to her before we came to live with the Eglain. It was lost when she was struck down at Naerost.
'You have given me something that I cannot truly repay, but I will give you something of import to me in an effort to repay you.'
'Yes, can I help you?'
Deliver the necklace to its rightful owner
An Honourless People
While hunting down the half-orcs, you discovered a necklace bearing an inscription and the mark of the Eglain.
You discovered a necklace upon one of the half-orcs in the central Lone-lands. Perhaps you can ask some of the Eglain if they know who the true owner of the necklace could be.
Collected a dwarf-banner

'I sometimes think I ought never have left the mountains and the home of my ancestors, but I sought after a life of adventure. After too many years looking, I found myself lost and then found again here amongst the Eglain.
'I have been here a long time now and consider myself one of them, but there are remnants of my own heritage that never stray, friend, and those remnants get stirred in times like these.
'I hear rumour of dwarves working with Orcs to despoil the tombs beneath the ruins of Thandobel to the south. I wish to know what kind of dwarf would tolerate Orcs, much less deign to work alongside them. Go to Thandobel and bring me one of their banners.'

'I know this blazon. My father told me of a revolt and battle long ago against a host of the Elves in Ered Luin. Skorgrím, a leader of the Dourhands, to whom this blazon belongs, led the assault and drove the Dourhands to near destruction.
'Buried beneath the mountains was he, by the quick actions of the Elves' leader, who sacrificed himself to deny Skorgrím victory.
'Dourhands in league with Orcs... grim news indeed, and there is no doubt of what must come next.'

'No self-respecting dwarf would abide the sight of an Orc, much less help the filthy creatures. Either the dwarves in Ost Cyrn are under the sway of a grim sorcerer, or they must be destroyed.
'I need your assistance to determine which. Bring me one of the banners from around their fortress.'
Bring the banner to Refr Quicksilver
Collect a dwarf-banner
Dour Dwarves

In Annunlos lays a ruin, long abandoned by the Eglain. Picked clean and having only the depths of the ruin unexplored, the Eglain left the places beneath the ruin be, as is their custom. However, the ruin now teems with life again as dwarves, presumably in league with Orcs, scour for treasures in the depths.

The ruins of Thandobel lie to the south of Refr Quicksilver in Annunlos.
Refr Quicksilver expressed a desire to learn what kind of dwarves would deign to work alongside Orcs and has asked you to go to the ruins of Thandobel and capture one of their banners.
Collected Dourhand axes (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'This dwarf is not one to brook betrayal, and I know now that the Dourhands are betrayers to all the Free Peoples. Consorting with Orcs is deserving of only one punishment.
'I'll not say that I am pleased by this situation, ${PLAYER}, nor will I look an opportunity side-long when it stares me in the face. Dwarves or not, these Dourhands need to be dealt with, and you seem to be more than suitable to the cause.
'I have a request of you, then. Return to Thandobel and wreak vengeance upon the Dourhands in the name of all the Free Peoples. But let us see something good come out of this evil. Bring me the axes of the Dourhands, for metal is not evil, and dwarf-metal can be used to the benefit of us all!'

'Ha! Fine iron indeed. Not as comely as other weapons but still made by dwarf-hands and crafted with care. I shall smelt the ill deeds from these weapons and craft them newly into arms and armour for all to use.
'Do not see shame in what you have done, but gain strength from the knowledge that you have done your part to stop the spread of evil.'

'The Dourhands here in the Lone-lands must not be allowed to delve deeper into the ruins. If they are delving into the mounds of Men and assisting the Orcs, then something grim and foul is at work here.'
Collect Dourhand axes (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Deliver the Dourhand axes to Refr Quicksilver
A Dwarf's Duty

In Annunlos lay a ruin, long abandoned by the Eglain. Picked clean and having only the depths of the ruin unexplored, the Eglain left the tombs beneath the ruin be, as is their custom. However, the ruin now teems with life again as dwarves, in league with Orcs, scour the ruin for treasures in the depths.
'Bring me those axes, ${PLAYER}!'

The Dourhands can be found within the ruins of Thandobel, south of Refr Quicksilver.
The Dourhand dwarves have forsaken their ties to their brethren by consorting with Orcs. Refr Quicksilver has asked you to bring vengeance upon the Dourhands in the name of the Free Peoples and to bring him a trophy of their axes.

Refr Quicksilver waits for you at the entrance to the cave, south of the Great East Road in the Lone-lands, north of Thandobel.
You should return to Refr Quicksilver with news of your victory against the Dourhands and bring him the axes you took as trophies.
Collected the Dourhand Overseer's medallion

'Somewhere in Mithrenost, there is a dwarf who oversees the labours of the Dourhands. Though the Dourhands have gone against their nature by consorting with Orcs, all hope for them may not be lost.
'Find the overseer of the Dourhands and defeat him. His defeat may break the resolve of his followers, and they may well turn from the dark path upon which they tread. Bring me evidence of the overseer's downfall, and I will hold you honoured for your efforts on behalf of the Eglain.
'The overseer will be savvy and strong... be wary if you hope to defeat him.'

'Hunulf and Gadaric did well with choosing you. A fine upstanding sort you turned out to be.
'Though it pains me to know that my brethren have fallen so far, I am pleased to have gained the kinship you offer, ${PLAYER}.
'I took a certain liberty with some of the metal of the axes you collected and crafted this fine piece for you. You can do with it as you will. You have earned it.'
'Search near the centre of Mithrenost for turned earth or a greater congregation of dwarves. The overseer will be there. Remember, do not be foolhardy and attempt this task on your own.'
Deliver the Dourhand medallion to Refr Quicksilver
Collect the Dourhand Overseer's medallion
Enemies of the Eglain

In Annunlos lays a ruin, long abandoned by the Eglain. Picked clean and having only the depths of the ruin unexplored, the Eglain left the tombs beneath the ruin be, as is their custom. However, the ruin now teems with life again as dwarves, in league with Orcs, scour for treasures in the depths.
'I will not soon forget what you did against the Dourhands.'
'It is fine to see you again, ${PLAYER}.'

The overseer of the Dourhands may be found within the ruins of Mithrenost, south of Refr Quicklsilver.
Refr Quicksilver has asked to seek out and defeat the overseer of the Dourhands at Mithrenost, in hopes that his followers will turn from their evil ways. He asked you to bring him evidence of the overseer's defeat.
Searched skeletons for Restless Shades (${VALUE}/40)
Search skeletons for Restless Shades (${VALUE}/40)
Fornost: Free the Fallen

At the Battle of Fornost, centuries earlier, some of King Arvedui's men turned against him, and Fornost fell to the Witch-king. Before he fled, Arvedui cursed these men never to rest until they fulfilled their oaths of fealty. Perhaps these Oathbreaker shades will be able to leave if the descendants of Men of Arthedain have forgiven their betrayal?
'There is still much work to be done!'
'Someone leads them all... I know it.'

The shades Emma Slee sent you to free remain near their old skeletons in the upper areas of Fornost.
Emma Slee wishes to free some of the shades of Fornost from the ancient curse binding them to Middle-earth. She hopes that as descendants of the Dúnedain of Arthedain the forgiveness of the Men of the North Downs might be enough to free the repentant shades.
Defeated Milkeyes within Rath Teraig (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'We need to keep our enemies penned within Rath Teraig as best we may. The number of goblins seems to grow each day, but our stout barricades have been enough to keep them at bay.
'However, those vile Milkeye cave-claws have taken to creeping up and burrowing beneath the barricades in the deep of night and threaten to undermine the walls if we can't find a way to stop them.
'If you could hunt a number of the creatures down, it should serve to put a halt to their incessant digging and gain us time to repair any damage they've already done.'
'Well done, ${PLAYER}! That should keep those vermin at bay for a while and give us a chance to patch up the barricades before the goblins have another try at us.'
Defeat Milkeyes within Rath Teraig (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Tralli Hammerfist
Cave-claws in the Narrows

Tralli Hammerfist is concerned about the cave-claws burrowing beneath the barricades. Until recently, the barricades have been strong enough to withstand the goblin assaults, but the cave-claws have now weakened them.
'The Milkeyes dwell south of the barricade, in the narrow passes within the valley.'

Milkeyes can be found beyond the barricades south of the dwarf-camp.
Tralli Hammerfist has asked you to enter Rath Teraig and kill off a number of Milkeyes, to prevent them from gnawing at the barricades.

Tralli Hammerfist is at his camp beyond the barricade at the northern entrance to Rath Teraig.
You should return to Tralli Hammerfist and let him know that you have done as he asked.
Defeated Gazrîp

'My thanks to you for standing by us on this. You are not here to simply cull the local vermin... you want to deal with the real threat: that is to say goblins!
'The foul things have been bubbling up out of the ground like bees from a kicked hive. I don't rightly know what has gotten them all riled up, nor do I much care, but I believe it is their leader, Gazrîp.
'If you're up for a fight, get in there and break some goblin heads! If we can shatter their morale by defeating their leader, we can pen them in through the winter. The snows ought to block up these passes till spring, and we will be free of them for a long while, at least.'

'Ha! Nothing like a rousing tale of goblin-slaying to warm you up on a cold day! Well done, ${PLAYER}. With your help, we shouldn't have too many problems keeping the goblins at bay till the passes fill with snow for the winter.
'After that, it will be up to the leaders at Gondamon and Thorin's Hall to figure out what we'll do about them come next spring.'
Defeat Gazrîp
Talk to Ingólfr
Goblins in the Valley
Ingólfr is tired of dealing with the goblins of Rath Teraig, which have become more aggressive of late.
'South of the barricade is goblin territory, so you should have no problems finding goblin necks to hew. Gazrîp will be another matter, but you will find him deep within the camp.'
'You've a skilled hand with a weapon, ${PLAYER}!'
'Thanks to you, we shouldn't have too many worries with the goblins in Rath Teraig until spring.'

Gazrîp can be found beyond the barricade south of Ingólfr's camp deep within the goblin camps.
Ingólfr has asked you to enter Rath Teraig and deal with the goblin-leader Gazrîp, in hopes that his death will teach the goblins to keep away from the barricades long enough for the winter snows to fill the pass.

Ingólfr is at his camp beyond the barricade at the northern entrance to Rath Teraig.
You should return to Ingólfr and tell him of your battles against the goblin-leader in Rath Teraig.
Defeated spiders in Rath Teraig (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Ah, greetings! Welcome to the beautiful Rath Teraig... the finest stretch of desolate rock and goblin-holes in all of the Blue Mountains. If you have come to help, we could certainly use it. Things have gotten worse of late, and now all manner of things are crawling up out of the ground around here.
'I'd personally be grateful if you could do away with a few of the spiders that infest the area. I used to run patrols in there now and again, but since they showed up, I haven't been able to bring myself to set one foot past this barricade... I've been afraid of spiders since I was a wee lad.
'So what say you? Are you up for the challenge, or would you rather join me freezing my hinder parts off till the snows come?'
'The whole barricade-guard -- both of us -- thanks you, ${PLAYER}, but I am personally indebted to you for killing those eight-legged horrors. Now, the less said of them the better!'
Defeat spiders in Rath Teraig (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Tralli Hammerfist
Spiders of the Vale
Tralli Hammerfist has asked for your help in destroying the spiders that lurk beyond the barricade into Rath Teraig.
'The spiders are scattered throughout the valley to the south. You should be able to find them without too much trouble.'

There are spiders beyond the barricade south of the dwarf-camp.
Tralli Hammerfist, deathly afraid of spiders, has asked you to defeat a few of the creatures for him.

Tralli Hammerfist is at the dwarf-camp beyond the barricade at the northern entrance to Rath Teraig.
You should return to Tralli Hammerfist with news of your success.

'${CLASS}, if you would take a moment, I have a request of you. A dear friend to me, Brethilwen, spends her days tending the grapes at Limael's Vineyard to the north and west. She sent word to me not long ago that she required a cask for a special wine she wanted to present upon the White Ships.
'I have crafted a cask for her, but need someone to take it to her since the preparations for our departure keep me very busy.
'Would you take the cask to her? You will find her to the north and west at Limael's Vineyard.'
'I only wish that this thoughtful gift from Bregedúr did not arrive during such dire times. With the situation at the Vineyard, I fear that the cask may go empty for our journey.'
DNT - NEVER SHOULD BE SEEN
Deliver the wine-cask to Brethilwen outside Limael's Vineyard
Need of a Cask
Bregedúr, at the Craftsman's Plaza in Celondim, asked that you deliver a cask meant for storing wine to his friend Brethilwen at Limael's Vineyard.

'You will find Brethilwen at Limael's Vineyard to the north and west of Celondim. Follow the road north-west and shortly after the river seek the small path leading to the west. You will find her along that road.'

You will find Brethilwen to the north and west at the outskirts of Limael's Vineyard. Make your way along the roadway heading north-west out of Celondim and follow the small path along the river to the west to find her.
Bregedúr, the local cooper at Celondim, asked you to deliver a cask to his friend Brethilwen at Limael's Vineyard.

'All filled and ready for delivery. I would like to thank you for your assistance, ${PLAYER}, as I would not have been able to see this last bit of harvest along without you.
'This cask is meant for another; however, I should like to see it sent along to my friend Bregedúr. It was he who sent it to me, after all... why should he not have the finest wine of the valley?
'If you would, take this back to him at Celondim. Follow the path to the east and turn towards the south-east across the bridge. You will find him at the crafters' market.'

'Thank you, ${PLAYER}, and thank my friend Brethilwen for knowing my intentions. I understand that Brethilwen was beset by goblins and that you fought many off to obtain this spirit. Know that it was for a worthy cause.'
SHOULD NEVER BE SEEN
Bring the wine-cask to Bregedúr
Return the Cask
Brethilwen wishes to thank Bregedúr for his kindness.
'Take the cask to Bregedúr at the crafters' market in Celondim, south of here.'

Bregedúr spends his time at the crafters' market in Celondim.
Brethilwen crushed the grapes you collected into a fine wine and sent them on to her friend Bregedúr in Celondim.

'Welcome to Falathlorn, ${PLAYER}. You can see the harbour-city of Celondim up the hill to the north-east, and the refuge of Duillond is further to the north.
'But I can see that you have a desire to fashion goods, to practice your ability to create things of substance and use. It is my recommendation that you visit my friend Gwaloth at the terrace overlooking Celondim, where many useful and comely goods are fashioned. Go up the hill to the north-east into the city and follow the path to the left as it winds up the hillside. Atop the stairs, follow the path southward to the terrace.
'Gwaloth will be pleased to help you learn how to begin your journey as a craftsman.'

'Mibrethil sent you to me? You must be interested in learning a crafting trade, then? Wonderful! Ered Luin will be better for your efforts, my friend! Speak with the Master of Apprentices on this terrace, for he can help you choose professions in which to specialize.
'Once the Master of Apprentices has welcomed you to your chosen professions, be sure to speak with a supplier. She can sell you the tools of your trade -- every profession has its own tools, so be not over-shy with your coinpurse! The novices will be happy to sell you any recipes you might wish to have, though I can tell you now that you will already know how to make a thing or two.
'Equip the crafting tools you plan on using and find an appropriate facility -- Celondim has a forge, workbench, and oven available for your use -- and begin practising your skills! You will advance in your chosen professions as you practice and seek out the teachings of others in the field. I hope you will become a skilled crafter, ${PLAYER}, and that it will bring joy to you and profit to Ered Luin!'
Talk to Gwaloth
Crafting: A Terrace in Celondim
Mibrethil has suggested that you speak with his friend Gwaloth at a terrace overlooking the harbour of Celondim where useful and comely goods are made.

'Gwaloth is on a terrace overlooking Celondim where many useful things are made. Go down the hill to the north-east into Celondim, then climb the winding stair on your left as it rises along the hillside. Atop the stair, take the southern path to the terrace and introduce yourself to Gwaloth. She will gladly aid you in choosing crafting professions.'
'I wish you good fortune with your pursuit of crafting, ${PLAYER}.'
'May your creations bring joy to those who need them.'
'The facilities of Celondim are yours to use as you like, ${PLAYER}.'
'Ered Luin will be a better place for your efforts.'

Gwaloth is on a terrace overlooking Celondim, located south of the top of the stairs that wind up the hillside around which the city is constructed.
The Elf Mibrethil suggested that you speak with his friend Gwaloth if you are interested in learning a crafting trade.
Collected polished agate (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'I am a jeweller by interest and by trade, and I have a great many pieces in various states of completion. I could finish many of these pieces, but I am missing the gems needed for the final settings.
'If you know a jeweller with a ready supply, I will give you some coins for bringing to me three polished agates of suitable quality.
'Your assistance will be greatly appreciated, for I have already neglected these pieces for too long and am eager to complete them. I have one or two items that may be useful to you, and would happily trade them to you in exchange for the agates I need.'

'These polished agates are just the sort for which I have been waiting, ${PLAYER}, and I thank you for them!
'Take these coins and items with my well-wishes, for now I can finish the pieces I have kept too long undone!
'Perhaps when this affair is finished, I shall find a place on one of the White Ships and sail away into the West. I will need to think on it.'
'Without three polished agates, I cannot finish these pieces as I hoped to do.'
Bring polished agates to Guleneth
Collect polished agate (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Crafting: Gems for Guleneth
The jeweller Guleneth has asked you to bring him polished agates he can use in the pieces he makes.
'I do not yet know if it is my time to take to the Ships.'
'What is left for me to do? It is a question I have long pondered.'

Guleneth is at Celondim in Ered Luin.
Jeweller Guleneth has asked you to acquire three polished agates that he can use to complete some of the pieces he has left unfinished.

'Before you leave, ${PLAYER}, I have one more boon to ask of you. I promised a bottle of last year's vintage to a friend at Duillond to the north, and my labours kept me too busy to fulfil that pledge. I hope this has not inconvenienced her.
'Could you deliver this bottle to Dolengyl for me? The refuge lies on the road that follows the river north beyond Limael's Vineyard.
'If you reach the dwarf-port of Kheledûl, you have travelled too far north. Perhaps you should make use of the horse from here to Duillond.'

'Splendid! I must admit that I wondered if perhaps Bregedúr would come through on his promise. I should have known that he would not forget a friend.
'Ah, this vintage has the promise of ageing nicely. Perhaps in some thirty years, it will have aged sufficiently. You have my thanks.'
'Are you in need of something? I am afraid I do not know how I may be of service.'
Bring the bottle of wine to Dolengyl
Gift for a Friend
Bregedúr promised a cask of the finest vintage to Dolengyl, an Elf at the refuge of Duillond.

'You are looking for Dolengyl of Duillond. The refuge is on the river, yes, but it is a far distance north of here. You want to head north across the tributary and past Limael's Vineyard. You would be wise to use the horse to reach Duillond.'
'I trust that Dolengyl was pleased to receive the bottle of wine, you delivered. Thank you again for all your help, ${PLAYER}.'
'I hope that cask was useful to you. You went through enough effort to get it.'
'Thank you for bringing me the bottle of wine from Brethilwen. If you are down that way again, please thank her for me.'

The Elf-refuge of Duillond lies on the north road by the river.
Bregedúr has asked you to deliver a bottle of last year's vintage to his friend Dolengyl.
Grape clusters picked from vines (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'By this time of the year, most of the grapes have been picked and the wine already bottled. This was a very generous season, however, and many of the vines are still laden with grapes. I would welcome your assistance. Wine-making is not easy work, but performing this task will certainly add to your appreciation of the wine you drink.
'Harder still when nasty goblins find their way into the fields and drive you off. I think though you might be sturdy enough to aid me.
'If you would, gather the grapes from the vines still hale and hearty enough and I will see that this cask is filled with the finest this vale has to offer.
'The vineyard is below us and further to the west along the stone path. Be careful of the goblins -- they are particularly nasty.'
'Very good, ${PLAYER}. Years from now, your efforts today will bring great joy to many. Hard work brings satisfaction, not just in wine-making but in all things.'
'Six clusters of grapes from this season's ripe vines should be enough. Any less than that, and I could not in good conscience bottle them.'
Pick the grape clusters from the vines (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring the grapes to Brethilwen
Gleaning the Field
Brethilwen, the Master-vintner of Celondim, believes there are enough grapes left on the vine for one last cask of wine.
'Six large clusters of grapes from this season's ripe vines should be enough. Any less than that, and I could not in good conscience bottle them.'

The fertile vines grow around a lake in a sheltered valley west along the stone path beneath Brethilwen. You will need to be wary of the goblins.
Brethilwen has asked you to pick the remaining grapes from Limael's Vineyard.

Brethilwen is in Celondim, south-east of Limael's Vineyard.
You should return to Brethilwen with your harvest.
Collected wine-flasks (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'My friend, I wonder if I can ask you to undertake a task for me? It is bad enough that the goblins despoil Limael's Vineyard, but recently a party of the wretched creatures broke into an old wine-cellar and stole a number of flasks of a rare and ancient vintage.
'No doubt the evil creatures have already drunk or destroyed most of the wine, but if you can recover any of the bottles from the goblins in this area, I would be deeply in your debt.
'You can find the goblins throughout Limael's Vineyard. I would not venture beyond into the Rath Teraig, however, as the goblins there are rather more dangerous.'
'Ah very good! You have done all that I could ask. Thank you for your efforts. Those wicked creatures will learn better than to raid my wine-cellars in the future!'
'Alas, I suppose all the wine is gone by now. But perhaps you can return to the field and continue your search?'
Bring the wine-flasks back to Brethilwen
Collect wine-flasks (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
A Rare Vintage
Goblins stole a rare wine from the vintner, Brethilwen.

There are goblins throughout Limael's Vineyard, north-west of Celondim. Brethilwen is at an old ruin overlooking the vineyard to the east.
Brethilwen has asked you to recover wine flasks of a rare and ancient vintage from the goblins who stole them.

'I have been thinking, ${PLAYER}. After all the trouble with Starkath over the bow, I don't believe I am worthy of it... especially since I could not even hold onto it.
'Please go back to Penglir and explain why I can't accept his bow. He may still be at Duillond to the south of Gondamon.
'I am a disappointment to my own folk and to the honour of Penglir's gift.'
'He feels unworthy? Did Celairant think that I gave my bow to him upon a whim? I did not give that bow idly to the first Man I met!'
Someone Worthy
After allowing Starkath to take the bow from him, Celairant is now certain that he is not worthy of the Elvish weapon.
'I am sure I do not deserve the bow. Please take it back to Penglir at the Elf-refuge.'

Penglir is at Duillond, south-east of Gondamon.
Celairant asked you to return to Penglir at Duillond and explain why he feels unworthy to bear the bow, having lost it once already to the dwarf-brigand Starkath.
Found Elvellon, the Elf-sword

'Celairant bears the blood of the Rangers of the North, and the name of a great hero is amongst his forebears, a Man I was proud to call my friend and companion. Perhaps Celairant is young as Men count the years, but then all Men are young by my count.
'In ages past, I honoured my fallen companion with a sword placed at his grave amongst the mounds of the Edain. It may be that the sword can yet be found in that place. It bears the motto Elvellon, or Elf-friend in the tongue of Men. Perhaps if you find the sword, that will convince young Celairant not to spurn my gift.'

'What is this? Surely not another gift? Nay, this is something else, is it not? What is the significance of this old sword?
'This is the sword of my ancestor? You say he was a friend and companion of Penglir? Now I understand. He gave me the bow in honour of my great-grandfather.
'What? You think the gift was made to me, not to my forebear? Well, it may be you are right, despite all. It will be a challenge to live up to those bygone glories, but perhaps someday I will be able to wield the bow without shame.'
'Oh, I wish I was worthy of Penglir's gift but I am just a fool, barely able to take care of myself much less such a glorious work of Elf-craft.'
Bring the Elf-sword to Celairant
Find Elvellon, the Elf-sword
The Elf-sword
After allowing Starkath to take the bow from him, Celairant is now certain that he is not worthy of the Elvish weapon.
'Find Elvellon and give it to Celairant with my blessings.'
'Thank you for your help. I will do my best to live up to Penglir's legacy and to the deeds of my great-grandfather.'
'Ah, ${PLAYER}, I have much to live up to. I can only hope to prove myself worthy one day.'
'He understands the meaning of my gift? Well, perhaps not, but at least he understands it was not given lightly.'
'I am certain that young Celairant will one day prove his worth.'

The sword Elvellon can be found at a grave marker amongst the mounds of the Edain, north-east of Gondamon. Celairant is at the hunter's lodge, west of Kheledûl.
Penglir has asked you to retrieve a sword which he placed by his companion's grave long ago and take it to Celairant.
You have recovered the stolen bow

'An Elf named Penglir gave me this beautiful bow but I've gone and lost it! Or more to the point, it was stolen from me. The Rangers make a point to stay out of the feud between the Longbeards and the Dourhands, so I was not expecting to be waylaid by brigands out of Kheledûl!
'They overpowered me as I was looking for a good place to practice outside the town and stole Penglir's bow! The dwarves and Starkath, their leader, skulk near the walls of Kheledûl.
'I knew I wasn't worthy to deserve such a rich gift. I'm a failure... an embarassment to Langlas and to the Rangers. So hapless am I that I dare not fight Starkath. Can you go forth and take the bow back from him?'

'You recovered the bow from Starkath? You have my thanks, ${PLAYER}! I have not much but my name, so my name is precious to me. I could not have lived with the shame of dishonouring Penglir's princely gift.'
'Please, recover Penglir's bow from Starkath!'
Bring the bow to Celairant
Collect the stolen bow
A Remarkable Bow

While on his way to Duillond, an Elf named Penglir stopped at the hunters' lodge and gave his bow to the young Ranger Celairant. Celairant accepted the gift, but feels unworthy to own such a thing of beauty.
'The bow must be returned to Celairant.'

Starkath can be found outside the walls of Kheledûl. Celairant is at Thrasi's lodge, west of Kheledûl.
Celairant told you that his bow was stolen at sword-point by a Dourhand named Starkath and his minions. He has asked you to hunt down Starkath and recover the bow.
Defeated wights (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Eastern Haudh Lin is home to some ancient burial mounds of the Edain, the Men who lived here in a past age. We have received reports of evil wights stalking these barrows and mounds. Such creatures are mere corpses animated by fell spirits, not the relics of the spirits of Men. As such, they are irredeemably evil, and it is our duty to exterminate them without compunction. I do not know why these creatures are abroad in these dark days, but I suspect some working of the Enemy.
'Be that as it may, I ask you to destroy the bodies of these evil creatures, and send their spirits back to the Shadow from whence they came.'
'Well done, ${PLAYER}. The Enemy may raise more wights from the bones of the fallen, and when they do it will be our duty to send them back to their ancient graves.'
Defeat wights (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
A Deathly Task
Eastern Haudh Lin suffers from a terrible threat; dread wights stalk the ancient mounds of the Edain, animated by evil fell spirits.
'The wights are some working of the Enemy and must be destroyed.'

Wights can be found amongst the mounds and barrows of the Edain, in eastern Haudh Lin.
Glamír has asked you to destroy the evil wights of Haudh Lin.

Glamír waits in the ruin south of the Grimwater within the woods of Western Haudh Lin.
You journeyed to the mounds and barrows of the Edain in Haudh Lin and defeated many wights.
Defeated spiders in Eastern Haudh Lin (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'This land has been sullied before by the dwarves and their keep on the hill and more recently by half-orcs and crebain. Now wicked spiders have entered the land, slaughtering the wildlife and endangering travellers.
'Thankfully, these evil creatures have so far only been found in the furthest north-east reaches of Haudh Lin, but these lands would be better for their absence.
'Seek out the evil spiders and drive them from their lairs in Haudh Lin.'
'Your help is most appreciated, ${PLAYER}. This blight of spiders might have spread throughout Ered Luin. Thank you.'
Defeat spiders in Eastern Haudh Lin (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Sickening of the Land
The tranquility and protection of Duillond, the Elf-refuge, does not reach so far north as Haudh Lin. As a result, foul creatures have begun to creep into that place of peace.
'The swarms of spiders that plague our land must be brought to an end.'

Spiders infest north-eastern Haudh Lin, far beyond Duillond.
Laergil has asked you to kill off as many spiders as you are able.

Laergil waits in north-western Haudh Lin.
You should return to Laergil and report your success.
Collected minor woodworking-lore

'It is my privilege to aid with the construction of the White Ships that bring the Eldar into the West, but I have wondered of late if there was any improvement, even of small value, that might be made to the wood we use for that purpose.
'If you know a scholar of some skill, I would appreciate any minor woodworking-lore you might be able to acquire.
'Thank you for your assistance. I have one or two small relics I can give to you for your trouble.'

'Thank you, ${PLAYER}, this minor woodworking-lore is just what I had in mind. I will spend some time in contemplation of it to see if there are any lessons I can draw from within its pages. Take these small items with my gratitude.'
'You have not been able to gather any minor woodworking-lore for me?'
Bring minor woodworking-lore to Raindis
Collect minor woodworking-lore
Crafting: Studying the White Ships
Raindis of Celondim has asked you to bring her some minor woodworking-lore that she can apply to the preparation of timbers used in the construction of the White Ships.
'The building of the White Ships is not easy.'
'I am always seeking to improve the wood we use in the construction of the White Ships.'

Raindis is at Celondim, in Ered Luin.
Raindis has asked if you would collect some minor woodworking-lore from a scholar so she can see if any improvements might be made to the wood that is used as the timber for the White Ships.
Collected rowan bowstaff (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Are you a woodworker? I have taken to practising my bow-bending, and I always have need of rowan wood with which to refine my technique.
'If you can bring to me three rowan bowstaves, I will appreciate it and give to you some coins and materials.'

'These will serve wonderfully well, my friend. I thank you for them and will resume my practice at once!
'I hope these coins and materials are of use to you.'
'I am still waiting for three rowan bowstaves, my friend. A woodworker should be able to prepare them.'
Bring rowan bowstaves to Laegon
Collect rowan bowstaff (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Crafting: Laegon Practises His Craft
The Elf Laegon has taken to practising his bow-making, and he often wants for materials.
'You must always practise your craft, ${PLAYER}.'
'There is no single means to succeed at a trade, my friend.'

Laegon is at Celondim, in Ered Luin.
Laegon has asked if you could bring him three rowan bowstaves he can use to refine his bow-bending techniques.

'Have you already been to the Michel Delving Craft-fair? You should definitely go, if you haven't already! There's a workbench, a forge, and even an oven just waiting to be used!
'If you think you have crafting in your heart, you should visit my friend Emerald Borings at the Craft-fair -- she's always happy to help someone get started making useful and pretty things.
'Pass east through Little Delving, and then follow the path south into Michel Delving. Take the south-west path from the statue of Marcho and Blanco in the town centre, and pass the stables on your right. Take the next left turn to reach the Craft Fair. Emerald will be happy to help you out!'

'Alf sent you to me? Good, good! We need more good folk with an interest in making useful and pretty things! Speak with the Mistress of Apprentices, and she can help you choose professions in which to specialize. Choose your professions with care, because you will expend a great deal of time and energy improving your skills.
'Once the Mistress of Apprentices has welcomed you to your chosen professions, be sure to speak with a Supplier who can sell you the tools of your trade -- every profession has its own tools, so be not over-shy with your coinpurse! The novices will be happy to sell you any recipes you might wish to have, though I can tell you now that you will already know how to make a thing or two.
'Equip the crafting tools you plan on using and find an appropriate facility -- Michel Delving has a forge, workbench, and oven available for your use -- and begin practising your skills! You will advance in your chosen professions as you practice and seek out the teachings of others in the field. I hope you will become a skilled crafter, ${PLAYER}, and that it will bring profit to you and to the Shire! I will give you a few coins to get you started. Use them wisely, and consider them an investment in your future as a skilled crafter!'
Crafting: Michel Delving Craft-fair
Alf Goodcliff thinks you could be a crafter of some skill and suggested you visit his friend Emerald Borings at the Craft-fair on the south side of Michel Delving.

'Pass east through Little Delving, and then follow the path south into Michel Delving. Take the south-west path from the statue of Marcho and Blanco in the town centre and pass the stables on your right. Take the next left turn to reach the Craft-fair.
'Emerald will be happy to help you out!'
'The Michel Delving Craft-fair is full of useful facilities for craftsmen.'
'The Craft-fair is on the south side of Michel Delving.'
'The Mistress of Apprentices can help you choose a crafting vocation.'
'Don't forget to buy needed tools from the Provisioner!'

Emerald Borings is at the Michel Delving Craft-fair, south-west of the statue in the town centre, past the stables, and along the first leftward turning.
Alf Goodcliff suggested you speak with his friend Emerald Borings if you are interested in pursuing a crafting profession.
You ran out of time!

'You did a fine job with that steed. It looks like the horse trusted you well enough. You also made it back more quickly than I expected. Men in my country...they would not believe a ${RACE} such as yourself could have done it so quickly!
'Now that you have proven that you can handle a steed I have another task for you...it will teach you endurance and holding your mount to its course. There is a stable-master in the land of the holbytla away to the west -- Michel Delving I believe they call it. The stable-master there is in need of a fresh Chestnut steed as well. Bring him his horse, and you will prove that you can hold to your saddle on a long journey!
'Hurry now! You have a long ride ahead of you. When you return, we shall see about continuing your training.'
<rgb=#FFFF00>Right-Clicking on the 'Mount' vitals display gives you the option to dismount your steed but will also cancel the quest.</rgb>
'You returned! I thought you might have been thrown from the saddle or lost. Your determination is strong...I have no doubt that you will make a fine rider.'
Take a fresh Chestnut steed to the stable-master in Michel Delving
Fresh Steed for Michel Delving
Éogar, the owner of Hengstacer, has asked for your help delivering a fresh steed to Michel Delving.
'Now that the steed has arrived I can finally sit down for a proper meal.'

The stable-master can be found in Michel Delving in the Shire, far to the west of Bree.
Éogar has asked that you ride a fresh steed out to the stable-master in Michel Delving.

Éogar, son of Hadorgar, is located at Hengstacer, north of Bree, far to the east of the Shire.
You should return to Éogar and inform him that you delivered the horse to the Michel Delving stable-master.

'Hello there! You wouldn't mind helping me out with a game of Hiders and Seekers, would you? You see, my friends Daisy and Polo have convinced me to play, even though they always hide in the same places! It isn't nearly as much fun when your friends are so unimaginative, as I'm sure you realize.
'It would be fantastic if you could round them up for me. I'll give you a coin or two if you help me out, but I don't know how many more times I can pretend to be surprised that Daisy is hiding in the bushes next to Peony Grubb's home, or that Polo is crouched behind the carved statue of Marcho and Blanco.
'You'll find the statue carved on a large tree stump just south of here, and I'm sure that Polo Brockhouse is hiding right by it. South-east of the statue, there's a small hill with several hobbit-houses behind a wooden fence -- Daisy thinks the bushes to the right of Peony Grubb's house are a clever place to hide. Find my friends for me, and next time I'll try and tell them I don't feel like playing Hiders and Seekers!'

'Rollo sent you to look for me? Oh, he always gives up so easily. I'm not sure that you can do that in a game of Hiders and Seekers -- I'm pretty sure it's against the rules. If you don't find the Hiders yourself, you aren't much of a Seeker, are you?
'Anyway, I'll wait here until Rollo finds everyone else. This is a great hiding spot, isn't it?'

'Ha ha! Rollo sent you to find me, did he? It always takes him so long to find us. Just between you and me, I don't think he's very good at Hiders and Seekers.
'I'll stay here and think about where I can hide for our next game!'

'Thanks for your help, ${PLAYER}! Hiders and Seekers is not much fun when your friends always hide in the same places. I don't think it's a game they're very good at.
'Wait a minute... you say that Daisy mentioned hiding until I found \qeveryone else?\q That's strange. I thought Polo was the only other hobbit I was supposed to be looking for! They mentioned maybe getting Odo to play, but I didn't think they'd actually do it....
'Here are the coins I promised you, but it sounds like your work as Seeker might not be done yet, ${PLAYER}!'
Find Polo Brockhouse
Find Daisy Brockhouse
Hiders and Seekers
Rollo Newbuck has been asked to play Hiders and Seekers with his friends, Daisy and Polo Brockhouse, but their unimaginative hiding places have made him lose interest in the game.
'I'll stay here until Rollo has found everyone else. I'm not convinced that you're allowed to designate someone else to be Seeker, but I guess I'll allow it since Rollo isn't very good at the game.'

'You found Daisy already? That's very good! She always chooses good hiding-places, like up near Peony Grubb's home. That's a great spot, although it isn't as good as some of mine, like right here in the shadow of Marcho and Blanco!'
'Polo is probably hiding behind the carved statue of Marcho and Blanco to the south of here, and his sister Daisy is always hiding south-east of there, among the bushes next to Peony Grubb's home.'

Polo Brockhouse is hiding behind the carved wooden statue of Marcho and Blanco in the centre of Michel Delving. His sister Daisy is hiding south-east of the carving, in the bushes to the right of Peony Grubb's home.
Rollo Newbuck is playing Hiders and Seekers with his friends, but they always hide in the same places, and he is tired of pretending to be surprised every time he finds them.

Rollo Newbuck is north of the carved statue of Marcho and Blanco at the centre of Michel Delving, within the circle of hedges that surround Town Hole.
Rollo is waiting to hear that you found Polo and Daisy Brockhouse.
'Peony said I could hide here, so it's not like I'm trespassing.'
'I wish I was as good a Hider as Odo Pipes.'
'I first thought of this hiding-place when I was working at the Bird and Baby.'
'Most Seekers look at the ground, and don't think of hiding-places that are higher up!'
'Odo Pipes was a good barrel-roller. Not as good as me, but still pretty decent!'
'Patrons at the Bird and Baby drink a lot of beer. I'm kept busy rolling barrels out, that's for sure!'

'This is serious, ${PLAYER}. I thought I was only playing Hiders and Seekers with Polo and Daisy, but it sounds like they talked to Odo Pipes and convinced him to play as well. You'd think they might have mentioned that to me!
'At any rate, Odo has a reputation for being the best Hider in all the Shire -- at least as good as old Bilbo was in his day, or so it's said among folk in The Bird and Baby. I don't know if it's true, but I do know that, unlike Daisy and Polo, Odo Pipes is sure to have a capital hiding-place, the very best!
'I'll have more coins for you if you can find him, ${PLAYER}. He'll be hiding somewhere in Michel Delving, so don't wander too far. You might want to talk to Polo and Daisy again -- they might be able to tell you where he could be hiding.'

'You found me! Very well-done, very well-done indeed! Next time I'll need to choose a better hiding-place, I suppose. I thought this one was perfect!
'You should return to Rollo and tell him that he knows how to choose good Seekers!'

'You found Odo Pipes? Excellent! He was on top of The Bird and Baby Inn the whole time?
'He must have some Tookish blood in him. You'd never get me up there, I can tell you that!
'Here are the coins I promised you, ${PLAYER}, and take my thanks as well! If they ever get me to play Hiders and Seekers again, I'll be sure to let you know -- that way you can give me a stern talking-to and ask me what I was thinking!'
Find Odo Pipes
The Top Hiding-Place
Rollo Newbuck has learned that Odo Pipes is also playing Hiders and Seekers, but Rollo doesn't know where the hobbit is hiding.

'You and Rollo haven't found Odo Pipes yet? It doesn't surprise me -- he's always been the best Hider in the Shire, you know.
'I don't know where his favourite hiding-places are, though. He really likes to climb things -- trees, fences, buildings. If you're looking for Odo Pipes, you probably should be looking in the sky!'

'Odo Pipes used to work here in The Bird and Baby -- in fact, he and I were responsible for rolling out the barrels when they were called for, and rolling them back when they were emptied.
'One time, he helped me climb up onto the roof to fix a leak up there. That was a very rainy Spring, and the rain was like to flood us out if the hole wasn't patched up!
'He was a good fellow, that Odo. After awhile he decided he didn't want to roll barrels anymore, and he moved on. I'm not sure what he's up to these days.'
'Rollo is in the square outside Town Hole, within the encircling hedges. Let him know that you found my hiding-place, and he's sure to be impressed!'

'Odo Pipes is the best Hider in the Shire -- I don't mind telling you that he's even better at the game than I am!
'I don't know where he's hiding, but I do know that he worked for a while stacking barrels at the Bird and Baby, just to the north. Maybe he mentioned his favourite hiding-places to someone in there?'
'You need to find Odo Pipes for me, ${PLAYER} -- he's sure to have found a really great hiding-place somewhere in Michel Delving!'
'Maybe I'm just not cut out for Hiders and Seekers.'
'No one ever lets me be a Hider. I'm always stuck being Seeker!'
'This is a great hiding-place. No one ever thinks of looking here!'
'Marcho and Blanco may have found the Shire... but they'd never find me!'

Odo Pipes is hiding somewhere in Michel Delving.
Rollo Newbuck has sent you to find Odo Pipes, rumoured to be the best Hider in the Shire. Odo is hiding somewhere in Michel Delving. Rollo thinks that Daisy or Polo, in their usual hiding-places, might have some clue to Odo's location.

Rollo Newbuck is east of The Bird and Baby Inn, within the stone wall around Town Hole.
Rollo is waiting to hear that you have found Odo Pipes and his hiding-place.

'I found a few old tablets in the South Fields that I'd be willing to give you if you helped me out, and maybe I could find one or two other useful things as well!'

'This will be just the thing, ${PLAYER}! I'll study this and become the best tailor in all the Shire -- you just wait and see!
'I've been saving up to buy something like this, so I'll give the coins to you instead, and these other things!'

Collected pie crust

'You've got to help me, ${PLAYER}! While my wife was out, I went and ate the pie crust she had baked...I couldn't help myself! I know that if I had waited, it would be filled with some delicious filling and be even better, but I've always been partial to the way my wife bakes the crust.
'Do you know any cooks? I need a replacement pie crust, and fast! If my wife gets back and sees the crust missing, why...she might not make another!
'I'll give you some coins and, and... half a dozen eggs if you can do this for me, ${PLAYER} -- now, quickly! Go get me a pie crust! I might have some other things lying about that I can give you as well!'

'You've got the pie crust there? Excellent, superb, wonderful! Here, hand it over!
'Yes, this will do perfectly! My wife will never know the difference, and she'll go ahead with her plan to fill it with something delicious: fruit filling, meat filling, who knows what she'll choose? I can't wait! Here is the reward I promised you, and my thanks for your trouble.
'This crust does look delicious. Maybe just a nibble...that won't hurt anything....'
'I need a pie crust, friend!'

'I'm not even going to look at this one, ${PLAYER}!
'Take these coins, eggs, and other small items, and my deepest apologies for troubling you over this! Twice!'
'I need a pie crust, friend! Yes, another one. I know!'

'Hello there! Do you mind helping me with something?
'I'm going to go camping with my friends in the Bindbole Wood, and we want to be sure we have everything all set. I still need two rowan camp-fire kits, though.
'Can you bring them for me? I'll give you some coins and other useful things for them, all right?'

'Thank you for these, ${PLAYER}! This is just what we need!
'Here are your coins and a few odds and ends, as I promised. Camping is so exciting, isn't it? I wouldn't want to do it outside of the Shire, though, that's for certain!'
'I still need two camp-fire kits, ${PLAYER}. Weren't you going to get them for me?'
Bring two rowan camp-fire kits to Crocus Stonybanks

Crafting: Camping Preparations
Crocus Stonybanks is trying to assemble some camp-fire materials so she can go camping with her friends.

Collected mushroom pie (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'I've eaten at The Floating Log almost every night for the past twenty years, but now they're working on the roof, and if you try and eat there you get plaster falling into your dishes!
'I refuse to eat there while the repairs are going on. I mean, honestly! I have my standards, and for mushroom pies I demand they be plaster-free! Is that too much to ask? I think not!
'If you know a worthy cook, I'd pay you for two mushroom pies, with coins and goods. I still need to eat, you know!'

'These pies look delicious! Thank you, ${PLAYER} -- maybe I don't need The Floating Log after all!
'Take these coins and other small items with my good wishes!'
'I'm hungry, and you haven't brought me the mushroom pies I requested!'
Bring mushroom pies to Odo Mudbottom
Collect mushroom pie (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Crafting: Mudbottom's High Standards
Odo Mudbottom is distraught that his favourite eating-place, The Floating Log, is currently undergoing repairs to its roof.
'No one wants to eat mushroom pies with plaster in them!'
'They should just close down the inn while the repairs are on, if you ask me!'

Odo Mudbottom is in Frogmorton.
Odo refuses to eat at The Floating Log while the repairs on the roof are underway, but he still wants his customary mushroom pies.

'My Aunt Prunella is as reputable a lady as you could hope to meet, but I'm worried that she might have done something a little reckless and could now be in terrible trouble! She'd been listening to that Tunnelly lass, and before you could say \qgoblins-in-the-Shire?\q, she'd gone off to see the creatures for herself!
'I just don't know what I'd do if my dear old Aunt actually finds goblins. Could you go look for her? Rumour has it that there are goblins in the north-west Greenfields.
'Aunt Prunella had a pretty umbrella that she carried everywhere, even on sunny days, so if you see a goblin with an umbrella, well....'

'Good gracious me, it could be that I might have gotten ahead of myself. Well, it's good that the old lady is safe. I am terribly sorry for troubling you about this. Take these coins, and I'd appreciate it if you didn't go mentioning this to anyone.'

'Oh no! You found Aunt Prunella's umbrella! I was afraid that you might.
'My poor, old Auntie! She was a tough, old lady, but I used to visit her all the time. Once every few months, at least! She will be missed, by one and all, I just know it! Scary is poorer for her loss!'
'If you do find Aunt Prunella's umbrella by one of the goblins that sneaked into the Shire out by the Greenfields... well, that's not happy news at all!'
Find Aunt Prunella's umbrella
Collect Prunella's umbrella
Bring Prunella's umbrella to Fosco Boffin
The Fate of Prunella Boffin
Fosco Boffin in Scary is worried about his aunt, a reputable hobbit named Prunella.
'Have you found Aunt Prunella's umbrella yet?'
'I suppose it doesn't pay to be too hasty. Lesson learned, all right?'
'Goblins are dangerous business, even if on this particular occasion Aunt Prunella was not in trouble.'

Goblins may be found in the north-west Greenfields. If one of them took Aunt Prunella's umbrella, it might be lying somewhere inside one of their camps.
You promised Fosco Boffin that you would look for his Aunt Prunella's umbrella. He fears that she ran afoul of goblins.

You promised Fosco Boffin that you would look for his Aunt Prunella's umbrella. He fears that she ran afoul of goblins.

Fosco was distressed by your recovery of his Aunt Prunella's umbrella; however, a neighbour informed him that she had actually been visiting her all day, and that Prunella had lost her umbrella earlier in the day. Fosco motions you over.
Defeated brigands (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'These strangers are a real problem hereabouts. I'm pretty sure they've been stealing food from the local farms, and it's just a matter of time before they cause worse trouble than that.
'That girl Violet probably went that way and found trouble, so I think you should deal with those ruffians. Maybe they'll take the hint and move back to wherever it is they came from.
'The ruffians -- brigands like as not -- are camped not far west of here. Their camp is on the heights of Narrowcleeve, south past a waterfall. It looks dangerous but you can ford the stream just before the cascade goes over the cliff.'

'I wish the Bounders had more hobbits. This sort of thing wouldn't happen if the Shire was guarded better in the first place.
'Well, no matter, here, please take these coins for your trouble.'
Defeat brigands (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Rousting Ruffians
Farmer Maggot's son Hammy is concerned about the continued presence of the ruffians west of his farm.

'Please try to drive off those ruffians for us. I hope it don't come to violence, but if it does, so be it. Their camp is at Narrowcleeve, west of this farm and on the far side of the waterfall. There should be a place where you can ford the stream not far from here.'
'Those brigands won't mess with the likes of us again!'
'Narrowcleeve would be a nice place to walk if it weren't for those brigands.'

The ruffians' camp is west of Bamfurlong. You must ford a stream at the top of a waterfall to enter the camp, which is set on the heights at Narrowcleeve.
Farmer Maggot's son Hammy has asked you to drive off the ruffians.

Bamfurlong is near the Brandywine River, south of Stock.
You have done as Hammy Maggot requested. You should return to him at Bamfurlong to tell him the news.
Defeated bats in the western Old Forest (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'The bats of the Old Forest have been a minor annoyance in the past, but of late they have grown very aggressive and even dangerous. They could become a plague in Buckland, so we need to reduce their numbers before that happens.
'There is a tunnel through the High Hay, east of here.'
'Well done. Here's your fee.'
Defeat bats in the western Old Forest (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

Forest Bats
Hodric Bracegirdle needs your help reducing the threats from the Old Forest.
'Bats may have their uses, but I find the creature foul, disgusting, disease-ridden beasts. There are simply too many too close to Buckland for my taste.'

There is a tunnel into the Old Forest, east of Hodric Bracegirdle.
Hodric Bracegirdle has asked you to reduce the number of bats in the Old Forest.

Hodric awaits word of your success.
Defeated bears in the western Old Forest (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'The bears of the Old Forest have always been dangerous, but in the past they were not very aggressive and could be avoided. Now they are roaming all over the place and may even come out of the forest to threaten Buckland if they aren't stopped.
'There is a tunnel through the High Hay, east of here.'
'Looks like you've been busy in those woods. Well a promise is a promise and you have earned this well.'
Defeat bears in the western Old Forest (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

Brumbald Tunnelly needs your help reducing the threats from the Old Forest.
'The bears in the old forest are far more aggressive than anything that I have ever seen. I would like to see their number thinned lest they climb the wall and make meals of us hobbits.'

The bears can be found in the Old Forest, east of his location near the High Hay. Look for the tunnel to the east.
Brumbald Tunnelly has asked you to help lessen the threat of bears.

'Giant spiders are a menace to everyone, but there have until recently been only a few in the Old Forest. Now their webs can be found in many places, and we are worried that they may soon spread to endanger everyone.
'There is a tunnel through the High Hay, east of here.'
'Good job. Those spiders are awfully creepy and I would never want to see them up close. It is lucky for us here in Buckland that there are folk like you nearby willing to help.'

Hodric Bracegirdle needs your help reducing the threats from the Old Forest.
'A spider that large has no place near a fine Hobbit settlement. I will thank you kindly to remove them from the Old Forest with haste.'

There is a tunnel into the Old Forest, east of his location near the High Hay. Search for the tunnel into the woods to the east.
Hodric Bracegirdle has asked for your help defending against spiders in the Old Forest.

Hodric Bracegirdle awaits word of your success.
Defeated wolves in the western Old Forest (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Wolves in the Old Forest have always been something of a threat to foresters and woodsmen, but they've recently become more dangerous and aggressive. We don't want them coming into Buckland, so it would be best to hunt them down now in the Old Forest itself.

'I look forward to not hearing howls in the night. Thank you, ${PLAYER}.'
Defeat wolves in the western Old Forest (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

Berangar Highknoll needs your help reducing the threats from the Old Forest.
'Howling wolves make for difficult sleeping. We need those beasts quieted and quickly.'
