'Leecher Cartwell in Combe has been wasting his healing stores on any rabble or riff-raff that wander through his door. Now, he expects me to fill his stores! It will cost him more than a few pennies this time, I can tell you that!
'Travel over to Brandy Hall in Buckland and speak with a good-for-naught hobbit there by the name of Hodric Bracegirdle. Get a crate of that oily salve he makes and bring it back to me.
'That salve should satisfy the leech.'

'What's that? Oh, that villain Stoutthrush! He's been demanding one thing or another of me ever since I lost that wager to him.
'I suppose I can spare some salve. I'll have to make more soon or I'll run out.'
'Where have you been? Cartwell might have found another supply of salve by now.'
'Where is the salve? If the leecher finds another source of salve, I won't be able to get as high a price.'
Collect a crate of oily salve from Hodric Bracegirdle
Bring the crate of salve to Bruner Stoutthrush
Healing Stores
Leecher Cartwell has ordered some supplies from Bruner Stoutthrush, who has in turn run out of stock.
'Hodric Bracegirdle in Buckland you say? It will be a pleasure not to deal with Stoutthrush the next time I need my stores filled!'
'Ha! That salve will fetch a handsome price from Leecher Cartwell!'

Hodric Bracegirdle lives on the forest side of Brandy Hall in Buckland.
The hobbit Hoderic Bracegirdle supplies Stoutthrush with the healing salve he sells to Leecher Cartwell.

Bruner Stoutthrush does business at the Combe-gate in Bree.
Hodric, not entirely happily, gave you the crate Bruner requested. You should bring it to Stoutthrush straight away.

'There's a pair of fine gentlemen, Mr. Larkspur and Mr. Hawkling, what have taken up residence at Adso Haybank's camp, along the Great East Road north of the Old Forest.
'Yes, sir, fine gentlemen indeed! Hunters of game, great and small. Last time they were through here, Mr. Hawkling asked me to procure them a bit of pipe-weed.
'If you'd be so kind, deliver this cask to them with all due haste. I'm sure Mr. Hawkling will tip you if you're quick about it.'
'So, that ill-favoured fellow, Stoutthrush, finally came through with our pipe-weed. Looks like I owe you for that wager, Larkspur!'
'Have you been to Bree lately? That good-for-naught, Stoutthrush, owes me a cask of pipeweed.'
Bring the pipe-weed to Roger Hawkling
Pipe-weed Delivery
Bruner Stoutthrush, a merchant in Bree, has asked you to deliver an order to two of his customers.

Roger Hawkling can be found at Adso Haybank's camp along the Great East Road, west of Bree, north of the Old Forest.
Stoutthrush wants you to bring the cask of pipe-weed to Roger Hawkling.
Collected stolen family heirlooms (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Ah, what troubled times we live in. Brigands have been raiding people's homes in Archet, Staddle, and Combe. Deplorable! Some of the poor folk have made their way here to Bree and told me their sad tales.
'Now I'd like nothing more than to help them but I'm just not made for adventures. Why don't you track down these villains and bring the stolen family heirlooms to me. Then I can return them to the rightful owners, the poor wretches. Just think of the looks on their faces!
'I hear there are brigands encamped in the Yellow Tree Ruins, south of Staddle; but it may be that some others in the Chetwood are also carrying stolen items.'
'Ah, you've found them! That was a kind deed. Now, let's just hope that I can find the poor people from whom these treasured things were stolen.'
'What are you doing lazing about while people are suffering? Go find those poor people's things so that I can return them! I'd do it myself but I'm just not the sort for such adventures.'
Bring the heirlooms to Bruner Stoutthrush
Collect stolen family heirlooms (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Family Treasures
Bruner Stoutthrush, a disreputable seeming gentleman from Bree, has decided to do a good deed for the refugees from the Blackwold attacks.

The brigands can be found in a large camp in the Yellow Tree Ruins, south of Staddle; but it may be that some others in the Chetwood also carry stolen items.
Whether as an act of beneficence or complete self-interest, Stoutthrush has asked you to collect stolen heirlooms from the brigands and bring them to him at Bree's Combe-gate.
Collected bear-pelts (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Winter will be upon us soon, and folk around here will need to keep warm. Those Southerners keep looting the site here and taking the most important things this camp has, chief among them blankets and pelts for keeping warm.
'I joined Adso here because the pay was good and hunting bear has long been my profession. Bear-hides can be used for good blankets, but I can only hunt so many, and there is need of me to cure the hides.
'If you are willing, there are a great many bears in a hollow just north of Outlaw's Haven. Outlaw's Haven is west and north of Adso's Camp. Get me some hides, and I will make it worth your while.'
'Excellent quality! Once I cure these and prepare them they will make adequate blankets. We will find warmth this winter after all.'
'You are not getting paid until you bring me ten pelts!'
Bring the bear-pelts to Roger Hawkling
Collect bear-pelts (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
A Matter of Warmth

Roger Hawkling agreed to assist Adso Haybank by offering his expertise on hunting bears throughout Bree-land. Since his arrival, Hawkling has seen an increased need for hunting, skinning, and curing bear-hides for blankets -- a commodity often stolen by the brigands.

Bears can be found throughout the southern Bree-fields, but a sizable sloth of bears can be found north of Outlaw's Haven found west and north of Adso's Camp.
Roger Hawkling has asked you to hunt some bears and bring him their pelts.
Collected boar-heads (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Boars can grow quite large and dangerous. The boars of Bree have always been a source of food, and the ones here in the southern Bree-fields are no exception. Adso and others have grown fond of one of my meals, boar's head stew.
'If you could help gather the heads, I can make my delicacy and keep folks here well fed.'
'Ah, a very fine job, to say the least!'
'You are not getting paid until you bring me ten heads!'
Bring the boar-heads to Roger Hawkling
Collect boar-heads (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
A Matter of Feed
Roger Hawkling is a complete hunter using every bit of the animals that he hunts. He has asked you to collect boar's heads to help him with the cooking he does at Adso's camp.

Boars range the wilds around Adso's camp and are strewn throughout the southern Bree-fields.
Roger wants you to thin the growing number of wild boars and bring him their heads. He cooks an amazing delicacy from them.
Collected wolf-pelts (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'You there, we've a wolf-problem which needs addressing. Some time ago, Adso bought a fine, fat milk-cow out of Buckland, but filthy wolves out of the Old Forest stole it, slaughtered it, and dragged it off.
'Hunt down the foul wolves in the northern part of the Old Forest. Bring me pelts as evidence of your work.
'I won't take any old, shabby pelt, mind you. I'll only accept the largest and most lustrous.'
'These are very fine, indeed! Oh yes, I believe I owe you a reward.'
'You are not getting paid until you bring me five pelts!'
Bring the wolf-pelts to Roger Hawkling
Collect wolf-pelts (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Roger Hawkling assists Adso Haybank by supplying the lodge with furs and meat.

There are wolves in the Old Forest.
Roger Hawkling has asked you to help repel the threat of wolves in the area, bringing him their pelts as evidence of your work.

'All the things you've gathered for me are useless, rotten, and ruined. Something queer is going on, what with the animals all upset and the Forest seeming, well, more awake than usual.
'There's a wise, old hobbit, a forester, who oft camps a ways into the Old Forest. Look for him beyond Old Muddyfoot's Hill, which you can find south-east of the Bonfire Glade. Maybe Gilly knows what's going on. I'd appreciate it if you'd talk to him... Gillemin Brandybuck, that's his name.
'I'm worried! We had to burn part of the forest when it got too uppity years back, but this is far worse than it was before. If the Bounders have to start another fire, they might destroy the whole Forest, and then where would we be?'

'Ah, so Toly Brockhouse sent you? Good. I've discovered something very odd happening here in the Old Forest, and you may be able to help! I found a strange glade to the south-east, infested with monstrous spiders. I've never seen the like before... almost makes me believe those stories about old Mad Baggins down Hobbiton way! They made me drop my pack!
'Even that is not the worst of it yet! I saw a tree walking about, covered in scars and looking like every leaf had fallen off like it were the dead of winter. Now, I see some strange things, being here in the Old Forest, but I never seen a tree like this moving through the wood killing every manner of life in its path.
'I tell ya, if it were the Old Man Willow himself come to stalk the Old Forest he would not be so cruel. Something has the forest in a dire state.'
Talk to Gillemin Brandybuck in the Old Forest
New Trouble in the Old Forest
Toly Brockhouse is disturbed by the fact that everything you brought him was spoiled. This, as well as the stirring of the forest creatures, has upset him.
'Please, talk to Gilly Brandybuck for me.'
'Oh, we had parties like this when I was a girl.'
'I hear you're talking to that old forester lately. He's a strange one, going in and out of the old forest all the time.'
'That old forester's a bad influence on the youth! He's convinced that wood-cutter boy it's safe to go into the forest.'
'That's my husband playing the lute. Isn't he talented? He was quite the catch when we were younger, yes he was.'
'I hear tell you went into the Old Forest to help the young wood-cutter. Very brave of you, ${NAME}. You won't find me setting foot in there!'
'I don't know about the Old Forest being haunted, that sounds like hogwash! But I sure wouldn't go running around in there.'
'The season is treating us very well. There'll be plenty of feasting this winter!'
'I've always said that old forester's as mad as the day is long!'

Gillemin Brandybuck's camp is a distance to the south-east in the Old Forest, beyond Old Muddyfoot's Hill.
Toly Brockhouse asked you to seek the counsel of an old forester named Gillemin Brandybuck.
Collected seasoned lumber
Collected savoury mushrooms (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collected bucket of maple sap

'These are strange days! Most hobbits stay away from the Old Forest, but my living depends on it, and I've never had any problems... till now. The forest creatures have all gone strange. I swear the tree-roots themselves moved to trip me up, and now I've sprained my ankle!
'I still need to collect some mushrooms -- they grow in the west part of the forest, between the Bonfire Glade and Bald Hill. Also, please bring in some lumber from my seasoning pile. The pile is to the east past the Bonfire Glade and a little south. And I need some sap from the old maple on Bald Hill, east of the Bonfire Glade.
'I'll gladly split my fee with you! Here, take my bucket for the sap, and thank you kindly!'

'My thanks, friend, for all your... what's this? This sap, it's already gone bad! And my seasoned wood... it's rotted! And these mushrooms... they're poisonous! Friend, you can't be blamed, but all this... it's useless to me!'
'Have you found everything yet?'
Collect seasoned lumber
Collect savoury mushrooms (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collect a bucket of maple sap
Bring the mushrooms, sap, and wood to Toly Brockhouse
The Wood-cutter's Tale
The wood-cutter has sprained his ankle and is unable to finish his chores for the day. He swears that the Old Forest intentionally tripped him.
'Have you found everything yet?'

The mushrooms can be found in the western part of Old Forest, between the Bonfire Glade and Bald Hill. The wood can be collected from the wood-cutter's seasoning pile east of the Bonfire Glade and a little south. The sap can be collected from the old maple growing on Bald Hill, east of the Bonfire Glade.
Because Toly Brockhouse, the wood-cutter, has sprained his ankle, he has asked you to gather mushrooms, wood, and maple sap for him.

Deliver the sap, wood, and mushrooms to Toly Brockhouse near the stables outside of Brandy Hall.
The Old Forest surrendered its bounty to you, now you must return to Toly Brockhouse.

'You are one for a good tale I see. Well then, a good tale I shall tell, I hope. The tree did not look alive, rotten to the core I think and seeking only vengeance. Mayhaps it was one of the tenders of the past spooked by some feeling of dread that washed over it or some such. I know only that it lay beyond the spiders that took my pack.
'It was foul and terrible to see, a great blight in the forest. If something in these woods has stirred them to something greater than mischief, I would first look there.
'You will need to cross the river here and search within the hollow where the spiders make their nest. That was the last spot I saw the tree.'

'I have always thought that Old Gilly was touched when he talked about the trees moving of their own accord, but now you tell me the same thing -- worse, that one talked! We should keep this to ourselves so as not to sow fear among the quieter folk here in Buckland.
'If you have dealt with the threat, then all should be well, and I will do my best to keep a look over my shoulder for any trees closing in upon me as I make my rounds in the Old Forest.
'I am ever... no, we are ever in your debt for stopping this threat from becoming too great a risk. Thank you, ${PLAYER}.'
Discover the source of the Forest's unrest
Talk to Toly Brockhouse
Haunted Forest
Gillemin Brandybuck believes the great tree he found is at the centre of the stirring of the Old Forest.
'I'd wager that spider nest has become a suitable home for that frightening tree. You might want to take some friends and have a look!'

'My word! This is worse than I thought! I've seen the trees move, but never a tree that talks. I don't know anything about witches, but they say those Barrow-downs beyond the Old Forest are haunted... perhaps ghosts haunt the wood now too!
'I've heard rumour that there are -- or were -- great ones even among trees, wicked and bent, who rule the Old Forest like kings. If it's one of these that haunted that old oak, it's no wonder the Forest was disturbed!
'Maybe now that you've put the spirit to rest, the trees will go back to sleep and the animals will calm. Well done... well done, I say! You should go speak with Toly and tell him the good news.'

The spider nest lies near the Willow Glade, to the south of Gillemin's old camp. Search there for signs of the angered tree.
Gillemin told you that the source of the forest's unrest likely lay within the spider hollow beyond the Withywindle River to the south, within the Old Forest.

Return to Toly Brockhouse near the Gate that borders the Old Forest and Buckland.
The dead tree has been slain, and though there is still great evil stirring within the wood, the borders of Buckland should see some manner of ease. You should return to Gillemin Brandybuck with the news.
Defeated fell spirits in the Great Barrow (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'The Age of the Elves is over, ${PLAYER}, and now the time has come for us to pass into the West. But ere we come at last to the Grey Havens beyond the land of the halflings, we wish to do what little we can to help against the Shadow that is once again rising in the East.
'Long ago, the Witch-king of Angmar sent many fell spirits out of Angmar and Rhudaur to turn the Barrow-downs into a place of terror, and we sense that they are again stirring. We fear that more of these spirits have come with the intent of increasing their master's horde in Bree-land. We would have you enter the Great Barrow and send these spirits back to their master. The spirits will likely be found behind a door displaying a skull.
'Othrongroth, the Great Barrow, is a terrible dread place. You should not enter Othrongroth alone, for it is a dark and dangerous place. Take those you can trust.'
'You have done well, ${PLAYER}; nevertheless, we shall sojourn here a short while longer to see that evil does not come to the simple folk of this land.'
Defeat fell spirits in the Great Barrow (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Aradia outside the Great Barrow
Heading West

Three Elves journeying towards the Grey Havens came to the Barrow-downs after sensing the source of great corruption welling within the Great Barrow. Their sojourn into Bree-land will not end until they help cleanse the land of an ancient corruption before passing into the West.
'Go forth with the blessing of the Elves and drive forth the enemies of the Free Peoples from Othrongroth and restore the Barrow-downs to the peace it once knew!'
'The Shadow of Angmar has not been lifted fully from the Barrow-downs, but your efforts were not wholly in vain.'
'Welcome and well met, ${PLAYER}. May the light of Elbereth shine upon your path, no matter how dark it seems.'

Othrongroth, the Great Barrow, is up the hill from the small encampment in the southern Barrow-downs. The fell spirits can be found within Othrongroth behind a door displaying a skull.
As one last favour before leaving Middle-earth, Aradia and her companions would like to help cleanse the Shadow of Angmar from the Barrow-downs. She has asked you to enter Othrongroth and send the fell spirits which dwell there back to their master.

Aradia is camped outside the Great Barrow.
You should return to Aradia with news of your success against the fell spirits of the Great Barrow.
You have rescued Maribell

'Oh, it's terrible! Blake, the brigand-captain who wanted the sword, came and told me he knew Nate was dead and that he knew I had something to do with it! I tried to tell him I didn't, that I would have another sword for him soon, but he wouldn't listen. He said he's taken my daughter, Maribell! If I don't give him another sword -- and soon -- he'll kill her!
'You must save her! Please! Get the sword from Lofar, then go to Blake's camp. It's in the Bree-fields, up north of Bree. I'm sure he'll release my daughter when he has the sword.
'Please hurry! I don't know what I'll do if they harm her.... You should bring a few seasoned warriors with you -- Blake's men are ruthless!'

'Oh, bless you! You've returned my daughter safe to me! I can't thank you enough. You've done so much for me, in more ways than you know!
'While you were away, I busied myself with Lofar's work. I had to do something to keep myself from being overcome with worry. No sooner had I finished the work, than Lofar came over to collect it. He seemed pleased with it -- even admitted that it came close to dwarf-work! He promised to send me more work in the future!
'${PLAYER}, you've saved my family and given me a hope for a brighter future. I can't thank you enough!'

'Those accursed brigands took Thistleway's daughter? This is bad. The sword isn't ready yet! And I know these types of fellows. They won't take \qno\q for an answer. They'll kill that girl!
'You'll have to mount a rescue and free Kenton's daughter! Hurry now! And gather friends... I fear you'll need them to face Blake!'

'Thank you, thank you! I filched the key a while ago, but I was too scared to use it. Now with you here, I can use it, and we can escape.
'Hopefuly we can get away before Blake notices!'
Talk to Lofar Ironband
Find Maribell Thistleway
Talk to Kenton Thistleway at Thornley's Work-site
A Blade For a Life
While you were gathering the materials Kenton needed to finish his work for Lofar Ironband, the brigand Blake took Kenton's daughter captive.
'Have you gotten the sword from Lofar yet? Please hurry, my daughter's life is at stake!'
'The sword was not yet ready? Hurry, do as Lofar said. Make your way to the Brigand's Watch and free my daughter! Please hurry!'
'Don't dawdle here! Go to the Brigand's Watch and rescue that poor girl! Hurry now!'

'Aye, good tidings! Glad no harm came to the lass. While you were away, I went over and collected the work from Kenton, and I must say that I think that Man has the hands of a dwarf. The work was excellent quality, so much so that I think I'll get double for it. I told him he could expect more work from me in the future.
'Seems my kind heart led me to a good find. Thanks to you, that is.'
'I don't know what I would have done if Maribell had been hurt.'
'Thank you again for all you've done, friend!'
'Turns out having that sword stolen was a good thing!'
'Who would have thought a Man could smith as well as a dwarf?'

Lofar can be found at the stone cottage north of the Bree cross-roads.
Kenton Thistleway told you that Blake, the brigand-captain, will kill his daughter unless he gets a new sword. Kenton has asked you to retrieve the sword from Lofar.

Blake's brigand camp is in the Bree-fields, north-west of Bree-town, directly west of Grimbriar's Post.
When you spoke with Lofar, he told you that the sword was not ready yet. He urged you to go to Blake's brigand camp and try to convince the brigand-captain not to harm Kenton's daughter. The sword will be ready soon. He also suggested you take friends in case there was trouble.

Kenton Thistleway can be found at the southern most section of Thornley's Work-site, north along the Greenway.
Blake, the brigand-captain, took Kenton Thistleway's daughter, Maribell, captive. You rescued Maribell, who has returned to Bree. You should return to Kenton with news of your success.

'Hail, good ${PLAYER:lady[f]|fellow}! I was wondering if you could help me with a bit of a problem. It seems that no sooner did I set my latest blade out to cool, than someone stole it!
'I didn't see who made off with the sword, but I suspect it was one of those Man-smiths working out at Thornley's. Their craft is nothing like dwarf-craft, and likely their jealousy of my workmanship moved one of them to steal my blade.
'If I were to ask them about my blade, they would just ignore me. You though, by the look of you, are a great warrior. If you were to ask them about my blade, they'll be honest with you. How about it, can you find my stolen blade?'
'Bah, I don't be needing to steal some dwarf-blade. People like my work... it's quality! You tell that Lofar that I didn't steal his fool sword and try to pass it off as my own!'

'What... a stolen sword? Stolen from a dwarf? I don't know what you are talking about.... Please, go away, I don't know anything about it....'
Kenton mops his brow, nervously.
'Yes, yes, I admit it! I took it. Please don't tell the constable! Please! I did it to save my family! See, a brigand named Nate, he told me that he would hurt my family, unless I made a sword for their captain, Blake. But I didn't have the iron to forge one, and I was desperate to save my family, so I took the dwarf's sword!
'Nate said that before he gave the sword to Blake, he was going to test the blade against the workers at the site of Thornley's silo, just before the graveyard and the boar-hollow. If you find him there, maybe you can convince him to return Lofar's sword and leave my family alone. What do you say?'

'Well, of all the insulting things to say! Those dwarves think that no one can smith as well as them. Well, if being busy means you do quality work, then mine is quality.
'Go tell that fool dwarf that I didn't take his sword!'

'Don't be bothering me with such nonsense. Dwarves always looking down on us, claiming we're jealous. Now they going to start accusing us of stealing?
'Shoo, off with you. I don't have to take this sort of nuisance! I'll complain to the mayor, I will.'
Talk to the smiths of Bree
A Dwarf-made Blade
Lofar Ironband has told you that someone has stolen his newest blade. He has asked you to find out who stole it and return it to him as quickly as possible!
'Have you found my sword yet? It was one of those Man-smiths working at Thornley's who took it, I know it. Go talk to them. Seeing a warrior like yourself will frighten the thief into confessing!'

Most of the smiths of Bree dwell near the West-gate or are working at Thornley's farm along the Greenway.
Lofar has told you that he thinks his latest blade was stolen by one of the Man-smiths. He thinks that a warrior, such as yourself, might intimidate the thief into confessing and returning the stolen blade.
The Barrow-key has been reforged

'I know that I promised you the story of the Great Barrow, but your tale has not yet ended. We need to finish the final chapter.

'Now I'll help that Kenton Thistleway by forging another sword, but with two conditions. The first one is that if the brigand doesn't come around looking for the sword, I get it back. Second, Thistleway gives me a hand and does some of the simpler work I've got piling up around here, while I forge the new blade.
'Here, take these things over to him to work on. The axe needs a new haft, the bellows need new leather, and the helm needs to be reshaped and reinforced. Take that over to Kenton and tell him if he gets it done, and I'm happy with the work, we'll call it even on the cost of the two swords.
'Now off with you, I've got to get to work on this new blade.'

'Bah, he wants iron straps? Kenton always needs something... he is straining the cost of this project. We have no straps in our stores.
'Here, take this old iron pot. He can make some straps out of that.'

'Of course I'll do this work for the dwarf. Here, let me see what he has sent....' Kenton examines the items. 'All of these can be easily repaired, but I don't have the materials to do it. I hate to ask this, but could you help me gather what I need?
'For the helm, ask Foreman Rosethorn over there for a few iron straps for reinforcement. The bellows will need some new leather, and I'll wager that some flawless hides from the boars near Bree will suffice.
'For the axe haft, I need something splendid to set in it. In the past, I've salvaged small gems from old trinkets that I've found in the boar hollow to the east. There are small mounds of ruins there, look like barrow-stones. If you search through the debris, you might find some suitable trinkets.'
'You're back, what did Lofar say? Is he going to make another blade? I have to have something to give Blake if he comes around!'
'Oh, good you've returned! Here, give me those things! While you were away, something terrible happened! Please, I need your help!'
'Have you gathered the materials I need to finish the work for Lofar yet?'
Bring the items for repair to Kenton Thistleway

'What are you doing here? The blade for the new sword isn't ready yet. Off with you! Go talk to that Kenton Thistleway if you must bother someone.'

Kenton Thistleway can be found at the southern end of Thornley's Work-site north along the Greenway.
Lofar Ironband has agreed to forge a new blade for Kenton Thistleway, but in exchange, Lofar has given you three items to take to Kenton for him to repair. The dwarf said that if he likes Kenton's work, he will call it even on the cost of the two swords he is having to make.

Foreman Rosethorn is east under the canopy at Thornley's Work-site. Boars can be found all over on the outskirts of Bree-town. The debris-piles in the boar-hollow to the south-east of Thornley's may contain hidden treasure.

For the bellows, gather some flawless boar hides. Finally, search the debris in the boar-hollow for trinkets Kenton can use to decorate the axe-haft.

Kenton Thistleway can be found at the southern edge of Thornley's Work-site, north along the Greenway.
Kenton Thistleway sent you to gather materials he can use to finish his work for Lofar Ironband. You should return to Kenton at once with the materials you found.

'Now, I want to set matters right. I do! And maybe you can help do that?
'See, like I said before, Nate said that before he gave the sword to Blake, he was going to test the blade against the workers at the unfinished silo site to the east. The site is just before the graveyard and at the top of the hollow of boars.
'If you find him there, maybe you can convince him to return Lofar's sword and leave my family alone. What do you say?'

As you kneel to examine Nate, it is clear that he is quite dead. His hand grasps the hilt of a sword, but the blade has snapped off and is nowhere to be found. You take the hilt from the dead brigand's hand.

'What? The blade broke, and Nate is dead? Oh this is bad... very, very bad. What if Blake comes looking for his sword? I won't have one to give him, and they'll do something terrible to my family! I need a sword to give him! If only I had another blade to give them.
'Wait, do you think Lofar would make another, if you explained the situation to him? My family is in danger! Could you please ask him?'
'Did you see Nate? Did you find the sword?'

'Another blade... he cannot be serious! I am already behind on other work, and now I must forge a new blade for Chief Watcher Grimbriar. \qTime is precious, don't give it away for nothing,\q my father used to say....'
Lofar cuts himself off, lost in thought for a moment, then continues. 'Actually lost my father to brigands a few years back... wouldn't wish that on anyone....
'Bah! Give me that hilt. I must be going soft. I'll do it to keep his family safe, but he's going to have to do something in exchange!'
'So, where's the hilt from my blade? At least I can salvage that for the new sword I have to make.'
Find Nate

'This is not good! In fact, it is downright terrible! All my work... gone! Just like that, quick as you please. Drat and double-drat!
'My notes are missing, and I'm absolutely certain that I placed them in my pack. There was a band of Tarkrîp Orcs from around Cirith Nûr, west to north-west of here in the North Bree-fields, come sniffing around the ruins. That's why I left my pack behind in such a hurry.
'I'm in no shape to take on Orcs. I'm an explorer, not a warrior. Those notes mean everything to me. Could you please find them and return them to me?'

'Orcs! I hate Orcs. Why would they run off with my notes like that? I'll tell you why... just to get my beard in a snarl, I would say!
'Now that my notes are safe, I can continue my research. Lofar will be pleased to know that my work continues unabated.'
'Drat and double-drat! I don't have time to re-write all those notes. If I don't get my original notes back, then I'll have to go home empty-handed!'

'My name is Oddvarr of the Blue Mountains, and I'm here in Bree-land on very important business. The only problem is I misplaced my pack.
'Now, I'm to investigate the old dwarf-ruins that are rumoured to exist here. I'm sure there are important discoveries to be made, and I'm the one to do it! I'm a famous explorer, you see.
'But I digress! If you could help me find that pack, I would be indebted to you. You start looking over yonder north, and I'll search this area and to the south. If you find anything, meet me back here!'

'Ah, there's my old pack! Thank you so much for returning it to me. I would be in a world of hurt if my notes....
'What? My notes are missing! Curse those Orcs! They must have thought they were valuable.'
'Still haven't found anything? Me neither. Let's keep searching.'

'Hullo, there. If you're here about our horses, I'm afraid we don't loan them out to just anyone. These horses are built for speed, not heavy labour. In fact, that reminds me of something.
'A dwarf came to the farm and requested some horses. Not sure what he intended to do with them, but by the looks of him he needed some pack animals. I told him that our horses weren't for hire, and he left in a huff.
'Seemed a bit peculiar... he did not seem quite right in the head. If you have time, perhaps you can check up on the old fellow. I saw him wander off to the ruins south-east of here.'
'Who's that there? Oh, hello! Sorry about that. These old eyes aren't what they used to be. Do you have time to talk? I could use some help.'

You receive the Great Barrow Key

'Greetings, traveller! I came to these barrows to investigate a tale...do you wish to hear it? Have you heard of Othrongroth, the Great Barrow? It lies just at the crest of this hill, a place of dread in Bree-land.
'But it was not always so and perhaps need not remain so. Evil things stir in the Barrow-downs and threaten to turn cautious fear into abject terror. Perhaps you might be interested in restoring the peace of the Barrow-downs? In return, I will place you within my tale of this Great Barrow.
'You will need only a few things to venture deep within these halls to end the evil stirring in its heart. First, you will need friends, and a good many, for the enemies risen now within those halls are greater by far than any who walk these lands. The next are resolve and courage, for the fear these creatures will cast upon you is a thing of legend. The last are my notes...they will let you know what next to do.'

Beyond the tunnels, heavy with mist and dust, down decrepit stairs built in an age before our own lay a door. The door leads to the final resting place of a great leader of Men, long dead, and a powerful shell claimed by the forces loyal to the Witch-king.
It was for safe keeping that the tinkers made the key before his tomb. A great door, replicated several times, to seal the dead beyond the reach of evil. Evil, it seems, proved too potent for mere metal to overcome. Yet something of power must remain for the key is split asunder in a way that reforging requries no tinker skills, one to be made whole at the forge where it was made.
Seek this forge at the foot of those decrepit stairs, in a pit before the great door.

Having obtained the two fragments of the key, you will need to seek the forge.
You will not need the skill to forge weapons, tools, or armour. The key desires to be remade again as it was meant to see that the Dead remained in slumber. Yet the Dead within will do what they can to see that the key is never remade.
When the hammer strikes the anvil your test will begin...pray to the Valar that you have brought friends who are true and stout enough to see you through.

To reconstruct the Barrow-key, you will first need to seek the twin brothers who hold the first fragment. The second lay with a fiend; alive for ages beyond our counting. These are but two fragments of the greater whole.

You found Amlach's corpse

'Oh, what a fine, strong person you are. You remind me of my own poor sons. They've been gone for some time now, and I've heard nary a word from them.
'You see, it started with my son, Malin. He was sure there were treasures out in the Barrow-downs for the taking and left seeking his fortune. After a few days passed, and he didn't come back, I sent his brother, Amlach, out after him, and I've not heard from him either!
'Now I've ventured here with these others after my sons. Amlach said he'd camp at the Dead Man's Perch on the eastern cliffs, but he was not here when we arrived. The others here think he's gone further south. Can you go and look for him?'

'You have returned with Malin's journal! He never let it out of his sight. What evil fate has befallen my sons?
'Amlach... dead? Malin... you must return and search for Malin, ${PLAYER}!'
'The Barrow-downs are a dangerous place. I hope my sons are safe!'

Addie's Missing Sons
Addie Wheatley, an impoverished, elderly woman afraid for her sons, Amlach and Malin, went into the Barrow-downs in search of her treasure-seeking sons.
'I simply must know what happened to my sons. My guides say that there are grey ruins in the south, sometimes mistaken for the Dead Man's Perch, perhaps my son Amlach is there. Please hurry!'
'Perhaps Malin still lives!'
'Oh, my poor Amlach!'

There is a place immediately upon entering that some mistake for the Dead Man's Perch.
Addie Wheatley said that her son Amlach was going to set up camp at the Dead Man's Perch, but was not there when she and her guides arrived. She fears that Amlach became lost in the southern Barrow-downs while searching for his brother, Malin.

You have found Addie Wheatley's son, Amlach, dead within the grave-stones in the southern Barrow-downs. In his hand, you found that he was grasping a tattered journal. You should bring the journal back to Addie, as she will want to know the fate of her sons.

'The Thornleys, farmers and workers of these lands for many generations, have been spared much danger from the brigands. Word has reached me however, that the patriarch of the family has gone missing as he went to deal with foes out of the north.
'If you are willing, I would ask that you visit Rose Thornley, to the west at her home, and ask after the well-being of her husband.'
'Help at last! We must get out of here quickly.'

'Robb has gone missing, but how do you know this? Are you one of those Southerners looking to steal this place? You'll find that we're harder than the land we live on!
'No... you are not... are you? Sent then by the Rangers? Never did trust them much, skulking about in cover of night, never talking proper-like, but I must admit a feeling of gratitude lately. Least-wise since Robb's gone missing.
'Robb went out with his father's sword trying to scare off those brutish men from the North. He left a few days back and has yet to come home. I am running out of excuses to tell the workers. Please, will you find him?'

'What of Malin? Have you found any sign of Malin? Please, find him!'
'Leave me in peace!'
'My boys, my poor boys!'
'Oh, that they never had come to these cursed lands!'

The journal you found seemed to indicate that Malin was taken to the southern Barrow-downs to a barrow overlooking an evil mire.
Addie Wheatley has asked you to search for her other son, Malin.

Addie Wheatley awaits your return at the relative safety offered by her guides at the Dead Man's Perch.
In your search of the Barrow-downs, you found both of Addie's sons, Amlach and Malin, but far too late to be of any help to either. The foul creatures of the Barrow-downs had killed them both and took Malin's remains for their own. You should return to Addie Wheatley and tell her what has happened to her son.
You ran out of time!

'Who are you and what do you want at Hengstacer, ${CLASS}? I have no doubt you have used the services of a stable-master...many of the skilled and trustworthy ones use my steeds to carry travellers such as you. The swiftest horses and ponies have all been foaled here in Hengstacer...there are none swifter of hoof west of the Mountains.
'From your raiment I can tell that you are a traveller...I know the hardships of the long roads between here and the Westfold but that is a story for a later time. If you are looking to learn how to ride a steed, I can teach you, but learning the skills is not an easy task. I have to deliver a fresh steed to the stable-master near the West-gate of Bree-town, but my grooms are busy with other tasks. You can start your training by bringing this Blonde Sorrel steed to the stable-master.
'After you deliver her safely, return to me, and we can discuss your training further.'
<rgb=#FFFF00>Right-Clicking on the 'Mount' vitals display gives you the option to dismount your steed but will also cancel the quest.</rgb>

'Thank you, ${PLAYER}, there are many more travellers down this way than the Bree-folk are used to. The stable-master there has almost been buried with requests for horses. If you are not too sore from that ride I have another task for you.'
Take a fresh Blonde Sorrel steed to the stable-master in Bree-town
Fresh Steed for Bree
Éogar, the owner of Hengstacer has asked for your help in delivering a fresh steed to Bree.
'You should get that horse to Bree at once...my good name is at stake!'
'Hurry on back to Hengstacer and thank Éogar for the fresh Steed!'

The stable-master can be found near the West-gate in Bree-town, south of Hengstacer.
Éogar has asked that you ride a fresh steed out to the stable-master in Bree-town.

Éogar, son of Hadorgar, is located at Hengstacer, north of Bree.
Return to Éogar and inform him that you delivered the horse to the Bree stable-master.
You ran out of time!

'There is one last task I would have you do before I ask you to prove your true quality.
'The stable-master at the dwarf-mines of Othrikar is an old friend of mine. We met along the road when I left the Riddermark after the king's health failed. I had promised I would send him out a fresh steed as soon as I could find a spare rider. I think you now have skill enough to lead your mount through greater perils than the lands of the holbytla. I am a man of my word and this Bay steed must be sent out at once. Before I can give you your final test, I will need you to travel into the North Downs and deliver it.
'Be careful...the road is long, and there are more dangers than loose stones and roots hidden in the hills of the North Downs.'
<rgb=#FFFF00>Right-Clicking on the 'Mount' vitals display gives you the option to dismount your steed but will also cancel the quest.</rgb>
'Well done, ${PLAYER}, that was the last of the horses that I needed to deliver. I hope you did not encounter many difficulties on your journey.'

The stable-master is at the dwarf-mines of Othrikar in the North Downs, far to the north and east of Bree-land.

'You believe you are prepared for riding, caring and training a mount? We shall see, we shall see.
'I have a course that I ride to clear my head and uncloud my thoughts... few have completed it besides myself. Around Hengstacer, I have placed twelve gates. My farmhand was tolerably fast, but if you can ride faster, I will count you a worthy student and teach you the basics. Simply ride through each of the gates on your mount before racing off to the next one. Be careful not to miss any gates! You will have to start over if you run out of time.
'When you are ready to start, you can use the Blood Bay steeds. I will start the count as soon as you accept this challenge, so be ready.'
<rgb=#FFFF00>Right-clicking on the 'Mount' vitals display gives you the option to dismount your steed but will also cancel the quest.</rgb>

'Well done! You possess more skill than I first guessed. I will now explain to you in detail some of the finer points of tending to your steed and controlling her.
'You should now be able to handle a horse on your own, ${PLAYER}.'

'Hello there! Are you here to help out Éogar? If you're looking for work to do around the farm, I could use your help. I need some assistance tracking down some of the ingredients for my famous snapper-soup.
'My soup is made with the meat of the snapper-turtle that lives in the lake to the east of Hengstacer. I usually send one of the hands to fetch me the meat, but they have been so busy, I would feel awful making them hunt down their dinner however slow it may be. I could also use more snapper-shells to make soup-bowls. Better not to waste anything, I always say.
'Hurry along now and fetch the snapper-shells and meat... the farmhands get awful hungry after a hard day of tending the horses, and I would hate to make them wait.'
'Ah! You were able to find the shells and the meat. Wonderful! I will get started on my soup right away.'
'Have you found enough snapper-shells and meat? The southern Meluinen can be found to the north and east of the farm.'
Bring the snapper-shells and meat to Emma Rosethorn

'Are you a jeweller? Do you know one? I really need the services of a jeweller, for I have lost my wedding ring, and I need a replacement before my husband Barton gets back from the Forsaken Inn!
'I don't know where it's gone, but it must have just slipped off my finger. If you can bring me a glittering copper ring to replace it, I'd pay you for your trouble!
'Don't tell Barton I lost the ring! I can't believe I could be so careless!'

'Thank you so much, ${PLAYER}! This ring looks exactly like the ring I lost, and Barton will never know the difference!
'Take these coins and other small items, please! You've really helped me out!'
'If you can get a jeweller to make me a glittering copper ring to replace my wedding ring, I'd really appreciate it, ${PLAYER}!'
Bring glittering copper ring to Verity Tyne
Collect glittering copper ring
Crafting: Verity Tyne Has Lost Her Ring
Verity Tyne has lost the glittering copper ring given to her by her husband Barton, and she is beside herself with worry that he will find out.
'You've been a great help, ${PLAYER}!'
'Don't tell Barton I lost my wedding ring!'

'You've been a big help to me, ${PLAYER}. Something about you tells me you could be a great help to many. If you are looking to further your charitable nature, you may want to speak with Second-watcher Heathstraw in Bree-town.
'Heathstraw is very much in the know of problems facing Bree. What with the refugees coming from the south and all the whispers of the rising dark, I think he's got a fair share of details to keep track of, poor fellow.
'You can find him through the Staddle-gate of Bree standing near the Boar Fountain in the Market Square.'

'Lolo? Used to come here often, he did. Good stout little fellow, good barker and good seller he is. Strange for a hobbit it's true, but then again they say that most hobbits living 'round here is queer.
'His information is correct though, Bree's seen its share of new blood recently, and not all have been of your quality.
'If you need work, I am certain that I can find you something.'
Into Bree

Lolo Wendingway mentioned that Bree-town is a-flutter with rumours of shadows growing and refugees pouring in from the south. He told you to seek out Second-watcher Heathstraw if you were looking to continue your assistance of Bree-land.

Second-watcher Heathstraw can be found near the Boar Fountain in the centre of the Market Square in Bree-town.
Lolo Wendingway mentioned that Second-watcher Heathstraw may have some knowledge of people needing things done throughout Bree.

'You see, the Watchers and I have been stationed in Staddle for only a short time to see to the defence of the Little Folk here. What with all the trouble we've heard Archet and Combe had, it seemed a wise thing to defend Staddle, especially since its crops feed much of Bree-land!
'My superior, Second-watcher Heathstraw, should know of our victories and that Staddle appears to be safe, at least for the moment. I dare not leave my post, though, so could I ask you to bring my report on to Second-watcher Heathstraw in Bree-town? He will probably be near the Boar Fountain. Just head north up the road towards Combe and turn left at the signpost.'

'You bring word from the Watchers in Staddle? Very good, very good. I'll take a look at that report, if you please.
'Ah, you bring good tidings! Goblins were a most unexpected threat, but it seems you dealt with them most expediently. And a good thing too...my men are spread too thinly to defend against all the dangers that have been rising up lately.
'You have my thanks again. Perhaps you may find work here in Bree as well.'
Talk to Second-watcher Heathstraw in Bree
Bring Redweed's report to Second-watcher Heathstraw
Report From Staddle
Watcher Redweed would like word of your victory against the goblins carried to Second-watcher Heathstraw of Bree.
'Second-watcher Heathstraw should be at the Boar Fountain in Bree-town, a short way north and west up the road. He needs to see my report sooner rather than later.'

Second-watcher Heathstraw is at the Boar Fountain in Bree, north and west of Staddle.
Watcher Redweed has asked you to deliver his message to Second-watcher Heathstraw.
Collected bronze buckler

'Have you ever seen such a disappointment, friend ${CLASS}? The Men of this town are wearing armour of such low quality, I'm surprised they can come out in the daylight without embarrassment!
'If Bree-town is attacked, these guards could not hope to prevail. They are badly in need of better armour.
'If you know a metalsmith of any skill, impose upon him for the making of bronze armour and a bronze buckler. It might not be much, but it's a start. Bring them to me and perhaps we will be able to turn these guards into a fighting force after all!'

'These will do nicely, ${PLAYER}. We will surely get this town's guards into shape with equipment like this!
'Here are some coins and other materials as a sign of my appreciation.'
'Have you not found a metalsmith able to pound some bronze scale armour and a bronze buckler yet?'
Bring bronze armour and a bronze buckler to Osur Stouthammer
Collect bronze buckler
Collect bronze armour
Crafting: Bronze for Bree-town
Osur Stouthammer is concerned by what he feels to be the sad state of the armour worn by the guards of the town of Bree and wants to ease the situation.
'You've done well for these people, as ill-equipped as they were!'
'It always pays to know a good metalsmith. Never forget that!'

Osur Stouthammer is in the crafting hall near the Boar Fountain in the town of Bree.
Osur Stouthammer is concerned by the low quality of the armour worn by the guards of the town of Bree and wants you to find a metalsmith willing to make some bronze armour and a bronze buckler he can give to the defenders.

'Gammy Boggs, one of the older hobbits here in Staddle, keeps tabs on all the hobbits on the farms east of the town centre. If you find yourself on the road east, look to the north at the second farm and you'll find Gammy looking out over the rolling pipeweed farms.
'She's always got something to say to passers-by and likely will want something done.'

'Redweed is such a good constable, always has a moment for Gammy, he does. I've been here since I was a little hobbit, through my tweens and on now into my older years. Seen a good crop of hobbit grown, and seen more wander into the hill overlooking Bree or down on to the Buckland or the Shire.
'Staddle is my home and I shall not leave any time. I know all the hobbits here, who has the long hair, curly hair, even the little blonde hobbit --\qhow curious,\q I said, when I seen him!
'Listen to me, prattling on.'
Gammy Boggs

Watcher Redweed mentioned that one of the older hobbits, Gammy Boggs, always bends his ear about the goings-on of the farms of Staddle east of the town centre. She might know a thing or two that needs doing out near the farms.

Gammy Boggs lives on the second farm north of the road east from the centre of Staddle.
Constable Redweed suggested that you speak with Gammy Boggs, if you wish to know more about what is going on in Staddle.

'Staddle is a tranquil place, or normally so. Recently however, the guards and constables have been fearful of the Midgewater Marsh and the tall-folk moving into ruins in the south.
'If you continue following the road to the south, you'll find Staddle centre. Talk to Watcher Redweed there and tell them that I sent you on to help!'

'Hullo there! You've come from Lolo, have you?
'You've come to the right place then friend. There is much happening around Staddle that needs attention and there are too few guards and constables to reach them all.'
On to Staddle
Lolo Wendingway mentioned that the people of Staddle are dealing with some peculiar goings-on and told you to visit Watcher Redweed for more information.

Watcher Redweed can be found in Staddle centre.
Lolo Wendingway advised you to seek out Watcher Redweed to help out with troubles brewing in the surrounding areas.
Defeated goblins at the Sunken Stones (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeated goblins at the Goblinhole Ruins (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Ah, I'm glad to see you! There are goblins in the Midgewater Marshes -- or so it has been told -- and if that is the case, we need to know how many we're dealing with. There are two sets of ruins in the southern expanse of the Marshes. I would ask you to go to these ruins and defeat any goblins you find. If there are goblins near both ruins, we'll have a better idea of how far they've spread.
'The first set of ruins are found south-east of Eldo Swatmidge's farm, east of Staddle. South of his home is a narrow stretch of land that extends into the Marshes and runs right to the Sunken Stones. The Goblinhole Ruins are far to the east and south of those.
'When you are done, check in with Bill Mossfoot. He and another member of the Watch have taken up station out in the eastern marshes, just to the south-east of the Midgewater Ruins.'

'It's as I feared, ${PLAYER}. If the goblins have already spread so far throughout the Midgewater Marshes, they intend to stay.
'If it were not for the spider-infestation at the ruins in the northern stretch of the Marshes, I would expect the goblins to seize those as well.'
Defeat goblins at the Sunken Stones (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeat goblins at the Goblinhole Ruins (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Bill Mossfoot
Scouting the Marshes
Watcher Redweed has asked for your help dealing with goblins that have taken up residence in the Midgewater Marshes.

'If you find goblins at each of the two sets of ruins in the southern Marshes, we will know the goblin-presence is widespread, and a very real threat. Take the east path from the town square until you arrive at the Widow Froghorn's farm, then follow the line of fences north a short way. Swatmidge's farm is down the hill to the east, within view of the Midgewater Marsh.
'South of his farm, a strip of land extends into the bog and runs right to the first set of ruins. The second set is far to the east and south of those.'

The Sunken Stones are located south-east of Eldo Swatmidge's farm, east of Staddle. The Goblinhole Ruins are far to the east and south of the Sunken Stones.
Watcher Redweed wants you to visit two ruins in the southern Midgewater Marshes and defeat goblins at each location to assess the threat the goblins pose to Staddle's well-being.

Bill Mossfoot is stationed south-east of the ruins of Midgewater Marsh.
Redweed told you to report your findings at the ruins to Bill Mossfoot.
Defeated Midgewater sappers in the Midgewater Marsh (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'The increasing number of goblins in the Midgewater Marshes troubles me, true, but I am even more concerned about the weapons some of them appear to be wielding. Swords and axes are bad enough, but the strange oil some of these goblins carry is likely to do much greater damage.
'I am not thinking only of the farms and crops of Staddle, though the threat of fire to food and pipe-weed is immense. I am thinking of the Little Folk. This is a threat beyond them, I think.
'The more of those fire-wielding goblins we can defeat here in the Marshes, the fewer will remain to threaten Staddle. I need you to deal with them, and quickly.'

'The increasing number of goblins in the Midgewater Marshes troubles me, true, but I am even more concerned about the weapons some of them appear to be wielding. Swords and axes are bad enough, but the strange oil some of these goblins carry have the potential to do much greater damage.
'I am not thinking only of the farms and crops of Staddle, though the threat of fire to food and pipe-weed is immense. I am thinking of the Little Folk. This is a threat beyond them, I think.
'The more of those fire-wielding goblins we can defeat in the Marshes, the fewer we may have to contend with here on dry land. I need you to deal with them, and quickly.'

'You have dealt with those goblins? Well done, ${PLAYER}.
'The goblins in the Marshes are still a threat, but now they should be easier to deal with. You have my thanks, ${PLAYER}, and now you have some more coin for your trouble!'

The burning oil carried by the goblin-sappers that have crept into the Midgewater Marshes are particularly worrisome to Bill Mossfoot, charged with the defence of Staddle.

'From your report, it sounds like there are many goblin-sappers in the southern stretch of the Midgewater Marshes. Keep a wary eye out for the guttering of flame in the mist, and you are sure to find them.'

'We might be close to dealing the goblins a decisive blow, ${PLAYER}. The only thing keeping them from fighting among themselves are their loyalty to the two chieftains that are rumoured to lead them: Gurzstâz and Gurzrum.
'If you were to slay these two chieftains, I think the goblins would fall to squabbling among themselves. Such squabbling will leave them unable to mount an attack on Staddle.
'The two chieftains will be fairly close together, somewhere in the Goblinhole Ruins, so that each of them can keep an eye on the other. Be careful... those chieftains will be the strongest of the lot!'

'We might be close to dealing the goblins a decisive blow, ${PLAYER}. The only thing keeping them from fighting amongst themselves are their loyalty to the two chieftains that are rumoured to lead them: Gurzstâz and Gurzrum.
'If you were to slay these two chieftains, I think the goblins would fall to squabbling among themselves. Such squabbling will leave them unable to mount an attack on Staddle.
'The two chieftains will be fairly close together somewhere in the Goblinhole Ruins so that each of them can keep an eye on the other. You may need to gather help...those chieftains will be the strongest of the lot!'

'Well done, ${PLAYER}. With these two dealt with, I think our immediate concerns for Staddle will be closed.
'Return to Watcher Redweed in Staddle and tell him of your success here.'

'You have done very well, ${PLAYER}, very well indeed! I reckon the goblins will be unable to mount an organized attack on the town without the leadership of those goblin-chieftains!
'You have performed a great service for both Men and hobbits, ${PLAYER}, and I'm sure the town of Staddle is in your debt. Now, Bree must know of our -- well I suppose it really is your -- great victory!'

'All of Staddle is in your debt for dealing with those goblins!'

'I'd wager Falco Greenhand is the best gardener in all of Staddle, and that's saying quite a lot. He's very proud of that garden of his, and not without reason -- it's quite a sight! Recently he hasn't been coming 'round to visit like he used to, though, and I'm a little worried about him.
'In fact, I heard that his garden is going through a rough spell, and it might not survive the season! Maybe you can find out what's going on, and put my mind at ease? Falco's farm is south-west of here.
'Falco's a good friend, and I'd hate to see him lose that garden!'
'Not trouble about him? Why I've known old Falco all my life, and I tell you there is naught he cares more about than his garden! I'm not going to stand around and do nothing!'
'Please, leave me alone! I don't need this right now. I have too much else to worry about than some busy-body! Shoo! My problems are not yours. Go tell Gammy that she should stop nosing about!'
Talk to Falco Greenhand at his farm
Talk to Gammy Boggs at her farm
Concern for a Friend
Falco's garden is failing for an unknown reason, causing distress among the people of Staddle.
'I'm not one to talk about friends behind their backs, but old Falco's been acting mighty queer lately. Could you have a talk with him? His farm's to the south-west of here.'
'Please, my problems are my own. Just tell Gammy Boggs not to trouble about me.'

Falco Greenhand's farm lies to the south-west of Gammy Boggs' farm.
Gammy Boggs, the local town gossip, has asked you to find out why Falco's garden is failing.

Gammy Boggs is at her farm, north-east of Falco Greenhand's farm.
Falco Greenhand did not want to trouble you with his problems and asked you to tell Gammy Boggs to stop nosing about.

'Maybe you can talk to some of the other Staddle-folk and see if they know anything about what is happening to Falco's garden? Someone surely knows something that might help!
'You can find them keeping watch over their own farms here in Staddle.
'We need to find out what is happening to Falco's garden, since he will not tell us.'

'Falco's garden? It was a special one, to be sure... seemed able to fight off that mould that showed up in the other farmers' crops. Falco always was the best gardener in Staddle. It's sad if what they say is true, and it's gone to ruin.'
'I haven't seen anything out of the ordinary. There are more animals around as of late, but I don't expect any of them have gotten into Falco's garden, or we'd have heard about it.'
'You say Lily knows what's going on with Falco, but won't say anything? Why, shame on that girl!'

'So Outsiders are now taking an interest in Staddle's business? Well, I did see something a bit strange a few days back. The moon was hiding behind a cloud, so I can't be sure, but I thought I saw several shadows out by the Constable's house, south-east of town. Not sure what that would have to do with old Falco, though.'
'Gammy! I wish I didn't know what I know, but I do. I promised Falco I wouldn't say anything... tell Gammy I wish I could help, but I can't.'
'Gardens? I've trouble enough with my spiders. I can't be of any help to you.'

'There's nothing that I can really tell you about Falco's garden, other than I would do just about anything to know his secret. Everyone else's garden got that awful mould, except his! Most beautiful garden I'd ever laid eyes on, it was.'
Talk to Staddle-folk
Talk to Gammy Boggs at her farm
Eyes of Staddle
Falco's garden is failing for an unknown reason, causing distress among the people of Staddle.
'No, I'm sorry, I don't know anything about what's ailing poor Falco's garden.'
'Falco's garden is his pride and joy... I wish I knew how to help him.'
'Just speak with some of the Staddle-folk mingling about town square or on their farms. One of them might know something about Falco's garden.'
'Falco's garden has always produced some of the finest pipe-weed and produce... even better than mine. There's no telling what has caused the terrible blight.'
'No, no, I can't help you... you just tell Gammy that. I just can't....'
'I don't know anything about gardens, but would you like to buy a spider?'
'Falco was always kind to Gar... I wish there were some way I could help.'

The people of Staddle can be found tending and watching over their farms or in the centre of Staddle.
Gammy Boggs has recommended that you speak to some of the Staddle-folk to learn what happened to Falco's garden.

Gammy Boggs is on the second farm north of the road near the Staddle farms.
The knowledge you gained from the people of Staddle will be of great interest to Gammy Boggs, the town gossip.
You have successfully driven off the brigands

'I think you should speak with Falco again. Maybe those mysterious trespassers are responsible for ruining his poor garden!
'His farm is south-west of here. Quickly, return to him and tell him what you learned.
'I hope the old fool will be more helpful to you this time.'

'Misery me, you've found me out! I made a deal with those wicked ruffians. They promised not to ruin my crops if I paid them. I did for a while, but when I stopped, they were true to their word, such as it is, and they ruined my lovely garden!
'They said their leader would be very unhappy with me if I didn't pay them, and not just that! They said he'd burn down the whole town! I heard that happened up Archet way, and now I'm worried it'll happen to Staddle too!
'I know I should have said something sooner, but I was so afraid -- this Sharkey they're trying to impress sounds fearsome. Perhaps Constable Bolger can help you stop them? Please go tell him at once! His house is south-east of here!'

'The ruffians have been driven off? They won't be coming back?
'Oh, thank you! Thank you, friend! Please accept this small token of my gratitude.
'I will do my best not to mess with Sharkey's Men again. Protecting my garden is not worth destroying my lovely town. Please tell everyone how very, very sorry I am.'

'Old Falco has put us in a tough place, sure enough. The Blackwolds have been lurking about the Chetwood for a while now, but they seem to be getting a little bolder since this Sharkey's showed up. They've started pushing folks like Falco about. Perhaps we can put an end to that here!
'All we can do now is wait....'
Talk to Falco Greenhand at his farm

Falco's garden is failing for an unknown reason, distressing the people of Staddle.
'You should speak to Falco again and tell him what you've found. It could be those mysterious trespassers are responsible for ruining his beautiful garden!'
'Brigands and ruffians? Oh dear, what's old Falco gotten himself into? I'm sure he meant no harm! You'd best hurry along to Constable Bolger. His home is east of here.'

'Far be it from me to spread tales, but I hear you even killed the miscreant that was leading that band of ruffians! That would have been a fine mess for old Falco, sure enough... thank you, ${PLAYER}!'
'I'm so sorry about all this! Please hurry and tell Constable Bolger... I'm sure those ruffians are on their way here!'

Falco Greenhand's farm lies to the south-west of Gammy Boggs' farm.

Constable Bolger's house is located south-east of Falco Greenhand's farm.
Confronted with the truth, Falco Greenhand confessed that he had made an underhanded bargain with ruffians. He has asked you to speak with Constable Bolger and warn him that the brigands are coming to burn the town.

Falco Greenhand's farm lies to the north-west of Constable Bolger's home.

'If Lily knows something, we can likely get her to talk. She'll be coy, as most hobbit-lasses her age are, but if you ask nicely, I am certain that she'll tell you what we need to help poor Falco.
'We need to band together and make certain that Falco gets all the help he can to get through this time.
'Go back to Lily at her farm beneath the hill -- it isn't far down the road to the east -- and try to find out from her what she saw.'

'Big Folk! Bad enough the Men in Archet burned their town, then ran into the Chetwood. I didn't know that there were some near here.
'Oh, Falco... whatever are we to do with you.'

'I told Falco I wouldn't say anything about what I know... but I might be able to tell you without saying anything, then I wouldn't be telling, would I?
'I like flowers, ${PLAYER}, but not just any flowers... I like the flowers that are my namesake. South of my house, down beyond the Yellow Tree, you'll find lilies, red ones!
'Get me a bundle of the lilies and keep your eyes open. If you look where you are, you'll notice the big problem facing poor Falco.'

'If you were looking around yourself down in the south Chetwood you likely noticed all the Big Folk there. Now you know my secret, and I never said a word!
'Oh, thank you for the flowers, ${PLAYER}. They are lovely.
'Now you can tell Gammy Boggs that you know what I know. I hope you can find a way to help poor Falco.'
'If you keep a watchful eye, you may notice that Falco has a \qBig\q problem.'

Gammy Boggs is certain that Falco Greenhand has gotten into some kind of trouble that he cannot get out of, and the cryptic message you received from Lily is not helping to ease her mind.
'Hurry along now! I'll not see a hobbit suffer while I can still be of assistance.'
'Hurry along now! I'll not see a hobbit suffer while I can still be of assistance.'
'Hurry along now! I'll not see a hobbit suffer while I can still be of assistance.'
'Look for my namesake down by the ruins, and you'll find the answer to Falco's problems....'

Lily Underhill can be found outside her home east of Gammy Boggs' home, at the foot of the hill, north of the road.

Collected produce from Asphodel Froghorn

'Asphodel keeps her farm going by selling her goods at the Farmer's Market. I made a deal with Himloc Grouse to pay double what others pay for her fresh vegetables.
'Could you go to her farm, collect the produce she means to sell, and deliver it to Himloc? Be sure to return the money to her when you are done.'

'Eldo didn't send a layabout, did he?
'And he's kind to his dogs? How about that?
'Since you've already proven yourself so useful, why not take this into Staddle and sell it to Himloc Grouse? He'll be in the town square, most likely. Maybe then we can continue our discussion of Eldo Swatmidge's good qualities, of which I am sure you will tell me there are many.'

'So you've got some produce for sale from the Widow Froghorn, do you? Well, I'll be taking it... and here's the payment.
'And before you start thinking I've gone soft in the head, that's double what I usually pay. Eldo Swatmidge and I have a standing agreement, on account of he asked me to pay double for any of the Widow's produce, then he gives me the difference. It's true what they say: a hobbit in love don't have no hobbit-sense at all!
'You bring that payment back to the Widow Froghorn and don't mention the agreement I've got with Swatmidge. That's part of the whole arrangement.'
'Are you here on account of the Widow Froghorn?'
'This seems like a bit much. Are you sure Himloc gave you the right amount? No, don't tell me. I have a feeling Eldo Swatmidge might have something to do with Himloc's generosity.'
'You didn't get any payment from Himloc? That's very unusual.'
Collect produce from Asphodel Froghorn
Bring the basket of vegetables to Himloc Grouse
Bring Himloc's payment to Asphodel Froghorn
Farmer's Market
Eldo Swatmidge is a successful farmer, but he is lonely. He has sought your help to woo his neighbour, the Widow Froghorn.
'If you are going to volunteer your labour, you might as well take my produce to Himloc Grouse.'
'You go take Asphodel's produce to Himloc Grouse in town... and don't forget to mention my kind treatment of my dogs!'

'I told you that you had impressed her! It sounds like we're making progress, yes it does!
'Oh, by the way, I told old Himloc that when he buys produce from Asphodel, he should pay double what he normally would, and I'd pay him the difference. I figured you should know -- don't be surprised when you talk to him!'
'Old Himloc kept up his end of the bargain? Good, good! Well, take that money on to Asphodel now and be sure to mention my good hobbit-sense!'
'You go take that payment back to the Widow Froghorn... but don't you tell her why I paid so much!'

The Widow Froghorn's farm is on the road west and south of Eldo Swatmidge's farm.
Eldo Swatmidge asked you to collect the produce that Asphodel Froghorn means to sell.

Himloc Grouse can usually be found in the town square of Staddle, west of the Widow Froghorn's farm.
Asphodel seems to think highly of you and has asked you to sell some of her produce to Himloc Grouse, the trader.

Widow Froghorn's farm is east of Staddle.
Asphodel Froghorn is waiting for the payment you received from Himloc Grouse for the sale of her vegetables.

'I've noticed my pipe-weed field is rather less robust than it should be. At first I suspected animals had gotten at it -- we have had some troubles with wolves ranging too near the town recently -- but I don't think that is the answer. What would wolves have to do with pipe-weed?
'I think the Blackwold brigands are to blame, ${PLAYER}! Men have had a taste for pipe-weed ever since we taught them the craft, and now I fear these villains have been sneaking in after dark to pinch some of my most promising crop!
'Take this letter to Constable Bolger and ask him what he intends to do about it! You'll find him south-east of here, on the outskirts of Staddle. He must do something. These Men have gone too far!'
'I don't know how many letters from Himloc I can put up with, friend. We had better do something about the brigands that are stealing from his pipe-weed crop before I get another.'
'Do you have something for me?'
Bring Himloc's letter to Constable Bolger
Message for the Constable
Himloc Grouse of Staddle is convinced that the Blackwold brigands have been stealing from his pipe-weed field and wants Constable Bolger to do something about it.

'If Constable Bolger does not do something about the brigands that keep stealing from my fields, I shall be forced to complain to the Watch in Bree about his inability to help the good folk of Staddle!'

Constable Bolger lives to the south-east of Staddle, on the outskirts of the town.
Himloc Grouse has asked you to take a letter to Constable Bolger communicating his concerns about the Blackwolds.
Defeated Blackwold thieves (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'If we don't do something, the Blackwold brigands will keep stealing my pipe-weed, ${PLAYER}! They sneak into my field under cover of darkness and take as many plants as they can carry, but if you can catch them in the act you might be able to put some fear into them!
'My pipe-weed field is on the hill above Eldo Swatmidge's home, east of Staddle, right near the western edge of the Midgewater Marshes. You ought to be able to handle them by yourself.
'The thieves try to steal from me day and night, so you'll want to keep watch for them. And if you see their leader, take care of him as well.'

'You put a stop to those Blackwolds, ${PLAYER}? I'm glad to hear it!
'I think the brigands will get the message to stay away from my pipe-weed from now on, thanks to you! Here, take these coins!'

'You need to stop them! My field is east of Staddle, on the hill above Eldo Swatmidge's home.'
'Those Blackwold villains won't steal my pipe-weed again, thanks to you!'
'My pipe-weed crop won't be going anywhere if I have anything to say about it.'

Himloc Grouse's pipe-weed field is on the hill above Eldo Swatmidge's home, east of Staddle.

Himloc will be pleased to hear that you have prevented the Blackwolds from stealing more of his pipe-weed.

'The Blackwolds have established a camp at Ost Baranor, south and slightly west of here. I suspect they sneak out every night to steal pipe-weed and produce.
'They are probably keeping Himloc's pipe-weed in a barrel somewhere within the ruins. If you can retrieve that barrel and bring it to Himloc, perhaps you will spare me another one of his letters!
'Good luck, ${PLAYER}. I do not relish the idea of more correspondence with an angry Grouse!'

'This is my pipe-weed? Thank you very much, ${PLAYER}! I knew those good-for-nothing Blackwold villains were trying to make off with my prized crop! At least I have these plants back, but... what if they come back and try to steal the rest of it?'

'You recovered the barrel of stolen pipe-weed from the brigands! Quickly, bring that to Himloc Grouse in Staddle! I can almost hear him starting to write a letter of complaint!'
'The ruins where the Blackwolds will have Himloc's pipe-weed are to the south of here, near the Yellow Tree. You can't miss them.'
'The brigands have my stolen pipe-weed in the ruins south of the Yellow Tree? If you can get it back, I'd really appreciate it, ${PLAYER}!'

'I am surprised at how earnest Eldo seems to be! Perhaps I shall give him a chance. A courtship could be just the thing to brighten my days.
'Tell him that I'll consider his courting me, but he'll need to sell his dog, Wanetta. I always come down with the sneezes whenever I am around dogs of her breed, and it is really unbearable.
'Hurry back with his answer! Oh, I'm all a-flutter like a little hobbit-girl!'

'What? He won't sell that dog? Now... now I want him courting me even more! What loyalty, and not even to a person!
'You were right all along, ${PLAYER}. Eldo Swatmidge might not be the most well-dressed hobbit in Staddle, or even the most well-spoken, but he's a good, hard-working, loyal fellow.
'Maybe someday there will be a cure for the sneezes I get around that breed of dog, and then not even Wanetta will keep me from my Eldo! Please go tell him at once, ${PLAYER}.'

'Sell Wanetta? I... I can't. I've had Wanetta here since she was a pup. She's given me litter after litter of good, strong pups. She's my prized dog! I can't sell her! If she was a hobbit and I was a dog, she wouldn't sell me, I know it!
'If that is what Asphodel wants... tell her I can't. I can't do it. Looks like I won't ever be courting the Widow Froghorn. Please don't think me ungrateful for what you've done, but I just can't lose my Wanetta.'

'Really!'
Eldo looks to Wanetta, 'Did you hear that Wanetta? Asphodel said yes!'
'${PLAYER}, I don't know if this is thanks enough for what you've done for me! Take this and know that I'll be everything I promised Asphodel and more!'

Eldo Swatmidge is a successful farmer, but he is lonely. He has sought your help to woo his neighbour, the Widow Froghorn.
'Oh, I'm so excited! Please hurry and tell Mr. Swatmidge so he can make arrangements to sell that dog of his. I can't wait!'
'Eldo's loyalty, generosity, kindness, and caring make him a fine suitor, I think!'
'I hope she understands, but I just can't sell my Wanetta. I just can't!'
'O joy! The Widow Froghorn will let me come a-courting!'
'That Eldo Swatmidge is simply a darling, isn't he?'

Eldo Swatmidge's farm is up the road to the north and east of the Widow Froghorn's farm.
Asphodel Froghorn stated she would allow Eldo to court her, if he was willing to sell his dog. You should return to Eldo Swatmidge with the widow's terms.

Eldo Swatmidge's farm is up the road north and east of the Widow Froghorn's farm.
Asphodel Froghorn found Eldo's loyalty so endearing that she is willing to put up with sniffles and sneezing. You should return to Eldo Swatmidge with the good news.
Collected fennel seeds (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Hoy there, do you know anything about dogs? Gar here has been feeling poorly since yesterday, and he won't eat a bite. I fetched him some fresh water from the well, and he just turns away!
'Maybe you could help me? Eldo Swatmidge knows a fair bit about animals, and he might have an idea about what's wrong with Gar. He lives quite a bit east of town, almost on the edge of the Midgewater Marshes, and I don't think Gar would be up for the walk. Just take the road east out of town to the Widow Froghorn's farm, then north from there and down the hill to the east.
'Eldo is a bit of a queer sort, but he loves dogs, so he can't be that bad, right? I'd appreciate anything he could do to help Gar!'

'What? Gar is sick? Why, he came from one of my Wanetta's litters!
'My own dogs occasionally eat something that doesn't set quite right with 'em. When they do I've got a herbal remedy my grandfather taught me that helps clear it right up. I have most everything on hand, but I'll be needing fennel seeds to finish it up proper.
'Fennel grows in the Midgewater Marshes, but it's hard to find because the Neekerbreekers have a fancy for it. It might be easier to find a Neekerbreeker that still has fennel caught in its pincers, than to find a fresh plant. Bring the seeds back to me, and I will mix up a remedy for Gar.'

'That remedy should make him feel a lot better!
'Good boy, Gar! That'll do it! You must have eaten something that disagreed with you, that's all. Here, you can wash that remedy down with -- hey now, what's this?
'I drew this water from the town well this morning, but it sure smells odd! Is this what made Gar sick?'

'You've brought me the fennel seeds? Good, good, give them here, and I'll boil them up with the rest of this.
'There we go. Take this remedy to Gar and let him drink it. He may not much like it, but make sure he drinks it all the same. He should recover soon.'
'Neekerbreekers in the Midgewater Marshes often get fennel tangled up in their pincers. If you can retrieve some seeds, I can make a remedy that should help Gar.'

Gar sniffs at the herbal remedy, and then laps some of it up. He slowly drinks the rest of the mixture.
Longo looks at you expectantly.
Gar looks at you unhappily. He does seem to be very ill.
Bring the fennel seeds to Eldo Swatmidge
