Ailing Hound
Longo Daegmund's dog Gar appears to have come down ill, and Longo is worried about him.
'You shouldn't dawdle here. Gar needs that remedy I made for him. Go back to Staddle and give it to him.'

'Eldo lives east of Staddle, almost on the edge of the Midgewater Marshes. Take the eastern path from the town square until you reach the widow Froghorn's farm, and follow the line of fences north, then down the hill to the east to Eldo's place.
'If anyone will know what's wrong with Gar, he will. I'm sure of it!'
'You're looking for fennel seeds to help Gar? Thank you, ${PLAYER}, but please hurry! I can't stand to see my poor old dog feeling so down!'
'You've brought a herbal remedy from Eldo? Quickly, give it to Gar! I do hope it helps him!'

Eldo Swatmidge lives east of Staddle and north and east of Widow Froghorn's farm.
Longo Daegmund has asked you to speak with Eldo Swatmidge about his dog's illness and learn if there is some remedy he knows that may cure him.

Neekerbreekers can be found most commonly in the southern Midgewater Marshes. Eldo Swatmidge's farm is west of the Marshes and east of Staddle.
Longo Daegmund sent you to speak with Eldo Swatmidge about a cure for Gar, his dog, but Eldo is missing the fennel seeds he needs to make the remedy. Eldo tells you that the Neekerbreekers have an affinity for fennel, and it may be possible to find some caught in their pincers.

Longo Daegmund and his dog Gar are by Ferdibrand Took's waggon just west of the town square in Staddle.
Eldo has prepared a herbal remedy to cure Longo's dog Gar of the illness troubling him and told you to have the dog drink it.

Longo Daegmund is next to his dog, Gar, by Ferdibrand Took's waggon west of the town square of Staddle.
Longo is waiting expectantly to speak with you.

'This is a fine farm, wouldn't you say? Yes, life has been kind to me. My only regret is that I haven't anyone to share it with!
'I think you might be able to help me, if you're of a mind. The Widow Froghorn lives up the hill to the west, and she's a fine lady, but she won't hear of me courting her. I've been sending letters to her for a while now, asking her to tea, to the dance, to watch o'er my dog... but she refuses every time!
'Now, Widow Froghorn -- Asphodel is her right name -- is always needing help around her farm. Maybe if you lend her a hand, saying a kind word about me now and then, she'll change her mind! Go west up the hill, then turn south by the fence at the top. Her farm is at the cross-roads.'

'Who might you be? Another farmhand Eldo sent to help me? I don't need his help, thank you very much and good day to you!
'No matter how many times I tell him \qno,\q he just won't give up. I swear, there's only one thing he loves, and it's those dogs he raises! If it doesn't bark or have a tail to wag, he doesn't know the first thing about it!'
Talk to Asphodel Froghorn at her farm
Widow's Farmhand
Eldo Swatmidge is a successful farmer, but he is lonely. He has sought your help to woo his neighbour, the Widow Froghorn.
'Asphodel's farm is west of here, closer to Staddle. Go up the hill to the west and turn south at the fence on the top. Don't forget to put in a good word for me every chance you get!'

The Widow Froghorn's farm is west and south of Eldo Swatmidge's farm.
Eldo has asked you to help out around Asphodel Froghorn's farm, taking the opportunity to put in a few good words for him.

'Would you make your way into the woods south of her farm and drive the bears away? This might show her that I am willing to see to her safety and show how caring I can be.
'When you're done, tell her!'

'Sent you again, did he? That Eldo Swatmidge is certainly persistent. I'll give him that, at least.
'He's honest, too? I'm glad you shared that information, ${PLAYER}, because it's certainly important. Or perhaps it isn't.
'Tell him that I appreciate the help around here, but my answer is still no.'

'Still no...? She is fickle, to be sure, but she's the finest lady in Staddle.
'Well, regardless, I think you made another fine impression. You're doing wonderfully, ${PLAYER}.'

'Eldo is surely persistent, and he seems to have a very good heart.'
'You haven't gotten worn out already, have you?'

'I must beg your pardon, but it's been a bit of a trial since I lost my Bodo. If you're here to lend a hand, I won't stop you.
'The pipe-weed is ready for harvest, so if you're still intent on helping out, you can bring it in. It's right there, on the other side of my wheat-field.
'But you should know that I'll not change my mind about old Eldo Swatmidge.'

'I see you've harvested quite a bundle of pipe-weed. You have my thanks -- a helping hand is appreciated, no matter where it comes from.
'You say Eldo is a good, solid hobbit? You would say that, I suppose, being in his employ.'
Asphodel takes the pipe-weed and hands you a folded, sealed note. 'Take this back to your good, solid friend. And don't read it!'
'My pipe-weed is planted on the other side of my wheat field there. You should find some ripe pipe-weed ready to harvest.'

'You're back! How did it go?
'What's this? Refused again! Well... I'm not going to give up! If you go back and tell her some more of my good qualities, I'm sure she'll reconsider. I'm sure of it!
'Did you mention how hard-working I am? I'm an honest fellow, and good to my dogs. They say you can judge the worth of a hobbit by how he treats his dogs, and I treat mine like royalty! You go help her out around the farm some more, and be sure to mention that. Like royalty!'
'Any good news, friend? Will the Widow let me court her?'

'I think there is something wrong with the water in the town well, ${PLAYER}! It certainly smells peculiar, that's for sure, and would explain why Gar has been feeling poorly.

'Go and tell Lily Underhill -- we can't have people drinking from the well until we can clean the water somehow! Lily lives over yonder, east of Boggs' Farm.'

'Longo thinks the well is poisoned? I don't know -- it seems a bit far-fetched. Perhaps he's just imagining it?
'No, no... Longo is many things, but a fool he is not. Who could have done such a terrible thing?
'I have an idea how to fix things, but I'll need your help to make the water safe to drink.'

Unwell Water
Longo Daegmund is convinced that something in the Staddle town well caused Gar's illness.
'You must do something about this foul water before someone else falls ill!'

'There's a wise-woman named Willowsong, who dwells by the Silverwater Spring. She may know a way to clean the befouled water. Draw a bucket of water from the well and bring it to her. Perhaps she'll know what to do.
'Take the road east from the town square to the Widow Froghorn's farm, then south to Constable Bolger's house. The Silverwater Spring is south-east of there.'
'This water smells most foul. Tell me, ${RACE}, why have you brought it to me?'

'I do not know who would do such a thing to the good folk of Staddle, but I know a remedy to cleanse the poison from their well-water.
'Bring me some handfuls of the wildflowers that grow near the Yellow Tree, south-west of the Spring. The blossoms possess a cleansing virtue that will purge the poison from the well.
'The Yellow Tree was a place of peace in times past, but now it is home to fearsome creatures. You must be courageous if you are to collect the flowers I require.'
'Yes, these are just what I needed. This will take but a moment. The water was indeed poisoned, but the blossoms of these wildflowers will drive the poison away.'

'The problem is that my coinpurse was in that pack, which means I can't buy pipe-weed to trade to Burl. Worse, if I don't get it back within the next fifteen minutes, I am sure to miss out on the good prices of pipe-weed in Staddle!

'My pack! You found it, and with time to spare, too! Take this as a token of my thanks, ${PLAYER}.'

'Now that the people of Archet have stood up against the Blackwold brigands, and we've got them on the run here, the tides are turning. Things are returning to normal, and I say it's time I did my part!
'I used to send honey down to Staddle in trade for pipe-weed, a business I'm ready to pick up again. My old trading partner, a hobbit by the name of Lolo Wendingway, used to peddle wares on the road between here and Staddle, to the south. When the Blackwolds came, I'll wager he holed up down there.
'If you happen to be in Staddle and see Lolo, please let him know I would like to renew our partnership!'

'You say you've spoken with Burl Beeman? Oh, this is bad, very bad indeed! I had a good and profitable arrangement with Beeman -- I would purchase pipe-weed from here in Staddle, bring it to Beeman in exchange for honey, and then use the honey to satisfy my outstanding contracts in Staddle.
'But as much as I would like to renew that arrangement, I am unable to do so at the moment! Unless... maybe you could do something for me?'

'These are just the thing, ${PLAYER}! Thank you very much! I'm sure the guards will enjoy their breakfast, and perhaps I will have found my recipe-book in time to make them a second breakfast myself!'

'You are the one that helped the halfling, Dob Sandheaver, are you not? It seems the situation is much graver than I first thought, and it has gone beyond stolen food-bags.
'The giant that attacked Dob is very small for his kind, but he is a giant nonetheless. How and when he wandered down to the borders of the Shire is a mystery, even to one such as myself, who sees many comings and goings unnoticed by other folk. He has begun to waylay many travellers north of Buckland and has even been sighted on the borders of the Bree-fields. At first I was content to watch him and wait, but I see now that he is a great threat.
'I would ask you to gather companions and face Svalfang. We Rangers have protected the borders of the Shire for years, but there are too few of us here to face this foe. I would not have Aragorn return to find the land he guarded for so many years in ruin because of my inaction. Find the giant and drive him forth from these lands.'

'You have defeated the giant? Well done! There have been many strangers lurking on the borders of that peaceful land. I do not doubt he would have caused many more problems than a few scared hobbits, had he not been dealt with.'

'Why hullo there! You're the one everyone has been talking about, yes? Well, I could use your help. I have big problems, and that's a fact! You see, I was on a trip to visit my dad away in Buckland after visiting my brother Gil at Hengstacer. I thought to myself, \qYou should take a shortcut... no use wandering all the way down to the Great East Road and all.\q That's when it all went wrong.
'Now I was walking along quiet as you will until about the time for elevenses, and I felt a dreadful hunger. I came upon an old bit of stonework in the Brandywood and sat myself down for a light snack. All of a sudden, quick as you will, a hefty burly fellow shows up, and with none too kind words mind you. He was much larger than the big folk of Bree... I am afraid I was quite scared of the brute and ran off without my pack!
'The stonework is north of Buckland in the Brandywood. I doubt that this giant Man -- Svalfang I heard him call himself -- will stay in his dreary little hut all day. Maybe you could sneak by and pinch my pack when he is out stomping and doing whatever large folk of his kind do.'

'You found it! You have my thanks. I don't know what I would have done if I hadn't found it.
'It looks like some of the food is a bit crushed and broken, but most of it still looks fine. That's the last time I take another shortcut, and that's a fact!'
'Have you found my pack yet? I lost it outside that stone hut in the Brandywood.'

'I met a traveller the other day, a man who seemed to me to have great wisdom. We spoke for a short time, and he said something that seemed to me of much importance: \qknowledge is the best defence we have against those who would do us harm.\q
'I got to thinking, and I think that traveller was right. We need sharp swords and broad shields, but if we study the deeds of yesteryear, we are sure to draw from them lessons that will serve us well even today!
'I want to instill in the men under my command some of these lessons. If you know a scholar of some skill, he might be able to make sense of the materials of the past and give to you some teaching of past lore. Bring some minor battle-lore and some minor weaponsmithing-lore to me, and I will pay you for the trouble, ${PLAYER}, with coins and other goods.'

'You've brought me some information on the waging of battle and the smithing of weapons, ${PLAYER}? I thank you for it! Only by studying the lessons of the past can we be prepared for the dangers of the present!
'Here are some coins and a few sundries for your trouble, as I promised.'
'If you can find a scholar to put together some minor battle-lore and some minor weaponsmithing-lore, the guards here are sure to benefit from the instruction!'

'If you could kill a few of them, you would be doing this town a great service. The Midgewater Marshes are east of Staddle, beyond Swatmidge's farm.
'When you are done, seek out Edda Twiggins in the south-eastern reaches of the Midgewater Marsh. She will be happy to hear of your progress.'

'Excellent, ${PLAYER}! It will be a while before the Neekerbreeker population again grows to be a threat to Staddle. It is good to know I can rely on you to deal with dangers to the town that do not walk on two legs!

If you confront the Blackwolds' leader at the farm, you might be able to recover some of the valuables they have stolen. Old Bauman's farm is deep in the Chetwood, at the end of the eastward path.

'What is this?
'Rurik? There's a Rurik Fennel living here in Combe. He's a... a locksmith! But why would he be aiding the Blackwolds, ${PLAYER}? Rurik's house is south-west of here, just behind The Comb and Wattle.
'You had best have a talk with Rurik. I will be very interested to know why he's been locking boxes for the Blackwolds. Very interested, indeed.'

Sageford sent you to confront the leader of the Blackwolds at Old Bauman's farm. You found a receipt signed by a 'Rurik' on the Blackwold's body. Constable Sageford will want to know about this.

'Rurik is a locksmith here in Combe. You should show him that receipt and ask him why the brigands appear to be common patrons of his.
'It seems odd that Rurik would be involved, he's a quiet man who keeps to himself mostly. Still we need to investigate every lead carefully.
'You should find him outside his home on the road that runs south past The Comb and Wattle Inn.'

'Yes, my name is Rurik. Yes, I'm a locksmith. What is this about? One of my strongboxes -- recovered from a brigand? -- and a letter? I see....
'I had hoped that I saw the last of the Blackwolds. You must understand, I did not willingly help them. My business is keeping things locked away, so I do not often ask questions of my customers. I filled an order for twenty strongboxes and upon completion was visited by the Blackwolds. One -- a tough fellow -- took my master key and threatened my life if I talked. One of the others with him called him Applewood.
'Please, tell the Constable that any aid was unwilling, and I only stayed silent because I feared for my life.'

'While this doesn't help us get this box open and the valuables returned, it does speak well of Rurik. I feel badly that he felt as though we could not protect him... but with what happened to Archet, I understand his hesitation.
'Let me think a moment on the name he gave us. Scouts are coming and going at all times... one may have mentioned seeing this Applewood.'

'The Blackwold brigands are on the run, no question about it. They're trying to regroup at camps throughout the Chetwood, but they suffered a real defeat at Archet.
'The brigands fled their old encampment up by Archet carrying a large lockbox, which they brought to one of their smaller camps in the Chetwood, north-east of Combe. If we can get our hands on that lockbox, its contents could be used to help those who lost property to the Blackwolds. There are a number of watch-fires along the road, so you'll need to find the right one.
'These villains have a great many debts to repay, ${PLAYER}. If you can return with the lockbox, the folk around here will be better for it.'

'Ah, you have returned with the brigands' lockbox! Now let me see what's inside, and we can sell the valuables to support the survivors of the Blackwold raids throughout the area.
'Locked! I should have guessed as much. Well, until we can find the key, we won't have any luck with this. There seem to be some initials carved in the lock: \qR.F.\q Most unusual.'

'The Blackwold watch-fires along the road in the Chetwood are far to the east, beyond the lumber-camp. When you reach the fence at the guard-house on the hill, cut across the fields to the left and keep walking until you are beneath the trees.
'The lockbox is most likely still at one of the Blackwold watch-fires.'
Bring the lockbox to Constable Sageford
Collect the Blackwold lockbox
Unpaid Debts
Now that the Blackwold brigands have been largely pushed out of Archet, Constable Sageford wants to redistribute their stolen goods to those who suffered at their hands.

The Blackwolds have many camps along the road east and north of Combe. Constable Sageford is in Combe.
Constable Sageford wants you to recover a brigand lockbox from one of the watch-fires in the Chetwood. Its contents can then be used to reimburse those who lost property to the Blackwold.
Collected the fishing pole

'I'm sorry, my mind is miles away. I didn't see you there. Did you help fight off the brigands? My dad did, he... he....' Gail chokes back a sob.
'During the Blackwolds' raid on Archet, someone broke into our house and stole many of our things. I don't care about most of them, but they took my dad's favourite fishing pole! I don't care if I get anything else back, but he wouldn't have wanted some filthy brigand to have it.
'Now that I've moved here to Combe, I've been meaning to ask Constable Wren if she could track down that fishing pole for me. Could you ask her if she has any idea where it might have been taken? She'll be at the guard-house on the hill east of Combe.'

'I have heard that many of the Blackwold brigands, after looting Archet, fled into the Chetwood. It seems that the Blackwold leaders are angry. They feel that the raid might have been more successful if their followers had been less focused on filling their pockets and more on acting together.
'The main encampment is east down the road and then deep into the northern woods. I suspect that many of the Blackwolds can be found within that camp.
'Mayhaps if you search in that area, you might find Gail's lost fishing pole.'

'You've found it! Oh, thank you, thank you!
'I've been thinking that the pole should be given to the waters of my dad's favourite fishing hole: the pond near the Hunter's Lodge in Archet. I think he'd like that.
'Thank you... thank you again!'
'Have you found my dad's fishing pole yet?'
Deliver the fishing pole to Gail Catchpole
Collect the fishing pole
Mourning the Dead
Gail Catchpole's father perished in the flames of The Mad Badger Inn, and many of their belongings were stolen by the Blackwold brigands.
'Gail will be pleased, I am sure, if you recovered her father's fishing pole.'

'I just know Constable Wren will have some idea where the brigand who stole my father's fishing pole has gone! She's usually out in front of the guard-house on the hill east of Combe. Please talk to her.'

Constable Wren can be found at the guard-house on the hill east of Combe.
Gail wants to find the brigands who stole her dead father's favourite fishing pole and retrieve it. She has sent you to ask Constable Wren for information about the brigands and where they might have taken her stolen goods.

The main encampment of the Blackwolds is in the Chetwood, north of the guard-house.
Constable Wren suggested that the brigand who looted the fishing pole belonging to Gail Catchpole's dead father may be near the watering hole beneath the Blackwold main encampment.

'Pardon me, do you think I could take up some o' your time? I haven't had any word o' me son Covell since this brigand nonsense began, and I'm mighty scared that he got caught up in some trouble.
'We lived in Archet till recently, but we had an argument -- I'm sure ye know how boys are -- and Covell left all in a huff. He said he would make his own way, down in Combe, and that's the last I heard o' him. Now that I've come to Combe, I hear he's gone east!
'If ye don't mind, could ye talk to Constable Wren for me? She watches the road east out o' Combe, and maybe she's seen Covell pass.'

'Looking for Covell Woodwright, are you? I've heard something about the boy, but I can't say his mother is going to like it.
'He's joined up with the Blackwolds. He hadn't been in Combe for long when they took him, either. He tried finding work around town, but he didn't have the stamina for hard labour.
'If you can talk to him, you might convince him to give up his new line of \qwork,\q but I doubt it. I wager you'll find him east of Combe, in the Chetwood. Just follow the path from the lumber camp north and east... you're sure to come across a Blackwold camp or two up there.'

'You fought with Covell Woodwright, but he escaped? Well, his sort will not be able to flee forever. I feel the time of the Blackwold brigands is coming to an end.
'It seems I was right, and he will never give up his lawlessness. His mother will not be pleased to hear it.'

'What? Covell has joined those villains in truth? I refuse to believe it! He's a good boy, even if he has a temper. He's a Woodwright, through and through, and would never do such a thing! Ye shouldn't say such horrible things, and to an old woman!
'Ah, what am I saying? I knew the boy had landed hisself in a spot o' trouble. Thank ye... thank ye at the least for finding him.'

'What's that? Me mother sent you to find me?
'I... I don't care! I've never been good at anything in my life, but now I've found something I can do and do right good! You're going to regret coming into Blackwold territory!'
Talk to Covell Woodwright
Reconnecting Ties
Maida Woodwright had an argument with her son Covell, and she has not seen him since. The Blackwold activity in the area has made her nervous, and she is seeking news of him.
'Covell Woodwright is probably with his Blackwold friends in the Chetwood, east of here. It could be that you will convince him to give up his lawless ways, but I rather doubt it.'
'It will not be easy, but you must tell Maida that her son has joined the Blackwold brigands. She should know the truth.'
'I hope Covell didn't get into any trouble! Constable Wren may have seen him pass. She watches the road east out of Combe.'
'Joined up with them Blackwolds? What's a mother to do! I hope ye can find him and convince him to give up them thieving ways!'
'I do hope Covell hasn't gotten into any trouble. Constable Wren at the guard-house on the hill east of Combe might know something.'
'My poor boy. I hope he'll come to his senses.'
'Covell was always a good boy! I don't understand what has come over him.'
'The worst thing about the Blackwolds is that they are normal people who've had a round of bad luck.'
'The story of Covell Woodwright is not unusual. It happens far too often.'

Constable Wren is at the guard-house, east of Combe.
Maida Woodwright has asked that you speak with Constable Wren regarding the whereabouts of her son, Covell.

Covell may be found at one of the Blackwold camps north and east of the Combe lumber camp.
Maida Woodwright sent you to speak with Constable Wren, who suggested that Covell joined the Blackwolds and would likely be found near one of their camps in the Chetwood.

Constable Wren patrols near the guard-house on the hill south of the lumber camp and east of Combe.
You discovered Covell Woodwright on the path leading through the Chetwood, and he attacked you. Though you defeated him, he escaped deeper into the woods. Constable Wren will want to hear of your encounter with the brigand.

Maida Woodwright is back in Combe.
Maida Woodwright must be told that her son Covell has joined the Blackwold brigands.
Collected bronze axe
Collected bronze blades (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'These are dangerous times. Those Blackwold villains are roving through the Chetwood, nearly unchecked! Yes, they suffered a defeat at Archet, but you could just as well call that a defeat for the people who live there! It'll be a long time before the town is rebuilt!
'I need to defend my family from those brigands, and I don't think the constables are up to the task. They mean well, but I trust the strength of my arms more than any well-meaning constable.
'Trouble is, the smiths are tasked with too many duties and their prices are far too high! If you have any connexions, or a weaponsmith that holds you in friendship, I'd pay you reasonable rates for a bronze axe and two bronze blades, and throw in a few sundries as well. The axe will serve me until I can replace the blades of my own sword and my son's with whatever you can bring me. Hurry now! The Chetwood is full of those villainous Blackwolds!'

'You've got a good heart, ${PLAYER}, and I know my whole family thanks you: my wife Kate, my son Nate, and my daughters Piper and Pepper.
'I give you these coins and a few odds and ends for your trouble, and I will get to replacing the blades of my old weapons with these new ones you have brought to me.'
'I need a bronze axe and two bronze blades, ${PLAYER}, if I am to defend my family from the brigands of the Chetwood!'
Bring a bronze axe and two bronze blades to Leighton Howard
Collect bronze axe
Collect bronze blades (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Crafting: Weapons for Leighton Howard
Leighton Howard has asked you to obtain some weapons of bronze with which he can defend his family.
'You have my thanks, and also those of Kate, Nate, Piper, and Pepper, I am sure!'
'Weaponsmiths around here have been making a fortune. Everyone needs weapons!'

Leighton Howard is in the town of Combe, in Bree-land.
Leighton has asked you to obtain a bronze axe and two bronze blades for him, because the local weaponsmiths are charging too much for him to pay, and he needs them to protect his family.
The grove of trees has been cleared
You find nothing of note near this stump
You find nothing of note near this stump
You find nothing of note near this stump

'Me old dad was a robber some years back and got his hands on a good deal o' riches, as I hear it. Constable caught him, but afore he was hanged, me dad told me where he buried his loot! I never needed it afore now, so I was content to let it stay buried. But I figure it's time to get my hands on \qwealth enough to keep you warm and shod,\q as me dear old dad called it. Can you take this pick-axe and dig the treasure up?
'Just take the road east from Combe to Constable Wren's post up by the guard-house. Climb over the hill on the right and walk down to the river-bank, where the Hanging Tree grows -- it'll have an X carved into it.
'You'll be helping me make a new start of things, and you'll have me everlasting thanks!'
'What? They chopped down the Hanging Tree? And ye dug at all the trees with an X? This is terrible! How will I ever find me dad's buried treasure now?'
'Where's the pick-axe?'
Find the Hanging Tree
Dig near stumps in the stump-field (${CURRENT}/${MAX})
Bring the pick-axe back to Ted Pickthorn
Beneath the Hanging Tree
Ted Pickthorn has found himself near penniless and in desperate straits. Rumour of his father's stolen wealth has brought him some hope, however.

'There are many other trees around the Hanging Tree. There were more hangings in those days, and they didn't want children seeing too much, so the surrounding trees helped to hide the robber-hangings from young eyes.
'Take the road east out of Combe, and at Constable Wren's post, head south. The Hanging Tree is on the downward slope of the hill south of the guard-house, on the bank of the river. You'll know it by the X carved into it.'
'All the trees are cut down? Maybe the X is still there. Please see if you can find a tree with the mark. Perhaps we'll get lucky and find my dad's treasure!'

The Hanging Tree sits along the river-bank south of Constable Wren's post, south-east of Combe.
Ted Pickthorn's father was once a robber in the Chetwood and had purportedly garnered a significant amount of wealth. Ted believes his father's ill-gotten gains are buried at the foot of the Hanging Tree. The tree is supposed to be marked with an X.
Although there is no way to tell which stump was once the Hanging Tree, it would not hurt to dig near a few of the stumps in search of the treasure.

Ted Pickthorn can be found on the east side of Combe.
Ted Pickthorn sent you to retrieve his father's loot from beneath the Hanging Tree, but you discovered that the tree, among others, was chopped down by the woodcutters of Combe. You dug at several places on the field, but found no sign of Pickthorn's buried treasure.

'Let me just... hmmm... find the right page. Ah! Here we go. I see, I see. So, you stand in the field of stumps and... hmmm... take this many paces... and then that many strides... of course! I remember! The Hanging Tree was the south-easternmost tree in that bunch. It was standing there closest to the Staddle Falls!
'Now just... hmmm... go back to that stump-field, and you'll find that thing you wanted. What was it you wanted, again? You were digging for something, right? Here, take this pick-axe, it'll make it easier to dig. Least I could do, you finding my ledger and all!'

'Wh-what are these? These boots were buried beneath the Hanging Tree? My dad was a villain to the end! \qWealth enough to keep you warm and shod.\q Shod, indeed!
'Wait... there's something rattling around inside the heel of this one.' Taking a knife from his pocket, Ted slices into the heel, and gold pieces tumble out into his waiting palm.
'Well, I'll be! My dear old dad told me true! \qWealth enough to keep you warm and shod,\q indeed! You have my thanks, ${PLAYER}! With this money, I'll be able to get a new start. I'll do better than my dear old dad, you wait and see!'
'You haven't brought me the treasure my dad buried beneath the Hanging Tree yet! Quick, hurry, before someone else finds it!'
Collect Pickthorn's treasure
Collected Pickthorn's treasure
Bring Pickthorn's boots to Ted Pickthorn
Pickthorn's Treasure
Mason Thorne's ledger revealed the location of the old Hanging Tree. Now you can search for Ted Pickthorn's treasure.
'You found out which stump was the Hanging Tree? Well, what're you standing here for? Go dig up me dad's treasure and bring it back here!'
'I gave you what... hmmm... you wanted to know, didn't I? You should go find... hmmm... whatever it was.'
'Did you find what you... hmmm... wanted? It looks from your face like you... hmmm... did. Good for you!'
'Thanks to my dad, I'll be able to make a new start!'
'I wonder if my dad buried any more treasure around the place?'
'All that for... hmmm... old boots....'
'You ever find that... hmmm... what was it? Tree, was it?'
'Oh, isn't it exciting? Young Ted's sure to do well.'
'It was so nice of you to find Ted's treasure for him!'

The south-easternmost stump in the stump-field -- the one closest to Staddle Falls -- was once the Hanging Tree.
After reading through the ledger you recovered for him, Mason Thorne was able to point you to the location of the Hanging Tree.

Ted Pickthorn is on the east side of Combe.
Following Thorne's instructions, you found the stump of the Hanging Tree. You dug up something buried beneath the stump, but it is not what Ted Pickthorn had led you to believe. His father's treasure appears to be a pair of old boots.
Collected Mason Thorne's ledger

'Maybe the woodcutters at the lumber-camp up east of here remember which tree was the Hanging Tree! ${PLAYER}, you've got to have a word with Mason Thorne, the Man in charge there. He just has to remember which o' the stumps used to be the Hanging Tree. He just has to!
'The lumber-camp is along the road, north o' the Big House. Please, I need that money to make a new start for meself.'

'The Hanging Tree? Oh, I remember seeing a few... hmm... hangings in my day. I... hmmm... do believe I wrote the site o' the Hanging Tree down in my ledger. I write down all the things I want to remember. So I can just look it up in....
'Well... hmmm... bless me! I think I dropped my ledger in the woods not far from here. Yes, I remember! We were surprised by some o' those Blackwolds, and I dropped my ledger on the road. I'd wager a captain o' those brigands picked it up!
'There are quite a few camp-fires to the north and east, along the forested road. You might find my ledger on one o' them Blackwolds! Bring it back here... hmmm... and I'll look up that thing you wanted to know about. A tree, was it?'
'Ah, you found my ledger! Now I can find that... hmmm... thing you wanted!'

'I expect a... hmmm... Blackwold has my ledger. One o' them captains is probably using it to plan their movements in the Chetwood! They're camped to the east. You'll have to get it from them, if you want to know... hmmm... where that tree is.'
Talk to Mason Thorne at the Combe lumber-camp
Bring the ledger to Mason Thorne
Collect Mason Thorne's ledger
The Logger's Ledger
Ted Pickthorn was greatly distressed when you told him the Hanging Tree and all the trees surrounding it had been chopped down.

'You tell those woodcutters at the lumber-camp that they can't go around chopping down trees willy-nilly like that!
'I realize that the people of Combe depend on the sale of that wood to get by, but this is me dad's legacy we're talking about! How am I ever going to find it now without digging holes up and down the Chetwood?'

'You say the site o' the Hanging Tree is inside Mason's ledger? Good, good! I'd love to see that ledger, uh, well... truth is, I can't read. Once you've got the ledger, you best get old Thorne to look it up.'

Mason Thorne is at the lumber-camp, north and east of the guard-house.
Ted Pickthorn asked you to speak with Mason Thorne, the foreman at the Combe lumber-camp. He may recall which tree had been the Hanging Tree.

Mason Thorne awaits you at the lumber-camp that lies east and north of Combe, south of the Chetwood.
Thorne sent you to retrieve his ledger from the Blackwold brigands encamped along the road. You should return the ledger to him at once.

'I look at you, ${PLAYER}, and I see a blank canvas, an uncarved block of wood, an untempered blade, an unread book... any number of things that have the potential for greatness, but are still waiting for that potential to be realized.
'I look around at my home, and I see wreckage, a memory of the comfort that this town once had. It can have that peace and comfort again, ${PLAYER}, if those like you will rise to the challenge! Skilled hands must be kept busy if they are to improve in their craft!
'My brother Roderick stands near the Craft Hall in Combe, south of Archet. From the Combe town centre, take the left path as it climbs up the hill. You'll see my brother part of the way up the hill. Tell him that you wish to learn a crafter's profession. The towns of Bree-land can only benefit from the application of your skills!'

'My brother sent you, eh? As well he should! The business up in Archet is unfortunate, but it serves to remind us of the importance of skilled crafters. It will take a great deal of labour to rebuild Archet and supply the people of Bree-land with everything they need to prosper.
'The Mistress of Apprentices to my left can help you choose professions in which to specialize. Choose your professions with care, because you will expend a great deal of time and energy improving your skills!
'Once the Mistress of Apprentices has welcomed you to your chosen professions, be sure to speak with the Provisioner within the Craft Hall. She can sell you the tools of your trade -- every profession has its own, so be not overshy with your coinpurse! The novices will be happy to sell you any recipes you might wish to have, though I can tell you now that you will already know how to make a thing or two.
'Equip the crafting tools you plan on using and find an appropriate facility -- the Craft Hall has a forge, workbench, and oven available for your use -- and begin practising your skills! You will advance in your chosen professions as you practise and seek out the teachings of others in the field. I hope you will become a skilled crafter, ${PLAYER}, and that it will bring profit to you and to the Bree-land.'
Crafting: Strong of Arm and Sharp of Mind
Following the burning of Archet, Edward Carver and his brother Roderick are hoping to encourage all those with potential to take up crafting professions for the good of the Free Peoples.

'Speak to my brother Roderick in Combe, to the south if you're interested in learning a profession, ${PLAYER}. When you arrive in the town centre, take the left path as it climbs partway up the hill, and you should see him right away.'
'I hope your crafting successes bring prosperity to the region!'
'The Craft Hall of Combe is a gathering place for skilled craftsmen.'
'If you watch the craftsmen at work, you are certain to have a greater appreciation for their skills.'
'The Craft Hall in Combe is south of Archet. Head east from the Combe town centre.'
'It is important to gather the finest materials with which to craft. This is true of people as well!'

Roderick Carver is by the Craft Hall in Combe, south of Archet. The left path from the Combe town centre climbs up the hill past the Craft Hall.
Edward Carver wants you to speak to his brother Roderick about taking up a crafting profession.
Collected padded gloves

'I work up at the lumber-camp most days, and I'll tell you this: I'm always getting splinters. I hate it! These tiny little pieces of wood are always flying up from the wood as we cut it, and they get their revenge through annoyance! Small annoyances, to be sure, but after a full day of it, you'd be sick to death of the things, and I've been working there going on three weeks now!
'And that's not all! The axes we use have wooden handles, and if you don't get splinters from gripping those things, then I'm a dwarf! I'm just about at the end of my wits!
'If you know a tailor of even small skill, I could do with a pair of padded gloves. I'll pay you for the trouble, of course, with coins and a few materials, and I'll be in your debt!'

'You've brought me some padded gloves, haven't you? Let me see them!
'Ah, these are just the thing, ${PLAYER}! I'd like to see the splinters from my axe-hilt get through these! Or rather, I wouldn't!
'These things aren't much, but I hope you can use them for something as useful as these gloves you have given me!'
'Find a tailor for me, ${PLAYER}, and fast! I need some padded gloves or those thrice-cursed splinters will drive me right out of work!'
Bring padded gloves to Geoffrey Fuller
Collect padded gloves
Crafting: Geoffrey Fuller Hates Splinters
Geoffrey Fuller has a real problem with the splinters he gets daily from working at the Combe lumber-camp.
'You saved my job at the lumber-camp, ${PLAYER}. Those splinters have met their match!'
'Those gloves were just the thing! I thank you again!'

Geoffrey Fuller is in the village of Combe.
Geoffrey is sick to death of the splinters he encounters every day during his work at the lumber-camp and has asked if you can bring him some padded gloves. A tailor should be able to make the gloves.
Defeated diseased Bristlehides (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Ah, a fine day to you! It's good to see the backs of the Blackwolds broken and peace settling over Archet once more. Now we can concern ourselves with less dire problems!
'Actually, you might be able to help with one of those problems, if you are interested. There seems to be an illness spreading among the local boars. And a terrible affliction it must be, for the beasts are more hostile than normal!
'We really must put an end to this illness, and the only way is to slay those afflicted. Would you do this?'

'Ah, you've taken care of the poor, blighted creatures. Every boar that has caught that foul plague will, in the end, have to be destroyed, but the few you've dealt with will slow the spread of the plague.
'Thank you!'
Defeat diseased Bristlehides (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Disease Among the Boars

Constable Thistlewool is troubled by the disease spreading through the boars in the wake of the destruction wrought on Archet. The boars must be destroyed before they infect the other wildlife and eradicate the diminished food supply in Archet.

'Are you looking for those diseased boars? They should be roaming south and east of the gate.
'It may seem a bit harsh, slaying the beasts without any concern for their meat, but the spread of that illness is to slay those afflicted. It is a sad duty, but one that must be done!'

Diseased boars roam the lands to the south and east of Archet's gate.
Constable Thistlewool thinks that the best way to end the disease afflicting the local boars is to slay those already infected.

Constable Thistlewool can be found near the ruins of The Mad Badger Inn in Archet.
Constable Thistlewool will wish to hear of your success.
Collected Builder Earur's toolbox

'Working with wood has always been my trade, so I thought to put my hands to the rebuilding of Archet. I had loaded up my tools and set out, when suddenly this mad boar came out of nowhere and overturned my cart!
'It was all my son Borin and I could do to make it here to Archet, and we had to leave the tools in the wreckage of the cart! If you head south to the gate that leads to Combe, you might be able to recover my toolbox. I'd really appreciate it, and the folk of Archet are sure to be better for it as well -- the sooner I can get started, the sooner this town will be back to the way it was!
'Watch out for that boar, though. You might be able to get my toolbox without attracting his attention, but you'd need more luck than I have to manage it!'
'You have my thanks, ${PLAYER} -- now Borin and I can get to work rebuilding this town. Take these coins for your trouble.'
'I'd really appreciate it if you could recover the toolbox from the wreckage of my cart. It's south of Archet, near the gate to Combe, but be careful -- that mad boar might still be nearby!'
Bring toolbox to Builder Earur
Collect Builder Earur's toolbox
Builder Earur
Builder Earur has asked you to recover the tools he lost when a mad boar overturned his cart on the road south of Archet.
'We'll have Archet rebuilt as good as new in no time!'
'I wonder what drove that boar mad? I've never seen anything like that before!'

Builder Earur's cart was overturned south of Archet, near the gate to Combe. Builder Earur is in Archet, north of the overturned cart.
Builder Earur has asked you to recover the toolbox he left in the wreckage of his cart, overturned by a mad boar south of Archet.

'Supplies here in Archet are limited and will certainly not suffice to repair the damage wrought upon the village. Now that I have my tools, I will be able to begin shoring the fences and repairing the buildings where I can.
'Archet will need more lumber if it is to recover completely from this attack. If you find yourself in Combe, to the south, seek out Taylor Green and let him know that I will need another order of wood from the lumber yard.
'If you've not been there before, listen well. The Combe Lumber Yard can be found by following the road south. Pass through the gate toward Combe and follow the road east up the hill. It will bend softly to the north east towards the Chetwood. There, in a soft dip before the North Chetwood you should find Taylor Green.'

'Archet's woes did not escape us here in Combe, and it's good what Earur is doing, no doubt in that. But the evil of the Blackwold has spread and now rests in the same wood where we need to collect the wood for Archet.
'I will see that we do what we can, but as you can see, we've troubles of our own.'
Message to Taylor Green

Earur wishes to aid the people of Archet and believes that there are enough supplies to begin the rebuilding process. To ensure that supplies do not dwindle too quickly he directed you to visit Taylor Green at the Combe Lumber Yard.
'Hurry along now. I'll get to work on what I can, but the lumber will not last long. Find Taylor Green at the Lumber yard east and north from the centre of Combe.'

Tell Taylor Green at the Lumber Mill in Combe that Builder Earur needs more wood in Archet.
Builder Earur mentioned that Archet would need more wood to completely rebuild. He asked you to visit the Combe Lumber Yard and tell Taylor Green that Archet needs more wood.
Gathered kingsfoil leaves (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Oh, hello! Thank you again for your help the other night. I shudder to think what might have happened if you hadn't freed me!
'While he's putting on a brave face, I am quite worried about Amdir's knife-wound. I asked how I could help, and he told me of some sort of remedy from the Old Kings involving some plant called \qathelas.\q He said I might know it as kingsfoil, but I've always thought that was naught but a weed. He says that some grows outside of Archet, but I'm afraid of the wolves and Men that prowl out there.
'Amdir said the kingsfoil could be found south of Archet, near some old ruins the men call \qBronwe's Folly.\q After you gather some of the leaves, could you bring them back here to me?'
'Thank you! I hope the draught Amdir told me of will help him. I wouldn't have thought such a small wound would have caused him so much pain!'
'Do you have those kingsfoil leaves I asked for? Please, do hurry! I hate to think of that brave Amdir in such pain.'
Gather kingsfoil leaves (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring the kingsfoil leaves to Celandine Brandybuck
Must be completed prior to the \qIntroduction.\q
Intro: Remedy of the Old Kings
The Ranger Amdir told you that he had asked Celandine Brandybuck to gather an herb called \qathelas\q to make a remedy for his wound, in case the blade was poisoned.
'Kingsfoil grows to the south, near some old ruins the men call Bronwe's Folly. You should hurry...Amdir doesn't look too well.'
'I do hope that remedy helps. Amdir is so pale!'
'I owe Amdir so much for saving my life. I don't know what I'd do if he didn't get better.'

Kingsfoil grows south of Archet, near some old ruins called Bronwe's Folly.
Celandine Brandybuck, too frightened to pass beyond the gates of Archet, has asked you to collect kingsfoil leaves for her, so that she can prepare the remedy Amdir asked her to make.

Celandine Brandybuck can be found with Amdir outside The Mad Badger Inn in Archet.
You have gathered enough leaves for Amdir's remedy. You should return with them to Celandine Brandybuck.
Defeated wolves at the wolf-den (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Combe has always relied on this lumber camp for her livelihood, and now the people of Archet will be relying on us to supply the wood to rebuild their town, I expect. There's no shortage of work, that much is certain!
'We'll need to start taking down some of the trees to the north-east, along the cliffs, but there's a wolf-den up that way that endangers our workers!
'Could you deal with those wolves for me? It's not safe to chop down trees near there, and I'm afraid we might lose some of our best loggers. Follow the cliff wall. You'll see the wolves, or they'll see you.'

'You took care of the wolves! That will make harvesting the trees by that den much safer. Rebuilding the burned buildings in Archet will require more wood than we have, and that's only one village!
'I don't think the Blackwolds have the numbers to try anything funny around Combe, but there's still Staddle. Too many raids, and we'll need to cut down the whole Chetwood to make the repairs!'
Defeat wolves at the wolf-den (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Den of Wolves
Woodcutters from Combe moving further into the Chetwood in search of quality lumber are seeking protection from the local wildlife.
'The wolf-den is north-east of here. Just follow the bend of the cliff wall, and you'll see it. It's not far.'
'Thank you for dealing with the wolves. It should be safer for us to do our jobs now.'
'That wolf den caused us a great deal of trouble before you showed up.'

The wolf-den is set in the cliff wall north-east of the lumber camp.
Woodcutter Taylor Green is concerned that the wolves roaming the woods to the north-east may be a threat to the woodcutters and has asked you to cull their numbers.

Woodcutter Taylor Green waits at the lumber camp to the south-west, north of the guard-house.
As Woodcutter Green requested, you put the fear of Men into the wolves of the Chetwood. He will be pleased to hear of your success.
Collected Sally's chain

'Have you heard that Archet gave them Blackwold villains what-for? Kicked 'em right out, they did, and good on 'em! If little old Archet can manage it, I say Combe can do one better, and sweep them Blackwolds out o' the Chetwood for good!
'Now I lost my Sally's chain when them brigands took over my farm. She's been gone for many a year, but that chain always did bring me comfort. One o' them Blackwolds probably picked it up, and I want it back! Farm's far to the east -- just follow the road past all them brigand campfires.
'Eh, what's that? No, it's a chain, not a necklace. What a queer question.'

'You found my Sally's chain and showed those Blackwold villains a thing or two, I don't doubt it! A lifetime o' thanks, ${PLAYER}!
'Ah, Sally was a good hound. We'd go hunting in the fall, and she could sniff out a coney from what seemed near a mile! It's good to have her chain back. It's all I've got left o' her, now.
'Take these coins for your trouble, ${PLAYER}, with my thanks.'
'My old farm is east of here, deep in the Chetwood. You'll pass by a lot of those brigand camps on the road, and the farm is on a small rise.'
Bring Sally's chain to Old Bauman
Collect Sally's chain
Old Bauman's Farm
The Blackwold brigands seized Old Bauman's farm during the early days of their uprising.
'I can hear her barking, barking away at some old squirrel. You get 'em, Sally! Ha ha!'
'Sally was a good dog, and no mistake.'

Old Bauman's farm lies far to the east of Combe, beyond the brigand camps in the Chetwood, at the end of the eastward path. Old Bauman is at the logging camp, south of the Chetwood, east of Combe.
Old Bauman lost his farm to the Blackwolds when they retreated from Archet, and he would like you to go there and retrieve his Sally's chain for him.
Collected Filbert's handkerchief

'My Uncle Filbert and I were having tea and discussing the state of things in Bree-land -- about how the folk in Archet showed the Blackwold brigands a thing or two -- when Uncle Filbert stood up and said, \qSomeone ought do something about these villains. I'm going to give them a piece of my mind.\q And then he left, without even finishing his tea!
'Up the road in the woods east of this camp, past the brigands' watch-fires, there's some ruins where the Blackwolds are holed up. Uncle Filbert has probably gone there to have a word with them. Though I don't think he will make the full journey, he's not as young as he once was.
'If he has, he's likely got himself into trouble. I dare go no further to search for him, but could you go look for him and make sure he's all right?'

'It's good to hear that Uncle Filbert is all right. He always says that I'll develop good hobbit-sense when I get older, but if he's any example, I'm not sure I will!
'Thank you for looking in on him, ${PLAYER}.'

'Finally, someone respectable! I was beginning to think no one out here in the woods had any manners! I simply couldn't stand by any longer while the Blackwolds have their way in the Chetwood! I marched right in and told them just what I think of their sort.
'They laughed me right out of their camp! \qGo back to Hobbiton, little boy!\q they said to me! I've never been spoke to like this, never! I wanted to leave, something in that big ruin is just a bit off, I say!
'One ruffian, Cole Sickleleaf -- he used to be a nice boy -- took my handkerchief. Could you bring it back to me? He ran off to the ruins all the way to the east, between the frightening ruins to the north and that Skunkwood's farm.'

'You, at least, have some decency. I thank you very much for returning my handkerchief and bid you a good day, as civilized folk are wont to do!
'I'm going to stay here and keep an eye on these impolite troublemakers. Maybe it's the Tookish blood I get from my mother's side of the family, but it'll take more than insults to send me back to town unsatisfied! Perhaps my presence here will remind these ruffians what it means to live in Bree-land!
'If you can tell my nephew, Posco, that I'm fine, I'd appreciate it. Good day!'
'One of those brigands inside the ruins has picked up my handkerchief. I just know it!'
Bring the handkerchief to Filbert Burrows
Collect Filbert's handkerchief
Posco's Uncle
Posco Burrows is concerned that his uncle, Filbert Burrows, has gone deep into the Chetwood to 'have a word' with the Blackwold brigands and wants to make sure he has not gotten himself into trouble.
'Uncle Filbert is probably sitting on a stump or rock right now! I would wager he never made it by the split in the road!'
'Have you got my handkerchief yet?'
'I'm going to keep an eye on these Blackwold villains. I don't trust 'em one bit! You go back to the Lumber Camp by Combe and tell my nephew Posco that everything's fine, and I'll be back soon.'
'It won't be long before these Blackwold brigands are kicked out of the Chetwood, if there's any justice!'
'Can you believe the brass of these Blackwold brigands?'
'Uncle Filbert is sure to get himself into trouble, sooner or later.'
'Uncle Filbert is a grand hobbit, but he's always challenging authority.'

Filbert Burrows should be somewhere along the road east of Combe heading towards the Chetwood.
Posco Burrows has asked you to look for his uncle, Filbert, and make sure he is unharmed.

Cole Sickleleaf is at the ruins between the main Blackwold encampment and Skunkwood's Farm.
You found Posco Burrow's uncle, Filbert, sitting on a stump at the cross-roads in the Chetwood. He wants you to collect a handkerchief taken by Cole Sickleleaf.

Filbert Burrows is waiting at the cross-roads in the Chetwood.
You should return Filbert Burrow's handkerchief to him and convince him to leave the area.

Posco Burrows is waiting for you at the Lumber Camp by Combe.
Filbert Burrows, determined to remain where he is until the Blackwolds relent, has asked you to return to Combe to tell his nephew, Posco Burrows, that he is fine.
Collected rowan hammer
Collected rowan haft (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Hello there, do you have a moment? I'm sorry to bother you, but I thought I would ask this of you, just in case you know something about woodworking.
'Mason Thorne has charged me with purchasing supplies for the camp here, but I've had a difficult time finding woodworkers willing to sell me some of the supplies we need.
'If you don't mind, could you bring me some supplies made of rowan wood? A rowan hammer and some rowan hafts would be perfect. I'd really appreciate it, and I'd pay you for them, of course, with coins and some odds and ends!'
'You have the items crafted from rowan wood I requested? Thank you so much! These look to be just what Mason wanted me to procure for the lumber-camp. I'll pay you, just as we agreed. Here you go.'

'No luck finding someone to supply rowan hammers and hafts yet? Me either! You'd think that Combe would be crawling with woodworkers, but it seems that everyone is out of stock or is just charging too much!'
Bring a rowan hammer and three rowan hafts to Ember Hayes
Collect rowan hammer
Collect rowan haft (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Crafting: Supplies for the Lumber-camp
The Combe lumber-camp is in need of supplies with which its workers can increase the production of useable timber.
'Thank you for the supplies.'
'Thank you again for obtaining the supplies I needed.'

Ember Hayes is at the Combe lumber-camp.
Ember has said she would pay you for a rowan hammer and three rowan hafts, if you could bring them to her. A woodworker should be able to make these items.
Defeated spiders at the Old East Path (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Aye, you might do. Interested in some work? See, I sent one of Jon Brackenbrook's hunters to clear out some spiders that have overrun the Old East Path west of here, but he's not returned.
'Fool probably went off to get an ale at the Mad Badger instead of doing what I asked! And he took my best axe, at that. Since the rascal's not done his job, I'll need you to go out to the Old East Path and clear those filthy spiders away from it.
'You ought to search for that hunter while you're there, in case he's actually trying to do his duty and gotten himself into a pickle. Not that I'm too worried about him, but I want that axe back!'

The puncture marks on the neck of the hunter reveal that he fell victim to the poison of the spiders on the Old East Path. In his hand, you see the axe Atli Spider-bane spoke of. You take the axe from his hand.
'The poor fellow...is dead? And I spoke so ill of him. I'll never forgive myself! Those spiders will pay, I tell you!'
'Do you have my axe? If that rascal hunter has lost it, I'll feed him his innards.'
Defeat spiders at the Old East Path (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Search for the missing hunter
Bring the axe to Atli Spider-bane

Spiders at the Walls
Atli Spider-bane asked one of Jon Brackenbrook's hunters to clear out some of the spiders which have overrun the Old East Path, but he has yet to return.
'Spiders are filthy creatures, and evil. They've choked up the Old East Path leading from Archet and need to be removed.'

The Old East Path is west of the hunter's lodge.
Suspecting that Jon Brackenbrook's hunter went off for an ale instead of the duty he was hired for, Atli asked you to go in and clear out the spiders. He also mentioned that you ought to search for the missing hunter, while you were out there.

Atli Spider-bane can be found out front of the hunter's lodge.

Collected Ann Granger's satchel

'Good day, pleasure to meet you. You know, I heard a bit about your adventures, and it got me wondering if you might do me a favour.
'You see, I was chased off my farm by those Blackwolds a while back, and in my flight, I dropped my satchel, which contained some valuables. Well, as I looked back, I saw one of those brigands pick it up!
'I joined up with the guard when I made it to Archet, but now I'm stuck watching this lodge and can't get back what's mine! I'd be most grateful if you could go to Blackwolds' Roost to the south of here and get my satchel back!'
'You found my satchel! I didn't think I'd ever see this thing again. Thank you!'
'The Blackwolds have a big encampment in some ruins south of the Hunter's Lodge. You should find my satchel there.'
Bring the satchel to Ann Granger
Collect Ann Granger's satchel
Stolen Treasures
When Ann Granger, a member of Captain Brackenbrook's garrison, was run off of her land by the Blackwolds, she lost a satchel containing things that were valuable to her.

Blackwolds' Roost lies in the ruins south of the Hunter's Lodge.
Ann Granger has asked you to go to Blackwolds' Roost and recover her stolen satchel.
Collected greater sickle-fly wings (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Hello there! Enjoying a nice stroll through the Marshes? I don't meet too many folk that can stand the smell, or the bugs, or the damp, so it's always nice to meet a kindred spirit! Say hello, Sniken! Who's a good boy, then?'
The Neekerbreeker in the cage responds only with an angry clicking sound.
'That wasn't nice, Sniken. I don't know what's gotten into you.
'He might be hungry. In fact, he might be wanting his favourite food: sickle-fly wings. If you kill a few of the greater sickle-flies, you might find enough wings to satisfy Sniken. That might cheer him up!'

'Those wings are just the kind that Sniken likes. You saved me some trouble hunting down those greater sickle-flies.
'Now, here's a treat for you! I'll give you a key to my chest over there. I put all the treasures I find in the Marshes in there. Maybe you'll find something you like!
'And the next time you take a pleasant stroll through the Midgewater Marshes, stop by and say hello!'

'The greater sickle-flies here in the southern Midgewater Marshes are a noisy lot, what their swooping around and collecting the midges in the air. My neeker here, Sniken, loves their wings, probably his favouritest food about.
'If you are lucky, the wings won't be damaged when you kill the creature, and you'll be able to pull off the wings. Then Sniken here will have a treat!'
Bring the sickle-fly wings to Roderik Neeker-friend
Collect greater sickle-fly wings (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Roderick Neeker-friend is worried about Sniken, his pet Neekerbreeker, and has asked for your help cheering him up.
'You're always welcome on my marshy turf, friend!'
'Watch out for the goblins. They really make the marsh much less pleasant.'
'Ah, there's nothing like the smell of swampy air. It smells like life!'
'Neek-breek, breek-neek, neek-breek, breek-neek.'
'Breek-neek, neek-breek, breek-neek, neek-breek.'

Greater sickle-flies are found mainly in the southern Midgewater Marshes. Roderick Neeker-friend is camped atop a cliff near the Goblinhole Ruins in the south-east part of the Midgewater Marshes.
Roderick Neeker-friend asked you to collect wings from the sickle-flies found in the Midgewater Marshes to help feed his pet Neekerbreeker, Sniken.
Collected glittering copper ring

'You wouldn't happen to be a jeweller, would you? Or maybe you're friends with one? I'm in a real situation, you see, and I need someone to fashion a glittering copper ring for me...and soon!
'I had some business at The Forsaken Inn, helping unload some of the crates from a delivery of foodstuffs sent from Bree, and somewhere along the way, I lost my wedding ring. My wedding ring! My wife is going to be furious!
'If Verity sees that I don't have it, well, I don't even want to think about that! That's why I need the services of a jeweller -- I need a glittering copper ring, and fast! I can't go back to Bree without one! I have any number of useful things to offer, if you'll just help me!'

'This glittering copper ring looks just like my lost wedding ring, ${PLAYER}! Verity will never know the difference!
'You've really helped me out, my friend. Here, let me give you these coins and other odds and ends along with my thanks!'
'I really need a jeweller to make me a glittering copper ring, ${PLAYER}! My wife Verity is going to kill me if I don't have my wedding ring when I get home to Bree!'
Bring a glittering copper ring to Barton Tyne
Collect glittering copper ring
Crafting: Barton Tyne Has Lost His Ring
Barton Tyne has lost the glittering copper ring given to him by his wife Verity, and he is beside himself with worry about what she will do when she finds out he lost it.
'You've really helped me out, ${PLAYER}, and I won't forget it!'
'Thanks again for your help, my friend. Don't tell Verity I lost my wedding ring!'

Barton Tyne is on the road between the town of Bree and The Forsaken Inn.
Barton Tyne has told you that he lost his wedding ring, and he is looking for the services of a jeweller to make a glittering copper ring to replace it. His wife Verity is sure to be furious if he returns without it.
Defeated Nishrûk

'Goblins swept in from the north and overran the ruins in the south, then were pressed into service by the strange Orcs in the north. Their leader, a cunning little runt called Nishrûk, hides in the ruins west of this encampment in the darkest reaches of Minas Eriol.
'Bram sent me here to see that the leader was destroyed and that these fine folk were watched over properly. Now, I know that the encampment is deep beyond the ruins to the west in an area that looks truly infested by goblins.
'Go to that section of the ruins of Minas Eriol and kill Nishrûk. I'll have a reward for you when the deed is done.'

'Heroes come from unlikely places. You've done very well, ${PLAYER}. Were I braver, I would have waded into those goblins on my own.
'While we may have dealt a blow against the goblins here in the west, it's unlikely that the tribe will scatter to the wind. They're well organized for goblins, almost as if there is a purpose to their actions. Something tells me that the Lone-lands is in for bad times... well, worse than usual.
'We'll survive -- we always do -- and thanks to you, we may be able to handle the goblins near our Inn. I promised you a gift. This was mine when I was still young enough to use it... I pass it now to you. May it treat you as well as it did me.'
Defeat Nishrûk
Talk to Deputy Osmann
The Goblin-leader
The goblins of Minas Eriol are led by a terrible creature named Nishrûk.

'Bram put too much faith in me, I fear. I am not a stout enough warrior to go wading through the number of goblins perched to the west. Better to leave that to folk like you. Hardy and hale folk who crave adventure.'
'Nishrûk won't be troubling anyone anymore...good work, ${PLAYER}!'
'These goblins are a problem, but I daresay they'll be easier to handle now that you've killed Nishrûk.'

The goblin's leader, Nishrûk, dwells in a goblin-fort built among the ruins south-east of The Forsaken Inn.
Deputy Osmann has asked you to slay Nishrûk, the leader of the goblins troubling The Forsaken Inn.

Deputy Osmann awaits you across the bridge at the eastern edge of the ruins at Minas Eriol.
You entered the ruins and defeated Nishrûk, as Deputy Osmann requested. You should return to him with news of your success.

'Greetings, young ${RACE}. I'm the Constable here at the Forsaken Inn. My body's too old for adventure, but my mind is young enough to know there's work to be done around here.
'Up north, beyond Weathertop, there are wolves and Orcs in the Midgewater Pass and boars scattered throughout Annunlos, all causing no end of trouble. I've a bit of a proposition for you: clear out the threats. If you bring me proof of your noble deeds, I will see that you get a fair reward.
'Are you interested?'

'Wolf-tails, boar-tusks, and Orc-shields... you are quite the skilled warrior. It may seem a menial task to you, but believe me when I say this is much appreciated.
'The people here at the Inn struggle enough without worrying about the wildlife and evils that are spreading unhindered. Ever since those lights appeared atop Weathertop, we've had one trouble after another, and there isn't a sign of relief in sight.
'Take this small reward... you've earned it.'
'Are you taking a rest so soon or aren't you up to the task? I need you to take care of those wolves, Orcs, and boars.'
Talk to Bram Ashleaf at The Forsaken Inn

Noble Deeds
Trouble of all manner surrounds the Forsaken Inn, and a retired Constable needs help protecting the Inn from the threats.
'You've quite a warrior's hand, ${PLAYER}!'
'I'm not as young as I once was. Thank you for your help!'

Wolves can be found in the Midgewater Pass. Orcs prowl north in the Weather Hills and the Midgewater Pass. Boars wander in Annunlos and the Weather Hills surrounding Weathertop.
Bram Ashleaf has asked you to help protect The Forsaken Inn by clearing the threat of wolves, Orcs, and boars from the area surrounding the inn.

'You likely know by now that there are Orcs in the south holding vigil on the ruins where once Men stood proud... and foolish. Now disease threatens to spread from Ost Cyrn. The Orcs have no concern for what they breed in their filth. Meat is left to rot and spoil and the innards of the foetid dead bloat and give birth to all manner of disease and corruption.
'We must seek to curb the plague before it spreads, and so I turn once again to you. There is only one way to destroy the plague-bearing filth left by the Orcs: fire.
'Take this tinder and flint and make your way to Ost Cyrn in the south, where the Orcs dwell. Set fire to the bloated corpses and barrels of filth therein.'

'You have our gratitude, friend. It pains many to know that the Orcs have claimed the lives of many Eglain who fought against them.
'We will breathe easier knowing that the winds will not carry pestilence from the South.'
'Be certain the filth of the Orcs has been purged.'
Burn bloated corpses (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Burn barrels of rotting flesh (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Return tinderbox to Stanric at Ost Guruth
A Plague Upon Us

Despite a small supply of arms and armour, Stanric of the Eglain is attempting to organize at least a meagre defence against the wild and dangerous beasts and other enemies which stalk the ruins the Eglain call their homes.
'Be cautious as you set the fires. It will likely draw the attention of nearby Orcs. Return the tinderbox to me when you are done.'

The source of the plague can be found in the encampments of the Orcs at Ost Cyrn, south of Ost Guruth.
The Orcs care little about the disease spreading from the corpses and barrels of viscera littering their camp. Stanric gave you his tinderbox and bid you burn out the disease spreading from Ost Cyrn.

Stanric awaits the return of his tinderbox at Ost Guruth, north of Ost Cyrn.
You set fire to the corpses and barrels at the Orc-camp in an effort to avoid the spread of plague. You should return to Stanric with word of your success.
Collected gore-crow eyes (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Death, pestilence, and terror stalk us, ${PLAYER}. Two have been dealt with, thanks to your effort, the third still soars above us with ever watchful eyes.
'It is the eyes that I want. I speak of the gore-crows, the black birds with sharp beaks and piercing eyes. They are spies along the road east and west from this place, and they are ever vigilant.
'Take their eyes and they cannot see and what they cannot see they cannot spread to their masters, the Orc and half-breed. Seek the gore-crows along the Great East Road and bring me their eyes to prove that the creatures will no longer speak of us to their fell masters.'

'Dead, yes? No more will these eyes spy down on us from above. Can we not find a bit of peace in that? I think that we shall.
'You have done us a great service once again, ${PLAYER}. There is little else needed for us to become well-prepared for what lay ahead.'

'While they fly through the sky, the gore-crows may see us here at Ost Guruth. I can tell you, ${PLAYER}, no matter how strong our people may appear, we cannot withstand an onslaught from the dwarves, half-breeds, or Orcs here in the Lone-lands. Their spies must be blinded.'

'Before you leave, ${PLAYER}, I would ask one other small task, left over from the last folk who stopped to aid us here.
'We have some bladders already cleaned and ready for water. I ask that you make your way along the Great East Road to the Last Bridge and fill this bladder with water from Mitheithel, the Hoarwell.
'The Bridge has stood through many ages, and we have found that the water taken from the northern end of the bridge is best. Draw the water, then return to me.'
'We have water now to fill our barrels. I am grateful for all that you have done for my people. Here, ${PLAYER}, take this and know the gratitude of all the Eglain of Ost Guruth.'
'Make certain to return to me once you have collected the water from Mitheithel.'

'Fill the bladder at the water's edge on the north side of the Last Bridge, then return here.'
'You have my thanks and the gratitude of my people for all you have done, ${PLAYER}.'

Collected poison sacs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Always we struggle to survive -- and we have done well in all the years I have dwelled at Ost Guruth -- but this is something the like of which I've not seen before. With the Elders working to defend against the evil in Agamaur, it falls to the rest of us to see to other defences.
'This, my friend, is where I come to you. Our numbers are few, and those capable of wielding a weapon are best kept close to Ost Guruth. You, however, are able to walk freely through the land and assist us in ways in which we cannot help ourselves.
'In the west, beneath the shadow of Amon Ros, lie great nests of venomous spiders among the ruins. Some are more potent than others. Now we have ways passed down through the ages of distilling the venom of the lesser spiders and making a medicine which helps to cure poison. If the venom is too potent it cannot be distilled. I need you to collect the poison sacs from ruin-web hunters and ambushers and bring them to me.'
'You have done well, my friend. This will aid us in preventing the deaths of many should we find ourselves beset by spiders.'
'In the west, beneath the shadow of Amon Ros, slay the less deadly of the spiders and take their venom sacs. The crawlers and the trappers should suit our needs well.'
Deliver the poison-sacs to Stanric at Ost Guruth

Despite a small supply of arms and armour, Stanric of the Eglain is attempting to organize at least a meagre defence against the wild and dangerous beasts and other enemies which stalk the ruins the Eglain call their homes.

Ruin-web hunters and ambushers dwell within the ruins of Amon Ros, west of Ost Guruth.

Collected boar-meat (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collected boar-stomach (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'We had a pen of boars once, poached now by Orcs and spiders in the west and south. Frideric means to make peace and asks such a meagre price to find that peace. Our stores will not hold long, and we need meat and water soon, or we will face famine.
'In the east, north of the road, you will find Dol Vaeg and a small encampment of our people. Find and speak with Northrim at this camp and assist him with his tasks. We must be well-prepared for this new future.'

'Stanric is a good man, and his words are true. We must prepare for the dark future ahead. As my companion, Cwendreda, will tell you, the ruins of Nan Dhelu have grown darker than ever we have seen.
'My task is mundane, but necessary. We require water-bladders and food as moving a large number of people from one location to another may take longer than we have to find new sources of fresh water and food.
'To make these bladders and feed our people, we will need a creature untouched by corruption. The boars in these eastern stretches will suffice. There are many boars east along the road but a handful of burrows can be found where the hills rise on the north and south sides of the road.'

'The bellies will be cleaned and the meat will be cured and salted. I will be able to fill our water barrels and feed my people.
'You have my thanks, friend.'
'Quickly now! I will need haunches of meat and boar-stomachs. We need meat and better ways of carrying the water back to Ost Guruth.'

Since long before Orcs and undead crept into the Lone-lands, the Eglain have had to deal with the menace of spiders dwelling within the ruins across the lonely stretch of Eriador. Now as the spiders are driven from the depths of their ruined homes, they creep closer and closer to Ost Guruth and threaten the folk who dwell there.
'You will find the elders of the spider-brood within the ruins of Amon Ros. Some are harder to find than others and will move from place to place. Hunt them down and destroy them.'

'No doubt you've seen spindly crawlers weaving their webs and trapping their prey, which happens to be anything that has life within its veins. Crawling monstrosities is what they are! Nothing good comes from them, and I have seen too many fall prey to their hidden nests.
'These foul vermin do not deserve the life they take so freely. Bring my vengeance upon them!'

'I have not been wholly forthcoming with you, ${PLAYER}, but I was afraid you might not be as honourable as rumour tells. But I shall now tell you my tale, so that you may understand my hatred.
'I was at Naerost when the goblins came. My son and I fled as the Wargs and goblins poured into the ruins, slaughtering all who could not escape them. My son stumbled at the edge of a ruin and slipped into the chasm below. I struggled to reach him, but there was no hope, the spiders were upon him nearly as soon as he touched their webs.
'They took my son from me as they took his mother many years back. My heart is heavy with shame for not telling you the truth.'

'It's my job to keep these passes safe for travellers, ${PLAYER}, but especially for the trade my kin wants to reestablish through these mountains. And there are threats everywhere!

'If you don't mind helping me out again, I'd ask you to post this sign outside the northern entrance to their keep. Head south-west from here. A slope rises up to Gabilazan and the Dourhand keep. There should be a suitable post you can affix the sign to.'

'You have done admirably with the task of posting those signs for me, ${PLAYER}, and I am sure you will exceed my expectations with this latest one!
'This sign warns travellers to beware of giants. I realize this might seem a little obvious, but the trouble with giants is that they can usually see you from a good deal further away than you can see them. One of the Elves in Rivendell told me a story about a giant that could fell an aurochs with a single stone from a distance of two miles! I'm not worried for myself, of course, but if any traders begin passing through the mountains, we'll want them to have at least some warning before entering giant country. Two miles, at least!
'Two passes run south through the mountains. You've already seen the pass of Gabilazan, but the pass of Rakhâs-bizar is further to the east. Travel south through Rakhâs-bizar and post this sign. 'In fact, these giants are so dangerous, I would recommend that you go with friends to attempt this task.'

'I was a jeweller of no small skill some time ago, and though I have now put down my tools, the pieces I fashioned during my youth are still precious to me.
'It is thus with sadness that I report to you that one of the necklaces I crafted but a few years ago has lost its setting! It has been too long for me to fashion a replacement, but if you know a jeweller who could do so, I would appreciate it.
'Bring me a glittering copper necklace, and I will pay you a fair sum. I have a few small items as well, including some leftover gemstones, with which I would be willing to part.'

'You have done as I asked and brought to me a glittering copper necklace. I thank you for it and give to you these coins and materials!
'I must admit, however, that this necklace does not seem as special to me as the one that I crafted with my own hands. Perhaps I will come to appreciate this one, but I had not expected to feel this way. That's a little strange, isn't it?
'Thank you for it, friend. I am sure I will feel differently in the morning.'
'Were you planning on bringing me a glittering copper necklace or not?'

'I did not think that necklace meant so much to me. How strange.'

'The Lonely Mountain seems so far away. Ah, how I wish I were there now! Our larders here in the Blue Mountains are scant, and we Longbeards are going to be here for some time.
'If you want to make yourself useful, go out and hunt some of the aurochs for me. There are plenty of those beasts wandering west of Frerin's Court to last all season, and we could use the meat.'

'Bravo, ${PLAYER}! We'll have a grand feast tonight and salt the rest of the haunches to last the rest of the season.
'Here, you may find use of some of this as well. It will keep you strong. If ever you are in need of such provisions, come and see me.'

'Aurochs herds are all about west of Frerin's Court. You can't miss them, what with their wooly hides and large horns. I reckon a half-dozen should do the trick. Don't want to take more than we need!'
