'I don't know what the problem is, stranger. My father was a metalworker, and my father's father was a metalworker, but I do not seem to have inherited their skill with hammer and anvil. I do not know where it could have gone, for I have no brothers, but that skill certainly has avoided me!
'You see, I decided it was time to make a new pair of bronze leggings for myself, but I did something wrong with the heat of the fire and my hammer-blows and ended up with something more akin to a belt. A belt fused in on itself, with something like a sleeve on one end. I can't wear that! And I wouldn't wear it even if I could figure out how exactly to try it on!
'If you know a metalworker of even small skill, I'll pay you for some bronze leggings. I'll give you my leftover materials as well! And don't tell anyone about my... mishap... if you don't mind.'

'These will do very well, ${PLAYER}! I don't understand how mine could have turned out so very differently, because these seem easy enough to make. I just don't understand.
'Here are the coins and materials I promised you. Take with them my thanks!'

'The cave is to the south-east in the Winterheights. Hurry now! I think I was nearing a vein of gold when they drove me out!'

'Ah, there she is! Thank you, ${PLAYER}. But I've sad news... a friend of mine told me that cave's been tapped dry. There's naught but fool's gold in there.

'We cannot undo the damage wrought by the cave-claws, but their future impact on the caverns will be minimal. Thank you, ${PLAYER}, for all you have done.'

The stone beneath Thorin's Gate is honeycombed by cave-claw burrows. If the damage continues, the entire area could be weakened enough to collapse on itself.

'You there! I sent Vífill to cut a quarter-cord of firewood for Noglond, but he hasn't come back. See if you can find him.
'Just follow the road to the west. There's a clearing out that way where we gather our wood.
'Be wary though... who knows what's delayed Vífill.'
'Goblins, here in Vale of Thráin? Nay, that's not likely. Surely not!'

'Ha! Well met! I was wondering when Grímkell would send someone. I was in the clearing, cutting wood for Noglond, when goblins fell on me from the shadows of the trees.
'I managed to kill two and wounded the last, enough to drive it off, but was wounded myself in the fight. The foul creature ran off to the south. Tell Grímkell what happened and to send help!'
Find Vífill
Cutting Cords
Grímkell, the commander at Noglond, sent one of his guards, Vífill, to cut some firewood and is concerned because Vífill has failed to return.
'Vífill still hasn't returned from the firewood grove just up the road.'
'I'll be fine... leave me. Grímkell must be told about the goblins immediately!'

'I don't doubt Vífill made up his story of goblins after hitting himself with his own axe!
'Oh? You think he told the truth? Not likely! But if you're so sure he's met up with goblins, maybe you can go find them.
'The goblins of the Blue Mountains sometimes carry these little things, fetishes I guess you might call them. Bring me one of their fetishes, and maybe I'll lend Vífill's tale my ear.'

'What's this? Oh...
'I must beg your pardon. It seems you and Vífill were right. Let's see now. Goblins in the Vale?'

Grímkell scoffed at Vífill's story of goblins in the Vale of Thráin, blaming Vífill's injury instead upon his own clumsiness.

'What? He doesn't believe me? Well that beard-chewing...! Forget I said that. He's a good commander, just a bit contrary at times.
'I suppose that you'd best go find one of those fetishes Grímkell wants. There are goblins to the south of my camp and a bit to the west.'

Vífill said there were goblins south of his camp.

'It is unthinkable that these goblins managed to sneak into the Vale of Thráin under my very beard. Well, there's nothing to do about it now but prepare for the worst.
'I need you to take the fetish you found to Bolli, the Captain of the Guard in Gondamon to the east. He must know of the goblin's incursion from the valley into Vale of Thráin.
'I've no doubt this is a sign of a larger threat.'

'You carry with you a fetish of the Blue Crag goblin tribes. It's clear that the vile creatures are on the move and intend to launch an offensive against the Vale of Thráin. Troubling news, to be sure.
'We must crush the goblin forces before they become an even greater threat. Their presence in the Vale is a festering blight on the land and if we don't stop it now, it will spread like a shadow across the land.'

'The goblins are growing more bold...we must redouble our vigilance.'
'It is well that you brought me the goblin-fetish. At least now we know what tribe we are dealing with!'

'Ha! Good work. I'm sorry I ever doubted Vífill, but who would have known that goblins would actually dare to enter the Vale of Thráin?'

'The wild lands around Gondamon are a bounty of such resources, but if we don't make full use of them, we might as well be giving them to the goblins!
'If you know a scholar of some skill, I would have him prepare for me some minor metalsmithing-lore and some minor woodworking-lore. Armed with these, I can surely prepare a plan for better using what we have. I will pay you for your efforts, of course.'

'Thank you for these, ${PLAYER}! Now I must engross myself in study and take what lessons from these I can!

'I need minor metalsmithing-lore and minor woodworking-lore if I am to make best use of the resources to be found on the low-lands surrounding Gondamon. Have you forgotten?'

'What happened to me? I was out hunting bear, and I came across this mother lynx and her cubs. The poor thing was tore up mightily by some hendrevail, and I was just able to grab her before they went after me. I twisted my ankle something terrible but it'll heal, as will this old she-cat.
'She left a litter behind her, but we're both too battered to save the cubs ourselves. I'd feel awful if something happened to them but I'm no use to anyone until my ankle mends.
'Perhaps you can venture up to the den by the standing stones to the north and bring back any of the surviving cubs? I'd appreciate it, and I'm sure the mother would as well.'

You peer inside the abandoned bear-den and hear the plaintive mewing of a hungry, frightened lynx-cub.
The poor thing is scared to leave the safety of the den, fearing attack by hendrevail.
With soothing words, you manage to coax the frightened cub from the safety of its den.

'There's a precious cub! Let me take him from you and... ooww! Quit your scratching! He's a feisty one, isn't he? Or is it a she?
'Poor little thing. Too bad its litter-mates didn't fare so well, but that's the way of things. Hmmm... nipping my beard now. Perhaps the wee thing is hungry?'
'Lynx raise their young in dens or small burrows, especially those abandoned by other animals.'

'Look at those paws! This one is going to be a fearsome hunter when its reaches full size.'
'Hahaha... it's lickin' me face!'
'Good to see a mother and child reunited, even if they're of the four-legged variety.'

'The cub is hungry, but he is too young to hunt his own food. His mother is still all scratched up and in no position to hunt either. Let's see... the only meat I have here at the lodge is either dried or smoked. I think they both could use some fresh, raw meat.

If you have trouble hunting a live rabbit, I have a string of rabbit traps scattered in the woods not far to the east and west of the lodge. I'd appreciate it if you would check the traps and bring back a plump rabbit.
'I'd hate to see mother and cub go without food.'
'This'll do for now, but we can't keep hand-feeding the things, or they'll lose that wild streak that makes them good hunters.'

'Whoa, nearly lost a finger there!'

'I do not know whether he remains unwittingly or willingly, for I cannot know the mind of the Dead, but I cannot see why he should choose to suffer so.'

'All right, while Noll here and I put this wheel on the cart, there's one last thing I'd ask you to do. Go back to Elsie in Trestlebridge and tell her that all's well here.
'Once the cart is fixed, Noll and I are going to take down a couple more trees and then bring our load down to the town. Of course, we couldn't have done that without your help! Thanks for that!
'Now hurry... won't do to stand around here waiting for Orcs!'

'Mattie and Noll are safe and sound? Oh, bless you! Bless you! That's the best news I've heard in many a day. I was fearing the worst, but I'm glad to hear my worries were for naught!
'I just hope they hurry up and get back to Trestlebridge! I don't think I'll get a bit of rest until I see them back.'
All's Well

Searching the Orc camp, you were able to find a wheel for Mattie Woodruff's cart. Although the wheel is a bit small, he thinks it should work well enough to get the cart and a load of lumber back to Trestlebridge.

'I think we'll be fine here. Noll and I should be able to get this wheel on without too many problems.
'All I'd ask of you is to go back down to Trestlebridge and tell Elsie that we're all right!'
'Thanks for that wheel. Noll and I should have it on the cart in no time!'
'I'll be a lot happier when we've got back to Trestlebridge with this wood!'
'I'm so glad to know that Mattie is safe!'
'I do hope Mattie and Noll start back for Trestlebridge soon!'
'It's good you found that wheel. I'd hate to be caught out here much longer.'

While Mattie and Noll fix the cart and load it with the lumber they've collected, Mattie asked you to go back to Trestlebridge and tell his wife that he's safe.

'You see, the other thing needed for the barricades is wood. In the past we would fell trees in the Nan Wathren when we needed lumber, but now the Orcs lurk there.
'We were so desperate for lumber that my husband, Mattie, and my brother, Noll Tobbit, risked leaving Trestlebridge and went north along the Greenway proper in search of trees to fell. It has been too long since I've heard from them, and I'm worried something terrible has happened.
'Would you search north along the Greenway for them? I can't bear to think that something bad might have happened to them.'

'So Elsie sent you? Well I'm glad for it!
'Well, we did run afoul of them Orcs... fortunate to have escaped with our lives, we are! But our cart here... well, it didn't get off quite as well, as you can see!
'No matter how many trees we fell, if we don't have our cart fixed we can't bring 'em back to Trestlebridge!'

'If we don't get a wheel for this cart, this lumber ain't going anywhere. I'd send you to Trestlebridge, but I doubt they'd have anything to spare. Every little bit there is precious.
'But there's some hope yet. See, there were some farmers escaping to Trestlebridge and their waggons got overrun by them Orcs. Well, their supplies were stolen and their carts broke up, but there might be a wheel from one of their carts that we can salvage.
'I don't think they dragged the carts into Nan Wathren, so I think you'll find the remains of them carts in that Orc camp straight east of here. If we're going to find a wheel to salvage, it'll be there, I'd wager!'

'Aye, you found one! This one looks like it'll work! It's a bit smaller than the other wheels, so the ride will be a bit rougher. But as long as we get this lumber to Trestlebridge, it won't matter how rough the ride is!'

'I don't think them Orcs dragged the broken waggons from that caravan into Nan Wathren, so I would search their camp due east of here for a wheel.

'When the Stone-trolls learn that Elves have returned to Lin Giliath, they are sure to attack again. There are too few of us, and we cannot hold out long. There is one defence which we can call upon, but there is no certainty that those I speak of will still answer the summons.
'I give you these runes -- \qcanel\q they are called -- and ask you to lay them upon the pedestal stones found throughout the marshes. Long ago, many of these stones were set east of Lin Giliath in a great curve bending to the south, but only three have survived the ravages of time and the elements. We must hope the guardians remember the meaning of the \qcanel\q.
'Return to me when you have placed all the runes, and we will learn if the errand was for naught.'

'You have placed the \qcanel\q, ${PLAYER}? That is well, though it seems the bog-guardians have chosen not to come to our aid.
'I suppose I was too eager for the old friendship between Elves and bog-guardians to be rekindled that I was hopeful to the point of blindness. Only disappointment can come of... wait, what is that?
'Look! A bog-guardian has come! And more! I shamed myself with despair, but now I see that it is never wrong to hope. You have my thanks, ${PLAYER}!'

'The bog-guardians remember their old friendship with Elves, after all this time!'
'The bog-guardians were beloved of the Ents, it is said.'
'Many creatures of the bog have become wild and feral.'

'I am pleased to see a face that does not belong to a troll. I came to Taur Gonwaith to seek vengeance on the trolls that attacked the glade of Lin Giliath and murdered my fair friend Lachenn. I can tell you that many of the Stone-trolls that attacked Lin Giliath will never again leave this place.
'They proved a challenge, and that one was about to squash me when you arrived. You have my thanks.
'Let us leave this place, friend, so I might return to Lin Giliath and tell my friend, Thaliollang, the course of my vengeance.'

'You survived a journey to Taur Gonwaith, ${PLAYER}, and lent your strength to Lagorlam!

Lagorlam, a member of the company of Elves who came north with Gildor Inglorion, entered Taur Gonwaith, seeking vengeance against the trolls who attacked Lin Giliath. He has not returned, which concerns Thaliollang.
'The death of Lachenn has troubled us all, and Lagorlam may not use as much caution as he ordinarily would. Seek him in Taur Gonwaith to the south-east and lend him whatever aid he may need.'
'Taur Gonwaith is a place of evil where the stone-trolls hold sway.'
'Had Gildor and my company arrived earlier, Lachenn might still be alive.'
'I had harsh words for Aglardir, and I now regret them. His sorrow is no less true than mine.'

Lagorlam has gone to the forest of Taur Gonwaith, south-east of Lin Giliath.
Thaliollang has sent you to find Lagorlam and make certain he is well.

Angmar's emissary must reside deep within the cave in Taur Gonwaith, south-east of Lin Giliath.
You should defeat the emissary of Angmar that has gained the allegiance of the Stone-trolls.
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTE: A fellowship is recommended for this quest.</rgb>

You have discovered the Etten Caves at Taur Gonwaith. Whatever has stirred the trolls surely hides within these vast caverns.
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTE: A fellowship is recommended for this quest.</rgb>

'You have earned more thanks than I have to give, ${PLAYER}, for defeating the troll-keeper of Angmar.
'Lachenn would have been pleased to know you. I name you Elf-friend and will not forget what you have done here, ${PLAYER}. I expect the Stone-trolls are not likely to forget either. Lin Giliath may have peace for a time.'
Search the Etten Caves for the leader of the trolls
The Troll-keeper
Someone evil has stirred the Stone-trolls, rousing them to wreak havoc upon the fair glades of Meluinen.
'Lachenn has been avenged, and the Stone-trolls may never again attack Lin Giliath.'
'That Angmar should already have power even in Meluinen is a sad tiding.'
'Cross the Downs with caution, ${PLAYER}, for the dangers increase with each passing day.'

Angmar's emissary must reside deep within the cave in Taur Gonwaith, south-east of Lin Giliath.
You should defeat the emissary of Angmar that has gained the allegiance of the Stone-trolls.
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTE: A fellowship is recommended for this quest.</rgb>

Thaliollang is at Lin Giliath, north-west of Taur Gonwaith.
Thaliollang will be pleased to know that he was correct in his belief: there was an emissary from Angmar among the trolls. To the benefit of all, you have defeated him.
Defeated Orcs in Meluinen (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Thaliollang and Lagorlam are so intent upon vengeance against the Stone-trolls that they are blind to all other threats, and I fear they will not retain enough strength of will to fight the other dangers that lurk nearby.
'Orcs of the Ongbúrz clan have established a foothold in Nan Wathren, the valley to the south-west, and their scouts intrude further into Meluinen with each passing day.
'Slay any Orcs you find that have crossed into Meluinen, ${PLAYER}, for they pose a great threat to Lin Giliath. You will surely find them south and south-west of here, along the line of the mountains.'

'You have done well, ${PLAYER}! I hope your efforts will serve as a warning to the Ongbúrz: they are not welcome in Meluinen, nor ever will be. This company of Elves may only be temporary stewards of Lin Giliath, but we shall oppose them as surely as Lachenn would, were he still alive.'
Defeat Orcs in Meluinen (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Orc Excursions
Meluinen is threatened by the presence of a large encampment of Ongbúrz Orcs in the valley to the south-west.

'Orcs of the Ongbúrz tribe have begun creeping into Meluinen from Nan Wathren, south-west of here. Defeat the Orcs that have already crossed into Meluinen to the south and south-west, and we may prevent, or at the least delay, any further incursions.'
'The Orcs of Nan Wathren will be wary now of sending scouts into Meluinen.'
'We will stay at Lin Giliath for as long as it takes to repel the Orcs.'

Orc-scouts have crept into Meluinen from the valley to the south-west of Lin Giliath.
Brethilwen has asked you to slay any Orcs you find in Meluinen, thus reducing the Ongbúrz threat.

Brethilwen is in Lin Giliath.
Brethilwen will be heartened to hear of your victory over the Orcs that had entered Meluinen.
Collected weapon-chests (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'North-men have been seen carrying chests laden with weapons into a cave, in the south. While the others dwell upon the malefactions of the trolls, I am concerned by the very presence of Men from Angmar not to mention their arms.
'Every sword-hilt we remove from the grasp of an Angmarim is one fewer blade that may be brought to bear against the Free Peoples. Seek out weapon-chests in the troll-cave and bring them to me. I shall destroy the foul blades.
'If even one of the blades we seize would have otherwise slain an innocent, I shall count this day's labour worth the toil.'

'These weapons are poorly made, and none of them exhibit the care needed to make a truly fine sword. I am not surprised by the lack of craftsmanship, for the Angmarim care little about such things, and these blades are as effective as they need to be to slay the innocent people who were their intended prey.
'You have done well to bring me these weapons. I will destroy them, and by so doing I hope we have together saved some lives. You have my thanks for this errand.'
'You have not yet recovered enough weapon-chests from the troll-cave in Taur Gonwaith.'
Collect weapon-chests (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring Angmarim weapon-chests to Baranwen

Disarming the Valley
Defeated a Hillman (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
North-men from Angmar have wandered into Taur Gonwaith.

'Taur Gonwaith was once a shady vale to the south-east of Lin Giliath, but the trolls have despoiled it at the hands of their Angmarim masters. If you can return here with several chests of the Angmarim weapons, I will destroy them.'
'The fewer weapons the Angmarim can draw, the safer the Free Peoples will be.'
'Taur Gonwaith was once beautiful, but now it is a dark and ominous place.'

The mysterious Angmarim are outside of the troll-cave in the southern part of Taur Gonwaith, south of Lin Giliath.
Baranwen has asked you to collect weapon-chests from the Angmarim and to return them to her so she can destroy the foul weapons.

Collected Ongbúrz venom-pouches (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'I have need of your assistance, ${PLAYER}. An Orc defiler, skilled in the use of poisons, joined the ranks of the Ongbúrz in southern Lin Giliath. He has begun to poison the waters of this glade, and all will be ruined.
'Slay the Orcs in Merenost and collect their venom pouches. I will make sure the pouches are never again used for evil purposes.
'While you are in the camp, put an end to the source of the vile poison once and for all by killing the Ongbúrz-defiler. Be careful, ${PLAYER} -- these Orcs are brutal and without mercy, and you may have need of allies.'

'The venom pouches. I take it that the defiler was slain as well? Many lives will be saved through your efforts.
'I find it strange that the Orcs would hunt their spider allies. They make themselves stronger at others' expense... and in the end, weakening the Enemy as a whole. Such is the way of evil things, for the spiders would not hesitate to drink of the blood of their Orkish fellows.'
'You have not yet obtained the venom-pouches I asked for, ${PLAYER}?'
Collect Ongbúrz venom-pouches (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring the Ongbúrz venom-pouches to Gandelin
Touch of Corruption
The Orcs of Merenost in Meluinen use spider venom to coat their blades and arrows.
'${PLAYER}, we must have some samples of the Orcs' poison so that we may create a cure for it.'
'You have made the Ongbúrz much weaker than once they were.'
'The time will come when we must push the Orcs from the Kingsfell.'

The Ongbúrz Orcs can be found in the ruins at Merenost, in southern Lin Giliath.

'I like you, little warrior. I wish to see some of your skill. Wargs are little creatures, much like you. The aurochs, they are more like us. Big, difficult to kill.
'If you can bring us the meat of the aurochs, the Suuri-lehmä will hold you in high esteem indeed.'
'Ah, delicious aurochs-meat! Such a little creature to bring down such a great creature. I am impressed, yes. You did well, little friend.'
'The aurochs are out in the field, little friend.'
Bring the aurochs-meat to Elder Tahvo

The aurochs herds roam the foothills and plains of eastern Nan Amlug.

Collected lynx-furs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'There's a cold winter coming. I feel it in my bones. We dwarves are a hardy folk, but if we're going to survive the winter, we will need more supplies.
'Hunt the troublesome lynx that seem to cover the lands hereabouts and bring me their fur. I'll craft their hides into warm gloves for our miners.'
'Thank you for your help, friend. I will fashion these furs into gloves to protect the miners from the bitter cold of the deep mines. Old Nine-fingered Doli will be happy about that, I can tell you.'
'I'll need more furs than this if I am to craft as many gloves as needed.'
Bring the lynx-furs to Quartermaster Orgrin

Defeated Wargs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Little traveller, will you prove your worth to me? I am Tahvo, leader of this clan. Will you hunt with us?
'Wargs befoul our lands, slavering beasts with long yellow teeth. They roam to and fro as if they own it. It is our land, not theirs.
'Hunt them, and you may earn my respect.'
'Oho! Oho. A feisty little wanderer, this one. Well, you have my attention, little friend. What can the Rauta-lehmä do to please this most intriguing guest?'
Defeat Wargs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Return to Elder Tahvo
Hunting Wargs
Elder Tahvo has asked you to prove yourself by defeating many Wargs on his turf.

Warg packs prowl the hills of eastern Nan Amlug, befouling the land of the Rauta-lehmä.
Elder Tahvo has asked you to prove your worth by slaying some Wargs.

Elder Tahvo is at Rosfold, east across the mountain range from Esteldín.
You should tell Elder Tahvo that you have fulfilled his requests, and many Wargs now lie slain by your hand.

'You have aided us well ${PLAYER}. The time for battle is very near now.
'One last thing I ask -- take this to Othrikar, the dwarf-mines north-west of here, and give it to Quartermaster Orgrin. This satchel contains many healing herbs we collected as part of our pact with the dwarves there, who will also aid us.
'Be well. We may not meet again.'

'Eh, what is this? Ah, the herbs promised by the Jorthkyn. Thank you for bringing them!
'They are strange allies, are they not? But these times are dangerous, and any force we can raise to halt the advance of Angmar is welcome.
'The Jorthkyn seem to have an odd affinity for plants, though they do not raise crops... I am not sure where they learned such lore but it is of great value to us now. Many of us shall doubtless be wounded in the battles to come, and the poultices that can be made from these herbs are potent for healing.'
Bring Iivari's herb satchel to Quartermaster Orgrin
Sealing the Pact
There exists a pact between the Suuri-lehmä and the Dwarves of Othrikar, that each would provide aid to the other.
'Take the herbs to Othrikar. The dwarves will have need of them.'
'The Jorthkyn's herbs shall help us against Angmar and the Dourhands.'
'Thank you for your delivering these herbs, ${RACE}.'
'You are a good friend to the Suuri-lehmä and to the dwarves.'
'The Rauta-lehmä have no honour. With your help, ${PLAYER}, we have taught them the meaning of the word.'

Quartermaster Orgrin is at Othrikar, north-west of Rusfold.
Iivari has asked you to perform one final task for him: he wishes you to deliver a satchel of herbs to Orgrin, the provisioner at Othrikar, as fulfillment of a pact between Earth-kin and dwarves.

'Greetings, traveller. I must ask your aid, for my tribe cannot help me. I am preparing the Suuri-lehmä for war, but I am not prepared myself.
'My brother stands across from me, armed with the weapons of Angmar, his mind filled with their lies. I have not been able to speak with him since this rift grew between my people and the Rauta-lehmä, who serve Angmar. I do not know where my brother's heart truly lies, whether he is torn within, as am I.
'I cannot lead my people to war while this doubt gnaws at me! Take this message to Oskari - he is somewhere within the Rauta-lehmä encampment at the place called Fashat Laug, well to the east of here. Perhaps he and others may yet be convinced to return to us before the end.'

'You bring a message from my brother? I see.
'Iivari is a fool who refuses to see the world as it truly is. He thinks that words alone can chase away the darkness - he does not understand the meaning of power.
'Take this to him. It is all the answer from me that he will receive. Now go, or the Rauta-lehmä shall crush you.'

'Ah. Now I know the truth. The rune you carry is a gift I gave my brother many years ago. The symbol upon it in our language means \qkinship\q. It has been etched over with a symbol we use to mean \qwithout value.\q
'The lies of the Angmarim run too deep, and my brother is beyond my reach now. I find my heart no less troubled by what I must do, but now I know that there is no choice....'
Bring Iivari's message to Oskari
Bring Oskari's rune to Iivari
A Brother's Plea

The two factions of the Earth-kin -- the free Suuri-lehmä and the Rauta-lehmä, who serve Angmar -- are preparing for war. Iivari, the War-master of the Suuri-lehmä, and his brother Oskari have found themselves on opposite sides of the conflict.
'Go. Take the rune. I have nothing more to say.'
'Please carry the message to my brother.'

Oskari is somewhere among the camps of the Rauta-lehmä at Fashat Laug in the eastern North Downs.
Iivari has given you a message to take to his brother Oskari. Iivari hopes that his words may be able to sway his brother and others of the Earth-kin to return to the Suuri-lehmä.

Iivari is in the Suuri-lehmä encampment, west of Fashat Laug.

'Oh, stranger, perhaps you will hear my sad story. I was a member of a group of merchants who were crossing the North Downs when we encountered a party of marauding Orcs.
'We fled from them, but did not escape tragedy. We encamped not far south of here, in a place I later learned was called the Snares, and with good reason. As we slept, our camp was raided by spiders! Only I escaped and was rescued by these Rangers.
'One of my companions was bearing a pouch of valuable gems on his person, which we were taking to Othrikar for trade. I do not doubt that it was still on his body when the spiders dragged him off. Could you go to the spider-lair and retrieve it? Without it, I will be destitute. The lair is to the south of here.'
'Indeed, these are the gems! Thank you so much for your help. I must give you a small reward for your courage!'
'Please find those lost gems, or I am ruined.'
Collect the gem pouch
Bring the gems back to Holger Tanner
Spider Gems
Holger Tanner is the survivor of a party of merchants ambushed by spiders in the Kingsfell. The merchants were carrying a valuable pouch of gems, which the spiders dragged off with one of the bodies.
'I am grateful to these Rangers and all for saving my life, but I need those gems back!'
'Thank you so much for recovering those gems. I'll be journeying back to Bree as soon as the Rangers say it's safe.'
'You are a brave ${RACE} to face those spiders for my gems.'

You have assisted the Rangers of Esteldín in their daily vigilance, maintaining that the lands of the North Downs are free from enemy control.
Collected goblin slave-collars (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Until recently, small goblin raiding-parties were the worst threat faced by the North Downs. But with the arrival of the Orcs out of Angmar, the goblins have themselves been forced by their greater brethren into servitude.
'Now, they watch the front-lines of the host at Dol Dínen, under command of the Orcs, awaiting their turn to be sacrificed for the greater glory of the Iron Crown. We should not make them wait overlong. If you are willing, make your way south-east out of Esteldín to the outskirts of the Orc-encampment at Dol Dínen and kill the goblins there.
'Bring me the slave collars worn by the goblins as evidence that your task has been accomplished.'

'Ah, you have returned... and successful, I see. Perhaps the Orc-generals will feel less secure with the wall of goblin-flesh thinned around them.
'In truth, though, this is but a small victory. The Orc army is vast, and the Dúnedain of the North are a dwindling people.'
'Be careful not to stray too far into the Orc-encampment... scouts report that the forces beyond the trenches include trolls. We cannot risk such an assault at this time.'
Bring goblin slave-collars to Elúr
Collect goblin slave-collars (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Forced into Service

A great host of Orcs spilled through Ram Dúath, driving the Men of the North Downs from their farms. Esteldín, home of the few remaining Dúnedain of the North, was spared discovery. It is from there that the Rangers begin to plan their counter-offensive against the black tide of Angmar.

Goblins can be found on the outskirts of the Orc-encampment at Dol Dínen, south-east of Esteldín.
According to Elúr, the goblins of the North Downs have been forced into servitude by the Orcs of Angmar and act as the advance forces of the Orc-host. The Ranger has asked you to dispose of the goblins, bringing him their slave collars as evidence that you have completed your task.

Raugzok, chief of the Wargs, can be found at Dol Dínen in the south-eastern North Downs.
You should defeat Raugzok.

You become aware of a presence; a chieftain has risen up among the Wargs of Dol Dínen, uniting the packs that run with the Orcs gathered there. Even a tenuous unity among such foul beasts is a danger to all.
You should slay the chieftain of the Wargs and shatter the courage of these beasts. The vile creatures linger near the Orcs, protecting their masters, and as such you will need the strength of allies to fight along with you.
You have defeated Raugzok, chief among the Wargs of Dol Dínen. Your efforts have done much to preserve the North Downs from the ravages of war.
Defeat Raugzok
Defeat Raugzok

Rumours have reached the ears of the Rangers at Esteldín that a chieftain has arisen within the ranks of the Wargs at Dol Dínen, uniting the packs.

Raugzok, chief of the Wargs, can be found at Dol Dínen in the south-eastern North Downs.

'The food-stores you gathered will help fill the bellies of my people, ${PLAYER}, but now we must put weapons into their hands!
'The Angmarim force the people of Donnvail to mine for a special sort of hot-burning coal in the hills north of the city, and they use this ore in the production of weapons. If we had some of this coal, we could set our smiths to forging weapons at once.
'The deposits of this special coal can be found among the canyons north of Donnvail. Take this hardened pick and use it to mine some of the coal, then return to me. Donnvail is north-east of Fail-á-Khro, and the canyons are north of the city's western wall.'
'You have done well, ${PLAYER}, once again! We will forge great weapons with the aid of this coal, and perhaps it will help us to cast off the yoke of Angmar!'
'Have you forgotten to mine the special coal that you said you would? The deposits are north of Donnvail's western wall.'
Collect Angmar coal (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring Angmar coal and coal-pick to Ekhagan
Fuel for the Forge
Their Angmarim task-masters force the people of Donnvail to mine a hot-burning type of coal from the hills north of the city.
'The deposits of this coal I seek can be found throughout the canyons north of Donnvail's western wall. The city is north-east of Fail-á-Khro.'
'We have provided for ourselves and taken from our enemies. That is good.'
'You will always be welcome at Fail-á-Khro, ${PLAYER}.'

Special hot-burning coal deposits can be found throughout the canyons north of the city of Donnvail, north-east of Fail-á-Khro.
Ekhagan has asked you to gather the special hot-burning coal he needs to work the old black iron of Angmar.

Ekhagan is at Fail-á-Khro, south-west of the city of Donnvail.
You should return to Ekhagan with the special hot-burning coal you have mined.
Collected bloodstone trove

'Welcome, ${PLAYER}, to the Búth Sánkhas of Aughaire. This is where we pass down stories of the lost days and preserve the tales of our people. Now that you are a friend of the Trév Gállorg, it is your duty to carry on this tradition as well.
'A great trove of bloodstones was stolen from us by the Trév Duvárdain before your arrival at Aughaire; it is a tale that deserves a better ending. Go now to Tór Gailvin, north-east of Aughaire, and reclaim this trove. You have already been to this fortress and are well-suited to weaving a proper end to this tale.
'The trove will likely be kept in an out-of-the-way corner somewhere within Tór Gailvin. Use caution as you go and search in every corner for the stolen trove.'
'Crannog's assessment was correct, ${PLAYER}. You are a worthy friend of the Trév Gállorg! I am pleased that we may now write a more satisfactory ending to the tale of the stolen bloodstones.'
'You have not recovered the bloodstone trove. Did you forget that it was surely being held in some hidden corner of Tór Gailvin, north-east of Aughaire?'
Collect bloodstone trove
Bring bloodstone trove to Latharna
The Bloodstone Trove
Latharna has welcomed you as a friend of the Trév Gállorg and asks you to set right some of the injuries the people have suffered of late.

'The bloodstone trove is being held somewhere within Tór Gailvin, the Trév Duvárdain fortress north-east of Aughaire. Search in out-of-the-way corners within the camp and recover what was stolen from us!'
'And 'lo, the bloodstone trove was recovered by ${PLAYER}, ${RACE} of the South!'
'The Trév Duvárdain did not account for the deeds of ${PLAYER}, mighty ${CLASS} from far lands!'

The bloodstone trove is in the fortress of Tór Gailvin north-east of Aughaire, probably hidden in an out-of-the-way corner.
Latharna has asked you to recover the trove of bloodstones that was stolen by the Trév Duvárdain.

Latharna is in the Búth Sánkhas in Aughaire, south-east of the market.
You have recovered the bloodstone trove from Tór Gailvin and should bring it now to Latharna.
Collected dull bloodstones (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'I have heard of your task, ${PLAYER}, and know exactly how you can prove your worthiness... to me, and to us all.
'This land must be coaxed to give us food, but she is more generous with gems, such as the bloodstones which we use in several crafts. But the shiny stones attract more than the Trév Gállorg who go searching for them; the hill-beasts covet bloodstones and will often fight to the death to recover them. Once the creatures have obtained such a bloodstone, the gem loses its shine! Only through the secret ways of the Trév Gállorg can the shine be returned to the stones.
'Show your mettle and recover dull bloodstones from the hill-beasts north of Aughaire! You will find many of the creatures among the chasms of Nád Nathair, though their wandering cousins may also bear the stones.'
'You have done very well, ${PLAYER}. I will tell Crannog of your service and polish these dull bloodstones to the sheen they deserve. They will then be used in the crafts of my people.'
'Hill-beasts north of Aughaire, especially among the chasms of Nád Nathair, will carry the dull bloodstones I seek.'
Collect dull bloodstones (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring the dull bloodstones to Lakhina
Lakhina has learned of the challenge that Crannog has set for you and knows what she would have you do.
'The hill-beasts of Fasach-larran often carry bloodstones. Look for them north of Aughaire, especially among the chasms of Nád Nathair.'
'I will polish the bloodstones you brought to a mirrored sheen.'
'Hill-beasts are ferocious creatures, and you are most brave to have hunted them.'

The hill-beasts of Fasach-larran often carry bloodstones they find on the ground. Many of the creatures make their home in Nád Nathair, north of Aughaire.
Lakhina has asked you to defeat hill-beasts and recover the dull bloodstones they often carry.

Lakhina is at the centre island of Aughaire, east of Crannog's ruling-seat.
You have collected dull bloodstones from hill-beasts in Fasach-larran and should now return them to Lakhina.
Collected crawler-flesh (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Placed roasted crawler-flesh
Tasgall has survived the Beast-lord's assault!

'These hill-beasts are growing more and more dangerous. We have heard that their leader is a matriarch of their kind, secretive and cunning, who in turn serves the drakes. If we can lure out this beast-mother and defeat her, the other hill-beasts may be cowed or routed.
'We know that these beasts greatly prize roasted crawler-flesh. I would ask you first to hunt crawlers in the area, bring their flesh back to me to be roasted, and then take the meat out to the hill-beast lairs where we may draw out this mother of the beasts.
'Beware though -- while the crawlers are no great threat, the matriarch may be a foe beyond the power of any lone warrior to overcome.'

'These Crawlers have been roasted to a fine... something.
'In any case, take this vile stuff to the hill-beasts. You will find the old gate into the valley occupied by the hill-beasts and drakes. A short way into these valleys you will find a small cave within which the Beast-mother is believed to make her lair.
'Place the roasted crawlers on the great stone just within the entrance to draw the creature out. It is then that you must strike!'

'Ha! Well done, Southron! I guess those rumours of the Beast-lord were false then - I had half expected you to face a mated pair of the horrid beasts!
'Wait... do you hear something?'

'Revolting stuff, is it not? But keep in mind, if you have got nothing else, you can live off it. Anyway, roasted it is even worse than raw, but the hill-beasts seem to like it.
'Hold a few minutes while I cook up this lot.'
'Bring me the flesh of crawlers so that I may prepare it for the beast-mother.'

'I am most grateful for your intervention. I had heard rumours from the hunters that there might be a mated pair of those horrible creatures up in the hills, but I had dismissed them as folly.
'Alas it was my own folly that drew the wrath of her mate down upon us and nearly cost us all our lives, please accept my sincerest apology and accept these tokens of my appreciation for saving my life.'
Bring the crawler-flesh to Tasgall
Collect crawler-flesh (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Speak with Tasgall
Lure out and defeat the Beast-mother
Speak with Tasgall
Speak with Tasgall
The Great Beast

The strange hill-beasts have become a serious problem of late. It seems that they are ruled by a secretive matriarch who serves the drakes. If she can be defeated, perhaps the threat of the hill-beasts will fade.
'You must slay the beast-mother!'

Crawlers can be found in the general area not far north of Aughaire.
Hunt crawlers for their flesh and bring it back to Tasgall to be roasted.
Tasgall has roasted the crawlers you brought him. You can return to him to learn the next step in his plan to defeat the Beast-mother.

The rock in the hill-beast lair is at the entrance to the valley, not far north of Aughaire.
Tasgall has given you some roasted crawler-flesh, which you should bring to a certain rock in the lairs of the hill-beasts.
Having successfully defeated the Beast-mother, you should return to Tasgall's camp and speak with him.
You have defeated the vengeful Beast-lord and saved Tasgall's life. Speak with him.

'You have done great deeds for the Trév Gállorg already, ${PLAYER}, and I know that you will do more still! Our distant kindred have not yet had the benefit of your friendship, and I grieve for them.
'They hunt their prey in the great swamp of Malenhad, east of Fasach-larran. It is a dangerous place, shaded by poisonous clouds and damp with foul water, home to strange beasts. Our hunters bring us much food and other things of worth from Malenhad, but we need to send them supplies so they can do their work.
'Bring these goods to Othran at Tyrn Lhuig, the hunting camp in the south-western corner of the swamp. You will find hunting-challenges there for yourself, if you are prepared.'
'You have come with supplies from Talaghlan? That is good, for ours were running short. Tyrn Lhuig has some of the finest hunters of the Trév Gállorg, but no Man can hunt without supplies.'
'Why do you come to this place?'
Bring the hunting supplies to Othran
The Brimstone Swamp
Taraghlan told you of a hunting-camp, Tyrn Lhuig, on the south-western edge of the great swamp of Malenhad.

'Bring those supplies to Othran in Tyrn Lhuig, the hunting-camp in the south-western corner of Malenhad. The hunters will have need of them.
'The great swamp of Malenhad is east of Fasach-larran. You will find it without difficulty if you follow your nose.'

Othran is at Tyrn Lhuig, the hunting-camp in the south-western corner of Malenhad, east of Fasach-larran.
Taraghlan has asked you to bring the supplies to his kinsman Othran at the hunting camp in Malenhad.
Defeated drakes in Nád Nathair (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'This, the Búth Sánkhas, has witnessed many tales, both tragic and triumphant, for the songs of the Trév Gállorg record all things. Many of my people have perished while testing their bravery and seeking to leave a glorious legacy, and their stories are passed from one to another here in the Búth Sánkhas.
'Bloodwing, the mightiest of the drakes of Nád Nathair, has claimed the lives of many such glory-seekers. She perches atop the great cliffs to the north of Aughaire and rules her brood of drakes with sharp teeth and cruel talons.
'The tale will be great indeed if you and your allies can best Bloodwing and her brood. Travel north to Nád Nathair and climb past the lower slopes where hill-beasts roam and seek out Bloodwing atop the cliffs. She is a mighty foe, not to be challenged lightly. Your tale will be the better for it.'

'Bloodwing is defeated? You have succeeded where many of my people have failed, ${PLAYER}! Crannog was right to call you friend of the Trév Gállorg, for you have brought us much good, and this only the latest!
'This reward was set aside for the one who would defeat Bloodwing, though few believed it could happen. I give it now to you.'
Defeat drakes in Nád Nathair (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Cuinthorn told you of the great drake Bloodwing and tasked you with defeating it.
'Bloodwing rules her brood from high atop the cliffs of Nád Nathair, north of Aughaire in Fasach-larran. Climb past the slopes where hill-beasts roam, and you will come to the drake's nest.'
'The Búth Sánkhas will ring with songs about your battle with Bloodwing.'
'You fought bravely against Bloodwing and will be long-remembered for it.'

Bloodwing rules her brood of drakes from the summit of the cliffs of Nád Nathair, above the lower slopes where hill-beasts roam. Nád Nathair is north of Aughaire, in Fasach-larran.
Cuinthorn told you of Bloodwing, a mighty drake who has claimed the lives of many great heroes, and wondered if you and your allies would be the ones to end her reign.

Cuinthorn is in the Búth Sánkhas of Aughaire, south-east of the market.
Cuinthorn is waiting to hear of your success against Bloodwing and her brood of drakes.
Defeated hill-beasts (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'I came forth from Aughaire intending to halt the spread of hill-beasts further into Fasach-larran, ${PLAYER}, but the creatures are too many.
'If you are deserving of the friendship of the Trév Gállorg, you will aid me with my charge. North-west of here, you will find a sloping path into Nád Nathair. It is a place of menace, and from there come the hill-beasts that prowl Fasach-larran.
'Defeat many of the hill-beasts you find there, and we will speak again when you return.'
'You have defeated a number of hill-beasts? I am glad to hear it, for now we may proceed with the next step in our hunt.'
Defeat hill-beasts (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Strange Beasts
Tasgall has tried to halt the spread of hill-beasts throughout Fasach-larran, but the creatures are too numerous for him to manage alone.
'The slopes of Nád Nathair are north-west of here. Climb them and defeat as many hill-beasts as you can, and I will think of some way we can fight them more effectively.'
'You found my brother? That is good, but you must aid Tasgall in his campaign against the hill-beasts if you are to earn my recommendation to Crannog!'

Hill-beasts stalk the slopes of Nád Nathair to the north-west of Tasgall's camp-site, in Fasach-larran.
Tasgall has asked you to defeat many hill-beasts while he thinks of some way to resist them more effectively.

Tasgall's camp-site is north of Aughaire and south-east of Nád Nathair.
You have defeated many hill-beasts and should now return to Tasgall.
Collected turtle-meat (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collected turtle shell-plates (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Perhaps you seek more challenging prey?
'The giant turtles of Malenhad are valued by my people both for their meat, which is edible, and for their shells. They can be deadly foes at close quarters, and if you fight them, you may damage their shells before you manage to kill them.
'I will pay for both their shell plates and meat if you think you are up to the challenge. The turtles live throughout this part of the swamp.'
'Good shells. Meat isn't spoiled yet. I will pay for this.'
'The turtles aren't too much for you, are they, Southron?'
Bring the turtle meat and shell plates to Othran
Collect turtle-meat (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collect turtle shell-plates (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Malenhad is home to turtles of enormous size, which the Hillmen value for their edible meat and tremendous shells.

The turtles live throughout the western reaches of Malenhad. Othran is at Tyrn Lhug, in the south-west corner of Malenhad.
Othran has offered to pay you for the meat and shell plates of the giant turtles of Malenhad.

'So, Southron, you have proven yourself more than worthy to hunt in the brimstone swamp of Malenhad. Perhaps you wish to gain even more glory? There is prey in this swamp that is too dangerous even for we who have hunted these swamps since time out of mind.
'I speak of the dreaded Ancient Ironscale, a monster so deadly that none of my people have ever faced it... and survived to tell the tale of it.
'I think it will be impossible for one southron, however doughty, to defeat such a foe, but even were you able, with companions, to kill this beast, I would be forced to admit you are true hunters and warriors of renown. The Ancient Ironscale is a rare beast, but it can sometimes be found amongst its lesser brethren in the swamp.'

'What? You have slain the Ancient Ironscale? I am astonished! I admit that I had not expected you to even make the attempt, not after telling you of its terrible menace.
'I must be honest with you, Southron, this was not quite the legendary foe I made it out to be. In fact, we hunters seek out the beast when we come of age in an ancient ritual amongst our people. Of course, not all of the youths return from these hunts....
'But still, it is a great accomplishment for one not born to the harsh, blasted hills and foetid bogs of the North. I must praise you for a worthy deed. You are a true hunter of Angmar.'
The brimstone swamp of Malenhad is also home to a terrible breed of beast, which the hillmen call the \qAncient Ironscale\q.
'The Ancient Ironscale is too great a challenge for you, Southron? I am not surprised.'
'You are stronger than you appear to hunt so well within Malenhad.'
'Welcome, mighty ${PLAYER}, slayer of the dreaded Ironscale.'

The rare Ancient Ironscale can sometimes be found amongst its lesser brethren in Malenhad.
Othran has challenged you and your fellows to slay the dreaded Ancient Ironscale, lord of the fell turtles of Malenhad.

Othran is at his camp in the western part of Malenhad.
You should return to Othran to tell him the tale of your victory against the dreaded Ancient Ironscale.
Collected swamp-fly wings (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collected Swamp-lurker legs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'There are many strange beasts in this swamp. Vile creatures abound in this place -- perhaps the evil air fosters their growth -- but even the vilest of vermin has its use.
'Swamp-fly wings are light, flexible, and tough and can be used for many crafting tasks. Swamp-lurkers are creatures of a truly strange nature, but for all their odd appearance, their legs make a tasty meal when roasted.
'Hunt these verminous beasts, and I will pay well for these trophies. You can find these creatures scattered throughout this part of the swamp.'
'Good, good. In Malenhad, we must make use of any beast we find.'
'Can you not find enough of the vermin?'
Bring the trophies to Othran
Collect swamp-fly wings (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collect Swamp-lurker legs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
The Value of Vermin
Malenhad, the vile brimstone swamp of Angmar, is rife with vile and disgusting creatures, but even the strangest of these creatures has its uses to the Hillmen of Angmar.

Swamp-lurkers and swamp-flies can be found throughout the swamp near the hunters' camp.
Othran has asked you to collect Swamp-lurker legs and swamp-fly wings, which his people use to their benefit.
Collected blade-beak ravager beaks (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'You there... you help Reko?
'Ravager claws. No, how do you say it? Beaks? Like birds? Yes, ravager beaks.
'You go get ravager beaks. I will give you shiny pieces of metal taken from Orc-folk. Many blade-beak ravagers not far.'
'You have brought me many beaks. That is good. Here is the shiny metal.'
'No beaks? No shiny metal.'
Bring the blade-beak ravager beaks to Reko at Lehmä-koti.
Collect blade-beak ravager beaks (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Claws of the Earth
Reko, the Earth-kin hunter, desires the beaks of blade-beak ravagers, though for what, the creature would not say.

Blade-beak ravagers can be found throughout Ram Dúath.
Reko has asked you to collect the blade-beak ravager beaks he desires.
Collected root vegetables (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Listen, little one. You are brave to come here and help us. Maybe if you are fighting Orcs and flying bat-women anyway, you will do us another service? We eat the fruits of the earth -- root vegetables -- that grow in the gorges to the east, the old little people call it Duvairë. But now the Orcs and flying bat-women make it hard for us to gather them. If you are there killing, maybe you can bring us some vegetables, too?'
'Very good! These will make a good stew. You have our thanks, little one.'
'We want the root vegetables that grow to the east in the Duvairë.'
Bring the root vegetables back to Eetu at Lehmä-koti
Collect root vegetables (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Fruits of the Earth
The Earth-kin are fond of a certain kind of tuber that grows in the gorges in the east side of Ram Dúath in the Duvairë -- the places now frequented by the Orkish-army and merrevail.

The root vegetables grow in the gorges on the east side of Ram Dúath in the Duvairë.
Eetu has asked you to gather vegetables for the Earth-kin of the Suuri-lehmä.

'You there...you will help the Jorthkyn, yes?
'Spiders make silk. We need silk. You kill spiders, take their silk, then we give you the Orcs' shiny metal.
'We have much shiny metal taken from Orcs. Little people like shiny things, yes?'
'Good silk. Here is the shiny metal.'
'No silk? No shiny metal.'
Bring the spider-silk to Aarnikka
Collect skeins of spider-silk (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Silken Strands
The Earth-kin, rugged, practical, and earthy as they are, make extensive use of silk, which they obtain almost exclusively from spiders.

There are spiders throughout Ram Dúath.
Aarnikka has asked you to collect silk from the spiders of the Ram Dúath.
Destroyed Tór Gailvin standards (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'I know of your test, ${PLAYER}, and am prepared to do my part.
'You have already been to the fortress of Tór Gailvin, the home that was given to the Trév Duvárdain by their new masters, the evil that sits in Carn Dûm. Raith believes that wresting the tokens of the Enemy from the Trév Duvárdain of Tór Gailvin is enough; I do not agree.
'Return to Tór Gailvin, north-east of Aughaire, and destroy the standards that fly above its walls. This will send a clear message to the Trév Duvárdain and their masters. I am sure of it. If you do this, I will tell Crannog the tale of your success.'

'You have returned alive from Tór Gailvin, and I delight to see it! The standards no longer fly above the fortress? I will tell Crannog of your victory over the Trév Duvárdain, but for my part I am satisfied and call you friend.'
Destroy Tór Gailvin standards (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Return to Tór Gailvin, the fortress north-east of Aughaire, and destroy the standards that fly above it. If you are able to do this, I will report your success to Crannog.'
'The Trév Duvárdain will not soon forget your deeds in Tór Gailvin.'
'Domongart cannot hold Tór Gailvin forever.'

The fortress of Tór Gailvin is north-east of Aughaire.
