Defeated Muiráthakh

'The lords of Carn Dûm sent three of their servants to quell discontent in Fasach-falroid, ${PLAYER}, and we must strike them now before any lives are lost!
'Muiráthakh, the Silent Judge, keeps his court east of here, in a dangerous section of the city; there is no law to justify his misdeeds. Travel with your allies to his court and bring him to his end. But beware of Fûshath the Beast, who acts as executioner for Muiráthakh and is never far from his master.
'Do this for the family of Uthagan, ${PLAYER}, as much as for the rest of the Trév Gállorg.'

'I have already learned of your success, ${PLAYER}! The family of Uthagan rejoices at your vengeance, wherever they may be.
'The lords of Carn Dûm will not be pleased that Muiráthakh has been cast down. Let them shiver in their palaces, and dread to hear our footstep approach, for soon it will be their time to join him in death!'
Defeat Muiráthakh
Muiráthakh, the Silent Judge
Raghnaid has charged you with ending the reign of Muiráthakh, the Silent Judge, who holds Donnvail in a grip of fear.

'Muiráthakh must be ended if Donnvail is to cast off the shackles of Carn Dûm. Find him at his court deep within the city, through the arch to the east. Beware of Fûshath the Beast, who often patrols near to Muiráthakh's court.'
'Muiráthakh is no more, and his reign is ended!'
'The family of Uthagan would cheer your defeat of Muiráthakh, ${PLAYER}.'
'Muiráthakh will trouble us no more. The Silent Judge, he shall remain...forever silent.'
'Donnvail shakes off the shackles of its oppressors.'

Muiráthakh, the Silent Judge, holds court deep within the city of Donnvail, through the arch east of Una and her allies.
Raghnaid has tasked you and your allies with ending the reign of Muiráthakh.

Raghnaid is within the city of Donnvail, north-east of Fail-á-Khro.
You have defeated Muiráthakh and should bring news of your triumph to Raghnaid.
Collected skull-amulets (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collected bloodstone-pendants (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'The Trév Duvárdain press us at every opportunity, ${PLAYER}. We must oppose them with all our strength, but still Crannog insists on caution. Caution!
'The Trév Duvárdain serve the commanders of Angmar now, and they carry their tokens. In return for their bondage, the Trév Duvárdain have been given the fortress-city of Tór Gailvin. We must take these tokens from them and show that the Trév Gállorg will not stand for such betrayal!
'The fortress of Tór Gailvin stands to the north-east of Aughaire. Travel there and wrest skull-amulets and bloodstone-pendants from the traitors who now live in that place. Return to me with these tokens, and I will tell Crannog of your efforts on behalf of the Trév Gállorg.'

'The evil lords of Angmar must be very displeased now with the Trév Duvárdain that were given Tór Gailvin, for you have bloodied their noses with your attack!
'I will tell Crannog of your success, and he will have no doubt of it: these amulets and pendants sing of your victory!'

'Tór Gailvin is north-east of Aughaire. Have you forgotten that I asked you to collect skull-amulets and bloodstone-pendants from its defenders?
'If you cannot do this, I will tell Crannog of your failure.'
Bring skull-amulets and bloodstone-pendants to Raith
Collect skull-amulets (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collect bloodstone-pendants (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Trophies of War
Raith has petitioned the chieftain of Aughaire for greater action against the Trév Duvárdain, and Crannog has recommended that you prove yourself by facing the dangers of Tór Gailvin.
'The Trév Duvárdain will not long hold Tór Gailvin. Soon they will fall.'
'You prove an effective ${CLASS}, ${PLAYER}.'

The fortress of Tór Gailvin is north-east of Aughaire, and its defenders carry the skull-amulets and bloodstone-pendants that Raith wants.
Raith of Aughaire has asked you to wrest signs of the loyalty of the Trév Duvárdain to Angmar from the defenders of Tór Gailvin.
Planted false orders (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'You fought well and bravely in Clúcath, ${PLAYER}, and I appreciate the mercy you have shown to me; Domongart and Avair did not understand, and perhaps they never will. I am no longer Drostan; now I am Soltakh, \qHe Who Is Changed,\q and Soltakh seeks to be redeemed.
'I can help the Trév Gállorg with what I know, brave ${RACE}: I know how the Orcs receive their orders, and we can use this knowledge to our advantage. Bring an ally or two with you on this excursion, and our success will be certain.
'The city of Dûn Covád, in the western hills north of Fail-á-Khro, is crawling with Orcs; these Orcs keep their orders in strongboxes located throughout the city. Take these pages I have in my possession; they were prepared by Domongart, but I have replaced several key points -- they will sow dissension and discontent among the Orcs if you place them in the strongboxes of Dûn Covád.'

'Very good, ${PLAYER}! I am hopeful we will quickly reap the benefit of our cunning. The next strike must land quickly, for it is aimed at a dangerous target: Gillë Andras, the Lord of the Western Marches.'
Plant false orders (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Soltakh
False Orders
Drostan, now stripped of his name and called Soltakh among the Trév Gállorg, is anxious to redeem himself.

'I will bring honour to the name Soltakh through you, ${PLAYER}, and the deeds of Drostan will be forgotten.
'The strongboxes into which you should place the false orders are located within the city of Dûn Covád, in the western hills north of Fail-á-Khro. Bring an ally or two with you, for the city is greatly defended.'

Strongboxes can be found throughout the city of Dûn Covád, in the western hills north of Fail-á-Khro.
Soltakh has asked you to slip false orders into the strongboxes used by the Angmarim chain of command for communication of tasks.

Soltakh is at Fail-á-Khro, south of Dûn Covád and north of Aughaire.
Having slipped the false orders into the Angmarim strongboxes, you should return to Soltakh at Fail-á-Khro.

'If the orders you have planted do their work, the leader of the armies that now threaten Fasach-falroid may be already doomed, ${PLAYER}, and not even know it! His name is Gillë Andras, and he is the Lord of the Western Marches.
'Even now, he is likely receiving his new orders: to travel to Dûn Covád with a small retinue to monitor the Orcs in that city under his command. He will be leaving the sturdy defences of his command in Donnvail and coming to the lesser defences of Dûn Covád. With your allies, you can make your way into Dûn Covád, north of here in the western hills, and defeat Gillë Andras apart from his lieutenants. As this plan ripens, Soltakh proves his worth! May Drostan be forgotten!
'Defeat the Lord of the Western Marches, ${PLAYER}. This blow will be a great strike for the Trév Gállorg, if you and your allies can see it done.'

'Our plan is fulfilled, ${PLAYER}, and you have brought great joy to Soltakh, \qHe Who Is Changed!\q
'Already the memory of Drostan falls from me. We have done much good this day, friend ${RACE}, and I thank you for it.'
The Lord of the Western Marches
Soltakh has arranged for the transfer of Gillë Andras, the Lord of the Western Marches, to Dûn Covád, where he can be faced on more even terms.

'Gillë Andras has likely been sent to Dûn Covád by now; if you strike quickly, you and your allies can face him without his defences!
'Dûn Covád is in the western foothills, north of Fail-á-Khro.'
'Your great deeds have saved Aughaire from the Angmarim!'

Gillë Andras, the Lord of the Western Marches, can be found within the city of Dûn Covád, in the western foothills north of Fail-á-Khro.
Soltakh has asked you and your allies to defeat Gillë Andras, the Lord of the Western Marches.

Soltakh is at Fail-á-Khro, north of Aughaire and south of Dûn Covád.
You have defeated Gillë Andras, the Lord of the Western Marches, and should now bring news of your triumph to Soltakh.
You have found a Token of the Silk-lady!

'The Silk-lady....I wish I knew more about her. I have heard only dark rumours of her presence in Bail Boglakh, but none among the hill-men here have seen her - or done so and lived to tell the tale at any rate.
'If you are willing to continue to aid me, I would ask you to gather your allies and scout within the fortress of Bail Boglakh to the north across the swamps, and see what clues you might find as to the whereabouts of this 'Silk-lady', if indeed she may hold my sister captive.'

'These tokens you have found certainly suggest that the Silk-lady does reside in Bail Boglakh as we suspected.
'But what is this? On the back of these tokens is an inscription of the high tower at Bail Boglakh... It must be there that this evil woman resides! My sister must be held within!'
'We need to find more evidence of the Silk-lady's presence at Bail Boglakh - we have naught but rumours to act on yet.'
Find a clue to the Silk-lady's presence in Bail Boglakh
Bring the tokens to Lornë at Tyrn Lhuig
The Blood-bond
Lornë only knows the Silk-lady as a name of fear, but hopes you may be able to find more clues in the Angmarim fortress of Bail Boglakh.
Lornë has asked you to gather some allies and seek out any clues as to the whereabouts of the so-called 'Silk-lady' of Bail Boglakh, an Angmarim fortress to the north of Malenhad.
You have slain Muirnë!

'So, it seems that the Silk-lady holds the key to my sister's fate, and that she is conveniently at hand in a nearby outpost.
'I must tell you, though, that the outpost is heavily-guarded, and what I have heard of the Silk-lady, I fear that you would not be able to fight your way to find her on your own. If you will undertake to learn my sister's fate, you should bring allies with you.
'If you do choose to confront her, take these tokens and approach her tower. Having slain several of her favoured minions, she should not refuse such a challenge from you.'

'What have you learned? What? No! It is impossible!
'No... but I must accept the truth of what you tell me. Muirnë was ever a wilful child, spoiled selfish. But still, to become a spider-keeper of the Iron Crown! I have wasted a year of my life weeping for the fate of a monster!
'Alas, this is a bitter draught to down. But dark though these tidings be, you have done what I asked, Southron. You have my thanks... I am too deeply in your debt, but I will try to pay you what I can.'
Challenge the Silk-lady
Return to Lornë and tell her of Muirnë's fate

Lornë believes that the Silk-lady is holding her sister Muirnë captive within the high tower of Bail Boglakh.
She has asked you to confront the Silk-lady in the hopes of freeing her at last.
'Alas, poor Muirnë! But it is better that she is dead than that she continue to serve the evil men of Angmar.'
'Would that you could have saved my sister, ${PLAYER}, but alas, it was not meant to be.'

The Silk-lady is in the Angmarim fortress of Bail Boglakh on the north side of Malenhad, which guards the road into eastern Angmar.
Lornë has asked you and your companions to confront the Silk-lady at the high tower therein, in hopes of finding and freeing her sister Muirnë.

You confronted the Silk-lady and learned that she was in fact Lornë's sister Muirnë. You defeated the Silk-lady in combat and now must bear the dark tidings back to Lornë.
Lornë can be found at Tyrn Lhuig in Malenhad.
Bail Róva commander Defeated!

'Listen well, stranger. To make my way here, I must do some hunting with the other men of this little camp, but in truth I am not here to live the life of a hunter. I am here for the sake of my sister, Muirnë, and if things have gone as I fear, I will take a blood price from her murderer. But I still hope that the worst has not come to pass, and if she still lives, I wish to rescue her from her captors.
'Many months past, she left our home in Aughaire to go questing with kin, but on the way I am told she was taken by the Angmarim. From what I can tell, they were encamped at the outpost of Bail Rova, but thus far I have been unable to learn more.
'Will you help me? That encampment lies to the west on the way to Ram Dúath. If the Angmarim had hoped to learn something from my sister, they would have brought her to the commander of Bail Róva.'

'So, she was not there after all. All my patience, wasted! But I should offer my thanks. I might have waited here much longer and still learned nothing!
'The Silk-lady...that is a name I have heard, though. Recently it has become a name of dread in these hills. Whispered tales speak of a cruel and vicious woman of Angmar who commands deadly spiders. It is said she is as dangerous to her fellow Angmarim as she is to the enemies of the Iron Crown....'

'What? Muirnë? You ask for her? Ha!
'You'll not find her here, Southron! She moved on long ago. Seek you the Silk-lady if you would know more.
'But I think the Silk-lady will not be troubled with your presence, Outlander...not if I kill you here and now and redeem the incompetence of my men!'
Look for Muirnë
Confront the Bail Róva camp commander
The Blood-price
Lornë told you that she joined the hunting party to find her missing sister, Muirnë, only she fears that the worst has befallen her.
'Please, look for my sister, Muirnë. I must hold to the hope she lives, until it is proven otherwise.'

The Angmarim camp of Bail Róva is North-west of Tyrn Lhuig, guarding the entrance to the Ram Dúath.
Lornë has asked you to look for some sign of her sister and if necessary to confront the outpost's commander for news of Muirnë.

Lornë is at the hunters' camp in Malenhad.
Muirnë was not in Bail Rova, but the Angmarim commander mentioned a Silk-lady who may know more. You should return to Lornë and tell her what you have learned.
Collected water at the banner-marked pools (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'There is much water in Angmar, but most of it is foul, poisoned, and deadly to drink. Even the rare springs of pure water can sometimes turn foul, when some old poison leeches from the soil.
'Of course, we must know which water is pure and which foul, but it is a deadly game to tell merely by taste. Instead we collect water from various springs and feed it to swamp-fly grubs. These creatures will sicken and die if they are given foul water.
'Banners have been placed at six of the shallow springs of the swamp where once fresh water could be found. Take these water-skins, find the banners, and collect water from the six springs, so that we may learn if the springs still run true.'
'Well done. I trust you remember which skin came from which spring? Very good, ${PLAYER}.'
'The springs await you ${PLAYER} -- I presume this task is not beyond you?'
Collect water at the banner-marked pools (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring the water-skins back to Murdaigán
Water of Life and Death
Malenhad has long been a place of poisonous waters and vapours, corrupted by the powers of ancient Angmar during the reign of the Witch-king. There is little of value left there.

The banner-marked pools are spread throughout western Malenhad.
Murdaigán has asked you to go to six springs in the swamp and collect samples of water which he can use to confirm whether those springs have not yet been poisoned by the filth of Angmar.

Murdaigán is back at the hunters' camp in the south-west corner of Malenhad.
Having collected several water samples, you should bring them back to Murdaigán.
Collected flame-worm hides (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Hold... I would have a moment of your time. You seem to be capable of looking after yourself in this harsh land. We hunt the beasts of the swamp, and our most valuable and dangerous prey are the fire-worms.
'Their hides are extremely tough, proof against both water and fire, and can be worked into armour, clothes, and all manner of useful things. If you should happen to collect any hides of the local worms, please bring them here, and I will pay you well.
'But then, you are a southron... you may not have the courage or prowess it will take.'
'Ha! This is good. We will both profit. Here are your coins.'
'Were the worms too much for you to handle, Southron?'
Bring the worm hides back to Rodakhan
Collect flame-worm hides (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Rodakhan the hunter has said he will pay well for worm-hides. However, worms are some of the most dangerous beasts of the swamp.
Flame-worms can be found in the south-east part of Malenhad. Rodakhan has asked you to collect flame-worm hides for him and can be found in the camp of Tyrn Lhuig.
You have found Machan

'Machan is a bold hunter. Perhaps too bold. He vowed to return with the hides of fire-worms from their lairs in Sálgaitë to the south-east, and he has not returned in good time.
'Would you look for Machan, Southron? It may be he is in need of assistance. I will reward you for your efforts....'
Find the hunter Machan
The Worm-hunter
Machan the hunter has gone missing after vowing to return with hides from the fearsome worms of Malenhad.

Machan the hunter should be somewhere in the region of Sálgaitë to the south-east.
The hunter Murdaigán has asked you to locate Machan, who was hunting fire-worms in Malenhad.
You have saved Machan

'Curse my foolish pride! I should never have ventured into this worm-lair on my own. There are just too many of them, and now that I have found this safe place, I do not dare try to sneak away on my own.
'Can you help me to escape? I would ask that you not tell the other hunters, for I would be ridiculed for the rest of my life.'

'Machan is safe then, is he? Good. He is an impulsive and proud man, and I had feared that he might have gotten in over his own head.
'Not that such a thing could ever happen, nor would his pride permit him to be rescued if it did.'
'I suspect that I -- and Machan -- owe you greater thanks than your tale suggests, and so I do thank you most sincerely.'
Talk to Machan when you are ready
Machan's Folly
Machan foolishly sought to hunt fire-worms alone and ended up trapped and wounded.
Help Machan to get out of the fire-worm lair.
Tell Murdaigán that Machan is safe.

'It occurs to me that this spirit you fought is after all a creature of the same ilk as those we seek to banish. He must not be controlled by the shrine, or he would not have been able to flee you so easily when he was on the brink of defeat.
'My guess is that another controls Deluches. The necromancers of Imlad Balchorth hide in a ruin high in the hills on the south side of the area. Quite possibly one of them is the protector of Deluches himself. I suspect, too, that you will find a second shrine in their lair. I was a fool to think they only had one.
'Find this master shrine. No doubt you will encounter your enemy again -- and mayhap the chief of the necromancers as well -- but this time if you are victorious, his defeat will be final...I hope'

'You have done very well indeed. Deluches was evidently the key to the necromancers' control over those spirits. It is unfortunate, though, that those which have been banished are but a small part of the host of Angmar.'
Banishing the Darkness
The sudden appearance of Deluches, the captain of the fell spirits, kept you from banishing the creatures from the shrine.
'Deluches escaped you once...he must not do so again!'
'You have undone the plans of the necromancers of Angmar. Well done!'

The necromancers of Imlad Balchorth can be found at the ruins high in the southern hills of the area.
The chief sorcerer of the necromancers, the Spirit-master, no doubt controls Deluches, the spirit-captain. Gautar has asked you to defeat him, and thus banish Deluches forever.

Eithel Úmfaer is in southern Imlad Balchorth, west of Myrkworth.
Deluches, captain of the fell spirits, has been summoned to Eithel Úmfaer, the master shrine in Imlad Balchorth, where he must be destroyed.

Gautar is back at Myrkworth, east and a bit north of Eithel Úmfaer.
You have defeated Deluches and banished at least some of the fell spirits of Angmar. You should bring the good tidings to Gautar.
Collected tokens of Angmar (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Angmar was avoided by my people long ago, for many things dwelled here that are better left alone. When we thought them gone, we foolishly came seeking wealth in this barren land. Unfortunately, with the coming of the False King, those fell things have been awakened.
'Perhaps the worst of the creatures which dwell here are the fell spirits, demons which have existed in Middle-earth since the First Age of this world. At the height of the Witch-realm of Angmar, the Witch-king had power to command these spirits, and it is said there are other creatures which have a similar power. It was these spirits that the Witch-king sent to the Barrow-downs after the passing of Cardolan. It is these spirits who stir the bones of the dead.
'I bid you to go west into Imlad Balchorth and confront these demons. Claim the Tokens of Angmar they carry. Perhaps we can use the tools of the Enemy to banish the fell spirits from Middle-earth.'
'That the sorcerers of Angmar would dare to commune with these fell spirits speaks well enough to their evil. No Man, dwarf, or Elf, pure of heart, would deign to do such... it is an abomination.'

'I know this is a dark task I have given you, but I bid you be of stout heart. In the end, we will be doing much to banish the dark spirits in Imlad Balchorth.
'The spirits are deep in Imlad Balchorth.'
Bring the tokens back to Gautar
Collect tokens of Angmar from Imlad Balchorth (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Spirits of Old
Imlad Balchorth is the dwelling place of a host of fell spirits, servants of Angmar.

There are fell spirits in Imlad Balchorth, in the southern upper passes, south and west from Myrkworth. Gautar is in Myrkworth.
Gautar has asked you to confront the fell spirits to learn if there might be a way to banish them from Middle-earth.
Deluches has escaped

'These tokens bear signs of Angmar, terrible sigils that may well be binding the fell spirits to this place. You must find the shrine used by the Angmarim in their rituals. I believe it is on an islet in a small pond in southern Imlad Balchorth. It may be difficult to find, for it appears as a large iron spike, which is not uncommon among the works of the Angmarim.
'If you call forth the spirits at the shrine, I believe they will come to that place one last time, there to be banished forever. It is a dreadful chance though...I will confess that my folk are not well-versed in dealings with evil spirits. I think the Elves would know more, and there are few enough of those in Angmar.'

'Alas, I had not reckoned that the spirits' master would himself be a fell spirit, able to interfere with your quest. Why, I wonder, was he able to escape you so easily?
'I have sent you into grave danger on a fool's errand. But perhaps we can still repair my error.'
Summon and defeat the spirits at the southern shrine

Gautar examined the tokens you recovered from the fell spirits and discovered that they bear signs of Angmar, sigils that may be binding the spirits to the mortal world. A name also was written upon them: Deluches.
'Have you banished the fell spirit Deluches? No? Please, you must draw him out and send him back to the Void!'

The shrine of the fell spirits is on an islet in a small pond in the southern part of Imlad Balchorth, south and a little west from Myrkworth.
Gautar has asked you to go to the shrine of the fell spirits in Imlad Balchorth. The shrine can be recognized as a large iron spike, a common feature of the works of the Angmarim which might make the shrine difficult to find.

Gautar is back at Myrkworth, north and a bit east from the shrine of Deluches.
You were unable to defeat the terrible captain of the spirits, Deluches, so the fell spirits could not be banished. You should return to Gautar and report these events.

'Know you aught of the lore of Angmar?
'Well, no matter. You will learn... if Nethraw will have anything to say about it. He is in a lonely vale, the Krúsle Lannan, far to the east of here, musing on the Seven Sentinels.
'I have no doubt he could use your assistance.'

'Well met, stranger! I have tarried here long, seeking to unravel a mystery from times past. Perhaps you can help me? Banfuir at least believes you to have some skill, else he would not have sent you.
'Look upon the seven statues behind me; doubtless you note that they each are missing the sword which they once held. This place is one of ancient evil, something that I have long studied, and I know too well the scars that have been left in its wake.
'This loathsome place may be where the doom of the northern kingdoms was wrought, but I will speak no more of it until I have recovered all seven of the swords.'
The Secret of the Swords
There are many old tales long forgotten in Angmar, but Nethraw is interested in only one.

The lore-master Nethraw can be found at the Krúsle Lannan, a considerable distance to the east of Gabilshathûr.
Banfuir suggested you speak with the lore-master Nethraw.

'Ah yes, where was I...? Well, the Seven Sentinels had sworn to keep a watch on Angmar, but there was no more kingdom of Arthedain to support them. The Seven maintained their vigil and upheld their oaths, but after many years, the six Men died. They were not replaced, as both Gondor and the remaining Dúnedain of Arnor had forgotten them.
'In sorrow, the Elf, whose name has been lost, made a vault in the knights' honour, and then he himself sailed west across the Sea. This is the vault of the Seven Sentinels, and an old tale tells that ancient treasure, imbued with a virtue for fighting the evil of Angmar, is buried here. Yet the keys to opening it are missing. The tale says that the vault can only be opened when the seven swords of the Seven Sentinels are once again raised, but the swords of those great heroes are long lost.
'Still, I have some clues. The first sword is called the Sword of Arvedui. It was borne by a knight who served Arvedui's son Aranarth, but who took up his vigil here rather than follow the other Dúnedain into obscurity. I believe that the sword is hidden somewhere around the dwarves' outpost of Gabilshathûr, which once was the site of the knight's watch-tower. The sword may still be hidden there, someplace.'

'Remarkable! So the tales are true! If this one sword has been found, perhaps the other six will reveal themselves as well! Perhaps the vault can be opened, and it may even hold some treasure that can be of use to us here!
'But I have raced ahead of myself. Recovering the other six swords will be no easy task. Indeed, it may well be an impossible quest. But we shall see....'
'Ah, I have no doubt the old tale is a mere fable. Or else the sword was lost long ago.'
Search for the sword of Arvedui
Bring the Sword of Arvedui to Nethraw
The Sword of Arvedui
Nethraw told you a tale of Seven Sentinels who swore to hold vigil over Angmar to ensure that the evil never returned.

'I am afraid I have let my enthusiasm for the old tales get the better of me.
'I should probably not have asked you to search for the sword, considering it is likely that either the sword was lost long ago, or else that the old tale is nothing more than a fable.'

The Sword of Arvedui is supposedly hidden somewhere around Gabilshathûr.
Nethraw has asked you to search Gabilshathûr for some evidence that the Sword of Arvedui was hidden there.

Nethraw is back at the Fane of the Seven Sentinels east, of Gabilshathûr.
You should bring the Sword of Arvedui to Nethraw.

'At last, the time has come to open the ancient vault! I believe each of these seven statues must be given the correct sword before the vault can be opened...but the tale is unfortunately a bit vague. I suppose we could try all the combinations, but that might take a long time.
'I have made a copy of the relevant verses -- here, perhaps you can puzzle it all out.'

'You have done it! This chest contains treasures of past ages forged to fight the forces of darkness!
'After all of your effort and the danger you have seen, it is only right that you choose one of these items as your just reward. The rest will be sent to my brethren to distribute.'
'Have you not recovered the treasure of the Seven Sentinels?'

'The third sword is called the Sword of Gondor. Of the host that fought the Witch-king at Fornost, many were knights and men-at-arms of Gondor, led by Eärnur, Prince of Gondor. One doughty knight, whose name has been lost, would not be outdone by the knights of Arthedain, and vowed to keep a vigil along with them.
'According to the tale, his watch-tower was at a place not far from here, called Maethad. Unfortunately, this place is infested with evil trolls, and worse, by the mighty Gertheryg, who are fearsome masters of arms.
'It would be all but impossible for you to venture into Maethad on your own, so if you would seek the third sword, I would counsel you to venture to the evil place only with stout companions.'
'You have impressed me mightily. The recovery of the Sword of Gondor is a great triumph over the evil creatures of Angmar, even if none of the other swords are recovered at all!'
'I knew I should not have asked you to go on this mission.'
Search for the Sword of Gondor
Bring the Sword of Gondor back to Nethraw
The Sword of Gondor
With the recovery of the swords of Arvedui and Rhudaur, Nethraw has become more confident that the remaining swords may be found.
'It will be very difficult to recover the Sword of Gondor if it is still to be found in Maethad.'

The Sword of Gondor is said to be found somewhere in Maethad, north of the Fane of the Seven Sentinels.
Nethraw has now asked you to search for the Sword of Gondor, in Maethad, a place garrisoned by many Trolls and Gertheryg. For this reason, you were cautioned not to venture there on your own.

Nethraw is back at the Fane of the Seven Sentinels, east of Gabilshathûr.
You should bring the Sword of Gondor to Nethraw.

'As I told you before, the other six swords will be much harder to recover, if indeed they still can be found at all.
'The second sword is called the Sword of Rhudaur. Evidently the Dúnedain knight who bore it was a descendant of those who fled the fall of Rhudaur long before and carried a sword from the days when Rhudaur was a kingdom of Arnor.
'According to the old tale, this knight's watch-tower seems to have once been found in the same location as one of the large Orc-camps north of Gabilshathûr. I know not which camp is the right one. But even if the sword can still be found, perhaps under such a marker as you found at Gabilshathûr, it will be no easy task to brave all those Orcs.'

'The Sword of Rhudaur!
'I am greatly heartened by your success! If the first two swords can be found where the tale tells, perhaps the remaining five will be found as well.
'The difficulty of collecting the swords grows. Make no doubt, I have asked you to find the easiest two swords first.'
'Alas, what have you done with the Sword of Rhudaur? Surely you have not lost it?'
Search for the Sword of Rhudaur
Bring the Sword of Rhudaur to Nethraw
The Sword of Rhudaur
You recovered the Sword of Arvedui, leading Nethraw to wonder if the other swords might not be recovered as well.
'I hope the Sword of Rhudaur is still there to be found. For all we know, it may long since have been looted by Orcs.'

The Sword of Rhudaur may be found at one of the fortified Orc-camps north of Gabilshathûr.
Nethraw has now asked you to search for the Sword of Rhudaur.

Nethraw is back at the Fane of the Seven Sentinels, east of Gabilshathûr.
You should bring the Sword of Rhudaur to Nethraw.

'The fourth sword is the Sword of Slaughter. The tale is unclear on this point, but I believe the knight who bore it was sickened by the carnage of the Battle of Fornost, and named his blade such because of the many corpses it left behind.
'The tale leads me to believe that this knight kept watch in the middle of one of the most dread areas of Angmar, in some high ruins a far distance west of the central island of Imlad Balchorth. Even then this region was known as a place of dread, a suitable place for this sword to be hidden.
'Again, I must warn you that allies will probably be required to recover this sword.'
'Four of the seven swords! Well done! But I fear the final three are in yet more dangerous parts of Angmar.'
'I fear this was but a foolish dream.'
Search for the Sword of Slaughter
Bring the Sword of Slaughter to Nethraw
The Sword of Slaughter
With every sword you find, Nethraw becomes more determined to find the others.
'I hesitate to ask you to venture into the accursed land of Imlad Balchorth merely for the sake of an old tale, but it seems there is some truth to the old story.'

The Sword of Slaughter is said to be found in a ruin in some high hills west of the large lake in Imlad Balchorth..
Nethraw has sent you to recover the Sword of Slaughter. You have been cautioned that it will be difficult to obtain without allies.

Nethraw is back at the Fane of the Seven Sentinels, east of Gabilshathûr.
You should bring the Sword of Slaughter to Nethraw.

'Next comes the Sword of Sorrow. This sword was carried by a knight who lost his lands and all his kin to the Angmarim. He swore his oath while bearing a terrible burden of sorrow and hatred.
'The tale says that this knight set up his tower not far east of here, in heights infested by evil drakes. These fell creatures are too fierce for any to fight on even terms, so yet again I must ask you to bring allies with you in the search for the sword.'
'We are near the end of our quest. There are but two swords left to collect!'
'Where is the Sword of Sorrow?'
Search for the Sword of Sorrow
Bring the Sword of Sorrow to Nethraw
The Sword of Sorrow
Four of the seven swords have been recovered, leaving only three.
'The Sword of Sorrow lies to the east, so the tale tells.'

The Sword of Sorrow is said to be found in drake-infested heights east of the Fane of the Seven Sentinels.
You have been sent to recover the Sword of Sorrow from its resting-place. Nethraw again suggests you take allies.

Nethraw is back at the Fane of the Seven Sentinels, east of Gabilshathûr.
You should bring the Sword of Sorrow to Nethraw.

'Finally, the last of the seven swords! This weapon is called the Sword of the Vigil, and it was borne by the leader of the Seven Sentinels, a knight who made his post in the most dangerous part of Angmar -- a place perhaps even more deadly than Carn Dûm itself!
'I speak of Nan Gurth, a place inhabited by terrible beasts and the most evil of foes. The tale tells not where in this dread place the sword can be found. Truly, I hesitate to ask you to go to such a terrible place, merely to satisfy my curiosity, and perhaps to uncover an ancient hoard. But too, it would be a shame to stop now, when we are so close!
'Certainly, as before, this quest is far too dangerous for a single adventurer to attempt alone.'
'The seven swords! Collected at last! I am trembling with excitement. But one small obstacle remains....'
'Where is the Sword of the Vigil?'
Search for the Sword of the Vigil
Bring the Sword of the Vigil to Nethraw
The Sword of the Vigil
You have recovered six of the seven swords, and Nethraw is most pleased.
'I would never forgive myself if I sent you to your death! Please be careful.'

The Sword of the Vigil is somewhere in Nan Gurth.
Nethraw told you the last of the seven swords may be found in a deadly place called Nan Gurth. He again warned you that allies will be required to obtain the sword.

Nethraw is back at the Fane of the Seven Sentinels, east of Gabilshathûr.
You should bring the Sword of the Vigil to Nethraw.

'The Sword of Twilight was carried by the lone Elf in the company of the Seven Sentinels. The name of that sword perhaps derives from the feeling amongst some of the Elves that their time in Middle-earth draws to an end, and perhaps is an allusion to the direction of their retreat. Who can say?
'At any odds, the tale says the Elf's sword may be found far to the north, not all that distant from the place my kindred have made for themselves to spy upon Carn Dûm. I believe the sword's hiding place is in a lair of great and terrible spiders. No one adventurer would be able to retrieve the sword alone, so once again I must counsel you to seek allies in your quest'
'You have done well to this point, but there is one great challenge left.'
'Where is the Sword of Twilight?'
Search for the Sword of Twilight
Bring the Sword of Twilight back Nethraw
The Sword of Twilight
Five of the seven swords have been recovered, leaving only two.
'I hope you will be able to retrieve the Sword of Twilight.'

The Sword of Twilight is in a lair of spiders far to the north, near Gath Forthnír.
Nethraw has sent you in search of the Sword of Twilight, It seems once again that allies will be required to obtain the Sword from its hiding-place.

Nethraw is back at the Fane of the Seven Sentinels, east of Gabilshathûr.
You should bring the Sword of Twilight to Nethraw.
Collected rough gems (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Greetings, ${RACE}. I heard what you did for us. We are all at your service, I'm sure. Perhaps I can point you to a good thing in the way of thanks.
'Hiding out here, we can no longer go out prospecting or mining some of the outlying gem-bearing lodes we found. We know, though, that some of the minions of the Enemy -- trolls, gertheryg, and the like -- have found those old mining locations and are gathering gems themselves.
'If you wish, you could go out hunting the Enemy in Gorothlad, in the general vicinity of Maethad. Many of those evil folk are no doubt gathering what gems they can, and you may be able to retrieve some of them. I'll give you a good price if you could bring me some.'
'Ha! You have done very well to gather all these stones. Have no fear... I will give you a good price!'
'Of course, not every troll is carrying around a hoard of gems! You will have to look harder!'
Bring the rough gems to Bothwar
Collect rough gems (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

The Dwarves of Gabilshathûr are unable to go out and prospect in these dark days, but they know that the armies of the Enemy have discovered some of their old mining locations and are extracting gems themselves.

Gem-bearing servants of the Enemy may be found in Maethad, the arena to the east of Gabilshathûr.
Bothwar has offered to pay you for any gems you can find on the servants of the Enemy.
Collected the gemstone-hoard

'You're a good sort, ${PLAYER}, and I feel that I can trust you not to betray my confidence in another matter.
'When I was called back to Gabilshathûr for guard-duty, I did not have time to recover a hoard of gems I had mined within the canyons of Gorothlad. I left it a bit near to the cave-claw nests in southern Gorothlad, and the filthy creatures likely have it surrounded.
'Can you recover the gem-hoard for me? It does the cave-claws no good to have it, their love for shiny things notwithstanding; the Dwarves of Gabilshathûr will be able to put the gems to good use.'

'Well done, ${PLAYER}! I have done more good for Gabilshathûr while on guard-duty than I ever did while mining: those gem-bearing rocks mined with all due haste, and a hoard of gems retaken from the cave-claws almost as quickly!
'You deserve all of the credit, of course. Do not let me understate your accomplishments! Take this reward -- it has been well-earned!'
'The cave-claws in the southern reaches of Gorothlad have likely taken my gem-hoard back to their nests. Look for them in the canyons south of Maethad, to the east of Gabilshathûr.'
Bring the gemstone-hoard to Bothwar
Collect the gemstone-hoard
Hidden Gems
Bothwar has told you the location of a cache of gems he was unable to retrieve before he was assigned his current duty in Gabilshathûr.
'You have a nose for gems, ${PLAYER}!'
'It seems to me that I am always being chosen for guard-duty.'

The gem-hoard is near the cave-claw nests within Dolroth in southern Gorothlad, north and east of Gabilshathûr.
The dwarf-miner Bothwar has asked you to retrieve a hoard of gems for him.
Mined gem-bearing rock (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'I am always glad to do my share of the work here at Gabilshathûr, as long as every other dwarf here pulls his own weight. It can be frustrating to be chosen for guard-duty when you have found a promising lode, but that is sometimes the way of it.
'If you don't mind helping out an eager miner, you could mine the gems from the rocks I have had to leave behind. You would be doing me a great service, and the wealth of Gabilshathûr will only be improved by your assistance!
'The rocks in question are north of Gabilshathûr. Follow the road northwards until you can turn east into Gorothlad. Through the sparse trees, you will come to the entrance of Maethad. Cave-claws often gather in the rocks outside Maethad, so use care while mining the gems!'

'You have my thanks, ${PLAYER}! I would rather mine, but I am a dwarf who knows his duty and would never gainsay my betters!
'So it is only right that we have mined those gem-bearing rocks after all...everyone is the victor! Take this as a reward with my good regards.'
'I will always perform my duty, but I would rather be mining. Have you not found the gem-bearing rocks to the east of Gabilshathûr and south of Maethad?'
Mine gem-bearing rocks (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring gemstone-rocks to Bothwar
Would Rather Mine
Bothwar of Gabilshathûr is aggrieved at missing an opportunity for mining some quality gems.

'You will find the gem-bearing rocks I had to leave unmined if you follow the road north from Gabilshathûr until you can turn east and pass through the sparse trees of Gorothlad. The stones are by the entrance to Maethad. Mine the gems from the stones!'

Gem-bearing rocks of the sort Bothwar described can be found outside the entrance to Maethad. He told you to follow the road north from Gabilshathûr until you could turn east and pass through the sparse trees of Gorothlad.
Bothwar is annoyed that he was pulled from his mining efforts to undertake guard-duty and has asked you to finish his mining.

Bothwar is on the bridge in the middle of Gabilshathûr, west and south of Gorothlad.
You have mined the gem-bearing rocks of which Bothwar spoke and should return to him with the fruits of your labour.
You have knocked some sense back into Arngrim

'Not everyone here does what he is told, ${PLAYER}: Arngrim is one of these. He has been acting strangely for a while now, but he has not refused direct orders until recently. He was ordered to return to Gabilshathûr for guard-duty against the Orcs, just as I was...only he didn't!
'He has long claimed that there was mithril to be found in this land, though every dwarf knows it be madness, but his delay in returning can only be explained by this cause: he thinks he has found some!
'If you are willing to help me with this one last thing, I will be very pleased. Arngrim may have abandoned his senses, but he is still a dwarf, and we owe him this much. Look for him atop the ridges on the very southern reaches of Imlad Balchorth, to the north of this outpost.'

'You have done well, ${PLAYER}! It is good that Arngrim has abandoned his mad quest...for now, at least.
'Take this reward and rejoice at a job done well. You have earned it!'

'You! You are here to steal it, aren't you! My mithril! My beautiful lovely mithril! The voice has told me so. The true sweet voice of the mithril! Nay, get back I say! Do not make me! Don't make me!'
Find Arngrim
The Scent of Mithril
The dwarf Arngrim has vanished after telling some of the other miners that he was sure he knew the location of a mithril vein in the hills of Imlad Balchorth.

'Arngrim should have returned for guard-duty instead of continuing his foolish hunt for mithril in these lands. Look for him north of here, atop the ridges on the very southern reaches of Imlad Balchorth.'

Arngrim is seeking mithril atop a ridge on the very southern reaches of Imlad Balchorth, north of Gabilshathûr.
Bothwar is concerned that Arngrim, slightly befuddled at the best of times, might have gotten himself into trouble in the southern reaches of Imlad Balchorth.

Bothwar is on the bridge in the middle of Gabilshathûr, south of Imlad Balchorth.
You have returned Arngrim to his senses and should report back to Bothwar.
Collected a First Marshals' mark

'Your weak frame and tender flesh will bruise too easily if you attempt this, sluggard! But if you desire great favour and glory in the name of the Great Eye, then perhaps you will throw your life away on this endeavour.
'Within the towers and keeps of these lands, our enemy takes root from time to time. When they do, First Marshals of their army stalk the halls as attendants and support for their masters.
'Storm their holdings and collect their marks. Bring me one, and I will be well-favoured indeed. Accept this task and fail, and I will feed your gizzard to the trolls!'

'Scraps! You bring me scraps! What am I to do with these, you pathetic ${RACE}? I should gut you where you stand and use your entrails to season the gruel.
'Such failures cannot be tolerated... but they must, only because you are the troops we have for our menial tasks. Begone from my sight.
Chieftain Durulkum mutters. 'Yes, this suits my purpose well.'

'Standing around, are you? What value you add to this army, ${RACE}. I can see you at the head of our army, strapped to the front of battering-ram, repeatedly slammed into the enemy's fortress!
'Get me what I need! Only towers and keeps controlled by the enemy will house the First Marshals, you worthless scum!'
Return to Chieftain Durulkum at Dâr-gazag
Collect a First Marshals' mark
First Marshals' Mark

First Marshals stand only behind the Captain-General in rank among the enemy army. Chieftain Durulkum wants their marks of rank to further the favour this war-host gains with Angmar, Mordirith, and Lugbúrz.

First Marshals can only be found in towers and keeps claimed by the enemy.
Chieftain Durulkum at Dâr-gazag informed you that the marks borne by the First Marshals of the enemy army gain great favour with Mordirith in Angmar.
Collected footmen's badges (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Listen well, ${RACE}. I'm not here to wipe your nose and look after you. I'm here to see that the war-host out of Angmar clears the way of the enemy. To do that, I need to prove that we're doing well against these curs.
'I need your help for that. These duties are beneath an Orc of the Krahjarn, and I'll not dirty my hands with such worthless creatures. You, on the other hand, seek the approval which I've already earned.
'So here's what we're going to do. You'll kill the footmen you find out there and bring me their badges.'
'These badges are barely worth my time, worm, but they'll have to do. Now, get out of here before I gut you!'
'What are you doing standing around here, slug? Get ou there and get those badges!'
Return to Dâr-gazag and speak with Chieftain Durulkum
Collect footmen's badges (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Footmen's Badges

Footmen, wardens, and scouts patrolling the wild of the Ettenmoors adorn their uniforms with badges denoting their rank. You have been tasked with recovering these badges and delivering them to Chieftain Durulkum at Gramsfoot.

Seek footmen, wardens, or scouts throughout the Ettenmoors and slay them.
Chieftain Durulkum directed you to seek out the weakest of the enemy soldiers and claim their badges as proof of your duty.
Collected Lieutenants' seals (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Across this foetid land you will find many who are clinging to the hope that they can defeat this war-host. I know as well as you their hope is ill-placed. We grow stronger with every passing hour, and there is no stopping the forces Mordirith sends forth from his palace in Carn Dûm.
'Keep your head about you when you face these foes, you pile of dung. I'll not tolerate failing easily. Your failure will cast me in an ill shadow, and I will see your failure purged before my name is tarnished.
'Collect the seals carried by the lieutenants in their army and return them to me. Much favour is earned by their acquisition.'

'This pleases me. Not enough to pay you a compliment, though, vermin. Yet, I am obligated to reward your efforts with something. This pittance will suffice.
'Whine or prattle on about how little I give, and I will drive my sword through your gullet!
'I serve Mordirith, Angmar, and Lugbúrz without question, so you should follow me as well.'
'Snivelling wretch! Why do you still stand here. Seek the lieutenants in the enemy holdings or areas they control. I will not tolerate failure. Go!'
Return to Chieftain Durulkum at Dâr-gazag
Collect Lieutenants' seals (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Lieutenants' Seals

Lieutenants watch over the sergeants and lesser guards of the enemy as they drive their war-efforts deeper into the Ettenmoors. Plucking the seals worn by each of these warriors will earn you greater favour with your leaders.

Positions held by the enemy are often watched over by the lieutenants in their army. You may even find a lieutenant flanked by sergeants in the wild-lands.
Chieftain Durulkum commanded that you retrieve the seals worn by the lieutenants in the enemy army and return them to him at Dâr-gazag.
Collected Captain-Generals' symbols (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Weakling! I charge you with a task that will see your body bloodied, broken, and left for the crebain. You will do this task because I say you will do this task.
'Fail me and live, and I will cover your flesh in the sweet drippings from the roasting rat-folk and drop you near the trolls. Your end will be painful and merciless, and I shall revel in it. Do well, and I will forgo the threat and let you live out your miserable life.
'Captain-Generals are present wherever the enemy controls. Slaughter them, skin them if you like, snap their bones and consume them... I don't care. Save the symbols they wear and return them to me!'

'A pitiful display of battle! Took you longer than a slug to crawl out of the dead târk's belly.
'Still, you've done what I asked... poorly, but you still deserve something for your efforts, worm!'
'You pathetic worm! Captain-General symbols will only be found on the leaders of the locations the enemy has taken! Get out there and do your part for this war!'
Return to Chieftain Durulkum at Dâr-gazag
Collect Captain-Generals' symbols (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Captain-Generals' Symbols
At the head of the enemy forces stand the Captain-Generals. Their symbols garner great favour amongst Angmar's army, and presenting these to Mordirith will undoubtedly earn you favour with Lugbúrz.

Captain-Generals can only be found at locations where the enemy army holds power.
Chieftain Durulkum directed you to collect Captain-General symbols from enemy leaders and then return to him.
Collected sergeants' patches (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Maggot! You try my patience by the very sight of you. Skulking about with a sluggard's look about you. You make me sick and long for the vile bile spewed from Carn Dûm's underbelly.
'I'd sooner speak with the Pale Folk than you, if I had the choice. As I cannot choose where I am forced into duty, I shall take pleasure in causing you limitless pain.
'Our enemy calls feeble creatures leaders. Simple things who command small units. Sergeants, they call them. Our war-host will thrive only when we show our strength, and what better way than by defeating the lowliest of their leaders. Find them and take their badges off their warm corpses. You will do this for me, or I will see that you are fed the leavings in the bile from the north.'

'Feeble, yes? Such creatures cannot hope to match the might of Angmar's Army. Mordirith will be pleased with my progress!
'You did well for me, filth. I will see that you are given favour.'
'You do not want to make a mockery of me, ${RACE}. I will see that you are relegated to scrubbing the stones of Carn Dûm clean for the rest of your days, if you fail me!'
Return the patches to Chieftain Durulkum at Dâr-gazag
Collect sergeants' patches (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Sergeant-at-Arms' Patches
Sergeants command smaller units of the enemy army. These feeble creatures believe that they can stand up to the might of Angmar's army, but they shall soon learn that they face a relentless foe.

Sergeant-at-Arms lead small numbers of Men, Elves and dwarves throughout the Ettenmoors.
Chieftain Durulkum directed you to obtain sergeants' patches before returning to him at Dâr-gazag.

'Another stripling barely ready to face its shadow! Well, maggot, you'll learn quick or die. Out there, in the wild of the Ettenmoors, we've got foes that'll fight harder than a few scattered farmers like in the North Downs.
'Pitiful little ${RACE}! You'll be dead within a week, I think, and set into the evening gruel. Nevertheless, I've orders from War-tyrant Akúlhun that I'll not disobey, and you'd be wise not disobey mine. We Krahjarn are Mordirith's favoured, which means we've got the favour of the Eye as well, and that power is undeniable! So listen well, slime!
'South of here, along the ridge at the foot of these mountains, you will find Dâr-gazag. Seek out Chieftain Durulkum and tell him you are the newest recruit!'

'You've the look of a coward, ${PLAYER}. You'd best prove me wrong. This is Dâr-gazag, our central keep. The enemy lay across the field of battle far to the east at Ost Ringdyr. We control this keep -- they control theirs.
'We've a number of things that need doing here to keep the war-machine turning, and you're the maggots that'll be doing what we need. Speak with Soldiers, Taskmasters, Chieftains, and Tyrants to learn what they need doing.
'Fail us, and your corpse will litter the battlefield or feed the forces. Succeed, and you might find yourself favoured by Mordirith, Angmar, and Lugbúrz!'
Talk to Chieftain Durulkum at Dâr-gazag
Report to Dâr-gazag, Maggot

Driven by a harsh Krahjarn Taskmaster, you find yourself within the Gramsfoot stronghold in the shadow of Mount Gram on the border of the Ettenmoors. Here to support your Ongbúrz brothers under the watchful eye of the Krahjarn, you are ushered south into the Steps of Gram in search of Chieftain Durulkum.
'Maggot! I've a mind to rend your flesh open and tear out your innards! Move now! I ordered you to Dâr-gazag and Chieftain Durulkum!'

Seek out Chieftain Durulkum at Dâr-gazag, along the ridge south of Gramsfoot.
Soldier Faltúrz ordered you to find your way to Chieftain Durulkum at Dâr-gazag.

'You little maggots make me want to vomit! Worthless sores on the hide of Mordirith's great army. Never killed before, never seen steel in the hands of a filthy târk, or Elf, or worse... a dwarf. You're nothing more than a heap of dung piled as high as you stand, and none will show you respect until you done proved yourself worthy.
'I don't see that happening, you worthless, good for nothing ${RACE}! You look like a slimy scum that crawled out from the deepest cave near the sludge spilling from the gutters in Carn Dûm! I've got to find something simple for a piss-ant like you to kill with ease... and I know just the things! We found them only recent-like, and they're a tasty bunch of rats. Not much fight in them, being as small as they are... might be a tough wrangle for you, though.
'Rat-folk with big bellies meant for stabbing live near the water in the wood south of here. Kill their farmers and gardeners, and if you don't fall on your face and break my cold black heart, return to me! Get a move on, you dung-hill rat!'

'Killed them did you? A fine start, ${RACE}. You may find yourself on the front lines someday, doing your service to the Iron Crown by being a body on the heap!
'Keep working like this, and we might find a way to promote you to the top of the filth-pile one day!'
Tasty Little Farmers and Gardeners

Upon arriving in the Ettenmoors, scouts were sent to the far corners in search of allies and enemies within the land. In the south, just across the Hoardale River, a secluded village of plump rat-folk was found, and the inhabitants there were found to be resistant to the forces of Angmar. It was also discovered that the folk were quite tasty.
'Get out there and kill them rat-folk, you worthless gob of flesh! Hoarhallow is found south of here and across the Hoardale River.'

Rat-folk with fat round bellies are rumoured to live in a village far south beyond the Steps of Gram.
Taskmaster Fikdag wants you to make your way into the southern area of the Ettenmoors in search of rat-folk.

Taskmaster Fikdag is at Dâr-gazag.
You slew the rat-folk with ease and now should return to Taskmaster Fikdag.

'When we discovered the rat-folk village in the south, our scouts engaged them to force them into the service of Angmar. Their leader rallied them together and organized their number into a fighting force that bested all but one of our scouts.
'I tell you this so you understand the disgrace that awaits failure in this task, ${PLAYER}. Seek out the leader of these rat-folk and carve his heart out of his chest!'

'You think this was a victory? My scouts tell me that Wat Mudbottom still lives.
'You beat him, yes! But he is not dead. There is no end to the incompetence found in the lesser tribes!
'A victory indeed, but a hollow one!'
Leader of the Rat-folk

When the rat-folk in the south were discovered, they scored a blow against the scouts who found them, slaughtering all but one. The leader of the rat-folk village was responsible for the attack, and Taskmaster Fikdag thinks that you can assist with exacting vengeance.
'Bring no more disgrace to this war-host, ${PLAYER}. We fight for the glory of Angmar and the favour of Lugbúrz! Find and kill the rat-folk's leader!'

Make your way south along the Hoardale River to the village of Hoarhallow.
Taskmaster Fikdag directed you to find and kill Mayor Wat Mudbottom, the leader of the rat-folk village.

Taskmaster Fikdag is at Dâr-gazag.
You stalked through the trails to the centre of Hoarhallow and struck down their leader. You should return to Taskmaster Fikdag with the news.
Collected hobbit-legs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'One thing that the rat-folk have proven to be, ${PLAYER}, is a tasty source of food. Their flesh is sweet and soft, tasting better than the flesh of any Man I have ever eaten.
'I will tell you this, while you stalk through their trails and amongst their homes, be wary not to destroy the meat on their legs. If you return them to me, I will be sure to give you a worthy reward.'

'Ahh, a tasty treat to fill my belly. Their flesh is supple and slides from the bone with ease when boiled in a stew.
'Keep up your efforts here in the Ettenmoors, and one day I might share some of the stew with you, ${PLAYER}.'
'Try my patience if you must, maggot, but my appetite will be sated. I would prefer the tender and tasty flesh of the rat-folk, but I will settle on yours, if you continue to taunt me!'
Return to Dâr-gazag and speak with Taskmaster Fikdag
Collect hobbit-legs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Tasty Little Legs

Though the rat-folk have proven a thorn in the side of Angmar's Army, they have also proven a viable source of food. Not only do the rat-folk have seemingly endless food-stores, but their flesh is sweeter than Man's.

Hoarhallow lay to the south on the eastern side of the Hoardale River.
Taskmaster Fikdag at Dâr-gazag has grown fond of the flesh found on the bones of the rat-folk, and he has asked you to collect some of their legs.
Collected brittleleaf-seeds (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Ar, ${RACE}. You can find a way to carry something back to me, I'm certain. It's a little task, hardly worth mention, I will admit, but then again so is feeding a bunch of thankless maggots like you!
'The rat-folk in the south grow a strange leaf. The leaf tastes terrible and more often than not the rat-folk burn it after drying it out, strange little blighters. But the seeds can be ground up and used as a fairly tasty addition to gruel.
'If you can gather up a bundle of the seeds, I would be very grateful.'
'These will do nicely and make the gruel taste more bland and less terrible!'
'The seeds can be found on the rat-folk, though more frequently in their fields or even in the areas of the woods nearby.'
Return to Taskmaster Gukthor at Dâr-gazag
Collect brittleleaf-seeds (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
A Dash of This and That

Taskmaster Gukthor admits hating the taste of gruel, but has found that the seeds the rat-folk use to grow their leaf adds a nice bite to the mash he uses in his gruel. He has asked that you collect ten seeds for the evening meal.

The rat-folk living south of Dâr-gazag along the river grow a plant that can be crushed to make a tasty spice.
Taskmaster Gukthor waits for you to return with the brittle-leaf seeds.
Collected chunks of slimy slug-meat (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'If you are looking for something more violent than scouting, who isn't, ${RACE}? You could help Taskmaster Gukthor out of Dâr-gazag.
'He cooks the meals for the forces there and needs help with gathering supplies. He told me to set new recruits out hunting for slug meat.
'You heard me right, maggot. You'll be hunting slugs for their meat. When you've got a large bundle make your way to Dâr-gazag far to the south in the Steps of Gram and give the meat you got to Taskmaster Gukthor, or come back here and I'll see they gets where they needs to be.'

'Dallying about, shifting your weight to and fro, is not helping the army in any way. Want to make yourself useful then, do you?
'Right then. All over the Steps of Gram are these giant slugs... we seen 'em before in the slave pits of Carn Dûm. They're tough things with a grand bit of meat on 'em.
'You want to eat, and I want to cook! So we got a bit of a good thing happening here. Go out there and kill the slugs and bring me their meat.'
'These'll do nicely. Firm and fresh. Time'll come soon enough to mash the meat up and make it into something edible.'
'Go out there are get some tasty, chewy slug-meat so I can make us some gruel!'
'You sluggard! You should have brought this to the cook, Gukthor! I've a good mind to give your hide to the slave mines in Angmar!'
'Get out there and get our dinner, cur!'
Collect chunks of slimy slug-meat (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Deliver the slug-meat to Taskmaster Gukthor or Soldier Graus.

Gruel comes from somewhere, and with an army as large as the forces Angmar has sent to the Ettenmoors, gruel is needed in great abundance. You have been charged with collecting the main ingredient in the mush Taskmaster Gukthor makes.
'Get out there and get our dinner, cur!'
'Go out there are get some tasty, chewy slug-meat so I can make us some gruel!'

Giant slugs make the Steps of Gram their home.
Taskmaster Gukthor awaits your return with the slug-meat he demanded.

Giant slugs make the Steps of Gram their home.
Taskmaster Gukthor awaits your return with the slug-meat he demanded.
Collected food-sacks (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Listen well, maggot! I'm charged with feeding our forces, and though I'd have no problems throwing good for nothing sluggards like you on a spit to serve for dinner, the war-masters have other plans.
'So I give you a task that you'll complete, or I'll go about changing the minds of those who can cover up their trails better than I, and you will be dinner.
'The rat-folk in the south grow food, and we steal it to keep our army full and happy. Now listen well! Men, Elves, dwarves, and even the rat-folk that stalk through the Ettenmoors can be carrying the foodstuffs we need. If you find any bring it to me... or there'll be no dinner!'

'It's not meat, but it tastes better than the mash we mince from slug-meat.
'We'll eat well tonight!'
'Get out there and get us some food!'
Return to Taskmaster Gukthor at Dâr-gazag
Collect food-sacks (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Not Just for Eating

Rat-folk living on the banks of the Hoardale, south of Dâr-gazag, are not only a succulent meal, but they are a source of replenishable food. The rat-folk are farmers, supplying the enemy forces with foodstuffs. Foodstuffs can be stolen and eaten by your army as well.

Rations are portioned to enemy forces and found in locations where they hold power.
Taskmaster Gukthor charged you collecting food for Angmar's Army.
Collected dwarf-beards (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Long have we fought in the mountain-hearts, through caverns and ice floes, over the halls of dead dwarves across our bridges and theirs. It is a battle that scars my folk, stays with us always. We hate the dwarves!
'Slaughter them all, we say. Take their beards and destroy them. They take pride in beards, or so it says. So we strip them of their pride, make them suffer as they make the goblins suffer.
'Bring us their beards, and we speak well of you. Bring the beards of the dwarves to me.'

'Look at these, so thick and full! We burn them on the fires and praise the Great Eye! We cull the dwarves! We meet them in battle and face them with our brothers from Angmar!
'Dead dwarves! Dead dwarves! We cheer your name by the light of fire, ${PLAYER}! We cheer and praise you to the Eye!'
'Take the dwarf-beards. Bring them here.'
Return the beards to Fim the Worm at Dâr-gazag
Collect dwarf-beards (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

The Snowreap long struggled against the remnant of the dwarves in the Misty Mountains. Even now, they dislike the thought of dwarves being so close to their home. As allies to Angmar's Army they are permitted to speak on the behalf of any who aid them.

Dwarves encroaching throughout the Ettenmoors wear full beards on their faces.
The goblins believe that the beards are a matter of pride amongst the dwarves and want you to help them humiliate their hated foes. Fim the Worm bade you strip the beards of the dwarves in return for favour from the Snowreap.
Discovered the Grimwood Lumber-yard

'Maggot! You need to learn your way about these lands, and I am tasked with seeing that you do.
'South and east, across the Hoardale River, you will find a swath of land called Hithlad. A forest ripe for harvesting covers the land there. It is called the Grimwood. We found rat-folk working there and drove them out, only to have the enemy come to their defence.
'You must scout through the wood and find the camp so you know where the battles will be fought in that wood. Return to me only when you discover this location!'
'Favour earned! Not for you, of course... you've simply been prepared for your future sacrifice for the glory of Angmar, Mordirith, and Lugbúrz!'
Scout the Grimwood Lumber-yard
Return to Soldier Faltúrz at Gramsfoot
Into the Grimwood
Soldier Faltúrz sent you to Hithlad, east of the southern stretch of the Hoardale River, to find the Grimwood Lumber-yard.

'My ire rises each time I see your face, worm. Let us be certain of one thing: you do as I say, and you live. Press me, and I will slaughter you. Find the Grimwood and return to me only after you know the location of the camp.'

The Grimwood Lumber-yard is found in the heart of the Grimwood within Hithlad, south and east across the Hoardale River.
Soldier Faltúrz ordered you to learn the location of the Grimwood Lumber-yard.

Soldier Faltúrz awaits your return at the Krahjarn-encampment at Gramsfoot.
You scouted through the Grimwood and discovered the Grimwood Lumber-yard. Now you should return to Soldier Faltúrz.

'A great goblin-king once lived within Mount Gram, ${RACE}. Now his kin are worthless wretches, easily beaten into submission and only worthy of labour. We've agreed to assist the miserable curs in their village to the east of here.
'Travel to Arador's End and seek out the village of Grothum. You will find Bok and tell him you are there to assist.'

'Help comes, yes! You here to help Snowreap! Snowreap helps Angmar! Snowreap helps Mordirith! Snowreap helps Lugbúrz!
'You come here, we give thanks!'
Talk to Bok at Grothum
Get to Grothum, Maggot

Grothum is the village in the north-eastern stretch of the Ettenmoors known as Arador's End. It is here that the Snowreap-goblins, who dwell in old dwarf-ruins throughout the Misty Mountains, have congregated to assist the war-host with the Isendeep Mine.
'I'll not tolerate this, ${RACE}. Get your carcase to Grothum, or I'll see it in this night's gruel!'

Bok is at the goblin-village of Grothum located in the north-east stretches of the Ettenmoors.
Soldier Faltúrz directed you to make yourself available to the Goblins of Grothum.

'Listen well, slug. Soldier Gazlup at Lugazag, a tower in the Steps of Gram, has work to be done.
'If we've lost control of the tower -- which you'd best hope we haven't, worm -- you'll need to wait for him to return to his post. He's far too valuable a soldier to risk in recovering the point!
'Lugazag is south and east of Gramsfoot in the greener section of the Steps of Gram. Hurry along, maggot!'

'Another recruit! Listen well. These lands teem with the enemy of the Great Eye. We must slaughter them all and clear the way for Mordirith! To arms!
'My task might seem worthless, but so too will the tasks given by Taskmaster Fash outside these walls. But they will earn you favour with Mordirith, Angmar, and Lugbúrz!'
Talk to Soldier Gazlup at Lugazag
Report to Lugazag
You have been ordered to make your presence known to Soldier Gazlup at Lugazag.
'Still here? Do you need me to thrust a sword into your ears! I wonder if you even have them! Go, maggot! Go to Lugazag!'

If the tower has not been taken by the enemy, you should find Soldier Gazlup at Lugazag, south and east of Gramsfoot, in the greener sections of the Steps of Gram.
Soldier Nartul directed you to speak with Soldier Gazlup at Lugazag.
Tírith Rhaw scouted

'Far to the east is a tower which often belongs to the enemy. We assail it now and again, but far too often, we are driven out.
'In time, we'll build a wall of bodies of recruits like yourself that we can use to shield the true forces of Angmar as we storm into the enemy's base and crush them!
'For now, I must send you on a fool's errand to learn the location of the tower. Travel east, across the Hoardale River and into the Coldfells. Find Tírith Rhaw, and scout the area, then return to me!'
'Survived the journey? Good for you, maggot. Before you get excited, you should learn your place... firmly beneath my heel, worm!'
Scout out Tírith Rhaw
Return to Soldier Nartul at Gramsfoot
To Tírith Rhaw
Your education continues with a trip far to the east to Tírith Rhaw, a tower in lands controlled by the enemy.
'Listen well to me, maggot. Standing here talking to me only draws my ire. Make your way east, across the Hoardale, and find Tírith Rhaw. Then, and only then, do I want to see your face!'

Tírith Rhaw lays far to the east beyond the Hoardale River.
Soldier Nartul directed you to scout out Tírith Rhaw in the Coldfells.

Soldier Nartul awaits your return at Gramsfoot.
You discovered and scouted the area surrounding Tírith Rhaw.
Tol Ascarnen scouted

'You're an ambitious one, ${RACE}. Very well then, I've a simple enough task for you. Simple indeed.
'Make your way east towards the Hoardale River. Find the island in the centre... just scout it out and have a look through Tol Ascarnen! If you survive, come back to me.'
'I had expected you sooner, maggot. You found it, though, and this means you survived! You might not be as worthless as I assumed!'
Scout out Tol Ascarnen
Return to Soldier Nartul at Gramsfoot
To Tol Ascarnen
You have been ushered out on a simple scouting mission to find the central keep called Tol Ascarnen.
'Still here. Perhaps I was right, and you are a coward. Tol Ascarnen, worm. Go there now, or I will bury my blade in your belly and spill your innards on this ground!'

Tol Ascarnen is on an island in the Hoardale River, east of Gramsfoot.
You were ordered to find and scout out Tol Ascarnen.

Soldier Nartul awaits your return at Gramsfoot.
You discovered and scouted the area around Tol Ascarnen.

'You! You here to help, yes? Of course, of course! Angmar and the Snowreap serve the same lord, the Great Eye. You help us, good.
'The mines, digging claws, nasty beaks, terrible flesh. They bite us, break us, sometimes kill! The terrible stone-eaters. The crawling death.
'You go now, kill the creeping, claw-skittering, cave-dwellers, yes?'

'Good, good! No more crawling claws in the cave. We work now, help the army!
'Glory to Angmar! Glory to the Eye! Glory to the Snowreap!'
Speak with Bok in Grothum
Menace in the Mines

Cave-claws dig through the stone and threaten the goblins working the Isendeep near Grothum. The leaders of the village implored you as an ally to the Snowreap to assist them in destroying the terrible little creatures.
'You help now, yes! The mines, go to the mines!'

Cave-claws can be found in the Isendeep mine.
Bok begged you to help defend the goblins in the mines.

Bok awaits your return at Grothum.
You slaughtered the cave-claws you encountered to defend the pathetic goblins. You should return to Bok with the news.
Collected hobbit-feet (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Caught me one of the rat-folk, I did. Tasty little morsel, sweet toes melting in the mouth. Can't have him! He's mine... ours, the Snowreap's! I'll call the trolls if you try to take him! But I tell Angmar's army how nice you be to Snowreap if you help me.
'Rat-folk has such tasty little toes, but this one makes such tasty little dishes with his little hands that we keeps him around to make our gruel better. The trolls like his food and eats less goblins, so we keeps him hidden. But I like their toes, the rat-folk toes.
'Get me their feets, get me the rat-folk feets, and I tells others how good you are to Snowreap!'

'You brought me feet! I tell everyone you help the Snowreap. Everyone I sees will know you helped us, filled my belly.
'Such a treat, a treat to eat the tasty rat-folk feet!'
'I wants to lick the toes, lick the toes off the bones!'
Return the hobbit-feet to Bok in Grothum
Collect hobbit-feet (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Tasty Little Toes

Bok captured himself one of the rat-folk one day, and he has proven a great asset. His toes tasted good when the goblin ate one, but the little man is a better cook than anything, and so they keep him alive to cook their meals. But this does not deter Bok from wanting to eat more rat-folk toes.

Hoarhallow is far to the south-west on the eastern bank of the Hoardale River.
Bok waits for you to return to him with the hobbit-feet you were sent to harvest.
Defeated guards at Tírith Rhaw (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Maggot! You've been conscripted, like it or not, to assail our enemy at the walls of their tower in the east.
'Travel across the Ettenmoors, always east, beyond the Hoardale River and Tol Ascarnen, to the shadow of Ost Ringdyr where you will see the tower Tírith Rhaw rising upon a great hill.
'Kill the guards about this tower to weaken our enemy, and you shall see respect. Fail, and you will face your doom.'

'A victory today, maggot! A victory!
'We shall drive these fools from the Ettenmoors yet, then bring the full might of Angmar into this land and drive forwards to meet the armies of Mordor in the south!'
Defeat guards at Tírith Rhaw (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Speak with Soldier Gazlup at Lugazag
Guards of Tírith Rhaw
Tírith Rhaw stands in the east, near the camp of the Free Peoples at Ost Ringdyr. The tower is under the control of the Free Peoples, and you are tasked with killing the guards in the area.
'Go to Tírith Rhaw, maggot! Kill the guards and give our army the chance that it needs to slaughter these fools!'

Tírith Rhaw is a tower in the eastern area of the Ettenmoors. It lay between the central keep of Tol Ascarnen and Ost Ringdyr.
Soldier Gazlup ordered you to slaughter the guards keeping watch over Tírith Rhaw.

Soldier Gazlup is at Lugazag.
You were tasked to kill the guards at Tírith Rhaw by Soldier Gazlup of Lugazag. You should return to Gazlup with news of your victory.
Collected fragments of troll-stone (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collected slabs of troll-stone (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Battles ebb and flow, ${RACE}. We fight war as we can and with the weapons at our command. Among those weapons are the trolls. As strong as they are stupid, massive as they are clumsy, and killing machines unmatched! With their benefits come drawbacks.
'The largest is their penchant for smashing walls apart. Holes in the wall mean that an enemy can easily breach our forces, so we must repair those holes. But the trolls pound the stone to dust and we haven't the numbers to dig a quarry here in the Ettenmoors, so we use the trolls.
'How, you wonder? Ever seen them in the sun? Solid as the rock from whence they were first drawn. The Coldeve-trolls wandering throughout the Ettenmoors often get caught in the sun and die. Chip away their stone and return it to me for repairs.'

'What's this? Ah, troll-stone, just as I asked. This will prove well for you, worm.
'Your efforts will continue to draw attention, and you will continue to earn the favour of the Krahjarn!'
'You're pushing me to wits' end, wretch. I'll not tolerate failure with a simple wave of my hand. Fail me and I'll slice your gullet wide and spill your innards on the ground. Now, get to work!'
Return to Gazlup at Lugazag
Collect fragments of troll-stone (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collect slabs of troll-stone (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Set in Stone

Enemies assail the walls of Lugazag often. Trolls are clumsy and strong and often throw enemy soldiers through walls, shattering the stone therein and making holes in the stonework that must be repaired. Fortunately, trolls are also dumb and turn to stone in the sunlight.

Soldier Gazlup is at Lugazag.
Soldier Gazlup directed you to collect troll-stone to repair the damage the trolls delivered to the walls of Lugazag.
Collected Morningthaw-haunches (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'You trespass where you are not welcome, ${PLAYER}. I shall allow this, for I know you mean to cull the enemy from our home, and I shall even pledge my bite to your effort for recompense.
'Long has my pack struggled to oust the Morningthaw-bears beyond the borders of the Misty Mountains. Long have we battled them and sometimes won. With the arrival of the Elves, the bears drove us back and flocked to their side. My pack came to your leaders and chose to work with them in service to Lugbúrz. I will order my pack to slaughter in Angmar's name, and now, I ask that you slaughter to sate my hunger.
'I want meat. Meat from the Morningthaw. Deliver me enough to sate the hunger of all my years, and I will drive the enemy from that tower by your side.'

'My hunger dies a little with every swallow, so sweet is the taste of revenge. They shall pay more than they know for their intrusion into these lands.
'Come ${PLAYER}! Let us tear the throats from the enemy and slake our thirst now with their blood!'
'I shall not join you in assailing this fortress until I am appeased. Bring me those hides and I will lead you against the foes within Lugazag.'
Return the meat to Mazauk
Collect Morningthaw-haunches (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Maw of Mazauk
Mazauk, a grizzled Warg of unknown years, pledges to join the battle against the enemy should you provide his den with the meat of his hated enemy, the Morningthaw-bears.

Morningthaw-bears can be found throughout the Ettenmoors.
Mazauk directed you to get meat from the Morningthaw bears.
Captain-General Lainedhel defeated!

'Ost Ringdyr is a thorn, ${PLAYER}. A place we can penetrate and nearly destroy, but one we cannot hold for any true time. Like us, the enemy is entrenched deeply at their camp of Glân Vraig, and Ost Ringdyr is simply too close to hold the keep.
'We can, however, slaughter their numbers and kill the master of the keep. This is what I ask of you, ${RACE}: go to Ost Ringdyr and kill the lord who commands the enemy there. Do this and you will earn favour with Angmar and Lugbúrz.'

'A day of victory for Angmar and Lugbúrz! This victory shall echo through the moors and mountains.
'You have earned the favour of the Great Eye, ${PLAYER}.'
Defeat Captain-General Lainedhel at Ost Ringdyr. You must not be defeated when the Captain-General falls
