Defeated Nengon
Defeat Nengon
Glinghant Corrupted

Glinghant was once the most beautiful place in all of Annúminas -- no small feat given the splendor of the ancient city at its height. Descriptions of the pools and gardens of Glinghant hold a special place in the hearts of my people. Even after the long years of decay, you could see the memory of its beauty.
The coming of Amarthiel and her legions to Annúminas is cause itself for sorrow, but of all the harm they have caused to this city, their possession and despoiling of Glinghant stirs me most to rage. I would cast them out of this place and restore the splendour it had of old, even should the rest of Annúminas fall. In that, I am not joined by most of my kindred, but such is my horror at the spoiling of Glinghant.
Amarthiel has many servants, but to Glinghant she has sent the darkwater: foul spirits of corruption led by a grisly demon called Nengon. If you should venture beyond the gate into the terraced steps of Glinghant, I would account you highly should you defeat Nengon and his corrupting brethren.

Nengon and his darkwater brethren are within the pools and gardens of Glinghant, beyond the court of Clorhir.
Harthadril has asked that you enter Glinghant and defeat the darkwater that have despoiled its beauty.
Found the pool on the second terrace
Found the pool on the third terrace
Find the pool on the second terrace
Find the pool on the third terrace
Impure Waters

The darkwater that have occupied Glinghant are vile, corrupting creatures sent by Amarthiel for the purpose of despoiling the beauty of its pools and gardens. The beauty it had of old is lost, and the water's taint now spreads through the city. I fear that the corruption will soon spread to Lake Nenuial if something is not done!
It was not an easy matter, but I spoke with Gwindeth, the Blue Lady of Nenuial, and acquired a phial of clean water with which we may be able to purify the pools of Glinghant. The phial does not contain much, so we must not waste it, but if it might be poured into the pools on each of Glinghant's three terraces, we might be able to purify the waters and thus lessen the corruption of the darkwater.
The entrance of Glinghant is here at the court of Clorhir. Pour some water from this phial into the pools on each terrace of Glinghant and return to me when you have done so. We may still be able to cleanse away some of this evil, ${PLAYER}! If I am not available when you return, please speak with Captain-General Daerdan, at Echad Garthadir, here in the city.

The entrance to Glinghant is located in the court of Clorhir, in Annúminas. Glinghant consists of several terraces, and every terrace supports a pool of water.
You should pour some water from the phial of clean water she gave you into each of the terrace pools in Glinghant.
Collected map to Esteldín
You find no sign of a map on this Ranger.
Collect map to Esteldín
Keep It from the Enemy

Knowledge can be the greatest weapon in war, ${PLAYER}. It can turn the tide of battle, for good or for ill. I speak to you now of a matter so urgent that there can be no delay, for it concerns knowledge that could spell doom for my people...not here in the city, but elsewhere in Middle-earth.
When the darkwater first came to Annúminas, some of my kindred attempted to banish them from the pools of Glinghant. I would have joined their fight, for its pools and gardens are dear to me, but Fainneleg commanded that I help with the initial defence of Gwaelband. I and Gwonil fought bravely and turned back an Angmarim assault, but while we survived to receive other assignments, the Dúnedain that fought in Glinghant did not. The darkwater overwhelmed them and the gardens were taken.
But worse still, one of my fallen brethren bore on his person a map to the hidden refuge of Esteldín, in the North Downs. Folly, perhaps, to carry such a map, but what has been done has been done. We must retrieve the map before it can be taken by the Enemy. The darkwater may not appreciate its significance, but one of Amarthiel's more corporeal servants might. We must not let it fall into their hands, ${PLAYER}. Seek out the fallen Rangers in Glinghant and retrieve the map to Esteldín from him that bore it. Do this quickly, my friend, for there is little time to waste! If I am not around when you return, please bring the map with all haste to Captain-General Daerdan, at Echad Garthadir, here in the city.

The fallen Ranger carrying the map to Esteldín is somewhere within the pools and gardens of Glinghant, beyond the court of Clorhir, in Annúminas.
Harthadril asked you to bring the map to Esteldín out of Glinghant.
Defeated Balhest
Defeat Balhest
Balhest, Lord of Ost Elendil

Ost Elendil, beyond the bridge of Ariant, was once the high seat of the kings of Annúminas. No longer -- after lying abandoned for a terribly long count of years, it is now held by the evil that came out of Angmar.
Of Amarthiel's lieutenants, the Black Númenórean named Balhest is surely the most cruel. He it is that sits in Ost Elendil and holds it against us behind an army of fell spirits and Angmarim sworn to him.
Balhest must be defeated if we are to retake the city, ${PLAYER}. If it can be done, it must be. The Dúnedain cannot fight this foe alone. If I am not here when you return, bring this news to Captain-General Daerdan at Echad Garthadir, for he will be most pleased at your success!

Balhest, one of Amarthiel's mightiest Black Númenórean lieutenants, is in Ost Elendil.
Legrindavor has asked you to put an end to Balhest so that Ost Elendil might be reclaimed.
The Door-warden of the Inner Chamber

The Black Númenórean that sits in Ost Elendil is named Balhest. He is a powerful foe, but he is not the only evil that resides now in that place. We have learned that the passage into the throne room where Balhest commands his forces is guarded by the Cargûl known as Guloth. If you are to defeat Balhest, you will first need to do something about Guloth.
He possesses some terrible power over creatures of shadow, drawing strength out of the darkness with which he commands them to his will. You must somehow sever Guloth's ability to strengthen the fell spirits under his command.
Ost Elendil lies across the bridge of Ariant. Go there only if you are able and willing to face not only Balhest, lieutenant of Amarthiel, but also Guloth the Cargûl. If the battle has drawn me elsewhere by the time you return, report of your victory to Captain-General Daerdan at Echad Garthadir, the Ranger-encampment here in the city.

The Cargûl Guloth is inside Ost Elendil, beyond the bridge of Ariant on the highest level of Annúminas.
Legrindavor has warned you that Balhest is defended by a fearsome Cargûl, Guloth by name, who wields power over creatures of shadow.
Valandil is once again at peace.
Restore Valandil's remains to peace
End Dolvaethor's Menace

We have learned some troubling news, ${PLAYER}. It seems that Dolvaethor, one of Amarthiel's Black Númenórean lieutenants, has entered Haudh Valandil. I can think of no good reason for Dolvaethor to enter the tomb, but many terrible ones!
Whatever Dolvaethor plans within the depths of wise Valandil's crypt, he must be stopped. You must do this, ${PLAYER} -- fighting your way across the bridge of Ariant and onto the island upon which sits Ost Elendil and Haudh Valandil will be terrible, but the Dúnedain lack the force of arms needed for this task. You and your allies, however, might be able to fight through.
Once you have defeated Dolvaethor within Haudh Valandil, set right whatever harm he has caused, then return to me. If the course of battle has drawn me elsewhere, speak instead to Captain-General Daerdan at Echad Garthadir.

Dolvaethor is inside Haudh Valandil on the island upon which stands Ost Elendil, beyond the bridge of Ariant, in Annúminas.
Glangilith has asked you to defeat Dolvaethor and put an end to whatever evil he plans for Haudh Valandil.

Defeat spirits in Ost Elendil (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Evil in Ost Elendil

I grieve to see Ost Elendil in the hands of the Enemy, ${PLAYER}. The great palace of the kings should lie untainted by the forces of evil, not brought low by the machinations of Angmar and its regent!
Fell spirits and their Angmarim masters now stalk the halls of Ost Elendil at Amarthiel's command. We must drive them forth.
Defeat the spirits within the palace and take from their Angmarim masters the blood-stained runes with which they are commanded. That may lessen Angmar's grip on the palace, shining jewel-that-was. If I am not here when you return, I ask that you bring the runes to Captain-General Daerdan at Echad Garthadir, the Ranger-encampment here in the city. He will be able to destroy the foul things.

Fell spirits and their Angmarim masters can be found in Ost Elendil, beyond the bridge of Ariant.
Legrindavor has asked you to defeat the fell spirits inside Ost Elendil and bring him the blood-stained runes used by the Angmarim there to command them.

Defeat kergrim in Haudh Valandil (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeat Shingrinder
The Kergrim Stalk Haudh Valandil

Ost Elendil, the great palace of the kings of old, is on the island beyond the bridge of Ariant. At its base is the entrance to Haudh Valandil, the tomb of Valandil son of Isildur. I fear that the tomb, long-undisturbed, has become the home to great evils: both of Angmar's design and otherwise.
Have you seen the vile creatures known as Kergrim? They are believed to be some relative of the cave-claw, but more prone to disease and the desecration of hallowed places.
Some of these beasts have come to Haudh Valandil, and they must be cleared from the tomb, especially their brute of a leader: Shingrinder, he is called, and he is vile. You will do this, ${PLAYER}, if you honour the ancient places of the Dúnedain, and you will return to me with news of your success. If I have been drawn elsewhere, report instead to Captain-General Daerdan at Echad Garthadir, the Ranger-encampment here in the city.

Kergrim stalk Haudh Valandil, the tomb on the island beyond the bridge of Ariant, in Annúminas.
Glangilith has asked you to defeat the kergrim that stalk the depths of Haudh Valandil, including their leader Shingrinder.
Collected priceless relics (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collect priceless relics (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
New Home for the Relics of Old

The Black Númenórean Dolvaethor has gone to Haudh Valandil at Amarthiel's bidding, ${PLAYER}, and I fear the mischief he may cause in that hallowed place. The halls and tombs are lined with precious relics of the past -- relics of both great historical and personal value to the Dúnedain -- and they must not be despoiled!
I ask you to recover as many of these priceless relics from the depths of Haudh Valandil as you can; my brethren will keep them in a safe place until the Angmarim have been defeated and the tomb is once more a place of peace.
The entrance to Haudh Valandil is located on the island, beyond the bridge of Ariant. Beware of Dolvaethor and the kergrim that have awakened within its depths and recover the relics with all haste! If I am not here when you return, report to Captain-General Daerdan at Echad Garthadir, the Ranger-encampment here in the city.

The entrance to the tomb is on the island beyond the bridge of Ariant, on the highest level of the city.
Glangilith has asked you to recover priceless relics from Haudh Valandil before the Angmarim ruin them.
'You are a hunter of great skill, ${PLAYER}.'
'Do not forget what I have told you of these lands.'
'My brother always sends hunters to me. I do not need his concern!'
'You are a skilled hunter, ${PLAYER}. The Eglain can tell.'
Talk to Hogahild
'Ah, a Hunter! Trumswith will be wanting to speak with you. It is not often that a good Hunter travels through these parts. I am sure you will be a boon to us here at Ost Guruth!'
Hunter: Wilderness by Ost Guruth
You have been encouraged to learn the wilds around Ost Guruth in the Lone-lands, so that you may better find your way there in all seasons.
'Return now to my brother Trumswith, and he will give you whatever reward he promised. You will find him at Ost Guruth, our Ruin-hold here in the Lone-lands.'

'I will not tell you where Hogahild has gone. You are a hunter! If you cannot follow her trail, I will teach you nothing!
'Unni, the dwarf stable-master just outside Ost Guruth, likely saw her as she left. Speak with him if you need to get your bearings, but following my sister's trail from that point will be up to you.'

'I did see Hogahild leave this morning. Lovely lass that Hogahild. Waved to me, she did! She was standing right over there, on those hills slightly east of here. If you're looking for her, I'd start your search to the east.'
The trail here is very confused, and the signs are difficult to read. You cannot tell in which direction the trail might continue from here.
The trail here is quite clear. Whoever made these tracks was moving without haste eastward.
The trail here is quite clear to your skilled eyes. Whoever made this trail passed north-east.

'Another of my brother's ridiculous challenges? Well, I must offer you my congratulations, even if I do not appreciate the stream of hunters he always sends following me on my errands! He insists that he does not do it to keep an eye on me, but I know better.
'Trumswith once hunted Trampletusk, a great aurochs, but when he finally encountered the beast he was so struck by its majesty that he spared its life. I understand that the beast has left these lands now, but I do not know where it might have gone.
'Return to my brother in Ost Guruth and tell him of Trampletusk; he will know that your hunt has been successful. I hope too that he will cease with these silly challenges! You hunters have enough to do without following me!'

'Your name is ${PLAYER}, and you are a hunter? The Eglain have lived in these wilds for many a year; the ways of the wild are the ways of the Eglain. If you seek to learn of secret paths through the Lone-lands, you are right to come to me.
'I, Trumswith, can show you the signs that will allow you to make your way through the Lone-lands at great speed, leading the way for those in your fellowship who are not skilled in the ways of the hunt. I will do this for you if you can prove to me that you have the necessary skill. My sister Hogahild left Ost Guruth this morning. If you can find her trail, follow it until you meet with her. Ask her the name of the only beast I have ever hunted and yet spared, and I will teach you what I can.
'Hogahild left Ost Guruth near Unni, the dwarf stable-master by the stairs. You can speak with him to get your bearings, but will then need to find her trail on your own.'

'You speak of Trampletusk? Very good, ${PLAYER}! You have followed the trail of my sister and proven yourself of worthy skill!
'I will teach to you what you must know of finding your way in the Lone-lands. You will now be able to show your fellowship the quickest paths to return to Ost Guruth. You have earned my respect, and I will repay you with these teachings.'

Trumswith is at Ost Guruth, the Ruin-hold in the Lone-lands, far to the east of The Forsaken Inn, just north of the Great East Road.
You have been told to speak with Trumswith, one of the Eglain at Ost Guruth, who can train you in the ways of the wild.

Hogahild left Ost Guruth near Unni, the dwarf stable-master there, but is now somewhere in the wilderness of the Lone-lands.
Trumswith has challenged you to follow the trail of his sister Hogahild. If you can return to him with the name of the only beast he has hunted and spared, information known to Hogahild, he will teach you secret paths through the Lone-lands to Ost Guruth.

Trumswith is in Ost Guruth, the Ruin-hold in the Lone-lands.
You have followed her trail to Hogahild, the sister of Trumswith, and she told you the name of the only beast her brother has hunted and spared: the aurochs known as Trampletusk. You should return now to Trumswith with this information and he will teach you what he knows about the wild paths of the Lone-lands.
'You are welcome in Aughaire, ${PLAYER}.'
'Do not let down your guard. West Angmar is full of danger.'
Find the Orc-skull
Bring Orc-skull to Torcall

'You call yourself a hunter? We will see, ${PLAYER}. We will see.
'If you are a true hunter, you will be able to follow the trail I took when last I hunted the Orcs of Angmar. I left by the north road from Aughaire. If you can follow my trail, you will find the skull of one of the Orcs I slew.
'Return to me with this Orc-skull, and I will show you what I know of the secret ways through Angmar. You will be able to come to Aughaire with speed far-exceeding that of lesser hunters.'
Hunter: Desolation by Aughaire
You have been encouraged to learn the ways of the desolate crags of West Angmar, so you may better find the way to Aughaire when needed.

A number of tracks can be seen among the loose stones here, but it is impossible to tell what might have made them or how long ago. It does not seem likely that Torcall came this way.
You have found Torcall's trail, but here it becomes confused and muddled among the stones. You cannot tell in which direction he left this place.
A battered Orc-skull lies among the stones. It is coated with a thin layer of ash and dust.
Judging from the signs, the trail here turns to the east.
Your keen eye detects that the trail here bends to the north.
The trail here runs north-east among the loose stones.

'This is the skull of which I spoke, ${PLAYER}. You are a skilled hunter, and I will teach you what I know of the secret paths through these lands.
'You will be able to lead your allies to Aughaire with great speed, if you pay attention to the signs and to what I have told you.'
'You do not have the Orc-skull? You will not have my teachings either.'

Torcall has hidden an Orc-skull somewhere within West Angmar.
You have been challenged to recover an Orc-skull that Torcall says is hidden somewhere in West Angmar. He left by the road north of Aughaire and slew an Orc at some point along his journey; if you follow his trail, you may be able to find it.

Torcall is in Aughaire, in West Angmar.
You have recovered the Orc-skull Torcall asked you to find and should now return it to him as proof of your skill as a hunter.
'Evendim can appear peaceful, but do not be fooled!'
'You have my greetings, ${PLAYER}!'

Bring scratched arrow-head to Horace Roxhythe

'Welcome to Tinnudir, ${PLAYER}. I can show you secret paths by which you can lead your fellowship here quickly, but you must prove to me that you are worthy to be taught such skills. You must know for what to look.
'I have hidden one of my arrow-heads somewhere in Evendim. If you can pick up my trail and follow the signs, you will be able to recover the arrow-head and prove to me that you are ready. If not, well...perhaps another hunter will succeed where you fail.
'I will tell you this: I crossed the bridge from Tinnudir to the mainland. So you will want to begin your search for my trail there.'
Hunter: Tracks Through Evendim
You have been encouraged to learn the lay of the lands around Lake Nenuial, so you may better find your way around its shores.
'I crossed to the mainland by bridge, but from there you will need to pick up my trail, if you are to find the arrow-head I have hidden somewhere in Evendim.'
There are tracks here in the soil, but you cannot tell what made them, or how long ago they were made. It is not likely that Horace came this way.
The trail here is muddled and confused. That Horace came this way is unmistakeable to your skilled eye, but you cannot discern in what direction he left this place.
Peering closely at the soil, you find a scratched arrow-head partially embedded in the dirt. This must be Horace's arrow-head.
The marks in the dirt leave no question: the trail here leads south-east.
There is little question to your keen eye that Horace's trail here bends south-west.

'Yes, this is my arrow-head! See these scratches here? I carved my initials there so I would be able to recognize it. A number of burglars have tried to pass themselves off as hunters, and I needed some way to catch imitations.
'I will teach you secret paths through Evendim, ${PLAYER}, so you will be able to lead your fellowship to Tinnudir with utmost speed.'
'You have not recovered my arrow-head, ${PLAYER}? Are you certain you are a hunter?'

Horace Roxhythe hid one of his arrow-heads somewhere in Evendim. He crossed from the island of Tinnudir to the mainland on the stone bridge.
You have been challenged to follow Horace's trail and recover the arrow-head he hid somewhere in Evendim to prove you are ready for his teachings.

Horace Roxhythe is at the Ranger-camp on the island of Tinnudir.
You have found the arrow-head that Horace hid in Evendim and should return it to him so he will recognize your skill as a hunter.
'Welcome back to Gath Forthnír, ${PLAYER}. If there is any welcome in this place, you have it.'
'May you always find the paths for which you search, ${PLAYER}.'
Find brooch

'Welcome to Gath Forthnír, ${PLAYER}. This is a grim and cheerless place, but we do what we must to stand against the shadows that press us.
'You seek to learn the secret paths to Gath Forthnír? I could speak to you all day, and if you did not possess enough skill as a hunter, it would not matter -- anything I could teach you would flow over you like water and mean nothing.
'You must prove to me that you have the skill, ${PLAYER}. When last I scouted the eastern lands of Angmar, I let fall a brooch I carried; I did not realize it was missing until I returned here. If you can follow my trail, you might find the brooch where I dropped it. If you are able to do this, return the brooch to me, and I will teach you what I know.'
Hunter: Waste Near Gath Forthnir
You have been encouraged to learn the lay of the waste that is East Angmar, so you may better find your way to Gath Forthnír when needed.

'I left Gath Forthnír and lost my brooch somewhere along the way. If you are a worthy hunter, you should be able to find my trail and follow it. 'You do not have my brooch? How can this be?'
Something came this way, but what it might have been eludes you and the trail is long cold. Your heart tells you that Maerchiniath did not come this way.
Maerchiniath certainly came this way; that much is clear. What is not clear is in what direction he set forth from this point, for the tracks are muddled and confused.
You find a fallen brooch partially-buried in the loose stones and dirt.
From here the trail leads north-west; that much is certain.
Close study reveals that the faint trail leads south.
The tracks turn to the south-east at this point. Maerchiniath certainly passed this way and not long ago.

'You found my brooch, ${PLAYER}, and by doing so have proven yourself a hunter worthy of reward!
'I will teach you the signs of the secret paths through this unpleasant land, so you may lead your allies to Gath Forthnír with great speed, if the need arises.'

Maerchiniath's brooch is somewhere in East Angmar.
The Ranger Maerchiniath has agreed to teach you how to find secret paths through East Angmar if you can follow the trail he took when he lost his brooch and bring it back to him.

Maerchiniath is at the hidden camp of Gath Forthnír, in East Angmar.
You have recovered the fallen brooch and should return it now to Maerchiniath.

'I have heard of all the good you have done, ${PLAYER}. You truly are an excellent Bounder and deserve the thanks of all Shire-folk!
'We don't go in for uniforms, but I must say that you've earned another feather in your cap. Take it with my thanks!'

'Talk to Second Shirriff Bodo Bunce by Town Hole in Michel Delving. He'll be very pleased to hear of all the good you have done!'
'Hello, Bounder ${PLAYER}!'
'What news of the bounds, friend ${PLAYER}?'
'You have proven to be quite the Bounder, ${PLAYER}!'
'You have my thanks for all the good you have done, Bounder ${PLAYER}.'
