You have been told to bring word of the many good deeds you have performed for the Shire-folk to Bodo Bunce.
Crafted Crests of Vigilance (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'I have heard that you have some considerable skill in the craft of metalsmithing, ${PLAYER}. I would ask something of you, if you would aid the Council of the North in their battle against Angmar.
'There are certain intricate symbols that we use to identify our warriors in the field in order to reduce the risk of enemies infiltrating our ranks. Unfortunately, these Crests of Vigilance are in short supply, and we have little time for their crafting, given our pressing need to maintain weapons and armour.
'You can learn how they are made here in Gath Forthnír. If you can aid us in this simple task, the Council of the North will be indebted to you.'
'Ah, yes, these will do nicely! Thank you, ${PLAYER}, for your assistance.'
'Have you no Crests of Vigilance for me?'
Present your Crests of Vigilance to Hróar at Gath Forthnír
Craft Crests of Vigilance (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Crests of Vigilance -- Introduction
The Council of the North is in need of a means to identify their warriors in the field.

Hróar is at Gath Forthnír in Angmar.
Hróar has asked you to craft some Crests of Vigilance and bring them to him.

'I have need of your help in another matter of metalsmithy. To our most esteemed heroes, we bestow a medal called the Crest of Valour, but it has been some time since we have had amongst us an artisan with the skill to craft these intricate devices. If you could find the time and resources to craft a few of these crests for us, we would be much obliged by your efforts on our behalf.'

'Ah, Crests of Valour, and finely made too. Our own smiths could craft no finer. It is a shame that so many of these medals will be awarded posthumously, but the honour of the fallen is as important as the honour of the living...perhaps more so, as it is all that remains to them.'

'We have more heroes than the means to honour them -- granted, most of them are already dead, or soon will be, but that is no reason to be lax in our duties to them.
'See if you cannot find up some metals and forge something worthy of a hero!'
Present your Crests of Valour to Hróar at Gath Forthnír
Craft Crests of Valour (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Crests of Valour -- Introduction
The Council of the North has need of tokens to bestow upon heroes of the war against Angmar.

Hróar is at Gath Forthnír in Angmar.
Hróar has asked you to craft some Crests of Valour and bring them to him.
Craft an Icon of Heroes (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Our highest award to those who have fallen in acts of unheralded bravery in the service to the Free Peoples is the Icon of Heroes. Alas, the gifted artisan who created it included some rather rare and difficult items in its design, and we have little to spare here. If you can find the needed materials and craft an Icon of Heroes, we would be greatly in your debt.
'Who knows? If you continue to prove your worth, then maybe some day such an Icon will lie upon your breast as we lower you into your tomb -- now there is a cheerful thought....'
'Once again, you have provided a valuable service. I am at your service and your family's!'
Present an Icon of Heroes to Hróar at Gath Forthnír
Craft an Icon of Heroes (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Icon of Heroes -- Introduction
The Council of the North is in need of a medal to bestow upon those heroes who have fallen in the service of the Free Peoples.

Hróar is at Gath Forthnír in Angmar.
Hróar has asked you to craft an Icon of Heroes and bring it to him.
Collected Dwarf-jewel (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'At your service, ${CLASS}. We dwarves have toiled long under these Mountains and have crafted many wonderful and beautiful things as you no doubt can see. But the skill of the Dwarves of Thorin's Hall lies not in our mastery of stone and rock, but in the cutting of gemstones and the smithy of strong iron! Though we pride ourselves most on our jewel-crafting over any of our works of baser materials.
'If you bring to me finely-crafted dwarf-jewels, you might prove yourself someone of worth to the Dwarves of Thorin's Hall.
'You have returned with the dwarf-jewels. Splendid!'
'You have returned without the dwarf-jewels? I do not have time for idle craftsmen. Return when it is finished!'
Bring the dwarf-jewels to Ísrath
Collect Dwarf-jewels (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Dwarf-jewels -- Introduction
The Dwarves of the Blue Mountains are known best for their jewel and iron-craft.

The Blue Stone Garrison is located just inside Thorin's Hall.
Ísrath has requested that you bring him crafted dwarf-jewels.
Collected Dourhand crest (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'At your service, ${CLASS}. The Dourhands have been removed from Thorin's Hall, yet our anger at their deeds has not been satisfied. Many of the Longbeards suffered greatly under Gormr, and his treachery must be met with revenge!
'It is rumoured that the Dourhands have found remains of their ancient home that was lost when the world was broken in the ruins of Orodost -- the Elves now call that place Sarnúr. Travel south of Thorin's Hall to this city and slay the Dourhands that you find there.
'The lesser dwarves and servants should carry the crest of the Dourhand family; bring me these crests that we may repay blood with blood!'

'You have returned with the Dourhand crests? That is well. The blood-price set upon the deeds of the Dourhands is high, and these crests are only a pittance of their full payment to the Dwarves of Thorin's Hall.'
'You have returned without the crests? The Dourhands must pay for their deeds! Return to me when you have collected the Dourhand crests.'
Bring the Dourhand crests to Tórth
Collect Dourhand crests (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Dourhand Crests -- Introduction
The descendants of Skorgrím Dourhand have ever been a thorn in the side of Durin's Folk, the Longbeards. Though now outcast, they remain a threat to the Free Peoples of Ered Luin.

The entrance to Sarnúr is south of Thorin's Hall and west of Noglond in the ruins of Orodost.
Tórth has asked you to enter the Dourhand stronghold of Sarnúr and defeat the creatures who dwell there, claiming Dourhand crests as the proof of your valour.
Collected dwarf-rings (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'At your service, ${PLAYER}. A fine adventurer such as yourself would appreciate the joy that I describe in the crafting of dwarf-rings. Such a thing is a wonder to behold! Aye, when you place a well-crafted dwarf-ring upon your finger, watching its gentle curves glimmer in the torch-light, it stirs even the coldest of hearts.
'I would ask you to prove your worth and bring me five dwarf-rings. Such a token would prove your alliance to the Dwarves of Thorin's Hall.
'It took a skilled hand to craft these dwarf-rings. I commend you on your success, ${PLAYER}!'
'You have yet to bring me the dwarf-rings? A talented provisioner not only knows how to be patient, but will also conclude the order they have been tasked with!'
Bring the dwarf-rings to Ísrath
Collect dwarf-rings (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Dwarf-rings - Introduction
The Dwarves of the Blue Mountains are best known for their jewel and iron-craft.

The Blue Stone Garrison is located just inside Thorin's Hall.
Ísrath has requested that you bring him crafted dwarf-rings.
Collected a dwarf-necklace

'At your service and your family's, ${PLAYER}. The finest jewellery in all of Eriador has been crafted by dwarf-hands in Thorin's Hall. But these Mountains do not give up their jewels willingly. They are filled with iron and coal, and it is seldom that precious stones or metals of great worth are found here.
'A few veins of a very precious dwarf-stone run throughout Eriador. It is not often that even a small gem of craftable quality is found, but when one is uncovered it is a sight to behold. When crafted into a necklace and laid upon the breast, you would be unable to find an unflattering angle. The gem sparkles like Kheled-zâram in the starlight and lays an enchantment of beauty and awe upon all who behold it!
'If you were to bring to me one of these necklaces crafted with a dwarf-stone, you would hold high honour amongst the dwarves of Thorin's Hall.'
'Amazing! Simply amazing! You have indeed earned high honour, ${PLAYER}.'
'You have returned empty handed? I do not blame you; a necklace of this magnitude is not something to be found hastily.'
Bring the dwarf-necklace to Ísrath
Collect a dwarf-necklace
Dwarf-necklace - Introduction
The Dwarves of the Blue Mountains are best known for their jewel and iron-craft.

The Blue Stone Garrison is located just inside Thorin's Hall.
Ísrath has requested that you bring him a crafted dwarf-necklace.
Collected First Age relic

'At your service and your family's, ${PLAYER}. The Dourhands have been mining in the Blue Mountains and have uncovered the remains of a lost dwarf-city, which the Elves are now calling Sarnúr.
'Though many of them are undoubtedly destroyed, ancient relics of the First Age surely still remain in the crumbling halls and deep caverns below the Blue Mountains. Can you imagine? The ancient works of the dwarves lying in the hands of those thieving murderers, it boils the blood! The Dourhands may lay claim to the treasures, but without proof of their ancestry, any dwarf may stake his claim, and I do it thus for the Longbeards!
'Retrieve any of these relics that you may find and bring them to me here at the Blue Stone Garrison. The Longbeards would be deeply in your debt for the return of any of the ancient works, great or small.'
'This is a wonderful find! I will send it off to the vaults right away. I am sure that the smiths will look over every inch of the relics. We are in your debt, ${PLAYER}'

'You have not recovered any of the relics? Dwarves often hide their treasures, but surely you weren't looking hard enough!
'Try searching the bodies of the commanding Dourhands and other inhabitants deep within Sarnúr.'
Bring the First Age Relic to Ásgeir
Collect First Age relic
First Age Relics - Introduction
The descendants of Skorgrím Dourhand have ever been a thorn in the side of Durin's Folk, the Longbeards. Though now outcast, they remain a threat to the Free Peoples of Ered Luin.

Sarnúr lies south of Thorin's Hall and west of Noglond in the ruins of Orodost.
Ásgeir has asked you to enter the Dourhand stronghold of Sarnúr and defeat the creatures who dwell there, claiming First Age relics for the dwarves of Thorin's Hall.

'Greetings, ${RACE}, you fight against the foes of Eriador in these lands, and this is good. There is no doubt within me that your resolve to win this battle is strong.
'Please, hear me out. We are assisting in this battle where we can, and we will continue to do so. I would ask, though, that you support us in our endeavours elsewhere to safe-guard Eriador from the machinations of the North.
'Should you wish to assist us, return to me, and I will arrange for you to take the place of one of my brethren while he patrols the wilds of the Ettenmoors.'

'Your efforts allowed one of our number to assist the Free Peoples greatly, ${PLAYER}. You are to be thanked for the efforts that you put forth.
'The Rangers of Esteldín are indebted to you. You are truly a hero in the war against the Iron Crown.'
Speak with Uirnen and complete your patrol of the Ettenmoors as a Ranger (Cost: 500 Commendations)
Talk to Uirnen at Glân Vraig
Aid from the Rangers
A scarce few Rangers from Esteldín came east to the Ettenmoors to support Lainedhel's efforts against Angmar's army.

'I expected that you would return, ${PLAYER}. If you are prepared, I will set you to your task and call one of our number to patrol the Ettenmoors in your stead.'
<rgb=#FF0000>WARNING: This quest begins a special session quest. You will be logged out of your normal character and take on the guise of a player-friendly npc. You will not be able to leave the Ettenmoors as this character and will attain a set of skills unique to this special player character.</rgb>

Uirnen is at Glân Vraig in the Ettenmoors.
The Rangers are attempting to augment the forces fighting in the Ettenmoors, but fear that committing too much to the battle will result in Angmar succeeding elsewhere. The Ranger Uirnen has asked you to speak with him if you wish to assist the Rangers with their duties.

Uirnen is at Glân Vraig in the Ettenmoors.
You should return to Uirnen and inform him that you have fulfilled your duty.
'Trolls will come help, but you must go work. I will send you. I have been told to send you.'
'Troll, come back. Now you come back. You do good work? Better have.'
Talk to Taskmaster Dromdas at Gramsfoot and complete a patrol through the Ettenmoors as a Troll (Cost: 500 Commendations)
Talk to Taskmaster Dromdas at Gramsfoot
Sticks and Stones
Angmar's inability to destroy the Free Peoples holed up in the farthest reaches of the Ettenmoors has prompted the army's leaders to summon more trolls from the north.

'You go now. Troll, come here.'
<rgb=#FF0000>WARNING: You will be logged out of your current monster play session and logged into a new one. This new avatar is not permanent and cannot trade items or otherwise interact with much of the world.</rgb>

Taskmaster Dromdas is at Gramsfoot.
Angmar's army wishes to dislodge the Free Peoples from the Ettenmoors and has enlisted the assistance of trolls to undertake the endeavour. Of course, the work of Angmar must continue and the troll's work must be completed. If you wish to help the trolls, you should speak with Taskmaster Dromdas again.

Taskmaster Dromdas is at Gramsfoot.
You should return to Taskmaster Dromdas and inform him that you did the work he requested done.
Your patrol is complete
You are defeated
Patrol the Ettenmoors for 60 minutes
Do not be defeated
Ranger in the Ettenmoors
Patrol the Ettenmoors in search of the Enemy. You must patrol for 60 minutes. After 60 minutes you will be returned to your post.

'Trolls have been called from the north. We must redouble our efforts, else the Free Peoples here will fall, and Angmar will flood Eriador through the Trollshaws. Steel your nerve, brother, and know that the hero who stands at your post will not fail us.'
Patrol the Ettenmoors.
Your patrol is complete
You are defeated
Patrol the Ettenmoors
Do not be defeated
Trolls in the Ettenmoors
Patrol the Ettenmoors in search of the enemy. You must patrol for 60 minutes. After 60 minutes you will be returned to your post.
Patrol the Ettenmoors.

'Trolls fight. You die too fast. We strong where you weak.
'You go to troll-home now. Troll come here and fight. We win war. Take all. I send troll home when done.'
'Trolls do good. You do good, too. We smash and crash and bash! Târks die!'
Talk to Taskmaster Sharkúlob at Gramsfoot and complete a patrol through the Ettenmoors as a Troll (Cost: 500 Commendations)
Talk to Taskmaster Sharkúlob at Gramsfoot
Slaughter the Free People
The trolls of Angmar have a singular vision, one that involves destroying the enemies of Angmar.
'You go now. Troll come here.'

Taskmaster Sharkúlob is at Gramsfoot in the Ettenmoors.
The trolls from Angmar, in an effort to speed the victory of Angmar's army, are willing to come to the Ettenmoors to fight the Free Peoples in exchange for your services in the North. You should speak with Taskmaster Sharkúlob.

Taskmaster Sharkúlob is at Gramsfoot in the Ettenmoors.
You took the place of a troll in Angmar while it wrought destruction against the forces of the Free Peoples in the Ettenmoors.

'Take heart! The battle here is ours, and though the foe has breached the walls of Lugazag, we may yet hold back their tide. Listen well, for I have an offer that you must consider strongly, ${RACE}.
'You are a proven warrior, a hero amongst the Free Peoples, and we ask this only of those who are willing. Lainedhel asked for assistance from the Rangers, and we have come to offer our aid. We have duties that need looking after elsewhere in Eriador, and if you are willing to stand there in our stead, we will remain here to fight the foes from the North.
'Think on this and speak to me when you have an answer to my request. I will wait here, friend.'
'Your duty is done, and we have done much to further solidify the strength of the Free Peoples here in the Ettenmoors. You have our thanks, ${PLAYER}.'
Talk to Gelbes at Glân Vraig
Talk to Gelbes
Against the Stone-foe
Rangers have come to the Ettenmoors to stand against the trolls sent from Angmar. They seek assistance with their patrols from the heroes of the Free Peoples.
'What say you? Will you take up the duties of a Ranger to further assist the Free Peoples in the Ettenmoors?'

Gelbes is at Glân Vraig in the Ettenmoors. Speak with her to call a ranger to the Ettenmoors.
The Rangers will assist in retaking Lugazag, but they request that you take the place of a Ranger in Eriador while they come to the Ettenmoors to fight in your stead.

Gelbes is at Glân Vraig in the Ettenmoors.
A Ranger came to the Ettenmoors in your stead and fought valiantly, while you patrolled Eriador in his stead. You should now return to Gelbes.
Your patrol is complete
You are defeated
Patrol the Ettenmoors
Do not be defeated
Ranger in the Ettenmoors
Patrol the Ettenmoors in search of the Enemy. You must patrol for 60 minutes. After 60 minutes you will be returned to your post.

'Trolls have been called from the north. We must redouble our efforts, else the Free Peoples here will fall, and Angmar will flood Eriador through the Trollshaws. Steel your nerve, brother, and know that the hero who stands at your post will not fail us.'
Patrol the Ettenmoors.
Your patrol is complete
You are defeated
Patrol the Ettenmoors
Do not be defeated
Trolls in the Ettenmoors
Patrol the Ettenmoors in search of the enemy. You must patrol for 60 minutes. After 60 minutes you will be returned to your post.
Patrol the Ettenmoors.

'There is no rest for the wicked, ${PLAYER}. There is much yet to do...mainly getting forces here to stand against the enemy.
'Our troops are scattered throughout the wilds of the Ettenmoors, and we must make them aware of our victory. We can do this by setting a large beacon fire.
'Make your way through the Ettenmoors and gather the wood need to make this pyre, then return to me so we can light the fires to call our war-host home.'
'Yes, this will do nicely. If only there were more like you within our ranks, ${PLAYER}. The speed at which these slugs move is abominable.'
'Get out there, sluggard! You've a job to do!'
Deliver the materials to Soldier Kaasak at Tol Ascarnen
A Blaze for the South
Angmar claims the central keep of the Ettenmoors, but the main army has yet to receive the news. The War-tyrant has ordered his soldiers to collect the materials needed to set a beacon fire.

Head south from Tol Ascarnen into Hithlad to seek out the wood needed to build the signal fires to the south.
Though your forces took Tol Ascarnen, the keep is woefully undefended, and Kaasak has ordered you to build a pyre to call in reinforcements from the south. You should make your way into the Ettenmoors and search for kindling, timber, and larger logs to build a beacon fire large enough to call in reinforcements to Tol Ascarnen.
The Orc-archer has seen you
You worthless sack! You failed!

'${PLAYER}, I have worked with you before, and though I must continue to berate you in front of others, I believe you have earned my favour.
'I wish to assist Uzulthrang in his quest to recover Tol Ascarnen, and to that end, I would ask that you undertake a very dangerous mission for me. I have an archer who will fire a blazing arrow into the trees when you arrive within them. When this is done, a force will cross the bridge to battle into the keep.
'My only fear is that the foe is strong in those woods. This could mean your defeat.'
Stand in the open among the trees near Tol Ascarnen's western wall
Defeat is not an option!
A Blaze in the Trees
Paashum is trying to make his superiors in Angmar's army notice him. To that end he has asked you to undertake a mission involving great risk but a potential for great success.

Make your way to the copse of trees in the woods on the western side of Tol Ascarnen. Make your presence know there.
Paashum asked you to make your way into the small section of woods on the western shore of Hoardale near Tol Ascarnen. He hopes to send a force into the keep after setting the woods ablaze. You will need to be obvious enough to attract the enemy's attention.

'There is no rest for the wicked, ${PLAYER}. There is much yet to do.....mainly getting forces here to stand against the enemy.
'We need a fire so big that Lugbúrz will take notice! Ha! On the western parapet, we will build a massive beacon and call our reinforcements!
'Get your brethren together and bring us the wood we need to build that pyre. Go now, maggot!'

'We will build a fire and they will come. The western bridge will be safe! Best you think on this in the future, whelp. We might often have need of this type of defensive service.
'Best to be prepared, no?'
'Get out there, sluggard! You've a job to do!'
Deliver the materials to Soldier Kaasak at Tol Ascarnen
A Blaze for the West
Angmar claims the central keep of the Ettenmoors, but the main army has yet to receive the news. The War-tyrant has ordered his soldiers to collect the materials needed to set a large beacon fire.

Head south of Tol Ascarnen into Hithlad and the Grimwood forest to collect the wood needed to build the blaze.
Though your forces took Tol Ascarnen, the keep is woefully undefended, and Kaasak has ordered you to build a pyre to call in reinforcements from the west. You should make your way into the Ettenmoors and search for kindling, timber, and larger logs to build a beacon fire large enough to call in reinforcements to Tol Ascarnen.

'Listen well. In order to build a horn with which to call reinforcements to Tol Ascarnen, we need to gather some more parts, such as a strong and tall piece of heartwood to place the horn and sinew upon. Your task is to head south into Hithlad -- more importantly, the Grimwood -- to collect the heartwood of a Leafcull Huorn.
'You must be certain to collect a perfect heartwood, for no other will be able to withstand an assault from the Free Peoples. We must build a strong horn, understand?
'Go now and collect the heartwood from the Leafcull in Hithald.'
'A good find. When the horn and sinew are collected, we will have all that we need to build the horn.'
'Get a move on, sluggard. We need that heartwood, or the horn cannot be built. If I have need to warn you again, things will get very uncomfortable for you at the sulphur pits.'
Talk to Soldier Kaasak at Tol Ascarnen
Bleeding Heart

Building a horn to summon reinforcements to Tol Ascarnen requires that several pieces be collected and assembled for an Orc to watch over and use when the Free Peoples make their assault against the fort.

The Leafcull Huorns make their home in the southern woods of Hithlad. Find the Huorn amonst the trees south of the Grimwood Lumber Camp in Hithlad, to the south-west of Tol Ascarnen.
Angmar's forces at Tol Ascarnen are building a horn to call reinforcements to the fight when the Free Peoples return to assault the area. Kaasak has tasked you with collecting the heartwood of a Leafcull Huorn to act as the stand upon which the horn will rest. Damaging the heartwood will make it useless.

'When the War-tyrant told me that he didn't like the bare walls we had here, I was at first confused. Don't smirk... you would be too, whelp, thinking that the War-tyrant wants to decorate the walls with something other than the mark of the Iron Crown or Lugbúrz. But then he tells me... oil, great gobs of boiling oil.
'We're going to need this oil, and we can only get it from the Free Peoples... the very ones we're trying to boil! We know there is a camp of them over the bridge to the south, so that is a good place to start.
'Scouts tell us that they can be found all throughout the Ettenmoors as well, though the best location is at Ost Ringdyr to the east. Get the oil and bring it back here. We'll cook up a nice surprise for the wretches.'
'This will do nicely. Get others to the task so we can build the iron belly and cook us some meals.'
'Get to work, slug. I'm not in the habit of taking kindly to those who shirk their duties!'
Deliver the oil to Soldier Glat at Tol Ascarnen
Cooking Sauce
The Free Peoples will return to take Tol Ascarnen, and Angmar's defenders wish to strengthen the walls with deterrents that will drive the foe away.

Oil can be found on the Free Peoples fighting throughout the Ettenmoors. The closest camp is over the southern bridge, though a larger group can be found at Ost Ringdyr, far to the east.
Angmar's Army is shoring up the defences at Tol Ascarnen. Glat needs oil with which to douse the Free Peoples who attempt to assail the keep.

'We won the day, no thanks to sluggards and dullards like you. Now we must continue to press our enemy, lest they regain a foothold and strike against us.
'We've received reports that there is a dwarf who arrived at the enemy encampment somewhere on the east side of the Hoarwell River. We must get to him before the enemy can call him to action.
'Gather some other maggots and make your way across the river to assail that Marshal Án at the camp. Stop him before he arrives to assail Tol Ascarnen. Do not fail us!'

'You fight well, at least within the company of a great many. You think that makes you something more than a maggot? Think again, slug. You are not worthy of Angmar's honour, no matter how much you think you have earned.
'Soon, when the true war begins and this battle is behind us, you will see. You will march in front of our war-host and fall first to the blades of our enemies.
'I hope to become a Taskmaster someday... do you think this speech was chiding enough?'
Return to Soldier Paashum at the encampment north-east of Tol Ascarnen
Counter Assault

An overeager dwarf-warrior made his way to the camp east of Tol Ascarnen when Angmar captured the keep. This dwarf would call the Free Peoples to his banner and make an assault against the fortress on his own, if given leave to do so.
'Quickly! We cannot risk this dwarf facing our champions in battle.'

The Free Peoples' encampment is somewhere to the east of Tol Ascarnen.
Paashum sent you to the enemy encampment of Tol Ascarnen to find and defeat First Marshal Án. You should not attempt this alone as Án is a powerful combatant.

The Angmar-encampment is somewhere to the west of Tol Ascarnen.
A successful assault against the Free Peoples' encampment resulted in the slaughter of the First Marshal and many of the forces located in the encampment east of Tol Ascarnen.

'You there, worm. I've a mission that will get you killed or earn you great favour with the War-tyrant. This should please you. But then again, you might be the worthless slug that so many say you are, ${PLAYER}.
'Personally, I'd not give up my gruel to stand by your side longer than I must...but that may change.
'We must weaken the enemy at the southern bridge. To do this we must destroy the flag which faces south. With it gone, we will dishearten them, scattering the forces on the bridge back to their encampments and reduce a great number of defenders near Tol Ascarnen.'

'Scouts told me of your success, but I find your need for approval amusing. You did well for a worthless sack of slug-meat.
'You'd better fight harder than you work, else this battle is truly lost.'
Return to Soldier Paashum at the encampment west of Tol Ascarnen
Destroy the Southern Flag
Angmar suffers in misery as the Free Peoples hold Tol Ascarnen.
'Get to it maggot. While those forces stand, we will face a much harder fight.'

Flags call the enemy to Tol Ascarnen facing south on the Hoardale island. Cross the river and destroy the flag located north of the southern bridge.
Paashum has tasked you with a mission to destroy the flag which calls the enemy defenders to the southern bridge over the Hoardale River.

Paashum is at the encampment on the western bank of the Hoarwell River, west of Tol Ascarnen.
You carefully sneaked to the flag calling the Free Peoples to the defence of the southern bridge and destroyed it. This set-back will surely give your forces a chance to defeat the enemy within Tol Ascarnen.

'You there, worm. I've a mission that will get you killed or earn you great favour with the War-tyrant. This should please you. But then again, you might be the worthless slug that so many say you are, ${PLAYER}.
'Personally, I'd not give up my gruel to stand by your side longer than I must... but that may change.
'Our number lost out to the enemy at Tol Ascarnen, and now we must take the keep back, but there are many foes standing in our way. We can lessen this number if we can down their banners. Scouts report that the fools at the western bridge will scatter to other posts when their banner is lowered. If we can destroy that banner, we can increase our chances at winning the day.'
'I saw the flag fall, cur. You did well. Well enough that I might consider you as a warrior on the front line in the assault. Ha!'
Return to Soldier Paashum at the encampment west of Tol Ascarnen
Destroy the Western Flag
Angmar suffers in misery as the Free Peoples hold Tol Ascarnen.
'Get to it maggot. While those forces stand, we will face a much harder fight.'

Cross the bridge to the north-east of the camp and destroy the flag against the crumbling walls near the western shore of the Hoardale island.
Paashum has tasked you with a mission to destroy the flag which calls the enemy defenders to the western bridge over the Hoardale River.

Paashum is at the encampment on the western bank of the Hoarwell River, west of Tol Ascarnen.
You carefully sneaked to the flag calling the Free Peoples to the defence of the western bridge and destroyed it. This set-back will surely give your forces a chance to defeat the enemy within Tol Ascarnen.
Collected Rockwithers's horn

'We've won the keep for a moment only, cur. You've a new task handed down from the War-tyrant himself, and you'll see it done or feel my boot!
'Across the river to the south, in the woods of Hithlad, stalks a great beast with shaggy fur. This beast has two great horns, though only one is needed for our purpose. The horn belongs to the mighty Rockwithers. We think it is the eldest of the Thistledown herd. Slaughter the beast and get its horn. Together with the sinew of drakes and the heartwood of a great Leafcull Huorn, we will build a horn to call our brethren to battle.
'To the south with you and don't return without the prize, maggot!'

'It's about time, you useless bag of flesh. I've a mind to flay your hide just for you taking so long.
'No matter... you did what was needed, and though I've a mind to see you suffer for your sluggard's way, I'd rather see the horn built so that there is a better chance we hold this tomb of stone.
'I'll pay you attention as you deserve. Take no solace though, you weak-livered wretch: it's a fleeting bit of accomplishment for you in a lifetime of worthless and wasted effort.'

'I told you not to return to me until you'd seen this through, you maggot. If your body wouldn't make such a nice blockade when the Free Peoples return, I'd gut you now, but I'd rather wait and use your sorry carcase as a shield myself.
'Get out there, sluggard! You've a job to do!'
Talk to Soldier Kaasak at Tol Ascarnen
Collect Rockwithers's horn
Horn of Rockwithers
Tol Ascarnen has fallen to the combined might of Angmar's army, but their forces are meagre, and they must fortify quickly, else the Free Peoples will regain a foothold here.

Rockwithers can be found among the Thistledown Grazers, south across the Hoarwell River.
Angmar's forces at Tol Ascarnen are building a horn with which to call reinforcements to the fight when the Free Peoples return to assault the area. Kaasak has tasked you with retrieving the horn of the great aurochs, Rockwithers.

'Well, the War-tyrant isn't satisfied with just oil. He wants iron, he says, for the oil.
'My head swims a moment, and I realize what he's saying. We need ore, iron ore to build a great iron belly to house the oil. Then we'll heat the oil and douse those wretches. Cooked meat for all!
'We know that the Isendeep Mine houses a great deal of ore. Go there, or if you think it too far a trek, find the dwarves. Those bearded slugs carry the ore sometimes.'
'This will do nicely, get others to the task so we can build the iron belly and cook us some meals.'
'Get to work, slug. I'm not in the habit of taking kindly to those who shirk their duties!'
Deliver the ore to Soldier Glat at Tol Ascarnen
An Iron Belly
The Free Peoples will return to take Tol Ascarnen, and Angmar's defenders wish to strengthen the walls with deterrents that will drive the foe away.

Iron ore can be found on the dwarves who fight for the Free Peoples or from the Isendeep Mine to the north.
Angmar's army is shoring up the defences at Tol Ascarnen. Glat intends to build a massive iron pot to heat oil with which to douse the Free Peoples who attempt to assail the keep.

'We are to build an iron cauldron and fill it with boiling oil to pour upon our enemies. I'd advise against eating the boiled flesh... it'll taste something awful, slathered in oil, sluggard. Better to eat them raw if you ask me.
'Still, the War-tyrant speaks, and you act. Get the iron we need from either the dwarves stationed throughout the Ettenmoors or from the Isendeep Mine in the northern section of Arador's End bordering the Misty Mountains.
'Stop staring at me all slack jawed and step-to.'

'We need more soldiers like you, willing to do everything they are told without questioning the wisdom in the actions, mindlessly obeying my orders.
'Good work!'
'Get to work, slug. I'm not in the habit of taking kindly to those who shirk their duties!'
Deliver the ore to Soldier Kafaaz at Lugazag
Iron Belly of Lugazag

Lugazag belongs to Angmar, and the Free Peoples must be kept from within its walls. The War-tyrant bade his soldiers build a pot to boil oil in with which to douse the enemy as they try to assault the main corridor.

Iron ore can be found on the dwarves who fight for the Free People or from the Isendeep Mine to the north.
Angmar's army is shoring up the defences at Lugazag. They intend to build a massive iron pot to heat oil with which to douse the Free Peoples who attempt to assail the tower.

'We are to build an iron cauldron and fill it with boiling oil to use against our enemies.
'Why would we eat flesh soured by the taste of oil? Fried flesh cannot be as healthy as raw meat picked from the bone, but I digress.
'The War-tyrant wills it, and we cede to his will. Head into the Ettenmoors and collect the iron carried by the dwarves or collect it from the Isendeep Mine. I care not where you get the materials, just return them to me and quickly. We must prepare!'
'A savage temperament and a quick worker... you are an able one, aren't you? I shall speak well of you to the War-tyrant. You might yet earn his favour.'
'Get to work, slug. I'm not in the habit of taking kindly to those who shirk their duties!'
Deliver the ore to Soldier Gozad at Tírith Rhaw
Iron Belly of Tírith Rhaw

Tírith Rhaw belongs to Angmar, and the Free Peoples must be kept from within the walls. The War-tyrant bid his soldiers build a pot to boil oil in with which to douse the enemy as they try to assault the main corridor.

Iron ore can be found on the dwarves who fight for the Free Peoples or from the Isendeep Mine to the north.
Angmar's army is shoring up the defences at Tírith Rhaw. Gozad intends to build a massive iron pot to heat oil with which to douse the Free Peoples who attempt to assail the tower.

'Oil will fill an iron pot and be boiled. The liquid will pour onto our enemies, and they will die in agony. Can you think of anything more glorious?
'Of course not! The War-tyrant ordered this, and we fulfil his will like good little soldiers. So, worm, you are to go into the Ettenmoors and hunt the Free Peoples, for they carry barrels of oil to light their torches and spark their cook-fires. We will use this against them.
'Return the barrels to me, and I will fill the iron pot.'

'You did well, little soldier. A lickspittle of a different sort you are. I am pleased with what you've done, and so I say that you are a good soldier. Now be off with you, else my pleasant nature may turn foul.'
'Get to work, slug. I'm not in the habit of taking kindly to those who shirk their duties!'
Deliver the oil to Soldier Kaafaz at Lugazag
Oil Well
The Free Peoples will return to take Lugazag, and Angmar's defenders wish to strengthen the walls with deterrents that will drive the foe away.

The Free Peoples carry barrels of oil that can be used to fill the iron pots being built at Lugazag. Seek out the Free People guarding locations throughout the Ettenmoors and slaughter them for the oil they carry.
The War-tyrant desires to use boiling oil at Lugazag to punish the enemy as they make their assault. You were sent into the Ettenmoors to collect barrels of oil from the foe.

'Listen well, maggot. The War-tyrant wants to lay traps for the enemy, and so we shall. We've told the goblins in Grothum that they'll be sending us some fools capable of holding a crossbow and pulling its trigger. First, though, we need to get the goblins bolts they'll use to make the enemy dead.
'The enemy carries blades, and these blades can be shattered. Kill the enemy and shatter their blades. Then return those blades to me. We'll fasten together enough bolts to keep the goblins firing.
'Across the bridge to the south, you will find a small encampment of the enemy. Start there. Just know that you will find the enemy at any of the locations they control and always at Ost Ringdyr in the east.'
'Good work, maggot. A few more now, and we'll be ready to call in the goblins.'
'You maggot! I gave you an order. Get it done or taste my fist.'
Deliver the shattered blades to Soldier Glat
Shatter Their Blades

Angmar seeks to reinforce Tol Ascarnen, employing the assistance of goblin-archers, who hide behind the walls and launch deadly attacks at the Free Peoples foolish enough to enter the tunnel leading to the inner courtyard.

The Free Peoples carry weapons from which the blades can be taken and used to craft crossbow bolts. The Free Peoples can be found at any of the locations they control, including the encampment south of Tol Ascarnen.
In an effort to better fortify Tol Ascarnen, the War-tyrant has called to the goblins at Grothum and told his soldiers to craft bolts for the goblins to shoot into the tunnel at the mouth of the keep. Glat has left the task of obtaining the blades of the Free Peoples to you.

'Listen well, maggot. The War-tyrant wants to lay traps for the enemy, and so we shall. We've told the goblins in Grothum that they'll be sending us some fools capable of holding a crossbow and pulling its trigger. First we need to get the goblins bolts they'll use to make the enemy dead.
'There are many trees within this land, and though I'd rather take an axe and cleave them all down, the War-tyrant says that'll take too long and wants us looking for the chaff that has already fallen.
'We need to make many arrows for the goblins, so it is up to us to collect as much of the smaller bits of wood as we can. Search across the Ettenmoors and return the wood to me.'
'Good work, maggot. A few more now, and we'll be ready to call in the goblins.'
'You maggot! I gave you an order. Get it done or taste my fist.'
Deliver the kindling to Soldier Glat at Tol Ascarnen
Striking Shafts

Angmar seeks to reinforce Tol Ascarnen, employing the assistance of goblin-archers, who hide behind the walls and launch deadly attacks at the Free Peoples foolish enough to enter the tunnel leading to the inner courtyard.

Search the area of Hithlad for the kindling needed to make the arrow shafts. Hithlad and the Grimwood forest are south of Tol Ascarnen.
In an effort to better fortify Tol Ascarnen, the War-tyrant has called to the goblins at Grothum and told his soldiers to craft bolts for the goblins to shoot into the tunnel at the mouth of the keep. It falls to you to collect the wood for the shafts.

'We'll need reinforcements against these maggots. For that we need a way of calling more forces to the keep. The War-tyrant wants us to build a great horn to summon our forces to patrol the keep, and we'll do what he wants or feel the crack of his whip. This means that orders trickle down to you, and that means that you do my bidding, whelp.
'Take others and head north into Arador's End. Find the Wintersebb-drakes there and slaughter them for the pieces of their innards that join their bones. Collect them and return them to me.
'Whatever you do maggot, don't destroy the sinew. Ruined sinew is useless.'

'This will do well. I'll see that you are rewarded for your effort. Don't let a success like this go to your head though, whelp. You've a long way to go before the War-tyrant sees you as more than gristle on a tasty slab of rat-folk.'

'You've got nothing to offer me. Do you take me for some fresh recruit still carrying the stink of brimstone on his flesh? I've a mind to gut you now, but you've a job to do, and I will see that you do it. Get out there and get me what I need!'
Talk to Soldier Kaasak at Tol Ascarnen
Stringy Innards

Building a horn to summon reinforcements at Tol Ascarnen requires that several pieces are collected and assembled for an Orc to watch over and use when the Free Peoples make their assault against the fort.

The Wintersebb-drakes are found north, in sections near the Hoarwell's source and at the foot of the Misty Mountains.
Angmar's forces at Tol Ascarnen are crafting a great horn to call reinforcements to the fight when the Free Peoples return to assault the area. Kaasak has tasked you with collecting sinew from the Wintersebb-drakes to secure the many horns that will adorn the post.

'I've got orders to get oil into an iron pot and set it boiling so we can cook the enemy as they crash into our forces at the entrance to this tower. We'll oil them up before they go in and slow their progress.
'Find oil, maggot. We need to protect the wee boggarts. Sure there be none here, but the War-tyrant told me to tell you that!
'Now get to work!'

'Soon we'll have cooking flesh at our entrance, and we'll feast until our bellies are full. Still... I think that the meat will not be as sweet as the fresh kill of those rat-folk far to the south-west.'
'Get to work, slug. I'm not in the habit of taking kindly to those who shirk their duties!'
Deliver the oil to Soldier Gozad at Tírith Rhaw
Oil Up
The Free Peoples will return to take Tírith Rhaw and Angmar's defenders wish to strengthen the walls with deterrents that will drive the foe away.

The Free Peoples carry barrels of oil that can be used to fill the iron pots being built at Tírith Rhaw. Seek out the Free People guarding locations throughout the Ettenmoors and slaughter them for the oil they carry.
The War-tyrant desires to use boiling oil at Tírith Rhaw to punish the enemy as they make their assault. You were sent into the Ettenmoors to collect oil from the foe.

'It has come to my attention that your studies of the mysteries of Middle-earth have progressed considerably, ${PLAYER}. For many long centuries, those of us here in Rivendell have had limited opportunities to explore the world beyond, and soon the time shall come for us to take our leave and sail into the West with our brethren.
'Even those of us who live lives without measure cannot hope to know all the mysteries of the world, but we hope to carry with us into the West as great a trove of knowledge and history as we may, and so if you could aid us in this endeavour, we would be most grateful.
'To this end, I would ask you to pen some scholar's writs for us, so that we might add them to our libraries and ensure that they will forever adorn the shelves of luminous Valinor.'

'Ah, you have penned a few scholar's writs. Very good! These are a few more slivers of knowledge that shall not be lost to us when we embark on our journey into the West.
'Thank you, ${PLAYER}. We shall not forget your efforts on our behalf.'

'It is true that there are far more pressing matters at hand in the world today, as dark shadows sweep across the land and threaten all, but no matter how great the darkness becomes, that knowledge we collect here shall escape into Uttermost West, where it shall be forever beyond the grasp of evil... so do not dismiss the importance of this task!'
Present your scholar's writs to Cachúnir in Rivendell
Craft scholar's writs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Scholar's Writs -- Introduction
Cachúnir has expressed a desire to take as much history and lore of Middle-earth into the West as is possible.

Cachúnir is at Rivendell in the Trollshaws.
Cachúnir has asked you to pen some scholar's writs to be preserved in the libraries of Valinor when the Elves of Rivendell sail into the West.

'${PLAYER}, you are one of those who may be counted among the wise and learned of Middle-earth, and I need your help in recording the mysteries of these lands both great and small, before the time comes when I and my brethren must depart into the West.
'If you could see your way to penning some studies of the Unknown before you go, I would very much like to add your wisdom to the annals that we shall carry with us to Valinor.
'Certainly, the Elves of Rivendell will look favourably upon you should you undertake this task on our behalf.'

'Your studies of the Unknown are most interesting. Would that all such riddles could be explored in the time that remains to us, but with all the time in the world, that task would remain unfinished. We must simply be grateful for that which we can complete. I -- and all of Rivendell -- thank you for your efforts.'
'I see that the shrouds of the Unknown remain tightly wound around us. I hope your studies prove more fruitful upon your next journey, for the time remaining to us is limited.'
Present your Studies of the Unknown to Cachúnir in Rivendell
Craft Studies of the Unknown (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Studies of the Unknown -- Introduction
Cachúnir has expressed a desire to take as much history and lore of Middle-earth as possible when the Elves of Rivendell sail into the West.

Cachúnir is at Rivendell, in the Trollshaws.
Cachúnir has asked you to pen some studies of the Unknown and bring them to him.

'There are some jewels of knowledge that surpass even the most brilliant gem or bauble. It is one such that I would have you compile for us here at Rivendell, that we might bring it before our brethren in the Uttermost West, that they might gain once more from the lands that they once called home.
'Pen for me an essay entitled 'Of Mysteries Most Profound,' and your name shall be sung in the Last Homely House with reverence and gratitude.'

'Ah, let us see....
'Of Mysteries Most Profound' -- a title fitting for a study of one of the grand riddles of Middle-earth.
'Would that we had a hundred scholars such as yourself, ${PLAYER}, though even then it seems that countless enigmas would remain before us.'
'Take your time with that paper, ${PLAYER}. A great deal of research and study must go into such a craft. Perhaps some travel in the wilds would help you clear your head?'
Present 'Of Mysteries Most Profound' to Cachúnir in Rivendell
Craft 'Of Mysteries Most Profound' (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Of Mysteries Most Profound -- Introduction
Cachúnir has expressed a desire to take as much history and lore of Middle-earth as possible when the Elves of Rivendell sail into the West.

Cachúnir is at Rivendell, in the Trollshaws.
Cachúnir has asked you to pen an essay entitled 'Of Mysteries Most Profound' and bring it to him.
Collected tomb-raiders' sashes (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Greetings, ${PLAYER}. You have arrived at a difficult time... we have been stretched terribly thin by the incursions of the Angmarim into our lands and by the number of lawless brigands that have been stirred up by the gathering clouds of war.
'It is against the latter which I hope you can aid us. The bands of tomb-raiders have become so bold of late that they have taken to wearing sashes of allegiance to their various unsavoury leaders. I would have you bring me these sashes as proof of their defeat.
'If you can do this for us, then I will see to it that your name is regarded well among the Wardens of Annúminas.'
'Your actions speak well of your skill and bravery. Would that I could reward you more handsomely for your efforts, but our resources are drawn thin, and our thanks must suffice for the time being.'

'Time is not on our side, ${PLAYER}. There is no shortage of enemies -- particularly those carrion-seekers who would raid the tombs of our ancestors.
'Surely claiming a few sashes from them should pose no great challenge, should it?'
Bring tomb-raiders' sashes to Cannuion at Tinnudir.
Collect tomb-raiders' sashes (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Tomb-raiders' Sashes -- Introduction
Cannuion told you of the terrible threat the Angmarim and tomb-raiders pose to the Rangers of Evendim.

Tomb-raiders can be found throughout Evendim. Cannuion is at Tinnudir.
Cannuion has asked you to collect the tomb-raiders' sashes of allegiance and bring them to him.

'As members of our kindred come of age, we once would send them on pilgrimages to notable places of our forefathers. In this time of war, however, we must make changes.
'I have heard that you have some considerable skill in the craft of weaponsmithy, ${PLAYER}. Perhaps you could forge for us ceremonial daggers which we can bestow upon our young warriors? It would earn you considerable respect among the Rangers of the North if you could do this for us.'

'I see you have completed the ceremonial daggers which I asked of you. I thank you for your time and effort on our behalf, yet we are always in short supply here, so I will gladly accept any more you may be able to craft for us.'
'Ore is not terribly common here in Evendim, as I understand it, but we have a need for more ceremonial daggers, if you can find the materials you require to forge them.'
Present your Ceremonial Daggers to Cannasgam at Tinnudir
Craft Ceremonial Daggers (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Ceremonial Dagger -- Introduction
The Rangers of the North once sent their youths coming of age upon pilgrimages to notable sites of their forefathers, but war has necessitated a change.

Cannasgam is at Tinnudir in Evendim.
Cannasgam has asked you to forge ceremonial daggers and bring them to her.

'In the matter of weaponsmithy, you have few peers, and I would ask an important favour of you.
'Among those of our kindred who have joined the Wardens of Annúminas, there are those who must be recognized for feats of valour above and beyond the call of duty. Upon these heroes, we bestow ceremonial blades fashioned in a likeness similar to the sword of kings, which was wielded by Elendil and broken at Barad-dûr.
'If you have the skill to forge these blades, it would gain you great favour among my people.'
'You have brought me the ceremonial blades as I have asked, and they are among the finest crafted I have yet seen! My thanks to you, ${PLAYER}. You have earned much honour in the lands of Evendim.'
'I understand resources are scarce, but if you could see your way to crafting a few ceremonial blades for us, we could surely use them.'
Present your Ceremonial Blades to Cannasgam at Tinnudir
Craft Ceremonial Blades (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Ceremonial Blades -- Introduction
The Rangers of the North confer ceremonial blades upon the greatest of their heroes.

Cannasgam is at Tinnudir in Evendim.
Cannasgam has asked you to forge the ceremonial blades, which the Rangers of the North confer upon their greatest heroes.

'Among the Wardens of Annúminas, we traditionally signify the authority of our leadership via the Warden's Sceptre. Alas, tradition also dictates the inclusion of a rather rare ore in its construction.
'If you can forge for us such a sceptre, the Wardens would be greatly obliged to you.'
'Aye, that is a Warden's Sceptre, and elegantly forged as well! My thanks to you and your kin, good ${PLAYER}.'
'Remember, should you come across the ore required, we would be greatly appreciative by your crafting of a Warden's Sceptre for our use.'
Present your Warden's Sceptre to Cannasgam at Tinnudir
Craft a Warden's Sceptre (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Warden's Sceptre -- Introduction
The Wardens of Annúminas signify their leadership with a special token, the Warden's Sceptre.

Cannasgam is at Tinnudir in Evendim.
Cannasgam has asked you to forge a Warden's Sceptre and bring it to her.
Collected Orc battle-medallion (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'So, ${PLAYER}, are you ready to face the Orcs in all their strength? Many have marched down now through the passes of the Ram Dúath, and their main encampment lies south-east of here in Dol Dínen, where they prepare to strike down into the heart of Eriador. We have not nearly the numbers needed to face them in force, but we sortie forth and skirmish against them daily in an effort to slow their advance and weaken them before the inevitable battles to follow.
'Those among the Orcs who have faced and survived battles are awarded battle-medallions. If we can defeat these veterans, the resolve of the greater force will be weakened, and there is some hope that they might be held at bay.
'Bring me Orc battle-medallions as proof of your strength and valour, and we shall support your efforts in any way we can.'
'Well done! You have fought long and hard against the Orcs of Dol Dínen. We thank you for your stalwart efforts and shall find some way to reward you as our meagre supplies allow.'
'You have been unable to gather many Orc battle-medallions? Alas, there is no shortage of Orcs to claim them from, if you can find the strength and courage to face them....'
Bring Orc Battle-medallions to Nethúr at Esteldín.
Collect Orc battle-medallions (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Orc Battle-medallions -- Introduction
Nethúr told you that veteran Orcs carry special medallions which signify their achievements.

Orcs can be found in Dol Dínen, south-east of Esteldín, in the North Downs. Nethúr is at Esteldín.
Nethúr asked you to collect Orc battle-medallions and bring them to her.

'Are you not a tailor of some skill, ${PLAYER}? If so, we have a task in which you might aid us. For many ages, it has been our practice to send those of our kindred who are coming of age on pilgrimages to notable places of our forefathers. The war against Angmar has forced us to change this.
'Here in Esteldín, we give our youths special sashes to signify their coming of age, but supplies of fabric and those with the skill to craft any quantity of them have been short. Most cloth has gone for bandages.
'If you could weave a few of these sashes for us, we would be quite grateful.'

'You have brought more Rangers' sashes? Very good. We have a need, for we have a number of youths on the cusp of adulthood -- I only wish that more of them could survive their first battles with the Orcs....'
'Both time and materials are in short supply, but if you could find the resources to produce more Rangers' sashes, it would be quite helpful.'
Present your Rangers' sashes to Techeron in Esteldín
Craft Ranger's sashes (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Rangers' Sashes -- Introduction

Techeron has asked you to craft sashes for the Rangers of Esteldín to bestow upon their deputies and followers as they wage battle against the forces of Angmar.
Turn in Rangers' sashes to Techeron to improve your standing with the Rangers of Esteldín.

Techeron is at Esteldín in the North Downs.
Techeron has asked you to craft a number of Rangers' sashes for the youth of his kindred and bring them to him.
Collected barrow-treasures (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Greetings ${PLAYER}. I have been very interested in the doings here at the hunting lodge. It seems the only place here in Bree where people would even think about heading up to the old Barrow-downs. Well, there I go talking before explaining. You see, I am quite interested in the place -- the Barrow-downs that is. Ancient cities, old kings, and treasure beyond imagining! My dad, Newbold, has told me such wonderful stories. It seems somehow he got quite a few pieces of old histories out of the Downs, though he never would tell me how.
'I have tasked every hunter who frequents this lodge to travel to the Barrow-downs and retrieve some of the Barrow-treasure, but it seems that none of them have the nerve. As for those Rangers, they aren't ones to be pushed, if you get my meaning. I have heard talk that the treasures within the underground barrows are some of the finest. One of the hunters goes on and on about removing the treasure and breaking some curse laid on it... all a bunch of nonsense if you ask me.
'If you would travel to the Barrow-downs, venture into the underground barrows and retrieve some of the old Barrow-treasures, you would be held in high regard, I'm sure.'

'You have done it! Look here, ${PLAYER} wasn't scared to go up into those old hills, ha!
'Don't mind the other hunters, they are all superstitious fools. They think the Barrow-downs are haunted, can you believe it!'
'You have returned without the Barrow-treasures? I had hoped you wouldn't be scared of some old bones in the hills....'
Bring the Barrow-treasures to Tad Leafcutter
Collect barrow-treasures (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Barrow-treasure -- Introduction
It has long been a legend among the Bree-folk that great treasure still remains buried in the barrows of the Barrow-downs, but there are few among them with the courage to seek it.

Barrows are scattered across the Northern and Southern Barrow-downs. Tad Leafcutter is at the Bree Hunting Lodge in Bree-town, east of the Barrow-downs.
Tad Leafcutter has asked you to enter the various barrows within the Barrow-downs and recover some of the Barrow-treasures which lie there.
Collected a Cardolan trinket

'I have heard your name whispered before in these streets. I know who you are, and I know your intentions, so I will not waste your time. You have perhaps heard of Black Riders who came through town, causing geese to scream and dogs to howl? Well, they are more than just Men in black cloaks, and they are a far greater danger than any of these simple folk know.
'The Riders have awoken something, something that should have remained sleeping. You have no doubt heard at least a part of the tale of the fall of Cardolan? It was a nation divided by war and decimated by a Plague borne on winds out of Mordor, their remains inhabited with the servants of the Witch-king! The awakened spirits have heard their master's call once more, and I fear for the safety of Bree. I have been tasked to guard it at all costs.
'What I ask of you is to enter one of the barrows and put to rest the bones that still dwell within. Once the barrow housed a great ruler of Cardolan, now it is known as Haudh Iarchith, and Men shiver to hear its name whispered. Enter into Haudh Iarchith and put to rest those that wander its halls. Some of the wights might carry trinkets of Cardolan. Bring them to me as proof of your deeds, and you will earn great respect among the hunters of Bree who would not dare to enter those halls of madness.'
'I did not doubt that you would finish the task, ${PLAYER}. It is well that you have returned, however, for your strength will be needed sooner than you think.'
'You have not recovered any of the Cardolan trinkets?'
Bring the Cardolan trinket to Anglinn
Collect a Cardolan trinket
Cardolan Trinket -- Introduction
The Barrow-downs were once a haven of the Rangers of Cardolan. They fell long ago and became of place of terror beneath the shadow of the Witch-king of Angmar.

Barrows lie scattered across the Northern and Southern Barrow-downs. Anglinn is at the Bree Hunting Lodge in Bree-town, east of the Barrow-downs.
The Ranger Anglinn has asked you to banish the wights beneath the Northern and Southern Barrow-downs and bring him trinkets of ancient Cardolan which they might be carrying.
Collect wooden figurines (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Welcome, traveller. I would ask what brings you to Bree, but so many strangers have been arriving from the south and east that it no longer matters what they come for.
'The Men of Bree are artful woodworkers. Our crafts are carried and traded across Eriador. Just last season I had word from a dwarf that he had received one of our wooden figurines as a gift from a travelling merchant.
'That got me to thinking; why not sell these figurines as a novelty for travelling merchants to bring back as petty gifts? The woodworkers of Bree are worked hard enough as it is without the extra burden that I would place upon them, but maybe you would be able to find more of the figurines? You would be doing a mighty service for the Men of Bree, ${PLAYER}.'
'You found more wooden figurines? I can tell that this was crafted with care ${PLAYER}, the woodworkers of Bree thank you.'
'I know an adventurer such as yourself must be very busy, but if you have the time would you bring me wooden figurines?'
Bring the wooden figurines to Maggie Smallwood
Collect wooden figurines (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Wooden Figurines - Introduction
The woodworkers of Bree pride themselves in their craftsmanship.

Maggie Smallwood is at the Bree Hunting Lodge, west of Bree's South-gate.

'Have you stopped in the streets of Bree and listened, really listened, ${PLAYER}? The sound of a minstrel's instrument can usually be heard throughout Bree, though it is becoming rarer by the day.
'You see, the usual fair for the woodworkers of Bree besides hunting bows and farmcraft was wooden instruments. Clarinets, harps, and viols...ah, the beautiful viols! Those are one of the harder instruments that our woodworkers craft here in Bree. Well, what with all the commotion with the brigands hereabouts, the woodworkers have been hard-pressed by the demand for all manner of spears, bows, and staves, and they haven't the time to craft new viols!
'If you would, find five viol and return them here to me. It would be for the worst if the streets were left without music.'

'Ah, these are finely-crafted viols. Listen to the soft, sweet sound!
'You have done a great service to Bree, ${PLAYER}.'
'I fear that without new viols, the streets of Bree may become deprived of music sooner than you would think....'

'A terrible fate for certain, but no different than they shall do to us. The ore can be found in the Isendeep Mine to the north or from the goblins of Grothum in the north-east. Go quickly, friend, for we must prepare our defence.'

'North of here, in the place called Arador's End, you will find drakes. These creatures have very strong sinew that ties their bones and muscles together. 'Why hello again. I was beginning to think you wouldn't come back after you brought me that nice present. I thought maybe you were taken by one of those terrible wolves.

'But more and more of us have been disappearing lately; I think that it may be wolf-mischief. We need a brave rooster such as yourself to go warn the other coops and find out exactly what is going on! There are coops at Brownlocks' Farm to the east and slightly north on the road to Needlehole, Cotton's Farm to the east in Bywater, and Bamfurlong far to the east and south along the river.'

'Wolves? Of course, I have seen the wolves! Have you looked around? Almost our entire coop has been taken!

'What is that now? Wolves, no, of course not, not here in the Shire. I have heard rumours of them, yes, but they are just that, rumours.
'Chickens get to talking, you know, and can come up with wild, fanciful stories. The only Wolf on this farm is a dog! Of course, the farmer's dogs may be why we have no wolves. They are good protectors.'

'Wolves here, in the Shire? Wolves have not dared to venture in so far since the old times, or so legends tell.

'I'm a pig, you fool rooster! Can't you see I'm in enough trouble as it is, what with all these nasty shrews about? Sometimes I wish that I was a pony.'

'What do you want? Protect your coop against wolves? I have my own farm to protect and no time for others.
'My but you would make a nice snack. Be on your way, rooster.'
'Shooing off a few wolves is mighty tempting, but I've too much work to do here. Besides, what if the wolves come here?'

'Ho there, rooster! You aren't one of ours! What are you doing here? Trying to steal some of our hens for your coop?
'Wolves? We haven't any wolves around here, but if they show their shaggy faces at Bamfurlong, you can be sure we'll deal with them.'

'I thank you for your bravery, my fellow rooster, but I fear that it may not have been enough to save many of us from a terrible fate. While you were away, I had time to think over the circumstances and consider our options. If we do nothing, our numbers will surely dwindle. A similar doom befell Dora Brownlock's coop, and I fear ours is not far off.
'I cannot leave the coop; I have too many responsibilities with half of the coop under my supervision. I will set this task upon you: travel out into the world, even beyond the borders of the Shire. Speak with other animals you encounter and see if you can find anyone willing to help us in our plight.
'You should begin by seeking out animals here in the Shire.'

'Now what is this? First three hobbits sleeping in the forest, and now a chicken?
'You want me to help protect your coop from wolves? My friend, I would sooner eat you, particularly since chicken is very high among my dietary choices.
'However, seeing as you were brave enough to speak with me in the first place, I will forego my lunch for now.'

'Our lumber-yard is overrun by those pesky beasts from the north. I think I know a way that we can weaken them but it is a bit dangerous. The wolves prowling the dark places of these lands are enemies to everything and everyone, we may be able to use them as a distraction to better enable you and your number to defeat the Enemy at the lumber-yard.
'To do this we need to get the wolves good and angry and then get them to recognize that the lumber-yard is the source of their woes. I think if you get their talons and put them on one of the stumps near the lumber-yard that you can get a pack to attack it. That is...if you are willing to.
'You should find the wolves scattered throughout these lands, some in the woods to the east and other across the river and up the hills to the west.'
'Yes, these should get those wolves riled for certain. Now we just need you to get them to a proper place. Look for the cut stump at the outskirts of the lumber yard on the side nearest the river.'
'Hurry along and get those talons. They might just do the trick.'

'It is good to see you, ${PLAYER}. The war fares no better, and the strength of the Enemy seems to ever increase despite our efforts and sacrifices. With one such as you at our side, we would push the matter towards the heart of the enemy's seat of power in Carn Dûm.
'If you can summon the courage, I would have you strike at the large Orc-encampments around the putrid swamps of Malenhad in southern Angmar. There, you will find Orcs who have fought long in their campaigns in the distant east. These foes have a deadly experience upon the battlefield, and their loss will wound the strength of Angmar.
'Claim the campaign-medallions they hold and return them to me.'

'You are one of the few who have returned from those foetid swamps and survived to tell the tale.
'I am glad to see that your efforts were not for naught, for here you bring me many of the Enemy's prized medallions... and with them a measure of their strength has been hewn away.'
'Ready yourself well before you head into the hills and swamps of Angmar to do battle, ${PLAYER}. It is not a place for the weak of heart or the unprepared.'

'A fine day to you during dark times, ${PLAYER}.
I have a matter of craft for you. We have need of fine cloaks for the Rangers of Esteldín. They are something of a mark of pride, not to mention being remarkably useful to those who must live for long periods out among the forests and hills, but they suffer much wear, and our supplies of them are coming up short.
'If you could craft a few Rangers' cloaks for me, I and my kindred would be much obliged!'

'There we are, cloaks fit for men who must travel far and fast.
'My thanks to you, for every bit helps during this time of hardship.'

'The Men of the North have long come to know the Rangers as folk of dangerous mystery -- how are we supposed to impress anyone wearing shoddy, worn cloaks with tatters and holes in them?
'Well if the truth be known, it is really more about keeping warm and dry out there on the fields during long rainy evenings. The tattered cloaks make a much more dangerous impression.'

'I have a matter of sombre import, ${PLAYER}. Many of our bravest fellows have fallen in battle against the Orcs who stream down through the passes from the North, and we would honour their deeds both for their sake, and for the morale of those who must inevitably take up their standard and march forth to die in their stead.
'Your skill is such that I would ask you to weave a tapestry of the deeds of our heroes to exemplify the life and death of those who fight under the banner of Esteldín, that they might be remembered in more peaceful ages to come.'

'This tapestry, finely woven and glorious in its tales of valour, shall serve our purposes well! Would that I might some day stand beside those brave spirits whose tales are chronicled herein.
'Thank you, ${PLAYER}. Your skill in these matters is unsurpassed, and the Rangers of Esteldín stand in your debt.'
'So many have fallen with their tales and songs known only to a few. Could you see it in your heart to craft a tapestry to record their lives and deeds for those who follow?'

'Mordirith the coward has escaped us... but did you notice that the blade of Dúnachar was still lodged within his breast? I wager the pain of that blade's light shall be a constant reminder of the evil he has committed.
'While my revenge is not yet complete, I would wager there will be others who will complete this task. For now, I can take solace in this fact...
'A moment, someone approaches!'

'What an unsettling end to our battle. I fear that there is much more to that old woman than what we see upon the surface.
'However, we cannot deal with that matter now. We should leave here before we are overrun with Angmarim or their servants!'
'We should tarry here no longer. Are you prepared to leave? I will show you the secret ways out of Carn Dûm and back to Gath Forthnír.'

'It seems my long imprisonment in Carn Dûm has served us well. We have come far into the the Witch-king's keep unnoticed. It would be folly to think, though, that our fortune will hold. Already, Mordirith may be aware of our presence.
'Steel yourself for the battle ahead. I have few words of advice to offer you, other than to warn you that Mordirith is a master of trickery and illusion. He will try to break your resolve with his words. Do not let him! Keep to your hope and trust your companions.
'Shall we go now?'

'Hullo there, my young ${RACE}. Have you come to learn about the Mathom Society? I know quite a bit, as I have been a member for over four years now! Come closer...my eyesight is not as good as it once was; I turn one hundred this year, you know.
'Five years ago, a group of hobbits began to take a close interest in the Mathom House and the recovery of mathoms across the Shire. We have the most splendid meetings and discuss all sorts of things: where we would be likely to find mathoms, who holds private collections of mathoms from which we could borrow, or even what differentiates a mathom from a non-mathom! Most of the meetings occur over dinner, and we have begun to get quite a turnout. Why, just last week Baldwin Foxtail proposed to add to the main floor to increase the number we could fit at the table. Who would have thought so many hobbits were interested in history?
'Though we have some wonderful plans, we have not actually begun the process of going out and collecting the mathoms. That is where youngsters such as yourself come in! If you happen across any mathoms in your travels be sure to bring them back here so they can be organized and catalogued. It would be a pity to lose any more mathoms. A good deal of our collection has been diminished ever since old Bilbo took some of our most interesting pieces with him when he went and got himself killed, or lost -- you know, I don't rightly remember what happened to the old fool now that I think about it....'

'You have returned with some mathoms? Oh, Brombard will be overjoyed! I will put these down into storage right away. If they ever get put on display, I will make sure your name is added to the plaque that accompanies them.'
'Are those mathoms you have there? Oh, they aren't? I knew that, of course. I was only joking with you....'

Collected a well-kept mathom

'We have been busy as bees these last few days organizing the Mathom Society members and finding storage for all the new mathoms that have been pouring in. Soon enough, we may be forced to use the old storage tunnels. We have never had this much activity before, and I think it is too much for some of the younger hobbits. I overheard some grumblings from young Baldwin outside over finding a honey-roasted chicken for the next Mathom Society meeting when he should have been labeling mathoms! Some of these young hobbits seem more interested in the meeting dinner-menu than the wonderful new mathoms.
'Anyhow, we have found that many of the mathoms are not in very good condition. I don't know what has happened to many of them -- to tell the truth I don't know what most of them do or did! What I do know is that they are not of display quality. What would we have to show of all our hard work if we have no display pieces?
'If you come across any well-kept mathoms, be sure to take extra care when delivering them to us. The more intact they are, the better. And do try to at least wipe them clean before you drop them off...some of them have had some very queer things on them.'
'A well-kept mathom! I will get it to the Master Chef right away; he is so good at cataloguing the smaller mathoms, you know.'
'Have you found any well-kept mathoms yet, ${PLAYER}?'

'Hullo there, my name is Baldwin Foxtail son of Brombard Foxtail...he's the keeper of the Mathom House, you know. I am one of the more important members of the Mathom Society; I am in charge of overseeing the collection of the delectable menu items for our extravagant Mathom Society dinners, as well as the labeling and cleaning of several of the more significant sections of the Mathom House storage collection.
'We have run into a bit of trouble, what with all the adventurers coming in with new mathoms, I have never seen so many in all my life! Old Greylond seems to fix all of us to get the mathoms sorted and organized before he thinks about the dinner menu, quite silly if you ask me.
'Our Master Chef has been locked up in the cellar of the Mathom House for so long now that I am worried he may have forgotten how to cook! I am worried even more that he will not have time to cook up his specialty, seasoned beef with cauliflower, in time for our next Mathom Society dinner.
'We can't hold the dinner without something to serve! Do you think you would be able to find us some seasoned beef with cauliflower? You would be doing the Mathom Society quite a service.'
'You found us some seasoned beef with cauliflower? You have saved me! I can not thank you enough, ${PLAYER}.'
'Did you find any seasoned beef with cauliflower yet?'

'The members of the Mathom Society do their best thinking when they have a full stomach. Most of our ideas do not come to us until after we have finished with the Mathom Society dinners that accompany every Mathom Society meeting.
'We have had a problem finding enough strawberries for our strawberry dessert-wine. One of the main tasks of the Mathom Society members was to go on a weekly strawberry-picking in order to make enough strawberry dessert-wine, but with all of the work we have been tasked with, I doubt we will be able to find enough in time for our next meeting.
'If you are looking for a task, bring us five bottles of strawberry dessert-wine. It would be awful if we did not have something to sip after dinner. Why, I doubt any planning would get done at all without it!'
'Those look like fine bottles. I will make sure to sample these bottles personally to ensure that they meet the strict Mathom Society standards.'
'Did you acquire those bottles of strawberry dessert-wine yet? I am simply dreading the meeting without them.'

'Hoi there! I am Argirion, boatswain aboard the Gilminuial -- or at least I was until we were beset by a great storm! The Gilminuial is a ship belonging to we Rangers that sails up and down the Baranduin providing much-needed supplies to the Wardens of Annúminas in the North.
'That work, though, was brought to an end with the storm. Our ship was grounded, the quartermaster and I were washed overboard, and our cargo lost. I know not if anyone else survived the disaster and would be pleased if you could search northward for the Captain.
'It is also vital that the cargo be recovered, for it was intended to supply the Wardens as they fight the evil that has come to Annúminas. I am sure it is strewn all along the Brandywine.'

'Ah! You have come from Argirion? He and Mindambeth are well? That is good.
'You may return to Argirion and let him know that all survived the wreck and are now repairing the damage. Do as Argirion requested and gather the cargo before you return, however... it is vital for the defence of Annúminas.'

'It is good to know that my kinsmen did not perish in the storm.
'Thank you as well for recovering this cargo. Bring it to Mindambeth, as well as any more you may find as you journey along the Baranduin.
'As thanks for your efforts, you may choose something from the ship's stores that have survived. Mindambeth will see to your reward.'
'Have you found some of the lost ale and cram? The Wardens will need both if they are to continue to keep Annúminas from falling completely to the Iron Crown!'
Bring the lost cargo to Argirion

'Apparently everything that you have done out here has not gone unnoticed. Despite protests against offering you more rewards, the First Marshals have issued a writ saying that I must offer rewards to those who have proven worthy of the honour.
'Now this brings us to the question that is burning in that primitive little brain of yours: 'How do I prove my worth?' Simple answer for a simpleton; bring me tokens of valour and it will do much towards proving your worth.'

'You got them all. Excellent work. This key opens the First Marshal chests behind me. I know what you're thinking.
'What am I supposed to do -- open one chest, open all chests, or what?
'I can solve this for you simply. The key will only open one chest. You want to open more, you need more keys. You want more keys -- you go through me. You got that?
'All right. These are treasures found while we fight this war. Do yourself a favour and don't ask from where they came.'

'Valorous or not valorous -- doesn't matter. I'm the one with the keys.
'Until you prove to me that you're something more than another would-be warrior who stands about asking: How will we stop this army of Angmar at our walls? How will we fight that?
'Get out there and earn some Tokens of Valour.'
Deliver the Tokens of Valour to Quartermaster Ash
