'You work your entire life to stand against evil and spit long and hard in its face and you get stationed here handing out free items to folk like you. There was a time when I was the finest soldier in all of Eriador, but now I push quill over parchment, and count the number of keys on a ring or tokens in hand.
'Let's get on with it then. Seems you made a name for yourself out there in the wild, and the Second Marshals tell me that you are owed favour and reward. Good news for you, nothing but a pain in my nethers.
'Here is what we do from now on. You show me that you have been a good little warrior by handing over the tokens of valour you collect. I hand you keys in exchange. It is simple enough for even your primitive brain to understand, I think.'

You fool! Calling the beasts now would bring them against our forces!

'Being sent here to Grothum was bad enough, now I have to deal with these fool târks and dwarfs stalking the mines. I'll not have this, maggot!
'We know them drakes stalk the mines, and it is time that we use their strength against our foes! We need to call them to action and get them to fight their leaders!
'Very near where their leader stands is a nice, flat rock just waiting for slabs of meat to be tossed atop it to get those drakes running. Get some haunches from those aurochs and toss them on the slab. That ought to get the drake's attention. Then we'll see how strong these wretches truly are!'
Place the thistledown haunches on the flat stone in the Isendeep

Angmar must not control the mine
Call the Beasts!
Drakes stalk the mines and are a foe that often destroys the Orcs and trolls within the mines. It is time to turn that power against the Free People.

Search the areas south of Tol Ascarnen or west along the plains south and west of Dâr-gazag for the thistledown grazers. Collect some of their haunches and bring them to the slab within the depths of the Isendeep.
Soldier Golb directed you to turn the force of drakes often found stalking the Isendeep Mines against the Free People. He wants you to draw the drakes in with the promise of aurochs meat.
The haunches are placed, the drakes are sure to come. You should hide.

'The mines are fallen to Angmar again and I will not stand for it, ${PLAYER}. We must get the mine back.
'I suggest that we use the drakes stalking the depths as cover for our attack. Search the lands south of Tol Ascarnen or west and south on the plains of the Steps of Gram for the Thistledown grazers. Collect haunches from those beasts and deliver them to a flat stone near where the Tyrant holding the mine keeps his company.

Search the areas south of Tol Ascarnen or west along the plains, south of Dâr-gazag for the Thistledown Grazers. Collect some of their haunches and bring them to the slab within the depths of the Isendeep.

Huorns of the Grimwood

To retake the Grimwood the forces of Angmar will need to be vigilant and assisted, so thinks Taskmaster Gazgortag. He thinks that the living trees near the lumber camp will come and fight for the forces of Angmar and sets you to the task of calling them to the fight.

Seek a Leafcull Huorn within the southern stretches of the Grimwood. Cut out its heart and place it on the stump near the Grimwood Lumber Camp.
Taskmaster Gazgortag believes that you can draw the Huorns into conflict with the Free People currently occupying the Grimwood Lumber Camp. He directed you to cut out the heart of the leafcull Huorn in attempt to draw out the enemy.
Caragdal has arrived to fortify the Grimwood!

'To the west, in a tower draped in the webs of their mistress, lay a great spider. She will come to us and oversee the collection of wood through her minions if we beseech her aid.
'Go there now, maggot, and speak with her. Bid her draw the spiders from the tower to the woods surrounding this camp.
'Be quick!'
'Be swift. I will not suffer the slings and stones of those accursed little folk any longer. The time has come to decimate their ilk and wipe the world clean for our conquest.'

'So Caragdal is on the move? If you weren't such a blubbering weakling, I'd say you were beginning to be of some worth to us here! At least you do not fail in all that you attempt. You have impressed me... for now.
'What are you looking at? Get back to work!'
Escort Caragdal to the Grimwood Lumber Camp

'Greetings, my little rooster-friend! What is this? Your coops are threatened by wolves?
'Wolves are among the most craven of the Dark Lord's servants, and this proves them even more so. Unfortunately, the troubles here are much greater, with effects more far-reaching, than those which trouble the Shire.
'I am sorry, but I cannot leave the Eglain just yet.'

'I am the steed of Aragorn son of Arathorn, Chieftain of the Dúnedain of the North. What have I to do with chickens?

'You wish for me to protect a chicken coop? Until I was wounded, I fed my cub by stealing chickens.

'Oh, please! My dear rooster, we have much more important things to do, such as napping. Besides, we must keep our mistress's house clear of mice and rats. We haven't time to run all the way to the Shire!'

'Who art thou, rooster? I am a noble steed of Rohan. Thy troubles are beneath my hooves.
'Even were I of a mind to lend thee aid, I have not long been in this place and know not of this land called the Shire. Begone, bird, for I have naught to do with thee.'

'Wolves? Ha! We fear no wolves! They will not withstand our onslaught. They will be the next to fall!
'After we destroy the helpless red squirrels, we shall conquer the wolves, and then the world! No one can stop us!'

'Oh dear! I found such lovely grass here, but I can't seem to find my way back off the roof of this hobbit-hole. Do you see a path?
'My dear rooster, how can I help you when I am stuck here? If I could find a way down, I might speak with my bull...wolves are too vicious for me.'

'I am trapped in a cage out in the middle of the Midgewater Marshes, and you want me to help you? I think you have it backwards, rooster. I am the one in need of help.
'This Man here is more than a bit mad! If he throws any more of those dreadful dead midges in this cage, I think my carapace is going to split!'

'I have heard rumour that a hidden camp exists near unto the very gates of Carn Dûm in the far north where brave heroes gather to contest the power of Angmar itself.
'I cannot say precisely where Gath Forthnír -- as it is called -- lies, but should you find this place, speak with one called Annábla, and she will tell you more of their purpose.'

'You have been sent by Arohir, yes? It speaks highly to his confidence in you that he would tell you of our existence at all - and so I have high hopes that you may indeed be able to help us in our desperate cause.'
The Council of the North
Arohir of Esteldín has bade you seek the hidden camp of Gath Forthnír in the far north, somewhere east of the gates of Carn Dûm, and once there to speak with Annábla.
'You should speak with Annábla at Gath Forthnír in Angmar, ${PLAYER}.'
Speak with Annábla of Gath Forthnír.

'Have you heard of the Wardens of Annúminas? They are a branch of our order who guard the ancient tombs and ruins which mark the long-ago abandoned capital of Arnor.
'News has come to me that they stand hard-pressed, as bandits and refugees from the North Downs have begun to loot the old tombs in increasing numbers, and darker rumours of the presence of Angmarim agents who seek entrance into the ancient city itself.
'Travel to the camp of Tinnudir and you will find Cannuion, who will be most grateful for any aid you can render.'

'You have been sent by Arohir? Good, we have great need of trustworthy warriors to help us against the growing threat of robbers and the like that have grown up in recent months here - for we are few, and it threatens to overwhelm us.'
The Wardens of Annúminas
Arohir of Esteldín has bade you seek the camp of Tinnudir along the eastern shore of Lake Evendim, and once there to speak with Cannuion.
'Speak with Cannuion at Tinnudír on the banks of Lake Evendim, ${PLAYER}.'

Cannuion is at the Ranger-camp at Tinnudir, in Evendim, to the west of the North Downs.
Arohir has sent you to speak with Cannuion in Evendim.

'Have you yet been to the encampment of our brothers in the North Downs? Once fair Esteldín still serves us honourably even now as a base for our Rangers to train and prepare as the forces of Angmar pour down from the northern wastes.
'Not that we don't need your help here, but you may wish to speak with Nethúr in Esteldín -- I've heard that matters there have become quite dire as the Orcs encamp in ever greater numbers and threaten to overwhelm our people.'

'Calenglad sent you? Hah, and here I thought they might need your help even more than we - but it is true that matters here are not to my liking, for the Orcs outnumber our forces greatly, and it is only a matter of time before the last bastions of the North come under attack.'
The Rangers of Esteldín
Calenglad of Tinnudir has bidden you speak with Nethúr of Esteldín in the North Downs concerning the Rangers of Esteldín and the Orkish forces pouring down from Angmar.
'Nethúr at Esteldín will wish to speak with you, ${PLAYER}.'

Nethúr is at Esteldín, far to the east of Evendim.
Calenglad sent you to speak with Nethúr.

'Greetings, ${PLAYER}, have you travelled to fair Rivendell? I have had business there on occasion in the past, but lately a friend of mine by the name of Imyl sent warning to me that I should no longer travel through the Trollshaws, for fear that I should fall victim to bands of roving hill-men who have come down from the north in the last year or so.
'I count myself a friend of the fair Elves of Rivendell, and if matters have come to this, I fear that they may be in some peril. Should you find your way to Rivendell, seek out Imyl of the Last Homely House, and aid her, if you may. I would be most grateful.'

'Broderic sent you here? To aid us?
'What a dear, foolish man he is. I doubt there is much that you can do to aid us, for our borders are tested by the shadow at every turn. However, if you are determined to lend us aid, then I will gratefully accept your help.'
The Elves of Rivendell
Broderic Willowmeade, a man of Bree-town has bade you seek out Imyl in the Last Homely House of Rivendell, and offer aid to her if you may.
'You should speak with Imyl at the Elf-haven of Rivendell.'
Speak with Imyl of Rivendell.

'Hello there, I was wondering if you might be able to spare a moment. My Uncle Bilbo and I share a birthday, September the Twenty-second, and I have celebrated it by holding a small gathering in his honour every year since he left Bag End. Even though the day has passed, I thought it would be nice to get the old rascal something for our birthday anyway.
'It is a small gift, but I was hoping that you could bring it to him. He wouldn't take a present from me now -- he would say, \qIt isn't right, Frodo my lad, what with it being past our birthday and all,\q but perhaps he wouldn't turn down the gift if it was delivered by someone else.
'Would you do this for me?'

'Ah, he did enjoy the gift, splendid! And here I go, having you carry off presents for others without thought of yourself. A wonderful ${RACE} if I ever knew one!
'I believe I have something here for you. It isn't much, just a trinket. A small toy really. Why, I remember the day I was giving these out at my eleventy-first birthday not seventeen years ago...but I am going on with old tales again.
'Thank you for your help, ${PLAYER}.'

'What is this now? A present from Frodo for our Birthday? Well, isn't that curious, for I was planning on giving young Frodo a present of my own! It has been a tradition of mine ever since I arrived here in Rivendell to give out presents on my birthday to the Elves. They don't much understand the custom, but they always accept the gifts graciously. Wonderful folk, the Elves.
'I always set aside a present for Frodo and have in fact been carrying it around for a few days now! I would more than likely forgotten about it had you not reminded me.
'Take my present to him, if you would; he is often troubled, and it may brighten his mood.'
'Hmm, yes? Can I help you with something?'

'Bilbo accepted the present after all? Well, that did go better than I expected!
'And what's this? A present for me, from Bilbo? He is always full of surprises.
'Go back and tell him thank you very much, and that I will come to visit him later.'
'Did you deliver the present to Bilbo?'
Deliver the present to Bilbo Baggins
Deliver the present to Frodo in Rivendell
Belated Birthday

Frodo Baggins and his cousin Bilbo -- though he calls him Uncle -- share the same birthday, but have been unable to celebrate together for seventeen years.
<rgb=#FF0000> NOTE: This quest will be removed from your quest log when the current festival ends. </rgb>
'I certainly hope Frodo enjoys my gift.'
'Have you found my dear cousin yet, ${PLAYER}? It is important that you do so before our birthday is over.'
'Let Uncle Bilbo know that I appreciate his gift.'

Bilbo Baggins is in the Hall of Fire in the Last Homely House at Rivendell.
Frodo Baggins has asked that you deliver a belated birthday present to Bilbo.

Frodo Baggins is in Bilbo's room on the ground floor of the Last Homely House, in Rivendell.
Bilbo Baggins has asked that you bring Frodo a birthday present in return.

Bilbo Baggins is in the Hall of Fire in the Last Homely House, in Rivendell.
Frodo Baggins has asked you to thank Bilbo for his gift.

'We cannot grieve now for Laerdan, ${PLAYER}. Amarthiel will not hesitate to make use of her newly-found knowledge. If only we had been able to seize the palantír in time, her search for Narchuil might have remained fruitless! Nay, there is little use in dwelling on the past. Take comfort in this, ${PLAYER}: we know what Amarthiel saw within the depths of the seeing-stone, for she spoke of it when you and Laerdan entered Barad Tironn! Did she not speak of the wilderness of the Trollshaws? She has revealed to us her next movement, and if we act with haste, we may yet find Narchuil before she does.
'We have not the numbers to prevent her servants from leaving Evendim, but we can at least be alerted of their movements. Two of my brethren watch the roads out of Evendim, and they must be told what to expect: that Amarthiel may be planning to send her servants by various roads out of Evendim. Seek Torogethir at the Evendim Gate, north-east of here at the pass to the Fields of Fornost, and Galthoniel on a small rise overlooking the Barandalf, far to the south of here and east of the halfling-village of Dwaling. Tell them what we suspect of Amarthiel's plans, and that they are to send ravens to Tinnudir at the first sign of the Angmarim's movements.
'They are not to engage any such patrols in open battle! Go with haste, ${PLAYER}! When our strength in arms is found lacking, information must be our greatest ally.'

'Thank you for the news, ${PLAYER}, though it is worrisome. I think it unlikely that Amarthiel would choose to send her warriors to the Trollshaws by the road I watch, but I will send a raven to Calenglad at once if it does come to pass.
'But I must disagree with Calenglad's wishes on one matter: if Amarthiel does choose to send her Angmarim south along this road, I will not stand idly by. Though I fall in battle with the Enemy, I will keep at least some Angmarim from passing into the Shire. Nay, do not seek to change my mind! I will not be swayed in this.
'I will send my raven first, of course.'

'You have my thanks, ${PLAYER}. I wish we could prevent the Angmarim from leaving Evendim in search of Narchuil, but I know that we do not have the strength of arms to succeed in this. At least we will know when the patrols have set out.
'I should have expected Galthoniel to refuse my wish that she not engage the Enemy in battle, but I would not have her throw her life away lightly! My heart tells me that if Amarthiel chooses the long road to the Trollshaws and passes through the Barandalf, Galthoniel's sacrifice will do naught to forestall the inevitable.
'Now that we will have warning when the Angmarim begin their search, we must begin our own, ${PLAYER}. If we are to find Narchuil, we must learn everything there is to know about it. The time has come to confront Mordrambor.'
'I will take your news to heart, ${PLAYER}, and send a raven to Calenglad at the first sign of Angmarim leaving Evendim. I have seen naught yet, however. It has been unusually quiet.'
Book 11, Chapter 1: Watching the Roads
Laerdan has been lost within the once-proud halls of Barad Tironn, and now the Dúnedain must prevent Amarthiel from acting on the knowledge she gained by her use of the palantír.

'I will not be swayed in this matter, ${PLAYER}, and Calenglad was fool-hardy to ask it of me! I will send a raven to Tinnudir at the first sign of Angmarim, but I will not stand by and allow them free passage southward.'

'We may not have the numbers to keep the Angmarim from leaving Evendim and travelling to the Trollshaws in search of Narchuil, but I want to know the moment that they do. Torogethir and Galthoniel, the Rangers charged with guarding the roads out of Evendim, must be told what to expect.
'Torogethir is north-east of here, just west of the Evendim Gate to the Fields of Fornost. Galthoniel has a small camp-site on a small rise that overlooks the Barandalf, south-east of Tinnudir. Look for her east of the halfling-village of Dwaling.
'Tell them not to engage the enemy, but to send ravens to Tinnudir at the first sign of Angmarim passing out of Evendim.'
'I have seen no sign of Angmarim leaving Evendim. When I do, I will send a raven to Tinnudir at once.'

Torogethir is at a small camp just west of the Evendim Gate to the Fields of Fornost, north-east of Tinnudir. Galthoniel has a camp on a small rise overlooking the Barandalf, south-east of Tinnudir and east of the Shire-village of Dwaling.
Calenglad has asked you to bring news of possible movements of the Angmarim out of Evendim to Torogethir and Galthoniel, the Rangers tasked with guarding the roads.

Calenglad is at the Ranger-camp on the island of Tinnudir, in Evendim.
You have told what Calenglad has guessed of Amarthiel's plans to the Rangers Torogethir and Galthoniel, and they will remain vigilant for any sign of Angmarim moving out of Evendim.

'Mordrambor has proven an unreliable and dangerous prisoner for us thus far, ${PLAYER}, but now he will recompense for his betrayal. He will tell us what he knows of Amarthiel's lost ring, Narchuil, or he will never again see the light of day. He cannot know its location, or his mistress would have had no need for the palantír, but anything he can tell us of its power or history may be of use.
'I will go with you to speak with the Black Númenórean. He has proven able to ensorcel the minds of others, and we will have better fortune if we confront him together and steel ourselves against his trickery.
'I have some words for our prisoner concerning the fate of Laerdan, as well. Mordrambor will rue the day he sent the Elf to his death. Speak with me when you are ready to go.'

'There are no words, ${PLAYER}, for the evil Mordrambor has done this day. I thought we had seen the last of the grief he could cause, but the treachery that sent Laerdan willingly to his doom is as naught compared to the sorrow I feel for the loss of my kindred.
'Colhamnir... Carchammadel... Tadan....
'Too many lives lost, and in the very heart of the place we held safest! How could Angmar strike us even here? We cannot search for Narchuil now, ${PLAYER}. Mordrambor has dealt a fatal strike against my kindred, and we must rest. My people need time to grieve -- they cannot fight on forever in the face of such losses! I am sorry.'
Talk to Calenglad and confront Mordrambor about Narchuil
Book 11, Chapter 2: Mordrambor
Calenglad has decided that before you begin your search for Narchuil, you must learn what you can about the ring from Mordrambor.

'Are you prepared? Mordrambor has proven himself an ill house-guest, but he may know something of Narchuil which we can put to use. He has not yet seen the wrath of the Dúnedain, and I would speak to him of Laerdan's fate. He will tell us what he knows, but you must steel yourself against his sorceries!'
<rgb=#FF0000>This is a Solo quest, and cannot be completed with a Fellowship.</rgb>

Calenglad is at the Ranger-camp on the island of Tinnudir, in Evendim.
Calenglad has decided that you and he may learn of Narchuil's power or history by confronting Mordrambor together, and such knowledge may aid you to recover it before Amarthiel does.

Calenglad is at the Ranger-camp on the island of Tinnudir, in Evendim.
Mordrambor has escaped from the keep on Tinnudir. Many Rangers were slain during his passage, and Calenglad now seeks to hold together the Dúnedain in the face of these losses.
Collected Annúminas city-stones (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'My people need time to mourn, ${PLAYER}, or they will be unable to continue the fight. The greatest weapon Angmar wields in this war is hopelessness, an overpowering dread that seizes the hearts of good folk and saps their will to stand against evil. It has been brought to bear here on Tinnudir with terrible success.
'I have set my brethren to gathering stones from Annúminas with which we may construct cairns for our fallen kindred. If you would travel to the great city and help with the collection of these city-stones, I know that Tadan, Colhamnir, and Carchammadel would have been honoured by your service in their memory.'

'These will do nicely, ${PLAYER}, and I thank you for the gesture.
'There is still no word from Torogethir or Galthoniel. It seems that Amarthiel too has been delayed in the beginning of her search, or she busies herself with celebrating the escape of Mordrambor and the deaths of my people. We will have our vengeance upon them both, but the time of its coming arrives too slowly!'
'You have not collected enough stones yet, ${PLAYER}.'
Collect Annúminas city-stones (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring Annúminas city-stones to Calenglad
Book 11, Chapter 3: Cairns for the Fallen
Calenglad fears for the resolve of the Dúnedain and has set them to gathering stones with which to build cairns for their fallen brethren.

'Stones from Annúminas, far to the south-west, on the shores of Lake Nenuial, will be used to construct cairns in the memory of our fallen kindred. It would have filled them with honour to be buried beneath the stones of the City of the Kings.'

Stones from the buildings of Annúminas can be found all throughout the great city and would be ideal for constructing cairns in memory of the fallen Rangers.
Calenglad has asked you to collect stones from throughout the streets of the City of the Kings with which to make cairns for Tadan, Colhamnir, and Carchammadel.

Calenglad is at the Ranger-camp on the island of Tinnudir, in Evendim.
You have collected stones from Annúminas to use in the building of cairns for the Rangers slain during the escape of Mordrambor and should return now to Calenglad.

'It is time, ${PLAYER}. There is a place not far from here of which Carchammadel was particularly fond in life -- Barad Rath, an overlook crowned in ruins high above Lake Nenuial. That the tomb-robbers had made frequent use of it was a sorrow to her. We have decided to build the cairns for our fallen kindred at its crest.
'Will you join us in remembering our fallen and add a stone to their cairns? Speak with me when you are ready, and we will depart.'

'I thank you again, ${PLAYER}. You did not know Tadan for long, but he was a good man, and I know he appreciated your visits, despite the dangerous tenor of the duty in which you found him. I do not blame him for what happened, and I ask that you do not, as well -- Mordrambor has ensnared folk greater than you or I.
'I feel that my people will be able to fight once again, and with renewed determination. We will not forget what Mordrambor and Amarthiel have done, but neither shall we wallow in our grief! Our vengeance, when it comes, shall be magnified ten-fold by our losses, and they will regret their misdeeds!'
'Yes, ${PLAYER}? What is it?'
Talk to Calenglad and travel with him to Barad Rath
Talk to Calenglad
Book 11, Chapter 4: Remembrance
The Dúnedain of Tinnudir have gathered to construct cairns over the bodies of their fallen brethren, and Calenglad has asked that you participate as well.

'We will travel now to Barad Rath to remember the fallen, if you are ready.'
<rgb=#FF0000>This is a Solo quest, and cannot be completed with a Fellowship.</rgb>

Calenglad is at the Ranger-camp on the island of Tinnudir, in Evendim.
You have been invited to join the Dúnedain in remembering their kin slain by Mordrambor during his escape.

Calenglad is at the Ranger-camp on the island of Tinnudir, in Evendim.
The remembrance of the fallen Dúnedain was interrupted by the appearance of a raven sent by Torogethir: Amarthiel's troops have begun their search for Narchuil.
Fleet-wing brings a dreaded, but expected, message: Amarthiel's troops have begun passing through the Evendim Gate in search of Narchuil.
'The air is chill, and my heart is heavy with sorrow. All battles bring grief in their train, but beyond the veil of sadness lies the hope of victory.'

'I had hoped we would learn something of Narchuil that might aid us in finding it before the Angmarim, but that hope, like so many others, has been dashed. We have been delayed by Mordrambor and must now follow Amarthiel's forces eastward, where I had hoped to stay before them.
'No matter. There are many tall hills between here and the wilderness of the Trollshaws, and if we must follow, we will do so knowing what to expect. You should leave Evendim heading east and pass through the Fields of Fornost. A short distance north-east of Trestlebridge stands the great hill of Amon Raith. Stand at its peak and <rgb=#FF0000>look</rgb> eastward. If you see the Angmarim ahead of you, continue to Amon Sul, which is called Weathertop by many, in the Lone-lands, and do the same: <rgb=#FF0000>look</rgb> eastward from its summit.
'I am worried that the Angmarim may attack villages along the way. By scouting their position from the heights, you will be able to learn of their progress and follow them wherever they are headed.'

'You bring warning from my sister that the Angmarim have come to Tâl Bruinen? Her warning is welcome, but my scouts have already encountered the Enemy.
'Do you know why they have come to this place? Can you tell me what brings them to these woods, so far from their evil homeland?'

'You are seeking the Angmarim that passed this way not long ago? I saw them coming from a great distance and managed to hide myself before they arrived. I feared I would be found, for at the head of their number marched a man of great evil; a Black Númenórean, if I do not miss my guess. It seemed to me that he stared right at my hiding-place, but at just that moment he was interrupted by some thought that caused him to turn and gaze off into the distance to the west; I know not what it was, but he shortly resumed his march, and the company passed into the east.
'Your face tells me that you have had dealings with this man, and the memory is full of sorrow. From what I overheard, it seemed their course lay to the south, among the cheerless lands of Tâl Bruinen. My sister Candelleth has a camp in Tâl Bruinen. To reach it, follow the road east of here until you are nearly within sight of the Bruinen, and you will come to a dirt path that winds southward with the Bruinen on your left and a tall rock-face on your right. Stay on the path, even as it crosses streams and winds through the underbrush, and you will surely come across one of Candelleth's scouts, who can guide you to her camp.
'Tell Candelleth of the Angmarim that have come to the lands of her watch. Tell her, as well, to be wary. I fear to think what errand could have brought this Black Númenórean so near to Imladris.'

'Certain places within the woods and crags of Tâl Bruinen have an unsavoury air. The few travellers that pass by them oft report an unsettled feeling, a troubling disquiet. This in itself is not unusual, for the land remembers many things that we have forgotten and makes such memories known to us, though we recognize them not. But to learn that such a relic of evil as the ring by which the Champion of Angmar knew her greatest strength could lie hidden within these woods -- it could explain much.
'Look to the south-east! Do you see the stone-work within that narrow pass through the rocks? That place is called Delossad, and it is a ruin of which I know little. Of Elven-make it is, but the air is heavy all about it. Look for Muildir by the narrow pass to Delossad, and he will tell you if he has seen anything of note.
'The other site I have in mind is Eryn Singor, a den of the wood-trolls in north-west Tâl Bruinen. The creatures grow from saplings in that wooded and watery grove, and it is therefore rarely troubled by outsiders. Might Narchuil lie within the reedy beds or buried in the mud of Eryn Singor or the depths of Bar-e-Therchir beneath it? One of my scouts, Lavanthir, has studied the ways of the wood-trolls. Look for him outside the entrance to Eryn Singor.
'When Muildir and Lavanthir have given you what aid they can, return to me with Narchuil or with any information about its location which you have learned, and we can decide our next course.'

'Do not give up, ${PLAYER}. I had thought Narchuil might have been the cause of the troubling disquiet that hangs over Eryn Singor and Delossad, but it was only a guess. It seems that Rivendell is getting nervous about the rumours they've been hearing about Goblin-town falling under the sway of Angmar or some-such, so they sent me and my lanky friend here to take a look around and see what's what.
'Can't say that we know for sure whether Angmar is involved, but we did find a large goblin-encampment on the surface just a short ways north-east of here. Normally the goblins prefer to stay down in their caves away from the sun, so that's a tell-tale sign that something is wrong.
'We've been making little forays now and again against the goblins, but for now we've got to keep an eye on this pass -- make sure they don't start heading west to join with the smaller tribes scattered about the Misties. Perhaps you would care to take a try at them in the meanwhile? There are plenty to go around, and it would give you a chance to determine their strength. I would also say the exercise will do you some good -- you are looking a bit winded from the heights here.'

'I've got a plan in mind, and those fire-pots the goblins wield are at the heart of it. They are making them in large numbers in there, and while goblins may be industrious, they are also careless. You should be able to steal a number of those fire-pots, and with a bit of work, we ought to be able to use their own weapons against them.
'The thought of that entire camp in flames brings me a certain childish delight, so let's get to work!'

'Ha! Good work, ${PLAYER}. Now let us see those. There is not much a goblin can come up with that a dwarf can't sort out in short order.
'What's this...?'

'No luck with the fire-pots yet?
'From what you have described of the camp, it sounds like they keep most of the finished pots in the smaller camps up in the slopes and ravines above the main camp.'
Collect goblin fire-pots (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring the goblin fire-pots to Eywind near the entrance to the High Pass
The goblins of Goblin-town have been producing large numbers of their fire-pots in preparation for war.
'Bring me some of those goblin fire-pots, ${PLAYER}!'
Eywind believes that the goblins' fire-pots can be used against them to burn down their camps. He has sent you into their camp to steal a number of them for him to examine.

The goblin-encampments are north-east of Eywind's camp, near the gates of Goblin-town.
Eywind asked you to steal fire-pots from the encampments on the slopes and ridges near the gates of Goblin-town and bring them to him.

'It would seem that there are indeed some limits to the ingenuity of dwarves, Master Eywind. Fortunately, I happen to know a Wizard who is far wiser than either of us -- particularly when it comes to matters of fire.
'I remember many years ago when Mithrandir would come to Rivendell to celebrate momentous events with us, and often his fireworks would be central to the evening festivities. It so happens that in discussing the nature of his fireworks, he mentioned a draught which he uses to enhance the virtue of his displays.
'It occurs to me now that if we happened to have a bit of this draught on hand, we might make excellent use of it when it comes time to deal with these goblins and their fire-pots once and for all.'

'What is this? An Elf named Nogmeldir sent you for what? Ah, now I recall him. Bright fellow, though a bit impetuous. He wants my fire-draught does he? Whatever for?
'Goblin fire-pots? An entire camp of them? I think I see what the fellow is about. I do happen to have a vial left... where was that? Ah, here it is!
'Now, be careful with that! No more than a few drops mind you, and keep it away from the lamp oil, or you will soon find yourself lacking your eyebrows... if you are fortunate.'

'Were you successful? Yes, that is the draught Mithrandir mentioned. It does not look like much, does it?
'I will speak with Eywind on how we might best employ this, and then we shall see....'
'You have not had an opportunity to travel to Rivendell yet?'
Talk to Gandalf in Rivendell
Bring Gandalf's draught to Nogmeldir
Gandalf's Secret Recipe
Nogmeldir recalled a special draught which Gandalf the Grey mentioned using in his fireworks to enhance their power.
'Speak with Gandalf, ${PLAYER}. He may have a suggestion.'
'Take the phial to Nogmeldir, ${PLAYER}.'

Gandalf is in Bilbo's room on the ground floor of the Last Homely House, in Rivendell.

'By Durin's Beard, this will be a fine day indeed! This draught of Gandalf's is precisely what we need to make a shambles of the goblin's fire-pot camps.
'I went down to take a quick peek at the encampment while you were off to Rivendell, and I found what we're after. That big thing on the lower slope, with the scaffold and the huge burning cauldron on it? That is the heart of their production, and that is where we will strike.
'They've got stored materials for their fire-pots all over the camp -- all we have to do is slip Gandalf's draught into that cauldron and give it a tip, and the mixture should do the rest of our work for us... you mark my words!'

'Haha, well done! 'Tis a fine thing indeed to watch an enemy's schemes blow up in their own faces, is it not ${PLAYER}?
'Would that we could blow the entirety of Goblin-town sky high as well, but I fear that it'll not be nearly as neat a conclusion when at last that dark warren falls....'
'No luck yet with Gandalf's little potion eh? Time's a wasting - lets get to the good part!'

'It will take some time to repair the keys, and if you would be willing, you might be able to help me with a small matter.
'I gifted a number of fine gems to a traveller who possessed an interest in learning the finer points of jewelsmithy, but he was beset by goblins. Though he escaped with his life, many of the gems were stolen by the creatures. Journey to Goblin-town, which lies within the High Pass, and return to me with a handful of these coveted gems. By that time, I shall likely have finished restoring the keys you have brought to me, and I will be able to return the stolen gems to my unfortunate friend, as well.
'You will not find these gemstones in possession of goblins on the surface, for the creatures that seized these gems likely brought them into Goblin-town, the better to protect them.'

'I thank you for this service, ${PLAYER}, for Goblin-town is a vile place and not easily traversed. My friend will be surprised and pleased that you have recovered the gems he thought lost, and he is sure to learn much of jewelsmithy by studying them.'
'Where are the gems for which I asked?'

'Goblins within Goblin-town, in the Misty Mountains, will have the coveted gems I seek. Return to me with a handful of these gems, and I will give you the keys I am able to repair. In this way, my friend will have the gems again, though I do not have the time to recover them myself.'

'Hearken, ${PLAYER} -- many of the Angmarim that came to Tâl Bruinen are searching elsewhere, but some of them have returned to search the ruins.
'Defeat those that you find here and return to me before you search inside. I do not want them to see you opening the door.'

'${PLAYER}, are you all right? The Black Númenórean appeared outside Delossad, and I only had a moment in which to hide myself. Were it any other opponent, I would have engaged him in battle, but I could not hope to defeat him without others of my kindred. He came to the door and passed inside, and I followed behind him in secret, hoping beyond hope that I might oppose him in the final need.
'I shudder to think what he might have done had he known I was there!
'Let us leave this place, friend. You can tell me what you have learned as we travel out of the shadows of this sad ruin!'

'Very good, ${PLAYER}. Your exploration of the ruins should now be uninterrupted. A word, though, before you try the door again, my friend: Delossad is an ancient place, and some memory of great evil hangs over its stones. I fear that something terrible came from there and would ask you to keep a clear head while you are inside.
'Examine anything that seems unusual, for I believe that the memory of whatever sorrow hangs about that place will make itself known to you. Learn what you can, but remain wary -- creatures of the dark are drawn to such places, and you may need to defend yourself from them.
'I will stay on guard out here, watching to ensure that no enemies enter Delossad while you are within.'
'Let us leave this place. Memory hangs on its stones like a shroud and fills me with unease.'

'You say that Amarthiel's forces have recovered Narchuil? This is terrible news, ${PLAYER}, and undermines all that we have here sought to accomplish!
'Lord Elrond must be told. Seek for him in the library of Imladris and give him these grim tidings, as well as the diary of Sara Oakheart. He will know what can be done, if anyone will.'

'Your tale fills me with sorrow, ${PLAYER}. The fall of Narmeleth is a sad tale known by few, and then only in part. Of her imprisonment by Laerdan, following the battle of Fornost, I knew nothing. It grieves me that Laerdan believed I would not suffer Narmeleth to live -- the slaying of a captive is not the way of the Eldar, and she would have been safe in my house, though she remain Amarthiel.
'I believe we can guess at the sad fate of Sara Oakheart, last in a long line of Narmeleth's keepers. I do not doubt she treated the daughter of Laerdan kindly, but her payment was doom, and more than that: Amarthiel learned the dark arts from a cruel master, and it seems she took the visage of her jailor for her own. An unhappy fate!
'I am certain of one more thing, ${PLAYER}: Angmar has not yet recovered Narchuil. The ways of the Enemy are the ways of deceit -- do not give in to despair! If Narchuil had been found, Amarthiel would have recalled her minions, and she has not done so. She may have learned some new information concerning its whereabouts, but her servants have yet to find it, of this I am sure. We must remain vigilant against them, as always, and continue our search.'
'No Blah!'
Bring rotted diary to Elrond

Deep within Delossad, Mordrambor gave you the terrible news that Narchuil has been found. Lord Elrond must be told.
'Speak with Lord Elrond in the library of Imladris and tell him what you have seen. Give him, as well, the diary of Sara Oakheart. I hope that he will know what to do, ${PLAYER}, for I do not.'

'Listen to this, ${PLAYER}:
\qL fears the worst. I will carry out his wishes by breaking the keys to Sithad -- the stones of Tâl Bruinen are heavy and will serve -- and hiding them.\q
'I do not know where Sithad may be, but it sounds as if Laerdan was keeping this \qN,\q Narchuil, within its walls, and at some point Sara broke the keys to this place and hid them. And look at this, further in:
\q...must stand at the stairs of Sithad, looking up towards the entrance. Turn to the left and walk forward to the wall, and then turn right and follow the curve until you see four pillars through two pillars. Walk between the two and look to the right of the four. I will leave the keys always in the shade.\q
'I wonder now if Sithad is not an antiquated name for a place we already know, ${PLAYER}? Language changes over time, and Laerdan has lived for many years; the name by which he knows one place may not be that which it is called by others. As I say the names aloud, it comes to me that Sithad bears something of a resemblance to Delossad, does it not?
'I think we have deciphered the first part of the riddle, friend ${RACE}! Go to Delossad and use the journal to locate the hidden keys of which Sara has written. I am sure it is the place!'

'I am greatly heartened by your success and by my reading of the clues! I am sure that Narchuil is within Delossad, ${PLAYER}, and one of the keys within this box will open the way for us!
'A jeweller of great repute lives in Imladris. Her name is Merilos, and she will be able to remake these keys for us. Be warned: she is stern and slow to befriend, and while she will certainly help us, she will likely ask for some service in return. She does not gift her work freely, for it is of great value and precious.
'Look for Merilos in Imladris, at the Spire of Meeting. Bring her this box of broken keys and ask her to mend them. I wish you good fortune in this.'
'You found nothing? I was certain this was the place!'
'I will be able to remake about half of these keys. The rest are completely beyond repair. Are you satisfied with this?'
'You do not have anything for me?'

'Among other tasks, Eywind and I have come up into these forsaken mountains in search of a companion of mine by the name of Glorwen. She came here some weeks ago with the same duty we have: to explore the strength and purpose of the goblins of High Pass and ensure that they do not move against Rivendell without warning.
'Unfortunately, she has always been easily distracted by the hunt, and I find it likely that she has managed to while away the past weeks entertaining herself and has quite lost track of the time.
'When last we heard from her, she was going to explore a set of giant-ruins to the east, rumoured now to be inhabited by a large pack of Wargs. If you would help us find her, you should begin your search there.'

'What is this? Glorwen's bow? Yet you say you saw no other signs of her save a torn cloak?
'Had the Wargs slain her, it is likely they would have torn her to pieces and let the evidence lie plainly about. If there was no sign of her body, then it is possible that she yet lives. Perhaps she escaped? But I think that unlikely, for she would have gone back for her bow, or come to us in need of aid.
'I have no answer to this riddle, but perhaps the Wargs might?'
'You have found no sign of Glorwen yet? Hopefully, she is simply out hunting goblins and Wargs; nevertheless, I am becoming worried...'

'It is good to meet you, ${PLAYER}. I was just telling Indor here of my latest kill: a mighty and noble white hart, the likes of which I have never before seen and will never see again! I tracked him down from the Gladdalf and into Nan Tornaeth, but he became frightened, and I lost the trail. I picked it up again amid the Bruinen Gorges and followed him south into the hills alongside this camp. The light was failing, and as he passed westward and I behind him, I loosed a number of my arrows. I know I felled him, ${PLAYER}, but I could not follow in the dark.
'He is out there, my friend: the hunter Wistan's greatest kill! If you come across the body of the white hart, collect my arrows and the carcase and bring them back to me. My hunt of the white hart will surely make for a fine tale or three about the fire, and there will be a place for you, as well!
'The hart was making westward, but even taking his last strides, he would have steered clear of the Gauredain or the wood-trolls. Look for the body to the west of Echad Candelleth and between the dwelling-places of those creatures.'

'Wéthorm is staying at Thorenhad, north of here in the Bruinen Gorges of the Trollshaws, north of the bear-dens. Pay close attention to his first bite of my toad stew, because I want to savour my revenge!'

'Very good, ${PLAYER}! These legs and mandibles are very unappealing and will be just the thing!
'Do me a favour and grind them into mush on that grinding stone, will you?'
'The grinding stone is right there, ${PLAYER}. Grind all the crawler pieces into mush, and then I can add them to the stew! We will teach Wéthorm to play tricks on us!'

'This will do nicely, ${PLAYER}. It looks terrible, and it smells worse! It is perfect!
'Now, take this toad stew and bring it to the Dwarf Wéthorm at Thorenhad. Tell him that I made some additions to the stew to make it taste even better, and I wanted to share it with him. 'Don't be ridiculous! My husband is fine -- in fact, he's inside the house right now, resting from his ordeal! You see, when those wolf-men attacked the waggon, he wasted no time at all: he broke open the crate of figurines and started throwing them at them. While they were distracted, he crept by them down the path and escaped into the woods! He got turned around, or he would have stopped at Echad Candelleth to see the Elf Tongannel again, but he was already nearly to the Last Bridge when he regained his bearings. He came home, bemoaning the loss of the figurines, and I put him right to bed to rest.
'But you have recovered the figurines he meant to sell! He'll be so pleased. I think I will forbid him from making another such journey, however -- we will sell them here in Bree, and that will be more than enough. 'You have come late to warn us, for the danger is known to us already.
'Last night, just after dark, we had snuffed out the candles, locked the door, and were just getting into bed, when I thought I heard something moving around in little Whelan's room. Whelan is just a babe, so you can understand my worry: I thought a bird might have flown into his room through the window, which we always leave open a crack so the breeze can come in, and I did not want him to be frightened. But when I went into his room to check on him, I saw that it was not a bird at all, but a monster: a terrible, creeping thing hunched over on bony legs! It was moving towards Whelan's cradle and making a terrible noise in its throat.
'Its intent was clear -- it meant to harm my child! I let forth a cry such as you have never heard and leaped towards it; I do not know what I thought to do, but the thing sprang out the window through which it had crawled, vanishing into the night.'

'My heart has been ill at ease for the last few days, ${PLAYER}, and I hope that you can put my fears to rest. A traveller from Bree by the name of Tim Strawley came to Echad Candelleth on his way south; a craftsman he was, and he bore wooden figurines of exquisite quality that he hoped to sell in far-off markets. He desired to raise enough money to support his young wife, Nora, and he was enthusiastic about his prospects.

'Have you seen them, ${PLAYER}, the worms that crawl throughout the woods and crags of Tâl Bruinen? They are born in the rocks high above the Bruinen, to the east of Echad Candelleth. Their sire is Sarlug, a most vile creature, and their dam is Sarnemil, ferocious and protective.
'I sought to end their terror once, but I was alone and could not defeat them -- I rue now the decision that made me take flight, but I thought them grievously wounded, unable to cause more harm. I was wrong. Their hatchlings have now matured, and more are brought into the world every day. Soon, Tâl Bruinen will be overrun with the creatures.
'I would be grateful if you would finish what I began. Cirith Ulunn lies directly to the east of Echad Candelleth, upon the high mountains. You will need to return to the Tâl Bruinen road and travel to the north-east, down to the Bruinen, and there cross the river to the eastern bank. You will see a long path winding up into the mountains. Follow it to its height, then turn south into Cirith Ulunn. Sarlug you will find there, but Sarnemil will likely flee. West of Cirith Ulunn, on the very edge of the cliffs, a single monument rises from the earth. Stand there on the cliff-edge, and <rgb=#FF0000>look</rgb> into the distance: you will likely see where Sarnemil has fled. Return to me when you have defeated both Sarlug and Sarnemil and have thinned the numbers of their offspring.'

'Welcome, traveller. You found this brooch in the footprint of a giant? I did indeed lose this in Tâl Bruinen, but I saw no giant footprints there. The giants do not usually travel from the mountains that far south; Tâl Bruinen has been clear of them for as long as I can remember.
'If there is a giant wandering those lands, I would like to know what it sought.
'You speak with Arifael -- a better sort of giant, if you will -- at his home upon the slopes of Amon Nendir. The hill lies to the south of the High Moor. He may know something of this giant's wanderings.'
Down from the Mountains?
You discovered a series of giant footprints in Tâl Bruinen and a brooch belonging to Ringhul, marchwarden of the High Moor.
Bring the brooch to Ringhul on the High Moor

Arifael lives on the slope of Amon Nendir, south of the High Moor on the eastern edge of the Trollshaws.
Elrohir is concerned about the giant footprints you saw in Tâl Bruinen and wants you to ask Arifael if he has heard of giants wandering that far south.
The challenge has been issued
Defeated Blackfang

'I know this is asking much of you, but if Thorgest believes that the only way we might learn something from the Wargs of Starkhath is to challenge their leader, then I can see no other way forwards.
'Glorwen's life may hang in the balance -- if she yet lives at all. For her sake as well as yours, take care and arm yourself well.'

'Your tidings chill me to the bone, ${PLAYER}. Few are those who have escaped from the dark, twisted caves of Goblin-town once they have ventured within.
'The hatred of the goblins for my kin is great, and Glorwen's torments will be long and cruel at their hands.
'We must prepare -- by stealth or force of arms -- to rescue her, for even should we lose a dozen heroes to the darts and blades of the goblins, still our suffering will be as nothing compared to hers should we leave her to their devices!'
Find the totem of challenge and defeat Blackfang
'Who dares? You are not of the pack, and yet you would challenge me? So be it....'
Thorgest told you that you may be able to learn of Glorwen's fate by confronting their pack-leader, Blackfang.
'Seek the Wargs' Totem of Challenge, ${PLAYER}... you may learn something of Glorwen's fate.'

The totem of challenge is in the centre of the ruins of Starkhath.
Nogmeldir has asked you to find the totem and call out the Warg-leader Blackfang.
Return to Nogmeldir at Vindurhal and tell him of Glorwen's capture by the goblins of Goblin-town.
Cleared brambles from road (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Cleared treacherous stones from road (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeated great glen-bucks (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'The road that passes through Tâl Bruinen is little more than a dirt path for most of its length, but it is still used by travellers who pass south heading for Hollin and must be kept in usable condition.
'I have been charged by Lord Elrond with keeping the road clear, but it is a time-consuming duty, and I am often at a loss to keep it free of hazards.
'The path runs north of Echad Candelleth and south towards Hollin and often becomes choked with brambles and treacherous stones. Furthermore, the glen-bucks often stray near to the road and threaten travellers. If you can clear the road of these hindrances, I will reward you for your time.'

'Thank you for your service, ${PLAYER}. It is of great importance to Master Elrond that the road remain clear, especially in recent days.
'I cannot speak more on this subject, but know that you receive this reward with my thanks and with those of Master Elrond as well.'
Clear brambles from road (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Clear treacherous stones from road (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeat great glen-bucks (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Bainthir
A Bumpy Road
Bainthir has been charged with keeping the road through Tâl Bruinen clear.
'It is important that the road through Tâl Bruinen remain clear.'
'You are welcome at Echad Candelleth, ${PLAYER}.'

The road runs north of Echad Candelleth and south through Tâl Bruinen.
The road that runs through Tâl Bruinen often becomes choked with brambles and treacherous stones and is threatened by glen-bucks. Bainthir has offered you a reward if you can help him with his duty of keeping the road clear.

Bainthir is at Echad Candelleth, the Elf-camp in Tâl Bruinen.
You have helped clear the road which runs through Tâl Bruinen of many hazards and should return now to Bainthir for your reward.
Defeated Stone-trolls in Tâl Bruinen (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Greetings, ${CLASS}. I've a bit of a problem. I hunt many creatures which come out at night, but alas, it has become too dangerous. Stone-trolls have begun coming down from the mountains at night and wander the paths below.
'I haven't the skill nor knowledge to deal with trolls. You look to be a sturdy adventurer, perhaps with some experience with trolls...would you mind hunting a few? Perhaps then, they'll stay in their mountain haunts.'

'The woods of Tâl Bruinen can be dangerous and frightening when the moon is hidden among the clouds, but your deeds this night have made the area more safe for unwary travellers. I thank you, friend!'
Defeat Stone-trolls in Tâl Bruinen (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Cerys
Wandering Trolls
Cerys is concerned about the Stone-trolls that wander into Tâl Bruinen during the night.

Stone-trolls sometimes wander out of the north into Tâl Bruinen by night.
The hunter Cerys has asked you to defeat the Stone-trolls that come into Tâl Bruinen at night.

Cerys is at Echad Candelleth, the Elf-camp in Tâl Bruinen.
You have defeated a number of wandering Stone-trolls and should report of your victory to Cerys.

This barrel is lying just off the road that runs through Tâl Bruinen, but most curiously, it is full of pipe-weed! It is already a rare thing to see waggons pass this way, but waggons carrying pipe-weed are even more rare.
You take a pouch of pipe-weed from the barrel and resolve to bring it to nearby Rivendell. Perhaps someone there will know what caused this barrel to come here.

'You found this pipe-weed in a barrel by the side of the road? How strange, and how lucky...my pouch is just about empty!
'I thank you for this, friend! I wouldn't worry too much about the mystery, though -- the smoking of pipe-weed must be catching on in all circles, not just those of hobbits or Wizards. And why not?
'Take this with my thanks!'
'You don't seem to have anything for me?'
Bring pipe-weed pouch to someone in Rivendell
Surprise Pipe-weed
You found a barrel full of pipe-weed just off the road that runs through Tâl Bruinen. Most unusual....

'You found a barrel of pipe-weed out in the wild? That's odd, but I say it's a pleasant sort of odd, don't you?
'I have enough already, but Frodo or one of his friends might have run out and would thank you kindly for some more. They are in my room on the ground floor at the moment, I believe.'

'A barrel of pipe-weed, just lying by the road? I know that Pippin would bring a whole barrel of the stuff with him, if he could, but I'm fairly certain he didn't on this trip!
'Just yesterday he did tell me his own supply of pipe-weed was running low, and I expect he would thank you for this pouch of it, despite the curious circumstances surrounding it.'

'You found a barrel of pipe-weed out there in the wild? You've got some fortune, and no mistake!
'Pippin has just about run out of his own supply, and he'd thank you kindly for that pouch you've got there.
'I wonder how that barrel came to be lying by the road like that?'
'A barrel of pipe-weed, just lying out there in the wilderness? That's queer, and I don't care how well-preserved the weed seems to be, I don't trust it.'

Someone in Rivendell, north of Tâl Bruinen, may know how the barrel of pipe-weed came to rest off the road in the wilderness.
You found a barrel of pipe-weed in the wilderness and have taken a pouch from it to show someone in nearby Rivendell.

This heartwood was taken from one of the Wood-trolls of Eryn Singor and shines with an inner light.
A woodworker in nearby Rivendell might be able to fashion something of great worth from such a valuable find.

'Where did you find this shining heartwood, ${PLAYER}? The Wood-trolls of Eryn Singor? It is of great quality, and from it I could fashion goods both useful and powerful!
'This is the least I can do for you, friend ${RACE}. Please take this with my thanks.'
'You have nothing for me, friend?'
Bring the shining heartwood to a woodworker in Rivendell
Valuable Heartwood
You have taken shining heartwood of unusually high quality from one of the Wood-trolls of Eryn Singor and should find someone who can make use of it.

A woodworker in Rivendell might be able to fashion something of great worth from the shining heartwood you found.
