Defeated tempest Wargs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Glorwen had been tasked with scouting the strength of the Warg-packs in the Misty Mountains, especially those who prowl through the High Pass, near upon the gates to Goblin-town. She has failed to return, so we must continue her mission.
'The ruins to the east were once inhabited by capricious giants, but it is said that they fell at odds with the goblins of Goblin-town, and most moved south and east of here, being unable to pursue the vicious goblins into their underground kingdom. Now those ruins appear to have become the lair of a large pack of Wargs, who are likely allied with the goblins.
'Test them, if you would, and see if they fight or flee -- if they fight in the face of losses, then it is likely they are held under a strong pack-leader and remain allied with the goblins.'
'So, ${PLAYER}, you have returned already? It seems the Wargs remain organized in some fashion, and likely friendly to the goblins - would that there were some way to break their foul alliance.'
Defeat tempest Wargs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Against the Pack
The Elf-scout Glorwen, friend of Nogmeldir, vanished when hunting near the giant-ruins.
'Defeat the Wargs, ${PLAYER}, and perhaps we will learn something of Glorwen's fate.'

The Wargs occupy the giant-ruins in the north-east part of the High-pass.
Nogmeldir has asked you to do battle with the Wargs to test their strength and numbers.

Nogmeldir is at Vindurhal, west of the giant-ruins.
You should return to Nogmeldir and tell him what you have learned of the tempest Wargs.
You have found the stone remains of three mighty Stone-trolls

'Many years ago, my grandparents lived in a quiet village not far from here. It was a peaceful place, and they were very happy, but one day three monstrous Stone-trolls came to the village and caused great destruction. My grandparents fled, and eventually my grandfather built this cottage here on the bank of the Bruinen. His son lived in the cottage with them, and I was later born here.
'I grew up and took a wife, and my parents left me the cottage when they passed on; Afanen and I have lived here ever since. I have always wondered whatever happened to those three trolls: Bert, Tom, and Bill they were called, and the names send shivers down my spine even today!
'I'm sure they must have come to a bad end, being trolls, but if you can find where they ended up and learn the tale of their undoing, I'd be very glad to hear it!'

'Bert, Tom, and Bill, you said? My goodness! Yes, yes, I know of them, and more than that; they invited me to dinner once! Well, I say \qinvited,\q but that's not quite true. You might say I invited myself, but hoping to pick a troll's purse is not as easy as you'd expect, and if caught in the act you might very well be cooked!
'I was there with the dwarves, you see, and when I didn't come back from my little bit of burglary, the dwarves came to see what had happened. Soon enough, the trolls had bagged them all, and a debate had begun concerning how best to cook us and eat us! Well, Gandalf turned up, as he does when most needed, and sure enough the trolls had spent so long bickering that they were quite turned to stone at sun-up! So that's what happened. I've written it all down in my book, but to have lived it is a much different experience than to read about it!
'If you want to visit old Bert, Tom, and Bill, you'll find them in the wilderness of the Trollshaws, off the road.'

'Ah, so that is what happened to those old trolls. I am glad to have heard the story, ${PLAYER}, and thank you for the news! It is good to know that old Bert, Tom, and Bill came to an unhappy end after what they did to my grandparents' village.
'You have my thanks for the tale, and I will give you this as well!'
Find someone who knows the fate of Bert, Tom, and Bill
Find Bert, Tom, and Bill
Bert, Tom, and Bill
Garbert's grandparents were driven from their village many years ago by three marauding trolls, and Garbert wants to learn what became of the villains.
'I'll not forget Bert, Tom, and Bill in all my days!'

'If you are looking for the one who defeated Bert, Tom, and Bill, three trolls who ought to have spent more time thinking and less time bickering, you have found him!
'But the tale should be told by another; look for burglar Bilbo in the Hall of Fire to tell you the tale. He knows it most intimately, and if he perhaps downplays his own part in the events, it is only to his credit.'
'The trolls probably met their end somewhere within the Trollshaws. I do not know who might know the tale of their undoing, but if you can find someone who does, I would appreciate it.'

'Garbert is always going on about the trolls that ran his grandparents out of their village. If you can find where the trolls ended up and learn the story of their undoing as well, maybe he will finally stop talking about it!'
'This Bilbo sounds like a great hero, does he not? I wonder what else he has written in his book?'
'It is good to know those trolls came to a bad end.'
'Bert, Tom, and Bill won't be troubling us, and that is a relief.'

The trolls that terrorized the village that Garbert's grandparents once lived in probably met their end somewhere within the wilderness of the Trollshaws. Garbert lives in a cottage along the banks of the river in Tâl Bruinen.
Garbert has asked you to find the location where the three trolls of which he spoke met their end and to learn the story of their undoing.

Garbert lives at his cottage in Tâl Bruinen, on the banks of the river.
You have learned what befell the trolls Bert, Tom, and Bill, and have visited the glade where they were turned to stone. You should return to Garbert with the news.

'With your discovery of Glorwen's bow, we are left with little but dire tidings in the search for her, but at least you have not come upon her gnawed bones, so we can be thankful for that.
'Unfortunately, few Wargs are inclined or even able to speak the tongues of the Free Peoples, and I am afraid my own experience with their kind can be summed up entirely on the point of a yew shaft, so I have little insight to offer. I do not know how we might learn more of her fate from them.
'Eywind's people lived up here for many years before they were driven out, and some few still linger. Perhaps he could offer more insight than I?'

'Well, while it is true that I've fought and slain many a Warg in my day, I have had little cause to speak with them beforehand.
'But if my memory serves me a-right, there is a pair of brothers who have lived up in these mountains for quite some time as hunters and trappers. If anyone might have learned something about that pack, it would be them.
'The last I heard, they were holed up in the ruins of Hrimbarg -- an old dwarf-place to the east and a bit south of here -- still pursuing their trade. If you can find them -- and they still live -- they might be able to tell you more.'

'So, this Thorgest told you of a means to pose a challenge to the leader of the Warg-pack?
'It sounds to me like a novel means of having one's self ripped limb from limb by ravening Wargs, but if there is some chance that we might be able to learn something of Glorwen's whereabouts from this Blackfang, then perhaps it is worth the risk!'

'What do you want? Something about that pack up there to the north? I used to hunt the aurochs up that way, before I moved into the worm-scale business, and I learned a fair bit about the Wargs in order to stay alive. If you want to find one that will talk, that would be Blackfang, the pack-leader. A few others might know the tongue of Men, but they won't talk to you. It will be him that speaks for the pack and strikes bargains with the goblins -- but he won't speak to you either...unless you were to call him out.
'You see, Wargs are big on strength and survival of the fittest and all that -- so while there is no way a pack would ever accept YOU as a leader, they would still look to the pack-leader to kill you if you laid down a challenge to his leadership, just to prove his strength. If he backed down or refused, he would lose face -- and for a Warg, that can be fatal.
'The custom of challenge varies from pack to pack, but in this one it's simple. There is an old goblin totem in the middle of the ruins they live in -- you just go stand next to that for a few minutes and that signals you want a fight. Blackfang will have to come out and face you sooner or later or lose face with his pack. Of course, he's the pack-leader because he IS the strongest one up there, so you take care or he will tear you apart.'
Talk to Nogmeldir
Way of the Pack
Nogmeldir seeks to learn more about the Tempest Warg-pack to the east in order to find some way to discover the whereabouts of the Elf-scout Glorwen.
'The brothers at Hrimbarg deal with these beasts on a regular basis...they may know more than I.'
'You should speak with Eywind...he may know more about the Wargs.'
'You should return to your friends at Vindurhal, ${PLAYER}. I have told you what I know.'

Eywind is at his camp with Nogmeldir, at the entrance to the High Pass.
Nogmeldir suggested you speak with Eywind concerning the Wargs and what the dwarves know of them.

The dwarf brothers are said to dwell at Hrimbarg, to the east and a bit south of Vindurhal.
Eywind suggested you find the dwarf-brothers he spoke of and ask them what they know of the Wargs of the Misty Mountains.

Nogmeldir is at Vindurhal, a little north and to the west of Hrimbarg.
You should return to Nogmeldir and tell him what you have learned of the Wargs.
Defeated Gauradan wind-master (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeated Gauradan wolf-born (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Forgive my lack of manners, but I have been in better sorts. You try playing host to a sorry lot of adventurers that barge into your quiet home up in these remote heights, while you have a Gauradan-arrow stuck in your leg....
'Ah well. I'm not much one for company, but as you can see, I have fallen on hard times, so if you are willing to lend a hand, I suppose I would be obliged. You see, I lost the hunters that ambushed me out in that blizzard, but they've been sniffing around closer and closer to my little home here, trying to figure out where I went. If they find it and tell the others... well, that will be the end for old Thorgest, I'm afraid.
'I know it's dangerous, but if you could see your way to making the lives of those hunters difficult -- and short -- it might discourage them from trying to hunt down this dwarf.'

'Thank you, ${PLAYER}. You have taken a great burden off of my mind, what with all that has happened lately. Did you happen to see my brother Thorkell while you were wandering about? No....
'Oh, that's right, he's dead isn't he?
'Sorry, I'm not in my right head... don't feel so good....'
Defeat Gauradan wind-masters (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeat Gauradan wolf-born (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Eliminating the Trail
The dwarf-trapper Thorgest was recently ambushed by Gauradan hunters who badly injured him. He is afraid that they may yet track him.
'The Gauredain are a fearsome foe... be wary.'

The Gauradan hunters can be found throughout the southern reaches of High-pass.
Thorgest has asked you to throw the Gauradan hunters off his trail by defeating several of them before they find his dwelling.
You should return to Thorgest at Hrimbarg in central High-pass and tell him that the Gauradan hunters have been defeated.
Searched Gauradan-baskets (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'It... it seems the wolf-men have gotten the best of me after all....
'My body feels cold as stone, and this roaring fire is no help at all. Their spirit-callers have laid a curse on me, or that arrow was dabbed in some kind of poison, I know not which.
'I've no healing lore beyond the setting of bones and the binding of cuts, nor are my wits about me. I hope that if it is poison or curse, you might find something among the Gauradan camps that can cure it -- please, I beg you to go see what you can find, though I can offer little advice as to what might help.'

'What are these? I... I do not know what to make of them.
'I have no lore to aid me. If you have not found some way to cure me among their belongings, then my last hope is gone.
'Forgive me, I have no strength left.... I must sleep now and trust to fate that I will awaken again. Would that my brother were still here to watch over me....'
Search Gauradan-baskets (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Chilled to the Bone
Thorgest appears to have fallen terribly ill from the Gauredain's poisoned weapons.
'Have you found anything that might suggest a cure for me yet?'

The Gauradan-camps lie to the south of Thorgest's dwelling.
Thorgest has asked you to search through the camps of the Gauredain in the hopes of finding some cure for the affliction they have placed upon him.

Thorgest's dwelling is to the north of the Gauradan camps.
You should bring the Gauradan-relics you have collected to Thorgest to see if he can discover a cure among them.
Found the Ice-fang antidote

'I beseech you, ${PLAYER}! I do not think Master Thorgest has much longer to live, unless we can find some way to cure his illness. With his brother gone, I do not wish to bear sole witness to the end of his line in this harsh and lonely wilderness.
'Before he fell to this delerium, Thorgest spoke to me of the wolf-men who felled him. It seems that there is some defiler among them that was likely the culprit of his downfall... and perhaps the only one who would know its cure.
'If you can find this spirit-caller, perhaps he carries the cure to this terrible malady on his person. Whatever you do, please hurry!'

'What is that you have there? The Gauradan spirit-caller carried it? It looks awful... but time has run out for poor Master Thorgest.
'Whatever that is, it cannot do any further harm, and if there is any chance it might save him, we must take it! Please, see to him immediately!'
'What? What is this? Are you trying to poison me further? It is horrible! Let me die rather than drink another drop of it! No! Let me be...!'
Thorgest moans almost inaudibly, and you have found nothing to ease his suffering.
Discover if Jakka of the Gauredain carries an antidote
Bring the Ice-fang antidote to Afwald
Apply the Ice-fang antidote to Thorgest
Thorgest's Last Hope
Thorgest has been poisoned by the Gauredain, and Afwald, Thorgest's assistant, believes the chief spirit-caller of the Gauredain may hold the key to curing him.
'Have you defeated Jakka yet? He may have the cure for Thorgest.'
'Hurry! There is little time...give Thorgest the antidote!'

The Gauradan-camps lie to the south of Thorgest's dwelling.
Afwald has asked you to try and find the chief spirit-caller of the Gauredain in the last desperate hope that he may hold the cure to the poison that is slowly killing Thorgest.

Afwald is at Thorgest's dwelling, north of the Gauradan-camps.
You should bring the Ice-fang antidote to Afwald before Thorgest succumbs to the poison.

Thorgest is at his dwelling, with Afwald.
Afwald has told you that Thorgest is fading quickly and that you must administer the antidote to the dying dwarf before it is too late.

'Greetings, ${PLAYER}. You have come at a most fortuitous time. Have you spoken to Lord Glorfindel? He seems troubled recently, but will not speak of it.
'You have become familiar with him, have you not? Perhaps he will reveal his concerns to you. If you are willing, go to him near the Bruinen and speak with him.'
'Glorfindel sent you? Indeed, the Shadow of Angmar reaches even here to the Rift of Nûrz Ghâshu. It is well that you have come, for we will need aid in turning back the Shadow.'

'So you have spoken with Faimir? Her concern is kind, but there is nothing she can do.
'A friend of mine, Iorelen, journeyed into Angmar to the Rift, a place the servants of the Enemy call Nûrz Ghâshu. It is said that a great evil dwells there beneath the Mountains of Angmar, and he went to seek news of it. Glathlírel, another ally of mine, had gone there long ago and did not return, though it is said among the Wise that the evil there was contained.
'Perhaps you may be of help. You have ventured into Angmar, have you not? Perhaps you can make your way to Iorelen's camp far to the north east in the land of Angmar and learn of Glathlírel's fate.'
Into the Rift
Glorfindel is troubled about recent events and the recollection of a greater evil in Angmar.
'You should speak at once with Lord Glorfindel.'
'I have heard rumour that Iorelen lives still and may be found far to the north and east, in Angmar.
'Iorelen was once a member of my company. Will you find him and speak with him regarding the dangers at Núrz Ghâshu'
'If you are trusted by Glorfindel, I will put my trust in you as well.'

Glorfindel is near the Bruinen in Rivendell.
Faimir suggests that you speak with Glorfindel and learn what it is that troubles him.

Iorelen is at Iorelen's camp far to the north-east in Angmar.
Glorfindel requested that you seek Iorelen and learn whether he still lives.

'This great broken link was once part of the great chain which bound the Balrog Thaurlach within his prison. You wonder if you should perhaps bring it and the news of the Balrog's defeat to Master Elrond in Rivendell.'

'Greetings, ${PLAYER}! What is this you say? You found the prison of the Balrog Thaurlach?
'It is well that you defeated him. Long ago was he chained, though he should have been destroyed. It was not in wisdom that he was spared.
'But that is a long tale, full of sorrow. You should speak with Glorfindel, for this concerns him greatly. You may find him outside standing next to the Bruinen above the falls.'
'Hail and well met, ${PLAYER}. I understand you wish to speak with me?'
'Why do you wish to speak with me?'
Talk to Glorfindel
The Fall of Thaurlach
You have defeated Thaurlach and hold in your possession a broken link of the great chain which once held the Balrog in his prison.
'Speak with Glorfindel and tell him of your victory against the Balrog Thaurlach.'
'There are not many alive who can claim to have ever seen a Balrog, much less defeated one in combat. I know of only one in Middle-earth who can claim the latter.'

Elrond is at the Last Homely House in Rivendell, in the Trollshaws far to the south of Angmar.
You have defeated the Balrog Thaurlach and should inform Elrond Halfelven of your deeds.

Glorfindel may be found outside the Last Homely House standing next to the Bruinen.
Elrond suggested you speak with Glorfindel about the defeat of Thaurlach, for the tale concerns him greatly.

You defeated Thrâng, and in the process, learned that the Ghâshfra serve the Ever-seer. Eimyr, Chieftain of the Eldgang, should be told at once, for he has been deceived by the Ever-seer and unwittingly serves his evil purposes.

'You have defeated Thrâng of the Ghâshfra? You have earned a great reward from the Eldgang.
'What is this you say? The Ghâshfra serve the Ever-seer? The Ever-seer seeks to unleash the Great Evil upon us?
'The Eldgang will not stand idle and allow this thing to happen. We have been betrayed!'
'The Eldgang have naught to do with you, little one. Begone!'
Bring the Sword of Thrâng to Eimyr at Norbar
A Villain Unveiled
You have defeated Thrâng and uncovered the plot of the Ever-seer.
'You have earned the respect of the Eldgang, little one. Now we will see to the Ever-seer!'

Eimyr can be found within Norbar in The Rift of Nûrz Ghâshu.
You have defeated Thrâng and hold his weapon as proof of your valour. You should go to Eimyr and tell him of the Ever-seer's evil betrayal.

'Hail and well met, ${PLAYER}. Were you sent here to aid us? Let me tell you of my mission, then perhaps you will know whether you may aid me or not.
'I was sent both to protect Jónsi, who is here to investigate rumours of ancient mines within the Rift, and to seek out a rare and particularly deadly variety of mushroom -- Curtamusgan -- which grows within. The spores of this mushroom might be used by the Enemy to create a terrible weapon.
'If you would enter the Rift and find one of these mushrooms for me, I can have it delivered to Rivendell, so that they may prepare a defence against the poison. Beware, though, the mushrooms may use its spores as a defence against threats to it.'

'This indeed a Curtamusgan, ${PLAYER}. I will have it delivered to Rivendell by the swiftest means possible.
'Take this reward with the gratitude of the Free Peoples.'
'You have returned without a Curtamusgan?'
Talk to Galasebdir
Mushroom for Rivendell
Lore found in the library of Rivendell tell that a particularly deadly variety of mushroom grows within the Rift of Nûrz Ghâshu. This mushroom might be used by the Enemy to create a terrible weapon.
'Curtamusgan are very valuable mushrooms, highly desired in Rivendell.'
'Your efforts have been a great help to us. If you can find any more Curtamusgan, it would be of tremendous benefit to Rivendell.'

Curtamusgan may be found within the Rift of Nûrz Ghâshu.
Galasebdir has asked you to bring him a Curtamusgan, so that the scholars at Rivendell might study it and prepare a defence against its poison should Angmar use it as a weapon.

Galasebdir is at Iorelen's camp.
You have found a Curtamusgan and should bring it to Galasebdir at once.
Defeated Barz
Defeated Zurm

'Greetings, ${PLAYER}! Are you here to aid us in our struggle against the Orcs of Angmar?
'Angmar has sent two tribes of Fire-orcs into the Rift, which they call Nûrz Ghâshu, to mine the metals which may be found there -- which I suspect are of the finest quality! It would be far too dangerous for me to venture alone into their mines, but perhaps you could, with aid.
'If you go there, seek out Barz and Zurm, the Gorthorog-overseers of Bornabar, and defeat them. I understand they not only put Orcs to work, but also slaves from among the Hillmen of Angmar.'

'You have defeated Barz and Zurm? That is wonderful news, ${PLAYER}! Those vile beasts will do no more harm to the stone of the Rift.
'Take this reward...you are well-deserving of it!'
Defeat Barz
Defeat Zurm
The Craft of the Enemy
Two of the Orc-tribes of Angmar, the Blogmal and the Tarkrîp are in conflict over mining rights in Bornabar.
'Barz and Zurm are terrible taskmasters.'
'You did well to destroy those Gorthorog...their mining was destroying the stone of the Rift!'

Barz and Zurm are in Bornabar, within the crumbling seal below Iorelen's camp.
Jónsi has asked you to enter the mines of the Orcs and defeat the Gorthorog-overseers, Barz and Zurm.

Jónsi is at Iorelen's Camp.
You should return to Jónsi and tell him of your victory against Barz and Zurm.

'Master Elrond sent me here to the Rift, which is called Nûrz Ghâshu by the Enemy, to investigate rumours of forays therein by Angmar's forces. There are veins of valuable metals and a variety of deadly mushrooms which might be used to produce a terrible weapon for the Enemy.
'Lord Glorfindel told me, as well, of a legend of a race of giants which dwell deep in the heart of Nûrz Ghâshu. This legend greatly interests me, for it is said these giants, the Eldgang, are not of an evil bent and may help us to combat Angmar.
'Will you enter the Rift and seek out the Eldgang? If you find them, I will reward you according to your deeds.'

'The Eldgang still dwell within the Rift? If they can be swayed to join in our fight, we could well defeat Angmar.
'Rivendell should be informed at once!'
Learn more about the Eldgang
The Eldgang

Iorelen was sent to the Rift of Nûrz Ghâshu to investigate the activities of Angmar in the area and the existence of a deadly mushroom found there which could be used by the Enemy to create a terrible weapon. He is also seeking a race of giants of which he learned from Glorfindel at Rivendell.
'I am interested in learning more of this Eldgang.'
'You are not like the other little ones who have come here, the Ghâshfra...perhaps you will help us?'

The Eldgang can be found deep within the Rift of Nûrz Ghâshu.
Iorelen has asked you to seek out signs of the Eldgang, the legendary Fire-giants of Nûrz Ghâshu.

Iorelen is at Iorelen's Camp.
You should return to Iorelen with news of what you found within the Rift.
You have defeated Thaurlach

'The Ever-seer lied to the Eldgang. We will no longer listen to his foul words.
'For many centuries, we suffered the cruelty of Thaurlach, a Balrog of the Great Enemy, and fought against him. When the Blue Wanderers came with the Elf Glathlírel and chained Thaurlach, our people were glad and helped to watch him. Now the Ever-seer wishes to free Thaurlach and use him for his own evil purposes.
'Go to Gorthban and help Glathlírel, who remains here still in vigil over Thaurlach's prison. She will know what to do.'

'What is this you tell me, ${PLAYER}? The Balrog Thaurlach has been defeated? That is a hope we dared not dream of. Your name shall be recorded in the lore of the Elves as long as time shall last.
'Take this as a reward for your dauntless courage.'
Defeat Thaurlach
An Ancient Threat
Eimyr, the chieftain of the Eldgang, realized the folly of his ways and has chosen to stand against the ancient evil which lies within the halls of Nûrz Gâashu.
'Go to Gorthban and aid the Elf Glathlírel.'
'Thaurlach is dead? You should go forth and proclaim these tidings to the overworld.'
'Your name shall be remembered by the Elves for your deeds, ${PLAYER}.'

Glathlírel stands vigilant outside of Gorthban.
Eimyr has instructed you to find Glathlírel and aid her against Thaurlach, a Balrog of Morgoth.

Iorelen is at Iorelen's Camp.
You have slain Thaurlach and should tell Iorelen of your deeds.
Defeated Ghâshfra (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Little one, you may be of help to the Eldgang. While we did not build this place, it is our home now, and it is threatened by the Ghâshfra from the surface world.
'There are many places in Nûrz Ghâshu where the Eldgang cannot go, for they are too small. Perhaps you would go into these holes and drive forth the Ghâshfra? Then we may have peace again.
'There are many Ghâshfra in Nûrz Ghâshu. They are like a plague.'
Defeat Ghâshfra (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Threat of Fire
The Ghâshfra, a breed of Fire-orcs from Angmar, have invaded the Rift of Nûrz Ghâshu.
'Please destroy the violators of our home, ${PLAYER}.'
'Many have noticed your work with killing the Fire-orcs ${PLAYER}.'

Orcs of the Ghâshfra can be found throughout the Rift of Nûrz Ghâshu.
Hyrrokkin has asked you to defeat the Ghâshfra which have invaded the Rift of Nûrz Ghâshu.
Defeated Thrâng

'Ho there, little one. Perhaps you will help with our troubles here? The Ghâshfra, the Fire-orcs from the surface world, have come to Norbar and war wih us. Perhaps you will help to drive them away?
'The name of their chieftain is Thrâng. If he is slain, the Ghâshfra may learn not to trouble the Eldgang. Asmólf sought Thrâng, but was sent instead to the intruders' mine by Eimyr at the behest of the Ever-seer.
'Perhaps you will do this for us? Thrâng may be found within The Rift of Nûrz Ghâshu. If you defeat him, your aid will not be forgotten.'
'Fire-orcs have invaded the Rift? We must be wary and learn more of the situation in Nûrz Ghâshu.'
Defeat Thrâng
Aiding the Eldgang
The Fire-giant city of Norbar has been invaded by Fire-orcs from Angmar.
'Defeat Thrâng, and you will have greatly aided the Eldgang.'

'You have defeated Thrâng? You are a brave warrior among your folk. You will not be forgotten by Tortrygg.'
Tortrygg seems to have little more to say. It may be that Glathlírel may have more insight as to how you should proceed.
'The Ghâshfra are a dangerous breed of Orc. We must proceed with caution.'

Thrâng is within The Rift of Nûrz Ghâshu.
Tortrygg has asked you to find and defeat Thrâng, leader of the Ghâshfra in the Rift of Nûrz Ghâshu.

Iorelen is at Iorelen's Camp above The Rift of Nûrz Ghâshu.
You should bring your report of Thrâng's defeat to Iorelen and learn how you should proceed.
Defeated Narnûlubat
Defeated Zogtark

'You are a friend to us, little one? Then hear me, Tortrygg of Norbar. Evil Fire-orcs came from the surface world to conquer us and unleash the Great Evil. They kill us, we kill them...it does not end.
'I ask you to help us end this war. Help us to drive back the Fire-Orcs. If you can slay Narnûlubat and Zogtark, two of the leaders of the Ghâshfra, the Fire-orcs, the others might leave.
'Will you help us? Narnûlubat and Zogtark may be found within Noruidor.'
'You are a mighty warrior, little one. You are deserving of this reward, though I fear your success was not enough to drive away the Ghâshfra.'

'Ah, thank you for the help, ${PLAYER}. I will recover in time from these wounds, but nothing can help my brother, Thorkell. When last I saw him he was trapped in the jaws of a great worm. I can only hope his end was swift.
'The worms will have left naught to bury, but they do not eat dwarf-steel. If you dare venture within their caves and retrieve what remains of my brother's belongings, I shall reward you richly.
'You can find the worm caves to the south-east.'

'Ah, is this all that remains of my fair brother Thorkell? Would that I had fallen in his stead....
'But nay, I speak as a fool in my mourning! My dear brother was ever the warrior and adventurer -- moreso than I. He gave his life as he chose to save mine, and I'll never again gainsay his valour for doing so. Nor will I dishonour his name by failing to live as he chose that I should.
'It seems that I have much to do, ${PLAYER}, and wallowing in my grief while the merciless wind wears down these mountains will not get it done!'
'Have the worms devoured everything? Something must remain of my brother's belongings that you can recover....'

Echad Candelleth sits atop a hill in Tâl Bruinen, south-east of Thorenhad. Elrohir told you to head east along the main road to the Bruinen, where you will find another white marker stone.
Elrohir told you to go to Echad Candelleth and aid Candelleth's company, while he and Elladan inform their father of the threats you discovered in Nan Tornaeth.

'My brother and I will see to it that our father is notified of the threats in Nan Tornaeth, for there is more yet to be done in the wilds. The Trollshaws are dangerous, as you have seen, ${PLAYER}, and it takes the labour of many Elves to keep the wild at bay.
'South along the river, you will find the wooded hills of Tâl Bruinen. Echad Candelleth stands high atop one of the hills there. Travel east until you see the river, and you will find yet another white marker stone. Follow the dirt path to the south that climbs the hills above the western bank of the Bruinen. After you pass into Tâl Bruinen, keep a close watch on the path, for the wilderness encroaches upon it, and it may be difficult to make out. The land, too, is damp, and the path may be crossed by several quick-flowing streams.
'I am certain that Candelleth will have dispatched a scout to guide friends to her encampment. Lend whatever aid you may to Candelleth and her company.'

'Greetings, traveller! If you are looking for Echad Candelleth, you have nearly found it! You simply need to climb the slope to the south-east. As you crest the hill, you will see the encampment among the ruins.
'Introduce yourself to Nestael, and she will tell you of these lands and what you might do to help.'

'It is a pleasure to meet you, ${PLAYER}, for we have much need of aid! Tâl Bruinen has become a place of great danger: Gauredain from the far north have found their way here and have established a camp in the south-west, the Dâg Taushakhu in the depths of Eryn Singor urge the Wood-trolls to greater and greater malevolence, and the rock-worms of Cirith Ulunn threaten travellers in these lands.
'A number of hunters have come here as well, and we grant them what hospitality we may. Treat them with kindness, for they are our guests. Furthermore, servants of Angmar have come to Tâl Bruinen. They have focused their attention on the small ruins to be found throughout the woods, but I know not what they seek.'
Seek the white marker stone indicating the path to Tâl Bruinen
Talk to an Elf-scout in Tâl Bruinen
Talk to Nestael
A Road Seldom Travelled
The markings on this stone indicate that you should take the dirt path leading south from the road and up the hill
After your defeat of the gaunt-man Gúrdring in Nan Tornaeth, Elrohir told you of Echad Candelleth, an Elf-camp in Tâl Bruinen, and suggested that you lend its keepers your aid.

Echad Candelleth sits atop a hill in Tâl Bruinen, south-east of Thorenhad. Elrohir told you to take dirt path south as it climbs the hills above the western bank of the river. He advised that you to pay close attention to the path, as it is covered in brush and crossed by streams, but said that you might find a scout somewhere along its length to guide you to the encampment.
Elrohir has asked you to help the Elves at Echad Candelleth with their charge of keeping Tâl Bruinen free from danger.

Nestael is at Echad Candelleth, the Elf-camp in Tâl Bruinen, just over the south-east hill from Haradir's post.
Haradir told you to introduce yourself to Nestael at Echad Candelleth, and she would let you know what aid you might lend.

'So...it is done at last, and my brother's memory is avenged. Thank you, ${PLAYER}. It will be far easier to go on with business knowing that my debt to Thorkell no longer weighs so heavily upon my chest.
'What to do now, though? These mountains have grown ever more dangerous in these past few years, and Afwald is not the adventurous sort to join me on the hunt. Perhaps I will need to find a new partner, or give up the hunt at last?
'I've no patience for the comforts of civilization anymore -- I think I will stay here and take my chances with worm and wolf-man.'

'All you have discovered will contribute to us keeping the Misty Mountains safer in the future. If our number was larger now, I have no doubt that Glóin would once again brave the depths of Goblin-town himself and destroy the goblins there. Alas, we are small in number, and there are greater threats to contain elsewhere. Let us be direct then....
'Glóin would like you to be watchful for the goblin and troll, Rakothúrz and Horm, within the Great Goblin's throne room. Lord Elrond mentioned that the forces of Angmar wanted to draw them into the conflict in the north and west, and if we can destroy them we may save the lives of countless allies.
'Search the throne room in Goblin-town for this troll and goblin, and after they are defeated, return to me. Goblin-town is to the north and east.'

'Well done! A victory against such a terrible foe is surely a great thing.
'You have our thanks and should be content to know that you have saved the lives of many who would surely have suffered terrible fates at the hands of those foes.'
Talk to Tralli Gemfinder
Rakothúrz and Horm

Information received from the letters you recovered in Black Speech led Glóin to offer rewards for the defeat of Rakothúrz and Horm, a goblin-handler and a terrible Cave-troll found in the Great Goblin's throne room in Goblin-town.
'Seek out Rakothúrz and Horm within the throne room of Goblin-town.'
'Rakothúrz and Horm will do no ill to the Free Peoples, thanks to your efforts.'

Goblin-town is to the north-east of Glóin's Camp and the throne room should lay straight through the many tunnels.
Tralli Gemfinder directed you to find and defeat the troll and goblin, Horm and Rakothúrz, within the Great Goblin's throne room.

Tralli Gemfinder is at Glóin's camp in the Misty Mountains, outside the entrance to Goblin-town.
You should return to Tralli Gemfinder with news of your success.
Elrond has returned the orders to you

'We have no time to waste, ${PLAYER}. Take these directly to Master Elrond in Rivendell and beseech him to translate them. We have already been delayed too long.
'It is vital that we learn what the Uruks are up to. If they are able to muster the goblins of the Misty Mountains, who knows what force will be arrayed against us?
'Quickly now. Rivendell lies to the south-west, if you were not aware already.'

'Master Glóin was wise to send you to me. It appears that his fears regarding the goblins have proven true. Though I am loath to say it, it appears a new goblin-leader has emerged within the hollows of Goblin-town. This new Great Goblin has united the goblins in there and even now defies the emissary sent from the north.
'Glóin should be told that the emissary from the north is under orders to force the goblins to heed the call of Angmar. Warn him of this and tell him to be cautious.
'Take the orders back to him and bid him read my words.'
'You should never see this text.'
'The Great Goblin? But this cannot be! Gandalf slew the Great Goblin with Glamdring. Another goblin has risen in his place, I am sure of it. This news is most distressing.'
'You should never see this.'
Show the orders to Elrond at Rivendell
Deliver the orders to Glóin at his camp in the Misty Mountains
Glóin looked at the set of orders recovered from the Uruks in Goblin-town and found that they were also written in the Black Speech.
'Return to Glóin swiftly. He must be warned at once.'
'Quickly now, show those orders to Master Elrond at Rivendell. We haven't much time!'

Elrond is at the Last Homely House in Rivendell, south-west of Glóin's camp.
Glóin realized that another set of orders written in the Black Speech would take too long to translate and sent you to Rivendell in order to speak with Elrond directly.

Glóin is at his camp just outside of Goblin-town, north-east of Rivendell.
Elrond Halfelven made marks upon the orders and warned you that the goblins had a new leader, a Great Goblin who was defiant of the Uruks' intrusion in Goblin-town. He sent you back to Glóin with the translated orders.
Collected the orders

'As I mentioned before, the papers spoke of visitors from the North, and at first I expected that they were Angmarim, like the ones we have seen crawling through the hills. It seems that the Angmarim here are not dealing with goblins at all, but rather great Uruks have come to Goblin-town to press the goblins into service.
'Vighar Roadwalker has a list of names that the Elves discovered among the papers. Speak with him, and perhaps he can offer you rewards for some of the goblins mentioned therein.
'I also would have you seek out the place where these visiting Uruks have been sent in Goblin-town and discover their whole purpose.'
'More Black Speech. We cannot waste any more time, ${PLAYER}. The words written here must be translated quickly.'

'Be sure to speak with Vighar before you return to Goblin-town. He has a list of the names found in those papers.
'Be careful as you seek out the Uruks. Any one of them may carry orders for the goblins, but there may be one who is more clearly a leader among them.'
Collect the orders
Return the orders to Glóin at his camp outside of Goblin-town
Rumours of the North
Glóin further explained the writings found on the sheaf of papers you recovered, which entailed a visitation by emissaries from Angmar.
'Have you collected the orders yet, ${PLAYER}? Please make haste!'

Goblin-town lies to the north-east of Glóin's camp.
Glóin sent you back to Goblin-town to find the orders carried by the Uruks from Angmar to the goblins of Goblin-town. You will need to locate the place within Goblin-town where the Uruks have gathered.

Gloín awaits you at his camp just outside of Goblin-town.
You should bring the papers you recovered to Glóin so that he may evaluate them.
Defeated Wargs in Goblin-town (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Wargs are not something we want to contend with, ${PLAYER}. I remember them circling below me long ago as clear as if it were happening now. Their eyes alone could cause the hardiest dwarf to lose heart. Even Gandalf the Grey seemed afraid of such a pack arrayed against us that night. I know that you have dealt with Wargs before with all that is brewing in the wild places, but Wargs with goblins is another matter. The goblins and Wargs have long been allied, and together, they are terrible.
'Now look here... this word appears to be a name. I am not certain what it means, nor am I a scholar wise enough in this foul tongue to know what it truly says. I know only that we must deal swiftly with these Wargs.
'Return to Goblin-town and hunt them down. Kill as many as you can and then return to me. I will see about getting these writings translated.'

'Goblin-keepers with the Wargs already? This does indeed mean that something darker and evil lies within Goblin-town. Fortunately, I received word from our friends at Rivendell about the orders you found.
'Those orders told of visitors from the North being escorted to a specific part of Goblin-town, a place where the armies of Angmar are gathering.
'It also spoke of a goblin sent there to watch over the visitors.'
Defeat Wargs in Goblin-town (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Glóin at his camp outside of Goblin-town
Memory of the Wargs
Glóin noticed one word which he recognized among the papers you found: Warg.
'Hunt the Wargs in the tunnels of Goblin-town. In the meanwhile, I will work on getting these papers translated.'

There are Wargs in the tunnels of Goblin-town, to the north-east of Glóin's camp.
Glóin explained that, though he cannot decipher the full meaning of the documents you found, there is something sinister within. Seeing only a name and the word for Wargs, he sent you back into the depths of Goblin-town in search of the Wargs allied with the goblins.

Glóin is at his camp outside the entrance of Goblin-town.
Entering Goblin-town, you found your way into the many twisting tunnels and defeated many Wargs. You found goblin-keepers with the Wargs, which may interest Glóin.
You found a sheaf of nasty looking papers on the corpse of this goblin

'You did well against those goblins, but something you mentioned has me concerned. I fear that the sheer number of goblins milling about at the entrance to that place is greater than I expected. It can only mean that they are stirred up to some task or afraid of something deeper in those accursed halls. It merits further investigation.
'Make your way back there, ${PLAYER}, and look for the goblin-leader before the main hall. Something is amiss within those halls, and we must discover the truth, sooner rather than later.
'If you find anything out of the ordinary, return to me so we can put an end to it quickly!'

'Black Speech! Accursed creatures! There is something brewing in that place, I am certain of this now.
'This sheaf of papers is more than enough evidence that the goblins in Goblin-town are working towards some nefarious end. We shall need to delve further, I think, to see the true state of affairs here.
'I recognize this word. Wargs....'

'Be swift, if the goblins are given enough time they may be prepared to move against the West. The people of the North Downs are already suffering enough, and if we can do something to ease their suffering here, we shall!'
Talk to Glóin at his camp outside Goblin-town
Search for orders among the goblins in Goblin-town
Order from the Darkness
After hearing how you fared against the goblins at Goblin-town, Glóin grew more concerned.

The main entrance to Goblin-town is just to the north-east of Glóin's camp in the Northern High Pass.
Glóin believes that there may be something afoot within Goblin-town and bade you return to its halls in search of evidence exposing the reason behind the muster of the goblin-forces.
Defeated goblins in and around Goblin-town (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Discovered Goblin-town's main gate

'I first encountered the goblins of Goblin-town when I was with Thorin's Company on our quest to reclaim the Lonely Mountain. They had captured us and dragged us into their vile tunnels, cracking whips and singing terrible songs. We had our vengeance upon them at the Battle of Five Armies, but they simply returned to the Mountains and began gathering their strength again.
'Now with darkness rising everywhere, they have become a threat again...a threat we must hinder as quickly as possible. The entrance we were taken through was hidden, probably a postern gate. Ahead is their main gate. Enter it and wreak havoc among their number.'

'So many goblins! You say that there were more than enough for your blades, and I have no reason to doubt your word. I fear that my friend Dwalin may be right. The Darkness reaching into the Blue Mountains may also be stretching here to the Misty Mountains.
'We must investigate further, I fear, and that means you must go back into the darkness of Goblin-town.'
Defeat goblins in and around Goblin-town (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Discover the main gate into Goblin-town
Talk to Glóin at his camp outside Goblin-town
Goblins at the Gate
The hatred between goblins and dwarves runs deep, and Glóin wants to go on the offensive against the goblins before their threat grows too great.
'Be careful, ${PLAYER}. The goblins are treacherous creatures, and they will not hesitate to throw a bag over your head and drag you down to their prisons or mines!'

The main gate into Goblin-town is to the north and east of Glóin's camp.
Glóin has instructed you to enter the main gate into Goblin-town and defeat many of the Overland Goblins near the entrance.

Glóin is at his camp, just outside the entrance of Goblin-town.
Goblin-town teemed with goblins, and the forces within were ferocious and many. You steeled your nerve and struck against them, felling many as you pressed through the entrance of their terrible kingdom. Now you should return to Glóin with news of your success.

'Hail, friend, I would have a moment of your time, if you please. I have a request that may seem out of the ordinary. Long ago, I travelled through the Misty Mountains with Thorin's Company. We found ourselves in trouble within the mouth of a cave in those Mountains and ended up in a terrible place filled with goblins.
'I fear that the recent increase of goblins here in the Blue Mountains, specifically at Sarnur, might mean a greater mustering of goblins throughout Middle-earth. I have heard reports that a friend from the same company is in the area now, and I was hoping that you could seek him out and see if there is anything that he has seen with regards to the goblins.
'His name is Glóin, and he can be found at his camp in the western foothills of the Misty Mountains, far to the east of here, beyond the Lone-lands and the Trollshaws. Seek him out and warn him of the changes in the goblins' behaviour here.'

'My old friend Dwalin sends words of concern! Ha!
'To be true, his concerns are well-founded. The goblins here are as riled as those in the Blue Mountains...moreso perhaps. There is word that the Elves under Master Elrond's care have even sent scouts to see what transpires within the halls of Goblin-town.
'I have a mind to investigate myself, but the dwarves here need my assistance as the Dourhands and their allies are our main concern. Still... it may merit investigation.'
Talk to Glóin at his camp in the Misty Mountains
Dwalin's Concern
Dwalin is concerned about rumours that he has heard about stirrings in the Misty Mountains.
'Be swift! There could be great danger afoot in the Mountains.'

Seek out Glóin at his camp in the western foothills of the Misty Mountains, north of Rivendell, far to the east of Ered Luin.
Dwalin wants you to bring word of warning to his friend Glóin in the Misty Mountains. He believes that the increased goblin activity may not be restricted to the goblins in Ered Luin.
You have spoken with Gandalf
You have spoken with Frodo Baggins

'I would hate to ask this of you, ${PLAYER}, but there is another place I would like you to go. The way is quite dangerous, and I simply am not sure whether I should indeed ask it of you, but it is a very important place... it is really where this whole mess began.
'Deep within Goblin-town, there is a cave. I've mentioned it before, I'm sure. A wretched creature called Gollum once lived there. Gandalf says he is related to hobbits, but I just cannot imagine it.
'At any rate, I would like you to find that cave and get me proper directions, as I stumbled into it quite by accident during my adventure with Thorin and Company. But perhaps you should speak with Gandalf the Grey and my nephew Frodo... they might have some reservations about anyone going there.'

'Well then, you have returned, and that means you have spoken to my nephew and my friend Gandalf. They aren't keen on your going to Gollum's cave? Well, I suppose I can't blame them, but I simply must know what has become of that place and how to find it again.'

'Uncle Bilbo is a dear old hobbit, and he remembers his adventure fondly, but I do not think he even now understands exactly how terrible this whole thing is.
'Gollum is loose, and he is searching for... well, he is searching for something he once possessed. If you go to that place, hope he has not returned there himself.'

'Bilbo wants you to go where? While Gollum no longer dwells within that cavern, it is by no means safe. You will have to pass through the ranks of goblins in Goblin-town.
'What did he tell you of his encounter with Gollum? Nothing? That is good, for it entails knowledge which you need not be made aware of.
'I cannot hinder you, if you believe yourself up to the task, but I warn against it.'
Talk to Gandalf in Rivendell
Talk to Frodo Baggins in Rivendell
Talk to Bilbo Baggins
Preparing for the Dark
Bilbo Baggins has completed his book and would like to make certain that his memory of the important locations and events is correct.
'You really should speak with Frodo and Gandalf before you leave. Let me know what they think of this adventure I have tasked you with. You'll find them in my room on the ground floor.'
'I dread the place you speak of, though I have never been there myself. Bilbo's encounter there has laid on me a terrible burden and has brought me great woe.'
'Be cautious should you seek Gollum's cave, for the journey is long and perilous. The goblins will not likely let you pass unharmed.'

Gandalf and Frodo are in Bilbo's room on the first floor of the Last Homely House, in Rivendell.
Uncertain of the task he has set before you, Bilbo Baggins wants you to speak with his nephew, Frodo Baggins, and the Wizard Gandalf the Grey before setting forth on your journey.

Bilbo Baggins is in the Hall of Fire in the Last Homely House at Rivendell.
Gandalf and Frodo warned you of the dangers found in the cavern in the dark. You should return to Bilbo Baggins with their opinions.
You have spoken with Glóin
You have spoken with Dwalin

'All this talk about Goblin-town and my adventures with Thorin and company has brought back many memories. I was wondering if it wouldn't be too much a bother to have you visit my old friends. I have heard tell that Dwalin is at Thorin's Hall in the Blue Mountains, away west of the dear old Shire and that Glóin is encamped in the Misty Mountains, north from here.
'I wonder if they have any memories of Goblin-town which I could add to my book. Would you visit them and find out for me?
'I would go, but I pledged I had made my last journey. Well, my last journey for a long while anyway.'

'Bilbo Baggins? Old Burglar Baggins? There is a name I have not heard in many, many years.
'So he would like my impressions of Goblin-town? Well, they were not good, that is for certain. All the whips, the stench, the goblins, the wretched songs they sang... it was a dreadful ordeal altogether.
'And to make it worse, when Dori lost our burglar in those tunnels, and Gandalf demanded we go back for him... well, we nearly despaired. Then he appeared out of nowhere, alive! Oh, that was a strange day.'

'So you were able to find Dwalin and Glóin? Oh, that is good.
'And Dwalin was impressed by my reappearance after escaping Goblin-town? Well, it never would have happened if I hadn't fallen into that dratted Gollum's cave and found... well, found my way out.
'It's a pity that Gollum-creature escaped the Elf-king's people.'

'Bilbo has you researching Goblin-town? We had a terrible time there. I was sure the Great Goblin was going to make an end of us... but then Gandalf came along and saved the day.
'The fire went out, and all we could see was a towering column of smoke and sparks and Glamdring flashing blue in the dark. The Great Goblin fell dead, and his folk went all wild.
'We still might not have escaped that place, if it hadn't been daylight outside.'
Talk to Glóin in the Misty Mountains
Talk to Dwalin
Talk to Bilbo Baggins in Rivendell
My Dwarf Friends
Bilbo Baggins has completed his book and would like to make certain that his memory of the important locations and events is correct.

'Good old Bilbo. I have never met a burglar his equal. We were lost in the great Mirkwood without him. And oh the surprise he gave us when we fled Goblin-town.
'I tell you friend, Bilbo Baggins is a magnificent burglar.'
'If you would, please speak with my old dwarf-friends about their memories of Goblin-town. Dwalin is at Thorin's Hall, Glóin at his camp in the Misty Mountains.'

'I remember well of what Bilbo speaks, and I would rather not enter that place again. Darkness stirs in these lands now, and we might yet need to fight our way back through those forsaken tunnels and ancient halls.
'Be cautious if it is Bilbo's charge to send you there.'

Dwalin is at Thorin's Hall far to the west, beyond the Shire. Glóin is at his camp north of Rivendell.
Bilbo Baggins would like to know if his dwarf-friends Dwalin and Glóin have any recollections which would make good additions to his book.

Bilbo Baggins is at Rivendell in the Trollshaws, south of Glóin's camp and far to the east of Thorin's Hall.
Dwalin and Glóin both shared stories of their adventure in Goblin-town. Now you should return to Bilbo.
You have discovered the hidden entrance to Goblin-town

'Well, hullo there! You seem a bit of an adventurous sort... perhaps you wouldn't mind helping out an old hobbit?
'You see, I have been writing a book about my travels with Thorin and his Company -- off to deal with Smaug and get Thorin's gold back -- and I am afraid I may have gotten confused on some details. My memory isn't what it used to be, and I am unsure of the directions to some of the places we visited.
'Perhaps you would help me? All you need to do is find the Back Door of Goblin-town... if you find the place, I have remembered them a-right. High in the mountains, along the stretch called the High Pass, we travelled and at night found a dry place in a cave midway up the mountain. You should find the entrance there. If not, well, try and find the correct directions for me, if you would be so kind.'

'Oh, you found it! That is wonderful.
'Do you know, we found the doorstep quite by accident. We were camping there, taking refuge from a storm and some wayward boulders -- the giants were out playing catch, I suppose -- and were set upon by goblins!
'Gandalf the Grey blasted a few, but we were captured and dragged down to Goblin-town. From there, the tale only gets more exciting.'
Find the hidden entrance to Goblin-town
Talk to Bilbo Baggins at Rivendell
Passage to Darkness
Bilbo Baggins has completed his book and would like to make certain that his memory of the important locations is correct.
'Those directions I gave you should lead you straight to the doorstep of Goblin-town... I hope.'

Bilbo Baggins described the location and advised you to use his description to find the hidden entrance to Goblin-town that he and the dwarves of Thorin's Company once came across on their journeys long ago.
Bilbo Baggins would like you to help him correct the directions to Goblin-town that he has written in his book.

Bilbo Baggins is at the Last Homely House in Rivendell, south-west of Goblin-town.
Having completed the task Bilbo set you to, you should return to him at Rivendell.

'I have concerns ${PLAYER}. Elrond asked if we had seen a scout dispatched to Goblin-town from Rivendell. He surely would have come by here, but we have had no sight of him.
'I fear he may have been captured by the goblins. If this is true, then I can only hope that he lives still and is kept somewhere in the prisons within Goblin-town. Venture within and see if you can find Aeglas.'

'I thank you and Master Elrond for your concern, but I am in no imminent danger.
'The goblins are strong foes, but not so strong that I cannot leave this place. Yet, there is much that we may do together.'
Find Aeglas within Goblin-town
A Missing Scout
Glóin believes that a scout sent to the north has become a prisoner of the goblins of Goblin-town.
'Aeglas went to scout Goblin-town...I fear he may have been captured. Find him quickly and rescue him, if it proves he needs it!'

Seek out Aeglas in Goblin-town, to the North of Rivendell, in the Misty Mountains.
Glóin explained that Elrond dispatched an Elf to investigate the stirrings of goblins from their mountain stronghold at Goblin-town. Fearing that Aeglas has been captured, he hopes that you may yet find him alive within the depths of the goblin city.
Defeated Kaushar
Defeated Goblin-town lashers (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Your discovery in Goblin-town has us all on edge around here, ${PLAYER}. Something terrible is amiss, and we must be vigilant against that growing darkness or face a terrible foe when they are organized.
'Glóin would like to see that this never comes to pass and has asked me to find those willing to face the strongest enemies within Goblin-town.
'The translation of the sheaf mentioned goblin-lashers keeping troll-drummers in line in the deep places of Goblin-town. We need you to go there, seek out these lashers, kill them and their leader, then return to us.'

'This news is bright indeed, friend! You are proving an invaluable asset to us.
'We are in your debt, and I personally thank you. I have no desire to face a host of trolls driven forward by cruel goblin masters.'
Defeat Kaushar
Defeat Goblin-town lashers (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

The notes you discovered spoke of trolls being kept in the deep parts of Goblin-town, drumming to stir up the goblins and prepare them for battle. Glóin has tasked Vighar with organizing parties to enter the drum areas and kill the trolls and the leader of the lashers there to lessen the threat that they represent to the people west and east of the Misty Mountains.
'We do not know where the trolls and the goblin-lashers may be within the stronghold. We know only that the notes you recovered makes mention of them.'
'We shall call you ${PLAYER}, Destroyer of Goblin-town, one day, I think.'

Goblin-town is to the north-east of Glóin's camp.
Vighar has asked you to find your way through the stronghold to the area where the troll-drummers are watched over by the lashers. Kill several of these goblins and their leader, Kaushar.

'Glóin tells me that you have been working with him to discover why the goblins of Goblin-town have become so bold. I thought you would like to know that he informed me of a good number of leaders within Goblin-town that need to be found and disposed of to weaken the goblins' resolve.
'I do not know where within the depths you will find these leaders, but when you do, you should deal with them expediently.
'Goblin-town is to the north-east of this camp, and you will find these goblin-leaders throughout the place.'

'There are too many goblins, if you ask me -- but then, one is too many. However, if they are this organized, then there must be someone leading them... someone with greater authority.
'We must remain vigilant, ${PLAYER}.'

'Find the goblin-leaders in the depths of Goblin-town. When they have been dealt with, return to me. Goblin-town is to the north-east of Glóin's camp.'
'Your efforts are greatly appreciated, ${PLAYER}.'

You found the goblin leaders throughout Goblin-town. Dâgal watched over the Orcs from Angmar, Zagh travelled the tunnels yelling at the guards, and Farmak was found running through the tunnels in search of intruders. Now that thay have been defeated, you should return to Vighar.
You have spoken with Glorwen
You have spoken with Oghûk

'There are prisoners in this place other than I, and of them I would know more. One is an Elf-maiden, for whom I am concerned. The other is one of the goblins' own.
'I know not how the Elf-maiden came to be here, but she has not been treated well. If you would, go to her and learn her tale. I would know how she was captured by the goblins.
'As far as the goblin goes, though I am loath to ask this, I would have you speak with him as well. He has been treated no better than the Elf-maiden, and that makes me wonder why he was imprisoned and not simply slain.'
'Stop looking at me, ${RACE}. You have been killing goblins all through Goblin-town. I'm in enough trouble as it is to dig a deeper hole for myself. Unless maybe you help me....'

'Glorwen should not be concerned for me. I will see that she is freed in good time. For the moment, I think the goblins are otherwise indisposed.
'If the goblins and Uruks are indeed in contention one with the other, perhaps we can find a way to use that knowledge to our advantage.
'I will also warn you to be cautious of your dealings with Oghûk. He is a goblin, and we cannot trust him, but the information he may have could be important.'

'${PLAYER}, I do not speak often of our journeys with my Lord Thorin, but I feel I must now. Long ago, we travelled through these mountains with Burglar Baggins and became captives of the goblins of Goblin-town. Taken down into the dark for what seemed forever, we eventually came to the centre of that place and met the Great Goblin.
'We were without hope in that place, for it was so dark that even our dwarf-sight was diminished and all hope seemed lost. The Great Goblin discovered weapons upon our persons that had been used to fight his kind in ages past and became furious, and hope drew ever farther from our hearts. Thorin, my lord and our leader, remained defiant, and though he attempted to placate the goblin, nothing would calm his rage. At the moment when all seemed most bleak, Gandalf the Grey appeared and slew the Great Goblin, freeing us from Goblin-town and the clutches of the goblins there.
'This news of a new Great Goblin puts a cloud of dread over my heart. If it is true, then we have no choice but to destroy him before the goblins are organized enough to march to the east against Dáin Ironfoot and the dwarves of the Lonely Mountain, or to the west against the Men of Eriador. I ask you to make your way into the throne room with your allies and find this Great Goblin and end him before his shadow grows so large that it looms over all within it. Will you do this?'

'This old dwarf has had hope restored by your hand, ${PLAYER}.
'All dwarves everywhere will know your name when the threat climbing across this world is quelled, you have my word on this. The word of a dwarf is stronger than the mountains upon which we stand.
'Ashûrz is no more, and we have you to thank for this.'

'Greetings, ${PLAYER}! I have something to offer you. Since the eviction of the Dourhands, the prosperity of Thorin's Hall has been on the rise of late -- and with the Men of Bree-town clamouring for our goods, even more so!
'Such riches seem to draw folks out of the stonework, if you will, and so we've recently been opening out some wider tunnels and adding room for people to move in as they seek work in our mines and crafting-halls. You should go take a look and see if anything there fits your own needs!
'Seek out Rúni at the gates of the Thorin's Hall community. There is always room for another hard worker here!'

'Good day, ${PLAYER}. While you no doubt know that the presence of the Elves in Middle-earth has dwindled in the past age, it might surprise you to know that the communities along this river have grown in recent years as more and more of our brethren arrive awaiting their turn to sail into the West. We have even found it necessary to raise a new neighbourhood to accomodate those who are making the journey, as well as those who may be travelling no further, but wish to live here and aid in the work we do here.
'I must admit, it is rather exciting to live in a community where there is such vibrance and life, and I have delayed my own journey twice already to remain here and enjoy the company of so many purposeful folk.
'But I digress. Should you seek your own dwelling here in our community upon the shores of the river, find Barchiril at the gates of the neighbourhood and speak with her. She should be able to help you.'

'Greetings ${PLAYER}! It's a fine day to be looking for a place to live, isn't it? The Shire has been most prosperous of late, most prosperous indeed, as the Men of Bree-land have come to rely upon us for ever greater stocks of quality produce and our unmatched flavours of pipe-weed.
'Of course, prosperity draws people to it, and our communities are growing. We even have a new neighbourhood now just south of Michel Delving. If you would like to see it, one such as yourself might even be interested in purchasing one of the new properties we have for sale there!
'Seek out Andy Brockhouse at the gates of the Michel Delving community and see if any of our fine holes suits your fancy!'

'Greetings, ${PLAYER}! Hear me out for a moment, or you will miss the opportunity of a lifetime! As anyone with an ear to the ground knows, troubles in the South have brought new settlers here from across Eriador. With such a migration may come such blights as crowding and refuse -- even the rumours of war from the North, as well as the South -- and old Bree-town lies huddled within these old walls, becoming ever more pressed as each new arrival joins the throngs.
'Now a new settlement has been founded within a stone's throw of town! In the hills south-east of Staddle, new homes and estates are being built for those who have arrived of late. There is room for more, however.
'Seek out Nan Henwood at the gates of the Bree community and find your destiny as a proud land-owner in our fine township!'

'Ah, it is good that you have come by, ${PLAYER}! We've just recently completed some of the new homes that we will be offering to the prosperous and industrious folk of Thorin's Hall here in our community.
'What with the Men, Elves and hobbits all clamouring for our ore, business is brisk indeed, and it has brought many a fine miner and forge-crafter to our doors of late. You too, it seems.
'Well, waste no time, I say. Go ahead in and take a look around. You will find whatever it is you are looking for! The craftsmanship of our builders is second to none other in the Hall, and your money will be well spent indeed if you buy a home from us.'

'Greetings ${PLAYER}, and welcome to the community of Duillond. The shipwrights of the Grey Havens labour ceaselessly to make ready the White Ships that depart into the West, but for many who come here the wait may still be a long one, and more come each day on the wings of the dark tidings that now stretch across the land.
'Thus we have found it necessary to build new villages here along the river's edge where travellers may await the day of their departure, or for those who do not wish yet to sail into the West, who choose to live here and provide services for those who do.
'Please enter our fair community and see if there is anything within that might suit your need, be it for but a short while or for a long time to come.'

'Hallo there, ${PLAYER}! Have you come to take a look at the fine holes of our community?
'Not in living memory has the Shire seen such a time of growth and vitality as this! It is a time of industry and wealth for the taking if you know how... why, you would think we had all become dwarves or something!
'So for those with the ambition and means, a home of your own is not out of reach any more! You can go ahead and take a look for yourself if you like. I'm quite sure something will catch your eye!'

'Ah, welcome to the gates of the Bree community, ${PLAYER}! We have built this neighbourhood to accomodate the migration of people from the South, but there is room for more. Perhaps you would be interested?
'Don't let mere rumours of war and strife from afar dissuade you! With your patronage, our community stands poised to become the most prosperous neighbourhood in all the North!'

'I'll sign your petition, you can be sure!'

'A petition for a new Yule-planner? Of course I'll sign it!
'That Lobelia has been nothing but trouble since she moved to Bag End. What I wouldn't give for young Mr. Frodo to return.'
'A petition for a new Yule-planner? Of course, I'll sign it!'
'What's that now? Why of course I'll sign your petition!'
'I'll sign your petition!'
'You were able to find a way to get Lobelia out of her office? Give that paper here!'
'A petition for a new Yule-planner? Of course, I'll sign it!'
'A petition? Why would I sign a silly thing like that?'
Talk to the inhabitants of Hobbiton
Serve Lobelia with the petition
Yule Be Sorry

The Book of Festival-law holds precedent for removing Lobelia Sackville-Baggins from her 'post,' but it will not be easy.

'What's that now? Why of course I'll sign!'
'You were able to find a way to get Lobelia out of her post? Give that paper here!'
'What do you want? Can't you see that I am busy preparing for this year's Yule-feast?'

Hobbiton lies far to the east of Michel Delving.
Will Whitfoot has given you an official petition and has sent you to Hobbiton to find ten inhabitants to sign your petition.

Lobelia Sackville-Baggins is at Bag End on the Hill in Hobbition.

'As I said, there is nothing I can do to help you with Lobelia Sackville-Baggins, as much as I would like to.
'Your only hope for getting a new festival-planner would be to search the Book of Festival-law for any adjuncts to the existing laws.
'I sent the Book of Festival-law to the library in the Great Smials for safe keeping. If you wish to further pursue the matter, you should seek out that book.'
'You found the Book of Festival-law! Let me have a look.'
'Have you found the Book of Festival-law yet? It should be in the library at the Great Smials in Tuckborough.'
Search for the Book of Festival-law
Talk to Will Whitfoot in Michel Delving
The Book of Festival-law

Will Whitfoot mentioned the Book of Festival-law, which may contain more information about Lobelia Sackville-Baggins' supposed post as Yule-planner.
<rgb=#FF0000> NOTE: This quest will be removed from your quest log when the current festival ends. </rgb>

The Book of Festival-law is in the library of the Great Smials in Tuckborough, far to the east of Michel Delving.
