Will Whitfoot is at the Town Hole in Michel Delving, far to the west of Tuckborough.
You should return to Will Whitfoot with the Book of Festival-law.

'Why hullo there! I am guessing you have come about the rumours? Well, I am afraid they are true; Lobelia Sackville-Baggins is the official Yule-planner for the Hobbiton Yule-feast! It's dreadful, simply dreadful! She has already announced that we will be getting nothing more than harvest-vegetables at the feast. The gall of some folk!
'Lobelia also told us that we ought to end the festival early this year, what with all the roustabouts that have been coming in...says it isn't safe for decent folk to stay up late outdoors. Naught but vegetables and an early bed...what is a respectable hobbit to do?
'What's more, no one in Hobbiton is rightly sure how she came by the title. For years, old Mad Baggins held the position, and in turn Frodo Baggins took it after his disappearance. Something isn't right about the whole affair. Do you think you would be able to help us set things to rights?'

'It's bad enough that Lobelia has got her hands on old Mr. Bilbo's hole and has taken to threatening her neighbours and such, but now she has got herself made the official Yule-planner! She'll ruin the holiday, and that's no mistake.
'That Lotho of hers don't take truck with festive drinks and parties, and she loves that boy enough to make a mess of it all for him. What's a Yule-feast without a good mug, I asks? And what is all this nonsense about ending the feast early this year?
'It's bad business, ${PLAYER}. Mark my words, she'll ruin it for us all. Perhaps you could see about dealing with the problem on behalf of us Hobbiton-folk?'

'Have you heard? Old Lobelia Sackville-Baggins has gone and got herself made the official Yule-planner this year! It's dreadful, I says. Old Bilbo at least knew how to throw a particularly fine feast -- if a bit odd -- but Lobelia, now....
'She wants to serve vegetables and tea! Fine for a garden-party, but a Yule-feast? I daresay it's an outrage!
'It's that Lotho's doing, I'd lay odds. He needs a good lesson taught, but I guess no-one's got the courage. Perhaps you might talk to Old Flourdumpling, old Whitfoot the Mayor, about finding someone else?'

'After all her fuss about my pies, Lobelia was made the official Yule-planner. Now she wants to leave my pies out of the feast altogether! I'm not usually one to brag, but my pies are well thought of in Hobbiton, and I just don't think it fair that they should be left out...in favour of vegetables!
'Why I'm sure Opal Goodbody put her up to this outrage...she never did like me. Well, I can deal with her, but who is going to deal with Lobelia?
'Maybe you would find out how she managed to get her position and can find a way to do something about it? It would be a blessing to all of Hobbiton if you could!'

'I think it is just delightful that Lobelia was made the official Yule-planner this year! She has such a wise head on her shoulders. I know that Lotho has been out and about, spending large amounts of money...I'm sure it's going towards the feast!
'I'm sure all those rumours about Lobelia wanting vegetables and tea and an early bedtime for the feast is foolishness. Lobelia is a hobbit, after all...what else could a hobbit ask for than a wonderful feast?
'Well, I'm sure all those tom-fools begging Old Flourdumpling to remove Lobelia from her position are just jealous. You wouldn't happen to be one of them would you?'

'It's a sad day, my friend. Here I thought there would be orders going to and from Bag End with no end when Lobelia was made the Yule-planner, but there ain't been no mail at all; no letters, no provender, no gifts, no nothing.
'Well, Hobbiton will be bad off this year if Lobelia stays in her position. What's to become of the Yule-feast? It's a pity, it is.
'Hey, maybe you could look into her appointment? It smells a bit fishy to me...what with all the ruckus in the Southfarthing, and this Chief buying up land in the Northfarthing. It would be nice to have something to celebrate, and Lobelia being removed from her position would certainly be something to celebrate!'

'Old Lobelia has been pestering the Shirriffs about maintaining order during this year's Yule-feast. Who made her the boss anyway? Well, I suppose Mayor Whitfoot did, but that doesn't mean I have to like it.
'She wants all the inns closed during the feast this year and plans on having tea instead of beer! Can you believe it? Well, open or closed, I'll be sitting right here in The Ivy Bush come Yule.
'Maybe you would ask around and find out how exactly Lobelia managed to worm her way into Old Flourdumpling's good graces?'

'It's hard enough managing a stable in the Shire, but when I heard that Lobelia Sackville-Baggins was made the official Yule-planner this year, I almost climbed on one of my ponies and rode out of Hobbiton as quick as I could. It's a poor joke, if you ask me. What good can come of it?
'Lobelia has all the joy and capacity for pleasantry as a spoiled egg. It smells, I tell you, and the rumours of her plans for the feast smell worse.
'Perhaps you could look into her appointment? There has to be a mistake; I'm sure of it!'

'Shut me down for Yule, that's what she wants to do! Who? Why that Lobelia Sackville-Baggins! She was made official Yule-planner, if you can believe it!
'Why what's a feast without good cheer? And how do you get good cheer without an inn? It's a terrible mistake...it has to be!
'Maybe you would go find out the truth behind these rumours? It's madness, I tell you!'
Inquire among the Hobbiton-folk for an explanation of Lobelia's post as Yule-planner
Search Sandyman's Mill for anything out of the ordinary
Talk to Will Whitfoot
Yuletide Woes
Found an invitation

It appears that Lobelia Sackville-Baggins is the Hobbiton Yule-planner.
<rgb=#FF0000> NOTE: This quest will be removed from your quest log when the current festival ends. </rgb>
'Lobelia took a pony-cart up to Michel Delving maybe a month ago, but that is all I know.'

'I have heard a thing or two, but I am not one to spread rumours.
'But if you have to know, I heard she paid off Old Flourdumpling off in Michel Delving for the position.'

'Lobelia Sackville-Baggins is trying to cheat Hobbiton out of their Yule-feast? I would love to help, but I fear my hands are tied in this matter.
'Lobelia came not a month ago seeking the laws relating to local Hobbiton feasts. If I remember correctly the Hobbiton-law states: Whosoever resides in the Hill at Bag End shall be charged with the planning and coordination of all local feasts and festival-activities and shall preside over said feasts in the absence of the Mayor.
'This law being a holdover from when the Baggins family was the chief residence of the Hill. Because the law was not changed or a new planner appointed, there is simply nothing I can do.'
'I haven't heard aught else save that we're all to eat our vegetables and get a proper nights rest. The cheek of it!'
'Lobelia has been coming and going on festival business, but I haven't heard how she came to the job.'
'Lobelia's post as Yule-planner? No, I haven't heard anything as to how she came by it.'

'I'm sorry, but I haven't heard anything about how Lobelia came by the Yule-planner post.
'Whatever shall we do? Yule will be ruined if Lobelia has her way!'
'The Yule-feast will be simply wonderful this year! The best that has been held for many a long season; leastwise, better than any that old fool Bilbo ever planned, that's for certain.'
'Be off! Can't you see we have a great deal of planning left to do before the Yule-feast?'
'Sorry, I haven't heard anything.'
'Lobelia? I heard she was up to some mischief away in Michel Delving...I'm sure that's how she came by the position.'
'If you need any help looking for information, I might be able to help you after another pint or two.'

'The Yule feast? Why my dad and I were personally invited by Lotho Sackville-Baggins, but why I would tell the likes of you anything more is beyond me.
'Now be off! I have important things to be doing up at the mill without the likes of you snooping about my business.'
You have been asked to inquire among the Hobbiton-folk for an explanation of Lobelia's post as Yule-planner.

Sandyman's Mill is north of the bridge over the Water in Hobbiton.
Ted Sandyman's unusual behaviour might suggest a need to search Sandyman's Mill for anything out of the ordinary.

Will Whitfoot is at the Town Hole in Michel Delving, far to the west of Hobbiton.
You should report your findings to Will Whitfoot, the Mayor of the Shire.

'Well it seems your little plan worked! Fiddlesticks!
'Another party ruined, no thanks to you. Why don't you go tell your good friend Hamfast what you've done here? No doubt he put you up to all this, what with his precious Marigold being sent up here to embarrass me so.'

'So that Lobelia was planning on keeping all the best food for herself and her own? I'm glad that you were able to set things to rights, and so are the rest of the folk here in Hobbiton.
'We only thought it proper to get you something. Lobelia was right, in a way: we don't have much in the way of spare proffer, but we share what we can, especially for those who have given us as much as you!
'We would like you to have this Yule-tree. It's a transplant -- my nephew Halfast brought it down from the Northfarthing. We were going to plant it in the yard, but seeing as how you helped us so...well, Marigold thought it would be best if you took it for your house.'
A Happy Hobbiton

You were able to stop Lobelia's plan to keep all the best Yule-feast food for herself.
<rgb=#FF0000> NOTE: This quest will be removed from your quest log when the current festival ends. </rgb>

Gaffer Gamgee is outside his hole on Bagshot Row at the foot of the Hill.
You should tell Gaffer Gamgee about Lobelia's folied plans.

'Your pardon, friend, but could I beg a favour of you? I have this work order for materials and labour over in the Thorin's Hall community that I need delivered immediately to confirm our work dates with the purchaser. I know this is not much notice, but I can pay you well for your trouble.
'I need you to take this to Rúni over by the gates of the Thorin's Hall community, west of Thorin's Gate. You can't miss it.'

'What is this? Ah, the work order from Tyrvi. Thank you very much! We have been hoping to see this for a few days now.
'Go ahead and bring this work order to Rambi in the market square of the community. While you are there, why don't you take a look around...let me know if you see anything you like!'

'You have a work order from Tyrvi? Has this been signed yet?
'Finally! I've been sitting here on my thumbs for two days now! It's a shameful waste of time, if you ask me, but you can be sure that MY work will be done promptly at least.'
Bring the work order to Rúni
Bring the work order to Rambi

'Ah, forgive me, traveller, could you aid me for a moment? I must deliver an important notice, but I cannot leave Duillond right at the moment.
'I have this order for fine woods in the Duillond community that I need carried immediately to confirm the time of delivery. Could you take this to Barchiril over by the gates of the Duillond community across the river and south at the cross-roads beyond the bridge?
'It should require just a few minutes of your time, and Barchiril should compensate you well for the effort.'

'What is this? Ah, the confirmation from Badennas. Thank you very much! We have been hoping to see this for a few days now.
'Would you be so kind as to bring this to Barthavron for me? He is a craftsman who can usually be found in the market square of the community.
'Should you see a home that might suit your needs while you are inside, please do let me know.'

'My thanks to you. It is good to know that Badennas has completed my order. Our construction of the most recent homes will soon be complete, thanks to her efforts.
'It seems strange to be building new and afresh even as so many of us seek to leave these lands. Be it one year or a thousand, our people still need places to live while they await their time to sail into the West.'
Bring the work order to Barchiril
Bring the work order to Barthavron

'I just need you to take this to Andy Brockhouse over by the gates of the Michel Delving community, south of the town proper.'

'What is this? Ah, the work order from Overhill. Thank you very much! We've been hoping to see this for a few days now.
'Could you do me a favour and take this in to Rolf Bracegirdle? He's a furnishing decorator in the community market square.
'And take a look around while you're there. I don't know if you're looking for a house right now, but you might see something that catches your fancy.'

'It seems that our wood order is finally on its way.
'Thank goodness! My stock is just about gone as it is. I was going to have to start chopping trees myself just to stay in business! Imagine!'

'Excuse me a moment, but could I beg a favour of you? I have this work order for materials and labour over in the Bree community that I need delivered immediately to confirm our work dates with the purchaser. I know this isn't much notice, but I can pay you well for your trouble.
'I just need you to take this to Nan Henwood over by the gates of the community a little ways south-east of here, east of those old ruins.'

'What is this? Ah, the work order from Sarabeth. Thank you very much! We've been hoping to see this for a few days now.
'Say, while you're here, could you take this to Bill Twiggins? He should be in the market square of the community.
'I don't know if you're looking for a house right now, but take a look around while you're there and let me know if anything catches your fancy.'

'What? Today? Where did this come from? Sarabeth? I didn't know this was going to be today! Oh no, Nan's going to kill me....
'Please excuse me. I have some things I need to see to immediately!'
Bring the work order to Nan Henwood
Bring the work order to Bill Twiggins
Building the Bree Homestead
Bree is a small town, but growing everyday due to the travellers coming up the Greenway from the South.

Nan Henwood is near the gates of the Bree homestead, south-east of Sarabeth Lowbanks, east of the old ruins there.
Sarabeth Lowbanks has asked you to deliver a work order confirmation to Nan Henwood.

Bill Twiggins is in the market square of the Bree homestead.
Nan Henwood has signed the work order and asked you to take it to Bill Twiggins.

Glóin is encamped outside the entrance to Goblin-town.
Nogmeldir has asked you to find Glóin and ask for aid finding Glorwen.

'So, Blackfang revealed Glorwen's fate to you before he was himself torn to pieces by his own pack? I deem it a fitting fate for such a monster, but not for poor Glorwen!
'There is but one glimmer of hope that remains -- the hatred of the goblins for my people is such that they will not kill Glorwen if they can help it. They would much rather keep her in endless toil and torment until her will to live breaks and she either loses her mind or dies of her own accord.
'Luckily, Glorwen is no faint maiden to be easily broken by such as they, and thus we may have some time to effect her escape -- but I would not have her suffer a minute longer beneath at the tender mercies of the goblins!
'I have heard that Glóin, a dwarf yet still a friend, has set up a camp outside of Goblin-town. Find him and he will share with you what he knows of the depths and dungeons hidden beneath.'

'Leave me be! Touch me again, and I'll break your arm as I did the last of you filthy beasts who dared try it!'
'Oh! Forgive me! In this eternal darkness one does not come to expect a friendly face at the door...Who are you and how have you come to this hellish place?! Are you a fellow prisoner who has found a means of escape? Or a truly foolish ${RACE} who has come down here of your own accord?
'Never mind -- it matters not. All that matters now is that we free the others and find our escape from this deadly prison, before we meet our ends so far from the light of the stars.'

'They think an Elf is caught within the dungeons down beneath? Goblin-town has re-awoken and I fear there's more than just one trapped in those depths. I do not remember where the dungeons are within, it was a long time ago. It will be up to you to explore and find where they are being kept.'
Down, Down to Goblin-town

Having defeated the Warg pack-leader Blackfang and discovered the likely whereabouts of the missing Elvish hunter Glorwen, you now face the grim task of proceeding into the depths of Goblin-town itself to effect her rescue!
'Hurry, ${PLAYER}! You must find Glorwen in Goblin-town before it is too late!'

Glorwen is imprisoned in Goblin-town.
Nogmeldir has asked you to find and rescue the scout Glorwen.

'As if we'd not enough to deal with here, it seems that a few of Rivendell's scouts have gone astray, somewhere east of here, up in the High Pass. A pair of them that passed through some few weeks ago said there were rumours that a new Great Goblin has arisen in Goblin-town and were going to see if they were true...and make trouble for them if they were.
'Well, there's trouble a-plenty up in these mountains without a pair of flighty Elves stirring up more, mark my words, but go they did, and we've not heard aught from them since. One of my folk went along with them -- a fellow by the name of Eywind -- so they ought to be fine.
'Now that I think about it, Eywind is a bit of a hot-head himself. He went tagging along with the others as he fancied he would find a bit more adventure up in the High Pass, as he put it, so maybe it would be best if you did go take a look and see if they're all right....'

'Ho there friend! What brings one such as you into the frozen peaks of the High Pass?
'Vighar sent you, did he? Good fellow -- well, it turns out we're fine here. Plenty of goblins to go around and the weather's not so bad, once you get used to it.
'Now, we do have quite a few things on the docket, if you will -- that and it seems my skinny friend here has lost his fellow. Glorwen got up here a bit before us, and while she left signs of her safe arrival, we've seen naught of her since. He's a cool one, but I think he's starting to get a bit worried.'
Talk to Eywind in the High Pass
Into the High Pass

Vighar Roadwalker has told you of a trio of scouts sent forth from Rivendell and passed through his camp some weeks ago to scout the eastern reaches of the Misty Mountains, as they rise up into the High Pass. These three -- the Elves Nogmeldir and Glorwen and the dwarf Eywind -- have been tasked with determining the strength of Goblin-town, where it has been rumoured that a new Great Goblin has taken the throne, and may be preparing for war against settlements on either side of the Misty Mountains.
'You should seek out my kinsman Eywind up in the High Pass. He and his companions should be encamped out past Pinnath Fenui, up through Cirith Daur.'
Find Eywind and his companions in the High Pass, through the passage that runs past Pinnath Fenui and through Cirith Daur to the east.

'So you are not happy with your Harvestmath horse? Well, I can offer you an exchange, as I would not want one of my horses where it was not desired. However, this is not a decision to be taken lightly, so I will give you a moment to think about this.
'If you are really sure you want to exchange your horse, speak to me again, and I will give you a receipt in return. You can then exchange the receipt for a different horse.'

'So you have decided you want to exchange your Harvestmath horse after all? So be it. Look over this receipt and tell me if it looks fine to you.
'And this time, I hope you are more sure of your choice. Choosing a horse should not be something done lightly!'
'Have you made up your mind?'

'While you have come far as a Lore-master, ${PLAYER}, and have surpassed the abilities of many, there are those of such ability that none shall ever surpass. They are the Wizards, who were aged and wise when they first came to this Middle-earth and whose knowledge has only grown since then. Their arts lie beyond most understanding, although some insight can be gained from them.
'For instance, it is said that one of the Wizards, Radagast the Brown, resides among the Eglain in their camp near the cursed swamp of Agamaur. He is a friend of the wild and all the creatures of nature speak to him. It might be possible to gain insight into this ability from him, if you but ask him.
'If you would gain such a boon, travel to the Eglain encampment, which lies in the Lone-lands, and speak to Radagast there.'

'I need a favour, friend. I need to rush an order for an important client of mine over to old Clar Whitethorn in Bree-town.
'Clar is the finest taxidermist in Eriador, y'see, but he's an ornery type and doesn't like being rushed. I was hoping you might get this order over to Bree as quick as possible so that he can take the time to do it right.
'Could you see your way to helping me out here?'

'Ah, good day to you ${PLAYER} - I have need of a courier, if you are willing.
'There is a fine taxidermist by the name of Clar Whitethorn in Bree-town with whom I occasionally do business, and I have a new order that I'd like taken to him. This piece is particularly important and I would rather not trust the order to the post in these uncertain times.'

'Say ${PLAYER} do you know a big fellow by the name of Clar Whitethorn, over in Bree-town?
I need to get an order to him for one of my clients as soon as I can. It's important, but I'm afraid it quite slipped my mind until just this morning, and the post won't get it there in time.
I don't suppose you could take this to him for me? It would be a great favour!'

'Hello there ${PLAYER}, fine day isn't it?
'I was going to take a hike over into Bree-town today, but I'm afraid this restocking is taking longer than I thought - but I have an important chore I need taken care of, if you're willing to help.
'I have this important order from a client that I need filled by old Clar Whitethorn, he lives in Bree-town -- one of the finest taxidermists I know, in fact. If you could get this to him, it'd be a great load off my chest.'

'What's this here? An order from one of those furnishers, is it?
'Hmm. Bit of a rush job, isn't it -- they can't never get things set out in a timely fashion, can they? Still, if the price is right, so be it.
'It looks to me like you got the short end of this deal, though. Tell you what: I've got a little left-over something in the back. It's just taking up room now, and I've got new pieces I've got to get to work on, so I'll let you have it for your trouble in coming over here so quick.'

'I would ask that you be careful with your choice this time, though. My father already looks down on these Bree-steeds... I would not wish him to think those that ride them have addled wits.'

'Have you come seeking a steed of your own? I may be able to help you. My father is teaching me to become a Horse-master in my own right someday, but currently the horses I breed lack the stamina his possess. However, they are more tame than my father's horses, so you should be able to ride one, if you so wish.
'I will grant you this boon, though, only in exchange for helping me. My father has made an arrangement with the Stable-masters of Bree. Instead of refunding their money for horses that have proven unusable in their trade, he has offered to do work for them. These tasks usually fall to me, but if you do some of these tasks for me, I will allow you to ride one of my steeds.
'The first task is to bring a sack of grain to Bill Rosewood at the stables near the West-gate of Bree. The grain is over to the east, by the silo.'

'Ah good, you have returned. You have my thanks for doing that for me. I...dislike those tasks and will be happy when the day comes when I can direct another to do such things. A true Horse-master has more to think of than delivering grain or mucking stalls.
'Now, though, to finish our agreement. You have done all that was asked of you, so now I will allow you to ride one of my tame mounts.
'Thank you again, and perhaps when you are more experienced, you can return and try to ride one of my father's mounts. Prepare yourself, though, my father won't let just anyone ride his steeds!'

'Well hello there! Without a word of direction, you come in and muck out one of my stalls. I never get that kind of service from Gaelm! Not that I need much help around here, but if he's trying to live up to the agreement his father put into place, he's not doing too good a job!
'Oh well, perhaps that's something that's learned with time. Anyway, there's nothing else I have to do today, so if you want, you can head on back to Gaelm and tell him all the work is done!'

'So Gaelm got you to do deliver the grain, did he? He has a ways to go if he's going to be half the Horse-master his father is! Never seen a boy try to avoid the less \qpleasant\q tasks that go along with breeding horses as much as Gaelm.
'Oh well, if he fooled you into doing his work for him, who am I to complain? As long as the job gets done!
'So, now that you are here, you'll need to do something else for me. The stalls at both my stables and Bert Goldenleaf's down by the South-gate need mucking out. How about drawing some water from the Boar Fountain in town and taking care of that for me?'

'Good job. Normally I would ask Gaelm to muck out all the stalls, but seeing as you probably didn't know what you were getting into, one will be fine for now.
'That's about all I need of you today, but Bert Goldenleaf's stalls are in about the same shape as mine. Why not go and give them the same treatment? Draw some water from the Boar Fountain and use it on one of Bert Goldenleaf's stalls.'

'We of the Trév Gállorg have long maintained our watch upon the northern plains of Fasach-falroid, but we are too few in these trying times to guard the whole expanse.
'We have seen enough to know what we face: a union of the Orcs of the Ongbúrz tribe and the Angmarim. Separately, they are dangerous, but together, fighting for a common master, I fear they may be unstoppable.
'You must put an end to their alliance, ${PLAYER}. Travel north into Fasach-falroid and defeat Orcs of the Ongbúrz clan and their Iron Crown allies. The city of Dûn Covád, far to the north in the western hills, will surely have many of these foes for you to strike.'
'I greet you in your time of triumph, ${PLAYER}. The Orcs and the Angmarim have been taught that their union will not be permitted. For that, I thank you.'

'Your Fém draws near to its fulfillment, Southron. There is one last warrior you must defeat, and if you prove to have the mastery, you will fight for the Trév Gállorg in Clúcath against the Trév Duvárdain.
'Your opponent is named Nekhtan, and he is the son of the last warrior to engage in Clúcath, the very Clúcath where the Trév Duvárdain listened to their Angmarim masters and violated the rules of the rite. Though he sued for mercy, the mercy that Clúcath should have granted, Nekhtan's father was slain by Avair, warrior of the Trév Duvárdain. That was the act by which we knew the Trév Duvárdain could not be redeemed and were lost to us, though we shared kinship in years gone past.
'There is a great tree to the east of Aughaire, and Nekhtan goes there to train in the skills of combat. Leave Aughaire heading north, then turn east and follow the line of the hills a short distance until you see the great tree in a basin to the north. Defeat Nekhtan and return to me for my judgement.'

'You have defeated Nekhtan, and earned the right to stand for the Trév Gállorg in Clúcath against the Trév Duvárdain. This is a chance for great honour, Southron, and a chance to show our foes that the Trév Gállorg are not to be dismissed so readily.
'We will stand always against them, and you will be the warrior to remind them of our opposition!'

'I have been too long in training here in the wild, stranger, for I have heard naught of your deeds. You have a Fém to earn the right to do battle in Clúcath? That is foolishness. The Trév Duvárdain do not hold by the tenets of that rite; listen to one who knows of these things!
'I have honed my body to a knife's-edge so that I may exact my vengeance upon them and upon their Angmarim masters. I will not willingly stand by while you attempt to take my place in Clúcath, unless you prove to have the mastery.
'We fight! If you deserve the honour of standing against the Trév Duvárdain, you must prove to me that you are the stronger warrior!'
Challenge Nekhtan
Crannog's Fifth Challenge
At the behest of Crannog, you fought and defeated three of Aughaire's strongest warriors for the right to represent the Trév Gállorg in the Clúcath, but one more test remains.

'Nekhtan is filled with a great desire for vengeance on the Trév Duvárdain for the unlawful death of his father in Clúcath, and it drives him to great fury in battle.
'He trains in the skills of battle at a great tree east of Aughaire. Leave the settlement by the north road, and then turn immediately east and follow the line of the hills for a short distance. You will see the great tree in a basin to the north. Defeat Nekhtan and you will earn the right to fight on behalf of the Trév Gállorg in Clúcath.'
'It is the fulfillment of your Fém to stand for us in Clúcath.'
'You will bring glory to the Trév Gállorg.'
'There is no more use for words.'
'Leave me.'

Collected Tasgall's Gift
'You fought bravely and well, ${PLAYER}, and from your actions was Soltakh born.'
'That Fail-á-Khro is ours once again is a joy to me.'
'Long will we remember your deeds in Clúcath, friend ${RACE}.'

'The time of Clúcath is almost upon us, and you must prepare yourself to do battle; despite your prowess against the warriors of the Trév Gállorg, it will not be enough. You need a greater ally: that of knowledge.
'Many among the Trév Gállorg witnessed the unlawful breaking of the rites of Clúcath in which Nekhtan's father was slain, and they may have some words by which you will avoid a similar fate.
'Osbail, by my ruling-seat, can tell you how Násan met his end and perhaps give you some manner of avoiding a similar fate. Camran, at the centre island of Aughaire, will tell you which of the warriors of the Trév Duvárdain you may be facing. Tasgall, hunter of the hill-beasts south-east of Nád Nathair, may have learned something during his sojourn that will be of aid to you. Speak with these three, and any others who may be able to help, and return to me before long. The Clúcath will not wait forever.'

'I salute you, ${PLAYER}! I have not yet returned to Aughaire, for I have been keeping a watch on Nád Nathair to ensure that the hill-beasts do not rise again. Rona will understand.
'You have been chosen as the warrior for the Clúcath? I am frozen with amazement! I believed the death of Násan and the betrayal of the Trév Duvárdain had ended that rite forever. You defeated Nekhtan in single combat? He cannot have been pleased with that; if Avair is chosen as the warrior of the Trév Duvárdain, Nekhtan will see it as a lost opportunity to avenge himself upon his father's murderer.
'I have carved a small figure from the tooth of Murragrath, and I would like you to have it. Carry it among your belongings. Perhaps it will bring you fortune in the trials ahead.'

'I am sure the Trév Duvárdain have not forgotten how you destroyed the standards that flew above Tór Gailvin, and neither have I. I will tell you what I can about what you may face at the Clúcath.
'The warrior who slew Násan and sullied the rite is named Avair, and she is a master of the bloodied arts. She has slain many of our people in the years since the last Clúcath, and her name strikes fear into the hearts of all but Nekhtan, who has sworn to end her. Domongart, leader of the Trév Duvárdain, surely thinks that Nekhtan will be our warrior; he may put forth Avair in the hope that Nekhtan will be blinded with rage and easily defeated. It is difficult to say, and there are others.
'Drostan of the Trév Duvárdain is fierce, but his most recent battle ended in a cowardly retreat; he fought with Fonghala for one day and one night before he escaped. He favours fighting from a distance, and fears the dangers of standing toe-to-toe with an opponent. He is surely hurting for the chance to redeem his honour. Perhaps I have been no help at all, ${PLAYER}. Even so, I hope that you can make use of what I have said.'

'You have taken the wisdom of my people? For your sake and the sake of the Trév Gállorg, I hope you have, Southron.
'The Clúcath will soon begin at Fail-á-Khro. Speak to me when you are prepared, and we will go to meet destiny.'

'I should have known, when you helped me against the Wargs that came to Fasach-larran, that you would bring great honour to the Trév Gállorg. But I fear this may be too much for you, ${PLAYER}. The Trév Duvárdain have already broken the rules of Clúcath once; who is to say they will not do so again?
'Our great warrior, Násan, met Avair of the Trév Duvárdain as the sun rose above Fail-á-Khro. For a time, everything seemed as it should: first Avair had the mastery, and then Násan took the advantage. But as the Clúcath drew on, the chieftain of the Trév Duvárdain, Domongart, became restless. Next to him sat two strangers, Men of Carn Dûm, it is thought.
'Domongart suddenly rose to his feet and gave forth a tremendous cry: a pre-arranged signal? Násan's attention was diverted, and at that moment Avair knocked him to the ground. The Clúcath was over, but Domongart was not satisfied, and he demanded that Avair slay her helpless foe. This she did, and it was clear that the Trév Duvárdain, our kin of old, were hopelessly corrupted. Násan's son, Nekhtan, swore to avenge his father, but you must do it in his place, for you have bested him, and he is not fit to stand for the Trév Gállorg in the Clúcath. Be watchful, ${PLAYER}, when the Clúcath begins. You must be prepared for anything.'

'At last we have been redeemed, ${PLAYER}, and have triumphed over the Trév Duvárdain and their Angmarim masters. Násan has been avenged, and Domongart has paid for his betrayals.
'He who was called Drostan has come to join the Trév Gállorg, but his name is lost; he will be known henceforth as Soltakh, \qHe Who Is Changed.\q She who was called Avair did not accept this choice; she is now neither Trév Gállorg nor Trév Duvárdain. She has done much evil and could only see that in others; though Nekhtan might have forgiven her past, I feel she could not. She wanders now the trackless lands, a woman with neither name nor home.
'Your Fém is at an end, and I salute you not only as chieftain of the Trév Gállorg, but as Crannog, humble tribesman of Aughaire, as well. Perhaps Tasgall's gift brought you good fortune after all, and perhaps it did not. May you decide for yourself whether you believe in it, but believe always in yourself, friend ${PLAYER}. I deem that you make your own fortune.'
Talk to Crannog and travel to Fail-á-Khro

'Prove yourself worthy of being called a friend to the Trév Gállorg of Aughaire. I will give you such a Fém if you do all that I ask of you.

There can be no more hiding and no more flinching from battle. 'I am ready for you, Southron. I have the strength of the aurochs! If you are the one to face the Trév Duvárdain in Clúcath, you must be strong indeed!

'You have done much for us already, ${PLAYER}. Could it be that you might be the warrior we need to best the Trév Duvárdain in Clúcath? It is possible. You will need to defeat Aughaire's strongest warriors if you are to complete this Fém and prove more deserving than they to take on this burden.
'You will find Feradakh at the Búth Luikh, south-east of Crannog's ruling-seat. He is a master of fighting from a distance; you must keep him close, if you can, or he will become a most deadly foe.

You must finish the battle quickly, or she will certainly outlast you; the tale-spinners still speak of her battle with Drostan of the Trév Duvárdain, which lasted a full day and night before he retreated in cowardice.
'Moridac is the aurochs-keeper of Aughaire, and it is said he has the strength and fortitude of the creatures with which he spends most of his days.'
'It is the law of the Trév Gállorg that only the strongest may fight in Clúcath.'
'The Trév Duvárdain will put forth their strongest warrior; we must do the same.'

'This is a dangerous Fém upon which you embark, ${PLAYER}!'
'What tales will echo within the Búth Sánkhas, ${PLAYER}! Tales of Clúcath!'
'Can it be that Clúcath is really going to happen?'
'You must know what happened at the last Clúcath, ${PLAYER}, surely?'
'The memory of the last Clúcath against the Trév Duvárdain is full of sorrow.'

'Long have I served my people as chieftain, and I have given many dozens of Fém to those of age among my people, and to those few travellers I deem worthy of calling friend. It is a heavy burden, for a Fém is not to be granted lightly. If it is beyond the reach of the one to whom it is assigned, the blame falls upon me, as chieftain.
'I give to you now your Fém. I give to ${PLAYER}, ${RACE} from the South, this Fém: to begin the rite of Clúcath, the ancient privilege and burden of the Trév Gállorg. It has been long since the Clúcath has been called, and the memory of the last is grim; but its time has come again. Thus is ${PLAYER}'s Fém given.
'Raith will tell you what this Fém involves, ${PLAYER}. Speak with him at once and begin.'

'I am happy that Crannog has given you a Fém, ${PLAYER}, but I am surprised he has chosen you to begin the rite of Clúcath. In ages past, each of the tribes selected a warrior to fight on its behalf in a ceremonial combat, called a Clúcath. The victorious tribe was understood to become the leader of all the others until such time as another Clúcath was called. It has been many years since the last, during which the Trév Duvárdain violated the laws of mercy required by the ceremony and slew our champion.
'North of Aughaire is a hilltop where the Clúcath has always been held. The place is called Fail-á-Khro. Travel to Fail-á-Khro, and when you reach it, you must turn north-east. After some distance, you will see a line of torches ascending another slope. Atop this final slope lies the Cairn of Honour. Climb the Cairn and retrieve the Stone of Clúcath from atop it, then bring the Stone to Crannog.
'We must trust our chieftain. If he believes that the time has come for Clúcath, he surely has some knowledge we do not.'

'You have taken the Stone of Clúcath. It is now only a matter of time before the greatest warrior of the Trév Gállorg will face the champion of the Trév Duvárdain, and much will be decided.
'The warriors of Búth Luikh will now speak with you concerning tasks with which they desire your aid. Help them if you will, but know that you have another obligation.
'Your Fém is not yet complete.'

'Hill-beasts thrive on the large crawlers that infest Fasach-larran. With enough we might be able to lure Bangrath and Murragrath out of hiding.
'I care not where the crawlers come from, but there are many of them throughout Fasach-larran. Kill crawlers wherever you find them and bring their remains to me. I will prepare a mixture that may seem repulsive to you and me, but will be hard for our foes to resist.'

'The remains of these crawlers are not pleasant to smell or look upon, but trust me when I say they are a delicacy to the creatures we hunt. I will prepare bait from this with which we can draw Bangrath and Murragrath out of hiding.'

Sorkha of the Trév Gállorg is worried about the lesser watching-stones that have been erected in the city of Dûn Covád.

'Somewhere within the city of Dûn Covád are three lesser watching-stones. I need you to find their locations and return to me with this information.
'The city is located far to the north of Aughaire, in the western hills of Fasach-falroid.'
'When we attack the city of Dûn Covád, we will avoid the watching-stones.'
'The watching-stones of Angmar are a deadly menace to the weak-willed.'

Three lesser watching-stones can be found somewhere within the city of Dûn Covád, far to the north of Aughaire, in the western hills of Fasach-falroid.

'Muiráthakh, the Silent Judge, brought a number of warriors with him from Carn Dûm; they protect him and uphold his judgements. While they remain in the city, Donnvail will never be free.
'Look for Iron Crown warriors and crossbowmen in the neighbourhood beyond the eastward arch, ${PLAYER}. Bring your allies and defeat these servants of Muiráthakh.
'We must undermine his rule if Donnvail is to break free from the bonds of Carn Dûm.'
'You have done much to restore the peace of Donnvail, ${PLAYER}, and I thank you for it. The lords of Carn Dûm will learn not to trifle with the Trév Gállorg!'
Defeat Iron Crown warriors (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeat Iron Crown crossbowmen (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
The Minions of Muiráthakh
Muiráthakh, the Silent Judge, commands the loyalty of many warriors sent from Carn Dûm. Artagan wants them eliminated.
'Beyond the eastward arch, the servants of Muiráthakh protect the Silent Judge and his unlawful rulings. Bring allies and make an example of these warriors and crossbowmen who serve him.'
'Donnvail will soon be free, ${PLAYER}. I am sure of it!'
'The lords of Carn Dûm will learn not to trifle with us!'

Iron Crown warriors and crossbowmen can be found in the neighbourhood beyond the arch east of Una's allies.
Artagan wants you to undermine Muiráthakh's rule in Donnvail by defeating his servants.

Artagan is in the city of Donnvail, among Una's allies.
You have defeated many of Muiráthakh's servants and should bring news of your success to Artagan.

'There is great work to be done in Donnvail, ${PLAYER}, and we have need of many allies if we are to carry it out. Artagan, Raghnaid, and Enan have made plans to combat the evil masters that control the city, but it will take many hands and great courage.
'But all can contribute. If your allies are not near at hand, you can still aid our efforts here; bring my message to Branan at the front gate of Donnvail: tell him that we will soon move against our Angmarim masters and all must be made ready!
'We will be here when you return with allies, ${PLAYER}, but until that time you can still aid us; take my message to Branan.'
'Una plans to move against our Angmarim masters? We need many allies, ${PLAYER}! Travel south to Aughaire and tell Crannog of our need!'

'You bring word from our kindred in Donnvail, ${PLAYER}? That they will soon move against the lords that control them is no surprise to me; the Trév Gállorg will not bend forever and will strike back before they break.
'I will send all who can to await the signal, and they will move against Donnvail when the time comes. I urge you to gather allies and go to Una's aid, as well. One ${RACE} will not be enough to defeat the foes arrayed against them, even one so worthy as you.'
A Call for Allies
Una maintains her vigilance within Donnvail and wants you to take a message out of the city.
'Speak with Crannog, ${PLAYER}, far to the south in Aughaire. He must be told of our need for allies.'
'Branan is at the front-gate of Donnvail. Tell him that we will move against our Angmarim masters as soon as we have allies enough!'

Branan is by the front-gate of the city of Donnvail, north-east of Fail-á-Khro.
Una has told you that your allies can aid her in the struggle against Angmar, but if your allies are not near at hand, you can still aid her by bringing a message to Branan.

Crannog is at his ruling-seat west of the central island in Aughaire, south of Fail-á-Khro.
Una and Branan have come to the conclusion that the time to rise against their Angmarim masters has almost arrived, and Crannog should be petitioned for aid in the effort.

'I do not know you, stranger, and it is my Fém, my tribal duty, to know all those who come to these lands.
'If you come in friendship, and are strong in body and spirit, you have nothing to fear. Present yourself to our chieftain, Crannog, and he will find a Fém for you to perform. If you are weak or dull-minded, there is no place for you here. Travel south into the lands of the soft, or go north and find someplace to die.
'Crannog's ruling seat is here in Aughaire, west of the settlement's central island. I withhold my greeting until you have been accepted by Crannog and have a Fém of your own to perform.'

'You have come to Aughaire, but you are not one of us. You are of ${RACE}-kind. If you wish to be counted a friend of the Trév Gállorg, you must undertake a tribal duty, a Fém.
'I may have such a task for you.'
Present Yourself to the Chieftain
A warrior of the Trév Gállorg explained the need to prove yourself to his tribe.
'If you wish to be counted a friend of the Trév Gállorg, you must present yourself to Crannog, chieftain of Aughaire. His ruling seat is west of the centre island.'
'Obey Crannog in all things, for he is most wise.'
'We of the Trév Gállorg are a proud people.'
'It is my Fém to guard the people of Aughaire.'

Crannog's ruling seat is in Aughaire, west of the settlement's centre island.
You have been told by a Trév Gállorg warrior to present yourself to Crannog to be charged with a Fém, a respected tribal duty.

'Your victory has driven the Trév Duvárdain into the north, and my people have retaken Fail-á-Khro, ${PLAYER}. But we cannot yet rest.
'Return to Fail-á-Khro and speak with Cána if you wish to aid us further against the Trév Duvárdain.
'Fail-á-Khro is north of Aughaire, and many of my people hold it against the enemy.'
'Your legend is already growing, ${PLAYER}. May you grow it further by aiding us as we drive the Trév Duvárdain even further into Fasach-falroid!'
Fail-á-Khro Retaken
You have survived the Clúcath, and Fail-á-Khro has been retaken by the Trév Gállorg.
'Fail-á-Khro is to the north, ${PLAYER}. Speak with Cána there if you still wish to aid the Trév Gállorg, even after all you have already done for us.'

Cána is at Fail-á-Khro, north of Aughaire.
The Trév Gállorg have retaken Fail-á-Khro and now seek your assistance to hold it.

'Crannog is waiting for my judgement of your worth? This is no small burden, and I will not make my decision lightly! But I thank him for your attention, for there is something you can do to earn my judgement.
'My brother Tasgall is a hunter of no small worth, but he has not returned from his latest foray into the wild. I ask you to travel north into Fasach-larran and search for my brother.
'Give him your aid, and if he deems you worthy, so too will I, and Crannog will hear of your deeds.'

'My sister sent you? She worries always, despite my assurances. But you are not one of the Trév Gállorg and do not have a Fém!
'I will help you test your strength, and perhaps my task here will go more quickly for it. The hill-beasts of Nád Nathair have proven a savage menace.'
Rona's Concern
Rona is very worried about her brother Tasgall, who travelled into Fasach-larran and has not yet returned.
'My brother Tasgall left Aughaire travelling north, and he has not returned for some days. Go to his aid, if he has need of it, and I will give Crannog my judgement of your worth!'
'You must help me end the menace of the hill-beasts.'
'The hill-beasts must be dealt with.'
'Help Tasgall with his errand, and you will have my well-wishes.'
'Return to me when you have lightened all of Tasgall's burdens.'

Tasgall left Aughaire travelling north and is likely somewhere in Fasach-larran.
Rona has agreed to give Crannog a favourable report of your doings if you render your aid to her brother Tasgall.
Defeated Wargs in Fasach-larran (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Our chieftain is testing you, southron? If you are stout of heart, you will prove yourself worthy. If you are not, I do not lie when I say that coming here will be your greatest mistake.
'Some days past, I was surprised by a pair of Wargs among the foothills north of Aughaire. They are vicious, dangerous creatures, and my escape was made more difficult by my refusal to lead the pair by straight paths to the settlement; but this I would not do!
'But I am fleet of foot and know the land hereabout, and I made it back safely, if winded. But the Wargs are newly-arrived to Fasach-larran, and it will not be long before they make it here. Defeat these dangerous creatures! You will find them not only in Fasach-larran, but also within the fortress of Tór Gailvin, north-east of Aughaire. Whether they guard the Trév Duvárdain there or serve as jailors, I do not know, but I know they must be defeated, either way. If you do this, I will tell Crannog of your victory.'
'You have done very well against the Wargs, ${PLAYER}! I will tell Crannog of your victory and may he be pleased.'
Defeat Wargs in Fasach-larran (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Predators in the Foothills
Osbail had a dangerous escape from Wargs in Fasach-larran, and the encounter impressed upon her the threat the creatures pose to Aughaire.
'The Wargs of Fasach-larran are north of Aughaire, and the fortress Tór Gailvin to the north-east also holds their menace.'
'The Wargs rue the rumour of your footsteps, ${PLAYER}. I know it.'
'The Trév Duvárdain allow the Wargs free passage through Fasach-larran, the fools!'

Wargs can be found in Fasach-larran, the foothills north of Aughaire. They can also be found in the fortress of Tór Gailvin, north-east of Aughaire.
Osbail has asked you to defeat the Wargs that threaten Aughaire from the north, and in return, she will tell Crannog of your efforts.

Osbail is by Crannog's ruling-seat in Aughaire, west of the settlement's centre island.
You have defeated many of the Wargs that prowl Fasach-larran and should report of your success to Osbail.

'We have done very well this day, ${PLAYER}, despite the interference of the Trév Duvárdain. Tell me if you are ready to return to my camp-site; I will not speak of Drostan and his ilk until we are safely out of danger.'

'I have the crawler-remains you gathered, ${PLAYER}; do you smell their awful stench? To the hill-beasts, this odour will be impossible to resist!
'Let us begin our hunt, and we will lure Bangrath and Murragrath from hiding. Keep a watchful eye, for hill-beasts will be drawn to the scent of the bait I carry.'
Talk to Tasgall
Instance: The Matron and the Master
Tasgall's plan is ready, and the two of you must attempt to end the threat of Bangrath and Murragrath.
Tasgall's hunt has brought the two of you to the slopes of Nád Nathair.

'Are you prepared, ${PLAYER}? The rite of Clúcath will determine the fortunes of the Trév Gállorg, but we must be on guard: Domongart has been treacherous in the past, and there is small reason to expect that today will be different.
'But if you are victorious, it will mean much. It must be chanced.'

'The Trév Gállorg have triumphed, ${PLAYER}! You have brought victory to Fail-á-Khro, where sorrow has reigned too long.
'Speak with me when you are ready to return to Aughaire, and we will go.'
'We will return to Aughaire in triumph, ${PLAYER}. When we left it, we left in doubt. We return now with the certainty of victory.'
Talk to Crannog
Watch the Clúcath unfold
Defeat the warriors of the Trév Duvárdain
Instance: The Rite of Clúcath
You have come to Fail-á-Khro to engage in the ceremonial rite of Clúcath on behalf of the Trév Gállorg.
'Leave me be! I have no need of your sympathy! I curse the Trév Gállorg, and you most of all, fool ${RACE}!'
'I do not understand, ${PLAYER}. Why did you spare me? What have I to live for, now that I have been cast from the Trév Duvárdain and my name taken? I am Drostan no longer...but who shall I be now?'
'My heart is at ease, ${PLAYER}. My father has been avenged, and I have upheld the principles of the Trév Gállorg and of Clúcath. I owe you much.'
'You fought well and bravely, ${PLAYER}. It was an honour to stand with you.'
Crannog is waiting to walk with you to the site where the Clúcath will be performed.
The Clúcath is about to begin: Crannog of the Trév Gállorg and Domongart of the Trév Duvárdain are face-to-face.
The Clúcath has begun, but the rules of the rite have not been followed! You must now fight to defend yourself against the enemy, for there will be no mercy.

Crannog is at Fail-á-Khro, waiting to congratulate you on your victory.
You have been victorious in Clúcath and should speak now with Crannog.

'Though I believe that Angmar has not yet recovered Narchuil, soon they will learn somewhat of its keeping, if not from their long search, but from Laerdan himself. The tortures devised by the Enemy can mar the mind as well as the body, and Laerdan holds great knowledge.
'I would lay this task upon you, ${PLAYER}; return to Calenglad in Evendim and seek Laerdan. It may be that his time in Middle-earth has already been brought to an untimely end, but I have my doubts against it, for Laerdan is strong and wilful, and would not easily betray his purpose by force.
'Go quickly to Calenglad in Evendim and find any tidings that you may of Laerdan, be they good or ill.'

'Hail, ${PLAYER}! It is well that you have returned, though it be under such circumstances. Word has come before you: an Elf-messenger out of the House of Elrond, bore tidings that you have come to seek the fate of Laerdan.'
Book 12, Chapter 1: Elrond's Request
You have returned out of the wilds of Tâl Bruinen with news that brings concern to Elrond of Rivendell.

'Calenglad still maintains most of his men at Tinnudir, off the western shore of lake Nenuial.
'Go with haste; ${PLAYER}! Laerdan may not be long for Middle-earth.'
'Calenglad is wise in his fashion; I trust that he will be able to help you discover the fate of Laerdan.'

Calenglad is at Tinnudir, off the eastern shore of Lake Nenuial, in Evendim.
Elrond has asked you to return to Calenglad and begin a search for the Elf-lord Laerdan.

'You must not tarry here long, though your presence comforts me in my grief, for you possess something that the Wise must take upon themselves as a burden.
'Make haste to Rivendell, ${PLAYER}, and do not forget Narucham in your tale, for his deeds should be accounted among the valiant of these dark times.
'Hurry now, for Elrond must know of Narchuil's fate.'
<rgb=#FF0000>You will automatically travel to Rivendell in the Trollshaws when you accept this quest.</rgb>

'I am troubled, ${PLAYER}, not only for the fate of Narchuil, but for Laerdan as well.
'He has faced many hardships, but because of his boldness, the Enemy has not been able to recover Narchuil, and for that he has drawn their wrath. But that does not excuse his words at the Council, and his actions have troubled me.
'His anger is hot within him, and I will not seek to make another council as of yet. Return to me when his heart has cooled, for it is fitting that the one who gave him his freedom should be his emissary.'

'So, Narchuil has been broken. This is strange news indeed! I was right to doubt that the Enemy had recovered their full strength, but this...it is something that had not entered into my counsels before now.
'Not long before you arrived, Laerdan awoke from his dark dreams. He must be questioned about this, for surely he had some knowledge of it. He has studied the ring Narchuil and the deeds of Amarthiel more closely than any among the Wise.
'A council of the Elf-lords must be called and doom proclaimed, for we must decide what will be done with the ring Narchuil.'
Speak with Elrond in Rivendell
Speak with Elrond to attend his Council
Speak with Elrond in his library
Book 12, Chapter 10: Half-truths
You discovered in Barad Dúrgul that Narchuil had been partially unmade and that it lies now in two pieces, only one of which was held at Barad Dúrgul.
'Narchuil has been broken...return to Elrond with this news at once!'
'Did you give Elrond my tidings of Narchuil?'
'What did Elrond's Council have to say regarding Narchuil?'

'Are you ready, then, ${PLAYER}? I will call together the Elf-lords, and the council will begin.
'Would that the wisdom of Lord Celeborn and Lady Galadriel were at our disposal.'
<rgb=#FF0000>This is a Solo quest, and cannot be completed with a Fellowship.</rgb>
'They have no right to judge me in this, or to deny me!'
'I fear for the heart of Laerdan.'

Elrond is at Rivendell in the Trollshaws.
Gwathryn told you to take the half of Narchuil which you recovered to Elrond.

Elrond is at Rivendell in the Trollshaws.
When you are ready to attend the Council of Narchuil, you should speak again with Elrond.
<rgb=#FF0000>This is a Solo quest, and cannot be completed with a Fellowship.</rgb>

Elrond is at Rivendell in the Trollshaws.
You should speak at once with Elrond.
Collected Amarthiel's Command

'The Enemy has not been idle in your absence. A great host has removed to Angmar, or so their trail led that way, for we did not follow them long, believing it to be some trickery or ill deed.
'Of the fate of Laerdan I have heard no word. My scouts have reported that a number of Amarthiel's servants have been making furtive movements around Annúminas; maybe it is that one of them holds a clue to what you seek.
'Go and defeat the Angmarim that still plague the city of Annúminas. One of them must know something of Laerdan.'
'What have you there, orders from the Enemy? This might be of some help....'
'Have you found any news of Laerdan, ${PLAYER}? One of the Angmarim that still plague Annúminas may hold the clues you seek.'
Search defeated Angmarim at Annúminas
Bring Amarthiel's Command to Calenglad
Book 12, Chapter 2: Unfit Fate
All is not well in Annúminas, according to Calenglad. The Angmarim are acting feverishly within the ruined city, and a large force also returned to Angmar.
'One of Amarthiel's servants that still plague Annúminas may hold the clue you seek.'

Angmarim can be found throughout Annúminas.
Calenglad has suggested that you may find some information about Laerdan's whereabouts among the Angmarim.

Calenglad is at Tinnudir, north of Annúminas.
You should return to Calenglad with Amarthiel's Command.

'It seems that there is a chance that Laerdan yet lives! It is well that Laerdan's life has not been squandered at the treacherous hands of the Angmarim, but what have they learned from him?
'I fear now the folly of allowing the unhindered passage of the Enemy out of our lands. But for good or ill that deed has been done, and now you must make all haste to Barad Tironn with trusted companions, for there lies the last hope of Laerdan. Once his usefulness to the Enemy has been served, his life will be forfeit, unless they have some other evil contrived for him.
'Hurry now to Barad Tironn. My scouts have reported to me that most of the Angmarim have removed from that place, and now only a small contingent remains behind to spoil and lay waste, believing in their folly that we will not return. Speak with Forchon when you are ready to leave.'
<rgb=#FF0000>This quest is meant for a fellowship. If you choose to undertake this quest solo you will receive an inspiration bonus, but the challenge will be great.</rgb>
'Laerdan lives, but has been taken away? You have learned much that I have feared in my heart already, ${PLAYER}. That is yet another set-back for us to consider....'
Speak to Forchon and enter Barad Tironn
Book 12, Chapter 3: Barad Tironn
The orders you recovered from the Angmarim contain clues as to the whereabouts of the Elf-lord Laerdan.
'Forchon will be able to bring you to Barad Tironn, ${PLAYER}. Go quickly! I have many things to consider while you are on your errand.'
'You did well at Barad Tironn. Go now and report to Calenglad.'

'Are you ready to enter Barad Tironn? Calenglad bade me lead you unseen into that place.'
<rgb=#FF0000>This quest is meant for a fellowship. If you choose to undertake this quest solo you will receive an inspiration bonus, but the challenge will be great.</rgb>
'All of your valour will be needed to save Laerdan, ${PLAYER}.'

Laerdan may still be at Barad Tironn in Annúminas.
Calenglad has instructed you to accompany Forchon to Barad Tironn to continue the search for Laerdan.
Forchon can be found in Tinnudir, off the western shore of Lake Nenuial, in Evendim.
<rgb=#FF0000>This quest is meant for a fellowship. If you choose to undertake this quest solo you will receive an inspiration bonus, but the challenge will be great.</rgb>

Calenglad is at Tinnudir, off the western shore of Lake Nenuial, in Evendim.
You should speak with Calenglad and tell him of your deeds at Barad Tironn.

'When you left here in pursuit of Laerdan, I sought counsel of my own, and I sent ahead scouts led by Gwathryn, one of the greatest trackers left here, to my northern company.
'Go as swiftly as you might to Tármunn Súrsa, east of Carn Dûm. That is where you should find what you seek. The more urgent is your quest now that it is known Laerdan lives. Freeing him would be a mighty blow to the Enemy and would hearten those that fight against them.'
<rgb=#FF0000>You will automatically travel to Tármunn Súrsa in Angmar when you accept this quest.</rgb>

'Hail, ${PLAYER}! Calenglad told me that soon you would follow. It is well that you have come so soon.
'It was not long before we were able to find the trail of the host that departed Evendim, for they were many and feared no pursuit. They were many days ahead of us and were travelling with all speed back to their accursed fortress.
'Thus they came within sight of its walls before we were upon them, and I saw not the Elf Laerdan.'
Book 12, Chapter 4: In Pursuit of the Enemy
Calenglad has sent ahead Gwathryn, one of the most skilled men of his company, to Tármunn Súrsa to spy out the ways of the Enemy.
'You should seek out Gwathryn at once, at Tármunn Súrsa in Angmar.'
'It is well Calenglad sent someone as brave as yourself, ${PLAYER}.'

Gwathryn is in Tármunn Súrsa, east of Carn Dûm, in Angmar.
Calenglad has sent you to speak with Gwathryn, one of his scouts in Angmar.
Collected Angmarim staves (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'The Hillmen of Angmar are a wild folk and prone to superstition. The priests and priestesses of the cult of the Angmarim are able to use honeyed words to exert a great influence over them.
'If we are to win the war against Angmar, we must put a halt to the confusions of the Enemy. The priests of Angmar must not be allowed to spread their evil lies.
'You will find them near the altars throughout the Bails of Himbar to the west. Bring me back five of their staves as proof of your deed.'
'Well done, indeed. Hopefully, this will keep Angmar at bay for a while longer.'
'Where are the staves I asked for? Do you not wish to help us defeat Angmar?'
Collect Angmarim staves (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring staves back to Maerchiniath in Gath Forthnír
Cease and Desist
The priests and priestesses of the cult of Angmar have a strong influence over many of the Hillman-tribes.
'Have you confronted all the priests and priestesses of Angmar in the Bails? If not, you should continue at once!'

The priests and priestesses of Angmar can be found near the altars throughout the Bails of Himbar, which lie to the west of Gath Forthnír.
Maerchiniath has instructed you to go forth and defeat the priests of Angmar, bringing him their staves as evidence of your success.

Gath Forthnír is to the east of Himbar.
You should return to Maerchiniath with the staves you took from the priests of Angmar.

'You have done well so far, but I have need of your services a bit further. There is a nearby cavern area where the merrevail live. They are led by one of the evil morroval-lieutenants, if such a word applies.
'Her name is Iarvael, and she haunts us even in our dreams. Please remove her threat once and for all, then return to me when the deed is done.
'This will be no small task, and you should gather one or two of your friends to help you, ${PLAYER}.'

'You have done the Rangers of Gath Forthnír a great service. You have allowed us to stop taking the defensive posture.
'We must take this fight to Carn Dûm!'
Cries of the Host
Himbar is haunted by the merrevail and their kindred, the bats. These creatures prey upon the Rangers of Gath Forthnír, showing no mercy.
'If you desire to assist us in our plight, journey west and find the cavern and defeat Iarvael.'

The merrevail hunt throughout Himbar, the lands west of Gath Forthnír.
Thoriel has asked you to remove the lieutenant, Iarvael, from the morroval caverns.

Thoriel waits for you in Gath Forthnír, the hidden Ranger-camp east of Himbar.
You have defeated Iorvael and should now return to Thoriel with news of your victory.

'The text you recovered told of an alliance between Angmar and the Dourhands. Our scouts tell us that an emissary of the Dourhands has come to treat with Angmar.
'You should investigate the matter. There have been many reports of dwarves near the tower of Minas Angos near Barad Gúlaran. We must stop this alliance from happening, no matter the cost.
'Defeat the emissary, Laugi Goldentongue, then return back to me when the deed is done. If you are to succeed, you should take allies.'
'The downfall of the Dourhands' emissary will be sure to sever the alliance between these two evil powers. Well done, ${PLAYER}.'
Enter Minas Angos and defeat the emissary of the Dourhands.
Laugi Goldentongue, Emissary of the Dourhands
Having discovered a pledge from the Dourhands, you must enter Minas Angos and defeat their emissary to stop an alliance between them and the Iron Crown.
'Laugi Goldentongue must be defeated, else the Iron Crown and the Dourhands will forge a stronger alliance.'

Minas Angos is a tower in Barad Gúlaran, south of Gath Forthnír.
You must travel to Barad Gúlaran and defeat Laugi Goldentongue, the emissary of the Dourhands, inside Minas Angos. Brúnfair suggested you take allies.

Brúnfair is at Gath Forthnír, north of Barad Gúlaran.
Having defeated Laugi Goldentongue, you should return to Brúnfair and tell him of your victory.

You have retrieved a piece of paper written by the hand of a dwarf. As you read the scrap of paper, it becomes clear that you have waylaid a messenger of Angmar.
'...it is with dire urgency that I travel to your land. The forces arrayed against us are too great. We must form an alliance, if the Dourhands and Angmar are to survive....'
Reading this grave news, it becomes clear that this must be shown to someone in Gath Forthnír immediately.

'You have found what? This is dark news indeed if the Dourhands have come to pledge themselves to Angmar. We must not let this happen.
'You have taken a key first step by defeating Angmar's messenger, but we must not let the Dourhands continue to remain here. We must stop this alliance at all cost!
'I think I have a plan....'
'I am sorry, I would help you if I could, but without the parchment you speak of, there is little I can do.'
Speak to someone at Gath Forthnír who would know about these pledges.
Pledge of the Dourhands
You have found a scrap of paper indicating that the Dourhand dwarves and Angmar seek to strengthen their alliance.

Someone in Gath Forthnír will surely be interested the information you uncovered.
You have acquired information about Angmar's allies and plans. You should immediately inform someone of this development.

'The text you recovered told of an alliance between Angmar and the goblins of Goblin-town. Rumour has been told that Angmar and Goblin-town have had troubles entreating in the past. It is strange to find the goblins here. Perhaps this emissary is here without the knowledge of his leaders.

'It seems that he fears an imminent attack upon the town by Orcs out of the North Downs, and is asking for any able-bodied warriors to aid them as soon as possible.

'So you're off to aid Captain Trotter in Trestlebridge are you? We'll be sorry to see you go, but hopefully you can do as much good there as you have for us here.'
<rgb=#FF0000>WARNING: Completing this quest will immediately send you to Trestlebridge in the North Downs.</rgb>
Trouble at Trestlebridge

Frideric the Elder has received an urgent request from an old companion of his -- Captain Trotter of Trestlebridge -- requesting any aid that he might muster from Ost Guruth in staving off a threatened Orkish incursion upon the town.
Speak with Captain Trotter and see what aid you can offer him!

Speak with Frideric in Ost Guruth to arrange a fast mount to Trestlebridge.
<rgb=#FF0000>WARNING: Completing this quest will immediately send you to Trestlebridge in the North Downs.</rgb>

'Greetings ${PLAYER}, as glad as I am to have more help here given how things are going, we have need of more experienced warriors, and I would not see you needlessly slain on our behalf.
'Nonetheless, I have received a missive from an old friend of mine - Constable Bram Ashleaf - out in the Lone-lands. It seems that the usual lawlessness out there has become unmanagable, and he is looking for brave souls to aid him in bringing it back under control. I can at least provide you with a quick mount for the journey should you wish to try your luck at the Forsaken Inn, where he is quartered?'

'So, you've decided to go lend a hand to Constable Ashleaf?
'That's just as well - things are getting dicey around here and I wouldn't want to see a promising hero such as yourself cut down before you're ready to face the darkness that's looming over Trestlebridge.'
<rgb=#FF0000>WARNING: Completing this quest will immediately send you to the Forsaken Inn in the Lone-lands - getting back is another matter...</rgb>

'What do you want, ${PLAYER}? Have you returned to gloat that you were chosen as the warrior to fight in Clúcath against the Trév Duvárdain? The vengeance for which I have trained so long has been stolen from me!
'I am sorry. I see the wisdom in it, though it be hard. It is the way of my people that the strongest warrior should take the heaviest load, and you have proven yourself the master. I must put the needs of the Trév Gállorg before my own vengeance.
'Tell Raith, at Crannog's ruling-seat, that I am at ease. Go forth to the Clúcath with my blessing, friend ${RACE}.'

'You have taken it upon yourself to make peace with Nekhtan? That is good, ${PLAYER}. I know now what I only believed before: Crannog was right to give you this Fém. You truly are a friend to the Trév Gállorg.'
An Understanding
Nekhtan was upset that you were chosen to engage in Clúcath against the Trév Duvárdain, seeing it as the loss of his chance for vengeance.

'I have set my anger aside, ${PLAYER}. I no longer have any ill will toward you. Give this news to Raith, that I am satisfied with Crannog's choice of warrior for the Clúcath.
'You will find Raith at Crannog's ruling-seat in Aughaire.'
'We understand each other, ${PLAYER}.'
'I am sorry for my anger, ${PLAYER}. It was misplaced.'

Raith is at Crannog's ruling-seat, west of the centre island of Aughaire.

'It is a hard time here in Angmar. I miss the warmth of my home. The sooner we stop the Angmarim, the sooner we can leave this accursed place! I need you to help me as you are helping the others.
'There are many fell spirits in Imlad Balchorth, and they give rise to more wights for Angmar's army. Let us thin their numbers, shall we? It gives me a chill that they even exist!
'If we can reduce their number, perhaps we can make our way back to friendly lands more quickly.'
'You have lessened my burden and helped me to sleep better at night, I hope. Thank you, good ${RACE}. I look forward to working with you again!'
Defeat fell spirits in Imlad Balchorth (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Banish the Spirits

'The fell spirits of Morgoth dwell in Imlad Balchorth...I fear we will never escape this place unless they are banished.'

'You are a brave soul, but this next task I ask of you is no small achievment and requires the staunchest of allies! The fell spirits and wights of Imlad Balchorth are terrible, but pale in comparison to their masters.
'I will need you to make your way to the far western depths of Imlad Balchorth and hunt the Gaunt-men. They are responsible for this raising of the Dead and must be stopped if we are to escape this horrid place!
'Go west with your fellows and destroy this menace, then return to me!'

'Impressive! You are a great ${CLASS}, indeed, to accomplish such deeds. They will sing songs of you one day, I am sure of it!
'Thank you so very much. Perhaps soon I can return to my home.'

'Go west and find the Gaunt-men and destroy them. Hurry...and bring your friends!'

'They haunt my dreams! I want off of this forsaken rock and back under my own. Please help, good friend, and eliminate those shambling wights. Thin their number, and perhaps our guards will no longer have to deal with the threat of them every night.
'They lie in wait to the west in Imlad Balchorth. Destroy as many wights there as you can, then return to me. I do not know why we ever came to this abominable land -- there is no wealth in this waste -- but I want out, even if it means cutting down every walking corpse in Angmar!'

'Wha? Huh? Another book? How many of these books are there? For goodness sake, I'm never going to get any sleep!
'Well let's get this over with. Speak to me again if you want to complete Book XI.'

'Some days ago our bravest scout leave to spy upon the Orcs as they travel through the pass.
'He sent message that he found something worse - a dark cleft filled with evil bat-creatures he has not seen before... but that is last we hear from him.
'Can you find our scout? See that he is safe? He had small camp hidden high up along wall of the valley to the east - if he lives you find him there.'

'Chief Tuokki send you to help me? Could have sent someone bigger, I think...but I am hurt and will take your help gladly!
'Evil things gather here in Ram Dúath. More evil than Orcs, more evil than Men who serve dark lords. I shall tell you of them!'
In the Dark Clefts

Chief Tuokki has asked you to seek out one of the Earth-kin -- a scout who was sent into the next valley to spy upon a band of deadly bat-women who have made lair somewhere in the hidden clefts of the Ram Dúath. The Chief informed you the scout had a small camp hidden high up along the wall of the valley to the East.

'Thank you again my friend for your assistance. Now I have the perfect bouquet, fit for the stunning beauty of the woman I want to impress. If you don't mind, I would like to impose upon you once more. Could you please deliver my gift? I cannot chance accidently meeting her.
'While I'm sure of the address on the Scholar's Stair, please find out which of the houses on the road belong to my sweet lady by asking Barliman Butterbur, the proprietor of The Prancing Pony. He is knowledgeable in the goings-on within Bree and he surely would know where she lives. Please check with him before delivering the bouquet.'

'So, my friend, I hear you are assisting Master Crabapple with a few things. He has sent ahead a description of the lovely lady, and I approve. I know what lady he's showing a fancy for. The poor fellow is simply too shy.
'Well, take me for a ninnyhammer! What with all the customers and business, I've plumb forgotten where her house is. Oh, wait! Now I recall...
'Follow the road outside the Pony towards the West-gate and turn left up the Scholar's Stair. Her house will be either the first or second door after the first bridge. There should be a vase nearby...it will serve as a perfect container in which to place the gift.'

'Wonderful! You've returned! I trust you delivered the flowers to my sweet lady?
'I feel my heart welling up with excitement for the moment she finds my gift!'

'Good heavens! The bouquet was delivered to the wrong address! I know for sure that the beautiful woman does not have cats.
'Oh dear, I should have been more detailed in my description. She definitely lives on the Scholar's Stair. Would you please pick up the bouquet from the wrong door and ask her neighbours for the correct address?'

'My name is Fern, Fern Coppersmith. Have you been looking for me all this time?
'How lovely! Avery Crabapple made this beautiful bouquet just for me? That is simply the sweetest thing anyone has ever done. Between the two of us, I must admit that I've been watching him as well, hoping that he would say something. If it doesn't sound too forward, I was hoping he would get past his shyness to speak with me. In fact, I even sent him some sweets I made. Since he didn't mention them to you, I can only assume that I must have delivered them to the wrong address as well.
'If I could ask for a small favour, could you please collect the sweets for me and deliver them to poor Avery? I certainly hope he enjoys them.'

'Goodness! Those sweets are for me from the beautiful and generous Fern? This is fate, my friend.
'How funny that both of us delivered gifts to one another and both sent them to the wrong address. I suppose all this nervousness and anxiety could have been avoided if I just spoke with her in the first place.
'I thank you so much for helping us. When I'm done with my tasks, I will have to go and speak with her in person, now that I have the courage! Thank you again!'

'Greetings, friend! I was wondering if you could help me, as I am in a precarious position. I have found that my affections for a particular woman have grown into something I can no longer ignore. She is the beautious flower amongst the weeds. She walks in my dreams and the sound of her voice is a melodious tone that bards could sing about for the ages. Of course, there is a slight bump in the road. I have not actually spoken to her. I simply cannot muster the courage to approach the lovely woman, as I have only watched her from afar walking around town. What would I say? I fear I would only make a terrible first impression.
'This is where my request comes in, for I have a brilliant plan to woo the woman of my dreams. Please, would you go and collect three types of flowers from all over Eriador... only the best for my sweet lady. Bring them back to me, and I will create the most beautiful bouquet a lady could want. I only need three varieties of flower for the bouquet. I will need a Marigold, a Violet, and a Primrose.
'Marigolds can be found near the stone circle outside Michel Delving, violets near the stone circle beyond the Bree West-gate, and primroses near the stone-circle outside Celondim in the Blue Mountains. Take care and return as quickly as you can!'

'Excellent! You have managed to find the perfect blooms to help make the perfect bouquet for my sweet lady. You have a wonderful eye for flowers!
'I truly appreciate all your help in finding these rare flowers. I will go ahead and create a beautiful bouquet worthy of the woman of my dreams. I am confident that this is the way to her heart!'

'Hello again! Did you forget where to find those flowers? I will need marigolds, violets, and primroses. I hope you find them soon, as I cannot wait to create a beautiful bouquet worthy of the woman of my dreams!'
