'Gertheryg are some of Angmar's most terrible minions. Great troll-like creatures, they are cunning, skilled with arms and armour, and are not affected by the light of the Sun as other trolls are.
'We have observed parties of gertheryg moving back and forth from a worm-infested cave named Ologfil in the vile Malenhad. I sent a scout, Bethad, to find out what he could of the place, but he has not returned, and I fear the worst.
'Please go and explore the cave, perhaps you can find Bethad within. I fear that it would be most unwise to explore this cave alone, so you should go with what allies you can gather.'
'So Bethad was captured by a gorthorog captain? His lack of caution is far from commendable, but it is good to know that he is safe now. My thanks to you foreigner.'
Find Bethad in Ologfil
Speak with Fonn in Tyrn Lhuig
Ancient Lair
Fonn has learned that Gertheryg have been seen travelling to the cavern of Ologfil in Malenhad. He has sent a scout to investigate, but the scout has not returned.
'I fear that something has become of Bethad in Ologfil. I would ask that you go there and search for him.'
Fonn has asked you to explore the caves of Ologfil in Malenhad to the north of Tyrn Lhuig, to determine the fate of Bethad who was investigating the presence of gertheryg.
Speak with Fonn in Tyrn Lhuig and tell him of Bethad's rescue.
You have discovered Bethad's prison!
You have defeated Ulkrank!
You have freed Bethad!
'What valour you have shown to come so far into peril for my sake! I and my family shall be forever in your debt - now quickly, let us be away from this horrible place.'
Find Bethad in Ologfil
Defeat Ulkrank
Free Bethad from his imprisonment
Instance: Ancient Lair
Fonn has learned that gertheryg have been seen travelling to Ologfil in Malenhad. He has sent a scout to investigate, but the scout has not returned.
The hillman Bethad must be somewhere in this foetid cave - whether he could possibly be alive or not is anyone's guess.
Bethad has been imprisoned by the gorthorog war-leader Ulkrank, who must be slain before the scout can be safely freed.
With the death of Ulkrank, you should be able to free Bethad from his prison and escape from the dark lair of Ologfil.

'Hello again, ${PLAYER}. I wanted to thank you for your help. I've gone ahead and sent a note over to Miss Coppersmith, and we will be meeting for tea later today. I couldn't have done it without you!
'In the meantime, please let me introduce you to my friend, Gredlan Mugwort. He has come up with a wonderful plan. He thinks that if we work together, we can create bouquets and gifts for suitors to give their sweethearts.
'We would appreciate it if you would go out and pick more of those lovely flowers; you can come back and trade them in to Gredlan in exchange for a wonderful present. We look forward to seeing what flowers you bring back! You can pick all the blooms from flower patches around the areas where you found the flowers I asked for. Violets are found most often in Bree-land, primroses in Ered Luin, and marigolds in the Shire.
'Do not worry if you feel as if you do not have enough time to find all the flowers you need today. You can always come back tomorrow and try again!'
Collect as many flowers as you can in one hour
A Fistful of Flowers
'Flowers grow everywhere, really...if you know where to look.'

After the success of courting the lovely Fern Coppersmith, Avery Crabapple has decided to partner with a friend of his, Gredlan Mugwort. Together they will create lovely gifts and flower arrangements for suitors.

Patches of violets can be found in Bree-land. Patches of primroses can be found in Ered Luin. Patches of marigolds can be found in the Shire. Gredlan Mugwort is in Bree-town.
Avery Crabapple has asked you to collect flowers from throughout Bree-land, Ered Luin, and the Shire and bring them to Gredlan Mugwort.

'Now that we have the clover, it must be brewed! The only place in the whole Shire which makes Bullroarer's Brew is the Golden Perch. The original recipe was made by Bandobras himself and passed down from inn-keeper to inn-keeper at the Perch; they have been making it for over two hundred and fifty years!
'The clover is one of the main ingredients and also what gives it its green colour. Bring the clover you collected to Gunderic Grubb at the Golden Perch, and you should have some Bullroarer's Brew before the day is out.
'The Golden Perch is located in Stock. Hurry back as soon as you can with the Bullroarer's Brew.'
'Hullo, friend, my name is Tobias Brockhouse, official Inn League Games-master; can I help you with something?'

'I just received a fresh batch of Bullroarer's Brew from Gunderic Grubb. Thank you, ${PLAYER}.
'You have paid your respects...now for the Bullroarer's Challenge! You have heard of the Bullroarer's Challenge, haven't you? Every year the Took family hosts the Bullroarer's Challenge here in Brockenborings, some Hobbits like young Belgo practice all year for the event!
'Speak with Tobias Brockhouse, just east of Brockenborings. He will explain the rules to you. If you complete the Bullroarer's Challenge, return to me, and I will reward you with a special prize!'
'More clover! And just as we were running short. Thank you, ${PLAYER}. You are doing the Bullroarer proud, you are!'
'If only I had more clover....'
Deliver the clover to the Golden Perch
Place Bullroarer's Brew by the statue

'Welcome! Are you here to pay your respects to the Bullroarer? Bandobras 'Bullroarer' Took...he is my ancestor, you know, and the greatest hero of the Shire. A long time ago, an army of goblins invaded the Shire...goblins, of all things!
'Well, the Bullroarer, he wouldn't stand for it, no sir. He gathered all the Tooks and other brave hobbits he could muster and rode out on his horse against them. You heard me right, ${PLAYER}, a horse, a full-growed horse! The Bullroarer was four-foot-five, as the family records tell, and could ride a horse just like the Big Folk.
'Every spring we honour his memory by holding The Feast of the Greenfields. We usually place tankards of Bullroarer's Brew, Bandobras's favourite drink around his statue, but so many folk have come out this season that we are completely out of clover, one of the main ingredients. You wouldn't be able to go out and get us more clover, would you, my good ${RACE}? The clover only grows on the Greenfields, north of Brockenborings.'
'You gathered the clover we need? Excellent! We should have more Bullroarer's Brew in no time!'
'Have you found the clover yet, ${PLAYER}? It grows in the Greenfields, north of here.'
Collect clover (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring the clover to Sigismond North-took
Bullroarer's Brew

The most popular part of the Shire's Spring Festival is the consumption of large quantities of beer, especially Bullroarer's Brew.
<rgb=#FF0000> NOTE: This quest will be removed from your quest log when the current festival ends. </rgb>
'This is my favourite holiday!'

The Greenfields are north of Brockenborings in the Shire.
Sigismond North-took has asked that you collect clover used for making Bullroarer's Brew.

Sigismond North-took is in Brockenborings, south of the Greenfields.
You should bring the clover you collected to Sigismond North-took.

'Hullo there, my young ${RACE}, have you come to have a look around, or perhaps you're looking to make a donation to our worthy Mathom House? We accept all sorts of mathoms you know, it's amazing the odds and ends that Hobbits young and old have managed to collect and what you can see here runs the whole gamut! If you ask me, this old museum says more about us Hobbits than any book or story could hope to tell.
Right now we're looking for mathoms that have been given as gifts for some kindness or aid rendered. The stories behind such objects are of great interest to us, regardless of what the mathom itself might be. Anything you could bring us along those lines would be a fine gesture indeed.'

'What's that there? You received this mathom as a gift from one of our fellow hobbits? Ah, this is a fine thing indeed, an ancient tradition -- well, as old as any of them I know of at any rate. You're sure you have no need for it? Fine, fine then, I'll happily take it and see if I can find a suitable place for it in our collection!'
'Haven't come across anything interesting of late have you? No? Ah well, that's fine though -- feel free to have a look around.'
Bring your gift mathoms to Greylond Bottomley

'Welcome, ${PLAYER}, my fellow Expert Treasure Hunter. Ours is a secret club, and we permit only the most skilled to practice our art. At any rate, the unskilled do not seem to last very long!
'I have assumed the name \qPonto Oats\q for the duration of my stay here in Oatbarton, for it is a name that draws no attention to itself. Where I walk, the shadows hide me and leave no memory of my passage! That's the sort of thing you need to learn, ${PLAYER}.
'But enough about that, because there is work to be done! The village of Dwaling is a short distance from here, and it has been occupied by ruffians! They are led by someone called \qThe Chief,\q and many strong Men serve him. One in particular, the Chief's main enforcer, is a hulking brute wielding a deadly club. He chased many of the inhabitants of Dwaling from their homes when the brigands arrived. We will do something about this brute, friend ${PLAYER}. Speak to me when you are ready to hear my plan.'
'You did passably well, ${PLAYER}. You didn't demonstrate a great deal of flair, but I suppose you got the job done. You can keep the club, if you like.'

A burglar named Ponto is somewhere in Oatbarton, the hobbit-village on the very northern border of the Shire, almost in Evendim.

'The village of Dwaling is just down the slope, ${PLAYER}, and it is full of brigands. One of the Chief's Men wields a deadly club; without this weapon, I warrant he would not be a match for even a single ${RACE}!
'Some of the brigands remain on guard, but many of the villains are sleeping by the fires near Pearlina Gamgee's house. Sneak up to those sleeping; their leader's club is likely on the ground by his resting place.
'Seize the club and return to me, ${PLAYER}! But do not engage in battle! If you are seen by even one of the Chief's Men, our task ends in failure!'
'You did it, ${PLAYER}! We'll make an Expert Treasure Hunter out of you yet! You must give me details of the recovery while we return to Oatbarton.'
'Let us be off, friend ${PLAYER}! I look forward to the tale of your deeds this night!'

'Kol at your service! Things were looking rather hopeless around here, but with you about, perhaps we will stand a chance of surviving... if we can get enough provender, that is.
'Now, everyone here is all excited about the Orcs, and it's true that food isn't much of a problem if an Orc has lopped off your head. However, I'm not much with an axe, so I'll spend my time worrying about what I can help with, and that's food. We only have enough provisions for a few more days, and I think it is time to look for other sources of food.
'I am reluctant to bring it up, but I have heard that the Orcs eat norbog-legs and slug-tongues, and while I'm sure such provender is not much for taste, it keeps them alive. It might do the same for us as well. Could you gather some legs and... tongues from the nerbyg and slugs found in Duvuinen?'

'Ah, so you are back... let me see what you have there!
'Oh my, it is worse than I thought. What vile creatures those Orcs are if they live off of food such as this! And the smell... perhaps there is something we can add to it to make the taste less vile.'

'The nerbyg and slugs infest Duvuinen. I hesitate to say it, but please gather some legs from the nerbyg and tongues from the slugs.
'If we were not in such desperate straits, I would not even consider it... but I can see no alternatives!'
Bring the ingredients to Kol
Desperate Straits
Kol, a resident of Gabilshathûr, told you of their desperate need for food.

Nerbyg and slugs can be found in Duvuinen, north of Gabilshathûr.
Kol has asked you to collect norbog-legs and slug-tongues to help supplement the provisions at Gabilshathûr.

'There is much that we owe to you, ${PLAYER}. You have given us hope that one day we will throw off Angmar's yoke. There are others, though, in these lands that need such hope as well.
'There are tales and whispers that there are dwarves to the east of Rammas Deluon. If it is true, they have hidden there long and well, but as Angmar stretches forth its hand, they may soon find they can hide no longer.
'If you wish to discover if these tales are true, travel past Rammas Deluon and look for these lost dwarves. The dwarves' hall should be somewhere south of Duvuinen.'

'You have come at the behest of the Men to the west, have you? Good, good, someone who is not our foe, but a friend...or so I hope!
'I suppose it was foolish for we dwarves to come here those years ago, but we were chafing under the rule of the Dourhands and left Othrikar in hopes of finding gems and ores. At that time, Angmar's evil was dormant, and later we paid too little heed to its growing power. Once its Orc-armies marched forth from Carn Dûm, we were cut off.
'Now we are hard-pressed from all sides and could use your help, if we are to survive in these blighted lands. We cannot give you much in return, but if we survive, perhaps one day we can lend our strength to throwing down Angmar!'
Find the hidden holding of the dwarves
Talk to the leader of Gabilshathûr
The Lost Dwarves

Búdan told you that there are others who may need your help in Angmar. There are tales of a hidden holding of the dwarves, east of Rammas Deluon. If the tale is indeed true, the dwarves have hidden themselves well, but Búdan fears it is only a matter of time before Angmar discovers them.
'What? You have come from the west to aid us? Speak to Avar immediately!'
'So you have crossed Rammas Deluon, have you? Friendly folk here are few and far between, so I am glad to see you. You should inform Avar that you have arrived...he will be most pleased to see you.'
'If you are seeking to find the truth behind the tales of the dwarves I told you of, you will want to cross Rammas Deluon and look for their holding south of Duvuinen.'
'The tales are true? Well then, speak to someone within this \qGabilshathûr\q immediately!'

The dwarf-holding lies to the east of Rammas Deluon and south of Duvuinen.

'${PLAYER}, it has become clear that your loyalties stand firmly with our House. The Elves of Rivendell are grateful for your service, and already a few of our bards take up their quills, prepared to spread the knowledge of your deeds in harmonious melodies.
'After some discussion, the Defenders of Imlad Gelair were instructed to welcome you to our sanctuary high upon the hills, overlooking The Last Homely House.
'You will find Imlad Gelair to the south, across the Falls of Imladris at the end of a low road which leads west. When you arrive, speak with Atharbain. She will be expecting you.'

'May I have your ear for a moment, ${PLAYER}? I have a matter that I would discuss with you -- one requiring a degree of discretion. You are Sivullinen, an Outsider, and in this matter I cannot trust one of my own kin. It is an issue that runs deep in our history and would cause great turmoil if it was to become widely-known.
'One of the elder tribes of the Lossoth once held an ancient treasure, a symbol of our people's pride and vitality in this harsh land that they had been entrusted with. In time, it was lost, and this loss was a matter of great shame to that tribe -- and indeed all Lossoth. Now it seems that this treasure may at long last be within our reach again, but we must act quickly before our chance is lost.
'If you would aid me, go south and speak with Esko at Pynti-peldot -- he knows the old tales better than anyone, and it is he who learned of the re-emergence of this great treasure. He can set you upon the correct path, if you hurry.'

'Menikko has sent you to speak with me about our lost treasure? I know of what you speak, but lower your voice lest someone overhear. He speaks of the Jä-koru, the Jewel of Ice -- the oldest treasure of our people, long revered in story and song and lost for many long years now. The Jä-koru is a great shard of ice, but this ice never melts, nor can it be shattered by hammer or chisel. When struck by the sun's rays, it returns the light three-fold in a great array of brilliant colours.
'This was no relic of Man. Our most ancient tales say it was given to our people by a great spirit of the frozen sea to bring light and beauty to our hearts during the coldest winters. The Hylje-heimo lost the Jä-koru as their Elders travelled up from the south. Their shame was so great that never would they speak of how it was lost.
'No matter how it was lost, it may now lie in the hands of the Angmarim. My own folk say that they are promising the Hylje-heimo Elder its return, so long as they ensure that the Council of Elders makes no agreement or alliance with the Men of the South. Any fool can see that our people's days of freedom are numbered should the lands of the South fall beneath the heel of Angmar, and yet the lure of the Jä-koru is so great that the Hylje-heimo Elder does indeed speak foolishly in council. So, ${PLAYER}, for the sake of both our peoples, I think it wise that we attempt to retrieve the Jä-koru before it is too late.'
Talk to Esko in Pynti-peldot
The Jewel of Ice
Menikko has told you of a lost Lossoth treasure that has now returned to light.

Esko is in Pynti-peldot, just south of the great bay.
Menikko has asked you to speak with a man named Esko to learn the story of the lost Lossoth treasure.

'You would know what course I have chosen to take? Very well. I told the Council that Narchuil will never be reforged, but I believe that my own words may have been hasty.
'I do not believe now that the ring sank with Arvedui in the Ice-bay of Forochel. Aearil, one of the ship's crew, knew of Narchuil and its power. I do not think he would have allowed such an heirloom of my house to sink into the Sea.
'For that reason, I will myself return to Forochel and seek the ring. You may attend me if you wish... then perhaps Elrond's concerns will be lessened.'

'${PLAYER}, these last days have been disturbing. The Council of Narchuil did not end as I would have chosen, but I will not deny Laerdan the quest he desires. I fear, however, that he may depart Rivendell upon a rash course.
'Would you speak with him for me? Learn what course he intends to take and his purpose. I do not believe that Narmeleth will ever be recovered, for a dark power dominates her mind. I sense the influence of a Power greater than a single minor ring.
'You will find Laerdan in his quarters on the lower floor of my house. With your aid, I hope Laerdan will use greater wisdom in his choices.'
Book 13, Chapter 1: The Northward Road
Talk to Laerdan

'You have returned from Forochel and with the fragment of Narchuil! And what is this, you say? The shade of Arvedui remained there? A foul end to a good man! May the Valar have mercy upon his spirit.

'At last! The final fragment of Narchuil has been found! I must prepare now to take the ring south... the plans are nearly complete.
'I was perhaps wrong to wish Narchuil reforged. I see now how dangerous the thing may be. It must be destroyed, and I believe there is but one place where that may be done.

'The Last Homely House is fast becoming a prison to me. I do not feel welcome here. Yet on the other hand, I do not feel right leaving just yet. I fear if I leave these halls, I will never return, and I would not leave in such bitterness.
'Perhaps you would take up my search, until such time that I can leave here in good conscience? I know a dwarf who trades in the southern reaches of Forochel. Perhaps he might have some insight as to where you should begin the search.
'You can find Dáthi at Kauppa-kohta in Taur Orthon. He knows more about Forochel -- if such could be said about anyone -- than I.'

'Ho there! You say you come from Laerdan the Elf? Aye, he was here some time ago, seeking a lost ring or some such, but to no avail. Can you imagine hunting for a ring in the snows of Forochel?
'Nevertheless, his quest may not have been as foolhardy as I had first believed, for Men out of Angmar have moved through this region, and with them others that I have never seen before. They reminded me of the Men of Gondor, but stranger. They seek something here as well, and it may be that your quests are related.
'If you wish to find your lost ring, you must speak with the Snowmen, the Lossoth, who call themselves the Lumi-väki. This is their land, and they know it better than anyone. I suggest you speak with Lassi at Sûri-kylä, for he knows best the mind of their chieftain.'
'You are a stranger here, a ${RACE} from the South. We do not see too many of your kind, and we welcome even fewer....'

'In wisdom have you been sent to me, and only with wisdom will you earn the favour of the Lumi-väki. Yrjänä will not speak with you until you have earned the Favour of Wisdom, which I will confer upon you after you have completed my task.
'Look next to me. There will you find things of importance to the Lumi-väki, things that help us to survive in these cold lands. Put these things in their proper order, then return to me. How will you know what the proper order is? Through wisdom, of course.
'Warmth is of great importance in these frozen lands, so fire is a boon companion. Even more important is water, for without water there is no life.
'Once you have fire and water at your disposal, you have done much, but do not rest yet! You must then have stout weapons to protect yourself, but first obtain food enough to lend yourself the strength to wield them.
'But before you obtain any of these necessaries, a wanderer in these lands must have clothing warm enough to protect him against the cold when fire cannot be made and water cannot be found.'

'You have finished! And what have you learned?

'There is a näkijä, a seer, who dwells outside the village. She is powerful and does not fear the Lord of Storms. She may help you find your ring.
'You will find Saija at Näky-kolo north west of Kuru-leiri; that is on the western edge of the Ice Bay. She is haughty and proud, but you may find in her an ally against Mordrambor.
'Go, seek the wisdom of the ages.'
'Thou art not of the Lossoth, but are a ${RACE} from my lands of old. Why come ye into this terrible place?'

'You come from Yrjänä? I have no fear of the stone-dwellers from Angmar. They can do me no harm. I will share with you what wisdom I have.
'Long ago, a king from the South came into Forochel, seeking refuge from the Witch-king of Angmar. Arvedui was his right name, but we called him the Gaunt King, because he was frail from hiding in the ancient mines of the dwarves.
'The Gaunt King begged for aid from the Lossoth, which was given but hesitantly, for the Lossoth feared the wrath of the Witch-king. The Gaunt King stayed with the Lossoth until a great sea-monster appeared in the Ice-bay, bearing many Elves. We warned the Gaunt King not to go forth upon the back of the beast, but to wait for the summer, so that the power of the Witch-king would not be so strong. He would not listen, and the storms slew the beast.
'It is said that the body of the beast may yet be seen in the Ice-bay, north and east of here. It may be that you may find the knowledge you seek upon its corpse.'

'Thou dost not belong in this place, but it matters not. Alas, so much evil has befallen this world. I remain here in penitence, for my own curse was brought down upon my head.

The storms of the Ice Bay brought ruin to the vessel and all aboard her, and in despair and wrath I cursed myself for my pride. Redemption does not lay beyond hope, however, and those who follow in my footsteps may yet bring me peace.
'In the dwarf-mines south in Länsi-mâ, where we first hid from the agents of the Witch-king, we were forced to abandon many things. One such item is a book of heraldry which details the lineage of my people. Go forth and find it, then bring it to the Dúnadan who watches these cold lands at Sûri-kylä. 'These past few months have been getting more and more difficult. There are too many beasts in the forest, and there are not enough hunters to collect our supplies for the kelkka.
'You can help us by collecting moose-antlers, sinew, and driftwood. The antlers are important, you see. They are flattened into the luisua of our sleds, keeping them light but ever so strong. Most any moose you hunt in our forests should provide you with a generous amount. The sinew comes from the wolverines all around Kauppa-kohta. Their meat is too tough for eating, but perfect for lashing the kelkka together.
'There is something strange about the driftwood, though. The lake cares for it, cradling the timbers until they emerge on the southern shore like smooth gems from a Kivi-väki trader's pouch. The wood glows like the moon, and because the kelkka are formed from it, they will always guide us back to our homes. My people depend upon the kelkka to take our goods from village to village. Your help will be greatly appreciated.'
'This is a hyvys -- a kindness -- you have performed. These materials will help us to make enough sleds for the hunters and for the Elders.'

'If you wish to explore our lands with impunity, you will have to earn that privilege; no Lumi-väki tribe nor any of our kin will so much as answer your queries if you have not been vouched for. And I warn you, not all of my kinsmen will be as welcoming as I. Be courteous, be wary, and be silent unless spoken to.
'I am open-minded, however. If I am given three reports of your worth, you will be granted the tolerance of the Lumi-väki. My son, Kaj, seeks aid in some endeavour or other. I have not the time to attend to it. You might begin with him; he is standing just to the east. And now that I think of it, Niko, our Master of the Hunt, has been looking more harried than usual lately; follow the road south-west and you can find him at his camp on the north side. He may not welcome your assistance, though; he does not think much of Sivullinen. Lauri, my best scout, may also need assistance. You can find him near the stable-master.'
'My people speak well of you, Sivullinen. You will find tolerance among the Lumi-väki.'

'Go away, Sivullinen. I have no time for the likes of you! What? Ora sent you? What for? To help me? Do you both suffer from snow-dreams? What help could you be? Go away! You can in no way help me -- I doubt you can even hunt!
'Let you prove yourself? I am not having you crash around the tundra, scaring off what little game you do not maim! Hunting in Forochel is serious business. Hunting requires patience, stealth, silence, cunning, planning. If you can prove that your feet can be silent as your mouth is not currently being, you may prove more than completely useless, and we will talk again.
'We hunt härkä. There are several herds of them nearby; look to those to the south-west and to the north. Those thrice-blasted Susi-väki have been sneaking around recently, trying to trap our härkä, and they are not too careful about how much damage those brutal traps of theirs might do to the poor beasts before they come to put the wounded out of their misery. Go and find those traps and disable them. Härkä can be somewhat skittish, so stay calm -- if you hurt one, the whole herd might run, and then you may be certain I will use your bowels for a bow-string.'

'You destroyed the traps? And the herds have not scattered to the four winds?
'Well, I did not think a Sivullinen like you would be able to do it. Perhaps you can be of some use to me after all, seeing as my other hunters are all occupied....'

'As I said, my other hunters are currently occupied with other tasks, and one lies wounded in Pynti-peldot -- not that I am ever actually given enough hunters to get everything done in any case. Anyway, it looks like another harsh winter, and it is my job to make sure it does not wind up being unbearably thin. You can help with that.
'I want you to hunt sûri-hirvi. They roam all over Itä-ma, so you ought not to have any trouble finding them. We use their antlers for building, decoration, even fires -- oh yes, bone and antler will burn if you force air the right way, and it is not like there are so many trees around here that we can burn them freely. The meat, when frozen or salted or smoked or air-cured, can last for a season or more.
'Bring me many antlers and cuts of meat. We will find a use for them.'
'Ah, excellent. These will do nicely, Sivullinen.'
'Well? Are the sûri-hirvi around here too much for you, Sivullinen?'

'Greetings, Sivullinen. I am Kaj of the Lumi-väki, also named Warg-skinner, Claw-wearer, Plague of the Susi-väki, and Spearer of the Ancient Mursu. I am embarking upon a delicate endeavour: an ancient Lumi-väki ritual. I will need certain things.
'Go to Altti the trapper at Jänis-leiri, west along the road, and ask him to loan me his sledge. I will also need rope. There should be a few extra coils at the scout-camp, out on a little island on the other side of the road, south of here. And furs, thick, soft, and warm; I do not care what kind of animal they are from. Something that will feel good on soft skin... what kind of look is that to give me? It is part of the ritual!
'I do not have time for this; I must prepare. Go find these things for me, or get out of my sight and stay out of my way!'

'Who are you and what do you want?
'Kaj sent you? I am not sure what that boy thinks he is doing, having me lend one of my own sledges to a Sivullinen.
'Take it. But tell Kaj it will go very hard with him if anything happens to it!'
'Ah, excellent! Now we can truly begin.'

'What are you doing back here without the things I need?
'Sivullinen really are not much use, are they?'

'Ah, ${PLAYER}... you helped me before; perhaps you can help me again. Look at this! My second blade -- apparently a cheap and weak piece of smithing, for which I will disembowel that merchant if I ever see him again -- has gone and snapped clean in two from the cold! Blasted, brittle, low-quality steel.
'I am going to need another sword -- something decent. There are more of those wild men along the shore-line, towards that pretty little shrine the Lossoth have. I will wager one of them would have a blade worth wielding! It seems only fair, as they tried to rob me of mine, that I should rob them of theirs. You had best be wary, though; the Gauredain are a fierce people.
'The shrine is north-west of here, near some dwarf-ruins, but be careful: the way is dangerous.'

'Ah! Let us take a look at it.
'Well, fine craftsmanship it is not, that is for certain... but it is strong, and it is sharp, and it will withstand this beastly cold.
'It will serve admirably until I return home and can obtain a new blade. My thanks!'
'You have not found a good sword yet? Please, keep trying! A champion with only one blade is at less than half a warrior!'
Find Déornyd a new sword from a Gauradan
Find Déornyd a new sword from a Gauradan
Bring the Gauradan-sword to Déornyd at Pynti-peldot
A Sword Shivered
You returned Gránung to Déornyd only to learn that he has a problem with his other blade.
'The ruins known as the Lonesome Stones can be found by following the water's edge north and west from Pynti-peldot, and I saw Gauradan warriors all along the way.'
'Two blades, each worthy of a champion! Well done, ${PLAYER}!'

Gauredain roam to the north and west of Pynti-peldot, near the Lonesome Stones.
Déornyd has asked you to replace his broken sword with one stolen from one of the Gauredain.

'I have been proven wrong about you, Sivullinen. Your deeds will be remembered here, and I will lend you aid. If you continue west along the main road you will reach an encampment of the Kivi-väki, which they call Zigilgund. Nearby is the fabled graveyard of the norsu, which is a sight well worth the trip.
'You will wish to speak to Thórth, the leader of these Kivi-väki; he seems to be of strong character.
'Best of luck, ${PLAYER}, and may your travels be safe.'

'Welcome to Zigilgund. I am Thórth.
'So you have been through some of the Lossoth lands, I gather, if Ora sent you. She does not trust outsiders easily -- when our expedition first passed through there some time ago, it took some doing to get her to so much as let us pitch tent within Pynti-peldot during a blizzard!'
Talk to Thórth
Dwarves and Mammoths
You have earned the respect of the Lossoth-chieftain Ora, who will now further guide your exploration of Forochel.
'Follow the main road to the west if you wish to find Zigilgund.'
'Zigilgund? It is to the west. The easiest way is simply to follow the main road.'

Zigilgund is far along the road to the west of Pynti-peldot.
Ora suggested that you speak with a dwarf there by the name of Thórth.
Recovered Gránung

'Greetings, ${PLAYER}! My name is Déornyd of the Eglain. Among my own people, I enjoy a certain renown -- though it is paltry indeed when compared to that of my sister. She was the reason I became a Champion: her courage was unshakeable, her voice commanding, and the flickering of her blades was like the shimmering dance of moonlight on the Red Swamp. She fell in battle against minions of the Enemy, and the world has been a little dimmer ever since.
'I took up her sword, which is named Gránung. I have wielded it as best I could in defence of justice, until recently, when I was travelling here from Taur Orthon through the ice canyons. I was ambushed by something -- all I saw was a flash of fur. Altti, a trapper, found me and brought me here, but without my sword!
'I believe it to be still in the canyons south of here. Please, I beg you, help me recover Gránung! My family's honour as well as my own are at stake.'

'Can it be?
'It is! Gránung, bright as she shone in the time of my ancestors!
'Blessings on you, ${PLAYER}. You have recovered that which was most precious to me.'

'Have you found it? You have not?
'The ice canyons are south of here; the road leads right to them. I think that is where Gránung must still be. I beg you, please find it!'
Recover Gránung
Return Gránung to Déornyd
My Sister's Sword
Déornyd has lost his prized weapon, a sword belonging to his sister, who was a champion of great renown among the Eglain.

'Have you found it? You have not?
'The ice canyons are south of here; the road leads right to them. I think that is where Gránung must still be. I beg you, please find it!'

Déornyd thinks his sister's sword is still in or around the ice canyons, south of Pynti-peldot.
Déornyd has asked you to find his sister's sword and return it to him.

'You have helped me once, Sivullinen; perhaps you can help me with something else?
'We here in Pynti-peldot are the main source of tusks from the great kalpa-kita that roam the area, which are made into intricate carvings for which the area is well-known, then sent south to Kauppa-kohta to be traded or sold.
'We are running low on our supply of tusks, and I would have you bring me more. Kalpa-kita are found especially in a little wooded dell at Leijona-kotin, west along the road and then south, beyond the homestead of Lumi-talletta.'
'Ah! I will be able to make wonderful carvings with these... thank you, Sivullinen!'
Collect kalpa-kita tusks (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Return to Kimmo with the kalpa-kita tusks
Cat-tusk Scrimshaw
Pynti-peldot is the primary source of cat-tusk scrimshaw in Forochel. The Lossoth carve the large tusks during the long winter nights, and sell them to south-landers.

'Have you enough tusks to provide some winter occupation for myself and my friends? No? Why not?
'Kalpa-kita roam all over Itä-ma, but are found especially in a wooded dell called Leijona-kotin, west along the road and then south, beyond the homestead of Lumi-talletta.'

Kalpa-kita can be found in and around their den at Leijona-kotin, as well as roaming the rest of Itä-ma.
Kimmo has asked you to bring him some tusks from the kalpa-kita which roam Forochel.
Kimmo is at Pynti-peldot. You should return to him with the kalpa-kita tusks.
The statue has melted in your pack

'There is a place at the edge of the Ice Bay sacred to the Vesi-henki. It is traditional to leave a carved-ice statue there as a plea for the blessings of the spirits upon the weather and the hunt.
'I have carved the statue, and it is safely stored in the cold, but I am not as young as once I was. Would you take it to its proper place? You will have to be quick, as it will melt from the warmth of your body near your pack if you take too long.
'Follow the water's edge to the west and north, passing through the old ruins known as the Lonesome Stones, and you will find a path leading down from them to the water's very edge. Beware the beasts on the way, and the deadly bite of the Bay!'
'Excellent work. It is not an easy journey, I know, but you have done Pynti-peldot a great service.'
Place the ice statuette at the shrine of the water-spirit
Return to Kimmo at Pynti-peldot
Ice at the Water's Edge
Kimmo the artist wishes to make an offering to the water-spirits on behalf of the people of Pynti-peldot.

'Follow the cliff-edge of the water, to the west and north, passing through the old dwarf-ruins known as the Lonesome Stones, and you will find a path leading down from them to the water's very edge. There you will find the shrine to the Vesi-henki. Hurry! The statue will melt and make a poor offering if you take too long.'
'Thanks to you, the Vesi-henki was correctly honoured. I am grateful.'

The Lossoth shrine lies along the shore of the Ice Bay, to the west and north of Pynti-peldot, past and downhill from the dwarf-make ruins known as the Lonesome Stones.
Kimmo has asked you to find the Lossoth shrine to the water spirit and place the statuette on the pedestal there before it melts.
Tell Kimmo back at Pynti-peldot that you have correctly placed the statuette.
Destroyed Gauradan-fetishes (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Ora thinks your intentions are noble, then, does she? That remains to be seen. But if you should care to investigate something....
'You know of the Susi-väki? Yes, they who wear the pelts of their pets. It used to be that they were no real trouble, as their haunts were far from ours. Recently, however, I have had reports from Scout-master Lauri that Gauradan-fetishes have been spotted within the northern exit of the Jä-kuru, the ice-canyons that lead to Taur Orthon, south of here.
'The Susi-väki use fetishes to mark the extent of territory that they claim or intend to claim as theirs. With these, they now threaten our main route to the south. Go and destroy some of those fetishes -- that should throw them into some confusion. If it keeps happening, they shall soon enough get the message that their incursions will not be tolerated.'
'Excellent. If I have my way, we will never see one of those thieving, looting Susi-väki within the bounds of Itä-mâ.'

'A dark rumour has reached my ears, ${PLAYER} -- it seems that the long-abandoned ruins in the eastern region of the Lone-lands have been corrupted by some evil presence.
'I do not yet know the nature of this corruption, but if it continues to spread, it may well pose a danger to anyone attempting to travel through those lands. I need you to scout out the area and return to me with any news about the extent of the problem.'

'What you have seen is most disturbing. The lands of the eastern Lone-lands appear to be cursed by the powers residing in those ancient ruins.
'I cannot say what this forebodes, but it is not good. All we can do for now is watch and try to hold these strange apparitions at bay.'

'Greetings, ${PLAYER}. I fear that with all that has been happening in recent months we have been remiss in our own defence... just recently a small group of Orc-scouts were slain by our Rangers on the very doorstep of Esteldín. I need not tell you that it is only the secrecy of Esteldín that protects it from the full brunt of Angmar's assault. We cannot take any further risks!
'I need you to patrol the lands immediately surrounding Esteldín and report back to me with any movements the Enemy makes.
'I would stay clear of the large Orc-camp at Dol Dínen if I were you -- we have already lost too many scouts there, and I cannot afford to lose any more.'

'So, we continue to be surrounded by enemies -- though the enemies that most concern me are those who lie to the east of us, as the Orcs continue to stream down out of the Ram Dúath.
'In time, they will find us -- I only hope we are ready by then.'

'Our bretheren in Evendim are preparing an offensive to break the foul occupation of Annúminas, but these preparations have left them with no scouts to spare in patrolling the far side of Lake Evendim -- that is where you come in.

Candaith saw a company of Orcs climbing to the summit of Weathertop, preparing fortifications and barricades as they went. The Orcs have foul plans for the hill and must be defeated before they work some great mischief.
'If you are prepared, I will lead the way. We must be swift, else the Orcs may succeed at whatever foul mischief they have planned!'
'You have my great thanks, ${PLAYER}. The Orcs of the South shall advance no further into the Lone-lands.'
'We must remain watchful, of course. Do not relax your guard.'

Candaith is at his camp at the north-west foot of Weathertop in the Lone-lands, far to the east of Bree.

'There was to be an old ritual by which Kaj thought to win my heart? How thoughtful of him. I have always been interested in the old ways! But he has found one even older, a feat of courage that has impressed even my three brothers! I did not think such a thing could be!
'Oh, there will be a wedding. Kaj cannot back out now, and should he try he will find the mammoth was nothing compared to my displeasure! We will have to find something for our new mammoth pet to do during the ceremony... perhaps give rides to the children?
'Thank you for your part in this. We can sort out the rest ourselves, but I may call on you for help with some of the things I will need for the wedding.'

'You are fortunate to be able to witness this ritual, you know; few Sivullinen get to see it. It has... well, fallen out of use in recent times.
'I just need to set things up with these components.
'You will do your utmost to ensure this goes smoothly. Some folk may object to this ritual, but no-one is getting hurt! I promise.'
'I think we should be able to handle this matter from here on out.'

'Who are you? What are you doing here?
'That braggart Kaj? He does not deserve Pinja -- I do not care if he is the chieftain's son!
'Get out of our way. We will teach him a lesson he shall not soon forget! If you try and stop us, then you shall be taught in his place!'

'I see what is going on here, outsider. You came here to help Kaj steal away my sister! Many others have tried, and always my brothers and I have shown them they are too weak to wed her. And yet only you and Kaj stood bravely before this untamed mammoth....
'If you wish to wed into our family... but no, I see that Kaj has managed to steal away something of Pinja's before you have had the chance. He has carried away her heart, somehow! Bah.

'If you can hunt the moose for me and bring me some meat, we should be able to get underway soon. I am so sorry for all this trouble!
'The moose graze in the forest surrounding us. Thank you, my friend!'

'Through the trees he says, just go through the line of trees. Ha! Surely we would be wandering for a week or more that way. My shortcut is the only way to...oh my, I beg your pardon!
'You see, my fellows and I were on our way to...well, that is of no consequence. In their haste, they took a road that we should not have been following, and it seems I have lost track of them.
'I quickly dispatched my raven towards the rocky outcropping to the south-west to see if any tracks were left in the snow. So far, she has not returned. I was about to go retrieve her, thinking she got stuck in the trees, but my bear-friend, Linden, is not well and requires my help here. If you are headed in that direction, could you look for her?'

'How she managed to get lost among Wargs is a mystery to me, but obviously it was through no fault of my own.
'She seems to be beckoning towards the icy cliffs to the west. I believe my fellowship must have been there within the last day or two. I think we will be able to follow their trail if Linden here is able to raise her spirits.'

'Linden's spirits are finally picking up. It seems that after all this time, I should be packing to journey on with you instead of my fellows, but alas I must be on my way to meet them.

'Sivullinen, we must talk quietly, but quickly. There is a horrific threat along the gentle shores of our lake. I have heard Valtteri's hunters gather in the twilight at the gates of the town in hurried whispers, readying themselves for some kind of assault. I try not to be a curious person, but if Valtteri is concerned, then the likes of me should bolt for the fair fields in the South!
'I heard them talk of a Surmâja who by night watched us from the battered peaks and spoke to Angmar in a voice we dare not try to understand. This Surmâja, whom we call Blökk, was bred long ago in that horrid land and now waits in the shadows for the right time to signal an attack upon us.'
'I fear Valtteri is not moving quickly enough. Someone needs to strike down this craven beast. Will you do this? Blökk wanders among the other Surmâja, along the west shore.'

'You killed Blökk? You just...walked up and defeated such a cunning beast? If Valtteri's hunters were so careful, I find it hard to believe that you were able to eliminate the Surmâja without more deliberate planning.
'You might think we are a foolish people, ${PLAYER}, but we do not tolerate being insulted. Take this and be on your way. I will pay a real hero far more.'

'For many long winters, we have sparred with the Susi-väki for control of these harsh lands, but we have not truly fought a war in the memories of our fathers or even our grandfathers. Now war comes upon us, unlooked for and uninvited. The Susi-väki assaults have become more vicious and frequent, and dark allies have joined with them -- the Kivi-väki from the South who name themselves Dourhands, as well as the Angmarim from the East.
'More Men and dwarves from the South have also come to us of late, seeking to make an alliance with us. To accept their offers would draw us remorselessly to war, but to reject them may well leave us at the mercy of ancient enemies. So I ask you this: Will you show us your strength in war and strike against the Susi-väki who are our enemies? If so, I would have you attack the boundaries of their ancestral homeland itself, far to the West across the Ice Bay.
'On the southern edge of the great glacier where both of our peoples have long hunted and fought, the Susi-väki have long maintained a line of wards marking the edge of their lands. Burn these wards, and in so doing, let the Susi-väki know that the Lumi-väki and their allies shall make true war upon them -- and stain every flake of snow with blood, if need be -- should they continue their aggression.'
'Well done. This act shall declare to the Susi-väki that their aggression shall not go unanswered.'

The Lossoth of Forochel have found themselves swept up in the rising tide of war in their northern realm, for the Angmarim have incited the ancient hatred between the Lossoth and the Gauredain. Hoping to make an alliance with the Lossoth, representatives of Men and dwarves from the south have come to Forochel to lend their aid.
'Have you destroyed the markers of the Susi-väki yet?'

The Gauradan wards run in a line north of the Guaredain encampment Barad Gaurhoth, near Zigilgund. These wards are far across the bay to the south-west of Sûri-kylä.

'${RACE}, do you seek to be of help to the Lumi-väki? Then you will help me.
'Thanks to these trying times, our larders are nearly out of dried fish, and we need more. Will you go and speak with Olavi and have him bring me as many buckets as he is able?
'You will find Olavi east and slightly south of Sûri-kylä at his fishing camp along the road to Itä-mâ.'

'Nôra sent you for more fish? That may be difficult.
'The shoreline has been held against me, both by the Rauta-väki and by the kantâ that have been driven into the area. I have been completely unable to fish, but you look like you have a steady hand and unyielding patience... perhaps you would go and fish for me?
'Take a fishing-pole and fish down by the waters along the ice bay west of here; that is where the particular fish Nôra is looking for usually run in the largest numbers.'
'The fish! I hope it was not too much trouble. I know how Olavi can be about his fish.'

'Bah! This will not do at all! What is a guardian without his shield? He is but half a dwarf, I reckon. I will not be satisfied until I have my shield repaired.
'Go and speak with the Lossoth craftsmen here in Sûri-kylä. They are strange Men, but perhaps they will be able to repair it. Otherwise, I do not know what I will do.
'The Lossoth craftsmen can be found inside the Great Lodge in Sûri-kylä. Now, run along! I will not have you waste any more time hovering about like a gnat.'

'Shame? Why, the gall of that Man! I would go and speak with Rauno myself, if I had not already had a falling out with him.
'I innocently inquired after the making of his craft, but he would not speak on the subject. We exchanged a number of words, and now he will not say a word to me! He is an evil-tempered lout; I would not think his silence a great loss were it not for my present need.
'Perhaps you could speak with him and see if he will give me one of the sturdy shields of the Lossoth. I will not be able to travel back to the South without a new shield!'

'I wonder that this shield remained unsundered for as long as it did, ${RACE}. Its craftsmanship is very poor and the materials from which it is made are of poor quality.
'I will not repair this worthless shield. I would bring shame upon myself and my family if I did so.'
'The kilpi is finished. Take it to Nef, and bid him to seek his companions and return to his own home.'

'I do not cherish the thought of making a shield for Nef. He came to me with wild requests, and when I told him what I had at hand for materials, he said many things that I will not repeat now. I do not need to offend your ears also.
'But if he will not leave until his shield is completed, I will make it, if only to see him depart. The items that I require would be hard-bone and worm scale. Both are rare, and both are vital to the making of kilpi -- shields, as the Kivi-väki calls them.
'Hard bone can be found on many of the beasts throughout Jä-rannit, while worm scale should be found on the worms of the same region. Return to me when you have found these items, and I will craft the shield for the small outsider with the long beard and bad temper.'
'You have returned with the hard bones and worm scales? I will begin work on the kilpi right away. It should not take long, as I have already completed much of the work while you were away.'
'Have you recovered any hard bones and worm scales yet, ${PLAYER}?'

'Well now...this looks like a decent piece of work.
'Thank you, ${PLAYER}. This should do, though I will want to replace it with something a bit more durable once I reach Bree again.'
'Has Rauno finished my shield yet?'

'The Susi-väki are brutes, grown stronger and more savage than those who follow a civilized path. It comes as no surprise to me that their response to our warning is only to redouble their assaults in challenge. I had no true hope that it would be otherwise, for it has ever been this way with them.
'Now the war begins in earnest as their hunters roam far and wide upon the ice, searching for either man or beast to slay. They shall be the ones we hunt, for they are poorly organized and vulnerable, depending on their raw strength alone rather than the more deadly tools of cunning or numbers.
'We shall winnow their numbers now, before they form into true war-bands, which would offer a much greater threat to us. Go and seek these Susi-väki upon the glacier, west across the Ice Bay.'

'It is well that you have returned, for your efforts, difficult though they may have been, have not proven to be enough. While you were away, the winds brought the howls of the Susi-väki here. Our long years of struggle with these brutes have taught us some of the meaning of their howls. Few of my people have ever heard such a fierce howl as this, and it could mean but one thing: The Susi-väki have chosen a war leader.'

'Now the battles have begun in earnest, ${PLAYER}. The Susi-väki, stung by their losses, have begun to gather into bands where their enormous strength is multiplied. Even the hearts of our fiercest warriors may feel the cold touch of fear when facing the Susi-väki in wrathful numbers.
'These brutes do not gather gladly, however...only a strong leader can bring them together in any semblance of order in battle, and such leaders are rare among the Susi-väki.
'There is one such leader, Nadelek, of which we have heard rumour recently. He lives in their home village of Barad Gaurhoth. You have proven your own strength and bravery -- if you can find and defeat this war-leader, you will have deprived the Susi-väki of one of their greatest weapons in the battles ahead.'

'Good, you have returned. With their war leader dead, the Susi-väki will fight among themselves until another proves strong enough to bring them all into line. By then, perhaps our numbers will be great enough to repel such a war band.
'Or so I hope. Until then, we are at peace, and we have you to thank. We shall be forever grateful, ${PLAYER}. Thank you.'

You have placed the fish upon the ritual stone

'At the beginning of every season, we give offerings to the spirits of the wind and the spirits of the water. For as long as our people can recall, we have made these offerings, and they have always brought fish and fair weather to our villages.
'Recently, we have not had an abundance of fish, and the storms have been sudden and terrible. This must be because of all the strangers and the Rauta-väki...their lack of offerings must be upsetting the spirits!
'You must hurry! Take this ritual fish and place it upon the ritual stone along the edge of the Ice Bay where the Angmarim have now occupied. Also, take this bag of feathers and throw them into the wind at Reodh Fuil, near to the pass into Forodwaith where the wind blows strongest.'
