'Greetings, Sivullinen! I am Launo of Hirvi-heimo. It has come to me that you are a warrior of some renown, and we have need of such as our battles with the Susi-väki to the west grow more frequent and deadly.
'One of my tribe has been studying the old ruins on the northern edge of the great glacier across the Ice Bay. We believe that they were built by the dwarves, but it has lain abandoned for longer than our tales recall. I received a message from my kinsman a few days ago claiming that he had seen fell spirits clambering among the ruins. Where they might have come from he could not guess, and he dared not approach too closely for he is no warrior himself.
'I ask you this, will you go to speak with Arre? His messages are disturbing, and in a time of war and strife, we can ill afford to ignore such an omen.'

'Launo sent you? Good, good. There is something evil afoot here, and I know not what it might portend. See that fortress up on the mountainside above us? It has long stood cold and silent, built by a lost tribe of dwarves who came here hoping to find ore and riches -- to no avail. It has lain abandoned for many generations of our people.
'But no more! Lately I have seen figures moving about upon its battlements, and a deadly cold hangs over it, making the frozen blasts upon the open jätikkö seem inviting by comparison.
'The air of evil about it is palpable, and I dare not approach it myself, for I am no warrior. Will you go there and discover the secret of those strange spirits that now haunt its walls?'

'What is this? It is so cold that it burns flesh! You say you found this around the neck of one of the Râto you fought in Kibilzahar?
'Alas, none of my lore speaks to such evil mâginen, and I cannot divine its purpose, but I can say one thing for certain: the amulet itself is of Susi-väki craftsmanship, a work of crudely-beaten silver set with an ice-jewel.
'This leaves us with precious few means to learn where it came from or how it came to be enchanted so....'
'Have you found nothing in Kibilzahar? There must be some clue there to the nature of this nameless evil.'
Talk to Arre
Defeat wights in Kibilzahar (${NUMBER}/10)
Defeat wights in Kibilzahar (9/10)
Collect a frozen amulet
Bring the frozen amulet to Arre
Slaves of the Ice
Launo told you that rumour has come to him that the ancient dwarf-ruins of Kibilzahar have become haunted by fell spirits.
'Speak with my kinsman Arre at Kuru-leiri.'
'What manner of spirits haunt Kibilzahar, I do not know. Will you investigate for me, Sivullinen?'
'What manner of spirits haunt Kibilzahar, I do not know. Will you investigate for me, Sivullinen?'
'What manner of spirits haunt Kibilzahar, I do not know. Will you investigate for me, Sivullinen?'

Arre is at the camp of Kuru-leiri, in the northern reaches of the great western glacier.
Launo has asked you to speak with Arre concerning the fell spirits he reported.

Kibilzahar lies upon the northern slope of the glacier, north-west from Kuru-leiri.
Arre asked you to explore the ruins of Kibilzahar. Perhaps you may solve the mystery behind the appearance of the fell spirits.

Kibilzahar lies upon the northern slope of the glacier, north-west from Kuru-leiri.
Arre asked you to explore the ruins of Kibilzahar. Perhaps you may solve the mystery behind the appearance of the fell spirits.

Kibilzahar lies upon the northern slope of the glacier, North-west from Kuru-leiri.
While exploring Kibilzahar you discovered that some of the wights wandering through its ruins were wearing strange amulets. You should retrieve one of these amulets for Arre.

Arre is in Kuru-leiri, south-east from Kibilzahar.
You should bring the frozen amulet you found in Kibilzahar. Perhaps he will be able to tell you more about it.
You have found orders concerning the Jewel of Ice

'Now that you know the story of the Jä-koru, I think it is time that we address the matter at hand.
'A spy of mine claims that the Angmarim plan to bring the Jä-koru back into Forochel some time soon... but we do not know how or when they might do so.
'As you have likely noticed, there is an encampment of Angmarim near the Ironspan, which is the most likely route they would use to bring the Jä-koru here... assuming it was held in Angmar itself all these years. If you do battle with the Angmarim there, you may be able to find one who knows something of the Jä-koru, or at least evidence of its passage if they have already brought it through.'

'Ah! Well done, ${PLAYER}! At last we have the Jä-koru very nearly in our hands!
'According to these papers, it is already here in Forochel -- the Angmarim plan to hold it for some time yet, to hold it over the head of the Hylje-heimo and continue to manipulate the Council until such time as their servants among the Susi-väki and Kivi-väki have hurt us badly enough that we are ready to sue for peace -- and slavery to Angmar. Only then will they relinquish the Jä-koru.
'Obviously we cannot wait while this happens -- if we can capture the Jä-koru for ourselves and present it to the Hylje-heimo in secret, then we can ensure their support in the Council and join forces with the peoples of the South in time to stop this evil before it consumes us all.'
'You have not yet found any trace of the Jä-koru? Please continue your search...we cannot afford to fail in this!'
Search for evidence of the Jewel of Ice
Search for evidence of the Jewel of Ice
Bring the Angmarim orders to Esko
The Ransom of Angmar
Esko told you the tale of the Jewel of Ice and how the Angmarim are using it as leverage against the Lossoth.
'The Men of Angmar are evil and do us ill to withhold the Jä-koru.'
'The Men of Angmar are evil and do us ill to withhold the Jä-koru.'

The Angmarim are encamped near the Ironspan, in the mountains of Forochel well to the east of the bay.
Esko has asked you to search the encampments of the Angmarim for some evidence of the Jewel of Ice.

The Angmarim are encamped near the Ironspan, north-east of Pynti-peldot.
Esko has asked you to search the encampments of the Angmarim for some evidence of the Jewel of Ice.

Esko is at Pynti-peldot, south-west of the Ironspan.
You found a set of orders that tell when and where the Jewel of Ice will be brought into Forochel. You should bring the orders to Esko at once.
Collected dwarf-picks (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Greetings, ${RACE}. I am Thórth, the head of the expedition to the Icereave Mines, such as it is.
'We were expecting a convoy, but recently I received news that it was attacked. Bad enough that it was carrying foodstuffs and armourer's supplies: those can be acquired locally with only a little effort. But it was also carrying mining-picks, and those cannot so easily be replaced.
'Forge new ones? Do you have any idea of the work that goes into a superior dwarf-pick? To make something that can hew the hardest stone, and extract the most precious of metals therefrom? Bah! No, if we're to support ourselves by mining, we must have our picks back. They were scattered around Norsu-hauta, the mammoth graveyard just south of here. Retrieve them and you shall be rewarded.'

'Dourhands? Surely not!
'${PLAYER}, this is serious. Dourhands in this remote area! They will have to be rooted out, every dwarf Jack of them.
'At least you found the picks -- that's a job well done, and doubly valuable if you prevented them from falling into the hands of stinking thin-bearded Dourhands.'

'Have you not yet found those picks? The rock won't mine itself, you know!
'As I said, check south of here, in what the Lossoth name Norsu-hauta, the place where mammoths go to die.'
Collect dwarf-picks (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Return the dwarf-picks to Thórth
Return the dwarf-picks to Thórth
Scattered in the Graveyard
On its way to the dwarf-outpost of Zigilgund, a convoy bearing vital supplies, especially mining picks, was attacked, and its contents scattered.
Collect the dwarf-picks that were scattered when the supply convoy bound for Zigilgund was attacked. Thórth said they would likely be in and around the nearby mammoth graveyard.
You have found the dwarf-picks that Thórth sent you to recover. You should return them to him at Zigilgund.
Found bent key

'Attacks from those thin-beards is no small matter, ${PLAYER}. They are organized -- they must have supplies, and a plan, and a leader to be this far north.
'I found some old maps of the Icereave Mines, and one of them shows a room inside. If I were the wagering sort, I would lay my money on those Dourhands planning to take over the mines, and that their leader would be claiming that particular area as his own.
'You will need to find a key. Perhaps one of the other Dourhands might have one?'

'Excellent work! Let's take a look at it....
'Oh blast, the key is bent! Ah, well. Not to worry... I think I can fix it.
'Hold on a moment....'
'You will be getting into no locked rooms without a key. I suggest you go find it.'
Take a key from a Dourhand within the ancient Icereave Mines
Bring the key to Thórth
Take a key from a Dourhand within the Icereave Mines
The Key to Their Greed
Thórth suspects that whoever is leading the Dourhands at the Icereave Mines is hiding in a locked area within the mines.
'You will need to find the key to the locked place in the mines, ${PLAYER}. I would guess one of the Dourhands might have one....'

The Icereave Mines lie to the south-west of Zigilgund.
Thórth has asked you to drive the Dourhands from the Icereave Mines.

Thórth is at Zigilgund.
You should return to Thórth with news of your victory.
Defeated Arnmórth the Exacting

'Right! That ought to just about do it. The key be fixed.
'One of my cohorts caught an' interrogated a Dourhand just a little while ago, and found out that they're bein' led by a right vicious dwarf, name of Arnmórth the Exacting. He's the greediest Dourhand since Skorgrím: thinks o' nothin' but gold and how to keep it. Ye'll need help defeatin' him, just to warn ye: he's likely to have plenty o' guards.
'Now, take this key, find his quarters, open that door, and give 'im what for! ...And bring the key back when yer done -- once the Icereave Mines be ours again, we'll be wantin' to use that room.'

'Hah, excellent! I'll wager Arnmórth didn't even know wha' hit him!
'${PLAYER}, ye will always have a welcome by the fires an' at the tables within the Icereave Mines -- once they're ours again. Ye've more than earned a reward.'
'Where's the key? Why are ye back here? Don't tell me ye've been driven off by them thin-beards!'
Defeat Arnmórth the Exacting
Return to Thórth
Arnmórth the Exacting
Thórth has fixed the broken key, and wants you to gather allies and find and defeat Arnmórth the Exacting within the Icereave Mines.
'Go find the quarters of Arnmórth the Exacting in the Icereave Mines, and defeat him! ...I've fixed the key for ye, what else're ye waitin' on?'
Find the inner office within the Icereave Mines. Bring allies.
Return to Thórth at Zigilgund with the key, and report your defeat of Arnmórth the Exacting.
Collected marbles (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Pardon me, my good ${RACE}, but can you help an Eglan far from his home out? I am having the worst luck! The bag what was holding my marbles split open, and by the time I noticed it, all the marbles were gone.
'Then, even worse, is that I saw a beast out in the snows there gobble one up! And I do not think it was the only marble what was lost that way either.
'It is a bit disgusting, I would agree, but I need those marbles back. A burglar needs his whole bag of tricks! Bring me back my marbles -- you will have to dig through more than one kind of creature's stomach, I would wager.'

'Ah, thank goodness! I missed these things -- want to watch me juggle them? No? Ah well.
'Unfortunately, the missing marbles have not been the worst of my troubles....'
'Where are my marbles? You have not had any luck?'
Bring the marbles to Warstang
Collect marbles (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Lost My Marbles
Warstang, a burglar currently residing in Zigilgund, has lost his marbles -- they seem to have been scattered and eaten by various beasts -- and wants your help recovering them.

You may find the beasts that ate Warstang's marbles scattered throughout Länsi-mâ.
Find Warstang's lost marbles in the bellies of the beasts who ate them and return them to him at the dwarf-outpost of Zigilgund.
Reclaimed Warstang's pouch from a Guaradan thief

'I do not believe this, and it is a bit embarrasing, honestly, but... someone has gone and stolen my belt-pouch! A burglar burgled -- I shall not soon live this down.
'If I had to guess, I would put the money I do not have anymore on the thief being a Gauradan. There are not many beasts around here with thumbs to unhook a pouch. I wonder if they train up to burgle, too...?
'But look here, I need my pouch! Will you help me again? You can find the Gauradan thieves out in the wastes to the south-east of Zigilgund.'

'Wait, my pouch is here. So what is hiding in this pouch...?
'Oh dear, this is not mine: it is the Guaradan thief's pouch! I had best not look inside it. I really do not wish to know what a Guaradan keeps in his pouch.
'Thank you for your efforts anyway, ${PLAYER}! The least I can do is give you a little from my own pouch....'
'Where is my belt-pouch?'
Reclaim Warstang's pouch from a Gauradan thief
Bring the pouch to Warstang
Reclaim Warstang's pouch from a Guaradan thief
Who Burgles the Burglar?
Warstang, the Eglan-burglar staying with the dwarves at Zigilgund, has had his belt-pouch burgled from him.
'Have you found my pouch yet? No? Well, keep looking, then! The Gauredain are found to the south-east of here.'

The Gauradan thieves can be found south-east of Zigilgund.
Warstang has asked you to recover his stolen belt-pouch from the Gauredain.

Warstang is currently residing in Zigilgund.
You should return the belt-pouch to Warstang.

'I have studied this amulet a bit more, but it remains a mystery to me. There is only one I know of who might be able to tell us of its true nature. He is of the Susi-väki -- a näkijä who was exiled from their midst for some crime he would not tell me.
'A few years ago, Nicca came upon me out in the wastes and saved my life as I lay there frozen and near to death. I spoke with him for a time and learned a little of the Susi-väki and their ways before he sent me back here.
'He still lives, I think, in a hidden place near the southern end of the jätikkö. If you can find him and show him this amulet, he might be able to tell you the truth of its mâginen and purpose.'

'You come through cold and evil to speak with me? You are not of the Gauredain. You are not Lossoth. Both would kill me. Who are you? Ah, names do not matter here in the endless ice -- you have brought something. Something made of ice and hatred. Show it to me.
'My kin who are lost to me made this, but the magic is not theirs. It comes from the dark land to the East, where the dead walk. I know its purpose, and it is very evil. Among my kin, those who show fear are exiled out into the frozen wilds to die, from the cold or the arrows of the Lossoth. My fate is the same.
'It is said that fell spirits wander the cold forever, howling against their fate, and these howls become the shriek of the wind upon the ice. Something took these spirits from the ice and trapped them in tombs of frozen flesh and bone, enslaving them. They have become warriors of the dark lords of the East -- those same lords whom I spoke against, earning exile from my kin who are enthralled by them.'
Bring the frozen amulet to Nicca
Exiles of Winter

Arre told you of a strange Gauradan mystic he once encountered upon the glacier. He appeared to be an exile among his people, but was wise in their lore. It is possible that he could tell more of the strange frozen amulet that you found in Kibilzahar.
'The Gauradan Nicca may be of some help to you.'

Nicca lives somewhere along the southern edge of the great glacier, in the hills east of Barad Gaurhoth.
Arre suggested you speak with Nicca and learn what you may of the amulets.
Defeated Delucheleg

'The fell spirits of Kibilzahar bring cold and ice and make it a terrible place. You must bring warmth and fire to that cold, desolate place of stone.
'Once, when the Kivi-väki were there, there was warmth. They lit great fires to warm the very stones. So must you do to banish the spirits. Be warned though. There is a dark manâja hidden there. It is he who commands the spirits, and he will not like the fire. You must not take this foe lightly, or you too will die there, a frozen corpse that walks.
'Now go. This is not a place for you. It is mine, and I shall die here alone when my time comes.'

'A servant of Angmar? Here upon the very jätikkö? The Elders will be furious to hear that the Rauta-väki have already stretched their hands so far into our lands.
'Thank you for your help. If Nicca was indeed correct and that creature was the one raising the Râto, then soon perhaps the dark mâginen will fade and they will haunt Kibilzahar no more.
'Allow me to give you this gift for all you have done. I must go soon and tell the Council of Elders what has transpired here.'
Summon and defeat Delucheleg
Talk to Arre in Kuru-leiri
Cold as Death
Nicca has told you of the fell spirits which wander the glacier and the creature that draws them forth, entombing them within the frozen husks of Men to serve as dark warriors.
'Delucheleg is very old and very evil...be wary of his power.'

Kibilzahar lies to the north-west of Kuru-leiri.
Nicca told you that some evil power has trapped fell spirits within the bodies of wights in Kibilzahar. Only the warmth of fire can banish them. He has told you to re-kindle the ancient fires that the dwarves once used to heat the ancient fortress. He also warned you of an evil lord who haunts that place, and to be ready to face him should you go there again.

Arre is at Kuru-leiri, south-east of Kibilzahar.
Having defeated Delucheleg, the Gaunt-man responsible for raising the wights, you should return to Arre and tell him of your discoveries and battles.
Saw Juhani to safety
'Thank the Ice Spirits! Every time I have tried to escape on my own, I have been turned back by the long fangs of the kalpa-kita. Will you escort me back to the road?'
'Thank you! You have been of great aid to my friend.'
Defend Juhani
Talk to Tero in Zigilgund
Of Great Aid
Juhani, reported missing by his friend Tero back in Zigilgund, is trapped on the isle of Kissa-sari.
Juhani, reported missing by his friend Tero back in Zigilgund, is trapped on the isle of Kissa-sari. He wishes your help in ensuring him safe passage.
You have escorted Juhani to safety. You should tell Tero that he is now safe.

'I am quite worried about the threat from the North, these Gauredain of which we have seen so many in recent weeks.
'They are not native to this land, for though some believe that they are Men of Eriador gone wild, bereft of morals and virtue, I do not believe that to be true. I believe that these Gauredain come from the far land of Forochel. There, the bitter ice has kept alive an ancient race of evil Men who have long been in the service of the Enemy.
'Travel to this land and see if what I speak is true. If it is so, then I fear that the Gauredain are a greater threat than we have anticipated.'

'Gauredain? I do not know of such...ah! You mean the Susi-väki! Yes, the Susi-väki live on the western edge of the Ice Bay, though they do not trouble us this far south. We have more pressing issues than the Susi-väki here in Kauppa-kohta.'
Go to Kauppa-kohta in Forochel and learn of the Gauredain
Northern Threat
Tongannel is seeking information about the origin of the Gauredain.
'Have you travelled to Forochel yet? That icy land lies north of Tyrn Fornech in Evendim. Search for someone in the village of Kauppa-kohta who might speak on this matter.'
'The Gauredain do come from the land of Forochel...that is dire news indeed.'

Forochel lies north of Evendim through Cirith Rhiw, north of Tyrn Fornech. You should start your search in the village of Kauppa-kohta.
Tongannel has asked you to go into the frozen North and seek news of the Gauredain.

'We have had many strange travellers in these lands, though none as strange as the fellowship that recently passed through Aughaire, seeking for the land of Forochel. That land lies to the north and west of this land, though I have never seen the mountains of snow, nor frozen shores of the sea.
'They had an old map that claimed ancient dwarf-mines filled with treasure lay somewhere within the land of Forochel. If you were to travel to those lands, I would ask for you to seek out one of their company and lend them aid if you are able. They did not seem a very capable company, and it would ease my heart to know that a ${CLASS} such as yourself would look out for them.
'Forochel lies north of Evendim, through Cirith Rhiw, north of Tyrn Fornech. You should start your search in the village of Kauppa-kohta.'

'You were sent by Helegdir to ensure we were safe? Yes, yes, that is all well and good, but it is not my fault, you see. Those other fools got themselves lost. If I had my raven, things would be much different.'
Talk to Cenlieg
The Lost Fellowship
Helegdir has asked for your help in ensuring the safety of a group of individuals known as the Lost Fellowship.
'Have you found the lost fellowship yet? You should start your search in Kauppa-kohta. I heard them discussing that village as their first destination.'
'Thank you for seeking the lost fellowship, ${PLAYER}.'

Forochel lies north of Evendim, through Cirith Rhiw, north of Tyrn Fornech. You should start your search in the town of Kauppa-kohta.
Helegdir asked you to seek out a member of a fellowship of adventurers who journeyed to Forochel, passing through Aughaire in Angmar.

'Have you heard of the land of Forochel? It lies north and far to the west of here and is an inhospitable place filled with grinding ice and strange peoples. Though I have never been there, one of my cousins, Leithólf, recently led a group of my people up to Forochel to seek their fortunes trading with the Lossoth.
'If you were to travel to those lands, I would ask you to seek out Leithólf and ensure that he is safe. I have not heard from him in many months, though that is his way, coming and going for long stretches of time without correspondence to his kin.
'He said that he would be taking his caravan to Kauppa-kohta. A strange sounding name for a town, isn't it? He said it lay north of the land of Evendim through Cirith Rhiw, the Gate to the North.'
'My cousin Glóin? I have not had word from him in many long months. It is good to know that he is well, though with my troubles here, I do not know when I would be able to travel back to visit him.'
Talk to Leithólf
Distant Relations
Glóin is seeking news of one of his distant cousins who is trading in the land of Forochel.
'Have you started your journey to Forochel yet, ${PLAYER}? It lies north of Tyrn Fornech. Seek the town called Kauppa-kohta.'
Forochel lies north of Evendim through Cirith Rhiw, north of Tyrn Fornech. You should start your search in the village of Kauppa-kohta.
Collected the spear and mammoth tusk

'I lost my spear in the side of a mammoth! Can you believe it?
'I was hunting nearby -- just south of here -- and saw a beauty of a beast, with a pair of amazing tusks, and I thought one of them would make a fine trophy for over my mantel-piece back home!
'It was a fine, straight cast, but the stupid thing just ran off with my spear sticking out of its flank, and me left behind feeling a fool. Will you look for it? I would be surprised if the beast made it very far. If you find its corpse, bring back one of its tusks, too!'

'My spear! I swear no other flies as true! I would have been terribly upset never to see it again. Let's take a look at that tusk, now.
'Ah, it's a beauty, isn't it? Look at the... now wait a minute. Look at this! There are markings on this tusk! I cannot make head nor tail of them, though.
'Never mind! It will still make a fine trophy.'
'You are not much use to anyone, are you? Go find that spear!'
Find the mammoth that was speared by Sigrík
Bring the tusk and spear back to Sigrík
Where Norsu Die
Sigrík lost his spear while hunting mammoths.
'It's me spear, and one of that Mammoth's tusks, that I'm wantin'! Look in the place they go to die, south of here.'

The mammoth should be found somewhere south of Zigilgund.
Sigrík has asked you to find his missing spear, which should be stuck in the corpse of a mammoth. He asked you to collect one of its tusks as well.

Sigrík is at Zigilgund, north of the mammoth's corpse.
You should return the spear and tusk to Sigrík.

'I must admit, I've no idea what these odd markings mean. But there is a young Lossoth, an apprentice seer of some sort, apparently -- näkijä is what they call them -- who might know something.
'Mika has been on some sort of quest down in that mammoth graveyard, Norsu-hauta, just south of here.
'Would you go there and ask him about the markings.'
'What do you bring me? Let me see. Where did you come by this tusk?'
Talk to Mika
Mika Might Know

Sigrík has let you borrow the tusk you found for him, with the mysterious markings on it. He suggested that a Lossoth näkijä's apprentice by the name of Mika, who lives in Norsu-hauta, might know what to make of them.
'Go talk to the Lossoth-boy! I'm no help if you are curious about the markings on that tusk. Now, if you want to learn about spear-making, I'm your dwarf....'

Mika is at Norsu-hauta, south of Zigilgund.
Sigrík has asked you to speak with the young näkijä Mika about the markings on the mammoth tusk you collected for him.
Defeated tundra bears in Länsi-mâ (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'You have by now likely run into some of the great white kantâ that roam this area... or if you have not, you will soon. Majestic beasts, are they not? Ill-tempered, too.
'One thing that many do not know about them is that they are sometimes scavengers, when they cannot find fresh kills or are too lazy to hunt. They will eat carrion and gnaw on bones to crack them open for the marrow. Their favourite treat is norsu bone-marrow, and a norsu-corpse after a small family of white kantâ has been at it is far from a pretty sight.
'It upsets the norsu and makes them more likely to move the whole herd further away. We cannot afford to lose such a huge source of meat, bone, and fur! Drive off some of the kantâ... there is only so much competition we can afford.'

'Good. You have done well, ${PLAYER}. Kantâ that size are not easy prey, as I well know, but you have helped safe-guard the norsu-herds of Länsi-mâ for a little longer.
'Please, take this reward for your efforts.'
Defeat tundra bears in Länsi-mâ (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Mika
Undisturbed Rest
The great white bears of Länsi-mâ often scavenge among the remains of mammoths, which can drive the herds away.
'The kantâ are found all over Länsi-ma, especially in areas containing norsu. Look nearby as well as far off!'

Tundra bears can be found throughout Länsi-mâ.
Mika has asked you to drive off a number of tundra bears.

Mika is at Norsu-hauta.
Now that you have defeated many tundra bears, you should return to Mika.
Defeated Gauradan seer

'This is not good. This tusk was marked by the hand of one of the Susi-väki, but the words of power used are Angmarim. This tallies with what I know of a Susi-väki seer who has been seen nearby recently. A Man of Angmar must be trying to teach the Susi-väki how to ensorcel our Norsu!
'I have heard tales of the evil fetters Angmarim place upon their beasts, twisting them into fell creatures through time and despair. This must not be permitted in Länsi-mâ. Find and stop this seer!'
'Your task was well performed, ${PLAYER}. However, it would seem that we yet have a significant Angmarim threat to suppress.'
Defeat a Gauradan seer who is trying to ensorcel a mammoth
Keeping the Norsu Pure
Mika recognizes the markings on the tusk as Angmarim sorcery in a Gauradan hand. He wishes you to find and defeat the Gauradan seer who dares try and twist one of the Lossoth's mammoths.
'This is no time for hesitation. Seek out the Susi-väki seer here in Norsu-hauta.'
Search around Norsu-hauta for the Gauradan seer who is trying to ensorcel a mammoth.
Return to Mika in Norsu-hauta and tell him of your success.

'This Angmarim sorcerer dares to try and corrupt our Norsu, using idiot Susi-väki as tools. I suggest you look to the east and slightly north, on the slopes of those peaks just there across the road. They are rarely visited by us, and so play host to many undesirable creatures and väki.
'Search the area near Norsu-leiri! You must find the sorcerer who is giving the Susi-väki these tainted and dark instructions, and defeat him!'
'Blessings of the Ice Spirits on you! The proud and mighty Norsu are safer through your actions.'
Angmarim Sorcery
Mika wants you to defeat the Angmarim Sorcerer who is attempting to train the Gauredain to corrupt Mammoths.
'East and north, at the foot of the hill at the top of which Norsu-leiri was built long ago. That is where I suspect the sorcerer will be.'

The Angmarim sorcerer may be found east and north of Mika's camp.
Search near Norsu-leiri for the Angmarim sorcerer who is teaching the Gauradan the vile rites to ensorcel mammoths.

Norsu-hauta is south and west of the sorcerer's camp.
You should return to Mika in Norsu-hauta and tell him of your victory.
Collected icebay salmon (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
The sea here boils with icebay salmon!

'With the Gauredain gone, we can reclaim this outpost for the Sea-watchers. We know many things about the sea: the way its currents twist and wind, the signs of its anger, and the places where it hides its fish.
'We have turned our eyes to the oceans and found a large kill of fish forced against the shore by the current. Gathering those fish would keep Barad Gaurhoth satisfied and assure us favour in the eyes of the sooth-sayers.
'The fish can be found near the shore where the sea boils and bubbles. Fish there and we will reward you with the blessings of the healers.'
'Ah, the winds sing lauds of our efforts. Surely the favour of those who see the truth is upon us, but take this small gift from us as well, and go in peace.'
'If there are no fish we are not doing what is needed.'
Collect icebay salmon (${CURRENT}/${MAX})
Bring the icebay salmon to Tapio
Bounty of the Sea
The sea-watchers have scouted a large number of fish in the ice bay, but cannot leave their post to go fishing.
Tapio told you to fish where the sea bubbles and boils.
Bring the icebay salmon back to Tapio.
Defeated ice-worms (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'We grow weary. Soon the Gauredain will overtake this outpost.
'The furry worms have encroached upon our outposts. Defeat the creatures and teach them the error of their new boldness.'
'You have defeated some of the ice-worms? The news gives me great pleasure.'
Defeat ice-worms (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Worry About Worms
The threat of the furry worms has been growing in the wake of the Gauradan raids.
'Track the furry worms and defeat them. They grow bold in the wake of the Gauredain raids.'

Ice-worms can be found throughout Talvi-mûri.
Jyrki has asked you to defeat the furry worms that threaten the Lossoth encampments.

Jyrki is at the hunter's way-post at the northern end of Talvi-mûri.
You should return to Jyrki with news of your success.
Reclaimed provisions (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'When the Gauredain stormed into our camp, they stole our supplies: our packed fish, tinder, grease, many things that we must now shiver here without.
'We have dispatched our own parties to find these packages, but any help you could provide would be greatly appreciated.
'The Gauredain are cruel and care little for the actual provisions. Most likely they simply scattered them about. Please search south of here and see if you can reclaim some of them.'
'Oh, how those packed fish call to me! All of these good things you have brought back for us, we are honoured to have had your help.'
'We must have our provisions if we are to remain at this post.'
Bring the provisions to Oiva
Reclaim provisions (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Reclaiming From the Raiders
The Gauredain repeatedly raid Lossoth hunting outposts, both to antagonize the Lossoth and to take their provisions.
Search south of Karhu-leiri for the scattered provisions of the Lossoth.
Collected bear-haunches (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Every day, the Susi-väki raid our stores and steal our food. How are we expected to survive without food?
'Another supply must be found, and I think I have it. We must have meat from the kantâ, or we will be forced to leave this place.
'You can find kantâ -- what I believe you call bears -- throughout Jä-rannit.'
'This meat will do wonderfully...I thank you.'
'Our food-stores are so low! Bring me the bear-meat as I asked.'
Bring the bear-haunches to Raija
Collect bear-haunches (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Harsh Prospects
The Lossoth-outposts were damaged in the last Gauradan-raid. With their stores dwindling, the Lossoth must turn to bears as a source of food.

Bears can be found throughout Jä-rannit. Once you have the meat, bring it to Raija in Karhu-leiri.
Raija has asked you to replenish their stores with bear-meat.
Defeated kalpa-kita in Itä-mâ (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Unbelievable! How were they able to press down on our camp yet again? For many months now, the kalpa-kita have been roaming into Itä-mâ, preying upon small creatures taking shelter near our outpost. As their prey runs low, they move closer to us. We watch for them constantly, but their hides are white like the snow, and they can be still when they lie in wait.
'Last night, they attacked us, and now it is time for them to know the cost of striking at the Lumi-väki.
'Make them flee like the wild creatures they are. Find the kalpa-kita throughout Itä-mâ and make them rue the day they came here.'

'It seems that for the moment our guards will be able to deal with the remaining kalpa-kita. Tonight, we will feast!
'There is no way they should be able to launch another attack for at least a few days.'
Defeat kalpa-kita in Itä-mâ (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Âtos
Encroaching Kalpa-kita
The kalpa-kita have slowly been encroaching on Lossoth territory and are now beginning to launch small raids on Lossoth-outposts virtually every night.
'The kalpa-kita must be made to fear the Lumi-väki. Be their teacher....'

Kalpa-kita can be found throughout the tundra of Itä-mâ.
Âtos has asked you to help purge Itä-mâ of the kalpa-kita scourge.

Âtos is at Pynti-leiri.
Now that you have defeated many kalpa-kita, you should return to Âtos.
Collected Ore (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'I am shivering just standing here! We have dressed in as many furs as we can carry, but the winds become harsh as they whip through this canyon. If we are to maintain our camp here we will need to rely on a more unusual source of fire.
'There is a strange kind of rock which seems to grow out of the snow which is occasionally found in the icy plains. If we set fire to this stone it begins to burn like wood, but will keep burning for much longer. We will keep searching for wood, but if you are able to bring us back more of the fire-stone, our camp will be much better equipped for weeks to come.'
'Thank you, friend. I will light the hearth, and soon we will sit and talk of many travels. My, it is easy to forget how heavy this ore can be!'
'You were unable to collect the ore? We may need to soon pack what we can and make haste away from this place. Hopefully that task is not beyond you.'
Collect Ore (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring the Ore to Turkka
Ore for the Forge

The Lossoth in the eastern tundra have a difficult time staying warm enough in the winters, because of a cold wind that whips through the canyon below.
They have discovered a rare kind of ore, which burns longer than wood.
'Please find the ore we need, I'm too cold to be polite at the moment.'
Search for ore-bearing rocks in the area surrounding Pynti-leiri.
Bring the ore you have collected to Turkka in Pynti-leiri.
Defeated the Great Snow-matron

'It gets tiring, keeping the peikko away from our post. They are persistent, but it is not because they want to harm us.
'The Gauredain are surely provoking these beasts. If we are able to intimidate their herd, the peikko will be so confused when the Gauredain come that they will lash out at them instead of us.
'Defeat the herd's elder, and her cries will surely disrupt the whole herd.'

'It would seem that for the time being, the peikko will let us go about our business. Perhaps the Gauredain will not sleep so easily tonight.
'However, much work remains to be done.'
Defeat the Great Snow-matron
Drive Them Out!
The Snow Beasts have been forced out of the Lossoth outpost in the Western Tundra, but will return unless their matron is defeated.

The Great Snow-matron can be found in the western tundra.
Defeating the Snow-matron will frighten the yeti herd and turn them against the Gauredain.
Collected salt (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Now that the outpost is secure, we can begin gathering a most valuable resource: salt. Our post is assigned the task of watching the springs and collecting chalky salt which can be sold at a handsome price to workers in the southern forests. They use it somehow when they build our sleds.
'We must stay and keep watch. If you can go and collect the salt from the vents, we will make sure to pay you well...'
'Well, this is a fine amount of salt. The sled builders will have quite a lot of work ahead of them! Take with you this token of our appreciation, and our thanks.'
'The salt is not with you I see. Well, I suppose we'll do it ourselves. I was concerned from the beginning about an outsider doing work that is best done by Lossoth.'
Collect salt (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring the salt to Väinö
A Simple Remedy
Chalky salt is an essential export which the Lossoth in the Western Tundra trade to the snow sled builders in the south. The salt is used to cure rawhide strips, which are used as thread.
'Collect some of the salt for us, and we will be sure to reward you.'
Far to the west in Länsi-mâ there are hot springs around which salt encrusted rocks can be found. Gather salt from these rocks to bring back to Väinö in Norsu-leiri.
Return to Väinö in Norsu-leiri with the salt you have collected.
Collected the Jewel of Ice

'The orders you captured from the Angmarim have made several things clear now. The Angmarim do indeed hold the Jä-koru, but they have no intention of turning it over until Forochel lies safely within their grasp.
'Nevertheless, to silence the doubts of the Hylje-heimo, they were recently obliged to bring the Jä-koru into Forochel to prove their claim. Now is the time to strike and reclaim the Jä-koru before they return it to some dark vault in Angmar. It is in the keeping of one of their most trusted captains, a man named Roibeard. He has made camp somewhere within the fortifications of the Ironspan.
'I must ask you to infiltrate that fortress by whatever means possible and wrest the Jä-koru from him.'

'Can it truly be? We had thought ourselves cursed by fate and never to see it again, but you have truly brought it -- the Jä-koru!'
'${PLAYER}, your name will go on in song and story for many generations to come as the one who restored to us our greatest treasure!'
'You must find the Jä-koru, ${PLAYER}. Time is running out and soon it will slip from our grasp forever....'
Bring the Jewel of Ice to Esko at Pynti-peldot
Collect the Jewel of Ice
Claiming the Jewel
Esko has told you that the Hylje-heimo may be swayed to side with the Free Peoples of the South if the Jewel of Ice can be recovered.

Roibeard is at the Angmarim encampments near the Ironspan, north-east of Pynti-peldot.
Esko has told you where the Angmarim are holding the Jewel of Ice. You must retrieve it before it can be returned to the vaults of Angmar.

'One thing remains to be done: you must take the Jä-koru to the Council and present it to Rikitsa. It is important that you be seen returning the Jä-koru to its rightful place before the Council... such a gift should solidify support for an alliance against Angmar within the tribes of the Lumi-väki.
'Rikitsa and the Council are at Sûri-kylä, well to the north.
'My tribe is greatly in your debt -- as are all of us for the friendship this may yet forge between us.'

'Forgive me, but I have no time to speak with one such as... it cannot be! Where did you...? The Angmarim said... no. It does not matter -- is that truly the Jä-koru?
'To finally see it returned to us -- to see the shame of our failure dissolved at last -- such has been the dream of the Hylje-heimo for many generations. To have it given to us freely, as you give it now, that goes beyond even our greatest hopes. I... I fear I have misjudged and said many foolish things in these chambers for the sake of our lost honour. I will work now to rectify that, and the nature of our true enemies -- and our friends -- will be made clear at last.
'Thank you, ${PLAYER}, though words seem too simple to express our gratitude to you for this. I hope you will understand, nonetheless, what it means to us.'

'Why have you come here, ${PLAYER}? Your people have no place among the Lumi-väki. We neither require, nor desire your aid.
'Now begone and do not trouble me again.'
Present the Jewel of Ice to Rikitsa in Sûri-kylä
Treasure of the Lossoth

Long ago, lost in an unknown battle, the Jewel of Ice was the most revered treasure of the Lossoth. Unbeknownst to all, it has been held in Angmar and was used to ransom the obedience of the tribe who was once entrusted with its protection and eternally shamed by its loss.
'The Jä-koru must be taken to Rikitsa at Sûri-kylä.'

Rikitsa is at Sûri-kylä, well north of Pynti-peldot.
Esko has asked you to bring the Jewel of Ice to Rikitsa at the Council.

'You have helped everyone in Zigilgund by your actions, ${PLAYER}, directly and indirectly. You have earned our trust and our gratitude.
'You mentioned to me that you wish to continue to explore the icy wonders of Forochel. To that end, I recommend that you leave Länsi-ma altogether, and head north-east, to the Lossoth capital, Sûri-kylä. There you will find an old acquaintance of mine, a Ranger by the name of Lothrandir.
'It is a long journey. Follow the road east from here, through Itä-mâ, where the road will turn northwards. Once you are in Jä-rannit you will come to several forks in the road; always stay near the edge of the Bay. Curve up north and eventually west, following the norsu-tusks.
'I wish you well, ${PLAYER}. Good-bye and good luck, wherever you fare! Hopefully when you visit again, Zigilgund will once more have been made splendid, and the Icereave Mines will echo with the ringing of picks and toasts over ale!'

'Well met, friend. You have found your way to Sûri-kylä, the fabled Lossoth city in the ice. I understand that there are several folk in need of aid.
'For now, rest, eat, drink, be merry, and be welcome here.'
Speak to Lothrandir in Sûri-kylä
The City in the Ice
Fotri has agreed to give you directions to the famed Lossoth capital, Sûri-kylä.

'Well? What are you waiting around here for?
'I know that the Lossoth are prickly folk, but surely you don't fear the welcome you will receive in Sûri-kylä that much!'
Make your way far to the east and north to Sûri-kylä, the City in the Ice.
Collected Lossoth spear-heads (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Greetings, Etelä-vieras. I welcome you to Forochel. Would you seek to aid the Lumi-väki? If so, then I have a task for you.
'The Lumi-väki have become masters of this icy realm, using our bone-tipped spears to protect ourselves from the great beasts that threaten us in our hunts. Of course, not every spear lands true. So many spear-heads are lost. However, these spear-heads are quite difficult to make, so the loss of even one is bitter to us.
'If you find any of our spear-heads and bring them to me, you will earn the gratitude of all Lumi-väki.'

'Ah good! You have found some of our spear-heads! We will put these back into use soon!
'I will gladly welcome any more you find.'
'Have you found any of our spear-heads yet? We lose many of them in the hides of the great beasts that we hunt. Perhaps if you defeat one of those beasts you will find a one.'
Bring the Lossoth spear-heads to Juha
Collect Lossoth spear-heads (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Lossoth Spear-heads -- Introduction
Juha told you how the Lossoth protect themselves from the aggressive creatures that inhabit Forochel with their bone-tipped spears.

Juha is at Sûri-kylä and Pynti-peldot in Forochel.
Juha has asked you to bring him any Lossoth spear-heads which you find during your travels.
Collected Gauradan-claws (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Ah, ${PLAYER}, you have proven to be a boon companion to the Lumi-väki in our struggles, and now I would ask you to be a further aid to us.
'Perhaps you have heard how sorely pressed we are by the Gauredain. These terrible Men surround us on all sides and threaten our very survival. Thinning their number would be of immeasurable help to us.
'If you do defeat some of these vile creatures, bring me back the strange claws they wield as weapons as proof of your victory.'

'Ah, you have many claws here. Very good. Perhaps these Gauredain will be less of a challenge to us...or at least I so hope!
'If you defeat any more Gauredain, bring me their claws as proof of your victory, and you will earn more esteem in the eyes of the Lumi-väki.'
'Have you defeated any of the Gauredain yet? If so, bring me their claws as proof of your victories!'
Bring the Gauradan-claws to Juha
Collect Gauradan-claws (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Gauradan-claws -- Introduction

Juha told you how the Lossoth are struggling to survive the attacks of the Gauredain. He asked you to defeat some of those evil Men and bring back the claws they wield as weapons as proof of your victory.

Juha is at Sûri-kylä and Pynti-peldot in Forochel.
Juha has asked you to thin the numbers of the Gauredain threatening the Lossoth and to bring him the claws they wield as weapons as proof of your victory.
Collected a Lossoth luistin

'I can see that fortune smiled upon the Lumi-väki when you came to Forochel, friend, for you have done much to help us. I would ask for your aid again, but in a matter less dire than some others.
'Perhaps you have seen the Lumi-väki run across the ice? We do this with bones which we strap to our shoes -- we call them luistin. Our people have used these for centuries, travelling at great speed across the frozen land. At times though, one may stumble and fall and lose a luistin. Such a loss is a bitter one, as these luistin are difficult to make.
'If you encounter any luistin in your travels, bring them to me. I will try to reunite them with their owners.'

'You found one of our luistin! I will try my best to find out who the owner of it is, as I am sure they have missed it.
'Thank you, friend ${CLASS}!'
'You have not found any of our luistin yet? I am not surprised, for we do not lose them often. However, if you do find one, I will gladly take it and try to return it to its owner.'
Bring the luistin to Juha
Collect a Lossoth luistin
Luistin -- Introduction
Juha told you how the Lossoth are able to run across the ice at great speed with the bones they strap to their shoes.

Juha is at Sûri-kylä and Pynti-peldot in Forochel.
Juha has asked you to keep a wary eye open for any of the luistin the Lossoth may have lost during their travels through the frozen wastes and bring them to him.
You have found Juhani

'Your pardon, but I could really use a bit of assistance...
'I've got a good friend, a Hunter by the name of Juhani, who was due back a good little while ago. Went out looking for furs -- kalpa-kita, you know, they have right soft and pretty furs. Sell well, in the south, keep us in pipeweed and ale, as well as non-essential goods and supplies.
'It has now been too long, and I am concerned. Please, go look for him! Kalpa-kita infest an island in the middle of the river, south and a bit east of here.'
Find Juhani
Wayward Hunter
Tero is worried; his colleague and friend Juhani has gone missing.
'Have you not found any trace yet? Might try heading south and looking on the island called Kissa-sari....'

Kissa-sari is an island in the river to the south and slightly east of Zigilgund.
Tero suggests you search an island known as Kissa-sari for his friend Juhani.
Defeated the great winter-worm at the fourth dwarf-channel
Defeated the great winter-worm at the seventh dwarf-channel
Defeated the great winter-worm at the tenth dwarf-channel

'Will you help me? It's the most infuriating problem!
'We are trying to run water from the springs nearby to our encampment -- I want a hot bath! I don't think that's too much to ask, do you? Not in this unrelenting cold.
'Unfortunately, the great winter-worms have other ideas. Have you seen these creatures? Rather like furred drakelings, huge, heat-loving, cold-resistant, and very territorial. There are three water-channels in particular where they have disrupted our work. Please, in the name of steaming hot bathing-chambers everywhere, put a stop to this!
'You will find them north of here, where the water steams.'

'Ha hah! That'll teach 'em!
'Delighted, my dear ${RACE}, simply delighted with you, I must say. I'm one step closer to a long, hot soak. But there appears to be a bit more to do....'
Defeat the great winter-worms (${CURRENT}/${MAX})
Speak to Weth in Zigilgund
Not in Hot Water
Great winter-worms have been interrupting the dwarves' efforts to get hot water from nearby springs. Weth is most annoyed.

'Right, I've had reports and figured out where the worst of the worm attacks are happening. They seem to be concentrated at three channels -- the fourth, seventh, and tenth.
'Ridding us of the big worms at those channels would be worthwhile indeed -- then maybe you can have a nice hot bath too!'
You have made a dent in the population of worms around the dwarf-channels Weth described to you. You should return to him at Zigilgund.
Defeated Ringdagnir

'It would appear our efforts have stirred Ringdagnir, a very large winter-worm. Until his attacks are curbed, there is no hope for my bath.
'Will you do this one more thing for me? Will you defeat Ringdagnir and end the threat of the winter-worms?
'You can find Ringdagnir on the westside of the hot springs near Zigilgund.'

'Bless you, ${PLAYER}! Thanks to you, I have a fighting chance of finally soaking the cold out of my old bones and the grime from off my skin!
'To the bathing-chamber!
'Oh... and please, take this as a reward.'
Defeat Ringdagnir
Return to Weth with news of your success
The Root of the Problem
The root of the problem with the great winter-worms which have been attacking the dwarf-canals seems to lie with a particularly vicious worm dubbed Ringdagnir.
'What are you doing here? Ringdagnir is not going to leave on his own, you know. Go down to where the water steams and drive him out!'

Ringdagnir can be found on the westside of the hot springs near Zigilgund.
Weth has asked you to defeat the great winter-worm Ringdagnir.

Weth can be found in Zigilgund, south of the thermal vents.
You have defeated the great worm Ringdagnir. Weth will be pleased with you.
Defeated peikko in Länsi-mâ (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'So, do you fancy yourself a bit of a hunter? Ha! Of course you do! Few make it through the wastes of Forochel without collecting a tidy variety of trophies. Well, if you are looking for a challenge -- something a little out of the ordinary -- I've got one for you.
'Have you seen the man-shaped, white-furred, snout-faced snow-beasts? They are clever, they are devilishly strong, and they are hard to kill. The Lossoth call them peikko, and they are becoming a more and more serious threat as their numbers increase.
'Kill several of them, and your legacy will be assured. They can be found all over, but especially in a cave they have infested. Go directly east of here and up the side of the hill and look for a cave entrance.'

'Ha! I hope you gave those abominable creatures a taste of your blade, ${PLAYER}!
'That is not the end of the matter, though... there is more to do.'
Defeat peikko in Länsi-mâ (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Keli
Beastly Things
Peikko have long terrorized the snowdrifts of Länsi-mâ. The time has come to deal with them.
'What are you doing here? Afraid or just forgetful? Go kill those peikko! East and up the hill, I said!'

Peikko can be found east and up the mountains from Zigilgund, in a cave.
Keli has asked you to defeat a number of peikko.

Keli can be found at Zigilgund, west of the peikko-cave.
You should return to Keli with news of your victory.
Defeated the great snow-matron

'Well, my fine ${RACE}, it would appear that there is method behind the recent madness of the snow-beasts. The peikko have been stirred up, you see, by the return of the great snow-matron.
'I thought her existence was a bit of a legend, told to us by the Lossoth as a cautionary tale, but it turns out she is quite real. Since she has come back, it is all an honest dwarf can do to make his way through Länsi-ma without having an ice-boulder hurled at his head.
'Do us all a favour, ${PLAYER}: rid Itä-mâ of this threat! I believe she is within the same cave I told you about before: east and up the hill.'
'It would seem there are more and more reasons to sing your praises, ${PLAYER}! You have done well by me and mine.'
Defeat the great snow-matron
Return to Keli at Zigilgund
Mother of Beasts
Keli has figured out why the snow-beasts have been so aggressive recently and wants you to kill their matron.
'What are you doing here when the snow-matron is still living comfortably in that cave? East! Up the hill! Get yourself going.'

The great snow-matron can be found in the cave east and up the hill from Zigilgund.
Keli has asked you to rid Forochel of the great snow-matron who has been stirring up the peikko.

Keli is at Zigilgund, west of the peikko-cave.
You should return to Keli with news of your victory of the great snow-matron.
Collected elk-haunches (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Mining, and the other sort of work we do around here, makes for hungry dwarves, as you can well imagine.
'Our stores are running low, however, especially since one of our supply lines was attacked and looted. We are low on everything -- cloth, ale, tanned leather and hides, fastenings and armour trimmings...the worst, however, is that we're very low on meat.
'Elk-meat dries, smokes, freezes, and cures nicely, as well as making for juicy roasts. Bring me some back, if you can. You can find Elk throughout Länsi-mâ.'

'Excellent! I can practically taste the steaks now.
'We will put a few of these onto the fire right now -- no hungry dwarf will be able to resist that sizzle once they hear it! And the rest will contribute to travel rations and our stores.
'Well done, ${PLAYER}. You will be remembered with every full belly.'
'You can't find Elk? Or are you no good at hunting them? Serves me right for asking a stranger to help.'
Bring the elk-haunches to Ríki at Zigilgund
Collect elk-haunches (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Feeding the Need
Ríki is worried about low supplies for his hungry miners.

Elk can be found throughout Länsi-mâ.
Ríki has asked you to help restock Zigilgund's stores with Elk-meat.

'What brings you to this place, traveller? An expedition of my folk has come to Hollin to seek our kinsman Balin within the vastness of Khazad-dûm, but I deem this has naught to do with your affairs.
'Still, our lords Bósi and Brogur have recommended that we accept whatever help is offered to us in this matter. Did they mean outsiders, I wonder?
'If you truly wish to aid the dwarves in reclaiming the halls of their fathers, speak with Tulk on the other side of this archway. We have not heard from Balin for many years, and we may find the great halls of Khazad-dûm empty, or full of danger.'

'Welcome to Hollin, ${PLAYER}. We have followed our lords Bósi and Brogur here with the purpose of reclaiming the Mines of Moria, lost to us for too many long years. If you are willing to aid us in this venture, we will be grateful for as long as the mountains stand above the halls of our fathers.
'Know this, though: Khazad-dûm was long ago taken from the dwarves by violence and slaughter, and has remained devoid of our kind throughout the long years. Balin led an earlier expedition to reclaim the great city, but there has been no word from him for many a year.
'We do not know what we may find within the Mines of Moria.'
Book 1 -- Chapter 1: Strangers in Hollin
An expedition of dwarves has come to Hollin intending to reclaim the lost halls of Khazad-dûm.
'Tulk is just through this archway. Seek him out if you wish to help the Iron Garrison reclaim Khazad-dûm, ${PLAYER}.'

Tulk is east of the ruined gate near the Walls of Moria, in the south-east of Eregion.
Ráthwald has told you that an expedition of dwarves has come to Hollin to seek out Balin within the halls of Khazad-dûm. He has told you to offer your aid to Tulk just beyond the ruined gate where he keeps watch.
Defeated cave-claws and deep-claws (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

Durin VI is standing with the party in the deep caverns beneath Khazad-dûm.
Durin is waiting to speak with you.

Durin VI is standing with the party in the deep caverns beneath Khazad-dûm.
Durin is waiting for you to clear the cavern of cave-claws and deep-claws.

Durin VI is standing with the party in the deep caverns beneath Khazad-dûm.
Durin is waiting to speak with you.
Durin VI and his party is walking to the mithril deposits in the caverns deep beneath Khazad-dûm.

Durin VI is standing with the party in the deep caverns beneath Khazad-dûm.
Durin is waiting for you to help break through the cracked wall beneath Khazad-dûm.
Some great terror has slumbered beneath Khazad-dûm for a long age.
The dwarves are fleeing from the great terror that has been awakened beneath Khazad-dûm!

Náin is standing with what remains of the party in the deep caverns beneath Khazad-dûm.
Durin has been slain by the terrible creature that slept beneath Khazad-dûm, and now Náin is the ruler of the dwarf-kingdom.

'This cavern is deep and untamed, Nafni, and something seems to have stirred up the cave-claws and deep-claws that burrow here in the depths.
'Be so good as to clear this cave of the beasts so we may proceed to the mithril deposits in safety.'
'Very good, my friend. Now we will show the Elves the great bounty of mithril that still lies beneath Khazad-dûm!'

'We must retreat, Nafni! We have no other option!
'But I swear on my father's name that I shall slay this Balrog, this ancient evil, this horror from a distant age!
'Khazad-dûm will not fall!'

'There thou art, Nafni! Where hast thou been? Lord Durin has been asking for thee; the Elf delegates from Lothlórien are soon due, and he has some business to which he wants thee to attend before they arrive.
'He sits on his throne, Nafni. Go to Durin and lend him thine assistance, as is thy wont and thy duty.'

'The Elves are nearly here, Nafni, escorted by Náin, the son of Durin. They will surely be impressed by the majesty of Durin's halls, but let us not reveal our pride. The way of the dwarf is to be humble before his guests, Nafni, as thou dost know well.
'They shall not but help to marvel at the halls of Durin. Do they not live among the trees? The great pillars of Durin's city are like to trees, but shaped from the very roots of the stone Earth in stunning artistry!'
'I thank thee, Nafni. I see that they have come, and I am ready to speak with them about the continued friendship of the dwarves.'
'We will go at once, and impress upon our visitors the glory and bounty of the dwarves!'

'Thank thee for coming, Nafni. The delegation of Elves will be here very soon, and I had hoped to ask thee something.
'We have not had as many dealings with the Elves as once we did, and it is my hope that this meeting will rekindle the old friendships. The glory and wealth of Khazad-dûm is limitless, even if mithril is becoming more scarce by the year, but with the aid of the Elves we might delve even farther afield.
'We must look to the future. It is to that end that I wish to make a gift to my son Náin, for he will be king when I am gone, though it not be for many years.
'Speak to Melkólf Stonecarver on the western side of the hall about making a statue for my son. It will stand in this throne room when the time of his kingship is nigh.'

'Thank thee, Nafni. Melkólf is an unparalleled artist whose works will always have renown for their place within Khazad-dûm.
'Go to Sverri at the front gate of the throne room and await the delegates from Lórien. My son will be escorting them hither.'

The year is 1980 of the Third Age. You are Nafni, a trusted servant of Durin VI, the Lord of Khazad-dûm, and have no idea what will befall your fellow dwarves on this fateful night.
'Clear this cavern of cave-claws and deep-claws, Nafni! We must be able to proceed to the mithril deposits in safety.'
'I need thee to break through the wall, Nafni. There is sure to be mithril on the other side!'
'Thou must not keep our lord waiting! Speak with Durin by the dais at the north end of this great hall!'
'They are impressed, are they not, Nafni? But do not keep Náin waiting! He has asked to speak with thee!'

'Melkólf Stonecarver is my court sculptor, and does very fine work. He will make a statue worthy of my son Náin, who will reign in Khazad-dûm when I am gone, years hence, if fortune is kind.
'Speak to him on the west side of this hall, where he is wont to stay when he is not working.'
'Tell my father that the party from Lothlórien has arrived, Nafni. He will be at the dais on the north end of the throne-room, as usual.'

'We had not been here long before it became clear that some power was keeping a watchful gaze on Hollin. Filthy crebain have appeared in great numbers, spying on our efforts and troubling the workers. I do not know to what purpose news of our efforts may be put, but their presence has made Bósi uneasy, and that is enough for me.
'To the south, you can see where the Sirannon once flowed, but it has dried up and the stream-bed is now empty. Walk along the banks, defeating any of the spying crebain you see there, and bring me their talons. We can put those vile birds' claws to various uses.
'More importantly, though, you will be hindering whatever fell plan the master of these spies may be brewing for my kinsmen.'
'Thank you for this, ${PLAYER} -- not only for the talons, but for defeating agents of whatever power believes that the dwarves have no business here in Hollin, or in Khazad-dûm.'
'You have not collected enough talons from the spying crebain, ${PLAYER}. Look for them along the dried-up Sirannon, to the south of where we stand.'

Chapter 2: Along the Sirannon
You have offered your services to the expedition of dwarves that has come to Hollin to reclaim the halls of Khazad-dûm beneath the mountains.

'Look to the south along the banks of the dried-up Sirannon if you wish to find the spying crebain that have caused us so much trouble, ${PLAYER}. I do not know whom these filthy birds serve, but I do not believe that their master can mean us any good.'
'I cannot stand crebain. Filthy creatures, and too ready to spy on us.'
'The Sirannon was once a noisy stream, but no longer.'

Spying crebain can be found along the banks of the dried-up Sirannon, south-east of the ruined gate in the area near the Walls of Moria.
Tulk has asked you to defeat the spying crebain along the banks of the Sirannon and to bring him their talons, which can be put to various uses.

Tulk can be found east of the ruined gate in the area near the Walls of Moria.
The dwarf Tulk awaits your return with the talons you collected from the spying crebain along the Sirannon.

'I've written a report for you to bring to Bósi, ${PLAYER}. Show him this document and he will determine how best to utilise your assistance.
'You will find Bósi near some of the waggons beyond the rocky outcropping to the south-east. Just follow the road as it bends around the outcropping and turns north-east.'

'Thank you for bringing me this, ${PLAYER}, and also for your efforts on our behalf. Our work here has been going more slowly than we expected.
'My cousin Brogur and I determined to seek Balin within Moria some months ago, but it took many weeks to assemble an expedition of dwarves willing to accompany us. We chose a roundabout way over the mountains so as to speak with Lord Glóin, a close friend of our fathers, about Khazad-dûm.
'His words were grim; I do not think he believes that our expedition will succeed. 'It has been too long without word,' he said to us, 'for Balin son of Fundin to live still within the Mines.' I am beginning to perceive the likelihood of his warning, ${PLAYER}.
Bring Tulk's report to Bósi
Chapter 3: Bósi the Dwarf
Tulk has asked you to bring a report to Bósi, the leader of the expedition of dwarves. Bósi's kin have come to Hollin purposing to enter Moria.

'If you follow the road south-east as it bends around the rocky outcropping you see there, you will find Bósi by the waggons as the road turns north-east.
'Bring him the report I gave you. He will find something for you to do to aid in our efforts here.'
'Hello, ${PLAYER}.'
'How goes the work, friend?'
'Thank you for bringing my report to Bósi.'
'What awaits us within Moria, I wonder?'

Bósi is overseeing some of the waggons along the road through Hollin, south-east from the Hollin Gate and then bending to the north-east.
Tulk has given you a report to bring to Bósi, one of the dwarves leading the expedition to Hollin.
Collected broken pick-axes

'When we arrived at the Hollin Gate some days ago, we found the Doors of Durin sealed by rubble and debris. Our road seems poorly chosen now; I wonder if the Dimrill Gate on the eastern side of the mountains is open.
'Dwarves of our expedition have been working to unearth the Gate, but it is lean and hungry work. Bring them these lunches so that they may harbour strength for the labours ahead.
Travel north up the slope between the rocky walls and you will find workers resting all along the path to the Hollin Gate, and there are more along the edge of the water before the Doors. Speak with Wárr at the Gate when you have done this, and he will have further tasks for you.'

'You've come at just the right time, ${PLAYER}. We're really going through pick-axes up here, and if we break any more it will hinder our progress in digging out the Hollin Gate.
'Bring these broken pick-axes back to Lord Bósi, and tell him that we'll need some replacements, and quickly, if we are to continue making good progress.
'You will find him near the bank of the Sirannon, south of the winding road that ends here at the Gate.'

'Ah, thank you for this. I was afraid I might waste away without something to eat soon!
'We'll have unearthed the Hollin Gate before too long, but it's not easy work. We work in shifts in order to get the job done as efficiently as possible.'
'You haven't brought a lunch for me?'

'Hello there, and thank you for this lunch. My stomach was just beginning to grumble.
'My kinsmen are wondering what it is we'll find within Khazad-dûm: Lord Balin, alive and well? Great riches of mithril? Countless Orcs and goblins?
'I suppose we'll see, but I'm hoping for the mithril.'
'You don't have a lunch for me?'

'You have my thanks for the lunch, but I will have to eat it when my shift is done.
'We'll be through this rubble in no time. 'Tis odd, though; my pick tells me that this debris hasn't yet settled. I'd wager a waggonful of Moria-silver that this collapse happened recently.'
'I want a lunch, and you have not brought me one.'

'Ah, a prepared lunch! Lord Bósi is doing a fine job keeping us fed and rested. We will repay both him and Lord Brogur with all of our strength, and be through this rubble in no time!
'What will we find beyond this Gate, I wonder?'
Deliver prepared lunches to dwarf-workers (${CURRENT}/${MAX})

Chapter 4: Outside the Gate
Bósi has asked you to help re-supply the workers attempting to unearth the Hollin Gate with lunches in order to keep their spirits high.

'You're going the wrong way, friend; these stairs are blocked at the top by a stagnant pool. If you're looking for the road up to the Doors of Durin, you want to turn around. Keep the grey stone of the cliffs on your right, and follow it back the way you came, towards my uncle Bósi.
'If you follow the line of cliffs, keeping them on your right, you will find the road that winds up to the Doors.'
'Bring those lunches to the workers along the road north of here that winds up to the Hollin Gate. They will need the sustenance to maintain their strength.'
'Thank you for delivering those lunches. You should now speak with Wárr, supervising the work at the Hollin Gate.'
'Bring those pick-axes to Lord Bósi and request some replacements, or we will have to abandon the work here at the Hollin Gate until we can make more tools.'
'I haven't had any tidings from Wárr for some time. I wonder how his supplies have been holding up. Did he not have a message for me?'
'Where is my lunch? I will need it when my shift is over, you know.'

'This lunch will be just the thing to refresh me after my long labour, and I thank you for it.
'We would not have followed just anyone here to Hollin and the darkness of Khazad-dûm. Lords Bósi and Brogur are young, true, but they are stout of heart and their fathers earned great renown as part of Thorin's Company. This could be our chance to achieve glory of the same kind.'
'Where is my lunch? Surely you haven't forgotten it!'

'Thank you for this lunch. I will eat it in a moment.
'There is something about this lake I do not like, but I cannot figure out what it is. It makes me uneasy.'
'You have not brought me a lunch?'

'Thank you for the lunch. You are truly courageous to help us thus...or have you not yet heard the tale of Durin's Bane?
'At any rate, you have my thanks!'
'No lunch for me? What is this madness?'

'Oh, I see. These pick-axes are broken, which means that unless we can get replacements to Wárr, all work on excavating the Hollin Gate will be suspended. We have to do something about this, ${PLAYER}, and quickly!'

Dwarf-workers can be found north of Bósi's encampment, all along the winding road that runs up to the Hollin Gate.

'We had no way of knowing the Gate would be in this state, ${PLAYER}, and didn't think to bring extra pick-axes with us. Still, this area has many stout trees which should provide ample strong branches, perfect for pick-handles. We'll sharpen the metal heads ourselves and attach them to the new handles.
'I sent my son Bori to collect stones upon which we could sharpen our axes, but he has yet to bring me any. Gather branches from the bases of trees and help my son collect sufficiently sharp stones, and return to me when you have done both. Bori is probably wasting time with his friend Bróin at the stairs east of here. Those two care more for the spinning of tales than they do for working!'
'You have my thanks once again, ${PLAYER}. All the materials have been gathered, and my dwarves will begin working on new pick-axes right away.'
'It is very important that we have the branches needed to repair the pick-axes. How else can we remove the rubble that blocks the Doors of Durin?'
'You have not yet brought me enough thick branches, ${PLAYER}. Look for them at the bases of trees around the area.'

'We'll get those pick-axes to the workers right away.'
'There is still a great deal of work to be done.'

'Hello, ${PLAYER}. Did father send you to oversee on the charge he gave me? To tell you the truth, it hasn't been going very well.
'I was supposed to find suitable stones for sharpening the pick-axes for the workers at Hollin Gate, and I did find two of them, but then I got a little distracted. My friend Bróin and I have been discussing the treasures we might find within Moria, you see, and I lost track of the time.
'I'll give you these two stones I already found, if you like. Find the rest of them for me and I won't forget it! I had some luck looking along the dry bed of the Sirannon, but not every stone there is suitably sharp.'

'Perfect! These stones are just what my father wanted me to collect, and will surely sharpen our pick-axes to a fine point indeed.
'Bróin and I cannot wait to get into Moria proper; that is where the real glory awaits! I don't mean to look down upon the work everyone is doing out here, but the real adventure is waiting in the depths. Dangers unmeasured, I'll not doubt, but treasure in equal score, and honour, and renown!
'You have my thanks for your assistance, ${PLAYER}.'
'Look for stones along the dry bed of the Sirannon, but know that not every stone will be sharp enough for my father's purpose.'

'Bori is a good lad, and will grow into a fine dwarf. I reckon his preference for tale-spinning over hard work will pass in time. My cousin Brogur and I were no different when we were his age.
'It will take some time to fashion pick-axes from the materials you have delivered. While my dwarves are working on that, I ask you to lend your aid to Brogur. If you truly wish to assist the dwarves, not a moment shall be idly spent!
'You will find my cousin north of here, somewhere along the road that winds up to the Hollin Gate. He is gruff, even for his line, but will welcome your help.'

'What did you say your name was? ${PLAYER}?
'Is that even a real name? You'll need to work especially hard to make up for that!'
Chapter 6: Cousin Brogur
Bósi thanked you for your part in gathering materials for the crafting of new pick-axes, and sent you to Brogur so you may lend your aid to his cousin.

'Brogur is stern like his father before him, but respects strength and friendship. He will welcome your aid.
'Look for him north of here, along the road that winds up to the Hollin Gate.'

Bósi's cousin Brogur is somewhere along the road that winds up to the Hollin Gate, north of Bósi's position.
Bósi has asked you to lend your aid to his cousin Brogur while the pick-axes are being crafted.

'Some madness has seized the wolves of this area, driving the creatures into blind fury. They are far more aggressive than is usual for their kind, and I fear they may attack our expedition before long.
'Can you hear their shuddering voices on the wind? I sent my son Bróin to challenge these beasts of Shadow, but he has not returned. He is probably wasting time with my cousin's boy, wagging his tongue by the stairway yonder.
'Return to the Sirannon's dry river-bed and climb the opposite bank whence the fell clamour comes. There is a cave, Filgogân, in the far south-west there. It could be that you will find some explanation for the creatures' wrath within that cave. I fear you must help my son with his task, for he has not yet spoken with me about its successful completion! Talk to my cousin Bósi when you're finished.'

'You say you found a burned wolf-corpse on the other side of the Sirannon? I do not have the answer to this mystery, ${PLAYER}.
'While you were helping my cousin, the new pick-axes were finished. They are of very high quality and will surely be of great help at the Hollin Gate.'
Find the cause of the wolves' madness
Help Bróin with the task Brogur gave him
Chapter 7: Wolf-voices on the Wind
Brogur is concerned about the unusually aggressive behaviour of the wolves in the area and wants them handled.

'My son Bróin is probably wasting time by the stairs, idling away the hours with ceaseless chatter. The source of the shadow-wolves' madness is likely south of here, across the dry river-bed of the Sirannon. Perhaps you will find some clue in the cave Filgogân, in the south-western corner of this area?'

The cause of the wolves' fearsome behaviour may be found among their lairs, south of Brogur's location and across the Sirannon's dry river-bed. Brogur believes the cave Filgogân may hold some clue to the wolves' madness, in the far south-western corner of the area. You have learned something of the Shadow-wargs' madness and aided Bróin with his task, and have been asked to speak now with Bósi.
Defeated shadow-wargs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'You're the traveller who helped Bori with gathering those stones, aren't you? I thought so -- I have an eye for faces, and never forget a name, especially one belonging to an adventurer! Of course, the more dangerous deeds you accomplish, the more memorable you'll be, ${PLAYER}!
'That's what I'm hoping to do, you know. Once we get inside Khazad-dûm, Bori and I will become great heroes, and stories of our adventures will be told all over the land. Years from now, 'The Glorious Tale of Bróin the Mighty' could inspire young dwarves just as the songs of Durin and of Thorin Oakenshield inspire Bori and me today!
'If you'd like to help me with the task my father gave me, though, I wouldn't turn it down. There are shadow-wargs to the south, across the bed of the dried-up Sirannon. Defeat some of the beasts for me, if you would; I've already slain one of them, but that's not really enough. May good fortune be with you, friend!'

'You have returned, ${PLAYER}, and in victory over the shadow-wargs! You truly are an adventurer of great worth, are you not?
'In all honesty, my battle with that shadow-warg wasn't exactly worthy of song; I was too frightened to do more than survive. I guess I'm not much of a hero. Is it in me to do great deeds? Will there ever be a song sung about me, or will my name be forgotten?
'You are most kind, ${PLAYER}. I hope I will soon have the chance to prove myself as you have done.'
Defeat shadow-wargs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

Chapter 7: The Glorious Tale of Bróin the Mighty
Brogur's son Bróin has asked for your help fighting off the dangerous Shadow-wargs that lurk beyond the Sirannon's banks.

'I really appreciate this, ${PLAYER}. Your battles with the dangerous shadow-wargs are sure to be an important part of your tale.
'You'll find them south of here, on the other side of the Sirannon's dry river-bed.'

'Let me know when you are ready, ${PLAYER}, and we will walk together to the Doors of Durin. With these newly-repaired pick-axes, our dwarves will soon clear the way into Moria.'

'We are in full retreat, ${PLAYER} -- the beast of the pool is too much for our meagre weapons!
'If only we had some relic of the old days, we might stand a chance against the creature. The weapons of our Fathers were of a stronger and keener make, their craft forgotten; today's forge-skill is lesser.
'A cache of weapons was discovered in one of the caves near here shortly after we arrived. Perhaps one of those will stand worthy as a bane to this monster.'
Talk to Bósi and travel to the Doors of Durin

The dwarves of Bósi and Brogur's expedition await the opening of the Doors of Durin.
