'We will stop at the outpost here for a moment before continuing on to the gates, ${PLAYER}. We will need to establish a camp once we are inside the mines, and I want to ensure that everything is prepared.
'You still have the pick-axes, yes? Good. Follow me.'

'What is it, ${PLAYER}? You say you saw something stir out in the water? What was it?
'I don't see anything now. Are you sure you didn't imagine it?'

'You have been a great help to us in our work here in Hollin, ${PLAYER}, and I know that you will be a great boon once we are inside Khazad-dûm proper.
'I would hereby be honoured if you would bear a pick-axe and help us to clear away the remainder of this rubble that blocks the Doors of Durin. This is an historic opportunity, friend ${CLASS}, and it is my joy to offer it to you in return for the many services you have given us already.'

'Did you see how the flesh of that creature deflected our blows, ${PLAYER}? We need more than ordinary weapons if we wish to stand against the Watcher of the Black Pool!
'It waited in the depths, watching as we strove to open the doors, and struck just as we were most vulnerable. Curse its foul hide for taking Bróin, and many other fine dwarves beside!
'They will be avenged, but for now we must retreat. We cannot hope to enter the Doors while it lurks before them.'

'Those pick-axes will be a great help, ${PLAYER}, even if you took your time bringing them here. Our workers are almost through the rubble already!
'Don't worry about that; what's done is done. I'm more concerned with this pool -- there's something about it I don't like. It makes me feel uneasy.
'Some of my dwarves have been casting stones into the water, and I'd appreciate it if you could get them to stop. It makes me nervous.'

'Very good, ${PLAYER}. I appreciate your help. I understand that many of my dwarves are restless, but there's just something about that water I don't like. I will be relieved when the workers have finished removing the rubble from in front of the gate and we can leave this unpleasant shore.'
'We must retreat with what survivors remain. We will return to visit our vengeance upon the Watcher in the Black Pool!'
'I don't like this, ${PLAYER}; something is wrong. The air is too still and quiet.'

'Very good. These pick-axes look to be in good shape, and will be a great asset as we finish unearthing the last of this rubble.
'You can leave them in that crate to the south there, right next to Lord Brogur.'

Found Thurmaer's lucky arrow

'Curse my luck! Everything has gone wrong of late, and now I am stuck here in this tiny camp in the middle of nowhere. Without my finest arrow, I've no hope of putting things aright again either. I need your help, if I can beg it of you!
'Since I was separated from my fellows and found myself in this farthest and coldest extent of Forochel, things have only gone from bad to worse. Now I have lost my lucky arrow -- I know it flew truly and struck that worm I was hunting, but moments after I let it fly, I was ambushed by a band of Gauradan-hunters! I escaped from their ambush and made my way back here, but I twisted my ankle badly during the flight and cannot retrieve my precious arrow. It has been with me for many a long hunt now and to lose it this way -- it is a terrible omen, I say.
'I am sure my arrow remains in the scaly hide of that worm. The hunters in this camp call it Beleganc and say it is the most cunning of its breed upon the glacier. Finding it out there will be no simple task I fear.'

'Aha, my lucky arrow! You found it!
'Many thanks! Perhaps my luck is beginning to turn for the better at last. After the last several days, I had begun to wonder if things would ever turn for the better.
'Now all I have to do is find my map!'

'No luck finding my arrow? Well, it has been that kind of week for me.
'At least there is no-one here who seems to know cards, or I would have surely lost every coin to my name by now, the way things are going.'
Find the worm Beleganc and retrieve Thurmaer's arrow from it

Thurmaer lost his favourite 'lucky arrow' during a recent hunt in Talvi-mûri. He was stalking a particularly cunning Snow-worm and had just loosed his arrow when he was ambushed by a band of Gauradan-hunters and was forced to flee. Though he made it to shelter, Thurmaer twisted his ankle during his flight.
'Will you recover my arrow from the worm Beleganc?'

Found Thurmaer's Map

'All of this started to go wrong after we were separated by a blinding snow-storm. I was ambushed by the Gauredain after losing my way. It was there that I lost the map. The battle was tumultuous, and once it was over, we were scattered and the map was gone -- stolen, I think, by the retreating Gauredain.
'Well -- and I hate to admit this as a hunter and scout -- but my sense of direction is not exactly the best. I make up for it by being an excellent navigator, but without that map there was not much I could do to help find the others, and eventually I found myself all the way up here.
'I need to get that map back if I am ever going to find the rest of my fellowship! Can you help me hunt down the Gauredain until we find the one who stole it?'

'I see you have managed to retrieve my map at last. I owe you greatly for this!
'It seems that my luck may finally be back on track, thanks to you. Soon I shall be able to set out to find the rest of my Fellowship and reunite them at last.'
'Good luck and good hunting to you!'

'If I cannot find that map, I will never be able to find the rest of my fellowship.
'It is my fault they are all lost -- I should never recover, I think, if one of them dies because of my mistake....'

'Ah, a face from civilized lands at last! Perhaps you can help me? Our fellowship came here to Forochel a few days ago, but through folly and mishap we became separated. I have spent the last two days fleeing through this trackless wilderness trying to escape from wild beasts and wild men alike, until finally I found some refuge here.
'Imagine my dismay when I discovered that several sheets of my most prized anthem had been lost during my flight! I need to get those sheets back! Thinking back through my misadventures of the last few days, I think I know where they might have been lost. You see, there was this enormous bear, which tried to steal the rations from my pack before I managed to calm the creature with my songs and slip away -- only to stumble into a band of those horrid snow-beasts or whatever they are -- I think the locals call them peikko? In any case, I had nearly beguiled the lot of them with my finest performance yet, when a Gauradan-hunter snuck up and nearly put a spear through me!
'Needless to say, those wild men are poor patrons of the arts at best, and I took my cue to flee into the night. It was not until I later found a chance to collect my wits that I realized my prized anthem was gone! Will you please hunt down those horrid beasts and retrieve my music? I may be able to make it worth your while.'

'You found them? You found them all! Oh thank you so much!
'This is one of the greatest anthems of our age -- er, that is, it will be once I have finished it. You will come by to hear my performance when it is ready, won't you? I should be able to finish it once I find the rest of my fellowship, and we get out of this forsaken wilderness.
'There is just one more little problem though....'
'Oh, ${PLAYER}, please can you help me find those missing sheets? I really cannot bear to lose them like this.'

Three Sheets to the Wind

After becoming separated from the rest of her fellowship by a storm, Burgthryth was pursued through the wilderness by a variety of hostile beasts. During the course of her flight, she lost some of her most prized sheets of music and despairs of ever finding them again.

Burgthryth believes the first of her sheets was swiped from her pack by a Tundra Bear. You will have to hunt them down until you find the one that stole it -- assuming it has not already been devoured.

Collected some cat-gut
That is disgusting...

'I am sorry to be so much trouble, ${PLAYER}, but I could use your help with one more thing before I set out to find the rest of my fellowship. You see, while you were out trying to retrieve my pages, I decided to give it a try myself. Unfortunately, while I was travelling along the banks of the river to the south-west, I came face-to-face with the biggest kalpa-kita I have yet seen here -- and he looked hungry!
'Well, to make a long story short, you know how they say that music soothes the savage beast? Ha! Do not wager your life on it! That horrid cat barely let me get out the first verse before he ripped the strings right out of my prized lute! I was so angry I could have bashed him senseless with my lute right then and there -- but then I would need a new lute and not just a new set of strings, so I ran instead.
'As for the strings, I have just the thing -- could you find that sabre-tooth and drag his sorry carcase back to me? I have never used cat-gut strings before, but I think now is the perfect time to give them a try! The Lossoth here say they have hunted this cat before without much luck -- they call him Laulu-vihâja... he supposedly has a den on that island in the Lune.'

'You got him? Wonderful! That will teach that stupid cat to disdain my talent! I hope he sounds good. Ah well, nothing but to get him strung up and give him a try....
'Thank you, ${PLAYER}. I will have to be off soon to try and find the rest of my fellowship -- wherever they have wandered to in this awful place. I hope I see you again someday!'
'You still haven't found that accursed beast? Oooh, it makes me so mad to think of him wandering around out there, waiting to pounce on some other poor unsuspecting minstrel....'

'Thank you for finding me out here -- but I am afraid I cannot go back with you. You see, when the Captain led those Angmarim off as he fled, a few remained and gave me a good chase too. I was able to escape, but...
'...but you see, I dropped his banner in my flight! Oh, I am a worthless herald! The Angmarim took it and returned with it to their camp out on the ice somewhere.
'It has been in the Captain's family for generations -- my father carried it for the Captain's father, and his father before that and so on. I cannot go back and face him without that banner. Please help me retrieve it!'

'A fine greetings to you again, ${PLAYER}! Any luck finding my wayward herald out there?
'Yes? Splendid! Plucky little fellow isn't he? I knew he'd come through all right. My sincere and heartfelt thanks to you for your help, friend.
'I suppose I'd best go retrieve him, shall I then? Once we've got that matter in order, then we'll need to find the rest of the Fellowship!
'Good luck to you, ${PLAYER}, should our paths cross again and you need my aid, you just let me know.'

'You found it? Ah, you are a wonder, ${PLAYER}. You have saved my honour and that of my family!
'Now that I have got the banner back, I can finally make my way to Sûri-kylä and meet up with the Captain again. What a relief! No, I would never have expected him to come out here looking for me. No-one in that entire fellowship has the slightest sense of direction you know, even the hunter!
'So, if you would be so kind as to give him detailed directions on where he can find me, I would be much obliged. It is a bit too dangerous for me to go wandering around on my own out here.'
'Please, you've just got to get that banner back for me. I can't possibly face Captain Ward having lost it for good.'

'Ah! 'Tis good to see a face from the south in this harsh land. The locals are a fine enough sort but not the friendliest towards strangers, if you know what I mean. Perhaps you could see your way towards helping out a fellow countryman in need? You see, my fine young herald has gone missing! Several days ago the two of us were separated from our most excellent fellowship during a battle to the south. Afterwards, my herald and I came further north, hoping to re-group here in Sûri-kylä -- unfortunately, we stumbled upon a patrol of vile Angmarim on our way here!
'Well, though I fought valiantly, my herald somehow managed to lose his way in the confusion of battle -- you know how heralds are, no sense of direction whatsoever -- anyway, I am certain he managed to escape, but since then I have seen no sign of my faithful companion.
'I know this region poorly at best and would be most indebted to you if you could help me find my wayward herald. I cannot go off in search of the rest of my fellowship until I have him safely in tow again!'

'Thank goodness you are here! I was wondering if anyone would ever find me out here before I froze to death!
'Did Reginald send you? He is not here with you, is he?'
Find Reginald Ward's missing herald
An Unheralded Hero

Reginald Ward has not only become separated from his Fellowship, but seems to have mislaid his herald as well. The two were separated during a battle against the Angmarim on the shelf at the edge of the Ice Bay, south-east of Sûri-kylä. Reginald is hoping that someone more familiar with the lands of Forochel can help him find his lost herald.
'Have you found my herald yet? I'm quite concerned about the young fool!'

Reginald's herald was lost somewhere on the ice-shelf, south-east of Sûri-kylä, on the eastern edge of the Ice Bay of Forochel. Reginald Ward is at Sûri-kylä, north-west of the ice-shelf.
Reginald Ward asked you search for his herald and return him to Sûri-kylä.

'Can this be? You have helped me and all of my companions? I would not have believed it could happen. We were in such a state that I thought we would never get back to looking for the lost treasure. You truly are a hero to me and mine, friend.
'Please go and tell our Captain, Reginald Ward in Sûri-kylä of your great feat!'

'It would appear you have done a great service for myself and all my wayward companions, ${PLAYER}. All that remains for us is to regroup and begin our search for the lost treasure once more!
'Quickly now, tell our Captain, Reginald Ward, of your great feat! He can be found in Sûri-kylä here in Forochel.'

'What is this? You have aided my lost companions and myself? Amazing! I had nearly given up hope of all of us having our ills addressed, but thanks to your efforts, all has been set to right!
'Please now, go quickly and tell my party's Captain, Reginald Ward, of what you have done for us! He can be found in Sûri-kylä here in Forochel.'

'From what you tell me, it seems like you have aided all of us, myself and my wayward companions! I am greatly in your debt. I must think up a suitable reward for you, give me just a moment, please....'

'Now that I hear your tale, I am stunned. You have encountered all of my lost companions and helped them as best you could? What joyous news! Perhaps we will find that lost treasure yet!
'Quick now, go and tell my Captain, Reginald Ward, about your great deeds! The last that I heard was that he could be found somewhere near Sûri-kylä.'

'I shall sing a great song of your selflessness, ${PLAYER}. You have done all that my wayward companions and I have asked of you and have sought very little reward. Now that all our woes have been addressed, I am sure our party shall regroup and go in search of the lost treasure once more!
'Quickly now, bear this wonderful news to my Captain, Reginald Ward, in Sûri-kylä.'

'What a mess we were in, but from the sound of it, you have untangled all my companions' problems, ${PLAYER}. And now you have helped me as well! Soon our party will regroup, and we will find that lost treasure...I know it! I can almost feel the gold coins running through my hands now!
'Please, go and tell my party's Captain, Reginald Ward, of your success. He should be near Sûri-kylä. You never know, he may have a reward for you.'

'I am nearly speechless with joy, ${PLAYER}. The good you have done for my companions and me will not soon be forgotten. In fact, I still cannot get over the fact that you helped Cenlieg the Lore-master. I can hardly stand the man! Oh well, the treasure we seek will make it all worthwhile, in the end... at least, that is what I hope.
'Now, friend, do not let me trouble you further. You have done us all a great service, and perhaps if we do discover the treasure, I shall share a small portion of it with you. For now, all I can offer is my gratitude and a small token of my esteem.'

'Now that you have learned the ways of the fisherman you will be needing supplies. Though the Elves of Rivendell excel in the craft, a Man of the Trollshaws -- Garbert by name -- has fallen on difficult times.
'Garbert was injured, as Men so commonly are, and cannot travel. His sale of fish and fishing supplies has been much diminished, and I worry for him and his family. He is very skilled in matters of the rivers and waters for a Man; his prowess almost reaches that of Elrond's folk.
'If you wish to find supplies, I would ask that you visit Garbert. He should be at his cottage in Tâl Bruinen, south of here, near to the river.'

'Why, hello there! It is unusual to see a fellow fisherman this far down the Loudwater, what with the times being what they are these days.
'You say the Elves sent you? I have had dealings with some of their folk, but I did not know that they thought so highly of me to send me business in my need!'
Talk to Garbert
Hook, Line, and Sinker
Haldúr has informed you that Garbert has fallen on hard times and could use some business.
'Have you visited Garbert? His cottage is south and west of Rivendell along the Bruinen in Tâl Bruinen.'

Garbert is at his cottage in Tâl Bruinen, south and west of Rivendell.
Haldúr has asked that you visit Garbert and purchase fishing supplies from him because of his injuries.

'Hullo there, ${PLAYER}. How do you do this fine day? I'm in an awful spot of trouble; perhaps you can assist me?
'It is my sister, Misty Bolger, you see. She is the muscle of the family, while I am the brains. It is she who goes out each day and fishes our daily catch, and I keep track of the sales and teach young fishermen the trade.
'It seems that last night my notes were used as a napkin for a simply delectable fish medley. Those notes had the totals and sales of our fish for the last week! Could you please go and see my sister in Bywater and ask her if she recalls the number of fish that she caught last week?'

'Used the notes as a napkin -- what will he do next? I am out here fishing every day for our keep, and he can't even keep track of his own notes!
'It is a good thing that I always keep records of my own. This isn't the first time Estmar has accidentally had his notes go missing.
'I will send another copy to him right away! Thank you, ${PLAYER}.'
Talk to Misty Bolger
One Fish, Two Fish
Estmar Bolger has accidentally lost the notes pertaining to his family business.
'Have you visited my sister yet? She is east and north of Michel Delving in the town of Bywater.'

Misty Bolger is north and east of Michel Delving in the town of Bywater.
Estmar Bolger has asked that you visit his sister, Misty Bolger, and find out how many fish she caught last week.

'At your service, ${CLASS}. Now that you have learned the ways of the fisherman, perhaps you could aid me in delivering a message to an old friend.
'I wish to inform Nokki of my latest catch, the largest I have ever seen and I daresay the largest ever caught in Ered Luin! It was enormous, I tell you -- nearly a stone in weight! A pity that I don't have proof of my catch, for after I had the beast in my bucket it made a mighty leap and escaped back into the channel.
'Go to Noglond and speak with Nokki. Tell him of my catch and see if he has caught any bigger.'

'Another fish-tale from Refkell? You are the third person this week to come from him with stories of a giant catch that managed to slip through his fingers.
'But never mind that. If you are in need of fishing supplies you will find no greater store of equipment to suit your needs anywhere else.'
Talk to Nokki
Refkell is incredibly proud of his last catch and wishes to show it off to his friend.
'Have you told Nokki my tale? He is at Noglond, south of Thorin's Hall, along the road to the Low Lands.'

Noglond is south of Thorin's Hall, south and east of the Vale of Thrain, along the road to the Low Lands.
Refkell has asked that you visit Nokki and tell him of his latest catch.

'Hail, ${PLAYER}. Now that you have learned the subtleties of fishing, perhaps you could aid me in a small task?
'I have a business arrangement with a fisherwoman, Joy Bloomer, in Staddle. She often brings up choice cuts of fish, as well as a number of oddities that she finds while fishing in the rivers and lakes of Bree-land. I, for my part, send her business and keep her supplied with items that she cannot acquire in Staddle.
'Bring her news that her latest shipment has been sent. You will find Joy Bloomer east of here, in the town of Staddle. You will arrive on foot well before her shipment reaches her, and I would give her the peace of mind knowing she will soon have her supplies.'

'Ah, word of my supplies! Thank you, ${PLAYER}. I have been expecting this delivery for some time now.
'And what of yourself? It seems that you have the look of a fisherman about you. Henry Oakeshott has always sent me the finest fishermen, and I, in turn, have supplied them with only the finest gear. If you are looking for fishing supplies, you need look no further than Joy Bloomer!'
Talk to Joy Bloomer
Teach a Man to Fish
Henry Oakeshott has prepared a shipment of supplies for Joy Bloomer, a local fisherwoman, and needs someone to deliver a message to her.
'Have you brought Joy Bloomer word of her supplies? Please hurry along and tell her, she is east of Bree in the town of Staddle if you have forgotten.'

Joy Bloomer is in Staddle, east of Bree.
Henry Oakeshott has asked that you speak with his business partner, Joy Bloomer, and assure her that her shipment will arrive soon.

'A summons arrived here by raven this morning, ${PLAYER}, calling you to the House of Elrond, far to the east. I do not know why Elrond Halfelven requests your presence, but it must be for an errand of some urgency if he sends ravens on the wing here to Echad Garthadir.
'Does the Elf-lord have need now for the strength of the Race of Men? That friendship was never sundered, tested though it be by the passage of Time.
'You will find the House of Elrond far to the east, in the hidden vale of Rivendell, beyond the Trollshaws.'

'${PLAYER}, may I have a word with you? Master Elrond requests your presence in Rivendell on a matter of some urgency. His messenger did not reveal the reason for this summons, but said only that Elrond has need now of the strength of the Race of Men.
'Travel along the eastern road beyond the Trollshaws to the hidden vale of Rivendell and speak with Elrond in his house. We will do our best to stand against the Shadow in your absence, and wait eagerly for your return.'

'${PLAYER}, I have a message for you: Master Elrond requests your presence in Rivendell on a matter of some urgency. His messenger did not reveal the reason for this summons, but said only that Elrond has need now of the strength of the Race of Men.
'Descend from the mountains and return to the vale of Rivendell that you might speak with Elrond in his house. We will do our best to stand against the frozen dangers here and wait eagerly for your return.'

'Master Elrond wishes to speak with you, ${PLAYER}. He says the Elves have need of the strength of the Race of Men and wishes you to speak with him about some matter of urgency.
'Go inside and speak with Master Elrond in his library.'

'Welcome, ${PLAYER}. I am pleased to see you well. We must be thankful for every journey that ends in safety, for these are dangerous times and the shadows grow ever long outside Rivendell.
'A small company will soon be setting forth on a mission of great secrecy to combat this growing dark; I am loath to speak in detail of their errand, but know that it will do great hurt to the Enemies of this Age if they succeed.
'The fate of the Race of Men concerns you closely, ${PLAYER}, and I know that you are trustworthy. Two doughty Men prepare to set forth on this perilous journey; lend them your assistance as they prepare to leave. I speak of Aragorn son of Arathorn and Boromir of Gondor. Look for them in one of the guest rooms along the road that winds up the southern slope of the Vale of Imladris.'
'Thank you for helping Aragorn and Boromir with their preparations, ${PLAYER}. The fate of all your people is bound to the success of the mission they must undertake.'
Talk to Elrond in Rivendell
Help Boromir with his preparations
Help Aragorn with his preparations
Talk to Elrond in Rivendell
Foreword: Bulwark of the West
The Men of the West have long stood against the Shadow, and their courage is needed once again.
'You represent all members of the Race of Men, ${PLAYER}. Speak to Elrond Halfelven in the library of his house in Rivendell with courtesy, but let him know too of our strength.'
'Travel to Rivendell and speak with Master Elrond within the library of his house. I will wait for you here.'
'Descend from the mountains and return to Master Elrond's house; he waits for you in the library and should not be kept waiting.'

'Though sundered by geography and the long miles, the fate of the Race of Men lies heavily upon Aragorn, Boromir, and yourself, and binds you all together.
'Speak with them in the guest rooms along the road that winds up the southern slope of the Vale of Imladris and aid them in their preparations.'
'Go inside and speak with Master Elrond, ${PLAYER}. You will find him waiting for you within the library.'
'The Race of Men must stand against the growing dark.'
'You are a worthy representative of your people, ${PLAYER}.'

Elrond is in the library of his house in Rivendell.
Elrond Halfelven has summoned you to speak with him on some urgent matter.

Aragorn and Boromir can be found in one of the guest rooms along the road that winds up the southern slope of the Vale of Imladris.
Elrond has asked that you help your fellow Men, Aragorn son of Arathorn and Boromir of Gondor, prepare to leave on their dangerous -- and secret -- mission.

Elrond is in his library within the Last Homely House, in Rivendell.

'Hello there, ${PLAYER}; it's always a pleasure to see a friendly face! I imagine Elrond was reluctant to let you know about the journey we are leaving on, but I think Gandalf might have had something to do with allowing it. He is very mysterious, as usual, but he generally has his reasons, even if we can't always see them!
'My uncle Bilbo wanted me to write up some notes of my adventures so far for his book, so I took a walk to a sunny spot here in Rivendell and started writing up a few things. Before long, though, I found myself getting drowsy, and when I awoke I forgot all about my papers! I seem to have left them out there.
'If you don't mind, do you think you could bring them back for me? I was resting in the stone pavilion at the Imdolen Look-out, just north of Rivendell. You will find my notes there, I'm sure of it.'

'Welcome, ${PLAYER}. You are a long way from home. You have come for these notes? I hope Frodo is not upset at my having read them. He has weathered many adventures already, but I wonder how many roads still await him and the rest of his Company? His uncle will need more pages than this to write of them in their entirety! He has come now only from Hobbiton to Rivendell; how many more pages will it take before he sees his destination?
'We all have our parts to play, ${PLAYER}: Men such as Aragorn; dwarves; even hobbits such as you and Frodo will have an impact on the great events of our Age. Yes, even I have a role to play, though my time has not yet arrived.
'Return these notes to Frodo with my good wishes, and with my hope that he can return again to Imdolen when the errand of the Company is finished, there to sleep once again in the sun.'

'You found my notes, ${PLAYER}? Thank you very much for bringing them back to me, though now that I look at them they seem very short. How very different it was to live through these few lines!
'Do the Elves feel this way, looking back on their long lives? How strange it must be! Does time pass more slowly for them, or more quickly? What must it be like to remember so much?
'I suppose we will never be able to understand that, ${PLAYER}. We are simple hobbit-folk, and that's what we will stay, I imagine. Thank you again for your help; I know that Bilbo will be glad to have these notes.'
'I left my notes at the Imdolen Look-out, if you could return them to me.'
Look for Frodo's notes at the Imdolen Look-out
Bring Frodo's notes to him in Rivendell
Foreword: Hobbiton to Rivendell
Frodo Baggins has been writing up some notes about his adventure for his uncle Bilbo, but has misplaced them.

'May all of the Company return safely to Imladris when their errand is over.
'I believe you will find Frodo in Bilbo's room on the first floor of my father's house. Return to him his notes and give him my good wishes.'
'Rivendell is such a relaxing place that it is easy to lose track of time. If you can bring me the notes I left behind at the Imdolen Look-out, north of Rivendell, I would really appreciate it.'
'I have spent some time looking at the maps here, just in case.'
'To my great relief, Gandalf has agreed to join the company!'
'I must keep track of our goings-on for Bilbo, or he will be very put out.'

The Imdolen Look-out is a stone pavilion north of Rivendell that overlooks the valley.

'A summons arrived here by raven this morning, ${PLAYER}, calling you to the House of Elrond, far to the east. I do not know why Elrond Halfelven requests the presence of a halfling, but it must be for some errand of importance if he troubles to send ravens on the wing here to Echad Garthadir.
'It is most peculiar, ${PLAYER}. Have your people had dealings with Elrond Halfelven before this? In any event, you will find the House of Elrond far to the east, in the hidden vale of Rivendell, beyond the Trollshaws.'

'${PLAYER}, may I have a word with you? Master Elrond requests your presence in Rivendell on a matter of some urgency. His messenger did not reveal the reason for this summons, but said only that Elrond has need now of you. It is most odd for a halfling to receive such a summons!
'Travel along the eastern road beyond the Trollshaws to the hidden vale of Rivendell and speak with Elrond in his house.'

'${PLAYER}, I have a message for you: Master Elrond requests your presence in Rivendell on a matter of some urgency. His messenger did not reveal the reason for this summons. It is most odd for a halfling to be called in this way, and I cannot fathom the reason for it.
'Descend from the mountains and return to the vale of Rivendell that you might speak with Elrond in his house.'

'Master Elrond wishes to speak with you, ${PLAYER}. Halflings truly have come to the notice of the Wise and the Great, have they not?
'Go inside and speak with Master Elrond in his library. I wonder on what business you have been summoned?'

'Welcome, ${PLAYER}. I am pleased to see you well. This is a safe journey for no one, not even doughty Men or dwarves or Elves, and for a halfling to come so far is commendable.
'A small company will soon be setting forth on a mission of great secrecy to combat the lengthening shadow of Evil that spreads across the land; I am loath to speak in detail of their errand, but know that it will do great hurt to the Enemies of this Age if they succeed.
'Several of your people have chosen to be a part of this company; even now they prepare to depart. I ask that you aid these halflings with their preparations: you are of their kind and may lend them courage for the task ahead. You will find them in a room on the first floor of my house: the lodgings of Bilbo Baggins. Aid them as you can, for much depends upon their courage.'

'Thank you for helping the halflings with their preparations, ${PLAYER}. Gandalf says of your people that they have unseen reserves of strength and are stout of heart, and I hope it is true.
'Much depends on the success of the journey they will undertake.'
Help Frodo with his preparations
Help Pippin with his preparations
Help Sam with his preparations
Foreword: Hobbits Far Afield
Hobbits generally stay in the Shire, never wandering far from their homes, but occasionally there are... exceptions.

'Now halflings have been called to the counsels of the Elves. What could possibly be next? The salamanders of Lake Evendim?
'Ah, I mean no offence. Seek out Elrond Halfelven at his house in Rivendell, far to the east, for he has summoned you. Perhaps he will summon a Man next, for it is strength of arms he will surely need in these dark times.'
'You must make the journey to Rivendell, far to the east beyond the Trollshaws, to speak with Master Elrond. What causes him to summon a halfling, I wonder?'
'Return to the Vale of Imladris and speak with Elrond inside his library. I wonder on what business he wishes to see a halfling, even one so unusual as yourself!'
'You will find the hobbits in the room I gave to Bilbo on the first floor of this house. Aid them with their preparations, that they may have courage for the dangerous road that awaits them.'

'I wonder what business Elrond wishes to speak with you about? You are a worthy halfling, do not mistake my meaning, but I am curious about what matter calls you to his attention.
'You will find him inside his library.'

Elrond waits to speak with you in the library of his house in Rivendell.
Elrond Halfelven has summoned you to speak with him on some urgent matter.

Frodo Baggins, Samwise Gamgee, and Peregrin Took can be found in Bilbo's room on the first floor of Elrond's house.
Elrond has asked that you aid Frodo, Sam, and Pippin with their preparations. As you are of their kind, you may be able to lend them courage for the dangerous secret journey that awaits them.

'...a small bit of flint, spare cloth for stitching patches... what am I forgetting? Bless me, I know it's something I'll be needing!
'Oh, hullo there, ${PLAYER}! You've caught me in a bit of a pickle: too much packing to do and not enough time in which to do it! Bad enough to leave something at home what you'll be needing when you're strolling through the Westfarthing, but worse when you're on a trip like the one Mr. Gandalf has planned for us!
'Do you think you could run to the Forges of Rivendell and pick up a few items from Grafinn for me? I'll write up a list, of course! Now, what am I missing?'

'Yes, I do have all of these items, but I cannot accept these coins from Master Gamgee. I gift these items to him as a member of the Company that bears all our hopes and will brook no argument! Besides, I have little need for the monies of mortal-kind.
'I give him these items freely and would give any member of the Company all that I could, though it be in no way comparable to the burden each of them carries. Return to Master Gamgee and tell him that any items I have are his for the errand of Elrond.'
'I do not see this coinpurse of which you speak.'

'Thank you very much for buying these goods for me, ${PLAYER}; I wouldn't have sent anyone but an honest hobbit to do it, I don't mind telling you. I gave you enough coins, I hope!
'He wouldn't accept my payment? Well, that's queer, and no mistake! \qAlways pay for your goods, Samwise, and you'll never want for them,\q is what my old dad always says, and I've always done right by that.
'Elves are strange folk, putting such importance on us small folk, and them so great and noble! Still, thank you for running my errand; these goods will surely help me on the next!'
'You haven't bought the items yet?'
Bring Sam's coinpurse to Grafinn
Bring both the coinpurse and the goods to Sam in Rivendell
Foreword: Last-minute Packing
Samwise Gamgee is trying to pack up everything he will need for the journey that lies ahead, but he is worried he might forget something.

'I'm just not sure what I've forgotten! What would my old dad say? \qYou keep thinking, Samwise, or you'll never get it sorted out, and then Mr. Frodo will have to do without whatever it is, and he'll find someone else to do for him!\q
'I need to keep thinking, ${PLAYER}! Can you visit Grafinn at the Forges of Rivendell and speak with him about the items on my list? There should be enough in that coinpurse to buy everything.'
'It is my honour to give Master Gamgee those items, and I refuse any manner of payment for them. Return to him in Bilbo's room on the first floor of the House of Elrond and tell him of my gift!'
'Samwise, you ninny, what are you forgetting?'
'Think, Samwise, think! What is it you're forgetting?'

Grafinn is at the Forges of Rivendell in the north-west corner of the valley.
Trusting you as a hobbit of good sense, Samwise Gamgee has given you a small coinpurse and a list of items to buy from the provisioner at the Forges of Rivendell.

Samwise Gamgee is in Bilbo's room on the first floor of the House of Elrond.
Grafinn has given you the items Sam requested, but has refused to accept the coins he sent for their purchase.

'By my beard, ${PLAYER}, it seems like you have been entrusted with news of our errand, and why not? Elrond seems to be wise enough, for an Elf; he seems to know good character from bad. But I am ready to put an end to this waiting. Give me goblin-skulls to cleave!
'If you are as sick of waiting as I am, why not bring this message to my father at his camp in the mountains? Ask him what he thinks of the likelihood that Gandalf might let us come to the halls of Balin, in Khazad-dûm. It could be that Balin found Thrór's ring somewhere in Moria! Now would that not be something?
'My father Glóin's camp is north of Rivendell, in the Misty Mountains.'

'Many troubles could be avoided and much time saved if certain parties paid more attention to the things that were said to them: if Gimli son of Glóin was not interested in listening to the tales told at the council, he should have given his seat to someone else!
'His father is correct: Balin could not have found in Moria the ring of Thrór, last of the dwarf-rings forged of old, for though it was given from Thrór to his son Thráin, it was taken from Thráin in captivity.
'As for Balin himself, the lack of news from Moria is troubling, but I will not muse needlessly on his fate. Return to Gimli and tell him that the errand of the Company must be first in his thoughts. There is no room for other concern.'

'Gandalf has that to say, ${PLAYER}? I am not to be blamed if the mind wanders during such a long discussion -- you and I are dwarves of action, given to fighting and carousing, not idle chatter!
'Thank you for your aid, my friend. It is to be hoped that Balin's work in Moria prospers, and that Khazad-dûm will shine again! Perhaps if the errand of the Company succeeds, you and I will go there someday and lend our strong arms to the effort! I am sure Balin will appreciate our help!'

'My son is not as attentive as he believes himself to be, ${PLAYER}, if he thinks Balin may have found the ring of Thrór within Khazad-dûm. Gandalf told us the fate of Thrór's ring while at the Council!
'We are dwarves, ${PLAYER}, so you understand the call of stone and gems, and in all of us there lies a slumbering desire to see the halls of Khazad-dûm alive and shining once again. It could be that Balin son of Fundin works there now, restoring the splendour of its ancient cities, but I do not know if that is a vain hope. There has been no word from Moria in many long years.
'I cannot tell my son the mind of Gandalf. You should speak with the Wizard yourself if you wish to know his plans. I believe he is in Bilbo's room on the ground floor of the House of Elrond. Speak with him to hear of Moria, for I will not speak of it more.'
Talk to Gandalf in Rivendell
Talk to Gimli in Rivendell
Foreword: Sons and Fathers
Gimli is anticipating the journey of the Company, but is anxious for it to begin. He has mused on what lies ahead for long enough already.
'Gimli is in one of the guest rooms along the road that winds up the southern slope of the Vale of Imladris, with the other members of the Company.'

'My father is at his camp in the Misty Mountains, north of Rivendell. Ask him if he thinks Gandalf might let us visit Balin in Khazad-dûm. Imagine what a boon it would be if he found Thrór's ring there!'

'I do not pretend to know the minds of Wizards, ${PLAYER}. Speak with Gandalf if you wish to know more about his plans for the company. You will find him in Bilbo's room on the ground floor of the House of Elrond, I expect.'
'This is one dwarf who is ready to set forth!'
'Enough waiting! There is a journey to undertake!'

'It does my heart good to see a ${RACE} such as you, ${PLAYER}! Aragorn there seems a strong Man, but he seems to prize the friendship of Elves over that of his own kind. So many Elves in this place! Every hour we spend in this hidden valley prolongs the struggle of Gondor; how many men will fall in its defence ere we depart?
'My sword-arm itches for battle, and my horn longs to be sounded! You understand the need we have for haste, ${PLAYER} -- you are not like these others, who live for such a long span that the concerns of the present must seem trivial, or meaningless. But it is not so!
'Climb the winding road to the south entrance to the valley and ask the guards there if they have need of my vigilance. I will spend the time until we depart guarding the borders, if they have need of my strength.'

'What did you say, ${PLAYER}? The Elves have turned down my offer of aid? This is what I expected, though it grieves me to see it so clearly: the Elves believe they have no need for us, ${PLAYER}! They may change their opinion if Gondor falls, and change it quickly -- do they not see that our people are their last real defence?
'Have they forgotten the great deeds of our people that have made this land safe? We must remind them, my friend. Go to the Hall of Fire, in the House of Elrond, and remind some of the Elf-singers there of the great deeds of our people: of the Gondorian cavalry, perhaps, and of Elendil and his sons. They will not then undervalue the contributions of our people!'
'You have eased my mind, ${PLAYER}; though it seem we struggle alone, it is not so. That is why we fight on; not just for our own people, but for all peoples.'

'We have things here at the entrance to the valley well in hand, ${PLAYER}. I appreciate the intention of our visitor from the South, but we have no need of his assistance: Imladris has been safe from attack for long years before either he -- or you -- walked in Eriador.
'Thank him for the offer, but tell him his concern is misplaced. The Elves can protect Imladris.'

At Boromir's urging, you recite the tale of the ride of the Gondorian cavalry that pursued the Witch-king from Fornost, where the forces of Angmar were routed.
'A good tale, and the deeds of Prince Eärnur are worthy of remembrance, as are those of many strong Men besides. But your tale has ended before Eärnur's horse gave way in terror of the Witch-king. Were it not for the arrival of the Elf-lord Glorfindel, things may have gone ill for the Captain of Gondor that day.
'But your point is clear: against the great evils of the Shadow, Elves and Men must stand together. It is a lesson gladly remembered.'

At Boromir's urging, you recite the tale of Elendil and his sons, and the strength they brought to bear in the Battle of Dagorlad at the Black Gate of Mordor.
'I know this tale, but I know it by another name, for in Imladris it is called \qThe Song of the Last Alliance\q and involves more characters: not just Elendil the Tall, but Gil-galad our king, and Master Elrond, and Círdan the Shipwright.
'But you have reminded me of this, and I urge you not to forget it yourself, ${PLAYER}: neither Elves alone, nor Men alone, could have withstood the power of the Enemy at the siege of Mordor.'

Boromir of Gondor is restless waiting in Rivendell and is eager to depart on the secret errand of his company, but he is concerned that the Elves of Rivendell do not appreciate the sacrifices of his people.

'Every hour we spend here is an hour of battle for Gondor and the Men of the South, and still we wait! I must work off this restlessness. Speak with the guards at the southern entrance to the Vale of Imladris and see if they have need for the strong arm of Boromir of Gondor.
'This place has its defences, but too few strong men and women, if you ask me on it.'

'The Hall of Fire is on the ground floor of the House of Elrond, ${PLAYER}. Remind the Elf-singers there of the great deeds done by Men and Women throughout the years, and those that are still being done today!'
'Thank our visitor from the South for his concern, but tell him the Elves can protect their own borders.'

'If the borders of Imladris rested on the shoulders of our visitor from the South, I do not doubt that he could be of use defending them. But the Race of Men is shortlived, and he could not defend them long.
'I mean you no disrespect, ${PLAYER}, but does the Man of Gondor really believe that the Elves cannot safe-guard their own haven?'
'Many lands have peace because of Gondor's strength -- may it never wane!'
'Men by the Gap of Rohan are friendly to my people; that is the way we should take.'

'Hello there, ${PLAYER}! I'm afraid the Company has enough hobbits for now; we outnumber each of the other races, you know, although Merry says that Gandalf probably counts for more, whatever he is.
'Merry and I just got back from a nice long stroll around Rivendell, seeing the sights and keeping out of trouble. I borrowed a splendid walking-stick for our hike from Elrond's library. It was simply excellent -- I wonder if he would let me bring it with me on the journey? Probably not; he didn't want Merry or me coming along, after all, but Gandalf put in a word for us. A Wizard would know we wouldn't stand to be left behind!
'If you don't mind, maybe you could visit Elrond in his library and thank him for the use of that walking-stick? Tell him I will come along and drop it off before we leave.'

'You say Peregrin Took borrowed a walking-stick from this library? There is no such item kept here.
'Surely the young hobbit did not mistake the Sceptre of Annúminas for a common walking-stick? I trust Gandalf without question, but still I have reservations about Meriadoc and Peregrin joining the company. They are young and do not understand the dangers ahead.
'They will remain with the company, but I am displeased with the youngest hobbit. Peregrin should return the Sceptre; that need not be stated.'

'Did you thank Elrond for the use of that complimentary walking-stick, ${PLAYER}? Rivendell really is a hospitable place, isn't it?
'The... the sceptre of Annúminas? They shouldn't keep it in a place where people will assume that it's free for anyone to use, ${PLAYER}! Well, I will just bring it back to Elrond and say there was a little misunderstanding, and... oh no! It's gone! I must have left it out there and forgotten to bring it back with me! Now that I think about it, I don't remember using it on our way back, Merry!
'You're a hobbit I can trust, ${PLAYER}! You've got to find it for me! There were some large grey stones in the northern part of the valley that we climbed on top of, west of the road that winds up into the mountains, right next to those great forges. I must have left it on top of those large boulders!'

'Thank you for returning the Sceptre of Annúminas on behalf of your kinsman; I wonder if we should keep such relics under the guard of watchful eyes while your people are here in Imladris.
'No harm has been done, ${PLAYER}. I am not angry. You have done well.
'I hope, however, that Gandalf understands the mischief Meriadoc and Peregrin might cause as members of the Company. The errand will be perilous enough without their tendency to fall into trouble.'
'You have not recovered the Sceptre of Annúminas. Gandalf's belief in the good faith of your people seems to me to have been misplaced.'

'Just in time, ${PLAYER}! I will return this Sceptre to Elrond just as soon as I get a chance. I'm a little busy right now, but I will get to it sometime.
'I hope Elrond isn't too upset, and that he still lets me go with Frodo and Sam and the rest of the Company! Being left behind would be a terrible punishment! I wonder why no one sees it that way? Every time I say that to Strider he just smiles and agrees, but I can't tell if he is just humouring me.
'Thanks again, ${PLAYER}! You can always count on a fellow hobbit when you're in need!'
'No Blah!'

Foreword: The Walking-stick
Meriadoc Brandybuck and Peregrin Took enjoyed strolling about Rivendell, and Pippin made use of a walking-stick he found in the library of the House of Elrond.
'Return to young Peregrin Took and ask him to bring back the Sceptre of Annúminas. It is a relic of much importance and should not have been removed from the library.'

'Elrond knows that we would never let Frodo and Sam embark on this journey by themselves. I know they would have the help of Elves and dwarves and Men, but it's just not the same as having your friends with you.'

'I don't remember exactly where Pippin might have left the Sceptre, but we were climbing around on some giant grey boulders in the northern part of the valley, west of the road that leads up into the mountains. I'd wager the Sceptre is on top of those boulders!'
'Elrond is probably in the library, so you can just stop in and thank him for letting me use that splendid walking-stick. I'll return it before the Company sets out, of course.'

'Merry and I were walking in the northern part of the valley, ${PLAYER}, and we climbed up on some really large boulders. I bet the sceptre is on top of those boulders! They were west of the road that leads up into the mountains.'
'I wonder if Elrond is sore at me? I don't think we got off on the right foot.'
'How was I supposed to know that was the Sceptre of Annúminas?'
'I told Pip that the sceptre looked a little fancy for a walking-stick....'
'All's well that ends well, right? I'm sure the Elves aren't really upset.'

'Elrond has entrusted you with knowledge of our errand, ${PLAYER}? I am glad. I go with Boromir to his city of Minas Tirith, a journey that lies along that of the rest of the Company for many leagues. And yet, the route to take is still undecided.
'I see two ways for the Company to take: we might make for the Redhorn Gate, the pass over the mountains that descends into the Dimrill Dale, where lie the still waters of the Mirrormere; or, we might head for the Gap of Rohan, by which Boromir came north. There are difficulties associated with each way, but one of these two must prove the better route.
'I will continue poring over the maps, ${PLAYER}; will you speak with Gandalf about these two routes? I believe he is in Bilbo's room on the first floor of the House of Elrond.'

'I do know of this third way, and Gandalf knows too that I am loath to bring the Company through the mountains by that road. It is a dark way and dangerous. I will say no more of it now, but I hope it will not come to that. My heart tells me that the Redhorn Gate is safest for our purposes.
'Thank you, ${PLAYER}. You have done me a service.'

'Two ways, you say? What are the two ways over the mountains that Aragorn proposes?
'The passage of the mountains could be difficult; the Redhorn Gate is very high up, and in winter, the heights may be treacherous. I do not believe the Gap of Rohan will be open to us; that way would bring the Company too close to Isengard, and Aragorn will understand why we must not go that way.
'But there is a third way through the mountains. I will not speak of it here, but Aragorn will know the way of which I speak. Return to him with my misgivings.'

'There are two ways over the mountains our Company might take, ${PLAYER}: to the Dimrill Dale by way of the Redhorn Gate, or through the Gap of Rohan. I will keep looking at these maps, but in the meantime perhaps you can ask Gandalf which of these ways he thinks is best.
'I believe the wizard is in Bilbo's room on the first floor of the House of Elrond.'

'You will find Aragorn in one of the guest rooms along the road that winds up the southern slope of the Vale of Imladris. Give him my misgivings about the two ways he has suggested and tell him that there is indeed a third way we might take.'
'Regardless of the ultimate road we take, our course is set for some weeks out of Rivendell.'
'We will see what fate awaits us on our separate roads, my friend.'

'A summons arrived here by raven this morning, ${PLAYER}, calling you to the House of Elrond, far to the east. I do not know why Elrond Halfelven requests your presence, but it must be for an errand of some urgency if he sends ravens on the wing here to Echad Garthadir.
'Does the Elf-lord have need now for the strength of the dwarves? That friendship has waned over the years, has it not?
'You will find the House of Elrond far to the east, in the hidden vale of Rivendell, beyond the Trollshaws.'

'${PLAYER}, may I have a word with you? Master Elrond requests your presence in Rivendell on a matter of some urgency. His messenger did not reveal the reason for this summons. Perhaps Elrond has need now of the strength of the dwarves? That friendship may have waned, but let it not break forever! There are too many evils abroad for dwarves and Elves to meet in anger.
'Travel along the eastern road beyond the Trollshaws to the hidden vale of Rivendell and speak with Elrond in his house. It must be important.'

'${PLAYER}, I have a message for you: Master Elrond requests your presence in Rivendell on a matter of some urgency. His messenger did not reveal the reason for this summons. It must be important if Master Elrond requires the presence of a dwarf in his house. Take no offence! I merely mark it as unusual.
'Descend from the mountains and return to the vale of Rivendell that you might speak with Elrond in his house.'

'Master Elrond wishes to speak with you, ${PLAYER}, about a matter of some urgency. What matter concerns both Elves and dwarves, I wonder?
'Go inside and speak with Master Elrond in his library.'

'Welcome, ${PLAYER}, I am pleased to see you well. Be not uncomfortable in my house! The friendship of Elves and dwarves may have waned over the long years, but it must not be sundered.
'A small company will soon be setting forth on a mission of great secrecy to battle this growing darkness; I am loath to speak in detail of their errand, but know that it will do great hurt to the Enemies of this Age if they succeed. Among this company is one of your folk, a dwarf named Gimli, and an Elf of Mirkwood named Legolas; he is a prince of that folk. They must work together if their errand is to succeed, but for some time Elves and dwarves have been... reluctant to do so. I would have you aid them with their preparations. By your example, I hope they will set aside their differences.
'Look for them in one of the guest rooms along the road that winds up the southern slope of the Vale of Imladris.'

'You have the ear of Elrond, ${PLAYER}, and his trust, and that means you will have mine as well; the animosity between our peoples has been... exaggerated... over the course of the long years. In these dark times we should not focus on the distant past, but should instead strengthen the bonds of friendship, for we will have need of them against the Enemy.
'In a similar fashion I fear my bold words following the Council at which the great threat was exposed may have upset some of my fellows: the Elves Galdor and Erestor. I would not have them nurse resentment of my words overlong! They argued in favour of the westward passage; though I did not blame them for it, I spoke with some heat against that course.
'If you bring them word of my regret, perhaps they will forgive my brashness -- the errand of the company is urgent, but I was wrong to speak so harshly of its opposition. Speak with Erestor at the Haven of Orladion, north-west of the House of Elrond. If you, a dwarf, bring word of my regret, Erestor's eyes may be newly opened to the need for cooperation among all peoples. Ask Erestor if he knows where Galdor may be found, for he too deserves my apology.'

'${PLAYER}, Legolas has nothing for which to apologize. His words were no more strident than my own, or Galdor's. These are difficult times and friends should not be afraid to voice their concerns with friends.
'I asked of him this: \qIf the instrument of our grief is unmade, as seems to be the course we must take; what will become of the majesty of the Elves? What victory is there in that?\q Legolas did not waver in his reply, and I forgive him for the heat of it. Even Elrond, wisest of lore-masters, does not know what will happen if the errand of the Company is successful. But it must be undertaken; that much is clear to me now, though the sight of it came sooner to Legolas.
'Galdor of the Havens? He is at the stables in the north-west corner of the valley.'

'${PLAYER}, you have come on behalf of Legolas Greenleaf? Rare it is for an Elf to send a dwarf to speak his words! I jest with you, courageous ${CLASS}.
'I have already forgiven Legolas for the fire of his argument, for it is clear to me after some reflection that all other courses we might take were not real solutions, for the instrument of dread has a way of making itself known again, though you send it over the Sea or to any place thought secure.
'No, I have forgiven Legolas many times over for his frustration. Indeed, I would give him this white knife as a sign of my forgiveness. Bring it to him with my good wishes, ${PLAYER}.'
'Thank you, ${PLAYER}! You bring me great happiness with the news that Galdor and Erestor have not borne me any resentment, and I will bear this knife in honour of their friendship.'
'You have not yet spoken with Galdor or Erestor, ${PLAYER}?'

'The time has come for the Company to depart on their errand of secrecy, ${PLAYER}. As you have been of some assistance with the preparations, you may join the members of my household as we see them on their way.
'Tell me when you are ready to wish them well.'

'It is done, ${PLAYER}. All our hopes now rest upon the nine members of the company: Nine Walkers to stand against the Nine Riders of the Enemy. May they come to no harm and return in safety, their task completed.
'There is nothing we can do now for them. We must stand tall against the Shadow and keep its attention focused upon us, far away from those who can do it the greatest harm.
'That is our task now, ${PLAYER}. Do you accept it?'

'Keep an eye upon these lands while we are away, my friend. Our errand is a dangerous one, but there will be danger behind us, too, and my footsteps will be easier if I know that ${PLAYER} remains behind to protect against them. My own journey will carry me far from here.'
'So begins a new journey. Let us go forth boldly, I say, rather than skulking from shadow to shadow, and let the Enemy quail at our coming!'
'It is done, and they are beyond my aid. For all of my wisdom, I cannot see the end of their road. May they come to it in safety and return to Rivendell in victory.'
'Everything seems to be ready, ${PLAYER}, and we're about to leave. Hopefully, I will see you again once this is all done with!'

'The number of the Company has been chosen, ${PLAYER}, and any more would threaten the success of its mission.
'You have business remaining in Eriador, brave ${RACE}: defend its people from the lengthening shadows. If the errand of this Company fails, Eriador will have need of heroes before the final darkness.'

'This is it, ${PLAYER}. Wish us luck, and we'll be sure to come through all right. Leastways, we'll make sure to lend Frodo all the help we can, and do whatever Gandalf needs us to do.
'We'll see you when we get back, and that's a promise!'

'Samwise, you dunder-head! You've gone and forgotten to bring a bit of rope with you. I knew there was something you had forgot!
'Bill here will have too much to carry as it is, and I've lightened his load as much as I can.'

'You are dealing with the blood-leeches? Pity. It is a pleasure to watch them feed on the corpses.
'Still, Morven's word is but one step removed from that of our Mistress; you are wise to obey.'
'It is a shame that you had to destroy the blood-leeches, but they will be back. They breed from the corpses, you know.'
'The Tarkrîp need to learn discipline. We could teach them something of it, you and I. Bleed some of them and kill the rest. The ones that remain will be more... vigilant.'

'I have an important assignment for you, Bloodletter; if you carry it out well, I might allow you your choice of the treasures from our latest captives. The Trév Gállorg may be poor, but sometimes they fashion things of great worth, and you might earn yourself a pretty bauble.
'I have received word that our Mistress will be coming to Sammath Baul to question the Elf Laerdan, and I want everything to run smoothly during her visit.
'The corpses in the tower have given rise to tremendous blood-leeches, and their filth and disease has been... distracting... for the rest of my servants. I want you to destroy the blood-leeches before the Mistress arrives.'

'You have cleared the tower of blood-leeches? You will go far, Bloodletter. Perhaps I will tell our Mistress of your dedication when she arrives.
'What? The Tarkrîp are all asleep, and Lozudurkh as well? I would never question our Mistress, but I do not understand why she would send such spineless sluggards to guard Sammath Baul. Surely the bloodletters under my command are sufficient?
'Awaken all of the sleeping Tarkrîp and that useless Gorthorog as well! If he is to be Key-master, he should be at his post outside the tower! Use your boot if necessary, Bloodletter.'

'Our Mistress has arrived, Bloodletter! Since you have been of such use, I grant you this boon: to watch her interrogation of the Elf Laerdan. Some few of your brothers have also been given this great honour, that they too may be rewarded.'

'You heard our Mistress! Allies of the Elf will soon arrive to bring him to freedom.
'Return him at once to his cell, Bloodletter. We will not give his friends the pleasure of seeing him alive.'

Instance: The Prisoner of Sammath Baul
The Elf Laerdan has been imprisoned in Sammath Baul, where he is kept under the watchful eye of the torturer Morven and her Angmarim bloodletters.
'I will not allow the Tarkrîp to spend this time in slumber! Awaken them all, and that worthless Gorthorog as well!'

'If you delay any further, I will have you put to death, Bloodletter! Will you enjoy being bled by your fellows and thrown into a cell to rot out the last moments of your pitiful life?
'No? Then eliminate the blood-leeches from Sammath Baul and do it quickly! Our Mistress will be here soon!'
'These Trév Gállorg have been in Sammath Baul only a few days and already I tire of their wailing. Perhaps I will ask Morven if I may kill them.'
'Morven has been given free reign to do as she will in Sammath Baul. If she allows it, these Trév Gállorg will not see the light of morning! I can hear their screams in my head already. Beautiful.'

'What is our Mistress thinking? Why assign Tarkrîp to this tower, instead of one of the more formidable tribes? Surely she has some plan.
'I do not know what it could be. Perhaps after I kill these prisoners, I will spend some time in contemplation of our Mistress's purposes.'

'Lozudurkh has done little but sleep ever since he was assigned here, the fool. His failure at Annúminas is well-known.
'I would gut him myself, but it seems the Mistress has something in mind for him. Why else would she name him Key-master of the tower, when countless of her servants are more deserving?'
'The Tarkrîp are worthless. Sammath Baul was better protected before they arrived! What could the Mistress possibly have in mind?'
'Maybe we will be lucky and Lozudurkh will not come back from his post.'
'That useless Gorthorog! Ask Morven if I can do away with Lozudurkh, will you? His stench is drawing the blood-leeches.'

'Of the Ring-lore of Eregion, I will speak little. It is dangerous knowledge learned from the Dark Lord and should not be explored further.
'However, I will tell you this: in the days of Eregion, our lord, Celebrimbor, gave to an Elf-friend, a Man of Bree-land, one of his shaping tools. I would expect that this tool was buried with him, as is the custom of Men.
'Surely you may find someone in Bree-town who might know the location of the barrow where the shaping tool lies. Perhaps someone at their Town Hall or a patron of the inn there, or even a member of their Watch.'

'Well now, what is it you wanted again? Oh, the Barrow-downs...why didn't you say so? That place has a bad name, if you don't mind me saying, and I would stay away from there.
'But if you're determined to know more about them, you should ask Newbold Leafcutter up at the Scholar's Stairs Archive.'

'What? You want to go to the Barrow-downs to find some kind of tool? Why, we've had enough trouble with spooks in this town.

'I have little doubt of the Enemy's intentions, though I do not know whether they will bear out. That is our one hope.

The tomb of Maenadar the Craftsman has recently been disturbed and any relics which might have lain there have been removed....
'That's too bad, ${PLAYER}. More and more foul travellers have been arriving here from the South, and it would be no wonder that some of them are grave-robbers.'

'One last hope remains, ${PLAYER}, and vain it may well be. You must travel to Mirobel and try to put an end to Amarthiel's plans there.

'Master Elrond awaits you in his library, ${PLAYER}. You should speak with him at once.'

Travel to Mirobel and try to stop Amarthiel

With your defeats in Bree-land and Forochel, little remains now but to throw yourself at Amarthiel's forces in a vain attempt to put an end to her plans.
'Master Elrond awaits you in his library... you should go there at once!'

'Your stand against Amarthiel is the last hope for Eriador, unless the Company fulfils their task....
'You must travel to Mirobel in Eregion, far to the south, if you are to have any chance of stopping her.'

Mirobel can be reached by travelling far to the south, into the land of Eregion.

'There is no more aid I can give you. With the hide of Bregmor and Celebrimbor's shaping tool, there is naught to keep Angmar from rekindling the forges of Eregion and reforging Narchuil. You have failed, but think not too poorly of yourself... the chances were slim at best.
'You should return to Rivendell and bring this dire news to Elrond Halfelven. Perhaps he will know what to do now.
'Rivendell lies in the Trollshaws, far to the east in the shadow of the Misty Mountains.'

'So the Ring-forges will burn again. Amarthiel will reforge Narchuil and use it to lead her armies against Eriador. At her side will be Mordrambor, who appears to have sided with her once more.
'If this happens, the North will be crushed, and though Rivendell will stand, it will only be a matter of time before we, too, are overrun.
'We must put an end to Amarthiel's plans, once and for all.'
Talk to Elrond at Rivendell
Book 14, Chapter 14: The Heavy Burden
With hide from the dragon Bregmor and Celebrimbor's shaping tool, there is nothing more Eglamír knows of that Amarthiel will need to rekindle the forges of Eregion and reforge Narchuil.
'Angmar is one step closer to claiming all of Eriador. You should return to Elrond at once!'

Elrond is at Rivendell in the Trollshaws, far to the east of Celondim.
Eglamír suggested that you bring news of your failure to Elrond at Rivendell.

'You should return to your Vanha-väki, this Eglamír. I am sure he will want to know of your failure. Do not forget to tell of the involvement of Mordrambor. What it means, I do not know, but perhaps others will know what it foretells.
'I believe you said he dwells at the Vanha-väki place called Celondim, far to the south and west in the Blue Mountains. I would hurry there and speak with him.'

'Alas! There is little hope now that we may hinder Amarthiel from reforging Narchuil and bringing her armies to bear upon Eriador. Especially if this Lord of Umbar, this Mordrambor you spoke of, is aiding her once more!'

Book 14, Chapter 13: Frustrated Hopes
You failed to stop the machinations of Angmar in Forochel, leaving the servants of Amarthiel free to rekindle the forges of Mirobel.

Eglamír is at Celondim in Ered Luin, far to the south and west of Forochel.

'Your Vanha-väki sends you to find the lair of the great lohikârme, the creature called Bregmor? I know somewhat of him, though I have never seen him.
'It is told among the Lumi-väki that Bregmor was once the scourge of these cold lands. Many hunters tracked him, but none ever returned. It came to be that one day Bregmor ceased to hunt the Lumi-väki, and we saw no need to anger him further.
'If you wish to visit the lohikârme, you may do so yourself. You will find his lair far to the west, south-east of Jotunstath, the home of the Elukka, the Ice-giants as you call them.'

'Bregmor was an evil creature, but it is sad still that such a great beast perished in such a lonely way.

Find and enter Bregmor's lair

Eglamír believes that the minions of Amarthiel may be seeking the hide of the Dragon of Forochel to repair the great bellows of Mirobel, the Ring-forges of Eregion, and sent you to learn of Bregmor for Yrjänä, the chieftain of Sûri-kylä.
'I will not send my people to die for you. If you wish to see the lohikârme, go yourself.'

Yrjänä is at Sûri-kylä, far to the east of Bregmor's lair.
You failed to stop Angmar from obtaining the hide of the dragon Bregmor and should now return to Yrjänä with your news.

'It is tragic news that you bring from Bree-land. If I had to guess, I would say that Angmar is trying to rekindle the forges of Mirobel in Eregion...perhaps they plan to forge a new ring or repair an old one?
'Ah well, it is of no matter. There is much harm to be done if Angmar succeeds. However before they rekindle the forges, they will need to fix the great bellows. The bellows were originally made of a fine Elven leather that could withstand the test of time, but those are now rotted.
'Angmar could, however, replace the Elf-leather with dragon-hide. It is strong and durable. There is rumour that a dragon -- lesser though he might be -- once dwelled in the frozen wastes of Forochel. Go to Sûri-kylä and speak with their chieftain, Yrjänä. He may know more.'

'One of the Vanha-väki sent you to me? The last I remember seeing was the one named Laerdan, and he failed in his task.
'What does this Vanha-väki wish of the Lumi-väki?'
Talk to Yrjänä at Sûri-kylä
Book 14, Chapter 11: The Great Bellows of Mirobel
Newbold Leafcutter could help you no longer and suggested you return to Eglamír at Celondim.
'Yrjänä dwells in the Lossoth village of Sûri-kylä in Forochel. He may be able to guide you to the dragon's lair.'

Eglamír believes that Amarthiel's minions may be trying to find the lair of a dragon which may still dwell in Forochel, the hide from which may be used to repair the bellows of the forges at Mirobel. He suggests you go to the frozen north and speak with the Lossoth chieftain Yrjänä.

'There is little else that I can help you with, ${PLAYER}. It's a pity that tool was stolen... I would have dearly loved to see it.
'Ah well, perhaps you should return to the Elf who sent you... Eglamír was it? He may have more words of wisdom for you.
'Celondim is far off, I understand... in the shadows of the Blue Mountains. You will want to start off soon.'
'This is ill news, ${PLAYER}. With that tool, Angmar may do great harm in Eriador....'

Newbold Leafcutter suggested you return to Eglamír for more advice.

'${PLAYER}, to arms! Angmar approaches! The False King sends a host against Aughaire in great wrath.

'Your efforts contributed greatly to our victory, but the war is not won yet, ${PLAYER}. Angmar is weakened, but they will press on. Your strength will be needed here and in other battles, I fear.'
