'A moment, if you please, ${PLAYER}. We've already lost contact with four good dwarves inside the Brackwater, and I want to be sure you know what you're in for if you dare to follow them.
'The cave seems to have many winding tunnels, and the whole network of passages is very dark, unwholesomely so. Cave-lizards crawl from rock to rock amid the damp, and are more ferocious than their small size would have you believe.
'If you mean to delve into the Brackwater on some errand, be cautious! Thin the cave-lizard horde while you are there. The creatures are a menace to any who tread too near their lair, and I do not know how long it will be before the gate is cleared and we can leave this place.'

'It is good to see you return from the depths of that noxious cavern, ${PLAYER} -- too few have done so.
'Fewer cave-lizards lurk now among the stagnant pools to threaten the unaware, it would seem. I thank you for your service, and reward you with these coins. May they be of use to you!'
Defeat cave-lizards in the Brackwater (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Can only be completed before the Expedition enters Moria.
Expedition: Danger Beneath the Surface
Valgút has warned you about the cave-lizards that make their home within the Brackwater, and wants you to defeat some of them if you purpose to enter the cave.
'You will have no trouble finding cave-lizards within the Brackwater, ${PLAYER}. Indeed, they will likely find you!'
'The Brackwater is no place for those who hate the damp.'
'Thank you for dealing with the cave-lizards, ${PLAYER}!'

Cave-lizards can be found throughout the cave known as the Brackwater; its entrance is in the hill along the slope that winds up to the Hollin Gate.
Valgút has asked you to defeat several cave-lizards that dwell within the Brackwater and threaten the safety of the expedition.

Valgút is outside the entrance to the Brackwater, on the slope that winds up to the Hollin Gate.
You have defeated many of the dangerous cave-lizards within the Brackwater and should return now to Valgút.
You have found the body of Ógur. He is dead.
You have found the body of Súlki. He is dead.

'Hm, pardon? Can I help you? My cousin and I have a great number of things to manage here, and I do not have a moment to spare on other matters!
'You wish to help? Well, if you're willing to work, I can certainly find a use for you. I dispatched four of my finest dwarves to investigate the cavern that flows with water; it is just up the slope to the east, and they have not yet reported back. If you can find these four inside the Brackwater and bring me word of their findings, I will reward you for your trouble.
'Now that you have a task with which to busy yourself, pray do not linger about, for I find it distracting. Leave me! There is much I must consider.'

'These creatures are more dangerous than you might expect, ${PLAYER}; be careful as you search for the rest of my party! We were separated not long ago by the vicious beasts, and I have been unable to locate my fellows since.
'I heard Súlki calling for help not long ago, but I have not heard him in some hours. I fear he has fallen into danger.'

'Brogur sent you to check on us, ${PLAYER}? I cannot blame him, for it is well past time that we returned to give our report!
'We were separated shortly after entering this foul dank cavern -- Brackwater indeed! I heard Ógur shouting from somewhere up above here about some sort of treasure he had found, but then his calls faded and I have heard nothing from him since. Where Súlki and Wethur ended up I do not know.
'I hope you can find my kinsmen, ${PLAYER}. We four have had poor fortune in this watery cave, and Brogur will not be pleased by our report.'

'Thank you for the tidings, ${PLAYER}, even though they are grim. I am saddened by the losses of Súlki and of Ógur. There is much work still to be done before we have cleared the Hollin Gate of the rubble that chokes it, and they were strong of arm and sturdy as the hardiest of our race.
'But your payment was not only for good news, and you have earned this reward. Take it and make yourself useful! There is still work to be done.'
Find dwarves that entered the Brackwater (${CURRENT}/${MAX})
Found dwarves that entered the Brackwater (${CURRENT}/${MAX})
Can only be completed before the Expedition enters Moria.
Expedition: Four Dwarves
Brogur sent four dwarves to explore the cave known as the Brackwater, but they have not yet reported back to him. He is anxious to learn their fate.
'The Brackwater is the cave just up the slope to the east, on your left. Four of my best dwarves went inside to explore the cave, and have not returned.'
'It saddens me to lose so many good dwarves, but the way to Khazad-dûm must be opened.'
'These hills are riddled with caves, and the caves are full of danger.'
'Time is wasting! There is still much work to be done!'

The four dwarves are somewhere inside the Brackwater, the cave up the slope east of Brogur.
Brogur wants to know what happened to the four dwarves he sent to investigate the Brackwater, and has charged you with finding them.

Brogur is outside the cave known as the Brackwater, down the slope to its west.
You have found the four dwarves Brogur sent into the Brackwater, and should report to him of their fates.

'Be careful, ${RACE}! This cave is home to a large encampment of half-orcs; they haven't been here long, but it seems to me that they are mustering their strength for some evil purpose. Once they are prepared, I fear that they will strike against my people!
'We cannot let that happen. If the Iron Garrison is to survive, we must ensure that the half-orcs are unable to construct an effective offence.
'Seek the camp-fires of the half-orcs inside Filgogân, and collect pieces of information from each of them. If you can retrieve any orders, maps, reports, or letters, we can surely leave these half-orcs too disorganized to pose a great threat to our expedition.'

'This information you have brought me paints a disturbing picture, ${PLAYER}. Someone has drawn arrows on this map in what looks to be blood, tracing a course down from the Trollshaws and into Hollin. And these orders are difficult to read, but seem to command the half-orcs to search for halflings. Could they mean Shire-folk? In Hollin? I confess I do not understand the meaning of these riddles.
'The half-orcs may not be here to stop the expedition, but they still threaten the work of the dwarves. It is to be hoped that your efforts have left them in disarray and unable to carry out a manoeuvre against my people.'
'You have not returned with all of the information we need, ${PLAYER}. Go back into the cave, if you dare, and find the remaining half-orc camp-fires!'
Collect information about the half-orcs (${CURRENT}/${MAX})
Bring information on the half-orcs to Símbi
Can only be completed before the Expedition enters Moria.
Expedition: Orders for Half-orcs
The dwarf Símbi has asked you to enter the cave Filgogân and obtain as much information about the half-orc camp as possible.
'The half-orcs are sure to have the sort of information we're seeking at each of the camp-fires they've built inside the cave Filgogân. Orders, maps, plans, and letters -- all will be of use to us.'
'I am keeping a watchful eye on the half-orcs that occupy Filgogân.'
'The half-orcs are disorganized, and should be unable to mount an effective attack.'

Information about the half-orcs can be found at their camp-fires inside the cave Filgogân, south-west of Bósi's camp, across the dried-up Sirannon.
Símbi has asked you to obtain information from each of the half-orc camp-fires inside the cave Filgogân.

Símbi is outside the cave Filgogân, south-west of Bósi's camp, across the dried-up Sirannon.
You have gathered a great deal of information about the half-orcs in Filgogân and should bring it all to Símbi.

'Someone sent these half-orcs to Hollin, ${PLAYER}; it is clear to me that Graug, the chieftain who ordered the camp established inside Filgogân, has his own master. I want to know who this might be.
'I will reward you handsomely for evidence of this overseer. Enter the cave and do battle with the half-orcs, and bring me whatever common thread binds these half-orcs in loyalty to Graug's mysterious master.'

'You say the half-orcs carried these stones, each of them painted with this hand symbol? This is not Graug's mark; it must certainly be the emblem of his master.
'I do not recognize it. I will show this mark to Bósi when I return to the camp; perhaps he will understand its significance.
'Thank you for your help, ${PLAYER}, and take these coins with my thanks.'
'You have yet to find sufficient evidence of whoever oversees these half-orcs, ${PLAYER}. Go back inside and stop wasting time, unless you are not hardy enough for this task!'
Bring painted stones to Símbi
Can only be completed before the Expedition enters Moria.
Expedition: The Common Thread
Símbi wants to know who has sent the half-orcs to Filgogân, where their presence threatens the expedition of dwarves that has come to Hollin.
'Perhaps the half-orcs carry some sign of their loyalty to Graug's mysterious master. You should enter the cave and bring me proof of this common thread.'
'Graug may lead these half-orcs, but he reports to another master.'
'We must keep the half-orcs from leaving Filgogân and threatening the expedition.'

Half-orcs inside the cave of Filgogân, south-west of Bósi's camp and across the dried-up Sirannon, surely carry some proof of their loyalty to Graug's master.
Símbi has asked you to ascertain the common thread that binds these half-orcs together, and bring evidence of it to him.

Símbi is outside the entrance to the cave Filgogân, south-west of Bósi's camp, across the dried-up Sirannon.
You have recovered stones, crudely painted with the emblem of a hand, from many of the half-orcs within Filgogân, and should bring them now to Símbi.
The strongbox contains only dust.

'I am glad you're here, ${PLAYER}. My party became separated shortly after we entered the Brackwater, and I have not yet been able to regroup with them.
'I almost found my friend Ógur, however; he seems to have made it to the top of the waterfall down this passage, somehow, and I heard him shouting about some sort of strongbox that he found at the top of it. I fear that the cave-lizards must have been drawn by the sound of his shouting, for I have not heard from him since.
'If you can find the same passages he used to come to the top of the waterfall, however, you might be able to find the treasure of which he spoke! I will reward you handsomely for news of it, ${PLAYER}, and for news of Ógur's fate as well, of course.'

'You found the strongbox? Well, where is it? What treasure did Ógur find that can justify the losses we have suffered here?'
Throttólf's face falls as you tell him the strongbox contained only dust.
'I see. Perhaps I was a fool to expect a mighty treasure, but as we are so close to Khazad-dûm, I thought perhaps....
'It doesn't matter. Thank you for your help, ${PLAYER}. The real riches are sure to be inside the mines, rather than in these damp caves. This strongbox must have contained the belongings of some brigand long ago, and no treasure at all. It is a pity.'
Find the strongbox at the top of the waterfall

Expedition: The Top of the Waterfall
Throttólf wants you to find the top of the waterfall inside the Brackwater and see if you can recover the treasure Ógur mentioned.
'If Ógur found some passage that could take him to the top of the waterfall down that passage, I am sure you can do the same. What treasure might the strongbox contain, I wonder?'
'Imagine the treasures we will find within Khazad-dûm itself!'
'I was too eager to believe there could be treasure in the Brackwater. I was wrong.'

The treasure of which Ógur spoke may be at the top of the waterfall deep within the cavern known as the Brackwater.
Throttólf has asked you to find the passages leading to the top of the waterfall so you can investigate the possibility that some treasure might be found there.

Throttólf is in the cave called the Brackwater, near the entrance, down a passage from the base of the waterfall.
You found the strongbox at the top of the waterfall, but whatever treasure it might once have contained has long since fallen into dust. You should return to Throttólf with these tidings.
You find a chipped gold tooth among the bones
You have failed to find the gold tooth you seek
You have failed to find the gold tooth you seek

'Keep it down, ${PLAYER}! I have managed to remain unseen by the half-orcs until now, but they are camped all throughout Filgogân and I do not know how much longer I can remain undetected.
'I have been searching the cavern for my friend Lofrík, who disappeared in the vicinity of Filgogân shortly after the expedition arrived in Hollin. I fear that he was killed by the half-orcs, but I must know for certain!
'The half-orcs construct grim piles containing the bones of their victims: you can see them at various locations throughout Filgogân. Lofrík had a distinctive gold tooth; this is an unpleasant business, but I will reward you well if you can search through these piles and return to me with his tooth, if you find it. I hope you do not find any such thing, but if you do, at least I will then know of Lofrík's fate.'

'I had hoped you would not find anything, ${PLAYER}, but at least I know now of Lofrík's death and can mourn at last. I will weld his tooth into the haft of my axe, and in this way he shall help me cleave many a foe. We shall seek vengeance, he and I together.
'Lofrík! Alas that you will never see the halls of Khazad-dûm shining as once they did. I will avenge you upon the heads of the half-orcs who invade this land of our sires, land where their labour once shaped the stone into immeasurable splendour. May your memory burn long beneath the earth.'
'You have not found Lofrík's distinctive gold tooth? I am glad, but I must ask you to keep searching the bone piles here in Filgogân. Some instinct tells me to fear the worst.'
Search bone piles in Filgogân for Lofrík's gold tooth

Expedition: Unpleasant Business
Trausti is worried that his friend Lofrík may have been killed by the half-orcs, and wants you to search for his distinctive gold tooth.

'I would be grateful to you if you were to search the skull-piles these half-orcs have made throughout Filgogân for the gold tooth of my friend Lofrík. I hope you do not find it, ${PLAYER}, but if you do, at least I will know his fate.'

'Bósi has assured me that the Hollin Gate will be excavated soon, but I am still worried that our expedition might be left outside Khazad-dûm for some days. The hills echo with the howling of wolves, but little else can be heard; how they make us shiver in the stillness! Hollin of old was full of life, but now even the birds seem suspicious and hostile.
'These hills are riddled with natural caverns, though none approach the splendour of even the unworked passages of Khazad-dûm. Unpleasant creatures have taken refuge in some of these, and I fear they will cause trouble for my people if we remain here overlong.
'To the south-west, across the dry river-bed of the Sirannon, is the cave called Filgogân. A company of half-orcs has an encampment deep inside that place; if you care to assist the dwarves of this expedition, you will thin their numbers and defeat their leader, Graug.'

'You have my heartfelt thanks, ${PLAYER}! The half-orcs are not welcome in Hollin so close to Khazad-dûm, and now Graug knows it. Little good it does him now, though, eh? Ha!

'Don't I have news for you, traveller! My neighbour, Provincia, was quarreling with her husband so loudly that it quite caught my attention! And you'll never guess what about. Can you guess? I shall tell you what: apparently he would not let her buy silks for a new dress. Whyever would she need a new dress? I cannot imagine why; she has ten already, and they are in decent shape as they are. Do you want to know what I think? I'll warrant she just wants to compete with Bessie Hawthorne's dresses, for I hear Bessie has eleven. I, for one, am quite content with my eight dresses. What do you say to that?'

'I spent all my week's pay in the Auction Hall, I did. You should lend me some money. A fine traveller like yourself must have some money, and I shall turn it into a handsome profit for you. What do you say to that: yes or no?'

'My poor head, how it throbs! Pray, do not disturb me, unless you brought me more ale. I know I ought to be ashamed of myself for drinking so much, but what's a man to do? Bill Ferny kept goading me on. Look where it got me....
'My mother will give me an earful when I wander home stinking of beer. Alas, alas!'

'I dance all day! If I ever stop, my legs will turn to trees, so I dance, dance, dance all day, every day! What can a man do with two trees for legs? They tell me I'm mad, but they will not think so when their legs turn to trees.'

'Once reforged, it may possess the strength to face the creature that lurks within the Black Pool, ${PLAYER}. You should bring it to the Forge-master for reforging, and mayhap your newly-refurbished blade will at last best the flesh of the cruel Watcher.
'Take this weapon to Snár and he shall reforge it anew, and then perhaps we shall see its true potential.'

'Welcome back, ${PLAYER}. Did that weapon of the Elder Days prove worthwhile, or was it a fruitless chase?'
Ráthwald's eyes widen in surprise.

These papers are full of runes you do not recognize translated into the Common Tongue. It means nothing to you, but the strange runes are of some interest, for they do not look to be any language that you recognize. The papers are signed \qFalgeirr Twisttongue.\q

'Hammer and tongs! These papers must date back to the time of Durin's rule! A very promising find, ${PLAYER}.
'Falgeirr Twisttongue was a famous riddle-master and tinkerer of words. These runes are utterly foreign to me...so I believe they may be a special language he made up! 'Tulk is waiting to speak with you just inside the Doors of Durin. You remember him, do you not? He is pleased that you proved such a boon to the expedition and will be delighted to speak with you again.'

'${PLAYER}, hello! Here we are, inside Khazad-dûm at last! There is a great deal to be done at the several camps we are establishing here, and you can help us to succeed at the mighty task before us!

Chapter 13: Khazad-dûm At Last!
The dwarves have entered Moria at last, but their work has just begun. You will need to assist them in their struggle if they are to find any success in the forgotten halls of Khazad-dûm.

'We have established a presence within Moria, ${PLAYER}, and will stage further excursions into the depths from this room, the Chamber of the Cross-roads. This once served as a guard room for watching the three passages just to the south, but has been empty for many long years.
'Many creatures have thrived in the darkness during the long absence of the dwarves, especially the gredbyg, fierce and loathsome insects spawned from the deep.
'Seek out all varieties of gredbyg in the Western Levels, to the south and west of this chamber, and eliminate them. This will be the first small step in reclaiming the Great Delving for my people. There is much to be done before true progress is to be made.'
'Good work! You are ever a friend at need, and I am at your service. You continue to impress me with your inextinguishable fervour towards our cause!'

Bósi has established his command centre at the Chamber of the Cross-roads, a guard room once used for watching three passages that lead deeper into Moria.

'This chamber is steeped in history. It fills my heart with wonder!'

'The gredbyg were a dreadful hazard, and despite your efforts they will undoubtedly return in time, but we cannot spend overlong dealing with this minor threat. To wholly wipe them out would involve resources beyond what I can provide. We must turn now to other matters, and defend ourselves from the returning gredbyg wherever we must.
'What I truly desire above all else is a chance to look at records and histories from the Old Days. Who knows what secrets lie untold beneath the dust: pages, tablets, and tomes to be found throughout the caverns of Moria?
'There should be store-houses located within the Great Delving of Moria, and they are thus named: the Chamber of Knowledge, the Chamber of Wisdom, and the Chamber of Deep Thought. Find these store-houses within the Great Delving and search them all for records of the Old Days. Return to me when you have found something from each area.'

'Excellent, ${PLAYER}! These records and histories are very old, and probably harbour many ancient secrets. They are sure to be tremendously valuable!'
Bósi examines each of the records in turn, and his face falls somewhat as he reads.
'Records of goods bought and sold, inventories of iron and other metals... these are of some interest, to be sure, but....'
Bósi trails off, and then brightens.
'Wait a moment, ${PLAYER}. You might have something here after all.'
'You have not brought me what I require.'
Find and search the Chamber of Knowledge
Find and search the Chamber of Wisdom

Bósi has asked you to seek out three store-houses within the Great Delving of Moria and attempt to recover any surviving records or histories.

'The three store-houses of which I speak are called the Chamber of Knowledge, the Chamber of Wisdom, and the Chamber of Deep Thought. Look for them somewhere in the Great Delving of Moria, and bring me records or histories from each.'
'Who knows how much knowledge was lost in Moria, long ago?'
'Great secrets lie within these caverns. We will unearth them!'

'These pages mention something curious indeed, ${PLAYER}: an axe made entirely of mithril, light enough to be wielded one-handed but strong enough to fell any foe or rend any armour with a single sweep! Zigilburk, it was called, and it appears to have been forged in Durin's time by one called Ongli. Hm. I have not heard that name before. How can it be that one so skilled would not be remembered in legend?
'There is more to be learned on these pages. Could it be that Zigilburk might yet be found?
'My son Bori has been wracked by grief ever since Bróin was slain before the Doors of Durin. Bring him these pages and tell him of Zigilburk. It will do him well to have other thoughts upon which to brood. Go up the stairs on the eastern side of the chamber and through the door into the Chamber of Command; my son Bori is there, and Brogur also.'

'Alas that Bróin is not here, ${PLAYER}. This is just the sort of adventure he would have relished. Still, I may be able to help you, though my heart will not be in it.
'It seems that the dwarf who sought to forge Zigilburk relished his privacy, and by the grace of Durin he was given a secret forge at which to work. These pages do not reveal the location of the forge, but they do mention a trick of some sort that would open the door. The nature of this trick is lost, but these pages indicate that it was recorded at Katûb-zahar, the Word-hoard of Durin.
'Katûb-zahar was once supposed to be on the eastern side of the Great Delving, somewhere north of a great statue of Durin. I am sorry, but there is little else with which to guide you. Find the location and return to me, and perhaps I can unravel some more of the mystery.'
'You have not brought me anything of note?'

'You found the location of Katûb-zahar, the Word-hoard of Durin? I am deeply impressed. It is a shame that your report tells of a great infestation of deep-claws and cave-claws; I hope the beasts have not ruined too many of the records and histories kept in that place.
'It seems that Ongli, the great craftsman who may have forged Zigilburk, was very protective of his privacy. Durin granted him a secret forge at which to work: Nâr-khelab, the Heart of Fire. The way to Nâr-khelab was locked by means of some trick known only to a trusted few.
'These pages do not mention the location of Nâr-khelab, but they do say that the trick to opening the way was kept in Katûb-zahar. Now that you have found the Word-hoard of Durin, you can search for this trick.'
'You have not yet found Katûb-zahar, my friend.'

'If we can find both the location of the Heart of Fire and the secret to opening its doors, it could be that Zigilburk will return to us from the darkness.
'I will ask the other dwarves of our expedition if they have come across any sign of Nâr-khelab. Perhaps someone has encountered some clue, though I am not hopeful.
'You must return to Katûb-zahar, the Word-hoard of Durin, and search for the secret to opening the door. The deep-claws you found will not make it easy, but you are strong enough to deal with them. 'This looks very promising indeed, ${PLAYER}. Let me see what I can learn from these pages.
'Many of the words are faded, and the parchment is rotten.... Curse the deep-claws and cave-claws that nest now in Katûb-zahar!

'The door will be hidden until... the following steps are taken.... This word must be \qOngli,\q which means that he must be hailed as a master blacksmith, or congratulated for his fine works, or...saluted, I think. And then these words are to be spoken: \qBâb kanon zuhûk!\q

'My nephew has told me of this wild goose chase, ${PLAYER}. How can we be certain that Nâr-khelab, this Heart of Fire, ever existed at all? We would have heard tales of such a forge, surely. And Zigilburk: an axe made entirely of mithril? Ludicrous. This would surely have been featured in many of our tales before now, as all dwarves would sing its praise until the end of time.
'You would have better luck catching a wild Redhorn Goat than you would finding this ridiculous forge. This \qsecret\q to opening the door that you have recovered is nothing more than a mad dwarf's mutterings.'

'You will always have my respect for what you did before the Doors of Durin, avenging my poor son with your excellent weapon, but I must be honest with you: I believe you are wasting your time. As long as you will be trapessing around in the dark looking for this flight-of-fancy forge, you might as well accomplish something worthwhile, ${PLAYER}.
'There seems to be a large goblin presence among the Silvertine Lodes, far to the south and below the Great Delving. As long as you are searching for this fabled Heart of Fire, you may as well slay goblins while you do it -- especially the ones that have moved into Gamil Filik, the Elder-mine. The goblins are many, and bringing an ally or two might be a good idea.
'In fact, why not steal some of their maps? They have long lived here in the darkness, and their crude maps may show the way to this mythical forge of yours, as well as being useful to those of us seeking paths that actually exist.'

'I cannot complain about this errand of yours, ${PLAYER}: you have slain many goblins despite your search for a forge that likely never existed.
'These crude goblin-maps tell me nothing I didn't already know: that goblins are filthy, disgusting creatures, and their maps are worthless.
'Show them to my cousin Bósi, though. Perhaps he has more patience than I and will tell you something useful.'
'You have not brought me anything of interest.'

'The goblins have made their homes here in the darkness for a long time. These maps might have secrets to show us, however unsavoury they seem.'
Bósi peers at the maps for a long while, and then his face creases into a wide smile.
'I may have unravelled our riddle, ${PLAYER}! I do believe that we can discern the location of the Heart of Fire from these maps!'
'You haven't brought me anything? How curious.'

'The time of the dwarves is truly at hand, ${PLAYER}! How ludicrous we were to fear that some curse might lie upon Moria after all these years. Had we returned before now, Moria might be thriving already!
'What's done is done. We are here now, and many of the dwarves of our expedition have ventured forth into deep tunnels, seeking great riches that must surely lie untouched within the caves of Moria.
'If you come across Rókur or Útrygg during their explorations of Zelem-melek, be sure to lend them any assistance they may require. They set out through the southern passage from the Twenty-first Hall, but where they went from there I do not know.'

'He owes you his life, ${PLAYER}. He has always been headstrong and impertinent, but I cannot blame him here. Desire to claim the riches of Khazad-dûm has blinded many dwarves to the minding of their own safety. Still, he is fortunate that you came along when you did; uruks are fierce and not to be underestimated.
'Tell me more of this uruk scout. There is something about your story that gives me pause.'

'Hail, ${RACE}. I have been exploring the lost halls of my fathers; it is a remarkable experience! The great history of this place fills me with wonder at every turn.'
Rókur's eyes narrow and he stares piercingly into the shadows.
'Did you hear that? There's someone there! Prepare yourself for battle!'

'Hello there, ${RACE}. Lord Brogur sent you to help me? I appreciate the offer, but I have no need of your assistance. In the halls of my fathers I need rely on none but the strength of my own arm!'
Útrygg cocks his head and glares into the shadows.
'I may have been too quick to speak, helpful ${RACE}. There is someone there in the shadows. Prepare for battle!'

'The White Hand will have to wait, ${PLAYER}, because Wárr has sent me word that he wants your help. You remember Wárr, don't you? He supervised the opening of the Hollin Gate, and has a very high opinion of you -- as do we all, of course!
'His team of workers have been excavating the Chamber of Mazarbul, the Chamber of Records, located just north of the Twenty-first Hall and on the right.
'Walk there and speak with Wárr about the task he has for you. We will discuss the White Hand problem upon your return.'

'There you are, ${PLAYER}. I have some work for you, if you don't mind getting your hands dirty.
'This place was called the Chamber of Mazarbul because it once stored important records of its day. At some point during the long years that Moria stood empty, the ceiling seems to have collapsed. As you can see, the whole room has been filled with rubble and debris.
'We're trying to search through the debris for anything of interest we can find. Help my dwarves with this task and bring me anything noteworthy.'

Brogur takes the book from you and flips gingerly through some of the brittle pages. His breath catches as comprehension appears to dawn on him.
'This is the Book of Mazarbul, and it seems to contain a record of Balin's settlement. It is grim reading, ${PLAYER}.
'If you would be so good as to bring it to my cousin Bósi, he will want to see it. He has always had more of a stomach than I for records such as this. I do not want to read of their horrific end. It is enough for me to know that they are dead.
'Bósi is still in the Chamber of the Cross-roads in Durin's Way, north of the Great Delving.'
'Is there something you would show me?'

'What have you brought me, my friend?'
Bósi leafs through the book, and a look of deep sadness settles upon his features as he comes to understand what the brittle pages are saying.
'This is a record of Balin's expedition, and tells of their unhappy end. At least we now know what befell our kin in Moria -- Black Pit indeed! Or so it seems in my grief. I will read it from the beginning, but in the meantime I would have your help with another matter so that I may devote my attention to this.'

After the death of Balin, his expedition to reclaim Khazad-dûm is imperiled by a seemingly endless onslaught of Orcs... and worse than Orcs. Something moves in the darkness of the Black Pit, an ancient creature of shadow and flame that drives all before it.

'We have to get you out of here, Captain Ori! We must retreat to the Twenty-first Hall and hope that we can hold them off there!'
'We have to get you out of here, Captain Ori! We must retreat to the Twenty-first Hall and hope that we can hold them off there!'

'Were we wrong to come back to Khazad-dûm, Captain? With Balin slain, this endeavour seems ready to fall: the Orcs are too many!
'No, no! We will stand! I will die a dwarf! Let none call Lóni coward!'

'Things are not well, Captain! There is no end to the creatures -- for every Orc we cleave, two more spring from the darkness!
'Still, we are the Dwarves of Khazad-dûm! We will not let these Orcs drive us from the halls in which we have lived for years too few!'

'Now that it comes down to it, Captain, I grieve that our return to Moria has been so brief, and so full of sorrow. Was Balin wrong to lead us here, and to expect that whatever curse lay upon these halls had been lifted?
'It is too late now to ask such things, but I would not have this hopeful journey come to such an end, to be forgotten forever, to come to nothing.
'Captain Ori, I beg you: finish writing our account in the book where such things are recorded. There it is, on the tomb we erected for Lord Balin; it was begun by others, but I would have you finish it. I do not want our fate to be forgotten!'

'I was not certain you would still be alive, Captain Ori, but I rejoice to see you so. I wanted you here for our last defence. We are still waiting for word from the scouts you sent west, but so far there has been nothing.
'And now the Orcs have taken the bridge and the second hall, and close in on our position from all sides. We are certain to follow Frár and Lóni and Náli, my captain, even if we hold out for a little while.
'Hark! Who is that? Is that one of the scouts?'

'What can we do, Captain? We have no hope of standing against them here in the hall. They will overwhelm us with their vast numbers.'
Thíli listens to your plan, and his face hardens, his eyes stern and bright.
'You are right, Captain. We will retreat to the Chamber of Mazarbul, and make what stand we may! There we may last long enough to make them feel the sting of our axes and hearken our battle-cries!'

'My captain, I bring sad news! The pool has come all the way up to the wall at west gate; there is no hope of escape that way. Noble Óin's mission has ended, and in failure -- in surprise he was taken by the Watcher in the Water, and the weapon he bore availed him naught.
'The surrounding halls are filling with Orcs, Captain! It was all I could do to make it back here, but it has been for nothing!'

'Captain Ori, you have arrived at last! I feared we would be overwhelmed before you arrived, but with your strength we may yet push back the Orcs!
'O, that Balin were still alive! We have need of his leadership; against this horde of Orcs we must move with one mind, or we will not survive the fall of evening!
'I was cut off from Lóni and Náli during the last attack. We must join them on the far side of the Bridge, but many Orcs have crawled up from the pit and stand between here and there. We must defeat them before yet more arrive!'

'Bósi has tried to keep it quiet, but rumour travels quickly in the passages of Moria. Most of us are now aware of Balin's end. They were surrounded: Orcs from the east and below, and the terrible creature in the pool by the Hollin Gate.
'We cannot afford for that to happen again, ${PLAYER}, but if it does, it is my responsibility to make sure that we have enough supplies to withstand a long siege.
'I want you to leave Moria and speak to Thórgnyr just outside the Doors of Durin; tell him to send us as much food as he has to spare and to arrange for more on a regular schedule. We will not be put in the same dire place as Balin's company. I would see us avenge them so they may then rest in long peace beneath the stones.'

'So the troubles within Moria have begun already? I am not surprised that they have come, but I did not expect that they would be upon us so soon. I would have urged more caution, but I held my tongue. Bósi and Brogur are capable dwarves, and I did not wish to heed the warnings of my heart.
'I approve of this decision to order an increased frequency of deliveries into Moria. I have long said that food has been too slowly sent into the mines, for any number of obstacles could besiege our supplies, within or outside of the mines.
'I will give you the first of these deliveries; bring it to Slóthi in the Chamber of the Cross-roads and tell him that more will follow.'
'Ah, the first of several deliveries from Thórgnyr, I hope? Good, good! We won't be shut off from the outside world and caught unawares this time. We will be ready for anything!'
'Where is the first delivery? You have brought me nothing, yet haste is needed.'

'I do not like that well. I looked down it and couldn't see the bottom, but I'm pretty sure there's water down there. It makes me nervous.
'What if the Orcs find the bottom of the well and try climbing up? They could use it to get into this room without the sentries noticing! I don't need to tell you what a disaster that would be.
'I'd feel better if you could find the bottom of the well and make sure there's no way for the Orcs to climb up into this chamber. Melmar went looking for it, but I never heard back from him. I don't know how you'll get to the bottom safely, but you should find a way down to the Water-works and then look for Narag-kheleb, the bottom of the well. I expect you will find it south-west of the mighty aqueduct in the depths. Don't jump down the well itself, though, unless you think you could fall for uncounted fathoms and land alive on your feet.'

'You say that Melmar found the bottom of the well, and that he is confident that the Orcs cannot climb it? That is good news! I am less worried now about its presence.
'We may do all right after all, my friend. Thank you for investigating this for me.'

'This is it! Do you see that hole in the cave ceiling above us? That's the bottom of the well in the Chamber of the Cross-roads. I don't think we need to worry about Orcs climbing up, though.

He would not tell me what has him so excited, but I am glad to see that he is keeping his spirits up; I have not seen him so cheery since before my son was slain by the Watcher in the Water.
'It is a valuable lesson to turn our grief into strength. Just ask Ashpar about the strength of the dwarves!'

Bori greets you warmly and then looks around conspiratorially.
'I think I might be onto something, ${PLAYER}. While visiting my father yesterday, I snuck a peek at the Book of Mazarbul, and I saw something interesting: a line near the end saying that the dwarf Óin sought to find \qthe upper armouries of Third Deep,\q and some mention of a mighty axe. Do you think that Óin might have gone looking for Zigilburk?
'If we were to find the mithril axe Zigilburk, I think it could turn the tide of the coming storm! Óin must not have found it, but if he had, do you think Balin's expedition might have survived? We shall never know.
'Journey into the Water-works and look for room plaques; memorize them and return to me with their locations, and we might be able to find the armoury for which Óin searched! Slay any of the deadly creatures there, as well; if I am correct, there may be another journey there in our future!'

'Welcome back, ${PLAYER}! Tell me about the chambers you discovered. From the room plaques you saw, I may be able to discern which one is mentioned in the Book of Mazarbul, the armoury Óin sought.
'The Hall of Mithril, yes... I think that must be it, ${PLAYER}! Well done!'

Chapter 6: Bori's Suspicion
Bori suspects that he has stumbled upon something that will enable the dwarves to turn the tables on the threatening Orcs of Moria.
'Bori wants to speak with you about something; I know not what.'

'The Water-works are likely crawling with dangerous creatures. Defeat them and memorise the locations of the rooms there, and I may be able to discern the location of the armouries for which Óin was seeking.'

'Imagine how unstoppable we would be if we could retrieve Zigilburk from the darkness of the past. I would fear no attack of the Orcs, that much is certain!
'I have a good feeling about this: The Hall of Mithril must certainly be the armouries for which Óin sought. If only he had found them in time, the dwarves of Balin's expedition might have survived!
'It is too late for them, friend, but not for us. We will travel to the Hall of Mithril in search of these armouries. Speak to me when you are ready.'

'${PLAYER}, we are heroes! Bróin lives still, and the mithril axe Zigilburk has come out of the darkness just at our time of greatest need!
'Can you believe our good fortune? Why, at this rate in a week's time we will surely drive the last Orc howling like a cur from Moria!'

Chapter 7: The Drowned Treasury
Bori believes you have discovered the location of the armouries sought by the doomed dwarf Óin many years ago, and which might contain the mithril axe Zigilburk.

'This adventure might not be easy, but if we can find Zigilburk within the depths of Ghân-gharâf, it will all be worth it!'
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTE: It is suggested that you complete this quest while in a fellowship. Inspiration will assist you if you choose to undertake this challenge alone or with a smaller group.</rgb>'

Bori is in the Chamber of Leadership off the Twenty-first Hall, in Zelem-melek.
You and Bori discovered Bróin, still alive despite great hardship, and brought him safely from the drowned treasury where he found the mithril axe Zigilburk.

'If you and your allies can clear the flooded passages that lie between Gundlajân and Ghân-gharâf, we might yet find the armouries written about in the Book of Mazarbul.
'Could it be that we might find Zigilburk there? I hope so, ${PLAYER}!
'If the records I have studied are to be believed, dwarves erected great mechanisms here to seal off several of the passages when the gredbyg grew too numerous. You will need to deal with the creatures and learn the means of operating the mechanisms to clear the way. I will follow you once I have finished examining the map of these places, for it is very confusing and we will need to keep our bearings.'

'I... cannot believe....'
Bróin shudders with the very effort of speech.
'The beast... in the water! Beware, friends....'

'Are you really... here... my friends? Is this some... apparition?'
Bróin coughs, and you see for the first time the axe shining by his side: an axe so fair, bright, and cold that it can only be made of mithril.
Bróin catches your glance and smiles weakly.
'The beast brought me to this place... thinking to save me for later... I expect; one of its victims bore this. He is all bones, now, but I owe him my life, whoever he was. I could keep the beast at bay... with the axe made of mithril... but did not have the strength to escape. I would... surely have starved.
'You say Bori is with you? What... a wonder. I shall give him a surprise, I expect! Good old Bori!'
'Let us... get out of here, ${PLAYER}. I am glad... this place will not... be my grave.'

'You should go now to see Bróin. I know that he will want to speak with you about his grand adventure.
'He's resting in the Peaceful Path, a camp that my father has made for those recovering from wounds received while reclaiming the mines from the Orcs and other unwelcome creatures that dwell in this place.
'The entrance to the Peaceful Path is along Durin's Way, north-east of the gardens there. There you will find Bróin recovering from his ordeal.'

'Friend ${PLAYER}, I... I thank you for rescuing me. This is not the adventure I had in mind when we arrived in Hollin.
'When the creature of the pool took me from before the Doors of Durin, I thought I was doomed. But the creature must have had a mind to save some of its prey for later, and so I was left within the watery treasury in the depths of Moria, as was Óin so many years ago.
'He found Zigilburk, ${PLAYER}. Who knows how long he wielded it to fend off the monstrous creature in the depths? And yet, in the end, even with the mithril axe itself, he could not escape. That would have been my fate as well, if you had not found your way into the watery depths and driven away the beast.
'I desire adventures no more. No songs or tales for me; I have had enough.'
Chapter 8: Bróin's Tale
Bróin is alive, and is resting from his ordeal now in the Peaceful Path.

Bróin is resting in the Peaceful Path, a camp established on Durin's Way, north-east of the gardens there.
Bori is sure that Bróin would like to speak with you about his adventures.

'You have rescued me from the Drowned Treasury, but still I am afraid. I fear that the recovery of Zigilburk will prove ill for the dwarves -- there is something about the axe that fills me with dread, and I worry it will awaken unwholesome greed in my people. Already Bori has risked much in his desire for this weapon.
'Please return to the Chamber of Leadership and tell Bori of my concerns. His words as we left the flooded chambers where I had been trapped by the Watcher filled me with worry.'

'See? Just as Bori said, nothing bad has happened, ${PLAYER}! Not to us, anyway; Mazog cannot say the same!
'Bróin's worries are needless.'

'It's good to see you. I am glad that Bori was kind enough to send me a bit of help here.
'Down below, Mazog's men have been hard at work. Can you defeat Mazog's closest servants, ${PLAYER}?
'They are called the Pûlpum, and they seem to serve as his most loyal and formidable bodyguards and can be found in the area below.'

'What tidings do you bring from my friend? Bróin is worried? He has been through much hardship, but he must realize the glory that awaits us! We are so near to casting the Orcs out of Moria that I can taste it! We cannot stop now, now that we have the means for victory. Do you not know the story of Azog? I will not recount it for you now, for it is grim, but know that Mazog, spawn of his spawn, is surely hewn from the same block as he: terrible and merciless.
'More of our scouts have returned, and they believe they have found the location of Mazog's fortress; it is a place called Zabadgathol, in Nud-melek.
'One such scout, Glúmur, is located near Zabadgathol, travel to Nud-melek and speak to him.'

'Return to Zabadgathol, and search that place for treasure coffers. I want to learn more about Mazog's mysterious ally.'

'You have returned with the treasure coffers? Good, good. Let us have a look inside.'
Bori opens a coffer and appears very surprised by what he sees inside.
'These are no mere trinkets, but powerful and valuable relics. Look at this, and at this! Evil-looking, to be sure, and wreathed with cruel sigils. And two runes: D.G.

'If Dol Guldur has truly allied with Mazog, there is no time to waste, ${PLAYER}! We will assault Zabadgathol before their plans can come to fruition. With one stroke, we will slay Mazog and end this war between Orcs and dwarves before any force from Dol Guldur can use our conflict to its advantage.
'It will be just like our raid on Stazgnâkh, only this time I will wield Zigilburk, and we will march openly to victory! Our foes shall perish beneath the bite of the mithril axe; this is what it is for, my friend! This is why it comes again out of the darkness!
'Tell me when you are ready, and we will assault Zabadgathol and slay Mazog. I will hand-pick a few others to accompany us.'

'Tragedy befalls us at all turns! Was my nephew foolish to challenge Mazog so? Perhaps, but he is a dwarf! How could he not challenge the spawn of Azog, thrice-cursed by dwarves?
'To lose both Bori and the axe Zigilburk is a grievous blow, and I fear to think of what this sorceror, this Gorothúl, may have in store for us. It seems clear that though the armies are Mazog's, Gorothúl is making the plans.'

'It is up to you and your friends now. You must rally my people and coordinate the defence of Moria. We have prepared for war at three key locations: the Deep-way, the Way of Smiths, and the Twenty-first Hall; if these locations fall, we are lost.

'You have left me speechless, ${PLAYER}! With your help, we live to fight another day!

'Let us prepare our defences!'

'We are with you, ${PLAYER}. We will stand against the Orcs to the end, whether into ruin or triumph, though the Orcs thirst and slaver for our very blood....
'...And then we will close the door if we must. If it comes to that, your presence will strengthen our resolve regardless.'
<rgb=#FF0000>This quest involves a Skirmish that can be completed at Solo, Small Fellowship, or Fellowship group sizes by using the Skirmish Join Panel. This Skirmish has a minimum level of 55.

'I must confess to you that I did not think the Orcs would be able to counter our plan. It is good that you were with us when things went sour, or this would be a grim day for the dwarves indeed!
'Instead, victory! The Heart of Fire remains in our power, and we live still to use it!'
Complete Skirmish: Battle of the Way of Smiths
Chapter 5: The Battle of the Way of Smiths
The Way of Smiths, in which lies the secret entrance to the Heart of Fire, must be defended from the Orcs.

'We must protect the Heart of Fire!'

Stóthkell is in the Heart of Fire.

'It comes down to this, ${PLAYER}: if we lose the Twenty-first Hall, we lose Moria. The Orcs will strike soon, and the stroke will be hard and fast. We cannot fall here, or we shall not find our footing again!
'If we must, we will retreat from the forward barricades. Better to lose some ground than to lose good dwarves!'
<rgb=#FF0000>This quest involves a Skirmish that can be completed at Solo, Small Fellowship, or Fellowship group sizes by using the Instance Finder Panel. This Skirmish has a minimum level of 55.
If this is your first Skirmish, you should visit one of the Skirmish Camps found throughout Middle-earth and speak with a Skirmish Captain to properly train.
