'We owe you more gratitude than can be expressed in words or salutations. The Twenty-first Hall still stands, and my folk remain upright to cleanse the filth that infested these slumbering halls!
'What a day this has been! From retreat and dishonour springs glory and triumph! Let Mazog cower before the Dwarves of Khazad-dûm!'
Complete Skirmish: Battle of the Twenty-first Hall
Chapter 5: The Battle of the Twenty-first Hall
The Twenty-first Hall is a major centre for the dwarf-presence in Moria, and must be held at any cost.

'The Twenty-first Hall must not fall to Mazog!'
<rgb=#FF0000>This quest involves a Skirmish that can be completed at Solo, Small Fellowship, or Fellowship group sizes by using the Skirmish Join Panel. This Skirmish has a minimum level of 55.
If this is your first Skirmish, you should visit one of the Skirmish Camps found throughout Middle-earth and speak with a Skirmish Captain to properly train. Skirmish Camps can be found in the following regions: Ered Luin, Bree-land, the Shire, the Lone-lands, the North Downs, the Trollshaws, Evendim, Forochel, Angmar, Eregion, Moria, and Lothlórien.</rgb>

Wíli is in the Twenty-first Hall.
The time has come to defend the Twenty-first Hall from attack by the Orc onslaught. Speak with Wíli to arrange the defence.

Wíli is in the Twenty-first Hall.
You have successfully defended the Twenty-first Hall from the Orc attack, and should speak now with Wíli.

'We have withstood the initial attacks of the Orcs, but for how long will our good luck last? Not long enough, I fear; the Orcs are simply too numerous, and with the support of Dol Guldur, Mazog can surely wage his war long enough to overturn our defences.
'We must seek help of our own. Though the friendship of the dwarves with the Elves of the Golden Wood has suffered strain over the long years, it has never, I hope, been truly abandoned. We need their assistance now more than ever, or we are lost.
'You must seek the aid of the Lady Galadriel. We dwarves know little of her, but it is said she wields some great power. Some say she is fell and perilous, others that she is kind. In this dire time I would risk an audience with her, though I am afraid. Speak with one of the wardens at the bounds of Lothlórien and ask to speak with the Lady of the Wood, ${PLAYER}. Who better than you? You are an Elf-friend and a dwarf-friend both. I understand that there may be great platforms among the trees across the river called Nimrodel, south-east of the Dimrill Dale. You may find wardens of Lothlórien upon them.'
'A singular request! You are bold, stranger, to seek an audience with the Lady Galadriel. I, Haldir of Lórien, cannot permit you to enter this land.'
Talk to Haldir upon a flet south-east of the river Nimrodel
Book 6, Chapter 1: Desperate Times
You have helped the dwarves to stave off the first attacks of the Orcs, but Bósi does not think his people can stand against these foes forever without the friendship of the Elves of Lothlórien.

'We defeated the Orcs this time, but they are too numerous. Without the aid of the Elves of Lórien, we will be overrun.
'I hope that the Lady Galadriel will help us. Look for wardens of Lothlórien upon the platforms in the trees south-east of the river Nimrodel.'

There are wardens on the bounds of Lothlórien, east of Moria. Such Elves may be found on great platforms, or flets, among the trees to the south-east of the river Nimrodel.
Bósi believes the dwarves cannot turn Mazog's Orcs aside for long if they are truly supported by some force out of Dol Guldur, and wants you to seek an audience with Galadriel of Lórien. The dwarves need allies if they are to stand in Khazad-dûm.
You have defeated enough goblins in Moria to satisfy Haldir
You have defeated enough Orcs in Moria to satisfy Haldir

'The Orcs of Moria are awake. Once they were content to burrow in the deep roots of Fanuidhol the Grey, Celebdil the White, and Caradhras the Cruel; now they pour from the doors of the Black Pit to threaten these woods.
'You say you have fought the Orcs and goblins of Moria -- if you are truly their foe, then show me! How many have you slain in the dark tunnels of Moria? Will I be satisfied that you are the friend you say, and not a spy in league with those forces who wish us ill?
'I will judge your tally, but I promise you nothing.'
'The record of your victories affirms your claim, ${PLAYER}. I am sorry I doubted you, but these are dangerous times. We have had many strange visitors at the boundaries of Lothlórien before you.'
Complete the 'Goblin-slayer' deed in Moria
Complete the 'Orc-slayer' deed in Moria
Chapter 2: An Enemy of the Orcs
Haldir of Lórien has refused to grant you an audience with Galadriel unless you can provide proofs that you are an enemy of the Orcs of Moria.

'If you are truly the enemy of my enemies, you can prove your vow by slaying Orcs and goblins within Moria. Complete these two deeds and perhaps the tally of your foes will be sufficient to satisfy my skepticism.'

Haldir is at his camp on the boundary of Lothlórien.
Haldir has asked you to provide proofs that you are a foe of the Orcs and goblins of Moria by completing two deeds: slaying many Orcs and goblins in Moria.

Haldir is at his camp on the boundary of Lothlórien.
You have completed two great deeds within Moria, and it could be that the tally of your victories over the Orcs and goblins of Moria will be enough to satisfy Haldir of your intentions.
You have successfully defended Orophin

'I have sent word to Lady Galadriel, ${PLAYER}. She will weigh your need and determine what role the Elves will play in these new deeds in Moria.
'In the meantime, I would appreciate your help in patrolling the boundaries of the wood. Speak to my brothers Rúmil and Orophin and offer them your aid; they speak little of the Common Tongue, but hatred of the Orcs will be understood by all enemies of the one Enemy.
'You will find them on the far shores of Nimrodel, to the north. If you walk along the northern banks of the river, you will find my brothers.'

'I thank you for helping my brothers, ${PLAYER}, and for safe-guarding the eaves of Lórien.
'The Lady Galadriel has sent word to me concerning your petition and the fate of the dwarves. I will relay to you her message.'

Rúmil bows his head to you and points into the distance, away from the eaves of Lórien. He then shrugs, and puts a hand on his bow.
He may not speak the Common Tongue, but his message is clear: for the moment, his post is quiet. The Orc threat is gone, for the time being.

Orophin is about to speak when something distracts him suddenly.
'Yrch!' he hisses.
Talk to Orophin
Talk to Rúmil
Chapter 3: Rúmil and Orophin
Haldir believes you are an enemy of the Orcs and goblins, and wants you to help defend the bounds of the Golden Wood while Galadriel is sent word of your need.
'Speak to Rúmil and Orophin, along the northern bank of the river Nimrodel, and offer them your aid. Perhaps when you return I will have received word from Lady Galadriel.'

Rúmil and Orophin are stationed along the boundaries of Lothlórien. Haldir told you to walk along the north bank of the river Nimrodel to find his brothers.
Haldir has asked you to lend your aid to Rúmil and Orophin. They do not speak much of the Common Tongue, so if you cannot speak to them in Elvish, your mutual hatred of the Orcs must transcend the need for words.

Haldir is at his camp on the boundary of Lothlórien.
You have spoken with his brothers and repelled an attack by the Orcs, and should return now to Haldir.

'A short time before you arrived, an even stranger company came to Lórien. Blindfolded, they were brought to Cerin Amroth, for in no way would we endanger the safety of our land. Sad tidings they brought with them, and grief...'
Haldir pauses, and then goes on.
'The Lady Galadriel sent a small party of Elves into Moria following the tidings this company brought with them. She says if you wish to save the dwarves, you will render your aid unto those Elves, for their task in Moria is very important. They have made a small camp in Gwathrendath, the Shadowed Refuge, among the Foundations of Stone.
'The Lady says that an evil greater by far than the Orc presence lies beneath the Foundations of Stone, and must be faced if your dwarves are to be saved.'

'I would welcome you to the Shadowed Refuge, ${PLAYER}, but it is not a cheerful welcome; none should wish to come to this place. We are here at the behest of the Lady Galadriel.
'Some terror has made its home in these caverns, and it is loathsome and evil.'
Talk to Lenglammel at the Shadowed Refuge
Chapter 4: Deep Is the Abyss
Galadriel has told you that by helping the Elves in the Shadowed Refuge, you will be helping the dwarves of Moria as well.
'The Lady Galadriel did not tell me the nature of the evil beneath Nud-melek, just that you must help the Elves at the Shadowed Refuge to defeat it, or the dwarves will be lost.'

The Shadowed Refuge is among the Foundations of Stone beneath Nud-melek.
Galadriel sent word to Haldir that if you would save the dwarves in Moria, you must work together with the Elves she sent to the Foundations of Stone to face some great evil.
You have helped Forglinn with his task.
You have helped Dithaliwenn with her task.

'This is a grim and unwholesome place. The air is heavy and stagnant and reeks of the unseen terrors that slither about in the darkness.
'But for the Lady Galadriel we brave the Black Pit, and we will do as we are bid until we can be of no more use here.
'She has sent you to us for a reason, ${CLASS}. The Lady sees many things in her Mirror; perhaps she has seen what fate awaits us in the abyss. Help the Elves of my company, and we will see all that may come to pass in this place.'

'Mazog must not be aware of the great evil that lurks beneath Moria, or he would not play such dangerous games. His Orcs are no match for what lies in the roots of these mountains.
'Or perhaps Gorothúl, this sorceror from Dol Guldur, has whispered honeyed lies in the ear of Azog's spawn. He may believe his Orcs have the upper hand, but they do not.'
Help Forglinn with his task
Help Dithaliwenn with her task
Chapter 5: The Black Pit
In order to save the dwarves in Moria, you have come to aid the Elves of Gwathrendath, sent into Moria at the behest of Lady Galadriel.
'Help Forglinn and Dithaliwenn to combat the evils that crawl among the Foundations of Stone, and we may learn what our destinies hold.'

Forglinn and Dithaliwenn are in the camp of Gwathrendath, among the Foundations of Stone beneath Nud-melek.
Lenglammel wonders if your fates may be revealed if you help the Elves of her company stand against the darkness.

Lenglammel is in the camp of Gwathrendath, among the Foundations of Stone beneath Nud-melek.
You have aided the Elves of Lenglammel's camp and should speak to her again.
Defeated Globsnaga Orcs throughout the Foundations of Stone (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Mazog has sent many of his kind down here to the Foundations of Stone for some purpose. They seem to be seeking something, but we have not yet determined what that might be.
'It is clear at least that they are having very little success. Nay, these Orcs are being seized by some madness of mind and body that rages within them like a fire, erupting soon onto the surface as a sickening corruption of the flesh.
'This illness makes them even more dangerous, ${PLAYER}, though they seem to lose all reason. They are the Globsnaga now. Defeat them wherever you find them throughout the Foundations of Stone, for their mindlessness makes them more cruel and merciless than before.'

'We still do not know what causes the corruption that has taken hold of Mazog's Orcs and made them the fierce and mindless Globsnaga, but it is enough for the moment to know that their numbers are fewer.
'Thank you, ${PLAYER}.'
Defeat Globsnaga Orcs throughout the Foundations of Stone (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Chapter 5: Taken By Madness
Some madness of mind and body has seized the Orcs of Mazog's command that have come to the Foundations of Stone.
'Look for Mazog's Orcs throughout the Foundations of Stone, corrupted by the mysterious evil that has taken these caves. They are the Globsnaga now, and though mindless, they must be defeated.'

Orcs of Mazog's command, corrupted by the sickening evil, can be found throughout the Foundations of Stone.
Forglinn has asked you to defeat as many of Mazog's corrupted Orcs, the Globsnaga, as you can. The creatures seem to be mindless, but are still dangerous.

Forglinn is in Gwathrendath, the Elf-camp among the Foundations of Stone.
You have defeated many of the Globsnaga Orcs, and should return now to Forglinn.
Collected Pûlpum Orders (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'The dwarves that seek to reclaim Moria, as foolish as they are, do not deserve the fate that Mazog's armies have chosen for them. But why has Mazog sent so many of his Orcs here to the Foundations of Stone, when they might otherwise be used to attack the defences of the dwarves?
'There is some foul purpose in it, ${PLAYER}, and I believe Gorothúl, the sorceror from Dol Guldur, will be at the root of it all. Mazog would not do this by himself; what possible reason could he have for splitting his forces?
'Seek out the members of the Pûlpum that Mazog sent to the Foundations of Stone. They may now be Globsnaga, corrupted by the evil of this place, but it could be they still hold the orders that sent them here. Bring these to me if they exist! You will find the Pûlpum especially among the tunnels near the great underground lake, and on the few outcroppings that break its surface.'

'It is difficult to learn much from these orders, but this I can discern: Mazog is seeking to enslave some of the nameless horrors beneath Moria. But why he wishes to do this remains unknown to me, for he does not need nameless allies to crush the dwarves; they are near enough to destruction as it is.
'No, he must have some other target. I fear it may be the Golden Wood, home to my Lord Celeborn and Lady Galadriel. Mazog does not have the foresight for such a plan. This must come from Gorothúl of Dol Guldur.
'Thank you, ${PLAYER}. We have learned much from your efforts that will be of use to us, and to the dwarves as well.'
'You have not brought me the orders I seek, ${PLAYER}.'
Collect Pûlpum Orders from Globsnaga Pûlpum (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring the Pûlpum orders to Dithaliwenn
Chapter 5: Mazog's Searchers
Dithaliwenn wants to learn for what purpose Mazog has sent his Orcs into the caverns among the Foundations of Stone.

'The Globsnaga Pûlpum may still carry their orders, ${PLAYER}. Wrest them away and bring them to me, if you can. We must learn why Mazog has made this move.
'You will find the Pûlpum especially on and around the great underground lake.'

Pûlpum ensnared by the corruption of the Globsnaga can be found throughout the Foundations of Stone, but especially on and around the underground lake in its depths.
Dithaliwenn wants to learn to what purpose Mazog has sent so many of his Orcs to the Foundations of Stone, for it seems to be an uncharacteristic move. She wants you to defeat Globsnaga Pûlpum and wrest away any orders they may still carry.

Dithaliwenn is in the camp of Gwathrendath, the Shadowed Refuge among the Foundations of Stone.
You have collected orders from the corrupted Globsnaga Pûlpum and should bring them to Dithaliwenn in Gwathrendath.
Placed Elf-stones at abyss cracks (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'The nameless creatures in the depths of the earth are not to be trifled with, but still Mazog insists on attempting to enslave them. There can be no doubt that the hand of Dol Guldur is causing him to try this foolish course, but I have no pity for him. These creatures are deadly, and they approach Gwathrendath more closely with each passing hour.
'And still Magor does not return! This is not like him to be so tardy! Were he not so strong, I would be worried, but Magor trained with Celeborn in the Elder Days and can take care of himself.
'There are cracks in the walls not far from Gwathrendath. Place these beryls in front of the cracks to dissuade the nameless from approaching the cracks.'
'You have done what you could, ${PLAYER}, but where the nameless are concerned I hope only that it will be enough.'
Place Elf-stones at abyss cracks (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Chapter 6: Evils Beneath the World
Lenglammel is worried that the nameless creatures sought by Mazog have been approaching her camp too closely.

'Nameless creatures sometimes crawl through cracks in the walls of the abyss; place these Elf-stones near them to dissuade them from doing so. You should also defeat the nameless beasts wherever you see them, for they are most dangerous, and are becoming more fell and numerous by the hour.'

Cracks in the abyss can be found throughout the Foundations of Stone, not far from Gwathrendath.
Lenglammel has asked you to place Elf-stones in front of abyss-cracks near the camp to dissuade nameless creatures from approaching.

Lenglammel is in the camp of Gwathrendath, among the Foundations of Stone.
You have done what you can to counter the threat of the nameless creatures that lurk among the Foundations of Stone.
This hat is burned and ashen, but certainly once belonged to Gandalf the Grey
This rubble is burned and broken, and blocks further passage up the stair

'When first we arrived here at the Foundations of Stone, we did so at the request of Lady Galadriel, and had one primary objective: to learn what fate befell Mithrandir, the Grey Pilgrim, in these very depths.
'Yes, I speak of Gandalf. He passed into the shadow of the abyss, and it was the hope of the Lady that he might be found, and found safe. The Elf Magor sought him for many days, but found no sign.
'Magor still has not returned, ${PLAYER}, and I am beginning to worry. There are two places I would have you search for sign of either Mithrandir or Magor: the top of the bottom portion of the Endless Stair and the Black Lake. When you have searched both places, I hope you will have some sign of either the Wizard or Magor.'

You describe your discovery of Gandalf's burned hat in the middle of the Black Lake and of the rubble that chokes the endless stair. Lenglammel sighs.
'Your news of Mithrandir and the lack of news concerning my friend Magor both fill me with anxiety, for we still do not know their fates. I thank you for it, but it could be that Magor at least may soon return to us.
'Dithaliwenn found something while you were away.'
'You have brought me nothing useful.'
Search the Black Lake
Search the top of the bottom portion of the Endless Stair
Bring the burned hat to Lenglammel
Chapter 7: Beyond Light and Knowledge
Lenglammel has so far been unsuccessful at her primary mission in Moria: locating and rescuing Mithrandir, if one can indeed rescue a Wizard.

'Several places remain to be searched, ${PLAYER}: the top of the bottom section of the Endless Stair and the Black Lake. Perhaps you will find some sign of Mithrandir or the Elf Magor at these places. I pray that you do.'

The Black Lake and the bottom of the Endless Stair are both among the Foundations of Stone.
Lenglammel has asked you to search several locations for sign of either Mithrandir or the Elf Magor.

Lenglammel is in her camp of Gwathrendath, among the Foundations of Stone.
You have searched both locations, and found the burned hat of Gandalf in the middle of the Black Lake. The Endless Stair has been choked by burned and blackened rubble. It seems that Gandalf survived long enough to do battle with the Balrog, but what happened then is unknown to you. You should speak now to Lenglammel.

'Dithaliwenn found an Elf-stone, much like the ones I gave you earlier, by the cave-mouth to Azanarukâr, from which emanated a vile stench. You did not place this stone, ${PLAYER}. It must have been Magor! But why would he have left the stone rather than return to the camp himself?
'I think the cave Magor found must be the source of the great evil Lady Galadriel sensed beneath Moria, ${PLAYER}. If you can rescue Magor from its clutches, he may be able to tell us something of its power.
'Gather your courage, friend. Whatever this new fell-craft be, if it could best a great Elf like Magor in combat, it must be dangerous indeed!'
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTE: Inspiration will assist you if you choose to undertake this challenge. This instance can only be completed by a solo or two person group.</rgb>

'Magor told us everything, ${PLAYER}, and he has set off on a journey back to Lothlórien to inform the Lady Galadriel of what has transpired.
'Your feats are truly incredible, my friend! Not only have you rescued Magor, but you have thwarted the plans of not only the Orcs, but, more importantly, of Gorothúl of Dol Guldur as well!
'You are wholly remarkable. You have Magor's highest praise, and my own.'
Talk to Lenglammel and travel to Azanarukâr
Chapter 8: New Devilry
Dithaliwenn has found a clue to the lost Elf Magor's whereabouts near Azanarukâr, and Lenglammel wants you to find him.

'Go with courage, ${PLAYER}, into the depths in search of Magor. He may be able to tell us something about the great evil that Lady Galadriel has sensed in the depths.'
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTE: Inspiration will assist you if you choose to undertake this challenge. This instance can only be completed by a solo or two person group.</rgb>

Lenglammel is in her camp of Gwathrendath, among the Foundations of Stone.
Lenglammel is waiting for you to speak to her about travelling to Azanarukâr in search of Magor and the mysterious evil that dwells there.
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTE: Inspiration will assist you if you choose to undertake this challenge. This instance can only be completed by a solo or two person group.</rgb>

Lenglammel is in her camp of Gwathrendath, among the Foundations of Stone.
You have won a great victory in the depths beneath Moria, and should speak now to Lenglammel.
Defeated Moria Orc-berserkers (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
'Let us leave this place, ${PLAYER}. We have been too long in the presence of this evil, and my heart longs for relief from the dread of it.'

'Back! You will never defile me with your poison! Good, they are gone; I am relieved. I thought for certain I would become like them: a monstrosity. They came upon me unaware, surrounding me and taking me captive. One hears rumours of such twisted fates, but now I have seen the wicked pool of filth that corrupts the very depths of this place -- I saw it with my own eyes.
'I will give you a moment to collect your thoughts, and then you must follow me. We will crush these monsters before they can corrupt aught else beyond this wicked place. This will be a great task. I can only imagine what horrors we will face as we penetrate the area.
'Hurry; gather your wits and make ready!'
Defeat Moria Orc-berserkers (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Magor, the Elven prisoner
Instance: New Devilry
The Elves of Lothlórien have sent you deep into Azanarukâr to find out what has happened to Magor and discover what is really going on in the unmapped depths.
Upon entering Azanarukâr, you are confronted with the battallions of Mazog's elite troops. The Elves have asked you to remove the threat of Mazog in Azanarukâr by defeating their leaders.

You have defeated the leaders of the Moria Orcs that Mazog sent to Azanarukâr and found Magor, the lost Elf. Now, Magor wants you to help him defeat the Nameless creatures that dwell deep in Azanarukâr. He will need assistance in putting an end to the scourge.
Magor has helped you clear the way to a darker deeper lair. Sensing great danger, he has gone for help, leaving you to seek out the new threat. Seek out the evil ahead and defeat it.
You have killed two great Regmyl that have claimed to guard Azanarukâr for a long time. You hear horrible bellowing roars ahead and can only guess at what danger lurks behind the next turn.

'You must return to Lothlórien at once, ${PLAYER}. The Lady Galadriel will want to speak with you about what has happened here, and what it will mean for the future.
'Speak with Haldir atop the flet south of the river Nimrodel and he will arrange a meeting with the Lady.'

'The Lady Galadriel can see much in her Mirror, but it is not known to her or any Power whether what she has shown you will come to pass.
'One day, perhaps, you will look back on your long road and make sense of what you saw today. Only time can tell such things.
'I thank you for the service you have provided my people, and may the light of the Elves shine upon your path and guide your steps aright.
'For those unfamiliar to Galadhrim, we shall name you Friend, and allow you to enter our fair home.'
Talk to Haldir and arrange an audience with the Lady Galadriel
Chapter 9: The Mirror of Galadriel
You have overthrown a terrible power deep beneath Moria and have been summoned by the Lady Galadriel of Lórien.

'The Lady Galadriel has called you to her garden, for she wishes to speak with you. I will take you to her.'
<rgb=#FF0000>This is a Solo quest, and cannot be completed with a Fellowship.</rgb>
'You must go at once, to speak with Haldir atop the flet south of the river Nimrodel about arranging an audience with the Lady Galadriel.'

Haldir is atop a flet outside Lothlórien, south of the river Nimrodel.
Lenglammel has told you to speak with Haldir about arranging an audience with the Lady Galadriel.

Haldir is at his camp outside Lothlórien.
Galadriel has seen many things about your future in her Mirror, but you cannot make sense of the confused images.

'I am aware of your kindness to Magor beneath the mountains, ${PLAYER}. You are now held high in his esteem, and he accords you great fondness for your part in his rescue.
'Strange deeds unravel on the many paths of your journey, for as your footsteps lead you to and fro, I perceive that many fates are entwined with your own. Some of your tales seem ended, but locked doors may yet be pried open.
'My Mirror can show many things, and you may ask it what you will. But heed this before you peer into the water: many valuable answers may come unbidden. Look now, and see what may be seen.'

'Some light is now shed on the riddles, do you not agree? The clues left behind among the Foundations of Stone begin to form a clear picture at last. Gandalf the Grey strove in Moria with Shadow and flame, and they fell, and perhaps rose again. Who had the mastery?
'It has been said that my eyes see farther than many who are deemed wise, yet keener eyes we need to pierce the darkness that shrouds Mithrandir from my sight. Who can spy upon Moria from all sides and gain rumour of the fate of Gandalf? Only Gwaihir the Windlord can do this.'

'I have carried Gandalf before now, and if he yet lives, I will carry him again. I will send out the sharpest-sighted eagles to seek him from every corner of this land, and I will fly until we have learned what befell him.
'If he is to be found, I and my kind will find him.
'Return to the Lady and tell her I will do this.'

'I know that Gwaihir will find Mithrandir, if he is to be found.
'Haldir will show you from this place, ${PLAYER}. I will call for him.'
Talk to Galadriel
Look into the Mirror of Galadriel
Talk to Galadriel
Listen to Galadriel's words concerning your fate
Talk to Gwaihir
Instance: The Mirror of Galadriel
The Lady Galadriel wishes to speak with you in her garden in Lothlórien.

'Gwaihir is resting in the rear of my garden. Speak to him, and we shall ask him to spy from the heights for rumour of Gandalf. He may yet live. I do not think that his purpose upon Middle-earth would be so soon spent, for his tasks will be great ere the end.'

Galadriel is waiting for you in the centre of the garden.
You have been summoned to Galadriel's garden in Lothlórien, for she hopes to speak with you.

The Mirror of Galadriel is in the centre of her garden.
Galadriel has invited you to gaze into her Mirror to see what you will.

Galadriel is waiting for you in the centre of the garden.
You have seen strange sights within the Mirror of Galadriel, including confusing images of Gandalf and a terrible creature: a Balrog, Durin's Bane.

Galadriel is waiting for you in the centre of the garden.
The Lady Galadriel has seen more than the fate of Mithrandir in her Mirror; she has seen some hints of your fate as well.

Gwaihir the Windlord has come to rest in Galadriel's garden.
Galadriel has asked you to speak with Gwaihir concerning the fate of Gandalf the Grey.

'The armour you found is a beautiful piece of craftsmanship, ${PLAYER}. What interests me particularly are these gouges in it: look here, and here. I believe this was carried in a creature's claws.
'Attacked by bats? Well, I suppose... but why would a bat carry a piece of armour about? This is most peculiar.
'When inspecting finely crafted armour, there is one dwarf who I would count on beyond all others: Sigdan. Talk to him here in the Chamber of the Cross-roads, he may have some insight into this strange find.'

'Yes, I am Sigdan. Your servant, brave ${CLASS}. Why have you sought me out?'
Sigdan looks carefully at the claw marks in the armour.
'These scratches are too deep to have been caused by even the largest of bats. It would have taken something much stronger to have pierced armour this well made. That is really all I can say.'
'Sigdan doesn't think this was done by a bat, and neither do I. The bats fit into this in some way, but I have yet to figure out how.'
Talk to Sigdan at the Chamber of the Cross-roads
Talk to Rambi in the Chamber of the Cross-roads
Heralds of Corruption
You found a piece of armour. When you picked it up, bats attacked you.
'Sigdan will likely know more about that armour. You can find him here in the Chamber of the Cross-roads.'

Sigdan is in the Chamber of the Cross-roads, north of the Dolven-view.
Rambi told you to speak to his friend Sigdan about the armour you found.

Rambi is at the Chamber of the Cross-roads in Durin's Way.
Sigdan has given his evaluation of the scratches in the armour you found.

You have found an ornate chest-piece from a set of heavy armour, old but of superlative craftsmanship and raked with claw-marks, lying seemingly unattended. You may wish to find out more about it.
Perhaps a dwarf in the Chamber of the Cross-roads will know more.
'An ornate chest-piece, you say? Surrounded by bats... that is interesting.'

'I am glad you're back, ${PLAYER}! I have just received a message from Thettmárr at the Deep Descent: it would seem that Nykr, a miner from Menem-berej, has gone missing, and all of the dwarves of this area are now looking for him.
'Will you help, ${PLAYER}? He could easily have passed right under our noses in the dark. I know Nykr well -- what could he have been doing off by himself? The mines are not safe....'

'Nykr dead! That is a tragedy beyond bearing. Why, that fool; what could he have been about?
'I will send notice to the other camps to call off their search. Poor, foolish Nykr!'
Search for Nykr
Return to Sori with news of Nykr's death
One Absent Miner
Sori just received a notification that a miner by the name of Nykr has gone missing in the Silvertine Lodes, and many dwarves have begun to search for him.
'Why would Nykr just up and leave in such a strange manner? Something strange is afoot.'

Nykr could be anywhere, but it is up to you and Sori to search in the southern tunnels, while the dwarves of other camps search near their own sites.
You should search for Nykr in the southern passages of the Silvertine Lodes.

Sori is on the platform in the southern tunnels of the Silvertine Lodes.
You should return to Sori with the news that Nykr has been found -- dead.

A grim silence pervades the mine, interrupted only by the alien sounds of the Gredbyg. Discover what you can of Balin's mining expedition.
You have found the picks of Balin's miners, and naught else but danger.
This area matches Wigfast's descriptions....

'The strangest thing happened when you were away this last time, ${PLAYER}. I heard a very long echo... and it sounded rather like a dwarf-shout.
'The sound came from the north-east of here. Will you go explore? I should like to head back to the Dolven-view.'

This rucksack may indicate the source of the strange echo heard by Wigfast. It appears to have once been owned by a dwarf, but the dwarf is nowhere to be found.
Your strong suspicion is that he fell right through the perilous crack in the path. But what was he doing so far from any established hubs in Moria?

'You have had some strange encounters, to be sure! White Hands and Uruks and goblins and rucksacks and deep rifts... better you than me, ${PLAYER}!
'Well, I am glad you've made it back safe and sound. Take your rest here at the Dolven-view, where the light is bright and the fire warm.'
Find the source of the echo
Investigate the rucksack near the rift in the path
Complete the first objective in the journal
Complete the second objective in the journal
Talk to Slagvi in the Dolven-view
A Long Echo
Wigfast heard a strangely long echoing shout to the north-east of Gazatmur, and wonders at what the sound could have been.
'A very odd echo it was! Chilling, if truth be told. It could not have been too far from here.'

The source of the echo can be found by following the stairs behind Wigfast's hiding place, and heading north-west from there to the upper levels.
You should search for the source of the echo.

You spot a rucksack in the north-east corner of the Great Delving, perched near a great rift in the path.
You should search the rucksack.

Near the rucksack is a book, a journal, with a dwarf's objectives written down.
You should complete the objectives intended by the dwarf who perished.

Slagvi is in the Dolven-view in Moria's Great Delving.
You should tell Slagvi of all you encountered on the eastern side of the Great Delving.
The trap has been set!
Pukhlor has fallen!

'I explored this secret passage while you were distracting the goblins inside Gamil Filik, and I am quite pleased to report that it is safe. It brings us to a tunnel right near Pukhlor, who looks to be a terrifying foe, the likes of whom I had not anticipated.
'But there is good news: I thought I espied a loose bit of rock that would make a good trap for Pukhlor's downfall. If you sneak behind through this hidden passage, I think you will be able to get through and crush that villain by luring him to the trap.'
'So our goblin neighbours will likely not trouble us in the future? That is excellent news, ${PLAYER}. Thank you for helping Stíling at Gamil Filik.'

'So Pukhlor lies in a grave of stone. Hopefully that will remind the goblins to whom Khazad-dûm truly belongs.
'I do not care what evil lords support them, the very bones of Khazad-dûm stand against them.'
Use the hidden passage near Stíling
Arm the trap and lure Pukhlor into it
Return to Stíling (you may use the hidden passage)
Talk to Thettmárr at the Deep Descent
Stíling pointed out an ancient dead-fall in the mines, constructed by the Dwarves of Moria long ago, and suggested that it might be used to the advantage of the dwarves.
'The goblins at Gamil Filik will soon fall, thanks to your efforts.'

The hidden passage is just near Stíling in the hall near Gamil Filik.
You should enter the hidden passage to sneak behind the goblin camp.

Stíling has asked you to find the dead-fall trap and arm it, then lure Pukhlor to his death beneath the rocks.

Stíling is at his spot outside of Gamil Filik.

'Well, ${PLAYER}, we have been lucky so far in that the goblins infesting Khazad-dûm seem to be terribly disorganized, with inept leaders.
'Nevertheless, we cannot relax our guard. If I read things rightly, there is one particular leader among the nearby goblin-tribe who has been bold enough to organize a raid against the Deep Descent, and I think it would be best if he doesn't live long enough to carry out his ploy.
'See if you cannot perhaps weaken the goblin-forces in Gamil Filik, and deal with their chieftain while you are at it.'
'So, Gathrok has fallen. That should set the goblins back again in their efforts to organize against us.'

'I think it would be best for all of us if the goblin Gathrok did not live too much longer....'

'Forgive me for asking, ${PLAYER}, but could you lend me a hand? I joined this expedition as a librarian, hoping to uncover the lost lore and mysteries of Khazad-dûm, but there is so much to be done around here that instead I've been assigned a list of labourious tasks to which I fear I am ill-suited!
'It appears that a recent rock-fall has littered the road between here and the Twenty-first Hall with rubble that makes travel difficult, and we need that stretch of the passage cleared if we are to continue to supply the Twenty-first Hall.
'The rock-fall occured in the eastern-most area of the Great Delving, along the path just south of the gate to the Lonely Span.'
'Excellent! With that path clear again, it will be much easier to deliver supplies to the Twenty-first Hall.'

'Keep working. We must get enough of the rubble clear that we can safely move supplies to our deeper encampments.'

'So you have decided you want to exchange your ashen after all? So be it. Look over this receipt and tell me if it looks fine to you.
'And this time, I hope you are more sure of your choice. Choosing a horse should not be something done lightly!'

You have discovered the goblin-encampment. A deep, gruff voice barks sharp orders.

'According to Kambi, the chieftain said to go through the broken wall above the eastern stairs. We must see if this goblin-tribe does, in fact, lurk in the shadows. I also want to know more about this voice the chieftain was so fearful of.
'Head to the east through the crack and locate the tribe.'
'By Durin's beard! Someone has come to help me! I was cut off from the rest of my group venturing forward through this area, and I found myself here....'
Find the goblin-tribe
Speak with the dwarf near the goblin camp of Snaga-maudhûl
A Watchful Glance
Kambi, wounded by a goblin near Durin's Threshold, spoke of the ramblings of his attacker. Túbi Thickfist wants this tribe's camp found as soon as possible.
'Before we do anything else, we must first find that goblin-tribe. According to Kambi it should be found through the broken wall above the eastern stairs.'

The goblin-camp can be found through a crack in the wall above the eastern stair.
Túbi Thickfist has asked you to locate the goblin-camp.

Jarmárr is near the goblin camp of Snaga-maudhûl.

'I am glad a greater warrior than I is here to do some damage to these menacing little fiends. Their camp here utterly threatens all travel from Durin's Threshold to the Dolven-view and beyond.
'All dwarves who come into Moria will pass this way, and we cannot have Snaga-maudhûl looming beneath the roadway! On your way through, ${PLAYER}, please thin out this malicious nest of goblins.'

'Ho there! Are you hurt? No, I can see that you are not. But you seem to have hurt many goblins during your short stay in Snaga-maudhûl, and I'll thank you for that!
'I am here to assist travellers who may be hindered on the road as they pass that rotten goblin-camp, but since you seem to have waylaid them, I will help you on your way!'
Defeat Moria soldiers in Snaga-maudhûl (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Wegil on the north-east side of Snaga-maudhûl
Sealing the Gate
Jarmárr wants the newly discovered goblin-camp removed. Snaga-maudhûl is a threat to all who travel from the Hollin Gate into the rest of Moria.
'The goblins must be driven from Snaga-maudhûl if we are to reclaim Moria for the dwarves.'

The goblin-camp lies in the tunnels beyond the crack above the eastern stair.
The dwarves want to end the goblins' reign over the tunnels below to ensure the safety and security of their foothold.

Wegil is on the north-east side of Snaga-maudhûl, standing watch on the road.

You have found a plaque bearing the strange runes of Falgeirr Twisttongue, author of the papers you found in Katûb-zahar. When translated, they read as follows:
I can sizzle like bacon; I am made with an egg, I have plenty of backbone, but lack a good leg, I peel layers like onions, but still remain whole, I can be long, like a flag-pole, yet fit in small holes. What am I?
Solve Twisttongue's Riddle
A Riddle in an Old City
Falgeirr Twisttongue, a dwarf with a penchant for riddles, left messages throughout Moria for those with the key to solving his strange runes and twisting words. You have just such a key.

You should try and solve Falgeirr Twisttongue's riddle:
I can sizzle like bacon; I am made with an egg, I have plenty of backbone, but lack a good leg, I peel layers like onions, but still remain whole, I can be long, like a flag-pole, yet fit in small holes. What am I?
The solution to the riddle can be found somewhere in the Silvertine Lodes.

'Interesting! I should hang onto this, if I were you. It might come in handy if you find any more of Twisttongue's riddling in Moria.'

'The goblins of Gazatmur have stationed archers upon those platforms. Anyone who tries to attack them directly will be slaughtered. They will make the road perilous for those trying to move through the Great Delving.
'The platforms are of typical goblin-make, from what I've seen: clever idea, but shoddy. There is a major pin at the base of the shaft that holds the platforms up: pop that out with one or two good whacks of your trusty hammer, and the whole thing comes right down.'

'Good work, ${PLAYER}. They will put those platforms back up sooner or later, but in the meantime, our forays against the goblins will be a little more successful without all those arrows raining down upon us!'

The goblins have built a series of platforms from which their archers can rain arrows upon any attackers bold enough to confront them.

'I am sure Wigfast could use help with assessing the situation down there. He is brave for going off to scout, but I do not think he will be of much use by himself.'
'Ah! Did Slagvi send you? Just in time -- I was about to try to venture in there and start lobbing off goblin-heads all by myself, though I am ill-equipped for such a venture!'

'Do not worry... what could possibly go wrong? Return to me when you have tried this solution.'

'So, the mixture only made Kraibag angry, you say? Then perhaps we used a little too much rhubarb. We will tweak it some more and then try again.
'I am confident that with the right balance of spice and punch, with the correct undertone of...'
Ansurr continues to ramble on about making what sounds more like a pie filling than a mixture to battle a fungus such as that infecting the Orcs.
Use the mixture on Kraibag

The dwarves believe that they have created a mixture that will destroy the fungus-growth infesting the Orcs and allow them to be easily defeated.

Delf-View: Dwarf Doors
The white cloth strip turns green as the water soaks it
This looks like a good spot to use the white cloth strip

Welcome to the Rotting Cellar, but I would not become too comfortable here. There is a strange fungus spreading throughout these deeps, and it threatens the expedition's success. We are not certain whence it came, but I have a suspicion. I believe the fungus to be spreading through the water. We must know where this growth is coming from.
'Take this cloth strip and dip it in the waters below. If it changes colour, then things are indeed quite bad.
'Return to me with the results.'

'So it is in the water. That is disturbing indeed. But perhaps to our advantage.
'I must ponder this information further. Orcs are a tricky foe, but I have never had to fight a fungus-growth like this before.'
Use the white cloth strip to test the water
Find a good spot to test the water
Bring the soaked green cloth strip to Sylfa at the Rotting Cellar
Some Kind of Safety
Sylfa wants to know the extent and scope of the fungus-growth. He fears the water may be the cause of a strange fungus that is spreading through the Water-works.
'Hurry up and test that water. You do not want to end up like those Orcs, do you?'

The water of the Water-works is west of the Rotting Cellar.
Sylfa told you to take the white cloth he gave you and dip it in the water of the Water-works.

Sylfa is in the Rotting Cellar, east of the Water-works.
You dipped the white cloth strip in the water, and it turned green. You should return it to Sylfa at once.
Destroyed mushrooms (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'I have a fear, ${PLAYER}. We have been using some of the mushrooms around here for cooking with our meals, but I do not think all of them are safe.
'There are some mushrooms down near the water's edge, growing in that tepid pool of fungus. I believe the Orcs have eaten those, and that is what caused them to become infected.
'To deal with this threat -- at least to slow its spread -- I would ask you to go and destroy those mushrooms. While an Orc is still an enemy, it is an easier enemy to kill than one of these fungus-infested creatures.'

'They are destroyed, and that is that. I am glad to know they looked different than the ones around here... we should not have anything to fear from what we have already eaten, but I might be a little more careful about which ones I cook from here on.'
Destroy mushrooms (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Return to Thrand in Hulwul-nefekh
Mushroom Picking
Thrand believes the fungus forms into mushrooms growing on the lake. In his opinion, the Orcs must have eaten the mushrooms, and that is what caused them to become infected.
'Destroying those mushrooms should stop the spread of this fungus-infestation. You can find them at the water's edge to the west.'

Mushrooms can be found around the water's edge to the west of the Rotting Cellar.
Thrand thinks destroying the mushrooms will slow the spread of the fungus into the Orc-population.

Thrand is in Hulwul-nefekh in central Water-works.
You have destroyed many mushrooms and should now return to Thrand.
Collected fungus-spores (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'I have been talking with Ansurr and studying the cloth you brought back at the Rotting Cellar, and I have come to a conclusion. I believe the fungus would rather be in the water than living on the Orcs.
'The only reason it is on the Orcs is because it cannot get back to the water. If you could bring me back several spores from the infested Orcs, I can study them and learn more, perhaps even prove my theory.
'You can find these infested Orcs near The Chamber of Dark Waters to the east of here.'
'These are perfect, ${PLAYER}. Thank you for bringing these to me. I am sure they will prove useful.'
Collect fungus-spores from Globsnaga Orcs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Return to Gyrgir with the spores
Drawn to the Water
Gyrgir believes the fungus would rather live in the water than on the Orcs. He wants to study the infestation further.
'I believe the spores will unlock everything. I must have several to test my belief.'

Globsnaga Orcs can be found on the banks near The Chamber of Dark Waters, south of the Rotting Cellar.
Gyrgir wants you to gather fungus-spores from several Globsnaga Orcs. He believes with them, he will be able to learn things important for creating an antidote.

Gyrgir is in Hulwul-nefekh, west of The Chamber of Dark Waters.
You defeated several Globsnaga Orcs and managed to gather enough fungus-spores for the dwarves to research. You should return to Gyrgir in Hulwul-nefekh and deliver the spores.
Defeated Orcs in The Chamber of Dark Waters (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'The Orc-attacks that have come lately have been terrible. We barely beat back the last one a few days ago, and then they suddenly stopped.
'I know we haven't killed them all... I can feel them at night, lurking beyond the torch-light. I fear they are preparing a final assault that will be the doom of us all. We cannot wait for the hammer-fall, ${PLAYER}. We must take the battle to them before they are ready and move from their attack.
'That is where you come in. I want you to take them unaware. Their encampment lies near The Chamber of Dark Waters to the south. While you press the attack, several of my men will move westward to a new outpost. When you have finished, meet Ansurr there.'

'Thank you for holding them off, ${PLAYER}. You bought us enough time to make our way over here. It's not... ideal, but it will do for now.
'They were covered in some sort of fungus-growth, you say? That must be why they stopped attacking us. Something else attacked them... but what could it be? What could be down there?'
Defeat Orcs in The Chamber of Dark Waters (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Ansurr in Hulwul-nefekh
Lying in Wait

The Orcs have not attacked the dwarf-post at the Rotting Cellar in several days. Sylfa fears they are preparing a larger assault and wants you to press the attack while most of the dwarves at the Rotting Cellar advance westward to a new outpost.
'Keep the Orcs at bay! We do not want to give them an inch with which to launch their own assault.'

Orcs may be found in The Chamber of Dark Waters to the south of the Rotting Cellar.
Sylfa has asked you to make a pre-emptive attack against the Orcs while his fellows advance to the west.

Ansurr is in Hulwul-nefekh, west of The Chamber of Dark Waters.
You observed that the Orcs you defeated were different than those you had seen throughout Moria, with odd growths covering them. Ansurr should be made aware of this.
Defeated Urbhrum

'Every night at the Rotting Cellar, I used to engage in battle with one of the Orcs of Moria. We would fire our arrows back and forth, listening for the twang of the bow string, searching for our enemy in the dark. It broke the monotony of guard duty, but a dangerous game it was. At rare times we traded taunts -- though we were each careful to move so as not to be discovered -- and I learned this creature's name is Urbhrum.
'Urbhrum had not loosed upon us for several days now, and I fear he has fallen to the fungus. These infected Orcs are unpredictable and dangerous. I do not know what drives them, but an Orc of Urbhrum's skill under the influence of the spore could be a terrible threat.
'Go to The Chamber of Dark Waters, east of here, and seek out Urbhrum. If he is to be found, destroy him, lest his arrows return.'
'The deed is done? That is well. Urbhrum was a dangerous opponent before, but I fear he would have become more so under the influence of the fungus.'
Find and defeat Urbhrum
Talk to Ansurr at Hulwul-nefekh
Missing Arrows

Ansurr has traded arrows with the Orc Urbhrum for several weeks now. Neither have hit their targets, but he has enjoyed the challenge of their nightly duels. He has not seen an arrow for several days and fears his opponent has fallen to the fungus.
'I dare not think what evil Urbhrum may be capable of under the influence of that terrible fungus. Orcs are vile enough creatures to begin with!'

By the flight of the arrows, Ansurr believes Urbhrum can be found amid the fungus-covered Orcs of the Water-works.
Ansurr has asked you to find and defeat Urbhrum near The Chamber of Dark Waters, east of Hulwul-nefekh.

You should return to Ansurr and inform him of your victory against the infected Urbhrum.
Goblins of the Great Delving

'On our way here from the Rotting Cellar, we saw much of the fungus in the Water-works. We need to take swift action to ensure that we are not overwhelmed, and also, we must ensure that the Orcs do not maintain even a small foothold by our water-wheels.
'Speak with the others and do what you can to help them out with their plans. Meanwhile, I have another request of you.'

'I thank you for helping them all with their plans. I am sure some did more than others, but they have all proved valuable.

Flík has reached safety
'Hurry up and get me out of here! I wish I had never wanted to come out here. All I wanted to do was make my father proud, and now I am about to become goblin-stew! Stop dawdling and let us go!'

'So you found Flík? And he was well? Not too badly hurt? That is very relieving news.

'I hate this place... get me back to the Deep Descent!'

'I have noticed some very evil-looking dragonets during my travels throughout the Silvertine Lodes, but with no sense of where their hive could be until I came here. I believe they have made their home in this old city here.
'If you slay them at their own hive, I believe we will be cutting off the entire population of the menaces throughout the entirety of the Silvertines. Will you help, ${PLAYER}?'

'I am deeply indebted to you! This will make a great difference, I think, for dwarves all over the Silvertine Lodes. You have my thanks, ${PLAYER}.

'This will be my head for sure. I was not supposed to send Flík out with any tasks, but he kept begging me.
'His father is leading one of the eastern parties of the expedition; if he knew I let his son go out there and he never came back, they would probably throw me down one of these fissures here!
'I will never be heard from again -- unless, of course, you could find him. You would be saving my beard if you managed it!'
'Who are you? Are you a friend? Did Styrr send you to find me? I hope so! I begged for this task, and now all I want is to be back safe in camp.'
Find Flík

This journal page describes a hope to reach the old libraries of Khazad-dûm, known as Katûb-zahar. The dwarf who owned this book was seeking an old text within which is rumoured to detail the ancient methods of blending mithril with other metals, along with many other secrets of its proper forging.
It seems a worthy search. You should continue the fallen dwarf's quest.

'You found a journal on the road with the objective of recovering this book? Amazing! But....
'Alas! The years and the foul vermin infesting Khazad-dûm have been most unkind... so many pages are ruined!
'No matter. With enough time, I'm sure I can piece it back together, even if it takes me years!'
Find the ancient tome

Some of the ancient archives of Durin's Folk are located within the Great Delving, or so says a journal you encountered on the road.

'A journal of a fallen dwarf pointed you to the levers of the Dolven-view water sources? How strange! What a brave dwarf, and you were very good for making the effort on his behalf, whoever he was.

'Ah, greetings to you, good ${RACE}! I am Gufi, at your service. It is a great day to be a dwarf, I tell you, and I am privileged to see the retaking of Khazad-dûm in person!
'As we arrived here, I noticed the railway directly to the west. I sense that there are untapped mining prospects there, for the lodes of the Silvertine are the richest in veins in all of Moria, and likely in all of Middle-earth.
'Would you be so good as to scout prospective paths in the tunnels, and hang signs at any clear dead-ends so that we know where to start our search?'

'Dread, you say? Bah! A dwarf does not fear a little dreariness in a mine-shaft! According to you, that is the best and only road, and so that is where we will begin! I thank you for your report, ${PLAYER}, however nonsensical its delivery!'
Scout dead-end passages (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

Bright Prospects, Dark Rails
Gufi is confident that the dwarves will be able to reclaim Moria quickly. He is eager to scout out potential mine-sites.

The railway tunnel is directly west of Gufi's camp, and can be reached by following the track directly there.

Collected goblin armour-scraps (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'The make of the goblin-armour disturbs me, ${PLAYER}. It is finer than I would expect them to have -- and certainly to make themselves. If the goblins are being supplied with armour and equipment from elsewhere in Khazad-dûm, then I think we had best find out where that source is and remove it.
'However, I cannot be certain of my fears unless I have some of their armour to examine. For that purpose, I would have you collect some of that armour from the goblins while you're in Gamil Filik.'

'Ah, I had feared this was the case. Upon a closer look, it is no mystery where this came from -- these suits incorporate old pieces of dwarf-metal and armour from long ago. The craftsmanship is so fine that even the vast span of years between has not destroyed it.
'Unfortunately, what time could not ruin, the foul hands of goblin-smiths have. Some of these pieces must have been re-beaten and re-worked a dozen times by now and worn by even more goblins over the years since they were looted from the fallen or from hidden armouries of old. I fear they are of no use to us now.
'They serve only as another reminder of the ancient tragedies that engulfed fair Khazad-dûm in darkness.'

While it is a fine thing for us when goblins fight each other, we cannot allow them to gain a foothold here within the bounds of Khazad-dûm when they already control considerable forces without!
'I need you to hunt down and defeat the White Hand's emissaries before they are able to convince or intimidate the goblins here into joining him!
'My scouts spotted one in the goblin-camp of Ninknakh Faltor, another in Gloku-ru, and the third was at Durin's Crossing, between here and Jazârgund.'

'So, that's the end of the emissaries of the White Hand... and good riddance. Our only hope against these odds is to keep the goblins disorganized and to encourage them to prey upon each other as much as they prey upon us.

Líkmund's Tasks
Collected supply-crates (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Líkmund sent you to help me? Well, that is most fortuitous timing, good ${RACE}. I have just the task for one such as yourself.
'We are running dangerously low on supplies. I was bringing a cart over from Durin's Threshold, but we were ambushed outside Manarbul. We were driven back before reinforcements could arrive, and the goblins made off with our supplies!
'I would be greatly appreciative if you could hunt down those missing crates. It will be a lean week indeed before the next shipment otherwise, and we might even be forced to abandon this camp. The goblins fled north towards Mudmulzarâk.'

'This camp is of great importance to our expedition. From here, we can keep an eye on anything that tries to move between Durin's Way and the Great Delving in the south.
'Without these supplies, we might have been forced to abandon this vital watch-post!'
Collect supply-crates (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring the supply-crates to Gansi
Lost Supplies
The dwarves escorting a cart of supplies from Durin's Threshold were ambushed just west of Manarbul. The cart was destroyed, and the supply-crates stolen.
'Please recover those crates, ${PLAYER}. I doubt we will be able to maintain our post without those supplies.'

The goblin-thieves were last seen fleeing north along the road towards Mudmulzarâk.
Gansi has asked you to recover the stolen supply-crates from the goblins who took them.

Gansi is at the Chamber of the Crossroads, south of Mudmulzarâk.
You have collected the supply crates stolen by the goblins and should bring them at once to Gansi.
Defeated goblin guards (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeated Captain Gomîg

'Collecting supplies and scouting chambers is all well and good, but I've got something a little more dangerous in mind. Goblin-hunting!
'As you have surely noticed, nearly every room and corridor of Khazad-dûm is crawling with them, and those causing us grief here in Durin's Way seem to take orders from a single leader. We have all got to do our part to drive them out, and that includes you!
'Search to the west for the goblin captain, who goes by the name of Gomîg. He and his personal guard have been harassing any who travel unaware between the Chamber of the Cross-roads and our outpost here at the Door to the Clouds.'

'You have dealt with quite a few goblins in the last day or so, ${PLAYER}, and more importantly, you have rid us of Captain Gomîg. That should make it easier for us to move between the western part of Durin's Way for some time.
'Not that they will stop coming after us. It is only a matter of time before a new captain rises, but we can use this opportunity to fortify our position before that happens!'
Defeat goblin guards in Durin's Way (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeat Captain Gomîg
Talk to Siggir at the Door to the Clouds
Plenty to Go Around

The dwarves at the Door to the Clouds are constantly on guard against the goblins, who vastly outnumber them. A goblin captain and his personal guards have been making things difficult for travellers between the Chamber of the Cross-roads and Zirakzigil.
'If you can cull a few of the captain's guards, he might be easier to deal with alone.'

Captain Gomîg and his guards can be found in the northern passages west of the Door to the Clouds.
Hoping to clear the way to the Chamber of the Cross-roads, Siggir has asked you to defeat the captain of the goblins in western Durin's Way.

Siggir is at the Door to the Clouds.
You should return to the Door to the Clouds and inform Siggir that you have defeated Captain Gomîg and his guards.
Krum has explored the camp

'One of my dwarves, Krum, has discovered a large goblin-camp in the westernmost chamber of Durin's Way, which the creatures call Ninknakh Faltor in their vile tongue. He has only scouted around the outskirts and has asked for help investigating more closely.
'I cannot spare any extra men for this, but if you would go and ensure his safety I would be grateful. You can find him near Ninknakh Faltor to the north of here.
'When you have learned more about this encampment, return to me.'

'So, the camp was larger than Krum first thought. It is good to know more about it.
'Fortunately, it lies off the main road to Jazârgund, and we can for the most part avoid it.'

'Líkmund sent you? I welcome your aid!
'The camp is just around the corner. It is large, but I am not yet sure how large it truly is.
'Let us find out!'
Find and talk to Krum
Talk to Líkmund at the Chamber of the Cross-roads
Stronghold of the Goblins
Krum, one of Líkmund's dwarves, has discovered a large band of goblins in Ninknakh Faltor at the westernmost end of Durin's Way.
'The camp Krum found is large -- we will need to keep an eye on it, lest the goblins there launch a foray against us. That would make for a pitched battle indeed....'

Krum can be found to the north of the Chamber of the Cross-roads, near Ninknakh Faltor.
Líkmund has asked you to speak with Krum regarding the goblin-camp he found and aid him as you may.

Líkmund is at the Chamber of the Cross-roads, south of Ninknakh Faltor.
The camp at Ninknakh Faltor was indeed quite large and well-fortified, and you were only able to explore it in part. You should inform Líkmund of what you learned.
Destroyed the drums (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Forgive me, ${PLAYER}, for any rudeness. I am not permitted to leave my post here, but those incessant drums are driving me mad! I've not had any decent sleep since we arrived here.
'The band of goblins responsible for that din are encamped just north of here in the Hall of the High Stair. Could you do me a favour and silence those drummers?
'What I would not give to have just one night's peace!'

'Thank you for your help, ${PLAYER}. I am very much looking forward to taking my nap in a while. It may seem like a small thing, but the better rested we are when the battle is joined, the more favourable towards us it will go.'
Destroy the drums (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Fostólf in the Chamber of the Crossroads
Drums of War
The dwarves at the Chamber of the Crossroads have gotten little sleep since arriving. The goblins nearby have been pounding on drums without respite, sending booming echoes throughout Durin's Way.
'Please destroy those confounded drums. They beat on and on without end...I cannot get a wink of sleep.'

The goblin-drummers are encamped in the Hall of the High Stair, north of the Chamber of the Crossroads.
Fostólf has asked you to destroy the goblin-drums so that he and his companions can get some sleep.

Fostólf is at the Chamber of the Crossroads, south of the Hall of the High Stair.
All of the goblin drums have been silenced. Fostólf should be able to get some rest at last.
Collected dwarf-letters (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'We have many traditions, ${PLAYER}, and this one is not the least. When we head into battle, we bring with us a letter. If we fall, that letter will be returned home by the survivors, if any remain.
'Many of us have come to Moria, and some of us have fallen...and now it appears that the merrevail have discovered these letters and have taken a perverse pleasure in keeping them as trophies of victory against us. The honour of our warriors and the peace of mind of their families demand that we recover these letters from the enemy whenever possible and return them to their rightful homes. Will you help us retrieve these letters?
'If you come upon one of our fallen in Durin's Way, search the body for their letter. Return any letters here to me before the merrevail can get to them.'

'You have retrieved the letters of the fallen? My thanks to you, ${PLAYER}.
'The messages contained herein will bring a sorrowful, but much needed close to the grieving of their families. I will see that they make their way safely to Durin's Threshold.'
'Please ${PLAYER}, do what you can to retrieve those letters....'
Collect dwarf-letters (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Listein at the Door to the Clouds
Send Them Back Home
The merrevail haunting the tunnels of Khazad-dûm have stolen many letters from the dwarves who have fallen in battle in Durin's Way.
'Those letters must be found and brought back home. We owe the fallen that much at least.'

Letters can be taken from merrevail looting the bodies of fallen dwarves in the halls of Durin's Way.
Listein has asked you to reclaim dwarf-letters before they are be taken away by merrevail.

Listein as at the Door to the Clouds, near the entrance to Zirakzigil.
You should bring the dwarf-letters back to Listein.
Helped Fostólf
Helped Gansi
Helped Rink

'Welcome to the Chamber of the Cross-roads, ${PLAYER}. We are fairly busy here, as you can no doubt see, and could certainly use your help. Our encampment is a vital link in the supply-chain between Durin's Threshold and the Twenty-first Hall, far to the east. It is also nearly impossible for anything to get past us here without us spotting them, so it's very important that we not fail to hold this chamber against anything the goblins and Orcs can throw at us!
'If you are of a mind to help us out, you should speak with Fostólf, Rink, and Gansi over there... they have some rather important matters that need attending to, or so they tell me.
'I am sure I can find something for you to do, as well.'
'Thank you for helping us out, ${PLAYER}. Now that we are settled in this chamber, we can see to some other pressing matters!'
Help Fostólf
Help Gansi
Help Rink
Talk to Líkmund at the Chamber of the Cross-roads
Líkmund's Companions
The dwarves at the Chamber of the Cross-roads need help establishing their presence there.
'Help out Fostólf, Rink, and Gansi. No sense in wandering off into the darkness without some purpose... you will just be fresh meat in the goblin's next stew!'

Fostólf, Rink, and Gansi are in the Chamber of the Cross-roads.
Líkmund suggested that you speak with Fostólf, Rink, and Gansi and learn what tasks they might have for you.

Líkmund is in the Chamber of the Cross-roads.
You should return to Líkmund and tell him of your efforts on behalf of Fostólf, Rink, and Gansi.
Little Revolution
Defeated Zâhof
Planted the Mordor-banner on Zâhof's throne

'The White Hand Uruks here had one purpose: to take command of the Orcs and goblins of Khazad-dûm and turn them against the forces of Mordor. Why they were ordered to do that, I do not know, but their intentions are clear to me now. Now it is time to tip the balance. Before they have a chance to overwhelm us, I want to force them against each other.
'There is a powerful White Hand Uruk leader, Zâhof -- one who has united many of the goblin-tribes between here and the gate -- who now stands over Durin's Way, claiming it as his own. The time for his fall has come, and for Mordor to be given the responsibility for his demise.
'My scouts report that Zâhof reigns in Fehem-dûm. Find him, defeat him, and place this banner of Mordor upon his throne.'

'So Zâhof has finally fallen. With his fall, the rest of the White Hand's forces have begun fleeing from Khazad-dûm. With pressure from both the forces of Mordor and from Durin's Folk, they believe it is not a cause worth fighting for.
'This is a great victory for us indeed, but do not relax your vigilance yet. We have but lit a small flame... now begins the work of turning it into a raging fire.'
Defeat Zâhof
Plant the Mordor-banner on Zâhof's throne
Talk to Ión at Jazârgund
Little Revolution
The White Hand Uruk leader has established his camp in Durin's Way and is aligning the banners of several goblin and Orc-tribes under his rule.
'Zâhof has outlived his welcome in Khazad-dûm. It is time for him to fall... and for Mordor to take the blame.'
'Hurry up and place that banner on Zâhof's throne! Those loyal to him must believe that Mordor committed this act!'
'You have showed great courage in driving forth the White Hand from Khazad-dûm!'

Zâhof can be found at Fehem-dûm, east from Jazârgund.
Zâhof is the leader of the White Hand Uruks in Moria. If he falls, Saruman's plans for the deeps fall with him.

Zâhofs throne is in Fehem-dûm, east from Jazârgund.
Ión wishes to stir up strife between the Orcs of Moria and Mordor. He gave you a banner to plant upon the throne of the fallen White Hand Uruk.

Ión is at Jazârgund, west from Fehem-dûm.
Ión will be pleased to hear Zâhof is dead and the Mordor-banner has been planted on his throne.
Defeated White Hand Taskmasters (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'I have heard reports of White Hand Uruks all over the Great Delving, but did not believe any had pressed this deep. I have seen them, taking hold of the halls to the west, and I fear what their purpose might be. I suspected their plan would be to enlist some of the goblin tribes to supplement their forces, but now I fear something more sinister.
'The ones I am particularly concerned with are the White Hand taskmasters. They seem to carry considerable influence among the Orcs of Khazad-dûm. I would ask you to defeat as many of them as you can... perhaps it will dishearten the others.'

'So most of their number has fallen... that is good. I dare say they will have a difficult time at recruiting any goblins without them.
'Until the White Hand has been driven from the halls, I will not be satisifed... but you have done your part, ${PLAYER}.'
Defeat White Hand Taskmasters (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Borgar at Jazârgund
Badgers as Shepherds
The dwarves at Jazârgund are concerned about the presence of White Hand Uruks this deep into Moria.
'If the White Hand takes over Khazad-dûm, or allies with the forces here, then we will be but the first casualties of this war.'

White Hand taskmasters can be found in Fehem-dûm and Hadâd-dûm, east of Jazârgund.
Borgar fears the White Hand Uruks are wresting control of the Orcs and goblins of Moria. He wants to thin their ranks.

Borgar is at Jazârgund, west of Hadâd-dûm and Fehem-dûm.
Borgar will be pleased to know that the White Hand Uruks' numbers have been greatly reduced.
You have found insects in Gamli's bed

'Ho there, friend! You don't see anything... moving... in my bed, do you?
'My sleep has been quite disturbed of late by the feeling of something crawling across my skin. I refuse to lay beneath those blankets again until I am assured there is nothing alive within them.
'Take a look for me, ${PLAYER}. I dare not touch the blankets.'

'This is intolerable! Insects rustling around where I lay my head is quite unacceptable! It is not to be borne, I tell you!
'Where did those hideous little things come from? We have hardly been here a day, and already we are infested.
'I think now I shall need a thorough wash....'
Examine Gamli's bed
Talk to Gamli
Gamli the dwarf harbours fears that something might be hiding within his bedding.
'Don't you see those awful things crawling in my bed?'

Gamli's bed is in the Durin's Threshold camp.
Gamli seems concerned that there might be something hiding in his bed.

Gamli is at the Durin's Threshold camp.
You should speak with Gamli regarding what you found in his bed.
Defeated a deep-claw (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'The first order of business: I have noticed a number of deep-claws roaming awfully near to the Dolven-view, haven't you? I think there is a great nest of them nearby.
'They are mild enough beasts, but their tunnelling cannot be borne. It is dangerous, and I think it is the very reason for all the pitfalls, collapses, and general rumblings in Moria.
'Let us lessen their numbers a bit. What do you say?'
'Hello again, ${PLAYER}. I am glad to see those deep-claws did not make slivers out of your hide! Well, you have done the dwarves of this expedition a good turn indeed.'
Defeat deep-claws (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Return to Wafri in the Dolven-view
Claws of the Deep
Deep-claws roam the great Delving, especially naer the Dolven-view. These monstrous tunnellers make the deeps unstable.
'Please, take out some of those deep-claws before they can collapse all of Moria. I fear they will be a persistent problem in your travels here.'

Deep-claws can be found in the Great Delving, especially on the east path from the Dolven-view.
You should defeat many deep-claws in the Great Delving, but it would be wise to focus your attention on the east path towards Zelem-melek.

Wafri is in the Dolven-view camp in the Great Delving.
You should speak with Wafri and tell him that you've defeated many deep-claws in the surrounding area.
Joy in the Time of Sorrow
The column stands steadfast

'I just narrowly escaped from the Orcs to the east. They had me captive for an entire week, but I kept my eyes open and saw many useful things. It is time for you to make what I saw work to our benefit, ${PLAYER}.
'The camps are built within our ancient halls, but the Orcs have been careless. There are several columns that with a little work look like they would fail and bring the entire cavern crashing down upon the Orcs.
'The decaying columns are east of here, in the Orc-camps at Fehem-dûm and Hadâd-dûm. All you should need to do to bring the cavern down upon the Orcs is pick away at the stone... then run!'

'The columns did not collapse? But surely, they must have. Did you push hard enough? Did you try striking them with hard steel?
'I suppose there was naught you could do... our stone-work is among the finest.
'Now I simply do not know what to do. It will not be long until the Orcs come again, and then I suspect they will not be interested in taking prisoners.'
Damage the decayed columns (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Hamall at Jazârgund
Crashing Down
Hamall noticed several decaying columns in the caves around the Orc and goblin-camps. If they were to be damaged, the cave should come crashing down atop the enemy forces.
'Damage the columns, drop the rocks on the Orcs and goblins, and then we will attack!'

The decaying columns can be found in the Orc-camps at Fehem-dûm and Hadâd-dûm, east of Jazârgund.
Hamall noticed several decaying columns within the nearby Orc-camps. He assures you if they are damaged enough, everything will come crashing down and destroy the camps.

Hamall is at Jazârgund, west of Fehem-dûm and Hadâd-dûm.
Hamall should know that none of the columns collapsed, and the cavern did not collapse.
Collected dwarf sheet-music (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'If only the bard had not left. One night, he just seemed to lose his senses, started yelling into the darkness and went screaming from camp, throwing his music everywhere. I think the future would look much brighter, even down here, if we could just sing the songs of old once more.
'Perhaps if you could find the bard's music, we could use it to bolster the spirits of the dwarves here at Jazârgund... a light in the shadow, so to speak.
'The sheets of music will likely be spread throughout the Orc-camps at Fehem-dûm and Hadâd-dûm. It would be a dangerous venture... are you prepared for such a challenge?'

'The songs of old! You found them all. I thought when the bard fled, we had lost everything.
'How you managed to find these, I do not know, but we are deeply in your debt. This will do much to restore the morale here.'
Collect dwarf sheet-music (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring the sheet-music to Hamall
Remembering the Old Songs
The spirits of the dwarves at Jazârgund have fallen very low, and many think that some cheerful songs would help improve their morale.
'I long for the songs of old. If only the bard had not fled into the dark.'
'These songs will now live forever in our memories!'

The dwarf-bard's sheet music has been spread throughout the Orc-camps in Fehem-dûm and Hadâd-dûm.
With the failure of his plan, Hamall wishes to raise the spirits of his fellow dwarves in Jazârgund. He believes collecting the songs of old lost by the maddened bard will help achieve this goal.

Hamall is at Jazârgund, west of Fehem-dûm and Hadâd-dûm.
Hamall's spirits will be greatly raised by the ancient dwarf-songs you recovered.
Destroyed accursed armourer (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
