'I cannot thank you enough for dealing with the worms that threaten our supplies from Rivendell, but I have another task for you that should prove to be a more decisive step in safe-guarding our deliveries.
'To the south of Pend Eregion in the east, there is a small clump of large hills. On the north side of these hills are a series of dens the worms use to raise their young. It is here that you will find Brunanc, lord of the worms of Pend Eregion.
'I want you to draw him out by smashing any eggs you may find on the north side of those hills. Draw out Brunanc and slay him, then return here to me.'

'Excellent work! It is unlikely that the worms will recover from their loss any time soon.
'This should give us a short respite in which we can gather our strength. The Elves of Gwingris owe you their gratitude, ${PLAYER}. Thank you.'
Defeat Brunanc
Talk to Daegennan at Gwingris
The Worm-sire
The worm Brunanc and his spawn terrorize the paths leading from Rivendell to Gwingris.
'Has Brunanc been defeated, ${PLAYER}?'
'Thanks to your efforts, deliveries from Rivendell have resumed. Thank you, ${PLAYER}.'

The worm-eggs belonging to the spawn of Brunanc lie upon the hillsides south-east of Gwingris.

'The half-orcs have pushed far beyond where any of us had thought they would dare, even so far as the Redhorn Gate.
'Though none marked their passage, they did not leave in secrecy; leaving foul banners of the White Hand upon the hill-side. Go and remove these banners. We must not allow the half-orcs to believe that they can roam freely throughout this land, which once belonged to the Elves.
'The half-orc banners can be found throughout the Redhorn Gate to the north-east.'
'You have thrown down the banners of the half-orcs? The fingers of the White Hand have grown long, but not long enough that we will be forced to endure the sight of its tokens upon our doorstep.'
'Have you returned with the banners, ${PLAYER}? They can be found throughout the Redhorn Gate to the north-east.'
Talk to Rostoriel at Echad Dúnann
Collect banners (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

Half-orcs have placed banners throughout the Redhorn Gate, signifying their allegiance to Saruman the White and staking their claim to the area.
'You have dealt a great blow to the White Hand, ${PLAYER}!'

Defeated crawlers (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Even the smallest worm has its place in Middle-earth, but it seems that Saruman's corruption can reach those both large and small.
'The worms of Emyn Naer have been feeding upon the corrupt flesh of the wanton slaying of the servants of Saruman. They have grown heavy with the vile flesh, and they no longer feed only upon the remains of the dead, but have been seen feasting upon the living.
'This plague must be put to an end, ${PLAYER}. The crawlers can be found throughout Emyn Naer, south-west of Echad Dúnann.'
'Though they will not be wholly destroyed as long as Saruman's corruption remains in Eregion, you have eased the burden upon the land.'
Defeat crawlers (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Tinúriel at Echad Dúnann
Emyn Naer's Pests
A plague of crawlers has been a cause of concern for the Elves of Echad Dúnann.
'The crawlers can be found throughout Emyn Naer, south-west of Echad Dúnann.'
'You have done a great service for Eregion, ${PLAYER}.'

Crawlers can be found at Emyn Naer, south-west of Echad Dúnann.
Tinúriel has asked that you slay the corrupt crawlers of Emyn Naer.

Collected holly-leaves (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

This branch is covered in aromatic holly-leaves. You have heard that the Elves can brew fine teas from the leaves of many different trees. Perhaps one of the Elves in Gwingris can brew something from these holly-leaves if you gather more?
'What is this that you have brought to me, ${PLAYER}? Ah, holly-leaves. I can indeed brew a fine tea from these.'
'What is this that you have brought me, ${PLAYER}? Ah, holly-leaves. I can indeed brew a fine tea from these if you bring me more.'
Bring the holly-leaves to Celebrandir in Gwingris
Collect holly-leaves (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Holly-leaf Tea
While holly-berries are generally considered to be poisonous, holly-leaves are often used in the brewing of tea.

Holly-trees can be found throughout Glâd Ereg. Celebrandir is encamped at Gwingris in the northern reaches of Glâd Ereg.

Collected lynx-pelts (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'The host of Rivendell has a number of trackers skilled in the art of subtlety and stealth in the wild, though few can rival the tawny lynx in these traits. His coat is like a fleeting shadow in the holly-trees, and he stalks his prey unseen with nary a sound.
'Go and hunt these lynx and bring me back their pelts. With a few of their hides, I will be able to fashion cloaks for our trackers that will let them stalk with the same skill as the lynx of Eregion.
'There is a saying in Rivendell among the trackers, \qWhere the Warg howls, there also the Orc prowls.\q With these cloaks we will be able to ensure that no Wargs will establish themselves in fair Eregion. Our hunters, so slyly robed, will not allow it.'

'These are fine pelts, ${PLAYER}. I will begin work on the cloaks at once.
'If only Aragorn were with us! He has spent much time tracking in these lands and would lend us much aid in the battles to come.'
'I will need more lynx-pelts, ${PLAYER}. Lynx can be found north-east of Echad Eregion in High Hollin.'
Talk to Lengliel at Echad Eregion
Collect lynx-pelts (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Moving Unseen
The Elves in Eregion use lynx-pelts to craft their cloaks.
'The Enemy will not see us coming, thanks to you, ${PLAYER}.'

Lynx can be found prowling in High Hollin, north-east of Echad Eregion.
Lengliel has asked you to collect lynx-pelts for her, so that she can make cloaks for the scouts.

This necklace is encrusted with grime and filth, but it glows with a radiance that shines through the stains.
After wiping off some of the dirt, you can see that it is an Elf-necklace made by a skilled hand. You should bring it to Ladenthir in Echad Eregion. He may be able to shed more light on its origin.

'You did well bringing me this treasure. It is a relic of the Second Age of this world, made by a smith of the Noldor...its beauty could be mistaken for no other craftsman's work.
'I will send this treasure to Rivendell. Maybe there, Master Elrond can identify the exact smith who wrought it, and it can be cleaned and restored by Elves of his household; though doubtless it will never be restored to its full glory after its long neglect and mistreatment by the servants of Saruman.'
'Yes? Can I help you?'
Bring the necklace to Ladenthir in Echad Eregion
An Ornate Necklace
One of the half-orcs of Barad Morlas was carrying an ornate necklace, you should return it to Ladenthir.

Ladenthir is in Echad Eregion, south of High Hollin.
You should bring the necklace to Ladenthir for further inspection.
Defeated lizards (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'This land was once filled with the beautiful music of birds. Squirrels played in the heather, and deer wandered the hill-slopes of the mountains. But they are all silent now, driven off or killed by the invading evils.
'When the half-orcs and Uruk-hai of Saruman came, they brought with them foul creatures, none more destructive than the Lizards in Ulundín, near the southern tip of Emyn Naer. They sneak into trees and eat birds, find the unsuspecting squirrel in the holly-bush, even catch the mighty deer unaware in the mountains.
'Go south-west into Ulundín and slay these creatures. If they are driven from the land, perhaps the wild inhabitants of Eregion will return in time.'

'You have killed many of the lizards, ${PLAYER}, but there are many more yet to be driven forth. Perhaps someday soon, as the Elves count the days, we will hear the song of birds and the soft feet of the rabbit again in Eregion.'
Defeat lizards (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Tinúriel at Echad Dúnann
A Plague of Lizards
Great lizards have been eating many of the small creatures of Eregion, stripping the land of much of its beauty.
'You can find the lizards in the southern tip of Emyn Naer in the area known as Ulundín.'
'Song will return to Eregion thanks to ${PLAYER}!'

Lizards can be found in Ulundín in the southern tip of Emyn Naer, south-west of Echad Dúnann.

Anurandir has escaped Barad Morlas

'I... I am the leader of the trackers of Echad Eregion... we have kept a close watch on the half-orcs of Barad Morlas. Through our vigilance we have marked the coming and going of their messengers, supplies... even intercepted orders.
'I was captured, please, help me escape. I fear that soon they will be back to torture information from me.'

'Anurandir returned and spoke with me, I could hardly believe his tale! You are truly a ${CLASS} of great skill. Anurandir returned to his duties in the wild, but your rescue will not soon be forgotten.'
Save Anurandir

Anurandir was captured by half-orcs, and it is up to you to save him.

'The ruins of Pembar are a sad place, once filled with the music of harps and the soft tap of jeweller's hammers. Now it is filled with the stench of rotten flesh and evil beasts.
'One of these monsters has been spreading the filth of his kind throughout the ruins of Pembar, a great worm: Nethgarch. Go to Pembar and seek out this worm-sire. Without him, this line of worms will fail.
'Pembar is north-east of Echad Eregion and south-east of Glâd Ereg. He will be lurking somewhere within the ruins.'

'The beast is slain? The worms have never encroached this far south; it is ill tidings for one who still dwells east of the Sea.
'But you have accomplished much, ${PLAYER}, and should be rewarded for your valour.'

'Nethgarch may be found at Pembar, north-east of Echad Eregion and south-east of Glâd Ereg.'
'With Nethgarch slain, the worms will diminish in Pembar. I thank you, ${PLAYER}.'

'This land has seen many battles; its history is written in blood, though now it wears a veil of peace...for at least a short while. But the peace it knows is but a fleeting phantom.
'As the minions of Saruman and Mordor intrude upon Hollin, many other evil creatures have come here as well, not the least of which are the wolves. They have driven off what few birds and kindly beasts that once dwelled here, killing what does not escape them.
'The howling of the wolves in Tâl Caradhras is worse than the silence that follows in the wake of the foul beasts. Go and cull their number, then return to me when the task is complete.'
'You did well, ${PLAYER}. The wolves will not soon forget your fury! Maybe Tâl Caradhras will have peace, if only for a short while.'
Defeat wolves (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

As the forces of Saruman and Mordor scour the land of Hollin for the Ringbearer, evil creatures creep into Eregion.

Adjusting this mirror has helped the paths of the Dolven-view to be much better lit than they were previously. This will likely save many from falling or taking a wrong turn.

'So you were the one that adjusted the light, were you? At first I thought there was a fire, and that we were about to be attacked, but then I realized that the light was a warm, gentle one.
'I knew then that it came from one of the ancient mirrors I've heard so much about. I am only happy that I lived to see the beauty of the light system in Khazad-dûm.'

The paths to and from the Dolven-view are dark, but adjusting an ancient light-reflecting mirror has helped to light the way.

Swivelling this mirror back into place should restore a little light to Khazad-dûm. Once finished, you should seek out the dwarf Thettmárr at the Deep Descent.
'You are making Khazad-dûm just a little more habitable every day, ${PLAYER}. These mirrors will once again light our ancient home.'

You stand before a mirror deep within the Water-works. It is used to illuminate these flooded depths, but has been twisted out of position. The creatures of the deeps loathe the light it reflects, but that very light is the greatest hope for the expedition. Perhaps shifting its angle will return much-needed light to the Water-works.

'Excellent work. I can see the reflected light from here.
'There is much of Khazad-dûm buried beneath the waters here. Without that light, we would never be able to fully map and explore it.'
Speak with Sylfa in the Rotting Cellar
Mirror in the Mire
The mirror located deep within the Water-works has been twisted and is no longer illuminating the flooded depths.

Sylfa is in the Rotting Cellar, on the eastern edge of the Water-works.
Sylfa will be pleased to hear the mirror has been adjusted, and light shines throughout the Water-works, at least for today.
Swivelling this mirror back into place should restore some light to the halls of Khazad-dûm. Once you have finished, you should seek out someone at the East Gate of Moria in Nud-melek.
'You found and corrected that mirror's position? Excellent! Did you run into any trouble?'
Speak to a Guard at the East Gate of Moria in Nud-melek
Reflections of Stone Trees
The dwarf-mirrors of Khazad-dûm once illuminated the underground halls, but many of them have since fallen into disrepair or have been knocked out of alignment.

Dwarves hold the East Gate of Moria in Nud-melek.
You should tell a guard of your continuing efforts towards lighting Khazad-dûm once more.
The statue is missing most of the body from the waist up

'Do you see that shattered statue just in the centre of the hall, friend ${RACE}? According to records and carvings we have found, it once depicted a brave dwarf by the name of Helgi Goblinbane.
'The goblins of Moria have been systematically smashing all images they can find of him -- I am not even sure that this isn't the last remnant of his legacy! It was nearly whole when I first arrived, but just recently a party of goblins reduced the statue to the state in which you now see it. They carried off the pieces, boasting that they would become objects of ridicule in goblin-camps throughout the Mines.
'If you are prepared for a dangerous and noble undertaking, go look closely at the statue's base, so that you will recognize its pieces when you go seeking them.'

'So, do you think you can recognize the statue's pieces now, if you were to run into them elsewhere?
'I think the rest are in goblin and Orc-camps throughout Khazad-dûm. I would start by heading east to Jazârgund -- that's the direction in which the goblins who smashed the statue fled.'
Examine the statue
Talk to Uxi at the Chamber of the Cross-roads
Uxi fears for a wonderful statue of Helgi Goblinbane, a dwarf of great renown once, whose name resonates among the goblins the way Azog's does among the dwarves.
'It is a pity that such a great work of art would be shattered so. Is there aught you can do to aid in its recovery?'
'The road you have set yourself on will not be an easy one to follow, friend.'
'Your path will be long, but you may yet cover yourself with glory.'
'You are the one looking to repair the statue, yes? I believe I saw some Orcs dragging its torso into the depths of the Water-works, probably toward The Chamber of Dark Waters, south of here.'
'Have you checked south of here, to the Chamber of Dark Waters, for any of the missing statue pieces?'

The statue base is in the courtyard hall just to the south-east of Uxi.
Uxi told you to examine the statue base so that you will be able to recognize its other pieces.

Uxi is at the Chamber of the Cross-roads, north-west of the statue.
You should return to Uxi for more instruction.
The mirror in Tharâkh Bazân has been rendered useless once more. It seems that the creatures there insist on moving it out of position.
'So the mirror once again reflects light through the halls? That news lifts my spirits.'
Talk to Oxi at Jazârgund
A Light in the Garden
The creatures in Tharâkh Bazân keep tampering with the mirror there.

Oxi is at Jazârgund, east of Tharâkh Bazân in Durin's Way.
Oxi will be pleased to hear the mirror has been re-aligned and is useful once more.
Found the statue's arm

Helgi Goblinbane's statue would not be complete without an arm to grip a great axe.
The goblins of Durin's Way destroyed the statue, and its parts can be found scattered throughout Moria. A dwarf named Uxi endeavours to reassemble this statue.

'Thank you for your assistance, ${PLAYER}. It would have been a pity if this piece had remained in the hands of the Enemy.
'I will send this over to Uxi right away, for his devotion to the statue of Helgi Goblinbane is legendary already.'
Find the statue's arm
Talk to Arnod at Tharâkh Bazân

Helgi Goblinbane's statue would not be complete without an arm to grip a great axe.

The statue's arm is at Sulnul-dûm, east of Tharâkh Bazân.
You should collect the arm of Helgi Goblinbane's statue.

Arnod is at Tharâkh Bazân, west of Sulnul-dûm.
Arnod will be delighted to hear you found the statue-piece.

'According to our maps and Balin's own records, there is a mining site along the tunnel where you began to fret for your safety.
'You should try to overcome your worry and see what you can find there of Balin's expedition. My hope is that there is great potential in that mine for our own dwarves!
'Do let me know what you find, ${PLAYER}. I am counting on you!'
'By axe and sword, ${PLAYER}! You have my deepest apologies. I did not realize how bad things really were down here. We will need an entire garrison to clear these mines properly.'
Talk to Gufi to travel to the mine-site
Talk to Gufi at Menem-berej
They Mined Too Fast
Despite the dread you felt, Gufi wishes for you to explore an old mining site set upon by Balin's expedition.

'Very well then! You will see; we will be finding veins of mithril and clusters of gems in no time!'
<rgb=#FF0000>This is a Solo quest, and cannot be completed with a Fellowship.</rgb>

Gufi is at the Menem-berej encampment in the centre of the Silvertine Lodes.
You should speak with Gufi to travel to the prospective mining site.

Gufi is at the Menem-berej encampment in the centre of the Silvertine Lodes.
You should speak with Gufi about the survey-expedition.

The mirror in the Redhorn Lodes, used to reflect the light and illuminate the mine, has been knocked out of alignment, likely by the Orcs who roam there. The dwarves will have difficulty exploring safely if they cannot see.
'Thank you, ${PLAYER}, for fixing the mirror. Now I can see, at least until those blasted Orcs knock it out of alignment again.'
Talk to Auti near the grodbog hive
Reflector of the Redhorn
The mirror in the Redhorn Lodes is constantly being knocked out of alignment by the White Hand Orcs dominating the mine.

Auti is camped just north of the grodbog hive, west of the mirror, in the southern cavern of Redhorn Lodes.
Auti will be pleased to hear that the mirror in the Redhorn Lodes has been re-aligned.
The inhabitants of the Flaming Deeps seem to hate the mirror; they abhor the light it reflects. But the dwarves need that light, for it shows the way and makes it safe to explore and mine.
'Thank you, ${PLAYER}, for re-aligning that mirror. Although, I suppose I shouldn't get too pleased yet, for I am sure the creatures down there have already shoved the mirror out of alignment again.'
Talk to Thórgnyr in Anazârmekhem
Reflection of Flame
The mirror in the Flaming Deeps is constantly being disturbed by Deep-worms, fiery dragonets, and the Ghâsh-hai. Keeping it correctly aligned is a nigh-impossible task.

Thórgnyr is in Anazârmekhem, north of The Cross-roads of Ash.
Thórgnyr will want to know that you re-aligned the mirror.
This mirror stands alone in a terrible corrupted mire of passages, with the fungus creeping around it. You should tell someone at the Shadowed Refuge of the mirror you found in the deeps.
'My thanks, ${PLAYER}. It won't be long before something or other decides to fiddle with it again, I'm sure, but for the time being it's just a bit brighter down here, don't you think?'
Speak with Drafli
A Glimmer of Hope
The mirror set within the Foundations of Stone is the sole source of pure light in these stygian depths. The evil things that creep about often ruin its alignment to restore the darkness.

Drafli is in the Shadowed Refuge in the western reaches of the Foundations of Stone.
You should tell Drafli that you have re-aligned the mirror.

By swiveling this mirror back into place, you will help to restore the old lighting system to the dark and dangerous halls of Moria. It is a small victory for the dwarves' expedition, but a victory nonetheless.

'Ah, ${PLAYER}! I wondered who brought the light back to this hall. Your efforts to restore the lighting system are a great endeavour, you know. It may seem a minor task, but I think this is a great deed!'
Speak with Simbi at the Twenty-first Hall
Reflecting on the Past
The mirrors of Moria often get knocked out of alignment by the unwelcome inhabitants of the deeps.

Simbi is in the Twenty-first Hall in Zelem-melek.

Instance: The Siege of Barad Morlas

The Elves have launched an attack to retake Barad Morlas from the Dunlendings who have invaded Eregion. While the initial attack was successful, a larger force of Dunlendings fell upon the Elves while they were caring for their wounded. Now trapped among the ruins and pinned under assaults from the Dunlendings' siege-engines, the Elves are in desperate need of aid.

While the Elves are skilled warriors capable of easily fending off the Dunlendings' assaults, the siege-engines in the field have them pinned down and are dwindling their numbers. You must take to the field, find the siege-engines, and defeat their crews, buying respite for the Elven defenders.
With his siege-engines out of commission and his assault faltering, the Dunlending commander is leading a final attack against the bridge. He must be stopped.
Having defeated the Dunlendings and routed their forces, you may now use the ancient forge to empower your infused sapphire with the blessings of the Elves.
Speak with Perimbant to return to Echad Dúnann.
The Elves at Barad Morlas have been overrun!

'The forge hidden within the ruins of Barad Morlas in Eregion should prove suitable to imbue the quality you seek upon your weapon.
'Unfortunately, those ruins have been held for the past several weeks by a force of Dunlendings from the south. Luck is with you, however, for a company of my brethren have set forth recently to dislodge the Dunlendings from Barad Morlas and retake the lands that are rightfully ours.
'If you can bring me an imbued sapphire which you will need to obtain the quality you desire, then I shall dispatch you directly to Barad Morlas. By the time you arrive, the situation with the Dunlendings should be well in hand.'

'Ah! You were able to acquire an infused sapphire. I will pack this among the supplies you will need for the battle at Barad Morlas.
'When you and your companions are ready to leave, speak with me again. I should have your supplies ready.'
'You will need to bring me an infused sapphire before we can begin.'

'Tidings have reached me that you fought most valiantly in the siege of Barad Morlas and saved many an Elf. My thanks to you indeed, ${PLAYER}.
'Now let me aid you once more. I shall use this empowered sapphire to imbue an Elven quality upon your weapon, and we shall see what you may make of it.'
'Were you not able to imbue the stone? Without an empowered sapphire, I cannot help you.'
Bring an infused sapphire to Perimbant

The Siege of Barad Morlas

The Elves of Rivendell have sent a small force of soldiers to retake the ruins of Barad Morlas from the Dunlendings of the south. Within these ruins lies one of the ancient forges where many items of power were made in the elder days.

'I fear I have received ill tidings from the Elves sent to assault Barad Morlas, ${PLAYER}. While their attack went as well as can be hoped, and the Dunlendings were routed without the loss of a single Elf, some injuries were inevitable.
'As my kindred settled down to treat their wounded and fortify Barad Morlas, a much larger Dunlending force has fallen upon them unexpectedly. The battle rages even now, and I do not know how it fares, but I can arrange for swift travel to their aid if you are prepared!
'If we can hold Barad Morlas against this assault with your help, then surely the Commander there would be more than happy to allow you the use of our forges.'
'My thanks to you for defeating the assault upon Barad Morlas! You have saved many an Elf by your selfless actions!'
Perimbant has asked you to bring him an infused sapphire which may allow your weapon to be imbued with an Elven quality. Where you may find such a sapphire, the Elf does not know.

'Have you heard a great creaking and churning in your travels of the Water-works? That sound is from one of the ancient water-wheels which once powered the great forges of Khazad-dûm. Without those wheels, the forges would overheat, and all the dwarves would have burned and met their end.
'However, not all of the wheels still work. The Great Wheel has long stood dormant, and it is time we renewed its churn. If you can, do us a favour and drive out some of the creatures in the area. If we are to refire the forges, we will need to control the wheels first.
'The water-wheels can be found by The Great Wheel, south-west of here.'

'So you found it?
'Well, I am impressed. Many would have succumbed to the waters or the creatures of the deeps. Your help is greatly appreciated.'

'I studied the samples you brought me and have determined how we can best thin out everything down here with one simple stroke. The deep-toads are the key to the survival of the lizards and spiders. To strike the deep-toads will be to strike their predators as well.
'How, you ask? The lizards are unaffected by the venom of the spiders, and so the spiders cannot weaken them, making them undesirable prey for the spiders. Also, the lizards have enough cunning to avoid the webs of the spiders. The toads, on the other hand, are nearly mindless in contrast; lizard and spider alike have little difficulty trapping and devouring the toads.
'If you remove the toads, the spiders and lizards will have no choice but to fall upon each other. Will you do this?'
'Excellent work, ${PLAYER}. I have faith that soon the creatures in the Water-works will no longer be a threat, and we will be able to retake it with ease.'

'If we thin the toads, the rest will kill each other off. I am confident in this!'
'It will take a little time, but we will eventually be able to recover the Water-works from the creeping things which dwell here.'

'The goblins keep smashing the dwarf-lamps. Without them, we cannot safely find our way through the halls and move supplies between the camps we have established throughout Khazad-dûm.
'We either have to find more materials to craft more lamps or find a replacement. The latter may be easier, now that I think of it. I believe we can use bits of glass-spider legs to replace the crystals. In order to do this, though, I will need a great many of those legs.
'If you would, go out and hunt down some glass-spiders and bring me their legs. You can find a good many of the beasts to the west, near The Lost Palace.'

'I no longer have the iron I need to build the braces to support the failing bridges.
'The Ghâsh-hai have many iron weapons. If you were to collect some and bring them to me, I could melt them down and be able to make what we need. You can find the Ghâsh-hai roving all over the Flaming Deeps.'
'These swords will work perfectly. I will put them into the crucible, and they should be melted down in a short time.'

In order to repair the bridges in the Flaming Deeps, the dwarves need iron to forge braces and supports.
'It will take many Ghâsh-hai swords, but it is the one source of iron that is abundant in these halls.'

Repaired sluice-boxes (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Those White Hand Orcs will not get away with this! I had just repaired the sluice-boxes throughout the Redhorn Lodes not yesterday, and they are broken again. I know I am getting ahead of myself, but if we are to begin mining again, we will need those boxes to sift through the ore. It would be nice to just have one less thing to worry about.
'If you could head out into the Redhorn Lodes, south-east of here, and fix the sluice-boxes, I would be very grateful. You can find them among the bases of the elevated tracks. Take this pry bar; it should help you.
'When you are finished, return to me, and we will see about some sort of reward.'

'Thank you, ${PLAYER}. I know I may seem a bit mad to you, but there is a giant list of things for us to do to return Khazad-dûm to its former glory.
'While this may have been something that was not anywhere near the top of the list, it is nonetheless one more thing we can cross off.'
Repair sluice-boxes (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

The sluice boxes used to filter the mined ore have been damaged and broken.
'I know it seems like a trivial task, and that I am getting way ahead of myself, but the fewer things to worry about, the better.'

Auti asked you to venture into the Redhorn Lodes and repair the sluice-boxes the White Hand Orcs had broken. They do not serve an immediate value, but once the mining operations are restored, they will be used to filter the ore.

Defeated White Hand Orcs in the Redhorn Lodes (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'This is no longer acceptable, friend ${CLASS}. These White Hand Orcs are acting as though they can just march into our ancient realm and take it for Saruman the White.
'We surrendered Khazad-dûm long ago under the terror of Durin's Bane, and the Orcs laid claim to it in our absence. We cannot let another usurper take what is rightfully ours! Eventually we will reclaim every last inch of the Mines the Orcs have despoiled...and that begins now!
'Cull their numbers. Make them start at every flicker of shadow at the edge of their vision, make them worry it may be a champion of the Free Peoples come to exact a bloody price for their affrontery! Look for them to the south-east, among the ancient structures of the Redhorn Lodes.'
'Ha! Wonderful, ${PLAYER}. A grisly task well-deserved. We will have the realm back in hand soon enough!'

Ingifast worries that the numbers of the Orcs in service to the White Hand are growing too quickly and may eventually be able to compete with the Orcs and goblins of Moria for the honour of being the greatest annoyance to the dwarf-expedition.

'I do believe that is a smile of success on your face, ${PLAYER}. I take it this means you have given those Orcs something to fear!'

'The Orcs in the Dimrill Dale are in disarray. They know not whom to listen to nor whom to trust and have even fallen to fighting each other. It is now time to show them to whom the Dale truly belongs.
'Return south-east to Uruk-gashan, Drû-garmadh, and Athmadhul. Find a suitable place in each and plant one of these dwarf-banners. Let them know the Dale will always belong to Khazad-dûm, and Khazad-dûm will always belong to Durin's Folk.
'When you have accomplished this, return to me. If you succeed at this, you will have certainly earned a reward.'

'I see the banners flying high over the camps of the Orcs. It is a fitting sign.

'The next step in my plan is a challenge. A White Hand scout has a patrol-route that runs along the edge of the Chittering Hole...they are distrusting of the insects there. There are a few crates near that place, and I want you to leave the evidence you collected on one of them -- the whole bag, yes...because it's more visible and off the ground, that's why!
'The important part is not to be seen! It's vital that the Orcs think one of the other scouts left it -- or better yet, play upon their superstitious nature. There are many things within the Mines that they view with near-worshipful fear.

'You did well by culling the Orcs. Now it is time to strike a lethal blow against all three camps. Each has a powerful leader, but more important than that, each has an envoy from Mazog, responsible for carrying messages back and forth from the commander of Moria's Orcs.
'Return to the camps south-east of here -- Uruk-gashan, Drû-garmadh, and Athmadhul -- and defeat the Moria Orc-emissaries. Breaking their communication lines with Mazog will surely turn them against each other for control of the Dale.
'May you find good fortune awaiting you upon this quest, ${PLAYER}, and may you return with due swiftness.'

'With their link to Mazog severed, the Orcs have begun fighting among themselves. Soon, the Dale will once again belong to us!
'You have done well, ${PLAYER}.'

Defeat the Orc-emissary at Drû-garmadh
Defeat the Orc-emissary at Athmadhul

The goblins encamped below the Dolven-view have become a great threat to the dwarves, driven by their overseers to greater violence than is usual for them.

'Return to Mazam-dûm and defeat the largest, fiercest-looking beast that you can find. Let them realize that, whether they have faces or heads or not, we do not fear even the greatest of their defenders!
'Mazam-dûm lies upon the eastern shore of the lake.'
'Hah! Excellent! No more shall those creatures be able to think -- if they do, in fact, even think -- that their mere size and strangeness will keep our weapons from drawing their blood!'

'I doubt such horrors would have peopled Durin's worst nightmares. In his name, rid us of some of this infestation!
'You will find many of these infested Orcs to the south, around the encampment they call Dalgum-ru.'
'This situation is revolting! It is a good thing you've gotten rid of some of those Orcs, ${PLAYER}, but our work is far from done!'

'You have greatly lightened my mind, ${PLAYER}. Now perhaps I can just put the whole business out....
'What! You saw dwarf-corpses there? And they were gnawed upon? Ai-oi!'

'Take this water-skin and fill it with fresh water. Add that to the Orcs' stagnant spring, and I feel confident we could see some significant results!
'The only place you will find fresh water around here is within the small cave nearby. Once you've filled your water-skin, take it and empty it into the Orcs' spring at Dalgum-ru to the south.'

It relates how he repaid a service from his friend Falgeirr by creating many stone plaques, inscribed with various simple images, and decided to keep some for himself, that he might leave clues for his own descendants as to where his family's treasure was hidden.

\qI have a hundred legs and cannot stand. I have no head and a long neck. I cannot see, but I am neat as can be.\q

This map is old, frayed, and has been handled a great deal. It depicts a hidden chamber and bears complicated instructions for the making of a very unique torch.

'What have you here? Show me -- let's spread it out on the ground and take a proper look.
'This map is old, but it is not from the Khazad-dûm of Durin's time. I am certain of that: look at how straight the lines of these runes are. These are of a style popular some few centuries ago in Ered Luin. It gives instructions for the making of a torch the likes of which I have never even heard! By Durin's beard, look at what it takes... why, this oil-coated base will be hard enough to find.
'One moment. I have it! The Warg-riders sometimes bear similar torches, dipped in rock-oil: take one from one of them, and you will be one step closer to crafting this torch. Head east down Khadar-zarâm, then look to the south.'

'This should do very nicely, ${PLAYER}. Very nicely, indeed.
'Now, let us examine the map for the next component of this torch....
'The next instructions are... somewhat unpleasant. Do you know where to find deep-crawlers? We need to gather their ichor, turn it into a paste and smear it all over the torch. Apparently the ichor has some effect on the colour or brightness of the torch, I am not sure which.
'I have seen deep-crawlers to the south-east of here, beyond the foot of Khadar-zarâm, yet before the Bridge of Khazad-dûm. Look for them around the eastern pools.
'Bring me whatever ichor you can, and we will proceed to the next step.'
Talk to dwarves in the Twenty-first Hall about the map

'I recognize that deep-crawler ichor is not exactly the most appealing thing to be gathering. I would suggest you try to keep it from getting on your clothes.'

'Your glow well-nigh announced your return, my good -- and slightly dripping -- ${CLASS}.
'It is the work of but a few moments to turn this into the paste described in the instructions the map bears....
'I'm not entirely sure that my finger will ever stop glowing green. Whatever will they ask for next?
'Are you sure you want to continue on this endeavour, my foolhardy ${CLASS}? It gets no easier. The next thing the instructions call for is a very rare ore -- we dwarves call it narfulz ore, because when hammered thin, it will burn with a white light that spears like a sunbeam in the dark. Aye, fire-metal! I have heard of it being used as a light, but rarely, as it is hard to find and refine.
'You will find narfulz ore to the east. Head into Nud-melek, to the edge of the Bridge of Khazad-dûm, and search that area. Rocks with the ore present have a green vein running through them.'

Shadow Map
In His Memory

'Yes, yes; I recognize that locket. It belongs by right to a dwarf by the name of Nykr. How do you come to have it, traveller?'
Roárr is shocked as you tell him all that you know regarding Nykr and the curious piece of jewellery.
'Alas for Nykr! He has fallen. So now you have come with your fell tidings, searching for answers as to why he would risk his life for so small a trinket. That is an excellent question, friend, but I fear I have not the answer. By all means, ask the other dwarves here at the Orc-watch about it.'
'Nay, I didn't know a Nykr. Why do you ask?'

'I met Nykr a few times in passing, and once he did indeed bring out this locket from inside his shirt to show me. He always kept it near his heart, so it must have meant a great deal to him.
'I'm sorry, but I know no more about it.'

'Nykr? I believe there is a Nykr staying at the Deep Descent.
'Oh. I see. My apologies.
'Nay, I do not know what that locket means. Best of luck in your search!'

'I have hoisted quite a few tankards with Nykr -- may the stone bring him peace -- but never have I seen this necklace.
'My condolences, to you and to his kin.'

'Finna's handiwork! Explain yourself at once, ${RACE}. How did you come by that? There is only one such example east of the Blue Mountains, and it belongs to my good friend Nykr!
'...Ah. So I suppose I should say belonged. What sad news.
'Finna is one of the premier carvers back home. She is also, or rather, was, Nykr's sweetheart. Their betrothal was made formal only shortly before he joined this expedition.
'Many regrets will follow us home; this one will make up part of my burden. When you next speak to Róarr, remind him that Nykr has a cousin, Kuli, who will have to also be told.'

'You know the story? Tell me!
'How lovely...excuse me a moment, I seem to, ahem, have a stone-chip or some rock-dust in my eye....
'I will send word to Gufi, and he will see that the news makes its way back to Nykr's loved ones, especially Finna Frostbeard.'
Find a dwarf in the Orc-watch who knows why Nykr died for his locket
Talk to Róarr at the Orc-watch
Finna's Locket

A dwarf named Nykr turned back during a rout because he had dropped a pretty puzzle locket, which cost him his life. His friend Gufi, distraught at this nonsensical choice, wants to know why this trinket was worth dying for.
'Let Róarr know that the locket belonged to Nykr's love, Finna.'
'I would ask the other dwarves around here why Nykr valued this locket so highly.'

There are many dwarves at the Orc-watch.
Róarr was surprised at Nykr's passing. While he did not know why his friend valued this little hand-made locket so highly, he suggested you question the other dwarves at the Orc-Watch.

Róarr is in the Orc-Watch.
Róarr will want to hear of the locket's significance, so that he can relay the information back to Gufi.

'This will not be easy news to deliver to Nykr's next of kin. I would do so myself, but my duties here prevent me from leaving.
'I suppose you will have to do it! There is much honour in performing this duty.
'His cousin Kúli is, as Kafli mentioned, the only member of Nykr's kin that I can think of who came with us to the Mines. You will likely find him to the south-east, at the Chittering Hole, studying the creatures there.'

'Aye, friend ${CLASS}? How may I be of service?
'Nykr dead! Alas, that is a tragedy beyond bearing. He was friend to many, reliable, kind...it will not be easy to spread this sad news.'
Talk to Kúli at the Chittering Hole
Next of Kin
The sad news of Nykr's passing must be delivered to his next of kin, a dwarf by the name of Kúli, who is studying spider behaviour.
'Kuli is out studying the creatures at the Chittering Hole.'

Kuli is at the Chittering Hole, south-east of the Orc-watch.
Róarr asked you to find Kúli at the Chittering Hole and deliver to him the news of Nykr's death.

'Poor Finna! I pity the messenger who delivers this news. I don't suppose you're going to the Lonely Mountain...? No, that would have been too easy, I suppose. Ah, well. To Nykr! Let us hoist a tankard in his memory!'
'Nykr is dead? What woe! This is a sad day indeed. Never again shall he and I quaff my son's good ale together!'

'${PLAYER}, Nykr's passing is a cause for great grief. I can think of only one way to properly celebrate his life, and death, in correct accordance with our most ancient and venerable dwarf-traditions.
'Nykr was friends with many on this expedition, and they are stationed from the Hollin Gate to the ruins of the Bridge of Khazad-dûm. Will you honour Nykr's memory with them, by quaffing a good ale with each of them where they are staying at the ten major encampments of my people throughout the Mines?'

'You did not know him as long as we, but you proved yourself a stouthearted friend to Nykr, my good ${RACE}.
'It will be through the noble actions of people like yourself, willing to both fight for the future and respect the traditions of the past, that the glory of Khazad-dûm will once more be sung throughout the world!'
Talk to Kúli at the Chittering Hole
Drink to Nykr's memory with his friends (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
In His Memory
You have celebrated the life and death of Nykr Locket-bearer with his friends (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Kúli wants Nykr's death to be reported and celebrated in the true dwarf-fashion.

'Ah, I remember Nykr well. He will be missed. When we were but little dwarves together, I remember once he hid from me a gem I'd mined myself, with my own little pick, which I prized above all my other possessions, until I apologized to another child I had insulted. I took years to fully forgive him....'
'I met him in passing several times. Good craftsman, could hoist a tankard with the best of us.'
'Let us all salute Nykr! To the memory of Nykr Locket-bearer!'
'Nykr's passing will be long mourned, and his life's story sung until I too pass, or may my beard be cut from my face.'
'O, what a grievous day! I am moved... I shall write an epic ode to the memory of the Locket-bearer!'
'What? Nykr, dead? This news bows my shoulders and weighs upon my heart. It seems that every day we receive more dire news... it makes me wish I had never heard the name Khazad-dûm!'
'Ho there, ${PLAYER}! Raise a glass to my fallen friend!'
'Nykr died as he lived, brave and faithful to the lovely Finna. May all of us find in our lives the happiness theirs held!'
'I grieve to hear your tidings, ${CLASS}. What tragic news to have to spread!'

You should visit, in no particular order: the Shadowed Refuge, Jazârgund, the Deep Descent, Anazârmekhem, the Dolven-view, the Chamber of the Cross-roads, the Orc-watch, the Twenty-first Hall, Durin's Threshold, and the Rotting Cellar.
Kúli wants you to speak with Nykr Locket-bearer's friends in each of the dwarf-outposts throughout Moria, telling them of his death and hoisting a memorial tankard in his name with them each.

Kúli can be found north of the Chittering Hole in the Redhorn Lodes.
Having muddled your wits with Nykr Locket-bearer's friends all over Moria, you ought to return to Kúli, his kinsman.
Grodbog Young
Defeated gredbyg at the Chittering Hole (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'I have recently noticed a strangely large number of gredbyg who seem to consistently linger around a set of doors to the south-east, at a place called the Chittering Hole within the Redhorn Lodes.
'I do not know what they are protecting -- or looking for, if not protecting -- but I believe that if a giant bug wants something, I should prevent it from obtaining whatever that is. Call me queer if you like, but I maintain that this is wisdom.
'How about you go disrupt their gathering a little? Head to the Chittering Hole, south-east of here, and defeat some of them. Hopefully, they will retreat.'
'I take it this means there are fewer gredbyg around those doors? Excellent! But they kept returning you say? I do wonder what they want there....'
Defeat gredbyg at the Chittering Hole (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Auti at the Orc-watch
Gredbyg at the Doors
Auti has noticed an unusually large number of gredbyg who seem to be protecting a doorway.
'I have never heard of bugs defending a door before...perhaps a nest or food, but never a door.'

The gredbyg are stirring at the Chittering Hole, south-east of the Orc-watch.
Auti is curious as to why so many gredbyg are gathering outside a door. He asked you to defeat several and see if the rest scatter or remain.

Auti is at the Orc-watch, north-west of the Chittering Hole.
Auti will be intrigued to hear that the gredbyg returned and defended the doors.
Defeated gredbyg in Nud-heden (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'I knew I was right to try and foil those horrible creatures! You will never imagine what I recently overheard.
'The gredbyg are raising their young behind the doors they were guarding! Behind that door is a chamber we have named Nud-heden...it was once one of our nurseries. And nay, I am not overreacting! Don't you understand? They are raising their young where once we dwarves raised our young. It is revolting! May my beard wither if it does not stop, and soon!
'Return to Nud-heden, within the Chittering Hole, south-east of here. Venture inside and defeat any gredbyg you find within.'

'Dead, you say? Are you sure?
'Well, that's good. I will send someone else soon to ensure those blasted bugs do not try to occupy those spaces again!'
Defeat gredbyg in Nud-heden (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Auti at the Orc-watch
Auti received reports that behind the doors the gredbyg were guarding, they are raising their young.
'You are wasting time!'

Gredbyg can be found within Nud-heden, in the Chittering Hole, south-east of the Orc-watch.
Auti wants you to slay the gredbyg who are nursing their young.

Auti is at the Orc-watch, north-west of Nud-heden.

Defeated the grodbog-queen

'${PLAYER}, we have done much, but we have only delayed the inevitable. While the grodbog-queen still lives, these events can only repeat themselves. No, she must be struck down. That is the only way the insects will stop coming.
'Return to Nud-heden within the Chittering Hole, south-east of here. Venture within, find the grodbog-queen, and defeat her. Only then will we be left in peace.'

'I thank you, ${PLAYER}. Now we can begin to reclaim that structure and return it to what it once was. Khazad-dûm will not be restored to glory all at once, but stone-by-stone, it will shine once more.'
Defeat the grodbog-queen

'Hurry! You must destroy grodbog-queen before she lays any more eggs.'
'It is a relief to have those vile gredbyg removed from Nud-heden!'

Auti is convinced the grodbog-infestation will not be resolved until their queen is defeated.

Rune Rocks
The rock glows with strange runes
You are near a rune-rock

'Wéorn, at your service. I am an historian. Khazad-dûm's greatest treasures, I believe, are in the records she has managed to keep safe for us, awaiting our return, protected from the ravages of time and Orc alike.
'Some of these records mention strange things only called rune-rocks...and the context seems to indicate it does not mean merely a stone inscribed with written runes, as one could find anywhere in Moria. The text speaks of them in terms of weapons or defences -- the dialect is a bit obscure here and there....
'Will you help me look for them? I have a feeling we will be glad of the knowledge.'
'You found one? Truly? What a wonderful bit of luck!'
Examine a rune-rock
Find the rune-rock
Talk to Wéorn at the Shadowed Refuge
Words of Light
Wéorn has discovered records of a mysterious item called a 'rune-rock,' an item that intrigues him.
'Now, I'm not sure where I would start looking...except that if these rocks are actually defences or even weapons, I would search in places where battle would be likely to occur.'
Wéorn wants you to find and examine a rune-rock, whatever that is, though he does not know where to find one.

Wéorn is at the Shadowed Refuge.
You should return to Wéorn and tell him of your discovery.
The rock-warden is approaching
Defeated the rock-warden

'I have further examined some relevant records, ${PLAYER}, and I think I may have some new information... these rune-rocks were used to ward off evil creatures in the deepest delvings during Durin's day. But I wager they had never seen the nameless horrors we have uncovered!
'And yet... I have a feeling that the rune-rocks may prove crucial, somehow. You may laugh, but when I follow my feelings, good things tend to happen. Let us follow this one, shall we?
'I think that if you press the runes on one of these rocks in the right order -- don't worry, I will teach it to you -- they make a strange sort of writing. More of an idea, really; an idea of light, and civilization, and truth, and honour, and courage. Will you try it?'

'What did you see?
'And you say it was discomfited by the rune-rock's glow? Interesting. I wonder....
'It's not that simple, is it? Can these nameless things be fought through words, language, speech... names?'
Use the rune-rock and defeat the rock-warden
Talk to Wéorn at Shadowed Refuge
Warding Runes
Wéorn thinks that the rune-rocks can be used to ward off an ancient evil, or at least mitigate its powers.
'Bless me, did I forget to tell you where that rock was? Look for it at Mazam-dûm, on the eastern shore of the lake in the Foundations of Stone.'

The rune-rock lies near Mazam-dûm, on the eastern shore of the lake in the Foundations of Stone.
Wéorn would like you to press upon certain runes on a rune-rock in order and see what happens.

Wéorn is at the Shadowed Refuge in the Foundations of Stone.
You should return to Wéorn and relate how the rune-rock irritated a Nameless creature enough to draw it out of hiding.

'The Orcs flowing from Khazad-dûm have found a powerful ally in the Wargs here in the Dale. This is a very bad thing for us here, as we cannot match Warg-riders in combat. They are too fast and too strong.
'If we want to fight this new menace, we will first have to strike at the Wargs. Head south-east, to Athmadhul, and thin the numbers of the Wargs there. Once we have done that, we can begin to think about the riders.
'Be careful, ${PLAYER}, for the beasts are dangerous, even singly. Return to me when you are through.'
'The Wargs have been silenced, but there is much yet to do. The Orcs yet remain, and they are a dangerous foe.'
Defeat Wargs at Athmadhul (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Ótam at Mekhem-bizru
Silence of the Wargs
The Warg-riders of the Dimrill Dale have been harassing the dwarf-encampment at Mekhem-bizru since it was first established.
'If there are no Wargs to ride, there will be no Warg-riders to raid.'

Wargs can be found at Athmadhul, south-east of Mekhem-bizru.
Ótam wants you to thin the numbers of the Wargs so there will be fewer Warg-riders to trouble the dwarves.

Ótam is at Mekhem-bizru, north-west of Athmadhul.
Ótam will be pleased to hear that the Wargs around Athmadhul have been thinned.
Defeated Moria riders (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'The Wargs have been severely reduced, and that is good, but I have no doubt their numbers will soon be restored. Their weakened state right now, however, gives us our opportunity to strike at their heart.
'There are many goblins at Athmadhul who now lack Wargs to ride. If you were to attack them, they would not have their mounts to aid them, and they should fall easily in combat.
'Return to Athmadhul to the south-east and defeat the Warg-riders.'
'The goblins were defeated before new mounts could arrive. Very good tactical strike. Now there is but one more thing to do.'
Defeat Moria riders (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Ótam at Mekhem-bizru
Riders in the Dale
The Warg-riders in the Dimrill Dale have been terrorizing the dwarf-encampment at Mekhem-bizru. With the Wargs thinned, it is now time to strike at the riders.
'If we attack the goblins before they can ride, then they are not Warg-riders. They are only goblins, and goblins we can defeat handily.'

Moria riders can be found at Athmadhul, south-east of Mekhem-bizru.
Ótam wants you to defeat the goblins training to become new Warg-riders.

Ótam is at Mekhem-bizru, north-west of Athmadhul.
Ótam will be pleased to hear the goblin Warg-riders have been defeated.
Destroyed gates (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'The Wargs have been defeated, depriving the goblins of new mounts. The goblins have been defeated, depriving the Wargs of new riders. Now, the time has come to destroy the very training track itself and deprive them of future Warg-riders altogether.
'Return to Athmadhul, to the south-east and destroy the fences that frame the track. Without those, future Warg-riders will not have the finesse to manage successful close quarters combat.
'It is a small step, to be sure, but not an insignificant one.'
'With the track destroyed, we will have little to fear from the Warg-riders. My axe will cut down any but the best... and thanks to you, we no longer have to fear that.'

'I am concerned, ${PLAYER}, as I am sure you are, by the capture of Amarthiel. Though she has been stripped of Narchuil, she may still pose some threat to the unwary.

I must concern myself with these things, as well as others, and I have tasked none less than the Elf-lord Glorfindel with the matter of Amarthiel. See what counsel he can give you, and maybe you can offer him some aid in rendering his judgement.

'I am surprised, ${PLAYER}. I had not thought that you would be the one who should choose to come and listen to a broken Elf-maiden's tale.'

'The matter of Amarthiel is grave indeed. It is a strange fate that Amarthiel, or Narmeleth as she now wishes to be called, is again imprisoned where she was once held for so long.
'She must be questioned, and though Master Elrond has bidden me to address this matter at once, I still have many other duties to which to attend. I would ask you to go and speak with her; perhaps you may glean some information of use from Amarthiel.

'Narmeleth's death pains me, though it may seem strange to say such a thing after all the evil she once wrought. The fall of Mordirith is a hope beyond hope, and the destruction of Narchuil and Mordrambor will be a boon to our efforts in Angmar.
'Bring news of the fall of Mordirith to Rivendell, for it will ease the counsels of the many there who must still take thought for the north.'
'You are ${PLAYER}, are you not?'

'The words of Glorfindel have shown their wisdom, by Narmeleth's hand or by none, though doubtless you played a great role in Mordirith's downfall as well, ${PLAYER}.
'Do not burden yourself with the oppression of grief. With Narmeleth's noble sacrifice, she has redeemed herself and earned a place among the greatest of our kind in the Undying West.
'Our foe in the north has finally been defeated. I deem that such an end has been put to him that he will trouble Middle-earth no longer; Eärnur can finally go to his long sleep.
'It seems that Laerdan has one last part to play in all of these events. While Failloth, one of the caretakers, was cleaning Laerdan's chambers, a parcel was found addressed to you, ${PLAYER}. It would seem that he left it for you before he left for Eregion.
'I have asked that the parcel remain in Failloth's keeping until your return to Imladris. Now that you are come, you should seek her and claim Laerdan's legacy.'

'Ai! Mordirith has fallen! These are tidings indeed, though woven with tragedy, as are all things in these days of strife. Narmeleth was a valiant Elf, strong beyond the measure of the wise.
'Take word to Master Elrond. He should hear these words from one who witnessed the event!'

'The hilt of Dúnachar! I trust it was not too difficult to find?
'Gather companions and speak to me again when you are ready to assail Gador Gúlaran. Time is wasting, and our road will be long and dangerous.'

'Though few believe it, I have been freed from the evil that once ensnared me. It was as the lifting of a veil and a release from chains that held me for so long. I am no longer consumed by the ring, Narchuil, nor the desire for it.
'I have dire news -- a warning for those that would listen: As Amarthiel, I had heard whispers of a hidden city of the Dúnedain, Esteldín. I had sent out a master spy to divine its location, and by now they surely must have located it.
'The Rangers must be warned of this threat; if the spy is able to infiltrate Esteldín, they will move a large force against it in secret. Travel to the North Downs and warn the leader of this camp against the treachery that I have sown.'

'I am glad that you have returned, ${PLAYER}.
'I was not always as you have known me, for though I was doomed to failure, my heart's intentions were ever true. Alas that Shadows will corrupt even the noblest of goals.
'I have much to tell, if you will hear me.'

'I was young and foolish, and Sauron taught me the secret arts of Ring-lore, and by that I was ensnared. With his aid, I forged a potent ring, powerful enough to sway the hearts and minds of those around me. Yet he regarded not in me the skill of a Ring-smith, but the prowess of a warrior, cruel and beautiful.
'But the violent losses of Narchuil and my father have purged me of the spell and the spirit that bound me to Sauron's will. I am truly free, though I have paid a bitter price indeed for my folly so many ages ago.
'I regret all the deeds I wrought under my spell of madness. Each death by my hand is a crushing weight that I will bear forever, even into the Undying West, if I am ever allowed into those hallowed halls.'

During the Second Age, the Dark Lord comes to Eregion in fair guise to beguile the Elves with the promise of secret knowledge. He captivates Narmeleth, drawing her from the protection of her father Laerdan and Celebrimbor's people, and the seeds of her corruption are sown...

'${PLAYER}, I wish to do some good in the fight against that evil which I created. Mordirith has recovered Narchuil, and doubtless he will seek to use its powers soon.
'Mordrambor is arrogant, but he has skill in the Dark Arts of the Enemy and is no less wicked than his master. He, too, remains a threat that I allowed to persist.
'I wish to aid in healing the hurts I have inflicted upon the world, even if by the least act. If you would but speak to Lord Glorfindel for me, I will accept my judgement, whatever it may be.'

'Would you speak with him for me? Learn what course he intends to take and his purpose. I do not believe that Narmeleth will ever be recovered, for a dark power dominates her mind. I sense the influence of a Power greater than a single minor ring.
'You will find Laerdan in his quarters on the lower floor of my house. With your aid, I hope Laerdan will use greater wisdom in his choices.'

'You would know what course I have chosen to take? Very well. I told the Council that Narchuil will never be reforged, but I believe that my own words may have been hasty.
'I do not believe now that the ring sank with Arvedui in the Ice-bay of Forochel. Aearil, one of the ship's crew, knew of Narchuil and its power. I do not think he would have allowed such an heirloom of my house to sink into the Sea.
'For that reason, I will myself return to Forochel and seek the ring. You may attend me if you wish...then perhaps Elrond's concerns will be lessened.'

'All right, it appears I may -- may! -- have been wrong. Perhaps.
'I've been sending such glowing reports to my friend Tyki, too...well, theories, anyway. Ideas. About the source of the fungus. He has some ideas too, in fact. Why don't you go talk to him?
'Tyki is at the Shadowed Refuge, far to the south of here. Head east into Nud-melek but turn south just before you reach the Bridge of Khazad-dûm. Continue south past Mazog's forces and into the Foundations of Stone.'

'Hello there! Tyki, at your service and your family's.
'Ah, good old Káti sent you? Gracious me. Did he bend your ears about his strange pet theory? The invisible stone-lines? It seems I receive another long letter from him every other week about it. Ha! Yes, that sounds like him. Had you go investigate them? And what did you find?
'I suspected as much. Well, no matter. His ideas may have been...off the trodden path, but he is right in one respect: it is vital to discover why Khazad-dûm is being plagued with this unnatural infestation!'
Talk to Tyki at the Shadowed Refuge
Fungus and Shadow
Káti is disgruntled that his theory seems to be wrong. He thinks you may garner more information from Tyki, a dwarf at the Shadowed Refuge.
'Tyki knows a great deal about mushrooms and infestations and things of that sort. You should consult with him on the possible source of this fungus.'

Tyki is at the Shadowed Refuge in the Foundations of Stone, far to the south-east of the Twenty-first Hall.
Káti believes his friend Tyki at the Shadowed Refuge may know more about the fungus.

'What? Speak up, ${PLAYER}, if you need something. I am Klintur. Are you also here to study the spiders? No? Whyever not?
'Well, look at them! Disgusting things. They have been infected by something, is what I think, but I have no idea what. I have been keeping some of them in cages below this cliff and go down to study them when I get the chance, but I have a small problem. One of them keeps managing to get free. There are many more out there, but the last thing we need is for her to get to the others and bring an entire clutch down upon us.
'Head down the cliff here and then look along the path to the north. She normally does not go far, I think she views this as some sort of wicked game. If you prod her enough, she should come running back to the safety of the cage.'
'The spider is back? Good, ${PLAYER}, good. That brings me some relief. I know she is a relatively little thing, but I've no doubt she could bring back a horde if she escaped.'
Encourage the escaped spider to return to its cage

'I think we need to find the reason for this strange madness being displayed by these spiders.
'I think that your answers may lie a little deeper into the dark. I have a friend, Jari, east of here, who is about to embark on a little voyage of discovery around Tunzelgund. Look for Jari and accompany him, if you would, and you may find the answers for which we're all searching.'

'By Durin's beard! I have no idea what that creature you described to me was, ${PLAYER}, and that's the truth, or may I never hoist another tankard!
'This nameless horror must be involved at the root of the problem...but how can we fight it?
'Don't look so surprised. There is a time for study and thought and lessons and speech, and a time for the axe of a dwarf to do the speaking!'

'Ah! Greetings, ${PLAYER}...come to help, have you?
'Let's start this way. If we are lucky, we won't need to journey very far....'

'When I was young, my father told me tales of the early days of Khazad-dûm. All of these stories ended abruptly, however, and no matter how many times I would ask, he would never tell me what happened next. I know now that the dark days were not spoken of.
'I fear by not talking about these defeats, about not even attempting to learn from them, we are dishonouring our forebears. I know Khazad-dûm keeps within it the tales of those lost battles.
'I sense that wise old Arnod may know where to look for record of these tales, but I dare not ask him myself. Perhaps you could ask him? Simply feign ignorance on the matter if he becomes angered.'

'So, you want to know about the battles of old? And not our victories? That sort of talk could get you in a lot of trouble around here, for those things simply are not discussed. But Búkk is a close friend, so I suppose I could help.
'Khazad-dûm, in fact, does still hold record of those days, though the goblins have strewn the pages all over, and what is left may be difficult to interpret without knowing more about the history of those days. Head east of here, into Salab Nurjundul, and explore the halls to the north and south. Return any pages you may find to me, so that I may help us to understand their meaning.'

'You found them, and the pages are all here! The complete tale of one of the great defeats of the Dwarves of Khazad-dûm, a priceless find!
'Allow me to study these pages a bit more before revealing their discovery to Búkk.'

Moria still holds the secrets of the past, including tales of the dwarves' great defeats by the Orcs of Azog.

'Speak with Arnod, over there. He should know where to find what I seek. Oh, and if you could, don't mention that I asked you to do this.'
'So, the great halls still hold record of the battles. I knew they did, and now I want to read them even more.'

Arnod wants to help in understanding the history behind the tales you found.

'${PLAYER}, I fear there is trouble brewing. Arnfinn left several days ago, heading east towards Jazârgund. He said he was going out to search the nearby chambers, to learn anything he might about Mazog and the Orcs.
'He has yet to return, and I fear for his safety. Would you look for him? He was last seen heading towards some of the Orc infested areas to the east. I fear something may have happened to him... and that could lead the Orcs back here!'

'So Arnfinn is safe? That lightens my heart, ${PLAYER}. He is a brave adventurer like you, but I worried he had taken an arrow in the back. I do not approve of him staying out there, but that decision is his to make... he is a reasonable dwarf.'

'Thank you for your help, friend. I was doing all I could to give us an advantage against the Orcs when I was set upon. The Orcs kept me trapped back here, taunting me with tales of Azog and the days of old, when the Orcs slew the dwarves in scores. I shudder to recall those days.
'Please, go back to Tharâkh Bazân and let Búkk know that I am unharmed, but will not yet be returning. The information we need may be found out here somewhere.'

Not to my fellow dwarves, for they will not appreciate them; to truly honour those who have fallen, we must tell our tale to those figures of lore. Of course, this is not truly possible, but we may still honour their memory in another way.

'Durin's Stone is a treasure of the dwarves. It is in that spot, staring into the Mirrormere, that Durin decided to settle here and build Khazad-dûm. The stone serves as an eternal reminder to all dwarves of what is rightfully ours.
'I fear for the safety of Durin's Stone. The Orcs spewing forth from Moria have set up a camp around it, and daily I see several of them working on reducing it to dust. This cannot be allowed to happen.
'Head to Uruk-gashan, south-east of here, and defeat the Orc-sappers around the camp. They are the ones with the knowledge to reduce the stone to dust and are the greatest threat to our ancient monument.'
'The Orc-sappers have been stopped and the stone is safe for now. This lightens my heart, but there is more to do. We have not yet ensured Durin's Stone will remain for the generations yet to come.'

Talk to Haflith at Mekhem-bizru

The dwarves fear the Orcs are preparing to destroy Durin's Stone, which marks the revered place where Durin I first looked into the Mirrormere.

'You stopped the Orc-sappers, ${PLAYER}, but I fear you were too late. It is not your fault. I should have gone myself as soon as I saw them. Although Durin's Stone has been saved, severe damage has been done.
'While they were preparing to destroy the stone, they chipped off many pieces. It has been defaced and made the fool of. There is but one course of action for us to take: we must reclaim what is left.
'Head south again, back to Uruk-gashan and search for the broken off bits and pieces of Durin's Stone. Gather up what you find and bring the pieces back here. At the very least we can salvage those, and perhaps one day, make the stone whole again.'

'It is as I feared. The damage was done already. Still, the rest of the stone stands, overlooking the calm depths of Kheled-zâram.
'One day, perhaps, these fragments will rejoin the rest. For now, I will keep them here, safe, in the event the unthinkable happens and Durin's Stone is laid ruin.'

'You have done everything I have asked, ${PLAYER}, and I thank you for that, but we are not yet done. The audacity of these fiends amazes me. It is not enough that we have cast down their sappers, nor gathered up what they attempted to destroy. They persist!
'One Orc in particular is leading the entire throng. I will die before I see him succeed in tearing down what remains. This must end here and now.
'Return south, to Uruk-gashan and defeat Istash. Durin's stone will never be safe so long as that foul Orc still walks among the living.'

'You have done it! Istash has fallen, Durin's Stone still stands, and my heart weeps with joy. We dwarves are not an emotional people, as I am sure you have found in your ventures, but the destruction of Durin's Stone would have made any dwarf sob.
'You have the thanks of all dwarves, and I am proud to call you my friend. Durin's Stone will continue to stand for many generations to come, and serve as a place where all dwarves can come and remember who we are... and why we are here.

'All of these Orcs around the Dale concern me. Were they all still in Khazad-dûm, I would feel better, but out here, they can inflict great damage. They have dug countless new tunnels into the depths from which they can launch attacks nearly anywhere at anytime. We can cripple their ability to do that if we control this place.
'I have seen the stockade of a great camp to the south-west. I do not know what is going on in there, but smoke rises from it almost constantly. It is clear that they are up to something which will cause us great trouble if we allow it to continue unchecked.
'Head south-west, to Drû-garmadh and investigate the camp. Thin out some of the Orcs there as well... that will make a second strike go more smoothly.'

'So, you have reduced their number, but they have begun making the machines of war. This will require an immediate strike. It will be better for us to catch them unaware than to face the grim alternative.'
