Destroyed Moria catapults (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'The siege-weaponry you saw in Drû-garmadh disturbs me greatly. I do not believe the Orcs could effectively use it in Khazad-dûm, but with it, they could dominate the Dimrill Dale and possibly threaten the outskirts of Lothlórien, although there seems to be some power within the Wood which defies them.
'Venture back to Drû-garmadh, south-east of here, and destroy the Moria siege-engines and Moria catapults. It is vital to our ability to hold the Dimrill Dale as a strategic location.'
'So, the large weapons of war have been smashed into tiny pieces. This is good news, ${PLAYER}, but until the builder responsible for them is defeated, there will only be more to destroy tomorrow.'
Destroy Moria siege-engines (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Destroy Moria catapults (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Alrekur in Mekhem-bizru
Bane of the Wood
The Orcs at Drû-garmadh have begun building siege-engines and catapults with which to wage war upon the Dwarves of Khazad-dûm and the Elves of the Golden Wood.
'Those siege-engines must be destroyed, for the safety of all!'

Moria siege-engines and Moria catapults can be found in Drû-garmadh, south-east of Mekhem-bizru.
Alrekur fears the siege-weaponry being built in Drû-garmadh and wants you to destroy several siege-engines and catapults.

Alrekur is in Mekhem-bizru, north-west of Drû-garmadh.
Alrekur will be pleased to hear the Moria siege-engines and Moria catapults being built in Drû-garmadh have been destroyed.
Defeated Nûst

'The Orcs' ability to wage a large-scale war has been hindered, but only temporarily. More must be done to cripple their offensive capabilities.
'We must strike against the leadership. If there are none to command the siege-weapons, they are nothing but a pile of timber awaiting a flame. If the commander is defeated, the camp is no threat.
'Nûst commands Drû-garmadh. Head back south-east and defeat him and end this threat.'

'The head has been chopped off, and the snake lies limp. With Nûst defeated the camp is in disarray. I do not feel they will be making a coordinated attack at any time in the future. Thank you for your help.'
Defeat Nûst
Talk to Alrekur at Mekhem-bizru
Herald of War
The dwarves believe if they defeat the leader of Drû-garmadh, the threat will be defeated as well.
'Defeat Nûst, and the siege-weapons are but piles of wood.'
'The Orcs will have a terrible time rebuilding their war-presence in the Dale!'

Nûst is at Drû-garmadh to the south-east.
Alrekur believes if Nûst, Drû-garmadh's leader, is defeated, the camp will no longer provide a threat.

Alrekur is at Mekhem-bizru, north-west of Drû-garmadh.
Alrekur will be pleased to hear Nûst has been defeated.
Craftsman of Destruction
Burned wood-piles (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'The Orcs have been cutting down trees in the Dimrill Dale, but it does not appear to be just for camp-fires. No, they have cut far too many trees for that. I fear they may be up to something more devious.
'While they are not needed within the depths of Khazad-dûm, Orcs are able to construct great weapons of war, weapons capable of laying siege to village, town, or city. I fear that is where all those trees are going.
'Head to Drû-garmadh, south-east of here, and set flame to the wood-piles you see. Hopefully that will delay them long enough for us to devise a plan to end their destruction once and for all.'

'I saw the smoke from here. That should set them back at least a few days, and hopefully they will venture into the outskirts of Lothlórien to fell trees... the Elves there will quickly dispatch them.'
Burn wood-piles (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Dagfari at Mekhem-bizru
Fuel for the Fire
The Orcs at Drû-garmadh have been gathering up supplies of wood with which to build massive siege-weapons.
'Hurry up and get down there. You will not want to have to deal with that wood once it has been turned into a catapult.'

Wood piles can be found in Drû-garmadh, south-east of Mekhem-bizru.
Dagfari, hoping to delay the construction of any siege-weapons, wants you to head to Drû-garmadh and burn the wood-piles in the Orc-camp.

Dagfari is at Mekhem-bizru, north-west of Drû-garmadh.
Dagfari will be pleased to know you burned the Orcs' supply of wood.
Defeated Moria siege-masters (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'The Orcs no longer have the materials to build more siege-weapons, which is a strong blow against their continuing ability to wage war; however, we have yet to reduce their existing ability.
'Our next strike needs to focus on making sure the weapons they have are useless. Return to the south-east, back to Drû-garmadh, and defeat the Moria siege-masters. Without them, the siege-weapons are nothing but piles of wood.'
'The siege-masters have fallen, and thus their weapons stand idle. We have little to fear from Drû-garmadh, yet there is one final strike yet to be made.'
Defeat Moria siege-masters (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Dagfari at Mekhem-bizru
Masters of War
With the materials for building gone, the dwarves want to next eliminate the operators of the siege-weaponry.
'If the siege-weapons do not have masters, they are no threat.'

Moria siege-masters can be found at Drû-garmadh, south-east of Mekhem-bizru.
Dagfari wants to next eliminate the Moria siege-masters who operate the great siege-weapons.

Dagfari is in Mekhem-bizru, north-west of Drû-garmadh.
Dagfari will want to hear of the defeat of the siege-masters.
Defeated Lûrkh

'The Orcs will not be able to make war upon us today, which is good. It allows us a moment of respite, though only a brief moment. They will have more catapults and siege-weapons built within days, and more siege-masters will pour out from the deeps.
'There is only one way to put an end to this camp. There is an Orc, Lûrkh, who is a master weapon-wright. It is his guiding hand that has made or directed all of the siege-weapons you have seen.
'Return to Drû-garmadh, to the south-east, and defeat Lûrkh. It is the only way the Dale will be safe.'

'This is a joyous day, indeed! With Lûrkh defeated, the making of siege-weapons has come to a halt. Now our foothold here and the outskirts of Lothlórien are both safe from serious threat--though I daresay the Elves would not tolerate Orcs on their borders.'
Defeat Lûrkh
Talk to Dagfari at Mekhem-bizru
Wright of Destruction
The dwarves do not believe the threat of the siege-camp will be silenced until the Orc-wright making the weapons is defeated.
'I feel we have only delayed the Orcs. In order to truly put an end to this operation, we will need to destroy the mastermind behind the weapons.'
'The Orcs will have a hard time recovering from the loss of their chief builder.'

Lûrkh is at Drû-garmadh to the south-east of Mekhem-bizru.
Dagfari does not believe the siege-weapons will stop until their mastermind, Lûrkh, has been defeated.

Dagfari is at Mekhem-bizru, north-west of Drû-garmadh.
Dagfari will want to hear of the defeat of Lûrkh and the end of the siege-camp.
Defeated Orcs at the Fallen Ice (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Orcs are a trickier lot than you might give them credit for. Travelling from Eregion to here in the Dale through the underground of Khazad-dûm can take days, even when you know where you are going. Heading through the Redhorn Gate is much faster, especially when you are bringing large and heavy loads.
'Mazog has dispatched a company of Orcs to the Fallen Ice, north-west of here. They are attempting to dig through the wrath of Caradhras.
'They cannot be allowed a second path through the mountain. Head up there and interrupt their efforts.'

'Mazog will have to resort to the depths for his travels now. While he has always had them, it is easier for us to stop him when he only has one route.
'Thank you, ${PLAYER}, for your aid.'
Defeat Orcs at the Fallen Ice (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Raskwith at Mekhem-bizru
Digging West
The Orcs of Moria are attempting to dig through the avalanche blocking the Redhorn Gate and gain access to Eregion.
'The longer you stand here, the more the Orcs dig! Get a move on!'

The Orcs are digging at the Fallen Ice, north-west of Mekhem-bizru.
Raskwith asked you to stop the Orcs who are attempting to dig through the avalanche at the Fallen Ice.

Raskwith is at Mekhem-bizru, south-east of the Fallen Ice.
Raskwith will be pleased to hear the Orcs' efforts have been disrupted.
Opened cages (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeated Morroval-slayers at Tith-maudhûl (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Orcs infested with fungus is bad enough news for us, but infected Orcs captured by merrevail is even worse. These creatures are canny, and I worry what they may be up to. If they can learn how to turn this fungus into a weapon, it will be many more centuries before dwarves rule these depths again.
'There is a camp, Tith-maudhûl, where I believe they have these Orcs locked up in cages. While the thought sickens me, free the Orcs from their prisons and defeat any merrevail in the area who might also be infected.
'I do not wish to think of the danger this situation poses to us all.'

'The camp has been destroyed? That is good news. We no longer have to fear the fungus being used against us by the merrevail.
'Another of my scouts mentioned overhearing one of the merrevail mention that their leader -- I don't know her name, but they called her She-Who-Must-Be-Obeyed -- had the idea of capturing Globsnaga goblins. Whoever she is, she's maliciously clever.'
Open cages (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeat Morroval-slayers at Tith-maudhûl (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Bési at the Fanged Pit camp
Fungus Takes Flight
The merrevail have captured several fungus-infected Orcs and are keeping them in cages. The dwarves are worried the merrevail might discover how to turn the fungus into a weapon.
'Hurry! Every moment we delay is a moment the merrevail have to make use of that fungus!'

The morroval-camp is at Tith-maudhûl, east of the Fanged Pit camp.
Bési asked you to free the infected Orcs from their cages and defeat any merrevail in the camp who might also be infected.

Bési is at the Fanged Pit camp west of Tith-maudhûl.
Bési will be pleased to know that you freed the infected Orcs from the cages and killed any merrevail that have been infected.
With the merrevail defeated, you may now destroy their siege-weapon
You have destroyed the morroval siege-weapon

'Reports indicate that the merrevail are a larger threat than we initially thought. Like the great armies of the South, they have great siege-weaponry with which to wage war. This is disturbing news.
'If we are to succeed here, we must infiltrate their workshop and destroy those constructing the siege weapons. Erlar is waiting for you to help assault their camp. You will find him east of here, within morroval-territory, at the base of the siege-camp.'
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTE: Erlar must survive.</rgb>

'So, Erlar's plan worked. I admit, I initially had doubts, but he has a mind for such things.
'With those weapons out of commission, we can venture deeper into the morroval-camp without fear of reprisal.
'Erlar said that some of the mervyl were being chivvied along by their female counterparts with threats of \qBogrian's wrath\q should they err. Whoever this Bogrian is, they fear her most sincerely.'

'Hadi sent you? Good! I have made all the preparations and now is the perfect time.
'The merrevail have left the siege-workshop undefended. We can sneak in and catch them unawares. On your mark, the battle will be joined.'
Talk to Erlar
Destroy the morroval siege-weapon
Talk to Hadi at the camp in the Fanged Pit
Workshop of the Winged
The morroval-workshop has been busy making weapons of war. Hadi is tasked with putting an end to their labour.
'Erlar is waiting just outside the morroval-camp. I ask you to make haste, ${PLAYER}, lest he be caught before our strike can be delivered.'

Erlar is waiting just outside the morroval-workshop, east from the Fanged Pit camp.
Hadi asked you to speak to Erlar and help him assault a morroval siege-weapon workshop. Erlar must survive!

With the workshop clear of merrevail, the nearby siege-weapon can be dealt with.
Hadi asked you to help Erlar assault a morroval siege-weapon workshop.

Hadi as at the Fanged Pit camp, west of the morroval siege-camp.
Hadi will want to know that your assault with Erlar was successful.
Struck the mirror
Bogrian has been forced to flee back into the darkness

'I have talked to the others here and gathered all the information you gave them. I believe, with the damage you have already done, we are prepared to strike against the queen of the merrevail.
'Our scouts tell me that she has one of the ancient mirrors of Khazad-dûm in her possession, and she values it very highly. I believe if you were to try to damage the mirror, she should quickly respond with force. That will be your opportunity to strike. Do not waste it.
'You will find it at the top of a tall tower, east of here.'
'So, Bogrian took the cowardly way out and fled after the battle. I am not much surprised. I sense she is far from through being a thorn in our side, but for now, at least, the victory is ours.'
Summon Bogrian by striking the mirror, then drive her off.
Talk to Folkath at the Fanged Pit camp
The morroval-queen has laid claim to one of the ancient mirrors of Khazad-dûm. If it were tampered with, she would surely respond with angry force.
'The queen of the merrevail will fall, and these caverns shall belong to Durin's Folk once more.'
'We have won, for a time at least, the caverns of the merrevail.'

Bogrian's mirror is at Dâr-rukh, atop a tall Moria-mirror tower which overlooks the morroval-caverns to the east.
Folkath believes the time has come to strike against the morroval-queen. He knows she has an ancient mirror she values highly, and Folkath believes if you were to tamper with it, Bogrian will appear and attack.

Folkath as at the camp on the western edge of the morroval-caverns.
Folkath will be pleased to hear that you wounded Bogrian and forced her to retreat from the battle.
Destroyed nests (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeated slingers in Skoiruzg (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Merrevail above ground take to the skies at night. In Khazad-dûm, however, they nest and sleep in several perches high above the caves, as though they were queer birds. If those perches were to fall, they would be forced to the ground, where we might meet them with our steel.
'The greatest collection of perches is in the furthest camp to the east, Skoiruzg. While you are assaulting their nests, take care of any slingers you come across. When we attack, we need to make sure we can get in close, and their ability to fight at range could pose problems.
'Hurry, ${PLAYER}. Much depends upon your success.'

'Excellent work, ${PLAYER}. Now the merrevail will be forced to the ground, where we are on even footing, and with fewer slingers, we can bring our axes to bear upon them without fear of darts. Now they have become the prey!
'Ha! I wonder what their queen will think of her slingers now that they've failed to protect their nesting areas!
'Yes, their queen. It seems that they are ruled by one they call She-Who-Must-Be-Obeyed.'
Destroy nests (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeat slingers in Skoiruzg (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Gúri at the Fanged Pit camp
Birds of Prey
The merrevail use several perches as nests. Gúri believes that if they were destroyed, the colony would be crippled.
'We must force the merrevail to the ground and ensure our approach will be unfettered.'

The morroval-camp is located at Skoiruzg, far to the east of the Fanged Pit camp.
Gúri asked you to destroy the morroval-perches and defeat several morroval-slingers.

Gúri is at the Fanged Pit camp, far to the west of Skoiruzg.
Gúri will be pleased to hear that the morroval-perches have been destroyed and the approach to the camp is free from the attacks of the slingers.
Solved the riddle of the ship
This is the wrong locker

A riddle, written in Falgeirr's strange runic language:
Weight in my belly, Trees are my back, Nails in my ribs, Feet do I lack.
Solve Twisttongue's riddle
Riddles in the Flames
You have found another of Falgeirr Twisttongue's plaques at Anazârmekhem in the Flaming Deeps.

The solution to Twisttongue's riddle can likely be found somewhere in the Flaming Deeps.
You have found another of Twisttongue's riddles:
Weight in my belly, Trees are my back, Nails in my ribs, Feet do I lack.

This is a piece of the torso of the statue of Helgi Goblinbane that once stood outside of the Chamber of the Cross-roads.
The goblins of Durin's Way destroyed the statue, and its parts can be found scattered throughout Moria. A dwarf named Uxi endeavours to reassemble this statue.

'I have heard of the dwarf Uxi's endeavour to reassemble Helgi Goblinbane's great statue! So the statue's torso was nearly lost to the flooded depths? I am glad you came when you did.
'It seems like the water rises daily. Before long, the statue might have been lost to history. I will send this piece along to the Chamber of the Cross-roads.'
Talk to Águti in the Rotting Cellar
Torso of Helgi Goblinbane
You have discovered the torso of the statue of Helgi Goblinbane.

Águti is at the Rotting Cellar to the north.
Águti will want to know you found a piece of the shattered statue.
Helgi Goblinbane's stern visage once more overlooks this hall

'You have gathered all of the pieces of Helgi Goblinbane's statue! Uxi is waiting for you at the Chamber of the Cross-roads.
'The statue is now ready to be assembled once again, to strike fear into the hearts of goblins and Orcs in all of Moria!'

'You have gathered all of the pieces of Helgi Goblinbane's statue!
'The statue is now ready to be assembled once again, to strike fear into the hearts of goblins and Orcs in all of Moria!'

'The statue is now ready to be assembled once again, to strike fear into the hearts of goblins and Orcs in all of Moria!'

'You have gathered all of the pieces of Helgi Goblinbane's statue! Uxi is waiting for you at the Chamber of the Cross-roads.
'The statue is now ready to be assembled once again, to strike fear into the hearts of goblins and Orcs in all of Moria!'

'You have gathered all of the pieces of Helgi Goblinbane's statue! Uxi is waiting for you at the Chamber of the Cross-roads.
'The statue is now ready to be assembled once again, to strike fear into the hearts of goblins and Orcs in all of Moria!'

'${PLAYER}, you have done what I thought was the impossible! Because of your actions, the name of Helgi Goblinbane shall continue to strike fear into the hearts of the Orc-kind within Khazad-dûm.
'The statue-base is there in the centre of the court. Will you do the honours of reassembling it?'

'Bellows and anvil, ${PLAYER}; what a long, strange trip you've been on. Those goblins and their Orkish allies nearly got away with their plan to erase the name of the legendary Helgi Goblinbane from not only their memory, but perhaps, in time, also from ours!
'I... this is such a beautiful act, from one who is not even planning to settle permanently within Khazad-dûm's magnificent halls. I am so proud of you! I just... I... excuse me. I seem to have a fleck of stone-dust in my eye....'
Talk to Uxi at the Chamber of the Cross-roads
Put the statue back together
Talk to Uxi at the Chamber of the Cross-roads
Reassembling the Statue
You have retrieved all the pieces of the statue which the goblins had stolen and scattered.
'Quickly, put it back together before the mortar dries!'
'It is an incredible thing you have done, ${PLAYER}! You should be proud.'
'You have safe-guarded not only our art and history by your actions, ${PLAYER}, but also our pride!'

Uxi is in the Chamber of the Cross-roads in Durin's Way.
You should return to Uxi, for you have gathered all of the missing pieces of the statue of Helgi Goblinbane.

Uxi is in the Chamber of the Cross-roads.
You should return to Uxi to celebrate the statue's reassembly.

'Ah! What an excellent find, ${PLAYER}. Many of us are very interested in Uxi's efforts to reassemble this particular statue. I will have this piece sent to him at once.'

'Ah, this is an interesting artifact. It appears to be the shoulder and arm of the Helgi Goblinbane statue that Uxi wishes to reassemble. It is incredible that this piece has travelled so far!
'I will have this sent to Uxi at once. He will be glad to see it safe.'

You have discovered the top of the head from the statue of Helgi Goblinbane.

'What's this now? The helm from a Helgi Goblinbane statue! Hammer and tongs, he was in many of my favourite stories when I was but a young dwarf! The Tale of Helgi's Hammer... Goblinbane's Gilded Helm... The Lay of the Goblin-rout... Helgi and the Maiden's Beard-ribbons! Ah, such fine tales!
'I have heard that Uxi in the Chamber of the Cross-roads endeavours to find and reassemble all of the pieces of the statue. I will have this delivered to him at once.'

Helgi Goblinbane's Helm

'And what brings you to our camp this fine...?
'What do you have there? Surely that isn't...?
'LET ME SEE THAT AXE AT ONCE!'

'By Durin's beard! Do you know what you have there?
'That's a lady's axe, that is! Look at the delightfully feminine curve of the steel! And this playful little spike right here! And look! The curve of that decorative etching imitates the distinctive handle of a fine-toothed beard-comb, such as only a high-born lady would use.
'What a find, friend ${PLAYER}! You must bring this to an acquaintance of mine, by the name of Kafli -- he is a student of lore, history, and society. You will find him in the Orc-watch, far to the south of here.'

'You have done us a great service already, friend, but there is something you should know about the Mines before you accompany the Iron Garrison into the mountains. Speak to me if you are willing to hear what I have to say.'

'You have been a tremendous help to us, ${PLAYER}, and have aided us with so many tasks! You have enabled the exploration of both the Brackwater and Filgogân for lost friends and hidden treasure, and have valiantly withstood the threats within.
'But the halls and caverns of Khazad-dûm may harbour even greater danger, and I want you to know what you will be getting into before you follow us past the Doors of Durin.
'Return to Ráthwald who stands guard by the camp of Echad Dúnann, and have him tell you the tale of the fall of Moria. He will speak of dark times, but you should know the story before you walk into the dark, even if it makes you think ill of Khazad-dûm -- though I hope it will not be so.'

'You have been a tremendous help to us, ${PLAYER}, and have aided us with so many tasks! You have helped us to explore both the Brackwater and Filgogân for lost friends and hidden treasure, and have stood tall against the threats within.

'You have already lent great service to our expedition, ${PLAYER}, and I do not wish to be held responsible if you come to a...bad sort of end. The history of Khazad-dûm is sad and grim, and it is Bósi's wish that all who lend their aid to our cause know what might await them inside the mines.
'I will tell you the story of the fall of Moria, if you will hear it, and give reasons why Khazad-dûm is called \qMoria\q by the Elves: \qBlack Pit.\q
'Listen well, and if you still wish to follow the dwarves into Moria, we can talk it over.'
Talk to Ráthwald
Talk to Ráthwald and listen to the tale of the fall of Moria
Talk to Ráthwald
The Fall of Moria
Because you have provided a great deal of assistance to the dwarves of Bósi and Brogur's expedition, they want to ensure that you know the story of Moria's fall before you help them further.
'Listen well, ${PLAYER}, and I will tell you the tale of the Fall of Moria.'

'Though Náin and his kinsmen stood against the great evil that slew Durin, they did not stand long: Náin was killed by the shadow the following year and the dwarves were forced to abandon Khazad-dûm. Many of the Silvan Elves fled Lothlórien in terror of the nameless fear, flying southward and cursing the dwarves as they went.
'From time to time some brave dwarf has been known to seek those halls. Lord Balin is the most recent, but despite some encouraging reports shortly after his expedition arrived, we have not heard from him in many years, and begin to despair of finding him again.
'Bósi fears that he has perished, but it could be that Balin lives still within some deep hall. It is possible, but my thoughts are like to Bósi's. Thank you for listening to the tale, my friend. You see now how important this expedition is to my people.'

Ráthwald is by the archway near the camp of Echad Dúnann in Eregion.

'Come, let us speak some more about riddles, and maybe we can learn something from one another.'

The orders read thus:
'Scour the lands of Eregion. Leave no stone unturned. Go with your champion, Llygad, Blade of the Dunlending, into the School at Tham Mírdain and assist my Uruk-hai, and there you must obtain what knowledge you can and return it to me.'
And so the missive ends, brief but unmistakably clear. If there is still any knowledge to be gleaned from the wisdom of Tham Mirdain, the Elves of Echad Mirobel should be informed.

'Our enemies to the south grow bold. We must endure so many foes in this land, but I think with your efforts these tasks will prove less painful than they have in the past. The arrival of this delivery does not weigh more heavily upon me, rather it inspires me to greater hope.
'We know now that the White Hand has intentions for the School at Tham Mírdain, so we can set a task to focus upon them. Thank you for showing me this message, ${PLAYER}. You have acted rightly.'
Speak with Gelirwen at Echad Mirobel
Collect Order from Dunland (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Dunland's Champion

The Dunlendings scouring Eregion have been ordered to pillage anything they believe to be of merit to whomever is at the root of the White Hand activity. Though the forces are scattered amongst the ruins of Eregion, there are a good many who have been sent to a more specific location.

Echad Mirobel is in the south-western stretches of Eregion.
You have found strange orders pertaining to the ransack of the School of Tham Mirdain, and a champion of the Dunlendings who will lead this assault on the lore-vault of the Elves. You should bring this message to Echad Mirobel, where someone will hopefully know what to make of it.

Opening the message reveals orders from a captain of Angmar:
'We are to dispatch forces to the Elf-lands of Eregion and there search among the ruins for any remnant of their bygone era. Outlying ruins are to be scoured but the main thrust of our forces will be upon the Ring-forge itself.
'Chieftain Gûrsh will be in charge of this expedition, a testament to the Orc's great assistance in our clandestine warfare. Serve him well.'
The message ends there. The Elves present at the Ring-forge may well want to know of this message. They can be found far to the south-west in the ruins known as Echad Mirobel.

'My thanks, ${PLAYER}. We know that the Angmarim are further defiling the ruins of our past, but we now have greater information on what they seek and who leads them.
'This information will undoubtedly prove useful. We shall redouble our efforts in searching among the ruins here within Echad Mirobel.
'I wonder, though, if you would be interested in some other work involving the Angmarim....'
You should not see this
Deliver the missive to Ornras at Echad Mirobel
A Strange Message
You have discovered a message among the belongings of a man of Angmar, slain in battle.
'These lands are long lost to us, but still...we shall seek to stop the Angmarim.'

Make your way to the ruins at Echad Mirobel located in the south-western reaches of Eregion.
The message you found speaks of Angmar's desire to scour the remaining ruins for any remnant of power or knowledge that can be used to further strengthen their forces in the North. It mentions that an Uruk named Gûrsh has been placed in charge of the expedition.

The note is terribly damaged by fire, but bits of it still convey some meaning, which is frightening and clear: Igash and Kranklûk were indeed something more nefarious than they appeared. Mazog may well know what they are, but he is unaware of their allegiance to the true Enemy. General Talug of Fil Gashan is nothing more than a gift from the Black Uruks to Mazog.
The note continued to explain that General Talug's army was growing more massive by the day and would soon be ready for some manner of transformation.
You should bring this to Teitur, Narfi's agent watching over Fil Gashan at Anazârmekhem.

'Preposterous! Raf was correct...I owe him an ale. Aye, we made a wager. He was telling tales of how this Orc seems to have a strange shadow around its eyes...I should have listened.
'It means that we need to be swift about our assault against Fil Gashan, I fear. Time is now of the essence and necessity, it seems.'
Bring the charred note to Teitur in Anazârmekhem
The Illusion of Leadership

A charred and crumpled note found on the corpse of Kranklûk confirmed some suspicions held by the dwarf-agents watching over the Forges of Khazad-dûm. What is worse, it mentioned that Talug, the general of Fil Gashan, was nothing more than a puppet.

Teitur is at Anazârmekhem.
You discovered the note on the corpse of the Uruk Kranklûk, and after divining what you could, it became clear that it should be brought to Teitur who watches over Fil Gashan at Anazârmekhem.

This crystal, discovered on one of Moria's Orc-kin, appears to be different than any other crystals found within Moria. You should bring it to someone who may know something about its origin.
Perhaps you could speak with Falgir at the Deep Descent. He may have some knowledge regarding a crystal of this sort.

'A worthy find indeed. Though I am unclear of where this came from, I know from stories that there were many such crystals stored in a treasury that we are intent on finding.
'But... this could not be such a treasure as the vault is long forgotten and well hid. It is unlikely that Orcs could have found the entrance. Yet, what if they have?
'Suddenly, I fear that this discovery is more dire than I had thought, ${PLAYER}.'
Talk to Falgir at the Deep Descent
The Fractured Crystal

Many crystals can be found within Moria, but this one seems different than the others. Darkened by time and appearing burned out, perhaps there is something to be learned from this crystal fallen from a Moria Orc.
'I fear that crystal is an ominous find friend.'

Falgir is at the Deep Descent.
You should bring the crystal you found to a dwarf who might know of such things.

All that is left of Igash is a dry and vile husk, as if the body was nothing more than a shell. You collected a small piece of this husk, which might be studied further. Perhaps you should deliver it to Narfi at the Twenty-first Hall.

'A strange fire? Aye, I know very well that look. Twice I have seen the master of the Forge and twice have I seen something in his eyes that was not right, as if something dwelled deep within the Uruk that was unnatural to his kind.
'I have spoken to others of this, and we fear that this is some new fell creature, perhaps born in the dark depths of Khazad-dûm. Or... perhaps something reborn. Regardless, they do not occupy positions of power other than the leadership of these locations. Kranklûk within the Forges is just another menace to be removed.'

'I have never seen such a thing, but the fire you describe in this creature's eyes is as well-known to me as it is to Pálmar. My agent watching the Forges of Khazad-dûm says he has seen the same look within the eyes of the leader there.
'I wonder if there is something unseen happening with these Orcs, something more vile than the smell these beasts typically give off.
'Make your way to Pálmar and tell him what you found. Perhaps he can give you more insight to what this is and means.'
Bring the husk to Narfi in the Twenty-first Hall
Talk to Pálmar at Anazârmekhem
A Desiccated Husk: The Fanatic's Tale
Igash appeared to be different from other Orcs. An unearthly fire burned behind his eyes, and when he fell to your blade, something was left behind and this husk is now an item of some consternation.
'You should speak with Pálmar at Anazârmekhem about Igash.'

Narfi is at the Twenty-first Hall.
You discovered that Igash was something more than a typical Orc and are looking for some answers to newfound questions.

Pálmar is at Anazârmekhem.
Narfi could give you very little information about the strange husk, but he thought that his agent, Pálmar -- posted in Anazármekhem -- may know something about the strange fire behind Igash's eyes.

The note reads:
'Mazog, something's off with that Uruk Kranklûk. The boys see it, too. I think we'd best start paying close attention to those troops disappearing in the deep dark of that shadowy place. There might be something more than mushrooms there.'
Perhaps there is someone in the Twenty-first Hall who can help you with this.
'Orcs afraid of something other than us dwarves? Ha! It seems that this has something to do with the rumours I have heard from our Elves and the company I sent to the Shadowed Refuge.'
Bring the message to Veúlfur in the Twenty-first Hall
Afraid of the Dark?
Upon defeating Talug, you discovered a note scrawled hastily and in nearly illegible handwriting. After some time you were able to make out what it said.

There might be a dwarf who can help with the note in the Twenty-first Hall.
The note seems to indicate that General Talug has some measure of both fear and apprehension of what lay in the deep dark places of Moria.

Where the blade should meet the hilt there is only a thin space where once a blade fit. This hilt is heavy and cast in very dark iron, wrought not by the hand of dwarves.
Perhaps Garthar at the Deep Descent can help you discover the fell means by which this object was made.

'What is this you have here? I do not like the feel of this thing.
'No blade, not made by dwarves... not made by Orc either, if my eyes do not deceive me. This blade was crafted within the darkest forges of Middle-earth, I would gather. An Elf may know more, but there is no time for sending you all about the world.
'I would venture that this is one of the blades told of that made the wraiths what they are. If there are others of these blades in Khazad-dûm, you should take great care to steer clear of them, lest you meet a terrible fate.'
Talk to Garthar at the Deep Descent
An Empty Blade
You discovered a black hilt in the belt pouch of an Orc-wraith within the Forgotten Treasury.
'Be watchful for such dark weapons, ${PLAYER}.'

Garthar is at the Deep Descent.
Garthar may be able to afford you some level of knowledge about the strange hilt you found.
You have defeated Chieftain Gûrsh
Defeat Chieftain Gûrsh
Chieftain Gûrsh

Scouts reported seeing a strange uruk, and overheard the Orc-overseers under his command calling out \qChieftain Gûrsh\q as he strode away toward the Library at Tham Mírdain. It appears that we have identified the leader of this war effort out of Angmar, and now we must do what we can to end this menace.
I would ask you to enter the Library at Tham Mírdain and challenge Gûrsh to a battle. If you can draw him out and defeat him, we will have effectively eliminated the leader of the northern forces.
We must be careful, however, not to attract the attention of the Orcs and Dunlendings from the South, for we do not have the strength to combat north and south should they suddenly join forces. The more stealthy we are, the better our chances to best all foes. Gather no more than two companions for this assault, for our hope is in secrecy. Before you make your assault, you should speak with Maegamiel.

Chieftain Gûrsh, leader of the northern forces of Angmar, can be found in the Library at Tham Mírdain, just to the south-west of Echad Mirobel.
Ornras of Echad Mirobel has asked you to take a small band of fighters and unseat Chieftan Gûrsh, which will hopefully weaken the enemy presence from the north without drawing the attention of the south. Enemies have been scavenging the Library for forgotten history that might be useful to their cause.
Collected Angmarim iron

'To our great dismay, we have learned that the Angmarim have established an outpost amongst the ruins of Mirobel. Through the repeated efforts of valiant folk such as yourself, we have done well to thin their numbers and ease the threat they present. There are... other matters at hand, however... and these matters, while requiring the Angmarim to further establish themselves in these lands, could prove particularly dangerous if our efforts prove vain.
'To that end, I will dispatch you to Mirobel in search of a very rare iron found only on the borders of Angmar and Forochel. This iron, taken from deep within the core of the frozen mountains, can be worked into a terrible metal in the hands of a skilled artisan. Though I think it improbable that such an artisan is among our foes, I would rather err on the side of caution and ensure the safety of my people.
'Only the Angmarim would be allowed to carry this iron. Search among them for the iron. Return to me when you have proven my inkling right or wrong.'

'This is an unnerving discovery. None of our efforts have yielded any indication that there is an accomplished weaponsmith amongst the Angmarim camped here, yet still they carry the Angmarim Iron with them.
'We must remain diligent in our efforts to thwart these enemies, ${PLAYER}. Your work does not go unnoticed.'
'Search the ruins in Mirobel for the Angmarim. They, if any, will carry the Angmarim Iron. Should you find any, return to me with haste.'
Bring Angmarim iron to Ornras at Echad Mirobel
Collect Angmarim iron
Out of the North

Angmarim scour Eregion in search of any remnants of the past that may further strengthen their forces. The small band of Elves found at Echad Mirobel wish to preserve the ruins as they are, and have asked you to assist them in this mission.

The Angmarim can be found throughout Mirobel in southern Eregion, near the Elf-haven of Echad Mirobel.
You should seek out Angmarim in Mirobel and collect proof that they travel with Angmarim Iron. If the fears of Ornras are true, the tide could easily turn against the Elves with the forging of great weapons on the enemy's side.
Collected Angmar's Brand (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'I hate to do this, I must ask you to assuage my fears and return to Mirobel, and to the presence of the Angmarim there. You have done much already, but the hardships are never done when such foes are at hand.
'My heart warns me that there is a smith among the Angmarim capable of working with the iron you discovered. I would ask that you return to Mirobel and search many Angmarim there. You might very well find a smith bearing a Brand of Angmar. In fact, I expect that you will.
'I have seen these brands before and they denote a level of respect to the prowess of the smith who possesses the item. Only a great smith would carry one, and only a great smith would work with the fell ore you found. If you eliminate this smith, the bearer of the Brand, you may do more than you guess to hinder the dour work of this presence from the north.'

'Coupled with tidings we are receiving from scouts throughout Eregion and those very nearby, the proof of this smith is grave news. Still, I am heartened to know that he is dead, and can assist the enemy no more.'
'Have you found a smith yet, friend? I fear our time is running out.'
Return the Brand to Ornras at Echad Mirobel

A Matter of Knowledge

When these lands were held by our brethren, the land flourished in wonder and beauty. The library halls were brilliant and the greenery lush. Many believe that Elves love only nature, and that admiration is indeed strong, but it is not the only beauty we see in the world. Knowledge is beautiful also, and in the library at Tham Mírdain, much knowledge was kept.
When these lands fell to darkness the library was pillaged and many tomes within were stolen...or worse: destroyed. Yet it appears that the Enemy believes there may still be knowledge within the walls of Tham Mírdain. If this is true, we must do our part to reclaim the books for light, honour, and the memory of the Elves.
If you are undertaking the challenge of scouring the library for lost lore, I would ask that you seek to recover as many books as you can from within the ruins.

The Library of Tham Mírdain is south and a little west of Echad Mirobel.
As you work towards cleansing the Library of Tham Mírdain, you should keep a watchful eye for any tomes which may still be intact.

Purging the Overmasters

Overmasters command the slave forces of Angmar. The Men we encounter in the ruins are too bold and brash to yield to the lash of an Overseer, so I do not think that these will be the slaves to which I refer. Nay, I think that there is something else digging under the Overmasters' watchful eyes.
Our scouts mentioned seeing the leaders entering the Library at Tham Mírdain. We can unseat them from this place if we keep our foray small -- no more than three, for, as before, we do not want to attract the attention of the southern enemies in this area. This is a frustrating way to go about things, but unless many reinforcements arrive unlooked for in these parts, we will have to continue to chip away at our foes.
I hope you can go through the Library in safety, friend. It will not be easy, but I have faith that you can do this. May the blessings of the Eldar keep you, ${PLAYER}.

Ongbúrz Overmasters can be found in the Library at Tham Mírdain, just to the south-west of Echad Mirobel.
Hethugúr of Echad Mirobel has asked you to defeat Orc Overmasters at the Library, and to bring no more than a small handful of stout companions with you. The southern forces must not be alerted of your presence, so attacks against either side must be small and covert.

Commander Târsh

Based on what we know of the White Hand's movements in this area, I have discerned that there is an intelligent uruk-hai at the head of the enemy forces here in Eregion.
He is currently commanding the effort to scour the ruins of the School at Tham Mírdain to the south-east of Echad Mirobel. He is a fearsome warrior by all accounts, and his name is Commander Târsh. I would have you enter the School at Tham Mírdain and face down this clever uruk-hai.
It is said that his ego is large, and that he fancies himself a warrior without equal. Perhaps we can use this against him. Take no more than two others into the School, for we do not want to attract the attention of our northern enemies as well. We have our hands full enough with our more aggressive manoeuvres against those foes, and it would be grievous indeed if they were to join forces.

Commander Târsh can be found in the School of Tham Mírdain, south-east of the Elf-refuge of Echad Mirobel.
Commander Târsh, a pride-filled uruk-hai, leads the forces of the White Hand in an attempt to gain information of old from the School in which he has established his host. Gelirwen wishes you to enter the School and face down this brute with the aid of a small fellowship.
Collected a symbol of the White Hand (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'At one time, the School at Tham Mírdain was a bastion of the free exchange of knowledge. Students of every art would gather in the courtyard or the great hall and there discuss history, crafts, arts and music. All manner of topics dear to the Elves would be shared among those scholars.
'When war darkened these lands, the knowledge prevailed in other areas of Middle-earth, but many scars of what transpired here remain upon the Elves. Now, the School is a reminder of the brighter days we once shared with our brethren.
'We cannot abide the arrival of the White Hand within its walls, and so we must do something to drive the Enemy out. Here in Mirobel, we have had signs and portents that a great leader drives the forces of the White Hand. I would ask that you search for them throughout Mirobel and search the enemies for a symbol of the White Hand... with that, I may be able to discern the identity and location of their leader.'

'Yes, this symbol is the one that I sought. I had seen glimpses ere you brought me this piece, but now I can study it closely. We have discerned that it belongs to one named Târsh, a commander of the forces of the White Hand.
'This symbol was the last piece I needed to know what we face. I am grateful to you for your generous deed, ${PLAYER}.'

'The White Hand must have a leading figure somewhere here. Scouts have brought me other pieces of evidence, but I still do not have enough information to learn what I must. I need a symbol from one of the White Hand to confirm that the leader is indeed who I believe him to be.'
Deliver the White Hand symbol to Gelirwen at Echad Mirobel

Out of the South

Forces loyal to Saruman have moved up from the south and begun to sift through the ruins of Eregion. News of their arrival reached Echad Mirobel; there, the small force of Elves employ the assistance of any willing to aid them in driving this foe from the Elf-lands.

A symbol of the White Hand may be found among the enemies throughout the lands around Echad Mirobel.
Gelirwen wants to preserve the memory of the School at Tham Mírdain and save it from the befouling evil currently residing there. She will not risk lives without first knowing the enemies that are to be faced. She has asked you to obtain a symbol of the White Hand from among the enemies to help her learn about these foes.

Biting the White Hand

Uruk-hai and Men of Dunland hold the School of Tham Mírdain, and there is little that we can do. I have heard that there are small forces making their way into the Library of Tham Mírdain to deal with the threat out of the north. I hope to do the same against the foes we face from the south.
The School at Tham Mírdain was once a place of learning where ideas were exchanged freely, and the Elves would discuss important matters and knowledge. It lays in ruins now, but the forces of White Hand think that there may still be something within those walls worth taking.
I would ask that any who wish to assist us enter the School at Tham Mírdain and purge the White Hand presence from within that forsaken place. You will find the entrance south-east of our station here.

The School at Tham Mírdain is located to the south-east of Echad Mirobel.
Lefnuichen, an elf at Echad Mirobel, asked that you drive the White Hand out by force, for the uruks and Dunlendings have taken over the School that rightfully belongs to the Elves.

Blade of the Dunlending

Gelirwen informed me that a great leader -- nay, a champion -- of the Dunlending entered the School at Tham Mírdain to assist the Uruk-hai and Dunlending forces in their ransacking efforts. This leader of the Dunlendings will serve this purpose all too well if he is not stopped.
I would ask that you make your way south-east of Echad Mirobel, and break into the School at Tham Mírdain; there you should defeat Llygad the Blade. With their leader overthrown, perhaps we can rouse fear in the hearts of the Men of Dunland.
You may wish to bring friends with you, ${PLAYER}. This will be a dangerous venture, for there are many warriors within the school that stand between you and your quarry.

Llygad the Blade leads the forces of Dunland from within the School at Tham Mírdain, the entrance of which is south-east of Echad Mirobel.
Faellion wishes for you to defeat the champion to dismay the Dunlending forces from their warmongering intentions.

Musings and Teachings

If you are to enter the School at Tham Mírdain, I beseech you to seek out whatever remnants of the great knowledge held within you may find. There may be nothing remaining therein or there may be some scrap of knowledge that seems to be naught, but if there is even the least of scraps, the Enemy must not be allowed to obtain it.
What knowledge might remain in the School would be held within the main hall, where all would come to listen to the discourse presented by the greatest crafters of Eregion.
Seek out this knowledge and bring whatever you find there to me.

The School at Tham Mírdain lies to the east, up a small incline from the northern slopes of Echad Mirobel.
Evil threatens to claim the lost knowledge of Eregion, and it falls to you to recover this knowledge before it is truly lost forever. Faellien has asked you to bring any scraps of knowledge you find back to Echad Mirobel.
Defeat dark defilers (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Orcs are bad news -- of that, there is no debate -- but some Orcs are worse than others. Garthar and myself ran into some trouble with a brutal sort of Orc a short time back. We thought nothing of it at the time, as we bested the foe, but they proved powerful... while alone. I cannot imagine that their power would diminish at all in a crowd.
'These Orcs use the very shadows in the mine against you. Be careful when you fight them, but fight them nonetheless, and when you have bested them in the vault, return here to me.
'The Forgotten Treasury lies a fair journey to the south and south-east of our location here in the Deep Descent. Do yourself a favour, my friend: do not travel within the place alone.'

'Most excellent work, ${PLAYER}! The fewer Orcs we need to deal with, the better off we are. Khazad-dûm shall be free of this dreadful infestation quickly, at this rate.
'Your efforts will be remembered by Durin's Folk.'

Dark Defilers

Crystals have been discovered in Moria, bearing marks of the Forgotten Treasury, a sealed vault hiding a substantial amount of wealth. This discovery has piqued the interest of some dwarves who now wish to uncover the vault and save its contents from the pilfering Orcs.
'Milling about and talking to me does not thin the population of dark defilers. You had best gather friends and make your way to the Forgotten Treasury as soon as you can.'
'Good work defeating those blasted defilers!'

Dark defilers can be found within the Forgotten Treasury to the south and south-east of the Deep Descent.
Falgir asked that you find and hunt down the dark defilers watching over the new inhabitants of the Forgotten Treasury.

The Deep Descent of Moria can be found north and north-west of the Forgotten Treasury.
You found and slew a fair number of the dark defilers who lurked throughout the interior of the Forgotten Treasury.
You have spoken to Garthar

'A moment of your time if you would, friend.
'When first we entered this place, we had no intention of pushing as far as we did so quickly. Now that we have breached this far down into the depths and we see the horror of what transpired here, there are some discoveries that make many of us uncomfortable.
'It is bad enough to know that there are Orcs and goblins all about, but to think that they have breached some of our most hallowed and secret holds... gives one reason to hoist a hammer and crack some goblin-skulls. Still, we have orders and we must abide them, lest we endanger everything we attempt here.
'My friends Garthar and Hafberg are concerned about some discoveries we've been seeing as of late. Crystals, dull and black-looking -- more like glass than crystals -- have been turning up here and there, and we do not know what this signifies. Speak with my friend Garthar, if you would, and see what he knows.'

'Garthar thinks that the vault is breached, does he? Well then, that makes decisions more obvious, if you ask me.
'Are you still looking for a bit of work?'

'Aye, these crystals bear the mark of the great dwarf treasury long forgotten beneath this place. Mithril may well have been the true wealth of Moria, but it was not the only wealth we knew here. There were many riches to be harvested from these mines.
'Anything that was not mithril was taken to treasuries throughout Moria and there stored for safe-keeping. Complex puzzles guarded the treasure therein, and now they are well-hidden by the ingenuity of the dwarves.
'I also know that one of our treasuries was recently breached by enemies. Our orders bid us to stay here, surely for our own safety, but I have a good mind to disobey. Alas, I have no more news to share, but feel free to tell Falgir all that I have said.'
Talk to Garthar in the Deep Descent
Talk to Falgir at the Deep Descent
The Forgotten Treasury: A Relic of Ages Past

Crystals discovered in Moria, bearing marks of the Forgotten Treasury, have piqued the interest of some dwarves who now want to excavate the location and save its contents from the pilfering Orcs within Moria.
'Garthar is a knowledgeable fellow. He will have more to tell you about these crystals.'
'I have no more to tell you. Return to Falgir; you must have seen him before. He is here in the Deep Descent.'

Garthar is in the Deep Descent of Moria.
Falgir confided in you about the discovery of crystals thought long lost, now turning up all throughout Moria. He has asked you to speak with Garthar to see if he can shed some light on the matter.

Falgir is in the Deep Descent in Moria.
Garthar told you a bit of history of the vaults in Moria, what they held and how he fears that one such vault is breached. He now wishes you to tell Falgir what you have learned.

'If you are to enter the vault of the Forgotten Treasury, we must prepare you for what you are to face. It is located to the south and east of here, though more southerly than east.
'Between our hold and your destination are many Orcs. These Orcs are likely a smaller, stupider breed than the ones you will encounter inside the Treasury, for it would take cunning enemies to enter such a protected place.
'It would do you well to hunt the lesser Orcs for a short while; this will give me time to prepare you for the adventure. Head south-east and south of here and collect a bundle of scraps from these Orcs, then return to me when you have enough.'

'Good work! These certainly came from good strong Orcs, which means that you must be ready for the fight ahead. I will tell you all I know, then send you to speak with Garthar and Hafberg, for they, like myself, have tasks within the vault.'
'You have not yet defeated the Orcs as I have asked? Are you sure that you are ready for the larger task at hand?'

'If you are making your way into the Forgotten Treasury, I would ask that you do me a favour and collect any of the crystals that you find within.
'They have very little value outside of this place, but their qualities were never fully researched, and history states that none who touched the things ever felt that they would be used for good purposes.
'If you make your way to the Forgotten Treasury, south and south-east of the Deep Descent, collect as many of these as you can and return them to me.'
'Excellent work, friend. Though it is unclear what purpose these would be used for, I would rather we hold them in safe keeping than allow them in the hands of the Orcs now plaguing Khazad-dûm.'
'Keep a watchful eye out when you are in the Forgotten Treasury for the depleted crystals. Should you find any, I would like to keep them safe.'

'If you are travelling into the Forgotten Treasury, as I expect you are, I would ask that you take the time to see that any relics or coins already taken out of the place are returned to us here. We would not like to disturb anything that is still intact within the treasury itself, but anything already spoiled by the Orcs should be returned to us here.
'Should you find anything befitting, I would ask that you collect these items from within the Treasury and return them here to me at the Deep Descent.
'The Forgotten Treasury lies to the south of here.'

'Ah, so many already taken. When we found the Forgotten Treasury upturned by the Orcs, some wanted to treat it as a tomb.
'I prefer that we be wise about preserving what we can of the past. Your efforts in this will help us do that.
'Thank you, ${PLAYER}.'
'Search among the despoiled ruins or any of the Orcs you defeat within the Forgotten Treasury. You should return any relics you find to me.'

Relics and Coins
The Forgotten Treasury houses a good deal of wealth discovered or mined in Moria in the elder days. Seeing that these remnants of the past are maintained for the dwarves is a duty worth undertaking.

The Forgotten Treasury is in Menem-berej, directly south of the Deep Descent.
You should search the Orcs and any spoiled ruins for relics or coins of the Forgotten Treasury. Hafberg would prefer that you not unearth any that may still be lying about untouched.

'The Forges are lost to us now... but we will reclaim them one day, and there is no time like the present to begin.
'Raf and Sigir, my two aides, need help in clearing out the Forges. They can be found here within Anazârmekhem. Speak with them, learn of the duties they are beholden to, and when you have finished assisting them, I will send word on to Narfi that you have successfully aided us in staving off the invasion of Lothlórien.
'While I have little love for the Elves, it will do us little good if their greatest stronghold falls.'

'Aye, Raf and Sigir both said that you proved a most willing and capable ally. We are fortunate to have folk like you aiding us here.
'Were it not for you, the Orcs may have turned out more arms than we could have handled and a fully armed and armoured force would have swept clear through the Dimrill Dale.
'Fortune shines on us that this will not be the case. You have my thanks, and word has been sent to Narfi that you are true, honest, and decisive. You have our thanks, ${PLAYER}.'
Help Raf drive the Uruks out of the Forges

Claiming the Past

The Forges of Khazad-dûm were once the heart of smithing within Moria. Here, the mighty dwarf-smiths would work the mithril and forge their greatest wonders. In the time since its fall, the Forges of Khazad-dûm have been flooded with massive lava-floes and populated by the Orcs of Moria and their troll and goblin-labourers. Here the Orc war-host hammers away incessantly, as they built their weapons and siege-engines in preparation for their war against Lothlórien.
'Speak with Raf and Sigir. They can tell you what is expected of them and what must be done to ensure that the forges are maintained while the Orcs are driven out of that place.'

Raf and Sigir are at Anazârmekhem.
Pálmar asked you to speak with Raf and Sigir and to assist them in clearing the Forges of Khazad-dûm.

Pálmar is at Anazârmekhem, north-east of the Forges of Khazad-dûm.
You assisted both Raf and Sigir with their tasks and should now speak to Pálmar to obtain his favour with Narfi.
Defeated Kranklûk

'If what I surmise is true, this Uruk is no common foe. It is a Black Uruk of Mordor, a blackened spirit riding the Uruk's own strength.
'It is possible that this fiend is even unknown to the army it leads, but who can say for certain? It may all be a trick of light in this place and the dark shadows that lurk in every hall of this once prestigious home.
'Use caution and shield yourself from flame and shadow when you face this foe. Enter the Forges of Khazad-dûm, south-west of Anazârmekhem, and defeat Kranklûk, the leader of the Orcs in the Forges.'

'This is a great victory, ${PLAYER}. This foe was something more terrible than I feared and still you walked out of the flaming depths victorious.
'I will tell Pálmar of all you have done.'
Defeat Kranklûk

The Forges of Khazad-dûm were once the heart of smithing within Moria. Here, the mighty dwarf-smiths would work the mithril and forge their greastest wonders. In the time since its fall, the Forges of Khazad-dûm have been flooded with massive lava-floes and populated by the Orcs of Moria and their troll and goblin-labourers. Raf has asked you to find and defeat the Black Uruk Kranklûk. He told you to shield yourself from fire and shadow when facing this terrible foe as he fears that it may be something more than a common Uruk.

Raf is at Anazârmekhem, north-east of the Forges of Khazad-dûm.
Kranklûk proved to be a powerful Uruk and perhaps something more. Still, after scaling down the terrible pit that the Forges of Khazad-dûm has become, you found and defeated the foe.

'It is a terrible shame, what happened here. When I think of all the wonders that were forged within the true fires of this place, and then I think of this....
'Well, there's no time to dwell on that. There is work to be done, and that means I must tell you a bit about this place. Within the walls of the Forges of Khazad-dûm you will find Orcs, Uruks, goblins, and mindless trolls. The goblins mine, the trolls carry foul-smelling powder to and fro, and the Uruks fire the forges so they can craft their arms, all the while carrying bits of precious mithril everywhere they go. Mind you, the mithril is no bigger a sliver the width of your fingernail, but with enough...oh the wonder of it!
'Regardless, the mithril is rightfully ours. I ask you to go there and collect it from the Orcs within. You will find the Forges of Khazad-dûm to the south-west of Anazârmekhem. Make your way there and return to me with the bits.'

'Mithril! It is not much, but enough to put a smile on the face of this old smith.
'I will keep this well and safe and offer you such great thanks that you might never know how pleased I truly am!'

'I know it is a lot to ask, but even a small amount of mithril will prove worthwhile over time. You should find bits on any of the forces now inhabiting the Forges of Khazad-dûm to the south-west of Anazârmekhem.'
Bring the Mithril Bits to Sigir at Anazârmekhem

'I will tell you this, ${PLAYER}: there are some fates worse than death. For tools of the dwarves, one such fate is to be held in the hands of an Orc, and that is precisely what transpires within the Forges of Khazad-dûm. If I had not seen the tools myself, I would not believe it...but I saw them leaning against the anvil as that Uruk forged away!
'Such a thing is incomprehensible to my poor eyes. I will not abide this. I need you to collect the dwarf-tools from within the Forges of Khazad-dûm. You will know them, as they rest against Orc-anvils throughout the forge itself. Collect them and return them to me.
'You can find the Forges of Khazad-dûm to the south-west of Anazârmekhem.'

'There now, little hammer and vise. We have seen you safely home. Well, ${PLAYER} has at any rate.
'You have my blessing, my friend, and I will be sure to inform Pálmar. Thank you for all you have done.'

'It is one thing to be destroyed, quite another to be brandished by an Orc. I will not have it. Collect the dwarf-tools that the Orcs are using at the Forges of Khazad-dûm and return them to me.
'The Forges can be found to the south-west of Anazârmekhem.'

'I do not speak much of this, but the Uruk-leader of this place has something of a darkness dwelling behind his eyes.
'Raf knows more of this than I, as he has spent much time deciphering and looking at old tomes and studying runes. Speak with him about the blackness in the Uruk-leader of the Forges.

'Aye, Pálmar and I both saw the black fire in the Uruk's eyes. There is something within it that is not normal. I have seen such things before, I fear, but only the most fiendish of creatures. 'I surmise that this is the same power that flows through the Uruk master of the forges, but there is naught that proves this as the case and so we can only surmise.

'My assistants and I have been watching this place for some time now, and we have learned much of what is going on within the walls of Fil Gashan.
'My aides can explain in greater detail, but let me tell you what I know. Orcs are not the most clever creatures, though not stupid by far. We learned a good deal while sneaking within Fil Gashan ourselves. We hid beneath their noses simply by wearing rough-shod armour. Of course, we stayed away from the ones that seemed a bit more clever, but you might find the same success.
'If you are willing to help, I will surely tell Narfi that you assisted me, once Úlfur, Vagun, and Yngvi are all pleased with your efforts, that is. You can find them here in Anazârmekhem.'

'A worthy accomplishment, ${PLAYER}, very worthy indeed. While there is much work still to be done to reclaim Moria, I think that we have staved off this foray against the Elves. No need to anger others, I say.

But it makes him slow, and metal gets hot when heat is applied.
'Aside from this, we only know that he is Mazog's chosen general and thus his right-hand. Defeat Talug and cripple Mazog? It is a difficult question to answer, but we can hope this is the case.

The Grand Stair once stood at the foot of a great cross-roads within Moria. At the height of the great city, it led to all areas of the halls and was a majestic wonder to behold. 'Never have I seen such a terrifying beast ridden by so confident a goblin. They must be destroyed, and to accomplish this, you must enter the Grand Stair, north-east of the Orc-watch.'

'You have done well to defeat this foe. I am certain that this goblin was one of the strongest I have ever seen.

'In my earliest moments here at the Orc-watch, I knew that there were terrible things in the deep. I heard rumblings through the walls, and then one night, as I stood outside the Grand Stair to the north-east, I heard the drums. Giant drums carried by goblin-slaves pounded in a terrible rhythm by other goblin-slaves. All under the watch of an Uruk-handler armed with a sharp brand. The goblins also carried a massive litter, and on that litter slept a massive troll.
'Its chest heaved in time with the drum-beats, and I could see a massive scar on its chest. As I watched, one of the goblins lost its footing and slid into the depths below along with the drum on its back. The other goblins stopped drumming, and without warning, the troll leapt awake and began slaughtering the goblins. Only after a moment of poking and violence administered by the Uruk did the Beast quiet. The drumming began anew, and the troll fell back to slumber.
'Whether it is a gift or a weapon to be used against Igash, it must be destroyed. Enter the Grand Stair and find this beast. When you have accomplished this task, return to me.'

'An incredible success and effort, ${PLAYER}. I can only imagine that the battle was difficult, but you succeeded, and that is all that matters.
'I tell you, never had I seen a troll with such terrible skill and power, and yet you have bested the Beast. You are truly a potent warrior.'
