The Flaming Depths

Deep within the halls of Moria, flames lick out of oily pools. It is here that the Ghâsh-hai make their home. A faction of these is aligned with the master of Moria, Mazog, and has come to the Grand Stair to pay tribute to their leader.
'Be careful, for it appears that the flesh of these Orcs could scorch any who come near them.'

Ghâsh-hai Orcs can be found within the Grand Stair, north-east of the Orc-watch.
Ossur sent you to face the Orc-forces of the fiery depths of Moria, who came to the Grand Stair to pay their tribute to Igash, an Orc devoted to Mazog.

Ossur is at the Orc-watch, south-west of the Grand Stair.
You should return to Ossur and inform him that you have defeated many of the Ghâsh-hai.
Defeated Gothghaash the Firecaller

'While the Ghâsh-hai prove to be a potent foe, they too have leaders, and theirs made his way into the Grand Stair some time ago.
'The Ghâsh-hai tend to gather near flame. When you make your way to the Grand Stair, search for a source of flame, and there you will find their leader, Gothghaash.
'Find him and destroy him, so that we might more easily remove the foe from the Grand Stair. Travel north-east from the Orc-watch to find the entrance to the Grand Stair.'

'With the head of the tribe removed, we should be able to keep the power of the Ghâsh-hai at bay. This news is very good, ${PLAYER}.
'We shall reclaim the Grand Stair in no time.'
Defeat Gothghaash the Firecaller
Talk to Ossur at the Orc-watch
Master of Flame

Deep within the halls of Moria, flames lick out of oily pools. It is here that the Ghâsh-hai make their home. A faction of these is aligned with the master of Moria, Mazog, and has come to the Grand Stair to pay tribute to their leader.
'Be prepared to face a foe at home in the flame. Seek Gothghaash within the confines of the Grand Stair to the north-east of the Orc-watch.'

Gothghaash can be found within the Grand Stair, north-east of the Orc-watch.
Ossur told you of Gothghaash, the leader of the Fire-orcs, and directed you to find and defeat him.

Ossur is at the Orc-watch, south-west of the Grand Stair.
You should return to Ossur at the Orc-watch and tell him of your victory over Gothghaash.
Defeated the Devoted
Defeated Igash

'I know little of Igash... only that he is followed without question, and that his Devoted seems to be nothing more than an ordinary weak-willed Orc. The two of them clutch the many tribes with an iron fist, commanding and taking at will, always unchallenged.
'Igash commands his forces from on high, and the path to him should be clear. Climb the old bridges, up to the highest platform. There, I suspect, he will sit vainly upon his crude throne. But beware... his Devoted will be keeping watch along the way.
'Make your way north-east, ${PLAYER}. There, you should enter the Grand Stair and defeat Igash and his Devoted. But be wary, for the Stairs climb high; a false step will be your doom. Only sure-footed folk should risk this excursion. May the paths of the dwarves guide your feet well.'

'I hope that this challenge did not prove too difficult for you, ${PLAYER}.
'Igash indeed does draw strength from those within the Grand Stair, assuming their skills while they still live. This would make him a terrible foe to face, I am certain, but how else can we obtain the tribute he maintains if not by defeating him whilst all the others still live?
'For now, I am grateful that you have defeated this terrible enemy.'
Defeat the Devoted
Defeat Igash
Talk to Avar at the Orc-watch
The Fanatic and His Devoted
The Moria Orcs hold control over the Grand Stair, and leading them are Igash the Fanatic and his Devoted minion. Alongside them are a host of fearsome Orcs from the very heart of Moria.

'There may be other ways to defeat Igash and his Devoted. I know that Thithrand has stated he believes that the White Hand may be planning an assault against the Moria Orcs. Still, it would be best to weaken the foe now, for Igash draws power from the forces offering tribute to him.
'It all seems very strange to me, ${PLAYER}.'

Igash and his Devoted are high up in the Grand Stair, north-east of the Orc-watch.
Avar has asked you to go forth and defeat Igash and his Devoted.

Avar is at the Orc-watch, south-west of the Grand Stair.
You should return to Avar and inform him that you have slain Igash and his Devoted.

'I have watched the comings and goings of the Orcs here and come to know that there are two of great note. The first is Igash, a fanatical leader who is pledged to serving Mazog. He rules the Grand Stair and uses his Devoted, the second of these Orcs of note, to keep his troops cowed.
'Igash collects great tributes from the other Orc-tribes and stores them in his throne room. He coerces them into delivering more of this tribute to him in an effort to play them against one another and gain wealth for his master.
'I have paid closer attention on this foe so that we might ruin his power and drive him from the Grand Stair. There are two tasks I would have you complete to satisfy my call for assistance. Will you aid me?'

'Aye, the tasks are done. The Moria Orcs are weaker, and your efforts will grant us the ability to keep a closer watch on these forces. Once you have completed the tasks for Thithrand and Ossur, I will send word on to Narfi that the Orcs of the Grand Stair are no longer a threat.'
Help Avar defeat the leaders of the Orcs within the Grand Stair
Help Avar weaken the forces of the Moria Orcs in the Grand Stair
Talk to Avar at the Orc-watch
Mazog's Minions

The Grand Stair once stood at the foot of a great cross-roads within Moria. At the height of the great city, it led to all areas of the halls and was a majestic wonder to behold. Now it has fallen to the care of Igash, a lieutenant of the Moria Orc-leader Mazog. Igash assembled the forces of Orcs and trolls within Moria in one place and has collected tribute from each to one day bring to the leader of the Orcs. For now, each tribe vies for favour from the lieutenant, a fanatical follower of Mazog.
'The leaders of the Moria Orcs must be slain and their number must be thinned. If you complete the two tasks I lay before you, you will earn my favour.'

Avar is at the Orc-watch.
Avar has asked you to assist him with two tasks to earn his faith and satisfy him that the Orcs of the Grand Stair are no longer a serious threat.

Avar is at the Orc-watch, south-west of the Grand Stair.
Now that Avar's tasks are complete, you should return to him with your report.
Defeated Gazathrug Enforcers (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeated Gazathrug Lurkers (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Igash's throne dais is patrolled by his master guard. These Orcs seem to be of the same breed found throughout Khazad-dûm, but are stronger and more deadly.
'We must be diligent in dealing with these Orcs, lest they bring their war-plans to fruition.
'You will find the Orcs beyond the bridges of the Grand Stair, north-east of the Orc-watch.'

'With their numbers dwindling, it will not be long before the Moria Orcs are naught more than a memory in this area. Your efforts are exemplary, ${PLAYER}, and you will be known throughout these halls as a hero to all.
'I thank you for your efforts thus far.'
Defeat Gazathrug Enforcers (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeat Gazathrug Lurkers (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Avar at the Orc-watch
War Host Assembled
The Moria Orcs hold control over the Grand Stair, and at their head are Igash the Fanatic and his Devoted. Alongside them is a host of fearsome Orcs from the heart of Moria.
'Be cautious as you travel through the Grand Stair and defeat as many of these foes as you can.'

The Orcs can be found at the Grand Stair, north-east of the Orc-watch.
Avar has tasked you with defeating the Orcs who guard the throne of Igash.

Avar is at the Orc-watch, south-west of the Grand Stair.
You should return to Avar with news of your success.

'Narfi was wise to send us help. We have been watching the Grand Stair for some time, and I fear that we are woefully outnumbered. I have split our number: myself, Ossur, and Thithrand have placed our focus on different forces arrayed within the Grand Stair. When all our tasks are complete, I will vouch for you with Narfi, and we will lay claim to this area once again. Until that time, however, there is much to explain.
'Within the Grand Stair are five tribes of Orcs and trolls. There are those from beyond Khazad-dûm: the White Hand and the Warg-riders. I have set Thithrand to the task of tracking their movements. The second are the deep-dwelling forces of trolls and Orcs of fire. Ossur watches over this host. Lastly, there are the Moria Orcs, flocking to Igash the Fanatic, a lieutenant to Mazog. Igash has collected wealth untold at his throne at the crest of the Grand Stair. I know not what he will do with this treasure, but I know there must be a way to lay claim to it all.
'When we are satisfied that the tasks set before you here at the Grand Stair are complete, I will send you back to Narfi at the Twenty-first Hall.'

'Though the Grand Stair still remains a pale reflection of its former glory, the threat posed by the Enemy here is diminished greatly. I do not think that they can effectively mount an offensive from this location.
'I will send word to Narfi that you have assisted us most well, ${PLAYER}. This duty will not go unrecognized.'
Assist Ossur with the trolls in the Grand Stair
Assist Ossur with the Fire-orcs in the Grand Stair
Assist Avar with the Moria Orcs in the Grand Stair
Assist Thithrand with the Warg-riders in the Grand Stair
Assist Thithrand with the White Hand Orcs in the Grand Stair
Talk to Avar at the Orc-watch
Steps of the Grand Stair

The Grand Stair once stood at the foot of a great cross-roads within Moria. At the height of the great city, it led to all areas of the halls and was a majestic wonder to behold. Now it has fallen to the care of Igash, a lieutenant of the Moria Orc-leader Mazog. Igash assembled the forces of Orcs and trolls within Moria in one place and has collected tribute from each to one day bring to the leader of the Orcs. For now, each tribe vies for favour from the lieutenant, a fanatical follower of Mazog.

'Once this place was a wonder to behold leading to all places within the realm of Khazad-dûm. Now it has fallen to such disrepair. This must be rectified, and your aid will be needed here.
'Assist Thithrand with the White Hand Orcs and the Warg-riders. Assist Ossur with the trolls and Fire-orcs of the deep. Assist me with forces loyal to Igash and Mazog.
'When you have completed these tasks, I will inform Narfi that the Grand Stair is no longer able to support the efforts of the Orcs against Lothlórien.'

Avar, Ossur, and Thithrand are at the Orc-watch.
Avar has asked you to complete the several tasks needed to reclaim the Grand Stair before he sends you back to Narfi at the Twenty-first Hall.

Avar is at the Orc-watch.
The dwarves of the Orc-watch are satisfied that the forces of the Orcs within the Grand Stair no longer pose a threat to Lothlórien.

'My scouts have sent me rumours of a foe named Mazog giving orders to the forces of evil in Moria. I would hazard a guess that they mean to make war to the east, burning through the forest as they go. This must not be allowed to take place... not while I draw breath, nor any of the dwarves here in Moria.
'Too long have we been exiled from this place, and too long will we suffer if the Elves are harmed because we were away. I have sent my brothers below to scout two locations in which we have seen greater numbers of Orcs.
'The first of them is at the Orc-watch, south-west from here. You will want to go there and speak with Avar, the eldest. My second brother is at Anazârmekhem and goes by the name of Pálmar. The youngest, Teitur, is also somewhere in Anazârmekhem. When you have done all that they ask, return to me.'

'There are few words more important to the dwarves than respect and honour. You have honour in abundance, ${PLAYER}, and have thus earned our utmost respect. Your tales will be sung in our annals, lest we forget the great service done for the dwarves and Elves in this difficult time.
'With this great duty fulfilled, I tell you that I am indebted to you greatly, as are all the free folk who dwell in these great halls.'
Complete Avar's tasks in the Grand Stair
Complete Pálmar's tasks in the Forges of Khazad-dûm
Complete Teitur's tasks within Fil Gashan
Talk to Narfi at the Twenty-first Hall
Enemies of Lothlórien

Orcs gather beneath several banners, but flock towards a single cause. This is disconcerting for the dwarves, and the intent of the war-host of Moria spurs the staunchest of Durin's Folk to action against the Orcs in the halls they have claimed for many years.

'You will find Avar first at the Orc-watch, south-west of the Twenty-first Hall. He watches over the gathered troops within the Grand Stair. Next, seek out Pálmar at Anazârmekhem; he watches the Orcs work tirelessly in the Forges of Khazad-dûm. Last, speak with Teitur at Anazârmekhem and ask him to inform you of Fil Gashan, where an Orc-general gathers an army and prepares his host for battle.
'Make haste, ${PLAYER}. There is no time to lose.'
'There walks a true and honourable hero! All hail ${PLAYER}!'

Narfi's brethren can be found at the Orc-Watch and Anazârmekhem, south-west of the Twenty-first Hall where Narfi holds his post.
Narfi has asked you to visit his brothers, Avar, Pálmar, and Teitur at the Orc-watch and Anazârmekhem and learn what assistance they need.

Narfi is at the Twenty-first Hall, north-east of the Orc-watch and Anazârmekhem.
After many difficult forays into the very heart of the Orc-strongholds of Moria, you have had decisive victories and thwarted the creatures' attempts to make a devastating blow upon the Elves of Lothlórien.
Defeated Skûm
Defeated Urauth

'You must be the ${RACE} that Falgir has been going on about. I suppose you do have the look of an adventurer, though you seem a little soft around the middle. Ha!
'He tells me you mean to enter the Forgotten Treasury to the south and south-east of the Deep Descent. If you do, I wanted to warn you about the troll-twins, Skûm and Urauth.
'They are quite alike in temperament, it is said. Some of our company have come across them at times, but few ever survive. Should you find yourself facing them, I will be greatly in your debt if you would deal with them once and for all. Our scouts last saw them in the area where the Forgotten Treasury was found, south and south-east of our location here in the Deep Descent.'

'This news brightens me with newfound hope. Still, I cannot forget all the pain that those two monsters have caused.
'You did well, though, ${PLAYER}. It appears that my hope was not misplaced at all.'
Defeat Skûm
Defeat Urauth
Return to Hafberg at the Deep Descent
Skûm and Urauth

Crystals have been discovered in Moria, bearing marks of the Forgotten Treasury, a sealed vault hiding a substantial amount of wealth. This discovery has piqued the interest of some dwarves who now wish to uncover the vault and save its contents from the pilfering Orcs.
'Have you met the twin trolls yet, friend?'
'The twin trolls are no more, thanks to you.'

Skûm and Urauth were last seen near the Forgotten Treasury, south and south-east of the Deep Descent in Moria.
Hafberg told you of the twin trolls, Skûm and Urauth, alike in every way, and how they terrorize the dwarves in the area. You were asked to defeat them should you find yourself facing them.

Hafberg is at the Deep Descent, north and north-west of the Forgotten Treasury.
After a long and difficult battle, you defeated the twin trolls to avenge the dwarves who fell to their cruelty.
You have reached the Western Gate of the Twenty-first Hall!

'You've been a great help to us, ${PLAYER}, and if you haven't been that way yet, you may want to head east to the Twenty-first hall and see our encampment there. The Twenty-first hall was one of the greatest halls in all of Moria in it's day, and will soon be so again if we are successful!
'The hall can be reached most directly by the road that leads east from here -- you can reach it by the passage that leads south-east out of the Chamber of the Cross-roads. It is a wide road built in a winding natural passage through the rock. Luck is with us, for it seems the goblins make little use of it, and the way is as safe as any down here... as long as we can keep watch on it at any rate.
'When you reach the hall, find Wárr and tell him how we are doing over here; he is the supervisor of the Twenty-first Hall expedition, and he'll be eager for news. He'll probably be in the Chamber of Mazarbul, just off the passage to the north of the Twenty-first Hall.'

'What's this, then? Líkmund sends word from the western halls of Durin's Way, does he? Good. I am happy enough to hear he still lives, for these are deadly halls.
'I suppose you're here to lend a hand, and not just to see the sights I suppose, though they are fine enough for any!'
Find the Western Gate of the Twenty-first Hall
The Winding Way
Wárr is most likely anxious for news of the rest of the dwarves from the expedition. A natural passage, great and winding, connects the Twenty-first Hall with the Chamber of the Cross-roads.
'You should let Wárr at the Twenty-first Hall know how our expedition fares.'

Wárr is in the Chamber of Mazarbul, just north of the Twenty-first Hall, far to the east of the Chamber of the Cross-roads.
You must travel east from the Chamber of the Cross-roads through the great winding road leading to the Twenty-first Hall.

Wárr is in the Chamber of Mazarbul, north of the Twenty-first Hall, far to the east of the Chamber of the Cross-roads.
Líkmund has asked you to speak with Wárr and relay what you know of recent events from the Chamber of the Cross-roads.

Winiel is in the Water-works in Moria.

'Lore-master ${PLAYER}, how good to see you. I trust I was not too difficult to find?
'I understand that you have come to a point in your studies that will require more aggressive research in order to better your skills. I believe I know just the thing to help you on your way.
'Come, let us speak further on how we can help each other.'

Winiel is in the Water-works in Moria.
You have been instructed to look for the lore-master Winiel.

'Well met, ${PLAYER}. I am at your service, and your family's. I have heard much praise of your deeds in Moria, and I will gladly share anything I have to teach with such a noble Guardian as yourself. The time is nigh for the dwarves to reclaim their ancient home of Moria, and your aid has been invaluable.
'I see that you are here because your strength as a Guardian has outgrown your skills somewhat. I believe I can teach you a skill that will serve you well into the future.
'Let us speak further of how you can contribute to our cause here in Moria, for there is much to do.'

'By all accounts, Valthor was last seen at the Foundations of Stone in Moria.'

'Why hullo there! If you are looking for Pada, you have found him! So stand up straight and let me have a look at you, ${RACE}.
'What have we here? You certainly have a sincere look to you, and a sort of kindness in your expression. Yet you are worn with travel and toil, and sadness too. I think I know why you are here.
'Come, let us talk for a while. I can see that you are also a Minstrel of great skill, nay, not by your instrument, but by the very look of you! Did you not know that Minstrels shine with a subtle radiance? Yet we bow under the heavy burden we carry, for we give our hearts that others may endure.'

Pada has travelled to Moria to lend his aid to the dwarf-expedition that has gone to excavate the mines.

'Well met, Warden ${PLAYER}. No doubt you have come here to learn from my own experiences defending home and country from the forces of the Enemy.
'I will be glad to show you what I know; but first we must act together to quell the forces of the Enemy here in Moria.
'Let us speak further and see how we can help one another.'

Sadreda is at the Foundations of Stone in Moria.
You have been directed to speak with the great warden Sadreda.

'If you are looking for more work in the area of the Great Wheel, I would suggest you find Foreman Indrith. He headed down there some time ago, and rumour has it that he is holed up there. Apparently, the fungus was not reason enough for him to abandon his charge.
'He may require your assistance. He'll probably be within the Wheel-house, beneath the Great Wheel.'

'Ansurr sent you to aid me? You must be hearty to have made it through the creatures and the fungus. That is good to know, for I have work to do here, and if you are willing to labour hard, I am willing to set you to work.'
Talk to Foreman Indrith in the Wheel-house
Foreman of the Great Wheel
Foreman Indrith made his way into the Wheel-house within the Great Wheel of the Water-works. The dwarves of Hulwul-nefekh are concerned that he may need help there.
'You may find Foreman Indrith in the Wheel-house, beneath the Great Wheel, south-west of Hulwul-nefekh.'

Foreman Indrith is in the Wheel-house, beneath the Great Wheel, south-west of Hulwul-nefekh.
Ansurr suggested to seek out Foreman Indrith and aid him however you may.
Collected the gear

'If we sheared a gear, and I believe that we did, we need to get a new one. During my time in the Great Wheel, I have explored many of the tunnels that feed these wheels.
'On one of my journeys, I spotted a gear in a room beside the tunnels. However, I thought nothing of it, and left it where it lay. I believe you will need to recover this gear before our work can continue.
'You can make your way deeper into the Great Wheel from The Drowned Deeps or through the gate across the way. Hurry!'

'You have the gear? Wonderful!
'While you were gone, I heard the rumble of something great moving amid the Water-works. Whether our wheels begin to churn once more or some other force lurks nearby, I do not know....
'Maybe a little caution would not hurt, after all....'
Find a new gear in the tunnels of the Great Wheel
A New Gear
The Water-works is a site of importance to the dwarves who wish to remain in Moria. Once such dwarf, Foreman Indrith, has made it a mission to repair the channel there.
'Search the tunnels of the Great Wheel. I saw a gear lying about on one of my journeys... perhaps it still remains.'

Foreman Indrith believes that you sheared a gear while trying to force the wheel housing in the Great Wheel to start turning once more. He believes another gear is located in the tunnels of the Great Wheel.
Foreman Indrith is in the Wheel-house, beneath the Great Wheel, south-west of Hulwul-nefekh.
You flexed your arm for Foreman Indrith
Wait for Foreman Indrith to turn the wheel

'With the number of toads and lizards reduced, we should get a better idea of what is clogging up the works. It is going to take some time to clean out the pipes, though.
'Well, that can wait for later. I have another task that I will need your help with. Of course, I first need to see if you are strong enough to help me.
'Roll up your sleeves and let me see how much muscle you have there.'
'Well, I have seen greater sinews on a chicken, but you will have to do. Come along, ${PLAYER}, let us see if we can get this wheel to move.'
'That was not right. I think that we sheared a gear, and our work cannot continue until we have a new one. Lucky for us, I believe I know where we can find one....'
Show Foreman Indrith how strong you are by <rgb=#FF0000>flex</rgb>ing
Step to the Wheel to aid Foreman Indrith

The Water-works is a site of importance to the dwarves who wish to remain in Moria. Once such dwarf, Foreman Indrith, has made it a mission to repair the channel there.
'Come now, do not shy away from this. A simple <rgb=#FF0000>flex</rgb> is all I need to know if you are strong enough to help me.'

Foreman Indrith is in the Wheel-house, beneath the Great Wheel.
Foreman Indrith wants to make certain that you are strong enough to assist him with turning the wheel. Perhaps you should <rgb=#FF0000>flex</rgb> for him.

Foreman Indrith is in the Wheel-house, beneath the Great Wheel.
Foreman Indrith has asked you to help turn the wheel.

After showing the foreman that you were strong enough, of which he was dubious, the two of you attempted to turn the wheel behind him. A terrible noise was heard, and the foreman looked baffled.
Defeated the Watcher in the Water

'We have found the location of the Watcher in the Water, the beast we faced outside of Moria... and a terrible foe indeed.
'The dread it causes shakes the foundation of the strongest willed warriors and only through the great power of the light shall it be overcome completely, it appears. Beyond those doors, it is clear that there is a great foe of Durin's Folk, and only those with the stoutest hearts and strongest resolve should enter.
'You will not face this foe with only a few allies. You must go in force, and you must all be prepared for the worst. Enter the Vile Maw, and if you survive, return to me.'

'Defeated? Defeated! Ha! All hail you, Hero of Khazad-dûm! All hail the heroes who defeated the fiend.
'The Watcher is defeated and shall stir no more! There are cheers to be cheered and songs to be sung bearing your name, ${PLAYER}.
'A happier day in this dwarf's life has not yet been seen!'
Defeat the Watcher in the Water
Talk to Kaldi outside of the Vile Maw
A Final Foray

The Water-works is a site of importance to the dwarves who wish to remain in Moria. One such dwarf, Foreman Indrith, has made it a mission to repair the channel there. His tasks for you led to the discovery of the Watcher in the Water.
'I wish you well in your foray against the Watcher in the Water.'

The Watcher in the Water lairs within the Vile Maw.
Kaldi warned you that the foe within the Vile Maw was one that would drag the very hearts of those near it towards oblivion without the great power of light on their side. Be cautious and take two fellowships of your staunchest allies.

'While walking along the water's edge, I noticed ooze filtering out of the stone near the water where the drains would push the run-off from within. I came running back here and have not gone near the water since.
'You seem an adventurous sort. Perhaps you would care to take a sample of the water near the edge for me. You will not have to travel far... anywhere to the north-east of here should suffice.'

'Rumours abound that you are of a tougher mould than most, ${CLASS}. I will admit that you look doughty enough, and your eyes are fiercer than many I see. Perhaps you would hold up against a most difficult foe that threatens our cause.
'We know that Igash sits at the top of the Grand Stair, collecting tribute from the other tribes of Moria Orcs. The White-hand Orcs, however, seem to give him no loyalty whatsoever.
'And yet, merely to confront Igash will be but a pittance to so mighty a ${CLASS} as yourself. If you can defeat him without harming the other Orc leaders except those of the White Hand, you will truly earn my respect. You cannot slay the Devoted, either. I would advise you to bring such friends as you can trust for this venture.'

'I am tremendously impressed! You have done credit to your fame, great credit indeed. Something troubles me still, though. By your description of this foe, it sounds to me like evil will not be held at bay for long in the Grand Stair.
'Do you think Igash is gone forever? You saw him bested, I know, but my heart tells me that he will be back before long. A creature so twisted and wicked does not often fall after one defeat. Mark my words -- there will be trouble again soon....'
Return to Sigurd at the Twenty-first Hall
Do not kill the Devoted
Do not kill Gothgaash
Do not kill Glothrok
Do not kill the Beast
The Grand Stair - Igash Unleashed

Once a great and beautiful cross-roads of Moria, the Grand Stair is a vile haven of many of the gathered tribes of Orcs. Igash, regarded as a leader by all of the varied groups, gathers tribute from every tribe to give to Mazog, the mightiest and greatest of Orcs in Khazad-dûm. The dwarves wish to unseat Igash's Orcs from this Grand Stair and stop Mazog from receiving valuable and unsavoury gifts.
'Igash is one of Mazog's most terrible captains... he must be defeated with due haste!'

Many tribes of Orcs prowl the Grand Stair, south-east of the Twenty-first Hall.
Geirr has asked you to defeat Igash in the Grand Stair without defeating any other members of the Moria Orc tribes. In doing so, you will assist in efforts to reclaim that cross-roads for the dwarves, and prove your great worth to Sigurd.

The dwarf Sigurd can be found in the Twenty-first Hall, north-west of the Grand Stair.
You have defeated Igash without defeating any other members of the Moria Orc tribes; Sigurd is waiting to hear of your foray.
The Lost One has been defeated
One of the Fungal-workers was killed

'Rumours abound that you are of a tougher mould than most, ${CLASS}. I will admit that you look doughty enough, and your eyes are fiercer than many I see. Perhaps you would hold up against a most difficult foe that threatens our cause.
'Beneath the Sixteenth Hall there is a terrible beast known as the Lost One. It summons wretched gredbyg to its aid when it attacks, and they can be quite the hindrance to any that oppose their master. To defeat the Lost One after the threat of gredbyg has been removed would be but a pittance to so mighty a one as yourself.
'Nay, to earn my respect and rise to the challenge I give you, you will take down the Lost One without hurting the gredbyg, however much they harry you. I would advise you to bring friends on this venture if you wish to return in victory.'

'I am tremendously impressed! You have done credit to your fame, great credit indeed. Something troubles me still, though. By your description of this foe, it sounds to me like evil will not be held at bay for long in the Sixteenth Hall.
'Do you think the Lost One is gone forever? You saw him bested, I know, but my heart tells me that he will be back before long. A creature so fey does not often fall after one defeat. Mark my words -- there will be trouble again soon....'
Defeat the Lost One
Return to Sigurd at the Twenty-first Hall
Do not kill the Fungal-workers
Sixteenth Hall -- Do No Harm

In the Sixteenth Hall, defilers and other Orcs, sworn to some dark power, poison their brethren with a fungal disease. The source of this evil lies far beneath the surface of this stronghold, once inhabited by the dwarves. The dwarves in Moria wish only to drive the Orcs and the evil of the Sixteenth Hall away from their former realm.
'Have you defeated the Lost One as I asked? It is a challenge, to be sure, but one that must be faced!'

The Lost One is below the Sixteenth Hall, south-east of the Twenty-first Hall.
You have been challenged to prove your great worth by defeating the Lost One without making the battle easier by killing his summoned gredbyg.

The dwarf Sigurd can be found in the Twenty-first Hall, north-west of the Sixteenth Hall.
Sigurd will be very impressed to hear that you met his challenge of defeating the Lost One while the gredbyg harried your efforts all the while.
Defeated enemies in the Dark Delvings (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Word of your renown has spread far and wide throughout these long tunnels, ${CLASS}. Aye, don't be modest -- I can see in your eyes the bright look of a valiant adventurer. I would know your ilk even without reinforcement from the rumours.
'Are you up for a small challenge? South-east of this hall lies the Dark Delvings, a terrifying place that none dare approach. A nameless malice is there, brooding in the dark, corrupt, evil, and wretched. Many footsteps and strange sounds echo from the Delvings. I think you know of what I speak. You have seen the Nameless foes, have you not?
'An adventurer such as yourself would look forward to a little dare such as the one I am about to propose: go into the Dark Delvings and slay many enemies there. Fear will not keep you from a place that all others shun. I would have the Nameless destroyed, for it would be a terrible thing if they were to spread into the mines.'

'I must be honest: I was not sure that you would be up for this challenge today. But I am glad to have been wrong on this occasion! Forgive me for not thinking better of you, ${PLAYER}, for the rumours of your courage were more than true.
'Here is a token of my appreciation. I hope to see more of you in the following days, for you are quite the asset to our endeavours here.'
Defeat enemies in the Dark Delvings (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Return to Geirr at the Twenty-first Hall
Dark Delvings -- Illuminate the Dark

In the Dark Delvings, the most forsaken depths of Khazad-dûm, the Nameless hold sway over the bitter shadows. Like other creatures that hide in the Black Pit that is Moria, the Nameless dread light, but they will not turn aside from any opportunity to spread corruption and dismay. These terrible foes must be purged from the Dark Delvings before they are able to wend their way into other parts of the mines.
'I do not know what the creatures are that infest the Dark Delvings, but they are a threat to us all.'

The Dark Delvings are far to the south-east of the Twenty-first Hall.
The dwarf Geirr has challenged you to make your way into the Dark Delvings and defeat many Nameless foes therein.

The dwarf Geirr is in the Twenty-first hall, north-west of the Great Delvings where the Nameless roam.
Geirr will wish to hear if you have been brave enough to enter the Dark Delvings and face the Nameless ones in battle.
Enemy slain (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

The Forges of Khazad-dûm, once a glorious smith-hall for the dwarves of Moria, have fallen into evil hands. The Forges now serve the Orc masters of Moria and are used to build all manner of weapons and war-machines for an assault against fair Lothlórien. Brogur and Bósi's dwarves, wishing to reclaim Moria, aim to prevent this at any cost, for they would see the Elves and dwarves reinstate old alliances for the good of both.
'The Orcs have defiled our ancient Forge...they must not be allowed to continue!'

The Forges of Khazad-dûm are far to the south-west of the Twenty-first Hall.
The dwarf Geirr has challenged you to make your way into the Forges of Khazad-dûm and defeat many Orcs therein.

The dwarf Geirr is in the Twenty-first hall, north-east of the Forges where the Orcs hold their camp.
Geirr will wish to hear if you have been brave enough to enter the Forges of Khazad-dûm and face the Orcs in battle.

'Word of your renown has spread far and wide throughout these long tunnels, ${CLASS}. Aye, don't be modest -- I can see in your eyes the bright look of a valiant adventurer. I would know your ilk even without reinforcement from the rumours.
'Are you up for a small challenge? South-east of the Twenty-first Hall looms Skûmfil, the foulest of halls in Moria. Orcs pile their dead within, leaving them to fester, and the vilest of creatures have flocked there to feast upon the waste.
'An adventurer such as yourself would look forward to a little dare such as the one I am about to propose: travel to Skûmfil and defeat as many of the foul creatures as you can. The more kergrim and gredbyg you can destroy, the safer Moria will be.'

Return to Geirr at the Twenty-first Hall
Skûmfil -- Clearing Corpses

No living Man, Elf, halfling, or dwarf will want to set foot in Skûmfil, grave of the Orcs, feeding and breeding ground of vile kergrim and slavering gredbyg. There the Orcs pile their dead, and there disgusting creatures feast on rotten waste.
'Clear away the kergrim and gredbyg from Skûmfil... those creatures only grow stronger off the corpses of the Orcs.'

Kergrim and gredbyg grow strong and wicked among the Orc-corpses of Skûmfil, south-east of the Twenty-first Hall.
Geirr has challenged you to defeat many of the vile creatures that lurk in Skûmfil as proof of your worth as a warrior. Few are wilful enough to withstand the reek of that horrific place.

Geirr awaits tidings at the Twenty-first Hall, north-west of Skûmfil.
You have defeated many kergrim and gredbyg in vile Skûmfil, and should now return to show Geirr that you are indeed as valiant as rumours have described. He will be glad to learn that you have proven yourself against the vile threat in the halls of the corpses.
Defeated Bonetooth
Defeated Old Gnawer

'Kergrim are disgusting creatures, feeding off the rotting flesh of the dead. I think it should be one's duty to destroy them. Nothing good can come of such behaviour.
'Look for Bonetooth and Old Gnawer, both kergrim. Find them and slay them so they can no longer perform their vile acts upon the dead.
'You will find them in Skûmfil to the south-east of the Shadowed Refuge.'

'It is good to know that we will no longer need to fear the likes of such creatures. Would that we should never need to do battle against such terrible foes again.
'Alas, that is not our lot. Still, you have done good work this day, ${PLAYER}. I thank you and will inform Throstur of your efforts.'
Defeat Bonetooth
Defeat Old Gnawer
Talk to Odmar at the Shadowed Refuge

Skûmfil is nothing more than a dumping ground, a place where the fallen Orcs of Moria are discarded when they begin to reek. It is here that two foes have gathered, each intent on using the corpses found therein for their own purposes. The kergrim and other scavengers as a source of food, and the insects as a place to lay their eggs to spawn future generations.

'I do not know how these beasts found their way within Skûmfil, but I think that we should be pleased to know that it will be our task to remove them. Head to the south-east and enter Skûmfil. Find the two kergrim, Bonetooth and Old Gnawer. Defeat them, then return to me.'

Bonetooth and Old Gnawer are within Skûmfil, south-east of the Shadowed Refuge.
Odmar wants you to put an end to the kergrim-leaders who brought the corpse-eating creatures through the tunnels of Moria to Skûmfil.

Odmar is at the Shadowed Refuge, north-west of Skûmfil.
You found the two kergrim, one ancient and the other a summoner, and destroyed them both. Odmar, at the Shadowed Refuge will be pleased to know that this is done.

'It falls to me to oversee the slaughter of the leaders of this disgusting encampment. The Sixteenth Hall was once used as housing and storage for the Dwarves of Moria, but now it is an infestation of Orcs!
'Well, I aim to put a stop to this problem. Enter the Sixteenth Hall, north-east of here, and remove the taint of the guardians, curse-shouters, and those especially dreadful Orcs that explode into spores when they draw near.
'Do these things, and then return to me when you are done, for I should like to count the notches on your weapon. This gloom on me will ease when I see evidence of the Orcs' downfall.'
'Your weapon is handsomer after this deed, is it not? See how it glows with pride! I will inform Mallas that you have done as I asked. You have the thanks and goodwill of the dwarves, my friend.'
Return to Odmar at the Shadowed Refuge
Leaders of the Hosts

The Sixteenth Hall is an area overrun with Orcs, many of whom suffer from a terrible illness that causes fungus-like growths on their bodies.
Mallas, an Elf ally to the dwarves, believes that there is something secret beneath the Sixteenth Hall and wishes to learn the true purpose and source of the plague.

'The filthy creatures deserve the disease that plagues them, but I will not sit by and abide their presence in our mines any longer. Get into the Sixteenth Hall and see that the clean-up effort is begun.'

Guardians, curse-shouters, and fungal Orc bombs can be found in the Sixteenth Hall, north-east of the Shadowed Refuge.
Odmar sent you to find and destroy the Orcs that he believes are leading this diseased incursion into the Sixteenth Hall.

Odmar is in the Shadowed Refuge, south-west of the Sixteenth Hall.
You fought valiantly against the infected Orcs of the Sixteenth Hall and defeated many guardians, curse-shouters and the Orcs bearing terrible fungus. You should now tell Odmar that you did as he bade.
Defeated glow-worms in the Dark Delving (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'More dreamscapes from my nightmares. I have seen the glow of the worms, the tendrils looking like gleaming diamonds dropping from the heavens.
'They are never diamonds, only worms, descending now to swallow my head choking my breath and ending my life. I awake from these nightmares without breath and sweating.
'Will you help me end these nightmares, end the terror? Kill the glow-worms in the Dark Delvings. You will find the Dark Delvings far to the south-east from our location here at the Shadowed Refuge. Kill them and return to me.'

'Sleep. I hope to sleep, but the gloom in this place darkens my dreams still. I hope that there will come a time when light returns here, and radiance once again holds sway.
'For now, I take solace in what you have done for me and will see that Gelirwen is informed that you served me well. Thank you, ${PLAYER}.'
Defeat glow-worms in the Dark Delving (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Return to Ymar at the Shadowed Refuge
A Fell Glow

In the deepest dark of Moria there is a place where the only light that shone emanated from dwarf-lamps and luminescant fungus. Now, these delvings are dim and darker than ever and home to creatures that exist in nightmares. Yet here they are, and Veúlfur's agents sent to the Shadowed Refuge draw little comfort in knowing that there is something within the Dark Delvings that commands the Orcs to poison themselves in a manner that gives them over to some greater will.

'If I knew the worms were dead, I might better rest even in the belly of Khazad-dûm, so dark and deep. Please breach the Dark Delvings to the south-east of the Shadowed Refuge and kill the glow-worms there.'

The Dark Delvings lie far to the south-east of the Shadowed Refuge.
Ymar's nightmares continue, and he needs you to help him rid them from his mind. He asked you to breach the Dark Delvings and kill the glow-worms there to set his mind at ease.

Ymar is at the Shadowed Refuge, far to the north-west of the Dark Delvings.
You found the glow-worms within the Dark Delvings and defeated them as Ymar had asked.

'The kergrim are foul creatures, consuming the dead for sustenance. How and why they found their way into Khazad-dûm, I do not know, but they are here, and something must be done about them.
'Odmar, Ymar, and Glorelloth each have tasks associated with the kergrim in Skûmfil that they may be willing to share with you. If you complete these, I will inform Veúlfur that you have done all I asked at Skûmfil.
'You can find the three of them within the bounds of the Shadowed Refuge here.'

'Your work here is complete in my eyes, ${PLAYER}. I will send word on to Veúlfur and inform him that you have satisfied my needs here at the Shadowed Refuge.
'You have my thanks.'
Help Ymar to control disease in Skûmfil
Help Odmar defeat the kergrim-leaders of Skûmfil
Help Glorelloth collect samples in Skûmfil

Throstur is at the Shadowed Refuge.
You completed each task assigned by Ymar, Odmar and Glorelloth within Skûmfil and should now return to Throstur.

'We must rid the place of these carriers, in order to help purge the disease. You must go to Skûmfil, south-east of the Shadowed Refuge, and rid the place of these disease carriers.'

'I will tell Throstur of your efforts. He will be pleased that this is done.
'I thank you, friend. I thank you.'

'The kergrim are rife with disease, this much is true, but I am not certain that they are behind the plague affecting the Orcs. However, it is possible that they are, and so I ask that you collect samples from the kergrim and their ilk within Skûmfil.
'You will find the place south-east from the Shadowed Refuge. Take small strips of their hide and return it to me so that I might better determine if the kergrim are infested with the same kind of illness that plagues the Orcs.'

'It will take some time to examine these samples and determine whether the plague is the same or different than that borne by the kergrim. I will also inform Throstur that you have done as I asked.
'Thank you, friend.'

'Collect strips of flesh from the kergrim and return them to me. You will find the kergrim within Skûmfil to the south-east of the Shadowed Refuge. The place is filled with corpses of dead Orcs, but if the disease is alive in the kergrim, then perhaps the Orcs are contracting the disease as they bring the bodies to the pit.'

'So that is what I want done. Go to Skûmfil and kill the gredbyg there. There are many of the things, and each and every one of them needs to be destroyed.
'It may seem a bit brash, perhaps, but insects should never grow this large. Skûmfil can be found south-east of the Shadowed Refuge.'

'Glad to know that you met with good success. This proves that you are a decent warrior indeed.

Talk to Lar at the Shadowed Refuge
A Beneficial Poison

Skûmfil is nothing more than a dumping ground, a place where the fallen Orcs of Moria are discarded when they begin to reek. It is here that two foes have gathered, each intent on using the corpses found therein for their own purposes. The kergrim and other scavengers as a source of food, and the insects as a place to lay their eggs to spawn future generations.

'If there are too many of those gredbyg, everything in Moria will be overrun. We cannot risk the gredbyg carrying disease or becoming such a numerous menace that they replace the Orcs once we drive them out of Khazad-dûm. We must kill as many as we can now.
'Go to Skûmfil south-east of the Shadowed Refuge and deafeat the gredbyg there.'

Skûmfil lies to the south-east of the Shadowed Refuge.
Lar wants to see the gredbyg within the depths of Skûmfil defeated. The insects are trying to breed in the bodies dumped by the Orcs within Skûmfil, and if left unchecked, they could breed too quickly to control. Lar also wonders if they might be the source of the plague affecting the Orcs.

Lar is at the Shadowed Refuge, north-west of Skûmfil.
You fought against numerous and varied gredbyg within Skûmfil and now must return to the Shadowed Refuge to inform Lar of your success.
You have slain The Lost One

'The Sixteenth Hall is a vile place, ${CLASS}. The Orcs there bear a terrible disease, but there is something more that troubles me.
'My intuition is excellent, mind you, or else I would not be troubling you with my guesswork. I have been watching the enemy closely from my watch; based on their behaviour, I would venture that something lies hidden away yonder.
'Delve as deeply as you dare into the Sixteenth Hall and discover their secret! Worry not; I do not think this will be a fool's errand. You can find the hall by making your way north-east from the Shadowed Refuge.'

'There is no name for a horror such as that, but my feeling of foreboding has passed now that you say it is gone. I can breathe a little easier now.
'I will tell Mallas of your great deed, ${PLAYER}.'
Find and eliminate the source of Lar's worry
Retrurn to Lar at the Shadowed Refuge
The Secret Beneath

The Sixteenth Hall is an area overrun with Orcs, many of whom suffer from a terrible illness that causes fungus-like growths on their bodies.
Mallas, an Elf ally to the dwarves, believes that there is something secret beneath the Sixteenth Hall and wishes to learn the true purpose and source of the plague.

'Though I send you into grave danger, I cannot tell you much more of this errand, for I do not know myself. I hope you will trust me in this: all the signs indicate that there is something of significance to be discovered in the Sixteenth Hall.

The Sixteenth Hall lies to the north-east of the Shadowed Refuge.
Lar has asked you to delve deep into the Sixteenth Hall and see if you can locate the source of his unease.

Lar can be found in the Shadowed Refuge, south-west of the Sixteenth Hall.
You should return to Lar and tell him what you discovered and slew: a terrible headless creature in the depths of the hall, lurking in a room full of spores and slime.
Defeated Uammaethor
Defeated Nestaduan

Defeated Ulugon

'These gredbyg have no thought of their own, that is what I think. I know that there is a big insect in Skûmfil, and wherever you find that, you are sure to find what is in control.
'There are other gredbyg though, smaller ones that have a bit of independence; those are the nasty ones that I think we need to eliminate. So that is the task I will give to you.
'If you are willing to help me, you should make your way toward Skûmfil located to the south-east of the Shadowed Refuge. You will find the warrior-caste gredbyg there. Kill Ummaethor, a larger warrior, and its guards, then return to me here at the Shadowed Refuge.'

'Excellent work, I shall inform my superior that you performed your task admirably and completely.
'You have my thanks.'

It is here that two foes have gathered, each intent on using the corpses found therein for their own purposes. The kergrim and other scavengers as a source of food, and the insects as a place to lay their eggs to spawn future generations.

'The gredbyg within Skûmfil mean to breed in the corpses of the fallen. We must stop this, but more, we must stop their warriors. Find the warrior called Uammaethor and slay it within Skûmfil. You can find it south-east from the Shadowed Refuge where we now speak.'

Defeat snarling overseers in the Dark Delvings (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeated Dark-maw masters in the Dark Delving (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeated dark world-eaters in the Dark Delving (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'The nameless creatures of the dark are a blight on Khazad-dûm and must be destroyed. I ask you to go to the Dark delvings far to the south-east of our location here at the Shadowed Refuge and destroy the evil creatures that dwell there.
'We cannot suffer their existence when it is within our means to rid them from the world. The dwarves built lamps in the Dark Delvings long ago to keep the nameless horrors at bay...they may still exist, but some of these Nameless seem to have overcome the wards.
'Please, go there and clear away the evil things.'

'Aye, there is something of honour in this place yet. You have proven it thus.
'I will tell Gelirwen that you have done what I asked, and you will be well-respected always by myself and my brethren.'
Defeat howling overseers in the Dark Delvings (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeat snarling overseers in the Dark Delvings (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeat Dark-maw masters in the Dark Delving (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeated dark world-eaters in the Dark Delving (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Moggi at the Shadowed Refuge
The Things in the Dark

In the deepest dark of Moria there is a place where the only light that shone emanated from dwarf-lamps and luminescant fungus. Now, these delvings are dim and darker than ever and home to creatures that exist in nightmares. Yet here they are, and Veúlfur's agents sent to the Shadowed Refuge draw little comfort in knowing that there is something within the Dark Delvings that commands the Orcs to poison themselves in a manner that gives them over to some greater will.

'Use the lamps as you can, but I do not think that all the Nameless there will be driven away. Do not fight them in the dark as that is their home and their strength will grow.
'Defeat these nameless horrors in the Dark Delvings, far to the south-east of the Shadowed Refuge, then return to me.'

The Dark Delvings lie far to the south-east of the Shadowed Refuge.
Moggi made mention of lamps placed in the Dark Delvings by the dwarves and how they may drive back some of the Nameless, but he thinks that there are others who are unafraid of such Light. Use caution as you fulfill this task.

Moggi is at the Shadowed Refuge, far to the north-west of the Dark Delving.
You fought your way into the Dark Delving and there defeated many of the nameless horrors. You should now return to the Shadowed Refuge and inform Moggi of your success.

'Greetings, I have expected your arrival since first I saw the others in the Shadowed Refuge speaking with you. You show little fear of this place, but the right amount of respect to know that nothing here is safe. I also see that you do not let the gloom affect your heart, and this brings a smile to my face.
'I am here at the behest of Veúlfur, who is posted at the Twenty-first Hall, and I have been watching as you seek to discover the secret of the plague carried by the Orcs. I too am after this secret.
'There are four others here whom I have asked to assist me. I would ask that you entreat with them, here in the Shadowed Refuge before making your way into the Dark Delvings to discover what secrets they may hold. Ymar, Moggi, Pentlenn, and Glorelloth will all require your aid. Please, speak with them.'

'I will send word to Veúlfur and share with you great knowledge, given me by those you aided.
'The Gurvand you faced in the Dark Delvings was not the architect of this plague. Nay, it was the work of another, and we still do not know the identity of this creature. Its malevolence knows no bounds, and we shall need to remain vigilant here for signs that it might be rising ever closer to the surface.
'You have our thanks for aiding in this discovery.'
Help Ymar rid the Dark Delvings of the glowing worms
Help Moggi rid the Dark Delvings of the terrible things in the dark
Recover the runes from the Dark Delvings for Pentlenn
Discover the secret of the Dark Delvings for Glorelloth

Now, these delvings are dim and darker than ever and home to creatures that exist in nightmares. 'Speak with Ymar, Moggi, Pentlenn, and Glorelloth ask them what must be done within the Dark Delvings. Once you have finished their tasks, I will send word to Veúlfur of all the aid you have rendered to us here in the Shadowed Refuge.'

'In the darkness, nameless things watch us. I have seen them, but with light we can defend ourselves. I have seen savagery in my time, but these Nameless do not turn back from the light. I think this is because the lamps once filled with the power of light are diminished.
'I wish for you to enter the Dark Delvings and collect up the shattered and fractured runes found within, return them to me, and I will see if I can repair them.
'You will find the Dark Delvings far to the south-east of the Shadowed Refuge.'
'I will begin my efforts to restore these runes immediately. I thank you for all that you have done, ${PLAYER}.'
'The Dark Delvings are far to the south-east of the Shadowed Refuge. Please, enter that place and find the fractured and shattered runes from within the halls and return them to me.'

In the deepest dark of Moria there is a place where the only light that shone emanated from dwarf-lamps and luminescent fungus. Now, these delvings are dim and darker than ever and home to creatures that exist in nightmares. Yet here they are, and Veúlfur's agents sent to the Shadowed Refuge draw little comfort in knowing that there is something within the Dark Delvings that commands the Orcs to poison themselves in a manner that gives them over to some greater will.

'Gelirwen asked me to discern what manner of fiend dwells deep within the Dark Delvings, but I have yet to understand the true horror within that hold. I know that there is great evil there, a nameless thing unaffected by the power of light. Radiance is rebuffed by the strength of its corruption. I know only that something there is evil beyond my understanding.
'So I caution you, ${RACE}, that when you enter the Dark Delvings you must be prepared for something as ancient as the Elves, savage and terrible.
'Discover what evil dwells there and return to me here at the Shadowed Refuge.'

'Such an evil can not be loosed upon the world. You have done well to drive it back into the darkness, though I do not think that an evil so great is so easily disposed.
'I have hope within my heart that it is gone and know that you speak no lies to me now. The Gurvand is defeated -- at least for now -- and I will inform Gelirwen of your efforts.
'Thank you, ${PLAYER}.'

In the deepest dark of Moria there is a place where the only light that shone emanated from dwarf-lamps and luminescant fungus. Yet here they are, and Veúlfur's agents sent to the Shadowed Refuge draw little comfort in knowing that there is something within the Dark Delvings that commands the Orcs to poison themselves in a manner that gives them over to some greater will.

'The nameless things within that place will not shy from the radiance in your hearts. In fact, I think that the dark shall strengthen them. While this is true, they may lose their strength in the light so be wise in your approach.
'Seek the source of evil within the Dark Delvings and return to me once you have dealt with it.'

'I will take time to study these and determine if there is a threat to be found here. I will tell Mallas of your efforts.

'In the Sixteenth Hall lie many evils; we thought that Orcs were the greatest. Yet recently I saw from my watch some growths of fungus spattered throughout the hall.
'I hail from the woods, and lichens do not generally make me afraid, but these fungi did so. Indeed, my skin crawls when I remember them. There was something terrible about those growths.
'I yearned to go back and study these things, but there is so much else to do ere I will have time, and I do not wish to put this off. I ask you to enter the Sixteenth Hall in my stead. Go to the north-east of the Shadowed Refuge and collect samples of this fungus for me. When you bring them back, I should be able to discern what ills can be derived from this new silent foe.'

'I am not familiar with this species. It bears no semblance to any fungus I have seen in all my long years.
'I will need to take more time to study this, but I consider your service complete, for you have done exactly as I bid. You have my thanks.'
'You will need to search the Sixteenth Hall for the fungus of which I spoke. You can find the Sixteenth Hall north-east of the encampment here in the Shadowed Refuge.'

In order to further your skills as a hunter, you have been instructed to seek out Armbeald in the Redhorn Lodes of Moria.

'Well met, friend Hunter. You have sought me and here I am, so what would you ask of me after coming all this way? I see that you wish to find more than a mere shooting-trick today.
'There comes a time in all our lives when standard skills of the trade simply won't suffice, and we must go deeper. Is this why you have sought me, greatest hunter and trapper in the lands from whence I hail?
'Perhaps I can help you. If you pass the test, I will teach you everything I can, for you will indeed be worthy of learning if you can overcome the challenges you have in store. Come, let us speak further.'

Armbeald is at the Orc-Watch in the north-west region of the Redhorn Lodes of Moria.
You should find Armbeald, a renowned hunter who should be able to assist you with further advancement at a high level of skill.

Defeated lizards in the Water-works (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Well now, you can see that this place is in a state unfitting for a dwarf like myself: too many leaks and not enough production. Add to that all the toads and lizards skittering about and... well, I am sure you understand what I mean.
'I suspect that the toads and lizards are being pulled along with the currents and getting stuck in the pipes, gumming them up.
'Do me a favour and thin out their number here and in the Water-works surrounding the Great Wheel, then return to me. We will see if we can get these pipes working as they should.'
'Good, good. We can now see if the Great Wheel is ready to turn on its own once more, then set about fixing these leaks.'

Defeat lizards in the Water-works (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

The Water-works is a site of importance to the dwarves who wish to remain in Moria. One such dwarf, Foreman Indrith, has made it a mission to repair the channel there.

'We have to clear the pipes first, then we can think about getting the Water-works up and running. I already sent a dwarf ahead to examine the workings, but we must keep our attention here for the time being.
'Do your best to rid the area of lizards and toads, and when you think you killed enough, return to me, and we will see if we can get the wheels working correctly again.'

Toads and lizards can be found within the Water-works surrounding the Great Wheel.
Foreman Indrith believes that the toads and lizards may be clogging the piping of the Water-works.

You cleared a good many toads and lizards out from the Water-works surrounding the Great Wheel and should now return to Foreman Indrith to inform him of your work.

'Troubles abound in Ered Luin, but this not the least. Rumours abound of an ancient spider, Gaelnath, that has come into the possession of a particularly important dwarf-make rune-stone.
'If you are up to the challenge, head back into the Foundations of Stone and look for Tunzelgund along the northern edge of its central region. To the north of Tunzelgund you will find Gaelnath.
'I want you to get this rune-stone and take it back to Márus. He will know what to do with it.'

'What is that you have there, ${PLAYER}? Amazing! This is an ancient Rune of Restoration.'
Márus frowns as he looks over the rune-stone.
'It would seem that this stone has seen too much foul corruption in the dark of Khazad-dûm. We will have to do what we can to restore it to its former power.'
'What did Dwalin want of you, ${PLAYER}?'

'I am glad you are here, ${PLAYER}; well met, indeed! For I'm Celofa, Mistress of Riddles. How I love riddling! I can see by the twinkle in your eye that you know just how I feel on this matter.
'I shall be happy to trade some riddlish skill with you, but first I have a more mundane task. Complete it, and the riddling will begin!
'There's a nasty Orc, Bidroi, down in the Eastern Deeps. He doesn't like riddles, that one. I seem to have upset him when I told him a terribly befuddling one, and he was so confused that he fell right down a set of stairs into a great hole, and had to shout and roar for his fellows to come and free him. He is not very happy now, and is rather a threat to the good people here, I'm afraid. Deal with him, and then return to me.'
'Splendid! Now let us begin our game of riddles.'

'There is an Orc not far from here, in the north-western region of the Flaming Deeps. He is responsible for the deaths of more dwarves than any other single Orc I know of in this place.
