'You have the look of an experienced Warden, ${PLAYER}. As you well know, ours is the job of protecting homelands, no matter how odd \qhome\q might seem.
'In this case, the dwarves seek to reclaim their ancient home of Moria, likely the largest city ever known to the peoples of Middle-earth.
'If you would lend your aid, the dwarves of the Iron Garrison would be most grateful, as would I. There are many Nameless that infest the south-east reaches of the Foundations of Stone. Hunt them down, then return to me when you are finished.'
'Well done, ${PLAYER}. Let us speak of your next task.'
Defeat Nameless in the Foundations of Stone (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Sadreda at the Shadowed Refuge
Nameless hordes plague the deep places of Moria.

Nameless can be found in the south-west reaches of the Foundations of Stone.
Sadreda has asked you to prove your worth by defeating the Nameless.

Sadreda is at the Shadowed Refuge in the Foundations of Stone, north-west from the lairs of the Nameless there.
You should return to Sadreda with news of your victory.
Nightshine has been defeated

'Well, we have come to it. There is no time like the present for these horrible deeds. You must gather your friends and your strength, ${PLAYER}, for you will need both before the end. Head into the place known as the Dark Delvings, and bring this bait we have concocted.
'Once inside, look for the place where the World Eater was fought in the days of old, and leave the bait there. There should be no mistaking the place.
'I do not know what you must do to proceed from there. I am sorry I cannot be more helpful, but if you cannot find a way, then you will have little use for what I wish to teach you upon your return. I wish you the best of luck, Guardian.'

Dithrik's chest swells as you approach, and he seems to be sizing you up as if seeing you for the first time.
'You have done well this day, ${PLAYER}. Few others in the history of the ages could have accomplished what you did this day. Few indeed, for I tried also, and barely escaped with my life.
'From this day forth, you are my shield-brother. You have earned the title in my eyes, and indeed in those of all dwarves. Let any who question your valour come see me, and I'll set them aright with a dwarf-fist to the eye.'
'The World Eater earned its name long ago when the dwarves brought their picks too deep into the heart of the mountains. Have you brought it to its knees?'
Defeat Nightshine
Return to Dithrik in the Foundations of Stone
Challenge the Darkness (Optional)
Dithrik has given you the final task in your quest for advancement as a Guardian.
Defeat the World Eater in the Dark Delvings
Return to Dithrik in the Foundations of Stone
Collected the yellowed tooth
Collected the chipped tooth
Collected the stained tooth
Collected the flat tooth

Armbeald turns the skull over in his hand and frowns.
'Four teeth are indeed missing, but not through any act of violence. It looks like they were extracted, rather than knocked off by some careless gesture. I can venture a guess at what happened here.
'The Orcs of the White Hand favour bones as cosmetic trophies and trinkets. After the dwarf was murdered, his teeth were taken and his flesh devoured. Orcs are terrible creatures, and sport with their prey. They have no dignity, no respect for the dead as we do. They would just as soon despoil their own kind in this hideous manner.
'It is likely that the missing teeth can be found on the White Hand Orcs. Large teeth such as these would be considered valuable and are likely in the posession of the more senior amongst our nearby foes.'
'Well done, ${PLAYER}. We have begun to avenge our unfortunate friend.'
'Remember to look for high-ranking Orcs. They're more likely to have the missing teeth.'
Return to Armbeald in the Redhorn Lodes
Collect the yellowed tooth
Collect the chipped tooth
Collect the stained tooth
Collect the flat tooth
Passage of Foes

Armbeald has tasked you with finding the four missing teeth from the skull you brought him. He suggested you go to the White Hand Orcs in the Redhorn Lodes and search among the higher-ranking soldiers there.

The Orcs suspected of taking the teeth are in the White Hand Orc-fortress in the Redhorn Lodes.
Look for high-ranking Orcs in your search for the missing teeth. They should be defeated and their remains searched, and if any teeth are found, Armbeald in the Redhorn Lodes will wish to see them.
Defeated the Mad Captain

'The final step of your quest will take you into great peril. I believe this Dark Warden you slew was but a servant of another creature we call the Mad Captain.
'Gather your friends, ${PLAYER}, and head into the Dark Delvings, south-east from here. Once inside, you will need to use this charm to summon the Mad Captain. Look for a foul altar, and place it there. The Mad Captain will be sure to come out then.
'Rid Moria of the Mad Captain's foul evil, then return to me.'
'Excellent work, ${PLAYER}! Your efforts will be remembered for ages to come.'
'Is the deed done, ${PLAYER}? Is the Mad Captain no more?'
Summon and defeat the Mad Captain
Talk to Sadreda at the Shadowed Refuge
Safe-guard (Optional)
Sadreda has determined that the Dark Warden which you slew was but a servant of a more vile creature known as the Mad Captain.
'The Mad Captain may be found within the Dark Delvings in the Foundations of Stone.'

The Mad Captain dwells within the Dark Delvings, south-east from the Shadowed Refuge in the Foundations of Stone.
Sadreda instructed you to use the crude charm he gave you to summon and defeat the Mad Captain.

Sadreda is at the Shadowed Refuge in the Foundations of Stone, north-west from the Dark Delvings.
You should return to Sadreda with news of your victory.
Defeated Brestir

'You have done well indeed to come as far as you have on your journey as a Guardian, but I would be most curious to see how you perform in a well-matched situation. My friend Brestir, as strong a dwarf as any you'll meet nowadays, is waiting to match you in a duel.
'Travel to the Bridge of Khazad-dûm and look there for Brestir. If you can best him in a fair duel, you will surely be ready for my next task.
'My heart tells me that you are ready, but Brestir will return to me and perhaps have more to tell me. Forgive me for my lack of trust, but there are some things that must be proven beyond doubt before they are assumed.'

'I am impressed, and humbled. All dwarves are doughty and tough, but Brestir is reckoned to be among the strongest of our race. You must be a truly accomplished warrior and Guardian to have bested him thus.
'You have passed the test, and you have my praise and apologies. My heart spoke true when it told me you were ready, and did not need to be tested. But I hope you will forgive me, for the sake of fairness.
'We must now look forward, ${PLAYER}. Let us see to your next task.'

'I greet you, Guardian. You sought Brestir, and now you have found him!'
'Dithrik has sent you here to be tested. I will test your resolve in combat and determine your worth, and I will not check my tongue when I return to give my assessment. If anything is lacking in your skill, mighty Brestir will find it out, and Dithrik shall hear of it!
'Well then, fledgling, are you ready to face me in combat? Then come! Baruk Khazâd! Khazâd ai-mênu!'
Challenge Brestir to a duel at the Bridge of Khazad-dûm
Return to Dithrik at the Foundations of Stone
Litany of Defiance
Before continuing your learning, Dithrik would like to see how you fare in a duel against the dwarf Brestir.

The Bridge of Khazad-dûm, where Brestir can be found, is north of the Foundations of Stone and east of the Second Hall.
Dithrik has invited you to challenge his friend Brestir to a duel to see if you are prepared for the challenges ahead.
Return to Dithrik at the Foundations of Stone
Drâgh has been defeated

'Your final task will be to defeat Drâgh. Gather your friends, ${PLAYER}, for this will not be an easy feat.
'Take this effigy into the Grand Stair and summon forth the cruel Orc that poses so great a threat to the folk who wish to reclaim their rightful home. I do not wish him to harry the free peoples of Moria any longer.
'Return to me when you have succeeded in banishing this creature, ${PLAYER}. I hope that your arrows will fly true and bring him down once and for all, so that he troubles us no more.'
'Well done, ${PLAYER}. You are indeed worthy of this reward!'
'Is it done?'
Defeat Drâgh
Retun to Armbeald at the Redhorn Lodes
Return to Armbeald at the Redhorn Lodes
Set the Trap (Optional)

The White Hand Orc-leader, Drâgh, can be found in the Grand Stair of Moria, bringing terror wherever he roams. A dwarf of the expedition was killed, and you have been asked by Armbeald to avenge the innocent by felling this evil foe.

Drâgh can be found at the Grand Stair, east from the Redhorn Lodes and north-west from the Shadowed Refuge in the Foundations of Stone.
You should defeat Drâgh at the Grand Stair to prevent his further interference with the dwarf expedition in Moria.

Armbeald can be found at the Orc-Watch in north-west of the Redhorn Lodes.
You should return to Armbeald and tell him that Drâgh has been defeated through the efforts of you and your friends.

'It would be a shame if this beautiful instrument were never to leave these halls, for there are many in Middle-earth who would be heartened by its gift of song. Dark places are everywhere, ${PLAYER}, including the hearts of Men, Elves, dwarves, and hobbits alike.
'Darkness prevails especially in times such as these, where doom seems inevitable. You have seen the Orcs prowling as sure as Men walk, and wights leaving their barrows to trouble the fields upon which they fell, and Warg-voices rending the stillness of a quiet night.
'My thoughts often turn to a dear old friend in Bree-town who goes by the name of Erling Goodbody. He has suffered much hardship of late, and my songs used to cheer him. I have such a song here; but I'm afraid I don't have time to make the journey. Do you think you could go and play this song for him in my stead, ${PLAYER}?
'Erling usually spends his days in the thoroughfare in front of the Prancing Pony. Find him and play him a song to raise his spirits. When you have done this, please return to me, for I wish to hear tidings of my friend.'

'Oh...forgive me, friend! I did not realize the music had stopped. Pardon me for one more moment...'
Erling Goodbody closes his eyes and smiles, and then opens them again to look at you with a warm expression.
'That may have been the most beautiful song I have ever heard. Since my friend Pada went away, I admit I had fallen into a sort of gloom, for life has grown hard for many of the good folk of Bree, and it is difficult for me not to fret and worrit on all the woes of the world.
'But...when you began to play on that instrument -- I say, I was quite taken away! Why, I fancy I heard singing birds, flowing water, the sound of the sun, whatever that may be, and of things growing in the earth. You played admirably, ${PLAYER}. Thank you for this diversion.'

'Well done, ${PLAYER}! I knew this would be just the ticket to bring smiles to more than one face today. Now Erling is happy, and I am happy for him! And I can see that even your own spirits have been raised by your selflessness. That is the best thing about being a Minstrel, is it not?
'But do not be content just yet. From here, the quest turns a bit more perilous. Do you think you are ready?'
Speak with Erling Goodbody
Return to Pada
'Hallo there. What can I do for you?'
Song of the Hopeful Heart
Erling is delighted with your song
Now that you have recovered the instrument, Pada has asked you to head to Bree and use it to brighten the spirits of some of the townsfolk there.
Play a song for Erling Goodbody in Bree

Erling Goodbody can be found in the thoroughfare in front of the Prancing Pony.
Pada, a widely-respected Minstrel, has asked you to cheer a friend of his from Bree using the great instrument you recently recovered.
Speak with Erling and let him know that Pada sends his best.

Pada is in the Foundations of Stone in Moria.
You should return to Pada and tell him that his friend Erling Goodbody was very pleased with the song you played.
Collected lore-fragments (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Well met, ${PLAYER}. It is good that you have come to me. I see in your eyes the hunger for knowledge that drove me to greater pursuits in ages long passed.
'Here in the Water-works, it is easy to find odd bits of dwarf-knowledge thought lost to the ages. If you are up to the task, I would have you gather some of these texts and bring them to me. It is likely we will both end up learning a great deal together.
'Your search should focus upon the larger buildings in the Water-works as well as any large gatherings of foul creatures here. Return to me when you have found a significant amount of material for us to study.'

'Well done, ${PLAYER}. These will prove most valuable in the days to come.
'We must move on to your next task, for we have little time to lose.'

'Continue your search for more lost knowledge here in the Water-works.
'Such knowledge is likely to be in and around the larger buildings here, but I would not be surprised to hear that some of the local wildlife have gathered them up out of curiosity.'
Collect lore-fragments (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Take the lore-fragments back to Winiel
Beacon of Hope
Winiel has come to the Water-works, seeking the lost knowledge of the dwarves.

Lore-fragments can be found throughout the Water-works.
Winiel has asked you to search for lore-fragments of the ancient dwarves.

Winiel is at the Rotting Cellar in the Water-works.
You should bring the lore-fragments back to Winiel.
Snapjaw has been defeated
Acquired musical text

'The instrument you've found will undoubtedly serve you well on your ventures, for you are a great minstrel, and such a tool well befits you. There is nothing better than a tune played from the heart on a piece such as this, but we are still missing a key thing: written music!
'There is a deep-claw in the Redhorn Lodes, Snapjaw, that is known to hoard papers and scraps of text to make nests for its foul broods. I believe that if you go there and slay that beast, you will find the very sheet we seek.
'Snapjaw was last seen just south and west of the bridge that crosses the crevace south of the Broken Stair. Go there slay this deep-claw, ${PLAYER}. Search its hoard for any musical knowledge that may prove useful and bring it back to me, and I will see if you have found the missing ticket.'

'You were very brave to face that beastly deep-claw, ${PLAYER}! This looks to be precisely what we needed.
'Now, let me see what is scribed on this sheet....'
Pada begins to pore over paper you've brought him.
'Have you beaten Snapjaw? The beast resides in the Redhorn Lodes.'
Defeat Snapjaw in the Redhorn Lodes
Acquire musical text from Snapjaw's corpse
Return to Pada
Bring the texts to Pada
Echoes of Battle
Pada has asked you to find a special sheet of music to accompany the instrument you recovered.

The deep-claw Snapjaw can be found in the Redhorn Lodes south-west of the bridge that crosses the crevace south of the Broken Stair.
Snapjaw has been rumoured to hoard a great deal of paper-scraps and texts, undoubtedly some of great historic value, to build nests for its brood. Pada wishes you to recover a sheet of music that can likely be taken from Snapjaw upon its defeat.

Pada is in the Foundations of Stone, east from the Redhorn Lodes and then south to the Shadowed Refuge.
You should return to Pada with the musical text you have found, and hopefully it will be the one that he is seeking.

'${PLAYER}, while you were away, I received a message from Thorin's Hall... asking for you. Dwalin would like to speak with you regarding your recent efforts here in Khazad-dûm. He is quite knowledgeable of old dwarf-runes and will likely be a source of great help to you.
'Thorin's Hall lies far to the west in Ered Luin. You should travel there as soon as possible, for Dwalin is a very important dwarf.'

'Well met, ${PLAYER}. Aye, I've heard tell of you many a time.
'I myself have some skill in runes. When Thorin's Company had reclaimed the Lonely Mountain, we hid the treasure and safe-guarded it using our own rune-craft.'
Dwalin looks far off, as though recalling some memory long forgotten, then smiles.
'But enough about me; I've asked you here to help out with a matter of some great importance to our efforts to retake Khazad-dûm.'
Talk to Dwalin at Thorin's Hall
Rousing Words
Márus received a summons from Dwalin at Thorin's Hall, requesting your presence.
'You should speak with Dwalin in Thorin's Hall.'

Dwalin can be found in Thorin's Hall in Ered Luin, far to the west of Moria.
Márus has instructed you to go to Thorin's Hall and speak with Dwalin.
Acquired musical instrument

'Well met, ${PLAYER}, and welcome to the Foundations of Stone. Your renown as a Minstrel precedes you, and I'm honoured to meet you at last. Together I hope we can bring light to this place.
'I see great strength in you, but doubt also. And where there is doubt, there is dread, and morale can wither and break under such strain. But fear not -- you need naught but inspiration, which may then be used to infuse your heart with newfound power and will.
'I can help you in this regard. To begin this last leg of your journey, I would have you acquire an instrument that once belonged to a great Minstrel. Legend has it that this piece could be well heard singing high above the clamour of battle, drowning out fear, anguish, and even death with its clear music. I have learned that an Orc, Shîk, has been seen with this instrument here in the Foundations of Stone.
'They say that Shîk likes to play in the foetid pools along the northern edges of the Foundations of Stone and is especially fond of the waterfalls that feed them. Go and recover the instrument, and then return to me.'
'Splendid work, ${PLAYER}. This is indeed the instrument I have sought. Now, let us see to your next task.'

'Venture out into the Shadowy Deeps, ${PLAYER}. You should find an Orc by the name of Shîk.
'Kill the Orc, and bring the instrument back to me.'
Bring the instrument to Pada
Acquire the instrument from Shîk in the Foundations of Stone
Triumphant Spirit

Pada has tasked you with recovering an ancient instrument from an Orc within the Foundations of Stone. He wishes to see your skill so that he can assess how best to teach you what is left to be taught.

The Orc Shîk can be found in the Foundations of Stone. Pada mentioned looking for Shîk in the pools of water with waterfalls along the northern edges of the Foundations of Stone.
Pada has requested that you venture forth to recover an excellent and famous instrument from the unworthy Orcs to help further your final education as a Minstrel.
Cracktooth has been defeated

'I have deciphered all I can from this text you recovered, ${PLAYER}, but there is still something missing. This composition is almost complete, yet it is so far from being the full song I know it should be!
'I want you take what I've written so far and head into Skûmfil east of here. While there, keep an eye out for the deep-claw Cracktooth. I believe it may be in posession of the remaining text, for deep-claws always seem to be gathering for their foul nests.
'Gather your friends and strength for this fight, for it shan't be easy. Your companions will look to you for inspiration, so you must be wilful and strong...but I will not tell you how to be a good Minstrel, for you know that well already! Return to me when you have found the scrap I seek, and you will then be ready for all that I have to teach you.'

'${PLAYER}, this is it! You have found and restored a lost piece of wonderful music, ancient beyond reckoning, but timeless too. Surely you appreciate what a great thing you have done, for music is woven into everything we know. There is even music in silence, if you listen closely.
'It has been a pleasure working with so great a Minstrel as yourself. I hope that my lesson is worth your troubles; indeed, you have taught and inspired me as well! I see now that you will stop at nothing to pursue a worthy cause, and here I had doubted that your will would prevail in this dark place.
'You have restored hope to me, my friend, and I did not even know that my hope had failed. May your music ever bring you light when your feet take you down dark roads.'
'Is it done, ${PLAYER}?'
Defeat Cracktooth in Skûmfil
Return to Pada at the Foundations of Stone
Return to Pada at the Foundations of Stone
A Fellowship's Heart (Optional)

Pada has deciphered the musical text you acquired and transcribed it to a composition that you can now read and perform. In order to practise your newfound knowledge, Pada has tasked you with entering Skûmfil and facing down the deep-claw Cracktooth.

Cracktooth is in Skûmfil in Moria, east of the Shadowed Refuge in the Foundations of Stone.
You should defeat and search the deep-claw named Cracktooth in Skûmfil, for it is likely that the last bit of text can be found upon that beast.

Pada awaits your return at the Foundations of Stone in Moria.
You have defeated Cracktooth and recovered the lost text missing from the composition being compiled. The completed work should help you on your way to being a truly heroic Minstrel.
Collected Nameless head (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Well met, ${PLAYER}. You sought Dithrik, and Dithrik you have found. I am a defender of my fellow dwarves, and of all the good peoples of this Middle-earth; in that we are akin.
'I can see that your shield arm is as strong as the very stone that holds mountains, and in your eyes I recognize the light of keen hope that defies the darkness of despair. You are a true Guardian, and I have just the task for one such as you.
'There is an ancient horror from days even before Durin's Bane plagued our home of Moria. Dwarves have seen him near here, in the Foundations of Stone, and rumours of his terror spread far. Find and slay the Nameless, for they walk unchallenged. Bring me the unspoiled heads of these creatures so that we might prepare a suitable bait for the elder terror.'
'Excellent work, ${PLAYER}. Now, for your next task....'
'Our quarry has a gruesome taste in its food, but it hunts all things that venture too near. The Nameless should suffice to please it'
Return to Dithrik in the Foundations of Stone
Collect Nameless heads (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Thrill of Danger
Dithrik has tasked you with acquiring materials that will aid in challenging an old horror from ages long passed.

The Nameless beings and the ancient creature prowl the vicinity of the Foundations of Stone, especially to the south-east of this region.
Dithrik has asked you to collect twelve unspoiled heads from the Nameless of the Foundations of Stone.
Defeated Helegfan

'We must restore this rune-stone to its former power, ${PLAYER}. There is no doubt that a fell power has corrupted this stone. There is a shadow-grim, Helegfan, that is known to take pleasure in the perversion of good, and this stone reeks of his foul corruption.
'Helegfan was last known to make his home within the Sixteenth Hall, north from here. Use the rune-stone to summon it forth and slay it.
'Return to me when the deed is done, and we will see if the corruption can be undone.'

'Well done, ${PLAYER}!
'With the fell spirit defeated, the rune-stone will no longer be subject to his corruption. You have done a great thing in restoring this dwarf-stone to its former glory.
'You have the gratitude of all the Longbeards, ${PLAYER}. Take a well-deserved rest and reward. You've earned both.'
'Is the deed done, ${PLAYER}? Has the spirit been banished?'
Use the rune-stone to summon Helegfan
Defeat Helegfan
Talk to Márus at the Shadowed Refuge
Secrets Long Forgotten (Optional)
Márus determined that the rune-stone you found has been corrupted by a fell spirit within the depths of Moria.
'Use the rune to summon Helegfan, ${PLAYER}.'

Helegfan can be found within the Sixteenth Hall, north from the Shadowed Refuge, at the southern edge of Nud-melek.
Márus has asked you to enter the Sixteenth Hall and defeat the shadow-grim Helegfan, cleansing the rune-stone of the spirit's corruption.

Márus is at the Shadowed Refuge, south from the Sixteenth Hall.
You should return to Márus with news of your victory.
Collected the book

'I fear you must venture back into Moria and search the deepest reaches of the Water-works. Scour the waterways that give the area its name.
'An ancient toad, named Greatroar, was known to be attracted to items of great knowledge. If you should find her, slay her. The book is as likely to be in her belly as anywhere else in Moria, if the creature still exists!
'Once you have acquired the book, take it back to Winiel. She will be able to translate these writings with the aid of that book.'

'Well done, ${PLAYER}. This is a splendid find!
'I can hardly contain my excitement at solving this mystery we have uncovered!'
'Did Mirwen have any advice for us, ${PLAYER}?'
Bring the book to Winiel at the Rotting Cellar
Defeat Greatroar and collect the book
Knowledge of the Lore-master
Mirwen was pleased with the texts you brought her, but was also unable to immediately translate them.

Greatroar is somewhere in the Water-works of Moria, far to the south of Rivendell.
Mirwen told you to find the toad Greatroar and defeat her, for the toad long ago swallowed a book of dwarf-lore.

'At least our dwarf-friend is no longer scattered in pieces among the wretched Orc-hordes. We have restored a little of his stolen honour. Alas for this poor fellow and the wretched errand that brought him to his doom.
'I wonder if there was anything behind this attack. Orc-savagery is not surprising in any circumstance, but the taking of trophies is not something that average Orcs do. I wonder what force drives this particular horde, and who commands them?
'We shall find out, ${PLAYER}. Take these pieces to my friend, Frosti Groundshaker, in Thorin's Hall by the auctioneers south of the throne. He is very scholarly, and enjoys solving puzzles such as this.'

'What's that you have there? Ah, that poor dwarf! He went out to do some scouting and exploring. What a terrible end to meet. Terrible! Well, Armbeald was right to have you come to me with evidence of the murder. I have a knack for solving this sort of thing.
'So these teeth were extracted and found as trophies on Orc-leaders bearing the symbol of the White Hand? I bet I know who is behind this. I have heard rumour of a brutal Orc-master near the Redhorn Lodes, and his arm is long. He commands many of the White Hand Orcs in the vicinity.
'I will make you a little idol, an effigy of sorts, with some runes carved upon it, and I wager it will summon the Orc if you brandish it with that intent. You should return now to Armbeald.'
'Yes? Do you have something for me?'

'Ill tidings! I have heard of this beastly White Hand Master, and the rumours say that he is very strong, and his command expansive. He will be a difficult foe for a bow and arrow alone.
'But Frosti Groundshaker is a useful fellow, is he not? This effigy will be valuable in what is to come next.'
Give the items to Frosti Groundshaker in Thorin's Hall
Give the items to Frosti Groundshaker in Thorin's Hall
Return to Armbeald in the Redhorn Lodes
Return to Armbeald in the Redhorn Lodes
Strength of the Earth

Having discovered the signs of foul play among the nearby Orc-horde, Armbeald has asked you to seek out Frosti Groundshaker, a wise dwarf who is learned in many lores, to discover more about White Hand Orcs and their behaviour.
'You should show your grisly trophies to Frosti Groundshaker...he may know more than I about them.'
'You should let Armbeald know what we learned.'

Frosti Groundshaker is in Thorin's Hall, by the auctioneers south of the throne.
You should take the pieces to Frosti Groundshaker in Thorin's Hall so that he may shed some light upon what may be going on.

Armbeald is at the Orc-Watch in the Redhorn Lodes of Moria.
Frosti Groundshaker has made you an effigy with some runes that may help to draw the attention of the Orc-wraith. You should return to Armbeald in Moria and he will instruct you on what to do next.

'Strange... the dwarves use our certh, though I understand they use some letters to represent different sounds, but these fragments you brought me are all but unintelligible to my eyes.
'If anyone could decipher these it would be Mirwen. Her knowledge of ancient writings is unparalleled.
'Take these to Rivendell and look for her there. She is an ever-vigilant student and so spends most of her time in the library. Start your search there.'

'What is that you have there? Let me see....
'Ah yes, very nice indeed. But there is something missing. I can help you; but these writings will not be enough.'
'Yes? What may I help you with?'
Take the fragments to Mirwen in Rivendell
Share the Power
Winiel was unable to translate the texts you brought to her.

Mirwen is in Elrond's Library at the Last Homely House in Rivendell, far to the north of Moria.
Winiel has asked you to take the fragments to an Elf named Mirwen.
Acquired dwarf-skull

'Here we come to it, ${PLAYER}. You wish to learn, and I am willing to teach you, if you can do what I ask.
'You have the look of an experienced enough woodsman and hunter. I know of a skill that will aid you greatly, but the path you must follow to attain it will not be easy. Sometimes it is more useful to track friend than foe, so let us start there.
'One of the dwarf-workers of the expedition went out many days ago on a scouting mission that took him through the southern region of the Redhorn Lodes. You should search there for evidence of his passage, and see how he fares.'

'How terrible! I sought evidence, yes, but I had hoped it had not come to this. Let us examine the poor fellow's skull for clues as to what happened to him. If we can avenge him, that will suffice for your challenge!
'He was killed recently. Some teeth are missing, also. What shall we make of this?'
'Have you found anything yet, ${PLAYER}?'
Acquire evidence of dwarf-worker's passage
Return to Armbeald in the Redhorn Lodes
Armbeald has asked you to track the path of a missing dwarf-worker and bring back any evidence you find of his passage.

The dwarf-worker was rumoured to have passed through the heart of the Redhorn Lodes, by the east to west mine cart track just north of the passage leading into the Flaming Deeps.
You should collect evidence of his passage and bring it to Armbeald, who wishes to see the progress of the dwarf's mission.

Armbeald is at the Orc-watch in the Redhorn Lodes of Moria, north-west from where you found evidence of the dwarf's remains.
You should return to Armbeald with the skull you have found, which has been cleaned of all its flesh.

'There are things you need to learn before I continue your instruction, and not all of them can be learned here.
'Before we continue, ${PLAYER}, I want you to speak with another member of our order, Mosco Mudbottom. You will find him at Ost Guruth in the Lone-lands, far to the north and west of Moria.
'Mosco, I am sure, will have a task for you. Think of this as part of your training...a test of endurance and patience.'

'Well met, ${PLAYER}. You have the look of one of our order about you.
'Sadreda sent you, you say? Well, I can see why. You have the look of an experienced adventurer that yearns for more knowledge.
'I think I know just the thing.'
Talk to Mosco Mudbottom at Ost Guruth
Forced March
Sadreda has more for you to do, but requires one last task of endurance before he begins.
'Mosco Mudbottom may be found at Ost Guruth in the Lone-lands.'

Mosco Mudbottom can be found at Ost Guruth in the Lone-lands, far to the north and west of Moria.
Sadreda has instructed you to speak with a warden by the name of Mosco Mudbottom.
Collected the Dark Warden's head

'Rumour has reached me here of many dark things that dwell in Moria. The place has an ill reputation, but there is supposedly a creature the dwarves dredged up there that is particularly vile. I'm quite surprised Sadreda did not send you after it himself.
'You should travel back to the Foundations of Stone and seek out the creature known as The Dark Warden. I can't promise it actually exists -- rumours are rumours, after all -- but if it does, it should be defeated.
'If it does indeed exist, bring its head to Sadreda as evidence of your victory.'

'I see your journey was well worth the effort, ${PLAYER}. And what is this you have?
'I see...Mosco Mudbottom was right. I do know how you must proceed from here.
'This next step will be most perilous...are you ready?'
'What is it, ${PLAYER}? Do you have some news for me from Mosco?'
Talk to Sadreda at the Shadowed Refuge
Defeat the Dark Warden and collect its head
Offensive Strike
Rumour of the dark things that dwell in the depths of Moria have reached even the ears of Mosco Mudbottom in the Lone-lands.
'The Dark Warden may be found in the Foundations of Stone in Moria.'

The Dark Warden, if it exists, dwells somewhere within the Foundations of Stone in Moria, far to the east and south of the Lone-lands.
Mosco Mudbottom has tasked you with discovering the lair of the Dark Warden and bringing the creature's head to Sadreda.
Collected the mithril chisel

'Well met, ${PLAYER}. There is an air about you that hints at your experience. From your attire, I must assume that you are a Rune-keeper much like myself. If greater knowledge is what you seek, then I can help. First, however, I have a task for you.
'Ancient Rune-keepers used fine chisels to carve out their speech-craft in stone. The finest of these tools were made of mithril and were said to have power in their own right.
'One such chisel has been seen recently, and I think it appropriate that we reclaim this instrument to further your own abilities. There is an Orc, Folok, in the south-west portion of the Redhorn Lodes near Malmezel. Seek out this Orc and slay him; our scouts believe they have seen the chisel in his possession.'

'Excellent work, ${PLAYER}.
'This is indeed a fine tool of dwarf-craft. Let us hope that it has not been fouled by its recent owner.'
'Is the deed done, ${PLAYER}?'
Talk to Márus at the Shadowed Refuge
Collect the mithril chisel from Folok
Prelude to Hope
The Orcs of Moria have looted many of the great treasures remaining in Moria after the fall of the dwarf-realm.

Folok has been seen in the south-west portion of the Redhorn Lodes, near Malmezel, at the western edge of the Redhorn Lodes.
Márus has asked you to defeat the Orc Folok and recover the mithril chisel.
You have won the battle

'Now that you have that old riddle of mine, I suggest you go out and put it to good use. There's no better way to learn than by doing, I say. I've gathered what information I can from all these texts you've brought me, and I think I shall be able to give you a nice reward for this next bit of burglary I'll have you do. Don't you love a good challenge?
'There is a terrible enemy in the Sixteenth Hall, an Orc named Unur. He is a curse-shouter of no small skill, and he hates Burglars more than anything, for it may have come to pass that I plucked some valuables from under his nose and sneaked away unnoticed. He will answer a summons, but be wary and bring company with you! I'll warrant he'll have some friends too.
'I may have picked his pocket, but I hadn't the gall to face him down in a fair fight. If you can defeat him, you will prove a great Burglar indeed, and I will humbly teach you all that I know.'

'I am tremendously impressed with your skills as a Burglar, ${PLAYER}, and I do believe you have surpassed even myself in skill. I did not think anyone loved riddles more than I, but I see that you may be the greatest riddler I have ever met!
'Now, do take this reward. You have earned it, and no mistake!'
'Have you been to the Sixteenth Hall, ${PLAYER}? Unur still prowls those grounds, and he is wroth.'
Defeat Unur and his trolls
Return to Celofa
A Confounding Riddle (Optional)
Celofa has given you a challenge to better learn the use of the riddle she gave you.
'Unur is a foul creature... the likes of him cannot be allowed to roam free.'

The Sixteenth Hall is north from the Foundations of Stone just south of Sigin-tharâk, and that is where the curse-shouter Unur may be found.
Celofa wishes you to do what she could not: to summon Unur with your scroll and defeat him in fair combat. He will likely have companions, so you should be sure bring allies on this venture.

The great Burglar Celofa can be found in the Foundations of Stone.
Celofa awaits tidings of your adventure and looks forward to humbly teaching you all that she knows.
Defeated Ruingal

'Your investigation has proven both fruitful and distressing. Apparently the dwarves of old were plagued by a fire-grim of no meagre stature, perhaps a servant of Durin's Bane.
'If this creature is allowed to linger here, it is entirely possible it will find aid from the other agents of the Enemy that have come to claim Moria. We cannot let that come to pass!
'Gather your friends, ${PLAYER}. Head into the Forges of Khazad-dûm, east into the Flaming Deeps, then south at the Cross-roads of Ash. Once there, use this tome to summon the fire-grim Ruingal and defeat him.'

'Well done, ${PLAYER}.
'With the fire-grim banished, the Mines of Moria are one step closer to recovery, though I know not if the Elves will ever see such things come to pass... their time in Middle-earth is ending.
'Take this as your reward. You have more than earned it.'

'Is the deed done, ${PLAYER}?
'Do not despair if the task proves more challenging than you had anticipated. Hope and fellowship are your strongest weapons in the face of evil. Look to them for strength.'
Use the tome to summon Ruingal
Defeat Ruingal
Talk to Winiel at the Rotting Cellar
Light of the Rising Dawn (Optional)

Winiel has deciphered the lore-fragments you brought her with the aid of the book you acquired from the toad Greatroar. With your aid she has gleaned knowledge of a fire-grim that haunts the Mines of Moria.
Enter the Forges of Khazad-dûm, summon the fire grim, Ruingal, and slay it.

Winiel is at the Rotting Cellar in the Water Works, north-east from the Forges of Khazad-dûm.
You should return to Winiel with tidings of your victory.
Found the missing text

'I am terribly perplexed by this deceptive scroll, friend Burglar. It teased me with hopes of learning a very great and mischievous riddle, but then played a trick on me by being incomplete from the start!
'I think I know just where to hunt next for the missing text to this naughty scrap of lore. In the Foundations of Stone are many Orcs, most of whom have become infected with the unhappy fungus that plagues the area. One in particular, who goes by the name of Horngaz, has apparently gained his own appreciation of scrolls and books. Yes, an Orc who likes riddles -- a peculiar event, is it not?
'Find Horngaz, ${PLAYER}, and see if he has the missing text we seek. I shan't sleep a wink until I can find out the rest!'

'Well done, ${PLAYER}. Well done, indeed!'
Celofa immediately starts reading the text you brought her while absently handing you an old scroll.
'Here, you may take this. I've learned all I can from it and I think you could make good use out of it.
'In fact, I know just the thing to help you learn how to use it.'
'I cannot bear the suspense, ${PLAYER}! Do you have it? Why must you tease me?'
Find the missing text
Return to Celofa
A Startling Twist

Celofa thinks that the remaining text that pairs with the scroll you found earlier is in the posession of an Orc named Horngaz. The remaining text must be found in order for her appetite for riddles to be sated.
'Have you found Horngaz yet? I am sure he can be found in the Foundations of Stone somewhere.'

Horngaz is somewhere within the Foundations of Stone.
Celofa has asked you to acquire the missing text from the Orc Horngaz.

Celofa is in the Foundations of Stone.
You should return to Celofa with the scroll.
Defeated Orcs in Fil-gashan

'For your final task, ${PLAYER}, you will take this battle-horn into Fil-gashan and look for the battle standard of the Orcs therein. When you find the standard, make use of it and defeat the Orcs that come to your call...and come they will. There is no way they can ignore the insult of their former leader's battle-horn being used to challenge them.
'Begin your search in a place where many Orcs gather. It is likely that their battle standard is there; and more likely still that the Orcs will answer the call of their fallen leader's battle-horn.
'Remember that your task in this fight as a captain is to inspire your fellow warriors to continue the fight.
'When you have won the battle, return to me.'

Garnyd salutes you.
'You have done well, ${PLAYER}. Your deeds have inspired warriors on the field of battle and will inspire man, woman, and child for years to come.
'You have shown your worth, and I daresay its worth is greater than the mithril that was once the fame of Moria.'

'Is the deed done, ${PLAYER}?
'Remember that your task in this fight as a captain is to inspire your fellow warriors to continue the battle.'
Challenge Orcs inside Fil-gashan near their battle standard
Talk to Garnyd at Anazârmekhem
In Harm's Way (Optional)
The call of Nanulg's battle-horn would be such an insult to the Orcs of Fil-gashan that they would not dare to ignore its call.

Fil-gashan lies in the south-western reaches of the Flaming Deeps.
Garnyd has instructed you to use Nanlug's battle-horn to challenge the Orcs in Fil-gashan.

Garnyd is at Anazârmekhem, north from Fil-gashan.
You should return to Garnyd with news of your victory.
This book-case does not contain the scroll that you seek
Found a scroll of riddles

'All right, ${PLAYER}. To begin, let's have you go out and dig up some old dwarf-style riddles... or at least riddles that dwarves wrote down. They needn't be dwarvish in origin, of course, but since Moria has such a great store of everything imaginable, just waiting to be uncovered, one would think that some excellent riddles can be unearthed here.
'Now where was I... Ah, yes. Riddles! There are some old shelves in the Western Deeps, but you will find nasty Orcs too, I'm afraid. Try searching the shelves for any good riddles and bring one back to me.
'And about those Orcs: they might hear you if you make too much noise rustling and rummaging about those shelves. I'd keep my eyes open, if I were you, and make quick work of it.'

'Well done! This is a treasure, and no mistake!'
Celofa purses her lips and avidly peruses the faded text, eyes alight with hopeful mischief.
'Now hold on; this text is incomplete! This won't do... won't do at all.
'We'll have to find the missing text to go along with this scroll you found, ${PLAYER}.'
'Did you find that scroll yet?'
Find a scroll of riddles
Return to Celofa with the scroll
Tracking Treasure

Celofa has sent you out to the Western Deeps in search of ancient dwarf-style riddles. Apparently clues can be found on the book-shelves there, but Celofa warns that making too much noise may attract the nearby Orcs.
'So, ${PLAYER}, have you discovered any of the dwarf-make riddles I requested of you?'

The Western Deeps are north-west from the Redhorn Lodes. Celofa suggested that you start your search between Gabil-mamach and the Hall of Flowing Water.
Celofa has asked you to search through any stacks of scrolls you may find in the Western Deeps between Gabil-mamach and the Hall of Flowing Water, but she warned that your search may alert the Orcs of that area to your presence if you are not careful.

Celofa is at the Foundations of Stone, south-east of the Western Deeps and the Redhorn Lodes.
You should return to Celofa with the scroll you found.
Collected Nanulg's horn

'${PLAYER}, you have no doubt begun to understand the important role you play on the field of battle. But do you understand the importance of your counterparts among the enemy?
'There is an Orc at Hurmulkezer to the south-east named Nanulg. He commands the respect of many Orcs around him and represents a great obstacle in the dwarves' campaign to retake the Mines of Moria.
'I task you now with striking a strategic blow against the Orcs of this region. Find Nanulg and slay him. When you do, be sure to take his battle-horn. The horn alone will lower the morale of the Orcs that knew him in life.'
'Well done, ${PLAYER}. Now for your final task.'
'Is the deed done, ${PLAYER}? Have you brought me Nanulg's horn?'
Collect Nanulg's horn
Bring Nanulg's horn to Garnyd at Anazârmekhem
Routing Cry
The Orcs at Hurmulkezer are led by a great War-leader named Nanulg. Without him, they might fall into disarray.

Nanulg is at Hurmulkezer, south of Durin's Court along the southern edge of the Flaming Deeps.
Garnyd has instructed you to defeat Nanulg and take his horn.

Garnyd is at Anazârmekhem, in the northern reaches of the Flaming Deeps.
You should return to Garnyd with Nanulg's horn.
Raised Eldur's spirits
Raised Lythur's spirits
Raised Skafti's spirits

'We have seen that your actions will no doubt inspire those around you, but all too often it is a captain's words that embolden the hearts of people around them. It is said that the words of great captains throughout the ages have turned the tides of battles that would have otherwise been lost. Without the power of speech, a captain is little more than a common warrior.
'For your second task, I would have you speak with three dwarves. The first, Eldur, can be found at the Rotting Cellar, which lies west from here. The second, Lythur, is encamped at Durin's Threshold at the western edge of the Great Delving to the north-west. The third, Skafti, is at Jazârgund in the middle of Durin's Way to the north.
'Use your words to lift the hearts of these dwarves, for they have seen all too much despair and are now filled with sorrow.'

'Well done, ${PLAYER}. You are an inspiration to the people of Middle-earth.
'Let us see now to your next task.'

Eldur's eyes light up ever so faintly as you approach him. You hear the tale of his recent defeat and remind him that death is but another step in one's journey through the ages.
Hearing this, his mood brightens and he nods slowly.
'Thank you, Captain. You have given my heart the strength that had been stolen from it naught but a few days ago.'

Lythur stands to attention at your approach. You hear the tale of his recent encounters in Moria and offer him words of encouragment.
Hearing your words seems to put his mind at ease, and he relaxes visibly.

Skafti meets your eyes and a look of recognition crosses his face.
'I've heard of you, ${PLAYER}. Your deeds have reached even the ears of the dwarves under the mountains. You need not speak another word. I know why you have come; and I say that a true captain's measure is in their mere presence, as you have shown me just now.
'If you will excuse me, Khazad-dûm is not yet under the rule of its rightful masters. There is much work I must do, and no rest to be had until this great Durin's Folk is completed.'
Raise Eldur's spirits
Raise Lythur's spirits
Raise Skafti's spirits
Talk to Garnyd at Anazârmekhem
Rallying Cry
Many of the Longbeards struggling to reclaim Moria have been daunted by the seemingly impossible task set before them.

Eldur can be found at the Rotting Cellar, just west of the Flaming Deeps. Lythur can be found at Durin's Threshold at the western edge of the Great Delving, north of the Silvertine Lodes. Skafti can be found at Jazârgund in the middle of Durin's Way in the northern reaches of Moria.
Garnyd has asked you to raise the spirits of three dwarf-soldiers found throughout Moria: Eldur, Lythur, and Skafti.

Garnyd is at Anazârmekhem in the Flaming Deeps.
Now that you have raised the dwarves' spirits, it is time to return to Garnyd.
Agents of the North
Agents of the South
Dark Delvings
Drummers of the Deep
Entering the Vile Maw
Defeated Orcs in the Water-works (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'I am normally not so cautious a dwarf, ${PLAYER}... but I fear something terrible has followed us to these flooded depths.
'The Orcs of these deeps have been here longer than us... perhaps they know what lurks in these stilled pools. Defeat them, we have no need for further interference at the Great Wheel. I have heard that the fungus has consumed the Orcs, but no matter, they may still know something we do not.
'If they say naught, it may be that the creature is gone from this place.'

'The Orcs are afraid of tentacles dragging them down into the water? This bodes ill, my friend.
'I already sent my aide, Kaldi, to the Vile Maw. It is not far from here, but now I worry that I may have made a grave error in judgement in coming here!'
Defeat Orcs in the Water-works (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Foreman Indrith in the Chamber of Wheels
Two Problems, One Tool
The Water-works is a site of importance to the dwarves who wish to remain in Moria. One such dwarf, Foreman Indrith, has made it a mission to repair the channel there.
'Go fight the Orcs out there in the Water-works, then return to me with your report.'

Orcs can be found in the Water-works, east and north-east of the Great Wheel.
Foreman Indrith wants to best two problems with one foray. If the Orcs in the Water-works are afraid of anything, they may mention it as they fight.

Foreman Indrith is in the Chamber of Wheels, beneath the Great Wheel.
While ridding the Water-works of the Orcs, a few of the creatures did mention that they were afraid of tentacles dragging them down into the cold water.

'Now that we have the findings, we can send them on to someone who will know what we should do.
'Make your way east to the Great Wheel and speak with Foreman Indrith. He will be able to tell you if there is anything wrong with the water and how we can best deal with the situation.
'I am afraid something terrible is going on here.'

'This is grave indeed. It appears that we have found something after all.
'In fact, it seems as though we found the very thing we had hoped we would not find since facing it outside of Khazad-dûm.'
'We must persevere though, ${PLAYER}.'

'This is a sample of the water near the Vile Maw?'
He examines the fluid.
'Not good. There is something there, and I think that we need to be cautious about what we do. When you return to Kaldi, tell him that I said it is time for a final foray.
'You should head back to him now at his encampment outside the Vile Maw.'
'Can I help you with something?'
Deliver the sample to Foreman Indrith at the Great Wheel
Talk to Kaldi at the Vile Maw
Reporting the Findings
The Water-works is a site of importance to the dwarves who wish to remain in Moria. One such dwarf, Foreman Indrith, has made it a mission to repair the channel there.
'Hurry back to Kaldi and let him know what I have learned.'
'Hurry now, get that sample to Indrith at the Great Wheel to the east of here.'

Foreman Indrith is at the Great Wheel to the east of the Vile Maw.
Kaldi handed the sample back to you and sent you to speak with Indrith about what is wrong with the water and to find out what should be done at the Vile Maw.

Kaldi is at his camp outside the Vile Maw, west of the Great Wheel.
Foreman Indrith did not like what he saw within the water and sent you back to Kaldi with a special message.
Forges of Khazad-dûm
The Forgotten Treasury
General's Command
The Grand Stair
The Host of Flame
The Masters of Moria

Collected a barrel of fungus (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'I have known for some time that there was something truly vile happening at the Foundations of Stone. Before I sent my agents to the Shadowed Refuge, I saw Orcs -- or things that looked like they were once Orcs -- picking through the fungus there. They had these great barrels on their side that they stuffed the fungus into and then mashed to a fine pulp.
'Before I send you off to the Shadowed Refuge, I want you to understand what this means and how vile this truly is. On the outskirts of the shadowy dark, you will find these collectors. Hunt one down and bring its barrel back to me.
'Begin your search south-east of here. When the ground grows moist and the area dark with traces of red emanating from the fungus, you will know you are in the right place.'

'Aye, this is the same mush that I recall seeing before. Did you get a good look at the beast that carried this? Good... good.
'You see, I believe that the Orcs there are changing themselves to become more like that thing, and that is what my agents are looking into at the Shadowed Refuge.'
'Get me one of those barrels. Search to the south-east for an Orc fungus-collector. They all carry the barrels... I remember that all too well. When you have one return here to me.'
Return the barrel to Veúlfur at the Twenty-first Hall
Collect a barrel of fungus (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Something Wicked

In the deepest regions of Moria, there are strange and frightening creatures. Veúlfur dispatched a host of his finest agents to the Shadowed Refuge to meet up with Elves there to investigate rumours of the deep dark.

Orc fungus-collectors can be found at the Foundations of Stone, south-east of the twenty-first Hall. Veúlfur is at the Twenty-first Hall.
Veúlfur wants you to be prepared for the undertaking he intends for you and asked you to retrieve a barrel from the Orc fungus-collectors as the first step in your preparations.

'I have dispatched my agents to meet with the Elves who came to the Shadowed Refuge. They are at the Foundations of Stone now, and they all have tasks that I have set them to. We are too few in number to undertake them on our own.
'I would ask that you complete all the tasks set forth by Mallas, Throstur, and Gelirwen then return to me. We must understand better the foes that we face out of that dark place.
'You can find my agents and our Elf-allies within the Shadowed Refuge, located to the south-east of the Twenty-first Hall.'

'A terrible discovery is this Gurvand, creatures without heads, and Orcs being claimed by the fungus. What terror is this that dwells within the darkest depths of Khazad-dûm?
'Your efforts have done much to prove that there is indeed a great evil yet lurking within these halls. We are in your debt for assisting us in our investigations. Further, we are indebted to you for ridding us of such a terrible creature.
'We shall ever more call you a hero of our folk. You have our deepest thanks and will be written of in the annals of Durin's Folk, I promise you that, ${PLAYER}.'
Assist Mallas with his efforts at the Sixteenth Hall
Assist Mallas with his efforts at Skûmfil
Assist Throstur with his efforts at Skûmfil
Assist Gelirwen with her efforts at the Dark Delvings
Return to Veúlfur at the Twenty-first Hall
Nightmares in the Abyss

In the deepest sections of Moria, there are strange and frightening creatures. Veúlfur dispatched a host of his finest agents to the Shadowed Refuge to meet up with a company of Elves there to investigate rumours of the deep dark.

'Orcs fear the place, but far be it from a dwarf to not enter a cave that needs exploring. My agents at the Shadowed Refuge south-east of the Twenty-first Hall can all use your help.
'Our allies there are also aiding us in better understanding just what kind of threat grows from that place. Will you go there and help Mallas, Throstur, and Gelirwen?'
'Hail to you, ${PLAYER}, the Light in the Darkness.'

Mallas, Throstur, and Gelirwen are at the Shadowed Refuge, south-east of the Twenty-first Hall.
Veúlfur wants to better understand the enemy appearing from the edges of the shadowy dark. He sent you to the Shadowed Refuge to assist his agents and allies there with various tasks meant to divine the dangers and meanings of the nefarious creature found therein.

Veúlfur is at the Twenty-first hall, north-west of the Shadowed Refuge.
You successfully assisted all of Veúlfur's agents at the Shadowed Refuge, earning from them honour and respect.

'I am glad that Veúlfur was able to earn the favour of so stout a warrior as yourself. We are in need of such spirit in this darkened place. The gloom here clouds our sight and disheartens even the hardiest among us.
'Veúlfur likely told you that I am charged with watching the Sixteenth Hall, and with the aid of dwarf and Elf alike, I am cataloguing my findings to report to Veúlfur of any significant movement in this area. If you are willing to aid in our vigil, I will be certain to mention your assistance in my report.
'There is much to be done. I suggest speaking to the others who aid me already. Each can be found here within the Shadowed Refuge. Lar, Ymar, and Odmar are the dwarves who mind the Sixteenth Hall, and the Elves are named Pentlenn and Glorelloth. When you have spoken to them and given them what they need, return to me with tidings.'

'This is ill news. The appearance of a nameless evil such as this beneath the Peasant Halls belies an even greater corruption of the Orcs than I foresaw.
'Your information gives us but a piece of the puzzle that is unfolding in depths. It is clear, though, that the curse-shouters here are working to infect other Orcs for some fell purpose. What it is, I cannot guess.
'Yet it is good to know that the disease is not something that can be passed easily among enemies of evil such as ourselves.'
Aid Glorelloth: collect fungus from the Sixteenth Hall
Aid Pentlenn: collect samples from the Sixteenth Hall
Complete Odmar's task in the Sixteenth Hall
Complete Ymar's task within the Sixteenth Hall
Complete Lar's task in the Sixteenth Hall
Return to Mallas at the Shadowed Refuge
Plague Wind
The Sixteenth Hall is an area overrun with Orcs, many of whom suffer from a terrible illness that causes fungus-like growths on their bodies.

'Would that we had greater numbers and were not daunted thus by the Sixteenth Hall. As such, however, we must rely on the assistance of others to learn what threat looms in the darkness.
'Speak with Odmar, Lar, Ymar, Pentlenn and Glorelloth in the Shadowed Refuge for instruction.'

The Watchers of the Sixteenth Hall are in the Shadowed Refuge in Moria. The Elves and dwarves you seek are named Lar, Ymar, Odmar, Pentlenn, and Glorelloth.
Mallas has asked you to help his fellows at the Shadowed Refuge do various tasks in the Sixteenth Hall.

The Elf Mallas is at the Shadowed Refuge.
You have completed the tasks set before you by the dwarves Ymar, Lar, and Odmar and the Elves Glorelloth and Pentlenn, and should now bring tidings to Mallas of all that has transpired.
Collected strips of infected flesh (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'I am hoping to assess the disease spreading throughout the Orcs within the Sixteenth Hall, but I dare not enter the Hall by myself, for I am no warrior.
'If you are willing, I would seek your aid. Acquire many samples of tissue from the Orcs to see how potent is their disease, and if it may be passed on to others.
'This will not be an easy task; you should do your best not to allow the infected Orcs to come into close contact with you, for they may be contagious. You will find the Sixteenth Hall to the north-east of the Shadowed Refuge. Collect the samples and return them to me when you are finished.'

'I will need time to study these samples, but you have served me well thus far. I will be sure to tell Mallas what you have done for me.
'I thank you, ${RACE}, and I am glad to find you hale after so risky a venture.'
'You will find the samples I need in the Sixteenth Hall, north-east of the Shadowed Refuge.'
Return the samples to Pentlenn at the Shadowed Refuge
Collect strips of infected flesh (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Infected Samples

The Sixteenth Hall is an area overrun with Orcs, many of whom suffer from a terrible illness that causes fungus-like growths on their bodies.
Mallas, an Elf ally to the dwarves, believes that there is something secret beneath the Sixteenth Hall and wishes to learn the true purpose and source of the plague.

The Sixteenth Hall can be found north-east of the Shadowed Refuge.
You should collect samples from defeated Orcs in the Sixteenth Hall to allow Pentlenn to observe the behaviour of this disease. He advised that you do your best to avoid becoming infected yourself.
Defeated crawlers (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Bless my beard! I am glad you are here. I made the mistake of seeing them, and now I can't get them out of my head! They are there when I close my eyes, infesting my nightmares, and every thing I see, I mistake for one of them! How my skin itches and crawls! They grow in the very bellies of their victims and spew forth to plague my sanity.
'I cannot go back into the Sixteenth Hall, for I do not wish to see the creeping crawlers again -- once was enough to do lasting damage! Call me a coward if you must. I will not go near that place as long as the crawlers are there.
'If Mallas sent you here to do my bidding, you will slay the crawlers to the slithering last. How I hate them! How the sight of them weakens my knees....'

'They are gone, all gone... good. I believe you, but I see them still. I wonder if this nightmare will ever cease.
'Why am I the only one to have these dreams and visions? I do not like it. Nonetheless, you have done me a great kindness, and I will tell Mallas of your worth.'

The Vile Infected

The Sixteenth Hall is an area overrun with Orcs, many of whom suffer from a terrible illness that causes fungus-like growths on their bodies.
Mallas, an Elf ally to the dwarves, believes that there is something secret beneath the Sixteenth Hall and wishes to learn the true purpose and source of the plague.
'The Sixteenth Hall is to the north-east of the Shadowed Refuge. Do not tarry!'

Crawlers can be found in the Sixteenth Hall, north-east of the Shadowed Refuge.
Ymar seems to be affected differently than all the others who keep watch at the Shadowed Refuge. He is haunted by visions of crawlers, and wishes you kill them while you are in the Sixteenth Hall.

Ymar is at the Shadowed Refuge, south-west of the Sixteenth Hall.
You have slain many, many vile crawlers and should inform Ymar that the nightmarish threat has passed.

'Your skill in battle cannot be denied, ${PLAYER}.

'For your second task, I want you to travel to Thorin's Hall. Ascend the steps toward Dwalin's throne and proclaim your prowess as a champion to all gathered in the halls of the dwarves!'

'Well done, ${PLAYER}. Your skill in battle has lived up to your reputation.

'Well done, ${PLAYER}. I have no doubt that your deeds will live on long after your spirit has departed from Middle-earth.

'You have done well to have come this far, ${PLAYER}, and have humbled me in the meantime. Now, let us see to our final preparations before we send you off to face one of Moria's oldest nightmares.
'The glands of crawlers that slither throughout the Water Works give off a strange scent that has been known to draw attention from the enemy, as one poor dwarf of the expedition was unlucky as to discover. If you wish to ensnare the ancient creature, the heads you acquired for me earlier will need the addition of the glands from these glowing crawlers.
'Go now to the Water Works and slay the glowing crawlers that infest that place. When you have acquired enough, return to me quickly and we will see to your final preparations.'

'Disgusting, you say? I never said that handling anything from the old roots of the earth would smell of daisies. If you wish to work with more pleasant odours, go deal with the Elves! Maybe an Elf-maid will need assistance in finding a favourite flower.
'Nay, such work is not for you or me. We are Guardians, hearty and true. We fear no darkness and turn our noses from no sickly smells, not when there are walls that stand or good folk in peril. Let us hurry now, before these lose their potency....'
'Be sure to bring me plenty of glands from the crawlers that infest the Water Works. Without them, our bait is incomplete.'

'I cannot wait to discover this new map's secret! It looks as though it may show a destination to the south-east of here. Were I you, I would search within Nud-melek -- let's see, you said it curved downwards... perhaps the southern section of the Second Hall?'

'Amazing, you found it! Now that we know where it is, getting there again will be much quicker.
'You may wish to bring a friend or two if you are going to plumb the secrets of this chamber. Who knows what dangers may lie within?
'I suspect the strange riddles on the back of this map will help you in this last exploration. I will make you a fair copy of them, so you can bring them into the chamber with you.'

'Can it be? You are the one? The axe you describe is known to me, but only in legend. It was prophesied that one not of our number -- the nearly forgotten secret council of Elves and dwarves -- would find it once more, within our ancient headquarters in the deepest recesses of the dwarf-mine.
'That map you found was a last desperate attempt to leave a record, should Dragonslayer's hiding place be forgotten -- a situation thought impossible then, but we did not forsee the rise of Durin's Bane, the abandonment of Khazad-dûm, and its degeneration into feared Moria. When Smaug was terrorizing the Lonely Mountain, some of us were instructed to search for records of where Dragonslayer might be hid and found nothing.
'You, brave ${RACE}, have discovered a treasure beyond compare. Lord Elrond shall be alerted, as well as Lady Galadriel... your name will be sung by council-members for Ages to come.'

'Bless my sturdy boots, what a tale! Clues and maps and shadows and riddles and monsters -- this will make quite the story to tell in my old age!
'So you found the innermost chamber of this strange place.... What did you find there? An axe? An axe marked \qDragonslayer\q? Durin's beard!
'${PLAYER}, I think there is more to this than meets the eye. I am loth to give this advice, but I think you ought to speak to one of the Elves here in Moria -- I think Lenglammel might be the one to ask, but you'll have to go down to the Shadowed Refuge to find her. Describe your travails, and what you found at your destination, and see what she has to say.'

'I can teach you more about the relationship between runes and the natural world, ${PLAYER}, but it may not be an easy lesson.
'Consider the fury of a storm in the mountains: it fumes and roils, full of wrath. Now think on the rune that describes the storm. Does it capture the meaning of the storm? Its anger, or its motion?
'Let the storm inscribe its power on the runes that describe it, ${PLAYER}. You must come with me if you are to learn this lesson. Speak with me when you are ready.'

'You saw the markings the lightning left on the rune-stones, ${PLAYER}; I cannot explain them, except to say that the words we use to describe certain events, and the runes we use to describe those words, did not arise by accident.
'There is power in even the smallest of words, even such power as you beheld in the clouds of the storm atop Amon Sul.
'You will be more adept at wielding this power in the future, ${PLAYER}. Indeed, you are better at it already, though you may not have observed this to be so!'

'Be wary, for I have seen evidence of Orcs prowling in these parts of late.'
'Are you ready to go, ${PLAYER}? Let us remove ourselves from the storm.'

'You have done well, ${PLAYER}: not only to fulfill my instructions, but also in dispatching the Orcs!

'The rumours were true, ${PLAYER}: you are certainly a highly-skilled Warden and deserve every measure of the reputation you are earning!
'I would place the safety and well-being of my friends in your care at a moment's notice, if there was such a need.
'I thank you again, ${PLAYER}.'

Warden: Watching the Marches
Your spear-arm is strong and your heart is stout. With your like watching over the marches of Middle-earth, the forces of the Enemy shudder with dread.

'So, ${PLAYER}, you think there are things I can teach you? Yes, I have heard of you. All of us who range the wilds of Eriador, be we Elf or Dúnadan or Eglan, have heard the tales. And yet you have sought me out, so what am I to do with you?
'I am no sage, hiding in some old broken skull of a keep, speaking riddles to all who cross my threshold, and you are not the first warrior to ask me my secrets.'

Hrotha is in Ost Guruth in the Lone-lands.
You have been told to speak with Hrotha, a Warden of great fame and skill.

'The secrets of our trade hark back to Daeron and Fëanor themselves, but both Elves and dwarves have added much to the depth of our craft. Many ancient secrets of the written word lie hidden in the forgotten places of Middle-earth.
'The road ahead is hard, but what thing that is worth doing is not? The gaining of wisdom is ever a struggle, but it is a fulfilling one. If you believe you are ready, then say on, and I will set your feet upon the path to greater knowledge.'

'Great is your skill with runes, ${PLAYER}. Seldom have I met one with a deeper understanding of their mysteries. And yet, can we not all learn new things, no matter how wise we may be?
'Little need be said of Elrond Halfelven. His knowledge is as broad as the Sundering Sea and deep as the pools of Celebrant. The runes are not strange to him, for he has studied them since the Elder Days.
'Go to him, ${PLAYER}, and seek his guidance. His wisdom will shed light where all is in gloom.'

'Mae govannen, ${PLAYER}, Elf-friend. It is ever a joy to meet one who studies the crafts of old, for such lore is fading in the world, and I fear will soon be lost on this side of the Sea. For three Ages now I have watched as the Rune-keepers of my youth dwindled in number. It gladdens my heart to meet one who studies them anew.
'Know, then, that the Angerthas and the Tengwar do not give up their secrets lightly. Long study awaits you, great though your power may be. Do not take the easy path of wresting the power from the runes, but consider each, both alone and in the company of other letters. I have pored over ancient tomes since the ink was fresh upon their pages, and yet I still do not know their full meaning. Each time, there is something new to be learned.
'Patience is the key... a patience that Men cannot know, and that will vanish from Middle-earth when the Elves and dwarves are gone, for the Dúnedain shall become as other Men. A light will go out of the world then, but if you treat the runes with care, ${PLAYER}, it will burn yet a while longer.'

'Oft of old I studied with Elrond, and each time was like the rising of the sun. My mind is to his as a spring's trickle is to the torrents of Bruinen. There is no better place to learn the worth of runes than by his side.
'How I envy you the chance to go to Rivendell and hear the wisdom he speaks, one more time. Ah, but my place is here now, and I fear I shall see Rivendell nevermore.'

'We rune-keepers are not a vain lot, ${PLAYER}. You and I both know that knowledge is a treasure of the mind, not of our garments. Still, it is also true that others do not give us our due respect if we do not garb ourselves as they wish to see us. Such is the way of the unenlightened.
'Now is the time for you to gain the attire that will win that respect. Seek out the materials I need, and I will make for you such equipment that befits a rune-keeper.
'First, I will need the vines that grow through the hides of the creatures which lurk in Glâd Ereg in Eregion and the hide of the cold-worm Helchuan, who dwells in Forochel. May your way be a safe one, ${PLAYER}.'

'Very good, ${PLAYER}. These are a fine beginning. Now you must fetch the second set of items, as soon as you can.
'These include the paws of the barghests which prowl Fornost in the North Downs and Haudh Iarchith in Bree-land and the corrosive droplets of the brimstone-leeches of Angmar.'
'I am still waiting for the first set of items, ${PLAYER}.

'So, ${PLAYER}, we have two sets of the necessary items. Now only the third remains, and your garment shall be complete. Go now and finish your labours.
'I need now a Badge of Command from the uruk Lagmâs at Urugarth and a horn from the Gorthorog Târlug at Carn Dûm.'
'Without the proper materials, I cannot complete your garment, ${PLAYER}.'
'This is the last of it, ${PLAYER}. Your task has been long, but now your garment is complete. Wear it well, and all shall know that you are a keeper of runes.'
'Without the last set of items, I cannot complete garment, ${PLAYER}.'

'The time has come for you to delve into the deeper secrets of rune-craft, ${PLAYER}. As with the runes themselves, the stones upon which they are graven are key to their power.
'Just as a warrior needs a sword of fine steel, so too do we need rune-stones to accompany our gifts. It is in the shaping of your stone that you will achieve wisdom.
'Here is my counsel on what materials will aid you for shaping your stone. First, bring me stone from the Misty Mountains, oft carried by the goblins there, and runes from the foul sorcerer Ánraig at Annúminas. Make haste, ${PLAYER}, if you wish to bear your weapon soon!'

'I will prepare the stone while you go forth and seek the second set of items. Among them are the horns of the nerbeglir of Angmar and claws from the Wargs which can be found in Angmar, Forochel, and the Misty Mountains.'
'I am still waiting for the first set of items, ${PLAYER}.'

'Well done, ${PLAYER}. You prove your worth again and again.
'One set of components remains before your stone is complete. Follow the counsel I gave you, and though the path you walk may be dire, the reward at its end shall be great.
'Find for me a Sigil of War, borne by Gruglok in Urugarth, and a Rune of Winged Dominance from Mormoz and Azgoth in Carn Dûm.'
'Your rune-stone will not be complete unless you bring me the proper components, ${PLAYER}.'

'Most impressive, ${PLAYER}. Your rune-stone is nearly complete. These items will seal its power just so.
'There. All is well. Accept this rune-stone, ${PLAYER}, and use its secrets well. The greatest craft of the Rune-keepers of old rests in your hands.'
'Without the last set of items, I cannot complete your rune-stone, ${PLAYER}.'

'A good spear may be a Warden's best ally, ${PLAYER}, but what good will it do when an Orc-archer riddles you with arrows? Or some warrior from Angmar puts a sword in your guts? Answer that, if you can. You will need some fine gear if you are going to face the greater threats in this world.
'If you're up to the task, I will guide you as you collect the items necessary to craft items of worth to one such as you. Bring me the components I need, ${PLAYER}, and we will see about making such items of virtue as would be of benefit to you.
'The first items I will need are hides from the hoary-aurochs which dwell in the Misty Mountains and the hide of the boar Redtusk, who roams the hills of Eregion.'

'Well, that is a beginning, ${PLAYER}. I will get these hides tanned and boiled, and you go get the next items on the list while I stitch them together.
'I now require the barbed tails of the barghests of Imlad Balchorth and the spinnerets of the spiders of Angmar.'
'You waste my time, ${PLAYER}. Do not trouble me until you have what I told you to gather.'

'Two batches out of three...the end of this work is in sight now, ${PLAYER}. This last bit will be the hardest, though.
'Bring me a Rune of Evil Presence from the sorcerer Sálvakh at Carn Dûm and the teeth of a Gorthorog...perhaps from Dushkâl, Brízrip, or Thordragh at Urugarth.'
'I have a heap of hides waiting, ${PLAYER}. Why are you here without the remaining items?'
'Ah, and now our work is done, ${PLAYER}. Take this gear and let it protect you from the worst the Enemy has to send against you. May it serve you well, friend.'
'So close to done, ${PLAYER}, and yet you seem confused. Find the last set of items!'

'And to that, I will tell you as I have told the others: I know no secrets, or none that could be called wisdom. I trust my spear and my arm, my corselet and the strength of my heart. And perhaps that is the greatest lesson of our kind, to trust in yourself, the weapon you wield, and the armour you wear.
'Very well, then. That is where we shall begin, if you want. I will see you properly armed, and we will call that a kind of wisdom.'

'You have proven yourself, ${PLAYER}. I doubted the tales folk told about you when first I heard them, but now I am sure they are all true...or as close to true as a minstrel can manage.
'Now it is time for you to seek out one who knows more than any of us of the skills of the Warden. He may not be one of us, but he has fought alongside us many times, for longer than I have been alive. Some in Bree call him Strider, but his true name is Aragorn son of Arathorn.
'Aragorn is a wanderer by nature, but great deeds are in the offing, and I think you should be able to find him where the Wise gather. Find him, ${PLAYER}, and give him my regards.'

'We are well met, ${PLAYER}. I should be troubled that you have found me so easily in these times, but if you bear greetings from Hrotha, I know your intent cannot be ill. He is a great Warden, and if he thinks well of you, then I do as well, for he does not give his friendship lightly.
'Courage is the greatest virtue of our kind, ${PLAYER}. All else may fail us, but never our bravery. We are the bulwark between the darkness of the world and those who could not bear to behold it. Without stout hearts, even in the face of death, we cannot hope to prevail against our foes. So your spear may fail you, and yes, your habergeon as well, but your spirit must never flag. This is the greatest lesson I have learned, through all my long years and travels.
'This, then, is my word, ${PLAYER}: go always with valour, and always remember that you must protect all who need it.'

'Aragorn has had many haunts, though his true home is the wild. Often he dwells among the Dúnedain of Esteldín, though he has not been seen there in many months, if the word I hear is true.
'Bree, too, has seen the back of him for some time, from what folk say. That fool Bill Ferny would not speak ill of him quite so much, if he thought \qStrider\q might return.
'If I were to guess, I would suspect him to be involved in all the goings-on at Rivendell. But if he is there, it is surely in secret, so tell no one.'
