'So, the spear...your weapons are good enough for a vagabond warrior, but we wardens deserve the finest of spears, do we not, ${PLAYER}? Yes, I believe we do. Otherwise we might as well be Dunlending rabble jabbing at things with pointed sticks!
'Then let us make one for you, shall we? Yes, a spear that befits someone of your repute. Then the minstrels might sing about it as well as you!
'It means work for you, of course. I cannot do it all myself, after all, and nor should I! Bring me the breastplates of the Angmarim who swarm upon Annúminas and the spear of the Gauradan Bryok in Forochel. Go on now, ${PLAYER}...the Enemy will not wait while you dawdle!'

'Ah! This is good. This spear will do more good in your hands than it did in Bryok's, we can be sure of that.
'Let me get started, then. No sense dallying, is there, ${PLAYER}? You go find the next items and bring them back to me when you have them.
'I now need remains from the wights that roam Angmar, Forochel, Annúminas, or Helegrod and the gem-crusted claws of the cave-claws of Angmar and Sarnur.'
'I do not see the items I asked for, ${PLAYER}.'

'You have returned? You have much resolve, ${PLAYER}. Many folk would have balked, but then that is what sets us apart, is it not?
'All right, then. Just one more set of items, and the spear will be yours. Bring to me a blood-stained tally-stick from the Orcs Gríshakrum, Kughûrz, and Dafrim in Urugarth and the crimson horn of the Gorthorog Barashal, who dwells in Carn Dûm.'
'This spear will not be much good unless you bring me what I asked for, ${PLAYER}.'

'That is it, then! A lot of toil for one weapon, but all the great arms of legend took much sweat and blood before they were ready.
'Here is your spear, as I promised. It is yours now, so use it well. I suppose it will not truly be finished until it has been bathed in Orc-blood, will it, ${PLAYER}?'
'${PLAYER}! What are you doing back here without those last items?'

'Your skill in battle cannot be denied, ${PLAYER}.
'The difference between a good champion and a great one, however, is their renown. The peoples of Middle-earth need to know that there are warriors in the world capable of incredible martial prowess, risking their lives to fight the Enemy.
'For your second task, I want you to travel to Thorin's Hall. Ascend the steps toward Dwalin's throne and blow this horn, then proclaim your prowess as a champion to all gathered in the halls of the dwarves!'

'Well done, well done!
'Now, ${PLAYER}, for your next task.'

Thrymur is near Dwalin's throne in Thorin's Hall.
Speak with him now that you have proclaimed your deeds to all assembled in Thorin's Hall.

Valthor is at the Shadowed Refuge in the Foundations of Stone in Moria, far to the east of Thorin's Hall.
Now that you have boasted to the dwarves, return to Valthor.

'You have collected all the materials, and I have assembled the torch this map calls for -- now it is time to see what we shall do with it!
'A lit torch is a fit weapon against few creatures; I suggest you find an ally, perhaps two, in case you have to move around while the torch is lit. While you are looking for the help, I will just send a runner to bring the unlit torch into the cave described in the map.
'Speak to me again once you are ready to leave.'

'Another map? Are you sure?
'My curiosity burns within me! Will you follow this strange story to the end?'
Talk to Geirfast at the Twenty-first Hall
Talk to Geirfast at the Twenty-first Hall
Flame and Shadow
Geirfast has identified the small cave described in the map and will send the wondrous torch you have assembled to it while you find an ally or two.

'You are prepared to go? I hope you have some help...
'I sent that runner, as promised -- he returned to say that he was barely able to stick his head into the cave before he was blasted with a pygmy drake's fire-breath! He dropped the torch and legged it back here with some alacrity. So be ready!'

Geirfast is in the Twenty-first Hall.
You should speak with Geirfast again when you are prepared to travel to the strange cave.

Geirfast is at the Twenty-first Hall.
You should return to Geirfast and tell him of the strange map you saw projected on the wall by the light of the torch.
Hadi has told you of a location where you might spy on Bogrian's scouts

'We have done our best to keep watch throughout this cavern, and have been learning more about Bogrian and her maidens.
'Hadi overheard some of the merrevail talking, and a few key phrases piqued my interest. Will you speak to him and find out what he knows?'
'Their queen wants to flee to the Mirror-Halls in Zirakzigil? Durin's beard!'

'It is true that I overheard some of Bogrian's tribe speaking of her whereabouts, but before I could learn her location I was spotted and I fled. I have not the courage to go back. You will need to spy on some of her scouts, yourself, to find out what is truly going on.
'Head north out of camp, then bear east and hug the cliff-face. The scouts have a meeting-place just south of the entrance to Tith-maudhul. Once you've overheard a little of their conversation, defeat them -- the fewer scouts their queen has, the better for us!'
Speak to Hadi to find out what he knows
Spy upon and defeat two scouts (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Folkath at his camp in the Fanged Pit
Bogrian's Curiosity
The morroval-queen, Bogrian, has fled into hiding. Folkath and the others have begun investigating where she may next appear.
'Seek out Bogrian's scouts and learn what you may from them. The merrevail roost at the just north of our encampment.'

Hadi resides in camp with Folkath at the west edge of the Fanged Pit.
Folkath recommends that you question Hadi about what he has learned of Bogrian's clan.
Seek out the scouts at their habitual meeting-place, south of the entrance to Tith-maudhul, and try to overhear their conversation before you defeat them.

Folkath is at the camp on the west edge of the Fanged Pit.
You should return to Folkath with news of your success.
Defeated Bogrian's morroval-guards (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeated Bogrian's morvul-defilers (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
You have used the horn to summon Bogrian, the merrevail queen
Bogrian has fallen before you

'Bogrian, the morroval-queen called She-Who-Must-Be-Obeyed by her subjects, has fled with a small, but dangerous detachment of her personal morroval-guards and morvul-defilers to Zirakzigil.
'It would seem that she has commanded them to guide her to the entrance of the great Mirror-halls of Lumul-nar, in the hopes of forging an alliance with the merrevail who reside there. We cannot allow that expedition to succeed.
'Best of luck, my brave ${RACE}. If you manage to stop Bogrian, report to Oxi at Jazârgund. Do you know the way to Zirakzigil? It is far to the west of here, beyond the gardens of Tharâkh Bazân -- it is quite some distance on foot, but I will allow you to use my goat to travel there quickly.'

'You have thwarted the will of the winged queen! For this great deed, I will ensure that your name is recorded alongside those of the brave dwarves who have distinguished themselves through their acts of valour here in Khazad-dûm.
'Please, accept my thanks and this reward.'
Defeat Bogrian's morroval-guards (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeat Bogrian's morvul-defilers (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Use the horn on Bogrian's banner to summon and defeat her
Talk to Oxi at Jazârgund
Death to the Maidens
Bogrian has fled to Zirakzigil with a detachment of her personal guards to search for the entrance to the Mirror-halls of Lumul-nar.

'You must think like your enemy, ${PLAYER}! If I have taught you nothing else, I hope you have learned that. What I mean is, these creatures will have taken the high ground, where they will be least vulnerable. I would begin my search at the peak and move down.
'You may use my goat to travel with haste to Zirakzigil, free of charge. May she carry you swiftly.'

The passage to Zirakzigil lies west through the gardens, then north.
Folkath has instructed you to prevent Bogrian's expedition from bringing back any potentially valuable or dangerous trophies from the Balrog's remains.

Bogrian's banner is located among the merrevail detachment on Zirakzigil.
Bogrian may be called out of hiding by using the horns on her banner to summon her forth.

Oxi is at Jazârgund, south and east of the entrance to Zirakzigil.
Oxi is awaiting your return and hoping for your success.

'Welcome to Moria, ${PLAYER}. You join us at a momentous time! I am the master of the expedition group here at Durin's Threshold. Other expedition groups have already moved further on into the depths of Khazad-dûm, hoping to find Balin's expedition of some years ago and learn of their fate.
'My fellow dwarves are having a difficult time settling in, for a number of reasons. If you could assist them, I would be most grateful.'
'Thank you for all that you've done, ${PLAYER}. We are certainly off to a better start here now.'
Assist Gamli
Assist Ráthulf
Assist Athils
Speak with Thormóth
Welcome to Moria
Thormóth, leader of the dwarf-expedition group that holds Durin's Threshold, has asked you to help his folk get settled after the ordeal at the gate.
'You should speak with Gamli, Ráthulf, and Athils, here in Durin's Threshold.'

Gamli and Ráthulf are in Durin's Threshold. Athils is in the North Wing of Durin's Threshold: up the stairs, to the north, and then west.
Thormóth has asked you to speak with some of the dwarves who are having difficulty in settling Durin's Threshold.

Thormóth is in Durin's Threshold.
Having lent a helping hand at this first expedition site, you should now return to its leader.

'You have done all that is needed for our little camp, ${PLAYER}, and we appreciate your help! But I expect you are excited to delve further into Moria, as we are.
'The Dolven-view camp is the central camp of the dwarves in the Great Delving. I expect that several dwarves will have settled there, and established many useful town services.'

'Greetings, my good ${RACE}, and welcome to the Dolven-view! 'Tis a fine view indeed -- or at least it would be were it not cluttered with the cook-fires of a goblin horde beneath us....
'No matter. We will defend the Dolven-view at all costs, and find some way to drive these vermin from our ancestral homes. Mark my words ${PLAYER}, this will once again be a city of wonder and beautiful to behold, though we give our lives to achieve it!'
Talk to Slagvi at the Dolven-view
To the Dolven-view
Thórhall has encouraged you to head east to the Dolven-view camp, the central hub of the dwarves in the Great Delving.
'Are you not excited to press further into Moria? We certainly are.'

The Dolven-view camp lies east of Lamab-dûm, at a somewhat central cross-roads in the Great Delving.
You should follow the lit road as best you can to the Dolven-view.

'Interested in taking a look at the true Mines of Moria now, are you? I can't blame you, for tales speak of their wonder and beauty!
'What I wouldn't give to have gone with the dwarves who went to the Silvertine Lodes... but I have a job here, and I mean to do it!
'Take the south path from the Dolven-view and you will find yourself at the Deep Descent in no time -- it is really quite close. You might be able to help the dwarves there quite as much as you helped us!'

'Welcome to the Deep Descent, ${PLAYER}! We miners have great hopes for the Silvertine Lodes.
'Are you here to look for ways to be of use? Never fret... there is more to be done here than we can handle!'
Talk to Thettmárr at the Deep Descent
To the Deep Descent
There is much work to be done for the Longbeards to reclaim their ancient home of Moria.
'You should speak with Thettmárr at the Deep Descent encampment as soon as you feel ready to take your leave.'

The Deep Descent is along the south path from the Dolven-view, at the north edge of the Silvertine Lodes.
You should take the path south to discover the dwarf-hub at the Deep Descent.

'You have done more than we could ever have hoped in the Silvertine Lodes, so it is time to send you back to the upper levels to help out in Durin's Way. You should make for the Chamber of the Cross-roads, which lies to the north of the Great Delving.
'Give my greetings to Líkmund when you get there, if he's still breathing.'

'Thettmárr sent you to check up on us, did he? More like he sent you to check up on ME.
'I still owe him a hefty gambling debt from our last outing together, and I'm betting he wants to make sure I live long enough to make good on it.
'Well, we could use the extra hands anyway, so you're welcome to stay if you have a pair of them to lend to our efforts!'
Speak with Líkmund
To the Chamber of the Cross-roads
Thettmárr has asked you to check on the progress of the dwarf-expedition at the Chamber of the Cross-roads, in Durin's Way. Once there, you should speak with Líkmund.
'Líkmund is with the expedition at the Chamber of the Cross-roads in Durin's Way. You should speak with him as soon as possible.'

To reach the Chamber of the Cross-roads, head north from the Deep Descent to the Dolven-view camp. From the Dolven-view, follow your map and the main lit roadway towards the Chamber of the Cross-roads.
The strange light of the torch has projected a map onto the wall
Pick up the torch
Instance: Flame and Shadow

Geirfast recommends bringing an ally or two along for the lighting and placing of the torch.
He left the torch just inside the entrance of the cave described in the strange map, which contains esoteric instructions for its lighting.
Bring the torch to wherever it needs to be, further within the little cave.
Found the dwelling place of the Swamped One
Defeated the Swamped One

'It is good that Sadreda sent you, ${PLAYER}. I have need of a strong warden such as yourself.
'To the south of here lies the swamp of Harloeg. I believe you may be familiar with its denizens already?
'I have heard rumours from frightened adventurers of a nameless creature of horror down there. Apparently, it can be found by venturing near an old altar in the ruins of Harloeg. Go and confront this creature, then return to me.'

'Well done, ${PLAYER}! Sadreda's faith in you was well placed. Wardens such as yourself will always be welcome here where the good people of Middle-earth dwell.
'You have my thanks, and the thanks of the others here at Ost Guruth, ${PLAYER}.
'There is one last task I will ask of you before you return to Sadreda.'
Find the dwelling place of the Swamped One
Defeat the Swamped One
Return to Mosco Mudbottom
Along the Watch-tower
Musco Mudbottom is concerned with the defence of Ost Guruth and has asked you to investigate rumours of a foul creature to the south.
'The Swamped One may be found in the ruins of Harloeg.'

The Swamped One can be found in the ruins of Harloeg, south-east of Ost Guruth.
Mosco Mudbottom has asked you to deal with a Nameless creature that is rumoured to be lurking in southern Harloeg. Mosco mentioned that the Nameless will likely be near an old stone altar.

Mosco Mudbottom is at Ost Guruth, north-west of Harloeg.
Now that you have confronted and slain the Swamped One, return to Mosco Mudbottom and tell him of your success.
Complete the deed \qDens of the Beasts\q
Complete the deed \qThe Ruins of Eregion\q
Talk to Tinúriel at Echad Dúnann

'Hail, ${PLAYER}. Have you seen much of the Eregion? It has much changed since Elves lived here, and there is little of the Elves left here. I have spent much time learning these changes, so that we can move quickly here to Echad Dúnann unseen by the eyes of the Enemy.
'If you would seek to learn these paths, I would share such knowledge with you. First, though, you must explore Eregion. Many of the landmarks and points I reference would be useless to you unless you saw them first with your own eyes.
'Go and explore Eregion. Once you have done so, return to me, and I shall share with you my knowledge of the secret way to Echad Dúnann.'
Hunter: Lay of the Land
You have been encouraged to learn the hidden tracks and paths of Eregion so that you may travel there more quickly.
'I can see that you have not yet fully explored Eregion. You must do this first, otherwise my instruction on the hidden path to Echad Dúnann would be useless to you.'

'You have explored Eregion, ${PLAYER}? This is good. These lands are much changed, and there is little of the land that remembers the Elves. Even though we camp here now on an errand for Master Elrond, we soon will be gone, and I fear the land will forget us completely.
'However, those are matters for another day. For now, Elves walk these lands and our knowledge can hamper the efforts of the Enemy. Here, ${PLAYER}, take this guide and learn from it. Use such knowledge well.'

Explore the Elf ruins and dens of the beasts found in Eregion.
Tinúriel told you that for you to learn the quickest route to Echad Dúnann in Eregion, you must explore the land and learn its hidden tracks and paths.

Tinúriel is at Echad Dúnann in Eregion.
Now that you have explored Eregion and become familiar with its ruins and the dens of the beasts here, you will be able to understand Tinúriel's instruction on the secret way to Echad Dúnann.

You are not sure where this coin came from, but it seems to be a relic from Khazad-dûm, called Moria by the Elves. There are many who would be interested in such a relic and would likely provide you with a great reward!
<rgb=#FF0000>Bring this coin to any of the following people to receive your reward: • Jon Brackenbrook in Archet • Dwalin in Thorin's Hall • Mayor Will Whitfoot in Michel Delving • Barliman Butterbur in Bree-town • Cardavor in Celondim</rgb>

'What do you have here? A coin of some sort? Doesn't look like much... and what's this, some sort of doors on the back? What a queer coin you've brought me!
'I suppose it is worth something, although surely not much. Perhaps Keeper Foxtail would like to put it on display in the Mathom House.
'Yes, that should be fine. Here, choose something that you feel is appropriate for a coin such as this.'
'Hmm? Do you need something?'

'A dwarf-coin of some sort, is it not? I have heard of such things, but I never thought to see one. Where did you come across it?
'I would gladly give you something in trade for this coin. Choose what you would like, and we shall finish our trade.'
'Hello, can I help you?'

'A dwarf-coin of some sort, is it not? I have heard of such things, but I never thought to see one. Where did you come across it?
'I would gladly give you something in trade for this coin. Choose what you would like, and we shall finish our trade.'
'Hello, can I help you?'

'I cannot believe it! It is an ithildín coin! It is said that many were minted to commemorate the friendship of the Elves of Hollin and the Dwarves of Khazad-dûm. Most were lost... where did you come across such a treasure?
'Please, friend, trade this coin with me. I have many things to offer in trade. Choose something you think appropriate!'
'Greetings. Is there something you seek from me?'
Turn in your ithildín coin to receive your reward
Ithildín Coin

You have found a mysterious coin inlaid with ithildín. This rare metal was made by the Elves from mithril long ago. The image of the Doors of Durin, the doors that guarded the West Gate of Moria, is found on one side of the coin, while the other has the image of a hammer and anvil, the signs of Durin.

'I cannot believe it! It is an ithildín coin! It is said that many were minted to commemorate the friendship of the Elves of Hollin and the Dwarves of Khazad-dûm. Most were lost... where did you come across such a treasure?
'Please, friend, trade this coin with me. I have many things to offer in trade. Choose something you think appropriate!'
'Greetings. Is there something you seek from me?'

'Barliman Butterbur at your service, friend! That's quite a strange coin you've got there! Looks like a dwarf-coin of some sort... I've seen a few from guests, mind you, but not one like this. Not sure even what it's made of!
'Well, not sure I would take it for a meal or a room, but it probably has some value to someone... if only as something interesting to talk over!
'I will offer you a trade. I've a number of things travellers have left behind. You can trade this coin for one of those. How's that sound?'
'Hmm? What can I do for you?'

'Hail, friend. I see you have found an ithildín coin. These coins were minted by the Dwarves of Moria in the days of their friendship with the Elves of Eregion. See here, engraved here are the Doors of Durin, which were inlaid with this same metal.
'Most of these coins were lost when Moria fell into darkness. If you would have it, I would like to keep this coin. It can serve as a good reminder in these dark times of the fellowship that can exist between dwarves and Elves.
'However, I would not ask you to go away empty-handed. Choose something you find acceptable, and we shall make our exchange.'
'Hail, friend. Is there something that you need?'

'I cannot believe it! It is an ithildín coin! It is said that many were minted to commemorate the friendship of the Elves of Hollin and the Dwarves of Khazad-dûm. Most were lost... where did you come across such a treasure?
'Please, friend, trade this coin with me. I have many things to offer in trade. Choose something you think appropriate!'
'Greetings. Is there something that you need?'

Bring your ithildín coin to one of the following people to receive a reward.
• Jon Brackenbrook in Archet • Dwalin in Thorin's Hall • Mayor Will Whitfoot in Michel Delving • Barliman Butterbur in Bree-town • Cardavor in Celondim

'You have done much for the Iron Garrison here in Moria, ${PLAYER}, and I know that you will do even more in the future. There is value in remembering deeds done, for they shape us and can affect successes to come.
'Do you remember the watery darkness of Ghân-gharâf? Into the depths with Bori you travelled, seeking the mithril axe Zigilburk; find it you did, and more beside: Bróin, taken from before the Doors of Durin!
'Peer into the Reflecting Pool and experience this memory anew, ${PLAYER}. You will find that recalling your past may do you some good in the present.'

'The tale of your deeds grows ever longer and more full of glory, ${PLAYER}, and your assistance during the great battles of Moria must surely be one of the most notable!
'Your aid proved invaluable during the Battle of the Deep-way, friend ${CLASS}, when hope seemed to be lost. But it was not so, and you helped the defenders to carry the day!
'If ever you wish to revisit the desperation and horror of that battle, you should peer into the Reflecting Pool. War with the Orcs is dangerous and difficult, but there is honour and glory to be had there too.'
'I am happy that you have revisited your defence of the Deep-way, ${PLAYER}. Only by studying our past can we gain knowledge to aid our future.'

'We dare not approach our old camp until we find some way to defeat the creature in the Black Pool, ${PLAYER}. I cannot let you pass.
'A number of dwarves of our expedition are resting at Echad Dúnann, just to the west. Speak to Hundi there; he was instrumental in uncovering the cache of weapons of which I spoke.'

'Ráthwald is right, my friend. Without a truly magnificent weapon forged in the ways of Old, we cannot hope to so much as score the flesh of that ancient creature.
'But legends of the past sometimes turn up when least expected. My friends and I found a cache of ancient weapons not long after the Iron Garrison came to this place. Select one of these weapons, and it may be that your choice will help us clear the way into Moria of that terrible creature.
'Take too this tracery to engrave upon your weapon, for I know of one who can help you understand the uses of these ancient relics.'

'Hundi is at Echad Dúnann, the camp just to the west there. Speak to him about the cache of weapons his team recovered from one of the caves of Eregion.'

Hundi is at Echad Dúnann, not far to the west of Ráthwald, in Eregion.
Ráthwald has asked you to speak to his friend Hundi, who aided in the recovery of a cache of weapons that may prove useful.

'We dare not approach our old camp until we find some way to defeat the creature in the Black Pool, ${PLAYER}. I cannot let you pass.
'A number of dwarves of our expedition are resting at Echad Dúnann, just to the west. Speak to Hundi there; he was instrumental in uncovering the cache of weapons of which I spoke.'

'Ráthwald is right, my friend. Without a truly magnificent weapon forged in the ways of Old, we cannot hope to so much as score the flesh of that ancient creature.
'But legends of the past sometimes turn up when least expected. My friends and I found a cache of ancient weapons not long after the Iron Garrison came to this place. Select one of these weapons, and it may be that your choice will help us clear the way into Moria of that terrible creature.
'Take too this tracery to engrave upon your weapon, for I know of one who can help you understand the uses of these ancient relics.'

'Hail, friend. Wardens such as myself strive to scour evil from our homelands wherever we may find it and wherever we may call home.

'Many young rune-keepers are seeking this fell spirit, but I doubt any would succeed alone. They will need your help.
'If you are willing, enter the Sixteenth Hall and aid a rune-keeper in this task. Return to me when you have succeeded, and I will reward you.'

'While performing the sombre task of cleaning Laerdan's chambers once and for all, I uncovered a note from Laerdan made out to you, ${PLAYER}, along with a parcel that he left behind. Master Elrond bade me hold these items in my keeping in hopes that you would return.'

'My heart goes out to Laerdan, ${PLAYER}; his was a sad story. I know, as does he, that you did everything for him that you could.
'This parcel is yours, as he wished it to be.'
Read Laerdan's note
Volume I, Epilogue -- Laerdan's Parcel
A parcel has been found addressed to you in Laerdan's old room.
'You should read the note from Laerdan I have given you, ${PLAYER}.'
'You have played a major part in the war against Angmar, now we must turn our attention to the War against the Dark Lord.'
'It is a sad duty I have....'

You should read Laerdan's note before opening the parcel he left for you.
You spoke to Failloth in Rivendell and learned that Laerdan had left a note and a parcel behind for you in his room.

Failloth is in the courtyard of the Last Homely House, in Rivendell.
You have read Laerdan's note and should speak now to Failloth.

'This may be the most difficult part of your passage to the Chamber of the Cross-roads, ${PLAYER}, because it is so dark.
'You want to travel north-east through the darkness, following the sloping paths as they descend to buildings made by the ancient dwarves.'

'You are looking for the Chamber of the Cross-roads? Well, you should start out by heading north from here.
'Wait! Hold on a moment! There's a great fissure in the floor just to the north! Be careful as you go -- you can skirt it on the left, but only if you pay attention and see it!'

'Do you see the large structure to the east there? The camp known as the Dolven-view is built atop that large building. The road to the Deep Descent runs south from the Dolven-view, passing into the Silvertine Lodes.
'Wait! You cannot get atop the Dolven-view from here. Travel north, watching out for great fissures in the road, until you find another guide. He will show you the winding path up to the Dolven-view.'
'You are looking for the Chamber of the Cross-roads? You want to head east of here to the Palace of Náin. Watch out for the great fissure in the path, and make your way around it on the left!'

'Do you see the paths to the east of here? If you take the southern path upward and follow the winding road at the top, you will come to the Dolven-view. The Deep Descent is among the Silvertine Lodes, south of the Dolven-view.
'Wait! Be careful! There is a great fissure in the road just to the east. You will need to step carefully around it.'

'You are getting nearer to the Chamber of the Cross-roads, ${PLAYER}. Climb this path and pass north through the Palace of Náin. Your road will then bend to the east, where you must be careful to jump across several fissures in the floor.
'After a short time, you will see a mighty bridge on your left; it travels north, through the Dwarf-lords' Gate.
'That is where you must go.'

'This is not the path you want if you are looking to find the Dolven-view, and beyond it the Deep Descent. The path you want is that one, to the south. The winding road at its head will take you to the camp at the Dolven-view.'
'Do you see that reddish-glow to the north-west, ${PLAYER}? You must follow that passage if you are seeking the Chamber of the Cross-roads.'

'You have nearly come to Bósi's command centre, ${PLAYER}!
'Head east until you see stairs on your left. At the bottom of those stairs you will see another set of stairs on your right. You will then be at Manarbul, and the door to the Chamber of the Cross-roads will be to the north!'
'The Chamber of the Cross-roads? The entrance is just to the north there!'

'There is so much work to be done, ${PLAYER}, here and elsewhere in the Mines! This has been a great victory for the Iron Garrison, but this is only the beginning of our toils beneath the mountains.
'You must aid our people here at Durin's Threshold, and at our other encampments, if we are to have victory in Khazad-dûm.
'When you have performed some of the tasks here in Durin's Threshold, you should seek for the Dolven-view and for the Deep Descent. Speak to Bennt Sharp-eye at the Dolven-view, to the east of here, and to Thettmárr at the Deep Descent, among the Silvertine Lodes. They will have ways for you to assist the Iron Garrison.'

'I am glad you have come to the Deep Descent, ${PLAYER}. A ${CLASS} such as you should be able to help my people with many of the tasks that need doing here among the Silvertine Lodes. We are particularly plagued by the goblins of Gamil Filik!'

'Welcome, ${PLAYER}, to the Chamber of the Cross-roads! This shall be my command centre for a time as we establish our presence here in Moria. We will busy ourselves with making ready to restore the mines and cities beneath the mountains.
'I will never forget the great deeds you have done on behalf of the Iron Garrison, and I eagerly await tales of your future achievements. I am ever at your service, and may your feet lead you well in the darkness of Khazad-dûm and beyond.'

'Welcome to the Dolven-view, ${PLAYER}. As you can see, the Iron Garrison is hard at work making everything ready for our resettlement of the Mines.
'Speak to the people here and help them with their tasks. We must see to our safety before we can push any further into Khazad-dûm.'
Talk to Bennt Sharp-eye in the Dolven-view
Talk to Thettmárr in the Deep Descent
Talk to Bósi in the Chamber of the Cross-roads, on Durin's Way
Foreword -- Book 2: Echoes in the Dark
You have entered Khazad-dûm at last, and the dwarves have begun to establish their camps within its dark passages.

'When you have performed some of the tasks here in Durin's Threshold, you should seek for the Dolven-view and for the Deep Descent. Speak to Bennt Sharp-eye at the Dolven-view, to the east of here, and to Stíling at the Deep Descent, among the Silvertine Lodes. They will have ways for you to assist the Iron Garrison.'
'You should travel to the Dolven-view and the Deep Descent, ${PLAYER}, and continue to help the Iron Garrison. There is so much still to be done!'

'When you are satisfied with the aid you have provided the dwarves here at the Dolven-view, you should speak to Bósi for more work. You will find him at the Three-fork Camp on Durin's Way, north of the Great Delving. He has established a command centre in the Chamber of the Cross-roads.'

'When you are satisfied with the aid you have provided the dwarves here at the Deep Descent, you should speak to Bósi for more work. You will find him at the Three-fork Camp on Durin's Way, north of the Great Delving. He has established a command centre in the Chamber of the Cross-roads.'

'You are looking for the Chamber of the Cross-roads, ${PLAYER}? You have quite a trek ahead of you, for Bósi's command centre is a good distance from here.
'You will want to look for Iron Garrison Guides like myself as you make your way to the Chamber of the Cross-roads; we will steer you a-right!
'Bósi's command centre is not far along Durin's Way, but Durin's Way is a long way to the east. Start your journey east and north by climbing these steps.'
'The Dolven-view and the Deep Descent are both to the east of here, ${PLAYER}. Climb up these steps and keep watch for other guides to show you the way to the other camps.'

'The road to the Chamber of the Cross-roads? As you keep heading east, you will pass into a series of very dark caverns, lit only by some curious blue crystals.
'Follow this sloping path as it curves and descends, watching out for the gredbyg, vile insects that inhabit the darkness.
'Another guide of the Iron Garrison should be by a railing in the midst of the dark cavern.'

'The road to the Dolven-view, and beyond it the Deep Descent? As you keep heading east, you will pass into a series of very dark caverns, lit only by some curious blue crystals.
'Follow this sloping path as it curves and descends, watching out for the gredbyg, vile insects that inhabit the darkness.
'Another guide of the Iron Garrison should be by a railing in the midst of the dark cavern.'

'Be cautious on this leg of your journey to the Dolven-view and to the Deep Descent, ${PLAYER}, because it is so dark.
'You want to travel north-east through the darkness, following the sloping paths as they descend to buildings made by the ancient dwarves.'

Bennt Sharp-eye is in the Dolven-view, far to the east of Durin's Threshold, in the Great Delving. Stíling is in the Deep Descent, among the Silvertine Lodes, south of the Dolven-view.
Tulk has asked you to provide assistance to the dwarves at Durin's Threshold, the Dolven-view, and the Deep Descent.

Bósi has established a command centre somewhere within Moria and is waiting to speak with you there.
The Dwarves of Moria will be able to guide you to Bósi's new command centre, a guard room with a strategic location somewhere within the mines.

'Looking for some sweet raid gear are you? Well, I am the man, er dwarf to help you! I've made just about all this stuff, and while it has crushed my soul, the black lump that is my heart is warmed to see you enjoy these items.

'I wish you a Yule to remember, ${PLAYER}. The festivals to honour the seasons are always my favourite times of the year. Nature goes through such wonderful changes; indeed, the beauty can be quite overwhelming.
'I have a tradition at Yule where I make wreaths from the boughs of the evergreen bushes and present them to the others as a way to honour the winter season. I am nearly halfway done with this year's wreaths, but unfortunately I have run out of branches.
'If you could, head into the hills to the west and retrieve some for me so I can finish making the wreaths. I would be greatly indebted to you.'
'These branches will do perfectly, ${PLAYER}. I will sing the songs of Yule while I craft the remainder of the wreaths, and I will add your name in thanks.'

'We mark the passing of every winter with a great feast and celebration of Yule. In addition to roasting many haunches of boar, the festival features a tasting of some of the finest ales in all of Bree-land.
'Alas, I must revise -- every other year there was a tasting. The cart delivering the casks from the western hills was attacked by brigands just outside of town. The driver made it back here unharmed, but all of the kegs were lost. The brigands have gone too far this time! Too far.
'Do you think you could go and gather up what's left of those casks for me? He said he was attacked while riding on the Greenway around Thornley's work area, just after passing a farm. If I'm not mistaken, you will find what I'm looking for in that direction.'

'Some ale! You have found it! I'm so glad it was not broken or carried away like the others! This is a great day indeed. You shall be hailed as a hero from this day forth, ${PLAYER}.
'Had the tasting not taken place this year, I imagine I would have been quickly run out of town.'

'Good tidings to you, ${PLAYER}. It is a glorious Yule this year, but I feel a pang of distress. The dwarves are lucky enough to experience all the wonders of winter -- seeing your breath in the morning, the way an ale thaws frozen fingers and toes...and of course the crisp white covering of good snow.
'I hear the weather in Bree is unseasonably fair this year, which is a terrible tragedy to the good folk of that land. While I have not the power to change the climate itself, perhaps I can help to bring them some measure of the spirit of the season. Just a bit more snow and my cart will be full enough that some should last the voyage.
'Could you help me gather snow for my journey, ${PLAYER}? Not just any snow will do; it has to be very dry and hard-packed. You should find some in piles just west of Frerin's Court. Return to me with as much as you can carry, and hopefully Bree will see some real Yule cheer.'
'This is good snow, ${PLAYER}, and just enough to fill the waggon. I will be sure to let the peoples of Bree know that you helped to bring them one of the essential delights of the Yule season.'

'I have watched the turning of more Yule-seasons than a child such as you could fathom, friend. Every year, we mark its passing by gathering the mistletoe from the young fir-trees. Some of it is used in infusions, some for decoration, but mostly we use it to remind us of the fleeting passage of time.
'I have not yet gone gathering this year, for I fear there may be too much for me to do here. If I cannot see the mistletoe, I will mourn much, when I should be celebrating. Winter is the beginning of the cycle of spring's rebirth, not a death, as many mortals see it. Yule and mistletoe serve to remind us of this.
'If you could be so kind as to follow the road north towards Thrasi's Lodge, you will find young fir-trees just before the bend, adorned with freshly-grown mistletoe. Bring some back to me so I may rekindle my hope of the season's rebirth.'
'You have my greatest thanks for bringing me this mistletoe, ${PLAYER}. One must never forget that life means death, yet death brings new life.'

'Unfortunately, I fear my family may be disappointed this year. I have run out of apples to press for the cider. I had so much other planning to do, it simply slipped my mind.
'I don't suppose you would be willing to fetch me some apples? I don't need many. You can find them to the west, at Appledore's Orchard.'

'So your search has borne fruit has it? Thank you for this. The promise of finding a hand-axe of great lineage makes your efforts worthwhile!'

While Moria is most well-known as a mine, there is much more to it. It was home to a vast and ambitious culture of dwarves. They were warriors, crafters, and scholars. The knowledge the Dwarves of Moria had amassed is often overlooked when compared to the scale of their structural and prospecting achievements. 'The Iron Garrison's chief interest in this place is the recovery of ancient strategem and tactics. Building plans, too, are of interest. But so far in my research, I have seen far too many of these and not enough in the vein of creative offerings. Does that sound queer to you? That there would be interest in prose coming from someone of the Iron Garrison?
'It isn't queer at all. Not all of us hunger for a swift and violent reclamation of Khazad-dûm. Some of us seek to revel in new discoveries and enjoy the art and prose of our long lost brethren.

'I am sorry, ${PLAYER}; my words were borne of frustration, not of dislike. Every hour we spend in idleness here is an hour during which the shadow draws closer to my city.
'I have seen little of Aragorn, and even less of Gimli -- the dwarf seems to have gotten over his distrust of Elves easily enough! Even now he is off with Legolas, atop one of the trees at the crest of the hill of Cerin Amroth. Speak to him and see for yourself.'

'${PLAYER}! When Milwen told me another traveller from over the mountains had come to Lothlórien, I had no idea it would be you! We have come such a long way, haven't we? There is still a long way to go, but here in Lothlórien I have found it difficult to worry too much about the road ahead.
'You have to tell Sam and me what has happened since we parted, my friend! It feels like a lifetime has passed since leaving Rivendell, and several at least since last I saw Bag End!
'But Sam does not seem as surprised to see you as I am, ${PLAYER}. You haven't become the chief conspirator of another conspiracy, have you, Sam?'

'By Durin's beard! I did not expect to see you again so soon, ${PLAYER}. I am glad to be surprised!
'Legolas has been showing me the woods of Lothlórien, and the majesty of these trees, so like to stone-carved pillars beneath the mountains, fills this dwarf with amazement. But even in a land of marvels, its Lady is the greatest one of all!
'Still, I am ready to return now to the ground. If you ask me, the trees are best admired from below, rather than up among their branches!'

'Well hello there, ${PLAYER}! I have to admit I did not think to run into you here in Lórien! You're on the wrong side of the mountains, aren't you? Aren't we all!'
Merry's face lights up as he laughs long and loudly.
'Pippin is around here somewhere, taking a nap, I believe. No, I wouldn't wake him -- we'll all have plenty of time to catch up, I imagine. Lothlórien is so peaceful, it's hard to remember how hard our road will be, and has been!
'I wonder if you might track down Boromir; he doesn't seem to be having as good a time here as the rest of us. I think he's impatient to get going again, but maybe seeing you again will cheer him up. I last saw him on the north-west outskirts of the great clearing from which Cerin Amroth rises.'
Chapter 2: Ringbearer's Respite
Milwen has told you of a number of visitors to Lórien who will be interested in speaking with you.
'The hobbit Frodo Baggins rests with some of the members of his company at the top of Cerin Amroth. I know he will be pleased to speak with you, and to hear news of Eriador.'

'Gimli is in the trees above the crest of the hill of Cerin Amroth. Speak to him, and see if he is ready yet to leave these woods. I would not have expected a dwarf to trust these Elves so readily, but he has done so.'

'I can still hardly believe you're really here, ${PLAYER}! Unless I'm far off, it seems to me that Sam does not seem nearly as surprised. You haven't become the chief conspirator of another conspiracy, have you, Sam?'

'Boromir does not seem content with our stay in Lothlórien. I wonder if he will be cheered by seeing you, ${PLAYER}?
'I saw him last on the north-western edge of the clearing from which rises Cerin Amroth. Find him and see if you can lighten his mood!'
'Mr. Merry is taking a walk somewhere around Cerin Amroth. I know he will be happy to see you, and to hear your news. He was planning to rest in one of the private gardens nearby.'

'Hullo there, ${PLAYER}! Me, a conspirator? It's not like that at all, Mr. Frodo, and you know I'm not cut out for the keeping of secrets, despite your teasing.
'It's just that so many queer things have happened to us already, and this place being so Elvish and all, I'd just about given up being surprised when something out of the ordinary happens. And here comes ${PLAYER} out of the woods, right enough!
'You should find Mr. Merry somewhere around this hill, ${PLAYER}; I know he'll be pleased as anything to see you! He's taking one of his walks, and might be resting in a private garden nearby.'

'Legolas and I were just about to take another walk among the trees of Lothlórien in search of patrolling Orcs, ${PLAYER}. Why don't you come with us?
'What do you think, Legolas? Is there room in our party for a third? Surely ${PLAYER} will enjoy seeing the beauty of the wood, and the possibility of hewing an Orc or three will only sweeten the appeal of such a tour!'

'I wish I could help the Iron Garrison with their efforts in Khazad-dûm, ${PLAYER}. The Mines have brought me great sadness, but I would have them restored, and the Iron Garrison will need able-bodied dwarves if that is to happen.
'But I cannot. My road lies with Frodo, and I will see this errand through before I return to the Mines. The need of the Iron Garrison is great, but Glóin's son does not turn aside from one charge to begin another!'
Gimli's brow furrows, and then his eyes light with wonderment.
'I am struck by the thought, ${PLAYER}, that Bósi's tidings may not have been unknown to the Lady Galadriel. At my first meeting with her, it seemed to me that she offered a choice; a choice between continuing the Quest and leaving it to others. And here arrives just such a point of decision!'

'I would be delighted if you would join us, ${PLAYER}. The beauty of Lothlórien is best when shared, though we must all remain alert -- even when walking among the trees of Lórien -- for the Orcs of Moria have come down into Nanduhirion and are able to sneak past the borders on occasion.
'Let me know when you are ready to go.'

'I will not blame Gimli if he decides to help the Iron Garrison with their difficulties. Lord Elrond laid no bond upon us to accompany Frodo any farther than we would.

'Things are not going well for the Iron Garrison in Khazad-dûm, ${PLAYER}. Mazog still rules much of the deeps and many of the levels from his stronghold of Zabadgathol, and many good dwarves have fallen to his forces. Some, like my own son Bori, are still captives, or worse! I cannot bear to think what torments they may have suffered behind the walls of Zabadgathol.
'Still the dwarves of the Iron Garrison struggle to reclaim the hidden caverns, but for every beauty that is unearthed, two evils seem to spring forth from the depths!
'I have come to enlist the help of the ruler of these Elf-woods. If Celeborn of Lothlórien wishes to reap the benefits of friendship with the dwarves, he must reciprocate in kind. You are trusted by these Elves, ${PLAYER}. Tell this warden, this sentry, of our plight. Perhaps they will listen to you.'

'The Lord of the Galadhrim has much wisdom, and it is his wish that the dwarves not face the darkness of Khazad-dûm unaided.
'So it will be, and you too shall stand against whatever evils lie now beneath the mountains, ${PLAYER}, if this is your wish.'

'For the sake of the Iron Garrison I have put up with the indignity of being blindfolded during the passage here, ${PLAYER}, but my people could teach the Elves of this place something of courtesy were they to visit Khazad-dûm.
'Let us see now if the ill manners of the Elves spring from their Lord.'

'Out of respect for you, ${PLAYER}, and as a courtesy for the good you have done us, I have been told to find you and send you to the eaves of the wood.

'We will bring this dwarf to speak with Celeborn, ${PLAYER}, but you will be held responsible for him. You will be accountable for any and all of his actions while he remains within the Golden Wood.

'That is my decision. I will not abandon the Quest with which I have been charged.
'I hope you will give to Bósi and the rest of the Iron Garrison the aid that I would have provided if I were there, ${PLAYER}. When the errand of this company is finished, I hope to return to a reclaimed Moria, and your efforts will help make that possible.
'Bósi said he would return to the Chamber of the Cross-roads near Durin's Way, in Moria. Go now to him, and give him both my regret that I cannot now return and my fervent good wishes for his success.'

'I am glad you're here, ${PLAYER}. These Elves have been sent by Celeborn for the purpose of helping us drive the evil out of Khazad-dûm, so they say, but they seem much more interested in casting blame about than in doing anything helpful!
'This cavern, Buzun-ghâr, was found shortly after you departed, and many of my folk were impressed by the state of it. The gardens still thrive! At least, up here they do; something rots and corrupts the plant-life as you descend.
'But while we could use some real help in clearing the cave of danger, instead these Elves speak often of \qdigging too deeply\q and \qdisturbing things best left undisturbed.\q If this is the best Celeborn has to offer, I'd rather he kept them in the woods!
'You talk to Corunothiel, ${PLAYER}, and see if I'm wrong. You'll see I am not!'

'Listen to me, ${PLAYER}, for this Orvar will not listen to reason. Some evil lives at the bottom of this cavern, and if this place is not sealed away the evil may spread.
'This is always the way of dwarves! Why must they always dig into places they were not meant to go? Will they not be satisfied until no evil remains beneath the stone, and all have come to the surface to lay waste to the homes of the Elves and other good people?'

'Welcome back to Khazad-dûm, ${PLAYER}. I am disappointed that Gimli did not return with you, but I am sure he had his own reasons. His father Glóin has long been a close friend of my father and Brogur's father, and Gimli surely retains the honour of his forebears.
'This is my first dealing with Celeborn of Lothlórien, and I must confess I am not sure what to make of him. He has sent a number of Elves to help us, and while I appreciate the assistance, they seem perhaps too eager to blame the dwarves for all troubles, both present and past.
'They have established a camp with one of my dwarves, Orvar Bellhammer, in a newly-excavated passage off Durin's Way: Buzun-ghâr. It is located in the very south-eastern corner of Tharâkh Bazân, in the southern wall, right near the exit from those gardens. You will find Tharâkh Bazân to the north-east of this chamber; yes, the tree-filled area on your map there. Journey there and lend Orvar your aid -- he is having... difficulties... getting along with these Elves.'

'The messenger sent by Bróin was very clear that we should deal first with the corruption within Buzun-ghâr. 'If you will allow me this, ${PLAYER}, I must tell you that Bróin has not been the same since you returned him to us; it is no fault of his own, for he endured much in the watery den of the Watcher, curse its name, but the son of Brogur may be now a little touched in the head. And then to lose his cousin Bori to the forces of Mazog! It cannot have helped.
'Treat him kindly and with patience, ${PLAYER}, but if the requests he makes of you seem a little peculiar, you will at least know the cause.'

'Hello again, ${PLAYER}. My messenger returned from Buzun-ghâr with the news that you were in the depths trying to end the corruption that was found in that passage; I see that you were successful.'
Bróin seems about to say something else, but decides against it. After an uncomfortable pause, he begins again, and this time the words come in a torrent.
'I cannot understand why we waste so much effort on such insignificant tasks while my cousin Bori languishes in the dungeons of Mazog! Why still do my father's dwarves mine while Bori is held? He may not still live, but if he does, just as I endured in the watery den of the Watcher, could it not be that every hour we waste brings him closer to death at the hands of the Orcs? And still no one does anything!'
Bróin takes a long breath, making an effort to calm himself.
'My father has asked me to search for records of mined nodes in Khazad-dûm, but I cannot bring myself to do such useless work. If you will do it in my place, I can continue trying to think of some way to help Bori. Look for these records in any of the old archives in the Great Delving: the Chambers of Wisdom, Knowledge, or Deep Thought, or in Katûb-zahar.'

'You have returned with the mining records? My father will be pleased, even if I am not. Why must we waste so much time on meaningless tasks such as this when my cousin remains a prisoner of Mazog?'
Bróin takes the mining records from you with a sigh, but as he reads, his eyes widen and his face brightens.
'Do you... do you understand what you have found, ${PLAYER}? Ha ha! These are not simple mining records at all! These pages may hold the key to rescuing my cousin Bori! Listen to this:
'\qMelkólf Stonecarver commissioned for detail work on rear wall of Rushdurinul during night-time for completion of Zurr-thurkh; special instructions withheld by order of Durin.\q
'The word Rushdurinul drew my attention, ${PLAYER}, for that is the name of the throne of Durin, the very throne that Mazog has claimed for himself. To then see the name Zurr-thurkh, or \qsecret road...\q could it be that this dwarf, this Melkólf Stonecarver, was tasked with creating a secret passage out of Durin's throne room for the king to use in the event of danger? If this passage was completed, it might be used to gain access to Mazog! It might be used to rescue my cousin Bori!'
'You have not returned with the mining records, ${PLAYER}, and I cannot blame you. What a waste of time!'

'You've done it, ${PLAYER}! Look at these drawings: this is clearly Zabadgathol, which means these hallways here connect to Rushdurinul, and...'

'See this tunnel here? I would wager all the treasures of Khazad-dûm that this passage appears on no maps save this one!
'Now where can we gain access to this passage, Zurr-thurkh, the \qsecret road?\q If we follow it along this way... we...'
Bróin's smile becomes a mask of confusion.
'Unless I read this wrongly, ${PLAYER}, it seems that Zurr-thurkh connects to... Buzun-ghâr? Can this really be?'
Find the workshop of Melkólf Stonecarver and search it for mention of Zurr-thurkh
Chapter 7: The Lost Workshop
Bróin believes you have discovered mention of a secret passage into Rushdurinul, where Mazog has established his throne, and might use it to rescue his cousin Bori.

'The passage to Melkólf Stonecarver's workshop can be found in the side of Zirakzigil. Take the western exit from the Peaceful Path. Once you are outside, turn west and climb a short slope to the cave entrance. You must enter and search for any mention of Zurr-thurkh.
'I will stay behind on this one. I will accompany you on the next adventure, I promise! There's just a great deal to do here, as I am sure you understand.'

The passage to Melkólf Stonecarver's workshop can be found in the side of Zirakzigil; take the western exit from the Peaceful Path, and then turn west and climb a short slope to the entrance.

'How many fates must have entwined for the Iron Garrison to break open the entrance to Buzun-ghâr just when we need it, ${PLAYER}? If the \qsecret road\q was built, you will find the entrance to it deep within Buzun-ghâr! It must be a portent to have happened this day, of all days!'
Bróin suddenly finds himself unable to meet your eyes.
'I wish I could come with you to walk the \qsecret road\q and rescue Bori, ${PLAYER}, but there is still so much to do, and... well, I am needed here. We will fight together on the next adventure -- I swear it.
'Return to Buzun-ghâr, located south-west of here, in the south-eastern corner of Tharâkh Bazân, and speak with Orvar Bellhammer. He will accompany you along Zurr-thurkh, if it exists, though he should be your only companion, in the interest of secrecy.'
<rgb=#FF0000>This is a Solo quest, and cannot be completed with a Fellowship.</rgb>

'You say there is a way behind the walls of Zabadgathol, into Rushdurinul, where Mazog has set his throne? I don't know, ${PLAYER} -- it seems unlikely to me.'
With an eyebrow raised, Orvar listens to your explanation of Bróin's idea that it might be possible to rescue Bori.
'This is all well and good, but why isn't Bróin coming with you on this errand, ${PLAYER}? If you ask me, he's still not over his experience in the watery den of the Watcher. It seems to me that Lord Brogur has been trying to give his son trivial tasks to coax him from this brooding, but it has yet to work. Bróin will not be himself until he is able to conquer whatever fear clutches him.
'No matter. If you descend once again into the depths of Buzun-ghâr, where you stood against Grawulun the Caerog, and can find the entrance to this Zurr-thurkh. I will join you on the other side.'

'You see the good that can be done when Elves and dwarves work together, ${PLAYER}; Mazog was right to fear the alliance and hope that it should never come to pass!
'The dwarf Bróin came to Lossathrod, winded from a long run, and asked that we accompany him in his pursuit of you. He claimed to have made an error by leaving you to attempt the rescue of his kinsman with Orvar alone, and his regret of that decision spurred him onward. You are fortunate that he regained his courage when he did, ${PLAYER}, you and Orvar both!'
Find the entrance to Zurr-thurkh and use it to get behind the walls of Zabadgathol
Chapter 8: The Secret Road
You have located the plans for a secret escape tunnel out of Durin's throne room. If it was ever constructed, it might be used to enter Zabadgathol in secret to rescue Bori.

'If you can find the entrance to Zurr-thurkh in the depths of Buzun-ghâr, near where you fought Grawulun the Caerog, I will meet you on the other side. Then we will see if we can rescue Bori from the clutches of Mazog!'

'I am needed here, ${PLAYER}... there is so much to be done. I swear I will accompany you on the next adventure.
'Return to Orvar in Buzun-ghâr, in the south-eastern corner of Tharâkh Bazân, south-west of here along Durin's Way, and ask him to accompany you on the \qsecret road.\q You may yet rescue my cousin Bori from the clutches of Mazog!'

Orvar Bellhammer is in Buzun-ghâr, located south-west of the Peaceful Path, in the very south-eastern corner of Tharâkh Bazân, along Durin's Way.
Bróin has asked you to speak with the dwarf Orvar about accompanying you on the secret road into Rushdurinul.

Orvar has agreed to meet you inside Zurr-thurkh, if you can find the entrance, in order to mount a rescue of Bori from the clutches of Mazog.

Corunothiel is at Lossathrod, the encampment in Buzun-ghâr.
You have emerged from Rushdurinul victorious over Mazog, but have learned the unfortunate news that Bori and the other captives have been sent to Dol Guldur with Gorothúl. Corunothiel is waiting to speak with you.
There is no sign of Bori among the Orcs.

'I got to thinking, ${PLAYER}, after you left, about all the things that you and others have been through, and I realized something: I can no longer stand by while others fight my fight.
'Once I resolved to leave my self-pity behind, I hurried to Buzun-ghâr and convinced the Elves there to come with me in pursuit of you. Our fortunes held, and we arrived just when most needed!
'I must hope that Bori is still alive, and that he is one of the two dwarves sent to Dol Guldur. It is only this hope that can keep me fighting.'

'The dwarf Bróin came to Buzun-ghâr not long after you left, and gave such a rousing speech that we could do nothing but follow him here. Who knew dwarves could speak with such vigour?
'And now he has a prisoner, and has spoken an oath beside. I hope it will not end poorly for Bróin or his friends, for there is a curious power to vows taken lightly.'

'You were right, ${PLAYER}! This was once Rushdurinul, the great throne room of Durin! The Orcs have surely given it a crude new name, but it will always be Rushdurinul to the dwarves!
'Fight on into the Orc encampment, and search for Bori, Bósi's son! I will watch the rear to ensure that no creatures from Zurr-thurkh surprise us while we are doing battle with the Orcs!'
'Let us leave this place, ${PLAYER}, and arrange for the prisoner to be kept somewhere safe. Mazog will not trouble us on the journey or he will lose his life, and painfully!'

'This is incredible, ${PLAYER}. Can we really use this passage to get behind the walls of Zabadgathol? For how long has this tunnel remained undiscovered by dwarf or Orc?
'Let us find out!'
'We will confront Mazog directly, ${PLAYER}, and force him to tell us where Bori has been imprisoned!'

'Lord Celeborn wishes to speak with you about what has happened, ${PLAYER}. Return to Talan Haldir and speak with Haldir about arranging an audience with the Lord of Lórien.
'You will find Talan Haldir in a great tree on the banks of the Nimrodel, outside Lórien.'

'It is good to see you again, ${PLAYER}. Is it true that you have defeated Mazog in his own lair?'
Haldir smiles as you briefly tell your tale.
'You are truly an astonishment to me, my friend; I did not really expect the rumour to be true.
'Let me know when you are ready to see Lord Celeborn, and I will bring you to him as he requested.'

'The winds of change are blowing, ${PLAYER}, and I fear they carry with them the onset of war. Lothlórien cannot remain isolated and in safety forever.
'Lord Celeborn's gaze must turn toward Mirkwood and the great shadow that lies over Dol Guldur. When the time comes to cross the river and fight, as it seems we must, I will call for you.
'Had I once thought it might not be necessary, I do not any longer. Too many signs seem to point in that direction. Stay well, ${PLAYER}. We will have need of you yet.'

'Hello, friend! Is it not a fine spring day? This is just the sort of weather that makes a festival so pleasant, with the gentle breezes and the bright new greens. Are you looking at that maze yonder? That is just what I was thinking of too. It is a fine day indeed to be lost in the foliage!
'So you wish to try your luck at picking a path? That is a worthy goal. I went just the other day, in record time. I'll warrant you can't get through even if I gave you a more than generous amount of time. In fact, I'd be willing to wager a fair prize on that very challenge.
'Give a shout if you get lost and need me to come looking! I'll not think less of you -- some people get quite lost in such a confusion of ways. But do not walk so quick that you forget to savour the sweet smells of green growing things, for you'll not find them any other time of year.'

'Oh! You startled me! I did not expect to see you for another several hours at least. You did rather well, ${PLAYER}, but you have to go much faster if you are to beat my time. But never mind; I am impressed just the same.
'Come to think of it, you deserve a reward! Accept this token of my respect for a Maze-master in training. I hope that you enjoyed the greenery as much as I did when I went through.'

'Greetings, ${CLASS}. I wish to speak to you of a matter of importance to me. Long ago, when this ruin was a thing of beauty, I tended the groves and kept the lore of Edhelion. I have returned now to see that this place is restored to the beauty and reverence for which it once stood. My efforts to collect and catalogue the lore go poorly. Even worse, the blight affecting the trees has left me with little hope....
'Hope, however, is never truly lost, and so I ask you to assist me. These trees have resilient seeds, and if any have survived the years, they will be found in the embrace of the leaves scattered about their trunks.
'I know that you must test your mettle against the creatures now plaguing the trees, so I hope that this small task will not hinder your goals. Will you assist me?'

'The gift of life, that is what these seeds represent. I am pleased that your efforts proved to be fruitful. To know that we shall recover the beauty and knowledge of Edhelion stirs such joy within me that I shall remember your efforts always. Thank you, ${PLAYER}.'
Return the preserved seeds to Gailthin
Seeds of the Past

The trees of Edhelion, long dormant since the departure of the Elves, shed their seeds long ago. The Elves at the refuge believe that life still exists within the preserved seeds found in the large piles of leaves beneath the barren boughs.
'We will once again read the lore of our folk beneath the boughs of these trees, thanks to you.'

The copse of trees Gailthin speaks of lay a short distance from her.
Gailthin asked you to search the patches of leaves for any sign of preserved seed that might be used to restore the grove to its former beauty.

'Even in this fallen refuge, there are threats that we must confront. Without the watchful eye and care of the Elves, Edhelion has become home to many unnatural creatures. You will need to know how to defend yourself and defeat these threats.
'You must learn skills from others, like myself. We can guide you through your training and help you become stronger.

'I am pleased to know that you have completed your meditation and training. The road ahead is filled with many challenges, and we must all prepare ourselves for what is to come. I think that this lesson will be one that remains with you.'

If you're having trouble getting a block, try using <rgb=#00ff00>Guardian's Ward</rgb> to increase your chances of blocking enemy attacks. Once you have blocked an attack you will be able to use your <rgb=#00ff00>Shield Swipe</rgb> skill. Strike the <rgb=#ff0000>Targeting Dummy</rgb> with <rgb=#00ff00>Shield Swipe</rgb>.

Defeated Orcs in Nanduhirion (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'I have never seen the Orcs like this, ${PLAYER}; they pour from the gates of Moria as they have not done in years, and establish camps and outposts all along the road between here and there.
'If you would be a friend of Lórien, you must help us discourage the Orcs from this endeavour. Seek out these enemies to the north-west, and defeat them wherever you find them in Nanduhirion.
'The more Orcs you slay, the safer will be the road between Lothlórien and Moria. Their boldness worries me greatly.'
'You have done well, ${PLAYER}. We will not forget your help to us, though there be always more to do.'
Defeat Orcs in Nanduhirion (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Down from the Mountains
Hadroneth is worried about the mass of Orcs that have poured from the gates of Moria into the Dimrill Dale, and wants you to thin their numbers.

'The Orcs have come forth from inside the mountains -- into Nanduhirion, the Dimrill Dale, to the north-west. You must slay these foes wherever you see them if you would be friend to the Elves of Lórien.'

Orcs can be found all along the road that leads through Nanduhirion, the Dimrill Dale, north-west of Talan Haldir.
Hadroneth has asked you to thin the numbers of the Orcs that have come forth from within the mountains.

Hadroneth is on Talan Haldir, along the banks of Nimrodel.
The Elf Hadroneth is waiting for you to report of your success slaying the Orcs that have poured from the Gates of Moria into Nanduhirion.
Set fire to Orc barricades (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'You have slain many Orcs, but their camps in Nanduhirion are still a danger to those forced to travel the road between here and Moria. The Orcs have erected barricades outside their outposts along the road.
'Set these barricades afire, ${PLAYER}, and perhaps we can convince the Orcs to return to their vile warrens beneath the mountains.
'You will find barricades to the north-west, outside the camps of Uruk-gashan, Drû-garmadh, and Athmadhul, along the road that runs through Nanduhirion.'
'Very good, ${PLAYER}! Setting fire to their barricades will tell even the most dull-witted Orc that he is not welcome in Nanduhirion, so close to Lórien. You have done well.'
Set fire to Orc barricades (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Hadroneth
Too Close to Lórien
Hadroneth is concerned about the Orc camps that have been established in Nanduhirion, and wants you to tear down the barricades that have sprung up outside them.
'The Orcs build barricades outside the camps they have established in Nanduhirion to the north-west. Set these barricades alight! You will find them along the road that runs from here to Moria.'

You will find barricades to the north-west of Talan Haldir, outside the Orc camps of Uruk-gashan, Drû-garmadh, and Athmadhul, along the road that runs through Nanduhirion.
Hadroneth has asked you to damage the permanence of the Orc camps in Nanduhirion by burning down the barricades they erect outside them.

Hadroneth is on Talan Haldir, located on the banks of the Nimrodel, south-east of Nanduhirion.
You have set fire to many of the Orc barricades in Nanduhirion and should report now to Hadroneth.
Defeated Orcs in Nanduhirion (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Set fire to Orc barricades (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'The Orcs have not yet left Nanduhirion, ${PLAYER}; it seems they still have designs on Lórien.
'You have helped us before, and if you continue to do so we will not forget it. Neither will the Orcs, if you continue to harry their fell endeavours in this way.
'Travel north-west to the Orc camps along the road that runs through Nanduhirion. Slay the Orcs there and set fire to any of the barricades they have built anew. We will never cease our efforts to push the Orcs back beneath the mountains, and protect the borders of our fair land.'
'Once again you have proven yourself a worthy enemy to the Orcs, ${PLAYER}. I will let you know when next we have need of your strength and skill.'
Defeat Orcs in Nanduhirion (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Set fire to Orc barricades (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Aiding the Elves I
Pleased with your efforts on behalf of the Elves of Lórien, Hadroneth has asked you to continue your campaign against the Orcs that have invaded Nanduhirion.

'The Orcs are still a threat to travellers on the road that runs from here to Moria. Defeat the Orcs and set fire to the barricades they have erected outside their camps in Nanduhirion, to the north-west.'

Orcs can be found north-west of Talan Haldir, along the road that runs through Nanduhirion to Moria. They have erected barricades outside their camps along the road: Uruk-gashan, Drû-garmadh, and Athmadhul.
Hadroneth has asked you to defeat Orcs in Nanduhirion and to set fire to the barricades they erect outside their camps along the road.

Hadroneth is on Talan Haldir, located on the banks of Nimrodel, south-east of Nanduhirion.
You have continued your efforts against the Orc invaders of Nanduhirion, slaying many of their number and setting fire to the barricades they have erected along the road.
Collected Orc weapons (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeated Orc waylayers in Nanduhirion (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'The Orcs still endanger travellers on the road through Nanduhirion, ${PLAYER}. The work of their foes is never done, it seems!
'You are familiar with their camps now: Uruk-gashan, Drû-garmadh, and Athmadhul; return to these foul encampments north-west of here, along the road that runs through Nanduhirion, and steal more of their weapons from the racks within. An Orc without a blade is an Orc from which we have little to fear.
'Slay too the Orc waylayers that prowl along the road that runs between here and Moria. They cannot be allowed to menace even the few travellers that come this way.'
'Again you have proven an able ally, ${PLAYER}. I will let you know when we have need again of your help; with so many Orcs this near to Lórien, I fear it will not be long.'
'Have you had any success against the Orc waylayers along the road? Where are the weapons I asked you to take? Do not tarry...the Orcs are deadly when left to their own devices for too long.'
Collect Orc weapons (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeat Orc waylayers in Nanduhirion (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

Aiding the Elves II
Satisfied with your efforts on behalf of the Elves of Lórien, Maethoron has asked you to continue your campaign against the Orcs that have invaded Nanduhirion.

'Return to Nanduhirion, to the north-west, and defeat Orc waylayers along the road. Look too for the Orc camps on the road between here and Moria, and steal the weapons you find. The Elves of Lórien will not forget your efforts.'

Orc camps can be found all along the road that runs through Nanduhirion, north-west of Talan Haldir. Orc waylayers prowl along the road as well, and can be found on the outskirts of the camps there.
Maethoron has asked you to continue your efforts against the Orcs of Moria that have invaded Nanduhirion: defeating their waylayers along the road and stealing weapons from their camps.

Maethoron is on Talan Haldir, located near the banks of Nimrodel, south-east of Nanduhirion.
You have stolen weapons from the Orc camps of Nanduhirion and defeated more Orc Waylayers along the road, and should return now to Maethoron with news of your success.
Collected Orc Weapons (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'The Orcs of Moria seem to be of a limitless supply, ${PLAYER}, but the weapons they wield seem to be much less available; every sword or axe we take from them is an Orc we render defenceless, if only for a short time.
'The Orcs have established camps to the north-west, along the road that runs through Nanduhirion: Uruk-gashan, Drû-garmadh, and Athmadhul. Journey to these three camps and steal any of the weapons you find within.
'I will not forget any of your deeds against the Orcs that have invaded Nanduhirion, so perilously close to Lothlórien.'
'Very good, ${PLAYER}. Each of these weapons will be greatly missed by the Orcs, and will make our task of defending Lothlórien easier!'

'The Orcs have established camps along the road that runs from here to the gates of Moria, in Nanduhirion. You must venture to those camps, to Uruk-gashan, to Drû-garmadh, and to Athmadhul, and steal Orc weapons from the racks.'

Cruel Weapons of Moria
Maethoron knows that the Orcs of Moria are more limitless than the weapons they wield, and wants you to steal some of these weapons from the Orc camps in Nanduhirion.

The Orcs have established three camps along the road that runs through Nanduhirion, north-west of Talan Haldir. Racks of weapons can be found throughout these camps.
Maethoron has asked you to steal Orc-weapons from the camps of the Orcs in Nanduhirion.
Defeated Orc waylayers in Nanduhirion (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'The Orcs are becoming more bold, ${PLAYER}, and their waylayers have made travel along the road through Nanduhirion very dangerous for the unwary traveller.
'If you are a friend to the Elves of Lórien and share our concerns, you will do something about these Orcs in particular. Travel north-west into Nanduhirion and defeat the Orc waylayers where you find them: along the road and near the outskirts of their camps in the area. The road into the Golden Wood must be made safe.'

'Excellent, ${PLAYER} -- you have waylaid the waylayers most admirably.
'As long as the Orcs of Moria threaten the road through Nanduhirion, the Dimrill Dale, the Elves of Lothlórien will not be able to rest. We will strike at the Orcs wherever we may, and if hardy warriors such as yourself will help us, we will have victory against them.'
