Hinder the Orc-schemes
Maethoron is worried about the growing number of Orc-waylayers on the road that runs through Nanduhirion toward Lothlórien.

'Orc Waylayers have become more bold in recent days, and have taken up positions along the road that runs through Nanduhirion to the north-west. You should teach them to fear the good-hearted peoples once more.'

Orc waylayers can be found all along the road that runs through Nanduhirion, north-west of Talan Haldir.
Maethoron has asked you to waylay the waylayers in Nanduhirion so that the road may be made safe.

Maethoron is on Talan Haldir, near the banks of Nimrodel, south-east of Nanduhirion.
You have defeated many of the Orc Waylayers that make travel on the road through Nanduhirion difficult, and should report of your success to Maethoron.
Defeated slugs in Edhelion (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Long have we waited to return to Edhelion, and now that we have, we find the ruins of our once-great home overrun by filth and vermin. I recall the vibrance of this place and wish to restore it to the glory it once held.
'The pool, beneath the blighted trees to the east, was once a place where we could reflect in peace and feel the cool water and breeze off the mountains. Now, it is swelled with filth shed from the slugs which make it their home.
'Would you assist me and clean out the slugs from the pool?'

'It may seem a small deed, but from the many small deeds that shall be done in this place, we shall achieve the greatest goal. Edhelion will be restored through the efforts of all. No single Elf shall claim greater glory than any other.
'Beyond the gate of Edhelion, you will find Laergil and Orodlin, two of our brethren working to mend the division between the dwarves and Elves. Speak with them, if you have the chance.
'I am told that they have taken comfort in the outpost to the south, beyond the western gate of Edhelion.'
Defeat slugs in Edhelion (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Dorollas in Edhelion
Intro: Befouled Pool

Since the abandonment of Edhelion, terrible creatures of unnatural ilk have found their way within the walls. In a tepid pool of water, a filthy creature has taken residence, and the Elves, intent on restoring the refuge of Edhelion, want your assistance in removing the vile things from the pool.
'These slugs are great unnatural creatures. They have grown to enormous size and have a sickly quality to them. We must destroy them to cleanse the pool of their filth.'

Slugs infest a pool within the walls of Edhelion, east of Dorollas.
Dorollas has tasked you with cleaning the slugs from Edhelion so that healing may begin in the once-beautiful refuge of the Elves.

Dorollas is west of the pool in Edhelion, near Elladan.
You should return to Dorollas and tell him that you have successfully purged the vile slugs from the pool.
Defeated insects near the trees of Edhelion (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Armed with new knowledge and a clear recollection of the past, I must ask you to assist us in our first strides to reclaim this fallen refuge. Nearby, just to the north, there is a copse of trees before a golden gate. These trees were once one of the grandest sights in all of Edhelion. Now, sadly, they are a ghost of their former selves. Barren and blighted, these trees remind us of our failure and the betrayal wrought upon us by the Dourhands.
'Worse still, they have become home to foul and twisted insects. We must eliminate those insects lest they infest new plantings, and there may yet be a way to save the ailing trees.
'Go now and strike down the creatures plaguing the trees of Edhelion. Return to me when you have completed this task.'

'You are ready now to leave this place. Elrond has chosen another path for you, and I was here only to ensure that you were ready for the journey. I am confident now that you will prove everything we expect of you, ${PLAYER}.'
Defeat insects near the trees of Edhelion (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Dorongúr Whitethorn in Edhelion
Intro: Plague Among the Trees
Prepared and armed with new skills, you are tasked now with a battle against the vile creatures that blight and plague the trees of Edhelion.
'You will find the insects near the copse of trees a short distance north of here. Destroy them, then return to me.'

The insects may be found at the copse of trees north of Dorongúr Whitethorn, near the golden gate.
Dorongúr Whitethorn charged you with helping to reclaim the refuge of Edhelion by eliminating the insects that have made the nearby trees their home.

Dorongúr Whitethorn is south of the trees.
With the insects defeated, you have proven yourself worthy to Dorongúr Whitethorn. You should return to him and tell him of your victory.
Recovered arrows from Orc corpses (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
You successfully brought the arrows to Meredhrandir!

'The Orcs remain in Nanduhirion, ${PLAYER}, and as long as they do, the Galadhrim will have need of arrows to oppose them.
'Return to the border of the Golden Wood, east of here, and look for more Orcs slain by the arrows of the Elf-archers. Recover the arrows from their corpses, as you have done before, and return them to me.
'Do not stray too near the border, however! If the hidden Galadhrim do not recognize you as a friend, they may waste some of their arrows on you, and I will need to send other adventurers to recover them from your unfortunate body! That is not how your story should end.'

'Another delivery of arrows, ${PLAYER}? Perfect! You have sealed the fate of more Orcs of Moria by bringing these to me.
'The Elves of Lórien will not forget your continuing efforts on our behalf.'

'You have returned with more arrows, ${PLAYER}? Very good! I have prepared a bundle of arrows for you to bring to Meredhrandir at Mekhem-bizru, as before.
'Pick them up from the crates right next to me, and carry them west and north along the road through Nanduhirion, to Meredhrandir at the camp just outside the eastern gate of Moria.
'Stay out of deep water, or you will be unable to hold onto the arrows for long!'
'You have not brought me enough arrows yet, ${PLAYER}.'
Recover arrows from Orc corpses near the border of Lórien (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring Elf-arrows to Celegúien
Pick up a bundle of arrows next to Celegúien
Aiding the Elves III
Encouraged by your efforts on behalf of the Elves, Celegúien wishes you to continue the work you began against the Orcs.
'East of here, along the north and south border of Lórien, you will find Orcs slain by the Galadhrim. Recover arrows from their bodies, as you have done before, and bring them to me.'

'Pick up a bundle of arrows from the crate next to me, and carry them to Meredhrandir at Mekhem-bizru, the camp just outside the eastern gate of Moria. Follow the road north-west through Nanduhirion, and avoid the Orcs that prowl nearby as you carry the arrows to Meredhrandir.'

The corpses of Orcs slain by the hidden Galadhrim along the border of Lothlórien, east of Echad Andestel, can be the source of more arrows desired by Celegúien. She warned you against going too near the border, for the Galadhrim will shoot if they do not know you.

'If you are willing to be of further aid, ${PLAYER}, I would ask that you seek out the counsel of Orthir, a Scholar of the Trees who has made the woods of Lothlórien, and especially the majestic trees in and around Cerin Amroth, his particular study. Describe to him the symptoms you found on the Malbrethil saplings and follow his advice. You will find him not far west of here, near the path.'

'Whence do you come, ${CLASS}? From Orthir? That is strange; he usually has little patience for visitors. Perhaps you should start from the beginning....
'Singing to the saplings! What a lovely cure--marvellous in its simplicity! If we are to take what the Scholar of the Trees says to heart, more music will have to be made throughout these woods, to replace the natural tunes of beasts and birds that have been silenced by the trampling of so many feet.
'The mention that you say Orthir made of the first Malbrethil-tree has given me an idea....'

'Mae govannen. You were sent from Mallendathor? Very well, what assistance do you need?
'Ah! The Melbrethil! The first Malbrethil-tree was a gift from those who dwell beyond the Sea. We prize them so because they listen to the harmonies of Middle-earth itself and breathe them out to their surroundings. But you say they are suffering? This is no small matter....
'I fear that since our lands have been...visited...by so very many of the friends and allies of Gandalf the Grey and Elrond Halfelven, the forest and its beasts have been quieter--frightened, perhaps. I think that you might remedy this were you to <rgb=#FF0000>sing</rgb> to the saplings. Any song will do. Perhaps hearing of your homeland will strengthen them. When you have sung to them, seek out Sendiel, another warden of the woods, whom I last saw in a clearing in Gelirdor, south-west of the hill of the First Malbrethil.'

'Yes, well. You really can't seem to get enough of that hedge maze. No matter! No one will ever beat my best time. Only one minute and a few seconds more!
'I am sorry to have to break this to you, but it is folly to think that you can match my time. Try if you must, but I simply do not wish for your hopes to be disappointed. It can be so discouraging to fail.
'You still mean to try, do you? Very well. You have one minute. I am not worried. No one will ever beat my time. Now please, leave me be! I am trying to enjoy the spring before it fades into another sweltering summer, and I cannot do it if you are hovering about me like a gnat.'

'Please do not come around and bother me anymore, ${PLAYER}. Your very presence somehow saps the beauty out of a fine spring day, and I find that I do not enjoy it quite so much when you are near.
'Come to think of it, I do not like mazes after all. They are rather too green for my liking. Too much green is unpleasant, in certain lights.
'Here, take your reward. Enjoy your silly maze if such a silly, silly, pointless thing can truly be enjoyed.'

'I think a good compromise will be your running of the maze within just over half the time previously allotted. Three minutes should do the trick. My minute record is not to be outdone, of course.
'Don't forget to shout if you get lost and need me to come looking! I'll not think less of you -- some people get mighty lost in such a confusion of ways. 'We will spread the word to other adventurers like yourself -- the more we can learn of the Orc plans, the better prepared we will be when the attack comes.'
'I thank you, ${PLAYER}, for these numerous plans. The schemes of the Orcs will be studied so that we may be prepared for the attack that is surely coming.'

'I am still waiting for more battle plans from you, ${PLAYER}. The writing of Orcs and goblins is murky and disjointed, and we need many pages of their notes if we are to unravel their plans. 'It is time, ${PLAYER}. We must hope our preparations are sufficient, for I fear the attack of the Orcs will be upon us at any moment. We must discuss our plan to repel them.
'There are three passes into Fanuidhol: the Western Pass, the Northern Pass, and the Eastern Pass. We will have defenders at each of these passes, for if any of them fall, Lothlórien will be imperilled. But it is not enough to stand against the Orcs; we must turn back their assault and remove their foothold within Fanuidhol. Scouts tell me they have four encampments among the hills and have erected an idol to the Enemy at each. By carrying a Banner of Lórien to each encampment, your allies will be able to destroy the idol. You will not have much time to destroy all four idols, ${PLAYER}, and will need to move with all haste. But beware! The Banner-carrier will be a very ready target of the Orcs.
'Speak to me when you are ready and have gathered allies, and we will travel to the passes into Fanuidhol.'

'Lothlórien is safe for now, but the Orcs may attack again. You and your allies have my heart-felt thanks.
'In the event the Orcs launch another assault, we will be ready, and I ask you to stand with us again if the need comes.'

Further up the hill are the three passes that gate entry to the Golden Wood: the Northern Pass, the Western Pass, and the Eastern Pass; a number of my people have already gone to each of the passes to defend them.
'Travel up to each of the passes and make note of the skills of the Elves at each location: melee combat, ranged combat, or the healing arts. Then return here and tell myself and my two friends where you would like us.

'Mae govannen, traveller. Welcome to the celebration of Ethuilwereth in Duillond. I hope you will enjoy the wonders that the spring season has to offer before you, too, wander off to the Spring Planting in Bree-land. The hedge maze there is drawing many of my kindred thither.
'A company of Elves, led by clear-headed Saelthaliel, went to the Spring Planting many days ago to observe the green walls on the Horse-fields. I have not heard from them since, and I truly did not expect that they would be away so long.
'If you find yourself at the festival grounds in Bree, please look for Saelthaliel or any of her company. Remind her that Ethuilwereth will not go on forever, and that she and her company should hasten back if they wish to enjoy it before it has passed away until the next turn of the seasons.'
'I am not at all surprised that Calendui has sent you to me. Our stay has been overlong indeed, but perhaps you will be able to help me.'

'Are you enjoying the Springfest? It is a fine time of year! But my friend Gísi, who loves this festival most, is nowhere to be found. He travelled to the Spring Planting of Bree many days ago to try his luck in the hedge-maze there, but I've heard not a word from him since.
'If you go to the maze, could you look for him? I know that he would not wish to miss the festival of the dwarves. I am worried that some strange fate has befallen him.
'Just...try not to get lost among the greens yourself before you speak to Gísi.'

'The Springfest! Goodness -- do you know I had nearly forgotten all about it? Because -- pardon me, my eyes; they will not stop tearing for all the laughing I do these days! Oh, if only you could see! The mirth! I may not go back for many days yet.'

The dwarf Gísi was supposed to be back from the Spring Planting in Bree several days ago, and Mákr desires to find out what has become of him.
<rgb=#FF0000> NOTE: This quest will be removed from your quest log when the current festival ends. </rgb>
'You should go to Bree, traveller! You will find the Hedge Maze in the Horse-fields.'

'I am glad you have come. I could use some assistance, if you please. You might wonder why I am standing all alone at a festive springtime event, but I am actually waiting for my friends. I have been waiting for some days now.
'We all entered the maze together, as a group, but sometime during the course of things we became separated, and only I came out. I have been waiting for them all these days since!
'Do you think you could go into the maze and remind them that we must soon be away back to our own Ethuilwereth celebration? I would go in again, but I am afraid that I will miss them once again, and we could be here even longer if they go back to look for me! I am beginning to regret our decision to come here....'
'You spoke to all of them, and yet still they tarry! I do not know how I will ever get them out. I am beginning to think that bringing them along was not the most prudent idea....'

'We Elves do not notice the turning of the days. Saelthaliel's concern is unfounded; I am not lost, but enjoying the fresh foliage.
'I suppose it matters not. I will leave now. Where is the exit? I do not ask because I do not know. I just want to make sure that you know how to get out.'
'Saelthaliel is too hasty. But I suppose she is correct; I will come. I will...follow you for a while, if you don't mind.'
'Are you lost? I can see that you are. You needn't be ashamed. Just follow my path, and I will lead us both back to Saelthaliel in time.'

'The door? Oh, I am sure I must have passed it a hundred times and paid it no heed. I could find it again in a moment if I so desired.
'I stay only because I worry if you can get out yourself. I will watch which direction you go, to make sure you go the right way....'
'I am sorry, my mind was elsewhere. I have been looking for the exit for days! I have never been good at this sort of thing -- every leaf is distracting. Will you lead me out?'

'Saelthaliel is waiting? I had almost forgotten her. I find this maze most inhabitable. I am not sure I have a mind to leave just yet.
'Pray tell, though -- where is the door? I ask merely out of curiosity, should I ever want to find it. I am not sure that time will come, but just the same...it will be good to know it is there.'

'My name is Tuilinn. What are you called? ${PLAYER}? The name is familiar...are you a friend to Aragorn son of Arathorn? Ah yes, you helped reforge Narsil from its shards! It is a pleasure and an honour to make your acquaintance.
'I remember when all of us here at Cerin Amroth once greatly doubted his fitness to court our sweet Undómiel...but I am sure you know the tale of their romance. What? You do not? I suppose, with Elessar being as close as he is, it is not all that surprising. Nevertheless, if you are interested, you should certainly learn the tale, as it is sweet indeed.
'Oh, not from me. I have only pieces of it myself; I shall, however, send you to those from whom I learned the rest. Pennasseth, known as the Keeper of Stories, has befriended one of the visiting hobbits, along the path towards the city. Naeris, called the Guardian of Lore, can usually be found in a clearing east of here in Gelirdor, with his friend Sendiel. Meluibrennil, currently visiting the lovely garden of Santhirwen, south of here, helped care for Arwen Undómiel when she was young.'
'You have learned the tale? It is sad, but beautiful, is it not? I hear that Arwen now resides again with her father in Imladris, awaiting the day when Aragorn claims his rightful inheritance.'

'Gladly will I share what I know of the tale of Aragorn and my dear little Arwen. Aragorn, called Elessar after the green Elf-stone given him by the Lady Galadriel herself, was just shy of his fiftieth year; still a brash youngling. He was weary, having been long fighting and travelling throughout many kingdoms, and had stopped in Lórien on his way back to Rivendell from the borders of the Black Land of Mordor. The Lady of the Golden Wood insisted that he cast off his ragged travelling apparel and dressed him in silver, white, and Elven grey, such that he appeared almost more than a Man -- nearer to an Elf-lord from the Isles of the West, tall and stern.
'At that moment, Arwen Undómiel, the Lady of Imladris, saw him again for the first time in nearly thirty years. At that moment, indeed, was her choice made: to follow, await, love, protect, and honour Elessar, and share with him the Doom of Men.
'They had but a brief season to wander together through the woods and glades of Lothlórien. The hill of Cerin Amroth was their most particularly beloved place: that is where they wandered barefoot through the blossoms of niphredil and elanor, and it was there that they finally plighted their troth and sealed their fate.'

'Mae govannen. I am Naeris, the keeper of the histories of the Galadhrim. I have memorized the lays and poems, the lineages, the heraldry, and the great martial and political deeds of our people. How may I be of service? Ah, I see; a tale of recent days, then.
'I have read a tale recorded by Elrond Halfelven of the solemn discourse he held with the son of Arathorn, fifteenth Chieftain of the Dúnedain. The Lord of Imladris had read the heart of Aragorn and seen the new-born love there for Arwen Undómiel. He told Aragorn of the great doom that awaited him: either he would rise above all his lineage since the days of Elendil the Tall, father of Isildur, or he would plunge into darkness with all the remnants of his kin; also, that in the many years of trial that lay before him, he would neither take a wife nor bind a woman's troth to himself, until he should be found worthy of doing so. Elrond further warned Aragorn that the Evenstar of her people was too far above him, and he too young for her. He explained how the long life and youth of the Eldar were hers while her father stayed here, and that she would be able to follow him into the West when he should go. Were she to choose to bind herself to a mortal, her doom would be bleak; her life, shortened. She would never marry a mortal, unless he was king of both Arnor and Gondor.
'The next day, Aragorn son of Arathorn took his leave of his mother, Gilraen, and left the Last Homely House to go forth into the wilds; he was soon, however, seen once more, here in Lothlórien. It is an abiding sorrow and grief to many of us that young Arwen Undómiel will not come with us when we go. Now, I tire...hold this tale close to your heart; consider it, learn from it. Farewell, patient ${RACE}.'

'Mae govannen, my good ${CLASS}. I am Pennasseth, though I am sometimes called the Keeper of Stories. Have you a tale to share? Ah, a tale to request! And none less than that of Aragorn and Arwen -- wonderful.
'I first met Aragorn when he was a very small child under the care of Elrond Halfelven, with whom I too was staying. His mother, Gilraen the Fair, brought him thither to live when he was but two years of age, his father Arathorn having been recently killed on campaign when an Orc-arrow pierced his eye. Estel, as Aragorn was then known, was a sweet child, serious and intelligent, with no awareness of his kingly lineage -- he would not be given that until his twentieth year -- and we all doted upon him.
'Since its occurrence during the Elder Days, we have sung of the great romance of the Man Beren One-hand and the Elf-princess Lúthien, also called Tinúviel or Nightingale. I tell you this because I know of the first time Elessar set eyes upon the beautiful Undómiel: he was singing of Beren's first view of dancing Lúthien, clad in silver and blue, dark-haired and gem-crowned. Just then, Arwen Undómiel, clad and bejewelled in nearly the same manner, walked before him; believing himself the recipient of a vision, Aragorn called out -- just as Beren had -- \qTinúviel! Tinúviel!\q Is that not a sweet tale?
'No, he hadn't ever met her before, despite the fact that she is Elrond's child. Why? It is simple: she had been living here in Lothlórien, for this is the land of her mother's kin.'

'Now that you know the sweet history of Elessar and his lady-love Undómiel, perhaps you understand the solemnity of their joining and their parting.
'The happiest time they had together was the season they spent in Lórien, especially here upon Cerin Amroth. It is the habit of many of us who have known either of them to spend time upon the hill in the sunshine, reflecting upon the sacrifices they have made for each other. It is a good way to put one's problems into perspective, among other things.
'Would you like to do so as well? It must be during the day: as Aragorn said when they spoke their promises, neither the Shadow, which he always repudiates, nor the Twilight is for him, being mortal. Go to the southern side of the hill and <rgb=#FF0000>meditate</rgb> upon these matters for a time.'
'You have the peaceful look of one who has meditated, ${PLAYER}: solemn and peaceful.'

'Turmoil threatens our Golden Wood for the first time in many a year, ${PLAYER}; the ravages of Orc-kind to the north-west, the unusually aggressive river creatures to the south-east... I worry that fear may be taking more of a toll upon us than we might admit.
'I have an idea, and if you will help me see it to completion, it may aid in staving off the insidious dread that is the Enemy's weapon. Now, the golden flower we call elanor and its pale counterpart, niphredil, are nearly as much in the heart of every Elf as is Cerin Amroth itself, the hill upon which they grow. Their smell revives us; their gentle colours rest our eyes. Please, pick some and bring them to my friends elsewhere in Lothlórien.
'Maliriel is the Feast-mistress at Imlad Lalaith: follow the road east and south until you reach the Hythe, by the river. Ambendel is at Echad Andestel -- you may already have met him. Retrace your steps back to northern Nimrodel, south-west of here. Talan Fanuidhol is west of Cerin Amroth; there you will find Bahanneth, the quartermaster.'
'Mae govannen, ${PLAYER}. The hearts of Elves throughout the Golden Wood beat a little more lightly thanks to your errand.'

'Your pardon, friend, but I have no time to speak with you just now; there is too much to do to prepare for tonight. Whatever message Tuilinn has can wait... what have you for me?
'Elanor! And sweet niphredil. These shall have pride of place at my table tonight. Their smell will enhance every dish!
'My sincere thanks. Please, tell Tuilinn that she knows well how to lift a busy Elf's spirits.'

'Whence come you, friend, bearing pale niphredil and golden elanor?
'From Tuilinn at Cerin Amroth! My heart is gladdened by her gesture and by yours in bearing these blossoms here.
'Ah, these flowers never seem as bright when plucked from other hills! My sincere thanks to you, friend ${CLASS}; know that Ambendel is at your service.'

'I have no time just now for any... what is that aroma? By sea and stars! Whence came these blooms?
'Tuilinn has, as always, cut to the heart of the matter in her own quiet way. My steps are now lightened.
'I shall display these, that all the warriors here might also benefit from their sweet smell.'

'I beg your pardon! I needed a moment to compose myself, but I have dashed the water from my eyes and quit my uproarious laughter long enough to devise a wonderful plan. I am not a cruel dwarf, but this is an opportunity I cannot miss.
'You see, I came to this maze many days ago, hoping to see the sights, pass on through, and move along. But as I picked my way, I heard an Elf muttering about not being able to find the exit, but he grew silent when he perceived my presence. He followed me for a bit, but took a wrong turn. I came out at last, and I waited.
'Do you know that I have been here all these days since, and I have not seen so much as a hair from a single Elf-head, save that one standing near, waiting for her companions? My mirth has grown greater with every passing hour! This is the best festival I have ever been to. Now take these signs and post them everywhere you can and point them this way and that! Let us see how many more days it will take them now.'

'Oh, that is delightful! None have come out yet. Would you like to wait with me? We can fetch a pint at the festival and return in a moment, and then we shall continue to enjoy this most memorable scene.'

'All right, ${PLAYER}. Now that we've gathered evidence that there are some unusually strange creatures in the Water-works, we ought to have someone more knowledgeable than I take a look at what you've collected. Such a person should be able to shed some light on the matter.
'My old friend Hethuwen conducts studies of this sort in Shadowed Refuge, for she has a curious nature. Seek her there, and tell her I sent you to speak with her. She should be able to offer insight that will be helpful to us.'

'Well met, ${PLAYER}. How can I be of service to you? I hope nothing dire has brought you here this day.'
Hethuwen takes the package you brought and reads the note attentively.
'I see...Hasta, my zealous friend, is pursuing another wild rumour.'
Hethuwen shakes her head and a slight sigh can be heard passing her lips. She does not trouble to hide her amused smile.
'All right, all right, ${PLAYER}. Very well. I will help Hasta once more, but this is the last time! Just give me a few moments to look over these specimens, and I shall see whatever there is to see.'
'Yes? Can I help you?'

'The impertinence of the Elves is forgivable because of the hope Celeborn has kindled with the intent of his well-meaning message. I wish that I could invest every pair of hands in the expedition to re-igniting the lost lore of Durin's Day as our Elf-neighbour describes.
'Alas that I cannot spare them, for I know that fell rumours hiss from the deep wells of Nalâ-dûm where the water-wheels once spun; long ago did Khazad-dûm hum with the murmur of great power surges leaping across the caves. Celeborn's message has put a warmth in my heart... there must be a way to solve this problem.
'${PLAYER}, will you come to our aid again? I would ask you to travel to Nalâ-dûm with a small company and defeat whatever menace lurks there, for something has destroyed the works that once pumped life into these silent halls. If you find anything of value while you are there, I would give you a sturdy reward for such priceless knowledge.'

'I do not think I can bow low enough to show you the honour I feel, ${PLAYER}. Truly, I cannot believe the extent of your success. The Dwarves of Khazad-dûm owe you much for what you have accomplished today!

'While you are there, you should defeat many lizards. As long as they are living there, the Water-wheels of Nalâ-dûm will never be clean as they should be. Return to me when you are done, and tell me if I guessed right. There are great dangers there, so I would take a friend or two.'

'The scales of rock-worms are hard as bone and can strengthen our armour with very little smithing effort. I'll not lecture you on our process of tailoring these scales to fit our hauberks, for I fear there isn't time for proper instruction.
'If you could collect some rock-worm scales while you are there, I would be very grateful. The scales may turn many an Orc-sword, and the warriors shall be in your debt.'
'So many scales! I am at your service, ${PLAYER}. I hope that you did not meet too much hardship in Nalâ-dûm.'
'Did you find any scales for our armour? You should find them upon the worms of Nalâ-dûm.'

Bring the worm-scales to Dór

Dór of the Chamber of the Cross-roads believes that worms will be among the creeping, slimy beasts in Nalâ-dûm where the Water-wheels sleep. The scales of rock-worms can be used to lend extra strength to armour.
'Have you been yet to Nalâ-dûm in the Water-works? You may find the scales I seek upon the worms there.'

The scales can be found on the skins of worms in Nalâ-dûm, below the Chamber of the Cross-roads in the Water-works.
You should collect scales while in Nalâ-dûm for the dwarves to tailor into their armour. This will strengthen their defences significantly.

'My good ${CLASS}, your efforts were quite successful but the Orcs do not lack for numbers, and they continue to move supplies out from the depths of Moria.
'I think you should pay them another visit. We would not wish them to become complacent, after all, would we?
'Defeat the smiths that have come to replace those slain and destroy their new weapon-stores, then return here to me.'

'The Orcs may not be the most powerful of foes, but they are numerous, determined, and some among their number are dangerously clever in the ways of siege-craft -- particularly when they are crafting designs supplied by the Enemy himself.
'You have stolen away many of the parts they had hoped to use in the construction of cunning engines of war, but some remain, and even without them their smiths will strive to build more primitive -- but still quite lethal -- weapons.
'I would like to see most of those Orcs defeated, for without them, their soldiers have no real hope of infiltrating the defences of our forest.'
'Excellent work, my friend! As long as we can continue to disrupt their preparations, the Orcs shall find their efforts to assault Lórien fruitless and most costly indeed.'
Defeat Orc-smiths (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Destroy weapon-stores (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

Disarming the Foe
Bahanneth is concerned about the siege-parts you stole from the Orcs. Even without them, they will be able to construct primitive weapons to conduct a siege.

'The Orcs will have some trouble replacing those stores quickly, ${PLAYER}. Well done!'

'I am Bahanneth, the Quartermaster of this force. Are you here to help in our struggle against the Orcs? Our scouts have noticed that they are cutting a great deal of lumber -- likely for use in constructing fortifications and siege-engines. We must not stand by while such a threat develops!
'Were matters more urgent, I would ask you to burn those supplies, but as things are not yet that pressing, I would have you take these phials of liquid and apply it to their wood piles before they are finished curing. This will weaken the wood, rendering it useless for their purposes -- but without their knowledge.
'The Orcs have also recently brought a number of crates out from their stores deep in Moria -- I would like you to steal the contents of a number of these crates so that we can perhaps guess at what evils they are preparing.'

'Excellent! These parts were for the construction and repair of siege-weapons. The Orcs shall have to make do without them, thanks to your efforts.
'You also dealt with their supplies of lumber? That is well.'

Collect contents from crates (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

Bahanneth's scouts report that the Orcs of Fanuidhol may be preparing to attempt some sort of incursion or even a siege of Lothlórien. He has asked you to take some pre-emptive measures to disrupt their plans before they pose any real threat.

'My thanks for your help disrupting the Orcs' plans for siege. It is not that they have any hope of overcoming the defences of Lórien, but we must save all our strength for the far greater battles to come....'

The lumber and crates are at the Orc-encampment of Drûmaudhul, north-west of Talan Fanuidhol.

'Blasted nuisances! Even the dullest dwarf knows that you don't over-mine a cavern. Riddle it with holes, and the whole floor is apt to collapse. Well, the cave-claws don't know that and their incessant digging is going to be the ruin of us all!
'What? You expect the Dourhands to do something about it? A clever jest, but I'm not laughing. Can you lend us some aid in dealing with the pests? The cave-claws, mind you...not the Dourhands. Although....
'Be that as it may, the Rockbelly Pit is overrun with cave-claws. Head east and up the hill to Winterheight. The entrance to the Pit is there.'
'You certainly took care of that problem. I'll see to it that the Dourhands do their part from now on.'
Defeat cave-claws (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Bolli in Frerin's Court
Cave-dwelling Menace
The stone beneath Thorin's Gate is honeycombed by cave-claw burrows. If the damage continues, the entire area could be weakened enough to collapse in upon itself.

'Cave-claws! I hate them! Always ripping up the ground, leaving piles of earth in their wake. And who has to clean up their mess? The Longbeards, that's who!
'Give us a hand, will you?'
'You did a good thing back there!'

Cave-claws are found near the buildings and caves to the east of Thorin's Gate and inside the Rockbelly Pit caves near Winterheight, south-east of the Frerin's Court.

'The dwarves' establishment of a foothold in Durin's halls could not have come at a more fortuitous time, for I find that the presence of a certain guest in our lands has drawn the eyes of many foes, near and far.
'There is a great presence of trolls in Dâr Narbugud, and they are deadly foes even when running carelessly about. Imagine the damage that could be done to the dwarves when the trolls are guided by leaders.
'The dwarves are doughty fighters, but I do not believe they will withstand the might of well-led trolls, least of all trolls corrupted by the sickness and plague brewing in Dâr Narbugud. You should destroy the leaders outright, and the lesser trolls will surely be weakened without proper guidance from their superiors. This task will require a great force, to be sure.'

'You have done well, ${PLAYER}! I rejoice that you have returned in triumph. It is no small feat to have bested such brutal creatures as the wicked trolls you have faced. You must have the favour of Lady Galadriel to have survived a battle of this magnitude without falling.'
Defeat Rung
Defeat Blagh

Dâr Narbugud: Bastions of Doom

The Elves believe that trolls give a great advantage to the enemy in battle, due to their massive strength and hardiness. The troll-leaders in Dâr Narbugud must be eliminated in order to weaken the enemy's forces.
'The trolls you seek can be found in Dâr Narbugud. You should gather your allies and make haste, ${PLAYER}. The Lord and Lady fear that the dwarves' foothold is not yet strong.'

The trolls you seek can be found in Dâr Narbugud, near the Dark Delvings at the southernmost tip of the Foundations of Stone.
Donfuin has asked you to defeat the trolls' leaders, which should disorganize the trolls and deflate their usefulness in battle.

Donfuin stands just outside of Dâr Narbugud.

The hilt is ice-cold and gives off a fell glow, and it is blackened with the remnants of its Nameless bearer. You would cast it aside without further thought, for it is a sickening relic, but something catches your eye: Elven-script. The letters inscribed upon the hilt are clear, unfaded Sindarin.
This artifact may have a colourful history. How did it come to live in the hands of this hideous creature? You should bring the hilt to one who may recognize it.

'What treasure have you unearthed in Dâr Narbugud, ${PLAYER}? It was a keen observation that let you perceive the writing beneath the grime, for the words have lost their power and their light.
'This is a Silvan blade from the Second Age, and its script tells of sun on golden boughs and likens them to the mighty arm of a marchwarden. I would not be at all surprised if an inhabitant of Lórien knew the one who bore this sword.
'This is the blade of a guard or a warrior who drew upon the beauty and majesty of the mallorns to lend him power when he bore this blade into battle. A warrior of the woods may know this haft.'

'Bright were the eyes of he who bore this blade to battle long ago. Yes, I remember the sword and the bearer! He was my friend, and we went forth together into many perils.
'Seasons uncounted have turned since he departed Middle-earth to go to the Undying Lands, as is the fate of all my kin. I have remained and will watch over this land until the time of the Elves has passed.
'I have often wondered what became of him, for my heart whispered that he never came to the Sea. Did he meet his doom in Moria where the Nameless walk on black roads? Alas!'
Bring the hilt to Celeborn at Caras Galadhon
Find someone who may recognize the hilt
Dâr Narbugud: The Bewildering Inscription

One of the Nameless creatures that prowled the twisted passages of Dâr Narbugud was found carrying a strange sword-hilt, bearing an inscription in unmistakeable Sindarin letters. While this haft is now fell and cold to the touch, its history might be of interest to one who remembers its making.

Celeborn can be found in Lothlórien's main city, Caras Galadhon.
You should show the corrupted hilt you have found to Celeborn, whose wisdom and long memory may dispel the mystery surrounding this artifact.

Celeborn believes that the sword hilt will be recognizeable to someone who lives in Lothlórien. He surmises, based on the words on the handle, that the warrior of old was a loyal protector of the Golden Wood.
You should seek someone who may recognize the befouled relic.

'You have felt the malice in Dâr Narbugud during your long toils there, have you not? I suspect that you will find a great force at the heart of the evil will. Such is always the case in the black places of the world, as I am sure you have found in your many ventures.
'If you intend to complete the greater task I have given you of banishing the darkness, you must first uproot the evil that is the source of the pestilence.
'May you and your allies go well, ${PLAYER}, and do not allow your valour to waver. Those with pure hearts beating in their breasts will not be swallowed by the sickness of Moria. Defeat the menace and come back hale to allay my fears for the safety of Free Peoples.'

'Glad am I to see you well, ${RACE}. I am heartened indeed by all that passed in Dâr Narbugud, the beating heart of corruption in Moria.
'The dwarves of the expedition will feel the good of your deed at once, for the bane of their purpose there has been felled by the might of your valiant host. You shall be honoured by the Elves also for quenching the flames of a threat that may have spread far and ruined many fair things.'
Defeat the Mistress of Pestilence
Defeat the Blind One

Celeborn of Lothlórien believes that the restoration of the natural world is key in the battle against the powers of evil in Middle-earth.

'I bid you take care, ${PLAYER}, when you face the source of the sickness in Moria. It will not be an easy task. Go to Dâr Narbugud; do your best to stand against the blight that corrupts the fiends who wish to bring harm to all that is good.'

The source of the pestilence in Moria is near the Dark Delvings at the southernmost tip of the Foundations of Stone, in a foul place called Dâr Narbugud.
Donfuin wishes you and your allies to defeat the Nameless sources of the sickness spewing from Dâr Narbugud, thus removing the threat of the fungal plague's spread.

'When you travel to Dâr Narbugud, I believe you will find it filled with an unwholesome air. It is my expectation that the very air provides a lush breeding ground for the corruption that takes place in that sickly place.
'You should seek out the vents from whence the noxious air passes. If you destroy the belching mouths, perhaps the things that grow so freely amongst the gases will not find the environment so hospitable.
'I imagine that you will find great fumaroles in Dâr Narbugud, ${PLAYER}. I have studied things of this kind, and wherever there is bad air in an enclosed space such as this, a gasping vent is usually the source of the trouble.'

'I take it the air of Dâr Narbugud was not to your liking, ${PLAYER}? I am not at all surprised.
'You did well to destroy the living vents that gasped the foul fumes into that sickly space. There will now be less fodder for the vile things that grow there.'

'There will be lesser creatures in Dâr Narbugud, mere pawns who are but carriers of the sickness their masters wish to spread.
'I believe that the weak, virulent pawns of plague must be wholly destroyed, ere they can emerge from Moria and spread the fungus throughout these lands. I know of no cure for the disease they bear, nor is an Orc deserving of our pity, no matter how much they suffer. They relish torture, and the despair of all creatures but themselves.
'Be wary, for Dâr Narbugud is a terrible place. You should go in strength.'

'You have done well this day, ${PLAYER}. I know that the slaughter of the weak, no matter how vile, cannot ever be a pleasant task. But take heart: if you are gripped by black thoughts, you have done a great service to the world beyond this deep pit.'

In order to keep the pestilence from creeping to the fair lands beyond the walls of Moria, the Elves of Lothlórien believe the fungus-infested Orcs must be stopped ere they emerge from Moria.

'Kind ${CLASS}, you have done much for us in these ventures to Dâr Narbugud. I see that our wishes are the same: we both desire to see the balance of Moria restored and for all the unnatural blights to be swept away.
'Please take this ere you depart. It is a phial of pure water from Galadriel's garden, clear and clean as spring rain, and blessed by my Lady ere it was passed to my hands. You may use it to purify the deadly liquid in the chambers where the Orcs undergo their transformation.
'The roots of evil will wither and die with this draught flowing as blood in their veins. A little purity may go far in that forsaken place, ${PLAYER}. This draught of Lórien will bring an end to the fell winter of sickness and plague in Dâr Narbugud.'

'You have done well, ${PLAYER}! You have played a great role in our time, for Moria and for fair Lothlórien as well.
'The sickness bred by the contamination of the waters in Dâr Narbugud will not trouble us further, thanks to you and your noble companions.'

'Târgrat is a proud and arrogant creature...he will not abide your mockery.'

'Whence hail you and wherefore come you here, brave ${RACE}? To have come this far into the Golden Wood, you must have earned the trust of the archers who guard our borders. That is why I feel able to ask you for aid: I have orders that I fear I cannot fulfil alone. Will you help?
'Have you ever sighted one of the majestic Great Eagles who hail from eyries north of the High Pass in the Misty Mountains? Well, my orders are to keep a stringent look-out for one of them -- it is not my privilege to know why. Will you go to the nearby Telain -- Talan being our word for the platforms in the trees that you call flets -- and <rgb=#FF0000>look</rgb> for them?
'Talan Brethil is south-east of here, along the banks of the Anduin. Talan Gwilith and Talan Fanuidhol are well west and a bit south of here, along the border of Fanuidhol, where the Orcs have recently emerged from Moria.'

'Nothing? You are certain? Ah well.
'The truth is, I have no idea why any of the Great Eagles should be paying us a visit at this time anyway.'

'You have my thanks for this delivery, ${PLAYER}. This wood will serve nicely as a cask for fine Elven wine.'

'Our efforts here are to recover the land from this new threat, that is clear. We are also here at the behest of our kinsmen.

'Nature calls once again from the vale, I can feel it course through my being. We cannot rest on this virtue, but you have brought hope where there was sorrow, ${PLAYER}. You have earned my favour.'

Dwalin Lord of the Longbeards of the Blue Mountains Steward of Thorin's Hall'

'Greetings, ${PLAYER}. You come at an auspicious time -- but one that finds me ill prepared for my duties. You see, I am the Mistress of the Feast for Lothlórien, and it falls to me to prepare a great banquet.
'Yet I find myself with few hands to prepare such an event, for many have been called away to guard the borders of our forest or to sojourn further afield against the foes of the Elves.
'So I ask you, if you will, to seek out my companions who labour here and to the south towards the vineyards, and offer them whatever aid you may in these preparations, for time grows short!'

'${PLAYER}, I am delighted! You have made all the preparations seem so much less arduous and allowed me to more fully devote my time and attention to the complicated ones.

'${PLAYER}, you have considerably lightened my burdens! You have my gratitude.'

'We cannot let another moment pass without informing others of the arrival of the goblins. Perhaps Lord Dorongúr's protection is weakening as we make our way to the shores to depart -- or perhaps the Enemy grows stronger faster than we expect.
'Regardless, ${PLAYER}, we must send word back to Celondim and my superior there. Quickly, return to Laenin the Glade-watcher at Celondim and tell him of what you have found.
'You will find Laenin at the docks in Celondim north-east of this vale.'

'This discovery is worrisome. I will see that this information is passed along to Lord Dorongúr at Duillond.
'We never would have learned of this if not for you, ${PLAYER}. We are in your debt.'
Talk to Laenin the Glade-watcher at Celondim
A Word of Warning

The discovery of a goblin-crafted collar about the neck of the wolves in the valley of Nen Hilith sparks serious concern amongst the Elves. Quick action will be necessary and those with the ability to do something about the menace must be informed.
'Hurry back to Laenin and report what we have found here. He is at Celondim to the south-east.'

Hurry back to Celondim and speak with Laenin the Glade-watcher.
Your discovery of a wolf-collar hewn by goblin crafters has proven a frightening occurrence to the glade wardens. You have been charged with bringing this news to their leader in the Elf-port of Celondim.

'Please lend me your aid in driving them off!'

'The crebain are descending even now! Stand by my side, and we shall drive them off!'

'Recent travellers through our outpost say they've seen large numbers of hendrevail across the river to our south. If you're looking for the source of their numbers, that's as likely to be it as not.'

'The bravery and cunning of your allies have bested the mighty trolls of Dâr Narbugud, ${PLAYER}. I was not certain that you would be up to the task I placed upon you, but you are a worthy warrior. I know now that you can accomplish great deeds.
'Now that the first step has been taken, I believe that we can behead the force that threatens to rise against ourselves and the dwarves. Without its head, a serpent will not survive. I believe the same will apply to the armies being rallied in Dâr Narbugud.
'Take your allies and go back, ${PLAYER}, and defeat the leaders of the Orcs who writhe with the fungal plague. With these masters gone, the servants will not be half so deadly as they are now.'
'You have done very well, ${PLAYER}, but there is more that must be done. Lord Celeborn wishes to speak with you.'

Talk to Donfuin
Dâr Narbugud: Champions of Virulence

The great leaders of the Globsnaga in Dâr Narbugud are essential to the strength and strategy of the enemy. They must be destroyed before they can lead their Globsnaga-hosts to war against the dwarves and Elves of the neighbouring lands.
'Dâr Narbugud, as you know, lies just south of here. You should go there and defeat the pestilent leaders of the Globsnaga forces.'

The leaders of the Globsnaga can be found in Dâr Narbugud, in the southern-most reaches of the Foundations of Stone.
You should defeat each leader of the Globsnaga to sever the head of the force that rallies in in Dâr Narbugud.

'We do not often welcome strangers within our borders, ${PLAYER}, but here we shall make an exception for you. Lady Galadriel is aware that you are recently come from Moria, where you have done much to help secure the dwarves' footing there. She bade me not to hinder your crossing of the Nimrodel. You are welcome to take refuge in our talan and share of our provisions, for I must speak with you at length on a serious matter.
'You may have noticed that Orcs are pressing closer and closer to Lothlórien, fairest of Elven-homes, and that there are plots and stirrings in Moria to set all the Free Peoples in this area ill at ease. It is therefore crucial that the dwarves hold fast in their newly reclaimed home; their coming was an unforeseen blessing at a most fortuitous time! Our enemies' eyes are divided with stout warriors and builders shaking the walls of their dark haven.
'But the dwarves are not secure. They need our help. In the Chamber of the Cross-roads, you will find an important dwarf who goes by the name of Hrólfur. He oversees much of what the expedition endeavours to accomplish. He did not wish to speak to our messenger, but you have reputation as a hero among the Iron Garrison. He will listen to you! Hasten to him if you will, and bring him this note. I want you to help the dwarves as a token of good will from the Galadhrim.'

'I am relieved beyond all of my expectations that you have done so well in your task, ${PLAYER}. But do not wander away just yet -- there is someone I would have you seek.
'Please stay a moment more and hear what I have to say.'

'So you come from the land of the meddling Elves, do you? I am sorry you took the trouble of coming all this way for naught! I know what they seek: for their backs to be shielded by the blood of the dwarves while they wander ever in peace in their haunted eaves.'
'I will read this message, but... what? Indeed, I am a great fool. Lord Celeborn speaks of Moria flooded with rays of light and the creaking of the water-wheels. Such ideas were lost to us when Durin fell.
'I now have two great tasks to achieve. Lumul-nar and Nalâ-dûm, as Celeborn describes from his long memory, were great halls from whence the light and water flooded Khazad-dûm. They now lie dormant, surely under the sway of evil, as we find with all the once-fair halls of our great kingdom. Can you help us to restore them, ${PLAYER}? Please find some information on how this can be done!'
'Is there anything you want? I am a busy dwarf, traveller.'
Bring Celeborn's letter to Hrólfur
Help the dwarves regain control of Lumul-nar
Help the dwarves regain control of Nalâ-dûm
Talk to Haldir at Talan Haldir
The Good Will of the Galadhrim

The Galadhrim of Lothlórien feel the pressing of danger upon their borders from many sides, but never so violently as the recent attacks from Moria since the arrival of a secret company in the Golden Wood. Haldir, a marchwarden of the Nimrodel, wishes to secure a friendship with the dwarves of Khazad-dûm so that the evils of Moria may be kept at bay, for the safety of both lands.

'Time is pressing, ${PLAYER}. Make haste! Hrólfur is in the Chamber of the Cross-roads in Moria. I only hope that you will find him more friendly than our first messenger did. The letter explains all -- if he is rational, he will heed our words.'

Hrólfur, an important overseer, can likely be found in the Chamber of the Cross-roads in Moria, in Durin's Way.

Haldir awaits news of your good deeds towards the dwarves upon his flet near the River Nimrodel, on the western border of Lothlórien.
You should seek Haldir and inform him of all that passed while you assisted the dwarves.

'Remember, a Captain does not best serve his companions by running recklessly into the fray. Nay, it is when he stands behind and directs the efforts of his fellows that he truly shines. There he can see weaknesses in his enemies or press his companions forwards and inspire them to victory.

'I find that there is always more to do if we are to keep evil at bay. Lord Celeborn wishes now to speak with you. When you are able, you should go to Caras Galadhon, the city at the heart of our realm.
'I will return to my duties of guarding our borders and watching... watching for the tides of change. You see, change comes with every passing moment, but once in an age, the flowing rivers of time will swell and flood, and things will never be as they were ere the waters came.
'This is no time for the rambling of a wary Elf, though. Lord Celeborn is afraid of what brews within Moria. Lady Galadriel fears it too. There are rumours that our stainless lands will not withstand this threat. I think you know of what I speak, but I will not darken the day further by speaking of it here.'

'Welcome to Caras Galadhon. A friend of Mithrandir and his Company is a friend to the Elves of Lothlórien also. My Lady spoke well of you when first she heard of your coming, but I wished to see for myself how well you served Haldir and Baranglim before employing your skills myself.
'As you have surely seen, Moria is beset with perils, but none so virulent as the disease borne hither and thither wherever the Nameless and sickly creatures prowl. My Lady and I fear that with the brewing of war, the fungus-carriers will be unleashed as the final weapon, and I do not deny that this would be a deadly blow to our stainless land.
'Please go to the cavern where the infected army amasses and bring this phial with you when you go. Use it in the darkest place, and the darkness will shrink and wither as if the full sun and fresh air were beating upon it from the above world. You must gather a full host of allies for this venture, for it will not be easy.'

'Ah! ${PLAYER}, you return hale! You have done what few could in this day and age. Your great deeds are indeed as worthy as the rumours boldly declared. You shall have the blessing of the Elves wherever you go from this day forward. You have saved Moria, Lórien, and undoubtedly the larger world from a terrible fate.
'Alas that we cannot celebrate... not yet. My heart quails again when I look to the East. Perhaps your path will lead you thither someday....'
Talk to Celeborn at Caras Galadhon
Use the phial of light
Use the phial of light
Talk to Celeborn at Caras Galadhon
Dâr Narbugud: The Heart of the Scourge

Celeborn, Lord of Lothlórien, is gravely concerned by the final and most perilous threat in Moria: the plague of fungus threatening to spread with the infected Orcs as they rally to defend their caverns against the dwarves and Elves.
'Gather what strength and nourishment you can while you are here, ${PLAYER}. You should prepare yourself for the death and corruption you will meet in Dâr Narbugud in Moria's Foundations of Stone.'
'Speak with Lord Celeborn as soon as you are able, friend. We must do our best to rid Moria of its ills. Go to Caras Galadhon, if you can.'

Celeborn is in Caras Galadhon, at the heart of Lothlórien.
You should speak with Celeborn at the behest of Baranglim to gain his counsel about the final and most important task to be achieved in Moria.

Dâr Narbugud is in the Foundations of Stone in Moria, to the south-east near the Dark Delvings.
Celeborn has given you a phial of Elven light to bring to the heart of plague, sickness, and corruption within Moria.

Celeborn stands at the heart of Lothlórien, in the hidden city of Caras Galadhon.
You should speak with Celeborn and share the tale of your great success in Dâr Narbugud, dealing a heavy blow to the creatures who would cover the world in sickness.
Collected the Elf-stone
You have banished the evil from this place

'My friend Baranglim has watchful eyes and a wise heart. He has seen much, and I know that Celeborn has taken counsel with him recently regarding the Enemy's activity on the borders of Lórien. Baranglim has gone to Moria to see what can be seen.
'Rumour has reached us of a great rousing of a war-force out of Moria. The Orcs have taken the Halls of Crafting, and use the forges of the dwarves to brew war. You should seek Baranglim in Moria, and aid him. I know he made for the Flaming Deeps.'

'Well met, ${PLAYER}. I have been expecting you since my counsel with Lord Celeborn. Haldir has told you a little of our plight, has he not? I will continue the story.
'Not long ago, a strange company came under our protection. They passed through Moria and brought behind them a trail of bold and angry Orcs. Our foes rally at many outposts on our borders. They have great strength and are driven by bitter malice. Their armour is thick, such as we have not seen since the dwarves wore the armour of Durin's time, and their weapons are hard and cruel.
'I believe they are using the Halls of Crafting in Moria to produce great stores of tools to assist them in the war. Lord Celeborn agrees, and we fear for ourselves and for the dwarves. Will you go to the source and banish the evil from that place? You will need stout allies to aid you on this venture. Take this Elf-stone; if you defeat our enemies and place the Elf-stone there, they will fear to return.'

'I thought that it would be so! I am glad your venture was not in vain, and that you escaped from the peril unharmed. Lady Galadriel made a subtle remark about your coming to our lands, and I discerned from her words that you were a doer of great deeds. I see that you will have much influence over this harrowing time, and that gives me hope.
'I was sure you would rise to this challenge admirably, and you did so. You have my thanks. A burden has been lifted from my mind.'
'Did you see to the evil in the Halls of Crafting, ${PLAYER}?'
Talk to Baranglim
Place the Elf-stone in the Halls of Crafting
Talk to Haldir
Halls of Crafting: Banishing War

Baranglim of Lórien, a perceptive scout, has theories about the movements and activities of the Orcs in the Halls of Crafting. He believes that war is brewing and that the Orcs are producing a great store of armour, weapons, and vile draughts within Moria.
'Do not tarry overlong, ${PLAYER}, for haste is needed if we are to defeat the enemies who are fueling the war. Enter the Halls of Crafting through the door to my left.'
'Baranglim is in the Flaming Deeps of Moria, near the Halls of Crafting. You should go to him and hear what he has to say, for he has quick eyes and a perceptive mind.'

Baranglim can be found in the Flaming Deeps of Moria, near the Halls of Crafting.
You should go to Baranglim and speak with him about what must be done to weaken the Orc-forces rallying to assault Lothlórien.

Haldir is upon his talan on the banks of the Nimrodel, in Lothlórien.
You should speak with Haldir and tell him all that you saw and achieved in the Halls of Crafting.

'Ancient battles were fought at the ruins of Dol Ringwest, and we had thought the evil purged. Now, goblins toil within the ruins and desecrate the memory of the place.
'I would ask that you do your best to clear the goblins from these ruins. It will ease my heart and perhaps aid my brother Toronn to leave in peace.
'You will find the goblins in residence of Dol Ringwest to the west of Duillond. Please, make your way there and drive these foul creatures from the ruins.'

'The memory of that place will always be one of melancholy. Knowing that the goblins have been purged restores a small amount of hope to me, ${PLAYER}.
'You have brought a timely resolution with regard to Dol Ringwest, and I thank you for this.'

'While in the ruins, I would ask that you seek out the leader of the goblins there, Durglup. He is a particularly nasty goblin and should not be underestimated.
'You will find this creature within the confines of Dol Ringwest, to the west of Duillond. Return to me when the beast is slain.'

'The Dourhands do nothing to stem the growth of the wolves in this area. It is no surprise, to be honest. Despite their newfound ties to their cousins the Longbeards, the Dourhands are the same dwarves that Skorgrím led against Edhelion centuries ago. We cannot expect them to be proper stewards of the land.
'Go into the wilds and cull the wolf population. You can find them on and near the frozen lake down the road from here. You can also find them within the confines of the Berghold, once a holding of the dwarves now lost to these wolves.'
'Collect the pelts from these creatures and see them delivered to Nos Grimsong, a Longbeard, within Frerin's Court. Nos, a friend of the thrushes, will understand the meaning behind the furs.'

'Ho there, ${RACE}. What brings you to Frerin's court? Ah, grim business I see.
'I understand well that nature is thrown into imbalance here. Our cousins have not been the best caretakers of this land. I only hope that Lord Dwalin can talk some sense into them.
'The lesson will not go to waste on me. You have my thanks.'
'Is there something that I can do for you, good ${RACE}?'

When the Elves left Edhelion, evil was able to regain a foothold in the valley. One of the creatures to return were the wolves. They now stalk the valley and make misery for the dwarves of Thorin's Hall.

'I am glad Haldir sent you my way, ${PLAYER}. Thank you for offering to share the burdens that have weighed upon me since first we learned of what stirred in the Halls of the Dwarves. I have observed a rousing of Orcs from Moria as has not been seen in many a long day.
'In the Halls of Crafting, a great leader of the Enemy's forces is overseeing the war and the gathering of foes. They would be naught but a mindless rabble if there were no greater leaders among them, so I must assume that there is one around whom the stormcloud rallies.
'The Orcs speak his name with fear when they do not perceive our watchfulness. He is Thaguzg. It is a name I do not like to speak. You should defeat this foe ere you partake in the cleansing of the Halls of Crafting. I know it will not be easy, for his minions are strong; therefore he will be mighty. You should bring many friends with you on this venture, and may you return in good health to look upon our fair lands again.'
'You have done well indeed, ${PLAYER}! It is more than I dared to hope. Glad I am to see you well upon your return, with no grievous wounds. You have the thanks of the Galadhrim.'

'Cruel Thaguzg will surely be found in the Halls of Crafting in Moria. You should travel there when you have gathered strong allies to your side.'

Thaguzg can be found deep within the Halls of Crafting, in the southern reaches of Moria's Flaming Deeps.

'Many have made the mistake of believing Orcs to be mindless, useless war-mongers, but it is Elves they take after, shaped in a darker likeness of ourselves. It is true that many lack true cunning or skill, but some Orcs are foes to be reckoned with. These are keen of mind and can be brilliant in their efforts to cover the world in darkness.
'I believe that the Orcs in the Halls of Crafting are of this nature. That place is rife with an abundance of tools, and it is just the sort of place a fertile Orc-mind could use to devise weapons meant to inflict great wounds upon his enemies.
'When you go to the Halls of Crafting, look out for the Orcs who stand proudly among the rest -- Âmbal and Bashkuga they are called; they will be the masters of the craft. Their minds cannot be left to inhabit a place where so many fell devices will be produced.'

'Ah, ${PLAYER}! You cannot know what a great deed you have done this day. All Orcs are deadly, but brilliant and crafty ones are all the more so. You may have saved many, many lives by felling Âmbal and Bashkuga, experts of the crafts of war.'
Defeat Bashkuga
Defeat Âmbal
Talk to Baranglim
Halls of Crafting: Experts of the Forge
The wisdom of Baranglim, a watchful scout of the Galadhrim, warns that the movements of the Orcs indicates organized leadership of the war-force that brews in the Halls of Crafting in Moria.
'The Halls of Crafting are in Moria's Flaming Deeps, friend. You should hurry and defeat Âmbal and Bashkuga, for their continued foothold there will come at the cost of many dear lives.'

Âmbal and Bashkuga can surely be found in the Halls of Crafting in Moria, found in the southern reaches of the Flaming Deeps near Fil Gashan.
Baranglim has asked you to defeat Âmbal and Bashkuga, the expert Orc-artisans in the Halls of Crafting, for they cannot be allowed to produce more weapons of war to be used against dwarves and Elves alike.

Destroyed draught

'Let me share a disturbing story with you before you hasten into Moria's Halls of Crafting. Three nights ago, I trailed a small band of rough-looking Orcs as they sped to rejoin their host in the Halls of Crafting. They were weary, and they complained bitterly to their leader.
'The leader then passed a flask among his companions, and as they drank I caught the scent of a strong, bitter liquor; it seemed to burn their very tongues. But when they stood again, they appeared more grim, for their eyes blazed with a newfound fervour. We Elves have drinks which lend us strength on long journeys, but I had not fathomed that the Orcs could ever craft such a draught.
'When you go to the Halls of Crafting with your companions, you should all seek to destroy as much of their supply as possible. I will not deny that my heart quailed at seeing the Orcs so roused, ${PLAYER}. If this mixture is indeed being produced to strengthen an army, we have great reason to be concerned.'

'You did a brave and dangerous deed to go to the place where this wicked drink was being produced. I hope that the Enemy was caught unawares by the arrival of your small but valiant host and did not have time to harden themselves against your coming.'
Destroy the foul draught of the Enemy
Talk to Gornellon
Halls of Crafting: Odious Draughts
Gornellon of Lothlórien is concerned that the Orcs, ever in their foul mimicry of the Elves, have devised mixtures meant to lend them unnatural strength, not unlike the mirúvor draught of the Elves.
'I fear of what the Orcs may be capable of with that terrible draught lending them strength and stamina. You should hasten to the Halls of Crafting and destroy as much of the draught as you can.'

The Halls of Crafting are in the southern reaches of the Flaming Deeps in Moria, near Fil Gashan.
Gornellon, a wary Galadhrim scout, wishes you to destroy the draught being made to lend strength to the Orc forces planning an assault against Lórien.

Gornellon is outside the Halls of Crafting, in the Flaming Deeps.
You should speak with Gornellon and inform him of your success against the Orc-draughts being brewed in the Halls of Crafting.

'Baranglim tells me that you are in Moria to fight the Orcs who have been troubling the borders of our land. I am glad of it, ${PLAYER}, for our guards are hard-pressed to keep the Enemy's advances at bay in Lórien. I have seen many things in my long days of watching over the woods, and I have great concern for the force of arms being mustered here.
'I worry about what will become of us if the Orcs hold the Halls of Crafting in Moria, for there is dwarf-made armour there and great weapons of old that would be fell in the hands of evil. The dwarves deserve to reclaim the weapons and armour that remains unspoiled, if any indeed remain.
'With armour shielding the dwarves and not our foes and weapons of old clenched in their worthy hands, I foresee that the tide of this war could change ere it breaks upon the eaves of our fair realm.'
'You have done remarkably well, friend. Your eye for quality is excellent; these pieces will indeed be more than acceptable to our new neighbours in this dangerous chasm that is Moria.'
'Have you found anything of use? The Halls of Crafting can be found in the Flaming Deeps of Moria. You should go there with a small host of companions if you wish to be successful in your venture.'

This brood-queen is far more fearsome than any spider you have come across before and seems to be manipulating many of the events around Archet.

'You are most worthy of the name Spider-bane, O Slayer of Iornaith!'

'Hello, ${PLAYER}. Hrólfur tells me you are here to give us a leg up on our enemies. I will not turn my nose up at the help! The illumination of our halls will wreak havoc on the ill-accustomed eyes of Moria's foes.
'When I was exploring Durin's Way, I very nearly found myself in Lumul-nar, where you plan to go. But some great evil there sapped my will, and I decided I valued my life more than my curiosity at that particular moment.
'I saw and heard many clues of what terror may lurk within, but I do not wish to speak of it. All I ask is that you defeat whatever holds Lumul-nar, the Hall of Mirrors, in its evil clutches. But I beg you to bring a friend or two with you, for I had not the heart to make this venture alone.'
'The creature is defeated? Then you have done what I could not! I applaud you, ${PLAYER}. Your services to the Iron Garrison will never be forgotten.'
Defeat the evil presence in the Hall of Mirrors
Talk to Frár
Lumul-nar: The Bane of Illumination
Frár of the Chamber of the Cross-roads explored near the entrance to Lumul-nar, the Hall of Mirrors, and recalls that a great feeling of menace turned him from his path.
'The menace of Lumul-nar awaits you in the Hall of Mirrors, ${PLAYER}. You should strike north from here, towards Zirakzigil. The entrance to Lumul-nar is beyond there.'

The Hall of Mirrors can be found in Zirakzigil, to the north of the Chamber of the Cross-roads.

Collected a lesser ring (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'The merrevail that I believe to reside in Lumul-nar are greedy creatures by nature, so I can only assume that they possess hoards of dwarf-relics. How my beard quivers to think of those distasteful wretches handling our precious goods!
'When you go to Lumul-nar, I bid you to reclaim as many such relics as you can from the creatures that dwell there. Curse their vile filth! I wonder what you will find when you go?
'You should bring a friend or two with you, ${PLAYER}. I do not think it will be easy to wrest the precious goods from the grasp of such horrid beasts as the ones you will face on this venture. I do not want to see you wheeled back to me in pieces, torn limb-from-limb by the greedy wretches of Lumul-nar.'

'Rings! Of all the things I imagined, this was not one of them. These rings are lesser rings -- the seven Great Rings given to the dwarves were lost, yes, but lesser rings were handed out to those blessed by the favour of Durin. You have found them! We did not even know where to begin looking. Now the ancient heroes of Moria can be remembered as they deserved, for these rings are inscribed with their names and those of their families. I wonder if any of these families have survived to our generation....
'What a delightful project this will be, to reunite my folk with such an important piece of history! Thank you, ${PLAYER}!'
'Have you found anything of worth in Lumul-nar?'

Lumul-nar: The Lesser Rings
Frár believes that the greedy creatures of Lumul-nar may have some relics of interest in their possession, and wishes to know all that he can of any ancient tokens found in the Hall of Mirrors.

'I believe Hrólfur wanted me to arrange this meeting with you because I am the only dwarf thus far to venture so near the entrance to Lumul-nar before my courage failed. I heard many chilling shrieks that made me tremble, and the smell was terrible.
'All I could imagine was fluttering bat-wings blocking out the sun, and where there are bats, there are surely fearsome merrevail to be found as well. These hideous creatures cannot be allowed to continue their inhabitance of this promising hall if the rumours of the mirrors are true.
'Go to Zirakzigil, north of here, and you will find the entrance to Lumul-nar as I did. If I were you, ${PLAYER}, I would bring a stout companion or two with you when you go.'

'To defeat so many of the vile beasts was quite a feat, ${PLAYER}! You have done very well indeed against our foes in the Hall of Mirrors. We will surely be able to make progress there after your deeds today.'

'Though my brother is avenged, I fear that in my sorrow I spoke too plainly to a younger dwarf who now risks his own life to avenge his own brother, a member of Gellir's company.
'The dwarf, Sigurdór, went towards Kheledûl to avenge his brother, but likely is at a tower on the outskirts of the port with the deposed dockmaster, Svanr. Follow the road east beyond Thrasi's cabin, towards the shore, and keep an eye out for Sigurdór.
'I pray you are not too late to stop his folly.'

'Áskell told me not to go, but I would hear nothing of his warning. My brother Arndór was not much older than myself, and I felt I must avenge him. I failed.
'The Dourhands are too rooted within that port for one dwarf, more miner than warrior, to dislodge. You, though, you are a hale and hearty warrior, else you would not be here....'
Talk to Sigurdór near Kheledúl
Another Brother's Sorrow

Áskell, at Gondamon, told you that one of Gellir's company left a brother of his own behind. Sigurdór, the brother left behind, has gone to Kheledúl seeking his own vengeance. Áskell asked that you seek him out as the port has been overrun and it's dockmaster deposed to a tower on the outskirts of the port.
'You must hurry to Kheledûl to stop Sigurdór from doing something rash. Kheledûl lies to the east of here.'

Sigurdór is at a tower along the road to Kheledúl east of Gondamon.
Áskell directed you to find and stop Sigurdór, a hot-headed young dwarf, from committing a terrible folly.
Defeated Dourhands at Kheledûl (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'I did attempt to fight my way through the port in search of the leader, to no avail. His cowardice keeps him well hidden and his lackeys gave my legs a good beating. Were it not for Svanr, I likely would have fallen to them as well.
'I failed to avenge Arndór. I am not fit for another foray, but you have helped Askell, and I hope that you will help me.
'Below us, in the valley to the east, lay the port of Kheledúl and therein the Dourhands. Will you go there and strike down a goodly number of the forces there so I might be able to give my brother the vengeance that he deserves?'

'My brother may not know that this has been done, but I do and this will give me leave to rest at night. I am ever in your debt, ${PLAYER}.
'I will miss my brother, but I will know that his death is avenged and that the Dourhands are weakened now to a point where we Longbeards may drive them, finally, from our lands.'
Defeat Dourhands at Kheledúl (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Sigurdór
Exacting Vengeance
Sigurdór, at the tower outside of Kheledúl, has asked you to avenge his brother where he cannot.
'Carry out my vengeance, ${PLAYER}! The Dourhands of Kheledûl must pay for their affrontery.'

Kheledûl lies below the tower where Sigurdór waits.
Sigurdór asked you to make your way to Kheledúl to exact vengeance on the Dourhand dwarves for his slain brother.

Sigurdór is at the tower outside Kheledúl.
You exacted vengeance upon the murderous Dourhand dwarves responsible for slaying Sigurdór's brother, Arndór. Now you should return to Sigurdór.

'You have earned the trust of my people, ${PLAYER}, but it will do you no good to pass beneath the eaves of the forest unless someone alerts the archers hidden along the border of your nature.

Sober revellers admonished (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'My dear ${PLAYER}, I thank you for your help with the preparations for the <rgb=#FF0000>evening revels</rgb>, but there is one last matter. Even among our people, there is the occasional tendency to over-sample the fine products of our local vineyard, and the revellers can become a bit more loose with their tongues than I prefer.
'I must see to my duties as hostess and greeter to guests as they arrive... and so I was wondering if you could help me keep some of our more inebriated guests in line?
'I find it is easiest to determine who has overindulged by listening to their manner of speech. It is the way of the Elves of Lothlórien to remain quiet and well-mannered even during our revels -- so should you hear someone raising their voice over-loud or becoming unseemingly boisterous, it might be best to remind them of their manners.'
'The revels continue undisturbed? My thanks to you, ${PLAYER}.'

Maliriel has asked you to help keep an eye on the guests, during the <rgb=#FF0000>evening revels</rgb> to ensure that matters do not get out of hand, as they are occasionally known to do.

'Our scouts watch them from the telain that border the forest there and contrive their downfall. It is fair enough sport, but only a prelude of the battles to come should our true hopes fail us.'
