The letter reads:
'Be it known that I, Jon Brackenbrook, overseeing the rebuilding of Archet, write this on behalf of ${PLAYER}. I fought alongside ${PLAYER} in an attempt to thwart the Blackwold brigands and their Angmarim masters.
Should it be within your power, give ${PLAYER}, some measure of welcome and thanks for all that they have done.
Jon Brackenbrook
Apparently, Jon Brackenbrook wishes you well in your future endeavours.

'I heard what you did. Mundo will never admit to it but what you did with the tall folk will be talked about behind your back for years! To think, you helped save not only two hobbits from the Shire, but a whole town.
'Merry me, you must have a little Baggins in you. Here, take these and then look through my wares. You may find something there to your liking, adventurer!'

'I remember your face and your actions. You are a hero to us all.
'I will do what I can, though we do not have much to offer at the moment. Take these and then speak with me again to see what else I can offer you.'
Deliver the letter to Constable Thistlewool or Postman Newbuck
A Message of Thanks

Your assistance against the bandits who burned and raided Archet is worthy of much merit from the people of the Shire and Bree-land. Jon Brackenbrook has seen that you are given some measure of favour.

Deliver the letter of thanks to Constable Thistlewool in Archet or Postman Newbuck in Little Delving.
Jon Brackenbrook has written a letter on your behalf thanking you for your assistance with the Blackwold brigands who recently assaulted and destroyed much of Archet. He hopes that you will gain some measure of thanks from others.
The Elves have suffered too many casualties! (${VALUE}/12)
You failed to report back in to Raingon!

'You have come none too soon, ${PLAYER}. The Orcs have been launching small assaults against us of late, and our scouts have seen another raiding party heading this way.
'I need you at the base of these telain to help our soldiers on the ground drive off the Orcs with minimal casualties. We cannot afford to lose any more of our people, or we will be left shorthanded when their true assaults begin.'
'The Orcs come even now! Prepare our defences and reinforce our guards where you may! The Orcs will attack both here and at Talan Fanuidhol!'
'The marchwardens tell me that you have acquitted yourself well during the recent skirmish. Allow me to offer you a token of our appreciation.''
Talk to Raingon at Talan Gwilith
Fanuidhol attackers defeated (${VALUE}/30)
Talk to Raingon at Talan Gwilith
<rgb=#FF0000>Elvish Soldiers defeated (${VALUE}/12)</rgb>
Fanuidhol Skirmish
The Orcs in Fanuidhol have been launching frequent small-scale attacks against the borders of Lórien to test and weaken the resolve of the defenders before they launch a major assault.

Raingon is at Talan Gwilith.
You should speak with Raingon to prepare the defences for battle.
Raingon has asked you to defeat the attackers out of Fanuidhol at both Talan Gwilith and Talan Fanuidhol, while protecting the Elven soldiers.

Raingon is at Talan Gwilith.
With the assault turned aside, you should speak with Raingon.
Defeated Anduin lizards (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Greetings, ${PLAYER}. I am the master huntsman of Egladil and the lands surrounding it. I and my hunters provide much of the meat we partake of during feasts and banquets in Lothlórien, though we are careful never to take too much from the forest's bounty.
'Unfortunately, I have recently seen a new sort of creature about which threatens to throw matters awry -- a variety of large lizard that breeds along the banks of the Anduin. They used to be quite rare here, but of late their numbers have grown rapidly. Perhaps something evil has driven them from their territory upstream? I know not, but they are voracious hunters, and if we are to keep sufficient game within the bounds of Lórien's forests, then we must trim their numbers quickly. Will you lend us your aid?
'It is unfortunate that Aesbrennil has not yet found a proper recipe for their tough meat, or we would be well-lardered indeed upon these beasts.'

'Commendable work, ${PLAYER}. I have no ill-will towards those creatures, but their presence here threatens the bounty of Lothlórien.
'Perhaps when this dark time has passed, they shall return to their rightful grounds and prosper there again.'
Defeat Anduin lizards (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Farasdúr near the Vinyards of Lórien
Invasive Hunters
Strange lizards have recently come to infest the forests bordering the Anduin, killing off many of the native animals.
'The Anduin lizards are a vicious breed and must be driven from Lothlórien.'

Anduin lizards can mostly be found in Egladil in the south-east reaches of Lothlórien.
Farasdúr has asked you to defeat several of the Anduin lizards that have encroached upon the hunting grounds of the Galadhrim.

Farasdúr is near the Vinyards of Lórien in Egladil.
You should speak with Farasdúr near the Vinyards of Lórien.
Collected bear-meat (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'We have had much reason to gather and share meals of late, both for honouring the visitors who seek respite in our land, and for the tragic news that reached us in the wake of their arrival.
'For the most part, our people are more than content to subsist upon the bounty of our breads and the greenery cultivated by our gardeners, but we also enjoy the hunt and a fine roast now and again. After all, it does not hurt to bolster the morale of our folk with a little indulgence in such dark times, when battle seems always close at hand.
'To this end, I would have you hunt a few of the wild bears to the west, in the rocky dens of Brochos. Their meat is rich and well worth savouring when properly prepared.'

'Ah! A choice set of cuts, ${PLAYER}. The upcoming feast shall be fine indeed!
'I only hope it bolsters the strength of our guests, for it seems that they will have a long and perilous journey ahead of them.'
'Have you had poor fortune in the hunt? I suppose the bears can wait, but the upcoming banquet cannot! Please go to Brochos as soon as you are able.'
Collect bear-meat (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Farasdúr near the Vineyards of Lórien
The Bears of Brochos

The Elves of Lothlórien subsist mostly upon the flowering bounty of Lothlórien, but there are those among them that enjoy the chase of the hunt and a finely cooked roast upon special occasions as well.
'The bears of Brochos produce a very hearty meat.'

Bears can be found in the dens of Brochos, which is a ways to the west of the Vineyards of Lórien.
Farasdúr has asked you to hunt the bears of Brochos and return with rich meat.

Farasdúr is near the Vineyards of Lórien in Egladil, east of Brochos.
You should bring the bear-meat you have collected to Farasdúr.
'On this level of Telain Galadhrim, you will find the class trainers.'
'This ladder will take you up to the Elves of my kin who grant bartering rewards.'
'The vault-keeper has a residence on this level of Telain Galadhrim.'
'On this level of Telain Galadhrim, you will find the Elves who grant bartering rewards.'
'Spend your gold leaves and silver branches wisely!'

'Welcome, ${PLAYER}, to Caras Galadhon, beloved city of Lord Celeborn and Lady Galadriel of Lothlórien! Count yourself among the fortunate few, friend ${CLASS}, for not many outsiders have seen the beauty of this place and could report of it. What make you of Caras Galadhon thus far?
'You wonder how you will find your way among the tall mallorn-trees? It is not as confusing as it may seem at first, my friend, and I will help you to learn your way around.
'To reach Telain Galadhrim, the flets upon which the trainers reside, follow this path to the west and take the first right turning. Follow that path to my friend Randiron, who will guide you further.'

'When Trevadiel heard there would be another visitor to Caras Galadhon, she hurried to the entrance with all haste; she delights in greeting those unfamiliar to the city, and there are so very few of those that she rarely has the opportunity.
'Look above us, and you will see Telain Galadhrim, a series of flets upon which Elves of the many professions can be consulted for guidance and services. Climb the steps that wind up the bole of the tree here to reach the talan upon which the class trainers reside.
'You will find Rainen on the flet above, and she will continue your tour of the city.'

'On this high flet of Telain Galadhrim you will find those of my kin entrusted with the rewarding of valuable items to those who have proven themselves true friends of the Elves of Lórien.
'Bring any Lothlórien gold leaves or Lothlórien silver branches to the Elves on this flet for your rewards.
'I hope you will enjoy your stay in Caras Galadhon, ${PLAYER}, and that you will be a valuable contributor to the good welfare of Lothlórien! Namárië!'

'Many of the services you might need in Caras Galadhon can be found here at Telain Galadhrim.
'On this level you will find the class trainers, a vault-keeper and our hall of trade. If you cross the flet to the ladder on the far side and climb the ladder there, you will find a mailbox for your use. On that level you will find vendors for the scholarly and jewelsmithy pursuits, as well as a healer and provisioner.
'But for now, climb this ladder here to reach the next level and speak with Padril on the level above.'
Talk to Randiron near Telain Galadhrim
Talk to Rainen at Telain Galadhrim
Talk to Padril at Telain Galadhrim

'Climb this ladder to reach the higher level and speak with my friend Padril, for she will conclude your tour of Telain Galadhrim.'
'To reach Telain Galadhrim, follow this path to the west and take the first right turning. Follow that path to my friend Randiron, who will guide you further.'
'How are you enjoying Caras Galadhon, ${PLAYER}?'
'I hope you are enjoying your time here, friend ${CLASS}.'
'It is my pleasure to welcome newcomers to Caras Galadhon, rare as it is.'

'These winding steps will take you to the flets of Telain Galadhrim.'

'You knew the Grey Pilgrim, ${PLAYER}, did you not? He was known by many names, travelling to and fro as he did, but to us in Lórien he was called Mithrandir. News came lately that he had fallen in the shadows of Moria; his travels now are ended.
'These three behind me sing now a lament for him, but the words cannot fully express the sorrow that descends even into Lórien at his passing. We will need time to mourn, but there is little time left to us in this Middle-earth. We will take our grief across the Sea.
'If you have words of comfort, save them for Losdirith, who watches the gate to the garden of Lady Galadriel. He has taken the fall of Mithrandir very much to heart, and I have heard that his grief has made him act strangely. Follow the path south to speak with Losdirith.'

'Mithrandir meant so much to all of us, ${PLAYER}, and his passing brings with it a measure of grief I did not ever think to feel. But it is not sorrow that fills me with these confusing thoughts. Nay, it is something else: a dream I have dreamed these past three nights, and I have no reason to believe I will not have it again this night.
'I dreamed I stood within golden leaves, high atop a flet, and as I stared through a break in the trees, I saw a great eagle in the north-east sky. And I heard the voice of Mithrandir, but I could not make out the words.
'There is such a place here in Caras Galadhon, ${PLAYER}! The leaves grow close over the edge of one of the flets of Telain Neduil, north-west of here. Stand there and <rgb=#FF0000>look</rgb>, and perhaps you will see something of Mithrandir!'

'You did not see anything, ${PLAYER}? I am saddened to hear it, but will not give up hope that my dream will one day come true. I will go myself to Telain Neduil every day, and perhaps one day I will see the sight of a Great Eagle bearing forth Mithrandir.
'I thank you for supporting me in this, even if it may seem futile to you. Mithrandir has fallen, but the lesson he taught to me is that even in dark times, we must hope for bright days to come.
'Take this as a token of my friendship, ${PLAYER}.'

'This is too noble a thing for one such as I!
'Furthermore, it is certainly a woman's necklace, but I cannot say to whom it belongs for I have not seen its like before.'

'It is beautiful -- and you offer this to me as a gesture of your affections?

'Truthfully, I have not seen its like before. Such a fine piece would likely belong to someone with considerable responsibility and a more honoured position than mine.'

'What a fine trinket you have there!
'You found it by the spring? That is odd, for it has the look of a noble lady's jewel. I wonder how it came to rest there.
'The Elves who possess trinkets like this would be found in Caras Galadhon, but those ladies rarely venture into secluded corners of the forest.'

'Do you think this necklace would go well with my attire? I am rather afraid it would set the colour of my eyes in a poor light.
'On our Mistress of the Feast I think it would look quite radiant, however, though I have never seen her wear such jewels as this.'

'Where did you get this necklace, ${PLAYER}?

'You cannot know what this means to me, ${PLAYER} -- to live a thousand years with only his memory. Had I lost this forever... nay, such a loss would have been beyond my strength to bear. I am in your debt, kind randir.'

'Something strikes me as odd about Aragorn Elessar, ${PLAYER}. I received a message from Milwen at Cerin Amroth requesting his presence, and he declined. He was very polite, but I do not understand why he would not wish to return there. The rest of his Company has spent some time at Cerin Amroth in leisure, but he has not done so.
'Perhaps he needs a reminder of the beauty of the hill. Travel to Cerin Amroth and retrieve a bloom of elanor from Milwen. Bring it back here and give it to Aragorn in the Company's Pavilion. He will surely agree that the beauty of Cerin Amroth is such that he must return there.
'You will find Milwen by the arches on the western side of the hill of Cerin Amroth, north of Caras Galadhon.'

'Well, this is certainly a friendly challenge, ${PLAYER}. I will give you a bloom of elanor possessing such beauty that Aragorn Elessar will be captivated at once and will have no choice but to return.
'I must confess I can think of no reason for him to decline my invitation here. He seemed to be quite happy during his prior visits. It is a mystery I cannot unravel.'
With a smile, Milwen hands you a bloom of the elanor that grows upon the hill.
'Bring that to Aragorn in the Company's Pavilion in Caras Galadhon, ${PLAYER}, and he will hasten to gaze upon the hill of Cerin Amroth again!'

'Well? Did you succeed in my friendly challenge?'
Miluiel listens to your description of your encounter with Aragorn, and his face falls.
'I had no idea, ${PLAYER}. I did not suspect that Aragorn would have such a reason for not returning to Cerin Amroth. I... I am filled with regret for the asking!
'And yet my heart tells me that Aragorn Elessar will one day walk again among the trees, and climb the hill of Cerin Amroth, and stand there again in happiness. Will it be before his long road is ended? I cannot say.
'I thank you for this, ${PLAYER}.'

'Welcome, ${PLAYER}, to Caras Galadhon! My company has been given this pavilion for our use, but I have not seen many of them today. Just young Peregrin, and he seems comfortable enough.'
You hand him the bloom of elanor, and a cloud passes in front of his face; for a moment Aragorn seems to see only the golden flower. Then the cloud passes, and Aragorn once again meets your gaze.
'My heart will dwell always on Cerin Amroth, ${PLAYER}, and the memory of those fair days is pleasant; thought of them keeps my feet walking the long road. I will not return to Cerin Amroth until the long road is ended, whether it be at the end of this journey or the longest. Tell Miluiel it is not despite the beauty of Cerin Amroth that I stay away, but because of it. But my heart sang when I was there, as it always did, and always will.'
Aragorn looks again at the bloom of elanor, and is transported to some distant memory; he knows you not, and you feel you have an answer for Miluiel.
'You do not have anything for me?'

'No, I have not received a letter from Istarien lately. Why do you ask?'
'Mae govannen, ${PLAYER}.'
'We must remain vigilant in our defence of Lothlórien.'

The five pages of Istarien's letter to Rilhathel can be found on nearby flets and in the area around Istarien.
The pages of an embarrassingly private letter Istarien was writing have been scattered onto nearby flets by a mischievous breeze, and she wants you to retrieve them.

Istarien is on one of the upper flets of Telain Galadhrim.
You have recovered the pages of Istarien's letter and should now return them to her.
You search the distance for Amroth's white ship, but it does not appear
You have arrived at the docks

'Lord Celeborn and Lady Galadriel have ruled in Lothlórien for countless years, but they were not the first masters of the Golden Wood. You can hear the tale of Amroth and Nimrodel from others, but know that it is a sad song and does not end as you might wish.
'Amroth sailed into the Sea without his beloved and never returned, but every year my family travels to the circular docks that extend into the Celebrant so we can <rgb=#FF0000>look</rgb> into the distance for Amroth...though his ship sailed from Edhellond in the far south.
'This tradition allows us to feel closer to our forebears, and I would like for you to experience that connexion as well. Take a moment to remember Amroth of Lórien, ${PLAYER}, for those who have gone before should not be forgotten.'
'Very good, ${PLAYER}! I am glad you have taken a moment to remember Amroth's last voyage out to the sea, where he was lost and came not again to the land that he loved.'
<rgb=#FF0000>Look</rgb> into the distance for Amroth
Find one of the circular docks that extend into the Celebrant
Talk to Pennasdir upon Telain Glorelloth
A Moment for Amroth
Amroth was an Elf-lord who once ruled in Lothlórien, but was lost at Sea, never to be seen again.

'Travel to the circular docks that extend into the Celebrant, south of Imlad Lalaith, and <rgb=#FF0000>look</rgb> into the distance for Amroth. It is a tradition that brings us closer to our shared history.'
'It is good to take a moment every now and again to remember those who have left us.'
'Amroth was once Lord of Lórien, but he was lost long ago.'

The circular docks that extend into the Celebrant can be found south-east of Caras Galadhon, south of Imlad Lalaith.
Pennasdir has asked you to stand on one of the circular docks that extend into Celebrant and to <rgb=#FF0000>look</rgb> into the distance for Amroth.

Pennasdir is on Telain Glorelloth, in Caras Galadhon, north-west of the docks.
You have participated in Pennasdir's tradition of looking for Amroth down the Celebrant and should return now to the Elf.

'Watching the gates of Caras Galadhon is hungry work, ${PLAYER}, and too often a thankless task.
'I have prepared packets of lembas for you to bring to guards at the various gates within the city: to Losdirith at the gate of the garden of Lady Galadriel and to Minathlang at the entrance of the city.
'I hope the lembas will restore the strength of the guards and tell them their service is appreciated by all of us.'

'You have delivered the lembas to the guards, ${PLAYER}? Very good! Take this for your trouble and know that you have made them feel that their service is appreciated, as surely it is by every member of the city!'
'Thank you for this, ${PLAYER}! I will enjoy this lembas tremendously as the hours pass.'
'You have not brought me anything.'
'Thank you very much for this lembas, ${PLAYER}. Sometimes the hours pass in tedium, and it will give me the strength to maintain my vigil without complaint.'
'You have not brought me anything.'
Bring packet of lembas to Losdirith
Bring packet of lembas to Minathlang
Talk to Basdan upon Telain Bangad
Lembas for the Gates
Lembas is the fabled waybread of Lórien, and a staple for those who stand long guard-shifts.
'Bring those packets of lembas to Losdirith at the gate of Lady Galadriel's garden and to Minathlang at the entrance of the city.'
'The guards of Caras Galadhon should have more recognition for their service.'
'Thank you very much for bringing the lembas to the guards.'
'Thank you for bringing by that packet of lembas.'
'It does not take very much lembas to give one the strength to carry on.'
'I have not forgotten the lembas you brought to me, ${PLAYER}!'
'Thank you again for that lembas, my friend!'

Losdirith is at the entrance to the garden of Lady Galadriel. Minathlang is at the entrance to the city.
Basdan has given you packets of lembas to bring to the guards at various gates within the city.

Basdan is on Telain Bangad in Caras Galadhon.
You have delivered packets of lembas to the guards and should return now to Basdan.

'The Orcs of Moria are a matter of great concern, ${PLAYER}, and we need to be prepared for the attack that is surely coming.
'Pick up a crate from the stack and carry it to Sileffind at the entrance to the city. But be careful, for you will not be able to climb any ladders while you are carrying the crate!'
'Thank you for bringing these supplies here, ${PLAYER}! We will now be better prepared to stand against the Orcs.'
Pick up a crate from the stack near Aesgyl
Talk to Sileffind at the entrance to Caras Galadhon
Lothlórien Preparations IV
Aesgyl has prepared some supplies to aid with the defence of Lothlórien from the Orcs of Moria.
'You can pick up a crate from the stack here and carry it to Sileffind, ${PLAYER}. He is helping prepare for the defence at the entrance to Caras Galadhon.'
'You need to speak to Sileffind now that you have delivered the supplies, ${PLAYER}.'

A stack of crates is next to Aesgyl on Telain Galadhrim. Sileffind is at the entrance to Caras Galadhon.
You have been asked to carry a crate to Sileffind at the entrance of Caras Galadhon.

Sileffind is at the entrance to Caras Galadhon.
You have delivered a crate to Sileffind and should now speak with him.

'It is good to see you here, ${CLASS} ${PLAYER}. Adventurers are not often permitted within the boundaries of Lothlórien, but that you are here tells me that the Lord and Lady truly intend to defend us from the Orcs at any cost.
'Have you met my beloved? He often stands guard at the entrance to Caras Galadhon with my brother Rilhathel; Belvagor is his name. Now that you are here, perhaps Belvagor can take a rest from his station and share a bottle of wine with me in peace. It will do him good to have a break from the worries of facing the Orcs.
'Travel to the Vineyards of Lórien, south-east of Caras Galadhon, in Egladil, and speak to the vintner Glasnír. He will give you the bottle of wine which I have requested... a special vintage that has great meaning for Belvagor and me. Bring the bottle to Belvagor and tell him that I request he share a relaxing day with me.'

'You have been sent by Bruicheron for the special vintage she requested? I will retrieve it for you.
'I remember when this vintage was laid down; it was many years ago now, and I was gratified to see we still had some bottles of it remaining, for Bruicheron noticed that it had been laid down on the very day she met Belvagor. She requested that I set some of that vintage aside, saying that it had special meaning for her: it was exactly as old as her love for Belvagor.
'She asked you to bring this to him? You will likely find him guarding the gates of Caras Galadhon.'

'What is this that you have brought to me, ${PLAYER}?'
'This vintage has special meaning for me and Bruicheron, ${PLAYER}, and it would delight me to no end to share it with her among the golden leaves atop a great mallorn. But my duty is here, and it is for her sake that I must maintain my vigil. The Orcs cannot be permitted to threaten beautiful Lórien or any of its people, especially not she who is dearest to me.
'Bring this vintage to her now and tell her I will join her as soon as I am able. But I must be certain the Orcs are not near enough to launching an assault.'
'You have nothing for me?'

'I understand, ${PLAYER}. Belvagor has his duty, and he would not be my beloved if he did not treat it seriously. But woe betide any Orc that threatens even a single hair of his!
'I will keep this bottle, unopened, until such day that Belvagor is free to take the peace he deserves. He will set aside the vintage of war, and we will once again enjoy the comfort we have earned.'
'You have nothing for me?'
Talk to Glasnír at the Vineyards of Lórien
Bring the wine to Belvagor at the entrance to Caras Galadhon
Bring the special vintage to Bruicheron
The Vintage of War
Bruicheron is hopeful that her beloved friend Belvagor will leave the Orc-fighting to others and instead share a relaxing visit with her.

'The vintner Glasnír is just outside the Vineyards of Lórien, south-east of Caras Galadhon. Retrieve the special vintage of wine I have requested from him and bring it to my beloved Belvagor, currently guarding the entrance to Caras Galadhon. I would share it with him on a relaxing day, a break from his troubles.'

'You have retrieved the special vintage! Bring it now to my beloved Belvagor, currently guarding the gates of Caras Galadhon, and tell him I would share it with him on a relaxing day, that he may forget his troubles.'
'Bruicheron wanted you to bring this special vintage of wine to Belvagor, did she not? Look for him at the gates of Caras Galadhon, to the north-west.'
'Return to Telain Glorelloth, ${PLAYER}, and tell my beloved Bruicheron that I cannot yet join her for a day of peace.'
'One day, Belvagor will be able to have the peace he so deserves.'
'It pains me to know Belvagor cannot enjoy a day free from the troubles of duty.'
'I will fight the Orcs until Lothlórien is safe for my beloved Bruicheron.'
'We must deal with the Orcs.'
'One day, I will rest from my duty, but that day is not yet here.'

The vintner Glasnír is outside the Vineyards of Lórien, south-east of Caras Galadhon.
Bruicheron has asked you to retrieve a special vintage of wine from the vintner and to bring it to her beloved Belvagor, with the request that he join her for a relaxing day.

Belvagor is guarding the gates of Caras Galadhon.
Glasnír has given you the special vintage of wine requested by Bruicheron, and now you should deliver it to Belvagor.

Bruicheron is on Telain Glorelloth, in Caras Galadhon.
Belvagor has decided his duty requires him to remain on guard against the Orcs for the moment, and he regretfully cannot yet join Bruicheron for a day of relaxation. You should return to Bruicheron with the tidings.

'Do you have a moment, ${PLAYER}? I am a fletcher, and it is my duty to fashion arrows for the quivers of the Galadhrim. I have done this for many a year, and my shafts have been the doom of many an Orc. But I recently finished an arrow different from all the rest.
'My friend Faengris, with whom I learned the craft of bow-making and arrow-fletching, was recently slain by a company of Orcs that came down from the Misty Mountains. When the sharp pains of grief lessened somewhat, I set to making an arrow of such bite that it could kill a marching line of Orcs with one shot when fired from a quality bow.
'This arrow in memory of Faengris may be some small comfort to his widow, Núrelleth. Bring it to her that she may see that the Orcs will pay for his death. She can often be found on Telain Glorelloth, where the flets extend over the encircling hedge.'

Núrelleth looks at you silently for a moment before taking the arrow from you and examining it sadly.
'It is most kind of Cúbenn to have worked so long on this arrow in memory of my husband, ${PLAYER}. Their friendship was very important to Faengris, and he spoke often of Cúbenn's skill at bow-making and arrow-fletching. Faengris....'
Her fingers trace the pattern on the fletching, and she no longer seems aware of your presence. After a moment, Núrelleth looks up again.
'This is a fine arrow indeed, ${PLAYER}, but Faengris would not want it wasted on the Orcs.'
'You have not brought me anything?'
Bring the vengeance arrow to Núrelleth
In Memory of the Lost
Cúbenn has crafted an arrow in memory of Núrelleth's husband Faengris, slain by Orcs.

'There is little I can do to relieve Núrelleth's sorrow, or my own, but I hope the knowledge that this arrow I have fashioned will slay many Orcs will be of some comfort to her. Look for her on Telain Glorelloth, where the flets extend over the encircling hedge.'
'My husband was slain by Orcs of Moria, but he will never truly leave me.'
'Faengris was always quick to laughter. Even now, I can see his sparkling eyes.'
'I come here every day...to look into the distance and think of Faengris.'
'Was Núrelleth pleased with the arrow I made in memory of Faengris?'
'How is Núrelleth's sorrow? Have you visited her today?'
'Núrelleth may not wish to spend the arrow on Orcs, but I will avenge Faengris.'

Núrelleth can be found on Telain Glorelloth, where the flets extend over the hedge that encircles Caras Galadhon.
Cúbenn has given you the arrow he crafted in memory of Núrelleth's slain husband Faengris.
'Faengris would be a boon in these dark times. He is missed by many here.'

Núrelleth is silent for a moment.
'Do not misunderstand me, ${PLAYER}. I am grateful for Cúbenn's thoughtful gift of this arrow, and I am pleased that the Orcs could be made to pay for the death of my husband...but it is not enough. I cannot put into words how important Faengris was to me, but vengeance upon the Orcs would in no way repay them for what they have taken from me.
'No, instead I want the memory of my husband to live on in Lothlórien. I want to tell my people what he was, and why it is such a sorrow that he is gone.
'There is a lonely tree on the bank of Anduin, just east of Imlad Lalaith. Bring this arrow to that tree and set it at its base. Faengris and I would watch the sun rise in the east sitting by that tree, and I would like this arrow to remain there in remembrance of him.'

Núrelleth is silent for a moment, and then gives you a brief smile.
'You have been a great comfort to me in my sorrow, ${PLAYER}. I wish only you had been able to meet Faengris, for he would have delighted to hear tales of your adventure.
'Thank you for listening to my grief, friend ${CLASS}. You will be a friend to me always for this.'
Place the vengeance arrow at the base of the lonely tree
Talk to Núrelleth at Telain Glorelloth
Upon the Lonely Bank
Núrelleth wants the memory of Faengris to live on in Lórien and to do more than simply slay some Orcs in his name.

Núrelleth sighs, her face a sorrowful mask.
'The lonely tree where I would like you to place the arrow is east of Imlad Lalaith, on the banks of Anduin.'

'Mae govannen, ${PLAYER}. This is a beautiful place to watch the sun rise in the mornings. Anduin sparkles like gold in the light of the sun and like silver by the light of the moon.
'The tree there sees them all.'
'I wish you could have met Faengris, ${PLAYER}.'
'Sometimes I can hear the voice of my husband on the breeze.'
'This lonely tree watches the sun rise every morning and set every day.'
'The reflections on the surface of Anduin can play tricks with the eye.'
'The other night I thought I saw someone sitting beneath the tree, but there was no one there.'
'I thought my vengeance arrow would be used to slay Orcs. But it is fine.'
'I wish Faengris were here.'

The lonely tree where Núrelleth wants the vengeance arrow placed is on the bank of Anduin, east of Imlad Lalaith.
Núrelleth wants the Elves of Lothlórien to remember her husband Faengris, and to that end, she would rather the vengeance arrow stand in his memory rather than be used to slay more Orcs.

Núrelleth is on Telain Glorelloth, on one of the flets that extends over the hedge that encircles Caras Galadhon.
You have left the vengeance arrow at the lonely tree as Núrelleth requested of you and should now return to her.
You have made it to the flet-runner in time

'Have you yet learned your way through our fair city, ${PLAYER}? Caras Galadhon is both beautiful and complex and to find your way around can be daunting for the newcomer...what few newcomers there are.
'Those who become especially skilled at finding their way among the telain throughout Caras Galadhon are known as \qflet-runners.\q
'Do you have the necessary skills? I challenge you to find the flet-runner atop the high flet of Telain Galadhrim, by the mailbox and the entrance to the Crafting Hall, with utmost haste!'

'You have surprised me, ${PLAYER}, and I know Celechest will be surprised as well! You have demonstrated both a cursory knowledge of our city and a quickness that has let you reach me in time, but there is much more for you to prove if you wish to be known as a flet-runner.
'Look for certain of my friends throughout the city if you wish to engage in similar tests of your awareness and fleetness: Leginiel, Lagordal, Bregradel, and Lintwen. They will measure your skill.
'Nevertheless, you have earned this gold leaf, ${PLAYER}.'
Find the flet-runner by the entrance to the Crafting Hall

'You completed my challenge, ${PLAYER}, but there will be others.'
'Not just anyone can become a flet-runner.'

The flet-runner can be found on a flet with a mailbox high above Telain Galadhrim, near the entrance to the Crafting Hall.
Celechest has challenged you to quickly make your way to a certain flet-runner.

You are not sure where this coin came from, but it seems to be a relic from Khazad-dûm, called Moria by the Elves. There are many who would be interested in such a relic and would likely provide you with a great reward!
<rgb=#FF0000>Bring this coin to any of the following people to receive your reward: • Jon Brackenbrook in Archet • Dwalin in Thorin's Hall • Mayor Will Whitfoot in Michel Delving • Barliman Butterbur in Bree-town • Cardavor in Celondim</rgb>

'What do you have here? A coin of some sort? Doesn't look like much... and what's this, some sort of doors on the back? What a queer coin you've brought me!
'I suppose it is worth something, although surely not much. Perhaps Keeper Foxtail would like to put it on display in the Mathom House.
'Yes, that should be fine. Here, choose something that you feel is appropriate for a coin such as this.'
'Hmm? Do you need something?'

'A dwarf-coin of some sort, is it not? I have heard of such things, but I never thought to see one. Where did you come across it?
'I would gladly give you something in trade for this coin. Choose what you would like, and we shall finish our trade.'
'Hello, can I help you?'

'A dwarf-coin of some sort, is it not? I have heard of such things, but I never thought to see one. Where did you come across it?
'I would gladly give you something in trade for this coin. Choose what you would like, and we shall finish our trade.'
'Hello, can I help you?'

'I cannot believe it! It is an ithildín coin! It is said that many were minted to commemorate the friendship of the Elves of Hollin and the Dwarves of Khazad-dûm. Most were lost... where did you come across such a treasure?
'Please, friend, trade this coin with me. I have many things to offer in trade. Choose something you think appropriate!'
'Greetings. Is there something you seek from me?'
Turn in your ithildín coin to receive your reward
Ithildín Coin

You have found a mysterious coin inlaid with ithildín. This rare metal was made by the Elves from mithril long ago. The image of the Doors of Durin, the doors that guarded the West Gate of Moria, is found on one side of the coin, while the other has the image of a hammer and anvil, the signs of Durin.

'I cannot believe it! It is an ithildín coin! It is said that many were minted to commemorate the friendship of the Elves of Hollin and the Dwarves of Khazad-dûm. Most were lost... where did you come across such a treasure?
'Please, friend, trade this coin with me. I have many things to offer in trade. Choose something you think appropriate!'
'Greetings. Is there something you seek from me?'

'Barliman Butterbur at your service, friend! That's quite a strange coin you've got there! Looks like a dwarf-coin of some sort... I've seen a few from guests, mind you, but not one like this. Not sure even what it's made of!
'Well, not sure I would take it for a meal or a room, but it probably has some value to someone... if only as something interesting to talk over!
'I will offer you a trade. I've a number of things travellers have left behind. You can trade this coin for one of those. How's that sound?'
'Hmm? What can I do for you?'

'Hail, friend. I see you have found an ithildín coin. These coins were minted by the Dwarves of Moria in the days of their friendship with the Elves of Eregion. See here, engraved here are the Doors of Durin, which were inlaid with this same metal.
'Most of these coins were lost when Moria fell into darkness. If you would have it, I would like to keep this coin. It can serve as a good reminder in these dark times of the fellowship that can exist between dwarves and Elves.
'However, I would not ask you to go away empty-handed. Choose something you find acceptable, and we shall make our exchange.'
'Hail, friend. Is there something that you need?'

'I cannot believe it! It is an ithildín coin! It is said that many were minted to commemorate the friendship of the Elves of Hollin and the Dwarves of Khazad-dûm. Most were lost... where did you come across such a treasure?
'Please, friend, trade this coin with me. I have many things to offer in trade. Choose something you think appropriate!'
'Greetings. Is there something that you need?'

Bring your ithildín coin to one of the following people to receive a reward.
