'I must say, I never expected the outpouring of generosity we have received. Certainly we have paid for the services we have been given, but the harvest is so great that we have no means to transport our goods to Adso's Camp.
'I must ask you a small favour. Just outside of Brandy Hall, to the south, there is a stable where I have seen Toly Brockhouse, the local woodcutter, speaking with folks.
'I am certain that he will be willing to help. Could you speak with him and see if he can spare a waggon for the trip to Adso's? Let me know what he said when you are done.'

'Toly will help us? This is wonderful news. We will begin preparing the crates for loading and should get on the road by the next morning.
'We truly could not have done this without you, friend. Please, take this... it should cover the cost of travels and a little more.
'I am concerned for Toly though, what trouble could there be in the Old Forest?'

'Trumric Ragwort needs a waggon? I suppose I could spare a waggon and a couple of mules to share the load towards the camp. Trumric is a good fellow and will surely return them when he is done.
'With the trouble we are seeing in the Old Forest, it seems unlikely that I will have need of all my waggons in the forseeable future.
'Tell Trumric that I will send along a driver, two mules, and a waggon by sundown on the morrow. I should expect that he can have it back to me within a week... and if you are looking to help out around here there is plenty to do.'
Talk to Toly Brockhouse in Buckland
Talk to Trumric Ragwort in Newbury
Sharing the Load

The hobbit Trumric Ragwort is pleased with all the help he has received in Buckland thus far, but the materials that he and his companions have collected for Adso's inn exceeded expectations. He has asked you to secure waggon travel to Adso's camp.

'We can do much of the preparations now, but getting these goods to Adso is going to be harder than expected. People have been so willing to aid us that we fear many of the goods may spoil before we get them to Adso. Will Toly not help us, or have you not had the chance to ask him yet?'

'I am still trying to figure out how you were able to carry all these hides and other items. Adventurers are resourceful folk it seems. I think we shall need a waggon to get our goods to Adso... and soon: the carcases are growing ripe.'
'The salts will keep the meats for some time, but I fear without a proper place to smoke the meat, we will only have cured meats and no smoked meat. We could really use a waggon.'
'Hurry along now! I will get my driver and waggon ready. Trumric will begin to worry if he is not told soon.'

Toly Brockhouse can be found outside the stable near Brandy Hall.
Trumric Ragwort asked you to seek a waggon from Toly Brockhouse to help transport all the goods that he and his fellows have collected since arriving in Buckland.

Trumric Ragwort is awaiting your return in Newbury, just inside the gates of Buckland.
Toly Brockhouse seemed concerned with events in the Old Forest, but was amenable to lending Trumric Ragwort the waggon for his journey to Adso's camp.
Defeated Lebrennil

'One thing I know about spiders is that they typically move in broods. At the head of the brood, you're likely to find a queen -- a female that cares for, watches over, and commands the lesser spiders.
'I gather that there is a brood-matron in that hollow. Though I am not certain where, as I did not see her.
'Be wary, and if you do find her, let me know, and I will see that you are rewarded. The hollow is just beyond the river to the south... you will know it by the webs hanging from the trees.'

'Good riddance! We are better off without that queen creeping about. The trouble with spiders that make their way into canopies and hollows is you never know when they have grown too big to deal with properly.
'Thank you for all you have done.'
Defeat Lebrennil
Talk to Gillemin Brandybuck in the Old Forest
A Matron in the Hollow
Gillemin Brandybuck believes the great spider-nest could also be contributing to the stirring of the Old Forest.
'That spider nest is likely watched over by a potent matron. I have seen that type of thing before. It does not mean it has happened again, but you never know!'

The spider-nest lies near the Willow Glade, to the south of Gillemin's old camp.
Gillemin warned that you should be wary of a matron within the spider-nest.

Gillemin Brandybuck awaits you at his new camp, south-east of Old Muddyfoot's Hill.
You should return to Gillemin Brandybuck with news of your success.
Defeated spiders in the south-east Old Forest (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collected the forester's pack

'Before you go... well now, as I said before, I think that nest of spiders I found has something to do with all the queerness stirred up in the forest. But there are too many spiders for me to deal with myself, and the Bounders will only come with fire and axes.
'If you make your way into the heart of that nest to find the tree, maybe you can clear out some of the spiders and collect my pack. The spider-nest is south across the Willow Glade.
'I was only able to make it to the outskirts of the nesting ground before the spiders chased me away. I dropped my pack just within the bounds of the hollow and would have gone back if I had not taken such a nasty spill.'

'Though I do hate disturbing the natural order in this place, I cannot be sure that the spiders now in this area are natural. I swear they appeared from nowhere.
'Thank you for recovering my pack and clearing some of them out of that valley.'
Defeat spiders in the south-east Old Forest (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collect the forester's pack
Bring the pack to Gillemin Brandybuck in the Old Forest
Evil on Eight Legs
Gillemin Brandybuck believes the great spider-nest could also be contributing to the stirring of the Old Forest.
'I'd wager that spider nest has something to do with what's got the forest all stirred up. You might want to take some friends and have a look!'

The spider-nest lies near the Willow Glade, to the south of Gillemin's old camp.
Gillemin has asked you to gather some friends and investigate the spider-nest he found.

Gillemin Brandybuck awaits you at his new camp, south-east of Old Muddyfoot's Hill.
You should bring the pack you found to Gillemin Brandybuck.

'You have done so much, I think that it is time to meet the hobbit you have been helping, Adso Haybank. You will find that he is a caring fellow with much on his mind.
'His camp is difficult to miss as the work is happening right along the roadside. You will travel east along the Great East Road for some distance, about halfway to Bree, before you arrive.
'When you get there, you should be welcomed. Thank you again, ${PLAYER}.'

'You must be ${PLAYER}. I have been hearing a lot about you. My associates in Buckland sent along a message about your work. They speak very highly of you.
'I am glad to finally meet you. Would that the circumstances were better, but no reason to bother you with that now.
'This -- once finished -- will be my inn; a dream I have had for years, an inn that would attract the Big Folk and hobbits alike. You have helped me come one step closer to my dream, and for that, I am in your debt.'
Talk to Adso Haybank at Adso's Camp
Mr. Haybank Meet...
Trumric Ragwort has given you directions to go and meet Adso Haybank himself. He deems it only fitting for all the work you have done.
'You will find Mr. Haybank along the road to the east. You will need to travel for some time as he means to make an inn between Bree and the Shire.'

Adso Haybank is at his camp, about half the distance between Bree and the Buckland Gate, eastward along the Great East Road.
Trumric Ragwort sent you on to meet Adso Haybank.
Canopy and Hollow
Defeated Talûntûm

'${PLAYER}, a moment please.
'I understand that Mothelen wishes you to enter Burgûl-stazg...perhaps while you are there, you will attempt to defeat Talûntûm, the captain of the camp? With many goblins deserting their posts, the enemy there is already in a weakened state...slaying Talûntûm may just be the key to breaking their spirits once and for all.
'Talûntûm will likely be found in the bulwark at the rear of the camp. Return to me when the deed is done.'
'Well done, ${PLAYER}! The goblins of Burgûl-stazg will not likely recover from that blow, unless a new leader rises among them.'
Defeat Talûntûm at Burgûl-stazg
Talk to Dagorchiel at Echad Mothelen
Crushing Resistance
While searching for information about the evil which drove many goblins to desert Burgûl-stazg, you learned that the enemy forces there are commanded by an Uruk called Talûntûm.
'Talûntûm is a fierce foe...be careful, ${PLAYER}.'
'Welcome, ${PLAYER}, Talûntûm-bane!'
'Your efforts in Burgûl-stazg will not be forgotten, ${PLAYER}.'

Talûntûm may be found within the bulwark at the rear of Burgûl-stazg, north-west from Echad Mothelen.
Dagorchiel has asked you to defeat Talûntûm, the captain of Burgûl-stazg.

Dagorchiel is at Echad Mothelen, south-east from Burgûl-stazg.
You should return to Dagorchiel with tidings of your victory.
Defeated a goblin-deserter in the Dourstocks (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'${PLAYER}, as we expected, we found another enemy encampment here in the Dourstocks; however, something seems to be terribly wrong. There are not enough goblins and Orcs in Burgûl-stazg to mount any kind of counterattack against Echad Sirion, and more goblins are deserting everyday.
'Perhaps you could go out into the Dourstocks between here and Burgûl-stazg and see if you can find any of the deserters. You might be able to learn what has them so terrified.
'When you learn something, return to me.'
'This becomes more mysterious. From what you say, it appears the leaders of the encampment are up to something that has even the goblins unnerved. We shall need to learn exactly what that is....'
Defeat goblin-deserters in the Dourstocks (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Mothelen at Echad Mothelen
The Elves of the Golden Host discovered a second enemy encampment on the western edge of the Dourstocks, but something seems to be wrong.
'Something queer is occuring here, ${PLAYER}. Keep your eyes sharp and your wits about you.'

Goblin-deserters can be found in the Dourstocks, between Echad Mothelen and Burgûl-stazg, to the north-west.
Mothelen has asked you to hunt down some of the goblin-deserters and discover what has terrified them.

Mothelen is at Echad Mothelen in the western Dourstocks, south-east of Burgûl-stazg.
You should return to Mothelen with the information you have gathered.
Destroyed the idol of the Necromancer

'An idol of the Necromancer, which the White Council had discovered was in fact the Dark Lord himself...though Sauron may have been driven forth, his minions still serve him at Dol Guldur. It is said that the Lieutenant of Dol Guldur commands there once again.
'There is no telling what grief will come of these goblins' foolishness. That idol must be destroyed!
'Go at once, ${PLAYER}. Enter Burgûl-stazg and find that statue. Let nothing stand in your way. An icon of such dark power cannot be permitted to remain!'

'You were attacked by the shades of Men? It was rumoured that the Woodmen who had lived in the Dourstocks had fallen into evil over two-hundred years ago and had worshipped the Necromancer. It appears those rumours are true.
'It is well that you destroyed the idol, but I fear a terror has been unleashed unlike any this land has seen.'
Destroy the idol of the Necromancer
Talk to Mothelen at Echad Mothelen
Purging Evil
You learned from your investigation of Burgûl-stazg that the goblins, under orders from their captain, stole an idol of the Necromancer from the haunted ruins.
'You must stop these Orcs' vile plans, ${PLAYER}. They know not what powers they are toying with.'
'I am relieved that you have destroyed the idol of the Necromancer, ${PLAYER}, but I fear a darker evil has been unleashed....'
'Thank you, ${PLAYER}, for your assistance. Now, at least, we know what caused the goblins to desert.'

The idol of the Necromancer can be found in Burgûl-stazg, north-west from Echad Mothelen.
Mothelen has instructed you to find and destroy the idol of the Necromancer.

Mothelen is at Echad Mothelen, south-east from Burgûl-stazg.
You should return to Mothelen with news of your success.
Found a deserter's note

'${PLAYER}, we must learn the root cause of the goblins' fear. Something is taking place at Burgûl-stazg, and it must be stopped, but first we must learn exactly what it is.
'You should go to Burgûl-stazg and see if you can find anything out, but be careful not to be seen by the guards. Detection of your presence may make your quest more difficult. Look for goblins that are especially nervous.
'Return to me when you have learned more.'

'This note is written in their foul Black Speech, but I know somewhat of it.
'Interesting! The goblins have stolen an idol from the haunted ruins. It is no wonder that they are terrified. I dare not consider the horrors they have unleashed!'
Uncover the mystery at Burgûl-stazg
Talk to Mothelen at Echad Mothelen
A Shadow on the Camp
The goblin-deserters roaming the Dourstocks indicated that something their leaders were up to in Burgûl-stazg was the cause of their desertion.
'${PLAYER}, enter Burgûl-stazg and gather the knowledge we require.'

Burgûl-stazg lies to the north-west of Echad Mothelen.
Mothelen has asked you gather information from nervous goblins at Burgûl-stazg; however, he also warned you to avoid being seen by the guards of the goblin-camp.

Mothelen is at Echad Mothelen, south-east from Burgûl-stazg.
You should bring the deserter's note to Mothelen with what you have learned.
Burned a barrel of Warg-food (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Greetings, ${PLAYER}. Might I have a word with you?
'Goldínwen believes that we can only reduce the threat of the Wargs by destroying both the beasts and their handlers. I, however, believe there is a much more efficient way to handle them: destroy their sustenance.
'When next you enter Maudhul-ulur, look for barrels of food for the Wargs...if you destroy these, the Wargs and their handlers will be forced to retreat or at least refrain from foraying against us. This flint, steel, and kindling should be of help.'
'Their food burns? That is well. It will, however, take some time before we notice any results.'
Burn barrels of Warg-food (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Nordan at Echad Glamodúd
Burning Dinner
Nordan has a different approach to dealing with the Wargs and their handlers than Goldínwen's.
'Have you burned the Wargs' food yet? No? Then you must return to Maudhul-ulur.'
'The Wargs and their handlers cannot maintain their presence here long without food.'
'Your efforts here are greatly appreciated, ${PLAYER}.'

Barrels of Warg-food can be found at Maudhul-ulur, south from Echad Glamodúd.
Nordan has asked you to enter Maudhul-ulur and burn any casks of Warg-food you may find.

Nordan is at Echad Glamodúd, north from Maudhul-ulur.
You should return to Nordan with tidings of your success.
Destroyed a crate of supplies (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Destroyed weapons (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'You have removed many of the defences protecting Ashúrz Maufulug by disarming the traps of the Orcs, but there is more yet to do. Our forces in the Mirk-eaves are but a small portion of the company that ventured from Lothlórien. We must weaken the enemy, if we are to defeat them.
'I bid you foray against the camp and destroy any weapon-racks and crates of supplies you may find there. Without these, the Orcs will be hard-pressed to defend themselves.
'If you have lost your bearings, Ashúrz Maufulug lies to the south and a little west of here.'

'Well done, ${PLAYER}! The Orcs will not be able to maintain their presence here much longer without those weapons and supplies.
'I have one task left for you, if you would hear me out....'
Destroy crates of supplies at Ashúrz Maufulug (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Destroy weapons in Ashûrz Maufulug (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Glamodúd at Echad Glamodúd
Destroying Their Means
You eliminated much of the threat of traps and archers that made attacking Ashúrz Maufulug a particularly hazardous proposition, but there is more yet to do.
'Do not return, ${PLAYER}, until you have destroyed the weapons and supplies of the Orcs. They are a threat to our very survival.'

Weapon-racks and crates of supplies can be found in Ashúrz Maufulug, to the south and a little west of Echad Glamodúd.
Glamodúd has asked you to further weaken the Orcs of Ashúrz Maufulug by destroying their weapons and supplies.

Glamodúd is at Echad Glamodúd, south and a little west from Ashúrz Maufulug.
You should return to Ashúrz Maufulug with news of your success.
Planted banner at Fállug

'${PLAYER}, it is good that you have come. Our forces swept through this area like a storm, but we were unable to signal our kindred in Lothlórien that all went well.
'If you would, I have a task for you. Take this banner to Fállug, the ruins of an Orc-tower overlooking the Anduin to the south of here, and brace it with stones. Surely you will find a suitable pile of stones there.
'When our banner flies for our kindred to see, return to me.'

'Welcome back, ${PLAYER}. You have planted the banner? Then all is well.
'Once the threat of siege is lessened, Lord Celeborn will muster a greater force to join us.'
Plant banner at Fállug
Talk to Tethafnel at Echad Sirion
Establishing a Foothold
The Elves of the the Golden Host landed on the shores of the Mirk-eaves and drove the Orcs of the river-banks into the forest. Once they secured the shores, they established a camp there.
'Does our banner fly yet upon Fállug? The ruins lie to the south, overlooking the Anduin.'
'Our kindred in Lothlórien will be pleased that we have attained such a victory so quickly.'
'Our banner now flies at Fállug, thanks to you, ${PLAYER}. May it stand forever!'

Fállug lies to the south of Echad Sirion, overlooking the Anduin.
Tethafnel has asked you to plant the banner of the Malledhrim at Fállug so their kindred in Lothlórien will know of their victory.

Tethafnel is at Echad Sirion, north from Fállug.
You should return to Tethafnel and let her know that you have planted the banner as she requested.
Defeated Darkwing spies in the Mirk-eaves (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeated a Warg-scout in the Mirk-eaves (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'If you have a moment, ${PLAYER}, I would speak with you. Our forces landed recently upon this shore and drove off the Orcs after a mighty battle; however, many dark creatures have been seen lurking upon these shores still.
'Many Wargs and crebain roam the Mirk-eaves, undoubtedly spying for the Enemy at Dol Guldur. The eyes of Dol Guldur must be blinded to our movements. If you would purge the crebain and Wargs from these shores, I would be most grateful.
'Be wary upon your task, for goblin-scouts also roam the beaches, and they may ambush you.'
'Very good, ${PLAYER}! It will be long ere the eyes of Dol Guldur will be fixed upon us. Perhaps by then, the rest of our forces will have joined us.'
Defeat Darkwing spies in the Mirk-eaves (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeat Warg-scouts in the Mirk-eaves (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Faroniel at Echad Sirion
Eyes of Dol Guldur
The Elves of the Golden Host have established an encampment on the shores of the Mirk-eaves and seek to protect it against the spies of the Enemy.
'Have you defeated the spies of Dol Guldur? Their masters must not learn how small our camp is.'
'The hounds of the Enemy are a vicious breed, best used as war-beasts, but they are silent enough to make good scouts, as well.'
'The crebain of Dunland serve Saruman the White, but I distrust all crows.'

Crebain and Wargs can be found throughout the Mirk-eaves.
Faroniel has asked you to blind the eyes of Dol Guldur by defeating many of the crebain and Wargs which roam the Mirk-eaves.

Faroniel is at Echad Sirion in the Mirk-eaves.
You should return to Faroniel with tidings of your success.
Defeated a Taughâsh Warg-keeper (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Besides slaying the Wargs, perhaps there is another way to make their Warg-breeding ineffective. Every camp has a leader, and these Wargs have many handlers.
'If you would, go to Maudhul-ulur and defeat any goblin-keepers you find. Perhaps by defeating the handlers, the Wargs will be thrown into disarray.
'When you have slain the goblin-keepers, return to me.'
'You have done well to defeat so many of the goblins, but I fear it is still not enough. This beast has many hands, but only one head....'
Defeat Taughâsh Warg-keepers in Maudhul-ulur (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Goldínwen at Echad Glamodúd
Handling the Handlers
You were unable to defeat all of the Wargs, but Goldínwen has another plan.
'Please...you must defeat the Warg-handlers of Maudhul-ulur, or they will continue to threaten Echad Sirion.'

Goblin Warg-keepers can be found at Maudhul-ulur, south from Echad Glamodúd.
Goldínwen has asked you to defeat the goblin Warg-keepers in order to throw the kennel into disarray.

Goldínwen is at Echad Glamodúd, north from Maudhul-ulur.
You should return to Goldínwen and report your success.
Defeated a Taughâsh Warg (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'${PLAYER}, I am sure you learned that there is a kennel of Wargs, kept by several goblins, not far to the east of Ashúrz Maufulug. Maudhul-ulur is what the Enemy calls it.
'This camp is surely where the Wargs roaming the shores of the Mirk-eaves are coming from, and it is a threat we must deal with at once. I need you to enter Maudhul-ulur and defeat as many Wargs as you can.
'When you have completed your task, return to me.'
'There were too many Wargs for you to destroy utterly? That is a pity, for we cannot hope to attack Ashúrz Maufulug while the beasts still wander.'
Defeat Taughâsh Wargs in Maudhul-ulur (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Goldínwen at Echad Glamodúd
A Howling on the Wind
Beside the Orc-camp at Ashúrz Maufulug, the Elf-scouts discovered a smaller kennel of Wargs and their goblin-keepers not far to the east of the stronghold of the Orcs.
'You have not slain the Wargs of Maudhul-ulur? That is fell news. Perhaps you should return there to complete your task.'

Wargs can be found at Maudhul-ulur, south from Echad Glamodúd.
Goldínwen has asked you to defeat many Wargs at the kennel nearby.

Goldínwen is at Echad Glamodúd, north from Maudhul-ulur.
You should return to Goldínwen with the news that you have defeated many Wargs at Maudhul-ulur.
Defeated Âthruk

'In the end, I believe the only way to truly reduce the threat of the Wargs is to defeat their leader. Cut off the head, and the serpent will die.
'Amid the Wargs of Maudhul-ulur, there is a Warg-rider who leads them all. Defeat Âthruk and his beast, and the Wargs will surely be thrown into disarray.
'Return to me when your task is done, and I will reward you as best I can.'

'Excellent work, ${PLAYER}! The Wargs of Maudhul-ulur will surely fear us now.
'You have earned this reward and the gratitude of the Malledhrim.'
Defeat Âthruk at Maudhul-ulur
Talk to Goldínwen at Echad Glamodúd
Killing the Wolf
The organized Wargs of Maudhul-ulur remain a great threat to the Elves of the Malledhrim.
'Âthruk still lives? That is ill news. He must be slain, or the Wargs remain a threat.'
'The hounds of Dol Guldur have been muzzled at Maudhul-ulur, thanks to you, ${PLAYER}.'
'The Wargs of the Mirk-eaves will fear the Malledhrim.'

Âthruk can be found at Maudhul-ulur, south from Echad Glamodúd.
Goldínwen has asked you to defeat Âthruk, the overseer of Maudhul-ulur.

Goldínwen is at Echad Glamodúd, north from Maudhul-ulur.
You should return to Goldínwen with news of your victory.
Collected a token of Dol Guldur (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'We took the Orcs by surprise when we landed, and quickly routed them into the forest; however, we believe they may either have another camp nearby or are preparing a retaliatory assault, for we have recently seen goblin-scouts on occasion.
'We have dispatched our own patrols to find their camp, but have thus far been unsuccessful. If you would, scour the Mirk-eaves for these elusive scouts. Perhaps they may carry some clue as to their camp's whereabouts. They have a mastery of stealth, so it may be difficult to find them.
'Also, you should speak with Tethafnel and Faroniel here at Echad Sirion. They may have other tasks for you.'

'These tokens bespeak of several encampments, ${PLAYER}. I will send scouts out immediately to find them.
'Remain here, though...I may yet have a task for you....'
'Did you find no evidence of the goblins?'
Collect tokens of Dol Guldur from goblin-scouts (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Falasgon at Echad Sirion
Patrolling the Beach
The Elves of the Golden Host landed on the eastern shore of the Anduin and drove a wedge through the heart of the Orcs, but there is still danger within the Mirk-eaves.
'Have you learned anything yet? We have seen goblin-scouts throughout the mirk-eaves, but they are masters of stealth.'
'These tokens denote different tribes or companies. This does not bode well....'
'There are more Orcs here than we first realized....'

Goblin-scouts can be found sneaking throughout the Mirk-eaves.
Falasgon has asked you to find and defeat some of the goblin-scouts that have been spotted near Echad Sirion. Perhaps they might carry something that will suggest the location of their camp.

Falasgon is at Echad Sirion in the Mirk-eaves.
You should bring the tokens you found to Falasgon for his examination.
Defeated a Taughâsh archer (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'The traps were only one of many defences Ashúrz Maufulug maintains, ${PLAYER}. The Orcs are also defended by several skilled archers.
'These archers patrol the outskirts of Ashúrz Maufulug for signs of approaching enemies. Defeat these archers, or we will be unable to attack the camp.
'When you have completed this task, return to me.'
'Very well done yet again, ${PLAYER}! However, there is still a great threat within Ashúrz Maufulug.'
Defeat Taughâsh archers at Ashúrz Maufulug (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Glamodúd at Echad Glamodúd
Removing the Stinger
The Orcs of Ashúrz Maufulug have placed many traps around their encampment, but those were only one of many defences.
'The archers of the Taughâsh are highly skilled. They are a threat that must be removed.'

Orc-archers can be found patrolling the outskirts of Ashúrz Maufulug, south and a little west from Echad Glamodúd.
Glamodúd has asked you to defeat the Orc-archers who defend Ashúrz Maufulug.

Glamodúd is at Echad Glamodúd, north and a little east from Ashúrz Maufulug.
You should return to Glamodúd with news of your victory.
Defeated Morsharpat at Ashúrz Maufulug

'You have done well to weaken the Orcs so. There is but one vital task left for you to do, ${PLAYER}: sever their sword-arm.
'Deep within Ashúrz Maufulug, you will find their captain, whom we have learned is called Morsharpat. He is a vicious creature of great skill in arms. Slay him, and the Orcs will be easy prey.
'When you have accomplished this task, return to me, and I will reward you as best I may.'
'You have defeated Morsharpat? Then victory is nearly ours! You have earned this reward, ${PLAYER}.'
Defeat Morsharpat at Ashúrz Maufulug
Talk to Glamodúd at Echad Glamodúd
Severing the Sword-arm
You have weakened the Orcs of Ashúrz Maufulug by disarming their traps, leaving them vulnerable to attack.
'Morsharpat still lives? Until he is defeated, the Orcs of Ashúrz Maufulug will remain a threat to us.'
'It shall not be long before our forces at Echad Sirion will rain death upon the Orcs of Ashúrz Maufulug!'
'Hail, ${PLAYER}, bane of Morsharpat!'

Morsharpat is at Ashúrz Maufulug, south and a little west from Echad Glamodúd.
Glamodúd has asked you to defeat Morsharpat, the captain of the Orcs at Ashúrz Maufulug.

Glamodúd is at Echad Glamodúd, north and a little east from Ashúrz Maufulug.
You should return to Glamodúd with news of your victory against Morsharpat.
Now that you have seen one of the Orc-traps, you know what you are looking for
Disarmed an Orc-trap (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'The Orcs of Dol Guldur have established a camp at Ashúrz Maufulug, not far to the south-west from here. Unfortunately, we learned that there is also a kennel of Wargs located to the south of here. Goldínwen will have more knowledge of that camp, as she is the one who discovered it.
'When I tried to get closer to Ashúrz Maufulug, I nearly set off a trap set by the Orcs. I found no others, which I thought strange, until I realized that they were perhaps spread out to discourage larger forces from moving against them.
'If you would, search the fields between here and Ashúrz Maufulug and see if you can find any more traps. Disarm any that you find -- eventually we will want to attack the camp directly -- then return to me.'

'The traps are disarmed? Very well done, ${PLAYER}!
'Do not go far...I have another task for you.'
Find an Orc-trap
Disarm Orc-traps (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Glamodúd at Echad Glamodúd
Springing the Traps
The Elves of the Golden Host have discovered that the Orcs of Dol Guldur have established an encampment at Ashúrz Maufulug, within striking distance of Echad Sirion.
'You must disarm those traps...we cannot defeat the Orcs of Ashúrz Maufulug while they remain.'

Orc-traps might be found anywhere between Echad Glamodúd and Ashúrz Maufulug, to the south and a little west.
Glamodúd has asked you to find and disarm any traps the Orcs may have placed in the Mirk-eaves.

Orc-traps might be found anywhere between Echad Glamodúd and Ashúrz Maufulug, to the south-west.
Glamodúd has asked you to find and disarm any traps the Orcs may have placed in the Mirk-eaves. Now that you have seen one of the Orc-traps, the rest should be much easier to find.

Glamodúd is at Echad Glamodúd, north-east of Ashúrz Maufulug.
You have disarmed many of the Orcs' traps and should now return to Glamodúd with your report.
Defeated Laehendiel at the Dreadweaver's Lair
Defeated a spider (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'If you are willing to aid me, ${PLAYER}, I could use your help. When I was scouting for the location of Burgûl-stazg, I came across a great spider.
'I cannot walk these woods of our kindred of old and not purge it of these creatures. Defeat as many spiders as you may, and their vile mistress Laehendiel. Her lair, I believe is at the Dreadweaver's Lair, south-east from here.
'When you have completed this task, return to me, and I will reward you for your efforts.'
'I am pleased that you were able to slay that vile spider-queen. You have earned this reward.'
Defeat Laehendiel at the Dreadweaver's Lair
Defeat spiders in the Dourstocks (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Lavanferon at Echad Mothelen
Attercop, Attercop
Many dark and evil things dwell in the southern reaches of Mirkwood, spiders not the least.
'Defeat Laehendiel and her brood, ${PLAYER}...they are a threat to the Malledhrim.'

Spiders may be found throughout the Dourstocks. Laehendiel may be found at the Dreadweaver's Lair, south-east from Echad Mothelen.
Lavanferon has asked you to defeat many spiders and their mistress, Laehendiel.

Lavanferon is at Echad Mothelen, north-west from the Dreadweaver's Lair.
You should return to Lavanferon with tidings of your success.
Defeated Carcharan at Gorotham
Defeated a bat (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collected the stolen satchel

'Alas, ${PLAYER}, I have proven a coward when I should show no fear. When I was scouting for the location of Burgûl-stazg, I was swarmed by bats. These vile creatures were not the cause of my fear, however; among them was a great creature that emanated terror. I have no doubt that it was a vampire, such as those which once dwelt in the lands ages past.
'In my terror, I dropped my satchel. It contains many items which may be of use to the Enemy and must be retrieved, but I cannot face that creature again. I ask you to face Carcharan and recover my satchel.
'Carcharan inhabits a cave in Gorotham to the north-east of here, beyond Burgûl-stazg. While you are about this task, please slay as many of those vile bats as you can.'

'Ah! You have destroyed Carcharan and recovered my satchel? That is well.
'You greatly deserve this reward!'
'You have not slain Carcharan, nor retrieved my satchel? That is ill news.'
Defeat Carcharan at Gorotham
Defeat bats in the Dourstocks (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collect the stolen satchel
Return to Lavanferon at Echad Mothelen
A Cloud of Bats
Many dark and vile creatures dwell beneath the eaves of southern Mirkwood. Among these are terrible bats...some of which are creatures of an ancient age.
'I am sure the creature that I confronted was no mere mortal...I am sure it was a vampire of Morgoth.'

Bats may be found throughout the Dourstocks. Carcharan may be found in a cave at Gorotham, north-east from Echad Mothelen, beyond Burgûl-stazg.
Lavanferon has asked you to recover his lost satchel and to defeat the bats of Mirkwood, including the vampire, Carcharan.

Lavanferon is at Echad Mothelen, south-west from Gorotham, beyond Burgûl-stazg.
You should return the satchel to Lavanferon with news of your victory against Carcharan.
Defeated Blackmaw
Defeated a wolf (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Hail, ${PLAYER}! Please stay and speak with me. While my companions fret over the strange happenings in Burgûl-stazg, my forays into the western Dourstocks have discovered more threats, and no less dangerous in my opinion.
'One of these threats is the black wolves. These beasts are vicious and unpredictable. I have also seen a great wolf, which I have named Blackmaw. His lair lies some distance to the south-east of here at the Packhowler's Hill.
'I bid you go forth and defeat as many of the wolves as you can and lay low Blackmaw.'
'It is well, ${PLAYER}, that you have returned victorious. Such evil cannot be allowed to persist in this place which was once the fair Greenwood.'
Defeat Blackmaw at the Packhowler's Hill
Defeat wolves in the Dourstocks (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Lavanferon at Echad Mothelen
Muzzling the Pack
Many dark and evil things dwell in the southern forests of Mirkwood. Among those are the black wolves.
'Blackmaw and his pack have been terrorizing the flanks of our host. They must be defeated!'

Black wolves can be found throughout the Dourstocks. Blackmaw can be found at the Packhowler's Hill, some distance to the south-east from Echad Mothelen.
Lavanferon has asked you to defeat many wolves and their pack-leader, Blackmaw.

Lavanferon is at Echad Mothelen, some distance north-west from the Packhowler's Hill.
You should return to Lavanferon with news of your success.

'${PLAYER}, I fear something dire is about to occur. The shadow of the Necromancer lies still upon Mirkwood. I know little more of these forsaken shades, but perhaps you may learn more if you speak with Prestadír at the Haunted Inn.
'The Haunted Inn lies to the east of here, deeper into the Dourstocks.'
'${PLAYER}, you have come to me at a fortuitous time. Something is amiss here. The shades of dead Men roam these lands. Of what broken oaths could have cursed them here, I am not yet sure....'
Talk to Prestadír at the Haunted Inn
Broken Oaths
The appearance of the shades at Burgûl-stazg disturbed the Elf Mothelen, foreshadowing a more dire evil.
'${PLAYER}, you must journey to the Haunted Inn and speak with the Ranger Prestadír. I am certain he could use your assistance.'

Prestadír is at the Haunted Inn, east from Echad Mothelen.
Mothelen suggested you speak with Prestadír to learn more about the shades of the Dourstocks.

'${PLAYER}, I have received word from Falasgon at Echad Sirion: the second enemy encampment has been discovered. It appears, though, that this encampment is not nearly the threat that Ashúrz Maufulug had been.
'You should travel to Echad Mothelen, far to the north-east from here, in the western part of the Dourstocks, and speak with the patrol captain, Mothelen. He will be able to tell you more.'
'Welcome, ${PLAYER}, though I wish it were less disturbing circumstances. Something queer is afoot in this place, and we need your help learning exactly what that is.'
Talk to Mothelen at Echad Mothelen
The Enemy in the East
The Malledhrim of Echad Sirion have discovered the location of yet another enemy encampment.
'Hurry to Echad Mothelen, ${PLAYER}. Mothelen has need of your assistance.'

Mothelen is at Echad Mothelen, far to the north-east from Amon Angened.
Dannaswen has suggested you speak with Mothelen regarding the recently discovered enemy encampment in the western Dourstocks.

'${PLAYER}, while you were gone, one of our scouts discovered the location of an Orc-encampment to the south and another to the north. However, these tokens you brought me belong to four different tribes or companies. I fear there are other camps we may not have found yet.
'While I send more patrols out to find the other encampments, you should travel to Echad Glamodúd, near the Orc-camp, and speak with Glamodúd, the chief scout there. He will give you further instruction.
'You should also speak with Aemeldir here at Echad Sirion... he was involved on the initial attack against Durbúrz-stazg and may know more about the remnant of the Orcs there. We must not be caught unaware between enemy forces!'
'You have come from Echad Sirion? That is well, for we are in dire need of your assistance.'
'Greetings, ${PLAYER}. Yes, Falasgon is correct. I could most certainly use your assistance....'
Talk to Glamodúd at Echad Glamodúd
Talk to Aemeldir at Echad Sirion
Enemy Upon the Threshold
The presence of goblin-spies in the Mirk-eaves also infers the presence of an enemy encampment somewhere in the vicinity.

'You should meet with Glamodúd at Echad Glamodúd, south-east from here, at the southern foot of Amon Angened, where the main way-post of the Malledhrim has been established. He will tell you what aid he may need.
'Aemeldir here at Echad Sirion will know more about Dúrburz-stazg.'

Glamodúd is at Echad Glamodúd, south-east from Echad Sirion, at the southern foot of Amon Angened. Aemeldir is at Echad Sirion.
Farasgon has asked you to speak with Glamodúd regarding the Orc-camp to the south and Aemeldir regarding Dúrburz-stazg, the encampment to the north.

'Hail, ${CLASS}, and welcome. I am the leader of this company, though I fear I do poorly with the safekeeping of our goals. Perhaps I am rather too lenient with the whims of my good people, for I gave Nífdir leave to investigate the whisperings, and now it has been many days since his return.
'The whisperings, yes. Have you not heard them? We all perceived the shudderings and discontent amongst the trees as we travelled through the drowned lands. Good Nífdir wished to remain and hear them, for he is more concerned with the trees than with the Orcs and wraiths. He loves all forests, however bleak and black they seem. I had not the heart to forbid him.
'Did I do wrong to leave him behind? It has been many days since we parted ways to the west of here, in the heart of the swamp. I yearn to know if he has come to harm, but I do not wish to send others into danger for my foolishness, for we are precious few, and our mission is clear. I have already compromised our plans. Will you seek Nífdir?'

'Nífdir lives! You lift a great burden from my shoulders with this news, ${PLAYER}; I thank you. You have been very helpful.
'I do wish he would hasten with his work, however. Perhaps you can help him to speed this along, for I fear that further delay will compromise our aims.'

'Mae govannen, mellon. Nenedhel sent you to find me, did he? I am sorry to have given him anxiety on my behalf, and I hope that he will forgive me. I fear I am not ready to leave just yet. Can you perceive the wrath and fury of the trees all around us? I must know what angers them so.
'Please return to Nenedhel with my apologies and word that I am whole and well. Tell him that I will return when I can, but not before I attempt to discern what ails the trees of this swamp. I do not think they are evil! Alas, my heart is saddened by their pain.'
Seek Nífdir in the Drownholt
Talk to Nenedhel at Estolad Mernael
The Glowering Trees of the Drownholt

The Elves of the Drownholt are missing one of their own -- a curious Elf who fancied he heard the sorrow of the trees as they made their way through the swamplands. He has not returned, and his companions yearn for news of him.
'Nífdir was last seen to the west of here, deep within the swamp, but that was many days ago. I hope that he is safe....'
'You are very good to have sought me for Nenedhel's peace of mind! Please assure him that I am well enough.'

Nenedhel parted ways with Nífdir to the west of Estolad Mernael.
Nenedhel, leader of the Malledhrim in the Drownholt, has asked you to seek Nífdir in the swamp-lands.

Nenedhel is at Estolad Mernael, east of Nífdir's small camp.
You should speak with Nenedhel and assure him that Nífdir is safe, but not yet ready to rejoin his companions.
Mirk-huorn defeated (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'My host of the Malledhrim will not be marching without Nífdir among them; I will wait for him, but he must not tarry long. Please make sure he knows this. If you can find a way to assist him so that his work does not delay him overlong, you will be helping me also.
'Go back to Nífdir, ${PLAYER}, and lend what aid you can. I do not know if there is much that can be done for the poor inhabitants of this foreboding swamp. Many of my folk feel that there is no hope or heart left in the swamp-lands...but you should not despair.
'The fear from Dol Guldur has thrown a long shadow across these once-fair woods, yet the power of the Elves is strong also. Do not give up hope.'

'Ah, ${PLAYER}! I am surprised to see you and very pleased that Nenedhel sent you back to me. When we passed through the swamp-lands, we all heard it -- the wrath and pain from deep within the hearts of the trees. The others took a wide detour to avoid the glade that seemed to be the very heart of malice.
'I have a way with trees, but I fear these Huorns. I am no warrior, you see, so I have been watching their movements from this outlook. But perhaps you, a worthy ${CLASS}, will have better luck if you approach them.
'Try to speak with them, but do not let yourself come to harm! You might be met with much hostility if you dare this task. Be wary, friend.'

'That is a sad tale, ${PLAYER}! Most of the creatures you will find as you wander this dour forest are evil and have always been evil. But trees have long, long memories, unlike the other children of this Middle-earth -- that is why they are so familiar to me, I think.
'It is long since these trees have had any hope, but they have not forgotten the brighter days. Poor creatures! Perhaps I can devise a way to help them, if you could give me a moment to think....'

This Huorn's twigs shiver menacingly as you draw near, but it does not attack. It is a very old tree, and its will is strong. Surely this is the tree that the Elves perceived as they passed Sâd Meryrn.
As you stand at its roots, your mind is impressed with recollections of a fair green forest full of new life, and of a shadow of fear, ever-growing. The green life withers, blackens, and dies. Evil poisons consume the very water and air.
Talk to Nífdir at his camp
Approach Mirk-huorns (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Approach the largest Mirk-huorn and attempt to speak with it
Talk to Nífdir at his camp
The Writhing Glade
Nífdir wishes to learn what ails the violent trees of the Drownholt, and help them if it is possible to do so.
'Please hasten to Nífdir's aid, mellon. The Malledhrim will not march while one of their host remains behind. He can be found to the west of here.'
'Go, ${PLAYER}, and speak with the trees of Sâd Meryrn if you can! But you must defend yourself if they attempt to attack you, for I would not have you come to harm on my behalf.'

Nífdir can be found at a small camp to the west of Estolad Mernael.
Nenedhel has asked you once again to seek out Nífdir in the heart of the Drownholt.

Huorns can be found in Sâd Meryrn, due south of Nífdir's small camp. You should travel north and west to reach their glade.
You should approach Huorns and attempt to speak with them, but Nífdir has advised you to be prepared for much open hostility.

The Wrathful Huorn stands in Sâd Meryrn.
One Mirk-huorn does not seem as malicious as the rest; you should approach it and learn what you can from it.

Nífdir is at the camp overlooking Sâd Meryrn from the north.
You should speak with Nífdir and tell him of the strange conversation of sorts that passed between yourself and the Mirk-huorn.

'I can think of one small gesture that might do some good. The mallorn trees of Lothlórien, thriving under the power of Galadriel and the care of the Galadhrim, inspire all who harbour love for the wilderness. The mallorns will resist stain as long as the Elves are here to tend them.
'I want you to go to my friend Menassiel in Lothlórien, at Cerin Amroth. Surely her heart will be moved by your tale, as mine is. I would like to plant a mallorn sapling here, in this glade. It will give hope to the Huorns. I do not think it will fully quell their wrath, but it has been long since they have seen any light. They deserve a glimmer of hope, for someday the shadows of Dol Guldur will trouble this place no more.
'Go to Menassiel now, ${PLAYER}, and see if she will help you.'

'You indeed tell a sad story, ${PLAYER}. Thank you for offering to return to that dangerous place for so generous a deed. Not many outsiders love the trees as much as we Galadhrim do.
'I only hope that I do not send this child to its death in that forsaken swamp. Please see that it is cared for, if you pass it by. It has some power to spread its light and dispel the cruel corruptions of Mirkwood, but...nay, I will trust to hope. The power of Galadriel is in the very sap of this young one.
'Return to the glade if you dare, ${PLAYER}, and plant this seed. See that none disturb it.'
'You have returned! I am glad. Let me see what Menassiel has given us.'
'Have you been to see Menassiel yet? She can be found near Cerin Amroth in Lothlórien.'
Talk to Menassiel at Cerin Amroth
Bring the mallorn sapling to Nífdir
A Gift of Gold
The Elf Nífdir is moved by the unhappy state of the Mirk-huorns and the tale of their slow loss of hope. He wishes to do something to alleviate their sadness and despair.
'Bring this little seedling to Nífdir, mellon. It is my gift to the aged trees who live in despair. I hope it brings them light, as the mallorns have done for us also.'
'Menassiel stands near Cerin Amroth, in Lothlórien. You should go to her and see if she will help us.'

Menassiel can be found at Cerin Amroth in Lothlórien.
You should speak with Menassiel and see if she will gift the Huorns of Mirkwood with a young mallorn, a light to dispel the shadows upon their wretched existence.

Nífdir is at his camp in the Drownholt, west of the Malledhrim outpost of Estolad Mernael.
You should return to Nífdir to show him the seedling donated by Menassiel.
You have planted the seedling

'Here, mellon; take the seedling back and keep it safe. Do not let any harm it!
'Menassiel chose a promising young mallorn, and I am very pleased to offer this to the Mirk-huorns. Good fortune upon this venture, ${PLAYER}. I hope all goes well this time.'

'You have not been gone very long, ${PLAYER}, but it sounds as though much has been accomplished! You have my thanks. I am glad Nífdir will have fulfilled his wish to be of aid to the pained creatures here.'
Plant the mallorn seedling in Sâd Meryrn
Plant the mallorn seedling in Sâd Meryrn
Talk to Nenedhel at Estolad Mernael
Rending the Shadows of Sâd Meryrn

You now carry a gift of light and hope for the corrupted Mirk-huorns of Sâd Meryrn. However evil they now seem, these old creatures of Mirkwood stir pity, for their long memory has not let them forget the taste of clean air and sunlight, when life was greener.
'I hope that you can find a way to help the trees, ${PLAYER}. No creature deserves such suffering.'
'You have done very well, my good friend! You should speak with Nenedhel now and tell him that I will be along shortly. Thank you for all you have done.'

Sâd Meryrn can be found due south of Nífdir's camp, but you should strike north and west to reach the glade.
Nífdir has asked you to plant the mallorn seedling in Sâd Meryrn.

Nenedhel awaits news of Nífdir's endeavour at Estolad Mernael, east of Nífdir's encampment.
You should speak with Nenedhel and inform him that Nífdir's task is complete.
Collected luminous stinger (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Welcome to our small stronghold, good ${CLASS}. We are beset by dangers all around, both in the swamp-lands and beyond. There are many poisonous things, and while they do not threaten us, a great risk is posed to our horse-friends, and those of other races who travel with us as well.
'I saw the fell glow of fireflies as we travelled here, and such a sickly light can only be poison from such a creature. Could you collect the stingers of these flies? I could use the venom stored within to craft an antidote, as a precaution.
'Please collect for me as many stingers as you can, but be careful -- I do not wish to see you come to harm. These insects are strong and swift and will have no mercy upon any who draw too near.'

'Thank you, ${PLAYER}; you have done well to bring me these. Now I can set to work at making a draught that will act against this venom.
'What a sickly glow emanates from it still!'
'Have you collected any stingers from the fireflies? They can be found throughout the Drownholt.'
Collect luminous stingers (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring the luminous stingers to Rocheledh at Estolad Mernael
Luminous Poisons

Rocheledh is concerned that many sources of poison are potential threats to those who assist the Golden Host on their venture through Mirkwood. He wishes to craft an antidote to have on hand against the firefly poison.
'You may find the stinging flies throughout the Drownholt, glowing among the darkness of these dense trees. Be wary of their poison, mellon!'

Fireflies can be found throughout the Drownholt in Mirkwood.
Rocheledh has asked you to collect the venomous stingers of fireflies so that he may craft an antidote against the poison. He fears for safety of the Elf-friends who travel with the Malledhrim.

Rocheledh is at Estolad Mernael in the Drownholt.
You should bring the stingers you collected to Rocheledh so that he may craft a useful antidote from their luminous venom.
Defeated swamp-cats in the Drownholt (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'How eerie! I can see them from this very spot, when they dare to come into view. Surely you have been hunted by them on your way here, have you not, ${PLAYER}? I am speaking of the dire cats of this vile black swamp.
'I daresay those beasts have never had a wholesome meal in their lives, for generations uncounted. They seem to be driven mad by our presence, for apparently we and our horses seem like the best food that has ever presented itself before them.
'I do not like how they prowl and stalk. Please go and thin their numbers so that the good folk who may have need to travel can do so without being eaten.'
'Well done, my good ${RACE}. I am sure the tentative paths of this swamp will be safer now for those who have need to travel. We can rest easier now.'
Defeat swamp-cats in the Drownholt (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Laidhriel at Estolad Mernael
Stalked by Shadows
The swamp-cats of the Drownholt prowl hungrily about, stalking any that move about unawares. They are causing the Elves of Estolad Mernael great unease.
'If you can thin the numbers of swamp-cats about Estolad Mernael, we will all be much safer.'

Swamp-cats can be found in the drowned lands of the Drownholt, all around Estolad Mernael.
Laidhriel has asked you to defeat many of the hunting swamp-cats that stalk the camp.

Laidhriel can be found at Estolad Mernael, the Malledhrim camp in the Drownholt.
You should speak with Laidhriel and tell her of your success against the evil swamp-cats of the drowned lands.
There is a terrible rancour about this particular pool

'We are terribly distraught, randir. This dear one fell ill as we passed through the swamp-lands. It was day when we crossed the Drownholt, and Alagos bore me hither. But after a time his step became slower, and the moment we had successfully defeated the Orcs in a great skirmish, he collapsed where he stood.
'He seemed to sleep, but alas, he recedes further from my calls every moment! I fear there is not much time to cure whatever malice ails him, ${PLAYER}. What wretchedness could affect him thus? The Drownholt is an evil place.
'Until we know exactly where this began, I do not think we can help him. I fear to leave his side, though -- I am doing everything I can to hold him here. Could you go into the swamp and seek the source of this malady?'
'How awful! I could not perceive the difference when I walked through that pool upon Alagos, for the evil of this swamp is overwhelming wherever I go. I wonder what troubles the waters there....'
Explore the Drownholt for the source of illness
Talk to Nestawen at Estolad Mernael
The Mysterious Affliction

One of the horses travelling with the Malledhrim has fallen ill, and the Elves begin to lose hope that he can be healed. His illness began as they passed through the Drownholt and has grown steadily more grave over time.
'Please hurry, ${PLAYER}. I do not think I can keep Alagos with us much longer if I do not know more about what befell him in the swamp!'

Nestawen rode upon Alagos on her route to Estolad Mernael.
You should explore possible routes Nestawen may have travelled and look for anything out of the ordinary that could have induced the steed's strange illness.

Nestawen can be found at Estolad Mernael, the Malledhrim camp in the Drownholt.

'Now you must return to Imlad Lalaith and tell Braiglinn that we have seized our first foothold across the river. 'I will see to the rest of the preparations necessary for Echad Sirion to serve as the camp for our first excursions into Mirkwood.'

'We will do all that we can to see both of these done.'

'The first crossing was a success, ${PLAYER}? That means it is time for the second, smaller company to cross Anduin.

The first crossing of the Anduin by the Malledhrim has been successful, and now it is time for the company charged with transporting Mazog to cross as well.
'Return to the launch-officer, Calengoth, near the boats, and he will ferry you back to Lothlórien so you can speak with Braiglinn. Tell him it is time for the second crossing.'
'Alfirimbes has begun making preparations to bring Mazog out of the Mirk-eaves and closer to the fortress of Dol Guldur. Speak with her at the camp of Echad Sirion, across the river.'

'Are you ready to meet the company responsible for the dangerous undertaking of bringing Mazog to Dol Guldur in exchange for the prisoners? I will bring you to them and make the introductions.'

'The success of the Hidden Guard's errand will depend, I think, upon secrecy. We must ensure that the Orcs of Mirkwood do not learn of Mazog's presence beneath the eaves, or they will surely launch an attack upon us in such number we cannot repel them.
'To the south-east are two forts from which the Orcs of Mirkwood maintain a watch over this part of the forest. Search any coffers you find at Maudhûl-ulur and Ashúrz Maufulug for Orc-communications and defeat any of the Taughâsh you find in the Mirk-eaves as you do.
'If you can return to me with any plans or messages that mention Mazog, we can determine how to proceed. If they are aware that we have brought him out of Moria, we may need to act quickly to survive.'

'I see. I admire the determination of the Greyhammers and am sure that Lúth and the rest of his family will be a great help to the Golden Host, but I hope he will spend more time with his duties and less time explaining the various grievances he bears against the Orcs.
'We have all suffered at their hands, and Lúth no more than the rest of us. Achardor might say he has suffered less than some.
'Mazog will account for all slights in time, both real and imagined. Raddir spoke with me while you sought the dwarf. It is time to bring Mazog deeper into Mirkwood.'

'At last, someone who will listen to me! I might have known it would be you, ${PLAYER}. You are held in great esteem by my lords Bósi and Brogur and have proven yourself a friend of the Iron Garrison. You will be a friend, too, of the Greyhammers!
'These Elves do not have the experience with Orcs that we Greyhammers do! Oh, they seem understanding enough when I recount the many grievances my family has suffered at the hands of Mazog and his forebears, but I can tell they think I exaggerate. Do I exaggerate the wounding of my grandfather Thormar at Azanulbizar, who walked with a limp ever after? Or the curse levied against my father Tandri by Bolg himself, that he never again find valuable ore in the deeps?
'I just want these Elves to acknowledge how dangerous Mazog is, even in captivity, and to post a Greyhammer sentry wherever he is being kept. You go back and tell Alfirimbes that. My family deserves this honour after all the hurts Mazog and his kin have wrought on mine.'

'You found a report addressed to Mazog in the coffer of the Orc-leader at Ashúrz Maufulug? Let me see what it says, ${PLAYER}....
'Fortune is with us, my adventurous ${CLASS}: these Orcs do not yet know we have captured Mazog and brought him into Mirkwood. They think he resides still in Moria; the errand of the Hidden Guard remains secret.
'A problem arose while you were away. Lúth Greyhammer, a dwarf of Bróin's company, has become increasingly agitated about the plans of the Golden Host. Speak with him here at Echad Sirion, if you would, and assure him that we are doing all that we may to make this journey a safe one. His family has many grievances with the Orcs, but I fear the Greyhammers may do us ill if they do not keep their heads about them.'
'You have not yet found any plans of the Orcs that mention Mazog?'
Find a coffer in Maudhûl-ulur or Ashúrz Maufulug containing information about Mazog

Alfirimbes believes the success of the Hidden Guard's errand depends on keeping the presence of Mazog a secret from the Orcs of Mirkwood.

'Lúth Greyhammer walks throughout the camp of Echad Sirion, making known his feelings about this endeavour. Speak with him and keep him calm, ${PLAYER}. He may unknowingly do us harm if he persists in his unrest.'

'Raddir has plotted a course through Mirkwood that avoids some of its more overt dangers, but this first leg may be treacherous. The path he has chosen winds through the foetid marshlands of the Drownholt. He names it Râd Cened and tells me it should be free of Orcs.
'But Raddir spoke of other hazards, the like of which we may not expect: spongy earth that clings to the foot, thickets of briars that will catch clothing and armour and break your concentration, great pools of stagnant water that can slow your progress to a crawl. You and the other members of the Hidden Guard will need to be cautious of these and other dangers. Few travel through the Drownholt, unless they have very good reason to do so. Keeping beneath the Enemy's notice until Mazog is at his doorstep is one such reason.
'Speak with me again, and I will show you to the rest of the company for this leg of the journey.'

'I do not know what we can do, ${PLAYER}. Only Raddir knows upon what paths he planned to bring us to Dol Guldur with our captive, and without him, the secret ways are veiled to us. I fear our errand stands on the very brink of failure before it has begun.'

'I worried that the Greyhammers would become a problem, ${PLAYER}, but what could I say about it? Nothing, and now they have gotten themselves -- and us as well -- into trouble!
'Otri Greyhammer can tell you more. I saw him last inside the Haunted Inn, raging at the hearth there to anyone who would listen.'

'Hello again, ${PLAYER}. This waiting has already begun to wear thin, and my patience was stretched to begin with! The Elves have not yet decided which way to go. Perhaps you can help them decide, if anyone can.'

'${PLAYER}, will you help me? You had better, for that is why you're a part of this foolish endeavour, is it not? I would not speak ill of the plans of Bósi and Brogur, but Bróin has not had the experience of his uncle or his father, has he? Nor that of the Greyhammers, truth be told!
'Now two of my brothers have gone missing in the swamp, and if the Elves know the difference between treacherous ground and solid footing, they have taken care not to tell us which is which!
'Find Rósar and Stígur Greyhammer, somewhere among the fens of the Drownholt, ${PLAYER}, and find them quickly. There are watery terrors in that place, and no self-respecting dwarf would be pleased to be stuck in such a vile marsh with the only help to be had these Lórien Elves!'

'Rósar and Stígur were just here, ${PLAYER}, and they had the strangest stories to tell. Each of them reported seeing familiar faces among the tangled bushes and briars and hearing voices on the wind, but when they approached, filled with amazement to see lost friends in such a place, there was no sign of anyone. But lo, further ahead...an encouraging wave and a smile!
'This place fills me with unease, ${PLAYER}. Thank you for rescuing my brothers. Without your aid, I fear there would have been two fewer Greyhammers in this world come sundown, if sundown ever truly leaves this grim wood.
'Bróin is in the cellar. Tell him my brothers are safe and ask him, too, if the Elves have come to an agreement on how to proceed. The sooner we move on from this place, the happier this Greyhammer will be!'
As you stare into the glassy eyes of the dwarf, you come to know that this is not Rósar Greyhammer at all, but an image conjured out of the evils of the marsh. Do not let it lead you astray!
As you stare into the glassy eyes of the dwarf, you come to know that this is not Stígur Greyhammer at all, but an image conjured out of the evils of the marsh. Do not let it lead you astray!

'My brothers went into the fens of the Drownholt, south of the Dourstocks, and never returned. It is said there are watery terrors within the marshes of the Drownholt, and I believe it! Rumour has it an Elf was lost to one of these!
'If some evil has seized hold of my brothers, I must know about it so I can add its name to the list of Greyhammer foes!'

'The death of the Elf Raddir has made uncertain the fate of this journey, ${PLAYER}, for none of the Elves know by which way he planned to bring us in secret to Dol Guldur.
'Speak with the Elves here in the cellar and try to decide on the proper course. Someone must step forward and take charge, or it will be next winter before we advance even a single step...and who knows what will befall Bori in the meantime?'

'This is as I expected, ${PLAYER}: ask three Elves which way is best to take, and you will receive three answers, each different.
'We have little time left to waste. I want you to scout these proposed roads, my accommodating ${CLASS}, and assess the dangers along each.
'Perhaps that will aid with our decision. Seek the scouts we sent to the Scuttledells, Emyn Lûm, and Taur Morvith and question them about the dangers they have encountered.'

'I have decided what we must do, ${PLAYER}. The path through Taur Morvith would bring us too near the Orc-camps in that valley, and we are certain the direct way through Emyn Lûm, along which the Golden Host will march, is already being watched. No, our path lies through the Scuttledells. It will be dangerous, but that will itself serve as a cloak for spying eyes.
'Speak with Issuriel in the cellar of this inn and tell her I have chosen her suggested path.'

'Raddir brought us into the Drownholt despite the danger for a reason, ${PLAYER}. He must have planned for us to take the southernmost way towards Dol Guldur and to bring us in secret up to the southern base of the rocky spire upon which the fortress stands.
'We should therefore head south through the stony reaches of Taur Morvith. That is the way Raddir wanted us to go, I am sure of it.
'The other members of the company may disagree, but we must at least set out, or his death will have been for naught!'

'I do not know what to do, ${PLAYER}. I believe Raddir thought to approach Dol Guldur by the ways least likely to be watched by the forces of the Enemy, but our excursion into the Drownholt....
'I have to believe that Raddir knew what he was doing, ${PLAYER}, and that he knew the risks. But still he took us into the Drownholt; he must have had a good reason.
'The Enemy would never expect us to take the road through the Scuttledells, for that place has a dangerous reputation. That is the path of greatest secrecy, and only through the Scuttledells will we come to Dol Guldur with our prisoner and our presence unannounced.'

'I see, ${PLAYER}. I do not know if I should be pleased that our path will bring us into the Scuttledells, but my heart tells me this is the way we must go.
'There is one more thing, ${PLAYER}. I hesitate to mention it, but something has been bothering me for a while now....'

'We cannot wait here for a revelation that may not come, ${PLAYER}: we will never know what road Raddir intended for us to take.
'No, we must decide and decide quickly. The quick road will be the safest road. Let us move directly eastward to Dol Guldur by the straightest way; Raddir believed our greatest strength was in secrecy, but the dangerous path through the Drownholt cost him his life.
'Let us be done with secret ways. The straightest course, like a swift arrow, is the one we should now take if we wish to avoid a similar fate.'
