'Does it seem to you as if the Enemy's numbers are growing rather than waning as we battle them? It is because they are.
'When we launched our strike across the river, Dol Guldur was manned only by its garrison and the watch they had placed upon the river -- now we have received news of a great army approaching through the forest from the East.
'Already forward elements of this army have arrived to bolster Dol Guldur's strength, and when the main body arrives, we shall surely be driven back across the river. We have little time left to us, but we have nearly achieved our objectives, so take heart, my friend.'

'Does it seem to you as if the Enemy's numbers are growing rather than waning as we battle them? It is because they are.
'When we launched our strike across the river, Dol Guldur was manned only by its garrison and the watch they had placed upon the river -- now we have received news of a great army approaching through the forest from the East.
'Already forward elements of this army have arrived to bolster Dol Guldur's strength, and when the main body arrives, we shall surely be driven back across the river. We have little time left to us, but we have nearly achieved our objectives, so take heart, my friend.'

'Does it seem to you as if the Enemy's numbers are growing rather than waning as we battle them? It is because they are.
'When we launched our strike across the river, Dol Guldur was manned only by its garrison and the watch they had placed upon the river -- now we have received news of a great army approaching through the forest from the East.
'Already forward elements of this army have arrived to bolster Dol Guldur's strength, and when the main body arrives, we shall surely be driven back across the river. We have little time left to us, but we have nearly achieved our objectives, so take heart, my friend.'

The Elf waypoint can be found marked by a stone to the north of Emyn Lûm.
You should scout the first waypoint of the patrol that Fuirgam has asked you to undertake and defeat any Orcs you might find there.

The Elf waypoint can be found marked by a stone to the north-east of Emyn Lûm.
You should scout the second waypoint of the patrol that Fuirgam has asked you to undertake and defeat any Orcs you might find there.

The Elf waypoint can be found marked by a stone to the east of Emyn Lûm.
You should scout the third waypoint of the patrol that Fuirgam has asked you to undertake and defeat any Orcs you might find there.

The Elf waypoint can be found marked by a stone to the south-east of Emyn Lûm.
You should scout the fourth waypoint of the patrol that Fuirgam has asked you to undertake and defeat any Orcs you might find there.

Fuirgam is at Ost Galadh.
You should return to Fuirgam and report in.

'So you have come through the dark halls of Moria to sunny Nanduhirion, have you? Mae govannen, ${PLAYER}. The eaves of Lórien are near, and if you gain the trust of my people you shall find refuge beyond the Nimrodel. These are very dangerous times in which we live.
'Word of your ventures has reached my ears. I bid you what welcome I can as you emerge from the darkness, and I say this to you also: take care! Many evil things have stirred from the dark, and this dale is not safe.
'Upon the Nimrodel is a talan belonging to Haldir, a protector of the eaves of Laurelindórenan. He will offer you refuge. The way is hidden! Seek him beyond Echad Andestel, and wet your feet in the Nimrodel, near the bridge that is broken. South of that bridge and upon the shore is a great mallorn-tree. Upon that tree you shall find Haldir. He will trust you if he knows you have come with my leave.'

'Welcome to Lothlórien, ${CLASS}. We have had many strange visitors of late. You shall find refuge here, if refuge you seek. I am very pleased to make your acquaintance, for even in this remote place we have heard rumour of your valour.'
Speak with Haldir at his talan
Refuge upon Talan Haldir

Meredhrandir at Mekhem-bizru is concerned for your well-being with all the Orcs of Moria so stirred in the Dimrill Dale. He has recommended that you seek refuge in Lórien and appeal to the good will of Haldir at his talan, which is hidden.
'Haldir and his brothers are the Marchwardens of Lothlórien. They make their post at a flet to the south-east.'
'Many strangers have wandered in our fair eaves of late, randir.'

The talan of Haldir is at the banks of the Nimrodel, south of the road that leads to the broken bridge.
Meredhrandir at Mekhem-bizru has urged you to seek the protection of Haldir before you come to harm so near the stirring mouth of Moria.

Mat Heathertoes is found in Beggar's Alley, south-west from Scholar's Stair, then west under the Mud Gate from the Stone Quarter.
Newbold Leafcutter told you to speak with Mat Heathertoes next.

The Bree Jail can be found by following the road east through Bree past the Bree Town Hall, then bearing south.
Mat Heathertoes suggested you speak with Lily Appledore at the Bree Jail.

The Bree Auction Hall lies east through the Woodsmen's Gate, then south.
Dawn Appledore instructed you to speak with one of the auctioneers at the Auction Hall.

Tad Leafcutter is outside the hunting lodge, which can be found by following the road outside of the Bree Auction Hall west to its end.
You have been instructed to speak with Tad Leafcutter.

Graeme Tenderlarch is at the Bree Town Hall, almost due north-west from the South-gate.
Tad Leafcutter told you to return to Graeme Tenderlarch.
'You will find the Scholar's Stair south-east under the arch and into the alley east before the dwarf-statue. Speak with Newbold. He is a good old fellow.'
'Mat Heathertoes lives in the less savoury part of town to the east. The refugees from the south seem to be taking up there more often than anywhere else in Bree.'
'You'll find that most villains find their way to the jails. South and east beyond the Town Hall but before the wood gate.'

'Time for you to visit the other thieves in Bree, the auctioneers.
'You will find them beyond the Wood Gate.'
'Speak with the leaders of the Men of Bree. Follow the road west outside of the auction hall.'
'Speak with the leaders of the Men of Bree. You will find them west down the road.'
'Return to the Town Hall and speak with Graeme Tenderlarch.'

Lalia's Market is just north of the Boar Fountain in the Market Square.
Second-watcher Heathstraw has suggested you browse Lalia's Market and speak with the proprietor.

'Look here! Another new face in Bree-town, and not one of those swarthy Southerners, but a right honest ${RACE}. This is heartening to see.
'Graeme told me that there may be folk stopping in as they learned about the more important areas of Bree. Well, here it is... the crafting-hall of Bree. We have all manner of crafters here at Three-farrow. You can feel free to ply any trade you know within this hall.
'I was told to send you on toward one of Bree's most precious pieces of art, the Boar Fountain, to speak with Second-watcher Heathstraw for a bit of history. You will find him just up the hill to the north at the Boar Fountain in Market Square.'

'Well, well! It is good to see you again. I assume that you are on your tour of Bree and looking for some information about the town. Well, I am not the historian that certain other folks are, but I do know a bit about the town and the reason that the boar plays such a big part in the decoration of the town.
'When Bree was settled, the area was prime hunting-grounds for wild boar. The beasts served as the primary source of meat for the first settlers and have become something of a symbol of tenacity. The Boar Fountain was built to honour those first folk who settled Bree and used the wild boar surrounding the township as provender.
'Well now, it's a pleasure talking to you, but you'll want to be on your way to see the wares at Lalia's Market! Say hello to Lalia herself inside the store, it's just across the square from here, to the north.'

'Well, well, we've been getting a mighty large number of travellers coming into Bree. You don't have the look of one of those Southerners, though....
'I am Barliman Butterbur, and this is the Prancing Pony, finest inn in all of Bree-land. You can feel free to drink here and stay here, if you've the coin. Now I'm forgetting something... it's like that, so busy and all. Oh yes! I am to send you on to your next stop upon your tour through Bree.
'Leave my inn and head down the hill, west beyond the Inn Gate. A short distance from there you will see the road split. Turn north and visit Lily Sandheaver at the first house there.'

'Hullo, friend! You must be new to Bree and on an errand from Mayor Tenderlarch! It is good to make your acquaintance. I am Lily Sandheaver... I handle all the goods grown by the hobbits living on the hill.
'I also like collecting historical heirlooms, which reminds me that my hireling hasn't yet sent me anything... I hope all is well.
'Oh, I am to send you to visit the West-gate to speak with Harry Goatleaf. Just head west towards the gate, and you should see Harry there. You may want to speak to Bill Rosewood too... he minds the horses of West Bree.'

'What do you want? Tenderlarch is a fool, thinking that any of us want to take our time to speak with people who'll be in Bree causing no end of trouble. He should focus on affairs that he can truly handle.
'Get out of my sight. Talk to Watchman Cardoon if you want more help. He's right down the road to the east.'

'Greetings, ${PLAYER}. Goatleaf sent you here? He's been acting queerer and queerer recently.
'No matter of concern, I am certain. You should visit the vault next. You will find it down the road to the south. It is a large, stone building with two guardsman keeping watch.
'Enter the vault and speak with either Tad Gardener or Maud Foxglove.'

'Welcome to the Bree Vaults. We charge nothing to store many of your goods, and for a small but increasing fee, we will store even more.
'We have protection from the town guard at all hours of the day, so you can be certain that your valuables are safe here.
'Feel free to look around out front before heading across the way to Whitethorn's Taxidermy.'

'Welcome to the Bree Vaults. We charge nothing to store many of your goods and for a small but increasing fee, we will store even more.
'We have protection from the town guard at all hours of the day, so you can be certain that your valuables are safe here.
'Feel free to look around out front before heading across the way to Whitethorn's Taxidermy.'

'Hullo friend, welcome to Whitethorn's Taxidermy. My son and I, along with Mr. Whitbread, can fashion wondrous trophies from the more unique finds you come across in your adventures. You can display these wonders within your homes if you choose.
'Have a look if you like, and when you are ready, take the road outside my home to the south-east beyond the Iron Monger's Gate to the Stone Quarter. Turn east before the statue of the dwarf and follow the alley to the scholars. They are good fellows and quite knowledgeable about Bree. Speak with Newbold Leafcutter in the Scholar's Stair.'
Talk to Bonny Thatcher at the Three-farrow Crafting-hall
Talk to Second-watcher Heathstraw near the Boar Fountain
Talk to Barliman Butterbur at The Prancing Pony Inn
Talk to Lily Sandheaver at her home
Talk to Harry Goatleaf at the West-gate
Talk to Watchman Cardoon in Bree
Talk to Tad Gardener at the vault
Talk to Maud Foxglove at the vault
Talk to Clar Whitethorn at Whitethorn's Taxidermy
Talk to Lalia inside of Lalia's Market

'Welcome! Welcome to my little store. I was told to expect new faces walking through as I've had the honour of being added to our town's tour!
'The citizens of Bree have been exceptionally welcoming of my little venture here, and I've been busier than ever stitching and sewing and managing the items on display.
'The outfits near the front of the market rotate monthly, and all other designs come and go when the time is right. Please feel free to visit us and browse our wares at any time!
'Now, when you're done here, it would do you well to meet Barliman Butterbur. He's another successful proprietor as he owns the busiest inn in all of Bree. You will find him north along the road beyond the Market Gate within The Prancing Pony Inn.'
'Lalia's Market is located on the northern side of the Market Square, right next to the Boar Fountain. Lalia herself can be found inside.'
A Tour of Bree
Bree's mayor, Graeme Tenderlarch, thought you might like to get acquainted with the town proper. He has sent you out into the square to begin a journey through the streets to tour the town.
'The Three-farrow Crafting-hall is east and north of the Bree Town Hall. Seek Bonny Hatcher there, she will explain to you about the crafting hall of Bree.'
'Seek out Second-watcher Heathstraw just up the road near the Boar Fountain. I am certain that he will have some interesting information about Bree-town.'
'Barliman Butterbur is one of Bree's most noteworthy residents and you will find that his establishment is both well-run and oft busy. Seek him to the north at the Prancing Pony.'
'Miss Sandheaver's home is just down the hill to the west. She lives in the first home on the road that stretches north.'
'Harry Goatleaf is just down the road west toward the gate. He's a rather ornery man if you ask me, but he surely has something to share.'
'I told you, I have nothing to say to you. You want to know something more of this town, talk to the watcher back towards the east. Cardoon is his name.'
'You will find the vaults to the south of here, just beyond the guards in the old stone buildings there.'
'You will find the taxidermist across the way.'
'You will find the taxidermist across the road.'
Talk to Newbold Leafcutter
Talk to Mat Heathertoes in Beggar's Alley
Talk to Lily Appledore at the Bree Jail
Talk to an auctioneer
Talk to Tad Leafcutter at the hunting-lodge
Talk to Mayor Graeme Tenderlarch at the Bree Town Hall

'Much of the history of Bree and Bree-land is stored within these walls and within other safe places throughout the city. We are being more diligent than ever to keep safe the history of our land.
'Foul Men are lurking about all over town, and there is tell of shadows that leap out at folks in recent days.
'You should speak with Mat Heathertoes. He and folk like him, those without much, are hardest hit by these ruffians. Turn left outside our door and head south-west beyond the dwarf-statue under the eaves to find him.'

'Greetings, stranger. Not sure why Tenderlarch is having you visit us here in Beggar's Alley... all we have to offer is in the ruins to the north. Still, he paid me some coin to see that you met me and heard what I have to say about our little part of Bree.
'Most folks pay us no nevermind and don't hear us asking about the sounds from the alleys at night: ghosts prowling about down by the South-gate and the terror that grips the lot of us.
'Most of the brigands have moved in here, pushing the few good folk who live here out. I wish Grimbriar had not run off. Heathstraw is a good fellow, but not as clever as the Chief Watcher.
'I am to send you to the Bree Jail for your next stop. Don't worry though... it's unlikely that they will arrest you. From here head east along the road until you pass the Bree Town Hall, then bear slightly south. You will see the stocks in front of the Jail. Speak with Lily Appledore inside.'

'Welcome to Bree. Take a good look around you... these are the cells where those who mean ill to the people of Bree find themselves, ${PLAYER}. It is also where we train future recruits for the Town Watch and guard.
'The difference between the two is subtle, but the Watch has more power to also roam the countryside to protect the many farms of Bree. Recent weeks and months has seen an increase in brigand activity, and the Watch is terribly strained. Any help you can give would be appreciated.
'On to your next visit, ${PLAYER}. From the jail, head east under the Woodsmen's Gate, then turn south. Look for the bronze boar standing outside the Bree Auction Hall and enter. Speak with one of the auctioneers within.'

'This is the Bree Auction Hall. Here you can trade materials with other craftsmen and adventurers at a small cost, which helps support Bree-town.
'You can search through our ledgers to see the items that people are currently offering. If you choose to list an item with us, we will hold it for an agreed upon amount of time and should the item sell, we will take a portion of those proceeds to pay for our services... the rest will be sent to you through the Post. If the items fail to find a trade, we will return the item to you and keep your deposits. The ins and outs of the auctions can be difficult to understand. The mayor will furnish you with a note explaining this when you are done with your tour.
'You should visit Tad Leafcutter next. You will find him at the end of the lane to the west.'

'This is the Bree Auction Hall. Here you can trade materials with other craftsmen and adventurers at a small cost, which helps support Bree-town.
'You can search through our ledgers to see the items that people are currently offering. If you choose to list an item with us, we will hold it for an agreed upon amount of time and should the item sell, we will take a portion of those proceeds to pay for our services... the rest will be sent to you through the Post. If the items fail to find a trade, we will return the item to you and keep your deposits. The ins and outs of the auctions can be difficult to understand. The mayor will furnish you with a note explaining this when you are done with your tour.
'You should visit Tad Leafcutter next. You will find him at the end of the lane to the west.'

'As a representative of the Men of Bree, I welcome you to our township. Beyond the doors behind me, you will find the Bree hunting-lodge. When you have earned enough respect among the Men of Bree, you can find your way within the halls to purchase items from the hunters.
'You should make your way back to Graeme Tenderlarch at Town Hall. Head east along this road until you reach the East-gate, from there turn north-west and follow the road to Town Hall.'

'Well then, you have been to every corner of Bree and should be able to find your way around more easily now.
'With all the claims of ghosts near the South-gate, brigands running folks out of Beggar's Alley, and the flow of refugees from the South, Bree is bustling... and not in all ways good. The Southerners are a bit of trouble that has me most concerned. More so than ghost-stories from the South-gate; those stories have been about for years.
'I hope that you have arrived here as a boon of hope, ${PLAYER}. Again, I welcome you to our fair town.'

'Now then, Bree is a fairly large town, and there are many places to visit and people to meet. I would like to help you with this and have asked many of the townsfolk to bid you good welcome when you speak with them. This town needs as many allies as it can find in these dark times.
'Your first stop will be to the north, just beyond the Trader's Gate to the Three-farrow Crafting-hall. Enter the building and speak with Bonny Thatcher.'

The Three-farrow Crafting-hall lies to the north of the Bree Town Hall, through the Trader's Gate.
Graeme Tenderlarch has bid you to enter the Three-farrow Crafting-hall and speak with Bonny Thatcher.

The Boar Fountain lies a little to the north of the Three-farrow Crafting-hall.
Bonny Thatcher told you to speak with Second-watcher Heathstraw at the Boar Fountain in the Market Square.

The Prancing Pony Inn is north of the Market Square.
Lalia has instructed you to speak with Barliman Butterbur, proprietor of The Prancing Pony Inn.

Lily Sandheaver's home is west of The Prancing Pony Inn.
Barliman Butterbur told you to speak with Lily Sandheaver at her home.

Harry Goatleaf can be found at the West-gate, west of Lily Sandheaver's home.
Lily Sandheaver told you to speak with Harry Goatleaf.

Watchman Cardoon is east of the West-gate of Bree.
Harry Goatleaf told you to speak with Watchman Cardoon.

The vault is found to the south of Watcher Cardoon. He told you to follow the road and look for the large, stone building protected by two guards.
Watcher Cardoon instructed you to speak with Tad Gardener or Maud Foxglove at the vault.

You will find Whitethorn's Taxidermy across the road from the Bree-town Vault.
You were told to speak with Clar Whitethorn at Whitethorn's Taxidermy.

Make your way south out of Whitethorn's Taxidery before you reach the statue of the dwarf turn left, to the east, and make your way to Scholar's Stair. Enter and speak with Newbold Leafcutter.
Clar Whitethorn directed you to speak with Newbold Leafcutter within the Scholar's Stair.

'${PLAYER}, yes? The Watch has been awaiting your arrival. News of what you have done travels quickly, and in this time of need, every ray of hope is necessary. Our mayor, Graeme Tenderlarch, wishes to speak with you. You will find him within the Town Hall.
'Travel along the road to the south and look for the large stone plaza. The entrance to the Town Hall can be found there. Enter and speak with our mayor.'

'${PLAYER}, yes? The Watch has been awaiting your arrival. News of what you have done travels quickly, and in this time of need, every ray of hope is necessary. Our mayor, Graeme Tenderlarch, wishes to speak with you. You will find him within the Town Hall.
'Travel along the road to the south-east and look for the large stone plaza. The entrance to the Town Hall can be found there. Enter and speak with our mayor.'

'Hello! Welcome to Bree-town. You are most welcome here, ${PLAYER}. Allow me a moment of your time, and I will do my best to see that you learn of all that Bree has to offer.
'Bree is a large town, the largest in the north, and certainly the most populous as well. I know that we do not seem like much, but in truth all roads lead to Bree, and it is for that very reason that I have asked to meet you.
'Bree has suddenly become rife with folk of a most unsavoury sort, and each day, it appears that more arrive. My Chief Watcher, Grimbriar, took it upon himself to investigate a number of claims coming from the farms around Bree-land, or I would have you speak directly to him about these matters.'
Talk to Graeme Tenderlarch at the Bree Town Hall
Meeting the Mayor

Your arrival in Bree comes at an auspicious time. Brigands scour the countryside, and travellers from the South bring an air of fear to the populace. Your exploits, having reached the ears of Bree-town's mayor, make a meeting with the mayor possible.
'The mayor is at the Town Hall. Visit him there.'
'The mayor is at the Town Hall. Visit him there.'

The Bree Town Hall is found at the court near the Mustering Hall, south of Second-watcher Heathstraw's post.
Second-watcher Heathstraw has asked you to make your way to the Bree Town Hall and speak with Graeme Tenderlarch, the mayor.
Welcome to Bree-town

'As I mentioned before, brigands have become a true threat to the safety of Bree-land. My Chief Watcher has moved to the outskirts of town, just outside the West-gate and north along the Greenway, to a small stone cottage in an attempt to thwart the brigands' plans.
'Would you be willing to visit him and see if he has made any progress against the threat that these Southerners pose to our city? It seems to me that every day more and more of these brigands find their way into Bree, and while some are simple refugees, I fear a growing number mean this town ill.
'Talk to Chief Watcher Grimbriar as soon as you may.'

'Tenderlarch sent you? Good, I could use another hand out here.
'If Tenderlarch had his way, we'd have asked those blasted Rangers for help. Fortunately, I convinced him that my Watchers can handle whatever this upstart threat is.
'With your help, we'll have these brigands driven back into the South Downs in no time.'
Talk to Chief Watcher Grimbriar outside Bree-town
The Trouble with the Southerners
Now that you are acquainted with Bree-town, Graeme Tenderlarch has decided to ask you for some real help on the outskirts of town.
'Speak with my Chief Watcher north along the Greenway at a stone cottage outside of the West Gate of Bree.'

Chief Watcher Grimbriar is at a stone cottage along the roadway, out the West-gate of Bree and north along the Greenway.
Graeme Tenderlarch, the mayor of Bree, asked you to speak with Chief Watcher Grimbriar regarding the brigands threatening the safety of Bree-land.
Examined Silvan records (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'${PLAYER}, when you next wander the ruins about Ost Galadh, please keep an eye for any old plaques or engravings that might remain? There must be some left, and my hope is to record their lore as we knew it in the days before we left this place to the wilds.
'This may mark my last chance to do so before we withdraw back to Lothlórien -- and likely before I myself head into the far West -- but my duties compel me to remain within this encampment, and I dare not venture forth against Fuirgam's command!
'I beseech you...would you venture forth into the ruins and make record of any engravings you find within? They would be of great interest to me and my fellow scholars, and who knows when or if we might ever look upon them again?'

'Ah, so I was right, there were some remaining records of the old settlement. I have no time to pore over these now, or Fuirgam will be cross with me, but I thank you for your efforts.
'Fuirgam himself once lived here in Ost Galadh, before it was left to the forest. Alas, the memories of those who left this place seem dark and difficult, and I have yet to find one who will speak at any length of it, and so these words of stone provide my only window to the past of this place.
'One day I will catch Fuirgam in a more talkative mood and obtain the whole story, but he is oft reticent, and it might be another Age before I pull it out of him. That is assuming of course that any of us do not find ourselves in Valinor prematurely....'
Examine Silvan records (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Agorin at Ost Galadh
Ancient Records
Agorin, the record-keeper of the Malledhrim, has asked you to foray into the Wild Ruins and collect notes on the ancient Sylvan records scattered among the ruins there.

'Would that I could have shown you this place when it was still called Greenwood the Great by Men and dwarves! It was as wonderous and beautiful as any city my brethren among the Silvan Elves had built, a fair reflection for grand Lórien in those days.
'Now it is....
'I would be alone now, please.'

The Wild Ruins lie to the south of Ost Galadh.
Agorin has asked you to examine and record the records of the Silvan Elves of Ost Galadh in the Wild Ruins.

Agorin is at Ost Galadh, north of the Wild Ruins.
You should return to Agorin at and tell her what you discovered about the records of the Silvan Elves that once inhabited this place.
Destroyed corrupted relics (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'There is no other way, ${PLAYER}: while it pains me more than anything to order it so, any Elven relics remaining within Minas Gîl must be destroyed...and quickly! Their purpose has been corrupted beyond recovery, and the powers they now shape at the hands of the Enemy are too dangerous to be left unchecked.
'Return to Minas Gîl and destroy these artifacts wherever you find them within, so that they are of no further use to our enemies.
'In the meantime, I shall attempt to divine who or what has brought about this evil deed, so that we may have our vengeance upon them for this grievous loss.'

'All the relics are destroyed then. I...very well. You have done as I asked, though I had long dreamed to return to the West holding such treasures of my youth aloft. I must harbour no such hopes in this dark place.
'I shall focus instead on the task at hand, and nothing more. All that matters now is the defeat of the sorcerer responsible for this evil!'
Destroy corrupted relics (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Agorin at Ost Galadh
Corrupted Memories
Agorin revealed that the relics of Minas Gîl have been irreversibly corrupted by the sorcerers of Dol Guldur.

'Please...I would rather not speak of the task I have set before you.
'It was hard enough to ask it of you once; I could not do it again....'

The corrupted relics lie within Minas Gîl, east of Ost Galadh.
Agorin has asked you to destroy the corrupted Silvan relics within Minas Gîl.

Agorin is at Ost Galadh, west of Minas Gîl.
You should report your success to Agorin.
Defeated Sharpfang

'Sorry news, I am afraid. One of my kin was slain in the forests just west of here, by wolves no less. Though we have encountered many Wargs trained as curs of the Enemy since we entered Mirkwood, we had thought the common wolves would stay at bay from our forces. It seems we were wrong, and there are those among them that would stalk our scouts should they travel alone.
'Those of us who have learned the guttural speech of their kind have made out the name 'Sharpfang' among their wild howls -- it seems this leader claimed the kill, and I would see the beast put down as a lesson to the others that they dare not obstruct the Malledhrim.
'They have been seen to gather some evenings by a stone circle to the west of the Wild Ruins called Hrigg Vidukuni by the Woodmen who dwell in Mirkwood. You may be able to find their leader there and deal with him.'

'Excellent. With the crebain kept at bay and the wolves leaderless, I think we have dealt with the feral threats of Emyn Lûm for the time being.
'Long enough to do what we must, for we shall not tarry long beneath these dark boughs.'
Defeat Sharpfang
Talk to Fuirgam at Ost Galadh
Fangs Bared
One of Fuirgam's trackers has been ambushed and slain by wolves in the forests of Emyn Lûm.

'I fear that Ivorel will have naught but unkind words for me when we return to Lothlórien.
'I have pushed her and her scouts to the point of recklessness -- and spent several of their lives in so doing -- but we have no time for delicacy, and we need their eyes on every road and ravine.
'If you should encounter her in the Scuttledells, please aid her in any way you may. I would very much like to see her return home unharmed.'

Sharpfang may be found at Hrigg Vidukuni, west of the Wild Ruins, south-west of Ost Galadh.
Fuirgam has asked you to travel to Hrigg Vidukuni and search the area for the Emyn Lûm pack-leader, Sharpfang, and defeat him.

Fuirgam at Ost Galadh is at Ost Galadh, north of the Wild Ruins, north-east of Hrigg Vidukuni.
You should return to Fuirgam with news of your success.
Defeated crebain within the Wild Ruins (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'While there do not appear to be Orcs in the ruins surrounding us, the presence of so many crebain disturbs me.
'The Enemy has been known in the past to use them as spies, and while my sentinels will shoot any from the sky that dare come too close, it will be difficult to hide any of our movements from them.
'Perhaps you might enjoy a relaxing hunt? I need their numbers thinned considerably to teach them to fear for their lives should they continue to haunt those ruins.'

'Good work, ${PLAYER}. There is no way we will dispatch all of them, but if enough fall to our arrows then the rest will be forced to keep their distance, and their value as spies to the Enemy will be greatly reduced.'

'So, ${PLAYER}, the tower of Minas Gîl now lays open to us -- I should tell you something of its nature before you enter therein.
'Minas Gîl was once an observatory built by the Elves of Ost Galadh, my kin of old. We used it to study the stars in their myriad dance across the sky. We gathered much knowledge of the heavens there long ago, and some relics may remain from among the mechanisms and arts that we employed in those studies.
'Once you gain access to the tower's interior, see if you can gather any such relics. It is likely that the Enemy has turned them to their own uses or destroyed them altogether, but if you can recover any, I would be very interested to see them.'

'What is this!? These devices...they have been touched by sorcery most foul, turned from their simple purposes to ends most evil....
'The firmament of stars above us, which we Elves have always revered most among all creation -- for they were made by Elbereth -- light a great Void of which we know little. But it seems that our Enemy knows something of its true nature, for our instruments which once turned to the study of the stars of Elbereth now look deep into that endless Void and draw upon it to sustain the shadows which they now bring into our world!
'There is nothing I can do to unravel the corruption of our relics, ${PLAYER}, had I the time to even attempt it. They must be destroyed and quickly if we are to prevent more of these unnatural spirits from being drawn into the light of our world!'
Find Silvan relics (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

Agorin believes that relics of the Silvan Elves might remain within Minas Gîl, from the time when it served as an observatory studying the heavens above Ost Galadh.

'Agorin tells me that you are helping her untangle the mysteries of Minas Gîl, ${PLAYER}. That is well, but take care, do not let yourselves be drawn into the mists of what once was. We have a mission here that must not fail if Lothlórien...no, if all of Middle-earth is to survive.
'If there be some evil in Minas Gîl then deal with it and be done, but do not let Agorin become distracted by it. We need her aid against the greater evil of Dol Guldur.'

'Would that my duties would allow me to visit my beloved Minas Gîl again. Just to see it there through the mists, standing almost within reach is almost more than I can bear.
'But while my heart beckons me to it, I know that it cannot be the tower I remember, for surely the Enemy has twisted it beyond recognition.
'I know my place is here alongside Fuirgam and the others, for the sake of our future rather than our past...and yet....'

'Something stirs atop the tower of Minas Gîl, ${PLAYER}, I can feel it from here. Powerful sorcery is being wrought and will soon come to its culmination -- we must put an end to it before it is completed!
'The power I feel gathering is too great for you to face alone, and it is likely wielded by the sorcerer responsible for the desecration of Minas Gîl, against whom I would seek swift vengeance!
'You should prepare for an assault upon the tower's summit -- little time remains!'

'So, it was Gúlbenn who wielded the sorceries atop Minas Gîl? I have heard his name before -- he was said to be a powerful sorcerer, descended from the bloodlines of the Black Númenóreans. It is good that his evil has come to a final end, and the spirit he sought to summon has been cast back into the Void.
'Minas Gîl shall never serve the Elves again, but now perhaps it may be left to fall into timeless ruin among the silence of the forest.'

'${PLAYER}, a serious matter has come to my attention. Our scouts have examined the tower of Minas Gîl -- you can just make it out on the slopes to our east through the mist -- and they have returned to me with tales of deadly spirits of shadow surrounding it, and a shadowy ward upon the door that prevented them from gaining access to the tower's interior.
'I do not yet know what transpires within that tower, but it reeks of the Enemy's sorcery, and we dare not ignore such a threat so close to the path of our advance. Fuirgam has tasked me with ensuring that the threat is dealt with, and so I turn to you for aid.
'To begin with, can you do battle with the spirits surrounding the tower and bring me some aspect of their being? They are almost certainly bound up with the ward upon the tower itself, and if I can divine its nature, then we may be able to break it.'

'Such odd gems! They seem almost unreal and weightless, as if they were formed of smoke or mist made solid....
'This is enough, though. The nature of these gems tell me that the ward upon the door is no physical thing at all or even true magic -- it is a glamour woven of shadows, no more.
'Now that you know its nature, you will find that it has no power over you, and it will unravel at your approach, as do so many of the Enemy's lies once they are laid bare to the light.'

'Welcome to Ost Galadh, ${PLAYER}. Once long ago it was an outpost of our kind, when this forest was still called Greenwood the Great -- but that time is long past, and the power of Dol Guldur is great here now.
'While our forces have taken and secured this courtyard as a base to strike at Dol Guldur, we have neither the time nor forces to explore and secure the surrounding tangle of ruins and forest. In this, I am hoping that you can aid us.
'If you can take the time to quickly scout the more extensive ruins immediately to our south and report back on what you find there, it would be most helpful. What we can see from here suggests that it is mostly inhabited by wild beasts -- but even they must be assumed to be servants of the Enemy in a place like this, so foray with care.'

'So, the ruins are overrun with cruel and evil beasts, but little sign of goblins or Orcs? Good.
'These solitary footprints you mention, though...those are of considerable interest to me. When Lord Celeborn dispatched me across the Anduin, he bade me keep watch for a strange creature he named 'Gollum'. More than once he was nearly captured on the outskirts of Lothlórien, but he slipped away each time. Celeborn suspected he may have crossed the river to avoid capture, and it appears he was right.
'My sentinels claimed to have spotted a strange creature in the wild a few days ago -- they thought it a goblin, but were unable to capture it before it fled into the twisting ways of the Scuttledells. Your discovery tells me that our mysterious interloper was likely this Gollum creature. Would that we had laid hands upon him then!'

'Before you run off, I wanted to ask you for another favour. While that brigand was talking to me I saw some of his seconds bullying one of my workers, while two others made off with a lot of my produce.
'That produce feeds my workers and keeps them strong. I need to get that back if they are to remain hale and hearty.
'I am certain you will find that the produce has been distributed to any of these foul brigands in the southern Bree-fields, but there are plenty near the ruins where you are going. Would you recover the produce for me?'

'You did it! Look at these onions still green and fresh. My workers as well are indebted to you now. I haven't much more to give, but you have earned at least this much.
'Thank you, ${PLAYER}.'

'I am worried that my workers will grow ill without proper meals, and the only way to have proper meals is by eating one's vegetables!
Please hurry and get my produce back before it spoils, or worse... is eaten by those foul brigands!'

'I do not know what to do. The brigands told me to pay them three equal payments and that they would spare my workers and myself. I held my part of the bargain. Now they want more. I haven't anything left after sending workers to Buckland for supplies and the meagre rewards I can offer folk for helping out here and there.
'I cannot allow my workers to suffer for my mistakes. I fear I may need to stop work on the inn, but Chief-watcher Grimbriar is working against the brigands here... so I must ask. Would you be willing to help me send a message to these brigands?
'I hear that you have already done some work against the brigands before... I am sorry if I am mistaken. But, these are evil Men, and they must be stopped. If you are willing to help, could you return to the Old Sweetgrass Farm and send a message to these brigands? The Old Sweetgrass Farm is a short distance north-east of here.'

'It's done then, and too late to change now. Oh me....

'Nails are running low... yes, the brigands even took our nails! Can you imagine? Thieves of a different sort than I have ever seen. We needn't fret over the nails, though, and with the cost of iron where it is, I have reasoned a better solution to the problem with building Adso's Inn. The only problem is that the solution lay to the south within the Old Forest.
'In the shadow of the giant trees, there you will find roots. Massive tendrils poking from the earth with the strength of the ages. If we can get tough vines from those roots, we can craft strappings to tie our crossbeams together and save the remaining nails for everything else that we need to build.
'What say you? Do you have the heart to face that dark and gloomy place to collect up some strapping from those roots?'

'Good work! These will do exactly as I expected. We can use these to lash together the beams we need for as long as this place will stand.
'Thank you for your work.'
'Strengthen your heart and face your fears. There is coin to be made if you return with the treasure I seek from the Old Forest.'

'Lord Celeborn is making preparations for a great incursion into Mirkwood, not for conquest, but to forestall the attack from Dol Guldur that must surely come. We are gathering supplies and making all things ready for the passage of the Malledhrim, the Golden Host, and the Lord and Lady are carefully selecting those who will lead it.
'One of those I think likely to travel with the Golden Host is named Issuriel; she is a student of history and of the mysteries of the natural world and spoke often with Mithrandir on the rare occasion his business brought him to the Golden Wood. She seeks to know the true nature of things and loves the unravelling of puzzles and secrets above all else.
'Issuriel has been asking for you, ${PLAYER}. She wished to hear the tale of Mazog's capture in the depths of Moria from your lips and had questions to ask of you. Look for her on the high flet atop Cerin Amroth.'

'It is a pleasure to meet you at last, ${PLAYER}, and I hope you will assist the Golden Host when the time comes to push forward into Mirkwood. Lord Celeborn has asked me to be involved in planning for the offensive, so in order to fully understand the mind of the captive Mazog, I listened to Corunothiel's account of his capture.
'With interest, I learned of your infiltration through the secret way into the throne-room of Mazog, but Corunothiel ceased her tale at the point where the Orc-leader was captured. I pressed her for more information, but she said the memory was grim, and she did not desire to relive it so soon.
'Tell me what happened following the capture of Mazog, ${PLAYER}. How were you able to escape from the very heart of Mazog's throne room...and with the king of the Orcs still in tow?'

'The tale of your escape from Rushdurinul with Mazog still a captive was more harrowing than I expected, ${PLAYER}, and I thank you for recounting it to me! If we are to work with the dwarves to bring Mazog to Dol Guldur, as Bróin intends, we must learn from the lesson of your tale: the Orc-king is not to be underestimated!
'I trust that Bróin's people are crafting new shackles for Mazog, to begin with the most obvious lesson of your escape.
'But there is more, friend ${RACE}! The words of Mazog make me wonder. Look first to your own doorstep before taking the fight to that of your enemy, it is said by the Wise!'

'Issuriel wishes to speak with you concerning the capture of Mazog, ${PLAYER}. Look for her on the high flet atop Cerin Amroth.'

Issuriel of Lothlórien can be found on the high flet atop Cerin Amroth.
Haldir has told you of the preparations being made for the departure of the Golden Host into Mirkwood and desired that you speak with Issuriel, an Elf being considered to lead the Malledhrim. She had questions to ask of you concerning the capture of Mazog.

Issuriel is on the high flet atop Cerin Amroth, in Lothlórien.
Issuriel wishes to hear the account of your escape from Rushdurinul with the captive Mazog, as the other Elves present were reluctant to tell her the rest of the story.

Issuriel is on the high flet atop Cerin Amroth, in Lothlórien.
You have recounted the rest of the tale concerning your escape from Rushdurinul with Mazog, and Issuriel has heard something to cause her concern.
You have forced Mazog to submit
Bróin has been defeated!
You have come to the entrance to Zurr-thurkh and should now ensure that Mazog's words are merely empty bluster before leaving.
Despite his attempt to escape, you have forced Mazog to submit. You should speak now with Bróin.

'It is too soon to celebrate over-much, ${PLAYER}, I know; but to have come even this far is something extraordinary!
'And yet, I wonder: Mazog is of great value to the forces of the Enemy. Can it be that they will consider a trade? If we were to bring Mazog before the gates of Dol Guldur, would Gorothúl accept Mazog's life in trade for that of my cousin Bori?
'I have sworn a vow that my axe shall end Mazog's life, but if greater good could be accomplished by his survival, well...it becomes a more difficult question, ${PLAYER}. We cannot abandon Bori now!'

'That was close, ${PLAYER}, but we have managed to bring Mazog once more under control. I should have known he would have some fight left!
'One thing is certain, friend ${RACE}: we will need to make some stronger shackles to hold our prisoner in the future!'
'Take these shackles, ${PLAYER}, and use them to bind Mazog's wrists. They are made of iron and should be strong enough to keep him secure as we fight our way from this place.'

'Now we need to make our way from Rushdurinul, ${PLAYER}, but I fear we have taken too long already: this place will soon be swarming with Orcs. If we hope to escape from here with our lives and that of our captive, we need someone to manage the flow of battle.
'I suggest that you accept that role. You will need to tell us what our support role should be as the battle ebbs and flows. Should we focus on improving your morale, your power, the strength of your attacks, or the fortitude of your defence?'

'You think these bracelets can bind Mazog in his own domain? You are a fool if you think I cannot sunder these with even the smallest effort!
'But I will wait until you are most vulnerable, ${RACE}, and then you will feel my hands around your neck!'
'Quickly now, before more Orcs attack, let us take Mazog with us and leave this place behind!'

'Rule here? You think I want to rule here? I have no desire to rule this miserable kingdom! You have no idea what is happening, do you?
'Gorothúl's master is generous to his friends. He looks out for them. He tells them things. Mine will be the greatest of his armies!
'\qWhat reward do you desire?\q Gorothúl asked of me. \qOnly the kingdom that should be mine,\q I told him. \qThat place will not do,\q he said. \qMy master has commanded me to draw forth the great terrors of the abyss. That kingdom will never be free of them,\q he said, and only fools would disbelieve his words!'

Listen to the discussion of Mazog's fate

'We have ended Gwathnor's growing strength and dispersed the forms of Grawulun that were drawn to Azanarukâr, ${PLAYER}. We have won a short victory, a small respite -- without the beacon of Gorothúl, it will be some time before Gwathnor and his servants can again find the world above.
'But it will not last forever. We do not possess the means of destroying these creatures, lesser spirits though they be -- they are beyond our ability. We can hinder them for a time, and hope the peace we buy is worth the dangers.
'I feel it is.'
'Are you ready to leave? There is nothing to hold us here; we should return to the upper levels, where the air is clean.'

'Here we are, ${PLAYER}, where once we came before: the deepest reaches of Azanarukâr. I have come here often since we first met, though better equipped than on that adventure. The Lady of the Wood has given me a great Elf-stone and many things have fled before its light.
'We should be cautious, as there were Regmyl here before, and I saw them carrying an artifact of great evil. I do not see them now, but they are surely not far.
'Let us proceed, friends, and see what lies before us in Azanarukâr.'
Talk to Magor
Destroy Gorothúl's beacon
Defeat Gwathnor
<rgb=#FF0000> Do not allow Gwathnor or his allies to approach the exit </rgb>

Instance: Return to Azanarukâr
You have come to Azanarukâr with Magor in search of an artifact left by Gorothúl in the depths.
In the depths of Azanarukâr, Magor wishes to fight alongside you in search of the artifact he believes Gorothúl left there.
You have found the relic within Azanarukâr, and should destroy it to prevent further of Gorothúl's schemes from hatching.

Gwathnor has awakened, and he must be defeated in order to prevent the growth of his power.
<rgb=#FF0000>Do not allow Gwathnor or any of his minions to approach the door.</rgb>
Magor is waiting to speak with you in the depths of Azanarukâr after your defeat of Gwathnor and the forms of Grawulun.

'Much of Mazog's ramblings in the depths of Rushdurinul could have been empty bluster, the boasting and threats of a caged animal. But one thing he said troubles me more than any other: the revelation that the reward he seeks is the rule of another kingdom. Long have the Orcs and the dwarves battled in the caverns beneath the Misty Mountains, and the lineage of Mazog has been at the forefront of that conflict.
'If Mazog, descendent of Azog's line through his son Bolg, has decided to abandon rule of Moria, it can only be because he feels Moria will no longer be fit to rule. What great evil must his ally Gorothúl have set into motion in the depths that could so devastate that vast kingdom and make it unfit even for the rule of Orcs?
'Return to Gwathrendath in the Foundations of Stone and speak with Lenglammel and Forglinn there. They have spent a great deal of time in the depths and may know something about what we might be facing.'

'It is good to see you again, ${PLAYER}, for I share the concerns of Issuriel: there is more to Gorothúl's interest in Moria than we have so far uncovered.
'Great terrors dwell in the deep places, this we know, for you have faced several of them: nameless beasts that fear the light of the sun, but also the servants of the great spirit that reigned in Moria and ended the dwarf-kingdom. The Balrog of Moria now is defeated, but at the cost of Mithrandir's life and the vast extent of his power.
'But the servants of the Shadow and the Flame were defeated not by the power of Mithrandir, but by your courage and that of your allies. Take no offence at this, ${PLAYER}, but your abilities do not begin to approach that of the Wizard. I fear that your defeat of the servants of Durin's Bane may not have the permanence afforded that of their master's defeat.'

'Your words confirm what I have been hearing from Lenglammel and Magor, ${PLAYER}: Gorothúl set something in motion before he left for Dol Guldur with the captive dwarves and the mithril axe of the Iron Garrison.
'Did he work some evil to allow the servants of Shadow and Flame to recover their strength and return to places once thought free of their danger?'

'I had hoped to see you again on the shores of Anduin, ${PLAYER}, well on our way to exchanging the Orc-king for my cousin Bori's freedom, but it was not yet to be. The Elves of Gwathrendath are right: Gorothúl seems to have set some plan into motion here in Khazad-dûm.
'After you returned to Lothlórien to speak with Celeborn, Orvar went back into the depths of Buzun-ghâr. He said he had a \qfeeling,\q some idea that things were not quite right. The wilting rot was already beginning to retreat, but he felt still some vile presence, and below the ledge where you handily defeated Grawulun the Caerog, Orvar discovered a dreadful ward covered in unspeakable runes. He sensed it calling, calling into the depths, and smote it with his axe until it was destroyed.
'I believe Gorothúl left this relic in Buzun-ghâr in order to draw Grawulun the Caerog to it, ${PLAYER}. Grawulun did not find that place accidentally, friend ${CLASS}. He was drawn there.'
Talk to Lenglammel at Gwathrendath
Talk to Forglinn at Gwathrendath
Talk to Bróin in the Peaceful Path
Chapter 2: What Gorothúl Left Behind
Issuriel worries that the words of Mazog may reveal a hidden threat to the Elves of Lothlórien and the Dwarves of Moria.

'The Elf-outpost in the depths of the Foundations of Stone in Moria may hold some answers concerning the danger I fear Gorothúl has raised. Speak with Lenglammel and Forglinn there and hear what they have learned.'

'You go to speak with Bróin about this new danger? I am glad; he must deal with the possibility that all is not well within Moria before setting forth to rescue his cousin Bori.
'Bróin is in the Peaceful Path, located along Durin's Way.'

'Bróin remains still in the Peaceful Path, the place of rest established by the Iron Garrison off Durin's Way. You should speak to him about this new danger we suspect is growing, for it will affect his planned rescue of Bori.'

Lenglammel and Forglinn can be found in Gwathrendath, the Elf-outpost in the depths of the Foundations of Stone, in Moria.
Issuriel believes that Gorothúl may have set into motion some evil that might ravage Moria in such a way that even Mazog is seeking another kingdom to rule.

Bróin is in the Peaceful Path, located off Durin's Way.
The Elves in Gwathrendath agree with Issuriel's assessment that Gorothúl set some evil into motion before leaving for Dol Guldur. Bróin should be notified of this, for it concerns the Iron Garrison and may affect his plans for the rescue of Bori.
A wave of dread passes through you as the relic is destroyed, then is gone.

'Now that Orvar has destroyed the hidden relic Gorothúl left in Buzun-ghâr, that cave should be free of danger. We need not fear that Grawulun or others of his kind will return to that place.
'But Gorothúl may have left other relics of evil throughout Moria; indeed, I think it likely, and recent reports from our scouts indicate one such location: the Mirror-halls of Lumul-nar. Merrevail have corrupted the mirrors of Lumul-nar that once fed light from the outside into the deep reaches of Khazad-dûm; the light no longer shines. A number of explorers ventured to Lumul-nar to investigate. Few returned, reporting that the merrevail of that place have been given great courage; their defiance is strong. What else have they been given, I wonder? A relic of Gorothúl's?
'The entrance to Lumul-nar is on the side of Zirakzigil, amid the snow. Find the relic inside, if it exists, and destroy it. Bring one or two allies with you, ${PLAYER}! A small fellowship of the brave-hearted will be required to find the evil relic there.'

'I knew it, ${PLAYER}! I knew you would find Gorothúl's relic in Lumul-nar. It is good you destroyed it. The merrevail we should be able to keep in check; if the relic had drawn Grawulun or another Caerog to Lumul-nar, our success might not be as sure.'
Destroy the Gift of Gorothúl in Lumul-nar
Talk to Bróin in the Peaceful Path
Chapter 3: A Relic in Lumul-nar (Group)
Bróin believes that Gorothúl gave a relic of evil to the merrevail that infest the Mirrors of Lumul-nar.

'The entrance to the Mirror Halls of Lumul-nar is outside, on the side of Zirakzigil near the smoking crater. Bring a small fellowship of allies with you, for the merrevail at Lumul-nar are dangerous foes.'

The entrance to the Mirror-halls of Lumul-nar is outside, on Zirakzigil, near the ruined crater where the Balrog lies smouldering.
Bróin believes that one of the relics Gorothúl left behind in Moria was given to the merrevail infesting the Mirror-halls of Lumul-nar and wants you to destroy it.

Bróin is in the Peaceful Path, located between Zirakzigil and Durin's Way.
You have destroyed the relic Gorothúl gave to the merrevail in Lumul-nar and should return now to Bróin.
A wave of dread passes through you as the relic is destroyed, then is gone.

'My uncle Bósi sent word while you were out. He thinks he knows where another of Gorothúl's relics may be found, and the location is just as dangerous as Lumul-nar, if not more so: the Water-wheels of Nalâ-dûm.
'Travel to the Chamber of the Cross-roads with your allies and speak with my uncle to learn more about Nalâ-dûm.'

'Greetings again to you, ${PLAYER}! I did not have the opportunity to properly thank you for helping to broker this alliance between the Iron Garrison and the Elves of Lothlórien. So I thank you! In Mazog, we have a prisoner worthy of exchanging for those Gorothúl brought to Dol Guldur: my son chief among them. O Bori! Be strong and courageous during your torment!
'Scouts report seeing a relic of unquestionable evil among the Water-wheels of Nalâ-dûm, but were unable to route the flow of the canals in such a way as to reach it. You must determine the proper workings of the system if you are to find and destroy this relic of Gorothúl's.
'Bring several allies to the entrance of Nalâ-dûm in the Water-works. Delving into the flooded deeps will be dangerous, for the mechanisms are very old and have not been used for many years.'

'Very well-done, ${PLAYER}. The destruction of that relic should keep further evils from being drawn to the Water-wheels.
'Now we must look to the future.'
Talk to Bósi in the Chamber of the Cross-roads
Destroy the relic of Gorothúl in Nalâ-dûm
Talk to Bósi in the Chamber of the Cross-roads
Chapter 4: A Relic in Nalâ-dûm (Group)
Bósi believes another of Gorothúl's relics may be found at the bottom of Nalâ-dûm, where the great wheels of Khazad-dûm lie dormant.
'The entrance to Nalâ-dûm lies in the Water-works. Bring a small fellowship of allies with you in search of Gorothúl's relic.'

'My uncle Bósi thinks he knows where another of Gorothúl's relics may be found: among the Water-wheels of Nalâ-dûm.
'Go speak to him in the Chamber of the Cross-roads, off Durin's Way, and he will tell you more about Nalâ-dûm.'

Bósi is in the Chamber of the Cross-roads, located off Durin's Way.
Bróin has told you to speak with his uncle about the Water-wheels of Nalâ-dûm.

The entrance to Nalâ-dûm can be found in the Water-works of Moria.
Bósi reports that a relic of Gorothúl's lies among the Water-wheels of Nalâ-dûm and will require careful usage of the mechanisms to reach and destroy. He also recommends you bring an ally or two.

Bósi is in the Chamber of the Cross-roads, located off Durin's Way.
You have destroyed the relic left in Nalâ-dûm by Gorothúl and should report your success to Bósi.

'Bróin told me about your capture of Mazog in Rushdurinul, and it was clear to me that if Mazog is to be brought to Dol Guldur in exchange for my son's freedom, we would need more powerful shackles to hold him. You were able to subdue the Orc-king when he broke free once; we cannot risk the necessity again.
'Therefore I commanded the smiths at the Heart of Fire to craft new shackles for Mazog. We have little mithril as it is, but they should have been able to make very strong bands indeed by mixing small quantities of it with other metals.
'Speak to Stóthkell in the Heart of Fire and see if the shackles are ready.'

'I am sorry, ${PLAYER}. Bróin's concerns are real and understood, but bringing Mazog into Lothlórien is simply unacceptable. Even shackled, Mazog cannot be allowed within the Golden Wood.
'We spoke earlier about the marks Gorothúl left at certain locations in Moria, ${PLAYER}, and you have done well to eliminate some of them. Magor reported to me while you were gone that one at least remains....'

'Yes, ${PLAYER}, yes. We combined a small quantity of mithril with other metals to make these shackles. In fact, some of the weapons and armour you previously collected for my smiths were melted down and used in their making.
'These bands will secure Mazog for the journey into Mirkwood. He will not break free of these, or I would be ashamed to call myself Stóthkell of the Iron Garrison!
'Bring these to Bróin for his approval. He is resting in the Peaceful Path, preparing for the journey.'

'Ah, the shackles! Yes, these look very sturdy indeed. Mazog will not be able to break from these as he did in Rushdurinul, ${PLAYER}.
'We have run into a... disagreement... with the Elves of Lothlórien concerning the plan to bring Mazog to Dol Guldur in exchange for my cousin's freedom. Celeborn has refused to allow us to bring the Orc into the Golden Wood, though it is clearly the most direct route. He wants us instead to skirt the woods, a journey that would take much longer!
'Lenglammel in Gwathrendath awaits my response. Give it to her, grudgingly: we will take the long way with Mazog, though it displeases me tremendously! Tell her, too, that I trust the Elves will shoulder some of the burden of this inconvenience! The delay this will cause is intolerable, and we are asked to bear it! I will do so, for Bori's sake.'
'The shackles are not ready? This is taking much too long!'
Talk to Stóthkell in the Heart of Fire
Bring the mithril shackles to Bróin in the Peaceful Path
Talk to Lenglammel in Gwathrendath
Chapter 5: Shackles for Mazog
Bósi has sent you to retrieve the mithril shackles being crafted in the Heart of Fire to contain Mazog.
'You remember where the Heart of Fire is, ${PLAYER}, surely? It is off the Way of Smiths among the Silvertine Lodes. Speak to Stóthkell and ask him if the shackles for Mazog have yet been made.'
'I have given you the shackles, ${PLAYER}. I did not know there was time to be wasted; why have you not brought them to Bróin in the Peaceful Path?'

'Tell Lenglammel in Gwathrendath that I am not pleased with the requirement that we not bring Mazog into Lothlórien on the way to Mirkwood. Instead, we will take the long way around, losing precious days in the process, solely to please the ridiculous requirements of the Elves of Lothlórien. Tell her that and leave out none of my words!'

Stóthkell is in the Heart of Fire, off the Way of Smiths, among the Silvertine Lodes.
Bósi has asked you to journey to the Heart of Fire to see if the shackles for Mazog have been made.

Bróin is in the Peaceful Path, located off Durin's Way.
You have collected the shackles to be used to secure Mazog for the journey into Mirkwood and should bring them now to Bróin.

Lenglammel is in Gwathrendath, the camp of Elves in the depths of the Foundations of Stone.
Bróin has sent you to tell Lenglammel that the dwarves will not bring Mazog through Lothlórien on their way to Mirkwood, skirting the wood instead. He also wants you to express his displeasure with the requirement.

'Magor has been venturing into the depths ever since you rescued him, ${PLAYER}, saying only that he considers it his personal duty to prevent the nameless dangers in Azanarukâr from ever leaving there.
'On his most recent journey into the fires of those caverns, he beheld a number of Regmyl carrying what appeared to be an idol of some evil significance. He followed them for a time, but at one point they seemed to become aware of his presence, and he found it necessary to retreat.
'Gather your strength and speak to me, ${PLAYER}. I will bring you to Magor. Together, you must return to Azanarukâr, learn if the Regmyl's idol is a relic of Gorothúl's, and destroy it.'
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTE: Inspiration will assist you if you choose to undertake this challenge. This instance can only be completed by a solo or two player group.</rgb>

'We are readying to leave as quickly as we are able, ${PLAYER}, but the preparations of the Golden Host cannot be hurried overmuch, lest we doom its mission to failure. It will take some time for the dwarves to bring Mazog to the edge of Mirkwood, and that will allow all the necessary preparations to be made.
'I hope you are ready when that time comes, ${PLAYER}. Both the dwarves of the Iron Garrison and the Elves of Lothlórien will rely on your courage and ability. I hope too that this expedition is not a mistake. It has been a long time since the forest bore the name Greenwood the Great.
'I will see you again, ${PLAYER}, when the time has come.'

'You have sent Gwathnor and Grawulun formless into the depths, ${PLAYER}, and not a moment too soon! I cannot say if this is the last of the relics left by Gorothúl in Moria, but we have bought some time at least.
'As long as Gorothúl remains alive, so too does the danger that he may create more such beacons, once again drawing forth Gwathnor or Grawulun...and next time we may not find them before they achieve their full level of power.
'You must go now to Haldir on the flet just outside the Golden Wood. Tell him that the dwarves of the Iron Garrison have agreed to bring Mazog to Mirkwood on an indirect route that will not pass through Lothlórien, as requested. Tell him, too, that the expedition of the Golden Host must occur with as much haste as can be arranged. Too great a delay, and we may find ourselves hemmed between Dol Guldur on one side and Gwathnor and Grawulun reborn on the other!'
Talk to Lenglammel to travel to Azanarukâr
Talk to Lenglammel in Gwathrendath
Talk to Haldir at Talan Haldir

'Are you ready to go? Magor has travelled ahead and will meet you in Azanarukâr.'

The body is cold to the touch but the wounds appear fresh -- though the lack of blood surrounding the man's body is disturbing. In his hand, the man clutches a note.
His position and a trail of disturbed earth makes it appear that he travelled through the gloom of the Barrow-downs to reach this point. The note is chewed and crumpled and the only legible words are: 'between the Old Forest and the northern Barrow-downs. Send help.'

'You, you came here instead of seeking Barliman and the Watchers. Oh this is a fine mess.
'I'll not forgive Barliman soon for the tale he spun for my Lalia. If you have arrived to assist us, then I am pleased to see you. Just concerned that you mayn't be capable to lead us out of this terrible place.'
Speak with one of the survivors of the ill-fated expedition into the Barrow-downs
Speak with Bob at the refugee camp twixt the Old Forest and north Barrow-downs.
The Failed Delivery

You happened upon a poor adventurer on the outskirts of the northern Barrow-downs. Clutched within the corpse's hand you found a note to Barliman Butterbur. Apparently, his assistant Bob came to the Barrows to find his daughter and found his way to the west between the Barrow-downs and the unforgiving darkness of the Old Forest.
Find the camp of survivors between the Old Forest and the north Barrow-downs.
Destroyed Orc-banners (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Welcome to Taur Morvith, ${PLAYER}. We have few warriors to spare with the strength of our forces heading towards Gathbúrz and Dol Guldur...your aid is most appreciated.
'Can you make out those Orkish fortresses down below? They call them Krul Lugu in their Black Speech. Krul Lugu marks the southern flank of our advance, and I am tasked with ensuring that they are unable to mount a strike against us at Ost Galadh. The Orcs are cut off from the bulk of their forces in Dol Guldur, so their numbers are not great...but ours are spread even more thinly here, so we are trying to keep their attention occupied rather than risk a large-scale battle. To that end, we strive to demoralize and blind them, keeping them in place and paralyzed with uncertainty.
'I have a simple task for you: Destroy their war-banners. It is naught but a symbolic effort, but as they appear to be bereft of strong leadership, it should be sufficient to set them back before they can rebuild their courage.'

'Yes, I can see it from here even through the mist. You have made them quite angry by the looks of it -- angry, but uncertain, and that is a fine line we must walk.
'We need to keep them off balance, but not enrage them into risking a headlong assault that might threaten our flank.'

A shade found wandering in the Barrow-downs -- meaning no ill, it seems -- felt the pull of its brother and struggles to appease whatever force has returned to awaken them.

'Long did I rest, now awake, as vengeance claims trinkets to call a curse upon our bones.
'As it was in life, so too in death. His curse on us still as we yearn for sleep.
'My ring, forgotten, may still be found. Speed along, living, to a tomb of ground.'
Cryptic as it may be, it appears the shade is looking for something. Perhaps you can search the many barrows throughout the north Barrow-downs for clues.

The Wandering Shade's barrow is in the northern Barrow-downs.
Your investigation lead you to a barrow where the earth was recently disturbed by the movement of the heavy, stone door to the grave within the mound. You should search the barrow, for signs that link the shade to this location.

${PLAYER},
I ask, at your convenience, that you visit me in the Bree Town Hall. I wish to thank you personally for attending to an issue that has long plagued the folk of Bree. I hear that it was by your hand that the haunting of our town is ended, and I wish to see the hero of Bree for myself.
Graeme Tenderlarch, Mayor

'I had thought the reports of the haunting were drunken ramblings. Imagine my surprise when I was approached by the gate Watchers at the South-gate. They told me it was you, ${PLAYER}, that quelled the spirit once wandering the alleys of Bree.
'For that I am in your debt, as is this town. Please, accept this as payment for your deeds, which until now had gone unnoticed.'
'Welcome to Bree.'
Return to Graeme Tenderlarch at the Bree Town Hall
Graeme's Thanks
Graeme Tenderlarch asks you to visit him after finishing a task that plagued Bree.

Graeme Tenderlarch is at the Bree Town Hall.
You received a post requesting that you meet with the Mayor of Bree, Graeme Tenderlarch.

'Addie deserves better than the news that you were forced to deliver her. I would ask, if you are willing, that you attempt to finish what her sons could not.
'Addie is poor... we took her along thinking that we could do a good service only to end up here in this tragedy. Her sons came here to try and change her fortune, only to meet their end. I am certain they were searching for the rumoured treasures of Cardolan.
'I have oft heard the tales myself of treasure held deep within the ruins of Ost Gorthad. If there is any truth to this, then the treasure lies at the deepest parts of Ost Gorthad in the hands of a terrifying creature.'

'What is this? The treasure that my sons sought? Given over in kindness by yourself and my guides?
'I cannot... this, this is what my sons sought, a way to see that their mother would not die penniless. I shall keep this, keep it always in memory of their sacrifice.
'Thank you, ${PLAYER}.'
'Leave me to my misery. My sons are gone....'
Bring the treasure to Addie Wheatley
One Last Chance

Edith Sweetrose believes that there may be a way to bring the old woman, Addie Wheatley, some solace. She believes that deep within the ruins of Ost Gorthad there may be treasure worthy of what the woman's sons were searching for, but it is only legend.
'It pains me deeply to see the hurt on Addie's face. Will you not help her by recovering the lost treasure so that her pain may be reduced?'

The treasure is rumoured in the protection of a wight Lord at the deepest point of Ost Gorthad. Addie Wheatley is at the Dead Man's Perch in the Barrow-downs.
Edith Sweetrose wants you to search for the treasure of Cardolan to ease Addie Wheatley's pain over losing her two sons.

Defeated angry bears (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeated large barrow-crawlers (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'At the edge of the Old Forest, south through the Barrow-downs, there are many bears suffering from a terrible plague. The only way I can see to save them from their agony is to destroy them and ensure that they do not spread this plague into the remainder of the Old Forest.
'You will find the bears and the plague-carriers deep to the south where the walls of the Old Forest meet the Barrow-downs. Destroy the bears and then destroy the diseased crawlers infesting them.
'You may find some of the disease-carrying crawlers outside of their hosts as well.'

'There is no joy in taking natural life, but when that life is too far beyond recovery, it is our duty to see that it suffers no longer.
'Think on this and know that what you have done is for the good of all. You are well thanked, friend.'
Defeat angry bears (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeat large barrow-crawlers (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

At the Forest's Edge
Bob Redthistle told you that the bears near the bounds of the Old Forest, deep within the southern Barrow-downs, are being devoured from within by barrow-crawlers.

'I fear that the bears have contracted a terrible illness and to save others that may yet remain unmarred by the disease spreading through the wild, we must act. Head to the south and cleanse these poor beasts of their ills.'

The bears and the disease-bearing crawlers can be found on the border of the southern Barrow-downs and Old Forest.
Bob Redthistle wants to destroy the diseased bears before they spread their plague throughout the Old Forest.

'Long have I lived within the bounds of Bree-land, and my family has long exchanged tales of the people that lived in these lands. We spoke of their relationship with the Old Forest and how it was by their hand that the Forest began its slide to ruin.
'It is for these reasons that I find sorrow in these lands and not fear. Deep to the south, where the eaves of the wood are too strong to penetrate, you will find moving trees who have long been separated from their brethren.
'These once-noble trees are ruined and rotted from within, and I must ask that you destroy them. It is for the good of all that we end them before they become something even more vile than they already are.'

'There is no joy in the destruction of things natural. However, when the natural order is corrupted, it becomes a necessity to stop the corruption from spreading.
'Thank you for all that you have done.'
Defeat corrupted trees in the southern Barrow-downs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

Unfortunate Harvest
Corrupted trees in the southern Barrow-downs, broken free of the bounds of the Old Forest, have fallen to corruption.

'Corruption eats away at the roots of the once noble things that watched the Old Forest. It pains me to know that they must meet an end. I cannot abide them to fester... they must be destroyed. Head to the south and see that they are destroyed.'

Corrupted trees may be found deep within the southern Barrow-downs, at the eaves of the Old Forest.
Bob Redthistle asked you to deal with the threat of the corrupted trees found in the southern Barrow-downs, where the barrows meet the Old Forest.

Bob Redthistle awaits your return and information on the trees he sent you to destroy in the southern Barrow-downs.

'The corrupted trees must be purged out of the southern Barrow-downs but they may yet return to the natural fold. To determine this, I will need their seeds.
'Collect their seeds and return them to me. If they can be saved, I will see that the seeds are brought to a place where they can grow into natural creatures once again.
'You will find the corrupted trees deep within the southern Barrow-downs where the walls of the Old Forest are too thick to pass beyond.'

'Yes, it appears that some of these seeds are not destroyed or marred by corruption.
'It is possible that they will grow strong and true and return to nature one day. I thank you for what you have done, ${PLAYER}.'
'Search far to the south where the Barrow-downs meet the Old Forest. You will find the trees bearing the seeds I require in the shadow of the great forest.'

'In all my years of heading into these haunted lands, never have I seen anything like this. You must trust me friend, I would never have taken folk into the Barrow-downs had I known what walked here now. We shielded them as best we could, but the fright is still too much to ignore.
'It is the howling of the barghests. It will drive us mad if we cannot quell it. Could you help us? Kill these beasts, these terrors, so that we might have some rest to regain our strength for a return to Bree?'
'Yes, I heard their howls turn to barks, then whimpers. You have done well. We will enjoy the respite your actions have earned us.'

Howls That Shake the Spirit
Guides out of Bree fear for their wards as the terror of the Barrow-downs are now unleashed in the north. This unexpected course has forced them to drastic action.

'Barghests are terrifying beasts capable of breaking a man's will with their howl alone. These people cannot withstand such terror and we need to clear these creatures out to make our passage safe for a return.'

Barghests infest the northern Barrow-downs.
The howls of the barghests are enough to frighten less hardy souls near to death. The poor folk of Bree trapped between the Barrow-downs and the Old Forest are weakened by their journey and need rest that the howls will not afford. Reginald Sickleweed asked for your assistance in driving the barghests off.

'While we pushed through the fiends and the fog, we lost a few people. Some headed deeper into the mists of the Barrow-downs, and we hope they survived to reach a safe location in the south.
'Others were stricken with a terrible pox. One of these men was not as ill as others, but being sick, he offered to take word back to Bree requesting help.
'I fear that the disease comes from the crawlers and rats infesting this land. If this is true, then we shall need to clear a path through the Barrow-downs so we have a safe path out. If you are willing, kill these creatures but be wary, their bites and even their flesh may cause some vile illness or disease.'

'You have our thanks. When we make ready to move out of this accursed place, we will need as much of the area clear as possible. These folk are not as used to travelling as those of us who spend our lives on the road.
'We shall need every advantage we have available to prevent the loss of more lives.'

Carriers of Disease
Guides out of Bree fear for their wards as the terrors of the Barrow-downs are now unleashed in the north. This unexpected course has forced them to drastic action.
'You will find the diseased creatures all over the northern Barrow-downs. Seek them out and purge them so they cannot spread their disease further.'

Crawlers and rats can be found throughout the northern Barrow-downs and these vermin are likely carriers of disease. You have been asked to kill these creatures so that the refugees hiding at the camp between the Barrow-downs and the Old Forest will have a clear path to follow when they leave.
Sal Haywood believes that you can help her create a path for the Bree-folk to follow when the time comes for them to move. She asked you to rid the Barrow-downs of many of the vermin therein.

'Our forces were split when we entered the Barrow-downs and were set upon by wights, barghests, and all other manner of fell creature here. Some followed myself, while the others headed south.
'There is a place where the hill rises high and separates the southern Barrow-downs from the northern Barrow-downs. It is called Dead Man's Perch, and I pray that the name does not hold true.
'It overlooks southern Bree and is a flat area that we have oft camped at, if necessary. I pray you find the others there.'
'The others are alive! This news is pleasing. Though we still face great peril, we at least know that the others live.'
'The others live? This news fills me with hope. Now, we must focus our efforts on helping these folk and seeing that we, too, can escape from this accursed place.'

'These will do well. I am unclear what the power truly is behind these eyes, but I know that I have seen the ill that these creatures can bring about.

'Defeat the walking dead here and return their skulls to me. I will reward you well for these endeavours.'
'Yes, this proves a good many victories. You have done a great service to the people of Bree-land this day.'
'I have a small collection of materials that I am willing to trade for the wight's skulls. If you are willing to collect them, I am willing to provide you with this reward.'
