'I will take the advice of my other watchers under careful consideration. You must understand, however, that the Rangers are brutes in their own right and have long been a menace along our borders. 'As I said, there are others within Bree-land who need assistance and you have proven a valuable ally and more than capable combatant. I would have you visit one of these folk. Adso Haybank is a hobbit building an inn along the Great East Road stretching between Bree and Buckland. He has sent a message that brigands are stealing his materials and threatening the lives of his workers. If you would, please visit him and see what can be done. I will continue to think on an alternate course of action.
'You will find him west along the Great East Road, south of this cabin, between Bree and Buckland.'

'Grimbriar could send no one else?
'Woe is me and mine. We have much trouble here, and I truly hope that you are able to help as the Chief Watcher thinks you can.'

'Greetings, traveller. My name is Ivorel, and I serve at Celeborn's request as the scout-leader for the Malledhrim expedition into Mirkwood. Alas! His trust in me was misplaced, for we have come to ruin here in this twisted place! Few of my scouts have returned at all, but worst of all is the loss of poor Hal Tiller!
'Hal was a young hobbit of an unusually adventurous strain who begged to join us in this expedition. He was also a burglar with an unusually light step -- even for his kind -- and of such earnest heart that I accepted... and in so doing I surely signed the warrant for his death. My fellow scouts were all of fine mettle and experience, and the risks they knew well, but poor Hal was but a child compared to them, and I should never have allowed it.
'I cannot abandon my watch for my duty to the Malledhrim is clear and should any of my scouts yet live they shall come here. Yet you are clearly an adventurer of great mettle to have come this far yourself -- would you help me discover the fate of poor Hal? There must be some trace of him in the Scuttledells....'

'What a cruel fate for such a young innocent! These look to be the claw-marks of a Black Dog on the pack -- there is only a spark of hope left, for we have not yet found his body.
'Most likely because he was torn to pieces by the Black Dogs....'

Innocence in Peril

Ivorel, the leader of a scout expedition into the Scuttledells, is concerned about the fate of Hal Tiller, an adventuresome young hobbit who asked to be allowed to aid the Elves on their expedition into Mirkwood. Ivorel fears that the inexperienced hobbit may have been slain by the horrors lurking in the clefts of the Scuttledells.

'I saw several halflings accompanying the band of strangers who came into Lórien these past weeks, and they were taken into the Lady's presence and set, or so I am told, to tasks most dire.
'I had thought that perhaps they held some hidden strength, not apparent to the eye, and so I allowed young Hal to join us when he offered his services.
'Now though I feel sick, as if I had sent a child into battle ahead of me. He must be alive, or I shall never forgive myself.'

Search the southern Scuttledells for signs of Hal Tiller.
Ivorel suggested a few places where he might most likely be found as part of the mission he was assigned, but she believes that he is most likely dead.

Ivorel is at her camp in the Scuttledells.
You should return to Ivorel and show her the pack you found.
Collected gnawed bones (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'I must not give up all hope for poor Hal, though in a place as cruel as this I dare not hold too much....
'We must hunt down the black dogs that cornered him and see if we can find any clues to confirm his downfall... or perhaps a body so that we might at least put him to rest, though the Black Dogs are rarely so considerate as to leave much behind.'

'What are these...? No!
'Are these all that remains of Hal Tiller? I was a fool to ever let him come here!
'I will see his bravery avenged! The creature who did this deed must pay thrice-fold!'
YOU SHOULDNT SEE THIS

Gnawed Bones
Ivorel feels personally responsible for poor Hal Tiller, a young hobbit that accompanied her scout expedition.

'What possessed an innocent such as Hal to join us out here? These halflings are not known for such spirit so far as I have heard, though tales do speak of a few. Nevertheless, even the boldest halfling should not come to such a place as this!'

Black dogs can be found throughout the Scuttledells.
Ivorel has asked you to hunt down black dogs in the hopes of finding some clue -- or perhaps the remains -- of Hal Tiller.

Ivorel is at her camp in the Scuttledells.

Defeated Trapjaw

'One of my scouts managed to return on his own, ${PLAYER}, and he brings important tidings. The evening before last he found himself tracking an unusually large and cunning barghest -- he believes the creature may have been stalking little Hal Tiller at the time -- but he lost the trail when he was himself ambushed and injured.
'This creature -- named Trapjaw by the local folk -- evidently cornered and killed Hal a short while after. Now all that is left to us is to avenge the hobbit and destroy this monster before any more fall to it!
'My scout tells me that Trapjaw has a lair out among the Scuttledells, a distance north of here. Find him and slay him, ${PLAYER}, in the name of Hal Tiller.'

'Trapjaw is dead... and... what? You claim that Hal Tiller yet lives?
'We shall see about that! The little trickster has caused me more worry and care over the last week than I have known in two-hundred years! Here I thought him tormented or dead, and he has been off shirking duty to play hide and seek in the ravines!
'When he returns, I will make him wish that he was safely tucked in Trapjaw's belly!'
Trapjaw looks up from his grisly meal angrily, then leaps to his feet to attack!
Find Trapjaw
Talk to Ivorel at her camp
Avenging the Innocent

One of Ivorel's scouts has returned to tell of a deadly black dog named Trapjaw who was seen following Hal Tiller's trail two days ago. Ivorel believes that Trapjaw is likely responsible for his death.

'Hey there, my good ${RACE}! Glad to see a friendly face out here. That overgrown dog and I have been hunting each other in circles for two days straight! Luckily, I was just ready to spring my trap when you showed up, or it might have gone badly for you.
'Well, I'm off to continue the hunt! Good luck to you!'
'The lives of the hobbits are short enough and far too innocent for such matters. It grieves me deeply to realize that I am responsible for the death of one such....'

Trapjaw's lair lies a distance to the north-east of Ivorel's camp in the Scuttledells.
Ivorel has tasked you with avenging Hal Tiller by hunting down the deadly black dog, Trapjaw, within the Scuttledells.

Ivorel is at her camp in the Scuttledells, a distance south of Trapjaw's lair.
You should speak with Ivorel and tell her that Trapjaw has been slain and that Hal Tiller is alive.
Elf freed (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Greetings, ${PLAYER}. You have not come at a particularly auspicious time. Most of our number is already lost to us out in the lands that we call the Scuttledells.
'We were sent out to scout the terrain but a few days ago, but only a few of our small company have yet returned, and they tell of twisted ravines crawling with evil things. To the north, in particular, are the spiders that give this place its name, and it is there that I believe several of our comrades have been ensnared by the spiders.
'There may yet be time to free them before they are slain, if we are fortunate. Can you assist with this deed?'

'It appears that some of the scouts did not survive...I had feared as much, but at least you were able to rescue most of them.
'Unfortunately, even among those who returned, most were too ill from the spiders' venom and their entrapment to continue, and I had to send them back to Ost Galadh to recover.
'Could I have you stay here for a while longer to aid us? The Scuttledells are too dangerous for us to leave unattended while facing the forces in Dol Guldur.'
Free Elves from the cocoons (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Miluimil at Ivorel's camp
Entangled Elves
A number of Ivorel's scouts have not returned from their mission in the Scuttledells. Miluimil saw some of them entrapped by the spiders to the north.

'Fuirgam has forbidden his troops from entering the Scuttledells. He gauges the odds of a band of regular soldiers facing ambush and entrapment too great to risk so many Elves.
'I cannot say that our scouts have fared much better though, and it leaves us to dig our way out of our own mess without the help of soldiers from Ost Galadh.'

The ensnared Elves may be found in the nests of the spiders to the north of Ivorel's camp.
Miluimil has asked you to set forth to free his ensnared companions.

You should speak with Miluimil and tell him that the scouts have been freed.

'Keep one eye to the skies, ${PLAYER}. There are a number of the Enemy's black-feathered servants about. My scouts will be hard pressed to move unseen with such keen eyes above us.
'Defeat them quickly if you should come upon them in the ravines and gullies below... the fewer that make it back to Dol Guldur alive, the better.'

'So, there are fewer of the Enemy's crow-spies about? Excellent.
'If we can move about unseen, we have a better chance of rescuing a few of our people from these cursed ravines.'
Defeat Scuttledells crows (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Ivorel at her camp
Black Wings
If Ivorel's scouts are to have any hope of moving without the Enemy knowing their every step, the crows of the Enemy will need to be kept at bay.

'Agorin tells me that even when our Silvan kin still inhabited Ost Galadh, they warned their children to stay away from these dangerous ravines and dells, but that later they would challenge each other to dare the maze despite their elders' warnings.
'Now only a hardened warrior has any chance of surviving in this place. It is hard to imagine her holding fond memories of this death-trap.'

Scuttledells crows can be found throughout the Scuttledells.
Ivorel has asked you to hunt down Scuttledells crows to prevent them from finding her scouts or reporting back to Dol Guldur.

Ivorel is at her camp in the Scuttledells.
You should speak with Ivorel and tell her that many of the Enemy's flying scouts have been slain.

'It seems that Celeborn himself has said that we must not permit Gollum to fall into the hands of the Enemy, for the creature holds some knowledge that would upset the entire campaign of the Malledhrim against Dol Guldur.
'I know not what morsel of knowledge this Gollum creature possesses to so trouble the brow of mighty Celeborn, but we must move quickly if we are to prevent his capture!
'The goblin you interrogated claimed that the Orcs had pursued Gollum into the caves to the north, did he not? Swiftly then! Let us rush into peril, all wiser thoughts of caution unheeded, for now is the time!'
<rgb=#FF0000>WARNING: This is a solo quest, and cannot be completed in a fellowship.</rgb>

'Aye, it appears that Gollum has slipped our noose once again. It is a bit embarrassing, I will admit. There are few who can so readily outwit me in the brush.
'Our most important task has been achieved, however: the servants of Dol Guldur have been slain or chased off empty-handed, and Gollum's trail grows cold behind him.
'So long as he does not choose to consciously betray it to the Enemy, I think Celeborn's secret is safe for the moment. I doubt they will get another chance at him here in Mirkwood now that he is on his guard against them... but then, we may not either.'
Talk to Miluimil to travel to the caves

'I have received dark news indeed, ${PLAYER}. One of my scouts has told me of a deadly queen to the Blackvenom spiders - a brood that infests the caves in the northern Scuttledells. One of his companions fell to her, succumbing to a poison so quick and deadly that he was compelled to flee from her as swiftly as he could.
'We have little chance of destroying the brood so long as this creature lives, but I do not think you should dare to face her without some counter to her poison!
'If you can gather samples of the Blackvenom spiders' poison, I may be able to help you concoct such an antidote. Gather a few venom glands from Delúris' brood, then we shall make our preparations.'

'Be careful with those, ${PLAYER} -- the venom of the brood is not so deadly as that of Delúris herself, but it is not to be taken lightly.
'It is similar enough that I should be able to concoct an antidote from it, then perhaps you will be able to defeat Delúris without fear of her deadly sting!'

Miluimil's scouts have reported on the existence of a deadly spider-queen named Delúris that lurks in the northern depths of the Scuttledells. Her poison is so deadly that none who have dared face her have survived.

'Keep an eye open for an Elf named Gladiel. She passed through here a while ago seeking some passage and muttering about another brood of spiders she called the Saewathel.
'As if one brood of these creatures was not enough...I know nothing of the Saewathel, but she seemed concerned about their presence and seemed to be seeking some way through the Scuttledells towards Dol Guldur. I could not help her, I am afraid.'

'Fuirgam sent word to look for that Gollum creature? Well, the Scuttledells is an ideal haven for the likes of him, I am afraid. I was part of the effort to capture him on the fringes of Lórien a few weeks ago, but we had little success. One would think he could vanish into thin air, the way he evaded us.
'Very well. I doubt we will find him out here, but at least if we do catch sight of him, these ravines may act to trap him where we can lay hands on him. One of my scouts reported seeing a small, goblin-like creature scuttling furtively about in the Scuttledells. I thought little of it at the time, but if Fuirgam's suspicions are correct, it may have been Gollum.
'Here are a few places where he might be lurking, so keep a sharp eye out.'

'So, it seems very likely that Gollum is indeed in the Scuttledells, but this news you bring of Orcs and goblins also hunting the Scuttledells is ill indeed.
'It is one thing if we are unable to lay hands upon this Gollum, but quite another if the forces of Dol Guldur were to do so. Fuirgam seemed most concerned that this might occur.
'Whatever happens, ${PLAYER}, we must not allow Gollum to be captured by the Orcs!'

'Yet the tone of his message seemed almost desperate -- as if all might be undone were Gollum taken by the Enemy -- and so we must bend all our will to his capture if it be possible at all.'

Defeated Delúris

'Are you ready to face Delúris, ${PLAYER}? I have completed the antidote. Be sure to use it swiftly should you feel the sting of her poison upon you -- you will not have much time.
'The antidote's effects are short-lived, should the battle draw on, you may have to use more, but a few drops should suffice to counter her sting.
'She lairs in the caves up at the northern end of the Scuttledells, and many of her brood are gathered there, so take great care lest you be overwhelmed by their numbers before you even reach her.'

'And so the evil brood-queen has fallen. Well struck, ${PLAYER}...without their progenitor, the vile brood will wane as they are hunted to extinction. But much of that task will have to wait until after the fall of Dol Guldur.
'For now, it is enough to know that Delúris is gone and my scouts no longer need fear her black venom.'

Black Venom II
Having helped Miluimil craft an antidote from the poison of her own brood, you are now prepared to sojourn against Delúris the brood-queen of the Scuttledells.

'Where have all of these horrid spiders come from, I wonder? Agorin did not speak of such beasts when recounting the time when she lived within Greenwood the Great.
'Yet Celeborn once spoke of a black and evil creature that passed this way in the intervening years as the forests darkened, crawling out of the Misty Mountains and passing through the forests into the south, whereupon it again disappeared.
'Could it be that these creatures are the spawn of that evil?'

Delúris' nest is in the northern Scuttledells, north of Ivorel's camp.
Miluimil has asked you to confront and defeat the spider-queen Delúris and has supplied you with the antidote to her venom.

'With your help and the help of those Rangers... the Rangers, you came to me because of them didn't you? Well I should thank them, but now that I have my notes and focus, I want to get to the task of investigating these ruins.
'Would you be willing to make your way west down the hill to the Old Greenway Fort to tell that Andreg fellow that I am grateful for his assistance?
'You may want to make mention of the Orcs skulking about in the north too.'

'Oddvarr? I cannot say that I recall the name or the dwarf. If you say that he was forgetful, then perhaps he meant to send you on to Saeradan.
'This other bit of news is disconcerting. We must investigate, I fear.'
Talk to Andreg at the Greenway Fort
Down the Hill
Oddvarr finally remembered that he requested aid prior to your arrival.

Andreg is at the Old Greenway Fort, west of Hengstacer.
Oddvarr has asked you to tell the Ranger Andreg that he is grateful for the Rangers' assistance and that Orcs have come down from the eastern stretches of the North Downs as well.

${PLAYER},
I write to you on behalf of my captain, Strider. I am tasked with watching the events here in Bree-land and have learned that you have done much to assist the folk here. Your recent efforts in Bree-land came to my notice when I learned you aided a hobbit with a problem with brigands.
Your efforts against the brigands are admirable, and though you may have thought they were at an end, I regrettably must inform you that they are not yet finished. Bill Ferny, a citizen of Bree, in his own self-interest, endangers the lives of all the citizens of this land with his actions.
If you are willing, make the journey north along the Greenway to my cabin. You will find it east of Thornley's farm between Bree and the borders of the North Downs.
Saeradan

'It is good to finally meet you, ${PLAYER}. Your efforts in these lands restore hope where it is needed most. I only hope that we can lean upon you for more assistance.
'We must work diligently to undo the harm that has been wrought on these lands. I pray that we are not too late in beginning our efforts.'
'Is there something that I can help you with?'
Deliver the note you received to Saeradan
Saeradan's Call
You received a letter from a Ranger named Saeradan requesting your presence at his lodge along the Greenway, north of Bree.

Saeradan's cabin is found north along the Greenway between Bree and the North Downs. You will find his cabin in a small copse of trees abutting a steep hill east of Thornley's Farm.
You should go at once to Saeradan and learn what aid you may be to him.

'Your reputation precedes you. We are well aware of your efforts here in Bree-land and abroad. We, the Rangers of the North, thank you for all you have done. I wonder, though... are you willing to aid us ever more? Are you willing to stand against foes that have long risen up against the Men of Middle-earth, threatening to tear us out by our roots and make this world over in the grim visage of evil?
'I think you are willing and able. It is for this reason that I ask you to make your way north along the Greenway to the place where a pass cuts towards the eastern hills. There, in the ruins of the Greenway Fort, you will find one of my brethren.
'His latest reports tell me of a great danger growing out of the north, and he is in need of much assistance.'

'Saeradan is a man of his word, as am I. Your arrival comes at a critical moment. There is much work to do and too few of us here to complete all that must be done. Perhaps we will slow the progress of this foe by our combined efforts.
'This, at least, is a good hope to have.'
Talk to Andreg at the Greenway Fort
My Brethren's Call
One of Saeradan's brethren recently called for aid against a foe that the Rangers of the North know all too well.
'You should speak at once with Andreg.'

Andreg waits at his post at the Greenway Fort, north along the Greenway from Saeradan's Cabin.
Saeradan sent you to assist Andreg, one of his kindred.
Defeated Gazbúrz

Defeated Tarkrîp bone-smashers (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'I need you to head northwards, beyond Hengstacer Farm and through the lands where hunters go to make their living. If you encountered a small scouting group of Orcs just outside of Hengstacer Farm and even more encamped on the southern edge of the gorge, then I fear that a larger encampment may have found its way to the ruins in the east -- near the northern lakes of Bree-land.
'Go there and seek out the Orcs' leader and his minions. Defeat them, if you can, and return to me so that I know this deed is done. If you find an encampment there... then we know the North Downs have fallen.
'Please hurry.'

'It is done then. The Orcs must have overrun the valleys of the North Downs. The borders are breached.
'We must send a warning to my brethren far and wide. Your efforts are of great importance, ${PLAYER}.'

'We cannot afford to stay this investigation any longer. The Orcs have already proven more resourceful than we expected. If they organize quickly in the northern fields of Bree-land, then there is no telling how far they will travel southwards.
'Investigate the southern ridge of the gorge to the north.'

You have been instructed to search east along the gorge far to the north of the Bree-fields, beyond Hengstacer Farm, for an Orc-leader and his entourage.
Andreg fears that the Orcs have pushed too deeply into Bree-land, though only a small number of Orcs came through Trestlebridge. This concerns him greatly. He sent you to investigate and to strike a blow against the Orcs.

'While we did not capture Ferny, we did stop the threat for the moment. This will please Saeradan, and we should make haste to inform him of this success.
'Return to his cottage, south along the Greenway on the east side of the road, and tell him what you have accomplished.'

'While catching the coward, Ferny, and presenting him to Grimbriar would have established greater acceptance between us, I am pleased to know that the Orcs have been stifled for the moment.
'Still, we cannot be certain that we have stopped their efforts altogether, and I must ask you to continue your efforts for the moment.'

'Should you find anything of the sort, return it to me here at my post.'

'This find leaves me more concerned than before. Still our focus must remain here in Bree-land. There are lives to save here as well as in the North, and we must establish at least one bulwark against the Orcs.
'Thank you for doing this, ${PLAYER}.'
'Perhaps you will find nothing, but I still wish you to look through the Orcs' belongings to ensure that the people of the North Downs remain unmolested.'

Andreg has asked you to search the Orcs along the Greenway's eastern borders for signs of a struggle against the Men of the North Downs. Though the Rangers hope that the Orcs have not attacked the Men of the North Downs, they wish to investigate and ensure that this is not the case.
Collect stolen supplies (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'If we are to investigate Cirith Nûr, then we should also do what we can about recovering the many supplies the Orcs have received from raids and from the corrupted Men who aim to assist them.
'You are sure to find these supplies neatly tucked away in crates, packed far differently than Orcs would pack their provisions while marauding through the countryside. Collect these supplies, and I will see that they are restored to the Men of Bree and Trestlebridge.'

'Recovering this much from the Orcs will surely help to alleviate much of the suffering that Bree and Trestlebridge have felt from the encroachment into their territories.
'I thank you much for your efforts.'
'Have you found any supplies among the Orcs at Cirith Nûr? The beasts have stolen much as they have made their way here, not to mention what they have received from their allies here in Bree-land.'
Bring the supplies to Andreg at the Old Greenway Fort
Collect stolen supplies (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'I must send you next to the north-east to speak with the owner of Hengstacer Farm. Recent events surrounding the farm have reached my ears and speak of a dwarf who has come under attack by Orcs while looking for assistance from the farmhands.
'If you are willing, head north-east and speak with Éogar, the owner of the farm.'

'Orcs? You sound like that foolish dwarf who was here not long ago. I will tell you the same that I told to him... talk to my farmhand, Cam Applewood.
'He is the one spreading the hay over there.'
'Are you here about our horses?'
Talk to Éogar at the Hengstacer Farm
Talk to Cam Applewood at the Hengstacer Farm

'Cam will be the one who might help you. Speak with him.'
'You should speak at once with Éogar at the Hengstacer Farm.'

'Greetings, traveller. It seems as though you found yourself far away from the safety of Bree, which means that you are probably like myself and my friend here: adventurous spirits. We'd be out and about more if it weren't for those Orcs to the west. As it is, the safety of our camp seems to be more important than the money we could make by filling our bounties.
'Of course, if you are willing to assist us, we have some materials that we would happily part with should you want to help us.
'I am looking for turtle-shells to furnish the blacksmiths of Bree who often use them to create forms to fashion their shields from. You can find turtles all around the lake area here in northern Bree.'
'These will do nicely. Now tell me, which of these fine rewards would you like to claim for your efforts?'
'The turtles can certainly be a dangerous foe if you are not careful. Seek them out but watch your fingers.'
Bring the shells to Walt Whitrose
Collect thick turtle-shells (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

Walt Whitrose is collecting turtle shells to furnish to the Blacksmiths of Bree. Turtle-shells can be used as a good form for creating shields.

Walt Whitrose would like you to collect turtle-shells and return back to him behind the stones near the falls where the gorge meets the lakes.

'Aside from boars, I was also hunting bears in an effort to collect massive hides that could be turned into rugs, wall hangings and blankets if need be.

'These will do nicely and surely satisfy the order which I have. Thank you for all that you have done thus far, friend.'

'I came to the north to find tusks, a prized item for hunters throughout Bree. The tusks that I seek sit aside antlers within establishments to hang cloaks and overcoats upon. I have been tasked with collecting a good many of these, but the number of Orcs in the area, frankly, gives me pause to venture too far from our camp.
'You seem a bit more hardy than I, and I am willing to pay you for collecting the tusks which I need. Are you willing to help me?'

'These are perfect!
'I owe you a great deal, friend. Here, please take these and know that you have helped me greatly.'
'You will find boars all over these lands. Hunt them for their tusks and return to me when you have several.'

'Greetings, friend, did the missus send you over to talk to me? I've told her time and again, Mr. Thornley too, the horses will get spooked if we bring them in with what goes on here at night.
'There are wolves all about these lands and they've a den to the west where the Brandy Hills begin to rise in the distance. Until we thin out the number of wolves, we cannot risk the horses being moved here.
'If we thin out their number, I will think about bringing the horses out here to the farm. I'll even pay to get the help we need. Interested?'

'It's good to know that the number of wolves has been reduced. Still, these hills seem to be crawling with wildlife not usually seen this close to inhabited land. There must be something that has them all spooked.'
Defeat wolves in the north Bree-fields (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Nate Brittleleaf at Thornley's Farm
A Hollow of Wolves

Nate Brittleleaf explained that the wolves to the west of Thornley's Work Site, near the tall rise of the Brandy Hills, encroach further and further towards the Farm every night. He will not allow the horses to move into the stable until the wolves are handled.
'How is your search for that wolf den coming? I'm still seeing a lot of those wolves around here.'

The wolf-den is west of Thornley's Work Site.
Nate Brittleleaf asked you to thin out the number of the wolves that prowl near Thornley's Work Site.

Nate Brittleleaf is at Thornley's Farm.
You should return to Nate Brittleleaf and tell him that the wolves have been dispatched.
Defeated bears in the Northern Bree-fields (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Have you seen the bears around here? They stumble so close to the farm both day and night that I think they are either growing tame... or worse.
'If they continue to come closer to the farm, then it is possible they will attack, and if we put the horses in their stable before then... well the Thornleys will certainly lose much. If you are willing, I can offer up some coin for thinning out the bears around the area. You will find the bears I am speaking of roaming about from the Old Greenway Fort in the east through the Brandywine Hills in the west.
'Return to me when you've culled this lot.'

'You did well, and I did make a promise to offer you pay, but I cannot say that I am willing to bring the horses here yet.
'Look around you, see them out there... bears. I truly think that they are the greatest threat we face here in Bree-land. Surely, I do.'
Defeat bears in the Northern Bree-fields (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Return to Ray Thistlebur at Thornley's work-site
Bears Craving Honey

Ray Thistlebur believes that the bears surrounding Thornley's work-site are out for more than honey and that they will soon attack the site. He refuses to allow the horses to be moved into the stable until the bears are driven off.

'Others think that there are greater threats than bears in this land. Everywhere that I look, I see them as a greater threat than any I have seen. We have got to do something about their encroaching and growing population.'

Bears can be found throughout the north Bree-fields.
Ray Thistlebur has asked you to thin the number of the bears in the area.

Ray Thistlebur awaits your return at the stables at Thornley's work-site.
He will be pleased to know that you have done as he asked.
Defeated boars in the north Bree-fields (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'The others are concerned about the carnivores stalking about these lands, but I am worried about the boars. They are certainly capable of eating meat, but it is their bedding habits that concern me.
'The number of boars in these lands is enough to trample down the surrounding fields and destroy the food supply we need for the animals.
'It is for this reason that I would ask you to hunt the boars. Will you help?'
'Good. With fewer boars milling about, there will be more opportunity to feed the animals that we will move onto the work-site soon.'
Defeat boars in the north Bree-fields (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

Boars Making Beds

Boars are everywhere throughout Bree, but they are not always welcome. Ham Greythistle does not appreciate the number of boars treading through the nearby fields and wants their number thinned, lest they destroy some of the food sources for the animals meant to stock Thornley's Work Site.
'You will find boars all around the north Bree-fields. There may be a few to the west of here as well.'

Boars can be found throughout the north Bree-fields.
Ham Greythistle has asked you to hunt boars for him.

Ham Greythistle awaits your return at Thornley's work-site.
You should return to Ham Greythistle and inform him of your success.

'Saeradan must know that though our efforts here are successful, we cannot know the breadth of the invasion southwards. He must also know that our brethren to the north have been unable to prevent the spread of the Orc-tribes.
'Make your way south along the Greenway to his cabin and bring him these tidings.'

'Where we succeed in stopping their spread here, we fail in the north. This is dire news. Worse yet is the news that we likely did not prevent all of the Orcs from moving through Bree-land.
'I fear for the lives of the Rangers watching the passes and roadways throughout the southern reaches. I will continue to hold my post, but I must ask you for more assistance.
'For all your efforts thus far, however, I offer you thanks and this small token of our appreciation.'
Talk to Saeradan at his cabin
The Fall of the North Downs
Andreg is concerned about the Orcs which have breached the borders of Bree-land from the North Downs.
'Quickly now! Saeradan must be told of what we have learned. This is of utmost importance.'

Saeradan is at his cabin, south of the Old Greenway Fort.
Andreg told you to speak with Saeradan regarding the spread of the Orcs from the North Downs.
My Brethren's Call
Examined engraved stones (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'A word of caution, ${PLAYER}...if you head into the Scuttledells towards the east, you will soon find yourself among a number of barrows from which the Dead have risen to serve our Enemy. It was for good reason that he once hid beneath the name of the Necromancer after all.
'These are not ancient barrows, however. None such were here in the time when my people lived in Emyn Lûm.
'Thus I do not know who -- or what -- rises up against us now. Seek out the barrow-stones if you can and take note of their engravings. Perhaps we can learn more about the nature of this place and how best to subdue it.'

'I see. The runes you have discovered tell a painful tale indeed. One of the Men brought by Sauron from the East was literally worked to death in the construction of his fortress here upon Amon Lanc many years ago.
'Even in death these Men are yet forced to serve, their barrows serving as a line of defence should Dol Guldur be pressed. Or their bodies at least, for the Dark Lord cannot bind their spirits.'
Examine engraved stones (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Whence the Dead?
Ivorel wishes to learn the origins of the Dead that stalk the eastern reaches of the Scuttledells.

'The Fate of Men is puzzling indeed to we of the Firstborn. To die and leave the world itself? To go where? It is said that even the Lords of the Uttermost West do not know the full answer.
'But no matter their fate, it is a dishonour to allow creatures such as the gaunt-men to make use of their empty husks.'

The barrows are in the eastern reaches of the Scuttledells, north-east of Ivorel's camp.
Ivorel has asked you to study the stones in the barrows, looking for any engravings that might describe their history and give some clue as to the nature of the threat they contain.

Ivorel's camp is south-west of the barrows.
You should return to Ivorel with the engraved stones you found.
'Would you like to level up with the Iron Garrison Guards?'

'So you are not happy with your Springfest horse? Well, I can offer you an exchange, as I would not want one of my horses where it was not desired. However, this is not a decision to be taken lightly, so I will give you a moment to think about this.
'If you are really sure you want to exchange your horse, speak to me again, and I will give you a receipt in return. You can then exchange the receipt for a different horse.'

'So you have decided you want to exchange your Springfest horse after all? So be it. Look over this receipt and tell me if it looks fine to you.
'And this time, I hope you are more sure of your choice. Choosing a horse should not be something done lightly!'
'Have you made up your mind?'

'Thank goodness you are here. We heard from Rivendell that Gandalf the Grey had battled the Ringwraiths upon this very hill, and now servants of the Witch-king have been drawn here.
'The minions of Angmar have come already to Amon Sûl. I have laid a trap for them, but I fear this will be a foe beyond my strength alone.'

'You have done a remarkable thing here today. Few in Middle-earth can claim to have faced a Cargûl, let alone defeated it in battle. This will serve as an important blow to the Enemy. Today was a good day.'
Inform Candaith that you have arrived
Push back the first assault

Servants of the Witch-king have been drawn to Weathertop following a confrontation between the Nazgûl and the Wizard Gandalf the Grey. The Ranger Candaith has laid a trap to defeat the Cargûl who leads the dark forces to the ruins of Amon Sûl.
Candaith has been preparing the defences on the peak of Weathertop. Speak with him to confirm the plan for defeating the impending assault.
The first assault has begun. The Enemy will stop at nothing to destroy Candaith and reclaim what they lost.
The second assault has begun. Dark and powerful forces are at play.
The third assault has begun. The Enemy's power is waning under the strain of sustaining this unnatural attack.
The leader of the Enemy's forces and architect of this attack has finally made his appearance on the battlefield. Defeat this servant of the Nine.
Defeated Brungúr
Defeated Thorún
Defeated Mordeloth

'The Men of the East who were brought to construct Dol Guldur were driven hard by their masters, yet unbeknownst to them their final resting places were being prepared by evil beings who would become their masters in death as well, once the life was driven from them by their brutal labours.
'In these runes I see the inscriptions of three fell hands...gaunt-masters in the service of the Nine, who even now summon fell spirits to draw the Dead from their graves to move against us.
'These three sorcerers must be destroyed before they complete their rituals, or the numbers of the Dead will multiply greatly, and we may find ourselves hard pressed to hold Ost Galadh from them.'

'Excellent! With those fiends no longer a threat, the spells they have laid upon the barrows will begin to unravel.
'If the barrows themselves are sealed, then the greater part of the danger shall be contained.'
Defeat Brungúr
Defeat Thorún
Defeat Mordeloth
Talk to Ivorel at her camp
Masters of the Dead
Three gaunt-men called Gaunt-masters have been building a wight-army to use against the Malledhrim.

'The foul art of raising wights is a sorcery of unequalled evil. That creatures such as the gaunt-men may summon their spirit-brethren from beyond the Void to defile the corpses of Men is unimaginable!'

The Gaunt-masters can be found in the eastern reaches of the Scuttledells.
Ivorel has tasked you with destroying the three Gaunt-masters who are raising the Dead from their barrows.

Ivorel is at her camp in the Scuttledells.
You should inform Ivorel of the destruction of the Gaunt-masters.
Brungúr's barrow has been sealed
Thorún's barrow has been sealed
Mordeloth's barrow has been sealed

'The inscriptions you described to me speak of the great labour that went into the building of Dol Guldur as the abode of the Necromancer. Many men were brought here from the far east, and they worked upon its stones, and their labour was cruel beyond endurance. As they died of weariness, they were interred in the barrows here to continue their servitude eternally as guardians of last resort.
'They remain his servants still, and now are called forth to stay our advance against the tower, animated by fell spirits of Morgoth -- but many remain that have not yet awakened, and we must ensure that they do not come forth in greater numbers. We must seal these barrows so that their inhabitants remain therein forevermore.
'Shut the barrows and place these seals upon them -- these seals were given to me by Agorin before I left Ost Galadh, for she suspected that these barrows would be disturbed. I give them now to you.'
'You have sealed the doors of the barrows, ${PLAYER}? Well done. We have only to banish the fell wights that roam still in the Scuttledells... then perhaps peace will find this part of the forest.'
YOU SHOULD NOT SEE THIS
Seal Brungúr's barrow
Seal the barrow of Thorún
Seal the barrow of Mordeloth
Talk to Ivorel at her camp
Sealing the Barrows
Ivorel is concerned that the damage caused by the Gaunt-masters may not be reversible, but the barrows must be sealed to prevent more of the dead from emerging to threaten the Malledhrim.
'It is an evil fate that the shells of simple folk like the Woodmen should be made to serve the Enemy....'

The barrows lie to the north-east of Ivorel's camp.
Ivorel asked you to shut the barrows of the Scuttledells and place seals of Elven-make upon them so that the fell spirits of Morgoth cannot rise up as wights.

Ivorel is at her camp, south-west of the barrows.
You should return to Ivorel with news of your success.

'It is a riddle indeed, and my curiosity is far from satisfied. While many of the shades seem hostile, surely some will not be so, if you approach them in peace. What I am proposing, ${PLAYER}, is that I hope you will make another try at uncovering the full tale behind this town.
'Cross the bridge into Audaghaim and learn if any of the spirits will have words with you. I am sure there is a story here to be unearthed. I am most interested in the blank grave-stone, but I would not be surprised if all were tied together to some strange event.
'With Dol Guldur so near, this town cannot have met a happy end.'

'Who are you, and why do you disturb our peaceful town? Why do you pry? We have nothing to hide. Our forest is fair, and its resources plentiful. Our folk want for naught. Leave us be!
'We are but simple woodsmen and have been so for many centuries. Many of our folk are set in their ways, but a little change has never hurt anyone. There is always room for a people to grow. And what better time could there be for us to grow and change for the better?
'The graveyard, you ask? What of it? Every mortal creature must die, and so we bury them, as is our tradition. There is nothing unusual about Audaghaim. Now move along, or you shall be sorry.'

'Now that is a curious tale! Some points caught my interest as you conveyed the shade's message. He spoke of fair trees, as if he still sees Mirkwood as it was before the Watchful Peace ended.
'He also mentioned that his folk were simple, but that change seemed to be imminent. Based on the years on those tombstones, it is safe to assume that the dark Lord's reclamation of his seat at Dol Guldur was the change of which he spoke.
'So the Dark Lord came, naturally. How did the Woodmen receive him? We are getting closer to an answer, but it is a shame that the shade did not offer the whole story.'
Find a shade in Audaghaim who will speak with you
Return to Idhrenfair with the evidence
Unconvincing Innocence
Idhrenfair's curiosity has been roused by the grave-stones. He believes that something went amiss in this town if it is filled with such restless shades.
'There is nothing to see in Audaghaim, for we are but a simple folk. Move along, or you will be sorry indeed!'
'See what you can learn in Audaghaim. I am certain a brief search will be fruitful.'

Shades can be found in Audaghaim, east of the Haunted Inn in the Dourstocks.
Idhrenfair would like you to glean information from any shade in Audaghaim who is not hostile.

The Ranger Idhrenfair awaits you in the Haunted Inn in the Dourstocks, west of Audaghaim.
You should return to Idhrenfair and convey the words of the shade to whom you spoke.

'We have the truth now, but it should not stop here. The murderers should not be allowed to dwell under their curse in this way, their guilt smothered and pacified by denial and lies!
'You must confront the shade again, but armed with the truth this time. I wish to see if he will admit his wrongdoing like an honourable man, but somehow I doubt he will.
'The mystery is solved, but what good is it if the murderers are allowed to endure? You will do much for the memory of those worthy Men who perished in this horrible time for Audaghaim.'

'Welcome back, ${PLAYER}! You have done a very, very good deed in the name of those who fell while resisting the Dark Lord's evil influences. It is a tragic tale, but it is for the best that you did not allow its denial to be endured.
'You should be proud of what you accomplished today, even if it is too late to benefit the poor woodsmen who fell so many years ago. Their story should not be buried under the corruptions of Mirkwood, for they were heroes, and the truth deserves to be woven into song -- not forgotten, as the murderers would wish.
'Guilt and denial are the cruelest of enemies, my friend. You did well to fight them with such vigilance.'

'No! It is impossible! That...that story is no longer true. We destroyed that past and moved on with our lives. Why do you disturb our long peace with evils better left buried? That tale cannot be allowed to endure! You shall pay dearly for your meddling, Outsider!'
Confront the condemned villager once more

'It will be my pleasure to guide the Hidden Guard across the river on this, the first step of their journey.
'May it end in victory.'

'Welcome, ${PLAYER}! We are the Hidden Guard, formed by order of the Lord and Lady, and it is our mission to bring Mazog to the gates of Dol Guldur, there to trade his life for those of the prisoners held in that fortress. Secrecy is our watchword, and surprise our ally!
'Issuriel has told me already of your great deeds. I know you will be a vital member of the Hidden Guard on this journey!'

'At last we are underway, ${PLAYER}! If you have faith in these Elves, this \qHidden Guard,\q then I will as well.
'May our journey through Mirkwood be swift, and our return trip be the swifter, with Bori and the other captives hale and hearty!'

'Lord Celeborn and Lady Galadriel have determined that the Elves of Lothlórien must stand allied with the dwarves of Moria, as long ago they once did. They have selected a number of Elves to oversee the passage of Mazog through Mirkwood to Dol Guldur, where the Orc will be exchanged for the prisoners held by the Enemy in that fortress.
'I will bring you to these Elves, this Hidden Guard, as they make their preparations.'

'The Elves of the Hidden Guard were chosen for their varied expertise in a number of areas: Sigileth for her skill in melee combat and Raddir for his expert tracking ability.
'Were it my decision, I might have let Achardor join the main force of the Malledhrim rather than the Hidden Guard, given the recent tragedy of his brother's death. But I am sure Lady Galadriel had her own reasons for speaking on his behalf and believes he will be an important part of the Hidden Guard.
'I will bring you to the rest of the company, ${PLAYER}.'

'I am Sigileth, ${PLAYER}, and I know already of your deeds. You are welcome to accompany us upon this errand, though I have my doubts as to its wisdom. It is a sorrow that the dwarves have lost their own to the cages of the Enemy, but that is the way of war. Returning Mazog to his allies seems indefensible to me.
'If Lord Celeborn and Lady Galadriel see value in it, it is not the place of Sigileth to question.'

'Mae govannen, ${PLAYER}! It is good to see you again, and I welcome you to the ranks of the Hidden Guard. The knives of Sigileth, the bow of Cúcheron, the path-knowledge of Raddir, and the strong will of Achardor will see this mission through, and the friendship between Moria and Lothlórien will be stronger for it.
'Let the Enemy quake when he learns of the approach of the Golden Host, and he will think nothing of the Hidden Guard until we be at the gates of Dol Guldur and demand the prisoners kept there in exchange for the life of Mazog.'

'My brother Faengris was slain by Orcs that came down from the mountains following the company that sought refuge in the Golden Wood recently, and I desire to end Mazog's life myself! It pains me to know we must turn him over to his allies, and I have argued long against it already.
'I petitioned Lord Celeborn to let me accompany the group transporting the prisoner, but he denied my request. Only once the Lady Galadriel spoke to him did he change his mind; I do not know what she said, but I am grateful to her for it! Now I will keep a close eye upon Mazog for the duration of the journey, and if he gives me the slightest reason, I will take my vengeance upon him.'

'It is a pleasure to meet you, ${PLAYER}. I know that you will be a great asset to us upon this errand. If we are to bring the Orc-leader to Dol Guldur with the hope that we can exchange his freedom for that of the dwarf prisoners, we must do so in secret. Our numbers are not so great that we can resist a determined effort to take him from us before reaching the fortress.'

'Through the long hours of my captivity, I came to remember details from those stories I had long since forgotten. I remembered how Gandalf brought to Thorin Oakenshield the key and the map given him by Thorin's father Thrain...who was then a captive in the dungeons of the Necromancer, in the dungeons of Dol Guldur.
'How came Gandalf into those dungeons? Why, ${PLAYER}, he must have found a secret way in!'

'You have done it, ${PLAYER}! This secret way into the foundations of Dol Guldur is just what the Golden Host needs to take the fortress by surprise!
'Both Raddir and Mithrandir have aided us, even in death.'

'The dwarf may be on to something, ${PLAYER}. I remember too the stories of Mithrandir, and though the plight of the dwarves was not one that concerned us in days past, I have heard the tale of which he speaks. More than that, a friend of ours played a part in it!
'Poor, unfortunate Raddir journeyed with Mithrandir on that long ago quest to the dungeons of the Necromancer. He spoke, on a time, of the ways they trod together, and that there was a secret way into the foundations of the fortress seems a certainty to me.
'We must find it, ${PLAYER}. It must be somewhere in the base of the rocky spire on which Dol Guldur stands, either in Gathbúrz or the Ashenslades.'

'Quick thought and quicker action, ${PLAYER}! I have come to expect both from you, and it is fortunate for my continued good health that this is so!
'We cannot take Mazog that way. The spiders become increasingly dense in that direction, and I saw some great bulk moving behind the spiders. There is terrible menace that way.
'Achardor and I will remain on guard here with Mazog; the spiders have woven great webs behind Issuriel as she passed to the north-east. Clear the way of webs and find Issuriel, and we will follow afterwards.'

'For good or ill, we must walk this dangerous road, ${PLAYER}; our path lies through the Scuttledells.
'The rest of our company have gone on ahead and will hold the way for you to bring the prisoner to each of them. Spiders and black dogs are everywhere, so remain alert!
'You are familiar already with the support I can provide: I can make our foes bleed out their life-blood, or I can support you with power or morale. Let me know which you desire by shouting your commands for me by this banner.'

'We may not have much time. Ensure that Mazog's shackles are secure and bring him ahead to where Achardor and Cúcheron await. The sooner we emerge from this web-infested warren, the better for all of us!'

'This is not how this was supposed to end, ${PLAYER}. Not only has our charge been poisoned by the venom of Saebereth, but so too has Issuriel. There may not be hope of survival for either of them.
'We cannot proceed any further like this. We must go to the nearest outpost of the Malledhrim, to recover from this sad development.
'If we can recover, ${PLAYER}. If we can.'

'I am so glad to see you, ${PLAYER}! I thought being here on a mission of such importance would give to me bravery enough... but here among the webs my courage fades, and I just wish to be home.

I will support you as I did in the Drownholt: with power, with morale, or with a bit of both. Together, my courage will be the greater against the spiders of this place.

'We will fight together! Make use of this Malledhrim banner to provide commands to me: either to support you entirely with offence or defensively, or with a pleasing blend of the two!'

'Seek out the scouts Lamwen, Súlthel, and Laeglang in the wild lands of Gathbúrz, east of here and before the walls of Dol Guldur. Tell them to return and that the final leg of the Hidden Guard's mission will be undertaken.
'With the information of these scouts, we will be best prepared to effect the exchange of Mazog for the dwarf-prisoners.'

'There has not been a great deal of activity beyond the walls of Dol Guldur, ${PLAYER}. By now they are surely aware of the Golden Host; do they suspect any of its real purposes, I wonder? It is a great offensive, true; but do they suspect that we do not seek victory? That we are drawing their eyes to a point of our choosing, rather than theirs?
'I will return to Ost Galadh at once. It is to be hoped that we have not alarmed the Enemy overmuch, and we will catch them unaware in all respects.'

'Achardor gave me a message for you, ${PLAYER}. Your friend, the dwarf Bróin...he cannot be found. He has been missing ever since you left to recall the scouts. Achardor does not want to wait for him; he says that he wants to be rid of Mazog at once and have the errand completed.
'Speak with me when you are ready, and I will bring you to the Hidden Guard so you can discuss the matter with them.'

'The Hidden Guard has failed, ${PLAYER}. Achardor is slain, Mazog is taken, and Bori remains in captivity.
'Sigileth is mourning with Issuriel inside Gadorgar. She has asked not to be disturbed.'

'From my exploration, it seems likely that Gathbúrz will serve as the staging area for the armies of Dol Guldur when they move to attack Lothlórien. There are a number of camps here, but the Orcs are fortunately not yet massing here in great numbers.
'I will return to Ost Galadh and share what I have learned.'

'You have met me on my way back from the southern marches among the Ashenslades. The land there is blasted and dead, and the stench of evil is everywhere.
'It appears that Gorothúl has trained evil Men in the arts he learned from his own master; they are seeking to bind fell spirits to their service in the far reaches of the Ashenslades.
'I will return to Ost Galadh with my report of that place.'

Chapter 10: The Exchange
The mission of the Hidden Guard goes on: it is time to call back the scouts of the Golden Host and to bring Mazog to the gates of Dol Guldur in exchange for the prisoners.
'Tell Gruingalas I will be there soon. He is at Ost Galadh, is he not?'

'Lamwen, Súlthel, and Laeglang are somewhere in Gathbúrz, east of here and outside the long walls of Dol Guldur. Learn what they have discovered from their time scouting the wild lands between here and Dol Guldur and tell them to return here in preparation for the exchange of Mazog.
'We must know everything there is to know of the dangers in Gathbúrz before the Hidden Guard makes its move.'

'Will you not speak with Achardor? I know that Bróin will want to be a part of this final stage of the mission, and Achardor must not let his anger blind him to the dangers of haste.'

'Report to Gruingalas with the news I have given you. I will return shortly and give him further detail on the Orc-presence in Gathbúrz.
'He is at Ost Galadh, I believe?'

'You were going to return to Gruingalas in Ost Galadh and tell him what I have seen in the Ashenslades, were you not? I will be there as soon as I may, but surely you will arrive before I do.
'Please hurry, ${PLAYER}. It might be important.'

'There is little time to explain, ${PLAYER}, so I must be quick! After you gave the Laidhris to Mazog and the more I dwelled upon it, the more I came to regret that necessity. If only another dose could be made!
'I spoke with the Elf Barvessain atop the great tower here in Ost Galadh, and she said that more unmarked venom sacs of the Saewethil might be found, with time, but that the Sereglos flower is so rare that finding another one would be impossible. The conditions for such a flower to grow are so specific that only if the growing season could be slowed might such a flower still be found.
'I walked through the forest for many hours, heading north, and passed into lands beyond the reach of the Golden Host. I walked, and walked, and walked, and just as I was about to turn back in defeat, I beheld a grave mound among the tangled undergrowth. A stream flowed by its side, and now and then droplets of the water splashed atop the mound, where, bursting forth, grew a single flower, still in season.
'With this second Sereglos flower, and another unmarked venom sac, another dose of the Laidhris might be made!'
'It is over, ${PLAYER}. So many have died, and still Bori languishes within the dungeons of Dol Guldur. How can we hope to fight such evil?'

'Lord Celeborn believed some of the Nazgûl had come to Dol Guldur, but did not know for certain which of the Nine had done so. Now we do, though it is of little comfort to us.
'The Lieutenant of Dol Guldur commands the others; he is second only to the Witch-king, he who hailed from Angmar in the north. The Lieutenant of the Tower rules the fortress; it is he who struck down Achardor.
'The Gloom of Nurn was a wild-man of that land; it is peopled now only by slaves of Mordor. He wields a war-hammer in battle.
'I know nothing of the Black Blade save that he hailed once from Lebennin. He is fully a thrall now, as are all the Nazgûl, though it was not always so.'
Sigileth ignores you, her face a mask of anger and grief. You decide to leave her be.

'I was most wrong about the dwarf Bróin, ${PLAYER}. I have come to regret my words about him, and perhaps about all dwarves. To make such a seemingly futile journey in search of the one thing that might save someone he barely knows, someone not even of his own race...he showed a fortitude I had thought only Elves could possess. And he did it with much less complaining than I have done!
'But look at him. His journey north into the far reaches of Mirkwood has taken a toll even on his stout form; he needs to rest. The guards at the gate ahead will see his exhaustion as weakness, and we cannot afford that.
'Will you tell him to remain here in such a way as to spare his feelings? He has proven himself to me and to the others for the rest of time; he has no need to accompany us the rest of the way. He helped Issuriel, and now I wish to help him save his cousin and the rest of the dwarves.'

'Thank you, ${PLAYER}. It feels good to have a reason beyond revenge for this errand of ours. I still burn with hatred for the Orcs, but now too I desire to rescue the dwarves, whereas before it was only a vague purpose.
'We will do this now for Bróin.'
'None of those dwarves is Bori, ${PLAYER}? I thought not. They have been cruelly mistreated and seem close to death. Where is Bori?'
'I do not like this, ${PLAYER}. We must make Gorothúl turn Bori over to us, in addition to these three dwarves, or we will have failed. What can we do?'

'I am sorry, ${PLAYER}. Give me just a moment....'
Bróin leans on his walking-stick and tries to catch his breath.
'I walked many miles to the north in search of the Sereglos flower, and though I have my father's hardiness...it was still a most taxing journey. That it ended in success, and that Issuriel will recover from the Gwigael poison, was enough to give me further strength, but....
'One more moment, friend. I will have my breath back in a moment....'

'I do not want the guards at the gate to think we are weak, ${PLAYER}. They would not think so if they knew the distance I travelled, and in so short a time!'
Bróin laughs.
'I wonder if that will be the main verse of \qThe Glorious Tale of Bróin the Mighty,\q after all? It did not seem so glorious when I was hurrying through the dark, tripping over stones and treacherous roots, searching for a flower that might not even exist in the world any longer.
'Maybe my part in all this is over, ${PLAYER}. I do not want to hurt the negotiations for Bori. I will remain here and guard the rear. I trust that Achardor and the others will be able to fulfill this mission.'

'Well, here we are, ${PLAYER}. Now we will see if this errand was not as foolhardy as first it seemed.
'I will have Cúmaeth at the ready, in case we find our first belief justified!'

'Your offer does not interest me, ${PLAYER}. What use do I, Gorothúl, have for a useless Orc such as Mazog? Lord of Caves? He is lord of nothing! The dwarves crawl all over his caves like worms on mouldy bread! Bolg would be ashamed of his son, and Azog would slay him for dishonouring his family line!
'But it would humour me to hold Mazog in the dungeons of this fortress until the world's ending, so he may have time to think about how he failed his Master.
'I will accept your offer.'

'What is the meaning of this, ${PLAYER}? While you were recalling the scouts on the perimeter of Dol Guldur, the dwarf Bróin vanished from Ost Galadh. He told no one where he was going...and right on the eve of the exchange of Mazog for his kin!
'You had spoken for him, ${PLAYER}. You failed to speak of his cowardice! Do all dwarves abandon their companions when the road turns treacherous?'

'Look! Already Issuriel's strength returns! The Laidhris is working to fight the Gwigael poison!
'I...I do not know what to say. While I railed at unjust fate, the dwarf combed the forest for many miles to find a way to save Issuriel! It should have been me, ${PLAYER}....
'I cannot believe I was beginning to listen to the words of Mazog! Now there are no delays. We will go to the gates and exchange Mazog for the prisoners and be done with him at last!'
'It is no use, ${PLAYER}. We have failed. Let us go now inside Ost Galadh, though there be little we can do now.'

'I know of... an antidote. The ingredients are very rare... but....'
Issuriel winces, clearly in a great deal of pain. When she has recovered enough to speak, she weakly continues.
'I need an unmarked venom sac from... the same brood of spider, Saewathel, or Blackvenom... and a flower. The flower Sereglos grows upon untended barrows... in Mirkwood. It blooms only for a few days... in the year... and dies. There may not... be any remaining... this season....'
She gasps for air and is silent.
'I understand, ${PLAYER}. I will allow no one to enter Gadorgar. We are all doing everything we can.'

'I have nothing to say to you, ${PLAYER}. I cannot understand how we have come to this point, saving the life of a filthy Orc and allowing a friend to... to....'
Achardor visibly brings himself under control.
'Tell Gruingalas outside the door that no one is to come into Gadorgar. I want no one disturbing Issuriel. She needs... rest.
'The scouts should also be recalled in preparation for the exchange of Mazog.'

'You found... found the components. Good, ${PLAYER}....'
Issuriel closes her eyes briefly, then opens them again sharply.
'Find Barvessain! She... she can make... the antidote....'
She struggles visibly, then manages to gasp out, 'She is somewhere in Ost Galadh!' before sleep takes her.
'Where are... the ingredients...?'

'What is this? A Sereglos flower? How did you find this? These bloom so rarely and under such specific conditions....'
Barvessain trails off as you explain the need for an antidote to the gwigael poison.
'Laidhris, it is called, and I can brew it from these ingredients immediately. But there will be enough for only a single dose. I hope this will not be a problem.'
'You have nothing for me?'

Mazog is visibly ill, his body weakened from the effects of the gwigael poison. Still, he manages to sneer as you give him the Laidhris antidote.
'Kolfrangíz....' he manages to mutter and gives a short barking laugh before lapsing into sleep.
Mazog sneers at you.

Chapter 9: Coursing Venom
Issuriel knows of someone who can brew an antidote for the gwigael poison, but the components are so rare that it is only realistic to expect a single dose.
'I have given you the single dose of the Laidhris that I was able to brew. I hope you can use it to cure whomever is afflicted with gwigael. It is a terrible poison.'

'A Sereglos flower... I have heard tales of them, but they are so rare and bloom so infrequently that I cannot say I have ever seen one.
'There are barrows just to the north of here, and they cannot have been tended for an age. Is it beyond hope to think a Sereglos flower might grow upon one of them?'

'The Sereglos flower... grows only on untended barrows... in Mirkwood... for... a few days out of the year. I do not know... where any may be. It may be already too late.
'We also need... an unmarked venom sac... of the same brood... as Saebereth....
'Look in the Scuttle... the Scuttledells.'
Issuriel is asleep. She told you to find Barvessain, somewhere in Ost Galadh, and to have her brew the antidote to the gwigael poison.

'Thank you... ${PLAYER}....
'It is important... that the Hidden....'
Issuriel is unable to finish the thought before she lapses again into unconsciousness.
'Tell Gruingalas, right outside, what I have told you! Now leave us!'
Mazog has fallen asleep, but already his strength is beginning to return.

Issuriel is barely conscious, but her mouth forms a thin line when she realizes what you are trying to give her.

Issuriel is fast asleep and does not hear you.

'Perhaps it was foolish to think that treating with the Enemy was possible, ${PLAYER}, but there was enough to gain that it seemed worth the attempt. It has now failed, but the forces of Dol Guldur will see the effect of betraying us beneath a flag of peace.
'The main arm of the Golden Host has camped at Thangúlhad, a camp east of here, in Gathbúrz. Present yourself to Ningloril there, for she will have something a ${CLASS} such as you could do for the benefit of the Golden Host in the next stage of this campaign. A word of warning: Ningloril is stern, and not given to idle jest. Do not try her patience, or it will go ill for you.'

'Are you here to lend your aid, ${PLAYER}? We are met in time of war, though it be a war for which lasting victory may not come. Celeborn has started the Golden Host marching not to win the day, but as a delaying action.
'Even a failure here will be of some value, for the real aim of the Golden Host is to keep the attention of the Enemy, and that we have for certain. I hope we will live long enough for it to be of consequence.'

'The Orcs of Dol Guldur are being made into a dangerous fighting force, ${PLAYER}, under the leadership of ferocious uruk-commanders. A great force of the creatures are being organized into troops in several great Orc-camps in the northern reaches of Gathbúrz.
'Bring the fight to these camps: Búrzkala, Kúfuzg, and Hongoi, and defeat their uruk-commanders, for without them the Orcs will be less effective and the oncoming assault must be weaker.
'You should also find any battle plans that may be lying about these camps. We may learn when to expect their attack, that we may brace against it.'

'I could hear the shouts coming from the Orc-camps even from here, ${PLAYER}; you have done well to sow disarray in the camps of the Orcs!
'Much of these plans are indecipherable to me, but I do recognize the word \qdush,\q meaning sorcery, and this circled area can mean only one thing: peril for the Elves lies there!'
'You have not returned with anything of interest to me?'

'If you stand by this banner and shout your commands for me, I can provide support in battle. Arrows I let fly from Cúmaeth can slow the attack speed of our foes or make difficult their movement; additionally, I can pepper our enemies with such a flight of shafts that their general defences are broken.
'Use this banner of the Malledhrim during battle to tell me which of these tactics you desire!'

'I have not seen creatures of that sort within a league of Lothlórien, ${PLAYER}. They fill me with disgust. Still, we triumphed over them, and Cúmaeth has many arrows left in reserve.
'There is a tunnel just ahead; it lies upon the route Raddir selected for us. I do not wish to bring Mazog through there until we know it be clear.
'I will stay here and guard Mazog. Enter the tunnel and clear it of any dangers and then return here to me. Then you can bring the Orc safely through the tunnel.'

'The tunnel is clear? Good. I fought off some more fen-lizards, but it was nothing I could not handle with Cúmaeth.
'Ensure that Mazog's shackles are secure and bring him through the tunnel. You should have no more problems.'

'This journey has already cost us a great deal, ${PLAYER}, and with every loss, it becomes more difficult to keep this wretch alive!
'I cannot stand to look at him. To tally up the pain he has already cost us would take a long while already, and I worry he is not done adding to it!
'Let us leave this cellar for now. Achardor will watch him... and Sigileth and the others will watch Achardor.'

You call his name and try to get a response from the Elf, but it is already too late: Raddir is dead.
There are no signs of a struggle or any mark of injury that you can see, but despite that puzzle, one thing is clear: the Hidden Guard has lost one of its own.

You explain Cúcheron's desire that you clear the tunnel of dangers before bringing Mazog through it, and Raddir nods.
'That is a good idea; the creepers here remained asleep for Sigileth and I to pass through, but of course Mazog would have sought to awaken them at the worst possible moment! Cúcheron is perhaps more canny than I gave him credit for being!'
Raddir seems to think for a moment, and then haltingly begins.
'I came back here because I thought I saw... I thought I saw someone I knew, ${PLAYER}... a friend. But it could not be, for this friend... this friend has not walked this way for many a year and has since gone where none may follow.
'If I did not know better, I would have sworn it was he. But here there is nothing but creepers. It was a trick of the light, my error in the dim.'

'According to Raddir, this is the mid-point of Râd Cened, the road he has chosen for us to take through the Drownholt. You are lucky, Mazog, that we have need of you alive! Were it my decision to make, or Achardor's, you would be slain already and left to rot within one of the foetid pools of this swamp!'
Mazog says nothing, and Sigileth continues.
'This banner of the Golden Host will allow you to select a support role for me to use during battle, ${PLAYER}. I can draw the life-blood of our foes with Lanchigil and Egnassigil or provide you with morale or power support. It is up to you.'

'We have done well to repel these attacks, ${PLAYER}. Ensure that Mazog's shackles remain secure and bring him further into the Drownholt.
'You will encounter Raddir next along Râd Cened. Give him my thanks for planning this route. We have done well to weather its dangers, and Mazog's presence is still a secret to the Orcs of Mirkwood.'

'We have come part of the way, ${PLAYER}, but there is a long way to go yet; the Drownholt is perilous, and while Raddir has chosen our road with care, we must still use caution. The rest of the Hidden Guard have gone on ahead, for we cannot move as a group if we are to maintain our secrecy. You will bring Mazog to the members of our company, further ahead in the fen.
'Did you hear that? Something approaches! I will leave the coordination of our attack in your hands; shout your commands of me by this banner, and we will repel whatever evil approaches! My talents are for the restoration of morale and power, though they will be of no use for our prisoner. Do not let Mazog sustain injury!'

'We have done well to repel the creepers of the Drownholt, ${PLAYER}, but there will be more, I am sure of it. We must protect Mazog from their barbs and grasping tendrils, though our hearts be not fully in it!
'Make certain his shackles are secure, and travel forward with him through the swamp. Cúcheron should be just ahead.'

'What a delight! Look how fall the Elves that seek to imprison me, one by one. Perhaps you will be next, ${PLAYER}, ${RACE} that deserves it so!
'So end all enemies of Mazog, Lord of Caves! No shackles can bind me forever, and if my hands be bound let my legs carry me to the allies that must have done this, the allies that even now seek to free me from bondage!
'Ho, Orcs of my distant kin! You seek to free Mazog, and he will be free with the rewards of generosity!'

'We cannot talk here, ${PLAYER}. We have blocked the Orc's escape, but now we must gather the rest of the Hidden Guard and devise a new plan. Without Raddir....'
Achardor's face is a storm-cloud of emotions. He brings himself under control, but it is clearly an effort.
'We must rejoin the Malledhrim. There is a village called Audaghaim among the Dourstocks. The plan was for the main body of the Malledhrim to use it as a supply point before advancing further into Mirkwood. We must go there and discuss what is to be done.'

'The memory of our desperate journey overland out of the Drownholt is a hazy one, ${PLAYER}, but we have arrived at Audaghaim. It is a place for us to lick our wounds, though not all our wounds can be healed, here or anywhere.
'I cannot believe Raddir is gone! Can our mission have failed even as it begins?
'I will sharpen my blade. It may drink the blood of our prisoner soon, once we see wisdom and abandon this foolhardy errand.'
'I need some fresh air, ${PLAYER}. Let us go out onto the porch of the Inn. The sight of our prisoner makes me feel ill.'

'There will be no better time than this to assault the tower of the Nazgûl, ${PLAYER}. Lord Celeborn has determined that we cannot withstand the counterattack should all of the armies of Dol Guldur move on us at once; this will be our final offensive.

'Meanwhile, you and your allies will enter the fortress by the secret way used by Mithrandir and engage in a skirmish within the tower. The Enemy will be in disarray, not knowing on what front to do battle, and we will have the day.'

'We have had victory, ${PLAYER}; at least so much victory as we had a right to expect. We cannot hold this fortress, and it may not be long before the Enemy strikes back at us with such force as it will take to push us back across the river.

'The Golden Host is to have two objectives: to bring battle to the Enemy in Dol Guldur at a time of our choosing, before he can attack the woods of Lothlórien in force, and to exchange Mazog, the prisoner of the Iron Garrison, for the captives in the dungeons of Dol Guldur.
'Your aid has been requested for both of these aims. Speak with Braiglinn, by the hythe up the slope from the docks of Lothlórien. He will recount to you details of each plan.'

'It has taken a great while, ${PLAYER}, but at last the preparations are complete. The Malledhrim, the Golden Host of Lothlórien, are now ready to cross the river Anduin and assail the forces of Dol Guldur.
'I do not yet know the specifics of the plan, friend ${CLASS}, but it seems the Golden Host is to have two objectives: to bring battle to the Enemy in Dol Guldur at a time of our choosing, before he can attack the woods of Lothlórien in force, and to exchange Mazog, the prisoner of the Iron Garrison, for the captives in the dungeons of Dol Guldur.
'Your aid has been requested for both of these aims. Go now to Imlad Lalaith on the shores of the Anduin and speak to Braiglinn there. He will recount to you details of each plan.'

'It was not easy, ${PLAYER}, but we have made the crossing and expelled the Orcs from their fort atop Amon Angened. The Golden Host is now ready to begin the passage into Mirkwood.
'I hope we are not wrong in this. A great deal is at stake.'

'You have come at last, ${PLAYER}; I had begun to wonder if you would not wish to be part of the first crossing! But I am pleased to see this is not so.
'See you the river Anduin? Its currents are strong, though this be a calm enough place to cross, and once we land on the far shore we will need to be ready for anything. The landing may be uneventful, but then it may be tumultuous indeed. It will be up to Fuirgam, on the other side of Anduin, to ensure that all goes as smoothly as it may.
'Once we are secure on the beaches, I will arrange for a second crossing to bring the company that will escort our prisoner to Dol Guldur. Are you ready to travel upon the first boats across? Speak with Calengoth down at the docks if you are ready.'
Talk to Braiglinn at Imlad Lalaith
Board Calengoth's boat and assist Fuirgam with his tasks among the Mirk-eaves

'Speak with Calengoth down at the docks; he will have a boat you can use to make the crossing. Once on the other side, you should assist Fuirgam with the many tasks necessary to secure a foothold in Mirkwood.'

'I am filled with anticipation, ${PLAYER}, and my fingers seek the strings of my bow eagerly! The Golden Host is now ready to depart, to cross the river and bring the fight to the Enemy. It has been long since we have done more than watch our borders; too long.
'Go now to Imlad Lalaith on the shores of Anduin, in Lórien, and speak with Braiglinn. He will recount to you the details of the Golden Host's aims.'

'Gollum has slipped through our fingers yet again! I have good reason to believe that he has fled to the north, into the Scuttledells -- a warren of ravines and gullies infested with spiders and other foul beasts.
'I have sent instruction to my scouts there to be on the look-out for him, but I have received no word from them since and fear that something may be amiss.
'Would you be willing to journey into the Scuttledells and lend my scouts aid in capturing Gollum? He is more elusive than any creature I have encountered before, and they may need your help. Speak with Miluimil.'

'Fuirgam believes Gollum is now here in the Scuttledells? I would feel better about our chances of finding him if most of my scouts were not already missing themselves.
'These ravines are treacherous to any who dare them, and I fear we will be lucky to emerge from them unscathed, much less to capture one such as this Gollum within them.
'Nevertheless, Fuirgam's order is clear, and he would not have made it if the need were not dire. Let us see what we can find of this lurking creature, shall we?'
Talk to Miluimil in the Scuttledells

'I have known Fuirgam for a long time, ${PLAYER}, and I have rarely seen him this upset over anything. Since that Gollum creature escaped into the Scuttledells he has seemed preoccupied with the matter.

'I managed to track Radagast south and there met friends, the Eglain, who make some ruins here in the Lone-lands their home. They are a solitary and quiet people, having shunned societal obligation for a simple life eked out here. The few that do venture towards the more civilized areas of the world are still different than most you will ever meet.
'Because of this nature, they are truly wary of anyone who wishes to traffick with them or their allies, and it seems that Radagast has enlisted their aid, not only now, but at some time in the distant past. I fear that you will need to earn the right to speak with Radagast.
'I have done what part I can. My horse will take you south and west to The Forsaken Inn. There, you should seek an audience with Gadaric Munce. He will know your name. Be safe, ${PLAYER}.'
'You have toiled long, and we are grateful for all you have done. You appear to have the best intentions towards our people. For this, we will grant you the request you ask.'

'Candaith is a good man who has taken a chance by giving us his word that you can be trusted. For his sake, and our continued friendship with him, I hope that you are worth the risk.
'We are a simple people who wish to remain apart from society, but there are efforts that all must undertake to survive, and we will ask you for assistance to prove that you are worthy.'
