'${PLAYER}, I have news of Radagast, but I must ask you once again for assistance here. The letter you recovered from Bleakrift speaks of the Orcs' true goals: taking control of Amon Sûl! 'We cannot stand against the force when they are assembled, but we can once they are splintered. They wish to establish a base that will allow them a vantage over the entirety of the Lone-lands. We must foil their plans, ${PLAYER}!
'Return to me when you are ready. Together we shall scale Amon Sûl and defeat Rigûl, their leader, before he can carry out his master's will!'

'Do not concern yourself with the Orcs that remain. This far removed from the South-lands, they will dwindle and become only a small danger to travellers through the Lone-lands.

'I've been tracking wolves and other prey for the greater part of my life. Never had I seen anything like it, and now I hope to never see anything like it ever again. It stood nearly the height of a man at the shoulder with jaws twice the size of my head!
'Worse, it was led by Orcs! Orcs! I've heard tales, but never had the misfortune to see one. Now, I have the displeasure of their acquaintance and a terribly light set of packs to show for our misbegotten hunt.
'I'm asking, not without humility, that you offer up some assistance to those of us who have so recently seen our fortunes dashed. There are wolves all throughout these hills. Their pelts will fetch a good amount of coin back in Bree. I would be willing to pay you an up front sum for your assistance in keeping our livelihood intact. What say you?'
'You are a truly generous hero! We thought our lives lost, then our livelihoods, now we have a small bit of hope that we can recover. We shall ever be in your debt.'
'Without something to trade on our return to Bree we will be truly hungry hunters. If only we could gather enough pelts, we might yet restore our ruined traps and equipment.'
Talk to Dale Sageford
Collect smooth wolf-pelts (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

Hunters out of Bree tracked what they thought was a large wolf through the northern stretches of the Midgewater Marsh and into the Midgewater Pass only to find that it was something far worse. Now, they are trapped and in dire need of assistance.

Dale Sageford and his companions make their living in pelt-trading, and the Orcs took everything they had and left them to die. He has asked that you aid them in recovering some of the pelts so they can put food into their stomachs upon their return to Bree.

'Dale and Sam are too busy whimpering about losing our traps and our equipment. Fools! What we need to do is gather up our weapons and trudge right on back to Bree. We've lost traps before. In fact, most times you'll lose several traps when hunting prey that is worth hunting. We do have little means, but we should have enough to survive. What we do not have is our weaponry.
'The Orcs made off with everything of value. Some things, I am willing to part with; other items, like my bow, Sam's halberd, and Dale's mace, we cannot go on without. The journey home is treacherous as well, and knives will likely not see us through that journey.
'I do not have much, but if you can find it within you to assist us, then I will give you what I can share. The Orcs likely are still carrying all of our goods.'
'These will certainly help. Now, if I can only get these two to stop licking their wounds, gather their composure, and head back towards Bree, I might sleep in a real bed within a few nights.'
'If I had my bow, I would leave these whimpering children behind and accompany you to fight these Orcs.'

'We had hoped to be spending a few days at The Forsaken Inn, eating some of Old Mugwort's stews, but now we are just hoping that the strips of dried meats we have left will last us. That is, unless you would be willing to help get us some meat. Beggars are not choosers, and we would be pleased to get even the stringiest of wolf-meat. Though, I will share a secret... there is choice meat on a wolf.
'If you are hunting them anyway, would you collect some choice cuts that I can slice into strips and further treat so that we have enough food to return to Bree?
'There are wolves prowling all throughout the hills of the Midgewater Pass.'

'These are fine cuts indeed. I shall be able to cure enough meat for a trip to Bree and back to this accursed land.
'Thank you so, ${PLAYER}. You have shown me that there still is hope though the skies above are darkening.'

'You shouldn't be having a hard time finding wolves, as they hunt all along these hills. Trapping... now that might be more difficult. The blasted Orcs destroyed everything we had, or I would offer to lay traps for you.'

'This may seem a strange request, but it is one that I feel necessary.
'There is an inn on the border of the Midgewater Marsh and the Lone-lands, The Forsaken Inn. It is operated by a man named Anlaf. He was holding rooms for us as we meant to stay there for a few days before returning to Bree.
'With all that has happened, it is clear that we will not be making the journey south over the hills to visit the inn. Could you make your way there and let the innkeeper know that we will not be coming?'

'Sam Thistlebur? I do not recall the name. Of course there have been more folk passing through here than normal. Usually, there are very few pressing toward the east or coming from that way. Those dark shadows have caused this land to stir in ways I had not seen through most of my life.
'Their rooms are freed. Ha!'

Word to Anlaf
The hunters from Bree, camped within the Midgewater Pass, asked you to take word south to The Forsaken Inn to alert the owner of the Inn that they will no longer need their rooms.

'Anlaf is a queer sort, not the happiest fellow I have ever met. Still, he runs an adequate establishment and Leiva is one of the finest women I have ever met. Could you let them know that we will no longer need the rooms at The Forsaken Inn.'

Head south to the border of the Midgewater Marsh and the Lone-lands and seek out the owner of The Forsaken Inn, inform him that the hunters no longer need their rooms.
Sam Thistlebur asked that you make your way to The Forsaken Inn to tell the innkeeper that he no longer needs to save their rooms for them.

'To the south, over the hill and through the vale that lay just beyond my camp, you must take care to avoid goblins. Their number has grown swiftly in recent days. Beyond them, a good distance south you will find a road stretching east and west. This is the Great East Road.
'Follow it west, towards Bree, and over a ruined bridge you will find a crumbling and nearly collapsed inn...The Forsaken Inn as it is called. The owner therein and his workers and guests will likely need assistance as this part of the world has changed greatly in recent weeks.
'Do not tell them I sent you...only offer your aid. They will likely and sorely need it.'

'More strangers passing through? No? Well then, if you aim on staying you might want to find a nice parcel of the floor to take up. The inn is dangerously close to full for some reason. I am not complaining -- coin is coin, even if there is little to spend it on in these parts.'

'These lands have become much darker in recent days. Since my time wandering in the eastern stretches of the Lone-lands a dark shadow has flocked down from the sky. Now they patrol the western lands as well as the east in search of something for their unseen masters.
'I speak of the crebain. Vile creatures with a gift of intelligence greater than they should possess. We must do what we can to thwart their efforts. Kill these vile birds and collect their eyes. It is the only way to ensure that they cannot return the information that they have gathered to their masters.
'You will find them all throughout the Weather Hills.'

'Though it seems an ignoble task, I tell you plainly that this was necessary. The crebain are spies for eyes from afar and they seek some grand prize here. With all that I have seen in these lands as of late, I fear that there is some great wheel turning, and I can only hope that our part can slow its progress.
'Thank you, ${PLAYER}, for all you have done.
'If the crebain find what their masters desire, there is no telling the size of the invasion that this land will face. We must do our part to see that this does not come to pass.'

Candaith explained that the crebain circling the areas near Weathertop are not some innocuous bird, but that they are, in fact, creatures of ill-omen sent from afar to spy upon these lands. 'I am glad to see that you have returned, friend. We have made it here to The Prancing Pony in your absence and have been holding it, but I fear we won't last much longer. The brigands are coming at us with a vengeance which I cannot match. I am glad to have you by my side once more.'
'Oftentimes during Skirmishes such as these, you will find you have other allies, such as myself, aiding you in your battle. In some cases, if those allies fall, you will lose the Skirmish.'

'We often know little about the enemy's forces or where exactly they may come from. From scouting, I know that we are facing brigands, half-orcs, and wolves of varying skill and strength. But I do not know what combination of those might come at us at any point. Stay on your guard and be prepared to alter your defence at any moment to best defend against the enemy's assaults.'
'That Orc was one of the lieutenants I was speaking of. You did well to defeat it.'

'Bree is safe! You have done us a great service by aiding the cause. I could have held for a short time, but that half-orc with Bill Ferny and Harry Goatleaf surely would have done me in had I been alone. I thank you greatly for your aid.'
'I thank you again for your help in freeing Bree. It will be long before what you have done is forgotten.'

'A problem has arisen for the Malledhrim, my friend. Our forces are being harried by groups of Warg-riders who are ranging throughout the Mirk-eaves. Normally, we rely upon speed and our superior skill in battle to ensure victory even when outnumbered, but the Warg-riders' great speed allows them to harry and assault my soldiers at will.
'We need you to help thin out their numbers and keep them at bay...at least until we have secured the Mirk-eaves from the Enemy. When you have done this, return to me for further instructions.'

'While there are doubtless more of these beasts and their goblin-masters in Dol Guldur, you have done well to thin their packs for the present.
'With our soldiers free to manoeuvre in small bands again, the Orcs will be pinned down and unable to leave their camps for fear of assault.'

The Taughâsh tribe which guards the Mirk-eaves against invasion use Wargs and Warg-riders to patrol the beachhead.

'The keen senses and swift gait of the Wargs have ever been a danger to our scouts and skirmishers. Here, for once, we move in force with the strength to drive them back, but your help in winnowing their numbers would be much appreciated.'

Taughâsh Riders can be found throughout the Mirk-eaves.
Fuirgam has asked you to defeat the Taughâsh Riders that have been harassing the flanks of the Malledhrim soldiers invading the Mirk-eaves.

'Welcome to our temporary establishment, ${PLAYER}. You may rest here a short while, but pray do not get too comfortable. There is a task I would have you do.
'Several days ago, our host split in two, and half our numbers travelled south to explore the swamplands in the Drownholt. We have not heard from them since, but it is important that we establish some lines of communication with them.
'I do not think the distance is very far, but it will be a treacherous journey. There is no friendly creature in Mirkwood, randir -- not one. Laidhriel will receive you, when you find her. She travels among the southern host at Estolad Mernael.'
'Mae govannen. I am glad Athradnir sent you to us, mellon! There is much to be done in this drowned land, for we are beset by many troubles.'
Talk to Laidhriel in the Drownholt
The Drowned Wood
Athradnir, a Galadhrim stationed at the Haunted Inn, wishes to convey a message to Laidhriel at Estolad Mernael.

'The host you seek travelled south, into the part of the forest known as the Drownholt. You should speak with Laidhriel, who goes with them. It is best if we maintain communication with those stationed near us.'

The second part of the Golden Host set off south, to the drowned part of the wood known as the Drownholt.
You should seek Estolad Mernael, the camping place of the Elves in the Drownholt, so that the Elves stationed in the Dourstocks can maintain communication with their brethren nearby.
Collected wolf-pelts from the Darkrage wolves (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Do you hear the howling from the trees, ${PLAYER}? We hear them, but we cannot see them when they wish to be scarce -- nay, not even my long-sighted Elf-friends. The Darkrage wolves of Mirkwood are vicious beasts, and their attacks upon the Malledhrim are ceaseless.
'While they are no match for the Elves of Lórien, I believe they are acting on more than instinct. They harry us day and night and seem more bent on distracting our guards and archers than coming in for an actual kill. Such prey as we are not appealing to these beasts.
'I am not sure what motivates them, but I would see them hindered. You should venture into the Dourstocks and remove the harrying threat of these sly beasts. Please bring me as many hides as you can collect, and I will examine them for anything strange. At the very least, the furs will make hardy provisions for my kindred when I return to them.'

'Ah! The skins of the Darkrage wolves! I thank you, friend. I am glad you were able to hunt so many without being hunted yourself. Now, let us see....'
Prestadír takes a hide and examines it long. It seems to be of interest to him, though you cannot perceive that it is anything extraordinary.
'Did you observe the strange pattern of the skin? There are subtle striations all over it, as if branded. I believe these beasts are in the service of the Necromancer.'
'How many wolves have you killed thus far? They can be found throughout the woods near here.'
Collect wolf-pelts from the Darkrage wolves (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring the wolf-pelts to Prestadír
The Sly Beasts of the Dourstocks

Darkrage wolves wander the Dourstocks, harassing the Malledhrim and their efforts. These bold creatures attack at every opportunity, then swiftly vanish into the black trees beyond the sight of the sharp-eyed Elves.
'The wolves can be found all throughout the Dourstocks. If you do not find them, it is likely that they will come to find you. Keep your wits about you, ${PLAYER}! This is a deadly wood.'

Darkrage wolves can be found throughout the Dourstocks and in Audaghaim.
The Ranger Prestadír has asked you to collect the pelts of several of the evil wolves that harass the Malledhrim-guards.

Prestadír can be found in the Haunted Inn in the Dourstocks, near the abandoned village of Audaghaim.
You should bring the wolf-pelts you have collected to Prestadír, for he wishes to examine them.

'You handled yourself very well against the Orcs, swine, and wolves. I think that you may be able to assist my Deputy.
'He headed out to the camp on the far eastern side of Minas Eriol. He is watching over one of the workers there and the brother of that ornery fellow, Gadaric.
'If you are interested in helping him out with the tasks I put before him, seek him at the camp on the far eastern edge of Minas Eriol.'

'Bram sent me help?
'He sent me here to watch over this hobbit -- Old Mugwort -- who is proving to be far more difficult to watch than I like. He also wanted me to make certain that this fellow Hunulf was kept safe.
'Then I receive a message from him that he wants all these other problems handled and... well, thankfully you are here now.'
Talk to Deputy Osmann
My Deputy
Constable Bram Ashleaf, satisfied with your assistance, has another task for you.

'Finding the camp may be a bit difficult. You need to head east along the road until it climbs steeply as it passes by Weathertop. When that happens follow the southern vale and wrap down toward the south and east. You should find it hidden up on a rise near the eastern entrance to Minas Eriol.'

Deputy Osmann is at the camp on the east side of Minas Eriol.
Constable Bram Ashleaf sent you to aid his deputy. He thinks that you will be able to see that the deputy keeps his charges safe and also assist him in his various tasks.

'Thus far you have proven true to your word. My judgment, however, is often clouded by my passion, and for this reason, I will send you on to my brother. He will know whether you are true of intent.
'You will find him by following the roadway east to where it begins to rise. There is a vale to the south that will lead to the back side of Minas Eriol. He is encamped there with others.
'Pass his test... perhaps you will earn our trust and earn passage to speak with one who knows much of what transpires now in these lands.'

'Gadaric sent you on to me? This is good news. My brother sought vengeance, it is true, and I swear to you just. We lost many when the goblins came here.
'Many are gone and still lost to us... it is good that you are here and willing to aid us.'
Talk to Hunulf Munce
My Brother Hunulf
Gadaric, feeling that your efforts have been honest and true, believes you may be able to assist his brother Hunulf.

'Seek out my brother, Hunulf, encamped at the east edge of Minas Eriol. You should follow the road eastward until it climbs steeply. Follow the path through the valley south of the road, then continue east towards the encampment.
'Speak with Hunulf. He will know how to better test you.'

Hunulf Munce is at the camp on the eastern side of Minas Eriol.
Gadaric Munce sent you to speak with his brother Hunulf.
Defeated Lûz

'Since you are headed north-east into the goblin infested hills and vales, I think I ought to ask you one more favour and issue you one more warning.
'There are Wargs among the goblins, and a good many of them. Old Mugwort -- a dear friend of mine and the cook here at The Forsaken Inn -- hates them fiercely. I hate the goblins, though, and seeing that I do, I want you to be mindful of the pack-master, Lûz.
'If you see him, steel your nerve and grab your steel. It will be a difficult battle, but you should defeat him. When you do, return to me with news of the fight!'

'Ha! What great news to know that such a menace has been dealt with so swiftly! You have proven that you are truly a good ally to the people in this inn. I wonder if there is any more that I can have you do....'
Defeat Lûz

Goblin Pack-master
Lieva Dourlily asked you to keep a watchful eye out for a goblin leading not only the goblins, but the many Wargs that bolster their number.

'I like hounds. Hounds can be friendly, and they say were once noble beasts. But these Wargs are big hulking beasts, larger and meaner than other wolves. We cannot allow the pack-master, Lûz, to continuing raising these beasts! Get out there and deal with him.'

Seek out the goblin, Lûz, at the goblin-camps north-east of The Forsaken Inn.
Lieva Dourlily told you to be wary of the goblin pack-master, Lûz, and requested that you defeat him if you find him.

'Over the years, as we have studied and collected the items left in these ruins, we have earned a living for our people. Many of the goods that will help to purchase much needed items for our folk have been lost in the spiders' lairs over the years.
'If you are already entering the valley to assist us with the spiders, then I would ask that you take the time to reclaim these valuable treasures for us. You will likely find them wrapped in thick webbing, scattered throughout the valley floor.
'Cut through the webbing and find the valuable items and return them to me.'

'These treasures do not appear to be more than old tarnished coins, but they are valuable to many collectors. Customers from Bree will often purchase them from us by bartering food or other goods for these coins. Any soul diligent enough to search through these ruins will sooner or later stumble upon many of these coins.
'The Half-orcs in the north scour the ruins even now in such an effort.'

'You will find that the treasures once carried by many of my people have tumbled into the valley beneath Minas Eriol. There, they have become trapped in the spiders' webs. Sift through the webs and collect these treasures. It will ease some of our difficulties.'
Talk to Hunulf Munce
Collect Eglan-treasures (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Lost in Their Webs
Hunulf Munce told you of many valuable treasures lost in the webs of the spiders beneath Minas Eriol.

Beneath the ruins of Minas Eriol, to the west of Hunulf's encampment, lay a den of spiders. Many goods and valuables, necessary for the Eglain's continued livelihood have gone missing within.
Hunulf asked you to make your way into the dangerous valley beneath the goblin infested ruin of Minas Eriol. He warned that spiders there are in possession of many Eglan-treasures that must be recovered for his people.

'When the goblins came into Minas Eriol there was panic. Many ran towards the savages, and others fled through the valley beneath the ruins, hoping to escape the spears and sharp teeth of the goblins, only to fall prey to the spiders beneath.
'Those that entered the valley and did not emerge must be burned. It is only fair to save their bodies from the terror that awaits them. If you are willing, I will ask that you burn the corpses of the fallen.
'You will find the entrance to the valley north and to the west at the front of Minas Eriol, or over the bridge and through the goblins to the west.'

'The lost will not be forgotten. The goblins have wrought much pain upon my people, but not as much as others. The spiders in these lands are filled with true malice and an intelligence unseen.
'Your efforts give my mind some measure of ease. Thank you.'

'You can enter the spider's vale through the northern entrance, through the goblin-infested ruins west over the bridge, or through the eastern corridor to the north of the ruin-entrance there. Please, see that the dead are given proper rites.'

'My friend, as that is what I think of you, there is something that I wish to share. In the east, there is a ruin which dwarves have long pilfered. We stayed far away from them as they have oft been filled with ire and anger toward the Eglain.
'Not long ago, a contingent of dwarf-kind stopped in Ost Guruth for the briefest of time. Some, enthralled by tales of the dwarves in the ruins asked to remain in these lands to investigate.
'Since this time they have found an underground ruin where they say they are closing in on secrets about their cousins living there. If you are interested in aiding them, you will find them at a place just north of the ruins to the east within a cave mouth cut into a tall mound.'

'Hunulf sent you? Good Man, he. It is true that the two within this cavern came from the West. I came here long ago and live among the Eglain, but duty tells me to come with these cousins of mine and aid them in their search.

'Greetings, ${PLAYER}! I hope that you are well.
'Within the depths of Sarnúr, there are tales of lost lore remaining still within the halls. There are those that believe that the Dourhands are searching the area for pieces of faded parchment that are scattered about. Please travel to Sarnúr yourself, recover these pieces of faded parchment, and return to me with them.
'Sarnúr can be found south of Thorin's Hall, deep beyond the ruins of Orodost, which is located on the western mountains of Ered Luin.'

'Thank you for journeying into that dark place and returning the scrolls.
'I will begin to decipher the runes that are found on this collection of parchment.
'If you journey to Sarnúr again, I may ask that you seek out more of these parchments.'
Collect faded parchment (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Rútur in Thorin's Hall
Gathering Ancient Scrolls
There are rumours that ancient scrolls remain in Sarnúr from the days before the great cities of the Dourhands were destroyed by the great cataclysm which tore Ered Luin.
'I am sure you will find many scraps of ancient scrolls in the ruins of Sarnúr.'

Pieces of faded parchment can be found in Sarnúr, south of Thorin's Hall, reached through the ruins of Orodost.
Rútur has asked you to recover any pieces of faded parchment you might find in Sarnúr.

Rútur is in Thorin's Hall, north of Sarnúr, just outside the Blue Stone Garrison.
Now that you possess the pieces of faded parchment that Rútur requested you gather, you should return them to him so that he may decipher them.
Destroyed supply-crates (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'The battle goes well thus far, ${PLAYER}, but the Orcs in the nearby fortresses are proving tenacious. It seems they have also laid in supplies for a prolonged siege, should it come to that... but we cannot afford to be tied down here for so long, or the might of Dol Guldur shall push us back into the Anduin!
'We bid you fight your way into those camps and destroy their supplies. This will both weaken their defence and ensure that none of them are able to retreat with valuable stores back to their dark tower.
'When you have completed this task, return here to me for further instructions.'

'The supplies have been destroyed? Well done, ${PLAYER}. Without those supplies of arrows and provisions, the Orcs will not be able to hold out much longer...and the rest of our forces are coming ashore and moving further into the forest as we speak.'
Destroy supply-crates (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Fuirgam's Aide at Echad Sirion
Foreword: Out of Supply
The Taughâsh tribe defending the Mirk-eaves against the Malledhrim rely heavily upon stores brought to their encampments before the invasion began.

'While we seek to destroy the Enemy's supplies, our own stocks are in complete disarray.
'Poor Amrúnwen was caught totally unaware by Celeborn's sudden order for an attack and has been struggling mightily to put all in order, but the scale of our assault is of too great a scope, and she cannot possibly maintain the line.
'At least this battle shall not last overly long, and so if we must go hungry, it will only be for days, not weeks. I am more worried about our medicines and poultices, which we have great need of.'

Supplies can be found at Durbúrz-stazg to the north of Echad Sirion and Fállug to the south.
Fuirgam has asked you to find and destroy the supply-crates in the Orc-fortifications of the Mirk-eaves.

Fuirgam's Aide is at Echad Sirion, on the eastern banks of the Anduin.
You should return to him with news of your success.
Defeated goblin-runners (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'I have a little challenge for you, ${PLAYER}! Do you see all of those Orc-fortifications out there? They communicate with each other through trained runners -- goblins, usually -- who carry messages from one to another. Defeat those messengers, and their communication will be disrupted.
'If you are fortunate, you might even capture a message or two from them, though they usually memorize the information they are supposed to deliver to avoid such issues.
'When you have done as I have asked, return to me here.'

'So, were you able to learn anything from the goblin-runners? No?
'Do not fret. They are rarely entrusted with anything of import, and this stage of the battle should not last long enough for anything we learned from them to matter much.
'Our main goal is to cut them off from each other and leave them disorganized, and in that, you have performed admirably.'
Defeat goblin-runners (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Ivorel at Echad Sirion
Expedition: Disrupting Communication

Communication between the Orc-fortifications scattered across the Mirk-eaves are handled by goblin-runners who rush messages from one to another. The defeat of these runners not only would cut the encampments off from each other, but may result in the interception of important information about the Enemy's movements.

'In recent years, my scouts have kept a watchful eye upon Dol Guldur, and in the past, the Lord and Lady have forbidden any assault upon it, believing the risk of defeat too great should our forces prove unable to tumble its obsidian walls.
'What counsel has changed their minds, I wonder? It must have something to do with our recent visitors from afar.'

Goblin-runners can be found throughout the Mirk-eaves.
Ivorel has asked you to intercept and defeat the goblin-runners that carry messages from camp to camp in the Mirk-eaves.

Ivorel is at Echad Sirion, on the eastern banks of the Anduin.
You should return to Ivorel with news of your success.
Defeated Stargûsh

'Ho there, ${PLAYER}. I have a challenge for you. You have journeyed into Fanuidhol and know what dangers we face in the Orcs of Moria. If we strike fear into their hearts, that threat may be lessened.
'What I would have you do is enter the camp of Bolg Maufulug and burn the standard of the Orcs there. With their banner in ashes, they will know that we are strong enough to defy them.
'Bolg Maufulug lies to the west and a little north of here. Be wary, though, for I do not doubt the camp is championed by a powerful Orc or other creature...if the champion arrives, defeat him as well. When you have done this deed, return to me.'
'You have burned the banner at Bolg Maufulug and defeated their champion? Well done, ${PLAYER}!'
Burn the banner at Bolg Maufulug and defeat Stargûsh

'A handful of our soldiers have gone missing and I fear they may have been cut off from our forces during the initial rush of the assault. Keep a watchful eye out for any of them while you are out in the Mirk-eaves and lend them whatever aid you can if you do come across them.
'They are skilled warriors in their own right, but there are a great many Orcs still roaming the area....'

'It seems that you have managed to recover our missing soldiers, ${PLAYER}. Excellent.

'Greetings, brave ${PLAYER}. It is good to see you.

'Greetings, ${PLAYER}. I wish to thank you for entering the caverns and dispatching those foul creatures.

Thievery and Mischief
While the Rangers of the North were distracted in the South, brigands and ruffians took an opportunity to wrest control of Bree....
The first step to driving the brigands out of Bree is to reclaim the South-gate and gain access to the city itself.

Defeated Angár Irongut

'The Dourhands must be stopped, and I am willing to bet that there is a leader among them who directs them to deal with the Orcs... a terrible cur who needs to be removed so that dwarves everywhere can hold their heads up with pride!
'This is my task. Find this leader, likely in some hidden passage or lair, eliminate him, then return to me.
'I think you should look first within Iorvinas... the ruins there would be an ideal lair for such a mongrel.'

'Already, I feel the fire of my blood beginning to cool. The fool Dourhands need to remember their place. It is bad enough what they did to Thorin's Hall.
'I and all dwarves of good repute owe you a debt of gratitude, ${PLAYER}. Take this and know that you have made a friend this day and wiped a black smudge from the world.'

'Find the leader of the Dourhands within Iorvinas and see that he is ended quickly and with prejudice. We cannot abide such curs to sully the names of the Seven Fathers!'

'We left the expedition moving towards the east to investigate what the Dourhands are doing here in the Lone-lands. We have seen both Orcs and dwarves in this place, and nothing here makes a dwarf feel welcome!
'Our fears are that the Orcs and Dourhands are trading with one another. Nay... we fear that they are working together, supplying one another with materials, tools and weapons, and we want a stop put to it!
'Go into the ruins below and see if you can find any Orc-made weapons on the Dourhands in the section to the west. Return to me if you find any. This will tell me plainly what we face.'

'I can hardly believe what I am seeing! Dwarves and Orcs are enemies! This is something that should never have occurred, never!
'Our cousins have fallen so far in these long years. Now it is clear to me that their leader must meet an end....'
'Have you found any proof yet? I am hoping that this is just a terrible circumstance, but something in my belly tells me otherwise.'

'He may have left his family's lands, but he remembers that he is first and foremost a dwarf! The Dourhands can no longer be considered part of the greater dwarf-kingdom, having fallen enough to live so close to Orcs without the sound of battle.
'Because of this, I am requesting that you lend us your aid. Defeat the Dourhands and the Orcs in this ruin and return to me.'
'I knew it! Fool Dourhands! We should rid the world of the lot of them! There must be a leader here... one that makes them do these things.'

'There is something within these walls, something of value. I can feel it! Orcs likely can too, and of course the Dourhands know, but they seem more interested in the ruins to the north and west.
'The Orcs are fine at making weapons and crude tools, but if my feeling is right, they require specific tools. I bet that is what the Dourhands are giving them.
'Hunt down the Orcs and see what they are getting from the Dourhands. Return to me when you have evidence that there is something going on between the Dourhands and Orcs in this ruin.'

'As I thought, sturdy and bearing the fine sharp point needed to cut new holes in thick stone. Orcs would rather use their swords and axes.
'This is ill news indeed, but it speaks to an issue that has long haunted the Dourhands and one that we can likely stop here and now. Logi will handle the issue with our ill-fated cousins.
'I want to focus on the Orcs and seeing that they fail at whatever nefarious purpose they have here.'
'Have you found anything? I am certain that the Orcs in this ruin will have some measure of evidence upon their being!'

Worried that the Dourhands and Orcs have struck some bargain, dwarves from an expedition to Rivendell have come westward to investigate a ruin.

Henir believes that there is something of value within the ruins where he hides. He does not think that the Orcs can get the materials on their own and wants to know if the Dourhands are providing them with tools needed for their work.

'The Orcs are working with the Dourhands? This is terrible news. The Orcs are recent arrivals in these lands and have been busy digging at a ruin in the east. They have slain many Eglain and taken another of the ruins that we once claimed as our own.
'Could it be that the Dourhands assisted them in this? Friend ${PLAYER}, will you make your way along the road to the east?
'Some distance down the road, you will find Ost Guruth and the leader of the Eglain, Frideric the Elder. Tell him this news.'

'This news is unwelcome. We knew only that these Orcs came from the north and west. They came under cover at night, lit fires at the ruins, and slaughtered our folk who were there.
'Since that time, they have turned their attentions east towards the great river and south to the mire. They leave the northern swamp for the Dead....
'You, ${PLAYER}, are in the home of the Eglain. We ask that you treat our people and the land about you with respect.'

'The rules are very simple -- race through each gate, and you mustn't fall off your steed before the time runs out. 'Do you feel up for this challenge? Only the most spirited riders should even attempt such a feat! It is sure to be very dangerous. I myself would never attempt such a thing!'

'The Eglain have always kept their distance from Nan Dhelu. The ruins have an ominous feel that cannot be avoided.
'Since coming to this location, I have fought against some of the creatures there and found that they carry treasures that will bring us much in the way of trade.
'While you are fighting against these foes, I would ask that you collect these items so that we may earn something from the aid you are providing.'

'Yes, these are a very valuable find. If we can determine that none of these are ruined or corrupted, then I think they will earn us a great deal of supplies from the traders in Bree-land.
'Thank you for this, ${PLAYER}.'

'I am certain that the wights within the ruins of Nan Dhelu are in posession of rare and valuable treasures. If you would search through their remains to find them while you fight in those ruins, the Egalin would be grateful.'

Collect valuable treasures (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Aid to Earn

The ruins of Nan Dhelu have often given the Eglain ill feelings, but the arrival or emergence of the Dead from within the ruins has them even more fearful. A brave warrior, Cwendreda, was sent to watch and learn about the ruins and her tasks now fall to you as terror begins to grow from within those once great halls.

Nan Dhelu lies to the north of the ruins of Dol Vaeg.
Cwendreda has asked you to keep a watchful eye out for any treasures that you may find within the ruins of Nan Dehlu. She believes that the wights within the ruins may carry them.
Defeated the Master of the Ruins

'Though I bear a great deal of pride, I can admit that I know fear, and no greater fear has come over me as seeing the Master of the Ruins. It roams Nan Dhelu with a skeletal wight at its side at all times and is itself a creature of extreme terror.
'Should you happen upon this creature, I would advise running. If you stay and fight and emerge victorious, tell me and I may offer you a reward.
'The Master of the Ruins wanders throughout the ruins and is never in one place too long.'

'Just knowing that the creature has been defeated brings a wisp of hope into my heart. You have done much to aid the Eglain this day, ${PLAYER}, and have done much to earn this.
'Thank you for all that you continue to do for my people.'
Defeat the Master of the Ruins
Talk to Cwendreda at Dol Vaeg
The Master of the Ruins

The ruins of Nan Dhelu have often given the Eglain ill feelings, but the arrival or emergence of the Dead from within the ruins has them even more fearful. A brave warrior, Cwendreda, was sent to watch and learn about the ruins, and her tasks now fall to you as terror begins to grow from within these once great halls.
'Be careful, ${PLAYER}. The Master of the Ruins is the most fearsome creature I have ever seen. Be wary as you wander through the ruins of Nan Dehlu.'

The Master of the Ruins wanders within the ruins of Nan Dhelu, north of Dol Vaeg.
Cwendreda warned you to be cautious while searching Nan Dhelu for the Master of the Ruins and offered you a reward should you defeat the monster.

Cwendreda is at Dol Vaeg.
Cwendreda awaits your return and the news that the Master of the Ruins has been defeated.

'A moment of your time, ${PLAYER}, but know that the task I will ask of you will take more than moments and set you on a course for true danger.
'Some time back, before the darkness spread from the east and north, we witnessed the arrival of the Dead at Nan Dhelu. We have often stayed afar of that place as something there always set unease upon us. Now, though, the evil emanating spreads fear throughout the people.
'I dispatched one of our strongest kinswomen to watch the ruins... she is there now with her companion who is there at the behest of Stanric. Should you wish to aid us further, make your way to the ruin of Dol Vaeg, east along the road and north to the highest hill, and assist her.'

'Frideric is a strong leader and wise. I have learned much just by watching the comings and goings within the ruins. I know that there is wealth to be gained from within that place as well.
'If you are here to help, then I will gratefully accept any help you offer.'
Talk to Cwendreda at Dol Vaeg
Supporting our Scouts
Frideric directed you to Cwendreda, located at the ruins of Dol Vaeg. The woman is there watching, tracking, and attempting to stave off the spread of the Dead from within the ruins of Nan Dhelu.
'Head east along the road and search for the highest hill in the north. Dol Vaeg is there.'

Make your way to the ruins of Dol Vaeg and speak with Cwendreda. The ruins are east and north of the Great East Road on a high hill.
Frideric the Elder, in an effort to further garner your help for the Eglain, sent you to Dol Vaeg to assist Cwendreda.
Defeated the Dead at Nan Dhelu (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'We know that there are a great number of Dead within this place. We have learned of these foul beings from our stone-speaker and our friend Radagast.
'We know that they are evil and that they hate all that live. I must ask that you make your way to the ruins and destroy the Dead there, for they are a blight on these lands and should be purged.
'You will find a great number of these creatures, some bloated, some barely sheathed in flesh, and others bereft of flesh within the borders of Nan Dhelu. Banish them from the ruins, then return to me.'

'This cannot have been an easy task. The Dead are creatures that inspire fear within the most courageous of hearts.
'We Eglain are indebted to you, ${PLAYER}. I offer you this meagre gift for your efforts.'

Evil in the Ruins
You have rescued one of the captured soldiers

'I fear that a few of our number have been captured by the Orcs, pathfinders who came across the river in silence before our attack to mark the landing spots and eliminate the Enemy's sentries.
'Most of them have returned since we began our assault in earnest, but a few have not, nor have we seen any sign of their bodies, which the Orcs would have left to rot had they been slain. Thus I must believe that they yet live and are held captive nearby...most likely in the central fortification upon Amon Angened, as they have not had time to move prisoners to Dol Guldur.
'However, once we assault that fortress in earnest, they would most certainly kill any prisoners held there. If you could manage to get them out before then, the Malledhrim would be in your debt.'
'So the rescue attempt was a success? My thanks to you, ${PLAYER}! Now Fuirgam can launch his assault upon that fortress without fear for our brethren.'

'Agorin sent you? Here?
'Well, I will not debate your bravery, friend ${RACE}, but let us fly swiftly!'
Rescue a captured soldier
Talk to Agorin at Echad Sirion
Expedition: A Daring Rescue

A few Elves who were among the first to cross the Anduin to make way for the main landing were captured by Orcs. If they are not rescued before the Malledhrim make their final assault upon Amon Angened, the prisoners will likely be killed.

'Hurry, ${PLAYER}! Fuirgam's assault upon the fortress will begin as soon as his forces are in position! If you cannot rescue our scouts from Amon Angened before he begins his attack, their fates are sealed.'

Elvish prisoners are being held in the Orc-fortress upon Amon Angened, south-east of Echad Sirion.
Agorin has asked you to mount the rescue of Elvish prisoners from their Orc-captors.

Agorin is at Echad Sirion, on the eastern bank of the Anduin.
You should return to Agorin with news of your success.
Destroyed Orc-catapults (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Destroyed Orc-ballistae (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'We are nearly ready for a decisive assault upon Amon Angened, but my men have warned me that a set of siege-engines lies in wait, looking upon the steep paths that we must scale to take the fortress.
'To muster an assault under the rain of such dark engines would result in needless death and might even cause our assault to falter.
'If you can destroy those engines before we begin the assault, the Orcs will have no choice but to face us in battle, where our valour shall prove unmatched!'

'You need say nothing, ${PLAYER}. I witnessed the smoke rising from the burning engines of the Orcs with my own eyes.
'We shall begin the assault shortly. Before night falls, the Mirk-eaves shall be in our hands, and we shall continue our march upon Dol Guldur.'
Destroy Orc-catapults (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Destroy Orc-ballistae (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

Foreword: Engines of War

The approach to the Orc-fortress atop Amon Angened is watched by many siege-engines based at the Gostannon. If those engines cannot be destroyed before the Malledhrim's attack, the Golden Host will suffer grievious casualties beneath the hail of bolts and stones.

'It has been many long years since the Malledhrim have gone to war afield, ${PLAYER}. Such engines as the Enemy fields against us now seemed a distant, unpleasant memory... but too well do we recall their power.
'We will face many such as we approach Dol Guldur, so be on your guard.'

Siege-engines can be found at the Gostannon Orc-camp, north-east of Echad Sirion.
Fuirgam has asked you to destroy the Orkish siege-engines in the Mirk-eaves.

Fuirgam's Aide is at Echad Sirion, on the eastern banks of the Anduin, south-west of the Gostannon.
You should return to him with news of your success.
Jammed the gate mechanism

'We must ensure that the commanders in Dol Guldur cannot get reinforcements into the Mirk-Eaves during our assault upon the fortress.
'Any large number of troops would have to come through the Gostannon, the gate upon the road that leads to the east. The Orcs still control it for now, but I am certain that we will soon capture it as well.
'For the moment, I need you to see that the gate is made useless to them. Try to jam the mechanism by which it is raised and lowered on this side. It will not slow them down for long, but by then our assault will be complete and the Mirk-eaves will be ours.'

'The Gostannon has been jammed?
'That will not slow the Orcs down for long, but it does not have to. Within hours, the Enemy's fortification up there will have fallen, and I will welcome any assault they care to waste against us there.'
Jam the gate mechanism
Talk to Fuirgam's Aide at Echad Sirion
Foreword: Barring the Gate
The Gostannon guards the way between the Mirk-eaves and the Dourstocks in the east. It allows the Enemy passage to reinforce their armies in the Mirk-eaves.

'Our scouts tell us that the roads that lay between here and Dol Guldur are poorly defended. If we can take the fortress and that gate before the day is out, the Enemy will not be able to field forces quickly enough to prevent us from advancing at least as far as the ruins of Ost Galadh.'

The Gostannon lies in the north-west corner of the Mirk-eaves, some distance to the east of Echad Sirion.

'He is large and thick at the legs, bearing the look of a warrior and the strength of many. He is called Galrîp, and he is the leader of the trolls in Harloeg. What a gift it would be to know that he was defeated.
'A gift worthy of lasting peace, it would be. He will wander through the swamps of the south. He will hide among the trees and his brethren and be difficult to face.'

'It is done then. While our homes are lost, the creature responsible for our exile is no more, and we can find peace here in these lands. The Wargs and Orcs will prove more a nuisance than a danger.

'I, too, am interested in what you had to tell of the graveyard. I find I am ill at ease in this place, and my curiosity has been raised by your tale of the stones in the plot below. The Elves care not for the troubles of Men long departed from this world, but they hold a great interest for me.
'East of here, across the bridge, you will find a town that fell long ago. I believe it was called Audaghaim, and there are many shades there. Fell spirits of the Enemy do not trouble me, but I believe there is something more to this place, and I wish to know what it is.
'Will you confront the shades? I do not think they are wholly evil. Perhaps they bear some knowledge that will reveal what befell this place.'

'Now, this is a bewildering find. Let me see those.'
'These coins, as you have surely noticed, are tokens of fealty to the Necromancer in Dol Guldur. They are from nearly six hundred years ago, when this simple town of woodsmen was filled with warm-blooded folk, and not the cold spirits that linger in cursed rage.
'These were gifts, and some pact was exchanged with Dol Guldur. What happened here? What cruel fate has made these people linger to fill the very air with such wicked dread?'
'I do not like this feeling of unease that has settled upon my shoulders. Have you spoken to any shades?'

'The Dark Lord has a remarkable talent for corrupting nearly all that is good, but even he cannot doom mortal Men to remain cursed after death by association alone. Such a curse would only take hold for the deepest of betrayals, when the hearts of Men are willingly inclined to evil...only by the greatest of Powers can the spirits of Men be held to this world.
'These tokens of fealty are surely only the beginning of the story. The Necromancer persuaded his woods-dwelling neighbours to swear allegiance to him, but what after that? I have my suspicions. One hears oft of such tales.
'You should search the rubble of the town and see if any history can be found. Perhaps there are records kept by these Woodmen in the months preceding or following the intrusion of Dol Guldur.'

'Ah! This is just what I was hoping for. I am not surprised that someone took the time to bury it. Many pages are missing, as you can see, as is the case with many aged books, but these were deliberately ripped out.
'Is it not a fine coincidence that the pages that were removed are from TA 2461, and the same week that marks the \qaccidental\q deaths of many folks who rest in the graveyard yonder?
'I would dearly like to find those missing pages, or at least hear the account that is missing from this book.'
'Have you found anything of interest?'

'Our brethren, long sleeping in the earth, are now taken from their slumber by fell spirits out of the past, spirits called by their master to march by his side in the fortress of Garth Agarwen.
'Now they stir where once they slumbered. West, once our home, now in ruins, the Dead walk anew. Our time is short to strike back against the past, but perhaps thou art willing to aid us?'

'We draw closer now to release. We will know that it is by the hands of others that our opportunity for freedom was given.
'Know thou, that we will in our eternal slumber be as eternally grateful.'

Talk to Narthan at Ost Haer
Pushing Back the Past

Before the dawn of the Third Age, the kingdoms of Rhudaur, Arthedain, and Cardolan stood in opposition to one another at the cross-roads of the Lone-lands. As Rhudaur fell to vile corruption, some Men of Arthedain were held responsible for the desecration of the land and they have long waited to see a time when they could make amends for their greatest failures.
'The Dead walk again in the ruins to the west. Seek them there and end them.'

There are wights in the ruins west of Ost Haer.

'Should you enter that place... search for my ring. Though it cannot end this curse, perhaps I will recall the joy that once filled my heart.
'I fear that it now rests upon the finger of one of the bloated creatures within the ruins or southern bog.'
'Were there warmth to one such as I, I would know it again. I will treasure this little bit thou hast done for me. I will recall thine efforts always.'
'I fear that the ring is in the possession of the bloated wights within the ruins or southern bog.'

Something Yet to be Found

Before the dawn of the Third Age, the kingdoms of Rhudaur, Arthedain, and Cardolan stood in opposition to one another at the cross-roads of the Lone-lands. As Rhudaur fell to vile corruption, some of the Men of Arthedain were held responsible for the desecration of the land, and they have long waited to see a time when they could make amends for their greatest failures.

Narthan's ring might be found upon one of the wights roaming west of Ost Haer.

Defeated Gostoth

'Of deeds, we were the same. In name, we shared our last. Lost to us through death, returned to us through the shadow which grows in this land. He is not what he was. There is no memory there, there is no knowledge of what came before, but the body rises and must be laid to rest.
'I speak of our brethren, but not so. I truly speak of the thing called Gostoth which wanders the depths of the ruins west of Ost Haer.
'Seek thou this creature and destroy it, lest it plague us still.'
'Rest again, dear friend. Rest at last. With effort, we shall soon join you and know the peaceful slumber for which we yearn.'

'Mae govannen, Elf-friend, and welcome to our meagre refuge. You may tarry here, if you wish, but I think you may be of some use to me ere we depart this place.
'Have you ventured north and beheld the ruined walls of the Elves who lived here long ago? We ourselves have only espied them from a safe distance, but some of our scouts did go that way and have not returned. There are merrevail who live there now; all the signs are there -- the filth, the intense evil in the very air....
'I suspect that there are great hoards of relics beyond those sinister walls. The filth of the merrevail dulls all things fair, but they care for treasures with a fierce jealousy. I believe there will be memories of the Elves among the foul refuse. Will you search the ruins for treasures of worth? These relics belong in the possession of the Elves, where they can be properly attended.'
'How odd! Was there really nothing of worth -- nothing at all? I was sure that the merrevail there were guarding something. I am still not convinced that there is nothing of worth there.'
Search treasure-piles for relics of worth (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

Filth and Riches

Mírdiniel of the Malledhrim is interested in the Elf-ruins to the north, especially because of their close proximity to Lothlórien. She wishes to recover relics of the Elves who lived there to learn more of them.
'The ruins you seek are to the north of here -- Dannenglor, I believe they are called. The name is known to me, but the history is not.'

'I am glad that you have come to our aid, my good ${RACE}. As our path leads us through Mirkwood, we see many evil things which we wish to make right. Alas that we have not the resources for such a great undertaking. Even the smallest good deeds must often go undone, for our eyes are fixed upon one target only.
'Dannenglor was once an Elven-home and is overrun now by shrieking beasts of all kinds. The merrevail and mervyl are violations of nature, and even the bats of this forest are unwholesome and evil.
'If you wish to make Mirkwood a little better on behalf of the Galadhrim who must pass through it, you should cleanse those ruins of the vile swarms of bats that give strength to the presence of the merrevail. Will you do this for us? Dannenglor will never be fair again, but you can perhaps begin to cast the evil from within its walls.'
'I am glad to see you well after your venture into Dannenglor...and not a scratch upon you! You have done a considerable kindness to all the Elves of Middle-earth, ${PLAYER}; you have my thanks!'

'This will not do. I believe that the most important treasures left behind by our brethren will be found on the merrevail themselves. You should return at once to Dannenglor and wrest what you can from the hideous beasts!
'Be very careful, for the mervyl and merrevail are deadly foes. The ruins, as you know, are fraught with peril. You should defeat enough merrevail to get a sense of what sort of treasures they bear.
'When you have collected a fair number of relics, you should bring them to me. I will be able to tell more about the Elves who were here before and perhaps discern some of the history of this place.'

'Well done, ${PLAYER}! I see that you had more success this time. I should have guessed that the filthy beasts would have kept the dearest treasures for themselves, for they have no wish to share among one another. Such is not the nature of these wicked foes.
'Why, these are interesting -- mere crumbs from the treasure that precedes them! I should dearly like to find the source; such an object would be sacred in Lórien and would be properly tended and honoured by the Elves, as it was meant to be.'
'Have you found anything of value on the merrevail?'

'The western stretches of this poisoned land teem with creatures long dead, now stalking the ruins.
'It is not fear that drives this request, but an instinct to survive. These creatures must be destroyed. Enter the swamp to the north and west or even some smaller sections of the east and destroy the wights who have so recently stirred back to action.'

'Knowing that you have destroyed as many of these creatures as you have gives me a moment to consider that we will once again reclaim these lands as the shade Dannasen states.

'${PLAYER}, you have come for me at last! I did not dare to hope for rescue, but I cannot deny that I am pleased to see you!
'You need to make ready for our escape -- pick up some of these barrels of nightshade and bring them out into the hall. If any additional guards are on their way, the fumes from the nightshade should render them unconscious!
'Let me know when you have adequately prepared, my friend! At that time we will make our escape!'

'We have made it into the dungeons, ${PLAYER}, and now it is up to you to find and rescue Bori. We believe he is being held in a cell in the East Wing.
'We have managed to keep our infiltration silent thus far, and some of the guards in the East Wing may be asleep on the job. Let them sleep and rescue Bori!'
'We ran into some trouble without you, ${PLAYER}, but victory is ours this day! Let us leave this grim dungeon!'
'Let us be free of these dungeons! I am ready to see the sun again, or as much of the sun as can be seen beneath the trees of Mirkwood.'

'I am ready to be free of this place, ${PLAYER}! Let us leave these dungeons behind us!

'These small treasures almost certainly came from a priceless Elven creation, a treasure beyond treasures, and a gift to the memory of the Elves who walked here once. Such a prize should not be left to be swallowed by filth and corruption.
'Once more, ${PLAYER}, I must encourage you to go on a quest for a relic of my ancient kindred. I do not think the acorn will have fallen far from the oak. I believe this greater treasure is still somewhere in Dannenglor, waiting to be reclaimed by those who will return it to its proper glory.
'Go to Dannenglor once again, if you dare. This treasure will surely not be unguarded, so go with care. You will have done a great deed for my kindred if you manage to return to me in triumph. Good fortune to you, mellon!'

'Two young and headstrong youths of the Eglain, Elsa and Eriac, entered Agamaur with a small company. They sought to find the power behind the threat to their people, but if the Gaunt-lord Ivar has come to Agamaur, I fear they face a power they cannot overcome. They need your help.
'The Red Swamp is divided into two regions. The southern marshes, Haragmar, you know. Elsa and Eriac entered Agamaur, the northern marshes, through the Red-pass. It is a passage known only to the Eglain... and myself.
'I will accompany you, for the shadow that has come to Agamaur is too powerful for you to deal with alone. There is no telling what evil awaits us in the swamp. Return to me when you are prepared to leave.'
'Thank you again for your aid, ${PLAYER}. You should speak now with Radagast the Brown; he is waiting for you within the tower here in the camp.'
'Yes, yes, this shall do nicely. I shall remain here and help the Eglain fight against Ivar. I cannot allow innocent creatures to be used for such evil purposes.'
Talk to Radagast the Brown at Ost Guruth
Talk to Elsa in Agamaur
Talk to Radagast the Brown in Agamaur
Book 2, Chapter 15 (Solo): The Red-pass
Radagast told you that members of the Eglain, led by Elsa and Eriac, had entered Agamaur, the northern marshes of the Red Swamp.
'You should speak now with Radagast; he is inside the tower here in the camp.'

'Are you prepared to leave? Good! We must go at once... I fear time is running short for our young Eglain friends.'
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTE: This instance can only be completed solo. You must not be in a fellowship to begin this instance.</rgb>

Radagast the Brown is in the tower at the end of the main avenue in Ost Guruth.
Radagast the Brown waits to lead you into the passage to Agamaur. When you are prepared to leave, you should speak with Radagast again.

Elsa is in the camp within the ruins.
You should speak with Elsa about your victory within Agamaur.

The Eglain and the shades of Arthedain have established a small encampment within the ruins. Elsa of the Eglain waits to speak with you.
Your battle against Ivar's darkwater was a victory, or so it appears. The Gaunt-lord retreated into the north, pursued by Radagast the Brown, and has not been seen since.

'That creature commands great power, but against a heart full of hope and trust in one's allies, such power means nothing. Thank you for your help here, my friend. We have done well this day. Ivar's spreading corruption is stayed, at least for the moment.
'I must return now to the Eglain-encampment and help end this evil forever. There is more that you ought to do here, if you are willing. But we will not speak of such matters now.'

'Neven orders me to hold my post, and I must obey. He is our commander. I am under his charge, as are my men. Honour binds us, even greater than the curse of Iarwain Ben-adar.
'I will not forsake my commander, though he is so very changed. I cannot disobey his orders while he remains. If thou wish us to fight, thou must entreat with Neven. His seat is to the north.'

'We were beaten. There is no way to hide this. This Ivar commands the water, the wights, the forest itself. He cannot be beaten by my meagre force, and I fear there is something far more terrible within the ruins to the north.
'I know there is little time before a great evil spills forth from Garth Agarwen. Our only hope is Radagast, only he will be able to stop this Ivar. Please, go north to the gate of Garth Agarwen with him. Stop the Gaunt-lord Ivar.'
'Shall we return to the Eglain-encampment now?'

'We must go west to the Eglan-encampment. Elsa and Eriac will be waiting, and I can better attend to the corruption from there.
'The power which continues to corrupt this swamp is terrible, but we may not have to face it alone. The beasts tell me that there are shades of Emelin's kind which dwell here and may be convinced to aid the Eglain. I do not know why they do not remain with their own kind, but they at least have not brought harm to the Eglain.
'Now, we must hurry... the very trees scream in pain. I must see what I can do to help them as quickly as possible. Follow me, though I cannot promise aid, for I fear I will need all of my strength to face Ivar the Blood-hand.'

'A wight, a fell creature of Angmar... how could I have not seen this? So long have I lingered in this swamp, cursed by Iarwain Ben-adar to bring the salvation -- or the destruction -- of the Red-maid, she who dwells within Garth Agarwen, a Power now under the influence of the gaunt-men.
'I was blind to what Neven had become. Now, I shall make amends. Now, we shall make our battle and strive to fulfil our curse.'

'Hurry now, the Gaunt-lord Ivar is not far from here, near the gates of Garth Agarwen to the north. He may not reveal himself immediately, so we may need to draw him forth.
'The way ahead will be difficult, but do not give up hope. We shall triumph this day if we do not lose heart!'

Ruins of the ancient kingdom of Rhudaur, twisted by time and the touch of a dark evil, lay before you. Alongside Radagast the Brown, you must find Elsa and Eriac and assist them against the Gaunt-lord, Ivar the Blood-hand, and his undead minions.
'I will not forsake my commander, though he is so very changed. I cannot disobey his orders while he remains. If thou wish us to fight, thou must entreat with Neven. His seat is to the north.'
'Elsa and I fought as best we could, but there were too many wights. Speak with Elsa. She may know how we should proceed against the evil in Agamaur.'

'We lost so many. The wights, there were too many. The Gaunt-lord... the Gaunt-lord cannot be defeated.
'We should flee... I-I am sorry. Speak with Elsa, my will is too badly shaken to speak more.'

Speak to Radagast to see if there is something else he would have you do.

'I can hardly believe it! You actually made the journey all they way to Forochel and fought that beast?

'Listen closely, ${PLAYER}. It seems those oh-so-wise Elves in Rivendell have managed to get their trousers in a bunch over some great squalling lizard that has made a nest in the mountains above the House of Elrond.
'More to the point, they are offering a nice sum for anyone brave enough to rid them of it! Rothlúg is its name, and they say it only attacks in the midst of a great storm, so keep your eyes open.
'Oh, and you had best bring friends if you want to survive...otherwise I'll just save you the trouble and send your portion of the bounty straight off to the casket-maker in Trestlebridge....'

'It is a strange scale indeed...I've not seen its like before.

'The only news I have is that he usually lurks in the forests of the Trollshaws, somewhere north of the road, near some statues or the like? I heard that third-hand, and it didn't make much sense to me, but I hope it helps.'

'My, my...now that's a club all right. I wonder where he found that? It's sure as silver that he didn't forge it himself, and no Man nor Orc could ever wield it.

'Good day, ${PLAYER}. Are you looking for some work? Well, here's a nasty bit of business that needs tending to....

'What is this? A crystal?

'So, it appears that someone kept a faithful record, but this record was not to the liking of those who carried out the murders.
'If you are still invested in the story of this town, you should look into finding the missing pages. Perhaps they have been destroyed, and perhaps not.
'But where to start? In the case of hidden relics, sometimes it is best to start where you began. That blank gravestone was the first thing to rouse my interest in this mystery, and perhaps it can tell us more now.'

'I should have stood with the four who resisted, but I did not. I watched it all happen. Only when they had perished did I feel the effects of the true evil that was at work in Audaghaim. Too late did I record the truth.
'When they found what I had written, they came after me as well. I anticipated them. Here is a copy of the truth that was destroyed. Let this be my last effort on behalf of the true heroes of Audaghaim who resisted the evil corruptions of the Necromancer. Our blindness was our undoing!
'Yes -- the Necromancer came and promised much, and we saw the opportunity for progress and prosperity. The four that stood against him attacked the altar, and we cut them down in the name of Dol Guldur. They cursed us as they fell.
'Ah! My oath is fulfilled, my redemption nigh....'

'Ah! You have found the lost pages! I am astounded. May I take a look?
'At last, the truth -- and so it all comes together. Some of the townsmen resisted, and they were executed by their own folk. That settles the mystery. The guilty shade you spoke to before was the one who led the movement to accept the Necromancer's advances here. He was also the one who led in the murders.
'Everything is documented in this account, until the Record-keeper writes of his own guilt for not standing up for his fallen townsfolk. Here he writes that he knows his enemy will destroy the truth and execute him as well. This is the last entry by his hand.'
'Have you found anything of interest yet?'

'So, we are armed at least with the knowledge that there is a mystery. The shade's words were very contrary to the stark reality to which we bear witness today.
'There is much evidence that these accursed folk became tied to the Dark Lord in the second year of his sojourn at Dol Guldur, but we must now look deeper. We have given the shades a chance to tell their own story, but it seems that they wish the truth hidden from us.
'You should search everything but the shades themselves when you go to Audaghaim this time. Seek some evidence of the Necromancer's influence and search for any signs of violence...or perhaps a stockpile of weapons. If you can find these things, we will gain more understanding of the events that occurred here.'

'Ah...I think I see. How sad! But I suspected it would be something of this nature. There was murder in this town...of that you have seen strong evidence.
'Here is what I think the condemned shade meant when he said that many of his folk were set in their ways, and that change was coming: The change was the Dark Lord, and some Men resisted.
'I believe the shades trapped here have done their best to pretend the evil events never happened, though it means their redemption will never be achieved. Even the gravestones lie. These shades believe that all is as it was just before the Necromancer corrupted them. The murders are buried, collectively hidden. All were guilty, and all are determined to deny the truth.'

'Despite the losses, our assault upon Dol Guldur must be judged a success, ${PLAYER}, if not a lasting one. An army marches from the East to reinforce the fortress, and the Golden Host cannot hope to stand against the combined might of this new army and the Orcs already within Mirkwood.
'But we can sting this latter force, sting them with our arrows and the bite of our blades, and make them count the days until their reinforcements arrive. This we must do, ${CLASS}.
'Make the climb once again to Dol Guldur and slay Orcs within its bounds. Find too the locations where great concentrations of the Enemy reside, the entrances to the Warg-pens, the Sword-hall, and the Dungeons of Dol Guldur.'
'The Orcs must be counting the days until their reinforcements from the East arrive, ${PLAYER}! This is no lasting victory, to be certain, but it tastes sweet all the same!'

'The Golden Host has assaulted the fortress of Dol Guldur, but now we wait for the hammer-blow to fall. We do not have the numbers to stand long against the armies that approach from the East, so we must do what we can before the Enemy's counterattack.
'Scouts report that among the Orc-camps in Gathbúrz, numerous enemy forces have been seen entering a cavern in the hills. Many of the Orcs carry barrels full of some odorous substance with them into this cave. They call this place Gath Ulunn, and our scouts fear the Orcs are using this cavern as a hatchery for breeding worms.
'Find Gath Ulunn and defeat Orcs and worms alike within its passages. Tip over any of the barrels you see within the cave, ${PLAYER}. We must hinder these breeding efforts soon, lest we face an army of worms as well as an army of Orcs! You may wish to have a few allies with you, for Gath Ulunn is sure to be crawling with both Orcs and worms!'

'It pleases me to know that you have dealt with the threat of Gath Ulunn. The Orcs will be unable to raise enough worms now to threaten the Golden Host while still we remain within sight of Dol Guldur.
'You have given us a great gift with this deed, ${PLAYER}: the gift of time. I thank you for it.'

'It grieves me to tell you this, ${PLAYER}, but Sigileth of the Hidden Guard fell during the assault on Dol Guldur. She fought bravely, and slew countless Orcs, but in the end, Lanchigil and Egnassigil availed her not. I retrieved them from the body of a slain Olog-hai.
'Sigileth was given to carving a notch in the hilts of her knives when one of them delivered a killing stroke -- there would not be sufficient space on the hilts left following her final stand in the fortress of Dol Guldur.
'She desired to make a gift of the knives to Lord Celeborn when the hilts were full of such marks. Will you deliver Lanchigil and Egnassigil to him? It is what Sigileth would want.'

'It saddens me to know that Sigileth of the Hidden Guard will not return to this land she loved. She knew the dangers she faced and wrote the tale of her victories on the hides of Orcs with her beloved knives.'
Celeborn sighs and carefully studies Lanchigil and Egnassigil.
'It was the desire of Sigileth to gift me these knives, and I do not wish to gainsay that desire; but so too does it grieve me that they will no longer strike fear into the hearts of her foes, remaining as they would within Caras Galadhon.
'I propose then a compromise. I will retain one of the knives, and its brother I give to you to do with as you will.'
'You have nothing for me?'

'The Golden Host has accomplished what it set out to do, ${PLAYER}: we have delayed an attack by the forces of Dol Guldur, kept their attention focused upon the doorstep of the fortress, and proven strong our friendship with the dwarves of the Iron Garrison. We wait now for the next stroke to come, and must stand against it as best we may.
'The dwarves Bróin and Bori have returned to Moria bearing the mithril axe, Zigilburk. When next you return to the Twenty-first Hall, Bori desired that you visit him in the Chamber of Leadership. He wishes to discuss the final fate of the mithril axe.'

'Thank you for coming back here to Khazad-dûm, my friend! It was a long journey for Bróin and me, and we spoke at length concerning the mithril axe. It has brought us little but misery, and my cousin convinced me that it could still do great harm in the future, if wielded.
'Truth be told, I did not need much convincing! I have seen first-hand the recklessness the axe stirs in the hearts of those who wield it; my stay in the dungeons of Dol Guldur speaks loudly of this point!
'Our fathers initially resisted, but have now grudgingly assented to our plan: the dwarves cannot retain possession of Zigilburk. Speak to me again, and we will make this a reality.'

'I must thank you again, ${PLAYER}: abandoning such a precious and valuable weapon is not an easy thing, even for dwarves for whom it has brought such grief. But it is for the best. Desire to possess items of such beauty and value has often led my people down the path to misfortune. With your help, Bróin and I have had the chance to turn aside from that path before it was too late.'

'So it is done, then. It is good to know that Zigilburk will trouble the dwarves no more.'

'Thank you for coming here for us, ${PLAYER}. Bróin is just ahead, with Zigilburk.
'It is for the best; the mithril axe should remain unused from now on, left for all the ages of the world in the watery chamber where it was found.'

'Welcome back to Khazad-dûm, ${PLAYER}. For the great service you have done my family and for rescuing my son from the dungeons of Dol Guldur, you will always have a home here, if you want it.
'I know Brogur is not pleased with the idea of leaving Zigilburk in the depths of Ghân-gharâf, untouched, but the mithril axe has brought us little but grief. I agree with my son and my nephew on this.'

'Do you intend to go along with this foolish decision of my son and nephew to leave Zigilburk here in the depths?
'This is a mistake, ${PLAYER}. I am certain any misfortune brought upon us by the mithril axe would have befallen us even without it.
'Why abandon such a weapon? Surely we will have need of it again! Can you say we will not?'

'This is the last time I will stand within the walls of Ghân-gharâf, ${PLAYER}. I remember when I crawled, dripping and scared, out of the pool, and lay my eyes upon this flooded chamber.
'Were it not for Zigilburk clutched in the hand of the dwarf Óin, friend of my grandfather's, I could not have kept the terrible beast of the pool at bay.'

'I have not seen you since you passed into Moria, ${PLAYER}! How has the legendary weapon I gave you from the relics unearthed in Eregion served?'
Hundi's brow furrows with disappointment at your answer.
'You had it reforged? Oh, I see. Well, that is sometimes the way of weapons, is it not?'

'I knew you would not miss this moment, ${PLAYER}, ${RACE} that you are! It seems that adventure follows you wherever you pass.
'The feats of heroism we committed in the depths of Buzun-ghâr and in Rushdurinul are still a wonder to me... and will be until the end of my days, I am sure.
'The tales of which we have been a part will echo to the carven heights of even the grandest ale-hall of Khazad-dûm!'

'We have certainly come a long way since I enlisted your aid for the Iron Garrison, have we not, ${PLAYER}? Who can say they expected you to be of such help to us? I must admit I did not!
'We Dwarves of the Iron Garrison are gathering to witness the sealing of the mithril axe in the very depths of Ghân-gharâf. I am sure all will wish to speak with you as you make your way to Bróin.'

'Ah, these tunnels will not be used by dwarves following this day. What tales will spring up among our younger kin concerning our actions here, I wonder?
'Already, I have told my boy of the great skill with which you dispatched goblin-runners in the Flooded Deeps for me, ${PLAYER}. He is amazed at the number... though to be truthful, I have forgotten how many it was. Fifty? One-hundred?'

'It was well done, ${PLAYER}, and it has been a pleasure working to reclaim the halls of Khazad-dûm with such a staunch ally as you!'

'You were a big part of our success in keeping the lines of supply flowing, ${PLAYER}, and we thank you for it.'

'Look, Wili, if it isn't our counterpart, ${PLAYER}!

'It was no easy thing, keeping the Orcs from returning while you were still within their camp, but we managed it!'

'I have come to witness the sealing away of Zigilburk myself, ${PLAYER}, and few of my dwarves could bear to come with me. The mithril axe was forged at the Heart of Fire during a time long past, and for it to no longer be wielded seems a great shame to me.
'I understand that the axe has brought grief to the Dwarves of the Iron Garrison, but as a forge-master and a dwarf in whom burns the fire of craft-work, the moon above the mountains will set today upon a different world.'

'Watch your step, ${PLAYER}. The footing here is treacherous.'
Sweina thinks for a moment, and then laughs.
'Who am I to tell you what is treacherous? We first met when I boldly charged into the deepest reaches of the Silvertine Lodes to challenge a nest of goblins in combat! I could have handled myself admirably, and was about to do so, but your intervention was still appreciated.'
'You are almost to Ghân-gharâf, ${PLAYER}. I did not think it would be this far, but Melmar here assures me that it is close.'

'Very good, very good, my friend! I am glad you have come; I know it is important to Bróin that you be here.
'I remember still how you took it upon yourself to slay the crebain that sought to spy on the Iron Garrison at our encampment just outside the Hollin Gate. Who knows what evils you forestalled that day, ${PLAYER}? Those filthy birds would report no news of our doings to their mysterious master, thanks to you.
'And thanks to the dwarf who asked you to do it, as well!'

'Look at us, ${PLAYER}! Did you ever think we would be in this place, about to leave a weapon of such power buried behind great stone walls, never to be used?
'Is this the right course of action? Well, that is for Bósi and Brogur, and their sons, to decide. We do our duties, as they are assigned to us, and must trust that they know best.
'Did you doubt me when I sent you to salvage useable weapons from all around Khazad-dûm? It was for a good cause, was it not?'

'My dwarves have been called upon today to collapse the passage leading to Ghân-gharâf, once the mithril axe has been left within. It is strange to me to be covering up a passage, rather than uncovering it!
'Indeed, you helped my dwarves unearth the Doors of Durin at the West-gate, did you not? We have had much hardship since then, but look now at the glory of the Iron Garrison! The true work has only just begun!'
'Let us return to the Twenty-first Hall. We have done what we set out to do, ${PLAYER}. We have made the difficult choice... the right one.'
