'I have told you of my hatred for the Orcs, ${PLAYER}, and you know that no bounds can hold it! My passion for slaying Orcs cannot be contained by the borders of this forest, nor by those of any region in this Middle-earth!
'I have envisioned the grandest statement possible of my hatred for the Orcs. Let them rue the many times they have crossed the Greyhammer family and gnash their teeth in anguish that they ever did so!
'You will travel to every region in which an Orc, goblin, or uruk has caused harm to a Greyhammer and slay one of their kind, and you will shout \qFor the Greyhammers!\q as you do so. Then perhaps the Orcs will know and fear my family, as they should! Do this first in Mirkwood, Lothlórien, and Moria, and work your way westward in sequence. Then speak to my father Tandri in Thorin's Hall, in Ered Luin, and tell him of this glorious deed!'

'What in the names of all the dwarves has my son had you do? Travelling to all the regions in which a Greyhammer has been wronged and slaying a single Orc in each? I cannot believe you humoured him thus, ${PLAYER}! Does a ${CLASS} such as you have nothing more pressing to do than this?
'If my son Lúth and his brothers spent less time dreaming up ways to tell folk of their grievances with the Orcs and more time mining and working, perhaps we would have found some precious gemstones by now!
'Take this for your effort, ${PLAYER}. I will speak to Lúth myself. It is high time he began doing something productive with the time he currently spends complaining to strangers about his lot in life!'

'I am sorry to ask this, but I cannot leave my post, and someone needs to bring the word to Núrelleth that Achardor has been slain.
'Neither the telling nor the listening will be easy, ${PLAYER}, but she deserves to know what has happened.
'Núrelleth is in Caras Galadhon, on Telain Glorelloth. Be gentle with giving her the news. Her husband was slain by Orcs not long ago, and now Achardor too will not return from the siege of Mirkwood.'

'I know already why you have come, ${PLAYER}. Lady Galadriel visited me several days ago, at nightfall, to bring me the sad tidings that Achardor would not return from Mirkwood.
'I think I already knew it, ${PLAYER}, even before the Lady came to see me. I cannot explain it.
'If you have unanswered questions, please pay a visit to Lady Galadriel. You will find her at the House of Celeborn, here in Caras Galadhon.'

'You have come to ask me something about Achardor's fate, ${PLAYER}? I know what it is you will ask.'
Galadriel turns to face you, and you see that her face is a mask of sorrow.
'Achardor begged leave of Celeborn to accompany the Hidden Guard on its mission to Dol Guldur, and my husband denied his petition. Only at my word did Celeborn relent, and Achardor was permitted to begin the errand that would end with his death.
'You know that my Mirror shows many things; can I have known where this road might lead Achardor? I did know, and it is with such knowledge that I spoke on his behalf. Do you think me cruel? Would it have been crueler still to prevent Achardor from seeking his vengeance? It may have been, or may not have been. I am not to be the judge of it and do not wish to make excuses.
'I wanted to explain, and I thank you for listening, ${PLAYER}. The waters of my Mirror are changeable and changing, and many things can be seen...or not seen.'

'It is good to see you again, ${PLAYER}! I am spending my time while we remain in Mirkwood refining the process of brewing balms and salves to heal the hurts of those wounded during the assault on Dol Guldur. It is slow work, but that is the price of truly useful business.
'A number of my company have reported to me the location of places that may contain useful alchemical ingredients. From Gath Ulunn, behind the walls of the Orc-camp in Gathbúrz, you might recover egg-shells from the worms being bred in that place. I hear too that the Hall of Lights, a cavern among the Mirk-eaves, is home to pestilent glow-worms and their queens; you might bring me slime from them that I could turn to useful purposes.
'My friend Cairches informs me too that the ruins of Agistath, located among the Dourstocks, appear to be the final resting place of aged Audaghaim wine. If you can bring me all of these useful ingredients, my work will be accelerated.'

'You have returned with the ingredients I seek, and so quickly! I did not expect you to return with such haste, but you have my thanks for doing so.
'When crumbled into a fine powder, the egg-shells will be used as part of an unguent that can shield the bearer from the effects of fire. The slime provides the base for a soothing salve that can mitigate the effects of poison.
'The wine? It is thirsty work, the brewing of potions and the crafting of salves! You have my thanks, ${PLAYER}, and those of the Elves who will be burned or poisoned as the campaign in Mirkwood continues!'
'You have nothing for me?'

'We have won as great a victory as we might have hoped, ${PLAYER}; the assault on Dol Guldur has surely set the plans of the Enemy back a step. An army marches from the East to reinforce the fortress, and we do not have the numbers to oppose it in strength.
'And yet until it arrives, there are still strategic objectives that can be won to strike further still against the forces that hold the fortress.
'Gather a small fellowship of allies and take one of these strategic locations, ${PLAYER}: the Warg-pens, the Sword-hall, or the Dungeons of Dol Guldur. We will sting the Enemy while we may!'

'We may not hold it long, but let this be a reminder that the Golden Host still must be feared! We do not possess the numbers of the Enemy, but we make up for that lack with skill and with strength!
'The fortress of Dol Guldur is not unassailable, and we will continue to strike beyond its walls until such time as Lord Celeborn deems we must retreat. I remain here in the Golden Wood, to my dismay, but at his command; and from here I form the plans by which we can best leverage our abilities.
'The Enemy is surely learning that our abilities are not what he believed them to be. The Elves are not weak. The Elves, and their allies, are strong.'

'When this campaign ends, I will lay down my bow and depart the shores of Middle-earth. I have had my fill of fighting. But still I am intrigued by the mystery of Audaghaim. What happened to this town, and to its people? Scouts recently discovered some ruins amid the Dourstocks, where gaunt-men roam and shades flit among the trees.
'I cannot leave this place until I know what connexion there is between Audaghaim and the ruins of Agistath. I cannot bear to leave this mystery unsolved, to rest heavily upon my mind during the uncounted years!
'Travel to Agistath for me and investigate the ruins, ${PLAYER}. This is the only tie to these lands I have left. I have spoken with Issuriel about this, but she does not agree with me. She has returned already to Cerin Amroth, and there will stay in contemplation for a little while yet.'

'There is a sad story behind Audaghaim's abandonment, I am certain; but it is to be hoped we have given whatever spirits still linger here some measure of peace.
'My time in Middle-earth is nearing its end, ${PLAYER}. I have no more need for my bow, Cúmaeth. If you desire to have it, it is now yours.'

'Tell me what you discovered among the ruins of Agistath.'
Cúcheron listens intently as you describe your adventure among the ruins, and the broken wooden toy you found.
'I think the townsfolk of Audaghaim fled this place, ${PLAYER}, with what possessions they could carry. Why they fled with such haste, or where they were heading, I cannot say, but it seems certain that few made it out of Agistath with their lives.
'There are graves among the weeds here in Audaghaim. Is it possible some of the townsfolk were left behind? It is clear to me that the wooden toy you found should be returned to its home. Leave it at one of the graves here in Audaghaim, and perhaps the shades that linger here and at Agistath will have some measure of peace.'
'You have nothing to do with this?'

'Thank you for coming to see me, ${PLAYER}. I have spent many days in restful peace here in Cerin Amroth, and it has done me a great deal of good; the effects of the Gwigael poison are now just a memory, and the spells of weakness have passed.'
Issuriel pauses for a moment, and seems unable to meet your gaze.
'I do not regret my decision to do without the Laidhris antidote, ${PLAYER}. Events unfolded differently than we thought they would, but I could not let the mission end in failure because of my own selfishness. Raddir did not have the choice I did, nor did Sigileth. Only Achardor seems to have understood what I came to know: that I would have closed my eyes forever if it meant the death and loss that happened to that point would have had a reason; that it would have mattered.
'Still, I am grateful for the actions of Bróin. I have picked a beautiful flower from the slopes of Cerin Amroth. Will you bring it to him in Moria, with my good wishes and my thankfulness? I understand he is recovering in the Peaceful Path, along Durin's Way.'

You give Bróin the flower and tell him of Issuriel's words.
'Well, uh, I don't know what to say! I... well... it is an honour, of course, and....'
Bróin turns a bright shade of pink and manages to stammer out an apology before starting again.
'It was nothing, of course, just the decent thing to do, and she such a noble Elf and all, and being so courageous on my people's account. It would be a dwarf of little honour who would abandon Issuriel to that vile poison. A Dourhand might, but no son of Brogur nor of Bósi, for that matter!
'She has the heart of a dwarf, I will tell you that! I mean... by that I mean that she is as brave as a dwarf, you understand, and not that she has my own heart, though of course she does, for how could she not? But what I mean is....'
Exhausted from the effort, Bróin lapses into confused silence and stares at you, red-faced.
'I should stick with the Orc-slaying, ${PLAYER}. I find it to be much easier!'
'You have nothing for me?'
Bring Issuriel's elanor blossom to Bróin in the Peaceful Path
Volume II, Epilogue: Issuriel's Flower
Given time to reflect on her adventure with the Hidden Guard, Issuriel has come to a decision concerning her future.
'I owe my life to Bróin. I did not think to count a dwarf among my closest friends, but now I cannot help but do so.'
'It was nothing, ${PLAYER}. Anyone would have done what I did for Issuriel!'
'I should comb my beard before I next see Issuriel. It is all tangled!'
'Have you seen Bróin recently?'
'Bróin is very brave, is he not?'

Bróin is in the Peaceful Path, located off Durin's Way, in Moria.

It may seem impossible that so small a creature can have so large an impact on the world, but it is the case that the small insects driven to madness by the caretaker of the woods of Agamaur are such creatures. Grimbark has long held control of the Arboretum at the behest of the Red-maid and with his corruption has driven all living denizens of the swamp mad.

The Huorn Grimbark is lost to the corruption that has long plagued this land. It is an unfortunate end for a once noble creature, but Grimbark cannot be redeemed.

Optional Objective: Key Locations

In the short-lived time before Rhudaur fell beneath the sway of Angmar, there were three champions and a king who led the Men of Rhudaur with honour and justice. In the Arboretum, the three were interred in a place where the peaceful woods would watch over them and the people could visit them in quiet reflection.

The Garth Agarwen Arboretum was home to many important locations. These included the tombs of three of their champions: Fuirvaw, Hargram, and Halvegil, a statue to their first king, Nailion, and the founding stone that served as the marker for the bounds of their land: the Stone of Mingond.

Once the loyal caretakers to the elder Huorns of the great wood, the bog-lurkers of Agamaur are a fallen and corrupt group of beings beyond saving. They have learned to relish the blood of the living, and in so doing, have become the very evil they once stopped from spreading through the lands.
Once noble guardians of the forest, the bog-lurkers in the Arboretum of Garth Agarwen are now twisted and terrible creatures thriving on blood. They must be slain for they cannot be saved.

Survival -- Barrow-downs Phase 2
The inhabitants of the Barrow-downs do not like uninvited guests.

As you look down, you find a remnant of a fallen branch. The bark appears to be ashen-coloured and smells of decay, though something still speaks of an ancient beauty it may once have possessed.
Perhaps you should bring this to Himeinior at Barad Angol to see if he can tell you anything about the branch.

'Thank you kindly for gathering such an exquisite specimen, ${PLAYER}. I have gathered several such branches myself, and this is the best of them thus far.
'Sadly, it appears as if this poor branch has been blighted by some form of foul sorcery. It seems as if this sorcery has consumed its life and has left it naught but a husk, bereft of its former glory.'
Bring the blighted branch to Himeinior
Scratching the Surface
You discovered a blighted branch in the Ashenslades, corrupted by an unknown disease.

Himeinior is at Barad Angol, a small camp at a tower overlooking Sâd Doldúr.

Alas -- this Elf breathes no more....

Alas -- this Elf breathes no more....

'You must make one final venture into Dannenglor, ${PLAYER}, and this is the most important one. Pray do not return until this last hope is either verified or put to rest forever, for my heart cannot bear the suspense much longer.
'I need you to go back to the morroval-roost and search high and low for my friends, the missing scouts. You have proven yourself more than capable of battling the vile foe that wanders that place, and so I put my last hope in you.
'Three went forth, and three you must account for, be they alive or dead. Go north one last time, Randir, and do not leave until you find them.'

'Alas, alas! It is just as I feared! Let this be a lesson to us all that no matter what distractions may tempt us while on this dark and seldom-travelled road, we must not stray from our course. Vainly did they pass into the West, never to return.
'Truly does my heart despair at this terrible news, though I long expected it.
'You have my most heartfelt thanks for your part in this, my dear friend. I would still be driven mad with worry, but for your efforts. You are most deserving of the trust of the Malledhrim.'
Search for the first scout in Dannenglor
Search for the second scout in Dannenglor
Search for the third scout in Dannenglor
Talk to Fernachar at the Haunted Inn
Dwindling Hope
With one last effort and dwindling hope, Fernachar urgently wishes to locate the whereabouts of his missing friends and see them safely returned.
'Pray make haste! There cannot be much time, if they are indeed alive at all. Go to Dannenglor and do not return until you have learned aught of their fate.'

The missing Malledhrim scouts can surely be found in Dannenglor, north of the Haunted Inn.
You should search Dannenglor for the missing Elves, though whether they are alive or dead is yet to be seen.

Fernachar is in the Haunted Inn in the Dourstocks, south of Dannenglor.
You should speak with Fernachar and tell him that the three scouts met their doom in Dannenglor.
Defeated merrevail at Dannenglor (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'The merrevail at Dannenglor are deadly foes, and I fear that my friends met their doom if facing them unawares. Your exploration thus far served one purpose -- to prepare us for facing the threat on our northern side.
'You should go back to Dannenglor, this time armed with the knowledge you have gained from your first exploration. Cut down as many merrevail as you can, and then report back to me when the way is clearer.
'If you can do this, we will surely be able to find my lost friends! I dearly hope that they live yet, but I am deeply troubled, deeply troubled....'
'You have done well, ${PLAYER}. I believe we are coming closer to uncovering what happened to my lost brethren.'
Defeat merrevail at Dannenglor (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Fernachar at the Haunted Inn
Hewing Fell Wings
Fernachar has asked you to defeat many merrevail in pursuit of the Malledhrim scouts who have been waylaid at Dannenglor.
'How have you fared thus far, ${PLAYER}? The merrevail are in Dannenglor, to the north.'

Merrevail can be found in the Elf-ruins of Dannenglor, north of the Haunted Inn in the Dourstocks.
You should fight the merrevail in pursuit of the Malledhrim Elves who were most likely waylaid at the gates of Dannenglor.

Fernachar awaits you anxiously at the Haunted Inn in the Dourstocks, south of Dannenglor.

This blade surely belonged to an Elf, but it lies near a great stain of blood

'Hail, ${CLASS}; welcome to our meagre establishment. It is not much, but it is safer than the wild woods beyond that door. I hope you will be careful when you venture out again -- a small party of our own went out to explore, and they have not returned.
'I will not deny that I am very worried for them. They espied the Elf-ruins to the north of here, which, if memory serves, was once the fair Elven-realm of Dannenglor. They left some days ago, and I fear the worst....
'Will you search for them, and scout the ruins so that we know what we are up against? Be very careful -- I do not wish you to meet the same fate that they met.'
'Alas! This does not bode well. My fears are all but confirmed. Oh, ${PLAYER}...do you think there is any hope?'
Search near Dannenglor for the Malledhrim scouts
Talk to Fernachar at the Haunted Inn
The Lost Explorers
A small party of explorers set off for Dannenglor and have not yet returned, and Fernachar is anxious for word of their fate.
'Dannenglor is to the north. You should follow the road there, for that is the path our friends took when they ventured thither.'

Dannenglor is to the north of the Haunted Inn.
Fernachar has asked you to search the ruins of Dannenglor for signs of the Elf-scouts who went that way. You should approach Dannenglor cautiously, following the road where the Elf explorers went.

Fernachar awaits you in the Haunted Inn in the Dourstocks, south of Dannenglor.
You should speak with Fernachar and tell him of the worrying scene you beheld when you approached Dannenglor.

'You have been sent to aid us and aid us you may, mellon. There are many tasks ahead of us, and our numbers are fewer than we would wish, especially with our scouts missing in the north.
'This forest is rife with poison-fanged spiders, seemingly everywhere one looks. They spout from the Dreadweaver's Lair, south-west from here.
'You should defeat as many Mirkwood spiders as you can, mellon. They are ever a threat to the Elves, and are our enemies of old.'

'Suillaid, mellon. You have our thanks for your efforts to pave the way for our offensive against Dol Guldur. This forest is still evil, but it is a little less so with every malicious spider that is brought to death.'

The spiders that roam the Dourstocks spill out from the Dreadweaver's Lair, making the forest all the more perilous for the Malledhrim.
'Spiders can be found everywhere you look, ${PLAYER}. If you have trouble finding them in the woods, you could investigate around the Dreadweaver's Lair, south-west from here.'

Spiders can be found throughout the Dourstocks.

'You have done well indeed, but you will not believe what report I have heard. One of our scouts returned and said he saw a deadly-looking spider bearing a great burden -- an Orc that was unconscious from poison.
'This spider carried her prey in the direction of the Dreadweaver's Lair, south-west from here. Will you pursue her there? I fear for our safety with such a monster roaming about, though I'll not hold her choice of food against her.
'If you can rid the Dreadweaver's Lair of this menace, I do believe we will have secured the Dourstocks against the greater threat of spiders, ${PLAYER}.'
'Very good! The spider threat is greatly lessened now, thanks to you, ${PLAYER}. The Malledhrim owe you much.'

'You have done well to thin the pack, ${PLAYER}, but still the creatures persist, and with more fervour than ever. They press closer and closer with every passing night.
'It becomes clear to me that these are no reckless wild beasts. Nay, I believe they are driven by some fell hand. Their efforts against us are not those of animals, but of a host of enemies rallying their defences against an invasion.
'Surely someone from Dol Guldur has tamed this pack for their own evil purposes. You should try to draw him out, whomever he is! Go to the Pack-howler's Hill, my friend, and see if anyone answers your summons.'
'Good! I am glad we are rid of the Orc who twists the animals here for his evil purposes. You have done well indeed, ${PLAYER}, and I thank you for your efforts on behalf of the Golden Host.'

Challenge: Ivar

Ivar the Blood-hand is a Gaunt-lord, a being of great and dark power, made in mockery of the Wizard Radagast the Brown. He is weakened at the moment, not only by his meddling with Radagast, but also as he continues to raise his army of Dead within the bounds of Garth Agarwen.

Ivar the Blood-hand must fall. His strength must fade, and he must become what he should have been all along: a memory of a bygone age. His strength is born of raising the Dead and returning those that have fallen back to battle.
This is his role, and stopping him from achieving this role, no matter how minutely, will see that the mark of his hand is removed from the land. To do this, you must ensure that his banners remain so that at his death his power is split between them.

Defeat Créoth (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Optional Objective: Créoth

When Men first settled in these lands, the Hillmen of Rhudaur settled Garth Agarwen and treated nature as they should. As time passed and the influence of the Witch-king spread throughout the kingdom, the Men fell to corruption and turned against nature, poisoning the land and its caretakers.

Créoth watch the entrance to the barrow of Garth Agarwen at the behest of the Gaunt Lord, Ivar. They are the first line of defence and a formidable opponent. These Men, loyal to the corrupt being that their ancestors helped to create, are without conscience and filled with malice. Their redemption is unlikely, and it falls to you, in this place, to defeat them.

Not all Dead are reanimated bodies returned from the grave to lay waste to the innocent and pure. Some take whatever form they can, even if it is only part of a whole. When no body can be found, the fell spirits will seek another refuge and finding only an arm, or other body part, they will inhabit the creation and destroy life through this means.

Decayed can be found within unlikely locations, lurking in the crevasses and darkness of stone corridors throughout the barrows. Exposing these creations will require you to spring their trap, but do not be surprised; keep your wits about you, and you will destroy these vile creations.

Optional Objective: Unnamed Tombs

Not all Men of Rhudaur were Men of evil. Some were heroes or Men of noble deeds in their time. They are lost now, within the mire of this land and lost to the corruption of their people. Still, they exist in unmarked graves in these barrows.

Though the Rhudaur fell quickly, they had heroes, and not all the Rhudaur were part of the malignancy that crept into the land. There are five such heroes entombed within the Garth Agarwen barrows. You should visit their graves. If for no other reason than to know that these Men were not the culprits behind the great tragedy of this land.
Defeated wights (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeat wights (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Optional Objective: Wights

The time of Men is not so long, and the time of Rhudaur before its fall to corruption and alliance with Angmar was shorter still. Heroes, warriors, sacrifices, thieves, villains, and many others were buried in the barrows near the Red-maid's spring. Here, the Gaunt-lord Ivar has chosen to begin raising his army.

Wights patrol the befouled land in an endless journey through the mire. They wait until they will be called on by their dread lord, Ivar, to make war upon the living and began their campaign of corruption through the land. It need not be this way. Armed as you are, you can aid the Free Peoples of the world by ridding the land of these foul creatures.
Collected tokens of bondage from morvul-slaves (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'How have you found Mirkwood thus far, randir? It is not to my liking at all. Several of our number have gone missing on a mission to Dannenglor. We know now that the place is rife with merrevail.
'If you find yourself there, you should defeat many of the morvul-slaves and see if you can learn of this morroval-nest. Any interesting relics you come across while in Dannenglor would be of use to me in discerning the nature of these beasts.
'Just be cautious when you go, ${PLAYER}. It bodes ill that our scouts are still missing. I worry very much that this particular mission will be perilous for you.'

'Thank you, randir, for bringing me these. These tokens look to have been crafted by the beasts themselves, for they are very crude. This means that there is a leader among them, binding them to a life of allegiance towards defending their roost.'
'Have you collected any tokens fromt he morvul-slaves?'

Dangerous morvul-slaves stalk the city of Dannenglor, protecting their kind from intruders.
'The morvul-slaves can be found defending the keep their kind has pillaged -- the Elf-ruins of Dannenglor, to the north of here.'

Morvul-slaves can be found in Dannenglor, to the north of the Haunted Inn in the Dourstocks.

'Now that we have learned a bit of the nest of merrevail in Dannenglor, I think we can take some action against them. Those tokens you collected were made by one of their own.
'I am guessing this particular morvul is a strong brute, and you would do well to remove him if we are to secure Dannenglor against these beasts.
'I am sure he keeps well hidden. Hopefully when you return to Dannenglor, you will find some way to summon him to a confrontation. I do not think he will be able to resist a direct challenge. Be careful, ${PLAYER}; this is sure to be a dreadful challenge.'
'Wonderfully done, ${PLAYER}! You have given us much aid in this dark and dreary place. Everything we do to combat the countless evils here plants a seed of hope.'

'In the ruins below, there are many ancient pillars that have stood in this area for generations...since the days when the forest was called Greenwood the Great. These pillars may reveal valuable clues regarding the strength of the rituals being performed within Sâd Doldúr.
'Will you journey among the ruins in Sâd Doldúr and examine these pillars for me? Travel the path below to Sâd Doldúr and among the outer ruins, you will find three such pillars.
'When you have examined them, return to me for further instruction.'
'It is good to hear that these ancient pillars appear to be resistant to the sickness spreading across the Ashenslades. It bodes well for our ability to stop the spread of the blight elsewhere. '

Pillars of Another Age

Among the ruins outside Sâd Doldúr, there are a number of ancient pillars that have resided in this area for a number of years. These stones are ancient and may lead to valuable clues about exactly what is happening to the Ashenslades.
'The pillars I wish for you to examine lie to the south, below this camp.'

The ancient pillars can be located among the ruins of Sâd Doldúr, which can be found by following the path below, down the mountain until you reach the ruins proper. There are three pillars, located in the northern, central, and southern portions of the ruins.
The cairn stones located among the ruins appear to be resistant to the blight that is sweeping the area. Himeinior asked you to travel to each of these locations and examine the pillars.

Himeinior is at the camp near Barad Angol upon the hill, north of the pillars.

'Well met, ${PLAYER}! Your foray into this evil tower shall not be soon forgotten by the Elves who survive the offensive. We are indebted to you for breaching the lower defences of Barad Guldur.
'From here I believe we can look to advancing further up the tower -- not a small feat, I assure you.

'Belvaer, the commander here, has given some instructions for you, ${PLAYER}. Further up this tower lie horrors of Mordor which yearn to smother the light of the world beyond these fell eaves, corrupting Middle-earth as they have corrupted Mirkwood.
'If you are to march further, you do so in the face of great peril. If you feel able, you should scour this place for any clues or information that will be of use in our campaign against the Enemy, whether it be within these walls or abroad in the greater fight against the Enemy.
'I wish you luck, ${CLASS}! Please bring your findings to me -- but this is not a path that you should walk alone. Bring many strong friends with you upon this venture.'
'Hail, mellon! I am glad to see that you have returned in one piece. Do tell of what you saw in the tower....'

Collected water-samples in the Drownholt (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'We are very busy here with planning our offensive, as you see. Unfortunately, this does not leave me with much opportunity to pursue my usual studies. I am a scholar of nature, you see, as are many of my kindred.
'I have great interest in the natural world, even one as corrupted as this black forest. At home in Lórien I have a great collection of water-samples; it has taken me many long years to build. It would be a shame to leave the Drownholt without expanding my library.
'You would be doing a great favour to me if you would take samples from pools in the Drownholt as you go thither. Such items would be worth more to me than gold, ${PLAYER}.'

'How wonderful, ${PLAYER}! I think these will do very well for the purpose of my studies. I hope to learn much of Mirkwood from these drops, for they can tell me many long tales of the rain and the plants and the earth of these parts. I suspect these will be sad tales, but perhaps some helpful knowledge can be gleaned from them in time.'
Collect water-samples in the Drownholt (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

Laidhriel is interested in collecting samples of water to keep for study upon her return to Lothlórien so that she can better understand the environs of Mirkwood's swamp-lands.

'I am so glad that you are willing to gather phials of water for my collection! I very much look forward to studying the samples you bring me, for there is much to be learned of a place from its still waters.'

Samples of water can be collected throughout the many shallow pools of the Drownholt in Mirkwood.

'Olog-hai are trolls of enormous size and devestating strength, and these have been well-armed against us.
'Gather your companions and stop them if you can, lest their rampage buy enough time for the Orcs to rally their forces against our attack.'

'With their Olog-hai fallen, it remains to be seen what the masters of the tower will do next. I suspect they will now hold against us, risking no more of their strength until the eastern army arives.

'We know we do not have the power to pull down Dol Guldur now, ${PLAYER}, and with an enemy army approaching, it is only a matter of time before we must retreat. My people are swifter than any enemy bound by foot, but we cannot run faster than Wargs.
'There is a force of these beasts housed in Gathbúrz, and if they are free to pursue us when we begin our retreat, they will pull down many a valiant Elf, ere we can reach the boats.
'Those Wargs must be slain ere the time for our withdrawal comes, and I believe that you have the strength to accomplish this task.'
'Your hunt has gone well, and the Wargs of Gathbúrz have suffered badly this day. That is one less threat to worry about when it comes time for us to withdraw back beneath the boughs of Lothlórien.'

'While it is the Nazgûl in that black tower who command all of the forces here in Mirkwood, it is the uruk-lieutenants and generals who actually give the orders and organize the troops.
'There is a large encampment of these brutal Orcs deep within Gathbúrz, and if they can be rooted out, then the rest of the rabble will fall apart, leaving them as useless fodder upon the battlefield.
'I would bid you seek out the Black Uruks of Mirkwood and slay them. When you have succeeded, return to me.'

'Ha! With the number of the uruks in Mirkwood depleted, there will be few left to help drive the Dark Lord's armies when they come to cross the Anduin!
'With any fortune, our archers will have naught but practice at targets as they attempt the crossing: a display I find myself looking forward to.'

The Black Drivers

The Black Uruks are the masters of Gathbúrz, driving the Orcs and goblins into battle beneath their lashes. As long as they remain in command, it will be difficult to fully break the forces defending Dol Guldur. More importantly, if the uruk-leaders can be defeated, then the masters of the tower will find it considerably more difficult to prepare the upcoming army for their inevitable assault upon Lothlórien.
'I am impressed by your skill, ${PLAYER}, but I will be more impressed when you have returned with news of the defeat of the Black Uruks of Mordor.'

Black Uruks can be found in Gathbúrz.

Found an engraved dagger

'Have you seen the sentries, ${PLAYER}? I do not refer to the Orcs, of course -- there is little challenge in avoiding the eyes of Orcs. I refer to the ones carved of stone, with unblinking eyes that strike your will with a crushing darkness if you should stray too close.
'We have quickly learned to stay away from them as much as we may, but they make manoeuvering through Gathbúrz difficult, and I imagine the inner walls of Dol Guldur are likewise defended. We must find a way to defeat their power if we are to achieve our goals here.
'The robed Cargûl have been seen tending to these stone sentries on occasion... if you could approach close enough to defeat one, then perhaps you might be able to find something to aid us against the stones.'

'So you found these knives upon the Cargûl? I am not certain if they can help us or not. They look similar in make to the dread morgul-blades carried by the Nazgûl....
'I think you had best bring this to Agorin in Emyn Lûm. She might have some insight as to what might be done with them.'

'In truth, I had not imagined that the watchers would be so powerful that even Agorin cannot answer them. This will be a serious thorn in our sides as we do battle for control of Gathbúrz.
'Still, at least she found a way for you to avoid their power. I shall have to see if we can get our hands on a few more of those blades....'

'These knives were carried by the Cargûl who guard the Watchers of Dol Guldur? They are not morgul-blades, though they are indeed of a similar make. Unfortunately, I do not think they can be used to negate the power of the watchers... however, there may be another way.
'I can bind these blades as tokens that you may keep upon you. They are still evil things, I fear, but so long as you carry them, the watchers will not be able to distinguish you from their own dark servants, thus you should be able to pass them unmolested.
'That is the best I can do for you, I am afraid. Lady Galadriel cannot cross the river without leaving Lothlórien defenceless, and Mithrandir is lost to us. I do not know of any other who might be strong enough to break the power of the watchers.'

'It is said that the satching stones of the Enemy are possessed of fell spirits and that the Cargûl which guard them were once knights of Eärnur of Gondor... you would do well to be wary.'
'It is said that the watching stones of the Enemy are possessed of fell spirits and that the Cargûl which guard them were once knights of Eärnur of Gondor... you would do well to be wary.'

'Gathbúrz lies in a state of near-anarchy before our assault, and now it is time to push it over the brink!
'General Tímurzgrat -- a Black Uruk of deadly repute -- has come to the fore in an effort to force order upon the soldiers of the Enemy. His head is ripe for the plucking, and unlike that fool Fikthrug, the masters of Dol Guldur will find Tímurzgrat far more difficult to replace.
'Take great care though: Tímurzgrat is no mean foe; he is quite skilled in combat as well as command, and you will likely need stalwart allies at your side to defeat him. When you have gathered your allies, seek him at the tower some distance to the north of here.'

'With Tímurzgrat's fall, so falls Gathbúrz. We should expect no further organized resistance from that front until the eastern army arrives.

'Listen to me carefully ${PLAYER}, the tower of Dol Guldur is our ultimate objective, but it is not fated to fall to us this day. We have not the power to bring down those walls -- not as long as the Eye of Sauron is turned towards Lothlórien -- and soon Mirkwood will be overrun with Enemy reinforcements.
'We are here to draw the enemy's ire and to inflict as grievous a wound as we may before we are driven back across the Anduin. The Orcs of Dol Guldur will eventually fall upon the Golden Wood, but we can and will delay that day.
'Thus our true goal here is to destroy as much of the garrison of Gathbúrz as possible before then: soldiers, supplies, leadership...whatever we can lay to ruin before we are forced to retreat. Every Orc you slay here is one less to ford the Anduin when they come against Lothlórien in the coming days.'

'Well fought, ${PLAYER}. The garrison of Gathbúrz is disorganized and vulnerable. You can inflict many casualties there while the Orcs vainly attempt to drive us off of this hill.
'Look to your own survival, though: we cannot afford to lose many, or we will find ourselves overwhelmed ere our task is complete.'

War of Attrition

The battle upon the slopes below Dol Guldur rages fiercely. As the Malledhrim attempt to lay siege to its walls, the Orcs of Gathbúrz launch one counterattack after another in an attempt to drive them back.
'The foul Orcs of Dol Guldur dare tread upon this ground, once the home of Elves...for that, they must perish.'

Orcs can be found throughout Gathbúrz.
Rodelleth has bidden you lay waste to the Orc-soldiers garrisoning Gathbúrz, to hinder their own imminent assault upon Lothlórien.

Rodelleth is at Thangúlhad in Gathbúrz.
You should return to Rodelleth with news of your success.

'The Orcs of Gathbúrz are a shattered force, but we must continue our forays against them to keep them from regrouping. I am asking the Malledhrim and our allies to mount frequent patrols through the area north of here, skirting their fortifications and engaging any enemies attempting to reinforce those positions.
'Are you up for the task, ${PLAYER}? If so, I bid you good fortune. Return to me when your patrol is complete.'

'There are still a lot of Orcs down there? I expect there are still hundreds of stragglers wandering back into the encampments after fleeing from the force of our initial assault.
'The real problems will start when the first elements of that eastern army begin to arrive... we must be ready for them.'
Patrol the first point in northern Gathbúrz
Patrol the second point in northern Gathbúrz
Patrol the third point in northern Gathbúrz
Patrol the fourth point in northern Gathbúrz

Scouting in Force
Handelen fears that the Orcs are mustering their forces in the northern reaches of Gathbúrz.
'Our survival here depends upon performing routine patrols to sight the approach of the Enemy.'

The first point is north-east of Thangúlhad. The second point is to the north-west of the first, direcdly north of Kúfuzg. The third point is directly north of Thangúlhad, a little south of Búrzkala. The fourth point is just north-west of Thangúlhad.
You should scout the waypoints of the patrol that Handelen has asked you to undertake and defeat any enemies you might find there.

Handelen is at Thangúlhad in Gathbúrz.

Mirefang has been defeated

'There is one more task I would have you do for us if you can, randir. While you were away, I felt a great malicious gaze bent upon me from this very spot. My eyes were barely able to pierce this gloom, but I beheld at some distance a terrifying cat. He does not seem pleased with our presence in his swamp.
'I saw him pace off to the west, surely towards his lair, wherever that may be. This cat is as death itself, and surely you will find a trail of death around the home of this terrible beast.
'Go west if you dare, ${PLAYER}, and attempt to remove this great threat. He will strike soon if we do not, and I fear to match wills with such a fiend.'
'You have slain this menace, then? Thank you, ${PLAYER}. I cannot tell you how relieved I am. I have not felt at rest since I first beheld the brutal beast.'
Summon Mirefang and defeat him
Talk to Laidhriel at Estolad Mernael
Terror of the Drownholt
A large and wary panther called Mirefang stalks near the Pool of Creeping Death, feeding upon the corpses of those who have died there.
'You should hunt for this cat I saw, ${PLAYER}. This swamp is perilous enough without menaces of his ilk stalking about in the gloom.'

The vicious cat Mirefang can be found to the west of Estolad Mernael, near the Pool of Creeping Death.
You should summon and defeat this vicious hunter before he decides to hunt you, for his attack is sure to be deadly.

Laidhriel awaits you at the entrance to Estolad Mernael in the Drownholt, east of Mirefang's lair.
You should return to Laidhriel and inform her of your defeat of Mirefang.

'We have split into many factions in order to organize our assault on Dol Guldur. While we feel that this is the best way to plan our offence, we worry very much during those periods in which we hear nothing from our kindred while they establish their footing.
'It is not safe to send scouts out until we hear from the advancing party, so we wait. If you are going to Emyn Lûm, will you keep an eye out for the host that marched thence? They will welcome your presence gladly, for we are stretched in every direction.
'Emyn Lûm is a dangerous wilderness to the east of here, closer to Dol Guldur. You should seek Fuirgam, for he is a commander of that faction. Be wary, ${PLAYER}; keep your wits about you! We do not know what evils lie yonder.'

'Mae govannen! How fare my kin in the Dourstocks? I am glad you have come -- I was anxious for word from Athradnir. Now that we have established a line of communication, there will be but one more small burden lifted from my shoulders.
'There is much to be done between marches, as I am sure you can understand. Will you be staying with us for a while?'
Talk to Fuirgam in Emyn Lum
The Road to Emyn Lûm
Athradnir is anxious to hear what has become of the Malledhrim host who marched east to Emyn Lûm, for the closer the Elves draw to Dol Guldur, the more perilous the journey becomes.
'Fuirgam is a commander among the host that marched east to Emyn Lûm -- you should speak with him first.'

Fuirgam should be among the Malledhrim at their stronghold in Emyn Lûm.
You should seek Fuirgam and establish a line of communication between the Elves of Emyn Lûm and the Dourstocks.
Collected dry branches (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'How these fires smoke! How can this poor steed recover when the air is filled with putrid fumes from this polluted kindling? This will not do....
'The firewood we have collected around this camp has been completely soaked through with vile swamp-water and dries poorly in this climate. It burns through far too quickly, and we must tend it constantly. The smoke is terrible, as you see!
'I saw a rise to the west of here where some thick trees seemed to grow in a great cluster. Would you be so good as to search there for dry kindling? You may be able to find some on that higher ground. It would be a great help to us.'
'Thank you, randir! These branches will burn much better than the soggy, rotting logs we picked up around here. This place will be a little more hospitable to us now.'
'Have you found any firewood yet? Dry branches might be found on higher ground in the Drownholt.'
Collect dry branches (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring the branches to Rocheledh at Estolad Mernael
A Smoking Fire
Most of the kindling immediately surrounding Estolad Mernael is very damp and causes the camp-fires to smoke and burn badly. Dry wood must be sought in other parts of the Drownholt's swampy terrain.
'Search on higher ground to the west of our camp. Hopefully some better firewood can be collected there.'

Dry branches for kindling can be found throughout the Drownholt where the ground is a little higher, due west of Estolad Mernael.
You should collect dry branches for the Elves at Estolad Mernael.

Rocheledh is in Estolad Mernael in the Drownholt, tending his sick horse.
You should bring the dry branches for kindling to Rocheledh, who will be grateful for the cleaner camp-fires.

'I have ill news, ${PLAYER}. It seems that we've got a little vermin problem, if you will. I was minding my own business and taking a stroll through the cellars beneath this tower when I heard a bit of a noise.
'Well, I put my ear to the rock for a quick listen, and what do you think I hear? Picks and shovels, ${PLAYER}, picks and shovels! What's more I could hear goblin voices muttering in Black Speech. It seems that a band of goblins has been set to work and mean either to bring down Thangúlhad around our ears or invade it from below.
'Either way, we've got to stop them and quickly! My brother and I can deal with the goblins' works, but we'll need a stalwart companion to keep the vermin off of us while we're about our labours. What say you?'
<rgb=#00ff00>WARNING: Death From Below is a high difficulty solo challenge quest. Beware, all who enter therein.</rgb>

'That should be the end of the goblin-sappers. You have my thanks for your aid.
'I wouldn't be surprised if they try again after they finish licking their wounds, but from what Rodelleth tells me, we will not be here much longer anyway.'

'Hello there, ${PLAYER}. Have you had a look down there in the Orc-camps yet? It's a real mess. Orcs and goblins aren't too good at staying organized when you put a good fright into them, from what I've seen.
'Anyhow, I noticed that they have got the oil for their siege-engines piled up in great heaps of boxes and crates, just lying about. That's dangerous...you never know when it might catch fire!
'If you were to steal a few of their fire-pots and use them to set the rest ablaze, I imagine it would help add a warm glow to these dreary slopes for the evening.'
'Ha! I could see the blazes from here, ${PLAYER}! That will teach the fool goblins to leave dangerous toys lying about! Good work, my friend.'

'The foolish goblins have left their fire-oil stores out where they can be tampered with...I trust that you will do what needs to be done....'

'So, we've managed to capture this tower, and it grants us a fine look at the surrounding land, but one thing I have seen that doesn't sit well with me is the Orcs moving a number of catapults nearby.
'The weather here in Mirkwood is not the finest at the best of times, but in a few hours it's going to include a fair hail of falling rocks, if you catch my meaning.
'Be a good sort and see if you can set a few of those on fire, would you? It is one thing being rained on day and night, but I'm not wanting a sharp crack on my head to go with it.'

'So you managed to wreck a few of the Orc's toys? Well that's done then, on to the next order of business shall we?
'Time is of the essence, if we're to bring that great pile of rock down around the ears of those cloaked fiends!'

'Good day, ${PLAYER}! It is a fine day for a battle, don't you think? It will be a pleasure indeed to see that dark spire crumble, but we've got some messy business to attend to in Gathbúrz first.
'The goblins have built a number of nasty little toys for the Orcs of Gathbúrz, a few of which we have captured here... but the rest have to go. These Elves may be the finest warriors I've seen outside of Thorin's Hall, but fancy swords and bows don't help much with a yard-long bolt pinning them to the ground!
'Those ballistae are the greatest threat to Rodelleth and her warriors, so you should deal with those first. They are easy enough to break once you reach them. A couple of good strikes with a hammer or blade will put them out of commission quickly.'

You can scarcely hold these robes as you fear that the wraith who bore them may yet be lurking within their depths.
Steeling yourself, you shake the tattered robes in search of any clue as to the identity of their former owner and their fate.
Finding nothing, you decide it best to take them with you to Belvaer. Perhaps he will know what to do with them.

Belvaer takes the robes from you and looks them over, utterly nonplussed.
'You have accomplished that which I never dared hope, even in the farthest reaches of my dreams. Our entire campaign here may very well owe its success to you and your good companions.
'Your deed is far too great for me to honour properly, ${PLAYER}. You should take these with you and go to Celeborn in Lórien. Take this coin with you and present both to him. He will wish to hear your story.
'May the grace of the Elves guide you on your way, ${PLAYER}. You are a true hero.'

'Well met, ${PLAYER}. I am well aware of your deeds prior to our campaign in Dol Guldur. I have heard also of your most recent exploits to further our cause there.
'Those robes you carry are most foul indeed; I would believe your tale just from these, let alone the coin of challenge given to you by Belvaer.
'Take these as gratitude for your heroic efforts in our campaign against the enemy forces at Dol Guldur.'
Talk to Belvaer at Dol Guldur
Talk to Celeborn in Caras Galadhon
Barad Guldur: The End of the Nightmare

Upon your ascent, you faced and bested one of the Nine Ringwraiths in battle. The robes of the Nazgûl are the proof you bear of this incredible deed, and the Elves below will wish to see what you have accomplished this day.
'My thanks are not enough now, mellon! You should go to Celeborn and tell him the story you just told me. Show him these robes. Your feat should not go unnoticed in the chaos of this war.'

Belvaer stands below at Dol Guldur.
You should speak with Belvaer and show him the remnants of the Nazgûl you slew.

Celeborn is in Caras Galadhon, his fair Elven-home in Lothlórien.
Belvaer gave you a coin to present to Celeborn along with the tattered robes of the Nazgûl you slew.

Challenge: Dúnlang

Not all who occupy Garth Agarwen are given over to corruption. Some are taken from their homes or the sites where they worked and brought to the ruins where they are enchanted and taught a new way of thought through foul magic. The Créoth warlord, Dúnlang, is possessed of the gifts of Angmar and captures members of the Eglain to corrupt and turn into mindless minions of the Red-maid.

Dúnlang was given the power to enslave weaker minds, and many of the Eglain have gone missing over the years. He makes his home deep within the ruins of the Garth Agarwen Fortress and is in the process of converting members of the Eglain into devoted members of the Créoth clan. You should save them from the influence of this man, but not harm them in the process.
One of the Red-maid's Créoth has been defeated

'My sisters are far from me...I cannot hear their songs or feel their gentle breath among the trees. Barren are those trees, nearly lifeless, choked out by roots bloated with something that has a bitter taste of iron. Where are you my sisters, and what is before me?
'I cannot see beyond the red of this land, but I sense something sweet among the bitter ferns and swollen roots. Are you real? Am I still imprisoned in the land?
'There is life in you -- I feel this. There must be life elsewhere in these lands. Perhaps I can find this life anew and nurture it back to health.'
Aid in the cleansing of the Red-maid
Allow the Créoth to sacrifice themselves to the Red-maid
Challenge: Naruhel

The Red-maid is lost -- or so it seems -- to the corruption wrought upon her land at the hands of corrupt Men. These Men stand before her, ready to sacrifice themselves for the Red-maid, and they deserve this fate. However, the nobility of your blood will be a greater reward for her, and when these Men fall before her willingly, she will see that the noble are attempting to destroy her and ignoble keeping her this way.

The Créoth will sacrifice themselves to the Red-maid to restore her strength and connexion to the corruption within the swamp. These Men deserve nothing better than death, and your presence in standing against the Red-maid may alert some part of her to the folly of her ways. You should let these Men die and strengthen the Red-maid, then defeat her. Perhaps a piece of her will understand that the corruption has grown too great, and she must return to the natural world which she was once part of.

Fil Gashan is the barracks and training grounds of the Orcs in Moria. Within those walls, a fearsome general has been readying his troops for an assault upon the Elves of Lothlórien to the east of Khazad-dûm. Brogur and Bósi's dwarves, wishing to reclaim Moria, intend to prevent this at any cost, for they would see the Elves and dwarves reinstate old alliances for the good of both.

Fil Gashan is far to the south-west of the Twenty-first Hall, and General Talug can be found in the depths of that place.

The Forges of Khazad-dûm, once a glorious smith-hall for the Dwarves of Moria, have fallen into evil hands. The Forges now serve the Orc-masters of Moria and are used to build all manner of weapons and war-machines for an assault against fair Lothlórien. Brogur and Bósi's dwarves, wishing to reclaim Moria, intend to prevent this at any cost, for they would see the Elves and dwarves reinstate old alliances for the good of both peoples.

Once a great and beautiful cross-roads of Moria, the Grand Stair is a vile haven of many of the gathered tribes of Orcs. Igash, regarded as a leader by all of the varied groups, gathers tribute from every tribe to give to Mazog, the mightiest and greatest of Orcs in Khazad-dûm. The dwarves wish to unseat Igash's Orcs from this Grand Stair and stop Mazog from receiving valuable and unsavoury gifts.

Many tribes of Orcs prowl the Grand Stair, south-east of the Twenty-first Hall.
Geirr has asked you to defeat Igash in the Grand Stair without defeating any other members of the Moria Orc-tribes. In doing so, you will assist in efforts to reclaim that cross-roads for the dwarves and prove your great worth to Sigurd.

No living Man, Elf, hobbit, or dwarf will want to set foot in Skûmfil, grave of the Orcs, feeding and breeding ground of vile kergrim and slavering gredbyg. There, the Orcs pile their dead, and there, disgusting creatures feast on rotten waste.

Hwandrin and her brood ever belch unwholesome filth upon the corpse-ridden halls of Skûmfil, south-east of the Twenty-first Hall.
Sigurd has challenged you to defeat Hwandrin in Skûmfil as proof of your worth as a warrior. Her threat is great, yet few are wilful enough to withstand the menace of such an old and malevolent being.

Challenge: Caeryg

In the Water-works, ancient Caeryg rumble through the halls. Their presence is causing the Dwarves of Khazad-dûm great concern. They often fight in packs and are quite dangerous to those who attempt to disturb them.
Deep in the Water-works, there are great Caeryg lurking. You should find them in the hidden rooms of the Water-works and banish them from Moria.
In the farthest depths of the Water-works, there is the greatest of Caeryg, Caerlug. Defeat him to claim your reward.

Challenge: Thaguzg (Daily)

Once filled with the thunder of dwarf-hammers and smiths, the Halls of Crafting are now dominated by foul Orcs. Led by the evil Black Uruk, Thaguzg, they are building weapons for a massive assault upon Lothlórien itself.
You should defeat Thaguzg without his minions' assistance. They must not reach him, or great woe will befall your fellowship.
Defeated Ergoth
Defeat Ergoth
Do not kill all of a single type of Ergoth's minions
Challenge: Ergoth (Daily)

High up in Zirakzigil, there lies a cave. This cave was a means to harness the light of the sun and bring it down to the depths of Moria. Years of neglect have brought this system to its knees, and now the cave is home to merrevail, Wargs, and other dark creatures.
You should defeat the morroval-queen, Ergoth while she is at her strongest. If you weaken her first, you will not be able to claim the greatest of rewards.

In the depths of Dol Guldur, prisoners languish in the stronghold's vile Dungeons, lost to those who care for them. Only the Dungeon's Warden knows their fate, but they cannot be freed as long as he stands guard.

You should save as many prisoners as you can while you engage in battle with the Warden of the Dungeons.

You should speak with Carl Proudfoot and inform him of your success.

'Welcome, welcome! This is quite an odd event, don't you think? To race around on these great tall beasts -- I am not sure I like it at all! But folk come from near and far to take a chance on this game and prove their skill.
'The rules are very simple -- race through each gate, and you mustn't fall off your steed before the time runs out. When you see two gates next to one another, you must choose which path to take, be it high or low. The low path may be muddy, and the high is sure to be dry, but precarious indeed. There will be other hurdles to disrupt you as well.
'Do you feel up for this challenge? Only the most spirited riders should even attempt such a feat! It is sure to be very dangerous. I myself would never attempt such a thing!'
'I have never seen such excellent riding in these parts, ${PLAYER}! I am very impressed. Take these leaves and my congratulations!'

'Scattered among the ruins below, fell spirits of Morgoth have risen and now haunt the grounds. These creatures have begun appearing in staggeringly large numbers near Sâd Doldúr.

Dear ${PLAYER},
This is your invitation to the Yule Festival! I have my hands full as usual, but there are new Events for you to enjoy. Bring this note to Gísli Strongclub in Thorin's Hall, for he has requested all the help he can get, and he shall introduce you to all of the excellent and exciting events being offered this fine winter in the meantime.

'Hello, hello! I see you have found our new ale-hall, and I am glad you have, for I need all the hands I can get! People have come from all around to steal my beer. It's not just any beer, but the most glorious beer in all of Middle-earth.
'The problem is that once someone tastes it, it seems they can't get enough, and now they are attacking from all sides to get at it. I'm afraid there is nowhere near enough to go around. Please say you'll help me! The whole festival is at stake.'

Instance: Challenge at the Gate

One of the Nine known to mortals as The Gloom of Nurn has emerged to answer your challenge at the gates of Dol Guldur. You and your allies must gather all of your strength if you have any hope of defeating him and his forces.
Defeat the Gloom of Nurn and his forces before the gates of Dol Guldur.

'The walls of Dol Guldur are beyond our power to topple unless and until the power of the Nine is broken, but that does not mean that we are powerless against them. Long has the overweening pride of the Enemy been a weakness to exploit, since days of Morgoth himself.
'The task we face now is not so different than that of old, and so shall our strategy likewise be similar, for I would have you gather a host to lay siege to the gate of Fennas Guldur and issue a challenge against those who lie within. If one of their captains -- perhaps even one of the Nine -- can be drawn into battle, then we can deliver a stinging blow against them that they will not soon forget!
'There is a stone near the gate of Fennas Guldur from which you should issue your challenge. I will give you fair warning, though: even though singly the Nazgûl are not as powerful as they are in greater numbers, they are still fell beings of greater power than you. I suggest that you keep your guard, or you may meet your fate at Fennas Guldur.'

'You and your companions have defeated none less than the Gloom of Nurn, one of the Nine, in a place where his strength was at its greatest! Well fought indeed!
'I fear this victory is temporary, however, for it is not in our power to destroy the Ringwraiths, but Nurn is weakened and bereft of his form for a time, forced to flee to Minas Morgul until he can gather his tattered strength and is recloaked.
'It is the Gloom that would most likely have stood at the vanguard of any strike against Lothlórien, but no longer! Unfortunately, with the fell-beasts they ride to speed his return, I do not think it will be long ere he is seen again.'

Collected pristine webbing (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Good day to you, though the circumstances are dark ones. I have heard tell that you are a worthy and brave adventurer who has aided the Malledhrim in this deadly venture into Mirkwood. Though my cause is less worthy -- but no less deadly -- I have need of your aid if you will help me.
'The silk of the giant spiders of Mirkwood is of surpassing quality and has myriad uses if it can be collected pristine and fresh. I have need of quite a bit of this silk -- not the least to produce bandages for those wounded in these battles.
'I myself am well-studied in the lore of runecraft, and I may have some writings here that are of interest to you to trade for your efforts.'

'You have brought the webbing I requested?
'Ah! My sincerest thanks to you! Such creatures do not stalk the realm of Lothlórien, so it is rare for me to have the opportunity to collect so much of their silk.
'What can I offer you in trade for your efforts?'
YOU SHOULD NOT SEE THIS
Collect pristine webbing (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Legindir at Ost Galadh
Silken Strands
The silk of the spiders in the Scuttledells is very strong and useful for a variety of purposes.
'Have you brought me the spider-silk I requested?'

Spiders can be found throughout the Scuttledells in Mirkwood.
Legindir has asked you to collect pristine webbing from the spiders and environs of the Scuttledells.
Collected an iron ingot (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collected burnished worm-scales (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Ah, ${PLAYER}, it's good that you have come by... I have a proposition for you! Though most don't know it, the iron-lodes in this section of Khazad-dûm always had trace amounts of mithril in it. My forefather tried for over a hundred years to find some way to extract it, but never had any luck.
'I have other uses in mind for it, but I need some rather large quantities of the black iron that the Orcs have been using to forge their weapons in the Flaming Deeps. The Orcs often trade and barter the ingots among each other for other goods so they are easy enough to come across.
'Do you think you could get ahold of a good stack of them for me? Oh, it almost slipped my mind, but I also need a number of worm-scales as well. Worms are plentiful down here, so see if you can get me a few of their scales while you're about it, would you?'

'Are these the items I asked you to gather? Excellent!
'Would that I could extract the mithril from them, but better dwarves than I have tried and failed. Nevertheless, the debased alloy itself should prove useful for my work.
'Now then, what can I offer you in return for your efforts? I have a few things that you might find most useful!'
YOU SHOULD NOT SEE THIS
Collect iron ingots (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collect burnished worm-scales (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Myndil at Anazârmekhem
Crafting: Trace Metals

The black iron forged in the Flaming Deeps of Moria often has slight traces of truesilver in it. Though the precious metal is not recoverable, this odd alloy does have its uses for knowledgeable masters of lore and craft.
'If you bring me the items I requested, I'll have an attractive reward for you!'

Iron ingots and burnished worm-scales can be collected from the Orcs and worms inhabiting the Flaming Deeps.
Myndil has asked you to collect black iron and burnished worm-scales for him.

Myndil is at Anazârmekhem in the Flaming Deeps of Moria.
You should bring the iron and scales you collected to Myndil at once.

'You think it's strange to be talking to a cat? Well, I think it's strange to be talking to you, ${RACE}! Would you like to be flagged as having completed Volume II Book 8 of the Epic quest series? If so, speak to me again!
'Do I even need to tell you how this works? Oh well, just in case you weren't paying attention: completion of this quest will flag you as having completed Volume II Book 8 of the Epic quest.'
Level Up: Volume II: Book 8
Completion of this quest will flag your character as having completed all the quests in Book 8 of the Epic quest series of Volume II.
Talk to Elevensies to complete Volume II, Book 8!
Challenge: Battle of the Sword-hall Completed
Light the Challenger's Brazier, then engage and defeat all three champions at once
Challenge: Battle of the Sword-hall

In the Sword-hall of Dol Guldur, the fell champions of the arena train tirelessly to hone their prowess in battle. You have been challenged to prove your superior might by defeating all three champions of the Sword-hall at once.

The Sword-hall is at Dol Guldur, the enemy stronghold of Mirkwood.
You should endeavour to defeat all three champions of the Sword-hall at once -- a great challenge that will earn you much renown.
Challenge: Meat for the Warg-pens Completed
Clear the pens of all meat-slabs
Challenge: Meat for the Warg-pens

The Wargs of Dol Guldur gain unusual strength from eating specially-prepared meat. You have been challenged to defeat the Wargs who have already consumed this vile feed, right down to the last morsel.

The slavering Wargs reside in the Warg-pens of Dol Guldur.
You must goad the Wargs to consume all the slabs of vile meat located throughout the encounter, then attempt to best them in their strengthened state.
The History of Audaghaim
The Lost Explorers

'In the shadow of Dol Guldur, the small outpost known as Helethir has been established by the Golden Host. A dear friend of mine, Danfennas, has begun to investigate the ashen colour of the trees within the Ashenslades, and I wish for you to speak with him.
'Will you travel to Helethir and seek out and assist Danfennas in learning what malady has affected the trees in the area? Whatever blight has fallen upon the Ashenslades, it cannot be of a natural order.
'You can reach Helethir by travelling the path north and east of here.'
'I had hoped that Perindúr would be able to send someone to help. Our fear is that the sorcerers of Sâd Doldúr are the cause of the blight that is gripping the trees of the Ashenslades.'
Talk to Danfennas at Helethir
Travel to Helethir

To the south of Dol Guldur, Danfennas seeks out information regarding the pale quality of the trees around the Ashenslades. He has joined several others in Helethir, a small camp to the south of Dol Guldur, to investigate the area.
'Helethir lies to the north-east. Go there at once, ${PLAYER}.'

Danfennas is at Helethir, north-east of Mithechad.
Perindúr has asked you to speak with his friend Danfennas regarding the plague upon the trees of the Ashenslades.
You have defeated Giltârk (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Seems as though we have been here forever...still, there seems to be something happening in the hills not far from here to the north.
'The other day while Sam and Dale were walking in the valley a man, appearing badly injured and wearing a heavy cowl approached me for some ointments. I happily obliged, but as he made his way toward the north I was concerned. He seemed to have an odd gait.
'With the discovery of those Orcs and half-orcs up in those ruins, I am beginning to think that he may have been one. Maybe you can find him and put my fears at ease by giving him a proper rest?'

'I can not believe that I sold items to him. Though you say that they look much like Men, I should know better. I have seen these creatures for some time now.
'I thank you for your efforts.'
Find and defeat Giltârk (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Speak with Aggie Honeysuckle
Not What He Appeared

Aggie Honeysuckle mentioned that she was approached by a brutally beaten man, which she is now questioning was actually a Man. She has asked you to assist her in finding out if the man is indeed, what he appeared to be.

'Not sure what his name was but he wore dark greys and had a patch over his eye. If you find him, please do your best to rid him from the land. I would hate to think that I helped those things in any way.'

Make your way north to the ruins in the northern Weather Hills and hunt down the leader of the Half-orcs and Orcs there.
Aggie is concerned that she may have helped the half-orcs or Orcs in the ruins to the north and asked you for help in getting rid of her strange patron.

Return to Aggie at the hunter camp near the bridge in the Midgewater Pass and tell her that you have defeated Giltârk.
Aggie is at her encampment to the south of the ruins where you found Giltârk and the other Orcs and half-orcs.
Collected furled banners (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'A moment of your time, if you can spare it. There is a crumbling ruin of a fort to the north of this location, slightly east as well. This fort is overrun by Orcs and half-orcs.
'This alone is cause for concern, but they fly banners of the White Hand. In our travels through the valley here, we have seen these Orcs and half-orcs growing more and more brazen. We need to collect proof that they are organized and get that information into the hands of the authorities in Bree.
'Go to the ruins, get the flags, and return them to me furled so as to not cause concern when we bring them to Bree.'

'I am certain that these will prove useful. These Orcs and half-orcs continue to force their way further and further towards Bree-land's borders. We must alert the Constables and see if there is a way to slow them down.
'Thank you, ${PLAYER}.'
Collect furled banners (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring the furled banners to Dale Sageford
Furled Banners of the White Hand

Dale Sageford directed you to the ruins north-east of the hunter's camp in search of the flags posted by the Enemy. He believes that they will be invaluable in assisting the Constables in Bree in finding a solution to the arrival of these fiends and the menace presented by the White Hand.
'So, did you find the banners?'

Flags stand among the ruins and valleys north-east of Dale Sageford's encampment.
Dale Sageford remains at his encampment near the bridge over the Midgwater Pass. You should return to him when you have collected the flags from the ruins in the north-east as he asked.

Dale Sageford is at the hunter's camp, south-west of where you found the banners.
You should return to Dale Sageford with the furled Orc-banners.
Defeated half-orcs in the north-east hills (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeated an Orc in the north-east hills (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'I have seen these Orcs and half-orcs as we get a little bolder in our strolls from this site. Each day they seem to be sending scouts closer and closer toward Combe, but they seem to be looking for a way to pass around Bree.
'I know that they are up to no good and I hope that you are able to help me out here.
'I want to cut this foe down, now, before they execute whatever terrible plans they have for this land. Are you willing, able and ready to do so? They can be found to the north in the ruins there. Go there and crush this foe before it grows too large to contain.'

'Serves them right. What are they planning? We should send word onto Grimbriar. He will likely send scouts to watch this area closely in the future.
'Though, the southrons keep him busy these days.'
Defeat half-orcs in the north-east hills (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeat Orcs in the north-east hills (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Sam Thistlebur at his camp
Orcs and Half-orcs in the North-east
Sam Thistlebur believes that the Orcs and half-orcs in the ruins to the north are a terrible blight on the land and wants your help in driving them out.
'You will find the Orcs and half-orcs to the north amongst the leaning ruins on the hilltops and in the valleys below. Be cautious they seem very tough.'

Make your way to the ruins north of the hunter's encampment and defeat the Orcs and half-orcs you find there.
Sam Thistlebur directed you to make your way to the north to fight and slay the Orcs and half-orcs in the ruins there.

Return to Sam at his encampment south of the camp where you fought and defeated the Orcs and half-orcs of the White Hand.
Sam is waiting for your return. It is certain that he will be pleased with all that you have accomplished.
You have defeated Temair the Devoted

'The Men who dwell beyond these walls are misguided and lost. So lost that they cannot be redeemed according to Radagast; their atrocities against nature are so great that there is no forgiveness.
'They are lead by a woman. A terrible woman named Temair who they believe is a link to the Red-maid and because of this she is revered as something greater than they are.
'I ask that you push beyond these walls and seek out this woman. Bring her down and prove these misguided Men that they have misplaced their faith.'

'It is good to know that she is gone. It is wrong of people to place themselves above others and claim divinity when doing so.
'You have our respect, ${PLAYER}.'
Defeat Temair the Devoted
Return to Arienh
Temair the Terrible

Arienh knows that there is a leader amongst the Créoth in the ruins of Garth Agarwen, a terrifying woman who the Men revere as a conduit to the Red-maid.
She has asked that you disprove this fallacy by defeating the woman and proving to the Créoth that their faith is misplaced.
'You will find Temair before the entrances to the Fortress and Arboretum of Garth Agarwen. She preaches there by a large pyre. Seek her out and destroy her.'

Temair can be found before the entrances to the Arboretum and Fortress within the area of Garth Agarwen.
Arienh asked that you bring the leader of the Créoth, a terrible woman named Temair, to justice. She preaches within the confines of Garth Agarwen.

Return to Arienh at her encampment at the entrance to Garth Agarwen.
Temair was found exactly where Arienh told you she would be. Dispatching Temair proved simple enough and you should now return to Arienh.
Collected war-orders (${NUMBER}/10)
Collected Target List

'There is much work to do. We know that the Enemy has begun to mobilize and march in several different regions of Middle-earth, but we have yet to glean their targets. Without knowing where they are going, we cannot adequately prepare defences and ensure the people will be safe.
'I need you to go out and hunt down anything that may have orders. Orcs, goblins, trolls, uruks, Warg-riders, anything that would be entrusted with plans. It matters not where they are, hunt them in Forochel, Eregion, Bree, Mirkwood, Angmar, anywhere. These orders are important enough that all of the Enemy will have them.
'Once you have collected several of them you will need to find a target list. Bring them all back to any Skirmish Captain. We will decipher the orders, compare then against the target list, then send you off to either prepare the defences or reclaim what they have already taken.'

'I know of the messages from my grandmother, ${PLAYER}, and I know too that my father has asked you to gather the Dúnedain that they may ride south to the aid of Aragorn.
'We knew this day would come, he and I, and have both long prepared for its arrival. It has been my part to craft an item of beauty and of use, an item Aragorn will have need of before all is done. He knows of its making, and it will be a sign to him that the hour has indeed arrived when he must seize that which is his. I hope it will be a comfort to him, too, in distant lands.
'When the Dúnedain are all assembled, I will send for you. I must be sure someone can bear this item to him. I will call you before the Rangers depart.'

'Golodir was a strong man and true of heart, but my father is right. He has suffered much. I did not know.
'I know very little of Corunir, beyond that he be loyal to a fault. Did he not remain in Aughaire for years, awaiting Golodir's return from beyond the Rammas Deluon?'

'I am pleased you received my summons, ${PLAYER}. I apologize for being so close as to the reason for its urgency, but there are dangers on the road, and I did not wish any information that might do us harm to fall into the hands of evil Men.
'Two days ago, courier-hawks arrived in Rivendell bearing messages from Lórien. The messages were short, but even in their brevity they caused me pause.
'The messages are from the Lady Galadriel. I understand some of their meaning, but I can only guess at the full import of her words.'

'And so it shall be, ${PLAYER}. You will walk the paths of Eriador one more time, in search of these Dúnedain. They will gather others of their kin, and when all is made ready, the Grey Company will set forth.
'It will be done as Galadriel of Lórien has asked. We respond to her messages with the haste we must, and with the messenger those messages deserve: a ${CLASS} of proven loyalty, to gather the Grey Company in time!'

'It will not be easy to gather the Dúnedain as quickly as it must be done, ${PLAYER}. It would be best for you to bring the message to certain of Aragorn's kin, that they may then speak to the rest of their people, while you travel to those of more distant lands.
'I have prepared the names of those to whom you must speak. Walk with me, and I will tell you where they can be found.'

'Once you have met Radanir in the Trollshaws and told him that the Rangers must assemble, you should travel west into the Lone-lands. At the base of Weathertop, you will find Candaith. He is sure to join the Grey Company.
'After you have spoken to Candaith, you will travel into Bree-land to speak with Saeradan at his cabin. He is not as prone to wandering as others of his kin, but he must be told of Aragorn's need.
'But there are other Rangers you must find.'

'Halros, Halbarad, and Calenglad will speak with others of the Dúnedain near the borders of the Shire and throughout the North Downs and Evendim, but there are two more Rangers you will need to find personally. The distances are simply too great for anyone but you to cover in time.'

'Very good, ${PLAYER}. Perhaps now we will have an answer for why this haste is necessary.
'Is that Elladan? It is! Perhaps he will have some answers for us.'
'Very good, ${PLAYER}. Many hopes rest on your journey through Eriador to gather the Dúnedain for their journey!'
