'The sons of Elrond have already left for Thorenhad to prepare for the coming journey. Elrohir did say that one of the Dúnedain, a Ranger named Radanir, was staying for a few days at their camp. As Thorenhad is nearest to Rivendell, you should travel there first to speak to Radanir before seeking the others.
'I have met few of Aragorn's kin, but Radanir is known to me, for he journeys oft into the trackless Ettenmoors and often stays here in Rivendell. For a time, my brethren sought to convince him to join the company in song in the Hall of Fire, as Aragorn would, but Radanir would have none of it.
'Travel to Thorenhad, north of the Bruinen Gorges in the Trollshaws, and speak to Elrohir. He will introduce you to Radanir. Once the Ranger is told of the messages from Lórien, you can seek out the others Master Elrond suggested.'

'You are looking for Radanir, ${PLAYER}? He left not long ago, and he took no horse; the Dúnedain will ride when they must, but he has confided to me that he is more comfortable when on foot.
'Always behind his words to me was a current of...I do not know how best to say it, other than to say that Radanir seemed always to be waiting for something, somehow. I wonder if the tidings you bring are those for which he has waited so long? I wonder too if they will send him from the Trollshaws, and for how long? I will miss his visits if this be so, for I will not remain in this Middle-earth for much longer.
'I will not delay your errand for personal reasons, ${PLAYER}. Radanir spoke to me of his plans. He learned that a war-band of Orcs from the Ettenmoors has established a camp within the Laenan Caves here in the Trollshaws, and sought to confront them. The Laenan Caves are in the north-west reaches of the Gladdalf, the wood-troll infested marsh of the North Trollshaws.'

'Aragorn is my chieftain, and it is my duty to go to his aid, though all the dangers of Middle-earth lie in between. This is the moment for which the Dúnedain have prepared, and I will not now abandon my kin.
'I have learned that an Orc raiding party from the Ettenmoors has established a camp within this warren of tunnels, ${PLAYER}. I cannot leave them here, unchallenged. Will you brave these caves and deal with these foes? Somewhere deep within this confusing warren is the entrance to a once-abandoned tomb of Men. If the Orcs have found it, that is where their leaders will be. Thorenhad is less than a day's march from this place, and I will not suffer these Orcs to live that they may threaten what I hold dear.
'I will make ready to depart, as you have asked, but I will be grateful if you destroy the Orcs and their leaders within the Laenan tunnels and the ruins that lie at their back. After you have done so, return to Elrohir at Thorenhad and tell him of your success. The sons of Elrond lost their mother to such a party of Orcs; they would not forgive us if we let these foes be.'

'I thought to give Radanir word of our meeting at my father's house, ${PLAYER}, so he would have some expectation of the road ahead, but it seems he has left Thorenhad and gone again into the wilderness of the Trollshaws.
'He has left a few parcels here, so I am sure he intends to return, but he should be told the message you bear as soon as may be. I and my brother have already begun to assemble some of the supplies the Rangers will need as they head south, but it will take some time before they are ready.
'Speak to Elweleth, by the horses, for she will know where Radanir planned to journey, if any will. Radanir is slow to laugh and to smile, but in Elweleth's company, I have observed it most frequently.'

'You have given Radanir the message? Good. He will be able to find some others among the Dúnedain if they are to be found within the Trollshaws.
'But now you must travel west to find others of Aragorn's kin.'

'The Dúnedain may be scattered across the wilds of Eriador, but my brother and I know the locations of some few, and from those few will you learn where others may be found.
'The Ranger Candaith was a help to us as we scoured the lands to the south following the rage of the Bruinen; we spoke as often as speed would allow on that journey, and he had many interesting tales to tell of the Lone-lands. You will find his camp there, at the base of Amon Sûl...of Weathertop.
'Tell him that Aragorn has need of his kin. Candaith will be certain to join the Grey Company, for his loyalty to his chieftain cannot be questioned.'

'So the time has come at last to stand with Aragorn son of Arathorn, my lord and the chieftain of the Dúnedain. In my heart I knew the day would come, for as the shadows have lengthened, the need for Aragorn to accept his mantle has become all the more pressing.
'I have come to love the lands between The Forsaken Inn and the Last Bridge, and it will grieve me to leave them, but I will do so; I will join the Grey Company and travel south as you have asked.
'While I make ready to leave, will you retrieve a hidden cache of supplies I prepared some time ago? I left a sword, some gloves, and a few other supplies north-east of here, atop a small rise called Echad Sûl, in the shade of a tree. Recover this cache and bring it back to me, for I will have need of it in the lands to the south.'

'What are you looking at? It seems to me that these lands should be big enough for you to find a path that takes you out of my sight, little ${RACE}.'
Orskdulug follows your gaze and smirks.
'You like this sword? Found it, I did, and these gloves and a few choice other items. Sometimes you find these little caches in the wild, left by Rangers, I suspect. Easy pickings, if you ask me.
'Looks like you might be easy pickings, too. I'll be taking your gear and your coins, friend. Without a fight, or with one...it is all the same to me!'

'I would have been willing to part with the contents of the cache, ${PLAYER}; items hidden in the wild, once found, should go to their finders. But once Orskdulug sought to use my items to rob you, as far as I am concerned, he gave up his right to them.
'I am pleased to have them back. Thank you.'
'You did not recover the cache?'

'You should next bring your message to Saeradan, in Bree-land. He is more settled than some others of my kin, but no less a vital part of the Grey Company. We will have need of Saeradan's calming wisdom on the road south, for though we have need of haste, so too do we need to keep our wits about us. Too often can the hasty road lead to carelessness. Saeradan will help prevent this.
'Look for him at his cabin near the town of Bree, in Bree-land. He lives east of Thornley's Work-site, in the Northern Bree-fields.'
Candaith gives you a wistful smile.
'It is true, we don't know what we will find as we ride south. I look out over these Lone-lands and wonder what will happen to them when we have gone. But this is something we must do. Each of us has sworn an oath to Aragorn our chief, and none of us will break that oath. We know the risks. None of us would join the Grey Company if we felt its errand was not important enough to brave those risks. For my part, I will not give in to fear of the unknown. We all have our role to play, and I hope only that when I have played mine, the world will have been better for my having been in it.'

'That fellow Saeradan does come to the Pony from time to time, and we talk about the state of things in Bree. Not as often as I'd like, of course! For every moment of peace there are ten things that need doing, and no way to make them all fit in the time available! Still, I do what I can, and wouldn't trade the Pony for anything!
'Folk say Saeradan's a Ranger, but if he is, he's more respectable than most. Has a cabin just near Bree, you know, and even spares a smile for his neighbours, which is more than I've seen from some others of that kind.
'Will you look at me, going on and on like this! There's no time for idle chatter...there are foodstuffs sitting in one of the parlours that need to be brought out here for preparing. Will you go and fetch some of them? Apples, pears, mushrooms...you'll see the crate, you will, and you'll be a big help to me if you hurry!'

'Thank you! You've been a great help to me today, and I won't forget it. So much to do, so very much to do, but you're welcome to stay as long as you like. Join the company, sing a song, warm yourself by the fire!'
Barliman pauses and his eyes pass briefly over the crowd.
'There is one more thing, actually, ${PLAYER},' he says in a hushed tone.
'There have been a few rude types come to Bree lately, and they've been scaring off some of the townsfolk who like to come to the Pony of a night; regular visitors, you know, good folk who come by for a spot of ale and some cheer.
'Do you think you might have a word with the fellow at that table there? Uchdrud, I think his name is, and he's a coarse sort. Maybe you can encourage him to finish his mug of beer and find somewhere to go for the night? Only he hasn't rented any lodgings here, and I'd just as soon he took his loud friends somewhere else. I would tell him myself, but there's so much to do....'

'I see, ${PLAYER}. I will travel south with as many of the Dúnedain as can be gathered in haste. Aragorn has need of us, and that is all that we need know.'
Saeradan looks wistfully around the yard.
'I fear for the people of this land, ${PLAYER}, without the Dúnedain to protect them. Great numbers of an unruly sort have already come to Bree, and the brigands of the countryside will have no want for members while the Rangers are not around to keep their ranks in check.
'I will make ready to depart. While I do so, will you speak with Barliman at the Prancing Pony? He does not think much of Rangers, but I would have you ask him to take especial care of his Inn and the town for the next several months, if it comes to that. He will not understand, but I want him to have at least some warning that troubles may lie in store for Bree.'

'I was right to worry, then? I feared it was so. Very few of these people know that the safety they feel is the result of the tireless work of the Dúnedain.
'And yet our road must take us south, into lands far away from the well-meaning proprietor of the Prancing Pony. He may not trust Rangers, but my people are no less fond of him and his simple life than they are of their own sons and daughters. I hope his town and his inn will remain safe until we return...if return we can.'

'What did you say to me? I have as much a right to this table as anyone here. More so, once the rest of my friends get here! Oh, there will be changes around here, I don't mind telling you.'
Uchdrud scowls at you.
'Are you still here? You've made me mad, and now you're going to pay for it! I will see you outside, by the North-gate of Bree, if you have any courage at all. We won't be bothered there. I will teach you a lesson about respecting Uchdrud and his boys...a lesson this whole town is going to have to learn!'

'I didn't think you'd show, ${PLAYER}. We're going to own this town in a couple weeks, and that fat innkeeper in there will have to beg for table-scraps from Uchdrud and his boys.
'Just like you'll need to beg for mercy in a few moments, ${RACE}. I may even grant it!'

'Halros loves the Shire and its people and has watched over them for many years. It may not be easy for him to leave them, even upon an errand as urgent as that of the Grey Company.'

'I have walked of a time with Aragorn and the Wizard, Gandalf, at Sarn Ford, and they both spoke oft of their love for its people. I do not think they would wish the Shire to be undefended.

'My mind is made up, ${PLAYER}, and now it is time for you to continue with the task Lord Elrond of Rivendell has set before you: to gather more Dúnedain to swell the ranks of the Grey Company as it travels south to the aid of Aragorn.
'Your next journey should take you to Esteldín, the hidden encampment of the Rangers in the North Downs. Halbarad will surely wish to travel south with the Grey Company, but he is often away from Esteldín; speak with the Ranger Daervunn instead, and he will tell you where Halbarad may be found.
'Daervunn is often in the centre of Esteldín, seeing to the general defence of the people who live in the North Downs.'

'For long years have the Dúnedain wandered in the wilderness, ${PLAYER}. Your message confirms what I have long suspected: the hour is near at hand when my people must come forth. I will ride to the aid of my friend and chieftain, Aragorn son of Arathorn, and let no Man or beast stand in the path of the Grey Company!
'There is evil still here, ${PLAYER}, and if we Dúnedain leave Eriador to fend for itself, what then? We win little if, when all the deeds of the Age are done, the northern lands are lost to evil, their peoples destroyed.
'Daervunn told you why I have come to this place? Already I have destroyed three idols the Angmarim brought out of Carn Dûm, but I believe three remain. Destroy these statues of their most-prized leadership and the Angmarim here may abandon hope of raising Angmar into prominence again. Return to me when you have done so, and we can speak again.'

'You have completed what I started, ${PLAYER}, and I am grateful for that! You have my thanks, too, for bringing me word of Aragorn's need for the Dúnedain. We will ride to him with all the haste that can be mustered, through whatever perils await.
'Return now to Daervunn, in Esteldín, with this command: he is to select as many of the Rangers of that camp as he feels can be spared without jeopardizing the safety of the people of the North Downs. We ride to Aragorn, but I will not allow us to dismiss our responsibilities in Eriador.'

'You bring worrisome tidings, ${PLAYER}! What danger has Aragorn encountered in the distant south that makes the Dúnedain his closest allies? Perhaps I misspeak. Perhaps it is not that the Dúnedain are closest, but instead that they be the most true.
'Halbarad must hear what you have to say, but he left this morning to deal with a serious danger. Word came down to us that a number of foes fleeing from Angmar in the days following the defeat of the False King sought to establish a settlement in a cave in the North Downs.
'Halbarad travelled to this cave, now called Tham Úmdúr, to attempt to forestall or defeat these foes before they can use the relics they plundered from Carn Dûm to make the foundations of a new Angmar. Find Halbarad at Tham Úmdúr, in the shadow of Ost Crithlanc, far to the east of Esteldín, in Nan Amlug East, and give him your message. Help him end their plans before they begin.'

'I will do as Halbarad wishes. I too do not wish to endanger the people of the North Downs by our absence.
'I will speak with the rest of my kin here at Esteldín. Other lands wait for your message.'

Calenglad gazes for a moment out at the clear waters of Lake Evendim.
'I will go with the Grey Company. That is my duty, and I will not shy away from it. But first I want to save some of the relics of Annúminas from being plundered. 'The blood of the Dúnedain flows through my veins, and they will always be my people, but I have another people now as well, and I want them to be safe. I speak of the Lossoth. 'Gun Ain's life is her own, now. Whether it will be long or short will depend upon the choices she makes. If she spurns our help and continues to harass the Lossoth, it will be short indeed. Perhaps she will find a way to leave her troubled past behind. It is to be hoped she will do so, for otherwise she will perish, alone and without the name for which she grieves.
'You have done as I asked, and now the Lossoth will be able to bring in their rightful prey without interference. I will do my duty, as I said I would. I will join the Grey Company on the south road.'

'I see. I do not agree, but if that is the will of Elrond, there is little enough I could say to dispute it. Corunir, then, should be told of the Grey Company's mission. You will find him at Aughaire, the settlement of the Trev Gallorg in Angmar.'

'${PLAYER}! You have come just in time, for I do not know what I would do if you had not arrived! Golodir, my captain...he is in grave peril!
'The death of his daughter, Lorniel, brought him to the very brink of despair, but I thought his triumph over the False King would bring him the peace he sought. For a time it seemed it did, but lately he has lapsed into such a pit of grief that he seems not to know even we his friends. His sorrow fuels his anger at the remnants of Angmar, and he goes alone into even the most dangerous strongholds of evil. The False King is gone, but not even Golodir can long stand against the servants that still remain in many of those places!
'But he has gone too far this time, ${PLAYER}, and I do not know what to do. I need your help, for in his grief and rage I fear that Golodir is blinded to the danger, and where he goes there can be no return. He travels alone into the Rift of Nûrz Ghâshu, ${PLAYER}! We must rescue him!'

'You have my deepest thanks, ${PLAYER}, for aiding me in the rescue of Golodir from the very depths of Nûrz Ghâshu. He must have drawn the notice of Erebún during one of his excursions into the cities of Angmar following the defeat of the False King. Who knows what would have happened if the rogmul had maintained his dominance?
'We can be glad that did not happen, ${PLAYER}. I think it is best for Golodir to come with us as part of the Grey Company. It is not healthy for him to remain in this land, as marked with grief as it must be for him. The wide southern lands will do him good, I am sure of it.
'He will be kept busy, as we all will be, and I believe that to be the best means of rising above grief, as he must and will. Thank you again, my friend.'

'If you are keen to have a special mount yourself, you should venture to the Horse-fields in Bree or to Michel Delving's Delving Fields. There are tricky race-tracks there, and any who challenge the very strict timer must do their best not to get caught in the mire.

'Have you wandered yet to the horse races, o randir? The Elves do not mind the obstacle course, for we have a way with steeds. A whisper usually does the trick, and the horse's feet shall never go astray.

'The Algraig herdsmen we encountered in the Windfells are of a tribe called the Uch-lûth -- the Clan of the Ox -- who dwell in Nan Laeglin. 'So, ${PLAYER}, now that you've done so much for us, perhaps there is one more thing ye could help us with. I daresay it will be dangerous, though!
'There is a great beast -- some kind of troll or ogre, I don't know -- that haunts the bluffs and passes hereabouts, crushing folk with great boulders as they pass near. Occasionally it comes down out of the hills and roams the forest, they say, though I've never seen it.
'The Grey King we call it, for it's king of this wood, to be sure. Perhaps ye could rid us of this fearsome beast? You've proven a great friend so far, so how about it? A Northern Cousin?
You wandered across a strange and suspicious hobbit in the wilds of the Gloomglens... a long-lost Stoorish brother, no doubt.
'Ye will need to prove yourself worthy of our trust... our folk have been too long estranged.'
'Welcome back, cousin!'
'I can't wait for our first crop of your amazing weed to come in!'

Defeated Enaid-helgi

'A Stone-eater! Our Lûth-fathers told how they had seen your kind long ago in the mountains, but I never would have believed it if I didn't see ye now! Stone-eaters have always been a thing of legend to us.
'What? Ye say ye are not a Stone-eater? Ye call yourself a dwarf? I have not heard of the like. No matter... we've naught to do with the likes of ye.
'Well, I won't say we won't have naught to do with ye... if ye can prove your faith with us. Some of our hunters say that have seen an evil Cun Annun howling atop a plateau to the north-east of here at night. Enaid-helgi, we call it. If ye will slay the beast, Maer Brochtû might give ye a fair hearing.'

'You have slain Enaid-helgi? A deed most wondrous! I am sure Maer Brochtû will wish to speak with you now!
'As well, take this gift... you may find it useful when dealing with the dangers in these woods.'
Defeat Enaid-helgi at night

'Enaid-helgi is a thing of terror... you should be careful!'
'Greetings, Stone-eater! Did your meeting with the Maer go well?'
'Welcome back...Violed says she has some prime stones in her garden, if you're hungry!'

'A giant! Fearsome tales have we of your kind! What do ye want of me? Are ye going to eat me? Though to be truthful, I would have expected a beast of greater stature....
'Now what is that ye say? No giant are you, but a Man? Some of our elders swear they've met Man-creatures before, but I can't say that I have. Why should we deal with the likes of ye?
'Well, if ye want to speak with Maer Brochtû, you'll need to do something for us. To the east of here is a small gully where our hunters found a strange shrine...perhaps made by one of ye big Men. At night, the hunters claim to have seen a terrible goat-demon, which we call Gavar-diavol...defeat the creature, and we may have more to say to ye.'

'Most amazing, tall one! Maer Brochtû will surely wish to speak with you now!

'Something particularly evil stalks this corner of Enedwaith. We have no idea how they came here, but the wolves of the Black Dens are altogether unnatural. They look like wolves and seem to behave as such, but they are not mortal creatures. They are fell spirits that stalk and hunt Men.
'Nor are they aimless -- they are seeking something. The locals say that some were seen in Eregion weeks ago, ranging far and wide in search of their prey, but then they left and returned here to their dens. Only when we of the Dúnedain came did they emerge and resume their hunt...for us it now seems. They can be slain as any wolf might be, but with death they melt away like a shadow in the light of the noon sun.
'When you rescued me I was hunting one of their kind that seemed unique -- a great feral shadow that dominated the others. It was my hope that should this one be slain, then whatever power binds them here would be broken -- but as you know, I became the hunted instead and am still too injured to try my hand at it again. Would you take up my hunt? I cannot say what will come of it, but the passage of our brethren through Enedwaith would be considerably simpler without packs of Shadow-wolves nipping at our flanks the whole way.'

'So, even with the defeat of the Fang of Shadows, we still seem no closer to breaking the spell that binds these terrible spirits.
'Well, at least that one shall not hunt today, though I suspect we shall see it again before long. My thanks for your efforts...and hopefully a short respite.'

'Many Dunlendings were sent up from the southern regions to fight in Eregion and claim the Ring-forges. It seems that Saruman is seeking something there, though I know not what. 'The livery that some still wear may be of some use to us, however. It is difficult for Men of the North to pass as Dunlendings -- doubly so for we of Dúnadan descent -- but were we to don the livery of Saruman's army and skirt away from habitation, few would look closely enough to discern us, and we might pass through the South unmolested.

'The origins of this amulet are very old, and now that it has been repaired, it does indeed appear to be what I have been searching for.
'The amulet itself is not an extraordinary thing; however, it may be the key to ridding this area of the shades that roam the land. This amulet belonged to Cadelhin, the son of a chieftain, who perished ages ago. I believe that this amulet may be able to be used to awaken him, and that he may be a powerful ally in attempting to cleanse these lands.
'If you wish, I can lead you to Cadelhin's barrow, so that you might use the amulet to summon him.'

'What Cadelhin speaks of is a tale that has been passed along for generations.
'His people have fallen to an ancient curse for breaking an oath. They are bound to roam the land without rest, shackled for their atrocities.
'My hope is that by learning what exactly happened we might be able to release them from their curse.'

'I am grateful to you for your assistance. Weakened am I and weary of this curse. My people suffer from this curse because of my father, but I am not wholly without blame.
'I was a very capable hunter, and sought out the Rhi Helvarch, a powerful spirit near here, to bless my betrothal. Upon completing an arduous challenge, the Rhi Helvarch blessed the amulet that you recently recovered. The marriage was not to last, however, for my father murdered my wife and sundered the amulet. My belief is that when my father slew my wife and broke the amulet that I had given to her, the curse unfolded upon us. Such an act of betrayal is what brought this down upon us.
'Please go, so that I might regain my strength and summon those that would aid me. I will send word to the man that led you to this place when it is time to return.'

'Following my father's betrayal, I led a group of friends away from my home, as none of my followers could believe what my father and his men had done.
'We saw no other way to avenge this foul deed but to stand against them. Unfortunately, after some time we were defeated, and I was laid in this barrow and held here, never to be free. I will need to gather strength before I can assist you further.
'What? Wait... to arms! The shades of my father's men seek to destroy me and recover the amulet. Please, defend me as I muster my strength.'

'By your efforts, the summons was brought throughout Eriador, ${PLAYER}, and now the Dúnedain have responded. Many of their number have come to Imladris, and they prepare to depart for the southern lands that they may come to Aragorn in his time of need.
'You will ride with them, if you see fit to do so, but I have been made aware that my daughter desires first to speak with you. She is at Imdolen, on the slope north of Imladris, overlooking the road that climbs up into the Misty Mountains.'

'You have returned from your errand, ${PLAYER}, and have come to speak with me, as I asked? My delight cannot be hidden, friend ${RACE}, for my own undertaking has also come to an end, and its fruit waits now for a bearer!'
Arwen solemnly hands you a tall staff, wrapped closely with a black cloth bound with thongs.
'I have made this gift for Aragorn. The days are short, and it may be that our hopes will soon be ended. This standard I have made for him will fly aloft at a time of his choosing, and he will know for what he fights. May it bring courage to my Elfstone and those with whom he stands!
'Bring this gift and my words to Halbarad, by the stables in Imladris, for he has consented to bear them both on the journey south.'

'You bring both a gift and a message for my chief from the Lady Arwen? I see.'
Halbarad listens as you recount Arwen's words and gravely accepts the standard you carry.
'I will carry this burden on our journey. It will come to Aragorn, though all the perils of our road lie in between. When will this standard be unfurled, I wonder, and against what sky will it be raised aloft?'
'You have nothing for me?'
Talk to Arwen at Imdolen
Bring Aragorn's standard to Halbarad in Rivendell
Book II, Chapter 1: Wrought in Secret
The Grey Company has come to Rivendell, and there are only a few things left to be done before they begin their journey south.
'This is the moment for which the Dúnedain have waited, ${PLAYER}. It will not be long now before we ride forth to meet our destiny.'
'I see my sister has at last finished the gift she was making for Aragorn! How long will it be until it is unfurled, I wonder?'
'We are making ready to depart. It will not be long now before we take the southern road.'
'It was a long ride from the north-lands, ${PLAYER}, but I too have come to Rivendell to depart with the Company. They have need of my knowledge of the southern lands.'
'I carried the message to several other Rangers upon leaving Laenan, ${PLAYER}, and they have come to ride with the Grey Company.'
'Bring this gift and my words to Halbarad, by the stables in Imladris, for he has consented to bear them both on the journey south.'
'My daughter is at Imdolen, overlooking the road that climbs into the Misty Mountains, north of Imladris. She desired to speak with you before the Grey Company departs.'
'My gift to Aragorn goes south with the Grey Company.'
'My gift to Aragorn was wrought in secret. Few only know of its making.'

The Lady Arwen is at Imdolen, on the slope that overlooks the road into the Misty Mountains, north of Rivendell.
Elrond has asked you to speak with his daughter Arwen before you depart with the Grey Company.

Halbarad is by the stables in Rivendell.

'All is nearly ready, ${PLAYER}. While I finish the final preparations for our departure, I ask that you speak with some of those who will accompany us south. Ensure that they are prepared for the road and rested enough for the first leg of our journey.
'I saw Golodir just to the north-east some minutes ago, speaking with Elrohir. Radanir was just to the east of the two of them, beneath the foot-bridge.
'Lothrandir is just across the way, speaking to his horse Mithúl. He knows a great deal about the lands through which we must pass. Ask him if he has any further information about the road which may help us move with haste. Once you have spoken with those four, find Candaith by the stables gate and speak to him about what lies ahead.'

'Everyone is nearly ready to ride: the Dúnedain, the sons of Elrond, and ${PLAYER}, loyal ${RACE}.
'Are you familiar with our history, ${PLAYER}? As you are joining us on this journey, surely to go down in the annals of the Dúnedain, I would have you hear some of it, if you have not all ready.
'We have some moments. Let me tell you some of our history, that you may understand the weight of that which we are about to do.'

'My father had some curious words for me on the eve of this, our departure for the southern lands, ${PLAYER}.'
Elrohir gazes down the hill, deep in thought.
'He said that the time is approaching when we can no longer hold back, when we must do more than defend against the actions of the Enemy. He said that the time is coming when we may need to wager everything on a final throw, and by so doing we will have done all that we can. Better a death in far off lands in the service of a chance, however small, than death at home a certainty.
'We may not return from this journey, ${PLAYER}. My brother and I are at peace with that. I hope that you and these Dúnedain are as well, for I would counsel any who are not to stay behind.'

'My horse Legimbod is rested from the ride out of Angmar, and he is ready to undertake the next leg of the journey. His saddlebags are as light as I could make them, while still keeping the supplies we will need.'
Golodir takes a small pendant from one of his pockets and idly passes it from one hand to the other as he looks about the yard.
'This refuge has not changed in the many years since I last came here, but surely I, myself, must be unrecognizable. So much has happened, and so little of it good. But the ride here was a marvel, and I could feel the weight of the past falling from my shoulders with the feel of the breeze upon my face. Legimbod delighted in the speed, and I delighted with him! The southward journey will do both of us some good. I am ready to be off again.'

'Mithúl is ready for the next leg of the journey, ${PLAYER}. Indeed, his kind may be more prepared for what awaits us than the others of this Company! After all, Mithúl's eyes will be to the road underfoot, watching for loose stones and wind-blown branches; the eyes of the Dúnedain must be to the horizon, keeping watch for foes that may seek to slow our errand.
'I have spoken with Halbarad and the sons of Elrond about the road we will take: south through the Trollshaws and into Eregion, there to rest at Echad Eregion before passing south into Enedwaith.
'A number of Dunlending tribes called the area home when last I journeyed those lands. Some were friendly to outsiders, but most were not. The Draig-lûth, the Hebog-lûth... they are those you would be wise not to cross, and I will do my best to ensure the Grey Company does not entangle with them.'

'Glorengúr did not break a sweat in the short ride from Thorenhad here to Rivendell. He was ready to begin even yesterday.
'I could say the same for myself. I returned to Thorenhad to say good-bye to Elweleth, but I could not find her anywhere at the camp. I had meant to return this hairpin she had given me, but perhaps she feared the farewells. I suppose I did as well.
'We will soon set forth. I do not know what the future will bring, but I will do my duty with no complaint, and Glorengúr will do the same.'

Chapter 2: The Grey Company in Rivendell
The Grey Company prepares to depart from Rivendell for the wide southern lands and needs your help to make sure that all is ready.
'The road south will be long. We must ride swiftly and be wary of its dangers.'
'Are the words of my father correct? Is the time coming when we must no longer defend against the Enemy's moves, but strike against him with all the strength we can muster?'
'Legimbod is ready, and so am I. Together we will uphold our duty to Aragorn, our chief.'
'It is almost time to go, ${PLAYER}. Our road leads south.'
'When will this standard fly, I wonder? And what will that day signify for the Dúnedain?'
'This may be a perilous road, especially once we reach the plains of Enedwaith. Many of the Dunlending tribes will be hostile to us.'
'It will be many days before we come to Aragorn. May we be not late!'

Golodir, Lothrandir, Radanir, and Elrohir are preparing to depart in and around the stables of Rivendell.

You have spoken with several of the Rangers of the Grey Company in Rivendell and should now speak with Candaith.

'The early years of the Third Age saw the deaths of Isildur and his eldest sons, but his line was not ended, for his youngest son was kept safely here in Rivendell. He was raised far from danger and came to rule the North Kingdom. His descendents would not know peace, for the Nazgûl were to reappear, and their chief would wage war upon the Men of the West.
'In the year Nineteen Seventy-four of the Third Age, the armies of the Witch-king seized Fornost. The North Kingdom was no more, and its ruler Arvedui fled northward, to Forochel. But there he was lost, along with the heirlooms of his house.
'Some of the Dúnedain journeyed into the icy wastes to recover them. Do you wish to hear of their quest?'
<rgb=#FF0000>This is a solo quest and cannot be completed with a fellowship.</rgb>

'And so it was that Aragorn, Heir of Isildur through unbroken line down the long years, began his friendship with Gandalf, the Grey Pilgrim. He will be known by the sword that he bears, Andúril, Flame of the West, and by the Ring of Barahir, once lost but since regained.
'It is the task of the Dúnedain, and indeed of all friends of Aragorn, to ensure he safely comes into his birth-right. We will not question if this is the time for his ascension to the kingship. It must be so.
'Ride with us, ${PLAYER}, for we ride into history. Laegened and Haerdor, Corugúr and Glangon, all are remembered for the parts they played in the great drama of the Age. So it will be with us.'
Talk to Candaith in Rivendell and experience 'Session: The House of Isildur' or read the shortened account instead
Talk to Candaith in Rivendell

The history of the House of Isildur is full of dangerous escapes, glorious triumphs, and near brushes with tragedy, but even after so long the line remains strong. Three thousand years after the death of Isildur, Aragorn, son of Arathorn, is prepared to fulfill his destiny...

Candaith wishes to tell you some of the history of the Dúnedain so you may recognize the importance of the errand upon which you are about to embark.

'This is the tale of the Dúnedain that travelled north to Forochel to reclaim the heirlooms of the House of Isildur following the loss of Arvedui.'

'Some of the Dúnedain have already begun to ride, ${PLAYER}. Speak with Halbarad at the stables to see if he has any advice before the rest of us depart.'

'I have fit a new shoe to Saeradan's horse, ${PLAYER}. He will have no problems now.
'I wonder if the same can be said for the few who live in these lands. Those uruks spoke as if more would be coming, and we have no reason to doubt them. There has been much more activity among those creatures, many more of them on the roads in recent weeks. I do not like it.
'Well, give Saeradan my thanks for sending you my way, friend ${RACE}. I would have been in a great deal of trouble if you had not come along when you had, and the price of a new horse-shoe is a small price to pay indeed!'

'The first leg of our journey is complete, but not without incident: my horse, Erebrandir, has drawn up lame. There is something wrong with one of his shoes, and he cannot go on unless something is done.
'Halbarad says I should just engage another horse, but I have been speaking to the Elves here and they have given me another idea. Apparently a skilled farrier has recently passed through Gwingris. This farrier, Londan by name, could certainly repair Erebrandir's shoes.
'I understand that Londan left Gwingris heading east. If you find him and convince him to return, we will have been delayed but little.'

'Erebrandir is ready to go once more! His new shoe fits perfectly, a testament to the skill of Londan. I am worried about these uruks, though. If it is true that many of the creatures have come north through Enedwaith into Eregion, our ride south may quickly become more difficult than it has been to this point.
'Are they solely here for plunder, or is there another purpose that drives them?
'Londan gave to me the shoe he took from Erebrandir. It is yours, if you want it; some people believe a shoe such as this brings good fortune. I do not think that is the case, but I leave you to make up your own mind.'

'Our preparations are complete, and some of the Dúnedain have already mounted their horses and begun to ride. You do the same or engage one of the horses at these stables, and we will be off!
'Lothrandir and I have chosen a course that will take us south in several legs, the first of which leads south through the Trollshaws and into Eregion.
'We will meet up at Gwingris, in Eregion, ${PLAYER}, and we will have a rest.'

'Careful, stranger! There is a group of uruks in these parts, of great size and strength. I saw them not two hours ago.
'They were passing north, and though I could understand little of their cruel speech, it seems to me they were seeking treasure. There are ruins throughout these lands, you know. These uruks would like nothing better than a chance at plunder.'
Londan listens to your account of Saeradan's plight and agrees to tend to the needs of his horse Erebrandir. His face then freezes in a mask of fear.
'The uruks! They're coming back! Prepare to fight!'

Chapter 4: Riding South
The first leg of the Grey Company's journey will take them south through the Trollshaws and into Eregion.
'There are many more uruks in this land than there ever were before, ${PLAYER}. Tell Saeradan to use caution if he and his fellows insist on riding south.'
'Londan left Gwingris heading east. He is surely still in Eregion and could find time to repair Erebrandir's shoe if you are able to find him without delay.'
'Thank you for finding Londan, ${PLAYER}! Both I and Erebrandir thank you, for he has been able to fit my Lonely Wanderer with a new shoe. You should speak with him.'
'Many of our friends have already departed. Speak with Halbarad at the stables here to see if he has any final words for you.'
'Ride south into Eregion, ${PLAYER}, on your own mount or on one engaged from Rivendell. We will all gather again for a rest at Gwingris.'
'Many of our friends have already departed. I am about to go.'
'I am about to ride south with the rest of the Grey Company. You too should ride now!'

The Grey Company begins its ride south. Halbarad has determined that the Rangers will rest at Gwingris, in Eregion.

A confusion of tracks surround the fallen pack and lead off to the east

'The rest of the Dúnedain have gone on ahead. They wait now for us!
'We will meet up with the Company for the next leg of our journey further south of here, at Echad Eregion. May the wind at your back speed you onward! Erebrandir and I will see how stands up the work of Londan.
'Until we meet again at Echad Eregion, ${PLAYER}.'

'Hail to you, ${RACE}! You are in pursuit of the uruks? Your trail ends here, I am afraid: the ruins of Minas Elendúr that you see atop the cliffs here are crawling with the creatures, and with worse besides!
'Still you intend to scour the ruins? You are brave, my friend! If I cannot dissuade you, I at least will tell you what I have learned of the place. I will not myself journey there again, not for any sum! There are strange doings going on inside Minas Elendúr and its cursed cellars, and I have seen enough to last me!

'Yes, who are you? You are no Ranger, I can see that. It is an outrage, I tell you, when dwarves cannot take the road north from the White Mountains without fear of harassment!
'There we were, my father and I, when out from behind one of the large stones you see scattered everywhere in these lands jumps the largest uruk you've ever seen. He beat his chest with a gloved hand, shouted the name of his clan -- I'll never forget it -- then knocked out my father Fúni and dragged him off!'
You ask him in what direction the Sharkúnakh uruk took his father, and his brow furrows with puzzlement.
'Sharkúnakh? No, no. The name he shouted was Ninkoth. In all the confusion I can't remember what direction he went, but if you can find the site of the attack, which was to the east of here, you may see some tracks or something.'

'We have called a halt, ${PLAYER}, and it may be for longer than we originally intended. We have received a call for aid from a dwarf coming north from the White Mountains, and Halbarad has determined it to be serious enough to justify a stop.
'The dwarf's name is Fúsi -- Fúsi Gem-cutter -- and he will speak to you about his problem. He will speak to anyone, it seems!'
Talk to Radanir at Echad Eregion

Chapter 5: Forces at Work in Eregion
The ride of the Grey Company continues, with the Dúnedain travelling further south into Eregion.
'If you can find this Ninkoth uruk, you may be able to find my father! We were attacked somewhere to the east of here!'
'You found tracks leading east from the site of the attack? Why have you not yet followed them, ${PLAYER}? It is the least you can do, is it not? I say that it is! I do indeed!'
'Fúsi Gem-cutter is here at Echad Eregion, and his problem is serious enough that Halbarad has extended our halt here. Talk to Fúsi and see what he needs.'
'Halbarad wants us to help this dwarf Fúsi. I do not know why he thinks it so important.'

'I do not know why Halbarad is so intent on helping these dwarves, ${PLAYER}. I cannot begrudge it of him, even if it seems needless, given our haste. You should follow the tracks at the site of the attack to the east.'
'Ride forth to Echad Eregion, ${PLAYER}, and we will all meet up again for the next leg of the journey.'
'Dwarves cannot travel through this land free of danger? It is an outrage!'
'I cannot believe those uruks thought to trouble us!'

'The Elves at Gwingris would not tell me much of these ruins, but they told me enough to whet my curiosity: that this was the site of a battle, long ago, and none of the people who lived here were spared the sword. But the goal of the enemy was not treasure, for the coffers were left untouched. Untouched!
'But there is something strange about the rooms and corridors of Minas Elendúr, and the cellars of Delotham, which run beneath it. You see things, sometimes, disturbing things. It is as if the horrors that fell upon that place scarred it in some way, some way that the stones have not forgotten. It would be a brave ${RACE} indeed to explore the place from top to bottom!
'Some rooms in Minas Elendúr can only be reached by stairs within Delotham, and the opposite seems also to be so! I do not know why the Ninkoth uruks have come to this place, but I feel it must be as bewildering to them as it is to me! Wherever they are keeping this dwarf for whom you are looking, it will not be easy to find!'
'By Durin, a friendly face! I had all but given up hope of rescue, and here you appear as if from nowhere! Hurry, there is not much time!'
Find Fúni Gem-cutter somewhere within Minas Elendúr
Chapter 6: Fúni Gem-cutter
Fúni Gem-cutter has been taken to the abandoned ruins of Minas Elendúr by the Ninkoth uruks.

'This dwarf for whom you are looking is somewhere in Minas Elendúr? Well, you will have your hands full looking for him. These ruins are a bewildering maze crawling with uruks of the Ninkoth tribe and other dangers. It is enough to drive a man mad!'
'My father is somewhere in the ruins of Minas Elendúr? You need to rescue him, ${PLAYER}! The Elves say that Minas Elendúr is far to the east of here!'
'I have had an idea, ${PLAYER}, and we cannot leave until Fúni Gem-cutter is rescued.'

'I have been asking the Elves here for information about Minas Elendúr, but there is not much to tell. The ruins were the site of a terrible battle, long ago, and have remained empty ever since. They can be found far to the east of here.'
'Something is not right within these ruins, friend.'
'Your eyes may play tricks on you within these ruins.'
'I have been told there was a great battle here, long ago.'

'These uruks call themselves \qNinkoth\q, but I care not; they are as miserable a creature as any I have seen. It seems they have come north on the heels of another breed, but these have designs of settling down in these lands. What an idea! Better up here than down near Zigil-jabâl, my home in the White Mountains, but still too close for comfort. We have had troubles there enough.
'The Ninkoth uruks kept me alive for a purpose, friend. They've been bringing golden trinkets to me from throughout the cellars of this place, with the idea that I could somehow fashion them into items of worth. Which of course I can, but would never do for these creatures!
'I cannot bear the thought of these treasures being left here for the Ninkoth. Explore these ruins, gather up the treasure, and bring it back to me! I would not mind a bit if you took some time to slay some uruks, either! Oh! You may want to make a map!'

'My father is back, ${PLAYER}, and he was very pleased at your performance within the ruins. He's been deep in conversation with one of the Rangers here.
'I think they want him to make something, but what it is I have no idea! That Ranger, Radanir, might be able to tell you more.'

'I have just been talking with Halbarad, ${PLAYER}, and now this whole affair with the Gem-cutters makes sense to me. I now know why Halbarad thought this delay to be necessary, and I agree with him.
'He has a commission for Fúni Gem-cutter, a task for which Fúni is well-suited. He wants Fúni to make an imitation of the Ring of Barahir.'
'Excellent, excellent! We will bring these treasures out into the sunlight with us. Let us go, ${PLAYER}! I will meet you back at, what was the name? Echad Eregion? Tell my son I am on my way.'
'I am still waiting for you to do what you said you would do!'

'Halbarad can tell you more, but as he said to the rest of us, \qWhat chance is it that puts a wandering jewel-crafter right in our path at this moment?\q He is right. It is a small chance, surely, but a happy one.
'Talk to Halbarad, here at Echad Eregion, to learn more about his plan.'

'Think of this, ${PLAYER}: the line of Isildur is recognized by the heirlooms of that house: the shards of Narsil, now reforged; the Sceptre of Annúminas, long kept in Rivendell; and the Ring of Barahir, almost lost in Forochel but regained. I believe you have heard the story.
'And now, this Grey Company rides to the defence of Aragorn in the southern lands, lands increasingly under the sway of the uruk. Danger crowds around us upon every side, but our own safety must be secondary to that of Aragorn. Imagine, therefore, if a member of our company is slain or taken captive by the Enemy. If that man bore a ring of the same description as the Ring of Barahir, would that not give his captor pause?
'I have therefore made this proposal to Fúni Gem-cutter: to craft rings so like to the ring of Barahir, based on Candaith's description, that should any of this Company fall into the hands of the Enemy, it may sow confusion into his mind. This confusion may buy the true Heir precious time. Tell me when you are ready, and we will go with Fúni to the forges he will use.'

'It is done, ${PLAYER}. I hope that this was just a momentary delay that we will never have needed; but in the sad event that one of our friends is slain or captured by the Enemy, perhaps his Bebarahir will buy our chieftain Aragorn some precious seconds.
'All of our struggles are for him, for the return of the heir of Isildur, the return of the king of Gondor.
'We must soon be off again. Our destiny awaits us in the wide southern lands.'

'I wish to thank you for recovering both halves of this amulet, Duvodiad. My hope has been that when this item is mended, that it might weaken the shades that stalk this troubled land. I fear a great evil has bound them here, and they have become dangerous.
'Take both pieces of the amulet and seek out several of the unusual cairn stones that dot the landscape. These ancient cairn stones are covered with inscriptions that are much older than those that surround them. The inscriptions on these stones match that of the amulet and can hopefully be used to help mend it to its original shape.
'Travel to the south-east and locate several of these cairn stones. Place the amulet upon them, then bring me word of the effects, if any, you witness.'

'This amulet may very well be the symbol of an ancient settlement here. The cairn-stones that you visited are said to date back to that time, and now the amulet appears to be mending itself.
'I believe those cairn-stones were left by a branch of an ancient lûth -- clan -- that fell to conflict within itself. This may be what caused the shades to be bound here.
'My hope is that somehow this amulet will allow us to put these poor spirits to rest.'

'I've received a different sort of orders from Jónar, the head of this here society. He hates the Inn League so much that he has assigned me a rather different task than my Inn League neighbour there. Shh, he mustn't hear us!
'We have received word that Nathalan, a fellow up visiting Angmar, has requested some Swill from The Forsaken Inn. Instead of Swill, though, I want you to bring him mead...plain old mead! Specifically that from The Plough and Stars in Brockenborings.
'This should be a fine trick. He will be expecting something wretched, and instead he will be all confounded, thanks to you!'
'It is mead you want? Well, you have come to the right place for mead. We have a fine mead right here!'

'You have brought me Swill! I'll finally be done. Let me take a look. Oh my gracious, that is absolutely disgusting. I can smell it from here!'
Nathalan takes a long swig of the mead, grimacing the entire time.
'Foul! Despicable! It holds up to the rumours...hm. That aftertaste isn't so bad. I don't suppose you...brought another?'
'Have you brought me my Swill?'

It is the year Twenty-nine Fifty-six of the Third Age, and Aragorn son of Arathorn plans to begin the great journeys by which he would come to know the world. He is waiting to speak with you, for he wishes to bid farewell before he travels into the south-lands.

It is the year Twenty-nine Fifty-six of the Third Age, and Aragorn son of Arathorn plans to begin the great journeys by which he would come to know the world. But first he must bid farewell to the friends of his childhood.
Aragorn and Túgonn have encountered an old man on the road through the Dimrill Dale.
Gandalf the Grey is waiting to speak with you.
Aragorn is waiting to speak with you.

'We have come this far without incident, Laegened, but the road north is certain to become more dangerous. Little is known of the Snowmen of Forochel, but if they are opposed to the Witch-king, we will surely find them to be allies.
'Still, the ship bearing Arvedui should have returned by now, and its absence fills me with worry. We must press onward, no matter what we find. The sooner we learn what has befallen King Arvedui, the sooner we may leave this cold land!
'There are worms on the rise ahead, Laegened. Use your skills at remaining unseen and clear a path for us, that we may bring the waggon up the road safely. The trade goods we bring may loosen the tongues of the Snowmen as to the fate of our king.'
'Very good, Laegened! Now that the worms are cleared from the pass we can resume our journey northward into Forochel to learn what we may learn.'

'We have come to the end of our road, Laegened! Look there! The ship that was to carry King Arvedui back home lies in ruin!
'Wish now as you never have before! Wish that he was not aboard the vessel when it broke apart!
'We cannot tarry here, though dread lies heavily upon my heart. Hurry, Laegened!'

'It must be the Ring of Barahir! It possesses no power save its value as an heirloom of the House of Isildur, but its value in ancientry cannot be doubted!
'Did King Arvedui have some sense of the fate that awaited him? Surely not, but it is curious that this ring has escaped where he was unable.
'We have brought great store of provision with us. We will barter for the return of the ring, and it will go south with us, though its master cannot. We must be content with that.'

'There are great things in store for Aragorn your chieftain, Túgonn, but he must arrive at them in his own time. It is the solemn duty of all the Dúnedain to protect him, for he is descended from Isildur in line unbroken, and one day he must rule in Gondor.'
Gandalf smiles with amusement, peering at you from underneath his eyebrows.
'But these are mighty words, and the time is still far off. We all have work to do before that day comes, not just Aragorn, and not just -- in our small way -- the Wizards, but you as well, Túgonn. You will not travel with Aragorn on his journey into the kingdoms of the south, for he has made up his mind, but you still have your role to play. In friendship, you will carry it out and have victory, I am certain, for that is a weapon no servant of the Enemy fully understands.'

'I am glad the tall king had a son to continue his rule. Long may his heirs rule their far-away peoples!
'He spoke of great treasures and valuable things. He said they were carried upon the sea-monster's back, and that they could be used against the Witch-king for the betterment of both our peoples. But now all are lost. Nothing comes back out of the frozen water.'

'We are almost there, Corugúr, for good or ill. I fear that we will not find Arador our chieftain still alive, but we cannot call off the pursuit until we know for certain.
'The Hill-trolls of the Ettenmoors make their homes here on the Troll-height, and the tracks lead into the cleft just ahead. I will climb the rise and scout the area from above. There are goblins in these parts as well; I leave their fates up to you, but know that the trolls must be our main concern.
'Good fortune, Corugúr! May we not be too late for our chief.'

'Alas, we are too late! Arador has been slain! Curse these vile trolls!'
Glangon wipes away a tear and composes himself as best he may.
'His son Arathorn is chieftain of the Dúnedain now, though he want it not. And him newly-married, as well! There is nothing for it, Corugúr. We must return with the sad news. I pity Arathorn for the responsibility that now falls to him, but we must console ourselves with the knowledge that the line of Isildur will continue. What a sorrow if it were to end in this world!
'May Arathorn reach a different fate than his father! Let none come to this Troll-height without remembering the fate of the Chieftain of the Dúnedain. From this point forward this height will be known as Arador's End and will be a warning to all.'

'We have been friends for many years, Túgonn, and we have explored the wild lands of Eriador together. Your friendship means a great deal to me. But I have said nothing for which you should be angry with me. I have told you before that I planned to adventure in the south-lands, then to return when I have done deeds worthy of my father and grandfather. You cannot come with me, my friend.
'If I am to lead the Dúnedain, needs must I perform feats worthy of that obligation. It is something I must do alone, Túgonn.'

'The ring-making is going well? Good. I gave the jewel-smith a description of the ring of Barahir as I remembered it, and if he has the skill he claims to have, his imitations should be suitable.
'Elrohir wanted me to send you to him, if you had a moment. He was contemplating our plans beneath a tree in the courtyard to the north of here, if you would speak with him.'

'The crafting of the rings sought by Halbarad goes well, ${PLAYER}? Good. If these preparations give our enemies even the slightest pause, the time they take will be counted five and seven times in value.'
Elrohir pauses for a moment, thinking, and then takes you into his confidence.
'Before we left Imladris, my father gave to me messages for Aragorn, confident that he would understand them. But I too understand their meaning, and that understanding fills me with worry. He bade me to remind Aragorn of the words of the seer Malbeth, and of the Paths of the Dead. I will tell you of...'
Suddenly, a shout breaks the silence, and Elrohir leaps to his feet!

'The work goes well, ${PLAYER}! Already some of the rings have been made, and they are identical to the description with which my father was provided. But the gold is running low! Very little gold is needed for each ring, of course, but my father can use only small quantities of the material when it is melted, or imperfections will arise.
'Bring more coffers of gold to me from where they are being stored!'

'Fúni Gem-cutter has been working hard within, melting gold with which to fashion quality imitations of the ring borne by Aragorn our chieftain. Candaith, learned in lore as he is, described the ring to Fúni, and the dwarf has pledged that his reproductions will deceive all but the most studious observer.'

'According to Fúsi Gem-cutter, his father's work is going well and smoothly. With no more interruptions, I feel that we will soon see an end to this delay.'
Halbarad laughs softly, a sound that has been missing from the journey of the Grey Company, unnoticed until now.
'I say delay, but I feel better for having a secret held in reserve. Let our foes mill about in confusion, while the true heir of Isildur makes stealth his ally! It is good to be doing something.'

'${PLAYER}...a party of warring uruks...has climbed the path to this place. And I have seen others...in the distance. It will not be long...before they arrive....'
Halros grabs your arm, desperate to tell you something else.
'Golodir...stayed behind...to hold them back. Help...help him....'

'A party of...uruks! They have...climbed the path.... And there are others...in the distance. It will not be long...before they arrive....'
Radanir seeks to catch his breath, but the exertion has been too much and the urgency of his message cannot be restrained.
'Golodir...is at the entrance.... He hopes to...hold them back. Help him...help him quickly....'
'We have done well this day, ${PLAYER}. May Fúni Gem-cutter's work go as well!'
'Despair not, ${PLAYER}. We will defeat these uruks, or we will delay them for as long as is necessary for the remainder of our Company to complete the task for which we have come to these forges.'

'The camps can be found to the east and north-east of Harndirion. Please be careful, Duvodiad, for it is said that those ruins are cursed place and that foul spirits call it home.'
'The defeat of the sentries marks the beginning of the end for these foul duhirun. I appreciate your assistance, for it shows that there are duvodiad who will fight for my people.'

'I suppose I should be grateful for the kindness of any willing to aid a wounded man, even if it is from a duvodiad. I received my wounds when a small raiding-party from Gwâl Draig attacked and slew my fellows.
'On the southern shore of the river stands an encampment that these duhirun -- these blackguards -- call home. My party was sent to scout this camp to see if we could rout them from the area. The Draig-lûth butchered the entirety of our sister clan, the Turch-lûth, and now seek our demise as well. Our former brethren from Dunland call us Algraig -- Outliers -- and have ever been our enemies.
'Perhaps you will scout this camp for me? Seek out the entrances and dispatch any guards that you encounter. The camp can be found by following the southern shore of the river to the north and heading due east.'

'You again! I saw everything! Óli will not speak to you now because you were so mean to him before. He has been moping ever since, poor fellow.

'Sugared honeysuckle? Yes, I have it. Hate the stuff. If you want it, it's yours! I was going to throw it away.'

'Yes, I bought the sugared honeysuckle, and for quite the price too! Gamall's dishes are not cheap. But I wanted to give a special gift to Dwalin. I think he will look favourably upon me when it is time for promotions, you see. And who doesn't love candy?'

'The sugared honeysuckle? No, I do not have it anymore. I... used it in a recipe. Where is the finished dish? All right, you caught me! I did not cook with it. I merely gave it away and took credit for the recipe. Heikki Goldwatcher bought them from me. He wanted something home-made and sweet. Do not tell him!'

'Marauders have come to our lands, killing our livestock and threatening our people. Smoke rises from the south, and I fear that it comes from our cartrevs, burned in the night by the half-orc invaders.
'Glynn Brenin has forbidden our warriors from taking the field, fearing that the village itself might be burned, so I would ask you to seek out the cartrevs and see if anything remains.'

'It is good that Hamon's home remains whole, as does Emlun... I only hope Emlun escaped the wrath of the half-orcs. Alas for Rurith, Matho, and their families.
'I thank you for your assistance, Duvodiad.'

'Seek the cartrevs to the south and learn if any still remain there.'

'And what do we have here? A bit far afield aren't you, Duvodiad? You are not welcome here. The affairs of Dunland do not involve you, and your presence does naught but threaten the tentative peace of these lands.
'With the pact I offer, these lands shall be forever safe from the looming threat of the North-men under the protection of Isengard.
'Now begone, before I am tempted to rash and unsightly action to remove you.'

'And here I was just looking for a bit of sport among this backwater collection of hovels. I had not dared hope for any fool Duvodiad to offer themselves up to my blades.
'Alas, it shall have to wait. My lord has business to attend to with the brenin.
'But do not wander too far, little vagabond. Once our treaty is in hand, I shall have the time to deal with the likes of you.'
Talk to the emissary's champion in the Brenin's Hall
The Hand of Isengard
You have encountered an unusual pair of Men, sent it seems from Isengard to offer a treaty of fealty between the Uch-lûth and Saruman.
'You are not welcome here, Duvodiad!'

The emissary's champion is in the Brenin's Hall in Lhanuch.
You should speak with the emissary's champion.

'To the south-east of here is the village of Lhanuch. It is the only significant settlement of Men in Enedwaith -- though we have seen evidence of a lost clan called the Turch-lûth -- and we shall have to pass near it on our path to Rohan.
'Once it was a place we often stopped to rest on our journeys through Dunland, but no more. Some years ago there was an incident in Nan Laeglin, and Glynn Brenin, the chieftain of the Algraig clan known as the Uch-lûth, declared all outsiders -- or duvodiad, as they say -- unwelcome in his halls, especially those of us known as Rangers.
'I would ask you to enter the village in our stead. Isengard is in motion, and we must learn anything we can before we pass Dunland. Glynn Brenin and his people should be able to tell us what we need to know. The people of Enedwaith are wary of strangers, but their laws of hospitality are ancient and deeply held. They will not turn you away without reason should you come to them in friendship.'

'Who goes there? You have the look of a northerner about you. We have seen more of your kind of late, but I cannot say you are welcome here.
'If you seek the hospitality of the Hall of Lhanuch, then I will not stop you...but the days grow dark, Duvodiad, and you may not find the mood of the brenin's hall to your liking.
'Speak with the guard outside the brenin's hall. Perhaps he will let you in, perhaps not. Be the cause of trouble in our village, and you will be spitted to warn off the rest of your ilk....'

'Halt! Declare yourself before the hall of Glynn Brenin, brenin of the Uch-lûth!
'${PLAYER}? You must be one of the duvodiad that have been sneaking about of late. What ill-wind brings you before our gates like some beggar from out of the wild? If you wish to invoke the hospitality of our hall then so be it, but it shall be allowed at Glynn Brenin's discretion, not mine.
'One word to the wise, Duvodiad. There has been rumour that Rangers from the wild have been skulking about of late. By the law of this house, they are not welcome, nor those who would spy for them in our midst. So watch your tongue and your idle hands, lest they earn you trouble.'
Approach the gates of Lhanuch
Speak with the guard before the Brenin's Hall in Lhanuch
The Edge of the Wild
Himeinior told you that the Dúnedain are not welcome in the halls of Lhanuch, for the Uch-lûth are wary of strangers.
'We need the good will of the Uch-lûth at Lhanuch, ${PLAYER}.'

Lhanuch lies to the south-east of Echad Idhrenfair, in Nan Laeglin.
Himeinior has asked you to seek entry into the Uch-lûth village of Lhanuch.

The guard is at the entrance to the Brenin's Hall of Lhanuch.
The guard at the village gate instructed you to speak with the guard before the Brenin's Hall of Lhanuch.
You have repaired Penlhun's axe

'Tell me, Duvodiad, is it true that the powers of Angmar stir anew? Have the Elves truly allied with the Witch-king in the North as the tales say? Some weeks ago, warriors from the South under the direction of Isengard passed by to do battle in Eregion, but we have heard little but dark rumour since.
'No matter the details, war shall be upon us soon... you mark my words. Would that my father's axe was yet true, I would be unafraid of battle! It was made by the dwarves back when Thrór's folk lived in the mountains, but time takes its toll on all things, and it broke some years ago. None here have the skill to reforge such a weapon, but it is said that the dwarves yet remain in the far north and have shared some secrets of craft with the Men there as well.
'I was thinking that if this is true, then I might have the axe re-made. What of it, Duvodiad? Do you know the secrets of the craft or perhaps know a dwarf who might reforge my father's blade? Take it, if so. It is of no use to me now, and my brethren would have me melt it down to make a less worthy blade. I would not see it end so if it might be made whole again. If it can be done, then I shall be in your debt and shall speak in your favour at the Council of Brehur.'

'Penlhun gave you this? I will tell you what I told him. I cannot repair it.
'I do not know how Thrór's smiths forged it to such a temper, but anything I could do to it would make the steel so brittle that it would shatter at the first blow.
'You want this weapon repaired? Go to Thrór's Coomb. There is rumour that a mad dwarf lives there still among the ruins. Perhaps he can repair it.'
<rgb=#FF0000>If you have Master proficiency in the Weaponsmith profession, you may repair the axe yourself using the anvil in the Lhanuch crafting hall.</rgb>

'My father's axe! It is nearly as sound as the day he brought it from the dwarves!
'You have my thanks, Duvodiad. I shall do what I can to dissuade Glynn Brenin from aiding Isengard.
'We of the Uch-lûth should be our own people, not servants of some power-hungry wizard....'
Talk to Aedh at the Lhanuch crafting hall
Repair Penlhun's axe
Bring the axe to Penlhun
Bring Penlhun's axe to the mad dwarf in Thrór's Coomb

'This is a dwarf-axe! Whence did you steal it? From a Man?
'Where did the Man get it? From his father? This man's father was a dwarf? Well, you should have said so to begin with! I will gladly repair this for my half-brother!
'This shouldn't take long... here you go!'
A Weapon of Old

Penlhun Brehur, one of the leaders of Nan Laeglin, has asked you if you know of any way to repair the dwarf-axe handed down to him from his father. The axe was forged in Thrór's Coomb, and it is rumoured that at least one dwarf remains among the ruins. Alternatively, if you are a weaponsmith of considerable skill you might try a hand at repairing it yourself.
'Would that my father's axe were whole once more....'
'Tell Penlhun's father Nár sends his greetings... a good dwarf, he is. Or was? He is a dwarf, yes?'
'Talk to the mad dwarf if you want that axe repaired!'

Aedh may be found in the crafting hall.
You should speak with Aedh to learn if there is any way to reforge Penlhun's axe.

The mad dwarf dwells somewhere in the mountains surrounding Thrór's Coomb, far to the east of Lhanuch.
Aedh told you to seek out a mad dwarf in the valley of Thrór's Coomb and see if he can repair Penlhun's axe. Alternatively, if you are a master weaponsmith, you might attempt to repair the axe yourself at the forge in Lhanuch.

Penlhun Brehur is at the Brenin's Hall in Lhanuch, far to the west of Thrór's Coomb.
You should return to Penlhun with his father's axe.

'Within the village of Gwâl Draig, there must be someone who has set his people to this course of action. It is my hope that by defeating the brenin of the Draig-lûth these folk will no longer harass the Uch-lûth.
'Before his disappearance, my chief scout discovered Heilun Brenin and his guards standing near a large bonfire at the centre of their encampment.
'Seek out Heilun Brenin and his men and dispatch them, then return to me.'

'I believe that while the creatures that hunt the valley to the north-east may still be difficult to deal with, Heilun Brenin's defeat may make the Draig-lûth less of a concern.
'Thank you from the depths of my heart for all of your help. You will be remembered and spoken of well by me among the Uch-lûth.'

Brenin of the Draig-lûth
Within Gwâl Draig, there must be a leader driving his people to perform such cruel acts upon the clans of the Algraig.
'Heilun Brenin is a vile monster and should be punished for the wicked deeds he has committed against the Uch-lûth and Turch-lûth.'

Heilun Brenin and his guards can be found at the centre of Gwâl Draig, east of Gronu's camp.
Gronu asked you to defeat Heilun Brenin and his personal guards.

Gronu's camp lies to the west of Gwâl Draig, beneath Harndirion.

'Your presence here is no mystery to me, Duvodiad. Our village is caught between powers. On one hand, we have the emissaries of Saruman the White, who demand our fealty in battles to come, while the Duvodiad of the North once again tresspass unwanted upon our lands.
'Glynn Brenin will soon hold council to decide our course. We have no love for the Men of the North, but we are not blind...we see what is happening to our brethren in Dunland. They will serve Isengard as pawns in the war to come, and many will never see their homes again. Yet if we refuse, we may come to blows with our own kinsmen, or the savage half-orcs who serve under the banner of the White Hand. I cannot say which would be worse.
'Know that Glynn Brenin's mind is not yet resolved in this matter, Duvodiad. Prove your worth to the brehur, and he may yet find the will to reject the entreaties of Isengard. Otherwise, I suspect that your wandering friends will soon be hunted down by Saruman's armies, and our Men-folk shall march to war in the South, to what fate, I know not.'

'Following your departure, I was visited by a powerful emissary of the Rhi Helvarch. As he was the spirit that blessed my union, I asked if there was a way for my people to be freed from this ancient curse. He asked that I choose a champion to go forth and confront my father with what he has done.

'Whether it be to save us from savage raiders or starvation in the next winter's snow, we may indeed have to bend to Isengard's will....'
'Another day, another battle. If Saruman thinks we will join him with a boot upon our necks, he should best think again!'

'Umfrë the hunter it was, who rescued me from a ravening pack of strange white hounds shortly after I entered the forest -- Cun Annun, he called them.
'He seems a good Man, though when he realized I was a northerner he seemed dismayed. Nevertheless, he helped me tend my wound, and I had hoped to ask for his services as a guide through these woods. He left, though, in search of one of these hounds that he said had been terrorizing the people of his village of late. Yet a full day has since passed, and I have seen no sign of him. I fear he too may have been injured or killed beneath the forest's eaves.
'My leg is still not fit to walk -- if you could find Umfrë and help him return here, I would be obliged, as I owe him a debt, and he may be the only one who can help us through this forest.'

'My thanks to you, Duvodiad.
'These woods have grown more dangerous than ever in recent days. These Cun Annun that hunt and kill Men and beast alike are a terror from our old wives' tales.
'I do not know in truth what brings your people here, but I also in truth do not care to. Whatever your purpose, unless it is to bring harm to my people, I will help you if I may.'
'Please stranger, help me!'

'I would be grateful if you could find Umfrë and assure his safety.'

'Go then and curse you! Speak with our Elder upon Gwaed Brun at the heart of the forest. Perhaps he knows the way to the Huntsman's hall. I know it not.

'So you have come, Duvodiad. The Forest Lords have spoken to us and said you would come. It seems they would speak with you, if you are able to prove your worth to them. Most odd.
'Oh, do forgive young Enit. She knows little yet of the Forest Lords. They have ever been of fickle whim, and she takes such things rather personally, I am afraid.'

'Our tales say that the Rhi Helvarch came to these lands long ago, and that his power gradually claimed the forest, making it strange and dangerous to the unwary.
'But he has never pursued or hounded us, and the spirits that are drawn to him have rarely disturbed us... but now they have become filled with anger and lash out at any who enter the forest.
'These wild spirits have overrun the circle which lies nearest the Huntsman's hall. If they can be driven away, then perhaps we can beseech the Forest Lords to open the way within.'

'You have fought valiantly, but it does not seem that the spirits can be driven away by brute force. I feared as much.
'We must open the way nevertheless for so we have been bidden.'

'The forest has been disturbed and the spirits silent of late. I will summon one and speak with it, if you can bring me what I need for this ritual.
'There are several plants that are sacred to the spirits, but the forest has grown wild and terrible of late, and it is dangerous to travel within it. If you will gather the things I need and bring them to me, I will perform this ritual. Then we shall learn the truth of both your purpose and the forest's anger.
'Nearly everything I need can be foraged from the forest, but the living bark must be collected from the wild Wood-trolls which dwell to the west of here.'

'You have returned with what I require? In truth, I did not think you would emerge from the forest again, Duvodiad.
'That only means it is all the more important that I speak with the spirits of the Mournshaws.
'I shall begin....'

Enit looks pale and shaken.
'The spirits have forsaken me! Who are you, Duvodiad? What does it mean that you have come among us even as the forest turns upon its faithful servants?
'The Rhi Helvarch himself has never called upon the folk of Nan Laeglin. I do not know what this means, but I can neither help nor hinder you now....
'Go then and curse you! Speak with our Elder upon Gwaed Brun at the heart of the forest. Perhaps he knows the way to the Huntsman's hall. I know it not. May you meet your doom there, Duvodiad. May the great spirits of the forest consume you!'

'If you must find your way through this accursed forest, then I cannot show it to you, for I never go so deep... but the Derudh may know a way.
'A few among our people are chosen to learn the forest's secrets. Those that return claim to have communed with the spirits of the forest, but speak little of it. These are the Derudh of the Mournshaws.
'There is an ancient circle of stone in the northern reaches of the forest called Galar Culch where you might find them. Bring them some tithe of berries or the like, and they may grant you some piece of wisdom. Do not expect much from them, however, for they care little for duvodiad like you.'

'A path to the south? Once perhaps, but not in these days. The spirits of the forest have grown wild and more dangerous than they once were... certainly they would devour one such as you!
'I might commune with the spirits and speak with them myself, but there is a ritual that must be performed, and the things I need are dangerous to gather now.'

'Who are you, Duvodiad? How is it that you dare these woods and carry an offering in the way of our people?
'I do not care for your presence, nor your presumption, but our ways are old, and I would not break them in times such as these.
'Speak then... what is it that you seek?'

Umfrë told you of a small community of Dunlendings who are chosen by their clans to enter the Mournshaws and commune with the spirits who live there. He believes that they might know of a way through the deep woods into the south.
