'Several days ago, Daervunn entered the Mournshaws -- a great forest to the west of here.
'He was hoping to find a way through that forest to the south that would be hidden from the prying eyes of our enemies, but I have heard nothing from him since.
'The locals call the forest Galar-gwig, and believe it to be inhabited by powerful spirits that do not care for the company of Men.
'There is one group among the Dunlendings, called the Derudh that dare frequent the forest - and even among their ranks it said that one will occasionally vanish into the forest... never again to be seen beneath mortal sun.
'I'd watch your step there.'

'${PLAYER}! You are the last person I expected to meet here. I have not had much success here. The forest is treacherous and wild, and I do not know its paths. I have made the acquaintance of one hunter who will dare the place -- indeed, he rescued me from a pack of strange hounds just last morning.
'What little I know concerns tales of a gathering of 'lords' in the forest...wild spirits or some such according to the tales, but each story I have heard is different, save they all refer to a great Huntsman who leads them.
'My hope is that they might be a hidden company of Elves, hiding themselves from the people of Nan Laeglin behind veils of myth and folk tales -- that might be a real stroke of fortune if we could find them.'
Find Daervunn in the Mournshaws
The Haunted Forest

You have learned that an unknown Ranger of the Grey Company has entered the Mournshaws in search of a hidden path to the south.
The Algraig firmly believe this forest is haunted by powerful and fey spirits. Only the Derudh of Nan Laeglin and a few brave hunters dare enter the place.
Even fewer return....
'Seek out Daervunn in the northern reaches of the Mournshaws.'
'I have heard that a duvodiad wandered into the haunted wood....'

Find Daervunn the Ranger who has wandered into the northern reaches of the Mournshaws.
It is uncertain whether he still lives, but if so it is possible he has found a path into Dunland that is unwatched by enemy eyes.

'If we are fortunate, none of the rings of Bebarahir borne by the Rangers of our Company will need to serve the purpose for which they were crafted. Even so, I am glad to have them in the event they become necessary. A single moment of hesitation on the part of Aragorn's foes could make the difference.
'It is time again to ride! Let us cross south into the northern stretches of Dunland. The plains of Enedwaith will be the next stop on our journey.
'We will take our rest once we cross into the land of Fordirith, in northern Enedwaith. Dagoras will select the location, and you should speak with Lothrandir when we arrive at Echad Dagoras to learn the lay of the land.'

'The road south is a long one, ${PLAYER}. You should know something of this land and its people.
'The Men of Dunland are a wild people, and they care little for the Dúnedain and not at all for the Men of Rohan. They have warred with the Rohirrim and covet still their lands; it is their strongly-held belief that those lands belong to the Men of Dunland. They are proud and fierce, quick to anger and slow to forgiveness. They tolerate no weakness and are suspicious of outsiders.
'During my time here in the south-lands, it seemed to me that these Men had no identity as \qDunlendings,\q thinking of themselves instead as members of particular clans dominated by strong, wilful leaders. Dagoras has met already with the member of one such clan: Wadu of the Uch-lûth. He has set aside his suspicions, for the moment, and you might learn something of his people by speaking with him.'

'You have come with these men, but you are not one of them. The warning I gave to this man, this Dagoras, I give to you: my people will not allow you to interfere with their lives. You may pass through these lands, but you cannot stay.
'Strength only do they respect. Strength such as mine, or my father Suvulch. Even my sister Nona wields the sword, and I wager she does so with greater skill than any of these duvodiad.'
Find Echad Dagoras in Fordirith
Talk to Lothrandir at Echad Dagoras
Talk to Wadu at Echad Dagoras
Chapter 9: The Plains of Enedwaith
The Grey Company rides now south out of Eregion and onto the plains of Enedwaith, the northern stretches of Dunland.
'Wadu is here at Echad Dagoras. He has set aside the suspicions common to so many of his people and may be of help to the Grey Company.'

'It is time for the Grey Company to continue its journey south, ${PLAYER}. Ride south into Enedwaith, where Dagoras will establish a camp in Fordirith, the northern reaches of that land. Lothrandir will then speak to you of the dangers in that place.'
'It has been a long time since I journeyed in these lands.'
'The ways of this place are coming back to me after my long absence.'

Lothrandir will be waiting for you at Echad Dagoras, the next stop on the Grey Company's journey south into Fordirith, in northern Enedwaith.
It is time to ride south into Enedwaith. The Grey Company will stop for rest at Echad Dagoras, in Fordirith.

Lothrandir is at Echad Dagoras, the camp of the Grey Company in Fordirith, the northern reaches of Enedwaith.
The Grey Company has passed into Enedwaith, and you should speak now to Lothrandir to learn the lay of the land.

Wadu of the Uch-lûth has come to Echad Dagoras in Fordirith.
Lothrandir has asked you to speak with Wadu of the Uch-lûth.
Collected blood-marks from Dunlendings in Fordirith (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Recovered weapons from fallen Uch-lûth clansmen (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'The Uch-lûth will tolerate your presence, but other Dunlending lûth will be openly hostile. They have been given gold and have forgotten their true allegiances. Many of them travelled north into the land of the holly, but they have returned. They are cowards on their own, and they are cowards on behalf of their new master!
'But these lûth that fight for gold have no loyalty to their former brothers. They fight even the Uch-lûth! For every one of my people they slay, they put a mark in blood on a chip of wood. They believe their new master will pay them for every one of their kinsmen they slay. It is an abomination.
'They have already killed some of my people. Travel to the deserters' camps north of here and deprive them of the blood-marks they have already collected. Recover, too, the weapons of my fallen brothers. I do not want them taken by their foes.'

'Wadu at least seems pleased with you, ${PLAYER}. If his family ruled the Uch-lûth, perhaps our road south would be easier. Sadly, it appears that his father Suvulch, though respected by the brenin of the Uch-lûth, is not one of his brehur.

'Tell your duvodiad friends what you have done for Wadu. I am not certain about them, but about you I have made up my mind. Your strength of will is like to mine, and you are made of similar stuff, strong as the stones of Dunland.'

'Welcome to the Huntsman's Hall, mortal. There are few who dare this place in these latter days, and fewer still who stand here worthy of the fate that brought them hence. What brings you here, I wonder?
'So you come in the name of the Dúnedain? Such glory as they held was forfeit in long ages past, and now they come to slink through our lord's realm as thieves might?
'Yet it is not for me to judge, for the Huntsman has forbidden us to decide the fate of mortals here. Speak with him if you would buy passage for the lost lordlings of Númenór, if this is indeed their final call to battle.'

'Ye are not welcome here, ${PLAYER}. The peoples of Middle-earth have proven their weakness as many times as needed to convince me of their folly.
'Yet ever and again my lord in the Uttermost West has bidden me be patient. He tells me that it may yet come to pass that my bow need not be nocked ere the Darkness ends -- and yet I remain against that eventuality.
'And so I challenge thee, remind me again of the myriad faults of Men, the hubris of the Elves, the greed of the dwarves, and the timid cowardice of halflings. Or prove to me that there is some mettle left in the folk of Middle-earth to take their fate into their own hands. Join my hunt and see it through, that I may judge you worthy or not.'

'So you have completed the Wild hunt. It seems there is some spark of valour left within your kind, ${RACE}. Very well then. The Dúnedain lordlings may pass through my forests unmolested. The spies of the Enemy will not see them here beneath these boughs.
'But be wary nonetheless: evil things creep here now, though they be blind before my power, nor can I see what fate awaits the Men of the West as they march to meet their doom. But I do know this: few days remain before the decisive battles are joined. The eyes of the Uttermost West watch keenly the struggle here, for its outcome will soon be decided.
'Take care, little one, and may your hunt be fruitful.'

Darkest of Waters

Glinghant was once the most beautiful place in all of Annúminas -- no small feat given the splendour of the ancient city at its height. Descriptions of the pools and gardens of Glinghant hold a special place in the hearts of my people. Even after the long years of decay, you could see the memory of its beauty.
The coming of Amarthiel and her legions to Annúminas is cause itself for sorrow, but of all the harm they have caused to this city, their possession and despoiling of Glinghant stirs me most to rage. I would cast them out of this place and restore the splendour it had of old, even should the rest of Annúminas fall. In that, I am not joined by most of my kindred, but such is my horror at the spoiling of Glinghant.
Amarthiel has many servants, but to Glinghant she has sent the darkwater: foul spirits of corruption. If you should venture beyond the gate into the terraced steps of Glinghant, I would account you highly should you defeat them.

'You'll never believe this, ${PLAYER}! I decided a new oven was needed to begin preparations for the next festival. The labourers went to dig a pit into the side of the Hill, and lo! We all heard a shovel scrape against some wood, and before I knew what happened, a door was dug out!
'The door is locked now, but I'll wager it is a forgotten cellar of Bag End. Bag End is just above it, you see. Do you think that's where Mad Baggins kept his treasures? I suppose we can only guess...for Lobelia owns Bag End now.
'If you think she'll be letting anyone else dig around for Old Bilbo's treasure, then you go right ahead and ask her; be my guest! I won't be risking it...but it is terribly exciting, all the same!'

'I'll wager Lobelia sent you to inquire after that new door going to the Baggins' lovely burrow. If you ask me, the whole affair smells of trouble. I tell my young ones, and I'll tell you too: best to mind your own matters, and no harm will come of aught.'

'Are you here about that door as well? You listen here: that mad fool of a Baggins never said anything about a secret cellar, and neither did that awful nephew of his, Frodo. I could not be more angry!
'I've scoured the whole burrow and not found a thing that could be used as a key to a hidden larder. They meant all along to leave Bag End to me with none of its proper fixings.
'If you want to see so much as a doorknob inside that cellar, you must find me that key! That gardener down on Bagshot Row surely knows something, but he won't speak a word to me. You look like a big, ominous sort; you ought to wrangle the truth out of him!'

Directions to Hengstacer Farms:
From the West-gate of Bree, travel north along the Greenway until you pass Thornley's Farm on your left and an old ruined fort on your right. There is a thin trail, beaten by the hooves of Hengstacer horses and ponies that leads up the hill beside those ruins. Follow that trail to the east and north, and you will find your way to Hengstacer Farms.

'My letter found you then? Excellent news, and even more excellent that you are here.
'I am Éogar, master of horses here at Hengstacer Farms, and I will tell you that there are no finer horses in all of Bree-land. I supply my horses to all stables far and wide...there are none better save for those of my homeland Rohan.
'You have already used one of my horses, so you are aware of how good they are, but now I wonder. Are you willing to own such a fine specimen...I wonder?'

'Excellent. This food will last us a while -- hopefully through to the borders of Rohan where we should be able to trade for additional supplies with the Rohirrim, though it is a long journey.'

'What a terror! I ventured into the Haunted Burrow, for I was sure there would be treasure tucked away in every corner. I swore I wouldn't leave until I came away with a few riches.
'Instead of jools at the bottoms of various jars and whatnot, I found the most horrible things instead! Sticky, cold, wet, terrifying things. Unnatural things!
'When I came back outside for a bit of fresh air, I found that I'd lost several valuables in the meantime. Surely they are at the bottoms of the jars now, for other greedy folks to find. Now I am poorer than when I started! I dare not go back; will you help me?'
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTE: Only one Haunted Burrow quest may be underway at a time.</rgb>

These delicate bones have an ashy feel to them, like they will crumble in a moment if you trouble them. You imagine the dust of death filling your nose and eyes and squeeze your eyes shut unwillingly in anticipation.
Fortunately, your fingers grasp a shiny button before too long.

You plunge your hand into this jar, but the insides of it squirm as if alive! Bugs! Bugs! Bugs!
You bear it just long enough to bravely retrieve a pocket-watch held hostage by the creepy crawlies within.

Do you really have to reach in here? You ought to. Holfast said he searched in any unlikely place where treasure could be hiding.
Oh, it is sticky and terribly unpleasant. Are there words for such an awful sensation?
You search for a moment, your heart beating fast as can be, and pull out a very nice glove! Hopefully this belongs to Holfast....
You plunge your hand into this jar, but the insides of it squirm as if alive! Bugs! Bugs! Bugs!
What foul brew is this? The flesh is sickeningly cold and smells of something rancid. It is slimy, sticky, and the memory of it lingers on your hand even after you have withdrawn it.
You reach into the puddle, but the blood drains from your head as you realize that it is quite warm. Feeling very faint, you continue to feel around.

You tremble as you reach into the soft, sticky webbing of the large coccoon. It looks uncannily real, even though you suspect it may be a fake. It is cold inside, and you shiver. Did you hear something?

'I've lost so many things! My monocle, my button...let's see. What else? Oh! My ring and my pocket-watch as well. There was something else too....
'I was rummaging in many places, but if you can find everything I lost throughout the Haunted Burrow, I'll be tremendously grateful to you.'

'You are such a brave ${RACE}! I can't believe you were able to bear it in there! You are bolder than I, and no mistake about it. I am tremendously indebted to you, ${PLAYER}.
'I am beginning to recover a bit from my terrifying adventure. Did you see any treasure while you were inside? Maybe I'll have another look....'

'Oh help, help! My friends and me, we thought we'd go have an adventure together and look for old Bilbo's treasure! But one-by-one, they disappeared, and suddenly I was all alone!
'I made it out safe enough, but they're still inside! I can only imagine what a horrible nightmare they must be having in that burrow.
'Will you help find them and get them back safe, ${PLAYER}? I'd be so very grateful indeed!'
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTE: Only one Haunted Burrow quest may be underway at a time.</rgb>
'Thank goodness they are all alive! I was so terribly worried. Maybe I will venture back in myself some day. I would dearly like a peek at old Bilbo's hidden treasure.'

'A ghost! I saw a ghost! Do you think it was the Old Took? I am so frightened! He was angry at me for eating his dinner while he wasn't looking one night...do you think he has come back to haunt me? O help; pray don't be cross with me! I meant no harm....'

'Hello? Yes, I was here with May! And don't you be trying to shoo me out. I left the party because I saw a glittering at the end of a corridor, and I thought it might be treasure. A pretty coin it was, too!
'Now leave me be. I'll not be leaving until I've found a great hoard of treasure!'
'Hmm? I'm sorry, I was just having a bit of a look at some of Bilbo Baggins' old notes. What a curious imagination he had! Wouldn't it be terribly exciting if his wild stories were real?'
'Eek! Go away! You don't scare me!'

'Hmm. I was sure this was the exit. It was a left, then a right, then a left, then another left, then another left...and then another left, I believe. Shh, you're interrupting! I am trying to remember the way out. Now pray leave me be.'
'Snnff. W-who might you be? I put on a black cloak to sneak around and frighten my friends, but I'm afraid I am lost. Will you show me the way out?'

'You are awake, ${PLAYER}! Thank goodness. You were exhausted after what happened last night, but that Ranger got us all safe to Archet in the end.
'I am terribly worried for his friend! Amdir looks so very ill. You can check on him if you like; he is just over there, to the west of where I am standing. Do you see him there, across the lane?'

'So you are awake at last, ${PLAYER}? You earned your rest, for you fought bravely last night. As for myself, I found no peace in slumber.
'The blade of the Black Rider pierced only my shoulder, though not deeply. I am chilled, but it is no matter....
'Thank you for your concern, but it is Strider for whom I fear! He is charged with a great task, but he tarries for my sake, and for Archet's.'

'Hail, ${PLAYER}. Amdir is right -- I am torn asunder! I do not wish to leave him in this state, and Archet must be warned that the Blackwolds mean to raid the town, but I should be seeking a different Baggins right now!'

Intro: Strider's Charge

With the help of the Ranger Strider and his friend Amdir, you have escaped death at the hands of a group of brigands called the Blackwolds.
You are now in the peaceful village of Archet, and you have witnessed evidence that this town is at great risk of an attack from the very Blackwolds that held you captive.
'Did you wander in with those Rangers and halflings in the middle of the night as well? I hope you'll not be bringing any trouble with you. That wound looks suspicious to me!'
'Look not to me, but to Strider. It is he who is in need of your help this day.'
'That poor dear Ranger... he was so brave last night! I do hope that Strider can help him. I don't have any experience with such violent wounds.'
'I haven't had breakfast yet! This is intolerable. First kidnapped and now starved... I do not like Big Folk one bit!'

Amdir, very pale and wounded, is sitting in Archet near The Mad Badger Inn.
You should check on Amdir, for he was stabbed last night while helping to rescue you and the two hobbits from the Blackwolds.

Strider kneels beside his friend Amdir, near The Mad Badger Inn in the village of Archet.
You should speak with Strider, for Amdir implied that Strider's need is the more pressing.

'Can you seek out Cun Annun in this area and defeat any that you might find? They can be found roaming to the south and east of my camp.
'Be wary, ${PLAYER}, for they are no ordinary hounds. The Cun Annun are demons of the ancient world.'
'Thank you for dispatching these insidious creatures. I fear that their arrival may give credence to tales of a darker force at work in the Lich Bluffs.'

'Perhaps you can help, ${PLAYER}. The people of Archet will be in great danger when the Blackwolds execute the plan we witnessed last night. The Captain here, a Man named Brackenbrook, does not like my look, and will not heed my warnings.
'Pray, speak to him on my behalf, and see if you can rouse him!
'Every moment I spend here is a moment in which my true charge plunges blindly nearer to unfathomable peril! The Black Rider you saw last night seeks a Baggins, and our friend Mundo is not the one.'
'If Captain Brackenbrook says we're safe, then we're safe. He's always done a fine job at protecting our village! Why would the Blackwold wanderers suddenly attack us now?'

'You think the Blackwolds mean to attack us? Don't be absurd! They harbour no love for us, but they haven't a leader, and they fight more among themselves than they do with outsiders.
'They couldn't raid a squirrel nest, let alone our town!'

'Did you wander in here last night with those Rangers? I do not like the look of those fellows one bit, but I let them stay on account of the pale one's wounds.
'You say the Blackwolds mean to attack us, but I do not believe it, not without proof. Those brigands have always been about -- they are an unruly lot, but not murderous.
'I'll not be attacking them without good reason. If you must, talk to folks around town and get their opinions. If they are on your side, I'll consider the Ranger's warning.'

'I see that your friend is wounded, and I hope it was not the Blackwolds that did it to him....
'I truly trust Captain Brackenbrook, for he has always kept us safe since he took charge of Archet. I won't argue with the captain, but I will help the injured fellow in any way that I can.'

'Alas for peaceful folk everywhere! It is an enormous task to convince them that evil people with evil intentions will commit evil deeds.
'It seems that I cannot leave yet. Amdir needs my help, and I have pressing work to do in Archet to get these people ready for the impending storm. If you help me, perhaps I can leave before tonight.'

Intro: Captain Brackenbrook

Strider will rest easy if Archet is made aware of the imminent threat from the Blackwolds, but the leader of the town's garrison, Captain Brackenbrook, is distrustful of the dangerous-looking Rangers. He simply will not heed Strider's warning.
'Argue all you like! I won't be attacking innocent people without reason, brigands or no. And I think you'll find my townsfolk agree with me.'
'I am worried for Amdir and worried for Archet, but I must find the real Mr. Baggins before the Black Riders do. Brackenbrook is a fool to risk the doom of his people on his dislike for my looks!'

'The wights can be found throughout the southern and western barrows of the Lich Bluffs.'

'Amdir, my poor old friend! A shadow has crept over him... the Black Rider that stabbed him is more fell than any creature you will meet in your travels!
'We have little time, and we must stretch what time we have by doing two things at once. Amdir needs medicine, ${PLAYER}, and quickly. Do you know of a plant called kingsfoil? It has great power to heal.
'You should ask Captain Brackenbrook if he knows of any that grows in these parts. Offer him assistance as well, if it does not take you far out of the way. We must begin to work on him, and perhaps he will look more kindly upon you after you do him a good deed.'

'Kingsfoil, eh? 'Tis a nice leafy plant that grows around Bronwe's Folly, a ruin south of here. Help yourself to as much as you'd like; we've no use for it.
'And as for your offer of assistance, I will take you up on it! We are always in need of able hands, and you might as well earn your keep while you stay with us.
'My best man, Calder Cob, is having trouble with wolves of late. Perhaps you could help him on your way to do your gardening job for the Ranger.'

'Danger has found you much earlier than I predicted! It sounds like Calder Cob had it in for you before you even arrived.
'How did he know of you, if he was at his post? And how did that Blackwold know you were coming?
'Thank you for the risk you took to deliver the kingsfoil. I will think upon this riddle while I prepare a salve for Amdir.'

'The delivery of this phial is a grim but important discovery. It appears that these phials are being used to corrupt the bodies of the fallen in the Lich Bluffs. It may also partially be the cause of the corrupted cairn-stones.

'These barrows have long been home to the dead of the Algraig clans of the Dunlendings -- and many other older peoples -- the bodies lain to rest after the customs of these people. Recently, however, several of the barrows have been desecrated for some nefarious purpose. I have heard that some of the corpses have recently been dragged out of their resting places and left for scavengers.
'Perhaps you would be willing to travel into the barrows where these bodies have been seen and investigate for me? It is a gruesome task, but I fear a great evil is growing within this place.
'The barrows I speak of are located east of the main road, upon the southern border of the Lich Bluffs.'

'My fears are true, it seems: a dark force is at work, raising wights across the Lich Bluffs. It is a tragedy that the bodies of these good people are being used for such nefarious purposes.
'We will yet discover what evil force is at work here.'

'Hey, you there! Yes, you there! I'm very hungry!
'I haven't eaten since some woman gave me a bit of bread and jam for breakfast this morning. Such fare is hardly meant to feed a rabbit, let alone a full-grown hobbit like me.
'If you get me proper food, I will reward you handsomely. I want something hearty and delicious!'

'Hooray, you brought me pork! Or bacon! Or perhaps sausage... oh, it doesn't matter; I can make a little of each.'
Mundo weighs the parcel of meats in his hands.
'This will give me something to munch on for a bit; hopefully this provender will last me until I can go back home.'

Bring Mundo his lunch of fresh boar-meat
A Very Empty Belly
Mundo Sackville-Baggins, a fellow prisoner from the Blackwold camp, is naturally very hungry after the ordeal, for hobbits have insatiable appetites.
'What are you still doing here? Are you putting food in my belly right now? Do you have some hidden store of vittles? No? Then get moving, if you please!'

Wild boars, perfect for pork or sausage, can be found roaming the outskirts of Archet.
You should collect boar-meat for Mundo's next meal so that he doesn't waste away from starvation.

'I cannot decide which is more dangerous right now: Calder Cob's treachery or the ignorance of Captain Brackenbrook!
'If Calder Cob is his best soldier, I know Brackenbrook will not believe that he tried to have you ambushed by a Blackwold.
'I did some asking around while you were gone, and there is a Blackwold brigand in the stocks, across the lane from here; he is being held for highway robbery. You should question him about Calder Cob.'
'That is a serious charge, ${PLAYER}. Calder Cob has been loyal to me and this town since he was a boy....'

'Let me go! I'm a friend of Calder Cob's, and I'm innocent at that! This idiot jailor won't heed me.'
Otto quiets down as you tell him you know of Calder Cob's treachery.
'So you think you know the plan? Don't be smug; it's too late! By now, the gears of war be turning down in the south, and quick. Soon I'll be free, and you'll be the one in shackles... or worse.'

'It is good to make your acquaintance, ${PLAYER}. I noticed you were questioning Otto... does that mean that his mutterings have been truthful?
'Yes, I do believe what you have come to Archet to tell. It is unprecedented, but all signs are showing that the Blackwolds mean to attack us. How is it that they have the means?
'If Brackenbrook does not believe you, you may tell him that I DO, for what it's worth.'

After Calder Cob tried to have you ambushed by the Blackwolds, Strider wishes to prove beyond a doubt that he is an enemy to Archet.
'I taste vengeance on the South Wind.'
'Otto is a Blackwold, and he is being held in the stocks. You can find him across the lane from here, past where the hobbits are sitting. There you will find the Archet Jail.'
'You should repeat everything Otto said to Captain Brackenbrook. If any of it is true, it sounds like Archet is in for some real trouble.'
'I believe you, for what it's worth! I've never heard a brigand speak so dark....'

'If I am to speak openly against Isengard, I need evidence that the half-orcs serve Saruman. We do not wish to kneel to Orthanc, but there is much fear of what will happen if we do not.
'With true evidence of Isengard's involvement in these attacks, I and many of my people will be free to speak our anger and deny Saruman the easy submission he expects of us.
'If you can find some sign of Isengard's involvement with the raiders in Nan Laeglin, that will give me all that I need.'

'This is it then. Now we know for certain that Isengard has set these devils upon us to force us to heel.
'Neither I, nor any among my fellows who dare count themselves Men shall speak in favour of this emissary from Orthanc.
'I do not know what the future holds for us, Duvodiad -- it may be that in a season's time all of Enedwaith shall be burned and barren -- but at least we shall die as stalwarts and not as cowards.'

'Amdir looks so changed since last night! I almost feel like he's naught but a shadow when I look at him, like he isn't really there... how it makes me shiver!
'I saw Strider make a salve of kingsfoil for his wound, but my Gammer always used a different remedy when a young Brandybuck would get a nasty splinter -- sweet bilberry tea!
'I smelled bilberries by the water to the east of here as we passed in the night, which means they're in season. I would dearly like to make a tea for poor Amdir.'
'Well done! You have found more than enough for a good strong tea. This is sure to cheer Amdir right up! Give me a moment, and I will steep the berries in some boiling water.'

Sweet Bilberry Tea
Celandine Brandybuck believes that the medicinal qualities of bilberries will make a fine tea to stave off Amdir's apparent infection.
'I hope my Gammer's tea will make Amdir feel a bit better. It always cheered me up when I was ill!'

Celandine smelled bilberries by water to the east of Archet as she passed through last night.
You should collect bilberries, for they make a sweet tea to stave off infection, or so the hobbits' lore will tell you.

'Doesn't the bilberry tea smell delightful? It still reminds me of my Gammer, who made this for me when I was under the weather, even though my Gammer is long gone.
'You were such a dear to collect those wild berries for me, so I shan't be taking all the credit! Why don't you bring this nice brew to Amdir so he can thank you himself?
'You make sure he drinks it all up!'

'Did that tea perk him up? I knew it would! Bilberry tea always fixes me right up, and I know it would be especially sweet if it came from both of us, ${PLAYER}.
'I know Amdir will be back on his feet soon -- he is so brave!'

'Does... that tea smell of bilberries? That was very... sweet of Celandine, and very good of you to fetch her the makings. I am all the sorrier, for I cannot drink this now. I... I do not feel well enough just now.
'I will pretend to drink it. You must tell Celandine I enjoyed her tea. Please... do not let her know that her kindness was wasted on me!'

A Gift for Amdir
Celandine made some medicinal bilberry tea for Amdir, hoping that it will help to strengthen and cheer him against whatever shadow has come over him.

'...'
Amdir's eyes are now closed, and he makes no more effort to speak at this time. His face is as pale as ice.
'Quickly now! You mustn't let the tea get cold. I hope it makes Amdir feel better!'

Amdir sits across the lane from Celandine, in the centre of Archet.

'Does Ned speak true of his prisoner? If so, we would be wise to investigate Otto's threat of trouble in the south. I'll not question Calder Cob's lifetime of loyalty if there is no truth to back it up.
'But if you and Ned are right in your suspicion, this will be a very bad situation for us.
'Cal Sprigley's farm is to the south of here, near the gate to the town of Combe. If aught is going on, he'll know!'
'A stranger, eh? If Brackenbrook sent you, I'll take you in. I'm afraid you're the best thing that's happened to us all day!'
Talk to Cal Sprigley to assess the Blackwold threat in the south
Intro: Siege to the South

Captain Brackenbrook, worried about Otto the Brigand's mention of a Blackwold attack from the south of Archet, has asked you to travel to Cal Sprigley's farm to find proof of the brigands' intentions.
'Cal Sprigley's farm is south of here, beyond Bronwë's Folly if you follow the road towards Combe. I hope Cal can set this mess straight....'

Cal Sprigley can be found at his farm in the southernmost part of Archet.
You should speak with Cal Sprigley to assess the reality of the Blackwold threat.

'${PLAYER}, I fear the road below may be watched too closely for our company to move as secretly as our purpose requires. To this end, I have sent some of my kindred west into the Gloomglens to seek a less travelled path into the south.
'We need your aid here, but when all is ready, you should head to Echad Idhrenfair in the Gloomglens and speak with Idhrenfair himself. I am certain he could use your help scouting the way.'
'Welcome, ${PLAYER}. Saeradan sent you to aid us? That is well, for these myriad gorges are a mystery to be unravelled. Your aid will be greatly appreciated.'
Talk to Idhrenfair at Echad Idhrenfair
A More Secret Way
Saeradan fears that the road south into Dunland may be watched too closely, forcing the Rangers of the Grey Company to seek a safer route to Rohan.
'Echad Idhrenfair lies to the west in the Gloomglens.'

Idhrenfair is at Echad Idhrenfair in the Gloomglens, north and west of Echad Saeradan.
Saeradan has suggested you might help Idhrenfair seek a more secret path southwards.
The only gate is blocked! Archet is on its own now...

'I'm glad you're here! Some Blackwolds tried to attack us this morning, but we drove them off.
'We must get help from Combe, the next town over. It's south-west of here, and not more than a short journey away. They must bring their soldiers to Archet at once to help stave off the raid!
'Please make haste -- I fear the Blackwolds mean to attack tonight. The road here is crawling with brigands, but I pray you can make it safe to Combe.'

'B-blocked? No, it cannot be! My men travelled to Combe only yesterday for a delivery.... That is bad news, ${PLAYER}. The captain must be informed of what's going on at once!
'Here is a note for Brackenbrook. He knows my scrawl; he will believe you now.'

As Brackenbrook reads the letter from Cal Sprigley, his face is blank. He reads it a second time, and only then does he look at you.
'I have been a fool. Oh, what have I done?'
Go to Combe to plead for aid against the Blackwold threat

Cal Sprigley has asked you to gather what help you can from the nearby town of Combe.
'Please hurry, ${PLAYER}! I think the Blackwolds mean to attack tonight. I don't know how it came to be, but they are organized now. They pose a greater threat than I could have imagined.'
'Brackenbrook needs to know what the Blackwolds have done! You must get back to Archet -- I fear there isn't much time!'

The Combe Gate is not far to the west of Sprigley's Farm, along the road south from the town of Archet.
You should ask for assistance in Combe, for they have many well-equipped soldiers there due to their proximity to the dangerous Chetwood.

'In these days, previously tranquil lands are now fraught with danger and enemies at every turn. Already, we have expended most of the arrows we brought with us.

'My dad and the other farmhands, they gave chase to the brigands after the attack on our farm. I don't think the brigands expected us to put up such a fight after they surprised us. There weren't many of them, but I never saw them act so bold afore today.
'Only problem is, they ain't back yet. They ran off to the east, chasing the brigands into the woods. It was hours ago, though, and I'm very worried!
'Could you go look for them and bring them back safe?'

'No! It cannot be! My poor father... and the others, no, it cannot be, it cannot.'
Wil is silent for a long moment, his eyes closed, but after a great pause he is roused.
'I will have my revenge upon those Blackwolds, or I will die trying! Archet will never fall to such murderous fiends.'

From the myriad beasts you have defeated in Thrór's Coomb, you have manage to obtain a great trophy: Cloben's Fang.

Frithgeir is at Zudrugund, which lies within Nár's Peak, north of the river.
The fang you recovered will long serve as a symbol of the defeat of the gwiber that menaced Thrór's Coomb.
You must appeal to Jon Brackenbrook against his father's wishes

'You cannot fathom just how wrong I have been. I have trusted Calder Cob and heeded his advice for a long time... even after my own son tried to warn me of his duplicity.
'My son, Jon, is a worthy hunter, but he has not set foot in this town for over three years. He will never forgive me for the things I said to him.
'O, what a fool I am! I told him he was not welcome in Archet until he stopped behaving like a jealous child. Now he and his hunters are our only hope. But what can I do? He does not deserve to be dragged deeper into my folly. Nay, Archet must withstand this storm without help....'

'You come from the town, do you? I have been watching from the bounds... the skies have turned dark and fell, and there is a shadow of unrest over all of Archet, over Men and beasts and trees alike. Let me guess: my father has not the wisdom to observe such things, so you heard of his exiled son and came to me for aid.
'Come, then, out with it! I desire to hear what you have to tell.'

'Do not despair, ${PLAYER}! You have done remarkably well -- indeed, better than I could have done. You earned Captain Brackenbrook's trust.
'You must appeal to his son Jon against his wishes. I must leave soon, and Archet will need all the help it can get even if a father's pride is at stake.
'I am confident you will be able to bring the hunters in and give this town a fighting chance. In the meantime, I must make haste. Amdir assures me he just needs rest....'
Brackenbrook is hopeless -- you should ask Strider what to do
Ask the exiled hunter to come to Archet's aid
Intro: The Exiled Hunter

Captain Brackenbrook, in his loyalty to Calder Cob, allowed his own son to become estranged from him after his son and Calder Cob had a falling out. The Captain took Calder Cob's side, and his son has not set foot in Archet since.
'Nay, I will not ask Jon to come to our aid. I am not worthy to ask favours of my son. I will fall with Archet.'
'Nay, I will not ask Jon to come to our aid. I am not worthy to ask favours of my son. I will fall with Archet.'
'You have proven yourself to be both wise and brave, ${PLAYER}. I trust Archet's fate to you in my stead! You have given me a little more peace of mind.'

Strider has not yet left Archet, but he is anxious to leave so that he can pursue his true charge.
Strider is a wise Ranger who has seen many evil things come to pass; you should ask him what to do.

Jon Brackenbrook, the exiled son of the Captain, can be found in the Hunter's Lodge to the north-east of Archet.
You should appeal to Jon Brackenbrook and his hunters to come to the aid of the besieged town.
Defeated Blackwold brigands (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
A letter inside the satchel tells that the Blackwolds mean to attack tonight with the help of Angmar

'Calder Cob has shown his true colours at last! I knew him to be evil-hearted, but my father is too trusting. He does not like to think ill of people. His blindness wounded me, but he is a good man.
'So, to answer your question: yes, I will come to Archet's aid, I and my fellows. I am a hunter and a skilled warrior, trained by my father and Captain, and I would rather die than sit idly by while foul brigands crash upon a decent peoples.
'Let us see what there is to see before the storm is upon us. While I gather my warriors and my weapons, you should sneak into the Blackwold's Roost and uncover their plan of attack for tonight.
'Good work, ${PLAYER}, and fast too! This will be a great boon to Archet! Now we will be able to counter their efforts with the proper strategy.'
Defeat brigands to thin their ranks (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Gather information about the intended Blackwold raid
Bring the Blackwold-plans to Jon Brackenbrook
Intro: Into the Shadow
Jon Brackenbrook has sent you into the Blackwold's Roost, the heart of the shadow over Archet, in hopes that you can uncover their plan of attack.
'The Blackwold's Roost is south of here, across the lake. You should be able to find plans if you venture around. Just be prepared to fight as you go!'

The Blackwold's Roost can be found south of the Hunting Lodge.
You should defeat brigands to thin their ranks and gather information about their exact plans for the raid on Archet.

Jon Brackenbrook is mustering his strength in the Hunter's Lodge, in the north-east corner of Archet.
You should return to Jon Brackenbrook with the Blackwold-plans you have collected.
The East Path is fraught with danger, but in that danger lies hope
Defeated spiders on the Old East Path (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
This brigand scout met his doom at the dead end on the Old East Path

'What an excellent find, ${PLAYER}. These folk from Angmar sound like evil foes, but at least we know what we are up against....
'The plans also show a map that points to the Old East Path, which is just near here. We all avoid that path save for Atli Spider-bane, a visitor from east of the Misty Mountains.
'Speak with Atli and learn what he can tell you about the path. We can use the path to our advantage if we manage to successfully scout it.'

'Aye, I know all about the Old East Path. There are spiders everywhere! When you kill one, another takes its place.
'If we are to make use of the path at all, we should fight our way through and ensure that it is still blocked at the walls of Archet.
'The spiders will do some work for us against the Blackwolds. And what the spiders don't deal with, we shall come from afore and behind with our axes and our blades, and we will fall upon them like a mighty cave coming down!'

'That is good news! A dead end at the end of the path will work in our favour! The brigands will be slowed, and they will have the spiders at their heels, and the hunters will come from behind while the soldiers attack at the head!
'I will go to Archet to rally them and ready them for the storm that awaits them tonight.'
Talk to Atli Spider-bane about the Old East Path

The Blackwold-plans you collected reveal that the brigands, guided by the evil forces of Angmar, mean to attack under the cover of shadow by the Old East Path, which is overrun by spiders.
'Keep your wits about you, ${CLASS}. Spiders are deadly foes.'
'I think Atli's knowledge of the layout of the Old East Path will help us form a plan.'

Within the depths of the barrows, foul creatures are performing a dark ritual of death.

'Beneath Drug Haniad lies an ancient crypt that appears to be the cause of the darkness that is growing in the southern Lich Bluffs. One of our scouts recently reported seeing a crude entrance dug into the ground there, and from within he heard dark chanting.
'Could you seek out the entrance to this barrow and disrupt whatever foul ritual is taking place down below? If so, speak with me again.'

'I am glad to see that you were able to disrupt that grisly ritual. From what I understand, the body that was on the table was a new vessel for Ferndúr the Virulent.
'I fear that, unknown to us, one of the Lords of the Gauntmen settled here some time ago and has been using the barrows of the Lich Bluffs to raise wights for an army of his own.
'Thank you for disrupting the ritual, as it may have well saved the lives of the entire Grey Company and many of the men and women that call this land home.'

'Have they spotted me yet? I don't think so...good! They mustn't know the Ale Association is meddling, or else I fear there will be an all-out war between our two leagues.

'Leave it to hobbits to get lost underground! This is a capital opportunity for us to scare them silly. You should go find them and scare them in any way you can think of.'

'If you don't believe me, go see for yourself! But you'd be wise to steer clear of the wing of the cellar where the spooks have got to, if you ask me.'

While 'A Little Extra Never Hurts -- Part 1' can only be completed once per account, this quest, 'A Little Extra Never Hurts -- Part 2', may be completed by every character.

'You think it's strange to be talking to a cat? Well, I think it's strange to be talking to you, ${RACE}! Would you like to be flagged as having completed Volume II Book 9 of the Epic quest series? If so, speak to me again!
'Do I even need to tell you how this works? Oh well, just in case you weren't paying attention: completion of this quest will flag you as having completed Volume II Book 9 of the Epic quest.'
Level Up: Volume II: Book 9
Completion of this quest will flag your character as having completed all the quests in Book 9 of the Epic quest series of Volume II.
Talk to Elevensies to complete Volume II, Book 9!
Shadows from Afar

${PLAYER},
Please make your way to me in all haste. There is a matter that I believe is of great importance to you. Find me, as always, within our training hall at the Mud-gate in Bree.
Albra

'It seems that you have reached another important milestone in your journey as a ${CLASS}, ${PLAYER}.
'You may have noticed that I have in my possession a number of books that may help you to become a better ${CLASS}. Now that you are ready to read them, you should buy these books and learn what they have to teach you.'
'Players should never see this.'
Bring the letter to Albra Lowbanks in Bree
Your Legend Grows
You received a letter from your trainer in Bree-town asking for you to return to her. Apparently, there is something that she wishes to teach you.

Albra Lowbanks sent you a letter requesting that you visit her in the training hall in Bree.
Deliver the letter to Albra. She can be found in the training hall for burglars beneath the Mud-gate.

'Greetings, ${CLASS}. We have recently received word from our scouts that the outpost Gwingris in Eregion is in need of experienced adventurers like yourself.
'Head to Eregion and look to the north-west. There you will find our outpost of Gwingris. When you get there, look for the Elf Daegennan.'

'Greetings, ${CLASS}. We have recently received word from our scouts that the outpost Gwingris in Eregion is in need of experienced adventurers like yourself.
'Head to Eregion and look to the north-west. There you will find our outpost of Gwingris. When you get there, look for the elf Daegennan.'
'Well met, friend ${CLASS}. Are you here to help the Elves of Eregion?'
Talk to Daegennan in Gwingris
The Elves of Eregion

The Elves of Eregion need the help of experienced adventurers.
An Explorer of Eregion has asked you to travel to the Elven outpost of Gwingris in Eregion, to the south of Rivendell. Once you arrive you should look for the Elf Daegennan.
'${PLAYER}, what are you still doing here? You should heed the call of the Elves of Eregion!'
'${PLAYER}, what are you still doing here? You should heed the call of the Elves of Eregion!'

Daegennan is at Gwingris in Eregion.
You were instructed to seek out the Elf Daegennan.
Collected club moss (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
'The third ingredient I need are some clumps of club moss. You can find it growing among the rocks at the edge of the river to the north-west.'
'I trust this task was not overly difficult? The forest can be frightening to those who do not understand its ways.'
Collect club moss (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring the club moss to Enit at Galar Culch
Rituals of the Forest - Creeping Moss
Enit has asked you to retrieve several pieces of club moss as part of a ritual to summon one of the spirits of the forest.
The moss Enit has requested can be gathered along the edge of the river in the north-west region of the Mournshaws.

Enit is at Galar Culch in the Mournshaws.
You should bring the club moss you have collected to Enit.
Collected living bark (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'The final ingredient I need is the living bark taken from the wood-trolls that wander the Mournshaws. They can be found throughout the forest, but needless to say they shall not part with their bark quietly, for they hate all who intrude upon their domain.'
'You have the living bark? It should suffice, though I would rather you had not returned...'
Collect living bark (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring the living bark to Enit at Galar Culch
Rituals of the Forest - Skin of Wood
Enit has asked you to retrieve several pieces of living bark as part of a ritual to summon one of the spirits of the forest.
The living bark Enit has requested can be gathered from any of the wood-trolls that stalk the forests of the Mournshaws.

Enit is at Galar Culch in the Mournshaws.
You should bring the living bark you have collected to Enit.
Collected oak-branches (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
'The first ingredient I need is several sturdy oak branches recently fallen. You can likely find several in the forest to the west of here.'
'You have the oak branches? Very well, leave them with me and find the rest of the things I have asked of you.'
Collect oak-branches (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring the oak branches to Enit at Galar Culch
Rituals of the Forest - Oaken Limbs
Enit has asked you to retrieve several strong oaken branches as part of a ritual to summon one of the spirits of the forest.
The oak branches Enit has requested can be gathered in the northern stretches of the Mournshaws.

Enit is at Galar Culch in the Mournshaws.
You should bring the oak branches you have collected to Enit.
Collected mistletoe (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
'The second ingredient I need are a number of sprigs of recently cut mistletoe. You can likely find it hanging in the forest to the north of here.'
'This mistletoe is fresh enough, place it here. Do you have the rest?'
Collect mistletoe (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring the mistletoe to Enit at Galar Culch
Rituals of the Forest - Mistletoe
Enit has asked you to retrieve several sprigs of mistletoe as part of a ritual to summon one of the spirits of the forest.
The mistletoe Enit has requested can be gathered in the forest across the river to the north-west.

Enit is at Galar Culch in the Mournshaws.
You should bring the mistletoe you have collected to Enit.

You are not sure where this coin came from, but it seems to be a relic from Khazad-dûm, called Moria by the Elves. There are many who would be interested in such a relic and would likely provide you with a great reward!
<rgb=#FF0000>Bring this coin to any of the following people to receive your reward: • Jon Brackenbrook in Archet • Dwalin in Thorin's Hall • Mayor Will Whitfoot in Michel Delving • Barliman Butterbur in Bree-town • Cardavor in Celondim</rgb>

'What do you have here? A coin of some sort? Doesn't look like much... and what's this, some sort of doors on the back? What a queer coin you've brought me!
'I suppose it is worth something, although surely not much. Perhaps Keeper Foxtail would like to put it on display in the Mathom House.
'Yes, that should be fine. Here, choose something that you feel is appropriate for a coin such as this.'
'Hmm? Do you need something?'

'A dwarf-coin of some sort, is it not? I have heard of such things, but I never thought to see one. Where did you come across it?
'I would gladly give you something in trade for this coin. Choose what you would like, and we shall finish our trade.'
'Hello, can I help you?'

'A dwarf-coin of some sort, is it not? I have heard of such things, but I never thought to see one. Where did you come across it?
'I would gladly give you something in trade for this coin. Choose what you would like, and we shall finish our trade.'
'Hello, can I help you?'

'I cannot believe it! It is an ithildín coin! It is said that many were minted to commemorate the friendship of the Elves of Hollin and the Dwarves of Khazad-dûm. Most were lost... where did you come across such a treasure?
'Please, friend, trade this coin with me. I have many things to offer in trade. Choose something you think appropriate!'
'Greetings. Is there something you seek from me?'
Turn in your ithildín coin to receive your reward
Ithildín Coin

You have found a mysterious coin inlaid with ithildín. This rare metal was made by the Elves from mithril long ago. The image of the Doors of Durin, the doors that guarded the West Gate of Moria, is found on one side of the coin, while the other has the image of a hammer and anvil, the signs of Durin.

'I cannot believe it! It is an ithildín coin! It is said that many were minted to commemorate the friendship of the Elves of Hollin and the Dwarves of Khazad-dûm. Most were lost... where did you come across such a treasure?
'Please, friend, trade this coin with me. I have many things to offer in trade. Choose something you think appropriate!'
'Greetings. Is there something you seek from me?'

'Barliman Butterbur at your service, friend! That's quite a strange coin you've got there! Looks like a dwarf-coin of some sort... I've seen a few from guests, mind you, but not one like this. Not sure even what it's made of!
'Well, not sure I would take it for a meal or a room, but it probably has some value to someone... if only as something interesting to talk over!
'I will offer you a trade. I've a number of things travellers have left behind. You can trade this coin for one of those. How's that sound?'
'Hmm? What can I do for you?'

'Hail, friend. I see you have found an ithildín coin. These coins were minted by the Dwarves of Moria in the days of their friendship with the Elves of Eregion. See here, engraved here are the Doors of Durin, which were inlaid with this same metal.
'Most of these coins were lost when Moria fell into darkness. If you would have it, I would like to keep this coin. It can serve as a good reminder in these dark times of the fellowship that can exist between dwarves and Elves.
'However, I would not ask you to go away empty-handed. Choose something you find acceptable, and we shall make our exchange.'
'Hail, friend. Is there something that you need?'

'I cannot believe it! It is an ithildín coin! It is said that many were minted to commemorate the friendship of the Elves of Hollin and the Dwarves of Khazad-dûm. Most were lost... where did you come across such a treasure?
'Please, friend, trade this coin with me. I have many things to offer in trade. Choose something you think appropriate!'
'Greetings. Is there something that you need?'

Bring your ithildín coin to one of the following people to receive a reward.

You have obliterated Ferndúr's plague
Find a way to enter Ferndúr's chamber
Destroy all the corpses before defeating Ferndúr
Challenge: The Lost Temple -- Clean Sweep

Destroy all of the infected corpses in Ferndúr's chamber before defeating the Gaunt-lord himself.
<rgb=#FF0000>This quest will be cancelled if you leave the Lost Temple before completing it.</rgb>
Ferndúr the Virulent remains scheming deep within the Rhudauran temple.

Ferndúr the Virulent has nearly completed his deadly experiments beneath the lost Rhudauran temple.
The plagues he has concocted are too deadly to be allowed to fester. You must <rgb=#FF0000>destroy all the corpses within his chamber before the Gaunt-lord himself is defeated</rgb> in order to ensure that every trace of them is obliterated.
The Elves have travelled to Edhelion to investigate Elrond's terrible premonition....

'Here we are, as Dwalin bade, standing among this party of Elves who arrived when we did. But now what? Who should we talk to?
'That fellow over there, the dark-haired one, looks to be the leader of this company. Dwalin sent us to find out why they are here, and if we may be of any assistance to them.
'You are the more courteous dwarf, ${PLAYER}. Go on -- speak to that tall fellow! Do you think he speaks Westron?'

'Interesting! We have followed the signs of my father's dream to this place, and the dwarves have followed the signs of trouble here as well.
'I wonder if the two quests are not unrelated, ${PLAYER}. What do you think?
'Well, let us begin our investigation, now that we are all here. Elrohir, my brother, has already gone out to scout the lands. Dwalin, though a dwarf, is a friend to Rivendell. We will lend him what help we can.'
Talk to Elladan son of Elrond
Intro: Elrond's Errand

A party of Longbeards and a party of Elves have returned to Thorin's Hall after a long absence from both. Nos Grimsong of the dwarves has come to offer his aid to the Elves and to find out why they have returned at this time.
'Please speak with that tall Elf on Dwalin's behalf! He stands just there, beneath that gate facing the ruins.'

Elladan, a son of Elrond Halfelven, stands not far from Nos Grimsong.
You should speak with Elladan to learn on what errand the Elves of Rivendell have ventured so far into Ered Luin.
<rgb=#00FF00>The first assault has been broken. There are a few short moments to rest before the assault continues</rgb>
<rgb=#00FF00>You have defended against the second assault. There are a few short moments to gather your breath before the next arrives</rgb>
<rgb=#00FF00>You have defended against the third assault. There are a few short moments to gather your breath before the next arrives</rgb>
<rgb=#00FF00>You have defended against the fourth assault. You should return to Brogur before the final assault</rgb>
<rgb=#FF0000>Brogur has been defeated</rgb>

'The barricades are set and my dwarves stand ready. All that must be done now is to wait for the Orcs to come.
'I would ask that you follow the ebb and flow of the battle and aid where you are needed most. Also, do not forget to unfurl the banners of Khazad-dûm. They can help stir the hearts of all Free Peoples to great deeds and may even help turn the tide of battle. However, do not use them lightly, as once unfurled, a banner's strength is spent.
'Prepare yourself, as I fear it won't be long now....'

'It was a glorious battle, ${PLAYER}. One that shall be long remembered! The Orcs thought they could use trickery to gain the upper hand, but they could not stand in the face of our combined might.
'Now, let us finish our business here and see what else we can do to push back these foul Orcs!'
Talk to Brogur in the Deep-way

Push back the second assault

Brogur must survive the assault
Skirmish: Battle of the Deep-way
The Deep-way, a passage connecting the Great Delving to the Water-works, must be defended against the Orc onslaught.
Brogur is leading the defence of the Deep-way against the forces of Mazog. You should report to him to receive your assignment.
The first assault on the Deep-way has begun. Protect the barricades!

Dorollas believes that Skorgrím is the Dour King in Elrond's dream

'My father is great among the Wise, and his dreams and foretellings do not often stray from the mark. These are the words he imparted to me:
\qBlood-red footsteps Upon snow coloured black, Where the Dour King walks to take back his throne and finish what was begun.\q
'I am no riddle-master, but some of the Elves of my company have skill in solving such things.
'Come, let us speak with the riddle-masters Merethen and Dorollas, for Dorollas bade us come here. Hopefully they know where to start looking.'

'I was the one who led the party here, for I believe the Dour King is none other than Skorgrím, king of the Dourhands of old.
'There is only one problem with my logic: Skorgrím has been dead for many long years. He died here, when he tried to raid Edhelion for Elven relics that he believed would ensure his immortality.
'I hope I have not led the party astray, but my heart tells me Skorgrím is part of this story.'

'Mae govannen -- I am here to help solve the riddle that is Elrond's dream.
'Look yonder, ${PLAYER}. Thorin's Hall belches smoke and soot, and the white snow of the mountain is black ere it touches the floor of the valley.
'\qUpon snow coloured black....\q What do you think? It is rather literal for a riddle.'

'Dorollas led us here because he believes that Skorgrím is the Dour King in my father's dream? Had I known, I would never have let this party be led here. Skorgrím is dead; my father watched him die!
'But Merethen believes she has found a piece of the puzzle -- the black snow, dirtied from the Dourhands' slovenly stewardship of these halls.
'I will permit the investigation to continue, but I am very skeptical and disappointed in Dorollas's judgement.'

'It was across this bridge that brave Talagan brought the library's walls down upon Skorgrím and himself, thus putting an end to Skorgrím's lust for immortality. The walls smote them both as they crumbled.
'But that is a strange flower, one that I have never seen before. Is it familiar to you, ${RACE}?'

'I am lucky to be alive after the injuries I bore the day Edhelion fell. I...I do not think I have the will to go back into that place.
'It is only a shadow of its former glory now. Only pain remains.'

'I was here when Edhelion fell. I was a healer, but my strength in mending was not enough to mend the hurts caused by Skorgrím and his Dourhand warriors.

'Henric,
Strange things are afoot these days in and around Oatbarton. First there was that mysterious relic that appeared in Bungo Grubb's pipe-weed fields; killed the crop dead, it did, and left everyone else worried for their own!
But now things are even worse. Hobbits have been disappearing left and right. And these aren't Tooks I'm talking about, neither! No, these are good, honest Bolgers and Boffins, as solid and dependable gentlehobbits as you could hope to meet! Not a flaw among them, save being over-fond of their food and drink, and that's not a flaw at all in my estimation!
I don't know for sure what could have caused this recent spate of disappearances, though I have my guesses. I have not seen as many of the grim-faced Rangers lurking about in recent days; is it the same in Bree? In any event, if you know of a stalwart adventurer, be sure to send him or her to me at once. I am worried for my friends here in Oartbarton! We're within the bounds of the Shire, of course, but the rest of Evendim is a dangerous place, just to our north, and even Oatbarton has been frightful of late.
Wishing you the best, your devoted cousin,
Fenric'
<rgb=#FF0000>This Quest Arc begins with 3-Man Small Fellowship content, progresses through 6-Man Fellowship instances, and finally culminates in a 12-Man Raid. It is recommended that you complete Volume III Books 1 and 2 beforehand, but is not required.</rgb>

'Things have been a mite worrisome about my fire for the past few evenings, ${PLAYER}. Talk of the surrounding lands has been grim, with little good cheer to be had, even in the common room of the Pony! That's a sure sign of trouble, isn't it?
'Why, just recently one of the good hobbits of Bree gave to me a letter he received from one of his relations out Shire way, and he talks of trouble as plain as the nose on your face, or on mine! Mysterious relics appearing out of the blue, promising crops suddenly failing, and good solid hobbits vanishing, with no reasons given!
'I was never over-fond of Rangers, but they seem to be gone now. No one has seen that Strider for weeks, and few other grim-faced Men of his stripe have been seen since either. Is it possible the Rangers really did protect the peace of the countryside? In their absence, things seem to be getting worse, that's for certain.
'If you're of a mind to, you should travel to the town of Oatbarton, in the southern reaches of Evendim but within the Shire-bounds, to speak to Fenric Banks. His cousin Henric, who showed me his letter, is worried and wants to make sure that everything is all right. You are just the ${RACE} to see it done, that is clear to me!'
<rgb=#FF0000>This Quest Arc begins with 3-Man Small Fellowship content, progresses through 6-Man Fellowship instances, and finally culminates in a 12-Man Raid. It is recommended that you complete Volume III Books 1 and 2 beforehand, but is not required.</rgb>

'What brings you to Northcotton Farm, ${PLAYER}? Something's not quite right here, and I'm glad to have your help! This is the last place Gladiola Farmer was seen before her disappearance. We'll get to the bottom of it!'

'Ah, hello there, ${PLAYER}, it is a pleasure to meet you. I wish we met under happier circumstances, because things have not been going well here in Oatbarton, as you must know if you saw my letter to cousin Henric!
'The Bounders have been kept busy in recent weeks, but now things are happening within the Bounds: strange relics appearing in pipe-weed fields overnight, crops dying out suddenly; it's the worst I've ever seen it!
'But now hobbits are disappearing: first that thing appeared in Bungo Grubb's field, and not long after, Isenbard Bolger's up and gone. Then Crystal Bolger vanished, and afterwards Andy Boffin and Gladiola Farmer. A couple Bounders went off to Northcotton Farm, west of here and up the hill, where Gladiola Farmer was last seen. You should gather a couple friends and go investigate. I'm worried!'
Talk to Fenric Banks in Oatbarton
Talk to Bounder Boffin inside Northcotton Farm
In Their Absence, Chapter 1
Shadows are lengthening throughout Eriador now that many of the Rangers have left for the south-lands, and trouble is brewing in their absence.

'The letter Henric Banks showed me from his cousin Fenric is worrying, ${PLAYER}, wouldn't you say? It seems to me that troubles are increasing everywhere these days, and even the cheery common room of the Pony is not safe from these worries!
'I haven't seen hide nor hair from those Rangers recently, and if you'd asked me a couple weeks ago, I'd have been delighted! But now I'm not so sure. In their absence, the shadows seem to be lengthening and the troubles increasing! It's bad for business!
'You should travel to Oatbarton and see about helping Fenric Banks. The village is in the southern reaches of Evendim, but is within the bounds of the Shire. It is one of the most northerly of the hobbit-villages.'
'A couple Bounders went off to Northcotton Farm, west of here and up the hill, to look for the missing hobbits. You should gather a couple friends and go investigate. I'm worried!'

The Northcotton Farm is located west of Oatbarton's town centre and up the steep hill.

'My assistant, Tulip Grubb, has gone further into the farm in search of the four missing hobbits. If you do see any sign of them, be sure to tell Tulip. Keep your eyes open for any clues! Were those good folk hobbitnapped?
'There's something very strange going on here in the Northcotton Farm, that's for sure!'

'${PLAYER}! You've saved the hobbits! I did not believe I could free them myself, but I was able to stealthily speak with each of them before you came to their rescue, and the stories they whispered to me were very familiar! Crystal Bolger, up in her tree, spoke of a delicious smell that drew her to the farm, and Gladiola said something similar. Andy Boffin said the smell began so deliciously, but turned so foul when he started eating that it knocked him out with the power of its stench.
'I held my nose shut with one hand, and though my eyes watered furiously, I investigated the main farmhouse. There's an evil-looking creature back there, ${PLAYER}, and I think it was he who brewed that terrible poison! I think he was using it to lure hobbits into his trap, and Isenbard Bolger is still missing! That creature must still have him captive.
'He muttered to himself almost constantly. It seems that his name is Thadúr, and his poison is called Darkthorn. You've got to stop this evil creature, ${PLAYER}, you and your friends! You've just got to!'

'I get the impression that this Thadúr was an ancient fellow, which means that the mystery of his final words may be ancient as well. It could be that Tirith dan Forduath is an old name for a place that goes now by a new name! In fact, I am almost certain this is the case!
'If so, then you're not very far from solving this mystery, because a hobbit lives nearby who just loves the history and makeup of old words. If anyone knows what \qTirith dan Forduath\q describes, it'll be Ronald Dwale. He is an expert at languages and words.
'Ronald lives north-east of Oatbarton, just outside the village of Dwaling. If you would solve this mystery of words, you should talk to him at once!'

'Yes? You have a philological question for me? Wonderful, wonderful! It is my favourite study of all: the study of words!'
Ronald Dwale listens eagerly as you recount the final threatening words of Thadúr the Ravager.
'Ah, very interesting, yes. Tirith dan Forduath. A bit on the easy side, but it does have a few points of note. \qTirith\q is \qguard\q, and \qdan\q gives us \qagainst.\q So this is a location that guards against something, some threat. But what threat?
'Words, as you have certainly observed by now, sometimes behave differently together than they do apart, and such is the case here. Forduath is a construction composed of two words joined for the purpose of linguistics: in this case \qforn,\q \qnorthern,\q and \qdúath,\q \qshadow.\q You are looking for a place once known as \qGuard against the Northern Shadow,\q and I think I know the place!
'It is not called that anymore, of course, and in my studies I have learned that it was also once called Orod Elon, the \qMountain of the Stars and Stones.\q But now it is called Stoneheight, and it is on the North Downs, north-east of Amon Raith. A road leads north of a deserted farm-house, climbing up to the heights.'
'A friendly face? At last! Oh, my friend, it is terrible! War and death have come to Stoneheight! This place is lost!'
Talk to Ronald Dwale about Thadúr's final words
Talk to Benedric Jacklin in the town of Stoneheight

You catch a glimpse of movement out of the corner of your eye.

'It was terrible, friend! A tall, menacing figure stalked through the streets of town while his cruel allies slew anyone that moved! I do not know what he wanted, but he moved with a single-minded purpose; I think he was looking for something.
'But why would he visit this destruction upon Stoneheight? Ours was just a town of peaceful folk whose other homes had been lost in the fighting with Orcs out of Angmar! We have done nothing wrong! We were just trying to get a fresh start!'
Benedric is on the very edge of tears.
'There may be others who were able to hide from that terrible figure. You have to search Stoneheight to see if anyone survived! But be careful... the allies of that frightful apparition may still be here!'

'Who is it...? Are you... a friend...?'
The man is near death; his wounds seem most severe. He coughs weakly and his face contorts painfully. He gathers the little strength he has left, determined to tell you something.
'I... I think I... did this.... I think I drew the horror... to Stoneheight....'

'We came here...for a new life. I met a merchant...he had a helm, said it had passed through the hands of...many adventurers. Inlaid with gems, it was....
'He offered a fair...a fair price...and I thought I could pry the gems loose.'
Seward coughs again, and his body shakes with the pain of the effort.
'I could not...loose the gems. Woe betide me! I think...I think the helm's true owner...came to claim it! Ivar! Ivar the Blood-hand! He stalked through the town....
'My home...is further in. See if the helm...is still there. But beware the Blood-hand!'

'It feels strange to say that we have been fortunate in such circumstances, ${PLAYER}, but still it is so: for Ivar the Blood-hand has left our town behind. He must have found what he came to find and was content to leave his servants behind. They have now been dealt with!
'But now the real work -- the work of rebuilding -- must begin...if anyone will even want to rebuild this town, that is!'

'I found this tablet on the ground on the way here, ${PLAYER}. It is covered in evil runes, and I cannot read it, but I believe it was dropped by the Gaunt-lord as he passed through Stoneheight. Perhaps if you can uncover its meaning, you will be able to make some sense of this attack.
'You know Elrond of Rivendell? It is rumoured that he is a master of lore, and he might be able to read the markings on this tablet. Perhaps he can tell us what it says.'

'If you are here to explore this Lost Temple, I must warn you, friends! The Gaunt-lord Ferndúr has come to this place, but to what purpose I cannot guess. There is something else, too, something that I cannot explain.'

'These are evil runes, ${PLAYER}. I can read them, though it is not pleasing to do so. The tablet contains directives for Ivar, as you supposed, from the Gaunt-lord named Gortheron. He is instructed to raise an army of wights with which to crush the Free Peoples.
'It is curious, ${PLAYER}, that Ivar's actions in the town of Stoneheight do not seem to have been in line with these orders. Why did the Blood-hand destroy the town as he did, and then leave it? Would not following his orders be more important?
'There is more here: he is told to keep a close eye on Ferndúr, for though he was the Master of Imlad Balchorth for many years, Gortheron has not forgotten what happened to Ferndúr's people in the depths of his temple.
'I do not know what this is in reference to, ${PLAYER}, but I do know where this temple, this Lost Temple, is located, because a scout of Rivendell has observed worrisome activity there of late. Assemble a fellowship of allies and find her at Ost Chall, in the northern reaches of Nan Tornaeth.'
'You have nothing for me?'

'Ferndúr the Virulent would be worrisome enough, ${PLAYER}, but he has hired a mercenary band, and they have been prowling about the grounds of the Lost Temple. It is highly unusual, and I do not know why Ferndúr would deign to work with such Men. It is my understanding that the desires of Men are beneath the notice of such creatures as the Gaunt-lords.
'But this mercenary band is certainly in the employ of the Gaunt-lord. Make your way through the grounds, and you will see it is so; enter the crypts and look for signs of what Ferndúr is planning.'

'I don't have the will to fight you, ${RACE}. Just leave me be. We were given good coin to come to this forsaken place, but once we descended into this crypt, something didn't feel right to me.
'I told them I would go no further. Coward, they called me, and left me here with a knife in my side to keep me company. Some payment! Didn't know Colfrith before yesterday, but me and Rimbald had done lots of jobs before this one. I guess that's what friendship is good for...these days....
'But they'll get theirs! If the screams I heard not long ago are any indication, they already have! Ha ha ha ha!'

'It's all over now; I care not a whit for them! Let 'em suffer, I say. They should have listened to me and saved their own lives; could be they're wanting for the blade they stuck me with, eh? Ha ha ha!'
Scristan's laughter seems to cause him pain, and he wheezes with the effort of it.
'But I don't like being deceived, ${RACE}, and that gaunt fellow's coin wasn't good enough to get me to go further into this place without explanation. I want you to make him pay for tryin' to use us. His coin'd need to be better to get Scristan to throw his life away!
Scristan laughs again, painfully.
'My life's been thrown away, without my consent! That's a good deal cheaper, it seems. Find this gaunt fellow, this Ferndúr, further in and make him remember me.'

'You and your allies have done well to dispatch Ferndúr, ${PLAYER}. He was as cruel to his allies as he was to his enemies, and my investigation of the crypts has confirmed what previously I only suspected. But now the story is clear to me.
'Long ago, the Men of Rhudaur waged battle against the other remnants of the North Kingdom. They worshipped Ferndúr, believing he could grant them the victory...and indeed, the plague he harnessed would be so great a weapon that Arthedain and Cardolan could not hope to stand against its threat.
'He gave to them the plague, the Red Cloud, but they could not control it. The Men of Rhudaur who lived and worshipped at the Lost Temple were laid low by the weapon they sought to wield. It was their undoing, but Ferndúr did not weep for them, though it cost him many servants. He merely laughed as the Red Cloud claimed its victims.
'I am glad you have ended his threat.'

'Do not underestimate this creature. If he is more beast than thinking being now, he is an animal uncaged, and will fight with ferocity.'

'Pirita found this tablet cast aside in a corner of the fortress. She showed it to me, sure of its significance but not its meaning.
'If I read this illustration rightly, it is a map of the southern lands spoken of by our friend Lothrandir; the lands he once lived in and now to which he has returned. See these four lines? They all come from one point and travel across the map in many directions; this one at the northern edge of the map arrives at an island. It must be Sâri-surma. Four lines, four Gaunt-lords.
'If you follow this line southward, to where all the points meet, you will find the one who commanded Drugoth to come to Sâri-surma. The line goes to the land called Enedwaith. In its south-western reaches, among the Lich Bluffs, stands the ruin of a mighty stronghold. It is in this place that the lines meet.'

The flower has a poisonous, deathly look to it....

'I have been told Skorgrím's body was discovered by Thorin's folk back when he inhabited this land, before his death.
'The dwarf-miners dug into the mountain and exposed the ruined cellars of Edhelion, and that is where the corpse lay perfectly preserved -- in the Silver Deep Mine.
'When Talagan brought the library down upon them both, they fell to their grave below. You could search for Skorgrím's body where last it was seen, if you seek it still. For my part, I have no wish to look upon Skorgrím again.''

'That is a vile, little flower, and one I have not seen before. You say it grew where Skorgrím died, and where his body lay in death for all these years? Such magic is not common with dwarves....
'His body has been moved, though we do not know where. It seems that the flowers follow him in death. Perhaps they will lead to his new grave.'

'I heard one of the guards here talking -- down yonder is Gormr, the Steward appointed by Thorin Oakenshield before he left. Gormr is the reason we have come, and the leader of this Dourhand rabble you see all over the place.
'You are the well-spoken one in our party, ${PLAYER}. You might as well go speak with him and find out what he has done here...and why he has grown silent over the years.'

'Is that ${PLAYER}? It has been long indeed since last we met. I remember you: you were the dwarf that discovered Skorgrím's body the day I discovered the relics he sought. The Longbeards of Dwalin's party are not welcome here, but you...you I might allow, for your good deed.

'I'm afraid you have come here for nothing anyway, ${PLAYER}. No one is to gain admittance to Skorgrím's Tomb. It is a sacred ground, and only descendants of Skorgrím -- that is, the Dourhands -- have leave to enter.
'You are more than welcome to pay your respects to our fallen king at his Shrine, which is just east of here, in the Rockbelly Pit. Skorgrím was a great king, after all, and deserves tribute.'

'So you walked in our shrine, did you? As you can see, the Dourhands' reverence of our fallen king is very great. The Longbeards and the Elves do not understand such loyalty, so this was perhaps a good lesson for you.
'But do not go away just yet. I'm sure we can think of more tasks to occupy you while you trespass, eh, ${PLAYER}?'
