'On the bluff above us is a catapult that Angmar brought along on its way to the city. We managed to damage it enough that they left it behind, and now we intend to repair it and use it ourselves.
'It certainly won't reach Annúminas, but that is not our goal. We wish to use it to fling ropes over the colossus. That will allow us to climb and begin repairing the areas we cannot currently reach.
'Search the debris scattered along the banks of the river and see if you can find the following supplies: Several bundles of rope, some pieces of driftwood, a few small flywheels, and a couple of pouches of oil. Once you have found them, bring them to Cudhaer at the catapult on the bluff just to the south of here.'
'Ha! I had heard that someone was coming to help me out, but I did not know you would have everything with you as well. This is a very fortuitous event!'

'There is a small ruin on the west side of the Barandalf called Lithost. It is nothing more than a shell of the walls now, but I feel we should make an effort everywhere we can.
'Crawlers have filled these ruins. This normally would not be a terrible thing, nature is generally kind, however these crawlers are diggers. They burrow holes throughout the ancient bricks and stone. In time they could bring down this very colossus.
'Head to Lithost and search out the crawlers. The ones we are interested in stopping will not be on the surface. Flip over some rocks and defeat whatever you find beneath them.'
'We will still need to get down there at some point to reinforce the walls, but you have provided us some much needed time. Thank you.'

Introduction to Forestry

Foresters collect wood from fallen branches. They are also adept at treating the wood for use; but this is not the end of a Forester's knowledge, for they also cure hides from the beasts found throughout the wild. These learned skills provide woodworkers and tailors with the materials necessary to ply their own crafts. This gathering profession is much-needed and often profitable in Middle-earth.

'Well, look here, another would-be tailor. I am pleased to meet you and looking forward to helping you get started.

'Let me see what you were able to do....'

He rubs his hands over the fabric.

'I hope you did not tear up your cloak. Or did you sell it for some meagre coin? Well...I cannot pass you without seeing your handiwork. Back to the workbench with you!'

'I see the cloak there on your person. May I see it?'
He takes a moment to admire your handiwork.
'This is a well-crafted cloak. Your needlework is even and tempered, and the cloak will drape properly on the back. You are well on your way towards becoming a tailor. Well done, ${PLAYER}.'
'Have you forgotten something? I do not see the rough cloth cloak that you were supposed to deliver to me. You should return with one.'

'Let me see what you have done.'
She examines the cloak closely.
'An excellent piece of handiwork, ${PLAYER}. You did very well in making this cloak.

'Head to the small encampment in Tham Ornen. Our scouts witnessed the angmarim tacking things to the walls there. I believe it to be copies of plans and discovered information. Gather up several of these and bring them back to me.'

Torogethir monitors the pass from the North Downs into Evendim and watches over the fortresses of Fornost and Ost Heryn.

'All of the soldiers who served at Ost Heryn signed documents that swore their allegiance and service to the North Kingdom. To truly honour that, they would have gone to defend Fornost when it was besieged.
'Most of the soldiers at Ost Heryn were cursed due to nothing of their own doing. It is a difficult position to be in as a soldier: do you follow the orders of your commander even when you know they are wrong? Can you blame a soldier for doing so?
'They still carry those Writs of Honour after all of these years. Gather them from the spirits and return them to me. Perhaps I can find a way to consider them honoured and release them from this torment.'
'For being as old as they are, the spirits have kept these writs in amazing shape. I can read every letter of the contract. Now, to see if I can find a way to honour them.'

'I have spent many a day observing the spirits within Ost Heryn. They move as if they are still on patrol, walking the walls and paths, seeking out the Enemy. Many times they found one.
'Tomb-robbers have tried to ransack Ost Heryn, correctly presuming the ruins of the fortress hold valuables. They have not accomplished much, though... they fear the spirits and try to avoid them, for when the spirits find them, they do attack, and the robbers lose more than win.
'The robbers within the ruins present two problems. They are slowly carting off our legacy, and they are not allowing the spirits to be at rest. I wish you to drive the tomb-robbers out... we shall see if that helps to quiet the ruins.'
'Good! With those robbers out of the ruins, we shall see if the spirits calm.'

'When Fornost sent forth the call, Ost Heryn did not answer. She remained dormant, allowing the fortress of the North Downs to fall to the Enemy. That decision rested solely with its commander.
'He has paid dearly for his decision that day. His spirit stands before the doorway into Ost Heryn, ever watchful of all around. He has never been allowed to stop or rest. The more I watch him the more I pity him... punished for eternity for a decision made in a moment ages ago.
'I feel he has paid his due and wish to end his penance. For this to be done, I believe that he must share in the fate that Fornost suffered on that dire day: he must taste the pain of the defeat himself.'
'I sensed the commander leave this place not long ago. I believe he has finally found peace after all these long years. I thank you for delivering it to him.'

'Ost Heryn is an ancient fortress made to watch the pass between the North Downs and Evendim. She was to answer the call of Fornost and support it if the need ever came. The need -- and the call -- did come, but support did not. Ost Heryn abandoned Fornost.
'For that, all who served within were cursed, branded as Oath-breakers, and left to stand their posts until they redeemed themselves. The time for redemption has come, and we are going to deliver it.
'I have devised a couple of plans for doing this. I do not know if any will succeed, but I believe they are all worth trying.'

'It will take a few days for everything at Ost Heryn to settle down. When things of this power and nature are stirred, they do not immediately calm. I will watch the progress and report back if we were succesful.'

'I know Humfrey thinks this is all manageable, but the situation has become dire. That should be clear to anyone.

'Grant me a favour and drive off a few of the beasts. Hopefully, that will reduce their numbers enough to allow the natural fauna to return.'

'Attempting to reduce the salamanders' number did not work. I swear that I have seen more in the past hour than I did the entirety of the day yesterday. I thank you for your efforts, but we must find a different approach to dealing with this problem.
'The salamanders make nests along the shoreline, and in them, they lay their eggs. From these eggs, new salamanders hatch. The salamanders here seem to be especially aggressive breeders.
'Wander the shore, find these eggs, and smash them. Perhaps we can stop the salamanders by ensuring that the next generation fails to spawn.'

'I can still see flecks of shell in your hair. This plan will take a while to resolve, as we have not done anything to the current spawning of salamanders, but hopefully as they are driven out -- with none to replace them -- we can reclaim this island.'

'I might be seeing things -- I have been out here a long time and Humphrey is not exactly the sanest of company -- but I would swear I saw a young salamander riding along the back of a lake-skimmer as it danced over the water.
'If I did see this -- and this can actually happen -- it could be disastrous if somehow the salamanders were carried across to the western shore of the lake, where they could begin to multiply and spread without any natural bounds to stop them.
'Head to the beach and destroy any lake-skimmers you find. We cannot take a chance on this.'

'That boy over there -- Kelsey is his name, I believe -- showed up in camp recently and has been lurking around. I am not sure if he is perhaps scouting us to see what of value he can make off with, but I do not trust him.
'Do me a favour: approach him and converse with him... perhaps you can discover his motives.'

'Kelsey finally got someone to come help us? He's a good boy, but has taken his time finding aid.
'You say Orchalwë knows you are here as well? He has a desire to restore the pact that we once both honoured? The Rangers let their end go long before we did.
'It will take some time for me to determine if I believe he is being truthful.'

'It pains me to admit that the boy is not wrong. My very impression of him proved that just now. He comes asking for our help, something we used to openly give to all, and we watch from the distance and shadows, distrustful and on guard. Today, we shall end that.
'We once had an agreement in place with the people of Ost Forod. They would watch the northern lands and protect the road from Forochel. In return, we would supply them and see they were taken care of. We have both lapsed in our parts of the agreement.
'Tell Kelsey that the Rangers will uphold their portion of the agreement and will help Ost Forod. He may not know what that means, but I suspect he will direct you to see someone who does.'

'I have come to this camp to enlist the aid of the Rangers with the problems that face my people, but these Men seem so distrustful!
'It's almost as if they think Ost Forod is full of tomb-robbers! Certainly times are hard, and some of my people have turned to plunder, but there are far more decent people at my home than the unsavoury sort these Rangers fear.'

'They said that they would help? This is marvelous news to me. But words are not of much value. The winter is coming, and the winds from Forochel are cold this year.
'There is much to do in Ost Forod. There are some rewarding bounties posted, and an adventurer of your skills could well find yourself gainfully employed in no time! Just cross the bridge back to the mainland, then follow the road to the cross-roads. Once you reach it, take the northward road up into Tyrn Fornech, and you'll see Ost Forod in no time!
'One of the arbiters, Basil Gummidge, will be pleased to see you and hear of your news from the Rangers.'

Fortress of the North
Ost Forod was once a stronghold protecting the trade routes and gateway to Forochel. Now it is a shell of its former glory, and there is much blame to go around.
'Kelsey is just over there. Do not worry... I will not take my eyes off of him.'
'I only hope it is not too late for this pact to be restored. With Angmar coming, we cannot afford for it not to be.'
'We have let our part of this bargain slip for too long. Please help us restore it. Make Basil see that I am genuine in my intent.'
'Will no-one here help us? The winter will come soon, and the stores are low.'
'Basil is the arbiter of Ost Forod... he will know what all has to be done around the town to prepare.'

'You have shown the Rangers are serious in restoring the pact between us. It is now time that we step up here and honour our end of the agreement.
'We said we would watch over Evendim from the north, guard the trade routes with Forochel, and ensure the enemies of the Rangers did not enter from those lands. They have entered and are already here, that much we cannot change, but we can drive them back out.
'Speak with my associates around town, the same who you helped prepare for the winter. They have each been tasked with scouting a threat. They will know more about what to do next.'
'The north is secured, and we can honestly say we have now done our part. We are not yet done, though. The years of hardship created another problem, which it is time to finally address.'

'The winters here are colder and harsher than the rest of Evendim. We do not have the lake to warm us, and the winds blow straight through the mountain passes from Forochel. It is difficult to prepare for everything we need.
'Often during the winter, we run hunting parties out to find whatever elk or bear are still foraging about. I worry that this year we will not find any. There are more tomb-robbers camped in the hills than I remember from any year before, and they will all want to eat.
'Head out into the hills west of here and encourage some of these tomb-robbers to move on. They will be bad for this winter, and we simply cannot afford them taking the food sources we will desperately need.'

'They chose the path they wanted to walk, each and every one of them. They took greed and fortune over an honest living. Those of us who remain here, who have suffered but remained just, will now have the food we need.'

'It is time to build up our foodstuffs and prepare for the coming cold. Elk-meat takes time to dry and cure... it is not done overnight, and it must be done before the cold-snap hits. It cannot cure if it is frozen.
'That means it must be gathered now so it has enough time that we will be able to enjoy it later. There are few things that warm a belly more than a spiced, dried piece of elk-meat on a frozen winter night.
'Head into the hills... you will find the elk roaming about them. Bring back enough haunches that we will be able to get a few weeks of meals from them.'
'These are very nice haunches. Looks like the elk had plenty of plants to feed upon this fall.'

'The winter cold will chill you to your core if you are not ready for it. It is especially dangerous at night, when one does not awaken from the bitter cold. Blankets are very important if you wish to wake in the morning.
'We had plenty to go around last year, but it seems the robbers are not just pilfering tombs these days. A store-house was emptied just last week, and we are now short of blankets.
'Bear-hide is the ideal material for making new ones. It is thick and with brushing will be made soft. Plus, there are plenty of bears just south-east of here, at a place we call Nan Orngon.'
'These are perfect. Nice and large with only small nicks and tears. I can make enough blankets to keep us all warm for the entire winter with these.'

'Blankets are not the only things that keep you warm in the winter. A good, roaring fire is just as important to have. To keep it going, you need wood, though... lots of it and plenty dry.
'Our stores are low this winter. With folks leaving to join the tomb-robbers, we have fewer honest people left to do the work necessary to get ready for the winter. We have had to focus everyone on food. The fire-wood pile has stayed very short.
'The best wood is out near Nan Orngon. The bears root it up while they are digging for grubs. It is dry, but burns for a long time. If you could gather up a bunch of branches, it would be very helpful.'
'We will still need to gather more wood in order to make it through the winter, but it is nice to see the wood-pile grow for the first time in a long time.'

'We have now both honoured our sides of the pact, after ignoring it so long. It feels good to have that relationship restored. I hope that in the future we can build and make it grow and flourish.
'I am prepared to take a large step towards that. I know where the tomb-robbers make their primary camp. It is a small island at the north end of the lake called Rantost. Many of the relics they have pilfered are kept there until they can find buyers for them. I imagine the history they are keeping there is immense and invaluable to the Rangers.
'Months ago, I sent three of my men to join the tomb-robbers. They are now on the isle of Rantost, still working for me. I am now willing to use them and have them expose themselves and challenge Rantost for the Rangers. Seek them out, and they will tell you what to do next.'
'I'm doing nothing suspicious, just standing around waiting for the next boat. Wait, what's your name? Who sent you? Basil, you say? Then it is time we got to work.'
Talk to Eliot Bencroft at Rantost
Spies and Robbers
The isle of Rantost is where the tomb-robbers have made their central camp. A great deal of history is being kept there.
'If Evendim is to be restored to glory, the tomb-robbers must be stopped.'

Rantost is north-west of Ost Forod.
Basil sent you to meet with several spies he has among the tomb-robber camp on the isle of Rantost.

'The tomb-robbers are far more organized than we have previously thought, and Rantost is the hive of their villainy. Everything they plunder from the tombs and crypts of Evendim comes through here.
'We have been watching for a while, and each of us comes up with a way to hinder their efforts. If we can curtail them enough, we may allow the Rangers an opportunity to strike. This would let them end the tomb-robbers, recover their relics, and strengthen the restored friendship between Ost Forod and Tinnudir.
'Speak with my associates here for what we feel needs to be done. The list is not long, but it should make a heavy impact.'
'Chaos reigns within the camp. It seems the time is ripe to launch the true offensive.'

'The tomb-robbers store all of the relics they bring here. They sort them and, depending on their value, place the more valuable items in crates and the less valuable items in barrels.
'The crates are kept deeper within the camp, in more guarded locations. The barrels are strewn about here and there. They are still valuable, but the crates are the most valuable.
'I have not been able to get a count of how many crates and barrels there are around the island. The Rangers will need to know how many there are so they can prepare accordingly. Please get their number for me.'
'Good! This will tell the Rangers how many men to bring and how much they will be carrying back.'

'The robbers use a group of rowboats to transport the relics to this island. The only other ships they have beyond that are small dinghies, not strong enough to carry the relics from the island.
'If we can strike there, Rantost will be further isolated, and the relics will remain on the island until we want them to move.
'The rowboats are mostly along a small channel that runs through the centre of the island. There may be one or two on the far side, however. Burn them all.'

'Welcome to Oatbarton, traveller. We are home to some of the northernmost farms in the Shire. That means our crops have a distinctly sharper taste and our pipeweed lingers on the tongue.
'The main producer up here is the Northcotton Farm, just up to the west of town. They are getting ready for their harvest and annual market. I am sure there is plenty to do.
'Head on over to the farm and speak with Albin Northcotton and see what you can do to help him out.'
'Are you here to help? There is so much to do in order to get ready for the market.'
Talk to Albin Northcotton
Northcotton Farm
The Northcotton Farm is nearing harvest season and preparing for their annual farmer's market.
'The Northcotton Farm is just up the hill to the west.'

Albin Northcotton is at the Northcotton Farm, west of Oatbarton.
Northcotton Farm is getting ready for their annual harvest market and could use an extra set of hands.

'We are terribly behind this year. Almost nothing has been done, and I do not know how we possibly can get it all done. The harvest has not been the greatest so we have been spending all of our time trying to get what did grow to stay alive.
'In order to have a proper farmer's market, there are many things we must still have. We have to have pies and premiere pipe-weed. We need to clean the place up and get the animals ready for petting. We also told Nibs he could participate this year, and I hear he's had some trouble as of late.
'If you could help us get all of this ready, we would greatly be in your debt. This may be the last year we can have this market, and I'm going to do whatever I can to make sure it's the best!'
'I cannot believe it is all done and ready. I was sure we would have to cancel... but not only are we ready to go, you've gotten us ready early!'

'You have helped us greatly, and for that I am very thankful. I have one last thing to ask of you.
'The market will be opening tomorrow. I was hoping you would head up the road to Dwaling and let the hobbits there know that, thanks to some outstanding help, we are starting the market a little early this year.
'Just follow the road east from Oatbarton, and soon enough you will come to Dwaling. Find Hob Hillbrow and let him know.'

'I am supposed to make several pies for the market, but I haven't had the time to gather up all the ingredients that I need to begin baking.
'The first step is to make the crust. For that, we will need a few things, but the first is flour. To make that, we will need to gather some wheat, then bring it to the windmill for grinding.
'Wheat can be found in the fields here at the Northcotton Farm. Edulf Tunnelly is at the windmill to the west.'
'You're back just in time. I just finished up grinding the wheat. Looks like you've got plenty of flour for those pies.'

'You want to have this wheat here ground into flour? I can certainly do that for you. It's going to take some time, though, and I can't guarantee you'll get all of it back.
'We've been having trouble with rats getting into the windmill and eating the wheat and flour. We always seem to end up short no matter how much we put in.
'If you could scare off a bunch of the little rodents, I can make sure you get all the flour you need.'
'This flour is perfect. Soft and fluffy, not lumpy. Very nice job. Now, on to the filling.'

'I have started working the flour to make a crust for the pie, but I don't have anything to fill it with. Can you imagine an air pie? Wouldn't be very filling, I imagine.
'I use grape jam to fill my pies. There are some vineyards here on the farm where you can pick fresh grapes, which will then need to be crushed. To crush them you will want to place them in the tubs at the vineyard, then <rgb=#FF0000>dance</rgb> upon them. I know it sounds like madness, but it makes the texture perfect and feels so fun between your toes. After they are crushed, bring them to Theobald Longfurrow. He will add some syrups and sugars to make the perfect jam.
'The vineyard is north from here. Start by picking the grapes. You can't have jam without grapes!'

'You crushed these pretty well... almost too well. You still want a few chunks here and there to give the jam -- and thus the pie -- a good consistency.
'Let's see... a little bit of sugar... some syrup... stir that up... some rhubarb... seal the lid... and there you go! Jam fit for a pie.'
'This jam is delicious. Usually we would let it sit and thicken for a few days before using it, but we don't have time for that this year. Now, I believe that eggs are next on the list.'

Collected flax fibres at last! (8/8)

'This is getting absurd. Tanathron over there, that weaver -- yes, the one glaring my way -- simply will not give me fibres for the linen I need for the special boots.
'My supplies are running low, and he is a key supplier, but he refuses to help me! It is because his own supply of flax is running low, and he hoards his ingredients so that his stock never depletes.
'I am afraid I've gone and made him angry with my demands. Perhaps you can reason with him; please try, ${PLAYER}.'

'What? So I like having a balanced supply of ingredient and product. What of it? If I have no ingredients, tomorrow I shall have no product. I do not think it is unreasonable for me to demand ingredients if I am going to generously give of my finite supply.
'If you want your own ingredients for your own endeavours, you will have to collect ingredients for me first. Flax plants grow along the road to Celondim. You'll be able to see the pale blue flowers amongst the grasses.'

'Good. Now we can proceed with our arrangement. At least someone around here can be reasonable, AHEM!
'Here are some flax fibres.'

'Splendid, ${PLAYER}! Your patience and politeness did wonders here, I see.
'Tanathron is a stubborn fool who has no business being in this trade, but it is what it is, and I should learn to make do.
'Unfortunately, I have a sad feeling that I will go through the same thing all over again tomorrow, when my supplies run low again.'
Speak with Tanathron
Collect flax plants (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring the flax plants to Tanathron and collect the fibres

'I am ashamed to be admitting this, but I'm out of twine, ${PLAYER}. I, Master Boot-maker of the Garden Shrew Stomping event....
'It is true. Hard to believe, I know. Could...could you please fetch me some more? I usually get mine in Celondim, where the Elves who tend the docks craft a fine strong thread.
'You are a good sort of ${RACE}, ${PLAYER}. Truly.'
'Twine! Marvellous. I was beginning to wonder if you lost your way. Well, this should do for a short while, at least. My thanks, ${PLAYER}. You are more useful than you seem at first glance!'

'I'm nearly out of the cherry wood I use for the most important part of the boots...the sole! The sole is fortified with this gentle, moderately dense, strong wood.
'It is the perfect -- yes, perfect -- wood for knocking out a pesky, oversized shrew without really hurting it. Elves do not like to hurt creatures, you see. Well, I suppose shrews tempt us to use violence more than most animals of the wild, but we have come up with a fair compromise.
'Cherry branches grow around clusters of trees in the pastures along the road to Duillond. I am sure there will be plenty of branches on the ground to replenish today's supply.'
'These are just the branches I need! Many thanks, ${PLAYER}. This will ensure that the shrews are given just the right amount of dissuasion against their terrible behaviour.'

'Elves would never harm shrews. Never. We wouldn't even consider such a gruesome ideas. Shrews are good, fine creatures.'

'This shrew business is positively ruining the Festival for me. I almost didn't come this year. I really didn't.
'This is such a violent game, and it offends me terribly! Stomping on shrews is so far beneath the dignity of the Free Peoples that I refuse to participate, but I have come up with something better to do. I would like to propose that we actually do something useful for the festival to try to salvage this catastrophe.
'I saw some lovely flowers growing in the fields outside of Duillond. You should collect them, and plant them in here. That is a proper Festival activity for you.'

'That's much better, ${PLAYER}. You and I understand what it truly means to visit a Festival. There should be something lovely and beautiful to feast our eyes upon. No unconscious shrews or chewed-up gardens. I'm glad we found something proper to do.'

'This event is a disaster! If the shrew infestation wasn't enough to ruin our spring celebration, we now have a shortage of boots!
'They're not just any boots, you see. They're specially made by the boot-maker here in Duillond. He uses great care and technique to make a very special boot that is just menacing enough to strongly discourage the shrews from remaining here.
'Can you please go find out what is holding up his next shipment? I worry that I will be out of Shrew-stomping boots by the end of today.'

'So we are back on schedule, then? That is good, ${PLAYER}. I was growing very anxious. I hope the Boot-maker did not give you too much trouble.

'We cannot have this. We just cannot. Do you see how dark it is here? The market lasts well into the night, even after second supper sometimes. If people cannot see where they are going, someone could get hurt!

'So the paths are all lit? Good, now those wandering after dessert have nothing to fear!'

'The oath with Ost Forod has been resworn, and we stand stronger today because of that. It is a great burden off of my shoulders to have those wrongs now stand righted.
'Now we turn our attention to the western shore and to a friend we have had far longer than Ost Forod. A friend who stands at the end of his time and weeps for the state of the land.
'Use the boat and venture across to the Eavespires. Speak with Longbough once you arrive. Let him know the Rangers will do whatever they can to soothe his pains.'
'You say a Ranger sent you? He is wise to know the lake and forest are in pain.'

The Eavespires is a small camp on the north-western shore of Lake Evendim.
'While we can restore the ruins, the lake and forest will not heal without Longbough.'
Defeated Gauredain at the Even-rills (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'So, Longbough has sensed that the Even-rills are threatened? He has never been wrong, so even though I have not seen what he feels, I trust this threat to be real.
'The enemy is likely the Gauredain, Men from the North, the cold wastes of Forochel. They dabble in dark alchemy and evil magic, things that turn nature into abominations.
'Clear out the camp they have at the Even-rills. If even a few remain, then more will come.'
'So, as you defeated the Gauredain, they began to scatter and flee? Good! They will think twice before returning to that place.'
Defeat Gauredain at the Even-rills (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

Wolf-men from the North
The Even-rills are a series of pools and waterfalls that meltwater from Forochel runs through before entering the lake of Evendim.
'The Even-rills supply all the water this lake holds. If they are made foul, the entire lake will become fouled as well.'

The Even-rills are north-east of the Eavespires.
Lithuifin asked you to head to the Even-rills and defeat the Gauredain there.

'We do not know how long the Gauredain have been encamped within the pools of the Even-rills. They might have already done great damage to the lake. We must know what they are doing there.
'The Gauredain believe in nature and its abilities and powers, though they do not understand whence these powers derive. While we use the virtues instilled therein by the Valar for good and healing, they use it for more nefarious purposes. They should have gathered up several pouches of herbs and plants they are using within the pools.
'Find and bring me these pouches. I may be able to determine what exactly they are poisoning the lake with, and if need be, may be able to concoct a cure.'
'It will take me some time to study these, and if fortune is with us, we will not need to use what I learn.'

'It used to be a rare sight to see Longbough weep. In the many years I have been here with him, it happened once, maybe twice, per year... usually when a sapling he knew got snapped in a storm.
'Over these past few months, it has happened more frequently. The pain Evendim is feeling is slowly killing him. While these tears are created from pain and evil, they are a great force for life and good.
'Take this vial... it contains a few tears which I gathered last week. Pour them into the pool at the top of the Even-rills. The waters will be purified and restored.'
'The water glowed lightly, then felt cool against your legs? I believe that means it worked and whatever damage may have been done by the Gauredain should fade from the lake.'
Pour the Ent-tears into the pool

'Above the lake... hoom... where the water pools and flows, then thunders over rocks and stones, I see Men, hoom, hom, dressed as wolves splashing in the waters.
'They carry foul bags, filled with poison and death, hom, and they spread it upon the waters. The Even-rills cry waterfalls into the lake. Perhaps you will help, hoom, my Elf-friends?'
'My roots taste fresh water once more, hoom, for the first in a long time. The Even-rills are purified.'

'The men from the north, who dress like wolves, are not like the Rangers from the east. They worship the land, but then use it to create evil and darkness. They are a foul breed of Man, one I do not trust.
'They have begun coming further south, even to the edges of this grove. This causes me great worry.'

'Hoom-hom... the men dressed in wolf-skins are of no concern anymore, so says the silky-haired ones. I believe them, hoom. The trees of the mountain they are atop no longer call to me... they have returned to slumber.
'The trees to the south, though, hom, scream out in agony. They call for help. Big men, giant men, nearly as tall as Longbough, hoom, rip the trees from the ground. I can feel their agony.'

'The trees there now live and move, but not as Ents or Huorns, they have been twisted into Wood-trolls, dangerous abominations of nature.

'I came here this year to enjoy the greenery and get away from the noise of my home. I wanted to get lost in the quiet and the smells of spring. Instead, I come on the day when the tweens from the Shire arrive.
'You wouldn't believe the mayhem inside the Maze! Please, can you make them go away? Make them be quiet! They're running around harrying and annoying everything on two legs!'

The young hobbit stops to listen to your stern reprimand, giving you a defiant look.
'I wasn't being that loud!'
'Thank you, ${PLAYER}! I cannot fathom how such little folk can make such an enormous racket. Hopefully they will be a little quieter now.'

Terrible Tweens

Young hobbits in their tween years have made a trip up to the Hedge Maze, and there hasn't been a moment's peace ever since.

'My ears are still ringing with their shouts. Please, ${PLAYER}, make them stop!'

This hobbit-gardener uses a cat to hunt down shrews....

The Gaffer, a sensible gardener, has methods not unlike the Elves of Duillond

'Well, I never thought I'd see the day when we hobbits would have these graceful old Elves beat, but it seems this is just such a day! This will make a grand story at the Ivy Bush.
'As you can imagine, we have many farms and gardens in the Shire, and naturally we have shrews to pester us as well. But I guarantee you that even the simplest hobbit has more wisdom in dealing with shrews than all these Elves combined!
'Don't believe me? Go talk to the farmers around Hobbiton and Michel Delving! See what happens when shrews dare to pester them! Then you can come back and tell these poor, hapless Elves what you've learned.'

'Hello there! Shrews? Yes, we've been known to see a shrew or two. I'll tell you the secret to getting rid of them...talk VERY LOUDLY about winter being just around the corner.
'Shrews hibernate in winter, you see. Just talk about how cold it's getting, and how it's supposed to snow tomorrow. You'll see. They'll be running for their warm, cozy burrows in no time!'

'If you're wanting advice on gardening, you've come to the right hobbit. Shrews are nasty critters, determined to ruin my work. There are two ways to deal with them. Either trap them, or chuck an apple at them! Aim for the head if you decide to chuck an apple. I suppose stomping on them would work too, if you're quick.'

'He said what? Why, that little....
'Nay, don't listen to me. There is no reason for me to take offence. Perhaps our little dirty-footed, cheeky, gap-toothed guest is correct. Perhaps we Elves have something to learn from these hobbits.
'They must be truly gifted farmers to have grown so fat. Yes -- do go to the Shire. Learn what you can from the dumplings -- I mean, halflings -- on how to best get rid of shrews.'

Maengamiel listens keenly as you tell the tale of your journey in the Shire.
'That sounded like a productive venture, ${PLAYER}. Sleeping cats, lies about the season...but at least one hobbit resorts to similar methods to those we use here. I believe an apple hurled at the unruly beasts would give me a great sense of satisfaction.
'Know-it-all hobbits don't seem to know so much after all.'
'You want to know how we keep shrews away from our fields? It's very simple! My cat here, Waldy, is the finest shrew-hunter in all the Shire. Watch what he can do!'

'I have an especially difficult challenge for you. There is a strong, dire beer in the Hedge Maze, and one swallow will find you bereft of your senses. You will wake far from where you began, and have no memory whatsoever of how you got there. All exploits along the way will have been forgotten.
'If you can navigate the maze while drinking those dire beers as you go, I will be tremendously impressed.'
'Well done, ${PLAYER}! I didn't think you had it in you to manage that task! Most folks give up after the first few drinks, dizzy and confused. I admire your persistence!'

'There is much work to do here in order to reclaim the city -- more than we may be able to do -- but we shall still try. At the least, we may preserve some of what is here.
'Orchalwë has come with us to Annúminas. There is much anger within him. I do not trust his judgement to let him go out into the city on his own. I fear he may place himself into a situation he cannot survive.
'I ask you to accompany him. There is much he will want to do, and I believe his goals to be true. Make sure his means of achieving them do not allow him to fall to the darkness.
'Orchalwë will find you when you use this smoke signal. Work with him to reclaim our city.'
'We have worked very hard to clear these ruins, and I am quite pleased with our work. There is still much to do, but I feel we will accomplish our goal.'

'I do not know if we will ever have the force to retake the city. We may have to simply wait for Angmar to find whatever they want and leave on their own. Hopefully, we can prevent too much damage to the city until that day comes. I thank you for all of your help.'

'Unlike the estates in the hills which you cleared for us earlier, Annúminas holds a special place for me. This is where my ancestors lived their lives.
'They shopped in the markets on these streets, worked in these buildings, fished from this harbour. They danced in the halls of Ost Elendil, swam in the waters of Glinghant, mourned in chambers of Haudh Valandil.
'Now, everything they stood for, what they strived their entire lives to build, the good they brought into this world and nurtured, I fear is now nothing more than the flicker of a dying flame.
'I for one will no longer stand by and watch as Angmar destroys all that I love. It is time that I draw my sword and join this battle.'
'Though it is tempered slightly, my wrath is not yet sated.'

'The lord of this pack of mongrels is called Mangle-maw. He is as terrible as they come, but you will not be able to get close to him without the rest of the pack tearing you apart...unless you can challenge him, that is.
'Wargs always choose their pack-leaders in battle and usually have some place where they issue challenges to each other until enough of them have been ripped apart that the rest are too frightened to fight the one on top.
'No ranking Warg can refuse a challenge, so if you step in there, they will fight by tradition...beat enough of them, and Mangle-maw will no doubt face you.'

'I don't suppose that Wargs would ever accept you as their pack-leader, but you have thrown the pack into chaos by killing Mangle-maw.

'The evil matron of this particular Warg-pack has unleashed yet another litter of the filthy beasts upon the world. She may not look like much, but when I was sneaking about earlier, I saw her pups strip the flesh off of an entire ox in a just a few minutes... which gives me an idea.
'That evil spice you made... there is a bit left, yes? A light sprinkle of that into the pups' next meal ought to keep them subdued while you deal with their mother!'

'Well, that should take care of the matron then. I am afraid her pups are probably too tough to expire to a single dose of that spice, but I don't think I could bring myself to kill off a bunch a pups anyway, even if they are Wargs.

Displayed Ranger-flags from the monuments of Angmar (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Annúminas is our city. The ruins and buildings were built by my forebears, and they are monuments to our history, memories of the glory of the past.
'The Angmarim not only dare to occupy what is ours, they defile it with foul monuments to their false king. It is a slap in the face of every Dúnadan that those stones stand within our city.
'We cannot hope to tear the monuments down...they are too large and we are too few. In the time it would take us to destroy them, they would have us surrounded with more warriors than we could possibly defeat. No, the answer is subtler.
'We will take the monuments and claim them for ourselves. There are six spread throughout the city. Once we find them, I will protect you while you fly a flag of the Rangers from it. We will turn their monument into ours.'
'While their monuments may still stand, they now spread our message and stand as symbols for the Rangers of Evendim. They may come, but we shall stay.'

'Before the city became a battleground, I used to come to this place to sit and watch the water. I would spend hours letting my mind wander as I gazed over the small, rippling waves.
'I have not felt peace and contentment like that in a long time. It is something I dearly miss, and I hope that one day I can sit and enjoy that feeling again.
'Let us take a small moment to rest and forget these terrible times we live in. <rgb=#FF0000>Look</rgb> to the horizon with me and let us wish for happier times.'
'Did you see it too? The small light on the horizon amid the darkness of the clouds? There is hope yet for us all. We will withstand this storm.'

'Take some time and read the names that are left before they join their fallen companions, lost in time.'
'One day, we will rebuild this temple, and those who have fallen to preserve it will be etched into the new pillars.'

'In the days of old, women and children would come here on clear nights. The stars reflect off the waters below and look as if you could reach out and grab them. The mothers would give their children coins to make a wish and throw to the waters, sending their hopes and dreams out among the stars.

'I can see several coins that are still in these waters, never having made it...wishes that never had a chance to be fulfilled. Gather those coins up for me, and I shall see that they make it to the lake.'

'I will make sure these are brought to Tinnudir where they can be sorted and protected.'

'This bridge leads to the island of Tyl Annûn, the home of our most valued crypt and the former palace. The torches along the bridge burn blue in memory of the fallen kings.
'It was custom to sprinkle incense into the flames as you crossed the bridge. The scent would waft into the palace and honour the leaders.
'I encourage you to partake in this practice.'
'I smelled the incense, and I am sure they did as well. My ancestors and kings have been respected and honoured.'

'The Angmarim often assault us down this path from the east. They dash from stone to stone, staying protected from our arrows until they are close. It makes defeating them a dangerous task.
'Let us clear some of this rubble out of the way to make that a more difficult proposition for them. I will take it once it is gathered up. I am sure we can put it to some use.'
'I am sure we can put this to good use fortifying a position or stabilizing a building.'

'The Angmarim are savage men whose cruelty knows no bounds. The corpses in these cages are of Rangers who attempted to bargain with Angmar to preserve whatever of Annúminas they could.
'In response, the Angmarim hung them in these cages until they died, and now they leave their corpses there for the birds and animals to devour.
'Let us get them out of there and allow them to rest peacefully. Even if you tried to make a deal with the Enemy, you do not deserve this for eternity.'
'Now they can spend the rest of time in peace.'
Remove the corpses from the cages (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

Redeeming the Defiled
The Rangers here tried to bargain and make deals with Angmar.
The corpses should be removed from the crow's cages to allow the fallen to rest peacefully.
Orchalwë will be pleased to see his dishonoured brethren will now rest peacefully.

'Much good work has been done this day within these ruins, and from what I hear, that is only the latest you have done to aid our cause. Evendim and Annúminas hold no special meaning to me -- my line is drawn from the lands to the south -- but I know what it means to those whose forebears called this place home.
'Orchalwë is one such Ranger. He has gone through much these past few months: helplessness, despair, doubt, anguish, anger, rage. I did not think he would come through to the other side and still be standing within the light... that is, until you came here. History, ruins, relics, memories of the past are all important and valuable things, but I would trade every one of them in a moment to see the hope in Man restored. That is something you have done, and I will forever be grateful.
'Orchalwë has returned to Tinnudir to the north. I ask that you venture to the small island once more and speak with him before your path takes you beyond the shores of Evendim.'

'If you had asked me but a month ago where we would stand today, I would say here on this spot, but not in this place. I would have told you that we would be besieged, trapped within the tower on this island. Tomb-robbers would be plundering everything in sight, and Angmar would stand firm, ruling over Annúminas. We would be a withering shell waiting for the final blow.
'But I look over the waters today, and that is not the morning I awoke to. Our estates and ruins lie in peace and undisturbed, and while the city still echoes with battles, I believe we shall carry the day. Even if we never rebuild what has been physically destroyed here, we have already regained what was lost. We have had pride in our heritage. We have stood and fought like our forebears did. We have earned the privilege to be called Rangers. In that, we have reclaimed Evendim and Annúminas. From the ashes of the ruins, through our deeds and acts, the Kingdom of the North has begun to rise again.
'You will forever be in my thoughts, ${PLAYER}. There is much to do yet, but I believe now that we can accomplish our goals. I wish you the best on your journeys.'
Orchalwë has returned to Tinnudir and wishes to speak with you.
'You have done much for us all, and for that, the shores of Evendim will always be a home for you.'

Orchalwë is at Tinnudir, north of Annúminas.
You have been instructed to speak with Orchalwë.

'We are on schedule once again? Well done, ${PLAYER}...I don't know what we would do without you.
'Come back often! Our demand for boots is high indeed, and supplies always dwindle.'

'I take your delivery as a sign that more boots are in demand than ever. Alas.'

'I am glad to finally get some aid. We have been trying to do all that we can down here, but with every move we make, our enemies are already there waiting for us. I have discovered why, but we just have not had the numbers to do anything about it. Not long after you freed Rantost, several boats landed on the shore here. I watched a meeting between the newly-arrived tomb-robbers and the forces of Angmar. Afterwards, the robbers headed up into the hills, and the Angmarim resumed their search.
'I can only fathom that an accord was struck. The tomb-robbers would spy for Angmar and report on our movements from above. In return, Angmar would give the robbers any relics from the city that they did not want.
'If we are to move forward into the Way of Kings, the ancient burial ground of our ancestors' rulers, our actions must be shrouded to the Enemy. For that to happen, we must empty the hills and claim them for ourselves.'
'The hills have been cleared, and we are prepared to venture into the Way of Kings more boldly.'

'I have been watching the robbers as they have moved about the hills above us. They seem to focus on two primary ruins, Tham Sarch and Tham Laegamon. I know from my days as a child playing in those hills of a third ruin: Arthobel.
'The tower that stands there would make for a very strategic position. You could clearly see over the Way of Kings below you, watch the waters of the Baranduin to the south-east, and on a clear day, see Tinnudir.
'Last I remember, the heavy doors to that place were sealed tight, and none had been within in many years. I ask you to venture to the south-west, up into the hills, to the entrance and <rgb=#FF0000>look</rgb> around to see if you notice any recent activity there.'
'So they have not yet found a way in either? That plays to our advantage.'

'Some people go through life never changing, always repeating the same mistakes and errors time and time again. It seems the tomb-robbers here in Evendim are no different.
'After Rantost, the few that remained and fled had a choice to make: a defining moment in their lives. They could have returned to Ost Forod and started to live honourable lives again. Most sailed south instead.
'They have come here, made bargains with an enemy they cannot fathom, and have returned to their old ways. While they use Tham Sarch to signal the Angmarim below, they are also stripping it bare. They have had their chances and moments and defied them all. They have been judged, and it is time they accept their sentence.'
'So it is done? Good. It may seem as if I am overly harsh, but if you continue to reject good time and time again, can you be anything but evil?'

'Now that Orvar has destroyed the hidden relic Gorothúl left in Buzun-ghâr, that cave should be free of danger. We need not fear that Grawulun or others of his kind will return to that place.
'But Gorothúl may have left other relics of evil throughout Moria; indeed, I think it likely, and recent reports from our scouts indicate one such location: the Mirror-halls of Lumul-nar. Merrevail have corrupted the mirrors of Lumul-nar that once fed light from the outside into the deep reaches of Khazad-dûm; the light no longer shines. A number of explorers ventured to Lumul-nar to investigate. Few returned, reporting that the merrevail of that place have been given great courage; their defiance is strong. What else have they been given, I wonder? A relic of Gorothúl's?
'The entrance to Lumul-nar is on the side of Zirakzigil, amid the snow. Find the relic inside, if it exists, and destroy it. Bring one or two allies with you, ${PLAYER}!'

'I knew it, ${PLAYER}! I knew you would find Gorothúl's relic in Lumul-nar. It is good you destroyed it. The merrevail we should be able to keep in check; if the relic had drawn Grawulun or another Caerog to Lumul-nar, our success might not be as sure.'

'Tham Sarch has not been a site of much importance before this week. Earlier in the week, the tomb-robbers occupied it and began looting it. While the looting angers me, they are presenting a larger issue which we must deal with.
'Whenever we move, I see glints of light from the hillside. We know the Angmarim and the tomb-robbers have an accord, so they must be signalling them as to our actions.
'This is something we cannot allow to continue. We must hinder their ability to signal each other about our every move. Head to Tham Sarch and collect the mirrors the tomb-robbers there are using to alert the Angmarim.'
'These are exactly what I expected. They may look small to you, but catch the glint of the sun just right, and you can signal someone from a great distance.'

'Up on the hill above us, if you travel to the west, you will find the ruins of Tham Laegamon. This was the rulers' retreat during the days of the North Kingdom. They would go there, stare down upon their city, the lake, and their ancestors and ponder the future.
'Now, a foul presence occupies the ruins, and while they look down upon all the same things, their purpose is dark and evil. Tomb-robbers have come to fill those ruins. They are ransacking more from it each and every day.
'The robbers must be stopped. There are not many more beyond these few here in the hills. If we draw the final line here, I believe Evendim may have a future free of them.'
'There are a few more within the Way of Kings itself, but hopefully we shall soon be rid of the tomb-robbers entirely.'

'These have longbows with which they fire burning arrows at us. That allows them to track us in the night and eliminates stealth as a tactic for us, thus it has caused us many difficulties.
'I would like you to take the longbows from them. If we cannot freely move throughout the Way of Kings, we cannot proceed... and we must proceed.'
'Now we can burn these and give the Enemy a fire to watch for a night.'

'You have done much for us, and it feels unfair to ask for more, but I must. The tomb-robbers we drove from Rantost fled to the south and are now threatening our hold within the Way of Kings. The Way of Kings is where the ancient rulers of my people are buried. Those that watched over Annúminas and Evendim from on high now sleep below. Their memories are to be cherished and thought of often, but their tombs are not to be disturbed.
'I have also heard rumours and whispers of another force amongst the ruins. I believe you have encountered them already within the estates to the east of here. I fear we have little time to determine their motives and defeat them before it will be too late.
'Head south to the Way of Kings and meet up with Nimbellas at his camp and see what you can do to help.'
'There is much work to be done, and if we are to succeed, it must be done quickly.'

'Greetings again to you, ${PLAYER}! I did not have the opportunity to properly thank you for helping to broker this alliance between the Iron Garrison and the Elves of Lothlórien. So I thank you! In Mazog, we have a prisoner worthy of exchanging for those Gorothúl brought to Dol Guldur: my son chief among them. O Bori! Be strong and courageous during your torment!
'Scouts report seeing a relic of unquestionable evil among the Water-wheels of Nalâ-dûm, but were unable to route the flow of the canals in such a way as to reach it. You must determine the proper workings of the system if you are to find and destroy this relic of Gorothúl's.
'I shall have a scout lead you to the entrance of Nalâ-dûm in the Water-works. Delving into the flooded deeps will be dangerous, for the mechanisms are very old and have not been used for many years.'

'Very well-done, ${PLAYER}. The destruction of that relic should keep further evils from being drawn to the Water-wheels.
'Now we must look to the future.'

'The path between here and the great city was once one of grandeur and unrivalled beauty. Tombs, crypts, and monuments to those who had ruled the North Kingdom lined the road. You were flooded with a sense of honour, justice, wisdom, and valour.
'It pains me to look out and see what has become of them. Some destroyed, some empty, robbed of everything but the stones themselves, some swallowed up by the lake. It is not the end that men of that stature deserve.
'We have not yet taken an accounting of the state of each of the tombs. While you are venturing within the Way of Kings, could you stop by each of them and let me know how time has treated them?'
'So, four are being used, one lies destroyed, one is dormant, and Elendil has retained its majesty. We will have to do something about the four that are open... and quickly I fear.'

'With the threats thinned, the crypts scouted, and these keys in hand, we are ready to venture into the tombs within the Way of Kings.
'We will focus on the four you discovered to be opened: Haudh Eärendur, Haudh Valandur, Haudh Arantar, and Haudh Eldacar.
'We have each spent some time researching these crypts and reviewing our notes from what we have seen while posted here. There is much to do.'
'You have done much to help us preserve these tombs and crypts, ${PLAYER}. If the rulers below still lived, I know they would honour and praise you.'

'The tomb-robbers have found the place where they will make their final stand. Within the tomb of Haudh Eärendur, they now scramble to take whatever they can. Once they have enough, they will leave Evendim never to return.
'Once you enter, they will have nowhere to go, and we can end this once and for all... on our terms. None shall go unpunished for the acts they have committed against our ancestors.
'Head to Haudh Eärendur and defeat whatever tomb-robbers you find within. End this today, ${PLAYER}.'
'That is one threat we shall never have to worry about again.'

'Alas, the tale of the North Kingdom is one of tragedy. Eärendur son of Elendur was the last King of Arnor, before his sons splintered the North Kingdom into the realms of Arthedain, Cardolan, and Rhudaur. Unfortunately, much lore of those final days was lost with him.
'He rests still in his tomb, Haudh Eärendur, and with him, we believe, some fragments of the knowledge of the last days of Arnor. Would you perhaps venture into the tomb and take rubbings of any engravings you might find there?
'Be wary, for I do not doubt that enemies, beasts, or the elements have invaded that tomb, as they have so many others here.'
'Thank you, ${PLAYER}. These rubbings will help us piece together an important part of our history.'
Collect rubbings within Haudh Eärendur (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'When we came here, we thought the only trouble that we would have in these tombs would be a few robbers and then making sure the walls did not come down upon us.
'No-one foresaw the kergrim, whatever they are. All I know is that they are vicious carrion feeders that will sooner kill you than look at you.
'A group of them have taken to living within Haudh Valandur. That is a problem I need you to rectify.'
'So it is safe to venture within then?'

'Valandur was one of the kings who ruled over Annúminas during its glory years. He was a wise and just man, and he was known to his people by his sceptre.
'As he judged a case or complaint, he would carefully ponder the words that were being said. To maintain order, only those holding his sceptre were allowed to speak. When he had made a decision, the sceptre would shine with a white light.
'We had thought this sceptre lost to history, but recently I have seen a kergrim stalking around Haudh Valandur holding it. I believe he makes his nest within the tomb. We must have Valandur's sceptre returned to us!'
'This sceptre is amazing! It is difficult to believe that after all these years it is still intact.'
Collect the sceptre from the kergrim within Haudh Valandur

'We know little about the reign of Arantar. I have been in his tomb before... a modest place indeed. He was clearly of some importance and must have done something of worth, but that knowledge has been lost to us.
'However, like all the Kings of the North, he wielded a ring gifted to him by the Blue Lady. Legend has it that some virtue resides within the ring, though of no power as significant as the Rings of Power. Nevertheless, it is the prize for which the Angmarim search, I am certain of it.
'Head to Haudh Arantar and drive the Angmarim out. Let them know that they have a formidable foe to deal with, and the tomb-robbers will protect them no longer.'
'They will soon learn to fear our approach, thanks to you.'

'Upon taking the throne, each of the rulers of Annúminas was given a ring by the Blue Lady. This signified their right to rule and also identified them to others from outside the kingdom.
'It has long been rumoured that these rings also had some form of extra power. Not like the Rings of Power themselves, mind you, but something else.
'I believe Arantar's ring may still be in his tomb, and that is what Angmar is desperately searching for. See if you can find it first.'
'Yes, this indeed is Arantar's ring. I will see it gets sent to Tinnudir immediately.'

'Unlike Haudh Arantar, where the Angmarim are just ransacking and destroying the crypt, the searching at Haudh Eldacar seems to be much more methodical. Very little has been removed thus far.
'Whatever they are looking for there must be of great importance to their purpose here in Annúminas.
'We must delay them while we discover what their goal is. If you were to drive out the party currently searching within, it would buy us valuable time.'
'I do not yet know their ultimate purpose, but I know that we have set it back, if only ever so slightly.'

'We still do not have a grasp onto why Angmar has come here... and why now? There must be a reason that eludes us.
'One step we can take to try to figure it out is to see if we can get our hands on the orders one of their leaders carries. I have seen one of them near the entrance to Haudh Eldacar. I believe he is leading the searching there.
'Find him within and recover the orders from him, then bring them back here, and maybe we can begin to unravel this mystery.'
'I cannot understand much of this but I can make out a name... Amarthiel. Does that mean anything to you?'

'I have just received word that our encampment in Annúminas is under heavy and near constant assault. Echad Garthadir is our one foothold in the city itself, and we cannot afford to lose it.
'I believe that we can handle what is left to do here within the tombs. Please, journey to Echad Garthadir and join the fight there!'
'Welcome to the centre of the conflict, ${PLAYER}. If tomb-robbers or Gauredain gave you trouble in the past, I would advise you leave now. The battles here are for true warriors.'
Talk to Adadhrond at Echad Garthadir
Eye of the Storm
Echad Garthadir, the Rangers' encampment within Annúminas, is under constant assault.
'I do not know the horrors you will find once you get to Echad Garthadir, so steel yourself for anything!'

Echad Garthadir lies some distance from the Way of Kings, within Annúminas.
The Rangers have sent you to lend aid to Echad Garthadir.

'The hobbits in Oatbarton have a market every year at the Northcotton Farm. By now, word has usually spread to us of the event, and many will change their trip to Evendim to be sure to catch it.
'We have not yet heard anything from the Small Folk, and I am beginning to worry something is the matter or may have happened.
'Oatbarton is to the West of here on the southern border with the Shire. Once you get there, speak with the Bounder in charge of the town.'
'Well, I would certainly hope the market is still going to happen. I'm nearly out of pipe-weed!'
Talk to Nod Gardener in Oatbarton
Going to the Market
Every year the hobbits of Northcotton Farm, in Oatbarton, have a farmer's market.
'I believe you might find the Farmer's Market in Oatbarton an interesting diversion.'
Oatbarton is in the Shire, on the southern border with Evendim.

'We oft keep in touch with the Elves of the Rivendell. One called Barachen I consider a close friend. A letter I received from him not long ago indicated that trouble was afoot within the Trollshaws, and he was seeking my advice. I worry for him.
'He has a small camp far to the east of here, in the Trollshaws, just beyond the Last Bridge from the Lone-lands. Would you go to him and learn what troubles him?'
'So, the Rangers of Evendim have sent you to help?'

Orchalwë has asked you to speak with his friend Barachen.
'We have just gotten word from Rivendell that Master Elrond wishes to speak with you. I know not what about, but I have found it is best not to keep powerful Elf-lords waiting.'
'It is good you have come. We are in dark times, and there is much to do. I have heard of your deeds in Evendim and believe you can help bring a light to these lands as well.'

'You should go at once to Rivendell and speak with Master Elrond.'
You have been called to Rivendell, in the Trollshaws, for there is much to do there.

'When I stayed in Esteldín, I made friends with a group of Earth-kin that lived not far from the refuge. They were holding out valiantly against the oppression of Angmar. Seeing what we have gone through here, I think of them and wonder if they are well.

'Angmar pushes against us hard. There is much help we could use.'

'You have done a great deal for us here in Galtrev, ${PLAYER}. I am sure you will be back, for our city is great. Yet if you wish to continue your travels through Dunland, you should head south to the Starkmoor.
'I am sure there are folk in need of aid there, as well. Perhaps they too feel the oppression of Isengard. Saruman has stretched his White Hand perilously far into our lands.
'A fellow named Andras just led his caravan in that direction...perhaps you can overtake him on the road, and he can show you around.'

'A thief on the road! Help! Help! Oh, why will no one help me?
'You...you are not here to steal my wares? Ah! Perhaps you can help me, then. As you see, I am in a bit of trouble.'
Find Andras in the Starkmoor
To the Starkmoor
The Starkmoor is a land to the south of Pren Gwydh.

The Starkmoor is to the south-west of Pren Gwydh.
You should search for Andras, the leader of a caravan, on the road from Pren Gwydh to the Starkmoor.

'${PLAYER}, my friend, you have the look of one who is growing ready to leave. I want to thank you for all that you have done for us during one of the Stag-clan's most trying times.
'Galtrev is the largest village in Dunland, and it is not far to the south-east of here in Pren Gwydh. I doubt you will encounter any folk of the Caru-lûth if you venture there, but surely you will want to stop there as you make your way through Dunland.
'I will miss you, ${PLAYER}! You are always welcome in Lhan Tarren.'

'What do you want here, Stranger? Why should the White Hand grant you admittance?
'I'm not sure I like the way you're looking at me, ${RACE}.'
Gain admittance to the village of Galtrev in Pren Gwydh
From Trum Dreng to Galtrev
Galtrev, the largest village of Dunland, is in Pren Gwydh to the south-east of Trum Dreng.
'You will find Galtrev if you take the road south-east. Make sure you come back to visit, if you can! You will be missed by all here, ${PLAYER}.'

Galtrev, the main village of Pren Gwydh, can be found by taking the road south-east from Lhan Tarren in Trum Dreng.
You should go to Galtrev as you make your way through Dunland.

'The force gathering in Wulf's Cleft is no feint. The clans are gathering in force and mean more than to push us from Dunland... they intend to march upon Rohan and likely Edoras itself!
'You must take this news to the outpost captain here at this camp immediately.'

'Greetings, ${PLAYER}. From what I have heard recently it seems that matters with the Dunlendings may be coming to a head soon. What have you seen out there?
'It is worse than I feared then. My scouts told me that a considerable force was gathering in Wulf's Cleft, but by your count it sounds like a full ten-thousand men or more have gathered beneath the banners of the clans... and they are nearly ready to march?
'I will tell you now, we have not the men or horses here to hold the Ford against half that many. Grimbold must be told, and soon, or we shall find ourselves swept back across the Isen.'
Talk to the Rohirrim-captain in the Heathfells
The Forward Bastion
The Rohirrim commanders need to know that a great number of Dunlending troops are massing in Wulf's Cleft, just west of Isendale and are nearly ready to march on the Ford of Isen!
'Take word to the camp-commander at once!'

The Rohirrim-captain is at the encampment in the Heathfells.
You should relay the tidings regarding the Dunlendings at Wulf's Cleft to the captain of the Rohirrim outpost.
Defeated denizens of Ost Dunhoth (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Do you think you are ready for a true challenge adventurer? Gortheron the Doom-caller, most powerful and leader of the Gaunt-lords, has come to Enedwaith. He stands now in his fortress, Ost Dunhoth, and plots to claim all of Middle-earth for his Dark Lord.
'I do not know if he can be stopped, but we must do what we can to slow him. I ask that you venture to Ost Dunhoth and slay as many of its denizens as you may. Gortheron is a threat we cannot ignore.'
'It may only be a small victory, and short-lived, as no doubt those forces will be replaced, but we can rest easy today knowing it was a victory.'
Defeat denizens of Ost Dunhoth (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Return to the Rangers of Thrór's Coomb
Denizens of Ost Dunhoth
Ost Dunhoth is the fortress of Gortheron the Doom-caller.
'If we are to survive these dark times, we must strike where we can.'

Ost Dunhoth is in southern Enedwaith.
You have been asked to venture to Ost Dunhoth and defeat many of its denizens.
The Rangers in Thrór's Coomb will be pleased to hear you have culled some of Gortheron's forces.

'Ah, good... you look to be the adventurous sort! I have a problem that I was hoping you might assist me with. It seems that some of the patrons have been complaining of terrible wailing noises coming from the walls and floor in the cellar. I'm sure it's nothing, but business hasn't been great lately what with the rumours that the inn is haunted!
'Now, I'm too busy to waste my time on hogwash like that myself, but perhaps you might be interested in taking a look? If naught else, you could confirm that it's a rumour and nothing more....
'I should warn you, though, the customers don't normally start complaining about the noises until about midnight, so you'll probably have to hang around here until then. I'll even throw in as much ale as you can drink to help you pass the time!'
'Excellent! You'll help? Fine, fine... ah, right, the free ale? Once I start to pour it, time will just pass away and before you know it, it will be midnight! Just sit back and enjoy....'
Talk to Anlaf about the free ale
Inn of the Forsaken: Stroke of Midnight

Patrons of The Forsaken Inn have been complaining about terrible wailing noises coming from the floors and walls of the cellar. The proprietor of the inn has requested that you wait around until midnight when the complaints of the noises usually begin.
You will need to be full of ale if you are to pass the time.
The book-shelf slides open to reveal a staircase descending into darkness
A suspicious-looking man stands before you
You have discovered the burial chamber of Captain Rabghul
You have freed Umín of the necklace's power

'It... was controlling me... my thoughts, my actions. I could see its purpose. It wants nothing less than the destruction of us all.
'Quickly! You must leave this place before it comes back. It is not through with us yet! Just leave me here... I was the one who desired the necklace above all, and I shall be the one to destroy it!
'You have no time to lose! Cross to the other side of the ship and leave through that cave there!'
Investigate the source of the wailing noises
Explore the depths below The Forsaken Inn
Talk to the suspicious man
Continue to explore the caverns

You find yourself inside The Forsaken Inn at midnight. The innkeeper has asked that you investigate the source of the wailing noises coming from the cellar.
Patrons have already begun complaining of the noises in the cellar. Explore the area and see if you can uncover the source of the noises.
The book-shelf was hiding a secret passage leading down into the earth below the Inn. You should explore this cavern and see if you can locate who or what is making those noises.
You have found a suspicious-looking man reading a book and staring at the glowing, rune-marked door in front of him. Who is this man, and why is he down here? You had best ask him.
Umín, the man you met in these caverns, has agreed to assist you in your exploration of this place. You must use his expertise to make your way deeper into the caverns.
You have discovered what appears to be a burial chamber. Perhaps Umín could shed some light on this place.
Umín has been crushed by the cave-in. You must press on without him. You are on your own now, so be always on guard.

It is Umín. Alive and well, it seems... too well even. It appears that he has gained an almost supernatural strength in his absence. He wears a red, glowing necklace around his neck. He is also a bit angry with you... you will have to defeat him if you want to survive.

The spinning blade-trap has knocked the necklace from Umín's neck, and it lies glowing on the floor. Umín himself lies crumpled on the floor. Why did he attack you?
Speak with him and allow him to explain....

'Is it truly over? I am sorry for all the pain I have caused. I was blinded by the necklace before I even set eyes upon it.... It consumed my thoughts and my life. 'Just leave me here with my thoughts....'

Defeated elk at Tham Nambarth (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Tore down ivy at Tham Nambarth (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

Tham Nambarth is the nearest of the ruined estates and our first priority. While the threats to it are not great, they must not be trivialized in their importance, for Tham Nambarth is being reclaimed by nature itself.
Tham Nambarth was once a great hall... you can see that in what still stands today. This will not be the case for long, though, and not because of looters or goblins. It is the ivy! It grows deep into the cracks in the walls and slowly pushes the bricks apart until nothing is left standing.
It is also threatened by a source that itself is not threatening: a herd of elk has settled within its walls. They are not a problem of themselves; however, soon they will bring predators: wolves, hungry robbers, Wargs, and goblins from the northern hills.
Defeat elk at Tham Nambarth (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Tear down ivy at Tham Nambarth (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Tham Nambarth
Tham Nambarth is the most well-kept of the estates that lie in ruin within the Twilight Fields.

Tham Nambarth is in the Twilight Fields, east of Tinnudir.
Orchalwë's journal details several things that are currently assailing the ruins of Tham Nambarth.
Defeated tomb-robbers at Tham Varan (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'The next estate within the fields is Tham Varan. It is a place we know little about. The records we have found only describe its name. It is an enigma indeed.
'The only thing I know is that the tomb-robbers have been swarming over it as of late. Given our focus elsewhere, it has been ripe for the picking, and they have slowly stripped out any valuable information we could find to glean its identity.
'It is not enough that we battle nature and time as enemies to our history, we have to deal with greedy robbers who want to deny us our past and identity. It cannot be tolerated.'
Defeat tomb-robbers at Tham Varan (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Tham Varan
Tham Varan, the south-easterly estate, is shrouded in mystery. Its identity has been lost to time, and the robbers there carry off more clues every day.

Tham Varan is east of Tinnudir and Tham Nambarth.
Orchalwë's journal speaks next of Tham Varan, a ruin of unknown ownership besieged by tomb-robbers.
You feel that Tham Nambarth is under control. The next page in the journal speaks of Tham Varan
You feel that Tham Varan is under control. The next page in the journal speaks of Tham Ornen
You feel that you have done all you can at Tham Ornen. The next page in the journal speaks of Tham Andalath
The goblins have fled, terrified of whatever may roam in the darkness. You have reached the end of the journal. You should return to Orchalwë

'The land to the east of here is called the Fields of Twilight. Within it are the ruins of several ancient estates. These places were once home to powerful families within the kingdom. They grew grain and raised animals used to feed the city and provided work for many of the people.
'Now, they are disgraced by robbers, overtaken by nature, desecrated by goblins, and one now even serves as a camp for a force from Angmar. It is an affront to all who draw their heritage from the shores of this lake.
'I have detailed in this journal notes about the estates and the threats availing them. Please, take it and read from it as you explore the Fields of Twilight. It will guide you if you choose to help us reclaim these ancient ruins.'

'Are you here to join in the treasure hunt? It seems that with each passing day, more newcomers come through seeking to learn the secrets of our trade. You'll need to hurry if you wish to join the others. Head across the path to the Treasure-hunters' Camp, and you will find Halthor Goldeneye, he will instruct you further.
'Oh, and one more thing: Halthor can be a bit...gruff at first meeting. Don't let it discourage you! He will soften once you have proven yourself.'

'More green hunters! Every year, you lot get sloppier than the last. I've half a mind to call off the treasure hunt altogether! But today, you're a lucky ${RACE}...we're short of able-bodied hunters, and Aldúlf has convinced me that we should give you a chance.
'Now that the formalities are through, welcome! I am Halthor Goldeneye, hunt-master and senior cave-claw trainer of the Treasure-hunters' Camp. You'll be wanting to get out and start hunting I suppose. You might want to have a look around the camp first and speak with some of the seasoned hunters before setting pick to earth, though.
'Go and search for Tór Wayseeker...he is a master at digging.

'Here to learn about the fine art of unearthing treasure, are you? There's not much to it; 'all in the wrist' as they say.
'Take this treasure-pick and give it a go. Bring me back whatever you discover, and we'll see if you've got what it takes.'
<rgb=#FF0000>You must have a Treasure-hunter's Pick in your inventory to excavate a dig-site.</rgb>

'Excellent! You'll make a fine treasure-hunter; you've already mastered the hardest part!
'I've been told to send you over to Orn Gemfinder, the dowsing instructor. Superstitious nonsense if you ask me. I much prefer my arm and eyes to a bit of crystal, though Halthor Goldeneye believes strongly in it.'

'One of the new hunters! Young Wayseeker sent you to learn about dowsing, I suppose? The lesson shouldn't take long...dowsing is easy to learn, though quite difficult to master.
'Do you see this crystal? Simply take it by the chain and hold it steady. Focus on the area you wish to dowse and, well, you'll just have to see for yourself!
'You can borrow my crystal and practice on the three dig-sites in front of me.'

Using a dowsing gem without a dig-site selected will still consume the gem.</rgb>
<rgb=#FF0000>Use the Neophyte Dowsing Gem in your inventory to complete this objective.</rgb>

'Very good! You'll make a fine dowser!

'You...yes, you there! You're ${PLAYER}, are you not? Hurry along, I've been expecting you.
'I've been instructed to teach you in the care and handling of cave-claws. We've found and trained a very docile breed of the beast. They rarely, if ever, cause trouble....

'You turn a blind eye to a corner of this region for just a moment and something momentous happens that you missed. Somehow, with all of our focus on the tomb-raiders and brigands in the south, a scouting force from Angmar has slipped into one of the ruins.
'This is a disaster for us on several fronts. Something here is of enough value for Angmar to send a force to find it, something that we do not yet know of ourselves. If they were to find this thing, it could turn the tides of war, not to mention what could happen if they find the refuge of Tinnudir. If they use that knowledge to somehow find Esteldín...I cannot entertain those thoughts.
'We must drive them out, and we must sow confusion among those who remain. Their plans have been tacked to the walls of the ruins. If their numbers were thinned and their plans destroyed, perhaps we will stand a greater chance.'
