'Tham Andalath was the ancient home of a great smith, one who made the weapons for the line of kings themselves. While most of his work has been lost to history, his influence is seen in every blade we wield. Goblins now camp within the walls of the ruins... foul and wicked creatures.
'They are more clever than I often give them credit for and very devious. However, if done correctly, one can trick them into believing something much larger is going on around them and frighten them into a panic. Night and day, the flames of Tham Andalath are constantly burning... the goblins never let them go out. They must fear the darkness and believe something out there will get them if the fires are not lit.
'If we were to be both the quencher of those flames and the object of terror in the darkness, the goblins will flee from the ruins with great haste. Once they are gone, another part of our history falls back within our hands.'

'Ah, my friends. I have a personal favour to ask. Two nights ago, a small band of riders joined us from the fields of Rohan, and glad I was of the additional men and horses...but alas, just this morning, I learned that one of the riders was a passing acquaintance of mine, and a much-beloved kinsman to Théodred, my prince.
'Dunstan is his name, and it seems he came here hoping to prove himself in battle...yet he wears too few years upon him and does not understand the peril of our position here.
'I need someone to retrieve him from the front where he and his men rode, and quickly, for I think there is little time left before the Dunlendings make a move against us...then it will be too late.'

'Fishing is disgusting! I had no idea my dinner would be so vile before my mother turns it into a meal.
'My brother usually catches fish for us, but I gave him some sass about it and now he claims he won't until I know what it's like to catch my own dinner.
'I'm told I must dig up worms before I can start, but I would rather starve than go anywhere near a slimy worm! I will pay a handsome reward if you're so good as to help me.'

'So you dug up the worms? Good. Now what do I have to do?'
You explain that the next step in fishing is generally to place the bait on the fishing line's hook.
'WHAT? That's disgusting! I won't do it, I won't! YOU do it.'

'How horrid! That poor worm is still wriggling! What am I supposed to do with that?'
You explain that the fishing line must be cast into the water so that fish will be tempted to nibble at the bait.
'You want me to DROWN it now? That's cruel! I simply won't do it! Catch those fish yourself, if you please.'

'Five fish! Marvellous! How slimy they are...but no matter! My brother will be impressed, and that is all that is important right now.
'Where do you think you're going now? You don't expect me to bring these all the way to my brother in Hobbiton, do you? Please deliver these at once, before they spoil, thank-you-very-much.'

'Thank you for helping me catch my dinner, ${PLAYER}! Now I just need you to -- what's that? You don't want to help me anymore?
'Hmph. Well, I suppose you've done enough for today....'

'That sister of mine certainly does take her time to catch fish for dinner. But still -- I am impressed! She caught five fish for dinner? To be honest, I didn't think she had it in her. She is not so useless after all! I bet YOU couldn't catch five fish on one day. It runs in the family, you know.'

'Hail, Duvodiad. Will you stay a moment? We have need of a strong warrior like yourself in our little band.
'We can find work for you and reward as well, for there is much to be done, and even more to be gained....'

'Ah! You must be ${PLAYER}! Come, come. Make yourself at home. I like the look of you, ${PLAYER}! A good, strong, sturdy ${RACE} -- that is what I like in a warrior.
'You have done us a great service by rescuing our headstrong little huntress. Elain is a brash girl... but we would be helpless without her!'

'Hold, Duvodiad. Let me have a look at you.
'Ah, you are the kind ${CLASS} of whom Elain spoke! We have been expecting you. You have our gratitude and our hospitality.
'We do not make a habit of welcoming outsiders into our midst, but exceptions are to be made for a hero. Come... there are many who wish to thank you, and most of all the Elder. He can be found within.'

'I knew you would come, ${PLAYER}! I hope Cadelh did not give you any trouble on the bridge -- my people are suspicious of duvodiad, but I told them about how you rescued me from the outcasts.
'The Elder wishes to speak with you, my friend. He means to give you a proper welcome.'

'You are willing to join us, then? Good, consider it done. You are one of our small clan now. We are not so different; we all want the same things: wealth, power. Run with us, and you shall have both! Of this, we have been assured.'
You should speak with the look-out in the northern pass of Trum Dreng.

Lhan Tarren, the village of Elain of the Stag-clan, lies to the south of where you found her.
You have been urged to seek the hospitality of the humble Caru-lûth clansmen while you pass through Trum Dreng.

Elain made it safely back to her village, Lhan Tarren.
You should speak with Elain briefly before presenting yourself to the Elder of the Stag-clan in Trum Dreng.

The Elder of Lhan Tarren is inside the bounds of the village.
You should speak with the Elder, for he wishes to thank you for your kindness to Elain.
There looks to be no honour in what the Dunlendings want you to do
The Stag-clanswoman is free... prepare yourself for the wrath of the outcasts

'There are not many of us, but we are enough to stir up some trouble when we wish to! You will find that we value those who are strong and war-like, duvodiad or no.
'Come, I will bring you to the others.'

'You do not look so evil, Duvodiad. Please... if there is any good in you, free me! My village depends upon me; I am their chief huntress and protector.
'My weapons were taken from me, but I will help you fight. I beg you!'

'Thank you, friend. I am Elain... and you have the gratitude of myself and my village.
'Should you wish it, you may have refuge in Lhan Tarren for as long as you like. We do not normally invite strangers into our midst, but I will tell the Elder what you have done for us.'
'Let us leave here.'

The entrance to the court of the Wild Hunstman has been opened and is waiting for you to explore within.

'Tonight is the Feast of the Running Stag, our clan's annual festival. It is an important ritual, and you must join us and share our fare. Tonight, you are of the Caru-lûth, the Stag-clan!
'Now, be off with you! I must prepare, and I cannot remember where I left the three ritual pieces... curse this old head of mine!
'The crown, the spear, the hair... where did I leave them...?'

'Oh! You are a kind one, ${PLAYER}. I am ready to replace the rest of the Stag-clan with just you, if truth be told. Ha!
'Do not pay me any mind. They are a useless, little clan, but they are no less dear to me for that.
'Thank you for helping an old man gather his wits. Now I may begin to prepare for tonight.'

Find the second piece of the ritual set

The Stag-clan of Trum Dreng
You have passed into Dunland and now find yourself welcomed into the homes of the simple folk of Lhan Tarren, a small village inhabited by the Caru-lûth, the Stag-clan.
'It was not always so difficult for me to remember where I left things. My poor, old head!'

The items for the ritual feast can be found somewhere in Lhan Tarren.
You should help Elder Riagán find the items that he has lost, for they will be needed tonight at the feast, and it seems as though his old mind has forgotten their whereabouts.

Elder Riagán can be found in Lhan Tarren, musing over the whereabouts of the items you found.
You should bring the pieces of the ritual set to Elder Riagán for tonight's feast.
Collected meat for the Feast of the Running Stag (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Welcome to Lhan Tarren! The Elder has sent word that you will be joining us for the feast tonight. Many hungry people will be there, along with Stag-clansmen from other parts of Trum Dreng.
'It is my duty to prepare the meat, but since our clan's huntress was taken captive, the men have been hard-pressed to find food. Our tribe is not what it once was....
'But do not worry yourself; you look to be a sturdy ${RACE}. Will you participate in the hunt, ${PLAYER}? We wish to feast on boar and oxen tonight.'

'Oh! So much? This is more than enough, ${PLAYER}. And it did not take you an expedition of many days to bring it back.
'The Elder says that you are to be treated as family while you pass through our village, but we have need of a stout provider like yourself....'
Hunt game beasts of Trum Dreng (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring the game-meat to Hav
Meat for a Hungry Clan
While the clan's chief huntress was missing, the meat for the Feast of the Running Stag was perilously neglected. A productive hunt would rectify this situation.

'If you are to hunt the boar and oxen of the plains, you can find them roaming throughout Trum Dreng, not far from our village.
'Very few people in our village are able to hunt these days....'

Boar and oxen roam the rough plains around Trum Dreng.
You have been asked to hunt the beasts of Trum Dreng for the Feast of the Running Stag that takes place tonight.

Hav can be found in Lhan Tarren, the Stag-clan's village in Trum Dreng.
You should bring the meat you collected to Hav at once so that she can begin roasting it for the feast.
Collected kindling for the bonfire (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Picked scented herbs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Honoured traveller! I am so glad that you brought Elain back to us in time for the feast. Many feared that she was dead. If only she would take a husband, she would not get into so much trouble! But she is a headstrong girl.
'I wish to build this bonfire to represent the depths of my gratitude that she has come back to us safe and whole. It should be towering, burn hot as the summer, and smell of fair flowers.
'I will need more kindling and scented herbs to fuel it as it burns, if it is to be so great. Will you help me collect these things?'
'Ah, these will do just fine. Take heed tonight of the bonfire...it will fill the air with lovely scents and will burn as hot and bright as the stars in summer.'
Collect kindling for the bonfire (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Pick scented herbs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring the kindling and scented herbs to Ivor
Building the Fire
The Feast of the Running Stag is in need of a significant bonfire, so you have been asked to collect a fuel mixture of kindling and scented herbs.

'The fuels I need are simple. They can be found in the plains around our village. You could collect them in half a day if you wished.
'The fire must burn as bright as the spirit of Elain and as that of her saviour!'

Kindling and scented herbs can be collected on the stark and rough plains around Lhan Tarren.
You should collect herbs and kindling for a magnificent bonfire to be lit at the festival.

Ivor awaits you in Lhan Tarren, the Stag-clan's village of Dunland.
You should bring the kindling and scented herbs you gathered to Ivor, who wishes to use them to fuel an especially magnificent bonfire.

'Have you been enjoying your stay thus far, dear ${PLAYER}? There are not many hours left until the Feast of the Running Stag, and I want to make certain that everyone is ready precisely at sundown. The ritual is an important part of our heritage.
'My good clansmen are not always the most observant when it comes to these things. Indeed, the blood of the Stag-clan grows thin, and only Elain and Guto show promise of growing into true Stags.
'My feet are sore and my words are tired, but I do what I can to nurture my folk, so that they will be able to carry on when I am gone. I wish that they could be more like you! Please, will you go and remind them all to be present at sundown?'

The Elder listens with a sad smile as you recount your conversations to him.
'Aye, they are generally a soft lot. But that is no matter... I am glad they are coming. Most of them, at least. Thank the Gwirod for Elain; she is a jewel among coals!
'My grandson is a good boy, but like a bull in both body and mind. I pray he will learn to think of living as oft as he thinks of war. When I die, he will lead this clan in my stead....
'Yes... I hope there is still time for him to learn.'

'I will promise no such thing, Duvodiad. My grandfather believes in the preservation of our culture, but I believe in the preservation of our lives.
'If you failed to notice, one of our clanswomen was attacked not many days ago. Someone must remember these things, rather than remember a history lived long, long ago.
'I am grateful to you, but I make no promises. Now, stop troubling me and go humour my grandfather somewhere else.'

'Aye, I know. The Elder sent someone to remind us all yesterday, and the day before that as well. We will all attend, as we do every year, but I do not see the point in continuing on with this ritual.
'We go to humour the Elder; that is all.'

'Is it really that time again? It is a tedious way to spend a night, but at least we can enjoy a feast.
'I do not see the point of carrying on this old tradition. No one cares but the Elder.'

'Bah! The Elder's eyes are not good, nor is his memory. He will surely not notice if I am not present at the Feast of the Running Stag. It is an old tedious rite, anyhow.
'But I see that you are here to nag me in his place, which means that you will tell him. Very well, I will go! But there is no sense in it.
'I will surely sleep while the rites are performed; wake me when it is time to eat!'

'Do not worry, ${PLAYER}, I will attend! I intend to learn more of the rites of the Stag-clan. I fear that the Elder shall soon need assistance when he performs the Feast of the Running Stag. Someone will need to be his eyes when he is blind.
'Will you be there, my friend? I have been hoping to share the meal with you, after what you did for me.'
Remind villagers to attend the Feast of the Running Stag (${CURRENT}/${MAX})

Counting the Antlers
The Elder has asked you to remind the gentle folk of Lhan Tarren that the festival is to begin at sundown.
'You will find the clansmen about Lhan Tarren. You will not have to search far.'

The people of Lhan Tarren can be found throughout the village.
You should speak with the members of the Stag-clan to remind them to be present at the Feast of the Running Stag. Their presence will ease the Elder's worry that his clan has grown soft and weak.

The Elder awaits you in the village of Lhan Tarren.
You should return to the Elder and tell him that you spoke gentle reminders to many of the villagers.

'And now the members of the Stag-clan who live beyond Lhan Tarren must receive their summons as well. Once a year, a crow from our village flies down to remind the solitary folk that it is time to join their brethren for an evening.
'The crebain can be found in the village. Will you be so good as to set them off in the direction of the farms? The birds know what to do from there.'

'The birds are off, then? Good! Very good. I think the Feast of the Running Stag will be a memorable one, thanks to the help that you have lent us. We have not had an able-bodied warrior like yourself with us in a long time, save dear Elain and my stubborn grandson Guto.
'Now, you may spend the rest of your time as you please until the Feast of the Stag begins. I have no more need of you, but there is always work to be found in Lhan Tarren, and never enough hands found to do it.'

'You are a useful sort of ${RACE}, ${PLAYER}! The crebain are here in the village -- you will not have to look far. I think you will find the birds very obedient to your wishes.'

The crows can be found throughout the village of Lhan Tarren.

'It seems this barren land is twice accursed. Not only have we the Dunlending barbarians ready to fall upon us, but the most recent messenger from the Ford claims that he was ambushed and pursued by Orcs as he travelled through the vale east of here.
'I do not know where they come from, but we have problems enough without those foul curs pouring down from the mountains upon us. See if you can hunt a few of them and discover where they are coming from.'

'So, the Orcs are indeed coming down out of the mountains... and in significant numbers.
'These had best be wandering bands of raiders and nothing more... if they are allied with the Dunlendings, our hold on Dol Baran is as good as lost.'

Orcs in the Heathfells?
Small bands of Orcs have been spotted wandering in the foothills in the northern Heathfells. The Rohirrim are not sure where they hail from, but they are a threat that must be dealt with.
'Hunt the Orcs in the Heathfells, ${PLAYER}.'

Orcs can be found throughout the northern part of the Heathfells.
Captain Cadfrith has asked you to defeat the bands of Orcs that have crept into the northern Heathfells and discover where they are coming from.

You have found the Orc-cave

This blade was taken from a fallen Orc in the Heathfells. While forged in the usual crude and utilitarian manner of the Orcs, it appears to be almost brand new.
Somewhere nearby must be a cave or encampment where these particular Orcs are forging weapons. If you can find it, you should be able to tell the Rohirrim of its presence so that they can take action against them.

'As if you aren't a sight for sore eyes. I have seen naught but Orcs for days now. A band of them struck my father's caravan a few days north of here. We were minding our own business, and this rabble fell upon us without warning.
'Well, we fought them off, of course, but my father died in the battle. The rest of our caravan returned south to Zigil-jâbal, but I swore an oath of vengeance against them.
'I don't suppose you could lend me some aid here?'
Find the Orc-cave in the north-east Heathfells
Talk to Ondor the Dwarf at the Orc-cave
From Whence They Came

While fighting Orcs in the Heathfells, you found a sword one of them dropped. While it bore the usual crude hallmarks of Orc-crafting, it was very nearly brand new, suggesting that Orcs must have a lair nearby where they are forging these weapons.

Orcs can be found in the northern Heathfells.
Cadfrith has asked you to defeat bands of Orcs that have crept into the northern Heathfells in hope that you can discover from whence they came.

Ondor the Dwarf is at the Orc-cave in the north-east Heathfells.
You should speak with the dwarf Ondor.

'Hey there, my good ${RACE}, I don't suppose you would be up for a quick bit of sport?
'This cave is packed full of Orcs, and I see no reason to leave it as is... it is better to seal the lot of them in the dark below!
'I have found a weak point in the rock here that should bring it down, but it will take a few minutes and make a whole lot of noise, so I could use a hand holding the Orcs off until I can bring it down.'

'There we go, and a job well done, if I do say so myself. Ondor is my name, by the way. I followed a raiding party for three days until they disappeared in here... after they smashed my family's caravan and killed my father, of course.
'The rest of the family is headed back south to find refuge in Zigil-jâbal -- but I swore to hunt down the ones that did for my father. Of course, I cannot tell one Orc from another, so now I am left trying to deal with the whole lot of them.
'It looks like it could take a while... well, no sense staying here. There is too much to do. Perhaps I will see you about, if we are both lucky!'
Help Ondor collapse the cave
Talk to Ondor
Imminent Collapse

You have come upon a cave entrance in the northern Heathfells, on the border of Isengard, where you have encountered a rather unusual dwarf. Seemingly without heed to his own safety, he seems to have set about collapsing the cave entrance, which he claims leads to a warren of Orcs below.
'These rocks are not going to knock themselves over. Let's get on with it!'
'When I start swinging this pick, the Orcs are likely to come running, so let me know when you are ready....'
Help Ondor the Dwarf collapse the entrance to the Orc-cave.

Ondor has collapsed the cave-entrance

'Well, I suppose that's the last of the Orcs. It will take them weeks to dig out that mess... lazy curs.
'If it were dwarves trapped in there, they would be out in a day!'
'It has been a pleasure working with you, ${PLAYER}.'
'All right, here we go. Keep an eye on that cave, and if any Orcs come running... well, you know what to do.'

You have come upon a cave-entrance in the northern Heathfells, on the border of Nan Curunir, where you have encountered a rather unusual dwarf. Without heed to his own safety, he has set about collapsing the cave-entrance, which he claims leads to a warren of Orcs below.
Defend Ondor as he works to collapse the cave-entrance.

You should speak with Ondor the Dwarf once more.

'We do not get many travellers down this road. Is there something that I can help you with? What could you possibly want down this way? The Avanc-lûth do not take kindly to duvodiad.
'There is a small band of us here, but we ask for naught, nor do we need anything from you. If you insist, you may speak with Alun. He is leading a scouting party nearby.'

'Bethan sent you here, did she? Interesting. I am not certain that she was wise to do so, but we have naught we can hide here. The land is open as far as you can see, and there is not anything to see. Why would you even want to come here?
'Perhaps you can prove that you would be a valuable ally to the Avanc-lûth. Food and supplies are scarce here, as you can see. Maybe you can help us gather some things.'
Talk to Alun at the look-out camp
Outsiders Not Welcome
As you entered the Dunbog, you stumbled across the Avanc-lûth. You clearly get the sense that these people do not like strangers, nor do they want you anywhere within their bog.
'You should speak with Alun.'

Alun is encamped to the south-west, near a large bent tree.
Bethan has asked you to talk to Alun if you wish to learn more about the people of Dunbog.
Collected wild turnips (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'${PLAYER}, I am pleased that you are here. Ever since Elain was attacked by the Dragon-clan, I have not been able to calm myself. What if we are attacked? We have not the stores to feed our village if some catastrophe were to befall us.
'There should be a few hours yet before the Feast of the Running Stag. I happen to know that wild turnips are in season, and they grow in the fields to the south this time of year. Would you be so good as to collect some so that our stores may be supplemented? It would do much to ease my worries.'

'These were all the turnips you could find? I suppose it will do, for a short day's work. It is not much, but I thank you.'
Grigor turns back to his troubled thoughts.
'What can we do, what can we do...?'
Collect wild turnips (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring the wild turnips to Grigor
Fear of Famine

The peaceful people of Lhan Tarren are rattled by the recent violent aggression of the Dragon-clan in Trum Dreng. It would ease the disturbed fears of the villagers to see their food-stores supplemented.

'I am in constant terror of what state we would be in if you had not brought Elain back to us. But how can we prepare against such a terrible situation? If only we had harvested more crops this year....'

Wild turnips tend to grow in the fields south of Lhan Tarren.
You should collect wild turnips to help bolster the food-stores in Lhan Tarren.

Grigor resides in Lhan Tarren, worrying over the food-stores and the distressing thought of a future emergency.
You should bring the turnips you gathered to Grigor.
Defeated wolves in Trum Dreng (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'My grandfather talks of the importance of remembrance, family, and clan pride, but what of the real dangers pressing against us? Every year, more people of Trum Dreng fall to the evils of the wild.
'My people dwindle, and they are weak and afraid. The old blood of the Stag will likely not survive another generation.
'If you want to truly help my folk, worry less about the Feast of the Running Stag and more about the wolves that loom nearer and nearer.'

'I am sorry if I put you to any trouble, ${PLAYER} -- though I am not sorry that we have fewer wolves to harry us.
'My grandfather and I see things very differently, and I was only complaining, but it was wrong of me to tease you about doing the work of my own people.
'I find that I often despair of our future, when we are so hopeless and useless a people. I am glad you are among us now, even if only for a short time.'
Defeat wolves in Trum Dreng (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Guto at Lhan Tarren
Bolder Every Day
The wolves of Trum Dreng press ever closer to the village, and Guto cares more for the safety of the Stag-clan than preparations for a superfluous festival.
'Do not waste my time with silly thoughts of feasts and festivals, not while we are troubled by wolves and worse!'

Wolves roam the rocky plains south of Lhan Tarren.
You should slay wolves for the protection and well-being of the Stag-clan.

Guto holds his post at Lhan Tarren, the village of the Stag-clan in Trum Dreng.
You should speak with Guto and tell him that you slew many wolves while roaming the wilds beyond the village.
Defeated Red-eye

'${PLAYER}! We seem to have a little time left before the Feast of the Stag begins. I wish to finish the hunt I began the day I was taken, but the Elder has asked me to help him prepare for tonight.
'There is an old fiend who has brazenly walked into town and stolen hens from right under our noses. His howl sends a jolt of fear down the spines of my kin. I was stalking him to his den to the south-west while the Draig-lûth rogues were likewise stalking me.
'His name is Red-eye, an evil old menace of a wolf, and I intend to see him on the end of a spear! If you happen to slay him while you are out in the plains, I will be even more impressed with you!'

'Old Red-eye's cruel howls will trouble the Stag-clan no more! Perhaps now our roosts will remain at peace.
'Come, ${PLAYER}. It is almost time for feasting and the telling of tales. You have done quite enough for one day!'
Defeat Red-eye

Elain, the huntress you rescued not long ago, wishes to finish the hunt she began on the day she was captured.
'The wolf I sought was deep in a den, and I stalked him for many long hours before I became aware that the Dragon-clan was trailing me in the same manner. They took me before I could get too close!'

Red-eye was said to be at a den to the south-west.

'You have done enough for the day, my friend. More than enough! Now it is time to take up your seat as an honoured guest of the Caru-lûth.
'Our annual festival is almost upon us. I hope it will not be so bad as the impetuous young fawns have led you to believe... ha!
'Speak with me again when you are ready.'

'I fear for what may have taken place in the herd-lands after that crow returned last night. A farmer lives there with his son, and a farmhand as well. I must ponder what to do....'

'This is very unsettling. The poor bird tried to land, but friendly hands did not receive it. We will surely scout at first light.

Instance: The Feast of the Running Stag
The Feast of the Running Stag has been disrupted by the ill omen...
You have arrived at Lhan Tarren as the Feast of the Running Stag began and have been invited to join the Stag-clan for the evening.
Talk to Elain
The Feast of the Running Stag is about to begin.
You should perform the <rgb=#FF0000>/sit</rgb> emote near the bonfire to observe the festival.
The Feast of the Running Stag has begun.
You should observe the Feast of the Running Stag.

The Elder's ritual crown can be found at the doorway from which he entered.
You should collect the crown and carry it carefully to the Elder.

The Elder's ritual horse-tail can be found at the doorway from which he entered.
You should collect the horse-tail and carry it carefully to the Elder when he is done speaking.

The Elder's ritual spear can be found at the doorway from which he entered.
You should collect the spear and carry it carefully to the Elder when he is done speaking.
The Feast of the Running Stag continues.
The Elder has called an early end to the Feast of the Running Stag this year, due to likely danger in the south where some of his people live.
Collected bog-reeds (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Well, well. Another duvodiad trying to please us. I am tired of your kind coming into our bog, thinking you can change the world with your mere presence. Well, it will not happen, but you can make my life easier, and I will let you live.
'Fetch me bog-reeds so I can string these bows. The reeds around here grow strong, like us. They are better than any other material out here.
'You doubt me? One more word and I will... never mind. Go gather reeds!'

'Well, you are not completely useless like the others I have seen come through here. Still, my life is no better, and the Elders will just send me out for more bow-strings tomorrow. Thank you for nothing, ${RACE}.
'Now get out of here before I decide to stop being nice.'
'Perhaps you should get me some more bog-reeds?'
Talk to Nye at the scouts' camp
Collect bog-reeds (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Because I Said So
The scouts of the Dunbog have tasked you with several gathering exercises. Nye specifically does not like you and has instructed you to do his task for him.

Bog-reeds be found the north-east area of the Dunbog. Nye is also encamped in the north-east Dunbog.
Nye has intimidated you into fetching him more bog-reeds for bow-strings.
Collected beetle-shells (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Since you are so persistent, perhaps I can put you to some use. The Elders have asked us to gather supplies while we are out here on watch. I personally would rather be in my hut with my wife keeping warm.
'Do you think you can help me then? We need to collect shells from the beetles in the area. We use their shells for armour and cooking, and their meat is passable. But the shells are what we are looking for... undamaged, of course. Bring them to me when you are done.'

'Impressive. This will make my time here go much more quickly. Thank you.
'Perhaps there is more to you than there seems, Duvodiad. My wife will be happy when I return home sooner than usual.'
'Shells. We need shells from beetles. It is not black powder magic... just kill beetles and harvest their shells.'
Talk to Alun at the scouts' camp
Collect beetle-shells (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Protective Shells
As you entered the Dunbog, you stumbled across the Avanc-lûth. You clearly get the sense that these people do not like strangers, nor do they want you anywhere within their bog.

Bog-beetles can be found in the Dunbog. Alun is encamped in the north-eastern part of the Dunbog.
Alun has asked you to gather beetle-shells for the Avanc-lûth and bring them to him.
Collected toad-legs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Since you seem to be doing Alun's labour, then you can help me, as well. I am not certain what I did to upset the Elders, but they always give me the worst tasks.
'They want me to gather food -- which is what I am accustomed to -- but toad-legs? Toads are disgusting creatures and make even worse food. Nevertheless, it is what they demand.
'If you are to be of help, go hunt toads and take their legs. Bring them back to me, and perhaps I will not think of you as the bog-scum you are.'

'Well done, ${PLAYER}. You have saved me a tremendous amount of time and effort doing work that I detest.
'Take this and go do your other tasks. These chores will not complete themselves.'
'Perhaps you could keep gathering toad-legs for me? There are toads all around here. Hunt them and bring back their legs.'
Talk to Séarl in the north-east Dunbog
Collect toad-legs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Fancy Feasts
Séarl has been tasked with gathering food for the Avanc-lûth. He personally does not have a taste for toad-legs, but that is what has been demanded by the Elders.

Toads are all around the camp-fire where Séarl is encamped in the Dunbog.
Séarl has asked you to fetch toad-legs for him.
Collected turtle-eggs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Do you know what the hunter's favoured game is in the Dunbog? Turtles. They present a challenge because they protect themselves so very well. We love hunting them... too much, perhaps.
'The turtles are in danger of vanishing from the Dunbog. We cannot let this happen. We must protect the turtles.
'Go forth and gather turtle-eggs from around the edges of the great southern bog. We need to save the eggs so that we can make sure there are always turtles to hunt!'

'You have done a great thing, stranger. Saving the turtles is very important to the hunters of the Avanc-lûth.
'Please, take this as a token of my appreciation.'
'You still need to save more turtle eggs and quickly. Collect all the eggs and return here when you are done.'
Talk to Rhodri at the hunters' camp
Collect turtle-eggs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
The Turtle or the Egg
Rhodri is worried about the endless slaughtering of turtles and feels that eventually there will be no more turtles in all of the Dunbog.

Turtle-eggs can be found throughout the southern Dunbog.
Rhodri has asked you gather turtle-eggs from all over the southern bog so that the turtles can be saved.

'You have helped us greatly already, but any one person can perform a handful of tasks. Perhaps you can assist our hunters if you truly wish to prove your courage and strength. They oft gather to the south-east.
'The hunters will have much for you to do, I am certain. Hurry there, and if you return successful, then I am certain that the Elders will speak with you.'

'So you believe you can hunt, Duvodiad? We shall see. The beasts of the Dunbog are stronger, faster -- and probably stranger -- than anything you have seen before.
'We do not lay traps. We hunt...with our bare hands, if necessary. Come fight with us. We shall see if you live to tell the tale.'
Talk to Harri at the hunters' camp
To the Hunt
You continue to earn the trust of the people of the Dunbog. The Avanc-lûth must constantly hunt and scavenge, or they will go hungry quickly.
'You should find the hunters at their camp to the south-east.'

The hunters' camp lies to the south-east of Lhan Rhos.
Bain has asked you to talk to the hunters and aid them, with the hope that your success will convince the Elders of Lhan Rhos to speak with you.
Collected mud-balls (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Greetings. You are new here, are you not? Well, that is wonderful. I love meeting new people, even if we do not get to meet many very often. Since Bain has you helping us, I have a chore for you.
'As you can see, we are a village of huts... lots and lots of huts. Sadly, these huts do not stand up well to being half-submerged in swamp-water all day. They are in constant need of repair, and what better way to repair them than with mud. It patches holes and makes things new again.
'Can you bring us some mud-balls then? The beetles of the area east of here love to gather up the mud and roll it into neat little balls. I am not sure why, but we use them to patch our huts.'

'A true gatherer. Impressive. Usually the beetles put up more of a fight for these. I am not sure why they want them, but they guard them jealously.
'Thank you for gathering these. Perhaps, you will stay for a while so we can learn more about the world beyond the Dunbog? We do not often have the opportunity to talk to duvodiad.'

'I do not think that is enough mud to patch up even one house. We will need a lot more mud-balls to take care of all my repairs today.
'You can find the mud-balls to the east, near the beetles' nesting grounds. The beetles sometimes carry them as well.'
Talk to Edhow in Lhan Rhos
Collect mud-balls (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Patching the Huts
Every hut needs repairs, and the huts of the Dunbog are no different. In fact, they need repair even more than most.

Mud-balls can be found where the bog-beetles dwell, east of Lhan Rhos, and sometimes upon the beetles themselves.
Edhow has asked you to gather up as many mud-balls as possible and bring them to him.

'You have done all that we have asked of you and even dealt with Nye's rudeness without complaint. I am impressed. Perhaps you can do the Dunbog some good, unlike the other duvodiad that have passed through here... and I am now one step closer to returning to my wife.
'There will be few who will venture out of doors with you around. Speak with Bain, and perhaps he can help you gain some trust among the People of the Avanc.
'Lhan Rhos lies to the south-west of here. You cannot miss it, for there is not much else to see in that direction.'

'What are you doing here? Alun sent you? He is too trusting these days. Strangers dance their way through our lands with no regard to the plights of my people. Nevertheless, I will trust him this once.
'If you wish to help us, you must help our village. War has not touched these lands, but that does not mean the weather and hardships of life avoid us. Why do we live here, you ask? That answer is not yours to have quite yet.
'For now, help us further, and we will make sure your questions are answered in time.'
Talk to Bain in Lhan Rhos
To Lhan Rhos
Alun has become impressed with you and your performance and recommends you to the Elders of Lhan Rhos.
'You should speak with the Elders at Lhan Rhos.'

Bain is at Lhan Rhos, south-west of the scouts' camp.
Alun has asked you to talk to Bain, but warned you that most of the inhabitants of his village will not trust you or speak with you.

While fighting in the Dunbog, you came across this mud-covered object. It seems like a child's toy... perhaps someone in Lhan Rhos will want it back.
You should return to the village and find the owner of the toy.

'Who are you? Wait, you have found my toy! Thank you, thank you. May I have it please?
'I did not think I would ever find it. Did nasty beetles take it? They always steal our things. I hate them!'
Find the owner of the toy in Lhan Rhos
A Shiny Bauble
While fighting in the Dunbog, you came across a mud-covered object. It seems like a child's toy.

Lhan Rhos is at the centre of the Dunbog.
You should return the toy to its owner.
Collected turtle-shells (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'There are some people that speak highly of the virtues of the beetle-shell. How can they even begin to talk about the beetle-shell when there is a much better shell for many more purposes?
'I speak of the turtle-shell, of course. Can you tell me that you can make a shield out of a beetle-shell? Can you make food for a whole village in one single beetle-shell? Nay, you cannot.
'So we hunt turtles, and we take their shells, and we thank them for the amazing things that we can only do with a turtle-shell. Gather for me many turtle-shells, and we will all be happy as a village.'

'You now know the power of the turtle-shell firsthand. You have learned why I am so incredibly excited about collecting these great shells.
'Thank you very much. You have proven -- to me at least -- that you are a good hunter and a duvodiad to be trusted. So will I tell Harri.'

'Does the turtle elude you? We need to collect the shells. The turtles will not just give them to you. We are sorry we have to kill such a magnificent beast, but it must be done. We must survive against the outside world and the threats that mount against us.
'Collect the shells of the turtles in the southern bog, then hurry back to me.'
Talk to Luarch at the hunters' camp
Collect turtle-shells (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
He Says Shield Shells
Turtle-shells are used for many purposes in Lhan Rhos.

Turtles can be found throughout the southern Dunbog.
Luarch has asked you to hunt turtles in the area and collect their shells.
Collected Avanc-meat (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collected Avanc-skins (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collected Avanc-tails (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'One of your first tasks of the hunt will be to survive. I cannot teach you that, it is something you must learn on your own.
'Once you have mastered survival, we will hunt some avanc. A mighty beast, the avanc.
'We will need to collect as much of their meat, tails, and hide as possible, so try to be precise with your attacks! We go at once!'

'You did well, friend. I am impressed. Do all duvodiad fight as well as you? Actually, nevermind, I know the answer. They do not.
'We must find more suitable tasks for you then, since even the mighty avanc seems easy prey for you.'

'You have not hunted enough avanc to impress me. Anyone can get lucky and kill one avanc. Do you think it so easy that you try to cheat me?
'Go kill avanc in the bog and do not return until you have.'
Talk to Harri at the hunters' camp
Collect Avanc-meat (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collect Avanc-skins (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collect Avanc-tails (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Avanc for Every Need
The avanc, to many beyond Dunland a mythical beast, serve as a staple for the people of the Dunbog.

Avanc can be found throughout the Dunbog.
Harri has asked you to help him fight the mighty avanc.

'You have done much already for the People of the Avanc, and you have survived all of the challenges my men and I presented you. I am impressed.
'You may go and speak with the Elders. Tell them that you have my respect and gratitude. They will be able to help you more with the duvodiad you seek.'
'It is time that we spoke, ${PLAYER}. We have been keeping watch on you, and you have proven good to the Avanc-lûth. It is time that we spoke of some of the secrets of Dunbog.'
Talk to Elder Déin at Lhan Rhos
Back to Lhan Rhos
The hunters are very impressed with your work. You have earned the respect of the Avanc-lûth Elders, and they wish to speak with you about the plight of the Dunbog.
'You should speak with the Elders at Lhan Rhos.'

Lhan Rhos is to the north-west of the hunters' camp.
Harri has asked you to return to the village of Lhan Rhos and speak with the Elders there.
Collected baby slug-meat (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'All of us need to eat. It is as simple as that. The Dunbog does not offer the most traditional food sources, but we think it is some of the best provender ever eaten.
'I become hungry just thinking about our delicacies. You may not really understand, and that is fine. I am not asking you to eat it, just bring some. What am I talking about? Slug-meat, of course...specifically tender, baby slug-meat. The taste is nothing short of amazing.
'There are slugs to the east of the village. The baby slugs are protected by the adults, so be careful. You do not want to be attacked by a group of angry slug-matrons!'

'Well done, Duvodiad. Baby slugs are difficult to hunt. The mothers seem to be able to communicate well with their young. Thank you. We will enjoy this during our next feast.
'You are well on your way to proving that you are not just another intrusive duvodiad.'

'I...we...need that slug-meat. How are we to hold feasts if we do not have it? Hunt the young slugs, for they have the meat we need. You will find them to the east of town.
'But be quick. If the mothers are able, they will protect their young before you attack. Aim for the young first. Once they are injured, they will not be able to flee.'
Talk to Bain in the centre of Lhan Rhos
Collect baby slug-meat (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Slugs for the Slaughter
Bain insists the the meat from baby slugs is a delicacy in Lhan Rhos. The slugs, however, are protective of their young.

Slugs reside east of town. Bain is at the centre of Lhan Ros, west of the slug bogs.
Bain wants you to hunt baby slugs for their meat.
You have defeated Bloodmaw

'You are ready for the ultimate challenge, ${PLAYER}. We must defeat the avanc called Bloodmaw. All of these avanc come from her. She must be dealt with, or Lhan Rhos may one day be overrun. If you can do this, you are truly a friend of the Avanc-lûth.
'Bloodmaw will not be easy prey. I have sent many hunters into the ruins to fight her and none have reported the deed is done. Go... gather any help you wish or prove that you can do it yourself, just come back when she is dead.'

'Indeed, you are worthy of the name of hunter. Well done. The Elders will hear of your great deeds when the day is done.
'Thank you for your bravery. You have put my hunters to shame.'
Defeat Bloodmaw, the avanc matriarch
Talk to Harri at the hunters' camp
Hunting Bloodmaw
The avanc of the Dunbog are ruled by a terrible matriarch, Bloodmaw.
'Defeat Bloodmaw, ${PLAYER}, and you may receive my respect.'

Bloodmaw may be found at the centre of the Withered Stones in the southern Dunbog.
Harri has asked you to kill Bloodmaw, the Avanc matriarch.

Harri is at the hunters' camp, near the western edge of the southern Dunbog.
You should return to Harri and tell him that you have accomplished all that he has asked.
Defeated vicious war-hounds (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeated cunning hunting-hounds (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Do you hear that howling, ${PLAYER}? Those are the Dunlendings' war-hounds. They have released entire packs of them into the wild parts of the Heathfells to harry our scouts and messengers.
'Those beasts are nearly a match for a Warg. We have to drive them off, or we will lose precious time in getting word to the Ford and back should the Dunlending army begin to move.'

'Those beasts have been hounding us for days now. I am glad you were able to drive some of them off.
'Now we need to get word through to the Ford about the Dunlendings' increasing presence in the Isendale.'
Defeat vicious war-hounds (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeat cunning hunting-hounds (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Captain Cadfrith at the Rohirrim encampment
The Hounds

The Dunlendings have released packs of war-hounds into the wild to harry Rohirrim scouts.
You must drive these beasts off lest they harry the Rohirrim attempts to track the Dunlending's movements in the Heathfells, and waylay messengers.

War-hounds can be found throughout the Heathfells.
Captain Cadfrith has asked you to defeat packs of Dunlending war-hounds that have been released into the Heathfells.

Captain Cadfrith is at the Rohirrim encampment in the north-west Heathfells.
You should return to Captain Cadfrith with your report.
You have defeated the Hound-master

This collar was taken from a slain hound in the Heathfells. Crafted of heavy leather, studded with crude iron, it is clearly of Dunlending-make.
The Dunlending Hound-masters leash their beasts upon such collars, and if these dogs wear them, then their master cannot be far away. Perhaps you can defeat him and scatter his hounds.

'So, one of the Dunlending barbarians crept behind our lines to guide the hounds against us?
'Well done discovering his hiding place and dealing with him. That should scatter his packs for good.'
Defeat the Hound-master
Talk to Cadfrith
The Hound-master
You found a heavy, studded collar upon a slain Dunlending war-hound. If the beasts still wear collars as they roam these hills, then their master must be somewhere nearby.

The Dunlending Hound-master has set camp somewhere in the Heathfells.
You should find the Dunlending Hound-master and defeat him and his hounds.

Captain Cadfrith is at the encampment in north-west Heathfells.
You should inform Captain Cadfrith of the Dunlending Hound-master's defeat.
The Elder is grateful that Elain, just returned, may be spared the danger this once
There seem to be hostile Dunlendings on the road. Try following the river
You hear muffled voices, coming from the west bank

'This is dreadful, ${PLAYER}... you saw the crow with your own eyes. I know something terrible has happened where Trev and his folk live in the herd-lands.
'Trev, his farmhand Celun, and his son Dilwun have been helping to feed our folk from the wealth of the herd-lands for a long time.
'We must investigate. I worry that Elain's safety must be compromised again, or Guto's. I do not like throwing my only warrior into danger, or my only grandson. Alas! What am I to do?'

'Do you mean to hurt us, Duvodiad? You and many others, I am sure. Well, get it over with.
'We are outcasts, and there is nothing left for us. We do not even have the means to escape into Enedwaith now. The Draig-lûth will see us. We have no food. At least you can grant us merciful death.'

'You offer to go in Elain's stead, ${PLAYER}? Is there no end to your bravery and generosity? You, a duvodiad to us, would put yourself in danger to find a missing man you have never met?
'It does not seem possible. I do not know how we can ever repay you, good ${PLAYER}!'
Tell the Elder that you volunteer yourself to investigate his missing clansmen
Take the road south towards the herd-lands
What of the Herd-lands?
Since the craban from the farm on the herd-lands returned injured and without the presence of its recipient, the people of Lhan Tarren have been worried about the herdsman Trev and his family.
'I am so worried, ${PLAYER}. I do not know how to protect my people with what little strength we have left.'

'Are you certain that you want me to remain here? I am accustomed to danger, ${PLAYER}. But... I suppose the Elder wants me near in times such as these.
'I wish more than anything that my people were more like you so that I could fulfill my duties....'

Elder Riagán is in Lhan Tarren.
You should tell the troubled Elder that you volunteer your own strength and skill for the task of finding out what might be wrong in the south.

The herd-lands can be found by following the road south from Lhan Tarren.
You should travel down the road in search of what may have intercepted the crow.
Collected stolen food-stores from the Dragon-clan scouts (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'You do not mean to kill us, then? If you are here to help the farmers, you are probably too late. The Dragon-clan warriors destroyed and took everything.
'We passed through the farm two nights ago, but the next morning the deed was done. We heard the screams and saw the smoke.
'We have not had any food or water since. They do not seem to know that we are here, but what does that signify? It seems that we are going to starve in this very spot.'

'I... I thought that was the last we would see of you, Duvodiad. This is very generous! This will feed us until the chaos dies down. I hope we will be able to make our escape to Enedwaith soon.
'Thank you. Our odds were never very promising, but you have just improved them.'
Collect stolen food-stores from the Dragon-clan scouts (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring the stolen food to the hiding Dunlendings
Twice-stolen Stores
The herd-lands, recently captured by the Dragon-clan, had many food-stores that were meant to feed the peaceful inhabitants of Trum Dreng. The Dragon-clan invaders have stolen a great deal of it.
'That Dragon-clan has grown cruel over the years. That farm was peaceful -- there was no need to do what they did there. But in this land of savages, such acts should not be a surprise.'

Stolen food and supplies can surely be found on the Dragon-clan scouts who invaded the farm.
You should steal food-stores back from them and bring them to the starving huddle of outcasts.

Ceri, the leader of the small band of frightened outcasts, is at their tiny camp on the overlook just north-west of the herd-lands.
You should return to Ceri whith the stolen goods you have collected so that his folk may survive their journey through these harsh lands.
The herald has fallen

The message you found upon the Hound-master speaks of a Rohirrim herald who is travelling to parley with a Dunlending brenin. The Hound-master has been instructed to waylay and kill the herald before he arrives at the meeting.
While the Hound-master has been defeated, it appears that his allies have already departed to hunt down the herald. You should find the meeting place and rescue the herald before the trap is sprung.

'Welcome to the Ford of Isen, ${PLAYER}. Some word of your exploits has preceded you here, thanks to the work of my outriders.'
Grimbold stands silently in thought for several long seconds as you hand him the herald's horn and tell him of the battle in which he fell.
'Fastgyl was a good and brave man. He knew it likely that any offer of the Dunlendings would be rife with treachery, but he took it upon himself to speak with them in hopes that this war could be averted.
'I thank you for abiding with him in his last hours.'

The herald lies dead at last from a mortal arrow-wound, and you rise from your death vigil.
Gripping his horn you determine to deliver it to Grimbold at the Ford of Isen and tell him of the herald's fate.
Defend the herald of the Rohirrim
Check on the Rohirrim herald
Talk to Grimbold at the Ford of Isen
Herald of the Rohirrim

You found a message upon the Dunlending Hound-master regarding a Rohirrim herald who has been sent to speak with a clan-leader among the Dunlendings. The herald is to be ambushed and slain before he reaches his destination.

'What is this? You are no wild man... what are you doing out here?'
...
'I... I see. Well, we knew this was a danger when I agreed to parley with their chieftain.
'It was supposed to be a secret, but it seems there is little hope of that now.
'Wait - do you hear that? The baying of those accursed hounds of theirs. They have found us already!'

The herald is supposed to be travelling towards Dol Baran from an encampment at the Ford of Isen.
You should find and defend the herald of the Rohirrim.

The body of the fallen Rohirrim herald lies before you.
You should collect the fallen herald's horn and return it to Grimbold.

The Ford of Isen demarks the eastern boundary of Dunland. The Rohirrim have established an encampment on the western side of the ford, where Grimbold of the Grimslade can be found commanding their local forces.
Bring the horn to Grimbold and tell him of the herald's fate.
Blow the Horn of the Rohirrim
You blow the Horn of the Rohirrim
The Rohirrim have come to your aid

'You are a fine ${RACE} to stand by me in my final hour.
'Take my horn to the Ford and let Grimbold know that I have fallen. Tell him I am sorry....'
The herald's voice trails off into laboured breathing as he closes his eyes in pain and exhaustion.
He does not speak again.
The herald has fallen silent, his breath coming in a few last ragged gasps as his life fades.

'You are correct... I hear the baying of the Dunlending hounds approaching even now.
'It seems we were fools to trust these wild men to parley fairly, but so be it... let us show them the quality of our valour!'
Talk to the Rohirrim herald
Blow the Horn of the Rohirrim
Defeat the Dunlending attackers
Talk to the Rohirrim herald
Instance: Rohirrim Herald
Having quickly moved to rescue a herald of the Rohirrim from a Dunlending ambush, you have arrived only in time to desperately fend off the attackers.
Defend the herald of the Rohirrim from his ambushers.
Overwhelming numbers of wild men are approaching. Summon the Rohirrim to your aid.
Hold out until reinforcements arrive.
With the battle over, the herald you strove to protect lies dying. You speak to him, hoping to bring his final words to his allies at the Ford of Isen.

'We have delayed too long already. I am ready to go, ${PLAYER}. Return to Halbarad in Lhanuch, and we will decide how best to proceed south into Dunland.
'We will leave this place behind, and none too soon! If we had left earlier, we could have left with Candaith and my fallen brothers, and not without them.'

'The south-west passage into Dunland will take us through Trum Dreng, ${PLAYER}. It is a forested land, where shadows pool in the hollows between the hills.
'As I scouted ahead, I saw emblems and totems of a horned stag, but few people. They are likely to be on the edge of the conflicts in Dunland, though if it be by their choice or by necessity I did not discover.
'You are welcome to come with my group into Trum Dreng, ${PLAYER}, and we will learn the truth of it.'

'Corunir is right. This delay has been costly. If what you say is true, and Saruman does know of our errand, we travel from hardship into even greater peril. And yet, we must not despair or turn from our road, or our brethren will have fallen for naught.'
Halbarad sighs, his brow creased with worry.
'There are two paths we could take into Dunland, and I propose that we split into smaller groups and travel each of these paths...we will be less likely to be noticed as we cross into Dunland.
'Prestadír and Braigiar have scouted our options. Speak with them to hear of the two roads that we might use to enter Dunland.'

'You have heard what we know about our possible paths into Dunland. Each way could be dangerous, and we will not know what awaits us until we get there.
'Which road do you wish to take into Dunland, ${PLAYER}? Each will have its dangers. Make your choice and tell Braigiar or Prestadír which group you will follow: Braigiar if you wish to travel through Trum Dreng, or Prestadír if you wish to enter the Bonevales.'

'The south-east passage into Dunland will take us through the Bonevales, an inhospitable and barren land. The crags and valleys are dusty and barren, and its people are tough, like coffin nails.

'If we had not delayed, we might have left with our fallen brothers, and not without them. Go to Lhanuch and tell Halbarad that I will be there shortly. You will find him in the centre of the village.'
'I would be pleased if you would join my group on the journey into Trum Dreng, ${PLAYER}. Its forested hills are steeped in shadow, cold and mysterious.'
'There are two paths that we might take into Dunland. Speak with Prestadír and Braigiar concerning what they have learned about the way into Dunland.'
'I would be honoured if you travelled with my group into the Bonevales. It is an inhospitable land and barren, and it would be good to have your company.'

'Very good, ${PLAYER}. I welcome you into the group that will travel into Trum Dreng, the Land of the Stag! We will do our best to come that way into Dunland free of danger.

'Let us be off at once! We can stop and see how things fare once we have crossed into Trum Dreng.'

'Here we are. We have crossed into Dunland, and now find ourselves in the Land of the Stag. Be on your guard. We need to know what the situation here is, and we can only know that by observing its people.

'I am glad that you have chosen to accompany my group into the Bonevales, ${PLAYER}. The road will be dangerous, and I could use your abilities. We will be mostly in the open and exposed unless we are very careful to stay in the shadow of the cliffs.
'We will not travel by the road! I will meet up with you just west of the road as it enters Dunland.
'Let us be off at once! We can assess what awaits us once we cross into the Bonevales.'

'We are here, ${PLAYER}. We have crossed over into the Bonevales. We need to know what the situation in this valley may be, and what threats could endanger this leg of our quest.
'Bledhun here tells a tale of mysterious happenings. You should hear him out and do as he says. We will need allies in this land.
'Once you have aided Bledhun and his friends, we can meet up again in a hidden valley to the south. It will be the perfect location from which to scout the twisting ways of the Bonevales. Travel ahead and meet me at the camp there.'

'This will be a good place from which to launch our exploration of the Bonevales, ${PLAYER}. We should help the people of the Bonevales as much as we can, for they could be valuable allies against the dangers that await us further south.'

'Who are you, Duvodiad? You do not belong in this land. You are not welcome.'

'I did not think to see you again, Duvodiad, but I was wrong, yes. I heard the cries of that pathetic Ox from here!
'Folk of many clans live in Galtrev, but those who have grown wealthy from the gifts of Saruman float to the top. We of the lower village work hard just to get by, but the task-masters in the upper village live off of our labours and return the products of them to the Wizard.
'Perhaps you can be of some use to the Hebog-lûth, the Clan of the Falcon. We stand against those who have thrown in with Saruman.'
'This land belongs to the Ox Clan! You will not leave here alive!'

'People of many clans have listened to the promises of Saruman, and where his words are not enough, his gold does the trick. Even the folk of Galtrev are put to work to further the Wizard's aims.
'At the lumber-camp north-east of here, trees are felled and the wood prepared for carting to Isengard. Go there, steal their axes, and throw them in the pond east of the lumber-camp. Even if they fish them out, the rust will make the axes unreliable and difficult to use. Members of the dragon clan may have brought the axes to other settlements in Pren Gwydh. Those will do as well!
'A simple act of rebellion, maybe, but its effect could be sweeping.'

'You caused some trouble out there, I trust? Ha! Good. There is more for you to do.
'Wood from the lumber-camp has already been collected and is being stored in the upper village until it can be carted south. Take this torch and burn the wood-piles! That will make them scurry!'

'Wonderful, wonderful! Oh, you are a treat, my new friend.'
Catrin cackles with delight.
'The Hebog-lûth, the Falcon-clan, stands against Saruman and seeks to cause trouble for those who side with him. I think you will be a comfort to us...and perhaps we to you and yours.'

'Quickly! There is no time to lose. The Pristine Glade is being threatened. We protect one of the last of the sacred Old Trees. It helps us survive in this otherwise impossible land. As protectors of the Tree, we can not allow anything to happen to the Glade.
'Go quickly. Do not waste time. Protect the Glade to the west from Saruman's prying eyes and soldiers.'

'You have made it in time, I hope. The Elders sent word that you were coming to defend the Glade. We have been protecting this Sacred Tree for generations. There is no duty with higher honour.
'We must protect the Glade from Saruman's destructive ways. This is one of the last remaining Old Trees. We have heard that he has destroyed all others in Dunland. We cannot allow this to happen here.'

'I am very thankful for all that you have done, ${PLAYER}. You have given the Avanc-lûth much to think about. It seems that the outside world will invade into our own no matter what we do. It would be best that we prepare for that time, rather than hide from it.
'I hope that the duvodiad you seek can be of help to you. They are part of a group who seek to protect Dunland from the upcoming storm and call themselves the Boar-clan, in honour of the clan who resisted the White Hand to their very end. We may have to join them in their fight sooner than we had anticipated.
'You will find them to the north, just south of Lhan Colvarn, the Village of the Condemned. It was once Lhan Rhos before Saruman forced us to move here.'

'Anurin sent you, did he? Well, it is about time the Avanc-lûth came to their senses. We need fighters, not speakers.
'Come! If you are ready, we need to destroy these Abominations before any more of them escape Lhan Colvarn.
'I do not have time to mince words with you, Duvodiad. Either you are ready to fight, or you can go back and join the Elders. The time for words is well past.'

'We have much to talk about, Duvodiad. Here in the Dunbog we are able to stay out of the affairs of the rest of Dunland. We know that storms brew on the horizon, but we make certain that we keep out of the rain.
'Part of the reason is that we have a constant reminder to the north of what happens when we do not mind our own affairs. The last time that we interfered, Saruman took many of our people and did foul things to them. I am not sure what he was doing there, but he returned one day with an army of twisted monsters, abominations to nature.
'Now we need to deal with the attacks of the Abominations every day. Go north and help stave off the attacks of these creatures, and when you are done, speak with Anurin.'

'I should not be impressed since you have done all that we have asked, but I am. You do as we ask without thought or question.
'The Abominations are a sad tale, indeed. They also kill without thought or question but for all the wrong reasons. We watch them, but we are wary of destroying them all because it is not in our nature.
'Now, I may have information regarding the Dunlending strangers you are seeking.'

'We have been here looking for signs of Saruman's plans for quite some time. While we do not know what his end goal is, we now know that the time of his attack seems imminent. He is much more active now and has done worse things than we had ever expected.
'We need to move upriver and warn the rest of the Boar-clan resistance. The easiest way to get there will be by boat down the river past Wulf's Cleft.
'We must prepare for the trip, however. There are rumours that some of the clans are uniting and forming large forces. We cannot travel with a small group of people. There is a large amount of driftwood near the borders of the river along the bog. We can make oars for the trip with it. Hurry. Gather as much as you can carry.'
'Well done. We will begin carving these immediately in preparation for the voyage. Make sure that you have gathered everything else, then we will talk more.'
'We need more wood if we are to make oars, and we need more oars if we are to go east. Please hurry.'

'All of this killing sickens me. Blaire and the others just want to kill anything that moves and has a White Hand emblazoned upon it.
'Well, I will not stand for it. These were once our people. It is not their fault that Saruman wants to make half-orcs and uruks. They did not ask to be made into this.
'Warn our twisted kin and save them. They are not abominations. We need to help them, not destroy them. Go north to Lhan Colvarn and tell them to leave before Blaire and the rest destroy the camp. You may see them as abominations, but I ask you to look more closely.'

'Thank you for saving our twisted kin. I know that some may have resisted your help. That is all right. It is a sad but foreseen loss.
'I hope that Blaire and the Boar-clan will understand now that these are not monsters... they are just like us. One day, this will never happen again. Thank you for saving our people.'

'So, Duvodiad, you have passed through many dangers to come here. I do not believe in chance, so it must be by someone's -- or something's -- design that you are here.
'Believe it or not, word came hither of your journey -- nay, fear not... your secret remains secret. You have assuredly met some of my brethren in arms in the Dunbog... I have learned of your coming through them, and through northern duvodiad who passed through Carreglyn not long ago.
'If you will aid me with a few tasks, I may be able to lend assistance to your cause, as well. First, I would like you to patrol our territory... Warg-riding goblins plague our lands, and I wish to learn whence they came, so that we may drive them back. Seek for signs of the Warg-riders on the banks of Lhun Avanc, at the Barnavon Mine, upon Hen Turrau, and at the shrine of the Uch-gwirod, whom you might call Munfaeril. What say you?'

'Your patrol was not fruitless, though the discoveries are not what I had expected. I am grateful for your efforts. I will review the evidence you have brought to me, and perhaps we will still learn where these Warg-riders come from and what their purpose here is.
'In the meantime -- and if you are willing -- I have more yet for you to do.'

A World of Trouble

After escaping the perils of Wulf's Cleft, you have arrived at the village of Barnavon in Carreglyn. There is little sense of safety in this place, though no one has yet made an overt gesture of hostility.
'The first place to look lies at Lhun Avanc. Be wary, for legend tells that the Great Avanc lairs there, waiting for the foolish to fall into its trap!'
'The second place to look will bring you near to the Barnavon Mine. The workers there may need your assistance.'
'The third place to look is found at Hen Turrau on the hill above the Barnavon Mine. It has long been a watch-tower of my people, but I fear it is now being used for evil purposes.'
'The final place to look is at the shrine of the Uch-gwirod. Long ago, the Ox-spirit dwelt there and spoke oft with my forefathers. Perhaps she may be persuaded to intercede on our behalf once more.'

This placard describes the ritual used by the Derudh of Dunland to call upon the ox-spirit Munfaeril, which they call the Uch-gwirod, for aid. The troubles in Barnavon may be cause enough to attempt such a feat.

'I am pleased that you have heard my summons, good ${RACE}. Does it surprise you that your coming is of my design? I care very much for the People of the Ox, but Madin Brenin has fallen to corruption. He and his people oppress the remnant of the Turch-lûth, the People of the Boar, and plot war with the Horse-lords who are in the favour of the Valar. This cannot be tolerated.
'I ask that you go to Barnavon and bring this message to Madin Brenin: if he does not turn from his evil ways, he and his people will feel the wrath of the Uch-gwirod and the Huntsman.
'Take my sigil as proof of my words and speak with me when you are ready to depart.'

'Alas, Madin Brenin was a fool, and his son no less. Yet, the true blame for these evils falls to one of my own kindred, and I fear they will all suffer in the end.
'I thank you for bringing my warning to Barnavon and grant you what grace I may.'

'You know by now that Saruman of Many Colours seeks to sway the clans of Dunland to wage war against the Horse-lords of Rohan. Here in Barnavon, my people -- the People of the Ox -- have pressed the last remnant of the Boar-clan into service in the mine, extracting ore to make weapons and gear for Saruman's allies.
'It is an abuse that Madin Brenin will come to rue, I believe, for it goes against what his grandfather stood for when he granted refuge to the Boar-clan. However, should the mines cease to be worked, it will go poorly for the Turch-lûth -- the Boar-clan. We have received word of troubles there, and the miners are frightened. If something is not done soon, I fear the backs of the Boar-clan will feel the Brenin's wrath.
'The Barnavon Mine is the second place where I asked you to seek for signs of Warg-riders... will you help with this?'

'You have proven yourself a friend to the unfortunate, and thus I will consider you a friend as well. Will you continue to aid us?
'Fear not concerning the weapons the ore from the mine will bring into being... the resistance will see to it that not all is as it seems. Concern yourself only with the well-being and good will of the Turch-lûth of Barnavon... they may find they have a stronger will than Madin Brenin believes.'

'You have completed many tasks on behalf of the Turch-lûth, the People of the Boar. There are not many of us alive today, but those of us who are will continue to grow and thrive.
'I know that you fear that the iron we mine will continue to be made into weapons of war for Saruman -- and that is true -- but Gwilum has friends among us who will see that such weapons do not prove their worth.
'Thank you.'

'What? Who are you? You have come to help? That is well, for we are in great need of aid, and the accursed Ox-dung will not see fit to lend it!
'The mine has been overrun by bugan. They came out of nowhere and fell upon us as we laboured. We were able to fight our way out, but not without loss. Many are wounded, many dead.
'We are in need of medicine, duvodiad. Red clover grows in the hills near the mine, especially around Hen Turrau. Would you collect some and bring it here to me?'

'It is done!
'Take this meillionen salve and these bandages to the wounded miners and bind their wounds, then return to me.'

'Ah! Yes, these will do nicely. It will take but a moment to finish the salve, then I will have more for you to do.'

'I might have heard someone from the herdsman's family the night the Dragon-clan came. I heard a terrible scream, but there was naught that we could do without weapons.
'There was no light at all. No light... only screams. The screaming went on, then was silent. Whatever happened to that poor family, it was nothing good.
'It is good of you to want to look for them, but are you certain it is worth the risk? It is folly to seek the dead while their killers lurk nearby.'

This is undoubtedly Trev, the chief herdsman in these lands.

You have discovered the last member of Trev's family, and he too is dead... murdered and left at the river-bank to be carried away when the rains come.

This man probably worked for the farmer, but he lies face-down in the water. It is obvious that he has not drawn breath for too long now....

'I haven't eaten in a full two hours! My friends were supposed to sup with me, but they need to find me first. I'm the best hider in all the Shire, you see, so it may be a while yet before I can take my meal.

'Will you stay and sup with us? I am sure Inir would be pleased.'
'Mam says I will feel better after I have eaten... thank you for bringing food to us.'
'After I make your hood, I will make a warm blanket for my tad.'
'I am sure the Ox-dung are none too pleased with you... thus am I most happy, ${PLAYER}.'
'The food you brought will keep my family until I return.'
'Your gift is most graciously received, duvodiad.'
'The food you brought is appreciated... I only hope it does not bring the Brenin's wrath down upon us.'

'Gwilum sent you, duvodiad? The old man is good to our people, and if he trusts you, then I will lend you a measure of trust as well.
'Indeed, my people are oppressed, treated as less than the earth we walk upon. We are given no ground to till and what animals we raise are often taken by the Brenin to fill his larders. The Uch-lûth are slowly starving us to death.
'Rumour tells that there are excess stores gathered throughout Upper Barnavon, perhaps to provision this mad war of the Wizard's. Will you seek these stores and apportion it among my people? Perhaps if you do this deed, suspicion will not fall upon the Boar-clan.'
'My thanks to you, ${PLAYER}. This was an act of great charity to the People of the Boar and will not be forgotten.'
'Thank you, duvodiad! With Yago gone, food will be even scarcer... now my children will not have to go hungry.'
'Leave me and my family to our grief!'

'What is this? Even though I refused to work in the mine, you bring me this food?
'I must gather my tools at once. I cannot permit this charity, without showing some myself.'
'Nay, I told you that I will not work the mine!'
'With Matho gone, I did not know how I would feed my children. You must have been sent by the Turch-gwirod to free us from the oppression of the Ox-clan!'
'Must you bring us more grief?'

'Is this the new generosity of the Uch-lûth? Ha! I did not think so!
'You are a boon to the People of the Boar, duvodiad... may the Turch-gwirod bless you.'

Talk to Kai in Barnavon
Food for the Hungry
The Ox-clan of Barnavon, allied with Saruman the White, holds the remnant of the Boar-clan in thralldom and oppression.
'You have brought joy to me and my son in an evil time.'
'Mam is a little happy now since you brought that food, duvodiad.'
'At least my children will not starve. For that, you have my thanks, duvodiad.'
'Mam says we should relish eating the ox-meat you brought, but I think it's rather tough... I prefer boar.'
'Thank you for bringing food to us... I was hungry!'
'Mam says we are going to have a feast tomorrow!'
'You have provided for my daughter better than that lout Matho.'
'I am sure the Brenin will not even notice this food is missing from his stores... I thank you for it!'
'Mam is going to make bugail-pastai for dinner tonight! It is my favourite!'
'I must ask your pardon, but I have no time to speak with you.'
'You have risked much to bring this food to my family. Perhaps I should rethink my decision not to help in the mine....'
'Tell Gwilum that I will not work in the mine.'
'I am thankful for the deliverance of my husband from the mine!'
'Blessings upon you, duvodiad! This provender will go far to feed my family!'
'The sight of you brings me great joy, for you have been a boon to my people.'
'On behalf my husband, Inir, and our children, I thank you for this food and ask the Turch-gwirod's blessing upon you.'
'How may I be of help to you, Hero of the North?'
'This act of kindness shall not be forgotten, duvodiad. I will sing your praises before the Turch-gwirod!'
'What can I do for you, duvodiad?'
'Thanks to you for this food, for I shall not be so aggrieved when I leave to work in the mine.'
'Please forgive me... I must prepare to leave for the mine.'
'This food will leave my family able to care for itself while I am at the mine. My thanks to you.'

Defeated Prudwen Brehur

'You there, young duvodiad. Gwilum sent you to help us? He is a kind child... a true child of the Ox.
'If you wish to help, then I have a task for you. Prudwen, the chief of Madin Brenin's brehur, is also the overseer of the Barnavon Mine. So many of our men have perished or become infirm from working that terrible place.
'I ask that you go to the home of Prudwen Brehur and teach him the meaning of kindness and compassion in a way that only one such as yourself might accomplish. Will you do this?'

'I confess that I knew the Brehur would not heed kindly words. I also confess that this is exactly the outcome I had intended.
'I hope you will forgive an old woman for using you thus. You may tell Gwilum that I appreciate his offering of peace.'

'So, Old Gwilum wishes to help us against our oppressors? His goals may be served by serving ours.
'Much of our oppression comes from the labour we must endure to provision and supply Saruman's war efforts. If you were to burn some of the supplies that the Brenin's men have collected thus far, it may go far towards hindering the Wizard.
'Will you do this? The Brenin must be taught that Dunlendings should stand for Dunland, not a Wizard from afar.'

'Indeed, you are resourceful, Duvodiad. The Boar-clan and its allies thank you for your aid.
'This will perhaps hinder the efforts of Saruman in Barnavon, but perhaps it will also teach the Ox-clan what it is like to go hungry.'

'Rhuwalhan refused to release the captives? Curse his bones and may his spirit rot in whatever place of punishment he now dwells!'

'As I have tried to make you understand, I am a member of that resistance you first came upon in Lhan Rhos. This resistance has taken the guise and mantle of the Boar-clan, the Turch-lûth, as a symbol of defiance. Why, you may ask?
'The Turch-lûth were a clan of the Algraig in the land to the north you call Enedwaith. When the Turch-lûth refused to bow to Saruman, the Draig-lûth destroyed them almost utterly.
'The people here in the lower village are all that remain of the true Turch-lûth. Madin Brenin's grandfather gave them refuge out of kindness, but Madin himself has placed them under thralldom. They are now little more than slaves of the White Hand. I ask that you go now into the village and speak with the People of the Boar and learn what you can do to help them.'

'My thanks to you, ${PLAYER}. The Brenin and his brehur shall incur the wrath of Saruman for their inability to supply iron for the Wizard's war, but they may now be too frightened to retaliate against the Turch-lûth.'

'Yago is dead? N-no... this cannot be true! How dare you say such things, Duvodiad?

'Thank you, ${PLAYER}. You have proven a true friend to the Boar-clan once again.

'Wilim lives! What joyous news! May the blessings of the Turch-gwirod be ever with you!'
'Siam was hurt, but lives still? Then we shall be thankful that worse did not come upon him. We shall prepare for his joyous return!'
'Inir will be a welcome sight... praise be to the Turch-gwirod for his safe return!'
