'While you were lending aid to the Turch-lûth, I looked over the items you brought me from your hunt. I fear the news is grim. It is clear to me now that the Warg-riders are in fact servants of Saruman of Many Colours. It also appears that the Brenin and his brehur are in league with them!
'I believe I now know the origin of the Wargs... one of the items you brought to me was a piece of rune-marked tree-bark. It is in the tongue of my own people and can be found upon ritual trees in the Gravenwood. I believe that the Warg-riders must be encamped somewhere near the Gravenwood, along the road to the north.
'You should know as well that other duvodiad from the north passed that way, Men allied with the Boar-clan resistance. One of them -- Amlan, I believe his name is -- is encamped just within the eaves of the Gravenwood. If you would help me against the riders, I am certain Amlan will have a reward for you.'

'Well met again, ${PLAYER}. So you were able to bring aid to old Gwilum and the Boar-clan? That is well.
'Now, however, I have a vital task for you....'

'Artisans can no longer execute their recipes at ordinary workbenches; instead, they must use the superior workbench, like this one beside me.
'Before granting you access to artisan recipes, I want to make sure that you are truly proficient as an expert. 'I hear that your work was greatly admired in Esteldín! That is evidence enough for me that you are a true artisan, ready to use a superior workbench. Superior facilities can be found here and in many high-level areas throughout Middle-earth. I look forward to watching your progress as a jeweller!

'As you see, Jeweller, I have little now. There has been much suffering. This trinket you give me is of significant worth to my people. A polished ruby is believed to be a stone of fortune, and I am sure this gift will help me in days to come. Thank you, ${PLAYER}!'

'Thank you, ${PLAYER} -- this is a generous gift! I had lost my gold ring while I was scouting Nan Amlug, and that ring was a great boon to me in my travels. This replacement is even greater than the original. Your skill as a jeweller is evident.'

'Ah, this is a fine piece for my set. I am a collector of sorts, so I have a good eye for crafted goods. Daemirdan was not exaggerating when he implied that you were one of the most skilled jewellers he has encountered in a long time.'

'Indeed, I will set you on the path to Saeradan and the Horse-lords, but first I need your assistance. My mission in this wood is to scout for signs of Gwyllion, the Old Woman of the Mountain. My efforts have proven unfruitful as of yet, but perhaps with your aid, that will change.
'As we journey towards the scout-camp, perhaps you may help scout the forest between here and there? If we find signs of Gwyllion's passage, you can then deliver word of it to Saeradan.
'What say you? We will need to stay along the north face of the southern hills, for that is the section I am assigned to scout, and I can only take you as far as the pass to the Isendale, for I must part ways with you there.'

The Rangers Saeradan, Amlan, and Andreg have tracked Gwyllion, the Old Woman of the Mountain, from the Windfells in Enedwaith to the Gravenwood of Dunland.
<rgb=#FF0000>Completing this quest will make it impossible to acquire new discoverables from Andreg and will fail the Tracking an Old Goat deed and any unresolved discoverables.</rgb>
Andreg has asked you to help him scout the Gravenwood -- specifically the path to the Rohirrim scout-camp -- for signs of Gwyllion's passage.

Andreg is preparing to part company with you. You should speak with him to find out where to go from here.
<rgb=#FF0000>Completing this quest will make it impossible to acquire new discoverables from Andreg and will fail the Tracking an Old Goat deed and any unresolved discoverables.</rgb>

'When we first came to this place, we stumbled upon a party of Rohirrim scouts, led by Théodred, the king's son. They were attempting to creep behind the Dunlending lines, but unfortunately for them, the Horse-lords are not the most cautious warriors.
'We helped them to sneak past their enemies and establish a camp here in the Gravenwood. Saeradan remained with them, believing it to our mutual benefit to aid them. Their mission here might help us to regain Gwyllion's trail.
'You should head east at once to the Rohirrim's scout-camp and join with Saeradan. Take this whistle...it is made to sound like the call of a bird not found here. If you sound it, Andreg will come to take you to Saeradan.'

'${PLAYER}! It is good that you have come, though I must say I did not doubt much that our paths would cross once more.
'There is great evil afoot, and we could use your aid!'

'You have been of great aid to me upon this road, ${PLAYER}. I must turn aside now and scout the woods to the south and east.
'If you turn north, you will eventually come upon the Rohirrim scout-camp, where Saeradan awaits you.
'Farewell, ${PLAYER}. May we meet again!'
<rgb=#FF0000>Advancing this quest will no longer allow you to summon Andreg and will cancel any quests bestowed by him that are currently underway.</rgb>

'${PLAYER}, when I and my companions first came here, we noticed almost at once a queer stillness about the forest. There is undoubtedly a foul presence at work here, and I would wager that Gwyllion has something to do with it, but thus far we have been unable to find the source.
'Perhaps you will aid us in this task? There are two trees -- one to the north-west and one to the south-west -- which were clearly once used in some Dunlending ritual. One is called the Mustering Tree, for it is where the forces of Dunland gathered to go to war against Gondor and Rohan long ago. The other is called the Tree of Tribute, for a brave Dunlending warrior stood alone there against a strong force of their enemies and sacrificed himself to allow his clan to escape.
'Search these places for any clues, then follow the signs wherever they may lead. When you have discovered the source of the evil here, return to me. I have provided you tools to dig with, should the need arise.'

'${PLAYER}, if you wish to be of aid to me, I have a task of great import -- though it may not seem so at the first. I sent several scouts out into the Gravenwood to discover any movement of Dunlending forces, but I have not yet heard from any of them.
'Would you seek out the scouts and learn if any ill has befallen them? It has been too long, and I fear for my companions. Their names are Thurbald, Elfrith, and Cuthric. Thurbald and Cuthric have gone north and east into the Gravenwood, while Elfrith has returned south to watch the road to Wulf's Cleft.
'I will reward you for your efforts.'

'This news is distressing. The Orcs are of little concern to me -- let them consume the Dunlendings' wood -- but the companies of Dunlending warriors troubles me. From what you tell me, they will be converging upon the Mustering Tree, and that is an ill omen.
'Despite the enmity the Draig-lûth have shown to their own countrymen, I think it more likely that both companies are meeting as allies to join the host gathering in Wulf's Cleft.
'I must think upon this problem.'

'Léofward sent you? That is well, for I have discovered an encampment of Draig-lûth -- Dragon-clan warriors -- moving down from Enedwaith. News of their movement should be taken to Léofward at once... I will remain and keep an eye on the encampment.
'If you wish to be of further aid, I may have other tasks for you before you leave, though.'

'You there, Léofward sent you? I have news for you to take to him: a band of Orcs bearing the mark of the White Hand has entered the Gravenwood and has been clear-cutting the forest here. I know not for what purpose, but they have been shipping the wood eastward.
'If you wish to be of further assistance, I may have other tasks for you before you go.'

'Indeed, I am well, ${CLASS}. I have discovered an encampment of warriors of the Uch-lûth, the Ox-clan, marching eastward out of Carreglyn. I daresay they are up to no good. Take this news at once to Léofward.
'If you wish to be of further aid, I may have other tasks for you before you leave.'

Rhus points to the buckets of sudsy water lying nearby.

'So much for the Rohirrim! Only through deception and with a small force could they remove Wulf as lord of all the land! The history of Dunland is a full one, and you Elves know little of it.
'But I am pleased to have taught you this much, at least: that there is more to know. Perhaps there can be an understanding between your people and mine after all. Go tell Penrod, to the north, that my previous misgivings have been lessened.'

A Full History
Evan of the Falcon-clan is mistrustful of Elves and wants to be sure you know it.
'Your friends, those other Elves...ask them how much they know about Dunland. Not much, I would wager! You Elves are all the same, always looking down on the shorter-lived peoples!'
'Go tell Penrod that my misgivings are lessened. He is to the north.'
'I still think you should ask this Evan what he knows about the history of our people, ${PLAYER}. Not much, I would wager.'
'I am glad that Evan's clan resists the promises of Saruman, ${PLAYER}, but I will not pretend to care about the history of Dunland. That will have to be enough for him.'

Elladan is south of the Brenin's house, by the ruins of the ancient fort near Tûr Morva. Elrohir is on a small rise overlooking the lake, west of the entrance to Tûr Morva.
Evan wants you to ask Elladan and Elrohir what they know about Dunland. He thinks they, and all Elves, look down on the shorter-lived races.

Evan is just inside the entrance to Tûr Morva.
You have spoken with Elladan and Elrohir concerning their knowledge of Dunlending history and should now report it to Evan. You may wish to be tactful.

Penrod is among the northern buildings of Tûr Morva.
Evan has decided he is not as angry about Elves as he once was and wants you to tell Penrod.
This axe is of fine dwarf-make, sharp and strong
Most men would need two hands to wield this heavy sword
This staff is well-balanced, and could be deadly in the right hands

'Mair told me that there was a dwarf with the company, but I did not believe her. But here you are! We see so few of your people here.
'Is it true what they say about your cities under the mountains, that they stretch for leagues and leagues? How can you build for so long, and so great a distance? Do you not miss the daylight?
'You must excuse my questions. You are only the second dwarf I have seen in many months, and the other did not speak to me, as he met only with the Brenin. You should speak with Lheu Brenin, and he can tell you of your kinsman.'

'We truly do not see many dwarves in these lands. Lindar was quite close with Lheu Brenin, and the gifts he gave to him were most thoughtful. I wonder if the Brenin will have occasion to use any of them but the sword, given these times.'

'What can I do for you, ${PLAYER}?'
You tell him that Arwel wanted you to ask him about his previous dwarf guest. Lheu Brenin laughs heartily.
'Arwel has always been fascinated with your people; I think he wishes he had been born a dwarf! That would be a loss for the Falcon-clan; my daughter Mair has always been fond of him.
'It is true, we played host to one of your people not long ago. His name was Lindar, and he gifted me a weapon when he departed. Dwarves are keen of eye, yes? Examine these weapons and tell me which of them was his gift to me.'

'Well? Which weapon was a gift from Lindar?'
You tell him your answer, wondering what his reaction will be. His surprise is obvious.
'All three of them? Are you certain? Why do you say that?'
You tell him that it was not your examination of the weapons that led you to the answer. Instead, it was the visible reaction on his face every time you handled one of the weapons that made you realize the question was not a fair one.
'Ha! That will teach me to think I know the ways of dwarves, ${PLAYER}! Well done, indeed! Lindar did gift each of these to me: the axe as a present from his people for past aid, the sword to combat present strife, and the staff to lean on in my old age, if I live to see it.
'You are indeed a rare dwarf! Go speak with my Brehur, Penrod, to the north. He wanted to speak with you.'

Arwel is delighted to meet a dwarf, considering how few he has seen, and tells you about another who visited the Brenin recently.
'You will find Lheu Brenin outside his house at the top of the village. Speak with him about your kinsman, the other dwarf that passed through Tâl Methedras recently.'
'The weapons are right there on the table. Which of them was Lindar's gift to me?'
'Penrod is the first of my Brehur and wished to speak with you.'

'A moment, if you would, Duvodiad. You have come from the lands of the Algraig, from Lhanuch? Did you see a young man there named Anirin?'
You tell her that you did encounter such a man, rescuing him from peril in the depths of the cave called Lhaid Ogo.
'My son! My Anirin! Thank the spirits! Oh, ${PLAYER}, you must give me any word of him you have.'
You tell her that he seemed to be doing fine and planned to return to Tûr Morva once he recovered from the experience.
'Thank you for these tidings! You must bring them to his beloved, to whom he is promised. Her name is Wenda, and her home is down the hill to the south.'

'You have news of Anirin?'
You tell her about your encounter with Anirin in the depths of Lhaid Ogo, in Enedwaith, and she seems relieved to hear he plans to return soon.
'I told him not to go, but he could not be persuaded. Anirin is stubborn! He gets that from his mother.
'Thank you for saving my beloved, ${PLAYER}. I am indebted to you, and when Anirin and I have married, our family will be indebted to you as well. It is our way.
'Return to Seren and thank her for sending you to me.'

'Wenda is such a nice girl. She did not want Anirin to bring Lheu Brenin's message to the Algraig, but he saw the need and could not be dissuaded.
'Have you met Penrod, the Brenin's first Brehur? He is among the northern buildings of Tûr Morva. He was looking for you.'

'I saw you speaking with Anirin's family. It was a difficult decision for him to make, to be the bearer of Lheu Brenin's message north to the Algraig, but he knew its importance. He is swift; it is one of the reasons the Brenin tasked him with that journey. He will be back with his mother and with Wenda soon enough.'

Seren is the mother of Anirin, the messenger you met in Enedwaith and rescued from Lhaid Ogo. She wants news of her son brought to those who love him.
'Return to Seren and thank her for thinking of me. I will be glad when Anirin is safely returned, but any news of him makes my day brighter.'
'My son is promised to Wenda, who lives down the hill to the south. She will want to hear any news of him you can give her!'
'Penrod wanted to speak with you. Look for him among the buildings to the north.'

'Your Ranger friends have already been very helpful, ${PLAYER}. If the clans loyal to Saruman try to strike us before we are ready to leave, we may yet have a chance.
'Speak with your friends and see how they progress with their tasks.'

'Ha! Ha! I am sorry your friend Radanir is unhappy. Mucking out the oxen is not a pleasant task, but if it is not done, all suffer. There are very few desirable tasks when it comes to preparing for war, ${PLAYER}, but all must be done.'
Penrod laughs heartily.
'But I am not ankle-deep in manure, am I? Perhaps I will find someone to take Radanir's place. We are grateful for the help and do not want any of the Rangers to resent volunteering it!
'Thank you for your help and theirs, ${PLAYER}. The clans arrayed against us are fierce and merciless, but they do not have allies from the North, as we do!'

'We are doing all we can, ${PLAYER}. I have been assisting Rhus with the tanning; it is dirty, odious work, but the Falcon-clan needs the leather if they are to have fresh armour for its warriors.
'I saw Radanir not long ago. He was not very happy about something, but would not tell me what it was. Right now I am working to clear this brush so we can stretch some more hides as they come in.'

'There is a great deal to do before the Falcon-clan is ready, but this work will be worth it in the end. We have few enough allies in this land. If the sweat of our brow can help the Hebog-lûth stand against the clans loyal to Saruman, the work is worth it.
'We have already brought much in the way of food. Once it is dried or preserved, it will be wrapped and ready. My arms ache, but not so badly that I must stop.'

'I know allies among the Dunlendings are precious few, ${PLAYER}, but I do not see what is so different about the Falcon-clan than others that we have seen.
'They have me mucking out the oxen! I have seen more manure already in Dunland than I have in my entire life back north. I could be doing something useful, but instead they hand me a hay-fork and a broom and tell me to get to work.
'I do not like these men, ${PLAYER}, and it is not because of the manure. There are plenty of reasons, but the smell of manure has made me forget most of them. I say we bid them farewell and leave them to their own devices!'

Rangers Put to Work
Penrod wants you to check in on some of the Rangers who are helping the Falcon-clan prepare for war and see how they are doing.
'Your Ranger friends are helping us prepare for war. You should check with them and see how they are doing.'

Halbarad, Radanir, and Braigiar can be found throughout Tûr Morva.
Penrod wants you to check on with members of the Grey Company helping the Falcon-clan prepare for war with Saruman.

'If it took only courage to win battles against Wizards, the Falcon-clan would have marched south, put Saruman in his place, and be on its way home already...but it is not enough.
'Tûr Morva must be made ready. Rhus prepares the leather that Taf will fashion into armour. Our Brenin's daughter, Mair, trains youthful fighters in the combat arts. Idele sees to the gathering of foodstuffs for the journey. All have their work, but still it will be a while before the Falcon can fly to war.
'With your help and the help of the Rangers, it will go more quickly.'

'The preparations have been coming along very well, ${PLAYER}. These Rangers are hard workers, but none more so than you, good ${RACE}!'
Penrod's approving laughter fades, and he becomes solemn once again.
'Lheu Brenin wishes to see you. The emissary from Isengard that he captured is giving the guards trouble.
'Go see the Brenin outside his home, up the hill to the south.'

'All of Tûr Morva is alive with the sound of work, ${PLAYER}. It is good. There are many clans siding with the Wizard in this conflict, and I feared the Falcon-clan would not be ready if it came to war with them. With your help and that of these Rangers, the Falcon can show its talons!'

Penrod has told you there is much work to do before the Falcon-clan can have much hope of standing against Saruman.
'Every man and woman of Tûr Morva has a job to do if the Falcon-clan is to stand against Saruman. Help them all with their tasks, and the preparations will go more quickly.'

'Lheu Brenin wishes to see you. The emissary from Isengard that he captured is giving the guards trouble.

'All of Tûr Morva is alive with the sound of work.'
'These Rangers are hardy folk. They are a great help to us.'

Lheu Brenin is outside his home, up the hill to the south of Penrod, in Tûr Morva.
Penrod has told you that the Brenin wants to see you concerning some trouble with the captive emissary of Isengard.

'You know of the emissary Saruman sent to us to force our cooperation? He is being kept under watch in the prison-cave. He has not told us anything of use yet, but perhaps you can inspire him to speak.
'Go into the prison-cave and speak to the guard Nai. He will allow you to press the captive for information. Return and tell me if the captive has anything useful to say. If he does not, perhaps his usefulness is at an end, and Nai can be given something else to do.
'The prison-caves are to the south. Follow the path and you will see the entrance among the ruins on your left-hand side, in the cliff.'
'You have the permission of the Brenin to speak with the prisoner? Very well. You may go in. He should pose you no danger. He knows that if he tries anything, he will do without meals.'

'What have you learned from our guest, ${PLAYER}?'
Lheu Brenin listens to your report of Dondhreg's words.
'There is truth there, I fear, if only a kernel. We must learn how large the kernel may be.'

'Have you come to gloat, ${RACE}? You are no Dunlending. Do not mistake these people for friends. It will be you in my place next! Mark what I say!'
Dondhreg glowers at you, his eyes full of hate.
'They cannot defeat Saruman. They are fools to try! The other clans are wiser and know which way the tide is going. Already, most of Dunland pledges their swords to my master. His armies come from Dunbog and Carreglyn and Starkmoor, and these unprepared fools will find themselves on the wrong side of the wave!
'It could have been different. I care not. It is enough to know that my captors will be slain by their own kinsmen soon enough, and you gloaters along with them!'

Book 4, Chapter 8: The Messenger of Isengard
Lheu Brenin wants you to speak with the emissary of Isengard he is holding captive in the cave behind Tûr Morva.
'You can go on in. He will not bite, if he knows what is good for him.'
'He is full of bluster, but I pay it no heed. We are out here, and he is in there.'

'Enter the prison-caves and speak with Nai. He will allow you to talk to the prisoner, and you may learn something of use to us. If not, well...it is of little account to me whether he lives or dies.
'The prison-caves are to the south. Follow the path and you will see the entrance among the ruins on your left-hand side, in the cliff.'
'You cannot stand against Saruman. Too many of the clans are already sworn to him. You have lost before you have begun.'

'You slew a good number of them, ${PLAYER}. For that, I am grateful. Your thirst for vengeance against the evils in this world is greater than my own.

'The man responsible for your friend's imprisonment is a soldier under my command... an over-privileged fool from a minor noble house of Edoras. It would not surprise me in the least if his family had unsavoury dealings with Isengard... and it happens that this man has volunteered to guard the prisoner today.
'I happen to know that this fellow is more fond of strong drink than is good for him. If he were to be swayed by such temptations during his watch, there is a danger that the Ranger would slip away.
'That would be most unfortunate, as dereliction of duty is a severe offence that carries a stiff punishment. In any case, I have little more to say on the matter. Good day, ${PLAYER}.'

'What is that? Ale? Bah, you will have no such luck, I am afraid. The Dunlendings raided our camp two nights ago and made a fierce fight of it. Only a few of our men were hurt, so it could have been worse, but the distraction of the attack bought their kin a few minutes to inflict some real hurt on us... they stole our entire supply of ale!
'I can tell you what that will do to morale around here unless we can get that ale back, but Grimbold will not let us send out men on a dangerous mission just to retrieve some casks. He says it is 'frivolous.'
'Bah! You would think he would know better after leading men of war for so many years.'

'What is this? Our dear lost casks... you are a fine ${RACE}, indeed!
'I have no means to thank you enough, but should you need a drink, I will make certain that you get your fill before the rest of these louts drain the ale dry.'

'No, I will not be dissuaded, Gríma. He is an old man and does not deserve this treatment at the hands of our master. If Saruman fears Gandalf plans to hatch an evil plot, keep him imprisoned, yes, but in comfortable quarters. The pinnacle is exposed to the elements. It is cruel treatment, not befitting Saruman the Wise.
'It is not our place to challenge Saruman's decisions, but I will do what I can to ease Gandalf's stay with us. An extra ration of bread will do no harm.
'There is no need to tell Saruman of this, of course.'
'Promise me that you will not tell our master about this. We have done nothing wrong, of course, but there is no sense in disturbing him. What is one more loaf of bread? No one will miss it.'
'They have been long in conversation, Gríma. What do you think they are speaking about?'

'Could you make any sense of that, Gríma? Our master holds you in closer confidence than he does me. Have you heard nothing of these matters?
'I need not be counted among the Wise to know that they have Radagast worried, and that gives me reason to worry as well!
'I am sure our master will know what must be done. That is why he is the Wizard, and we are the servants! We know our place, do we not? We do!'

'Gandalf seems much older than I remember from his last visit, older and weaker. Look at him there, then look at our master. See how Saruman's raiment glows! Gandalf's cloak seems so tattered.
'It is charitable of our master to offer his wisdom to the Grey Wizard. Perhaps he could offer some finer clothing, as well!'

'Our master was right, Gríma! The guards report that Gandalf was seen riding hard alongside the river, and now he is here! Radagast has done as he was asked!
'Let us go meet Gandalf and bring him to Orthanc!'
Gandalf's horse is tired from its long journey and will benefit from a stay in the stables with food and water.

Saruman listens as you breathlessly recount Acca's recent delivery of a loaf of bread to Gandalf, and their ensuing conversation. His face is a thundercloud.
'Why did you allow Acca to do this? Dog! What would you have done if he allowed Gandalf to come down? What would have been your answer if my worthless steward had freed him?'
Saruman masters his anger, but his tone is no less stern.
'From this point onward, none will climb the steps to the pinnacle save myself. I will have Acca thrown in the dungeons, where he will have time enough to consider this betrayal. He will have not even a crust to chew upon; let him eat slop instead.
'You will perform Acca's duties in his stead, until I have others for you. And I will, Gríma. Soon you will return to your homeland. But not yet.'

'It is done. Radagast will find Gandalf, if he is to be found, and I doubt not he will speed with all haste here to Isengard.
'There are some other small matters I need you to attend to before my guest arrives....'

Thak eyes you hungrily, confident that he has caught you doing something suspicious, so you appease him: you start talking.

'Don't tell him about this! I'm sorry, I didn't mean anything by it. Really! You don't need to trouble Morflak about this!'

'Thak gave you some trouble? Doesn't he know you're one of mine? I will have one of my boys take care of him. No one disrespects Morflak!'

'You have done as I asked! Good, good! I hope setting that black powder aflame will be the distraction that we need to make good our escape.'

'The guards do not bring us to work on the surface very often, but the last time that they did, I saw some of the great war-machines being constructed within the Ring. Book 4, Chapter 27: Repaying Treachery
You have escaped from Isengard with the help of Baldgar, but he did not survive. You should rejoin Théodred at his camp in the Gravenwood to decide what to do next.
Baldgar is dead. You should return to Théodred's camp in the Gravenwood to learn what has become of the Grey Company during your captivity.

'Not every member of the Falcon-clan agreed with Lheu Brenin's decision; those that did not were slain or forced to flee. One of those who escaped is the woman Seren, and it is from her that I have learned much of what befell within Tâl Methedras.
'I had been working closely with your friend Saeradan before you were captured, and he now burns with the desire to free what Rangers still live, if any do. He is very wise, and it seems if there is any hope of rescue he may be able to devise it. Speak with him on this account.
'You might also seek the advice of my trusted friend Hogawise. He excels in battle and has been a boon companion on this excursion into Gravenwood.'

'You must tell me of your time in Isengard, ${PLAYER}. It cannot have been pleasant, and you were often in my thoughts.
'I heard what happened within Tâl Methedras from Radanir. Some time after you were secreted away to Isengard, he managed to escape the prison-cave with poor Braigiar. The two of them fought their way into the centre of Tûr Morva, but then....'
Saeradan sighs heavily, and he seems in that moment much older than his years.
'Braigiar did not make it. They cut him down in the road, and only Radanir escaped. He has gone back with some of Théodred's men to try and recover Braigiar's body, but they have not returned.
'Many of our friends have fallen, and the rest are still captives of Lheu Brenin. According to Radanir, Halbarad and the sons of Elrond are still alive, but who can say for how long?'

'I cannot believe this! How can this have happened?'
The old woman is quivering with anger and grief.
'The Brenin called the heads of households to him, and declared that we were at last ready to reap our reward; we had only to bend the knee to Saruman. But Lheu Brenin himself had said to us the Hebog-lûth would not be the tool of some Wizard! He said it often, and loudly, and we came to believe it!
'I have no love for these Horse-lords, and this strutting princeling least of all, but what can be said? The honour of the Falcon-clan...sold to Saruman? Wulf sought his enemies in open battle! He was no Wizard's hireling!'
Seren chokes back angry tears.
'My boy Anirin has not returned yet from the lands of the Algraig, but his beloved spoke out against this treachery and is still a prisoner! What will I say to him if she dies?'

'There is no sense in delaying this any further. Your friends are held captive by our shared enemy. This enemy has a strong defensive position, but we have this advantage: we know where he is. Once the Falcon-clan leaves Tâl Methedras, that advantage dissipates. We must deal with them here, before they leave that valley.
'Once the Falcon-clan leaves the valley, my men and I must retreat to hold the Ford. The defence of Rohan is my main object. Until that time, I will help you free your friends.'

'We crossed the Ford of Isen in secret to learn what the Men of Dunland were up to, but it is worse than we suspected. I think it surprised the leader of the Falcon-clan, as well. It seems to me that he was biding his time until the victory of one side seemed assured. Then he needed to simply throw his lot in with the side likely to come out the victor.
'Let us hope that he is mistaken, ${PLAYER}. I think that he is undervaluing the prowess of the Men of Rohan. I would take ten Rohirrim on horseback over a thousand Dunlending wild men. I have spoken with your friend Saeradan, and it sounds like these Rangers are the same. The more of them we free now, the fewer thousands of Dunlendings I need concern myself with! Ha!'

'The Orcs seem to have quartered two groups of slaves separately down here. Most of the ones I've seen have been those wild men, the Dunlendings. I'm not sure where the Orcs have been getting them, but there's a lot of them down here.
'A couple of days ago, though, the Orcs started bringing in small groups of those horse-folk, the Rohirrim. They all looked pretty banged up, so I'm guessing they were captured in battle up above.
'Anyway, those folk don't seem to like each other much more than the Orcs, but if we're going to put an end to this, we'll need to get them to work together. If you can find out who is leading each group and talk to them, maybe you can convince them to put aside their differences and kill the Orcs instead of each other.'

'Who is there? A duvodiad? You wear no chains, yet you do not carry the mark of the White Hand either...who are you?'
'...'
'Ah, well, perhaps there is some spark of hope down here after all. Most of us were brought here after we were unable to pay levies for the war against the horse-lords or tried to escape conscription.
'Our own brenins betrayed us and sold us to these monsters. Now we find ourselves enslaved next to the very same demons who invaded our lands and brought this fate upon us. It is too much to bear... but at least they will suffer the same fate as we.'

'We have been betrayed enough already, ${PLAYER}. You may believe the horse-lords trustworthy, but we have fought them since the days before my father was born.
'You cannot trust them. Every time we have made some agreement with them, we have lost land, honour, or the lives of our finest warriors. We try to fight back, and they claim yet more land from us. Once all of the plains of the east were ours! But now... now we....'
Meriun pauses for a moment, struggling to regain his composure.
'What you suggest -- to die in battle, whether it be at the hands of the vile Orcs or the cursed forgoil, that would still be better than to starve and die grubbing through the rock like a blind worm.
'If you can convince the horse-lords to fight off the Orcs -- rather than stabbing us in the back -- then I will convince the others to ready themselves.'

'Who are you, ${RACE}? One of Saruman's lackeys?'
'...'
'I see. Well, you would do best to keep hidden down here. If the Orcs catch you, you will be in here with the rest of us... or more likely dead.
'Most of us were captured two days ago when our band was ambushed by Orcs as we were returning to the Ford. Now we are being forced to work the mines alongside the Dunlendings... those fools sided with the Orcs and have found their reward down here as slaves.
'It serves them right, I suppose, but that does not help us any. I do not think any of us are going to survive very long down here....'

'You have a plan to help us escape, but you would have us fight alongside the wild men? Such an outlook may serve you well in polite company, but I think you give these barbarians far too much credit.
'They fight bravely enough, but they know nothing of honour or justice. These are men whose own lords sold them into slavery, and you believe we can trust them to stand by us in battle? More than likely, they will try to bargain away our lives in return for their own freedom.
'But I see your point... we will die down here soon enough whether or not we are betrayed. If you can convince them to go along with this plan, then I will vouch for our cooperation if we can find some way to fight our way out of here.'

'Thank you, ${PLAYER}. This... this was a terrible thing that happened. We must move forward... and I hope we can have revenge as we take our next steps!

'There... did you hear that, ${PLAYER}? Those blasts you're hearing in the distance... it sounds like thunder down here, but it's actually one of those fool goblins playing with something new and dangerous.
'It sounds like something that mad, old Wizard up in the Shire might have cooked up, but I don't think he would be sharing it with the goblins. No, I'd wager Saruman is behind this devilry somehow. Anyway, goblins are nasty enough with their usual toys... I don't relish fighting them armed with whatever that is.
'Let us see if we can dissuade them from using it any more....'

'There is something dreadfully unsettling about a creature too stupid to know that the weapon it's holding is as likely to kill it as the person it's fighting. I just wish it made them easier to fight, but that kind of madness is hard to counter.

'What an incredible act of kindness. Thank you, ${PLAYER}. Not many would choose the path you followed. You are a shining example to us all.

'There is something strange here, ${PLAYER}. While you were gone, one of my men and a few of the Dunlendings were taken away... not by the Orcs, but by a Man.
'He wore strange raiments, marking him as a person of some station, but I do not know whom he served. He was looking for the strongest and healthiest of the men among us. For what purpose, I do not know.
'They were taken away to the north, and the Orcs laughed cruelly as they left. You must find out where they were taken... and what fate could possibly be worse than to die in this dark pit.'
The prisoner seems to slip in and out of a daze as you cut him free, but he quickly recovers his senses once the bonds are removed.

'Good. I do not know whether they have escaped the cave or gone into hiding awaiting our own attempt, but either way we are now ready to make our escape.
'We will talk with them later and see if we can determine what this Golvorn was up to, and whether he was truly in league with the Wizard Saruman.'

'Interesting. It seems that my servants have not been thorough enough in securing the slaves of late.
'No matter, you have already saved me the trouble of sending them to hunt you down. But wait, you do not have the bearing of one who seeks escape. You have come to fight... me?
'Truly? Well then, I imagine you will make a fine specimen for Saruman's experiments. I shall have to take care not to injure you too severely!'

'You are a duvodiad here... you do not belong here any more than I do. Among the vales and cairns of the Bonevales, a clan has long dwelled. This clan called the Dievlig -- Accursed in the Westron -- are Oathbreakers and were driven into the Bonevales as punishment.
'Recently, strange occurrences and evil rumblings have been heard from the cairns that have long laid dormant. Will you search for signs that might explain what is happening here?
'Journey west from here and see what you can find. When you have found the signs I seek, you should find my friend, Caron, and deliver the evidence to him. I last saw him heading west through the valley.'

'Ah, it appears, ${PLAYER}, that we have another duvodiad in our lands. In these troubled times, sadly, outsiders seem to be the people who are the most willing to give aid.

Recently, there have been rumours of strange occurrences in the Bonevales, which have brought Bledhun into the ancient burial grounds.

'Recently, a large army was gathered within the Bonevales, poised to attack the Algraig clans of Enedwaith. However, Yorath, a great Brenin among the clans, summoned the warriors south to Wulf's Cleft to ready an attack against the accursed strawheads.
'Following the withdrawal of the forces, Trehéarn, Brenin of the Dievlig, began attacking all those who would assist outsiders like yourself. My band was scattered throughout the valley.
'Will you seek out those who survived the attack and assist them if possible? Travel east and look among the rocks and hills for my companions. When you have found them, return to Bledhun and let him know we are safe.'
'I am glad to hear that some of our band survived the Dievlig's brutal attack. I swear that the treachery of the Dievlig shall not go unpunished.'

'Caron sent you? Then we shall speak.
'We had a peaceful arrangement with the Dievlig at one time. We would bring them goods, and they would allow us to pass unimpeded northwards. Ever since the warriors marched to Wulf's Cleft, the Dievlig have become increasingly hostile to those they saw as duvodiad -- outsiders.
'They attacked our band, and we were taken unaware...only a small number of us survived.'

'Caron sent you to find me?
'I do not understand what has happened. Will you please let any of my companions you come across know that I escaped the Dievlig's attack unscathed?
'Thank you, Duvodiad.'

'I do not have anything left, I swear! The raiders before you took it all, please do not hurt me! Wait... you do not have the look of rival clansmen.
'My name is Andras. I was taking this caravan to Avardin for the upcoming auction when I was beset by the Dragon-clan. They are an evil lot, and I suspect they answer to Isengard. Saruman is not the friend that he claims to be. There are few who can see through his tangled web of lies, and my clan, the People of the Ox, least of all, it seems. I seek to change that, but to do so, I must be in a position of power. Among the Ox-clan merchants that means money, which I had hoped to raise at the coming auction.
'Please, I ask your help. I have not yet had time to assess the damage to my caravan. If you could check my cart and goods, then venture out against the raiders, I would be grateful. They came from the hill to the east.'
'It is a strange day when a duvodiad has more kindness than clansmen you have known your entire life. A very strange day, indeed.'

'Will you attempt to recover the sigils from the dunlendings atop the hill? If so, journey south and up the hill. The scouts will be the ones carrying the sigils.'
'You have done me a great service, Duvodiad. The cowards will not sully the memory of those who stood beside me in honour.'

'Among the cairns to the south-west, the bodies of those that have long lain in eternal rest have begun to stir and rise up from their graves. I would know what evil causes this to happen.
'Perhaps if you examined the cairn-entrances, you might find some evidence of the power behind this abomination. Will you do this for me?
'Journey south and then west through the valley. There, you should find the cairns.'

'When the wights first emerged from their graves, I had hoped someone had simply crept into their cairns and removed their bodies.
'However, it appears as if these cairns were disturbed from the inside. I fear what this might mean for the interred.'
Examine cairn-entrances (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Bledhun at his encampment in the Bonevales
Resting Place
The resting places of the honoured dead in the Bonevales have been defiled in some manner, causing the Dead to rise.
'Have you examined the entrances to the cairns yet?'

The cairn-entrances lie to the south and west of Bledhun's camp.
Bledhun has asked you to examine the entrances of the cairns to see if you can discern what power is behind the raising of the wights.

'Within the past moon, our ancestors have begun to rise from their resting places here in the Bonevales. These once-great heroes' bodies have been twisted and corrupted and attack those who still draw breath.
'If you journey south and west into the valley, you will come across these terrible wights. Defeat them, if you would, for such an abomination should not be permitted to continue.'
'Unlike the Lich Bluffs to the north, this place has always remained undisturbed, until now. We must discover what has caused the wights to walk among us.'

This hastily scribbled note reads:
'To those who remain, I wish you the best. For the past months and days, there have been grim portents of what is to come. Shadows are falling all around us, and we fear what may come. The cairns stir for the first time in this place.'

'I am relieved to hear that more survived the attack than I first thought, but I fear what is to become of this place.'

This sword bears a striking similarity to those that the Dievlig wield.

'I fear this bodes ill for us, Duvodiad. It appears as if there are some among the Dievlig who have been complicit in raising the wights from their graves.

'You have done much good work to help me, and I am very grateful for that, but I fear the most difficult parts are still ahead of us. Bedwur is the auctioneer here... he is the local leader of the Ox-clan, and a very powerful man. He is also as corrupt as they come, having long ago given his will to Saruman.
'Unfortunately, he is an evil I must deal with if I am to pay off my debts. Any transaction of noticeable size must go through his auction, and he happily takes a price from each lot.
'I need some time to take inventory and get everything cleaned and ready for sale. While I do that, you go talk with Bedwur and secure a position in the upcoming auction. You can find him near the centre of town by the auction-platform.'
'So, you represent Andras, do you, duvodiad? I hope he has brought something worth selling this time. I do not tolerate my time being spent and my money wasted.'
Talk to Bedwur in Avardin
The Auctioneer
Avardin is run by Bedwur, a leader among the Ox-clan who runs the auctions and controls the local economy.
'Bedwur will likely ask you to do some small tasks. I would be grateful if you could, while I prepare things here.'

Bedwur is in the centre of Avardin at the auction-platform.
Andras asked you to speak with Bedwur regarding the auction.
Defeated Wargs at the Hound's Rest (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'You are preparing an auction? Yes, I am interested. I am in need of cattle, for I sold my last ones to the war-effort. I made a decent profit, but I fear I sold too many. The Warg-packs to the east devoured the few I had left.
'I am willing to buy more, but not until I know my investment is safe and secure. If you were to head into the hills east of here, to the rock the Wargs call home, and thin their numbers, I will consider coming to the auction to buy cattle.'
'I can tell from the stench upon you that you have been fighting Wargs, and given that you are standing here, I assume you were victorious. I will attend the auction.'
Defeat Wargs at the Hound's Rest (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

The Wargs to the east have devastated the local cattle population, and Folant seeks to rectify the Warg-problem before he will attend the auction.
'The Wargs are not good for business. I will not attend while there are so many wandering the hills.'

Wargs can be found to the east of Avardin in the Starkmoor.
You should go to Hound's Rest and defeat Wargs.

'You are looking for more sellers for the auction? I have a necklace which I am nearly done with and almost ready to sell. It is crafted of Warg-teeth. Dunlendings who wear them are powerful and demand respect from all around them, whether they retrieved the teeth themselves or not.
'There is one last tooth which I need to finish this necklace, then it will be ready for sale. On the rock to the east is a powerful Warg, larger than the rest, called Hormgrat. His tooth shall be the centrepiece of this necklace. Bring it to me, and I shall sell in your auction.'
'With this, my necklace will be noticed by everyone. You will command respect and power when you wear it. I will come to your auction.'
Collect Hormgrat's tooth
Bring Hormgrat's tooth to Cadvan

Warg-teeth necklaces are highly valued as a symbol of strength in battle and power among the Dunlending clans.
'No other tooth shall do. It must be that of the most powerful Warg on the rock. With that, I can command any price I wish.'

Hormgrat can be found at the Hound's Rest to the east of Avardin.
Cadvan asked you to get him a tooth from the most powerful Warg on the rock to the east.

'Herding is the fastest way to make money here in Avardin, presuming you have the right connexions and enough money to start with. The clan tightly controls who can have cattle and how many. There are tags that are sold and attached to the animals. If any animal is found without a tag, it is brought to auction, and Bedwur keeps whatever the profit is. He is also the one who sells the tags.
'I had a herd of cattle that strayed too far to the east, and many were devoured by the Wargs. I have sold the herdsmen to the mines to regain some of my losses, but now I need enough to get started again. If you can get me the tags from my dead cattle, I will sell them at auction. They can be found around the rock to the east.'
'Yes, these were indeed mine. They should bring a good price. I will attend your auction.'
Collect cattle-tags (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

Due to limited grazing grounds, cattle are a controlled and regulated resource.
'Those tags are often worth more than the cattle that they are placed upon.'

'An auction, you say? I wish to trade cattle. I have saved enough to buy many tags, and my uncle is willing to give me several head from his herd. I have the land for them to graze on, but not the means to keep them safe.
'If you are venturing to the great rock to the east, you will find several smaller stones around it. With enough of them, I could build an enclosure around my land to keep my cattle safe. If you bring me the stones, I will attend the auction.'
'With these, I can make an enclosure that will keep my livestock safe. I will attend your auction.'

'I am more than willing to help out; however, auctions are very time-consuming, and I have a reputation to maintain. I need assurances that there will be enough merchants in attendance to make it worth my time.

'Saruman cheated me out of much money with this last auction. You cannot go against the Wizard... once he names his price, the purchase is finished, whether it is fair or not. At the end of the day, however, I will always get paid.
'The goods he purchased are travelling by caravan south to Wulf's Cleft. I do not know whether they plan to stay there or head further to Isengard, but I do know they will not make it. You will intercept them before they reach the camp.
'Head south and follow the road. When you find them, be quick about it. They are evil men and do not deserve any quarter. Bring back the goods you find there. Once this is done, there is only one more task I will require of you before the boy will be considered free of his debt.'
'Very good! It appears that my goods survived both the trip and the battle in good condition. With these returned, I can now obtain the profit that Saruman denied me.'

Bedwur is feeling cheated by Saruman the White and wishes some retribution.

'There is one last thing you must do for me, then I will consider Mabon's debt paid, and he will be free. If you fail me now, I will sell the boy off to the mines.
'To the south of Starkmoor is Wulf's Cleft. The armies of Dunland have been gathering and training there. I often sell them weapons, armour, and slaves for training practice. Lately, the sales have been slowing. You are going to fix that for me.
'There is a cliff to the south that overlooks Wulf's Cleft. Once there, I want you to do as much injury as possible. The more weapons and armour you destroy, the more I can sell the warriors tomorrow. Speak with me when you are ready to go, and I will show you the path.'
'You are looking for Mabon? I do not know where he went, but I have my suspicions.'

'Make sure you do as much damage as possible. I have a fresh set of conscripts and weapons ready to sell.'

'Mabon is not the first child to disappear from these lands. For the past several months, nearly one vanishes per week from Avardin, mostly orphans. They disappear in the night...naught but a few tracks heading to the south-west are ever seen.
'Those who have caught a glimpse tell of a horrible creature, an abomination of nature, striding across the plains with a bag over his shoulder, filled with lost children.
'If you wish to find this boy you must venture to the swamps. Head south-west along the roads until you find Dunbog. They may know more of this abomination there.'
'What do you want here?'

Dunbog is an untamed swamp to the south-west of Avardin. Few live there by choice.

'If we are to recover anything from the homestead, we must move quickly. A group of Dragon-clan raiders just passed by here. They must have copied down some of the items from the ledger before you recovered all of the pages.

'You see, we have a draught we give to the trees when they become upset. It slows them down, makes them more tree-like, less dangerous. So if the Wise are to be believed, and trolls are just a bit Entish, then perhaps it would work on them?'

'${PLAYER}, I have heard many dark tidings regarding the purposes and plans of Saruman the White. Long has he been a friend to the Rohirrim -- and even now he holds much sway in the Golden Hall -- but I cannot allay my fears any longer.
'If Saruman has indeed turned against us and allies himself with the likes of the Dunlendings, and even Orcs and goblins, then we must know. Yet I am bound by the strict command of Théoden King not to trespass upon the Vale of Nan Curunír to the North, where lies Isengard.
'Will you go in our stead and learn of the purpose and strength of Saruman, that we may know the depths of his treachery before it is too late? I think you will find a friend near the valley....'

'Well met again, ${PLAYER}, and a wonder it is to see you here after so long a road. Alas, many of my kinsmen have not made it this far. I have not heard from Braigiar since his start into the Gravenwood and young Amarion failed to return from scouting shortly thereafter... I know not their fates.
'Yet I dare not dwell on such matters, though this journey has left me all but empty, for I have yet to complete my task.
'We find ourselves now before Nan Curunír, and beyond in the tower of Orthanc sits Saruman the Traitor. Looking across the destruction wrought in this vale, it seems clear now that his wisdom has faded, to be replaced by madness. You should make yourself familiar with the land, my friend, for if we are to find our way to Isengard, we must learn its lay ere we are discovered.'

'So, now you have seen some small part of Nan Curunír.
'Among the western hills, a great infestation of goblins and Wargs has taken root. Across the river to the east, an encampment of Orcs -- Uruk-hai this tribe is called. They are strong and do not fear the sun. To the north lies Isengard itself.
'We must proceed carefully, for there are enemies all around us.'

'Grimbold's emissary will arrive shortly. You must escort him to the gates of Isengard and ensure that no ill befalls him there. Perhaps we shall have some answers as to the full extent of Saruman's treachery at last.

'Such is the influence of Saruman's voice upon the unwary. Even now, I find myself wishing to believe the truth of what he said, though I need but look around myself to see his dark intent.
'I do not know what words Ordwaer will return with, but I fear it will only serve to confuse matters further for Théodred and Grimbold as they weigh their next choice.'

'Saruman is growing in power by the day. The clans here have all fallen to him and soon they will be forced to march to war for him. They will be slaughtered in the plains of Rohan for no reward, while the Wizard reaps all the benefit.
'My clan, the Boar-clan, has done all it can to stand against him, but our efforts have not yielded any true victory. We simply do not have the power to stand against him, but I believe I have found a way. In the hills to the north, past the borders of our lands and into the forests of Thrór's Coomb, I found a weapon. It is ancient and powerful. If there are more to be found, then we might be able to stand against the Wizard.
'However, I do not know where to look for more such weapons -- there were no others in the area around this one. Seek out Frithgeir the Dwarf at Zudrugund and learn whether he can help us. He has been sympathetic to our cause in the past.'
'A powerful and ancient weapon, you say, found here in the hills of Thrór's Coomb, which is to be used to stand against the Wizard Saruman? I may indeed be able to help you.'
Talk to Frithgeir at Zudrugund
There is Gold in the Hills
There are tales of powerful weapons and armour in the hills of Enedwaith that might prove to be useful in the battles to come.
'If we can find more of these weapons, we can make an earnest stand against Saruman of Many Colours.'

Frithgeir is at Zudrugund in Thror's Coomb in Enedwaith.
Ariene found a powerful weapon in the hills of Enedwaith and believes Frithgeir may know where to find more.

'Word has come to us that Saruman has taken an interest in legendary weapons for his own armies and has built a great forge full of Orc-slaves for the creation of this dangerous supply.
'He must be stopped! Will you sneak into the forges and defeat his smiths and slave-drivers?'
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTE: This is a solo quest and cannot be completed in a fellowship.</rgb>

'Ah! I am glad to see you whole, ${PLAYER}. Saruman is dangerous enough by himself... but I shudder to think what he would be like towering above a great army of strong Orcs and uruks, each wielding a weapon of superior make.'
Investigate the Forges of Isengard

Saruman is devising his own legendary items to supply his war-efforts. His forges must be shut down.
'Are you ready to travel to the forges of Saruman? It will be dangerous, but I know that you are a great warrior.'

'The past few months, during the night, the Draig-lûth have been hauling bags and crates through the forests of Thrór's Coomb. The weapon you told me about must have fallen out of them.
'I have not yet been able to determine where they are taking their goods, though. I have watched them wander the hills, criss-crossing back and forth, looking or searching for something as they go. I wonder if they do not know where they are going either.
'Head down into the hills and forest below and see if you can find the Draig-lûth. Perhaps one of them may have a map that shows where they're going or will give us a sign to pursue.'

'I do not know what this means. It's indecipherable to me. Nothing more than scribbles and nonsense. These symbols here -- a fish and a volcano -- seem to refer to things that aren't even in Enedwaith let alone Thrór's Coomb.
'Perhaps Nár will be able to tell us more, presuming he is lucid. I suppose there's nothing to lose. Bring it down and show it to him, and let's see what he says.'
'Fire burns over a sea of gold beneath the rising sun. Teeth, scales, claws... ripping... rending... tearing....'
'If this is what he said and wrote, Nár must not have been having one of his lucid moments. This makes almost less sense to me than what we started with. Allow me to think for a moment.'

The Draig-lûth have been hauling treasure into hills of Thrór's Coomb.
'If we don't know where they're going with those bags and chests, we can't do anything.'
'I cannot make heads nor tails of this map. We have no choice but to see if Nár can be helpful.'
'Teeth, tails, claws, scales... and fire... terrible, roaring fire.'

The Draig-lûth can be found in Thrór's Coomb in Enedwaith.
Frithgeir asked you to search the Draig-lûth in Thrór's Coomb to see if you can find a map indicating where they are taking their treasure.

Frithgeir is at Zudrugund in Thrór's Coomb in Enedwaith.
The map is full of scribbles and nonsense. Perhaps Frithgeir will be able to help you decipher it.

Frithgeir examined the map and found nothing he could decipher. He suggested you bring it down to Nár in the library and see if he could make anything of it.

Frithgeir is at Zudrugund in Thrór's Coomb in Enedwaith.
Nár mumbled what seemed to be a bunch of nonsense while scribbling on the map. Hopefully, Frithgeir can help to translate the mad dwarf's ramblings.

'I have spent some time thinking about what Nár said and examining the map and his changes to it. I have come up with a theory by breaking down Nár's ramblings.
'In the eastern part of Thrór's Comb is a cave. The sea of gold speaks of the treasure the Draig-lûth is bringing there. Around the cave entrance you will often see drakes sunning during the day. I believe they are the teeth and scales he refers to. The fire must be part of an offering the clan makes to the dragons they worship.
'Head into the eastern hills of Thrór's Coomb and seek out this cave. If you find it, venture within and see if you find the weapons and armour you seek. If not, we can do nothing more for you. Be wary... I doubt the Draig-lûth will give up their treasures willingly.'

The cave entrance is believed to be in the eastern hills of Thrór's Coomb in Enedwaith.
Frithgeir has translated Nár's ramblings and believes they refer to a drake-guarded cave.

'Recently, Cadthorn, one of our messengers, failed to report back. He is a capable courier that had gone to receive word from Edoras regarding our strategic goals for Forthbrond.
'Will you set forth and discover Cadthorn's location?
'Begin your search to the north and slightly west from here along the cliff walls. Surely, he has set forth from Edoras already.'

'The messages that Cadthorn bore were of import, but this edict from Edoras was the word that we sought. It shall be known among the captains.
'Thank you for bringing us this news.'

'I was unexpectedly attacked by Orcs and their ilk. They ambushed my party and stole a satchel that bore important messages for Forthbrond. Many of my companions fell, and I barely escaped with my life.
'I was given word to bring to Grimbold and his captains: Théoden King has commanded that Isengard is to be called friend, and any reports to the contrary should come only from his son, Théodred.'

'Could you ask around, please? Please, please, please! Maybe one of the other children took it. I know Myve was looking at it quite a lot when my father first gave it to me....'

'So you come seeking to reclaim the palantír? I knew someone would be back for it; yes, it was my craban that brought it to me!
'But hearken: a palantír is no toy for a child.
'I am Rook, an apprentice Wizard. You should leave this dangerous object in my capable hands for the time being.'
'Envus is missing that silly shiny ball? Sure I looked at it, but I did not take it. What would I do with a ball like that? I want to play with spears, not useless, shiny toys.'

'I heard you mention Envus' missing toy -- a shiny ball, you say? I think I saw a crow taking off with just such a ball last night.
'It is strange, I know, but there could be no mistake. It was a black bird flying off with a shiny object clutched in its talons, heading north-west.'

'What qualifies me to be an apprentice Wizard, you ask? I studied long under Saruman the White as his servant and caregiver to his flocks of crebain. I watched him closely, then stole away one night to pursue my own lofty dreams!
'And now here I am, a Wizard in the making. I shall soon be the great Wizard of Dunland! But first, I need a Ring of Power.
'I learned much in Isengard about the Great Rings, and I must have one of my own if I am to be respectable in this profession.'

'A Great Ring! I can feel the power surging from it. It is a wonder you did not keep it for yourself -- but ah, you are wise. You know that you are too weak-minded to bear such a heavy burden.
'Yes, it is best to leave such things to the great Men, like myself. How did you come by this, ${PLAYER}? Does it not look marvellous upon my finger?'

A Ring of Power?
The master of the crows seems to believe himself to be a Wizard in the making and requests a Ring of Power to help him achieve his great ends.

'Have you found a Ring of Power? No? You are not searching hard enough. I would like to have one by nightfall, but it is my understanding that they are very difficult to come by. It may take you all day!'

'It seems not long ago that you stood there before me asking me how you get your hand on an Orc-cleaver like mine; all wide-eyed and timid in awe of this incredible specimen. Now look at you, a veteran in your own right, capable of standing with me - well, near me anyway, as I look down from on high at all the other new recruits looking to make their mark here in the Ettenmoors.
'You were scared like they are; we were all scared, but that doesn't mean we are cowards. We can face down the Orcs, and the spiders, and Wargs, and even the uruks, we can take them and now you can look good killing them.
'The Captain-Generals have seen fit to make some new cloaks for you all. All you need to do is choose and the cloak is yours. The Captain-Generals have limited the supply and I cannot hand too many out, so you should act quickly.'
'Looks like you have come back to make a decision. So, what is it going to be?'
Speak to Ash at Glân Vraig
You must choose your reward before 11/1/11

'I am well on my way to being as great as Saruman, ${PLAYER}, but there is something more I would ask of you. As I observed my master of old, I saw that his robes appeared white, but shimmered with many subtle hues.
'I am quite certain that the subtle colours help to infuse the power that the lord of Isengard possesses. I need an iridescent cloak! With such a garment, I too shall be powerful beyond belief!
'I do not care how you find it, but I want a many-hued cloak.'

'Ah! Look how it glistens! Now black... now green... now violet. Incredible, ${PLAYER}. It looks like the plumage on my dear craban-friends.

'Ha! Perfect, ${PLAYER}, and excellent timing, for I was beginning to grow impatient.

'A week ago, I had a fully running stable here. You may have noticed that we do not have any horses here anymore. I suppose that is well because I do not have anything to feed them. I also do not have anyone to take care of them.
'My stable-boy left, because his father was taken to Wulf's Cleft to serve the army. The boy ran off to work the fields and scavenge the Moor to provide for his mother and siblings. Had he stopped and talked to me, I would have helped however I could.
'I believe the boy is here in Avardin. Please find him and let him know that I will provide for his family. Once he returns, we can work on the rest of the stable.'
'Levelha says he will pay me enough to take care of mam and my brothers and sisters? Of course, I will go back then. I should have asked him to begin with.'
'With the boy returning, I can now turn my attention to the stable.'

'A traveller wishes to gain access to Galtrev? Tell me, why should the White Hand wave you into Saruman's most productive new village?
'Galtrev is home to many wonders and conveniences that cannot be found anywhere else in Dunland, but only labourers and workers and close allies of Saruman may come here now!
'If you enter, you are to find work immediately. Travellers will find no easy accommodations here; report instead to each of the overseers in town. The supply lines are blocked, our shipment is late, and I will not answer for the failures of my inferiors!'

'A recruit for the labour force? I don't like the looks of you, but we will take what allies we can. The White Hand does not discriminate!
'This is my work area here -- staffed by incompetent mongrels, as you can see.
'If you want to work for me, I'll have you know that I am completely blocked by the second Overseer. His supply line has been held up all day, and I can't make any progress without him! Go find out what's keeping that shipment, and be quick about it!'

'Who do you think you are, bullying me about my shipment schedule? The insolence of some folk these days... the third station hasn't sent over anything today, and we can't even get started.
'If you want to make yourself useful, go find out what is holding them up.'

'Are you questioning me? Who are you, anyway? I haven't seen you around these parts, and you don't look like one of the clansmen.
'Whoever you are, you can tell the gate-keepers that we will have their shipment ready, if the fourth station ever comes through with their promises. I don't know what those sluggards are about, making us wait so long!'

'I know everything is held up; you don't have to remind me, whoever-you-are! These lazy fools who work for me here can't seem to do anything right, and I can't punish them fast enough to fix matters.
'I don't know why our great lord would wish to ally himself with such feeble, incompetent folk. They would be more useful as food for the uruks than as suppliers and warriors.
'It looks like you have just volunteered to flog these useless mules until the supply lines are running smoothly again!'

Galtrev: The Capital Settlement
You have ventured into Galtrev, the capital settlement of Dunland in Pren Gwydh. It would appear that the White Hand currently governs this expansive village.
'If you are as lazy as the rest of this rabble, you will fit right in, stranger. Go find out where the supply lines are blocked, and be quick about it!'

The White Hand Overseers can be found in the lower areas of Galtrev, guarding their four respective posts.
You should speak with White Hand Overseer at the west gate to see if he needs your help.

Flint Ironheart, the Overseer at the fourth workstation, seems to be at the root of the delay in the day's productivity.
You should speak with Flint Ironheart and find out if there is anything you can do to help.
The servant of Saruman is better pleased with the day's progress

'If the guards sent you here to join the labour force, then you have come to the right place. We are hopelessly behind, as you see, and blocking the entire day's supply chain.
'Here is your first task: go flog, beat, and torture the workers until they are productive again. I want them working twice as fast! I want them doubling their production! If they still don't work, kill them, and take their place!
'If you can manage to get them working today, you will likely be welcome to come and go from Galtrev as often as you like.'
'What a relief it is to have such a kindly traveller in Galtrev! Flint Ironheart is finally distracted; perhaps now I can rest.'

'You're not so bad, ${PLAYER}. Has anyone ever told you that before? When I whip those sluggards, I could swear they are even less productive than before.
'Someday you should show me your flogging techniques. They seem to be most effective!
'Well, get moving! Find more work, so I can finally finish that nap....'

It appears that the overworked townsfolk who labour to fill the White Hand's shipments are behind in their duties and attracting unwanted attentions from the White Hand Overseers.

'${PLAYER}, my friend, you have the look of one who is growing ready to leave. I want to thank you for all that you have done.
'Galtrev is the largest village in Dunland, and it is not far to the south of here in Pren Gwydh. Surely you will want to stop there as you make your way through Dunland.
'You are welcome back any time.'

'What do you want here, stranger? Why should the White Hand grant you admittance?
'I'm not sure I like the way you're looking at me, ${RACE}.'
Gain admittance to the village of Galtrev in Pren Gwydh
From the Bonevales to Galtrev
Galtrev, the largest village of Dunland, is in Pren Gwydh to the south of the Bonevales.
'You will find Galtrev if you take the road south. Make sure you come back to visit, if you can! You will be missed by all here, ${PLAYER}.'

Galtrev, the main village of Pren Gwydh, can be found by taking the road south from the Bonevales.
You should go to Galtrev as you make your way through Dunland.

'So you leave us to make for Trum Dreng? I know little of that land, but I hear that it is mostly uninhabited. But if you wish to explore it, that is up to you, of course.
'You can find it by travelling south through the Mournshaws of Enedwaith, though there may be other paths with which I am unfamiliar. It is a stark land in the north-west of Dunland.'
'Thank you for helping our huntress, kind duvodiad!'
Find someone in Trum Dreng who will welcome you, and help them

Trum Dreng is in the north-west of Dunland, below the Mournshaws.
'You can reach Trum Dreng by travelling south through the Mournshaws in Enedwaith, ${PLAYER}.'
'I am sorry, traveller, but our town is not open to Duvodiads. We do not trust strangers here. You should head north along the road to get back to lands that may welcome you better.'

Trum Dreng can be found by travelling south through the Mournshaws. It is in the north-west corner of Dunland, directly west of the Bonevales.
You should visit Trum Dreng in your travels through Dunland and help whoever is willing to talk to you there.

'Hey there, ${PLAYER}! Have you come to take part in Sandson's Egg Scramble? Well here are the rules: Just remain in the chicken yard here. When the event begins, Sandson's finest chickens will come out of their coops and start laying eggs! They tend to become a bit perturbed what with all the folk about, so they'll run about a lot, and things can get a bit confusing.
'If you can collect five white eggs before I call time, you'll win a bonus in Faire tokens! Also, opening the eggs will also grant additional tokens whether you win or lose.
'Oh, I should mention that some mischief-maker seems to have slipped some unusual ingredients into the chickens' feed, and we've been getting some rather, er, unusual eggs now and again. Seems that there are collectors that value them though, so while they won't count towards the Egg Scramble, you may want to grab them nonetheless.'

'You've got quick feet and steady hands, ${PLAYER}! Congratulations on winning Sandson's Egg Scramble!

'We have come to the cross-roads, ${PLAYER}, and sooner than I expected. I want to help the Prince of Rohan, for without his aid and that of his doughty warriors, my men and I would still be captives of the Falcon-clan. But we cannot abandon our journey; our duty lies with Aragorn, and we must find him in Rohan or die searching. We cannot stay to help Théodred with his battles.
'I want you to go with the prince, ${PLAYER}. I want you to lend him your strength and your wisdom and your courage. You can travel south more swiftly than we can; even hale and hearty, our diminished number would take some time to make ready, and we are wounded and tired.
'Make your farewells with my kin, ${PLAYER}. I know they will want to say good-bye. Saeradan is there, by the fire. He knows what I have in mind, though the others may not.'

'Halbarad told me his decision, and I will not speak against it. But I will miss you, ${PLAYER}, and I wish you might still travel with us. I know Erebrandir feels the same way! He has not forgotten the farrier who crafted him a new shoe in Hollin, nor the ${RACE} who saved the farrier.
'You have a skill beyond strength of arms or the reach of knowledge, ${PLAYER}. You find friends wherever you tread, and where they cannot be found you make them with kindness and generosity. Halbarad does not realize how close he came to spending the rest of his days in the prison-caves of Tûr Morva, but I do.
'Consider this, my friend, and do not forget it: Prince Théodred was at this camp for days before you escaped from Isengard and held council with me. But he did not move to rescue my kin until he spoke with you. Nay, do not console me! I am not ashamed. Your ability to rally people to your side is yours alone, and it is a power you must not forget. It has saved many lives already, and I know it will again.'
Talk to Saeradan by the fire at the camp in the Gravenwood

'You are leaving us now? How can this be Halbarad's decision?'
Corunir stares at his feet for a short moment before he meets your gaze again.
'I suppose the Prince of Rohan has need of you. I cannot blame Halbarad for wanting you to help hold the fords of the Isen. I think your tale of the army Saruman is preparing within Isengard shook him deeply, and if that crossing is lost then the kingdom of Rohan will surely follow.
'We have been through a great deal, ${PLAYER}, have we not? It seemed we would stay within the musty library of Zudrugund with Nár and Frithgeir for the rest of our days, did it not? Even thinking now of climbing up to Nár's Peak makes my legs ache. I want you to have these spare boots of mine, in memory of our time spent in that high place.'

'I am worried about Golodir, ${PLAYER}. He endured much in the depths of Carn Dûm, as you know, and he will never truly forgive himself for Lorniel's death, but this journey has done much to relieve some of his hurts. I think it is simply this: he has a purpose again. There is work to be done, and until we find Aragorn, as we are sworn to do, it remains unfinished.
'But our captivity in the prison-caves changed something within Golodir. There is a dangerous glimmer in his eye that I have not seen before. It worries me, ${PLAYER}. I am afraid for him.
'We were speaking not long ago, just to the west, but my heart was troubled, and I left him there. Will you seek him out and see if my worries are for naught? I hope they are. My mother always said I worried enough for the whole family, but the dangers through which we have come and to which we ride deserve even more worry than I can manage.'

'You are leaving us, ${PLAYER}? It may be Halbarad's decision, but I would not leave, even if he ordered me home again.'
He looks up at you, and you do see a hint of the hardness in his eyes that so upset Corunir.
'There are matters still left undone here. The cowards who slink in the caves beneath Tâl Methedras still live, ${PLAYER}. They spoke to us as friends, gave us shelter, took the sweat from our brows, and repaid us with treachery. I will repay them in kind. My lost brethren and my lost friends demand this of me.
'Lheu Brenin? You jest, ${PLAYER}. He is a fat man whose courage depends on a hundred of his people at his back. I have faced the evil of Mordirith...he is gone, and I still live. Lheu Brenin is nothing compared to Mordirith.'

'Neither of those forces must cross the river Isen.'
Calenglad's bleak expression is lightened by a wry smile.
'You should say good-bye to Radanir. If you do not, we would never hear the end of it. He is east of here, I believe, on the path.'

'Sit with me a moment, ${PLAYER}. I know you are leaving us, and that Théodred has need of you at the Ford. That is the way of it, is it not? We go where we are needed. The Grey Company owes its freedom to you and to the Prince of Rohan, and this is how Halbarad seeks to repay the debt to Théodred. Perhaps he thinks our debt to you is too deep to repay so easily?'
Radanir raises an eyebrow and subjects you to close scrutiny.
'Once this is all over, if such a thing is possible, you and I will meet at some inn in some peaceful land, and I will buy you a drink and you will buy me three, and we will wonder when we got so old.'
He looks back at the Tree of Tribute, and seems to decide something.
'I think Calenglad is wrong. I think it is just a tree.'
