'Something is near, ${PLAYER}! It must be the wraith we have sought... it makes my blood run cold!'
Nona looks at you with wide eyes, and you are suddenly reminded that she has not had much experience with creatures of such evil. She puts her hand on the hilt of Wadu's sword, her sword, and her former fright is replaced with grim determination.
'We found it. Now what do we do with it?'

'The danger has passed, ${PLAYER}. The wound was deep, but it did not fester. And yet, I did not wish to leave this girl to the care of my healers. The risk that her wound was caused by a morgul blade, and that she could become a wraith like the creature you encountered that night, compelled me to heal her hurts personally. If that had proven the case, I would have ended her suffering. It would have been a mercy, and necessary to safe-guard Lothlórien and indeed all lands.
'Do you think me cruel? I am glad it did not come to that. I do not believe her wound was caused by a morgul blade, and it is my hope and belief she will live. I am... surprised. We will speak more of it later, away from watchful ears.
'The girl Nona is sleeping. When she is awake you will be brought to her. For now you should rest, ${PLAYER}. Dream no troubling dreams! In Lothlórien your rest will be peaceful. I am certain of it.'

'I will never call my people distrustful again, ${PLAYER}. The blindfold felt somewhat unnecessary to me. Only the most urgent of need has driven me here, and I would not want to return!'
Horn's face softens, and his brow creases with worry.
'Do you think the girl will recover? I saw the way those Elves looked at her wound. Whatever they saw there, they did not like it. If it was not an Easterling blade... what does that mean for her? What is wrong? ${PLAYER}?'

'I did my best for you, ${PLAYER}, but you are not going to be pleased. He did not understand why we should heal the hurts of this Dunlending girl.
'Eventually he relented somewhat, and he has agreed that our healers will do what they can for the girl.'

'There has to be some other way, ${PLAYER}. You spoke of the Elf-witch in the woods to the north along Anduin. My people shun that place as a den of evil glamour, but... if there was a power that could heal this girl...'
Horn glowers at you, his eyebrows knitted together angrily.
'A pox on her! I will not have her blood on my hands, or on her own. Lead us to this Elf-witch, ${PLAYER}! I have heard the tales. Perhaps she will be unable to bewitch me if I am expecting it! Why did you ever bring this girl to Stangard, ${PLAYER}? This is not her place.'
Horn gazes into the middle distance, and in a quiet voice he continues.
'In Stangard, is a sword valued more highly than the life of a girl? What sort of man would willingly serve in such a place?'
He shakes his head, and the urgency returns to his voice.
'Well? For what are you waiting? Let us go at once!'

Nona lies crumpled on the ground before you, soaking in the blood from a sword-wound in her side. She struggles weakly to speak.
'${PLAYER}... are you...?'
The effort is too great for her; she needs the aid of a healer if she is to survive this wound. In the back of your mind, one worrying question refuses to go away. From what blade did she take this wound? Did an Easterling blade cause this injury, or was it the blade of the Nazgûl?
You prepare yourself for the long journey back to Stangard with Nona.

'Do not... let them...'
Nona struggles to speak, but the effort is too great for her to make out the words. She beseeches you with wide eyes, but you cannot meet her stare. Your gaze keeps returning to the blood soaking the floor beneath her.
She tries again.
'Wadu's... it was...'
You cannot give the Rohirrim what they demand. There has to be another way to save her life.

'${PLAYER}... is everything... all right?'
Nona's breathing is ragged and shallow, and the gash in her side still bleeds around the cloths with which you tried to staunch it.
When you brought her to Stangard she was barely conscious. You found Horn near the entrance and begged for his people to tend to Nona's hurts. He sought out the leader of Stangard to see what could be done, and has not yet returned.

'There is clearly some glamour on this land. I feel as if I could take on any foe and achieve victory, or cross any landscape, no matter the obstacles!
'Your Elf-witch works wonders! Only song could do justice to her powers of healing! The relief I feel is... it is overwhelming, ${PLAYER}. The girl will live!
'Unless it is rude to ask it, I would like to return to the forest floor now. I will return to Stangard by myself, but I would like to see you again! Once the girl is recovered, bring her as well. If I am to compose a song of your adventure, I will need both of your accounts, after all.'

'You have journeyed far, and have come very close to death and sadness. And yet, still you skirt the gravest danger and come safely through the other side. I hope that our mutual friends fare as well.
'I told you earlier I had nothing to do with your dream, and this was true. But when you described your visions to me, I did not tell you everything I suspected. It seemed clear to me that your paths must cross one of the Nine. I believed the girl would die.
'And yet, unbelievably, she did not. Either through your own actions, or hers, you both escaped the clutches of the Nazgûl. And either through curious good fortune or powers unknown to me, our mutual friends seem to have outdistanced its pursuit.
'But there is no rest for we who worry for their safety. The Nazgûl is not the last danger they will face. They, and you, are not free of evil's clutch just yet. Rest for a time, but not for long.
'There are plans to be made, ${PLAYER}. We will speak again, and soon.'

'Are you familiar with the Stone of Friendship, the Cuthstan? This memorial has fallen under some ruin, with unseen culprits removing a section of the statue.
'Men have been dispatched and have set up camp to keep watch for vandals, in the event they should return. Go there now and speak with Lanbert, Sergeant of the outpost. See what can be done to aid him in his task.'

'Welcome to the Cuthstan, friend. I am Lanbert, the Sergeant of this camp.
'My men have been guarding the statue from further harm, after we discovered that a band of Mountain-orcs appears to be responsible for the damage. You are welcome to stay and help us, so long as you do not put anyone in needless danger.'

'The fate that befell me and my men is more frightful than any the living can imagine. The decision I made that day long past will haunt me for however long I remain in this realm.

'To the south, brutish men have gathered and seek to pilfer the relics of this land. It disgusts me that they have remained mostly beneath the notice of your allies. Return to whoever sent you here and alert them of their foolishness.'

'Here -- if you have time, here are some seeds. There are fertile enough spots in the plains of Eorlsmead.'

'You planted the seeds at the old abandoned farmstead along the south river-bank, did you? That is wonderful news! Now, if only the fools here would have the wisdom to harvest it when it is time.

'${PLAYER}, while the brigands will be but a small challenge to disperse, I think, there is yet another threat within their encampment. Our scouts have seen there the shades of vile Oathbreakers of Gondor who betrayed their leaders at the Field of Celebrant and were cursed to haunt the land forever.
'Wynstan and Bagmund each have differing opinions concerning what should be done about them, if anything. I must confess that I am uncertain that there is anything we can do at all, but you should speak with them and make that determination for yourself.
'I will warn you, though: if you choose to heed the advice of one of these men, do not expect the other to lend you his ear.'

'${PLAYER}, these creatures are the shades of men who fell to corruption, 'tis true, but their curse affords them the opportunity to redeem themselves...this is an opportunity we must open to them, so that they may continue the fight against the Dark Lord.'

Though concerned first and foremost about the vile thefts from Parth Celebrant, Aculf is also uncertain about what to do regarding the Oathbreakers which appear to be aiding the brigands.

'One of those that fell to the curse was not of my company...he merely sought shelter with us after faltering in his task. Cabed is his name, a messenger of Cirion sent to find aid from the North-men. However, seeing his fellows fall and sensing the futility of his charge, he fled instead to the south...to Ost Celebrant.
'The curse compounded with his guilt has driven him away from us. I do not know whether he truly seeks redemption or merely escape.
'Seek him out near Ost Celebrant. I fear that there are things occurring in that ruin that have fallen beneath notice. Perhaps he can be of help to us...I only hope he has not fallen to madness like the others.'

'Why would you seek an audience with me? I am a failure, a traitor to the great kingdom of Gondor.
'Doron sent you? Curse that man. He deserves only the worst of fates for what he did to so many of us.
'The shadow that has fallen on Ost Celebrant has fallen beneath the notice of the Horse-lords and Doron alike. I have seen what lurks within these walls, and Doron has been given a chance to redeem us all...and it must be Doron, for I have no desire to atone for the folly of another.
'Listen to me, and I will guide you to the answer.'

Doron has relayed the tale of how he and his men came to be cursed. He now wishes for you to meet with one of his men, who has become aware of more sinister dealings in Parth Celebrant.
'Seek the messenger Cabed...he may be able to reveal more to you.'

'To understand the doom falling upon the Field of Celebrant, you must first understand our past.
'Long ago, the kingdom of Gondor was besieged by a Horde of terrible Easterlings. They had forded the Great River at the Undeeps and sought to crush our forces here before sweeping into Gondor proper. While we fought valiantly, there was nothing we could do to stop the onslaught of Easterlings. My fellows and I were sent north to seek the aid of the North-men in desperation.
'With us, we each carried a trinket. Before I fell, I buried the trinket in hopes that my failure would be forgotten. However, having returned, I know that can never be the case. I would ask that you seek it out. I buried it just outside the walls of Ost Celebrant. Perhaps it still remains there.'

'So, you have found it. Thank you, I never thought I would see this again. This arrow was to be the symbol of our plight to the North-men. I was sent to deliver it at any cost, but I...I just could not do it.
'I feared death, and now see what my cowardice has brought me. I later learned that one of the messengers survived and made it to the north...my shame has only grown.
'But enough of this, there is more to be done.'

'I have done all that I can to aid you. This arrowhead and blade should be all you need to spur your allies to action. If it does not, I fear the field will again fall to the enemies of Gondor.
'Take this to them with haste, each moment you do not act only gives the enemy more time to prepare.
'Consider my duty fulfilled, even if my spirit remains. Farewell.'

'You have returned...I was beginning to worry. You were gone for some time...what is that you are carrying?'
Idmar glances with wonder at the red-tipped arrowhead, but then suddenly notices the blade you hold.
'This arrowhead is very important to my people, and I will have it sent to Stangard. It must be hung in the mead-hall to honour our ancestors' service. But...where did you get that blade? Speak quickly.

'This is unsettling news, ${PLAYER}. Bring this blade to Doron, immediately. I will muster my men and hope that we receive more support from Stangard. Go now!'

'Was Cabed willing to aid you? I know he despises me for my actions, but as you know, I only did what I thought was best....

'So, an Easterling has invaded our ruins. I will not fall victim to the same folly twice, ${PLAYER}. Journey to Ost Celebrant with me, and together, we will drive him from this land.
'There is no time to wait for your allies, you must go now, before it is too late. I will meet you at the gates, make haste!'

'It is terrible, just terrible! Stanric has died! He was healthy as could be, and on a mission to improve things, and for a time things were getting better.

'Gadda has committed treason and abandoned his post here, and Sithric vows to arrest him and those who went with him on sight. They have set up an outpost at the abandoned farm. Gadda wishes very much to speak with you!'

'${PLAYER}! You received my message; that is the only good that has come of this mess! You are truly welcome here, my friend.

'Now that you have seen our new mission here in carrying on what you began, I hope that you will help me one last time. If I return to Stangard, it will be my death... but I could not serve under such a man as Sithric. Stanric was my commander.
'I fear that there was treachery involved in Stanric's death, ${PLAYER}, but I cannot go back to investigate. No one will talk to me -- they will only arrest me or kill me on sight. I hope that you can discover what really happened.'

'I am glad to see you again, my friend. Things are not well here since our good leader passed. How fares Gadda? I wish he would return to set things right....
'Gadda told me he suspected treachery in Stanric's death, but I have not the courage to ask anyone. Too many here have grown loyal to Sithric.'

'Sithric ordered guards to arrest you? Why, I heard nothing of that! And how suspicious that nobody saw Stanric die or even saw him sick. He was in perfect health just the day before.
'I am beginning to grow roused, ${PLAYER}. The investigation should not stop now!'

'You again? I would be careful if I were you... I hear Sithric has the guards on order to take you in for treason and trespassing.
'But you asked about Stanric... and indeed it is curious that he died so suddenly, not ill, not frail, strong and hale as an ox. I did not see it, myself, so I cannot say more.'

'I... do not wish to speak too loudly on this issue, but I agree with Gadda. I was half tempted to leave with him, but I fear the repercussions.
'Things are worse than ever now, and I think Stanric was trying to stand up to Sithric... that is, right before he died. It is strange, is it not?'

'Nobody saw what happened, but Stanric seemed healthy and inspired just before his death! In fact, he kept talking about you. He was trying to motivate people to do what was right and not what was ruled.
'He felt that the council was too slow to make decisions, and Stangard had suffered too long. And... it seemed that the men responded very well to his guidance. Then... he was dead!'
'You! Sithric is wanting to have words with you. Come along nice and quietly to the lock-house....'

'I have found no trace of the creature we were tracking. Our eyes could still follow him through the shadows, but we cannot see into the depths of every crag and cave in these hills, and we may have lost his trail.

'It is as I feared, we have lost the trail. I shall take this news to Gwaihir, perhaps we will be able to track our target again with his help.

You have arrived in Ost Celebrant and now must summon Doron to your side

'The time has come, ${PLAYER}. We can wait no longer, as every minute we delay brings you and your allies closer to your doom.
'Make haste, travel to Ost Celebrant. Once there, call me forth with a horn of your allies' make, and I will fight by your side.
'There is no time to waste. We must strike!'

'You set siege Ost Celebrant by yourself? If it were anyone else, I would think him mad, but I believe your tale.
'The threat that Easterling posed was great, and it is with shame that I admit my blindness to his presence. The danger of more organized brigands serving under the Eye, no less, was of great concern. Nevertheless, your work here with my men and me is finished. Your contribution to our plight has been immense, and it was an honour to serve with you.
'To the east, more of my fellows are making forays into the Rushgore. If you would aid us more, I have more yet to say to you.'

'It is good to see you again, ${PLAYER}. With my ancient enemy again defeated, I feel at ease. My curse may not be lifted, but I know that along with you, I was able to stand against my foe without the fear that consumed me so long ago.
'The Horse-lords have a strong ally in you. Take the knowledge you have gleaned from our battle in the ruins and bring it to them. I sense the rumblings of a larger conflict in the near future.
'As for me, I will remain with my men. They lie in disarray, and it is my hope that I can one day rally them at my side again.
'Glory to Gondor! Farewell....'

'The battle is won. You fought with such valour, and I am proud to have served at your side.
'I sense my oath remains unfulfilled as I still linger at your side. I fear that some other threat remains beyond our sight.
'You have done well, and I have yet more to speak, but now is not the time. I will return to my post among my men. When you can, come speak with me.'

'They wanted to head down into the Gorge and investigate the old prospecting sites. We told them not to waste their time, but I guess they had already spent much coin on that fool's map, so they insisted on heading down all the same.
'For the first week or so, they got on all right -- set up some sort of camp, made a few runs into town for supplies -- but we have heard nothing recently. It has been a while, and I do not have high hope that you will find them alive, but if you can find out what happened to them, it would take some weight off my mind.'

'In times long past, my men and I were stationed in Ost Celebrant, a gorgeous Gondorian fortress that overlooked the Limlight river.
'We were under siege by a terrible force of Easterlings for some time before this, and eventually they claimed Calenardhon -- the land which became Rohan. They drove us north, into these fields, and it was here that we prepared to make our final stand.
'My men and I guarded the Limlight, hoping to keep their forces from the south at bay, while our leader, Cirion and his force secured the rest of the field.
'The night we were cursed began as I was patrolling back from the Limlight with my men....'

'The wrong choice was made, but how could I have known? Some of my men were overjoyed by our tainted riches, while others condemned my actions.
'Cirion never forgave us...the oath we made to protect Gondor was broken by my actions, and all suffered for it.'
'Let us leave this memory, there is more to be said.'

'The wild goats in these hills are exceptionally lean and are often poor sources of meat, but their rough hides can still prove to be quite useful. Goat-hides may be tanned into leather, then used to produce a wide assortment of important equipment, which Stangard desperately needs.

'Greetings. You must be ${PLAYER}. The Lady Galadriel suggested that we might encounter you and your friends here.'

'A few days ago, we saw a pair of Elves headed down into the Gorge under cover of darkness. They did not seem to be trying to hide, but by the time we noticed them they were already well past us...we did not dare go after them.
'The way they were dressed, I would say they must have been servants of the Sorceress of the Golden Woods to the north. I have no idea why they would come down here, though, and as long as they stay away from Stangard, I am not of much mind to interfere with them.
'Still, it is my duty to keep an eye on what is going on down there, so if you should happen upon them -- and survive -- I would be interested to know what those two are up to.'

'The Rohirrim asked you to learn our purpose here? I do not suppose that it occurred to them to just ask us themselves? It is for the best, I suppose. The Men of Stangard have long held a great fear of our people in their hearts...and in truth, we do not discourage this. It helps dissuade them from intruding upon our forests without the need for cumbersome treaties or shows of force.
'We have come to speak with the ancient Onodrim of Fangorn...the Ents. Have you met one in your travels before? We hope to convince them of the need to rouse themselves from their long peace, lest the course of the world pass them by still asleep here in their deep forest.
'Alas, it seems that they already face their own concerns, and I cannot convince them to aid us. I think you should speak with them yourself...perhaps you and your allies may be able to help us resolve this situation?'

'I have considerable learning as a healer, and I examined Greylimb. I must admit my knowledge fails me when dealing with these creatures.
'Anyhow, I expected to find that he had been poisoned -- likely by some vile effluent dumped into the river by Orcs in the Misty Mountains or the sort -- but now I believe it to be venom from a creature.
'I do not know how such a venom might have found its way into the Limlight, yet its source cannot be far off, for such venom does not keep its nature long.
'The only hint I have seen of such would be the spiders that hunt the northern edge of the Gorge. But what spider would prey upon trees...or would dare to prey upon the Ents?'

'Greetings, little ${RACE}. Hoom, you have come at a strange time, hoom-hom, strange indeed. Why, we have not had so many guests beneath our boughs in many years. Ta-rum! Perhaps since I was an Enting even. Perhaps never before? It is hard to say.
'It is sad, then, that you come to us with such troubling tales. Of war, of sorrow, of the ancient Enemy returned. I would tell you to go, that my people have already had their fill, hoom! All the memories of war that we could ever desire and many that we would forget. We would remain here in our forests while such sorrows exhaust themselves in the outside world, and we endure.
'But they have already come, ta-rum, or so it seems. My companion Greylimb has fallen ill, and that is a rare thing indeed for my folk, unless the winter should bite so deep that our bark cracks in the cold. Hoom-hom! Something has sickened him in a way we do not understand, and some of the trees have likewise grown ill here on the edge of the Forest.
'I can feel it now too, it is as if some poison has seeped into the very ground beneath our roots...but from where? We do not know. Hoom, Greylimb may be able to tell you more, if he feels up to speaking.'

'What is this? Hoom-hom, more of the little folk among us? How queer, how queer indeed. Would that I felt fit for company, but I fear I am not. Not at all fit, I am afraid. Ta-rum! I feel as weak as an ancient fir facing his last storm.
'Nay, I am not that old. Why? Do I look it? If you had asked me a little while ago, I would have said that I felt up to another Age at the least! But not anymore. Now, I feel mighty old indeed. Hoom! I just hope the beetles do not notice. Detestable things, beetles.
'It is something in the roots I would say. That is where it started, sort of a strange tingling in the water. An odd taste, but I did not think much of it. I like to take my drink down by the river you see, each morning. But I noticed that the trees...they were not looking so well. Hoom-hom, it was not long before I felt ill myself.'

'The only way to be sure of the source of Greylimb's affliction would be for you to bring me samples of the spiders' venom that I could compare to the poison I found in his blood.
'Alas, I cannot defeat such a creature myself...even my companion Ordhrien would be hard-pressed against those monstrosities.'

'Our deepest roots sicken, and the water of the Limlight runs foul with venom. The Elves tell us it must come from near to this place, but there are no spiders here, hoom.
'Ta-rum! I have just remembered, then! Greylimb told me about it one long summer's day...of a cave he discovered nearby when he was but a slender Enting. Beneath the waters of the river, he said it was, where many of the ancient roots of the forest gathered to drink. Hoom! but he could not show it to me, because we are full-grown Ents now, and too big for the narrow ways within.
'It opens nearly onto our grove here -- over there, next to the Limlight Falls -- but we have seen no sign of spiders creeping about the entrance. Hoom-hom! If they are within, I cannot say how they came to be there.'

'Spiders, you say? Hoom. We have not had any spiders in these woods for many years, many long years indeed. There is bad blood, you know, between the Ents and spiders. That goes far back...hoom, far back indeed.
'Let me see, I believe it was some years after the Men of the Sea and the Elves drove back the old darkness again, and not so long after the Gardens of the Entwives were laid waste, that an old, dark-hearted spider wove her lair not far from here, in the darkest part of old Fangorn. There she waited, preying upon any so unfortunate as to wander in among her maze of webs.
'Of course, in those days, there were few who came here, for the forest had been roused to great anger after the desolation of the Gardens, and many of those who had once lived near the forest had died in the war or been driven away, so there was little prey for one such as she. I believe she grew ever more ravenous, and in time, we discovered that she had even tried to slake her endless hunger with the living sap of the trees, and so, ta-rum, we turned our anger upon her and her brood.
'We drove her out then, brushing aside her webs as a child brushes aside cobwebs, and hounded her until she fled beneath the roots of the Misty Mountains. Hoom-hom! We never heard her name again...what was it? Let me think. Hoom! Gurthúl? Yes, I think that was it.
'Do spiders live so long? I would not think so, but then, I am not a spider, so I cannot say. She would not return here though. She is not strong enough to fight us, and her webs are no hindrance to an Ent, for we can crush stone if we are so inclined. But still, Greylimb is ill from a spider's venom, and the trees around us sicken....'

'You gathered those samples, did you? I do hope you were not bitten. Such a bite would likely be fatal, you understand.
'This is a queer thing. The samples you brought from the larger varieties of spider are dangerous, certainly, but I do not think they would harm an Ent. The Onodrim are quite resistant to such things. But this glowing venom...you say it came from a much smaller variety of spider? It is the most potent I have seen. It is very likely the same venom that has afflicted poor Greylimb. Fortunately, with a pure sample available, I should be able to brew a draught that may help purge the venom from him, in time.
'But mysteries remain. How is it that a spider came to possess such a venom, seemingly meant to kill trees and Onodrim, and how did this venom find its way into the water and the roots of the trees here? If we cannot stop it soon, much of the forest along the river's edge will soon sicken and die. You may want to ask the Onodrim if they have seen these spiders lurking about at the forest's edge of late.'

'Gadda's concerns are well-founded. There is much going on here that Stanric could not have known about when he was alive, for I am sure he would not have approved. I can let you explore the tower, but I fear to rouse the suspicion of my peers.
'There is much evidence here of Sithric's dire corruption. Find any such evidence you can and bring it back to Gadda; hopefully, it will aid his cause.'

'Aye, this is everything I had noticed as well. I do not think anything has been missed.
'I was starting to worry that I was losing my wits, but I am relieved that you have reacted as I did!'

In order to prove that evil deeds are afoot in Eorlsmead Tower, evidence must be gathered.

'Gadda was right to trust you. I will remain here and keep an eye on this place. Take what you have found back down to the farm and show Gadda, for he will be very interested.'

'The tower near here has long been under the control of men I do not consider trustworthy. I have seen many carts of goods enter full and leave empty...things I believe intended for Stangard.
'A few weeks ago, a longstanding friend of mine was enlisted to join them. Would you be so good as to find out what he knows? I fear to approach the tower, for I am wanted for treason at Stangard.
'My friend's name is Swithulf.'
'You are a friend of Gadda? That is well. I do not feel any kindness towards the happenings surrounding this place, nor towards the men who serve here.'

'The men at the tower have long made me suspicious.'

'Oh, you noticed those old ruins out there in the Gorge did you? I must admit, they are from before even my time, so I know little about them.
'You could ask Ordhrien about them, she is a fair bit older than myself and may know more.'

'Erymeldir said that you should ask me about those ruins?
'His ignorance has less to do with his tender age than it does with his flighty nature and lack of interest in anything that does not catch his fancy at the moment.
'Any child of Lórien could have told you what they were, for once they were part of Lórien itself, long ago.
'If you wish to know more about them, you should speak with the Gorge itself, for fragments of the spirits that once dwelt there with us yet remain, for those who know what to look for. Return to the Gorge by starlight and look more closely at those faded lights you have seen in your wanderings, and you may learn of its past.'
Talk to Ordhrien
Fallen Stones and Forgotten Tales
You discovered a number of unimagineably old ruins within the Limlight Gorge. They appear to be Elvish, but it is impossible to say what age they may have hailed from.

He suggested that you may want to ask Ordhrien about them as she is a good bit older than he.

'Do you have a moment, ${PLAYER}? In all of our recent turmoil, there is something that completely escaped my memory. To the east lies Parth Celebrant, and more importantly, one of my men, Brifard.
'I sent him out with a peasant to gather reeds for Stangard, but he has yet to return. Brifard means well, but sometimes he fails to see the importance of small tasks.
'It would mean a great deal to me if you would track him down. He should be at a small camp in northern Parth Celebrant, just outside Thinglad. You have my thanks.'
'Of course, Stanric would send someone. Come then, let us speak.'

Stanric is troubled by a late delivery from one of his men, Brifard, in Parth Celebrant. He wishes for you to seek out Brifard and discover why he is running so late.

Stanric has asked you to attend to one of his men, Brifard.

'Ah, hello, ${PLAYER}! We are off to a rough start here, to be sure, but is this not an exciting time? Already we have excavated these most impressive forges.

'Many of our expedition have pressed forward -- for better or worse -- but two were supposed to return, and they have not.
'Will you seek out Dagfinn? He made for Shemeldurj many hours ago and has not returned. You can find it by pressing east from here, then turning north at your first opportunity.'

'Oh! You startled me! I am sorry, I just cannot stop hunting. There must be treasure in this room, stowed away somewhere.
'My father gave me a map of this place, passed down from the time when the Longbeards inhabited Moria, and there were notes of great promise in this hall. I meant only to come in and explore, but... I cannot walk away when there is a hope of buried treasure!
'Will you help me look?'

You explain that you rooted through many corners of Shemeldurj, but found nothing of promise, and perhaps it would be wise for everyone to return to Durin's Threshold.
'No! No, I cannot believe it. I've treasured that map all my life. I cannot accept that it would lead me here, only to find this hall empty!'

'That fool. Just because he treasured a map for a lifetime does not mean that the map was ever going to be accurate. Shemeldurj is likely as dry as a bone now. I hope he returns soon to take some rest.'

'They are watching all of our movements and running communications hither and thither! I fear that many dwarves using the roads here will lose their lives to this unhindered flow of malicious information.
'I am sure you wish to hasten eastwards, but if you could do me this favour as you pass through the camp, I would appreciate it!'

'Oh! Hello there! Did you just fight your way through Snaga-maudhûl? That is incredible!

'If you wish to go further into Moria, you will want to follow the road towards the Dolven-view. Perhaps you will encounter more dwarves along the way, and they can help you get there.

'You have dealt a blow to the goblins laying hold to the Hall, and this is a welcome first step in taking back the High Stair.
'We must continue to be vigilant against the goblins, for they will not easily retreat. I am most thankful for your help, you have given me great hope.'

There is nothing here but dust and tremblings of the earth

It may be wise to report to the dwarves that strange flora seems to be creeping into Moria. There is something about the look of that fungus and the surrounding area that is strangely unnerving.

'You found an unusual fungus? I am not surprised. Well, fortunately it seems somewhat contained. Hopefully the Palace of Náin is the only place where it grows.
'In the meantime, I will make sure to warn my folk to steer clear of that place, in case this fungus is of a putrid nature.'

'A fungus? That is no surprise, ${PLAYER}. Such things grow in damp places all over the earth.'
Thórhall listens as you explain that you are aware of the nature of fungus, but that this one was strange and new and gave you a sense of foreboding.
'Upon my word... you do look a little peaked. Perhaps you should bring this news to the Dolven-view camp. That is where we are headed as well.'
Tell Thórhall of the fungus you saw
Tell someone in the Dolven-view camp about the fungus

'Well done, ${PLAYER}! As long as that banner stands, the Lonely Span will be safe for the members of this expedition and all the Free Peoples who wish to use this road once more! It was a small task, but a meaningful one.'

'Durin's Way is home to precious few of the artifacts of our ancestors, many of which have been lost or destroyed by the goblins.

'A message? I was not expecting any messages, what is this about?'
You deliver the message, and Listein looks it over.
'This artifact was not far from here at all! This is wonderful news, ${PLAYER}. With this information, I may be able to preserve another once lost artifact!'

'I have information that one such object, a mythical shield, was last seen in Uflûmp-mur, just a short distance east of The Door to the Clouds. The goblins would have a difficult time destroying such a sturdy shield, so I am hopeful it may still be found there.'
'What a wonderful find this is, a true treasure of the dwarves. Thank you, ${PLAYER}. The safe-guarding of this shield will ensure that the legend of our craft does not fade from knowledge.'

'Not all endeavours have gone well for us in Moria. One early settlement in Durin's Way was an outpost built by Gerwith, at Gloku-ru to the south. The encampment became overrun by goblins and was burned entirely, while only Gerwith and a few others managed to escape.
'The goblins threaten to fortify Gloku-ru and remain a persistent danger to us if we do not act against them. Head there and defeat as many of them as you can. Then report to Gerwith in Tharâkh Bazân, to the east, when it is done.'

'It is good to see you, ${PLAYER}. I am glad to hear that the goblins have paid for what transpired at Gloku-ru. When I think back to that day, I can still feel the heat of the fire all around me....
'Well, your deeds have given me hope. Perhaps one day I will build a new outpost at Gloku-ru, and I will make it known that it was only possible thanks to your bravery.'

The writing on the bill is scrawled in a messy hand, as if the author had many such notices to prepare and could not mask his impatience with the task. It reads:
'Greetings to you, friend! Have the delicious smells emanating on a hungry day from Mandrake's Finest Stews and Sauces caused you to desire that meal-time was nearer? If so, you know the high quality of Sig Mandrake's preparations and know what is at stake, should they be hindered.
'Sig Mandrake has a need for interested parties to help him with the preparation of such a stew. Speak with him at his shop here in Bree, east of the Mud-gate, for the details.'

'You are here about the turtle soup, I presume? I have had callers all day! Perhaps I prepared too many of those notices. My hobbit-friend has been very eager about posting them, I must say.
'I have come into possession of an order for a large batch of turtle soup. Normally this would not be a problem, but the desired recipe is most specific about the sort of turtles that can be used. Not just any turtle will do. They must be tiny turtles, and these are found only at very specific locations.
'You wish to join the ranks of the many, many adventurers who have agreed to help me with this? Good, I suppose. Tiny turtles, like those I need, can be found south of Bree, along the northern bank of Halecatch Lake.'

'These will do, these will do, ${PLAYER}. I am waiting for more people to bring in turtles. This is a very large order of turtle soup, and it will take many more turtles than I have received so far. Fortunately, it seems as if everyone in Bree is pitching in! It is a wonder there are still turtles to find!
'I have not yet begun to prepare the soup. I am waiting until I have enough turtles for it.'
'You have not brought me the turtles I need!'
Talk to Sig Mandrake
Collect tiny turtles from the northern bank of Halecatch Lake (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring tiny turtles to Sig Mandrake in Bree
Turtles in the Soup
Someone has placed bills in the town of Bree requesting help with a certain matter involving turtles.

'The turtles I need can be found on the northern bank of Halecatch Lake, to the south of Bree. You will see many other folk trying to catch turtles for me, I expect, so good luck trying to find any of the small creatures I need!'

Mandrake's Finest Stews and Sauces can be found in the town of Bree, east of the Mud-gate, by the south-western fountain.
You have read a posted notice desiring help with preparing a stew of some sort and should report to Sig Mandrake in his shop for the details.

Tiny turtles can be found on the northern bank of Halecatch Lake, south of the village of Bree.

Made Grobo Dogwort a little happier (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'You did good work out there, ${PLAYER}. You made it back more quickly than a lot of these so-called adventurers. Perhaps you would be willing to help me with something else?
'One of the Little Folk who lives up Staddle way sent word that he was eager to help me gather turtles for the turtle soup. Benegar Longbottom, he said his name was, and he's been keeping the turtles he gathered for me in his uncle's shed.
'Go to the village of Staddle and ask Grobo Dogwort if you can collect the turtles his nephew has gathered for me. Be sure to ask him in his house first; don't just barge into his shed without asking. Grobo Dogwort is a neighbour of Eldo Swatmidge, on the eastern side of the village of Staddle.'

'Oh my! Are you here about the... the... the turtles? Please tell me that's why you are here!'
You assure Grobo that you have indeed come for the turtles, and he breathes a tremendous sigh of relief.
'Good, good! You have no idea what that means to me! My nephew Benegar collected a bunch of turtles and has apparently been keeping them in my shed. I went in there this morning to fetch some supplies for breakfast, and what do I see? Tu-tu-turtles everywhere! They must have used their horrible little beaks to loosen the tie on the bag, and they have scampered loose!
'They are crawling all around the shed! Do me a favour and pick up the bag inside the shed, then gather up the turtles! Let me know when you have done it. I am so scared of tu-tu-turtles I cannot stand to do it myself!'

'That's the turtle-carrying sack, is it? They are in there? Oh, I can hear them plotting to escape again! The tiny little monsters!
'Can you imagine how horrible it would be if they grew any larger than this? Oh, I cannot bear it! They are bad enough at this size!
'I don't know what Benegar was thinking, keeping them in my shed. He knows how I feel about turtles!'
'They are still loose in my shed! It's horrible! Go get those turtles, ${PLAYER}!'
Talk to Grobo Dogwort
Pick up the turtle-carrying sack in Grobo Dogwort's shed
Save Grobo Dogwort's peace of mind by gathering up turtles from his shed (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Show the turtle-carrying sack to Grobo Dogwort in his hobbit-hole
Grobo's Request
Sig Mandrake is pleased at the help you have given him and wants you to collect the turtles being stored by Benegar Longbottom at his uncle's house.

'I cannot stand turtles! Their tiny little snapping beaks, their tough little shells, their deceptively-quick legs! I cannot stand them!
'Go into my shed, pick up the turtle-carrying sack my nephew left there, and gather up the terrifying little monsters! Come back and tell me when you have done it!'

'You have got the sack, but you haven't gotten enough turtles! They are still scampering around in my shed on their tiny little legs, snapping angrily at the air, waiting for me to go inside again! They will nip at my ankles, I know they will, oh dear! Go collect the horrible little monsters, ${PLAYER}!'

'Benegar Longbottom sent word that he gathered many of the turtles I need and is keeping them in his uncle's shed.
'Go to Staddle and speak with Grobo Dogwort for permission to collect the turtles his nephew collected for me. Grobo Dogwort is a neighbour of Eldo Swatmidge; look for his farm on the eastern side of Staddle.'

Grobo Dogwort has a hobbit-hole in Staddle.
Grobo Dogwort's nephew is keeping a bag of turtles in his uncle's shed, and you should ask Grobo Dogwort if you can collect them.

The turtle-carrying sack is somewhere inside Grobo Dogwort's shed, a hobbit-hole adjacent to his home.
Grobo Dogwort is terrified of turtles and wants you to put the ones loose in his shed back in the sack in which his nephew was keeping them.

Turtles can be found all throughout Grobo Dogwort's shed.
Grobo Dogwort is terrified of turtles and wants you to collect all of the creatures that escaped from the poorly-tied sack his nephew left in Grobo's shed.

Grobo Dogwort is in his hobbit-hole, adjacent to the turtle-filled shed, on the eastern side of Staddle.
You have gathered up the turtles that plagued Grobo Dogwort and should speak to him now that they are safely ensconced once again in the turtle-carrying sack.

'You know, I haven't seen my nephew Benegar since he left that bag of turtles in my shed. I hope the boy has not gotten himself into some turtle-related mischief!
'Return that bag of turtles to Sig Mandrake at his shop in Bree and see if he has heard any more news of my nephew.'

'Oh dear... it seems that I was mistaken. There are no turtles here. There is something worse!'
He looks around conspiratorially, and then whispers a single word.
'Murder!'

'Ah, you have brought another bag of turtles. Good, good. This is the one Benegar Longbottom set aside for me, is it? I would say I almost have enough tiny turtles to begin making the turtle soup. Not just yet, but very soon, I would say.
'I did see the boy not long ago. He said he found a place where he's sure to catch twice the turtles anyone else has caught and ran off to prove it. I told him there were no turtles to find at the place he described, as I have only ever seen frogs there, but he insisted.
'If you are looking for him, you can see for yourself, I suppose. He was going to an island in the middle of one of the Everclear Lakes, north-west of Bree.'
'You have nothing for me? What is the meaning of this?'
Bring bag of turtles to Sig Mandrake at his shop
Find Benegar Longbottom and talk to him among the Everclear Lakes
Twice the Turtles
Grobo Dogwort wants you to return the turtles to Sig Mandrake and ask the shop-keeper if he has seen Grobo's nephew Benegar Longbottom.

'Bring that bag of turtles to Sig Mandrake at his shop in the south-western section of Bree, ${PLAYER}. I'm terrified that they might escape again!
'And be sure to ask him if he's seen my nephew Benegar anywhere about.'

'The boy said he was going to look for turtles on an island in the middle of the Everclear Lakes, north-west of Bree. I told him you only ever see frogs on that island, but he didn't believe me and said he would bring back twice the turtles of any single person. I don't believe him, but he certainly seemed confident.'

Sig Mandrake is in his shop east of the Mud-gate, in the village of Bree, located in the south-western section of the town.
Grobo Dogwort wants you to bring the bag of turtles to Sig Mandrake and to ask the shop-keeper for any news of Grobo's nephew.

Benegar Longbottom went to an island in the Everclear Lakes, north-west of Bree, to look for turtles to provide Sig Mandrake.
You have learned where Benegar Longbottom went and should look for him to make sure he is safe.

'If you are looking for tasks, we have plenty of them, ${PLAYER}. The most pressing issue is probably that of our closest neighbours....
'Stíling, one of our miners, has sent back reports of a great goblin settlement too near here, unfortunately. The name of the place is Gamil Filik, and you can find Stíling there making an assessment of the threat.
'Head south from the Deep Descent and then take the east path at the cross-roads, and you should find Stíling there.'
'Well met, good ${RACE}. As you see, I have discovered some very unfriendly neighbours to the Deep Descent....'
Find Stíling at Gamil Filik
Enemies of the Deep Descent
Thettmár has asked you to find Stíling, who has gone off to scout the eastern roadways.
'Stíling can be found near the goblin encampment of Gamil Filik, south and east of here.'

Stíling is scouting the outskirts of Gamil Filik in the Silvertine Lodes, south and then slightly east of the Deep Descent.
You should speak with Stíling and offer your services against the goblin threat.

'Well, maybe not murder, but they sounded very serious, and I'm afraid it won't be long before their plans come to fruition!
'I was crouching down in the mud here, looking for turtles, when two shabbily-dressed Men came wading out to the island! They looked like they didn't want to be seen and kept peering over their shoulders back in the direction of Bree. I thought at first they were here to look for turtles at my prime turtle-catching spot, but then they started talking. And their words! Oh my!
'They spoke of a group that has infiltrated Bree and is gathering strength, watching and waiting. And when they are ready, they are planning a surprise for the village, one the Bree-folk will not soon forget! \qQuick-wit Culver's sharpening his blade,\q the seediest looking Man said, \qand Twisted Garrett has all the rope we'll need.\q
'They left after that, but not before discussing the password the infiltrators use to get into their hideout. It's \qAnother infiltrator is here!\q and if you say it to their door-man, you can get inside and stop this before they are ready! Their hideout is in Bree, south of the High Stair, and their door-man stands out front. Stop them, ${PLAYER}!'

'What's that? \qAnother infiltrator is here?\q All right. I don't recognize you, but our group is pretty large by now, so that doesn't surprise me. As many as it takes, am I right?
'We might have chosen a better password, I suppose, but at least it's easy to remember.'
Talk to the door-man at the infiltrators' hideout and give him the password
The Password
Benegar Longbottom overheard two shabbily-dressed Men discussing a 'surprise' for the town of Bree, and now he wants you to infiltrate their hideout and stop their plans.

'I don't know what the infiltrators are planning, ${PLAYER}, but we are very fortunate I overheard some of their plans! You need to go to their hideout and use the password to get inside and foil their plans before the preparations are complete!
'The password is \qAnother infiltrator is here!\q
'Their hideout is in the village of Bree, south of the High Stair.'

The infiltrator hideout is in the village of Bree, south of the High Stair. A door-man stands out front and will only let you inside if you repeat the password.
Benegar Longbottom overheard some shabbily-dressed Men talking about a secret group planning some evil surprise for Bree and wants you to infiltrate the infiltrators.

'You have told me the password, so you can go on in. I will show you the way. Lots of people are already inside. I let in Quick-wit Culver, and Twisted Garrett, and a few of the others.
'Let me know when you are ready to go in.'

'I can't believe it, ${PLAYER}! This has been the best birthday ever, and now I have so many new friends to share this home with! Look at all the little fellows!
'That party was such a terrific surprise and must have taken so much planning! Thank you for being a part of it, my new friend!'
Talk to Otis Woodman and explore the infiltrators' hideout
Talk to Artie Root
The Infiltrators' Surprise
Benegar Longbottom overheard a group calling themselves 'infiltrators' planning a surprise for the village of Bree and wants you to stop them before their preparations are complete.
'You are free to enter the hideout. I will escort you inside, then return to my post.'
Otis Woodman, the infiltrator door-man, has agreed to let you into the hideout if you tell him you are ready.
Artie Root is in his house in Bree and wants to thank you for coming to his little party.

'Will you look at this? All of my friends have gathered to surprise me with a birthday celebration! I cannot believe it!
'Thank you, everyone, thank you!'

'Disappointed? Absolutely not! I don't care much for turtle soup, in the first place. And look at all those little fellows, running around like they own the place!
'Perhaps they should! I have a spacious home not far from here, and I understand that the mayor has been known to turn a blind eye to the keeping of numerous pets within homes in Bree. I could give these little snapping gentle-turtles a fine home!
'They will stay with me! It's settled! This is the finest birthday of all! I have been surprised by my old friends, and have acquired numerous new friends! ${RACE} and turtle alike!'

'I haven't seen you around here before. Are you sure you're one of us? This has been a long time coming, and I don't want some outsider spoiling it.
'Folk won't soon forget what we do here today, not if my name's Quick-wit Culver. Which it is! You see this blade? I can slice clean through anything I set my mind to, that's how sharp both edges are: the blade, and my mind!
'I've been cutting things all morning, and I'll cut more before the day is through! See if I don't!
'Go into the main room and see if Garrett is all set up. There isn't much time left.'

'I almost forgot the main course, Artie! What good are thick slices of crusty bread without anything to dip them into?
'We all chipped in some coins to purchase a large order of turtle soup from Sig Mandrake's well-known shop. He should be here with the soup any moment now!'

'I couldn't bring myself to do it, ${PLAYER}! After seeing all of those little turtles, with their tiny shells and their little snapping beaks, I just could not bring myself to turn them into soup!
'I brought them here, tied up in a sack given to me by Grobo's nephew. I left it over by the door. Perhaps we can return them to the wild, and my customers will forgive me for not making good on our deal.
'I will refund their coin, of course!'

'I have not yet unpacked my ropes! They will hold, I am certain, but I need more time! There are a lot of things we still need to hoist!
'Oh, after all this planning, to be undone at the last for a lack of time! I saw how sharp Culver's knife has become! If I don't hurry he might use it on me next!'
'I will show you to my home, ${PLAYER}. You can help carry some of my new, beaked friends!'

'Perhaps you can do me a good deed and smash the ugly crawlers, and while you are at it, collect some of the luminescent goop that gives them their eerie glow. I believe I can fashion some of that goo into a torch of sorts, which will light the way for me in this accursed dark.'

'Ah, lovely! Well...perhaps not lovely, but you know what I mean. I can smear this goop on anything, and it will provide a light for me as I wander in the dark. You have probably saved me from many a false step, ${PLAYER}!'

'The horse's stall looks satisfactory for the time being, but it would seem this horse arrived with no horseshoes. I managed to check the hooves without getting kicked, and they're doing fine for now. Soon, though, he will need a set of shoes made. Please head to Bree-town and talk to the blacksmiths to see if one is available to make a set of horseshoes for us.'
'Sorry, I can't help you make horseshoes at the moment. A few new orders just came in.'

'Ah you need some horseshoes made? Sure, I can make those for you. Do me a favour, and grab the items I need while I put the finishing touches on this item.
'I'll need you to find me an old horseshoe as a template for scale of the new ones, some scrap metal and a few crates of nails.'
'These are just what I needed to make the horseshoes. Give me a moment and I'll have these for you.'
'I'm helping Flint here with his new order. You'll need to find another blacksmith to help you with these horseshoes. You may want to try Matt over there.'

'Thank you for taking the time to head into Bree-town and seeing this request through. The horse will appreciate this set of shoes! The stable-master is the only one here trained in replacing shoes, so I'll give these to him right away.'
Find a blacksmith in Bree-town to help you
Find an old horseshoe
Obtain crates of nails (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Obtain scrap metal (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring the items to Matt Haywood in Bree-town
Bring the horseshoes to the stable-helper in Combe
Worse for Wear
The stable-helper found out the horse needs a set of horseshoes made, and asked you to look into having the blacksmiths of Bree help make some.
A blacksmith in Bree-town should be able to help us make a new set of horseshoes.
The items needed by the blacksmith to forge new horseshoes can be found around the forge area.
Matt Haywood can be found at his forge near the Western gate of Bree-town, and is ready to help make the horseshoes.
The stable-helper in Combe will be happy to receive the horseshoes for the newly arrived horse.

'The stable-master has put new horseshoes on the horse, but we need the stall back to house Combe's travel-mounts. It's time to take the new horse to Hengstacer Farm in the Horsefields of Bree.
'Last time Éogar was here, he left behind an old saddle, and I've been meaning to return it. This seemed like a good opportunity for taking care of two tasks at once, so I tried to fit the saddle on this horse, but he almost killed me in the process. It appears this horse is not ready to be ridden.
'Could you take this saddle to Éogar at the horse-farm and let him know the horse will be heading there soon?'

'Thank you for this saddle! I've been meaning to stop by Combe to pick it up.
'Did you not say the horse would be heading here soon? It looks like the horse from Combe arrived just as you did. I do not think the Stable-master of Combe would have let the horse go free on its own, and I suspect it followed you here. This horse might be connected to you more than you know....'
Talk to Éogar in the Horsefields
Proof of Trust
You have done a great deal to help the horse settle into Combe, but it is time for him to prepare for the next step in his journey.
Éogar may be found at Hengstacer Farm in the Horsefields of Bree, a bit north of Bree-town.

'You seem trustworthy enough. Do not make me regret this decision, or I will send the Constable after you!
'By my authority, I will grant you the temporary status of Honourary Postman. Show Percy the badge and let him know that you are willing to help.'

'Hail, ${PLAYER}. Are you here to help with the festival invitations?'
'Any person who handles mail in Bree must have a Postman's Badge, or face the consequences of the law. I can authorize trustworthy individuals by bestowing them with an honourary badge, but only with the agreement that it will be used for helping Percy in his current situation. Can I trust you in this?'
A Postman's Badge
Talk to the Bree Postmaster
The Bree Postmaster can grant Honorary Postman's Badges to individuals he deems trustworthy.
Speak to the Bree Postmaster to request a Postman's Badge, in order to assist with finding the lost invitations.
Harvested ore-samples (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'You may wonder why we have come to this vast deep, ${PLAYER}, and scattered to the wind as we did.
'The Silvertine Lodes are famous for being the first and primary source of true-silver, or mithril as it is called by many. A large branch of miners have gathered for an expedition to search the Silvertine from head to toe, starting at the toes in its roots here.
'We have not had much chance to mine yet, as we are beset by dangers and missing dwarves and other mishaps. Would you care to do the honours of mining ore in the vicinity of the Deep Descent?'

'Ah! You're back, wonderful! Let me take a look at what you've collected.'
Styrr carefully examines each piece of ore closely by holding them up to his squinting eye, and rolling them gently in his fingers.
'No mithril yet. Just ordinary iron here, I believe. This is disappointing, but I am not surprised... nor shall I give up hope! There are many places yet to explore in the Silvertine Lodes!'
Harvest ore-samples near the Deep Descent camp (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring the ore you collected to Styrr
Ore Samples I: The Deep Descent
The dwarves of the Silvertine Lodes mining expedition have a universal hunger for the discovery of mithril, or true-silver in the common tongue.
'Ah, have you found any ore nodes yet? It would really gladden our hearts and give us a sense of purpose if you could show that mithril awaits us!'

Ore veins can be found in the vicinity of the Deep Descent camp, and down into the passage reaching towards the Silvertine mines.
You should mine small ore veins in search for traces of mithril.

Styrr is at the Deep Descent camp in the Silvertine Lodes.
You should bring the ore you collected to Styrr in the Deep Descent.
Harvested ore from a mineral deposit (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'The real reason I have come to this forsaken tunnel is to search for mithril along these dark, forgotten paths. Up where the glow-worms infest the mine-shaft, I believe there will be plenty of ore deposits to harvest. Will you bring me a sampling of what you collect?'

'Hello again, ${PLAYER}! Let us take a look, eh?'
Sori gently inspects each piece of ore you brought him, as carefully as Styrr did before him.
'Hm. No mithril that way. But perhaps in another spot nearby.'
Harvest ore from deposits in the mine-shaft (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring the ore samples to Sori
Ore Samples II: The Mine-shaft
The dwarves of the Silvertine Lodes mining expedition have a universal hunger for the discovery of mithril, or true-silver in the common tongue.
'Any sign of mithril yet?'

Ore deposits can be found in the glow-worm infested mine-shaft near Sori.
You should collect ore from the deposits so that Sori may assess the likelihood of mithril being found in this area.

Sori is on a platform in the southern tunnels of the Silvertine Lodes.
You should return to Sori with the ore you collected.
Collected an ore sample (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'The mine-shaft may be fairly empty of good prospects, but perhaps the very tunnel around us may provide a better yield. Will you search the surrounding area once more, and again I will look at your harvest for signs of mithril.
'My heart yearns to see just the slenderest vein! The hope such a discovery would kindle in my folk is beyond description, ${PLAYER}.'

Sori again scrutinizes all of the ore you collected from the surrounding tunnels.
'Nothing. Alas! I will have to search more on my own, but my hopes are rather low right now. Regardless, you have my gratitude, ${PLAYER}. I am certain you did your best! Perhaps there is no true-silver left to uncover....'
Harvest ore from deposits in the southern tunnel (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring the ore to Sori
Ore Samples III: The Tunnel
The dwarves of the Silvertine Lodes mining expedition have a universal hunger for the discovery of mithril, or true-silver in the common tongue.
'How is your collection coming along? I would love to have a look when you've gathered enough of a sampling.'

Ore-deposits can be found in the tunnel near Sori, and in the south-heading passage of the Silvertine Lodes.
You should search nearby for deposits of ore, and bring samples back to Sori for inspection.

Sori is in the southern tunnel of the Silvertine Lodes, perched on a wooden platform.
You should bring the ore you gathered to Sori so that he may inspect it for mithril.
You have found the door mentioned by Sori... not hidden, but a door plain to see

'I think we have done enough here to establish that mithril is not likely to be found in this part of the Silvertine Lodes. I may pack up and return to the Deep Descent, or Menem-berej. I have not yet decided.
'If you wish to continue your exploration, however, you should search for Öndótt. I hear he was making his way to the old dwarf-city that was rumoured to be in the south of the Silvertine Lodes. The only way to reach it was by a hidden door in a passage near here. Make your way to Öndótt, if you will, and then I believe you will have seen all there is to see in these parts.'

'Oh! Hello there, traveller. I did not expect anyone to come along with me, but my curiosity to behold this place could not be contained! Marvellous and surprising, is it not? The civilization in the Silvertine was once very great, I think. I should like to explore here!'
Find the hidden door in the southern passages
Find Öndótt in the ancient city of the Silvertine

The final exploration of the Silvertine Lodes involves following Öndótt to the old abandoned city in the southern Silvertine Lodes.
'I am afraid I cannot be more helpful. You must explore and seek the hidden door yourself!'

Sori mentioned a hidden door along the southern passages of the Silvertine Lodes that would help you follow the dwarf Öndótt.

'It would appear that we have another problematic inhabitant of this city. Deep-claws have made themselves quite the little nest here, and as long as they remain, the Old Silvertine City will be hopelessly polluted. They have uneven tempers, those beasts, and they weaken the foundations of Moria.
'You ought to go clear out that wretched nest, when you have spare time.'
'You got rid of those pesky deep-claws? Good, I am glad to hear it!'

Destroy filthy nests (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Öndótt
Unwelcome Tunnellers
Menacing deep-claws seem to have built a nest in the Old Silvertine City.
'Go clear out that deep-claw nest when you get a chance, eh, ${PLAYER}?'

The nest of deep-claws can be found in the Old Silvertine City in the southern Silvertine Lodes.

'I notice a strange light of many colours coming from the far end of this ancient city's edge, ${PLAYER}. What could it be? Will you go and take a look? I worry there is some goblin camp-fire perched near us, and the goblins are ready to spring!'

'What do you have there, ${PLAYER}? Ah! Were these fair crystals the source of the light I saw, and not a goblin-fire? That is wonderful! We can harvest those crystals for lamps in these desolate parts.'

A tiny trace of mithril has been found at last!

'We have searched for mithril all over the Silvertine Lodes by mining mineral deposits, and found not a trace.
'I noticed some deposits along the walls here. I am sure they will come up dry as well, so I dare not get my hopes up. But, we had best finish what you started and take a look, don't you think?
'Bring me the ore-samples you collect, and I will look it over.'

'Well, let's have that ore. I will take a look.'
Öndótt looks at each piece of ore with a scrutinizing stare. Suddenly he jumps as if startled by a ghost.
'What -- I cannot believe it. ${PLAYER}... you have found mithril. It is a tiny trace, very small, but... by Durin's Beard, you have found it! And naturally the old city sits on a source. You must send word to the rest of the expedition, my friend! We will settle ere long!'
Harvest ore from mineral deposits (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring the samples you collected to Öndótt
Ore Samples IV: The Old Silvertine City
You have mined for traces of mithril in every corner of the Silvertine Lodes but this one, so you had better give it one last try.
'I have little hope, but we had best try one last time.'

Ore deposits can be found along the rock-walls of the Old Silvertine City in the southern Silvertine Lodes.
You should collect ore from the mineral deposits along the walls.

Öndótt is at the top of the stair in the Old Silvertine City.
You should bring the samples you gathered to Öndótt.

'You have done all that I could have hoped for here, ${PLAYER}, and now I must endeavour to send you to the Deep Descent camp and tell them the wonderful news: that mithril has been found at last!
'Do not tarry; in fact, you should take my goat! I will stay here and defend the work you did to make the Old Silvertine City safe for my folk. I am sure Thettmárr will wish to set up camp here straight away!'

'Mithril! What? You... you found a tiny vein of mithril in the Old Silvertine City? I cannot believe it, truly I cannot. That is wonderful news, ${PLAYER}! We will have to send reinforcements there. What a discovery, upon my beard!'
Use Öndótt's goat to travel north and speak with Thettmárr
The Deep Descent Awaits
Now that you have done all you can for the dwarves in the Silvertine Lodes, Öndótt wants you to tell Thettmárr and the dwarves of the Deep Descent that mithril has been discovered at last.
'Quickly now! Take this goat, and make haste!'

Öndótt's goat is beside Öndótt himself in the Old Silvertine City.
You should use the goat to return to the Deep Descent with haste and speak with Thettmárr.

'Our stock of horseshoes on the farm has run out! We need someone to help us replenish the stock by running down to Bree-town to find a blacksmith who can fill an order quickly.
'Would you be so good as to bring some new shoes for my horses?'

'Certainly I can help you with Éogar's request, as I just finished my previous orders. To help you make them, I'm going to need an old horseshoe, some nails for the shoes, and some scrap-metal. Please bring these items back to me, and I'll make them right away.
'All of the items I require should be found here in Bree-town. The old horseshoe should be close by, probably in the fields across the street. The scrap-metal can usually be found among the trash in Beggar's Alley, and the crates of nails should be in the Market Square.'
'Ah! These are exactly what I require. This iron isn't the greatest quality, but it will do. I'll finish these for you as soon as I can.'

'Thank you for returning with these horseshoes! Horses seem to be arriving almost hourly these days, and I wasn't sure what I was going to do. These will come to good use, and I am sure the animals here appreciate your help as much as I do.'
'Sorry, I'm busy with new orders from Combe and can't help you with Éogar's request.'
'I am really busy with an order that I need to finish as soon as possible.'

'Lately I have been desiring a rare herb that I haven't tasted in ages. I used to only find it in very high places, but not where it's too cold. I believe it might be found on the highest summit in these lands, at the top of Weathertop. Could you head there and kindly gather a few herbs for me if you happen to find them?
'My master and I used to travel quite often, and I grew a fondness for this herb. It has been ages since he has taken me very far beyond this ruin. Maybe some day soon we will roam Middle-earth again as we used to.'

'Thank you for appeasing my appetite of herbs that I have sorely missed! My master has been busy with the important events unfolding here, but he will be happy to be reminded of our travels together when he sees these herbs. These are exactly what I was looking for; I cannot thank you enough.
'You may or may not know this already, but there seems to be something special about you. My master and I have travelled to a lot of places in Middle-earth over the ages, and I have met many horses in my travels. Rarely have I encountered a steed of your spirit, or such an air of authority as yours....'

You found the source of evil that drew you here. This was once a horse bred to serve the forces of Sauron. There are many horses in the service of the Enemy, but this creature was the steed of a Nazgûl, one of the Nine.
The scent of evil here fuels a fire you have never felt before, and you know this horse is an arch-enemy. Its death is bittersweet; you would prefer to have done battle with it yourself.
The enemy left fragments of armour and strips of cloak behind. Destroying the trophies of evil will satisfy your anger at the existence of such a creature. Search the area and destroy the trophies of this fallen enemy.

Destroying the trophies left behind by the enemy quenched your rage, for now. A powerful force was involved in driving this creature away, and it was injured badly to meet its doom at this spot.

It lingers as a receding wave would leave small pools of water upon the sand. What could have done this to such a powerful creature? You must find the source of this energy.

'The Enemy has turned his attention to steeds of late; he uses traps to tear or break our legs. These wicked mechanisms must be destroyed, but be careful, for they will likely be guarded. Once a steed is snared, enemies try to ambush the rider before the horse can break free.
'You look like you can handle yourself better than most horses I have ever seen. Please help us destroy the horse-traps and their makers!'

'The Rangers here, and we steeds especially, thank you for destroying the traps that our enemies laid for us. You have had a taste of war, and it looks as though it did not break your spirit. You are made of strong stuff, friend...and I hope to see you again before long.'

'I have had ample time to study the pages you delivered to me, ${PLAYER}. Understanding these tales is simpler than I had imagined. The author describes the events in great detail and with incredible accuracy. The stories that are told within are tragic, but important to our history.
'You should have the honour of delivering the completed story to Búkk. He must surely wonder what has been found since you and he last spoke. Share with him the knowledge we have uncovered and give him my regards.'

'I have been eagerly awaiting your return, ${PLAYER}. What news from Arnod?
'Ah, this is outstanding! These pages recount one of the greatest battles of my forefathers in Khazad-dûm... and in such detail! We have just as much to learn from the victories of old as we do our failure. There is no dishonour in defeat when all have fought bravely.
'These records are not safe here in Tharâkh Bazân. Take this tale to Borgar in Jazârgund, so that they may be preserved for future ages.'

'What tale is this you bring to me, ${PLAYER}? I know it not.'
Borgar looks carefully over the aged pages.
'Azog... this is a tale most grim. It is a sad moment in our history, but an important one as well. I had thought the pages of this tale were forever lost. I shall be sure to preserve these stories for Búkk, and for all our kin. Many thanks, brave ${CLASS}.'

'The beauty of the gardens never ceases to amaze me. Many of the crystals that grow naturally here in Tharâkh Bazân are used throughout Khazad-dûm as a source of light.
'In some locations, the merrevail have been destroying the crystals we have placed, in order to extinguish any visible light. Many of our corridors and halls have become darker than the blackest night.
'We must collect more crystals to replace the ones that have been destroyed. Search Tharâkh Bazân for naturally formed crystals, and I will make sure they are put to good use.'
'You have brought me quite the assortment of crystals, great work! We will use them to bring some of the warmth and beauty of these gardens into the dark corners where no other light can pierce.'

You have collected a healthy looking plant root (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'When I was merely a lad, my grandfather taught me about a certain plant that had nourishing properties. He called this plant mud-root, as it only grew near the edges of fresh water. By boiling the roots of this plant, he could extract the oils within and create a brew that was hearty enough to rouse a sleeping dragon! Well, that is what he claimed. I doubt he ever saw a dragon. Nevertheless, the brew was strong and could be put to use in helping our sick and wounded recover more quickly.
'I have not seen such a plant in some time, but I am hopeful that it may be growing here in Tharâkh Bazân, as there are many pools and streams of fresh water to be found. If you come across any healthy roots growing near the water, please return them to me so that I may examine them.'

'These are exactly what I had hoped for, ${PLAYER}! Yes these are the mud-roots I remember from my youth. I had all but given up hope that I would see them again. You are well deserving of my praise.
'I will wait for you to take your leave before beginning the boiling process, the smell is quite horrible, and it often attracts the deep claws.... I wish you luck on your travels.'

'There are more threats in Moria than we originally guessed, my good ${RACE}. We have had your aid in dealing with the Uruk-hai and goblins here in Durin's Way, but an entirely new menace threatens to spread from the east; the merrevail, an ancient ally of Morgoth.
'A large tribe of merrevail have taken residence in the Fanged Pit. Folkath and some others have taken camp there in order to deal with this threat, but they are in sore need of supplies. I have prepared this sack of goods, take the provisions to Folkath if you are ready to help in his task.'

'Welcome, traveller. It is good to make your acquaintance, ${PLAYER}.
'Ah, I see you have brought supplies from Oxi! I was deeply worried that we might be cut off from Jazârgund, but appears you made it here safely. Many thanks to you.'

'There are other dwarves in Khazad-dûm that are in greater need than we are. Simbi in the Twenty-first hall has asked that we send you to him. Good luck to you my friend. We will not forget your bravery.'

'There are few places in the world as large and mystifying as Khazad-dûm. With its wide chasms and twisting paths... it is easy to become disoriented! Because of this, I have been working hard on obtaining detailed maps of each hall and pathway we secure.
'Directly to the east you will find a passage known as the Winding Way. I had a beautiful map, detailing each section of the path, stretching all the way to the Twenty-first Hall... but some of the careless guards here placed their mugs of ale and various other liquids directly on top of it. They have utterly ruined it!
'I need a replacement and it must be accurate. Would you take this parchment and detail a new map for me, ${PLAYER}?'

'You drew this, ${PLAYER}? Why, this is even better than the original! I appreciate the detail you put in. Have you not considered a career in map-making?
'Whenever I travel the Winding Way, I will think of you. You have my thanks.'

'This is bad news, ${PLAYER}. The terrible beast that assailed us outside the West Gate has made its lair here amongst the Water-works.
'You must return to Simbi in the Twenty-first Hall at once, and inform him of our plight. We have had many successes here in the Water-works, but this terror could destroy everything we have worked for.
'I will inform Indrith and Ansurr of your passage. Go with haste!'

'What word do you bring? Will our great wheels churn once more?'
You relay your tale of what you have seen within the Water-works.
'No! How many more must fall before that beast troubles us no longer? This is... an unfortunate turn. We have not the numbers to make an assault on the beast yet, but perhaps in time we will. You and your allies may be able to deal a final blow against it, but I sense you are not yet prepared.
'The expedition must press on - the time for vengeance against this beast will come. For now, we must reclaim Zelem-melek.'

'We have had word from our kindred in the Great River of a heroic traveller who passed through Stangard. I can see that you are this same ${RACE} of whom such praise was spoken.

'Ah... the famous wandering ${CLASS}! Your reputation precedes you, ${PLAYER}. I bid you welcome to Langhold. I am sure you will find plenty to keep you busy here, for we are often beset by ruffians and wild creatures.'

'By your estimates, they are not weak by any means, but perhaps we may discourage them still.'

Khundolar Easterlings can be found throughout the Brown Lands, but especially at their encampment, Lashkarg, to the south of Etheburg in the Brown Lands.

'Thanks to Dagbert's treason, we are forced to deal with the Khundolar sooner than expected, but perhaps there are ways to weaken or discourage them.
'Make a foray against Lashkarg and defeat some of the Easterlings there. Perhaps by making a show of strength against their encampment, they will believe our numbers are greater than they actually are.
'If you find Dagbert among them, do not hesitate to end his life. Treason is a crime punishable only by death....'

'As vast as you say Lashkarg is, I doubt this attack has deterred them at all.

'Uh...good work, ${PLAYER}. I confess I was not sure I would see you again, but you have proven quite hardy!'

'Perhaps if we burn these banners, we can convince them that the Eye is not greater than the Mark, and they will depart. I hold no great hope of this, but should you accomplish this deed return to me with the results.'

'Alas, it is as I expected. They were not deterred.

'My wife, Cíllan, has a better temperament for welcoming guests to Langhold than I. I would sooner bid you to go find your own food, but my dear wife upholds the customs of Rohan. She has grace, despite agreeing to tolerate my bad behaviour for so many long years!
'Cíllan will give you the welcome you deserve as an honoured guest in our city, ${PLAYER}.'

'Ah, the traveller from Stangard! You must be weary from your long road. Do not mind my husband -- he is an unceremonious man, but he is a good Thane, and still strong.
'Come! Let us drink together, and share a meal. This custom is a pledge of honour from us that you will be safe from all harm in Langhold. It is a pledge on your part also: while here, you must respect our ways and cause no harm, and stir no trouble.
'Will you perform this gesture of goodwill?'
'Ah, the traveller from the western-lands. Welcome -- I am a city guardsman, but I am a little busy at the moment....'

'You have my wife's approval, eh? Do you? Good, good. She is a gentle soul, and she loves the old customs. I suppose there is no harm in them, especially if they make our guests behave themselves while they stay here.
'Now, you are free to roam about and do as you please. Do not let me keep you.'
