The City of Dol Amroth

'Welcome, honoured guest. Did you enjoy your tour of our fair city? It is a beautiful and peaceful place, full of art, music, and bustling markets.
'Alas for the war that threatens us all. I fear that we will lose our way of life, if my father Imrahil cannot help Denethor uphold Minas Tirith against the shadow that looms in the east.'

'Have you ever seen a finer fountain? I have lived here all my life, but I still come every day just to gaze upon it. It is the pride of Dol Amroth.
'If you are travelling through, the Court of the Fount is where you want to be. Here we have the finest goods for sale from all over the world, brought from our ships. It is always bustling here. Never a dull moment!'
'Are you a travelling artisan, friend? If so, you have come to the right place, for you'll not find a better crafters' area for leagues upon leagues.'

'We get many travellers in Dol Amroth. I bid you welcome! I also say to you: Mind your behaviour while you are here. Drink and make merriment as you will, but do try not to cause a disturbance.
'Here is the Keep of the Swan-knights, where the finest soldiers of Dol Amroth execute the will of Prince Imrahil, or the lady Lothíriel who now governs in his place. A fine prospect, is it not?'
'I am the master stone-mason in these parts. Only the best stoneworkers in Gondor may study under me, and most will never master the art themselves.'
'This is the finest place for a concert in all the world. Musicians come here to practice, too, so there is always music upon the air. Oh, but how I love a sweet melody!'
'My pardons, I was lost in thought. People often come here to lose themselves in their thoughts, for this is the Scholar's Quarter. Here you will find the great minds of Dol Amroth.'

'Well met, stranger. Are you here to see the wharf? It is perhaps not the best view of Dol Amroth, but I have always found it the most beautiful place in the city.
'Here you will find all of the fishermen hard at work, and the tall ships rest ere they set out for another great adventure.
'Is there a better smell on earth than clean sea air and fresh fish, and the salt of sea and sweat?'

'What is this you have brought me? Ah, that girl Barían who comes to me every day, did her father do this? He was a great stone-mason.'
You explain that this is Barían's own work, and Laegened stares at you incredulously.
'I confess that I had no idea she was so advanced in her artistry. I have never had a young lady as an apprentice before, but I can see that she has what it takes. She may even become a master someday.'

'He has accepted me as an apprentice!? This is wonderful, ${PLAYER}, truly wonderful. I cannot wait to start!
'Thank you so much for your help. I did not know if he would even like the stone, but getting it to him has been such a great hassle.'

'What do you mean, not interested? You mean she would rather dirty herself with rocks and dust than accept my courtship? I do not understand.'
You decide it is best to leave this poet to ponder the state of the world on his own, rather than try to explain to him that he has thoroughly misjudged the character of the woman he claims to love.

'Here, I did away with your odd notes and composed a poem of better taste, more suited to woo a lovely young lady such as Barían.
'Bring this to her, if you please. I know she will not be able to resist my sweet words. Do tell her where to find me when you're done, please.'

'I am sorry, but I'm busy. I am trying to get Master Laegened's attention.'
You apologetically hand Barían the poem written for her, and she reads it with a scowl.
'I don't have time for this nonsense. I'm trying to get an apprenticeship, but Master Laegened won't even see me. He says he has too many worthless apprentices already. I want to show him my work, but I cannot haul it up the stairs!

'You found something? Let me see what you found!'
Artamir takes the crumpled parchment from you and unfolds it, but in mere moments he shakes his head.
'This is written in the speech of the Orcs, and no reputable Man of Gondor ever studied such words. My father never trusted the written word to begin with; Ilcamir was a man of action and of deeds, and I am no different than my sire!
'But I can tell you this much, even without knowing the words themselves: this parchment contains orders for the Orcs. They have been sent to this dreary land, much as I have been. But for what purpose?'
Artamir's brow is creased in thought as he considers what goal the Orcs might have within the Dead Marshes, but your worry is deeper than his. Did Frodo come this way? And does the Master of the Orcs know it?

'I trust you, ${PLAYER}. I will tell you the nature of my errand in this miserable land, and perhaps you can better help me accomplish it and then return to my home in triumph. I would give anything for this victory, my friend! The gratitude of the Steward would do much for my family's position.
'Long ago, the peace of Gondor was threatened by Wainriders from the East, cruel men who rode down their enemies in great wheeled chariots. It is said that Ondoher, one of the last of the true line of Kings, faced the Wainriders in battle on the great plain but was defeated. No sign was ever found of the King or his force, and Steward Denethor believes that the Wainriders might have driven him into the Dead Marshes before he perished.
'You think it unlikely? I would say so too, but for this. Denethor had of late a dream, in which he beheld the banner of the King flying proudly against the night sky. Could it be the banner of Ondoher, last of the line of Kings descended from Meneldil, Anárion's son? The strange waters of the swamp must have preserved it, after all this time, and I must find it and return with it to Minas Tirith!
'If these Orcs have found the King's Banner, they might be keeping it in a storage cache in their camp. Return to their camp and search these caches to ensure they have not!'

'Not all who come this way have kindness in their hearts. There are those who wish to harm this land and its people, and they will find no welcome from me or my sisters.'
Roamingstar opens her golden hand, and reveals a number of pebbles. They are worn smooth by the currents of the Gilrain.
'Leave these on flat stones to the south, ${PLAYER}, away from the banks of the river. For this small favour you will have the blessing of Gilrain.'

'I thank you for this favour, young one. It has been long years since I cast my eye beyond the banks of the stream. When last I did it brought only grief.'
Sadness wells in the deep pools of Roamingstar's eyes, and her words are nearly whispers.
'An Elf-maid tarried on the banks of Gilrain, lulled to sleep by the beauty of my song. She was reminded of her home, and I delighted in her presence, for my sisters had gone away and I was filled with loneliness.
'But she was needed, and when she awoke the delay had cost her the life of her love. He was an Elf-lord and a prince, Amroth by name, and he waited for her... but she never came. He died believing she was lost forever, and when she awoke it was he who was lost.'
Roamingstar's words trail away into silence. After a moment, the girl Roniel stirs.

'Oh, hello! Are you a friend of my mother? I was separated from her during the fighting. I ran and ran, and at some point I dropped my doll, but then I was just so tired and fell asleep.
'I think I had a lovely dream, but I cannot remember much of it now. I suppose it is time to return to Linhir. Do you think it is safe? Tell my mother I am on my way home. Her name is Mornil.'
Roamingstar is silent, lost in her thoughts.

Now he has returned, and the years have not touched him as they have weathered me. His strength remains, timeless and unchanging! He will destroy the Corsairs as he did before.
'So that is why I celebrate, and you should too! Follow in his train, friend, defeat Haradrim and Corsairs in Lebennin, and find him at Pelargir. Show him badges of the enemies you defeat, and he will know the people of Gondor have not forgotten him! Thorongil! Thorongil!'

'My brothers Erchar and Herion are fine warriors, though a bit rash in their decisions.
'We defended Linhir valiantly but the constant watch left us tired. Like brothers often do, we fall to quarreling. You speak soothing words to the deer in the language of animals, words taught to you by Grimbeorn and others of your kind in your youth. The deer's panic gradually subsides, though its ears still twitch at every sound.
The frightened creature's demeanor tells you that Clothar is right to worry: a large predator is nearby.

'What is it, what is it? I can't bear it... is it the bear?
'No! Don't tell me!'

'I knew there was something peculiar about you, ${PLAYER}! Not everyone can speak to animals, after all, can they? You... you are a skin-changer! Not just tales, but tails, as my old da' used to say! I cannot believe there are really people such as you in this world!'
For a moment, Clothar looks as if he is going to faint dead away, but then he recovers himself, and sticks out his hand.
'It would be an honour to shake your hand, ${PLAYER}. Did I say there must be few folk like you in this world? That is a shame, for you could have killed that bear but chose not to do so. 'Let us leave this forest behind us, ${PLAYER}. I have had quite enough adventure for today, thank you very much!'

You reach out to the bear once more, drawing upon your natural affinity for the creatures. A low rumble confirms your belief: something has put a great and terrible fear into the bear, setting into motion this frenzied assault.
'Friend,' you speak to it in reassuring tones, and the bear speaks its name.
Suddenly, a great shudder seizes the creature's body, and he attacks once again!

The fear in Bramblesnarl's eyes is now gone, replaced with different emotions: respect, and admiration.
Your calming words, and the strength of your resolve, have brought Bramblesnarl back to his senses. In the language of his kind, he tells you of a frightening wraith that stalked the plains where lie the barrows of long-dead Men. The visage of that terrible king awoke in Bramblesnarl a primal fear, and he could not shake the madness that held him in its grip.
With a thankful snort, Bramblesnarl turns and walks back among the trees.

Your ancestor Beorn had a special kinship with the creatures that made their homes near his lodge, and you have inherited some measure of this quality as well.
You try to draw upon this portion of your nature to calm the mighty beast before you. What has driven this creature to such rage?

'I must say, you are a tall one! From where have you come and what are you called? ${PLAYER}? That is quite an unusual name. What business brings you to Archet? We have our own share of troubles, and have little need for outsiders to bring theirs.'
You tell the woman that you have travelled from afar seeking the Ranger Aragorn. She thinks for a moment, and then shakes her head.
'He was here, it is true, but he has gone. He left just before the Blackwold brigands launched their attack on our town, reducing it to this state. We could have used him in the defence. To speak the truth, we could have used you as well, had you arrived a little earlier. You look to be a strong one.
'I do not know where the Ranger has gone now, but Jon Brackenbrook might know. He has assumed command of the rebuilding process, now that his father has perished. You will find him in front of the wreckage of the tavern, I imagine. I saw him there earlier.'

'Well, I must say I never expected to see one of your kind in these parts! You are of the line of Beorn, are you not? Your stature and demeanor seem unmistakable to me. I have never met any of your family until today, but I have heard tell of your people from Rangers and other wild folk.'
You tell Jon Brackenbrook why you have come to Archet, and he nods.
'Yes, Aragorn was here, though he goes by the name Strider in these parts. He left with some haste, but I heard from others he was loath to do so, and wished to stay and help us with our troubles. He made for the town of Bree, unless I have heard wrong.
'But stay, my tall friend! Do not hurry away just yet. You come to us in our darkest hour, when the Blackwold brigands have burned our town and slain many of our friends. My own father perished in the night, struck down by the Blackwolds and their hateful allies from the north... from Angmar. I know you wish to seek out Aragorn, but if you truly share his ideals you will spare a moment here and there to help people who need it. The experience will make you stronger, and together we may prevent other towns from being burned in the name of evil. Think on it, ${PLAYER}.'

'The Ranger Aragorn was here, it is true, but he left before the Blackwold attack. I do not know where he went, but Jon Brackenbrook may know. Jon is in charge of rebuilding the town now that his father has died.'

'Aragorn is a Ranger, which means he travels often in the Wild, and he is looked upon with mistrust by the folk of villages beyond the mountains. Much like me, now that I think of it!
'Here, I will go with you a short way, and I will tell you what I know of the path through the mountains, and how to find the Bree-land...'
You have prepared for the journey, and now it is time to leave the land of your home in search of the Ranger Aragorn.
Langhar smiles at you, but before you speak with your sister you should finish your first chore: defeating the sickle-flies that buzz nearby.

'These goblins thought they could best me? Foolish creatures! It would take two dozen goblins to draw blood, and still I would be their better.
'Hurry to the lodge and tell Grimbeorn the goblins have lost any of the wits they may have once had.'

You quickly tell Sterkist about the goblins that attacked you and Langhár.
'That is very peculiar, ${PLAYER}! Beorn put the fear of our kind in the goblins when he stalked these vales, and we have done our part to maintain their terror of us, have we not? What could make them think to stray once again to this side of the river?'

'Yes, young one. I have made my decision. You will leave this sheltered land and bring a message of warning where the Wizard believes it must go. I long thought our folk could remain separate from the other peoples, as my father wished, but these are no longer those days.
'Perhaps I will send others in the days ahead, but for now you will represent the line of Beorn in the wider world. Act with strength and clarity of purpose, , and let all who see you say, 'There goes a ${PLAYER:woman[f]|man} of Beorn's line. Cross ${PLAYER:her[f]|him} at your peril!'
'I do not believe in long farewells, young one. Learn your task from the Wizard, say good-bye to your siblings, and bring no disfavour upon our line.'

'Good, good, good! I worried that Grimbeorn would not see the urgency of this matter, but reason has won out. I have always had a way with bears and beasts, and, well... you see... nevermind, nevermind. Not important!
'A dark power is rising, ${PLAYER}. I cannot put a name to it, if indeed it has a name, but something has unsettled the natural world. I will seek the greatest of the Five Wizards, for he has made a study of many things unknown to me and may know what is happening.
'I want you to seek out someone else. He is a Ranger, and his name is Aragorn. He has been enmeshed in the affairs of Wizards for some time now, and if the rumblings I sense are a real danger, as I fear, I know that Aragorn must take especial care not to fall prey to them.
'The last I heard, he was travelling through the Bree-land, beyond the mountains.'
Sterkist growls at you in the language of bear-kind, but the words you speak are filled with affection. He bristles, and finally relents.

'Has it come to this, ${PLAYER}? Do you serve those lazier than you, fetching lost cows and running errands?'
Ofolmóth laughs harshly.
'You are of Beorn's line, as am I, but I have not forgotten what that means. To you it means little! We should live our lives with ferocity, seizing each moment with tooth and claw. No one is my master.
'I fear you have grown soft, ${PLAYER}. Only by harnessing your Wrath in battle can you truly live up to your heritage! Prepare yourself for battle and test your skills against me!'

'There are few like us, ${PLAYER}. That is why I test you as I do. The legacy of Beorn is rare and dwindling. We must use it to be the strongest of his children and grandchildren! As we do battle, the Wrath fills our hearts, and drives us with great ferocity, empowering the skills we use in combat!
'Let our foes beware! They tangle with the line of Beorn at their peril!'

'I find nothing so maddening as weakness, ${PLAYER}. Drive it from your body with training and practice! The line of Beorn deserves nothing less.
'Follow the surrounding fence and practice your skills against the sickle-flies you find. Such training will make you stronger and more fierce!'

'I did not think to see you again today, my ${PLAYER:sister[f]|brother}! Most afternoons you spend daydreaming in the sun with Sterkist. What is different about this day?'
You tell Langhár that Radagast the Wizard has paid a visit to Grimbeorn, and that Ofolmóth set you to fighting the sickle-flies for practice. Your sister smirks and adopts a gruff, snarly voice.
'Fight! Roar! Battle! Growl! The line of Beorn is the finest of all,' she booms in a passable impression of Ofolmóth.

'Did I not tell you your time would come soon, my ${PLAYER:sister[f]|brother}? Perhaps I am as much a Wizard as Radagast himself!'
Langhár laughs cheerily.
'No, that is not what I want. I want to explore the lands beyond our home, , as you are about to do. I want to seek adventure! I will follow you sooner rather than late, , I assure you!
'Until we meet again, ${PLAYER:sister[f]|brother}! Find this Ranger, deliver Radagast's message, and do not have your fill of adventure before Sterkist and I can join you!'

You approach the milk-cow and she lows nervously. Something has caused her distress. What could it be?
When you were young you developed the ability to understand many of the animal languages, a gift of your ancestor Beorn. You call upon this natural facility now to speak gentle reassurances to the milk-cow.
Before long her calm nature returns and she begins to move slowly back to her pen.

The Wizard Radagast has come to Grimbeorn's lodge, and your mind races to determine the reason. Your brother Sterkist wants your help to learn what has brought the Wizard from his Mirkwood home.
Varthmath may know what brought Radagast out of Mirkwood, and you should find him at the animal pen to the west of the lodge. Your cousin is a man of few words, but his keen ears miss little.

'How many afternoons have we spent in this way, ? Once the work is done, and our chores finished, it seems every day sees us staring out at the pond of Grimbeorn our elder, thinking airy thoughts.'
Sterkist sighs, as he often does on such afternoons, and scratches idly at his arm.
'You are my ${PLAYER:sister[f]|brother}, , and we keep no secrets from each other. Is this all we have a right to expect? The blood of the skin-changer flows within us, and must move us to greater deeds than this!'

'I have only seen Radagast once or twice, and that was when we were very young; do you remember? We were very small then, and he was kind to us, but I do not think he enjoyed leaving his home in Mirkwood.
'Something serious must have happened to draw him here, my ${PLAYER:sister[f]|brother}! I will sniff around the lodge and see if I can overhear any of his conversation with our sire, and you should talk to Varthmath at the animal pens. Our cousin talks little, but he hears much, and he might know something.'

'What brings you hither, cousin?'
You tell Varthmath that Radagast the Wizard has left Mirkwood and is speaking with Grimbeorn, and that you hoped he might have heard why. Varthmath responds with a brusque snort.
'I know what brings him here: his own business. If it becomes a concern of ours, Grimbeorn will let us know. Until that time you should mind your own matters. Even better: you should make yourself useful to me.
'One of our milk-cows has wandered from the pen. Find her before she gets outside the surrounding wall, and tell her to return.'

'No pleasant journey draws me hither, my ${PLAYER:sister[f]|brother}. I have been sent to put an end to one of our folk. I held no warm feelings for Ofolmóth, and I do not think you did either, but he is still blood. It saddens me that this action is necessary, but Grimbeorn has commanded it and I think it just.
'Some weeks ago, Ofolmóth began straying further and further afield, and I think he encountered someone beneath the trees of Mirkwood. From this mysterious stranger he heard cruel whispers, and Grimbeorn believes these whispers took root within Ofolmóth's heart. He spoke vile words to Grimbeorn and others of our folk, and fled from our land. Now we hear that he has killed without mercy, striking down innocent folk without care or reason.
'I am glad you answered my letter. Ofolmóth is strong and fierce, but he is of our blood, and I need someone at my side if I am to go through with this unpleasant duty. He deserves this judgement, but I do not know that I could carry it out alone. Speak to me when you are ready, and we will make for where he was last seen.'

'Let us go at once. I am eager to have this unhappy duty behind me.'
<rgb=#FF0000>This is a solo quest and cannot be completed with a fellowship.</rgb>

'We have the victory, ${PLAYER:sister[f]|brother}, but it is not a happy one. I know that Ofolmóth was a danger to innocent folk and had to be confronted, but I wish it had not been so.
'His words were cruel, it is true. But I can also understand from where they came, and know that it was not Ofolmóth alone that chose this path. Others preyed upon his inclinations. Some great evil crossed his path in Mirkwood, and made use of him for its own purposes. He had no love for dwarves, but this evil aligned him with these Dourhands and their master Skorgrím. That is the evil we must face.
'I will stay here for a time to rest from my hurts, , and then I will bring these tidings to Grimbeorn. I thank you once more, and hope to see you again and in health. Guard your spirit well, and do not follow the dark path that brought Ofolmóth to his end!'

'Grimbeorn wanted me to send word if you were successful at the tasks he set before you, and I have done so. He told me he would journey into the High Pass to meet with you. You should go to him at the camp named Vindurhal, in the narrow space between the Eastern Bruinen Source and the North High Pass.'

'When I sent you forth to find the Ranger Aragorn at the urging of the Wizard Radagast, I did not believe in the importance of the errand. I thought you would complete the task and return, and we could return to living in our customary way. We would collect the tolls on the river-crossing, trade for what goods we need, and otherwise remain secluded from the outside world.
'But I have come to realize this cannot be. The forces of evil that gather on our doorstep will not be content to stay there. They may respect the might of Beorn's descendants, and would be wise to leave us be for a time, but one day they would seek to stamp us out. Our ferocity and our resilience would make them pay dearly, and the cost would make me proud, but then the line of my father would be ended.
'I do not want to wait until that day, far away as it may be. I do not want to become as a cornered bear: dangerous, but frightened. I want to strike out at the enemies that surround him,, and in that way keep from being cornered.
'Make yourself strong, ${PLAYER}. Strike fear into the enemies of our people, and aid good folk that lack the power of the skin-changers. You will become my weapon against the forces that assemble against us. That is all I have to say. Go with my blessing and that of your brothers and sisters. Let the memory of your mighty ancestor, my father Beorn, drive you to feats of greatness!'

'I am in amazement that Grimbeorn made the journey into the High Pass. Did his message to you justify the journey, ?'
You briefly recount Grimbeorn's words to Sterkist.
'Well, I am glad that he tasked you with this duty, my ${PLAYER:sister[f]|brother}. Real adventuring is difficult, tiring work, and this journey through the mountains to find you has already given me my fill!
'You can be the adventurer in our family, and with my blessing!'

'Can you believe it, my ${PLAYER:sister[f]|brother}? At last Grimbeorn has relented and given me leave to cross the mountains to find adventure! He has set a task for you, and put it to me to ensure you complete it. Consider this Grimbeorn's challenge to you: to face the mightiest foes with strength and endurance, and to best them!
'When I arrived at this curious home of Elves, I did what I do best. I made a number of friends, and it seems one of them is a master craftsman. He agreed to make a weapon and other fine equipment for you, if you are able to collect the many components that will be required.
'Grimbeorn demands that you become a shining example of our kind if you are to represent our family in Eriador, so I think you should undertake this task! Indeed, I look forward to guiding you toward its completion!'
'Grimbeorn has challenged you to wield the finest equipment you can.'

'Well done, well done, my ${PLAYER:sister[f]|brother}! I must confess to you that I did not think you would be able to complete the tasks Grimbeorn set before you.
'Adventuring is difficult, tiring work! When we used to dream of going on such quests, it seems we left out the sleepless nights and the aching muscles, for this journey is the first I have thought of them. And yet you have travelled far and wide and faced terrible foes without complaint! Perhaps Grimbeorn was right to send you after the Ranger, . I am weary after a much shorter journey!
'Grimbeorn has one more message for you. He wanted me to send word if you were successful at the tasks he set before you, and I have done so. He told me he would journey into the High Pass to meet with you. You should go to him at the camp named Vindurhal, in the narrow space between the Eastern Bruinen Source and the North High Pass.'

'It is good to see you again, young one, and strong. I would not have made this journey if I did not think it important to give you my blessing and a word or two of further guidance.
'When I sent you forth to find the Ranger Aragorn at the urging of the Wizard Radagast, I did not believe in the importance of the errand. I thought you would complete the task and return, and we could return to living in our customary way. We would collect the tolls on the river-crossing, trade for what goods we need, and otherwise remain secluded from the outside world.
'But I have come to realize this cannot be. The forces of evil that gather on our doorstep will not be content to stay there. They may respect the might of Beorn's descendants, and would be wise to leave us be for a time, but one day they would seek to stamp us out. Our ferocity and our resilience would make them pay dearly, and the cost would make me proud, but then the line of my father would be ended.
'I do not want to wait until that day, far away as it may be. I do not want to become as a cornered bear: dangerous, but frightened. I want to strike out at the enemies that surround him, and in that way keep from being cornered.
'Make yourself strong, ${PLAYER}. Strike fear into the enemies of our people, and aid good folk that lack the power of the skin-changers. You will become my weapon against the forces that assemble against us. That is all I have to say. Go with my blessing and that of your brothers and sisters. Let the memory of your mighty ancestor, my father Beorn, drive you to feats of greatness!'

'Allow me a moment to turn my mind from my brothers, ${PLAYER}. The recent battle in Linhir was brought to an abrupt end by the arrival of Aragorn and the Grey Host. Corsairs, Haradrim, and my fellow Gondorians alike threw down their arms and fled at the sight of them. I saw only Angbor standing amidst the tumult, but now he too has gone from these lands....
'It was a battle half-fought, and one that is bound to be finished. Our barricades are in ruin and many of our men are scattered still. If you would aid us in restoring our defences, I would be most grateful.
'Let us hope the Grey Host has left us for good... I doubt any of us could bear such terror a second time.'

'These Men repulse me, ${PLAYER}. They dishonour me and my people and cannot be allowed to hold sway over our waters.
'I hope that soon all of their number are gone from these lands, and that I can return to the Gilrain in peace.'

'Although there are few that believe my sisters and I still dwell in these lands, they have always strived to care for our lands and our rivers.
'These Men from Umbar... they do not honour these lands as the others do. They defile, they steal, and they dishonour and for no greater purpose than their own gain.
'Soon they shall levy their destruction against my waters as well, but already they have taken from my people. Those that still believe pay tribute to me and my sisters with baskets they float down my waters... but the Men have claimed those too!
'I do not know what drives them - be it greed or spite, but they must be punished for the harm done to those that honour us.'

'You have done well to heal the wounds of Men, ${PLAYER}. These outsiders have no love for our lands or the people within and will not stop until it all lies wilted and dead, but I shall do all I can to hold them back from the innocent.
'In all I have witnessed, few other times have come with such destruction and bloodshed. Let us hope that this one shall soon come to an end....'

'I have brought you here because I sense goodness within you, ${RACE}. You seek an end to the conflict that ravages my lands and burdens my people, as do I.
'Few still hold sincere belief in my sisters and fewer still have looked upon me in many long years. Of those that did... one came to regret it and I feel the shame still.
'Now these wounds lay bare as the Men from Umbar pollute and defile my lands. My waters can heal their destruction, but I cannot do this alone. Aid me, and I shall aid you in turn!'

'How are we to defeat the Dead? Neither man nor beast can raise arms against them and Garvir knows this well. They simply vanish from sight when we think them wounded and reappear not long after - it is a fruitless endeavour! The only hope we have is that they pass over the Gilrain and leave us be!
'I say we hold as best we can against the Corsairs and Haradrim. At least a blade might wound them!'

'I guessed as much, ${PLAYER}. It is hard to keep the men from despair in these dark days. I do not know what can be done... nothing outside of the Sisters in the stories of old could aid us now, but they are just that... stories.
'There is a man named Tancestel here who would speak otherwise, but he is old and foolish. Naught but children and the maddened dare pay him any heed.
'I do not wish you disrespect, but I would like to be alone in my thoughts for a time.'

'Long ago, the people of Gondor spoke of five sisters... one that held sway over each of the rivers of Lebennin. Now, most people think them little more than a tale passed down from their forebears, but I assure you... they are as real as I am.
'Before you ask... no, they have not revealed themselves to us, but it has been said that they return to watch over us in times of strife. With war at our gates and the sky smothered in fumes and smoke, I can think of no more likely time for them to return.
'The faithful of my people pay tribute to the Sister of the Gilrain and we hold river-stones in her honour. Take my stone and travel to the mere along the Gilrain. Once you are there, lay it at the water's edge and let us hope our faith has not been misplaced... or the Dead will consume us all.'

'The people of Lebennin are beset from the coast, and soon I fear that all of our land shall fall to the Corsairs. We have fallen beneath their notice for the moment, but I do not think it long until their attention turns to my people.

'Now, we must cut through this gloom and bring hope to our people, especially the young. One as well-travelled as yourself would be of great help in that regard!'

'We hold Linhir because of you, ${PLAYER}, but we lost far too much in the fight to hold it. I have sent my remaining guards to search for Garvir... but I hold little hope that he will be found. Either the current has taken him out to the bay, or his plate armour drew him down to the river-bed.
'I blame myself for his loss, and I curse myself for not seeing the folly of rushing out into the fields of battle with so few in my command. The war rages on in Lebennin... this much is clear to me now.
'Travel to the settlement of Sarnhad due east of the south-gate of Linhir, and see if you can aid the people there. Herion and I shall renew Linhir's defences while you aid the folk of Lebennin.
'And ${PLAYER}... should you find the scarlet-garbed man who slew Garvir in Lebennin, I shall not be denied the chance to run him through.'

Fearing a foolish alliance between the people of Lebennin and the Heirs of Castamir, Nimithil of Pelargir hopes to expose the treachery in Ost Anglebed.

'Rumours surround these men known as the Heirs of Castamir for his name was once held in great regard in Gondor... at least by some. There was a dark time in our history known as the Kin-strife, when our people fought amongst themselves to determine who was the true claimant to the throne.
'Castamir and his followers forced the opposition from these lands and soon ruled in Pelargir, but he was killed years later. The Kin-strife's ending was a bloody one, ${PLAYER}, and as long as it has been, many of the wounds between brothers have never fully healed.
'I have heard my own folk talk of them, and I grow more curious as to what they believe these Heirs seek in Gondor.'

'I care not if they are of the blood-line - Castamir the Usurper was a monster who spat in the faces of his people, and these brutal men have proven to be no better than him. To grant any of them the throne would be madness!
'Were I a warrior, I would drive them from Gondor myself!'

'I have heard rumours of the might of the one they call the Scourge. It is said he commands a vast army and can outsmart any foe in battle.
'It has been many years since Gondor has had a King upon the throne, and should he return the throne to Pelargir, the people of Lebennin might prosper greatly. This fighting is brutal to be sure, but for this cause, I would throw my lot in with him.'

'I do not care for this man or the outcome of his bid for the throne. I merely wish to make it through this war with my family intact.
'If he can stop the fighting, so be it.'

'The folk of my line once counted themselves amongst the followers of Castamir. His dishonour tainted our family's name for years, but perhaps his descendants can restore it.
'The people of Gondor have waited long enough for the rightful Heir - let us celebrate anew!'

'I do not trust these rumours... Castamir's sons escaped when he was slain, but I do not believe his line could have continued for so long.
'I will follow them if it allows me to keep my life, but they are cruel, vicious men and I do not think them proper leaders for Gondor.'

'Listen to me, ${RACE}, and hear my story. I no longer wish to be a part of this conflict. My scouts from the east have learned of Nerzus' demise. That same fate besieges me if I am to travel further into the coming storm. I followed the Dark Lord so long ago, I am not sure why I chose to follow him again. No good came from it, only death and restlessness for all time. If he had true power over his subjects, he would have freed us from this curse ages ago.
'I will leave this Vale and return to the mountains. First though, I ask a favour of you. When Isildur met with us, I gave him a gift as collateral for our oath of allegiance. Since the oath had been broken, the treasures were never returned. If you find these ancient treasures and return them to me, I shall leave Gondor in peace and command these restless men of Dunharrow to do the same.'

'I will keep the map, ${PLAYER}, and I will use it to design my adventure! Let us return to my hobbit-hole and make some plans, my inspiring friend!'

'Would you mind running back to my hole and retrieving the walking-stick? I thought it was easy to leave, and easy it was! Easy to leave without my walking-stick, but I miss it already and cannot go much longer without it. I hope you do not think me a fool for leaving it, but leave it I did.
'I will continue on to Bywater while you fetch the walking-stick, so we do not slow the journey overmuch. I will meet you in the centre of Bywater in a short while!'

'Ah, there you are, my travelling companion! And you have collected my walking-stick! Very good. That will be a big help on the miles ahead, I do not doubt it!
'I did not nip into the Green Dragon just for this ale, ${PLAYER}, though it is quite good and you should try some. No, I was being followed about town by a number of nosey hobbits, and came in here to evade them. I think perhaps we two should leave quietly and slip through the swamps around Frogmorton so we can leave without being pestered.
'I will meet you in the Frogmoors!'

'We found Marigold, ${PLAYER}!
'I have only recently become an adventurer of sorts, and I must say that my old habits and customs are difficult to shake, for this spooky forest makes me uncomfortable. But Marigold is just a young hobbit, and she has been coming in here and dealing with its dangers on a regular basis. Her gifts of mushrooms and treats must have bought the silence of her siblings, for Prisca would never allow this behaviour!'
'What could have brought cousin Bingo into the Old Forest? This is a long way from Michel Delving, and much more dangerous for an old hobbit!'

'Do you know that I never really believed I was a Boffin, ${PLAYER}? All of my brothers and sisters are so dull, happy to stay at home, as far from excitement as possible! Esmeralda might go dancing in the Toad Marsh, but when I suggested we walk to the Midgewater Marshes on the other side of Bree, and dance there, she refused! She threatened to tell our mother, so I did not push it. But isn't that dull?'
Marigold brandishes her sword and shield.
'I made this sword from a branch, and rescued this shield from a wolf's den when the wolves were gone. I didn't think any other Boffin would do those things, but now it seems cousin Bingo is an adventurer too! You do not know how happy I am to hear it!
'Anyway, you've found me just in time. I met a curious creature in the woods, and he offered to show me his home. You can come along too, if you like! I didn't catch his name, but he wore yellow boots and said his house was to the north-east of here!'
'This forest is very spooky, and it makes me uncomfortable to be here! How can Marigold come in here so often?'

'I must be honest with you, ${PLAYER}. I do not think it is wise for Marigold to follow this yellow-booted stranger to his home, especially if that home is somewhere in the depths of the Old Forest! Who would live in such a place?'
'This new friend of mine said his home is in the woods to the north-east. Let us find it!'
'We found Marigold, ${PLAYER}!'
'Cousin Bingo? What are you doing in the Old Forest?'
'Keep this to yourself, ${PLAYER}, but Marigold was always my favourite. If she is in trouble in the Old Forest, we have to find her!'

'Marigold has been going further and further into the Old Forest recently, and sometimes brings back mushrooms and other treats for the rest of us kids. It's dangerous in there, though. Bats and roots and wolves, she says!
'If you're going to track her down in the Old Forest, you'll need to deal with all of those at some point!'

'Have you ever seen such a cozy little cottage, ${PLAYER}? It is the home of my new friend Tom and his wife Goldberry. They are most mysterious, and I want to learn more about them if I can!
'Where did they come from? Why do they live in the Old Forest? I have so many questions, but whenever I ask them they only smile and have no direct answers for me!
'Still, I am so very pleased to have met them. What does cousin Bingo think of my new friends, I wonder?'
'What a strange place this is!'
'I must say I never expected to see such a cozy home in the Old Forest!'

'What a strange sight this is: a tidy little cottage in the middle of a dangerous wood, home to a most peculiar individual and his equally-mysterious wife! I never thought such a place existed, ${PLAYER}. If my journey ended tomorrow I would still count it an adventure full of wonders.
'I need to rest from our journey through the forest. Perhaps later I can speak with Tom and Goldberry and write a description of them for my own journal!'

'It was good to see my cousin Bingo for a short while, but I must ask him to be off as soon as he can. Either he has been a bad influence on Marigold or she has been a bad influence on him, but either way there is entirely too much adventurous spirit between them!
'We Boffins have been many things, but heroes? I don't know about that!'

'I have heard that some frightful creatures make their homes among the burial mounds of Men in the Barrow-downs, and we will need to face some of them if we go there. Watch out for ravenous barghests and giant crawlers, for they will be watching out for you!'
'I will see you back at my cousin Prisca's house in Newbury, ${PLAYER}! I do not want to stay here a moment longer!'
'Prisca thinks it was my idea to go jaunting about in the Barrow-downs, when it was the furthest idea in my head. That was mostly Marigold's idea!'

'That was amazing, ${PLAYER}! The Barrow-downs were everything I had hoped they would be! I was never scared, not really.
'I will need to come up with something truly exciting to top this most recent adventure!'

'We have to search the Barrow-downs for the remainder of the missing pages! Bingo shivers.
'That place has a frightful reputation and I did not plan to explore it, but now it seems I have no choice! We have to search the Barrow-downs for the remainder of the missing pages! 'I have heard that some frightful creatures make their homes among the burial mounds of Men in the Barrow-downs, and we will need to face some of them if we go there. Watch out for ravenous barghests and giant crawlers, for they will be watching out for you!'

'All right, ${PLAYER}. I would say it is time to see Marigold safely back to Newbury, and for our own journey to continue! I have enjoyed this brief stay at the house of Tom Bombadil, but there are many other places to see and people to meet!
'Would you mind speaking to Tom and retrieving my manuscript from him? I am most interested to hear what he thought of it, now that he has had plenty of time to read!'

You ask Tom what he thought of Bingo's manuscript, but the strange fellow is only puzzled.
'Your words are all a-scramble, young one. Tom remembers a great many things: the sun in the morning, the breezes of mid-day, the swelter of afternoon, and the cool of evening; but he does not know the pages of which you speak. There is no need for writing! If you spend all the day writing, that is a day you have missed!
'Do not look so glum! I am sure this writing will turn up. I may have set it down outside. There are so many things to see, happy distractions all, and sometimes things get lost. All is found in the end, hey!'

'Tom has misplaced my manuscript? Oh, bother! I know there wasn't yet much of it, but I still keenly feel its loss! I will not be able to recreate exactly what I wrote the first time! Perhaps I should just abandon this endeavour. I am not a writer, and I am not an adventurer!'
You seek to console the unhappy hobbit, and soon Bingo is slightly less despondent.

'I said this was a dark and dreary place, but look at those two in the corner. They seem to be colourful characters, and do not fit in with the rest of the assemblage. Let us see what has gotten them so worked up, shall we?'

'What's that? Your hobbit-friend wants to become a Treasure Seeker? I would love to teach him, but alas, it is not something that can be easily taught! If he does not have the natural proclivity for such adventures, he will be resistant to any training I might give to him. Also, I am about to retire, and intend to spend my time regaling Haley here with tales of my interesting and eventful life. So I would appreciate being left alone to do so!'
Theodore thinks for a moment, and then speaks apologetically.
'I do not mean to be so brusque. Here, take this riddle. It is apparently a clue to a treasure somewhere in the Lone-lands, a treasure I never found. If the two of you can solve this riddle and find the treasure, perhaps I will be able to teach the both of you something after all. Good luck to you, and good-bye!'

'May I see the riddle?'
You show Bingo the riddle, and he closes his eyes, deep in thought.
'This is a tough one, ${PLAYER}! Maybe you should study the riddle some more and see if it seems to describe anything specific.'

'Look who it is!'
'Can it be that we have found the very hobbit who drew the map I found in that cookbook?'

'Before I left the Shire for good, I spent some time visiting my old haunts and fixing the dear place in my memory. I can still see many of my favourite sunny paths and peaceful benches, even now. But one thing brought a sadness to my heart, and it was the belief that none of the dear hobbits I was leaving behind would ever experience the same joys I had in seeing the world. Oh, I knew Frodo would be all right; he'd always been an adventurous boy, but he was unusual in that regard.
'I conceived of a plan, ${PLAYER}. I would draw a map of the wider world, and I would leave it in a cookbook in the library at Tuckborough. Perhaps it would be found by an inquisitive hobbit, one who needed only the slightest of pushes to embark on a grand adventure.
'And look! I was right! Gandalf would be so proud of my inventiveness, ${PLAYER}! I do hope, for Bingo's sake, that there will be no dragons involved, as there were for me. Then I would feel most responsible, but for now it seems to me a lark and a joy!'

'Can you give Bilbo my manuscript so far and ask if he will read through it? I am too shy to ask him myself, but if you ask perhaps he would be willing to take the time to read it!'

'We still have our own parts to play, and I deem it important that we play them well! I wish to sail up the river on the deck of the Corsair ships, and come by that route to the aid of Minas Tirith. It is my hope that we will arrive in time and with such surprise that we can strike a blow to the fighting will of those who threaten the city.
'We do not have much time to prepare, but there are a number of tasks I have given my friends to perform that will help us set forth as quickly as possible. Help them with these tasks, if you would, for every moment we hesitate is a moment the Enemy would relish!'

'I asked that you help prepare the ships with haste, but I did not expect such speed even from you, ${PLAYER}! I thank you for your efforts and know that we are put in the best position we could be as a result.
'I have given some thought to this next request, my friend, and I hope you agree with me on this. I do not ask you to accompany me on the ships. Instead, I ask you to travel by land through Upper Lebennin and Lossarnach. We must learn the state of the war to the east. The vale of Tumladen and the town of Imloth Melui had strong walls of old, and were used as places of safety for the people in times of war. The people there will tell you much of what has transpired elsewhere in Gondor. Angbor will go that way as well, with his men, and will be a boon companion as you go.
'I have another purpose for you, my trusted friend. I want you to find Gandalf or true-hearted Faramir in Minas Tirith and tell them about our victory here. Tell no others! In Faramir I place the trust I would not give to the father. There is too much I do not know about the situation in the White City.'

'Did you fight in the battle, ${PLAYER}? I was stricken with a great fear as the shades of the Dead joined the battle, and I confess to you that I felt a great urge to run from them, as the Corsairs did. And yet, before my heart betrayed me and I succumbed to the terror, I felt a hand upon my arm, and I was reassured.
'Do you know who it was? It was Celairant, the young Ranger I took under my wing in Ered Luin. He is not as young as he was, and this journey has put some steel in him. It was an honour to stand with Aragorn, and the presence of Celairant was a comfort. I am proud to call him brother.
'When the Corsairs fled, many of them cast their weapons to the ground. Mandan went ahead to gather up the fallen blades. Find him at the north-west entrance to Pelargir and help him with this task, for there are many weapons to be recovered.'

'Oh! Langlas sent you to check on me? That was quite unnecessary, ${PLAYER}.'
Mandan scowls.
'Well, perhaps it was a little necessary. You see, I began to gather some of the weapons the Corsairs cast aside when they fled, but it was slow work and I decided my own skills might be better used elsewhere. You know of my talent for fashioning and applying salves, of course? There are many wounded folk who could use such treatment, and I will see to them immediately.
'Anyway, Celairant was gathering up the weapons already. You are welcome to go down to the docks and help him with that task, if you like.'
'Celairant was gathering up the weapons already. You are welcome to go down to the docks and help him with that task, if you like.'

'I will put these weapons into a barrel and ask Celairant where he wants it brought, but you should return to Langlas and tell him that I will be on short rations for the rest of our journey. I wish to give a portion of my provisions to some of the families the attack from Umbar hit hardest.'

'Yes? What do you want? Are you here to chastise me for treating Corunir unkindly? He has been a sharp thorn for these past few days, constantly asking questions about my well-being. He should have expected a rebuke!'
There is an angry fire in Golodir's eyes, an unfamiliar, smouldering rage.
'I know why, ${PLAYER}. Around matters of the Dead they treat me with delicate gloves. They look at me and they see my daughter, Lorniel. My grief was strong and will never truly pass, but this treatment fills me with such an anger I would strike them all down: Corunir, Halbarad, even my own chief, Aragorn!'
He falls silent. When he speaks again, his voice is little more than a whisper, and there are tears in his eyes.
'I... I do not know from where this anger comes, ${PLAYER}. It feels as if I hear voices of the past, unflagging and unrelenting, calling my name, taunting me...
'I will master these voices. I have been troubled by these feelings ever since we began this journey, and I have managed to stifle them. It has become more difficult of late, perhaps because of the unnatural skies... the evil presence of the Dead Men...

'I think we are doing fine, for the most part. We have been through a great deal already, and there is more hardship ahead, but if we stay true to each other there is nothing we need fear.

'Oh, yes. I told Daervunn about our agreement once this is all done. I did not think you would mind.'

'With all my musings I forgot to tell you something! Halbarad wanted me to send you to him. He has returned to Pelargir already. If you leave now you should find him just inside the north-west entrance to the city.'

'The appearance of the Dead Men may weigh heavily upon some others of our company. Golodir in particular seemed distraught by the passage under the mountain. Find Corunir, somewhere to the south of here, and see if he knows where Golodir can be found. The two of them are rarely apart.'

'Golodir's ill mood has returned after a short time at low ebb, and now he shouts at his own dear friends! 'I like this land, ${PLAYER}. It reminds me of the twilit wilds, far away in the North, where my heart remains. The wooded slopes encircling Lake Nenuial must be slowly shaking off the grip of winter, and in a few weeks the leaves of their trees may begin to fight through the remaining chill. No Winter lasts forever, and the coming of Spring will banish even the coldest of memories. Will this war be any different?'
Calenglad stands silently for a short while, musing on the question. Eventually he smiles, and gives you a conspiratorial wink.
'Radanir told me you agreed to treat him to a meal and drinks at a tavern of your choosing, once this is all over. If you have no objection, I would like to join the two of you there. I will look forward to that happy meeting!
'But there is still much hardship ahead of us, and with all my musings I forgot to tell you something! Halbarad wanted me to send you to him. He has returned to Pelargir already. If you leave now you should find him just inside the north-west entrance to the city.'

'Very good, my friend. You have disrupted the preparations of the Haradrim, and my men will be able to cross the Erui without fear of Southron fortifications. Even a force of four thousand can suffer many losses when attacking a much smaller force, provided the smaller force has time to prepare.'
'Find the vale of Tumladen in Upper Lebennin, and see how the war has treated the rest of the kingdom. I will follow behind with four thousand swords and strong men to wield them!'

'They say I am too old to fight, even if the desire to protect my home and my family burns as brightly within my bosom as it does within those of younger men. I am not afraid to die, if that death were to be in service of Steward Denethor or his brave sons!
'Still I have been carted here to wait for the end with the children and the women. What justice is there in that? They say the son of the Steward holds Osgiliath, but how long can he hope to stand against all the armies that pour out of the East? That city has changed hands before, but it seems to this old man that the next time it falls may be the last.
'When that happens, I think they will rue sending us away. The White City will have need of folk to wield swords, no matter their ages. Mark my words, and mark them well!'

'You have done good work here. I suspected that we would find these havens full of refugees from the White City, which means that the war will soon be joined if it has not already begun.
'Four thousand swords travel slowly, but when they arrive they will make all their points, with sharp arguments! We must make sure their path is free of obstruction. There is a good place to cross the River Erui, to the south, but it is held by the Haradrim. Let us go to the Crossings and defeat these Southrons so my army can pass.
'Any Haradrim in Upper Lebennin pose a threat to the Crossings, and they must be stopped!'
'The Haradrim hold the Crossings. They must be defeated.'

'As we left Minas Tirith, I saw smoke rising from Osgiliath. I hope Faramir holds it still, but I do not know how long even he can last. I have heard also that Boromir left on an errand to the north, and has not yet returned. I would feel better for my sons if Boromir returned and stood on the front lines... may it be soon!
'Right now we await word that it is safe to return to the city. Tumladen has enough supplies for its garrison, now absent, so we should be able to stay as long as necessary. But I hope this is resolved quickly.'

'Some folk have all the good fortune, and leave none for the rest of us! It is not fair!'

'Before he departed for Minas Tirith, Prince Imrahil charged me with the defence of the fiefs he left behind. I accepted this duty, knowing it might end in death, and left my son to protect my own lands. I engaged the Corsairs and Southrons at the city of Linhir, but we were heavily outnumbered and our defeat seemed certain.
'And then a new force joined the fray: a vast army of shadows from the forbidden paths under the mountains! They were Dead Men, and they brought death with them, silent and sure. My men cast aside their weapons and fled, but I stood my ground, and when I saw the banner of he who led them I was glad, for it was Aragorn, and he rode 'neath the standard of the King. 'Fearless' he called me, but what man can be afraid when a King has returned to a kingdom that needs him?
'I have four thousand men with me, and they will travel behind us. It will be slow going for them, so we will ride ahead and see what awaits them. Let us fight the Southrons in Upper Lebennin and clear the way for their swords! Then we will come to the vale of Tumladen and see the state of the war.'

'I have four thousand men with me, and they will travel behind us. It will be slow going for them, so we will ride ahead and see what awaits them. Let us fight the Southrons in Upper Lebennin and clear the way for their swords! Then we will come to Tumladen and see the state of the war.'
'Find the vale of Tumladen in Upper Lebennin, and see how the war has treated the rest of the kingdom. I will follow behind with four thousand swords and strong men to wield them!'

'Do you plan to travel to Minas Tirith? I would advise you to rethink your course! If the city is not already besieged, it soon will be! Much of my family has been evacuated, but my sons remained behind at the request of their commander. They will defend the city, and are glad for the chance, but I am afraid for them.
'As we left Minas Tirith, I saw smoke rising from Osgiliath. I hope Faramir holds it still, but I do not know how long even he can last. 'Right now we await word that it is safe to return to the city. Tumladen has enough supplies for its garrison, now absent, so we should be able to stay as long as necessary. But I hope this is resolved quickly.'

'You must be journeying to Minas Tirith! They are going to need you there, I am certain of it! There is going to be a war... it may have already started! Are you going to be in the thick of the fighting? I would be, if they'd let me!

'Oh, hello there, ${PLAYER}. How have you been keeping? I have been doing well.
'My father was not pleased with me when I returned to him in Tarlang's Neck, but he is always looking for a reason to be unhappy. I told him to look on the bright side, as I do. After all, we will never want for nails! I have never known him to have enough of something before, and now he does. How many can say that? Very few folk!'

'The Harlond is overrun? If we cannot get to the south-gate in the Rammas, we will not be able to bring our wares to Minas Tirith! What is it like to have good fortune? I would truly like to know, for I have never had it!
'If there is a bright side to this news, it is that I suspected it was so. No ill news is truly surprising to me anymore, ${PLAYER}! We cannot return to Galengam without selling his goods, so I sent Nethadan to Imloth Melui to find a purchaser for our Cemenduril liquor. Go north to the town and find my son, for he has not yet returned.'

'Hello there, ${PLAYER}! What good timing! I was just telling these ladies about some of our adventures. Do you remember when we fought off those Corsair raiders together? That was really something, was it not?'

'How unfortunate! How ill-fated! Even so, I think this will be a fine place to stay until the road is clear. This is the perfect place to bring our waggon of valuable healing liquors. Did you know that this town has produced some of the finest healers in all the kingdom?
'Now where was I? Oh yes! I have always sought to provide for my family and my dear old dad. He will never want for nails, for example....'

The message you recovered is addressed from Gothmog to 'the master of the great beasts,' and it commands this master to pull the ram through the city to the West-gate. We must assume that Gothmog or his superiors plan to use Grond to smash the gates of Minas Tirith.
'We have to stop it! If this message has not been delivered by another of Gothmog's runners, we have a brief window available to us before Grond begins to move once more. This hunter from the Blackroot Vale has been itching for a chance to prove himself. Take him and find Grond before it leaves the city, and damage or destroy the ram before it reaches the Pelennor. Once it leaves Osgiliath we will not be able to halt its progress, ${PLAYER}!'

'You look as if you have seen a ghost, ${PLAYER}, and if that terrible apparition's words are to be believed, mayhap you have!
'Is it true? Was this creature spared death? How can we hope to fight against such foes, if even a true strike with a keen blade cannot cure them of this existence?'
You ask Derufin that he not tell anyone of Gothmog's words, and he nods his assent, if reluctantly.
'I suppose that is for the best, but I do not like it. If the armies we face are led by creatures that cannot die, how long must we be expected to fight? How long must we stand, ${PLAYER}? I hope you understand that I am not afraid, but my brother is not as brave as I am, and I fear that he will not be willing to go on endlessly without victory.'

Derufin can be found among the Osgiliath Culverts beneath the city.

You managed to damage Grond, but learned an unsettling truth about the identity of Gothmog, a commander of the forces in Osgiliath.

'What is wrong? Is everything all right?'

'${PLAYER}! Derufin tells me that you were able to do some damage to the great ram, and it will be some time before Grond can be used against Minas Tirith. Why then has the colour drained from your face, and why do you bear that stricken expression?'
The thought of telling Damrod the truth weighs heavily upon you, but you know that the soldier already struggles on with very little hope. To tell him that the leaders of the Enemy's armies cannot be defeated in battle, and that death holds no permanence for such creatures of evil, would dash away any of his hopes that remain.
'Cheer up, ${PLAYER}. Your efforts have bought the defenders of Minas Tirith some time, and those extra hours, however brief, might prove the difference. Evil cannot fight forever. Faramir will be found, and our battles will be won! Get some rest if you can, ${PLAYER}. Soon we will look to joining the defenders of the White City, and our battle will begin anew. But for now you have done well.'
Damrod smiles heartily at you, but you think of the foe that was once Mordirith, and your heart is heavy.

'Quickly stranger, untie me so that I may live another day. Curse these damned Haradrim!'

'My thanks for helping me out back there. I was on routine patrol with a comrade when we were ambushed. One moment we were fighting back to back and the next our foes fell back - a clever ploy! - and we pursued them separately. Before I knew it, I was surrounded, alone, and taken as you found me.
'Now forgive me, but I must ask what brought you to these wooded shores?'
You explain that you are trying to reach Faramir with important information, and also that Luntil sent you to the Rangers' camp to lend what aid you could.
'I look into your eyes, ${RACE}, and see that you speak the truth. Alas, I can help you little, for I have not seen Faramir nor heard of his whereabouts for many weeks. I hope for your sake that the information is important enough to traverse these lands. Southern Ithilien is crawling with the Morgul-host.
'Now, let us speak of the debt you owe to Luntil. She is wise in many ways, and I will confess your help is sorely needed, so I deem that I should not release you from your word.'

'Now that we stand at the base of the Emyn Arnen, do you see the beauty of these lands? This rugged beauty is my home. My parents lived here for as long as they could but the threat in the east grew too great and we fled to Lossarnach when I was young. I vowed to do everything I could to save Ithilien so that one day my children may live here in peace. Now I ask of you: protect these lands.
'The Rangers have a camp-site - the Western Post - just north of here. Tell them I sent you to aid them. Some of the Rangers can be stubborn, at times, but I know they are in need of someone like yourself.'

You ask Duilin about Anborn.
'If you're looking for Anborn, he's at the keep. He seems awfully busy though. He doesn't even have the time to hunt with us! Isn't that right, Derufin?'

'Stranger, you are bold to come and ask me where my leader is. You should not even be in these lands. But you speak Gladhir's name, so I will allow you here for now. It will take more than that to earn my trust, however.'

'Duilin and Derufin? Anborn allows those two to stay, I think, because they amuse our fellow Rangers with their cheerful antics. There is little to lighten our hearts in these days. They cheer us, but they are of little use. I hope that you may prove otherwise, for we are in need of some extra hands in Bâr Húrin, presently.'

'Return to Gladhir and tell him of the Haradrim scaling the cliffs. I shall continue to monitor the situation and thwart their efforts until others arrive. Take care.'

'This is indeed dire. I do not wish to make you tarry longer than need requires if you do indeed have important news for Lord Faramir. I will muster nearby Rangers to put an end to the Haradrim plans to scale the cliffs. Pressing further into South Ithilien will be difficult. You should make your way to Bâr Húrin, the main stronghold of the Rangers south of Osgiliath.
'You will not be welcomed there as warmly as you might wish or deserve, I am afraid. Anborn, leader of Bâr Húrin, is distrustful of outsiders, perhaps to a fault. I do not think he will turn you away, however. He did not turn away two others, like you, who came recently to Ithilien. If you take a little time to earn his trust, I feel sure he will assist you.
Have hope, for I know you will find Faramir. May our paths cross again, ${PLAYER}.'

'My brother and I come from across the river. We're preparing to hunt a simply grand beast. Have you heard of the Mûmakil? They are giant, tusked creatures from lands south of here.'
You ask Derufin about Anborn.
'You can try talking to Anborn but I don't know how far you'll get. He admires our skill with the bow, but it ends there. You may have better luck with Thurindol. That Thurindol is a pleasant fellow, wouldn't you agree, Duilin?'

'Now I see you for a good sort, would you lend a poor woman a hand? My cart tumbled down that ridge whilst I was taking a shortcut into Arnach-town. I can't leave these sacks of potatoes behind, for the good soldiers must eat if they're to protect us! 'Whilst Dagor dreams of playing at war, he ignores the plain facts before him. Though we are many, we are ill-trained and poorly organized. If the Haradrim who have crept into Lossarnach were to attack now, we would be done for!

'The first rule of warfare, ${CLASS}, is to give the enemy no quarter. If they cannot pull back and regroup, they must either bend - or break.
'Now it so happens my men have espied some of the boats that brought the Haradrim into Lossarnach. They are here and there along the banks by the mouth of the River Erui. They have also noted piles of supplies, not far from the boats.
'I say: let us burn their boats; let us trample their supplies. Then they'll have nowhere to run. Then we'll have them! And by we, I mean me in thought and you in action. As a captain I cannot leave Arnach, and you are more than up to the task.'

'Even if Dagor's grand war-plans defend us from the Haradrim here, we may yet starve in the coming winter. Already we have missed first planting. We face hard times at our most fortunate!

Much of Lossarnach's farmland is burned and the first planting has been missed. Indir fears that if the Haradrim discover Arnach's grain supplies, no victory will forestall thin crops and starvation in seasons to come.

'The truth is, Lord Forlong left me with too many men. We sent as many as we could up to Imloth Melui, but the lads with war in their eyes couldn't bear to be cooped up behind those walls. I couldn't handle them all myself, so I made Dagor and Indir my captains.
'Like the sun and moon, those two are! Dagor's the more soldierly and fit for the role. Whereas Indir is clever and steady enough, but he worries and broods. We have enough darkness from the skies above! A captain should keep his head high.'

'Do not let my furrowed brows weigh on your heart, ${CLASS}.
'Dagor plays at war and good-hearted Baranor keeps watch over the township as if these were times of peace. While I would curb the one and rouse the other, to do so would be out of my place. So I, who harbour no dreams of war and glory, take the burden willingly. I will plan and brood so that their dreams are not darkened... and so Arnach remains safe.'

'Ah, would that I were off, marching with Forlong to war! Still, I will not let ill chance rob me of any glory. There are enemies in Lossarnach, now, and I may prove my mettle as a captain and warrior here, as well.
'Baranor sees. He smiles on me, and when Forlong returns victorious, Baranor will tell him of my deeds.'

'Ah, yes! Where was I? Welcome to Arnach! I can't give you half the welcome old Lord Forlong would do. But he's gone off to Minas Tirith - off to war - and here I am! Baranor, Captain of the Guard, is who I am, and I must do my best to fill his shoes. Only he left me with such a great lot of green lads, all restless and rousting about. It's like herding mice!
'So I've made captains of Dagor and Indir. There's Dagor over there. Destined for greatness, if you ask me. At any rate, between guarding Arnach and keeping watch on these damned Haradrim, we three have had our hands full, and then some!
'Now you look a well-travelled and sensible ${RACE}. Could you lend my captains a hand? I assure you, Arnachrim lives depend on it!'
'${PLAYER}! There's no time now. The Haradrim - they're planning an attack. Ah, what shall we do? We mustn't stand around. We must act!'

'Ah, you have my thanks, ${PLAYER}. I see a few of my men have returned already, and I am certain the rest shall soon follow.
'Yet, I know little of the fate of my captain, Faramir, and I shall not count him among the dead while he remains lost. I have a mind to search for him within Osgiliath, for none that survived our flight into the tunnels saw him escape.
'If you will join me and my men in our search for Faramir, you are welcome among us for as long as your journey allows it.'

Mablung's Rangers can be found throughout Osgiliath.
Mablung has asked you to seek the Rangers he sent to scout the surface of Osgiliath and order them to return to his post.
Search for Mablung's Rangers in Osgiliath (${CURRENT}/${MAX})

'It will be some time before I can return you to Arodor, stranger. Faramir is lost, as is Osgiliath, save for the secret ways beneath the city. You are fortunate, indeed, to have made it down here alive... for many of our company were not so swift.
'Our number is few, but several of my men scout even now from hidden ways within the city's walls. However, we cannot remain scattered any longer if we are to hold against the Enemy, so I would ask that you seek my men among the Enemy's forces in the city and order their return.
'If I know my men, they shall be well-hidden!'

The Ranger noticeably flinches and readies his weapon as you approach.
'I feared my position was discovered... I am sorry, stranger. Mablung has sent you?
'I shall return to the tunnels with haste, but I cannot abandon my post until my friend returns and we have saved more of our old records.'

'So, Mablung sends me to the surface to search for arms and now he wishes for me to return just as soon as I find a secure position? Faramir would not have us hide in the culverts and cower while our people die!
'I will return when I finish my task, and not a moment sooner. If I should die, it will be in the aid of my brothers, not backed into a corner like a hunted beast.
'The host of Minas Morgul has no shortage of workers and warriors, and I would deprive them of any advantage that may be left behind. Aid me, and I shall return!'

'You are fortunate that you did not bear the markings of the Morgul-host, stranger, else I would have struck you down before you dared step so close.
'I shall heed Mablung's order in time, but if you wish to count yourself among us, you shall aid me first - for there are far more pressing matters at hand.
'What shall it be, ${CLASS}?'

'You startled me, stranger! I have almost finished my patrol, but I could use your aid if I am to quicken my pace and return to the culverts.
'I promise you, I shall be a more gracious companion than any others you might find roaming the City of Stars.'
Lost, But Not Forgotten

'Have you passed through the square, stranger? I doubt you have... for your head still sits upon your neck.
'They gather the imprisoned in the theatre to the south, and then they drag them out into the square to be tortured... and beheaded. They play with the bodies, and they toss around the heads laughing with those horrible Orkish tongues. After a time they burn the corpses, but the heads they keep, and I do not know to what vile end - nor do I wish to.
'This is war, ${PLAYER}... make no mistake of that. If you are to be one of us, you must know the horrors we have endured. Make for the square and free any of our men that yet live, and slay any of those Troll-men that stand in your way!'

'I saw him scout near the old Palace of King Eldacar, but then he was lost from sight and I had to fall back. The Palace is a grim place, and I believe the Enemy seeks to use it as a stronghold for his servants - the Nazgûl. They spend much of their time up above on those vile beasts, but I have seen them pass among the forces here in Osgiliath and even the Orcs recoil at their approach.
'If he has gone into the palace, he is likely dead, but I wish to know for certain. Search the palace, and return to me here when you have finished. Only then shall we speak of returning to the tunnels.'

'My ally, Echil, has delayed in his return, and I fear that the Easterlings or the flames within have overwhelmed him.
'I must keep guard here, but if you could seek him out, I would be most grateful. He was to collect some of our writings as well as a few of the crumbling works that were never moved from the city long ago for fear that they might turn to dust at a touch.
'Aid him, and then return to me for then I shall heed Mablung's call and sneak back to the culverts.'

'Ah, a friendly face, I hope? I am fine but for a wounded leg... alas, these Easterlings gave me some trouble. Unfortunately for them, I gave them more. They spoke of some \qLord of Pinions\q, but I know none who bear such a title.
'I can return to Candúr, but I have not finished collecting our writings. We keep many of our writings as well as those we have taken from the Enemy's forces within the old archives, but the Easterlings have set flame to it all.

'Faramir and Boromir threw down the Great Bridge when last the Enemy tried to sack Osgiliath, but it appears that the Orcs have found a way to rebuild it... and allow it to bear the weight of enormous siege weapons.

'The host of Minas Morgul intends to siege the White City, but we do not yet know when the attack shall begin.
'We observed the Orcs hauling supplies to the Great Bridge, and have heard a thundering from above in the tunnels, but we do not know their vile designs. They have built several siege weapons on the western bank, but the bridge is broken and cannot bear the weight of the Mûmakil or their siege weapons on the eastern bank. I do not believe they will strike until their weapons can cross the river unhindered!
'If they have found a way to traverse the broken span, it could spell doom for Minas Tirith. Search the Great Bridge, and tell me of any Orkish craftwork you discover!'

When we still held the western shore, we stored a great deal of weapons within the armoury. Yet now, the Orcs and trolls roam its ruins and our weapon-stores are exposed.
'I have not been able to get close enough to gather many, but perhaps you can. If you return these weapons to me, I shall be able to hasten my return to the tunnels.'

'You saved my men from the blades of the Enemy, but not all of my brothers were so fortunate. Over in the western streets, by Meneldil's Square, the half-trolls sharpen their axes and await more men to bring them down upon. Although I did not think it upon our first meeting, you are a bold ${CLASS} and I would count your skills among the finest of my men. My brothers must be avenged, and I would have the honour be yours.

Brunil scowls at you.
'The sick are sick and the well are weary. I would not expect the Lady to come to these halls, but I suppose sending you shows that at least she thinks of us on occasion, toiling away for the health of her people. Tell her that we do what we can with less than we need, and if we complain we do it only as a result of much hardship.'

'Lady Vanyalos wishes to know the mood of the people? That is why Imloth Melui will thrive even in the absence of Lord Forlong, ${PLAYER}. What ruler cares as much about her people as Lady Vanyalos? Very few, I wager!
'When you return to her hall, please bring my assurances that we keep good watch on all who approach the vale. Nothing will threaten Imloth Melui without me hearing of it first!'

'How am I feeling? I have seen better days and better nights, ${CLASS}! Most of the warriors have already left this city, and now I am forced to remain behind and train youths and old men!
'This is a city of healers and potion-makers, not fighters. Even with the finest training I can give to them, this vale is nearly undefended! Tell Lady Vanyalos we must hope the enemy does not come to Imloth Melui, for that is the only way we might survive!'

'I thank you for judging the mood of my people, ${PLAYER}. If I were a potion-maker, I would think two parts despair and one part hopefulness a poor mixture indeed, but perhaps I should be grateful it is no worse.'

'I ask you to speak with the few trusted folk who remain, and learn if they have given up hope of victory and peace in Imloth Melui.
'Hathalon is my Master-at-arms, and he is responsible for training the few warriors who remain. If he has given in to despair, I fear the sickness will spread to his recruits. Merenir, my Captain of the Guard, oversees the flow of refugees by the fountain in the middle of town. And Master Healer Brunil treats the injured within the Hall of the Gentle Hand, on the western side of town. I rely on all three of these good people, and I need to know they are still able to carry out their duties.'
