'It is good to speak with someone new, even if you were driven here by sorrow and war. So many good men have gone away to Minas Tirith, my husband Forlong not least of them. Indeed, he exceeds them all, in girth, at least! My Forlong always had such a sense of humour, and fond of his dinners, too.
'One sound has fled beyond the walls of my city, ${PLAYER}, and I miss it almost as much as Forlong. The sound of laughter has quite vanished from the vale. Has its absence affected my people as grievously as it has me? I ask you to speak with the few trusted folk who remain, and learn if they have given up hope of victory and peace in Imloth Melui.
'Hathalon is my Master-at-arms, and he is responsible for training the few warriors who remain. If he has given in to despair, I fear the sickness will spread to his recruits. Merenir, my Captain of the Guard, oversees the flow of refugees by the fountain in the middle of town. And Master Healer Brunil treats the injured within the Hall of the Gentle Hand, on the western side of town. I rely on all three of these good people, and I need to know they are still able to carry out their duties.'

The Sights of Gondor's Garden

Lady Vanyalos listens intently as you describe your exploration of her city. When you are finished, she sighs happily.
'Thank you, ${PLAYER}. I think I will sleep now, and perhaps I shall dream of the places you have described to me. I am quite transported, in time if not in place, to the years of my youth, when I saw those sights beneath sun-filled skies, with a sun-lit heart.'
Clear water laughs loudly as it spills into the central fountain. Ancient arches peer from behind flower-laden trees.
It is cool in the shaded path and branches of the pines seem to whisper of things long forgotten.
Here the River Erui courses widely through great arches, crashing in a great fall on its journey south.
Where the Erui comes down from the mountains in great cascades, noise and peacefulness blend into one.
Blossom, river, and stonework alike are watched over by slope-side ranks of mountain pine.

'While you tread the paths of Imloth Melui, do not keep your eyes upon your feet! These fair arbors and gardens recall the grandeur of my kingdom's past. I have walked them many times since my youth, and to remember them is the sweetest respite.
'I ask you to take note of the loveliest sights you see here. When you return to me, you may recount them and so I will relive the pleasures I knew, through your fresh eyes.'

'We have to find these Corcur nomads and get them to return Spalvi's treasure. It's not right!'
'Enough conversation. I hear the Corcur approaching! Let us surprise them before they see us!'

'We will cover more ground if we split up, ${PLAYER}. I will circle around and see if I can find the Corcur nomads who attacked me. You should press forward and bring our friend Bingo to the front stairs. I will rejoin you at that point, and if neither of us have recovered my treasure we will then consider scaling the front gate.
'Luck be with you, ${CLASS}, and with me!'

'So the plan is for us to meet up with Spalvi at the front stairs? I think you had better go first, ${PLAYER}. I will be right behind you. Well... perhaps not right behind you, but a goodly distance back. Still behind you, though! Good luck to us!'

'If you could just... give me a moment... to catch my breath...'
Bingo breathes deeply and rubs his aching legs.
'I have never climbed as many steps in all my life as I have today, ${PLAYER}! I hope Spalvi knows how to open this gate, or we will have to turn around and go back, and I am less ready to climb DOWN these steps than I was to climb UP them the first time!'

'I did not find the Corcur that attacked me. They must be behind this gate, and when we get through I will make them pay for their crimes against me and my brothers, and will recover the treasure they stole!'

'You have the look of an adventurer. Did you have business with this Corcur filth? We have already put an end to their thieving. The Rothstone, Skorgrím's Star, is ours once again.'

'This has become quite a pickle, hasn't it? Well, I am sure this is just a simple misunderstanding, and I will sort it all out with these Dourhand fellows.

'What an adventure! This is going to make for quite an exciting chapter!'
'I am not happy about this, ${PLAYER}, but it is a bad situation and this is the only way for everyone to feel safe. I will bring you to the exit, and I implore you not to try anything.'

'As my men and I journeyed to Pelargir from Linhir, we felt a great weight upon us.
'Days without rest and the fatigue of battle had worn on us all, but this filled me with dread in a way that I had never known. And just as it took hold, it faded away, and those of my men that had cowered found their way to their feet once more.
'I have heard many rumours of what happened that day, but I do not know if there is any truth in them. I have not had much time to think on this matter until now, yet it still troubles me.
'Speak to my men of this, and see if there is any truth to these tales.'

'Since the sun was blotted out days ago, we have seen little without the use of torches, but what I saw I shall never forget.
'A flying beast bore a rider in darkened robes and the blade he held reflected what little light passed through the murky sky. As I looked upon him, a great pain overtook me and I turned away.
'When I turned to look again to the sky, he had gone.'

'Why do you ask me to recall such things?
'Before terror pulled me to the ground, I saw the form of a great beast above the ashen clouds. It let out a shrill cry as it flew overhead and then it was gone. I swear to you, I speak true!'

'As with Lord Angbor, I wish I knew what happened in that moment.
'My armour grew heavy and I fell to the ground before I could realize what happened. I regret that I cannot be of more help to you, ${CLASS}.'

'I do not doubt their words, my friend. Could this be one of the nine wraiths of which Aragorn spoke?
'Let us hope it has flown back to its master and shall not harry our journey to Minas Tirith. I will not allow its dread to burden my mind any longer.
'My men and I must press on into Upper Lebennin!'
Above the Ashes

'The Dourhands have launched a number of attacks on my people from a stronghold in the High Crag. That place is called Gabilazan, and it seems to be their base of operations in this stretch of the Misty Mountains.
'Go to Gabilazan and defeat the Dourhands there in order to learn where they are keeping Bingo Boffin!'

'The Dourhands have launched a number of attacks on my people from a stronghold in the High Crag. That place is called Gabilazan, and it seems to be their base of operations in this stretch of the Misty Mountains.
'You defeated many Dourhands but did not find Bingo? You should return to Gabilazan and conduct a more effective search!'

'Wait! Hear me out, ${PLAYER}! I am not your enemy!
'It is true that I deceived you and your hobbit friend, but I did not truly wish for either of you to come to harm. The more I dwelled upon it, the more I realized I could not stand with my brothers in this. When their guard relaxed, I freed Bingo from his cage and we fled from Gabilazan. But in our haste, that poor hobbit did not pay close attention to his footing, and the ground gave way!
'Bingo fell down this hole, and I fear he fell beyond the reach of my voice, for he has not responded to my calls. I think I heard splashing from far below, but I cannot be certain. If he did survive, he will need supplies. If you return to Gabilazan and collect bundles of food and the bottles of water the dwarves carry, we can drop them down the hole after Bingo! If he did survive, he will need any of the water and food we can provide to him.
'Please trust me, ${PLAYER}! I will do all I can to make this right!'
'Well? Where is Bingo?'
'Drop those supplies down the hole, ${PLAYER}! If Bingo survived the fall, he will be glad to have them!'

'I feel really bad about this, ${PLAYER}. I swear to you that I will help you find your friend, wherever he has ended up on my account. I am certain he will be fine, and we will all laugh about this when it is done. I will do some thinking about our next step, but know that I will not abandon the search until we find him safe and sound. I will make this right!'

'I have been trying for days now to convince the people to leave... to seek shelter in Tumladen.
'It is a great and fortified shelter for our people, one of a few in Gondor, and the brother to one that lies within the lands of Rohan. It is more than able to house all of the people of Lebennin and beyond, and its walls would keep us from the growing war in Gondor.
'My folk are headstrong, traveller. They think that since Pelargir has been reclaimed and no foes have come to our doors that we are safe. I do not think it so!
'Would you speak to them for me? Urge them to reconsider before it is too late!'

'I cannot say I'm surprised that many of them ignored your advice to seek shelter... they have paid me no mind either since the skies went dark.

'Skorgrím Dourhand dispatched a number of dwarves to map the caverns of the Misty Mountains. They never returned from Goblin-town, as far as I know, but if you were to find them their maps might tell us if there are any tunnels that could take us to Bingo's location.
'I will meet you at the South High Pass, far to the east, after you have found any helpful maps of the underground cave system.'

Willem Whisker whines at you plaintively, and you can see clearly his frustration at Bingo's absence, and that his search of Erforgh Cleft proved fruitless. You assure him that you will not abandon the hobbit. He snuffles in response, unconvinced.
You speak quiet words to the lynx, telling him that it will take your efforts, Spalvi's efforts, and most of all Willem's efforts, to find the cavern into which Bingo fell and to bring him back into the light.
The lynx snorts, but then grudgingly flicks his ears at you in assent. Now you should return to Spalvi and see if he has learned anything of use from the map you recovered.

'You found Bingo's pet lynx, and he has returned in peace. But why does he bare his sharp teeth at me?' Spalvi asks, suddenly frightened.
You tell him that Willem Whisker is not Bingo's pet, but rather his friend, free to leave at any point.
'I suppose that must be so, ${PLAYER}, for otherwise he would be long gone by now. But look at this map you brought me! I am afraid I have both good news and bad.
'The good news is that according to this map, an underground river runs beneath the mountains and seems to travel a long distance south. It could be that Bingo was carried by the current in safety. The bad news, well...
'I think we should travel to the Longbeard camp in the Western Bruinen Source area of the Misty Mountains for the bad news. I will stay outside the camp proper... do not tell them I am a Dourhand, for I fear my reception would be quite poor.'

'You must be wondering why I wanted to come to this Longbeard camp, ${PLAYER}. If the river runs south for as far as this map would indicate, he may have been carried into the depths of the ancient kingdom of Khazad-dûm. If that is so, we may need to seek the advice of the Longbeards, for I have heard whispers that they may be seeking to gain entrance to that place.'

Spalvi Dourhand told you he would meet you on an overlook in the Southern High Pass area of the Misty Mountains once you recovered some useful maps from the surveyors lost in Goblin-town.

'I feel terrible that Bingo has gotten lost on my account, ${PLAYER}. Our flight from Gabilazan was a hasty one, and I count myself fortunate that I did not stumble over the same unsteady ground as Bingo. He was not so lucky, and fell a long way. There must be a deep cavern down there, and possibly an underground river or stream. I thought I heard a splashing shortly after Bingo fell, but I cannot be certain.
'Such caverns beneath the mountains can be quite extensive. Skorgrím Dourhand ordered that a survey of such tunnels be taken, and he dispatched a number of dwarves to map the caverns of the Misty Mountains. They never returned from Goblin-town, as far as I know, but if you were to find them their maps might tell us if there are any tunnels that might take us to Bingo's location.
'I will meet you at the Southern High Pass, far to the east, after you have found any helpful maps of the underground cave system.'

You give Spalvi the map and he studies it briefly before folding it again.
'I will look at this in a moment, ${PLAYER}, but first I think you should know this. That lynx pet of Bingo's... what was its name again? Willem something? He followed me here at a distance, and I did not like the look in his eye. I think he blames me for his master's disappearance, and while he does have a point on that score, I am worried he does not fully understand that I have had a change of heart and want to make that right. Well, he followed me for a while and then bolted away to the south-east. Do you think he might have caught Bingo's scent? In any case, gauredain live in the Erforgh Cleft down that way, and I wouldn't want anything to happen to him.
'Not before you assure him that I am a friend, anyway!'

'I had begun to lose hope, my friend, but I fear our journey is not yet over. My father's condition is greatly concerning... he looks starved to the bone and his wounds risk infection!
'I wish to look over his wounds, but I do not wish him to see the worry in my eyes. Speak to him, and draw his attention for a moment.'

'My father needs the care of a healer, and Pelargir is no place for the wounded.
'There is a fortified haven nestled in the mountains to the east known as Tumladen. It is a shelter to my people during times of war, and indeed, many of the folk of Lebennin and Lossarnach have already sought refuge within its walls.
'It is there I must bring my father, and with haste.'

Sirgon gazes into the distance at the ruin of Pelargir, his eyes heavy and laden with tears. He musters a weak smile as you approach him.
'I believed none yet lived to search for me... but you have proven me wrong, ${CLASS}. You have renewed the hope that the Men of Harad stole from me as they forced me to watch my city burn.
'I may be but a lord of ruins, but my family lives yet and there is still a dawn waiting to pierce these skies.'

'My father is in dire need of food and rest, and I too grow weary... for bearing this blade and armour so long has tired me greatly. I know you desire to rejoin Lord Angbor, but if you would meet me and my father in Tumladen, I can aid you in readying yourself for the journey ahead.

'I share their concerns, my friend. These are uncertain times, and the fates of many may be decided by the actions of a few.
'It saddens me that their curiosity about the battle at Pelargir must go unanswered for the moment, but the Rangers have bidden me to keep my silence.
'Let us hope that Lord Angbor and Aragorn can reach Minas Tirith in time to repel the Enemy.'

'I have heard tales of many strange things at the battle of Pelargir, but I do not know what truth there is to any of them.
'You travelled with Lord Sirgon and his son... what have you seen?'

'Forgive me, traveller, I only wished to keep my hopes up...'

'When my father and I arrived here, the gate-warden told us of the many folk of Minas Tirith seeking shelter within these walls.
'Many, indeed. From what I can tell, they seem to delight in rumour-mongering, and I do not blame them, for thinking of unbelievable tales and happenings may be the only respite from this encroaching darkness.
'For my part, I have heard little of Minas Tirith in recent days, and I suspect that the folk here might know more. Speak to them while I tend to my father, and tell me of what you learn.'

'I did not believe I would ever think such things, but I am glad to be so far from my home.
'I have heard tales of a great army mustering in the ruins of Osgiliath, and though the Steward has sent his son, I fear for us all in the coming days.'

'A ${CLASS} or not, you would be wise to seek shelter here, traveller. The Steward showed great wisdom in sending us to safety.
'Minas Tirith's defences are great, but even greater are the forces of the Enemy who would see it torn down stone by stone!'

'Do you know what happened in Pelargir? The people of Glaniath that have come to Tumladen have told of hearing a great chorus of screams, even from so far away.
'What happened to the Corsairs and why do their ships still sail on the Anduin? Lord Angbor has come, and he does not speak to us as openly as he once did.'
You tell the woman only that you cannot speak on the matter.
'Why do you keep secrets from us? Does the war go so poorly?'

'Do you think we'll be safe here? My mother says we will be, but she hasn't spoken much since we arrived here.
'Father stayed in Minas Tirith to guard the gates, but I wish he had come along with us.
'If you travel that way, you'll look after him, won't you?'

'I know we are in a hurry to catch up to the Iron Garrison and see if Bingo can be found within Khazad-dûm, but I want to make a statement to some of these Elves. 'I do not wish to speak to the Longbeard who runs this camp, for fear of betraying my heritage, but you should talk to him and see what you can learn of this expedition to Khazad-dûm.'

'You think your friend Bingo might have been washed by an underground river south to Khazad-dûm? Well, that is quite a long way, but if you seek to enter those halls you will be in good company. 'You must forgive me if I am too direct, but I wish to learn more of the battle at Pelargir. You have travelled here safely and our walls remain unbreached, so I can only assume you found victory, but I am curious as to how.
'The Corsairs had many men... certainly many more than we could equal, especially after the great mustering at my brother's city. How then did they fail? Was it the valour of a few great men? And most curious of all... why do their ships still sail on the Anduin?
'Lord Angbor has just arrived, so I am told, so perhaps I shall ask him as well.'
You tell Lady Terenis that both you and Lord Angbor have taken an oath to keep secret the truth of the battle of Pelargir.
'Oh, have you now? I offer you a choice, ${PLAYER}... either tell me of the truth, convince Lord Angbor to speak of the battle, or I shall have you thrown into a cell for plotting against the people of Gondor.'

'It is good to see you again, ${PLAYER}! I trust you followed the boy on his errand?
'I had a suspicion you would, my friend, for you are a ${RACE} of honour. Yet, if what you say is true, Aragorn was wise to send me here. The Lady has no such power, I assure you. You need not fear imprisonment.
'You see, I bear a missive on his behalf meant for the Lady's eyes only. The war shall not wait upon her stubbornness, so let us quell her curiosity and continue to the East.'

You think for a moment, and decide that 'Bingo-dropper' or Hobbit-misplacer' are not the most complimentary of titles.

'I have something to ask of you, ${PLAYER}. Few others have heard me on this matter, but you seem the kind to heed the tales of strangers.
'In my youth, I often travelled the lands of Lebennin and spent much time upon the banks of its rivers. I knew well of the legends of our people as did all other children of Lebennin, but that was not the reason for my wandering. My father had taken ill in summer, and the disease claimed him by spring. My mother went silent for a year's time, and all looked upon me as a child of madness and misfortune. My only respite was in walking the banks of the Five Rivers, and so I went.
'The Erui was nearest to my home, and it, too, knew well of tragedy and death. It was there that King Eldacar slew the Usurper long ago, but many others fell and bloodied its shallows before the battle came to an end. It is said that the last of the Five Sisters, the Lone Lady of Erui, once looked upon our people with fondness, but the horrors that occurred in her waters led her to spirit herself away. It may seem a different tale from my own, but I have not yet reached its ending....
'You see, I sat near the falls at the Crossings one day and was overcome by the sadness of my family's fate. As I dried my tears, I saw something that has not left my mind in all my years. I saw the image of a woman's face gazing upon me from behind the falls. I dashed into the water and called out, but as soon as I drew close to the falls, the face had gone. To this day, I know the Lone Lady appeared before me and ever since, I have held close my belief in the Sisters.
'The Haradrim do not respect our lands or rivers as we do, and they do not know to fear the ire of the Five Sisters. The Lone Lady should not again suffer the blood of Men in her waters, and I ask that you seek her out at the Crossings as I once did. May she watch over Lebennin and keep us from the evils of war!'

Baranor can be found in Arnach, which can be reached by travelling east across the Erui at the Crossings or by use of the bridge near the beacon Minlos.
Lady Terenis has asked you to travel east to Arnach and aid the guards there in keeping the people of Lossarnach from harm.
Talk to Baranor in Arnach

'${PLAYER}, you have done much for me and my people, but I cannot keep you here any longer.
'Sleep has not come easily to me of late, but even when I find rest, my dreams have grown as dark as the skies. I have seen my brother fall to madness, the deaths of my sons, and great beasts of terror marching upon Minas Tirith. What sickness of the mind takes hold that would conjure such foul thoughts? I know not if any of these shall come to pass, but I must work to prevent them if I might. Lord Angbor has his own path to forge into the East, but I would ask something else of you.
'You may be the last to heed my words... so I beg you to travel to Arnach and speak to a warrior called Baranor. It may delay you, and it may even change your course, but I cannot let those that I love fall to such horrors.'

'If the Lady has sent you, I shall not deny your aid. Too many troubles have come to Lossarnach of late... and I fear I cannot resolve them all.
'Curious, though, that Lady Terenis sent you. Has she told you much of her sister, Lady Vanyalos? I suspect not. The two of them have not spoken for years... all over Lord Forlong, no less.
'Know this, I will not involve myself in the Sisters' feud, but I shall tell Lady Vanyalos of your intent to aid us.'
Disquieting Dreams
Lady Terenis grows troubled by increasingly dark dreams of her brother and her estranged sister.
Talk to Lady Terenis in Tumladen
Rage of the Erui

'You speak of unbelievable things, ${PLAYER}, but you assure me that my people are safe, so I shall hold your words to be true.
'This Glassiel you spoke of in Halach, she seems to be a most interesting woman and one whom I would like to speak with in time. Ah, but such things are for another day...
'I have one last thing to ask of you, my friend.'

'What is this armour you lay before me? An ornate piece despite such age and wear... it can be none other than the armour worn by the Usurper himself!
'As much as I wish to trust your words, I cannot fathom these tales you tell of the Five Sisters... they are naught but fables told to the young. Yet, the river has held close a relic of our bloody history, and I would not dishonour our people by ignoring such a find!
'I shall send this armour to Lord Sirgon and see it returned to Pelargir until this war comes to an end. Perhaps the Lady would like to hear more of your tale, but I can tarry no longer in Lebennin.'
'We will do what we must, ${PLAYER}. Are you prepared?'

Roamingstar can be found in her glade in north-eastern Dor-en-Ernil.
Roamingstar has rallied her Sisters and is now prepared to confront the Lone Lady. You should speak to her when you are ready.

Angbor can be found on a hill to the west of the Crossings of Erui.
You have aided Roamingstar and her Sisters in calming the Lone Lady's rage, and have also recovered pieces of Castamir's armour. You should bring the armour to Angbor near the Crossings of Erui.
Talk to Roamingstar, Maiden of Gilrain

'The Lone Lady...
'She has always been the most distant of my Sisters, but I never sensed such darkness within her. Only a great sadness... a sadness she has carried with her for many of your years. She never spoke much to us... never even speaking of her true name, but I wish she had come to us with her troubles. We have all seen horrors in the long years we have spent in these lands - she must know that she does not stand alone!
'The Men of Lebennin fought brother against brother and spilled much blood in her waters, but now you say the southern Men that seek to cross her waters are met by rotting suits of armour? I fear she will not be calmed easily, but my Sisters and I must reach her somehow.
'Travel to the Crossings of Erui... for it is there that my Sisters and I shall meet you. We shall put an end to this, no matter what action must be taken!'

Lady Terenis can be found in the Great Hall of Tumladen.
You have delivered Castamir's armour to Angbor, and should now speak to Lady Terenis.
The Sisters of Lebennin seek to calm their Sister's fury before it consumes both the Enemy and the people of Gondor alike.
Deliver Castamir's armour to Angbor near the Crossings of Erui
'Thank you, ${PLAYER}. You have brought peace to my troubled heart by shattering those war-horns. Let us hope my dream of them saw true.'

Indir can be found in Arnach, near the keep.

'There is no doubt in my heart: the Haradrim will launch an assault on Arnach. I lay awake at night, imagining how it will go, and last night I dreamt they came with a great blowing of horns. Imagine my surprise when one of my most keen-eyed men told me he had seen great war-horns among the Southron camps!
'Would you humour my whim, ${RACE}? You seem intrepid enough to do the deed. I believe they intend to use these war-horns to call the attack. If the horns were sabotaged, they may be unable to assail us in one overwhelming force. And perhaps, just perhaps, we might withstand them!'

'My captain is held prisoner by one of the Nazgûl... never has there been a darker day in my life.
'I know the strength of Faramir's resolve well, but so too do I know the might of the Enemy. If he yet lives and the wraith speaks true, we must act swiftly!'

The Black Blade of Lebennin and his captive can be found atop the Dome of Stars.
Mablung has asked you to free Fararmir from the Black Blade of Lebennin and attempt to banish his spirit before the coming battle.
<rgb=#FF0000>Note: You must complete \qThe Dome of Stars\q instance to complete this quest.</rgb>

You have triumphed over the Black Blade of Lebennin if only for a moment, and learned of Faramir's fate. You should return to Mablung with this news.
Free Faramir from the Dome of Stars
Confront and defeat the Black Blade of Lebennin

'I know not if Faramir lives or if this is merely one of the Nazgûl's vile designs to draw the last of us from hiding. I cannot know, and it pains me to face such uncertainty without the guidance of our captain.
'The Dome of Stars lies in the heart of the Enemy's forces and until they wrested control of the western city, it was there that the leaders of the host oversaw their cruel servants. It is still a place of great evil, and dread grips the entire isle on which it stands.
'The Enemy has thrown down the western bridge to the Dome, so the only way into the structure is across the eastern bridge by Rómendacil's Square. The Enemy has heightened their guard near the culverts, so I can guide you to the western side of the Great Bridge safely, but no further.
'Do not dare face the Black Blade alone, for you will need all the allies you can muster to stand against such evil. Faramir's fate may well rest in your hands, my friend. May your fellowship be the light to pierce these ashen skies...'
<rgb=#FF0000>Note: You must complete \qThe Dome of Stars\q instance to complete this quest.</rgb>

'You have come... seeking Faramir?
Struggling to speak, Norhún's coughs are wet with blood.
'He... is gone - gone from Osgiliath. We had made it to the western gates when the shadow... fell upon us. I threw myself in its path, and soon I was carried above by a terrible, winged beast. From the sky, I saw my captain escape... he passed along the Causeway and through the Rammas Echor before I lost sight of him.
'Tell the others of his fate, for they must know that he still lives!
'The wraith... he...'
Norhún's breath slows, and is still.

'I cannot believe it! I felt a cold rush pass over the city as I looked to the Dome outside the culverts... could that have been his foul spirit sent away to the Land of Shadow?
'You have done a truly great thing, my friend, but Faramir is not among your number.... Tell me, ${PLAYER}, what has become of my captain?'
Ashes and Stars, Chapter 6
The Nazgûl's lies are revealed, for Norhún's noble sacrifice allowed Faramir to escape Osgiliath alive!
One of the Nazgûl, the Black Blade of Lebennin, has revealed himself as Faramir's captor and now holds the captain of the South-rangers atop the Dome of Stars.
Ashes and Stars, Chapter 1
'You should speak to Damrod at once, my friend. With his own eyes, he saw the mighty blow Faramir dealt to the host of Minas Morgul and knows well of the chaos that followed.'

Damrod can be found in the culverts of Osgiliath.
Mablung has asked you to speak to Damrod about Faramir's daring attack that allowed many of their number to escape the city.

Mablung can be found in the culverts of Osgiliath.
You have spoken to Damrod about Faramir's gambit, and should now speak to Mablung about searching for Faramir in the tunnels under Osgiliath.
Talk to Mablung

'Our captain, Faramir, is lost. All of our number became separated after he dealt a great blow to the Enemy's forces, and we only realized our loss after we regrouped here in the culverts.
'To my dismay, I was unaware of Faramir's ploy. It must have been a plan he put into action swiftly, but such haste did not lessen its impact. I heard a great shriek in the distance, like the deafening sounding of a Mûmak's trunk, but shrill as the pitch of a bat's cry. No sooner had the forces of the Enemy rallied to its source, and we were overwhelmed. We scattered, leading the foes with us, but we all made for the western gates... for our escape.
'I did not make it so far - great trolls blocked my advance, and I was forced to abandon my escape. I fled into the culverts and there I found the others. So it has been...
'If Faramir made it beyond the western gates, he may yet live, but that is unknown to us all. Damrod, one of my most trusted men, saw first-hand the fury Faramir loosed upon the Enemy. While he knows little else of Faramir's fate, all must be told of our captain's valour... especially if it may be his last.'

'Mablung wishes for me to tell you of Faramir's daring assault? I shall tell it then, but until he is found, it shall have no ending.
'We had crossed to the eastern side of the city to disrupt the Enemy's forces before they could rally again. We were outnumbered, but we held the eastern end of the north-bridge for a time... until the most vile of the Enemy's forces took notice of us.
'A great, winged beast swooped down and swept a crowd of men aside, friend and foe alike, as if they were leaves amid the winds of a storm. Its wings blotted out the sun, and many of our number fled at once, but my captain and I held strong.
'Faramir took a spear from one of the fallen and called the beast as it clawed at the dead. Before I could stop him, he charged at the beast and thrust the spear into its dark heart. What happened then is a blur to me, for it let loose a great cry and thrashed in a fury as my captain and I fled to the west.
'We became separated on the bridge-rafts, and soon, forces of the Haradrim had cut me off from him completely. I was forced to retreat into the culverts, and that is where my story ends for now. Mablung seems to have a plan for you, and I would not deny him his chance to speak.
'Let us see what our next move shall be!'

'${PLAYER}, now you know of our plight. Will you stay and aid us here? Or do you heed the call of another? If you stay, our search shall begin at once, else I shall have to proceed with caution... for too few men still stand among us, and to weaken our guard is to invite defeat.
'If Faramir yet lives, I shall find my captain and have him lead his men to freedom beyond the Rammas Echor!'
Forced into the tunnels under Osgiliath after a daring ploy by Faramir, the Rangers of Ithilien, led by Mablung, now hope to reunite with their lost captain.

'Lúmithil was a bold Ranger, and I am saddened that the Enemy twisted him into something so vile. His death shall be mourned, and, if I were to have my way, avenged! Sadly, a foe who bears no form does not make vengeance an easy task...
'While I am glad that Faramir did not meet with such a fate, we are no closer to finding him, and I fear our trail has gone cold.
'Allow me a moment to ponder our course of action, and I shall speak to you once more.'
You have recovered Faramir's cloak, but his whereabouts still remain unknown...

The mysterious Ranger can be found somewhere within the ruined city of Osgiliath.
Mablung has asked you to search the ruined city for any sign of the mysterious Ranger you encountered in the sunken tunnels.
<rgb=#FF0000>Note: You must complete \qThe Ruined City\q instance to complete this quest.</rgb>
Pursue and confront the mysterious Ranger
Reclaim Faramir's cloak from the fallen Ranger

'I do not know what compels this man to flee at our approach, but it is clear that we must capture him before his madness can overtake him. His wound needs the care of a practiced healer, and yet he can still run as fast as any of our number. I fear that this bodes ill for us, ${PLAYER}, but I do not wish to abandon hope.
'Whether he is friend or foe, I would have you subdue him for his mind is not his own. You must not lose his trail this time, or I fear we will never have another opportunity to learn of his identity.
'Throughout your pursuit, he remained in the southern streets of the ruined city, so I would have you begin your search there once again. However, I suggest you bring your allies, for with them it may be easier to subdue this strange man and return to us in the culverts.'
<rgb=#FF0000>Note: You must complete \qThe Ruined City\q instance to complete this quest.</rgb>
Ashes and Stars, Chapter 4

The fallen Ranger can be found inside the Palace of Eldacar.
You have defeated the corrupted Ranger bearing the cloak of Faramir and should now reclaim it for the Rangers of Ithilien.

Mablung can be found in the culverts of Osgiliath.
You have defeated the corrupted Ranger that bore Faramir's cloak. You should now return the cloak to Mablung.
Garbed in the tattered remains of Faramir's cloak, the corrupted Ranger falls defeated!
Deliver the remains of Faramir's cloak to Mablung

Search further in the depths of Osgiliath
Approach the mysterious Ranger

'The tidings you bear disturb me, ${PLAYER}. The letter you bear mentions that terrible wraith thrust a blade into his chest, but that he did not die - only his body began to wither. It then reads only of a man succumbing to madness, and I fear his mind can only have grown more twisted since its writing.
'For Faramir to come to such an end would be devastating, and I fear that we must uncover this man's identity before our search can continue elsewhere. There are many ways out of these tunnels, but his flight cannot have taken him far from the culverts.'
'What news have you of your search, ${PLAYER}? There are many places where Faramir may have sought refuge in this sunken labyrinth, and I fear we shall not have time to search them all.'
The note is hastily-written and swiftly descends into madness and incoherence...
A mysterious Ranger stands near the gates...
The Ranger suddenly dashes away into the dark of the tunnels!

Faramir might be found somewhere within the sunken labyrinth beneath Osgiliath.

<rgb=#FF0000>You must complete the \qSunken Labyrinth\q instance to complete this quest.</rgb>

Mablung can be found in the culverts of Osgiliath.
You have recovered a troubling letter and encountered a strange hooded Ranger in the sunken tunnels of Osgiliath. You should now return to Mablung.

The letter can be found at the make-shift camp-site in the sunken labyrinth beneath Osgiliath.
You have discovered a small, empty camp-site in the tunnels beneath Osgiliath. You should take the note and examine it before pressing onward.

Faramir might be found somewhere within the sunken labyrinth beneath Osgiliath.
You have not yet found Faramir in the tunnels beneath Osgiliath, but you should continue your search deeper in the labyrinth.
Search for Faramir in the depths of Osgiliath
Examine the note at the abandoned camp-site

'We must begin our search, ${PLAYER}, and I would have us begin here in the culverts where we can move beneath the notice of the Morgul-host above. It is possible that Faramir also fled into the tunnels as we did when the fighting erupted after he speared the fell-beast, but there are many places he may have sought refuge - and too few of us to spare from our posts.
'Search the depths, but do not search alone. These tunnels wind far underneath the city as a vast, sunken labyrinth, and it is likely that some of the Enemy's forces have travelled down into the dark - unwittingly or not.'
<rgb=#FF0000>Note: You must complete the \qSunken Labyrinth\q instance to complete this quest.</rgb>
Ashes and Stars, Chapter 2

The Ranger is standing near the gate to Muzgásh's chamber in the sunken labyrinth.

Desperate to learn of their lost captain's fate, Mablung and Damrod begin their search for Faramir in the winding tunnels beneath Osgiliath.
'Let none forget the sacrifice of Norhún!'
'We have struck a devastating blow, but the Morgul-host still threatens the White City!'
'While Faramir lives, our hope shall not be broken!'

Damrod can be found in the culverts of Osgiliath.
Mablung has asked you to tell Damrod of Faramir's escape from Osgiliath.

Mablung can be found in the culverts of Osgiliath.

Talk to Damrod
Talk to Mablung

'What has become of Faramir, ${PLAYER}? Were you too late to save him?'
You tell Mablung of Norhún's sacrifice and his bravery in allowing Faramir to escape from the western gates of Osgiliath.
'My captain lives yet! I shall rest easier knowing Faramir made it past the Gates of the Sun, even though his fate beyond remains unclear. Such a sacrifice... Norhún shall be hailed as a hero among my people, I swear it.'
Mablung turns to Damrod and gestures for him to listen.
'Damrod, have you heard this joyous news?'

'You slew the wraith? Is such a feat possible? The servants of the Dark Lord do not suffer defeat easily, my friend... but let us hope that we shall be free of his evil for a time.
'Faramir has escaped beyond the Causeway Forts into the Pelennor Fields? This is a joyous turn, indeed, but I fear we must not forget the horrors looming above.
'I sense the war shall soon reach a turning point, and I hope you will be among us at that critical hour.'

'As merry a day as this may be, Damrod speaks true.
'The might of the Morgul-host stands poised to spill forth into the Pelennor Fields and to the very walls of Minas Tirith. Through your efforts, we have slowed their advance, but the thousands that rally above cannot be stopped... not by us alone.
'Take your leave, ${PLAYER}, and rest well after this victory... but be ready. For on the morrow, the war for Gondor shall truly begin!'
Ashes and Stars, Chapter 7
Through Norhún's steadfast loyalty and sacrifice, Faramir was able to escape the western gates of Osgiliath. Their hope restored, Mablung and his men make ready for the journey ahead.
Talk to Mablung of the Nazgûl's captive

'It cannot be! Hope is lost, ${PLAYER}. None can stand against the servants of the Dark Lord... their might is limitless!
'Even if this Nazgûl - this \qBlack Blade\q speaks true, how can we be assured that Faramir's fate will be any different than that of Lúmithil? Our captain may already serve the Dark Lord, if still he lives.'
The splintered remains of the spear that Faramir used to slay the fell-beast lay nearby...

The site where Faramir speared the great fell-beast can be found to the north-east of the Dome of Stars.
In desperation, Mablung has asked you to search the site where Faramir speared a fell-beast in hopes of uncovering where he may have gone.

The broken spear can be found near the ruined bridge to the north-east of the Dome of Stars.

Search the site where Faramir slew the fell-beast
Examine Faramir's broken spear

'We are without direction, my friend. The trail is cold, and none that live know of Faramir's fate. Alas for poor Lúmithil... may he be at peace.
'I have thought much on where our search might continue, and one thought has lingered in my mind. You have done much for us, but this may be too perilous a task to put upon you. Since our flight into the culverts, none of us have dared to return to the site where Faramir speared the great fell-beast.
'I thought our course wise, and it may still be, but I must ask you to travel there, my friend. What became of the beast? Did it fall as we thought? Has some hidden insight to our captain's flight gone unnoticed? These thoughts trouble my mind, ${PLAYER}, and I cannot rest.
'If you dare, travel far to the north-east, beyond the Dome of Stars... and search by the broken north-bridge. When you find Faramir's spear, you shall know you have found the site.'
Ashes and Stars, Chapter 5

'We must hasten our search, and work to corner this man - be he friend or turned foe.'
As you examine the necklace, the Ranger dashes up a nearby staircase!
As you examine the shield, the Ranger darts out beneath the broken bridge and flees!

Signs of the Ranger's passing can likely be found in southern Osgiliath, especially around the wharfs and nearby ruins.
Mablung has asked you to pursue the mysterious Ranger you encountered in the sunken tunnels of Osgiliath. By the way he took to escape, Mablung suggest searching the wharfs and the nearby ruins.

'You have told me much of this strange man, ${PLAYER}, but most troubling is your description of his clothing.
'By your account, he bears a cloak that belonged to none but our captain, Faramir. If this man is Faramir, our cause is lost, and we should forge a new strategy to escape the city before dawn. However, if he is not - who would be so bold as to take up a mantle beyond his standing and elude the aid of his brethren?
'Search the southern ways of the city, on both shores of the Anduin, for his path would lead him either to the camps of the Haradrim or the ruins of the armoury across the Orkish bridge-rafts. Track him, and capture him if you must - for we must learn of his identity!'
Ashes and Stars, Chapter 3

Mablung can be found in the culverts of Osgiliath.
You have lost the trail of the mysterious Ranger, and should now report his elusiveness to Mablung.
Disturbed by the note you recovered and your sighting of a mysterious Ranger in the depths of Osgiliath, Mablung sends you to the streets above to track this elusive stranger.
Talk to Lady Vanyalos in her hall on the north-east rise of Imloth Melui
A Visit to a Dreamer

'Forgive me, ${CLASS}. This is exactly Lady Vanyalos's dream, as she told it to me: a ${RACE}, looking as you, coming up this road under a strangely darkened sky. The description fits exactly!
'Lady Vanyalos will want to speak with you, and at once! You can find her within her hall on the north-east rise. I do not pretend to understand how this can be, but she will certainly be filled with wonder at seeing her dream made flesh. What can this mean?'

'Welcome to Imloth Melui, good traveller. Captain Merenir believes it was you I saw in my dream? Are you the only traveller of your kind who will visit us during this strange darkness, I wonder? Will Merenir send me every one who does? He is a good captain but perhaps not the best interpreter of dreams.
'Still, it is true and well known that I and those of my blood have had dreams of great portent. Are you a bearer of good tidings, ${PLAYER}, or ill? And if you were, would you know the difference?'

Lady Vanyalos can be found in the great hall on the north-east rise of Imloth Melui.
Merenir has asked you to pay a visit to Lady Vanyalos, insisting that somehow she dreamed of you.
It seems that your appearance and the timing of your arrival in Imloth Melui bears a striking resemblance to a dream Lady Vanyalos had the night before.

'I have had another thought, ${PLAYER}. If your friend Bingo wishes to write a complete study of the Elves, I would be doing him and his future readers a tremendous disservice if I did not supply him with one more book.
'This is the tome, my studious friend! It contains many of the songs of my people, and within their lines Bingo will find much to feed both his mind and his heart. Sad songs there are, but also songs of triumph and of glad delight.
'The other books I have provided will tell him of Beren and Lúthien, or of Gil-galad, but a true understanding of what they mean to my people can only be found in song.'

'You have returned, and with a book about the Elves? Lovely! I will take that from you, and get to work reading... at... once...'
Bingo trails off as he sees the stack of books you have for him.
'I asked for a single book, ${PLAYER}, and if I am being honest I was rather hoping for a slim volume. But you have returned with three others, and not a one of them of trifling size! If I were to set about reading these, my journey would be halted for a month or more! I wanted to write a chapter about Elves, not a dozen!
'Well, I thank you for the material, and I will read for a time. But it seems to me that a full understanding of the Elves would take a lifetime... or two! Is this why they live such a long time, the better to understand their own complexity? My goodness!'
<rgb=#00FF00>Bert Bartleby has arrived outside the gate to Caras Galadhon.</rgb>
<rgb=#FF0000>Next week: 'A Taste of War' (Recommended Level: 63, and it is further recommended that you have gained access to Mirkwood by obtaining Book 9, Foreword: 'The Dark Shore' from Calengoth at the docks, and completing his quest chain through 'Hilltop Assault.')</rgb>
'Your friend Bingo will be fully prepared to write of the Elves once you return to him with those books!'

'I am not sure what to make of our mysterious hosts, ${PLAYER}! They certainly seemed welcoming, but they are simply so... so...
'I do not know what word I can use to describe them! They seemed somehow other-worldly, but at the same time very much a part of this land. It strikes me as very odd that they can be both, but that is the impression they gave to me!'
Bingo suddenly slaps his forehead.
'I forgot to ask them my questions! If I am going to describe our stay in the Golden Wood for my book, I need to have a better understanding of the Elves and their Lord and Lady. If you can meet the Keeper of Stories that was mentioned by Lady Galadriel, perhaps I can borrow a book that will help me learn about Lothlórien and its people? Find Pennasseth at Cerin Nauth, and see if she will lend me such a book!'

'Welcome to Lothlórien, ${PLAYER}. I have already heard tell of your deeds, and any aid I can provide to you will be gladly given.'
You explain that Bingo wishes to write a chapter in his book about the Elves of the Golden Wood, and he was hoping that Pennasseth might be able to lend him a book he could study for that purpose.
'It is a noble thing, ${PLAYER}, to seek knowledge of a subject about which you know little. I will happily give to Bingo a book that contains some accounts of the history of the Elves. Beware! The book is many pages, but even so it will not cover the entirety of its subject! What book could hope to do so?'

'No, do not go just yet! I have given to you a book of history, for if Bingo is to understand my people, he will need to know from where they came, and the trials they faced in their journeys to this point. But that is not all! There are so many names and places described in that book that I fear your friend will be quite overwhelmed and confused.
'To that end, take too this book of maps. With it he will obtain a full understanding of the many places in which Elves have lived, and perhaps he will also attain an appreciation for the great scope and vastness of this Middle-earth, and the lands beyond!'

'If your friend Bingo examines those books, he will have a basic understanding of the history of the Elves and the lands that shaped their journeys, but it is still not enough. Such a study would leave out one of the most important aspects of my people's experience: the works of Art they fashion, and the Art that fashions them!
'This book contains descriptions of many such works, and in some sad cases that is all that remains, for many have been lost to the ravages of Time and the plots of the Enemy. From these pages, Bingo will learn much about the Elves that he can learn nowhere else!'

'Are you ready? Let us go down to that stand of trees, but keep your eyes open for more Orcs! The foul creatures seem to be everywhere in this land, despite its natural beauty, or perhaps that is what draws them here... so they can despoil it!'

'If I am going to describe our stay in the Golden Wood, I need to have a better understanding of the Elves and their Lord and Lady. If you can meet the Keeper of Stories that was mentioned by Lady Galadriel, perhaps I can borrow a book that will help me learn about Lothlórien and its people? Find Pennasseth at Cerin Nauth, and see if she will lend me such a book!'

'We should take a look at Durin's Stone, and perhaps I can sketch an illustration of it for my book. If we run into any dangers near the stone, you will take care of them, yes? My skill is with the quill, you know. Ha! You see?'

'I am glad we were able to see Durin's Stone, ${PLAYER}, and I am gladder still that you managed to defeat some of the vile foes that stalk through this land! This would be a lovely place if it were not for their foul presence.
'Look at this view! Have you ever seen such a vibrant shade to the leaves of trees before, and in this season? Unbelievable! Speak to me when you are rested from your recent exertions, and we can go down to the stand of trees together. We must keep our eyes open for more Orcs, of course!'
'I will meet you south-east of Durin's Stone, my friend! There is a waterfall near there that I simply must see!'

'I can hardly believe that we have been invited into the Golden Wood, ${PLAYER}, and that we are being given a personal tour of Caras Galadhon!
'I have so many questions to ask the Elves of this place. What brought them to settle here, and for how long have they lived in Lothlórien? Do they live lives of solitude, or do they travel? The sight of an Elf is a very rare thing in the Shire!
'I hope they do not think my questions rude, but I have to know as much about their people as I can, or my book will suffer for such a lack of knowledge!'

'I hope your friend is not offended! Our welcome to this wood is sincere, and it is my hope he will find it a place of peace and rest before continuing his journey.
'I will speak to the sentries at the gate of Caras Galadhon. The three of you will be welcome within the city from this point.'

'My mirror shows me many things, and not all of them will come to pass. I know of your own journey, and I know of young Bingo's as well. Is he truly surprised that his feline companion is on a journey of his own? It may be a useful reminder to him that all of us have our own paths to tread in this world, and while they may intertwine for a time, they will not forever.
'My own time in this land that I love will soon be ended, and my journey will take me elsewhere. For now, it is my pleasure to welcome all of you to Caras Galadhon. If you desire to learn more, seek out Pennasseth, our Keeper of Stories, at Cerin Nauth.'

'I am ashamed to admit that I never gave a thought to Willem Whisker's own journey, and now my face is as red as can be! What do you suppose he's seeking? If it is in my power to help him find it, I will do everything I can!
'You should have told me earlier, Willem!'
'Well, they have given me much to think about, that is for certain!'
You have come with Bingo a good distance into the Dimrill Dale, and a path leads to the east in the direction of the Golden Wood.
You defended Bingo from attack by an Orc raiding party, and now the hobbit is ready to continue his relaxing stroll through the Dimrill Dale.

'It is a good day for walking! The cool, crisp air puts me almost in mind of a leisurely stroll along the lanes of the Shire! And yet we are so far from the Westfarthing... indeed, we are so far to the east of the Eastfarthing that I have quite lost track of the miles!
'I can see the golden hue of the woods down this slope, ${PLAYER}. Let us walk and see what awaits us beneath the canopy!'

'Those Orcs wanted to spoil our relaxing stroll, but I'd say you countered their designs most effectively!
'Let us not dwell upon the shadows that darkened our path, but focus instead on the bright future that awaits us beneath the golden-hued sun and the trees ahead! Let us continue, and perhaps at a quicker pace!'

'${PLAYER}, we have been expecting you and your friends. The Lady of Lórien gave me particular instruction to set forth from the Golden Wood in search of you and your companions. I am pleased to see you have not come to harm.
'If your friend is willing, I would be happy to bring you beyond the bounds and before the Lord and Lady.'

'Ah, we have encountered a welcoming party, ${PLAYER}, and we seem to be expected! What a lovely turn of events!
'I will be delighted to accompany these fellows. Onward to the Golden Wood!'

'We showed those Orcs a thing or two, that's for sure!'

'I am not keen on participating in any battles, but I do believe that it is my authorial responsibility to see the inside of Mirkwood if my book is to be complete. I spoke with an Elf named Calengoth at the docks, but he refused my request that I be allowed across the river! He said he would not be responsible for my safety. Can you believe that?
'Well, I have had a capital idea! If we can prove that I am not afraid of Orcs, Calengoth will have no choice but to recognize that I deserve to cross the river! I have heard that Orcs have invaded an area in the north-western reaches of the Golden Wood, and that an Elf named Faelleron needs help to combat them. Let us find him and volunteer to help!'
'This is Faelleron. Tell him that I am not afraid of Orcs, and I would love to prove it to him!'

'You are the companion of Bingo Boffin? He is an amusing fellow, and insists that he is not afraid of Orcs. He asked me to write this note granting him permission to fight our foes, and I have complied, though on some level I must doubt whether this is wise!
'Here is the parchment. May it put his mind at rest, and if you will fight the Orcs in Fanuidhol, to the north, this simple act of script may prove worth the time and the ink!'

'I cannot say I agree with Faelleron's assessment, but this parchment does relieve me of any responsibility should anything happen to Bingo within the forest. I will no longer prevent him from crossing into Mirkwood, but know that you will need to survive the landing and do as the Golden Host commands before Bingo will be free to explore.'
'I am ready to begin the journey into Mirkwood, ${PLAYER}!'

'What excitement, ${PLAYER}! The Golden Host and the Rangers have crossed into Mirkwood and they are making their way toward a frightful-sounding stronghold in the south-east. I am glad to have seen within the woods, but I think I will leave a survey of this Dol Guldur to the experts!
'Instead, I think I will stay here by the fire and work on my book. This is not the most welcoming of taverns, but at least it is warm! I do wonder about the history of this place, though. This is one of the few buildings that seems to still be intact. Why not go explore the rest of the town, and report back to me when you have seen the sights? I will be here!'
<rgb=#00FF00>Bert Bartleby has arrived outside the Haunted Inn, in the Dourstocks of Mirkwood.</rgb>

'Hmm, your description of the areas nearby make them sound much as I expected, ${PLAYER}: tumbled down and in disrepair. Folk have not lived in this town for a very long time, and it feels to me that unhappiness lies upon it like a shroud.
'While you were gone I spoke with one of the Rangers, Aduiallin, and she gave me a lovely book of recipes. Perhaps I will work to bring some measure of cheer and comfort to this tavern by preparing one of the recipes from this book. Yes, that will be just the thing! But I will need to choose one to make, and that will not be an easy task!'

'I gave you a note granting permission to Bingo Boffin to fight the Orcs. Now go north-west to Fanuidhol and do so!'

'Well done, my friends! I am pleased that you have returned from your campaign against the Orcs in good health and with victory. It seems you did not really need my permission at all, but I am glad to have granted it all the same.'

'We did it, ${PLAYER}, we did it, and we also made certain the Orcs that threaten the Golden Wood know it to be well-defended by adventuring types such as ourselves!'
Bingo lowers his voice conspiratorially.
'And did you notice? The note that Faelleron wrote for us says that we have permission to engage with the enemies of Lothlórien, but it does not specify WHERE those enemies are to be found! Bring that parchment to Calengoth at the docks, and he will have no choice but to bring me across the river into Mirkwood!'

'I am sorry, but I told your friend that the Golden Host is beginning a dangerous assault, and I will not be responsible for his well-being. He would be better served remaining behind and writing in relative safety. What is this?'
You hand Calengoth the note from Faelleron, and he looks at it with surprise.

Bingo is in the Haunted Inn, located in the Dourstocks of Mirkwood.
You have learned that Adolinda is not a Ranger at all, but is instead a resident of Audaghaim lingering beneath a curse from long ago.

'I am sorry I deceived the two of you. My name is Adolinda, and I lived in Audaghaim long ago. A great evil was committed here, and I did not speak against it; for that I am cursed, never to find rest or peace.
'I arranged for your friend to find my old book of recipes, for I wanted nothing more than to pass on the activities that gave me such joy in life, when joy was possible. But I know now that it can never be, and it was the sense of family, the sense of belonging that I truly missed.
'Mirkwood was not always called such! Once it was Greenwood the Great, and the Woodmen thrived beneath its canopy. The recipes I wrote for my people made exclusive use of the herbs and creatures that dwelled within, but so many of them will never return, and those meals will never be made again. Such is the nature of my curse: all else will change, but I will not.
'Watching the two of you has been bittersweet, but it dispelled my loneliness for a time, no matter how briefly. I thank you for that kindness.'
'Oh my! Do you see that?'

'This experience has sent shivers down my spine, ${PLAYER}! I am astounded to learn that Adolinda labours beneath a curse, and has done so for who knows how many years? I mean, this place is called the Haunted Inn, but I did not really think...'
Bingo sputters into silence.
'To be fair, the lighting in here is very dim. I think my mistake is quite understandable, and Adolinda did not go out of her way to correct me, did she? I thought her name was Aduiallin, which seems to me more likely a Ranger's name than Adolinda! I must confess that I am pleased I need not try spider-meat now. But I am still hungry... I will need something! My rumbling belly could wake the dead! Oh. That may have been in poor taste. I am terribly sorry! But it does not change the fact that I have missed a breakfast and cannot continue my adventure until I have something!'
<rgb=#FF0000>Next week: 'Second Breakfast' (Recommended Level: 68)</rgb>

'This recipe does seem to be rather exotic, but I think that will be just perfect for our stay within Mirkwood. It calls for marshy taters, a little sage, some mint for seasoning, the meat of several crows, and... choice cuts of spider? Oh my. I do not know about that, ${PLAYER}! Perhaps if the meat is prepared just right it will not be unsuitable? I am dubious, but let us see how it goes. I will try to keep an open mind. After all, if I did not wish to have new experiences, I could have stayed back in the Shire!
'The author of this book must not have liked the name Mirkwood, for the descriptions always refer to 'Greenwood the Great!' That is very quaint. It seems as if some ingredients can be found in the southern swamps, throughout the Scuttledells, by the town south of Ost Galadh, and the tower to the east of it. It is difficult to tell, because the author refers to these places with different names than those we know!'

'I do not know what to tell you, friend. There is no Ranger by that name here, nor anywhere, unless our ranks are much larger than I realized or my memory is much worse than I believed. Perhaps both are true, but I do not think so.'
'Perhaps one day the curse will be lifted, but for now each day is the same as every other.'

'While you were gone, I went to look for Aduiallin to consult with her about how best to prepare this spider-meat so it will not taste vile or make us sick, but I could not find her. Could you ask one of the Rangers where I might find her? Prestadír seems to be in charge. He might know where she has gone.'

'I have been leafing through the recipe book that was given to me by Aduiallin, trying to decide upon what meal to prepare, and I think I have finally settled upon one. A tasty breakfast would be just the thing! I have been quite hungry ever since we came into this wood!

'I told Willem about this problem of ours, and he ran off. Can you ask around the Inn and see if anyone knows what has become of him? I expect he has gone in search of a second breakfast, and I would greatly appreciate your hastening him back here with it!'
Willem Whisker beams proudly at you. Perhaps the satchel contains something of use for Bingo after all?

'We are back in more pleasant lands. It is something of a relief to leave Mirkwood behind us, but... well, I have been worrying about something.'
Bingo's cheerful expression is gone. He seems quite upset.
'It is this appetite of mine! We Boffins like to have as many meals as anyone, and I am no stranger to nipping off to the larder for a snack or two between meals. But this hunger is sharper, in a way, than any hunger I can remember! I got to thinking about what has gotten me this hungry, and I realized that it began around the time we crossed the river into Mirkwood.
'There is something unnatural about this! Is this a curse? You need to have done something bad to be cursed. Didn't Adolinda say something about a great evil in her past? Well, I was thinking about it, and while I wouldn't say I have done anything especially evil, I wasn't honest with Calengoth, was I? We used deception to get him to allow us across the river! Is my increasing hunger a curse for my poor behaviour?
'You have to go to Calengoth at the docks and apologize for my lies, ${PLAYER}! I fear I will waste away from this curse if you do not!'

'You have come back, I see. What did your friend think of the Golden Host's adventures in Mirkwood?'
You explain Bingo's deception, and give Calengoth the hobbit's sincere apologies. The Elf nods solemnly, but there is a smile on his lips.
'Bingo must have a low opinion of the intelligence of Elves if he believed I was truly fooled by his deception. I was not. But it takes a large heart to admit such a thing, and my refusal to bear him across the river was borne not of malice but of concern for his safety. I accept his apology.
'I may also have the solution for his hunger. Give him this small packet of lembas, along with my well-wishes. I think the one will cure his hunger and the other may assuage his guilt, for I imagine the latter is the truest source of his curse, and once forgiven I expect he will be fine. That is my guess!'

'Calengoth accepted my apology? Lovely, lovely! I am glad to hear it! And what is this? Lembas? How interesting. It looks to be a type of cake, if a little plain-looking. It is a gift from Calengoth?'
Bingo takes a small bite and nibbles at it for a moment.
'Ah! I did not expect it to be so delicious! And how filling! My, this lembas has quite cured my curse, if such it was! It is good to have a full belly, for now I am ready to travel down the Great River in search of further adventures!'
<rgb=#FF0000>Next week: 'The Banks of the Great River' (Recommended Level: 70)</rgb>

'I have seen this lynx you seek! He ran right past the three of us, heading east! He disturbed the papers on this table! I think he was looking for food of some sort, but nothing here satisfied him, and he ran through Ost Galadh after a brief search.'

'Yes, I saw your lynx! He ran right past us, but not before jumping onto this table and scattering papers everywhere!
'He did not stay. He ran east out of Ost Galadh.'
'Oh, I have seen your lynx. He ran through here, disturbed the papers on this table, and continued on his way to the east. He is no longer in Ost Galadh.'

'I think I did see your lynx, from a distance. I saw him a good distance to the east, heading in the direction of Dol Guldur. He was making straight for the gate of Fennas Guldur, but I was beset by Orcs and did not see if he reached it.'

'I saw the lynx you seek. He was running at great speed to the south-east, in the direction of Fennas Guldur. Whether he passed through that gate and is now on the other side of the wall, I do not know.'

'Willem Whisker? What sort of a name is that?
'Rodelleth told me she saw a lynx running to the south-east, toward Fennas Guldur, but I did not see him myself.'

'I have just returned from Dol Guldur, ${PLAYER}, and I saw something most peculiar. There was a lynx fighting Orcs just within the gate of Fennas Guldur, to the east. As I crept away, I saw the lynx making his way north up a slope just behind the wall.
'If you are looking for this curious creature, you should go east to Fennas Guldur, and then climb the slope to the north once you are through the gate. If he is an enemy of the Orcs, he must be a friend to the Golden Host!'
'I do not think your lynx-friend is still within Audaghaim. He has gone elsewhere in the Greenwood.'

'I have just returned from Dol Guldur, ${PLAYER}, and I saw something most peculiar. There was a lynx fighting Orcs just within the gate of Fennas Guldur, to the south-east. As I crept away, I saw the lynx making his way north up a slope just behind the wall.
'If you are looking for this curious creature, you should go south-east to Fennas Guldur, and then climb the slope to the north once you are through the gate. If he is an enemy of the Orcs, he must be a friend to the Golden Host!'

'Do you know something, ${PLAYER}? I think I am ready to meet you back in Lothlórien! I will meet you out in front of Caras Galadhon, and perhaps we can find some real food, for now my belly is quite complaining!'
'You have to go to Calengoth at the docks and apologize for my lies, ${PLAYER}! I fear I will waste away from this curse if you do not!'

'Bingo must have a low opinion of the intelligence of Elves if he believed I was truly fooled by his deception. I was not. But it takes a large heart to admit such a thing, and my refusal to bear him across the river was borne not of malice but of concern for his safety. I accept his apology.

I think the one will cure his hunger and the other may assuage his guilt, for I imagine the latter is the truest source of his curse, and once forgiven I expect he will be fine. That is my guess!'
'The lynx that follows your friend Bingo around did not stay in the Inn. I think he was searching for food, and went somewhere to the east.'
'I saw that lynx run to the east. He was moving with a great deal of haste.'
'I have not seen any lynxes that match your description anywhere in the Drownholt. Perhaps you should travel to the north-east and ask if anyone at Ost Galadh has seen anything.'
You see a familiar figure ahead of you: Willem Whisker!

'This empty belly of mine has made it quite impossible for me to concentrate on further documenting our stay in Mirkwood, ${PLAYER}! I am glad that we were able to give Adolinda a momentary distraction from her curse, but the fact remains that her recipe for breakfast involved spider-legs, and while I am powerless to do anything about the curse, it is within my power to refuse a breakfast of hairy spider-legs! No spider-legs for me, thank you! Yuck!
'I told Willem about my dissatisfaction and my hunger, and he ran off. Can you ask around the Inn and see if anyone knows what has become of him? I expect he has gone in search of a second breakfast, and I would greatly appreciate your hastening him back here with it!'

Willem Whisker stands by a dirty satchel that appears to have once been the property of an Orc. The lynx beams at you proudly, and you pick up the satchel.
You take a quick peek inside, and the contents make you laugh in spite of yourself. You resolve to bring it back to Bingo in the Haunted Inn.
'You found Willem? Did you tell him to follow you back here?'

Bingo gingerly takes the Orc-satchel.
'What's that? W.W. found this satchel for me? How thoughtful! Does it contain food, do you think? The bag does seem to be rather worse for wear, but let's see... small trinkets... bent bits of metal... this is rather fuzzy...'
Bingo suddenly jumps backwards and drops the satchel onto the table. After a moment he begins to laugh.
'There are spider-legs in here! Willem, did you think I was unhappy about how FEW spider-legs ${PLAYER} brought back? That was not it at all! Why does everyone want me to try these unpleasant things? Do you know something, ${PLAYER}? I think I am ready to return to Lothlórien! I will meet you out in front of Caras Galadhon, and perhaps we can find some real food, for now my belly is quite complaining!'

'This is terrible, ${PLAYER}! He doesn't believe us! Beornings and Eagles give the warning, and Rohirrim ignore it!
'The enemies are massing on their doorstep, ${PLAYER}. We will have to do something about this... ourselves!'
<rgb=#FF0000>Next week: 'Enter the Easterlings' (Recommended Level: 75)</rgb>
'The men of Stangard do not fear anything or anyone.'
'We should help her with her task, ${PLAYER}! I have heard some frightening things about the Beornings, but she seems to have the right idea as far as the Orcs are concerned!'

'I have seen more than my share of Orcs by now, ${PLAYER}, but we are truly making these lands more safe with each meeting, aren't we? It is good we encountered Langhár here, instead of continuing elsewhere.
'She is the first Beorning I have ever met, and she is not what I expected. There have been stories about her people even in the Shire, and many of them portray the line of Beorn as being bloodthirsty and angry, more beast than man. It is true that Langhár has no mercy for her enemies, and does not speak well of the men of Stangard, but I am moved by the realization that she carries out her duty despite the outright rejection of those it serves.
'She helps those who refuse her help. I wonder how many of us would do the same?'
'Let the Orcs tremble in their caves! Perhaps now they will remain within, and trouble these lands no more. If the Rohirrim will not drive them out, it is up to us to take care of this blight.'

'Very good, my new friends. You have done well to fight the Orcs, and certainly better than the cowardly men of Stangard could have done!
'I too fought the Orcs among the Wailing Hills, and as I searched for foes to defeat I saw an Eagle in the skies to the north and watched it descend into a stand of trees. The Eagles have been on good terms with my people for many years.
'We should go to him and learn what he has seen from the heights. Such knowledge might be of use to me as I seek to accomplish my task.'
'Beornings are an interesting people, are they not?'

'Well! That was quite a rude greeting! Perhaps the animosity between the Elves and the Rohirrim is not the result of a borrowed item unreturned after all.
'If this fellow does not want me to come inside, I will respect his wishes. Perhaps we should find this woman of whom he spoke, and see if she needs our help? Sabert may not care if she runs afoul of some beast, but he should feel some responsibility if it were to happen!
'He said she went to the north-west?'
'I wish you luck, for so long as your feet take you away from Stangard.'

'I bid you welcome, travellers, and would advise you to avoid Stangard, if you have not come from there already. The men of that place do not recognize their own friends or allies, even as they have need of them.
'I am Langhár, of the line of Beorn, and I have set forth from the Vales of Anduin at the command of Grimbeorn. Orcs threaten the shores of the Great River, and someone must beat them back. The men of Rohan cower behind their walls, and they refused my offer of help. They are fools.
'If I returned to Grimbeorn with this tale, I am certain he would send me elsewhere, and leave the Rohirrim to fend for themselves. But the Vales of Anduin are not far from here, and any victory by the Orcs here might endanger my own home, so I will help the fools of Stangard, whether they accept it or not. If you would help me in this, defeat Orcs throughout the Wailing Hills! I am a skin-changer, and more than capable of felling these foes, but it seems the supply of them is never-ending.'
'Is she... of Beorn's line? I have heard tales of the Beornings! She looks very strong, and a little frightening! Why would the Rohirrim turn her away?'
'That was good work against the spiders, ${PLAYER}. Do you think Bingo is done speaking with Landroval yet?'

'You again? Was I not clear enough the first time?'
Sabert listens impatiently as you tell him what Landroval saw from high above: an army of foes gathering in the Brown Lands.
'Eagles? Skin-changing bear-folk? Nosey halflings, far from home? You keep odd company, ${PLAYER}, and there is no need for you to bring them here. The men of Stangard will face whatever foe tomorrow brings. Good day to you, and may it bring you and your peculiar friends elsewhere!'
'A great army is encamped in the Brown Lands!'

'Greetings, little ${RACE}. You would be wise to use caution in these lands, for you are bound to the earth and many dangerous beings crawl there, eager to do you harm. Indeed, some of these foes aim their weapons skyward, intending to do harm to my kind as well.'

'As I searched for foes to defeat I saw an Eagle in the skies to the north and watched it descend into a stand of trees. The Eagles have been on good terms with my people for many years.
'We should go to him and learn what he has seen from the heights. Such knowledge might be of use to me as I seek to accomplish my task.'
'Langhár saw an Eagle somewhere to the north? We should go find it!'

'Will you look at that, ${PLAYER}? I have never seen one of the Great Eagles before, and I never expected to do so. What an honour! Have you ever seen such majesty before? And he can speak!'
Bingo stammers with excitement.
'Do... do you think he will give me an interview for my book? I would not even know what to ask him, but I have to think of something. Oh, I am so nervous... I hope I do not embarrass myself. He seems so wise and well-spoken, and I am just a small hobbit from the Shire, and feeling smaller than usual!'

'This halfling may have come to Stangard with a desire to see our lands, but this is not a holiday retreat. There is nothing here for your diminutive friend. He is not the first peculiar visitor I have turned away from this outpost. With my ill fortune, he will not be the last.
'What is it that draws such unwelcome guests hither? Tell your friend to find the woman I turned away to the north-west, and perhaps the three of you can journey with haste away from Rohan. When last I saw her, she was headed in the direction of Frithstan's Camp. May the three of you find your way to some other land.'

'We should give Bingo some time to speak with the Eagles. After all, if we were to take him away now he would be able to think of nothing else!
'Let us defeat some of the venomous spiders that stalk among the Wailing Hills, and collect their venom-sacs. That way we will be giving Bingo time to speak with the Eagles and we will be combating a threat at the same time.'

'${PLAYER}! I have had a lovely conversation with Landroval and Meneldor, but I have learned something most troubling, and it has brought our chat to an end!

'This must be the woman. She looks very fierce!'
'That was good work against the spiders, ${PLAYER}. Do you think Bingo is done speaking with the Eagles yet?'

'Hail, travellers!'

'If this fellow does not want me to come inside, I will respect his wishes. Perhaps we should find this woman of whom he spoke, and see if she needs our help? Sabert may not care if she runs afoul of some beast, but he should feel some responsibility if it were to happen!

'The outpost of Stangard is a short distance to the south, but none of the Elves here will speak of it to me. That is not very neighbourly! 'If you grind up a certain type of dark mud with special river-side reeds, you can obtain a thick pigment. Adding water to this pigment will produce a high-quality ink that should serve your friend well. If you do as I instruct, he will be writing again with little delay.'

'Of course I think we should help the men of Stangard defend their outpost! We will help them survive this surprise attack, and you can count on me to document the excitement for my account!'
