'I bid you heed Oryat's words. If this boy or any other children venture into the Second Circle, he will do them harm.'
'That man would not truly do harm to me, would he?'
'Second Circle between the tavern and the Feasting Hall, O Champion of Brats. We can settle this there.'

'What fun we've had, strolling about, ${PLAYER}! I will not let that last grim turn spoil my enjoyment of the day, and I hope you won't either.
'Still, it will be hard not going to any Upper Circles. I owe it to the others to find some way out of this - or around it - if I can.'

'Got a spine then after all, have we? I reckoned there was a chance you might - so I made sure I had some friends at hand.
'Ha ha! Why should I chance a wound for the sorry likes of you!'

'You showed bravery just now, both of you. Sometimes we rush into a fight that might be averted. Other times we do what must be done, even though the consequences of our acts bring us no good fortune. You must ask yourself which you have chosen. But regardless of what lesson you draw, you will live with the result.
'You have won yourself freedom in the First Circle, but neither you nor any of the other children should venture up here anymore. Oryat will surely do you harm. I read that plainly in his eyes.'

'Not venture into the Second Circle? I suppose we dare not, lest Oryat find us. Oh, ${PLAYER}! What have we done? Somehow I felt for sure that if only you bested Oryat, he would never trouble us anymore.
'We had better not stay. I shall go back to the Old Guest-house now. I must think and talk with the other children.
'Will you meet me there?'
'A cautious step and keen judgement. Remember that!'
'They brought out new apple crates just this morning. Let us feed the horses!'
'Isn't it funny how their lips brush against your hand?'

'No doubt you saw, when we met, that I am not the only youth in Minas Tirith. Mind you, most left with the wains some days past. But a dozen of us remained for this reason and that.
'It is for them, as well as I myself, I wish to ask Himnir for some treats.'
'The Wrights' Market! I wouldn't mind poking my nose in there, anyway. This Amonel, she must be awfully clever with her hands. Tinkers are, you know!'
'Bring that broken whisk to Amonel, around or about the Wrights' Market, and I'll send treats for all your friends.'
'Run along. This will take a moment... or two. I haven't decided yet how the whisk could be fixed.'
'A tour of the city walls is just the thing. I wish to see everything I can up there!'
'Come! Come! You must see the ranks of soldiers. They are a sight to see!'

'She speaks nearly as well as the swan-knight, ${PLAYER}. Some things must be faced bravely...
'Do you know what I think? I think that you must face that swaggering soldier, Oryat! Surely you are a match for him. Surely you can cow him and make him relent.
'Please, ${PLAYER}. He will not leave us children alone until someone stops him. Oh, and how I would love to see you stand him on his head!'
'There are others over there!'
'Those soldiers, there. Let us get closer to them.'
'Run along. This will take a moment... or two. I haven't decided yet how the whisk could be fixed.'
'You - you talk to him, ${PLAYER}.'
'Second Circle between the tavern and the Feasting Hall, O Champion of Brats. We can settle this there.'
'Yes, let us go. Amonel will have mended the whisk, and Himnir will give all the children treats!'
'Run along, you two. I will go see Himnir myself, shortly, and tell him the ill news of his broken whisk.'
'Please, ${PLAYER}. Oryat will never leave us children be, if you do not face him. And how I long to see that sneer wiped from his face!'
'By the kings of old! You showed Oryat a thing or two!'
'I bid you heed Oryat's words. If this boy or any other children venture into the Second Circle, he will do them harm.'

'It's not only horses who enjoy a treat now and then. With you along, I might be allowed in the Foodmongers' Market. There is a 'monger there, Himnir he is called, who likes me well enough and might give me something to eat.'
Bergil's face grows serious and seems to think a moment.
'What that knight said about kindness was also very fine. Perhaps if I ask the right way, Himnir will send food to all the children.
'Yes, let us go find him!'

A thought seems to suddenly strike Bergil.
'Say, when did you get here, ${PLAYER}? Were you upon the Pelennor when Lord Faramir came back to us? How I should like to have seen that! I went to the gates with Pippin - that's the prince of the halflings I spoke of - when all the men arrived from Belfalas and Lossarnach and elsewhere. That was a sight to see. But they only rode in on their horses. That is fine, but it is nothing to a fight!
'How would you like to go up upon the walls and see what we can? I hear the Enemy is within the Rammas Echor now and would like dreadfully to see how that is. I can hardly imagine it!'

Himnir smiles indulgently at Bergil.
'Sweets not just for you, but also for the other children? Well, that is a bold thing to ask! Others would pay good coin for such a parcel of my goods. Ah, but who am I fooling? Like as not, I would have given it to you freely.
'Today, however, I have an errand you may run to earn your treat. This whisk I use to whip up cream for my pastries has come apart, and it is my favourite whisk!
'I ask you to bring it to Amonel, a tinker in the Wrights' Market, and beg her to set it right. In return, I'll have a bounty of sweets sent over for the whole lot of you.'

'Well, this is an odd pairing!'
The tinker eyes you and Bergil.
'So, old Himnir's favourite whisk finally failed him. Go lightly with it, I told him! Ah, well. Let me have a look and see what I can do.
'You come back in a while and with any luck, I'll have it fixed.'
'Let us go, ${PLAYER}. Perhaps Amonel has finished mending that whisk.'

Amonel greets you and Bergil with a low sigh.
'The whisk is not mended. Nor shall it be, for it is beyond repair. Himnir should not go so hard on so delicate a tool and I have told him so...
'Nor will I send you to bear this ill tiding for me. Some things must be faced bravely. A knight cannot send someone in his stead to face the foe, nor can he shirk his duty and let innocents come to harm.
'Go now. Somehow I think Himnir will send some sweets to your friends all the same.'

'And just what are you then, the champion of orphans and wretches? What gives you the right to stand between me, a soldier of Gondor, and that impudent, sniveling, little...'
He makes as if to go past you, then sees the dangerous look in your eye.
'Oho, is that how it is? You'd strike at me, would you, just to spare this urchin a bit of a thrashing? Just you try it. I'm a soldier trained and hardened, and I'll strike back. I'll strike whatever cheeky boy or foreigner I choose, to let them know their place.
'Now skulk away - or if you've any spine, meet me up in the Second Circle later, between the Feasting Hall and the tavern, and we'll see who strikes who, when it comes to it.'

Go to see the ranks of soldiers before the City Gates.

'Greetings! I am friend to the prince of the halflings. Have you ever seen a halfling? I'll wager you haven't.'
When you tell him that you in fact have, he seems crestfallen. A moment later, his face lights up again.
'All the same, you are a stranger in the city. Will you walk with me? I'll show you things to see. And we can go places I would be shooed away from, were I alone!
'Here, take this whistle. If we somehow get separated, you sound it and I'll come running.'

'Tanglemane is an incredibly picky eater. He will turn up his nose at almost anything! If you can find some food around Harwick that he will eat, I will let you have him for free. Otherwise, I will have to refuse. You understand, I'm sure. Find some food around Harwick that he will eat, and he will be all yours!'
'Well, what do you think?'
'Look at him, ${PLAYER}! He is not scary at all. In fact, he's quite little!'

'This pony is not scary at all! He seems very well-tempered, and I daresay I could walk up to him without fearing that he might bite me. He is rather hobbit-sized, if you ask me, and I think that is just the right size!
'His name is Tanglemane? It suits him well! I wonder how many coins Cuthbald will ask in order to part with him?'
'I think he likes you, Bingo!'

'I am glad that Bingo likes him! To be honest, I have not had much success finding an owner for Tanglemane, so I will be pleased to let Bingo have him for free. I have one condition, however.
'Tanglemane is an incredibly picky eater. He will turn up his nose at almost anything! If you can find some food around Harwick that he will eat, I will let you have him for free. Otherwise, I will have to refuse. You understand, I'm sure. Find some food around Harwick that he will eat, and he will be all yours!'
'I love him already! What a great pony he is!'

'I can't do it, ${PLAYER}, I'm sorry! These great beasts are simply too scary for me to even think of riding. And if I did, how long before I fell from the saddle? What a distance that would be! Too far for this hobbit, I tell you truly!
'I will not ride any of these horses! Tell Cuthbald good day, and give him my apologies, but there will simply be no sale today, or indeed any day! Not to this hobbit, at least!'
'Well? What do you think of these fine steeds? Noble creatures, are they not?'

'Well, that will not do. If this fellow expects to travel throughout the kingdom, he will need a horse. I cannot allow the two of you to leave Harwick without a sufficient steed for Bingo! If I let you go unprepared, It would do such damage to my reputation as the finest horse trader in this part of the Wold, meaning this area near Harwick, but not as far north as Langhold or south to Eorl's Hallow. Within those bounds I am the very best, and will remain so!
'Do you know something? I believe I may have one last chance to provide what your friend needs. Meet me on the west side of Harwick, near the Crafting Hall, and I will see what I can do.'
'I will not ride any of these beasts. I am sorry, but I simply will not!'

'I don't usually keep ponies, but this fellow came into my possession after a raid by the Orcs, and I have yet to find an owner for him.
'What do you think of him? His name is Tanglemane, but you could call him anything. I wasn't sure what I was going to do with him.'
'Will you look at this fellow! He is not scary at all!'
'I wonder what food Tanglemane will eat? We have to find something!'

'I've never seen this pony devour anything as quickly as he ate that apple, friend! Looks like you've found his favourite food, and it also looks as if Bingo has found himself a noble steed to carry him through Rohan!
'It has been a pleasure doing business with you two, and if you happen to put in a good word for me with anyone looking for horses, I'd appreciate it!'

'I am delighted to have met Tanglemane! He must truly be the Bingo Boffin of the pony persuasion, ${PLAYER}: small, friendly, and a picky eater!
'He likes apples, which is perfect, because I can't stand the things, as I believe I have told you before. He can have every apple in Middle-earth as far as I am concerned! We will make a great team, I can already tell. We won't covet each other's dinners!'

'Always a pleasure to make a sale, even when no coins exchange hands. Tanglemane was a bit of a nuisance to feed, so you're doing me a favour. And of course your friend needed a steed, as well. Everyone wins, ${PLAYER}.'

'Watch your hands around them! They might take a nip at you if you are not careful. They are princes all, not of the Mearas, of course, but surely very near to that finest of breeds.
'Feel free to examine these noble steeds and let me know which of them suits your fancy.'

I will hold you personally responsible if they do, ${PLAYER}!
'Folk say there is a horse trader named Cuthbald on the eastern side of Harwick. We can go see him, if we must.'

'Oh my. I hope these creatures do not come any closer! They look quite ferocious, and could take a bite out of this poor hobbit without even a second thought! I would be little more than a morsel to them, but this morsel would just as soon not be lunch, if you please!
'Are you quite certain I need to have a horse for this adventure?'

'Ah, you are here to purchase a fine horse for this fellow? I have several that might serve your needs; each one is fiery of temper, and will gladly gallop about the fields with speed you have never seen.
'Watch your hands around them! They might take a nip at you if you are not careful. They are princes all, not of the Mearas, of course, but surely very near to that finest of breeds.

'Oh, I do not know about this. I do not know about this at all!'
'Oh, I do not know about this.'

'What is wrong with Willem? He does not seem to be his usual self. Is everything all right, W.W.?'
Willem is jealous of all the attention Bingo is giving to Tanglemane. Anyone could see that.

'I think I saw something suspicious on the south-eastern side of the Mead Hall, behind some of the tents. Something red and bright caught the light and flashed in my eyes. I wonder what it was? I do not see it now, but perhaps if the light returned the red glinting object would reveal itself?'
'I did not expect to see Egwylf again so soon! Her errand must have brought her back to Rohan with haste!'

'The Blood Eye? It sounds dangerous!'
Bingo shivers, and then clenches his fists together.
'I am not afraid, ${PLAYER}! If we can help Egwylf apprehend these villains, we should do what we can! I will keep an eye out for them here in Cliving, and you should do the same!'

'A cult calling itself the Blood Eye has allied itself with Orcs of the Black Land. I believe there are three agents of the Blood Eye active in Rohan; I have tracked two of them here to Cliving.
'Will you help me find them? You will know them by the brooches or necklaces they wear: each one bears a red gem, prominently displayed. They are certain to be hidden in out-of-the-way corners of the city, away from prying eyes. If this is too dangerous for your friend Bingo, I will understand. But I would welcome your aid.'
'The two men I tracked to Cliving will look for hidden, out-of-the-way places somewhere in the city. Look for some sign of their presence!'
'We should search the city for some sign of these men! It sounds to me as if these agents of the Blood Eye intend no good for Rohan!'
'Did you find something?'
'Any luck yet? I have found nothing of interest, but it will not stop me from looking!'

'Jealous? Willem, there is no reason for that! I have never had such a wonderful lynx-friend before, and ever since you joined our little band of companions I have never forgotten how lucky I am to have you by my side on this adventure!'
Bingo grimaces.
'Well, I might have forgotten it once, but in my defence I forgot a lot of things when I fell into the caverns beneath the Misty Mountains. But it won't happen again, Willem! Tanglemane is a new friend, it's true, but you're the only W.W. in this group! I think you two should get along, or it will just break my heart in two. Say something, ${PLAYER}!
'Well, for now we should go up to the Mead Hall in Cliving and see what there is to learn about this town. But I want you two to get along! This adventure will not be as fun if everyone has hurt feelings!'
'Hello again, adventurers.'
'Look who it is, ${PLAYER}!'

'I did not expect to see the two of you again so soon, but the trail I followed has returned to Cliving. My errand in Stangard was brief; the men there will remain alert for my prey, but there are so few good men in Stangard I do not know if I should trust any net they might weave.
'There are forces at work in Rohan that seek to bring the kingdom low. It is with greatest shame that I tell you that not all of these evils come from without the borders. Some of the greatest evil is worked by men and women of Rohan! A cult calling itself the Blood Eye has allied itself with Orcs of the Black Land. I believe there are three agents of the Blood Eye active in Rohan; I have tracked two of them here to Cliving.
'Will you help me find them? You will know them by the brooches or necklaces they wear: each one bears a red gem, prominently displayed. They are certain to be hidden in out-of-the-way corners of the city, away from prying eyes. If this is too dangerous for your friend Bingo, I will understand. But I would welcome your aid.'
'I think our next destination should be the town of Cliving, in the Norcrofts to the south-west. I will meet you outside the entrance, if Tanglemane is amenable to the journey!'
You do not speak the language of lynxes, but even without that skill it is easy to understand what is wrong with Willem Whisker: he is jealous of Bingo's new friend, Tanglemane!

'Did you and Bingo find any sign of the agents of the Blood Eye, ${PLAYER}?'
You hand Egwylf the brooch you discovered and tell her that it reminds you of the Rothstone, a similar piece of jewellery you encountered in your travels. She nods.
'I do not know where the Cult of the Blood Eye finds these treasures, but they prize red gems above all others and look for them exclusively. Still, I have found that the men who bear these brooches are not unwilling to leave them behind when they near capture. Without these identifiers, they become nearly invisible to my pursuit, but it is not a complete loss, friend. They use these gems as proof of their allegiance, and without such proof as this, what Orc will be willing to trust they are who they claim to be?
'So one of the men I followed has been effectively declawed. As for the other, his trail has gone cold. I would ask for your help and for Bingo's, if you continue to offer it!'
'Oh, you should give that to Egwylf! I do not want it! I don't like the look of it one bit, not one little bit!'

'I do not like the sound of this Blood Eye group, especially if its members are in league with Orcs! Who would wish to ally themselves with such terrible creatures? I know that I would not, not for anything!
'I do not know if I can be much help to Egwylf in this. After all, she is a skilled tracker and has followed these agents of the Blood Eye for what sounds like a long time. But we are adventurers, and if we can help her with her task, we definitely should do so! It is a pity that the trail has gone cold. Do you think she will be able to pick it up again? If so, it may make for an exciting chapter in my account of our journey!'

Let us defeat enemies in the Wold and in the Norcrofts as we journey, and in that way our presence will be a boon for the good folk of Rohan!'

Talk to Egwylf outside the Mead Hall of Cliving
Search Wildermore for the missing agent of the Blood Eye
Examine the corpse of the desperate man, near the Lonely Height

'I think the missing cultist came this way, ${PLAYER}! I heard some of those Orcs talking, and they were talking about a man with a red gem. They said they let him climb the road up into Wildermore.
'They did not sound that happy about it, and one of the Orcs said that they should have taken him prisoner instead and made a meal out of him! What a terrible thought! I suppose they must be allies, if they let him pass, but I do not think I would work with anyone I needed to worry about around dinner-time!'

'You are looking for a man with a red brooch? I saw him, indeed I did! He jumped out from behind this rock and knocked me down! Before I knew what was happening, he stole my axe and ran off to the north-east!
'I will be fine in a moment. I twisted my ankle when I fell; otherwise I would never have let him steal my weapon from me! Go catch him, and quickly!'

'You are lucky you see me in this state, ${RACE}! If I wasn't already breathing my last dozen breaths, I'd make sure to take you with me into the darkness at the end!
'This cursed man attacked me with an axe. He was one of ours, he was! What a laugh that is! He had a strange look in his eye. Desperation, I think it was. He stole my plunder, all I had: a bag of dirty coins. He will find no joy of them, if he wants to spend them. No one in this thrice-cursed land will take them from him.
'He'll be dead before the sun comes up again. I will take that knowledge with me into the blackness, and it will send me off with a smile! Now leave me to it, ${RACE}, and be glad you did not see me in my prime!'

'I have been speaking with the people of Forlaw, as a true solver of mysteries would do, and it seems that some people saw a man with a red gem visit the barber in town. Did he try to change his appearance? We have to know for sure!'

'I have been speaking to some of the townspeople, and it turns out that someone may have seen the man with the red gem arguing with a group of Orcs at the camp called Kadar-golnauk to the north-west.
'Shouldn't Orcs be his allies? I wonder what the subject of their argument might have been?'

'The snow here is disturbed, and it looks as if he dropped this bag of coins in anger. I cannot say for certain, ${PLAYER}, but I think the man we are tracking is becoming increasingly desperate! Did he try to go to the city over yonder, to the west?'
Bingo looks toward the hilltop city of Byre Tor, and shrugs.

'These tracks are clear, and they do not go into Byre Tor. No, I believe the man we are tracking through Wildermore would give that city a wide berth. For whatever reason, he is not eager to cross paths with Orcs or Uruks, if he can avoid it.
'The tracks continue to the west, and do not go into the city.'
'I see no sign of him here. I do not think he came to this place.'
'The Blood Eye cultist will not be able to evade us for long! Let us hurry to Wildermore, and put an end to his villainy!'

'Did you find him? Your expression seems both satisfied and a little unhappy, and I cannot puzzle out its meaning.'
You recount what you were able to discern concerning the cultist's final moments, and hand Egwylf the Blood Eye brooch. She nods grimly.
'You and Bingo did very well to track this man, ${PLAYER}. He came to a sad end: seemingly disavowed by his allies, his supplies gone, alone in the snow, there to die, but there is no sympathy in my heart for him. He chose his path, as must we all; his was with Mordor, and he was paid in full for that choice.
'I believe this brings the count of Blood Eye agents at work in Rohan to two, and I ask you and Bingo to keep your eyes open for them. One of them is without his brooch, so keep your wits about you! Farewell for now! If I see you again, may it be in time of peace for Rohan!'
'You found him! Splendid work, ${PLAYER}!'

Bingo wears a philosophic expression.
'That Blood Eye cultist should not have gone off by himself. I think if he had friends with him things might not have gone that way for him. The Orcs were never his friends. They might be working for the same dark purpose, but they were not friends. It wasn't the cold of Wildermore that got to him. It was the cold in his heart!'
Bingo is silent for a moment, and then shakes his head.
'Or maybe it was just the cold after all. It is so cold here, and I am exhausted! He took us on quite a journey through Wildermore, and my feet hurt. I am glad we solved the mystery, but I will be gladder still when our adventure takes us back to warmer climes!'
<rgb=#00FF00>After you complete this quest, Bert Bartleby will arrive near the stable-master at Forlaw, in Wildermore.</rgb>
<rgb=#FF0000>Next week: 'Bert Has a Word' (Recommended Level: 88)</rgb>

This member of the Cult of the Blood Eye saw his fortunes turn sour in the snowy heights of Wildermore, and the cruel sorceries at play in that region proved his undoing. This man will work no more evils, but the Blood Eye has others to work its will.
Even in death, the cultist reaches for the brooch of the Blood Eye lying next to him in the snow. You wonder if the man believed his actions had been worthwhile, in the end, but the only certainty is that he will not be able to tell you the answer.

'This brings the count of Blood Eye agents at work in Rohan to two, and I ask you and Bingo to keep your eyes open for them. One of them is without his brooch, so keep your wits about you! Farewell for now! If I see you again, may it be in time of peace for Rohan!'

Willem Whisker stands by a number of abandoned sacks, but after a cursory sniff, he points his nose to the west. That must be where the cultist of the Blood Eye went after exhausting the contents of these empty bags.

'Yes, I saw this man you seek. He was just here, and very ill of temper! I did not like the look of him, and I liked his coins even less; they seemed to me to be of a sort used by Orcs and evil men, and I wanted nothing to do with them.
'I thought he would strike me when I refused to modify his appearance, but instead he snarled curses at me and stormed out. I would not repeat these foul words, but one sounded more like a place than an insult: \qKadar-golnauk\q he said. Take this name with you if you find it useful, and beware of this man you seek! I feel certain he could be very dangerous if pressed into a corner.'

'You are a fool if you come here to speak with words and not weapons, ${RACE}!'
The Uruk is taken aback when you ask about a man wearing a brooch with a red gem in it, but he quickly recovers.
'I know the vermin, all right. He went to the north-east when we would not help him, but you won't be following his trail... not in this life!'

'You are a brazen ${RACE}, aren't you? Not many of your worthless breed would ask such questions!
'I saw this rat you seek, and he was more cowardly than you, for he turned away from Fushaum-dorám even as he approached. He must thought better of meeting my boys and me, because he turned and fled to the west at the first sight of us.
'You should have done the same!'

'I saw this man. He tried to buy the loyalty of my boys with a sack of dirty coins, but we refused. We might both serve the Blood Eye, but I know if our spots were reversed that maggot would not give us a second look. Let him die on his own in the High Knolls! He will have none of our protection.
'It may be that I will find his sack of coins and take it from his corpse, with no effort on my part! That would be a lark!'

'I scouted ahead and found the trail of the Blood Eye cultist heads west. I believe that he is making for the heights of Wildermore. You would do well to begin your search at the sloping path that leads from the Norcrofts into Wildermore.
'One more thing, ${PLAYER}. The air is heavy with some sorcery; I felt the chill in my bones as I approached. There is something unusual afoot in Wildermore.'
The bag is full of the dirty coins sometimes used by Orcs

'I am ready to help Egwylf find the other member of the Cult of the Blood Eye, if you are ready as well! She said the trail has gone cold, but perhaps she has found some clue that will steer us in the right direction!'

'I am pleased the two of you will help me find this missing agent of the Blood Eye. He would sell the kingdom to its enemies, given the chance, and he must pay for his treason!
'I scouted ahead and found his trail leading west. I believe that he is making for the heights of Wildermore. You would do well to begin your search at the sloping path that leads from the Norcrofts into Wildermore.
'One more thing, ${PLAYER}. The air is heavy with some sorcery; I felt the chill in my bones as I approached. There is something unusual afoot in Wildermore.'
'I am ready to search for another of these villains! Does Egwylf know where the other one has gone?'

The Old Guest-house lies in the First Circle, just south of the City Gates.
Meet Bergil and the other children back at the Old Guest-house.

'We have set more than one thing right on this adventure, ${PLAYER}, and I am glad. But most of all, I am glad we can reach the Finding Place once again. We boys and girls have become used to looking in there - and the things we would find! Lost trinkets, sweets, a coin or two.
'I would have felt doubly ashamed, if I had cut all them off from that!
'But look at Landath over there, puzzling over the letter! I do wonder when Himnir's sweet treats will arrive. You must join us when they do.'
'Gelwen is just over there. You really should speak with her before we go.'
'This shall be a grand adventure, ${PLAYER}!'
'Then we shall meet within the hidden entrance to the cisterns? Good.'
'I hope my sister is right about the Secret Walker. But if she is going in there, then I will go, too!'
'What will we find, I wonder? Do you think a passage to the Fourth Circle truly exists?'
'I must confess, it is stranger and more wonderful than I had even imagined.'
'Oh... This is where all the water is!'

'Oh! Now that I am here, my doubts seem larger and my certainty smaller than it did before. But I shall be brave... so long as you lead the way before us. You are the grown adventurer and we are but children, after all, ${PLAYER}!'

'So you are ${PLAYER}. It is a pleasure to meet you. Bergil has told us of your adventure together and his plan.
'The others all think that the Secret Walker lives in the cisterns and are afraid to set foot inside. I think they are wrong, and that the Secret Walker is nothing but a story made to scare little girls and boys.
'In addition, I wish more than anything to see inside the cisterns. I imagine it must be wondrous and beautiful. Therefore, my brother and I wish to go with you. If you agree, then let us meet within the door.'
'If you could find that key to the hidden cisterns' door, then we'd be one step closer to reaching the upper tiers. It must be somewhere near the Wrights' Fellow-hall that it was lost.'
'Well, now my luck's taken a turn for the better!'
'Imagine, the Finding Place so near to the secret passage. We must go over to it at once.'
'The Finding Place! I wonder what we'll find in it this time.'
'What is it? What did you find?'
'Can I see?'
'I plan to go through the secret passage as often as I can. The Fourth Circle! I do hope some of the poets or minstrels or stage players will still play, even though these are times of war.'
'Maybe Gelwen is right and the Secret Walker is just a tale. But how can we be sure?'

'What is this?'
Bergil takes the letter and examines it.
'Oh, by Queen Beruthiel's cats! It's a letter Landath was meant to deliver. He must have lost it. How did it end up here? Well, that's the wonder of the Finding Place.
'Never mind that. Let us go tell the others we have found a way up - and get Landath his letter. Maybe there's even still time for him to deliver it!'

'Now that I think of it, there may be a way around the Second Circle, but... no, we must try, and with your help, ${PLAYER}, maybe, just maybe, it can be done.
'You see, I have heard that within the City Cisterns, you may climb right up to the Fourth Circle - which is just where we wish to go! Only, we'd never be allowed in through the Clean-waters. Not by ourselves. Not whenever we pleased!
'There is a hidden entrance, though, by the Wrights' Fellow-hall, that is seldom used. And as it should happen, one of the keys for it was lost just last week. I know because I heard Master Carethon cursing out the lad who lost it. If it could be found - if you could find it - why then, we'd be one step closer to that secret passage, wouldn't we?'

'Ah, ${PLAYER}, I knew you would find it! While you have been searching, I have spoken with the others, and Gelwen and Glatham have asked if they can come along.
'Would you lead the three of us into the cisterns? Ah, but perhaps you should speak to Gelwen first.'

'See, Glatham? The Secret Walker didn't appear and the passage DID go through, and look! Do you see where we are? The Finding Place is very near. What fortune! We must go over to it at once!
'Come, ${PLAYER}. You will see for yourself!'

Landath was supposed to deliver the letter three days ago. He is so upset he has asked you to examine the letter.

Landath stands in front of the Old Guest-house, in the First Circle, just south of the City Gates.
Tell Landath that the letter isn't in terrible shape.

The Clothiers' Fellow-hall is in the Third Circle, just south of the Pier.
Landath feels the letter can still be delivered if the seal is re-made. This can be done with Master Habdir's seal, found in the Clothiers' Fellow-hall.
'It makes me anxious, watching him work. What if something goes wrong? Let us walk around the forge and see some of the other smithing. It's a marvel to see, is it not?'
'Do you think he's done? Yes, I think maybe he is. Let's go over and see.'

'We haven't found Rhofin, but we have learned a thing or two. Let's see, now. He's gone to work, but he's not taking any commissions nor delivering them. And he's bought a hammer.
'Why that's it! He must be in the Forges of Cirion. Let's go see if I'm right.'
'It is done! Let us get home, to the Old Guest-house. I dare say I'll feel safer then.'
'I have made many a delivery up and down the City, ${PLAYER}, and none has had me quaking in my boots as this one has. You are a good ${RACE}. Thank you for saving my hide.'

'There you are, then. If it is not boasting to say so, I think this will please old Lord Forlong quite well. Now run along and bring that to Master Habdir. He's still got to work that into the strap!'

'What's this? Ah, the buckle. That took Rhofin a rather long time. Well, I imagine quite a few lords are dusting off their arms and armour and finding bits that need to be mended or replaced. Maybe even a few that were smaller round the waist, last time they garbed for war!'
'Just look and tell me if the letter is entirely ruined.'
'You'll need Master Habdir's wax and seal. I'm sure they're in the Clothiers' Fellow-hall... somewhere!'
'It will take forever to search the whole Third Circle for Rhofin. We should find Master Aglarang, and see if he knows where he is.'
'Well, we've got a start, haven't we? Ask about in the Merry Swan, Smiths' Market, and… what was it, Court of Eärnil?'
'Never mind that we seem to have found him. I won't breathe my sigh of relief until this errand's seen to the very end.'
'Look at how their hammers fall!'

'Is it not ruined beyond reading? Let me look.'
Landath apprehensively peers at the letter.
'Oh, by the White Tree, there is hope. But we can't deliver it with a broken seal. Would you - could you?'
Landath hesitates.
'If it is not too much to ask, do you think you might go into the Clothiers' Fellow-hall, find Master Hadbir's things, and reseal the letter with them?'
'Oh yes, Rhofin. He stopped to wish me health, as he often does, and showed the hammer he'd just bought. Broke his old one on the anvil, it seems.'
'I did see Rhofin, though it was earlier. Let me see... I do recall he mentioned he would neither be taking commissions nor selling his goods today.'

'Why - why you've done it! But I'm not out of this scrape quite yet, ${PLAYER}. The letter's still got to be delivered. Will you come with me? I'm feeling, well, faint of heart.
'It's supposed to go to a smith named Rhofin, but I've no notion where to find him. We should probably start by asking old Aglarang, the Master Smith. That's up in the Third Circle of course.'

'A message for Rhofin, you say? I saw him this morning, but that won't do you much good. Given the hour, he might be at the Smiths' Market, or maybe the Merry Swan, or even out upon the Court of Eärnil, despite these darkling skies.
'Ask about those places and you'll find him, like as not.'
'Rhofin? Aye, he was in here. Said he was going to do some work after his meal.'

'What am I to do? I should have delivered that letter three days past! I couldn't say if your finding it was a blessing or a curse! Either way, I fear my goose is cooked.
'Oh, I cannot bear to even look at it. Will you?'
Landath holds out the crumpled letter.
'He might be done with the buckle. Let us go and see.'
'Here comes the last trial, ${PLAYER}. We have done it, but we are over three days late! What do you think Habdir will say when we deliver the clasp?'

'Well, hello there, ${RACE} and young master! What is this here?'
He takes the letter and furrows his brow as he reads it.
'A buckle for Lord Forlong's armour? Broke it putting it on, did he? Ah ha ha ha! And as he's a lord, it must be a fine-filigreed buckle, musn't it? Rhofin's the man for such a job. Now you'll have to give me a moment, but I promise, it won't take long.'
'It won't be long. Just you wait.'
'It won't be long. Just you wait.'
'Go on. Take that buckle to Master Habdir.'

Araslant lies recovering in the Houses of Healing. If you should get separated from Bereneth, use Bergil's whistle to call her back.
Now that you have given out the flowers, you should return to Bereneth's father, Araslant.

'Oh good, ${PLAYER}, you are here. My heart felt like butterflies. My stomach felt like butterflies. My head felt like butterflies!
'You see, I was only told that Father was hurt, but I do not know how bad and I am afraid to see. And also the Healer, Delion is his name, is tall and grave and I am afraid of him as well.
'Still, now that you are here, I shall try to be brave. Father is brave and so are you, and I shall try to be as well.'

'Bereneth, is it you? You have come. Or do I dream once more?'
A nearly silent choking fit overtakes the wounded soldier.
'No, I dream not. Bereneth, it is you. And this good ${RACE} has brought you to me? No thanks...'
Another coughing fit overtakes him.
'...no thanks can suffice.'
'What is wrong with him? Is he dying? Oh, ${PLAYER}, what should we do?'

'If you please, ${CLASS}... I heard tell of what you did for Bergil and you see, the thing is... well, my father went out to fight when they rode to get Lord Faramir.
'And, well, he took a wound out there and is in the Houses of Healing now and I haven't been to see him and I should like ever so much to do that but I dare not go in all alone and it is just that I was hoping - I was hoping you might go in with me, if you would.'
'Do you think… do you think we might feed him an apple?'
'Oh, you feed it to him. I wouldn't dare!'
'Yes, I think it is time to see if Father is awake.'
'Is this for me? And here I thought I was all but forgotten.'
'I thank you, little one. My own daughters are far away, in Tumladen. You make my heart sore for the sight of them.'
The man takes the flower with a grave and sorrowful face, holds it to his nose, and nods.
'Try to understand what I ask, Bereneth. I prize these flowers you picked more than gold and that is the very reason why I would give it to my brothers in arms.'
'If it is Father's wish, let us give out these flowers to the other wounded men.'
'I saw to Araslant. Now there are others who need me more. Off with you and out of my ward.'
'We've given out the flowers. Now we should return to father.'
'Oh, thank you. Thank you.'
'Why, what a lovely flower. When I wake to its fragrance, I shall think I am in Lossarnach and these are not times of war.'
'A little maid, handing me a flower? Surely I am dreaming, but at least I dream no more of Orcs and mud and slashing swords.'

'You have given the flowers out? This kindness is a finer gift than any flowers.
'Bereneth, I would hold your hand until the end of days, but I must sleep and Delion might cuff you on the ears if he finds you here again. Will you visit me tomorrow? Are you brave enough to come on your own? Good.'
Shadowfax accepts the apple with gentle dignity.

'Oh, how regal he is!
'His mane is more like silk than silver, and he has not spoken, at least to us. But see his eyes, ${PLAYER}, see how wise they look. Do you think he understands? I think he does.'
Bereneth takes a deep breath.
'I think we should go back to Father now.'

'There you are, Bereneth. How good to see your face. And what do you have there? Flowers? Let me smell them. Mmm... ah.
'Delion has just come and gone, and I am much refreshed, though he interrupted my slumber and I think soon I will need to sleep again.
'Listen, there is one more thing I want you to do for me today. There are other men who are wounded worse than me, and who do not have brave daughters with big hearts to bring them flowers. Will you go about the ward and bring each of them some of the flowers you picked? That's my girl.'
'I will try to be brave, if that is what I must do to see Father.'
'Is he dying, ${PLAYER}? What should we do?'

'Ah...'
Araslant takes a long, unsteady draught.
'That is better. Bereneth, do not tremble for I am not so poorly as I appear. The healer who attends to us here, Delion, is as severe as he is thoughtless.
'He starves me and then brings me two meals at once. I ask for water and he leaves it out of my grasp. If I did not know better, I might say the sight of true war-wounds has unnerved the man.
'If you would do one thing more for me, daughter and friend, go and find him now. The poultice on my wounds is long past changing, and I require some other respites from my discomfiture, but I fear there is not a bell in all Gondor I could ring loud enough to catch that man's ear.'
'I tremble just thinking of that man. How could I ever go up to him and say - no, you will have to do it, ${PLAYER}!'
'Find Delion, if you can, and tell him I need attending some time before the next meal.'

Bereneth wipes her face, concealing a tear.
'I will come tomorrow, and the next day, and the next day, and the next day, until he is all well again.
'Are those footsteps? Do you think the healer's coming? We'd better go!'

'There you are, ${PLAYER}. You may be very brave, but I can run back to the Old Guest-house faster than you! Do you think Father will be well enough to walk tomorrow? What do you think I should bring him? Not another flower. I wonder if Mithrandir's steed will be there when I return? Maybe I can pet his neck, if he'll let me.'

'There, I made a bouquet of them. Isn't it pretty? Say, do you think it's true what they say about Mithrandir's steed, that he can talk and play the harp, and that his mane is true silver threads?
'Well, he is here in the High Stables, or so I have heard. Let us go and see for ourselves, if we can!'
'Do not worry for me, ${PLAYER}. A man's wound does not frighten me half as much as that Delion.'
'I don't see what was so hard or lengthy about that!'
'Let us go back to Father, ${PLAYER}.'
'We will just walk about a bit, and when we return, Father will have woken. First, I think, the Greensward.'
'We'll have a bouquet of them, and we'll bring them to Father!'
'Let us see if Mithrandir's steed truly is in the High Stables.'
'I am right here, daughter, and I have not gone deaf. I need only a little water. Will you bring me that cup there, ${PLAYER}, if that is your name? I fear it is beyond my grasp.'
'Yes, let's leave him and go back to Father. We have good news and how I would like to make him smile!'

'Oh, but I do not want to go away and leave him now! What if I have to come back alone? What if he, if he...
'Can we stay a little longer, ${PLAYER}? Please? I know, why don't we stroll about the tier, like you did with Bergil? Only it's so much prettier up here. Then we'll come back, and Father will be awake, and I will speak to him again before I go.
'First, let us visit the Greensward. It is just outside!'

'Have you brought the salve? You have not. You are empty-handed and I do not know who you are. Why is this little girl in my ward? There are wounded men lying about.'
You explain that Araslant needs the healer's help.
'His poultices might be nine days old and still there would be others in greater need of my aid here. I am but one man, though a healer trained and called, and these men, their wounds, I...'
The healer stares wide-eyed at his own hands.
'If you want my help, then help me. Go about and see what aid you can lend. I am healer, hosteller, and hand-holder all in one, and it is too much.'

'What? You're still here? You mean you actually attended to the men? I hardly expected - please tell me you did not have that girl at your elbow the whole time.
'Well, perhaps I shall have time to attend to Araslant. I would have got to him sooner or later, anyway. I am up to my elbows, not my eyebrows!
'Now leave me to my work, or you'll use up the time you have saved me. Shoo!'
'Do you think… do you think we might feed him an apple?'
'I know, let's pick some flowers. Surely, nobody will mind!'

Landath stands accused in Chandler's Lane, which is on the southern reach of the First Circle.
Talk to Landath to hear his side of the story.

'${PLAYER}, there you are! The sweets have come from Himnir and we've decided to hold a Finder's Gathering. Of course you will join us, won't you? Oh, but you must. You're to be the guest of honour!
'We can't have a gathering with just sweets, of course, and besides, everyone's got to bring a thing or two. That's what makes it a Gathering!
'Now what should YOU bring, I wonder? Hm... Well, we'll need some small ale. And you need only ask Húndil here in the Old Guest-house for some. Why don't you start there?'
'Look at this ragged urchin, will you, and tell me how he could have come by coin in this amount. By picking pockets, that's how!'

'Truly, ${PLAYER}, I would never steal a single coin, let alone this many! Didn't I set things right with Master Habdir in the end? By the kings of old, I swear, I found these coins in the Finding Place. But just you try and explain the Finding Place to HER!
'Please, speak to her. I only want to buy some candles!'
'The Old Guest-house has plenty of small ale. Just ask Húndil, inside. He might give it to you, or maybe you'll have to pay him.'
'Ask Meldis at the Wheel and Cask. With any luck, she'll have some small ale for you.'
'Húndil hadn't any? These are dark times, ${PLAYER}. Let us hope the Wheel and Cask does!'
'The small ale is back in my stores. Help yourself to it.'
'Soldiers' victuals from the butteries in the Lower Stores. That's the second thing you can bring, ${PLAYER}.'
'I'll just be studying the wall over here. I won't see anything you walk off with.'
'Landath went to the Wrights' Market for some candles. I would start searching for him there.'
'Oh, why do these things always happen to me? Please, talk to her, ${PLAYER}!'

'You vouch for this child? Well, he is dressed rather wretchedly and has a hangdog look, you must admit. But some other chandler will take his coin, if I don't. And if it is ill-got, let it be your conscience that wakes you at night!'

'You and Landath are back. Gelwen and Glatham aren't, but I'm sure they will be, any moment now. They're coming all the way from the Upper Stores, after all.
'Yes, I think it's best if we began without them. Everyone else is here and the hour grows late.'
'He thinks to buy my candles with purloined coin. Hmph!'
'Please, tell her I haven't stolen a thing and only wish to buy some candles!'
'You have saved my hide again, ${PLAYER}! You go ahead and tell Bergil I'm coming. I'll gather up these candles and be on my way in a moment.'
'The boy will have his candles, don't you worry. But I'll be rid of these coins as soon as business allows, in case they bear ill fortune!'

'Small ale, is it? Don't you want something stronger? Eh heh heh heh! But of course I know this is for the boys and girls, isn't it? Well, I'm afraid you'll be the bearer of ill tidings, for I haven't any. Gave those urchins the last of it three days back.
'Say, you might ask at the Wheel and Cask though. Yes, they might have some there.'
'Small ale? I have some and you're welcome to it. We may die tomorrow and those urchins may drink fine wine, for all that I care. You can go back there in my stores and take it yourself.'

'Small ale! Good. Now let's see, we've got the sweets, Mídion's brought bread, Landath's gone for candles and Gelwen and Glatham have gone for some jars of jam... ah, but what else could you bring, ${PLAYER}?
'I know! In the butteries of the Lower Stores, there are parcels of soldiers' victuals. They've got tack and some herbs, but most of all, dried meats. It should be awfully nice to have some meat, and I think the dried kind is the best that we shall get. Perhaps for you, they would be willing to part with some.'

'Why, aren't you the ${RACE} who gave Oryat a proper thrashing? Oh, word's gone round among the soldiers, right enough. And all agree - all but Oryat's cronies, leastwise - that it was a fine thing to do.
'Now you go on and take anything you like from the buttery. I'll look the other way, eh?'

'And the victuals! You are tried and true, ${PLAYER}, that's what you are. I wish I could say as much for Landath. He went off for candles quite some time ago and still has not come back. ${PLAYER}, will you go look for him in the Wrights' Market, and see if he hasn't got himself in some scrape or another?'

'What, no, I wasn't... oh, forget it.'
'Oh, um... these are mine. I was just... moving this stuff.'
'Get out of here! You have no authority here!'

'Though the future of our city may not look so bright, I will not see its dignity fall. Not before its walls do, at least...
'Thank you.'
'Um... thank goodness you're here! Some shady character just ran off... after dropping this bag of goods! I think they went... that way?'
'Big mistake, friend. I advise you to walk away while you still can.'
'Oh... if you don't tell anyone I was here, I'll give you a take of the goods!'

'Oh! Why are you bothering with such petty crimes as this?
'The enemies of men lurk ever closer!'
'These people are never coming back! What're they going to need their stuff for?'
'What do you want? Mind your business!'
Thieves confronted (${CURRENT}/${MAX})

'With so many people evacuating the city, many homes have been left empty.
'Unfortunately, there are some honourless thieves about that have taken the empty homes as an opportunity... and there aren't enough guards to take care of it.
'Would you mind looking for some of these foul thieves and teaching them a lesson? And return any stolen goods they have on them while you're at it.'

You can enter the cisterns at the southern end of the First Circle.
The mysterious woman has bade you repair the breach where the goblins entered the cisterns before you speak further.
'I have always loved the fountains outside the Baths. Let us stroll over there.'
'Speak not until we are back at my home. I must think!'

Lady Raenemel beams.
'Speak with the boy, ${PLAYER}. He will tell you all.'
'You will not believe your ears, ${PLAYER}. She says it was she who placed all the things in the Finding Place. But I think that also - ah, never mind that. You should speak to her yourself.'

'Where was I? These children have only the barest of notions what hopelessness there is, and though all should fall tomorrow, I will NOT have unquenched candles dimmed. I will not break that spell. Nor would you! I see it in your eyes. I know of how you stood up to that petty ruffian. Yes, I hear much, though I am not seen.
'I heard of Lord Boromir's end and it pierced my heart, it did. And now - Lord Faramir! Though all others remember them as grown men, noble and brave, in my mind they are but boys. For I was their tutor and governess, and the memory of the light in their eyes when I showed to them knowledge, truth, and wisdom - it fades not.
'But let us not tarry here.'

'${PLAYER}, there is something I must say. An explanation is in order. But no, not here.
'Walk with me.'
Lady Raenemel nods southward down the street.

'These children. One can plainly see - even from afar - how they are untouched, untouched by the dark despair that has fallen over this fortress-city. Untouched by even the Enemy's pall that has darkened the skies. And I cannot, will not...
'You see, it was my sons who first discovered the hole in that wall. And you should have seen the light in their eyes when they discovered what I had hidden there. Do you think, had they known it was I, the same light would have shone?
'Come. Up that way.'

'Do you know why I took you on this stroll? To explain to you how I would not budge. How I would remain a watchful statue, above and far off, and help only as I may from the shadows.
'But, I know not how, in endeavouring to explain myself, I have budged. Relented! I am a clouded pool, I am a troubled heart, but I cannot help but feel that beyond this pain I feel lies, might I call it... hope?'

'${PLAYER}! ${PLAYER}! I can hardly believe it. It WAS she who left the things for us. And she will come to see us now at the Old Guest-house, and we are all welcome to come here now, at any time. And she will let us see old rooms in the Houses of Lore we would never be allowed into otherwise. And any who wish it shall receive lessons!
'But I am going on, aren't I? Ha ha! This is a good day, ${PLAYER}, even if tomorrow will not be so. And I thank you, for you have brought many things to light, haven't you, in the end?'
'Speak with her, ${PLAYER}.'

'Do you doubt that I tutored the Steward's sons? Many years had I laboured in the Houses of Lore, and after my sons perished in Lord Denethor's bid to retake old Osgiliath, he was wise and kind and generous in charging me with his own sons.
'Few have seen my face in the years since they left my tutelage. Indeed, I have rarely left my chambers. But when I discovered the prizes I left in that crevice being taken not by the season or the month, but by the day - or more often - I found ways of watching the takers without being seen.
'Like you, I have watched over these children. Only, in my own way, and you must understand that. This is what I am trying to impart to you. My own way.'

'Had I gone to Tumladen with the wains, as I was meant to... but I am an old thing, withered with grief and more at ease with my books than with living souls. Do you know, I wander the City by night, greeting ancient stones like friends, taking care never to cross the path of a living, breathing soul?
'And so you must understand, ${PLAYER}, you must undertake for me - these children, though I will love them from afar, they cannot, I will not... I am old, you see, and crooked with grief...
'I am like a troubled pool, ${PLAYER}, and nothing is clear to me. Let us return. I must think. Yes, think.'
'Lady Raenemel's house is in the Fourth Circle, right by the Finding Place.'
'How did Lady Raenemel stay in the City, I wonder? I don't think anyone has ever seen her before!'
'She lives just around the way from the Finding Place! How many times have we gone past her, and never known!'
'Go on, if that's what she wants. I'll be all right.'
'I have some words that I wish to say to you... over there.'
'Over there, where there is a small garden beside the path.'
'Up the stairs to the wall-walk, where we may have a view.'
'Let us not tarry, but go on along the wall-walk.'
'I owe you much, ${CLASS}, but first the breach within the cisterns must be mended. You can be trusted with such a task, yes?'
'Here is the ${CLASS}. Bergil, would you be good enough to stay here a moment? This ${RACE} and I must speak alone.'

'Why look there. Good as any mason! You are full of marvels, ${PLAYER}.
'The lady, Lady Raenemel it is, she told me where she lives. We should go there now, and speak with her. She is in the Fourth Circle, near the Finding Place, of course.'
Several Mendings
Learn more about what happened in the Cisterns and the mysterious woman you found there.

It is good of her to keep my home a place of beauty and calm in my absence, while I am out here, protecting the prosperity of Gondor.
'Thank you for the news, traveller. It gives me hope, and it is a reminder of what I fight for. I shall one day return home.'

'I haven't had any Old Calembel in years. But you might find some in the Middle Stores.'
'If we've got any Old Calembel, it's far at the back. Take any you find in there. Nobody else seems to want it.'

'And with one sip, a flood of memories! How we sat at this very table, night upon night. Our glasses full of Beren's Blood and Old Calembel cheese upon our plates.
'${CLASS}, you have kindly furnished us with the wine. Can you find us the cheese, as well? Do some old men a kindness!'

'Old Calembel? Ah, well. I don't know what to say, but that some things linger and some things fade away. I haven't had any of that cheese for a good many years. Though now that I think of it, you might try the back of the Middle Stores, just up the way. You'll find all kinds of things back there, you will.'
'Do us a kindness and see if Imadan's got some Old Calembel cheese lying around.'
'What? Old Calembel? Aye, I think we might well have some, farther in. I'm not going back there. If you want some, you'll need to go yourself.'
'But now we have our wine and our regrettable cheese. Finish your tale, Forlong. You had so many bottles of Beren's Blood under your coats... and what then?'

'Why, old Minastúr, the last Master of the Burg stumbled across us! It was blind luck, and very bad at that. He knew at once we were the ones who'd done it, and he set to chasing us, waving that iron cane he went about with at us most menacingly!
'In fact, he swung at my head and nearly took it off. To this day, there is a mark against the stone that he hit instead!'

'Ah, now you go too far! I will not allow such a wanton claim to stand. Someone must be sent. You, ${RACE}, will you go out on the street and show this for a braggart's lie? It was just north of the Pier, Forlong, was it not? Against an alley-column? Yes. Will you go and see?'
'I will confess, this is not how I remembered it. Ha ha! No, it is quite... different.'
'Is this truly the companion to our youthful wine? My eyes tell me so, but my tongue calls them liars!'
'It is tart - or perhaps merely bitter - and yet mellow. Or perhaps not so mellow as bland.'

'Well, my dear friends. If we've learned something tonight, it is that in drink old friends stay true. In taste, they may differ. Ha ha! Ha ha ha!
'Let us wash away that unfortunate taste with another drink of Beren's Blood!'
'If you could settle this question of whether the old Master's cane-mark has lasted to this day, or not, we should be ever so grateful.'

'The mark can be seen? And you swear to it? Well! I cannot shout at the sun that it is night, can I? Ha ha!
'But we interrupted ourselves mid-tale. Please, carry on!'
'Well, what did you see? I was right, wasn't I?'
'Well! As I was saying, there we were with some bottles of wine tucked in our arms, but I, for one, had also a hat, bread, some flowers, and a small rolled up rug.'
'Be a good ${RACE} and ask old Imadan if he's got any Beren's Blood wine, would you?'
'That old Beren's Blood wine is over yonder, among the storage. Take what you please.'

'Beren's Blood?'
Imadan lets out a low whistle.
'You might say that old stuff's a bit beneath lords such as they. But I know what they're at. It's what they drank when they were young men and went free about the City. I suppose recollecting old times can recollect old thirsts, eh?
'There's some over there, among my stores. You may help yourself.'

'And there we were, stumbling down the darkened street, all that wine and what-have-you stuffed under our coats! Now what was it called, that wine? The name escapes me! And to think I drank so very much of it in those years!
'Ah, hold your tongue, Hirluin! I hear the dart of wit upon it before you ever moved your lips. Forgetting comes of drinking, you will say, and so that wine was its own undoing. I guess correctly, do I not? Ha ha! But let me think one moment... was it? ... yes! Beren's Blood, it was named. How I should like a taste of that wine now!
'You there, my good ${RACE}. Since you are standing right at hand, be so good as to go ask old Imadan if he has got any.'

Hirluin catches your arm as you come up.
'Give that wine here, friend. Should you place it before Forlong, we others might never have a taste.'
This is met with hearty laughter, not least by Forlong himself.
'Here friends - a glass for you Neldir, a glass for me, yes, and one for you, Forlong, old friend. To our days of youth!'
'Why, what have we here? It is a memory in the round, my friends! I thank you, good ${CLASS}. Hirluin, hand me that bread. Forlong, the knife. Let us put fond memory to our lips.'

'And look, we have drained this bottle of Beren's Blood. Why, friend, I know what you should do. You should run and place it on that stone he loved, as a tribute to his memory. Yes, that is just the thing!'

'The bottle is placed? That is good. We did well to honour old Authlin.'
Forlong closes his eyes and for a moment, the garrulous conversation comes to a rest.

'Hold! Hold! This is too much. Confess, Forlong, for NOW you have embellished! Ah, I know that set of the jaw. You stand by your story, do you? So be it.
'Friend ${CLASS}, as you have not wandered off, I wonder if you will settle another quibble. Can you find such things as these and bring them here? Surely they can all be found somewhere in this Circle. What did you say, Forlong? It was a hat, some bread, some flowers, and a small rug?'

'Ho ho! This is a mess! I am sorry, friend. Forlong, we see through your plans now. You fed us one truth in hopes we would swallow a lie!
'But tell me, even if you could bear all that in your arms, why in Isildur's name WOULD you?'
'That wasn't how it went at all. You haven't the grasp, and besides, your heart wasn't in it!'
'Lord Forlong here must not be indulged or allowed such extravagant tales. Do see if you can find those things somewhere nearby.'
'You will see, Neldir. It can be done and I did it!'
'Hm... Is this claim to be the wine... or the cheese?'
'How marvelous! You have brought the things. Now we will put it to the test. Can you walk from here to there and carry these? I do not even ask you to run.'
'If you are looking for Authlin, you have missed him by ten years. Though, for what it's worth, I have heard he died with a glass of wine in his hand and a song on his lips.'

'How many times have I heard Authlin the Minstrel's name spoken? There are many tales told of that man. Why that patch of green, across the way over there, was his favourite place to perform. They say the night air filled with his harp as he stood there and played sweet melodies to the stars.'

'Authlin? Why I knew him well, perhaps better than most, though I have not seen him in many a year. I will tell you something I remember of him. Sometimes, after a night of drink and merriment and song, he would confess to me that though his heart burned bright, there was a well of sorrow in it, too, and they ever wrestled. Sorrow for what, he would never tell. And then, sometimes, he would tell me he meant to fight the sorrow and love all the world until he knew his time had come, and then how sweet his rest would be. That is what he told me.'

'So Authlin lived a good life and died a willing death? Truly, that is the wisdom of old Westernesse!
'Let us honour him and raise a glass. You, too, friend ${CLASS}! You have earned your place, I think!'
'Well done. That was quite amusing.'

'Why, to woo the heart of my Vanyalos! Oh, do not give such frowns, you goats. None of us have forgotten the procession of maids swooning over you, Hirluin. Nor that tale of climbing the circle-wall, with... what was her name, that one maid with the dark hair?'
'That was an invention of the minstrel Authlin, and what is more, I think you know it. Though I hold that she spread the tale with as much relish as the minstrel ever did.'

'I doubt it not, Hirluin. The maids ever fell under your cold spell.
'Old Authlin, though. Now there was a minstrel of uncommon gifts! And a bit of a mischief-maker, too, wasn't he? But who would not forgive words so sweetly sung, or deftly penned! Of war he sang and kings of old, of flowery vales and shepherd's pipes, and of fair-eyed maids.
'You, Neldir, you have lived in Minas Tirith all this time. Does he live and play still? You know not? I must learn his fate. My good ${RACE}, may we lean upon your goodness once again? Will you go up into the Fourth Circle and learn what became of Authlin, Master Minstrel?'
In Days of Youth

'Tell me friends, were things so very grim back then, as they are now? For that is not how I recall it. Or perhaps, being less in stature and wisdom, we did not look beyond this city's walls. It is a happy thing, is it not, to see no farther than your own strong walls?
'Ah, but then wanderlust comes over you. Why, Authlin himself sang a sweet, sad song on the subject. I hardly think of a harp more fairly fingered, or words more surely put to melody. How did it go?
'When dawn over the - when over the mountain - no, no. Hirluin, help me here.'

'Ha ha! Whereas Osgiliath reminded us only of what had once been great, in Gondor, and is no more. Yes, let us not quarrel over this.
'Nothing makes peace so well as food and drink, but I see that we are low on food. Will our new friend do us another kindness, and ask them to bring another course?'
'More food is it? I'll have it brought. You've done enough going about and carrying things for those three.'
'There is more to be said, and remembered, and sung. And for that, we shall want more food!'

'The feast continues, and we have you to thank. It seems to me that we owe much to our new friend, for this happy time before the coming storm.
'Here, then, let us raise a glass and welcome you into our little company. To old friends and to new!'
'Let us have a cheer for our new friend's fine acting! It casts my mind back, it does. The times of war, when Thorongil and Denethor stood side by side.'
'Until they did not stand side by side, if you recall. Thorongil left us and then Denethor grew cold on him... though some say the order was reversed.'

'Aye, then it was Denethor's turn to lead us into battle. The Taking of Osgiliath! Or one of them, at least.
'It has always seemed to me, though both men were stern and serious, that when we marched under Denethor's command, it was a graver, more tiresome affair. By the look on your face, Hirluin, I see you disagree. Or no, that is not it. It is that you will not hear ill spoken of our good steward.'

'You read my face too well. Denethor is not so hard or uncharitable a man as I think you take him for. He is a good man with great - nay, unbearable burdens.
'But I am forced to confess that for me, too, the memories of Umbar shine somehow brighter, on recollection, than Osgiliath. I blame it on our youth and newness to battle, and the enchantment of journeying to foreign lands.'
'To old friends and to new!'

'To old times and the roads that led us here! To battles fought and battles yet to come. Yes, battles to come.'
For a second time, Forlong falls into silence.
'Food will be sent, presently. Do not worry. My lad will bring it up.'
'The war trophy stands in the Houses of Lore, up in the Fifth Circle. Will you bring it to me?'

'Why, that is it! And it is just as I remembered it. You see, Hirluin and Thorongil stood about as far as... there, back to back, their swords flashing. I had made a great rush, my axe hewing all in the path, for I had seen the sorcerer across the room begin to work some foul spell. Alas, a tall half-troll stood barring my way. Not for long! He took my axe like all the rest, though it stuck in him and I could not quickly draw it out. So, thinking on my toes, I wrenched this standard from its place and struck the cruel spell-weaver down where he stood!'
'You should pen a song, yourself, Forlong. You do a fine job singing your own praises.'

'Ever the sharp wit and sharper tongue, old friend! To my mind, you are too modest in never boasting for yourself. I will right both flaws and boast for you.
'Did you know that once Hirluin held at bay two, nay three dozen corsairs, merely by throwing knives? We were surprised, and found ourselves in an Umbar tavern, weaponless but backs against the stores of cutlery. He grabbed handfuls, and like rain they flew! Why, if you gathered the knives from these tables here, I feel sure Hirluin could still show you how it was done.
'You will show us how you did it, Hirluin? Oh, come. You must!'
'It amazes me to think you stood side by side with Thorongil. Now that is a name of legends and song! Tell me, friends, what was he like, in speech, and look, and action?'

'Names always seem thus, when they sail off and are never seen or heard from again! Ah, but Hirluin and I knew him well, back then. There was a greatness in him, and in truth, he always seemed to me as one of the men of Númenor, newly landed on Gondor's shores. All the same, he was a man, and had all such peculiarities as men have.
'Do you remember, Hirluin, what he did with his arm when he called us over to him? It was, no, I cannot do it from my seat. You, friend. See if you can do it.'
'Of all my acts of swordsmanship and cunning, you chose this to tell?'
'Take two fistfuls of knives off the tables. Hirluin will re-enact the feat.'

'I do this against all my better judgement. Let me see. We stood here and they, there. I turned and grabbed the knives and then... yes then I flung out my arm, like so.'
Two handfuls of knives clatter to the floor at Hirluin's feet.
'Bah! These knives are not weighted at all like those were. Who am I deceiving? I am an old man and I have forgotten much. I believe and hope, at least, my skill with a sword is not so far forgotten!'
'Give him the knives, friend. He will show you how it was done.'

'Come now. Only one who knew Thorongil, and knew him well, could have mimicked such a face! This is true art. It is uncanny!
'Well, now, Forlong shouldn't have all the fun. Why don't you try smoking your pipe? He always did so with a stern and thoughtful look, as though the pipe-bowl were giving him grave and secret council.'

'Why, that was just how Thorongil did it! Wasn't it, Hirluin? You hit it on the very first try. You have a talent for this, ${CLASS}!
'Now you really must try another. Ah, I know! Thorongil, when no one was watching, would sometimes sigh in a manner most melancholy. Can you sigh for us, friend?'
'That was very convincing, friend.'
'That was very like unto Thorongil's beckon.'

'I am amazed! Somehow, you have captured Thorongil. Have you ever acted upon the stage? Well, here is a challenge for you: there was a particular stern look - let us call it solemn - that would come over Thorongil's face when planning his battle strategy. Let us see you try such a solemn face.'
'There was dawn... and restless feet... and something, something to meet. I'm afraid those are all I can muster, old friend. Neldir, can you remember? No?'

'Yes, I remember Authlin, though I was but a girl, and I know the song as well.
I'll fly away and further roam But I will never turn back home No I shall... I shall....
'Is that how it went? Well, I have recalled some of it, at least!'
'Authlin's song must be recalled and sung, else we do him grave injury. And I would not injure the dead.'

You recite and hum what you were able to gather. Lord Forlong closes his eyes and thinks.
'Yes, yes, my friend. I think it is enough. Let us see. Ahem!
When o'er mountain sun comes rising With stirring heart and restless feet I'll find myself this home despising And yearn for distant lands to meet
I'll fly away, I will not stay Seeking fortune, love, and war I'll fly away and further roam But I will never turn back home No I shall wend back there no more No more, no more, no more, no more....
'There! So sad and sweet. There were other verses of course. Love was won and lost. Battles and fortunes, too.'

'That was a fine song, and it was just so that we went off to war, you and I. He sang of us, too, didn't he? Standing by Thorongil's side in the Breaking of Umbar. Though now that I come to think of it, he sang mostly of Thorongil, and of Umbar's Breaking. Still, we are named.'

'What? We have drunk in his memory and then forgotten his songs? Should people say Authlin was a drinker and not a master song-smith? This is an insult that cannot be endured!
'Do not look at me like that, Hirluin. I have not drunk my fill, nor am I anywhere near done with drinking! And I shall be ready with my axe, a match for any foe, now or three bottles hence! Even with the clasp on my armour un-mended.
'Now where was I? The song must be recalled. Recalled and sung! Most helpful ${CLASS}, you must find rememberers. Perhaps the barkeep here knows a line. Or Golasgil or old Aglarang. Bariel the Master Hosteller? Someone!'
'Alas, I am no poet and far less a minstrel.'

'That song about wanderlust? Why yes, I've heard it. I heard Authlin sing it many a time. How did it go?
I'll fly away, I will not stay Seeking fortune, love, and war
'That much I can recall. I'm afraid the rest is, well, not even a memory!'

'The song Authlin used to sing? Of wandering? Now that casts me back many a year! Hm... Over a mountain, sun comes rising... find myself this home despising... no, I'm afraid I have no more of it than that!'

'I can indeed recall that song. The melody is as clear in my head as if he were here. Hmm hmmmm hum hum hm hm hmmmm.... But the words? Well. No, I cannot muster a single one. Ah, how memory betrays a body!'

'Named? Ha ha, that makes it sound as if we merely stood about! We fought by Thorongil's side, Hirluin and I, and weathered the thick of it, far off there in the south. Now, I do not wish to be unfair. The strategem was Thorongil's, and never, I think, was there a finer swordsman - or a faster walker!
'But all the same, we had our own deeds worthy of song. Tell them, Hirluin, how I took the sorcerer's standard and with it struck him down as he stood there, chanting foul things!'
'Moreso than you have done, just now? You'd need to bring that battle-standard here and show them, to paint a clearer picture. You took it as a trophy, did you not?'

'By the seven-pointed star, I did! And left here, in Minas Tirith, within the Houses of Lore. Ah, to hold that fell thing in my hands again....'
Forlong turns to you.
'Ah, my friend, I have asked much of you. But would you do one more good turn for old Forlong? Would you go up to the Fifth Circle and fetch my trophy for me? I think you will find it in the Houses of Lore... somewhere.'
Umbar and Osgiliath
