'Ask among the magistrates up in the Sixth Circle. See if you can learn what became of Laranís.'
'There, Hirluin, that is the path you might have had. Two fine sons, and archers under the Steward!'
'Did you not note that the husband is dead? If that is where the other path led, then no thank you!'
'And I make for the third path, I suppose, for I wed but children never came to us. Do you wish you had sons instead of daughters, Forlong?'
'It was not the path for me. I have chosen another way through life, and hold no regrets.'

'Still, you must wonder sometimes what might have been. That maid old Authlin made so much of, who climbed the City walls to you - or didn't, as you maintain - do you never wonder what became of her? Nay, answer not, you would not confess it if you did. She was a magistrate's daughter, I think? Yes. Laranís, she was called.
'Let our new friend ask among the magistrates and councilors up in the Sixth Circle for us and learn what became of her. Then we will see if we can win a blush from that pale, fair face of yours!'

'Yes, I did know Laranís, long ago. She did not wed for many years, and some began to call her a spinster. When she did join in marriage, it was to an older man. I never met him. I do not think he frequented the Sixth Circle.'

'Laranís? Yes, I know her well. She is in Imloth Melui now and her sons are among Denethor's archers, posted up upon the gates. She is a widow, you know. That is what comes of marrying an older man, though the merchant's wealth he left her must console her grief to some degree. Or so I am told wealth sometimes can.'

'Thank you for sharing this time with us, my good ${RACE}. I feel a quiet coming on, and I see the same upon the faces of my friends. You are welcome here among us, but I think little more shall be said. Dawn will come soon, or what passes for dawn in these strange days. Yes. We'll greet the new day quietly.'
With that, Lord Forlong falls silent, and speaks no more.
'Our new friend returns! And have you beards? Let us look over them and judge.'

'You would have spoken better and more wisely if you had said sons as well as daughters, Neldir. No father with one strand of goodness in him has ever unwished his child, be they boy or girl. Nor could anyone unwish my two flowers.
'Why, I have their likenesses in a locket among my things. And now that we have called to mind that battle coming any hour, I dislike my locket there, so far from my breast. What if the horns should blow, and I were without it? No, this thought unsettles me. I am ill at ease.
'Friend, will you do one last thing and ease my mind? My quarters are up in the Citadel, in the Southern Great Guest-house. Will you go there, find my locket, and bring it here to me?'
'My locket will be among my quarters in the Southern Great Guest-house, in the Citadel. Will you bring it here and put my mind at rest?'

'There it is - my locket. See, friends, here are Vanyalos and our daughters. My heart warms to look on them. Oh ho ho, or is that the wine? No, no. Wine unlocks the doors of the heart, but love must light the hearth!
'Let us raise one final glass, my friends. You are so dear to me. We must hold this moment and savour it, and let tomorrow come what may!'
'There would be little point in giving ready fighting men errands about the city. It would only slow their response to the Enemy's attack - and we must assume they may attack at any moment, now.
'Nothing will come of this. It is a waste of breath.'

'I know not if they have beards to the very last man. But by the reports, Lord Forlong, they sound much like your people in Lossarnach, who have less of the blood of Númenor. That is where I cast my vote.'
'I shall take no sides, but only say that if every man among them has a beard, they are dwarf-kin. But if their beards vary as we do in height and the colour of our eyes, then I declare them Men.'
'They are dwarves, and I will have it shown! Our new friend here looks well-travelled and up for some fighting. Perhaps you could bring us back some Sûhalar-beards to settle this dispute.'
'Well! At least there are a handful fewer enemies to fight. That is well done, ${CLASS}, no matter who is right.'
'Bah! Why can you old fools not see that I am plainly right?'

'Do you see, Forlong, we have fallen to quarreling again. If Mithrandir were here, I think he would say it was the nearness of the Enemy, for discord and strife springs up wherever that shadow falls. Now let us take your own advice, friend, and make peace by raising a glass among well-loved friends.'
'You must settle this dispute for us. Slip out of the City and deprive some Sûhalar of their beards, so we may look over them and judge.'
'It is just as I said, they are like unto dwarf beards.'
'Those seem like the beards of mortal Men to me, only braided in a foreign fashion.'
'How people talked! Terenis spurned and her sister Vanyalos wooed in her stead. To this day, I am amazed that you dared defy Lord Denethor in which of his sisters you would wed.'
'Oh, it was not Denethor I trembled before, but Terenis! Her wrath lingers to this day. You should have seen it while the iron was hot!'

'You did put Lord Denethor in a difficult position, old friend. He could not take sides between the sisters, whom he loved. That he bore it silently and did not set his heart against you speaks much of him, I think.'
'You broke some few hearts in that time, yourself, Hirluin the Fair. How is it none of those smitten maidens ever softened your resolve and lured you into marriage?'
'That was well-spoken, Hirluin. And I hold that we must ever keep love's warmth kindled in our hearts, if we are to prevail against that which shall not be named.'
'Not named, but too soon joined in battle, I fear!'

'For this moment, I shall not dwell on that, Neldir. I am here with you, old friends and new, in a City I have loved dearly since my youth. And how could I not love it, when it was here that I found Vanyalos, my heart's desire? It was here I wooed her first, and then afterwards in the flowering fields of Lossarnach, my home.'

'Battles to come! Enemy hosts! Why, there is one perched under the very lintel of Minas Tirith, and here we have been, sitting, utterly ignorant of how they are getting on! Friend ${CLASS}, you are up and we, as you can see, are down. Would you dash outside, ascend the wall here, and gaze upon the state of the opposing force?'
'Mind you, we three are ready to leap up at a moment's notice and charge into battle. Even if I must do so with this blasted broken buckle! But we shall not leap spuriously, before the call, no!'

'They yet prepare. That is well. Let us err on the side of caution and vigilance, all the same. Will you find Húrin, Master of the Keys, and inquire as to our general state of readiness, and whether there are final preparations to which we might lend our hands?
'Húrin was down by the City Gates, last I saw him.'

'All greater measures have been attended to. The lesser ones are well in hand. Soon we shall have naught but to watch and wait. Neither Lord Denethor nor Mithrandir can foresee or even guess at what the Enemy plans. I know, for I have sat in their councils.
'As to Lords Forlong and Hirluin... if their men are at the ready and they come swiftly when the horns blow, that is all that can be asked of them.'
'Go find Húrin, Warden of the Keys, by the City Gates. See if there are final preparations to which we might lend our hands.'
'Naught to do but to wait, eh? My axe will be ready, come what may!'

'Have you heard there are axe-wielding Easterlings upon the field? So the scouts are saying. They have beards like dwarves and call themselves Sûhalar. Imagine you cross men such as they in battle, Forlong. Would there be confusion amongst these Sûhalar and the Men of Lossarnach?'
'One must wonder, Forlong, if these be ancient cousins of your kind. Neldir, do they all have beards, every one?'
'Cousins? Because they hold axes? What nonsense! Clearly they are dwarf-kin and no blood of mine!'

'Thank you for taking care of some of those efts. That may help encourage the people to return to this village. Either that, or the remaining efts may move in! Wouldn't that be something? Hmm... so what brought you out here anyway, ${CLASS}?'
You tell Humfrey that Bert Bartleby sent you with a coin-purse to find him and purchase some scrolls, tomes, or potions.
'Mister Bartleby! Well, imagine that. His family and mine were neighbours, you know. There was always such a racket coming from the Bartleby house. Growing up with fourteen boys will do that! How are Bert and his many, many brothers, anyway?
'I will take this purse from you and give to you these sundries. I am certain Bert will find something among them to his liking!'

'You found Humfrey and saved him from a predicament of his own making? That is very typical of a Rumming, ${PLAYER}, and is precisely what I expected! I see that you purchased some sundries from him. Let me see those.'
Bert looks through the small collection of goods.
'Ah, there is nothing here of note. It is a pity. Well, I will take the remaining coins from you, and... what? You gave him the entire money-purse? I expected some coins back, ${PLAYER}, especially for this bundle of nothing!
'Do not trouble yourself, my friend. I am not angry! Indeed, Humfrey may have gotten the better of me in this exchange, but many years ago I gave Humfrey a pittance in coin and he gave to me a creature that would become my dearest friend. I'd say we got the better of Mister Rumming in that exchange, wouldn't you, Rattlepacks?'

'Were you able to help Bert with whatever he needed, ${PLAYER}? Good, I am glad!
'It is a marvel to me that we have seen Mister Bartleby at so many places on this journey, and he has not had much to say until this point. I wonder where he learned such patience? I have known one or two hobbits that were the same in my day, youngest siblings all! Perhaps Bert grew up with several older brothers, and learned patience at home. He is a unique individual, for certain!'

'Thank you for looking after Humfrey anyway, ${PLAYER}.'

'Wait a moment, my friend. Describe the missing lore-master for me once more, will you?'
You repeat the description you were told by the guard at the west gate, and Bert nods with familiarity.
'I know this man, ${PLAYER}! His name is Humfrey Rumming, and we go back a long way. You see, the Rummings and the Bartlebys were neighbours! Our homes were a bit out of the way, so weeks would go by and you'd only ever see a Rumming or a Bartleby! As a result, you might say that each family tended to wear on the other's patience.
'After I retired from the adventuring life, one of the first sales I ever conducted was to Humfrey Rumming: I sold him the key to the tumbled-down ruin of Tollobel on the island of Tyl Ruinen. I wonder if he ever used it?
'You'll have to find him and keep him out of trouble! The Rummings, and particularly Humfrey, have never been good at staying out of it. That guard watched him leave from the west gate? I expect he kept moving in that direction, then. Find Humfrey somewhere to the west of Forlaw. If there is a settlement in that direction, he is likely to have headed that way; like a curious moth to a torch at night is Humfrey, and all the Rummings!'

'Ah, you seem to be a fairly impressive adventurer. A ${CLASS}? I knew it! I myself am one of the world's greatest lore-masters. My name is Humfrey Rumming. You seem somewhat familiar, but since I never forget a face I will say that it is a pleasure to meet you for the very first time, ${CLASS}!
'I have a fondness for small lizards of all types, and I have a skill at nursing such creatures back to health. It is a gift I must share with the world! To that end, when I saw a clutch of eggs nestled at the base of a giant pillar of ice, I naturally warmed them up and allowed the little creatures to hatch! Naturally.
'Well, it turns out that these little efts do not take kindly to people, or to wildlife, or to plants... I think they may have scared off the people of this village, for no one is here anymore. You had better do something about those efts, ${CLASS}. They are among the woods to the west, by the base of the mountains. And please call them \qefts,\q if you would. That is what all the great lore-masters call them.'

'That guard watched Humfrey leave from the west gate? I expect he kept moving in that direction, then. Find Humfrey somewhere to the west of Forlaw. If there is a settlement in that direction, he is likely to have headed that way; like a curious moth to a torch at night is Humfrey, and all the Rummings!'

'I spoke with Egwylf, and she recommended that we take the south-western road out of Wildermore into the Entwash Vale. Let us ride there at once, and hope for a thaw!'

'For a moment I felt dread upon my heart, and sensed eyes upon our small party.
'The feeling has passed, but I do not trust that its absence means we are safe. <rgb=#FF0000>Look</rgb> from here and see if you spy anyone with evil intent.'

'You saw something high in the sky and far away? Well, I don't see anything. Do you think it might be Landroval? He was quite large, I think, even for one of the Great Eagles, but from this distance even he might appear small. The eyesight of Eagles is supposed to be incredible, isn't it? I do think he would descend and say hello to us, if he recognized us.
'Egwylf told me there is a town to the south-west, across the river. The town is called Oserley, and from there we can explore West Rohan. Time to go, Tanglemane! Let's go, W.W.! Lead the way, ${PLAYER}!'
'Did you see anything? I thought I did, for a moment, but now there is nothing.'

'This is a difficult time for the people of Oserley. You might do well to set your course for elsewhere. What do I mean?
'Everyone here is on edge. Orcs have been seen on the plains of Rohan, burning and pillaging. Even the bravest warriors are seized by invisible terrors, reduced to shadows of their former selves.
'If you take my advice and leave Oserley and its troubles behind, you would be wise to leave at nightfall. The blanket of darkness may not shield you from evil eyes, but if it helps to protect the people that live here, I urge you to make use of it.'

'I just returned from my patrol, so I cannot tell you much of Oserley. But I can tell you that something is not right on the fields of Rohan. As I returned hither from the town of Stoke, a feeling of unease took hold of me. I saw nothing, but I would swear before my Thane that some creature watched me from afar.
'The stillness was broken by a terrible cry, bird-like and yet not so. I am glad to be back in Oserley, but the memory of that haunting cry stays with me. My blood freezes at the thought of it.
'It may have been nothing, but beware! We would all do well to remain alert when such evils are abroad in the Mark!'
'There is a town in West Rohan called Oserley. It is to the south-west, across the river. That is where we should go next.'

'I agree with Éoric. We should not stay here. Let us leave beneath cover of darkness, and find a less dangerous place for Bingo to continue his journey. Speak to me when you are both ready, and we will leave Oserley by a goat-track or hidden foot-path. If we were spied upon as we descended from Wildermore, it would be best for us to slip the notice of any pursuers.'

'Please tell her that we will bring her safely to Grimslade. I know that she has gone through a lot, but we cannot leave her here among these dangers, and she in such a state!
'The men at Helm's Deep told me that Grimslade is still peaceful enough, for now. It is to the south-east, in the Westfold. Let us go there, and quickly! This woman should not stay too near this unhappy scene.'

'We have made it safely to Grimslade. I do hope that our friend will be able to make a new life for herself here.'
The woman smiles at you and Bingo sadly. The scars of lost Marton will always remain, but her expression shows a resolve to rebuild and recover from the experience.
'This was quite enough for one day,' Bingo continues. 'We have been invited to take our supper in the Grimslade Mead Hall, atop the hill. I will meet you inside, ${PLAYER}!'

'I do not know when it happened, ${PLAYER}, but somewhere between Marton and here, Mercy gave us the slip!
'I don't understand why she would not want to make a home for herself among the people here in Grimslade. She could have been perfectly happy here in Rohan, couldn't she? We did what we could, I suppose. I hope she will be all right out there in the wild.
'At any rate, we have been invited to rest our feet and take some supper at the Grimslade Mead Hall, atop the hill. I will meet you inside!'

'This has been a long day, ${PLAYER}. So much of my journey has been pleasant, full of sunny days and good company, but the sight of Marton burning has... well, it has left me quite upset, and I am not sure what to do next. It is not just me, either. Even Willem seems to be rather down in the dumps.
'I am worried about the Shire. Is it time to return home? Oh, I do not know what to do! Thoughts of home can be comforting, but these thoughts of the Shire have me turned around and upside-down, and now I say to you quite honestly that I do not know which way is up!'

'I am not hungry any more, ${PLAYER}. War has already come to the Westfold, and the good people who dwelt in this town have suffered so much!

'My home...' she says sadly.

'I found this woman among the ruins! She seems to be in shock, and I have been trying to cheer her up as much as I can. 'Egwylf has decided that she must leave us. It is a pity, but she does have a duty to her kingdom. I do not blame her for it!'

Even Bingo can read the disappointment in Willem's face.
'I am sorry, Willem! We found him caught in a trap in the Trollshaws, ${PLAYER}, do you remember? That is no place to raise a family! Rohan is embroiled in war, Moria is too dark, the mountains are too cold....'
Bingo trails away, and looks around at the marshes of the Dunbog.
'Do you know something, Willem? Your cubs look satisfied to live here, and it seems that they've already developed a taste for toad-meat. The temperature suits them and they know the nearby landmarks, and now that you're back, your family seems to want for very little. What if ${PLAYER} and I built a bit of a shelter for you, and gathered some food for your family? We could also defeat some of the more unpleasant foes that stalk the marsh!
'This might not have seemed the perfect home before, but compared to the other lands we've seen, I think we might be able to turn it into the perfect place for your family! What do you say to that?'
'I hope this wall does the trick!'

I have really enjoyed our travels together, and I wouldn't trade them for anything! I... I'll miss you, W.W.. You take care of yourself and your family too, you hear me?'
A loud rumbling sound fills the air.
'Are you purring, Willem? No, couldn't be. You are a rough and tough adventurer, a veteran of many campaigns! It must just be my stomach rumbling. I never did get enough meals to suit me on this journey, and today is no different! Well... well... so long, Willem. I will take my rumbling belly away now, so as not to wake the little ones. You are welcome in the Shire any time. Any time, Willem, I mean it!
'It is difficult to say good-bye, ${PLAYER}, but we had better leave now or we won't! Let us go north-east to the nearest village in the Starkmoor. I think it is called something like Avardin, but I do not know for certain.'

'I am glad we were able to help Willem and his family, ${PLAYER}. I will miss that fuzzy fellow, though. I think I will try to do some writing in my book in order to keep myself busy for now, if that is all right with you.'

'Now you have done it, ${PLAYER}.'

'And furthermore, you know I am a Treasure Seeker of some renown. Well, ever since you gave Haley the Rothstone, I have found nothing in the way of treasure at all! It is as if some secret force has cast a shroud over my sight, preventing me from finding even the least valuable trinket or bauble.
'Every ruin is picked clean. Every chest or strongbox is empty. There is no gold, there is no silver, there are no gems. The curse of the Rothstone has so damaged my fortunes that I cannot even hope to amass a fortune of any type!'
'I should have warned you about this.'

'You said you met Humfrey Rumming, and he sent you to find me and Haley? Did he tell you that he sold us a number of treasure maps? They cost me a pretty penny, I don't mind telling you, and so far every single one has come up empty! All my hopes rest on the only treasure map I have not yet tried, but those hopes have become as faint as a guttering candle in a drafty room!
'Bingo said that you were in Avardin earlier today, and yet Humfrey's riddle sent you right back here? That sounds like very bad luck as well, ${PLAYER}. I think you too may have become ensnared in the curse of the Rothstone!'
'I feel badly about this, ${PLAYER}.'

'We need to do something about the Rothstone, ${PLAYER}. This string of bad luck has become unbearable. We have had such a grievous journey south that I am ready to turn around and head back north! That is how terrible this adventure has become!
'Ask Haley! She will confirm everything I have said to you!'
'He is nearly finished. I have grown able to tell.'
'I suppose we solved the riddle, ${PLAYER}. But we were just here!'
'Solve my riddle, and you will find your friends! They are somewhere in Dunland, but that is the only hint you will get from me!'

'It has been a long time, ${PLAYER}! I am glad to see that you found Bingo! I knew he would turn up again.
'Our own journey has been fairly uneventful. I think Theodore may be less of a Treasure Seeker than when I took him on as a pupil, if you can believe it!
'He will want to tell you about our journey.'
'You have seen Haley and Theodore since we parted in the Lone-lands? Oh, that must have been while I was lost in Moria. That was such a long time ago, I had quite forgotten!'

'I have a complaint to lodge with you, ${PLAYER}! Do you remember that shiny necklace you tried to give me back in Eregion? Well, that was not a fake at all, as I thought it might have been at the time. No! It was a real artifact of the dwarves, and Haley has held onto it ever since we took your leave in Eregion.
'And ever since, ${PLAYER}, we have been beset with ill fortune! This southward journey has been a constant cavalcade of catastrophe! And it is all your fault! That shiny necklace, that Rothstone... it bears a curse of ill fortune!'
'Theodore will go on for awhile, if you let him.'

'How do I know? I will tell you how I know. The weather has been terrible! As we made our way south through Eregion, the skies opened up and the downpour was torrential! You have never seen rain like this, ${PLAYER}. It was cold as ice, and each droplet hit the skin like hail!
'Thunder rolled across the sky, booming and crashing, and the wind threatened to pick you up and toss you against trees or stones! We were in that land for several days before you gave Haley the Rothstone, and I did not see any weather like that before. But afterwards? It was nearly constant, except for a few days when it was sunny and nice. But those days were the exception!
'Further proof: we had to pick our way across a stream when we entered Enedwaith, and I hurt my ankle sliding down the river-bed. It has only recently started feeling better.'
'Hello there, ${PLAYER}! It has been a long time, hasn't it?'
'Well hello, ${PLAYER}! I did not expect to see you in this place!'

'It rained once or twice. I haven't noticed that our luck has been any poorer than it ever was, ${PLAYER}.
'But if Theodore wants to turn around and head back north, I would not be opposed to travelling with you and Bingo for a spell, if you would have us as companions on your way.'
'Our luck has turned sour! And it is all because of the Rothstone!'

'The more the merrier, that's what I always say! Theodore and Haley will be more than welcome to journey with us as we head northward. It is about time we started that way, I would say. The Shire is still a long ways off, and it will be nice to have some company on the road.'

'You would like to find this pair? Well, you are in luck, because I know where they were going! While we were conversing, they told me that you have quite a head for riddles. I find that hard to believe. A master lore-master such as myself cannot be bested at the riddle-game!
'I will write down their destination in riddle-form, and if you can solve it, you will find them there! Good luck, ${CLASS}. Confine your search to Dunland, and let us see if your good fortune holds!'

'Polla sent you to talk to me?
'I am glad to meet you, but as you can see, I am busy at the moment.'
Gord nods downward at the crowd of women gathered before him.
'Góthrik has quit, eh? It's just as well. You'll do fine in his stead. Now then, shouldn't you be off meeting the others?
'Sorry for the interruption, ladies.'

'Hallo there! I am Robbo Gristback, but you may call me Robbo.
'I'm a practised lutenist and one of the two founders of the Cloudyheads along with my dear friend, Polla.
'Am I to understand that Góthrik has abandoned his position in the band? A shame... I'd rather grown to like having so many dwarves around. They remind me of home, as strange as that might sound.
'In the meantime, I hope you consider Polla's offer. I'd be glad to have you around as we ready ourselves for our biggest show yet!'
Daenar watches as you approach, but gives no reply as you introduce yourself. She merely smiles, and returns to walking about the garden.

'Ah, hello, ${PLAYER}! Polla has been talking to me about you since you first arrived, and I haven't seen her this excited in some time. For my part, I am glad to finally have a word with you!
'Truth be told, we are all a tad anxious to perform. We came to the city just before the battle intensified, and now it seems we are trapped in here with the folk of Gondor. We only came to perform a show, and if it could be our last, I would prefer it to be our finest.
'Góthrik is a fine dwarf, and I am disappointed that our paths are no longer aligned. Perhaps the fate of Gondor weighs too heavily on him...
'We could all use a bit more joy in such times. If you would join us, perhaps it might lift the gloom hanging over the City.'

'What - what do you want?'
Góthrik is clearly enjoying his time at the Wheel and Cask, but you inform him of Polla's request to return.
'Ho ho! I do not think so, ${RACE}... I have had enough of their demands, and not nearly my fill of these fine draughts. This is war-time - there are barely enough people to mount even a meagre showing! I don't know what Polla is on about!
'If these are to be my final days, am I to spend them lugging around instruments and picking up after Gord and the others? Nay, I am finished with them. Tell her that I quit!
'You are welcome to take my place, but do not say I didn't warn you.'

'He quits?! He can't quit!
'This will not do at all, ${PLAYER}. We cannot manage our performances without a stagehand - it is simply not possible!
'What do you think of Góthrik's offer to join us? He seems to have painted us in a rather grim light, but I assure you, we are good folk!
'If you are uncertain, why don't you speak to the others first and introduce yourself?'

Hollur is playing a drum as you approach, but does not stop as you begin to introduce yourself. Instead, he simply talks over it as he introduces himself in turn.
'Ho there, ${PLAYER}! I did hear your name correctly, didn't I? It is nice to meet you, and even nicer for you to take up Góthrik's duties in his absence.
'Oh, you haven't accepted yet? Hah! I must be getting ahead of myself!
'Robbo and I are busy practicing a little tune of ours, so I'll get back to it now if you don't mind. If you haven't met Robbo, make certain you introduce yourself to him. He's a fine hobbit, he is.'

'I hope the others gave you a warm welcome, ${PLAYER}! Don't mind Daenar - she's a bit of an odd one, if I might say so.
'You seem like a fine ${RACE}. Robbo and I have come a long way from the Shire and met many friends along the way - I would be glad to count you among them.
'If you'd like to join the Cloudyheads, you need only say the word and we can get to work!'
You see a dwarf tucked away in the shadows of the tavern...

'Hallo, traveller!
'Are you an admirer of music? My band, the Cloudyheads, has travelled about from the Shire to Bree to the Trollshaws to Rohan and now to Gondor! We've come to Minas Tirith to perform in its grand theatres and we're almost ready!
'Yet... in a manner of speaking, we are a bit stuck at the moment.
'The Stone Theatre is a lovely place and one I'd much like to show my family back home, but the workers within are far too noisy! We tried to practice earlier and they made such a ruckus that we had to leave!
'They seem like fine, diligent Men, but what good is a theatre if it cannot be used by musicians?
'If you would convince them to shirk their duties, even for an hour or two, I would be most grateful!'

'Oh, thank you! Those workers were being much too noisy when we tried practicing in the theatre earlier.
'If we are to perform in the Stone Theatre soon, everything must be in order. Sweeping and hammering have no place in a hall of music!
'I know it was a simple task to ask of one as travelled as you, but we are in quite the pickle, you see. Our stagehand, Góthrik, has been... lacking in his duties as of late. He has spent more of each recent day huddled in local taverns than he has with the band.
'If you would search the taverns for him, starting in the Wheel and Cask nearby, please tell him his help is sorely needed!'

'Hah, ${PLAYER}, glad you're still with us!
'It seems to me that this theatre has an odd shape to it, and I am curious how our instruments might sound in such a lofty place. I asked Gord to help, but he is in something of a foul mood and I know better than to press him.
'You could aid me greatly if you would sit in several different seats throughout the theatre and tell me how clearly you can hear my playing.
'Hopefully my fears are unfounded, but I have a bad feeling about this one.'

'Hullo again, my friend!
'On my long walk to the Hall of Air, I had quite the thought! These instruments we have are old and more than a bit warped from our long journey to Gondor. Can you imagine how great we might sound with what the very best the craftsmen of Minas Tirith have to offer?
'Yes, yes, I know. The instrument does not make the player, but humour me!
'Please, ${PLAYER}. Here is some gold - take it down to the markets and see what you can find!'

'Ah, you made it, ${PLAYER}! This City is too big for its own good, if you ask me!
'I decided it was best to humour Gord's request and take a look at the Hall of Air. Between you and me, he's always been worried about his voice. I know the theatre won't make any difference, but if it helps him perform, I'll hold my tongue.
'This theatre is a bit smaller, but I think it will do. Why don't you talk to Hollur? He's always keen on testing the acoustics of a space before performing, so you might be able to aid him.'

'Thanks for all the help so far, ${PLAYER}. I know it's been a bit frustrating to be shuffled around like this, but I think our troubles are finally resolved! I spoke to Hollur and Gord about choosing another theatre, and I was able to arrange something very special for us after speaking to one of the local players.
'I won't spoil the surprise just yet, but we're going to perform in the best theatre in Minas Tirith.
'Care to guess which one?'

'It is as I thought then...
'This will not work for us either. We'll either have to travel back down to the Stone Theatre or perhaps there's another we still haven't tried. Don't you worry, I'll speak to Polla about it.
'In the meantime, I think Robbo wanted to talk to you about something.'

'Ah, these are just the thing, ${PLAYER}! If these don't help us sound great, I don't know what will! I'll make sure they end up in the proper hands.
'I saw Hollur talking to Polla while you were gone, and I think she'd like another word with you when you have the time.
'We are so close now, my friend!'

'What is this, ${PLAYER}? What have you to show me?'
You tell Mithrandir that Maenir has transcribed a lost scroll without understanding its language and hopes to learn more of its origin.
'A simple translation? Certainly, he should have all the resources he requires... and within the city at that!'

'Pardon my intrusion, ${CLASS}, but there is a matter I would like to discuss with you. It is one I would prefer to keep quiet, if it is possible.
'A few days ago, a warrior returned from the Pelennor with a peculiar scroll. He claimed to have wrest it from a fallen Haradrim sorcerer and sought to have it displayed among the many trophies of battle here in the Houses of Lore. We honoured his request, but so strange was the text that I endeavoured to transcribe and study it in my own time. I was able to transcribe it, but this very morning the scroll was taken from its resting place above. I hurried to cover the theft and stored my transcript in its place, but it will not be long before its loss is noticed by those with a more discerning eye.
'I would have it returned, and I care not to see the thief punished - my only concern is that of the scroll. I have little advice to offer other than to begin by searching the trophy collection - if nothing is there, return with my transcript and we can discuss a new course.'

The collection of enemy trophies can be found on the second floor of the Houses of Lore.

'It is as I expected. If the scroll was all they wanted, then what is their aim? There are many collectors of queer trinkets in Minas Tirith and the lands beyond, but with war come to our gates, I doubt many have worried themselves with obtaining new artifacts and curiosities.
'I transcribed the text as neatly as I might, though I do not understand the very words I wrote! I thought to take it to the Archives to translate... but I do not wish to leave our collections unattended until this is resolved.
'You are a friend of Mithrandir, are you not? He knows much of old and strange languages, and perhaps he might aid us. Take my transcript to him, and see what he makes of it!'

'Can you not see that I am busy? Ah, I am sorry, ${CLASS}. There have been many folk about the Archives today, and it is a great challenge to maintain order with so many things out of place.'
You tell the archivist of Maenir's concern.
'Ah, Maenir... he is a good fellow, if a bit overbearing. As I said, several people have passed through the Archives today. Some studying the line of Kings, and others the Great Plague...
'Allow me to think a moment...'

'Although part of me still yearns for the knowledge we may have lost, I am glad to see the Enemy's words turned to ashes.
'If our thief seeks to speak it, there is only one place he might learn of or study such a language - in the Old Archives! I know of an archivist, Gúldil, who is unfailing in his vigilance and dedication to maintaining our old texts. If you were to speak to him, he might be able to tell you of unfamiliar faces that have come to the Archives this day. It is the best chance we have to track down the scroll before the hour is too late!
'Go to the Archives with haste, ${PLAYER}... I fear what power the scroll might restrain if even Mithrandir would not speak of it.'

'Did you speak to Mithrandir? I am most curious what he had to say about the text!'
You inform Maenir that Mithrandir urges the transcript destroyed and that the words themselves can only aid the Enemy.
'Can such things be? Some foul sorcery bestowed upon a mere scroll... I am relieved that I did not attempt to speak it!
'I urge you to do as Mithrandir asked, my friend. Here, burn it in the fireplace beside me.'
Talk to Maenir
Talk to Gúldil in the Old Archives

'I have translated the words on this scroll, but I will not speak them!
'The language is old... older than most, and it tells of nameless things torn from their depths and bound to Sauron's will. I shall say no more of it... this is a tool of the Enemy and no good can come of speaking these words. If ever you have doubted my words or judgement, trust them now. I advise you to burn this at once before any ill fate can befall you or this Maenir you spoke of.
'You may tell him that it contains something of fell design, but do not speak more on it - even if pressed. I do not wish him to worry his fellows on the eve of war for such things can turn the tide of battle before it even begins.'

'I heard a great calamity in the back of the Archives! Have you dealt with the thief?'

'Nevertheless, I am glad this matter has been resolved, even at such a cost.'

'I am gladdened that you were able to destroy both the original and the transcript of the scroll, but the skill to summon a creature as foul as a rogmul by words alone is outside the power of most Men.
'It is likely that one of the Nazgûl had a hand in devising this plan, and judging by the chosen language, I believe it to be the High Sorcerer of Harad - a Man long succumbed to his Master's will. Unknowingly, the warrior who brought it to the city only worked to lay the foundation for the Enemy's ruinous plans. You did well to banish the rogmul, but I fear it is not the last we shall see of it.

'Do you have a moment, ${PLAYER}?
'Forgive me if I am too direct, but I have heard your name spoken among the people since your arrival in Minas Tirith and I hoped you might aid me with a personal matter.
'My son, Círgon, has not been himself. My husband has gone to war and Círgon will not say it, but I know it tears at him. He has spent much time alone over the past few weeks, and does not even speak to his friends. He spends every morning down at the Baths sailing the ships he and Círhir built together. That, or he wanders Egalmoth's Green and sits alone in the dark of the trees.
'Is this how a child should cope? It does not seem so to me, and I worry for him. We all feel the loss of our loved ones and he must understand that we are together in our sorrows.
'Please, go find him, and tell him to return to me. I have prepared supper and I cannot allow Círgon to sacrifice another meal to his sadness.'

'Mother sent you, didn't she?
'She doesn't need to worry about me, you know. I just come down here to think about father and my family... and how things used to be. I don't want to talk about that right now.
'Oh, I was just about to leave to sail my ships! Would you like to come along?'

'${PLAYER}, I am glad you have come.'
Ristagír beckons to you to lean in and begins to speak in a hushed tone.
'I have a confession to make, my friend. I was only able to apprehend Tastan with such haste because he was of our order - he was of the Withered Tree. Seeing what he'd done... I had much to consider. I was disgusted, not only with his actions, but also with my own for aligning myself with such folk. I shall not be a part of a group that preys on the helpless under the guise of some noble goal. A pox on the Withered Tree!
'I only hope my family will understand - for it is hard even for me to understand my actions. Until this war is ended, I shall stand by my loved ones. It is there that I am truly needed.
'Círgon is a good boy, and I see much of my brother in him. I shall help him rebuild his ship and perhaps I'll show him more of the art until Círhir's return.
'Thank you, ${PLAYER}. You shall ever be welcome among my family.'

'Hello, ${PLAYER}!
'I am glad to see you again, and I hope you had fun with my ships. I certainly did until, you know...
'I'm sad that cruel man broke my ship, but Uncle has promised that he'll help me build a new one. It's so nice of him to help - he doesn't even like boats!
'I want to spend some time with my family tonight. Is that all right? I do not mean to push you out of supper!
'Maybe you can join me at the Baths when my new ship is done!'

Before you even approach Círgon, you can tell that he is devastated. He is visibly shaking and tears are streaming down his face.
'I don't know what happened... I-I don't understand! I went to bring my cart over and... now it's ruined! Why, ${PLAYER}?
'I told Father I'd look after them...'
You attempt to calm Círgon and assure him that you will uncover who was behind such a vile act. As you do, you notice scattered puddles of water leading away from the Baths.
'What does it matter? I can't repair it on my own!'

'Don't involve yourself in this, stranger. I am having some words with this one, and I do not have time to deal with you as well.'
You inform the man that you come on behalf of Círgon, and seek the person who destroyed his model ship.
'Círgon? I am Ristagír... his uncle. I am sorry to meet you under such circumstances, but I could not allow this man to flee after seeing what he had done. This wretch had it in his head to break a child's toy as some form of protest against the Steward. This is not a way for any to behave - no matter how aggrieved!
'Tastan here will be collected by the guards shortly, and then I shall bring Círgon back to his mother's house. I would be grateful if you would meet me there.'

'I cannot thank you enough for your help, ${PLAYER}.
'It breaks my heart to know what happened to poor Círgon's ship, but Ristagír has vowed to help him build a new model in time for Círhir's return. Ristagír is a good man, and I know Círgon will be glad to have him around more often.
'I do not know when my husband will return, but I hope it is soon.
'You are always welcome among us, ${PLAYER}. Let us hope brighter days are ahead.'

'As you are aware, battle is surely upon us. There will be casualties and there will be injuries. The casualties will be unavoidable. If we are to act fast and have the proper healing salves, we should be able to abate the injuries. I have been insisting that we stock up on herbs with healing properties but I do not know anyone who is willing to leave the safety of this city on the eve of battle. If you collect these plants, then I and many soldiers to come will be in your debt.'
Galathir shows you a book containing labeled drawing of several plants of the region with healing properties:
Tunglewort, a weed that grows in Osgiliath near the Anduin. Maiden's Helm, a flower only found in the northern woods of Lossarnach. Wanderbeard, a type of moss-flower growing at the base of the mountains in Pelennor. Settlegang, a green flower-less plant found in Talath Anor.
'Nicely done, ${PLAYER}.'
'You have done well. The other herbalists will take over from here and make potent salves. Thank you again for aiding the Houses of Healing.'

'We finished! I shall complain about my day to my brother the next time I see him. I apologize for taking my frustration out on you. These are difficult times and I feel like I'm often ignored by both my family and superiors.'

'I do not understand your jovial attitude, brother. How can you be happy in time of war!? Is it that hobbit friend? You spend so much time with that Halfling, it's like your own brother does not even exist! Bergil, your son, needs your guidance on the eve of battle. You may not see him tomorrow!'

‘${PLAYER}, I must confess, there is a shortage of staffing in all the buildings of the Citadel. Only the guard posts are fully stationed on the eve of war. Still we have nobles staying at the Southern Great Guest-house and eating at the feast-hall, Merethrond. I need some of my guards to leave their post and take on additional duties up here. Would you mind delivering these orders in my stead?
'Speak with Iorlas and send him to the Southern Great Guest-house to tidy up the baths. Also, speak with Beregond and send him to Merethrond to tidy up the tables. We must all do our part to keep this city running.'

'Beregond, I did not realize the weight you have been carrying. You know that you can always share that burden with your brother. I would treat Bergil as a son if the worst came to pass. Do not worry for your son; be with him instead. On the battlefield, I shall protect the both of you until the bitter end.
'I do not want to stop your friendship with the Halfling. He brings you joy and hope. That is something we all need.'

'Thank you, Iorlas. It is good to hear these words coming from you. I will spend more time with my family. Hopefully, Peregrin will be able to join us. I am sure we will all enjoy the hobbit's company.
'Now, ${PLAYER}, there is something that I must ask of you. I believe you came here to investigate our argument, most likely on Ormatar's orders. If you would be kindly to us, keep our quarrel a secret whilst we return to our posts. We would rather not get in trouble for this little family dispute.'

You explain to Ormatar that the noise was just some nobles who were staying at the Southern Great Guest-house. They were having a heated discussion but you calmed them down.

A Wager: In the Wind

The two soldiers listen to your account.
'Clearly, I have won. We said that if it fell, the wager was mine, did we not?'
Gradir pauses, shakes his head, and sighs.
'Bah! The gulls can take the rules. You swore there was an updraft, old friend, and it is plain to see that there was. Here, the wager is yours.
'Well, ${PLAYER}, it's a good thing you did not jump off yourself... though that would likely have won me the bet! Still, I thank you all the same.'

'Ah, what have we here? A ${CLASS}, is it? Perhaps you can help us settle this matter!
'You see, my friend and I cannot come to an agreement. We have argued back and forth and then forth and back, and I will confess that in a heated moment, Tawaris here has even wagered good Gondorian gold if he should be proven wrong.
'Come now, you'll hear us out, won't you?'

'What a load of fish-guts! First off, the winds clearly run along the pier down from the tower and fall to the land below. Winds going up. Ha! Doesn't rain fall? Has anyone ever seen rain fly up the pier?
'No, my friends. The winds go down, not up. So say I - and you say otherwise. How shall we settle this? There's gold in your pockets, Tawaris, that should really be in mine.
'What do you say to this? Our ${CLASS} friend here carries a chicken up to the pier's end and tosses it off. If it comes back, you've won. Down it goes? I've won!'
Tawaris nods in agreement and the two look at you expectantly.
'I'll save you the chore of carrying a hen straight from the First Circle. There are some hens in the Court of Eärnil, up in the Third Circle. Go for one of those.'

'Do you see the pier up there, or the Ship's Prow, as some call it? Well, a man told me that the winds race up its face so fiercely, you couldn't walk off of it if you tried. You'd be shoved back!
'It stands to reason, does it not?'
The chicken appears somewhat wind-blown and disgruntled, but otherwise unhurt
You drop the chicken and it sails downward, squawking loudly, but it is slowed by an unmistakable updraft!

'This will do the trick, ${PLAYER}! Now mind you, the ashes here are not quite what they are in Ethir, never mind the difference in the ale dregs, but it will have to do. Yes, it will have to do!
'There, now it's made. Go on, have a taste!'

'Well! The ${CLASS} can drink some rotgut and stay standing, perhaps. But one step and down you'll go.
'Let us put you to the test. Walk over to that left archer, tap him on the shoulder, and tell him he's aiming well. Then, over on my right, walk between the last two ranks of men there. And last... last... why, climb up upon that barrel there and give us a wave!
'Do all that, and I'll confess you can hold your rotgut after all.'

'Well, ${PLAYER}, you are a good sort! I would share a drink with you, if I had aught worth drinking.
'But alas! Tawaris here drank the last of our rotgut.'

'Ha ha! The ${CLASS} has done it, Tawaris, and this time the wager is mine. I'll have my gold back, thank you.
'You are welcome back for a drink with us any time, ${PLAYER}. And do not worry, the rotgut will wear off soon and the headache that follows will be fleeting, though quite strong!'

'Tawaris, you do grievous wrong to our ${CLASS} friend, a seasoned adventurer who could clearly stomach rotgut, even if most could not.
'Why, I dare say we are in disagreement once again. Let us wager on it, and perhaps I can win my gold back.
'${PLAYER}, find me what I need and I will make you some rotgut. If luck would have it, you can find all the ingredients on this very tier so I expect your trip to be swift.
'First, I'll need dregs from ale, which you might find at the Splintered Shield. Then I need hot ash from a brazier and some Healer's Caustic, which is a powerful and pungent tincture used for closing wounds.'

'Do not listen to this scoundrel. First of all, it was he who drank the last of it.
'But never mind that. Rotgut is not for the likes of you. Why, I have never met anyone but us fisherfolk of Ethir who could stomach it!'

Talk to Theodore Gorse in Avardin, in Dunland
'If you search a few of the likely spots around Galtrev, we may find some clue to Theodore's whereabouts. Knowing him, he has probably gone off in whatever direction will cause us the most trouble!'
'I do not know why he has taken the Rothstone, but I do know that he blames it for the misfortune he thinks has befallen us. Where has he gone with it?'

'Do you mind asking Theodore if he thinks this is a good route for us to take? He and Haley passed through there on their way south. I would ask him myself, but he seems to be quite occupied with his own thoughts at the moment!'
'It makes no difference to me where we begin... ill fortune will follow us wherever we go unless we do something about it!'
'This is unfortunate! Where can he have gone?'
'I wonder where Theodore has gone. Have you seen him?'
'So you found the Treasure Seekers? Well done, well done. Next time I shall make certain the riddle is more difficult to untangle!'
'I hope you are having a fine adventure. I know that I am, but I am a master of lore, after all. Adventure finds me wherever I go!'
'Your adventure continues, I expect?'
'How goes the adventure?'

'This is terrible, ${PLAYER}! Theodore thinks this treasure has caused him ill fortune, and he has gone to the lair of a dragon in order to be rid of it? He is going to find no end of ill fortune there, and he will be the cause of it!'
Bingo shakes with nervousness, and you are reminded of how he quaked with fear on the slopes above Helegrod, when Spalvi said that a dragon had once lived there. Now, many months later and many hundreds of miles further on, Bingo closes his eyes and clenches his fists. When he opens his eyes again a moment later, his jaw is set and his shaking has stopped.
'We have to stop him, ${PLAYER}. I am not going to let some dragon put an end to Theodore's story, no matter how much he might deserve it for walking right into its waiting jaws! I will talk some hobbit-sense into him! Let me know when you are ready, and we will go to the dragon's lair together!'

'Your friend Theodore purchased a number of treasure maps from me some days ago, and I understand that he made use of every one to no avail: there was no treasure at any location he searched... quite a pity for a Treasure Seeker! Mere hours ago he asked me about the last of the maps, and I assured him that there should be quite a collection of treasure there, given the nature of that spot. Well, he got a funny sort of look in his eye and said, \qWhat's one more treasure added to the pile?\q I see now that he had designs on returning a treasure rather than obtaining one.
'You want to know to where the last treasure map points? Did I not say? It guides adventurers to the lair of a dragon in Thrór's Coomb.'

'Now that you mention it, I have not seen Theodore for a while now. I know he was with us when we arrived at Galtrev, but now he seems to have gotten himself lost. That is so typical, ${PLAYER}!
'Perhaps we should look for him. If you search a few of the likely spots around Galtrev, we may find some clue to his whereabouts. Knowing Theodore, he has probably gone off in whatever direction will cause us the most trouble!'

'Have you seen Theodore lately? I must say that I haven't seen him since we arrived in Galtrev, but I am not sure exactly when I saw him last.
'Perhaps Haley knows where he has gone?'

'${PLAYER}! Something had been troubling me, but I had not been able to put the worry into words. While you were looking for Theodore, I finally realized what it was. I looked through my possessions for the Rothstone, the golden necklace you put into my keeping in Eregion, but I cannot find it anywhere!
'Theodore has taken it! I do not know for what purpose he has stolen the Rothstone, but I do know that he blames it for the misfortune he thinks has befallen us. Where has he gone with it?'
'Where can he have gone?'
'I have had no luck finding Theodore either!'

'This is a little embarrassing, ${PLAYER}. I would have said something before, but I was very busy with my own affairs and you did not ask, so I figured all was done with your knowledge and approval. I am sorry to learn that was not the case.
'You see, your friend Theodore purchased a number of treasure maps from me some days ago, and I understand that he made use of all but one of them to no avail: there was no treasure at any location he searched... quite a pity for a Treasure Seeker! Mere hours ago he asked me about the last of the maps, and I assured him that there should be quite a collection of treasure there, given the nature of that spot. Well, he got a funny sort of look in his eye and said, \qWhat's one more treasure added to the pile?\q I see now that he had designs on returning a treasure rather than obtaining one.
'You want to know to where the last treasure map points? Did I not say? It guides adventurers to the lair of a dragon in Thrór's Coomb.'
'I am very pleased that Theodore was not eaten by that dragon!'

'What a day this has been! I will need to spend some time coming up with the perfect way to describe that dragon. He was very impressive. I am glad I was able to see him, but I am even more glad that I was able to leave his lair without singeing the hair on my toes!
'I much preferred my encounter with the Green Dragon of Bywater to the Black Dragon of Thrór's Coomb, ${PLAYER}. Let us have no more dragons on this journey!'

'What am I going to do with you, Theodore?'
'Another successful adventure!'
'Oh, Theodore! You foolish fool of a man!'

'Let us go find our friend! No dragon will stand in our way!'
<rgb=#FF0000>This is a Solo quest and cannot be completed with a Fellowship.</rgb>

'I am sorry to have caused you such trouble, ${PLAYER}, but I am glad to be rid of the Rothstone all the same!
'In fact, it seems to me that our fortunes are already beginning to turn around. After all, I could have been devoured by that dragon, or roasted to a crisp... and neither of those things happened! Perhaps I should not be a Treasure Seeker after all. I think I might be more of a Daring Dragon Dancer, what do you think?
'Ha! I am only teasing, ${PLAYER}. Tell Haley not to look so cross with me!'
'Oh, that foolish man. What will we do with you, Theodore? This worrying will send me into an early grave!'
'All is well after all! What a relief that is, ${PLAYER}!'

'Thank you for rescuing Theodore from himself, ${PLAYER}. I am very grateful to have met you and Bingo, and Theodore should be grateful for it as well; I do not think I would have had the patience to drag this purple-garbed fool from too many more dangers of his own making.
'Let us hope the rest of our northward journey is quieter and less eventful!'
'What an adventure! I have no regrets, ${PLAYER}, and although Haley is grumbling I am quite certain she has none either!'

'Hold, stranger!'
'Well, who are ye? Strangers?'
'Do you think there may be some other hobbits in the Gloomglens? I do believe we should investigate and see for ourselves!'

'I hope ye will excuse our Rhus. He seems naught but a bumpkin, but still he is dear to us, despite himself! He is a good enough fellow, if a little afeared of outsiders. He may call ye Duvodiad, but I can see ye're more than that! The Maer will be able to tell for sure.'
'How lovely it is to meet hobbits from a new branch of the family tree, no matter how distant!'

'I extend ye the greetings of Maur Tulhau, ${PLAYER}. The folk of my village are most interested to hear what ye have to say of Bingo Boffin's journey. He could be one of us if he changed out of his strange garments and wore something more fit for the kinfolk of Maur Tulhau!
'We have proper traditions for the greeting of family gone long away and freshly returned. I think it would be suitable to greet Bingo with the traditional Welcoming Feast of the Stoors. It is no small thing, and we do not have the ingredients ready. If ye can acquire what we will need, we can set out the feast much more quickly!
'Speak to many of the villagers for some of the supplies, and search for others in the woods outside the village. There is much to be found before we can begin, and many dangers that ye might handle so we may dine in peace!'
'Ye should speak to the Maer in the back of the village!'

'There is to be a Welcoming Feast? What delightful news! We have had so few of them lately, and I tell ye that nothing brings the village together like a Welcoming Feast!
'Here, I will give ye some of my famous sprouted herbs for use in preparing the meal. They will add just the right kind of flavour as my folk enjoys, and I am sure Bingo will find it suitable as well!'

'A Welcoming Feast? I have just the thing to make it the finest such meal we have had in Maur Tulhau for some time: taters... giant ones!
'Take these fine specimens with ye, and they will be hearty enough to serve for many courses! A Welcoming Feast! I can hardly believe it!'

'I know why ye have come, ${PLAYER}.'

'Take it with my well wishes, and know that from this point forward, Bingo will measure every meal against this one... thanks to this gravy!'

'Is this a trick? Bingo wishes to invite us to a dinner party? We have all been neighbours for some time now, and we have never attended a party at his home before! Now that I think about it, I suppose none of us have ever invited him over for tea or for dinner either.
'Do we think we will attend? I... I suppose we can try, but we are not promising anything! Good day!'

'Cousin Bingo is inviting my family to a dinner party? It has been ages since I visited his home, and that was many young hobbits ago! Is his home big enough to accommodate all of my children?
'We will certainly try to attend, ${PLAYER}. It is just as well, for I think Marigold was planning a secret adventure to the Shire anyway, and perhaps this will satisfy her journeying heart somewhat... for the moment!
'I could do with a fine dinner. Taking care of all these children is hungry work!'

'Pull up a chair, ${PLAYER}! There is room for all at the Prancing Pony!'
You hand Milo the invitation and he reads it with interest.
'Delightful! I am not one to turn down a free dinner, and I remember that Bingo was quite an amusing fellow. I hope he shows a little restraint this time, because I remember he spent some time recovering from the entertainment here among the haystacks by the stables!
'I will be happy to attend, even if folk in the Shire are a little odd... compared to the hobbits of Bree, at least!'

'We are back where we started, ${PLAYER}, and still trying to decide what we should do next. For now, we have mostly decided that the food here could be better and that Anlaf does not clean the mugs well enough.'
You hand the invitations to Haley and she reads it with a smile.
'A dinner party? We will certainly attend, won't we, Theodore? Yes, we will. It will be nice to see Bingo at his home.'
Theodore nods distantly, already thinking about his next adventure, but you are reasonably certain he will attend Bingo's gathering.

'Oh, hullo there, ${PLAYER}! Welcome back to Rivendell!'
You hand Bilbo the invitation, and he reads it carefully.
'Bingo Boffin is having a dinner party? I am sure it will be a lovely time, but I am afraid I must decline his gracious invitation. I do not think I have as many journeys in me as once I did, and I am content to stay here in Rivendell for now. I will return to the Shire one day, I am sure of it, but I am not ready to say farewell to the Last Homely House just yet.
'Give Bingo my best wishes, and tell him that I am eagerly awaiting his book... when it is finished!'

'Welcome back to Khazad-dûm, ${PLAYER}! Do not tell me you have lost Bingo again, and need my help to find him?'
Spalvi laughs for a longer time than necessary. When he has finally stopped and apologized, you hand him the invitation. Ketill Map-maker, standing nearby, also takes an interest.
'I would be happy to attend Bingo's party! Ketill and I have been working to improve the Iron Garrison's foothold here in Khazad-dûm, but it is difficult work. There are many dangers still in the earth, and I am not sure we can master them. But we will try! That is the way of the dwarves!'
Hand-written, Hand-delivered
Bingo is inside his hobbit-hole in Michel Delving, north of the Town Hole.

'If you would, go down among our soldiers in the Second Circle. Listen there to the sound of their training. Find for me a cold knife and a sweaty rag.
'Then go out into the fields - as you are fit for such deeds - and explore our ruined farmsteads. Find for me some charred wood and trampled wheat. Then go in among our foes and hear the death-rattles of their dying soldiers. Observe for me the fell gleam in the eyes of one of their captains as he fights and falls.
'Hm... yes. When you have done what I ask, return to me and I shall make a poem fit for war.'

Dúrbethir takes the items you have brought him and listens with a grave expression to the impressions you gathered.
'Perhaps I asked too much of you - but yet, it is no more than we ask of every soldier here. Nevertheless, you have brought me ample inspiration. Let me ponder a moment....
'Dark the day and bright the fire The fires in the trenches' veins Veins go cold and life expires Expiring joy and dread and pain Dark the day and blood shall flow Dark the day and still we go
'Blood shall flow and fear shall clamour Clamour like the soldiers' cries Cries of fury, hope, and valour Valour chance and death defies Dark the day and still we go Dark the day and blood shall flow
'There, it is done. I have wrought a song for war. Perhaps we will take these words to our graves. If that is so, take my thanks as well.'
'What, did you think I would write lines about sweaty rags and bent wheat? You know little of a poet's work, ${RACE}.'

'Never have I been a poet of war. If we found glory in naught more than gleaming armour and feats of battle, then the Enemy has won his first victory against us.
'And so I wrought poetry of the grandeur of works or stone, of the beauty of blossom and branch, of the love of young men and maidens, fair and proud. When I put history to verse, it was of our works and journeys and failings.
'But today - today is a day of war! It is close upon us as the breath in our lungs, and I would write a song of it. As you came upon me here, I was brooding on how to begin. I think I must fill my senses with things dark, dread, and bloody. Will you help me in this?'

'The formalities of introductions can be dealt with later. If Lamlor sends you, then you are surely a skilled ${CLASS}.
'Some of the Enemy has diverted from those who push towards Minas Tirith and have traversed north into Far Anórien. I was planning on scouting along the Onodló River for signs of the Rohirrim, but another matter has arisen. There are drumming sounds I keep hearing. They grow increasingly louder and seem to be coming from an area in Taur Drúadan, north of the Grey Wood. Would you be willing to investigate the sound, and make sure that it is not an ambush?'
The chieftain does not seem surprised by your presence. Instead, it looks as if Ghân-buri-Ghân has much on his mind. He sighs and gathers his thoughts.

'Many have faith that the Rohirrim will arrive to aid us. I fear that folly may have befallen the riders. Perhaps all is not lost though. I have been told that you have spent much time out in the Pelennor, safely navigating through the thick of the Enemy. Would you be willing to ride north of Minas Tirith into Far Anórien and search for the riders?
'You should speak with Bregdal in Crithost. He is a trustworthy ally, and Errand-rider of Minas Tirith. I sent him to Crithost on a special mission to seek information on the whereabouts of the riders. His knowledge of safe travel through Far Anórien is unmatched. Ride swiftly my friend, as time is short!'

A Perilous Parley
'If you would be of aid to Ost Rimmon, then go with Gondrad to meet this ransomer and see he that he returns to me here in one piece.'

'If you ask me, this fellow would cut your head off quicker than ask your name. Would and could!
'Well, let's see what he's got to say.'

'Why look here, I still have my head on my shoulders! We didn't pull much wool over his eyes, did we, though?
'Still, we must count ourselves lucky. Now let us get going rather than test our luck any further!'

'Ah, there you are. Gondrad, you craven rascal, listen to me.
'I have received grim tidings that my sons and perhaps your Lord never reached Minas Tirith, but were waylaid by some enemy captain or highwayman on the way. As you should rightfully have been with them, I am sending you to treat with the ransomer.
'${CLASS}, I ask this of you: go with Gondrad and keep him safe. He has much to answer for, but I deem a foolish death to be insufficient punishment and a general waste of penance. I have no one more capable of keeping him safe, I am afraid, and must rely on you.'

'Ah - you've found me! Wait a moment, who are you?
'No matter. You have clearly come from beyond these walls and this bodes doubly ill for me. First, because if you came from out there, then Lady Glánhar will deem it safe enough to send me out there. And second, because she has surely sent you here to summon me for just that cause. Unless she merely wishes to whip me with another thirty lashes of her tongue! Oh, I deserve the lashings well enough. But even a guilty hound will hide his snout from his mistress' wrath.
'Well, there is no escaping it! Let us go and hear my Lady's command.'

'I can make neither head nor tail of what this tatter-tongued shepherd is trying to say. There is a bad man it seems, and a message, and I can get no more. I wonder, is he speaking in the tongue of sheep or of men?
'Bah! Why don't you try and see if you can get anything out of him.'

'A m-m-message the bad man b-b-bade me bear to Lady Glánhar. Only every time I think of- of- of what I've got to say to her, my heart quails and my tongue stumbles and right full tumbles over itself.'
He takes a breath and continues.
'I was standing in the shade of a tree talking to one of my sheep, when I looked up and there they were, all about me, fearsome swords in hand. And then the bad man fixed me with his eye and spoke.
'He holds the lives of three sons of this place in his hand, he said, and for a sum of gold he might let them slip through his fingers. He bade the keeper of this place - Lady Glánhar he must have meant - to meet him upon the eastern slope of Calenhad, above the river.
'I beg you, ${RACE}, to say it to the Lady here for I cannot!'

Glánhar's shrewd eyes go wide.
'What? My four sons and husband went to war after the last beacon. Unless - but he holds only three sons? What can it then mean...?'
Her face grows very sober.
'I see. If this ransomer said not my name but only 'The Keeper of Ost Rimmon', then I shall play the prudent course and send another in my stead.
'Now, where is that blasted fool Gondrad? Hoping to weather my wrath, it seems. Will you find the rascal for me? He is skulking somewhere in Ost Rimmon, I am sure.'

'Am I to believe that one of you is the keeper of Ost Rimmon? You are what, a fool of a stable hand and a hired guard? You must think Jarl Akhiz dull indeed!'
Akhiz lets out a savage chuckle.
'You drew the short straw, did you not, stable hand? Ha ha! But this guard looks to be of some mettle.
'Well, no matter. I hold two sons of the Lord of Ost Rimmon. In exchange for their lives, I demand two things: their worth in gold and, because I think you, ${CLASS}, can win it for me, a brooch that was stolen from me by a rival Jarl of the Variags. You will find his camp to the north-west, near the Firien Wood. He'll have it in some chest or another there, I am sure.
'When you have these things, you will bring them to me in the cellar in Bâr Nadhron. Now go, else I raise my price again.'

Lady Glánhar listens to your account of the meeting.
'So it is a cunning wolf we are dealing with, then. Hm! Gondrad, I am not done with you, don't go creeping off. I must think a moment. What does this man stand to lose? To gain? What does he know that he has not said?'
She falls silent with a frown.

'Go on. See if you can get anything out of the tatter-tongued wretch.'
'You - you must tell her the message - that the bad man bade her to meet on the eastern slope of Calenhad, above the river, and that he holds the lives of her sons in his hands.'
'Once you have found that good-for-naught Gondrad, return to me and we will devise a plan.'
'You told her? You are braver than I, ${RACE} - or you do not fear the Lady's ire as I do!'
'There you are. Mark my words - this will not go well for me!'
'You give the report. The less I speak, the less new trouble I can get myself into!'
'There is nothing for it. We must go see what Lady Glánhar wants. No good will come of it for you - or especially for me!'

'Do you see? It is just as I said.
'I would rejoice that my Lady does not wish to see me dead, but I know well enough that longer life means more time to punish me for my failings!'

'You will bring the gold and the brooch to me in the cellar in Bâr Nadhron, and in exchange I shall release the two brothers.
'What? The fool shepherd said three? The count has changed. Go now, or I shall grow angry.\q

The Ransomer's Rival
'Why, there it is. And you don't look terribly bruised or bloodied, for all that. Things are going well for us so far, aren't they? It's how I know our luck must be about to turn.'
'You must go with Gondrad and see the ransom paid. Tarry not. I have much work to do, and would dwell on what may become of my sons no more than I must.'
'Another chance to lose my head. What a fine day this is turning out to be!'

'This cunning wolf has named his price and I fear it must be paid. I ask the two of you to take this gold and to fetch the stolen trinket, and see if you can indeed buy back my sons from these men.
'It did not escape me that he first offered three sons for ransom and now counts but two. Yet I will not dwell on it. There is no time for grief or fruitless worry, now. We must act.
'But I beseech you both - show caution! You are treating with scoundrels and must be cunning yourselves - and cautious, beside. I would give much to see my sons alive before me, but your lives are not among the things that I would give.
'Now go.'
'That is the camp there, just as he told us it would be. You go on and steal back his brooch. I will remain here, doing my best to keep my head attached to my shoulders.'
'Those look very much like the men who assailed us before the meeting, do they not? I wonder if they will like you rifling through their things.'

A Look Before the Leap

You recount all that you saw to Gondrad and his face slowly twists into a frown.
'I see two reasons to be perfectly miserable, ${PLAYER}. First and foremost is that these men are truly as numerous, ruthless, and fell as we had feared. And secondly - you found no better reason to turn back and go home without completing the deal.'
'There is no way out of this, I am afraid. We must march right up to the camp and deliver the ransom... and if we are lucky, walk out with our hides!'
'We have both parts of the ransom now, so I suppose we must press on. To Bâr Nadhron, ${PLAYER}, though I have an ill feeling about this!'

'Look at that! This Jarl could certainly take Ost Rimmon. I wonder if he knows it?
'Now, I have been pondering what Lady Glánhar said about caution. Call me coward and cuff me on the ear, but I would scout around the edges of the camp and see what may be seen, if I were you.

A Recounting of the Sons

'Gondrad, know that Narvagol is dead. Father lies dead by his side. Your luck was not ill but a supreme blessing, for we were taken before even the sun had reached noon that day, and you, a commoner unworthy of ransom, would not have been spared.
'They wished to ransom all of us, of course, but Father and Narvagol sought glory instead and won it. We might have too, but the curs threw nets over us and saw us disarmed before we could cause any trouble. Then you came to our rescue, and here we are.
'All, that is, except for my brother Malhar.'
'He does not know. You must tell him, brother.'

'Well, we have made it out somehow, haven't we? Not... all of us.'
He grimaces and looks about him.
'Gondrad! Where in all Gondor had you got off to, and how is it you are here?'
'So we are to meet beneath a bent tree near the Mouths of the Entwash? Let us go and not linger here one worrisome moment longer!'
'Beneath a tree east of Bâr Nadhron, by the wetland's edge, is where we are to meet. Let us go - and with haste!'
'We may be safe now, but I'm well acquainted with trouble and I believe we're in for more of it!'

'Ah, friend! The prank your brother Narvagol played upon me has born ill fruit, indeed.
'In revenge for failing to polish his armour, he hid my belongings far and wide about Ost Rimmon. You could not find me, for I was scouring the cellar, and then you left so Lady Glánhar has showered abuse without respite upon me ever since!'
'How glad I am to see old Gondrad. How glad I shall be to be home again!'
'I still say we should have fought those dishonourable dogs. Perhaps in Ost Rimmon we can muster a fighting force and come back for them!'

'My brother Malhar slipped his bonds and escaped the Variags. I know not how, only that if anyone might have done so and survived, it was he. Our youngest brother is possessed of the quickest wits in a quick-witted family.
'We had agreed, while they dragged us to Bâr Nadhron, that if any of us escaped we would make for the Mouths of Entwash. I doubt not that he went there and is likely there still.
'We must return to Ost Rimmon, but I beg you, ${CLASS}, go into the marshland and find Malhar. I have every hope he yet lives and, if luck is on our side, has left some trail to find him by.'

'Who are you? You do not look to be a foe, so I judge you friend. I am Malhar, son of Lachnir.'
The young man starts to extend a hand, then winces and holds his side. He gives a wry, pained grin.
'Though if you were foe, I fear I should be somewhat at your mercy. I am starved and wounded and very ready indeed to get back out of this marsh!'
'We must return to Ost Rimmon but I beg of you, head into the Mouths of Entwash and search for Malhar. He may still be alive.'
'In truth, I would go with you, ${PLAYER}, but I see from my brother's stern look that it is not to be.'
'Narvagol, dead? That is a blow. And now the fact that I never polished his armour will haunt me to the end of my days!'

'There. I think I am ready to begin hobbling my way home. And see, ${PLAYER}, I need not live to old age. I am already acquainted with aches and infirmity!
'Luckily, I know these wetlands well and can find the path with ease. That is why we agreed to meet here, my brothers and I. When I need to rest we will stop. How is that?'

'Water,' Malhar croaks. 'I am parched. It is sapping my strength.'
He proffers you an empty water-skin.

'Now I must gather my wits and decide which way to go. We have come far enough that there may be enemies near. I must also think on what paths will let us make our way without being seen.'
Malhar furrows his brow and thinks for a moment.
'No, I cannot decide this just by brooding here. I must ask you scout ahead and bring word of what you see. This area stretches south and west of here. Canvas its breadth and return to me.'

'There it is, ${PLAYER}. My home soil. I cannot say how this view warms my heart. We have done it. We are out of the marsh and the going will be easy. Let us meet back at Ost Rimmon.'

'I have much to thank you for, ${PLAYER}, although I have much to grieve for, it appears. It is a sorrowful day, indeed!
'I had understood, as all Gondor marches to war, that men of my blood might be taken from me. I never imagined, though, that cruel fate would take them so near to my door or that your kind hands would free some of them from its grip.
'But enough of such goings-on! As I began - you have my earnest thanks. You shall ever be known as friend here in the Beacon Hills, so long as I am keeper of it.'
'Good? Then off we go. See if you can keep up, ${CLASS}! Ha ha!'
'So I was right! I am glad you could handle them, friend. We are nearly out. Let us keep up our pace.'
'Water,' rasps Malhar. 'Please.'
'Scout the area south and west of here. Then return to me and tell of what you have seen.'
'I have regained much strength and can find my way. Meet me in Ost Rimmon, so my mother can give you a full and proper thanks.'
'There you are, friend. See the family you have brought back together!'
'I could not say if Mother wished to slap my face or embrace me. I dare say she could manage to do both at once!'
'You found Malhar and you brought him home. No words of thanks could do justice to my gratitude for that.'
'I am but half-forgiven, it seems. But with her sons returned, she has other ears to cuff than mine in her daily rounds. And that, I well believe, is the best I could hope for!'

Malhar takes the water-skin in both hands and drinks greedily.
'There, that is better. How is it, ${PLAYER}, of all the things I asked you to fetch for me before setting off, water was not one?
'Well, we have set that right. Now let us be on our way.'
'I would swear that I heard something. Please look ahead and see if I'm correct. Use caution!'
