'You have my thanks, ${PLAYER}, and so does Bósi. Indeed, all who stood against the traitor Dómor and the terrible creature that enslaved him have the thanks of the King under the Mountain!
'It is clear to me now that the tale Dómor wove in Mordor was a lie. The ruby over which Eirek and Mogi quarreled was an invention of the traitor; the helm was the true treasure they found, and when he placed it upon his head he came under the dominion of Lachagar.
'Eirek and Mogi deserve better treatment than they received at Dómor's treacherous hands. Return to Mordor and find their final resting place. Search first at the location Dómor went after you encountered him; I believe he offered to check that spot to prevent you from seeing it yourself.'

'This is the location where Eirek and Mogi were slain, ${PLAYER}. We cannot bring them out of Mordor now, but this grave is too shallow to serve. They will be burned dwarves, as is sometimes done when no tombs can be made. Let the smoke of the burning serve as a warning to traitors.
'Return to King Thorin and tell him what is being done for them. He will wish to know.'

'You found the bodies of Eirek and Mogi? Dómor paid for his treachery, but I am still displeased that he proved corruptible. We pride ourselves on our resilience, but there are such evils in the Land of Mordor that even dwarves are not safe from their foul touch.
'I thank you for your efforts on behalf of Durin's Folk, ${PLAYER}. May your adventures continue, and bring you glory and treasure alike.'

'Remain alert for members of the Withered Tree. They have continued to speak against my rule, and while there has been no outright violence since the slaying of Mauthoi, still I fear it may come.'

'In shape and form this sapling is unmistakable, ${PLAYER}! This can be nothing other than young growth of the White Tree, but that has been dead for hundreds of years and this sapling can be no more than seven years old!
'How can this wonder be possible?'

'I see in this sapling much that identifies it as descended from the royal line of Telperion, Eldest of Trees, from which came through several generations the White Tree that grew in the Court of the Fountain. But that tree withered and died, and was left atop the city.
'But it seems now that a fruit was taken from it before it died, and was brought to this high hallow by unknown hands. It was left here on the mountainside, and the life within it lay sleeping. It remained here hidden for hundreds of years, much as the line of kings stayed hidden in the North.
'As the new age approached, the life sleeping within the fruit gave rise to this sapling, and it has grown here on the snow-line for a few years only. Remember this, King Elessar! The fruit ripens but rarely, yet if it does, one should be planted or the line might die out of the world.'

'I am Hasong. I come from Yâd Hakar, great kingdom to the south ruled by the tribe called Sokhûri. Great are our warriors, and greater still is Khas Rûktar, who leads the Sokhûri.
'We met on the field as enemies, for who can foretell the many paths that diverge in war? It is the way of the Sokhûri to fight fiercely when commanded, and fight we did. But in war there is always one who fails. This time, the armies that came from Yâd Hakar are the ones that failed.
'When armies fail, there are two paths. On first path, every man is slain, and army is gone. This is how tribes vanish. Sokhûri cause many tribes to vanish. Khas Rûktar cause it himself, sometimes. Second path called Kerem-thak. This happen when failed army does not want to vanish. Tribe wants to live.
'Hasong and Mauthoi sent by Khas Rûktar to speak to Gondor King. We sent here for Kerem-thak. Khas Rûktar wants peace.'

'I am Mauthoi, sent by Khas Rûktar for purpose of Kerem-thak. King Gondor will choose if terms of peace are acceptable.'
Mauthoi looks at you with a sly expression on his face.
'You are ${PLAYER}. Great hero, they say. I wonder what might have happened if you encountered Hasong or Mauthoi during battle. Victory... or defeat? Not know now, because of Kerem-thak. I wonder, but not enough to wish it happened. Mauthoi have family back in Yâd Hakar, and tales of ${PLAYER} very convincing.
'Peace best for all.'

'Thank you for meeting with the emissaries who have come to Gondor, ${PLAYER}. I have spoken with them now, and we will have further to say on the subject of peace in the future.
'I must be truthful with you, ${PLAYER}. I do not completely trust the men of Harad. It is much easier to sue for peace when your forces have lost in battle, and I do not believe that Hasong or Mauthoi would be so willing to extend peace to Gondor if our positions were reversed. Many good soldiers were slain by weapons of the Haradrim, or trampled beneath the feet of their Mûmakil. Is it a betrayal of those lives to make peace with those who slew them?
'No, I do not think it is, but it is an easier question to ask than to answer. It seems that the delegation from Harad honestly desire peace, and that is a first step. Thank you for your help in this, my friend.'
'King Elessar waits at the throne for you, and will be glad to have news of your adventures in Mordor.'

'We bring greetings from Thorin III, King under the Mountain, to King Elessar of Gondor! There will be friendship between Durin's Folk and the Men of Gondor, and let their enemies beware!
'This is the first I have seen of this city, and while there is impressive stonework here there is much that might be improved. If King Elessar wishes it, I am sure there are dwarves among us who would be willing to refine the walls and streets of Minas Tirith.
'I would do it myself if I had a team of dwarves and my tools at the ready, but sadly we have come for diplomacy, not for masonry. Perhaps later!'

'The folk of this city must have seen a number of dwarves before now, for we have been treated warmly and with kindness, though we be strangers here. This is my first visit so far south, and I am pleased at the quality of the stone I have seen to this point. It could be worked with more skill and more care, but I have always been choosy about such things, as are many of Durin's Folk.
'How much higher must we climb to reach King Elessar's throne? The air thins as we ascend, and it is not to my liking.'

'We bring messages of friendship and alliance from the Lord and Lady of the Golden Wood! Many are the preparations, already underway, that will further advance the joined purposes of Elves and Men, and Lord Celeborn and Lady Galadriel will delight in their completion.
'I have been to this White City, but it was long ago. It is not the shining jewel it was then, but under the rule of King Elessar the Elfstone I believe it can be again.'

'The people of this city have been welcoming, if guarded. They do the name of their city proud in this, ${PLAYER}!
'But I must remember that Elves are not seen in Gondor as often as once they were. These are unusual days for all of us, and there is little doubt the people of Gondor have become more used to unusual sights of late!
'We will not tarry, but will continue upward to the throne room of Elessar. I am eager to speak with him, for I was a friend of his betrothed when we were young, and am still very close with the Lady Arwen.'

'I think that may have defused the worst of it, but they are still angry. I cannot say I blame them, to be truthful with you. These Haradrim are only suing for peace because they lost the battle and the war. If they had won, they would have put us all to the sword and destroyed the White City stone by stone.
'But Elessar is my king, and I will do as he commands. I only hope the people of the city will do the same!'

'The Withered Tree has been sowing discord since my coronation, ${PLAYER}, but my allowing the Haradrim embassy into the city has stirred them into a tempest. They are a group of malcontents who think Gondor is doomed to ruin, and they are not allowing the defeat of Sauron to change their opinion!
'I do not completely trust the Haradrim, but in my heart I know that we must make peace with them if Gondor is to maintain its safety. I understand that this is not easy for my people, but I believe that it is right.
'I will do what I can to ensure the Withered Tree do not stir the townspeople to violence. Good fortune to you, ${PLAYER}! I look forward to your return, and hope that by then this matter will be settled and we will have peace.'
'Go to the king and tell him that the Withered Tree has stirred up further trouble, but we have it mostly in hand for now.'

'We are met in friendship, ${PLAYER}. Like Gimli with the dwarves, I have brought gifts for the city from the Elves, though our gifts are of a different sort: flowering trees and plants with which to enliven the various levels of Minas Tirith. You can see some of the things we brought in the Second Circle, once you are done conversing with Gimli and me.
'I asked Aragorn if he desired a replacement for the White Tree, since a dead tree does not seem well-suited for Minas Tirith's future, but he refused. He responded that there can be no replacement for it in all of Middle-earth, to his sorrow. He is not wrong, but I wish it were otherwise.
'Still, the many plants I have brought to the city should help to brighten the scenery and the outlook of the people who live here, and I hope they will also bring a measure of happiness to its king.'
'Legolas and Gimli will enjoy hearing of your exploits in Mordor, ${PLAYER}, as I have.'

'It was from an abundance of caution that I asked you to attend us, ${PLAYER}, for I feared interruption by those calling themselves the Withered Tree. I am pleased that no such marauder sought to do harm to Aragorn or to the scion of Nimloth. Indeed, I think now that no man of Gondor could bring himself to damage the young sapling, if he knew what it portended: a sign of growing goodness in the years to come.'

'For how long did the fruit of the last tree lie hidden above the city, ${PLAYER}? Long years indeed, though the sapling has yet to reach seven years of growth! I will take Mithrandir's advice to heart, and when ever the fruit ripens it shall be planted, so the line of the tree will not vanish from the world. The Wizard's lesson was not subtle; it is not lost on me that the line of kings is much the same. There is time yet, and my heart is lightened by this discovery!
'Thank you for your part in this, my friend. The sapling should be planted in the Court of the Fountain, and let the folk of the city draw hope from the sight!'

'At last it is time. Come now, ${PLAYER}, and tell no one where we go.'

'There are words I must speak to Aragorn, but I do not wish to be interrupted. This room will not do; there are too many guards about! Enough safety for a king, but too many listening ears.
'I have a place in mind where Aragorn and I may speak away from his guards. Fear not! His person will be safe, for I would have you attend us and stand guard. You will prevent any interruptions, especially by members of the Withered Tree that might seek to harm the king. Speak to me when you are ready to go, and we will wait for nightfall.'

'It's a terrible thing, just a terrible thing. I've been cleaning up some of the blood spatters. I figure some of the patrons might have accidentally stepped in some before anyone knew what was going on. There are bloody footprints heading for the door.'

'Lord Duinhir would not have done it himself, ${PLAYER}. He must have paid yonder victim to do the deed, and once it was done he silenced the murderer and made his escape. I will take some of my best men and apprehend him. You bring word to King Elessar that the culprit has been found.'

'My knife... my knife... someone took my knife and used it for the crime! I cannot remember when last I saw it, but I must have set it down somewhere. Yes, I remember cleaning it... was that the last time I held it in my grip? I remember looking out over the city and thinking of my sons... where was that? Maybe it was on the parapet on the north side of the... of the Fifth Circle? Go there, good friend, go there and someone may know something! I am depending on you, ${PLAYER}, and so too are Rosfin and the memory of my boys!'

'This must be carefully handled or it will mean war. The murderer must be found. I will try to keep the situation from getting any worse, but I understand Hasong's feelings. They came here under a banner of truce, and someone betrayed that peace. This is a grave injustice, and it must be set right!
'Learn from Hasong what you can, and then go in search of the murderer. Only his blood can save the infant peace now.'

'Mauthoi went by himself to tavern in your city, trusting the laws of Kerem-thak would hold. He trusted that people of Elessar's city would respect the wishes of Elessar... if those wishes are true. Or is it that Elessar sends another message, hiding his real intent behind others, and secretly laughs at death of Mauthoi, ordering it be done? Dhûrto!
'If ${PLAYER} came to Yâd Hakar, spoke to the Khas, and was promised safety... how would Elessar react to murder of ${RACE}? Would it mean war? Hasong asks, \qWhy should this be different?\q Prove to me that this was not done by Elessar, or I will return to Khas Rûktar with words of Gondor's true face: no different than lies... no different than Mordor! Dhûrto most vile!
'Mauthoi was killed at tavern called \qHaven\q in Third Circle of city.'

'I've never seen anything like it, ${PLAYER}. I've heard tales of fell spirits and shades controlling the bodies of their victims, but that's not what is happening here. I think Parthadan knew what he was doing, but once it was done he couldn't come to terms with it in his head. I think it broke him.
'I will bring him to the dungeons, but I do not expect he will be there long. Go to King Elessar and tell him what we found.'
Parthadan stares at you with haunted eyes. You have seen many unsettling things in your adventures, but this is among the worst.
'I will bring Parthadan to the dungeons. You should return to King Elessar and tell him we have found the murderer.'
'It is time you returned to King Elessar in Minas Tirith, ${PLAYER}. Tell him how the conquest of Mordor progresses.'
'You should speak to the king. Something terrible has happened; I have never seen him like this.'

A cursory examination is enough to reveal the cause of Mauthoi's death. He was stabbed in the back by a short, bladed weapon, probably a knife or a dagger. It seems that his killer then carefully lowered him to the floor so as not to attract too much attention.
The murderer must have taken the weapon with him, because there is no sign of it.

'It was dark in here. It's always pretty dark, so that isn't unusual. I can't be sure, but I think I saw a cloaked figure moving for the door a moment before anyone noticed the dead man. He may have had a limp, or an odd way of walking? I can't say for certain, but the more I think about it the more I wonder if this fellow might be the culprit.
'He might have had a beard? Maybe not. It was dark in here! I wish I had paid more attention, but you never think of that at the time, do you?
'I can't be certain about the limp, or the beard. I think he was cloaked, but it was awful dark in here.'
'Someone here might have seen something. If you talk to them, it could be they will remember something they forgot to tell me. Unlikely, but possible.'

'It's a terrible thing, just a terrible thing. I've been cleaning up some of the blood spatters. I figure some of the patrons might have accidentally stepped in some before anyone knew what was going on. There are bloody footprints heading for the door.'

'No one has remembered anything especially useful, ${PLAYER}. Whether there really was a cloaked or hooded figure here or not, it seems to me everyone has created one in their memory: a member of the Withered Tree brandishing a knife, slipping away before anyone thought to look at him.'

'Ah, ${PLAYER}. It is good to see you again. I have not forgotten how you helped me calm the unruly crowd the other day. Not enough, it seems; one of them took matters into his own hands. Did King Elessar ask you to look into the Haradrim murder?
'I have already spoken with some of the folk here, but you are welcome to see if they have remembered anything. I haven't moved his body yet, so you can check and see if there's anything I missed. He's over there.
'I have no love for the Haradrim, but this wasn't right. Curse the Withered Tree, they've gone and made things worse!'

'That word, \qdhûrto\q... it is the word Hasong uses for \qbetrayal.\q But the Haradrim emissaries are not the only ones who stand betrayed. This treachery is a betrayal of Gondor, and of me, ${PLAYER}.
'I want the murderer found. We cannot let this crime against Gondor stand unpunished. Search the tavern where Mauthoi was killed for any trace of the murderer. It is the Haven, and it is on the south-east side of the Third Circle of the city.'
'The body is right over there. I haven't moved him yet, but I don't want to leave him there for too long.'

'I didn't see anything I haven't already told Dúnor. This place is usually all a-bustle, even if the Lords of Gondor haven't been themselves since the battle on the field. First thing I noticed was that fellow lying on the ground there, and I figured he was well in his cups. When I went over to him I saw the blood, and called for the guards.
'You think the Withered Tree did this? It's not right to kill a fellow as wants peace, but you do have to wonder how many good soldiers died at his hands, or at the hands of folk like him. Not excusin' it, mind, just something to weigh, I'd say.'
'${PLAYER}! You have to tell him I did not do this! You know me! I did not kill them!'
'It is a long chance, ${PLAYER}, but it is a chance. Go to the parapet on the north side of the Fifth Circle and see if anyone there saw anything.'

'Ho there, ${PLAYER}! I have heard of your many deeds, and it is a pleasure to meet you at last! You are a friend of Lord Duinhir of the Blackroot Vale, are you not? Did his knife ever come back to him?'
You boggle at the man, your mouth agape.
'Did I say something odd? He comes here to this spot to clean and sharpen his knife, but it has been a few days since last I saw him. He left his knife behind, an accident of his recent grief, I expect. I would have brought it to him, but before I had properly decided, another volunteered for the task.'
You ask the man who it was who volunteered to return Duinhir's knife.
'Why, it was Parthadan, the Warden of the Green. I saw him only a moment ago, outside the Dome of the Sun on the north-east side of the Sixth Circle.'

Parthadan looks up at you with haunted eyes, and you know at once that he is guilty of the crimes.
'I know why you're here, ${PLAYER}. I have been wandering around the city, looking for reasons to go on, but I found none. It all seemed so clear to me, once, but I cannot recapture that feeling no matter how long I walk.
'I saw Duinhir cleaning his knife, and I thought of his sons, and I knew with complete certainty that the men of Harad had to die. But I serve on the Council of Gondor! I am the Warden of the Green! Who will speak for the folk of Pelennor who lost their homes during the war, if not I? So I took Duinhir's knife when he left it behind, and I paid a man in coin for the deed, and when one of the Haradrim emissaries went to the tavern, my man cut him down.
'It seemed so clear to me: if he lived he would speak my name, in time. So I took the knife from him and slew him too, but the clarity was already going. He was a man of Gondor; why did he need to die, when it was men of Gondor for whom the Warden of the Green sought to provide?'
You ask Parthadan how long he has been with the Withered Tree, and the haunted look is replaced with a confused expression.
'The Withered Tree? Oh, no, you've gotten it wrong, ${PLAYER}. I have never been one of those malcontents. Everything I did... I did for the good of Gondor. I would never join those villains. I wish I could explain to you where it went wrong, but it's just not clear to me anymore. We were at war, and then we weren't, and somewhere along the way I lost something important. I can't remember now what it might have been, but there was a time when I knew this was the right thing to do. It's gone now, though, and I don't think it's ever coming back. I wish I could tell Duinhir I was sorry. I think this is his fault, somehow.'
'You say you found something? Well, don't dawdle here! Go examine the new evidence and bring anything you find back to me!'

You tell Dúnor of the second murdered man and hand him the knife. He studies it with dawning realization.
'${PLAYER}... I know this knife. It is finely decorated, and gilt front and rear. This is the weapon of a lord, not of a common man. Do you see the black circle here on the hilt? That is a symbol of the Blackroot Vale, or I am a Mûmak. This is the personal dagger of Lord Duinhir. I would know it anywhere. The Lord of the Blackroot Vale murdered the Haradrim emissary. But why would he do this?'
You think of the fate that befell his sons, Duilin and Derufin, and wonder.
'He would not have done it himself, ${PLAYER}. He must have paid yonder victim to do the deed, and once it was done he silenced the murderer and made his escape. I will take some of my best men and apprehend him. You bring word to King Elessar that the culprit has been found.'
'I hope I have not done wrong by cleaning up some of the blood! I was only trying to help.'

'Duinhir was brought before me and he claims innocence of the crime. What say you to this, ${PLAYER}? I have heard his words, but I would hear what you think as well.'
You give Elessar your opinion, and he nods.
'There is no doubt that Duinhir keenly feels the loss of his sons beneath the trampling feet of the Mûmakil, the beasts wielded in war by the Haradrim. But why would he pay a man to commit this murder, only to leave behind his dagger, distinctive as it is? If the killing was fueled by a desire for vengeance, would he not wish to carry it out himself? Further, this act has now claimed two lives, one of whom can carry no burden for the deaths of Duilin and Derufin, no matter how slight.
'I will not rush to exonerate him; neither will I render hasty judgement. Speak to him, ${PLAYER}, and hear what he has to say of this. If there is anything he knows that may point to another, he should provide it, for Hasong will not wait long before returning to his country with a call for war.'

Duinhir turns his tear-stained face to you.
'I did not do this, ${PLAYER}! Tell him! You have to tell him I am not guilty of this crime! I hate the Haradrim for what they did to my boys, but I would not kill one, not like this! Let them face me in combat, man to man, and I would show no mercy, but I would not kill any among them like this, like a coward! How could I face Rosfin, having done this and brought shame to my king? I could not! You must believe me!
'My knife... my knife... someone took my knife and used it for the crime! I cannot remember when last I saw it, but I must have set it down somewhere. Yes, I remember cleaning it... was that the last time I held it in my grip? I remember looking out over the city and thinking of my sons... where was that? Maybe it was on the parapet on the north side of the... of the Fifth Circle? Go there, good friend, go there and someone may know something! I am depending on you, ${PLAYER}, and so too are Rosfin and the memory of my boys!'

'Sauron is gone, but he gave us many unwanted gifts before the War of the Ring came to a close. Dhûrto, ${PLAYER}. I cannot abide the sound of the word, but I know that this day, Gondor deserves it.
'I thank you for what you have done, my friend. An innocent man was spared, and for that we should be thankful. I will await news of your return, and hope that your adventures progress well, and simply. How is it that war can be so clear, and peace be so confused?'

Talk to Mílgamel
An Apprentice's Guide to Ithilien

'Not in all my days have I seen such gorgeous lands, ${PLAYER}! I have heard much of Ithilien, but the tales all fall short in conveying its true beauty. I am proud to report that I have identified many of the herbs Master Galathir seeks... but I could not help take note of the many, many strange plants I had never before set eyes upon. Some stirred memories of drawings I had seen in musty tomes within the Old Archives, and I cannot help but wonder what powers some of these might possess... but I can see Master Galathir frowning down at these foolish thoughts of mine!
'I hope the Rangers do not mind my brief company here in their... cave. I don't mean to disparage their choice of refuge, but it is a cave.
'Yet, I can't deny there's a homely warmth to it... perhaps I'll take a few notes about Henneth Annûn for my own keeping.'

'What do you want? Can you not see there are still many near to death and in need of tending? Even my healers are taking ill from lack of rest!
'If idle chatter is your wish, begone. If you have need of my ear, speak!'
You tell Galathir of your desire to accompany Mílgamel on her survey of Ithilien.
'So you have heard I am sending her off, have you? No matter. You know of her task? Certain herb-stores vital to my most trusty medicines dwindle near to nothing. If these can be found where herbalists long dared not tread, then she must make a thorough harvest. Mind you! I do not wish Mílgamel distracted by any strange roots and leaves we have no use for and which might prove harmful in the extreme!
'You will find Mílgamel in the House of Remedies ready to ride to Ithilien. She knows her course, ${CLASS}...so keep her from harm. I cannot afford the loss of another healer.
'Now leave me!'

'Excuse me, what is it that you want? I'm quite busy enough in my studies and have little time to speak.'
You introduce yourself to Mílgamel and inform her that you are to be her guide for Galathir's task.
'Oh! I am so sorry... I've been a mite overwhelmed by Galathir's demands as of late. He is a wise teacher, but his tasks are often far more daunting than he thinks them. Perhaps he has forgotten what it was like to be a novice...
'He has charged me with surveying our lands in the aftermath of the battle. I have taken careful note of the twenty-three leaves, flowers, and roots he wishes me to search for... but I can think only of what I shall see in the ruins upon the Anduin, in lost Ithilien, and beyond! I must calm myself. I can see Master Galathir frowning at me even now. I must stay true to my task!
'My survey is to begin in Osgiliath, but it shall stretch far beyond it. If you are to be my guide, I ask that you meet me near the old bridge in Osgiliath. I can ride that far, but I would prefer to do my survey on foot.'

'Oh, I almost didn't hear you over the roaring water!
'In all my days, I have never crossed the Great River... and I wanted to spend some time looking upon it before you arrived. All that lies ahead is known to me only through distant gazes, travellers' tales, and old maps.
'I know it as a land of striking beauty, even at a distance, but I know that there is an unseen danger lurking within it - else the Rangers would have naught to do but rest.
'Ah, but rest does not come easy these days...
'My brother was gravely wounded in the battle, and I tended to him in the Houses of Healing after he was taken from the Fields. I have never felt so powerless in my life, ${PLAYER}. Master Galathir and the lady Ioreth helped ease his pain, but his wounds were too many and too great. He lasted the night, but by dawn death had claimed him.
'I have kept his blade in my keeping, and I shall wield it if ever the need arises...'
Mílgamel pauses for a moment and stares into the rushing waters below.
'In addition to list of herbs, Master Galathir has given me a strict list of locations to direct my survey... perhaps some of them are familiar to you?'
Mílgamel hands you the list. The list mentions the old Houses of Healing in Osgiliath, the ruins of Bâr Aroth and Aelin Veren as well as the island fortress of Cair Andros in Ithilien, and mostly troublingly, the road into Imlad Morgul. At the end, it makes a note that the Rangers have been made aware of Mílgamel's passage into Ithilien and shall make arrangements at Henneth Annûn.
'Ah, so you do know them! Let us get started then, shall we?'
You have arrived at Henneth Annûn, and the cool glow of the cavern seems even more inviting than usual.
You have found Mílgamel and she appears to be admiring the ruined city from the causeway...

Galathir can be found in the House of Remedies within the Masters' Tier of Minas Tirith (After-battle).
Ioreth has asked you to speak with Galathir for she fears he might mislead a young apprentice in his tutelage.
Talk to Galathir in the House of Remedies

'Do not misunderstand me, ${PLAYER}. Galathir still possesses great skill as a healer, but he has lost sight of his shortcomings. In my long years in Minas Tirith and Imloth Melui, I have never found a shortage of new skills to learn and new draughts and tinctures to use in my work, from new trial and old lore alike. But Galathir has grown reliant on his own concoctions for his patients, and where one ill is healed another often takes its place.
'He has taken a new apprentice - a young woman by the name of Mílgamel. The poor girl has no idea that she might receive such misguided instruction! It is one matter for a certain draught or salve to seem the clear choice, and quite another entirely for it to truly be so. Indeed, there are many uses for Everworth, Trueleaf, Snagbane, Blushblade, Settlegang...'
Recalling that you have a certain urgency to your task, Ioreth trails off and pauses briefly.
'I have heard tell that Mílgamel shall soon make for Ithilien. Perhaps you would accompany her on your own journey back to the king's side, and while you do, help her see all she has to learn there, and not only that which Galathir has pre-ordained she should see. For they say that place was once the garden of all Gondor, and what forgotten herbs and herblore may await there, just as when I told Mithrandir of the old saying that the hands of the king... ah, but I see I am needed.
'Talk to Galathir and convince him of your worth in this task, and then speak to her. We shall make a great healer of her yet!'

Worts, Weeds, and Wastes

'I am glad you have come, ${PLAYER}.
'Even with so many here, there is a feeling of loneliness in the air. These men stare into the face of death... not that of a triumphant victory. I speak true, do I not?
'I can see it in your eyes. Something other than victory drives this advance - a purpose born of valour and kinship. I will not ask you of it, and I shall not tell the people of Minas Tirith of what I have learned here. Despair is a mighty force, and it can consume far more than hope alone.
'I have thought enough on that matter. Let us speak of more hopeful things.
'I see that you have brought many pages to me, but what is that under your arm?'
Mílgamel takes the crumbling volume of \qWorts and Weeds\q from you.
'This... this could be the original volume by Golgolas! It is ruined but for a few pages, but such a find you have made!
'Let me look at this for a time, and you should bind the other pages together into one. I'm certain you have the complete volume between them all!'

Amid the Orc-filth of Cair Andros, you have found a small pile of books. Most of them have various tears and tatters and a few have been burned.
You sift through the pile of books and come across what seems to be a few singed pages bound to the spine and back cover of \qWorts and Weeds.\q The rest of the volume is missing, but you are able to collect five legible pages.

While scouring the Halls of Healing in Osgiliath, you have found a decaying volume of \qWorts and Weeds.\q
Judging by the crumbling remains of its covers, it seems likely that this could have been the original version written by Golgolas of Ithilien. The pages are largely in poor condition, and those that are still legible have sustained some water damage from the ruined cistern nearby.
You carefully pick up the volume, mark the legible pages, and stow it away.

'I cannot thank you enough for your help with this, ${PLAYER}. Master Galathir hoped merely to survey Ithilien and gather some known herbs, but now I am on this journey, I feel my sight reaches far beyond his ken. What we can learn from this finished volume - why, for one, about this poisonous lichen and how it might heal the northern Wastes from their long blight.
'Even with the looming battle ahead, we must take the time to tend to these lands. If they fail us, any other victory may ring hollow. Should these brave men return from this battle, they must return to a beautiful Gondor brimming with new life... in place of all that was lost.
'I shall need much time to study Golgolas's work, but I believe we can bring forth new life in these blasted lands!'

Torngroth can be found far to the north in North Ithilien, Cair Andros can be found to the south-west of Henneth Annûn, Osgiliath can be found to the east of Minas Tirith, and Ioreth can be found in the High Hall within the Masters' Tier of Minas Tirith.
Mílgamel has asked you to investigate Cair Andros, Osgiliath, and Torngroth in the hope of finding more pages from \qWorts and Weeds.\q She also has asked you to return to Ioreth to obtain Galathir's transcription of the book.

'It is unlikely to be a simple matter, but there may be a way to discover more about this lichen. Once, I recall, Master Galathir spoke of a great tome - a supposed great collection of knowledge about the plants and such-like of Middle-earth, called \qWorts and Weeds.\q When I showed interest, he forbade me from leafing through it, for he said it contained spurious anecdotes of specimens not seen in his age, and besides, it was a damaged copy, far from complete.
'I... I have come to doubt much of my Master's wisdom. But - never mind that. This \qWorts and Weeds\q was penned by a Man of Gondor named Golgolas, who dwelt within Ithilien before it fell under the Shadow, and it is said it was widely read and copied by the Herbalists of that day.
'Do you think - would you visit the ruins and places of North Ithilien, and discover if any pages of that book still remain? Torngroth, Cair Andros, or Osgiliath, for example? Who can say, perhaps good, old Ioreth would share the pages Galathir would not.
'Meanwhile, I have asked the Rangers to provide me passage to the edge of the Wastes. Although they took much convincing, they have agreed. If I am to gain a better understanding of this lichen, I shall need to be closer to the lands of the Enemy - no matter how hostile they may be.
'They plan to take me to an army encampment - one with which they claim you are familiar. When you've gathered as much as you can of \qWorts and Weeds,\q find me far to the north.'

'You have come all this way just to see Galathir's transcription of \qWorts and Weeds?\q That's enough walking for you, ${PLAYER}! Now wait here a moment....'
Ioreth walks over to a nearby book-shelf and rummages through a few heavy tomes. She finally pulls out something that more closely resembles a sheaf of crumbling pages than a book, and then walks back over to you.
'Why, you could hardly call this a volume! Why does he keep this thing about, I wonder, if he thinks so poorly of it? Here, you take it. Perhaps he will end up being of more help without it...
'Do not worry, ${PLAYER}. If he asks for it, I shall tell him that you and Mílgamel had need of it for your task.
'Oh, and tell the king I wish his campaign well when you see him next!'

Ioreth can be found in the High Hall within the Masters' Tier of Minas Tirith (After-battle).
Aragorn has asked you to return to Minas Tirith and learn of the fates of the wounded as well as what further havoc may have been wrought by Galathir's overeager hands.

'Have you a moment, ${PLAYER}?
'With such a journey ahead, I count myself and this host fortunate to have you here at my side. Yet my thoughts stray back to Minas Tirith... and to those we left behind. Many dear friends and strangers alike now fight their own battles against illness and injury.
'It was with great sadness that I could not tend to them all, but the greater matters of the Dark Lord and the Ring-bearer's hidden quest have called me away. I know not if I shall ever return to Minas Tirith, and I worry for the fates of those we left behind if I fall in our final gambit.
'Do you remember the Master Herbalist we encountered during my brief time in the City? The one called Galathir? He was unfit for his post and could have caused great harm to those in his care, but I had not the means to send him from the Houses of Healing... not without declaring myself.
'I ask that you return to the Houses of Healing in Minas Tirith and speak with the healer Ioreth. Ensure that she keeps Galathir's ruinous tinctures from the wounded, and have her be my eyes in the High Hall.
'She will heed my words, even if they are delivered in my stead. You are one of the swiftest riders among my ranks, and I entrust this task to you alone.
'Go with haste, my friend. Once you have returned, we can continue planning our course into the Wastes.'

'You have come at the request of the king?'
You inform Ioreth that Aragorn has not yet claimed that title, and then tell her of his concerns about Galathir's healing practices.
'Whether he claims the title or not, I know him for what he is. He has the hands of a healer, and none but a king could work kingsfoil into such a potent medicine - and I would know! Still, it troubles me that he has grown concerned about Galathir's methods. Not precisely because I disagree, mind you, but because I did not think it would be so plainly noticed!
'I cannot send Galathir away, but I can help prevent him from treating any more of the wounded with Everworth. It is the least I can do for my king!
'However, there remains one other matter of concern regarding Galathir... and his new apprentice.'
On the eve of his final assault against the Dark Lord, Aragorn's thoughts turn to Minas Tirith and the wounded.

'The peculiar thing is not the arrow, but the state of the animal's body. The corpse is sickened and in a rapid state of decay. The Rangers say the ground surrounding the animal was devoid of flora.
'This is all very concerning. Perhaps it was unwise to pass Cair Andros by, after all. The forces from Mordor at Cair Andros must be coating their arrows with something most vile. Something not seen upon the Pelennor Battlefield (or else I would recognize it), and therefore, perhaps, concocted here in North Ithilien! It is not why Master Galathir sent me, or an inquiry he would approve of, but I must know what this substance is.
'I shall not accompany you to Cair Andros, as my lack of skill in combat would only slow you down - and endanger myself - but I beseech you, go and gather what you can of this poison, so we may study it.'

The worried thoughts of the Host of the West turn towards Frodo and Sam, who have passed beyond even Gandalf's sight. He knows only that the hobbits make for the dangerous pass of Cirith Ungol, their guide the creature Gollum, spared years ago by the mercy of Bilbo. Their guide possesses knowledge of this hidden way into Mordor, but another secret he keeps to himself: the identity of the terrible guardian that lurks within the tunnel through which they must pass...

'My thoughts are also with Frodo and Sam, and I fear for their safety in the company of Gollum. But I agree with Mithrandir that they must still be alive, for we would know if Sauron had the Ring.
'But my reasoning is not that of the Wizard. I travelled with Frodo and Sam for almost four months, and we had many adventures and braved many dangers. And even after so many shared hardships, I think Master Gamgee had only just begun to warm up to me, and perhaps did not yet entirely trust this \qStrider.\q
'He will not take his eyes off Gollum, even if Frodo perhaps will. I do not think Gollum will be able to take advantage of our Samwise, even if he thinks he can. They will be fine, inasmuch as any might be whose misfortune it is to journey in the Black Land.'
'Look for Daervunn where the northward road departs from the camp and ask him if the men are ready to leave.'
'Look for Daervunn where the northward road departs from the camp and ask him if the men are ready to leave.'

'What did Daervunn have to say? Are the men ready to march?'
You report the Ranger's words, and Aragorn nods grimly.
'It pains me that such a course is necessary, but I take satisfaction in knowing the great loyalty and courage of the men with whom I march.'
'This road will take us across the blasted plains of Dagorlad, to the very gate of Mordor. I hope you are ready.'
'If Aragorn says there is no other way, I will not gainsay him. This is the road we must take!'

'You were at the council of the captains, ${PLAYER}, and you heard the arguments for and against this march to the Black Gate. You must know of its importance, as I do.
'But still I am troubled. Before battle consumed Minas Tirith, I spoke with Faramir of his watch in Ithilien, and he told me that his men encountered two hobbits in the wild: Frodo and Sam. Briefly he held them, but he did not hinder their errand overlong and soon released them to their purpose.
'But a third there was, and he served our friends as their guide: Gollum. Faramir spoke against the creature, but Frodo believed he could be trusted, and intended to follow him through a secret pass into Mordor. The pass is called Cirith Ungol. It is an evil place. I know enough of that pass to know that danger lurks there in the darkness, and I fear that Frodo may trust his guide too readily. Alas that our roads ran apart!
'A fortnight has passed since Frodo and Sam departed from Faramir's care. My wondering mind worries at how little we know of their fates, ${PLAYER}, and conjures terrible scenarios of what could have befallen. What has happened to our friends? What has happened to the Ring?'
'Mithrandir desires to speak with you, my friend.'
'Too much time has passed without word of our friends. Did their guide lead them into some danger, as I fear? We cannot know for certain, ${PLAYER}, but neither can we dispel our worries.'

'In my heart I guessed that Frodo and Gollum would meet before the end, but I hope that Frodo does not trust blindly. If he remains alert to the possibility of deceit, perhaps he can prevent it before it leads our friends to harm.
'Or has it already done so? It has been two weeks since they left Henneth Annûn, and still there has been no word. If they fell prey to some treachery of Gollum's, surely we would have heard by now. Cirith Ungol...'
Mithrandir's voice trails away as his eyes search the horizon. After a moment his attention returns, and a smile briefly illuminates his features.
'I should not have given in to these fears, ${PLAYER}. The Ring remains out of Sauron's grasp. Let that keep our hearts afloat and allay some of our worries! For if Frodo were betrayed to Sauron, I feel certain that the Dark Lord would make use of the Ring at once, and we would know the end had arrived. That has not happened. The Ring, and Frodo, have not been seized by the Dark Lord. Every step that Frodo takes toward the Fire kindles our hopes.'
'The Ring, and Frodo, have not been seized by the Dark Lord. Every step that Frodo takes toward the Fire kindles our hopes.'

'The only hope of victory lies with Frodo, but we still have a part to play in this great struggle, ${PLAYER}. I asked Daervunn to prepare the men for departure, for I believed it might take longer than expected for the Host of the West to set out upon this last march. Heavy are the feet that dread the approaching road, but still they must step one before the other!
'Look for Daervunn where the northward road departs from the camp, my friend, and ask him if the men are ready to leave.'

'This road will take us across the blasted plains of Dagorlad, to the very gate of Mordor. The men stir with restlessness, but they will obey their liege, whether he be Éomer or Aragorn. Others there are, too, who have joined this host in cause of allied friendship; if they have not turned back now, I believe they will never abandon us.
'I have shared words with Peregrin Took here, and he too has a courage about him.'

'This is the road to Mordor? No one could mistake it for anything else, ${PLAYER}! It looks as I would have expected it to look, had I ever wanted to fill my heart with fright and my mind with unease at the considering... and I did not!
'Daervunn has had some kind words to say concerning my \qcourage,\q and I did not want to offend him by disagreeing, but I think he sees what is not there. If I were truly brave, would I feel so frightened at the prospect of taking this road? Certainly not! But Aragorn believes that we have to do this, and I have smarts enough to know he is more wise than I am. If he says there is no other way, this hobbit will not gainsay him. This is the road we must take!'

Calenglad is lost in his thoughts.
Aragorn is lost in his thoughts.
'None of us are free of worry, ${PLAYER}, or free of regret. But still we move forward in spite of those feelings. That is all we can do. That is what we must do.'

'Some of my kinsmen are deep in thought, contemplating the roads that have led them here, while they ready themselves for the road to come. Will you speak with some of them and put into words how grateful I am for all they have done? This is likely to be our last battle, and I want them to know that I appreciate their service not only as their captain or their king, but also as their friend and kinsman. This may be my last chance to tell them so, and I do not want to miss that opportunity.'

'I watched the departure of the Faint-hearted, ${PLAYER}, and I felt no scorn for them, though there was a time in my life when I might not have understood their choice. I see that their path too was in service of the Host of the West. Our own road takes us to Mordor, for we have the courage to go that way.
'I am not afraid of Mordor or its Black Gate. Neither am I afraid of the Dark Lord or his armies. I am not afraid of Mordirith, no matter what he names himself. I am not afraid of death, for I have lived a life enriched by friendship and laughter, and I know that endings must always come, soon or late.
'I am made strong by the love of my friends and the memories I carry with me, and no Orc or wraith or beast can conquer that strength. At long last I am at peace, ${PLAYER}. I will follow Aragorn to the end, with an unburdened heart.'

'Have you ever broken a promise, ${PLAYER}?'
Calenglad looks at you sadly, and holds up a finger to halt your reply.
'I have sought to live my life with honour, making good upon my promises and the oaths I have taken. I swore an oath to aid Aragorn my chief in all things, and I have done so as best I could. That oath has taken me far from my home and to the very doorstep of Mordor.
'But my heart remains on the shores of Lake Nenuial. I promised to return when my duty in the south-lands was done, but... it does not seem that any of us will return, after all. What were the words of Gwindeth? That the return of Elendil's kingdom would be worth some measure of sorrow? Did she speak the truth? I do not know, even now.'

'We have been through a lot together, ${PLAYER}, and most of it was unpleasant. I am not complaining, not really. If it was to be easy, it need not have been the Dúnedain's task to face it! I said as much to Elweleth once, but she has gone away, and will never return.
'Do you think that the folk of Middle-earth will appreciate everything Aragorn has done? I do not expect our names to be remembered, but if there is any justice, Aragorn will be remembered fondly and well by the people of Gondor and Rohan, at least.'
Radanir is silent for a long while, and you are about to leave him be when he speaks at last.
'It seems there will be no peaceful tavern for us at the end of this road, ${PLAYER}. After everything we have gone through, I suppose I am not really surprised.'

'Once I spoke to you of my travels, ${PLAYER}, of my adventures in the wooded lands of Enedwaith and the rocky heights of Thrór's Coomb, but they are dwarfed now by the memory of these last few weeks. From the dungeons of Isengard to the fighting on the Pelennor, our journey has been full of hardship.
'My mind turns now to my home, at Sûri-kylä in Forochel. I do not think I will see it again, but I am at ease knowing that I have done what I can for the Snowmen, and they will persevere as they always have done.
'I will follow Aragorn wherever he leads.'

'What did you see from atop the slag-hill?'
Aragorn listens to your account.
'All was quiet and still? I see, and I am not surprised. Sauron is waiting. I do not take the empty calm before the Gate to be fact, and neither should you. The Dark Lord's armies are arrayed before us, though we see them not. He waits to unleash them, for he wants to see what we will do.'
'Good luck, ${PLAYER}! Good luck to all of us!'

'This is a dead place, an empty place. I do not like it. There will be many places such as these as we get nearer to Mordor, ${PLAYER}. How could anyone live here?
'The answer to that question is a simple one, I suppose: no one does live here, not truly. Not good folk, at any rate.
'I have heard tell from the Rangers of Ithilien that there are a few sites throughout the Wastes in which evil folk dwell. These places should be scouted before the Host passes near. Find Dûm Boha in the Noman-lands, and Dol Acharn and Ondoher's Folly in Dagorlad, and defeat any enemies that may endanger the passage of the Host. Once the way is safe, the Host of the West will assemble outside the Black Gate and we will see what awaits us there.'

'Stand fast, men! They seek to cow us with their numbers, but each of us is worth a dozen of their mindless thralls!
'My limbs are heavy and my breath is short, ${PLAYER}, but I will do what I can to support Aragorn and my kinsmen.
'Fight on! Fight on!'

'I see that you have already slain your share of Orcs, ${PLAYER}! Legolas has also cut an impressive swath, but he tells me his supply of arrows will not last long. Perhaps you can help him with this?
'The battle has only just begun, but there is no need to worry about our respective tallies this time. There will be plenty of foes for all of us!'

'I have enough arrows for the moment, but Gimli is right: my supply will run low soon if the tide of enemies does not slow!
'Many archers of Gondor and Rohan have already fallen to the arrows of Mordor; some of their quivers remain full, or nearly so. Go to the archery lines and look for our fallen unfortunates. If you return to me with a number of their full quivers I will be able to maintain my current pace, and continue to support Gimli with my bow.
'I thank you for undertaking this helpful task, grim though it may seem!'

'Thank you, my friend. Set the quivers at my feet and I will use them as the need arises.'

'I heard Aragorn shouting his commands from the top of the slag hill to the south-west, ${PLAYER}. Climb the hill and see if you can aid him!'

'We have held the line of battle for now, keeping our foes from ascending the eastern hill, but it seems that our foes have redoubled their efforts to take the western hill.
'We are hard-pressed and can spare no man, but someone must go to the western hill and keep it from being taken! Can you go to the aid of Imrahil with haste enough, ${PLAYER}? I know you can! Fight your way to the slope of the western hill, and help the Prince of Dol Amroth throw back the tide!'
'${PLAYER}! The fighting here goes poorly, but with you here my spirits are lifted!'

'Is this to be the last battle, ${PLAYER}? My heart tells me this is so, and though it be a sorrowful thing I will be glad to see the end of war-time, and to have rest.
'A palpable hit, and another! I find no joy in battle, my friend, but I find that I am uncommonly good at it, truly! I will use that skill to defend the men at my side, until my last breath is stolen away by some lucky stroke!
'Fight onward, ${PLAYER}! Make our foes pay for the evils they have done, and hope still to do!'

'How goes the fighting on the western hill, ${PLAYER}? I trust that Éomer and Imrahil stand still against the forces of Mordor?'
You tell Aragorn that they are still defiant, but injuries have begun to mount among their soldiers.
'So it is with us, but we fight on. It will not be long now, but we will stand until the end.'

'All those quivers you brought me are spent, ${PLAYER}! There is knife-work to be done all around the hill, and plenty for all!
'I have this fight in hand, but I am certain there will be enough foes for you to slay if you go a-looking for them, or wait for them to seek you out!'

'I am glad the flow of the battle has brought you to me, ${PLAYER}. I wanted to speak with you again.'
You study the Ranger's face and see little of the doubt that troubled him at the Camp of the Host. He seems curiously calm for one who stands amid such tumult.
'After battle was joined, I stood with Aragorn and felled Orc after Orc; soon I lost count of the bodies, but there were ever more to replace them. With each swing of my blade, my sword lost its individuality. It was no longer my weapon only, but it was the weapon of every Dúnadan that ever took up sword for his king.
'With every swing, it seemed to me I was conducting a great music, and the tides of battle moved through and around me in a great swelling chorus. It was a drowning tide, and it swept the foes of Men beneath it, cleansing the land of their foul mark.
'I saw the great beauty of the land returning in full measure, the deep forests growing anew and the rivers flowing swift and clean. I saw twilight pooling in the hills, and the stars reflected in mountain lakes, crisp and cool.
'My eyes were opened to this vision of a new age, and though I saw it only for the span of a breath, I knew in that moment that Gwindeth had been right: such a kingdom would be worth some measure of sorrow. She will see it, though she fade into myth, and men question whether she ever existed at all. But still she will be there, among the falls and waters of Lake Nenuial, and she will remember.
'I am at peace, my friend. The evil of Sauron cannot last, even if every last one of us perishes before his gates. But let us hope we do not, ${PLAYER}! A new age is coming!'

'Help! Can you help me? I have slain a number of Orcs, but the last one staggered away with my sword still stuck in its gut, and now I have no weapon!
'Can you find me a sword? There must be a blade somewhere at the base of the hill, abandoned or dropped by a coward or by a corpse! Without a weapon I cannot do any good for Gondor, and I have no way to protect myself from the throng!'

'We are being overwhelmed, ${PLAYER}. I sustained an injury from an Orc's lucky swing, and now my arm hangs loosely; I cannot lift up my shield. My men have fallen back a short distance, but they cannot stand long against the tide. They will soon need to retreat once more.
'I ask that you fight across to the eastern slag hill once again; if the battle is turning against us here, it must also be going ill with Aragorn. Look for his friends, the Elf and the dwarf. I saw them from afar, but could not tell how they fared.
'They will need you as the battle goes on.'
'Help! Will no one help me? Alas for my injuries!'

'I welcome the concern of the Prince of Dol Amroth, but it is unnecessary! My own battle is well in hand.
'But I have another worry: the terrible flying creatures that carry the robed Nazgûl on their backs. They fall upon my soldiers and bear them aloft with their clutching claws... and then they drop them to the battlefield below. There is no protection from this!
'The safety of my men is my prime concern, for many soldiers of Rohan are unhorsed and such is not their preferred means of doing battle. Over the din of battle I thought I heard Rohirric voices crying out in alarm, to the south-west. That is where you are needed, not here with me!'

'I am glad to see you are still kicking, ${PLAYER}! I am afraid I can't do very much among all these warriors, but I aim to do the best I can for Frodo and poor Sam.
'I miss Merry, but at least he is back in Minas Tirith and won't need to see this fighting, not for today at least. I don't expect I can draw level with some of his deeds, not unless I were to smite that horrible Messenger, but that is all right.
'Be careful, ${PLAYER}! This beastly brood is out for blood!'

'The tide of enemies has swelled, and soon it will crash upon the shore of our shield wall; the tide will not draw back again until we are slain.
'I have taken it upon myself to watch Peregrin the Halfling. He is a soldier of Gondor and now more a member of the Guard than I, but it grieves my heart to think he might fall in this battle. I will protect him if I can, both for his sake and that of my son, whose friendship he possesses.
'Stay wary, ${PLAYER}. I wager our foes have not depleted the stock of their sorceries!'

'If what you relate is true, why then an entire army hides in wait below the ground! We know full well that overwhelming odds stand locked behind the Morannon. But we shall not face those until the ordained time of battle, according to Lord Aragorn's plan.

'I tell you, ${PLAYER}, I have wondered whether I were going mad. I would track an Orc Captain climbing the nearby eastern hills, only to lose track of him. Then, as if by some sorcery, I would espy him far west, where I should surely have seen him pass.

'Treasure? Ha ha! Yes, I see, now we get to the bottom of this foolish notion.
'I tell you once more: Mordor is no place for hobbits. There are things down that path beyond what either of you have ever reckoned or encountered. In truth, I should think you have had enough adventuring for three lives of hobbits put together, both of you.'

'More than we have reckoned or encountered you say? Yet we have encountered quite a lot between the Shire and here. Not just Moria and the Pelennor Fields, which I suppose you remember somewhat, but plenty in between when you were not around to nanny us. I say it is we who are capable of more than you imagine, thank you very much.'
'Old Bilbo came home with quite a lot of treasure, you know. They will be expecting us to do the same, I am sure of it.'

'Really, Gandalf, I don't see why we shouldn't be allowed to go in. Plenty of others have gone in - Sam and Frodo included. Well, I'll admit, they are not the best of examples.
'But we are not proposing to march right up the slope of Mount Doom. We wish only to take a few brief strolls in the place, to be able to say that we saw it with our own eyes, find a bit of treasure perhaps to take home with us....'

'Also, do not forget that Merry and I have each missed out on some part of the excitement that everyone else got to take part in, on account of those kidnapping Orcs and getting knocked on the head and prattling stern Gondorian healers!'

'Dear old Gandalf! I spoke those words in a rash moment and I am ashamed of them at once. Please forgive a foolish hobbit.
'But all the same, we have done so much. You must not take us for the young innocents who first stepped into Bree those months ago.'

'What a remarkable place Gandalf found for us. Amazing to think that it is ours! Can you imagine what it will look like after the Gondorians have tidied it up? I should like to chat with them and make sure some of our things are placed in some of the rooms and that the kitchens in particular are restored, if anything.
'My, but listen to me! A meal, some good company, and something to do and think about is welcome in this odd, free time after we won. But I hope old Gandalf doesn't think he's fooled us into forgetting about Mordor. We should still very much like to go. '
'Well I suppose we really ought to have a look around, and see what we can see, hadn't we?'
'Is this considered a common home by the Big Folk around here? It is bigger than any house we ever saw in Breeland, and I dare say the whole of the Smials would fit in this one main hall!'

'This place, Bâr Thorenion, is yours by royal decree of the kingdom of Gondor. You might think this is some jest of our old friend Aragorn, but in truth it was the soldiery and the rangers of Ithilien who petitioned him that it be so.
'I have brought you here prematurely, I confess. I know not how many men will be here tomorrow to make the place somewhat more habitable. I thought, however, you should like to see it sooner, so you could make your own plans.
'It will serve as a fine residence, indeed, for the time that you dwell here in Gondor before heading back Shireward. And, with any luck, it will keep you out of trouble and away from some of your more foolish notions -- for a few days, at least, if we are lucky.
'Well, come on then. Let us step inside!'

'I don't know if either of you observed the fact, but it so happens that we have everything we need for a simple makeshift meal - beginning with this old table someone happened to leave right here.
'I know that I could use a bite to eat. What about you two?
'There are crates of food and some bottles of old wine with the seals intact. Some light, a bit of straw for a seat, and a few plates will help. If you gather those, ${PLAYER}, Merry and I will work on cups, knives, and anything else we can muster up.'

'We have talked it over and made up our minds, Merry and I - but say, before I go into all that, look around you. See what those big folk have done to the place! It's hard to believe we were just here, when it was quite an old ruin. It's no ruin now. Gandalf must have been quite desperate to turn our heads away from Mordor if he felt the need to drag us here before they'd gone to work.
'Ah, silly me! But Mordor is exactly why we wanted to talk to you. We have not abandoned the idea of going only... well... we were hoping you might ask Éomer and Aragorn on our behalf. You see, we've got some things to attend to here before we set off. And if you ask me, Merry couldn't bear to see the disappointed look on Éomer's face if he should disapprove the idea.
'Will you do it? They have both been carrying on their kingly business around the Black Gates. You will find them just outside, in the Slag Hills, I imagine.'

'A word with you, ${PLAYER}. I know well enough that I have done little to hinder Merry and Pippin an excursion into Mordor. I hope I have lent some gravity to it, however. More importantly, I would ask you to stick by them.
'On this point, I ask a favour of you. Take them into Udûn when you go, and keep a sharp eye open for things that do not belong there. I have some reason to believe you may find something of interest to you and to our two meddling friends, if you do.'

'Pippin and I have just been enjoying the view, wondering if you'd ever arrive! We might as well start on down there, I suppose. Well, no point in loitering, now. Let's be off!
'What do you say we make our way to the first cross-roads on down into the valley? You can make it out from here, only just.'

'All this wandering about in the realm of the Dark Lord is well enough, though I don't see why another troll-hole laden with Elven blades hasn't presented itself just yet. But I will not keep this up with our stomachs growling, when so many fine provisions are weighing down my pack.
'You wanted to turn northward, Merry. Why don't we head up that way and stop at that flat bit, there? It doesn't look like anyone should bother us, and we'll restore ourselves properly before moving on.'

Merry looks uncharacteristically pale.
'I have lost my appetite for food, and adventure, and any promise of treasure or gold, Pippin. Let us call it a day and head back, shall we?'
'There you are, ${PLAYER}! We had been looking for you. What happy luck that you are here now!'

'Poke their noses into Mordor? That is exactly how they put it, I imagine. Well, to be honest, I would mislike the thought of those two going in alone. But if you will promise to stay close by and look after them, then they have my blessing.
'To Pippin I do grant leave.'
'Master Merry Holdwine wishes to see Mordor? I would not deny him it, for all that he has done and been through!'

'They said yes? I knew they would! Pippin and I have packed our packs. With the help of all these friendly big folk, we are well-provisioned indeed.
'Let us meet within - what's that they call it - the Foothold in Udûn?'

'Did you hear that too? I am hardly sure of myself, but I thought I heard something... something voice-like, coming from uphill.
'Quickly and quietly, friends, let us see what it was - if it was anything at all.'
'Then our little plan is advanced? I knew we could count on you, ${PLAYER}.'
'Imagine how it must have looked with all the Dark Lord's armies gathered there.'
'To the first cross-roads - then we shall see what we shall see and decide what to do from there.'
'Which do you think we shall stumble over first, adventure or treasure?'
'No sign of either treasure or adventure here, but then I suppose we've only just started. If you ask me, we ought to head up the road and have a look at all the soldiers' tents there.'
'Think of it, ${PLAYER}. We are on the other side. The front porch of the Enemy, you might say, though I am awfully glad he isn't home, nor shall be!'
'All these empty tents only put me in mind of what horrible things war and strife are. Perhaps we should see some of the forgeworks. Let us go on a bit and look for a path heading north.'
'Well for one, I hardly imagined the noise - or the stench!'
'Well, what is it, Pippin?'
'I say we set down on that flat patch I saw, just north of the main road and behind some tents. It would be the perfect place to have a bite to eat and restore our weary limbs.'

'Well! You can see what a hard time of things we have been having, Pippin and I. Still, I worry his head may fall off of his shoulders, for how swift and how often it's been turning this way and that!'
'Will you ask permission for us? We would go ourselves only - somehow it would all be better if you would do it. Aragorn and Éomer are likely just outside the Black Gates, in the Slag Hills.'

'Pippin is joking, of course. I am not the least bit ashamed to ask, but he is. Oh, just humour him.
'And before you go, be sure to see the gardens and the baths. It is beyond remarkable, is what it is!'
'The two Periain, Meriadoc and Peregrin, were here not long past, looking for you. They returned to Bâr Thorenion, but implored that you should join them as soon as you could.'

'Yes, hrm. Well, hm. Perhaps letting him go just now would be a bit hasty, after all. I feel sorry for him at times, for I do not like to cage any creature of any temperament in stone as he is caged. And yet you have shown us that he is unbroken and might still try to do much harm if he were freed.
'No, hm. I shall not release him. Not just now, at any rate.
'I am delighted that you have paid us this visit all the same, ${PLAYER}, and you must send my regards to the halflings Pippin and Merry, and remind them that they are always welcome in my woods!'

'Hm, hoom! Here is ${PLAYER} again. Remarkable that you should show up just as we were discussing all the events that had led to this.'
Treebeard indicated the flooded waste around them.
'And what, really, should be done with Saruman. Oh, yes, I know, hm, hm, Mithrandir bade us keep him up there. And now that we have settled in, we are not in any mood to be hasty, hoom! 'Hold a moment, ${PLAYER}. I know where you have been and guess what you have learned, for I have known the truth of it myself for some little while, though through somewhat different means.
'You cannot, of course, withhold the truth from Pippin and Merry in any broad sense, but allow me to counsel you that they need not hear every painful detail you have learned.
'Think for a moment, of the many days of happiness that lie ahead, and the bitter challenge that lies in wait for them after the long road home. Does that foreknowledge bear any good? I do not think it does. Prepare them for the hard truth when they can see it with their own eyes, for that is an honest kindness, but perhaps, no more.
'Weigh my words and act on your own judgment. That is all I ask.'

'There you are! What a grave face. Tell us what you have learned. Please, I cannot take the suspense a moment more.'
Choosing your words carefully, you confirm what the two hobbits believed they knew - that the Wizard must have been Saruman and that he had designs on the Shire. You suggest more generally that the Shire they return to might not quite be the Shire as they left it, but, with the words of Gandalf ringing in your ears, can bring yourself to tell them no more.
After a long pause, Merry finally speaks.
'I see then. Those fellows worked for Saruman, then, and fled him hoping to profit from a new master. Rotten luck for rotten apples, I say! And so all those barrels of pipe-weed were for more than his own smoking habits, I take it. Still, I don't see how much harm that can do. There is only so much Hornblower farmed each season, and if too much goes missing it is sure to be noticed.
'Pippin, ${PLAYER}, can we make a pact not to burden Frodo or Sam with this? They have been through enough, and if there is trouble of some kind in the Shire, I had far rather they learn that when we get there, and not have it spoil these golden days of celebration. It shall weigh on my own heart enough, I know, though I think I shall work hard to forget about it awhile.
'And yet, I know I cannot forget about going home any longer. That I shall remember every moment from this time forward, I am afraid.'

'I have word that Masters Peregrin and Meriadoc wish to speak with you, ${PLAYER}. It has something to do with Mordor, though I know nothing more of the matter. They will, of course, be found in Bâr Thorenion.'
'Pippin, you explain.'
A look of abject misery and fear is etched across the half-orc's lifeless face. Signs of a struggle on the ground about him clearly show marks of both pursuer and pursued, bearing roughly east.
'${PLAYER}! There you are. Do you have a moment? We have been discussing Mordor.'

'I have an idea. Gather the men from around camp, and some kegs of ale. Then, meet me back here. We will celebrate one last time before we march bravely into the Enemy's maw.'
'Well, my spirits are certainly lifted! We will march to our destiny with a song in our hearts. For Gondor and for all the Free Peoples. I think Forlong would not be ashamed of us, ${PLAYER}.'
'Thank you, ${PLAYER}. The men and ale are gathered. Here goes nothing.'
Take Heart, Men of Gondor

'Ah, what a strange lichen... it is both flaky and damp at once.
'Those properties seem ideal for its use as a poison, but I wonder how it might be used in combination with other flora from these lands and from the lands of Ithilien.
'I shall think on this for a time, ${PLAYER}. In the meantime, I have another task for you.'

'If your journeys in the Wastes take you beyond the edges of the battered road eastward, I would be pleased if you could find for me a sample of Trollstrife. That is the name of the lichen we sought, and according to Worts and Weeds, it seems to grow on the trunks of the few trees that remain in the Wastes.
'Even one sample will do, but please, do be careful! Do not handle it with your bare hands!

'Ah, perhaps a minute was too long! Look, the slag-water has eaten right through the planting box...

'I do not know if the Wastes can ever truly be healed, but I am certain they cannot while the Enemy still looms ahead. Go, rejoin your company. I shall tend to these and see them safely transported away from these lands.
'If you ever find yourself in Minas Tirith again after this war, I am certain I shall have much to tell you!'

'Ah, wonderful!
'Now then, I'll add a splash of this sickly water you brought to one of them and we can observe the results.'
Mílgamel walks to the central planting box and upends the phial of slag-water.

'That's right, ${PLAYER}... we are going to try to cross-breed the plants of the Wastes with those of Ithilien.
'Even if the Wastes never recover, we can save their unique plants and grow them within Ithilien if they are of need to us.
'I have set three planting boxes around this chamber, and I would first have you fill half of them with soil you gathered from the battle plain. I have already filled one half of each with soil from Ithilien. Next, you should plant my samples of Oxlip, Vetchling, and Horsetail alongside these hardy mushrooms you discovered.
'This way we shall see if they can live alongside one another in each variety of soil.
'I may still have a use for the slag-water you brought me, but that can wait...'

'While I work with the trollstrife you recovered for me, I would have you explore the Wastes further.

'Search the lands surrounding Haerondir for samples of soil and mushrooms if you would.
'If I have need of the good, I shall also have need of the very worst the Wastes has to offer us... so collect a small phial of water from the run-off surrounding the Slag-hills to the east.

'${PLAYER}, I am glad you have returned to us. Yet, I must disagree with the course Artamir and you have taken. Such reckless actions could have led the Enemy to Haerondir or endangered the entire host, but they have not... and for that I am grateful.
'Do not mistake my concern for anger, my friend, but I would urge you to dissuade Artamir from any other adventures he might think to embark upon. Given the length of your absence, have you returned with any news of our foes?'
You inform Anborn of the designs of the Black Númenórean, Burudagath the Bloodletter, and warn him against possible encounters with more hostile fell spirits upon the battle plain.
'These are grim tidings, and they are made all the worse by the looming battle. I shall do what I can to prepare us should these evils come to Haerondir. As for you, my friend, I have a new task - one with which Artamir shall not be involved.'

Haerondir can be found to the south of Ondoher's Folly in Dagorlad.

'I have outstayed my welcome in these lands, I think. I have found my mind unsettled and my thoughts drawn to my own death.
'This is no place for one such as me, ${PLAYER}. Twice you have helped me to realize my own peril, and I hope I shall not have need of a third opportunity.
'As much as I desire to spend more time speaking with Faramir of his life, our duties are to the Host of the West - and it is my duty to no longer impede them.
'All we have learned of the foes we now face... it goes beyond my knowledge and beyond my skill. Those we left behind at Haerondir, though... they could stand against them. Let us return there and tell them of what we have learned!
'I shall ride as swiftly as I am able, and I would ask that you do the same. Without your voice, I fear they shall not heed my warnings....'

'You have returned to us so late, ${PLAYER}, and I am afraid you have much to answer for in the eyes of captain Anborn. Artamir's errand may have endangered our entire cause, and for what? The chance to speak to a spirit?
'His foolishness may cost us more than time. You see, we returned to Haerondir after you departed and spoke to Anborn of your efforts to rescue Artamir from his delusions. He thought long on the matter and then chose his course. You must understand, my friend, Anborn sent an entire company to find you and Artamir on the battle plain. You have returned, but we have heard naught from them....'
You express regret at the effort put forth to ensure your return, but urge Laeglaw to understand that you have come with grave tidings about the foes lurking in Dagorlad and the coming battle with the Dark Lord at the Black Gate.
'I see, but Anborn has requested your presence at once upon your return, so I leave those matters to him.'

'Ah! Let us hope we have freed the last of those held in the Wastes, ${PLAYER}! I mourn for those we were too late to save, but I hold hope that the Dark Lord shall soon suffer the fate he deserves for these atrocities.
'I do not doubt the Enemy still keeps many slaves beyond the Black Gate, but we must look to the battle ahead before we can aid them.

'The Fane of Screaming... what a vile name for a place of such sorrow for the people of Gondor.
'I have heard tales told by Aragorn of the king of old, Ondoher, and the fate that travelled far to meet him in these lands. I believe that is a tale better told by Artamir - and in less pressing times. Suffice it to say, a king of Númenórean blood laid low by the Enemy's servants is not soon to be forgotten. They have twisted the loss of Gondor into a monument to their own Master.
'It is clear that these Orcs have defiled the hill and I fear many of the Dark Lord's prisoners have met their end on its summit - and without the mercy of a swift death. Even in war-time, and with a great battle looming, I cannot abandon those that still remain to such a fate.
'I could not forgive myself for turning away from their pain, ${PLAYER}, and I believe Aragorn would consider this the proper course as well.
'Travel to Ondoher's Folly, and free all of the prisoners you can find. I shall keep watch for your return, my friend!'

The spear can be found somewhere in the southern reaches of the Dead Marshes.
Faramir has asked you to seek the Wainrider spear that slew him in the Dead Marshes in the hope that it might grant you passage into Dol Acharn.
Search the Dead Marshes for the spear that slew Faramir

'I have looked upon the faces of the Wainriders at Dol Acharn, and though many of them are lost to my memory - one has never been forgotten. It is the face of their chieftain - the face of the man who slew me!
'Even now, I remember facing down the Wainrider chieftain with the north-men. All at once, it felt as if each of us stood alone in the battle against him and his kin. After his horse and chariot became stranded in the marshes, he ran me down himself and I could not flee in the shallows. The mud and murk held my feet and soon he was upon me. I fell, and the blood of the king's line spilled into the marshes. My folly had grown a terrible defeat into no less than a disaster for my people.
'His spear tasted the blood of Númenor, and he knew the victory he had won over Gondor could not be contested by any Man. Such a triumph grew a great arrogance within him, and as your friend Artamir told us, his death soon followed.
'You must gain an audience with the Wainrider chieftain if our ruse is to succeed, but it seems you shall find no such kindness without bearing a trinket of their peoples.
'I would have you seek the very spear that slew me in the marshes to the north. It is unlikely they will yield even once you bear it, but it is the only means we have to speak to their master.'

'Yes, ${PLAYER}... that is the one.
'It is rotted and rusted with the passage of time, but it can be no other. I can feel the spear piercing my chest anew even now...
'This pain... it cannot stop me now. It is time our ruse is tested! Let us see if the chieftain's weapon of old might be wielded against him, ${PLAYER}!'
Blood of Númenor
