'At least Débel did not allow my brother's home to fall into disrepair....'
Dori glances around Nori's home and pauses upon a stack of papers piled on the dining table.
'I think my brother left more hastily than he expected to, ${PLAYER}. Look!
'There are papers piled upon the table, and I see other curiosities left about that I would like to examine. Take a look at those papers and see if my brother has left any hint of his course or the names of other dwarves that we might question.
'Once you have done that, let us meet back here.'

'My brother believes that because the great cold-drake was defeated that our old hoards lay unguarded? By dragons, perhaps, but the Orcs will not have abandoned them.
'As the King under the Mountain said, Thikil-gundu is best forgotten. The Longbeards have found only misfortune and death in the Steel Keep. If I do not aid my brother, this expedition will be his doom.
'We are forbidden from travelling to Thikil-gundu, but perhaps King Thorin will be merciful upon my family and allow me to pursue him into the Ered Mithrin. It is the only course!
'Come, we must go at once!'
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTE: When you continue this quest, you will swiftly travel to the Hall under the Mountain.</rgb>

'Did I not say I was a dwarf of my word?
'I knew very little of the plans of the Keeper of the Coffers, but I knew enough. He made for the Steel Keep of old... Thikil-gundu as it was once named in the tongue of the dwarves.
'I could not follow him as he wished, but I offered to keep his home in order until his return. I have borne Nori's secret faithfully, but I do not wish to lose the favour of the King under the Mountain.
'Here, take this key. Perhaps Nori left behind some clue for his brother to find....'

'I do not appreciate your gaze. What business have you in the New-lodes?'
You explain to the dwarf that he matches the description of a dwarf Dori believed to be in league with Nori's secret expedition. The dwarf lets out a long sigh.
'Very well... I am Débel. I am not so deeply involved as you might believe, but yes, I know of these things. I suppose the truth would come out sooner or later, but I had hoped it would be after Nori returned to Erebor.
'I cannot give such information freely, but I can offer it for a trifle. If you were to clear out some of the deep-claws that have burrowed into the New-lodes, I give my word that I will share all I know of Nori and his expedition.
'What do you say?'

'You found the dwarf, did you? Very good! What did he have to say of my brother?'
You explain to Dori that Débel did not offer much in the way of new information, but he did offer up the key to Nori's home.
'A key? My brother entrusted his key to this Débel before me? We shall have much to discuss when next I see him!
'My brother was not one to leave things unorganised... he is the Keeper of the Coffers after all! However, if Nori has travelled to Thikil-gundu, I must know his course through the Ered Mithrin. They are unfriendly lands, now home only to Orcs and dragons.
'It is to Tumnu-dûm we must go. Those are the dwelling-halls of Erebor, and it is there Nori makes his home.
'I will await you outside his home. After all, you have the key!'

'You have the spare key, yes?
'Let us see what my brother left behind, ${PLAYER}. I hope it is of some use to us....'

Dori seems fixated upon the King under the Mountain and barely seems to notice your approach.
'King Thorin III Stonehelm, King under the Mountain, I beg leave to travel into the Ered Mithrin. You have forbidden Durin's Folk to return to the Steel Keep, Thikil-gundu, but that is not my purpose. I go in search of my brother, Nori!
'I am a loyal dwarf of Erebor. I have fought and bled in its defence... from the Easterlings... from Bolg! All I ask is the chance to save Nori from his folly!
'Will you grant me leave, King under the Mountain?'

'I hear your words, Dori of the Company.
'Your deeds and those of your kin are not forgotten to any who dwell in Erebor, but Nori has acted in defiance of my edict. Whether his expedition is successful or not, there will be consequences for him.
'I know well that your brother, Ori, was among those lost in Balin's expedition, and I know as well as you do that this bears a resemblance to our efforts to reclaim Khazad-dûm. Both Balin's expedition and the Iron Garrison have failed, and if future losses may still be prevented, they must be. And so, Dori, I grant you leave to follow your brother and put an end to his expedition.
'You will travel on my behalf, but you will go in secret as your brother did. You may form a company of your own choosing, but do not spread word of this to any untrustworthy ears. In addition, I ask that you find the remains of Vethúg Wintermind. He flew from battle gravely wounded and passed into the Ered Mithrin, but I desire proof of his death.
'Heed my words. Deliver Nori from his folly and retrieve for me a bone of Vethúg Wintermind. Only then will we speak of forgiveness....'

'You have my truest gratitude, King under the Mountain. I will do as you have commanded.'
Dori turns to you.
'What do you say, ${PLAYER}? Let us begin our preparations!'
After countless hours of study, Nori learned that the hoarding-vault laid 'beneath the eyes of the Seven'...
After clearing the dust away, Nori drew forth his armour of old. The time had come!
Dori looks around the empty home of his brother...
Thikil-gundu was lost, Nori thought, but it was not the way of dragons to abandon their hoards...
Thikil-gundu had once possessed great wealth, Nori thought, and now it sat unguarded and unclaimed...
Dori shifts uncomfortably outside Nori's home...
After Vethúg's defeat at the gates of Erebor, Nori enlisted his kinsfolk to follow him to Thikil-gundu...
The earth shakes as a deep-claw bursts forth!

'I do not understand, ${PLAYER}.
'What has compelled my brother to act so foolishly? He has lived a life of wealth in Erebor! He is the Keeper of the Coffers! Or he was....
'Bah! I should have confronted him. I saw dwarves speaking with him in hushed tones, but I thought nothing of it. Nori is a dwarf of some repute, after all.
'If only I knew the names of those dwarves, but... wait. I do recall one of them. This dwarf seemed to be of a line descended from both the Longbeards and the Zhélruka of the East. He was thin in the beard, but any dwarf would be proud to have such a moustache.
'He is a miner, I think. Search for him in the New-lodes of Narathâk, and perhaps he will be better able to explain why my brother has left for Thikil-gundu.'

'So Vethúg has fallen upon Winterstith....
'If what the Zhélruka say is true, Nori has already passed beyond the easternmost mountains to Skarháld, but Winterstith lies not far to the north. From what you have told me, Vethúg must have carved a path of frozen ruin through the foothills of the Ered Mithrin as he fell. Ah, but where does it lead? To Winterstith? To the heart of the Anvil itself? We must find out!
'Come, ${PLAYER}. Let us follow the Bitter Scar to its end and see what we discover!'

'We have arrived, ${PLAYER}. It may be named Skarháld in the Common Tongue, but I know it as Tharrazhâr.
'I know well the history of Tharrazhâr, but I must appear to be an old dwarf, frail of mind, to Ingór and his kinsfolk... at least for now. These walls of stone and azurite... they were wrought by Longbeards! Though I cannot contest it, these Zhélruka have no claim to this fortress.
'I have seen more unfriendly glances fall upon our Stout-axe companions, and so, I think we should press on once we have rested.
'Yet, I have not forgotten that Zádokh Flint-eye spoke of a company of Longbeards in Tharrazhâr. He may have spoken half-truths of Vethúg Wintermind, but who can say what will we find here?'
'It is time, ${PLAYER}. Let us see where the old cold-drake has come to rest.'

'Ah, why have you come to Ravenhill?'
You open the chest of gold and gem-stones before Arcah, and explain that Dori has offered a share of his treasure in exchange for the aid of the ravens.
'Aid of what sort, ${RACE}? These glimmering trinkets and baubles please me, but I would know what is to be promised if I offer our aid.'
You explain that Dori's brother has taken an expedition to the Ered Mithrin in secret and seeks for Thikil-gundu, the Steel Keep.
'That is an accursed place, ${PLAYER}. You may send three of my conspiracy into the Grey Mountains to search for Nori and his kinsfolk, but I will allow none to fly too near the Steel Keep.
'I have spoken.'

'It is time, ${PLAYER}.
'Our preparations are made, our goats are watered and well-rested, but one matter still remains.'
Dori gestures at the massive chest of gold and gem-stones before him.
'This is but a small measure of my share of the treasure reclaimed from Smaug the Golden, and it is still greater wealth than most dwarves will ever know.
'I want you to deliver it to Ravenhill, ${PLAYER}. The raven-chief, Arcah, and her people are fond of all that glimmers, and if her people would aid me in the search for my brother, I offer it all. I do not know if I could deliver it by my own hand, and so, I ask this of you.
'Once you have finished this business at Ravenhill, follow the long road beneath its heights into the Ered Mithrin. The Company shall await you along the road.'

'Ah, ${PLAYER}! It is done, then? Very good.
'I have known the raven-chiefs to be wise counselors, but whether their counsel is good or ill, they speak with sharp tongues. Has the raven-chief offered you any counsel on our task?'
You inform Dori that the raven-chief warned that Thikil-gundu was an accursed place, and that she would not send her ravens there.
'Accursed? I do not think so, ${PLAYER}. Thikil-gundu has been the doom of many Longbeards, but there is no curse upon it! A curse of dragon-kind, perhaps... but nothing more.
'That is enough talk of Thikil-gundu for now, I think. Let us hope the ravens find some sign of my brother's passage through the Ered Mithrin.'

'Very good, ${PLAYER}.
'After dusk, we will gather before the gates of Erebor and begin our journey into the Ered Mithrin under the cover of darkness.
'If you have any unfinished business in Erebor, I would see to it. The hour soon approaches!'

'Humph!
'Of all the dwarves I hoped to gather, I have found only four. I spoke first to the dwarves I travelled with on the quest of old to the Lonely Mountain, but only Bofur and Glóin have agreed to join us. Bifur offered no reason for his refusal, but I do not doubt he has seen enough of battle. As for the others, Dwalin must tend to his duties at Thorin's Hall in the Ered Luin, and I would not ask Bombur or the fine dwarves who bear him about to make such a journey.
'Ah, but the elder of the Stout-axes, the one named Spakorth... he is a keen dwarf! I spoke to him of our task in the Ered Mithrin, and he offered two of his finest warriors to me. Náth and Dréri are young in the years of dwarves, but if the wisdom of my kinsfolk should fail us, the might of the Stout-axes will deliver us from trouble.
'I have spoken enough of such things! You have gathered what I asked, and now you should prepare six packs. One for each of the dwarves of the Company, and one for my brother, Nori, for when he is found.
'Once that is done, return to me.'
Arcah casts an inquisitive gaze in your direction...

'Very well!
'I am not the young dwarf I once was, ${PLAYER}, but I am hale still in my old age, so I will lead the Company. However, I must find those willing to follow me into the Ered Mithrin for no promise of wealth or glory beyond my own gratitude. I know a few dwarves whom I can trust with such a task, and so I will speak to them myself.
'Ah, but such a company need not only be comprised of dwarves. After all, old Mr. Baggins was not a dwarf and he proved an invaluable ally of Durin's Folk. You are a strong ${RACE}, well-travelled and skilled in the ways of battle. Will you join me?'
You nod in assent.
'Good, good! We shall have need of a great many things in our travels, and so I would ask that you gather as many coils of rope, water-skins, and bedrolls as you can bear. Once you have done that, you should meet me and the others in Nori's home. Let us hope it is enough!
'Are we understood, ${PLAYER}? Swiftly now!'

'The air is thin up here, they all said it. You might be able to see further than in the low-lands, but the thin air makes it harder to hear sounds from far away, especially with the wind whistling among the rocks the way it does. My hands are covered in scratches, but at least I kept my eyes! For now, anyway, for now! Cursed birds!
'I will give a reward to any who slay the grey hawks of the Ered Mithrin, especially the largest and foulest of them. Keenclaw I have named him. He will never have my eyes, no matter how much he desires to dine upon them!'

'Did you know, kízinek, that river and stream hold secrets to what lies hidden under stone?

'Welcome, ${CLASS}. We are strangers here, among these strange dwarves. I have followed them at King Thorin's behest, as perhaps you have, too, to keep a wary eye upon all they do.
'Only now I have come not so much to fear what they do as to fear for them. They have stubbornly insisted on making camp among these ruins. They busy themselves with building anew, and seem little to fear for the many, many things around, above, and below that might do them harm. Have they no memory? No tales of what once dwelled here and made war with dwarves of their line and ours?
'Will you go about and patrol the look-outs of Skarháld, ${PLAYER}? It would put me greatly at ease.'

'We poor Zhélruka have travelled far, farther than you can imagine, only to reach Erebor. Here the way is harder and harsher than ever. I will linger here and tend to my brethren as they come through.

The bounty notice is written on coarse paper. It reads:
'I thought it was a tree at first, but what tree could exude such menace? It was more troll than tree, if you want this dwarf's opinion. What do you do with a thing like that? Chop it down? Stack it for lumber? I don't know.
'What I do know is that something should be done about it. I offer a reward for anyone who can uproot some of these wood-trolls from the Ered Mithrin. If you see the worst of the lot, the one that folk of these high places call Grazadhrú, be sure to give him your special attention. I don't like trees at the best of times, but these wood-trolls make for the worst of times, if you ask me!'

'Let us follow these Zhélruka to Skarháld, ${PLAYER}, but speak not of our true purpose.'

'Listen to me, ${PLAYER}.'
Dori's voice drops to a whisper.
'Do not think I chose my words to make a fool of myself. This Prince seems wiser than his kinsfolk, but I do not trust these Zhélruka.
'If they make for Dómekh then they make for Thikil-gundu, and the Zhélruka do not share the spoils of delving and war. If Ingór was to learn that our path also leads to the Steel Keep, I do not think we would find him so friendly much longer.
'I believe the only way this can be settled without the spilling of dwarf-blood is to accept Ingór's offer of passage to Skarháld.'

'Rust... and rime. It is as I feared, ${PLAYER}.
'Was Vethúg slain by Karazgar's hand or did the Weeping Warrior find some crueler purpose for the great cold-drake?'
Dori glances at the damaged remains of the bloodied, black arrow.
'If Vethúg Wintermind lives still, he will not have forgotten the hurts done to him by the Longbeards and Bardings....
'We must go.'

'I do not like the look of this....
'Either we have been deceived by the Zhélruka or Vethúg was not as wounded as he appeared to be! There is no mistaking that Vethúg tore this rift in the foothills of Winterstith, but it is where he has gone that concerns me!
'Do you see these marks in the earth? I first thought nothing of them, but there are signs of battle here among the fallen stones of Winterstith! Unless the great cold-drake battled only against rocks and ice as they fell, some other foe must have come to this place. I know few who could withstand the might of Vethúg Wintermind, and so, I fear this is the work of Karazgar!
'Perhaps you can uncover the truth of what has happened here, ${PLAYER}.'
A company of Zhélruka blocks the way!
Ingór crosses his arms and waits for Dori's response...
You are able to free a bloodied, black arrow from the frozen earth...
Only Karazgar, the Weeping Warrior, could have left this behind...
Shards of ice litter the ground, betraying a final, futile struggle by Vethúg Wintermind...

Talk to Dori at Skarháld

'You have done us a great service, ${PLAYER}. I wish I could offer you more in return, but I have told you all there is to tell!
'Nori and his company continued onward to Thikil-gundu without us, but not long after, the Zhélruka arrived....'
Órug pauses for a moment and gazes into the fire.
'I have known the Zhélruka to embellish their tales, but there are often hints of truth within them.
'There are many Zhélruka in Skarháld... perhaps a few among them will have the answers you seek!'

'What have you learned, ${PLAYER}?'
You inform Dori that only a few Longbeards remain in Skarháld and that Nori and the rest of his expedition followed the Men Angrún to Thikil-gundu. You also inform Dori that the Zhélruka made mention of Karazgar, Vethúg Wintermind, and strange dwarves wandering in the night.
'Strange dwarves? The Zhélruka have called the Longbeards many things in many tongues, but I have never known them to call us strange. I wonder what the truth of that tale could be....
'If Nori and his expedition have travelled to Thikil-gundu by way of the Men Angrún, he will have passed through Óinsbridge. It is there we must go!'

'I never thought to see Tharrazhâr with my own eyes....'
Dori looks around and appears lost in thought for a moment.
'Long ago, these mountains were rich and little explored, ${PLAYER}, but in his wisdom, Thorin I reshaped them into the Dwarf-kingdom of Grárik. It flourished for a time and great wealth was found beneath the peaks of the Grey Mountains, but that very wealth proved the doom of Grárik. Drawn by a powerful greed, it was the dragons of the wastes beyond that laid siege to Grárik. First fell Ablâk-khadar, the Stormwall, and its forges were extinguished. Second fell Tharrazhâr, and its keep was shattered. Third fell Aglâmbazar, the great Glimmerdeep, and it was there Smaug the Golden made his lair. Last fell Thikil-gundu, the Steel Keep and seat of Grárik, and I need not name the great cold-drake who slew King Dáin I and his son, Frór, along with countless others. The Dwarf-kingdom of Grárik was no more.
'I tell you this so you understand, ${PLAYER}. Tharrazhâr... bah, Skarháld, belongs to Durin's Folk!
'Are there any other Longbeards here in the remnants of Grárik? If Zádokh Flint-eye has not spoken true, gold will be the least of his troubles.'

Talk to Órug

'${PLAYER}....
'How have you come to be in this place? Does my mind now play tricks upon me?'
You inform Órug that you have come to the Grey Mountains with Dori and Company in search of Nori and his expedition.
'It has been many days since last we saw Nori and the rest of his expedition. Before we came to Tharrazhâr, the expedition was beset by Orcs of Gundabad. The Orcs were slain to the last, but a few of our number sustained grave wounds in the battle. It was decided that we would remain behind in Tharrazhâr and work to rebuild it as it was in the time of Grárik. After we restored the first hall of the keep, I saw that a small company of Zhélruka had arrived. At first, I thought nothing of it, but then more arrived... and more... and more out of the East. They must number in the hundreds now! There has been little talk between our peoples, but we have at least agreed to put aside our separate tongues. It is Skarháld now... not Tharrazhâr or Brúgrad!
'And so it has been! I wish there was more to be told, but I know only that Nori and his expedition continued to the south along the Men Angrún. It is the most well-travelled path to Thikil-gundu, but it was the work of Angmar... and even now, it is often travelled by the foes of the Longbeards.
'I have done my best to tend the wounds of my kinsfolk, but I am no healer. All I know is that a warm meal and a hot fire would do much to aid us!'

'${PLAYER}! I feared you would not return!
'When Ingór returned in your stead, he spoke of... wights that clawed and hewed his company. That is not the work of dragons! What devilry is afoot in Thikil-gundu?'
You tell Dori that none of the newly-slain Longbeards or Zhélruka remained to be found in the Grey Wrack.
'Where have they gone? Where has my brother gone?'
You hand Nori's axe to Dori, and his face sinks.
'No... no!'

'Hmmph! There is no comfort to be found in this place, but it will have to do. At least we are sheltered from the wind!
'Alas, there was little room for the goats atop Stánbalk, so Náth has stabled them below as best he can. If this snowstorm does not soon relent, they ought to try growing their winter coats!
'Let me see if my eyes do not fail me...'
Dori gazes into the Grey Wrack, squinting as flakes of snow become entangled in his eyebrows and beard.
'I see the blurred shapes you described, ${PLAYER}, but I cannot say who or what they might be. You are a hardy ${CLASS}, my friend. Will you descend into the Grey Wrack and find out?
'If they are dwarves, they might belong to Nori's expedition. If they are not, well... it is better to know what lies before us, I think!'

'Malek... Vozdo... all of them... dead! Why... why have you come here, ${PLAYER}?'
You tell Ingór that Dori's brother, Nori, made for Thikil-gundu. Ingór laughs weakly and grimaces. You notice several fresh gashes in his armour.
'So that... was the Longbeards' plan... eh? They can have it! Dómekh... is cursed! The Steel Keep is lost! It is not the drakes you should fear, ${CLASS}... for the Dead walk again! They have slain all in their path... Zhélruka... Longbeards... none have escaped but me!
'What am I to do now? Return to my people... as a coward? Beg the mercy of my own brother?'
You do not answer Ingór's questions, but you tell him that Dori and Company have made camp atop Stánbalk.
'Perhaps I will go to them, but... I beg you... do as I ask. Many Longbeards and Zhélruka lie slain before the Steel Keep... but that is no resting place for a dwarf! When the dwarves fought as one at Azanulbizar long ago, so many were the slain that they could not be borne away to the tombs of our peoples. And so, they were... burned... to spare them any indignity in death.
'Will you do this for my people, ${PLAYER}? Will you do this for the Longbeards? If the Dead seek to stop you, let them join the others as burned dwarves!'
'Go!'

'After all these years, it is unchanged....
'When Vethúg Wintermind froze the Steel Keep and made it his lair, the lands surrounding Thikil-gundu were shrouded in winter. Grárik, the Grey Realm, was ended. All that remained was the Grey Wrack. I had thought in time these lands would heal, but it is not so.'
Dori looks sorrowfully at the bones scattered before Stánbalk.
'Stánbalk was once the greatest defence of Thikil-gundu, and now... it stands watch over the dead.
'I think it unwise to press on without scouting Stánbalk. There may be more unseen dangers lurking ahead!
'Scale the remains of Stánbalk, ${PLAYER}, and look into the lands of the Grey Wrack.
'If you deem it safe, we shall make camp atop it!'

'What did you spy from Stánbalk, ${PLAYER}?'
You tell Dori that you did not encounter any foes near to the wall, but you noticed blurred shapes moving in the distance.
'It is strange that we have seen so few drakes this near to Thikil-gundu. If the Steel Keep remained the lair of Vethúg Wintermind since the time of Dáin, I would have expected more of his brood to lurk in the foothills of the Wrathhorn. Ah, but who am I to question a moment of good fortune? Perhaps my brother was right after all!
'I think we should make camp atop Stánbalk. Even if we are fortunate enough to encounter none of Vethúg's brood, the path to Thikil-gundu is still treacherous.

Dori asks the raven if it has seen any sign of Nori or his expedition. The raven croaks and chitters in answer. All of a sudden, the raven spreads its wings and looses a shrill cry.

'These are not glad tidings, ${PLAYER}. Nori is nowhere to be found, and two of the three ravens sent to search for my brother have become lost in the Grey Mountains. The ravens have spied black-arrows of Gundabad lying in wait beyond the forest, and they have fletched their arrows with the feathers of ravens! It is also said they are practised in the art of stealth, but I have not known many Orcs to possess such patience. If we are to reach Thikil-gundu, we shall have to remain on guard.

'I cannot atone for what I have done, ${PLAYER}. I have disobeyed the King under the Mountain, I have deceived my brother... and for what? Naught, I say!
'Even the gold we found is no boon to my people! There is a curse upon Thikil-gundu... and nothing in the halls of the Steel Keep has gone untouched by it!
'Once I was renowned among Durin's Folk... a hero of the Lonely Mountain! Am I now to be known as the foolish, old dwarf who dreamt of treasures lost?
'No... I will not let this be the end of it!'

'Our journey is over, ${PLAYER}... at least for the moment!
'Nori thinks himself a disgraced dwarf, but these hurts will heal in time! He has adventured as few dwarves have in their lives! Was I disappointed in my brother? Was I fearful that he had led himself to certain doom? Of course I was! But... he is my brother! Even if the King under the Mountain will not forgive Nori as I have, this will not be the end of our adventures!
'There is a fire in the hearts of Durin's Folk! An unquenchable flame! And you have proven yourself among us, my friend.
'We have forced Karazgar out of Thikil-gundu, and that is enough! Even so, there is some unseen evil lurking in our delving of old... and many questions linger in my mind.
'But this day, we honour the lost here among the halls of Tharrazhâr!'

I have felt many eyes upon us here, and I fear that my attempt at deception has not gone unnoticed. And so, I would have you tell Ingór that I seek my brother, Nori. It is the truth, and it should put his mind at ease. I seek not for wealth or glory... only for my lost kin.
'When that is done, ride for Óinsbridge. It is there we will reunite and take our next rest.
'Óinsbridge lies to the south beyond the forest, but the Thornholt is home to many dangers. Do not stray from the dark road!'

'It is good to see you again, ${PLAYER}.
'I do hope my kinsfolk have held their tongues in regards to your Kámbrada companions. From what Dori has told me, Náth and Dréri and the rest of their kinsfolk knew great hardship in Mordor before they came to dwell in the Lonely Mountain. Enough hardship, I think, that mere insults would do naught to wound them. Perhaps I am not so resilient, but I find the greatest insult to be dishonesty.
'Tell me, ${PLAYER}. Have you had any luck in finding heirlooms of the Longbeards or have you come to tell me the truth of Dori's little expedition? What is it you truly seek?'
You tell Ingór of Dori's lost brother, Nori, who travelled into the Grey Mountains against the will of his kin and the King under the Mountain.
'I see. Perhaps I have judged Dori too hastily....
'There is a byword among the Zhélruka. Its true meaning cannot be shared, but it speaks of one who is governed by a doomed obsession. Those unlucky few \qseek the Citadel\q. For Dori's sake, I hope his brother does not seek the Citadel.
'You may go, ${PLAYER}. May you find Nori before death or madness takes him.'

'At last, we have come to Óinsbridge.
'It is a fine respite from the gloom of the Thornholt, but the western reaches of the forest still lie ahead of us. If Nori and his expedition took rest here, it is likely that some sign of their passage has been left behind. And so, I have asked the others to search for signs of the expedition, ${PLAYER}. Would you join them?
'Oh, and do not be afraid to cross to the other side of the Forest River! The bridge may have fallen into disrepair, but it is still sturdy enough to bear the weight of a few dwarves and a ${RACE}, I think!'

The Anvil of Winterstith

'${PLAYER}! Was that blast from Hrímil Frost-heart herself? You tricked her into sealing herself inside! We seem to be safe for now. It will take some time for her to claw her way through all of that ice. What of Karazgar? Did you find him?'
You explain that Vethúg was slain, but you are unsure of the fate of Karazgar. He failed to sway Hrímil to his side, and was attacked by her, but you found evidence that he survived and escaped.
'Escaped?! Could he have slipped by us while we were fighting the drakes? That sneaky cur! If that is the case, we must find him, and bring him to justice once and for all!
'As for you, you have more than earned the gratitude of the Zhélruka clan. Go, rest, feast, be well. We will call for you when we find him!'

'Karazgar and his drake were spotted flying north, to the Withered Heath. He must be heading towards the Anvil of Winterstith!
'This is terrible, ${PLAYER}. The Anvil is crawling with frost drakes, and we know that it has reopened. If Karazgar adds their number to his forces, he will be unstoppable, and if the rumours are true, the Herald of Winter herself may be there!
'Wait, who is that? Did you bring someone with you?'

'What do those Longbeards and Stout-axes want? Why have they come?'
You explain that the Longbeards have their own score to settle with Vethúg Wintermind, and the Stout-axes would like to go to the Anvil on their behalf.
'Hmph. I have no love for those vépro-vlasa Kambrada, but if you personally vouch for them, I will allow it. You have done enough for the Zhélruka clan that I trust your judgment. You had best prepare them; if the Herald of Winter is there, we travel into the jaws of death herself!
'If you are brave enough to face what may lie inside the Anvil, gather your forces, and meet us there.'
<rgb=#FF0000>The Anvil of Winterstith 12-player instance is now available in the Instance Finder. </rgb>
Word has reached you that Karazgar is on the move, and the Zhélruka in Skarháld are concerned he may return soon. Hórin is leading a company to investigate, and has asked for you by name.

'${PLAYER}, I see my call has reached your ears! Good!
'The time has come to prove you are a true friend to the Zhélruka. Inek has tasked me with leading a hunting party, and I want you among its members. Our prey: The Weeping Warrior! His attack against Skarháld must not go unanswered. And, we must not wait for him to gather his strength and return as he so promised! No, we will find him, and we will disrupt his plans now, or we may as well abandon our plans in these mountains.
'One of my scouts has sent word that he was seen, and so we will follow. I will leave shortly for the Wyrmgap with what warriors I can gather. Meet me there.'

'${PLAYER}! You live! Dréri and Náth just returned. We could hear the great roar of the dragon from here! Tell us everything!'
You tell Nori of the death of Vethúg, Karazgar's failed plan and escape, and the fury of Hrímil Frost-heart. You pull the bone from your bags and hand it to him. He looks at it in awe.
'Hah! If only my old bones could have fought along side you. The minstrels will surely sing songs of that for years to come! And thank you for this! King Thorin will be pleased to hear of the end of that drake. The Herald of Winter, however....'
Nori's expression turns grim.
'Sealing herself inside the Anvil has only bought us so much time. She is a dragon of the ancient days, with power to rival Smaug himself. Perhaps even surpassing him! Erebor and the kingdoms of the North will not be able to ignore such a threat for long. We will have to come up with a plan to deal with this threat, and when we do, I am sure that we will call for your aid, hero.'

'${PLAYER}, we followed as quickly as we could when we heard you were going to track down Karazgar with the Zhélruka. I would ask a favour of you.'
Nori looks slightly uneasy and hesitates before speaking again.
'As you know, we failed in the task given to us by King Thorin. We were unable to bring down that cursed drake Vethúg Wintermind when we encountered him in Thikil-gundu. I... I blame myself for this. If Dori and the others had not come, I would surely have perished in that ancient keep. If you are going to face him and Karazgar, I ask that you do what we could not, and bring back a bone from Vethúg's broken corpse.'
He looks to his brother. Dori nods.
'I am shamed to ask this of you, as Dori and I have decided our adventuring days are behind us. Please, do this for us, so we may return to Erebor with honour.'

'Those old Longbeards do not speak for us. Dréri and I would be glad to travel with you into the Anvil. The glory of facing Karazgar and the monstrous drakes within awaits!
'This is the perfect opportunity to repay Durin's Folk for their kindness, and try to make peace with the Zhélruka clan. Ah, but I fear they may need some convincing. Perhaps if you speak to them on our behalf, they will allow us to join their company.'

Stolen Sweets
'Why, this is my favourite! Oh, thank you. Thank you!'
'Is that for me? It is? Hurrah!'
'Oh, thank you, ${CLASS}.'
'Thank you so much!'
'A warm drink! I will share this with the others. Perhaps they will share their sweets with me.'
'I have never had one of these. Is it as delicious as it looks? Well, if I do not like it, perhaps I can trade with one of the others.'

'We heard all about it, traveller. About the Eagle as great as a horse, and someone was going to find all the sweets and bring them back. I am sorry, we did not believe it was true.
'But look, we were mistaken, and now I am so happy!'
'Please, good traveller. Visit the snowy realms of Middle-earth and recover the treats. They are hot cross buns, plum pudding, gingerbread, peppermint treats, a flask of wassail, and fruit cake.'

'Good traveller, I must enlist your aid. One of the Great Eagles was bearing a sack of sweets from far-off Gondor hither to Winter-home. Alas! The bag was rent, and the sweets fell from it as she flew.
'She realized her mistake only as the last sweet fell, and with her keen eyes watched as wintry beasts seized it and ran off into the snow. She had flown among the cold and snowy regions of Middle-earth, she told us, to avoid the sun's great heat and to keep the sweets from spoiling.
'It is much to ask, I know, but those sweets were destined for the poor children of Winter-home. Will you visit the frozen regions of Middle-earth and recover them? I fear they may all have been seized by the creatures of those parts. The sweets that were lost, you should know, were hot cross buns, plum pudding, gingerbread, peppermint treats, a flask of wassail, and fruit cake.'

'You have the sweets? Why look, they are all in one piece. The artisans of Gondor wrapped their gifts well!
'Quickly, will you deliver them to the children? They have been waiting - and it is you who should see the joy on their faces, by all rights.'
You should recover the sweets.

'According to my map, there is a way to Afhân-binnîn through the feast-house of Amrâg-zahar. Let us search for it!'

'What a terrible cold-drake! We must slay it before it can lay more of its eggs in Thikil-gundu!
'What has become of my brother?'
'Karazgar must pay for the evil he has wrought!'

'${PLAYER}....
'What Karazgar has done cannot go unanswered. He has slain our kinsfolk, he has set the Dragons of the North upon the Lonely Mountain, and he has stolen and defiled the halls of Thikil-gundu! We seven must stand against him!'
Dori turns to Nori.
'Where has he gone, brother?'
Nori explains that Karazgar travelled into Zashar-tûmun, but he warns you that many Dragon-kind now lurk in the ruin-dwellings of Thikil-gundu.
'Karazgar must answer for the evil he has worked against Durin's Folk! Baruk Khazâd!'

'It is with great regret that we cannot bear Frór's remains from the Steel Keep. Thikil-gundu itself will have to serve as his tomb!
'The King under the Mountain demanded that we return bearing a bone of Vethúg Wintermind, but to instead return with the crown of Dáin might speak better of our deeds in the ruins of Grárik!'
Dori places the crown in a pack, and begins to study his map of Thikil-gundu again.
'We should descend into the lore-trove and continue to the northern halls. If we follow that path, we will come to Thikil-nesad! It was once the seat of all of Grárik, and it was there that King Dáin I ruled before he fell.
'Perhaps Nori has hidden himself away before the old throne of Thikil-gundu, but I fear many more foes lurk in these halls.
'Even so, we must press on!'

'Dori! I cannot believe my eyes!'
Nori rushes forward and embraces his brother.
'It has gone all wrong, brother. I am the last of my expedition. The Weeping Warrior ambushed us before the gates of Thikil-gundu, and he slew the few of my company that survived the Wrack.
'In vengeance, I faced Karazgar in battle. Though I landed many blows, he managed to wrest my axe from my hand! It is a coward's way out of a fight, I think! All I have now is this torch. It has kept me warm, but it is no weapon!'
Dori hands Nori the axe you found before Thikil-gundu.
'My axe! Karazgar will know its bite once more!
'You have found me, brother, and for that I am grateful... but I cannot let Karazgar escape Thikil-gundu! Let us seek our vengeance against Karazgar together!'

'Listen well, ${PLAYER}.
'If these old maps are to be believed, Durûz-mazal should lie beyond these doors. It was a great chamber wrought in honour of the Seven Dwarf-kings and in its centre, a great hoarding-vault was delved. It became known as Immêsh-khalt, and it held the whole of the wealth of Grárik in its depths.
'If my brother came in search of the treasures of Thikil-gundu, he and his expedition would not have had to look any further than Immêsh-khalt. And so, it is there we will begin our search!
'Let us hope these old gears still turn!'
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTE: If you become separated from Dori and Company, you can summon them to your side using the Horn of Erebor. In addition, you can access the map of Thikil-gundu by pressing 'M'.</rgb>

'It has been frozen solid!
'Is this some final insult by Vethúg Wintermind? If this is how the great cold-drake has chosen to guard his stolen gold, there will be no recovering it... not until all the halls of the Steel Keep are reclaimed. And many still lie ahead of us, ${PLAYER}!
'Many of these old gears are frozen or ruined, but we must find a way to travel deeper into Thikil-gundu. Unless my eyes deceive me, it looks like the gears to some of the eastern halls are intact. If we can reach the old lore-trove of Afhân-binnîn by some path, it would allow us to reach many of the deepest chambers of Thikil-gundu. We must find a way there!
'According to the notes Nori left behind, Afhân-binnîn can be reached through a small hall at the northern end of the smithies of Kall-khebâb.
'Let us find a way into Kall-khebâb, and then we will see if we can find the way into Afhân-binnîn. Besides, it would do us all well to warm ourselves by the forges, I think!
'But... we would be wise to remain on guard. Such silence brings me no comfort.'

'It is worse than I feared....
'The Dead walk the halls of Thikil-gundu, and through some vile means, Karazgar has mastered the will of Vethúg Wintermind!
'There is little to celebrate this day, ${PLAYER}, but we have found my brother... and that is enough!
'Let us return to Tharrazhâr, and leave this sorrowful place behind.'
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTE: When you complete this quest, you will swiftly travel to the Keep of Tharrazhâr in Skarháld. If you have not finished exploring or seeking treasures in Thikil-gundu, it is advised that you wait to talk to Dori.</rgb>

'How could so many vile spirits be drawn to this place?
'Dwalin once told me of the fate of Skorgrím Dourhand. Have you heard the tale?
'He spoke much of spirits, Gaunt-lords, bloody hands, and other things of which I knew little, but perhaps that was for the best! What a terrible fate for a dwarf... even for one as villainous as Skorgrím!
'What has happened? Has a curse fallen upon Thikil-gundu? So many dwarves have been roused from their rest to serve whatever evil now lurks here....'
Dori pauses and looks at the company of dwarves staring at a great geode in Afhân-binnîn.
'Wait a moment, ${PLAYER}. There is something familiar about that dwarf....
'No... it cannot be! That is Frór, the lost son of Dáin I. After Dáin fell to Vethúg Wintermind, Frór sacrificed himself so that his brothers and kinsfolk could escape from Thikil-gundu. It can be no other... the crown of Dáin I rests upon his head!
'We must banish whatever evil has taken hold of him!'

'Bah! Orcs? Hobgoblins? This was supposed to be the swiftest path to Afhân-binnîn!'
Dori studies his map of Thikil-gundu and turns it about a few times.
'It seems that there is another way to the lore-trove, but to reach it, we must pass through the old feast-house of Amrâg-zahar! The gears outside its doors appeared to be frozen when I stood atop the hoarding-vault, but perhaps the heat of the smithies might loosen them.
'We have been lucky to find only a few Orcs so far, but I fear that Karazgar and the Dragon-kind dwelling in Thikil-gundu may soon be aware of us. It is some consolation that those dwarf-wights are not fond of the dragons, but they are no friends of ours either!
'The swifter we find my brother, the swifter we can leave this place. Let us go!'
You feel a cold wind blowing from the rimed ruin-dwellings of Thikil-gundu...
Appearing to anticipate your arrival, Karazgar stands beneath a great crack in the Wrathhorn!
After sealing the western passage into Thikil-nesad, Nori suddenly notices Dori and Company!
To your horror, a great cold-drake rests among her brood at Thikil-nesad!
Athramóth falls defeated, but you hear a great commotion in the distance!
The remains of Frór, son of Dáin I, fall lifeless to the ground...
Set in gold and adorned with precious mithril, the crown of Dáin has not faded in beauty...
The hall into Afhân-binnîn is sealed by rubble and debris...
Amid the ruined remains of Amrâg-zahar, a passage leading into Afhân-binnîn lies open...
Slain long ago by Vethúg Wintermind, Frór, son of Dáin I, has been raised from death...
The old forges of Thikil-gundu are rife with Orcs!
Karkasht Crow-feeder falls defeated, and the heat of the smithies begins to spread through Thikil-gundu...
An enormous hoard of gold lies encased in ice beneath your feet...
'Come, ${PLAYER}. Let us see what has become of Immêsh-khalt!'
'The hall to Afhân-binnîn must lie at the northern end of the smithies. Let us see if the path is clear!'
'Let us search for Nori in Afhân-binnîn! If my brother is not here, we will be able to follow other passages into the deepest chambers of Thikil-gundu!'

'You again, ${CLASS}. I will not lie. It has been hard going, here in the Grey Mountains. Hard going even for a people that has come thousands of perilous, wearying leagues.
'Still, we dwarves are hardy folk and will not be daunted. When pressed greatly, we will ask for help... especially of those who show themselves good of will and worthy to the task.
'Will you assist us in our efforts? There is much, yes much to be done!'

'Ah, there is always more to do. They say the work of the dwarves is never done, and that is as true today as it was in days past! Explore the lands of the dwarves and see their travails through to their conclusion! I do not doubt further adventures await in the Ironfold and Ered Mithrin.'

'It would seem the mines are no longer safe. I will call back all dwarves at once.
'I knew this day would come, though a part of me did not want to believe it. Rukhûsh-minam!'
'Náin sent you? My friend, Easterlings are the least of our worries at Hammerstead. If only I knew what exactly it is that we should be worried about!'

'You have returned, and I see the look upon your face is one that carries dire news. Shadowy nameless things, lurking in the Iron Hills?! What could have caused this?!
'We must scout the mining entrances in Járnfast immediately!'

'${PLAYER}, I must speak with you. Ever since the Iron Hills shook and caused damage to Járnfast, I have heard strange stories. Aye, I have not paid mind to these tales of rumblings from beneath the ground and strange shadows lurking just out of sight. It would seem that I can not ignore these stories any longer.
'On this day I have received similar notes of concern from both Hammerstead and the Dáinlik. I hope it is nothing more than a coincidence, ${PLAYER}. Please speak with Rísti Graver at the Dáinlik and Aflur Smokebeard at Hammerstead. Find out what it is they are concerned over and report back to me. I do not have time to dwell on this further, but I can not ignore these trusted dwarves.'
'Oh, Náin finally sent someone! It has been difficult to stay on schedule here. You would not believe what I and my workers have seen!'

'It is as I feared. The final seal has been torn and will need mending. The mending will take time as working with mithril is not easy. The hole is small which explains why we are not seeing the true horrors that lie below.'

'I am glad you have found Grár's key and returned quickly. I was worried that over the years, it may have been lost within the caverns of Erebor, but we must not tarry. While you were gone we have felt rumblings in Járnfast. Doom comes ever closer.
'Meet me at the entrance to the Howling Pit as soon as you are able.'

'Halt. By order of King Thorin III, Mazalu Ugshar may only be accessed by Erebor's lore-masters until the situation in the Grey Mountains is resolved.'
You hand Glóthin the writ from Náin.
'A writ from the Lord of the Iron Hills? Aye, this is no ordinary writ but a pact between Náin and King Thorin III. I am sorry to keep you. Please continue and accept my apology. We have all been on edge since Karazgar decreed his intentions against those of us in the north.'

'Rukhûsh-minam, the Howling Pit. Three doors protect Járnfast from Rukhûsh-minam. Only one door remains locked and sealed. I have checked and the seal to that final door has not broken. There must be something wrong with Grár's Seal.
'The brave Dwarf Grár sacrificed himself to collapse the opening to the Howling Pit. The Seal of Grár has remained intact ever since, covering the pit. There are only two ways to open the final door. One is to break the seal, and doing so would most certainly lead to our doom. The second is to retrieve Grár's key. Yes, the doors can be opened with a secret key, stored for safe keeping within Erebor.
'Take this writ with you. It will explain the urgency to this matter to anyone who may find it odd of your actions. Seek out the scholar's abode of Mazalu Ugshar. The key remains hidden within. Hurry ${PLAYER}, time is of most importance!'

'In the days of the war against Angmar a thousand years ago, a group of King Arvedui's men forsook his call to arms. Arvedui cursed these men, saying they should know no rest until they fulfilled their duty. To this day, they have walked the Fields of Fornost, tormented by their failings.
'The time has come for these shades to be free at last. Assemble your allies and seek out the Oath-breaker captain. He can be found beneath the very walls of Fornost, north-east of here by some old, broken ruins of Arthedain.
'Beware, though; his was a fell fate, and he may not be friendly to those who remind him of his foresworn oaths.'

'Alas! I regret sending you on this foolhardy task. I had expected the shade to be of an ill mind, but not to go so far as to attack you! It seems that the Oath-breakers now serve the Enemy in thought and deed.
'Amarthiel... it seems I have heard that name before. I should not speak of such things now, but these are indeed dark tidings you bring!'
'It is our duty to offer the shades of Men freedom from their curse and call them to fight against Angmar... even more so in that these Men are our own kindred.'

'What? Who dares to interrupt my ancient vigil?
'You fool! How dare you remind me of our pathetic oaths to the craven Arvedui! We have sworn new oaths now!
'We follow Amarthiel, and soon we will sweep aside all the living fools of the North!'
The Oath-breakers

In the days of King Arvedui, last king at Fornost, a company of the king's men betrayed their oaths to Arthedain, allowing Fornost to fall to the armies of Angmar. Arvedui cursed these men to never know rest until they had fulfilled their oaths.

The shade of the Oath-breaker captain can be found north-east of Mincham's camp, in some scattered ruins by the walls of Fornost.
Mincham has asked you to find the shade of the Oath-breaker captain and recall him and his followers to their ancient duty.

Mincham awaits you at his camp.
The Oath-breaker captain told you that he and his followers had sworn a new allegiance to someone named Amarthiel. Mincham may know what this means.

'You have the look of an adventurer about you, friend. If that be so, the people of Bree-land have need of your strength and your cunning, your wit and your wisdom!
'There was a time I would send you to the Mayor of Bree, the better for you to become acclimated to our town, but that time is past! Too many dangers press in upon us for you to spend your time chatting with the town officials. Too many villains threaten the good folk of Bree-land for you to tour the city! Already I have used up too much of your time in conversation, when you could be helping good people who need the assistance!
'If there is one man who knows everything that happens in Bree-land, that man is surely Barliman Butterbur, proprietor of the Prancing Pony. He hears all that goes on; the real test will be sifting through his speech for what needs doing first! But I am sure you will be up to the challenge. Find him inside the Pony, atop the hill on the northern side of Bree. He will tell you where you might start helping the people of Bree-land, and we will all be the better for your services!'

'Yes, you are here to help? Oh, you are just in time. I need all the help I might find! I fear my dream of founding an inn at this spot is in danger of foundering, even before it has truly begun!'
'I am short of officers, newcomer. If you are here to aid me in my fight against the outlaws in the Bree-fields I welcome you without reservation. My friend Lofar may have need for you as well.'

'Hello, hello! You have come all the way here from Barliman Butterbur? He is a sweet dear to think of us hobbits, so far away as he is! He must have heard about the troubling goings-on in the Old Forest, I imagine. If you are willing to help on that score, there will be plenty to do!'

'You have returned, and with stories to tell, I imagine! I look forward to hearing them!
'I am a bit busy right now, I am sure you understand. If the Pony is to keep running, you know I must run right along with her! Ha ha ha!
'I am sure the folk of Bree-land are grateful for your help, friend! Your good name will be spreading even now, your reputation in these parts growing by the minute! You are welcome in Bree-land, and in the Pony, whenever you desire to visit! Good job and good day to you!'

'My friend Adso Haybank is a hobbit, a good sort, and he dreams of building an inn upon the road west of Bree. No easy task, that; take it from one who knows! But I wish him well and have done what I can, and if you will see to him and lend him some assistance I will have done more! He has a camp on the road west of Bree-town, on the way to Buckland.
'Ah, Buckland! That reminds me, don't you know it, there is trouble afoot there as well. You know that Bree-town is home to both hobbits and Men, of course. Well, Buckland is home to hobbits only, but I would count them as neighbours as well, of course! It seems they have had some trouble with goings-on in the Old Forest. If you speak with Celandine Brandybuck, a sweet young lass who lives away in Buckland, you are certain to hear about that forest trouble. Everyone has their hands full, whether they be tall or small!
'Oh, did I ask you to speak with old Grimbriar yet? There is hustle and bustle a-plenty, and one thing drives out another, even if you are uncommonly sharp, like yours truly. Grimbriar is the Chief Watcher, and he maintains a post on the road north of Bree-town. I understand he has had some trouble with brigands of late. Go see him and help him with the outlaws, and you'd be doing Bree-land a service!'

The Prancing Pony is located on the northern side of the town of Bree, atop the hill upon which the town is situated.
A guard at the gate of Bree told you to speak with Barliman Butterbur, proprietor of the Prancing Pony, if you wanted to learn where you might go to help the folk of Bree-land.

Adso Haybank can be found at his camp on the road west of Bree-town, on the way to Buckland. Celandine Brandybuck can be found in Buckland, west of Bree-town and across the river from the Shire. Chief Watcher Grimbriar can be found at a cottage along the road north of Bree-town.

'So it is news, then? There is no shortage of that, I tell you truly, and most of it bad! Listen well, my new friend, and you will hear some of what ails us in Bree-land. Investigate some of these leads and you will find adventures wherever you go, and turn some of the bad news to good!

The town of Bree is under threat from many directions, and its people have need of adventurers to set things right!

'Are you ready, ${PLAYER}? I hope big and little folks have laid out all the doormats that I gave them, because I plan to put on my best costume and visit every one of them!
'Will you do the same? Why don't you go put on a costume, gather some treats, and then come back and tell me all about it?'

You should wear a costume and collect treats from housing neighbourhood doormats.
To help participation in this event, be sure to place the doormat you received from Begonia Grubb on your own house! More doormats can be obtained from Mogo Bracegirdle.

Begonia Grubb can be found in Wistmead, by the Party tree, and in the town centre of all housing neighbourhoods.
Return to Begonia Grubb and tell her about the treats you collected while in costume.
Begonia Grubb has been giving out doormats and treats, in hopes of starting a Treats or Trickery tradition in housing neighbourhoods.
Talk to Begonia Grubb
'You will do it? Oh, how grand! If you haven't any costume, I have some old thing you can put on, as well. Here. Go - and tell your friends. What fun!'

'My friends and I do so love a good and frightening costume on the Fall Festival, you see, and so we were sitting about, trying to imagine how to get some others to join us in the fun.
'Then it came to me: the cleverest idea! We must put treats out upon the doormats of our houses. Then, and this is the important part, only those in costume may be allowed to have some.
''Yes,' said my friends, 'but how will we persuade anyone to go about all the bother?'
''But don't you see? It's plain as day,' said I. 'We must help them along.'
'And so we set to work, the three of us, and baked more treats than you could count, and fashioned some doormats just perfect for the occasion. You may have one, if you like, but you must promise to lay it out, and then go in for some Treats and Trickery yourself. That's what I'm calling it. Isn't it just the perfect name?'
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTE: This quest cannot be cancelled. </rgb>
A Promise of Treats and of Trickery

Talk to Iris Tunnelly
A Windy Walk Through Wistmead

''It is impressive, isn't it? Most mazes are not spooky, but the maze of Wistmead certainly is!
'Rumour has it that the wheat shifts in the night, reshaped by an unseen scythe. Careless hobbits might become lost in its winding pathways, and once that happens, they are seldom seen again....'
Ermentrude pauses for far too long.
'Until I go in and find them, of course. If you want to give the maze a try, I'll be here!'

'Hullo! Is this your first time in Wistmead?
'Welcome, welcome! I am Halinard Bunce, and I manage a few of the festivities here in Wistmead. I've a skilled hand in carving gourds and I dabble in crafting interesting ales!
'Of course, I am not quite so skilled as to join the ranks of the Inn League, but I hope the Harvest Festival affords me the chance to prove myself! Alas, my Fognoggin ale seems to be more 'interesting' than well-regarded, but I've laboured to improve its recipe. You are welcome to try it while you explore the spooky sights and sounds of Wistmead!
'I have heard tell that the Wistful Oak has a mind of its own, but it is just an old tree... right? Perhaps you should go and see for yourself!
'But enough about me... there is plenty of fun to be had here in Wistmead! I'll let you get to it!'

'Very good!
'I hope you enjoy Wistmead as much as we enjoyed building it, ${PLAYER}.
'On behalf of all of us, welcome!'

'Dear me! Have you been standing there for long?
'I am Iris Tunnelly, and I bid you welcome to Wistmead! I am quite new here myself, but I've done well to help Mr. Goldworthy and the others prepare the field for the Harvest Festival.
'How did I come to be here, you ask? Oh, you didn't ask? Well, it was the strangest thing!
'I was just leaving Staddle when a cloaked woman of Bree approached me. I did not know her face and she gave no name, but she begged me to bring to her any lost cats that wandered into the festival grounds. How could she know such a thing? But not an hour after I arrived in Wistmead, I found these cats wandering around the Wheat-maze!
'Aren't they adorable? Well, don't let them fool you! They are a handful!
'Between you and me, I think Mr. Goldworthy could stand to fill that old, smelly bog, but I have never been so excited for the Harvest Festival!
'Perhaps you can help us make Wistmead even better!'

'Hallo there! It would seem word has begun to spread about Wistmead!
'The Harvest Festival has long been my favourite of all the festival of the Shire, and after seeing that prank old Mr. Baggins played on Lobelia, I was inspired to craft something of my own. And here it is!'
Clearly proud of his work, Walaric gestures wildly in every direction.
'To my delight, Ermentrude Haybank, Halinard Bunce, and Iris Tunnelly have devised a number of new games and activities for the Harvest Festival.
'If you find them wandering the field, be sure to introduce yourself!'

Walaric Goldworthy can be found in Wistmead.
You have explored Wistmead and become acquainted with the other members of his team. You should return to Walaric Goldworthy before joining in the festivities at Wistmead.

Ermentrude Haybank, Halinard Bunce, and Iris Tunnelly can be found in Wistmead.
Walaric Goldworthy has asked you to explore Wistmead and acquaint yourself with the other festival-hands. You should take a look around.
Wistmead embodies the very spirit of the Harvest Festival.

'Ah! Old Golfimbul must have felt quite the shock when Bandobras the Bullroarer swung his club! Don't you think?
'I'll have more gourds carved soon enough. I must say I much prefer these to actual goblins!'

'Will you take up this club and send them flying out of the Shire?'

'Mister Goldworthy took great care to wrap many of the bushes in Wistmead in fine cotton webbing, but I think he has missed an important detail. There are no spiders in Wistmead! Or if there were... they're long gone by now!

Defeated Bâlak

'The text you recovered told of an alliance between Angmar and Saruman. I have investigated the matter and found that the White Hand has sent an emissary to treat with Angmar.
'As a result, there have been many reports of Orcs gathering near the tower of Minas Caul near Barad Gúlaran. We must stop this alliance from happening, no matter the cost.
'Defeat the emissary, the half-orc Bâlak, and return back to me when the deed is done. You will want to take allies if you are to succeed!'

'You have helped the Free Peoples avoid the greatest of threats in the North! An alliance of this magnitude would certainly have spelled the downfall of Eriador.
'Thank you for helping us push back evil this day.'
Enter Minas Caul and defeat Bâlak.
Emissary of the White-hand
Having intercepted a pledge from Saruman of Isengard, you must enter Minas Caul and defeat his emissary to stop an alliance between the Iron Crown and the White Hand.
'You must defeat Bâlak and keep the White Hand from allying itself with the Iron Crown.'

Minas Caul is one of the large towers of Barad Gúlaran, south of Gath Forthnír.
You must travel to Barad Gúlaran and issue a challenge to Bâlak, the emissary of the White-hand, inside Minas Caul.

Brúnfair is at Gath Forthnír, north of Barad Gúlaran.

'The text you recovered told of an alliance between Angmar and the goblins of Goblin-town. Rumour has been told that Angmar and Goblin-town have had troubles entreating in the past. It is strange to find the goblins here. Perhaps this emissary is here without the knowledge of his leaders.
'You should investigate the matter. There have been many reports of goblins near the tower of Minas Maur near Barad Gúlaran. We must stop this alliance from happening, no matter the cost.
'Defeat the emissary and return to me when the deed is done. If you wish to succeed, you will likely want to take allies with you.'
'You have helped the Free Peoples avoid the greatest of threats! An alliance between the goblins of the Misty Mountains and the Iron Crown would have been disastrous!'

'Laugi Goldentongue must be defeated, else the Iron Crown and the Dourhands will forge a stronger alliance.'

Minas Angos is a tower in Barad Gúlaran, south of Gath Forthnír.
You must travel to Barad Gúlaran and defeat Laugi Goldentongue, the emissary of the Dourhands, inside Minas Angos. Brúnfair suggested you take allies.

Brúnfair is at Gath Forthnír, north of Barad Gúlaran.
Having defeated Laugi Goldentongue, you should return to Brúnfair and tell him of your victory.

Find the northern hall that leads into Afhân-binnîn from Kall-khebâb
'According to my map, there is a way to Afhân-binnîn through the feast-house of Amrâg-zahar. Let us search for it!'

'What a terrible cold-drake! We must slay it before it can lay more of its eggs in Thikil-gundu!
'What has become of my brother?'
'Karazgar must pay for the evil he has wrought!'

'${PLAYER}....
'What Karazgar has done cannot go unanswered. He has slain our kinsfolk, he has set the Dragons of the North upon the Lonely Mountain, and he has stolen and defiled the halls of Thikil-gundu! We seven must stand against him!'
Dori turns to Nori.
'Where has he gone, brother?'
Nori explains that Karazgar travelled into Zashar-tûmun, but he warns you that many Dragon-kind now lurk in the ruin-dwellings of Thikil-gundu.
'Karazgar must answer for the evil he has worked against Durin's Folk! Baruk Khazâd!'

'It is with great regret that we cannot bear Frór's remains from the Steel Keep. Thikil-gundu itself will have to serve as his tomb!
'The King under the Mountain demanded that we return bearing a bone of Vethúg Wintermind, but to instead return with the crown of Dáin might speak better of our deeds in the ruins of Grárik!'
Dori places the crown in a pack, and begins to study his map of Thikil-gundu again.
'We should descend into the lore-trove and continue to the northern halls. If we follow that path, we will come to Thikil-nesad! It was once the seat of all of Grárik, and it was there that King Dáin I ruled before he fell.
'Perhaps Nori has hidden himself away before the old throne of Thikil-gundu, but I fear many more foes lurk in these halls.
'Even so, we must press on!'

'Dori! I cannot believe my eyes!'
Nori rushes forward and embraces his brother.
'It has gone all wrong, brother. I am the last of my expedition. The Weeping Warrior ambushed us before the gates of Thikil-gundu, and he slew the few of my company that survived the Wrack.
'In vengeance, I faced Karazgar in battle. Though I landed many blows, he managed to wrest my axe from my hand! It is a coward's way out of a fight, I think! All I have now is this torch. It has kept me warm, but it is no weapon!'
Dori hands Nori the axe you found before Thikil-gundu.
'My axe! Karazgar will know its bite once more!
'You have found me, brother, and for that I am grateful... but I cannot let Karazgar escape Thikil-gundu! Let us seek our vengeance against Karazgar together!'

'Listen well, ${PLAYER}.
'If these old maps are to be believed, Durûz-mazal should lie beyond these doors. It was a great chamber wrought in honour of the Seven Dwarf-kings and in its centre, a great hoarding-vault was delved. It became known as Immêsh-khalt, and it held the whole of the wealth of Grárik in its depths.
'If my brother came in search of the treasures of Thikil-gundu, he and his expedition would not have had to look any further than Immêsh-khalt. And so, it is there we will begin our search!
'Let us hope these old gears still turn!'
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTE: If you become separated from Dori and Company, you can summon them to your side using the Horn of Erebor. In addition, you can access the map of Thikil-gundu by pressing 'M'.</rgb>

'It has been frozen solid!
'Is this some final insult by Vethúg Wintermind? If this is how the great cold-drake has chosen to guard his stolen gold, there will be no recovering it... not until all the halls of the Steel Keep are reclaimed. And many still lie ahead of us, ${PLAYER}!
'Many of these old gears are frozen or ruined, but we must find a way to travel deeper into Thikil-gundu. Unless my eyes deceive me, it looks like the gears to some of the eastern halls are intact. If we can reach the old lore-trove of Afhân-binnîn by some path, it would allow us to reach many of the deepest chambers of Thikil-gundu. We must find a way there!
'According to the notes Nori left behind, Afhân-binnîn can be reached through a small hall at the northern end of the smithies of Kall-khebâb.
'Let us find a way into Kall-khebâb, and then we will see if we can find the way into Afhân-binnîn. Besides, it would do us all well to warm ourselves by the forges, I think!
'But... we would be wise to remain on guard. Such silence brings me no comfort.'

'It is worse than I feared....
'The Dead walk the halls of Thikil-gundu, and through some vile means, Karazgar has mastered the will of Vethúg Wintermind!
'There is little to celebrate this day, ${PLAYER}, but we have found my brother... and that is enough!
'Let us return to Tharrazhâr, and leave this sorrowful place behind.'
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTE: When you complete this quest, you will swiftly travel to the Keep of Tharrazhâr in Skarháld. If you have not finished exploring or seeking treasures in Thikil-gundu, it is advised that you wait to talk to Dori.</rgb>

'How could so many vile spirits be drawn to this place?
'Dwalin once told me of the fate of Skorgrím Dourhand. Have you heard the tale?
'He spoke much of spirits, Gaunt-lords, bloody hands, and other things of which I knew little, but perhaps that was for the best! What a terrible fate for a dwarf... even for one as villainous as Skorgrím!
'What has happened? Has a curse fallen upon Thikil-gundu? So many dwarves have been roused from their rest to serve whatever evil now lurks here....'
Dori pauses and looks at the company of dwarves staring at a great geode in Afhân-binnîn.
'Wait a moment, ${PLAYER}. There is something familiar about that dwarf....
'No... it cannot be! That is Frór, the lost son of Dáin I. After Dáin fell to Vethúg Wintermind, Frór sacrificed himself so that his brothers and kinsfolk could escape from Thikil-gundu. It can be no other... the crown of Dáin I rests upon his head!
'We must banish whatever evil has taken hold of him!'

'Bah! Orcs? Hobgoblins? This was supposed to be the swiftest path to Afhân-binnîn!'
Dori studies his map of Thikil-gundu and turns it about a few times.
'It seems that there is another way to the lore-trove, but to reach it, we must pass through the old feast-house of Amrâg-zahar! The gears outside its doors appeared to be frozen when I stood atop the hoarding-vault, but perhaps the heat of the smithies might loosen them.
'We have been lucky to find only a few Orcs so far, but I fear that Karazgar and the Dragon-kind dwelling in Thikil-gundu may soon be aware of us. It is some consolation that those dwarf-wights are not fond of the dragons, but they are no friends of ours either!
'The swifter we find my brother, the swifter we can leave this place. Let us go!'
You feel a cold wind blowing from the rimed ruin-dwellings of Thikil-gundu...
Appearing to anticipate your arrival, Karazgar stands beneath a great crack in the Wrathhorn!
After sealing the western passage into Thikil-nesad, Nori suddenly notices Dori and Company!
To your horror, a great cold-drake rests among her brood at Thikil-nesad!
Athramóth falls defeated, but you hear a great commotion in the distance!
The remains of Frór, son of Dáin I, fall lifeless to the ground...
Set in gold and adorned with precious mithril, the crown of Dáin has not faded in beauty...
The hall into Afhân-binnîn is sealed by rubble and debris...
Amid the ruined remains of Amrâg-zahar, a passage leading into Afhân-binnîn lies open...
Slain long ago by Vethúg Wintermind, Frór, son of Dáin I, has been raised from death...
The old forges of Thikil-gundu are rife with Orcs!
Karkasht Crow-feeder falls defeated, and the heat of the smithies begins to spread through Thikil-gundu...
An enormous hoard of gold lies encased in ice beneath your feet...
'Come, ${PLAYER}. Let us see what has become of Immêsh-khalt!'
'The hall to Afhân-binnîn must lie at the northern end of the smithies. Let us see if the path is clear!'
'Let us search for Nori in Afhân-binnîn! If my brother is not here, we will be able to follow other passages into the deepest chambers of Thikil-gundu!'
In the Halls of Thikil-gundu

Nori might be found somewhere within Afhân-binnîn. Afhân-binnîn can be found through Amrâg-zahar.
You have discovered a passage into Afhân-binnîn, and you should now search for Nori within the lore-troves of Thikil-gundu.

Frór the Lost can be found in the heights of Afhân-binnîn.
You have discovered the remains of Frór, son of Dáin I, brought to life by a fell spirit in Afhân-binnîn. You should defeat him and let him at last be laid to rest.

Dori can be found in Thikil-gundu.
You have defeated the fell spirit inhabiting the remains of Frór and recovered the long-lost crown of Dáin. You should offer the crown to Dori and learn what is to be done.

Thikil-nesad, the Steel Seat, can be found deep within Thikil-gundu.
Fearing that Nori has been discovered by the inhabitants of the Steel Keep, Dori now hopes to find him before the old throne of Thikil-gundu.

Athramóth and her brood can be found in Thikil-nesad.
You have discovered a great cold-drake resting among her brood. You should defeat Athramóth and make safe the old throne of the Steel Keep.

Nori can be found at Thikil-nesad.
Nori has fled into Thikil-nesad and unwittingly reunited with Dori. You should talk to Nori.

Dori can be found in Thikil-gundu.
You have reunited with Nori. You should now speak to Dori and learn what is to be done.

Zashar-tûmun, the ruin-dwellings of Thikil-gundu, can be found to the west of the feast-house of Amrâg-zahar.
Nori has warned you that Karazgar now prepares a great force of dragon-kind in Zashar-tûmun. You should find a way to Zashar-tûmun and confront Karazgar.

Karazgar can be found somewhere within Zashar-tûmun.
Nori has warned you that Karazgar now prepares a great force of dragon-kind in Zashar-tûmun. You should find and confront Karazgar.

Karazgar can be found in the western reaches of Zashar-tûmun.
You have found Karazgar, the Weeping Warrior, and you should now attempt to defeat him.

Dori can be found in Thikil-gundu. If you have become separated, you may call him and the rest of the company by using your horn.
You have repelled Karazgar and rescued Nori from the depths of Thikil-gundu. You should now speak to Dori.

Dori can be found in Thikil-gundu. If you have become separated, you may call him and the rest of the company by using your horn.
You have come to Thikil-gundu in search of Nori. You should now speak to Dori in Thikil-gundu.

The hoarding-vault of Immêsh-khalt can be found in the centre of Durûz-mazal, the Chamber of Faces.
Dori has directed you and the rest of the company to search the hoarding-vault of Immêsh-khalt for signs of Nori.

The smithies of Kall-khebâb can be found in the eastern halls of Thikil-gundu.
Determined to delve deeper into Thikil-gundu, Dori has asked you to find the smithies of Kall-khebâb so that you might gain passage into the other halls of the Steel Keep.

Karkasht Crow-feeder can be found in the smithies of Kall-khebâb.
You have discovered a massive hobgoblin leading the Orcs in the smithies of Kall-khebâb. You must defeat him if you are to continue deeper into Thikil-gundu.

A hall to Afhân-binnîn can be found at the northern end of the smithies of Kall-khebâb.
With the smithies clear of foes, you should now search the smithies for a way into the lore-trove of Afhân-binnîn.

The feast-house of Amrâg-zahar can be found through the northernmost doors of Durûz-mazal, the Chamber of Faces.
With the heat of the smithies now spreading through Thikil-gundu, Dori hopes to find another way to reach Afhân-binnîn and continue the search for Nori.
Talk to Dori in Thikil-gundu

'This next task you cannot possibly succeed at alone, or even with a fellowship of your closest allies. Nay, you must assemble a war-party if you are to defeat Bogbereth.
'No ordinary creature is she, Bogbereth, the Poison-queen of Himbar. You must strike swift and true against her, for her hide is as steel armour and her fangs are keen-edged daggers, dripping venom.
'Assemble your band of heroes and journey back to Torech-i-Bogbereth. You will find her there, unless she finds you first.'
'The great beast is fallen? Then her poisonous reign is ended. This has been another blow to the Iron Crown and the forces of Angmar, and we owe it all to you and your allies.'
Lunathron told you of a great, vile spider, Bogbereth, which hunts in Himbar.
'Have you assembled your war-band yet? Bogbereth will not fall without a fight, and despite your courage, you are no threat to her by yourself.'

Bogbereth hunts in the north-east reaches of Himbar, west and then north of Gath Forthnír.
Lunathron cautioned you not to face Bogbereth with anything less than a fully-armed war-party. She must be defeated, lest she continues to spawn more of her foul brood.

Gath Forthnír is in the eastern part of Himbar, south and east of Torech-i-Bogbereth.
Lunathron bade you destroy the great spider, Bogbereth. Now that she is no more, you can return to claim your victory.
You have found Ferndúr's lair

'You have stopped the evil engine of the Cauldron of Death, you have stopped the supply of money to the North Downs, and you have ended the terror of Deluches, but still the Dead rise! I fear this is the work of the dread sorcerer Lord Ferndúr. You have gathered allies and helped us to slow the spread of the Dead. However defeating Lord Ferndûr is no small task. If you would challenge this fell master of death, you must assemble an even greater force.
'I believe that Ferndúr is concerned more with the summoning of the fell spirits that are used to animate the shambling bodies of the dead than he is with the wights. You must return to the cursed isle in Imlad Balchorth, find the place where the fell spirits throng and destroy them. Destroy them all, and perhaps Ferndúr will appear, for he must know it when his summoned spirits are banished.
'Be wary, for this threat may be the gravest yet, faced in the darkness of Angmar, a monstrous evil whose only superior in the North is in the dread citadel of Carn Dûm itself.'

'Truly you have accomplished a deed worthy of the great tales of past ages. It may be long before Imlad Balchorth is cleansed of its ancient evil, but in a single stroke you have broken one of the main buttresses that support Angmar's vile strength.
'I salute you.'
Draw out and defeat Ferndúr
Talk to Throst
Ferndúr the Virulent
Throst believes that the sorcerer Ferndúr concerns himself with the fell spirits that inhabit the area not far from the Cauldron of Death.
'Find the fell spirits, and you will eventually find their master!'
'The slayer of Ferndúr! I will honour your name among the Free Peoples!'

There are fell spirits in a ruined area not far from the Cauldron of Death in the central island of Imlad Balchorth.
Ferndúr must be destroyed to disperse the evil threat in this cursed land.

Throst is back at Gath Forthnír, east from Ferndúr's lair.
With Ferndúr slain, you should return to Throst to tell him the tale of your deeds.

A Fortune of Harvest Spirit

'Is the Harvest Festival almost over? Well, we have certainly had our fill, you and I. To be entirely honest, I think I am ready for a brief rest. After all, Yule is hardly around the corner!
'Jests aside, I thank you for joining me. You have made this year's Harvest all the richer by your joining in, I assure you, ${PLAYER}.'

'I say, there is so much fun to be had around here, isn't there? I could go about from the first day until the very last and not get my fill of Haunted Burrows, Hedge Mazes, and Treats or Trickery!
'You feel the same, do you not, ${PLAYER}? Well, do not be shy! Seize the season. Persistent effort reaps rich rewards, as I like to say.'

'${CLASS}, we have been attacked!
