'There is a moving radiance held within this glass, ${PLAYER}, and it reminds me of something: the rotating beacon atop Barad Cúron, Tower of the Crescent Moon, in Minas Morgul. Is this a shard of glass from the beacon in the tower's topmost chamber?
'You have seen moon-letters before, and so have I. Can it be that Vóin wrote these secret words in the light of that beacon, knowing they could only be revealed by the same light? But what did he seek to hide? Did he record the location of the weapon sought by Gothmog?
'We must read the secret writing in the Black Book, ${PLAYER}. Let me know if you are ready to do so.'

'Are you ready? I do not know what we will learn from Vóin's secret writing, but whatever it may be we will discover it together.
'It is time to hear the rest of Vóin's tale.'

'Much that was obscured from us now seems clear, my friend. When the sword Dúnachar pierced Mordirith's form in the throne room of Carn Dûm, the purpose of the Witch-king was fulfilled, a thousand years later, but not in the manner for which he planned. Bonds were made that day, and months later, on the Pelennor Fields before Minas Tirith, they would be broken. He could not remember it, but one thousand years later, Eärnur's final act of resistance freed him from the domination of Mordor.'
Gandalf closes the Black Book and looks up at you.
'That is enough for now, my friend. We have come to the end of the moon-writing, but the discovery has stirred in me the certainty that I missed something in my earlier perusal of this tome. I do not know what it may have been, but I can sense its presence still.
'Ah, mysteries upon mysteries. Perhaps I will return to this matter when we have satisfied our other charge. Yes, I fear we have spent too many hours in study and neglected our other tasks.'

'I am beginning to worry, my friend. There must be some means of escape, some way to free you from the Nazgûl's grasp. I have searched this tower high and low, and delved into every corner of the vale, but... there is nothing.
'What is that? What did you say? You have thought of something? At last, Eärnur! Speak! Tell me what you have devised, and I will carry it out!
'What? Thafar-gathol? Why do you speak its name, here in the darkness of Morgul? That is of no use to us now, friend. We must think only of escape!'

'For all the time I have known you, Vóin, you have dreamed of finding your lost city. I do not want you to waste your years here in this tower seeking to prevent something I know to be unpreventable.
'Yes, I know my doom. Here in the heart of his power, I cannot hope to resist the Lord of the Nazgûl for much longer. He knows this. But he seeks not only a thrall. He wants something else: he wants to destroy my spirit, the fire inside me that so infuriates him. He wants me to despair, to fall upon my own sword, to say with word and deed \qyou have the victory, and I am bested.\q You were right, Vóin. That would be no escape, and would bind me to his will.
'Know you of Egalmoth? He was the lord of this city when it fell, but he did not wait in the tower for the Nazgûl to slay him. He rode out, defying the armies of Orc and wraith, and though he came in the end to death, I think his Onslaught will be long-remembered. I cannot do as he did, and I cannot keep the Lord of the Nazgûl from dominating my mind. But I can hinder the scheme he has devised for me, and cheat him of the total victory he seeks.
'None will know of this save you, Vóin. My own Onslaught will not become song or tale or legend. But it will be the deed of Eärnur, who resisted evil to the last.'

'It was in the city of Minas Morgul that I came to live, hiding in plain sight among the other wicked dwarves that served the Orcs and their foul masters. It was unpleasant work and cruel, but every disagreeable task elevated my position in the city and brought me nearer to my goal. Other dwarves claim the Zhélruka have no patience? I proved them all wrong, and was rewarded. In time the bosses gave me a new post: steward of the chambers within the tower atop the city.
'It was there I at last found Eärnur, and the few of his knights who yet survived.'

'We will think of something. There is still time.
'The Witch-king's pride will be his downfall. He thinks to rob you of the spark that drives you, Eärnur, the fire that so infuriates him. As long as that passion to resist him burns within you, he will not know victory over you.
'I have stayed here too long. I will be back tomorrow, my friend.'

'Think, Eärnur, think! There is still time, but... there is less now than there was. I have devised a hundred plans, each of them less likely to succeed than the previous one. But that does not mean escape is impossible. Never think that!
'I do not want to worry you, but... you should know. Silmahtar is... no more. The Houses of Lamentation claim another of our friends.
'No, we should not weep for him. Let his fate inspire us to escape, and we can mourn him when we are both free of the Black Land! Not just he, but Silmahtar and Calatúr both. Think!'

'And so ends the hidden runes Vóin left within the Black Book of Mordor, ${PLAYER}. If the knight Macilnis escaped Imlad Morgul and came to free lands again, Vóin does not tell. And yet... I think we have learned enough from this Black Book for me to suggest some possibilities.
'I believe Macilnis escaped the bounds of Mordor still in possession of Orthadel, the Rising Star, but not without injury. For how long did she journey, and to where did she go? We cannot know for certain, but it seems she did not make for Minas Tirith or word of her would appear once again, and it does not. I think she turned northward in an attempt to put as much distance between herself and the Witch-king as she was able. Did she survive the journey, and live out her days in peace? Did she succumb to wounds freshly-inflicted during her escape, or those she endured during the years of her torment in the dungeons? Was she recaptured by hunting-parties sent by the Witch-king? Vóin never learned which of these came to pass, and I cannot say.
'But of this I am quite certain. Whatever may have been the fate of this knight of Gondor, the blade she carried out of the Morgul Vale survived. Orthadel was of Elf-make, wielded first by Magoldir the Elf during the Siege of Barad-dûr and later by King Eärnur of Gondor, but in time its history was forgotten, and its name was lost. It became just a sword, handed down from bearer to bearer for many years. Somehow it found its way into the hands of a Dúnadan, and became an heirloom of his house.
'That is how it came to the Ranger Golodir, ${PLAYER}. Yes, though it endured much over the years, I think the sword that would be remade in the forges of Rivendell and renamed Dúnachar was once known as Orthadel. And so the Rising Star became the Avenger of the West.'
'Yes, it is conjecture only... but I believe it is true.'

'Vóin! What news of Eärnur? Tell me he still resists the torments of the Nazgûl!
'What? Escape? What has changed? I will not leave without Eärnur! You say he is already fled? Happy news! If you will open my cell, I will follow him to freedom! Dear, sweet Vóin!
'What of Macilnis? You go to free her now? Then I will away, and let us meet again when we are safely outside the Black Land! Farewell, Vóin, bearer of happy tidings and welcome escape!'

'Only one of Eärnur's knights could escape, but even that would require the guardians in the Vale to be occupied with some distracting mission. Something was needed to draw their attention away from the bearer of the sword.
'I knew Macilnis was more fleet of foot than Orolang, and would have the greatest chance of escaping the valley, so I gave to her the sword Orthadel and set her free. Only after she was fled did I go to release Orolang, but there was little time to waste: I sent the tower's guardians after him almost immediately, and he led them on a desperate chase... away from Macilnis. Alas, my friend! I had no choice! Anyone could see that.'
'Time was no friend of ours,' Gandalf reads aloud
'This is hard reading,' Gandalf says, looking up from the pages of the Black Book
'To Mordor I went then, seeking word of my vanished friend,' Gandalf reads aloud
'Every step I took in those dungeons was the heaviest of my life,' reads Gandalf
'But the grinding wheel showed no mercy. Time moved onward,' reads Gandalf
'After many months,' Gandalf reads, 'at last I found him.'
'Like a grinding wheel, time moved ever onward,' Gandalf reads

'I believe this will be our last delve into the words of our distant friend Vóin, ${PLAYER}. Yes, I say friend, for though the tome he left us comes from Mordor and bears the sigil of Sauron upon its cover, I have detected little malice on the part of the Zhélruka who wrote it. He has expanded our knowledge of the past, and for that I call him friend!
'The shard of glass reveals hidden writing that speaks of Mordor. That is where Vóin picks up the tale, and that is where we should follow in these Halls of Memory.'

'My mind wandered on the hard journey. I remembered our adventures together, and they brought a smile to my face even in that dark land. But there were other memories, too, and regrets, and those were less welcome.
'He had just become king of Gondor, and the crown was an ill fit. The taunts of the Witch-king at Fornost ate away at him. \qIf my horse had not bolted...\q he often began, but one of us was always there to keep him from dwelling upon it. If Magoldir had lived, his words might have kept Eärnur from going to Minas Morgul, but Magoldir was dead, and would never return from Durthang.
'Could I have stopped him? This is the thought that comes back to me again and again, as I write these passages in the dim light of the accursed beacon. He had just become king, and I trusted that his knights would keep him safe. Gondor was no land for Zhélruka, and I had deeds of my own to perform. I remember his words to me before I returned to the northern mountains. \qGo find your city, Vóin. Go find Thafar-gathol!\q I embraced him then, and bid him farewell. \qI will!\q I told him.
'\qGood!\q he responded. \qPerhaps then you will stop talking about it morning and evening!\q
'Seven years after that parting, I learned from travellers upon the road that King Eärnur went to Imlad Morgul with a band of knights, and vanished. I set out at sunrise the following morning, bid farewell to my wife, and resolved to find Eärnur.'

'If I could still move my arm, I'd slice yer throat....'
Ashaug coughs and black blood leaks from the corners of his mouth.
'The Sneak was on his way out like the High Up wanted... and then you lot come in swingin' knives around and it spooks him. Next thing I know, one of us gets bit... and another takes a tumble off the stair. You lot are easy enough to put down, but not him... and we couldn't even if we wanted to or we'd be for the Pits. Ah... but some thought it'd be worth the Pits to gut that little frog!'
Ashaug laughs weakly.
'We were at each other's throats in an instant... and we forgot all about your little revolt, shakglob. Always goes this way, anyway. A few'll get out, but it won't take long to round 'em up. Even if you find a way out of Lugbúrz, you'll never... escape... Mor....'
Ashaug chokes and his eyes widen.

'It's not far now... but I fear the worst is still ahead of us.
'Ashaug was right about one thing. Even if we escape the Dark Tower, we won't get far without being noticed. And it won't be Udûn for us after all this, I promise you that. We'll end up in the Black Pits or...'
Lethi visibly shudders.
'...they'll bring us to the Dead City. I... well, let's hope it doesn't come to that.'

'I suppose this is as far as I'm to go, ${PLAYER}.'
With a look of disdain barely masked on his face, Nagli eyes the Longbeards that have stopped him in Thorin's Hall.
'When the Longbeard expedition arrived, I recognized a few of them. They are led by a dwarf named Dwalin, and he is hailed as a hero by many Longbeards. He is an old dwarf, white of beard, and it is not unlikely that he has assumed the mantle of Steward in Gormr's absence.
'If his people truly slaughtered my own, there shall be further bloodshed between us... but I am no longer so certain who seeks to do harm to the Dourhands. You know much of the ways of the Enemy, and I must know if our people have been deceived to some foul end.
'I beg you, ${PLAYER}, speak to Dwalin on my behalf.'

'Aye, that's good enough. There's no time to pick through the rest with all these Orcs about....'
Lethi glances toward the Twisted Stair.
'We'll have to climb down to reach the gates. Quickly now!'

'Was that... the Dark Lord's prisoner? No wonder He wanted to be rid of it!'
Lethi sighs and regains his breath.
'It's a good thing you drove it off, ${PLAYER}. I swear it looked so sickly and withered, but it had the strength of a dwarf!
'Ah, but there's no time to dwell on that now. We've got to keep moving....'

'Hah! Did you think the Great Eye would just let you walk out of Lugbúrz, shakglob?'
Ushgrat whips Vaski before turning to you.
'You... Orc! Why is that one not in chains? And where did it get that knife?'
Ushgrat's eyes narrow as he looks you over.
'Clever, clever. That's your plan, is it, stone-filth?'

'What did you see? Is the way clear?'
You tell Lethi that you spied a massive uruk and a wounded Stout-axe on the causeway, and that many more Stout-axes have fallen in their attempts to escape.
'I knew they'd set a trap for us... I just knew it!'
Lethi gnashes his teeth in anger.
'Bah! Perhaps if I pretend to be your prisoner, we might be able to fool that uruk. If not, well....
'It's our only chance, ${PLAYER}. Follow me!'

'All of this can't be us… can it?'
'Why do the Orcs fight amongst themselves while our brethren make for the gates?
'Perhaps we have found some good fortune at last!'

'I think that might just fool them...
'Now listen, ${PLAYER}. There's a long causeway just ahead of us around that corner, and at its end... the gates of the Dark Tower.
'Since you look like a proper Orc, why don't you scout ahead and peer around the corner? If the way is clear, we'll make a run for it!'

Skorgrím glares at you. His eyes flash with an unearthly glow.
'You are far from home, aren't you?'

'That was quite the story, ${PLAYER}. I think it took all of us quite by surprise... a welcome surprise, of course! Not just any dwarf could do as you have done!
'It's been a long week for us Dourhands. Our Steward, Gormr Doursmith, was preparing a great celebration for Skorgrím, our king of old - a Ritual of Commemoration, he called it. But after the Longbeards came to Ered Luin demanding tribute, he sent us down here to close the pass. We've been at it for nigh on a week now and if my reckoning is right, we missed the celebration two... no, three nights back. Some thanks we get!'
Nagli appears to realize his grievances pale in comparison to the plight of the Stout-axes.
'Here I am complaining about missing a party to you, ${PLAYER}. Forgive my foolishness!
'I can't speak for everyone, but I think we would be glad to hear more of your tales when we return to Thorin's Hall. Perhaps you would even be welcome to stay among us for a time... if the Steward allows it.'

'Yes?'
Nagli swiftly recounts your tale to Rethvárd. After finishing, Nagli asks Rethvárd to bring you before the Steward of Thorin's Hall that he might judge your worth to the Dourhands.
'Aye, I can do that... just as soon as Bjarni arrives to take watch. He's almost an hour late now. It's not like him.
'I'd like to hear the tale from you, ${PLAYER}, if it's not too much trouble. It'd make the journey to Thorin's Hall seem faster for the both of us!'
Rethvárd visibly shivers.
'A chill wind blows. Do you feel it?'

'You seem a fine dwarf, ${PLAYER}, but you must understand... we Dourhands are also a lost people. We tended the hall of Thorin Oakenshield for many years, and what thanks do the Longbeards offer us? You heard Skorgrím! Naught but a massacre of our brothers and sisters!
'Whatever you think Skorgrím-king to be... he and the might of Angmar could help us to step out of the shadows of the Longbeards and reclaim our former glory. Flee to the Longbeards if you must, but if you do, know that I will not hesitate to raise my axe against you.'

'Something troubles me about Skorgrím's words, and that deathly Man makes me uneasy.
'I wish to trust the words of Skorgrím-king, but I cannot. Does he speak for himself or does Ivar speak through him? It is true that Steward Gormr ceased sending tribute to the Lonely Mountain some months ago, but our quarrels with the Longbeards never ended in bloodshed... until now.
'I wish to hear what the Longbeards have to say to these accusations. Has Skorgrím-king spoken true or is this some conspiracy guided by the hand of Angmar?
'Will you accompany me, ${PLAYER}? Perhaps the voice of a Stout-axe might do more to ease this unrest than that of a Dourhand....'

'Bah! What a mess they have left behind!'
'Who are you and what business have you in the hall of Thorin Oakenshield?'
You introduce yourself to Dwalin as a Stout-axe of Mordor who escaped imprisonment by the Enemy and fled to distant lands to seek refuge. You explain that you encountered Skorgrím and Ivar on the road to Thorin's Hall, and that Skorgrím claimed that the Longbeards massacred the Dourhands.
'A massacre? Aye, you could call it that, but it was the work of Ivar the Blood-hand -- not the Longbeards! Indeed, it was Ivar who roused Skorgrím from his long rest. But it was not some miracle of fortune that made it so... it was Ivar's vile sorcery and the unwitting sacrifice of many Dourhands that bound a terrible spirit to his remains. Whatever the Dourhands think of Skorgrím, he is not who he appears to be!
'Although I believe that your Dourhand friend means us no harm, he still has much to answer for and I do not doubt he wishes to hear the truth of this sorry matter for himself.
'If it is refuge you seek, you may earn it by helping us to restore these halls from years of neglect by the Dourhands. Even if he had not succumbed to evil, Gormr still failed in the task my lord set for him. If Nagli proves trustworthy, he may dwell in Frerin's Court... but he is forever banished from Thorin's Hall.
'Do you accept these terms, ${PLAYER}?'
You nod.
'Good, good. Now I have never heard of the clan name you mentioned, these Stout-axes, but you are welcome in Thorin's Hall so long as you work to aid the Longbeards.'

'Ever since I stood look-out over the city of Osgiliath, my mind was captured by the strange wonders of the Morgul Vale. Introduction: Imlad Morgul

'Welcome to Echad Uial, ${PLAYER}. Within any wood, we Rangers know how to travel at speed while remaining hidden; I find myself much more at home here than I did in the barren Wastes, where we last spoke. Come, we have much to discuss.'
You and Damrod share stories and the account of your recent adventures.
'Then you will assist us here in Rath Dúath, for now? Good! You have not changed, my friend. I am glad to hear it, for we have need of you here. Did you think otherwise?'

'${PLAYER}! You earned my respect and it has not wavered; word of your deeds in Gorgoroth and in the northern lands has made its way back to me and to the other Rangers of Ithilien. And here we now meet upon the very doorstep of Minas Morgul! That is incredible, my friend, and yet I should not have doubted our paths would lead us here, where there is evil to be faced. Is that not what we do, time and again? It is indeed!
'Faramir has regained his health, a gift of time and some say the healing powers of King Elessar himself, and he has led us here. There is a camp now, Echad Uial, and from there he plans to cleanse the city of its evil, and reclaim it for Gondor. Damrod travels with him and will be pleased to speak with you. Return to me when Damrod sees fit to release you!'

'${PLAYER}, I did not think to see you again. I heard that urgent matters took you away from the conquest of Gorgoroth and sent you far to the north. Well, much has transpired while you were gone, my friend. The Masters of Mordor have turned their attention upon the Dead City. I know not why, but their power has grown and whatever reasons they have for coming to Minas Morgul must be fell purposes indeed! We have come to stop them before they achieve... whatever it is they seek to achieve.
'We found Faramir in good health, commanding the Rangers of Ithilien. They entered the Morgul Vale, and it is their design to cleanse the city of evil and reclaim it for King Elessar. Faramir established an encampment, Echad Uial, nearer to the city. If you should travel there, they will be glad to have your aid.'

'You have done much to assist us in Rath Dúath, and I thank you for your efforts. Still, the Morgul Vale is filled with unspeakable dangers. Both the hills and the city must be faced and conquered if we are to banish this evil and cleanse the vale of the corruption that has seized it for so long.'

'${PLAYER}, you have returned! I'll wager your journey to the north was a success if you have returned to assist us at this hour.
'While we successfully secured Talath Úrui, fumes and fire aside, the memory of that place still unsettles me. Borangos has remained hidden, but I saw tendrils of his thought everywhere, and his servants still haunted me. Now they are gone, and it is as if they never were. Where did they go, and for what purpose?
'Pressing matters in the Morgul Vale drew us hither, and I must leave Talath Úrui behind. I will try not to dwell upon it, but still I worry. Let us aid Faramir with his task here, and we will turn to the matter of vanished Borangos when the city is cleansed!
'I am glad you are here.'

Training the Forces

'Have you come to train? Good, I could use someone like you: someone who has seen battle recently! The men who survived the fighting against the Ghâzab Bôron are too exhausted from the pitched retreat to even stand, and most of the soldiers we found here at Díngarth are unfit to take to the battlefield! If they cannot fight in a skirmish upon the Corpse-fields, how can they hope to survive the coming of the Storm of Wrath?
'Spar with these soldiers and teach them the techniques that have allowed you to survive upon the battlefield. I will watch and give you some recommendations after you have finished sparring. After all, I have seen battle with Huneric, Lord of the Thíuda, and I have picked up some of his techniques!'
'I have killed ten Orcs! How many have you bested?'
'I am happy to spar with you, friend!'

'You handled yourself well against eight of the soldiers under my command. It is important to anticipate your enemies' actions before they happen; otherwise you will always be reacting, and not setting the pace of the combat. When you know your enemy well, you can counter their blow before they even make the attack!
'These are the words of my father, and I have seen the truth in them for myself. Heed them well and you will never know defeat!'
'I would rather rest than spar, but Hildvar is looking this way! I suppose we should begin.'
'I have not seen combat in quite some time. Prepare yourself!'
'Let me see your skills. I am a quick learner!'
'I am ready to spar, my friend!'
'Go easy on me. I just recovered from an injury.'
'I am in need of the practice. I hope to learn much under the command of Hildvar.'

Removing Rotten Provisions

'This is embarrassing, friend.
'The siege has dragged on for so long that Díngarth is no longer in the centre of the fighting; the war continues further to the east. We have seen fewer and fewer soldiers within these walls, but ours is still a strategic fortification and must be occupied. The attention of the commanders lies elsewhere, however, and some small things have gone neglected.
'What are these small things? Well... some of the provisions have spoiled, and the meat we kept here at Díngarth has rotted. We do not need for our soldiers to be sickened by turned meat! Go and search the provisions for any which has gone bad and dispose of it.'

'You are sure that you have disposed of all the spoiled food? Good, good!
'I understand that Orcs have been known to feast on spoiled and rotten meat, but that is not something Isildur would allow for his own soldiers, and as his esquire I have taken it upon myself to see they do not have to do so!
'That was a lot of spoiled food, friend. Do we have any provisions at all left in Díngarth? We will need to do something about that....'

'We wait for battle, and the wait is long. It seems longer still when the air is quiet and nothing moves! I must have patience, but I am not the only one who is restless. Look around you, and you will see many others grow weary of this endless waiting!
'Let us brighten their spirits and take the stillness from their minds. How, you ask? Why, stoke the fires and share some stories. It will make the wait feel shorter.'

'For the first time in many days, I heard the low rumble of pleasant talk! There were tales of battles gone, happy memories of children, wives, and husbands waiting at home, loved ones all. Good memories were shared. Did you hear the same?
'We have lasted this long, friend. One day this siege will end, but if it is not to be today, we will not let the passage of another restless day drive us to madness, and give the lie to those already spent. We will wait. One day we will win, and this waiting will be worth it.'

'You have done well to combat the Dead upon the Circle of Sorrow. I ask you now to continue upwards, further into the city. I will stay here and continue to command the Rangers in these first two circles. Our scouts have found a nearby tower that should bring us to the next level: the Circle of Madness.
'Seek out the tower of Barad Elenath. We have all seen the merrevail flying above. It is certain they have already taken the next circle and the towers that stand upon it! When you are ready, prepare to take hold of Barad Elenath!'

'The Circle of Sorrow is nothing like what we just encountered upon the Circle of Wrath. This place is not for the living. No, it is the realm of the Dead. Streams of spirits move through the streets and strange glowing lights flicker among the old buildings. There is much here that we need accomplish before it is safe to delve further into the city.
'You should assist those you can in the Circle of Sorrow. When you have done this, return to me and we shall continue our efforts.'

'It is good to see you, ${PLAYER}. Thank you for helping us secure the tower of Barad Elenath.
'Damrod believes my time in Agarnaith has best qualified me to deal with the threat of Lhaereth the Stained and her minions. I am glad you have also come to this Circle of Madness, though the name is ill-starred.'

'You have done well to assist our efforts within the Circle of Wrath. By using the various towers within the city we can conceal our presence and continue our mission, and I urge you to do the same. Our scouts have found a nearby tower that should bring you to the Circle of Sorrow.
'Seek out this tower of Barad Orhant. It seems quiet and still; nothing stirs within it. But remain alert, and do not underestimate the wiles of those who dwell in Minas Morgul. Gather what is needed and take hold of Barad Orhant!'

'Our first order is to make sense of the city. While its layout is similar to Minas Tirith, we cannot mistake it for the White City! For many years, this place has suffered beneath the might of the Dark Lord and the corruption of the Witch-king.
'This Circle of Wrath is but the first of many challenges we will face here. There are many Orkish forces encamped here, and we must learn what we can of them before we can safely delve further into the city.
'Assist those you can in the Circle of Wrath. When you have done so, return to me and we shall continue our efforts, inward and upward.'

'I thank you for leading the charge, ${PLAYER}. We have successfully secured the tower of Barad Orhant, and now I see the stillness here did not signify emptiness. No, for the Dead can be quite still indeed, when they so desire it! It is a useful lesson.
'You have seen the strange glow upon this Circle, have you not?'

'${PLAYER}, over here, let us rest a moment!
'I must speak to you about something, and perhaps you already have your suspicions about me. I would expect no less from an old friend like you!'
The gruffness in Dolenthol's voice departs.
'It is your friend, Éowyn.'
She briefly reveals her face to you, confirming that she speaks the truth.
'I thought to insist to Faramir that I travel to the Morgul Vale with him, but decided otherwise at the realization that he would be overcome with worry for my safety. What preoccupations does the arrival of love bring to the hearts of men! He must focus on his own task, and not on the safety of his beloved. As at Pelennor, I have come in secret! Until now, the Rangers believe me to be only a new and eager recruit. I reveal this to you because I know you will keep my secret.'

'The paths of the spirits travel to the old Song-house of Lindalírë. There they are tortured and corrupted, by what I do not know and cannot say. We should travel to the old song-house and free those who have yet to be taken by the sorcery of Minas Morgul. We must be careful, for the Circle of Sorrow is full of ghastly horrors!'

'You have returned from patrolling the outer wall of Minas Morgul? What have you found?'
You tell Damrod of the small hatch you discovered at the base of one of the towers.
'I believe this may be our best option for entering the city. That tower is called Barad Angarth. Our scouts have spied Orcs patrolling the very top of the tower, and when night blankets the Vale they have seen the flicker of firelight in the windows. We should expect some resistance inside, but I think they will be unprepared for our attack. Quickly let us gather what is needed and prepare to take hold of Barad Angarth!'

'I thank you, ${PLAYER}, for leading the charge. We have successfully secured the tower of Barad Angarth. This will be our first base of operations in Minas Morgul, but likely not the last! From here we will work towards retaking the Dead City.'
Enter Barad Angarth, the Gate-wardens' Keep

The wall here is smooth and impossible to climb
The main entrance to Minas Morgul is too heavily guarded for a direct assault

'Faramir has commanded me to lead a group of Rangers into the Dead City. I would like you to assist us, ${PLAYER}. There are many challenges that await us within its walls, but the very first awaits us without! We must find a safe way into the city.
'I fear the most direct route, by way of the main gate, may not be the best choice. Our numbers are few and the foes arrayed against us are many. I would like you to patrol the outer wall and search for weaknesses; perhaps there may be some secret entrance, heretofore undetected. There may be some way for us to enter the city while remaining beneath the notice of those who dwell there.'

The entrance to Barad Angarth can be found at the base of the outer wall of Minas Morgul.

'Thank you for treating some of the Rangers. This is but a temporary solution. I would not be surprised if more of us also fall victim to this Morgul ailment. We must search for a remedy.'

A Song of Screams
You have defeated Girithos and put an end to his performance of torment at the Song-house of Lindalírë. The Rangers of Ithilien will be pleased with your efforts.

Minas Ithil was once a beautiful city, a beacon for the arts, and the Song-house of Lindalírë was the jewel in its crown, hosting the finest singers and musicians in all the kingdom. But those days are gone, and now the only sounds in the old song-house are the cries and wails of the Dead. The horrid Girithos oversees the tortured chorus of spirits, slowly corrupting them so they may join the ranks of the Dead who compose the army of Minas Morgul.

'Now that the most pressing task is dealt with, I can now continue to study the strange sorcery that envelops these lands.
'I wish to learn more about the glow of the Dead City, the Morgul-sheen. Would you search the Circle of Sorrow for dust of the same colour as the Morgul-sheen? Perhaps a study of this dust will help us to learn more about the sorcery and the glow both.'

The Witch-king, Lord of the Nazgûl, defeated but enduring

The Witch-king suffered defeat on the battlefield of Mordor Besieged, but it was not to be a lasting death... not while Sauron endured. The Lord of the Nazgûl would return, for his ultimate fate rested in the hand of another still to come, thousands of years hence.

Greatest and most feared of the Nine, the Witch-king stalked the battlefield but rarely, leaving the fortresses of Mordor only at Sauron's most pressing command. In later years the Lord of the Nazgûl would raise from nothing the Land of Angmar, wielding it in furtherance of the Dark Lord's aim to destroy the northern kingdom of Arnor, but at the close of the Second Age that was still far off in the mists of Time. During the Siege of Barad-dûr, the Witch-king could be found testing the weaknesses of the armies arrayed against his master, seeking the most valuable prize of all: information.

The Forsaken Reaver suffered defeat on the battlefield of Mordor Besieged, but it was not to be a lasting death... not while Sauron endured. The Nazgûl would return, for his was an existence beyond ending.

The Great Alliance of Elves and Men stood in defiance of Sauron for long years of siege, but even their bravest heroes came to fear his deadliest servants. These were the Nazgûl, and their number was Nine. They stalked the battlefield of Mordor Besieged, and were its most dangerous scourges.
From the distant south he came, bringing fear and fire to every coast he spied with his glass. His was a reign of blood, and he drew it from all who lived in sight and scent of the Sea. The Bane of Rhûn suffered defeat on the battlefield of Mordor Besieged, but it was not to be a lasting death... not while Sauron endured. The Nazgûl would return, for his was an existence beyond ending.

Once he was a great king in lands far to the east, accustomed to rule and unwilling to bend the knee to any other. But then came a giver of gifts and a promiser of power, and upon accepting these lures, the great king changed. No longer did he rule his lands with mercy, and neither did he remain in his own kingdom. He became Rhûn's bane, and by that name came he to be known as the Bane of Rhûn, and elsewhere.

The Grim Southron, defeated but enduring

The Grim Southron suffered defeat on the battlefield of Mordor Besieged, but it was not to be a lasting death... not while Sauron endured. The Nazgûl would return, for his was an existence beyond ending.

Few among the living ever heard him speak, but his visage was well-known, and feared. They called him the Grim Southron, and while Men quailed at his approach during the Second Age, during the Third the legend of his malice had only grown. In later days it was he that Lhaereth the Stained followed in secret to Dol Guldur, where she discovered Sauron and helped him recover, for a price. 'It has been some time since my last encounter with Ungwetári. Time has only made her more dangerous, more ravenous. Her wound has only increased her aggression and inflamed her hatred. We must do what we can to contain her and the Gúrzyul Rûkhor. To do nothing is to allow calamity.'

'Our efforts will hold the spider-horde in Torech Ungol, for now. Soon we must pursue Ungwetári herself, but until then I ask you and Legolas to return to the Rangers of Ithilien and inform them of Rûkhor's plot. We will soon need a small force to enter the deep tunnels: Remmorchant, the Net of Darkness. That is where we will meet the spider-queen. That is where I will end this. I will send for you when the time is right.'

You quickly inform Mablung of all you learned in Kaslokroz and of what occurred in Torech Ungol. Mablung looks both distressed and awe-inspired.
'Wait, wait, hold a moment! Let me see if I have this right. Rûkhor wants to rouse the wounded Shelob from her lair so she eats everyone and everything, and when she goes back to sleep he wants to take Mordor for himself. That is a terrible, terrible plan! And, not only that, but he convinced the Ungoledain to lead him right to her, and he gave Felgúr back his skin-changing? Then that poor fool went after Shelob, she ATE him, and almost ate you as well, but Celeborn, the Lord of Lórien himself, stepped in to save you?'
You nod and confirm that is the summary of what transpired. He takes a moment to steady himself.
'What a day, ${PLAYER}. What a day. I will send for reinforcements at once and move all available scouts to keep watch on Torech Ungol. No one will come or go without our knowledge. When Celeborn is ready to confront Shelob, we will stand with him.'

'Lord Celeborn speaks true. The Rangers must be made aware of what transpired here. Let us return to Mablung as swiftly as we are able.'
<rgb=#FF0000>You will swiftly travel to Echad Taerdrim!</rgb>

'You must tell me everything, ${PLAYER}.'
You tell Legolas of Rûkhor giving Felgúr back his skin-changing, the encounter with Shelob, and Rûkhor's final taunt. Legolas takes a moment to carefully consider everything.
'I believe his plan was to use Felgúr and yourself to lure Shelob out. He knew you would try to run, and perhaps she would follow you out of Torech Ungol into the Morgul Vale. But, he could not have anticipated Celeborn's appearance.

'Something is wrong. It is as if they cannot hear us at all and are completely entranced by some unseen force. I do not believe we will be able to capture one while they are in this state. We should do what we can to reduce this threat to the Rangers. When we are finished let us regroup in a safer area nearby.'

'I understand what the Rangers meant; the footprints of a Man, and then suddenly...'
Legolas goes silent. His eyes dart around, closely examining the prints.
'I think I see what they could not. The footprints do not disappear, they merely change shape! I am not surprised that the Rangers could not see the footprints of a spider, but they are an old enemy of my people and I know them well. I believe you have already encountered Men who can become spiders, have you not, ${PLAYER}? We have uncovered the presence of the Ungoledain!
'Let us continue in the direction of these tracks. We may find the skin-changers higher in these mountains.'

'These are indeed the Ungoledain. I spoke with Radagast about these strange skin-changers when we were last in the Vales of Anduin. He said they were following the call of one they named Mam Murgwid, and it was his belief that might be Ungwetári herself. There is much I do not understand, but if these Men choose to ally themselves with the spiders, then they are my enemy, and yours! But because they are Men, we should attempt to take one as a prisoner and bring our captive back to Echad Taerdim. An interrogation may yield useful information.'
'This foolish Ungoladan was easily dispatched... perhaps too easily. Why did he not shift into his spider form? It matters not; we desired a prisoner and now we have one.'

'I would like to begin with these mysterious \qwinged men\q. 'Good to see you came out of that attack unscathed, ${PLAYER}. I am no worse off myself, just the gnawed leg from earlier.'
He chuckles and then groans, stroking his injured leg. You ask him how he came to Cirith Ungol and if he knew anything of the tower.
'Ah... after you departed Lhingris, I worked up the courage to enter the tower myself. It was the site of a massacre! Dead Orcs and spiders everywhere, not much of anything alive inside. I continued on and found the gate wide open. I can tell by the look on your face that you know the gate of which I speak! Yes, I entered Torech Ungol itself! Barely made it out alive, but I slew a great many spiders while I could! I then found my way to that cursed forest, Taurlingol. Easier pickings, until that big one chanced upon me and my leg, thinking to have us both for dinner. Heh!
'I will stay here for now. The Rangers are gracious enough hosts. Get out there with Legolas and slay some more spiders for me! As for the tower, hmm, I think the spiders have surely overtaken it by now. If the Orcs and their evil masters attempted to re-take it, they must have failed.'

'You have returned. Forgive me, but I overheard most everything. It is a small camp.
'I am not sure I agree with Mablung's decision regarding the Ungoladan, but perhaps he can be of use to us.'
He turns to Felgúr and speaks just loud enough for him to hear:
'I will be watching you, Ungoladan. If you betray us, you will find an arrow between your eyes.'
Felgúr looks terrified and nods enthusiastically. Legolas turns his attention back to you.
'Atli's account of the tower is also troubling. It may have completely fallen to the spider-horde since we departed. The time has come for us to head towards the Winding Stair and Torech Ungol. We must race to find Rûkhor and the Ungoledain before their wicked plans reach fruition.'

Felgúr stares at the ground, grimacing. His former matriarch's words must have affected him. As you approach, he looks up and speaks, his voice almost cracking with emotion.
'I must speak with you, ${CLASS}! Rûkhor will betray my people, I am sure of it! But they will never accept me as I am now.
'I want to make a deal with the one in charge here! Tell that Mablung I will help him find my people and the Pale Herald if he helps me find a new life among Men. I can no longer hear the call of Mam Murgwid, but I can still sniff out my own kin.'

'Yes, I heard what the Ungoladan said. He was practically shouting! His suggestion is worth consideration. He is of little threat to us now that the enemy knows our location. He cannot skin-change and attack us himself, after all. Furthermore, several of my Rangers were injured in Rûkhor's attack and we are short-handed. Perhaps I can also pity someone who has lost everything....
'Fine. You can tell Felgúr he has a deal. Just make sure you keep an eye on him. He has not earned my trust, just a jot of leniency.'
'Come, let us return to Echad Taerdim.'

'When you are ready, let us depart for Echad Taerdim. Atli needs rest, and his wounds need to be better-tended than I can manage out here. I am also curious to hear if Mablung has learned more from our Ungoladan prisoner.'

'The Pale Herald has finally made his appearance. We must be cautious. A Gúrzyul is already a formidable opponent, but something about his Uruks unnerved me. Did you notice it as well, ${PLAYER}? They possessed the foul aura of dark sorcery. I must think on our next steps. If you would, please make sure the others were unharmed in the assault.'

'It appears your work was successful! Ugrukhôr's forces are preparing to retaliate against Gothmog's Orcs.

'Your work bears fruit, ${PLAYER}! Ugrukhôr's Orcs have moved to attack Gothmog's forces, and truthfully they do so as an unorganized mob, without discipline. If we tread carefully, we may be able to deal decisive blows to both armies!'
'Come with me. I will lead us back to Barad Angarth unnoticed.'

'Hello again, ${PLAYER}. We have learned that the invading Orc army is under the command of the Gúrzyul Ugrukhôr. Clearly, there is very little unity among the former servants of Sauron.
'I do not know why they have not pressed their attack on Gothmog's forces. It seems they entered the city, and then halted. Do they anticipate reinforcements? We must know more before we can act.
'Please venture further into Ugrukhôr's encampment and gather information about the stalemate between the two forces.'

'Ugrukhôr ordered his forces to enter the city, but they were unable to break through to the next tier and have stalled. I believe I know what we must do.
'Drive off the Orc captain Shakfut, and destroy nearby supplies so we can foment dissent among Ugrukhôr's forces.'

'The information you gathered was of the utmost importance. I agree with Dolenthol, our best hope of breaking this siege may be to turn the Orc armies against each other.
'My scouts tell me the Orcs have begun to gather in the western reaches of the Circle of Wrath. If we strike quickly, we might destabilize their forces; with strategy we may goad them into lashing out against Gothmog's forces.

The Tale of Felgúr

'He was surprisingly forthcoming! He must have understood that only useful information could stay our blades. It troubles me greatly that the Gúrzyul Rûkhor is here in Cirith Ungol. Perhaps the situation in the tower is worse than we thought.
'I believe Felgúr may be of further use to us. We should take him back to Echad Taerdim.'
'He appears to be regaining consciousness. Speak to him, and we will determine if he has any use to us alive.'

The Ungoladan groans, clearly in pain from his knock on the head. He realizes what has just happened and grimaces. You ask him if he might answer some questions for you. He sneers and looks away, only to see the Elf-prince's icy glare. He quickly changes his mind and speaks.
'I am Felgúr. Ask your questions.'
You ask him why he did not change into a spider, and why the Ungoledain are here in Cirith Ungol. He looks away. Is he... ashamed?
'I tried to avenge our fallen leader, Mengris Tásakh. The brown one stole my skin-changing. My people turned on me! They tried to eat me! I am nothing without the Spider, but I follow my people. I have no other life. We are here because we follow the call of Mam Murgwid. We must be close now. The others are entranced by it, but I can no longer hear the call. The Spider has left me....'
You turn to Legolas, to gauge if he has heard enough. Felgúr quickly speaks up again, fearing for his life.
'There is one other thing I must say! My people are being led astray by an outsider. A dark one! You must listen!'
'Please, hear what I must say!'
'I do not trust this \qPale Herald\q, but I am exiled and can do nothing. Kill me if you want. I have no fear of death now.'

The Sequestered Spiders

'I apologize for not arriving sooner, ${PLAYER}. I did see the spider you fought, and my suspicions were proven correct: these are the Mirkwood spiders, Iphantamel's own brood. This forest is too small to hold all that vanished from Eryn Lasgalen, however. Perhaps some have already entered Torech Ungol. I admit I do not fully understand the quarrelling between spiders. It matters not. The old enemy of my people has been found, and we must deal out vengeance upon them.
'I must tend to Atli's wounds, thus I must rely on you to venture into Taurlingol and slay my enemies for me. I know that you are capable of this task.'
You ask Legolas how he and Atli are acquainted. He allows the briefest hint of a smile to cross his face.
'Ah, I encountered him when we were last in Lhingris, in a very similar situation, in fact. He was engaged in combat with several very large brood-mothers, and I stepped in to assist him. I believe he was embarrassed, and accused me of \qstealing his kill\q.
'But that is quite absurd!'

'Well done, ${PLAYER}. With the death of Iphantamel's daughters, the rest of the spiders will likely disperse into Cirith Ungol. I will return to track and kill them myself, one by one. For now, we must escort Atli to Echad Taerdim. He should be able to travel on his wounded leg, but it is not safe to remain here.'

'Oof, thanks for the assistance, ${PLAYER}. And Legolas is here as well! I am happy to see some faces with fewer than eight eyes! It also helps that you're not trying to devour me. Haha! Erk....'
Atli doubles over and grabs his leg. His injuries seem to be worse than he let on.
'Aye, she chewed up my leg something fierce. Oh, don't worry about me, I will be fine. I just need to rest a bit....'

'I doubt there is much else to learn here, ${PLAYER}. I would like to continue on with our mission. We should next investigate the spiders to the east. The Rangers report the spiders there isolate themselves from the spiders of Torech Ungol. I suspect I may know their reasons for this, but I would like to confirm my suspicions with my own eyes before I share my thoughts.
'I will bring the Ungoladan prisoner back to Echad Taerdim. Mablung may wish to question Felgúr himself. I will meet you near the spider-infested forest, Taurlingol.'

'Now that the crisis is averted, I will return my focus to the Halls of Black Lore. It is undoubtedly in the best interests of the Free Peoples that everything inside is removed from the world. However, we witnessed Lhaereth adding the recipe for her perfected plague to the archive.

The Business of Spiders

'Welcome to Cirith Ungol, ${PLAYER}. I have much unfinished business to manage here, and I would appreciate the help of a skilled and trusted friend such as you.
'When we last left the tower of Cirith Ungol, it was besieged by spiders; if the Gúrzyul failed to reinforce the garrison, the tower might fall to the spiders, and that would unleash the spiders upon Gorgoroth, and perhaps the larger world! I have heard no reports of spider activity beyond Lhingris, so perhaps the Orcs prevailed. We will have to investigate.
'There is also the matter of the Mirkwood spiders. When my father faced our old enemy Iphantamel, she said that all of her daughters had left her. We suspect that they may have come here, at the call of their true mother.
'Finally, we must discover if Ungwetári yet lives. As valiant as Master Samwise is, I do not believe she would have succumbed to such a small wound, though it was inflicted by a courageous heart. She is ancient and powerful.
'There is much to do. We should begin by questioning the Rangers of Ithilien. They have begun scouting the area, and may already have some answers to our many questions.'

'Greetings, ${PLAYER}. How have you fared since our last meeting? I am certainly glad for the help of Legolas and yourself. You are among the most skilled ${CLASS}s I have ever met.
'Our goal in Cirith Ungol is to try to establish a knowledge of any threats to Ithilien that may still exist in this place. Specifically, where the spider presence is, their numbers, and if the Orcs have any forces here. Indeed, despite Shelob's apparent defeat, we have already established that the spiders linger still. As of yet, we have found no evidence of Shelob herself, living or dead, but have found many of her brood.
'We know not the situation in the tower. I sent some Rangers to approach as close as they could to it, which is not especially close, for the path is treacherous and spider-infested. They reported they could detect little Orc activity on this side of the tower. I do not know if they have simply moved the garrison closer to Dor Amarth, or if they have abandoned the tower entirely.
'We also noticed when we set up camp here that someone, likely an uruk based on the size of the prints, had passed this way very recently, heading east toward the tower. Mírthel and Gladhir may have more information for you.'

'Good to see you again, ${PLAYER}! I am afraid I have little time to catch up. We have come to a dangerous place, and there is much to be done. I can share what information I have.
'There is very little spider presence on the west side of Cirith Ungol, which does not surprise me as we believe they are mainly coming from Torech Ungol itself. However, we have found one puzzling thing for which I have no explanation: in several places, we have found sets of footprints—alike that of Men both in shape and size—that seem to disappear mid-stride! The others are speculating that they sprouted wings and flew! I am not sure I believe that, but it is certainly worth looking into. See if you can find some of these footprints to the north-west.'

You relay to Legolas all of the information the Rangers shared with you.
'Interesting. I am glad to have such skilled Rangers at our disposal. They have saved us a great deal of time.'
Legolas' attention briefly drifts away as he considers all you have said.
'Several mysteries now need to be unravelled. Why did the Uruk-hai pass this way? Did they come from the city or somewhere else? If they were headed to the tower, does that mean the pass from the east is no longer accessible to them? What are these spiders that sequester themselves from the others? What do these strange footprints mean, where Men can suddenly disappear mid-stride? We have much to consider, and much ground to cover.'

'Greetings, ${PLAYER}. It gladdens me to see a friendly face on the road! Legolas has asked for you. He is waiting at Mablung's camp just ahead. To reach it, just take this pass behind me and head up the Straight Stair. Be warned, if you are headed into Cirith Ungol, there will be many stairs and steep climbs in your future! And, of course, there's the spiders. Many, many spiders.'
He shivers at the thought, and bids you farewell.

'Greetings, ${PLAYER}! How have you fared since the Battle of the Black Gate? I have done some scouting myself, and can tell you what I saw.
'The spider presence is dense to the east, as expected. They continuously flow out of Torech Ungol like a foul stream. Among them are also several horrible varieties of gredbyg. None of this is surprising, but in the north-east I found a forest completely overwhelmed by webs, and a large brood of spiders that seemed to be separating themselves from the ones in Torech Ungol. Make of that what you will!'
Legolas waves to you as you approach the camp

'And so ends the Black Book of Mordor,' Gandalf murmurs with satisfaction
Gandalf has presented you with a choice concerning the ultimate disposition of the Black Book of Mordor.
Deliver the Black Book to Khîl Tale-spinner in his home

'Yes, ${PLAYER}, I have been expecting you. Together we have unearthed every secret hidden within the Black Book of Mordor by Vóin and Bozhéna, the long-distant dwarves who authored it. Only one question remains: what is to be done with the book now?
'I see a number of possibilities, my friend. It was Khîl Tale-spinner who gave the book into our keeping, and his claim is perhaps the strongest. Vóin and Bozhéna were his thrice-great grandparents, and if the book is to be kept by anyone still living today in Middle-earth, we might do worse than a Zhélruka relative of its authors.
'But there is another interest to be considered. The Black Book of Mordor contains a great deal of information that would be prized by scholars concerning the history of Gondor and the fate of King Eärnur. The book is truly deserving of a place of honour in the Houses of Lore in Minas Tirith. The scholar Covadil would gratefully accept the donation of it, and in that way Vóin's wish for Eärnur's struggle to be remembered in the future will truly be fulfilled.
'There is one other claim to the Black Book, ${PLAYER}. Indeed, the nobility of this claim might be doubted, but I believe it is still worth considering. I speak of the claim of Karazgar, the Weeping Warrior, who asked that you steal the book and deliver it to him. Yes, I knew of your encounter with him at the Old Ford. I chose not to say anything, but I am pleased my trust in you was not misplaced, and we were able to decipher the last of the book's mysteries.
'Why then might we entertain Karazgar's request, ${PLAYER}? Why, it is for that very reason: we know what the book says, and he does not. He believes it contains the secret to preventing his decline, or securing his power... but it does not. It does contain a great deal of confusion and mystery for one who does not know how to read it, and that is to say nothing of the trick with the shard of beacon-glass. What might he give up in exchange for a book he thinks will be of use to him, but is not, and cannot be? It may be an academic question, but those are always of great interest to me.
'So I leave the disposition of the Black Book of Mordor to you, my friend. Choose who should have it, and deliver it either to Khîl Tale-spinner in Járnfast, Covadil in the Houses of Lore in Minas Tirith, or Karazgar at the Old Ford. I leave the decision up to you, and with this choice we will close the Black Book of Mordor for good. I thank you again, ${PLAYER}.'

'Welcome back, my friend! Were you able to solve the mystery of the glass-shard and Vóin's book? Did Gandalf have any ideas?'
For a number of hours you describe what you learned from the secret writing in the Black Book, and conclude at last that your need for the tome has ended.
'You are giving it back to me? Well, I thank you for this! It seems that it properly belongs here in the chamber Vóin built, and with your assurance that it is not truly a tome of evil, I should think it will be quite safe to keep it here!
'Like my thrice-great grandmother Bozhéna, I too have found the aura of this hidden chamber to be one of peace and comfort. I am quite pleased to know more of these relatives of mine, who once were mere names, but now are much more than that! And to think my thrice-great grandfather Vóin defied the Witch-king himself, and not only that, but he may have at last ended his days in the halls of Thafar-gathol itself!
'Now that is a tale, ${PLAYER}. That is a tale indeed! Thank you for upholding your end of the bargain and delivering the Black Book back into my keeping, where it belongs. You will be my friend for always, good ${RACE}.'

'Hello again, my friend! Did the kingsfoil I give to you cure your headaches? I have some more here if you... oh, you are not here for kingsfoil? What brings you then to the Houses of Lore?'
You explain to Covadil that you have come into possession of a book that has much to say concerning the history of Gondor and you would like it to find a place on the shelves among other such tomes. You hand her the glass shard and begin to describe the account contained within the pages of the Black Book, but before you have gone very far Covadil interrupts with an apologetic smile.
'It isn't really up to me, but I can give the book to the masters, and they will study it for acceptability. If they deem it merits inclusion, and truly does contain knowledge of use to Gondor, they will add it to the collection.'
You wonder aloud whether any of the scholars in the Houses of Lore can read ancient Zhélruka runes.
'Oh, I doubt it,' she responds. 'I think I will just add it to the shelves myself. If you say this contains important historical knowledge, I believe you! None today can say what might be important to know for tomorrow! I say we preserve this tome for future scholars to mull over!'
Covadil takes the Black Book from you and carefully tucks the glass shard inside the cover.
'I look forward to reading it, ${PLAYER}! I have been trying to decide which language I should next set my sights upon, and it seems I have received my course: the runes of the ancient Zhélruka! Thank you once again, my friend! The Black Book will remain here in the Houses of Lore, waiting to enrich the knowledge of future interested scholars, and I am glad to have played a part in it!'

'I leave the disposition of the Black Book of Mordor to you, my friend. Choose who should have it, and deliver it either to Khîl Tale-spinner in Járnfast, Covadil in the Houses of Lore in Minas Tirith, or Karazgar at the Old Ford. I leave the decision up to you, and with this choice we will close the Black Book of Mordor for good. I thank you again, ${PLAYER}.'

Fires and Shadowfells

'My plan progresses apace! Even from here I saw the fires burning brightly across the Shadowfells! You have done better than I hoped. I shall alert the others.
'Those fires will not burn forever, and I fear the flame of my desire for battle might outlast them! May we attack soon, before they go out!'

'If we are to press the attack upon the tower of Barad-dûr, we will need to have a distraction. Otherwise the attack will fail before it is barely begun! I have spent many years in the mines, and the darkness of the Shadowfells is not unlike the caverns with which I am familiar.
'What is the best way to distract the darkness, you ask? Why, with fire, of course! I ask you to light fires throughout Emyn Duir, for the sorcerous creatures of the Shadowfells will not be able to abide their light, and the flames will draw the attention of anyone hereabout.
'By Durin's beard, I am certain this plan will work! It just makes sense, my friend, does it not?'

A Trap Upon Emyn Duir

You have set all of Terna's traps in the Emyn Duir encampments. It would be best not to return to Halroth unless absolutely necessary, for if you were followed you might endanger the secrecy of the mission. But you know Terna would be satisfied by the thought of enemies stumbling into her traps within their own camps, and you can't help but smile.

'I have scouted the Emyn Duir, and I have decided if we are to remain in secret here at Halroth, we must do something about the enemy forces that inhabit the lands nearby. I thought we might set traps around the mountain passes near Halroth, but I fear that might alert these very foes to our presence!
'And what happened then? Why, I had a brilliant thought! What about laying traps within their own encampments, all in secret? This would certainly confuse them, and they would not even think to look for us here. I have already made the traps. Would you be willing to sneak into several enemy encampments in order to set them in place? I am sure you would enjoy it!'

The New Recruit

'Thank you, my friend. I have learned much in the time that we have spent together. I am now to report to Hildvar to continue my combat training. I am sure that we will soon fight side-by-side, and let our foes beware!'

After so many years besieging Mordor, the Great Alliance is still in need of new recruits. Upon entering Díngarth you receive a missive: you have been entrusted with a new soldier in hopes that you can mentor and train the young man. You should seek him out as soon as you are able.

'Are you the one sent to train me? I look forward to learning all that you know! I was but a child when the war began, but now I am a man grown. Is it true that an Easterling horde is on its way?
'Oh, I almost forgot, I have a note for you. I have been waiting here so... I may have already read it. I hope you do not mind! It says that many great warriors have joined the battle and we should assist them. I am ready to leave, whenever you are ready!'

'${PLAYER}!
'It is good to see you, my friend. I have enjoyed our time together in Ered Luin, but this is not my home.
'You of all dwarves must understand! What has become of your people? Did Lethi and Vaski win their freedom? What of the others? I know it must seem a terrible thought, but I am sure one day you shall return to Mordor. But, it will be to see that your people at last live free from the Enemy!
'I know not where my journey shall take me, but I hope our paths cross again. After all, you shall have even more tales to tell then... and I think I shall have a few of my own!
'Farewell, ${PLAYER}.'

'Oh, I almost forgot!
'Your Dourhand companion, Nagli, is planning to depart on a journey of his own. He is a curious, helpful dwarf... unlike many of the Dourhands I have known. I must admit, I will miss seeing him in Frerin's Court.

'${PLAYER}, you have heeded my call, as I knew you would. You are a faithful ally to the Rangers of Ithilien.
'Faramir has given me orders to begin the long and arduous task of cleansing the Morgul Vale. Our hope is for this valley to once again be a part of Ithilien and Gondor. I shall be focused on the Dead City of Minas Morgul, while my fellow Rangers, Ereblen and Tordoron will focus on the whole of the Vale. There are many tasks in the days ahead.
'Our first task is to retrieve Lhaereth's book on her Great Plague. I am sure it can still be found within the Hall of Black Lore. Will you retrieve the book for us?'

You have done much to aid those allies of the White Company in Imlad Morgul. Thurindol, a Ranger of Ithilien calls upon you to lead the charge in reclaiming Imlad Morgul from the dark grasp surrounding the once proud city of Minas Ithil. You should speak to Thurindol, Ereblen, and Tordoron at Echad Uial as soon as you are able.

'You make a grave mistake if you have come to kill me, ${RACE}. What will that accomplish, hmm?
'What? You want a book from my master's archives?! What a foolish request!'
You raise your weapon at the Black Númenórean.
'Ah... perhaps we could arrange a trade. You see, a book from the archives went missing last night. If you retrieve it for me, I could transcribe this book of Lhaereth's that you seek and give you a copy? All I know is that the doors to the archives remain locked. Whoever stole the book enters without a use for doors. Be quick, for I am not certain how long my offer for a trade will stand, ${CLASS}.'

'It is good to see you again, ${PLAYER}. Injury from the Battle at the Black Gate prevented me from joining the Mordor expedition. Now that my injuries have healed, I have been called upon by Thurindol to assist in the reclamation of Minas Ithil. I am ready to provide every skill that I have mastered since becoming a Ranger of Ithilien.
'Speak with me if you wish for tasks and rewards in assisting with the reclamation of Minas Ithil.'

'My good friend, ${PLAYER}! I was hoping we would one day adventure together again! I have been quite busy since we last parted, securing Ithilien. When the White Company entered Imlad Morgul, I knew I must follow, so I pleaded with Captain Faramir to reassign me. I am here to follow Thurindol's orders and assist any Ranger in need.
'Speak with me if you wish for tasks and rewards in assisting with the reclamation of Minas Ithil.'

'Ah, I had thought this journal lost! You are quite resourceful to have reconstructed this account.
'Indeed, the words here-in are mine. All who were present were shaken to the core by the storm Gil-galad brought forth that day. I am sure you feel the same. Does that surprise you? Even Kings feel fear in the face of real power. And still, the knowledge that the Dark Lord has a ring of power all his own brings me pause. We must bury that fear, and hold on to our courage. This is our last stand against the darkness; Courage is our greatest weapon.'
He hands you the spine from which the journal pages originated.
'Keep this journal for yourself. Let it be a constant reminder of the power of our Great Alliance, and give you hope in the battles to come. The Enemy may have great power, but so do we.'

'${PLAYER}, you live! I was worried. You took a long time to leave Seregost and you spent all of it swinging at things that weren't there and yelling at things that weren't there. Then you collapsed and I had to drag you all the way here! I really need a nap now!'
You assure Viznak that you are well enough to continue your journey and do not need to be dragged all the way back to Minas Morgul.
'Good! Oh, I guess this is when we part ways. Thanks for coming back to my home with me. Makes coming home not so lonely. Bye bye now!'
'Oh, ho, I'm glad to be home! Viznak needs less excitement and more naps for a while. Maybe then I can be ruler of Agarnaith again! It's my swamp, but you can come visit!'

'${PLAYER}, you have returned. Was Viznak able to assist you in locating the third artifact?
'I see, you travelled to Agarnaith and undertook a trial of madness. I am glad you were able to overcome such a test of strength in both mind and body.'

'I'm back! Some good to tell and some bad to tell. Which first, good?
'Good is I know where the shiny is! Bad is that it's back in Agarnaith!
'${PLAYER}, I want to go home now anyway. Maybe we could go back to Agarnaith together. I'll help you get the shiny you want too! What do you say?'

'I overheard those serving the blight lady. They took the shiny to the big keep. Of course they did! It's not very guarded so we should be able to sneak in and get the shiny easily! Come on, let's go!'
'I'm still here. Thanks for the greetings! You have crafty task for Viznak? Sure, why not? I don't like the Blight Lady much anyhow. I'll find that shiny for you! You wait here. Be back soon!'

'It would seem each artifact presents a great challenge for those who seek its destruction. I believe we can assume the third rests somewhere in the Circle of Madness. Lhaereth rules this section of the city, and I do not advise a direct confrontation with her. No, we must instead tread with caution. We must find where the third artifact rests.
'Is it true that you have befriended a goblin from Agarnaith, ${PLAYER}? Perhaps a goblin could sneak into the Circle of Madness and learn things that we could not! I never would have thought that I would ask a goblin for assistance. Would you speak with this Viznak for me?'

Talk to Cuilion
'I'd hoped it would be you, ${PLAYER}.'

'I have received troubling news from Taen Orwath.
'It seems that Gothmog had plans beyond Minas Morgul. Word has spread of a place named Thuringwath. It is believed that the deathly cleft, Falch Gurth, that runs through the Mountains of Shadow might lead to it.
'I do not know what might be found in Thuringwath, but from what I have heard, it is nothing good. We have twice-walked bravely through the lands of the Enemy, my friend, but something about this leaves me uneasy. What need has evil to conceal itself in the lands of the Dark Lord?
'When you are prepared, ride for Taen Orwath. I hope my dread is for naught, ${PLAYER}.'

Taen Orwath can be found in the southern eastern hills of Rath Dúath.

'I am told that beyond this darkness lies Thuringwath, the Valley of Secret Shadow.
'It is difficult to believe the Enemy could have hidden such a place so near to Minas Ithil of old, but it is that uncertainty which has led me here.
'Have the Enemy's works crumbled to naught behind a veil of shadow? Or does some evil still dwell beneath the notice of Gondor?
'I must know the truth of it, but I do not wish to walk alone. Will you accompany me, ${PLAYER}?'
'Come, ${PLAYER}.'
'It is worse than I feared, ${PLAYER}.'
The Secret Shadow
Thuringwath, the Valley of Secret Shadow, has remained hidden among the slopes of Ephel Dúath since the Second Age of the world.

'I did not expect help to come so soon, but... we are in dire need of it.
'Nidhlas... is gone.'

'Have you heard all the talk of Thuringwath, ${PLAYER}?
'Prince Faramir told us to hold our post, but after one of ours found the way into Falch Gurth, it wasn't long before Nidhlas took his men into the pass.
'It's been days and I've heard no word from him or his men. To be honest, I don't care if the rumours are true or not.
'All I ask is that you go into Falch Gurth to find Nidhlas and his men. Will you aid me?'

Find Cannoth east of Barad Arthir

'There have been many worrying disappearances near Achathras, east of this location. Cannoth journeyed in that direction to scout a nearby pass, and we are waiting for word. Aye, we wait still, and longer than we expected. Has he run into trouble, or has some trouble run into him? Find him and learn what happened, if you can.'

'Your arrival is well-timed, for things are worse here than I feared! Through this archway, a path winds upward along the mountainside. There lies Gath Daeroval, the Shadow-roost. This place is home to Khatlob, the massive, voracious brood-mother of the roost. At least, so say the Orcs; it sounds from their talk that she laid the eggs from which sprang the terrible flying mounts ridden by the Witch-king and the rest of the Nazgûl.
'She is not the only danger within. The lower reaches are said to be guarded by Khúrthak the Rent, a great Olog that has long stood guard over this area... and over Khatlob. It sounds to me as if he is both her jailor and her protector. The Orcs say he suffered a grievous injury from her claws, and now fears to get too near.
'Such beasts that Khatlob bears can work great evil upon our forces in Imlad Morgul, and elsewhere. When you are prepared, you should follow the path and put an end to the brood-mother and her terrible spawn!'
Gone Missing
Cannoth was sent to investigate the disappearances of several allies, but now Cannoth himself has also vanished.

'We didn't make it far the first night.
'A dark cloud, like some unearthly wall of shadow, appeared in our path. Only Nidhlas was brave enough to reach out into the darkness, but he withdrew his hand almost at once. It was as if a deathly chill had taken hold of his arm!
'I thought that was going to be the end of it, but Nidhlas insisted that we make camp... and so we did. The rain fell cold, and we had too few tents. Many of us took ill in the night, but Nidhlas led the rest beyond the shadows at first light.
'See for yourself, ${PLAYER}. It is some old devilry, I think!'

Dolenthol and a number of Rangers stand amid a swath of slain Orcs

'As soon as we entered the Circle, Gothmog's Orcs were upon us. Prince Faramir and a few of his men were able to press deeper into the city, but many of our number were separated in the fighting.
'I do not know how many we have lost... and I do not know if the Prince still lives. If you would help me to find the others, I can lead the search for Faramir myself.
'If you find any lost bands of Rangers in the Circle of Death, tell them to meet us before the Tower of the Crescent Moon. If you don't... that is where you will find us.'

Talk to Candúr in Barad Arthir

'Prince Faramir believes it would be ill-advised to press our attack against Gothmog from Barad Arthir. I am inclined to agree.
'We may have taken the tower, but our position is precarious. The Circle of Despair has not been secured, and I dread to think what awaits us in the Circle of Death.
'If we do not first hold the Circle of Despair, we may soon find ourselves surrounded... and fighting a losing battle.
'To that end, Dornach has led a small company into the Circle of Despair. I would ask that you aid him as best you can.'

'It was a sorry tale Dornach told me of those who fell in the Circle of Mirth, but it heartens me to know that the Circle of Despair has been made safe.
'I have received word that reinforcements are already ascending the Dead City to support our efforts in the tower.
'We could not have done it without you, ${PLAYER}.'

'While you worked to secure the Circle of Despair, we worked to fortify the defences of Barad Arthir.
'It is unlikely Gothmog will be able to muster enough forces to breach the walls of the tower, but I have seen more surprising things in my time. We shall remain vigilant.
'After you left the tower, Prince Faramir led his company into the Circle of Death. I believe the Prince means to prepare a final assault against Gothmog, but he has kept his plans hidden... even from me.
'Once you have secured the Circle of Despair, please return to me.'

'You have done well, ${PLAYER}, and I hear Prince Faramir has changed his mind regarding the Dead City.
'It would be a shame to let Minas Ithil fall to its final ruin by the hand of Gondor, I think. It is good he believes so as well.
'These are glad tidings, but alas, there is another matter to discuss.'

'As soon as we entered the Circle, Gothmog's Orcs were upon us. We triumphed, but many bands of Rangers were scattered about the Circle in the fighting.
'I do not know how many we have lost... but I must believe Faramir and his men found refuge in the higher reaches of the Dead City. If you would help me to find the others, I will see that the Prince and his company are reunited.
'When you have done what you can, meet me near the Tower of the Crescent Moon.'

'It is a bright day for Gondor, ${PLAYER}, even in such a place of darkness.
'It had come to the mind of King Elessar that Minas Morgul might need to be razed to its lowest stones. Knowing what I do of the terror that still lingers upon Ithilien, even if Gothmog were defeated, I could not see another way. Yet, the words of Galadriel have kindled in my heart a desire to preserve what was lost so long ago.
'When at last we triumph over Gothmog, I shall plead to King Elessar to spare the Dead City that it might be restored by the hand of Gondor. Its stones shall be reshaped, its halls rebuilt, its archives written anew... and it shall again be Minas Ithil.
'Whether you knew of Éowyn's deception, I will not ask. I must admit, I had begun to suspect it myself not long after we entered the Circle of Death. Lady Éowyn is a hale warrior, finer than many Men of Gondor, and she need not answer for decisions made out of loyalty... or love.'

'We are fortunate to have an ally like you, ${PLAYER}.
'Faramir's heart is lightened, and the end of this strife no longer seems so distant. Many dark days still lay ahead of us, but we shall overcome all the evils that remain in this place.
'You have done much for me... and for Faramir. That we have come to the end of things together is all I can ask.'
'Let us see what lies hidden in Uialrond, ${PLAYER}.'

'I fear that Gothmog has laid a trap for us, ${PLAYER}.
'If we were to assail the Tower of the Crescent Moon, would we not be doing exactly as Gothmog intends? There is foul magic upon this city... and much of it seems to lead here to Uialrond. I know little of it save for old tales, but it is said that it was once a great council-hall of Minas Ithil. Yet, when I reach to open its doors... I feel some sort of presence resist me. Has Gothmog locked some evil away in Uialrond to be unleashed upon us?
'I cannot be certain, but I will not allow Gothmog to gain the advantage through deception. I have seen great, terrible wards of dread throughout the Circle of Death. I know not their true purpose, but if their magic holds fast the doors of Uialrond, they must be destroyed.
'We must learn what lies within Uialrond!'

'Once this was the Circle of Mirth, ${PLAYER}, but it does not seem so now. There are strange things afoot in this Circle of Despair.
'I saw Ugrukhôr's Orcs quail before shades of the Dead, and I do not blame them. Something terrible has happened here, for the Dead cackle and weep in equal measure. Those that laugh seem the cruelest spirits, and those that cry seem fearful even in death.
'If some knowledge of Ugrukhôr's plans can be gleaned from these Orcs, I will consider our efforts fruitful, but I would much like to know what terrible fate has befallen these shades of Gondor.'

'What a terrible spirit!
'I did not wish to believe it, but I am filled with sorrow for those who fell in the old Circle of Mirth. To be taken, still living, to the baths and drowned in its waters... it is unthinkable!
'We have done much to secure the Circle of Despair, and I would be glad to leave this place behind.
'Let us meet back in Barad Arthir, and look to the days ahead.'

'It is time we learned what has stirred the Dead in the Circle of Despair, and I believe whatever it is lurks within the old-bathhouse.
'Whatever foul magic has possessed these suits of armour must be borne of the unstilled waters of the baths. We shall need to put them to rest if we are to reach the bath-house unhindered.
'Come, ${PLAYER}. The sooner this is done, the sooner we can rejoin the others.'

'According to these orders, Ugrukhôr's forces make for Barad Cúron at all cost.
'Lhaereth and her merrevail shall serve to harry Gothmog's forces, and Ugrukhôr's forces will shatter the doors of the Tower of the Crescent Moon. When that is done, there is little hope of escape for Gothmog, but it seems foolhardy to treat his downfall as a certainty.
