<rgb=#FF0000>You may enter this instance by using the Instance Join panel. </rgb>

'${PLAYER}! Ah, if you have returned, that must mean it is time for Faeron's plan... Not that I'm not happy to see you! I suppose I'm just a bit nervous to be heading back to that place. Something about that Dark Archivist unnerved me. He barely reacted when Lhaereth struck him down!
'I will of course be ready to accompany you if that is your choice! The three of us conquered Seregost together, after all. What trouble could a library be?'

You hand Faeron the red tome given to you by Dolguzigir. His expression turns grim as he takes it. He opens it, and flips through the pages. The contents appear to disgust him, and he slams it shut.
'He did not deceive you; this is indeed the Great Plague recipe, penned by Lhaereth herself. I will make sure this is delivered to the scholars in Minas Tirith. With this, as distasteful as this knowledge is, we will have a chance. If Lhaereth deploys her plague again, the Free Peoples will endure.'
Word has reached you that the Rangers Faeron and Rhadrog are ready to infiltrate the Halls of Black Lore. You should return to the Stargazer's Spire to assist them.

You ask Dolguzigir for Lhaereth's recipe for the Great Plague. He cackles, and snaps his fingers. A blood-red tome materializes directly into your hands.
'As you wish, mortal! I look forward to seeing the fallout of Men gaining this knowledge!'

'Welcome back, ${PLAYER}. The time has come to return to the Halls of Black Lore. I hope you are ready.
'I have kept a vigilant watch on the Circle of Madness since you departed. Lhaereth's forces have ceased their frenzied attacks, as it seems whatever she seeks is not within the city. The Dark Archivist, Dolguzigir, has never left the Halls, but I have seen his forces, mostly some variety of Morgul Cultists, coming and going. They have finally let their guard down, if only slightly. If we wish to sneak in, this is our best chance! To that end, I have decided that you should take the lead on this mission.
'You are renowned for your skill, ${PLAYER}. I have no doubt that you have many allies whom you may call upon. If you deem it our best chance, you may muster a force to storm the Halls and take the plague recipe by force. Otherwise, Rhadrog and I will accompany you.
'Speak with Rhadrog, and let him know what you decide. And remember, we know not what strength the Dark Archivist possesses, but we should not underestimate him. He did dare to stand up to Lhaereth herself.'

Enter the Remmorchant
'We will hold these Bloodless Uruk-hai at bay! You must defeat Rûkhor at any cost!'
'Thank you, ${PLAYER}, for standing here with me before this terrible darkness. I cannot conquer it alone.'

'It… is done. Together we have done what I could not have accomplished alone. Ungwetári will no longer befoul this world, and I will be able to sail to the Undying Lands with peace in my heart. My sworn duty to defeat her has finally been fulfilled.
'Whether the Free Peoples learn of your heroism here or not, know that you have done them a great service this day. With the fall of another of the ancient evils, the world moves ever closer to the dawn of the Fourth Age. I am gladdened to know that heroes like you will be here to greet it.'

'Hail, ${PLAYER}. Now that you have arrived safely, final preparations can begin.'
You sense no trepidation in Celeborn's voice, only clarity and focus. He brings a calming presence to the soldiers in the camp.
'The time is nearly upon us, ${PLAYER}. I have only one task for you. You must call forth your most powerful allies and begin your preparations. We will need your great combat-skill if we are to succeed in this endeavour.'
Celeborn turns from you and looks toward the Remmorchant. His face hardens, the first sign of worry you have seen from him since you arrived.
'To be forthright, ${PLAYER}, I am not certain it is within our power to truly defeat her. When last we met, I was only able to seal her away. Our blades were unable to pierce her hide, though they were of finest Beleriand-make. But, I promise you this: we will not leave this place without finding a way to eliminate the danger posed by Ungwetári. It is time for her reign of terror to finally end.'

Word has reached you that Celeborn and the Rangers of Ithilien are prepared to enter the Remmorchant. They have called for your aid. You should return to Echad Taerdim in Cirith Ungol and report to Mablung.

'Forgive my coldness, ${PLAYER}, but was Felgúr even an ally to us in the end? Once he regained his spider-form, he quickly abandoned you.'
You suggest that perhaps Shelob's call was so overwhelming he was forced to obey it. The other Ungoledain were completely entranced by it, after all. Legolas's expression softens slightly.
'Perhaps you are right. It matters little. Felgúr is dead, and all that is in our power now is to avenge him.'
'You and your fellows must defeat Bratha Tasakh while we defend this tunnel. We cannot risk an attack from the rear while we are engaged with such a powerful foe. I will help you however I can.'
'There are too many of them! You must find a way to stem the tide of spiders and gredbyg so we can press on!'

'Welcome back, ${PLAYER}. If you are here, Celeborn's call must have gone out. The time to enter the Remmorchant is upon us.'
You can sense his unease as he says these words. You ask if anything is wrong.
'Ah, worry not, friend, I am just a little on edge. I know not what horrors I am sending my men to fight inside that fell pit. Well, save for one. She might overmatch an army, and we can send but a few into those sprawling tunnels. This is no battle such as that at the Black Gate, no, this will be a fight in cramped spaces and deepest darkness! But, we will do our part, no matter what it costs us.
'We have set up a small staging area near the entrance to the Remmorchant. The Rangers of Ithilien and the Galadhrim of Lothlórien have gathered. You should go on ahead. Legolas and Celeborn will be awaiting your arrival. I will see you there!'

'I need more loyal warriors to reinforce me! I ask you to return to my father at the Lonely Mountain and request that he send as many Longbeard warriors as he can spare. Too many were lost when the Frost-horde attacked, and I would not have us outnumbered by... by foes.'
'I have said my say. If Durin does not like the truth I speak, he is welcome to tell me himself.'
'Durin does not belong here. He is untested and unproven, and should go back to the Lonely Mountain with the rest of the Longbeards.'
'Durin should keep the Red Axe close. There are too few Longbeards at Skarháld for me to sleep comfortably, and he should not either.'
'Welcome back, my adventuring friend! What news of my son? What news do you bring of Durin? Has he brought to heel the Zhélruka that travelled without leave across my lands?'

'Things have not been going as well here as I might have hoped. I have been trying to ease tensions among the dwarves that have come to Skarháld, but it has not been easy. The Longbeards, Zhélruka, and Stout-axes here all take exception with each other, mostly for trifling matters. All three of these dwarf-companies suffered grievous losses at the teeth and claws of the Frost-horde, under Karazgar's direction, but we have seen no sign of the worms since you departed. The Weeping Warrior himself has not reappeared in that time... do you know anything about that, ${PLAYER}?
'But now it falls to me to get these dwarf-clans working together, and that is no easy thing. Perhaps you can ask members of each family what they think I should do on their behalf? Stout-axes, Zhélruka, and Longbeards up the stairs here at Skarháld are sure to give you their opinions on this subject, and it may help me decide how best to proceed.'
Durin is on the lowest level of Skarháld, near the stable-master, waiting for your report from the three dwarf-clans who inhabit the mountain fortress.

<rgb=#00FF00>It is recommended, but not required, that you complete 'The Black Book of Mordor' before beginning 'The Legacy of Durin and the Trials of the Dwarves.'</rgb>
'You have returned, my friend! I did not know when your adventures to the south might release you, but I am pleased it was sooner and not later! It is good to see you!'
Durin claps you heartily on the back. Then he lowers his voice and warily eyes the courtyard.
'Truthfully, things have not been going as well as I might have hoped. I have been trying to ease tensions among the dwarves that have come to Skarháld, but it has not been easy. The Longbeards, Zhélruka, and Stout-axes here all take exception with each other, even on trifling matters of little importance. All three of these dwarf-companies suffered grievous losses at the teeth and claws of the Frost-horde, under Karazgar's direction, but we have seen no sign of the worms since you departed. The Weeping Warrior himself has not reappeared in that time... do you know anything about that, ${PLAYER}?
'But now it falls to me to get these dwarf-clans working together, and that is no easy thing. Perhaps you can ask members of each family what they think I should do on their behalf? Stout-axes, Zhélruka, and Longbeards up the stairs here at Skarháld are sure to give you their opinions on this subject, and it may help me decide how best to proceed.'

'Durin wants to know what is to be done? Ha! This Stout-axe has a recommendation or two, but I do not think he is prepared to hear them!
'I am a Stout-axe, ${PLAYER}. Of all the dwarves in this Middle-earth, we have endured the greatest trials; I dare you to say otherwise. Many were the torments Sauron devised for our great king when Drása did not submit, and his people were enslaved. But we kept our honour, though we toiled without end in Mordor, and now that the Dark Lord is gone the Stout-axes have emerged to take what we will, and what we deserve. So I say again to this dwarf-princeling: ha! What authority has he to command any Stout-axe? He fought against the Frost-horde? So did all of us at Skarháld. I count his deeds there no better than any of ours.
'He will need a dozen such victories before he has matched even the least of my own.'

'Durin sent you to ask what should be done? He is no Zhélruka, that much is clear. If Bótuz Frostblood were still alive, he would not ask such a thing. He would simply tell us, and in no uncertain terms; woe be to the dwarf who did not comply with his command!
'The Longbeard prince is still as green as Spring in the low-lands. He would do well to keep to himself, and leave the Zhélruka alone. We are not his to command, though we must inhabit Skarháld together for now. That will be for a short time only. Durin will soon tire of adventure and return to his father's halls. Beneath the Lonely Mountain he will live well, while we Zhélruka remain here, sleeping on the cold stone and dreaming of Gundabad, the home that has been kept from us.
'He knows little of the Zhélruka, and cares for us less. I find it distasteful for him to pretend otherwise.'

'It seems we share the same affliction, my questing friend! Most of my companions have gone home, satisfied with their adventures, but you and I belong here in the mountains, courting danger and unafraid! I know there is a place of honour set for me beneath the Lonely Mountain, but no matter how great the feast I would still feel the emptiness in my belly. Only adventure can sate my appetite now. My son Gimli will discover this hunger runs in his blood, if he has not already! But from your recent tales I know he has!'
You tell Glóin that Durin is seeking advice from the dwarves at Skarháld.
'I would tell him to treat carefully with the Zhélruka and Stout-axes who have come here, for they are not his people and care little for Longbeards. Each of these kindreds defended Skarháld when the Frost-horde attacked, and each suffered losses. But there are fewer Longbeards here than Zhélruka, and although the Stout-axes were few in number to begin with, it seems to me that more arrive everyday. Durin must be aware of this. Let him keep the Red Axe near at hand.'

'What have you heard, my friend? Are your tidings as grim as I fear they will be?'
Durin listens to your report of growing unrest among the Stout-axes and Zhélruka, and of Glóin's concerns, and his face falls. He hefts the Red Axe thoughtfully.
'I came here too hastily, ${PLAYER}. Each of our peoples suffered losses when the Frost-horde attacked, but there were never that many loyal Longbeards at Skarháld to begin with. I only assumed command because there was no one else! Without a strong leader to unify each of the dwarf-clans here, I feared the Grey Mountains would prove a grave-cairn for all of us. They might still, but now it is not drakes of the Frost-horde I fear. I fear the disloyalty of the Zhélruka and the Stout-axes. Is there not betrayal in the history of both clans?
'I need more loyal warriors to reinforce me! I ask you to return to my father at the Lonely Mountain and request that he send as many Longbeard warriors as he can spare. Too many were lost when the Frost-horde attacked, and I would not have us outnumbered by... by foes.'

'Can King Thorin's son really be Durin the Deathless reborn? I hope so! I have been planning a statue of him, and it would be a shame for that work to come to naught. But I have spoken too long already, and should get back to my endeavours. Return to King Thorin with my good wishes.'
The statue of Durin is quite impressive. Stáli is more skilled than he is modest
King Thorin is in the Hall Under the Mountain, in Erebor.

'Long, long ago, before the mountains were shaped as they are now, Durin awoke in the caverns beneath a mighty peak that joined two great mountain-ranges of the north. He looked to the peak and gave it the name we have revered ever since: Gundabad, the Mountain-home.
'The fathers of other dwarf-clans began to awake elsewhere in Middle-earth after that, in pairs, but he had awoken first of all the dwarves, and alone, and we revere him as the father of the Longbeards. We are Durin's Folk, and our claim to these lands springs from he who first awoke beneath Gundabad. In time, other dwarves awoke to accompany Durin, and to serve him, but his closest friend was a mighty warrior who helped delve the great halls beneath Gundabad. Legend tells us this friend was also the first dwarf to brew mead, and later ale, but do not think so well of him! He it was who would take the name Mótsog, and lead the Greymauls in rebellion. But that was still some years away.
'The servants of Morgoth in those days were a constant threat, and together Durin and Mótsog fought bravely to defend the Mountain-home from them, but Durin grew restless. He desired a place where the Longbeards might know peace, and so he set forth in search of such a haven. He named his dear friend Mótsog the Lord of Gundabad, a decision he would come to regret, and departed the sacred mountain.
'Do you see the statue there? It was one of my first pieces, and dare I say one of my finest. I hoped to capture some small portion of Durin's majesty as he set forth on his journey to what would become the site of treasured Khazad-dûm.'

'Go on, feel free to admire the statue of Durin. I am quite proud of it! See his noble visage? I like to imagine he has just looked into the lake of Kheled-zâram, and has realized he is near to finding a place of great wealth and safety for his people.'

'Ah, thank you very much, my friend! I can see you are an astute patron of the arts and have a fine eye for detail. I agree that I have done an excellent job of capturing Durin's heroism and majesty.'
Stáli beams at you. You have clearly won him over.
'Durin the Deathless he was called, for he possessed a great span of years and it seemed he would not die. It was not so, for death comes to all, even to the very greatest of dwarves. And yet: we Longbeards believe that Durin comes back whenever the dwarves have need of him, reborn into a new form. It is true! He has come back to us five times during our long history, and we therefore count each Durin in a single line, from Durin I who awoke beneath Gundabad all the way to Durin VI, who perished in Khazad-dûm to shadow and flame. Some folk believe that the son of King Thorin Stonehelm may prove to be Durin the Deathless reborn, a seventh Durin to lead us into the future.
'I hope it is true, ${PLAYER}. I have been planning a statue of him, and it would be a shame for that work to come to naught. But I have spoken too long already, and should get back to my endeavours. Return to King Thorin with my good wishes.'

'Stáli spoke to you of Mótsog and the Greymaul Rebellion? Good. Now you see how even good-seeming friends can turn traitor, and why it is so important that my son be surrounded by Longbeards he can trust.
'I have commanded a great force of loyal warriors to go with you to join my son in the Grey Mountains. Durin will have his reinforcements!'

'The Greymauls were ancient dwarf traitors in the First Age who rebelled against Durin the Deathless, Father of the Dwarves. Their leader was named Mótsog, and he led the Greymauls in a bloody uprising against Durin. For a time they ruled Durin's holdings, but it did not last. Durin returned and put Mótsog to death, and the rebellion was quelled.
'I have been restoring a mosaic of this very event, if you would like to see it. It is over there, against the wall. It was damaged during the residency of Smaug, and once I have finished repairing the stones I will return it to the hall where once it stood. It will once again serve as a reminder that treachery is always rewarded with justice.'

'That mosaic stood in the Hall Under the Mountain with many others for hundreds of years, but the coming of Smaug was not kind to any of them. Many of the stones were lost, and it has been a time-consuming process to recreate the mosaic as it was.
'But when Stáli the Hewer commits to such a project, he sees it through to the end!'

'I will not allow my son to be outnumbered by his foes! Go to Nabgûn-mazaru, the home of Stáli the Hewer, south-west of the entrance to the Dwelling-halls, and ask him about the Greymauls. Then you will see the importance of caution, even among dwarves.'

'I do not like this, ${PLAYER}. I do not like this at all! Not every dwarf-clan is good-hearted, and treacherous, wicked dwarves have troubled the Longbeards throughout history. Our cousins in the Blue Mountains could speak at length about the exploits of the villainous Dourhands, and theirs is not the only name of ill repute. Durin will have his reinforcements! I will command the assemblage of a Longbeard army the like of which has not been seen in seventy years!
'Do you think this unnecessary? I assure you it is not. I will not allow my son to be outnumbered by Zhélruka or Stout-axes! The Zhélruka have long quarreled with my people, and the Stout-axes could not have remained thralls to Sauron for so long without it affecting them deeply.
'You remain unconvinced? Go then to Nabgûn-mazaru, the home of Stáli the Hewer, south-west of the entrance to the Dwelling-halls, and ask him about the Greymauls. Then you will see the importance of caution, even among dwarves. Especially among dwarves.'

'Welcome to Nabgûn-mazaru, stranger. Are you a patron of the arts? I must confess to you that my hours are quite full, with a number of half-completed works already. If you desire a painting or statue, perhaps to decorate your home, it will be some time before I am able to get to it. With that understanding set forth, what would you like?'
You tell Stáli that King Thorin did not send you to him with a task, but for information on the Greymaul Dwarves.
'The Greymauls? Why should they occupy his thoughts? Better to forget they ever existed, lest you doubt the decency of your closest friends and your family. But I will not disobey the King Under the Mountain, and will speak of them to you.
'They were ancient dwarf traitors in the First Age who rebelled against Durin the Deathless, Father of the Longbeards. Their leader was named Mótsog, and he led the Greymauls in a bloody uprising against Durin. For a time the Greymauls ruled Durin's holdings, but it did not last. Durin returned and put Mótsog to death, and the rebellion was quelled.

'You have proven yourself a ${CLASS} of great courage, ${PLAYER}, and I judge that you have an eye for strength and capability in battle. Will you measure your fighting prowess against some of the dwarves I have chosen to join this Longbeard army? I do not question their desire for glory; indeed, these dwarves fought bravely and well in time of war, and achieved much honour thereby.
'But their greatest deeds are many years distant now. These three heroes fought in the Sixth War of Dwarves and Orcs, but that was more than two hundred and twenty years ago, when Durin's Folk last set foot within Gundabad. The Battle of Azanulbizar ended that war, and our losses were too great to pursue the Orcs into Khazad-dûm. I do not doubt the bravery of these three! But I want to know they still possess sufficient weapon-skill to aid my son.
'Seek out Agnar Brokentooth, Lági Helmbiter, and Reithvald Red-ember in the passages to the Dwelling-halls and to the New-lodes, and challenge them to battle. If they still desire to join my son in the Grey Mountains after testing their skills against you, then they shall.'
'A chance to test my skills? I welcome it, and promise I will not go easy on you!'
'You had best prepare for a real fight, stranger! I have not lived so long in idleness! Indeed, I test my combat skill every day without exception!'
'You shall have a fight, then! I may be old, but I remain fierce and eager for battle!'

'Those three remain eager for battle? I did not really expect otherwise, but I thought it best to make certain. Thank you for indulging me in this, ${PLAYER}. May their greatest heroics remain ahead of them, in service to my son Durin!'

You remind Durin of the need for caution: Hrímil Frost-heart dwells somewhere behind the ice, sealed within the Anvil of Winterstith, and the speech of dragons is known to have a strange power.

'Yes, drake-hunting is a dangerous endeavour. They knew the risks when they set out from Skarháld, the same as us.
'Where did you find them? To the north-east?'

'Thank you for these, ${PLAYER}. My Longbeards are going to need every weapon on which they can get their hands, and I do not appreciate these Zhélruka raiding the armouries without notice. That practice must end, or they will face my wrath and that of my Longbeards.
'But there is trouble brewing in Skarháld, and I need my most trusted ${CLASS} to help deal with it before the situation gets worse.'

'My father's reinforcements from the Lonely Mountain have brought their own weapons, but those will not be enough if we are to truly assault Gundabad. Can I ask you to climb the stairs and find the armoury in the Skarháld keep? Bring back some of the swords and axes that are stored there, and we can better supply this fighting force.'
'Tell the Longbeard prince that if he wants those weapons he will have to wait for my Zhélruka brothers to return victorious from their hunt.'

'Some of the Zhélruka have gone into the mountains to hunt the remaining drakes of the Frost-horde? I would say to let them go, and good riddance, but we need those weapons!
'You had better go after them, ${PLAYER}, and save them from their own foolishness. I want them alive so they can hear my reprimands, but more importantly I want the weapons they stole. I have spoken with some of the reinforcements from the Lonely Mountain, and many of their weapons are of poor quality, damaged either from disuse or entirely too much use; there is no middle ground.
'Find the Zhélruka hunting-parties outside Skarháld and bring back those weapons!'

'Thank you for your help, friend. We will return to Skarháld, but there was another party of drake-hunters with us, and they have not yet come back. We heard their horn blowing some time ago, but it stopped abruptly.
'They continued on to the north-east, if you wish to search in that direction.'
'The second party continued on to the north-east, but I fear they are dead. You had better find out for certain.'
'Sound the traditional drake-hunting horn and help us slay whatever answers the call, ${PLAYER}. It waits there for you.'

'Did you hear that horn blowing? It ended suddenly. I think the Zhélruka hunting parties may have run into some trouble after all, ${PLAYER}. You had better go and bring back their weapons, for it seems they may not need them any longer!
'The horn sounded to the east of Skarháld. I think that is where you will find them.'

'Mugs of ale? Aye, that should help them set aside their differences... while they are drinking, anyway.'

'You were able to smooth things over with the quarrelling dwarves? I expected no less, ${PLAYER}.
'But now there is something else. Isn't there always?'

'It appears nothing was settled after all! You go find these unruly dwarves and get to the bottom of this, ${PLAYER}. Perhaps they will listen to you. If they do not, well... we will swing that axe when we get there!'

'I do not know anything about these Greymauls he mentioned, but his tone of voice was clear. He intended for it to be insulting, so I was insulted. This story of treacherous dwarves must be some fable of the Longbeards. We Stout-axes have our own tales, and no shortage of villains to which I might compare such as he, who speak without thinking!
'He would do well to remember the force of my punch, for if he says anything of the sort to me again he will face my fists once more, and this time I will hold nothing back!'

'You say you have it well in hand? I expected nothing else, my friend!

'While you were away, a brawl broke out on the upper level. I do not know the precise cause of it, but it seems there is some resentment on the part of the Zhélruka and the Stout-axes here at Skarháld. When I climbed up to investigate, the matter had been resolved, but....'
Even as Durin speaks, you hear shouting from up the stairs.
'There! You hear them? It appears nothing was settled after all! You go find these unruly dwarves and get to the bottom of this, ${PLAYER}. Perhaps they will listen to you. If they do not, well... we will swing that axe when we get there!'

'You want to know what happened? I said two words, little more than that, and turned to go. That treacherous slime knocked me down when my back was turned! He calls himself a Stout-axe, but I know what he really is! He spent so long in Mordor... he was a willing servant of Sauron, or I am an Elf!
'I called him a Greymaul, what of it? He shows his true nature with such a cowardly strike! I wager all the Stout-axes have some Greymaul blood in them, and it wouldn't surprise me if the Zhélruka did too! Yes, some of the Greymauls must have escaped Durin's judgement, and their descendants probably intermingled with the other dwarf families. It would not surprise me to learn that Greymaul blood might have led to the crimes and failings of even the Dourhands!'

'I saw it all. They were grumbling at each other for a good while, mostly about imagined slights, I expect, but before long they were each at a full bellow. Heilar called Imák \qGreymaul filth\q as he turned to go, and that is when Imák knocked him down.
'I do not know what he meant by that, but he is fortunate Imák used his fists and not his axe. I might have done worse.'

'You found the supplies for our expedition? Very good. At a young age I learned the importance of preparing for a journey, and my appreciation of such preparation has only increased with every passing year. You do not want to lack some crucial tool in the middle of the wilderness, I can tell you that! But you know that as well as I, my friend.
'I spoke to Imák and Venko while you were gathering up the supplies, and they said they will meet us at the pass that leads to the Wells of Langflood, far to the west of Skarháld, east and south of the broken Rushgate. They were not very happy about it; they believed their conditions would change Durin's mind and keep anyone from seeking out this raiding-party, but it was not so. Speak to Durin and then we will join our new companions.'

'I will await word of the raiding-party when you find it, and then we will turn our attention to the place from which it came: Gundabad, the Mountain-home of my people. For too long has it been kept by the Orcs, but their residency will soon come to an end!
'One more thing, ${PLAYER}. Keep a watchful eye on the Stout-axe and Zhélruka with whom you travel. They may not wish you ill, not directly, but they may treat you dishonestly if it serves their purposes. The Wells of Langflood are west of here, accessible by a narrow pass in the southern cliffs, east of the broken Rushgate. Journey there boldly, but with caution in your eye, and find this raiding-party before it can do more harm.'

'So you are ready to depart for the Wells of the Langflood? I know very little of that region, but I understand Glóin journeyed there during the Sixth War of Dwarves and Orcs, when he was very young. I am sure he will tell you anything you may need to know of that land.
'I will await word of the raiding-party when you find it, and then we will turn our attention to the place from which it came: Gundabad, the Mountain-home of my people. For too long has it been kept by the Orcs, but their residency will soon come to an end!
'One more thing, ${PLAYER}. Keep a watchful eye on the Stout-axe and Zhélruka with whom you travel. They may not wish you ill, not directly, but they may treat you dishonestly if it serves their purposes. The Wells of Langflood are west of here, accessible by a narrow pass in the southern cliffs, east of the broken Rushgate. Journey there boldly, but with caution in your eye, and find this raiding-party before it can do more harm.'
'Speak first to Durin, and then we will depart for the Wells of the Langflood.'
'Ah, there you are.'

'We are all arrived, my friend. This is the path that will take us to the foggy basin of Misthallow, through which runs the tributaries of a familiar river. The folk of these northern lands named it Langflood, but you would call it the Great River, or Anduin.
'The raiding-party from Gundabad was spotted somewhere near the Wells of Langflood. That is where we must go.'
'Why has the Longbeard prince not charged any of his people with this mission, Venko? That is what I want to know.'

'They will only undertake this errand if you go with them? This is outrageous, ${PLAYER}! No one else has assumed the mantle of leadership here at Skarháld, and I do so only unwillingly, but if I make such a command as this it should be followed, and without question! These dwarves will cause only trouble for me and mine, and if I want them well away from Skarháld then away from it they shall be, without negotiation!
'But what is it, Glóin? You have something to say?'

'Yes, Durin, I have something to say. I have seen a thing or two during my long life, and it has taught me much. I was among the youngest of the dwarves to fight at Azanulbizar... did you know that? Every dwarf-clan sent representatives to fight in that war, Durin, not just the Longbeards. Even so youthful as I was, I knew that each family fought for more than just their own glory; they fought for the survival of all dwarves.
'You should not send Zhélruka only, or Stout-axes only, in pursuit of this Orc raiding-party. Neither should you keep your Longbeards in reserve, for that speaks poorly both of you and of them! A Longbeard should go, and I volunteer myself. Let ${PLAYER} adventure there too, not just because Imák and Venko request it but because ${PLAYER} is a loyal friend and true, and will see this raiding-party destroyed. These are words of wisdom, Durin, and with age and experience they will come naturally to you. For now let them come from your friends and allies, for they want the same as you and will not lead you astray.
'${PLAYER}, will you gather the supplies we will need for an excursion into the Wells of Langflood? You will find satchels of foodstuffs, climbing gear, and assorted other supplies two or three levels up in Skarháld. While you do that I will tell Imák and Venko that we will be travelling companions, for the good of Skarháld and all the dwarves.'
'What is it, Glóin? You have my respect and for that I give you my ear.'
'Glóin is right. The two of you have leave to go with them in search of the Gundabad raiding-party. But you will need to collect some supplies before you depart.'

'My scouts bring word of a raiding-party set loose from Gundabad upon the inhabitants of Misthallow and the Floodfells. There are few enough of those, but if the Orcs move in those lands they will trouble any army that seeks to advance upon Gundabad. Someone must deal with this raiding-party... and I believe we might solve two problems with a single stroke! Why not send some of the troublesome Zhélruka or Stout-axes to confront this raiding-party? They will realize their true quarrel is with the Orcs, and during their absence some measure of peace may return to Skarháld. What were their names? Imák? Venko? Bring them this news of this task, and invite them to adventure on behalf of their people.'

Let Durin's trusted friend be a part of this errand too, and perhaps he will be more interested in its successful outcome, and our survival.'

'You know I desire to take back Gundabad for my people, and it will not be long before I drive the Orcs from that sacred mountain. But I am no fool, ${PLAYER}! Too often the hasty stroke goes astray, or so they say, and I know any assault upon the Mountain-home must be carefully planned. To that end, I sent a number of scouts to the Wells of the Langflood, swift and true, and they have now returned.
'But they return with news not from the foot of Gundabad, but from the lands to the south! They bring word of a raiding-party set loose from Gundabad upon the inhabitants of Misthallow and the Floodfells. There are few enough of those, but if the Orcs move in those lands they will trouble any army that seeks to advance upon Gundabad. Someone must deal with this raiding-party.
'Do you know something, ${PLAYER}? I believe we might solve two problems with a single stroke! Why not send some of the troublesome Zhélruka or Stout-axes to confront this raiding-party? They will realize their true quarrel is with the Orcs, and during their absence some measure of peace may return to Skarháld. What were their names? Imák? Venko? Bring them the news of this task, and invite them to adventure on behalf of their people.'

'Durin expects the two of us to go in search of a raiding-party from Gundabad? Is that what you are saying, ${PLAYER}? I cannot fail to notice that he has charged a Stout-axe and a Zhélruka with this mission, rather than any of the large number of his own folk that have come to Skarháld. I find that most curious, Venko, do you not?
'I believe the Longbeard prince is seeking to get rid of us!'

'Durin wants us to go face a raiding-party from Gundabad? I see the workings of his mind, and I tell you they are not as subtle as he thinks them to be! If Imák and I prove victorious against these Orcs, then the few folk who live along the Langflood will be made safer, and if we do not, well, Durin has only lost a Stout-axe and a Zhélruka in the effort. He will not mourn us overmuch, Imák, will he?
'In the interest of setting aside our differences, I will do as Durin requests, if Imák will do the same. I will venture to the Wells of the Langflood in pursuit of this raiding party... with two conditions only.
'The first is this: you must come with us, ${PLAYER}. You are a close friend of the Longbeard prince, and he would not send you into danger without reason. If you were to perish, I believe he would be aggrieved. So I ask that you come with us in search of this raiding-party. My second condition is that Durin send a Longbeard as well. Why should Stout-axes and Zhélruka go into danger when Durin's Folk remain behind in safety?
'Those are my conditions. Bring them to Durin with haste, ${PLAYER}, and see what this Longbeard prince has to say.'

'We will need to work together if we are to see this task accomplished. Imák? Venko? Do you not agree?'

'Do not speak to me as if I were a mere child, Glóin. You are my elder in years, it is true, and your beard is white, but you spent no time in the dungeons of Sauron, as I have. Doubt not that I will match both you and ${PLAYER} in courage!
'A raiding-party of Orcs? I have proven far better against much worse. So do not treat me as some youthful stripling!
'Once we arrive in Misthallow we will need to find a place to camp, and that means fighting whatever aggressive beasts stray near our prospective camp-site. I will slay my share of the creatures, so long as you pull your own weight.'

'None of us want to be travelling together, Glóin, but each of us has reason to hate the Orcs. Let that purpose unify us, and in a day or two, once the raiding-party is destroyed we need not remain companions.
'Let us look forward to that, and we should have little reason to complain. The Wells of Langflood await us, and after we can return to our own concerns.
'I have never seen the lands along the Langflood, but we should keep watch for places at which we might camp, sheltered from the wind and from threats that might roam near.'
'What say you? Can we work together in this matter, or will your squabbling continue?'
'Onward to Misthallow, then. The sooner we accomplish this task, the better: not only because it was commanded of us, but because my patience may not survive these dwarves for long!'

'You have returned from the Reikfoss? Tell me, ${PLAYER}. What did you make of this mighty waterfall of Misthallow?'
You give Venko your impression of the Reikfoss from the vantage point you found, and the Zhélruka nods solemnly.
'Thank you, ${PLAYER}. My brothers and I promised to look upon the Three Sisters on our approach to Gundabad, but the Frost-horde ensured that promise was not to be kept. I still look forward to my first view of the falls, but I am pleased you have done so in memory of Dúsek and Lékhun.'

'It seems that Longbeards and Zhélruka know the same sorrows, ${PLAYER}, and Venko has my sympathy. I too have lost a brother. Óin went to Moria with Balin, and died there. Some dwarves would be content to live out their lives in safety and in peace, but not my brother. Nor would I, before you say it!
'Neither would our Zhélruka companion, it seems. He still intends to see the sights that were denied his brothers, and plans no defeated return to the eastern lands. I find that commendable.'
'We have all lost people. The Zhélruka has my sympathy, but no more and no less than anyone who has suffered the same. Let the memory of his brothers strengthen his resolve and toughen his spirit.'

'We are not that far from the roaring waterfalls of Misthallow, ${PLAYER}. I charge you to find a good vantage point to the north where you can <rgb=#00FF00>look</rgb> at the nearest of the Three Sisters, the Reikfoss of Greylin, in honour of my brothers. Return then to me and I would be grateful to hear your description of it.'

I spoke to you of Azog, who led the Orcs against us during the Great Orc War, and perished beneath Dáin's heel at Azanulbizar? A son he had, Bolg, who commanded the Orcs at the Battle of Five Armies. Bolg died before the Lonely Mountain, but his line did not end there. Two were the sons of Bolg. One was named Gorgar, and if the words of Natsatúg can be trusted he calls himself now the Lord of Gundabad.
'Bolg's other son was Mazog, ${PLAYER}, the same Mazog who was slain by my old companion Bofur's grandson Broín, wielding the mithril axe Zigilburk. This new Lord of Gundabad possesses no shortage of grievance against the dwarves, but the death of his brother Mazog can only fuel that most powerful of desires: a thirst for blood, and vengeance.'
'I do not like it... no, not at all...'
'Where has the old Longbeard gone?'

'I have been reading what I have written down thus far, ${PLAYER}. Our expedition to Avabárg has shed new light on the past of my people. The Ai-thúda's urgency to find a better home is quite interesting. I myself have never dreamt of any home but Rohan.
'Now where shall the past take us in the Floodfells? As we know, Frumgar was weary of life in the Vales and so he led the Ai-thúda north, bloodying their spears on Orc and Warg as they rode. It would also allow us to better understand the hardships endured by the Ai-thúda as they travelled north.
'When the path is clear and safe, let us convene at the White Mare. It is all that remains of the Ai-thúda's short stay in the Floodfells.'

'Before we travel further north, I have been thinking about some moments in the history of the Ai-thúda that intrigue me. Have you heard of the mearas? North of here, between the Twainmantle and Reikfoss falls, Frumgar first beheld a herd of wild, silver-coated horses running upon the folde. This was the first sighting of the mearas, the mighty steeds with whom the fates of the Ai-thúda would ever after be entwined.

'Frumgar named his son Fram, and swore he would not know the same sorrow when he was grown. In my research, I learned that, six years after Fram's birth, Angmar fell. The kingdom's demise was sudden, coming only a year after the Witch-king’s final victory over Arthedain and the fall of Fornost. The chronicles of this time say an army of Elves and Men of Gondor, having come too late to save the northern Dúnedain, put the Angmarim to the sword and sent the Witch-king flying back to Mordor.
'Why do I relate this story to you? Angmar's fall had an important connexion with my people. At this time, Gundabad no longer had the Iron Kingdom at its back, and the moors and glens of the Welling-folds no longer seemed so daunting as they had to Marhwini a hundred years before. Fram saw this as an opportunity to lead his people to great things.'

'Not much more is known about the Ai-thúda and the Holbytlan. It is said that late during Lord Thíudric’s time, the Holbytlan reappeared. Even then, they were considered nothing more than children’s stories. We know that Thíudric died at seventy-nine, and his son Gunthar became lord when already old and ruled only a short time. Lóthar followed, and ruled well. Sightings of the Holbytlan proliferated during his time, as the songs say. Lóthar’s reign was also long, and saw little strife, though it was not unmarred by sorrow.
'Come, let us return to Thokvist. I have acquired all that I need for my writings and I do not wish to overstay my welcome here... if welcome it can be called.'

'Taurogrim? That is not what I was hoping to find. Hmm, I did notice a possible path west of here, across the Langflood. Perhaps that might be worth investigating as well? It could be more of the Taurogrim too, but we shall never know if we do not explore! Come, let us be off!'
You notice Fanglind listening closely to your conversation.
'Ah, right then, Thíudric, Gunthar, Lóthar. I see there in my writings a line of rulers where history becomes only lineage. Nothing more, nothing less. Those must have been peaceful times indeed.'

'Fram's friend! I just recalled an old children's song, which I believe mentions a hobbit? No, not a hobbit, but one perhaps of the little folk, or river folk, as they were sometimes called. Yes, there were some songs that told of Fram's friendship with a strange, Elfin folk in those lands who only revealed themselves to children; perhaps these songs were nonsense, as many such rhymes tend to be, but the resemblance between the Elfin folk and the Hol-búdlan of old cannot be ignored. You have heard tales of the Hol-búdlan too? Perhaps this is worth investigating!
'If there is any such remnant of the Hol-búdlan left in Misthallow, it will certainly not be in this valley. No, they most likely hid in the hills. There seems to be a path following the river, just east of here. Let us venture up it and see what we can find!'

'Frumgar was victorious. It was said, however, defeat only stoked the Orcs’ thirst for blood. Thirteen years later the Orcs returned to raze the Ai-thúda's lands and sack Avabárg.'

'In many ways the story of my people begins with King Marhári, of the Northmen. Disaster befell the Thíuda during the Battle of the Plains against the Wainriders. When King Marhári fell in that battle, his son Marhwini led the survivors on a long journey in search of a new home, ultimately resettling here.
'Marhwini’s people, the Ai-thúda or Horse-folk, were not well satisfied dwelling in the Vales. They desired open country where they could ride and graze their herds. Their scouts found this in the Floodfells, but Marhwini deemed it too rough and untamable a land, and too close to the threat of Angmar, to halt with his war-weary people.'
'Let us defeat these Orcs and honour the hardship endured by the Horse-folk for so many years.'

'Here Marhwini built the hall of Avabárg and named it the chief fortress of the Ai-thúda. This was not the safest of places, though. The coming of the Horse-folk roused the Orcs of Hithaeglir, who attacked them again and again over the next century. Both Marhwini’s son Forthwini and his grandson Forthári fell in battle to the Orcs, leaving only Forthári’s youngest son as heir.'

'Forthári’s youngest son was Frumgar, a boy of twelve, now Chieftain of the Ai-thúda. While still a youth, Frumgar became a hero of his people, befriending both the Longbeard Dwarves and the Wizards Gandalf the Grey and Barandil the Brown.'
'Frumgar even received an ancient sword of Westernesse, which he named Wrothbláda, from Curunír the White. With these allies he defeated the Orcs in battle at the age of seventeen.'

There may be some truth in this claim. I still wonder, which story is true? I fear the story of Fram may have been embellished in places over the years.'
'This seems a good enough place to rest for a bit.'
You can imagine Fram, uncertain in his decision to bring his people north

'You are heading to Limlók, yes? I will accompany you. It would seem the story I seek follows the same path. Might we stop at the Carrock on our way? I would very much like to see for myself. There is some Rohirric history there as well, if you can believe it.'

'Ah, you have done all the day's work? Good, good! I would say you deserve a rest and some honey cake. Ha!'

'You have returned. Is Léothred finished with his history? Oh, I see, he needs to travel north. I am afraid I can not allow that at the moment. I recently asked for one of the Eagles to gather news from the northern Beorning outpost of Limlók. I should think the Eagle will return with news in a day or two.
'Now that you are here, why not pitch in with the daily work? There is always much to do. I need wood chopped, berries picked, and some lost chickens tracked down.'

'Must I explain everything?! There is wood to be chopped right here at the Beorninghús. I am sure that ripe wild berries grow nearby in the Beorninglands. You will find them. As for the chickens, well the last place I saw them was in the bee pastures around us. Right then, get to it.'

'If we were to head north from Avabárg, that path would take us past the Beorninghús. Perhaps it would be in our best interest to check in with Grimbeorn. I do not wish to overstay my welcome in these lands!'

'The legacy of Théodwyne Sternbrow was a seed planted, and that seed came to bear fruit near the end of Cendric's rule. There, Cendric let it be known that the Éothéod had need of broader fields in which to roam. He even discussed with Cirion, Steward of Gondor, the possibility of finding land somewhere in the south.
'Let us rest. Then we shall continue to explore this history.'

'Frúma died while hunting in the Misty Mountains. His broken body was found frozen at the floor of a ravine several months after his death. Some said he was killed by a giant, others said that he fell in a winter storm.'

'Frúma's son Cendric succeeded him while he was still young. Cendric the Worthy proved an exceptional lord, both a mighty warrior and a noble ruler, and was also blessed with a lengthy reign of peace and plenty. When he died at age seventy-nine, having ruled for fifty-seven years, the Éothéod were more prosperous than ever before. Their numbers were beginning to grow too great for the Wells to support.'

'All hope for the Éothéod rested now on the shoulders of Théodwyne Sternbrow. There are few stories of Théodwyne, but the ones that do exist are powerful tales. She was the first, and to my knowledge the only, woman to rule the Éothéod. It is safe to surmise that Théodwyne did not have the support of all the thanes. Let us see what we can find at Framsburg to piece together this tale.'
The Tale of Théodwyne Sternbrow

'I overheard some goblins talking while I was in Sundergrót. At the time, I did not think much of it, but perhaps I should revisit what it was I heard.
'Do you find it odd that the goblins work and camp as if they are commanded, yet there is no commander in sight? Yes, well, I heard a few goblins talking about an important meeting that is soon to happen in Sundergrót. Could this meeting be with this mysterious, absent commander? I say we find this meeting, and learn what is really going on here!'
'Thank you for your assistance on our survey mission. I hope that you will return to Skarháld with us. Please, bring us word from Grimbeorn as soon as you hear something.'
'Aye, it looks like my curiosity was warranted. I am glad that we stopped those goblins from joining forces with Gundabad.'
'It is always a pleasure to receive assistance from the great ${PLAYER}. I hope our paths cross once more, my friend!'
'${PLAYER}, something bothers me about the goblins in Sundergrót. I know not what, but something is amiss! Agátur looks as if he has something to say. Spit it out, my friend!'

The Plight of Limlók

'${PLAYER}, is that you? Yes, I was attacked by a Warg-rider on my journey from the Thornholt to Limlók. I will recover in time. Is it true that Hunulf is dead? If only I could have made that journey with him, he would still be alive. Poor Hunulf, a true friend.
'I am glad that Hunulf was able to warn you about what we have seen. It has grown ever dire in the Thornholt. Fiskvat, that fool, refused to leave with us. He stayed behind due to his stubbornness and love for the Thornholt honey! I fear he will likely perish. Threkmóth the elder sadly died on our journey to Limlók. He was slain by the Taurogrim. The Taurogrim have been greatly angered by recent events. I believe the intrusion of the Orcs of Gundabad and purifying of the woods by the Elves has pushed them into an absolute frenzy.
'Oh and ${PLAYER}, you can trust the dwarves here. They saved my life multiple times on our journey. Perhaps you know them from your time in Ered Mithrin?'

'Now then, I hope you are a fighter. The Orc assaults would not be much trouble for Limlók, were it not for the additional Warg attacks. Limlók will fall soon if something is not done.
'I will not be making your stay a comfortable one, for Grimbeorn has sent you to assist us. And assist us you shall.'

'We rarely receive visitors of any sort in Limlók. Hertha visits from time to time, when she is not guarding the pass, but she grew up here and this is her home. Now then, what of Hunulf? He left here against my better judgment.
'I see, I am saddened to hear of his passing. His companion Vaskorn is still here in Limlók, resting from his wounds. He will recover. You should speak with him, by the well.'

'We learned quite a lot upon our first day at Framsburg. I do say, we shall learn even more tomorrow! Until then I will write down my findings and get some well-deserved rest. I suggest you do the same.'

'At last, we reach Framsburg! Now where to begin? Ah yes, Lóthar.
'Now it was Lóthar’s son Gundric who brought the most grief to his father’s rule, for he dared seek to ride one of the mearas. Like his longfather Gisilhári he failed, perishing beneath the angry hooves when the beast trampled him.'

'Grieving, Lóthar took in his one-year-old grandson, Bóra, and raised him as his own. During this time, a change befell the Ai-thúda. Due to close contact with both the dwarves and the Hól-budlan, their language underwent a series of changes, so that by the end of Lord Lóthar’s rule, it mostly resembled the later tongue of my people.
'Framabárg became Framsburg in their language; Hól-budla became holbytla, and their own name of Ai-thúda now was spoken as Éothéod. It also became tradition, after the fashion of Frumgar long ago, for the lords to name their heirs with words that meant lord or some variant thereof.'

'Lóthar’s grandson Bóra succeeded him, and during Bóra's rule, King Thorin I of the Longbeards was slain by Orcs in Ered Mithrin. This sparked the Fifth War of Dwarves and Orcs. The Éothéod found themselves pulled into the fighting that raged in the mountains around them, for the Orcs threatened them as well. This unrest lasted through Bóra’s rule and that of his son Maera, ending at last in the time of Théodric, Maera’s son.'

'With the Éothéod’s aid, the Longbeards once again drove the last Orcs back to Gundabad. Théodric would not break his namesake Thíudric’s ban upon entering the Mountain-home though. His reluctance played a part in King Glóin’s decision not to enter Gundabad either.'

'Lord Théodric was in turn succeeded by his son Haldend, a grim and rude-mannered man who urged his father to break the Ban of Thíudric and enter Gundabad. He yearned for the glory he had found fighting the Orcs, and at the age of fifty, only two years into his reign, he foolishly chose to attempt to ride a mearh.'

'Haldend was no more fortunate than Gundric and Gisilhári. The steed he chose kicked him in the head, cracking his skull. He survived, but the wound robbed him of his wits, leaving him unable to speak more than a few words or lift a sword.'

'I have learned much from our time in Misthallow thus far, ${PLAYER}. Now comes the time to make the trek to the great keep of my people's past. It is a relic and a keeper of memories both. There we will most certainly uncover many a hidden secret, and reaffirm many of the stories of old. Come, let us travel and establish a safe encampment near Framsburg. I would imagine that we will stay there to study the keep for quite some time.'
Legacy in the Mist

'The mearas ever after allowed only the greatest lords of the Éothéod and their sons and daughters to ride them. I believe there is one exception to this in all of history. Do you know of the horse, Shadowfax? Yes, the steed who has come to be companion to the Wizard Mithrandir. Shadowfax himself is a mearh.'

'Hailed as a hero by his people, Léod sought to prove his worth as his forebears had done and tame one of the mearas. Again, however, the attempt ended in disaster. Though he lasted longer than any before him, and the horse bore him far, it at last threw him and Léod's head struck a rock, killing him.'

'${PLAYER}, let me tell you one of most important tales told in all of Rohan about the history of my people. It is a story of a pivotal moment for us, about the son of Léod, a lad of sixteen, named Eorl....'

'And that is the tale of how horse and rider became one. It was the foundation of all of Rohan, laid right here!
'Now, long ago, after the fall of Wilderland, Marhari the Proud had declared that no leader of his people would be called lord until the Éothéod had come to their proper home. The Wells had seemed so in the time of Gisilhári and the others that followed, but now the Éothéod needed more, and until they found it Eorl would remain simply Master Eorl.'

'Yes, I too am well-rested and ready for the day ahead! Until now, we have only briefly touched upon the mearas. I wish to explore the bond between the Rohirrim and horses. One could say that it started with the wanderings of the Ai-thúda. I would argue that it was the taming of the mearas that created the real bond that I and my people have with horses. Come, let us find this bond, together.'
The Taming of the Mearas

'Náth wishes to have Sundergrót surveyed for minerals to see if the depths are rich enough to return to for mining. Make this your primary concern, but watch out for goblins. There are plenty lurking about! Anything you could do to thwart them would be much appreciated, my friend!'

'Bah, this place is crawling with goblins! Did you see the old ruins on our way from Skerabrygg to Sundergrót? Aye, Stramvárth and Egvárth, those old watch-posts are called. I would recommend we scout them ourselves and take care of any goblins lurking about the old ruins. You can not be too careful!'

'I thank you for clearing the old watch-posts, my friend! You have done a great service to us, and to the Beornings. The fewer the goblins in the Floodfells, the better, no? Ha, now let us continue with the survey mission!
'I have taken a glance inside Sundergrót and I am sure you can guess what it is I saw in there! Oh, that is correct, my friend: many more goblins lurking inside. Bah, too many for only the four of us. If we are crafty, we should be able to survey all of Sundergrót and thwart whatever plans those goblins have with the old dwarf-hold. Now let us continue on our mission.'

'Ah yes, Sundergrót. I have been studying the northern dwarf-holds during my time in Erebor. Sundergrót is an old structure, but it should be well-preserved; know you not how impressive is dwarf-craft? I agree with Agátur that it would be worth a survey. I know many have their eyes on Gundabad, and I do not blame them for that! But there are other Dwarf-holds still worth surveying, and not just the Mountain-home! Come, let us depart.'
'Ah, we all return and the survey was a great success! I believe we have found Sundergrót to remain a useful dwarf-hold! We must bring this knowledge back to Skarháld with us!'
Still more foes await you!

'Keep a hushed tone about you, ${PLAYER}. I hear the tread of Warg-paws: over the hill, within the valley of Misthallow. They come this way. Should we retreat and warn the village? If we run, we will lose sight of this band, and an unseen threat can be the more dangerous. No, we must stand our ground. I have fled too often of late. No more.'

'Yes, I am healed and ready to assist Runerik. Let us patrol the wilds of the Floodfells in search of any of these raiding parties. I will patrol the southern route and round the western hill towards the northern pass. You patrol the northern route past the horse rocks. We will meet up at the northern pass.'
'What? A Warg made it through Misthallow? Skarding is either in trouble or he has been overwhelmed... and I am sure he is not in trouble.'

'Our victory was for Hunulf. Our success was for elder Threkmóth. Until now, I felt lost, thrust from my quiet life in the Thornholt, a sudden victim of death and conflict. But I am now newly-resolved: I shall remain in Limlók and help protect this village. If Limlók is not kept safe, how will my Skoghús ever be so?'

'Is this a trophy from the dwarves? Why do they not present it to me themselves? I suspect they are a lazy bunch!
'Grr, I am not impressed, and yet it does not matter if I am or not! They should not be trying to impress me, for it is Grimbeorn whose approval they need, and that is an even greater challenge! Only Grimbeorn can make a pact for all Beornings to abide by. There is none other, so do not waste your time on me, ${CLASS}.'

'${PLAYER}, it is good to see you well. It was not long after you left Skarháld that Náth here and some others travelled from Erebor to assist us. Alas, our efforts took a turn for the worse. Some blamed a lack of leadership. Others were blamed for a failure to work together. I believe it was Gundabad that caught us off our guard.
'Skarháld is still well-defended, but for how much longer? The raiding parties from out of Gundabad are emboldened, and their numbers grow stronger with each passing day. What leadership there was at Skarháld sent emissaries from each clan to entreat the Beornings for assistance. We decided first to seek out the Beornings in the Thornholt at Skoghús. I am glad we got there when we did, or they would have all been slaughtered by an approaching warband!
'That was when we realized these Beornings have had no contact with the Vales in years. We offered to escort them to safety as a gesture of goodwill towards their people. Only hardship was found on our journey here. The path may never be clear of the evil that dwells in those woods!
'Now we await word from Grimbeorn. I hope he and the Beornings will aid us.
'Hmm, perhaps there is something we can do. I have heard that Beornings like good trophies as gifts, accepting them as a show of respect and goodwill. Yes, some Warg pelts would do, would they not? Would you mind gathering some Warg pelts for us? We are still resting from our arduous journey.'

'Well, I am out of ideas! I suppose we should just assist the Beornings as best we can, and wait here for Grimbeorn's reply. I do not like waiting. It makes me quite restless. Unless.... Hmm, I may have an idea, everyone!'

'I suppose you find it odd to see a Longbeard, a Stout-axe, and a Zhélruka travelling together, no? I will let Agátur explain in detail, for he says that I rarely arrive at the point of the conversation in a timely fashion. Ha, maybe, maybe, my friend!'

'The arrival of the Éothéod at the Field of Celebrant helped win the day and defeat the hosts of the East, saving the South-kingdom from ruin. As thanks for their aid, Cirion granted to the Éothéod the lands that Lord Cendric had spoken of, and which Eorl’s ancestors had desired since the fall of Wilderland. These were the green fields of Calenardhon, now all but emptied as the Dúnedain’s numbers dwindled. Swearing an oath of fealty forever to Gondor, Eorl accepted Cirion’s offer and sent riders to summon the rest of his people to join him in his new realm. Henceforth, the Éothéod, now known as the Eorlingas, would dwell in the Riddermark of Rohan, and Eorl and his descendants would be its kings.
'Let us return to Hlithseld, ${PLAYER}. It has been a long day.'

'There, I have traced the history of my people as best I could. I have filled in the gaps from the Ai-thúda to the Éothéod, and their journey to Rohan. I could not have done it alone. I thank you for your assistance, many times over!
'You are free to leave me here if you must. Yes, I have writing to do, and there is not a better place to write all this down than near the ruins of Framsburg. There are gaps yet to fill in the tale, this much I can see.
'I am still puzzled by many of the old tales and songs. What about the worm, Scatha, that Fram fought? Fram's deeds will need uncovering! The dwarves in the mountains must have played their part in history of the Éothéod too, yes? Hmm, I have much to think about. Perhaps I will call upon you again soon. Until then, my friend!'

'Nine years into Eorl’s rule, a man in green came to the Wells, bloodied and exhausted from long riding without rest. Borondir was his name, and he was of mixed Dúnadan and Thíuda blood. Cirion, Steward of Gondor, had sent him as one of six errand-riders in search of aid from the Northmen against an army of Orcs and Balchoth, Easterlings who had come to invade the South-kingdom in force.'
'Our time researching the Éothéod nears its end. This is a joyous finale, as it signals the birth of the Eorlingas. Let us continue!'
Birth of the Eorlingas

'I am Grandmother Madelgard Túcca, and you are quite the stranger! I'm only talking to you because you are the friend of an Eagle. We have great respect for the Eagles, but not much for... what are you? ${RACE}?! Hmm, perhaps you could earn more respect if you do something nice for Lyndelby. You see, I have been noticing snooping goblins nearby. If you send them away, I might rest a bit easier at night!'

'You sent those goblins running?! To be honest, I did not expect you to help us at all! It would seem the rest of the village is now working up the courage to meet such a helpful and peculiar stranger, such as yourself. Perhaps you would also like to meet the rest of us? We can be a shy people, but we will warm to you in time.'

'Oh, I am glad that the whole village was able to meet you! Well, all but two, I think. Yes, they went up into the mountains to explore some time ago. Following in the footsteps of the Fallohide. Anyhow, I would say you have been most helpful to Lyndelby. It nearly felt as one of our festivals, what with all the buzz in the air from having you around!'

'Greetings ${PLAYER}. I am surprised the town of Lyndelby greeted you at all. Some of the younger Men who once lived in these parts befriended a few of the Holbytlan. They were considered a curiosity, yet with their elusiveness, their presence quickly fell to mere rumours among the Men. We Eagles have kept watch over the Holbytlan ever since. All I ask is that you speak to no one of Lyndelby. We wish for the simple lives of the Holbytlan to be not disturbed.'

'From now on, you may call me Maddy. Everyone else in the village does! Hmm, it looks like you mean to depart soon. Have you another adventure afoot?! I'm sure you do! Well, before you leave, you should say good-bye to everyone! It is the neighbourly thing to do after all! Farewell, friend!'

Talk to Frethi
A Search for Answers

'It seems I must entrust this to you once more, friend. The stone must be taken far away from Erebor, but simply locking it away somewhere else will not be enough. It seems to possess a will of its own, seeking to be found in order to carry out some evil mischief or cause some grievous harm. From where did the stone come, and for what purpose?
'I know precious little myself, save that it was found long ago in Khazad-dûm. That is where you must begin your search for answers, dangerous though it will be. Yes, the mission of the Iron Garrison failed, and the dream of reclaiming Khazad-dûm is once more a dream only, but there are some dwarves still hiding in those caves. Large gatherings of dwarves could not remain, for the Orcs would find and crush them without difficulty! But here and there, some hardy Longbeards might still struggle to survive.
'Frethi the Explorer is one such dwarf. He may not still live, but he was without compare in his exploration of the deep places below Khazad-dûm. If he is still alive, he will be indispensable to you.
'I wish you luck, ${PLAYER}. Oh, and one more thing: if for some reason you cannot solve this riddle, cast that cursed thing into the deepest pit you can find and be done with it!'
<rgb=#FF0000> This difficult treasure hunt will require community teamwork and resources outside of the game itself. Good luck! </rgb>
'A hidden door! Let us see where it leads!'

'Hello, ${PLAYER}! There has been a great deal of Orkish activity in Khazad-dûm of late, but I hid myself down deep and they have not caught sight of me. What brings you all the way down here?'
You explain that King Thorin Stonehelm sent you to find him, and about the Secret Stone.
'Hmm.... Many secrets still lie hidden within the Foundations of Stone. If there are clues to be found about an artifact of Khazad-dûm that shares some connexion with the Nameless, this is a good place to start, if such a place could be called \qgood!\q I don't quite know for what we're looking, though. Let's see what we can find.'

'This chamber must be related to the Secret Stone in some way! We should continue looking around. I will see if I can read the rest of those runes. They are quite faded, but you have met no dwarf so tenacious as Frethi!'
The switch reveals a hidden door!

You peer into the illusion of the stone within the hand of the troll. Vivid imagery appears in your mind once more.
The troll, stumbling around in a stupor induced by the stone, broke through the ice and became trapped. Come morning's light, he was turned to stone. There the Third Stone waited for some time, until a Dourhand Dwarf chanced upon the statue. You see the Dourhand climbing the troll, chiselling the precious artifact from its stone hand. He grins wildly as he looks deep into its black surface, and runs off with it under his arm.
It is clear you must track down this Dourhand in order to find the stone.

You have found the decayed corpse of a Dourhand Dwarf. You are unsure how long it has been here, but the illusion of the third stone in its hand clearly indicates this is the dwarf for which you were looking.
You peer into the illusion of the stone within the hand of the dead dwarf. Vivid imagery appears in your mind once more.
You see him running along the road alone at night. He is trying to get the stone somewhere in a hurry. Suddenly, he is ambushed by a trio of Blue Crag goblins! He evades them, running north toward the mountains. Eventually, he is cornered against the cliff. The goblins kill him, and steal the stone.
It is clear you must track down these goblins in order to find the stone.

As you peer into the illusion of the third stone, vivid imagery appears in your mind.
You see a cave troll entering the chamber and breaking down the door with a massive club. He sees the stone on the pedestal and pauses, becoming transfixed. It entrances him, and he takes the stone and leaves.
It is clear you must track down this troll in order to find the stone.

The illusions have become more vivid. When you peer into the illusion of the stone, the frozen moment in time springs to life. This time, you can hear it as well.
You see the Blue Crag goblins emerging from the mountains. They look around nervously, muttering to each other. You hear a twig snap somewhere nearby. They pause, and pull out their weapons. A gauradan howls and charges at them from a higher slope. He bellows something at the goblins, but you cannot make out the words. The goblins try to fight back, but are quickly overpowered by the hulking beast-man. The gauradan notices the strange stone still clutched in the hand of the dead goblin. He begins to peer into it, but then winces, and looks away, disgusted by the foul magic attempting to enter his mind. Still careful to look away, he picks up the stone, and hides it in a pouch under his furs. He then runs off toward his village.
It is clear you must track down the gauradan in order to find the stone.

The illusions next show you a different gauradan tribesman negotiating with two Angmarim cultists. You are now able to hear their conversation with surprising clarity.
'You were wise to inform us of this, wolf-man. This will bring you great favour with Angmar.' 'I care little for your favours, cultist of Angmar. Take that dark magic far from here!'
The Angmarim turn and leave. Surprisingly, this time when the stone changed hands, no bloodshed occurred. It is clear you must track down the Angmarim in order to find the stone.

The illusion now shows you the moment that the Angmarim cultists were ambushed at the cross-roads by Rangers of Eriador. They were both easily brought down by their arrows. The Rangers carefully look through the cultists' belongings, and find the stone.
'Oh ho, what is this? Some hidden treasure?' 'I've never seen anything like it. Let me look at it more closely....' 'Snap out of it! This thing had you completely entranced! Put it away, quickly!' 'This is clearly some artifact of immense evil. Just being in its presence puts me on edge.' 'What should we do? This may be too dangerous to bring back to camp.' 'It must be brought to Aragorn, right away.' 'But he is in the field! You would have to travel past Fornost!' 'It must be done. I will ride as swiftly as I can. You two must return to camp.'
It is clear you must track down the mounted Ranger in order to find the stone.

The illusion shows you the Ranger's end. He rode through the Fields of Fornost as fast as his mount would carry him.
'If I can make it to the Greenway, I should be safe!', he mutters urgently. But then a pack of barghests began to close in on him, barking and snapping at his heels. When they reached the shallow pond, the moon's reflection spooked the horse, who reared up, knocking the Ranger to the ground. The Ranger tried to fend off the beasts, but it was the end of them both. As a final act, the Ranger hurled the stone into the pond, hoping no one would find it.

Unfortunately, it WAS found. Mordirith, Steward of Angmar, came looking for the missing cultists carrying a powerful artifact. The water did not obscure the stone to one such as he. The dark powers of the Nameless glow like a beacon to the eyes of a wraith.

An Unexpected Request

'Well met, friend. Tell me, are you ${PLAYER}? I have heard much about you from King Thorin! I admit I had been hoping to meet you in person. There is something... secret... about which I must ask. Come, let us move somewhere a little more private.'
'Come, friend. Let us speak in private.'

'${PLAYER}, you stand before me accused of the murder of Grímyr of Durin's Folk. My guard discovered you standing over his body, weapon in hand! You would already be clapped in irons if they had not also found this....'
He pulls a small object from a pouch and shows it to you: a small, perfectly round stone, darker than the deepest cave, blacker than night. As you look into it, something within the stone pulls at your mind, bidding you to look deeper. This stone is known to you. Thorin quickly puts it back into the pouch.
'Indeed. This is the Secret Stone. I had ordered it to be moved from its place and hidden once more, but Grímyr must have discovered its location and stolen it away. You are a hero of Durin's Folk, ${PLAYER}, and in my eyes you are innocent of any wrong-doing; do we not know how this stone can affect the mind? But it is clear to me now that the stone cannot be kept safely in Erebor.'

'Hello, ${PLAYER}. What brings you all the way down here?'
You ask Márus if he knows anything about removing rune-stones set up as traps on doors and describe the state of the chamber you found.
'Oh ho, that's quite clever! You know, I have heard of some of our forefathers using rune-stones to protect their vaults from intruders. Aye, let me try to remember the specifics.'
He spends a few minutes mumbling to himself, lost in thought.
'Right! I remember now! I should be able to help you, but it will be tricky! To dismantle the trap, you will need a powerful rune-stone of your own to protect yourself from the searing flames. I can craft that for you with the right reagents, but, you will also need to track down the original chisel used to carve the rune-stone! Aye, the ancient dwarf-craft is not easily undone. Here, let me write this down for you. Good luck in your search. I fear a chisel that old may be gone forever!'
He quickly jots down a list on a piece of paper and hands it to you:
To Make Rune-stone: - Powerful fire-enchanted chisel - Copper and obsidian rune-stone base - Polished dwarrowgleam
- Don't forget the original chisel!

'Did you find the chisel?'
You show him the ancient chisel and hand over the rest of the items on his list. His eyes light up.
'By Durin's Beard! This truly is a chisel of the First Age! Just look at the craftsmanship! If nothing else, thank you for sharing this with me, ${PLAYER}. Ah, if only it were not so urgently needed. I will get started on your rune-stone now.'
He gets to work on the rune-stone. A short time later, it is complete.
'Here you are. This will protect you, and allow you to dismantle the rune-stone. Ah, to do that, all you need to do is hold the chisel directly in the middle of the stone, and hit it with something. A hammer, the base of a sword, anything heavy will do. It should be that simple!'

You have found the key to this chamber's lock, but judging by the charred bones and blast marks, you should not attempt to use it right away. Below the lock, a rune-stone adorns the door, its carvings glowing an ominous red. If you are going to safely open the door, you will need to find some way to remove the rune-stone.

Grimbeorn wishes to hear of your efforts in the Wells of Langflood. You should report to Grimbeorn as soon as you are able. Your words will assist in Grimbeorn's decisions on how to best defend the Langflood, and perhaps he will know whether assisting the dwarves will benefit all in the northern lands.

'There you are, ${PLAYER}. I have been wondering when you would return. What news have you brought me from Limlók?
'I see, it seems that you and Skarding were able to protect the Floodfells from forces in Misthallow. That is good! I will make sure that needed supplies are sent to Limlók immediately.
'I also see your efforts at Sundergrót with those dwarves prevented Gundabad forces from claiming even more of the mountains. Hmm, well I do not much care for dwarves, but they did save Vaskorn's life. For that I am grateful. Now, I have given much thought to their request. While I will not send my people to foolishly fight for treasure and riches, I will see to it that we assist them when the time is right. I will know when that is. The north is my home and I know when it is in true danger.
'Oh, and to hear of poor Threkmóth! So much bloodshed! Please light a candle for the elder and give my word to the dwarves that the Beornings will not let them down.'

'To tell you the truth, I was expecting Grimbeorn to never answer our request. These are dire times, and there is no one else to whom we could turn in the north. I am very glad that he responded and gave us his word! That will boost the spirits at Skarháld, indeed!
'Now then, my friends, we have been through an ordeal or two together. What do you say about one more? Let us return to Skarháld! This time we will not trudge through the Taurogrim infested wood, however! Let us take the path from Misthallow to Ered Mithrin. It should be less treacherous now that the trolls have been dispersed!'

'I still hear their infernal caterwaulings!'

'You there! You look like you didn’t spend last night with as much ale as some of us. Do me a favour, and I’ll make it worth your while.
'My name is Ulthir, greatest florist in all the land. I’m sure you’ve heard of me? No? Well, no accounting for taste, is there. By the by, wedding season is the most important time of year for a flower monger like myself. I labour for months growing, harvesting, and transporting my renowned blossoms and arrangements from my farm to various cities. This week I have the misfortune of being stuck in this smouldering pile of rocks. Mmmf, my head.
'Where was I? Oh yes, I seem to have imbibed a bit more than I am accustomed to last evening. Ah, don’t look at me like that! Do you have any inkling how difficult it is to keep roses fresh from my farm to here?! The stress nearly eats you alive! I've probably gone down an entire tunic size! So I might have had more than I should have to drink. What do you care? You’re not my wife! Wait, you’re not my wife, are you?'
The merchant squints up at you with bleary eyes.
'No, no you aren’t. Right, listen. You help me out and I’ll make it worth your while!
'You hear that ruckus? Someone in this tavern fancies themselves a bard, but a croaking frog has more melody than that cacophony. Here, take these coins and toss them to whoever that dreadful squalling is coming from. I need at least ten more hours of sleep and they aren’t helping in the slightest.'
