'So you return, ${PLAYER}. What did they have to say of Prince Durin's plans?'
You inform Náin of what Agnar, Lági, and Reithvald told you.
'I should have expected such wisdom from the Dwarves of the Kharum-ubnâr! In truth, I find myself in agreement with them, but a dwarf of my reputation could hardly deliver such news to Durin. I would be called Náin the Slaked, and that is no title for the Lord of the Iron Hills!
'Were it my army, I would muster more forces to Elderslade and call upon distant cousins and allies, but that would be a matter to bring before my brother, Thorin. Ah, for once, I am pleased such a decision is not left to me!
'You must return to Annâk-khurfu on my behalf, ${PLAYER}. Let this be my guidance to the Prince: seek the wisdom of your father and stay your hand for the moment that it might soon swing with renewed strength.'

'${PLAYER}, what did Náin have to say of my plan?'
You deliver Náin's guidance to Prince Durin. The Prince's face becomes stern, betraying the faintest hint of embarrassment.
'I must admit, my friend, that is not the response I expected. But if uncle Náin believes I should send word to my father that the Gabil'akkâ might be the better for it, I have no reason to doubt his judgment. After all, it was not so long ago that I spent my days at the Quenching Trough in Járnfast, spared the battle before the Lonely Mountain by the will of my father. Ah, but when it is my uncle who urges restraint, only a fool would ignore his counsel!
'Perhaps I was too swift to dismiss Glóin's concerns. I shall have to apologize to him for my imprudence, if I might.
'It seems I have much still to learn, despite my station.'

'How fares my nephew at Annâk-khurfu, ${PLAYER}?'
You exchange welcomes with Náin, and then tell him of Prince Durin's plans to reclaim Gundabad. After a moment, you ask Náin what the Kharum-ubnâr in his garrison might make of it.
'It is a sound plan to my ear, but my eagerness for battle is well-known. I would not even wait for the morrow, were I a younger dwarf!'
Náin pauses.
'It may be that Thorin is not as well-suited to battle as I am, but he is keen in judgement. It was not by a mere whim that my brother sent three of the Kharum-ubnâr to aid the Prince. Beyond those three warriors, none of the Longbeards in the Gabil'akkâ, even old Glóin, have seen so much of battle and its costs.
'I will honour your request, if you would honour one of my own. I have seen Gorgar's ilk, all manner of evil beasts, and even some of those wicked Men of Angmar drawing nearer to Zarkul-sulûn since the battle at the gates, and I would not have them doubt our mettle. Slay them to the last!
'Let us see how the Kharum-ubnâr judge Durin's plan, ${PLAYER}.'

'What does Lord Náin ask of me?'
You tell Agnar about Prince Durin's plan to reclaim Mount Gundabad and ask what he thinks of it.
'We did what we could to hinder Gorgar and his army of Orcs on the field, but these old bones are not as strong as they were when I was a younger dwarf. I am as eager as Prince Durin to return to Gundabad, but it is a difficult prize to grasp — and I should know!
'After all, I was there when Komog, son of Azog, fell broken in its halls, and I remember how it fell just as quickly back into the hands of the Orcs after the war!
'Do not misunderstand me, ${PLAYER}. I think much better of our chances this time, but I would not press the attack until we are better prepared for what awaits us within.'

'It is good to see you, ${PLAYER}. But what has brought you here?'
You present Prince Durin's plan to reclaim Mount Gundabad to Lági and ask his thoughts on it.
'Although he has led the Gabil'akkâ admirably through this war, I have many misgivings in regard to the Prince's plan.
'Just look at the soldiers here in Zarkul-sulûn. They are tired.
'We spent the lives of many dwarves to win the gates of Mount Gundabad, but for those who survived, it is now a matter of will — and not all of the dwarves in the Gabil'akkâ can bear such a burden. Hardship is to be expected in war, but many of these soldiers do not know it as I do.
'In my youth, we spent six years of bitter war fighting our enemies, but even in the height of his fury, King Thráin knew the value of respite from battle. Many look back at that war as a single, great battle at Azanulbizar, but had we fought those years without rest, we would never have made it to the gates of Khazad-dûm.
'If Prince Durin would hear my advice, it is that our soldiers need rest and the time to heal for the coming battles. We have been fortunate thus far in the War of Three Peaks, but winning a battle does not win a war!'

'Lord Náin has sent you? I have much to report, ${PLAYER}, some for good and some for ill.
'Of the good, our defences have held against the Orcs and their numbers have dwindled since our encounter at the gates of Mount Gundabad. Those few that make their way to our line are unorganized and easy prey for the Zhélruka. In the past several days, I am proud to report that we have not lost a single dwarf!
'Ah, but of the bad, it should come as little surprise. We are still engaged in war, my friend. There is no time to simply take shelter and rest while Gorgar hides within the Mountain-home. After all, there are other ways out of that mountain and the Orcs must know all of them.'
You interject to ask Reithvald about Prince Durin's plan to reclaim Gundabad.
'Ah, that is not so simple a matter. My soldiers are in need of rest. I have seen enough of battle to know the signs of fatigue, even if they are too proud to admit it.
'Durin holds some of his army in reserve at Annâk-khurfu, and I would urge him to send as many soldiers as he can spare to relieve us. Even if only for a short time, it would be of great help to us for the coming battles!'
'Well, what had the elders of the Kharum-ubnâr to say of the Prince's plan?'
'Let us hope the guidance of the Kharum-ubnâr is enough!'
'If my uncle and I are in agreement, we will press the attack at dawn!'
'Ah, for once, I am pleased such a decision is not left to me!'
Although the din of war can be heard in the distance, Zarkul-sulûn is quiet

'Before this war began, King Thorin sent three elder warriors to aid his son: Agnar Brokentooth, Lági Helmbiter, and Reithvald Red-ember. They are Dwarves of the Kharum-ubnâr, the Brethren of Survivors. It is an order little known outside the line of Durin's Folk, but its members hold a place of high esteem in the eyes of King Thorin, and more importantly, those of his brother, Náin.
'I would wager there is little that might temper his fervour for battle as much as the word of one of the Kharum-ubnâr — let alone three of them!
'I believe Prince Durin intends to send word to Zarkul-sulûn that his uncle might be apprised of the plan to reclaim Mount Gundabad. It so happens that Agnar, Lági, and Reithvald are among his garrison. Need I explain myself further, ${PLAYER}? This must be done delicately, that the Prince is not undermined in the eyes of the Gabil'akkâ.
'You are a trusted friend, ${PLAYER}, and I am certain the Prince would send you on this errand should you ask.'

'Ah, ${PLAYER}! It is good to see you here once again, my friend.
'For my part, I have not sat idle since the battle at the gates of Mount Gundabad! After the death of Ránulur, Gorgar fled in fear from the Gabil'akkâ! And yes, I am quite aware that Hrímil Frost-heart may have influenced his actions, but it was a victory nonetheless. After so much hardship, a mere wall of ice cannot keep me from my prize!
'I saw you speaking with Glóin. All is well, I hope?'
You tell Durin that Glóin told you of a new plan to reclaim the Mountain-home and you request that you might be the one to bring word of it to Náin.
'Indeed! It is my belief that we should breach the ice on the morrow and hunt down Gorgar within the halls of Gundabad. Dwarves are hardier than Orcs, after all, and if we grant our enemies too much rest, all of our efforts in this war would be for naught. We are so near to victory, my friend! We mustn't let up now!
'As for your request, it is granted. Deliver word of my plans to Náin, and see if he finds it to his liking!'

'So this is Elderslade? Hmmph, it is smaller than it seemed in grandfather's stories!'
Hersegg pauses.
'It is beautiful, though, and Mount Gundabad is greater than I could have ever imagined. Ah, but this is not a time for tours. I should introduce myself to the Dwarves of the Gabil'akkâ and see what needs to be done!
'I'm sure I'll see you around, ${PLAYER}. After all, this won't be the last time you hear my name!'

'Ah, ${PLAYER}!
'It is high time you returned to my son, I think. After all, there is a war to be won and the Mountain-home awaits!
'Although I am certain my father Dáin would have been just as eager to join in the reclamation of Mount Gundabad, I am pleased that Hermáth will be there to guide Durin in the coming days of his campaign.
'You have done much to aid my son. For that, I and all of Durin's Folk thank you. May the Gabil'akkâ triumph!'

'A moment, ${PLAYER}....'
Hermáth Stormhammer looks to King Thorin and speaks.
'Do not fear for your son, Thorin. Your father, Dáin, was so proud when he was born, and rightly so! Each of us hoped that our sons would be Durin reborn... and though it was not fated to be for my son, I still hold hope that Durin will embody his namesake when the time is right.'
Hermáth Stormhammer turns back to you.
'Lead the way, my new friend... the Prince awaits us!'

'It has been a long time... but the Slade is still as I remember it.
'This old fortress had a different name during the Sixth War, but Annâk-khurfu is more fitting, I think.
'I am glad that our paths have crossed, ${PLAYER}. When the time comes to reclaim Gundabad, I will consider myself fortunate to have you at my side—and I am sure Durin will think much the same!
'I ought to not keep Prince Durin waiting, so I will meet you inside, my friend.'

'When I asked my father to send his aid, I did not expect you to return with Hermáth Stormhammer!'
Durin appears overwhelmed.
'Hermáth and I have spoken since his arrival, and we have agreed that the Gabil'akkâ will march on Mount Gundabad at dawn—in seven days, of course! Those that would answer the muster will need time to travel to Elderslade, and I eagerly await their arrival. Every dwarf shall have a role to play in the reclamation of Mount Gundabad!'

'Let me see what all this is about!'
Hersegg looks over the missive from King Thorin. Her bushy eyebrows raise and lower a few times until finally she lets out what seems to be a sigh of relief.
'Well, that wasn't what I expected....
'I must apologize for my curt introduction, ${PLAYER}. I am Hersegg, and I tend to Akrâz-zahar on behalf of the Kharum-ubnâr.
'As for that missive, it seems King Thorin wishes for me to introduce you to the works of my grandfather, Hermáth Stormhammer. He kept a detailed account of his experiences in the Sixth War of the Dwarves and Orcs, especially the Battle of Azanulbizar. In fact, a collection of his volumes are right over there! Although I am sure Prince Durin has heard tales of that war before, the King insists your study of it will be of use to his son and the Gabil'akkâ.
'But it's no use studying the battle without hearing the beginning of the tale, I say. King Thorin has given me a task of my own, but since I have a little time, I'd be honoured to read it to you.
'So, what do you say?'

'As for Nár, I think it's good that he has finally left Zudrugund behind.
'Since his return, Nár has made many friends in the Lonely Mountain. When he feels well enough to visit us here in Akrâz-zahar, I have heard his laugh and seen the light in his eye when he smiles. Although it pains me to even think such a thing, perhaps his addlement has been something of a mercy — some small kindness bestowed upon him by the First Crafter.
'Let us hope that Nár has found some measure of happiness again, even at so old an age. It is the very least he deserves!
'Now then, I must tend to the task King Thorin gave to me, and you ought to begin your studies of my grandfather's work!'
Hersegg gestures to a stack of books atop the nearby table.
'Those will tell you all you need to know about the Battle of Azanulbizar, ${PLAYER}. When you've studied it enough for your liking, you are to return to the King Under the Mountain.
'With any luck, I'll see you again soon.'

As his thoughts turn to Durin, Thorin's voice swells:
'I have always been the more cautious of Dáin's sons, and it has served me well. But for too long, I believed it would suit Durin in much the same manner.
'It was not so long ago that I sequestered Durin in the Iron Hills while battle raged in the Dale-lands, but now my son leads an army to reclaim the Mountain-home. I dared not dream that Gundabad might be within reach, especially after the failure of the Iron Garrison, and yet, my son has proven its possibility, both to me and to all of Durin's Folk.
'Durin is not as hot-tempered as my brother, nor is he as measured as his father—he is himself, and that is enough. Durin will err, as any dwarf will in his time, but I did not name him Durin that he would earn the name in his life—the name will earn him through his deeds.'

'Ah, very good!
'I have written my father a formal request for a new muster to Elderslade—one that comprises all of our trusted allies, even those unskilled in combat. When the time comes to reclaim Gundabad, we will have need for dwarves of every vocation!
'I have also made special note that I will not begin the assault on Mount Gundabad until the time of your return. If my father wishes to offer any guidance, I would prefer to hear it before the battle is upon us!'
Durin seals the missive he has written to his father and hands it to you.
'By entrusting you with this missive, I am entrusting you with the success of the Gabil'akkâ, my friend.
'Be swift and let nothing turn you from your path to the Lonely Mountain!'

'Welcome, ${PLAYER}.
'It has been some time since Glóin's message-raven arrived, bearing a warning that the line of Azog remains unbroken in Gundabad. What news do you bring of my son? How fares his campaign?'
You inform King Thorin of the events that have transpired since he sent the remnants of the Iron Garrison to Annâk-khurfu. You tell the tale of the battle on the threshold of Gundabad—of Gorgar's near-defeat and of the sudden danger of Hrímil Frost-heart, returned from the Anvil of Winterstith. You also tell King Thorin of Durin's desire to press the attack and how he was persuaded against it, at least for the moment, by Náin and dwarves of the Kharum-ubnâr.
'I feared you had come bearing ill tidings, my friend. So long as my son is well, it puts my heart at ease.'
Thorin glances at the mass of letters and parcels you have brought to Erebor.
'I appreciate that you answered me as swiftly as you did, but please, set all of that down. My subjects will see that they are delivered to the proper dwarves here in the Lonely Mountain.
'As for his missive, let us see what he has written.'

'A moment, my friend.'
King Thorin reads the missive from Durin.
'I see. Tell me, ${PLAYER}, how did my son come to change his mind, truly?'
You tell King Thorin of Glóin's concern and of his suggestion to speak to the Dwarves of the Kharum-ubnâr among the Gabil'akkâ.
'It was for that reason I sent them, and I am heartened that Glóin warned him against plans borne of vengeance. I only wish my son had heeded his words. Durin leads the greatest Longbeard army we have brought to bear in seventy years, but he is still young and, in truth, untested. Yes, he has found victory at many stops along his journey from the Iron Hills, but it is hardship that shapes a dwarf!
'Durin was fortunate to know my father, Dáin, in his time. He, too, was young when he answered the call of war, and I often wonder what he would think of how swiftly Durin has grown into his name.'

As he reminisces about Dáin, Thorin's voice softens:
'What can be said of my father, Dáin, that has not been etched into the very history of Durin's Folk?
'He was but a stripling when he slew the Great-orc, Azog, at Azanulbizar. It was he who answered the call of Thorin Oakenshield and defended the Lonely Mountain against Bolg and the goblins of the North, and in so doing, ushered in a time of peace between Men, Elves, and dwarves. And again, when the Enemy sent his servants to the gates of the Lonely Mountain, he died in defence of his people—a hero to his last breath!
'But despite all of his great deeds, I knew him as my father. I was his son, and Durin, his beloved grandson.
'I must confess that I often saw more of Dáin in Durin than I did in myself, but what greater dwarf could one aspire to be?'
'I will need some time to draft a missive to my father, so gather the letters and parcels here at Annâk-khurfu.'
'Deliver the missive to my father as swiftly as you are able, ${PLAYER}!'
'I have thought often both of my son, and of my father, Dáin, since Durin set off into the Grey Mountains.'

'It is true that many Dwarves of the Iron Garrison pledged themselves into the service of my son, and more still journeyed from our holdings in the Misty Mountains to aid the Gabil'akkâ. Even so, there are many Longbeards and trustworthy Dwarves of the Landorrim and Narfanghoth that might still be called upon.
'Durin has requested that I send a new muster to the Mountain-home. It will be done!'
Thorin pauses for a moment and strokes his beard.
'But so too does my son ask for my guidance, and that has given me much to consider.'
With great relief, you set everything on the landing before King Thorin's throne

'I must admit, I had not expected to send another messenger to the Lonely Mountain until this war was ended. I had hoped to send tidings of victory to my father—that I might finally prove myself a dwarf worthy of the name \qDurin\q!
'Bah, perhaps it was folly to entertain such stubbornness! If my uncle believes the Gabil'akkâ would be helped by again swelling its numbers, I see no reason to argue with him.'
Durin looks across the upper hall of Annâk-khurfu.
'I will need some time to draft a missive to my father, but I have had an idea!

'I will set to writing my father at once. After you have gathered all of the letters and parcels, return to me.'

'To that end, I have written a number of missives to be delivered to other Longbeard holdings across the world as well as those of our cousins, the Landorrim and Narfanghoth. 'It is time we dealt with the matter at hand, my friend.
'When I sent you to seek out Hersegg at Akrâz-zahar, I also gave to her an errand. Although I sent Agnar, Lági, and Reithvald to aid my son in his campaign, I must admit I hesitated to enlist another of my father's old friends in the Kharum-ubnâr. Not because I did not think him suited to the task, but for reasons I am ashamed to give voice. But I have shrunken from my duty for long enough!
'As I had hoped, Hersegg has sent word that I have been invited to visit her family's home at Vosh Torú. Whether this meeting goes well or ill, Durin awaits your return.
'What say you, ${PLAYER}? Will you accompany me?'
'I will show you the way to Vosh Torú, my friend.'

'You must understand, ${PLAYER}. Hermáth was my father's friend, not mine.
'After what happened at the end of the War, I feared he would want nothing to do with me. I know how dear Durin was to him, and my heart aches that his son fell in the defence of the Lonely Mountain.
'Yet, young Hersegg has her father's spirit. If Hermáth honours my request as he says, I think he will have a difficult time convincing Hersegg to stay behind!
'Ah, I must return to the Hall Under the Mountain, my friend. But, thank you for helping me to clear the air between us!'

Travel to Akrâz-zahar in the Dwelling-halls of Tumnu-dûm, in Erebor

'My son asks my guidance in winning a war.'
Thorin chuckles to himself.
'I may not be a warrior in the manner of my father, ${PLAYER}, but I know well enough that those of Kharum-ubnâr learned such lessons long ago.
'After all, it was Dáin who organized the Kharum-ubnâr after the war's end. It was to be comprised of those who survived the Sixth War, and those descended from Marasrân—the Burned Dwarves of Azanulbizar. Agnar, Lági, and Reithvald are not the only dwarves of that order who still dwell within the Lonely Mountain, my friend. Perhaps their wisdom might be of use to my son....'
Thorin thinks for a moment, stroking his beard. After a moment, he produces a small scrap of paper and writes upon it a short message.
'Within the Dwelling-halls of Tumnu-dûm, there is an order-hall of the Kharum-ubnâr. It is known among Durin's Folk as Akrâz-zahar, and there you might find a dwarf named Hersegg. She is barely beyond the age of a stripling, but she is the granddaughter of one of the greatest heroes of Azanulbizar, and more importantly, one of the dearest friends of my father, Dáin.
'I have written her a note asking that she might introduce you to the works of her grandfather, Hermáth Stormhammer. She, too, is well-studied in the lore of Durin's Folk, possessing wisdom beyond her years.
'Deliver this missive to her, and she will understand what I ask.'

'Good work on dealing with those night-time visitors. There is more work to be done here in Gundabad, and it is a long road that lies ahead of us. At least the travel on this road involves making a home, rather than searching for one.'

'You see the potential offered to us by the hall of Vérnozal? Yes, I have seen it too.
'Potential is not enough for the Zhélruka, however! This hall must be a place of beauty, restored to the shining beacon it once was. Right now the hall is covered in dust and crawling with small night-time beasts! Perhaps tonight you could take care of these unwelcome visitors for me.'
'I am here to assist Hórin and Scout-master Ausma on important missions for the Zhélruka. If you assist us on these missions, I will certainly share the rewards with you, ${CLASS}.'

'Ah, my friend, ${PLAYER}. We have undertaken many missions together, have we not? Aye, that we have! If we are to reclaim Gundabad for the Zhélruka, I say we will adventure together a great deal more. There is much history to learn of the Mountain-home and old halls to explore beneath the Three Peaks. Speak with Ausma or myself if you wish to carry out a mission.'

'I knew you would assist our cause!
'Advising Prince Ingór can be difficult at times, but it is always worth the effort. He has a good heart, and wishes only the best for his people. I am certain we will work closely together, for you have his ear as much as I do!'
'Welcome, ${CLASS}. I am glad that you are assisting the Zhélruka in Gundabad. Come see me here in Vérnozal when Prince Ingór decides that you deserve to be rewarded for your efforts.'

Durin's Bane and the Unslain

'So? Were you held in the grip of fear while in the presence of that terrible creature?'
You tell Dáin that you did feel great dread as you neared the East Gate. Visibly relieved, he lets out a great sigh.
'I am glad to hear it, Hermáth. I had begun to fear my father's death had stolen away my courage! But if even you quailed before that monster, I was right to forbid entry into Khazad-dûm; you are one of our bravest warriors! To speak truthfully, I am fortunate the Balrog did not slay me where I stood! It held a whip of crackling flames, and I tell you it was likely long enough to reach me. The spirit of Nafni the Unslain must have protected me!'
He sees your look of confusion at the mention of Nafni's name and epithet.
'Hermáth, do you not know of the great Nafni? He is the only dwarf since the First Age to survive not one, but TWO encounters with a Balrog! I cannot allow this gap in your knowledge of history to continue. Have a seat, and let me tell you the tale.'

'Forgive me: I am much better at cleaving Orc-skulls than I am at spinning tales. I will do my best.'
Dáin clears his throat and begins his story.
'In the year 1980 of the Third Age, Durin's Bane was unearthed in the Foundations of Stone. Nafni was there on that day, protecting Durin VI while the king treated his Elf-guests to a tour of Khazad-dûm's splendid mines. Durin fell to the Balrog's fury, but he ordered Nafni to survive and protect his son, Náin. And so he did, for Nafni was fleet of foot and was able to escape the terrible creature! He saw that fiend in all of its fiery terror... and lived. Upon hearing Nafni's recounting, Náin was enraged, and vowed revenge for his father at all costs.
'The brave soldiers of Khazad-dûm tried to push the Balrog and the Nameless horde in its train back to the depths, but slowly, more and more of the kingdom was to fall. A year later, Durin's son, now King Náin I, gathered his forces and launched one final, desperate attack against the Balrog, slayer of his father and target of his vengeance....'
<rgb=#FF0000>Complete 'The Fall of Khazad-dûm' to witness the events of Dáin's story unfold!</rgb>

Dáin continues the story of Nafni, now near its ending.
'And so Khazad-dûm was abandoned. Thráin I became king, barely older than I am now, and eventually he led our people to Erebor. Nafni earned his title \qThe Unslain\q for surviving his second encounter with the Balrog, and he would become a wise advisor and trusted friend to King Thráin. He was a great and noble dwarf of Durin's Folk.'
Dáin is pleased with his own recounting of the tale, but as his thoughts return to your present situation his face hardens and his eyes burn with anger.
'Though Azog is dead and his Orc-army routed, a greater foe prevents us from reclaiming our lost kingdom. Though all the dwarf clans answer our call to battle, it will not be enough. No power among the mortal races will ever be enough....
'Hermáth, I wish to be alone with my thoughts for now. Thank you for checking in on me.'
Dáin begins to tell the tale of The Fall of Khazad-dûm
You have felt the same dread that Dáin did. Moria is not safe to enter!

Still shaken by the sight of the creature beyond the gates, Dáin squints at you as you approach.
'Have you come to check on me, Hermáth? Hmph!'
He grumbles but spares you an uncertain smile.
'I always thought myself fearless. I have gone toe-to-toe with Orcs and trolls many times my size with nothing but the fire in my heart. But THAT foe... Durin's Bane! Standing in sight of just one such evil has shaken me to my core. Imagine an army of those fiends!
'You do not think me a coward, do you? I know you for a fierce warrior, Hermáth. I would have you go to the East Gate and feel the monster's presence for yourself! Then, at least, I will know I am not alone in my fear.'

'And that is all there is to tell of the doom of Thrór, ${PLAYER}.'

'Thrór had bidden Nár to stay and await his return, but it was not merely the word of his king that kept him from daring to enter Moria. In truth, and to his shame, Nár was afraid.
'For many days Nár hid among the trees outside the gates, lonely and troubled. When he dared to draw nearer to the gate and peer into the gloom, neither sound nor the faintest flicker of light emerged from within.
'More troublingly still, neither had Thrór.'

'When Nár awoke, his clothing was cold and heavy with rain. Nár's rest had ended abruptly, and in a daze, he tried to regain his bearings.
'Above him the sky loomed dark, its hue a sickly purple, and he could not tell if it was day or night. Aside from the sound of trickling rainfall, all was still and silent.
'Alas, Nár would have little time to ponder his situation.'

'Long after the realm of Grárik had fallen to the cold-drake Vethúg, and twenty years after the Lonely Mountain fell to Smaug, King Thrór and his folk came to dwell in a coomb near the wilds of Dunland. From the old stronghold of Zudrugund, Thrór ruled what remained of the two kingdoms he had fled in his life. His son was Thráin, a formidable warrior; his grandsons Thorin and Frerin, and granddaughter Dís, were yet young. His people were few, poor, and hungry, and they knew little joy since the loss of their homes in the North.
'Dotage and gloom took their toll on King Thrór, and he thought long of regaining the splendour of his fathers’ halls. But it was not in the halls of Erebor where Smaug now slumbered upon the heirlooms of his people, nor the frozen wastes in the north that called to him: it was Khazad-dûm itself! It had been more than eight hundred years since doom befell it - since the Elves named it Moria, but it mattered not. Thrór determined that he would reclaim it, and in so doing, restore the glory of his kingdom and of Durin's Folk. What true reason had he, none know for certain.
'Perhaps he had gone mad, or perhaps not....'

'Nár had known the truth at once, but wished not to believe it. It was Thrór.
'As Nár crept closer, there came a chittering laughter from beyond the darkness of the East-gate.'

'At first, Nár again made for the Redhorn Pass, but Orcs beyond counting had gathered there and watched him with their red eyes. And so, Nár fled back the way he had come. As he passed by the gates of Khazad-dûm again, more great Orcs, including some larger than any he had heard of before, had surrounded Thrór’s corpse and were hacking it to pieces. Into that hateful frenzy, a great mass of crows descended, and to them, the Orcs began to fling the scraps of the Dwarf-king. Nár dared not look again.
'Tear-blind, Nár ran on along the banks of Kheled-zâram, fleeing the Orcs and wolves that now hunted him in cruel sport. When at last he came to the ruins of Amdân, he found them barred, and black arrows hounded his every step. Desperate to escape his own doom, however, Nár thought of Kibil-nâla and leapt down the paths alongside the stream. By some stroke of fortune, Nár had won his escape, but behind him the laughter of Azog and the Orcs rang in his ears.
'For many months, Nár wandered in the wilderness, wracked with sorrow, the sight of his King’s defilement branded in his heart. At long last, he found his way north to the High Pass across the Misty Mountains, then made his way back to Thrór’s Coomb. By the time he entered Zudrugund the guards scarcely recognized him, so haggard and wild he had grown.
'Nár was never well in his mind again.'

'Although both Thrór and Nár saw many signs of Orcs in the dale, they were old and overtrodden. Outside Khazad-dûm, all was still and silent. Before them, the East-gate yawned open, as if to beckon the two of them forth.
'But the journey had been long, and Nár thought better of seeking shelter within Moria.'

'Hidden beneath the eaves of trees and stones at the foot of Zirakzigil, Nár built a fire and prepared what meagre meal he could that might befit a king and one road-weary traveller.
'When the supper was ended, Thrór stood at once. As if in answer, Nár knelt before the old king and helped him to fasten a shield to his arm.'

'And waited... until he thought he could bear it no longer.
'Despite every doubt, though, his resolve did not falter. Even if he were fated to live the rest of his days huddled beside a fire at Azanulbizar, Nár would not disobey his king — it was his duty to await Thrór's return.'

'...but whatever the case he summoned Thráin and gave to him what heirlooms of their house remained – chief among them his Ring, last of the Seven that had been given to the Dwarf-kings.
'He said to Thráin, \qRiches may yet spring anew from this bauble, my son. Or perhaps not. Yet one cannot breed gold without gold.\q When Thráin asked if his intent was to return to Erebor, Thrór remained silent. After a long moment, he said, \qThese bones are too old. I will not be avenged on Smaug - that fate, perchance, shall be yours, or your sons’. I have known too much of loss and of Men’s derision. I go to seek better fortunes, if they may yet be found.\q
'He did not say where he meant to go, and Thráin did not ask, but merely wished him fortune in his quest.'

Hoping to aid King Thorin in guiding the Prince to victory, Hersegg, grand-daughter of Hermáth Stormhammer, has offered to tell you the tragic tale of Nár.

'So you wish to hear the tale of Nár? I must warn you, ${PLAYER}, it is quite grim — even for a retelling!
'Ah, but first....'
Hersegg glances around Akrâz-zahar, making careful note of the dwarves still present.
'Ah good, it seems Frithgeir has taken him home. Nár is an old dwarf, and though it is no fault of his own, he is often forgetful and confused in his mind. It is as if the stones of a great mosaic were scattered upon the floor — all of the pieces remain in some form or another, but what it once depicted is lost.
'Even so, neither I nor anyone else in this hall would tell the tale in his presence!'
Hersegg lifts a small volume from her hip and flips through its pages, stopping at one page in particular.
'Let us begin.'

'As for Nár, there is far more to be said of his tale, but I shall tell it as briefly as I might.
'Nár was brought to Thráin in Zudrugund and there told his tale, and spoke the name of Azog, which all Longbeards have held with hatred ever since. All Thrór's court wept at the tidings, and tore their beards, then looked to Thráin who sat down heavily upon his father's throne and was silent.
'Breaking the silence, Thorin said, \qYou are King now, Father. What is your will? How shall we answer this outrage?\q
'All around the court, hands went to sword-hilt and axe-handle, and brows lowered darkly. But still Thráin sat quiet, and did not move. Seven days he remained thus, still as a stone, saying no word. Then, as a storm long gathering that breaks upon the mountainside, he arose, eyes ablaze, and cried: \qThis cannot be borne!\q
'From Thráin's yearning for vengeance arose the Sixth War of Dwarves and Orcs, called simply the War of the Dwarves and Orcs in our memory. Ah, but that is another tale!'
'Are you ready to hear the tale of Nár, ${PLAYER}?'

Slighted Hand

'Yes, I was on Strázhek's watch, but I stepped away for a moment. Zebena came by and told me that there was hot soup in the main tent. She took over my watch for a very, very, short while so as I could grab a bowl.
'Come to think of it... when I came back, she seemed surprised to see me.'

'Aye, I relieved Tébakh for a short while. I am ashamed to say that I may have… been distracted.
'You are not going to believe me, but I am sure that I saw a ghost! I was passing by the broken up statue when I saw something out the corner of my eye. A flittering of fabric, white-grey like sun-bleached bones. I thought it was someone’s cloak or something similar, but it vanished through the gap in the wall and was gone! I looked everywhere I could, but there was nothing to be found.
'Suddenly, I heard a sound back at Tébakh’s post, so I rushed back. It was just Tébakh however, returning with soup still in his beard. I mentioned not what I saw, as I knew it would be met with disbelief. Perhaps in the light of day you will find something I may have missed in the dark.'
'Welcome back, my friend. Please, tell me what you have found.'
Talk to Strázhek

'Hermáth! You must help me!'
'Ah, Thromur,' you say. 'How go things with Frerin? Do you find the work illuminating?'
'Being Frerin's esquire is the highest honour of my life, my friend. However, I may not be able to keep this role once he finds out what has happened. Talk to me in a moment, I need to be sure no one is listening.'
'Hmmm? Aye, it was supposed to be my watch last night, but Tébakh took over for me. Something I ate is wreaking havoc with my guts. Trust me, you don't want details.'

'Right. I think we can talk safely now. As you know, my master, Frerin, dealt a crippling blow to the Orc-chieftain, Urro. Urro got away with his life, but he was one hand lighter that day. From that day, Urro's hand has hung from Frerin's belt, and my master has not lost a battle since.'
Thromur looks around again nervously, then continues in a whisper.
'This morn while I was tending Frerin's armour, I noticed that the hand was gone! My master goes to war today without the luck of that grisly trophy! Please, Hermáth, look into this matter in my stead? If I were to do so, it would draw attention and the others may believe Frerin has lost his luck. The morale of the entire army is at stake! Start with Strázhek. He was on watch last night and may have seen something.'

'Ah, you have arrived at the most opportune time. We are launching assaults to secure points of interests in Gundabad. We need anyone available to fight to Gundabad!'

'How have you made out in collecting geodes? Yes, there are many more to collect, as well as other rare treasures to find in the depths of Gundabad. I seek assistance in finding these additional rare treasures and halting those who seek to destroy them. Can I count on your efforts, my friend?'

'Now that calm has returned to Vérnozal, perhaps you should put some of your other skills to use and assist Ausma and Hórin with a mission.'

'I have done nothing wrong! He says that I stole his goat, but he is wrong! I won it, legitimately, in a game of Hammers and Bones! I bet this Zhélruka liar doesn't even own a goat!

'That Longbeard stole my goat! I would know my goat anywhere and that goat is certainly mine! How can he have won my goat in a game of runic dice? I do not gamble! There is no way I would have sold my goat or gambled it away!'

'Oh my, I am such a fool! Not only is that rope indeed the one used to tether my goat, that gift is also mine.
'I have been trying to profess my love to someone special. I procured the perfect gift, but I lacked anything with which to tie it up! 'The army has been on the move and on the attack for so long that I fear some of our brethren have forgotten better days. What seems a small thing may in truth be a large comfort. I have carved these combs from bone and horn. Please, bring them to those in need. Our beards are our pride, and our bedraggled friends will appreciate freeing their locks from the tangles and knots travel and fighting have brought on.'
'What's this now? A comb? I was going to get around to that... give it here, then.'
'A beard comb? What are you implying! Well, give it here. Might as well put it to use.'
'What now? No, I haven't got a comb for you. Oh! You offer it to me! Well isn't that finely made. Give Elgur my thanks.'
'Oh! Give it here, will you? My own comb broke weeks ago. Well, I suppose you could tell that.'
'Excellently done, friend. This was a small thing, but is one that has the potential to impact our brethren greatly. No dwarf should go to war with his beard a tangled mess.'
Deliver bone combs (${CURRENT}/${MAX})
'Have you delivered all of the combs?'
'Ah, a comb? Thank you, friend. My thick fingers are no match for these snarls.'
'For me? You have my thanks. I will be sure to pass this along to others in need as well.'

Buried Promises

'Well met. I am indeed Elgun.'
You hand her the necklace and tell her its story. She holds it gently, a look of sad wistfulness on her face.
'Thank you for bringing this back to our family. My mother never doubted he loved her. I never got to meet my father, but now I have a piece of him, and of their love.'

'Elskur, Elskur... let me think. Oh! Oh yes, I do remember now. Grandfather often spoke of him. He was one of the Burned, sadly.'
You ask her about the necklace.
'Why no, grandfather never mentioned going back for that. I imagine that it could still be there!'
'How lovely this is! His wife was a woman of fine tastes and she would have loved this dearly. She joined her husband years ago, however. Their daughter Elgun, however, lives here in Erebor.'
A small mound of fresh dirt
It's still here! After all these years!
'She would have loved this view.'
'Have you seen Elskur? He was asking after you. Did he find you? No? Perhaps you could go and see what he's about? He was due back some time ago.'

'Ah, Hermáth. There you are. Listen, friend. I have a favour to ask of you. I have buried a necklace here for my wife. If... if something were to happen to me, would you dig it up and bring it to her? Tell her that I am sorry for the words I said when we parted?'
'Of course,' you say.
'Thank you, my friend. I should have given her the necklace before I left. She would have loved this view. Perhaps I shall return here with her one day, and this promise I ask of you will have been for naught.
'Tell Sárgo I shall return shortly, will you? I think I will take in this view for a bit longer.'

Shálun can be found at Amdân.
To your surprise, Shálun has produced Urro's hand. You should talk to Shálun.

'Hermáth... is that you?'
Shálun coughs and blood dribbles from his lip.
'Is... Urro... slain? What... of the Longbeard... prince?'
You tell Shálun that Thorin slew Urro and survived. Shálun smiles weakly.
'I... told Thromur... I would... make it right. Didn't... I?'

'We have done it... but I don't even know your names, my friends.'
You introduce yourself and Shálun. Amidst the battle around you, Thorin smiles slightly.
'You have my thanks, Hermáth... and you also, Shálun. Your deeds this day will not be forgotten among the Zhélruka, nor shall they be among the Longbeards—that I promise to you!
'Stay with Shálun, Hermáth. His eyes grow dark, and the comfort of a friend would do his spirit well.
'As for me, I....'

'I... I did not mean for that. Nor did I wish for Frerin's death. I only wanted... no matter.
'I will make this right, Thromur. I must!'

'What has happened?! The vanguard is in retreat!
'Come, we must find Frerin!'
'Stay with... me... a moment, won't you?'

'You have... my thanks, but I did not... see you in the vanguard. Did my father send for you?'
As Thorin tries to catch his breath, you explain that you came on another errand, but chose to aid the vanguard when you discovered what had befallen them.
'If you and your Zhélruka friend had not arrived when you did, I... things may have gone differently. I am not defeated yet, though.
'And Urro must pay for slaying my brother!'

'Fundin was a friend of my master's....
'From the looks of it, he was far from the only dwarf who fell in the vanguard's retreat. I fear for master Frerin, but I also fear for King Thráin and what remains of his vanguard.'
Thromur glances at the ground, his eye pausing at a few spots.
'There are many tracks leading to the south-east, and not all of them were made by dwarves. If the Orcs are in pursuit, we must aid the King and our kinsfolk before it is too late!'

'No. I... we are too late. What have I done?'
Shálun steadies himself.
'To lose a son is a pain no father should bear... not once, and certainly not twice.'

'There he is, Hermáth.
'Let us see what Shálun has to say for himself!'

'I know not of what he speaks.
'If there is more to this tale, I would hear it. And preferably before we come to blows!'

'Oh, so now you want to hear what I have to say?'
Shálun glances derisively at Thromur.
'So long as you keep that one away from me, I'll tell you whatever you want.
'I am no thief! Will you hear my tale?'
Instance: Bonds of Oak and Iron
After King Thráin and his vanguard set out to assault the gates of Khazad-dûm, a sudden revelation threatens to raise tensions between the Longbeards and the Zhélruka at Amdân.

'Shálun? I know him well indeed. This would not be the first time he has disrespected Frerin, but even I did not think he would stoop so low!
'Let us see what excuse he makes for this insult... this theft!
'Will you come with me, Hermáth? If you would bring your hammer, I would feel more at ease... though I should hope you need not use it!'

'I misjudged him... Shálun, I mean. My master is lost, but the King and Thorin live because of his sacrifice.'
Thromur lets out a sorrowful sigh.
'The Iron-folk have come at last... I only hope it is not too late!'
'Let us confront this thief!'
Bonds of Oak and Iron
The Battle of Azanulbizar has ended, but at unimaginable cost.

'At last, Azog is slain and those of his kin who survived have been driven back into Khazad-dûm. Alas, we have borne many losses of our own....
'For nine years, I desired only to avenge my father, Thrór, and now that is done. Young Dáin took Azog's head in retribution, and now I would see it set upon a stake as a warning to Bolg and all those who would dare to challenge the Longbeards—nay, any of the Dwarves of the Seven Houses!
'Let us return to the gates of Khazad-dûm, son of the Iron Hills.'

Talk to King Thráin at Amdân

King Thráin can be found at Amdân.

Dáin can be found at Amdân.
After the burning of the dead at Azanulbizar, King Thráin and the survivors of the Sixth War of the Dwarves and Orcs have returned to Amdân. You should talk to Dáin.

'Although I wish it had gone elsewise, the war is ended.
'Too many were the omens that followed the death of Azog... and I must heed them.
'You fought admirably, Hermáth, as did so many of our kin. But they are now Marasrân—Burned Dwarves, and we remain to reckon with our fortunes, both good and ill.
'I hold hope that Khazad-dûm will yet be ours once more, but such a prize will not be easily won.'

'Alas for Azanulbizar, Hermáth. Better it to remain in our memory as it was in the time of Khazad-dûm!
'It will soon be time to return to the Iron Hills, my friend. I, for one, will be glad to leave this place behind.'
'Let us go, Hermáth.'
A Final Reckoning
After coming to Azanulbizar at long last, King Thráin has called the Kings of the Seven Houses to council at Amdân.

'According to my father, King Thráin intends to call the Kings of the other Houses to council this evening.
'The sons of the other Kings and lords have been invited as well, so being the grandson of the Lord of the Iron Hills, so have I!
'You may not be of my blood, but you are my brother, Hermáth. A great battle awaits us on the morrow, and we must be prepared for it.
'Will you accompany me to the council?'

'Amdân is all a-bustle this morn, and it seems some of our cousins have already set out. I am eager to join the battle, but I will heed King Thráin's orders—father made certain of that!'
'What do you say, Hermáth? Will you join me?'

'Thrór is avenged.'
Dain's face is fraught with sorrow as he glances to where his father lays slain outside Khazad-dûm.
'Alas, there is one more thing to be done. Wait here, my friend.'

As you approach Dáin, he appears to hardly notice you.
After a moment, he opens his mouth as if to say something, but remains silent.

'Here we are at last!
'Owing to his wounds, King Thráin and his guard were forced to remain behind at Durin's Stone, but his son, Thorin, has come to aid us. In so short a time, he has made a name for himself by wielding that oak branch—the Oakenshield, they call him. Hah!
'Ever since Bolg fled our arrival at Durin's Stone, my father, Náin, has pursued him... now all the way to the gates of Khazad-dûm! When we catch him, he will fare no better than his other brothers... or his father for that matter!
'It's time, Hermáth. Let us join in the final attack!'

'Hah! See what the line of Azog has been reduced to!'
'I'm glad to see you here at the end of this war, Hermáth. I trust you and my son have slain your fair share of Orcs!'
Náin glances into the shadows beyond the gates of Khazad-dûm, gripping his mattock tightly.
'We have waited long enough for our vengeance. Let us see if this coward has found his spine!'
Dáin remains silent.

'Yes?'
King Thráin appears lost in thought, his gaze fixed upon the dark waters of Kheled-zâram. You tell him the final pyres are prepared, and that Thorin has sent for him.
'So be it.'

'Ah, Hermáth, I think we are ready to light the final pyres.
'Although I am not certain as to his reasons, I believe my father has gone down to Kheled-zâram. We all mourn in our own ways, I suppose, so perhaps he seeks the wisdom of the First Crafter. Alas, this duty is his alone!
'Would you go find him and tell him that we are prepared?'
'My heart is heavy, friend. I wish it hadn't come to this....'

'Ah, you return. But where is my father, Hermáth?'
You explain that King Thráin sent you to inform Thorin that he would arrive shortly, despite his leg-wound.
'He is stubborn as ever, I see. We will wait, then.'
You and Thorin wait for a time, until finally King Thráin begins to shuffle up the ramp to the central pyre.
'There he is!'

'It is time we honoured our fallen as best we can.
'We have stripped them of their mail, taken their weapons, and now we give their bodies to the flame. Bolg and the Orcs will never make trophies of them.
'To burn the dead is not the way of any of our peoples, but it must be done, and we must hold those we lost dear to our hearts and memory.
'Let us honour them together.'

'Nár is right.
'All among my Haban'akkâ have earned a night's rest, but far too many of our kin and cousins shall not wake again. Let Khazad-dûm bear witness to their deeds, both great and small.
'And so, we shall not return to Amdân tonight. Durin himself shall watch over us!'
'I crossed the threshold, and the First Hall laid before me....'

'Oh, Hermáth... I wish I did not have to speak of it.
'But I will say what I must.'

'At last our work is done, but it rings hollow, my friend.
'Many were lost in the fighting, but now even the dale itself lies barren and lifeless. I weep for my father, Náin. I wish he knew how soon victory would come after he fell. Along with the rest of our kin, he too will be burned, but he will remain in my mind as the proud dwarf he was!
'Our friends and cousins mourn their losses, and I would not leave them to grieve alone. I have paid my respects to each of them. I am certain they would welcome any words of comfort from you as well, Hermáth.
'Once that is done, you ought to talk to Thorin. I believe we need only await King Thráin before this grim task is finished.'

At first, King Thráin says nothing.
After a moment, he straightens his beard and turns to the other survivors.
'It is time, Hermáth.'
'Azog sealed his fate the moment he slew my father, Thrór. This shall be a fitting end for him, I think.'

Nár says nothing.
His face is stern, but it does little to mask the tears dried upon his cheeks.
'Oh, Hermáth, let us hope the burned are never forgotten. They mustn't be!'
Instance: A Final Reckoning

Ruins of the Ancestors

'Long have I desired to stand under those arches, and on those bridges. You have given me a wonderful gift on this day, my friend. You have my thanks.
'There is much work to be done, but first this damnable war must be won. Let us hope that the damage from the conflicts to come are minimum. We have much to learn from those who built before.'
'Let us travel the old ways of our forefathers!'

'I heard that you are heading east, towards the Kibil-nâla. I am Gori Stonesetter, Master Architect. An ancestor of mine worked to build bridges and buildings about the valley in ages past, when Khazad-dûm was still ours.
'I wish to examine the nearby ruins, but I need someone with a strong arm to mind my back. If you are of a mind to help, I would greatly appreciate it.'

Gori Stonesetter can be found in Amdân.
Gori has asked you to accompany him to the bridge that crosses the Kibil-nâla.

Gori Stonesetter can be found in Amdân.

Gori Stonesetter wishes to walk among the ruins his ancestors built ages past.
Talk to Gori on the bridge
Talk to Gori

'Khur Azan - the Dim-crossing. Built over two thousand years ago, and now here we are! A testament to our mastery over the valley. Look at these arches, and the detailing. Our ancestors were comfortable enough and had time enough to build grandly. This is no simple bridge over the Kibil-nâla, but a grand testament to the power and abilities of the builders.'

'See those pillars there? An ancestor of mine built them ages past! She left detailed journals of her time here. Sadly, the pages of the journal are as crumbled as the ruins, but I hope to learn more here. The stone of this valley has stood for many thousands of years.'
'I do believe I could spend decades just marvelling at the details here. But come, let us return to Amdân before more of the enemy comes looking for their friends.'

'Fundin's Steps. My ancestor spent much time working on this staircase. She wrote that she worked under the great stoneworker, King Fundin II. Landslides left the already ancient paths to Atrad-zarakh too perilous to safely traverse. They carved the stairs from the very bedrock itself!'

'My ancestor was close with Fundin’s widow, Vigdis. She wrote that the queen’s beard turned white when news of the king’s death reached her. Perhaps it was from grief, perhaps it was from having to take over the duties of ruling until their son, Kalin VI the Young, came of age in 501.'

Complete Mission: King of Claws

'We have done it! The throne of Zidir-nesad has been rebuilt!'

'Before us stands the throne of Zidir-nesad, once the seat of the Lord of Gundabad but now in ruin and disrepair. 'The sacred Jewel of Abhâr has been found... but there is a problem. It has been found by a Dourhand, Mangur Bentpenny, in the Welkin-lofts! I ask you to find a way to retrieve it from this Dourhand without causing too unpleasant an incident.'

'What is it you want, stranger? The Jewel of Abhâr? Bah, is that what this stone I found is called? Sounds important! Sounds even more important if you've come asking about it, I think!
'Do you expect me to just give it to you? I lay claim to it after all, found it fair! If you want this jewel, then what are you going to do for me? Hmm, let me think....'
'Aha! Yes, yes, I've got just the thing! I've always wanted the horn of a silver drake! They are rare beasts, but I've seen one or two here in the Welkin-lofts. You get me the horn of a silver drake, and then... then we'll talk. Not before!'

'My, this is a lot of treasure! Look at all these trinkets and gems! I almost feel badly, trading you this one jewel for all of this treasure... but a deal is a deal!
'Have your jewel and be on your way. Hmm, I might just pack it in. With all these riches, I could find a quiet mountain and live out the rest of my days in peace....
'Well, it's been nice trading with you, stranger!'

'What? You got the horn of a silver drake?'
Mangur Bentpenny mumbles under his breath.
'This fool should be dead.'
Mangur Bentpenny clears his throat and continues speaking to you.
'Hmm, I can see you really are serious about this jewel. Your desire to own this gem makes it more valuable, however. The price has gone up! The horn you gave me is not a fair trade. I need something more....
'Ah, Iron Crown treasures! My friends and I have been trying to acquire the Iron Crown treasures hidden in the Welkin-lofts, but to no avail! If you can find and bring us these hidden treasures, then I will relinquish the jewel to you. You have my word... again!'

'Hail, ${PLAYER}! Have you come to answer the summons of the Kharum-ubnâr? If you wish to aid them, my goats will take you to the Lonely Mountain at once!'

At the behest of King Thorin Stonehelm, the Dwarves of the Kharum-ubnâr seek the aid of skilled adventurers to secure distant dwarf-holds and to prepare Prince Durin and the Gabil'akkâ for victory in the forthcoming reclamation of Mount Gundabad.
If you wish to assist the Kharum-ubnâr, you should report to one of the Mission Recruiters throughout Middle-earth. They will take you to Akrâz-zahar, the hall of the Kharum-ubnâr in Erebor, the Lonely Mountain. Mission Recruiters can be found at Thorin's Gate, Gondamon, Bree-town, The Twenty-first Hall, Othrikar, Gabilshathûr, Glóin's Camp, Hrimbarg, Galtrev, The Dolven-view, Magh Ashtu, Járnfast, Erebor, and Minas Tirith (Midsummer).

'Welcome, and well met! I am glad the Kharum-ubnâr can count on the assistance of brave adventurers such as you.
'The time draws near to reclaim Mount Gundabad, and if Prince Durin is to succeed, we must bolster his army in their preparations and ensure that our brethren at distant dwarf-holds have not been left behind, especially those who remained in Angmar and the Misty Mountains.
'In short, King Thorin has entrusted us with aiding our brethren far afield and the brave Dwarves of the Gabil'akkâ. I will direct your efforts where they are needed most!'

Scraps of paper inside the out-camp might hold information intended for the hobgoblin leadership... but they might be intercepted by a daring adventurer.

'What did you find?'
You hand the parchments to Klúso. He quickly reads the messages, squinting at the crude Orc-scrawls.
'Some of these tidings are old, but some of this is news to me. It is interesting to hear that some lose faith in Gorgar... I wager we can take advantage of that, and wouldn't that be quite the Beard Bonus?
'I'll make sure these get to Ausma!'

'While I've been watching, I've seen quite a few runners come and go with scraps of paper to deliver to Captain Zúrthrug. I assume they are then passed on to the warlord and his closest advisors. Some of this intelligence is probably still in the camp, and will be useful to the war effort!
'Intelligence? In hobgoblins? Bah, there has to be a better word. Well, it will do for now.'

'Good work on a successful infiltration! I am pleased to learn that the Orc and hobgoblin relationship remains tense; we can exploit that. Still, this bargain with the Angmarim is concerning. Perhaps they need a good word from the hobgoblins to get in the good graces of the Frost-horde? We will need to find out.
'Finding Dushtalbúk's throne room is a good first step, but it is going to be hard to catch him alone. We should continue investigating the surrounding area, and see what we can find out about this Angmarim plot.'

'Ah, ${PLAYER}. Keep your voice down. The cave ahead teems with frost-drakes and their spawn! I expect Ausma sent you to see if I had found the drake-nest and if I had, to deal with them at once. Well, I have, so you should!'

'Ack! No, stay away! Wait, you not hobgoblin? You maybe... help me? Me don't want to end up drake food!'
The goblin senses your distrust, and changes his tactics.
'Please, wait! I'll make trade! Warlord sent me here for thieving, but I kept some of the shinies. You take, and you let me go, yes?'
You agree to the deal, and cut the goblin loose. The goblin cackles gleefully and produces a red crystal from under his belt. He holds it out to you, and you allow him to place it in your hand.
'Here! I took this from big hobgoblin lady. She not nice. You take, I go!'
Something feels off about the crystal, besides the stink of goblin upon it. You think Ausma should see this.

'I saw you fighting in there. I guess Ausma was right about you. You certainly are skilled! But what did that goblin give you?'
You show Molkha the strange red crystal. She gingerly takes it from you, and winces. She holds it up to one ear, listening carefully. Her eyes widen. She then hands it back to you.
'I can hear... screaming? Whatever this is, I don't want it! You should take it to Ausma right away. If Loknashra had it, it probably came from the Angmarim!'

'My goodness, ${PLAYER}! What a monster that must have been! I will be able to make something sturdy from this chitin, or my name is not Fúsi Gem-cutter! I mean, this is no gemstone, but my abilities are more wide-ranging than my name would suggest! And so it is with you, my friend.
'Thank you for your help!'

'${PLAYER}! I hope you have been well. We Gem-cutters are here to help! There may not be much use for rings and bracelets in time of war, but we're plenty resourceful folk; I know I can put my craft-skill to some other use.
'Have you seen the strange shelled creatures that crawl hereabouts? They look a bit like crabs, but they are much larger. Their strange and bulbous eyes fill me with unease, I don't mind telling you. The Orcs call them 'Ukhrâsh.'
'Well, I have had a thought, and that thought is this: perhaps we could use their shells to fashion useful articles for the war effort: shields, armour, who knows what else? But the shells of the small ones aren't thick enough to serve. Fret not! I have caught glimpses of a huge one! Only glimpses. I think it spends most of its time underwater, but I have a feeling that one's shell will be worth its weight in gold! I doubt you'll catch it out in the open, but perhaps you can lure it out with meat from the smaller uhkrâsh in the Pit of Stonejaws. I am hoping the big one is both scavenger and cannibal!'

'Your part in this play will be to collect weapons from the Orc-spies hereabout, and then I will scatter them around to make it look like the Orcs ambushed this camp. What can go wrong? Nothing, ${PLAYER}. Nothing can go wrong.'
'Ah, good work! I'll place these next to some of the defeated hobgoblins to set the scene. Let the master show you how it's done!'

'Ah, ${PLAYER}, you have returned. How are my apprentices doing? Tell me everything!'
You tell Ausma of the out-camp you ransacked, pinning the blame on Gorgar's forces; of the drake nest you disrupted; of the unpleasant information you learned regarding the Angmarim and Loknashra. You hand her the two notes you found. She reads them quickly and looks at you with an eyebrow sharply raised.
'The Cult of Drugoth? Wasn't he one of the Gauntlords? And isn't he dead? I think we're dealing with necromancers. And this Loknashra character seems to have more influence here than the warlord wanted to admit, if her agreement with the Angmarim was sufficient to end all hobgoblin-raids on their settlements. This is very troubling. Is there something else, ${PLAYER}? I see that look on your face.'
You carefully remove the crystal the goblin gave you from your bag and hand it to her slowly. She hesitantly accepts it, and winces.
'Ah, the Angmarim are still playing with their crystals, I see. This one seems a little different than those Mother Amma showed me in the Elderslade. A more thorough investigation will have to wait. We need to move on the Angmarim and remove them from the Pit of Stonejaws before they raise an army of ancient dwarf lords to kill us all!'

'Klúso has been sent to keep watch on Stazg Vozag, the hobgoblin out-camp. We know this is where runners from elsewhere in Gundabad deliver their missives and receive their marching orders, rather than entering Shakhajât itself. It seems the warlord takes his precautions very seriously. You should meet up with Klúso and hear what he has discovered.'

Klúso is startled as you approach, but he manages to slap a hand over his mouth before he can make a sound.
'Oh, ${PLAYER}, it's just you! I thought I was about to catch an Orc-dagger in my back! Hahaha... give me a moment to calm my heart!
'So Ausma sent you to get my report, hmm? Well, she was right that this is where the hobgoblins receive messages from elsewhere in Gundabad. Because of that, this camp has drawn the attention of spies, and I don't mean us! Ausma didn't specifically tell me not to do this so... I have an idea. You could do a lot of damage to the hobgoblins if you attack this camp, and because of the suspicion present on both sides, the warlord might assume it was the Orcs doing the backstabbing and not us dwarves! What do you say to that? Smart, eh?'

By order of Warlord Dushtalbúk,
All raids on the Angmarim settlements are to cease immediately. The Frost-bound and the Cult of Drugoth are negotiating a deal. Anyone who has a problem with this should report to Loknashra at their own risk!

'Great work out there, ${PLAYER}. I'll run around and place these Orc-swords before returning to camp, completing the ruse. I think we might actually pull this off! What do you have there?'

'Welcome to the Pit of Stonejaws, ${PLAYER}. We have reason to believe that the hobgoblin seat of power lies within these jagged caverns. We also believe that their leader, Warlord Dushtalbúk, and his advisors are currently here, holed up in their fort to avoid the growing unrest between the enemy forces.
'Our mission here is to locate their fort, discover the scope of their power, and if we are very fortunate indeed, slay the warlord himself. The timing is vital. If we can remove Dushtalbúk from the table before the hobgoblins and Orcs reconcile their differences, they may be unable to organize again before we deal a decisive blow and win this war.
'Because of this mission's importance, Prince Durin has personally asked me to oversee it. You, ${PLAYER}, will also be instrumental in our success. I have not come alone, however. I have taken on three apprentices that I would like you to meet. I have been teaching them the ways of stealth and of the dagger. Go, introduce yourself. 'Prince Durin has commanded you to join the effort in Câr Bronach? He has made a wise decision, I think.
'Before you arrived, Lord Glóin asked me to choose several of my scouts to make contact with the Zhélruka expedition. Since the Iron Crown still holds Câr Bronach, I chose Múta to lead the party. With her, I sent Kársa, Gárjan, and Uzvát -- three of my kin and fine scouts of their own.
'As you may or may not know, there is an eastern gate which leads out of Mount Gundabad. I am told it was long ago claimed by the realm of Angmar, and that whatever its true name once was was lost. It is called the Witch-gate, and it is the swiftest path into Câr Bronach.
'If you wish to aid Prince Durin, find Múta and her scouts beyond the Witch-gate. The Zhélruka will have their reinforcements... whether they want them or not!'

'That was not how I expected this battle to begin, but the tide has turned in our favour! The others have already joined the fight. Find them, and join me up ahead. I will need everyone's help to defeat the elder drake! For the Zhélruka!'
'Everyone is gathered and the reinforcements have arrived. Are you ready for battle, ${PLAYER}?'
'Right on time, ${PLAYER}! The battle is won! Our forces can deal with the rest of these hobgoblins. It is time we returned to Fellgát.'
'Come, ${PLAYER}, let us return to Fellgát. I desire the warmth of a camp-fire and the taste of an ale-flagon!'

'Your work cleaning up Fellgát truly paid off, my long-suffering but never-complaining friend! I am glad to have a proper camp to return to after a fierce battle.
'You fought bravely, ${PLAYER}, and though the day is won, I cannot help but dread what must next be done: Hrímil Frost-heart must be defeated. Gorgar and Dushtalbúk are but pawns to the Dragon, and now fully under her control! If anything, the Orcs and hobgoblins are even more dangerous now, for they work in unison rather than tearing at each others' throats. However, our campaign in Gundabad has had no small effect, and I suspect Hrímil will now pull back her forces to protect her lair. For all her haughtiness, she must be feeling rather cornered.
'The unknown factor in all of this is Loknashra. Hrímil was unable to control her, due to whatever dark magic the Angmarim instilled in her, and she spoke of revenge. I have a feeling she will soon make some move, and we must be ready for it... whatever form it takes.
'But enough of doom and gloom! We will face those foes another day. For now, rest, and drink with me! A cheer, for ${PLAYER}! For the Gabil'akkâ!'

'Our first order of business is to clear out the tents the hobgoblins left behind, and clean up their filth. It will not be pleasant work, true, but it needs to be done. While you are working on that, I will unpack our own tents and set them down here. Then you can prepare them for dwarf-use. We need shelter if we're going to survive up here.'

'Good work, ${PLAYER}! Fellgát looks like a proper camp already. Hórin made sure to pack an extra-large tent for you. That was smart of him, but the rest of us would have laughed to see your feet sticking out the end of a dwarf-tent!

'Bah, the bridge is out! I suppose I should not have expected the road to be in good condition after all these years. The Orcs certainly wouldn't maintain it! Let us see if we can find a way around by walking across that frozen lake down there. Hmm. Molkha should be around here somewhere. Keep an eye out for her signal.'

'Hello again, ${PLAYER}. Keep an eye on the sky, because this area is a drake hunting ground! A big one flies overhead quite often, hunting for goats. I've seen him pluck one right off the side of the mountain and carry it up to the cliff tops there, where I wager he has a nest of whelplings to feed!
'As for my report, I have both good news and bad. The good news is that I was able to observe the hobgoblins passing through here. The bad news is... well, I should just start from the beginning.'

'Now that the camp is ready to receive our reinforcements and provide us adequate shelter in this harsh place, it is time we venture out in search of our enemies. Ausma's apprentices Molkha, Kyrstig, and Klúso are out there in the wild somewhere, spying on the hobgoblin host. They are to signal us when they see us approaching and give to us their report. If we're lucky, they will have some information on why Dushtalbúk is all the way up here in the freezing cold!
'Let us begin by heading south up the Father's Path. It should wind all the way up the peaks, but who can say what condition the ancient road might be in? Lead the way, ${PLAYER}.'
'Let me start from the beginning. Here's what I saw....'

'It seems our enemies are forming alliances right in front of our faces! My blood boils to hear how they use fallen dwarves as bargaining chips in their games of state-craft! Even with those \qgifts\q, I did not foresee the Frost-horde accommodating the Angmarim in this fashion. From what I understood, Sauron's torture of Hrímil had made his former servants her hated enemies. I remember what she did to Karazgar, the Weeping Warrior! It may be that times change, or perhaps she has some nefarious plan in mind for her former foes? Bah, trying to understand the motivations of a Dragon feels like a waste of time. She means to use whatever is at her disposal to exterminate the dwarves, I'm sure!
'But I do think this news merits some investigation before we continue. We need to know why the Angmarim are up here in the first place, and we need to do something about this nest of drakes before they threaten Fellgát and our approaching reinforcements.'

'That is all I saw. Although the Orcs and hobgoblins are not on friendly terms, Dushtalbúk and Loknashra are forming alliances of their own. I expect that is bad news for us, yes?
'The Angmarim have set up camp to the south-east. They call it Mullach Cagar. I am afraid I do not know their aims, but that camp must be of some importance to them. They have poured no small effort into proving themselves valuable allies to the hobgoblins, seemingly to gain safe passage from the drakes. I hope you and Hórin can find out more. I have a very bad feeling about this.'

Hórin is leading an expedition into the peaks of Welkin-lofts to search for Warlord Dushtalbúk and Loknashra.
Completed quests in the Welkin-lofts for Dréri and Náth (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'We have come to these high peaks in search of the hobgoblin leader Warlord Dushtalbúk and his advisor Loknashra. Ausma's scouts spotted them leaving the Stonejaws and marching in this direction with a sizeable troop of soldiers. We do not know their goal here, or why they left the safety of their stronghold, but this is an opportunity we cannot pass up! If we catch Dushtalbúk out in the open on these mountain slopes, we can deal a major blow to Hrímil's forces.'
His face hardens, and he looks towards the sky, still haunted by his previous experience with the Dragon.
'We must defeat the leaders of the Orcs, hobgoblins, and whatever else remains under her sway before engaging Hrímil directly. She is more than enough for an entire army to handle on her own, trust me.
'Judging by the state of this place, we are on the right track. The hobgoblins must have passed through here and abandoned this camp. We cannot pass on such an advantageous defensive position for our own base of operations, so I must ask you to help clean up this mess. I know this is beneath your station, ${PLAYER}, but we are short-handed. Reinforcements will be arriving shortly, so this place needs to be in better shape! Dréri and Náth will take charge of this effort.
'In the meantime, Ausma's apprentices Kyrstig, Molkha, and Klúso have gone ahead to locate the hobgoblin force. It is a shame Ausma could not join us herself, but she is still injured from her attack on Dushtalbúk. After we sort this place out, you and I will go looking for the hobgoblins.'

'It was at the behest of Dáin, my dear friend and King Under the Mountain, that I embarked upon writing a complete account of the Sixth War of the Dwarves and Orcs. For too long, Durin's Folk had endured hardship after hardship, and it did not seem proper to dwell on such a sorrowful chapter in our history.
'Where my own memory and experiences did not serve the tale, I enlisted the accounts of others, chief among them the sons of Fundin and Gróin, and by his own request, King Dáin. For this, they have my truest gratitude.
'As a final note, I have laboured to construct this tale that the reader might see it through mine own eyes. If I should interject on occasion, it is only to make clear certain details or include aspects of the tale learned long after the war's end.'
Beneath the foreword, you notice a dedication.
'For Durin'

'Alas, such are the disadvantages of being the grandson of the Lord of the Iron Hills!
'But you, my friend... I suspect you could pass among the others in this great Haban’akkâ without a second glance, even with that hammer of yours!'
In the distance, you see the Haban'akkâ of Thráin encamped at Amdân

Dáin can be found among the Iron-folk at Amdân.
You should talk to Dáin.

'Hermáth, my friend! I was beginning to think we lost you on the Great-way!'
Dáin embraces you warmly.
'It is hard to believe that we are here at last. I have read the stories of old Azanulbizar, but none could describe it in such detail.
'It seems fitting that this war should end where it began, don't you think?
'And if what I have heard is true, we will not have to sit idle for much longer!'

'By the winter of T.A. 2799, King Thráin and his great reckoning-host, the Haban'akkâ, had made camp at Amdân, the ancient threshold of the kingdom of Khazad-dûm. It had been a long journey, for they had made a wide march around Lórien and come up from the south, treading the old stones of the Great-way.
'All through Amdân, Dwarves of the Seven Houses grew restless. I, like all of the Iron-folk, were camped near to the House of Thráin.
'Although few of us knew it at the time, it was to be the eve of battle.'

'As the battle continued on the slopes of Zirakzigil and Bundushâthur, I was recalled to Khur Azan. It seemed that Dáin's ruse had not gone as unnoticed as he thought, but more pressing matters were at hand.
'Indeed, the Iron-folk had marched forth from Amdân at last—not yet to join the battle, but to stand closer in reserve after King Thráin's vanguard burst through the Orkish encampment of Kamaz-kala, the furthest border of Azog's would-be realm.'

'As we heard at the council last night, King Thráin has ordered the Seven Houses to aid upon the fringes of the dale.
'Among them, the Landorrim, Narfanghoth, and Temámir have travelled to Zirakazhâr on the slopes of Zirakzigil. Once it is reclaimed from the Orcs, I fear they shall have to contend with the trolls we spied from afar.
'As for the Kámbrada, Zhélruka, and Abnúzhu... they have a harder path to take. If they can break through the Orkish outpost blocking the way to Tharkh Shathur, they intend to claim Ashmargathâl and set siege to Atrad-zarakh, the old warding-spire of Khazad-dûm.
'It is far too much, indeed, to ask of any one of the Seven Houses, but together, we will triumph! By Durin's beard, Azog will not live to see the morrow!'
Chapter 2: The Assault on Azanulbizar

'A moment, ${PLAYER}?'
King Thorin clears his throat, seemingly a bit uneasy.
'I believe it is time I spoke to Hermáth—both to offer him a proposal and to apologize.'

'My heart feels lighter this day, ${PLAYER}.
'I am pleased that Hermáth and I could finally speak plainly of our sorrows. And I am even more pleased that he has entertained the idea of joining the Gabil'akkâ!'

'Ah, good! Hersegg is home.
'It has been too long since last I spoke to Hermáth....'
King Thorin notes a look of surprise on your face. After a moment, he raises an eyebrow in what seems to be some sort of amusement.
'Hah! Hermáth may have grown old, but he is still a hale warrior—and very much alive! I thought that was clear, my friend!
'Hersegg seems quite engrossed in her reading. Would you find out if Hermáth is around?'

'Oh, I am sorry, ${PLAYER}. I didn't even hear you come in!'
You ask Hersegg if Hermáth is around, also noting the slight misunderstanding you had with King Thorin regarding her grandfather.
'Grandfather Hermáth? I never said he was dead!
Hersegg chuckles to herself.
'Yes, yes, of course. I'll let him know that King Thorin is here!'
'I think that went well, my friend.'

'Good, you're here! Are you ready to tear this place apart? Ausma must have gone to the throne room. We can't go the same way as last time. Trust me, I already checked: the hobgoblins removed the stairs! So, we're going to have to go through the front door, and through a lot of foes beside! If we make enough noise out here, maybe the distraction will help Ausma!'
'This must be the throne room! We might have to fight Warlord Dushtalbúk as soon as we enter. Are you ready?'
'Kyrstig wants to go in after Ausma? I am with her, of course! Stout-axes do not abandon their own!'

'Kyrstig wants to go after Ausma? Well, I applaud her bravery, but it seems risky to storm the hobgoblin fort with so few of us. And Ausma clearly ordered us to stay here. Hmm....
'All right, I'll do it, but if we get in trouble for disobeying her orders, you'll be the one to shoulder the blame!'
'It's decided then! The three of us will move towards Shakhajât. Come meet us when you're ready, and we will launch our attack!'

'And here we are, back at camp, all safe and sound.'
Ausma sighs deeply, clearly unhappy about the outcome of her mission.
'Honestly, my pride is more wounded than my body, but I will have to sit out on some of our upcoming missions. I will ensure Shakhajât has an adequate watch, and station myself in Vérnozal to oversee the Gabil'akkâ's operations. You and my apprentices have more to do, however! When it is time to make our move on the hobgoblins, I will send word to you to find Hórin. Until then, go, explore Gundabad, and win many battles for us!'
