'And so, the pyres burned away and so the ashen dale of Azanulbizar was abandoned. Although none beheld them at the battle's end, we later learned the Elves of the Golden Wood had borne witness to our deeds, spying the smoke from afar as it rose into the sky above the dale. As King Thráin had named them at Durin's Stone, the Marasrân—the Burned Dwarves came to occupy a place of great honour and reverence among Durin's Folk. Long after, among each of the Seven Houses, all a Dwarf needed to say about his ancestor was 'he was Marasrûn' and it would elicit grave nods and murmurs of respect.
'In time, the other Houses departed back to their homes, bearing the burdens of the arms and amour collected from their dead. As for the Iron-folk, we too departed, making the long journey back to Járnfast. Dáin became the Lord of Iron Hills in all but title, for Grór had become lost in his sorrows, surviving his father, brothers, and now his son alike with not one among them whose bones he could honour.
'Last of all, King Thráin and the exiles departed. They were few now and weary, having lost much and won little in the war, but south they went along the Great-way, until at last they returned to Zudrugund.
'The Sixth War of the Dwarves and Orcs was ended—the cost too great, the prize too small to hold.'

'Azog is slain, and the Ironfoot has taken his head. The Orcs should know the battle has turned against them!
'And yet, some of Azog's own clan still cling to their meagre holdings outside the Great Gates. It cannot stand!
'Slay these... Ufúrzrak, and drive the rest of his ilk back beyond the gates of Khazad-dûm! Azanulbizar will be ours!'
Before the gates of Khazad-dûm, crows pick at Azog's remains
Defeated Ufúrzrak Orcs at Muru Azog (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeated Ufúrzrak thrug-hai at Muru Azog (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Before the pass leading to the gates of Khazad-dûm, the survivors of the confrontation against Azog gathered anew. After the slaying of Azog, they had withdrawn from the encampment, anticipating another assault from the Orcs who still dwelt within Khazad-dûm. With them, they bore away only the head of Azog and the body of Náin Orcsfoe. Indeed, Náin's mail-collar had withstood Azog's blow, but the same could not be said for his neck. It snapped, and by all accounts, Náin had died in an instant.
'Little comfort this was to Dáin, who had remained silent ever since he ventured beyond the Great Gates. Even so, the head of Azog was the prize King Thráin had sought ever since Nár brought word of Thrór's death to the exiles at Zudrugund. And it had been won!
'Left nearly halt after Urro wounded him at Durin's Stone, King Thráin knelt among his guard, but his eyes would not be turned from Khazad-dûm.'

Ah, Hermáth! Though I tried to convince my father otherwise, he insisted on sending those messengers to find you.

It seems King Thráin's son, Frerin, and his esquire had something of an argument, and he sent that dwarf back to Amdân on some errand. Before Thromur could return, Frerin had no choice but to set off with the vanguard. Thromur! That was the esquire's name!
'Lord Grór has asked us to repel the Orcs at Kamaz-kala should we be needed in the dale, but once that is done, you should find out what has been keeping Thromur. He ought to hurry up or the battle will be over!'

'As King Thráin and his vanguard battled down the Great-way, we of the Iron-folk stood ready to answer the horn-calls of our brethren. None were more eager to join the fight than Náin Orcsfoe, but Grór forbade his son from following the vanguard to Khazad-dûm. With the Black Mattock in hand and his horn at his side, the Lord of the Iron Hills knew well his duty, but if news did not soon come of victory, he would sound the horn-call himself and send the full fury of the Iron-folk against Azog.
'Alas, in the vanguard's wake, the Orcs had reassembled at Kamaz-kala and yet unknown troubles were stirring at Amdân.'

'Ah, Hermáth. Is something on your mind?
'Shall I remind you of the tale of Nafni the Unslain?'
Dáin clears his throat and begins his story once again.
'In the year 1980 of the Third Age, Durin's Bane was unearthed in the Foundations of Stone. Nafni was there on that day, protecting Durin VI while the king treated his Elf-guests to a tour of Khazad-dûm's splendid mines. Durin fell to the Balrog's fury, but he ordered Nafni to survive and protect his son, Náin. And so he did, for Nafni was fleet of foot and was able to escape the terrible creature! He saw that fiend in all of its fiery terror... and lived. Upon hearing Nafni's recounting, Náin was enraged, and vowed revenge for his father at all costs.
'The brave soldiers of Khazad-dûm tried to push the Balrog and the Nameless horde in its train back to the depths, but slowly, more and more of the kingdom was to fall. A year later, Durin's son, now King Náin I, gathered his forces and launched one final, desperate attack against the Balrog, slayer of his father and target of his vengeance....'
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTE: Completing 'The Fall of Khazad-dûm' on any difficulty will advance this quest.</rgb>

Dáin continues the story of Nafni, now near its ending.
'And so Khazad-dûm was abandoned. Thráin I became king, barely older than I am now, and eventually he led our people to Erebor. Nafni earned his title \qThe Unslain\q for surviving his second encounter with the Balrog, and he would become a wise advisor and trusted friend to King Thráin. He was a great and noble dwarf of Durin's Folk.'
Dáin appears even more pleased with his most recent recounting of the tale of Nafni the Unslain.
'Khazad-dûm may have been abandoned, but the spirit of Durin's Folk has never dimmed!'

Talk to King Shâlim Nightcloak

'What do you say, Hermáth? The journey will be long, but hardship has not stopped us yet!
'Will you aid our kin and cousins at Ashmargathâl?'

'Yes, Longbeard? Do you bring word from King Thráin?'
King Shâlim Nightcloak looks to you. You inform King Shâlim that you have come to aid the dwarves on Bundushâthur.
'At least someone means to do what must be done then! I grow tired of these Zhélruka and Kámbrada. Not their warriors, mind you, but Usk and Vélat. For dwarves I thought to be sworn enemies, they seem to grow closer friends with each passing hour. That is all well and good, but it seems they have forgotten there is a war to be won!
'The Abnúzhu have slain many Orcs this day, and we will slay many more before its end. I would not leave this battle empty-handed, friend. Orc-bones can make for fine trophies!'

'If King Thráin means to bolster us only with a single warrior, I hope he has chosen wisely!'
King Usk stares you down, and then chuckles to himself.
'I welcome any aid you would give us, Longbeard. After all, Vélat and his Zhélruka have spun enough tales to last three wars, but if we intend to rout our foes, someone must do the fighting. A-ha!
'Among the Orcs at Atrad-zarakh, their smaller cousins have proven difficult to overcome. Between the bat-tenders and those wielding their crude explosives, it has made our approach much more challenging than I had hoped.
'Do what you can, and that is enough!'

'What is this? Does King Thráin not trust us in our task?'
King Vélat smirks.
'I jest, Longbeard! Between the Zhélruka and the Abnúzhu, we have things well in hand. Oh, and I must admit that my friend, Usk, and his Kámbrada have played a part in our success as well. Hah!
'Ashmargathâl was an easy prize to win, but Atrad-zarakh still teems with our foes. It would be far easier to look ahead without those accursed bats flitting about our heads!'

'Hail, friend, and welcome to Deepscrave.' Náin gestures to the oppressive darkness that surrounds the Berg-beam. 'A shame that I can only stand here and watch as the Orcs continue to brutalize the homes of our ancestors.

As if I can be hasty about seeking the death of one whose family caused mine -- and many others -- such grief! Whatever end I can grant him, I will make sure it is anything but quick and painless.

'I sent the scout Múta to investigate reports of missing supplies. She went downstairs to examine the supply area before leaving, and that was the last time anyone saw her. Normally, I would not be concerned for someone of her caliber, but we've received no word from her.

The master is in the muck, the master and the bones and the crystals. All in the muck, dragons in the mire. Never will I breathe clean air again.\q
'Fascinating, no? Could there be a dragon here in Clovengap? Aside from our frosty lady, that is. But another, perhaps? A second dragon?! Mired in the muck somewhere? By Durin's beard, this is too exciting.
'Oh! I almost forgot. The journal mentions experiments on some of the frost-drakes that followed Hrímil into Clovengap. They have taken up residence at Frósthel, a set of ruins across the river. You go deal with that, and I shall have a look at the fragments you brought me.'
'Ah! You return. Tell me of the drakes!'

'Corrupted drakes? Terrible news! Glad am I that you have dealt with this situation, my friend.

'\qMy master has demanded more tests. More more more tests. My master in the muck. The bones are leaking. Leaking leaking. I told Crágacha that she was not done. 'You have them? Give them here, my friend!'
As Múta examines her axe and dagger, a smile forms at the corner of her mouth.
'You have my thanks, ${PLAYER}. It'll be time to put them to use soon enough!'

'Did you find anything?'
You hand the orders to Múta. As she reads them, her eyebrows raise and lower a few times. After a moment, she scoffs.
'Bah! If these orders are to be believed, we and the Zhélruka have our work cut out for us. From what I can tell, the Iron Crown, as well as their Dourhand and Hill-men allies, now serve one named High Priestess Ásachal. I cannot be certain of it, but I would not doubt she is a descendant of the corrupt Men of Westernesse! It seems the Iron Crown has laid claim to that fortress across the valley—the Drearspire, they call it. It is said they seek something called \qCrûn Nasgadh\q, but I cannot glean anything else about it from these orders. Is it some sort of artifact? A spell of old Angmar? Whatever it is, I'm certain it won't be good for us or the Gabil'akkâ if they find it!
'Things are more urgent than they seemed, ${PLAYER}. Will you fetch me my weapons? The Dourhands took them and set them on a table over there—just out of my reach. I've an idea on how to escape from this cage, but I'd feel a lot better about it if I wasn't unarmed.'
Múta's axe is of a simple design, but it has clearly seen much use

'Before we set out, Múta warned us that some new purpose has kindled the spirits of the Dourhands and that they serve one of their own sworn to the Iron Crown: Brathar Crack-helm. We made every preparation... or so we thought.
'No sooner had we passed through the Witch-gate than we were caught in a trap! Múta was captured by the Dourhands, but I do not know what has become of Kársa or Uzvát. Alas, ${PLAYER}, I'm in no condition to mount a rescue.'
'I'm afraid you will have to manage that, my friend.'
As Gárjan braces his leg, you notice a lengthy gash in the armour covering his thigh.
'Bah, it looks worse than it is! At the very least, I can make it back to Bárgstad on my own to tell Ausma what has happened.
'Do not let these Dourhands get the last laugh, ${PLAYER}. Múta must be freed before it is too late!'

'${PLAYER}! What are you doing here?!'
Múta's voice shrinks to a gruff whisper.
'I didn't expect for help to be sent so soon, but given the circumstances, I'm more than happy to be wrong! When the Dourhands ambushed us, I saw Kársa and Uzvát escape to the east. But have you seen Gárjan?'
You tell Múta that Gárjan escaped and that he now intends to warn Ausma and Lord Glóin of the danger beyond the Witch-gate.
'It seems our efforts to foil the Iron Crown in Elderslade did not go as unnoticed as we hoped. After the Dourhands threw me in this cage, I overheard them mumbling about new orders from Brathar. Unfortunately, they were wise enough to continue their conversations where I couldn't eavesdrop on them.
'Why don't you see if some of them have been foolish enough to keep their orders on hand? I'll keep trying to free myself in the meantime!'

Nakrovak, a crystal-encrusted Warg, has asked you to listen to her tale.

'I am Nakrovak. My mate and I were captured many moons ago by Men in robes. They chanted over us and pierced our hides with crystals. The pain and the ensorcelled crystals drove my mate mad.
'The crystals had a different effect on me, however. My mind grew clearer. My body stronger. Rage and hunger were once all I knew. Now, there is sorrow, grief, and… something else I cannot explain. A softness….
'I managed to get away from my captors, but they found my den, weakened me with poison, and stole my cubs. As you have seen, I am not yet at my full strength.
'I dare not wait for the effects of the poison to wear off, for my cubs are in danger. Please, rescue them, and we will leave this place and go far away from two-legged peoples and their sorceries.'

'I owe you a great debt, ${RACE}. My intention is that our paths never cross again. If they do, however, and you require assistance, I will be there.
'My children and I will leave Clovengap once I have recovered.'

'Stay your hand, ${RACE}. I am in no shape to fight you.
'I can see that you are a formidable foe, and you seem not to be associated with the scum who stole my cubs. Listen to my tale, then decide whether I should be destroyed.'

'Welcome back, friend. Yes, yes. I saw the display. And one of the merchants came by to apologize to Nósni for the late shipment. Nósni had me moved here for the spectacular view, did he not? He has always been so thoughtful in his deeds, but foolish with the timeliness of his words.
'Hmmm. They were quite the thing, weren't they. I suppose I might find it in my heart to forgive him.'

'Hello, hello! Now the truth will out. You see, I know that Klátha's favourite thing is fireworks. I arranged to purchase special ones from Feredis of Minas Tirith herself!
'I have been waiting for the right moment to set them alight for Klátha. I had her moved here so she wouldn't miss the display, but... well, the delivery was very late and... oh. I can of course see how she would think I was trying to protect her. It was supposed to be a surprise, but... well, I suppose things have dragged on with no real news from me. I was so focused on my plan that I lost sight of how confusing my actions must have been.
'Well, will you help me light these fireworks? It may not be enough to redeem myself, but I have to try.'

'Oh, ${PLAYER}. That was spectacular! And probably the first time fireworks have ever graced these halls. If that did not win her love, at least may it grant me her forgiveness. Would... would you check on her for me? See whether I am allowed to speak with her again?'

'You again?'
You give Klátha the message from Nósni.
'Look towards the river? Hmm. I suppose I can do that. Not that it will matter, of course. But I suppose I can.'
Klátha's heart has turned against Nósni, but he's not ready to give up.

Instance: The Eldest House

'What... has happened? Who are you... and how did you come to this place?'
You introduce yourself to the old dwarf and explain that the Angmarim of the Iron Crown discovered the old delving after gaining entry to Gloomingtarn.
'It... should not be so, and yet... it is. I am... Thrástan.'
You ask Thrástan if he can stand. The old dwarf nods weakly.

'Of all the things I thought we might find in Mîn Lorg, another dwarf was not among them!
'It won't be long before the Iron Crown discovers what has happened. And despite his age, Thrástan looks a hale enough dwarf...
'We should leave this place while we still can, ${PLAYER}.'

'What... what is this place, my friend?
Hersegg glances around the entryway of what appears to be an ancient dwelling in the caverns of Gloomingtarn.
'It looks nearly untouched, ${PLAYER}, but how can that be so? Neither Orc nor dwarf have walked these halls in thousands of years, and yet, it is as neatly kept as any dwelling in the Lonely Mountain.
'Perhaps the notes of the Iron Crown were not so far from the truth after all. Could it truly be that Durin the Deathless once dwelt within this... house?
'We cannot allow the Angmarim to lay claim to it!'

'Another dwarf? What is he doing here?'
Hersegg looks at the Angmarim standing over an old dwarf.
'Let's listen for a moment and see if we can't learn more, ${PLAYER}. But if they even hint that they're going to harm him, I'm not going to let that happen!'
'We mustn't stay here, ${PLAYER}. Let us return to Watchers' Roost!'

'Lord Stormhammer need not concern himself with my safety, ${PLAYER}.
'As soon as I passed beyond the warding-runes at Zâram-mekhem, I understood what peril might await me in Gloomingtarn. And to be quite honest, I would sooner die than allow the Iron Crown to defile the Stone of Wakening.
'I will wield my axe as best I can, my friend. Let us hope it is enough!'

'Something stirs within me, ${PLAYER}, but I know not what it is...
'All I know is that the Shaper's hearth beckons to me! It is as if I were a stray ember returning to the forge...
'Will you accompany me up the old stairs, friend?

'I understand, ${PLAYER}. I see all that the Shaper wished of me!
'That I laboured as a servant of the great forge long before Durin laid dreaming beneath Mount Gundabad. And when my task was finished, so too did I rest for many years of the world.
'The time of my awakening has come—and my long slumber is at its end!'

'These stones... are familiar to me, ${PLAYER}.
'My memories seem clearer the nearer we draw to the Shaper's hearth. I came here once... I came with Durin...'
Thrástan trails off and begins mumbling to himself for a moment. After a moment, he grips his smithing hammer tightly.
'I must return....'

'Everyone is prepared then? Good.
'There is little time to waste!'

'I do not believe the Angmarim are the sort to make empty threats. But we have claimed the White Stone Forge... at least for the moment!
'If we have truly been led into a trap, it will not be long before it is sprung. In the meantime, escort Thrástan to the White Stone Forge. Even if our doom is soon to follow, I would do right by him and honour an old dwarf's last request.
'I and the others will prepare to make our stand—as hopeless as it may be!'

'By Durin's beard! What have we witnessed this day?!
'${PLAYER}, this is beyond all belief!'
'By Durin's beard! What have we witnessed this day?!'

'Hail, ${PLAYER}. I am the Forge-servant, Tamindur, wrought anew by the will of the Shaper... the First Crafter.... He Who Made The Dwarves!
'Invaders run rampant upon the Stone of Wakening, but no longer. By some lesser magic, they have come here unhindered, but they cannot oppose me nor my lord in the Uttermost West.
'Though you be not of the Eldest House, you shall be spared my wrath.'

'And that was the smallest scratch, mind you! If it had been closer, I surely would have lost my arm. Aye, it's a sneaky one. Especially for one of its size!
'Old Skárhogg, as I call it, has grown a bit too long in the claw, I think. If it is allowed to stalk the banks of Durthuzâram, there is no doubt in my mind that it will endanger the dwarves of the Gabil'akkâ.
'If you go to Skelstrand, seek out some sign of its presence. I only hope that you find it before it finds you!'

All the old tales spoke of a natural harmony in these caverns, but after what those Men of Angmar have done to the Mountain-home, I fear only discord will remain in their wake... at least for a time!

'Something has gotten to these worms, ${PLAYER}....
'I'm no lore-master, but I suspect the warding-runes did more than just keep the enemies of the dwarves out of Gloomingtarn. Ever since the Iron Crown made their way into these caverns, its creatures have been unwell, and I am afraid the glow-worms of Ormgren are no exception. Whatever balance was set in place long ago among these creatures has been broken with the warding-runes, and there is no craft or magic we possess that could repair them before the hour is too late!
'While I am thankful that many of the worms are still docile, a few have grown aggressive. They've begun to harass the miners and gnaw away at the ancient columns of Gloomingtarn. One among them, Thrastring, has even taken to devouring his own kind—and I worry he might develop a taste for dwarf too if we're not careful!
'If Gloomingtarn is to survive even after the Iron Crown are routed, we must put an end to Thrastring and his ilk.'

'It seems I had even more reason to send word to you than I first thought, ${PLAYER}.
'Do you see these runes, my friend? They read: \qALL MUST DEPART EXCEPT THE ELDEST HOUSE. DEATH AWAITS THE UNWELCOME.\q Not the most inviting, and for good reason! See what happens when some wicked Men render them powerless?
'Hersegg tells me that the Orcs' encampment lies directly in our path... or at least right beside it! As I am certain one as well-informed as you will have heard, Hersegg's grandfather, Lord Hermáth Stormhammer, has led an expedition into Gloomingtarn. Although it was said to have faced Orkish resistance upon passing through Zâram-mekhem, the Gabil'akkâ was able to secure a foothold deeper within the hallowed caverns—at an old overlook known as Watchers' Roost.
'That is where I wish to go, my friend. And now that you have come, perhaps Hersegg will finally allow me to begin my studies!'

'I must thank you for coming as soon as you did, ${PLAYER}. I have found myself in a bit of a bind.
'When my grandfather sent me to escort a new arrival to Watchers' Roost, I expected to find a capable warrior—not a lore-master of the Lonely Mountain. I mean him no insult, but a journey through the Ironfold is a much different task than the reclamation of the Mountain-home. I have no doubt that Spall means well, but as Prince Durin himself knows, the situation in Gloomingtarn is far more dire than we had hoped.
'The warding-runes were sapped of their ancient power by some fell artifact of Angmar, and without their protection, the Orcs and some wicked Men of the Iron Crown have invaded Gloomingtarn. Although we overcame the Orcs in our first encounter with them on our way to Watchers' Roost, they have bolstered their numbers from the Deepscrave and made camp at Drúkala.
'I am capable enough of escorting Spall on my own, but without some sort of distraction, I fear we will be waylaid by the Orcs before we reach our destination. As you might expect, Spall and I each have our own ideas of what might prove most effective in repelling the Orcs from Gloomingtarn. If you would combat the Orcs at Drúkala, I shall escort Spall and see that he can begin his studies in earnest at Watchers' Roost.
'And when you have finished with the Orcs, you should follow the thoroughfare and join us at the Roost. It is quite the sight to see, my friend!'

'I know this will come as some surprise, but my granddaughter has not shied from voicing her misgivings about your companion. However, I believe I see something of myself in him. Spall is a curious dwarf and he is well-learned in the history of the dwarves. Indeed, Spall might prove invaluable to this expedition. I was hesitant to allow him to begin his survey unaccompanied, but with you here, I see no reason to keep him from his studies!
'Besides, I need your help with another matter, my friend. After we established camp here at Watchers' Roost, I sent two companies to investigate some of the old passages of Gloomingtarn. One of my warriors, Vithin, led his company to Glittengrof, and another, Lokur, led his to Ormgren. My scouts spied a few glass-spiders near the entrance to Glittengrof, but I know little of Ormgren. Unfortunately, neither company has returned or even sent word—be it good or ill. Needless to say, I have become concerned. Either they have made some great discovery, or some terrible fate may have befallen them. If you find them in the course of Spall's survey, aid them as best you can. I would not leave any of my warriors behind!
'Go, ${PLAYER}, and tell Spall that he may begin his survey in Glittengrof and Ormgren—so long as you accompany him!'

'Lord Stormhammer has given me permission to begin my survey of Gloomingtarn? And you will accompany me? How wonderful!
'I had hoped to begin my survey at Abkân'aban, the great Stone of Wakening, but upon further thought, I suppose that is better left for last. Yes, Glittengrof and Ormgren shall be fine places to begin my studies!'
Spall begins to collect his things into his pockets and picks up a nearby axe.
'If it is all right with you, ${PLAYER}, I would like to set off at once!'

'By Durin's beard, you startled me! Did Lord Stormhammer send you?'
Vithin catches his breath and begins to whisper.
'Aye, I'm Vithin, but I'm afraid I cannot leave—not yet. Glittengrof and its crystals are indeed beautiful, but that doesn't mean much if it's overrun by spiders! Even worse, I've lost most of my company in these blasted webs!
'I can't just leave them! Will you aid me?'

'Have you heard much of Ormgren, ${PLAYER}?
'From what lore I've been able to gather, it seems that these were among the very first lodes delved in Mount Gundabad—and if legend speaks true, they were first mined by Durin the Deathless himself! I am eager to see how they have fared since the Elder Days, and I hope you are as well, my friend.
'Lord Stormhammer tells me that there is a small boat moored near Skelstrand that we might use to cross Durthuzâram to its eastern banks. I'm not certain how I feel about taking a boat out on the sacred tarn, but even I must admit that swimming seems a poor choice.
'Shall we then?'

'By Durin's beard, what has happened to this place?! The glow-worms have been devouring Ormgren from within!'
For a moment, Spall's face drains of colour and it looks as if he is about to faint. After a moment, he steadies himself.
'Perhaps... this was the will of the First Crafter. Yes... yes, it must be. And besides, ${PLAYER}, there is still much to be learned from these glow-worms. It is only a matter of knowing where to look!
'Are you familiar with how glow-worms digest what they eat, my friend? They possess complicated gizzards which become more effective when traces of stones and precious minerals are lodged within them. If we were to collect gizzards from these glow-worms, we might learn what ores and minerals they have recently devoured. And by we, I mean you, of course. I am a proud lore-master, not some butcher of beasts and insects!
'You don't mind helping me, do you? Oh, and only the adult glow-worms will have what I need, so you can leave the wormlets be!'

You tell Hermáth Stormhammer what little knowledge you gleaned from Thrástan's words. You mention that the dwarf appears to be suffering from a strange ailment, but you suspect that he wishes to travel to Abkân'aban, the Stone of Wakening.

You ask Thrástan if he was among the Haban’akkâ of Thráin during the Sixth War of the Dwarves and Orcs. He shakes his head solemnly, but his face betrays a pained expression.

'To my knowledge, there is not a single dwarf among the Gabil'akkâ named Thrástan!
'You see, ${PLAYER}... unless Thrástan was with us before the Iron Crown captured him, it is nearly impossible that he should have found his way this deep into Mount Gundabad. Even when the Haban’akkâ breached the Mountain-home during the Sixth War of the Dwarves and Orcs, we ventured no further than Máttugard. Even King Thráin deemed the Deepscrave too perilous to cross, and after all, Azog had yet to be slain!
'Perhaps he entered in the years that followed, but to elude the Orcs as far as Zâram-mekhem on his own is beyond the skill—or luck—of any dwarf I have ever known! Or that he could have dwelt here since the time of Durin the Deathless? Impossible! Only Durin himself was so long-lived among the Dwarves!
'I cannot make any sense of it, my friend. If he is truly of Durin's Folk, Thrástan must answer for himself!
'Question Thrástan, ${PLAYER}, speak to him, and learn what you can!'

A Hallowed Return

'Is everyone prepared to depart? Very good, ${PLAYER}.
'Let us return to Watchers' Roost and, at last, we can set about undoing the damage the Iron Crown has done to Gloomingtarn!'
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTE: You will swiftly travel to Watchers' Roost after advancing this quest.</rgb>

'Ah, ${PLAYER}, it seems our journey through Mount Gundabad shall have more than its fair share of surprises!
'My expedition and I will see to repairing the damage left by the Iron Crown, and we shall set the echo-horns across this great cavern into alignment once more. The warding-runes may never again repel our foes, but when the Mountain-home is ours again and evermore, I hope we find we have no need for them!
'I am certain Prince Durin and the others shall have need of your aid in the Clovengap and beyond, but I thank you for all you have done here, my friend. Without your aid, the secrets of our ancestors may well have been forgotten!
'Baruk Khazâd! For Gundabad!'

'You need not fear my wrath, ${PLAYER}. Approach, and let us speak!
'Long ago, when the Shaper's work was finished, I was bidden to rest beneath Mount Gundabad. In time, I awoke as Thrástan; different in form, but alike in mind and spirit to walk among Durin's Folk. In my long years of solitude, the two diverged, but I am now restored.
'At long last, my vigil nears its end and a new Age is soon to dawn. But fear not, I shall ward the Stone of Awakening from all evil that would seek to master it until I am called back to the Uttermost West.
'Yet many trials lay ahead for you, little one.'

'Let us not trouble our new benefactor, ${PLAYER}. Our gratitude is enough, I think, and there are greater matters in this world for one of such power to lend his aid.

'When Lord Stormhammer wishes to depart, I shall be prepared.'

'What an adventure, ${PLAYER}!
'From the Lonely Mountain to Elderslade and now to the very heart of Mount Gundabad... I am grateful our paths crossed when they did. Perhaps I was a bit too eager to confront the Iron Crown, but it all worked out in the end, didn't it?'
Hersegg smirks and looks to Tamindur.
'A victory hard won... and secured with as near a miracle as I've ever seen! The First Crafter himself must watch over us here in Mount Gundabad!
'I will be ready to depart in just a moment, my friend. Why don't you go and see if Spall is ready to set out?'

'Ah! There you are, ${PLAYER}!
'I was beginning to wonder if Lord Stormhammer forgot to mention where I'd gone, but no matter. Look out across the lake, my friend. Isn't Abkân'aban beautiful?'
Spall gestures to the massive island which rises out of the waters of Durthuzâram. His eyes are aglow with excitement and awe.
'It is the Stone of Wakening! It is said that it was upon those stones where Durin the Deathless first awoke—first of the Seven Fathers. What a sight to behold! Few Longbeards have been so fortunate to make such a pilgrimage, but would you accompany me?'
You tell Spall that Lord Stormhammer has asked you to aid Hersegg and the other warriors.

Although we haven't been able to recover any of them, I have seen the Angmarim of the Iron Crown carrying scroll-cases.
'If they didn't stop after stealing the Black Stone Anvil, who knows what else they might seek to pilfer? Scout the encampment to the north and see if you can't find one of those scroll-cases, ${PLAYER}. We've got to know what they're up to and what they've found!'

'Even the more docile worms have become a nuisance!
'It seems the glow-worms are uneasy with our presence here, which I can understand after so many years spent in solitude, but these are the lodes of Durin the Deathless! It is our right to explore them and reclaim them along with the rest of the Mountain-home. According to one of my miners, several others have been ensnared by the glow-worms and have become stuck in strands of glowing slime!
'Would you help free them, ${PLAYER}? I would've tried to help them sooner, but if I got stuck too, I think we'd all be in a bad way.
'If I don't hear back from you soon, I'll warn the others at Watchers' Roost!'

Echoes of the Ancestors

Echo-horns can be found in and around Drúkala in Gloomingtarn.
Since learning that the Orcs fear the strange echoes in Gloomingtarn, Spall has asked you to realign the echo-horns at Drúkala in an effort to drive the Orcs back into Deepscrave.
Realign echo-horns to unsettle the Orcs at Drúkala (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'So Hersegg will escort me to Watchers' Roost? That is excellent news!
'As for these Orcs, I have noticed that they have found some means to alter the alignment of the ancient echo-horns—the Ugrur-melakh, as they were so named in the tongue of my ancestors. It is said that they once channelled the very acoustics of these caverns into a deep, reverberating resonance. According to the lore I have studied, it was also rumoured they were possessed of some enchantment from the Elder Days. Alas, I have seen no such evidence with my own eyes!
'However, Hersegg tells me the Orcs have made no attempt to attack Watchers' Roost. Perhaps it is merely coincidence and they fear the warriors of the Gabil'akkâ stationed there, but I do not think that is all that is happening. Many of the echo-horns still lie undisturbed at the old overlook, and I think many of the Orcs fear to draw any nearer to them.
'I spotted several echo-horns around the Orcs' encampment and along the thoroughfare through Gloomingtarn. With one of the Ugrur-melakh destroyed, we will have to realign the remaining echo-horns to capture the resonance, but I am confident it will drive off the Orcs—at least for a time!
'I am certain you can figure it out, ${PLAYER}. I hope to see you at Watchers' Roost!'

As several Orcs flee back into the Deepscrave, it appears that Spall's speculation that realigning the echo-horns around Drúkala has indeed unsettled the Orcs and hindered their efforts to gain a foothold in Gloomingtarn. Although some of the Orcs appear to be fighting stubbornly against their own discomfort, the others' flight from Gloomingtarn has undone any advantage Gorgar's forces may have held against the Gabil'akkâ.

'After slaying no fewer than three—nay four—Zhélruka in the course of attempts to break him, I desire the horns of Crótharc as wergild for my fallen brethren. Crótharc was last seen roaming the eastern hillsides of Câr Bronach. Approach him with great care, lest you meet your doom! For the Zhélruka!
-Rádek'

'A bittersweet end, but the only one I could abide. Do not worry, friend, Crótharc did not actually slay any of my kin. But I was bested by a ram! I couldn't simply write out the truth of my failure for all to see—I had to employ my greatest skill: exaggeration! You understand, do you not?
'I only wish Crótharc had tolerated my saddle, but I could not be made to look a fool before my kin and kindred! A mighty, stubborn, but unwise ram he was—'twould have been better for the both of us if we had seen eye to eye!
'Take this for your troubles, friend. You have spared me a great deal of embarrassment and given me a trophy to carry home from this war!'

The Exiled Giant

'Go away!
'What?! You are still here?!
'You can ask me all the questions you you want. It does not mean that I will answer them!
'How could I even trust you? I can not even trust my own kind to make the right decisions. I can only trust these goats. If the goats trust you, then maybe I will answer a question for you.'

'${PLAYER}, have you returned! I was starting to wonder where you had gotten to!
'So the Grímklettar ally with the Dourhands, but not the Angmarim? I find this confusing! We know the Angmarim and the Dourhands work together! There is more at hand in Câr Bronach then I thought! Someone is driving a wedge in this alliance.'

'You have done as I asked, and the goats seem to find you acceptable. I will answer your question.
'Why am I here you ask? Crágan Bris was once a great settlement of my people. It is all I have left. You do not know much about Câr Bronach, I see. Then I will explain. This is where my ancestors came from. We once had a great city where the Drearspire now stands. Our home was taken from us by Men and we were chased away. Hraubrek wanted to reclaim our land. That is why we have returned. I followed Hraubrek because I believed in his wisdom. Now I am lost, for Hraubrek allies with our enemy. All our alliances have ended in death. How will this one be any different?!
'I have answered your question, now leave me be.'

The Dourhand Proposition
'Yes, the Dourhand is Rethvárd, our escaped prisoner. He has told me only what I needed to know. He would rather speak to you, ${PLAYER}.'

'I am glad that you came. Has Rethvárd filled you in? Good!
'I have been infiltrating Ásachal and her followers not for loyalty. Bah! They are nothing but an enemy to the Dourhand! I put my enemy close to see them fall! As we can both see, we have a common foe. I have been trying to get everyone to in Câr Bronach to work together. The hillmen are too timid, and as much as I have tried to sway the stone-giants, they seem to have other plans.
'I know that now is a good time to strike, while the Angmarim do not expect such an alliance to form. I also have heard, with good authority might I add, that atop the spire lies a stone of immense power! We can not let that artifact stay in the hands of the Iron Crown. Now, what do you say?
'Good. I am glad that you are with us! There will still be much work to accomplish after the Drearspire is taken. For that we will need the hillmen on our side. Let us rescue those who have been captured in an effort to show we mean to work together.'
'There you are, ${PLAYER}. So far, the Dourhands have kept their promise! We were able to take Agal Dûn and now sit at the entrance of the Drearspire. For Gundabad!'

'Your friend, Uzvát, has informed me that a representative of the Dourhands has a proposition for us. They wish to work together to topple High Priestess Ásachal and her reign over Tûr Fúar. I do not trust those who openly do the bidding of the Iron Crown. For that, we will not be involved.
'If you wish to listen to this Dourhand and work with them, that is for you and the dwarves to decide. I will think no less of you for what you decide, friend. Understand this: we will have no part in it.'

'Greetings. I bring direct word from Lord Brathar. He wishes to speak to you, ${PLAYER}. I will tell you where to find him. I assure you this is not a trap. I surrender myself again in good faith!
'Brathar has a plan. He has been building trust with the Angmarim, in order to crush them. All that is left in the plan is that he requires assistance from you and the Zhélruka!
'Please, just speak with him and Uzvát and I will make sure that the rest of your Gabil'akkâ remain at the ready.'

The Rhudaur-stone

'I believe Brathar is lying. He wants nothing more than power. Even I believed that he was doing all this for the good of everyone under the subjugation of the Iron Crown. Now I saw the look in his eyes when we won but the Rhudaur-stone was missing. It was not the look of victory, it was the look of defeat.
'Do with me what you will, but know that I will follow Brathar Crach-helm no longer.'
'Brathar Crack-helm, you had that coming. You have caused more than enough trouble in these mountains. No more, Dourhand.'

'Well done everyone! This is a fine day for the Zhélruka. I knew this plan would work. That is why I came up with it after all! Ha, that will teach Durin to doubt the Zhélruka. I jest, ${PLAYER}. Durin's wisdom knows no bounds, even if he underestimates the resolve of the Zhélruka.'

'I must say, my plan was mostly a success, even if Prince Ingór will certainly take most of the credit! I can not blame him though. We would not be standing where we are if not for Prince Ingór's invaluable leadership!'

'That crafty Claghórd. He must have known the Rhudaur-stone was moved! That is why he did not care if we took the Drearspire. A lingering question then remains. Where was the stone taken? Where did Claghórd retreat to?'

'So it is true! ${PLAYER} returns to the north.
'I am sorry that the Trév Duvárdain have arrived late. I would have very much liked to speak to you at Eiricháv. An urgent matter had called me away. Soltakh has told me what you have accomplished. It seems we were right to not trust the Dourhands after all, though we should have taken the tower by your side.
'I was secretly meeting with Hraubrek, the Chieftain of the Grímklettar, in the north. The Trév Duvárdain and the Grímklettar have much in common. We have a common enemy, share these lands, and have been dealt many hardships for both our kind. I thank you for your assistance on this day. The Trév Duvárdain, and all free hillmen owe you much.'

'We do not need to see eye to eye, ${RACE}. In fact, I do not think we ever will.
'Yes, talking to the Angmarim and accepting gifts from the Dourhands were all a ruse, for my real intentions were to form a secretive pact with the Trév Duvárdain.
'While there has been many lives lost, including my own kin, I will not hold you accountable. The ends have justified the lives lost. As Gundabad is a sacred site to the dwarves, beneath this spire is the sacred city of my kind. It has been lost for so long. Now, the pilgrimage is complete for those of the Grímklettar who remain.
'If you and the dwarves let us be, then we will let you live under the mountain in peace. We will keep Câr Bronach free of the Iron Crown. You have my word. Now, please leave. You are not needed here any longer.'
The Rhudaur-stone is gone!

'If you will accompany me to the Stagshorn's cottage and help me say good-bye, I would value your assistance most highly, for I have been putting it off. They live in a pleasant cottage to the south-east, beyond the old village of Glynafon.'

'Here it is: Fernbrake Cot, home to my friends Maddoc and Glenys, and their son Bran. The Stagshorns showed me much kindness while I ventured in this land, and I will miss them when I leave.
'I appreciate you being here, ${PLAYER}. Saying good-bye is always difficult, and I would like my friends to know they will have adventurers such as you looking after them once I have departed.'
'Let us work to make safe the wilds for those good folk who dwell in this land! Perhaps afterward you will help me with the task at which I have been delaying.'

Dangerous foes stalk the rocky woodlands of the Angle, and Ravaedron desires for you to help him combat them.
Ravaedron is along the road that runs south into the Angle from the Trollshaws.

'Mae govannen, stranger. You are come to the Angle of Mitheithel, but in a southerly direction rather than a northerly. That is curious indeed! I have found that travellers in this land do so mainly on their way to somewhere else; so it is with me. I am not long to remain here in the Angle.'
The Elf smiles briefly.
'But I have forgotten my manners! Let me cure this lack at once: I am called Ravaedron, and I came to the Angle some time ago on an errand given me by the sons of Elrond. Ah, you are known to them? Then let us be friends as well, for we share similar purpose: to make the wilds safe for those good folk who dwell there! It will be no great burden for you to aid me in this, will it? For there is something I must do, but I have been putting it off for later. Let us first face what dangers present themselves to us here in Mitheithel, and then perhaps you will help me again.'

'Very good, my new friend. You are most adept at facing such threats as these! It is little wonder that Elladan and Elrohir trust you so. Did they send you on such a mission as they sent me? I was directed here in search of dark servants of the Enemy, riders in black that ran afoul of the defences of Imladris. Ah... perhaps I should speak no more of them. Elrohir was most clear that it was a matter of some secrecy.'
Ravaedron mimes locking his lips with a key and hanging it on an invisible chain around his neck.
'Let us say instead that I found no sign of our quarry, and leave it at that. Even so my search was not fruitless, for I did find something that is now quite dear to me. I befriended a family of woodcutters, the Stagshorns. They live not far from here, and now I cherish their friendship, the last friendship I will ever make in Middle-earth, for my steps will now take me to the Grey Havens, and I will sail into the West, and this chapter of mine will be ended.'
Ravaedron laughs suddenly.
'Perhaps the Stagshorns will not be the last friendship I make here, ${PLAYER}, for I had not counted upon meeting you! But if you will accompany me to their cottage and help me say good-bye, I would value your assistance most highly... for I have been putting it off. They live in a pleasant cottage to the south-east, beyond the old village of Glynafon.'
'This is it: Fernbrake Cot, home of my friends the Stagshorns.'

'I am sorry you had to see that, ${PLAYER}. It pains me to say this, but perhaps Ravaedron was not as close a friend as we thought. His people and ours must simply be too different.
'Did he befriend us... out of pity? Do all long-lived folk look upon the men and women of the Angle as mere mayflies, alive for so short a time they must be safe-guarded and shown sympathy? I thought our friendship with Ravaedron was different, but I suppose it was not.'

'You will find the Stagshorns most agreeable, my friend. They are a charming couple, and their son Bran is quite a lively lad.
'I will let them know we are here.'
'Come inside, come inside! There are few roads in this land, and you must be weary from your travels!'

'Have you known Ravaedron long? We met him only recently, but he is dear to us, and the tales he has told us of long ago times and distant places have captured our imaginations! Did he ever find the prey he sought, the dark-robed villains that drew him to the Angle?
'We are sworn to secrecy, and will speak of them to no one else. But I confess the nighttime shadows seemed deeper after he spoke of the horseless riders loose in the wild!
'Still, we fear them not. My husband and I come from tough stock; none could long live in this land without being made hardy, or beginning so!'

'I have steeled myself for a sad parting, but your presence here should help. I am ready if you are, my friend.'
'Then let there be an end to my delays! \qSooner done, sooner past,\q as they say. It is not an Elven expression, of that I am certain.'

'I... do not understand, ${PLAYER}. I expected my farewell to contain a measure of sorrow for all of us, of course, but I did not think to quarrel. I do not want to leave it like this! But what can I do?'
Ravaedron frowns at the closed door of Fernbrake Cot.
'I am dissatisfied, ${PLAYER}. How can my friends wish for me to depart in this fashion? Did I not make clear to them that they will be protected by such adventurers as you even when I am gone? I am certain I did. I meant no insult.'

'I did not expect to see friendly folk in Glynafon, and my heart was ready for their absence, but the sight of wargs among the one-time burrows of my friends is more than I can bear. How many evenings did I spend alongside Meredud and Aderyn on their nightly strolls? How many days did I spend in conversation with Wenna, who gave me such lessons in painting that my art was ever-changed? Too few, I see now.'
Ravaedron frowns, his pleasant memories scattered like leaves before a storm.
'If I am grateful for anything, let it be this: I did not quarrel with my friends among the Stôrs when they departed these lands. That, at least, is a kindness.
'Let us defeat some of the wargs here in the Angle. If a large pack of the creatures passed through Glynafon, as you say, they will be a danger to those who live nearby. Then we will continue on to Tornhad, the Dúnedain village that is our destination. I have a request to make of the Rangers there, and we can tell them about the warg pack.'
'We have arrived.'
'We have arrived, ${PLAYER}. The Dúnedain range far and wide throughout the wilderness, but Tornhad has served as their relatively permanent home for many years.'
'Let us make safe the lands hereabout and meet up at the old mounds of Glynafon. It stands to the west of here and was once a most pleasant village, though it has remained empty for much of the age.'
'You should see the home of Meredud and Aderyn, who delighted in staying up late, and the burrow where Wenna painted such lovely landscapes! Ah, she seemed to possess the skill of the Eldar.'

'Well, it is no matter: whether they know of it or not, their lives will not be endangered by my decision to leave Middle-earth. I hope it is not presumptuous of me to say we will make certain of that!'
Ravaedron stares for a moment longer at the closed door, and then shakes his head.
'Still, I had hoped for a friendlier parting. I have seen many farewells during my long years, and I did not envision this one going this way. But I will not dwell upon it. I have spent too long dwelling on such things! Let us make safe the lands hereabout and meet up at the old mounds of Glynafon. It stands to the west of here and was once a most pleasant village, though it has remained empty for much of the age.'
'Let us make safe the lands hereabout and meet up at the old mounds of Glynafon. It stands to the west of here and was once a most pleasant village, though it has remained empty for much of the age.'

'Sights such as this are all too common these days, ${PLAYER}, and they stand in opposition with the memories I have of these places. This was once a thriving community of hardy folk toughened by the tilling of the rocky soil. I remember the pleasing sound of their voices, raised in song more often than not, and carried on the wind for miles around. They called themselves Stôrs, and it is my understanding that when they departed the Angle, they passed through many lands before finally settling in a small corner of Arthedain. I hope to see their land on my journey to the ships.
'But they have not lived here for more than a thousand years, and the wind has not borne aloft their songs for even longer, for it was the threat of war that caused them to leave. There was unrest throughout Rhudaur, and evil arose in Angmar, and the Stôrs felt no cause to sing. But when I knew them they were pleasant and full of joy.'
Ravaedron regales you with tales of the friends he once knew in Glynafon, and encourages you to see the home of Meredud and Aderyn, who delighted in staying up late, and the burrow where Wenna painted such lovely landscapes that she seemed to possess the skill of the Eldar.

'I have just begun to tell the Dúnedain the reasons for our visit here, ${PLAYER}, but they insist they have too many tasks to which they must attend, and have little time to listen! I have never found them to be especially polite, but on this day it seems worse than usual.
'What say you, Idhrenfair? I believed us to be friends, but it seems you cannot spare a moment for Ravaedron, though he departs on the morrow and you will not see him again!'

'I have known Ravaedron my whole life, and that means I am familiar with his old tricks: he has always had a flair for the dramatic quite unlike others of his people I have met.

'While I have your ear, ${PLAYER}, there is something I would like to discuss. Let us meet near Eitheldir, to the north, and we can speak while I conduct my last patrol for today.'

'Thank you for coming, ${PLAYER}. The Dúnedain have long protected folk who dwell on the edge of the wilderness, but we could not do so if our hearts were troubled. Our own families reside within the Angle of Mitheithel, and if we are certain they live in safety, the obligation we have sworn is more readily-performed.
'So it is that the Dúnedain conduct patrols such as these on the outskirts of Mitheithel, and on the approaches to Tornhad. In times of danger, the village can be evacuated and we move our families to a number of caves in the outlying hills. It has happened more and more often in recent years: an unwelcome change every time, but necessary. It is a cause of sadness for the old-timers, and a pleasing lark for the children, but for me it justifies our caution.
'What say you? Will you patrol these ruins with me?'
'Then let us begin, and remain alert for anything that might threaten the safety of Tornhad and its people.'

'I thank you again for hearing me out, ${PLAYER}. I cannot begin to understand the burden that Ravaedron must feel when he walks in this land. I want him to depart these shores and find the peace his heart deserves. I hope you feel the same, and will help him accomplish it.
'Let us return now to Tornhad.'

'Welcome back, ${PLAYER}. While you and Prestadír were gone, I received assurances from the others of his folk that they will keep out a watchful eye for the Stagshorns when I am gone. So that is all right.
'What did you and he speak about while you were away?'
'Let us return now to Tornhad.'

'But for you, ${PLAYER}, while I have your ear there is something I would like to discuss. Let us meet near Eitheldir, to the north, and we can speak while I conduct my last patrol for today.'

'Oranoril's company evaded the armies of the Dark Lord until they reached Eitheldir, but when they arrived below the stronghold they found the crossing of the Hoarwell already held against them. A brief siege followed, but the Orcs far outnumbered the few Elves that remained; the gates were broken and the keep razed. One by one the companions of Oranoril perished, until only she and three others remained.
'Together they performed one last act of defiance, fighting their way through the throng to Celebrimbor's body and prizing it from the clutches of the Orcs. With her last dying strength Oranoril, now the last living Elf in Eitheldir, took up the smith's corpse and leapt from the precipice into the foaming waters of the Hoarwell. And so even in his victory Sauron was robbed of his trophies, and his anger was without match.
'Furious that many of the Noldor had eluded him, and unable to find where they had fled, Sauron invaded Eriador from the Angle, intending to crush the realm of Lindon. Instead he found the Men of Númenor waiting for him, for they had answered the call of Gil-galad, and the combined forces of Elves and Men broke Sauron's strength. From whence came the final blow? Why, it came from Elrond and the folk of Imladris, for when their strength was recovered they returned with a fire in their hearts and Sauron could not stand against them. Defeated, it was his turn to flee; to Mordor he escaped.'

'After the war, the Elves searched both the Hoarwell and the Greyflood for the remains of Oranoril or Celebrimbor, but they found no sign of either. This precipice became a place of pilgrimage for many of the Noldor, particularly for those whose flight to Rivendell she had bought with her life.
'Ravaedron was one of these, ${PLAYER}, and I know it is not easy for him to walk today in the Angle, with such memories as these still fresh in his mind. Eregion remained desolate after the War of the Elves and Sauron, its shattered halls crumbling with the passage of the years, becoming overgrown with grass and vine, but the stones remember what transpired, and so do those who were there.
'This is why I do not gainsay Ravaedron his choice to leave Middle-earth. If that is the peace he desires, I want him to have it.'

'I am not as well-versed in the history of this land as some of my folk, but I know enough to share some of it with you, ${PLAYER}. Seven centuries into the Second Age, the great Elf-smith Celebrimbor journeyed from Lindon to dwell in the holly-forests at the foot of the Misty Mountains. That realm came to be known as Eregion, and it was the birthplace of many great works and treasures of craft.
'The heart of Celebrimbor's realm lay to the south of the Loudwater, but the Elves drove out the trolls and hostile Amonedain in between, constructing outposts in the wooded hills on the border-marches. The chief of these was this stronghold, Eitheldir, built to watch the crossings of the Hoarwell and to keep open the road to Lindon.
'The governance of the keep was given to Oranoril, a Noldor companion of Celebrimbor. She had served as a captain in the wars against Morgoth, and was renowned for both her loyalty and her ferocity.'

'I would not have begrudged them the shelter if they came by it honestly, and turned not to robbery. But alas it was not so.'
Prestadír gazes up at the sky, peering into the unknowable heights.
'It looks like rain,' he says, and then returns his gaze to earth.
'You have heard of the War of the Elves and Sauron, ${PLAYER}, in which the Dark Lord sought mastery over the works of Eregion? Celebrimbor perceived the designs of Sauron, but there was little time to prepare for the destruction that awaited the Elves.'

'Oranoril took charge of the remaining soldiers following the death of Celebrimbor; only her great skill of command kept the defeat from becoming an inescapable bloodbath, and she ordered her people to retreat. At the Hollin Ridge she watched with horror as Sauron's forces marched behind the ghastly banner they had made of the once-proud Elf-smith.
'Knowing a similar fate awaited her if she was caught, Oranoril devised a scheme to save what of her people she could. She chose a small force from her own household and tricked Sauron's army into pursuing them. On a grim chase she led them across the Bruinen into the Angle, while the bulk of her kindred escaped by secret paths into the mountains and then to Elrond's young refuge. Ravaedron was one of these, and he never forgot his last sight of Oranoril's company disappearing over the ridge, pursued by Sauron's foot-soldiers.'

'I... I don't understand, ${PLAYER}. Why have the Stagshorns discarded my painting? Did they not like the gift I made for them? This is... this is very hurtful! Was I upset by our quarrel? This stings tenfold that, and makes me question our friendship entire! Do they not understand that I must leave this land, but despite my certainty of that choice, the leaving is still difficult?
'But... how could they know that? They have not had the experiences of the Eldar, or faced such things as I have. Their sorrows may be shorter-lived than my own, but... they are no less deeply-felt.
'I think I have realized something, ${PLAYER}. My gift was well-intentioned, but it did nothing to address the permanence of my choice, or to soothe the wound it could cause. I sought an easy remedy, but no such remedy exists, or ever has.'

'Greetings to you, ${PLAYER}. Ravaedron sent you to help me? He has a great deal on his mind, and he need not ask for any forgiveness on my part! But I would tell him this, if he took the time to hear my words: \qIt is not on your head to solve every problem in Middle-earth! Leave the land as best you can, and treat those who remain with as much kindness as you have to give. If you do that, you will sail into the West with an untroubled heart, deserving of the peace you have earned!\q
'That is what I believe, anyway. Perhaps the Dúnedain are in no position to say such things, for our duty seems never-ending, as if it will never reach its conclusion! But I think these words will help Ravaedron, though I find them hard to follow for myself.
'But if you will help me gather the herbs I need, my work today will go twice as quickly! Keep an eye out for them after you have concluded your current business. I do not want you to run afoul of any beasts while your eyes are locked on the ground!'

Now mostly wilderness once more, it offers sanctuary for those who do not wish to be found. Nestled in the arms of two difficult to pass rivers, the Angle is home to Rangers, Elves, and refugees alike. But a recent infiltration of Orcs, brigands, and other servants of the Enemy has brought war back to the hills and riversides of the Angle once more.

'Ah, you return! I knew you were more than a match for those poor spirits. Come, let me see what you bring.'
You hand him an armband.
'Yes, it is as I thought. I think I know how we can help these warriors. The rivers that surround the Angle often ran red after the battles that were fought here. So much loss and violence has twisted some of the plants that grow in this area. On their banks, you will find twisted rotroot. Collect a bouquet of their flowers and bring it here.'

'In other lands, these flowers grow tall and proud. Here in the Angle, they grow twisted by the memories of violence and strife.
'I have prepared a pyre using an incantation for purifying and letting go. Here, take the armbands. Add them to the fire with the bouquet you gathered. May the hearts of the warriors find peace, and may the twisted flowers unfurl and bloom again.'

'Mae govannen! I am indeed Glatharn. I heard tell that you might be interested in offering assistance to our cause. I have a… slightly odd request. We are camped near the ruins of Tham Lumren. As with the rest of Haudh Erthaid, Tham Lumren has played host to countless battles. Many of which saw Elves and Men meet their demise. For some of those folk, a physical death was not enough to send their spirits onwards, and they lurk among the ruins, attacking blindly, and imagining that their last battle still rages.
'I have identified certain artifacts that I believe are tethering these troubled shades – twisted, golden armbands that they wore in life. Thalathril will not grant me leave to assist these confused soldiers, but you have the freedom to do so. Please, go and collect armbands from the shades.'
'Did you feel it, ${PLAYER}? Like a warm summer wind, and that sweet scent! I believe we have done it, friend. We are a small step closer to healing this land and granting peace to troubled souls.'

Idhrien is always welcomed back with smiles and laughter, and Mandan... well, Mandan's healing skills are welcomed, but the man himself can be rather abrasive. 'Today I have been tasked with a simple duty: patrolling the bounds of Thelgarth. Perhaps you will accompany me, and tell me of your adventures? It will help pass the time, and I fear nothing so much as I fear boredom and tedium! Has all the magic and excitement gone from the world?
'I will meet you near Thelgarth.'
'Let us keep on the watch for foes, though I expect few dangers so near to Tornhad. I desire real excitement, like that told in stories of old! But so far it has not presented itself to me.'

'Thank you for helping me with my patrol, ${PLAYER}. I know that a Dúnadan must put his duty above a concern for glory, and that I will always do... but still I hunger for excitement! Am I wrong to hope that such greater adventures may lie just over the horizon?
'The Angle is my home, and it is dear to me, but I hope to range further afield. I told you of the hillside caves my friends and I explored as children? I know every tunnel and passage of them, not just from those explorations but from nights spent hiding in the dark when we feared Tornhad was threatened by foes seeking the eradication of the Dúnedain. I know why we did not stand and fight... but sometimes I wish we had.
'I will uphold my oath, without question. But it is my small hope that doing so will bring me to distant lands I have never seen, to face dangers that no man has faced, and when my duty is done to hear it said that I did well. Is that too much to ask? I hope not, my new friend. Thank you once more, and may we see each other again... far from here!'

'Even with the combined might of the Gabil'akkâ behind him, Durin shall have need of you and your strongest allies if victory is to be won!'

'Many are the songs that will be sung of this day, my friend. At long last, Hrímil Frost-heart is dead and Mount Gundabad is ours. And I would be remiss to overlook the role you played in our victory, ${PLAYER}!
'With Hrímil's death, our conquest of the Mountain-home is all but certain. Gorgar is slain, and the line of Azog is ended. The Orcs and their wild cousins from the North have fallen into disarray, and it is my firm belief that those who linger within Gundabad will be routed in the days ahead.
'Even so, I grieve the loss of my uncle, Náin, and it is with great sorrow that I shall have to deliver word of his death to my father, King Thorin. My heart aches, too, that he was so soon to follow my grandfather, Dáin, in death.
'May his deeds and his memory never be forgotten! Long live Náin—slakeless, now and evermore!'

<rgb=#00FF00>It is recommended, but not required, that you complete The Legacy of Durin and the Trials of the Dwarves before playing 'The Hiddenhoard of Abnankâra'.</rgb>
'There are those who believe that Hrímil Frost-heart has abandoned Mount Gundabad. I say they are wrong! It is true she has fled, but only deeper into the Mountain-home—to Abnankâra!
'Does that name sound unfamiliar to your ear? It should, my friend. It is known to none who still live, save for me, and that is only because I share the memories of the Durins who came before me!
'Not long after the Greymaul Rebellion was ended and Motsóg came to dwell in solitude in the caverns deep beneath the Mountain-home, he confessed a secret to me—to the Durin I was then. Before that ruinous war between our peoples, he had set the Greymauls upon a great task: to delve a hidden treasury within the depths of Mount Gundabad. It was named Abnankâra, the Hiddenhoard, and it would have been the jewel of Motsóg's kingdom. Had the Greymauls succeeded in their plot to steal the wealth and mithril of Khazad-dûm, it is certain the spoils would have come to rest at Abnankâra.
'Whether it was by some sense of duty or mere curiosity, I—when I was Durin the First—heeded Motsóg's words and found the hidden way to the gates of Abnankâra. I strode within its halls only once, and when I had seen all that I meant to, I sealed it behind me—leaving the few, ill-gotten riches of the Greymauls to be forgotten. And so it has been for many Ages of the world!
'It lies still in the Clovengap, my friend, and in my heart, I am certain that that is where Hrímil Frost-heart has gone. I have sent my uncle, Náin, ahead with a small company to seek for the Hiddenhoard.
'Will you aid him, my friend? Will you see our long struggle for the conquest of Mount Gundabad to its end?'

<rgb=#00FF00>It is recommended, but not required, that you complete The Legacy of Durin and the Trials of the Dwarves before playing 'The Hiddenhoard of Abnankâra'.</rgb>

'Go on ahead, my friend, and see if we have broken through!'

'You say you heard a voice on the wind? It can be no other—we have found the lair of Hrímil Frost-heart!
'I shall send word to Durin at once, my friend. If ever I doubted his words, I have now all the proof I sought. Alas that the Black Mattock was lost in the Deepscrave! This will have to do....'
Náin hefts a war-mattock of the Iron Hills in his hand.
'In the meantime, ${PLAYER}, I would ask that you gather your strongest allies to Mount Gundabad. When you are prepared, we shall see what awaits us within Abnankâra!
'Even with the combined might of the Gabil'akkâ behind him, Durin shall have need of you—and of them—if victory is to be won!'
From deep within the darkness of the passage ahead, a voice seems to beckon you...

'I can hardly explain it, my friend. How could Durin know of such a passage? Could it be true?'
Náin absent-mindedly strokes at the air beneath his shorn beard before lowering his hand.
'You know of what I speak, ${PLAYER}. When Durin told me that he had proclaimed himself to be Durin the Seventh—Durin the Deathless reborn, I must admit I balked at his words. Durin confided in me, and he spoke of visions and of ancient memories that returned to him deep within Mount Gundabad. And so, you must imagine my disbelief when he told me that Hrímil had made a lair for herself in an old Greymaul treasury—the so-called Hiddenhoard of Abnankâra. Such a thing should not even exist!
'Yet, with each swing of those pick-axes, I find myself more convinced.'
Náin glances over his shoulder at the dwarves of his company picking away at the ice of Amgaruslun.
'It has been some time, my friend. Why don't you see if we have broken through?

You hand the mushrooms to Hal and he wrinkles his nose at the foul odour emanating from them.
'These are great! They look exactly how the healer described! ...I think.
'Now, she said you could ingest these raw and they would have potent healing properties! Let me just take a big bite to be sure....'
It does not take long before his face turns pallid and green.
'O-on second thought... did she want me to stay AWAY from these mushrooms? I was rather distracted, and perhaps did not pay close enough attention.... Oh dear....
'Do you think you could do me one more favour? The herbs she sent me to recover may be my only hope! Can you seek them out? And stay away from those mushrooms!'

'You there! You look more than capable of handling yourself in these woods. Could I perhaps propose a favour?
'My name is Hal Twayblade, and I have been tasked by a beautiful Elf-woman to collect herbs so she may prepare a number of useful medicinal remedies. However, I seem to be having some trouble recalling anything beyond her delicate features, her lovely tresses...'
Hal drifts away into his reverie. At last he seems to remember your presence.
'There was something else: she did say that a strange breed of mushroom grew in these parts, but I have seen neither stem nor cap of it! I want to get back to her as soon as possible, and I have yet to find any of these mushrooms she mentioned. The two of us will be able to cover more ground. Please say you will help me!'
To Heal a Healer

Maervellon remains outside the fortress of Thelgarth, in the Angle.
The half-orcs of Thelgarth are sure to have Maervellon's lucky talisman. Sure they are.

'${PLAYER}, just the adventurer for whom I was looking! How have been your travels in these wild lands, with which I am well-accustomed? Mine have been rather fruitless I'm afraid... until now, that is! I have journeyed hither and yon, and now my searching has revealed just who stole my precious talisman! The half-orcs who reside now in the fortress of Thelgarth, atop this very hill!
'What's that? I did not mention half-orcs before now? I am certain I did. You must have misunderstood me when I spoke of half of the foe-men arrayed before me being Orcs. An honest mistake. I forgive you.
'You have helped me so much to this point, I am sure you want to finish this, my friend! Climb up to Thelgarth and defeat as many half-orcs as it takes to find my lucky talisman!
'You'll help me see this through to the end, won't you?'

'That was quite a feat! So tell me, friend, which villain was it who pocketed my lucky talisman?'
You shake your head and hold up empty hands.
'Wh-what? But... that's impossible. Are you sure you bested the right ones?
'B-but that can't be, that necklace was given to me by some very important people... I can't have lost it....
'Listen, my friend, I suppose it is time you knew the truth. I am no Ranger. I merely wish I was as heroic and courageous as they are. I am but a humble traveller on whom the Rangers took pity. I looked up to them so much! I wanted to do everything just like they can! They looked after me for a few weeks, and during that time they gave to me that talisman as a way to keep that dream alive. I thought one of the brigands that attacked me might have taken it but in reality... I might have dropped it. I spun a yarn to save my pride. I am sorry, friend.'
So defeated, Maervellon slumps to the ground. As he does so, something startles him and he rises once more to his feet. Reaching into his back pocket, he pulls out an oddly shaped necklace. His face turns crimson.
'Oh! Er... ${PLAYER}, th-this is the talisman for which I was searching! It was... in my pocket the whole time? Oh, I am such a fool... to think I imagined a tale so dangerous, I myself believed it to be true.... Don't think too badly of me, ${PLAYER}. I was very distraught!
'But nonetheless, you helped me on this craban hunt the whole way. And though it proved rather unnecessary, it was not a thankless task. I will do my best to live up to the Rangers I so admire, and I think that may begin with the purchase of trousers with frontward facing pockets!
'Thank you for all your help, ${PLAYER}, and uh, sorry for all the trouble!'
A Talisman Found

'Rúdhan's injury is worse than we thought. We might need to stay here longer than I expected.
'But there is always food to be found in the wild, if you know where to look. There should be some berry bushes somewhere nearby, perhaps among the rocks to the north-west. Now, such a bounty will attract wild beasts, but that should be no real danger for such as you, should it? We heard the growling of what sounded like a large bear shortly before we made it to this river... but perhaps it has already moved on.
'We would both greatly appreciate any food you can bring back to us: berries, meat, or vegetables. When my husband's strength has returned we will move on.'

'Well if it isn't ${PLAYER}! How have you been, friend? I have some exciting news! While seeking more Orcs to find my lucky talisman, I remembered something: it wasn't the Orcs that took it!'
You ask him if he sustained a knock on the head during his brawl with whatever foes he fought.
'Ah, you jest, my new friend, but Rangers like me often do battle with whatever enemies cross our path: and in my case it was both brigands and Orcs, as I told you before. No, not together, not at the same time, but one after the other. I swear it.
'But I am pretty certain the brigands did not take my talisman, for they were frightened of the Orcs and would not remain in their presence for any period of time, I imagine. But you know who DID remain by the side of the Orcs? Wargs, of course!
'The Orcs I fought were warg-riders, and they must've stashed my talisman inside one of the supply pouches borne by their horrible steeds! So you see, all we have to do is find the warg that carries my talisman! There are lots of them around here, ${PLAYER}. You should check it out! You'd be helping a Ranger, and that counts for a lot in the wild, doesn't it?'

'Ah, ${PLAYER}, I hope you had better luck than I....'
You shake your head.
'Ah, well.' He curses under his breath before turning back to you.
'I suppose I'll just have to think of something else. There is a great fortress on the southernmost promontory of this land; perhaps I will check there. Should we run into each other again I hope to report that I found the talisman! Farewell.'

'I don't know what to say... I did not expect to find such virtue in the heart of a complete stranger. Yet here you are. Thank you, stranger.'

'Don't come any closer! Wait... you don't look like a spy... who are you?'
You explain yourself to the frightened woman and she lowers her hands.
'If what you say is true, then perhaps there is no need to panic. My husband Rúdhan and I have been running for days now, but we were separated from those who fled with us. We tried to keep going, but my husband hurt his leg quite badly. Now we have no supplies and it will be only a matter of time before the vile creatures that pursue us catch up!
'My name is Onora. Will you help us? We need firewood, and the satchel my husband dropped during our flight. We will be forever grateful for your aid.'

'Oh, you startled me! Well-met traveller, I am Maervellon, Ranger of these wood-lands. But I ask that you keep your voice low, for I am tracking down a voracious band of thieves. I trailed the brigands to this ruin, but now I see there are mostly Orcs here....'
The Ranger peers nervously about.
'There have been a few Orc raids through these woods of late, and recently we brawled a good while. Fear not, for I survived with nary a scratch, but those blasted thieves made off with my lucky talisman! It is a charm we Rangers keep for good luck while on the hunt.'
You ask him if he fought with Orcs or with brigands and he peers into the distance.
'Oh, you know... both, really. There were quite a lot of them. This might go a lot faster if you were to aid me in this endeavour. You do look capable enough. All I need is my talisman, you can keep any other treasure we find! So, what do you say? Care to help me retrieve my lucky charm and slay some Orcs?'

'You're back! Any luck?'
You shake your head. His expression breaks for a moment, but he quickly regains his smile.
'Ah, same results on my end, I'm afraid. Oh well, I'm sure it will turn up. I could've sworn... ah, no matter.
'Thank you for your help all the same, ${PLAYER}. I will think on this, and perhaps wander the area further south-east, beyond the old hobbit-burrows. That is the life of a Ranger, is it not? Until we meet again.'

'We are in your debt, ${PLAYER}, for the path to Gaerond was mostly clear of the foes we feared, and I know that was your doing. We are fortunate for the quick bow of the Elf who greeted us as well, though Onora distrusts him. If he is friend of yours he will be friend of ours as well, in time.
'Unless he is prone to jest. Perhaps not then.'

'Thank you, ${PLAYER}. We could not have made it this far without you.
'I know much of the north remains ahead of us, and the journey is not yet ended, but it feels good to have come so far from the dangers we left behind. Whatever awaits us, Rúdhan and I will face it together.
'Thank you for aiding us. You are a friend to our family and our folk from this day forward. You did not need to help us, but you did, and for that we are both grateful.'

'No, I have not left the Angle just yet, ${PLAYER}. Always I believe myself ready to leave, and always, it seems, something comes up anew! Why, just now my arrows saved the lives of two Dunlendings fleeing from some villainy in the south! A pair of half-orcs nearly put blades to their flesh, but my bow was the swifter.
'Their names are Onora and Rúdhan. They say they know you, and owe you their lives. I said they owe them to me as well, but I made the jest and they stared at me with frightened eyes, so I think I shall leave the jokes for my brother.
'You should speak to them, and then I really must return to Imladris. But something always comes up!'

'My leg is well enough now for me to walk, ${PLAYER}, but I am worried about the rest of the journey. You say there is a camp-site to the north-west, where friends will help us as you have done?
'I will entrust my life and that of my wife to you now, my friend, and I hope that trust is not misplaced. Will you go ahead of us and clear a path to this camp, this Gaerond of which you speak? Many are the threats that lurk still ahead of us, and I may not be able to move fast enough to evade them. But if you clear the way, perhaps we will make it.'
