'Hullo, what's this you have here?'
Lotho scowls at you.
'Do you think waving this list of names in my face is going to change my mind? The old bounds worked fine, back when the Westfarthing and Northfarthing ended where they should! Who needs Yondershire to be a part of the Shire? Not I, and not anyone, leastways not any good solid hobbits!
'You peculiar folk... listen up! We need to change the bounds so we can keep the Shire proper safe. Either you move, or you're not in the Shire anymore. It's that simple.
'There's no point trying to discuss it, and your Yonder-watch hasn't got any say in the matter. In fact, I'm sending my own personal Bounders into the Yondershire to make sure nobody tries tampering with the proper bounds. Ha!'

'It is good that you came back when you did, because this matter has become more urgent. The Yonder-watch has informed me that the hobbit seeking to change the bounds has been spotted near Needlehole! He is a sour fellow named Lotho Sackville-Baggins. Do you know him?
'Let us find him and see if he will abandon this misguided campaign of his.'

'You made it! That Lotho has never been much for discussion, and he's only gotten worse with age.
'Unfortunately for him, we've only gotten smarter and more serious, haven't we?'

'I won't let you get away with this, Lotho!'
Fredegar takes a deep breath and calms down slightly before speaking to you in a hushed tone.
'${PLAYER}, I have a plan. There is a Yonder-watch store-house not far from here, and it's become something of a secret hideout for me and my friends. Meet me there as soon as you are able!'
Fredegar turns back to Lotho.
'Until next time, Lotho. You haven't seen the last of us!'

Canvas of Defiance

'Now that you have spoken to these fine hobbits, you must see that I speak the truth! My name is Fredegar, and I have but one concern: the state of the bounds!
'There has been something upsetting going on in the Shire. I can't say any more than that, but you will have to take my word for it. There are frightening folk about, and...'
Fredegar shivers.
'The less said of that, the better. But I have also seen a number of ruffians moving about, and we can surely do something about them! Can I ask you to persuade some ruffians to turn tail and return to their homes outside the Shire? I know they have taken up residence in the ruins of Ost Lagorath to the north, but you might also find them prowling about elsewhere in the Yondershire.'

The young hobbit speaks to the small crowd that gathers around him.
'They say the Bounders protect the bounds? Why is that? That is because everything within the bounds is our home! We are hobbits, are we not? We will decide where the bounds are and where the bounds are not!'
The young hobbit turns his attention to you.
'You there! You look like you could use some more convincing. Speak to these hobbits gathered around. They will tell you I speak only the truth!'
'This is a fine and lengthy list of signatures! You have done well!'
'Fredegar speaks the truth. I have seen a ruffian or two cross the bounds of southern Yondershire. We have got to do something!'
'Fredegar is worried about Yondershire, and I believe him. We live a peaceful life but lately I've seen more and more troublemakers about!'

'He is such a good storyteller. I could listen to him talk about the bounds all day!
'Did you know the bounds of the Shire used to be different from the current bounds? I have seen the maps! Hubo Clayhanger has a book containing such maps in his collection! Now, what was the name of that author? It was someone familiar, but I can't remember why....'

'I don't have proof, but I think some of the stone walls that mark the old bounds are being moved! One day the old wall was intact, and the next? Why, it was missing a stone or two! Someone is up to something!'

'Listen to the tales told by ${PLAYER}, the ${CLASS} who has defeated many ruffians in Yondershire!
'So that's one thing settled, and I thank you for handling it. On to my second concern: someone is seeking to change the bounds, removing Yondershire from the Shire itself! This is unacceptable.
'Here, ${PLAYER}. Take this signature list and collect as many signatures as you can. We'll prove to the guilty party that the folk of Yondershire will not stand for his meddling!'

Hubo Finishes His Book

'I must confess something to you, friend. This feels silly of me to say to someone who has adventured far and wide... but I have never actually been to the Wellstones! I have been writing mainly about the accounts of others who have seen them! You see, I have not actually set one foot outside of Nobottle in my entire life! My mother took a trip to the Shire Proper a few months before I was born, but I don't believe that counts.
'And so my book remains incomplete! I need more information... I need an eyewitness account! Can you go to the Wellstones and look for any relics you might find? I will also make use of any etchings you can provide. That will be most helpful! Remember: the ruins in question go by two names, so you are looking for either the Wellstones or Bâr Faroth.'

'You have brought me even more than I expected! Look at these relics! And these etchings are so detailed that I feel as if I am myself transported to Bâr Faroth... without leaving the comfort of my own hobbit-hole!
'This is so much better than my book! Do you know something, ${PLAYER}? My book is FINISHED! Now I want to make a museum instead!'
The ruins are even more impressive than described in Hubo Clayhanger's book

'You simply must come back to my home. You can view my collection of books and regale me with tales of your most interesting and exciting adventures!'

Hubo Clayhanger's Museum of Wonders
'Would you look at that! Everyone in the village can now visit the Wellstones without having to set foot outside the Fox and Fiddle! Well done indeed, ${PLAYER}!'

'That looks quite decent, ${PLAYER}! Now the question is whether this decoration will actually attract new customers to the Fox and Fiddle... but I am at least willing to give Hubo the time to find out. He has purchased a LOT of food and drink from me over the years, you know.'

'I have had a tremendous idea, ${PLAYER}. There is ample space at the Fox and Fiddle, and Arno Diggle would surely not mind if we construct a small display case in one corner or another of his tavern. How much coin have I given to him over the years for food and drink, not to mention how often I recommend his establishment to others? This is the least he can do for us!
'Maybe you should first ask what he thinks before we begin building our museum beneath his roof. But how could he refuse?'

'What can I get you?'
You explain Hubo Clayhanger's curious request, and the proprietor of the tavern tilts his head to one side.
'Interesting idea. Hubo is one of my most loyal customers, and I suppose it is possible that such a display will attract some more business. I say go ahead!
'You see those crates over there? They are not currently in use, nor is the space beneath them. You can set up Hubo's museum over there, and we'll see how it goes. There should be nails and wood aplenty for your purposes throughout Nobottle.'

From Field to Pint

'Now that's a beer of which you can be proud! Delightful! Note the sense of accomplishment you now feel, and let it float your steps as you walk around Yondershire.'
Brewmaster Bloda Hopblossom grins at you.
'Aye, you'll have some walking to do, friend! You can't keep this brew all to yourself! You need to get it into the hands of our patrons! Visit every drinking establishment in Yondershire and bring the brew to our waiting customers... you'll get to see a lot of happy faces as you make these deliveries!'
'Hullo there! I am glad to see you! I was almost out of Nobottle brew! Have a drink to quench your thirst. You earned it!'

'Hullo there! Correct me if I'm wrong, but you seem to be the sort who enjoys a good brew! You're in good company here, friend! Now, let me ask you a question: have you ever fancied brewing up a good beer yourself? I find if you engage in the process you'll have a greater appreciation for every bottle you enjoy, and wouldn't that be quite a nice reward?
'I will be happy to teach you the way of it, for I am Bloda Hopblossom, the head brew-master of Nobottle, and mine is the finest beer in the Westfarthing... don't let anyone tell you differently! This may be one of the younger settlements in the Shire, as things are reckoned, but Nobottle is still centuries old by now... plenty of time for us to master brewing!
'Now listen to the many steps of brewing a beer of which you can be proud!'

Delivered brews!
'Good, good! You can leave those beers with me. That drink is for you: a token of thanks for making this delivery.'

'Hullo! Ah, I see Brewmaster Bloda Hopblossom has put you to work. It's been awhile since she's had to make a delivery herself!
'Have a drink before you leave. No sense crafting a batch and not having a taste!'
'I was wondering when someone would come around. I am nearly out of drink! You saved this establishment, and no mistake! Please make sure to have a token of my gratitude before you leave.'
'Ah, you are back! I believe the brew has fermented enough. Now the brew is complete and we are ready to fill all these empty bottles with delicious beer!'

You have learned a great deal about the brewing of Yondershire beer from Brewmaster Bloda Hopblossom and completed her deliveries to each of the grateful tavern-keeps. Revellers of Yondershire will no doubt sing your praises this evening, as they enjoy a mug or two of Nobottle's finest!
'The barley is right here at the farm. Make sure to pick only the stalks that are ripe and ready!'
'Good work! Now the barley needs to be malted. Look for the malting container here on the farm.'
'You are getting there! I love your enthusiasm! Make sure to use that enthusiasm when mashing the barley! That is the next step!'
'Now my favourite step, boiling the brew! I like the aroma it brings to the air!'
'The next step is to ferment the brew. This is an important step, though not the most exciting.'

'While you are waiting for the brew to ferment, you should collect some empty bottles. There are a few on the farm but we also have an arrangement with The Fox and Fiddle to make use of their empty bottles as well. We will need them all for the next step!'

Gytha peers at you slyly.

'Your hunt of those elusive and fearsome creatures was successful? I am impressed! I did not really expect you to succeed, but I am pleased that you have. Perhaps we are equals in the hunt after all, and even better: the villages of Yondershire are made safer by your efforts, which is the most important thing. Well done!'

'You there! Do you think you have what it takes to become the best hunter of game in all of Yondershire? Bold words, bold words! Well, I'll be the judge of whether you're worthy of boasting or not.
'How's about I put you to the test? Gamwich can always use more food in the stores for winter. Hunt each of the creatures to be found throughout Yondershire and return to me, and perhaps I will make you an honourary hunter of Gamwich.'

Shrews' Clues

'I am a little embarrassed, ${PLAYER}, but perhaps you can help me with something?
'I have always kept my Bounder supplies within a small shed, and never thought I needed to worry that someone might break in... but that very thing has happened! And I know the identities of the culprits!'
Frothard turns a bright pink.
'It's shrews, ${PLAYER}. They burrowed right under the wall of my shed and made a terrible mess. Worse still, they ran off with an important map of mine, and they have likely torn it all to pieces by now! Can you find all the pieces of the map and return them to me so I can put it back together?'

'Ah! Of course! I remember now!
'I buried my golf clubs to keep them safe while Foxden Heath was being tidied up and restored so it could serve as a golfing course once again!'
You ask why he buried the clubs instead of keeping them safe in his shed, and he laughs.
'Are you quite mad? I can't keep them in there: the shrews are always getting into that shed!'
'Hobbits,' you think to yourself.

'You found every scrap of the map! Wonderful!
'You see, this map holds the location of a treasure that I buried for safekeeping many years ago! It was so many years ago that I have, er, rather forgotten what the treasure was, but with the map restored I will be able to dig it up and find out!
'It had to be something valuable... why else would I have drawn a map? Follow the map and dig up the treasure, ${PLAYER}! I am very curious to learn what I thought to hide!'

'Thank you for helping me up. Did you see that goose? One minute I am minding my own business, taking home some fresh vegetables from the market. The very next minute, this horrible goose comes along, knocks me down, and pilfers all my beautiful cabbages!
'You must get back my cabbages!'

'That was the most excitement I have seen in several days, and you just missed all the fun! That goose ran in here, knocked down every bottle in its path, and ran out... just as you arrived!
'I do appreciate you cleaning up the bottles for me. Now good luck catching that silly goose!'

'You say there were three geese unleashed upon my neighbours, and not simply one loose goose?'
Prunella rubs her chin.
'That does explain why my goose was so tricksy. It was always able to cause the most surprising amount of mischief. Three times the normal amount, it seems!
'Who can say where those geese might have wandered off to now? Perhaps we will see them again one day. Thank you for all your help! Now I think I should find out if the farmer that entrusted me with that goose in the first place knew the full story of the silly creature....'

'Oh thank you for retrieving my cabbages, for by rescuing them you have saved me as well! How so, you ask? Well, cabbage stew is my wife's favourite meal and I promised to make it for her... for today is our wedding anniversary!
'I don't think she would have believed that I was robbed by a goose, let alone three geese. I am in your debt.'

Adamanda North-took has asked you to collect some rope from Anson Roper.

'Rope, is it? Well, you have come to the right place, but this is sadly the wrong time. It will take me some time to get your order together. If you want the rope today, I will need you to take on some of the tasks I had planned for myself or I shall fall behind in my work.
'You still want the rope? Very well. Firstly, my supply of flax is low for today and my next delivery is not until the morrow. Go gather some flax from the fields north of here.'

'Yes, yes, this will do! You did a fine job of harvesting the flax. If you ever give up this adventuring life of yours, you could make a fine farmer!
'Now then, some animal wandered onto the rope walk and chewed up my top and other wooden items I use to make rope. The top is a piece of wood with grooves cut into it, you see. It is essential for weaving strands of yarn into rope, and you had best believe it will not produce the same quality with the grooves all chewed up.
'Go into the forest and find some freshly fallen wood, will you? No need to cut anything down. We had a beast of a storm come through a few nights back. Knocked down all manner of trees that were otherwise healthy. Find a fine piece of wood for me that is not too dried out, rotted, or fragile. Bring me that and I will trade you for the rope.'

'You bring fortuitous news, my new friend! The foolish dinner my mother insisted upon has been cancelled! I suppose we can thank good ol' Pip for whatever prank he's off pulling. I am glad to know he is as keen on the machinations of our parents as myself. Which is to say, not at all.
'This leaves me free for the rest of the day to get on with my Grand Plan! Say, you seem to be rather accomplished and useful. Perhaps you could aid me in my endeavour? Excellent!
'We need a few things to make this happen, one of which is a spool of rope from Anson. You head over to Tighfield and collect that from Anson while I gather some of the other supplies.'

'Welcome back, friend. My, you look like you have been busy! What took you so long?'
You explain the tasks Anson had you complete. Adamanda guffaws.
'He made you do what?! That Anson is the laziest hobbit I know. I paid for that rope last week. Brought down a fine buck that I traded to him, and he has you running around doing a full day's work.'
She laughs again, shaking her head and wiping tears from the corners of her eyes.
'Ah, you return! Why yes, this is a fine piece of wood indeed. Very well, you have fulfilled my requests and helped me out a great deal. I thank you! Here is the rope Diamond requested.'
With her obligations for the afternoon cancelled, Adamanda North-took is free to focus on enacting her Grand Plan.

'Oh. You return. You were gone for so long that I forgot you were even doing something for me.'
She glances up at the sky.
'You are lucky, you know. To be able to travel so far and to see so many things. To make your own future.'
Adamanda is silent a moment and then sighs, and smiles brightly at you.
'Now then! Where is this net that took you so long to procure? We have Grand Plans to enact!'

'Well, well! Your first few knots were making me a bit nervous, but you seem to get the hang of it as you went on! Good for you! If you ever want to give up this wandering life of yours, I could see you taking up work as an Apprentice Net Weaver! Go on ahead and take the net to Diamond, and good hunting!'

'Hello to you, my fine ${RACE}. This is very nice rope and will make an excellent net. Tell Diamond I shall have it for her by mid-day on the morrow.'
You explain that you need it sooner.
'Well that's too bad for you, now isn't it? I have tasks what need doing today and haven't the time for net weaving.
'Although... how comfortable are you with bees? My hives are full of the sweetest honey but not always the sweetest bees. If you take some honey over to Pello at the Brimful Quiver, I could work on the net for Diamond. Mind you don't upset the bees, though. They are quick to anger a' times.'

Adamanda's laughter fades to a chuckle and she clears her throat, trying to hide her smile.
'Now that we have the rope, we can move on to the next step in my Grand Plan! We need a net! Take the rope to Ramsa Twelling in Gamwich and have her make us a net, will you? I am going to follow these tracks a ways and will meet you further along their trail.'

'Well now, you made your way back here far sooner than I expected! The net is not done yet, but look what I have found! A helper!'
She beams at you pointedly.
'Come now, here is the knot you want to use. With the both of us tying, this will be finished in no time!'

'Welcome, friend! What can I get for you today? Ah, you have come for Ramsa's mead is it? I thought you looked sweet!
'Let's have the honey then, and you may collect her bottle from the room behind me.'
With a fresh bundle of rope in hand, thanks entirely to you having been duped into trading for it, Adamanda is ready for the next stage of her Grand Plan.

The Aroma of Meals Past
Collected Gamwich herbs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

Wingard is scanning the texts you recovered when she suddenly bursts into off-key song and clumsy dance.
'O-Oh! Assistant! You're still here!
...
'You didn't see or hear any of that.
...
'Ahem.
'Assistant! I have made the most incredible finding. A shrub that grows in this area was actually used as a culinary herb. I will gather a small amount on my way back to Gamwich and make some test dishes. I would ask you to pick a greater amount and bring them to me in Gamwich.'

Wingard accepts the bundle of herbs from you, plucks one from the bundle, and rubs the leaf between her thumb and forefinger. The aroma that seizes your attention is bitter and vegetal, but it quickly gives way to a profound sweetness backed by a gentle peppery note. And just as quickly, the scent is gone.
'The test dishes I made were abject failures. Just horrid and... and gunky, if that's even a word. But the aroma is so arresting isn't it? Perhaps this wasn't used in the food itself, but as an aroma to appreciate before or after the meal. Maybe there are techniques that can properly draw out this herb's flavour.'
Wingard grips the bundle of herbs the way a child grips a new toy.
'Assistant, I am sad to say that this is the end of our partnership. At least for now. If my research yields a famous new dish, I'll be sure to credit you for your contribution. Perhaps I'll find a way to work your name into the name of the dish.
'How did you spell your name again? ${PLAYER}?
'Hmm.... In any case, thank you again, and I hope to see you around.'

'What makes for a good mathom? Well, anything I suppose. If I receive a mathom I don't like, I simply pass it along to someone else! Personally, though, I like receiving a mathom suited to my hobbies. Best mathoms I ever received are a hammer, a bundle of cheesecloth, and a short sword.'
...
'For three separate hobbies, of course.
'Why do you ask? Are you offering? If so a new wooden spoon would be great. I lost my old one during what I choose to call a 'grain mashing incident'.'

'What do I like in a mathom, you ask? The smaller the better! When you have as many friends and relations as I do, a lot of mathoms find their way into your home. I like to keep things tidy, so smaller mathoms mean they take up less space, which means I am less bothered!'
'Red. I like red things.'

'Judging by your outfit you must be a person of discerning taste. Perhaps you're the right person to help me! I'm in town visiting a friend. 'For years now, I have done my duty as a postman to the best of my ability, but as of late, I have found it quite overwhelming!
'It pains me to ask, but would you help me to handle this workload? I've many deliveries to make today, and I do not know if I can finish them all before sundown. And what would folk think of the Quick Post then?
'If you'd help me to get some of this mail delivered to Long Cleeve, I will see to it that you are properly compensated. Provided, of course, that the task is done to the standards of the Quick Post: No stopping to chat with nosey folk, and no swimming—at least not while you're holding one of my satchels! 'Oh, hullo!
'If you have a complaint to file against the Quick Post, I do ask that you submit it in writing and deliver it to my assistant, Ebbo. We are aware of a number of issues involving delayed or lost mail that some hobbits have reported over the past few weeks. Rest assured, the Quick Post will get to the bottom of it!
'With that out of the way, who are you? How can I help you today?'
You introduce yourself to Postman Grubb and ask what's happening at the Quick Post.
'Pleased to meet you, ${PLAYER}. I'm Walto Grubb, and I've been a postman going on twelve years. I'd say it's my calling, if you believe in such things! As for what's going on with the Quick Post, I wish I could tell you. Like I said, the mail's been turning up late or not at all, and the folk in Yondershire aren't too happy about it. I don't know if the Postmaster's been trying something new or altering routes, but I don't think that's it.'
Postman Grubb looks around and lowers his voice.
'Between you and me, I think someone's been tampering with the mail. If you're of a mind to help me sort this out, meet me inside the Quick Post.'

'I must apologize for the mess, ${PLAYER}.
'You see, we're a bit backed up here in Nobottle with letters and parcels due to be delivered to the Hithershire. Most folks down in Michel Delving, Hobbiton, and the like just call it the Shire, but it seems a bit odd to me, but I digress. We've had a few postmen come up from the Hithershire with small deliveries, but none of them are taking as much as they ought to to deliver back to the rest of the Shire. It's almost like they're trying to slow the whole thing down. For goodness' sake, we've had a parcel due for Stock sitting here for over a month!
'Ebbo received a delivery from the Quick Post of Waymeet this morning, and as usual, it was very light. Unfortunately, after I inspected the letters and parcels, I only became more suspicious that someone's been deliberately tampering with the mail.
'Why don't you head up front and take a look at them, ${PLAYER}? I am curious to know what you make of their condition!'

'Hullo there! What's this now?'
You hand Postman Grubb's letter to Postmaster Proudfoot. He unseals it, begins reading, and after a long moment, his eyes widen.
'Well, I don't like the sound of this at all. To my knowledge, the Quick Post has not altered our service to Nobottle, or Yondershire, for that matter! And we certainly would not make a habit of failing to make deliveries entirely!
'To his credit, Walto has provided a detailed record of the comings and goings at the Quick Post in Nobottle. One of my associates, Onyx Nethercot, has taken to maintaining the ledger, and I assure you, our records are current and accurate. A careful comparison between Walto's records and the ledger should tell us everything we need to know.
'You'll find Onyx behind the counter inside the Quick Post. Tell her to bring out the ledger and see if everything is in accord!'

'Oh, hullo! What brings you to the Quick Post today?'
You introduce yourself and tell Onyx that Postmaster Proudfoot has asked to see the ledger to compare it to Postman Grubb's records.
'Oh dear me, has some sort of mistake been made? Just a moment....'
Onyx leans down, produces a heavy ledger from under the counter, and examines its spine. After a moment, Onyx sets it down on the counter with a muffled thud.
'Here you go, ${PLAYER}. Take all the time you need!'

'A discrepancy?! I can't believe such a thing happened on my watch!'
Onyx pauses for a moment and composes herself.
'Fifty-eight pieces of mail sent out but only thirty-three actually making it to the Yondershire? That just doesn't make any sense. And besides, no one's ever lost that much on their routes—not since 'ere the days of Ned Harfoot!
'Here, ${PLAYER}, show the ledger to the Postmaster and see what he makes of it. If there's trouble with the Quick Post, it's not happening here in Michel Delving!'

'Ah, you've brought the ledger. Were you able to find what we were looking for?'
You tell Postmaster Proudfoot that you found clear discrepancies between the records of Michel Delving and Nobottle. He shakes his head solemnly.
'I'll have to thank Miss Nethercot for keeping such neat records. To be quite honest, that has never been a strength of mine. If it's all the same to you, I'd still like to examine it myself.'
You hand the ledger to Postmaster Proudfoot. He leaves through it, pausing in a few places and tracing along the page with his finger. After a short while, he snaps the ledger shut.
'It's as you said, ${PLAYER}. A discrepancy of twenty-five pieces of mail....'
According to the ledger, fifty-eight letters and parcels were bound for the Yondershire in the past month

'I knew it, ${PLAYER}.
'If Postmaster Proudfoot had caught wind of this, he'd have already put a stop to it. After all the work he's put in to maintain the good reputation of the Quick Post, there's no chance he'd let some sort of conspiracy drag it into the mud. I have to inform the Postmaster at once!'
Postman Grubb takes out a blank piece of parchment and inks a quill. He begins writing, periodically glancing to his ledger.
'Now, ${PLAYER}, I hope you don't mind, but I need to ask you to deliver this to Postmaster Proudfoot in Michel Delving. The Postmaster will have his own records on hand, and I would urge him to compare them against my own.'
Postman Grubb finishes writing, seals the letter, and hands it to you.
'I'm counting on you, ${PLAYER}. There is something afoot in the Shire!'

'Ah, I see. Is something amiss with that route in particular?
'For what it's worth, the satchels for Yondershire haven't been sent out for delivery yet. My assistant, Norbert, was handling them today, and last I saw, he was still wandering about Waymeet. If I had to guess, he's probably left the satchels about to collect any last-minute letters and parcels. I've told him time and again that he should keep an eye on the satchels, but he's always off looking at pipe-weed fields or busy chatting with nosey folk!
'As for the Postmaster's test, it'll take a little shuffling, but I think I can find an empty satchel around here for you. If you'd go collect those satchels and tell Norbert to bring them to Michel Delving without delay, I can have it sorted it out by the time you're back.'

'It's been a while since I've made the trip to Nobottle myself, but it's a nice route. It's a nice town, too. Truth be told, I've spent more than a few nights and even a few mornings in the Fox and Fiddle!'
Postman Twofoot finally appears to notice that you have finished preparing the satchel for Yondershire.
'All settled, then? Just the one letter? I suppose if it's just a test, that's for the best!'

'If the evidence of tampering that Postman Grubb discovered wasn't bad enough, we now know for certain that someone is interfering with the Quick Post. However, if these would-be conspirators don't know that they've been found out, we can use that to our advantage!
'Firstly, we must safe-guard the mail due to be delivered to Yondershire. After Onyx and the others sort it here in Michel Delving, it is sent to Waymeet for any final preparations and then carried along the usual route to Nobottle. Postman Twofoot oversees the Quick Post at Waymeet. You'll need to speak with him and ensure that any mail for Yondershire is returned to my care here in Michel Delving. Until this issue is sorted out, I don't want to take any chances!
'Next, I'd like to conduct a test of the route to Nobottle. Something is going wrong between Waymeet and Nobottle, and I want to know what it is! But I'd rather not risk someone's mail for the test....'
With a look of sudden inspiration on his face, Postmaster Proudfoot produces a piece of parchment from his pocket. He begins scrawling a lengthy letter, and after a long moment, he seals the letter and crumples it gently in his hands.
'Here, ${PLAYER}. I've written an exhaustive account of the weather over the course of the past week and a ranking of my favourite pies in the Shire. Perfectly innocent, I would think! I've not signed it, of course. I don't want them knowing I've found them out if something goes awry!
'When you arrive at Waymeet, ask Postman Twofoot to provide you a satchel. You'll run the route to Nobottle yourself, and if you meet with any resistance along the way, return to me at once!
'Hurry now, ${PLAYER}! The Quick Post is depending on you!'

My father, Cardavor, was injured in the fighting and Skorgrím fled Ered Luin, but other threats still remain.
'Alas, I am afraid my companion and I have not come here on a happy errand. Goblins were spotted crossing the River Lune into the ruins of Lhúngobel and it is possible they mean to interfere in the affairs of the Shire. In addition, we have captured a Dourhand, but he bears no weapon against us and begs our aid.

'I must admit I doubted your resolve, ${PLAYER}.
'I thought Halros a fool when he ingratiated himself to the halflings. It was our duty to protect these lands, not befriend its peoples. Perhaps I have misjudged my charge....'
Anthandir pauses and for the briefest moment, a pained look washes across his face.
'When the time is right, I will reveal myself to the halflings in the village they call Long Cleeve. For too long, they have caught only glimpses of me and Thorvellon. They think that my companion is some terrible Gnasher, some beast in the night, but we have protected these lands—vigilant and unseen. Yet, there is a shadow that rises in the east, and it grows in strength with each passing hour. If we do not stand together, then we shall die alone. Perhaps now it is best that they know of me, that they might call upon me in times of dire need.
'Go, friend, and aid those that you can. I ask only one thing: do not speak of me to Halros. Old wounds are best left forgotten.'

'I heard you coming, ${RACE}. If I did not deem you a friend, you would not stand before me.

'It is true that I have kept watch for many years and that the dangers facing the Shire have seldom grown so dire, but my duty is to protect these lands. '${PLAYER}, I have an undertaking that I believe you would be suited for. Servants of the Enemy, under the guise of riders in black, recently tried to cross the Bruinen. The river's waters swept them away at my command. Perhaps they no longer threaten Imladris, but we cannot be certain.
'Scouts have been sent out to determine whether the Black Riders truly fell at the Ford. My sons will soon set out to do the same, but I have also entrusted them with an errand of their own. I would ask that you travel with them to Lothlórien to meet with their grandmother, Lady Galadriel. Though I cannot fully reveal the purpose of their errand, I trust that the three of you will keep each other safe.
'Elladan waits for you outside. May your search bear fruit.'

'Hail, ${PLAYER}! Elrohir has gone ahead to search the Bruinen, but he wished to pass on his greetings as well.
'We're to travel south to Eregion, then through the Redhorn Pass into Lothlórien. Make any preparations you may require; we have a long trek ahead of us.'

'He must be close. Let's hurry.'

'Neither Elrohir nor I enjoy the idea of taking the pass, but I confess that Orcs are not the sole reason. Many years ago, our mother travelled through here to visit our grandparents in Lórien. She never made it to her destination -- Orcs captured her. When we realized she had disappeared, my brother and I set out to find her. After weeks of searching, we found her alive, but...'
Elladan's voice trails off as he turns away.
'...We'll keep each other safe. We must.'

'Quickly -- we must strike out for Talan Revail.'

'We're right at the doorstep of Caras Galadhon, but how can we stand idly by while Wargs sow chaos in the Golden Wood?
'${PLAYER}, you have been a stalwart companion. Not once have you faltered in aiding us, and for that we are grateful. Though you have honoured your promise to us and our father, we have one last thing to ask of you.
'Come with us to the north. Whatever the Wargs have planned, we'll put an end to it. Together.'

'I've been told your journey to Lórien was rather eventful, ${PLAYER}. Still, you persisted and completed your task admirably.
'Though travel and adventure have separated my sons from me before, every time they venture forth, my heart grows uneasy. For what parent can stand not knowing where their children are?
'But this time, I was comforted knowing you were by their side. Thank you. They have found a true friend in you.'

'We should rest here and gather our strength before continuing. We have yet to embark on the most difficult part of our journey.'

'Greetings. You have my thanks for defeating the drakes. I had no desire to involve myself with them, seeing as how they do not threaten me or my kin, but they did not care for my presence. At least I may now deliver my message more easily.
'We have not discovered any sign of the Black Riders, nor any other tidings of the Enemy's servants. However, wolves gather along the banks of the Anduin in great numbers. What this indicates, I cannot say I know.'

'Whatever killed these boars was an even match in size for our friend.' Elrohir holds up a feather that is certainly too large to belong to any normal bird. 'It seems I wasn't wrong about his location after all. He must have left the area once he realized he had intruded on something's territory.
'Of course, I doubt that creature, whatever it is, was an even match in power. After all, the Eagles are a more than capable folk. But this creature may be dangerous to anyone travelling through this area, and that does not bode well for our errand.
'Let's track it down.'

'That drake matron commanded a most fearsome brood! It'll be safer here now, though I fear that will change.
'We ought to head back to Pembar; Elladan must be wondering where we are.'

'${PLAYER}, I'm certain the Eagle noticed our presence and flew here, but I don't see him. Do you?'

'Once you are ready, we shall depart.'

'It's best not to tarry here any longer. The Redhorn Pass can be treacherous during the warmest of months, and we are fast approaching winter.
'Be on the look-out for Orcs most of all; they plague the mountain and have waylaid many an unfortunate traveller.'

'${PLAYER}, I am sorry. My desperation for answers clouded my judgement. The Bruinen must have left the Black Riders severely weakened; even if the last horse had survived, it would not have been able to carry its owner far. Perhaps they have vanished from the North, like Elladan said.
'I do not wish to dwell on what happened in the Redhorn Pass but... the cloaked figure eluded you too, didn't it? I suppose we'll never know who or what that truly was. To tell the truth, I am in no rush to find out myself.'

Mission: The Further Adventures of Elladan & Elrohir, Chapter 5
'Rest now, ${PLAYER}.'

'${PLAYER}, there you are! Our grandmother's garden is a sight to behold, is it not? I can forgive you for wanting to linger and take it all in. Though, I must caution you against wandering too far. We have given our word that you are trustworthy; however, the Galadhrim do not look favourably upon strangers -- as I'm sure you've realized.
'We must part ways to meet with our grandmother soon, but for now... shall we walk in together?' Elrohir smiles.

'You have my gratitude for keeping my grandsons safe. I was told that the three of you passed through the Redhorn Gate to enter Lórien. The crossing must have been... difficult for them. Their mother has long since sailed West, but our grief remains.
'The details of what transpired during your travels elude me. What news from Imladris? Did you discover anything?'
As you recount every step of your travels, Lord Celeborn listens attentively. When you finish describing your encounters with the Wargs from Shathur-munzu, his expression darkens.
'I'm sure my grandsons told you of our family's connection to that cursed place. This Ránulur may not be a threat at the moment, but I believe his tale is not finished. Should he decide to endanger Lórien again, he will not find mercy.
'Please, wait here. I believe my wife would like to speak to you once her business with our grandsons is done.'

'While my grandsons' reasons for being here are grave, I am glad to see them again. May our next meeting be under happier circumstances.
'They came to me with heavy hearts after what happened on Caradhras. Do not fret, ${PLAYER} -- your presence steadied them. Such wounds may never heal completely, but they can be soothed. My Mirror showed them visions of the past, moments that they hold dear. Sometimes it is a kindness to remember.'
As Lady Galadriel speaks, she studies you with keen eyes that almost seem to pierce through you.
'The coming days will be dire ones for Middle-earth. I foresee that you have your own part to play in the shaping of its fate -- indeed, you have already taken your first steps. Our paths shall cross again.
'But do not let such thoughts occupy your mind for now. Find peace under the mellyrn. Once you have rested and regained your strength, we will send you on your way.'

'The Warg mentioned a name -- Ránulur. I cannot imagine the \qChieftain of Wargs\q would allow another to command the pack unless he did not come with them. Now that we know they do not fight for Sauron, they are not a sizable threat. The remaining Wargs will either slink back to the Vales or fall to the Galadhrim. Lórien is safe.
'Perhaps Shathur-munzu will not be such a dark place one day. But for now, we must turn our gaze elsewhere. We'll let the scouts at Talan Revail know that the Wargs are no more, then return to Caras Galadhon.'

'Several Wargs ambushed us here before escaping to the south-east. Two scouts followed the fleeing Wargs and have not reported back. I fear that they may have been overwhelmed.'

Mission: The Further Adventures of Elladan & Elrohir, Chapter 4
'Onwards, then.'

'Shathur-munzu is a dwarf-ruin to the north, in the Vales of Anduin. Its history is not a happy one, but my brother and I have our own reasons for loathing the place. We... found our mother there, tortured by the Orcs. Even after our father healed her wounds, she could no longer bear to continue living in Middle-earth. The hurt had gone too deep. So she sailed West, to the Undying Lands.
'The thought often crosses my mind -- in the end, will I sail and reunite with her? Or shall I remain in Middle-earth and never see her again?
'...Forgive me. I did not mean to discuss such dark matters. If that Warg came from the Vales, then its brethren may be haunting the northern reaches of Lothlórien. We ought to continue towards Caras Galadhon. Once we gather more information there, we can decide on what to do next.'
For a moment, the twins linger to watch the bear cub and its mother. Elrohir breaks the silence first.
'Shall we?'

'It seems Elrohir's suspicions about the wolves were correct.'
Elladan's gaze falls upon the bear cub, which stares at your group warily.
'This little one must have gotten separated from its mother. Shall we help it return to her?' He smiles gently.

'Did you hear that?' Elrohir exchanges a look with you and Elladan.
Then you hear growls coming from somewhere up ahead.
Elrohir narrows his eyes. 'Approach quietly.'

'Under attack? By whom?
'This smells like Orcs to me, ${PLAYER}, but I cannot understand it. Orcs have not troubled these lands for many years!
'Come with me, and stay close. We will get to the bottom of this, and save the town if we must!'
'You should follow Meneldir outside, ${PLAYER}! I will be right behind you!'
'I think you'll find the people here to be friendly and welcoming, if you treat them kindly. Speak to Geralt by the fountain and see if I'm wrong.'

'But anyway, Mossward is a quiet village. Always has been! Cause no trouble and you can stay as you like. But first things first: you should pay a visit to our blacksmith, Skardí Bendblade. He'll clean and fix up your gear for you. His shop is just up those steps. Look for the sign with the anvil on it.'

'These Uruks have decorated their equipment with a sigil I have not seen before: the mark of a white hand. It may be the symbol of this raiding party, but for all the hurt this band has inflicted upon Mossward, they were still few in number and disorganized. What need have they for such a sigil? None now, thanks to our efforts, but still I wonder. I will think on it, ${PLAYER}.'

'I hope you don't mind me staring! We don't see many adventurers in these parts. The nearest we usually get is that Meneldir. Says he's a Ranger, but it seems to me that's just an excuse for having dirt on his clothes and disappearing into the wild at all hours...
'But anyway, Mossward is a quiet village. Always has been! Cause no trouble and you can stay as you like. But first things first: you should pay a visit to our blacksmith, Skardí Bendblade. He'll clean and fix up your gear for you. His shop is just up those steps. Look for the sign with the anvil on it.'

'Thank you so much for saving our son from those horrible creatures! What were they? Some breed of Orc? Why would they come to Mossward?
'We are most fortunate you were here, stranger!'

'My friend Skardí speaks the truth: you do not want to stride into battle without your weapons equipped, for they will do you little good at the bottom of your bags. He is right on this point, as well: Mossward is a quiet village, and few adventurers come this way, let alone one who carries ${PLAYER:herself[f]|himself} as you do. What road has brought you to Mossward on the border of Swanfleet, my friend?'
You consider what should be said of your past to this curious stranger. Would you speak of an upbringing that gave to you a desire to see distant wonders, or of the dangers that even now encroach upon the lands of all free folk, compelling you to fight on behalf of those who cannot? Before you can choose the right words, Meneldir raises his palm.
'I'm glad for any help you can give me. Stay close!'
'Just carrying around a bunch of equipment won't help you much in battle, as I'm sure you know. You want to be sure to equip your weapons before you get into a fight!'

'Very funny.'

You explain that adventuring is dangerous work, and sooner or later your morale is likely to run out. When that happens, you will find yourself at one of the many Defeat Circles scattered around the land.
'Very funny, stranger. I know that fighting is dangerous! That's why I will try not to fight enemies that look to be beyond my capabilities! But sometimes it's unavoidable, I suppose... and when that happens, if I'm defeated, I'll find myself at the nearest Defeat Circle to where I fell in battle?'
'What's my next adventuring lesson? And make it a good one!'
'Skardí spends more time fixing horseshoes than he does forging swords!'

'Skardí spends more time fixing horseshoes than he does forging swords! I mean no insult, Skardí, but it's true! What use does an adventurer have with a shop like this?'
You explain that as an adventurer engages in combat, equipped weapons and armour sustain durability damage, and folk such as Skardí Bendblade are able to repair them so you can keep using them. Additionally, shopkeepers throughout Middle-earth can sell an adventurer all sorts of items and equipment that will aid you on your journeys.
Skardí clears his throat and speaks up. 'That all costs coin, young Tegwyn, horseshoes and swords alike! But if that raid is a sign of things to come, I think the swords might become more in demand than they have been until now....'
'That's all well and good, but I want to hit something!'
'A scrap of parchment? You had better read it, ${PLAYER}. Perhaps it will tell us why this Uruk led his raiding party to Mossward.'

'Let's see if this parchment holds any clues for us.'
Meneldir briefly studies the crumpled parchment, but then he looks up, disappointed.
'I cannot read much of this. If this were an ordinary day, I would be grateful to have no reason to understand the Black Speech... but on this day it is a cause for frustration.
'Hold, ${PLAYER}. What has happened to this Uruk's blade? It did not fall far from his body, unless my eyes were somehow deceived.'

'What's that? Goblins and Uruks? Ordinarily I would say you were spinning tall tales and send you on your way without supper, but there was a good deal of excitement in the night a few hours past, and some of the hunters we sent out never came back!
'I am worried about them, but I am even more concerned that without the meat they were supposed to bring back, our food stocks will be thinner than planned. 'I will consider what you have told me, but I will consider it more quickly if you bring back some choice cuts of meat from the beasts of the Stoor-vales! Bring them to Cunedda Moltgig, our butcher, at his shop down the hill.'

'I don't know, ${PLAYER}.
'If the aims of the Three Wizards have changed, if they have been corrupted by evil, all of the Free Peoples of Middle-earth may be endangered.'

'We won't be caught off-guard again! If goblins and Uruks seek to raid our village again, we will make them pay a heavy price for it!
'Skardí Bendblade has been working to supply us with arms and armour, ${PLAYER}, so we will be prepared if another raiding party comes to Mossward. Will you bring us another barrel of the weapons he has fashioned for us? I will then distribute them to the people of the village.'

'Cadogan means well, and the folk of Mossward will fight to defend their homes from goblins and Uruks and anything else that threatens them... but against Wizards I do not think they will have a very high chance of survival.
'I will tell you what I know of the Three Wizards, ${PLAYER}, and I will let you judge our chances.'

Meneldir rubs his temple, deep in thought.
'Of all the Three Wizards, I have only met this one in person: Radagast the Brown, a master of shapes and hues and friend to all good-hearted beasts and birds. He wanders the wild places, secret lands known only to creatures of fur and feather... and I suppose known to some of my kin among the Dúnedain, as well.
'He seemed a jovial chap to me, when I met him. I cannot believe he would turn against us.'

Meneldir shakes his head.
'I know little about Gandalf the Grey. They say he walks the land with the aid of an old walking-stick, pipe-smoke curling about the tall hat he wears, but I have never seen him. I believe he must keep to himself, choosing not to become involved in the matters of the day.
'My former chieftain Strider knew him, and believed him to be a kindly soul. I have never known my chieftain to judge someone wrongly, and if he had it was not his fault but another's.
'Still, I would not have believed any of the Wizards could become corrupted, either....'
'I will tell you what I know of the Three Wizards that walk in Middle-earth. It is not very much, I confess it.'
'Aye, there's another barrel of weapons for the folk of Mossward. You can come behind the counter to pick it up... just don't touch anything else!'

'Skardí Bendblade has been working to supply us with arms and armour, ${PLAYER}, so we will be prepared if another raiding party comes to Mossward. Will you bring us another barrel of the weapons he has fashioned for us? I will then distribute them to the people of the village.'

Meneldir sighs heavily.
'I have always understood Saruman the White to be the most learned of the Wizards, and the greatest of their order. It is said he was sent here by the Powers to guide and instruct those who dwell within Middle-earth. At Isengard he lives, in a great tower built by the Númenóreans. Orthanc, it is called, and I have heard it contains a trove of knowledge and learning unmatched by that of any king or scholar.
'Can it be that Saruman no longer seeks to protect the Free Peoples of Middle-earth? I cannot believe this is so.'

'I cannot believe this, ${PLAYER}. Can it be true that Saruman commanded these Uruks to attack the folk of Swanfleet? Why would the Wizard wish to do harm to the folk of Mossward? He has ever been a watchful protector of Middle-earth! What can have changed?
'It must be a lie. There can be no other explanation. Let us return to Mossward and see how the people there fare in our absence. I... I cannot believe Saruman is capable of such treachery. There must be something else to blame for the Orc-presence in these lands.'
'I do not know much of Wizards. That has always been for the best, and if they choose to send Uruks to ravage our lands it is seeming a better choice day after day!'
'We should return to Mossward. I need time to think about this.'
'We must make ready!'

'After the fall of Beleriand, most of my people came to live in the land of Lindon, to the west, under the benevolent rule of Gil-galad. Bonds of friendship were made with the dwarves of Ered Luin, but a thriving trade in metal and gems with that people dwindled as the Longbeards suffered war and disaster of their own. Yearning for mithril to fashion into their works of art and beauty, many of the Noldor followed the dwarves as they journeyed eastward. Led by Celebrimbor, descendant of Fëanor, the Elves settled in the holly-covered hills beneath the west gate of Khazad-dûm. There was once again friendship and trade between Elf and dwarf, and Celebrimbor's city in Eregion thrived.
'Eregion was still a young kingdom when the Men of Númenor arrived. Tar-Aldarion, the king, sailed up the River Gwathló and debarked to explore the Swanfleet on foot. He befriended Celebrimbor and forged alliances with the Elf-smiths, and in return they taught some among his people techniques of armour-shaping and the graving of ithildin and moon-runes. In time, Aldarion grew old and came no more to Caras Gelebren, but the friendship between his people and mine endured.
'The friendship endured, but it was tested. The Númenóreans were a sea-faring people, and they had long exhausted the forests of their island home; they hungered for timber to build more and mightier ships. The Lady Galadriel, who dwelt for a time in Eregion and often danced alongside the lily-covered waterways, despaired to see the toll taken upon the wide woodlands by Númenórean axes. When the shipbuilders began to dredge her beloved Swanfleet and build dikes to channel the waters, she entreated Celebrimbor to stop the Men of Númenor from harming the land.'

'It pained Celebrimbor to see the woods and fens so ill-treated, but he did not want to harm his alliance with the Men of Númenor. He counselled them to take greater care of the land, but his words were not heeded. Galadriel's sorrow became too great, and she turned her attention to Laurelindórenan and other distant lands.
'Celebrimbor gave up the woods as lost, turning all his attention and skill toward mastering his craft. Together, Celebrimbor and his fellowship of jewel-smiths became the most renowned workers of riches in all of Middle-earth. If they could not halt the slow degradation of the land's beauty, they would at least seek to supplement and preserve it through their craft.
'And so they were ensnared.'

'Celebrimbor had kept one of the Three for his own. At the moment that Sauron placed the Ruling Ring on his own finger, Celebrimbor knew his danger. He removed his ring, and vowed to never wear it again, lest his mind be dominated by the Dark Lord. Those of the jewel-smiths who had similarly kept rings were made to give them up, sometimes by force, and the Three Rings were sent in secret to hidden bearers. Messages were sent to Men, dwarves, and Elves in which Celebrimbor admitted his folly and warned of the coming war. So were the folk made ready to defend Middle-earth, but it would not be enough to save Eregion from the ravages of Sauron.
'The gates of Mordor opened, and the armies of Sauron came forth. He would seize as many of the Rings of Power as he could find, but the Three remained hidden to him, and he touched them not.'

'But folk crossed the river at Tharbad before the bridge was built, and it should remain possible even now that the bridge is gone. We will travel north-west to Tharbad and see for ourselves, ${PLAYER}. Let us meet in the shadow of the broken bridge on the southern bank.'
'If you are making for Cardolan you'll need to cross the river at Tharbad. I'll be staying here where it's warm and dry!'

'Do not think this question too forward, but I must ask it: you are dressed as I was told the Dúnedain Rangers dress, well-suited for a life in the wilderness of the inhospitable north. Are you one of this kind? For they are the folk I seek, and my errand is urgent.'

'I feared I had offended him, but I tried not to brood upon it. I had not called upon him at his home, after all. If he should leave his tower and the vale of Isengard to interrupt my quest, let him bear the burden of my unpracticed tongue. I am a fighting man, as I have said before, and am unused to the ways of Wizards.
'I resumed my journey. I was already a long way from Gondor, but there was longer to go.'

'My obligation to call upon Théoden satisfied as best as could be managed, I left Edoras and continued my journey. I would pass through the Gap of Rohan and then turn north for lands I had never seen.'

'But as I neared the Fords of Isen, to my surprise I encountered someone I had not expected to see.

Though he was denied an audience with Théoden, Boromir spoke with several members of his court.

'Long has my father kept watch upon the Black Land of Mordor, and at his command the soldiers of Minas Tirith never relaxed their vigil. The Steward's commands are respected, as is right, but what man from the high walls of Minas Tirith could not see smoke rising from Mount Doom, far away and yet still too near? In the taverns of the city they named it a fell portent, and in the high chambers of council, my father agreed with his folk, though they knew it not.
'But none could have foreseen the onslaught that emerged from Mordor. A great force swept through Ithilien, driving our soldiers before it, and at Osgiliath we slowed its approach for as long as we could, and destroyed the bridge behind us.
'There was something strange about that battle, my friends. There were... strange omens... before and during the fighting, but neither my brother Faramir nor I could understand their meaning. We spoke of them to our father.'

'My father is wise in ways I could never be, for I am in my very bones a fighting man; the stories with which I grew up shaped me to be this. But the Steward of Gondor must be a learned man if he is to guide Gondor through such troubled times as these. What the name \qImladris\q meant to my father he would not say, only that it was a place far to the north where lived Elrond the Halfelven, who was said to be the greatest of the lore-masters of Middle-earth, canny and dangerous. \qFew or none in Gondor know where this place might be found,\q my father told us.
'My brother Faramir volunteered at once to seek out this place, and to ask Elrond Halfelven if he might know the meaning of the... many strange portents... we had seen in recent days. I knew the road would be full of danger, and took the journey for myself. My father was most wroth at my choice, and he argued against it, but at last he gave me leave to depart. He must have seen that I could find the secret dale in which Imladris lies and bring back knowledge to aid Gondor.'

'Before I set forth, my father impressed upon me the need for secrecy. \qEnemies could lurk anywhere, my son,\q he told me. \qRemember that Gondor needs you. Return with the knowledge the Halfelven can provide, as quickly as you can. More quickly, if you deem the quest to be a foolhardy one!\q
'I assured him I would not abandon the quest, and departed at first light, taking the west road into Rohan.'

'I don't want any trouble! Can you just leave me alone?'

'Our first destination will be the town of Herne, a village of farmers and traders that grew up at a crossing of the ways to the north-west of here, where the Greenway coming south meets with the road coming north out of Enedwaith.'

'Four nights ago, something... evil... passed through the centre of Herne. No one knows exactly what it might have been, but every night since a terrible fear has seized the town. Old man Aberthol says he saw something that first night, but... I don't know. He was an adventurer in his younger days, but he has such a reputation for tale-spinning that it has always been hard to tell the truths from the falsehoods in his stories.
'But something happened that night, and the town has not been the same ever since. You had best be moving on, you and your friends, before the dark comes again.'

'I have seen something like this before, ${PLAYER}. Well, I say \qseen,\q but I did not see it; say instead that I felt it, something dark and evil; it filled man and horse with dread. We stood in defence of the river at Osgiliath when this presence came upon us, and even the boldest among us were seized by a terrible fear. We cast down the bridge behind us, and only a few of us escaped.
'I have never felt a fear like that before, ${PLAYER}. Some of my men claimed they saw the figure from which the terror spread... but I do not know if I believe it. Might that evil have come north from Gondor, somehow? I did feel as if I were being watched at times as I rode through the empty lands... or were they not as empty as they appeared?
'I should speak with the old man the innkeeper mentioned. If his story matches those of my soldiers... that will tell me something of the evil that came to Herne.'
'If this man speaks true, it sounds as if some evil came to Herne... but what could it have been?'
'Some evil passed through Herne, but the ill feeling remained behind? What does it mean?'

'Our first destination will be the town of Herne, a village of farmers and traders that grew up at a crossing of the ways to the north-west of here, where the Greenway coming south meets with the road coming north out of Enedwaith. When last I came this way, the tavern at Herne was a pleasant enough place, although it could not truly compete with the Prancing Pony for entertainment and company. Crossway House it was called, a two-story building near the south gate.
'Let us be off.'
'These tavern names are so quaint. Crossway House? Prancing Pony? None of them will compare to the Mûmak and Keep of my city.'
'To Herne, then! Am I saying that correctly?'

'Four nights past, after the setting of the sun, I left my home to walk along the cobbled streets of Herne, as is my custom. This I have done for years, every night, ever since I gave up the adventuring life. You may think it odd, but I have found these moonlit strolls to keep something of my old wanderlust at bay. \qPerhaps this is the night I keep a-walking, Aberthol, old fellow?\q I've asked myself on occasion, but thus far I have always come back to my home and sleep comes quickly.
'But on that night, while strolling along the lane west of my home, smelling the night-flowers and listening to the sound of frogs down by the river-bank, I could sense that something was different. I can't tell you exactly what it might have been, but I was seized by a tremendous feeling of... I don't know... wrongness. I felt it in the pit of my stomach. There is a grassy place on the left between two buildings along that lane, and a single tree grows there. My eye was drawn to that tree, and as I watched I swear to you a deeper shadow moved out from behind the trunk.
'It made a strange sound as it moved, a whispering just beyond the edge of my hearing. It reminded me of being lost in distant woods, stalked by a dangerous creature I could not yet see, but this was no mountain-lion. I drew on all my reserves of courage, I tell you, and I turned to run, but even as my muscles tensed I knew it was too late. While I stood transfixed by the creeping shadow in front of me, a second dark figure had come up behind. This one towered above me, for it sat astride a great black steed, but I could not tell you how I had not heard the sound of its hooves on the cobbles as it approached.
'I must have fainted then, for the next thing I remember is being shaken awake by Bledri, one of the townspeople, carrying a lantern. He said he found me lying at the base of the tree between those two buildings on his way home, and with no sign of either dark figure anywhere about. But every night since, a terrible sensation of dread has fallen upon Herne as the sun disappears beneath the horizon.
'Do you know what they were, friends? Has anything of this sort been seen in Gondor or in Rohan? What business could draw such terrible creatures to Herne?'

'What did you learn from the old man, ${PLAYER}?'
You tell Meneldir of Aberthol's frightening night-time encounter. He frowns and strokes his beard.
'This does align with the story Boromir told us about the power he sensed at Osgiliath, but that is leagues away... what has brought it here a-horse at such speed? I may know one name of these creatures, but I will not speak it here.'
He turns to the innkeeper.
'Maddoc, might I ask you to open your doors to all the townsfolk of Herne this evening? Some evil has left its mark upon the village, and I think it would be safest if the townsfolk sheltered behind the strong walls of Crossway House tonight.'
Meneldir turns back to you.
'As for us, ${PLAYER}, I think we should hunt some game in Sedgemead to resupply Maddoc's pantry, gather up firewood so we can keep the town braziers burning all night, and bring word to the townspeople that they should shelter within Crossway House tonight. What say you to this plan? I will not leave these people undefended... I cannot.'

'You want the townsfolk to shelter within Crossway House tonight?
'If I hadn't found old Aberthol lying on the ground the night this started happening, I might think it wasn't necessary, stranger. But I believe something evil had him in its clutches, and it only departed when I drew near with my lamp.
'I will tell my neighbours your plan.'

'You want the folk of Herne to shelter within Crossway House tonight?
'If I hadn't felt the terrible dread that settles upon Herne when the sun goes down, I might object, stranger. But I will do as you say, and let my neighbours know to do the same. Something is not right in Herne.'

'Shelter in Crossway House tonight? Preposterous! My family will do as we have always done, stranger, and stay in our own home. There's a bad feeling about Herne of late, it is true, but with my door barred and the candles snuffed, my family has nothing to fear.
'Others can do as they will, but we will not cower in the tavern all night. This is some scheme of Maddoc's to fill his coffers, you mark my words! And old Aberthol has always been mad, ask anyone.
'Now good day to you, and do not bother me again!'

'The feeling of dread grows stronger! Prepare yourselves!
'Something approaches!'

'There's nothing out there, ${PLAYER}.

'I told you of the assault upon Osgiliath in the days of June, did I not, and of the strange omens surrounding the battle? One of these was a dream, a dream with the feel of prophecy. This I withheld from you, for I did not know what to think; in Gondor we rely upon the bright sword and the sturdy shield, and we are right to do so! A dream is a fleeting thing, and what man would put his trust in something that lives only in darkness, and vanishes with the sunrise?'
Boromir strokes his beard thoughtfully.
'I say dreams are fleeting, but this one was peculiar. It came to my brother Faramir on the eve of the attack upon Osgiliath, and then many nights afterward, always the same. It came once to me, and although my brother told me of the dreams, it was with mine own eyes that I beheld these details; they seem so real to me.
'In the dream I saw the eastern sky growing dark, and there was a rumbling as of thunder. But a light lingered in the western sky, and a clear voice called to me. \qSeek for the Sword that was broken,\q it said, \qin Imladris it dwells. There shall be counsels taken stronger than Morgul-spells.\q
'That is of great interest to any son of Gondor, ${PLAYER}! Any means of countering the evils that pour from the Morgul Vale are welcome in Minas Tirith! But the voice did not stop there. Speaking of Imladris, it continued.
'\qThere shall be shown a token that Doom is near at hand, for Isildur's Bane shall waken, and the Halfling forth shall stand.\q'
Boromir stares at you solemnly.
'For my brother to dream of this doom, the doom of Minas Tirith, on so many nights... and then for the same dream to come to me... I fear that we are running out of time. Gondor needs the wisdom that lies hidden in Imladris. But now we waste the hours hiding in this inn, when we should be moving ever onward!'
'It is over, ${PLAYER}. We are alive.'

'It is a relief to me that so many of Herne's folk listened to us, ${PLAYER}. I hope the walls of Crossway House prove strong enough to keep them safe... or that the evil has moved on, and this plan is made unnecessary. But I cannot risk that.
'These first hours have not been difficult for the people of Herne, for Maddoc made the wise decision to let his ale flow freely, and to set plenty of food upon his tables. The real test will come in the hours ahead.
'Will you speak with some of the folk here in Crossway House and determine their mood?'

'I have not seen Crossway House this busy for many months! Would that it could be in better circumstance.
'Some of my neighbours believe this is some scheme of mine, cooked up to increase my custom. Ha! If only I could claim to have thought of it! Alas, I am not that smart.
'It does seem as if nothing will come to Herne this night. Still, you and your companions have my thanks. It is better to be safe than it is to be sorry, yes?'

'There's nothing out there. At least, nothing I can see.
'I have given myself a couple frights already tonight, when the wind kicks up and throws back the shutters on the inn. But that is all... for now, anyway.
'I am glad to be in here with my neighbours, and not out there in the dark!'

'It is comforting to be inside on a night such as this, even if whatever came here before does not return.
'Sometimes, the conversation ebbs, and I think I can hear wailing outside the walls of the inn. But that's just my imagination... or perhaps it is the wind.
'We are safe in Crossway House, I hope. Your companions have their weapons, and so do you. You will keep us safe, if anything happens. Won't you?'

'I will tell you the honest truth, ${PLAYER}, for you and your companions have my respect, and I cannot keep secrets from you. I wish I had not come here tonight. Maddoc has been free with his spiced beer, and I appreciate it, but that changes nothing.
'I can see in the eye of my mind the crawling shape I encountered that night in town, and I know that if I look over my shoulder I will see its companion, sitting astride a steed black as night! They are waiting just outside the walls of the inn, waiting for me to emerge!
'Oh... I am sorry... it's just such a strong feeling. I was an adventurer, and now I am undone by the faintest whisper of a memory! I am shamed. There are so many folk here, and some of them heroes: Boromir of Gondor, Egfrith of Rohan... and I do not exclude you from that list, ${PLAYER}!
'Forgive me. I will find my courage. There is safety among so many good folk, after all. Those shadows will not dare to trouble us here.'

'${PLAYER}, Meneldir of the North, and Boromir of Gondor... my errand to this land is not as I told you. It is true that I was born in Faldham of the Norcrofts, and I hold the good of Rohan above all else, but my mission was not to seek the Dúnedain. Théoden King is ill, that much is true, but there is no cure to be found for his ailment, neither in the Riddermark nor in the Dúnedain's wilderness. He has grown weak, and has himself become a grave threat to the survival of Rohan! His people need a strong King, but he languishes in his sick-bed! He has forgotten the strength he once possessed, and can no longer lead the people who cry out to him! In days past perhaps he would have ridden out in glory, to die in battle and stir the hearts of the Rohirrim, but no longer.
'It was with the Wizard Saruman that I consulted on this, for he has long been a friend to Rohan, and he confirmed that which I feared: it is a weakness of the blood that troubles Théoden, and it must run too in the blood of Théodred his heir. The Wizard has much wisdom, for he has lived to see many lifetimes, and he can see that which the rest of us fail to recognize: Rohan itself suffers from an illness. He will treat this illness with a difficult remedy. He has found numerous Orcs, likely from their mountain strongholds, and prepares to send them against the kingdom. Through the crucible of this testing, the mighty men of Rohan will prove who among them is strong enough to lead. I say \qmen,\q but perhaps it will be a queen who proves able to save Rohan from this peril? The old lineages are not enough.
'Even with all his wisdom, Saruman cannot see all. When Boromir of Gondor rode near to Isengard, the Wizard sought to learn what caused the son of Denethor to depart his own land. Was Saruman's plan to save Rohan in jeopardy? He charged me to follow the son of Gondor north and to learn the purpose behind his quest. I kept a day's journey behind him, out of sight in the empty lands, but always near enough to find his course, until the crossing of the Greyflood at Tharbad. That is where I encountered you, Meneldir, and ${PLAYER}.
'It was an act of desperation to join your band, but I feared Boromir would escape my reach and I would fail my own quest. And yet I did fail, for in the brief time we journeyed together, I came to understand what drove Boromir to this land, so far from his home. He travelled these many leagues at a dream's behest, for nothing so certain as the slimmest hope that it might aid Gondor. So too is it with me and Rohan. Each of us would do the same for our own home-land.
'Even now I try to excuse my treachery, as if I could avoid judgement by not writing it down. There was more to my errand: once I learned Boromir's purpose, I was to slay him. I could not have done it in battle, for all my weapon-skill, but one of these nights, while he slept, I might have managed it.
'But I will not. I go now to bring Saruman the knowledge he craved. He will learn something from Boromir's dream, and it will need to be enough. I thought I could slay anyone, if it meant saving my kingdom, but I was wrong.
'I will command Aberthol to give you this letter in a few days. I want you to know what I have done, and not done, but I will not risk you stopping me.
'For Rohan, always,
'Egfrith.'
'I hope I have not done wrong.'

'I am sure Egfrith is fine, but it is worrisome she has not yet returned.'

'I see the print of hooves in the dirt. She must have stolen a horse in Herne and has already escaped into Minhiriath. She is beyond our reach now.

'I began this journey alone, and I must finish it alone.'
Meneldir seeks to protest, but Boromir holds up a hand.
'I have made up my mind. Egfrith's betrayal has opened my eyes to the sad truth that I can only rely upon myself. If the doom of Minas Tirith is truly at hand, I cannot risk casting aside this one chance to prevent it. I am sorry. It is for the best that I journey on to the hidden vale of Imladris... alone.
'I wish you both well! Use caution if you find yourself in the path of the evil power I felt at Osgiliath, the one that sent the Dead against Herne!
'I take my leave of you, though it leave my heart heavy... but I must. Farewell.'

'I wish it were otherwise, Boromir, but I respect your decision. Good luck to you on your journey, and I echo your words of caution!
'${PLAYER}, unless you too wish to leave me, I think we should return to the east gate of Herne before we continue in search of my friend Narndir, who will be able to guide us to the chieftain of the Dúnedain.'
'Farewell, my friends. After this I deem we will not see each other again until our journeys are done.'

'I have been thinking about Egfrith, ${PLAYER}, and about her lies. We have already been through much, and more still lies ahead... I don't want there to be any deception between us. Secrets have a way of growing when they are left in the darkness. A friend of mine described them like mushrooms, but less delicious. Aye, he was a hobbit, although that is not the only folk who appreciate cooked mushrooms!
'But I am stalling. Of course I am.'
Meneldir sighs heavily.
'I was born in Tornhad, a settlement of the Dúnedain in the Angle of Mitheithel, and I was one of that folk. I grew up playing in the woods and caves nearby, and when I came of age I swore the oath they all did: to protect the line of the king, as had been done for centuries, and to do as the chieftain of the Dúnedain and his trusted lieutenants commanded in all things.
'I failed in this, ${PLAYER}. I was commanded to keep watch on a certain house, for it was feared that trolls had come down from the mountains and might endanger the folk who lived there. I let my watchfulness lapse, and on an overcast day the trolls moved much further than anyone expected and a family was slain. I had broken my oath, and they suffered the consequence of my failure. I have not considered myself a Dúnadan since that day.
'Narndir and a few others promised to speak on my behalf to the chieftain, but my own shame burned like a fire, and I fled. I would not return to these lands unless our warning was dire... and it is. So now you know, ${PLAYER}. Judge me as you will, but the lesson of Egfrith has shown to me that it is better you know.'

'After King Artandil fell at the Deadmount,' Narndir writes, 'it was Amondir, the Lord of Tyrn Gorthad and Keeper of the Barrows, who rallied what remained of the Cardoladhrim host. Crying the King's name as he charged, Amondir rode down the fleeing men of Rhudaur. The son of Malgun was captured and later ransomed, and a costly peace between the kingdoms was purchased.
'The crown of Cardolan was offered to Amondir then, but he refused it. He would not name himself king, and instead he took the title of Prince; he would rule from Dol Ernil, his own keep in Tyrn Gorthad. The primacy of Cardolan waned, and Elendil's line now only held true in Arthedain. Amondir rode to Fornost to offer his fealty, and with the reunification of Arthedain and Cardolan beneath Argeleb, the newly-crowned King of Arnor, there was once again hope for the line of Elendil and the troubled kingdoms of the Dúnedain.
'But it would not last, for there was a power behind Rhudaur's evil, and it walked in secret.'
'The south-eastern reaches of Tyrn Gorthad? What might Narndir write of that fell place?'

'The plague of the Dead worsened,' writes Narndir, 'and even the children of Cardolan were not safe from it: countless children were stolen from their beds, or vanished from within otherwise sturdy and unyielding walls.
'Desperate to put an end to this nightmare, Prince Amondir set forth on a quest to find the cause of the Dead's unrest. He was the Lord of Tyrn Gorthad, after all, the Keeper of the Barrows. What had he to fear from the mist that settled upon the burial mounds? Was it not his people who were buried there? Were they not his own ancestors, his own kind, his own subjects?
'If he could not ease their burden and restore their restful peace, who could? Even as I write this, I find myself hoping, beyond hope, that the Lord of Tyrn Gorthad could put an end to it. But this has been my lifelong study, and I know how this tale ends... and it does not end with Amondir, for all his courage and his duty.'
'Narndir writes of a clear path leading up the northern side of Amon Firn? When you are near the top of the hill you should read the corresponding account in his journal.'

'Arthedain, Cardolan, and Rhudaur were enmeshed in bloody fighting for near all the years of their existence,' writes Narndir, 'but few battles had such a cost as the Battle of the Deadmount.
'Four hundred years after hated Eldamacil slew his brother Tarondor, another king of Rhudaur marched deep into the kingdom of Cardolan. King Malgun it was who broke the gates of Caranost at the head of an army of hill-folk. Much of the royal family was slain on that day, but Malgun was unable to find King Artandil; sensing his strength was near to over-reach, the King of Rhudaur and his armies fled across the South Downs.
'Maddened by his grief, King Artandil pursued them, and at last the soldiers of Cardolan caught up to the fleeing Rhudaurrim at a hill among the barrows. It is said they fought so fiercely that blood ran down the sides of the hill in great rivulets, and bodies filled the gullies at its feet, and when the fighting was done both Artandil and Malgun were dead, each having dealt the death-blow to each other.
'The hill is known today as the Deadmount. Red flowers bloomed there ever after, and do to this day. I picked one of these flowers on an overcast afternoon, when the sky was grey and it seemed rain must soon fall, but it never did. I enclose the flower within my journal; it will be a reminder to me that there can be beauty even in sadness.'
