Introduction to Prospecting

Prospectors mine ore-nodes to discover the raw materials hidden within. They are also adept at working the ore into ingots. Ore-nodes not only provide ore, but will often contain gems or other objects that are used by other professions. This collection profession is much-needed in Middle-earth.
<rgb=#FF00FF00>Be careful! You will need to complete the correct recipe and deliver the correct item outlined in this quest.
You will need to execute the smelt copper recipe and deliver a copper ingot. Failing to do so will force you to obtain new raw materials or to restart the quest after a 24-hour delay.</rgb>
'You should speak with the chief supplier at once.'

'First, ensure your <rgb=#FF00FF00>prospector's pickaxe</rgb> is equipped, then open the <rgb=#FF00FF00>crate</rgb> of ingredients that I gave you and make your way to the <rgb=#FF00FF00>forge</rgb>.'
<rgb=#FF00FF00>Ingredients for prospectors are found in chests, gathered from ore-nodes, and purchased from suppliers. You can also find ingredients in the Auction Hall.</rgb>

'Good work, so far. Get your hands back to work and refine that <rgb=#FF00FF00>copper ingot</rgb>.'
<rgb=#FF00FF00>To open your crafting panel, you can use the 'T' key or click on the crafting button (it looks like a hammer and anvil) in the lower left part of your UI.
Select the Prospecting tab in the craft UI and find the proper recipe.
Remember: in order to execute a recipe you must be near the proper facility. Prospecting requires a forge.</rgb>

'So you'd like to learn about prospecting? It can be a lucrative profession if you're willing to put in the effort.
'I'll walk you through the basics. If at any point you get confused, speak to me and I'll explain things again.
'I almost forgot the most important thing for every new prospector -- ingredients. Everything you need is inside this <rgb=#FF00FF00>crate</rgb>.
'Open it up, ensure your <rgb=#FF00FF00>prospector's pickaxe</rgb> is equipped, then make your way to the <rgb=#FF00FF00>forge</rgb>.'
<rgb=#FF00FF00>Suppliers provide the secondary ingredients necessary for Prospectors to refine the materials that they collect. As this is a collection profession there are no additional recipes to purchase as all are learned as you advance.</rgb>

'Let me see what you have done.'
She examines the item closely.
'The copper ingot appears to have been refined without a hint of impurity.
'Well done. Weaponsmiths and armoursmiths would be happy to forge something from work as good as this. You have the makings of a fine prospector.'
'Do you have the copper ingot I requested? Please make one then bring it to me for inspection.'
You should speak with the chief supplier to learn more about prospecting.

<rgb=#FF00FF00>Ingredients for prospectors are found in ore-nodes in the wild, sometimes in chests, and purchased from suppliers. You can also find ingredients in the Auction Hall.</rgb>
The supplier provided you with a <rgb=#FF00FF00>crate</rgb> full of ingredients that you can use to execute the prospector recipe. Open the <rgb=#FF00FF00>crate</rgb> to get the ingredients.

The Chief Supplier provided you with the ingredients necessary to create a <rgb=#FF00FF00>copper ingot</rgb>.
<rgb=#FF00FF00>To open your crafting panel, you can use the 'T' key or click on the crafting button (it looks like a hammer and anvil) in the lower left part of your UI.
Select the Prospecting tab in the craft UI and find the proper recipe.
Remember: in order to execute a recipe you must be near the proper facility. Prospecting requires a forge.</rgb>
The recipe is complete. <rgb=#FF00FF00>Do not sell the copper ingot!</rgb> It is time to show your handiwork to your mentor, the chief supplier.

A report of the activity at Amon Firn must be brought to the Ranger Taeras.
Talk to Taeras
Talk to Edrud

Calargyl has asked you to bring a report to Taeras of what occurred at Amon Firn.
Taeras is at the Scurloc Farm, in north-eastern Cardolan.

Taeras has suggested that you speak with Edrud Scurloc.
Edrud is at the Scurloc Farm, in north-eastern Cardolan.

'Well met. I am indeed Taeras. You may give me Calargyl's report.'
You tell Taeras what transpired at Amon Firn.
'Troubling times these are, but glad I am that we have one such as yourself to aid us. You have come at a fortuitous time to this farmstead as well. I came after hearing rumours of goblins and displaced farmers. We Rangers do what we can to shield these folk from outside intrusions, but our number are few and the enemies are many.
'Go and speak with the Scurloc and Hove families, if you have not yet already done so. They definitely could use your help.'

'Who are you?! What do you want? We might be missing folk, but I won't let you take what's left!
'Oh, you're not here to steal anything? I suppose you don't look like a goblin.'
She takes a shuddering breath and her shoulders slump.
'Aye, I am Edrud Scurloc. If you've come to help, you're just in time.'

'You have acted admirably in the defence of Cardolan, but I would impose a boon upon you, if you are willing. I need to make a report of the activity that we have seen here, but I also do not think it is time yet to give up my post.
'Will you bring word of what you saw and did here to my companion Taeras? He has gone on ahead to a farm that is west of here, chasing troubling rumours.'
A Report for Taeras

Village in the Sky

'That's the one! Thank you for retrieving this for me. The brigands have been pestering us folk for a while and I feared our family might lose it. Please deliver this to my cousin Gwenfor in Glyn Helyg.
'Now, the way to Glyn Helyg is very rough. I cannot personally show you the way. But I have an acquaintance that could. Follow the road east across the river and speak to Cranog Dambryn.
'They wander along the banks close to a watermill looking for odd trinkets.'

'Looking for Glyn Helyg, are ya? You and everyone else. The ruffians out of Radlaw have been causing all kinds of chaos for the Stoor-vales. How do I know you are not one of them?
'Tell you what. If you can stir up some trouble in Radlaw and perhaps teach a few of those ruffians a thing or two, I will show you the way to Glyn Helyg.
'Sound like a deal?'

'Ah, Leri sent you? Judging by your face, I'd say you are quite disappointed.
'This is indeed Glyn Helyg. And no, it is not a floating village. I'm going to have to give Leri what for!
'Ever since they left to go on their adventures, they've been spreadin' all kinds of fantastical rumours about this place. Tellin' all manner of folk that our humble town floats in the sky overlooking the river.
'You are not the first to appear to me with such despair. But enough about them. Thank you for deliverin' the parcel.
'It's quite important to our family.'

'Word travels fast in the Stoor-vales. Ruffians are in a panic in response to your actions.
'All right. I'll tell you how to find Glyn Helyg. You know the road you took to get here? Follow it north.
'I have left trail markers along the way for you to find the secret entrance to Glyn Helyg. They will point you in the right direction.
'If you follow the trail markers precisely, you should be able to find Glyn Helyg.'

'I have no problem with Rhiangar, and I wish she would warm up to me. I have made sure to care for her dear father in her absence, but Cadwallon missed her a great deal.
'It has been so difficult for him since the accident. Well, his troubles go back decades before that, to when his wife ran off. Oh, I should not speak of it.'

'You found it! What memories this brings back! After mother disappeared, I would pore over her written words for hours, searching for some clue as to where she went. I never believed she left us on purpose, as my father insists. No, I think she met some darker fate.
'The stew needs to cook over a low fire for many hours, and I also wish to check on the townsfolk and see how they are faring. Will you meet me at the Crossway House? Many people are still holed up in the inn, taking comfort from one another.'
'Thank you for meeting me here! The town is still reeling from the passage of those black riders. I want to help wherever I can. If you have time, perhaps you, too, could lend some aid.'

'Well, what did they say? Oh, Osian cared for my father in my absence, did he? I did not realize my father needing tending until now. No, he is a grown man and was capable when I left. I will not let that guilt creep in and take away the joy I had in travelling and studying in Bree.
'But what my father said is intriguing. Mother was going to look at ruins? His words are stirring a memory within me! ${PLAYER}, will you do me a favour and look for my mother's journal? It should be on the shelf in my father's library.'

'Why are you still here?! Hmph, well the wine is welcome, even if you are not. No offence meant, but my daughter does not need someone like you around giving her crazed ideas. She already ran off to the big city and abandoned her duties and me. She is back, but for how long?
'Her mother was the same way. Never content to settle down. Always running off to look at crumbled fortresses and searching for Elves and the little folk down south in Swanfleet.'

'While you were taking apart the bed, father had a guest arrive, as I am sure you noticed. That is Osian Beddow, and I am certain that he is the reason father was down at Tharbad, snooping around. I suspect he is also the reason father got injured years ago. Osian has always wanted to be Mayor, and though he whispers honeyed words into father's ears, his actions have led me to believe he is more of a wasp than a bee.
'Well, I have some work yet to do on the stew. Will you bring the wine to the table? Oh and, perhaps you could speak with them? I want to know what is going on, but Osian and I are not on speaking terms, and father clamps his mouth shut as soon as I enter the room.'

'Aye, I have abandoned my idea of using those craban feathers. A number of uses? 'I suppose the good ideas that spring up in autumn... well, they fall when winter comes. I'd rather deal with the threat of Uruk war-bands loose in the Swanfleet than present my wife with another one of my brand-new ideas! 'You know the road that passes through Swanfleet, of course. It begins on this side of the old city of Tharbad and runs east past the Wadewater until it reaches Enedwaith. There are not as many travellers along it as once there were, but Mossward is still a sheltered place of rest for those who come this way. Might it also serve to speed Uruks and other Orc-kind on their raids?
'Will you follow the track that runs from the north gate of Mossward until it meets up with this road? Once there, I would appreciate if you took a <rgb=#00FF00>look</rgb>, as you did before. You should be able to see both east and west for quite a distance, and if there are more raiders about, you might see them.'

'You say you saw no sign of Uruk war-bands along the road? These are good tidings, for it means the road is still a boon for Mossward, and not a bane, as I feared it might become.
'That road has been key to Mossward's survival for my entire life, ${PLAYER}. The portion of it we know begins at Tharbad, and although the road itself is broken in places and obscured by foliage, it runs through Swanfleet and passes on into Enedwaith. From there it enters Dunland, leads through the Gap of Rohan, and continues on into Gondor. They say it passes Minas Tirith and eventually ends at a port-city along the coast, although I have never journeyed in that land.
'North of Tharbad the road has another name. It is called the Greenway, and only Meneldir's people are like to remember when it and our own Old South Road were one and the same: the North-South Road between the kingdoms of Arnor and Gondor. That was long ago, even by their reckoning.'

'Will you follow the track that runs from the north gate of Mossward until it meets up with the road that runs east and west through Swanfleet? 'It is true, ${PLAYER}, that boot was one half of a pair that was dearest to my heart: they were my adventuring boots! They represent a life that I gave up to settle down with my wife Wenna, and now I only want to relive those days by telling tales of my exploits to my son Teg. Now these boots are my least-favourite, for they remind me of those days, and sometimes the memory is painful. I thought I would \qlose\q one of them; better that than have Wenna think I regret the choice I made to settle down!
'But here it is again, and it seems I will never be free of it! Did I not bring it far enough away? That must be it. Perhaps you could bring this boot further afield? Why not show it to one of the villagers in the Stoor-vales? That is pretty far away, and one of the residents of Clegur might be able to find a use for such an old, well-worn boot as this.'

'That is an interesting artifact you carry! It must have quite a story, I imagine!'
You tell Briallen Wynbuch about Geralt's complicated feelings about the boot, and about Wenna's belief that it remains her husband's favourite.
'Well, unlike some folk of other villages in the Stoor-vales, I believe that it is always best to be honest... but if you can't manage that, for one reason or another, then perhaps a compassionate solution is second best!'
Briallen produces a pretty flower from somewhere about her person, scoops up a handful of earth, and puts both inside the well-worn boot.
'You bring this back to our former adventurer's wife, and tell her that her husband asked for the Stoors to craft this delightful little planter. Perhaps it isn't the most honest of solutions... but I think in this way everyone might be made happy, and that is pretty good too, wouldn't you say?'
'Perhaps one of the villagers of Clegur will have some interest in that boot? That is pretty far away.'

'What is this?'
Wenna takes the old boot with the flower sticking out of it, a huge smile lighting up her face.
'What a beautiful gift! Oh, my Geralt! What a dear man he is, and so thoughtful for him to give up his favourite boot for this delightful little planter! This is the finest anniversary gift I could have imagined! Do you know I had believed he'd forgotten?
'I simply must have Skardí fashion a replacement boot in this exact style for my dear Geralt. Thank you again, ${PLAYER}. Our family is in your debt, for so many reasons!'

None of the town guards will be able to learn anything... you know how children are... but perhaps an outsider will be able to learn something?
'Several children lingered outside the provisioners' store-house a few minutes ago, and it could be one of the provisioners overheard some of their talk? We need to get to the bottom of this before someone gets hurt, ${PLAYER}.'

'A group of children? Aye, I saw them. They were hoping to get their hands on as much cheese as possible, which seemed a little odd to me. I did not give them as much as they requested, but I thought one small block from the store-house each would be fine.
'Those kids have been through a lot, what with the Uruk raid on Mossward, and I have seen few problems that could not be helped with cheese!'

'What are you doing here, ${PLAYER}? I thought you would have left Mossward by now. You had better get going, I think. So long!'
You stand your ground and ask Alla why the children of Mossward needed so much cheese from the store-house. Her eyes grow wide and a panicked expression crosses her face.
'We aren't in trouble, are we? It's just that we finally managed to turn the tables on the town bully, and you helped us do it! If we're in trouble, I think you should be also... it's only fair!
'You see, there's a boy named Dai, and he's always challenging us to these dares, and if we don't complete them then we look like cowards! You point out to the girl that she didn't complete any of the dares, since she got the information from you instead, but that Dai apparently did go to each of those places first to leave the items.
'I feel like this just means I'm very smart, ${PLAYER}, wouldn't you say? But because we completed those last two dares... don't argue with me, it still counts... then Dai has to fill his pockets with cheese and walk through Mossward.'
You ask the girl if she has considered that she might be the town bully after all, and she tips her head to one side, considering it.
'Huh. No, I don't think so. But I'll think it over.'
'The children gave no reason they wanted cheese. Does anyone really need a reason?'

'And uh,'
He leans in to whisper.
'Don't worry about the old man. I'll keep him company.'
'The racks of drying fish are behind me on the pier. Throw the salt I gave you at them. Just a thin coat will do.'

'All done? Thanks. And sorry about earlier. This has been a tough time for me... for all of us.

'I heard you and the scouts ran into some trouble. Tell me about it.'
You summarize your recent experiences. Madog heaves a sigh and continues speaking, though not to you or seemingly anyone in particular.
'Part of why I wanted to help establish this place, our Lhan Garan, was the hope to see our young people grow up away from the tragedy our homeland is experiencing now. I guess it followed us here. Maybe it was a fool's hope all along.'

'Hail, hail and well met indeed! Are you come from Sírlond? What a relief!
'I have been stuck down here for days! I managed to slip away from my captors and hide down here, but they're looking for me and patrol above incessantly. I feared I would never escape, but now you are here!
'I can make my own way out of here, but I need a distraction. When I was leading them on a chase a few days ago, I saw a curious crate in the tower above these steps. I believe that lighting that box with fire will create a fantastic explosion! If you do that, the patrolling guards will be distracted long enough for me to make my escape. Will you help me?'

'Hail again! This time under much better circumstances. Thank you for my rescue, and for bringing me back my horse, chewed though he seems to be. We would have both been gnawed upon much more, were it not for your help.'

'Well met again, my new friend! Mellanion has returned and brought word of your deeds! There are not enough words to thank you for what you have done! Additionally, while you were gone, a scout came back with news of Annaethel! She was found in the ruins south of here, but ran off when approached.
'I see you found the boy's hobby horse also. I think we can use this to help us get through to his mother!
'Give the toy back to Mellanion. I have an idea.'

'We have been here at Sírlond looking into the situation with the Orcs and, more recently, the restless dead. Though I encouraged her to leave him at home, Annaethel insisted on bringing her youngling, Mellanion. The child went missing during an Orc attack. Annaethel was convinced he survived, but after a few days of not finding him she took the loss very deeply.
'Annaethel's grief could not be lightened, and with it came a madness I have never seen before. She took to wandering away from our camp, and vanished one night. I have been searching for her and Mellanion ever since, and I am overjoyed that you have found her! My heart trembles, however, thinking that she has lured away someone else's child.
'I fear for Annaethel's safety, but even more for that of her child. I dare hope that he yet lives, but if that is true, he is a captive of the Orcs who dwell throughout Caranost. Due to their numbers, I am unable to penetrate the crumbled city, but perhaps you will succeed where I have failed! Please, look for signs of Mellanion.'

'Hail, stranger. You bring joyous tidings! Long have I wandered with a fell gloom blinding my eyes, but now that light has passed and my thoughts are mine once more! My son is safe and nearby! He is at Sírlond, you say? I will go there at once!
'Come and find me in Sírlond, and I shall reward you for all of your efforts!'

'Well met, honoured friend. You have done so much for my family, and for me! I thank you a thousand times over, and it is not enough. Please, take this as well as my gratitude. You brought my son back to me. You brought me out of my madness. How could I ever repay you enough?'

'My mother's grief is a dangerous thing. Here, take back my hobby horse. I have attached a letter to its bridle, letting mother know that I am safe and well.
'Grethron said my mother is at the ruins south of here, but he will not let me go to her. Please! You must find her before she is able to lure away any more children.'

'Impressive, no? Anyhow - you may be wondering why I asked you for the bird wings and why there's a rock tied to my favourite handkerchief. You see…'
He pauses dramatically, lowering his voice to a whisper.
'I am going to be the first hobbit to fly like a bird! I have been experimenting and studying things that fly. Birds, handkerchiefs that aren't weighed down by rocks… those sorts of things. My experiments have not quite garnered the results I was hoping for, but I have a new plan that is sure to work!
'Here is where you come in. I need you to gather some materials for me. If I go about doing it myself, there will be no end of questions and interruptions! I need the straightest branch you can find, rope, and the purple canvas that's hanging on one of the houses at the base of the southern cliffs.
'We are going to build a larger kite than anyone has ever seen before, and then I am going to leap from this edge like an eagle, and soar over Stoor-vales! You just wait and see!'

'Oh hullo! I see you managed to gather all of the things I needed for the kite. Well, ahem, you took too long and I got hungry and… I suppose I will have to put off flying for today. Eirlys baked an incredible apple pie for me and it would be rude to let it go cold. I might try flying tomorrow, we'll see.
'Maybe from a nearby hill, instead of…'
He looks up to the cliffs and swallows.
'…up so high.'
'Ah, you made it! Come, come, look over yonder! Is it not marvellous! On clear days you can see all the way to Tharbad! Right, maybe not, but is it not still a wonder? Go on ahead and take a look!'

Speak with the emissaries

'The Krahjarn are born to lead. We remember the wars against the first. We recall the first lash against our backs and how to revisit that on our lessers. We know what it means to lead, to oversee the battle, to watch the flow of a fight, when to inspire and when to instill fear.'
He snarls.
'We know what makes a maggot a maggot and how to make a whelp a warrior. Stand alongside us, whelp and we'll make you a warrior yet.'

'The Scara know the hunt, the strength of a sudden strike, the panic you instill from the shadow, and the tastiest, easiest places to tear flesh from bone. We teach the pack the way and it is for the warg or any to do the rest.'
He shakes his fur.
'We need only brutality and cruelty to bring down our targets quickly and as painfully as possible. Our pack can teach you, but you must do the rest. We waste time by standing still. Choose us and run free.'
'Off with you until you have spoken to each of the emissaries. Return to me when you are done. I shall instruct you further.'

'Well done, I am amazed you had the attention span necessary to speak with them all. There may be hope for you yet. Now to the matter at hand. Choose. Choose a clan to represent while you fight for Angmar.
'All will welcome you. Freely shirk your allegiance like you have done your duty for so long. Drink of their blessing until you find a home that is welcoming to you. They are ordered to show no malice toward each other for now. This truce may not hold forever.
'Mordirith wants to see these Free Folk brought low, so the clans were convened to find the strongest among you and then to determine the best way to eliminate the forces here. Align yourself. That is all you need to do.'
She smiles deviously.
'Do your best to prove to the master what clans should remain here in the Ettenmoors fighting and slaughtering the Free Folk.'

'Far be it from the Krahjarn to deny protocol. What, you think we're all war hungry tyrants like Akúlhun?'
He smirks.
'We are... some of us just hide it better. Talk with Malavin. That is the command. We will abide.'
'The pack is eager to hunt. The human is a barrier to our victory. Speak with her quick and then return to me.'

'I am Fathrug, and you look like you are ready to tear the flesh off a man. That is all we ask. Find the Men. Flay the Men. Leave their carcases littering the earth to turn the grass bloody. The Tarkrîp clan will strengthen your skills, help you stay in the fight longer. You'll be rather brutal about your business of hacking and rending the enemy, and while we won't teach you how to dodge a really nasty sword blow, we'll teach you to shrug it off and keep going.
'The Tarkrîp clan prizes scrappy warriors above all else, willing to strike at the enemy relentlessly!'

'You look soft, maggot. I should know the Ongbúrz are the heartiest clan in all of Angmar. We are not afraid of battle. We thrive in it. We revel in the clash of hammers, axes, and all the tools those bearded bastards bring against us. We know little fear. Our prowess in in our staying power.
'If you want to swing your blade wildly without thought about tomorrow, go talk with the Tarkrîp or the dogs. If you want to stand tall above all the others then take our blessing into battle. Toughness like ours should never be underestimated.'

'Come closer. Smell that? Mushrooms. Slime. Herbs. Poultices. The trappings of healers. Oh, yes, the other clans will tell you that they are the most stalwart, or furious, or violent, or sinister, but we are the force that keeps them standing. We are the strength behind them all.'
He chuckles.
'Half the pain that they don't feel is because of our stinking sludges and fungal brews. We know how to pound a spike into a missing arm if things go terribly ill, too. Sometimes the victim even survives long enough to make it more permanent.
'The others will tell you tales, but it is we that let them keep tongues wagging. Without us, they'd all be face down in the dirt. Stand with us. Stand with the Blogmal Clan.'

'She is born of the first enemy of Elves. She feeds her brood well and gives them all they need to spread the faith of the Dark Lord. Gifts that sting deeply, secretly, and brutally. Her poison courses to seep into the flesh and twist it to the darkness where she dwells.'
The queen chitters.
'She burns the victims from within so they sting, sting, sting, longer and more painfully. She is the corruption that seeds the earth with malicious intent. She is mother to her brood. Join with her and earn the gift to inflict suffering most profound.'

'Sharkey orders us north to help figh, so we come. We see why these clans fail. Too unbalanced. Too dedicated to destruction, or defence. Too dedicated to mysticism or the darkness.'
He shakes his head.
'No temperance leads to a quick end. Learning the field of battle, discerning the weakness and strengths of your enemy provides a clearer path to victory. It is an even path we walk. It is the teaching of our master that we prize. The method to strike hard, the method to stand tall, the method to withstand a strike and turn a blade.
'I would lead the White Hand against any of these other clans and leave them in shambles. Join us and you will see what I mean.'

War-tyrant Akúlhun directed you to the war tent to speak with an Angmarim sorceress there named Malavin. Apparently she is here to assist, inspect, or guide the war effort. Whatever her purpose, it does not sit well with the War-tyrant.

'Just what I need. A sorceress come from the north to tell me how the fight goes. Oh, she has the ear of the steward, but the arms are here, in the Ettenmoors. We've been fighting while they've been locked away in castles and steel barricades. What do they know about battling these people?'
It is a question that requires no answer.
'Bah... leadership back in Carn Dûm is looking for a new way to off these pesky Free Folk. So we got some new tricks available, meat. Each clan, and even the dirty dogs and sticky little spiders got their own emissaries here to help you new gits out. Oh and those southron Uruks too... talk to one of them and they'll give you a taste of what the leaders are thinking... don't get used to it though, maggot. These truces can only last so long....
'But first, they want me to send every maggot with snot dripping on their face up the hill to talk with her. Well... so be it. Better you go talk to her than me. She calls herself Malavin.'
There is a short pause.
'If you get a chance, accidentally spit on her for me, would you?'

'Another veteran of the way, or are you a new recruit? Honestly, I cannot tell the difference between a seasoned warrior and a whelp fresh from the pens or egg. I do, however, know a thing or two about obedience and seeing that orders are carried out.'
She smirks wryly.
'Mordirith is displeased with the efforts here and organized an effort to entice you... warriors... with gifts. Each of the Orc clans, the Scara-pack, and Brood of Shelob send emissaries to entreat. He even allowed the White Hand at this table. Perhaps, in time there will be more. For now, it is these few.'
She pauses a moment to look you over.
'It appears that the steward of Carn Dûm is correct in his assessment. You are all in dire need of help. I invite you then to speak with the emissaries here in Gramsfoot. Learn what they offer you and choose their blessing. Each has been ordered, for now, to entreat with all of you, provide for you until the council of our lord is complete.
'Run along now and learn from each of the emissaries here and then return to me.'
'Orders is orders. You need to talk to the Priestess first.'
'Talk with the skinny witch, then you can talk to me.'
'Abide by the council's will and speak with Malavin.'
'Seek she who speaks for the lord of Carn Dûm. Our brood will wait our turn.'
'Sharkey's orders are clear, we let the woman speak... for now.'
Intro: Allegiance and Blessing

Malavin instructed you to speak to each of the emissaries representing the clans of Carn Dûm and beyond. They have blessings that they will seek to bestow upon you, provided you will serve in their name.
Having spoken to all the emissaries it is time to return to Malavin for further instruction.

The War-tyrant seems displeased that emissaries from Carn Dûm arrived and made their way into the war tent. His demeanor is more grim than usual, and he has instructed you to make your way to the Angmarim sorceress who now resides in the tent within the confines of Gramsfoot.
Collect stones from the walls at Sarn Ford (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Thank you for these stones, friend. There is talk of building a cairn in memory of those who died at Sarn Ford, and I think it would suit the fallen for the stones to be taken from the walls here.
'It must serve... at least until the riders in black again cross my path. Then I will have my vengeance, or I will not. But at least I will be freed of my anger.'
'My anger must remain unsatisfied, and it is sorrow instead that must serve. Will you bring me stones from the walls that line the road here at Sarn Ford? I have need of them.'
Collected stones from the walls (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'An anger burns within me, stranger. Many of my friends died defending the ford against the evil force that rode us down some days past, and I want those dreadful riders to face the heat of my vengeance.
'But they are not men. Whatever they might appear to be, I know in my heart they are not men. Could my sword even pierce their black cloaks, or the physical frames they must hide? I know not.
'So my anger must remain unsatisfied, and it is sorrow instead that must serve. Will you bring me stones from the walls that line the road here at Sarn Ford? I have need of them.'
A Need for Stones
The stone walls at Sarn Ford should not miss a few of their number.
Rothavron is at Sarn Ford.
Bring the stones to Rothavron at Sarn Ford
Rothavron has a need for stones, and he has asked you to collect them from the walls at Sarn Ford.
Defeat Idwal Redclaw in Gaervarad
Defeat Emrys Redclaw in Gaervarad
Talk to Eilian Good-heart outside Gaervarad

'Idwal and Emrys are no more? Very well done, ${PLAYER}! You have my thanks, and when I report to my village that the Redclaw brothers have paid for their crimes, you will have the appreciation of an entire village!
'Good day to you, my adventuring friend! I cannot imagine our paths will cross again, but if they do I will know that fate smiles upon me, and I should expect good fortune for all the rest of the day!'

'There are two ruffians in particular that have caused a great deal of trouble back home. They are the Redclaw brothers, Idwal and Emrys, and their crimes are too numerous to recount! Let us just say that \qRedclaw\q is not just a family name, but a description of the sort of villainy of which they are most fond!
'They are dangerous, and they are somewhere within this structure! If you can put an end to their murdering, I will have a reward for you. And you will also have the appreciation of my entire village!'
Defeated Idwal Redclaw
Defeated Emrys Redclaw

'Hello there, adventurer! I trust that is what you are, yes? Very good! I am not an adventurer, you see, but a citizen concerned with an issue I have noticed of late: the increase of bad-tempered ruffians that threaten the peace and safety of these lands!
'You may call me Missus Good-heart, if it please you, and I may call you... what? ${PLAYER}? It is a pleasure to meet you, ${PLAYER}. I came here to give these brigands a piece of my mind, but now that I have arrived I think perhaps I was a bit over-zealous. There are two ruffians in particular that have caused a great deal of trouble back home. They are the Redclaw brothers, Idwal and Emrys, and their crimes are too numerous to recount! Let us just say that \qRedclaw\q is not just a family name, but a description of the sort of villainy of which they are most fond!
'They are dangerous, and they are somewhere within this structure! If you can put an end to their murdering, I will have a reward for you. And you will also have the appreciation of my entire village!'

Talk to Rothavron at Sarn Ford

'You have done well to oppose the brigands massing at Gaervarad. I must remember that one frightening experience does not eliminate the other dangers against which we must stand! That is easier said than it is done, friend.
'Thank you for helping the people I am sworn to defend.'
'Will you go to Gaervarad and deal with the massing of the brigands? If one danger is ignored, that will be the one that overmasters us, or so says my worried heart.'
Defeated brigands at Gaervarad (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Before Sarn Ford was attacked by the terrible riders in black, we received word that brigands were gathering at Gaervarad, to the south, and we planned to dispatch a force of Rangers to deal with them. Brigands! Such foes seem so trivial now!
'But no, I speak rashly. They are still a danger to the folk who live in these lands, though my people's concerns seem more pressing in the aftermath of the attack some days gone! There is never just one thing, is there?
'Will you go to Gaervarad and deal with the massing of the brigands? If one danger is ignored, that will be the one that overmasters us, or so says my worried heart.'
Never Just One Thing
Brigands have been massing to the south, at Gaervarad in Ruddymore, and Rothavron does not want the villains to be unopposed.

Rothavron is concerned about more than just the passage of the terrible Riders.
Cross the river north-west of Sarn Ford and talk to Andy Brockhouse in the Shire
Talk to Thornegil at Sarn Ford

'Black Riders? No, I haven't seen anything like that. Did you take a knock on the head? This is the Shire, and these are peaceful days! If anyone had seen a great big group of Big Folk on horses, all galloping together, someone would have said something!
'Now, it is true that sometimes a hobbit will see something that frightens him when he's out for a nighttime stroll, but nine times out of every ten the shadow that seemed to conceal something scary will turn out to be a fallen log in the road, or a deer frozen among the trees... and that more frightened of him than he of it!
'I appreciate the concern, but we hobbits know how to handle our own business. You go back to whoever sent you here in such a hurry, and you tell them all is fine in the Shire.'

'The hobbits do not report seeing anything untoward? This does not lighten my worries, ${PLAYER}, for it means whoever commands the terrible riders does so with a purpose beyond only killing. He must have had the riders separate, so as not to attract attention. But what do they seek if it is not open battle they desire?
'I am glad that Andy and his folk still live, but I do not know what to make of the creatures that broke our lines and scattered my people. Aye, I say creatures: in the misty night they looked like men to my eyes, but my heart says they are something else, and evil.
'Be wary as you travel these lands. Some of the creatures went into the Shire, but I think some of them remained here to trouble the Rangers, and keep us from opposing them.'
'I appreciate the concern, but we hobbits know how to handle our own business. You go back to whoever sent you here in such a hurry, and you tell them all is fine in the Shire.'

'Will you cross the river and see how fare the folk of the Shire? The terrible creatures rode us down, and I fear to think what they might do to the peaceful folk across the river. Look for Andy Brockhouse and see if he still lives; he keeps watch outside some of the neighbourhoods that lie near Michel Delving.'

'My people have long protected the borders of the Shire from the dangers of the wild world, but I have never seen such evil as that which scattered my people a few days gone. Dreadful riders in black left many among the Rangers injured or dead, and some of their number passed into the Shire... I know not how many.
'Will you cross the river and see how fare the folk of the Shire? The terrible creatures rode us down, and I fear to think what they might do to the peaceful folk across the river. Look for Andy Brockhouse and see if he still lives; he keeps watch outside some of the neighbourhoods that lie near Michel Delving.'
The Watch on the Shire
Andy Brockhouse is the housing broker of Michel Delving, and can be found north-west of Sarn Ford, by the Delving Fields.
Thornegil is at the crossing of Sarn Ford, south-east of the Shire.
Thornegil fears the terrible evil that crossed into the Shire will endanger the hobbits, and she wants you to check on them.

I want to hear what can be seen from that location.'

'You could see Sírlond from that location? That is what I feared, ${PLAYER}.

'Thank you for helping keep these lands safe, ${PLAYER}. Never before in my memory have we had to deal with such evil as these riders in black possess.'

'The passage of the terrible riders across Ruddymore has done something to the animals that live here. Talk to Sirvellon at Sírlond
'I heard the fighting from here, ${PLAYER}, and I know the Orcs now count fewer warriors among their number. You have my thanks.'

'To the west, a long bridge leads into Caranost proper, where Orcs dwell in great number. If you wish to help us, you will take up arms against their warriors. Many of those who shelter here bear injuries that prevent them from bringing the fight to the Orcs, but I see that you are no stranger to combat, and do it well.'

'If you come in peace and bear a helpful heart, then I welcome you to Sírlond. My wife Maedhril and I established this camp here among the ruins of Caranost to combat the evils that threaten the old city and the surrounding lands, and our numbers have only grown in recent days. Rangers fled here following an attack upon the river-crossing to the west, and others were drawn hither by the light of our fire. I welcome all as I welcomed you.
'To the west, a long bridge leads into Caranost proper, where Orcs dwell in great number. If you wish to help us, you will take up arms against their warriors. Bring the boar-meat and lynx hides to Haerandir outside Haudh Nirui

'These supplies are from Haerandir? They are welcome... but with reservation.
'My wife's brother is always doing this. \qSirvellon, I think you should do this,\q he says, and \qSirvellon, why did you not think of this?\q If I had known the ways of her brother when I fell in love with my Maedhril... but no, it would change nothing. She has all of my love, and always will.
'It was her idea to send him scouting for goblins when the three of us came south, and it was very wise. Trust Haerandir to annoy me, even from afar! But the supplies are welcome. He is right on this point: our provisions are beginning to run out.'
Sirvellon sighs.
'And that is the worst annoyance of all, is it not? That my wife's brother was right once again!
'Are you married, ${PLAYER}? If you are not, heed well my advice: discover if your intended spouse has any siblings... and do so in advance!'
'Perhaps you will help me obtain boar-meat and lynx hides from beasts here in the South Downs? Then we can send them along to Sirvellon and Maedhril, and I will worry less about them.'

'Bring that boar-meat and those hides to Sirvellon at Sírlond with my regards, and tell him too that I maintain my watch upon the Blogmal goblins that creep in the South Downs. Sírlond is east of Caranost proper, to the south-west of here.'

'Yes, these will do nicely! This meat and these hides will help Sirvellon and Maedhril restock the provisions I am certain they failed to prepare.
'Bring them to Sirvellon at Sírlond with my regards, and tell him too that I maintain my watch upon the Blogmal goblins that creep in the South Downs. Sírlond is east of Caranost proper, to the south-west of here.'

Collected lynx hides (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'My sister Maedhril married an Elf of Imladris. His name is Sirvellon, and he led an expedition south; even now the two of them have made camp near the abandoned city of Caranost. Their camp is called Sírlond.
'Theirs is a young love, only seven hundred years by my count, and sometimes I think they are blinded to the others' faults. Sirvellon is a fine Elf, but he is more short-sighted than my sister, and I fear he is so focused upon the Orcs that he will not obtain sufficient provision to keep the camp going.
'Perhaps you will help me obtain boar-meat and lynx hides from beasts here in the South Downs? Then we can send them along to Sirvellon and Maedhril, and I will worry less about them.'

Spirits Fell and Terrible
'Whichever form these spirits take, they are dangerous, and must be ended by those of us brave enough, or foolish enough, to take the chance. If you are either of these two... I wish you luck.'

'Please allow me to apologize, stranger. I called you foolish, for sometimes there are fools who come this way, but I see now that you belong not to that number. It is courage you possess, and not madness.
'What is your name? ${PLAYER}? Then know that I am called Faradan of the Dúnedain, and Tyrn Gorthad is under my and my kinswoman Gorwen's watchful protection.'
Defeated barrow-spirits (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeated barrow-wights (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Something has stirred to madness the spirits of Tyrn Gorthad, and it is not safe for travellers to come this way. No, do not misunderstand me: these hills have not been truly safe for hundreds and hundreds of years. But I deem you are an adventurer, and can handle yourself.
'Still, these are spirits fell and terrible. Sometimes they move through the grass and rustle the branches of the bare trees, and then you know they are there. Other times they house themselves in the body of a corpse, and become the animate Dead. Whichever form they take, they are dangerous, and must be ended by those of us brave enough, or foolish enough, to take the chance. If you are either of these two... I wish you luck.'

'That was very good work, ${PLAYER}. The Blogmal will fear to speak your name from now on, I imagine. I am glad to have met you, for any foe of goblins is a friend of mine!'

'Will you help me end the threat posed by the Blogmal goblins that creep in Haudh Nirui, to the north-east? You will be doing the folk who live nearby a good service, for such creatures never stay where they begin, and a goblin-raid can be a frightening thing.'

A Pair of Empty Tombs

'Bregach and Daethos are no more? I can hardly believe it, ! Such was their evil that I would have thought them impossible to best, and yet you have done so!
'They were fearsome foes from out of legend, and now they are ended. Perhaps you are yourself to be a figure of legend, my friend. I will await the word of your further deeds, and perhaps in a day to come I will sit by a warm fire and say \qI knew ${PLAYER:her[f]|him} in earlier days, when the legend was young!\q
'Ah, perhaps, my friend. I cannot believe you faced the wight-lords and survived. What a wonder!'
'Good fortune to you if you do find yourself in Dol Ernil, ${PLAYER}. Beware of the wight-lords I have named: Bregach and Daethos.'
Defeated Bregach
Defeated Daethos

'Gorwen and I were charged with keeping the watch on Dol Ernil, further to the north, and she is surely still there. I came south to bring word that some new evil seems to be at work within the fortress. Someone... or something... is opening the tombs. I have seen two such terrible wight-lords walking beneath the moon, figures that should have remained buried away forever.
'I know the names of those I saw. Bregach is one, \qquickbone,\q and the other is named Daethos, \qshadow fear.\q They are somewhere within Dol Ernil, I know not where. If you encounter them and are able to return them to the slumber of death, you will have my deepest thanks, and the appreciation of any who live near. Few are they, for this is a land of barrows, but think of this: the Dead have no need for sleep, and do not tire. If Bregach or Daethos desired to reach a settlement of peaceful folk, what town could possibly be beyond their reach?
'Good fortune to you if you do find yourself in Dol Ernil, ${PLAYER}. Beware of the wight-lords I have named.'
Two powerful wight-lords, Bregach and Daethos, now lurk somewhere within Dol Ernil, in Tyrn Gorthad.

'Good job, my very capable friend! Those brigand raiders must surely be regretting their choice of occupation now, I would say!
'Here is your reward, as promised. I will continue north just as soon as I am able, but for now I have a few more preparations to make. Perhaps we will meet again?'

'If you can defeat some of these Greenway raiders, I could see fit to part with some of my coin. I only need you to face the brigands that are here on the road, so no need for you to pass into the South-guard Ruins; it's the villains on the road that are the problem. What do you say?'

'Ho there, friend! Are you heading north? Oh, you may want to reconsider. There are brigands all along the Greenway, and they even squat in the ruins between here and Bree-land! The South-guard Ruins, aye, they are full of brigands, and they only get even more dangerous the further north you go!
'Who am I? My name is Good-heart. Master Good-heart, to my friends, and I hope you will prove to be one of those. You see, I am only a merchant, and if I am to make my way north to Bree, I would have to pass by those ruffians! Well, in my younger days perhaps I could have done something about those villains, but sadly my sword-swinging days are likely behind me.
'But you are an adventurer! No, do not try to deny it: you have the look of one. If you can defeat some of these Greenway raiders, I could see fit to part with some of my coin. 'No... what are you doing here?'
Melona the bounty hunter stares at you with dismay. You tell her that you and Master Good-heart have put an end to Maelgun Redclaw, leader of the brigands that blockade the Greenway. She shakes her head in disbelief.
'Am I to be so plagued with ill fortune? How many bounties am I cursed to lose because of your interference? \qMaster Good-heart?\q Do you mean Geralt Goodblossom, noted ruffian?'
You tell Melona that Geralt is a very common name, possessed by many folk in the south, and it is surely a coincidence. She shakes her head.
'I have been hunting Geralt and Eilian Goodblossom for several days now, but thanks to the injury I sustained in Sedgemead I have been always a step behind. While I hunted them, they hunted targets of their own: the Redclaw brothers, three powerful brigands who together directed much of the villainy present in these lands. Now that the three Redclaws are no more, the Goodblossoms are free to enact the next step of their plan: seizing control! They do not wish to free these lands of brigand control... husband and wife wish to consolidate it beneath their own leadership!'
You tell Melona that you have met both Eilian and Geralt, and would be willing to help her track them down.

'The leader of the raiders on the Greenway is a man named Maelgun Redclaw, and he is a very bad sort. Now, a few folk have tried this in the past, and he has slain them all... but he has never answered a challenge from one such as you, has he?

'This choice is an important one, for certain. But as the master has deemed, you can freely choose what clan you shall represent in the battle for a time.

'Are you willing to help us investigate and stop the brigands before something truly terrible occurs?'
'Wolves this close to Mossward are already problem enough. Add Men into the mix and those wolves will be trained to attack alongside them. We must put an end to this before it begins.'

'I do not envy you this task, ${PLAYER}. I am, however, grateful that you will do this for us. Be safe and swift.'
'With their siege weaponry destroyed, the Uruks will not be able to assault us at so great a range. We thank you for all you have done, ${PLAYER}.'
Mission: Siege-breaking

At a hill-fort, constructed by the Uruk of the White Hand, massive siege weapons threaten to prolong the occupation of the land. Destroying the weapons will weaken the Uruks and potentially give the people of the region a chance to battle back against the invaders.

'An expedition returned having discovered that there are ruins overrun by Uruks bearing the symbol of the White Hand. This is a transgression against the ancient inhabitants of this land. Something must be done.

'Make haste, ${PLAYER}, the longer the Uruks are able to hold the ruins, the more heritage they destroy.'
'A great effort to remove the Uruk from the ruins. We shall not forget it, ${PLAYER}. Nor shall we let you go unpaid.'
Mission: The Hand, Out!
Uruks bearing the symbol of the White Hand encamp in Elven ruins turning beauty into filth. You are tasked with driving the forces out.
'Strike quickly and remove their leader. We shall yet drive this foe from our lands. I will await your triumphant return.'
'Your effort to defeat the White Hand will not go unrewarded. This foe is great and you have proven yourself a worthy defender of the Free Folk. Please, accept this small token of our thanks.'
Speak with the mission giver and travel to the location of the Uruk encampment and defeat the war-leader there.
Complete the Mission: Bite the Hand

'Our scouts learned that there is a potent Uruk War-leader in the ruins. We believe that if we can remove it quickly, we have a chance to undermine the efforts of these invaders from the south. If you are willing, we ask you to make your way into the camp, find the leader, and remove it. Mayhap, in their absence, we can strike a harder blow and drive the remaining Uruks from the land.'
Mission: Bite the Hand
Return to the mission giver and let them know of your victory over the White Hand.
White Hand Uruks encamped within Elven ruins threaten the populace with great weapons of war. Scouts present an option to strike down the leader and throw the forces gathered into disarray.
'Elven relics of ages past, you see? Yes, our patron is an Elf in this case and we are obliged to assist them -- provided you are willing to assist us.'
'Our patron will be pleased that you succeeded in recovering the items they requested. It is our hope that this recompense pleases you as well.'

A rescue mission, not of the living, but of the historical items of the Elves. Speak with the mission giver to go to the ruins and retrieve the ancient bits of Elven history from the White Hand Uruks.
Complete the Mission: Sifting Through Time

'This is an odd request, ${PLAYER}, but suffice it to say, not everything we ask you to do is simply for the good of the effort. Sometimes, there are folk who are helping to arm us and fund our efforts to defend the lands who ask something peculiar of us. This is one of those times.
'A patron has asked for help in collecting anything of value from the crumbling Elven ruins. If you find some, I will have a scout meet you and collect the goods for our patron once you are done.'
Mission: Sifting Through Time
You retrieved the relics and handed them to the scout who arrived to lead you out. Return to the mission giver and tell them of your efforts.

In ancient Elven ruins, Uruks are set to despoil not only the ruins, but also to remove or destroy the remnants of an ancient past. An enterprising individual asked the scouts of Swanfleet to hire folk to sift through the detritus in the ruins for anything of value expecting that some Elf-nobles may pay for a piece of their history.
'Etta is pacing. It is never a good thing when Etta is pacing. Please bring back the berries as fast as you can!'
Etta Yewberry's husband is doing his best to provide for his wife, but a recent attack by the Orcs of Tharbad has left them bereft of any and all supplies they brought with them from Bree.
Collected ruddy bush berries (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

Tam Yewberry has asked you to gather red berries from the bushes in the ruins near Stonecrop Encampment.

'Do you have them? You do! Oh this is wonderful. I know it will only fulfil this temporary craving, but I cannot wait to see the smile these bring to Etta's face.'

'Hello there. Unhappy days these are. Look at our shelves! Empty after the raid by the Orcs of Tharbad, and I've a wife with child to feed! Etta is craving berries and... well, I learned with the first two children not to argue with a craving mother-to-be.
'Sadly, I am no warrior, and cannot leave the camp. But perhaps you can help us? To the north are some ruins, among which grow bushes covered with Etta's favourite berries. If you bring some back for us, perhaps we can stop her pacing.'

'Tam does so much for me, and he has been fretting over me ever since we crossed over into Cardolan. I am looking forward to making him a nice pair of leather breeches once you bring me those avanc hides.'
The many pools of Sedgemead are home to dangerous avanc, whose thick hides make for fine leather.

'Ah, perfect! These are exactly what I was hoping for. Thank you so much for your help!'

'Well met! Do not mind my pacing. I find myself restless being confined to these crumbled walls. My husband, Tam, did not want us to make this trip, and now it seems he was right to worry!
'I want to make him a new pair of breeches, but our hunter is otherwise occupied. If you head north, will you bring me hides from the avanc that lurk in the watery pools?'
Return to Etta Yewberry

'You return! How did you fare?'
You recount your deeds.
'Goodness me, that is impressive! Why, I think you may have just saved our village! You have my eternal thanks!'

'Oh, hullo! My name is Eirlys Dringarth - Mayor of Lintrev! Well, yes, we are but a small village. Even so - I take my duties very seriously, and there is some very serious danger afoot!
'From my watch-tower, I can see out for miles and miles. To the east, a fearsome foe has dug into the cliffs, building fortresses and huge spiked walls! Of late, the air has been filled with smoke in that direction. Their bonfires are so many that I fear for our little village! I do not wish to alarm my neighbours, but perhaps you could do something about this? They are very nearly on our doorsteps!'
The safety of the small village of Lintrev is dependent upon its residents leaving no trace of their whereabouts for their unsavoury neighbours to find.
Hid hobbit prints (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

Hide hobbit prints (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

You should let Heleth know that you have hidden her tracks.

The river is north-west of Lintrev, in southern Swanfleet.

'Hullo, hullo! Have you done it? Oh, marvellous! I would not have slept a wink had I thought those nasty big folk from up the road would have found us. Why, I have had such an upset tummy that I have not eaten in at least an hour!'

'Oh, hullo there. I am Heleth. Have you been down to the river? I was there earlier today, but the scariest big folk I have ever seen came thundering down the road! I dove for the bushes then rushed back here as quickly as I could.
'Alas, I forgot to hide my tracks! If you go down to the river, will you scuff over my footprints if you see them? Mayor Dringarth insists that we leave no trace of ourselves where the scary big folk can see them, but I am too afrighted to go back down myself.'
The siege engines of Sharmokal are deadly weapons with a secret design flaw.

Iago Rhudd is in Lintrev.
'Have you done it? Hahah! I almost wish I could be there to see it when they try to hurl their next rock and the entire contraption falls to pieces!'

'Hullo, there. Iago Rhudd's me name. Did you know that to the east we have some very unsavoury neighbours? Behind their walls terrible Orc-looking creatures have built deadly weapons, capable of throwing stones for miles! Well, maybe not miles, but very far, and with good accuracy. I have seen them practicing their aim on travellers on the road below.
'Now, I happened to get a look at one of these machines up close once - do not ask how, it is a long tale. In any case, there is a flaw in their construction and they are too much the fool to realize it. A single pin, when removed, can render the entire contraption useless! I will pay you if you sneak into their town and steal away these pins. Bring them back to me, that I might forge arrow heads with them, to be used to defend Lintrev!'
Bring the pins to Iago

'Folk do not realize how dangerous basket weaving is. The care you must take with sharp reeds, the danger in gathering them, the competition with those who try to steal your designs - it is certainly not a profession for those of gentler persuasions.
'Please let me know when you have reduced the number of sickle-flies east of Herne. They are liable to ruin my livelihood otherwise!'
Aggressive sickle-flies who love to feast upon valuable reeds are plaguing the ponds near Herne.

'Is it done? What a relief! Things are sure strange around Herne these days.'

'Well met! I am Aerona, basket weaver of Herne. If you are looking to make some coin, I am looking for some help. East of Herne are various bodies of water from which I often go to gather reeds with which to make my baskets. Of late, the reeds have been decimated by sickle-flies! Well, by their larva...'
She shudders saying the word.
'Bleh! If you reduce the number of sickle-flies there, I will pay you! This season may be near to over, but at least this way there will be fewer to breed for the next.'

Aerona has asked you to reduce the number of sickle-flies buzzing about the ponds and waterways east of Herne.
Herne is in western Cardolan.
You are asked to make your way into the hills to find three warg matrons who lead a pack of the vile beasts there. Speak with the mission giver in Lhan Garan to begin this mission.
The warg matrons were present in the pit and they were fearsome. You were victorious. Return to the mission giver in Lhan Garan and tell them of the success.
Complete the Mission: Into the Pits

'Grim news, ${PLAYER}. Wargs in the hills surrounding the town grow more aggressive, and it seems that there are leaders, or at the very least, tenders who drive their murderous attacks. Our scouts know the location of these feral things, but they show a strength unnatural that terrifies most of our unseasoned warriors.
'Would you help? There are three wargs in those hills that we believe are the leaders. Each with distinctive markings that set them apart from the rest. They should be easy to identify.
'Slaying, on the other hand... well, that is the difficulty is it not?'

'A word of warning before you go: avoid the pointy fangs and sharp claws. They will rend and tear your flesh if they pierce your armour.
'Good luck, ${PLAYER}.'

'With the matrons eliminated, the remainder of the pack should be far easier to handle. Still, these beasts are far more fearsome than a pack of wolves, and where they roam, Orcs and uruks are sure to follow. Thank you for your efforts, ${PLAYER}.'
Mission: Into the Pits

Along the hilltops in Swanfleet there is a group of dens where vicious wargs bed down, feast, and terrorize the populace. You are tasked with the grim duty of hunting down the warg matrons that keep the rest of the pack in line.
A change in leadership could throw the Southron Men in the area into disarray. The mission giver at Lhan Garan will have a scout lead you to the camp to remove the leadership.
The leaders of the brigands are defeated. You should now return to the mission giver in Lhan Garan and tell them of your victory.
Complete the Mission: Not as Many Heads

'My scouts report that there are leaders among the brigands who train them in the arts of battle. We had thought most of the Men coming from the south were brutes or brigands out to make a living as highwaymen. Now, we are not so certain.
'Yes, given the size of the encampment, we knew that something was amiss, but we did not understand the organization of the force until now.
'Knowing what we know now, there is a grim answer and call that was made. We want to eliminate these leaders and break the will of these brigands. Perhaps it will provide us the change to strike at them before they become more of a threat.'

'We hope that by eliminating the leaders we can weaken the resolve of the men from the South. Perhaps they will scatter without leadership. At least, we hope that they will fall to in-fighting and disarray providing us a slight advantage over the enemy.'
'A great effort and battle well fought. You have well earned your rewards, ${PLAYER}.'
Mission: Not as Many Heads

Recently, the scouts of Swanfleet learned that there are a small number of leaders charged with the training of the Men at a large brigand encampment. If they are removed, infighting may result and provide an opening for a counter attack.
'Trolls!? D-did you say, trolls? Indeed! This is terrifying news. We are not equipped to deal with trolls. Best it was you out there, I would not have been so successful.'
Something is lurking in the woods in the Stoor-vales and hobbit scouts want someone to look into what it is. Speak with the mission giver at Clegur to assist.
There were wood trolls lurking in the woods and ruins. This is not a good development and you should let the mission giver know.
Complete the Mission: Aberrations of Nature

As you approach you hear the hobbit mutter, 'this simply does not make any sense…' They look up at you.
'Sorry, I was just reading a report from the woods not far from here where one of the villagers said they saw a twisted tree stand straight up and tear the bark off another tree nearby. It must be someone who had a little too much at the tavern and went wandering... right?'
A brief few seconds of thought and they continue, 'Then again, mayhap there is something going on. Would you be willing to look into this?'

'I am not certain what you will encounter there, friend. I only know what my neighbours have been saying. They tell me that the trees are walking and moving of their own accord. That cannot be a good thing, can it?'
Mission: Aberrations of Nature
Something unnatural moves through the woods in the Stoor-vales. Hobbit scouts ask for assistance in discovering what is happening to the forest surrounding their homes.
'It is a shame that so many were slain, and a joy that those few could be saved. We are indebted to you, ${PLAYER}.'
Scouts believe that there may be survivors in the warg pits in the hills nearby. You are asked to go into those hills and rescue those you can, and burn the dead to stop the spread of disease.
The warg-matrons were present in the pit and they were fearsome. You were victorious. Return to the mission giver in Mossward and tell them of the success.
Complete the Mission: The Jaws of Death

'Reports come in from the hills that wargs are making the hillocks outside of town into dens. Aside from the clear threat that this poses, there is news that the wargs have taken a number of townsfolk. Some may yet live, it is unclear. Our scouts were not able to get close enough to confirm if there are any villagers in the bone pits.
'Will you go, find any survivors you can? Be wary, the wargs are cunning and cruel.'

'If there are any still alive from those taken, we must make efforts to recover them. Please make haste, ${PLAYER}. Any who are slain, should be burned to ensure that no diseases spread. A terrible end.'
Mission: The Jaws of Death

Recent events see the disappearance of a number of townsfolk. Wargs in the surrounding hills, emerging at night, have captured and potentially killed a number of the inhabitants. Scouts believe that there may be some townsfolk still alive in the hillock dens where the wargs make their homes.
Complete the Mission: Secrets and Plans
Men from the south are a great threat to the populace and specifically to Mossward. You are asked to enter their encampment and seek any secret plans they may have.
You collected the plans and handed them to the scout who arrived to lead you away from the camp. You should return to the mission giver in Mossward to tell them what you learned.

'I will tell you this, ${PLAYER}. Something terrible is amiss in these lands. Since riders pushed through here in the dead of night not long ago, there has been all manner of ill-fortuned and foul-mannered folk pouring in from the south.
'None are worse than the Southron Men making a large encampment. We know that they are planning something and need to know what it is.
'Great tents in their encampment are used for meeting between the leaders. It is possible, our scouts believe, that they are formulating some plan for an attack. We want to learn what they are planning so that we may thwart their efforts.
'Are you willing to help?'
'The encampment of Southron Men is very large and teeming with brigands with only fell deeds on their minds. We need to find out what they intend and quickly. Please be swift, ${PLAYER}.'

'These plans are more well-developed than expected. It is hard to believe that bands of brigands could be this organized. I fear that this setback will not hold them long, ${PLAYER}. Still, you have done well to prepare us for the future.'
Mission: Secrets and Plans

In a large brigand encampment, Southron Men gather in large numbers digging trenches, raising stake-walls and tents, and planning a terrible attack on the people of Swanfleet. It is unclear what their overall objectives are, but the scouts in the area want to learn more.
The request is a simple one: patrol through the pathways that make up the township of Clegur at night. Speak with the mission giver to assist.
Your patrol was not as uneventful as everyone presumed. It appears that the Men from the south are intent on invading every corner of Swanfleet if they can. Alert the mission giver.
Complete the Mission: Patrol the Township

'Ah, ${PLAYER}, a word for a moment if I may.
'Many villagers are concerned about what is happening all around us and were wondering if you might help put their minds at ease a bit.
'Nights are a little uneasy recently, and we just do not have enough Bounders to keep up with patrols. Would you be willing to help us keep watch?'
'It seems that the fears expressed by the townsfolk were warranted. I am glad that we employed you to patrol our streets. We need to double our own guard to ensure that our streets remain safe.'
'Honestly, ${PLAYER}, I think it will be an uneventful night and that the townsfolk are grousing, just to grouse. Still, if you are willing to go on patrol it will put minds at ease.'
Mission: Patrol the Township
Clegur is a relatively safe village. Still, the inhabitants are on edge with the recent events in Swanfleet and welcome the assistance of someone willing to watch over the village at night.
Helping with deliveries in the small cliffside village of Glyn Helyg might be the respite you need. Speak with the mission giver to embark on the journey of relaxation.
In a rather unexpected turn of events, there were brigands who decided to make their way into the village at night. Fortunately, you were there and able to drive them off.
Complete the Mission: Dangerous Deliveries

'Day and night folk are asking after food in the village and one of the more enterprising hobbits here is trying to meet the demands of an ever-growing populace.'
They wink at you.
'It is not our usual request, but the patron is willing to pay for the assistance of merely taking food from one place and bringing it to another. Should be simple to make these deliveries.
'Care to help?'
'Do not think that this is some easy task. Hungry hobbits are some truly cantankerous folk. You best be swift if you want to avoid their ire.'
'This seems highly unlikely and rather frightening. I am glad that you were here to force this threat away.'
Mission: Dangerous Deliveries

Glyn Helyg is a wondrous village carved into a cliff in view of a glorious waterfall. The tiered village is difficult to traverse, and the hungry hobbits there are always wanting more deliveries to be made.
After a failed raid on an encampment outside of Caras Gelebren, an Uruk leader was reportedly injured to point of near death. This development provides an opportunity for you to strike a vital blow.

The Uruk leader was not injured, he was more powerful than any of the other Uruks in the encampment. It appears that the information from the scouts was wrong or that there was something else at play with the war-leader.
Complete the Mission: Leadership Direction

'Fortune smiles on us, ${PLAYER}. A recent attack by the Uruks has cost them dearly as one of their leaders was reported to take an arrow in the knee. With an injury like that they will never adventure again. Now is our chance to strike.
'Head back into their camp, find the leader and finish the work already begun.'
'We have an advantage and we must take it. Please make haste, ${PLAYER}. If we can cleave the head from this force of Uruks, surely we will drive them from these lands.'
'How is it possible that our scouts were wrong? The enemy should have been near death. I wonder if there is something nefarious seeping into our scouting ranks. We will need to look into this.'
Mission: Leadership Direction

After a counter assault by the Uruks at Caras Gelebren, scouts learned that one of the Uruk leaders was injured in the fray. They have set you to finding the leader and finishing the work started in the previous battle.
An odd request to help out on a nearby farm in Lhunach. Speak to the mission giver to head down to the farm and help.
After an eventful day on the farm, it is time to return to the mission giver who asked you to go and help the famers with their work.
Complete the Mission: A Day on the Farm

'I have an interesting request. It seems a farmer nearby is having all manner of trouble with their crops. He needs a proper hand in gathering, protecting, and tending to everything on their property. Any chance you might be looking for a little work?'
'Not exactly work for an adventurer such as you eh, ${PLAYER}? Maybe this is the kind of thing that will bring you a measure of rest and recreation. What do you say, ready to work on the farm?'
'Was it as lovely as I expected it would be working on the farm? No? Well it seems that adventure has a way of finding you does it not, ${PLAYER}?'
