Gorgost defeated
Brogmarsh defeated
Defeated Rauzghuk

Wargs make the hills their home and collect an impressive number of bones. It is unclear if the bones belong to the free folk or other victims. Regardless, the threat from these beasts is too great to let them remain.
A rather large turtle is threatening the hobbit-folk fishing and dredging in the nearby swamp-land. Speak to the mission giver to help them out with this problem.
Having dispatched the turtle and her brood, you should now return to the mission giver and let them know of your deeds.
Complete the Mission: Terrible Turtle Trouble

'Hullo there friend. Would you be willing to help us with a rather large, small problem we have? It is not the kind of problem that we usually have in these parts. You see, there is a terrapin of unusual size living in the ruins at the edge of the murky water not far from here.
'Normally she leaves us well enough alone, but recently her little ones have been snapping up all the fish and even snapping at some of our folk.
'We know it seems cruel, but if we do not do something soon, we might start running low on food to feed our families. Sometimes we need to push back a little on nature. I am afraid that this is one of those times.'
'A pity that such a gentle creature is so incensed. We do not know what else to do. Please, do your best to be quick about this. Thank you, ${PLAYER}.'
'There was no other way than this. I am glad that you handled this so quickly, friend. Here, you deserve this for such unselfish work.'
Mission: Terrible Turtle Trouble

Turtles are not often something that hobbits fear greatly, but there is one in the ruins that causes them to tremble. The scouts from Glyn Helyg asked you for assistance in removing the menace from their midst.
Speak with the mission giver and alert them that you are prepared to visit Herne at night to discuss the intent of the suspicious folk lurking about the town square.
You have discovered that there are nefarious elements mixing in with other refugees making their way to Herne. You must return to the mission giver and tell them of this development.
Complete the Mission: Infiltration

'What I am about to ask you, ${PLAYER}, is something that pains me to do.
'The township of Herne could be in danger. Recently, many folks who are not known in the town have been arriving from other areas, likely because of the encroaching Men and Uruks from the south.
'The mayor and other townsfolk are concerned that there might be a certain element trying to infiltrate the town. Now, it is possible that this is just a bit of alarmist reaction, but we cannot be too sure.
'What we are asking is that you approach any of these newcomers and determine their intentions in the town. Can you help?'

'I dislike using subterfuge to find these miscreants, but it seems that we might do best to employ their own tactics against them. Speak with those out and about at night and ask them if they serve Sharkey, when they expose their allegiance bring them to justice.'

'Your efforts have made Herne safer, ${PLAYER}. Sadly, it seems that Herne will need to be very cautious about the possibility of infiltration for some time to come. This concern is not yours, but that of the town's leadership.
'They will be warned and counseled.
'Thank you for this assistance.'
Mission: Infiltration

Herne saw a fair bit of trouble recently, and the arrival of suspicious new folk has the town on edge. Scouts are concerned that the town is in danger from outside and hope that someone with your reputation might be willing to assist.

The post coming out of the Shire proper has slowed to a crawl because of something that has upset the deliverer responsible for crossing the ford. You are asked to speak with the mission giver to investigate.

Something was stirred in the wake of riders crossing the ford. You assisted the post-person in crossing the ford and now normal delivery resumes. Return to the mission giver and inform them of what transpired.
Complete the Mission: Stirring at Sarn Ford

'Well met, ${PLAYER}. Do not be surprised, we scouts know about you and all you have done. We talk. Do not worry, nearly all the discussion is good!
'In fact, we think that you are the right person for this request from a post-deliverer out of the Shire. It appears that San Ford is no longer as safe as it was in days past. Something happened there and there are now reports of evil spirits stalking any who cross.
'This post-worker needs to pass over the Ford and asked if there was any way that we might be able to help in their protection. That is where you come in, my friend.'

'The post is an important way for all of us to stay connected, and I daresay that this latest interruption is setting a good many of us on edge. If you are willing to help, I know that there are many minds that will be put at ease.'
'Living water, you say? Deary me this is not good to hear. Mayhap we will need to set up nightly patrols along the Ford. For now, we have you to thank for the return of our beloved Post.'
Mission: Stirring on Sarn Ford
Sarn Ford teems with unnatural energy since the passing of a stranger cloaked in black. A hobbit mail deliverer from the Shire asked for assistance in getting their deliveries across the Ford.

With both the pack-leaders now eliminated, the wolves should be quieter for a time whilst they fight amongst themselves to determine their new order. Return to the mission giver and tell them you succeeded.

What may be an error in judgement has raised the ire of a pack of nearby wolves with only one pack-leader now in charge. Speak with the mission giver to make your way to the ruins to finish the work of hunters.
Complete the Mission: Mother of Wolves

'We often think it necessary to take action when maybe we ought not have. This report may be one of those times.
'Hunters were tasked with thinning a large pack of wolves in a nearby ruin. In their zeal, the hunters managed to kill one of the pack-leaders, the male.
'Normally, this would allow the lesser wolves to fall on one another for a time until new pack-leaders rise, but the wolves in the ruins followed a breeding pair and the she-wolf has grown aggressive in her mate's absence.
'Our task is clear, we must eliminate the wolf matron before she drives the pack into attacking the village and does irreparable harm to the populace.'

'A new set of pack-leaders will rise to take their place, but for the moment, we will have respite from their attacks. I wonder though why the aggression was so great. There must be something stirring these creature more than normal.'
'Our own folly has wrought this end. A shame that the wolves cannot be more like faithful hounds, but it seems this is their nature. So we must do now, what we must.'
Mission: Mother of Wolves

Hunters, recently asked to assist in culling the wolves in the nearby ruins, eliminated one half of the pair who kept the wolves away from the populace of the town. Something has changed in the surviving pack-leader and she now seems to be testing the resolve of the townsfolk nearby. You are tasked with finishing the job the hunters began by eliminating the female pack-leader before she finds a new mate.

Removing the enemy's ability to see over long distances will give an advantage to attackers making their way against the forces of brigands. You should visit the mission giver in Lhan Garan to begin your assault.
After some effort you were able to neutralize the watch-towers and some of the enemy stationed at the encampment. Return to Lhan Garan and tell the mission giver of your success.
Complete the Mission: Among the Watch-towers

'When an enemy can see you coming from a great distance it puts you at a disadvantage. When that enemy is entrenched that disadvantage is even greater. At the brigand encampment, we have both issues at once.
'The brigands there built tall watch-towers that give them a clear view of the surrounding wilds. Any offensive that might be launched against them is immediately at a disadvantage. We also know that the brigands employ a volatile powder of some kind that we may be able to use in our favour.
'If we reposition some of that powder at the foot of the watch-towers we may be able to destroy them and take back the advantage. Are you willing to assist?'

'The advantage that the watch-towers provide is great. We cannot amass a force that will challenge them without them knowing that we are there. But, if you are willing to infiltrate, perhaps you will be able to sneak in and provide us the cover we need to begin a counter assault.'
'We shall watch them more closely and when the time is right, we will organize an assault of our own. We best plan as they will likely restore the watch-towers quickly.'
Mission: Among the Watch-towers
Watch-towers at the brigand encampment in Swanfleet provide a distinct advantage to the forces there. There is a desire to undermine their use by turning the tools of the enemy against them.
The Hove family farm is up in flames after an attack by ferocious goblins!
Doused fires (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
This bucket is perfect for the task!
Water sloshes over the sides of the bucket
Dousing the Flaming Farm
Find an empty bucket
Douse fires (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

You should let Erina know that you have put out many of the fires at Hove Farm.
Erina is at Sculoc Farm, in northern Cardolan.

You found an empty bucket, but now you need to fill it with water.
You should find the pond at the Hove family farm, in northern Cardolan.

Armed with a bucket of water, you are now ready to douse the flames burning at the Hove family farm.
The farm is in northern Cardolan.
'You did it? Oh, thank you thank you! I hope we can go home soon!'

'Who are you? Are you here to help? Oh, please say yes!
'Terrible goblins raided our farm! I want to go home, but they are still there and I can see the smoke from here! Please, please, please can you please put out the fires? Oooh, it is all going to burn if you do not! You must help!
'We have a beautiful pond where you could fill a bucket and use it to put out the fires!'

Erina has asked you to put out fires at the Hove family farm. You should look for a bucket at Scurloc farm with which to fill with water in order to douse the flames.
Scurloc farm is in northern Cardolan.
Return to Erina
Fill the bucket at Hove Farm
Eluna asked you to speak with the people of Lhan Garan.
Talk to Eluna
Talk to Murig
Talk to Deryn

Eluna is waiting for you.
Talk to Eluna.

Murig smiles warmly as you approach.
'You had no obligation to us, yet you continued to put yourself in harm's way at every turn. Thank you.
'The others and I will keep Lhan Garan safe. It will be here should you ever choose to come visit.'

'Farewell, ${PLAYER}. You have been a boon to us, and a genuine pleasure to get to know.
'Be safe on your travels.'
He thrusts a small parcel of bread into your hands.

'Hello, traveller.
'I'm sad to see you leave, but more than that, I'm grateful for your acquaintance in the first place. These past months have been quite the trial for all of us. Setting down roots in a foreign land, away from everything we call familiar, it's not easy. It makes every kindness feel more meaningful.
'Ardhun? Well, she's stuck with us now. In a selfish way, I'm glad she is. I much prefer her being here with me, even if she's going to sulk her way through the entire winter.
'Be kind to yourself out there.'
'Before you go, say good-bye to the children, please.'

Marget's attention is on Ardhun. It's only when you get close does she seem to remember the world around her.
'Say, traveller, you saw how she fought, right? How do you think I would measure up against her?'
Marget smiles at you, and there is a hint of danger and mischief in her eyes.
'About as well as I'd measure up against you, I suspect.
'I hear you are to leave us soon. I hope the rest of your adventures are at least half as exciting as the one we shared.
'Come visit us again. And bring bread. Deryn's tastes like medicine, somehow.'
Farewell to Lhan Garan

Eluna has asked you to say farewell to her students before you leave.
Talk to Murig, Deryn, and Marget.
Return to the mission giver

At the ruins of Nímbarth, a band of ruffians and brigands assaults the populace and lays waste to the beauty of the once great ruins. You are tasked with going forth and eliminating the brigand leader and their followers.
After defeating the brigands, you should return to the mission giver and tell them of your success so that you may receive your well-earned rewards.
Complete the Mission: Brigands in Nímbarth

'A word if I may. There are ruins called Nímbarth not far from here that are overrun by brigands. We would like to see them removed so that we might find some solace whilst travelling near the ruins. Too often these aggressive Men harry our folk and cause irreparable damage to the populace. Will you help us?'
'Be wary, for though they are a broadly disorganized group, they still pose a threat. I will send a scout to watch your progress.'
'Another victory for you, friend. We are all indebted for every effort you undertake. To say that we are grateful is an understatement. We owe you much. We hope this shall suffice.'
Mission: Brigands in Nímbarth
Brigands set roost in the ruins at Nímbarth. They are not welcome. You are asked to make your way there to defeat their leader and thin their numbers.
Speak with the mission giver
You are to make your way into the ruins of Caras Gelebren, tear down the banners of the White Hand and slay as many Uruk-hai as you find. Speak with the mission giver to undertake this mission.
You found a good number of Uruk-hai in the ruins and destroys the banners you found. Return now to receive your rewards.
Complete the Mission: Signs and Sigils

'Uruks in the ruins of Caras Gelebren, this will not do. Our request here is a simple one, go to the ruin, drive them out, and tear down their banners.
'We know that this cannot be done simply, but at least thin their number. They are numerous and strong, but with enough effort we may wrest the ruins from their control.'
'It seems such a simple request, but Uruks are monstrous creatures of both size and temperament. You would do best to be on guard as you venture among them, ${PLAYER}.'

'Excellent work, ${PLAYER}. It is good to know that there are still stout warriors like you willing to aid us. The Uruk-hai know the retribution that will come to them for every affront they raise against us.'
Mission: Signs and Sigils
Once a great home of the Elves, the ruins of Caras Gelebren are now despoiled by the arrival of Uruk of the White Hand. There is now an effort underway to push the Uruks out.
'You upheld your side of the bargain, ${PLAYER}, and so have I. Now take that blade to the Ranger before I change my mind! I still say I could have handled it.'

'I must be honest with you, ${PLAYER}. It is clear to anyone that you are already an experienced adventurer, with many skills. I did not really expect you to treat me like a grown-up. But you have taken the time out of your day to show me what it takes to become an adventurer!
'I have seen enough. You have upheld your side of our bargain, and I will do the same. Here's Madthrug's weapon, as I promised. You'll bring it back to that Ranger for me, I expect? Mother and father will be pleased, but I still say I could have handled such a weapon!'

Meneldir is by the east gate of Mossward.
Now that you have recovered the Uruk blade, you should bring it to Meneldir.

'You recovered the Uruk blade from Tegwyn before he hurt himself with it? Very well done, ${PLAYER}.'
Meneldir gets a faraway look in his eye, and gazes over the surrounding wall of Mossward.
'I remember being that age, and dreaming only of adventure, of excitement. I was not so very different from young Tegwyn when I was a boy growing up in the Angle of Mitheithel, where my people dwell. I do not judge him harshly for taking the sword, and I hope you will not either. His parents busy themselves with the work of fortifying Mossward's defences, and I daresay they remain unaware of the boy's mischief. I will not tell them if you do not, ${PLAYER}.'
Prologue, Chapter 2: Skills of an Adventurer
Bring the Uruk blade to Meneldir by the east gate of Mossward
Tegwyn agreed to relinquish the Uruk sword to you.
Travel to the ruins of the House of the Mírdain
Talk to Tarandir

'You heard nothing, yes?
'That is a great sorrow, and one made no less painful with the passage of time. Once you would have heard the songs of anvils and chisels, and those of laughter and friendship, but no more. All that remains of Caras Gelebren... of Tham Mírdain... of old Mirobel are ruins and dreadful memories.
'When I soon depart this realm, will I be healed of these wounds? I cannot say for certain, but I fear the answer—for neither seems befitting, either as gift or punishment.'
Tarandir pauses. His gaze falls upon the ruins of the lower city of Caras Gelebren. After a long moment, he turns to you.
'I thank you for hearing my tale, ${PLAYER}. It has done my spirit well to tell it one last time in Middle-earth.
'Oh, but one more thing... a word of warning, if you would hear it. The Enemy's hand, though maimed, may still seek to shape the days to come in Middle-earth.
'Be watchful of the evils in this world, my friend.'
You hear nothing but the wind and the gentle lapping of the water nearby...
The ruins of the House of the Mírdain loom before you

Tarandir can be found upon the ruins of an old watch-tower at Caras Gelebren in Swanfleet.
You have found a lone Elf in ornate armour standing among the ruins of Caras Gelebren. The Elf, Tarandir, has offered to tell you the tale of the doom of Caras Gelebren.
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTE: To advance this quest, you must complete the Skirmish: Doom of Caras Gelebren. If you have not yet completed the Skirmish Tutorial, you must first visit any Skirmish Camp and speak to the Skirmish Captain. Skirmish Camps can be found throughout Middle-earth in locations such as Bree, Thorin's Gate, Ost Guruth, and Rivendell.</rgb>

Tarandir can be found upon the ruins of an old watch-tower at Caras Gelebren in Swanfleet.
You have heard Tarandir's tale of the doom of Caras Gelebren. You should speak to Tarandir.
Hear Tarandir's tale and complete 'Doom of Caras Gelebren'
Talk to Tarandir
<rgb=#00ff00>Listen</rgb> at the ruins of the House of the Mírdain

'Hail, traveller. What has brought you to this place?'
You introduce yourself and tell the Elf of your adventures in Swanfleet.
'I am Tarandir, of the Mírdain, and I have come to Caras Gelebren on a last pilgrimage before I depart Middle-earth. Know you the history of this place? It stood in peace for many years, both before and after its destruction, but now Orc-kind roams it once more. It pains my heart to see it so, that these evils might remain after I depart.
'I was here when it fell long ago, ${PLAYER}, and though it is a sorrowful tale, I would share it with you.
'Will you hear it, friend?'
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTE: To advance this quest, you must complete the Skirmish: Doom of Caras Gelebren. If you have not yet completed the Skirmish Tutorial, you must first visit any Skirmish Camp and speak to the Skirmish Captain. Skirmish Camps can be found throughout Middle-earth in locations such as Bree, Thorin's Gate, Ost Guruth, and Rivendell.</rgb>

'And that is the end of the tale, ${PLAYER}. Although I did not see him fall, Faeldor was lost. My brother held the gates of Caras Gelebren against the Enemy for as long as he could... and I wish I could tell him how proud I was of him in that moment. But there is never time, is there? Even for the Eldar...
'Although the war continued on for years, I and the other survivors of my kin found refuge at Imladris. In time, what we were faded away, and it was as if the Mírdain were not to be named as such among the Elves—that the stain of the Enemy could not be scoured from our hands.'
Tarandir shakes his head.
'Might I ask something of you?
'Travel up into the city, stand before the ruins of the House of the Mírdain, and listen. That is all I ask.'
The Fall of the Mírdain

The ruins of the House of the Mírdain can be found at the easternmost point of Caras Gelebren.

Versus: The Heart of Barazinbar
A simple task. Speak with Uglash to travel to the Heart of Baranzibar in Moria. There, fight off the Free People who would take this treasured hall away from your allies.
Fight against the encroaching Free People in the depths of Moria. Speak with again to make the journey swiftly.
After fighting in the depths of Moria, there is only one thing left to do. Speak with Uglash and tell them how the battle went.
Speak with Uglash to travel to the Heart of Baranzibar
Complete a Battle in the Heart of Baranzibar

'Scouts found a hold in Moria where we can mine for material to make better weapons of war! We need adventurous sorts to go down into the dark and keep the Free People away from this find. You willing to fight, maggot?'
'Good choice. I always prefer volunteers to forcing you maggots into something you'll just get squashed doing. Now, get into the dark and destroy those Free People.'
'You fought. That is enough... for now. The Free People will keep attacking the Heart of Baranzibar. We will not relent.'
Deep in the Mines of Moria, forces of Angmar and the Free People clash for control of a dwarf-hall.
You completed a battle in the Heart of Baranzibar
Speak with Tordúr to travel to the Heart of Baranzibar
'There will be few others who will make the journey with you. Be safe and do all you can to thwart the incursion.'
'It matters not if you won, but that you fought. We must all do our part and we will fight in those depths until the force of Angmar plague them no more. Good effort, ${PLAYER_NAME}.'
Fight against the encroaching forces of Angmar in the depths of Moria.
Complete a battle within the Heart of Baranzibar

'Our allies from Moria tell of a concerning development in their mines. All manner of foul beast from Angmar infiltrated a place called the Heart of Baranzibar and move to claim this mine with rich deposits of ore. They ask that we forestall some effort here in the Ettenmoors to curtail Angmar's advance in Moria. Will you answer the call?'

Sant Lhoer, known as the Poison Gardens of Carn Dûm, is a dank place teeming with deadly plants, trees, and flowers, the likes of which have rarely or never been seen before in Middle-earth. Beyond the foetid, beryl-green waters which flow through Sant Lhoer, rise immense glass structures, including Bâr Heledh, the Glass House. It is here that the sorceress Oganuin plies her craft, experimenting upon creatures, plants, and people alike. To what end, and for what purpose? One can only assume the darkest of designs.

'You return triumphant, ${PLAYER}!
'I bow to your skill, for none but the most seasoned Mariner could finish the many tasks I set before you, let alone overcome the dread-beast Helchgam in its foul cistern.
'You have proven yourself a most worthy Mariner, my friend, and so it is my honour to present you with this weapon. May it will serve you well in your journeys!'

'For your first task in this trial, I shall require two materials. First, I will need a cask of the foul fire-oil carried by the Orc, Throghásh, who roams near the ruins of Eitheldir, and second, I have need of a number of the steel water-flasks carried by half-orcs and brigands here in the Angle of Mitheithel. Despite our best efforts, they have maintained an encampment in the ruins of Thelgarth, so it will not be difficult to find them.
'After you have brought those to me, I will task you to find materials that must be gathered further afield, in less hospitable lands.'

'For the next materials, you will need to travel to the lands of Angmar. I must ask you to gather several beaks from the venomous dread-turtles of Malenhad, and you must also bring me a collection of corrosive droplets from the brimstone-leeches that dwell amongst the befouled waters of Duvuinen.'

'For the final materials I need, you must again travel to the land of Angmar. Dafrim, Gríshakrum, and Kughûrz are fearsome Orcs of Urugarth. Word of their cruelty and prowess in battle has spread among the Dúnedain, and it is said that they delight in tallying a count of those they have slain by carving a notch into crude sticks. If you can best even one of them in combat, collect a bloodstained tally stick and bring it to me in Tornhad. It is said that Helchgam can be found in the sewers beneath the dread city of Carn Dûm, but I am afraid there is only one way to procure the putrid slime of Helchgam, and that will mean putting an end to it.'

'It is time you learned more of the ways of the Mariner, ${PLAYER}. In my youth, I spent many years among the Elves of Imladris, and I learned much from them and from their many visitors. An Elf of the Grey Havens named Galdor has come to Imladris, and I am certain that his wisdom would be a great boon to you in your journey as a Mariner. Before such a meeting can be arranged, however, you must be suitably prepared and outfitted!
'To that end, you shall have need of equipment that better reflects your skill as a Mariner and also the good you do for the people of Middle-earth, my friend. It would be my honour to fashion for you a weapon and a fine piece of a jewellery by which to represent your prowess, but I must give to you this cautionary word: these implements and articles will not be easily earned, for I shall task you with a number of trials to collect materials of worth to aid in their creation. Only when you have finished each and every one of my trials shall you receive the rewards I have promised you, for only then shall you prove yourself a Mariner befitting them. Such was the test that was laid before me in my youth, and so too shall it be for you!
'If perhaps you do not understand how each of these materials I shall demand relate to each of the others, then allow me to explain before you ask, my friend. These materials shall serve me two-fold, for some of them shall be put to use in the craft of your weapon and jewellery, and others will prove your worth as a Mariner and as one worthy of such equipment.
'If we are understood, then let us begin.'

'I bid you welcome, ${PLAYER}.
'The Ranger, Aelindil, is a friend of Lord Elrond, and I was told I should expect you. It is my understanding that you have come to seek guidance in the way of the Mariner. Indeed, I can offer you that, my friend—in some small measure at least.
'My lesson is this: the path of the Mariner is one of calm and hardship—of song and storms. Balance is a skill like any other, and there are many paths by which it might be achieved, but no Mariner should fear to stray from it in times of need. The Sea tasks one to perform with perfect mastery, favouring those with a sharp mind and a swift hand, and a Mariner must find harmony with its tides and currents—for those who do not will soon meet their doom. Perhaps you have spent much time upon the rivers and Seas of Middle-earth, or perhaps you have not, but consider my words, nonetheless.
'Alas, my time in Imladris must soon come to an end. I wish you good fortune in your journey as a Mariner, ${PLAYER}, and I applaud your efforts on behalf of the Free Peoples of Middle-earth! I regret that I cannot remain in Imladris to offer you more lessons, for my errand is one of great importance and urgency, but perhaps our paths shall cross again ere I return to the Grey Havens. Until we meet again!'

In addition, I require a number of hooked avanc-teeth. That will be a simpler errand, surely, for they can be found throughout the Angle of Mitheithel.'

'I'm told Mariners have a talent for telling stories, and that some of them know quite a few songs capable of lifting spirits in trying times. Shanties, I believe you call them. Is that so?
'These storms are always bad for business. Either none of my customers show up at all, or they make a great big mess of things! Nob and Bob were cleaning up the puddles for hours last time, and by the end of the night, we'd all agreed that I should put thicker rugs and mats by the doors. Now that I mention it, I never did get around to that....'
Barliman Butterbur pauses for a moment, pulls a small piece of parchment from beneath the counter, and scribbles something onto it.
'Nevertheless, a good shanty or two would do a fair bit to raise their spirits, I think. Besides, if my customers are entertained, I find they're usually a bit better-behaved as the night wears on!
'If you'd be willing to sing a few shanties at the Pony this evening, I can offer you a fair wage. What do you say, ${PLAYER}?'

'Very good! I'll see you this evening, ${PLAYER}. Just remember to get here before the storm rolls in!'
<rgb=#FF0000>This is a Solo quest, and cannot be completed with a Fellowship.</rgb>

'It was very kind of you to stick it out until the rain stopped, ${PLAYER}.
'I'm just sorry that old Bill Ferny gave you trouble. Why, I swear I have to run him out of here every week! To be honest, I don't know why Harry puts up with him. It seems your shanties were a delight to the rest of my customers, though. Some of them have even asked when you'll be coming back! I am told that I am sometimes forgetful, but that's just because there's simply so much to be done. I don't think your shanties will fade from my memory anytime soon, though!
'You seem a fine Mariner, my friend, and so long as I am its proprietor, you will always be welcome at the Prancing Pony!'

'Nevertheless, I thank you for your help, my friend. You have done the Iron Garrison a great service, and I will make certain that Brogur—and Bósi, of course—know of the Mariner who allowed us to find Durin's Crown. Let us hope it means that the reclamation of Khazad-dûm will soon be finished!'

'Bah! You have to think a little bigger than that, my friend. We are going on an expedition, not out for a day of fishing!
'Try again, ${PLAYER}. I must have a ship worthy of bearing witness to Durin's Crown!'

'Ha-ha! Now that is more like it!
'Now then, let us set out onto the Mirrormere. If you need to make any preparations, take whatever time you need, but do not keep me waiting!'

'I think that will do nicely! Now then, why don't you do the honours? No, no, I insist.
'You are a skilled Mariner, after all! I am certain you can build a suitable ship for our expedition.
'Well then, I'll stand back and let you get to it!'
Perhaps it looked better in your head?
Masterfully done!

'There is one small problem, though, my friend. After all, I could not sail a ship through Moria!
'I have prepared a few designs by which to build a ship, but I am short a few materials I need. Unfortunately, those Orcs over by Durin's Stone—the disrespectful lot they are—are currently in possession of my planks of ilex wood. Why don't you drive them off and collect some of that wood? Once that is done, I think we'll have all the tools we need to build a ship, and quite a bit less to worry about once we're out on the Mirrormere! After all, we don't want an errant Orc-arrow piercing our sails!
'Go on, my friend. There is no time to waste!'

'What is this? A map? Some sort of plan?
'From what I can tell, it looks like there was some great deluge long ago, and that the Lake has never receded. But how can that be? Why don't you take a closer look at it?'

'I am not certain what to make of this, my friend. I would ask that you travel around the edges of Lake Evendim to survey its waters and make note of what you find. There is something unusual about this tide!
'I think you shall need to survey Annúminas from a few locations to make sense of these markings. You should begin your survey here in Tinndur, and then continue your work in the Eavespires, Men Erain, and on the isle of Tyl Ruinen. That should be enough! Here, you may borrow my spy-glass to aid in your survey, but do take care of it. It is quite valuable to me!

'Welcome back. I can see by the smoke that lingers about you that you have been successful. May it be that your actions will keep these terrible creations from spreading into Angmar and beyond.'
Put witch's crown to the torch (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Mae govannen. My name is Galasdil, and I was travelling through Nan Amlug when I came across a plant so strange I paused my journey in order to study its origin. My investigation led me through the wasted lands of Angmar, to here - the gates of Carn Dûm.
'Within Carn Dûm's Sant Lhoer grow numerous plants, twisted and corrupted by the foetid waters of the rivers that flow through the area. Among these is the corrupted witch's crown, whose seeds carry lightly upon the winds. Even now, I see small fluffs of seed floating through the dank air!
'If you are brave enough to venture into the Poison Gardens, put any of these plants you see to the torch. They must not be allowed to spread throughout Middle-earth!'

'It is good to hear Lágsaith honoured your request. Maybe she will eventually recount these details on her own, without needing reminders. In the meantime, Eávair and Borgach will do what they can, while I keep an ear to the ground.'
Collected foul liquid samples (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'You are a traveller, no? Have you ever seen anything like this before?' He procures a few phials of viscous, violently green liquid.
'The Iron Crown did not maintain their sewers very well. We gathered samples from there for further studying, but Eávair and Borgach -- ' He nods to the two women nearby who are in deep discussion. ' -- are still figuring out how to break down and cleanse it. These impurities must be harming the land in ways we do not understand.
'Lágsaith loves to recount our expedition, though she does not linger on the details. Stories spread by word-of-mouth can cover larger distances than we ourselves can travel. If she described the foul liquid to more travellers such as yourself, someone with new information might come forward and help us in our endeavours.
'Should you seek her out for the full account, make sure to remind her of this.'

Sant Lhoer, known as the Poison Gardens of Carn Dûm, is a dank place teeming with deadly plants, trees, and flowers, the likes of which have rarely or never been seen before in Middle-earth. It is here that the sorceress Oganuin plies her craft, experimenting upon creatures, plants, and people alike. To what end, and for what purpose? One can only assume the darkest of designs.

'Beyond the iron gates of Sant Lhoer lie deadly gardens and glass houses full of fungi spewing forth noxious spores. Some of the plants within the Poison Gardens can kill one in an instant! Beyond the gardens, across the teeming rivers of green liquid, is Bâr Heledh, where an Angmarim sorceress is said to be experimenting upon plants, creatures, and free-folk alike. There are things which should never be attempted, and I fear she has gone far beyond that limit. I beg you to put an end to her endeavours.
'Before you venture into Sant Lhoer, you should speak with Dolág. Her brother Málruv was attacked and she tracked his captors here. She is nearly grieved enough to go in for him by herself, but if she did so, I fear she would not return.
'Please, offer her your aid if you are able.'

'You came! I... admit I did not actually expect you to.'
She is silent a moment, and when she speaks again, her shoulders are set more firmly.
'My gratitude runs deep. Let us go forth then, but take care. The waters here are foul and have a fell look about them. I shall follow behind.'

'What has happened to this giant? It looks nothing like the Jorthkyn I have encountered before. There is something strange going on with the creatures in this garden. The Orcs and trolls, and now the Jorthkyn - they all seem to be twisted, grotesque mutations. This is surely Oganuin's doing, if Rhúnelleth is to be believed. The Elf will be glad to know you put an end to this abomination of nature.'
You show her the iron key you found.
'A key! Now that must be for the gate to the north. I could see it far over the poison waters. Let us make our way there.'

'Look there, beyond the glass walls! There is some queer light flickering within. We have found Bâr Heledh, where Rhúnelleth says Oganuin is creating the creatures you have been fighting. Could my brother be within as well?
'Collect yourself, for I doubt not that she will have more fearsome surprises waiting.'

'I... greet you with joy, Southron. The things she planned for me....'
He shudders.
'You were just in time!'
'Words alone can not express my relief. Come, let us leave this foul place. Meet me back at Bail Avarc. I wish to get my brother to safety.'

'Welcome back, my new friend. Málruv is safe now, thanks to you. Though he is well in body, the horrors he saw within Bâr Heledh will stay with him all his days, I fear.
'However, I now have hope that people like you will help to create a new world where good folk are safe once more.'

'Who are you? I do not know you. Rhúnelleth sent you? The Elf meddles and has not stopped pestering me since I arrived here.'
She sighs and collects herself.
'In fairness, I have appreciated her concern, and she kept me from rushing into that foul place without a plan. I have scouted at the gates of the Poison Gardens, and I see much movement beyond its metal bars. I doubt I could proceed against so great a number of enemies, but you look formidable enough to give me some bit of hope.
'If you will lead the way, I will follow close behind. Perhaps Málruv can be found within! Let us meet then, in Sant Lhoer.'
'What sort of a vile world is it that we live in?'
'Won't you aid me in freeing my brother from the Iron Crown?'

In the depths of Thaurisgar, countless foul and twisted experiments roam the shadows--the terrible legacy of Aniochán the Harrower. Before the fall of Carn Dûm, Aniochán worked tirelessly to outdo his rivals and win the favour of the Steward of Angmar. Chief among his tools in shaping his fell creations was a curious ichor known only as the Bile of Ifrinn. Thought to be lost after a disastrous experiment claimed Aniochán's life, now this foetid and vile substance is in danger of being let loose into the world.

Not too long ago, a group of Trév Duvárdain defeated an Iron Crown sorcerer in the sewers of Carn Dûm. The tale is, as Lágsaith would have many believe, a rather strange one.
Completed 'Sagroth, Lair of Vermin'
The Lair of Vermin
Talk to Lágsaith in Bail Avarc
Complete 'Sagroth, Lair of Vermin' on any difficulty

Complete 'Sagroth, Lair of Vermin' on any difficulty.
Use the Instance Finder to enter 'Sagroth, Lair of Vermin'.

Lágsaith has concluded her tale.
You should talk to her in Bail Avarc.
'Down we travelled into the depths of the old sewers of Carn Dûm....'

'I would say that the story has come to a close, but the fate of our large rat friend remains shrouded in mystery. May it find some modicum of peace out in the wild -- preferably far, far away from the Iron Crown.
'Thank you for indulging me, friend. I've told this tale numerous times already, but I don't think I'll ever grow tired of it. Watching people react with smiles and laughter is enough for me. After all, what's the harm in some light-hearted fun amidst such dark days?
'Was I lying about the large rat? Well...'
Lágsaith gives you a wink.
'That's for me to know and for you to guess. If you think it would help you form a decision, come back again for another retelling!'

'You wish to hear the tale, eh? Well, I suppose I could grant you the privilege.
'Once my dear Aighrig returned from the east, our little group began hunting down those who still believed in the Iron Crown. We tracked one such fool named Gárvadach into the sewers of Dûn Bándrath -- or Carn Dûm, as it's otherwise known. Apparently, he sought to capture and tame a beast of some sort. Rumours of terrible monstrosities lurking beneath the city come and go, but...'
Lágsaith leans in for a conspiratorial whisper.
'I assure you, some of them have been very true. After all, why would the Iron Crown care about how their sorceries have poisoned the wildlife?'
She grins, then leans back.
'Gárvadach may have been a fool, but anyone who perceives the world as something to be conquered is dangerous. The land does not forgive such arrogance, nor does it forget.
'And so, the six of us pursued him....'
Talk to Soltakh at Bail Avarc

'It is good to see you, ${PLAYER}, but I wish we had met again in better days.
'Much has changed in your absence, my friend. I am afraid our troubles in Carn Dûm have only grown more dire since Crannog sent word.'

Crannog has sent you a missive requesting your aid at Bail Avarc in Angmar. You should travel to Bail Avarc.

You have arrived at Bail Avarc and should seek out Crannog.
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTE: Bail Avarc can initially only be accessed via stable-master routes. Bail Avarc can be reached via the stable-masters at Esteldín, Gath Forthnír, and the stables of Rivendell.</rgb>
Travel to Bail Avarc in Angmar
Find Crannog at Bail Avarc

\qMy friend,
After Carn Dûm was retaken from the servants of the Iron Crown, I and many others believed they fled into the East. Alas, it seems whatever errand sent them there was not undertaken out of fear, but that they might one day return in greater wickedness to Angmar. Now, the Angmarim of the Iron Crown who served the False King and the tribesmen of the Trév Duvárdain still loyal to them have reclaimed the city of Carn Dûm.
The Trév Gállorg have not forgotten the aid you offered our tribe against the False King and the oppressors of the Iron Crown, but I must ask for your aid once again. When first you came to Aughaire, I offered to you a Fém—a purpose, a challenge, and the duty of all those who would call themselves Trév Gállorg. You fulfilled your Fém and saw it to its end. This day, I write to bestow upon you a new Fém: travel to Bail Avarc and aid us in casting the Iron Crown from Carn Dûm, once and for all.
Chieftain and twice-humbled tribesman of the Trév Gállorg, Crannog\q
Attached to Crannog's missive is a small map of Angmar, denoting the location of Bail Avarc.
Despite your many victories over the Iron Crown from the frozen foothills of Forochel to the eastern reaches of Mount Gundabad, Crannog's missive leaves you uneasy and an old dread fills your heart. Is the Iron Crown truly diminished and merely playing at a return to its former prominence in Angmar? Or has each seeming defeat of the Iron Crown only served to advance some greater scheme?
Question after question comes unbidden to your mind. There will be time enough to think on all of them during the journey to Bail Avarc, you decide, and surely Crannog and the Trév Gállorg will have the answers you seek.
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTE: Bail Avarc can be reached via the stable-masters at Esteldín, Gath Forthnír, and the stables of Rivendell.</rgb>
Angmar Reborn, Prologue

Although the Angmarim of the Iron Crown and their allies among the Trév Duvárdain were scattered from Carn Dûm after the fall of the False King, Crannog, chieftain of the Trév Gállorg, has sent word requesting your aid at Bail Avarc, hinting that all may not be well in Angmar.

'Welcome, mistress. Your presence in this war-torn land is welcome. The filth that fights in the Lord's name falters at every turn. Perhaps with our hand to guide them we will turn the tide and finally force our way south to discover the hidden Elven stronghold. Though it is beneath you, your first task is to meet with War-tyrant Akulhún. You will find him behind you shouting incessantly in the shadow of the totems. Be warned, he has a temper.'
'Here's a specimen ready for battle! Now, if only I could get the Lord of Angmar to recall the damned emissary he's sent here. Welcome to the front!'

'Pay attention, maggot! You are nothing! A speck. I don't know why Mordirith sent you here, other than to die like the rest! Ha! You need to make an impression or, at least an introduction. Make your way to the totems surrounded by bonfires. Find War-tyrant Akulhún and report in.
'Now, get out of my face. You sicken me.'

'You have just been hatched, broodling, but already you must play an important role. Mordirith sends you here to aid in the war against the Free Peoples. We have no time to waste. You must now get your feet wet. All of them.
'Seek out the War-tyrant Akulhún near the totems and bonfires. He is the ultimate leader in the Ettenmoors and will give you your orders!'

'Well... well... a new pup fresh from a litter in the mires of Angmar. Finally ready to wet your pelt with the blood of our enemies? Good, bare your teeth. Gird your loins. Your first task is to meet the War-tyrant. Akulhún stands before the totems near the bonfires. Make your way to him and report your arrival.
'Go now. Make the pack proud.'
Tutorial: Out of Angmar
You are directed to speak with War-tyrant Akulhún, the leader of the forces in Gramsfoot. He awaits you at the totems and bonfires down the hill near the exit into the Ettenmoors proper.
Welcome to the Ettenmoors! It is time to learn your way around. Follow your orders and prepare to meet the enemy outside of the encampment at Gramsfoot!

'Always good to see the real warriors here in the Ettenmoors. I can help you survive, slaughter, even thrive in this war. You will need my help.'
The Orc swipes at you.
'Consider this a lesson. Speak with me again to continue your lessons.'

Tutorial: Power of Corruption
Malavin, the emissary of Angmar, directed you to return to where you began your journey in the Ettenmoors to speak with the corruptor there.
Speak with the emissaries

'The Krahjarn are born to lead. We remember the wars against the first. We recall the first lash against our backs and how to revisit that on our lessers. We know what it means to lead. To oversee the battle. To watch the flow of a fight. When to inspire and when to instill fear.'
He snarls.
'We know what makes a maggot a maggot and how to make a whelp a warrior. Stand alongside us, whelp and we'll make you a warrior yet.'

'The Scara know the hunt. The strength of sudden strike. The panic you instill from the shadow and tastiest, easiest places to tear flesh from bone. We teach the pack the way and it is for the warg or any to do the rest.'
He shakes his fur.
'We heed only brutality and cruelty to bring down our targets quickly and as painfully as possible. Our pack can teach you, but you must do the rest. We waste time by standing still. Choose us and run free.'
'Off with you until you have spoken to each of the emissaries. Return to me when you are done. I shall instruct you further.'

'Well done, I am amazed you had the attention span necessary to speak with them all. There may be hope for you yet. Now to the matter at hand. Choose. Choose a clan to represent while you fight for Angmar.
'All will welcome you. Freely shirk your allegiance like you have done your duty for so long. Drink of their blessing until you find a home that is welcoming to you. They are ordered to show no malice toward each other for now. This truce may not hold forever.
'Mordirith wants to see these Free Folk brought low. So the clans were convened to find the strongest among you in order to determine the best way to eliminate the forces here. Align yourself. That is all you need do.'
She smiles deviously.
'And when you tire of their boon, simply visit another to take their blessing in the first's stead. For the moment, it is simple. It shall not be forever. So do your best to prove to the master what clans should remain here in the Ettenmoors fighting and slaughtering the Free Folk.'

'Far be it from the Krahjarn to deny protocol. What, you think we're all war hungry tyrants like Akúlhun?'
He smirks.
'We are... some of us just hide it better. Talk with Malavin. That is the command. We will abide.'
'The pack is eager to hunt. The human is a barrier to our victory. Speak with her quick and then return to me.'

'I am Fathrug, and you look like you are ready to tear the flesh off a man. That is all we ask. Find the Men. Flay the Men. Leave their carcases littering the earth to turn the grass bloody. The Tarkrîp clan will strengthen your skills, help you stay in the fight longer. You'll be rather brutal about your business of hacking and rending the enemy, and while we won't teach you how to dodge a really nasty sword blow, we'll teach you to shrug it off and keep going.
'The Tarkrîp clan prizes scrappy warriors above all else, willing to strike at the enemy relentlessly!'

'You look soft, maggot. I should know the Ongbúrz are the heartiest clan in all of Angmar. We are not afraid of battle. We thrive in it. We revel in the clash of hammers, axes, and all the tools those bearded bastards bring against us. We know little fear. Our prowess is in our staying power.
'If you want to swing your blade wildly without thought about tomorrow, go talk with the Tarkrîp or the dogs. If you want to stand tall above all the others then take our blessing into battle. Toughness like ours should never be underestimated.'

'Come closer. Smell that? Mushrooms. Slime. Herbs. Poultices. The trappings of healers. Oh, yes, the other clans will tell you that they are the most stalwart, or furious, or violent, or sinister, but we are the force that keeps them standing. We are the strength behind them all.'
He chuckles.
'Half the pain that they don't feel is because of our stinking sludges and fungal brews. We know how to pound a spike into a missing arm if things go terribly ill, too. Sometimes the victim even survives long enough to make it more permanent.
'The others will tell you tales, but it is we that let them keep tongues wagging. Without us, they'd all be face down in the dirt. Stand with us. Stand with the Blogmal Clan.'

'She is born of the first enemy of Elves. She feeds her brood well and gives them all they need to spread the faith of the Dark Lord. Gifts that sting deeply, secretly, and brutally. Her poison courses to seep into the flesh and twist it to the darkness where she dwells.'
The queen chitters.
'She burns the victims from within so they sting, sting, sting, longer and more painfully. She is the corruption that seeds the earth with malicious intent. She is mother to her brood. Join with her and earn the gift to inflict suffering most profound.'

'Sharkey orders us north to help fight. So we come. We see why these clans fail. Too unbalanced. Too dedicated to destruction, or defence. Too dedicated to mysticism or the darkness.'
He shakes his head.
'No temperance leads to a quick end. Learning the field of battle. Discerning the weakness and strengths of your enemy provides a clearer path to victory. It is an even path we walk. It is the teaching of our master that we prize. The method to strike hard. The method to stand tall. The method to withstand a strike and turn a blade.
'I would lead the White Hand against any of these other clans and leave them in shambles. Join us and you will see what I mean.'
Spoke with the Shelob's Brood emissary
Spoke with the White Hand emissary
Spoke with the Krahjarn emissary
Spoke with the Scara-pack emissary
Spoke with the Tarkrîp emissary
Spoke with the Ongbúrz emissary
Spoke with the Blogmal emissary
You have spoken with Malavin

War-tyrant Akúlhun directed you to the war tent to speak with an Angmarim sorceress there named Malavin. Apparently she is here to assist, inspect, or guide the war effort. Whatever her purpose, it does not sit well with the War-tyrant.

'Listen here. A sorceress come from the north to tell me how the fight goes. Oh, she has the ear of the steward, but the arms are here, in the Ettenmoors. We've been fighting while they've been locked away in castles and steel barricades. What do they know about battling these people?'
It is a question expecting no answer.
'Bah... leadership back in Carn Dûm is looking for a new way to off these pesky Free Folk. So we got some new tricks available, meat. Each clan, and even the dirty dogs and sticky little spiders got their own emissaries here to help you new gits out. Oh and those southron Uruks too... talk to one of them and they'll give you a taste of what the leaders are thinking... don't get used to it though, maggot. These truces can only last so long....
'But first, they want me to send every maggot with snot dripping on their face up the hill to talk with her. Well... so be it. Better you go talk to her than me. She calls herself, Malavin.'
There is a short pause.
'If you get a chance, accidentally spit on her for me, would you?'

'Another veteran of the way? Or are you a new recruit? Honestly, I cannot tell the difference between a seasoned warrior and a whelp fresh from the pens or egg. I do, however know a thing or two about obedience and seeing that orders are carried out.'
She smirks wryly.
'Mordirith is displeased with the efforts here and organized an effort to entice you... warriors... with gifts. Each of the Orc clans, the Scara-pack, and Brood of Shelob send emissaries to entreat. He even allowed the White Hand at this table. Perhaps, in time there will be more. For now, it is these few.'
She pauses a moment to look you over.
'It appears that the steward of Carn Dûm is correct in his assessment. You are all in dire need of help. I invite you then to speak with the emissaries here in Gramsfoot. Learn what they offer you and choose their blessing. Each has been ordered, for now, to entreat with all of you. Provide for your until the council of our lord is complete.
'Run along now, and learn from each of the emissaries here and then return to me.'
'Orders is orders. You need to talk to the Priestess first.'
'Talk with the skinny witch, then you can talk to me.'
'Abide by the council's will and speak with Malavin.'
'Seek she who speaks for the lord of Carn Dûm. Our brood will wait our turn.'
'Sharkey's orders are clear, we let the woman speak... for now.'
Tutorial: Allegiance and Blessing

Malavin instructed you to speak to each of the emissaries representing the clans of Carn Dûm and beyond. They have blessings that they will seek to bestow upon you, provided you will serve in their name.

'A new recruit? Well then, let's get you outfitted and prepared for battle.'
The Orc seems all too pleased with his position.
'Once you start fighting and earning your keep in the Ettenmoors, I'll take commendations in exchange for my goods. You earn commendations for doing the work that no one else wants to do and slaughtering the Free Folk! Ha!'
<rgb=#00FF00>In Monster Play, completing quests and defeating Free People players awards <rgb=#FFFF00>commendations</rgb> and gold. <rgb=#FFFF00>Commendations</rgb> allow the purchase of not only skills, but also potions, food, and other items that provide short-term enhancements or immediate effects for your character.</rgb>
'Here, take this. Standard issue goods for all new recruits. Go on now. Open that up and see what I gives you!'

'There is hope for you, yet.'
The spider chitters.
'While using <rgb=#FFFF00>March!</rgb>, you can speak with allies and interact with items in the world. However, you cannot use any of your other abilities to fight against the foe while you are marching, so best to be quick to stop marching when it comes time to fight!
'Use the skill now, then visit the vendor Nadar near the front gate to learn more.'

'To strengthen your resolve, body, and abilities, you must earn skills and corruptions. In order to unlock the power of the corruptions and skills, you must speak with corruptors who will help you to unlock the deeper potency. As you grow in strength, so too will your access to greater and more malevolent corruptions.
'When you are prepared, speak with Lingemil. They will teach you more of your abilities, here in the Ettenmoors.'

When you speak with an NPC that has these additional roles, you will need to select the role you want to use from the context menu that opens when you speak with the NPC.</rgb>

'All eight legs and yet still no sense. Some spider tells you to spin a web and you just start spinning, hmmm? Well pay attention, and you might just learn something.'
The spider chitters.
'Good, speak with me again and purchase the skill <rgb=#FFFF00>March!</rgb>. Then, use the skill to prove that you have learned and know how to enable what you learn.'

Leave Gramsfoot by way of the hidden path along the mountainside to the west. Or, if you are feeling adventurous wander outside the main gate of Gramsfoot, but beware, the Freeps can attack you if you do not take the mountainside path. Your goal is to reach the keep, Dâr-gazag.

'Now, one last thing to do. The true power of our army lies at the end of a long path west out of the gates of Gramsfoot. There are other ways to get to the keep, but the safest path stays along the mountainside and keeps you above the fray until you are really ready to enter the fight.
'Go now, to the keep at Dâr-gazag and see the host assembled there to defend the Fragment of Mordirith's crown.'

Return to Akulhún for your newest orders

'There is little else that I can do to prepare you for what is beyond that gate.'
Uglash laughs.
'Time to prove yourself. Go to the War-tyrant. Tell him you are ready.'

'Listen well, Uruk. There are expectations that I have of you and our race. You should lead - from the back. Whipping these lesser creatures into a frenzy and making sure that the taste of flesh stays fresh in their gullets.
'You are prepared. Do not fail...'
He leans in close.
'Or I'll skin you myself.'
Tutorial: Know Your Role!
It is time to put all you have learned together and return to War-tyrant Akulhún for your orders.
Choose a clan and receive their blessing
'I do not care for the choice you made, only that you made one.'
The time has come to choose your clan allegiance. All you need do is speak with one of the emissaries and choose to represent them on the field of battle.

'This choice is an important one, for certain. But as the master has deemed, you can freely choose what clan you shall represent in the battle for a time.
'You should feel free to approach whichever tribe you choose without fear that you must always represent that clan. No, little worm, you can freely change your allegiances the same as you choose your diet for a day.'
She offers you a weak smile.
'Simply choose an emissary and accept their blessing. If you decide later that you dislike the benefits that their clan provides I am certain that they will abide by the master's law and allow you to freely choose your clan affiliation for now.
'Was that word too big for you? You seem to be staring at me more slack-jawed than usual. Perhaps, you should go make your choice.'

'Mae govannen, adventurer. I am Baranoth. I have come to assist in the cleansing of this foul place. While others would have you destroy any trace of defilement, I would have you aid me in understanding the very nature of what they sought to achieve here.
'There can be no guarantee that whatever twists the creatures in the apothecary has been contained within. We must endeavour to understand the corruption. If you find any notes of alchemical nature within, I urge you to preserve them and bring them to me. Make your way to the Medium Armour Quartermaster just to the west of Tordúr and purchase the gear you need to survive and thrive in the Ettenmoors.
Now that you are versed in the need for the gear that unlocks <rgb=#FFFF00>Audacity</rgb>, return to Captain-General Tordúr.
Speak with the Medium Armour Quartermaster and learn about <rgb=#FFFF00>Audacity</rgb>
'As a ${CLASS}, you should speak with the Medium Armour Quartermaster. They will have the gear you need to survive, and hopefully thrive, here in the Ettenmoors.'

'Greetings, ${CLASS}. Welcome to the Ettenmoors. Please, look through my wares and purchase all of the gear that you can. There is a vile pall that blankets this land. Our smiths have discovered a way to make wares that will allow those with stout hearts to overcome the miasma through sheer will, but this gear seems to be the only means by which we can focus.'
<rgb=#00FF00>Surviving in the Ettenmoors requires the acquisition of <rgb=#FFFF00>Audacity,</rgb> a special attribute unlocked with the gear you purchase here and earn throughout play within the Ettenmoors. You should spend a little coin to acquire your first suit of armour and accessories so that you can fully participate in the Ettenmoors.</rgb>
'If you are truly prepared, then there is only one more step to complete before you should enter the battle for the Ettenmoors.'

'My husband so greatly desires to speak with his people and mend the pain of the hurts they suffered that I fear he will give no thought to his own protection, ${PLAYER}. I turn then to you, and to those others who hold him dear!
'I ask this of you, ${PLAYER}, and of my husband's boon companions: Legolas of Eryn Lasgalen and Gimli the Dwarf, of Erebor. Where Elessar wishes to venture, I ask that you three travel first, with your ears listening and your eyes sharpened. Look for any sign that the Heirs of Castamir remain a danger to the kingdom or to the King, and make the path he plans to travel as secure as you may.
'Only this will ease the burden of my heart.'

'You will do as my Queen requests? I think it will prove unnecessary, but I do not want my bride to worry if it might be prevented! Nor do I want my people to wait for any help I might have offered.
'It is not an easy riddle to solve, ${PLAYER}, but I think I have the answer. The three of you will go ahead of me to visit the towns and cities of my kingdom, keeping watch for any sign of the Heirs of Castamir or their supporters, as Arwen requests, but you will go not only in search of danger. You will also go as my emissaries, and to begin my own mission of aid, doing what you can to help the people with their concerns.
'When you have determined the Heirs of Castamir are of no real danger to myself or the kingdom, you will return to me and I will depart with my own travelling companions to further your work. If this will satisfy my Queen and my Council, then I suppose I must be content with the delay. It will be a balm to my spirit to know that you three, at least, will have begun my mission to heal the kingdom of its hurt.'

'Another adventure begins, ${PLAYER}, of a sort. It will not take long to learn if the Heirs of Castamir are truly gone, and when we have done so Elessar can tour his kingdom.
'Let us start by journeying to the Harlond, my friends. The south-harbour is nearest to the city, and from there we can proceed west in search of news.'
Glindor has brought you to the Tower of Ecthelion, where King Elessar and Queen Arwen await you.
King Elessar is ready to speak with you about his plans.
King Elessar and his advisors discuss his plan to tour the kingdom and heal the hurts caused by the war.
Thalhír, the Warden of Laws, is in the Tower of Ecthelion and has been called to answer whether the Heirs of Castamir remain a threat to the peace of Gondor.
King Elessar and his advisors discuss his plan to tour the kingdom and heal the hurts caused by the war.
'King Elessar and Queen Arwen will see you now.'

'We accomplished much good in the fight against Mordor and the forces of Sauron, ${PLAYER}, and prevented the triumph of terrible evil! The War of the Ring, for so I have heard it called in the days since its ending, has left its mark upon us and upon our lands. Our victory came at great cost, and the losses suffered in its achievement still wound those of us who remain. Perhaps they always will. And yet, if I can ease the hurts of my kingdom, I would do it. Can I count upon you to help me with this aim?'
You assure Elessar that you are with him, and he smiles.
'I knew our minds would be alike in this. This, then, is my purpose: I wish to travel my kingdom, from town to town, speaking with the people. I wish to hear what it is they lack, and to provide it; I wish to know how the war has injured them, and do what I can to repair those injuries. I want my people to know that their King is with them, not a distant figure in the Tower of Ecthelion, but a man who knows them and will strive every day of his life to prove he is worthy of Gondor.
'I want to tour the kingdom, and see what I can do to heal the hurts of the war.'

'I hesitate to mention it, my King, for I understand the majority of your people are overwhelmed with happiness at both the successful conclusion of the war and with your marriage to the Queen. I do not wish to spoil the broth of positive sentiment by dwelling upon the inclusion of one or two poor ingredients, and those in such tiny quantities.'
Thalhír clears his throat and looks uncomfortable.
'But there have been whispers of discontent in the city following your happy marriage, my King. Few perhaps, but some. I am sure they will disappear in time, as did those of the supporters of the Withered Tree, but as of yet they remain. I have heard tell from other members of the Council that people in the lower circles of the city speak wishfully of the Heirs of Castamir, praying for their return and believing they soon will.'
Instance: A King Should See His Kingdom
Queen Arwen is in the Tower of Ecthelion and wishes to speak with you about a special task.
King Elessar is in the Tower of Ecthelion, waiting to hear if you will agree to this new plan.

'It is to the Tower of Ecthelion we go, there to audience with King Elessar and Queen Arwen, the rulers of victorious Gondor.'
Glindor, King Elessar's herald, is outside the stables in Minas Tirith (Midsummer).
Gimli is north-east of the Harlond, in King's Gondor.
Legolas is north-east of the Harlond, in King's Gondor.

'A king has returned to Gondor, ${PLAYER}, and all the kingdom celebrates! And yet he is not content to rest on the laurels of his deserved victory over Sauron.
'I was instructed to bring you to see him. Will you come with me?'

'My feet are sore already, ${PLAYER}, and we have come to just the first of the places Aragorn told us to visit. His kingdom is larger than it looks on the maps, and Legolas and I have already crossed it once!'
Gimli falls silent.
'I named him Aragorn again, didn't I? He will have as many names as a Wizard next, but he has been a trusted companion through many adventures, and for that I will learn them all.
'He is not the king of any other kingdoms, is he?'

'We have come to the South-gate of the Rammas Echor, through which lies the Harlond, the south-harbour of Minas Tirith. It was held by Orcs of Mordor during the war, and they did not expect the arrival of Elessar aboard the ships of the Corsairs!'
Legolas smiles.
'They did not expect Legolas Greenleaf or Gimli, son of Glóin, either. That much was clear to all!'
'There will be fewer Orcs to fight inside the Harlond this time, I wager.'
Chapter 1.1: A King Should See His Kingdom
King Elessar, recently crowned and newly wedded, is eager to heal the hurts of his kingdom and to move Gondor into an age of prosperity.
Talk to Othanar inside the Harlond
Clean up rubble piles inside the Harlond (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'What do you want, stranger? Don't like what you hear, do you? It doesn't matter to me what you like and what you don't. Gondor changed once, and it can change again; folk like you might want to watch where you stick your noses.
'Friend of mine in Arnach heard the Heirs of Castamir are gathering in strength and will soon return. Their leader Balakhôr survived the fighting and slipped away to safety before he could be executed... such a pity for the upstart king! Now Balakhôr plans to overthrow the new king and his foreign bride. It was them, and people like them, that brought the war upon us: the land remembers it all. Won't be long before it has its revenge upon them, using Balakhôr as its instrument.'
You insist that Balakhôr is very dead, and Berthon snorts.
'That's not what my friend in Arnach says, and I think I'll be listening to him and not to you, stranger.'
'That went well, ${PLAYER}.'
'Now move on. I don't like the smell of you.'

'How goes the work, ${PLAYER}? Gimli and I have made ourselves useful.
'Some of the folk here seem... distrusting... of Elves and dwarves. It may be caused by fear or by superstition, but most have given us a wide berth even as they keep one eye upon us. It is nothing to me, but Gimli is bothered by it.'

'Bothered by it? You wound me, Legolas! I am no delicate crystal, and can give insult better than any of these cowards... should the need arise, which King Elessar should hope it does not, since we are here on an errand of peace and restoration.
'But has the Elf-hearing of which you often boast abandoned you? For I heard those men speak the name \qBalakhôr,\q and it is not so common a name that it could belong to anyone but the leader of the Heirs of Castamir, about whom we seek tidings!'
'See that gathering of Gondorians to the east? Approach them and <rgb=#00FF00>listen</rgb> to their conversation, and you will see I have not invented this worry!'
'Is this true? Do they really speak of Balakhôr the Scourge?'

'Begin by cleaning up rubble piles throughout the Harlond. Earlier today some folk offered to pick up loose wooden planks around the port, and left them leaning upright at several locations to the south-west; if you can gather those for me I would appreciate it. And also take care of the rat problem, if you would.'
'Your friends work still, by the docks to the south-east.'
'Most of these folk have given us a wide berth even as they keep one eye upon us. It is nothing to me, but Gimli is bothered by it.'
The crowd glares at you with distrust

Legolas suggested that someone to the south-west must be overseeing the repairs of the Harlond.
Othanar asked you to clean up rubble piles, collect wooden planks, and defeat the rats that now infest the Harlond.
Othanar oversees the rebuilding of the Harlond by the north-eastern entrance.

'I do not think this expedition of ours will take very long, ${PLAYER}. If there are folk here who believe the Heirs of Castamir will return, they will soon see that King Elessar holds their fortunes dear and seeks to repair the damage done during the war. They will leave the Heirs of Castamir in the past, where they belong, and Gondor will move forward.
'Let us find someone inside the Harlond, to the south-west, who will tell us how we can help repair the damage done to the South-harbour.'

'You are here to help? That is good. We turn none away who desire to help cleanse the South-harbour of the filth left behind by the Orcs of Mordor! The land remembers the scars, but it is up to its people to stitch them up and allow them to heal. Despite many offers of help, there is still plenty to be done.
'Begin by cleaning up rubble piles throughout the Harlond. Earlier today some folk offered to pick up loose wooden planks around the port, and left them leaning upright at several locations to the south-west; if you can gather those for me I would appreciate it.
'There has also been an increase in rats here of late... I think they fled the Corsair ships for new homes, which I would not ordinarily begrudge them, but now the creatures trouble the food-stores we keep here for the workers, and I need them gone. Will you and your fellows complete these tasks for me? You will on behalf of the King? I do not see him, but very well. I care not for whom you do these tasks, so long as they are done.'
'Let us find someone inside the Harlond, to the south-west, who will tell us how we can help repair the damage done to the South-harbour.'

'You almost had me believing that King Elessar himself would bring these wooden planks to me, stranger. I am disappointed to see that is not the case.
'But you have my thanks for this work, all the same. Your friends work still, by the docks to the south-east.'

'You upheld your side of the bargain? I have done the same. I asked around Arnach, and... well, it seems that a few of the people here have heard that Balakhôr the Scourge survived the fighting at Pelargir and escaped into the wilderness. Some folk believe they saw him personally, though from a distance.
'He supposedly made camp to the south of Arnach, in view of the river. If you wish to learn the truth of it, I suggest you there begin your search.'

'This camp-site might have belonged to anyone. Just because it bears the signs of being a Corsair camp does not mean it was made by Balakhôr. Anyone could have come ashore here.
'Do I need to remind you that we saw him die aboard the Night-jewel? He could not escape from the Dead, and did not. It beggars belief, ${PLAYER}!'

'Gimli is right: this camp might have been made by anyone. Balakhôr did not leave the deck of the Night-jewel alive.
'But this too can be true, ${PLAYER}: it may not matter.'
'Balakhôr is dead. Why do the folk of Gondor have such difficulty believing it?'
'We should follow these whispers of Balakhôr to Arnach. Perhaps there we will learn from where they began. Arnach is to the south-west of here, in Lossarnach.'

'I will ask around town and see what I can learn of the Corsairs and about Balakhôr. Perhaps while I do, you will take care of some of the foes that do endanger Arnach? There may be some few brigands, as ever, but I speak mainly of wild threats: wolves, avanc, and any beasts that grow bold when unopposed.'
'Some folk believe Balakhôr survived the fighting at Pelargir and made camp to the south of Arnach, in view of the river. If you wish to learn the truth of it, I suggest you there begin your search.'

'Balakhôr died on the deck of his banner-ship, the Night-jewel, at the hands of the Army of the Dead. We saw him die. About whom, then, do these rumours speak? Do the Heirs of Castamir have a new leader?
'We should follow these whispers to Arnach. Perhaps there we will learn from where they began. Arnach is to the south-west of here, in Lossarnach.'

'Welcome, my friend, to Arnach! What brings you hither?'
You explain that you seek word of Corsair activity along the coast of Lossarnach, and that some folk of Gondor believe Balakhôr and the Heirs of Castamir still threaten the King's peace. Baranor rubs his chin.
'I do not doubt that some Corsairs fled into the wild when the fighting turned against them, but their numbers must be quite small, shouldn't they? I will ask around the town and see what I can learn. Perhaps while I do, you will take care of some of the foes that do endanger Arnach? There may be some few brigands, as ever, but I speak mainly of wild threats: wolves, avanc, and any beasts that grow bold when unopposed.'
