'Will you see Glassiel safely back to her home? Gimli and I will meet you at Glaniath when you return, and we will proceed together on to Pelargir.'

'If you wish to be of use to the folk of Lebennin, you can oppose some of the dangers to be found between here and my home of Halach. Wild creatures and the occasional hold-out from the war are still to be found prowling the lands between Erui and Halach.
'Meet me at my home when I have safely arrived and I can put you further to work. I understand you have been given a duty to help us by the King himself?'

'Bring in some fishing nets down by the piers, and gather up a couple crates of building materials around town, and you might fill the King's sails with wind, and leave the Heirs of Castamir without. Do these tasks for me and I'll share what else I know, and that would be a help to the King.'

'What if someone has taken Balakhôr's place, adopting his name and appearance in an attempt to rally the Heirs of Castamir? We should tell Baranor of this possibility, so he can keep watch and guard against it.'

'We will remain alert for any supporters of the Heirs who appear, and I trust you will do the same as you continue south and westward, to the Crossings of Erui. There are several small villages beyond the Erui that may foster similar sentiments as those here in Arnach. Good fortune go with you.'
'I hope the Lone Lady of Erui knows she now has the love and belief of all of Lebennin.'

'You say Angbor, the Lord of Lamedon, directed that the armour of the Usurper be sent to Pelargir for safekeeping? That was a wise decision, for Castamir's armour has already proven unable to remain lost. Better to keep it under the watchful eye of Sirgon, Lord of Lebennin.
'But a thought occurs to me. If someone were trying to convince others that he was Castamir's successor, or pretending to be Balakhôr himself, he might make use of artifacts such as armour or weapons that once belonged to the Usurper. We should make sure the armour came to Sirgon as Angbor intended.
'But Elessar also wanted us to help the people. Will you see Glassiel safely back to her home? Gimli and I will meet you at Glaniath when you return, and we will proceed together on to Pelargir.'
'I hope I did not miss many other such adventures while I was aboard the ship!'

'It is good of you to offer to bring me to my home, but I can find my own way.
'Still, if you wish to be of use to the folk of Lebennin, you can oppose some of the dangers to be found between here and my home of Halach. Wild creatures and the occasional hold-out from the war are still to be found prowling the lands between Erui and Halach.
'Meet me at my home when I have safely arrived and I can put you further to work. I understand you have been given a duty to help us by the King himself?'
'I speak of the Five Sisters of Lebennin, who protect these lands even now.'
'I speak of the Five Sisters of Lebennin, who protect these lands even now.'

'The blood spilt in these waters during the Kin-strife of Gondor so changed the Lady of Erui that she became estranged from her sisters, and turned her anger upon the folk who dwelt nearby. Not long ago she raised the Armour of the Usurper from these waters and did battle against her sisters, but at last they were able to soothe her rage and she was healed of her hurts.
'So I float these baskets upon her waters as tokens of both forgiveness and love, and I hope that she takes notice of them.'

'It is a good story, so far as it goes. A little unbelievable, I think.'
Gimli stares at you with amazement when you tell him it is true, and you witnessed the end of the tale as you passed through Lebennin during the war.
'Really? I missed more than I thought when I agreed to take the ship from Pelargir with Legolas! What happened to the Armour of the Usurper after the River-maidens calmed their sister of her anger?'
'They say the Heirs of Castamir are still around. If you are loyal to the King, as I am, you will remain on your guard in these lands.'

'How went your visit to Halach, ${PLAYER}?
'The Heirs of Castamir may never truly disappear, but I think it is becoming clear that their power wanes. An imposter is not as great a threat to Gondor as Balakhôr himself would have been.
'The time approaches when we can return to King Elessar and tell him his tour can proceed.'

'You helped make the lands between the Crossings and Halach more safe? I thank you for it! I was not in any danger, for the blessings of the Five Sisters are upon me, and their influence extends into the lands washed by their rivers. Still, it is a welcome deed.
'King Elessar was good to send you to us.'

'Mercy upon me for listening, stranger, but I understand you're here on the King's business? That is a joy to me and mine, for certain, but you might want to know that some of the folk hereabout aren't as true as my family. I've a-heard some talk that the Heirs of Castamir never surrendered, but lie in wait, fostering their strength.
'Seems to me a good way to fight some of these rumours might be to show the King is nearer to us than distance would indicate. Maybe you're here to do just that? If'n you bring in some fishing nets down by the piers, and gather up a couple crates of building materials around town, you might fill the King's sails with wind, and leave the Heirs of Castamir without? Do these tasks for me and I'll share what else I know, and that would be a help to the King.'
'The King will be pleased to hear how you helped the people of Halach, if such is your intent.'

'I thank you for doing the tasks I had set before me, friend! Do not be cross with me, for I put the time you spared me to good use!
'My loyalty is to the King, but some of the men I work beside are not as true to Gondor as I am. I have learned from their speech that the Heirs of Castamir have taken to lighting the beacons of Gondor when they find them unguarded, as a sign to their supporters. I do not know if it is true, but that is what I heard. Look for lit beacons and there will be serpents nearby, snakes who endanger the King and his kingdom.
'At least, that is what I was told. Go from Halach with my thanks, and with the warning I give you!'

'Balakhôr need not have survived to inspire those who believed in his purpose. Is it not possible he might have become, in death, more of a symbol to his people than he could have remained in life? A man can be slain; it is more difficult to fully destroy that for which he stood.
'What if someone has taken his place, ${PLAYER}? What if someone has adopted his name and his appearance in an attempt to rally the Heirs of Castamir? We should tell Baranor of this possibility, so he can keep watch and guard against it.'

'What have you discovered, ${PLAYER}? Was there any truth to the rumours spoken among the people of Arnach? Did Balakhôr survive the war?'
You recount to Baranor what you discovered, and what Legolas had to say about the fallen leader of the Heirs of Castamir. The guardsman nods grimly.
'Aye, an imposter could cause trouble for King Elessar and for Gondor just as easily as Balakhôr himself might have done. We will remain alert for any who appear, and I trust you will do the same as you continue south and westward, to the Crossings of Erui. There are several small villages beyond the Erui that may foster similar sentiments as those here in Arnach. Good fortune go with you.'

'These are the Crossings of Erui, where Castamir the Usurper perished long ago during the Kin-strife of Gondor, when his rebellion was at last ended, and the rule of the kingdom was restored. But Kings and Stewards rule from distant castles and towers, and our people need the blessing of nearer protectors.
'And so I and other good people of Lebennin float baskets on the river in memory of the Five Sisters, who protected this land in days gone. Some folk believed they were only a myth, but it is not so!'

'As you are going soon to Pelargir, you will bring these tokens to him and show him the mind of Glaniath's families, yes?'

'At any rate, the sooner we go to Pelargir the sooner we will return to Minas Tirith with the tidings we sought. We have heard plenty of whispers and rumours, but little in the way of real danger. I suppose that is good, but it is also a pity, for my axe needs swinging!'
'You wish to see Sirgon, Lord of Lebennin? His manor is down the street to the west.'
'Meet me in my room of keepsakes, to the north. I want to show you something.'
'See the keepsakes I have gathered in my life, and know what I have come to miss.'
'Speak with Arvellon and see what you think. He should be near the centre of town.'
'Will you gather tokens from the collection boxes around town so Lord Sirgon will see how many families support my proposal?'

'Welcome to my home, ${PLAYER}. I offer you what hospitality I can, though it cannot hope to match that of the King in Minas Tirith. What brings you so far from the White City?'
You tell Sirgon that King Elessar has sent you to help heal the hurts of the war and to prepare the way for his own tour of the kingdom.
'That is a worthy purpose. The war... the war may be ended, but the scars it left behind cut deep. How fare the towns within my purview?'
Reluctantly, you tell Sirgon the people of Glaniath have proposed that he step down as Lord of Lebennin and leave the lordship to his son Faltharan, and show him the tokens they cast for that purpose.

'Maybe the people of Glaniath are right, ${PLAYER}.
'The days of my youth are far behind me now. Who will follow a leader so easily captured in war, as I was by the Men of Harad? Respect is hard to gain, but easy to lose. There were moments I despaired, and thought Lebennin would be better served if I never returned.'
Sirgon sighs heavily and looks you in the eye.
'This was not supposed to be my life. Meet me in my room of keepsakes, to the north. I want to show you something.'

'I was once the master of the fleets of Gondor, ${PLAYER}. I sailed across the Bay of Belfalas at the direction of the Steward, and brought the might of Gondor to bear wherever it was needed. I remember the smell of the salt on the spray, the cry of the gulls overhead, the wind in my hair, the rocking of the ship's deck beneath my feet.
'When I was held captive during the war, I feared for my family and for the people in my charge... but I am shamed to admit that I also feared I would die on land. I was a man of the sea, ${PLAYER}, but in recent days I have felt penned up in this city, in this kingdom, in my very title. \qLord of Lebennin!\q Rather would I be once again the Lord of Ships, the Lord of Tide and Wave!
'See the keepsakes I have gathered in my life, and know what I have come to miss.'

'I did not understand this proposal when Arvellon told it to us, and I still do not. He expects Sirgon to simply abandon the lordship of Lebennin because a few families thought he should? No dwarf would do this.
'At any rate, the sooner we go to Pelargir the sooner we will return to Minas Tirith with the tidings we sought. We have heard plenty of whispers and rumours, but little in the way of real danger. I suppose that is good, but it is also a pity, for my axe needs swinging!'

'It brings me joy to see you return to Pelargir, my friend, with the spectre of war behind us!
'You wish to see Sirgon, Lord of Lebennin? His manor is down the street to the west. He will be pleased to see you, I imagine, but be warned that his captivity during the war left its mark upon him and his spirit is not as vital as once it was.
'He is still strong and stern, do not mistake me! But he is changed, and weariness lies upon his brow.'

'So many memories.
'Perhaps my son should succeed me. It took the folk of Glaniath to make me realize something I think I have known for these past few months, but did not express. My heart does not belong on land. I wish to sail again, ${PLAYER}!
'I can better serve King Elessar from the deck of a ship, as I did in prior years. Faltharan should rule in Lebennin.'

'My father has been seized by one of his moods again, I see. He has always suffered from the call of the gulls, the pull of the sea, but it has been worse in recent days.
'I do not desire to rule in Lebennin, but I will do so if that is my father's wish, and the will of the King.'
'Faltharan should rule in my stead, if the King will have him.'
'These stuffed birds were a wedding gift from an old friend, drowned at sea.'
'I traded for this gem in a seaside market, twenty years ago. It remains as brilliant today!'
'No, I never saw this creature alive! I recovered its bones on a southern voyage.'
'I have taken many an enemy's shield in battle. I display some of them here.'
'This fellow set one of my ships alight with evil sorcery. Now I keep an eye upon him here.'
'A friend gave me a number of tapestries depicting friendship between Gondor and Rohan.'
'This tapestry depicting Folca and the Boar was a gift. The Rohirrim hold him in great esteem.'
'This creature crawled upon my deck while we were in port. Now his head hangs upon my wall!'
'Would you believe I found this bear far to the south, in a land of snow and ice? It is true!'
'I found this fellow just off the Langstrand, a few years ago. He sings beautifully.'
'The Uruk who wore this boarded my ship just off the Shield Isles. Now it is mine.'
'The armour of my first slain Orc. Had I perished, my armour might be in a case like this one.'

'While Gimli and I waited for you to arrive, a resident of this town came to speak with us. Arvellon, he is called, and he was most interested to learn we plan to continue on to Pelargir. The matter that occupies his thought may be of interest to King Elessar.
'Speak with Arvellon and see what you think. He should be near the centre of town.'

'You are welcome to Glaniath, my friend, and on the King's business, no less! It is remarkable how much can change in the matter of mere months!
'The war left its mark upon Lebennin, and I expect it has done the same in other areas of Gondor. But here it marked us deep, for Sirgon our lord was captured by the Haradrim, and while he was freed from their bonds the experience changed him. I fear he is no longer suited for rule, and it would be just for the King to permit him to step down. Faltharan, his son, is fully capable of following his father as Lord of Lebennin.
'I have called for families of Glaniath to cast tokens in favour of this proposal. Will you gather these tokens from the collection boxes around town so Lord Sirgon will see how many families support my proposal?'

'So many tokens have been cast in support of my proposal! This is nearly all!
'I want you to understand that folk of Glaniath hold no ill will toward Sirgon in their hearts. His experience was a mournful one, and it is wrong to expect him to carry on without harm. Let him cede the rule of Lebennin to his son Faltharan. That will be best for him, and it will be best for the lands he must govern. I am certain King Elessar will approve, but we must take single steps first. Sirgon served Gondor, and with the war finished he has earned a peaceful rest, and should take it with our gratitude.
'As you are going soon to Pelargir, you will bring these tokens to him and show him the mind of Glaniath's families, yes?'

'I beg your pardon, stranger, but I could not help but notice your argument with that Elf over the way. Did he give you insult? I have seen such as he treat others with disrespect, and often enough that it has become to me a sad indicator that all of that folk believe themselves to be our betters.'
You tell the woman that he took issue with some statements you made about the new Queen of Gondor, and she studies you closely.
'Is that so?' she asks. 'Perhaps you would like to hear my own thoughts on the subject?'

'Castamir's armour remains where it was left? I told you it was so. But look here!
'The skulking woman is back. She watches us from yonder, pretending that we are not the object of her attention... but it is clear to me she spies upon us even now.'

'I have had an idea, ${PLAYER}. If we stage a performance for the benefit of this spy, we might be able to learn if she works for the Heirs of Castamir, and turn that knowledge to our benefit.'
Legolas smiles at you briefly before the Elf adopts a pained expression.

'I should have expected no less from such as you!' Legolas exclaims. Then he lowers his voice.
'Now you should stroll most casually in the direction of the skulking spy, my friend. Perhaps she will be interested to speak to you, and if you can draw from her some knowledge of the Heirs of Castamir or their supporters, we will be aided.

Angmar Reborn, Chapter 1
'He-Who-Was-Drostan knows well the ways of the Iron Crown.'

'Do not think ill of Nekhtan, my friend. He is right—I have not fulfilled my Fém.
'Neither have I forgotten the man I was not so long ago: Drostan of the Trév Duvárdain. Deeds alone cannot atone for my past words and actions, and I am well aware of that.
'However, I say there is still worth to be found in the life I once lived!
'Do you wish to hear the tale, my friend?'

'You wish to know what became of Crannog, do you? I thought as much.
'If that is what you truly wish, I will tell you.'

Nekhtan shakes his head.
'With their victory, Claghórd and the Trév Duvárdain had won the right to govern the affairs of the tribes of Angmar until another Clúcath was called. But Claghórd, guided by the hand of the Iron Crown, intended to make certain it never happened again. After a few days, Claghórd and emissaries of the Iron Crown came to Aughaire. They demanded that five of us come willingly to Carn Dûm or the Iron Crown would send their servants to burn our village in the night. Crannog pleaded with them to take fewer, and though it did not appear to please the emissaries, Claghórd relented, and asked only for one of the Trév Gállorg.
'Fearing what awaited our people in Carn Dûm, Crannog offered himself to the Iron Crown that others might be spared.'
Nekhtan's voice wavers.
'The old fool...
'His bargain had been for nothing, for the emissaries of Iron Crown returned the very next day and they were no longer so eager to negotiate. They took more of our people as each day passed, and soon, many of us fled Aughaire that they might not find us upon their return. Crannog had urged us to shelter at Bail Avarc, and so that is where we went.
'Fifty-eight of the Trév Gállorg have been taken, and we have heard naught of any of them. I only wish that Crannog were still here. He would know what to do....'

'Twice now Clúcath has claimed those dear to me: first, my father Násan and now, Crannog. I will not suffer another loss!
'These pretenders who still call themselves the Iron Crown hide behind the walls of Carn Dûm. I know that ways into the city still remain, and I think that Soltakh knows them better than he wishes to admit.
'Soltakh—or He-Who-Is-Changed as Crannog perhaps too generously named him—was once of the Trév Duvárdain, after all. His Fém remains unfulfilled, and he has much still to do to prove himself to the Trév Gállorg.
'If there are ways into the city, we must strike at the Iron Crown before their grip upon Angmar is too strong to be broken!'

'Much has changed since last you came to Angmar, my friend. In truth, even to my own eyes, it has changed since I returned.
'Not long ago, Crannog gave to me a Fém—a purpose—that led me into the east. I am ashamed to even think it, but I wish I had never left. After Carn Dûm was abandoned, I was to follow the remnants of the Iron Crown to the lands of Mount Gundabad. Many of the Trév Duvárdain travelled with them, despite the countless divisions that had grown between their tribesmen and the Iron Crown after the False King was deposed. The Iron Crown sought for something in the lands of Câr Bronach, but as their search grew more desperate, more and more of the Trév Duvárdain forsook the Iron Crown and fled into the hills.
'It was there I greeted them, neither as friend or foe, but as one who also sought to walk a new path. I gave shelter to them at Eiricháv, and for a time, it seemed that we might soon return to Angmar in friendship with nothing more to fear of the Iron Crown.
'Indeed, I heard that the High Priestess of the Iron Crown, a woman named Ásachal, had been slain in the heights of Tûr Fúar. Imagine my surprise, then, when I saw her lead her forces out of the gates of Agal Dûn some days after that!
'I tried to follow them as they crossed Bálach Iaran, but I was discovered. I managed to slay my attackers, but one of their crossbow bolts pierced my shin. It was only with the help of Aighrig that I was able to make it back to Eiricháv and tend to my wounds. Even so, I could not follow the Iron Crown until I could stand on my own again.
'By the time I got to Aughaire, it was too late. Crannog was nowhere to be found, and I learned from Nekhtan that another Clúcath had been called between the Trév Gállorg and the Trév Duvárdain.
'Alas, I cannot speak to what I did not witness. If you wish to know what happened, better you hear it from Nekhtan!'

'Yes?'
You ask Nekhtan what has happened in Angmar since the return of the Iron Crown. You mention that Soltakh spoke of another Clúcath—one called by the Trév Duvárdain.
'That much is true, ${PLAYER}. A great deal happened after Soltakh travelled into the east, and though he may not believe it, I do not begrudge him his absence when the Iron Crown returned.
'It seems so long ago now, but for a time Aughaire knew peace, or so we thought. The Iron Crown had crept back into the shadows, but from within the darkness, their gaze was still fixed upon us. I sensed something, and always I felt uneasy in the new way of things after the fall of the False King, but there was no danger to be found. The Iron Crown had gone. Carn Dûm was abandoned, and the Angmarim made for Bálach Iaran. After they crossed into the Iron Pass, we saw no more of them and they fled into the East.
'When many of the Trév Duvárdain returned from the East in the wake of their masters in the Iron Crown, I feared what might become of Angmar. And I was right to!
'It was not long after that the Trév Duvárdain began to trouble us once more, and though I did not know it then, everything we had fought for was about to be taken from us.'
'I have said enough and done too little. Nekhtan knows the truth of what befell the Trév Gállorg at Clúcath.'

'My heart is light with hope, even in so dark a place... Crannog lives!
'I cannot thank you enough, ${PLAYER}. I feared that we would be too late to save him. Alas, we must not forget what we have come here to do. High Priestess Ásachal and the Iron Crown must be stopped. The shard of Tauressar must be destroyed or any victory we win this day will ring hollow!'
Soltakh gestures to Nekhtan, and he returns a knowing nod.
'Do not worry for us, my friend. Nekhtan and I will get him out of here!'

'How glad I am to see you again, ${PLAYER}.
'Nekhtan and I were able to escort Crannog out of Gwathrenost, but I regret that we could not aid you in the last fight against the Iron Crown. You need not tell me of your success, though, for there are none in Angmar who do not know of it! By the time we returned to Bail Avarc, I heard shouts celebrating that the bódraillan were freed from the shard's enchantment. They cast down their weapons and walked out of Carn Dûm! My tribesmen—of both tribes—have returned to their families and loved ones, and it seems this terrible nightmare is at an end.
'I can hardly believe it... but the Iron Crown is no more! You are a true friend to Trév Gállorg!'
'Go, speak with Nekhtan. We must strike before it is too late!'

'Who... who is that there? Please... help me...'
Crannog struggles to see, his senses weakened by his imprisonment.
'${PLAYER}... can it be? You... came....'

'Welcome, ${PLAYER}. I am gladdened to see you again and in not so dire a circumstance!'
Crannog coughs, still clearly recovering from his imprisonment.
'Do not worry yourself on my account, my friend. Many of my wounds will heal in time, and those that might not will at least be soothed by a fine feast. After Mordirith was cast down, I wished to believe that the Iron Crown fell with him. But that is rarely the case, isn't it? Always there are those who cling to power, unwilling to face their own weakness.
'With your help, we have cast off the last of the sad legacy of the Iron Crown. After so many long years, we are free of the Witch-king and his servants!
'But now, we must decide what will become of Angmar....'
'You are a true friend of mine and of the Trév Gállorg. The Iron Crown has fallen!'

Angmar Reborn, Chapter 3

'For too long, I would not allow myself to believe what I knew to be true, but when I saw what became of the bódraillan... I...'
Finrúth buries her face in her hands for a moment.
'I am ashamed that I did not abandon the tribe when the others did. I held hope that the Iron Crown might still deliver us to some better future, but I see now that I was a fool. You are a friend of the Trév Gállorg, are you not? The Trév Duvárdain were not always like this, despite what you might think. We are a strong people, and as we always have, we did what was necessary to preserve our tribe. But Claghórd and Domongart before him have betrayed us to the Iron Crown for their own gain—to masters who care nothing for us.
'With that accursed shard, High Priestess Ásachal will take everything from us. There will be no Trév Gállorg, Trév Duvárdain, or even the Iron Crown—only the bódraillan and their terrible Witch-queen. And we won't even remember what we have lost!
'Before I left Carn Dûm, I heard that Crannog was being kept in the Witch-king's tower—Gwathrenost, they call it. The chieftain of the Trév Gállorg lives, but only barely, and I do not think the Iron Crown intend to free him. He has witnessed his people become bódraillan, and I think it is only some mercy or cruelty by High Chieftain Claghórd that spared him from that fate. Perhaps he has become one of them by now, perhaps not. That is all I know, Southron.
'I only hope that what I have told you can help to put an end to this before it is too late!'

'A stone that can bend wills...
'Such a thing was long considered a legend among the Trév Gállorg, but for it to truly exist? It is unthinkable!'

'You have my thanks, Southron.'
Finrúth eats, perhaps more swiftly than you or she expected. In between bites of rib and potato, she speaks.
'I must admit, I doubted the rumours that the free-folk of Angmar had taken to welcoming the outcasts of the Trév Duvárdain. When I arrived, though, I saw others of my tribe here among you and I knew that I had found shelter—at least for the moment. I have never been more grateful to have been proven wrong!'
Finrúth pauses, setting the plate on the ground beside her. After a moment, her demeanour sharpens.
'Do you know why I have come? Why I would turn my back upon my people all of a sudden? It is not that I have had a change of heart. The Trév Duvárdain were victorious at Clúcath and to govern Angmar is our right. I say to you that the Iron Crown means to cast us aside—and that those who lead the Trév Duvárdain are all too eager to let them!
'I saw things... things that I was not meant to see when the Iron Crown travelled to Mount Gundabad. Beneath Tûr Fúar, the Drearspire, I spied one of the lost Oath-stones of legend: Tauressar. I saw what becomes of those who swear oaths upon it, whether they wish to or not! If the Iron Crown is not stopped, we will all become bódraillan: oath-thralls! Our tribes will mean nothing to us!
'If you will listen, I will tell you everything I know. What say you?'
'Listen to me, ${PLAYER}, and I will tell you what I know of Tauressar and the bódraillan.'

A hearty meal and a waterskin can be found at Bail Avarc.

'You must listen to me... before it is too late!
'This land has known too much sorrow, and I fear that darker days lie ahead! I spoke to Soltakh and warned him that the Iron Crown means to make bódraillan of us all. He may not remember me, but I remember him. All among the Trév Duvárdain know of Drostan the exile... and of the one who was called Avair. I will speak no more of her—her deeds have not been forgotten to the Trév Gállorg and I doubt those of hers or Domongart's ilk would find welcome here among them.
'Do you know what I mean by bódraillan, Southron? It means \qoath-thralls\q in the tongue of my people, but it is worse than it sounds. The Trév Gállorg taken captive by the Iron Crown were the first... and their minds are no longer their own. I thought that was the worst of it, but then they took some of us! It won't be long now... until the rest are... taken and... changed.'
Finrúth appears to be exhausted, and she slumps against the nearby crates.
'I didn't have time to gather many of my belongings when I fled Carn Dûm and I am tired from the journey. Might... I beg for a meal and some water?'

'There you are, ${PLAYER}!
'So much has happened, and it is hard to speak to all of it. The Iron Crown is defeated, our people are free, and Iarandír is truly our land once again.
'After the parley, I now believe that there might be some measure of peace to be found between the Trév Gállorg and the Trév Duvárdain. It will not be perfect, for nothing is, but it is the start of something new—and that is enough!
'Crannog told me long ago that I would know when I had fulfilled my Fém. It is done, my friend, and I could not have done it without you.'

'It is beautiful, is it not? If I am not mistaken, the skies seem clearer this day than they have been since the days of my youth.
'As I said to you once, it is the place of a chieftain to direct his people to do great things, even in the face of danger. Many steps still remain on your path, but to guide you, I bestow upon you a new Fém.'
Crannog whispers in your ear.
'I am certain you will fulfil it, ${PLAYER}. If ever your path leads you back to Iarandír, you are welcome among us.
'It is a new day, my friend. Iarandír is our land and our fates are our own!'

'It has been many years since the Trév Gállorg and Trév Duvárdain last spoke beyond their duties to the rites of old. Perhaps it is time that changed...'
Crannog appears to ponder for a moment, and then turns his attention back to you.
'Let us send word to all of the Trév Gállorg and Trév Duvárdain, be they outcast or not. We will meet at Fail-á-Khro once more, but we do not meet to undertake the rites of old. For too long the shadows of Angmar have cast a darkness between us, and it is time that ended. We will meet to parley and settle what we may with the Trév Duvárdain. Although the title of High Chieftain has been left vacant, the Trév Duvárdain are the ruling tribe and I will not call another Clúcath after all that happened. Whether they choose to heed my words or not is their choice to make, and no matter the answer, I will honour it.
'But I would not squander the moment that has been set before us, ${PLAYER}. Angmar stands on the cusp of its rebirth, and it will be our hands that shape it—not those of the Witch-king, nor those of the Iron Crown.
'It is time we set out, ${PLAYER}. Won't you come with us?'

Angmar Reborn, Chapter 2
'You ought to speak to Lágsaith. It sounds like some of our work has already been done—and by a few of these Trév Duvárdain no less!'
'Please, hear me out! I swear I do not mean to deceive you!'
'We need to find out what the Iron Crown is doing at Sant Lhoer and Thaurisgar. If we can aid the others in the course of our efforts, all the better!'

'Even with all I know of the Iron Crown, it is hard to believe what you've told me, ${PLAYER}.
'I am glad that Oganuin will not trouble us any longer, but if the creations of Aniochán outlived him, I fear that our work might not be finished. Especially if what Indagir stole from Thaurisgar falls into unfriendly hands!
'However, it seems we're not the only ones who have been sneaking into Carn Dûm. I have heard that a company of the Trév Duvárdain journeyed into the depths of the city to hunt down a sorcerer of the Angmarim. If that is true, some of our work might have already been done for us!
'I am told that Lágsaith has been telling that tale to all willing to hear it. Would you speak to her and learn what has happened?'

'Well, what did you make of that? It's quite the story, but I wouldn't put it past the Angmarim to sink so low!
'While you were listening to Lágsaith's tale, a woman of the Trév Duvárdain named Finrúth came to Bail Avarc begging for shelter from the Iron Crown and rambling about something she called \qbódraillan\q. It is of our language, but I have never heard it spoken. It means something akin to \qoath-thralls\q, but as I said, I don't know what to make of it.
'As curious as I am to know more, she looked unwell. Perhaps her journey out of Carn Dûm was not a pleasant one, my friend. Knowing what I do of that city, it wouldn't surprise me!
'Once I was able to get a word in, I asked her to take rest in the tent over there until you returned. Would you check on Finrúth and see if she can explain what has happened?'

Rhúnelleth and Indagir can be found at Bail Avarc in the foothills of the Ephel Angren in Angmar.
Soltakh has asked you to aid Rhúnelleth and Indagir in their efforts at Sant Lhoer and Thaurisgar as it will advance the fight against the Iron Crown in Carn Dûm. You should help Rhúnelleth and Indagir.

'Like many of the Trév Duvárdain, I once lived in Carn Dûm. Before the downfall of the False King, we even had our own quarter in the city.
'When I was Drostan, I was given a small house by the Iron Crown. It is a strange thing to be gifted something that was stolen from your ancestors. The fools we were, and that too many of those I once called my brothers still are!'
Soltakh pauses for a moment, appearing to calm himself.
'Although many of them have been sealed, a number of hidden paths into Carn Dûm still exist. I can mark them on your map, my friend. I am told that the Iron Crown has taken up in Sant Lhoer and Thaurisgar, but I doubt they mean to tarry in the latter. After all, the old apothecary was already a dangerous ruin before I was cast out of the Trév Duvárdain!
'The Elf, Rhúnelleth, and a man named Indagir are seeking help in venturing into Carn Dûm. Would you speak to them and help them if you are able?'

'Legolas and Gimli told me about the woman you met. What were her words? \qOne of the beacons of Gondor remains lit, and it casts Castamir's shadow long and far?\q She may have been speaking in riddles, but I think it is more likely she meant her people keep one of the beacons lit even in the aftermath of the war.
'My scouts have reported smoke on the horizon to the north-west. It is possible Amon Anglebed could be the source of it. That is where you should go if you think to find more supporters of the Heirs.

'Gimli and I will return to Minas Tirith with news of what we have learned, but you still have work to do here.'

'Can I help you with something?' he asks carefully, and you respond by noting that the beacon casts a long shadow, like Castamir did in years past. The man smiles broadly.
'You must be the kindred spirit I was told to expect! What a pleasant surprise! Aithil described you to me, but I did not foresee that one of the King's close personal friends could possibly support our mission... and yet here you are! I need not tell you how useful it would be to have you with us, especially if you still have the ear of the King! I hope you have not aired your true feelings and endangered your friendship with him?
'My name is Maethon, and I have been keeping this beacon lit. It is to be a sign that although the war is over, the fighting is not yet done. The guards at Ost Anglebed try to extinguish it as often as they can, but my friends and I re-light it when their attention wanes; they cannot guard it at all hours.'
'One of the beacons of Gondor remains lit, and it casts Castamir's shadow long and far. If you are a friend to those who wish to see it remain so, you will <rgb=#00FF00>agree</rgb> with us.'

'I do not begrudge Elessar his choice of wife! Were he not King, he could marry anyone he wished, and he would have my blessing. But if he is to be King, he should put the needs of Gondor ahead of his heart's call. If Gondor is to have a Queen, she should be a woman of Gondor. Does he not know the history of his own kingdom? Eldacar married a north-woman and caused much bloodshed. Does Elessar desire another Kin-strife?
'The scribes named Castamir \qthe Usurper\q for trying to restore Gondor, and he perished for it. But even today there are some who believe in that for which he stood. If you join with them, you may be well-rewarded, and see the return of a King who prizes what Gondor should be.
'One of the beacons of Gondor remains lit, and it casts Castamir's shadow long and far. If you are a friend to those who wish to see it remain so, you will <rgb=#00FF00>agree</rgb> with us. We must act in the shadows, for now, and keep down our voices; you never know who might be watching us.'

'I have two questions for you, my friend. First, was she convinced by our display, and second, is she a supporter of the Heirs of Castamir, as we supposed?
'Yes to both? Very good, ${PLAYER}. I am sorry it fell to you to play this part, but if she believes your interests are aligned with hers, we may be able to follow this thread to its very source, and learn who now leads the Heirs of Castamir.
'You must keep these folk convinced, my friend, for as long as you are able to do so.'

'If it were up to me, I would have shown this woman the blade of my axe and gotten just as many answers, if not more! But Legolas says that would not be wise. Hmmph. Does it matter where the wisdom comes from, if it might be gotten more swiftly one way than by another?
'If you must be the play-acting spy today, so be it! But when it comes to fighting, as it always does, don't be too slow to set aside the lies and pick up your weapon!
'Legolas and I will return to Minas Tirith to tell the King what we learned on this journey, but you won't be coming with us. You have somewhere else to go, I understand!'

'I am grateful for your assistance, my friend, as we all are, or will be, when you meet the rest of us. And I think it will be soon, for there is to be a meeting!
'Our plans have accelerated, and the time to act is approaching!'

'Sorry I didn't meet you at the beacon, but Ladben was sniffing around.
'The guards really trust you, don't they? It was truly a stroke of good fortune that sent you to us! If you tell Halwen you need a barrel of weapons, I am certain she would give it to you, and happily! Delivering papers is one thing, but we will need weapons if we are to carry out our plans; eventually it will come to fighting. It always does! At least we will know we are in the right, when it comes.
'When you have the barrel of weapons, bring it to me outside the eastern entrance of the city, below the cliffs to the south. Hold on! Wait for me to leave before you speak to Halwen. We do not want to be too suspicious.'

'What do you need, ${PLAYER}?'
You tell Halwen that Ladben asked for you to bring him a barrel of weapons so he could rearm the guards of Ost Anglebed and keep troublemakers from re-lighting the beacon. Halwen nods.
'That has been a real problem of late, and they're using so much oil! What if we had need of it? You can of course bring him the weapons, my friend. There's a barrel of high quality weapons just on the other side of the fountain. Wait, don't go just yet! There's also a barrel of rusty old implements right next to it. Be careful not to bring the wrong one!'
'Over here!'
'We need to distribute those papers! I stashed them in a crate outside the steps to the Hall of Ost Anglebed. Retrieve them and hand them out to the people of the city!'

'Maybe you can do me a favour? Bring this beacon oil to Halwen for safekeeping. If we store the oil further away, that may prevent these villains from lighting the beacon every time we douse it. At least it will be made more inconvenient for them.
'Halwen guards the stores by the north-east fountain, in Ost Anglebed.'

'My husband and I were at sea when Balakhôr summoned us to join his fleet as he besieged Gondor. Instead we quit the war and sailed for home, and so were we robbed of our chance to spit upon his corpse; but not before he took something else from me, for my youngest brother died there in service to the Scourge. It meant we were near at hand when the uprising began, and when the waves receded, the Kindred of the Coins ruled in Umbar, and the Heirs of Castamir were only a foetid memory.
'Tumúldo and I swore to fight for the Kindred, and fight we have, but I was not certain that Gondor would have to die until this day. Now, however... I am sure of it. The Sea Shadow hates Gondor, and he has chosen the manner of its doom: the Song of Waves and Wind will spell the end of Elessar's Gondor, and you would be wise to leave the kingdom before it does.'

Tumúldo Fierce-water lies on the cold stone floor in a pool of his own blood, a Gondorian blade buried in his back. His wife Nakási kneels by him, her eyes burning with fury and with unshed tears.

'We have friends across the kingdom, hidden in plain sight. If we can rally the people of Gondor to our side....
'Aye, it could be done, ${PLAYER}. The folk of Gondor do not wish to be ruled by Elessar and his Elf-queen; nor do they wish to be made subservient to Umbar! If the Kindred of the Coins thinks to challenge us for the rule of Gondor once our plans bear fruit and King Elessar is slain, perhaps they will find we are not so easily conquered. I have to believe this is the way it will be.'

'No, there is something about you that is different. You are not with this rabble, even as they seek to court you. Tumúldo and I know well that achieving a goal can at times mean you must ally with your enemies.
'Are you willing to die with these folk? Or will you stand with me to repay their treachery? The next one they stab in the back might be you, or it might be a friend, or it might be a lover. Tumúldo was all of these to me.'
'I have nothing to say to you. Count yourself fortunate I do not cut you down where you stand. You may have deceived Maethon, but I am not fooled by this part you play, ${RACE}.'
'Introduce yourself to my friends, ${PLAYER}, and then we will begin.'

'Ah, do not trouble yourself overmuch. They will warm up to you when they learn how useful you will be to us.
'I hope Elessar has enjoyed his kingship, for it nears its end!'

'It is said that when Balakhôr the Scourge met his end, it was at the hands of Dead Men that he met it. They say it was the King Elessar who commanded the killing blow, but others stood nearby: an Elf... a dwarf... a hero who bore the name ${PLAYER}.
'I had no love for Balakhôr, ${PLAYER}. Nakási and I preyed upon the ships he sent forth from Umbar before he came to power, but afterward, when we did not cease our roguery, he took one hand from each of us. They were ours to keep, and so we did, though we replaced them with these made of metal.'
Tumúldo raises his left hand, and it shines in the dim light of the cellar.
'The hands he cut from us were preserved, and now they decorate the cabin of our ship, each forever clasping the other, a sign of our love... and also of our desire for vengeance. Your part in the death of Balakhôr has robbed us of that vengeance.'

'I don't understand how this could have happened! We heard no word from the Heirs of Castamir who remained in Umbar, but I believed they would send messages as soon as they could. From where sprang this Kindred of the Coins, and how could they so easily overthrow our folk? The Heirs of Castamir were so established in the city... I cannot understand it....
'What has become of Saklaphêl, the widow of Balakhôr, or of Balakhâd his son? What are we now to do?'

'Nakási, my love... you were right...
'Gondor... must die...
'The Song...'

'None of these vermin remain alive in this place, Tumúldo. You are avenged upon them.'
Nakási turns her eyes to you.
'Let us leave this place. Go ahead of me; I will carry the body of my husband. He deserves to rest forever in the Sea, and not in these vile houses of stone.'

'We pressed on to Agal Dûn, and it seemed for a time that the Angmarim of the Iron Crown meant to dwell within the old fortress.
'It had become like another Carn Dûm, and I began to wonder why they were so intent on returning to Angmar at all. We had left our foes behind, had we not?
'But it was never enough for the Angmarim, and their work had to continue....'

'In secret, the Iron Crown had sought for something far more powerful.
'Beneath Tûr Fúar, a terrible artifact had laid nigh-forgotten, but not to High Priestess Ásachal. In her studies, she had learned many things of Angmar at the time of its downfall and of the Witch-king's many evils that never came to light. Although nothing spoke so plainly of what she would find, I suspect she knew the nature of it. And she wanted it—that she might succeed where the Witch-king of Angmar had failed.
'One of her ilk, Rúvaran, was the man who stole Máltagar and with it, they meant to wrest the power of the Witch-king into their own hands. Her work took her often into the depths of Tûr Fúar, but none seemed to know where she laboured.

Above the fortress, legend spoke of a broken spire piercing the sky—Tûr Fúar, the Drearspire—and it was believed that powerful tools of sorcery might be found within it.
'All among the Angmarim had plans to find the power they sought. With a tool stolen from Barad Gúlaran, one among them thought to ascend to the now-vacant throne of Angmar. Whispers and visions of the Dead came to all who drew too near to Máltagar, and its wickedness seemed to grow as if it were feeding upon us.

'I cannot thank you enough for your kind words, and for this remedy. I will grieve for my family, and keenly, but you are right: if the dreams of Vanyalos were sent by the Powers, none would think her able to turn aside from them, or prevent the horrors so revealed. That would be arrogance unbefitting the Lady of Lossarnach, or indeed any woman of Gondor.
'Thank you for aiding Queen Arwen with this ritual of Elf-magic, ${PLAYER}. I appreciate what you have done, and will not forget it.'

'My friend Ioreth would tell you no remedy acts as quickly as we might wish, but I hope you will find the comfort you deserve, Vanyalos. Grieve for your husband Forlong, and for your brother Denethor, but think not to carry the blame of what befell them! In that you are blameless, and the fault lies with Sauron who wove it, or with the Valar who thought such dreams might be of use to you.'

'Arwen was able to provide some comfort to the Lady Vanyalos? I am pleased to hear it, but it is no surprise to me. She has always had a rare talent for putting folk at ease, which is only one of the reasons for which I am glad she accompanies me on this tour of our kingdom.
'She left me little choice, of course. But it will do Gondor much good to see its Queen.'
'I appreciate what you have done, and will not forget it.'
'I am pleased we were able to help.'

'How delightful to have been of service! When my Queen asked me to attend her on this tour of the kingdom, I never suspected we would be able to do such good, and so early on the journey! Of course, I never doubted her intent or her ability, but it does remind me of a saying from my youth, when I was just a young girl growing up among the flowers of Imloth Melui. It feels so long ago now, but of course that is natural, is it not? Anyway, this is the saying...'

'The Queen and her healer Ioreth mean well, ${PLAYER}, but they can provide no healing for me. Mine is no ordinary grief! This is not the sorrow of a woman whose husband marched to war and perished there, or that of a woman whose brother ruled a city and fell when it burned.'
The eyes of the Lady Vanyalos shine with tears, but sadness alone does not line her face. Her expression is haunted too by guilt.
'Would that I had no part in this! Then might I grieve as does the rest of Gondor! But I have done as they did not, for I dreamed of what would transpire, and I did nothing to prevent it! It is as if I put the axe in the hand of he who slew my Forlong, or cast the torch that set aflame the city walls behind which my brother Denethor perished! It is as if I, Vanyalos, did these things, by failing to prevent them!'

'Not all dreams have the meaning you give to them, Vanyalos, but my people know well that some there are to whom the Valar grant the gift of foresight. \qGift,\q I say, but if so it must be an unwelcome one.'
Vanyalos nods unhappily, and Arwen briefly takes her hand.
'None disbelieve you, sweet woman. Your dreams came to pass in the way you foresaw, and great is the pain to grieve, especially when the grieving must begin before the loss is suffered. But to think you might have prevented what the Valar showed to you... can you really believe it might be so? Does the Lady of Imloth Melui stand among the ranks of such as they?'
The expression of guilt on Vanyalos's face disappears, replaced with shock. Arwen continues.

'What do the folk of Arnach need us to do, ${PLAYER}?'
You tell Elessar that some of the folk believe he is here to punish them, as Kings and Stewards rarely came to their village before, but that others planned to pick berries and hunt for game to fill the village store-house.
'I am not going to punish them! They and their lord did more than could be expected of anyone during these past few months! We will help them with their tasks, my friend, and when we move on we will leave their store-house filled. Is that clear enough?'
'There should be some berry bushes south-east of the village.'

'This was my berry bush, ${PLAYER}. No, it is fine. The bounty of all these bushes will end up in the Arnach store-house. Mind not that I picked the finest berries from this bush before you arrived.
'While I chose to pick these berries, my sibling is more of a hunter, and brought down a deer not far from here. Perhaps you can start preparing the meat to bring back to Arnach? The deer should be just to the south-east of here.'

'I borrowed this bow from my brother Elrohir. I may be Queen, but I think it is important for the folk of Gondor to see that I work to provide for them, as does my husband. Will you return his bow and quiver to him while I finish preparing this meat? It has been some time since I had such a task, but I do know how it is done.
'Elrohir will be somewhere within Arnach, working alongside my husband.'

'She need not prove her hunting skill to me, though perhaps it is the folk of Gondor she thinks need convincing? Thank you once again for the return of my bow and quiver.'

'Aye, Baranor surely speaks truth: Tumladen must be emptying of refugees now that the War of the Ring has ended and the people of Gondor return to their homes. I would like to hear how that proceeds, but perhaps we need not bring the company there in its entirety.'

'Lady Vanyalos is not the only resident of Lossarnach who grieves the loss of Forlong; he was a most popular figure, and treated all the folk of the lands within his governance as if they were his own children. Sometimes he treated me in this way, despite the difference in our ages!
'\qGood old Forlong,\q they used to cheer. We fought together on more than one battlefield, ${PLAYER}, and he was always a true friend, and big-hearted. Aye, and his frame grew to match! Good old Forlong. Alas for war!
'The people of Lossarnach will need to provide for themselves until another lord is raised to the station, and I doubt not they will; but it will take time to replace such a hole as Forlong leaves. Let us travel south to Arnach and see what the people there need.'

'The people of Lossarnach will need to provide for themselves until another lord is raised to the station, and I doubt not they will; but it will take time to replace such a hole as Forlong leaves. Let us travel south to Arnach and see what the people there need.'

'Is that... is that the King? What is he doing here?
'Have we done something wrong, stranger? What could bring one such as he to our little village? Is he here to punish us? Have we not suffered enough?
'Oh, if only Lord Forlong had returned from the fighting! He would speak to the King and tell him we have done all we should!'

'That is King Elessar! I would know him anywhere!
'My family attended the royal wedding, stranger. Well, we were among the crowd, but even at so great a distance I could tell the King and his Elf-bride would be so happy in each other's arms, and would rule Gondor fairly and well.
'But I did not expect either of them to come to Arnach! He's going to get mud all over his fine clothes! Oh dear, I am so ashamed!'

'That is the King? Doesn't he know he is supposed to stay in his tower? What's he doing here in Arnach? I don't think he's a very good King if he doesn't know what he's supposed to be doing.
'We're supposed to be picking berries and hunting deer to fill the store-houses, now that the men have come back from the war. He's not going to do that, surely?'

'Sirgon has been showing me the state of the Gondorian navy, ${PLAYER}, and I confess to you that it is worse than I feared. The Corsairs of Umbar knew where to strike and with precisely how much force, and the ships that were once the pride of Gondor lie now at the bottom of the bay, or burned along the coast. It is true we seized some of their own vessels, without which we could not have arrived at Minas Tirith in time, but most of those were in poor shape, or are now.
'We do not know how much of Umbar's sea-power has been inherited by the Kindred of the Coins, but unless it is very little we have scant hope of repelling it, should the Kindred cross the bay with ships of their own. I have accepted Sirgon's suggestion that he step down as the Lord of Lebennin in favour of his son Faltharan, but there is a condition: he must supervise the rebuilding of Gondor's ships, and he must do it with utmost haste.'

'My King has done me the great honour of allowing me to step down, and I will do the best I can to repay him for it tenfold, as will my son Faltharan! Gondor's fleet is at its lowest ebb now, but I hope to restore its glory to such a height as has not been seen in hundreds of years! Perhaps then I shall set sail once again, as I do in my dreams....
'But I have a task, and it will occupy my every waking moment. My son has his own task, and it involves clearing out some of the unsavoury folk that have taken to preying upon the folk of Pelargir. Ships cannot be built without craftsmen, and craftsmen cannot work if they are being burgled and harassed whenever they cross the city!
'Will you aid my son with his task, and make the port-city more safe for my workers and for their families?'

'I have accepted Sirgon's suggestion that he step down as the Lord of Lebennin in favour of his son Faltharan, but there is a condition: he must supervise the rebuilding of Gondor's ships, and he must do it with utmost haste.'

'I do not know if I have the fortitude to follow my father as the Lord of Lebennin, but I will do my duty as best I can, ${PLAYER}. I have begun by trying to stamp out the brigands with whom my brother Lorvegil sought to seize the city, but they are many and well-hidden. Some may be allies of the Heirs of Castamir, and I have heard whispers that a new power rises in Umbar... I think they might seek to court it, if they can.
'But my father is right. If we are to resist foes from Umbar, we must repair and rebuild our ships. He planned to show the King how the work progresses, and you should catch up with them at the dry dock to the south-east.'

'I am not surprised to hear your report of the dwarves from Furukzahar, for I have heard the mutterings around Tumladen. The folk here wonder why the doors of the dwarves remained shut during the war and only opened when the danger had passed. I say they wonder, but that is not the truth; they know the reason, and resent the dwarves for it. Where was this help when it might have saved lives?
'I know each folk must look first after its own, but we could have used the assistance of Furukzahar before now. It is good you prevented the insults from turning to bloodshed; we have seen enough of it this year, at least, even if the Temámir stayed safely in their mountains and saw none.
'You go now to see King Elessar in Pelargir? Tell him of the agreement you brokered with Furukzahar, and also that the refuge of Tumladen stands strong, its purpose fulfilled, and with good fortune it will not need to be used again for many years.'

'It is good to see you back, my friend! How stands the refuge of Tumladen?'
You tell Elessar about the situation in Tumladen and of the expedition of Temámir Dwarves that came there to survey the state of the buildings, as well as the resentment felt toward them by some of the Gondorians.
'I understand their feelings, even as I wish it was not so. Perhaps I should accept the invitation of Furukzahar, ${PLAYER}, in order to repair the relations between my kingdom and theirs. But first there is work to attend to in Pelargir.'

'You go now to see King Elessar in Pelargir? Tell him of the agreement you brokered with Furukzahar, and also that the refuge of Tumladen stands strong, its purpose fulfilled, and with good fortune it will not need to be used again for many years.'
The dwarves stare at you warily.

'It is a pleasure to make your acquaintance, and I trust you speak with the king's own authority? The captain with whom we spoke earlier did not, and he spent many words telling us so, wasting his time and our own. I am pleased you have taken his place.
'My fellows and I were sent here by Hámisar, ruler of the Temámir folk who dwell in Furukzahar, stronghold of the White Mountains. Long have we worked alongside the people of Gondor, helping to repair and rebuild their cities, but the recent devastation is worse than any in our memory, and requires a good deal more effort and resources if it is to be made right.
'To that end, Hámisar wishes to send more crafters and dedicate more blocks of stone to the work. Defári, Setényil, and I have come to survey the needs of this refuge. Can you assure us that the King of Gondor will give us appropriate payment for any work we here perform?'
You tell Asitám that King Elessar is known for his fair dealings, and he greatly desires that Gondor be restored. The dwarf smiles broadly.
'Then he will not regret hiring the Temámir Dwarves of Furukzahar, my new friend! Let us continue deeper into the refuge and see how much work will be required.'

'I hope the King of Gondor appreciates your work on his behalf, ${PLAYER}, for most of his folk may not. Would they think to aid us, if our stronghold was directly threatened while their own towns and villages were not? I know the answer, though they believe otherwise. Thank you for helping us here keep the peace.
'I will bring my report back to Hámisar, and will tell him that the King has, for now, agreed to these repairs. Our price will be fair, and the friendship between our folk... well, there is more to be repaired than just stone, it seems. Will you convey an invitation to your King on Hámisar's behalf? He is welcome to visit us at Furukzahar at his earliest convenience. After all, it is one thing to do business between reliable intermediaries such as you and I, but when rulers can meet face to face it seems to me much more can be accomplished, better and more quickly.
'Good day to you, my friend.'
'Good day to you, my friend.'

Hámisar turns his attention to you.
'I gave my greeting to the King, but of course his companions are welcome here as well! He and I have matters to discuss concerning the ongoing relationship between our peoples and how the Temámir can best aid in the rebuilding of his kingdom. I would not think to bore you with such matters! I hope you will explore the beautiful corridors of Furukzahar and meet with my folk.'

'It is good to see you again, ${PLAYER}. I did not expect the King of Gondor to accept the invitation to visit Furukzahar so swiftly! It reflects well upon him for respecting the will of Hámisar, and upon you for bringing word to him with such haste!
'I hope you enjoy your stay here, and that King Elessar and ruler Hámisar are able to arrive at a fair and equitable arrangement that will enrich both of their folk.'

'What has brought you to Furukzahar? I hope you do not think to involve us in your wars? The Temámir of Furukzahar have always welcomed visitors from the other dwarf families, but Hámisar shut the gates for a reason. He did not intend to invite Gondor's war to our doorstep.'

'Do dwarves usually make people wait this long?'
'Do dwarves usually make folk wait like this?'
'I hope the dwarves will accept these gifts from us in the spirit of their custom, and as tokens of friendship from Gondor.'
'If the Dwarves of Furukzahar think to test my patience, I am determined to pass the test, ${PLAYER}. Give no sign of displeasure, my friend, and we will weather this challenge.'
'This is ridiculous! How long must we wait until they permit Elessar to go inside?'

'This is intolerable! How long do they intend to make us wait? We did not come here to be made to stand on the doorstep like common peddlers! Should any Temámir come to Thorin's Halls, would they be kept outside for the merest whim? I think they would not!'
Elessar gives Gimli a meaningful look, and the dwarf glowers at him.
'I am sorry, my friend, but this endless waiting is intended as an insult! You cannot see it? Did they not invite the King of Gondor to visit them? Or did they do so in order to slight you in this fashion? No Longbeard would stand for it, and I should think the King of Gondor would have more demands upon his time than would allow him to waste such time as this!'

'And still we wait! With whom do these dwarves think they are dealing? This is Elf-like behaviour, if you ask me!
'Perhaps you will refrain from telling Legolas I said that, friend? But this is ridiculous!'
'If the dwarves think to test our patience, I am determined not to fail the challenge, ${PLAYER}. Please make sure Gimli says nothing we will regret.'

'The stronghold of Furukzahar is hidden in a cleft of the White Mountains to the north of Pelargir? Then let us be off, and see if the hospitality of the Temámir is to be as noteworthy as their wisdom!'

'Welcome to Furukzahar, stronghold of the Temámir in the White Mountains. All are welcome within, of course, but affairs of state are such that the arrival of the King of Gondor demands a little extra preparation! I ask that you wait until I hear word from my brethren inside that you may enter.
'I do not wish to inconvenience you... but it is also customary to bring a gift when you arrive here. Perhaps some meat from the game that is to be found in this valley? I do not wish to impose a burden upon you, but it will be my great shame if I were to allow you inside without such a gift, and you were thought to be discourteous. I cannot allow that to happen, if it might be prevented!'

'We are here on a mission of friendship, ${PLAYER}, and therefore we will do what custom and tradition demand of us. Let us hunt some of the wild game to be found in this valley, and may the Temámir enjoy what bounty we can bring to them.
'I trust the game animals of this vale are plentiful, Sékhel of Furukzahar?'

'I do not wish to inconvenience you... but it is also customary to bring a gift when you arrive here. Perhaps some meat from the game that is to be found in this valley? I cannot allow that to happen, if it might be prevented!'

'Yes, this gift will do nicely. It is good you have done as my people expect, and our ruler Hámisar will be pleased to learn that the King of Gondor does not think himself above such customs as we hold in Furukzahar.'
Sékhel permits himself a small smile, and then shakes his head regretfully.
'However, it pains me to tell you that we are not yet ready to allow the King of Gondor inside. You will have to wait a little longer.'
'Let us hunt some of the wild game to be found in this valley, and may the Temámir enjoy what bounty we can bring to them. I trust the game animals of this vale are plentiful, Sékhel of Furukzahar?'

'It's true that you don't see Temámir in the North very often, but they did answer the call of the Sixth War of Dwarves and Orcs, and suffered losses as severe as any other house. 'We have no choice now, my friends. We should get as much rest as we are able. Whatever Hámisar thinks to keep from us, whether it is the continued presence of Khôltekh the Cunning in Furukzahar or some other deception, we cannot reveal it if he chooses to keep it hidden.
'We will depart in the morning. Rest for now... but lightly.'

'I do not like this, ${PLAYER}. Hámisar is hiding something. I think he would have preferred not to speak to us of the Kindred of the Coins, and had we left him the choice he would not have spoken of them at all. I believe this Khôltekh came to Furukzahar, but I am less certain the meeting was as Hámisar presented it.
'We should remain on our guard while we are here. Something about this situation does not feel right.'

'That Hámisar is lying to us. I don't know about what, or why he seeks to deceive us, but I can see it as plainly as you can see the beard on my handsome face.
'I knew there was something afoot when he made us wait so long on the doorstep! It was not mere discourtesy... it was villainy of some kind! We have yet to discover what type of villainy, perhaps... but villainy nonetheless!
'Do you think it has something to do with the unpleasant sensation of dread we felt by that door south of the throne room, ${PLAYER}? What is Hámisar keeping in that chamber?'
'What is Hámisar keeping behind that suspicious door, ${PLAYER}? Perhaps you can investigate further, but do try not to draw attention to yourself.'
'I knew there was something going on when they made us wait on the doorstep for so long. Did I not tell you so?'

'You are a companion of the King of Gondor? Have we met? My memory for faces is not what it once was, and I am far from my home. I am here visiting, but I believe I have information you should know.
'Quietly! We should not speak here. Let us meet inside the armoury, across the water to the north-east. There will be fewer unfriendly ears to hear what I have to say, and the noise of the forges should help to hide our conversation.'

'When I first arrived here, the Temámir showed me a great deal of hospitality, and Hámisar gave me his personal welcome. I was most impressed, for while I have been warmly greeted at every dwarf-hold I visited on my travels, Furukzahar outshone them all. But then it all changed.
'A few days ago, an emissary from the Kindred of the Coins arrived. His name you know, for Hámisar told it to you, but he withheld his epithet and the folk to whom he belongs. His full name is Khôltekh the Cunning, and he is a dwarf of the Temámir who hails from some distant land. And yet it was not from Umbar he came, or at least not directly; he came from the west. From conversations I overheard I understand that he received delivery of some artifact from the north, and he brought it with him to Furukzahar.
'Hámisar told you this emissary of the Kindred departed, but I think he is still here; it is the dread of the artifact he bears that you sensed outside the door where he shelters. I do not know why the Temámir became so cold to me after he arrived, or why their leader lies to the King of Gondor, but I thought you should know. I will speak with King Elessar briefly, if it can be arranged in secret, but I think you should all leave this place before it is too late. Furukzahar may not be safe for you.'
'Not here! We should speak inside the armoury, across the water to the north-east. The noise will help to hide our conversation.'
'I feel as if I struggle to stay afloat in deep water, and something tries to pull me under. I have felt this way for most of my time in the employ of the King, and the Steward Denethor before him!'

'Hámisar told you this emissary of the Kindred departed, but I think he is still here; it is the dread of the artifact he bears that you sensed outside the door where he shelters. I do not know why the Temámir became so cold to me after he arrived, or why their leader lies to the King of Gondor, but I thought you should know. I will speak with King Elessar briefly, if it can be arranged in secret, but I think you should all leave this place before it is too late. Furukzahar may not be safe for you.'
'This is all so overwhelming. How did I come to be here?'

'Do you really think Hámisar is lying to the King? Why would he risk such a dangerous deception? You don't think he's in league with the Kindred of the Coins, do you?
'I am just a scribe, ${PLAYER}, and not especially accomplished at that. I am not an adventurer or a hero like you; I left my home in Ethring a few months before the outbreak of war. Ever since I came to Minas Tirith and the service of the City, I have become embroiled in great events I find myself unable to comprehend.
'It is all very overwhelming to me. What is Hámisar keeping from the King?'

'This hall is so cold... but the Queen wants me to speak, so I shall speak.
'Long ago, and for always, I dwelt within and beside the River Gilrain, and my music was the song of sunlight on the water, and of wind in the leaves. But it was a lonely song, for my sisters had gone away and I did not think I would see them again. Animals came to the stream to drink, and birds to bathe, but except for such creatures I was alone and felt the pain of it... until one day.
'An Elf-maid tarried by the river as she journeyed southward from a distant land. She was more beautiful and radiant than anyone I had ever seen. I sang to her and she delighted in my song, for it reminded her of home. She danced beside my stream, and I was so gladdened by her presence that the music I made held more enchantment than ever it had before. She slept on the bank of Gilrain, comfortable and safe, and I was no longer alone. I dreamt that once she awoke she would fashion a home for herself in my wood, and I would teach her my song and she would call me sister. She would have children of her own, Elf-children of merry eyes and high voices, and I would show them the flower-fields and the secret springs, and they would fashion brightly-coloured petal-crowns to wear, and their mother would delight in them.
'It was a happy dream, but it lasted too long, and when she at last awoke many seasons had passed. The Elf-ship that waited in distant harbour for her to arrive could wait no longer. With selfish hands I stole that life from her, and I grieve every day at the sorrow I caused her. I did not intend such sadness to befall, and I would take it back if I could! And yet it is my doing, and the guilt weighs heavily upon my every moment.'

'I know what cruelty is, Maiden of the Gilrain. The world is cruel, and has always been. Can you know my story and say it is not so?
'Amroth was a king among Elves, but to me he was more; he was my love, and the brightest star of my night sky. \qWe must depart, Nimrodel,\q he said to me, \qfor the dwarves have awoken terrible evil, and if we stay it will endanger our folk too,\q and I believed his words. I believe them still, for I know what befell in the centuries since, as he cannot.
'Amroth went ahead to make ready the ship. I travelled with a small company to join him at that distant harbour, but the passage of the mountains was hard. The high crags filled me with unease; the rocky way troubled my heart. When at last we descended to the low-lands, I danced in the woods and became separated from my folk, so grateful was I to leave the mountains behind. The sound of the River Gilrain was beautiful, and its music had magic in it, and whatever else befell I can still remember how it was, and know that I loved it. I slept in peace for too long, and by the time I awoke a fell wind had come from the north and driven my love's ship from the shore, never to return. It is said Amroth leapt from the ship and braved the waves that he might wait for me... but never again was he seen by Elf or by Man, though I walked the shore for uncounted days and innumerable nights.
'I dwelled in sorrow from that day forth, never far from the Bay where I lost my love, and I have worn this mourning veil for so long I cannot remember the sight of the sun without it. I have held my grief close, but so too has it held me. Until now I believed the weight of those heavy chains was only mine to carry. I did not know you sorrowed too, Maiden of the Gilrain. It was not for you to feel this way. Do not burden yourself with the grief that is mine. I spoke of cruelty? The greatest cruelty is that this sadness must snare more than one heart, and for so many years!'

'And so concludes my Queen's greatest purpose in this journey, ${PLAYER}. She desired to ease Roamingstar's burden, and I believed we would need to visit the Cave of the Avorrim to make the attempt. But we were fortunate that Nimrodel was here in the Palace of the Swan, and now we have saved some time.
'I said Arwen's purpose on this journey was ended, but of course mine is only beginning! We must speak with Prince Imrahil about the continued presence of the Corsairs that threaten Gondor's shoreline, and also about the rise of the Kindred of the Coins in Umbar, across the Bay of Belfalas! But we have already achieved some good today, for Roamingstar and Nimrodel each deserve the peace and the happiness that their sorrows stole from them. I hope we have helped lighten their burdens today. I think we have.'

'There it is, ${PLAYER}. Whether it is called Tûr Dúvar, Gwathrenost, or countless other names, it is the dark citadel of the Witch-king of Angmar. But you know it well, don't you?
'From what we have learned, High Priestess Ásachal has stolen a shard of the ancient Oath-stone of Rhudaur, Tauressar, and brought it to Angmar that she might wield its power as her own. It is said that it was corrupted by the hand of the Witch-king himself, and that oaths sworn upon it bind the wills of its victims to the Oath-stone. Even so far from the battle in the south-lands, our tribes learned of the Witch-king's doom. Does Ásachal truly mean to master the Oath-stone in his absence? It must be destroyed before it is too late!
'Although we cannot be certain, it is likely the shard is now kept in the highest chambers of Gwathrenost. We have cleared the way, my friend. It is up to you now!'

'There it is, ${PLAYER}. Whether it is called Tûr Dúvar, Gwathrenost, or countless other names, it is the dark citadel of the Witch-king of Angmar. But you know it well, don't you?
'From what we have learned, High Priestess Ásachal has stolen a shard of the ancient Oath-stone of Rhudaur, Tauressar, and brought it to Angmar that she might wield its power as her own. It is said that it was corrupted by the hand of the Witch-king himself, and that oaths sworn upon it bind the wills of its victims to the Oath-stone. Even so far from the battle in the south-lands, our tribes learned of the Witch-king's doom. Does Ásachal truly mean to master the Oath-stone in his absence? It must be destroyed before it is too late!
'Although we cannot be certain, it is likely the shard is now kept in the highest chambers of Gwathrenost. We have cleared the way, my friend. It is up to you now!'

'I gave you my thanks for not speaking what you suspected in front of Coruchon, King Elessar, but you will have my thanks a hundredfold if you do this now: I entreat you to forbid Orgolas from leaving Lond Cirion, no matter what his father has gifted to him. Already it is nearly impossible to keep him from sneaking beyond the walls, but perhaps a command from the King of Gondor would stay his steps?'

'I understand this request you have of my husband, Marra, but I fear you may do more harm with the asking of this boon than you will prevent. Your son will not be kept from leaving your home if that is the purpose of his heart. Though the command be in the King's voice, Orgolas will know who wrote the words, and that knowledge can only breed resentment.
'You say Golasgil was a fine mariner, and I do not doubt he was! But what I have learned of your husband from my own is that he cared deeply for the people of Anfalas, and did not sail from them, or from you, without great need. Perhaps if Orgolas understood the cares and concerns of the folk he will rule when he comes of age, he will make the same choice, and the Wave-hunter will remain at its dock.
'This, then, is my suggestion: let your son come with our travelling party as we journey to Pinnath Gelin. It is my belief that Orgolas will see this land with new eyes, and he will grow into the responsibility he must one day have.'

'I do not know.'
Marra looks from the Queen to the King, and back again.
'What if this journey gives life to embers that might otherwise have been cooled? I do not see how such an adventure could prevent that which I fear for my son.
'But if you permit Daeram to also join your travelling party, that he may attend my son and keep him safe, I suppose I cannot refuse.'
Chapter 3.12: Grief and Duty
Orgolas is outside the keep of Lond Cirion.
Lady Marra has entreated the King to forbid her son from leaving Lond Cirion.
