'Do you have an interest in history? You should hear my father Mulúgu's account of the battle from one who fought in it! Seek him by the throne of Furukzahar, for he often goes there to advise Hámisar about matters of importance to our folk.'

'My father was sleeping? Yes, I should have realized. He is old, and while I treasure his wisdom and the tales he tells, he does spend much of his day sleeping by the throne. Of all the places in Furukzahar, that is his favourite chamber; he told me once it reminds him of the Court of King Jegín the Enduring, ruler of the Temámir Dwarves.
'But I promised you would learn of the Battle of Azanulbizar! More than two hundred years ago, all the dwarf clans answered the summons of King Thráin of the Longbeards, and assembled on the very threshold of Khazad-dûm to answer the violence of the Orcs with vengeance of our own. My father Mulúgu, very young in those days, served King Jegín and fought bravely among the ranks of her Temámir in skirmish after skirmish. Many of those who followed her have now passed on, but my father Mulúgu still lives, as does the King herself; Jegín remains King of the Temámir in our lands far to the south-east.
'Every clan of the dwarves suffered terribly during the war and at Azanulbizar, and King Jegín was not alone in demanding some recompense for the losses her people had suffered. For their service during the War of Dwarves and Orcs, the Longbeards granted to the Temámir some of the mountain strongholds they could no longer maintain, including this fortress. And so Furukzahar became a home for the Temámir. We have gotten along with the neighbouring kingdom of Gondor for many years, and I hope that will continue for years to come.
'The Temámir have always been the wise voyagers of the dwarves, walking long roads and sailing the vast seas in search of opportunity, quite unlike those of other dwarf-families. Like them, however, we are also loyal to our friends and deadly to our enemies. It has been a pleasure to speak with you about my people, and perhaps some day I will introduce you properly to my father. Until then farewell, my fellow student of history!'
Mulúgu sleeps peacefully on one of the benches, and you decide not to wake him

'Welcome to Furukzahar! The fortress has not had many visitors of late, due to the war in Gondor, but I am pleased to see that Hámisar has ordered the gates open once again. A number of noteworthy visitors have come to the fortress since then, friends from near lands and distant. This is a city of the Temámir, wisest of the dwarves, and we have made this home for ourselves far from our ancestral lands.
'It was not always home to the Temámir. Are you familiar with the Battle of Azanulbizar? Yes, the last great conflict in the War of Dwarves and Orcs. Two hundred years ago it was, but it was so momentous a battle that it is still spoken of by all the clans of the dwarves, including my people! My own father Mulúgu fought in it and achieved glory, when he was young... I am fortunate he survived the fighting, or I would not be here today!
'Do you have an interest in history? You should hear my father's account of the battle from one who fought in it! Seek him by the throne of Furukzahar, for he often goes there to advise Hámisar about matters of importance to our folk.'

'Hello there, stranger. Fancy making some coin? I have a job for only the most capable of adventurers, and you have just the right kind of look about you.
'Have you heard of a roc? Vicious, nasty creatures they are. Massive birds with talons like daggers, beaks strong enough to pierce the hull of even the sturdiest ships.
'Well, I represent a wealthy buyer who is interested in acquiring one of these beasts for himself. Fancies if he raises the thing from birth, it'll be loyal. Could you imagine? The power of a roc tamed.
'So here's the job: Go to the roc's nest south of here and nab one of their eggs. Bring it back to me, and you'll have enough coin to live comfortably for the rest of your life anywhere in the world.'
As you recall, Rocs are intelligent creatures, not the mere beasts that this brigand claims them to be. It may be worth warning the nearby rocs that someone has designs on their eggs.
'Finally, a visitor who has the sense to address me with any respect. I greet you. You may call me Raghda-gûn. You come bearing a warning for me? I will hear it.'

'You are a friend to the Free City of Umbar; I see that now. I will tell none of your arrival here. The merchant road runs along the coast southward to Rakhatâb, where it turns north and passes by a small fishing village, Khûtra. Umbar Baharbêl lies just beyond the hills past the village, the shining jewel of Umbarkhîl. Go in peace, and with my best wishes for your health and happiness.'
'Let us ask someone in the nearby settlement how best to reach Umbar Baharbêl. The conclusion of King Elessar's mission awaits us there... but we cannot complete this quest until we reach the city.'

'You have come to Jax Phanâl with a curious group, stranger. I hope you and your friends will cause no trouble here, for if you do, the Kindred of the Coins will see that it is the last trouble you make. Umbar Baharbêl has been made a Free City once again, and under the rule of the Kindred the Haradrim of the Great Southern Empire have been driven out of Jax Phanâl and other villages along Umbarkhîl, the Cape of Umbar. The Empire of Ordâkh has no claim upon us, and never will again. They plundered our valuables when they fled, and even now they muster their warriors at a camp to the south. They have no interest in some of the things they stole... they wanted only to deprive us of them.'
Jâkin studies your face carefully.
'Are you a helpful sort? Or do you only wish to learn what you can and move on, leaving we who struggle here behind when we are not useful to you? Few come to Jax Phanâl without reason, and fewer still leave the Shield Isles without some ill intent. I wonder what my silence might be worth to you? There must be some who would be interested to hear of your little group of travellers. Unless you are a helpful sort. Then it might be different.'

'I think we should help this man, ${PLAYER}.
'He is not wrong, for in other lands we have done as he said: moved on when we learned what we could, remaining only for as long as we needed to learn where next to journey. Now, it was war! So I do not think we could have done otherwise! But if we can help the folk of Jax Phanâl and also keep our presence hidden from those who watch for us, I believe we should.
'What would Jâkin have us do?'

'Jâkin uses us cleverly, ${PLAYER}. I recognize the tactic from my days of... banditry.
'But he is not wrong about this: his silence will aid us more than an errant word to the wrong folk, and if we might accomplish some good for the people here at the same time, how should I put it? Everyone wins, or at least no one loses more than anyone else, which is a start, and for me a change.
'What would he have us do?'

'Are you a helpful sort? Or do you only wish to learn what you can and move on, leaving we who struggle here behind when we are not useful to you? Few come to Jax Phanâl without reason, and fewer still leave the Shield Isles without some ill intent. I wonder what my silence might be worth to you? There must be some who would be interested to hear of your little group of travellers. Unless you are a helpful sort. Then it might be different.'

'You are a helpful sort, then? I smile to hear it!
'When the magistrate's forces drove the Haradrim from Jax Phanâl, the occupiers fled with whatever valuables they could find, but they were not... how would you say it? Choosy. Some of them stole books of great value to me personally, and I would have them back. These are not worth any great amount of Phârzi or Gîmli, but they do contain stories and accounts that are very dear to me, and I want them back.
'The Haradrim will have them at their camp to the south. Retrieve my books and defeat any of the warriors you must, and you will prove yourself a helpful sort.'
'The Haradrim will have them at their camp to the south. Retrieve my books and defeat any of the warriors you must, and you will prove yourself a helpful sort.'

'I am most grateful for this service you have provided this day! These books are very dear to me, and I could not bear to think of them in the hands of the Ordâkhim, never to be read again. They did not know the worth of the treasures they stole from us!
'You are a friend to the Free City of Umbar; I see that now. I will tell none of your arrival here. The merchant road runs along the coast southward to Rakhatâb, where it turns north and passes by a small fishing village, Khûtra. 'It is... almost like it used to be, isn't it?'

'Well, thank you for listening to me, ${PLAYER}. Let us return to the shore and see if the rest of the crew has made the crossing.'

'Thank you for taking my advice, ${PLAYER}. When every party gets something of value, you can be assured they will each stand by the bargain. I learned this on the river, in my old life, and it was a useful lesson.
'Let us return to the shore and see if the rest of the crew has made the crossing.'

'So this is the Cape of Umbar? The Corsair Daxamat tells me his people call it Umbarkhîl, and it is a land of beauty? For him it may be. For me I see only the land of the folk who stole my son Thorongil away. The sooner we get to the City of the Corsairs, the sooner I will have my vengeance.'
You remind Nauriel that the mission is to rescue Thorongil, not to take revenge, and she gives you a cool look.
'The Corsair Daxamat also says there can be two ways to say the same thing, ${PLAYER}. Perhaps it is the same with this.'

'I think we have made life a little more safe for the folk of Rakhatâb, but something still bothers me about the murder of that aged man. Why would one of the Corsairs at Kan Skûrja commit such an act? He was a recent arrival to Rakhatâb, much like we are, and yet they did not depart their encampment to threaten us. Did he possess something they wanted? The guards took the victim's belongings away, and unless we hurry they will put the evidence in a coffer within the keep.
'I have had an idea. I will go keep the guards occupied. You find the evidence coffer and retrieve the old man's belongings from it before they can finish bringing it into the keep!. We may find a clue among them. Let us meet up on the beach to the south-east of the city after you are successful!'

'What have you found, ${PLAYER}? Was Daxamat right? Is there any motivation for the victim's murder to be found among his belongings?'
You unfold the possessions you retrieved from the evidence coffer and study each in turn, handing them to Sirgon after examination.
'A note signed by someone named Galadaith? \qThere is no information I can give that you have not already been provided, but I assure you that if you offer proof of the deed, you will receive the reward to which you are entitled.\q That is a familiar name, but why?
'And a knife with a curious insignia on the handle. Is this a snake that coils around itself? See how it goes around the hilt? What does this mean?'

'I kept the guards talking for as long as I could manage, but I had to leave before they became suspicious. They believe without question that one of the Corsairs from Kan Skûrja is responsible. I see that your own errand was as successful as mine! What have you discovered?'
Daxamat takes the note and the knife from you, and almost drops them.
'What is... no... it cannot be. I know this symbol! This is... this is the knife wielded by The Blade-twist! I have heard tales of him ever since I was a child... but now he is slain, and will collect no further bounties.
'This... this is bad, ${PLAYER}. We knew the identity of three bounty-hunters hired by Saklaphêl to slay the Kindred of the Coins: The Blade-twist, our own Driftwood, and Cruel Dancer. I think Cruel Dancer seeks to eliminate her competition.'
'If there are clues to be found among his belongings, I do not understand them.'

'This man was just minding his own business; I heard him cry out as he fell. He was a stranger to Rakhatâb, that is true, but he has been here for a day or two. Why, I think I spoke to him yesterday, but I cannot remember what he was asking about. We spoke about recent events, I seem to recall, and about how the Kindred of the Coins has been dealing with the warriors of Ordâkh that refuse to leave our lands... but the murderer was not one of the Ordâkhim.
'And now this man is dead! Such things were not supposed to still happen after Ordâkh was driven from Umbar! The Kindred promised us peace, and for the most part they have delivered it!'

'You there! Stay back. No, I do not suspect you in this, for I saw you arrive. But it is not impossible for the murderer to have had help, so you make sure you keep yourself out of trouble. Guardsmen of Rakhatâb will be watching you.
'Did you say you heard a Corsair might have done this? A tall man, with a dark beard? I am not surprised. Even after the rise of the Kindred of the Coins in Umbar Baharbêl, many of the Corsairs refused to swear oaths of peace and loyalty to the new order. Some of them are camped even now to the north-east along the coast, and sometimes they adventure here to Rakhatâb to cause problems for the workers.
'Might one of them murdered this man? I think it likely.'

'Something smells fishy, ${PLAYER}. If my brother were here he would say \qit is the right of a Corsair to do as he likes!\q and think nothing of it, but there is something about this situation that feels wrong to me. Perhaps I am just not as bold a Corsair as my brother.
'But the camp of Corsairs to the north-east lies in our path. Perhaps we can help the people here by thinning their numbers, and when we return they may have captured the one who did this. What do you say to this idea?'

'We meet again, ${PLAYER}. It is a pleasure to speak with you, as it was before. But you did not know my name then, did you?'
The woman flings one arm dramatically outward and holds the back of her other hand over her eyes.
'Murder! Murder! Is nowhere safe anymore? This poor man was slain, right here in the open! Oh, it is terrible!'
She lowers her arms to her sides and laughs long and loudly.
'It is remarkable how simple it is to make people see what they want to see. I had all the folk of Rakhatâb believing they saw a tall bearded Corsair stab a man to death, right there in the open. Oh, the murder was real enough, and The Blade-twist did not see it coming. Weep not for him. No bounty-hunter should live as long as he did and remain in service. I will have the good sense to hang up my own knife before there is more life behind me than ahead.
'But I wanted to speak with you for a particular reason, ${PLAYER}. I would like to declare for ourselves a truce, and to work together where that is possible. The Blade-twist would share neither money nor information, and slay me with as little regard as I slew him; and that is familiar to me, and in this business that is right. But I observed you speaking with the man called Driftwood in Jax Phanâl, and I could not understand it. For what purpose did he ask you to help the people of that settlement? Not only for their silence. There was something else. I find that most interesting.
'Let us consider the Kindred of the Coins our mutual foe, then? I will help you find them, ${PLAYER}. The bounties belong to me... but it seems to me that you seek them for... other reasons. So long as our aims do not conflict, you may count Cruel Dancer among your allies... if not among your friends. It seems to me you may have friends enough. I trust you chose them carefully?'

'Who was that woman, ${PLAYER}?
'What? Cruel Dancer? You are joking!'
'I know what we do. We continue our journey. Our road leads to Umbar Baharbêl, and it seems there is a fishing village between here and the city, a village named Khûtra.

'This is a poor time to visit this village, stranger. Ever since the great quake shook these lands and the temple on the hill sunk into the earth, an evil has taken the lands hereabout. Famine has come to Khûtra, and disease, and... suspicious folk.'
He stares at you meaningfully. You ask if anyone who has come to the village lately might have inquired about a group such as yours, and he raises an eyebrow.
'Could be so. Could be maybe not. I would have to ask some of my neighbours, and while I'm asking I'm not bringing crab legs back to Khûtra, or collecting driftwood along the shore with which we can smoke the meat and improve the flavour. With the famine going on, that's one of the only reliable sources of food around here, and it is barely edible.'

'I would have to ask some of my neighbours for the information you want, and while I'm asking I'm not bringing crab legs back to Khûtra, or collecting driftwood along the shore with which we can smoke the meat and improve the flavour. With the famine going on, that's one of the only reliable sources of food around here, and it is barely edible.'

'You did as I asked? This surprises me, stranger.
'The answer to your question is that yes, you are not the only visitor to recently arrive at Khûtra. A woman there was, and she asked about folk such as those with whom you travel. I saw her again only moments ago, atop the rocks to the north-east.
'I think she is waiting for you to go to her.'

'You are not the only visitor to recently arrive at Khûtra. A woman there was, and she asked about folk such as those with whom you travel. I saw her again only moments ago, atop the rocks to the north-east.

'We have been through danger before, ${PLAYER}, and I have seen the horrors of war first-hand. What can Cruel Dancer do to me that I have not already suffered?

I looked into Saklaphêl's bounties not so I could claim one, but so I could learn what the Heirs of Castamir and the Kindred of the Coins were each, separately, hoping to accomplish, and whether that would endanger the lands across the Bay of Belfalas. I did not think such an inquiry would lead to anything like this, or a reunion with you!
'I am grateful for the latter, of course.'

'I do not think Cruel Dancer needs to worry that I might steal her bounties from her, but she has no way of knowing that.
'I will remain alert, and I recommend that you do the same. She is notorious, in her own way, and if half of what I have heard of her is true... we may be in some trouble, ${PLAYER}. The murder of The Blade-twist has the effect of removing one of her competitors, but it is also a message to us, a warning to stay out of her way.'
'Cruel Dancer will not know whether Driftwood's interest was real or just a pretense. He may now be in danger, and so may any who associate with him.'

'What do we do now?'
Caebar looks around nervously, and then surprises himself with a sudden laugh.
'I know the answer, of course. We continue our journey. Our road leads to Umbar Baharbêl, and it seems there is a fishing village between here and the city, a village named Khûtra.
'I do not think I am becoming any braver, ${PLAYER}, but it may be this adventure is making me more used to living through dangerous situations. Let us hope that continues to be so!'
He looks around again.

'This was the beacon-tower of Calatirion, ${PLAYER}, constructed by Elendil as a mighty monument of Númenor. I have heard tales from Glorfindel of the Vandassar that stood within it for much of its history, Airessar, as clear as crystal, shining so brightly it could be seen even from far off in the bay.
'I know it was destroyed by the Bright Company to loosen Sauron's bonds upon the Men of Harad during the War of the Great Alliance. The tower itself survived that battle, and would stand for almost three thousand more years, but it would not stand forever. When the Church of the All-Seeing came to Umbar in the vanguard of the Empire of Ordâkh, there were servants of that church who resented that which Calatirion represented; they were the Nazgûl, with the Forsaken Reaver at their head. With sorcery he and his allies toppled the tower, and the memory of that day has lived on in whisper ever since. Even Glorfindel wished not to speak of it, but he told me the name by which folk of Umbar recall that day: Mût Tadaul, the Death of Light.
'The Forsaken Reaver must have perished with his master when Frodo cast the Ring into the Cracks of Doom, ${PLAYER}. But Calatirion remains toppled. It is a reminder to me that evil deeds are not undone by the destruction of those who wrought them.
'We should continue to the east and then north along the road. We have almost reached the city.'
'There our destination lies!'

'We are almost there!
'The journey nears its end... and we are still alive, which is more than I expected, if I am being honest with you!'

'Ah, I had thought to help the people of Khûtra with their difficulties, but as I approached the temple I could not bring myself any nearer than this. Thank you for helping them combat these evils.'
Sirgon sighs heavily, a sound you have become accustomed to ever since the man who was once the Lord of Lebennin came ashore upon the Shield Isles.
'I quail at the sight of the Dead, ${PLAYER}, but there is something I fear even more than such as they, and it is a fear that takes the shape of a Man. I fear the meeting with Belondor that surely awaits me in the city ahead. I fear what he will have to say to me, but worst of all: I fear that I may deserve it.
'The Steward Denethor gave me the command to bring Belondor to justice, but I did not refuse it. When I believed I drove him to his death I felt the shame and the guilt of that pursuit, but to learn that he rose from the waves, that he survived... my shame and my guilt are doubled. Nay, they are trebled. And now he is one of those who leads the Kindred of the Coins against Gondor!
'I am sorry. I will pull myself together. I will be fine. You say Legolas intended to visit the wreckage of a tower? I believe that is Calatirion, on the hill of Kharn Arâx, to the south-west.'

'The emissary did well to send you to me, friend. Do you have need of a bed? Wine? Ale? Or perhaps a meal cooked in the style of the lands from which you hail? You need but ask and if it is within my power or the purview of this inn, I shall make it so. We are pleased that our land is more hospitable to those from abroad now that the Kindred watch over our people. We hope that this will bring about even greater commerce to our land, in time.'

'I am pleased to make your acquaintance and hope that you are finding our outpost as welcoming as we wish to make it, friend. This is a land reborn and her people celebrate the casting off of the yoke that restrained them.
'Tyranny is ended. We wake to a dream from a nightmare that lasted too long. The Kindred breathe life and liberty into the lands, and we are free to roam once again. Our roads are safer and travel and trade quicken their pace. Natural dangers remain, however: passage around the Cape is not always easy, and you may still prefer to visit the stables should you wish to journey to the fort at Rakhatâb, to the south! But you have my welcome all the same, should you have need of my service.'

'Come closer, friend, and look upon the wares that I oversee. All manner of goods, weapons, armour, and other such delights await you.
'A brisk trade returns to Jax Phanâl now that the tyranny of the past is ended. I will do my part to see that these items are safe-guarded. Once they are purchased, I return the profits to those who entrusted their goods to my care... for a modest fee, of course. I treat the goods under my care as I would my own children.
'That is, if I had any children!'
The barker laughs and returns to calling out auction details.

'It is good you have come to me. First, I will require a name for the ledger so that the people will come to know you for all that you do in these lands.'
She awaits your response and then scribbles some notes in a writing style you do not recognize. She then continues.
'Very well, that is all I require of you for now. If you wish to know more, I can spare a few moments to explain the purpose of the ledger-keepers.'

'I was not certain you would dare come here. But since you have, you will hear my words before you and your friend die.'
Mêshka holds up her hand, signaling to her guards that they should await her command.
'For years after Sirgon drove my intended to his death, I lived a life of mourning. Believing he died at sea, I married, and it was a marriage of great happiness... at least until its ending, when my husband was seized by the Church of the All Seeing and burned alive, sacrificed to its Dark Lord.
'Why do I tell you this? I tell you this so you will know I am no wilting flower. I have been forged of tough steel, hardened by fire and by the salt-spray. There is a reason Belondor was my first intended, for he is the same: made durable by his experiences.
'For he did not perish beneath the waves when Sirgon pursued him through the rocks of Shedax Khîn. He survived as a castaway among the Shield Isles, sun-scorched and bitter, until he was taken aboard an Ordâkhai galley. In time he came to Umbar and served in the Fleet-fast, becoming one of its dedicated defenders, but the rule of the Heirs of Castamir rankled him.
'He began a friendship with Azagath the Sea-shadow and others who would come to supplant the Heirs. This Kindred of the Coins rules wisely and fairly, unlike either the Heirs of Castamir or the Steward of Gondor. What final words have you to say, Sirgon? Will you beg the forgiveness of my husband? I will give your words to him, if they please me.'

'I do not beg for forgiveness, Mêshka, for I know forgiveness is not deserved. If there is a message to give from me to your husband Belondor, it would be this: the wound I suffered the night we duelled after dinner was mortal. It was not a deep cut, not physically, but that wound has stayed with me since that night.
'I will not beg for forgiveness, or say that following the command of the Steward Denethor protects me from your reprisal. But know that I was forever changed by what I did to your husband Belondor, though I did not know it. But now I see that I was.
'I believed I missed the sea, and sailing, and traced my miseries to giving up that life. But I see now that it was my friendship with your husband that I truly missed, and the innocence of my youth before I committed the act by which I am now forever judged, and judge myself. If this is the wound that is to slay me now, I welcome it. I ask that you spare ${PLAYER}, who had no part in earning this, but I will not run from it.'
'What final words have you to say, Sirgon? Will you beg the forgiveness of my husband? I will give your words to him, if they please me.'

Mêshka stares at Sirgon for a long moment... and then motions for her guards to stand down.
'We were all wounded on that night, Sirgon, and none of us knew how deeply. Your words ring true to me. I have spent years dwelling upon my hatred of you for the treatment suffered by Belondor at your hands, and at the hands of Gondor, and though that land is ruled now by a King and not a Steward, I believe in my heart that it would be no different if those events happened today and not long years ago. I did not forgive you then, and I do not forgive you now.'
Mêshka shakes her head, and for the first time today you see her smile.
'But men are weak, Sirgon. Know this: when the streets of Umbar Baharbêl filled with soldiers of Ordâkh and the Heirs of Castamir sailed with the Corsairs to Gondor, my husband Belondor weighed his hatred for Gondor against them... and he dispatched a ship for Pelargir, bearing a warning for you. I counselled against it, but it seems it did not matter, for the ship never arrived. No doubt it was sunk by the Heirs, and no warning ever came to you.
'My first husband was a good man, slain by Ordâkh. My second husband, Belondor, helped to overthrow those who killed my first, and he established a new order in Umbar, the Kindred of the Coins, which will usher in an era of prosperity and peace. If he has any fault, it is that he forgives too readily, and is pleased to forget the sins of Gondor if it means Umbar will have a fresh beginning; this is not a fault that I share! Therefore I give you your life, Sirgon, but I banish you from the Upper Ward. If I see you return I will order my guards to slay you where you stand. Now begone. Our business here is done.'

'I have... much to think about, ${PLAYER}.
'Let us leave the Upper Ward. I believe Mêshka was serious, and it is not safe for us to remain here.'

'The woman Belondor loved was a noblewoman of the city, and she was called Mêshka. I believe her home must be somewhere within the Upper Ward, and the folk within may tell us where she lives with Belondor. It is a gamble, of course: the two may dwell now within the Citadel of Winds, as befits a leader of the Kindred and his wife. But it might not be so, and folk of the Upper Ward may tell us.'
'Yes, can I help you with something? What is it?'

'I have not seen Belondor today, but you just missed his wife Mêshka! She was heading south toward the Sail-haven. She may have been bound for the market of the Upper Ward that is on the way, or one of those in the Sail-haven, and if you hurry you might still catch her.'

'I do not care for your choice of friend, stranger.'
Mêshka addresses Sirgon with hatred in her voice.
'You are bold to come here, Sirgon of Gondor, but foolish. My husband suffered much at your hands and those of your master. For you to come here now...'
She falls silent.
'Not here. You will come to the home I share with Belondor, and there we will speak. It is the north-east, here in the Upper Ward.'
'I was not certain you would dare come here.'

'I have spent our journey from the Shield Isles fearing a confrontation with Belondor, ${PLAYER}, but it seems I should have more feared his wife Mêshka! I warrant that she is more fierce than he is! I hope I have not endangered our own mission here. He will learn from her that I am in the city, that is true, but the personal nature of our conversation may mask that I came here at the command of King Elessar. Perhaps that will prove a helpful distraction for the Kindred of the Coins when the time comes to rescue the captives?
'I have much to think about. Thank you for helping me with this, my friend, and I am sorry to have brought you into danger. It could... it could have gone worse. But it did not. My apologies all the same, ${PLAYER}.
'I will continue seeking out information... just not within the Upper Ward of the city.'

'Khâsha sent you to me? For what purpose? If I can help you I will, but I do not believe we have ever met before. I think I would remember it!'
You tell Phêlex that you found a bottle among the Shield Isles with a note inside it, and his mouth drops open with surprise. You show it to him and he reads it with interest.
'I never thought to see this again, stranger. You see... I wrote this note almost thirty years ago, when my ship was boarded by Corsairs. I did not think to escape alive, and indeed none others of the crew survived. But I... I am not proud of this, but I threw myself upon their mercy, and they took me into their crew. For more than twenty-five years I lived on that ship, raiding and pillaging, living the life of a Corsair, a brigand of the waves. I am not proud of it... but I was alive, and I intended to stay alive.
'I returned at last to my Khâsha. It would have been a short reunion, and bittersweet, had I not befriended a smuggler by the name of Tumúldo Fierce-water. He encouraged me not to sail with Balakhôr, one of the Heirs of Castamir, and in that way he saved my life, for all who followed Balakhôr to Gondor perished in the war. Ever since that day I have supported the Kindred of the Coins. Loyalty to any others, and the life of a Corsair, are both behind me now.
'I ask you to understand, stranger. I lived a criminal's life, yes, but it was the only life I had available to me. Tumúldo understood that, and so did Khâsha, and now I dedicate my life to serving each of them. It really brings me back, seeing that note in its bottle, but I was a different man when I wrote it, and I have become a different man than the man I became afterward.'

'It is not our place to judge this man. Have we not all done what we must to survive? She Who Remained is no stranger to need, and neither are you, ${PLAYER}. Will it be the same with my brother? Perhaps it will.
'I will continue searching for information that will help us with our mission, but it is good to know the conclusion to the mystery of the note we found in the bottle in the Shield Isles. I was curious, and now that curiosity has been satisfied.'

'Where has Nakási Wave-reaper gone? I do not like this, ${PLAYER}.
'They say Elves and dwarves cause trouble? I say vengeful widows are more likely to cause trouble than we are, and that trouble will be worse!'

'Gimli and I will keep our eyes open for some sign of Nakási Wave-reaper, ${PLAYER}. It is true that she may cause difficulty for us if she finds us before we locate the ones she took captive.
'We will not relax our vigilance.'

'It is said \qWherever Elves and dwarves go, trouble is sure to follow.\q
'I am not saying I agree with it, but this is something you will hear in Umbar, if you keep your ears open. There are other whispers, as well: that Tumúldo Fierce-water got himself killed in Gondor, and his wife Nakási burned the White City to the ground to avenge him. I do not know the truth of it. Why, Tumúldo is probably still alive. He has disappeared before for weeks at a time, and I do not believe something just because I heard someone say it.
'The two of them are beloved by the folk of the Sail-haven, and have been ever since they helped us cast off the yoke of Ordâkh and the Church of the All Seeing. If something has happened to the two of them, Harbour Warden Eshmun will know of it. His office is in the tall blue tower to the south. I cannot guarantee he will speak to such as you... but you may find it valuable to try.'
'Have you had good fortune or ill so far, ${PLAYER}?'

'The people here do not know some of what we know, ${PLAYER}, and I recommend we keep it that way. If it became clear that some of the rumours they have dismissed are true... let us say it may become more difficult for us to accomplish our mission.

'I am happy to report that your friend has withdrawn his request for trial by combat. He does not want to remain imprisoned... but when I told him he had drawn Rothog as an opponent, he was unable to speak. Through the stammering I was able to discern that he preferred remaining a guest of the jail for awhile longer. \qUntil Rothog has retired,\q he may have said, but if I were a wagering man I would not expect that to happen any time soon. The half-troll Master of the Tor-gardens loves fighting that much, even when there is no need for it.
'Our business is now done. I thank you for the donation to the Fleet-fast.'
'Here he is!'

'Thank you, ${PLAYER}. I know Itûr wanted to be set free, but I also know he would prefer to be alive than to face an unwinnable battle, and Rothog's reputation in the arena speaks for itself.
'I do hope you will take pity upon me if I need coin in the future. I gave the last of my money away as part of this endeavour, after all. It was worth it, was it not?
'Aye, surely it was worth it. But keep me in mind at meal-times, ${PLAYER}, or I will waste away to nothing.'
'Thank you for the... donation. The Fleet-fast will make use of it.'

'Itûr was no martial novice when I knew him, but he was never especially skilled in combat. I think his success in the arena will depend upon the Hûlaz against whom he is matched.
'Let us go to the arena and see if they have posted the match-ups for the upcoming contests.'

'Rothog the Storm? He is my favourite of all the Hûliz who fight in the arena! How can you not have heard of him?
'He is a mighty half-troll who began as a ferocious pit-fighter and rose to command a ship and crew of his own; the Crow-feeders, they were called, for a great mass of carrion birds followed in their wake. When Rothog crossed Balakhôr the Scourge, he found himself once again consigned to the arena, forced to fight his former crew and friends. Balakhôr thought he would die... but Rothog survived for more than a year, sometimes fighting as many as ten bouts in a week!
'He became the favoured champion of the people, and though Balakhôr commanded the master of the arena to execute the half-troll and be done with him, she refused the command. \qFight him yourself, if you wish so badly to see him dead!\q I heard she answered.
'But before he could, Balakhôr sailed to his death in Gondor. And now Rothog belongs to the Kindred of the Coins... but he still fights in the arena, because he enjoys it!'

'Who are the two combatants about whom you speak? Rothog the Storm?
'You need not tell me the other name. Rothog never loses!'

'I was in the stands of the arena the night of the rebellion, when the Kindred of the Coins came to power and cast off the shackles of Ordâkh and the Church of the All Seeing, when the Heirs of Castamir lost their grip on Umbar.
'The ground shook, and we saw flames erupt away across the harbour. Rothog had been put to work fighting the few of his Crow-feeders that remained alive, as well as Men who had defied the Heirs. But that all changed when the whispered rumours became facts proclaimed: Mâkhda Khorbo, the temple of Sauron, had fallen. Rothog turned to face his opponents in the arena, and he spoke a single word. From where I stood I could not hear it, but as it was repeated by others it grew in volume and intensity, until the echo of that one word shook the very foundations of the arena.
'The word was \qHêlsi,\q and when the uprising of the Kindred was completed, Azagath Sea-shadow found Rothog the Storm sitting in the seats reserved for the Heirs of Castamir, surrounded by their half-eaten bodies. The half-troll did not join the Kindred of the Coins at once, but in time he did, and the people of the city love him. He still fights in the arena as often as he can, but now he does it for himself, and no other.
'What does \qHêlsi\q mean? It means \qFreedom.\q'
'Oh no. If Itûr must face Rothog the Storm in the arena, he has no hope for survival!'

'My friend Itûr has to withdraw his request for trial by combat! There is no possible way he can best Rothog the Storm in the arena! Perhaps if he was matched against someone else he would have some hope of victory... but Rothog is the most dangerous Hûlaz to ever fight in the Tor-gardens! Itûr could not have drawn a shorter straw than this!
'Take my money-purse, ${PLAYER}, and hurry back to the jail! There is no time to waste! We have to get the guard to allow Itûr to withdraw his request!'

The keeper thumbs through pages of scrawl, finally resting her finger on an entry, unmistakably your name.
'Nary a misstep since you arrived on these shores. Reports contend that you are a capable ${CLASS} with many talents. You have a penchant for heroism, a quality some find noble, and you appear outwardly compassionate.
'Your legend, thus far, is unstained by controversy or misdeed. Let us see you keep it this way, yes?
'If you wish to know more about the ledger-keepers, why we are here, why we are necessary, and how we came to be, I will explain it to you.'
She nods.
'But I warn you. Our history is... complicated. Our reason for being, while rooted in the dark past, looks to the promising future.'

'In the past, our role was to track the actions of those who would oppose the tyranny of the Heirs of Castamir. We did so in secret. We traded information we acquired to the counsel of leadership in exchange for freedom from the lash or the gallows.
'When the Heirs fell, and the Kindred of the Coins came to power, they chose a new path for our talents... one that we quite prefer.'
She offers a genuine smile.
'We fully embrace the need to understand the deeds undertaken for - and against - our burgeoning society. In their wisdom, the Kindred enable us to honour good deeds done for the citizens of Umbar.
'You will find that the people of Umbar will provide you with coins long held as the currency of our land. These coins are little more than keepsakes. We call them ûr in the singular and ûri in the plural. If you wish, you can exchange these coins with us, and we will track your undertakings in our records so that you earn respect, honour, and gifts representative of our culture.
'If you do not choose to use the coins, it will not matter. We will remain ready to track and memorialize efforts undertaken for Umbar Baharbêl and her people. We will record your efforts only when you choose that we should.'
She nods.
'Until you earn our trust more completely, this is all I can say.'

'My first customer was not a customer at all, for he did not buy anything. Disaster! No, I must try and stay positive. Perhaps he will tell his other wealthy friends. Why are you staring at me like this, ${PLAYER}?'
You tell Galengam that the richly-dressed man was Azagath Sea-shadow, leader of the Kindred of the Coins, and that if Cruel Dancer had seen him out and about in the Sail-haven she would have likely killed him where he stood. Galengam frowns.
'We should be glad that she did not see him, then. That would have been quite bad for business! Really, ${PLAYER}, I think your priorities are somewhat askew. You will never make it as a merchant in this world if you have such trouble remembering what is important!'

'A man from Gondor has opened a new market stall in the Sail-haven?' the man asks you. As you tell him that is true, something about his manner strikes you as odd. You ask him if he has an interest in goods from Gondor, and he smiles.
'I do, my new friend. Why should that be unusual? We have had our differences, Umbar and Gondor, but my land desires only to maintain the stability it has earned. It has been different in Gondor, but it should not remain so, should it? My Kindred believes that peace between our lands is possible... if Gondor will meet us along that path. What did you say you were called?'
You answer with your name, and he responds with another charming smile.
'Enjoy your stay in Umbar Baharbêl, ${PLAYER}. Let Azagath Sea-shadow be the first to welcome you to his land. I will not be the last, I warrant. We are a friendly people, as you are certain to discover. Now I will go to see the goods your merchant friend has to sell.'
This man is Azagath, leader of the Kindred of the Coins!

'Post those notices around the Sail-haven for me, perhaps to the south, and soon the customers will swarm my goods and you will have to save me from drowning... drowning in gold phârzi and silver gîmli, that is!'

'I told you the customers would come here in droves, ${PLAYER}! None can resist my rare and valuable goods, or my name is not Galengam! The coin will be rolling in before this day's end!
'This man is my first customer, and...'
Galengam lowers his voice to a hushed whisper.
'...and see how finely he is dressed! This man has money to spend, and I will see to it that he spends most of it at my stall, and no others!'

'The overland route from Gondor has been treacherous of late, and few merchants have come to my city during the months following the conclusion of the war. Did you come by ship?'
Galengam happily chatters away, describing a dangerous voyage across the bay and a brief stay in the Shield Isles. Azagath nods sagely.
'You have done very well to make the journey up Umbarkhîl, for the Cape has had its own share of troubles of late: famine, blight, and unsavoury types among them. You are to be commended for bringing your wares this far.
'I must be about my own business now, but allow me to extend the welcome I gave to ${PLAYER} to you as well, Galengam. I hope you will find the custom in my city to your liking! Farewell, my friends. Perhaps I will see you again.'
'Please take your time, my wealthy friend! You are certain to see something you will want!'

'Carver Gírma has agreed to answer any questions I might have, ${PLAYER}, and I must admit that this is a much finer reception than that I was given in Furukzahar! The Shoreward Stone may be off-limits to me, but if he gives me the answers I seek I will forgive that refusal, and harbour no hard feelings about the matter!
'Then let me ask the first question. I understand that one member of the Kindred of the Coins is a Dwarf of the Temámir who goes by the name Khôltekh. He wears a medallion of some kind, and this medallion sparkles with a most unusual shine, the like of which I have never seen in any jewel buried within the earth. What is this material, and where may it be found? I have never seen anything like it... not while awake, in any case!'

'You speak of Abâshal, my new friend! It can be no other! Some call it \qsea-opal,\q but unlike other jewels the iridescence that gives it value can shine with every colour of the rainbow, and the forces involved in its shaping can cause even those to shift in truly remarkable fashion! You will typically find it cut into small jewels or fashioned into flat panels, if you find it at all; it is most rare, and its naturally-occurring form is brittle. Only the finest of stone-workers can mould it effectively. I blush to tell you I am one such craftsman. The knowledge is known only to few.
'The Empire of Ordâkh and the Church of the All Seeing that they brought with them to Umbar believed the ornamentation of Abâshal to be blasphemous; almost overnight as much of the jewel as could be salvaged was removed from the city and hidden away in secret vaults. When the temple collapsed at the moment of the Dark Lord's fall, it seemed clear the time of his church and the dominion of Ordâkh was ended. The Kindred of the Coins adopted Abâshal as a sign of not just wealth, but of defiance to foreign rule. You will not be surprised to learn that each of the Kindred's leaders possesses a medallion such as that you saw on Khôltekh's person, each one inlaid with a small piece of Abâshal.'

'I understand that one member of the Kindred of the Coins is a Dwarf of the Temámir who goes by the name Khôltekh. What is this material, and where may it be found? I have never seen anything like it... not while awake, in any case!'

'Abâshal, the sea-opal! At last I have a name to apply to the most beautiful gemstone on which I have ever laid my eyes!
'I will have many more questions for my new friend here, ${PLAYER}. Do not let me keep you! I am disappointed the Shoreward Stone must be closed to outsiders, but I am delighted to know that not all of the Temámir guard their tongues as closely as the others I have met!
'I will remain and speak with Carver Gírma for a time. Abâshal! I would learn as much about it as I can!'

'It is my pleasure to speak of Abâshal! It has been a secret of my people, but as it grows in importance for Umbar I cannot avoid speaking of it to those who would hear more. That would not be right!'

'What have you learned of the defences within the Fleet-fast, ${PLAYER}?'
You give your report to Bruidis and she thinks it over.
'I see. If I believed most of the Corsairs' martial forces had perished at Pelargir, it seems that the Kindred of the Coins has rebuilt them enough to man the Fleet-fast, at least, very effectively. A frontal assault upon the Citadel of Winds is, in my opinion, out of the question.
'I could not utilize Rossaran effectively in the Fleet-fast, so I sent him to conduct his investigation within the Lower Ward. Seek him out in the Lower Ward to the north and find out what he learned while he was there.'

'Bruidis suggested I find some garb that would allow me to pass undetected within the Fleet-fast, but I refused her; it was not easy, but I do not want to skulk about in secret! If my swan-knight armour is not welcome here, then neither am I!
'She was not pleased about it, but she sent me into the Lower Ward to learn what I could about our opponents. I cannot say that what I have discovered will be of use to us, but I was able to learn how the people feel about some of the various leaders among the Kindred of the Coins.
'Azagath and Belondor are both well-loved by the people, who give them a large portion of the credit for the Sea-stone Mutiny. That is the name given to the overthrow of the Heirs of Castamir and the Church of the All Seeing, when the oppressors of the Empire of Ordâkh were cast out of the city.
'Hármelak, the Golden Queen, is respected more than she is loved. She is one of the wealthiest people in Umbar, but the folk of the Lower Ward distrust her riches; many of them believe she is indifferent to their plight, and would not spend a single coin on their behalf.
'Rothog the Storm is considered a champion of the Lower Ward, for no one lives there who has not heard of his exploits in the arena, or of the manner with which he dispatched many of the Heirs of Castamir during the Mutiny. They love him... but they fear him as well.
'Of the others I was not able to learn very much. I hope this information is of as much use to you as the recounting of the Fleet-fast's defences are to Bruidis! We shall see, I suppose. I will keep looking, ${PLAYER}.'

'I could not utilize Rossaran effectively in the Fleet-fast, so I sent him to conduct his investigation within the Lower Ward. Seek him out to the north and find out what he learned while he was there.'

'You ask what might happen to a friend of yours that steals? I can answer this very simply for you. Is he of the nobility? For if he is a nobleman, I say he is likely to escape judgement. If he is from the Lower Ward, I do not like his chances. Consider Hármelak, the Golden Queen! Her family has always been wealthy, but you cannot tell me that all of her dealings are and have ever been aboveboard!
'What is your friend's station in life? That will determine not only if he can commit his theft and live, but also how rich a lifestyle he will be able to maintain... and the duration of it!'

'You want to know what will happen to your friend if he begins a life of theft and burglary? I do not have enough information to answer this for you. The reason? I do not know how skilled he is at this trade!
'Yes, I call it a trade. If you speak to others about this matter, they will tell you he will be caught or killed by the guards, or be sent to face Rothog the Storm in the arena, or fall to his death from an upper balcony when he seeks to escape notice. But I say differently.
'I think if he is well-practiced at the art of thievery, he might well escape and live a long and full life feasting upon the fruits of his labours! It can be so in other areas... why not burglary as well?'

'What might have happened had I succumbed to that pull again? Had I climbed through one of the windows of a mansion in the Upper Ward and stolen the valuables I found within, would I be seized by the guards? Would I have been brought to yon building, there to fight and die for my crime? Would that have been right?
'I am curious about this, friend. Ask some of the folk nearby what might have happened to me in that case. I am interested to know.'

'What did visitors to this place have to say about my future, ${PLAYER}? To what ending do they believe I will come to when I breathe my last?'
You recount the words of the folk with whom you spoke, and Driftwood listens intently.
'They are all right, my friend, and they are all wrong. How can this be so? It is because you asked them what would happen if I gave in to my thieving impulses and returned to my past life, and I do not doubt that I would arrive at one of those endings if I did.
'But it is possible for a man to change, even one such as I am. I strive every day to prove it. It is not easy. But it is worth it.
'Thank you, ${PLAYER}. None of those endings are mine today... and for today that is enough.'
Driftwood has asked to you meet you in the Tor-gardens.

'I do not know why I came to the Upper Ward; something compelled my feet to bring me hither. I find myself eyeing the upper stories of the manors and mansions of this district, and wondering if the windows might be unlocked, the balcony doors unbarred. It is a remnant of my old life that brings these thoughts to me, a relic of the brigand once I was.
'I should not remain in this district. It is not safe for me to stay here. Let us continue on to the Tor-gardens, ${PLAYER}. There we will speak, and I will find it easier to resist my more dangerous impulses.'

'I should not remain in this district. It is not safe for me to stay here. Let us continue on to the Tor-gardens, ${PLAYER}. There we will speak, and I will find it easier to resist my more dangerous impulses.'
'This place is better for me.'

'Old habits are the hardest to lose, ${PLAYER}, and in another life I preyed upon the wealthy merchants and nobles who sailed upon the River Anduin. I relieved them of their wealth, at least, and in some cases of their lives as well. Even today I feel the pull of that life, though I have spent the years since then seeking to leave it behind me.
'What might have happened had I succumbed to that pull again? Had I climbed through one of the windows of a mansion in the Upper Ward and stolen the valuables I found within, would I be seized by the guards? Would I have been brought to yon building, there to fight and die for my crime? Would that have been right?
'I am curious about this, friend. Ask some of the folk nearby what might have happened to me in that case. I am interested to know.'

'This is most unusual. You want to know what might happen to a friend of yours that commits a crime, such as theft or burglary? 'I wonder if you might help me. It is a delicate matter.
'My brother Zûfan has been shaving down his coins, you see, giving the overseer less than her share. I told him not to, but he said he would never get caught. He started doing it for some of the other workers as well.
'Well, this morning I heard a rumour that the overseer caught on to these ruses, and now my brother has vanished. Even if he has run away, I just want to know he's all right. He may be a fool, but he is family.
'Go to our home and see if you can find any clue to where he went. Please, ${PLAYER}, can you help me?'
You discovered that there was a missing pack, oil lantern, and trail rations taken from the home.
Zûfan likely went to the place where the siblings used to hide as children, north from the city and then west along the cliffs near the shoreline. Go there and ensure that the brother is well.
Ulanor found Zûfan before you and exacted the blood price for his debts. You need to deliver this sad news to Ayaluk.
Zûfan likely went to the place where the siblings used to hide as children, north from the city and then west along the cliffs near the shoreline. Go there and ensure that the brother is well.
It appears a pack was taken
It appears an oil lantern was taken
Ayaluk is concerned about his brother. He went missing several days ago after a visit from a collector of debts.
Return to Ayaluk at his family home in Rakhatâb
Speak with Foreman Nûrut in Rakhatâb
Gain Kharishah's pledge
Gain Beliash's pledge
Gain Hûzo's pledge

'This is what we needed. Here, take these notes to the foreman and inform him there are witnesses who will pledge that these reports were never acted upon. Go quickly. I dare not leave for fear of retribution.'

'This is unconscionable! These lives have been damaged or lost! Their sacrifices were brushed away in the past, but the Kindred of the Coins pledged they would not allow such as this to happen here. This matter must be addressed.'
'Of course I have sent requests on behalf of injured or slain workers. How is it that nothing has been done to help their families? I pledge to stand witness.'

'I must supply reports when there are any incidents on site. How did you learn that nothing is being done about them? It does not matter. What matters is that you have my pledge. I will bear witness.'

'I will not send this information on to the foreman until I have the pledge of witnesses from the masters. It is our custom that there are those to bear witness against the accused and I will see that I follow our ancient rules. But, please, make haste.'
Received Kharishah's pledge
Received Beliash's pledge
Received Hûzo's pledge

Ayaluk says that he collected written requests from the different masters in the fort. He asked that you get their verbal agreement that they submitted these reports and requests and come back to him.
Gain Tankho's pledge

'Each foreman submitted reports of accidents, disappearances, and deaths, requesting the effects of the victims to be returned to their families, yet none of the families were compensated. Go to the different masters in the fortress and explain everything to them and gain their pledge that their reports were accurate.
'I would go, but I know I am being watched.'
'Yes, I have submitted those reports to the overseer. How were they never fulfilled? You have my pledge that I will bear witness.'

'Most recently, I sent a request to have pay sent to the family of a man who lost his arms in a terrible accident. He has not been seen since. I thought he simply returned home! I will stand witness to this.
'If the family was not recompensed and the man is missing there is something terrible at work.'
Bearing Witness
You have gained the pledge of all the masters that they will bear witness to filing these reports. It is time to return to Ayaluk.
Take the evidence supplied to you and deliver it to Foreman Nûrut in Rakhatâb.
Received Tankho's pedge
Ayaluk explained that he discovered reports from all of the masters of the different disciplines in the fort and asks that you have them pledge that the information he came upon is true.
Find and speak with Nûrut
Blood of My Blood - Epilogue
Ayaluk asked that you return to the foreman and express his heartfelt thanks.
The foreman was not at his post. Where could he have gone? You hear a nearby whisper that there is a new overseer; perhaps you should go and check.
Speak with Foreman Nûrut

'I want to thank the foreman for his assistance. I know that my brother always held him in high regard and he was the only person in this encampment, aside from you, I felt I could trust.
'Could you tell him how grateful I am for the help he provided to us?'

'It appears that the news reached the ears of the Kindred of the Coins before we captured the overseer. Word arrived with a contingent bearing Rothog's symbol and colour. They took the overseer away and departed; they have already set sail toward the city. It is likely to be a sentence to the pits for the overseer.
'For me, as you can see, I am in a new arena of my own. I pledge, my friend, to do right by the workers here. I will see the work done and do my best to protect them all.
'Thank you, deeply, for your guiding hand in this difficult time. You have proven your worth to us and that service is well remembered, ${PLAYER}.'
The foreman is not at his post, you hear a shout '...to the new Overseer!'
Ayaluk asked you to return to the foreman to thank him for his aid and concern.
Find Ulanor and rescue Ayaluk
Report the news to Foreman Nûrut
Speak with Foreman Nûrut at Rakhatâb
'The guards informed me that that overseer was apprehended. You managed to also save the lad. We are indebted to your service, but this work is not yet done.'

'I will not stand idly by while Umbar withers from within. The Heirs of Castamir were right: the Old Ways are best! We should return to them before we allow scoundrels who do not pay their debts to ruin our future. You fool. You and this meddlesome dwarf obstruct me for the last time. Prepare to die!'
Ulanor yields as her guard arrives. You saved Ayaluk!
Nûrut directed you to inform Ayaluk that he will confront the overseer and that the brother is expected to stand witness. Find Ayaluk at his family home in Rakhatâb.
Ayaluk was not within his hovel. You discovered a small pool of fresh blood in his stead. Deliver this news to the guard.
Ulanor is taking Ayaluk to the Corsairs for some evil purpose. Stop her and save Ayaluk.
Inform Ayaluk that the overseer will be brought to justice

'We cannot allow this to continue. I will bring the matter to the master of the guard.
'Return to the young dwarf and tell him that we will seek justice! Ask that he meets us here so that we may go together to confront the overseer; for his brother and the families of those that the overseer harmed within this fortress.'

'Hear me, friend. The master of the guard informed me that the overseer left her post and headed east toward the Corsair camp with a prisoner. It appears that Ayaluk's fear of being watched was correct.
'I can only hope that we can get to him in time. The master of the guard said he can spare none to pursue the overseer, but they will follow after you when he can.
'Make haste east toward the Corsair camp and track down the overseer. If you can, rescue the lad.'
Confronting the Problem
With the overseer apprehended and Ayaluk safely returned to Rhakatâb you should make your way to the foreman and inform him of the good news.
You find only a small pool of blood where Ayaluk should be

The foreman wants to confront the overseer with the evidence of her covering-up and pocketing the personal effects of those suffering ill fates in Rakhatâb. He asked you to first collect Ayaluk to stand witness.
Nûrut asked you to check in on Ayaluk and see if he is well and if he is satisfied with the outcome of the investigation and efforts to expose the overseer's crimes.
Find Ayaluk at his home and speak with him
'We should ensure that the young dwarf you rescued is well. There is little more that we can do to ease the pain that he surely feels, but the capture of the overseer should bring him some peace.'

'Justice will be served. That the overseer will meet the fate she deserves must be enough to honour my brother's memory. For the future, I hope that those chosen to take the lead in our rebuilding efforts will exercise care and good dealing! I would rather see the light that dawns on our lands than to dwell upon the shadow that obscures our past.'
Nûrut directed you to speak with the young worker and see how he is faring.
Speak with Ayaluk and complete 'Instance: Whispers of the Forge'
'We will wait for Ulanor to be on the long part of her walk. You distract the guard and I will slip in and out of her chambers to get the proof we need.'
'These notes are clear. The overseer is hiding something and we need the help of others if we are to expose it!'
Ayaluk asked you to meet him near the entry of the overseer's office.

'Friend, I have had a change of heart. The overseer here in Rakhatâb brings too much harm. My brother should not have been killed. I have watched the comings and goings of individuals with whom the overseer meets, and I believe that there is some rot here that must be cut out. I intend to slip into her chambers, get whatever information I can, and report it to certain folk who can do something about it.
'I only require a distraction long enough to cover my efforts. Will you help me?'
Whispers of the Forge
After assisting Ayaluk he returned to his family home with haste. He directed you to speak with him there.
Ayaluk asked you to distract the guards who watch over the overseer's office in the fortress. He is certain that there is something untoward happening here.

'You have my thanks again. There was a rising tide of dead washing close to Khûtra. Because of you, my people can walk the pathways around Khûtra without fear.'

Defeat wights near the Mâkhda Khorbo (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'It is fortunate that you are going out near the Mâkhda Khorbo. The dead have been getting more plentiful by the day. They are harrowing our merchants and folk passing to Umbar. If you could cull some of their number, you would have my thanks.'

'Not that it's any of your business, but my wine is gone! All the trouble I've been through just trying to smuggle such acquired delectables to Umbar... I should be paid a king's ransom!
'You look fairly capable. If you're lookin' to make some coin, I'm lookin' for someone to retrieve what I've lost!'

'Well, would you look at that. You came through!
'I promise not to harass upstanding, tight-strapped fellows like yourself from now on. You all can be quite useful!'

'We've got a good thing going aroun' 'ere, and I don't want to screw it up, but these kergrim are presentin' a huge problem for us and our clientele. If we can't get this population under control, we'll take huge losses.
'Why don't you make yourself useful, and get out there? Fight, and take care of the kergrim population count.'

'That's it then. A job well done.
'So long as we keep their numbers from going out of control, they shouldn't be a nuisance to this town.'

'You... look different. Not like them. Those filthy scoundrels. I never thought life would be like this. When I first set out for the isles....
'I've underestimated just how cruel and rough the life of a pirate is. Your life is constantly at risk and people walk all over you.
'But I've a plan. They don't take kindly to deserters but I've a boat near the western coast. If I could get the necessary supplies to make her sea-worthy I might just be able to be free.'
'You made it, and you have the things! I'll finally be able to go home! I can't thank you enough, stranger. These are dark times indeed, but the light shines forth where it can!'
Last Chance Escape
Large crabs can be found to the south-east of Khûtra. Go there and return with crab meat to feed the hungry villagers.
Return with crab meat to Umaris
Collect crab meat (${NUMBER}/10)
'Please, we have so many who are hungry. The crabs can be found to the east along the shore. Please hurry!'

'Help from outsiders? And you were sent by Roshat? He must be getting truly desperate.
'It's true we could use all the help we can get. Our lures are as good and our hands as quick as ever. It's the trout themselves that have changed. They have turned a pallid, slimy green, afflicted with some terrible disease. We know not why. Some of the hands have taken to calling it the stench, for obvious reasons. We cannot eat or sell any of the fish we catch, it makes any who eat it violently ill.
'I'll be honest with you, moreso than perhaps Roshat was – we really could use your help. We rely on the fish to fill our bellies and our coin pouches. I know Roshat has suspicions about the source of the disease, but he won't trust outsiders unless he sees your value.
'I don't know how to heal our fish, but I know how you could help fill our bellies and perhaps gain his trust. There are crabs to the east of here, along the shore, just beyond the village. They seem to be immune to the stench, at least so far. However, they fight back more than we gentle fisherfolk can handle.
'Would you go to the east and bring us back some crab to feed our people?'
'I am grateful. We are proud folk, but I'm not too proud to admit my people will have full bellies tonight thanks to you. You might want to talk to Elder Roshat again.'
Feeding A Village
Crab meat collected (${NUMBER}/10)
Umaris has asked for your help feeding the village using the large, fierce crabs south of Khûtra. Perhaps Elder Roshat will see your value once you've helped the village.
'We are not paying by the day. With all due haste, I recall I said. We need that necklace back.'

Search the ruins of the Mâkhda Khorbo for a heavy, ornate necklace that the Yâshalam family lost. The ruins of the Mâkhda Khorbo can be found in the hills east of Khûtra. Then bring it back to the Yâshalam Family Emissary, Miritah.
Find the Yâshalam family necklace
Return the family necklace to Miritah in Khûtra

'You seem uniquely equipped for a task that requires some... delicacy. The Yâshalam family lost something years ago that was taken to the Mâkhda Khorbo. We have reason to believe this family heirloom, a necklace, is still there in the ruins. Unfortunately for us, the dead are more at home than the living in the Mâkhda Khorbo.
'If you could retrieve this item for us, there would be a handsome reward for you. Not a word to anyone, though. Any rumours that leak out about the Yâshalams or this necklace would... displease the Lady Yâshalam.'

'Thank you for retrieving this. It is priceless to the Yâshalam family. If anyone asks, nothing was found in the ruins, and we never asked for this. I'm sure you understand.
'A curse? No, I think not. To commune with the dead is a privilege, not a curse, and one my family has not had in far too long.'

Make your way north and east through the woods in the shadow of the mountains outside of Rakhatâb and search for evidence of the creature the workers say dwells at Jâghimsa. Collect the sap from the moving trees within the wood.

'Collect sap and wood from Jâghimsa, the moving forest that is north and east of our outpost.'

'I could use your help, ${PLAYER}. The workers complain that the woods north and east of Rakhatâb are haunted, cursed, or worse. They said that a creature, like a living tree, stalks the woods and harries their attempts to get the sap, logs, branches and other needs we have from the woods.
'You have proven able and I would request that you investigate the woods for this... herder. While there, could you help me complete the quota of sap from the trees there? The sap from the living woods there are vital to our ship repair and maintenance efforts.'

'Something was shaking the mine shaft?
'A creature? The earth? No, you are correct. It should not matter what was shaking the mine. We should not return there. I will seek the council of the overseer to determine what should be done.
'Please, take this for your efforts, ${PLAYER}.'

'I wish only for the safe return of the workers. The metals that they mine are important, but not as much as their lives are worth... to me and to them, at the least, if not to the overseer! Please, make haste!'
To the east of Rhakatâb on the southern slope of the mountains there is a mining cave that suffered a cave-in. Go there and rescue the miners trapped behind the rubble.

'You assisted me before, and I have need with someone with your skills again. There is a cave not far from here along the southern edge of the mountains to the east. We have workers there, extracting metals for the forges. There's been a cave-in; many lives are in the balance. Please, can you help them?'
Dig Deep
The miners are safe, and you escaped the mine. Return to Hûzo and tell him that the mine is either unsafe or home to something that will make it unsafe for his miners to continue working there.
A mining foreman asked you to assist with a cave-in that occurred within a cave near Rakhatâb. The cave is east of the fort.

'You'll find the shells along the beaches. Hurry along.'

'You seem like you can handle yourself. I have a special request. I collect exotic sea-shells, the larger and more ornate the better. Unfortunately, the best specimens seem to be located along beaches infested with crabs.
'I would love to add to my collection. The sea-shells on that beach shine like no other. Would you bring me back some exquisite ones? I would pay you quite well for the trouble.'

'Beautiful, are they not? So many in the city desire things of beauty, but have no drive to do the menial tasks like collecting the items necessary to make their baubles. What fortune then there is in finding one such as yourself. Willing to do anything for a bit of coin and recognition.

'I do not need to know who you are. All I know is that you are not holding a rod, and so you are like us: a worker or a mercenary.
'If you are looking to earn a little favour from the workers and people here, we can allow you join our little game.
'The premise is gruesome, but the payout can be good.
'A good day is a day without injury or worse here in Rakhatâb. A bad day, on the other hand, I am sure you can imagine.
'All you need do is tell me what foreman will have tragedy befall their workers. If you choose correctly, you earn a share of the bets. If you lose, it is only a bit of coin. What say you?'
'If you would like to play, all you need to do next is tell me which foreman you think will have a worker experience an accident.'

'It won't be hard for you to track down Shúkurz. See that trail of footprints, leading out of the village? Heh, I bet he was a lousy scout in Gundabad.'

'I am sorry, ${CLASS}; I followed you from Mâr Naphra to find Kafagur. I had believed that it was a camp full of dangerous Orcs. Clearly, I was mistaken, and this investigation was faulty from the start.
'It's true that I am not from Umbar, but rather, Gondor. I... do not know if I can tell you what led me here, but you have my word: I will not harm the Orcs.
'Whether they believe me is another matter entirely. Though, after I judged them so rashly, I do not know if I deserve that trust.'

'Phocas doesn't seem like the bad sort. After all, he was willing to stop running long enough to listen to me. I'm sure we'll figure things out.
'I've got more I want to tell you, but I ought to take Phocas back to Kafagur first. I'll see you there.'

'Thanks for making sure I was all right, ${PLAYER}. Grúshul's right; I acted like a fool. Even during our journey out of Gundabad, we stuck to the wilds because we knew Men would kill us if they saw us. I should have been scared of Phocas.
'But... I remembered how we got out of Gundabad in the first place. With your help, and the help of others. I remembered Náin, and how he apologized to me.
'I guess I wanted to believe that sort of thing could happen again. Maybe it can.'

'I am worried for our rulers. 'We owe the Kindred much for dealing with the Heirs of Castamir and releasing us from the shackles of Ordâkh. I hope they are all right.'

'The Hungry Deep Tavern is the finest in the city, if you ask me. Every time I come here I eat too much.

And there was another, a scholar whose name I misremember... whatever happened to him? He ruled in the Tor-gardens, but now he is gone and that half-troll, Rothog, has his place in the Kindred! He frightens me.

'I and my brother will stand with you to rescue Thorongil, ${PLAYER}. Will we not, Corudan? Or have you had your fill of this place already?'

'I will stand with you, ${PLAYER}, not only because of your rescue, and not only because of the adventures we shared in the Kingdom of Rohan. I will stand with you because it is right.
'I was not mistreated by the Kindred of the Coins, despite Nakási's words and her frequent promises to exact revenge upon any who aid Gondor. At sea I was given permission to walk freely about the ship, and I followed her commands quickly and well. Did my captivity chafe? I cannot say it did not, but I felt it was in service of a noble purpose, and that was enough. Tatháta suggested I be allowed to walk freely about the ships and the harbour when we docked, but the Wave-reaper feared my servility was an act, and commanded her kinswoman to keep me tied to the mast while Nakási was away. I cannot tell you with complete certainty if she was right, ${PLAYER}.
'But I can tell you this. The Kindred of the Coins value their captives only for so long as they retain value. Had I proven a burden or unmanageable, I think I would not have survived the voyage to Umbar. It may be the same with the young heir of Pinnath Gelin. If he loses his value as a hostage, I believe he will not long survive in the Kindred's company.
'Nakási brought him to Azagath Sea-shadow in the Citadel of Winds, from where the Kindred rule this city. I will help you as I can... but how do you intend to enter the most well-guarded district of Umbar Baharbêl?'
'We will stand with them, will we not, Corudan?'

'When my brother and I returned to Umbar, his plan had been for us to visit some of the taverns and inns of the city so we could learn what had happened while we were gone, recruit a larger crew, and Jajax could acquire a more suitable ship. That plan ran into some trouble! But I think at its heart it was still a good idea, because at taverns people speak more freely. If there is any way into the Citadel of Winds, someone at one of the taverns may unknowingly speak of it.
'I hope I am not being too forward with this suggestion! But it makes sense to me, ${PLAYER}. If everyone splits up and checks different taverns in the city, we may more quickly learn of a means of rescuing Thorongil from Azagath.'

'Forgive Enât her distrust, stranger, but we have reason to be wary. Our master is very particular about the means by which we carry out his commands. We bring sea-water through the city to the fountains inside Sûr Birix, the Citadel of Winds, every morning, and every night those fountains are emptied to await our return the next morning. It is hard, heavy work, and there are fewer of us now than there used to be. Azagath has dismissed some of our fellows before now, but... no one seems to know where Sadûkh has gone.'
Enât hisses at Ushu to not say anything more, and the woman nods.
'He may be fine, and he may not. But without Sadûkh our work will be more difficult. Azagath smiles with his mouth, but his eyes are unmoved, and if we do not find some way to replace Sadûkh's burden we may be the next ones to disappear.
'Prove to me you can carry this bowl of sea-water without spilling a single drop, and perhaps you can accompany us into the Citadel. Bring it to the courtyard of the Teeming Net Tavern, to the south-east, and we will see if you are steady enough to join us.'
'We should not say anything.'

'Prove to me you can carry that bowl of sea-water without spilling a single drop, and perhaps you can accompany us into the Citadel. Bring it to the courtyard of the Teeming Net Tavern, to the south-east, and we will see if you are steady enough to join us.'

'You did well-enough, stranger. You may accompany us when next we perform our duties, and I will ask no questions of you. Your reasons for wanting to gain access to Sûr Birix are your own, but you must endanger none of my friends. If such treachery seems possible, I will alert the guards at once.
'Let this last warning guide your steps. Neither Enât nor I know what happened to Sadûkh, but of this I am certain: he saw something he was not supposed to see, some secret of the Sea-shadow, and now he has paid for it.
'Azagath is dangerous. We water-bearers may be beneath his notice... but it may not be possible to always remain so.'
