'I would not seek to supplant any member of the Kindred of the Coins, for ours is a necessary council and Umbar is made better by our efforts. But this too is its strength: the Kindred itself is more important than any individual member. Were Azagath to fall during your rescue of the Gondorian hostage, that would be a most unfortunate turn, but the Kindred itself would survive... and that is everything.'
Hármelak holds your gaze but lowers her voice.
'Azagath returned to the city in the grip of a curious superstition. Every morning he instructs some among his servants to carry empty bowls down to the docks beside the Harbour Warden's tower. They fill these bowls with saltwater from the bay. Once this is done, they then carry these bowls of saltwater through the streets of the city until they reach the bridge beyond the Fleet-fast. The guards let them pass, without fail, and once inside they fill the fountains within the Citadel with the saltwater they carry. At midnight, the fountains are emptied... and at dawn the process begins again.
'No one pays attention to the servants who carry the water, ${PLAYER}, not the folk of the city, not the guards of the Fleet-fast, and not Azagath Sea-shadow. Among these servants you could gain access to the Citadel of Winds, and whatever might befall then... well, it would be for the benefit of the city, would it not?
'I trust this discussion has been as illuminating for you as it has been for me. Rothog will see you out.'

'Be gone now.'
Before you turn to leave, you quietly ask Rothog why he is helping you. The half-troll stares impassively down at you and says nothing.

'When Balakhôr perished in the war and the power of the Heirs of Castamir was broken, I knew the time had come to act. We will speak of it further in the garden.'

'The Kindred of the Coins was my idea, ${PLAYER}, inspired by the Corsair councils that once governed Umbar between the reigns of tyrants. A King or a Queen or a Steward can begin with the best of intentions, but they can be corrupted. They can make the wrong choice, but a group can guard against such wrong choices. A group can see all the sides of a problem. In a city such as Umbar Baharbêl, only a council can lead effectively for the good of all. That was my idea, ${PLAYER}: a council of leaders that would not be subservient to any outside force; not Gondor, not the Empire of Ordâkh, not the Dark Lord Sauron or his servants.
'During the rule of the Heirs of Castamir and the Church of the All Seeing, I asked Khôltekh to fashion seven medallions in the form of large coins that could be worn as necklaces. Each was made of a different material, signifying our disparate backgrounds and influences, but each had something in common. Khôltekh embedded a shard of Abâshal, the valuable sea-opal treasured by his people, into each coin.
'Only days after Balakhôr perished in Gondor, a tremendous quake rocked the city. The temple of Sauron crumbled and fell into the earth, and I knew it was the time to act. I sent the medallions fashioned by Khôltekh to my chief allies, and the uprising began. The Sea-stone Mutiny would spell the end of outside authority over Umbar: that of Ordâkh, that of Gondor, that of Sauron. The Kindred of the Coins would make Umbar Baharbêl a Free City again.
'Let us speak further in my office.'
'Let us speak further in my office, to the north.'

'Azagath is a Black Númenórean, a blood-ally of Balakhôr during the Scourge's rise to power. Their friendship soured when Balakhôr sought to claim rulership over all of Umbar in the name of the Heirs of Castamir. Azagath opposed his bid, a duel was fought, and Azagath suffered defeat; he received a scar upon his face and pled for mercy. It was granted, and he was banished. We did not see him for many years, and during that time Azagath's warnings were proven true. I called for his aid during the Sea-stone Mutiny, and when he returned to the city he did so as a beloved hero. \qHadôru,\q they called him, \qHe Who Returned.\q
'There was no celebration for me, ${PLAYER}. I never fled the city, so I had no need to return a hero! I was here always: steadfast! Unyielding! The Kindred was my idea, but when the seven of us cast our lots for who would lead us, it was Azagath who prevailed. He is charming, any can see that, and the others believed he could more easily inspire the Umbari people than I could. I have been patient through all these troubles. Is that not inspiring?'
Hármelak stares at you with eyes of ice, and despite her words you can tell that being passed over for leadership of the Kindred bothers her more than she is willing to say.
'Do not misunderstand me. I would be content for any to lead us if he or she held dear the interests of the city, ${PLAYER}. But I think it is not so for Azagath. He has some plan of his own, a secret he keeps from the rest of us: The Song of Waves and Wind. I know not what it is, but it cannot be in the interest of my city.'

'I take you to see her,' Rothog continues. Some of the people nearby stare at you and the half-troll member of the Kindred of the Coins, many of them backing away or preparing to run if his attention turns to them.
'Now, ${PLAYER}. Hármelak does not like to be kept waiting.'

'Thank you, Rothog.'
Hármelak studies you silently for a moment. When she speaks again, her lips turn upwards in a faint smile.
'Welcome to Umbar Baharbêl, ${PLAYER}. I could have invited the others of your group, but I prefer to speak to you alone about this matter. You understand. It is not often that I have the opportunity to speak to such as you. It is the matter of our hostage that brings you here, I understand?'
You keep your expression guarded, but Hármelak's smile becomes more pronounced.
'Khôltekh prides himself upon knowing everything that transpires in this city, but he does not share everything with us. I have eyes of my own, and they see a great deal at a variety of interesting places: outside the jail in the Fleet-fast, by the home of Belondor and Mêshka in my very own Upper Ward, among the alleys of the Sail-haven. Your group has not remained hidden to my eyes, ${PLAYER}, and I know why you have come to my city.
'Let us continue our discussion by the fountain of my courtyard.'
'Let us continue our discussion by the fountain in my courtyard.'

'You stand in the presence of one of the wealthiest people in all of Umbar, ${PLAYER}, but know this: wealth does not grant complete power. How many of my rivals had riches but lacked the will to maintain their control? Now their wealth is mine. The folk of the city whisper that my fortune rivals that of many dwarf-lords, but their whispers are untrue: my fortune exceeds that of even the dwarf-kings! I am the matron of the most powerful merchant clan in Umbar, and we trade in all manner of expensive goods from across the Haradwaith: spices, jewels, silks, artwork, even relics of ancient days.
'I was widowed when I was young, and my husband's brothers sought to gain control of the business. They failed. It takes an iron will to prosper as I have. Did I not witness Mût Tadaul, the Death of Light, when I was but a young girl? I knew the evils of the Church of the All Seeing from a young age, but I saw too the value of maintaining the appearance of cooperation. In public I allied with the Ordâkhai occupiers and then with the Heirs of Castamir, but always I worked secretly against them. Quietly I set up a network of those opposed to the interlopers endangering my city. It brought me into contact with some who shared my goal of making Umbar Baharbêl a Free City: Azagath and Belondor, Khôltekh of the Temámir, the smugglers Tumúldo and Nakási.
'When Balakhôr perished in the war and the power of the Heirs of Castamir was broken, I knew the time had come to act. We will speak of it further in the garden to the north.'

'This is Lhanuch, the village of the Uch-lûth from which Nona came? I am pleased to see it. She did not speak of it often, but when she did her voice was fond... despite her attempts to prevent it, I think.
'You had better go on ahead, ${PLAYER}. Nona's people will remember you. Caebar and my sister and I will be considered... what was the word? Duvodiad? Yes, that was it.
'The three of us may be duvodiad, but in Lhanuch I believe you will be welcomed.'

'I knew you would one day climb this hill and come again to Lhanuch, ${PLAYER}. I saw it in the Pool of the King only weeks after my daughter Nona departed, following the dream that carried her away to fight another kingdom's war. She returned months afterward with a broken heart and a child in her belly, and I thought you would return in the company of this man, this Horn who was the father of the child. But sun and moon rose and fell, and it was not you who first came to Lhanuch with tidings.'
Suvulch frowns, and you remember that he considers himself more gifted with weapons than with words.
'It was a minstrel, an old one with white hair and a solemn face. He said he served a king of the horse-lords who perished fighting the Dark Lord, and he had sad tidings for Nona. \qHorn is dead,\q he said to her, and while she had raged with anger in the wordless months that passed, her fury was replaced all at once, and with sorrow. I wept with the two of them. Yes, even I! But I am her father, and I raised my Nona to be strong. Her tears showed to me how deeply she loved this Horn, even though she buried that love beneath the rage she held for him, and which he deserved! So I wept alongside them, and when the minstrel departed I embraced my daughter and I told her that I would never again say a cross word about the man Horn.
'I meant it even then, but in time I have come to understand he was a man of courage who believed he was not courageous, ${PLAYER}. That is a curious thing, and not common among the Uch-lûth. But perhaps not all can be as honest as Suvulch, who is certain of his courage and acts upon it every day.'
He roughly clasps your arm, and then points up the hill.
'My daughter sits by the summit of the village, by the fire on the right. She will be glad to see you.'

'${PLAYER}, my dear friend! It is good to see you again at last! If you waited a few more months you might meet my son or my daughter... but I am glad you did not wait.
'No, I do not yet know what my child will be! When the days feel longest I wonder if Hildegard would tell me whether I am having a son or a daughter... but I cannot bring myself to return to the soothsayer's cave. When Gléowine came to Lhanuch and told me of what transpired before the walls of Minas Tirith... it was as if I was hearing of it for the second time, seeing it again, feeling anew all the pain of it. So I will not return to Hildegard.
'Gléowine spoke also of your deeds, and I know Horn was avenged. I would have become Wadu's Ghost once more and done it myself, but you can see that I am somewhat occupied for now. So I thank you, and I know Horn does as well, and so does his child.'

'Stand aside, ${PLAYER}. To return here, after sending me away... his wits are more addled than they used to be! How can you explain his presence here?'
Nona's eyes boil with fury, but your keen eyesight reveals that the hand holding her brother's sword trembles. She does not want to become Wadu's Ghost again, despite her words and the anger she has nursed for Horn since he sent her away from the war. If only there was some way for you to break the tension. You cast your thoughts back to the days you spent travelling with Horn and Nona, and then you have it.
You recount your cautious steps within the deserted village of Dunfast, in Wildermore, when Nona had left your little party, leaving you in the company of Horn, the minstrel Gléowine, and Corudan. The Elf felt eyes upon your group, and it was with heightened senses that the four of you crept towards the bush that seemed to contain the unwelcome and hostile eyes. Horn valiantly approached the bush, his hand upon his sword, prepared to face whatever evil lurked within...
... and promptly fell down on his rump when the shrew within leapt out of its hiding-place
Nona smiles as you approach
Suvulch nods in greeting
Corudan encouraged you to climb the hill into Lhanuch and ensure that your group will be welcome.
Suvulch stands partway up the hill in Lhanuch.
Suvulch told you Nona is further up the hill within Lhanuch, and will be delighted to see you.
Nona sits by the fire near the summit of Lhanuch.

'This is Lhanuch, the village of the Uch-lûth from which Nona came? I am pleased to see it. She did not speak of it often, but when she did her voice was fond... despite her attempts to prevent it, I think.
'You had better go on ahead, ${PLAYER}. Nona's people will remember you. The rest of us will be considered... what was the word? Duvodiad? Yes, that was it.
'The rest of us may be duvodiad, but in Lhanuch I believe you will be welcomed.'

'I knew you would one day climb this hill and come again to Lhanuch, ${PLAYER}. I saw it in the Pool of the King only weeks after my daughter Nona departed, following the dream that carried her away to fight another kingdom's war. She returned months afterward with a broken heart and a child in her belly, and I thought you would return in the company of this man, this Horn who was the father of the child. But sun and moon rose and fell, and he never showed his face.
'My daughter sits by the summit of the village, by the fire on the right. She will be glad to see you. As for the others who wait below... who can say? If they do not speak the right words, they may learn the daughter of Suvulch can be even more dangerous than he is, and that is no small amount!'

'${PLAYER}, my dear friend! It is good to see you again at last! If you waited a few more months you might meet my son or my daughter... but I am glad you did not wait.
'No, I do not yet know what my child will be! When the days feel longest I wonder if Hildegard would tell me whether I am having a son or a daughter... but I cannot bring myself to return to the soothsayer's cave. If she had not spoken as she had, perhaps Horn...
'It does not matter. It has been months but my anger has not cooled. It is said the Uch-lûth love even more fiercely than they fight, and you should cross them in neither! Someone should have told that to Horn before he sent me away, the fool. Yes, I know he thought he was doing right. He was wrong, and should have listened.'
Instance: The Ghost Returns
Nona is prepared to become Wadu's Ghost and slay her former lover... but you cannot stand idly by.

'I have not had time yet to rest and to speak with my brother, for we have gone from one danger to another. I look forward to hearing of Corudan's adventures and telling him of my own. Perhaps that time has come.
'It may not last, for while the Kindred of the Coins has claimed to make this a Free City, it would seem an evil has taken root within the membership of that council. I do not think your business in this land is yet finished, ${PLAYER}. Azagath remains a danger... and my heart tells me he is not the only member of the Kindred who is not as they appear.'

'During the sea-voyage that brought young Thorongil and me to Umbar, I did what I could to keep the boy out of trouble. It was not always an easy task, and I tell you truly that it was a thankless one... but I am relieved that both he and I survived the passage. That he has also been brought safely from the Citadel of Winds... it is a sign of your prowess and my memory of our shared adventures that I am less surprised by that!
'I look forward to hearing of my sister's adventures and to telling her my own. I still cannot believe that she is alive, but of course she was always... stubborn. She might say the same of me, but I believe Sigileth has always been more headstrong than I am. Since you have spent time with each of us, only you can tell us for certain.'
Corudan smiles.
'No, you can keep your answer. I know what it is.'

'My brother always has a plan or a scheme in mind, ${PLAYER}! Do you think he had this planned all along? Is this why he refused to join your crew? It must be, surely!'
You consider whether to dispel Daxamat's notion of his brother, and decide not to do so. You suspect that it would take a ship's hold full of evidence to lessen Daxamat's opinion of his brother, and even then it might not be possible.
'My brother is really something, isn't he?' Daxamat asks you, and you have no choice but to nod in agreement.

'I have listened to the account of what transpired within the Citadel, ${PLAYER}, and my mind is clear. Belondor has no love for Gondor, and who could blame him for that, but he is not a monster. Whatever evil lies at the heart of the Kindred of the Coins, my old friend is not the cause of it. He would have prevented Nakási from slaying their young hostage... I am sure of it.
'Azagath and the web he has woven has my friend caught, just as I was enmeshed by the commands of the Steward Denethor. Belondor is not beyond saving. Of this I am certain.'

'It is done, for now, is it not? We have carried out the commands of King Elessar, though they have brought us far from our homes.'
Caebar looks out over the water, and shrugs his shoulders.
'I suppose I don't really have a home any longer, do I? My mother and my uncle Carlong would not welcome me back to Ethring, not even if they knew the part I played on this grand adventure. Especially not if they knew. It wasn't that large a part, but I'd like to think I was some help along the way.
'It is up to me to make a new home for myself now, somewhere out here in the world. I was so afraid of... I cannot say what I was afraid of, exactly... I think it was the \qbigness\q of the world, that sense of vast, open spaces, far beyond the land in which I grew up. It is so different here, but perhaps that is a good thing for me. I could not find a place in which to belong in the land of my birth. Maybe I will find a place here.
'Thank you for bringing me along on your voyage! I will do whatever I can to help King Elessar bring peace to Gondor, and if that causes further conflict with the Kindred of the Coins, well... I will do what I can to help. All you need do is ask, ${PLAYER}. I will follow wherever you lead!
'Just... maybe not aboard a ship next time,' he says, with laughter in his eyes.
Jajax is by the Harbour Warden's tower.
Nimrodel is by the Harbour Warden's tower.
The successful completion of your mission to Umbar is the result of those who helped you, and many of them are now by the Harbour Warden's tower and want to speak with you.

'Our mission to Umbar is completed, ${PLAYER}, for both captives held by the Kindred of the Coins have been rescued. I will return with Thorongil to Anfalas as soon as it can be arranged. His father Carandolion will be very pleased, but not surprised, to learn that we have triumphed!
'There will still be work to be done here in Umbar. I know it.'

'Has it been so long that you have forgotten the most important rule of all, ${PLAYER}? Never count Jajax out of a fight, for he will return and surprise you! It is a lesson the Prince of Dol Amroth has now learned. You should have seen his face when it became apparent that only Jajax could turn defeat into victory!
'Aye, it seemed defeat was certain. He has spies in this land, a band of whisperers and movers-in-secret that go by the name \qCircle of the Eagle,\q and when they reported to him that your ship never arrived, he despaired. A plan was conceived, a desperate plan, but it was considered the only option left to save the captive boy. The Prince could not achieve it, nor could the King. Only a Corsair would do. Only THE Corsair would do, and that means Jajax!
'It is good to be owed favours by Kings and Princes, ${PLAYER}, and I shall be well-rewarded for my part in this deception. I admit I believed the water carried by Nimrodel was in some way enchanted and would prove more effective that it turned out... but all is well now. It must be the good fortune of Jajax coming through in the end once again.
'How did my brother fare on your voyage? I hope he did not make too great a mess of things without me there to set him right!'

'For long years I believed I was no longer a part of the world, ${PLAYER}, and I sheltered with the Avorrim and stood at a remove from all others. The kindness of Arwen, and the good heart of Roamingstar, have taught me I was wrong. In gratitude I offered to play a role in their drama... was it very different than the role I played for so long, the role of Dorthaneth?
'I have set aside my veil of mourning, ${PLAYER}. It is good to be of help to my friends, no matter the dangers. Their kindness is like the warm sun upon my skin, and I welcome it.
'But do not mistake me! The danger of Azagath remains. I judge that he is no ordinary man; I felt Sauron's mark upon him.'

'I have spoken with the others, and I still do not understand one thing. If the Corsair Jajax arranged with Khôltekh to gain access to the Citadel with his prisoner... why did the Temámir not accompany Jajax inside? If he believed Jajax's prisoner was truly Queen Arwen, would he not want to be present at the Kindred's triumph?'
Gimli strokes his beard.
'Unless... unless Khôltekh knew that Jajax had not actually captured Queen Arwen. But why would he help us rescue Thorongil? Is he secretly working against Azagath's aims?'
You tell Gimli that your audience with Hármelak has shown you the Kindred of the Coins may not be as united in their purposes as it seems from the outside.
'That is why the King Under The Mountain is so important, ${PLAYER}. I will keep thinking about it. Khôltekh's place in all this makes my head hurt!'

'I have listened to the account of what transpired within the Citadel of Winds, ${PLAYER}, and it seems to me that Azagath Sea-shadow is no mere man. Nimrodel says she felt the mark of Sauron upon him... do you think he may be one of the Gúrzyul? If so, he has kept his nature hidden from the others of the Kindred and from the Umbari people. Nakási Wave-reaper spoke to you of the Song of Waves and Wind before she left Gondor, and I understand Hármelak mentioned it when you met with her, but she knew little more than its name.
'Can it be that the Song of Waves and Wind has as its foundation some evil of Mordor? If that is so, we cannot leave Azagath to make use of it... whatever it may be. The adventure that brought us to Umbar is over... but our work here is not finished.'

'It is everything I expected and more. Even now the flesh knits back together. Forgive my excitement. You see, the tail of the salamander is exceptional. You have defeated a creature that many have feared for years.
The Hunt for Nêjagil
Abido, inspired by the ease with which you accomplished all of the tasks he laid before you, asks for assistance in seeing his dream through. He wants you to hunt and slay Nêjagil.
Meet with Elder Madag about the strange disease afflicting Khûtra.

'We've heard troubling reports of an unnatural disease afflicting the people and beasts of Khûtra. Please, go to the village, investigate the disease and offer any aid you can.'
'You should speak to Roshat about the disease. He knows the most about it.'

Investigate the strange disease afflicting Khûtra's beasts and inhabitants.
Now that the fish are healthy again, Umaris has asked for your help feeding the village. Bring her a mix of healthy fish for a reward.

'Zerkho and Dorshet do not believe that there is a threat posed by the sea hawks and bog-lurkers as you attempt to relieve them of their limbs and eggs. I respect their knowledge but question that advice. I would use caution, friend.'

Speak with the expedition assistants to learn about the birds of prey and bog-lurkers on the Eastern Cape of Umbar. Though limited in use, there remains value in hunting these creatures. The assistants in the expedition camp will tell you more.
You spoke with Zerkho and Dorshet. They do not think that there is a threat from the seahawks and bog-lurkers you hunt in the north. Return to Luthana in the expedition camp.
Speak with Zerkho about the fauna in the hills
Speak with Dorshet about the fauna in the hills

'The hills and plains that meet the sea teem with an abundance of fauna, natural and corrupt. Cooks in the city use bits gathered from uncorrupted creatures to supplement the food served throughout the city.
'My role is to organize the collection and distribution of the materials the cooks require and reward any who aid in the effort. Discuss with Zerkho and Dorshet the benefits gained from gathering materials and the danger inherent to meeting the requests.'

'As you climb the hills far to the north and west of this expedition, you will see signs of uncorrupted fauna. Seahawks soar on the warm air rising from the land as it fights with cool breezes from the sea. Bog-lurkers, often mistaken for reeds or detritus, wander in large numbers.
'Cooks in Umbar draw the most value from these creatures.
'Sea hawks lay large flavourful eggs that epicures devour by the dozen. The profit gained exceeds the risk presented by disturbing the sea hawk's nests.
'Bog-lurker legs are a delicacy for the thin shaft of gelatinous meat drawn forth when boiled and the salty broth that remains after. Last, the seeds found on the lurker's back grow to stock our vegetable and spice stores.'

'I have no desire to harm the sea hawks making their nests in the northern part of the Cape of Umbar. Unlike the culinarians, I do not wish to steal their young. I want only to recover what they lose and what they find that was lost.
'I am sorry. I do not mean to be cryptic. The sea hawks lose their feathers, naturally and unnaturally. The sea hawks also find baubles and bits from shipwrecks.
'My patrons in the city desire these commodities and pay well for any who deliver them.'
'Speak with Dorshet and Zerkho. Their knowledge provides advantages in harvesting the materials my patrons require.'
Nature's Own

Speak with the expedition assistants to learn about the birds of prey and bog-lurkers on the Eastern Cape of Umbar. Though limited in use, there remains value in hunting these creatures. The assistants in the expedition camp will tell you more.

Return the hides to Khânai at the expedition camp
Proper Size of a Tent
Collected a water buffalo hide (${NUMBER}/12)

'You will find the buffalo wandering all land to the east here in the Cape of Umbar. They will roam savannah to desert in search of feed. Their hides should easily be removed once the great beasts are slain.'
With the hides collected and safely stowed, it is time to return to the hunter's encampment outside of Umbar Baharbêl to deliver the hides to Khânai.

'The blistering heat of the sun burns flesh and draws water from our skin. To protect ourselves from the danger that the sun presents, we use tents and other items to shield our heads. The buffalo that roam the outskirts of the desert have large hides conducive to these purposes. I ask that you hunt and skin the beasts for their hides and then return them to me.'
'A fine collection. I will return this to my patron in the city, and they shall be made into useful abodes for the populace.'

Khânai directed you to scour the lands surrounding the encampment but more near the savannah and desert for the water buffalo. You are to collect hides from the defeated beasts and return them to her at the expedition encampment.

Khânai suggests that the water buffalo dwelling in the areas within and near the desert to the north of the expedition have hides that are best for tents. The citizens of Umbar prize the larger hides, and she asks that you acquire some for her.
Collect buffalo haunches (${NUMBER}/14)
Deliver the buffalo haunches to Khânai at the expedition camp
'You will find water buffalo roaming the savannahs, plains, and deserts here in the Cape of Umbar. Collect the haunches from the beasts and return them to me here at the camp.'
Collected buffalo haunches (${NUMBER}/14)
Make your way into the plains, desert, or savannah to find water buffalo. Slaughter the beasts; carve haunches off their bones and deliver the meat to Khânai at the expedition camp.

Make your way into the plains, desert, or savannah to find water buffalo. Slaughter the beasts; carve haunches off their bones and deliver the meat to Khânai at the expedition camp. You will find them north, east, and west from the hunter's encampment.

'Water buffalo haunches provide several cuts of meat for the cooks of Umbar City to use in banquet dinners and feasts. They desire that we deliver a great deal of the haunches to them.
'As you hunt the buffalo, cut the haunches from the bone and deliver them to me. I will pay you for your effort and send the meat to the cooks in the city.'

'These haunches are expertly removed from the water buffalo. It is clear that you have undertaken tasks like this before. I will see that the cook's guild in Umbar becomes aware of your contributions.
'Please accept this reward for the assistance you provided.'

Khânai asked that you carve the haunches off the water buffaloes you slay in the Cape of Umbar. Cooks in Umbar City prize their meat in their banquet dinners.
Deliver the lizard frills to Khânai at the expedition camp

'Scattered across the desert, plains, and savannah in the eastern Cape of Umbar, you will find the frilled lizards in adequate numbers. Obtain fourteen frills from about their necks and deliver them to me here.'
Collected lizard frills (${NUMBER}/14)
Foray into the desert and obtain lizard frills from the reptiles there. You will need to travel north from the expedition camp. Once harvested, return the frills to Khânai at the encampment.
Collect lizard frills (${NUMBER}/14)

'There are oddities in nature that scholars believe are worth studying. The frilled lizards in the desert are among the natural creatures that Umbari scholars find fascinating.
'The thin membranous frills around the lizard's neck heal even if ruptured or removed. This regeneration is not unique among lizard-like creatures in Umbar. The process by which the membrane repairs itself is unknown; but our scholars are working toward understanding.
'We must help their efforts by acquiring lizard frills and delivering them to the city.'

'I do not care for the wanton slaughter of animals. I find it cruel and inhumane. However, I do support studying nature's mechanisms to comprehend how we might harness the natural powers and strength all around us.
'I believe this is the goal of our scholars, so I continue to support these efforts. Thank you for your assistance.'
The Frill of Them All
Foray into the desert and obtain lizard frills from the reptiles there. You will need to travel north from the expedition camp. Once harvested, return the frills to Khânai at the encampment.

Scholars in Umbar believe the membranous tissue of a lizard frill and the ability of salamanders to regenerate missing tails and limbs might help them reinforce their potions. They need more samples to study.

'There is a nest of bog-lurkers north beyond the city. I cannot say that the lurkers are a menace, only that the cooks of Umbar prize the seeds you can pluck from their backs. Their legs, too, are a delicacy enjoyed widely in the city.
'Because of these facts, they become the target of hunters. You will be paid if you join in this hunt.'

'Do not fret for the lurkers. They will recover. We have long hunted them and used them as a food source. We are careful not to reduce their population too far. We strike a balance with them and allow them to recover.'

North in the hills beyond Umbar Baharbêl, you will find bog-lurkers nesting in the fields as you approach the shore. Hunt the bog-lurkers for their legs and seeds.

Khânai instructed you to obtain sixteen glands from the spiders in their camp in the eastern stretch of the Cape of Umbar, and you have completed this task. Return the glands to her for your reward.

'I've another request from the scholars of Umbar. An interest in learning the secrets of nature inspires scholars to learn the secret of spinning spider-silk. Scholars believe that careful study of spider glands will provide insight into how the natural process of spinning webs takes place.
'Our task requires we obtain eight pairs of undamaged glands to assist in the scholars' research.'

'Such strange-looking organs. I don't know what I expected them to look like... I only know that this does not meet my expectations.
'I shall see these delivered. Thank you, ${PLAYER}.'
What Makes them Stick?
Collect spider glands from the spiders in the nest on the western edge of the desert north of the expedition camp. When you've collected sixteen of the glands, return the glands to Khânai.

You learned that the scholars in Umbar City are attempting to discern how the spiders can create the silk used to construct their webs. They want to collect spider glands to further their understanding.

'Make your way to the desert and collect pouches of spice from the sand-storms and sand-worms. You will find them north in the desert sands.'

Having recovered the spice that Khânai requested, it is time to return the sacks of freshly gathered herbs to her at the Hunter's encampment.

'Chefs in Umbar say that the blend of spices used to enhance the flavour of their dishes is more important than the collection of any other ingredient. The spice blend is rare and found only in the desert. Worse still is the method for collecting the spice.
'To obtain desert spice, you must eliminate the carrier. Strange winds streaking across the desert or sand-worms are known to be spice carriers. Seek them out in the desert land to the north and return to me when you've gathered twelve sacks full.'

'Once delivered, the cook's guild will further refine and separate the spice from the silt. The guild can include the spice in their recipes, package it for sale, and teach others the processes of refining the product.
'You completed the work asked of you. The guild will know that it was you that furnished the spice. Here is your reward.'
The Spice Flow
Seek spice from the sand-storms and sand-worms in the desert north of the expedition camp. Collect twelve sacks of desert spice and return them to Khânai.
Desert spice, used in many dishes enjoyed by the people of Umbar, requires collecting and sifting sand where desert fauna deposit spice. Khânai asked that you obtain spice for her.
Collect strands of spider-silk (${NUMBER}/16)
Return the silk to Khânai at the expedition camp
'Search for a large nest of spiders on the western edge of the desert to the north. Take care not to disturb too much at once, lest you face the wrath of the brood.'
Collected strands of spider-silk (${NUMBER}/16)
Return the silk to Khânai at the expedition camp. She will be pleased that you helped her meet the quote placed upon her.

'Merchant or magistrate, if you are a leader in Umbar, you dress in fineries offered by the outfitters who learned to refine the heavy silk of desert spiders into fine fibres and fabric.
'For those like you and me, not destined to walk the halls of leadership, we work to collect the materials that outfitters and tailors use to adorn the leaders with the trappings of their offices.
'Use caution when collecting the silk from the spiders in the desert. They are known to entrap many travellers and beasts who stumble like newborn calves through their nests.'

'I am impressed with the care you took in harvesting this silk. Too often, I will find frayed fibres dragged through the dust and dirt. Few understand that such carelessness ruins much of the material, reducing the price the silk earns when sold at market.
'Your efforts will earn top prices. Your reward reflects the care you took.'
Threads of Silk
Make your way north into the desert and collect thick silk webs from the spiders there. Be cautious; the spiders are cunning in their nests.

In the city of Umbar, the outfitters refine the silken webs of the desert spiders into fabric and dye it for use by the aristocracy. Khânai asked that you collect silks from webs and spiders to supply the outfitters in the city.
Speak with the scholar, Mallax
Speak with Khânai at the Hunter's Expedition Camp

'What the advisors teach you is learned from books and speeches. What I will tell is from experience of my own and that of travellers who make their way through the unforgiving desert.
'When there is a question of your safety move to the rocks.
'When your journey is beginning make sure to drink your water.
'Share your water with others only if they are trusted or of your kin.
'Do not linger on the hot sand too long.
'Now... you are as prepared as can be.'
Khânai made sure you understood that you should speak with the advisors visiting the encampment to learn what is hunted for in the desert and the dangers that the flora and fauna present.
Speak with Zerkho
Speak with the outfitter, Karbah

'The land to the east of the city and north of this encampment is barren and desert-like. There lay a wasteland where trees grow sparsely and danger lurks within the sand.
'Terrible creatures sift through the sand, spin it about them as they blow across the landscape, or, worse, lay traps to ensnare the unobservant.
'Above all else, one must be alert and informed when entering those lands.
'I advise consulting with the experts here within the expedition camp for their guidance and direction to understand why we hunt in the desert and what you should expect if you make your way there.'

'Khânai sent you to learn about why the chefs of Umbar desire us to explore and ravage the already ravaged desert land to the east of the city, eh?
'I will tell you, then. Across the desert grows an abundant array of aromatic and potent spices that give many of the dishes enjoyed by our aristocracy. It is for this reason that we send so many adventurers into the wastes.
'There are enemies there: grim winds that carry the spice, and worms that sift the sand to move, leaving spice in their wake, or, carrying the spice within themselves. These are each viable targets for the collection of the spices we desire.
'But be wary, the magical nature of the grim and the violent nature of the sand-worms should not be underestimated.'

'In the desert land east of Umbar Baharbêl, there is a great brood of spiders weaving deep nests and webs to ensnare beasts as large as water buffalo. It is these spiders that the aristocracy prizes. Not for anything other than the webbing and silk that the spiders weave.
'When worked through looms, the spider-silk can be turned into beautiful fabrics that are then dyed and manufactured to the specifications made by the great tailors of the guilds and sold to the well-to-do.
'Be warned, the spiders are foul creatures with a penchant for blood. And, sadly, they are very good at obtaining what they desire. You must simply be better at keeping yourself alive.'

'The reasons to hunt in the desert waste are many. As a scholar, the main reason that I choose is knowledge.
'We seek to understand the secrets of spider's weaving webs. We wish to know why the frill about a lizard's neck repairs itself as does a salamander's body. These mysteries are the puzzles that drive us back into the desert when we know the dangers are great.'
The Eastern Stretch
Having spoken with the advisors, you should return to Khânai and let her know that you are prepared to deal with the flora and fauna of the desert.
Khânai suggested that you should converse with the experts visiting the expedition from the city to learn more about the vale and the threats across the desert to the east and north.

'You will find spider eggs within the nest in the desert to the north. Be careful not to disturb the brood matron watching over the unborn menaces.'

After collecting enough eggs from the spider's brood lair, you should return them to Khânai at the Hunter's camp in the Cape of Umbar.

An inventive answer to the dangers presented in harvesting spider-silk is to control the brood in the city. Khânai asks that you collect spider eggs from the nest in the desert so she can deliver them to the scholars and outfitters.

'Scholars and outfitters in Umbar City concocted a plan to produce silk at reduced risk to people like us. They desire to gather enough eggs from the brood mother in the desert nest to cultivate a brood within the city.
'Should they succeed, perhaps our lives would be less fraught with danger. I will carefully package and deliver the spider eggs if you will collect them for me.'

'I dare not ask the scholars how many spiders hatch from these eggs. I will leave the rearing of these crawling menaces to those with a stronger stomach. I will focus on the worms that stalk the sand. They intrigue me more than anything with legs.'

North, beyond Umbar city, where the hills roll into the shore, sea-hawks soar above the land. They build nests in the crags and trees. They lay eggs prized by the chefs of Umbar. Collect the eggs and return to Luthana at the expedition camp.
Your efforts to collect sea-hawk eggs proved fruitful. All you need do now is return your precious cargo to Luthana at the hunter's expedition in the south-eastern portion of the Cape of Umbar.

'I will clean these items and separate those with value for shipment to the city's jewellers. I want to thank you for doing this. This effort is above and beyond what I am required to do. It earns me favour with the guild and the Kindred. This effort provides favour to the people of Umbar for you.'

'I am sure there is a way to draw the bird down from that height so you can take the message it carries.'

'Ah, thank you for this, friend! The fall of the Heirs and the rise of the Kindred diminished Achardis's capacity to gather information, yet she persists, and still she awaits requests from us. This bird network of hers... she calls them the Watchers on the Wing.'
He produces a small note and hands it to you.
'We need to send this message back to her. Bind the message to the sea-hawk's leg; it will do the rest. Return to me after the Watcher on the Wing has left.'
You gently remove the paper tied to its leg. The sea-hawk does not seem to mind, and in fact appears to be very comfortable exchanging the information for the delicious dinner you set before it.

'The threat of the Kindred of the Coins cannot remain unknown. After the fall of the Mâkhda Dahak-'
He shakes his head.
'Forgive me. I am Harthabor, and you should call that place Mâkhda Khorbo, my friend. My folly was not using the local vernacular. Do better than me.'
He begins again.
'After the fall of the Mâkhda Khorbo and the Heirs of Castamir, whispers and warnings from eagles throughout Umbar ceased. Worse, we lost contact with our leader in Umbar City.'
He stops and shakes his head again.
'The citizens call it Umbar Baharbêl, and so should you.
'Can you see why I need your aid?'

'We set forth to reestablish contact with the leader of the canaries in Umbar Baharbêl, but we were ill-prepared. Missteps and affronts to changes in custom abound. Many of our names are etched in their ledgers, and I know they are not written there because of our heroism.
'Through this archway to the east, I saw a sea-hawk perched atop a roof. That is a courier, I am sure of it! Every day, that bird arrives and perches there looking for something. I have seen a scrap of paper affixed to its leg! It likely seeks the eagle that used to watch this outpost, and has a message to deliver.
'I cannot approach it without drawing attention to me, but you have committed no offence and breached no customs. You can act as our eagle here.
'Coax the bird from its perch and obtain that scrap, then return to me.'

'That sea-hawk? We call her Watcher on the Wing. She's oft up there waiting for a scrap of meat to fall off a careless plate. She doesn't care much what kind of meat it is. She's harmless, as birds go.'
'That's the Watcher on the Wing. She's a vigilant bird. She perches at that spot each day she's here. Nary moves unless it's for a scrap of food or a shiny bauble. She's lovely though, isn't she?'

${PLAYER},
We hope this message finds you well. Your efforts throughout Umbar Baharbêl fill our pages with credibility and nobility unseen in these lands for ages. We are pleased that an ally like you is in our midst.
It is for this reason that I write to you. Your proven capacity for both compassion, discretion, and swift reciprocity are needed. At your earliest convenience, please return to me at Jax Phanâl. There is a matter of import I wish to discuss.
Zarai Ledger-keeper of Jax Phanâl

'It is fortuitous that you return to me. I sent you a letter. I was unsure if it reached you. That is of no matter now.'
She pauses and shifts uncomfortably.
'You prove yourself daily to Umbar Baharbêl. There is a matter that recently came to my attention. I would ask for your aid if you are willing to provide it.'

'Our roles, while necessary, breed discontent with some areas of the populace. Some believe, incorrectly, that our records detail all actions undertaken within Umbar Baharbêl and that we expose or trade secrets to the guards or Kindred's enforcers. Some believe we still serve the Heirs of Castamir.
'Neither is true.
'We humbly do our work as a form of penance for the years of torment wrought upon the populace. Self-preservation is a powerful motivator.
'Because of this, our couriers and aides sometimes find themselves the target of ire or worse.
'A courier travelling south toward Rakhatâb was assaulted and lost one of our ledgers during the attack. The courier is well. You needn't concern yourself with their welfare. I require your attention on the ledger.
'While escaping an assailant, the courier stumbled off his mount and ran east toward the mountains. Along the way, he dropped the pack containing my latest ledger. I no longer require the book; I need it delivered to my colleague Aphamâr at Rakhatâb. She usually stands across the path from the stable-master in Rakhatâb.
'Can you do this?'

'By order of the Kindred of the Coins: the Captain of the Haven, Eshmun, requires assistance in rebuilding the Sail-haven and safe-guarding it from the enemies of Umbar. 'Hail! I am Eshmun, harbour-warden and Captain of the Haven, and I was appointed to this station by the authority of Tumúldo Fierce-water—greatest, to my mind, of the Kindred of the Coins.

You tell Eshmun that you have come to help rout those loyal to the Heirs of Castamir from Umbar Baharbêl.
'Is that so, stranger? I must admit, I am more accustomed to visitors perusing our markets than leaping at the opportunity to involve themselves in the affairs of the Kindred of the Coins, but I have been left little choice, it seems.'

Eshmun's demeanour darkens.
'He was a good man. None who survived the Mutiny should have met with such an end, but still those craven louts cut him down for the crime of helping to rebuild the Sail-haven. I trust that Zemirah and Ahûd were confident in their judgements, but such a violent action taken against the people of Umbar—against the Kindred of the Coins—cannot go unanswered!'

Eshmun, Captain of the Haven, wants to assess the threat of the Heirsworn following the Sea-stone Mutiny.

'Before I took up this station, the Captain of the Haven and many of his harbour-guards were loyal to Balakhôr the Scourge and the Heirs of Castamir. Nearly all of them were slain in the Mutiny, but as you might imagine, having fewer men has made my efforts to rebuild the Sail-haven far more difficult—and I will not be made to look the fool when Tumúldo Fierce-water returns from his voyage!
'Rumours abound of the Heirsworn and their plots in Umbar, but aside from the few that hurl insults from the decks of their ships in the harbour, I see no greater plan at play in the Free City. I only know what I have seen with my own eyes, and to speak plainly, I am not the young sailor I once was!
'To that end, I would ask that you speak to Zemirah, the new master of the sailors' guild, as well as Ahûd and Râmax, the foremen of the ship-yards in the Sail-haven. If there is an imminent threat to Umbar, they will know of it.'

'Greetings!
'Have you come seeking to join the sailors' guild? I must admit, you do not look the sort at a glance, but our membership is... thinner than it was before the Mutiny. If not for that reason, then speak quickly, for my time is not idly spent. What do you need?'
You inform Zemirah that Eshmun hopes to assess the threat of the lingering Heirsworn in the Sail-haven.
'The Heirs of Castamir had many supporters in Umbar and a great many of them were members of the sailors' guild. In fact, my predecessor was one of Balakhôr the Scourge's most ardent followers, but I digress. I have done what was necessary to put my house in order, if you understand my meaning, but it is no secret that the Scourge's loyal captains still maintain a foothold in the Haven. From what I have heard, they find shelter on the decks of their ships, cowering behind their crews, or in the taverns of the Sail-haven. That is all I know, ${PLAYER}.'

'Yes?'
You tell Ahûd that Eshmun hopes to assess the threat of the lingering Heirsworn in the Sail-haven. In addition, he wishes to learn if they have troubled the work at the ship-yards of Umbar Baharbêl. Ahûd nods and smirks.
'Tumúldo chose wisely, I think. Age has not slowed Eshmun in the least, and though he might seem a kindly old man at first glance, he is every bit as vicious as his predecessor. The only difference between the two of them is that Eshmun fights for the people of the Free City... and, of course, that he did not end up in the waters of the harbour with a spear through his back.
'Nevertheless, I can say with certainty that none of the Heirsworn have troubled this ship-yard. I have only employed shipmen from the sailors' guild since the Mutiny, and even so, I have conducted routine inspections of these ships at every stage of their construction. I have seen the Heirsworn cowering at their ships at the edges of the harbour, but aside from petty theft and harassment, they pose little threat to our work here in the Sail-haven. It seems they mean to pillage the city and scatter like rats before the Kindred can slay the last of them. I say let them! Death would be a kindness for them—let them suffer their shame in exile!'

'When I was made Captain of the Haven, Tumúldo said it had to be me—Kindred of the Coins or not, he knew I could keep watch on the Sail-haven. Like it was with poor Râmax, I have known Tumúldo since he was a boy, and though our friendship has been a complicated one at times, we have grown to trust each other without question.
'Before Tumúldo departed on his voyage, he told me to do whatever I must to protect Umbar Baharbêl and its people from those who still put their faith in Balakhôr the Scourge. While these Heirsworn may not fly the black sails of old, they are still at war—only instead of with Gondor, who was too mighty for them to overcome, they have turned their hatred upon their own. I have seen Umbar changed again and again through turmoil in the course of my life, but we have never been so close to true freedom. The Heirsworn cling to the past, and their grip loosens with each passing day, but how many more must be injured—or killed—before they are finally only a memory? I say none! We shall pry each of their fingers loose until their grip is broken, and when that is done, Umbar Baharbêl shall truly be a Free City!
'You are a hale adventurer, and though I do not know your journey, I know that you share my hatred of those who call themselves the Heirs of Castamir. Let us work together and put an end to them, once and for all!'

If a merchant loses his stall or his goods to the actions of an undesirable few, the others band together to see that he is made whole, and the wrongful parties are... dealt with. That is why we must do something about the upstarts who have taken over the Raven and Albatross. They tried to send a message to the proprietor of this inn, the House of Twisted Vines, by ruining some of his prized trellises, as you can see. But this cannot go unpunished.
'I am a representative of the community here in the Upper Ward, and my name is Dehêbix. I speak for myself, but more importantly I speak for the community. For the sake of its people you will tell me what you know about these upstarts.
'You did not see the attack? Then I shall count upon you to mete out the justice that is required. The upstarts that did this can be found fortifying the Raven and Albatross here in the Upper Ward. They will not be afraid to kill you, I am afraid, but the community will reward you if you risk this danger.'

'My associates have sent word of your deeds to me, and I approve. Those upstarts will think twice before crossing the Golden Queen again, and if they do they know what will happen to them.
'Did I not say before that I am an agent of Lady Hármelak? I believe I made it clear to you that I represent the community of the Upper Ward, and if you are to spend time here you must know, or must learn, this simple truth: Lady Hármelak IS the Upper Ward. It is her coin that remunerates you now, and her favour you have earned. Cherish it, for it is of great value.'

'For as long as I can remember, our buildings were always draped in black. The Church did not allow any other colours to be displayed. A silly thing to concern themselves with, perhaps, but hasn't it always been about control?
'That is why the scholars and I continue to do our research. With every colour we return to the city, we spit in the faces of tyrants who tried to control us... and come what may, the people of Umbar will endure.'

'There you are. Behold!'

Recording Recollections

'My childhood memories before Mût Tadaul -- the Death of Light -- are hazy. But Mût Tadaul itself, I remember as clear as water.
'Ordâkh soldiers flooded the streets, tearing down banners of all colours as they went. The cries and the screams of people echoed around me. Umbar burned. My family ran to the docks in hopes of fleeing by water. When we beheld the burning remnants of ships that had attempted to do the same, we could only turn back.
'Many good people died that day. Some days, I am still there, and Umbar is still burning.
'As a Harâph, I have spun countless stories for eager listeners. This is not a story that I enjoy telling, but it is one that must be told. It must be remembered.'

'When the riots started, I joined along with other Hûliz. Too long had we been used as the Heirs' executioners. Perhaps it was the rush of finally fighting back, but I knew we would succeed. After all, we outnumbered those in power.
'Some of my fellows died believing they had helped change things. And they did. But I watch as the Kindred replace the Heirs. I watch as our most vulnerable citizens continue to suffer, just in different ways. And I wonder what the future holds in store for Umbar -- if anything else will change.
'I no longer fight as a Hûlaz. I cannot bear it.'

'The colourful banners around the city still surprise me, every day. When will I get used to it? I do not know. But I wish Mother and Father were here with me to see this.
'Worshippers took them from our home. If our neighbours had not found and hidden me, I would have burned along with them. I survived only because I was lucky. I hate feeling like that.
'The Church may be gone from Umbar, but its shadow still exists.'

'Thank you, traveller. These accounts are not the ancient texts that many of my colleagues seek, but they are just as important.
'History tells us of how Umbar was passed from empire to empire. The Church may have tried to purge the past, but simply look around and listen -- not everything was destroyed. The Númenórean and Hamâti architecture, the sounds of Umbari, Westron, and Ordâkhai words. The people and their stories. We were here. We still are.'

'Shajât sent you? Who is that?'
You tell the captain that Shajât also may have been called \qThe Ballast,\q and he groans.
'Oh, I see. Do you know why we called him the Ballast? He may not understand this, being so unused to a mariner's life, but ballast is a heavy material, usually iron, lead, or stone, placed in the hold of a ship to keep it steady. When used as a name for someone onboard a ship... it means that person is useless.
'He was just terrible, friend. During the days he was with us we encountered enough ill fortune and bad luck to fill a year. He tied the wrong knots, scrubbed the wrong floors, emptied the wrong pots, read the wrong weather signs, pointed out dangerous shoals as safe and safe shoals as dangerous. I have never seen someone less-suited to shipboard life. So I sent him away.
'We did not mean to hurt his feelings. Boys! I say we pass around the hat and raise some coin for the Ballast to begin a new life. Every man should put in some coin... and make his donation with the certainty that it will keep the Ballast as far from our ship as might be managed!'

'I will go to the Swain's Guild Hall, in the Lower Ward. I understand that is from where some of the caravans across the desert depart, and that is the new profession I have chosen for myself. I will see you there, friend!'

'You are not going to believe this, friend... but as I made my way here I was accosted by ruffians, and they stole the coins given to me by my former shipmates! Alas!
'The ruffians apparently make their home in a place called the Gut. Do you know where that is, and do you think you might retrieve the money for me? It would be a shame for the hopes of Captain Jidâlo and his crew to be dashed in this fashion! What will they think of their Ballast then?'

'The ruffians apparently make their home in a place called the Gut. Do you know where that is, and do you think you might retrieve the money for me? It would be a shame for the hopes of Captain Jidâlo and his crew to be dashed in this fashion! What will they think of their Ballast then?'

'This is a grand place for concerts and gatherings of large groups, it is true... but it also serves another purpose.
'A few months ago, I was drowsing on one of the seats here when the sun rose. To my great surprise, who should I see descending the steps but Tatháta the Beast herself, kinswoman of the Lower Ward? She is a towering, imposing figure; if you have ever seen her, you know she is not a woman with whom you should trifle! But on this morning she was not alone: she was walking two of her great hounds, the ones named Nûdil and Jôzi, around the amphitheatre. They worked up quite a sweat, the three of them, conducting great circuits of the structure.
'And it gave me an idea: if I did as Tatháta did, would I develop into as physical a specimen as she? So I have been coming here and walking down the steps, across the way, up the steps again, and following the curve of the seats back here. You should do the same! Why not make three circuits of the amphitheatre, friend? Be sure to start by running down the steps to begin!'

'From this observatory, scholars in Umbar Baharbêl once gazed at the skies above, studying the night sky for wisdom. How distant was that age of knowledge? Too long ago for one lifetime, my friend; the observatory was destroyed, and has fallen into ruin in the years since.
'But I have dreamed about the things you might have seen from its balconies and from the rooftop viewing platforms. Will you do something for me? I am a scholar of sorts myself, but my subjects are more terrestrial than those of the folk who once worked in the building above us. Will you take this small leather bag and fill it with sand from several locations east of the city? I will reward you for this work, of course.'
'Will you fill the bag I gave you with sand from several locations east of the city? I will reward you for this work, of course.'

'Thank you for doing as I asked, my friend. Did you observe that the sand you collected from each location possessed its own characteristics?'
You tell Charzâd that some of the sand was damp and some was dry; some was coarse and some was fine; some of the sand was brightly-coloured.
'And yet they were all, in the end, still sand?' Charzâd answers with a raised eyebrow. 'It reminds me of how I envision the stars in the sky. From our position here they all seem to be the same: twinkling dots of light, like jewels affixed to the heavens. But look at this!'
Charzâd reaches into the small leather bag and removes a handful of the sand you gathered. She opens her palm and lets the sand fall, where the individual particles drift and float restlessly on the breeze.
'Like stars,' she says. 'How different might the stars be from each other if we could only see them up close? Might the scholars at the observatory above us have learned the answer if they were not slain, the observatory not shuttered, and their work not lost? I think they might have.
'Thank you for doing this for me, my friend. Not everyone would! I know: I asked them. But take this for your trouble and your time.'

Zadok's clients can be found wandering around Black Anchor, and the Baths.
You have managed to collect debts from some of the Corsairs in the Gut. This should help Zadok make a respectable getaway.

'My money! You managed to get some of it back, and there is even some interest on top of it.
'You either took more than what was owed, or these people are familiar with the concept of loans after all.
'Perhaps I should rethink my business model rather than running away with my tail tucked between my legs.
'Thank you, traveller!'

'What do you want?
'I am at my wit's end. I cannot possibly make up for all the money I have lost. I thought this city and a new clientele would help me make big profits as a money-lender, but these ruffians don't understand lending terms or even the notion of paying back what's borrowed!
'In addition, they extort me constantly for more hand-outs. If I am to make it out of here and start over, I'll need help with collecting debts from these low-lifes.
'Could I hire you to be my muscle and perhaps intimidate a few of my clients into paying their debts?'
Principled Interest
Zadok has re-organized his business efforts in Umbar. Perhaps he can make it work after all.

'You want my money? Do you know who you are talking to?
'You have made a big mistake this day! No one touches my money but me!'

'I have been thinking about how I could actually make a profit here in Umbar.
'Sure, the usual clientele are not used to the notion of debts, but with your help, I can set an example in the city and perhaps even The Gut!
'There is a proprietor here who took out a massive loan in hopes of striking it rich, same as me. They have a healthy reputation in the Gut. If we could set an example with such a figure, debts would surely be paid on time and with interest.'

'These rumours tell of a street charlatan. They call him Ezôti. His words are sweet but his deeds are dark. He parades animals around for show. He whips them until they do his tricks.' Ilaya spits on the ground, to show her displeasure.
'He does not understand the pact between humans and animals. He does not see them as we do. To him, they are just a means to buy coin and praise. Cheap entertainment, to be used and discarded.
'Go to Umbar Baharbêl, find Gûshida. She can be found in the Upper Ward of the city. She is like you and I. She understands animals. She is looking to expose Ezôti and end his crimes. You've done much to help us and the animals here. Please, find Gûshida, and help the animals there. They don't have much time.'

After escaping the Citadel of winds, Azagath Sea-shadow, Belondor, and Nakási Wave-reaper entered the Mâkhda Khorbo. You pursued them into the temple of ash and blood and now scour the depths for the trio.

After a battle at the Tower of Winds that crippled their ship, Azagath, Belondor, and Nakási, Reaper of the Waves flee to the cavernous underground beneath Mâkhda Khorbo. 'I do not have a good feeling about this. That door leads outside!
'${PLAYER}, we must hurry. We cannot allow Azagath to escape us!'

'No... no...
'This cannot be! Azagath and his allies cannot have escaped us!'

'I beg you! Have mercy upon me and my fellows! We had no choice! Nakási Wave-reaper threatened to skin us alive if we did not help them cast off with utmost haste! There was a terrible light in her eyes, and I think she would have done it!
'Belondor's crew is fiercely loyal, and they manned the oars without argument. Even when Azagath told them their destination, they did not balk at it as I would have done!'
You ask the dock-worker where the leaders of the Kindred intended to row, and he shudders.
'Across the water, stranger. They made for the Temple of the All-Seeing. They made for the Mâkhda Khorbo.'
'For now they have escaped us, but not for long.'

'The guardsmen are in disarray. They speak of two groups: those loyal to Azagath and those who now question him. We should remain alert for the first, and learn what information we can from the second.'
Nauriel turns her gaze to the great hall, lingering briefly on the fountain in its centre.
'I wish you had waited for me to accompany you before you came here the first time, ${PLAYER}. Had you done so, we would not now need to make this venture... for Azagath's head would already be shorn from his body and I would be half of the way back to Pinnath Gelin!
'But what is done is done, and that undone remains undone. Let us speak to these women and learn if they support Azagath or oppose him.'

'When we aided you we did not think you intended to bring Gondorian sorcery to bear against the Kindred! We fled when the Corsair made your presence known to Azagath, but from the far side of the hall we witnessed the terrible creatures as they rose from the fountain. Where have they now gone? Do you plan to unleash them upon the city?'
You assure Ushu that the Five Sisters would not have harmed either her or her friends in any way, and now that Thorongil has been rescued they will not trouble the folk of the city. She considers your words.
'That is a comfort, but something yet confuses me. If these water-spirits answered to the call of Gondor, why were they dressed in Umbari garb? To my eye they were dressed as nobles of the city, and Enât told me the same.'
You tell Ushu that the Five Sisters did not appear that way to you, and she furrows her brow but does not seem surprised.
'For one thing to appear many ways is not unusual in these times. The Kindred of the Coins seemed to be one thing to us, and yet Azagath's words of late have cast another light upon it, a light fell and sickly.'

'Are you prepared, ${PLAYER}? We will likely face opposition from those still loyal to Azagath, and they will seek to keep us from reaching their master and his allies in the Kindred.
'Once we pass through this door, we must let none keep us from finding the treacherous leader of the Kindred of the Coins! Others of your crew will follow behind to keep Azagath from circling around us and escaping. Now let us fight!'
'The corridor to the south-east descends a long flight of stairs. Azagath and his allies must have gone that way!'

'Those warriors were guarding the north-east corridor, ${PLAYER}. That must be the way Azagath, Nakási, and Belondor fled.
'It is curious, but I see no one guarding the passage. Still, we must remain alert!'

'The boy Thorongil has been saved, but I still see a loose thread in the tapestry of evil that brought him, and all of us, to Umbar! One look at his mother's face reveals it, ${PLAYER}. No sum of gold or silver could make me dare to cross her, but the Kindred of the Coins has done so, and she has not forgotten!
'What does Lady Nauriel plan to do next?'

'Half of the job is done, my friend, but the other half remains, and its name is Justice.
'Three members of the Kindred of the Coins fled deeper into the Citadel of Winds when my son was rescued. They will not escape us. We must return to the Citadel and pursue them. Azagath, Belondor, and Nakási will pay for endangering my son.
'Speak to me when you are ready to return to that place.'
'What does Lady Nauriel plan to do next?'

'These foes will not escape us. We will pursue them into their very stronghold, and no hiding-place will remain unsearched. I will thrust my sword into every closet and cabinet within which one of these villains might hide!'

'Azagath has not escaped my Justice... he has only delayed it. Even as the water builds in power behind the dam that blocks the river, so will the strength of my vengeance increase for every day he remains unpunished. He will regret his flight.
'But what evils might he find buried beneath the Mâkhda Khorbo?'

'Bring me some relics from the Dead that walk near the temple, for they may allow me to learn the flavour of the evil that remains here. Bring me rusty weapons from the steps of the temple, gemstones from spectres and spirits, and finger-bones from the wights that lurk nearby.'

'Did you recover the items I requested?'
Sigileth examines the strange items you acquired from the vicinity of the Mâkhda Khorbo. After a few moments of study, she looks up at you.
'These blades are rusty from the salt of the sea breeze, and unsuitable for use. Only the Dead would wield these; no living servant of Sauron or of the Kindred would think to use such a weapon, unless there was no other choice.
'The gemstones are interesting. When such stones as these are found within the earth, they are usually quite clear, but the gems around which these spirits and spectres form are cloudy instead. See the shapes that seem to swirl within their foggy depths? They are most peculiar.
'I cannot read very much from the finger-bones you have brought to me. No, I do not need you to drag an entire wight here to me, as I threatened before! I have learned this, and it may be enough: these wights were given motion by spirits of evil. There must be a great number of such creatures still within the Mâkhda Khorbo, though Sauron himself be gone.'

'An Umbari woman has been watching us from down the hill to the east, ${PLAYER}. I do not think she intends to do us any harm, but whenever I face in her direction she quickly busies herself with some unobtrusive task.
'Perhaps you should see if she has any information for us, or at least determine that she does not mean ill?'
'What is it, Corudan?'

'I saw you speaking with those Elves near the ruined temple up on the hill. What purpose brought the three of you to that place? I have seen Elves of the Oasis from time to time, when I have gone to the markets of the city to sell my wares, but your companions do not seem to hail from across the desert. I judge they came from across the bay, perhaps from Gondor?'
You remain silent, and Rukân chuckles to herself.
'Worry not, stranger! I am no follower of the Church of the All-Seeing, and I steer clear from that temple, as should all goodly folk! Not long ago I witnessed Azagath Sea-shadow and some of his people disembark their ship in the cove beneath the hill, and I wondered what madness might have drawn them inside. Nothing good, I imagine. Pestilence and plague have troubled Khûtra in recent days, and something spoils the fish. After you have halted whatever evil drew you and Azagath to the Mâkhda Khorbo, you should return to me and I will tell you more about those ills.
'But for now let your companions know where Azagath and his allies debarked their ship. They possessed an evil intent... I am certain of it.'

'When the Golden Host of Lothlórien waged the Battle of the Tower in the forest of Mirkwood, I did not know of its success until many weeks passed... and every week felt as long as an age in the darkness beneath Dol Guldur. It was only when you delved deeply into those forgotten passages that I ceased to be She Who Remains and became once again Sigileth, ${PLAYER}, and learned that the Golden Host had achieved victory.
'But there was evil beneath Dol Guldur, and even today each of my senses are attuned to it. I feel the presence of Sauron's works here at the Mâkhda Khorbo, even as I did in those dark dungeons. It is not as strong here as it was in the Room of Voices, but still my senses are troubled by the feel of it.
'Bring me some relics from the Dead that walk near the temple, for they may allow me to learn the... I do not know the precise word to describe it, but this will have to serve... they may allow me to learn the flavour of the evil that remains here. Bring me rusty weapons from the steps of the temple, gemstones from spectres and spirits, and finger-bones from the wights that lurk nearby. Why finger-bones?'
Sigileth raises one eyebrow and you are surprised to hear mirth in her voice when she responds.
'I did not think you would want to drag a bunch of wights over here for my investigation, ${PLAYER}. Just their finger-bones will do.'
'The structure itself is not as damaged as I had thought it to be.'
'Azagath must think to acquire some evil beneath the Mâkhda Khorbo. He must be prevented from finding whatever it is he seeks, unless that be death.'

'I had forgotten how poor my sister is at keeping secrets, ${PLAYER}. I did not begrudge you your decision to go alone into the Citadel, no matter what Sigileth says!
'I would have gone with you, had you asked. But of course you know that!'
'An Umbari woman has been watching us from down the hill to the east. Perhaps you should find out what she wants?'

'What said our distant onlooker, ${PLAYER}?'
You tell Sigileth that Azagath and his allies made use of a sheltered cove beneath the hill on which rests the Mâkhda Khorbo, and they have now gone inside the lower tunnels for some unknown purpose.
'Then that is where your road leads, is it not? Corudan and I will guard the path and ensure none think to flee this way, while you muster your allies and face Azagath beneath the temple.'
<rgb=#00FF00>If you wish to participate in the raid, this is when 'The Depths of Mâkhda Khorbo' raid takes place during the story.</rgb>
'For now let your companions know where Azagath and his allies debarked their ship. They possessed an evil intent... I am certain of it.'

'My sister's thoughts dwell upon the evils that might lie within the Mâkhda Khorbo, but I need not see them to know that a corruption lies within the very heart of the Kindred of the Coins.
'But Azagath is well-loved by his people. Do the folk of Umbar Baharbêl know that he has betrayed them?'

'The structure itself is not as damaged as I had thought it to be. It is not difficult to believe the levels below-ground may also have survived the great quake that followed Sauron's fall, and remain somewhat intact.'

'I saw you in the Citadel, stranger. You were there. Were you also in the Depths of Mâkhda Khorbo?'
Belondor shakes his head sadly.
'The writing was there, but I did not see it until it was too late. There was cruelty in the Sea-shadow, as there was cruelty in all of us... but I believed it was needed against the evils arrayed against us. The Church of the All-Seeing, the Empire of Ordakh... these were foes against which we could show no mercy. The hatred I bore for Gondor...
'Aye, I would not show mercy to any warriors of Gondor who opposed us. But not children. The boy Thorongil was not yet a man, and Azagath would have drenched the stones of the Citadel with his blood. Nakási would have obeyed the command, and done whatever the Sea-shadow ordered. The writing was there, but even then I followed the two of them as they fled. In the Depths of Mâkhda Khorbo my crew paid for my inaction, my indecision. Azagath slew them with dark, unnatural magic, and their sacrifice meant nothing.
'Do you have a crew of your own, stranger? Do you know what it means to lose them all, and for nothing?'

'Have I heard anything of late concerning the Kindred of the Coins? I confess to you I have not paid very much attention to their dealings in recent days, for I have been much occupied with caring for my new friend Rûmina. She is asleep right now, but when she wakes she is like to cause quite a commotion, chasing either her tail or the rodents that infest the Lower Ward and the Sail-haven!
'She was the loyal companion of a Corsair captain and sailed from port to port with him, but now that he has retired from that trade he has given his ship-cat to me. She seems quite happy with her new circumstance, but she keeps me very busy!
'If you check back in with me perhaps you can help the two of us with something? That would be very good of you.'

'Keep your voice down, stranger! There are unfriendly ears about!
'Well, I do not know if there are, but it is better to stay on the side of caution, is it not? People say Azagath Sea-shadow was driven from the Citadel by a great beast, and only the swords of Nakási Wave-reaper and Belondor of the Fleet-fast saved his life! I have remained on guard for any sign of the sorcerers who unleashed the beast upon the Kindred, but so far I have not seen anything. They could be anywhere.
'You should come back to me when you have finished your own errands for the day. I may have learned something by then!'
'Will you return to the Upper and Lower Wards of the city and learn what people are saying about Azagath, Belondor, and Nakási?'
'Sometimes word travels slowly, and on other occasions it can spread faster than wildfire.'

'Pssst... stranger.'
The man stares at you with piercing eyes. After a moment you realize he is speaking to you nearly without moving his mouth.
'I saw a well-dressed man in blue and silver making for one of the north-south piers extending out into the waters of the Sail-haven,' he says. 'You might go see this man.'
