Curidwan has tasked you with destroying Ordâkhai founding stones at Ghât Lor. Ghât Lor can be found far to the east of Kûgrun.

'There is one more task we must accomplish, if we actually wish to defeat the Lâg Dávrit permanently. You were probably too young to remember, ${PLAYER}, but the Lâg Dávrit is a recent affliction. It's been here for a little longer than a man's span, afflicting Imhûlar. It came with the Men of Ordâkh, as they made their way north from their strongholds further south.
'I believe their founding stones may have something to do with the Lâg Dávrit. I have sensed a powerful, foreboding energy from them. I believe they must be broken, if the Lâg Dávrit is to be properly defeated, and not merely turned back for a season.
'This salve needs time to complete. The Men of Ordâkh make their camp at Ghat Lor. Destroy the founding stones there. I believe that will rob the Lâg Dávrit of its power. Return here when you are finished. Hopefully by then the salve and my chicken pie will both be done.'

'Thank you for your kindness. It is hard some days, to bear all the burdens nature has placed upon us. I only wish for Milingor's safety, and the safety and health of all the Adúrhid in this grove. It seems a tall order this day, and most days, however.
'If we are to survive, we need you to convince Usakâr to tell you what he knows of Cúridwan. If you can find her, please, let her know how desperately we need a cure for this Pale Blight. Look around you. This was once Laithór, the Emerald Woods. It has been transformed in a Man's span into Favrathór, the Forest of Bone. So many plants and animals are afflicted with disease. We have held it off for as long as we can, however now it has crept into Vartúlin itself. We have nowhere left to go.
'Avadhril knows more about Usakâr. She often treats with him. She will know how to find him and what boons to bring with you. I believe the Golden Maiden can help us survive. We just need to find her.'

'Lidath mâd, outsider. I am fond of Thórvilon, as I believe his heart is fair, but I do not agree that there is a way to save our people. We are destined to all join in Milingor's fate, and soon, I believe. Nevertheless, Thórvilon is our leader, and I will follow his wishes. If he wishes you to treat with Usakâr, I will tell you how to do so.
'Usakâr is one of the few friends we count among Men. He has always been a loyal ally and friend to the Adúrhid. It is customary for us to send with our envoys to him a gift, part of nature's bounty. As you can see, nature has struggled and her bounty is little more than leaves and ash this season.
'There exists not far from here to the east, however, a small grove of orange trees. When last I walked this orchard, there still were a few oranges clinging to life on one of the orange trees. Bring him a gift of those oranges. I wish I could offer more, but as you can see we barely have anything to give. The southern men have cursed this land. I fear there is nothing we few who remain can do to reverse their savage violence on Favrathór, what was once Laithór, the Emerald Wood, but which is now the Forest of Bone.
'After you have the oranges, continue east along the mountain ridge. Where the mountain meets meadow, there you shall find Dag Usakâra, the home of Usakâr.'

'Milingor? Yes, she is Wearying. But we can make her transition comfortable! I have just the thing.
'Here, take this poultice to her. It is little more than tea, I confess, but sometimes tea is exactly what one needs! At the very least, it is warm and will comfort her.'

'You bring oranges, so you must be an envoy of the Adúrhid. I keep telling them not to bother sending me fruit, I don't need it. But they, ah, keep to the old ways it seems.
'You are a strange envoy indeed, from the Adúrhid. What's that? Cúridwan? She is a myth! A legend! A terrible cook! Ah, perhaps the cat's out of the bag with that, I suppose. And cats seldom go back into bags once let out. Anyway!
'I have kept Cúridwan's location and identity jealously my own for a very long time. Still, this forest continues to worsen. I know the Adúrhid continue to worsen as well. As the forest goes, so they go. Perhaps it is time to pay Cúridwan a visit after all.
'Don't tell her I called her a terrible cook. She'll be feeding me her blackened chicken pie for months as a punishment. Alright, let's be off then, if you're ready! But keep close! These woods are quite dangerous to outsiders, and many have simply disappeared in them, never to be seen again. I long for the days when a burnt chicken pie was the most dangerous thing I had to dodge.'

This odd man before you must be Usakâr

Speak with Grove Elder Thórvilon and learn more of Vartúlin

Thórvilon greets you cautiously.
'Though you are an outsider, you have the look of someone capable. I am quite desperate, enough so that I would turn to a stranger for our salvation. This grove you see is dying. My people are dying. My wife... my wife is struggling. She is wearying, fading before my very eyes. I cannot bear it.
'These eyes have seen such sights... countless miracles over thousands of years. Never did I think I would see such nightmares as these. The land cursed, the ground parched, forests as dry and white as bone. All my friends, all those I love, destined to fade and be forgotten.
'I will not fade so easily. I will not let this grove crumble to dust. That is not my path. I have a desperate idea, and you seem capable. Will you help me - will you help our people?'

'There is a man who treats with us, Usakâr. His ways are strange, but I believe he may have a powerful friend - Cúridwan, the Golden Maiden. She is someone who could help us heal Vartúlin, this grove you see around you. Ever since the southern men made their way through our forests, the trees have started dying, turning hard and white as bone. We call it Lag Dávrit, the Pale Blight.
'I believe it is tied to the southern men, but I cannot be sure. Much of what they do is profane to nature, as they burn and cut the trees and brush they meet, rather than exist within it. I believe Usakâr knows more about the Lag Dávrit, as well as the knowledge of how to contact Cúridwan. She has the power to cure the Lag Dávrit, if she wishes it. I know it in my bones.
'Before you go after Usakâr, would you check on Milingor, my wife? She is behind me, half into the Veróth growing over the bridge. It pains me to see her so. I wish to help her, to stop her Wearying, as she feels it is not her time yet. But yet the Veróth still readily accepts her. I do not wish for her to go yet. Selfishly, I want more time with my beloved.
'Also, if there are any dead branches on her Veróth, please prune them. It is better for her. I cannot do it myself right now. I cannot bear it.
'Perhaps Grove-tender Ulthral has a poultice to comfort Milingor? You should stop there first. She is on the path above me.'

'Thorvilon asked you to check on me? He is sweet to ask. And thank Ulthral for me, for this poultice....
'I thought I would undergo the Trothúl, the Wearying, when I was ready to leave this place. I am not ready, little one. I don't want to go yet.
'There is much I would still see and do in this place, with Thórvilon. He tells me to save my energy, that I need to sustain my strength another season and that Cúridwan will soon help us. My strength is fleeting, little one. Each day I see a little less of this grove, my home. Each day I feel increasingly unmoored, less myself.
'I still feel the wind in my limbs, the dry, wheezing breeze. I feel the cold and the heat on my bark. I wish... I wish... I wish many things.
'I love Thórvilon very much. I will hold on for as long as I can.'

'The Lâg Dávrit has swept through Favrathór, the forest of bone. The beasts of the forest have not been spared either, afflicted with some disease the hateful men of the south brought with them.
'It is a heavy weight on my heart, but these afflicted animals - particularly the boars of Shakhdag and the servals of Tir Katar - need to be culled from their groups, lest the whole population become afflicted. Please, help us trim the population of afflicted boars and servals north of Vartúlin, but spare any healthy beasts you see. We will rely on them to repopulate Favrathór, whenever we can reverse the effects of the Pale Blight and restore Favrathór back into Laithór, the Emerald Wood.'
'Thank you. It grieves me to ask for your blade to wound any animal, but it is for the good of the greater forest, that Favrathór may flourish again.'

'Here. Be careful with them! These saplings are easily broken. Put one sapling in each fertile area you made.'

'That was perfect! We'll make a tree-bearer of you yet. Well, if Thórvilon allows it. For that you'd have to plant some of these saplings outside Vartúlin. But that was great! Just wait - just thirty years from now, this whole forest will be transformed.'

'There is much work to be done planting and growing, now that the Pale Blight can be properly combated. We could use your help, ${PLAYER}. If you wish to learn how we plant and tend to the forest, I and the other grove-tenders will show you. You will work with Ulthral, one of our grove-tenders on the high path above.
'First, however, we need to collect cinder from nearby cinder piles. It makes the soil fertile, and it is beneficial for new plants. There should be some right outside Vartúlin.'

'These new plants growing are so exciting! There is so much for us to do. We grove-tenders had our hands full just tending to the Veróthi and holding back the Pale Blight. Now we can focus on the fun part - growing new plants in rich soil. There is much to it - lend me a hand and I'll show you how we do it.
'This is perfect. Don't you just love that smell? It smells like home to me.
'Now we need to combine the cinder with a little water into each hole you see there. Then we'll fill the holes with small saplings.'

Becoming a Tree-bearer

'Thórvilon told me you are to be our tree-bearer? It is quite the honour. Almost never given to an outsider. Thórvilon must think quite highly of you.
'Well, your task is simple enough. Gather rich soil into this sack from throughout Vartúlin. Then come back here and carefully remove these young tree saplings you see. You are then to replant them in greater Adagím. Dig a small hole out, replant them and then cover their roots with the rich soil you collect. They are to be about 20 paces east, beyond the edge of Vartúlin. This will allow us to check them easily, to ensure they are truly hardy enough to withstand the Lâg Dávrit. Off with you then.'

'You have borne the first of many trees back to the forests of Favrathór. It is not again Laithór, the Emerald Wood, nor will it be for many years. But we have hope now, because of your actions.
'The Adúrhid use 'Tree-bearer' to denote someone who has done great works for the lands near their home. Though you are not Adúrhid, you have done great works near our home. You should know that not many outsiders get to wear this title. But for you, we will make a special exception. You may wear this name with pride.'

I have instructed the grove-tenders that you are the one to be given the honour of doing this. Speak with Culvair, one of our grove-tenders. He will explain more deeply. 'This is quite the blessing Cúridwan has bestowed upon us. We must not waste any of it. You were the one who sought her out and helped heal Vartúlin. It should then be your honour to heal greater Vartúlin.
'There are many soil plots and tree copses throughout Vartúlin. Spread a small but judicious amount of the salve on each. We will use Vartúlin as a staging point to heal greater Adagím. It is my intention to see Laithór, the Emerald Wood, reborn before I leave this place and undergo the Wearying.'

'I am relieved. I can breathe easier now. We have some time to finish our defensive preparations here. Thank you for your actions defending us - please, relax here in Vartúlin. You have proven yourself to me and the Adúrhid.'

Defeat Ordâkhai at Ghât Lor (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'The southern men make war on my people, outsider. I know not why, only that it is how it always has been. If not Men, then Orcs. If not Orcs, then Men. We wish to exist, and they seem to wish we didn't. Others of my kin worry about Trothúl, the Wearying that comes with age to my people. I have never worried about it. I have a duty, to my warriors and to my people to protect them. I will not fade until the threats to my people are removed. So perhaps I will live forever. That was a joke my friend, don't look so serious.
'The southern Men, who call themselves Men of Ordâkh, have made camp east of Vartúlin. They are quite dug in, with strong fortifications, based on what Surodith has told me. If you wish to help us, send them a strong message. Defeat a contingent of them at Ghât Lor. That will buy us time to make fortifications here, designed to repel any attack they make on us. Please, go to Ghât Lor and teach the southern Men a valuable lesson - that they reap the discord they have sown.'

A Small Hope

'Some recent days are difficult, outsider. So many of my kind have faded, so many long held friends have become faded memories. Sometimes when I hear the wind blow through these trees I feel I can hear their voices. It sounds like they are calling out to me, calling me home. But it is not my time yet. It is not my time yet...
'This helps. Knowing we can still make a difference in our little corner of Favrathór, it aids me in shouldering this lonely burden. Thank you.'

'There is much to be done, if your hands are willing. The Lâg Dávrit, the Pale Blight, has swept through our great forests. What once was Laithor, the great Emerald Wood, has been sapped dry, trees turned as bone and plants turned to ash. We now call these woods Favrathór, the forest of bone. But life still struggles to find its way, even within this dying land.
'As the Artar Grove-tender, I am responsible for tending and caring for the woods around you. As you can see, I am doing a quite poor job of it. These hands, though still skilled, are lined with more than experience and slower than they used to be. But more importantly, the Lâg Dávrit has made all of us grove-tenders quite powerless. It has ossified the great trees of the ancient forest. We few who remain do what we can to combat it.
'I have been known to scavenge seed, untouched as of yet by the Pale Blight. I plant it here in Vartúlin, that we might transplant these trees and bushes into greater Favrathór when the time is right. I have had good luck with finding unblemished acorns and berry seeds to the north, in both Shakhdag and Tir Katar. However, the beasts of the area have also suffered from the Pale Blight, many becoming sickened and frenzied. I dare not scavenge there anymore, for fear I shall not return. But I am no warrior. You seem much more capable. If you are willing, would you go there and gather more seeds? It is imperative to the forest that we gather and nurture new, unblemished life here in Vartúlin.'

I must warn you however, there are vengeful Curthádi spirits, Kintai who became wrathful or vengeful at the despoiling of the forests, who roam Róthirin. It is no longer safe for the Kintai to venture there. You, however, have the bearing of one who can handle yourself in a fight.
'It is our ancestral duty to plant more Sarláshi trees here in Vartúlin, that we have enough for all the Kintai Elves who undergo Trothúl. 'Will you go in my stead? This is a sacred duty I give to you. We are responsible for tending all of our dead, peaceful and otherwise. This extends even to the odious few who become Curthádi. 'I don't miss the dogs, but I know many others do. All that howling and yelling at all hours. But yes, that all stopped several weeks ago. It's been eerily quiet at night. I know the dogs used to gather in the north-east and south-east corners of Urmâkh. There might be something there. I always stayed away from the dogs.'

'Dogs? No, no dogs here. We used to have dogs and then they all just... vanished. I haven't heard a dog barking in weeks. It's strange, now that you mention it. We used to have lots of dogs in Urmâkh.'

'You've been gathering supplies to catch stray dogs? We used to have many, but they all disappeared recently. There are no dogs here in Urmâkh. No dogs at all. Who did you say you gathered these items for?
'Barûl? I've never heard of a Barûl. He isn't a resident here - I've lived in Urmâkh all my life.
'You can try asking around and talking with other Urmâkh residents, but we don't have a dog-catcher here in Urmâkh. All the dogs disappeared - we don't need one.'

'It is as I feared. I believe this dog-catcher may have designs on the fate of dogs, and possibly worse. You should speak with Niriga. Her husband is missing - he did not come home. I hope he is merely drunk and will soon stagger home after sleeping it off, but I fear this dog-catcher may wish ill of more than dogs.

It was there that my forces and many innocents were driven out recently by the forces of the All-seeing, those accursed Barkhûshim, false prophets to a dead lord. Many were killed or captured in the battle, including my husband, Eshtali. I will see them driven from Kûr Anzar, and they will drown in the river of blood I spill from them.

Your mission is to travel to Dûl Zidur and secure precious historical artifacts and scrolls before the Barkhûshim can destroy them.
Speak to Udlanu to travel.
You have recovered the artifacts! Return with the scout to Udlanu in Urmâkh with this report.
Complete Mission: Recovering the Past

'A local scholar, Zuhûl, has alerted us to a cache of historical artifacts and scrolls he believes the Barkhûshim stole away when they fled Kûr Anzar. We know from our spies that the Barkhûshim remnant is quartered in Dûl Zidur, to the east. The Barkhûshim hold no love for history, and destroy anything not related to their fallen lord. They burned much of our written history in Kûr Anzar, and we have no reason to believe they won't destroy this cache as well.
'Those artifacts hold great significance for all Shagâni. They reveal our history, our culture, and provide important lessons for us, mistakes we should not repeat. Please, go to Dûl Zidur and secure these precious pieces of our history. Defeat any All-seeing who try to stop you. We are counting on you.'

'I am grateful, and I know Zuhûl will be as well. I had thought these artifacts lost forever. We will take excellent care of them, I can assure you of that. Thank you for your bravery in beating back the Barkhûshim.'
'Your mission is clear, ${PLAYER}. You are to go to Dûl Zidur, recover the historical artifacts and scrolls, and defeat any Barkhûshim who move to stop you.'

'Investigate the grounds of Adakûr near the crypts of Esh-kimâkhi for signs of the travellers. I pray these travellers are merely waylaid, and may still return safely to their families. Please, our need is urgent, go now in search of them.'

'I have neither patience nor time for beggars. Nor do I have resources to spare for anyone who comes asking for handouts or assistance. The Khûdi Rebels sent me a messenger whom my people must save from an Ordâkhai raiding party near the bridge, and the man still seeks an audience from me several days hence.
'He is either a fool or desperate.'
She sighs.
'Perhaps a bit of both. I do not have the time or the resources to assist them. If you are as earnest as you seem, maybe you can help them. You will find him to the east near a hut.'

'Ningêna sent you?
'Forgive me. My name is Sûkal, and I am here at the behest of my people. I am from Khûd Zagin. More properly, I am from the outpost Jirush, the 'Swords' Cross' along the 'Road of Riches.' My people have thrown off the yoke of oppression from our Ordâkhai masters in the south, but their retribution has been swift and terrible.
'I see you are not from our lands. The times are dire, and the Ambarûli struggle with their own difficulties. We have been forced into hiding and seek help in ridding our land of our oppressors. If you would be an ally, take this coin and find Sigênik at Jirush. They will test your mettle and integrity.
'I cannot promise wealth or power, and I pray your intentions are noble.
'When the battle dins, cross the Wrackwade and follow the road south to Jirush. Be wary of Ordâkhai patrols. I thank you.'

As you reveal the coin to the man, he holds up a hand.
'The first lesson you must learn is discretion. There is an appearance of freedom here, but ever watchful are the eyes of the Ordâkhai on the rise to the north-west.
'We struggle for the future of our land and people. Our leaders are few, hidden, for their safety and their families. The few who remain here are vigilant in their watch and defence. You bear a gift we sent north to our cousins in Ambarûl. If they sent you here, then you shall be tested.
'Prove your value and integrity, and we welcome your assistance. Do not, and suffer the fate of our enemies.'

Malgat looks at you as you approach and nods to a servant. The servant brings you an offering of water.
'Another foreigner passing through our land? Do you mean harm? Or are your intentions genuine?'
He pauses.
'Time will tell your tale, I think.
'I am Malgat. I keep our food stores as best I can and outfit the caravans that pass through with what materials the desert offers... or I used to before time left the telling of my tale to others.
'If your intention here is genuine, you are welcome.'
'I welcome your return, ${PLAYER}. You have met the elders and now I think I am prepared to test you.'

Elder Zidemel opens his eyes as you approach. A servant approaches with a gift of water.
'Have you come to hear the tale of our returning king? Do you hear his voice in the wind, too? The wheels of prophecy turn.
'Soon, he shall return and lay low the enemy who so long forced our obedience and subjugated our wills.
'The faithful adherents who allay the spirits of their ancestors shall know his glory and light. Have you ventured to our lands to know his grace, foreigner?
'If you be an enemy, know that we shall root you out and lay you low when our king arises. But, if your intentions are noble, perhaps you can assist the infirmed with settling the debts of their souls.'

Nangar regards you with a smile. He motions to a nearby table with flagons of water.
'Drink your fill, stranger. You are welcome here if your weapon does not draw the blood of our people. I am Nangar. I see to the upkeep of the outpost, and as you can tell, I need assistance.
'Our enemies assail us from the north and the west. They leave us open to desert crawlers and creatures when they reduce our defences and steal our supplies. But we persist, and perhaps with some help from those from afar, we may thrive.'

'To prove your sincerity and ability, I have a simple task. The elders overseeing the continued functions of the outpost do so for reasons selfish or selfless. One among them allies with our cause.
'The others we bear no ill, but their mettle is not strong enough to withstand an Ordâkhai whip, and our trust cannot be misplaced.
'Meet with the elders. They will each provide a gift of water, as is customary. One will gift you the water differently than the others. We shall test your perception when you return.
'Fair?'
Igbâl regards you with disdain. Still, a servant brings you water, as is custom. The man near Igbâl clears his throat and beckons you.

'My Lord Igbâl offers you water and welcome. You come to our outpost from afar, and we offer you fair warning. Jirush is a difficult place to live. My Lord's desire is to return Jirush to the glory of our ancestors, a trading post grander than the caravansaries you will undoubtedly see throughout the land.
'He works with the other elders here to see that we can outlast the occupation from the south. The cost is of no matter to him.
'Should you decide to remain in our homeland, perhaps we can find use of your services. You will be handsomely paid for your effort.'

'Malgat is too kind. Though his time in the wild is over, he finds ways to assist us with our needs. He also maintains our morale, which is more difficult by the day.
'As he said, I outfit the outpost with hides, chitin, and frills. Whether we use them directly or trade them to caravans as they move along the roads, these are the primary goods we have to offer. Recent efforts by the Ordâkhai in the fort overlooking Jirush and their encampment in the south-east gave pause to our hunters. Our supplies dwindle to nearly nothing, and we risk losing what little trade we have.
'If you are willing, hunt the jackals and scorpions in the northern, western, and central areas of Khûd Zagin for their hides and chitin, respectively. Then turn west to hunt the lizards for their frills.'

'Who are you?'

'Zidemel found someone to help me with penance? Blessed are his words.
'Listen well, ${PLAYER}. I am Andur, the last of my bloodline. My brothers, sisters, and all their children are dead at the hands of the Ordâkhai. Zidemel said my family would live on if I gift a patch of the desert the blood of its sons and daughters mixed with mine.
'The desert sand-sifters to the south-east are the true daughters and sons of the desert. Collect drams of their blood that I may extend my lineage.'

'The Ordâkhai took my family from the world. I will not die the last of my lineage. Please, ${RACE}, help me. The sand-sifters gather in number south-east of Jirush. With their blood my lineage may live on.'

'I thank you for this gift, ${PLAYER}. I shall make my last trek into the desert and mix my blood and theirs. I will ensure my lineage does not pass into history with my death because of your actions this day.'

'Nangar is a good man. His refusal to understand the signs disconcerts me, but that is of little matter.

'The faithful understand the meaning of the Ishími as it wails across the land. I interpret Ishími's wails and guide the flock to their absolution. We faithful will usher our age of glory back into Khûd Zagin.

'Each of the adherents you can help listen to me here. Meliri is seated, as is Zidek, and Andyr leans there against the wall.'

'I heard the cries of joy from the faithful. I hear Ishími's joyous laughter. Soon, all will see as we do. The prophecy of his return is nigh. We shall, again, know our greatest leader. Like he, we shall rise from the ashes and be a gem of the world once more.'

'I trust you enough, ${PLAYER}, that I am willing to enlist your assistance in a matter requiring direct conflict against the fortress to the north-west.
'I need a distraction... one loud enough and long enough to provide me cover to sneak into the encampment and out again unseen.
'If you are willing, I know of a secret path into the encampment. Meet me at the top of the path beneath the Ordâkhai structure on the plateau. You will find it north of Jirush.'
'I will meet you near the secret path at the south-west foot of the plateau beneath the Ordâkhai encampment.'

'Sneak into the base and defeat the dôla — the captains — the lieutenants, and the other soldiers within. While you create the commotion, I will steal behind the walls and try to find plans drafted by the keep lord Jombahok.'
A Worthy Distraction
Nangar stole into the encampment and vanished from sight. You are to assault the Ordâkhai encampment providing him a distraction long enough to go about finding their plans.

You fought back the Ordâkhai and, hopefully, provided Nangar enough time and distraction to acquire the plans. Return to the hidden path at the south-western foot of the plateau beneath the Ordâkhai encampment to speak with him.

'Bosóta did not mislead us. It is as I expected, ${PLAYER}. Love is a force more powerful than self-preservation. One will do anything for those they love. Now we must counter this defection and ruse with another to raise Jombahok's hackles, setting him and Khârdu toward an irrevocable confrontation.'

'You did well to keep blood off the sashes, and the horn is in good repair. While you were at your task, I moved the bodies of the courier and his companions to the outskirts of Khârdu's encampment to the south-east.
'Take the sashes and the horn to that location. Place the sashes on the corpses and find Bosóta nearby and conceal yourself.
'Once settled, blow the horn. Speak with Bosóta to have him leave the hiding place, and if his mettle holds, he will play the ruse well enough to convince Khârdu of our deception and return to his captain's ranks.
'I warn you, this subterfuge is not without risk, and it is only the first step on a long path to absolution and retribution for my people.'

'I will play my part. I no longer wish to make war and this will set the steps in motion to returning to my family in the south.
'Tell your leaders that I will not betray them.'
Bosóta calls out, 'Captain Khârdu, my men set upon me as I neared your camp. We must speak!'
Khârdu shouts from above, 'Bosóta is that you?'

'We want to set the Ordâkhai at odds. We need the sashes worn by the men serving Jombahok at the encampment north of Jirush. Collect the sashes and horn from there and return to me.'

'Sûlmur's papyrus is impeccable. When we are free of the Ordâkhai and trade resumes in earnest, she will have my coin. Give me a moment, and I will pen a divisive letter to start a conflict.'
Galamê works quickly and quietly. Then hands a letter to you written in Ordâkhin.
'Nangar will need to trust me. The letter carries more weight if it is in Ordâkhin. I pledge, on my life, these words will drive the captains to blows.'

'Trust.'
Nangar smiles weakly.
'If I pass this letter to Amalíbi, and the words written by Galamê are a warning to the Ordâkh, then we are all as good as dead.'
He pauses.
'If I pass this letter to Amalíbi and the words written do incite the captains to violence, we may know freedom in my lifetime.'
He pauses again.
'My heart is heavy, and my mind swirls with myriad possibilities.'
He hands the letter back to you.
'Deliver the letter, ${PLAYER}. I vouch for Galamê. We must trust one another. All of us.'

Amalíbi takes the letter and looks it over.
'What is this, ${PLAYER}? I cannot understand this. Nangar places his trust in a translator who served the Ordâkhai. Can we be so sure this is not some communication to doom us all?'
She closes her eyes. You utter one word in response, 'trust.'
'Trust? Yes. I trusted you. So, I shall trust Galamê.'

You explain your need to Sûlmur. She hands you a sheaf of papyrus.
'If we are to know freedom, we must band together. I cannot head south to aid the Khûdi, but I can supply you with a small amount of my papyrus.
'Tell those who fight in the south. Should we drive our enemy out first, they will have our swords. Should they prevail, I beg they bring theirs to the north to aid us. And, when we are free, I shall expect their patronage.'

'I did not expect aid from the north, ${PLAYER}. It is humbling that you are willing to do so much for people you hardly know.
'Travelling caravans often look to make a little extra coin, and the Ordâkhai have coin to spare. I will admit, in the past, I have directed others to take work from Khârdu. He is fond of posting bounties for pelts or meat from the desert-dwelling beasts. You will find them on the pilings and pitons surrounding his encampment in the south-east. Collect one and return it to me so that I can validate the writing is in his hand.'

'Unmistakable, yes? He signed the document himself. He refuses to pass work like this to his subordinates. He is a very predictable man. Likely, that predictability is the precise reason for Jombahok's easy removal of Khârdu.
'I am pleased the rebellion has found a method to turn the men against one another. Now, we must all execute our parts. Take this letter to Nangar. He awaits you at his home.'

'Yes, yes, these will do nicely. A moment, please.'
Zidemel adds the blood to a crucible, mixes in an herb, and applies heat. He stirs briefly and then tilts the crucible, emptying its contents into an ink-well.
'Take this, ${PLAYER}. I have done my part. Now, please, leave me. I want to know no more of what is to come. I have a higher calling for which to prepare. You are to speak with Malgat now.'

Galamê studies the posting.
'I can match the writing, both in script and tone. However, I cannot match this papyrus. It is a finer craft than I have access to here in Jirush.
'Good fortune though, ${PLAYER}. North, in Ambarûl, there is a papyrus farmer named Sûlmur. The quality of her papyrus matches this posting. I expect the Ordâkhai captains purchased it from her.
'Go to her and collect a sheaf of papyrus and return it to me. I can then pen a response that will incite a battle between the northern and southern encampments.'

'Your assistance is welcome by all the elders now. Each prepares for the coming strife before our freedom.
'You have the ink, and you have the writing example. Take these to Galamê. He will write the letter to spark the fire to engulf our enemy and open the way to our freedom.'
Galamê hands you a letter in Ordâkhin

'We must foment the aggression these two Ordâkhai captains harbour toward one another. The response to Jombahok needs to be subtle and pointed. A slight so cutting that Jombahok commits too much to bringing down Khârdu.
'I would like you to discuss this with Nangar in Jirush. I think the best action is a 'personal' response from Khârdu. For this, however, we will need to enlist other members of Jirush.
'Go west along the road to Jirush and tell Nangar of our plan and gain his guidance.'

You share the details of your excursions for Amalíbi with Nangar. He ponders for a long moment.
'I believe our leader is correct. The response should be personal. A slight against Jombahok from Khârdu presented plainly and openly. It must be something that outs the former as a scoundrel to his men. The unrest within Jombahok's ranks ensures no choice but retaliation.
'Seek Zidemel's counsel on the best ink for an Ordâkhai curse. While you undertake the collection of whatever Zidemel requires, I will discuss with the other elders. Our time to unite and rise is nigh.'

'A curse, you say?
'A true curse? Or, a curse of words? These are very different. If you desire a curse of words, use scorpion blood. It is acrid. The blood burns papyrus rather than staining it like ink. When dry, it looks like caked blood. The meaning of letters written in such a manner is unmistakable - hatred.
'I know the method to distill the blood in this manner. I will need eight drams of their blood. The scorpions wander the arid lands north-west of Jirush or the crags of the buried quarry to the north-west.'
A Conspiracy Born
Galamê returns a letter to you written in Ordâkhin. He tells you it will incite violence between the two captains and asks that you deliver it to Nangar.
Nangar trusts the efforts of the other elders and appreciates your role in acquiring the letter. He puts his faith in you and the other elders and sends you to Amalíbi for the final decision.
Zidemel sent you to the quarry north-west of Jirush to collect drams of scorpion blood to distill and create ink to create a proper curse.

Malgat explained that Khârdu often pays travelling hunters bounties to clear beasts from the wastes of Khûd Zagin. He asks that you acquire a bounty posting and return it to him to validate Khârdu's handwriting.
You found a posting near the Ordâkhai encampment south and east from Jirush. You assume it is written by Khârdu. Return the bounty posting to Malgat for confirmation.
Malgat confirmed the posting was written by Khârdu. He then directed you to deliver the ink and posting to Nangar for further instruction.

Galamê states he can replicate Khârdu's writing. The papyrus he has, however, is not the same quality as Khârdu uses, and to make the curse authentic he needs papyrus from the farmer, Sûlmur in Ambarûl.

'While each of the elders does not directly support the rebellion, they do make efforts to assist the outpost and indirectly aid the cause. Please work with them, earn their favour and trust, and then return to me.'

'Your efforts ingratiate you to the elders. Forgive our further subterfuge. Our position is tenuous, and confrontation with the Ordâkhai will bring unease to the other elders. A few more measured moves, and I can assure the other elders of your intentions.'

'You have proven your ability to perceive one of our members. I am pleased by this. Now, however, I must ask you to assist our outpost in a manner which appeases the different elders and ingratiates you to each.
'Return to Nangar and ask him what you can do to aid the outpost of Jirush.'

'It is good to have another set of hands in these trying times.'
He offers a genuine smile.
'Do not worry. I shall not set you to tasks that directly confront our enemy, not yet.
'I think assisting the other elders to prove your value and intention will suffice.
'Igbâl is as stubborn as a sated camel. He will not speak with you. You will work through his intermediary Galamê. Malgat is a forthright man with honourable intent. His needs are varied, and though they seem selfish, they are not. Zidemel is an odd sort. He hears voices, as do his followers. Humour them. It should mean no harm to anyone to do so.
'Return to me when they are satisfied.'
'You have done well. Continue to prove yourself to Nangar. In time, you may yet be able to help us more directly. For now, friend, keep our contact to a minimum.'

'There are two in my care who suffer as they fade. Aítarshun can no longer wield a blade or move freely outside the oasis. The other, Filadal, can no longer leave the spot where she sits. Each looks to me to fulfil a wound or oath to be at peace before they fade.
'I have not the heart to tell them there is nothing I can do.
'I wonder, will you assist them?
'Aítarshun is found in the central island and Fildal can be found on the island closest to the shore.'

'I did not know the depth of pain that Filadal held or the depth of Aítarshun's oath. Your assistance gives me pause, friend.
'I believe there is something we can do for the men of Khûd Zagin.'

'Please introduce yourself and learn from Mashêm and Shulêga. They will assist in tracking and rewarding you for your contributions in cataloguing the history of Shagâna. Both are nearby in this small camp.'

'Your reputation, ${PLAYER}, speaks of a trustworthy and noble spirit. We hope you see the merit in our charge in this land. There are many secrets in these lands. There is history here in the Valley of Ikorbân, suppressed too long beneath a yoke of oppression and a veil of superstition. We seek only to understand the past of this land, our ancestors, and ensure that no harm comes to their memory due to the actions of the Sea-shadow.'

Kizeri, the leader of the Tale-wardens, asked you to visit and introduce yourself to the other members of her order, Mashêm and Shulêga. Each are located close to Kizeri in the shadow of Telperiën's Wall.

'Welcome to our encampment, ${PLAYER}.
'Do not be surprised. Captain Rothog told us to look forward to your arrival.'
She smiles genuinely.
'You made an impression on the Kindred of the Coin. An impression good enough that when Captain Rothog signed on to the expedition here, he asked that we, the Phetekâri of Umbar, join them to catalogue the journey.
'We could use assistance if you are willing. We are small in number and have discovered so much already, and we are only at Telperiën's Wall.
'Please speak to my companions, Mashêm, and Shulêga. They will provide more information.'

He nods.
'Very good. You will want to know why we are here.
'We Phetekâri are an ancient sect of scholars who hid away from the church of the All-seeing Eye. Only recently, with Captain Rothog's gracious involvement, have we emerged from our long secrecy.
'Our purpose is to collect and maintain remnants of the past for posterity and purposes of study and history. In your tongue, we are called Tale-wardens.
'We accompany this excursion to catalogue and collect the mysteries of the past to maintain for future generations. We will ask for permission to excise any materials we find of historical significance and will record the rest with as much accuracy as we can.
'For your part, should you help us, Captain Rothog supplied us with trinkets, clothing, and gifts he believes you may find interesting or beneficial.
'Make certain you speak with Shulêga, if you have not.'

'It is good you have come to me, ${PLAYER}. I overheard your conversation with Kizeri, and I am pleased to show you the wares that Captain Rothog sent with us to Ikorbân.
'Your assistance with collecting information, relics, and curiosities of the past allows me to offer you access to our small menagerie of treasures.
'We must be cautious not to upset or remove important Ikorbâni relics. We are observers and outsiders here. What little we know of the conflict in this land forces us to use great caution lest we make ourselves an enemy of the Ikorbâni. We are historians and cataloguers. Let us do right here, my friend.
'We will send word to you when your assistance warrants greater reward. After you speak with Mashêm, return to Kizeri.'
The Phetekâri, Tale-wardens
Return to Kizeri, the leader of the Tale-wardens, and tell her you have introduced yourself to her assistants at Telperiën's wall.

'We shall honour your efforts if you honour our place. The world grows darker and we only hope to bring more light before we can no longer see. We will not beg your assistance. We will reward your kindness with our own.
'We are the Adúrhid. In the common tongue, we are called the Oasis Elves or Kintai. A fitting name. Now you know us. Will you help us?'

Dagortas, an elder among the Kintai Elves asked you to introduce yourself to her assistants Thridarlan and Alidal. Each plays an important role in measuring and rewarding the value of those who aid the Kintai in the Valley of Ikorbân.
You spoke with Thridarlan and Alidal. You should return to the elder Elf, Dagortas. She will be pleased to know you met her assistants in Shonith.
Speak with the sage Thridarlan in Shonith
Speak with the quartermaster Alidal

'We have forgotten more songs than we remember, and soon we shall sing no more. We safe-guarded these lands for a reason long ago, but we cannot recall why or how.
'Our time ends, but we are not without hope. The natural order comes undone all around us, and it is all we can do to sustain what bastions remain.
'We plan for an unclear future; fully aware we will not be part of it. We ask you the impossible. We invite you to support us, though we cannot support you in kind.
'Thridarlan and Alidal will speak more about our requests, should you desire to help.'

'Dagortas carries the weight of many losses with her and is slow to believe there is good in the world. I believe there is still good and hope. Your willingness to speak with me shows me this is not untrue.
'Our numbers thin, this is true, but our duty remains. We seek harmony with the natural world and will work to maintain careful balance.
'Your aid in restoring and maintaining all things natural and pure will draw us closer and earn what gifts we can afford to provide.
'Please ensure you speak with Alidal.'

'Our gifts are not the usual bounty you find from Men. While trappings are necessary to survive in the wild, we tend to use our abilities to co-exist with our surroundings rather than destroy or harvest them for personal purposes or gain.
'We will share our knowledge and gifts with those worthiest of them.
'Ensure that you speak with Thridarlan.'

'You are welcome among us so long as you do not bring imbalance to the natural order. Speak with Thridarlan and Alidal to learn how you can aid us in our efforts to maintain our land, and how we can repay your efforts.'
The Adúrhid, the Kintai Elves
Dagortas, an elder among the Kintai Elves of the Ikorbân Valley welcomed you to Shonith and invited you to meet with her assistants in the dying oasis.
Speak with Dagâdah in the settlement of Iridír

'You have spoken with Kildûg and Nêkhur?'
You assert that you have.
'Then I offer a request and warning. If you are of noble heart, see to helping our people. If you mean us harm or prove ignoble in your efforts, prepare to suffer our wrath. For we are born anew and will fight any aggressors who mean to suppress our will again.'

Dagâdah, a leader of the Shagâna, known as the Ikorbâni by those from the north, directed you to entreat with his assistants Kildûg and Nêkhur. He also warned against doing anything to harm the people of the valley.
Speak with Kildûg, an Ikorbâni Tale-weaver
Speak with the Ikorbâni Quartermaster, Nêkhur

'Prove to us you are not here to steal our heritage, our land, or to further injure our people, and we will find a way to reward you.
'We do not have much wealth, but we have much need. All who would assist us are welcome. We are a proud and earnest people.
'If you assist us, we will not forget your effort or let your kindness go unnoticed.
'My assistants Kildûg and Nêkhur will explain more. Return to me when you learn from them.'

'As Dagâdah explained, we face many struggles here in Shagâna, the occupation by the Ordâkhai is chief among the challenges but only one small portion of our strife.
'The end of the war in the North and fracturing of the Ordâkhai forces in Shagâna provides strength. We choose freedom. We will reclaim our culture and all we lost under Ordâkhai rule. Nature revolted against them and poisoned the land. Our farms, the finest in Shagâna, fell to ruin while our healthy people marched to war.
'We recall the stories of our past, but the written word is lost. This is a sample of the difficulties we face. Prove yourself honest.'

'Dagâdah asked me to maintain our collected wealth and trade materials. I am pleased to do this work. I am overjoyed to furnish gifts to those who aid us in restoring our livelihood and culture.
'For too long, the Ordâkhai subjugated our people and put us beneath their heels. We struggle to recall our litanies, and the few who are literate face the arduous task of recovering our history and teaching our written word to future generations.
'It falls to that generation to learn our history, to trust in the nobility of outsiders, and to restore what is lost. If you are such a person, it will bring me joy to gift you a piece of what we still control and make.'
'Kildûg is good with faces, names, and our history. He will remember all you do and weave tales about you. Nêkhur watches over our wealth and will see you rewarded for assisting us.'
The Ikorbâni, the People of Shagâna

'${PLAYER}! Find my mother somewhere to the north and learn from her one of the great tales of Old Shagâna! To hear those names recounted will inspire the Dumûri to greater heights of combat prowess when they need it most!'

'We will not know defeat! We must triumph or the lands that lie behind us will suffer terrible torments at the hands of these vile creatures!
'Rahâzi is right in this, ${PLAYER}: our people should be reminded of the great heroes that came before us! Sing a song of the great hero Shurug-nîn to the fighting Dumûri and they will fight more fiercely than ever before!
'The melody is not as important as the words themselves! Sing of Shurug-nîn as she fought the great dragon Akhízi, the Winged Terror! 'Find my mother Girhâzi to the north and learn from her one of the great tales of Old Shagâna! To hear those names recounted will inspire the Dumûri to greater heights of combat prowess when they need it most!'

'Our people should be reminded of the great heroes that came before us! Sing a song of the great hero Shurug-nîn to the fighting Dumûri and they will fight more fiercely than ever before!
'The melody is not as important as the words themselves! Sing of Shurug-nîn as she fought the great dragon Akhízi, the Winged Terror! Sing of Shurug-nîn's powerful allies among Elves, both the ancient Kintai of the Emerald Wood and the more distant Elves who gifted her the mighty sword Orotheg! 'I have a personal matter with which I would ask your assistance, ${PLAYER}.
'I have received word from my spies of a rumour that my husband, Eshtali, has recently been seen outside the Crypts of Esh-kimâkhi to the south of here. What he is doing there, I have no idea.
'The leader of the Barkhûshim, that accursed Okhíso, claimed to take him when he drove us all from Kûr Anzar. I thought my precious Eshtali long since dead. I know it is dangerous, ${PLAYER}, but I feel a dagger of hope in my chest.
'You have accomplished much with me here. There is no one I trust more with this mission than you. Please, make your way to Esh-kimâkhi and look for him. You will know him by the crimson robes he always wears. And, ${PLAYER}? If you are to return with my husband, know that you will have given me a gift worth more to me than any victory in this war.'

'Thank you for that news. I had feared this day would come. I had hoped you would return with fairer news, but I appreciate your candor.
'Hope is a cruel master, and one that has now abandoned me.
'When I was a girl, my sisters and I would make shapes, shadows on the wall. We would make funny animals: ducks, and rabbits, and chickens. Oh, and the stories we would tell! The adventures those rabbits and ducks had! Such stories. My sisters have since passed, taken each by disease or famine or war. Sometimes I still see those shadows though; dancing, laughing, playing. I can still hear their laughter.
'When my husband would come home, I would first see him by the shadow he cast on the wall by our home. So broad and powerful, that shadow was the harbinger of my precious Eshtali coming home to me. Just like my sisters, I sought comfort in that shadow, always steady, strangely solid.
'After he was taken, I am ashamed to say I forgot what his face looked like, once so familiar to me. All I can see now of him is that shadow on the wall, insubstantial like a wraith, endlessly dancing through my memories.'

'Have you delivered the message to my father yet? Please, make haste. He almost never leaves his home in Jirush. You will find him there.'

'As I said before, my father's beliefs are profound.'
She manages a smile.
'Raphûz recounted the tale. It was a good story. I fought against the demon and nearly won. You both arrived to find the Alad gravely wounded, rending my body to restore itself. Together, you levied blows against it until it stirred no more.

'She understood the subtext of my concern without exposition. We are very much alike and also very different.'

'Do not lecture me on the little cruelty this does to the man. It is no worse than caging a bird meant to fly free. One may cause a short period of sorrow, the other a lifetime.

Raphûz listens to you recount the tales told by the Shagâni.
'The stories I learned are much the same.
'I think I understand.
'The tale is to soften the blow of loss. Though several people I spoke with warned that the Aladi are real.
'The Shagâni prize bravery and strength. They enjoy shared responsibility and family, and the Shagâni way is to provide for each other.
'It is strange to me. A people who suffered so long in oppression are still profoundly proud and hopeful.
'They have amazing fortitude.'

'When a man pursues me, I prefer he brings me the flowers of the floodplain. The blossoms are beautiful and easily tended.
'Oh, and the tale of a person returning as a beast is meant to scare children into obeying their parents, nothing more.'

You enquire about Shagâni customs and beliefs.
'A man and woman must work together to provide for their family. Without cooperation, there can be no success. Mutual respect is our way, a shared unity of purpose and direction.
'Anyone who tells you otherwise is without a partner.'

You enquire about Shagâni customs and beliefs.
'The story of the beasts and the Aladi is a well-known tale. Our elders use it to hide painful truths about death.
'I understand the reasons. Elders must protect the flocks from the horrors that would plague the young. Until now, the Shagâni had little hope beyond servitude and death.
'We will need to alter our customs to encourage the future generations toward hope, not fear.'

You enquire about Shagâni customs and beliefs.
'My mother told a similar story to me when my father did not return from a battle.
'She said he met an Aladi who traded our lives for his. She explained that he became a beast of the wild so that we may prosper.'
He chuckles.
'We did not prosper, but we lived. Until I had children, I did not understand the importance of protecting them from the harsh truth of the world.'

You enquire about Shagâni customs and beliefs.
'I care not for stories. I care for feeding my family, sheltering my family, protecting my family.
'I faced my fears without regard for consequence to win the hand of my love. I did not overcome the fear, but I found strength where I thought of her.'

'I want to know more about the Shagâni culture. Could you speak with members of this encampment and learn what you can while I do the same? Together, perhaps we can learn what the woman meant about the deer.'

'I only joined them recently and have committed no crimes! I was in the army but the rations are shrinking and our pay comes late, if it comes at all, these past few months. 'It is good to see Andur has returned unharmed. I could use his help with many odd jobs and errands, and I will gladly employ him for as long as he would like to stay. Not to say that you were not good help, ${PLAYER}, but I imagine that you will soon be moving on.'

'You have collected the stones? Thank you ${PLAYER}, we will be able to leave that much sooner now. She is almost better and will be fit to walk before long. Thank you once again for your help, ${PLAYER}. I will take the stones and will be off to Western Khanâg shortly.'

'Did you only just get here, ${PLAYER}? It seems that I caught up to you very quickly!
'I give you my gratitude again for taking a chance and trusting me. Most people would have slain me where I stood in the desert. You have given me a second chance at life, and I will not squander it. Thank you, my friend.'

'Welcome back, ${PLAYER}, did you find Andur?'
You fill her in on recent events, secretly still not entirely sure if Andur can be trusted to not steal the stones and the donkey.
'Oh, speaking of, there he is now!'

'${PLAYER}, what are you doing here? No matter, I could use your help. The donkey got stung by an usan-kûni, and I have been tending to the animal. The poor thing is in much pain, but I must try and keep her still to prevent the venom from spreading from her leg to other parts of her body. I think she will be fine, we only need a little more time to rest.
'I have not yet been able to collect any of the coloured stones for which Tibira sent us seeking. Since you are here, would you mind doing that while I keep the donkey calm? That way when she is ready to move on, we can head back to Western Khanâg immediately.'
Collected colourful stones from the loose gravel (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Andur found!
Andur is supposed to be in the hills east of Western Khanâg. You should go there and look for him.

'${PLAYER}, I had hired a man named Andur, who said he was your friend, to collect gemstone pebbles. I gave him a donkey and some supplies and sent him to an area east of here, where I know the colourful stones can be scooped up from the gravel.
'He has not yet returned, and I worry that he perhaps got lost or ran afoul of some beast in the desert. Would you mind looking to see what became of him?'
Though you want to think the best of Andur, you can't help but wonder if the man perhaps took Tibira's donkey, never to return.

'Ah yes, ${PLAYER}, there is a good amount of useable metal here. Thank you!'
Collected time-worn swords (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
You have gone to Shukabad and collected the time-worn swords there. You should bring them to Sigênik in Western Khanâg.

'Hashtal-gûr, traveller. You look like the sort who can handle themselves. I can see in your eyes that danger is not unknown to you. Tell me, would you help a humble craftsman?
'In a land as unforgiving as the Khûd, nothing should go to waste if it can be helped. Over the ages, many soldiers have come to the Khûd, only to meet their end here. One would not have to look too hard to find their gear lost to time in the desert. For example, at the ruins of Shukabad, I have heard there are swords to be found, just lying about on the ground. Scavengers do not bother with them because they are rusted and unusable. They are still made of fine metals, however, and a skilled craftsman would be able to melt them down and reuse the metal.
'It is easier to pick up these scraps than it is to mine new ores. If you are good in a fight anyway, as many of these metals are in dangerous areas. Should you be willing to face the dangers, go to Shukabad, west of here, collect any time-worn swords you find there, and bring them to me.'
Restoring Arms
Sigênik has asked you to travel to Shukabad, west of Western Khanâg, and collect time-worn swords there.

'You. You will help me, yes? Jackals roam these lands unchecked, free to go wherever they wish and to eat whoever they want.'
You ask her how you can help. Her wet, bloodshot eyes lock onto yours.

A Hard Day's Work

'My thanks to you. It's been fair too long since we had fresh blades. These will cut the Barkhûshim quite well, and any others who draw Mizâdi's ire. Give my regards, and that of the Subuzûri, to Nukûsh.'

'There you are. Well you've gathered plenty of both at least. Leave them there, I'll take care of the ore. Add the wood to the fire, it's getting low. Then you can bring these swords to Numûru. Hope you don't mind sweating, there's no loafing here.'

'The fires are hot and there's work to be done! My apprentice ran off, off to join Mizâdi's band, he did. I don't mind a good war, but not when it hurts the forge. How am I supposed to make blades for Mizâdi when there's no one to help gather ore for the swords and collect wood for the fires?
'You want to help? Well there may be some good left in this world after all. You can start by gathering some wood and ore, we have plenty of both outside of Urmâkh, to the east. Watch out for the jackals, they've been roaming closer and closer to the city proper.'

'Ah, that's enough to get me ahead for once. You move quick. You remind me of myself at a young age. Nice enough for you to help an old man with his tasks. I appreciate it. Anytime you want to come back, there's a spot at the forge for you.'

'If you are willing to search for the swords, perhaps you would be willing to go to Sûr Zugub as well? It is the home of sand-sifters; nasty things. I have never been there myself, but it is said that an entire Ordâkhai troop was lost there. Travellers claim to have seen the metal of their shields glinting in the sun, but none have dared enter the valley, lest they meet the same fate as the soldiers.
'If you can handle the sand-sifters, collecting those shields should recover quite a bit of metal I can work with. And speaking honestly, the more of those sand-sifters you can slay while you're there, the better. Sûr Zugub is to the south-east of here.'

Look near Jirush, to the south-east of Western Khanâg, for the missing goatherd.
Zidek's partner, Ubdun, is out herding goats but should have returned by now. The butcher has asked you to ensure the goatherd is all right and thinks he may have gone in the direction of Jirush.

Talk to Ubdun
Talk to Zidek
Give food to the hungry dog

You can see that the expression in Zidek's eyes has softened since he watched you interact with the hungry stray dog.
'You know, now that I think about it, it is possible I can spare some meat for the beast. If he works for it, that is. It seems that Ubdun could use a companion and protector while herding the goats, and this fellow looks like he needs a companion in addition to something to eat.
'Here, take that steak on the table and see if the dog will follow you to Ubdun.'

'What a wonderful idea! Zidek is so kind and smart. This is the perfect solution. No brigand dare attack me now! It will be good to have both a protector and a new friend. Thank you once again ${PLAYER}, for everything you have done. For all of us.'

The dog is whining, staring at the meat Zidek has for sale.
'Off with you, you pest!'
Zidek looks about, presumably for something to throw at the dog.

'That accursed beast has been coming around a lot lately. I have no meat to spare on a beggar, much less a beggar that is a mangy cur.'
You look at the dog who has soft, sad eyes, and he doesn't look like a mangy cur to you. You ask the butcher if you can buy some meat for the dog.
'Well.. as long as it is paid for.'
You pay him and he reluctantly gives you some meat.
You hold the meat out to the dog, and he takes it from you, careful not to bite your hand. He wags his tail and continues to lick your hand long after the food is gone.
The dog followed you!
Zidek tried sending the hungry dog away, but you took pity upon the animal and bought some meat for the dog. You should give it to him.
Needs Fulfilled

You have given meat you bought from Zidek to the hungry stray and can see that he is a gentle and intelligent dog. Afterward, you gave the good dog some pats that did not go unappreciated. You should talk to Zidek.

Zidek said he would feed the dog if he serves as the protector and companion of Ubdun the goatherd. He has pointed to a large, juicy steak on the table, and asked you to take it and see if the dog will follow you to Ubdun.
The dog has followed you, or rather the steak, to Ubdun's location, near Jirush. You should talk to Ubdun.
Zidek is trying to send the hungry dog away. You should talk to Zidek.
You have given meat you bought from Zidek to the hungry stray and can see that he is a gentle and intelligent dog. You should give him some pats.

'Thank you for all of your help, ${PLAYER}. It will be exciting to see if the traveller spoke true, and the soil from a dry river-bed is indeed better for gardens.'
'You have the soil! Wonderful! I will take it and put it in the planter with my seeds while you get water from the well.'

'Hashtal-gûr, may I ask you a favour?
'Another traveller told me once that the soil from a dried river-bed is very good for growing fruits and vegetables. I have this large planter and would like to try it, but I am not brave enough to go to the Usâl. Would you be willing to go to the old river-bed and collect some soil for me? Four of these sacks should do.'

'Those usan-kûni are quite large! I am glad to have both you and Girhâzi here with me. Let us move quickly though. This does not seem like a place where we should dally.

'Are we almost there ${PLAYER}? Amâsu wishes to travel quickly, but I believe we should slow down. She will not tell us if the journey is difficult for her. If we are close, I believe we should walk the rest of the way, for her sake.'
You assure Girhâzi that it is just ahead.

'This is very exciting, ${PLAYER}. I have not been on an adventure in many years! You should have seen me in my younger days. I was quite rough and tumble!
'Lead on, my dear. Do watch your step though, it seems there are a few usan-kûni in here.'
'You are quite right that this wall does not look like the others in this mine. Do you truly think it may be a door, though? What do you suppose may open it? This a puzzle indeed!'

'Níkhu, ${PLAYER}, we found it! I am stunned. I confess there was a part of me that believed it would never be found in my lifetime, and yet, here we are. This is a beautiful treasure trove of knowledge. The culture and history of Ambarûl has been preserved for us in this room. This will restore our sense of identity and help us to rebuild, to uphold our independence. Thank you, ${PLAYER}, you have done our people a great service, and we will never forget it.
'I will place guards here to ensure the safety of Dubarâkh, and you are always welcome to return here, should you desire it.'

We are only recently freed of Sauron, the All-seeing, and must not allow this new cult to take hold. The Anâkhi scorpion worshippers must be driven from our lands.
Raphûz wants to sit with you and discuss over a smoke and food about all that has transpired since his arrival in the Ikorbân Valley.

Speak with Raphûz at his post in Wrackwade

'In my excitement over the news of the revenge wrought in my father's name, I forgot to tell you I was reassigned to an outpost south-east of Iridír along the dry river near the Crossing of Sílabal, also called the Wrackwade. I will leave as soon as I am prepared.
'Should you find yourself in the encampment there, visit me. I will treat you to a meal and a smoke.'
'Let us enjoy the night while we can. Tomorrow will take me further into these lands, and who is to know my fate.'

'Did you see? She is as beautiful and free as she appeared from a distance. She thanked us for caring for and nursing her fawn back to health. My friend, I confess I am at a loss for words. She said 'Khûd Zagin, the land to the south.' I must consult with the people of this camp and learn their ways.
'I would very much like to speak with her again.'

'We will find him yet. I can see another hollow on the rise above. Let us move swiftly.'

'No, no friend. My resolve is stalwart. I only wonder which trail to follow to discover the beast.'
He looks at the paths and then chooses.
'Let us search there, friend.'

'Is this beast another Shagâni myth?'
He smirks.
'Come, I think there is another hollow above where the beast must be.'

'My friend, I could not have succeeded without you. I still will not stray so near to a boar that it could gore me without holding a weapon.
'But my fear of the creatures is diminished thanks to you.
'Please visit me in the Wrackwade, where I can thank you more formally.'

It Is the Wood That Cracks

'The wood has broken and so, hopefully, has the spirit of the southern Men. It is a severe lesson, but one the Ordakhai must learn, sooner or later. My thanks for your efforts, ${PLAYER}. You are like the wind, guiding the natural way of things.'

Return to Artar Ildarthos at Vartúlin

'We Kintai have a saying, outsider. \qWhen the tree resists the wind, it is the wood that cracks, never the wind.\q We all must be in balance with nature, never resisting its flow. These southern Men - these Men of Ordâkh - they are always out of balance, destroying the natural way of things. They have built great fortifications at Ghât Lor, further destroying our forests and sometimes even using the husks of our sacred Veróthi to protect themselves.
'Break their fortifications, destroy this blasphemy against nature and the Kintai. It will weaken them, and may make them think twice before they again twist nature to their corrupted will. We Kintai know that when the tree resists the wind, it is the wood that cracks. It is past time these Men of Ordâkh learn the same.'

'There it is my friend, the beast they call Urkhêru. It is as Ashâmi says, patience in all things.
'Let us make this a merciful and quick kill. I wish to return to Urmâkh and check on Ashâmi.'

'The beast is not here, my friend. It is proving very elusive.'
He smiles genuinely.
'I have something to confess, ${PLAYER}. On the road from Shonith to Urkmâkh Ashâmi, in a quiet moment, shared a kiss.'
He blushes.
'It was... amazing. In the quiet moments, even now as we hunt, I find my thoughts drifting to her. I only hope she feels for me as I feel for her.'
He shakes his head.
'Enough talk like this. Let us continue.'

'Not here. No matter, we will find the beast.'
He looks at you and smiles.
'We have come far, you and I. To think, it was only a short while ago I feared these creatures so much. With your assistance I learned there is little to fear.
'Ashâmi finds my stories of travelling with you amusing. She is a marvellous woman.'
He stares off for a moment.
'Come, friend. We have a pressing matter at hand.'

'Another battle and story to enter into my journal. I never imagined my life to be filled with such adventure and challenges. I feel pride, my friend.
'Perhaps my first steps into the valley were for my parents and their legacy. Now, however, every step I take is my own. I have you, your advice, your assistance, and I daresay your companionship to thank.'
He chuckles.
'Come, let us return to Ashâmi.'

'My friend, I am beginning to think this large boar Numûru speaks of is another Shagâni myth.
'Were Ashâmi here, she would tell me, 'Raphûz you must exercise patience and understand the mysteries of Shagâna reveal themselves when they are prepared, not you.''
He grins.
'She is a very wise woman. We should continue, so I can get back to her.'

'My fear of these beasts is much diminished. I have you to thank for this my friend. Let us make haste. I want to return to Ashâmi as quickly as we can.'

Speak with Ashâmi

'We are not the hunters here, ${PLAYER}. This serval is cunning beyond normal measure. We must be cautious.
'We will not become prey.'

She scans the woods and speaks softly.
'I kissed him. It was spontaneous, something I never expected do.
'I have not often allowed anyone to get close to me.
'My mother's disposition, love of life, and attitude of defiance in the face of great oppression shaped me. I am who am I because of her. Her marriage to my father was arranged. I never understood how she came to care for him.
'But, Raphûz,-'
She stops, alerted to a sound.
'What was that?'

'Thank you, ${PLAYER}.
'You're a capable warrior. Raphûz is a good judge of character.'
She manages a smile.
'I confess, while we were fighting just now, I was thinking of how I must survive so I can return to him. It is a strange feeling to me. One with which I am not entirely comfortable.
'I am glad we had time to travel together. I understand why he sees you as such a trusted companion. Let us return to Urmâkh.'
Ashâmi looks eager to speak after surviving the ambush
You survived the attack by Kanagir
There is still no sign of Kanagir
Ashâmi appears a bit shaken as she looks over the woods. You, too, have an uneasy feeling in these woods.
There has been no sign of the serval Numûru described to Ashâmi. The woods are eerily still and quiet.
Speak with Ashâmi to begin the hunt

'${PLAYER}, Raphûz speaks highly of your skill and how you helped him along his path to find me and his fate. I have seen how capable you are when you helped me with the Alad.
'Still, something here makes me uneasy. Do you feel it too?'
She breathes in deeply and sighs.
'Perhaps I should be more eager, like Raphûz. Come, let us hunt this creature.'

'Something is not right. Can you feel it?'
She looks around, listening intently and peering into the woods.
'If Raphûz were here, he would say, 'Is this another Shagâni superstition?''
She chuckles softly.
'I find his questions very amusing. He does not understand how much our superstitions kept us safe in the darkest of times. Our lives coming together as they have does seem to be something different.
'I never expected -'
She stops and points.
'Look, there. Let's go.'

'What use could we have for a Wizard? Folk such as that bring only trouble.'

'I have heard the arrival of a Wizard heralds the onset of good fortune! Wherever he walks, golden coins are said to fall from his pockets, and these are free for the taking by any who chance upon him!
'I have kept my eyes peeled for him, but my wife also expects me to make my purchases at the market and return to her. How am I to shop while there could be a Wizard and his golden coins so near, with me blind to his presence?'
'Have you seen him? Has a Wizard come to Umbar Baharbêl?'

'Ah, there you are, my friend. I wondered if you would come to see me here.
'I have overheard one or two fanciful beliefs about me and my Order while I rested here. I shall not test your patience by repeating them.'
You ask the Wizard where he keeps all of his golden coins, and he chuckles to himself.
'I see that you have heard some of them. Did you hear too that I apparently possess the ability to take on forms enough to put Beorn himself to shame? Alas, it is not so. Still, the Umbari were so eager to see this impressive figure they have imagined that they paid me little mind, and I entered the city with little fanfare. I have been quite untroubled today... or perhaps I should say I have not been disturbed by the Umbari. The threat posed by the Thardúth and their Utûgi warriors fills me with unease.'
They notice you listening to their talk and quickly fall silent

'Can it be so? Has the day come at last?'
Jaith looks about furtively before continuing with a hushed, eager tone.
'Rumours abound that the Wizard Inkanûsh now approaches the city! We guardsmen of Umbar Baharbêl trade not in gossip... but Kinsman Belondor's soldiers returned from Ikorbân with news of him, and they say he will perform feats of magic for any who ask him! These are dangerous times, ${PLAYER}, as you well know, and the Kindred of the Coins might have need of such feats if they are to keep their people safe.
'Will you go to the Waterway Market to the south-east and see if anyone has yet seen the Wizard Inkanûsh? The rumourmonger Tasâdi often holds court there at this time of day, and if anyone has heard anything about the Wizard, it will be she!'

'Rumours are like water, my friend. If you have the ability to keep it contained, you can control who receives it, and its value only increases. But once it is spilled, there is no returning it to the container!
'Whispers about the approaching Wizard have already spread throughout the market, and few are interested in what I have to say about him, for they can hear these tidings everywhere! My trade is in news and information... what now can I do?
'Alas for Tasâdi, once the most accomplished rumourmonger in all of Umbar Baharbêl! She is finished. Fine, then! Go to the south and <rgb=#00FF00>listen</rgb> to the whispers of my former customers. They know all that I have heard, and more beside!'

'Will you go to the Waterway Market to the south-east and see if anyone has yet seen the Wizard Inkanûsh? The rumourmonger Tasâdi often holds court there at this time of day, and if anyone has heard anything about the Wizard, it will be she!'

'This talk is getting out of hand, if you ask me. What use could we have for a Wizard? Folk such as that bring only trouble. 'It is good to see you again, ${PLAYER}! My mother Girhâzi asked that I join Shâra Mizâdi's forces to oppose the Empire of Ordâkh and keep safe my homeland of Ambarûl, and so I have done. Already there has been fighting! The Battle for Hamât ended in victory, of a sort, but the villain Bârshud escaped with his life.
'Shâra Mizâdi gifted me the blade of one of her Subuzûri, and I will wield it on her behalf for the good of Renewed Hamât, and for the protection of Ambarûl and Iridír!
'But we should not delay. The council may have already started!'

'You and your companions are of course welcome to accompany my forces as we move south in pursuit of Bârshud and his Ordâkhai! You have proven yourself a mighty ally already, ${PLAYER}, and have lent me aid and support beyond my most hopeful expectations.
'I know little of Wizards, but if your friend has powers to lend to my cause, I invite him to use them openly and as he will!
'Renewed Hamât welcomes you and your companions. My army will march south from the Ikorbân Valley and into Mûr Ghala, the Ridge of Plenty. We will put an end to Bârshud and prevent the Ordâkhai from ever again threatening our lands.'

'It is fortunate that his wisdom aligns with mine, or I would disregard his opinion on the subject. But it is not seemly to leave foreign dignitaries on the doorstep.
'Shâra Mizâdi and her assemblage will enjoy the comforts of the Citadel of Winds while I summon the rest of the Kindred of the Coins. I invite both you and your Wizard to attend our council as well, ${PLAYER}. These matters affect us all.'

'I know what your Wizard seeks, ${PLAYER}. He believes these ancient creatures, these Thardúth, remain a danger to us. I have heard the report of Kinsman Belondor's soldiers about the fighting at Utug-bûr, and to me it sounds like madness: the ravings of frightened men caught in the middle of a battle they cannot understand. Azagath perished at the hands of the Thardúth, and will not emerge from the darkness of Utug-bûr, but so too did those terrible creatures... is it not so? Who is it that remains to endanger us?
'Ordâkh remains, ${PLAYER}. This has always been the true threat, not the ancient demons from which your Wizard would have us cower. This is why Umbar will support Mizâdi's pursuit of her foe south across the Ikorbân and into Mûr Ghala. We are allies in this, for Ordâkh threatens us all.'

'This is not the first time I have come to Shagâna or to Umbar Baharbêl. When my purpose brought me to these lands, years ago, it was not as Mithrandir. Nor did I wear the name Gandalf when I crossed the Ikorbân River in search of answers among the great cities of the south. I was called \qInkanûsh\q by the people who dwelled in these lands, and let it be so again while we here remain. I have been a friend to all the Free Peoples of the North, but the names they gave to me ring harshly against Shagâni ears.'
Inkanûsh puffs on his pipe before continuing, but as he begins to speak again something draws his attention.
'There is a commotion at the gate, ${PLAYER}. If you are agreeable, we will together see what has happened to disturb the peace. Perhaps they have found someone that better fits their expectation of a Wizard?'
'Let us see what has caused this commotion at the gate, and if we might be of some service in ending it.'

'Hármelak is wrong. Ordâkh is not powerless, it is true, but the gravest danger facing these lands, and indeed all lands in Middle-earth, belongs to the Thardúth! How can this Umbari woman believe that Utug-bûr might be the only dwelling the Thardúth ever fashioned in all of Shagâna's vast reaches?
'Before I came to the city I dispatched some of our friends to travel north into Harondor. Legolas, Gimli, and the sons of Elrond will ensure the Thardúth and their Utûgi warriors did not go that way to endanger Gondor. If they discover such a threat they will send word to me.
'But our road lies to the south, ${PLAYER}.'
Chapter 14.2: The Wizard, the Queen, and the Kindred
