'As you search for sign of these invaders outside Vartúlin, I will tell Thórvilon what we know of the Utûgi and their Thardúth masters. Be careful. The Utûgi must be driven by some evil purpose if they dare approach the groves of the Kintai.'

'As you search for sign of these invaders outside Vartúlin, I will tell Thórvilon what we know of the Utûgi and their Thardúth masters. Be careful. The Utûgi must be driven by some evil purpose if they dare approach the groves of the Kintai.'

'So it is true: the Utûgi leave the lands in which they awoke and begin to threaten others nearby. Our mission grows more serious.
'But we cannot leave Imhûlar just yet. While you were gone, Thórvilon spoke to me of a woman about whom I must learn more. He says she is named Cúridwan, and she has been a friend to the Kintai for as long as he can remember.'
Inkanûsh looks at you closely, one of his eyebrows raised.
'Thórvilon is one of the Kinta Elves, ${PLAYER}, and his memory is long. How can it be that this woman has lived in this place for such a span? This mystery and others have prompted me to ask a number of questions I have not before thought to ask.
'I must speak with this woman. I must speak with Cúridwan.'

'I am almost... home. I have dreamt of living here once again in peace, but...
'For how long can I remain at Urmâkh, knowing that Shâra Mizâdi faces our enemies in distant lands? Her own husband Eshtali perished in recent days, and still she fights.
'But I know not if I am as strong as she.'
'I know not if I am strong enough to continue this fight.'

'It is always the same, ${PLAYER}. In this place I see young soldiers of old wars, fighting and dying in battles they did not cause and whose roots they cannot see. They fight against Ordâkh as I fought against Mordor, and they fight for Mizâdi as I fought for Gil-galad the High King. Do they think this will be the last battle they need fight, as I believed then? Did I call them young soldiers? Perhaps I am one of them after all, despite my years!
'I understand Mizâdi and her army will travel the longer way through Khûd Zagin into Mûr Ghala, avoiding the dangerous forest road, but Inkanûsh wishes otherwise. He would have us speak first with Thórvilon, the Kinta warden of the grove of Vartúlin. It is the Wizard's plan to take the forest road through what remains of the Emerald Wood, ensuring that the Utûgi did not go that way unseen.
'It seems a good idea to me. The creatures we fought at the Dagor Carlanthir were fearsome, and I do not want them to prey upon the Kintai. Our kindreds are long divided, but they remain Elves, and dear to me even from such distance.'
'I will follow Shâra Mizâdi even to death.'

'What brings you back to Vartúlin, ${PLAYER}?'
You tell Thórvilon that you have come with the Elf-lord Glorfindel and the Wizard Inkanûsh to secure the safety of the Emerald Wood on your journey to oppose the Empire of Ordâkh. The warden of the grove strokes his chin.
'My folk have noticed strange Orc-like creatures moving among the trees outside Vartúlin. We believed them to be Orcs at first, but these were dressed strangely and seemed a larger breed than the Orcs we have encountered before.'

'Inkanûsh wishes for us to speak first with Thórvilon, the Kinta warden of the grove of Vartúlin. It is the Wizard's plan to take the forest road through what remains of the Emerald Wood, ensuring that the Utûgi did not go that way unseen.
'It seems a good idea to me. The creatures we fought at the Dagor Carlanthir were fearsome, and I do not want them to prey upon the Kintai. Our kindreds are long divided, but they remain Elves, and dear to me even from such distance.'

'These creatures of Orc-kind of which Thórvilon speaks are almost certainly Utûgi, ${PLAYER}. If you will go search for sign of these invaders outside Vartúlin, I will tell him what we know of them and their Thardúth masters.
'Be careful. The Utûgi must be driven by some evil purpose if they dare approach the groves of the Kintai.'

'My folk have noticed strange Orc-like creatures moving among the trees outside Vartúlin. We believed them to be Orcs at first, but these were dressed strangely and seemed a larger breed than the Orcs we have encountered before.'

'Mizâdi intended to return to Urmâkh to regroup with her own soldiers before travelling south. Speak with her when you arrive, and give her my thanks. Her ambitions, and the army she commands to accomplish them, will be of great service to us if I am right and the Thardúth lurk within Mûr Ghala.'

'We will not travel alone, ${PLAYER}! Glorfindel has agreed to accompany us on our southward journey, and he waits for us at the town of Urmâkh, in Imhûlar. Once we have reunited with him, I suggest we meet with the Kintai at the grove of Vartúlin. Our road must pass deeper into what was once the Emerald Wood, but now that forest is changed and the Kintai will guide us safely within.
'Mizâdi intended to return to Urmâkh to regroup with her own soldiers before travelling south. Speak with her when you arrive, and give her my thanks. Her ambitions, and the army she commands to accomplish them, will be of great service to us if I am right and the Thardúth lurk within Mûr Ghala.'

'I am pleased to have your aid and support, friend, and that of the Wizard Inkanûsh! We reclaimed Kûr Anzar, but it was not enough. Even possessing the Crown of Renewed Hamât is not enough, for Bârshud remains alive to threaten my young kingdom and its people. We will only be safe when Bârshud has been slain and the Empire of Ordâkh knows the courage in our hearts and the strength of our sword-arms.
'Even now my soldiers heed this call. Stand by the gate and <rgb=#00FF00>look</rgb> for the warriors that come from Kûr Anzar to join me on the southward road into danger.'
'Even now my soldiers heed this call. Stand by the gate and <rgb=#00FF00>look</rgb> for the warriors that come from Kûr Anzar to join me on the southward road into danger.'

'Give me a moment to rest, if you would. I am not so young in years that I feel not the road, nor the fighting I faced before it.
'Shâra Mizâdi wrested my home of Kûr Anzar from the Barkhûshim and Ordâkhai that held the city, and for that she will have my gratitude and my loyalty. Aye, unto death! Many others of my neighbours and my friends feel the same. We knew not that we might be Hamâti once again, but the coming of the Shâra wakened us to this truth: history is an unbroken chain that links the past to the present, even as it lies forgotten in the dust, or trampled underfoot.'

'I cannot say for certain, but when last we spoke Cúridwan had crafted a salve that could help fight against the Lâg Dávrit, the blight tainting the woods hereabout. She expressed a desire to bring it not only to the grove here in Imhûlar, but also to those further east, in Adagím. \qI must do this, Usakâr,\q she said to me. \qWhat is the hurry?\q I responded, but there must have been some need for haste after all.
'She has always been a friend to the Kintai, and if she possesses a means of curing their dying forest, she would share it without question. She has a big heart, our Cúridwan. Often she speaks of her purpose in these lands: to heal them, and to fortify them against evil.
'She would not appreciate these Orcs in her home, I know that! She must have gone already to Adagím, and missed their arrival entirely!'

'It is true. That was my favourite hat, but Luhum-gêna kept stealing it right off my head. Not only that, but no matter how often I think she is slain, Luhum-gêna somehow keeps coming back. Eventually I decided to just let her keep it.'

'There are Orcs on the slope above us. I think they remain unaware of our presence, which grants to us the advantage. Shall we put an end to their menace?'

'I fear some of the Orcs may have already passed into Kûgrun. Even now the life of Cúridwan may be in jeopardy!
'Glorfindel and I will ensure it is safe out here, and we will join you within when we can. Go now, and hurry!'

'You are not an Orc, are you? No, you are not. That is a relief to me! It must be a relief to you as well, yes?
'If you are here to dine with Cúridwan, as I am, I must tell you that she is no longer here. Luhum-gêna was quite disappointed to learn of our friend's absence, as was I, but perhaps it is just as well. Neither of us expected the Orcs to find the hidden way into Kûgrun! Someone with more in the way of brains must have helped them find it, but they are not welcome.'

'The people called for me to join the Ghad Imghêda; as harbour-warden I could not refuse. I sought not to elevate my position, but with so many of the Heirsworn gone from the city, it would seem my days must be less eventful. This will fill them up.
'To the Umbari who called for me to join this august body, I made this pledge: to remain vigilant, not only of our enemies but also of our friends, and our chosen leaders. It appears to this old sailor that much of the trouble began when Tumúldo sailed to Gondor, and that done at Azagath's command. The old Kindred should have sniffed out the Sea-shadow's evil before he could use it to deprive the city of such a hero as Tumúldo, who might have opposed him.
'Others might be deceived, but not I, and not now the Ghad Imghêda!'

'The Temámir and the Umbari people must work together, and not at cross-purposes. For that reason, I was chosen to join the Ghad Imghêda.
'I feel I must apologize for the actions taken by Khôltekh during the past few weeks, ${PLAYER}. I have explained to the Umbari and to my own people that I consider it a failing of my own that I did not determine his true allegiances in time to prevent the tragedies that befell the city. I need not tell you that he acted alone and for his own interests, and it was not with the authority of the Shoreward Stone that he fell in with Ordâkh or with the Orcs of Mordor that were seen upon one of the vessels as it passed the city. I am grateful for the assemblage of Temámir who came to Thargushakâl and informed me of his treachery during the early hours of the uprising. They will be rewarded!
'The actions of Khôltekh shame his people. The Umbari can rest more easily now that I have joined the Ghad Imghêda.'
'One mystery remains to be solved.'
Rothog smiles at you, and his grin seems more ferocious than ever.
'The people of the city loved my husband. I will rule as part of the Ghad Imghêda in his memory, and on their behalf.'
'The Heirsworn will no longer pose a threat to us. I will see to that.'
'The actions of Khôltekh shame his people and his city. The Umbari can rest more easily now that I have joined the Ghad Imghêda.'
'The Ghad Imghêda meets even now at Dâr Rapha, east of the city. That is where I am going, for I wish to get a look at them. On these wise counsellors we put our hopes!'
'My brother Dax stands with this new Kindred as if he were one of them! That is an oversight, surely?'

'One thing followed another, ${PLAYER}. I am not sure what happened. But I am glad to see you safe and alive!
'At first I was just trying to carry out your will, telling the people what you told me... but as more and more folk learned that Hármelak and Khôltekh had imprisoned you and my brother, they became angrier and angrier. You helped many Umbari and Temámir alike when you came to these shores, ${PLAYER}, and it seems you have made more friends than you know!
'What began in confusion became a rebellion, Ilma-ghôli, the rising tide, and then there was no stopping it! Try as I might, I could not convince those who flocked to us that I was not cut out to lead them... and now they have made me part of the Ghad Imghêda. I don't understand how this happened, and yet every step of the way has led me to this moment.
'Is this how you feel every day, ${PLAYER}? I cannot get used to this!'
'How might things have transpired if Dax was locked away, and I was left to manage the uprising? Now that would result in a truly impressive Ghad Imghêda!'

'I wear these burns proudly in memory of Belondor, ${PLAYER}. I believe he sails now in the company of his friend Sirgon, and they are not bound by the oceans of the world.
'I sought not to join the Ghad Imghêda, but the people of the city demanded it. I could not refuse them. They ask for strength, and I possess it. It would be impolite to abandon them.'
Rothog grins, a frightful sight.
'Besides,' he says, 'all of my things are here.'

'Despite the land where he was born, my husband was a man of Umbar. The wife of such a man must be prepared for the voyage on which he might not return, and I was.'
Mêshka smiles sadly.
'That makes it little easier, ${PLAYER}, but one thing has lightened my sorrow. The people of the city loved my husband, and they grieve with me. The burden is shared across every Ward of Umbar Baharbêl, and so made less.
'They asked me to join the Ghad Imghêda and to rule in Belondor's stead. I agreed, and so honour my husband's memory and the love he held for this city and its people.'
'Each member of the Ghad Imghêda is impressive. Until they learn I am not, I will stand beside them and do the best I can!'
Some familiar faces await you: the Ghad Imghêda of Umbar Baharbêl
Dâr Rapha is up the hill to the east of the Gate of Songs, outside the city.

'Our return voyage was not as eventful as the first that brought you to these shores, ${PLAYER}!
'Umbar Baharbêl seemed on the very precipice of the cliff's edge when we departed, but all is now as it was. Let us ask some of the people nearby what transpired while we were away.
'You go to the east and find someone willing to talk near the Northern Ship-yard. The workers there are always willing to spend the day in idle chatter, and the tidings we seek are the furthest thing from trivial!'

'How could you not have heard? The Kindred of the Coins was overthrown, and a new Kindred raised in its place: the Ghad Imghêda, the Kindred Redeemed!
'Hármelak Golden-hand and Khôltekh the Temámir were in league with Ordâkh, allying even with Orcs of Mordor! They thought to sell this city to its oppressors, but they counted not on us: the common men and women of Umbar, the ship-builders and the sailors, the merchants and the scholars, the fishermen and the labourers.
'The people of Umbar Baharbêl rose up against them, and with one voice we spoke to them: \qIt will not be so!\q we shouted. The uprising lasted for the better part of the day, and into the night. There was bloodshed, for not every soldier at Hármelak's command threw down his weapons, but many saw the rightness of our cause and joined the just throng.
'Another group opposed us during the uprising: the Heirsworn, who have long troubled the peace of the harbour. One of my workers fought against them on the night of the uprising, and can tell you more. Her name is Jínen, and she was on her way to the Gate of Songs north of the city just moments ago. If you hurry you may find her there.
'But that is in the past. May the new Kindred better serve the interests of the Umbari people, free of the influences of Ordâkh!'

'Someone will tell us what transpired while we were away. Umbar Baharbêl seemed on the very precipice of the cliff's edge when we departed, but all is now as it was! Find someone at the Northern Ship-yard. east of here, who is willing to talk.'

'Yes, I fought against the Heirsworn during the uprising; I am not afraid to speak of it.
'They have always been the weakened side of the ship's hull, still long at sea, and I am not surprised that it eventually burst! The passage by the city of the Ordâkhai ships was a hammer-blow to that imperfection, and the Heirsworn believed their time had come at last to fully seize control once again. What made them so bold? I cannot say for certain, but whispers tell that many of their number had been secretly leaving the city for a number of weeks, rallied somewhere by the son of Balakhôr himself.
'The uprising was short but effective, and a new Kindred has been formed to lead Umbar Baharbêl in the days to come: the Ghad Imghêda! They assemble even now at Dâr Rapha, up the hill to the east. That is where I am going, for I wish to get a look at them. On these wise counsellors we put our hopes!'
'May the new Kindred better serve the interests of the Umbari people, free of the influences of Ordâkh!'

'Most of the crowd has not yet thought to look for us in Umbar-môkh. We can follow these passages to safety!'

'Hold it right there, Hármelak.'
The Temámir meaningfully grips the haft of his spear and nods in the direction of Khôltekh.
'I will not use this unless I am commanded to do so... but I will obey the order if it is given.'

'Spare me your indignation, Hármelak: you know what happens to those who gamble with the lives of others without taking care to slant the odds sufficiently in their favour. The Song of Waves and Wind proved very useful, and it may be that Gondor lies in ruin even now, but you failed to manage the people of the city, and they have turned upon you. That they think to also hold me accountable for your blunder is... unfortunate.
'But the memories of the people are short. You will be kept safe and unharmed until such time as it is politically advantageous for the Temámir to produce you.
'The waggons to the north will transport you safely out of the city and beyond reach of the crowd that calls for your head. This is much finer treatment than you would receive from anyone else; let us say it is in remembrance of the tyrants we overthrew, and the Kindred we led together, if only for a short time.'

Khôltekh motions for you to speak to him.
'You have nothing to fear, my Lady. The doors of Dâr Laja are strong, and the men who guard them are even stronger! None of the shouting throng will get inside.'

'The area from Dâr Laja to Bith Gabâr is packed with residents of the city, a shouting throng. Many in the crowd carry weapons, but for now they have not wielded them against us. I think that will not change, but I cannot say that with certainty.
'You must stay inside, my Lady. It is not safe for you out there. I fear we cannot protect you if you leave the safety of the Meeting-hall!'

'Dâr Laja is not safe for us, Hármelak. I know you trust in your guardsmen to keep the unruly throng at bay... but I have not that faith in them.
'The city has come alive with anger, and that fury is directed at you... at us. If we remain here, I believe we will be slain.'

'Hármelak and Khôltekh are missing. None have seen them since the uprising began.
'The people of the city who chose us to form the Ghad Imghêda expect us to redeem the Kindred of the Coins, to live up to its goals and not succumb to the rot that festered within it from its early founding. I hope it will be so, but that will be made more difficult if we cannot learn what befell Hármelak and Khôltekh during the uprising.'
'They may have perished during the uprising. What do you think happened to them when the people arose?'

'I wonder...?
'It is most likely they were caught and killed by the people they betrayed, but if that is so, where are the bodies? None have come forth to confirm either of their fates, so every suggestion is a supposition only. We can only guess at it.
'I do not like guessing, ${PLAYER}. I like knowing for certain.'
'Oh! I had almost forgotten, ${PLAYER}! I have news for you of your friends Corudan and Sigileth!'
'The Ghad Imghêda will remain alert for the reappearance of Hármelak or Khôltekh... just in case.'

'That is... a curious sight...
'In what direction do these animals travel?'
'Hers may not... but mine do. You say this may not be Silirtas... but if it is, I have to speak to her! I have to tell her I am sorry!'

'I urged you to come with us, Silirtas, to face a great and unknown evil. I thought despite every danger that lay ahead of us, if any need perish, it would be Sigileth of Lórien. I thought I could keep you safe! I am so sorry!
'When you were slain by Azagath before the door of Utug-bûr, I fell into despair. I thought I too must die to atone for that terrible deed, for robbing you of the life you might have had; only the voice of drew me out of that darkness.
'${PLAYER:Her[f]|His} words made me realize something, dear Silirtas. Every moment of every day, for every person in this Middle-earth, is a gift: not of treasure, but of choice. Every point in time gives you the opportunity to decide how you choose to use that moment. You chose to fight the fading of your people. You chose to venture with an Elf and a you had known for less than a day to combat an evil of the Elder Days. Those choices were yours, Silirtas, and I am inspired by them! I celebrate them!
'But I have learned there is one more choice you might make, dear one!'

Sigileth wipes the tears from her eyes.
'I have said my part. I believe Silirtas heard my words... but I cannot know for certain.'

'Corudan lost a great deal of blood at Kasukhín before we could stem its flow, and that would explain a chill of the body.
'But for you to feel it as well makes me think there may be another cause, an outward cause. This cold is not natural.'

'The Kindred of the Coins was neither entirely evil nor entirely good, ${PLAYER}. Like Hyarmendacil II, they achieved both lasting good and enduring harm. Does one erase the other? Wiser scholars than I may be able to weigh the value of each... but I cannot. Must we forget the instrumental roles played by Azagath and Nakási in the freeing of Umbar from the Heirs of Castamir and the cultists of Sauron? Must we forget Khôltekh's deeds during the Dagor Carlanthir, or Hármelak's advice that Dâr Laja be opened to the needs of her people? Must their later crimes strike from the record their earlier heroics and wise governance?'
Caebar studies the ground intently.
'Must my mother's refusal to see me erase the happy years I spent as a child in Ethring, ${PLAYER}? I think it cannot. So we celebrate the good and we work to remedy the bad, and by so doing we mend what wounds we can, and seek to avoid inflicting further harm. That is healing, of a kind, is it not?'
The Gondorian scribe heaves a sigh and looks up at you again, forcing a smile.
'From conversation with the Umbari I have sketched the members of the original Kindred of the Coins, ${PLAYER}. Umbar will remember both their fine qualities and their faults, neither excusing the other, and with these drawings I hoped to capture that balance. Choose one of your liking and it is yours; the others I will give to the city of Umbar Baharbêl, that it may remember its history and not forget it.'
'Look for these papers among Corudan's belongings, and give them to Caebar.'

Caebar accepts the papers and briefly studies them.
'Wait... you say that Corudan found these in an Ordâkh encampment in the Fearwater? I do not want to pester him with questions, ${PLAYER}, so let us speak of this outside.'
'Give Caebar the papers my brother collected during our time in the Fearwater.'

You find Caebar excitedly studying the papers Corudan retrieved from the Ordâkhai of Sûg Nidar.
'The soldiers would not have understood the meaning of this parchment, ${PLAYER}, but I do. They must have found it among the ruins of Kasukhín while searching for treasure; thinking it unimportant, they kept it unguarded among their belongings, where it went overlooked until it was picked up by Corudan.
'These are the words of Vinyarion, twenty-fourth King of Gondor, who bore the title of Hyarmendacil II: \qthe South-victor.\q Set down by a trusted retainer in his old age, only days before his death, these words claim that he repented of his long campaign in Harad, and wept at the bones of Shâraban, a city he destroyed in the days of his youth. On the return journey of his tenth pilgrimage to the lands he once conquered, he rested at the hilltop fort of Kasukhín and died there, peacefully, in his sleep. Sigileth tells me the land around that fort is now changed, and what was once a hill is now an island; might Vinyarion's bones lie there to this day, kept isolated from discovery by the creation of the Fearwater?
'His story raises complicated emotions in my heart, ${PLAYER}; he is considered very differently in Shagâna than he is in Gondor, and it is difficult to reconcile those two perspectives. I am put in mind of the relationship the Umbari must now have with the Kindred of the Coins that preceded the Ghad Imghêda, the Kindred Redeemed.'
'Yes, I will tell you what transpired after you left us.'

'I cannot say with certainty that the spirit was Silirtas, or that she heard my words. But I believe it was, and she did. I will not hurry to join her, but when at last I come to that place, I hope she and I will reside in comfort and in peace, beyond the loneliness and fear that so troubled Silirtas when she contemplated the unknown days ahead.
'That is my desire, ${PLAYER}. I cannot know if it will come to pass, but if hope leads us ever onward, the pleasant dream of it will live in my heart until the last of my days arrives.'

Caebar flushes.
'Oh! I am sorry to interrupt, ${PLAYER}! I did not know you had returned! I have visited our friends every day while Corudan recovers, and they have spoken to me of your adventure in the Fearwater.
'Please, finish your visit! I will speak with you afterward.'
'Caebar has visited every day, and kept us informed of events in the city.'

'That reminds me. My brother collected some papers from the Ordâkhai while we adventured in the Fearwater. He intended to give them to Caebar, but the matter has slipped our minds until now. Look for them among Corudan's belongings, and give them to Caebar.'
And as a light breeze passes over the sea, thus ends 'The Song of Waves and Wind'

'You should visit them at Dâr Tabib, in the Tor-gardens of Umbar Baharbêl. I know Corudan and Sigileth will be pleased to see you!'

'${PLAYER}, my friend... my wound is well on its way to healing... but to see you return with victory... eases the pain. I understand Umbar has been saved from... Nakási and Balakhâd? Has Gondor too... escaped from their wrath?'
You tell Corudan that King Elessar and his soldiers fought bravely against the Song, and Gondor survived. He smiles weakly.
'Then the last of Sauron's schemes... has been frustrated, ${PLAYER}. I am glad for my part in it...'
You insist that Corudan rest, and you will speak with him when he is more fully healed.

'I understand Nakási is slain and the Song of Waves and Wind defeated, ${PLAYER}. May there now be peace for a time!
'I heard tell that five ships of the Song survived the passage to Gondor, and waged war upon the Harlond? More might have joined them, had the rapids of the Ikorbân not proved too perilous; we saw the ruin of many smaller ships dashed upon the rocks as we travelled this way from Sûg Nidar. The builders of the fleet likely intended that to be a one-way voyage, but they had not counted upon Cúridwan's damaging solution, or your great haste in opposing those who escaped it.
'The raft-bridge of the Wrackwade did not last long against the Narghâk cannons. When we rejoined Rahâzi at Iridír she said her mother intended to see it rebuilt. It would not surprise me to learn she has already done so! But I have gotten ahead of myself. There is more to tell.
'While you pursued the Song toward Umbar, my brother and I and Cúridwan made our own way westward. Our return journey... was not uneventful.'
'Our return to the city... was not uneventful. My sister... will speak of it to you.'

'I have a personal matter with which I would ask your assistance, ${PLAYER}.
'I have received word from my spies of a rumour that my husband, Eshtali, has recently been seen outside the Crypts of Esh-kimâkhi to the south of here. What he is doing there, I have no idea.
'The leader of the Barkhûshim, that accursed Okhíso, claimed to take him when he drove us all from Kûr Anzar. I thought my precious Eshtali long since dead. I know it is dangerous, ${PLAYER}, but I feel a dagger of hope in my chest.
'You have accomplished much with me here. There is no one I trust more with this mission than you. Please, make your way to Esh-kimâkhi and look for him. You will know him by the crimson robes he always wears. I have sent Razâl ahead of you to scout the terrain, speak with him when you arrive.
'And, ${PLAYER}? If you are to return with my husband, know that you will have given me a gift worth more to me than any victory in this war.'

'Thank you for that news, and for his effects. Hope is a cruel master, and one that has now abandoned me.
'I remember when I was a girl, my sisters and I would make shapes, shadows on the wall. We would make funny animals: ducks, and rabbits, and chickens. Oh, and the stories we would tell! The adventures those rabbits and ducks had! Such stories. Those days have long passed, but when I close my eyes I can still see those shadows; dancing, vaulting, gamboling. I still hear their peals of laughter.
'When my husband came home, I would first see him by the shadow he cast on the wall. So broad and powerful, that shadow was the harbinger of my precious Eshtali coming home to me. Just like my sisters, I sought comfort in that shadow, always steady, strangely solid.
'After he was taken, I am ashamed to say I forgot what his face looked like, once so familiar to me. I can no longer see his face. All I see of him now is that shadow on the wall, insubstantial like a wraith, endlessly dancing through my memories.'

'Something you can do for me? Absolutely, get the word out. Mulnûri will not be beat, cannot be beat on these prices or this quality. Look at these tunics. You will find no higher quality anywhere in Shagâna. Umbar can only marvel at these textures, this softness, they cannot come close to matching me.
'Everyone needs to know. It's for the public good!'

'Help, for me? Unless you can get the smell of fire or this blasted soot out of the air, you cannot do anything for me. Why did I let my wife convince me to come back here? Blasted wars, terrible for business, and one's nose.'

'Thank you for your help setting up and helping usher in some of old Kûr Anzar.
'The people of Kûr Anzar will now look to us for a sense of normalcy. A warm belly and a new tunic may not seem like much, but they are more than many have had here in Kûr Anzar in some time.'
'There is still much to be done, and yet more to be celebrated! Please, help the vendors set up their wares and make both the residents and vendors feel welcome again.'
'It is so good to be home again. Help? No, no, no. I need nothing from you. I'm too excited for help... in a good way.'

'So much to do, so little time. Help? No, nothing I need, my dear. I'm just so glad to see people smiling again around here. At least I think they are smiling. Surely they are! It's hard to tell through the soot.'
'How is one supposed to turn a decent profit with all this rubble everywhere? Yes, you can help me. Get some of this rubble cleared away. My clothes are far too fine to be in a war.'

'Fair winds to you, my friend! Do you ride horses?
'In the fair land where I hail from, we take great pride in our breed of horses, highly valued not just for their speed and endurance, but also their courage and loyalty. We have a long history of grand competitions where riders display their animals and their skills, and I wanted to bring such an event to Zír Aktar's visitors.
'If you think you can handle one of our fine steeds, you are welcome to give our race course a try. I warn you though, only the most skilled of riders will be able to master such a tricky path in the amount of time we have allotted.
'The rules of the race are very simple -- race through each gate, and you must not fall off your steed before the time runs out. You will find obstacles and challenging terrain, but it is also a wonderful way to see the island. When you see two gates next to one another, you must choose which path to take, be it high or low. Each path has its own benefits and hinderances.
'Do you feel up for this challenge? Only the most spirited riders should even attempt such a feat! It is sure to be very dangerous, but you have an adventurous look to you.'
'Excellent riding, ${PLAYER}! I am very impressed. Take these tokens in reward of your achievement!'

'Are you ready to travel to Furtherholm? The first thing you should do when you get there is talk to Captain Khâtaphos. Ready? Then let us be off!'
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTE: When you continue this quest, you will swiftly travel to Furtherholm in the Shield Isles.</rgb>
Welcome to Furtherholm!
Ikhajât has whisked you away to the island of Furtherholm, where you should introduce yourself to Khâtaphos.

'My greetings to you, traveller. You are a traveller, are you not?
'As you may have already guessed, I am a visitor from a faraway land. I hail from The Shield Isles, in what you would call The Bay of Belfalas. I came here to spread the word that Midsummer is the perfect time to visit! There is an island called Zír Aktar, Furtherholm in Westron, that is welcoming visitors!
'On the island you will find soothing sea breezes, beautiful beaches and calming palm trees. Not to mention the delightful drinks and relaxing rooms at The Cracked Flagon, the local inn and tavern. Would you like to take a break from this place and enjoy all that Furtherholm has to offer? If you would like, I could guide you there and you will be sipping sweet spiced wines on the beach faster than you can say... something. I do not know where I was going with that. It will be fast.'
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTE: This quest will be removed from your quest log when the current festival ends.</rgb>
Talk to Khâtaphos inside The Cracked Flagon
Talk to Ikhajât

'Greetings! Welcome to Furtherholm! It is beautiful here, is it not?
'I beg your forgiveness, but this is a new venture for my crew and I, and we could always use some help. While you are visiting us, if you would like to chip in and assist the crew with their duties, you would be well rewarded. We have many of these Midsummer Tokens that we have... ah, come by, from our neighbours in Gondor. They are of no small value, as they can be exchanged for many wonderful gifts!
'If you lend us a hand, you can earn some of these tokens. Many, in fact! You can speak to Darôma, or the cook Sâghlem, here in The Cracked Flagon; they always have things that need doing. Outside, you will find Merkhâma and Maghôrdo, who both have more work daily than can be done by one person. Or two. I also may have something you can do for me now that I think about it. Ask me later, if you like.
'Do not worry! I use the word \qwork\q lightly, as everything is more fun when you are at the beach, am I right? Please accept this small welcome gift for coming to Furtherholm.
'Enjoy your stay!'

'Navigating the waters of the Shield Isles can be quite challenging. Irregular winds, unusual currents, and reefs hidden just below the surface pose many dangers to ships if the crew is not up to the task. Because of this, it is not unusual for flotsam from shipwrecks to wash ashore on the southern beaches. Maybe it is not so good for visitors to see these things and be reminded that journeys here do not always end in the way they planned!
'You would be doing me a great service if you would remove any flotsam you find on Furtherholm's southern shores.'

'Everyone has gotten the help they wanted? Thank you very much for helping them! And by them, I mean me.'

'My goodness, I am absolutely parched! It is important to consume many beverages whilst taking in the beach, you know.
'Be a dear and run over to the tavern and get me a refreshing beverage. Something strong, if you catch my meaning.'

'A picnic, you say? Oh, they appeared to be courting?'
The man chuckles as he takes the basket and begins to fill it.
'I have just the thing. A bottle of wine, some cured meats, a variety of cheeses, water biscuits, and a few figs. That should do them!'
'Oh ho, this is perfect, my friend. Thank you ever so much. And send my regards to Sâghlem.'

'Isn't this island such a magical place!?
'I heard that beachgoers have been known to enjoy themselves by burying each other in the sand! Buried in the sand, I say!? Well, I say to myself, I think I would quite like that! Only as the bury-ee I have no bury-er. But now you have come along!
'I charge you with the task of burying me in the sand!'
'You found it! Thank you so much. I have been eager to read what happens next. Clear skies and swift sails to you, my friend.'
'Oh yes, do give that here. This is just what I needed. Now go, you are blocking my view.'

'Fair winds to you, what is it that you need? Oh, you come to ask if I need anything? Now that I think about it, I would love to be reading my book right now, but I left it in my room at the inn. I am afraid that if I leave here to go get it, someone will steal my seat on this bench!
'Would you mind going into The Cracked Flagon and getting my book? I left it on the side table, next to the bed.'
'Ah! That will do perfectly! Thank you!'

'Greetings, my good ${RACE}. Since you appear to be assisting people, I wonder if you would do us a small favour.
'I daresay I did not plan our day well, as it would be a perfect day for a picnic, but alas, we do not have a picnic basket of food! If you would, nip on over to the tavern and fetch us a picnic, would you?'

'Bless me, you nearly gave a fright!
'Do I need anything? Well... if it's not too much trouble, I could use something to sit on. I'm enjoying the view very much, but this sand... I hate it. It's rough and irritating, and it gets everywhere. I think those folks over there with a blanket have the right idea. Could you perhaps bring me a cushion or some-such?'

'Fair winds to you, my friend! Have you ever flown a kite before?
'Watch them soar through the sky like a great bird! Feel the wind tug at your string; harness the very air for your personal enjoyment! ...Oh, you are already familiar? My humble apologies. Well, then you must already know of the glorious wonder kites offer! Do you need another? There is nothing like having a new kite to make all of your friends envy you.
'I am Tâlugar and I come from the famous city of Umbar Baharbêl, bringing beautiful kites from the furthest reaches of Middle-earth to trade for a small amount of coin. These kites are of the finest quality! ...You will think about it? That is all I could ever ask for, of course. No, I take that back. There is one thing I would ask of you.
'Since you are already familiar with kites, I will offer you payment if you let loose your favourite kite and let it kiss the sky in front of the good people visiting this island. Let them see the fun you have as your kite navigates the winds like a ship soaring in the heavens! If they see how much fun it is, they will surely flock to me to purchase one of their own!'

A rather plain name, I should say, but at least it is descriptive.
'My friend, I charge you with a quest. A quest unlike any other. Go forth and search every corner of Middle-earth until you find this \qParty Tree\q. '${PLAYER}! I have not seen you since your steps brought you to Umbar-môkh. I have come aboveground to ask Khôltekh... but my errand can wait. Something troubles you?'
You quickly tell Birûk that Nakási Wave-reaper sails a hostile fleet toward the city, and the banks of the Ikorbân River are not safe.
'I will delay you no longer! Tell the Kindred of the Coins what you have told me!'

'You know there is little to be gained by dying here, ${PLAYER}.'
Khôltekh lowers his voice so only you can hear him.
'Hármelak might have pretended she first heard the name \qThe Song of Waves and Wind\q from you, when you visited her in her manor, but she is not as clever as she thinks herself to be. Wealth cannot buy wisdom; only experience can do that.
'When Azagath told us of the Song's existence, neither of us believed in it. If the Dark Lord of Mordor could not rely upon such a fleet, of what use could it be to us? But it seems Nakási has done the impossible. The Narghâk I sent her from Ashâgir will prove the difference, I think.
'When Gondor burns, the folk of Umbar Baharbêl will rejoice.'

'Looks like this is it, ${PLAYER}.
'We have to put our faith in Daxamat now.'

'A hostile fleet approaches? My business with the Kindred can wait!
'There is coin to be made, ${PLAYER}!'
Temámir archers hold you at bay. You can fight no longer
At a gesture from the Golden Queen, the guards encircle you
Jajax has come with you to Dâr Laja to warn the Kindred of the Coins about the approaching danger.

'If by our warning we save the city, the Kindred will surely seek to reward us for our actions today, ${PLAYER}. Let us hurry!'

'Your face is lined with worry, ${PLAYER}. What brings you with such urgency to Dâr Laja?'
You tell Hármelak that Nakási Wave-reaper sails a secret fleet armed with Narghâk cannons and crewed by Orcs of Mordor and soldiers of Ordâkh down the Ikorbân River. She frowns uncertainly.
'So it is a fight, then. Fine! There are not enough of them to best both Jajax and ${PLAYER}!'

'Through our efforts, most of the ships were damaged and cannot sail... but not all! Balakhâd and Nakási will sail the remaining ships of the Song down the River Ikorbân, endangering all the lands through which it flows!
'Mount your steed, ${PLAYER}! The city of Umbar Baharbêl lies at the mouth of the river, and if you bring word of the approaching ships to the rulers of the city, they may be able to close the river gate before the Song of Waves and Wind passes the city! Speak to me if you will do this!'
'We will follow behind you as we can, ${PLAYER}, but you must ride with as much speed as you can! You must get to Umbar before the Song of Waves and Wind!'
'If this fleet is as dangerous as you say it is, the city is in grave danger!'

'What did you say? A secret fleet sails toward the city? And I was not informed?'
You tell Jajax that Nakási Wave-reaper and Balakhâd have taken control of the Song of Waves and Wind and equipped its ships with dangerous Narghâk weapons. If it is not kept from leaving the Ikorbân River, all of Middle-earth will be in danger.
'You need the Kindred of the Coins to close the river gate? You will want my help with this, ${PLAYER}. Let me know when you are ready for us to speak with them.'
'The Kindred of the Coins will listen to me, you will see. No one can refuse Jajax!'

'It is not much, Dax, but you can stay here as long as you need. I have lived here ever since Kinsman Belondor ordered my release from the jail following his return from Ikorbân. Many of my fellows were freed as well. I know not what Belondor saw there, but I am grateful for it!
'You can stay here until you learn what happened to your brother. There has really been no word of him since he and ${PLAYER} went to Dâr Laja?'

'A hostile fleet approaches from the river? Can this be so?
'I will share these tidings throughout the city!'
'A fleet of ships manned by the Heirsworn approaches from the River Ikorbân? How can this be?'
'Are we... are we in danger?'

'I know you for a friend of the city, ${PLAYER}. If you say a hostile fleet approaches Umbar Baharbêl, then it must be so.
'We must arrange for the defence of the city! We must get everyone away from the river!'

'What is this I hear, ${PLAYER}? Tell me what I can do!'
You ask Daxamat to spread the word to the people of the city that a fleet of dangerous ships carrying Orcs and Ordâkhai soldiers approaches from Ikorbân.
'I will! You should find my brother Jajax at the forum of Bith Gabâr... he will know what to do!'
'I will arrange for the defence of the city!'

'We must get inside that camp and get close to that main tent in the back. I am sure whoever is in charge will be in there. If we hope to save Surâsh and end these attacks, we need to know who these people are and what they are planning.
'We also must locate Surâsh, but we should only free her after we've scouted the enemy and found out all we can of their plans, as the noise and commotion may waylay any intelligence gathering.
'We must be stealthy as we move. There are too many of them for a frontal assault. Are you ready?'

'I cannot believe Nimasi turned on us. This is most troubling. Most troubling. And the danger to you was grave, I must be better about who I allow into the Subuzûri.'
Mizâdi appears to steel herself. A sudden coldness overtakes her face.
'I don't care how many soldiers the Hûl has proffered him. He has not yet felt the might of the Subuzûri.
'Very well. If it is a war he wants, then he shall have one.
'But I will not allow the people of Kûr Anzar to feel war's cold comforts once more. I will meet him in open battle. War is coming, ${PLAYER}. War is coming to Imhûlar.'
'Are you ready? Steel yourself, we are about to go into the lair of these monsters.'

'What an interesting story! This is a simple matter, indeed. Nothing that some skull-crushing can't fix and quickly, if I do say so myself.
'Were it up to me, and not my queen, I would accompany this scout south, find the blasted fools scattering their distasteful and ugly artistry hither and yon, and split them in twain with a good iron blade. I know Mizâdi prefers me here in Kûr Anzar, however, to assist with the rebuilding.
'Perhaps you can see to the skull-crushing this time, ${PLAYER}?'

'I should hope there will be no need for skull-crushing, Numûru's wishes notwithstanding.
'You were able to quickly find the missing scouts last time, so I believe you, ${PLAYER}, are the perfect one to go with Nimasi. Hopefully this conclusion is a happier one than that of the other scouts. Will you help Nimasi?
'If so, please, tell Nimasi you will go down to the south to investigate this disappearance.'

'Hashtal-gûr, favoured outsider. I would request an audience with my Shâra, though I know it not proper. The situation I find myself in is that dire.
'The scout who brought you news of a southern incursion not so long ago, Surâsh? She is one of the scouts with which I patrol. She has herself now vanished. We were supposed to meet at a certain hilltop two nights ago. In her place I found this strange banner. I believe it to be the same standard you found with her not long before. She told me the story.
'Would you ask the Shâra if she can spare some forces to investigate Surâsh's disappearance? We southern scouts are being picked off one by one like zizani. I fear the worst for Surâsh, and, if I'm honest, for myself.'

'So strange. This is indeed the same banner you and Surâsh brought me. Who could be doing this?
'I need to think on this for a moment. You should ask Numûru his feelings on the matter.'

'I knew our Shâra was both just and benevolent! Please thank her for me, and thank you, for your eloquence in relaying this need.

'You want shields? Everybody wants shields. Sârgud is so popular all of the sudden.

'I'll tell you what I can do. Sârgud performs miracles, you'll see! I have some shields almost ready. You gather me some more ore from the north-eastern hills to replace what I used here, and I will give the Shâra these shields. Yes, Sârgud's amazing. I know, I know, you don't even need to tell me.

'Word spreads through the city that a hostile fleet approaches on the Ikorbân River, and that has been imprisoned for trying to stop it. Can this be true?
'My wife Khâsha and I name a friend. Any who seek to harm ${PLAYER:her[f]|him} must answer to us! My deadliest days are behind me, but I have mates enough throughout the Shield Isles and the Cape to make things difficult for the Kindred of the Coins if they truly have betrayed the city, as the whispering suggests.
'If the word of the advance scouts can be trusted, it seems likely: they say you can hear Orkish voices from at least one of the approaching ships.'

'Rumours spread like wildfire throughout the Lower Ward. Is it true that has been imprisoned by the Kindred of the Coins? I can think of no reason for ${PLAYER:her[f]|him} to languish in the jail, especially if ${PLAYER:she[f]|he} sought to warn us about this approaching danger! Why would the Kindred support this attack?
'My husband owes a great deal to Tumúldo Fierce-water, who convinced him not to join Balakhôr during the war... but that was a different Kindred, and people say Tumúldo is slain.
'People also say you and your brother are 's close companions, Daxamat. Tell us what we must do to help, and we will do it!'

'The people turn to you for guidance, Dax!'
You stammer to Itûr that you don't know what to do. He rests an assuring hand on your shoulder.
'Ask yourself what ${PLAYER} and Jajax would do, if they were here.'

'Yes! That is exactly right, Dax!
'Today we begin to fight against those who would betray us! For ${PLAYER}, and for Jajax!'

'You are Daxamat, the brother of Jajax? I have been looking for you! I have tidings of him you should hear. I spoke to many people hoping to find you, but at last a rumour-monger directed me to this place. Now hear what I have seen!
'I was in Dâr Laja when your brother and my friend petitioned the Kindred of the Coins to close shut the river gate and prevent the approaching fleet from passing the city. Almost did I leave, but curiosity stayed my feet, and I watched from afar as they were seized by the guards! They were brought to the jail, and are now captives of Hármelak... even Khôltekh has sided with her! I can think of no just reason for him to do this!
'I fear the Kindred of the Coins has betrayed the city. Even now I hesitate to return to the streets; they may keep watch for any who witnessed their duplicity! proved a friend to many of us in the city... how can they justify imprisoning ${PLAYER:her[f]|him} after such monumental deeds on behalf of Umbari and Temámir alike?'

'You need a way to pass unseen from this refuge without being seen by spies loyal to the Kindred of the Coins? I would not call this day fortunate... but perhaps in this matter alone I have some good fortune to share.
'Pass through the door behind me and take the stairs down to the cellar. You will see what I mean.'
'I fear the Kindred of the Coins has betrayed the city. Even now I hesitate to return to the streets; they may keep watch for any who witnessed their betrayal!'
'Pass through the door behind me and take the stairs down to the cellar. You will see what I mean.'

'Ah, I see what your friend has in mind. I know a waterway to Umbar-môkh when I see one. With this I can enter and leave the refuge without detection by spies loyal to Hármelak.'
Birûk shakes his fists in the air.
'I still cannot believe Khôltekh would endanger the city in this way! I have never known to lie, and ${PLAYER:she[f]|he} was most clear that a hostile fleet sails down the river toward us!
'I may be able to contact someone who can get a message to the prisoners. I will return and let you know if I succeed.'
'I may be able to contact someone who can get a message to the prisoners. I will return and let you know.'

'It will not be as you say. The people of the city will know why I could not close the river gate. If the Song of Waves and Wind could not leave the River Ikorbân, Nakási would have turned the Narghâk cannons upon Umbar Baharbêl! Should we have sacrificed our own city for the sake of Gondor?'
You ask Hármelak if she truly believes that Nakási or Balakhâd would have destroyed their own city, and she waves a dismissive hand.
'You believe the people of the city share your uncertainty, ${PLAYER}.'

'I have a message for you from one of the Temámir. He says \qThe work continues. We need many hands to mine the Abâshal, and will forge new medallions from it. Remain alert for its shine, and stay safe: the mine is treacherous, but there will be a light in the darkness.'
The girl turns to go, but she hesitates. She faces you again, and you try to remember where you have before heard this voice.
'We watched as the ships passed the city. One galley tried to block the way to open water, and it was sunk. The terrible smoke of the cannons smelled foul. We saw Orcs on the deck of one of the ships. They cheered as the ship of Umbar burned; the water could not quench the blue flames.'

You never saw her face before now, but it was in Umbar-môkh that you spoke to Tephísa. She is one of the Terâsi, the forgotten children who make their way through hidden paths beneath the city. It must have been the Temámir Birûk who gave her this message to bring to you and Jajax.
Tephísa studies your face closely.
'I watched the flames destroy my home once, stranger. They were orange and red then, the embers lit by servants of Barkhûsh, but a fire is a fire. Those ships will set ablaze the homes of Gondor, but they will return, and when they return the conflagration will spread to the homes of Umbar.
'I can help you escape, but I have a price.'

You tell Jajax that Hármelak is lying.
'Aye,' he agrees. 'She lied before, and she lies again.'

'The hidden harbour is just ahead. We must cut through these foes if we are to reach Tatháta's ship!'

'Ah, this is more like it. I have always been more at home aboard a ship, even if that ship carries me to dangerous battle in defence of Gondor, of all places! At least the legend of Jajax will continue to grow!
'We will leave the uprising against Hármelak and Khôltekh in Daxamat's capable hands. Ha! Capable? There is a first time for everything, I suppose.
'I hope we are not making a grave mistake, ${PLAYER}!'

'Sirgon has been upon my mind these last few hours, ${PLAYER}. What would he say to know that now I sail to his home of Gondor in a desperate bid to defend it from destruction?
'Ah, I know the answer. He would smile and clap me upon the back, and say he would do the same for my own home. What do Gondor and Umbar have in common? Sons and daughters who would die for them, against any threatening danger.'

'I am sad, ${PLAYER}.'
You ask Rothog why he is sad, and he grumbles something you cannot hear. When you ask him to repeat it, he heaves a heavy sigh.
'I did not think to bring Húrshauk with me when we came to rescue you from the jail, and Tatháta says there is no time for me to go get him. Now he must stay behind in the city instead of joining the battle in Gondor.
'He will miss all of the fighting! Perhaps one of the members of Ilma-ghôli will bring him to Dâr Laja to slay Hármelak or Khôltekh? He would like that. Oh, I hope they do!'

'Sotóka is a fast ship, but the Song departed many hours before us. We may be too late to prevent Nakási from completing her mission.
'She is driven by vengeance, ${PLAYER}: not just for the death of Tumúldo, but for every injury and injustice she has suffered during her years of life. Each of these wounds has fed her hatred, and now she has been blinded by her desire for vengeance.'
Tatháta smiles grimly, a most rare sight indeed.
'That is the meaning of \qSotóka,\q ${PLAYER}: Vengeance. Is it chance or plan that speeds us in pursuit of Nakási aboard a ship of vengeance? I cannot say. The world is a curious place.'

'The Kindred of the Coins is dead, ${PLAYER}. It was created to protect the people of the city, not to burn them alive as did the Church of Barkhûsh. If the Umbari do not slay Hármelak and Khôltekh for their betrayal, I will do it myself.
'Below the city I witnessed Belondor and Rothog travelling with great speed, and pursued them. Had they supported Hármelak's treachery they would be dead already, but it seems these two have not abandoned their wits.
'We are to bring you by paths beneath the city to the hideout where the uprising began. Are you ready?'
You hesitate. Images of thatched Gondorian cottages wreathed by blue flame flash before your eyes, followed by homes in the Umbari style suffering the same fate. You remember a small voice asking you to destroy the ships and their masters.

'What is the cause for this delay, ${PLAYER}? The city above is a tinder-box ready to catch fire at the slightest spark, and Ilma-ghôli cannot now be stopped.'
You tell Belondor that you fear for the people of Gondor, unaware of the deadly danger that sails toward them, and for the people of Umbar. He nods.
'It had occurred to me that Nakási will not give up this fleet when her business in Gondor is completed,' he replies.
'She will return with it to Umbar Baharbêl, and any passing whim will be enforced by cannon and with Hungry Fire.'

'My ship Sotóka is moored in a hidden harbour not far from here, ${PLAYER}, and none can match her speed when her sails are full.'
You ask Tatháta if she would be willing to pursue the Song of Waves and Wind to Gondor, despite the danger, and she stares at you seriously.
'On my last voyage with Nakási, we sailed around the coast of Outer Gondor. Our purpose was to prove to the new King of Gondor that despite the defeat of Umbar in the war, the Kindred of the Coins was not without strength. Umbar would not be subservient; Umbar must be treated as a powerful neighbour, worthy of respect.
'But then Tumúldo was slain, and the light in Nakási's eyes changed. Hatred drove her. We encountered the grove of a tree-tender on the cape of Anfalas. Later I learned from Nestinanessornë that his name, at least in the tongue used by Elves and Men, was Leafshade. Nakási threatened to burn his grove as a message to Gondor, and I told her I wanted no part of it... but had Nestinanessornë not surrendered to her I know she would have burned that grove with fire and torches, and all of Gondor beside.
'Now she possesses the ability to do just that, ${PLAYER}. If my ship Sotóka can stop her, I cannot remain idly by and claim to have not aided her. For Leafshade, if not for any others, my ship is yours. Agents of Khôltekh and the Heirsworn stand between you and the hidden harbour. I hope you are ready.'

'None would mistake me for one of the Corsairs of legend; my prowess is not in combat or swordplay. I spent many weeks in the jail when the nobleman I thought to rob of his purse proved more vigilant than I expected, so I would not recommend you assign me tasks of thievery!'
Itûr laughs suddenly.
'There is one thing I can help you steal, Dax. Together we will steal the hearts of the people, right from under the noses of the Kindred! Folk have already come here searching for someone to lead them, and more are sure to come. We are going to need a place where we can make our plans.
'Maybe we should set up the room on the right so we can accommodate our growing numbers.'

'Folk have already come here searching for someone to lead them, and more are sure to come. We are going to need a place where we can make our plans. Maybe we should set up the room on the right so we can accommodate our growing numbers.'

'This is a start, but there is more to be done. The Kindred of the Coins has two places where their leadership can feel safe: within the Meeting-hall of Dâr Laja, and within the strong walls of the Citadel of the Winds. As our numbers grow, we will need to find some way of threatening these bastions, making the Kindred question its safety and the sources of its power.
'There is something else, too.'

'Hármelak and Khôltekh have imprisoned two of our most significant figures, Dax. The city will not forgive this outrage, and as word of it spreads, the dominion of the Kindred must begin to weaken. Did they underestimate how beloved ${PLAYER} has become to the people of Umbar Baharbêl? Did they underestimate the popularity of your brother Jajax?
'I think these were mistakes, Dax. But now we must ask ourselves an important question. For how long will the Kindred keep Jajax and ${PLAYER} in captivity? Are they still alive, and if they are, for how long will they remain so?'

'You are Daxamat, yes? The brother of Jajax? These men follow your command?'
Belondor looks you up and down, and releases his hand from the hilt of his sword.
'I should have known something was amiss, Daxamat. Hármelak's sudden interest in the Thardúth should have raised my suspicion, for always has she dismissed the servants of Morgoth we faced in Urash Dâr as less of a threat to Umbar than others. To ask Rothog and I to travel to Damarzâg, to learn if they have any presence there... it seems an obvious ruse, now, a means of keeping two members of the Kindred from interfering with her plans. When we departed I thought only that at last she was taking seriously the danger.
'But now we have returned, and we must decide what can be done. Where is ? We should ask ${PLAYER:her[f]|him} for ${PLAYER:her[f]|his} thoughts.'

'Rûmina and I can move unnoticed through the Lower Ward with great speed... until the moment we want to be seen, and to be heard. I am confident we can spread the news of Hármelak's betrayal of the city, and that Khôltekh may be aiding her. It will not be difficult: few of the Umbari failed to see the enemy ships as they passed the city, and it was apparent to all that their Corsair crews had joined hands with soldiers of Ordâkh and Orcs of Mordor. It is an outrage and a mockery!
'I understand there is a plan in motion to free your brother and ${PLAYER} from captivity? Has there yet been any word?'

'I bring good news from Umbar-môkh, Daxamat.
'My contact has spoken with . ${PLAYER:She[f]|He} and Jajax are being held within the Fleet-fast jail, and the Terâsi girl is willing to show us a secret way inside. She seemed very insistent that if she performs this task for us, we will see that the enemy fleet is destroyed. I know not if that is within our power... but I told her we would consider it.
'We need and Jajax freed. We can consider nothing until that happens, am I right?'
'One more thing! I understand there is a plan in motion to free your brother and ${PLAYER} from captivity? Has there yet been any word?'
'Something has happened upstairs! Are we discovered?'

'For now I relent. If you give me a reason to fight, I will not again lower my khopeshes until the battle is done!
'Belondor and I were away from the city, visiting the arid hills of Damarzâg and looking for evidence of the Thardúth. We found none, but when we returned to Umbar Baharbêl the shouting of its people could be mistaken by no one. Someone had allowed a fleet of Mordor and Ordâkh to pass by the city, and as it sailed into the Bay it turned its cannons upon Umbari ships! Even now the wreck of an Umbari galley smoulders with the blue flames of the Hungry Fire!
'Some members of my Kindred seem to have allied with this fleet, but only one arranged for me and Belondor to be away from the city when it arrived. This was the work of Hármelak! She knew this fleet was on its way, and she wanted to ensure Rothog did not stop it!'
You heave a sigh of relief as they lower their weapons

'You have given these folk their orders, Daxamat. What now is your role to play?'
You tell Belondor that you are ready to free your brother Jajax and the hero ${PLAYER} from the Fleet-fast jail, but before you can say anything else, he shakes his head.
'I think not, Daxamat. That is a dangerous undertaking. I cannot say how it has happened, but you have somehow become the leader of this rising tide, this Ilma-ghôli. Without you to focus these varied and disparate fighters, I think this uprising is snuffed out like a torch doused in sea-water. You must remain here at this refuge in order to coordinate the efforts of Ilma-ghôli.
'The rescue of ${PLAYER} and your brother must be left to others.'

'Rothog and I will lead this rescue mission. ${PLAYER} and Jajax are imprisoned by those we counted allies, even friends. The two of us must set this right.
'I will speak with the Temámir about this secret entrance he has discovered. Were it not now of use, I would rue its very existence! But it seems such a way into the jail will now help us bring our friends to freedom, and about that I will not complain.
'Regret not that you do not accompany us! There will be danger enough for you here, Daxamat. All of the city will soon come alive with anger, and you must be ready to guide its furious voice!'
'The Harlond burns. We have arrived too late.'
The assembled fighters of Ilma-ghôli listen to your directives

Your gathered allies await their orders in the planning room to the right of the entrance to the refuge.

'Imprisoned? We will need to do something about that.
'Something else troubles me. Some of the people with whom I spoke claim that Nakási commands the fleet, and she has joined hands with Balakhâd, the son of Balakhôr; their ships are crewed with Heirsworn Corsairs, Orcs of Mordor, and Ordâkhai soldiers alike. If this is true, fully half of the Kindred of the Coins have changed their loyalties: Nakási, Hármelak, and Khôltekh can no longer be trusted to lead.
'Where is Tatháta in all this? She has always been more solitary than the rest, but if she sides with the betrayers it will be difficult for Rothog and I to convince the city that our position is just. That way is certain to lead to bloodshed. I do not fear it! I would prefer not to slay my fellows if it might be avoided, but we need to remove the blight from the Kindred of the Coins in order to cleanse it, one way or another.
'But you are the leader of this band of fighters, Daxamat. Consider all that must be done, and give your people their commands. The uprising in Umbar begins now!'
'But you are the leader of this band of fighters, Daxamat. Consider all that must be done, and give your people their commands. The uprising in Umbar begins now!'

'Rûmina and I have many contacts within the Sail-haven and the Lower Ward. We will spread the news of Hármelak's betrayal, and rally the Umbari to march upon Dâr Laja. Corsairs and mariners, vendors and caravan drivers, even the troublemakers and brigands of the Gut... all these folk have reason to overthrow the rulers who think to sell us to Mordor or to Ordâkh!
'Even the Corsair Jeduth may join us in this. He has retired from the privateering trade, but he will see the rightness of Ilma-ghôli's cause!'

'I know of a place where many weapons are stored, Dax: beneath the Dahâl Huliz, in Kamrabezûr, are racks and racks of weapons for use in the arena. But that is not all we can take from there. The gladiators revere Rothog as both a great warrior and a leader of the city. If they are shown he sides with us to overthrow the villains who betray Umbar Baharbêl, we will have obtained not just weapons, but fighters to wield them as well.
'We must not underestimate the reputation of Rothog the Storm! The prospect of facing him in single combat was enough to keep me safely and content in the jail. I knew not that Kinsman Belondor would free me from captivity without fighting only days later, but I did know not to face Rothog on the blood-sands for my freedom!
'But today I will fight for freedom from the traitors who pretend to speak for Umbar... but I fight beside the Storm, and not against him!'

'There is no need to draw stones, as is the custom among my people in Khabârkhad; I know what duty is set before me.
'First I will go to Mekab-kuphâr with this unpleasant news: Khôltekh has jeopardized the lives, safety, and wealth of the Temámir people. I will bring those of my fellows who agree with this position to the Shoreward Stone, where we will seek an audience with Inîk Jewel-brow, the Hall-father. One way or another, Khôltekh will be removed from power for his part in this calamity.
'While I do this, someone else must make use of the secret entrance into the Fleet-fast jail in order to free your brother and ${PLAYER}.'

The Hidden Fortress

'Bârshud has fled, but our work is not yet finished. The remainder of the Ekhamâti Umûni and their Ordâkhai forces are holed up inside the hidden fortress before us.
'Dun Shûma, built by an ancient Shâr of Nísaka, is said to hold many of our ancestral treasures. I suspect there is one treasure in particular that Bârshud seeks: the lost crown of Aragín the Queller. Holding such a thing would give his claim to the throne of Hamât legitimacy. We must prevent Ekhamât from seizing it, at all costs.'

'We are victorious. I now hold the Lion-crown of Aragín the Queller, and must make official my claim to the throne of Hamât. This, I fear, is just the beginning of a long campaign.
'That sorcerer has given us a parting gift, a secret he expected us to take to our graves: Ordâkh is manipulating Ekhamât, puppeteering Bârshud to fight their war for them. The new Hul must be eager to regain control of all Shagâna, and will use unwitting vassals to do so. Even if Bârshud’s claim over Hamât is defeated, my people will not be truly safe until the threat of Ordâkh is eliminated for good.
'You have been by my side through all of this, ${PLAYER}. For now, I have little to offer but my sincerest thanks, but once this war is finally won, the Kingdom of Hamât will forever be in your debt.'

'I have placed a bucket of water to the west. Will you add the portions of the blight you collected to the water? I am interested in the effect they may have upon the water.'
'I have placed a bucket of water just over there. Will you add the portions of the blight you collected to the water? I am interested in the effect they may have upon the water.'
'Well, then. I know not what it means, but it smells terrible.'

'Cúridwan passed north-east in the direction of Laivárth. If you head that way too, might I trouble you to defeat some of the Orcs that lurk beside the path? They seem untroubled by the noisome fumes that now fill the air, and it is our burden to thin their numbers before they become emboldened. They have fashioned two camps near here, Mauthark and Mokh Grazádh, and if you defeat these creatures you will be aiding both the Kintai and your friend Cúridwan.'
'Your friend Cúridwan may be at the grove of Laivárth, to the north-east. You should look for her there.'

'The fungal corruption has begun to work on this grove as well, despite the efforts of its tenders to halt its spread. See the mark of the blight there, and there? My heart is heavy, and I have only just arrived! Imagine how it must feel to live in this wood, and watch the corruption advance with the passage of the hours, and of the days!'

'Your friend speaks the truth: it is difficult to watch the blight consume our land, twisting the trees in horrible mockery of their once-healthy forms. Some among my people believe the fungal contagion spews from a single entity: Sívigush, the Earth-terror; others believe the blight is itself alive, and Sívigush is in fact an evil composed of every tendril, mushroom, and spore released into the foetid air of Adagím.
'I know not what I believe. If you are willing to take this trowel and bring back a sample from several locations where the rot has taken hold, perhaps we can learn something that will be of use. I will speak with your friend while you conduct this study on my behalf, and help the two of you as I can.
'The rot is particularly bad to the north-east, north-west, and west of Laivárth.'

'If Cúridwan has gone ahead into Adagím, that is where our road must lead. But it is the foolhardy traveller who passes into an unfamiliar land without knowledge; we must not be unprepared.
'What can Thórvilon tell us of the woods into which we must go?'

'What can I tell you about Adagím that will not pain me? Very little, my friend. So much of the Emerald Wood has been tainted by blight and corruption that the beautiful forest of my youth seems somehow unreal. When the Ordâkhai came north, something they brought with them damaged the soil. The blight that slew the trees of Imhûlar began first in Adagím, taking the form of a terrible fungal rot. Many groves of my people were abandoned, until only Sul Madásh remained unspoiled.
'The Adagím of today is a nightmarish, boggy wilderness, despite the efforts of the Kintai. Some of us fled westward to Vartúlin, or to Shonith beside the Khûd, but I fear it is only a matter of time before the blight consumes every tree that once grew within the Emerald Wood of Nisigím.
'Perhaps Inkanûsh and Cúridwan together will be able to fight it, ${PLAYER}. I hope it is so! Hurry on to speak with Athgai at the border with Adagím, and hasten the meeting of these two wise ones!'
'It is the foolhardy traveller who passes into an unfamiliar land without knowledge; we must not be unprepared. What can Thórvilon tell us of the woods into which we must go?'

'Wait a moment, newcomers. Few come this way, save the Orcs, and it is my duty to keep watch for any who stray this far into the wood. What business have you in Adagím?'
You tell the Kinta guard that you are only passing through on your way south, but that you hoped to find Cúridwan somewhere on the way. Athgai nods thoughtfully.
'I stopped and spoke with her briefly a few hours ago, as I have stopped you. She said she possessed a salve that might cure us of the Lâg Dávrit. If only it might be true! She passed north-east in the direction of Laivárth. If you head that way too, might I trouble you to defeat some of the Orcs that lurk beside the path? They seem untroubled by the noisome fumes that now fill the air, and it is our burden to thin their numbers before they become emboldened. They have fashioned two camps near here, Mauthark and Mokh Grazádh, and if you defeat these creatures you will be aiding both the Kintai and your friend Cúridwan.'

'Perhaps Inkanûsh and Cúridwan together will be able to fight the corruption that has taken root in Imhûlar and Adagím. I hope it is so! Hurry on to speak with Athgai at the border into Adagím, and hasten the meeting of these two wise ones!'

'The road to discovery is often slow and riddled with setbacks. Such is the way of things.
'Your friend Glorfindel spoke to me of your search for Cúridwan. She has likely gone on ahead to Sul Madásh, largest of the Kinta groves within the Emerald Wood. But wait!
'Before you come to Sul Madásh, you should spend a moment at Tûl Ama, the Hill of the Mother. Look for it to the south-east, for it is on your way. The Old Mother, Amûma in my tongue, is unmistakable. You will know her at once, and Cúridwan is like to have stopped there herself.
'Farewell, my new friends.'

'Before you come to Sul Madásh, you should spend a moment at Tûl Ama, the Hill of the Mother. Look for it to the south-east, for it is on your way. The Old Mother, Amûma in my tongue, is unmistakable. You will know her at once, and Cúridwan is like to have stopped there herself.'

'I knew what to expect and still the sorrow cuts me deeply, ${PLAYER}. This great mother-tree of the Emerald Wood stood unharmed for untold years, but now the blight that savages Adagím works its evil even upon her. See the blood-red sap she weeps as she mourns!
'Can the Ordâkhai really have wrought this? The Kintai with whom we have spoken seem to believe this corruption began when that Empire crossed north... but how could they have caused such evil as this? Does it not seem beyond their capability, if not beyond their cruel intent?'

'For years I have pondered that question, friends of the Kintai, but no solution has come to me. I cannot conceive of such a thing: who would willingly inflict such harm upon this land, or upon Amûma and her children? I have long been the warden of this grove. Tending to her in this state has left me weak and sorrowful.'
Irsinith sighs heavily, and you are struck by the notion that she seems very much alike to the mother-tree she guards. You ask if there is anything you and Glorfindel might do to lighten her burden.

'She is gone? Did she not say she would wait here for us to return? I did not really know Cúridwan as well as my brother Ulishár did, but I was not aware her head was always floating away among the clouds! Have you known anyone else like that, ${PLAYER}? And if you have, how do you put up with it?
'Let us hope she went to Sul Madásh. I am not eager to chase her throughout Adagím any longer!'

'Let us make our way through the swamp to the north-west and continue our search.'

'I have done you a disservice, ${PLAYER}. I should not have spoken of my brother if I could not tell you all.
'Ulishár once took great joy in wandering far across the lands of Shagâna, west to the shores of Umbar and south to the fringe of the great desert of Gûl Sakhâsha. He would come back with tales of his adventures, much like the ones I believe you have had!
'Several years ago, he was captured by soldiers of Ordâkh. They imprisoned him in one of their cities, where he was made to labour. The watch on him lapsed as the armies of Ordâkh assembled and marched north to war, and a few months past he escaped and crossed the Mûr. Ever since he returned, he has been unwilling to leave the bounds of Sul Madásh.
'Now I have told you all, and I ask that you please speak not of this to Ulishár. Come, our destination lies to the south-west: the Elderwell. I remember Ulishár used to visit this place with Cúridwan, in happier times.'
'Come, our destination lies to the south-west: the Elderwell. I remember Ulishár used to visit this place with Cúridwan, in happier times.'

'I had hoped my salve could put an end to the Lâg Dávrit, the Pale Blight, but alas! It is not enough. The corruption birthed beneath Adagím fights against each of the arts I bring to bear against it, and the Pale Blight is a symptom only; so too are the fungal blossoms that spring all about us. I must strengthen my salve, and for that I need to learn more.
'I spied crocodiles to the north-west as I climbed to this place. Collect their teeth and some samples of the blight near which they live, and bring them to me for study. My mind is awhirl with the possibility that this corruption can be beaten and its harm undone.'

'I spied crocodiles to the north-west as I climbed to this place. Collect their teeth and some samples of the blight near which they live, and bring them to me for study. My mind is awhirl with the possibility that this corruption can be beaten and its harm undone.'

'But how can this be?'
The Wizard's brow furrows.
'It is true that some things were left unknown to me by the Powers that sent me to Middle-earth, that I might best accomplish my purpose... but the number of my Order is five. Far have I travelled across Middle-earth to oppose the evils of Sauron and his servants, and Radagast too has played his part. Saruman was the highest of my Order, until he succumbed, but even in that I see the role Saruman played in the defeat of Sauron.

How might \qthe Golden Maiden\q or \qthe Sorceress in Green\q be received in the cold northern lands, I wonder?
'The Wizards of the northern line and the Wizards of the southern line must be different, or they must each fail in their purposes. In this I see the wisdom of the Powers that gave to us our missions, separate though shared they may be.
'It is not for an individual to see the entire breadth of the tapestry. That is reserved for those who sent us, is it not?'

'Ísman rules above them all, the Sky-master. In his lordly form he observed the comings and goings of the Shoghór as they crossed the great desert; it was in feminine aspect that Ísman lit the stars to show them the way.

'Is it not better to remain in the land with which you are familiar, even if your memories fade and all that remains is the anger and disappointment of the Väiri? For all of my life I have been told this is the way of my people. I do not know what to think, ${PLAYER}.'

'If the Sorceress in Green here remained, she might already have restored the Emerald Wood! But of her I have received no word.'

'I know not what your brother would choose for himself, Ulishár. None but Baharúd can know if he would choose to remain in this land he loved or if he would accept the fate given to Elvendom at its creation.
