Wanted: Assistance with the procurement of honeycombs from a difficult position outside of Bree. If interested, speak with Lolo Wendingway at the cross-roads of Staddle, Combe, and Bree.
- Lolo

'Well met! I must confess, I had little hope that my notice would draw much patronage, being as vague as it was. Yet it gladdens me to see that there remain folk in these days who are willing to lend aid to another.
'Now, to the matter. I have a friend who seeks to begin a modest enterprise in the keeping of bees for honey. I told her there was no finer place to seek such sweetness than the bear dens nearby; and, for reasons of my own, I may have spoken somewhat too boldly of my ability to gather samples of honeycomb for her.
'Thus have I found myself in a rather uncomfortable position. My first efforts served only to stir the bears to wrath, and I must admit, with some shame, that I fled.
'It is my hope that you may prevail where I, alas, did not.'
Make your way to the cross-roads of Staddle, Combe, and Bree and speak with Lolo Wendingway about this venture.
Return to Lolo Wendingway at the cross-roads of Staddle, Combe, and Bree and deliver to him the honeycombs and good news.
Complete the mission: Honey Farmer's Woe.
A post from Lolo Wendingway looking for assistance with bears and honey.
Collect and deliver the keg of Green Dragon's Breath Ale to the The Green Dragon Inn
Collect and deliver the keg of Old Withywindle to the Golden Perch Inn
Collect and deliver Blagrove's Brown to the Bird and Baby Inn
Return to Everard Holebourne with news of your success
Collect the Toad's Tongue Ale and deliver it to The Floating Log Inn
Trouble with Deliveries for the Inns

'You truly pulled my toes from the flames, friend, and I am most grateful to you for it.
'I only hope the spiders will have the good sense to remain in the woods where they belong, henceforth. My poor pony shall be sore for a week, I fear, after all the exertion she has put forth.
'And, that is saying nothing of the state of my cart!
'Still, my chief trouble is put right for the moment, and that is thanks entirely to you. I shall not soon forget your kindness.'
Delivered the keg of Green Dragon's Breath Ale
Delivered the keg of Old Withywindle
Delivered the keg of Toad's Tongue Ale
Delivered the keg of Blagrove's Brown
Speak with Everard Holebourne at Overhill

Post:
Needed: a person with patience and a sturdy back to help collect and deliver kegs of ale and beer to the inns of The Shire.
- Everard Holebourne

'Oh, thank you kindly for answering my call. I am in a most dreadful pickle.
'I was on my way back from Brockenborings when my road was suddenly barred by spiders—great, creeping things, if you can believe it. My poor pony took fright, slipped her harness, and in the commotion all but turned my cart about.
'The fright of it drove the spiders off for a time, but I could do little more than haul the kegs down from the cart before my courage quite failed me. They remain there still, away to the north-east.
'I am sorely in need of a stout-hearted soul to gather up those kegs and see my deliveries completed.
'Each one is plainly marked and must be delivered with all due haste, if you would be so kind.'
Make your way to Overhill and seek out Everard Holebourne.

Find the cart accident north-east of Overhill and collect the Blagrove's Brown keg and deliver it to the Bird and Baby Inn, or Collect the Toad's Tongue keg and deliver it to the Floating Log Inn, or collect the Green Dragon's Breath Ale keg and deliver it to The Green Dragon Inn, or collect the Old Withywindle keg and deliver it to the Golden Perch Inn.
With all the deliveries completed, return to Everard Holebourne at Overhill and give him the splendid news.
A posting from Everard Holebourne of Overhill asks for assistance with making deliveries to the inns around The Shire.
Speak with Pete Shadetree at his forge near the Bree West Gate
Complete Mission: The Blacksmith's Lost Tools
Mission: The Blacksmith's Lost Tools

'If my need were not so great, I should never have trusted them with such a thing. But there you have it. I am in rather a bind, and I fear I have little choice but to ask for your help.
'Please, make haste. I have need of those tools, and I would dearly like to have them back.'

'You have recovered my tools! I scarcely believed I should see them again.
'I truly thought I could trust those folk, but they took my good will and repaid it by proving me a fool. I shall be more careful with whom I lend my things in the future.
'You, however, are an honest and good sort. I am most grateful for the trouble you have taken on my behalf.
'I shall endeavour to be less of a fool—and rather more diligent in my choices—from this day forward.'
Speak with Pete Shadetree at his forge near the Bree West Gate

Post:
Needed: an adventurer with a will of steel. I recently lent some tools to prospectors from the south. The ruffians returned without my tools and with a tale too tall to regale in this post. Seek me out at my forge in Bree-town if you can assist.
- Pete Shadetree

'Ah! You saw my notice. Thank you kindly.
'There have been a good many folk coming into Bree of late, and I have been busier than ever. I made a decision—one that seems rather foolish now—and, as a result, some of my tools have gone missing in a place far too dangerous for the likes of me.'
He sighs heavily.
'You see, the folk to whom I lent my tools made their way to a barrow away to the south-west. There, they encountered something that frightened them badly enough to flee. In their haste, they buried my tools and ran, leaving them behind.
'I need those tools recovered, if you are willing to take up my cause.'
Make your way to Bree-town speak with Pete Shadetree at his forge near the West Gate.
Return to Pete Shadetree with his tools. You will find him at his forge near the West Gate of Bree.
Complete the mission: The Blacksmith's Lost Tools.
A posting from Pete Shadetree asks for an adventurer to help recover his lost tools.
Speak with Thrasi at his lodge in Ered Luin
Complete Mission: Many in Need
Mission: Many in Need
'Do not underestimate the bears, friend. They are stronger than they look, though their meat, when properly cured, is a delicacy fit for a king under the mountain.'

'I trust the hunt was as lively as it was successful. You have seen to it that our larder will be well stocked for many days to come.
'I will set about curing this meat at once. You have my thanks again, friend.'
Speak with Thrasi at his lodge in Ered Luin

Post:
Those with a hunter's heart can find me at my lodge in Ered Luin. We have need of game meat to cure and stock our larder. Visit me if you can assist.
- Thrasi

'Thank you for answering my notice. There are many mouths to feed hereabouts, and too few strong arms to gather what is needed. I sent out word for hunters such as yourself to aid us in bringing in meat that may be cured and stored.
'If you are willing, I can guide you to the bear camp we have chosen for this work.'
Travel to Thrasi's Lodge in Ered Luin and ask him how you may help.
Return to Thrasi at his lodge and provide him the meat you collected.
Complete the mission: Many in Need.
A notice from Thrasi, a hunter in Ered Luin, asks for assistance in stocking the hunter's larder.
Speak with Brombard Foxtail at the Mathom-house
Complete Mission: The Missing Mathoms
Mission: The Missing Mathoms

'Here you are, indeed! Willing, able, and ready to teach those Dourhands a proper lesson in what comes of thievery!
'I can direct you to the very place the scoundrels are hiding. I would ask that, while you are about it, you recover the mathoms they have stolen from us. There are eighteen in all.
'Eighteen! A dreadful number to have gone missing, if you ask me.'

'All eighteen recovered, and a proper lesson taught besides! You truly are a good soul.
'We shall see to it that these are put in order and safely stored. If only we could persuade a few more good folk to join the Society and lend a hand with the cumbersome business of sorting, storing, and displaying the multitudes of mathoms we are forever collecting, perhaps such a calamity might not befall us again!
'It is a great deal of work, you know, keeping track of so many perfectly wondrous things.'
Speak with Brombard Foxtail at the Mathom-house in Michel Delving

Post:
Brigands and thieves stole several mathoms from our collection and we are in need of assistance in their recovery. If you can spare some aid, please visit me at the Mathom-house in Michel Delving.
- Brombard Foxtail

'A terrible calamity has befallen us here at the Mathom Society, and I scarcely know where to begin!
'With mathoms being delivered and discovered all across the land, we have hardly had a moment to organize them, catalogue them, and put them properly away. Why, they have been piling up faster than we can keep track of them!
'And now, to make matters worse, it appears that our latest deliveries have been pilfered by a band of Dourhand brigands, intent - apparently - on making the lives of decent Shire-folk as miserable as possible.
'The Bounders, bless them, are far too busy with the mundane doings of the Shire to go chasing after thieves on our behalf. And so, in a moment of desperation, I posted my request for aid.
'And now, here you are.'
Return to Brombard Foxtail with the mathoms and the news that the Dourhands have been dealt a blow.
Complete the mission: The Missing Mathoms.
Find Brombard Foxtail outside of the Mathom-house in Michel Delving and ask him how you can provide assistance.
A post from Bombard Foxtail of the Mathom Society requesting assistance with recovering mathoms from the Dourhands.
Collect seeds from Tordúril
Speak with Gonediad at the Spire of Meeting in Rivendell
Collect the blacksmith notes from Hemeldir
Preparing for Departure

'Irminiric, yes. He is a good man, and I did recently send him a letter at Glân Vraig. Lainedhal must have realized he was sent back to Bree for recruitment and sent the letter on there.
'Sadly, I will not be able to see him when I do depart, as my journey will not take me near his home. I had hoped to see him at Glân Vraig, alas, there are other plans now, it seems.'
He taps his foot.
'Tordúril, a woodworker here in Rivendell, has been gathering the seeds I planned to gift Irminric. And Hemeldir, the master of the forge will have the sword design. You will find them to the north-west of the Spire of Meeting.
'When you have acquired them, return to my friend at Bree and tell him that I will ever remember his stories, his ferocity, and the nights we bled together against our common foe in the Ettenmoors.'

'Ah yes, Gonediad mentioned this to me.'
He reaches into his robe.
'I hope I have not over-explained the methods used. I would hate to confuse the Man who wishes to learn this craft. Please, return this to Gonediad and tell him that I have done my best to detail the materials, direction, and methods used to craft this sword.'

'Gonediad's devotion to the man and to his position are both admirable. I have done as he asked and collected several samples of the seeds that make this valley beautiful and lush.
'Take them with you and see that they are delivered to Gonediad so that he may pass them on to his friend.'

'You have returned, and with the seeds and notes I have requested.
'My friend Irminric will be very pleased, I hope. I shall miss the lad. His tales were bold and entertaining for a Man. His sword arm strong, as well.
'Please, when you return to him, tell him I shall keep close his stories, and spread the tale of his bravery and prowess among those with whom I find my rest in the West. His deeds will live on, eternally.'
He offers a wry smile as he returns the items to you.
'Thank you, ${PLAYER}.'

After listening to the words Gonediad asked you to share, Irminric stifles a tear.
'He is a true friend. I shall miss our talks, and I shall ever be in his debt for giving me these gifts.
'Please, take this -- and thank you for all you have done for me.'
Collected Helemdir's notes
Speak with Sergeant-at-Arms Irminric at the South Gate of Bree

Post:
Needed: someone to assist a friend in fulfilling a promise. Visit me at my post at the South Gate of Bree for more information.
- Sergeant-at-Arms Irminric

'Hello, and thank you for responding to my notice.
'I have a friend, Gonediad, he is an Elven scholar with whom I bonded over stories and battles in the Ettenmoors. He told me he is preparing to leave, and never return. He has offered me a gift, but I cannot leave my post, and I was hoping to have someone help me.
'He said he wished to give me a design for an Elven sword and seeds from the trees of his home in Rivendell.'
He looks at you excitedly.
'Have you ever seen Rivendell? I was there, only for a few moments, but the trees and the land... hidden away as it is... well...'
He sighs.
'Can you seek out my friend and collect the gift he has offered me?'
Make your way to Bree-town and speak with Sergeant-at-Arms Irminric.
Gonediad asked you to collect a pouch of seeds from Tordúril and a sword design from Hemeldir north-west of the Spire of Meeting before returning the items to Irminric with a message of kinship.
Find and speak with the Elf Gonediad in Rivendell and enquire about the gift he is to give Sergeant-at-Arms Irminric
You have collected the seeds and notes from Tordúril and Helemdir, respectively. You should return these to Gonediad and let him know.
With his message and gifts in your possession, it is now time to make Gonediad's delivery to Irminric. Return to Bree and deliver the news and items to Sergeant-at-Arms Irminric.
A posting from a warrior named Irminric in Bree, the request is cryptic, at best.
Return the gifts and message to Sergeant-at-Arms Irminric in Bree
Show the notes and seeds to Gonediad
Speak with Brethilwen near the vineyard in Ered Luin
Complete Mission: Restoring the Vineyard
Mission: Restoring the Vineyard

'I require ten samples of my grapes, that I may be certain they remain sound and worthy of the vine. There is also a particular cask I desire to have recovered. It was the first barrel in which I ever aged my wine. Should you find it, I would be most grateful if you would return it to me.'

'You have done me a great service, my friend. The grapes yet retain their flavour and that distinctive tartness which gives my wine its character.
'With your aid, and my own resolve, I shall restore my vineyard and winery to their former grace. The work will be long, perhaps, but I have never been one to surrender easily to adversity.
'I am truly pleased that you answered my plea. Your kindness shall not be forgotten.'
Speak with Brethilwen near Limael's Vineyard in Ered Luin

Post:
My vineyard has too long been overrun by goblins, and the time has come to reclaim it and start a proper distillation of my wine once again. If you are willing to aid me, seek me out near my vineyard in Ered Luin.
- Brethilwen, the vintner

'I am pleased that you have answered my request for aid. My time here draws ever nearer to its end, and it is my wish to restore the vineyard before I depart, that I may leave it in the capable hands of another.
'I have long cherished the art of winemaking, and I believe my grapes yield a wine of rich and robust flavour. Alas, the goblins who have taken to my vineyard and winery seem to share my appreciation for them. They are many, and cruel besides, and none have yet been able to drive them away for long enough to restore my work.
'I would ask that you gather samples of my grapes and recover a cask of wine for me. While you are there, it would also be most helpful if you could see to these troublesome goblins and remind them that my vineyard is no place for them.
'It would ease my heart greatly to see the vines tended once more, before I take my leave.'
Make your way to the outskirts of Limael's Vineyard in Ered Luin and speak with the vintner, Brethilwen.
Return to Brethilwen near the vineyard in Ered Luin.
Complete the mission: Restoring the Vineyard.

A posting from the Elf maiden, Brethilwen, requesting assistance with removing goblins from her vineyard. She also desires the recovery of grapes and a cask from the vineyard, to ensure that she can restore production.
Defeat the Dunlending forces (${NUMBER}/20)

Destroy White Hand banners (${NUMBER}/5)
'Let us return to Echad Dúnann.'
Defeated Dunlending forces (${NUMBER}/20)
Destroyed White Hand banners (${NUMBER}/5)
Removing Their Foothold

Defeat the Dunlending forces at this fort and destroy the White Hand banners.

Speak with Refr Quicksilver at the cave entrance in the central Lone-lands
Complete Mission: Reclaiming Iorvinas
Mission: Reclaiming Iorvinas
'The stones are there; of that I am certain. My kin built those halls, and with your help, friend, I shall have proof enough to silence any who doubt it. Go well, and keep your weapon-hand ready.'

He studies the rubbings for a long moment.
'A bit more incomplete than I had hoped. Still, I must share these with my brother. In truth, this mark bears the look of a family sigil, or something near to it.
'This is a fine first effort, my friend. You have my thanks for all you have done.'
Speak with Refr Quicksilver at the cave entrance in the central Lone-lands

Post:
Requesting the aid of an experienced adventurer willing to get their hands a little dirty. Seek me out near the entrance to our home of old in the Lone-lands.
- Refr Quicksilver

'Iorvinas was a home of my people in ages past; I know it, deep in my bones, and I mean to prove it.
'My duties hold me here, but I sent others to scout the depths below. They found rune-stones within, marked with the signs of the builders.
'I need you to enter Iorvinas, take rubbings of those stones, and bring them back to me. There is, however, one small trouble: Orcs. The ruins are crawling with them, so keep your wits about you as you pass through the halls.'
Find Refr Quicksilver at the cave entrance in the central Lone-lands. He stands watch there. Ask him what he means by getting your hands dirty.
Return the rubbings you collected to Refr Quicksilver.
Complete the mission: Reclaiming Iorvinas.
A notice from Refr Quicksilver requests assistance in proving the lineage of the builders of Iorvinas.
Speak with Chief Tuokki at the Earth-kin camp in Ram Dúath
Complete Mission: Studying Corruption
Mission: Studying Corruption

'There is a creeping sickness in them. It goes into skin, into muscle, into bone. We must look at their flesh and study it, so that we may find a way to make them well again. We think, but we do not know, that a beast crawls among them and carries the rot.'

'I can see from the marks upon their flesh that our once-brothers suffer greatly. We must speak with our own people and use what skills we have. Perhaps then we will find a way to take away their pain.
'You have done all I asked, and more. For this, we call you friend. You have helped our once-brothers, and you have helped us.
'For this, we give you our thanks.'
Speak with Chief Tuokki at the Earth-kin camp in Ram Dúath

Post:
My pain grows with the loss of my once-brothers. They have turned ill-tempered and smell of foul earth. They are tainted by the land and more. We have need of help.
- Chief Tuokki

'Our once-brothers who till the earth with stone beaks grow sick in this land. They cry out for help, but we know little of the thing that makes our once-brothers ill.
'We cannot spare many of our number to aid them. So I turned to a way that is strange to us. Many have come here, like you, and helped us before.
'Would you help us, and our once-brothers?'
Make your way to the Earth-kin camp in Ram Dúath and seek out Chief Tuokki to ask how you can help.
Return to Chief Tuokki at the Earth-kin camp in Ram Dúath, provide the samples you collected, and tell him of the large cave-claw you faced.
Complete the mission: Studying Corruption.
A posting from an Earth-kin calling for help in learning why their 'once-brothers' have become plagued by corruption.
Speak with Nathronwen at Duillond and collect her seed pouch
Speak with Isferon in Duillond and collect his seed pouch
Deliver the seed pouches you collected to Dorongúr at Duillond
Speak with Ialadir in Celondim and collect his seed pouch
Speak with Gwaloth in Celondim and collect her seed pouch
Speak with Raindis in Celondim and collect her seed pouch
Seeds for a Remembrance Garden

'Gladly will I aid Dorongúr in the making of his remembrance garden. I believe his friend will be both surprised and comforted to know that such devotion has been given on his behalf.
'Go now with haste, and see that these are delivered safely.'

'Each of my friends is pure of heart and has given freely. These seeds shall bloom, and in their flowering may they strengthen my friend's resolve.
'His grief is deep, and too long has he dwelt upon what more he might have done to save his beloved from so untimely an end.
'These seeds may yet bring healing, for they were gathered from many gardens and bear the flowers and herbs that his beloved held most fair.
'For this, I thank you, friend.'

'Dorongúr's love for his friends is rooted deep in the grief he bore from Edhelion. Loss has shaped him in ways that few among us can fully understand.
'Take these, and may the seeds of my garden help restore the heart of the one he seeks to strengthen anew.'

'Dorongúr's request is born of deep love for one of our kin.
'His compassion has moved my heart, and with all haste I have gathered seeds for the garden of remembrance. Take them, I beg you, and tell Dorongúr that his kindness is a light by which others may be guided.'

'It gladdens me to know that Dorongúr's request is being fulfilled. His heart is noble, and his purpose no less so; gladly do I offer seeds for the remembrance garden he would make.
'Take this pouch, then, and bear it back to him, that his wish may come to flower.'
'I am glad to give these seeds to Dorongúr. May the garden he tends bring solace to his friend, for loss lies heavy upon the hearts of our kind.'
Collected Ialadir's seed pouch
Collected Gwaloth's seed pouch
Collected Raindis's seed pouch
Collected Nathronwen's seed pouch
Collected Isferon's seed pouch
Speak with Dorongúr Whitethorn among the smiths in Duillond

Post:
I request the assistance of a person of discretion for a task that is near to my heart. If you are interested, please visit me at Duillond.
- Dorongúr Whitehorn

'Mae govannen, and I thank you for answering my request. Be assured, friend, there is no shadowed purpose in it. I seek only to fashion a surprise for one dear to me; were I to be seen, the gift would lose much of its grace.
'I would ask you to gather seed pouches from Nathronwen and Isferon here in Duillond, and likewise from Ialadir, Gwaloth, and Raindis in Celondim.
'Nathronwen may be found beyond the bridge to the south, and Isferon keeps watch over the river to the north-west.
'Ialadir watches over the farm-lands of Celondim. Gwaloth keeps vigil near the crafters in the upper hills, and Raindis stands watch above the northern docks.
'Gather their seed pouches and return to me.'
Make your way to Duillond and find Dorongúr on the rise overlooking the river among the smiths.
Return to Dorongúr among the smiths at Duillond and deliver him the seeds you collected.
Dorongûr has asked that you speak with Elves in Duillond and Celondim to collect packets of seeds for a gift he is making for a friend. He does not want his friend to know about the gift.
A posting from Dorongúr Whitehorn asks for assistance in a personal task.
Speak with Longo Burrow at his farm
Speak with Longo Burrow at his farm in Tuckborough
Complete Mission: Tend and Defend Crops
Mission: Tend and Defend Crops

'My beans are ripe upon the vines and need gathering so that I may bundle up the bushels and send them off to market. And, if you can believe it, the new pipe-weed I have been growing is coming along splendidly. I should like to have the leaves gathered and dried, that I might see how they smoke.
'Oh, and there are meddlesome shrews making their way onto the hill. If you could do something about those as well, it would save the crop from being nibbled to ruin.'

'It is shaping up to be a wonderful harvest, after all! I shall begin bundling the beans as soon as we have finished with the niceties, and I will set the pipe-weed leaves to drying directly after. If all goes well, I may have the finest tobacco I have ever grown!
'I have you to thank for much of it, my friend. I—and my poor farm-hands—are most grateful that you have taken up the work while they are laid low. You have done us a fine turn indeed.'

Post:
My farm-hands are all feeling ill as of late, and I cannot tend to everything my farm needs. I am looking for assistance from those able to do some light farm work in Tuckborough.
- Longo Burrow

'I had thought I would lose a good portion of my crops—and perhaps my livelihood besides—until you came along. My farm-hands all took ill at once, the poor fellows. A terrible happenstance for them, and no small trouble for me.
'But now that you are here, and looking fit enough to lend a hand, I daresay we may yet come through this in good order.'
Find Longo Burrow at his farm in Tuckborough and ask him how you can help.
Return to Longo Burrow with your collection of beans and pipe-weed, and tell him that the shrew burrows have been closed.
Complete the mission: Tend and Defend Crops.
A posting from Longo Burrow in Tuckborough requests some assistance on his farm.

Speak with Tinúriel in Echad Dúnann in Eregion
Complete Mission: Removing Their Foothold
Mission: Removing Their Foothold

'You must drive the Dunlendings from this small fort and destroy whatever signs might lead the White Hand to this place. Leave them no trail by which they might find their way here again.
'Be relentless. This is an enemy not to be underestimated.'

'You have returned, and with you comes word of victory.
'If I seem overly pleased by this news, forgive me. It is only that I remember too well the hurts I suffered in these lands, and the sorrow that lingers here for those of us who have seen their former glory.
'We must remain vigilant in these lands. They may never again become what they were in the Elder Days of the Elves, but that does not mean all hope is lost.
'There may yet be a brighter future here; for those who come after us.'
Speak with Tinúriel at the encampment in Eregion

Post:
Assistance required. Forces of the Dunlending are attempting to establish a foothold for the White Hand in Eregion. Visit me in Eregion to assist with this issue.
- Tinúriel

'These lands hold many memories for the Elves. We remember when they were the seat of our people and the dwelling-place of our king. Now, much lies in ruin, and what once was has passed into memory. We cannot return to the days from which we came.
'Yet we may still have a hand in shaping what these lands shall become. It is for this that I ask your aid.
'Men from the South press farther into these lands at the bidding of the cruel master of the White Hand. If we are swift, we may yet halt their advance before they gain a stronger foothold.'
Report to Tinúriel in Eregion and see what you can do to assist her.
Return to Tinúriel and report on your success.

Speak with Idhrien at the Echad Dagoras in Enedwaith
Complete Mission: Unfortunate Circumstances
Mission: Unfortunate Circumstances

'Be wary, for the jailors will not freely abandon their stronghold. Guards will remain, and you may deal with them as need requires. My wish is that their cruel means of binding be destroyed, and that the bodies of the dead be burned with honour. A provisioner, a warrior, and an archer, I know, met their end within.
'Go with care.'

'Then it is done. To those who could no longer defend themselves, you have brought a final rest. For those who might yet be taken, you have weakened the chains that await them.
'When all this is ended, we shall cast down that place in full. Until that day, this small solace must suffice.'

Post:
My request is for a stalwart combatant to ensure that those unjustly imprisoned, or worse, receive the justice they deserve. Seek me at our encampment at Fordirith in Enedwaith.

'Grant me a moment to speak of the cause behind my request. We know of a place where grievous wrongs are wrought, and it is for those who have suffered there that I make this plea.
'Prisoners, whether warriors taken in battle or hapless folk ensnared by ill fortune, are brought to a jail nearby and there tormented, or worse. Of three who perished within those walls we have knowledge, yet their bodies could not be reclaimed.
'I seek one with courage enough to enter that den of sorrow, shatter the manacles that might yet bind others, and commit to flame those who paid the final price. Will you do this deed for me?'

Mission: It's Always Winter in Forochel

'Our hunters drove the herd between two great stones and were ready to set upon them when the Gauredain arrived with their war-beasts. Be wary of those beasts, for they are strong and bred for war. But gather what we need: the meat, the pelts, and the bones.'

'You have proven yourself an ally to us.
'With this food, we shall endure the long nights with full bellies. With these pelts, we shall make warm clothing and cover our tents against the bitter wind. The bones will serve us as weapons, stakes, and poles for our shelters.
'In these lands, nothing can be wasted.
'The cold takes all that is left unused.'
Speak with Ora at the main Lossoth Camp in Forochel

Post:
Our hunters require aid with stocking our larders as a potent chill covers our land. Those interested should report to me at our main encampment in Forochel.
- Ora

'It is high sun, and yet another day passes beneath the cold sky. Our larders grow bare, while our enemies creep ever closer.
'Our hunters had cornered a small herd of mammoths, intending to take them for their meat, pelts, and bones. We would waste nothing. The meat would fill our bellies, the pelts would keep out the cold, and the bones would become tools, weapons, stakes, and poles for our tents.
'But the Gauredain came upon them with their great war-beasts. They use the mammoths to breed beasts of terrible size for battle, and so our hunt was broken.
'I turn now to those who come from beyond our lands for aid.
'If you are willing, help us fill our stores once more.'

Mission: Stolen Weapons and Supplies

'Eight swords and eight axes were lost, and I fear they may now be in the hands of those knaves. Six crates of supplies were taken as well, containing salves, food, and other necessities for those who dwell here.
'If you are able to recover what was lost, return to me when the task is done.'

'You have returned and with you, all that was lost!
'I am most pleased that you happened upon my note, and more grateful still that you have returned from your venture unscathed.
'There is much hardship in these lands, and more than enough folk willing to do harm. It is good to know, then, that there is still courage and decency to be found in this world.
'You have my thanks, friend. You have done a good deed for us all.'

'I am pleased that my message has been found by one of such noble sort. In these days, scoundrels may take many forms, and danger is never far from the road.

'We have neither the strength nor the numbers to assault the tomb where the stolen goods were taken, but perhaps you may fare better than we. If you are willing, of course.'

Use the camp-fire beside the Têtikir Mentor

'When you venture forward, friend, focus on the details. Notice the smallest things, there are hidden treasures to be found in every grain of sand.
'Listen to the wind, hear how she brings tidings from your past, providing you guidance, and connexion to allies and ancestors, departed or distant. She will heed your call when you cry to her to smite your foes...
'This is the insight I can give you, friend.'

As you stare into the fire, the Têtikir Mentor begins speaking of family, friends, and warriors whom he has loved and fought beside. His tale weaves to the generation before his, and how they travelled from the steppes of his homeland in the east. His people carry a natural aversion to wolf-worshipping Khashkhilar, and so they are an ally against this common enemy.
The fire dances before you, and through the story-telling, images coalesce in the flames. In your chest you feel the hoof-falls of charging horses and the clash of spears against enemy regiments.
The visions shift from the story-teller's words to memories of your own battles, of riding across the world, and the battles you've fought beside kith and kin. You gain insight and understanding into how this knowledge can be used and, better, how to access it in the lands of Draugardh.
You have gained insight into the Têtikir Survival Skills
After learning the lessons and skills of the Scouts of Draugardh, the mentor sent you on to Kol Sákla to the east to seek teaching from the Têtikir.
The Têtikir Mentor asked you to use the fire to focus on his voice and his teaching. Focus on invoking the ancestors in the manner the Têtikir do to survive the wilds of Draugardh.
Speak with the Têtikir Mentor in Kol Sákla

'There is another group, further to the east at Kol Sákla. They are called the Têtikir. There is a mentor there who will teach you their ways. Tell them we sent you, and they will share their insight.
'We are all starved for allies in this land.'

'Another ally from the west? It is good to meet you.
'As with the Scouts, we are ever watchful of enemies in these lands, but where they would draw the enemy out, we find what others cannot see.
'We call our ancestors to watch over us to restore ourselves or our other allies. We cry to the sky to call down light to illuminate the darkness and strike fear into our enemies.
'In battle, our ancestors guide our weapons and arts to strike our foes more consistently. We do this by communion with fire.
'Come, commune with the fire, and hear my words. They will help you better understand how we survive in these lands.'

Your vision clears after a time and as you return to your senses the Têtikir Mentor beckons you to speak with him. You should speak with him at his camp-fire at Kol Sálka.

Speak with the Scout Mentor at Dhol Têg

'Good enough. The creatures here have yet to understand what we are doing with this communication. And, honestly, the marker you throw is more important. You show us where to shoot and if we are near, we will loose our arrows.
'Our battles give us insight into striking our enemies. When you look at the enemies in this land, you will want to target their joints. Take your time to plan your attacks and you set them up for more potent damage with successive strikes.
'Lastly, we are not the only watchers here in Draugardh.
'If you desire to draw forth the most powerful enemies here, feign injury or exhaustion after you defeat anything. If you succeed well enough in seeming wounded or nearly defeated, then the most potent of enemies will make themselves known and engage.
'We learned this lesson painfully, at first. With coordination and numbers, we now weaken the enemy through baiting these forces to fight.'
'You know all I can teach.'

After learning the lessons and skills of the Khemozêl, the mentor directed you to seek out another, like you, who may also have lessons and skills to share and teach. You will find the Scout Mentor near the bridge over the river to the east.

'We are vigilant in this land. Always keeping watch for one another and our earned allies. The land is too severe to go without assistance.

'Ah, ${PLAYER} returns. Did you run into trouble on your hunt also?
'As we trekked back to Khel Wêro with enough meat to feed the whole outpost, we were beset by a pack of wolves!
'I must confess that I was taken unaware when they first struck, and would now be greatly injured if it were not for Hêg-maka-Chêrd and her spear that I have thus far belittled.
'Never again! I will admit that her throwing of the spear when we were hunting was actually quite impressive. Her gloom-glass was as sharp as any blade I have ever seen, and the accuracy of her throw is astonishing! Direct hits through ribs to strike right at the heart. The goltur were dead before they hit the ground!
'She handled the wolves with no less efficacy, though her blade did break in the fighting. That is why she carries spares, and they are light enough to easily do so.
'Honesty, for all my vigour and strength, I was best put to use as a pack-pony, carrying her spoils home for her.'

'Do let me know when you've managed to gather those delothlín crystals.'

'Ah, ${PLAYER}. Welcome to Heledhris! A rather forbidding place, don't you think?
'The shadow of Mordor and Sauron's dark influence yet linger over this place like a forgotten curse, still lurking in its burning ravines and twisted jungles even after his passing from this world.
'There is one such remnant of this darkness that I wish to study - curious stones called delothlín by the locals, a greenish crystal which seems to originate from from lodes of dread-sheen, which Sauron experimented with for the crafting of fell weapons for his lieutenants.
'The locals reportedly consider these crystals to be accursed stones, often carried as charms by Sauron's followers as a symbol of his favour - but I would see for myself what properties they possess, and I understand that they can be found in local metal deposits, or occasionally in the possession of the former servants of the dark lord.
'Alas, neither of these sources is one I am suited to explore, and so I ask your favour in this matter, if you could gather some of these crystals for me to study?'

'Well, I have my results regarding the delothlín, and I'm afraid that the rumours of these crystals being corrupted and dangerous in nature was if anything understated. I would advise not keeping it on your person overlong if you're concerned about such things.
'Still, it is fascinating. It seems to adopt the nature of other things it is exposed to, and accentuates them in turn? It could have many uses - but that very malleable nature of the crystal has caused it to absorb the corruption that has laid upon these lands for long ages. Sauron's evil has seeped deep into the land and changed the nature the stones themselves - and these crystals most of all.
'As they are I would not dare make use of them in any craft or alchemy. The results would be... unpleasant. But one of our scouts in the north has brought me a tale of a strange and primitive folk who appear to have somehow made use of these crystals without falling prey to its curse, even though they appear to fear it greatly and avoid those who carry it.
'These 'Woses' may know some secret to the delothlín crystals, and it may behoove you to make the journey and speak to them - to learn what they know of it. But they are an odd and superstitious people. Take care, for we know nothing of their customs and they seem fearful of all outsiders.'
'You walk among the Khemozêl, and we do not often speak with outsiders, but twin wolves of fear and hunger stalk us in recent moons. We cannot turn away those who might offer aid.'
The Way of the Wose

'You may attempt the rites whenever you are ready. The three braziers I handed you can be placed upon the ground and lit, after which you must stand among them and make use of one of the recipes I gave you to perform the rite itself. Which version you decide to use depends mostly on which professions you excel in - their results should be the same.
'Make sure you have everything at the ready before you begin! All three <rgb=#00e4ff>braziers</rgb>, whichever <rgb=#00e4ff>recipe</rgb> you are <rgb=#00e4ff>proficient</rgb> with, and of course <rgb=#00e4ff>ten delothlín crystals</rgb> to be purified.'

'Success then? Incredible. Who would have known that such a strange folk possessed both the wisdom and the constitution for such a feat?
'Oh, but, you do look a bit pale, don't you....
'This is likely not a rite that should be performed without giving oneself a chance to recover from its side effects. As for myself, I think I may avoid this particular method. I suspect I may not quite have what it takes, and I don't want to learn the hard way whether that's true or not.
'Do be careful with it. I suggest you stop immediately should you begin to grow any additional fur, notice the lengthening of your teeth, or should find yourself suffering an unexplained urge to devour anyone.
'You know what I mean.'
The Rites of Purification

Speak with the Khemozêl crafter

'Now there's a rare sight indeed - a Westron in the Draugardh! What has drawn your people so far from your lands, into such a bleak and forbidding realm? Not dreams of conquest I hope - there's precious little to claim in these broken lands.
'The Khemozêl? A strange folk. They watch from afar and do not approach us, then scatter faster than rabbits when we spot them. Their ways seem simple, but they know these mountains and jungles well.
'You say they know of these strange accursed stones? Let me see what you have brought then, and we will discuss the matter further.'

'You have faced the Draugrim and returned whole. You are a brave hunter, and so we shall speak of the accursed stones - though take care your voice does not carry to the mountains above, should the stones hear you speak of them.'

'There are three rites that must come together to purify the accursed stones.
'The Rite of Ash, which is known to those who carve wood and walk among the trees.
'The Rite of Leaf, which is known to those who grow plants and gather their bounty.
'And the Rite of Stone, known to those who take from the earth the metals and shining gems that I craft into works with my own hands.
'Performed together, the rites ask the accursed stone to give up its evil ways and return to the true ways of the mountain that was its home. It then releases the evil within it, so that we may devour it.
'The last rite was most closely guarded, for the ways of stone and metal are dangerous, and few could be trusted with them. So it was lost to us when its keeper was taken by the mountain.'

'Bah! We devour the Evil! Not the stones.
'They are rocks and our teeth would break! Even a child knows not to eat stones....
'But listen to my words, outsider. You are not the only stranger in these lands.
'Now other men come, from the sunrise. We hide from them, for we do not know them or their ways - but they carry metal and work stone, as you do.
'If you do not know the Rite of Stone, maybe they do - for they have the mark of men who have lived beneath the terrible Eye for many long years. They know of the shadow that stood over all these lands until it fled.
'Take these to them and tell them what I have told you. Perhaps they will see the shape of the Rite of Stone in the other two, where I cannot.
'We would know those ways again, for the sake of our own people.'

'Ah, the accursed stones! Still your tongue, outsider, and speak not loudly of them....
'Yes, we long ago learned ways to draw the evil from the stones. But two winters ago woe befell my people, and the keeper of the Rite of Stone was taken by the mountain, before she passed her wisdom to another.
'We now have only the Rites of Ash and Leaf, and can no longer draw out the evil of the stones.'

'If you would learn more, then you must prove yourself. The wolves-that-were-men that have stalked us come ever closer in their search for us.
'If you can drive them away from here, then I will know you speak truly. Seek them out to the north-east, where they dwell in numbers among the stones of Daerhabar.'

'Ah, you're back with the crystals? Good. I've devised a way to purify and ignite the local iron ores in one of the Khemozêl's braziers, such that it should burn for the duration of the rite. In truth, the rites seem to simply require that the crystals be exposed to the smoke of each of these braziers, allowing them mingle around it, so that their uncorrupted nature can be drawn into them.
'As for this... 'devouring' of the delothlín's curse, I've been rather too nervous to try anything of the sort myself. I think perhaps it may require a spirit of more bravery and constitution than I have.
'Here, I will provide you with everything you will need to perform the rites, though in the future you may require the aid of fellow crafters to perform it properly.'
The Têtikir Weaponsmith has asked you to gather a set of delothlín crystals in order to study the Khemozêl rites of purification.
Gather delothlín crystals (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
'I think I've almost hit upon a solution, but I'll let you know what I've found when you return with the delothlín crystals.'

'I think I see. The stone's inherent nature is not evil, but it comes to reflect the world around it - and it has steeped in the shadow of the Eye for far too long.
'Yet the Woses have come upon a means of coaxing the stone to return to its original form, drawing the evil it has absorbed out in the form of a vapour or smoke that they then... devour. That's unsettling, though they seem unchanged by it, unlike the Draugrim - so there must be something to it.
'Let me study these for a time. Perhaps I can help divine the nature of their lost 'Rite of Stone'. These other two elements seem quite simple really - I suspect it's a matter of treating the local ore in such a way that it can be burned in the same manner as metallic dust or filings - yet there may be more to it. We'll need some delothlín crystals to test it upon, so if you can gather those, I'll speak with you again when you return.'
